Title: Best nail spa in Arugam bay on the water!
Text:
I had a manicure here and it really was professional and clean.  It is right on the Ocean so very relaxing. Suzanne was my consultant and her brother Dan who works there was very helpful when the local knowledge.  I will go back for massage and foot masssge. 
They also have s business in Hikkaduwa when you head South.

Title: Best for surfing
Text: Overall, it is a wonderful experience. We visited Arugam bay last month during our anniversary. You will find many things to do from the restaurants to the beautiful white beach. The water was warm, and the tide is calm and really good place for surfing. Its a perfect day to go to the beach and have a picnic.

Title: We Love Arugam Bay
Text: Great place to chill, swim, surf, eat, shop, have sunset cocktails, its the best!!! The vibe is layback and friendly. I would highly recommend to anybody!

Title: Sun and waves.
Text: Good place for surf and a few stores to going for shopping. Very good place for rest and surf. Good clean beach with warm water. Everyone are friendly and always smiling.

Title: Great swimming, surfing, great fish aznd friendly people
Text: This place is great for surfing but even if you are not a surfer you can have a wonderful time swimming around the bay, visiting the natural reserves, socialising or trying out local and international food.

Title: Raw piece of paradise
Text:
Just wrapped up eight days in Sri Lankas Arugam Bay - a rather rare part of the world in that its still relatively raw and untouched by commercialization and development. It truly is a surfers paradise, with a main point in Arugam Bay itself and various others within 15-20 minutes by Tuk Tuk. We spent most of our time at Whiskey Point as that was where the swell was best  we visited in early June. The beach is also spacious at that point and offers a lot of room to throw a towel down and swim/surf. Not much else though so would not recommend to stay near there. Arugam Bay is definitely where its at as there are restaurants/cafes and a few bars. 

Some points to make:

This destination is about surfing, yoga and chilling. Theres waves for all kinds of riders and many day trips on offer - safari, jungle, etc. Its crucial to go during the right season though. I imagine most restaurants and places are closed otherwise, which would be a shame as youd not get to explore this lovely place for what it is - a dream for many travelers! 

Theres not much of a beachfront; its filled with boats and so you probably wont spend much time laying on the beach in A Bay. This didnt bother us as we were busy surfing and then catching a break in the room mid day. But I can see some people putting up a fuss over this so figured its worth a mention. If you want to sunbathe a lot, stay somewhere with a pool. 

The mornings and evenings are lovey but it does get pretty hot & sweaty in the afternoon. Do yourself a favor and make sure you get a room with A/C. Nothing like being able to chill out in a cool room after a busy morning out on the beach or riding around. 

The area is predominantly Muslim so there are a lot of limitations on alcohol availability. You cant get beer or hard alcohol at that many places - maybe 3 to 4 spots along the main strip. Only one bottle shop with actual hard liquor (down a road at the end of Arugam Bay where there is a holiday inn sign) and one with beer (Meenas) to buy your own. Id suggest packing a bottle if you wanna enjoy drinks in your room or whatever where youre staying. Def places to grab cocktails though so no sweat if you just want a rum and coke here and there. This is something I wish I knew in advance - def wouldve liked to have my own supply for my room and by the pool in the afternoon or evening! That being said, Arugam Bay is cheap and the cocktails will only cost you like $3-$5 at the bars that have them so you can drink to your hearts desire even on a budget. Hideaway Resorts Bar has great cocktails. Spice Trail bar has wine and bubbles (by the bottle) - both are next to each other. 

Last thing: we split our stay between two places .. Bay Vista, with a beach view and balcony .. and Spice Trail, which had a pool. This was such a good combo. We loved sitting on our balcony and enjoying the beach views for a few days. But it was equally enjoyable to go for a refreshing dip in the pool when we moved resorts. Both in the best location as well. All in all, we had an awesome trip with loads of surfing & lots of down time to chill and read. Its a very mellow and chilled out place so definitely go expecting that kinda vibe. Happy surfing ??

Also, photo attached for transport service we used. Very comfortable and efficient for journey to Arugam from Colombo. Sanju is a great guy!

Title: Good place for surf and chilling
Text:
At far away 2011 year there was not too many surfers and tourists. The place is a bit wild, but good :)
You can swim or surf or walk around or rent a scooter and fly all around.
Very calm and slow environment :)

Title: Beautiful surf spots!
Text: Arugam Bay has everything you need, food service and many surf spots to enjoy! I especially loved being on the beach and swimming almost 24/7 and renting a Bike and self touring surrounding Lagoons, beaches and city streets. So much to see and do!

Title: Sleep where you can hear the ocean..
Text:
Just spent two nights in Arugam bay and will be return for another two on our way back South, as we really liked it. Surf was good for intermediates like us and I personally found the locals in the surf friendly (just dont jump on their wave-common surf sense). Board hire from Raphs was great, staff give good break tips. There are real coffee shops!!! and lots of restaurants to pick from. Locals will ask if you need a tuktuk, to eat at their restaurant, come surfing with their tour or even just say hello. . Remember, things are pretty slow for these guys atm. We were just polite and said hello, no thank you,no thank you, and walked on. We never felt pushed into anything tho. 
Tips-there are some nice places to stay at, some with character too! Prices are somewhat negotiable atm, so you could rock up and walk around or if not, Id recommend somewhere on the beach, then you can use their deck chairs for free. We just brought a smoothie each day at the restaurant near the main break and used their chairs. That worked also. 
Surfing? Booties could be handy, as there is a few metres of coral on the walk out at the main break but we didnt have any and all good.

Title: Beware of sexual assaults by locals
Text:
My partner and I have visited Arugam Bay in Sri Lanka a few times as he is a surfer. We found the town very commercial, very catered for tourists - which is fine. There are some lovely restaurants with great local food dishes and some really nice (basic) rooms. Many facilities here are overpriced because of this being a tourist hotspot, but that is to be expected.

Tuk Tuk drivers can be very full on - and annoying - when they dont take no for an answer and they overcharge horrendously. Most places are in walking distance so dont give in to the pressure unless you need to go out of town. Its cheaper to hire a bike or moped for those journeys.

What is truly awful, however, is I was groped on the main part of the beach by some young local lads. They came over, looking like they want to shake hands and welcome us. One shook my hand and then grabbed my chest, before laughing and walking away. It was disgusting, I was shocked and distressed and didnt know what to do. They were old enough to know better and at the end of the day, they just freely sexually assaulted someone in broad daylight!

I was already feeling uncomfortable as the men tend to leer and watch tourist women very closely - and Im not meaning when theyre in bikinis or swimwear. Just generally. So this is a warning to girls and women - please take care, avoid being out alone and especially walking on the beach or when its dark. It really isnt a pleasant experience and is treated as a joke by the men doing this.

Title: LOVE LOVE LOVE
Text: Must visit in Sri Lanka. We would stay forever!!!!!! Beautiful town full of beautiful people. It has maintained it's charm despite tourism and surfing industry and the fishing community is still prevelant. Beautiful beaches, strong waves in peak season and full of restaurants, cafes and bars.

Title: Really Good Tip
Text: Very relaxed atmosphere, perfect place to relax and enjoy the waves. Great restaurants too. The people are all very friendly and happy to provide information. Nice and safe beach; I like this beach, it's safe for everyone. I recommended it.

Title: Expected more
Text:
Perhaps it's because it's just the start of the season and also the local new year holiday weekend, but a lot of the bars and restaurants were closed.

What disappointed us most was the lack of good dineing.  
Having recently been to Galle, Mirissa and Ella, we found the restaurant options and quality comparatively lacking in Arugam Bay. We tried Karma, Spice Trail, Bay Vista, Geckos  Surfers rest and  Pizza Hub.
All of them disappointed in some way and the Pizza place actually ended making us sick due to stale seafood.

Title: Only place in Sri Lanka where we have felt unsafe
Text: Arrived here off season and it was deserted. Found ourselves being stared at constantly and as a woman I felt very uncomfortable. We were used to local people staring but then smiling at us. This was not the case here. My husband walked to local shop on the main street at 10 am and was surrounded by old men demanding money. It was only when an older hotelier started shouting at them that they backed off.Please this is not a reflection of Sri Lanka which we have loved but only of this conservative Village.

Title: Beautiful & Calm
Text: Very beautiful place.So relaxed. Sun rising is something worth to watch. But I think there must be certain rules to prevent garbaging this wonderful place.

Title: Surf camp Emotionland
Text: ???? A good place to first stand on the surf, to feel the ocean. Arugam is a village where nice people live, tasty forge, low prices, gorgeous ocean. Chic hummus at The Spice Trail??

Title: End of the road in Sri lanka
Text:
Simple little village on the coast with walking access to surf for all abilities and a range of accomodation
Changing so quickly which is proof that this is a great place to spend a day or more likely a week.

Title: Perfect for Wind Surfers, Lot of Wind Surfing Lessons Going On
Text: Though the entry is of a fishing village and looks pretty dirty, when you walk along the shore and reach a point were surfers are enjoying their moment. My kids learned to windsurf and were enjoying the evening.

Title: Great walk away from the bay itself
Text: We visited during the low season. Nonetheless, we enjoyed some excellent beach walks along the right side of the bay.

Title: Off season dullness
Text:
Beautiful stretch of sand with restaurants, bars and resorts. 
There is a surfer feeling to this location however the waves arent that incredible to draw that crowd exclusively.

1/3 of all stores/accommodations are closed during off season period and the other 2/3 are understaffed and understocked. 
There is also no nightlife during October to May.

The dogs on the beaches are very annoying. They will growl and bark at any stranger that passes by. Occasionally on a daily basis they will attack each other viciously which can make you nervous when you are in the vicinity.

Title: Too crowded
Text:
The beach is long but quite narrow. There are many small hotels/shacks and restaurants along the beach, some restaurants are really good, such as Gecko. The wood-fire thin crust sea-food pizza was yummy. 
About surfing at Arugam Bay, there are also nicer places near to Arugam Bay. The beaches at Panama (a village) offers big bays with wide beaches and surfs and much less crowd. Usually locals go there and then there are not many. You may need a local guide to bring you there. You may contact on the local guides, Manju, tel: +94(71)249-0256, to bring you to Panama Beach.

Title: Worth it if you like surfing and yoga in a young and easy going atmosphere
Text: You get surfers from all over the world during the season from June to September. The main point is not for beginners as there is a reef so be careful if you're still learning you may have to go a bit further to the left where you can find a good spot for beginners with a Sandy Beach. Locals are friendly and it's a nice spot to chill for a few days

Title: Clean, but rough sea in areas
Text:
The beach is really clean, lovely golden sand there is plenty of room with out being overcrowded, we had a section literally too ourselves.
The sea is rough but not so you cant take a dip but the currents can be strong so you wouldnt go out too far.
I believe further south you go there is a bay that is sheltered and isnt as rough but we didnt try this area.

Title: Amazing place for surfing
Text: What a great place for surfing. My main advice would be that you should book a hotel/hostel: beginners - closer to Baby Point and advanced - Elephant Rock. Waves at the Baby Point place are much smaller and affordable for beginners. The surfing gear and boards I rented at Hasan Surf House - prices: 400 rupee/day for a board, 1,500 rupee/1.5h surfing lesson included half day board after the lesson. The best and cheapest food was at Ranga's Beach Hut and the best fish at Hakeem's Beach Spot - 1000 rupee/person.

Title: Relaxing paradise
Text: Great to sit back, relax and chill. Family, teenagers, older persons can find all they need in this part of a beautiful island

Title: Nice beach, laid back with good surf
Text:
We spent a week here and liked the beach.  The kids surfed here despite being beginners and some of the waves being quite large.  

You can stand until quite far out (off and on) and the water is warm so you can stay in a long time.  Despite the wave power I didnt feel that you got sucked out to sea although you may drift further down.  

I felt the kids were fairly safe here which is great.  

In the evening there are a number of restaurants where you can eat fish on the beach.  Relaxing and relatively clean.

Watch out for the friendly dogs and puppies, very cute but the little rascals can start chewing your headphones ??

Title: Relaxing
Text: Depending on your interests consider the length of stay.  We didn't surf but relaxed very well on tbe beach for 6 days. Possibly a little to long.  Place will develop fast I'd suggest, nice to see it now. Felt like Bali in the 70s. Lots of young backpackers discovering themselves and the place really catered to them very well. A feeling of discovery.

Title: Huge waves
Text: beautiful beach, huge waves and fun. Loved it there, will defiantly be back again. Loved our hotel and loved the beach bars along the  bay.

Title: Nice little town for Surfers
Text: If you surf,, go to Arugam Bay.You will find may great surf.spots around the town. Easy to access by TukTuk.

Title: Great surfing place
Text: Is the best spot on the east coast to surf, if youre willing to take a bath you can try but the waves are too strong to let you easily go in the sea, there are a lot of cheap bars where you can drink and eat after you had a surfing day

Title: Lost Paradise
Text: Wish I had of gone 40 years ago. Over cooked now and developing not in a good way. If your going for waves definitely avoid the high season. Ridiculous amount of surfers from places that dont even have surf. Its a shame because geographical it would have been a beautiful place in its day. Eat in local restaurants as it is far cheaper than the usual tourist traps. The people are nice but all trying to make a years wage in a few months. Not sure why some people like it like this. Elephant eating in a rubbish dump finished it for me.

Title: Sri Lanka's version of Goa
Text: Lovely beaches, great surf, chilled out vibe.  in the summer A-Bay is home to hundreds of European 20-somethings having a great time.  It's all about the beach here and A-Bay itself is a short strip of resorts and restaurants catering for the western palate.  if you're looking for culture, try elsewhere - it is a little heartbreaking to see that the local community have had to put up signs asking holidaymakers to respect the culture and values and not wear bikinis on the high-street....

Title: Okay beach - locals can't be trusted
Text:
It's a nice place once you get away from the main strip. The locals unfortunately have not yet adapted to the fact that tourism can be fickle if a place gets a bad reputation. 

We had several negative experiences here, mainly to do with being ripped off, having our taxi driver attacked (because he wasn't a local) and having the local men harass the girls we were with. The guys working in our hotel were offering us drugs before we even got to our room. All in all, I would say avoid the place. 

The surf isn't great and the beach has oil slick stains. Much better beaches with much kinder locals just 100km or so away.

Title: Place you should not missed
Text: Great atmosphere in surf place where everything is dedicated mostly to surf ?? People are great and supporting you must try to have at least one lesson of surf ??

Title: What Bali was in the 1980's
Text: Great location with good selection of surf spots.  The beach is great and clean but in July was very hot,  Try and stay at a place with a pool if you have young kids.  There were so many great places to eat,  avoid beach restaurants as food was not great.  Only issue I would have is you need to tuk tuk to lots of the other surf spots and in July there were many people surfing who really should remain on dry land.  Very safe, lots of shopping a bit touristy but a fun location.

Title: Overrated
Text:
Arugam Bay is an amazingly overrated surf spot. Surfwise expect a slightly above average wave with 100-300 drunk idiots in the lineup on main point with 0 etiquette from dusk till dawn. All the other spots within 30 minutes are mobbed as well. Some like Peanut Farm and Whiskey Point even have lessons block everyone from surfing in whose not taking a lesson.

The worst problem is greed from the local populace. I switched rooms to the Spice Trail and paid only to have them up bill me another $40 a night over what we originally agreed due (and paid) to a "misunderstanding". We we're offered free wine and charged for it. I was offered a 10% discount and only given a $10 discount on an almost $200 room, and was originally told one check out time and told another the day I had to leave.

The Banana surf shop in Arugam Bay gave us a broken board where the repair job came off in the water and then tried to charge me for the cost of a new board. We eventually negotiated our payment down to $110 but it was still very aggravating and was made worse by the fact that the owner actually was threatening my wife.

This low level of business ethics is to be expected in Arugam Bay. Much of these businesses only operate from April-October and the locals all come out en masse to try to ring every penny they can out of the tourists. While some of this is to be expected it becomes harassment when you're walking down the street with multiple Tuk Tuk drivers following you and yelling constantly.

Of course the sidewalk collapsed as well and my ankle was severely hurt (maybe broken). 

On a plus side the food here is great. Lots of variety. Main beach is pretty if somewhat unsurfable. And there's cool spots to surf/visit if you go at least 45 minutes outside Arugam Bay. The wildlife safaris though a bit ghetto will allow you see great wildlife. 

If you come over here I'd recommend staying in Panama or some place at least 30 minutes outside of Arugam Bay then maybe visiting at night for a meal by Tuk Tuk. It will save you a lot of hassles.

Title: Veru nice looking beach
Text: We stop for one nigt during our Sri Lanka trip. Beach and restaurants near beach need more than one night for better understanding. Perhaps next time?

Title: Brilliant stretch of beach
Text: As I'm not a beach person, it's hard to appreciate these kind of places but this was a nice place with an incredibly long stretch of sand. Waves were a bit scary but that's the power of nature for you! Lots of accommodation and food options so if you're looking for a beach resort for a holiday this is a good alternative to the usual.

Title: Favourite all round beach in Sri Lanka
Text:
Were non surfers, but loved Arugam Bay. We went in June, which is ABays on season and it was buzzing, which is refreshing if youve been travelling the hill country, or the south and not really seen anyone. 

The weather was fantastic - really, very hot and the seas were rough, but fun to bob around in for a while to cool off or watch the surfers (or indeed surf) in the mornings and afternoons.

The beach is littered with nice little bars and restaurants. There are loads of places to eat, drink and stay in Arugam Bay. Try Rangas beach hut at the far end to stay, Matahari Secret Garden for a romantic drink, and Bambinos for a quick but super tasty bite to eat. 

Everyones really friendly and its a cheap place to live. A must if youre visiting Sri Lanka, especially if youre going in the European summer!

Title: Best place to relax and party sri lanka
Text:
I read the negative reviews first prior to visiting Arugam Bay and felt I shouls address these points first. 

If you rent a board do it via your hotel....I would recommend the Spice Trail. This way you avoid any shady damage coning! 

If you are going to be in the sea you may cut yourself. If this happens near corral or rocks they contain a fungi that wants to grow in your skin. Take antiseptic with you amd be prepared to propeely clean out the wond it will hurt but it wont get infected. Or alternatively use a lime like in Barley!

This for us after visiting 10 locations in Sri Lanka was the safest place to go out at night allowing visitors to sample the amazing street food and get a taste of real Sri Lankan cusiene! 

The surf is good!

Yes the beer is slightly more expensive anf the tuk tuks are more costly!

They are indeed on the weed sale, so if this floats your boat treat yourself if not they are not in your face which is great!

Visit here if you go to sri lanka!

Title: A smile is all you need
Text:
Arugam Bay is very relaxed and a little paradies on this earth. But please for everybody that will come: show respect to the culture and be polite to the friendly people that gives you holiday. It depends on the saison but when I was there I was a little bit shocked because of the tourist that were also unpolite to me and - dont know - lost their smile on the way.. 
I want to stay 3 nights but at the end it was 10 nights at Etnicos Surf Resort :-)

Title: Surf City!
Text: Great surfing town, even for learners, like me.  Beautiful beaches, nice centre strip, full of restaurants and a few great bars (limited due to local laws). Very  hospitable locals and friendly travellers.

Title: An over-hyped destination
Text: Few spots for surfers which quickly get overcrowded. Beach is dirty n not ideal for swimming. Hotels r dirty, lack basic facilities n hygiene n r way over-priced.

Title: Arugambay vist
Text:
We had a great time in Arugambay. Getting there is a bit of long drive but fully worth it. It's completely off the beaten track n a real surfing spot. Accommodation is much much cheaper than other beach spots in the island. 

Definitely worth going n one of the few uncrowded n uncrowned surfing places in the world.

Title: Only for surfers
Text: This beach is beautiful and the city is well developed (and consequently overpriced relative to the rest of Sri Lanka). But what makes this place a world class surfing spot also makes it a mediocre place to simply swim for us less cool non surfers.

Title: Get better hotels!
Text: All the hotels are soooooo average. Do some googling and what is offered for the same money in other places. Number one thing... get proper beds! Do not just push two single beds together. That happened in all 3 hotels we stayed in.

Title: My First sunrise at the beach
Text: this is a great spot to visit, specially if you are a surfer. great weaves, could be crowed in high season. In low season was good! a local and friendly place.

Title: Just Joy...
Text: Yeah, there's a lot of people there, but it all works out and you quickly get caught up in the relaxed atmosphere of the lifestyle there (for tourists). Wake up, surf, eat, surf, chill, beers, maybe surf, have fun, sleep, repeat!

Title: a beautiful remote part in the world
Text: Arugam Bay is a very quite and beautiful location , if you want to get away from the city life, it has some good surfing places, National safari park, nature reserves, lakes, rivers and lagoon, people are super friendly, foods and tasty and plenty with prices vary, sandy beaches, innocent faces and the thick jungles around with full of nature, a place to spend some time to be perfect.

Title: Chilly place, good waves
Text: Arugambay is a very chilly place. Surf at main point or relax at the nice beach on the northern end. But don't miss it. And if you want to see some of the other beaches around Arugambay call Jaya (+940773221466). He's a good guy and showed us every wave and surfspot around Arugambay.

Title: Overrated patch of beach
Text: If you're not a surfer, there's just money to be spent here on average offers. The place has potential, but the services barely meet average standards elsewhere in Sri Lanka. You can visit Yala wildlife park which is 45 mins away but as with any wildlife sightings, it depends on your good luck of catching interesting species. It's also hard to get to here - costly taxis or 7 hours of bouncing bus from the hill country. And another thing; given that there's loads of tourists, the place doesn't feel like Sri Lanka at all.

Title: What a beach!
Text: Such a lovely beach, we spent four days here in August and it was absolutely fantastic. Very clean beach, countless bars and restaurants, touristy and surfy but unspoilt

Title: Awesome bech
Text: We are going just visiting puttuvil in 1st day same day we wend part of puttuvil bech. So good but no one there.2nd day we wend arugam bay bech wow amazing place .we are really enjoyed.thank you

Title: Read below for a great cheap experience!!!
Text: If you are in Arugam Bay, make sure you rent a scooter around 4 in the afternoon for 1000 lkr or so. Drive through arugam bay and to the town panama. As soon as you reach it turn the first street right. Then head on the B355 into yala national park. We saw alot of water buffalos crossing the road, a deer, some lizards and 5 elephants very close on the motorbike!!! Way beter experience then any other safari tour in a national park. Very few tourist, make sure you do it in the afternoon!!

Title: Good times in the east coast
Text: Overall good experience. Being offered drugs doesn't really bother me but it might to some people. Good beach and good surf. The alcohol laws in Sri Lanka are weird so nightlife isn't very great.

Title: A super place to relax and learn to surf
Text: Arugambay bay is on the way to become a big tourist destination. The nay is great if u want to learn how to surf.one of the 10 best sirf G destinations in the world. The are instructors to teach u how. And at a really price.

Title: Relaxing time with good surf.
Text:
We had a great time here. Waves can get crowded but thats life.
Plenty of good food and things to do here. When busy it can be mayhem but its easy to avoid that if you find the right place to stay. Overall a vibrant place.

Title: Cool spot
Text: Very touristy area but we enjoyed our 4 night stay. Lots of food options including cheap local eats, long clean beach thats safe for swimming, nearby peanut farm is great for beginner surfers and theres lots of yoga around if thats your cup of tea. Its a decent sized town and theres a lot more happening than the likes of dikwella and talalla.

Title: Friendly Area
Text: I have visited nearly 40 countries and this has got to be the friendliest area Ive been to. The locals are always smiling and waving. Good place to learn surfing. Nice safaris not too far away.

Title: Love arugam bay
Text: Away from the crowds on the east side with hidden gems find the gecko restrooms for a truly local experience

Title: Beautiful bay
Text: Great bay some lovely restaurants and brilliant surfing.. we will be returning. Recommend little Lagoon if staying in area.

Title: Off season in Arugam bay
Text:
Just back from Sri Lanka, where I spent 2 nights in Arugam bay. Even though I knew it was not the peak season in the east of the country,I never expected it to be so quiet. I think it was a combination of being off season and Covid, that had the place looking like a ghost town.  There were very few restaurants and bars open while we were there and the streets were deserted after 8pm. It didnt help that there were power cuts also happening and lots of places had no electricity, which made it eerie walking home in the darkness.
In saying all that, we stayed in the Spice trail which was a great choice and the people were very friendly. They also arranged a safari trip to Kumana park, which is only a 45 min journey away and we saw lots of animals, with very little other people around. The beach is a real working beach with lots of fishing boats along the shore constantly going in and out with their catches. So dont expect a beach with lovely stretches of sand with plenty of sun loungers. Its not that type of beach.
I would certainly like to visit again when its peak season, to really see this place at its best and then make a better judgement.

Title: Enjoy the sunrise.
Text:
Take a stroll in the near by beach.
Experience the returning fishing boats with their catch & the once setting out.
The sunrise a breathtaking sight.

Title: Heard too tourist we but still loved it!
Text: A fun little town! If you dont surf three days would probably be plenty. We heard a lot about harassment from local boys but we never saw it! So glad we ended up going!

Title: The best bay and a must visit point
Text: Arugambay is a sunny and turkiz area at Sri Lanka. It takes about 7 hours driving from the international airport. Most places and restaurants are on the beach serving fresh juices and local food. Surfboard lessons are offered and it all feels like a one big beautiful tropical town.

Title: An amazing destination
Text:
We spent 4 days at Arugam Bay whilst attempting to escape terrential rain in another region.
The weather was superb, locals friendly & helpful. 
We arrived in time to watch a few days of the WSL tour & were lucky to see a few of the Sri Lankan wild cards in the early rounds.
All meals were fabulous, great Roti & Kottu from the Blue Caravan in the main street, ventured to Peanut Farm where a few of our group enjoyed a surf.
Overall a great time & would be happy to return on our next visit to Sr Lanka

Title: Surfers beach
Text: Nice place with mit too many tourists. In the evening the hotels can be loud because of the music from different parties going on

Title: I fell in love with this place
Text: I have been to so many place over the years. But Arugambay is something very special. First I thought this is just a surfing city and a beach. But you'll be amazed seeing how nature rich this place really is.

Title: best place to visit
Text: Lovely place in srilanka. Love to come back again. Nice beach and people. One of the best beach i have visited.

Title: Beautiful spot (for surfing)
Text:
Arugam Bay still feels like a small surfers hang out which is great. Nice play to hang out with fun little restaurants, bars and beach hotels. The beaches - although mostly not for swimming - are beautiful, especially around the main surf point. 

Besides surfing there is not much to do around here, so I wouldn't spend too much time here if not surfing.

Title: LADIES! TAMPONS!
Text:
Ladies, I have found a place which stocks tampons! As I've been travelling for a few months it's become apparent that tampons are very rare. So to help the women out that are in desperate need, arugam bay in the centre has a supermarket, called food (something) can't recall but they stock tampons. Of course for an extortionate price (980 Rupee) but, if in need this will be your life saver haha. Hope fully this helps! 
...It's in the centre across from a hostel, next to an Aussie swimwear store. They are near the counter. 
Cheers

Title: Overpriced, but nice
Text: It's a nice beach town but overpriced compared to everywhere else we traveled in Sri Lanka, stuff cost almost double.

Title: Awesome
Text:

Text: nice beach ,and the surf is unbeleaveable, very primative,if u want a beer there is a bottle shop out of town,bout 200 rupees,or there is the beer bar,well worth visiting in the main street,once u have been there a few times the beers are cheaper and they are not so rude,nice booly wood movies, try upstairs and watch the world go buy,mheading out of town towards the bridge is a little eatery calledhung or high time,very ordianary to look at, but by far the best sri lankan meals ive had.cheap and ,clean,must be good as the locals swarm there,and the rotti guy is making them while u are there,can no t reckon mend this place higher. strong coffee made with condendensed milk gets the morning off with a good start

Title: Beginner advise for surfers and swimmers
Text: Baby point is beach location ur looking for where waves are small and shalow water . Just get a big board and learn to paddle or stand on the board in this place(also water is warm throughout )  will have fun even if u dont know anything about surfing . All group or family can have fun at this spot. Cheers.

Title: Still unspoiled by many tourist
Text: This place is nine hours drive from the AirPort so not many standard tourist reach this place. Is is many surfers here because the waves comming to the long beaches are wellknown. It is still a fishing place with a lot of fishermen comming in with fish, lobsters and prawns that you can eat in the restaurangs the same evening to increadibly low prices. We really loved this place and the friendly people living here

Title: Love this town and beach
Text: We had 4 great days here, just laying on the beach, going to the lagoon, watched the fishermen, surfed and just had a great time!

Title: Beautiful beach, great surf break but too crowded
Text: The beach is wonderful, and the sunset here is incredible overloking the palm trees. There is a decent nightlife in the summer season. Good wave for surfing but way too crowded and  have been in multiple collisions here for people not looking where they're going.

Title: Laid back , great beach
Text: Stayed here in April for 3 nights on our honeymoon. Really enjoyed our time here. The beach was fantastic and because it's off season there were hardly any others around. Not all shops and restaurants are open but plenty to choose from and the seafood is great.  There is only one place to buy byo alcohol, it's at the rear of a restaurant opposite siams restaurant . Surf lessons a must. Some parts of the beach at the fishermen end a little dirty but during peak season it all gets cleaned up. I liked it more than tangalle

Title: Amazing Beach!
Text:
What a chilled place!  Beautiful crashing waves, great opportunities to learn to surf, plenty of places to eat and shops to peruse. 
Would highly recommend!

Title: Best place
Text:
If you like surf, you will love this place.
We had take 2 nights but finally we had spent 5.
Quiet and peaceful

Title: The best place in Srilanka
Text: We have visited Sri Lanka for our honey moon and honestly arugambay is the best place you can surf, enjoy food and music in a chill atmosphere. All the people are really nice. Go there and enjoy !!!

Title: beautiful quiet clean beach
Text: It's peaceful without a lot of people bothering you by selling things.  Waves can be a little strong but general good for a dip to cool off.  lots of places to eat up and down the beach.

Title: Over rated and disappointing
Text:
The bay itself is pretty with small boats lining the edge. Nice looking at the surfers and relaxing in the sun. There is a good selection of Resturant's to choose from along the mainstreet too.

Apart from this,arugam bay was not for me. It has a real  'club 18-30' feel about it and i feel i may have been too old to enjoy the hostels and party atmosphere which happened once the sun went down. Definitely not family orientated. We had originally intended to stay two nights but left after one. Im sure other people would love here,however i dont think i will be rushing back!

Title: Great Location to surf, chill and for safaris
Text:
This area is one of the best in Sri Lanka - Surfing, chilling on the Beach, Drinking and eating at of the nice Restaurants at the beach or going on tuktuk or jeep Safari is great there!

We can highly recommend Aloha Cabanas for your Stay there - directly on the Beach with a surfschool as well and nice beach houses!

Title: Perfect spot! Realy Nice beach and relax people :-) go to arugambay!
Text: Really nice beach and relax people :-) Great hotels/hostels. Go to Arugam bay! You never want to go away!

Title: Nice surftown!
Text: Nice surftown in the south east of Sri lanka. Nice laidback atmosphere, locals are very friendly. Surfspots do get crowded fast, and its defenitely not the true sri lankan experience (as it feels like any small surftown around the world). But still nice to go to after seeing the sights in the country and relax.

Title: Paradise
Text: What a lovely place! Heaps of Restaurant/bar and accomodations right on the beach,never too busy..Such a great holidays feel.Surf can get good but very crowded at main point. Tuktuk everywhere.Peoples here are really nice and helpful. Love this place

Title: Great Location
Text: Spent 9 days here as two couples and none of us wanted to leave. Lots to do, surf schools, safari, tuk tuk hire, general beach life and the food was incredible. Great place to chill out,  or be active. Do yoga and/or drink beer. It has it all, even some good shopping and cooking classes.

Title: Three days at Arugambay
Text: One of the best seas for surfing during the season. Also some good restaurants when you walk along the beach road in the evenings. Best is to check in at any hotel on BB basis and then go out for the meals.

Title: Most fun place in Sri Lanka
Text:
Well worth the long journey getting there. Stunning secluded beach if you go the the main bay and continue walking  right (south). Waves are v strong though even in off season. A bit more expensive than other Sri Lankan towns but better atmosphere. 

For getting back to Colombo there are three handy overnight buses that leave Potuvil in the evening and take approx 7hours. Costs only r430 for reserved ticket - well worth it.

Title: Okay Beach
Text:
Really i have seen many beaches in Sri Lanka and....
There are far more better beaches here to find. Only if you are looking for travellers you will find here plenty of them. 
But the beach unfortunately is not clean.

Title: Lovely beach and beach town and you don't even need to be a surfer.
Text: Really enjoyed our visit to Arugam Bay. Low-key easy going place. During low season (january) it was really relaxing. Still lots to do even if you don't surf.  Lagoon boat tour, strolls on the beach, Kumana safari, cooking classes, homestay visits in villages. Go out with a fisherman, you name it.

Title: Nice!!
Text: A little surfers village with good (reggea) bars and quite some tourists, in comparison with other places in Sri Lanka. We stayed in a little house near the 24 hours reggae bar. Always something to do!:-)

Title: Just go elsewhere if you are not a surfer
Text:
Suitable for surfer during season. 

There are many other places you could go instead. Hard to reach and very overpriced for what you get. Dudes offering drugs on the streets, alcohol problems, and men trying to ripe you off.

Really, there are many other experiences you can have, don't bother unless you meet the criteria above.

Local authorities should pay more attention.

Title: Breath in Breath out
Text:
You and the sea, that's why you come here in off season. You can do this if you are not a surfing enthusiast as this is world famous place for that.
We are not even swimmers. So for us soaking the waves on our feet is fun. Off season gives the sea to you. Only other people are fishermen. 
Its a great place for jogging on the sand in early morning. It may take an hour to explore the whole beach front if just keep walking....you can reach the next town almost.
Whole day can be spent watching and building theories about waves and their behavior.
About food there are few places even in off season. From very expensive to very cheap if you are ok walking into a roadside eatery. 
Getting in and out of town is tricky. You can take taxi, or local buses. The connection are available from nearby towns that you can even take a tuktuk to.

Title: Really special place out of season
Text: I would recommend this place out of season if you want to get away from it all. A really great alternative to the south coast. And you get it all to yourself - well almost.

Title: Nice surfing beaches
Text:
Arugam bay beaches are very famous for surf.
We visited nearly off season of surf even seen many did surfing.
Beach waves are little fast and more turbulent but many had bath and swim.
Lot of beach side rest and restaurants available.

Title: The nicest beach I've visited in SL...
Text: it was a family trip... went there in a August and the sea was quiet noisy... there was lot of tourists and locals when we get there... you can hire a surf board or else you can ride your own...there was some jet skies also... great place to enjoy...and a good place for a sun bath.... we stayed the like 6-7 hours...

Title: Great for camp fire and enjoying some beers
Text: Really nice and empty beach. At least in November there were mostly locals and some tourists. Beach is clean, swimming is great, some smaller waves, surfing is possible on the edges of the lagoon (15min walk from the middle)

Title: Maybe a great beach during on season but not during off season
Text: We visited Arugam Bay during the second half of November which is the off season. We didn't know what to expect because we don't surf and just wanted a few nice days on the beach. The weather was ok (some rain but expected) but what we really didn't like was that there was so much litter at the beach, we wonder if that's also the case during on season. Also the beach doesn't offer any bars and restaurants which are all located on the street. Another problem was that many restaurants and bars are closed during off season. I maybe suspect that Arugam Bay is a nice beach during on season but during off season there are other beaches better suitable to relax (for example Hikkaduwa and Merissa).

Title: very relaxed place / Best Wave
Text: An outstanding wave, world quality. Locals tend to drop in on any wave they like. Still it's an epic journey, worth getting there before it becomes too commercial.

Title: Overpriced and Overdone
Text: More expensive than a lot of other places in Asia.Local beer in bottles or cans and not much else available. Large can of tiger $6 + if you can find it. Food was great in a few places expect to pay $8 for a good meal. Enjoyed our stay though, just didn't budget enough. Try to avoid the tuk tuk mafia but it's almost impossible if you want to go somewhere. Locals are friendly but need to remember we are not all walking ATM machines spitting out cash

Title: Surf is epic, place is too busy...
Text:
The wave at main point on its day is truly world class and so easy to surf! If you can get one ...the wave is incredibly busy due to its ease of paddling out and take off. Meaning you will be dodging first day beginners trying to take off on overhead sets, can get pretty dangerous we saw lots of injuries and terrible tropical infections from the dirty water, had to have a few days out of the water on antibiotics myself for a small scratch that turned into a bad infection a week later. So definitely clean your cuts out everyday until fully healed! 

The town itself was pretty busy and akin to other westernised Asian countries, bars blaring out loud music till all hours of the morning on the weekends. We had a car so stayed a few miles out of town for most of the trip in Papermoon which was very nice and also staying on the point at Upalis was an awesome experience! Also there are some great restaurants in Arugam Hideaway and thaththas roti shop were by far the highlights! 

The local wildlife is incredible drive a km out of town at sunrise and sunset and you will see dozens of elephants crocodiles and amazing bird life! Lagoon Safari is a must!

Overall we had a great time as the waves were consistently amazing every morning! But Arugam itself left a lot to be desired and is definitely one for the backpackers and party goers.

Title: Not as chilled or as cheap as expected
Text:
I had mixed feelings about Arugam Bay: it was peak season and the place was busy and hot. A nice long beach, surfing and surf lessons, but swimming was also possible as long as you're OK getting through the waves.

However a lot of the eating places seemed to be over-stretched, with slow service, poor food, and high prices for what you get. The atmosphere in general was more "international backpacker" rather than particularly Sri Lankan.

It seems that the resort has expanded quickly over the last few years, and I think its suffering from growing pains. Hopefully things will settle down a bit and visitors will start to get better service at reasonable prices.

Title: not the best beach in Sri Lanka but good for surf and lots of elephants on the road 5 minutes away
Text: Arugam bay is good for the surf (but don't expect big waves) but the beach is not the best we saw in 3 weeks in Sri Lanka. The first days we went to the south end of the bay(where the fisshing boats are) because there's like a natural pool and it's very safe for the children. ANd the water is very hot!!! but after a  few days it became very dirty with lots of beer bottles and papers...so we went to Elephant Rock (15 minutes away in tuktuk) where the beach is lovely in a beautiful setting. And on our way home (around 6PM) you can see elephants living their lives  in the fields!! amazing experience!!! shopping was also nice in Arugam Bay. 30 minutes from Arugam bay, you can see lots of Elephants and crocodiles in a place called Panama. Finaly discover the Pottuvil Lagoon on a "double canoe/boat. It's simply beautiful and so peaceful

Title: Arugam Bay - like Bali of old!
Text: Arugum Bay is a relaxing little village full of young travellers from Europe keen to enjoy the beach and learning to surf.  If you are a surfer especially from Australia then you should hire a bike and look for surf breaks further along the coast as it is so crowded with people of low ability.  The restaurants have cheap local and Indian food and more expensive western dishes.  The bars are fun as well.  Great place to chill and work on your tan!

Title: Surf Paradise
Text:
I spent two weeks in this beautiful place. There are many different attractions, but the biggest attraction is definitely the beach. Surfing is the holy grail in Arugam bay. There are many surf teachers and you can easily rent a surfboard for two weeks. The prices for renting a surfboard are very cheap. I learned to surf in a few days, especially the people on the beach help you and give you many tips. 
The small city is lovely and has also attractions for non surfers, like snorkelling and markets. I have seen many places in beautiful Sri Lanka and Arugam bay was one of the cleanest. The people are very nice and like to help and just to talk. We went by bus to Arugam bay, it's a twelve-hour journey which is not in the best state. But it was a very nice and interesting drive. I recommend it for families, friends and couples.

Title: good time
Text: beautiful beaches, loads of surfing, Mambos on saturdays night is really good. A lot more touristy than the other places we went in Sri Lanka i really enjoyed it. As a girl you can wear shorts etc. Dont go to Sri Lanka and not go, we nearly made that mistake!

Title: Surfers only
Text: This was the worst place we visited in Sri Lanka, unless you are a surfer don't bother, the beach was covered in oil. The few hotels there are were overpriced and poor quality

Title: Best place for fun in Sri Lanka
Text: The place is real fun in Sri Lanka. There's so much to do here, you can party at night, enjoy really nice food. It is the best place to surf in the country. You can also get trainers here for surf. There are some nice pubs near YMCA, which would make your night.

Title: Kudakalliya, a very peaceful and unspoiled place to stay just outside Arugambay,
Text:
We stayed in Kudakalliya for three nights - bedroom doors opening straight onto the lagoon; monkeys feeding in the trees just outside; brahminy kites etc etc
Do not come here if you want or expect all creature comforts but if you want total peace and quiet, wonderful (and seriously good value) food, and such a friendly welcome then this is for you.
Shower under the stars, sunbathe and stargaze on the huge first floor balcony.
Lovely beach walks and only a short tuc tuc ride into town.

Title: WORLD BEST SURFING BREAK
Text:
Arugam Bay is a bay situated on the Indian Ocean in the dry zone of Sri Lanka's southeast coast. The bay is located 320 kilo meters due east of Colombo, and approximately 4 kilo meters south of the market town of Pottuvil.

The Arugam Bay area is home to a number of quality surf breaks, the most popular of which being 'Main Point' located towards the south of the bay. This is a right hand point break, with a rock/reef bottom, and has a number of sections with occasional barrels. Other breaks in the area include Whiskey Point and Pottuvil Point to the north, and Elephant Rock, Peanut Farm and Okanda to the south. These breaks have attracted a steady stream of international tourists for several decades. Arugam Bay has a good local surf scene and is home to some of Sri Lanka's most talented surfers. In recent years surfers from Arugam Bay have dominated national competitions.

Text: Arugam bay is really at the end of the small Shri Lankas world. East side )) Before getting here from Colombo you can visit the mountains aria ( middle of the island ). You can get there by train , which takes you through the beautiful view all there way! And in Arugam bay about 10 deferent surfing point around Arugam bay with a possibility to find what you want. Title: Surfers paradise?
Text:
I've been there in September 2012. It's totally different Sri Lankan experience, comparing to the West of the country. 

Not massive tourist destination back then and local workers were not so used of tourists - e.g. sometimes they brought cutlery after the food was on the table in the restaurants.

Title: Surfboards in Arugambay: Do not go to Dr. Dings
Text: We rented two surfboards for three days and I realised at the second day that the leash is broken. I don't know if it was broken when i rented it or how it happened. I didn't have an accident, I just used the surfboard. And I Wwas happy to notice it at the beach and not in the water. They changed the leash but when we gave the surfboards back they wanted us to pay 5000 rupies for the broken leash otherwise they wouldn't give us our passports. At the end we payed 3000 rupies - almost double the price for the rental of two boards per Day. It seemed to be a kind of basic business strategy.

Title: Still wonderfully rustic, relax and enjoy!
Text: Arugum Bay, on the South East coast of Sri Lanka is an oasis of tranquility...sparkling sea and warm sands..great value dining, and a world renown surf break!  Great Surfing is still the greatest pull to Arugum Bay and I highly  recommend Hassan's Surf House, on the main road, first shop on the left after the bridge.Hasan really know the surf, and his boards, and gives clear and fun lessons. Rental boards are in great condition and well maintained, and the shop also has a great range of Hasan Surf House branded t-shirts, boardies, rashies, etc. as well as new and second hand surf boards. Whether it's your first time on a board, or you find yourself in ABay and in need of a new board, I couldn't recommend Hasan Surf House more highly!

Title: Very unspoilt place (so far)
Text: Arugambe is still one of those places where mass tourism hasn't spoilt the charm.  Big hotels are on the way however but it still a good place to chill in the waves and watch the fishermen in the estuary.  I gotta say that the mangrove trip is a bit of a rip off. Far better to take an autorickshaw 10k north of Pottuvil where you can ask the local boatman to punt you round the mangrove.  beware, the sun is fierce.

Title: Moonrise kingdom
Text:
Pros: Beautiful place! The moon rises over the ocean are amazing. Lagoon safari tour was full of interesting wildlife.  Beach Hut is a great place to stay for economy travels. 
Cons: being a lone female traveller in off season made me a little conspicuous and I couldn't really get away from tuk tuk drivers out to make a living trying to sell me tours.

Title: crowds, israelies, and learn to surfers (ABay is Over)
Text:
ABay is totally over. The point cannot handle its own popularity. Crowds,israelies(they cant surf for ..................) and learn to surfers. Nice place Arugam will always have a special place in my heart from over the years not a world class wave by any stretch of the imagination but it use to be fun. NO MORE! crazily overcrowded surf and expensive accommodation.
Peppo

Title: Lovely beach for swimming and surfing
Text: I really enjoyed Arugam Bay compared to the rest of Sri Lanka, mainly for its layed back vibe and good choice of restaurants (although expensive!) I liked the beach it was beautiful for swimming and learning to surf. I found food and accommodation to be quite expensive and not great quality, but I didn't let it spoil my time there. If your a party goer there's plenty of party's at the beach bars and if your a couple it's lovely relaxing at this gorgeous beach. I wouldn't feel comfortable travelling here as a woman alone but with my partner I was fine. There's plenty of places to stay in Arugam Bay I don't think it's necessary to book online before you go, you'll find something better if you go and check it out for yourself. Good WiFi is hard to come across in the area I found the restaurants with the best WiFi were Geckos and Break Away cafe. Mambos (southern end of the beach) is over priced, look around and you'll find better places to eat! The sun beds at Mambos and Geckos are free though which is a bonus! Swimming all along the beach is great and the best place to surf is around the point. Tigri is the best place for cheap curries and western food. There's an ATM at Arugam Bay too so don't fret about needing to bring cash. Transport to the airport is expensive and can range between $120-180AUS. All in all I enjoyed my stay at Arugam Bay and would recommend it to beach lovers!

Title: Honest, Reliable, the best!
Text: I have visited Arugam Bay on numerous occasions and surprisingly, the visits were not to do the "surfing" thing. Instead, the visits were to meet Johnson. Johnson is one of the world's real gentlemen. To me he symbolises all that is good about honesty and integrity. Johnson is the manager of the very relaxed "Aloha Cabanas". Reasonably priced, "Aloha Cabanas" is a veritable home-away-from-home. The food is "simply good", and the "Aloha Special" is an experience that should be enjoyed by all. Johnson's surfing ability is renowned, while his surfing skills and teaching ability are appreciated by former students all over the world. To me, Johnson is the real Arugam Bay!
