Text: I've been recommended by a friend to ave Johnson organise my surfing trip here in Arugam Bay and give me lessons. He is just a magical person, that new how to pass on his passion for surfing to me. I had an awesome time learning with him. He new how to challenge me, teach me and help me to understand the waves.

Title: We love Arugam Bay
Text: This was my third time in A Bay and my husband's fourth stay.  We go for the surfing and laid back lifestyle, we always enjoy ourselves and stay at the Danish Villa.  There are some things that continue to disturb me about this sleepy surfing town.  One main thing is that single girls are not safe here by themselves despite a military and heavy police presence which seems to dominate more each year we come.  The tuk tuk drivers are lame and will offer you drugs despite most of them being part of the muslim faith and they dominate the taxi services and stop other cheap options and information about those options.  We again were scammed by taxi drivers coming from the airport to Colombo and endured a terrifying overland trip to A bay with very bad driving and no seats belts.  When leaving we had a trusted local man buy us bus tickets and get us a tuk tuk for 3 people for $11 to Akkaraipattu bus stand, nearly an hour north of A bay on a quiet and enjoyable road and caught a first class air conditioned overnight coach with room for surfboards to Colombo, it gets in about 5 am and there is little traffic in Colombo then, which is good as it is a hectic place - you wont see any advertising about this bus service.  When we were in Sri Lanka we hired a scooter from a guy up near Why Not restaurant and for $10 a day and then it got heaps cheaper each day we had it and it was fun scootering around and checking out locals towns and sights nearby, be careful about riding later in the afternoon though as the wild elephants are around.  Sri Lanka is a beautiful country to explore, hope you go and enjoy!!

Title: Only if you like surfing.......
Text: I dont want to sound like an old fuddy duddy. This is a small town on the coast DOMINATED by surfing. I enjoy soaking up local culture and especially the food and enjoy trying new places to eat everynight. Sadly with one or two exceptions I was deeply disappointed by this town. It is geared toward surfing and all that entails. It has very young customer base who are there for the surfing. I didn't mind this and was happy to swim and look forward to eating out later....I wish I hadn't. I found the service generally slow and indifferent and the food sadly below par for Sri Lanka ( it had been excellent in Kandy). Many of the restaurants do not have liqour licences and you wont be even able to get a cold beer. If its a full moon it becomes a bank holiday and you will not be served alcohol ANYWHERE. If you are a surfer you will love this place. If you want to eat , relax and socialise look elsewhere. I was also ( and alarmingly) offered drugs on a daily basis by a myriad of individuals, invariably tuc-tuc drivers. Sorry Sri Lanka I thought this place lets you down.

Title: Sri Lanka's Best Wave
Text: An outstanding wave, world quality. Locals tend to drop in on any wave they like. Still it's an epic journey, worth getting there before it becomes too commercial. Mangos is the best bar.

Title: Really nice place to spend a couple of days . . .
Text:
My partner and I spent three weeks travelling around Sri Lanka and decided to spend a few days here to break up the trip a little. It was a much needed rest and nice to see some other tourists and eat something other than rice and curry. 
We were there at the start of the season so it was not crowded and the Accommodation was nice and cheap. Plenty of reasonably priced food and drink and some good surf shops offering lessons, rental Etc.
There is also a good opportunity to see wild elephants about a 20 min tuk tuk ride rom here.
The beach itself was clean but the water was a light brown due to the sand being kicked up by the surf, at the southern end of the beach where the sea was pretty much flat, the water was crystal clear.
I hope to return.

Title: Great for Surfer Dudes and Dudesses
Text: If you're in to surfing come here otherwise its overrated. The beach is OK. There's a tourist beach scene but otherwise there is little else to offer. Like Bali dominated by dudes and dudesses.

Title: A great place to visit has not yet been over developed.
Text: I stayed at Hideaway Villas it is a great place to chill out after a surf. There are other places to surf besides Arugam Bay near by. I was there in May 2011 and I had the best holiday ever, I did not want to leave. The staff and Hideaway Villas were always helpful as I travelled there by my self. The food is fantastic and the people are so friendly. A good place to have dinner and a few drinks is The Physcodellic Lounge it is a roof top bar and restaurant with surfing movies playing under the stars.. The best time to go is from May to November for waves. The only draw back is the hell road trip from Colombo to Arugam Bay 8 hours drive I had drivers to take me. Don,t try and drive your self it is to dangerous not any road rules I think ?

Title: Caching the moonlit surf
Text:
The first time I visited Arugam Bay was back in 1994, when the Sri Lankan civil war  was at full tilt, and visits to the East coast were by the foolhardy or do or die surfers from Australia.

 it was just before christmas that year, when about 7 of us, in two vehicles, left Colombo early one cool December morning, and took the road to first Ratnapura, and then turned Eastwards on the Embilipitiya road to Arugam Bay. It took much of the day to reach there, as the roads were B roads, badly maintained, full of snaking twists and turns.The saving grace was the breathtaking scenery: we passed waterfalls, rice paddies, and sleepy vilages and towns until we reached Moneragala, the nearest large town to Pottuvil and the Bay. We had a late lunch at the Rest House there.
From here on, it was the war zone, The road was deserted, except for the odd bus and trucks carrying produce. Checkpoints, manned by army mostly , dotted the road.We had to stop and show our IDs inumerable times. From Siyabalanduwa onwards the checkpoints were manned by the Special Task Force, STF, the paramilitary special ops force that policed the East Coast.Tension was in the air. The checkpoint personnel were monosyllabic, surly at times, with red-rimmed eyes, pointing to sleepless nights and a lot of stress.Although the LTTE had not mounted a big operation in the East coast that year, there were small incursions al the time. I drunk it all in-the tension went hand in hand with the dark green foliage of the dense forests on either side of this road. If we got blown up on this road, it was all worth it-died on the road to Arugam Bay, chasing a wave, what an epitah, I thought.
When we passed Siyambaladuwa, the vegetation began to change.It was no longer wet zone tropical but dry zone, with its spiky foliage, a more yellowish colour, smaller leaves, and sparser.And the heat began to ratchet up.There were landscapes of green rice paddy fields stretching to the horizon on both sides of the road now. Occasionally there were small tractors trundling on the road. More checkpoints.
Then we reached Lahugala Forest Reserve, which was by the road, from which one was supposed to see Elephant herds snacking on the lush grass of the tank bed there. We stopped, and there were a couple of Grey Ghosts there. Their trunks swayed as they tore up the grass.It was our first sight of the magic of the jungles here, and well worth the 8-hour drive. It was getting towards dusk, and we had get off this road before the light went.
The road now was really bad, pot holed and very small, untouched since the 1950s , it seemed. On both sides were dry paddies and salterns, streching to the horizons. The road didnt allow for a speed in excess of 10 mph:it seemed quicker to walk, but we would probably get shot by the STF, who were probably patrolling out somewhere out there.
The final checkpoint was reached, when we got to Pottuvil, the dusty, one road, one horse - million tractor little town which would be immortalised in our minds as Potters. We stopped for a while in Potters, drinking in the sights while slaking our tea habit in a tea boutique. A town of bycycles and tractors, and rusty, beaten up up vans and STF soldiers carrying T-56 automatics. We had stocked up with fresh veggies and food in Moneragala, as wher we were headed to had a cook.There was only one hotel/guest house  in the Bay, the Stardust hich was owned by a Danish couple who had been here ages.But they charged major bucks for rooms.I and two friends, a couple, were going to stay in the run down guest house owned by a family friend. The others, another couple an their teenage son would stay in the Stardust.
There was a glorious sunset dying as we crossed the bridge into the Bay.The winds blowing from the sea promised something, maybe crab curries and grilled prawns.
The Stardust was immediately identifiable, set back on the left in its neat sandy grounds, a sold white building, with some small cabanas out facing the sea. We were in the Hideaway, a ramshackle old building, hidden away in a mass of Bourganvillea and some scattered coconut trees. It was run by a very dodgy caretaker, who met us smoking a cheroot, dressed in a sarong, and very suspicious of these dusty, sweaty oiks from Colombo, with a white girl in tow. After some preliminary sparring, he agreed to let us stay in the rooms upstairs.There were cabanas, but they were falling down, rat and mosquito infested, he said.
The owner of the Hideaway was involved in a court case trying to get rid of the caretaker, who had a reputation of using the place for prostitution and drugs. Arugam bay always had great rep for the best grass in Sri Lanka: I wanted to do some inhaling while I was there, i was all part of the package.
Problem-there was no cook:we would have to do our own dinner. Of all of us, I had the most experience of cooking, my friends were in the fry-ups, toast and cereal brigade.I got them slicing and dicing, and we had brought some chicken, which I managed to get into a semblance of a curry. The other layabouts did a salad, and we tucked in after a shower in our rickety rooms, which had  fans and mossie nets. No crabs and prawns tonight, but we were too tired to care, and after dinner we headed of to the Stardust down the road, the night starlit and still.
After several ice cold beers,and lots of chat , making plans for the days ahead we called it and staggered back, nearly dissappearing into some of the potholes on the road.

I collapsed on my bed, arranging the mossie net as well as I could and left for noddieland. 

I was woken up suddenly by what seemed to be the apocalypse breaking over the bay.It was World War Three:the bulding was shaking, there were flares lighting up the outside, and I could see tracer fire acing into the night,The noise was horrendous.Convinced I was going to die imminently, I ran next door to where my friends were, and leaped into their room. They were under the bed. I joined them.
"What the hell is going on?", my pal's English girlfriend yelled, as another mortar seemed to alight in the garden, shaking the paper thin walls.
"I think the Tigers are coming, J-, and I want you to surrender to them, seeing you are a tourist you'll;;be okay and as we are together they wont kill us" said my pal ,her boyfriend.Always thinking ahead my buddy R-.
I really wished I had eaten a crab curry and got hold of some Bay weed tonight:atl east I would have gone out with great memories. I thought of my mum back in Colombo, an all the things I hadnt done yet, the women I hadnt dated yet, the music I hadnt heard, the cars, I hadnt driven, the countries I hadnt been to,a long long Bucket list.
Then, as suddenly as it had begun, the fireworks stopped. 
We crawled out, shaken and well stirred, and looked out at he darkness.The Hideaway had no power anyway, so  it was dark everywhere.No sign of life, no signs of Tigers walking up the path, nothing. The stillness of the night returned, and even the cicadas began to chirp cautiously.It was around 3 am.
We opened some scotch to celebrate being alive, and went back to bed.
The next morning, we asked the first SF guy we saw what had happened. He laughed, albeit rather hysterically, I thought.
"Oh, that?Nothing to worry about, we were just getting rid of our old ammo stocks before the New year" he said walking away quickly.
Dumbfounded, we looked at each other and chalked it up to more of inimitable Sri Lankan humour.
The next few days were idyllic:we pickniked in a green dale beyond which we saw a hoard of copulating turtles, their shells glistening in the sun, saw ancient temples on beaches,saw Elephants and Buffalos together on th roadside, and visited Kudumbigala rock monastery, where the silence of millennia ruled the heights and meditation caves, the haunt of Bear and Leopard. We body surfed in some forgotten cove where the fish nibbled at our toes , and visited deserted, empty beaches running for miles., visited the hushed grandeur of Radella tank, where forest giants stalked the bund.
 I got my crab curry but no hash, which I got on another trip. Over it all lay the feeling of a frontier, a place forgotten by time and the hordes  of the  20th century. 
I have been to Arugam bay many times since then,  caught the surf one full moon night,but the world has changed:Gone are the checkpoints, the palpable taste of danger and tension in the air,Gone too are most of the Elephants. But Kudumbigala monastery remains the same, human history nothing but a blip in its millennial count, its caves a silent reminder of eternity.

The Hideaway is now a thriving resort, famous for its food, and the Stardust is still there,, although the Danish Manager was swept away in the  grea Tsunami of 2003. There are a host of small hotels and guesthouses, and the surfing is now on global to-do lists by all surfers.The jungles are still there, now dwindling sadly.The 21st century has come to the Bay.

But the feeling of a frontier is still there,although our experience was quite special.Perhaps you have to be Sri Lankan to realise we saw a frontier just before it began to change. When what we got couldnt be charged to a credit card or to a wad of dollars.

To paraphrase  the Roman Pliny we "watched the cold star Saturn, and saw honey come out of the air at the rising of the Dog-star just before the dawn." 

 Tread softly the dust of Arugam Bay, it carries memories.

Title: a bad experience
Text: For us the price doesn't match the service. First of all parking, at the Star Dust hotel, is a problem. We had been told to park in a certain place but early in the morning (5.45 a.m.) another customer, not anyone from the staff, knocked insistently at the door of our room asking us to move our car, as we did. In our room there wasn't a sealing fan but only a standing fan. There was water on the floor coming from the fridge, and the next morning I found my computer folder completely wet from the same water, as I had stored it on a shelf under the fridge. The hotel is very far from the place where it is possible to have a safe swim. And when the landlady saw us with our luggage ready to leave, after all this, she was only able to ask us to go and pay the bill, without any excuse. So as a conclusion it was a bad experience.

Title: Surfing the Best...
Text: Take it from me, if you're new to surfing and you want the very best in instruction, combined with humour (because you're going to need it!), contact Dulilp or Leseter Kokuhannadige. Undeniably the top surfers in Sri Lanka!  Not all surf is professional quality, but it's constant here in Arugam Bay. Hang-ten, and sometimes you fall-all!

Title: arugam bay surf totally overrated surf
Text: Please one of the top 10 surf destinations in the world. What a joke. No power and overcrowded with learn to surfers with no idea, The line up is full of idiots who dont know what there doing. It is only going to get worst with its increase in popularity. By all means go to Sri Lanka for a great holiday, beautiful place but seriously the surf sucks.

Title: Make sure you are there ON season
Text: My bad that I did not figure out that sri lanka has two very clear seasons and there was the definitively Off season when we visited Arugam. Looking forward to once try it when its on season as it seems like a very cozy and super social place when it´s full of surfers and ppl. Not a big tourist place, BIG plus. Stayed at Hideaway which I SO reccomend. writing a review of that separate :)

Title: Gorgeous setting, fantastic food, clean and great value
Text:
A wonderful Sri Lankan experience. Clean wooden cabanas set in a sandy courtyard just a stumble from the beach and a gorgeous and mega-chilled communal area for eating, working or just sitting staring at the sea.

We spent a week in Galaxy Lounge and loved every minute of it. The staff were friendly and attentive without ever being intrusive. Hassan the chef produced brilliant meal after brilliant meal, whilst his ever-smiling, younger assistant, whose name alludes me, worked hard to look after our every need.

The only downside for us was the sea was too rough for our six-year old to really play in and the surfing is a kilometre away at the other end of the beach, although a Tuk Tuk is easily found.

Thoroughly recommend if you want a chilled location that is quiet, clean and great value for money.

Title: Beginner surfer heaven
Text: Probably one of the best spots in the world for beginner surfers, although its claim to being one of the top 5/10 overall point breaks will be questioned by those with Aus/Indo/South Africa/Hawaii experience. Having said that, when it's on at the point there are long and rewarding rides to be had for the pros. Think Noosa, but without the rocks. Waves lack the punch of the aforementioned countries so longboarders will find toes-on-the-nose nirvana. Switch-foot, dead cockroach, soul arches...you'll pull out your full back catalogue.  Don't stress about bringing a board as new Thai-made mals are arriving by the day and can be rented cheaply. Because the waves get progressively smaller as they grind along the sand point it is brilliant for those learning or mid-range riders who what to cruise between Lion beers. If you persist, you will stand up here. It gets crowded but the break seems to handle it. There are other surf options a tuktuk ride away. It's in the dry zone of Sri Lanka, so those expecting jungle, monkeys and palm trees will be disappointed. Try the west coast in the opposing surf season. Beer on tap at the Siam View Hotel.

Title: wild sri lanka again
Text: took a brief east coast trip to Arugam Bay. did not know what to expect but loved the journey in- lots of natural scenery with wildlife.  the Bay itself was gorgeous - lots of sand dunes with unpretensious motels/guesthouses dotted  about- we stayed over night a Hideaway which is a rustic yet charming boutique type lodgings- the main building is really a family house with character- lots of books and magazines- realy laid back vibe  and the rooms are something special-your little cabana with privacy and view out to a lovely garden- great spot and nice break from the more touristy southwest

Title: Stunning Point Break
Text:
What an unbelievable hidden gem. Could have spent the whole week just at Arugam Bay. 

The water is bathtub warm, there are a number of different breaks that are not very crowded. The surfing was unbelievable. 

Stayed at PJs Beach Hotel which was a 100 metre stroll to the point break - and it was the best.

Cannot wait to go back.

Title: Great beach but beware of fighting youths
Text: Spent 6 nights at Arugam Bay in July. Great beach for surfing with a giant sand bar separating the surfing beach and mainland, giving a great swimming area for children inbetween. This is great for families who want to surf but need someone for younger children to swim. The surfing waves did get busy late afternoon but it was quiet early in the morning. It is easy to rent surf boards or body boards (around rps 500 for 24 hours) and tuk tuk are a plenty to visit some of the other places to surf. On the negative side we had a bad experience with groups of young men fighting (very violently!) on the beach near the point one afternoon. It went on for quite awhile, and people with young children were unable to leave the beach without passing through what was happening (we were able to swim away with our children across the lagoon). Eventually, the army (who have a permanent presence on this beach) called for reinforcements and things calmed down, leaving shocked (and crying foreigners) on the beach. We thought it was all over but the next morning at 8am two groups of young men were arguing again but it resolved itself quickly. Locals we spoke to played the whole incident down saying it was just the youngsters getting out of hand and it was nothing but it was a frightening experience for us and we did wonder if this was why the army and tourist police are permanently based on the beach. Maybe this was a one off and we were unlucky to be there as we had seen no other trouble for the 5 days we had been there before, but were glad to leave the tensions behind when we moved on.

Title: The Beach restaurant Arugam Bay Surf Resort
Text: A superb restaurant set on the beachside with wonderful views of the crashing surf. The service was excellent and so efficient compared with the other frustratingly slow restaurants in A bay. The food was excellent, with great choice including Authentic Sri Lankan Cuisine as well as Mexican, noodles, stir-fries, fresh fish, cold beers and more, it's good that you don't have to pre-book like other places. Really helpful and good natured staff.

Title: Hideaway in Arugam bay
Text:
I travelled from Colombo - Negombo - Kandy - Nuwara Eliya - Horton Plains - Arugam Bay(stopping in Ella for the fantastic view!) - Galle - Yala National Park (Overnight safari) - Galle - Colombo in 16 days. (I spent one whole week in Galle though)

Things I would HIGHLY recommend:
- Taking the train from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya - I could have stayed on it all day - the view was INCREDIBLE!
-Stopping in Ella - but you really only need a stop for lunch to appreciate the stunning views.
- Staying at 'Hideaway' in Arugam Bay. BY FAR the best place I stayed on this trip (apart from my friend's Villa in Galle - but unless we have the same friend you won't find anywhere more welcoming/clean/friendly and helpful as this place. On a travellers budget, of course. Although saying that I did stay in some high end hotels and I still would put 'Hideaway' up there!)  We had an air conditioned room, which was perfect. The staff were so very friendly (not overly so though - afterall, I am English! ;-)). The food was excellent! It is run by a Sri Lankan lady who appears to know exactly what the good things in life are. Somewhere chilled to relax, clean and with great service. I am a real foodie, so that fresh food was a real hit for me. She also gave us some excellent tips.
-Safari - we saw a leopard - I was over the moon! This however can be really hit and miss.

I drew on quite a lot of reviews before I went travelling so wanted to provide something vaguely useful too.

If I were to do this trip again I would probably miss out Negombo and spend a bit more time in the Hill Country. I enjoy a good view and a nice beach and this holiday had exactly that.

In a bid to manage your expectations however be ware that Sri Lanka is not easy to travel around. The best way is to hire a driver. But you do need to haggle. This is an expensive way to travel, and often hair-raising - apparently the best time to over take on the road in Sri Lanka is on a corner!!

Try:
Hoppers
String Hoppers
anything coconut related
all curries
Fruit on the train

Beware:
Street food (just take extra precaution)

Enjoy!

Title: Arugam Bay was Great, Hideaway Resort was Fantastic
Text: We had originally booked to stay in Arugam Bay for six days.  With four spare days in our plan it was easy to make the decision to spend them here also.  Arugam Bay is a very cruisy place with increadibly friendly locals.  The surf is always of at least a fun standard, though crowds can get a little thick out at the point at times.  We stayed at Hideaway Resort, which is on the main strip accross from the beach.  Our three person room was huge, with excellent amenities and always well kept.  The food was amazing.  Every night the menu would have a new delicacy that would always meet the standard of a 5 Star restaurant in Aus.  Sharon made it her duty to ensure that ourselves and the other guests were always looked after and I felt all too at home at the Hideaway.  I recomend to anyone!!!

Title: a highlight - very relaxed place
Text:
Arugam bay was a real highlight for us on a 6 week trip around sri lanka. 

SL seems to be a bit rip-off these days, compared with our last trip here in 2004, with silly prices for food and accommodation, especially in the south, south-east and near the "safari" zones.  But Arugam bay restored our faith. It's one of the last refuges of backpackers in the country (along with crazy hikkaduwa) and we had a real relaxing time here mixed with some exciting cycling journeys along the coast towards Panama village.

We stayed at Beach Hut, always busy even out of season, we learned. Cheap rooms and genuinely great food.

The main beach area is not the tropical beauty of, say, Thailand or malaysia, but that's more or less the case for all of sri lanka where the waves are generally enormous (ok if you're a surfer) and the beaches steep, not to mention strewn with plastic rubbish. Arugam beach was also a fishing beach which, apart from the inevitable scattered rubbish, made it all the more interesting.

Nearby trips can be made to Pottuvil town and, further north, Pottuvil point, a popular surfer hangout in season but almost completely empty when we visited. Be careful swimming here due to currents from the lagoon (even if it looks very picturesque). Also Panama village, south of arugam, is possible by bicycle or tuktuk where the journey itself is great, rather than the village which is ok for some food and drinks. An English guy has bought up the land encompassing the point so the current peace may or may not change in future. at the moment there is only a restaurant and a few basic huts at the point itself but I guess this is a busy place in surfing season. The caretaker, sidike, is a wealth of local info and good company for a chat. it's a lonely job he has!

Food is available from the guest houses or restaurants along the main road running behind the beach. We ate in the Beach Hut most nights as it was reasonably priced and very good Indian food.

Title: Tranquility at its best
Text:
We visited Arugam Bay and stayed at Rangas Beach Hut for few days. I loved the stay, food and the atmosphere at Beach Hut.  Arugam Bay is an amazing place, the beach to the limit our eye can find scenery. Since we went there closer to the end of the season not crowded as well.
We visited Kumana Bird Sanctuary as well, again calm and quiet.  Loads of different birds, enough number of crocodiles, elephants, different kind of other animals and If you are lucky you could see the leopard and bear as well. 
Can you picture where an Englishman, a Welshman, a German, an Argentine,  2 French ladies and 4 Sri Lankans at the same table, drinking, eating fabulous Sri Lankan food and having fun is not something u would get easily. I am sure the credit should go to Ranga for the atmosphere he creates in his Beach Hut. 
I will be there again soon!!

Title: Surf and sand
Text: Loved it, stayed at Hideaway one night, thankyou Sharon for your hospitality and another night at Avingit a bar with rooms to rent run by a great guy from UK called Adam, really friendly atmosphere and fabulous pizzas. I thought the locals were great, would certainly return when surf is up!

Title: Student trip disappontiment
Text: Saving whole summer money to visit Sri Lanka paradise ...I spent at Srilanka 3 weeks since beginning of September, 10 days of it in Arugam .... It's good place to chill... to learn surfing maybe ...but overall - lot of mess, prices too high in comparison to normal Asia, water like in a pond (can't see the bottom of the sea at all), beaches nothing close to paradise .... big disappointment

Title: Not a great beach for swimming
Text: It was interesting, the beach was full of fishing boats , We saw the boats all coming back with their catches early in the morning and all the men on the beach haggling over the cost of the fish.not a swimming or sunbathing beach although I think it was not surfing season. We went for a walk up the beach early evening and all the locals were getting in the water but it was quite rough .

Title: Better than Bali
Text: AS a seasoned Bali traveler I can say that this place is fabulous, better on the pocket and the food is delicious. Most meals cost $6-$10 and you can get a bed for $10 too. We went to surf loved the A bay point at sunrise and the set up was perfect for kids who are learning. Peanuts surf break was only 20 minutes tuk tuk and don't pay more than a 1000 rupees to tuk tuk to any local beaches! Potsville was also a really cool surf spot. Bars on the beach are aplenty and the drinks are reasonably cheap.Just go!

Title: Breathtaking beach!!
Text: Just spent a weeks down the east coast of Sri Lanka with my boyfriend.We were blad to be there, since it is one of the best beaches in Sri Lanka for all the beach lovers around the world. Perfect waves for surfing and perfect beaches for swimming. And we enjoyed the beach party's, perfect view of sun rise and sun set are breathtaking!! And the people around there are very friendly too!!

Title: Beautiful spot- also check out nearby Peanut Farm
Text: The bay itself is beautiful, especially at sunset (and doubly so at the onset of a warm storm) and sunrise when all the fishing boats come in. When it comes to the water though, at least for a non-surfer, the nearby Peanut Farm was incredible: a gorgeous, isolated little spot with families learning to surf and couples swimming. For 1200 ruppees, a tuk-tuk driver will take you from the main drag in Arugam Bay to Peanut Farm, and pick you up at whatever pre-determined time you like. During surfing season, there's a little restaurant there, and off season, the snack shop still runs.

Title: Worth a short visit, mind the dodgy locals though (ocean surf)
Text:
Just returned from a 4 week trip to SL. Such an amazing country and so many great experiences. The biggest let down was Arugam Bay. As an experienced 27 yr old surfer I was looking forward to this part of our travels the most.  I have surfed in many parts of the world and rented boards from all over with no issue. Ocean Surf is said to have the best name to rent boards but from my encounter I did not experience this. I rented an old fish board for $9 for the day. Before renting went over the board and was happy all issues were pointed out. After a great few waves at Whisky point I returned the board in the late afternoon. Upon returning the board me and the owner quickly went over it but he was more interested in talking about the surf I had (diversion?) and with this was my mistake, not going over the board in as much detail as in the morning. I walked out the shop and started to make my way down the street. I was chased by the owner producing this "miracle" damage on the board.The damage was a large ding that had cracked the fibreglass (the type of damage anyone would know that they had done and something that slaps you in the face its that obvious). After surrounding me with a number of his mates and a lot of back and forth I was forced to pay about $72 to fix this damage. These stories are all to common in Arugam Bay and unfortunately it was my turn after a perfect run. Avoid OCEAN SURF rentals!

Arugam Bay it's self is a bit try hard with the majority of locals there for the beach lifestyle and to try and pick up the fe male tourists. The service is terrible in most of the places and it was not uncommon to wait over an hour for a order to arrive. 

The only exception was staying at the Hideaway. Great accom, friendly service and the food was amazing. The Hideaway is the only place to stay in my opinion and after talking with many other tourists at the time they agreed and switched to the hideaway.

Title: Overpriced, dodgy locals, not worth the trip.
Text: This place is way overpriced for what it is. I've travelled all over Asia this being one of my last stops and I was disgusted at the greed that has taken the locals here. Just coming from Bali, Indonesia - the most touristy surf destination in Asia - i was shocked at how much the restaurants and guest houses and even tuk tuk drivers attempt to charge tourists in Arugam Bay. We're talking at least 4-5 dollars for the simplest of meals up to 12 for a decent one, when in Bali i could get absolutely fantastic meals for 2-3 dollars at most. Beers in Bali are cheaper even though they have a tax. When I was in Colombo beers were half the price they are in Arugam Bay, and food was a third of the price. Accommodation and transport is also overpriced. I've also heard from fellow travellers that they've been ripped off in certain board rental shops. Not impressed, if I was gonna spend that much money I would have stayed in Bali another month. The crowd on the main point is also pretty big and not many people seem to understand the etiquette of surfing, bad vibes all round really.

Title: Be careful of the Surf Shop you rent from
Text:
Hasan Surf House in Arugum Bay charged me 9,000 rupees for damage to a surfboard. When I said that was way too expensive he started threatening me. When I said I would go to the police he threatened me even more ... saying it would cost me much more and that he know how to get money from me because he is Sri Lankan. When I appealed to the Australian owner of the shop he just cursed at me and said he does not deal with people he let's his manager do that (threat and extort). Please be careful.
BTW, the prices for food and lodging are way too expensive for what you get there.

Title: Only come here if you love surfing
Text: Arugam bay seemed to be a popular surfing spot, but it wasn't good for much else. After visiting stunning beaches such as uppuveli and passikudah on the east coast, arriving at arugam bay was so disappointing. It's a small bay full of fishing boats, little space for sunbathing, and sea too wavy for swimming. Arugam bay is NOT a paradise stretch of endless sand!!! If you are a surfer or keen to learn, arugam bay would be ideal but do not come here if you want a paradise like beach. Everything about arugam bay caters for surfers. Due to this, it has a different vibe to anywhere else in the country - a lot of tourists and party atmosphere. ABay is an acquired taste :)

Title: It's just a beach
Text: Do not fly from Europe or the Americas just to come to Arugam Bay and surf. There are much better and closer  places to home. It's honestly just a beach and not that unique or better from any other beaches around the world. There are much prettier and better places to visit in Sri Lanka than here and around the world as well. You get hassled a lot by tuk tuk drivers and store owners making it a pretty annoying and tourist feeling area. On the good side, it's very undeveloped so you don't have that overdeveloped touristy feel. Just the locals trying to hustle you at every corner. I planned to stay for three nights and found it to be quite meh. I stayed one and went to Ella instead. Much better. Sri Lanka is an amazing country, but I wouldn't waste your time at a pretty average beach. Certainly don't come all the way here just for this location.

Title: Surfing Arugam bay
Text: Just spent a few weeks down the east coast of Sri Lanka  had some great waves .and was looked after by Hasan from Hasans surf house just as you come into town on the left side. He is very helpful and can not do enough for you. He also stocks surf boards for hire and sale and also does lessons .really worth the trip will be going again .

Title: Good place bad tuk tuk management
Text: I've visited Arugam Bay multiple times before and always had an amazing time surfing with friends, relaxing and exploring the local beaches and surf breaks. However, i recently visited Arugam Bay with 2 other friends and we had some issues with taking our boards to local surf spots via tuk tuk. Being three girls we felt safer travelling together in one tuk tuk with our boards as opposed to two of us travelling together and one alone. We were told however that we weren't allowed to take all three of our boards on the tuk tuk and the rule was only three! We found this rule quite bizarre considering a tuk tuk is made to seat three people. We were extremely frustrated and feel that if this continues to happen in the future then there will be many more upset tourists and after all Arugam Bay thrives on tourism!

Title: Arugam Bay - SHIM Beach Resort
Text:
One of the best beaches in the East coast of Sri Lanka. The beaches stretch for miles. The waves are a dream for surfers. This laid back stretch of the coast is very popular among the surfing fraternity. The people living in the area are friendly and in my opinion some of the most honest people I have come across.

We stayed in the SHIM Beach Resort. It has three rooms good showers and clean toilet facilities. Meals are provided on request. Only meters away from SHIM one can see fisherman using the oldest method of fishing in Sri Lanka - Dragnet fishing (Ma Del) If you like you can request the fishermen to join them pulling the net in. this is an experience you will remember. If you ask Mr. Ameen who is the owner of SHIM to buy fresh fish for cooking, he will gladly oblige. By the way Mr. Ameen prepares a wicked fish barbecue. Try it if you stay there. 

The sign post on the main road says it is 300 meters to SHIM but it is really about a kilometer and the last building before the beach.

You will witness the most beautiful sunrises ever in Arugam Bay. Hope you will enjoy your visit as much as I did.

Title: a good relaxing break with the locals
Text:
i went during off season and could only be more than happy since it was quiet and i have all the chance to mix around with the locals and spend more time with them chatting through the day.

Beach was rough and surfing/swimming was not really recommended. No sun light during the day as it was monsoon season.

BUT I LOVE IT !!!! the rain is nice and i like walking on a deserted street.

i had a good time there and would love to return just to see how crazy it is during the dry season.

for more personal experiences on my sri lanka travels, you may read on my blog at : 

http://pinparadise.blogspot.com/2014/03/sri-lanka.html

cheers !

PRANA

Title: Friendly locals
Text:

Title: Had bigger expectations
Text:
For tourists Arugam Bay offers a long street full of restaurants and one or two bars very close to the beach.
There are myriads of opportunities to stay. Starting from very basic to high class. 
The beach itself is not bad but at this time of the year (the season starts in March according to the locals) is absolutely deserted. This might sound quite nice at first but the sea here is extremely tough. Considering myself a decent swimmer and bodysurfer, I gave it some good tries but this ever-raging ocean is no fun and very unforgiving.

There are a few things to see around here, but as soon as you get out of the tourist bubble youll merely find yourself in very poor quarters inhabited by the locals  the effects of the tsunami are still very much present here. For us this meant having a slight feeling of guilt for staying there.

The food being served here earns 5 stars, always fresh, always extremely tasty and authentic.
Its a bit harder to buy or get alcohol than other places and the prices differ a lot, definitely watch out for that.

Probably just the wrong time to be here.

Title: Surf, Sun, Beers and Fun
Text: Arugam Bay is an awesome, inexpensive spot to go for surfing (mostly right-handers, although you can find a few OK beach lefts) for all people from beginner to advanced. It has a really relaxed tropical vibe, plenty of beach parties, friendly locals and lots to do in the surrounding area if the beach isn't really your thing. Mostly popular with people 40. I spent 3 weeks there and it was great. I'd go back.

Title: Hideaway - nice hotel
Text:
We enjoyed staying at the Hideaway in Arugam Bay.  Sharon is a gracious host and her hotel delivers on it's promise of comfortable rooms, good service and fine food.  We wouldn't have stayed anywhere else.

Also, don't miss out on the beaches south of Panama.  You can expect to be the only one there - other than, maybe, an underemployed fisherman - on a picture perfect, sandy beach.

Title: THE place to stay in Arugam Bay!!!
Text:
Hideaway is an absolutely gorgeous place and I believe the best accommodation and restaurant there is in Arugam Bay. Of my four-week round travel in Sri Lanka with my two young children, this place - it's beautiful aesthetics, loving attention to detail, superior food and incredibly kind and helpful owner Sharon and her staff; all culminating in creating the most enjoyable and relaxed, tranquil and peaceful atmosphere - stayed with us and would most certainly be the one to come back to. 

The bed and breakfast centers around the owner's old family holiday home, set back from the beach across the main road. The property consists of the main house and 6 or 7 bungalow-style units amidst a luscious, palm-tree adorned and color-kissed garden. 
The downstairs veranda style set-up of the main house functions as the reception, restaurant and open-air living-room - complete with old cupboards full of books, big rattan chairs and stone benches atopped with bright-colored cushions inviting you time and again to sink in and relax - all in one. Upstairs, enjoying a wide and beautiful balcony are a few rooms for rent. The bungalows come in various sizes. We stayed in one of the newer ones, which was a spacious (humongous bed and bathroom), minimalistic, clean - simply gorgeous unit.

Arugam Bay is a small village on Sri Lanka's south-eastern coast, which has become a (family)-surfer's heaven. The main street is lined with one bed&breakfast  - some bigger hotels starting to sprout about, which hopefully will not do too much harm to the very chilled and relaxed, not yet too overcrowded feel of Arugam Bay - cafe, imbiss, restaurant, bar, surfer-boutique and corner-shop next to the other, which makes for perfect beach-holiday strolling and hanging-out: picking up your breakfast before descending on to the gorgeous main beach, which has a few great (mid-)day hang-out spots; sorting yourself with any snacks or beach-wear utensils anytime; enjoying one brilliant dinner after the other during your stay - unless of course Hideaway just keeps tempting you back in - probably the most stressful decision-making aspect during our stay!!! 

I can only whole-heartedly recommend a stay in Arugam Bay and here at Hideaway!!!

ENJOY!!!

Title: Hide Away villas - perfect +
Text:
We stayed in 12 different accommodations during our 4 weeks trip through Sri Lanka. Hide Away is absolutely in our top 2. Why? Well located, quiet and close to everything important in Arugam bay. Spacious room, even for us travelling with with 2 young children and staying all in 1 room. Probably the best bathrooms in Sri Lanka; spacious, the first one with enough space to store your toiletries and a fantastic rainshower with STAR-view at night!

The owners do everything for you to be sure that you are heaving a great time. The menu changes every day, excellent cooking! The owner plays LIVE jazzy music (guitar) during dinner; a very relaxing atmosphere. No other place in Arugam Bay that even comes close.

Title: Awesome food
Text: Pitched up as a group of 10 or so, can we get fed? Can you give me an hour. Sure. Then we had the best meal we had in weeks in Sri Lanka. Rooms were nice, aircon was good but the bathrooms are a bit rubbish but clean enough. 30 secs across the road to the beach.

Title: Hideaway Villa and Cabanas - somewhere nice to chill out
Text: Arugam bay is a lovely little village and a good place to stop on the long drive from the south coast to Trinco.  We stayed at Hideaway, an old Dutch colonial house with big wooden verandahs, quaint old features and art work.  The owner has recently returned from living abroad and is lovingly restoring this old family holiday home and the cabanas in the lovely garden.  Some negative reviews I've noticed obviously relate to the former caretaker's management- the owner is refurbishing the rooms and establishing a quiet, cool atmosphere for laid back guests. We certainly had the personal touch and enjoyed great jazz and world music and delicious fusion cooking to order.  [ not cheap but of the highest standard].  I found the upstairs rooms with open fretwork walls, cool but prone to mozzies and, with no sound proofing, not a honeymoon venue! Next time - and we certainly plan to return to our helpful, charming hosts - we will try the cabanas which are being refurbished now.  A nice place for the discerning traveller, a short walk from a great, uncomercialised beach.

Title: Lovely little fishing town - great place to get away from the crowds out of season!
Text:
We chose to spend 3 nights in Arugam Bay based on reviews in our Rough Guide book, and we enjoyed our stay here. We were there in February, so it was out of season and the place was very quiet. We stayed the first night at the Beach Hut, which is a lovely hotel if you can get a decent room. However, we had a tiny room in the back, away from the beach, which was Rs.800, but was miserable, as it was infested with bed bugs or something else that bites. I probably only slept a total of an hour the entire night. The food there was great and it has a great atmosphere, though. We were lied to the day we arrived and told we would only have that room for the first night, then would be moved to a nicer one on the beach, which a more honest member of staff informed us the next day, was actually impossible, as they were fully booked. So, we packed up and headed elsewhere. We picked the Surf Resort (formerly Hillton), which was lovely. We had a spacious cabana just off the beach with beautiful views for just Rs.1000 (£5.65) per night. I'm sure rates increase during the surfing season. The food at the Surf Resort was good. We also tried the Siam View Hotel, which was okay for Thai food, and the Stardust Beach Hotel, which was a delicious, but quite pricey meal. 
Arugam Bay is a bit out of the way, but it's worth seeing.

Title: Favourite place in Sri Lanka - it's easy to get sucked into the laidack Suf village
Text:
We only intended to stay for 3 days, we ended up staying longer than a week. Enough said.

There's more to this great, off the beaten track, quirky little surf town than just surfing. Beautiful beaches, hot hot sunshine, hidden beach shacks selling cold drinks, local restaurants selling rice and curry and some of the best fish I've ever had. And of course, there's lots of surfing with great spots for beginners or for those more advanced. 

Food can be found for very cheap but, with only one wine store in town, beer can be pricey and often only sell the really strong stuff.

Title: Expensive and disappointing
Text: We had a lot of expectations as the comments were super positive. What a disappointment: food is ok but not Indian (fade or at least not spicy as in India), prices are exaggerated (min. 850 rupees for a dish) and service is poor (forget having your drink before food and lots of mistakes in ordering) and really slow.

Title: Reasons to Go!.
Text: Plenty of places to stay and eat, probably would only recommend if visiting wildlife park(excellent on our visit saw elephants, leopard, jackals, water buffalo, deer and various birds), surfing is apparently good although when we were there, several surfers were getting sick due to water quality, there are also various temple ruins nearby, of which the story was interesting.

Title: Greed overschadows surf vibe
Text: Arugam bay is a small strip along the coast. It is supposed to be the ultra relaxed surf spot. And yes, it has all the ingredients to be all that. BUT it's all about money here. I tried to buy a towel quality salvation army and they seriously asked more then 15 for it. Trust me I can negotiate and I know the prices elsewhere in Sri Lanka and I took into account that I'm foreign but the price did not change. It's just one example but it is indicative for Arugam Bay. Too bad I would say, cause there will be a village soon that can offer the same but with normal prices.

Title: Hippie charm
Text:
For some reason I felt that Arugam bay was very different from the rest of SL. The journey to get there is an adventure in it self. The first thing you notice getting in to A bay is that time just moves slowly here. The folks around are super friendly, be it the surfers on the beach, restaurant staff, the guy renting out bikes and even the guests at the hotel. Though the main area is sandwiched between the ocean and strip of land running parallel, it does have interesting fabric of many cultures melting together. 

I found eating and drinking out to be more experience than the rest of the country. Maybe because it's out of the way and not close to any big town except monaragala. But with that being said it has a little bit for everyone. Surfing, safari, lazy beach, ancient temples, wild elephants and a vivid nightlife. The old world hippie charm will make you come back to this enchanting village. 

Stayed at the hideaway, would loved to stay in the AC Bungalow. The main villa was hot and the walls were wafer thin, no privacy at all. But food was outstanding.

Title: Hands down the worlds worst surf location
Text:
If you like over crowded breaks, local surfers who have no concept of surf culture or etiquette, learners with Mini-Mals sitting at the peak bailing their boards, reef cuts that get infected from disgusting bacteria ridden water and the fattest laziest wave you'll ever surf, then Arugam Bay may just be the spot for you.

On my first night arriving at my hotel I was offered Marijuana and Cocaine and if that was not enough of a shock, the all night parties on the beach with thumping dance music that goes on until 7am in the morning (despite only a few locals remaining) sure did the trick. 

Its hard to find anything good to say about Arugam Bay, other than that the food is cheap and there are some genuinely nice locals (those that don't surf or operate in the local Tuk Tuk mafia). 

Take my advice if you have any sense between your ears, take your hard earned money and spend it on another country and go somewhere decent, this place is overrated and a complete crap hole to surf.

Title: Destress and enjoy
Text: when you work in hospitality, one of the best things you can do is to get away from it all. No service or quality expectations when my partner and i visited arugam bay, which was a good thing. we got greeted by friendly down to earth people, all looking to have a great time and ensure that the party is kept alive. the resorts are laid back and the beaches are beautiful. cocktails on the beach ans sunset views are worth the minimal spends out here.

Title: Some tourist culture is developing
Text: In contrast to our last visit in 2012 some new  hotels and restaurants built in this scenic surfing coastal belt. In contrast to shady clumsy buildings owned by local Muslim community last time, better tourist culture is developed as local and foreign investors have put down some money . Beaches are always great and excellent in moon light. beware of high waves and unexpected water levels.

Title: Lovely clean beach .
Text:
Although the sea is quite rough in September and the rain can be very regular , when the sun is shining Bentota beach is Beautiful.
If you require a local English speaking Tuk Tuk driver and guide for temple tours , Fish market tours,Turtle release and conservation tours and anything else you might need including shopping and money exchange them Denis is your man with hes brand new gleaming red Tuk Tuk.

Title: Great Beach
Text: Magic beach and ocean, really beautiful sand.  The ocean is strong so be aware of the current, it can easily catch you off guard. Very very quite stretch of beach, amazingly so.. nothing really going on, you can get surf lessons but thats about it.. Body surfing is great fun..

Title: Beautiful beach with limited eateries
Text:
Bentota beach, otherwise known as Ventura Beach, is a beautiful white sandy beach with clear waters that are quite rough and strong at times. We didn't go in the water but people were in swimming, and body boarding. 

We were surprised the beach wasn't lined with beachfront restaurants but there are sunbeds with umbrellas lining the beach that also serve food. 
We got sunbeds from "Nice Place", which was 500 lkr for the day Inc umbrella, then also had some beer, a delicious wrap, and other snacks throughout the day. They also tuk tuked us back to hotel for 250 lkr too. Very reasonable. 

There are plenty of places around to grab a sunbed, but I do wish there were more places to get shade and be off the beach.

Title: Holiday
Text: Nice long beach excellent views flat easy walk quiet during week busy weekends a few restaurants bars

Title: Stunning beach...

Food to Water activities ...King Coconut to Cinnamon...Turtles to Crocodile.Dont miss old Bentota River Safari where youll witnessed old Mangroves etc.. 
Go Experience yourself......

Title: Breathtaking
Text: If you happen to be around the area and your a beach lover then you definitely must visit this place. So peaceful and magical. I would highly recommend it.

Title: Warm sea and space
Text:
Bentota beach is lovely. Fine sand gently shelving into a warm sea. For most of the day there were only a handful of people on the beach but come a weekend evening the locals come with their families for a dip and the atmosphere is fantastic and friendly.
DO check out the warning flags as there are some strong currents. Near the Taj hotel on the north side where the beach dog legs to the south there is safer bathing. You can walk for miles seeing the fishermen folding their nets and hauling outriggers from the sea whilst singing songs. If you are going for a walk on the beach take water as there are no beach bars but you can occasionally walk through the trees to a hotel bar. Beware the sun is reflected from the sand and you will burn very easily as there is always a good breeze.
We had no hassle from any touts.

Title: Great swimming & surfing spots.
Text: A beautiful long stretch of golden sand on either side of the Taj hotel. Any travellers to Sri Lanka must spend some time here. There's loads of  accommodation, close to the beach, to suit any pocket & plenty of restaurants to suit any taste.

Title: A beautiful beach

Title: Short stay

Title: Massive beach - clean and not so crowded.
Text: Spent some lovely time on the beautiful, soft, golden sand and blue waters after a long, lazy lunch. Though it was afternoon, it was not very hot. There are deck chairs available for those who want to laze on the beach and water sports for those in the mood.

Title: Beautiful beach with low crowd
Text:
We stayed at one of the resorts at Bentota beach and I must say, this is one of the cleanest beaches in Sri Lanka and it's not too crowded either!

Most days, you'll have a vast beach area all for yourself and you can have a relaxed and cosy day at the beach!

Title: A beach for everyone
Text: I am staying at The Taj on Bentota beach and reckon this beach has a lot going for it. By The Taj there is a little cove that has the sun loungers and stuff if that's what you want. To the right and left as wide expanses of beach with few people on them. Sure you can find isolated places with loungers and umbrellas but most of the beach is untouched. The sand is lovely and soft. The sea at the moment is lovely and warm but it is very 'wavy' and not good for swimming, its fun though! This is why I don't give it 5 stars. There are a very few local sellers on the beach but they are very few and far between and do not hassle.

Title: Glorious!
Text: We spent two weeks based here at Bentota beach. Beautiful golden sands, turquoise sea, lovely people, great food and cols beer. Perfect!

Title: Superb clean Beach...

Title: Beautiful but disappointing
Text:
I just don't get why people rave about Bentota. Yes, the beach is huge and absolutely beautiful and unspoilt BUT there are no beach bars/restaurants, no toilets, no loungers/parasols. Unless you are staying at one of the big resorts and want to pay top dollar. 
Personally, I like to wander along the beach and choose a nice cafe/bar/restaurant to stop for a bite to eat and/or drink but you just can't do that here. Not that I'm an advocate of the over-populated tourist trap but it's nice to have a choice.
Additionally, the surf is so strong that it is not safe for even the most confident of swimmers.

Title: Beautiful beach with crashing waves

Not too many sellers and they are respectful & polite even though persistent.
All in all a Lovely beach and waking up each morning to its beauty is indeed a treat.

Title: Beautiful beach

Title: Sublime
Text: If you like quiet long wide clean soft sandy beaches with palm trees and vegetation on one side and the Indian Ocean on the other this is the beach for you.  Sunsets are a must to watch.  Ventura beach has sun loungers belonging to the adjacent hotels but further down it is completely clear.

Title: Quiet, Nice, Safe, Hot
Text: Rather Quiet beach if you compare to others in the subcontinent. Most of the areas are served by hotels next to the beach. Avoid March April as its very hot. Nice sunset. You will need special transport if you are not staying at a nearby hotel already.

Title: Great place

Title: Great beach

Title: Romantic
Text: This place is a must if you are thinking to visit Sri Lanka without kids, relaxing days, fantastic food, nice people who dedicated to make you feel  like a kings. Love it!

Title: Not recommended
Text: Me and my partner stayed at a lovely hotel right on the beach (the Avani). Whilst the hotel was nice we felt very uneasy walking around outside the hotel. The beach boys preyed on us and we got approached on both the beachside and the other road and train side of the hotel. The boys (who where actually older men probably in their 50s/60s in our experience) literally wait for you to step out of the hotel and approach you as soon as you leave the safety of the hotel. At first they seem friendly and want to chat but it then becomes apparent that they are not genuine and they are not to be trusted - on two occasions we wanted to go to the town and local market and on both occasions we got approached and both men (who at first seemed friendly and nice) took us the opposite direction (we realised afterwards) and luckily we trusted our instincts to stop and return to the hotel - we dont know where they where planning to take us and what their intentions where.... We like to get out and explore where we are staying (were keen travellers) but we didnt feel comfortable doing so in this area because of the men loitering around outside of the hotel.  Although we will return to Sri Lanka in the future we will not return to Bentota.

Title: Excellent for real swimming
Text:
Great beach (the best we've seen in Sri Lanka, out of 4 or 5) IF: 1) you don't want bars and annoying vendors on the beach, 2) you don't like crowds, 3) you like fine-grained sand and a clean beach, 4) especially, if you like swimming  not wading, but really swimming. There is a rock between the bay and the sea, it's about 900 meters from the beach, so it's a great swim.  When the sea is calm, you can swim very near the rock and see all kinds of fish (not much of coral reef, though, and whatever there is is dead).  When the sea is not so calm, be very careful  I stayed at least 1020 meters away from the nearest visible rock, and I could still see some rocks beneath me.  

The downsides: 1) The sea is very opaque (cloudy)  you can't see further than 1 meter, perhaps a little more.  This is because of the very fine sand floating in the sea (near the beach) and, above all, because of microscopic algae making the water green.  2) On the way from the beach to the rock, there is an area where somewhat dirty-looking foam gathers  you might want to swim around it.  3) Of course, as transpires from the above, if you like beach partying, this is not a beach for you.  4) The waves can be strong, so I am not sure it's a good beach for small kids.

Title: Bentota Sri Lanka Tour
Text:
Sri Lanka is a island country in Indian ocean. In Sri lanka trip you can get hill station, national park and sea beach, Metro life at a time.

Season for travel.
From mid September you can visit Sri lanka. November December and January are peak season in Sri lanka.

In the sri lanka vacation on 3rd day we went to bentota from Kandy. It is a beach destination in West coast of Sri Lanka. There we took bentota river boat ride. The boat has gone through mangrove forest. There are lot of water sports agent. You can easily book it. The cost of boat ride 10 USD per person. It was 40 minutes boat journey. There are lot of sports activity like speed boat riding, jet ski etc. We spent that night in bentota hotel. Bentota beach is very silent and clear and beautiful, but for taking sea bath it is quite risky. If tourist want beautiful but silence beach destination, then Bentota is the best option. 

Next day I took another boat ride. That is Madhu Ganga boat ride. The cost was 10 USD per person. This is 2 hr boat journey. After boat ride we moved to Galle. There we have seen light house, some old architecture. We came back in bentota hotel. Bentota to Galle distance is 75km. It will takes 2 hr. Galle is also a good place to hang out.

Title: The magnificent Bentota Beach Hotel
Text:
Bentota Beach Hotel, an icon in Sri Lankan architecture and a property with a rich history reconstructed by Bawas student, Channa Daswatte is a true tribute to Sri Lankas most famed architect Geoffrey Bawa. 

Standing on the balcony of the Geoffrey Bawa Suite, you see the sea on the right and the Bentota river on the left, and Sripada and the central hills on the far right, all in one view. This view, according to architect Channa Daswatte makes this property the one that links the land and the sea. 

The new Bentota Beach is not merely a recreation or a restoration. The main building of the old hotel has been reconstructed newly, as it was built by Bawa. This showcases Bawas wide  architectural influences ranging from Bali to ancient Sri Lankan monuments. Inside the hotel has the signature of Geoffrey Bawa and the period it was constructed in, but in a modern and functional representation. 

The lead architect Channa Daswatte has done an amazing job, not only to archive an iconic construction but also through his brilliance, make it a fresh, modern and functional. It is a museum and treasure trove of art and architecture, that concurrently delivers a guests expectections from a modern luxury hotel.

Text:
One can walk and walk and walk.
The golden sand caresses your feet, and with noone in the sight you are in unison with the wave music.

Regular hawkers but we found they don't harrass you and will take no for an answer. Regular guy with bicycle selling fantastic fruit, drinking coconuts, bananas, pineapples and delicious mangos for pennies. Water is bath water warm but can   be a little rough in places on breezier days. Beach tour operators every couple of hundred yards can strongly recommend Gayan and Sidu just off the Surf Hotel, honest, friendly and informative, they will arrange whatever you want and are very reasonably priced compared to the big tour operators. We thoroughly enjoyed our time here

Text: Lovely pristine beach,clear waters,uncrowded places, pleasure to swim .Scenic evening sunset views which is a pleasure to languish in.

Text:

Title: Great beach offering a relaxing experience
Text:
Loved the beach and we had a great stay in Avani Bentota.

There are a lot of activities that could be over the back and all centers are within few minutes of walking.

If you are into diving or swimming try to get that as early as possible as the sea gets to be rough a bit towards the afternoon onwards.

Could not love it more and looking forward to my next visit.

Mo

Title: Picture Perfect
Text: Crystal Clean water.. you can walk couple of hundred meter in the water, just nee high waves.. neatly maintained. You will notice heli taxi and para gliders occasionally..

Title: Perfect beach vacation
Text:
Bentota is one among the serene beaches in Srilanka, filled with numerous home stays and star accommodations. It is a calm and quiet beach if you are there in November I'm not quiet sure about the other months. You could do some surfing here, there are boards for hire and trainers to teach you some basic stuff.

The route to the beach is lined with great restaurants which mostly have amazing sea food options, I would suggest not to invest on buying Gems here since I feel like its a bit over priced and commercial.

There aren't too many shops so its just perfect to stay in the area and completely enjoy all the time on the beach.

Title: Fantastic views
Text:
What a gem, more or less had the beach to ourselves. 
Long sandy and clean beach. 
Great sunsets from the loft bar. 
The sea is not for children in December, don't know about any other months but it's got large waves and strong changing currents.
The sea is warm and if you respect it you can have great fun in the waves but don't go in alone and don't go out of your depth. 
Sun lounger hire x2 with brolly 1000 rupees with a coconut or two thrown in.

Title: Excellent clean beach with warm waters.
Text: If you are a  sand and beach person, this is the ultimate it long ,sandy and curved,so go for it.The water is warm and clean.

Title: Beautiful Indian Ocean Views
Text: This is a fantastic secluded soft sand beach. Hardly any people on it during all hours of the day! The sunset views are amazing.

Title: Lovely and long
Text: A nice beach though there are some public areas where people have left rubbish though this is only minor point

Title: wonderful beach
Text: This beach is just amazing. It's massive and very wide ranged. Must visit for those coming to Sri Lanka. The sunset in this beach is a must see

Title: Beautiful beach but very limited facilities
Text:
I love a good walk on the beach and Bentota's beach is beautiful - long, wide and very clean. But once you've walked up and then walked back, that's just about all there is to do. There didn't appear to be any facilities directly on the beach. Nobody so much as offered us a sun bed or tried to sell us a meal or drinks. Most of the restaurants were in the hotels that line the beach and many had 'residents only' signs which didn't encourage us to visit.
Beautiful but such a shame there's not much there. We wondered if we were just too early in the season but were told that this is pretty much all there is.

Title: Wow, wow, wow!
Text: This beach is just amazing. It's massive and very wide ranged. The best of all: there are just a couple of people around as the access is not that easy to get. There are just two hotels located at the beach but it's granted a public access. So if you're around Bentota and looking for a good spot to enjoy sunset, just go to Bentota Beach.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
Beautiful beaches, THE most kindest people you will EVER meet. Stayed in Aayu's guest house which i can't recommend enough. Go to rohitha restaurant and Happy Garden for food. And if you manage to meet Sasindu the tuk tuk driver you have struck gold on your holiday [he has a purple tuk tuk and wears a Jamaican hat]! 
Enjoy...this is one beautiful place.

Title: Watch out for swindlers
Text:
Very nice beach. 
BUT watch for the guys located at the beach close to The Surf Hotel. They offer car sightseeing and fishing tours by boat. We had a nice experience with the car sightseeing - payed 7000 slr for a 7 hours tour to Galle. Two days later they offered us a three hours fishing tour without giving a price. We could pay what we wanted based on the tour experience. 
The trip was a disaster, run by two young teenagers. When we came back, the managers put a hard pressure on us to pay 100 US$ - or 17000 slr. I got angry and payed 5000 slr. 
My advice: Stay away from these swindlers!

Title: Nice beach to spend time
Text: From the Cinnamon Bay Hotel we can walk to the beach. You can swim and dip yourself for hours in the beaches. Some place are rocky and they also provide scooter ride for rentals,

Title: VR
Text:
Good and clean beach morning walk was nice but evening sunset excellent if sky is clear we loved that
Soft sand loved walking on it

Title: Quiet Beach, Not Windy, a peaceful place to relax
Text: Perfect beach, quiet and relaxing and not crowded. If you wish to spend long, lazy days, this is the place for you.

Title: Great beach
Text:
Soft sand warm sea and drinks at the bar .
Really good beach to sit swim or just chill .
Easy accessibility you aren't near

Title: Mrs
Text: We loved walking around the villages by the river . We saw some lovely Buddhist temples and met some charming locals . A cruise along the river is a must with guides pointing out birds , lizards , plants and monkeys . The trip through the mangroves was fantastic!!

Title: Cool relaxing and silent place
Text: Bentota beach is a long beach with both private and public access. The beach is along the bentota - Galle railway line and is a nice time to spend in evening, you can try the local food along the side and its a nice place to chill out and enjoy

Title: Awesome
Text: if you want to spend 2 o 3 in the beach, Bentota us the place! Gorgeous beach where to walk and excellents hotels on the shore

Title: BEAUTIFUL
Text: Bentota Beach is quiet, clean and beautiful and warm to swim in, no seaweed no rocks  just pure soft sand it was so nice loved it.

Title: Sun, Sand and Surf
Text: Beaches spread several kilometres south of Bentota. Beaches are clean, water clear and sand soft. Good place to learn surfing. The southern end of Bentota beach is home to top end luxury hotels, there are many home stays as well to suit the needs of a budget traveller.

Title: Lots of rubbish
Text: This could be a beautiful beach but it is very polluted. Such a shame. We went for a nice walk along the beach but I chose not to swim cos of all the litter. We swam at the hotel pool instead.

Title: Beautiful beach but where are we meant to swim!
Text:
It makes no sense. Round the world experts and I use the word expert very lightly have placed us in Bentota for 7 whole nights! Supposedly its a good idea because of the beach and so many amazing water sports on the beach. Well so far weve found we cannot swim on the beach due to very rough tides and jelly fish, there isnt any water sports on the beach, only the smelly lake and all they want to do is rip you off! £45 for 15 mins on a jet ski...really? Its £95 at home for 2 hours in the actual sea going around seeing caves and beautiful islands like Herm and Sark. 
Im totally upset that we have been left here for 7 days and have another 4 to go!
If anyone has any idea where we can swim on a clean decent part of the beach please let me know but I didnt pay for a month in Sri Lanka to sit around permanently, eating and being ripped off to look at nature, which should be free anyway! Not impressed with any of this place so far. Its completely over rated.
My teenagers spent most of the time on his phone and thats when we can even get reliable WiFi which is meant to be included everywhere you go! Really disappointing holiday all round. Dont come to Sri Lanka for more than 7-10 days and dont spend more than 2 nights in any place. Its the same thing in every place you go apart from Nuwara Eliyah which is very green and cold. Still the same activities everywhere you go. Pretty dull tbh. Go to Indonesia or Malaysia.

Title: Great beach, good for swimming.
Text: Good beach, almost empty. The waves are not strong as in other beaches. But if you are looking for touristic places as restaurant on the beach or bar, this not your place. It is pretty calm.

Title: Good beach
Text: Basically only thing in bentota is the beach. Its a good place just for one night and to relax. We stayed at the ekho surf its a fine resort but bit expensive.

Title: Really beautiful beach
Text: A really beautiful beach which is very clean and quiet. Very soft sand and a few miles long it is very quiet here and lovely to walk on or have a paddle. There were warning signs saying not to swim due to Jellyfish, Stingrays and strong riptides most people heeded the warnings so you only see one or two people swimming. Few beach boys selling trips, saris etc but all very pleasant and smiling and a polite no is enough for them to leave you alone

Title: beautiful beach
Text: One of the most stunning beaches we have ever visited. Simply stunning and so clean. The beach is very quiet but beware the waves in the Ocean as very strong.

Title: Nice & Clean
Text:
I went for early walks on the beach which was very good
Lots of people of all ages were walking and strolling.
I did not see any one swimming!

Title: Lovely Beach without the Crowds
Text:
There are lots of different parts to Bentota Beach, there is a stretch that has a lagoon on one side, then it sprawls down alongside the road, so there are lots of different places to get to it from.
Whichever you choose its almost deserted, or if not you wont need to search far to get a section to yourself, the sea can be rough but if you search there are little coves that are relatively guarded.

The northern area with the lagoon is very shallow and you can walk out quite a distance without any trouble but you still have to be careful of waves and currents dependant on time of year.

One of the better and quietest beaches we found.

Title: Clean water beach...
Text:
Our hotel The Surf was just on the beach
The beach is clean with clear blue water sea.
I had a swim too in the sea..
You can see a lot of joggers both in the morning and the evening. Saw coast guards meticulously monitoring the beach.
Very nice experience.

Title: One of the Best Beaches I've Been To
Text: The beach is absolutely stunning! Very long and broad strip of sand with warm and beautiful ocean on the one side and beautiful green trees on the other. The sand is very pleasant and silky. Lots of nice bars and cafes. Great and safe swimming in the ocean, if you are a good swimmer and not afraid of waves and currents. Magnificent sunsets and sunrises.

Title: Stunning beach
Text: Lovely sea bathing and wonderful sunsets. The Bentota beach rock cafe was  lovely and the food wonderful

Title: Perfection.....
Text:
Soft sands
Clear sea
Perfect sunbathing and relaxing environment 
Rates to hire sunbeds and parasols worked out about £5 per day
So far on our Sri Lanka tour this is definitely the best beach

Title: Must Visit Destination
Text: A beautiful beach town.. Its a must visit for any Srilanka trip. Do spend at least 2 days here. One can further travel to Mirissa and Galle from here, which offers scenic and pristine view of the ocean. Explore small cafes and organic food joints with panaromic view in the background..

Title: A HUGE AND BEAUTIFUL BEACH
Text: It is a beautiful beach, excellent place for long walks in the astonishing nature of the Indian Ocean.

Title: Beautiful ocean, wide beaches
Text: The Bentota Beach is a fabulous spot, only an hour away from Colombo if you take the Southern Expressway. Very family friendly beach, good surfing on one end, and wonderful swimming on the other end.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Beautiful beach and awesome views. Love the sunset in the evening. Have a great time there and love this beach

Title: Relaxing stay quiet with beautiful water
Text:
Lovely beaches ,quiet and peaceful. We did notice quite a lot of litter on beach on our morning walk which wS disappointing. 

Railway line runs along the coast.

Title: Paradise
Text: Bentota beach is the perfect place if you are looking for a quiet place. You can rent a sun bed and an umbrella for a few dollars. The beach is clean with warm water.

Title: Long fabulous beach with cafes and bars
Text: It was impossible to walk the full length of this wonderful beach. The surf is amazing - but it clams for swimming in the afternoons. Some days the water was positively too hot! Good range of cafes and bars and hotels. Very clean and no one hassling us to buy things

Title: Nice Beach experience
Text: Nice beach, well maintained shore, can get your drinks/food and enjoy grabbing them with the awesome beach view.

Title: Long empty beach
Text: Great for long walks, ball games, frisbee, sunbathing etc but not always ideal for swimming ... hotel staff warned of under currents and flags on beach stayed red all week. Not appropriate for small children unless are very closely supervised for shallow paddling.

Title: Beautiful beach
Text: A beautiful beach . We had a very nice walk along it. Locals friendly and nice with warm Sri Lanka welcome. Didnt go into water but looked crystal clear

Title: Best beach
Text:
Bentotata beach is one of the best beach of srilanka. You can spent quality time at this beach.
Viddyapati chaudhary
Lucknow India

Title: One of the best beach near to Colombo
Text: A popular beach, around 80 km from Colombo, is very clean, quite & ideal for swimming & beach activities. In particular,the beach in good resorts like Taj is ideal for family vacation.

Title: Family friendly beach - good swimming
Text: Not too crowded. Some sellers of sarongs etc but not too in your face. Great swimming. We rented 3 sunbeds and 2 umbrellas for 1500 LKR. The Beach Cafe is good too.

Title: Beautiful Beach
Text:
A really beautiful beach that never seemed to be crowded no matter what time of day I visited!
There is the occasional beach seller (who I did actually buy something from once) but if you ignore them they do leave you alone and won't hassle you :)

Stunning sunset to be had from here!

Title: Good for morning walk. Clean beatch.
Text:
Very clean atmosphere. Excellent for jogging and walk 
Can have bath too 
This way you can enjoy a lot

Title: Really nice beach
Text: Which has a lifeguard service. The surf was reasonably big and through my experience I could see that there was a strong undertow from left to right. I spoke to the lifeguards prior to entering the water and while I went swimming they watched me on the water's edge. That impressed me as their rescue equipment was prehistoric.

Title: Awesome
Text:
Must see if in Sri Lanka.  The evening sunset is just awesome.  
Check out Dhabba an Indian restaurant on the way to Kosgoda turtle hatchery.  Mouth watering food.

Title: Best Beach for Surfing.
Text: Learned Surfing from well trained staff. Many 5star resorts are nearby where you can stay and enjoy the water sports. Well connected through roads, railways, with 24x7 private taxis and tuk-tuk available.

Title: Nice clean beach
Text:
