Text: The beach is nice, lot of surfers and also a spot to swin with turtles. On the other hand sometimes hard to find a spot where to enter the beach if your hotel is on the street and no public showers or dustbins.

Title: Loved it so much we went back.
Text: We first stopped for a short time on a tour, but saw that it had a lot to offer so when we had a free day in Columbo we took the two hour train ride to Hikaduwa. (Don't get suckered in to first class like we did, go second. See my other review) the streets are full of shops, bars, restaurants and some street food. We felt adventurous, so got some bbq fish and chicken from a stall at the beach car park. Wow! It's local, authentic, which means the fish is roughly chopped bbq'd sauced and spiced, as is the chicken and served in a cardboard dish. Lots of meat on the fish. Beautiful. Ask for spicy otherwise it will be mild. On to the beach. All manner of water sports on offer; scuba, snorkelling, glass bottom boat, surfing hire, lessons. We just swam and snorkelled in the warm water. At the southern end of the beach large sea turtles are found while wading in the shallow reef. Not sure why they stay there, they don't seem distressed at all the people's attention. Beautiful to watch up close. Lots of coconut vendors and beachfront restaurants. We had lunch at "Parrots paradise" (see other review). Don't forget to have them open the nut after drinking to scrape the flesh.. yum. We also bought a small bottle of calypso white rum from a bottle shop, well worth it to top up the coconut.  Beach gets really hot in the middle of the day with not much shade around, so maybe a cafe, restaurant or bar. Morning, terrific. Great day was had. ??

Title: It was a fun trip to sri lanka went there to celebrate bachelorhood.place is nice quiet,cheap and green
Text: Hikkaduwa is a nice place to chill,its a beach destination. You can get amazing sea food there and few good clubs to party

Title: Must see and visit! Seaturtles all day long
Text: If you visit Sri Lanka, you have to visit this beach. It has seaturtles all day long. They are free, and you can feed then with tang. The sunset is marvellous like on the rest of Sri Lanka.

Title: Crashing waves
Text:
We visited here quite a number of times during our week long stay In Hikkaduwa. Whilst is very beautiful, there is a VERY strong current so beware if you are planning a swim in the water. There were lots of people in the water but it frightened me and I never went out of my depth. There were quite a few surfers and lots of places where you could hire snorkels, a boat trip, scuba lessons, etc. There were also a lot of people selling coconuts, pineapples and items of clothing. If you show the slightest interest in the clothing the ladies are very difficult to say no to if you dont agree on a price. I witnessed this with a chap who wasnt happy with the price and the lady was very dogged in her attempt to make a sale. If you say no straight away, they leave you alone. There are a lot of fish very close to the waters edge and some locals feed them and you can see them almost jumping out of the water to get the food. We also saw a turtle very close to the beach and lots of tourists crowding around it and touching it - please do not touch them if you are lucky enough to see one yourselves. 
On a downside, there is a lot of litter around the beach and around Hikkaduwa in general.

Title: Busy Beach with Turtles
Text:
Came to spend the day here as on our beach, Narigama Beach waves are too big for swimming. For us it was too busy but for the couple of hours we spent here swimming and watching the Turtles it was worth the effort.

Unlike Narigama there are loads of people trying to sell you things like clothes, coconuts ??, food, hits of snorkels or trips to other places etc etc. So if you like that sort of thing this would suit you.

Title: Turtle Ahoy!
Text: Oh my god I loved this beach. Fairly calm in terms of waves and you get to see Ridley Scotts and a lot of them! They just practically swam around us while we fed them seaweed. Experience never to be forgotten.

Title: Just relaxing
Text: My favorite place to forget about everything , best beach in sri lanka , amazing people , the best place to meet new people, night life there is amazing all clubs are amazing even staff amazing & friendly

Title: Clean, crowded, DON'T touch or feed the turtles.
Text: A clean, smallish beach, some good snorkeling spots, better further along than the main beach. Don't be tempted to touch or feed the turtles, they are wild animals and should be observed with awe and respect, rather than encouraged to feed close to the shore or used for shameless to Instagram self-promotion.

Title: Turtle heaven
Text: A nice beach but no sun loungers,parts are easy to paddle and walk into the sea,it can get quite busy and boats are coming and going.The best part is seeing the turtles that are in the shallow waters along the bend of the beach,they seem to be there most of the day though we were told its usually early morning then late afternoon.

Title: A bit crowded but still nice and clean beach
Text: We visited Hikkaduwa for a day and first we thought it was over crowded but when walking towards south it was more calm, water was clear and we even saw a big turtle. We really enjoyed Your choise beach restaurant with its ambience and nice service.

Title: Nice Beach
Text: This Beach was close enough to our Hotel Aditya ,and supposedly the Best Beach in the Area,so we spent the Afternoon there ,It was a weekend so the place was crowded & palapas were hard to come by,we managed to get one with a little extra cash . The place was crowded & only one restaurant to serve Food & drinks. One section of the Beach is filled with Fishing Boats. all in all nice to visit ONCE

Title: Best beach in the area
Text: It's definitely worth the way if you are looking for that Paradise beach experience. Actually, from Unawatuna center ist just 5 min of tuktuk and 10 min walking. You can do it! There is a great view on the galle bay, clear water, the beach kisses the jungle and palmtrees all around it. Not crowded at all and locals also like to go there a lot. Stop by at Agnus Villa next door for a sunset drink on the rooftop for the most amazing view you can imagine

Title: Too much pollution from the boats
Text: There is a beautiful view of the Galle city, a lovely bar, but if a boat will starts its engine to go to Galle, you cannot breathe.

Title: Nice beach
Text: This is a nice beach but not maintained properly.  The access to the beach is through a jungle. If some efforts can be taken this will become a awesome experience.

Title: To crowded
Text:
It could be a beautiful little beach with a stunning jungle walk to reach it, but once we arrived I was disappointed with how busy it was, theres was no room to lay on the beach, large crowds of tours and extremely loud. 
Not peaceful as I envisioned

Title: More Remote
Text: Smaller and more remote than the other beaches in the area  check it out for more private swim time (though avoid Saturdays when throngs of locals are likely to come).

Title: Dirty, crowded, terrible!
Text: Lots of people, lots of trash everywhere, noisy. Really not a place you want to spend your time at if you want to relax...

Title: Nice beach
Text: The beach itself is really nice and beautiful. But there is a lot of trash everywhere! We really couldn't understand the amount of emply water bottles and plastic bags. Way down from the road to the beach is a bit difficult, I had troubles with my flipflops.

Title: A beautiful and serene place.
Text: The view of the sea is fabulous. Shorts above the knee are not allowed. Although they give a piece of cloth to cover up. The drive up to this place is very nice. The various stages of Buddhas life are also well explained and shown. A must visit place if you are around Galle.

Title: Beautiful beach
Text: Short walk through the jungle to get there. It was busy when we arrived but its worth a visit. Water is calmer here than Dalawella beach so you can to for a swim.

Title: White sand, clear water
Text: There are guys selling cold beer and coconuts on the shore we loved this beach.  We stand up paddled here which was awesome, then snorkeled for a bit before having a cold beer and chilling on the sand, the beach it a popular attraction and it was pretty busy.

Title: Very dirty
Text: This beach is was the dirtiest beach Ive seen not only in Sri Lanka, but also in my all Asia trips Ive been making for 12 years. Even the view is veautiful at beach, we couldnt swim well because the water is rocky. Furthermore, you shoul climb too many steps to back from the beach. For me, you should skip this beach if you are into swimmable beaches.

Title: Nice secluded Beach with shadow
Text: The beach is kids friendly (opposite many other beaches nearby) but the down side is that its difficult to reach with small children. There are two bars at the beach.

Title: Pretty beach but do not visit on the weekend
Text: Very nice beach but on the weekend is crowded with locals so looks nothing like the pictures. We walked from Unawatuna beach via the Japanese Peace Pagoda which was a nice walk and then a tuk tuk back to Unawatuna.

Title: Natural Beauty
Text: Simply put,  a beautiful beach,  with beautiful views, nice bathing and stunning views,  with a great vibe.  Very clean,  although it takes a bit of effort to clamber down and then back up a rough pathway.

Title: Worth the effort
Text: We enjoyed the challenge of walking to jungle beach and climbing over the rocks.Once there it was a nice little bay to swim and relax.There is a stall selling drinks and beer and a resturant at the top if you want something to eat.

Title: Not my cup of tea
Text: I was a bit disappointed, the way down between the rocks looks pretty but needs to be careful, a lot of garbage on the way and on the beach, view is pretty basic. Only monkeys are cool :)

Title: Terrible and dirty
Text: terribly dirty beach with full of locals .Actually among the greatest beahes in Sri Lanka this one was the worst .the jungle road was even not the easiest to reach .doesnt worth an effort

Title: Cosy Unawatuna
Text: We went to Unawatuna for three days just to end our holidays on the beach. This was beginning of August. Everyone said that it was better not to go because of the raining seasin but we saw really a little bit of rain. Unawatuna is a niice place close to Galle where we went around the fort. We went around with bikes and made nice jungle walks to the beach where we visited some hidden temples. Beautiful! There is very cosy street where are some nice restaurants and little shops. We realy liked to stay there even when it was not the season to be there for surfing or diving.

Title: Sadly not worth to see
Text: Unfortunately was this beach full of trash and not really inviting to spend much time there! ?? really sorry to see such things happening to the nature!

Title: Two Jungle beaches next to each other
Text: Actually two beaches. The main larger Jungle beach is accessed by a steep in part, stepped in other parts, quite uneven rocky ground from the car park of the same name on the Rumasalla road. A good stretch of curving sandy beach with one beach bar with a few sunbeds. Busy on National Day with locals but quite quiet another. A very pretty cove with stunning water colour, good swimming with no waves. Around the coast, 200 metres of large rocks to clamber over is the smaller beach. Still very picturesque, just smaller. This can also be accessed from the car park on google maps next to the Peace Pagoda and has a less steep walk to it that the larger jungle beach.

Title: Lovely beach but not for those of us who are older as access is difficult
Text:
Jungle beach is rather pleasant once you get there.

Access is via a mountain path that is medium long, rocky and uneven and whilst the agile and fit can negotiate it with ease it is difficult for most of us over 70 - as I am.

There is a nice shack on the beach that serves decent food at reasonable prices.

The water is fresh and clear, the beach nice clean and good sand.

When it came to leave I was told that the easiest route was to walk along the sea path back to Unawatuna. I was also told it would take me 5-10 min.

How wrong was this info. I am sure a mountain goat could have negotiated the uneven and loose boulders far better than my arthritic sloth like agility, the boulders are rather hazardous but eventually you come to another beach. Then you have to climb back up the mountain !!

Bad choice should have gone up the way I went down.

However the beach is nice, what would be nice is a boat taxi running at regular intervals from Unawatuna to all these small beaches, when and if this occurs I will go back but until then leave it to those who are more agile.

Title: Quaint and lovely
Text: This place is incredible if you go on a Sunday, because it will be filled wiith local people who go to the sea with friends and family, so there is a charming atmosphere: many different people enjoying their incredible sea in a local way, which is the vibe I love to discover and join when I travel. The little bay is lovely, you can rent sunbeds and there is a small cafè that serves good food and cold drinks, beers and cocktails too, at honest price seen the place, that is very difficoult to reach. You will have to follow a steep path from the main road -where you leave your transport mean- down to the sea level and its not advisable for people who have a walking problem, beacuse its not paved and in some parts there are slippery passages on rocks. Coming up will be a bit heavy, but its surely worth the effort. Go and visit the nearby temple too, Peace Pagoda, bcause its very close and its a great place for the soul and for the landscapes you can enjoy from its first floor.

Title: Definitely visit!
Text: This beach requires you to walk through the jungle, hence the name, till you get to the beach. Go early so it's not too crowded, find a spot and relax. You can get food/drinks from the shack, swim, snorkel or just relax. Leave in time, going back up at sunset isn't the safest.

Title: Plastic Beach
Text: We were expecting a little bit more out of our visit to Jungle Beach in Unuwatuna. The beach is littered with plastic and debris left behind from mindless locals and tourists alike. It is unfortunate as the beach could be beautiful if cleaned up and maintained better.

Title: The secret beach, keep it that way !!
Text: We went to Jungle beach, both of them. Recommended in loney planet. But it is so dirty, nothing to see underwater and you dont even want to go into the water because there is so much plastic and face masks and everything in the water. Also on the beach as you can see on the pictures. The wild life seems to adapt a little ( se picture)

Title: Great setting - but I hope they clean it
Text:
The walk there is cool and should be combined with peace pagoda, then once there its really junglish and cool - but oh so dirty. No fun to swim with the dirt. 

Note that the bar on the beach is closed since covid and has been reclaimed by nature.

Title: I felt like I was in a James Bond film!
Text: This is how a beach should be... just so beautiful. The only thing I don't like is that you will go there and I am greedy and want it all to myself! :-)

Title: Dont Bother.
Text:
Completely overrated. View of the bay and port of Galle/factories in the distance.
far better beaches in SL

Title: Very relaxing beach ??
Text: This beach literally is between a jungle as shown in the picture, its very cool and relaxing but very crowded as you have to go so early if you want a good place sit, i recommend not to go in any weekend or local vacation to avoid crowding.

Title: Overrated
Text:
Went here as had read great TA reviews. 
Very crowded - Need to be there very early if you want a sun-bed. Small eatery which was ok (and who I think own the sun beds). 
To be honest we went to better beaches in the area. Wijaya was much nicer with lovely restaurant.

Title: Nothing special
Text: Less than expected. Nothing special. Better go to Mirissa and visit Secret beach, which is more spectacular.

Title: A must visit Beach
Text:
It takes quite an effort to reach here. You have to pass through a path full of rocks and greenery. So wear comfortable shoes if you are planning to visit this place.

The effort of reaching looks fruitful once you reach the beach. The water is crystal clear and its not much crowded.   A small beach but a must visit if you are visiting Galle or unnawatuna. We came here on a day trip from Bentota

Title: Amazing intact beach.
Text: Amazing intact beach. Problem with baby jelly stings. Nice fish appreciated when snorkeling. Coconut trees

Title: Relaxing beach
Text:
Yes, its is a bit of an adventure to reach (down a steep hill and series of stairs), but that kind of adds to the experience of discovering  Jungle Beach.

Apply lots of bug spray for the descent.

The beach itself is lovely, although you need to be wary of the sharp coral the has collected as you enter, and several large rocks not far from shore. 

The cove is protected, so the sea is quite calm, even as the tide comes in and churns it up a bit. The water is extremely warm and its relaxing just to float around and enjoy the quiet. 

We went on a Monday, which meant it was relatively uncrowded. 

Its just sad that many people have clearly disregarded the signs to not toss garbage. You can find trash and discarded food all around the edges of the beach.

Otherwise, its a wonderful spot.

Title: Lovely cove and snorkeling a bit cloudy
Text: We went her a couple of times. I liked the walk down the uneven path, through the trees with monkeys over head. Lots of locals come here and everyone smiles as you pass. Buy water at the top. Food on the beach is great, we shared a big plate of rice. Boys at the bar are fun. There is only a squat toilet and it dont smell too good. Lo gets they charge if your not eating. The water has rocks in the middle but you can have a lovely swim here and sit in the shade. We walked round to the next beach watching the locals having fun. Then up the hill to see the temple and could here the ship wreck.

Title: Secret beach
Text: Its a tough walk through jungle to get here but it is worth it. Nice little beach with a bar serving cocktails at a reasonable price. Its pretty popular beach with both locals and tourists

Title: Great beach and snorkelling
Text: This beach is great. The sea is lovely and calm and excellent for snorkelling.  It can get busy so best to arrive quite early. Beer, cocktails etc are available and snorkelling gear can be rented.  The neighbouring beach has sun lounges and kayaks for rent and you can order food. We preferred this one as it was less busy.

Title: Amazing restaurant
Text:
This restaurant for me is the best in Unawatuna!!  I came here last year and thoroughly enjoyed it.  I had chicken satay to start which was awesome then belly pork.  It was just fabulous.  I finished off with creme bruleu which was just out of this world.  It was for two people so my friend helped me, but unfortunately we couldnt finish it.  I wanted to take it back to Wales with me.  As its our last night in Unawatuna tonight we couldnt finish our holiday without returning this restaurant.  Who knows I might even try something else!!    Just fab. 

We tend to eat early and arrive at this restaurant about 6.45 which we were told to do as it gets extremely busy after that.  I believe it closes at 10pm anyway.  Sometimes they have to close the gate early as they have so man6 customers still arriving late.

Enjoy!!!    Well worth it

Title: Crowded but awesome
Text: overcrowded by locals.. but for a reason... because its an amazing beach with crystal water... We descended to the beach from the pagoda and went back up from the other end. Recommend to go snorkeling..!  One of the highlights in my December visit for sure...!

Title: Way to crowded
Text: So many people, not a secret spot anymore. Actually more locals than tourists but still only go if you want to have 'fun'. The nearby Japanese Peace Pagoda is well worth exploring.

Title: Serene
Text: Jungle beach was a wonderful experience. The short easy stroll down the mountain to the secluded beach. There are locals down on the beach where you can rent a day bed or get a cocktail or beer. There are quite a few monkeys to be seen as well. A very relaxing place

Title: Beautiful pristine beach
Text: This is a place which requires some effort to reach and probably that's why it is so clean and unspoilt. The water is clean and the waves are gentle so good for swimming and playing around. Just that since it is cut off from the town you would need to leave before it gets dark!

User_Location: New York, New York, United States
Title: Crowded
Text: Not worth the long sweaty track there. Super crowded beach. Much more beautiful beaches further south west in SL .

Title: Don't go!!!!!
Text: A beautiful but VERY small beach!! Don't go there. So many people, a lot of dead corals in the sand, two of us got hurt in our feets when going for a swim. Only one tiny restaurant, they had some sunbeds (very hard in wood) for free of if you ate there, otherwise they wanted 1500 for a bed!!! This is a really tourist trap! There are so many other beautiful beaches, like Habaraduwa for ex.

Title: Mediocre Beach Amongst Hidden Gems
Text:
Very average beach more akin to a dumping ground for locals and used as a rubbish dump!
Very disappointing how much rubbish is strewn about the trails down to this beach! I would be embarrassed as a local and representative of this area at the state!
Once you arrive at this beach it is decidedly average compared to some beautiful spots far easily accessed.

Title: Disappointing and underwhelming
Text: What could be a very nice secluded beach is effectively a beach with fair amount of rubbish every where . These gold really need to establish a proper rubbish disposal and collection

Title: Waist of time
Text: We walked here and the walk was nice, but I wouldnt go here for a day trip. Many locals love this beach, which makes it crowded.

Title: Walk to remember
Text: This was a nice morning walk in the jungle to reach the beach. The sea water just tempts you to jump in the ocean as it looks too good. It's a small easy trek which anyone can walk through. Do visit if you are close by

Title: Amazing Spot
Text: A little 20 min walk from Unawatuna brings you to this lovely beach with green calm waters and a very quiet atmosphere. There are two beaches with shade from the trees where you can swim, do snorkeling or only chill. Perfect for families with kids. Close to Jungle Beach is the Japanese Peace Pagoda a very beautiful spot to watch the sunset.

Title: Off the beaten track but worth it
Text:
We visited here by motorbike (it would be a good walk from Unawatuna and is bumpy road either way!) in the evening and it was lovely. The beach is small but was full of locals playing football and had a very fun vibe, and the swimming was good. Lovely views of Galle and the coastline, and also a great spot to watch the sunset if you walk up the path from where cars park.

Its near the Japanese Peace Pagoda so worth combining with a visit there.

Title: Beautiful beach
Text: We took a morning walk to Jungle Beach. We wore flip flops, which probably werent the most sensible footwear. Its a bit of a hike downhill, with rocks and bits of shaded jungle. It was a beautiful walk and the beach itself was very pretty. There was a lot of rubbish lying around, but it was lovely to swim in the sea and cool down after getting there. There are two small shops there with cold drinks and beers. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Good but a hustle with young kids
Text: Beautiful beach but takes damage on the kids and parents if you have to carry them down. Beach could also do with a cleaning as it is filthy..... the views however are fantastic

Title: Tropical beach
Text:
Nice beach with tricky access but need to clear rubbish problem.
Great sunsets where you can sip a cold drink,.

Title: Nice stroll to a little beach
Text: Jungle beach is about a 20 minute stroll from west Unawatuna. Its not at all a secret beach! Theres signs most of the way as well as opportunistic fruit and clothes sellers. Its a well trodden path to a small beach, that has nice shade, two beach bars and a restaurant on the east side. It has views to Galle and snorkelling opportunities. It has a good vibe and local teens like to swim and drum there.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: Small beach located near Unawatuna. Easy to access with bike. Right on the corner near the main road there is bike rental with good prices.

Title: Beautiful beach
Text: Jungle beach ist a must! It is not easy to get there as you have to walk down through the jungle but it is worth it!

Title: Beautiful local beach
Text: Its quite a little hike through the jungle down a path to a beautiful little local beach where youll find as many locals as you will tourists??Youre a few stand set up to sell food down at the bottom as well as drinks so you dont necessarily have to pack anything

Title: Best beach
Text: Overcrowded on weekends but must go place to visit !  Calm water, soft beach. Love this place! Some places rocky entrance in to the water, but wount make much of a problem. Moderate place for snorkeling. If u travel this part of the world u Must visit this place!

Title: A nice walk ,but trail littered with garbage
Text: It was a simple hike to Jungle beach. The beach itself is lovely but very busy with tourists and locals . The trail had lots of garbage , empty beer and booze bottles and cigarettes. Very disappointing!

Title: Nice getaway from The main beach
Text:
Calm water, decent snorkelling, monkeys can be seen sometimes. 
We went by scooter and got charged 100 lkr and were given a dodgy fake receipt. Not the end of the world but just ruins it that locals wanna make unfair money from tourists.

Title: Quite underwhelming!
Text: Came here on morning at around 9.30am and it was really quiet with 2 tourists taking a morning swim and a couple of locals. It's definitely not the easiest beach to walk down to - loose stones in the road towards the beach pathway and then the pathway itself would be quite challenging for some. I can confirm there were around two big piles of trash (water bottles, wrappers etc), which made the beach quite unappealing to swim in.  That said, it looks to be an enclosed and small beach, so may be great for families or those looking to escape the tourists.

Title: Nice beach
Text: Nice beach, challenging walk down though, not an easy climb down for those with small children or the elderly or those with mobility issues.  Good snorkelling. Very few sun beds available.

Title: Over crowded weekend
Text: Small dark beach would be nice if it would be less tourists. Lost of fish so great for snorkeling but looots of turists

Title: Snorkeling visit
Text:
Took a boat from Unawatuna to come here & snorkel 

The beach has a lot of people which kicks up the sands quite a lot impairing visibility.

Otherwise an okay place , safe since it's a lagoon providing decent snorkelling near the rocky shoreline adjacent to the beach.

Title: More a waste dump than a beach!!!
Text: For me it was the most horrible beach I have ever seen in my life! And I saw a lot of beaches in Asia. Waste everywhere. And all tourists are laying next to piles of rubbish as its a normal thing. We were shocked and left immediately. Not worth to go there!

Title: Tired accomodation but food fabulous
Text: The restaurant food for breakfast and dinner outstanding truly a delight but the accommodation even though the rooms are big was a let down. We stayed in a Jungle room with twin beds that were so rickety and noisy that made sleeping difficult. Also the step down to the bathroom at night was dangerous. The beach was beautiful and pool area reasonably maintained but needed work. On the whole would have been a fabulous experience if rooms and pool been up to scratch.

Title: Small and with a city view
Text:
Small beach near Galle, that despite some fame has nothing special. Not much sand where you can relax, the beach is not secluded and it has some boats even around it. Also it is a beach with a city view in a distance not exactly the palm tree you probably are looking for.

It has the reputation of the being one of best near Galle, but nothing special. You will find better places.

Title: Truly amazing
Text:
Beautiful secluded beach but a little tricky to get too

Steep climb down with stairs only part of the way

But worth it when u get there

Title: Nice little secluded beach
Text:
A small little downward hike about 10mins or so to this lovely little beach was well worth it.
Got here just before midday and was lucky enough to get 2 beach beds.
Wasnt as busy thankfully as Id expected from reading some of the reviews so had a great time.
Food on offer also..
Japanese pargoda temple about 15mins up across the rocks to your left and then up a steep incline. 
We did it in Flip flops no problem.

Title: Good but crowded
Text: Lovely spot when you get there and relatively small beach so can get crowded. Some shade near the trees to be shared with local dogs. Great for simple free snorkelling with loads of fish. Boats available if you are keener

Title: Beautiful
Text: Lovely little beach, bit of a trek to get down to from where the tutu drops you off, well worth a visit

Title: Picuresque beach
Text: Its a bit of a hike down and up in the heat but worth for the white sandy beach and azure water. A nice cafe on the beach. "Traditional" toilet...

Title: Crowds
Text: It sounds ideal, but as you come around the corner and are faced with the sight of hundreds of people and sellers and boats and stalls, the idyllic image quickly shatters. Its a 20-30 minute hot walk up and down to the beach from the streets of Unawatuna and its not worth it once you get there.

Title: Nice Hidden Beach
Text: I saw no hips of trash described; the beach itself is rocky and small, but you may enjoy its peaceful waters. Many locals swimming.

Title: Too much litter
Text: Jungle beach is very beautiful, but it's a shame visitors and locals throw trash everywhere. There is no proper trash can and it seems that nobody cares about environmental destruction.

Title: Visit Early and Beat the Crowds
Text:
We coupled a visit to Jungle Beach with an early morning start at the close by Japanese Peace Pagoda. We arrived at Jungle Beach at around 8:00am and had the beach to ourselves. Beautiful sands and waters. 

I can however imagine this place gets very busy after around 9:00am, we left when others started to arrive.

Title: Hidden Jem
Text: If you want a beach to your self here you go, wake up early and either trek or catch a ride to the Jungle beach, if you reach here by 7-8am the place is your, enjoy a morning dip, with no one in sight. Romantic, peaceful and relaxing. Must Visit!

Title: Average beach
Text: If you want to swim the waves might be an issue here but if you dont mind large waves when you go for a dip. Jungle beach is for you. There is a small bar where you can have a beer I would not go for any food there.

Title: Lovely beach
Text:
We loved it here.  The beach is great for swimming as its very sheltered.
There was no rubbish as suggested by previous posts, in fact a few chaps from the Sri Lankan Navy turned up in a boat to litter pick whilst we were there.  
There were a lot of local family enjoying the beach which was very nice to see.
We preferred it to Unawatuna beach which reminded me of Bournemouth, but with more bars!

Title: Nice beach
Text: This is a very pretty little beach off the beaten track. It is quite popular though, not so secret nowadays. They have a juice bar doing juices, milkshakes and cocktails. Walk to the beach is through the jungle - lovely. Nice place for a swim and relax.

Title: Beautiful beach
Text: Get there early as its small and starts to get busy later. Gorgeous beach to enjoy a coconut on. Steep hill to get there though. Right near the Japanese peace pagoda so you can combine the trip if its a tuktuk ride away for you

Title: Great secluded beach - go early morning
Text: Great little beach about 30 minute walk from Unawatuna. Did the walk in Jandals/slippers/thongs. Go very early in the morning as the crowds start coming in from 9am onwards.

Title: Lovley
Text: Relaxing, clean and peaceful. Bit of a trek to reach but worth the rock crossing. The second beach is the better of the two.

Title: poor beach
Text:
not worth it folks 
bit disappointed 
better elsewhere
long walk down to beach and not much room to put towel down

Title: Morning swim
Text:
Was really nice but super busy being a public holiday.
Trek down is a challenge with little kids and older parents

Title: Glad I visited...
Text: I'm glad we went, as the monkeys in the tree were cute.  The middle of the beach had rocks, so it was best to swim either end of the bay.  It was a trek down the hill to get there and there is only one restaurant and all the sunbeds were taken so we laid on the sand.  I liked it for a change, however we only visited the once.

Title: A lovely beach - best mid-week
Text:
This is a delightful beach in its own little cove.  It is nicely sheltered and offers reasonably good snorkelling very close-by the shore.  The fact that you have to walk a bit to get here is a big plus.

We came two days before Independence day, which was a Saturday, so it was probably one of the busiest days, which meant it was overcrowded.  There was also a disappointing amount of litter.

I feel that if you came mid-week and it was not a major national holiday, this place would be really special.

Title: Less populated beach
Text: It was worth the walk to get there - much more pleasant than the local beach which tended to be a bit dirty at low tide

Title: Nice
Text: Nice place, but way to beach is very difficult. No way to get there with some health problems. Water is ok for smsll kids, and adults can swim there too. Food there is tasty, and you have choices. The water was clean.

Title: Hidden gem in Unawatuna
Text: Just 7mins drive From Unawatuna beach .. this place was an absolute find.. parked our car on top of the hill.. walked down the walking trail..reached the beach.. absolutely stunning clean water.. very few people .. perfect relaxation in d wAters..

Title: Sort of secluded beach away from all the traffic noises of Galle.
Text: Limited shops, but it is sort of near a jungle. A few steps to get in here but nice place to visit if you are able bodied. Shady walk in, tuk tuks avail to take you out and I guess, we walked from the Unawatuna past the Japanese peace pagoda along the rocks to get in. A bit challenging but ok if you are steady on your feet. We all need a bit of exercise when we are on holiday.

Title: Jungle beach
Text:
It's secluded beach.to get to it you have to cross lot of jungle and then you come to nice beach don't worry if the trek is too much you can either take tuk tuk or drink coconut for 20 pence 
There is a nice buddist temple donated by japan so all in all enjoyable day 
I would recommend

Title: Dirty
Text: Visited jungle beach on a recommendation from a friend and was severely disappointed there was rubbish everywhere and people urinating in the bushes it really isn't worth the hassle to get there.

Title: White jungle beach is better
Text: Visit white jungle beach first, it is bigger and less crowded than jungle beach. Worth the walk but is small and crowded.

Title: Pleasant beach midweek
Text: I would advise visiting here midweek as at the weekend apparently it gets packed with locals and there is high volumes of litter. They do a clean up Mondays and when we went on a Tuesday it was lovely and peaceful and has a small bar where you can order some juice, lion beer and other soft drinks with a small good menu. The water is calm here so it makes it easy to go swimming.

Title: Nice beach
Text:
A secluded beach in Unawatuna. Need to take a tuk tuk or a bike. The path to this is uneven. But the views from the beach is worth the walk. 

Try to visit early mornings to beat the heat

Title: Jungle beach - Disappointing
Text:
I had only heard great things about jungle beach so decided it was definitely worth a visit.

I walked there from Unawatuna and was glad I'd read reviews on here describing how to get there because it is not really signposted until you are almost there. 

I enjoyed the walk and locals were helpful in pointing me in the right direction. Don't expect an easy stroll - it is quite a trek on uneven and narrow trails with large rocks. However, you may be lucky to see monitor lizards, peacocks and other animals along the way like I did. 

When I got to the beach I was quite disappointed - maybe it was the time of year but the water was rough and dirty, the sands were littered with rubbish and debris. My belief that I could snorkel in tranquil waters and see lots of beautiful fish was instantly killed. In the 5 mins I tried to go into the water, I got scratched quite badly by rocks you cannot see through the murky waters.  Even when I tried to go into the water further up the beach, I quickly got out again due to the amount of rubbish wrapping itself around my legs. Such a shame - but I bet the waters are calmer, clearer and the beach cleaner at high season in Summer.

At least I saw a huge monitor lizard - that was really cool.

Title: Beautiful!
Text: Jungle Beach, Unawatuna - We visited having read about it in the Lonely Planet guise. Bit of a trek to get to but well worth it! Not a large place but it wasnt crowded either when my family visited in August. Cold soft drinks sold on the beach which was a welcomed sight!

Title: Fancy a short trek that leads you to the beach? Recommend the Jungle Beach Trek
Text:
Jungle Beach is really a short walk from Unawatuna (about 40-60 min) through the jungle then climb down to the beach that is secluded and overlooks Galle.

First came here over 3 years ago and it felt more exciting back then as it really was like a trek in the jungle but this time, felt that Unawatuna in general and the walk to Jungle Beach was now becoming more built up and busy. The walk passes through dozens and dozens of hotels and B&B's and it is likely to be more crowded and busy once the monstrosity of a hotel is built in the Unawatuna beach! So better get here quick before it loses its charm.
The positives is that because the area still belongs to the Dept of Wildlife, they have stopped or done away with the previous make-shift restaurants that were right by the beach at Jungle Beach.
It seems to be more of a place where a lot of locals come in for a day/weekend trip. Since we went there on a Sunday, it was very busy. Also a tad noisy but everyone seemed to be having a good time. 
You can swim here too but the sea is now seems to be littered.
Strangely though the walk from Unawatuna and though the jungle seemed clean and came across only a few discarded PET bottles.
The climb is only slightly difficult but recommend shoes unless you are a flip-flop pro in which case you can still easily do the climb up and down unless you are unlucky to do the trek on a rainy day.
Make sure to take lots of water though, as it is humid.
There are a few restaurants around in the vicinity before you climb down to the beach that offers local food for good prices. We didn't have lunch there, so no idea how the food was.
If you don't fancy eating after the walk, you can always a grab a bite to eat once you get to Dalewala road which has all the touristy shops/restaurants.

Title: Pretty
Text: I went here with some friends on a very hot day. It was full of people and its not a very big beach. There is a bit of a hike down to the beach so make sure that you have some good shoes. Also, the monkeys are not nice. Remember that for everywhere really. Inside the water, there is a lot of dead coral and its not the softest sand. Maybe some water shoes are your best bet for this beach.

Title: Great place for swimming
Text: Great place for swimming since there arent waves that would make it dangerous. We went there on Sunday and there were many locals playing ball and singing.

Title: No longer secluded
Text: While the boom in tourism is great for Sri Lanka it means previously secluded or quiet places like Jungle Beach are no longer off the beaten path or a secret. When we visited there were at least 100 people in the first small beach. Also filthy with rubbish.

Title: Spoilt by litter & Russians
Text:
Lovely beach accessible by a bit of a climb down a rocky path. Little shack on the beach who have sunbeds if you buy food/drink from them. 

Sadly lots of litter on and around the beach and in the water. Not idyllic crystal clear water for sure which is a shame. 

On our visit, lots of noisy Russians who decided it was ok to play their crap Euro pop at full volume from a portable speaker. Oddly the men spend a lot of time taking photos of their wives/girlfriends in various soft porn style poses. 

Maybe we where unlucky but as in Thailand it is better if you can find the places the Russians haven't.

Title: Beautiful by Night!
Text: Like an undiscovered Beach! I went there to see sunset and fullmoon. So romantic and beautiful!!!!!!

Title: Take your trash!
Text: It is sad, such a awesome place. Swimming with turtles, but sharing the experience with loads of plastic. Don't be a   muppet, clean your filth.

Title: Beautiful but crowded
Text:
Beautiful place to visit. Walking through the jungle next to the temple walk down to the beach only sad thing about this place it was not clean too many disposed plastic :( 
best for nature lovers and to do snorkelling  on the way you will see monkeys ??????????

Title: Dont waste your time here
Text:
The walk to this beach was full of rubbish. Distressing. The place is filthy and full of people drinking and with loud music. There is NO snorkling to be done. On leaving we decided to tale a tuk tuk and they are slmost mafia like. We eventually called a pick me car for a third of the price and the tuk tuk drivers ganged up on the driver when he arrived, stole his keys from the ignition and used a police like batton to hit him.
Dont bother going here

Title: Great spot for snorkelling
Text: Enjoyed a snorkel off the rocks and spent quite a lot of time watching sizeable puffer fish in action! Took my wife and daughter and felt safe as not a fast current...

Title: Upps
Text: What to write about this beautiful place. Full of garbage and people. It is truly a jungle beach, but i do not have the urge to pay a second visit to this place. There are much nicer beaches in south coast of SL

Title: Litter let it down!
Text: As much as I thought it was a beautiful spot, tourists (and possibly locals) have let it down by leaving litter behind on the beach. I feel the lack of bins hasnt helped this, but its still everyones responsibility to clean up after themselves.

Title: Quite a trek
Text: Think this beach is more for young fit people as it was a quite a trek to get there.it is aptly named as you had to go through a mini jungle to get to it.

Title: Best beach near Unawatuna
Text: A short ride by tuc tuc and you reach this little gorgeous beach. Calm, a restaurant snd some sun chakra.

Title: Good beach for swimming and snorkling
Text:
Flat beach with calm waves..found it peaceful n could easily spend couple of hrs swimming n snorkeling in the clear water.
The walking route to beach via jungle is great experience as well. Its a short walk though.

Title: Too crowded and many jellyfish
Text: This place is way too crowded with people for a very small beach. Also, there's jellyfish in the water.

Title: Better than the main beach
Text: There were two separate small beatches, which were both very nice. Its a bit far from the unawatuna beach. Most people go there by tuk tuk, but its also possible to walk there, if you like a bit of an exercise.

Title: Jungle Beach(Exotic Beach)
Text:
One of the pure exotic beaches in galle.
We have to take a short trip around 800 meters downwards to reach the beach.
It will be like a mini trekking experience with the path is very uneven till 300 meters. 
And  we have a steep downward path will be very hard for the children and older adults.
After the 300 meters of intense step path there are steps leading to the beach.
One of the exotic peaceful beaches in Galle or Srilanka. 
It will be good experience for kids and couples to spend time here.

Title: Really worth a visit
Text:
The perfect beach.Safe swimming with life gards.Stayed all after noon.
Ideal for adults and children.

Title: Ok beach. Nothing special. Quite dirty.
Text: A lovely walk down to the beach, quite steep and slippery so definitely dont wear flip flops.....you need comfy shoes! Went down to the beach where there are two huts for drinks and also sun loungers but the beach is very dirty. Broken glass in the sand, a lot of rubbish and shells everywhere. We walked down for a visit but didnt stay. Visit unawatuna beach for a more relaxing, clean beach.

Title: Scenic beach and surrounds
Text: Nice walk over the hill from Unawatuna. Be sure to get some photos of the peace pagoda and the shipwreck on your way to the beach. The ship wreck is located on the rocks between jungle beach and Unawatuna. The beach itself is split in two and either are good for a swim or snorkel. The coral is bleached but still plenty of colourful fish and the water is clean

Title: Relaxing
Text: Take the tome and enjoy a short walk down to the beach. While there is coral in the water it is still a lovely setting looking back to Galle fort. Lots of vegetation behind and the opportunity to have a cocktail and some food is an option.

Title: great beach
Text: Amazing beach.way better than Unawatuna.great guys working at the bar on the beach.you can have drinks and dinner there.well worth it.tuk tuk from Una around 400 ruppies (don't pay more)

Title: Nice view but no clean water.
Text:
We need trek down to reach this beach. Quite secluded. Eye catching water color. They even have tier swing.The view is really good. 
The beach restaurant people annoy you at times. The beach is not that clean.

Title: Beautiful sunny afternoon
Text: Upon reaching the parking area, visitors would need to hike down for about 10-20minutes, depending on your age and fitness level. Word of caution to families travelling with young children and the elderly, as there are some rather steep drops and slippery corners to get to the beach. Hence it is recommended to wear good shoes. The beach was a beautiful blue?? Glimpses of tiny, transluscent fishes swimming all about the water. Plenty of shade around to set up a picnic basket. Once done dipping, shower areas and changing rooms are available at a reasonable price back at the parking area. We truly enjoyed this experience with 2 elderly ladies and 3 young children in tow and highly recommend it!

Title: Cozy gem
Text:
Its a cool little place and I tucked away down a small path. 
Theres also a bar so you will not be thirsty here :) its a small beach with nice water.
Very chilled vibe

Title: Beautiful quite beach
Text: Great little isolated beach over looking a big town. Nice clear water and friendly and helpful locals. Only minus was the rubbish dumped on the track down to the beach.

Title: Rustic Fun
Text:
Its like stepping back in time. Rustic but free sunlounges, good fun local people.

This is a great beach which gets a lot of visitors from all over the world. Plus a great place to Meet friendly locals. Its a bit of a trek up and down, so if you are in fit give it a miss. Otherwise you should give it a go.

Title: Hidden beach
Text:
Nice little beach hidden from the roads.
You go to the top of a hill and from there you walk down through jungle to the hidden beach.

There you can find a beach bar and some sun beds.

Title: One of the most beautiful beaches in Sri Lanka
Text: We went in the morning during the week and there were only two other people there. Was calm, secluded and beautiful. Worth the walk down and probably the nicest calmest beach we visited in Sri Lanka, Apparently it gets very busy with locals on the weekend though.

Title: Nice but nothing from another planet
Text:
Jungle Beach is nice, small and more private, with vegetation growing almost right to the sea. 
There is a bar and you can rent canoes or do a boat ride.
It's very popular amongst locals and tourists.
It's ok but under that name I would have expected something more "wild", not so crowded and with not so many activities to join...
The way from the main road is long but easy, just the first part of Rumassala Road is quite steep and the last meters in the path out of stones and roots you need to watch out, but all in all is easy to get there.

Title: Hidden beach
Text:
Although a good tuk tuk ride away from main city center but worth the effort .. a short hike through the forest takes u to this small but beautiful beach with calm water .. there is one shack for coc
ktails and place to have a nice swim .  Sea can be rough at Unawatuna beach so for swimming this can be a better option.. be aware no life guard and can be real isolated at times .

Title: 'Waste' of time....
Text: Dont bother going. There are much better beaches. Its dirty, has no appeal and therefore a waste of time.

Title: Pretty Beach
Text:
A pretty beach a 30 - 40 minute walk from the middle of Unawatuna. Some steep hills. I think it is possible to go some of the way in a tuk tuk but you have to walk the last bit.

Jungle Beach is a small pretty beach with gentle lapping waves. The only thing there is a chap selling fruit smoothies freshly made and another lady was selling cokes and other soft drinks.

Nice beach to pass a bit of time on. We thought there would be some snorkelling opportunities but there wasnt.

Title: Junk beach
Text: Jungle beach should be renamed Junk beach. The beach is completely covered in rubbish and is a disgrace. Do not waste your time going down there.

Title: Nice
Text: We enjoyed a few hours here. It's definitely not as good as the reviews say as it's hard to get to and there isn't much beach. So check it out but it's definitely not a full day trip. Certainly don't go out of your way to see it .

Title: Wow beat beach in the southern coast
Text: Anyway who loves sun and the sand will admire this place its one of the safest and nicest beaches in unawatuna

Title: Nice day at the 'beach
Text: We had a lovely time at this beach.  The walk down was neat with the stone steps.  Restaurant was perfect for a fish lunch and several beers.  We went during the day and in June.  We did not experience any of the harassment described by the other reviewers.  There were boys playing frisbee on the beach and my boys took part. It was really enjoyable to see the blend of cultures.

Title: Nice place to visit with kids.
Text: The walk down to jungle beach is awesome. Great scenery, shallows for snorkelling and swimming. No corals near the shore.enjoying the sunny afternoon.Will be a nice hangout place for an nice evening.

Title: Small Beach
Text: Just a small beach near the Galle Fort about 5km with Tuk tuk. It is hidden small beach but it is nothing very special comparing with all other beaches in Sri Lanka.

Title: Great View
Text:
Small Beach with a nice view. Had to climb down to reach the beach. took about 10 minutes. 
The view is nice. With greeneries on both sides. 

Good place for a drink or two.

Title: Interesting walk down to beach
Text: Great little secret tucked away. We had a good walk down to the beach. Be sure to wear suitable footwear (sneakers are fine, flip flops would be difficult). Lots of locals there playing their own instruments which was fun. I wish there was someone selling beers there though! The Jungle Beach Inn (not on beach) wasnt open either.

Title: Unsafe
Text: Beach was okay but the way is terrible especially with children. Have to take an auto to reach to the hill than have to go for off road walk for 15 to 20 minuets to reach the beach. Auto driver's ask a lot for ride. Hanuman temple and Buddha temple are also there on the hill. It's totally a skip able place.

Title: Not really worth the walk
Text:
Better beaches with less effort 
Its quiet but there are no services on beach so I would say you are better going east towards thalpe where the beaches off the road are amazing .

Title: Overcrowed, dirty, smelly & full of trash!
Text:
We went during the public holidays so it was so busy with lots of noise, people & trash everywhere. There was so many public buses that was taking everyone there knocking anyone & any other vehicle off the roads.
The poor monkeys was eating plastic bags full of peoples trash that they all carelessly chuck aside. 
Disgusting seeing what could of been a beautiful spot completely ruined.

Title: Idyllic and Quiet
Text: An idyllic and quiet spot about 20 minutes from Galle Fort. 500 Rupees in a Tuk Tuk. Then a 200mtr walk through lush rain forest down to  a secluded beach. Get there early to secure a wooden Deck Chair,say 9:30am. Beach bar serves cocktails, spirits and beer and some meals.

Title: Cool and lovely
Text: 25 min by walk from Unawatuna and down the road you can meet monkeys and vaarans. The beach is 'movie-style'. No sunbeds but you can easily hide from the sun under the trees. Warm and quiet sea that is good for kids and for swimming. You can snorkle and see some fishes next to the stones of your right hands. And i strongly recommend to try mojito and pina colada with only people who serve it by the ground boat. The best in Una!

Title: Crowded and dirty
Text: The beach is very small and while visiting we noticed a big commotion in one of the small areas. It was monkeys eating all the trash gathered on the side of the beach! There are a few small carts selling coconuts, water and juice but then there is no place to throw the trash out so its gathered on the side. Dalawella beach was much better, even the main Unawatuna beach is cleaner and in my opinion, nicer to stay at.

Title: Fun beach!
Text: We made the mistake of getting here close to sunset. There's a 10 minute walk to through the trees to get to the beach. It's not at all lit up so make sure you have a torch of some kind on you. It can be a bit slippery and there are a lot of mosquitoes so take your repellent! The beach was nice, buzzing with locals, music, families and we enjoyed ourselves.

Title: Not great
Text: You can take a tuk tuk but we walked. It was super crowded and not very big. Not worth the trek at all. There are quite a few monkeys though.

Title: Amazing
Text: For us, the place was a bit crowded. We went on a Saturday and beside tourists, a lot of local people came. But it is amazing there. You have to walk down a jungle until you reach the beach. Water was very clear, sand very clean... paradise indeed

Title: Crowded and quite small
Text: Cannot say that I am amazed by this beach, as it is quite small and crowded. It must have been a lonely place some time ago, but surely not now.

Title: Should have listened. Proceed with caution.
Text: I should have listened to what I read. I should. That is the reason for this site. Despite, I read the reviews and I plodded on, misguidedly shunning the information I had read. Scootering up the hill from the Galle Road, caught up in a fracas between the private blue coaches, belching diesel fumes, and ferocious tuk tuk drivers who seem to think they are in the cast of wacky races and far more aggressive, thankfully with each other as opposed to the fat westerner on his borrowed moped. Reaching the top, we park, we walk, down down down the litter strewn Hill, over cobbles and past other weary travelers and locals making their way back up. We arrive, and what a load of rubbish. Literally, a load of rubbish. The beach itself, I imagine could be quite nice, but yet again the human race has let itself down, and ruined a place that could be so beautiful. If you go, expect to feel sad. I did.

Title: Trashy Beach
Text: The beach is very unclean and trashy. There are lots of plastic in the sea and also in the beach and the jungle. I ordered bottle of coke from jungle beach bar and it was warm not cool. The beach could be nice if trash and plastic cleaned out of the beach.

Title: Beach time
Text:
Good sandy beach protected by the bay. 

The local municipality needs to provide some bins to collect the plastic.There is a risk that this amazing beach could become another rubbish dump

Title: Busy but good for a visit
Text: We walked here from our accommodation in Unawatuna beach, there were helpful direction signs to assist us finding the beach. As it was a Saturday the beach was busy but not too crowded. Nice for a swim and no currents in the water

Title: The water is full of litter
Text:
We walked from Unawatuna beach area and it took about 30 mins, a bit of a bush track towards the end. 

We were there on a Saturday and Poya (full moon) so there was many locals. The water has a lot of litter so wasnt pleasant for swimming and limited beach area. Stick to Unawatuna beach for a swim. The walk was pleasant enough.

Title: Just Not Good
Text: Visited on a Sunday afternoon and never have I seen so much fresh litter across one beach! The beach was packed with locals enjoying the sun, but seemingly unable to clean up after themselves. Its a 10 minute hike down the beach and not at all worth it.

Title: Not worth it
Text: Its a long and arduous hike from Unawatuna, and when you get there, it's small, a bit crowded, with one stall selling drinks. It's also not very clean, with plastic bottles and rubbish all over the place

Title: Beautifull beach
Text: This is really beautifull beach. The sea is not rough in January and you can swim. You can also drink good coctail

Title: Beautiful little hideaway
Text: Take the time to navigate the rocky pathway down to Jungle Beach - totally worth it. The beach is clean and calm (we found maybe ten people lolling about), the water is swimmable, there's a small cafe if you need one, and it's all in all a bit of a hidden treasure.

Title: Come on SrI Lankan government
Text: A beautiful beach with delightful walk through the jungle which is being spoilt by rubbish - plastic , glass etc. One visitor cut his foot so badly on a broken bottle in the water requiring hospital and stitches. Take care !

Title: Nice beach, but dirty
Text: Jungle beach is a beautiful secluded beach in Galle bay. Sorrounded by palm trees and jungle, it takes a nice hike to reach it. The main problem it faces is that the sea currents bring trash from the bay and as a result jungle beach is dirty despite the efforts to burn the trash.

Title: Small beach
Text: Small beach with a small «restaurant». We did not dare to eat there as they do not have electricity. Lots of trash in the water and the woods. Other than that; a quiet beach.

Title: Disgusting
Text: Was the dirtiest beach that we have ever encountered . It was even worse than any Indonesian beaches that we have been to . Such a shame as it could be such a wonderful place.

Title: Not worth it
Text: Disappointing place as both the way thereto and the water are full of litter.... I can imagine the charm when discovered for first time but not such a natural place anymore. mihirripena is much more scenic and the unawatuna more pleasant...can be skipped without missing much..

Title: Best Part is Walking There
Text: The best part of Jungle Beach is the walk to get there - very quaint and scenic.  You are truly walking through jungle to get to the beach.  Other beaches are much nicer, beach wise, but this is an interesting and different hike if you are so inclined.  I hope that they clean it up...

Title: An absolute gem (but ruined by rubbish)
Text:
We stumbled across this incredible beach by chance. Its beautiful.

Then why the 3 stars? Its unfortunately littered with rubbish around the shoreline. We hope this is attended to as it is starting to now wash into the water.

We will change our review to 5 stars should this be fixed

Title: Very green, quite quiet
Text: Not easy to access but worth the short hike for a beautiful beach, with locals instead of tourists. Lovely to see pineapple and palm trees whilst swimming too.

Title: Difficult to get to
Text: Had to trek through jungle with few directions to get to this beach. It started to rain as well. This beach is popular with young local Sri Lankans.

Title: Local secluded beach on the edge of jungle
Text: The beach can be reached after a 30' min walk from Unawatuna through jungle, which is quite an experience itself. Jungle beach is a secluded place frequented mainly by locals, which makes its specific charm and authenticity. Worth a visit, especially as a counterbalance, if you are based in tourist-packed Unawatuna.

Title: Dirty beach with rubbish everywhere
Text: We did the hike to jungle beach yesterday and astonished at the amount of rubbish there was scattered everywhere along the way and when we got there. We were completely disappointed by the beach and literally stayed to swim for about 15 mins then headed back to unawatuna. It's really not what it's cracked up to be but has probably been ruined over time - such a shame!

Title: Paradise lost!
Text:
Im sure this small beach was once very lovely. It is now ruined. There is a large pile of plastic and rubbish about 50m from the beach entrance (and a lot more on the walk through the jungle and at the main road). There is a huge amount of plastic and rubbish in the sea - you get plastic bags wrapped around your legs when you swim. Its depressing and a bit disgusting. 
Admittedly it might have been the conditions on the day so I spoke
To the beach bar owner who said shops and people all along the coast are dumping trash into the sea and it winds up on Jungle Beach when the conditions are right, and nobody will help to clean it up.
I would avoid this place completely - the tiny beaches around the fort are cleaner and less depressing

Title: Nice place
Text: It is worth visiting these beaches and its surroundings. Beautiful view, and the path to the beach is already an adventure.

Title: Rubbish tip
Text:
I've visited Sri Lanka three times over the recent years and always make a visit to jungle beach. This time I was shocked and saddened to see how much rubbish and plastic were left on the beach. The locals who work at the beach bar must do something urgently to prevent these plastic bottles and other items from entering the water. 

I've added photos to show the rubbish tip on jungle beach. This tip was found at the far side of the beach, opposite the beach bar and sun lounges.

Furthermore the swimming experience at jungle beach was awful. I stepped on and swam through heaps of plastic bags. The worst part is that I spied a small turtle swimming through this too.

Unfortunately it's been raining and storming a lot in galle over past days so plastic from the beach is no doubt being pushed and blown into the waters. Me and my boyfriend tried to take as much rubbish as we could back up with us but there's still tons down there. The locals and tourists who enjoy this beach must be more waste aware and not dispose of their rubbish so carelessly.

I would like to add photos however the file sizes are too large and trip advisor only allows 5mb photo uploads.

Title: Fun trek to reach the beach.
Text:
Started off from Unawatuna beach and passed by a village along the way. Managed to find an old lady selling chilled, fresh coconuts along the way and had a fun conversation. 

No problems finding the beach there were signs and a well-trodden path when the tarmac gave way to dirt. 

Theres a small stall selling fresh fruits and drinks there so one should be well-taken care of.

However, Tuk-Tuks will be hard to find at the beachs entrance so you will have to walk out a little bit before you can find one (assuming that you do not want to walk back to your accommodation after a day of chilling by the water).

Title: Not too good to swim
Text:
Very good for a nice pic. 
But it's better to go to unawatuna if you want to go in the water. This beach has a lot of rocks

Title: Enjoyed
Text: I visited the beach in the first week of August, found it quiet and very beautiful but was rough for the swim. I enjoyed went down through the jungle and stairs to reach the beach.

Title: Quiet beautiful beach
Text: A secluded beach, with snorkeling and just a few vendors. Definitely worth a visiting if you have some time in Unawatuna

Title: Far away and not equipped
Text:
Yes, it is really detached. If this is most important to you, go on.
On the other hand, you have to go uphill, then downhill by forest path, and the beach is not equipped with showers or umbrellas, only a few sunbeds and single (a sort of) bar with some drinks of questionable quality.

Title: Nothing special
Text: Just a small beach with lots of palm trees around. Would've enjoyed it if it wasn't for lots of rubbish around.

Title: The name makes sense
Text:
My husband and I visited today, I obviously expected there so be some aspect of jungle to this place. However I didnt anticipate, when putting my sanders on that morning, that I would quite literally be hiking through a jungle to get down to it! The hike isnt a strenuous one as such but certainly I wouldnt recommend it to anyone with any mobility issues or anyone prone to falls/being off balance. Especially after a rain storm it can be quite slippery. 

The beach itself is beautiful and quaint, clean sand, blue sea, a little beach shack and a few sun loungers for chilling. 

My only criticism is the trash littering the beach, this place could really do with someone taking down a role of trash bags and doing a clean up mission!! Had I known this before I would have done so myself!! But beautiful for relaxing. 

1 piece of advise: dont play with the dog, he got quite nippy and over excited. A rabies jab is not what you want from your trip to jungle beach.

Title: Average at the moment
Text:
Walk to jungle beach is nice, but the beach are pretty messy at the moment with choppy waves, not the best swimming spot for the off season. My tip would be to stay East! Wish we did. 
Also, lots of rubbish on the second beach! Never very tempting

Title: Cosy little hideaway
Text: A 10min trek down a jungle slope (stairs) and you reach a little strip of beach. Soft sand and great waters. There are loungers on the beach that are free, and there is one small bar that serves alcohol and food. Probabky best to bring your own watee and snacks though. Definitely worth a visit! Tuk tuks at the jungle entrance ready to take you back to your hotel.

Title: It's more about the Jungle and less about the Beach
Text:
We were disappointed as we wanted to enjoy the sea and a nice beach on our last day in Sri Lanka. But we had to walk a lot in the jungle and when we finally got to the beach, it wasn't what we expected - rocks & waves. We had a child with us and we understood people recommend that beach for kids also - I still don't understand why.

I recommend Wijaya instead :) 
The day before we got to enjoy swimming with giant turtles in Wijaya.

Title: Public beaches are not maintained.
Text: As a result, they are polluted with plastics and flotsam. Coarse sand/fine gravel is uncomfortable to walk on. The shoreline often slopes rapidly to the sea, which is prone to large waves and undercurrents. Not recommended for very young and/or weak swimmers.

Title: Obly clean in front of Royal Palms and Tangerine
Text:
In front of the two hotels Royal Palms Beach and Tangerine, the beach is properly clean. North of these hotels, very dirty and no cleaning whatsoever it seems.

Kalutara administration has a huge potential for improvement if they are really keen on attracting tourists.

Title: Walk
Text: The beach is in a poor  and neglected state. Only good for walks nothing  else. Its better to look for other better beaches around.

Title: A lovely peaceful holiday
Text:
I found the hotel to be friendly and there was nothing that was to much trouble. 
The room was immaculate everyday and comfortable.  The view was stunning  from the room and my favourite part of the day was watching the sun go down from the balcony. 
The food was superb.. I especially enjoyed my egg hoppers in the morning ... the chefs do a wonderful job and I had no complaints about choice ... the traditional food was wonderful also. 
The bar staff were always happy to speak with you and were very accommodating letting my husband watch cricket .. there was plenty of tea and coffee available which I enjoyed as I cant drink beer 24/7
My highest praise goes to the lovely  pool guys . I have arthritis and struggle shifting sunbeds , every day they made sure I was ok and had a sun bed and plenty of shade .. I cant thank them enough.. 
Our rep Nigel was very informative and sorted out a great trip for us .
The only reason it didn't get the full 5 stars was continually being pestered on the beach .. my husband could cope with the banter but it got draining by the second week and it's not nice to be stared at when all you want to do is get some peace looking at the sea .. I do understand they have to make a living..
Thank you for a lovely stay

Title: North Kalutara Beach
Text: Lovely beach but not excellent - very strong waves and currents at different times of the day - red flags used when its not safe. Steep drop off at the waters edge and then a sand bar for about 15m. By the water the beach is sloped and not flat - there is a flat sandy area further back from the waterfront.

Title: Sunrise and Sunset View
Text: The beach is very nice and clean with loads of sea shells in the sand. There are big stones near the beach which makes it very interesting to watch while high tide. The best view is during sunrise and sunset. If you are staying in Anantara or Avani hotel at Kaluthara, you can enjoy their private Kaluthara beach. Must go beach if you love to relax.

Title: Interesting, both ?????? bathing and fishing boats
Text: sparse with people as there are not so many hotels along the beaches.  In the morning you see the fishermen coming in from the sea and you meet some cows that seem to stay close at night.

Title: A good place to wander about
Text: Long, reasonably clean and empty. A few colourful fishing boats to photograph and the occasional place for light refreshment - Sri Lankan style

Title: Nice walk
Text: Nice sandy beach to walk on. Not too bothered by hawkers who tend to congregate around the entrances to the hotels.

Title: Beach under renovation
Text: Problems caused by the sea earlier on so now putting in retaining wall to stop anymore erosion. Beautiful sunsets ??

Title: Vet clean and amazing sunset
Text: Very clean beach with amazing sunsets and lots of shells to collect and find - near the Avani and Anantara hotel and lots of Cafe outlets off the beach as well

Title: Beautiful beach but beware of the undertow!
Text: A beautiful beach that offers miles of golden sand. Near the hotels you can find restaurants but you can be bothered by beach sellers and guides offering tours. Be polte but firm and they'll leave you alone. A nice beach for sunbathing if that's your thing but you would need to be a really good swimmer to swim there. Large waves that break noisily onto a steeply shelving shore means that you'll need to shout to make yourself heard. If you venture into the water when the surf's up,make sure you're with someone because the undertow is evil and will take you right off your feet in a surprisingly shallow amount of water.

Title: Long Stretch
Text: We stayed at the Mermaid Hotel and from our room beach looked lovely. On our first walk in morning going south we found beach hard going for walking, its tilts too unevenly so you are walking lob sided we found, also with this being a fishing town quite a bit of diesel spillage and other rubbish along the way. Next walk we went in opposite direction and found the same. Hotel Mermaid cleans the beach right outside but obviously not the full stretch

Title: Stunning!
Text:
Beautiful Kalutara beach. 
Very clean and well kept. It was a pleasure to watch the early Fishermen in the morning pull up there boats on this lovely beach. 
Lots of local sellers directly outside hotel on the beach selling beautiful Sri Lankan beach wraparounds. 
Stunning place to just sit and think and watch the roller waves wash in.

Title: Narrow beach
Text: Nice sandy beach but very narrow  no sunbeds allowed on beach or chairs sea very tough large waves  good evening stroll

Title: Beautiful, but be aware
Text:
Long beautiful almost deserted beach lined with palm trees. How come you are all alone most of the time? Because the water is not safe to swim in, so be aware of high waves and strong currents.
Well worth a stroll anyway and you can get your feet wet and still be safe. But I would not recommend swiming for everyone, only strong swimmers. Definately not for small children.

Title: Nice and clean...
Text: Its a nice and clean beach and one can easily walk barefoot on the fine sand...Although the waves were very tricky during our visit, it was still worthwhile..

Title: Angry waves
Text: Lovely scenery, beautiful sand but even as a good swimmer, I did not dare swim in the water, the waves were too rough!

Title: Smooth white sand...
Text: Stayed at Tangerine Hotel - just a few meters walk to shore - wonderful waves and great beach! Life guards are on duty - the sea is suitable for swimmers..

Title: Not the Best for swimming
Text:
Best time to stroll along this beach is early morning when there are not the local people trying to sell you something, 
Tide and undercurrent make it not the safest of places for swimming.

Title: Peaceful Beach
Text: The beach is not that crowded, it is clean and peaceful. If you are in this area it is worth a visit.

Title: Disappointing
Text: The beach looks ok from a distance, but it is not sandy, it is rough grit and not clean with dog excrement, litter and worse still broken glass.  Shoes are definitely required for any strolls on the beach.

Title: polluted beach
Text: Here are photos of the beach outside Tangerine resort today. it has been like this since we arrived on Sunday.

Title: great beach sadley under used
Text: Butifull unmolested beach great for a stroll ,my Wife and I used to go down there for a swim everyday the sea can get rough so be aware of this.some litter scattered about which should be cleaned up.

Title: Beach Hotel
Text: It was brilliant just sitting eating your meal looking out at the beachfront when we was on our way to the hotel from the airport was a elephant just walking at the side of the road it was amazing.

Title: Lovely long beach
Text: Great for walking this stretch of coast. Sea can be rough and there is a rip currant. Red flags are often used.

Title: beautiful to look at....
Text: ...but dangerous to swim in  The waves was fare to high when we was there but to walk along the beach is amazing

Title: Nice to walk along at sunset
Text: Very soft sand that you sink into, good fun watching all the crabs fly out in front of you and run for the sea. Lots of people selling goods and tours but all are polite and not pushy.

Title: Good Beach
Text: Hotel Avani had private beach. Enjoyed morning walk and sunset . Although steep but fully secure for quick swim

Title: great for nice long walks  sea was a bit rough but expected at this time of year
Text: lovely beach and lovely local people to chat to   water was a bit rough at this time of year but was expected

Title: Nice clean beach
Text: Though it is a nice and clean beach but is very dangerous for swim. Just next to our resort, it was good for morning walk.

Title: Broken sea shells
Text: the beach looks lovely. it can be a little hard to walk on because it is all broken sea shells .Disappointed  that we could not swim in the sea. Red flag was flying all the time. We went in September, which is not the summer period, so may be a little less calmer in the main season.

Title: A clean and quite beach dotted with some water sport activities and restro!
Text:
A clean and neat beach, with space to enjoy without being bothered. 
The place is good for families and couples and was quite safe when we travelled.
The best part was there was no littering of any kind

Title: Beach near our hotel
Text: Very steep there was no way I would swim in this sea too rough and a steep ledge which would be a risk for anyone with a mobility issue.

Title: Great Beach Rough Sea.
Text: The beach on this side of the island is all you would want if the sea was calmer.  During our two weeks the red flag flew every day . Dont risk it

Title: Not a beach to spend too much time on
Text: Maybe it was a bad time of the year but this beach was not impressive. It was dirty and left untended by the abutting hotels, bars, commercial enterprises, etc. It could be so much nicer.

Title: Kalutara beach Shri Lanka
Text: I happened stay @ Royal coco resort for two days during my Shri Lanka travel in April 2017 Since the resort is lactated in the vicinity of Kalutara Beach ,I took a round of the beach both in the evening and night for two days continuously. The tourists  from the European countries were found to enjoy uncrowded beach.There are some restaurants serving sea food on the bank but thy are under thatched roof and attract a few tourists Massage centers are not in a good ambiance so I avoided visiting it.There are some beautiful trees and overall the beach is clean I would rate it as a reasonably good place to visit during travel to Shri Lanka. That does not mean one should go there specially.It could be included in the itinerary

Title: Golden Beach!
Text: Unfortunayely I was in low season, so, I could not manage to swim in the ocean, but loved walking barefoot on golden sands... It's fantastic!

Title: out of season it was awful
Text: We were there in low season and the beach was awful and dangerous. It was hard to imagine in high season it would be much better.

Title: Poor
Text: The coast is not good to visit even for a walk.Not a place to stop.Not a tourist attraction. Drive further South for  better beaches.

Title: Beautiful deserted beach
Text: The beach is not safe so swimming so the best thing about this lovely beach is that there r few tourists on sun beds it is just a fabulous deserted beach.

Title: Fantastic place
Text: Had  great  stay  and enjoyed  alot.. The  place  is very  good. The view  from the room  is great..Clean beach with always  safe guard ??.

Title: trip to yala national reserve
Text: what a great place to visit. saw 2 panthers, 2 bears, ,crocks, wild boar, troops of monkeys and numbers of. birds and small animals. However when we were there the Elephants went on holiday. others saw elephants on the days they went to visit however they never saw the panthers and bears. It looks like luck is the decider. LOVED it

Title: Beach
Text: Sea was very rough could not go swimming.sand is quite coarse . There were women there trying to sell dresses and a couple of beggars on beach

Title: Holiday Beach Time
Text: Our hotel was alongside Kalutara Beach and we went out onto it most days. The beach was quite clean compared to some I have seen in the Far East - only the odd bit of litter. The sea does look rough and appears to be deep but there is a shelf and once you have  crossed that it becomes very shallow.
