Text: We just hired one of the guys with a boat waiting on the bank of the lake. He took us all around the lake and was knowledgable about the wildlife and plants. Engine was quite noisy but he would turn it off and let us soak in the tranquility. Definitely worth doing.

Title: Beatiful tank
Text:
Take some time to try to spot birds and other wildlife. 
The terrace at Oak Ray lake resort is the perfect spot to do so.

Title: Beautiful lake with plenty of birds
Text: We just passed by the lake on a stroll one late afternoon, and were stunned by the beauty. There were pelicans, bee eaters and Kingfishers along with many other species. It was really a very nice Place for a stroll.

Title: Highly recommend boat safari for sunset and bird watching
Text: We went for a boat safari with Malaka the boatman. He is very knowledgeable on the type of birds and showed us a huge variety. The sunset views are also stunning. Highly recommend this.

Title: The lake
Text: It would have been nice to have been able to walk around this lake a bit.  It looks really pretty but they were doing construction so we couldn't go.

Title: Picturesque lake
Text: It's very pleasant to walk around the lake. The southern shore of the lake is especially picturesque. It's also interesting to see local bathe in the waters. Take this route when heading to Yatala Wehera from the city centre. There are also trees on the western shore with thousands of fruit bats roosting in the day.

Title: just OK
Text: The lake has a charm of its own. however, this really needs to be pepped up by the tourism dept since it is not visited because visitors just see The yala sanctuary and drive off. They need to propagate it and make it a tourist spot.

Title: A Must Do when in Tissa
Text: My partner and I took the boat ride just before sunset, and it was worth the 1,000 Rupees per pax we paid. We had a very friendly boat man who provided us with a brief on the birds that inhabited the lake. He brought us to the mini-island on the lake, as well as the area where all the black-headed ibises nested. He also pointed out to us the mass migration of bats from the padi fields to the lake area at sunset. The entire boat ride was an hour plus and the sights were priceless!

Title: Lovely evening on the Lake
Text: You can take boat trips on this lake, I arranged mine with a local fisherman (Nuwan), who sells fish besides where the safari drivers congregate. I arranged a price - 2500 rupees ( £12.50) for about 1.5 hours and a day and time of departure ( 4.30 pm). This is a lovely trip to take particularly if you are into wildlife and birds in particular, however the sunset views are just stunning as well, the added attraction is all the egrets coming into the trees to roost, making them look as if they are covered in large white petals, and the hundred and hundreds of bats ( large fruit bats) flying across the lake at dusk on there way to there feeding grounds.

Title: stuning view
Text: its a gorgeous lake and with stunning view superb. we had a long wall around the lake its was really awesome.

Title: Nice walk
Text:
Lots of birds to see as well as water buffalo. You can take a boat ride for 1000rps per person.

We walked up Wellawaya Rd as well to Debarawewa Lake which is also lovely.

The best part is just after you've turned onto Wellawaya Rd, there are 1000s of fruit bats hanging from the trees, at night they fly off over Tissa Lake.

Title: Best guide in Tissamahara
Text:
We have been in Tissamahara as a stopover between Unawatuna and Ella. We did not really know what to do and had to leave the other day very early to get the bus to Ella. Coincidentally when walking around we met Mr. Denzil. Normally I was annoyed of all these Tuk Tuk drivers that want to bring you somewhere but he was totally different. I instantly felt that for him it is not about money but about showing foreigners the beauty of his country and he totally did. He made our day! Without him the stay in Tissamaharama would have been nothing special but he definitely made it to one of the best days of the whole trip. He took us in his tuk tuk to see many different birds, buffalos, nice nature and above all these amazing trees full of bats. I have never seen something like this before. We also visited the temple with him. If you are interested, he will tell you everything about Buddhism!
Afterwards we decided to go to Ella with him instead of taking the bus and we did not regret it. We saw wild animals on the way, even elephants on the street close to Yala! He is a really warm, sincere and lovely person and we are happy that we met him!

Title: Gorgeous landscaping
Text: We did a walk near the lake on one evening and it was an amazing feeling. The walk stretches about 3kms and myself and my friends did the whole walk.

Title: don't miss the bats
Text: Lovely place to stroll around in the evening. Dont miss the hundreds of fruit bats that live in the trees. Ask the locals where they are.

Title: wonderful sunrise/sunset
Text: fantastic views at Sunrise and sunset, especially for nature lovers. boatrides during the day are nice; a lot of people swim or fish in this wewa. Also you can walk along the footpath, mostly in the shade of the trees. In the water you can find waterhyacinths, lillies, lotusflowers...

Title: Wonderfully beautiful and marvellous bird life
Text: The Tissa Wewa or lagoon is absolutely beautiful and if you are lucky enough to be staying in the vicinity do see it at varying times of the day. It has glorious light at sunrise, is lovely in the full sun of the day and has a really lovely appearance at sunset when the colours are reflected in the water. One of the great attractions of the place is seeing birds flying into the trees in the late afternoon to roost for the night. Generally bird life in this area is spectacular. You will also enjoy thousands of bats hanging in the trees near to the water. Overall this is a very special place and well worth exploring.

Title: loved the lake
Text: beautiful, real Sri Lanka... worth a walk around...dont just nip and out for a visit to Yala.. more to do !

Title: Great for a evening boatride
Text:
We did half a hour boat ride ,our boat driver spoke a bit of English so of not much help. 
Overall good sightings of birds in the island.
The sunset bought alive the bats flying of the tree and was spectacular.
Recommend a half hour ride at sunset .

Title: Nico to take the road east of the lake
Text: We rented a scooter and tried to drive around the lake. We went counter clockwise from the south of the lake, where the sidewalk is. You will pass a lot of guesthouses at first, but later come to a less explored area with farmers and cute houses (and lot's of hidden poverty). It's not possible to go around because the roas is blocked, but it's a nice sidestep from what everybody else sees at the lake.

Title: Bats and birds
Text: Go the far end (from the town) at about 5.30pm and watch the birds come back to roost for the night and the thousands of large fruit bats head out for the night. It is simply spectacular.

Title: Wildlife haven and spectacle
Text:
We visited Tissa reservoir, which is one of five in the area, a number of times during our three night stay in the area. It has an abundance of wildlife including the globally threatened Spot-billed Pelican and Watercock. We also saw three species of Bittern (Yellow, Black and Cinnamon). We also found a pair of Greater Painted Snipe on the north west corner, a difficult bird to find anywhere in its African and Asian distribution. 

Also along the western edge of Tissa Reservoir are heronries comprising a number of species. Some trees at dusk can resemble British Magnolia trees (whilst actually being the roost of mainly Cattle Egrets). 

The most spectacular sight for us was seeing the many thousands of Giant Fruit Bats leaving their roost at dusk and flying past an illuminated temple through our telescope.

Title: Beautiful
Text: We had a hotel next to lake. It was really beautiful in the eveings. We did every evening a walk there with the hotels dog. Was really nice :) Also you can see there a lot of birds and some other animals.

Title: Beautiful lake in Tissa
Text: We hired bikes and had a lovely cycle around Tissa, including cycling alongside this beautiful lake. We also passed input a number of times during our day at Yala and other excursions in the area. Well worth seeing whilst in Tissa.

Title: Stunning views!
Text: The best part of Tissamaharama is the lake, the paths around it and the views. I enjoyed every minute of this surreal place!

Title: Nice views
Text: We took an evening stroll along part of the Tissa Wewa, beautiful expanse of water, used by the locals for bathing in parts and many species of birds and Im sure other wildlife!

Title: Nice lake
Text: Very nice lake situated near Tissa and many locals coming to here for bathing. Many different kind birds specially fruit bats too..

Title: Cool environment
Text: Nice cool breeze environment around the Tissa Wewa. Quite a place to have lunch with a families or friends.

Title: Nice view
Text: This lake is a nice view and traditionally pilgrims used to be refresh before go to worship Kataragama temple. its so crowed in most of Holidays and  lost of local groups gather around  this. its not recommend for bath at all.

Title: Nice place
Text: it is a very beautiful place to visit.lots of lotus flowers in the lake.people can bath and swim in their. i swim too . but it is a very deep lake. when you swimming make sure not to go to deep area.

Title: Refreshing
Text: This is a nice and huge lake, surrounded by some settlements, greeneries and nature. Nice road around the part of lake to go around - cycling around in the evening was lovely, when I also saw some people were fishing. Its really refreshing with cool breeze and greeneries around.

Title: Serenity!
Text: Tissa Wewa (Tissa Tank), a huge man-made lake about 1.5km from the town center. In the evening, check out the huge flocks of egrets that descend onto the trees around the lake to roost. The road along the southern edge has a wide new Lakeside Walkway for strolling. You can even buy Dhal wade, fresh water fish bites, manioc chips from the wayside carts.

Title: Swimming in the Tissa lake was refreshing
Text: It was 40 degrees in Tissa so we decided to swim in the lake with the locals to cool off. Yes, there are crocodiles but we decided to inside the main group of 50 locals. I could taste the soap as the locals bath there every day. Our guide Rehun from 'why not getaway' tours  jumped in too and played tag with our children (aged 11 and 12) in-between the locals, who looked on amused. He thought New Zealanders were more adventurous.

Title: Stunning
Text: We went for a little walk around Tissa through the town and then out here  stunning place, especially the photographs.

Title: Artificial Reservoir
Text:
Tissa Wewa is actually an artificial reservoir, thought to have been constructed in the 3rd Century BC, either by Mahanaga of Ruhuna or his successor Yatala Tissa of Ruhuna. It was constructed to irrigate paddy lands and supply water to the flourishing city of Tissamaharama.

Apparently, the lake was restored in 1871 by the British to provide shade. It is definitely a good walk to take some pictures, go for a morning walk and do some picnics.

Title: Spectacular bird watching
Text: Pelican, spoonbill, pied kingfisher were the most remarkable of the birds we saw at Tissa Wewa. Pied Kingfisher was in full action diving into the lake several times for his catch. Lovely place to picnic.

Title: Better lakes elsewhere in Sri Lanka
Text: We had a short walk here one evening. Not a lot to do, just walk around the edge of the man-made lake. Lots of stray dogs around and heavy traffic. There are much better lakes in Sri Lanka to walk beside and look for wildlife. Wouldn't recommend.

Title: Clam and Beautiful Lake
Text:
Tissa Wewa is a large beautiful Lake. We were staying in a hotel which was at the Bank of Lake. Clean water and many birds on the middle Island makes you feel fresh.
Boating is available on the Lake and They also take you to Crocodile Safari.

Title: Picturesque
Text:
the lake is picturesque has crocs and buffalos and other wildlife in it. Check out the locals swimming even though there are crocodiles.
There is nothing else to do in Tissa other than go to the lake and use it as a base for the Yala safari.

Title: A vast lake
Text: Actually the lake was the backdrop for our hotel and we had to go just beside the lake to reach our hotel. A very calm and vast water body with variety of birds chirping around the lake in the morning

Title: Sunset boat trip.
Text: Lovely hour long boat trip around the lake just before sunset.  Saw many bird varieties, huge fruit bats and crocodiles. Lovely to walk around as well.

Title: Wildlife plus local's bathing
Text:
This is a pretty large lake. I was pleasantly surprised by its cleanliness, some rubbish around but not so bad.
There are lily pads and grasses growing in the lake and lots of fish and birds. We also saw a few terrapins swimming around and were told there are crocodiles too. 
This fact doesn't deter the locals from using the lake as a laundry, bath, swimming pool and general meeting place. 
We saw a lovely sunset over the lake and I caught a few fish on my travel rod much to the intrigue of the locals.

Title: Stunning view in a tranquil afternoon!
Text: I visited Tissa Lake on my way to Yala. The lake is really wide and water is so pure that you can even see fish swimming under you foot! The view is awesome for photography and walking along the lakeside. The sky is always bright which makes the view so picturesque! This place is highly recommend if you love lakes or ponds, like me :)

Title: Nice place!
Text: Nice for a walk or run in the morning before safari. Vast lake not far from city centre (10 min walk)

Title: Stunning Views at Sunset
Text: The highlight for us in Tissa.  Lots of birdlife. Plan to visit at sunset and take a leisurely walk along the lake.

Title: Beautiful sunset
Text: We had intended just walking around Tissa Wewa in the early evening but decided at the last minute to take a boat ride instead. We had a young Sri Lankan lad drive the boat, he also pointed out birds and was very sympathetic to maintaining the calm and quiet atmosphere by cutting the engine and allowing us to hear as well as see the birds. He was not a skilled ornithologist but had learnt a lot and was enthusiastic about what he saw. We had a lovely sunset and on the return saw hundreds of fruit bats.

Title: Beautiful lake, great for walking
Text: Take the time to walk next to this lake in nice weather, or during sunset. Its beautiful and a great experience.

Title: just beautiful
Text: it's one of the most beautifl places we visited in Sri lanka. you will see lots birds and even bats in this area. sunset is unforgetable too.

Title: Bundala with Ceylon Safari Tours
Text: Today we had another safari with Ceylon Safari Tours but this time we were off to Bundala with Chamara again. We had the same prompt pick up in the jeep just for the two of us. After Yala yesterday's Safari which is manic with many vehicles. Bundala  is the total opposite with only a few vehicles a day and the whole tour taken at a more leisurely pace. Another bonus is that you also get a park ranger to accompany you within the jeep and his name was Randika which means we had two experienced knowledgeable guides spotting the beautiful birds. We had a wonderful experience and spotted many birds and a couple of wild animals (elephants and crocodiles). The tour included a picnic spot in an absolutely beautiful spot on the coastline before we carried on with the tour. A wonderful trip made special with Chamara and Randika , many thanks to them both for a highly recommendable trip.

Title: Nice boot tour
Text:
Nice boot tour. Many different birds. Crocodiles. Friendly People.

Surprise as the road is relatively close

Title: A pleasant walk
Text: We had a pleasant walk by the tank in the early evening. It was amazing to see the bats on the move as night fell. Earlier we had seen a host of water birds including kingfishers, egrets and cormorants. It would be helpful if more of the lights worked along the promenade.

Title: Calm, peaceful, birds and bats
Text: We so much enjoyed returning to Tissa Wewa after a year of absence. The lake, an artificial reservoir has a long history dating to the 3rd century BCE when it was constructed to irrigate paddy fields. Today one can walk alongside the beautiful lake and see numerous birds and bat colonies. Early evening is a great time to be there when the birds are flying to their roosting areas. The whole lake has an atmosphere of peace and tranquility.

Title: Bats and birds
Text: Wonderful bird and bat viewing, friendly locals to help you with the timing and viewing. Pleasant natural environment.

Title: DIY-Safari
Text: It's great to go there in the early morning or late afternoon, because you will see a lot of wildlife. Birds, fruit bats and loads of monkeys are just close by the road. Grab a bicycle or a scooter and just drive around for your Do-It-Yourself-Safari. On our search for birds we took a small dirt road to nowhere and met a really nice family who invited us to their house for fruits and drinks. Awesome place!

Title: Amazing Boat RIde
Text: We went for a walk and we were able to get a boat ride. It was thrilling to go in the boat. The riders helped us to pluck some flowers too. It was awesome!

Title: Lake
Text: This is a beautiful lake on the Kataragama  Yala road.A pretty lake This lake is used to irrigate agricultural land.

Title: Not to be missed!
Text:
We were walking along the lakeside in the evening and were approached by one of the boatmen offering a boat ride for Rs1,000 per adult (free for kids). I was sceptical at first but our son insisted - mainly because of the birds that could be seen at the lakeside. 

I am glad we relented. The 1-hour trip was amazing. The boatman brought us to see colonies of cormorants and ibises nesting in the trees on the "bird island", and got so close that we could see hatchlings in some of the nests. We also got close to egrets perched on wading buffaloes.

The best parts were boating through a vast expanse of lotus flowers and watching thousands of bats and birds "changing shifts" in the dying light, with pink and orange streaks in the sky.

We did not plan for the boat ride but it turned out to be one of the best things we did in our Sri Lanka trip - minus the crowd.

Title: 'Hidden gem'
Text: The owner of our guesthouse recommended this place. It was truly gorgeous and really calm. A lot of birds to see, and a few crocodiles.

Title: Ask locals about the exact time when the bats fly away from the trees at sunset
Text: Probably the main reason or the biggest reason for you stopping by, if you consider doing that, will be to see a lot of bats sleeping on the trees at the lake and flying away as the sunset comes. Ask locals about the exact time when they go for that so you don't miss an opportunity to see something interesting that you don't often have a chance to see.

Title: Bats!
Text: Ask any tuk tuk driver to take you to the bat trees for 6.30pm. It's amazing. All the (10,000) fruit bat's fly out for the night. I felt like Sir David Attenborough should of been stood behind me! My pic doesn't do it justice!

Title: Very Pretty Lake
Text: This lake built during the kings era is one of the most beautiful lakes I have seen. You can go on boat rides to visit the trees with bats.

Title: water reservoir
Text: Beautiful scenery. Wish we had time to explore the area more. The view of the Tissa Maharamaya Dagoba is stunning. The Dagoba and Wewa(tank or reservoir) Built by the people in the 3rd Century Before Christ is impressive, even though the wewa nor the dagoba are not the oldest in the area.

Title: Watch birds from the rooftop terrace of the rain tree hotel
Text: I would highly recommend the "the rain tree hotel"  for the "free bird watching show" on their roof top terrace.  It is truly amazing to watch all the birds fly back to their sleeping trees and then see the fruit bats fly out into the dark- abolute recommendation!

Title: Tissa Wewa, Tissamaharama
Text: Tissa Wewa is one of the attraction place in Sri Lanka. Tissa Lake was constructed long time back and it is an artifical reservior. It cater to the needs of farmers in that area to irrigate paddy throughout the year. It also fulfills requirement of water to the people of that area.

Title: Accessible  Wetlands and free
Text:
The wetland fringes of the lake are full of fantastic birds easily viewed from the path . I was amazed to get clear views ,  photos and videos of 3 different Bitterns : Black , Yellow and Cinammon . This last bird is scarce and hard to see . Upali my very experienced guide had never had such good sighting . Other birds include : Stork-billed and White-breasted Kingfishers , Small Minivet , Jerdons Leafbird , and Common Iora . 
 The following morning we bordée an area between the lake and a nearby stream and found other new birds : Jungle Owlet , Brown Fish-Owl , White-rumpled Munia , White-naped Yellow Woodpecker and the endemic Sri Lankan Red-backed Woodpecker  . 
  This is a very rewarding birdwatching area very close to the town and it is free. You can spend many fruitful hours here in between visiting the more famous sites .

Title: Thissa Lake
Text: Great for a stroll along the walk around the lake and watch for all the different types of water birds. Or maybe you could take in a boat ride or peddle yourself around in a swan peddle boat.

Title: Beautiful like with amazing birdlife!
Text: We took a very cheap 1h boat tour and saw plenty of birds, bats and buffalos. You take a ride in the middle of lotus flours and get the chance to see the locals swimming and playing and then there is more than 20 species of birds to find! Not to miss, definitely!

Title: Good sun set and Bat tour
Text: We took a boat and went to the bat island. and saw a bird island too. good for photographs and a good guide from the hotel we stayed in.

Title: Evening boat trip
Text: We went out on an evening boat trip arranged by our hotel and it was well worthwhile. The lake was so tranquil covered in lotus leaves and flowers, loads of birds and no tourists!! We saw lots of huge pelicans roosting in the Rain tress and a huge colony of fruit bats awaking from their slumber! we even saw a few crocodiles too but that didn't seem to worry the kids splashing around!! This is a very beautiful and peaceful lake and worth the boat trip and also hire some bikes to ride around it!

Title: So large
Text: This is a beautiful lake, so large and photographic.   There were some lovely areas with water lillies and also area were the local kids were having fun in the water.

Title: Mister Denzil and the Bats
Text: This man knows almost everything about Tissamaharama,Budhism and the birds arround Tissa Wewa. We had the great oppurtunity to meet him and decided to tour arround with him - how lucky we were with his informations and places we stopped. I only can tell with my heart! He is such a great man - do not to miss a chance to travel with Mister Denzil - 0094 077 5300942

Title: Quaint with Clean Water
Text: This place is popular with both the locals with foreigners. The water is clean and suitable to have fun. The area is beautiful and serene too. Worth a visit.

Title: Very pretty lake at sunset
Text: Perfect for an evening stroll before your early morning game drive in one of the parks.  Loved all the birds flying in to nest on the tree in the middle island.  Lovely scenic countryside surrounds with rice paddys.

Title: Serene
Text: The serenity of this reservoir is heightened against the sky. There is little to spot in the water but the surrounding countryside is a photo opportunity.

Title: Gorgeous Lake
Text: Its a gorgeous lake, so calm and serene dotted with huge trees and greenery all around. It has a lovely promenade to walk, broad and clean. The promenade has cute tables and chairs for a lovely picnic lunch. Definitely recommend to spend an evening at Tissa Lake

Title: best place in tissa
Text: its was my fav place in tissa. i spent an entire afternoon here. so cool and calm and also clean. nice breeze and cool water. u can see  many birds here too. very cool and calm and natural

Title: I walked along the new walkway on the south shore of Tissa Tank.
Text:
Tissa Tank slash Lake
I walked in a circle to Tissa Dagoba & along the new walkway on the south shore of Tissa Tank. It was interesting to see some LARGE trees there. It is amazing no-one has chop, chop, chopped them down. Very good people of Sri Lanka. Thanks!

Title: Fantastic
Text: Great place in Sri Lanka. It's so close from the place where I stayed in Tissamaharama. I saw the sun rise in evening time and lot of birds too.

Title: boat ride
Text: great view. good to do boat ride. not to swim in there. nice in the evening sunset. Exercise walk a way is there.

Title: Beautifull lake
Text: Tissa wewa is a beautiful lake and apopular attraction . The pathways have been recently redone and is n8w wrll lit . A boatride to the islandis recommended

Title: Beautiful serene and tons of bird life
Text: We got some bikes and did a circuit around the lake and rice  fields. It was a fabulous day with the clouds mirrored across the water. It's very pretty and there are interesting birds everywhere. Lovely way to just stop and enjoy Sri Lanka.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Take a boat ride....go to the island....feed the deer in the island....watch the birds in the island.....thousands.....nest here.....don't swim.....except in places locals swim. Don't swim far.....stay very close to the bank......crocodiles!!! Ok......Dont swim......wash your face and feet only!

Title: Very Impressive Ancient Engineering
Text:
The Twin Baths are absolutely huge and considering how long ago they were commissioned and built, they represent a truly remarkable feat of engineering.
As the name suggests there are two ornate stepped baths side by side with beautiful carved steps and gates. There are two pools, one for the monks to wash and cleanse themselves and one to enter when washed and essentially rinse!
There is a working filter system at one end that keeps the water relatively clean but the guide says they are totally drained before the monsoons so as to allow new water to accumulate during the rains.
We'll worth a short stop, great for pictures.

Title: Beautiful and calm
Text: The trees were flowering during our visit in July, which made this particularly beautiful to visit and photograph. It wasnt too busy so could photograph without tourists popping into frame all the time. Interesting construction. Could use more English language details on history and construction and use.

Title: The monkeys were cool!
Text: So this place has massive potential but even the local guides arent quite sure what was happening here. Suggest coming up with a cool story of kings and Buddhas of past that resonates with people and going with it. Monkeys all over the joint.

Title: Twin Baths
Text: Really nice architectural and artistic design. worth visiting. You could only imagine how the royals enjoyed at the time they used the baths!

Title: An historical place with relevance
Text: Nothing great, but if you love history and culture then you can relate it to the early days and imagine how their life would be in those days.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Boring  for us. Just two square ponds used years ago now half empty and not cery clean wgen we visited

Title: Definitely Worth A Pause.  A Sight To Behold & Take A Photo Of.  A Place to Learn More About After But ....
Text:
honestly ... towards the end of a long hot day visiting ancients sights and temples in and around Anuradhapura ...

We were in and out of the van within 10 minutes.  This is all we could manage.  However we knew we were seeing a remarkable engineering fete and because of that I can honestly rate it excellent and I am glad I have seen it.

Title: Ancient ingenuity
Text:
These pools are interesting because of their engineering. It never ceases to amaze me what people come up with to manage their access to water. Especially in parts of the world where it is in abundance some times of the year and more scarce in others. 
There are tourist stalls around the pools but the vendors are fairly low key.

Title: Tour.
Text: Went here during our tour and found the site very interesting. The construction of the first pool was impressive but the requirement for a second one seems amazing in this day and age.

Title: An amazing design
Text:
These two bathing ponds were filled by guiding water into a pool, the sediment would have sunk alowing the clean water to overflow and into a pipe. The water then came out of a lion-s head spout into the bath. Apparently, the King and others would disrobe in a private area made of silks and other fabrics before entering the bath via the ornate steps.
I had wondered why there was a cobra carved into the bath's side; my guide informed me that it is a symbol of prosperity and good luck.
Would we visit this site again? Yes.

Title: You cannot help but admire the work of the builders
Text: We think technology is for modern man, but those who lived in the past were much wiser than we give credit for.  This huge man made tank (dam) supplies water into the bath area through a system of water &  drainage channels.  The baths are made from huge granite stones.  This site has a lot of potential if the Government could afford to re-establish the gardens & surrounding area.  Overall it is well worth visiting.

Title: Amazing
Text: This is also one of the must sees of Anuradhapuras ancient city. Its location is near many of the other sites, so its worth going by bike. A wonderful historical site. Best to go in the morning or late afternoon, as it gets very hot during the day. Bring water, or buy from some of the vendors,  at slightly inflated prices.

Title: Architectural Marvel
Text:
It is a part of UNESCO world heritage site of Anuradhapura. It is a masterpiece of ancient advanced technology built by Sinhales. It was used by monks for bathing. Underground inlets & outlets for water. There are 2 tanks.
Larger one is 132'length,51'breadth,18'depth.
Smaller is 91'length,51'breadth,14'depth.
All walls & floor are made by cut pieces of granite.
There are flight of steps with support. Large pots decorate it.
Well laid garden also.
Few small souvenir shops .
Entry ticket for SAARC Nationals is $12.5 or LKR 1937.5 /per person
For other tourists is $ 25 or LKR 3875 /per person
This is for all Anuradhapura sites.

Title: Impressing size and craftsmanship
Text: The twin baths are certainly an impressive piece of craftsmanship build in stone and filled by an ingenious draining system providing water to the whole are during the rainy season.

Title: You need to take a closer look ...
Text: These ponds were - just like some others - contructed in a specific way and include a few details (cobra, turtle and other ornaments). It included a water filter system and underground connections at a time when such things were unknown in Europe.

Title: Neat pair of connected ponds.
Text: These ponds are in really good condition and are separated by a raised walkway. The pools are connected underground. On the 2nd smaller pond at the rear is a carved 5 headed snake as well as a lion ( I believe this was a water spout). The  monks used these pools for their ablutions

Title: Huge stone pools
Text:
Twin ritual baths built in the 8th century. Worth a look because of their scale. There are a few stalls on one side selling fruit, drinks and tourist trinkets. 

The toilets here should be avoided at all costs!

Title: Interesting pools with good background story
Text:
These two pools were used by the monks - the seniors in one, where it seems they just sat at the edge, while or the "juniors" the other pool offered immersion and bathing. 
The fact that these pools existed is down to some amazing old technology to bring in water from the nearby sources - some of are also man made. 

This is only part of a large complex for the monks. It gives food for thought on what it must have been like. 
You do need a guide to give you the necessary insight.

Title: Retrospect
Text: If this is what the baths looked like, imagine what the whole complex looked like when it was still intact and in use. The construction leading water to the bath is amazing.

Title: Well kept and interesting
Text: Another short stop off whilst visiting Anuradhapura. Nice place to relax and very popular with Srt Lankans

Title: Twin Baths
Text:
Fantastic architecture and well preserved , though the water needed cleaning and local authorities should do more to keep area clean.
Must not forget to see the sculpture of the snakes which many visitors may miss as tucked away in one corner

Title: They are not twin but they are nice
Text:
I liked this place. They were the prettiest baths I saw. 

They are not really twin since they were built at different times, they have different sizes and architecture. We also do not know for sure what was their purpoise. But I thought it interesting something so old had a filtering system

Title: Want to get marry?
Text: They told us that if you want to get marry you.just have to sit next to pond and.stair into it in silence

Title: Nothing uncommon
Text: This baths is situated in nice park with many religious bulding. Not such a uncommon place, but not a waist of time.

Title: Simple yet cool to see...
Text:
It's a must to see as part of the tour around this place.
Stop and absorb it all. Pretty cool taking pics at the bottom of the steps when there is no water in there...
Definitely worth the trip

Title: Interesting pool
Text: This place was an unexpected find! When we got there there was a flock of monkeys crawling out of he jungle into these majestic baths. Would surely pass by this during your tour of the ancient city. There are also a few souvenir stands here.

Title: Worth a look
Text: Unfortunately Anuradhapura was the last site we visited on our tour and by that time you are a little Stupa'd, Budha'd and ruined out. It was interesting to see and note some slight discrepancies in who is believed to have used these - we were told locals or monks, other reviewers here say monarchy. Will we ever know? This site is surrounded by vendors, that spoils the effect a little.

Title: Two adjacent bodies of water
Text: The twin ponds were used for bathing tanks in ancient Anuradhapura city. One side of the pond still exposes the simple way in which the water was filtered before it entered into the ponds

Title: Historic Architecture
Text: Though this place is of historical importance but has not been well maintained. No description of the historical importance is available at the site. The water in the tanks is very dirty and should be changed or cleaned regularly to make it a good attraction

Title: Not for swimming
Text: Great place to visit. Just to appreciate how they could have constructed these so well, so long ago. Full of vile green water now - but did have fish and a turtle swimming in it (amongst the other rubbish)

Title: Interesting historical site
Text: This place made a change from visiting all of the stupas in Anuradhapura and was interesting to see. I imagine it was more impressive in its day, with an advanced system for cleaning the water to allow monks to bathe and ablute themselves. Only small, but definitely stop here on a tour around Anuradhapura.

Title: Don't bring your soap
Text: This is an extraordinary construction for its' time. The different levels where bathers would sit demonstrates a hierarchy. Despite the colour of the water you will find turtle or two swimming & there is no smell. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Kuttam Pokuna
Text: Considered as one of the best specimen of great bathing pools in Sri Lanka ... situated in Mahamewna Uyana near to Abhayagiri Sthupa..

Title: Quick site to take in
Text: The twin baths that are not twins.  This site makes one recognise the engineering at the time to work the water systems in this way.  Impressive

Title: Ancient swimming pool
Text:
This seems like a swimming pool but it s a bit different with a modern one.

Its called twin ponds as there two such ponds and now a days its not in use really ,even though its seems one of the great place to visit and see the and see the ancient technology in those sectors.

Title: Historic Engineering!!
Text:
A hydrological piece of engineering in the history of the kingdom of. Anuradhpura. 
Dress code is relaxed, however please consider this area as religious grounds.

Title: Nothing spectacular
Text: Not really spectacular. You can have a look when you are driving by anyways, but I wouldn't go there just for this...

Title: Nice
Text: Place is nice but if you are in hurry you can skip it to see more beautiful places.It was good but when I arrived there place was full with little students :D

Title: Interesting Cultural Find
Text: Not far from roadside and accessible by car. Our guide proved very useful in painting a broad history of the site. One would need a guide or printed information to appreciate the cultural aspects of the site

Title: Restored Baths
Text:
Twin Baths (Kuttam Pokuna)
For centuries this area had been depopulated by the Malaria Mosquito and the surrounding jungle had reestablished itself, covering the many temples and Stupa built by a long Line of Sri Lankan kings each trying to outdo his predecessor by building bigger and better. Fortunately some have been reconstructed by the Sri Lankan archeological society. One of these is the twin baths at Mihintale, consisting two large bathing pools, these days full of green stagnant water with the odd Terrapin in thrown in. However you can see how the water was changed every couple of days with fresh water where the worlds largest school for Buddhist Monks used to bathe.

Title: Steep steps to get to the baths
Text:
The twin baths are part of the Anuradhapura complex and is well worth a visit. 

Although there is only green stagnant water in the baths, they still provide great insight into the building skills of the ancient Sri Lankans. In order to actually get a good look at this structure, one must decend and then ascend a steep set of ancient stone steps. It is however, possible to get a glimpse of the baths from the top of the steps if you cannot navigate these steps.

Title: Quiet and nice place
Text: Our guide said that this pool never was an empty. In the monsoon time the pool is filled by water from rain. And on sunny days will never evaporate entire water from this pool. The water is still there and prepare for using like in an ancient time...

Title: Very well restored
Text: All sites in Anuradhapura including this one are well restored and maintained and worth a visit by all.

Title: Great Story
Text: The twin baths were interesting. Enjoyed walking around each pool and imagining how busy they would have been. Very quiet place.

Title: What a Nice Place for a Bath!
Text: This is truly an interesting place of history. The stone layout is amazing. What a place for the people during that time to use and enjoy.

Title: Must have been nice once
Text: I can imagine that it may once have been very pleasant bathing here. The pools are an interesting feat of construction, but only worthy of a short visit.

Title: Fascinating Ruins
Text:
These twin baths are part of the Anuradhapura ancient ruins. It is absolutely fascinating how these stone monuments were built. There isn't much to the twin baths but it is a picture worthy moment. 

This tour should be really be done only if you have a driver as otherwise it is very very hot! Remember to dress appropriately; long sleeves and perhaps in white too as the pilgrims do. This is all sacred land for the Buddhists.

Title: Simple yet cool to see...
Text:
It's a must to see as part of the tour around this place.
Stop and absorb it all. Pretty cool taking pics at the bottom of the steps when there is no water in there...

Title: Sri Lanka take 3
Text: This was interesting to see, but as these pools are no longer used by the monks it looked like 2 empty concrete pools,

Title: Bathing for Monks.
Text: These ponds look link swimming pools and supposed to have been used by Monks before morning rituals and prayers in ancient times.Water enters the larger pond through mouth of Makara( a mythical animal) and flows into smaller pond through an underground pipe.The water filter system and five headed Naga ( Cobra) reflect the engineering and artistic skills of the artisans from yesteryears.There are a line of shops on one side of the banks offering a variety of souvenirs at competitive prices.Don't miss to sip fresh coconut water to beat the heat.

Title: nice pool in the temple
Text: in the middle of buddha temple u find this pool, our tour guide was excellent, preferable to visit either early morning or afternoon because the weather is warm and you are barefoot so the ground is extremely hot

Title: It's ok!
Text: Two baths next to each other. There was lot of sellers next to it. This attraction was free of charge. Nothing spesific.

Title: Amazing complex
Text: You can't really rate just the twin baths as they are part of a much bigger, complex and sophisticated site. The whole system of hygiene water and movement is incredible.

Title: The biggest bath in the world
Text:
As I said at my previous comment, anuradhapura is very big. When you visit there you are giving 25 USD. But one day is also not enough to visit this attraction. But during the park, you should definitely visit twin baths (King and For Queen) , You will definitely love to be there..

Cheers
Ernur

Title: Just ok...
Text: We were driving past it when we stopped to take a look.  Nothing that incredible when comparing it to some of the other local sites.

Title: History
Text:
It is a good experience to see how was the life in this time.
You can walk around the Swimming Pools and understand how were running.

Title: Interesting
Text: The pools have an interesting way of looking the same size from some angles, but in my opinion they, as well as many of the temples are overrated. Don't eat my head, I have seen so many in so many countries...

Title: Kuttam Pokuna (Twin ponds/pools)
Text: The pair of pools were built by the Sinhalese in the ancient kingdom of Anuradhapura. These are considered as one of the significant achievements in the field of hydrological engineering and outstanding architectural and artistic creations of the ancient Sinhalese

Title: ONE OF THE MANY BATHS/PONDS OF THE CULTURAL TRIANGLE
Text: Two ponds, well conserved, located in the Northern part of the Anuradhapura site. One is 40m length and the smallest 28m.

Title: Nothing very significant
Text:
There are 2 ponds of average size which were used by the monks for bathing.Having seen a lot of ponds in historical areas with much more stone carvings or much bigger, I did not feel any thing very significant. Place is well maintained and it is interesting to note the way the water was channelised to the pond, filtering out the mud.

There is no separate ticket for this place. But I suppose the Anuradhapura area ticket covers this as well.

Title: Quite impressive
Text: The baths are mostly intact, unlike other ruined buildings on the site. Worth seeing. But not much to do other than walk around them. There are a few stalls selling tourist tat.

Title: Engineering expertise
Text:
Comparisons can be odious but as a layman I would venture to suggest that the Romans were more advanced than the Sinhalese.

Nonetheless this is a great engineering achievement given that it was built around AD600.

It was tranquil and interesting.  Worth a look.

Title: Attractive and inspring
Text:
These beautifully designed twin pools were serene when we visited in the mid afternoon.

There were only two other tourists apart from our group.

It was interesting to hear how the original inhabitants developed a water cascading system.  This site is in good condition.

Title: Kids will like this place
Text: These twin tanks hold a lot of fish and tourists can feed. Kids will enjoy. This is a photo spot. This is one of the few spots in Anuradhapura that does not have an entry fee.

Title: Great
Text: Its a nice piece of architecture which depicts how good the Sri Lankans were back in the day at designing.This is just near all other major monuments and sacred places.

Title: Not Quite Twins
Text: They call these the twin pools because they sit side by side, but one is larger and has more staircases down in to it.  All the same it was a pleasant place to visit and not very busy.  Also you can go to the far corner and view the filter system that was used to pour clean water into the pool...

Title: Excellent Condition, beautiful.
Text: In lovely condition evidently the Queen entered from the far end pond and the King nearer the road ornate reliefs at either end some local souvenir and drink stalls around.

Title: Wonderful historic and artistic feature
Text: The Kuttam Pokuna or twin baths are one of our favourite features of the many historic sites in Anuradhapura. The two pools were constructed by the Sinhalese for bathing purposes and are an outstanding achievement in terms of hydrological engineering of the time. Not only are they of archaeological and scientific interest but they are also a wonderful artistic feature. They have flights of steps leading down to the water which are decorate with scrolls and other artistic features. One can stand peacefully enjoying the tranquillity of the pools today whilst imagining Monks bathing in ancient times.

Title: a scenic paysage
Text: It is very good to have water space in a monastery complex, it is a solid stone building, but not a beauty.

Title: A piece of historic Sri Lankan engineering ingenuity
Text:
Anuradhapura is one of the most historic towns in Sri Lanka and history goes back to 11th Century AD. Kuttam Pokuna is one of the historic monuments in this city, but there are so many other monuments surrounding this as well. 

Kuttam means pair (two) & Pokuna means pond in native Sinhala language, so you will see two identical ponds opposite each other. As per the history, one pond (pool) is for the king & other one is for the queen, but not sure about accuracy of that data. 

If you love history and Pyramids, Anuradhapura is one the similar places to visit  but please make sure you do your research first, if not you might not enjoy it.

Title: Reflects great Sri Lankan engineering hisotry
Text: This is one of the Ancient swimming pools which depict capabilities of ancient engineers in Sri Lanka. It is made out of Granite with intricate carvings which will tells us how good was the technical know how of Sri Lankan craftmen. Kuttam Pokuna means Twin ponds. Build during King Agbo (575-608) period. May have been used by Monks. Great hydraulic marvels that must be visited by any one visitng Sri Lanka.

Title: see this as part of your local sightseeing
Text: The beautifully built stone baths were supposedly for monks to bathe in. Stop here for 10 minutes on a tour of the anuradhapura sights. You can buy cold drinks nearby. Boy it gets hot.

Title: Beautiful granite faced ancient bathing pools
Text: Along with many other sites locally, and there are a great many, these are superb examples of ancient Sinhalese architecture and aqua engineering.  This was a very advanced and sophisticated civilization and these two beautiful granite faced pools are yet more evidence of that, as well as being very photogenic.

Title: Impressive water management and carefully restored to original form
Text: Despite being green and poorly maintained, these enormous baths were apparently built to act as a laundry for the many hundreds of monks living nearby. Our guide advised us that they were definitely not built for the pleasures of swimming as fun and recreation was denied the monks . Pity, really - they look well worth a cooling dip...

Title: By itself not worth the trip
Text: Like most things on the Anuradhapura circuit, by themselves they are fairly boring, but adding the total of all sights makes it worth the trip. Yeah, the baths are old, but they have rubbish in them and basically are a stepped swimming pool with stagnant water.

Title: interesting ancient engineering
Text: Included in the general entrance fee for Anuradhapura city complex this is an interesting short attraction visit. You will only take a few minutes to view this pair of bathing pools and marvel at the  sophistication in engineering achieved over 2000 years ago. A number of market stalls adjacent and one or two beggars in the area. Public toilets (rare occurrence in Anuradhapura) 50 metres away and whilst not luxurious are usable for 20 rupees. Not a must do but worth stopping if passing.

Title: unbelivable
Text: Far away from the city,no buses on that route,tuk tuk are very expensive.............................................

Title: not so good
Text: well because it was part of the tour we went here but it was nothing so exciting about this place.. if you have time then visit..

Title: Part of general Anaradhupura entrance
Text:
It seems odd that each site within Anaradhupura has it's own review here. As this was my favourite part of Anaradhupura I thought I would allocate my review to the Kuttampokuna (twin baths).

The quietness of the baths, amazing intricate nature of their design and proxinity to a very good and inexpensive small place to eat draws me to them. Also, their resident turtle was friendly and an attraction in himself. 

I thought that given the size of Anaradhapura a driver or in our case cycles are a necessity. I estimate we cycle about 12-15km but saw only two thirds of the area. 

Sign posts are lacking and it is easy to miss certain sites within the area. 

There is so much to see in this ancient city that it is another must see place while in this part of Sri Lanka. 

Anaradhapura is let down by lack of sign posts and seeming lack of reinvestment of the tourist dollar.

Title: Amazing
Text: They are really beautiful, not exactly the same size, even if called twin pools. Nowadays I wouldn't put a foot in, the water doesn't look clean enough for an European. But you can imagine how it must have been.

Title: Pretty and quiet
Text: What strikes out is these twin ponds are ancient. The multi-headed naag at the end of one of them impressive and really hard to photograph. There is an interesting system of silt chambers to collect all silt from the water before it enters the ponds

Title: Still worth a visit
Text: The twin baths are yet another testament to the once upon a time grandeur of one of Sri Lanka's native kingdoms. I have to admit that before visiting Anuradhapura, I was not aware that Sri Lanka had such a long and rich history, that it had a civilization that was complex and advanced enough to rival that anywhere else. The whole time I was staring at the twin baths, I kept thinking "How could the people have afforded to build these back then? Where was the source of their wealth?" The twin baths, after all, are very big, especially for just two people. It can thus be looked at as either a symbol of wealth and power and/or waste and frivolous spending. Regardless, the twin baths are definitely worth a look, simply because they are so well preserved, even after a thousand years, unlike many of the other relics in and around Anuradhapura. Just be careful not to fall in! The water is indeed very green!

Title: Bath place of king
Text: This was supposedly the place where the king used to take his bath. Nothing much to see here other than two bath places filled with greenish water. It's not even fit to be classified under 'Attractions'. Can be totally skipped!

Title: Nice walk
Text: A relaxing stroll in the park kind of setting.  The trees shield the site from the sun so it's nice and cool to walk through.  When we visited, not a lot of tourists were there, a picnic under the trees by the twin baths should be nice!

Title: Must see at Anuradhapura
Text: I must admit that the highlight of all the sites in India/Southeast Asia are the water features at the palaces/temples and monasteries.  This one is no exception.  The sit contains two large pools with well sculptured stone and various carvings.  Though the site was crowded, it was able to accommodate the numbers and still seem serene.  There was also a lack of litter.

Title: What you don't see is interesting
Text: Allthough the twin baths are interesting, it's much more amazing to relase they made these intricate waterworks so many centuries ago. And could you please use some of the massive entree fees(US$ 25)  to Anuradhapura historical site to clean up all the litter. Would show as much respect for these sites as taking of your shoes.

Title: They were doing this well before the Romans
Text: This is an amazing example of the structural and hyrologogical engineering of the ancients in this area.  For a few rupees you can get some food to feed the fish and turtles in the ponds.    Don't know that I'd swim in it though the algae looks a bit ominous.  Nearby we're some busker snake charmers, pythons and cobra.    Our guide suggested r1000 was far too much to pay to handle the snakes.  He suggested half if not a tad less.

Title: Interesting spot
Text: The two pools and their history are quite interesting.  After a day of buddha images and dagobas, we were happy to look at something new.  We also enjoyed spotting fist and turtles - this might be a good spot for kids.  However, there's not much to see, so it's probably a 15 minute stop total - only worthwhile if you are already in the area.

Title: 2nd best place to see at Anuradhapura
Text: This place was neat and well preserved. It is a long way from the other sites so need a car to get there. It is also free, at the others you need to pay.

Title: Uninspiring
Text: Two baths with water. Nothing particularly interesting about them. If you are walking or cycling around I wouldn't make a detour for it.

Title: Go early in the morning
Text: Most people visit these baths and other places near Anuradhapura after 10 AM - Stay one night and visit early (start at 7 AM) and see them deserted which is good for pictures.

Title: Not a place to swim!
Text: You have to admit that the water management of previous eras was both far sighted and well engineered. Not a big site but certainly worth seeing.

Title: Beautiful symmetry
Text:
Not much detail but beautifully constructed ancient pools. Very atmospheric even in heavy rain which is when we were there.

Stop to look and walk around the pools. You'll appreciate the workmanship and the beautify of these ancient pools.

Title: Worth a look.
Text:
If you are visiting the Abhayagiri Vihara monastery complex, it is worth stopping to look at these ponds. 
Located at the side of a current roadway, the ponds are thought to bathing pools for the monks who resided in the monastery. 
The southern pond features a water spout in the form of a makara, and a guardstone featuring the Naga symbol (cobra).

Title: Really interesting
Text: We had a fab guide who was really knowledgeable and was able to give us loads of information, plus point out the most interesting carving etc.

Title: Part of the site, worth a visit
Text: Like other reviews i say many of the key sites at Anuradhapura. For the temples you will need respectful clothing. It was really hot visiting the site so when not in temple wear a hat have sunscreen and lots of water.

Title: Good visit
Text: I did all the temples in one day, theyre all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

Title: Kings Bath
Text: These were bathing pools used by the King & his followers. A quieter area of the great site. Watch out for the monkeys here, they stole lots of tourists items.

Title: Beautiful
Text: This was definitely one of our highlights of Anuradhapura.  Having seen many temples around Sri Lanka we were a bit exhausted.  This is a beautiful, quiet place to sit and reflect a while.

Title: Vacation
Text: Very old pools which are feed from underground means. Rebuilt years ago but are beautiful to see. People feed the fish in the pools. Very photographic.

Title: Grab a fresh coconut to drink here
Text: Just away from the mighty temples of Anuradhapura, are the twin baths of the monks of old. Watch out for thieving monkeys here and admire the craftsmanship of these magnificent baths. After a very hot and tiring visit to the oldest temples of Anuradhapura, a fresh shell of coconut juice was most welcome and we sat sipping the delightful drink just adjacent to these baths. It's an area of great peace and beauty and a welcome haven from the busy main tourist drag; well worth a visit at the chance to explore your inner self!

Title: Well preserved
Text: Unusually for this archaeological park these pools are relatively intact and well preserved and make for an interesting stop on your tour.

Title: Good for resting
Text: The twin ponds are a great place for a rest during your tour of the sacred city. Usually, there are not so many people. You can watch the fishes and we even saw two turtles.

Title: Pleasant
Text: Nice to imagine what life would have been like for the king and his court.  Nice detailed carvings, worth a visit.

Title: Twin ponds, but not exactly twins
Text: Twin ponds, but not exactly twins with one much larger than the other. Attractive, but only if you think in the context of trying to imagine the city at its pomp when these would have been the bathing pools fed by hydrological engineering allowing water to be fed through underground ducts and filtered before flowing to the pool.

Title: A large area with archeological digs
Text: This bath area has been discovered in the dig-for older and younger monks who lived in the temple. Interesting to see and imagine their way of life

Title: bathing ponds
Text: I can't imagine bathing regularly in ponds like these, but that is what happened back in the day, it doesn't happen now. (That I know of.) The water is green-ish.

Title: well preserved
Text: There are two baths, one older than the other. Because of the growing amount of people living on the terrain, one was not enough in the end.

Title: Take a small scoop of water which theyd then drop on your head and in your mouth
Text:
From my Blog:

A quick ride from Abhayagiri was Kuttam Pokuna, two baths which lay on the side of the road and are flanked by yet another shanty market. Though the baths themselves are not the most impressive bodies of water you can view, it was a rare experience to see the spiritual power these baths had over those more devout than I...

As I sat next to the pools, a line began to form at the top of the steps leading down to the bath. One by one, people began to descend down to the water and take a small scoop of water which theyd then drop on their head and put a few drops in their mouths. Though Ive never been to India or witnessed the spirituality of pilgrims at the Ganges, I can only assume seeing these people at Kuttam Pokuna was as powerful as witnessing those at the banks of that storied river.

Title: The baths of the Sinhalese kings...
Text:
Detailed and Interesting rock carving of the twin baths, even more interesting the engineering involved in supplying the water, back in the 8th century when the work was supposedly completed. With the palace itself practically gone, its hard to imagine how the entire place looked like when everything was standing and functional...
Compared to the treasure troves of Dambulla and Pollonaruwa, to us, the royal twin baths are only marginally attractive and of interest...

Title: Royal Bath
Text: This is where the King and Queen bathe days gone by.The pond is well maintained. A very good place to take a photo.

Title: Short stop of with intersting story.
Text: The twin baths are worth stopping at. You'll see interesting architecture and, if with a guide, you'll get the history.

Title: Best of stone work
Text: Twin ponds is merely not an attractive set of ponds but a place where one can observe ancient water purification and desilting system, sending water column through scientifically designed set of stone containers. Steps give access to water at any level and platforms give access along the perimeter of the pond. Structure is all in stone and polished to give neatness while decorative ornaments adore the beauty of the construction. The floral vases (Pun kalasa) at the entrances to the two ponds differ in design. A five hooded Cobra image on the wall is extremely beautiful.

Title: Pleasant Pools
Text: These are two pleasant pols of water. Look out for the various birds that come when you are walking around the site. On one site are a range of stalls selling mainly tourist stuff. However, over the road is a shop that sells large bottles of coke at a good price. Good to cool down with on a hot day.

Title: Part of Anuradhapura Ancient City ...
Text: This is part of the Anuradhapura Ancient City with entrance fee of LKR4,550 per person per entry. Kuttam means twin and Pokuna means pond, so it is literally the twin pond. It was built since Anuradhapura Kingdom as far back to 4th century. It is regarded as one of the significant architecture in terms of hydrological engineering by the Sinhalese. Beautiful and artistic architecture with peaceful surroundings. Fishes can be sighted in the ponds too. It is essential to hire a driver service while visiting Anuradhapura site since the attractions are located pretty far from one another. Nice place to stop over for 15-20 mins visit.

Title: Show piece of ancient Sri Lankan engineering skills
Text:
This has been built by great Sri Lankan kings.  It's made of two similar swimming pools.
One pool is slightly smaller than the other.  They are made out of granite.  around the pools you could see a granite wall with Ancient Sri Lankan carvings.  
There's a belief that ancient Sri Lankan stone masons had a technology to soften the Granite.

Title: Scenic stop off
Text: Very scenic pair of ancient tanks. Part of the sacred city and included in the ticket price for that area

Title: Visit only if you have the time
Text: There are twin baths right next to each other. This is the only place youll find such a juxtaposition. Thats it.

Title: ARCHITECTURAL GEM
Text: The pools, made out of granite, were constructed around 500 A.D. They were for the use of the monks. Water entered one of the pools through the mouth of a makara, a mythical beast with the mouth of a crocodile, the body of a fish and the trunk of an elephant. Underground piping connected them. They are different sizes and depths.

Title: Nice
Text: Interesting when you see it and read the debrief at the site....nice for clicks as well...a different dimension to Anuradhapura

Title: Nice pond but lame surroundings
Text: That pond is nice especially the carved cobra, but the view is ruined by too many shops on one side.

Title: Well carved water-Ponds
Text: This shows off the water engineering skills of the ancient Sri Lanka. There are two ponds here, used as bathing tank by ancient kings and queens. Later, these ponds given to monks and has attached to the Abayagiri stupa complex. Situated in Anuradapura sacred area, most people tend to visit this place with their families. As of the architectural value of these ponds, its so popular among the travllers.

Title: Huge baths
Text:
These baths are huge.  You can really appreciate how they were used, when and why as you approach. 

 It was fascinating to be told about the old drainage and filtering systems to keep the water clean, which goes to show how smart our ancestors were.

It was very quiet here and you could happily walk around, take pictures and enjoy the scenery without a rush

Title: Ancient city historical monuments
Text: This old structure will reveal the engineering g expertise of ancient Sinhalese and the well established monastic tradition which contributed to the spiritual and natural well beingof the people.

Title: Great engineering
Text: Worth the visit on your tour of sacred places and ruins. The twin bath are in very good condition and maintained by the department of archeology. The. Water filtering system is also interesting and certainly very clever for the time. Id advise to get a historical guide for the day. We found ours by the main Tourist Ticket Office next to the Archeology Museum ( Museum is closed every Tuesday!). Our guide cost us 3000LKR for the day (4 hours). He took us to all the interesting areas of the ruins. We would have never seen all this and got the history of the site without him. He also communicated with our driver so we were driven and picked up in all the right places. One last advice, at the end of the day, keep your tourist ticket. Do not give it back. Not sure what the trick was there but we kept it and were checked subsequently twice on the roads by guards. Without our ticket we would have had an issue Im sure! And we could visit an extra site with our driver.

Title: Visit to the ponds of the monks
Text:
An amazing engineering feat of ancient times. The twin ponds are where monks would take their daily baths. 
The naga sculpture ( a snake like structure) in the northern pond is the guardian of the water. Many art pieces are feature in these ancient sites each representing a different aspect of the art and history of the time.

Title: Twin ponds/ baths
Text: This was really interesting as the twin ponds/baths which were well engineered as our guide explained their purpose and how they worked.

Title: Okay
Text: These pools are well engineered but by comparison to the neighbouring relics really not of great interest.

Title: Very worthwhile visiting
Text:
Having seen the smaller royal bath in the ancient city of Polonnaruwa, I was quite impressed by this older twin bath in Anuradhapura.

Massive granite slabs, an underground duct with filtering system to bring water to the pool and the decorations around the massive pools was very interesting. It's very grand. Once again having a driver/guide drive you around this massive ancient site on an always hot or hotter day made it more enjoyable.

This area was not as shaded as the pond area in Polonnaruwa so be prepared for the searing heat of the sun.

Title: Well preserved
Text:
These are baths constructed in the eighth century and used by the monks for their ritual ablutions. 
They are quite well preserved considering their age.

Title: Shame about the rubbish
Text: Beautiful and proportionate stone carvings built by ancient Sinhala rulers. Twin Baths illustrates history of the class system. Both the ponds which are different in size need a fair bit of cleaning up as it is quite polluted and smelly.

Title: beautiful
Text:
with huge hungry fish in the ponds. Very picturesque. Go early, it gets really hot and sunny later. 
I liked the Queen's pond a bit better, honestly.

Title: Spot the difference !
Text:
The bathing spots for the monks. One side for the senior monks, the other for the main class. Interesting irrigation system to provide a foot bath around the two baths when it was functional.

A nice stop on your tour of the city. Still pretty complete, compared to other complex sights.

Title: Architecturally, It is amazing!!!
Text: This is really one of the best constructions made by Ancient Sri Lankans, It will be really good the government put some funds to clean these two ponds a bit.

Title: Great photo opp, but BEWARE of the "salesmen"
Text: Best advice: buy some stale popcorn from the kiosks to feed the fish. This makes for a great photo opportunity. Also, beware of pushy salesmen who WILL follow you to your car.

Title: Fascinating
Text: Given the age of these two baths, you have to wonder at the engineering and skills of water management these people possessed. Spot lots of fish and the occasional turtle too!

Title: Smelly and polluted
Text: It is quite amazing that these baths were built such a long time ago and the filtration system is quite ingenious. However the water was putrid, lots of rubbish around, mangy looking dogs and a strong smell of cow manure did not endear this place to me.

Title: Two Tubs
Text: They have good architecture in the walls, and a history story, but after all, it's just two ponds for bathing.

Title: 15 days in Sri Lanka
Text: We visited the twin baths.  Spent around 30 minutes there not much to see but the two pools where the king took a bath

Title: Inside the Anuradhapura City
Text: Twin Ponds are part of the city tour of Anuradhapura and of significance in the overall setup of the ancient city

Title: Two ponds
Text: Honestly, nothing much to see or do apart from two rather unexciting ponds. A quick glimpse from the car may be suffice. Sorry, there are tons of other things in this complex of much greater interest.

Title: Beautiful ancient baths - shame about the litter
Text:
We visited the baths as part of our independent tour of Anuradhapura. We'd recommend visiting when you haven't purchased an extortionate - $25 entrance ticket for the day - as it isn't required for this site. 

The baths are architecturally impressive and worthy of some photographs - so long as you can avoid the litter - which is such a shame.

Title: Awesome reminder of ancient Sri Lankan architecture and engineering
Text: The twin ponds are said to have served as swimming baths for Buddhist monks in the monastery attached to the Abhayagiriya Dagoba. The two pond are actually different in size. The water flows in to one and then to the other through a complex irrigation  system. The northern one  is about 40m in length and the southern about 28m. It is possible to see all the ancient sites in Anuradhapura in one day.

Title: Monks only bathing
Text: Lovely peaceful place and beautifully constructed baths with water  that comes from a spring below and only monks can bathe in them.j

Title: Impressive
Text: This pools are beautiful, have a great ancient architectural work ad nice details. Its amazing what people could achieve 2000 years ago. Now I wouldnt like to bathe in the pool because its full of rubbish (in and next to it) and the water is green. If authorities will take some time to clean this place it would be fantastic.

Title: Not for the monks
Text: The fascination with baths is interesting with a view to the fact that none of them was for the monks as that would have been a fun experience which was forbidden per se. This said, the structure is impressive in size and comes along the way from one sacred site to another. You cannot miss it, but it is not a must.

Title: Not so special
Text: The history and story of this place is so intersting. But the monument and bath are average. The cost for this park is not so cheap. It includes pollunarawura entrance.

Title: Very pretty site
Text: It was beautiful to see this site. It is maintained well and is quaint and hidden as compared to the rest of the sites in Anuradhapura. Its an architecture delight!

Title: Shame one cannot bathe here now!
Text: It must have been an impressive city in ancient times. Lots of interesting ruins around here. Best explored by bike early in the day.

Title: Photo lovers spot
Text: The twin bath is located a little away from the other main tourist spots of Anuradhapura . But is a beautiful place to to. It's filled up with water during the rainy time. A good spot of photo lovers

Title: The engineering makes this a worthwhile stop
Text: This is one of a number of sites in the ancient city of Anuaradhapura.  It is worth a stop to admire the engineering and wonder how 15 000 monks bathed in them.  It's a shame that they are not maintained with fresh water and what water is in them is algae filled rain water.  It's worth remembering all of these historical sites only reopened in 2009 after the civil war and this is a site that will be interesting to see what happens as the tourism market grows.

Title: Twin Baths
Text: Beautiful place to take some photos with some different ruins and sculptures. Lots of fish in the water you can feed.

Title: Nothing spectacular!
Text: This review is quite late. When visiting the Sacred City of Anuradhapura the Twin Baths will definitely be included in your itinerary. Both ponds were full of garbarge; I wonder if  any maintenance is being carried out by the local government. I spent only a couple of minutes taking photos.

Title: Ancient hydraulics
Text: Fascinating example of ancient engineering.  The water to fill these tanks was brought for a lake miles away.  An ancient type of sluice gate stopped the water long enough to drop suspended sediment before it entered the tanks.  Its a shame it is not more carefully tended today.  Both tanks have accumulated trash floating on their surfaces, marring what otherwise is a grand vision.

Title: Worthy of a quick photo stop
Text: These "twin" swimming-pool-like ponds are worthy of a quick photo stop. Our guide told us that they were likely used by monks at the monastery attached to Abhayagiri Dagoba.They are not identical, however.

Title: Beautiful
Text: I was surprised at how lovely these baths are. Since they're right inside the entrance to the Sacred City, it's worth a quick stop.

Title: Interesting symmetry and ingenious water drainage system
Text: Interesting symmetrical structure of historic value; clean, large and worth a visit if on the way.  Find out how water is captured and fed into the baths!

Title: Interesting engineering and history
Text: We visited this as part of a tour of Anuradhapura with a guide. The engineering involved to fill the baths was impressive, as was the filter to remove sediment as the water flowed in. Simple and ingenious. Worth a 10 minute stop as part of a tour of the area.

Title: Beautiful baths!
Text: The twin baths have beautiful stone carvings.  The engineering is impressive - reminded me of the Romans.  They're in great condition.  A lovely, peaceful place.

Title: Nice 2 ponds.
Text: These twin ponds are among the handsomest wworks of the anuradhupura piriod. Its very cham ponds. Its have stone carving also..

Title: Interesting to see
Text: Interesting to visit as part of your tour.  The scale is impressive. See my other reviews in anuradhapura

Title: Great ponds
Text: One of the many many attractions to see whilst visiting Anuradhapura.  We had a guide to explain things to us which was definitely beneficial at a cost of LKR2000

Title: Absolute Rip off
Text: The entry fee of AUD35  is daylight robbery to view this site. Not worth the money and should not be supported. Funds go to the government and nothing is spent on maintaining these sites. Clean up these sites instead of regulating on what the public can and cannot wear.

Title: Amazing cultural site
Text: Serene and breath taking. In the evening, the trees reflect in the water. Culturally significant site.

Title: Beautiful ponds with good architecture
Text: This place is full of greenery and twin ponds share a promiscuous history. Carvings on the walls are magnificent.

Title: Interesting social history
Text: If you travel by tuk tuk or bike you can miss the roadblocks and charges that you cop by car. This place has a very promiscuous history.

Title: Luxury twin bath Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka
Text:
It is huge and double pool..the architecture still in good condition
One of the best specimen of bathing tanks or pools in ancient Sri Lanka is the pair of pools known asKuttam Pokuna (Twin Ponds/Pools). The said pair of pools were built by the Sinhalese in the ancient kingdom of Anuradhapura.
Highly  recommended, near to the railways station

Title: Marvelous Ancient Bathing Ponds
Text:
Kuttam Pakuna (Twin Ponds) 

Kuttam Pakuna (Twin Ponds) are two bathing tanks built in the middle of a garden in 6th century AD by King Aggabodhi for the monks and students, as part of Abhayagiri Monastery Complex in sacred city of Anuradhapura. It reflects wonderful skills possessed by the Sri Lankans 2000 years ago in architectural engineering and hydrological technology. Both ponds are 51 feet wide and laid down in a row. The larger one is 132 feet long and 17 feet deep while the smaller one is 91 feet long and 14 feet deep. Underground tunnels were built to fill and empty the ponds.

Title: 2000 Years old Water Storage
Text: What a surprise... two thousand years old water storage... still entact... and appealing... a must visit for history lovers

Title: Nothing exceptional
Text: As in India we have lots of these types of ponds we were not impressed by the structure. You may stop for a short photo stop but nothing to keep you interested for long.

Title: An architectural master piece.
Text: The twin baths were built BC for the King and Queen. they are side by side and are exquisitely crafted and would amaze any one with an architectural flair.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Interesting that the baths are not identical in size, there is a wonderful snack bar selling nuts and fresh cut apples with salt and chilli which is amazingly restorative after a sweltering day in the heat.

Title: Worth stopping if you're passing, but don't make a special trip
Text: Two pools, water somewhat green, containing a large number of fish. Part of the Anurdhapura sacred city tour, but not worth going to see specially.

Title: Look out for the huge number of fish

Title: More protection required
Text: It is a wonderful site that Sri Lankans can be proud of. But it was putty to see a few plastic bottles and many plastic bags floating on the water. The garbage pile with food waste a few yards from the pond was another thing I thought should not be there if the site needs to be protected for the future generation. The shops very close to the pond should not be allowed to operate so close.

Title: Interesting, but nothing spectacular
Text:
Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura, of the "cultural triangle" sites, is the most out of the way, and least worth your while as a result.  I would only recommend it if you were staying in Sri Lanka over 10 days or if you are a big historical/cultural buff.  The ruins at Polonuwara and Sigiriya are more impressive.

The baths themselves are worth about 5-10 minutes of your time, hardly worth the amount of time taken just to get there, especially if you are using a bicycle or public transport.  They are, after all, the ruins of two baths (enter drumroll...).  The surrounding area is decidedly not tourist friendly, unless you prefer that look.  There are filthy (and closed at the time of my visit) bathroom facilities, a small shack selling a drink across the road, and lots of cows wandering about.  The area around was muddy (since it had rained recently), and the pools are not closed off.  Good as it preserves a better "look", but bad if you have small children.

I would recommend only at the tail end of a visit to Anuradhapura, which itself I would only recommend as a bottom tier attraction within Sri Lanka.  The exorbitant entrance fees alone make you almost obligated to enter.
