Before 7:30am, from 12noon to about 1pm and another time in the afternoon (around 4pm). There are large fields that cows wandering around to eat. They seem to be treated quite well. They also show cheese making process but it wasn't working when we were there.

At last, you can try their fresh milk, cheese, yoghurt, etc. with very reasonable prices. They're tasty except the milk with too much sugar in it. We recommend the cheese and yoghurt.

You can spend two to three hours here if you enjoy every part of the farm.

Title: A pleasant walk but the farm is only average
Text:
I would suggest to go to Ambewela farm only if you have a half a day free and you don't have any better plans :) and only to enjoy the trip, walk, sceneries. 
You can catch a bus from Nuwara Eliya to Ambewela.
But we preferred this route:
1. Bus N.E. to Nanuoya 15min-22LKR
2. Train Nanuoya to Ambewela 20min-15LKR (Ella train)
(You can enjoy stunning views over farms, tea plantations, Horton Plain and waterfalls)
3. Walk from Ambewela train station to Ambewela Farm 30min-free :)
(You won't miss the farm sign. The road is really well maintained, views are gorgeous, generally a pleasant walk)
4. Farm admission fee is 200LKR for adults, kids -1/2price
Inside there are cows, baby cows, goats, rabbits and a small cheese factory. To be honest, nothing expressive. Sheds are very smelly, animals are a bit dirty, no information about the farm history or how the cheese factory operates. Restaurant didn't have any proper meals (it was a big disappointment for us as we planned to have our lunch there). Should mention that the actual farm area is well looked after. 
Well, at this point you have to turn back and take the same road to the train station.  
5. You can come back by the same train+bus or take a direct bus to N.E.
** before you start your trip check the train and bus schedule :)

Title: Brilliant the farm better grass than in New Zealand or Denmark
Text: Must visit if you went to nuwara eliya I suggest you combine with a visit to worlds End or Horton plainsSnacks served sufficient for meal. Wholesome andClean

Title: Highlight of our trip to Nuwar Eliya
Text: This wasnt rated very highly by trip advisor, but by reading the reviews I knew my family would like it. We really loved the experience. First the view to the place was awesome - the greenery, the grazing areas for cows, etc. Then we loved feeding the cows. There were great spots for taking picture perfect photos. Then we had fresh hot milk in the restaurant, which i really liked. It tasted real good, and surprisingly didnt feel very heavy after that. Overall great experience. Those who are cow lovers, must visit.

Title: A visit to the New Zealand Farm
Text: We visited the New Zealand Farm as apposed to the Ambewela Farm (both are owned by Ambewela Farms) partly because I am a New Zealander but mainly because the scenery, apart from the farm buildings, is a snapshot of New Zealand. The likeness is almost unbelievable. We spent an hour walking around the various attractions at the farm and each drank a glass of warm milk.

Title: Saddening
Text: The cows that were kept in the various sheds seem to be in very sad conditions. The pregnant ones for example were all chained with almost no room for movement. Calves were sleeping on metal racks. Live rabbits (sold for meat) are kept in small individual cages where the floors of the cages are uncovered wire mesh. They are in really uncomfortable conditions.

Title: Amazing visit
Text: Visited the farm with relations and friends. Located in a lovely part of Nuwara Eliya with well maintained landscape and amenities. The animals looked in excellent shape and well cared for. Well worth a visit for a relaxing time.

Title: Very delicious milk and yogurt. All the animals were crazy and well bred.
Text: All the animals are very cute especially the rabbits. The staff was friendly and the animals were looked after well. A great experience.

Title: Must do
Text:
Their New Zealand farms have an amazing view. The panorama is like you are in Switzerland or Scotland. The local shop needs drastic makeover & better staff & hygiene.

The entry ticket is expensive seeing that not even a basic guide is provided.

Title: Good stop
Text: We passed this Ambewela Farms on our way to Hortens Plain from our hotel in Katukitula.  The travellers on the road that goes through the Farm onward to Hortens Plain can feast their eyes on cattle grazing in the meadows. The whole farm area is very picturesque. Hills on both the sides are so green and lush. On our return journey, we decided to stop at Ambewela Farm as they have a little restaurant.  We had their delicious yogurt there.  We are not milk fans.  We were told one can actually go and do the farm tour but we were not interested nor more importantly had the time for it. Took the opportunity to just soak in the surroundings and take lots of photos. If you have the time, it is a good stop.

Title: So refreshing
Text: This is one of the best loaction I loved in and around Nuwara Eliya. Lies little away from Nuwara Eliya (about 15 km) at the high hills - the surrounding and secenary on the way is beautiful and one would love to just sit and enjoy the nature with fresh and coold air. I went there in April 2013 and managed to see inside the farm which was just great. They have a restaurant as well and one can buy the products of this farm. However, it was bad when I went there with my family last Decemebr - we found it closed for a month which was even not informed to me by my hotel as they were also not aware. Anyway - must visit place and one should go via Sita eliya and botanical garden to see this both place and return from other side to see the beauty of countrysides.

Title: A heavenly view.
Text:
If this is not a heaven i would wonder how heaven is?
Its a greeny farm where you can see cows free in the fields. One hour for photo opp is life memory which is not forgetten forever.

Title: Scenic and Educational
Text:
Plan to drop in at this scenic and wonderful farm if you are making a trip to world's end/ Horton plains.
Find out for times when opened for public viewing to make a tour in the farm.
Last visited 2012

Title: A great experience for little kids!
Text:
We visited Ambewala farms during our stay in Nuwara Eliya. 
We went as a group of 2 families with 4 kids and it was extremely fascinating experience for all 4 of them! 
They drive is very beautiful and picturesque - with hills covered in mist and dotted with cattle grazing around. 
Inside the farm, milking of the cows is something you'd like to watch, if you have kids along. 
There are also plenty of other farm animals like rabbits, billy goats for children to interact with. There is also a restaurant/ canteen inside where you can buy food but could work at being a little more clean and well maintained.

On the whole, would definitely recommend this if you have small kids.

Title: good sightseeing
Text: We traveled to Ambewela the drive was really nice and the road was good,The surrounding area is gorgeous

Title: Beautiful scenery getting there
Text: A good way to spend some of the day.. The surrounding area is gorgeous. Keep in mind that it is a farm so you will smell some nice odors. 100 rupees to enter

Title: Way below expectation
Text: It is fairly long drive from Nuwara Eliya city centre to this farm and the roads are not great. If you intend to visit this place ensure that you club it with you visit to Worlds End as it is in the same route. I had gone with my kids so that they can experience the entire process from milking to packaging. The initial experience was quite nice however, it stops there and nothing further. The place is also not maintained well and there is no staff around who is keen to guide the visitors despite the fact that there is a entry charge to get into the diary. The surroundings is however lush green and huge areas for grazing, also the route is very scenic and will take any where between 30 to 40 minutes to reach from the city.

Title: Know Farming
Text: Must visit place, any chance should not be missed.  Great experience to see the nature and farming.  Visitors are allowed to go inside the farm.   Cheese making centre is also avilable.  Don't miss to hvae a cup of hot farm fresh milk.

Title: Dairy amidst a Serene Environment
Text: The road trip to Ambewela was a fabulous one! If you are lucky you can catch up on a Srilankan Railway train on the way. The entire farm is in a very scenic environment - very cool and refreshing. We were able to see large cows and milking plants. Of course, we made good purchases of local cheese also - which was too good!

Title: take your kids there
Text: Cool climes, Pastures more than green, Great place for kids and people who love to see the dairy industry indights to give it a go, dont miss to enjoy a hot glass of milk or munch a cube of fresh chesse

Title: Great experience for kids
Text:
We arrived here at around 3:30pm and left around 5:30pm.
Our boys 11&9 year old enjoyed the chance to pet the cows and see how they are milked.
We had fresh cow milk and fish rolls at the end of the day.

Title: Good experience for children
Text: A must visit for children. The experience will be remembered forever by children. Well planned and maintained by highly skilled workforcer

Title: Moo Moo and more Moo
Text: On the way to Hortons plains this dairy is the only one that has a tour of the factor and the cows. Its is worth a visit since it falls on the way but not really otherwise

Title: The Dairy Cattle were fantastic, the 550 heads them !
Text: The owners of this property must live on another planet if they are satisfied with the appearance and condition of this farm. Serious upgrading and renovation is needed. The Cheese area is a con job and should be deleted ,the weeds around the public toilets and the condition of the toilets needs attention . If you are presenting this tourism product to the world then you have to spend your income on cleanliness and better presentation. I worked cattle for 17 years and I enjoyed looking at the dairy herd. You must upgrade this product ,get your staff motivated and get the culture right. The Minister for tourism in your country would have to be disappointed?

Title: New Zealand it was..
Text: Green valley of Ambewela starts around 5km before the milking station where cows are kept.. was such a great place to be seeing cows and calves. They also breed rabbits also. Had fresh milk and bought cheese. Overall its a hidden gem don't miss it

Title: Exotic -Green Farms
Text: If you want to see greenery all around you, with buffaloes and cows grazing in your sight and just relax watching the mother natures, this place is a must visit

Title: Good for Kids
Text: Good place to visit if you or your kids not seen milk farm to know bit more about cows, milking process. Also have a small shop to buy yogurt, etc. We visited the place on our return from Horton Plans National park.

Title: Farm in the middle of Greenary
Text: This is real scenic beauty with Grren Farms all around. This is actually a Farm for Dairy (Ambewela Dairy Farm) with Hudreads of Cows, Calfs. Farms are actually grazing fields for these cows. Temperature is low in September End with floating clouds on the chest of these Fields. Good place to visit once. You can enjoy Pure, fresh & hot milk & other dairy products at caffeteria.

Title: Not for Adults but Yes for kids.
Text: Well, the place is normal. Nothing was interesting. You will see different halls/rooms for cows/goats/bulls. It could be a good place for kids as they will enjoy seeing animals. The way to this place is beautiful and there is some good spots for photos. We have stopped several times and we enjoyed the way.

Title: Good for kids
Text:
If you have schooling kids, its a must see. For Adults its just walk to see some cows & studs. Nothing much to see. 
When the staffs milk the cow what i've noticed is they are not keen in following hygienic procedures.

Title: Waste of time...
Text:
To be totally honest, a total waste of time...

If you've ever lived in Europe, Australia or NZ, there is not even the slightest thing special about this place. In fact, the way they treat their cows is very inhumane compared to the lush and abundant vegetation that surrounds the "cow feeding and milking enclosure".

Milk is 'alright'. Surrounding scenery is beautiful but you could really see the same elsewhere throughout Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Scenic Beauty.. Must visit
Text: Beautiful surrounding as well as the way..... It looks like you are in country side of Switzerland. Beautiful........

Title: Of little interset to European Visitors
Text: Guide was enthusiastic about this place but afraid it doesn't hold same appeal to British visitors that it obviously does to locals. On day of visit it was public holiday in Sri Lanka and place was packed with bus loads of locals fascinated by trip.

Title: Great place. Great weather.
Text: What a time we had! Rolling green hills, chilly weather, good breed of cows, cheese making. If you like photography, you should not give it a miss! You can spend  2 to 3 hours there happily clicking away. Highly recommended

Title: There is nothing to see here except cows?
Text: I have no idea why this place is so highly rated. First it takes forever to find this place and driving through maze of roads. Second the place is absolutely over crowded with school children. This is just a farm where you get to see huge cows. That is all! Do not waste your time and money on this place. Its cold outside and vehicles cant drive into the place so expect a very long walk in cold. If you are so desperate to see cows take a jacket with you and one more thing the place stinks of cow piss and turd. Avoid at all cost!

Title: One of the higlights or our trip!
Text: I loved visiting the farm!!! Our 7month old daughter who was otherwise grumpy all along loved it too! Saw baby cows, studs, had fresh warm milk from their cafe! Everything about this place is beautiful

Title: A little underwhelming
Text: A little disappointed with this dairy farm which is popular with the locals. Not a lot to see and there is an entrance fee which is becoming a little annoying in Sri Lanka. Smelly barns where they keep the cows, Bulls and calfs. Basic cafe where they sell their produce. On a positive note, the surrounding countryside is beautiful and reminds one of New Zealand or Australia

Title: Best cool climate you will ever find in Sri Lanka
Text: This is one of the best places to visit if you are closer to NuwaraEliya. About 14 to 15 Km's from NuwaraEliya town and you can visit this place while you travel to Horton Plains as it's on the way.

Title: Ambewela Farms
Text:
A beautiful cattle farm, to be more specific a milk farm. Situated in the hilly region of Nuwaraeliya, spread almost across 1000 acres, Ambewela farms is a must visit for people of all ages. Almost 2lac Cows from Netherlands are bred in a natural environment. The grasslands are lush green and picturesque. One can also have a look at the milking of the cows if lucky to reach at the particular time. We reached at 12:30pm and were fortunate to have a peep at it. There are different sheds where one can even have a look at the humongous Bulls, just born calves, grown up calves, expecting mother cows. Also the farm breeds Netherland goats and super huge rabbits. The baby calves are too cute. 
          The amazing part about the entire farm is, the way everything is very well maintained and kept clean at all times. Also they have the cheese manufacturing unit and a cafeteria where one can have all kind of milk products. Their drinking yoghurt is worth trying. Photography is not allowed once you enter the main farm, but you can photograph the huge number of lazing around cows in the lush Greenlands while on your way.
            If you are traveling towards Nuwaraeliya then this is a must visit. Entrance ticket is not expensive at all for foreigners as well. Hardly 200 SL rupees p.p.

Title: Strictly OK
Text: It is not at all great. Can be given a miss except unless you have small children who might be interested in looking at the animals. Infact they hardly show any cheese manufacturing. There is quite a bit of walking also, so not recommended for old people.

Title: Love Cows, visit this place !!
Text: I had visited this place in the morning when the climate was at its best, cool and drizzling. There were hundreds of cows grazing all over the place and was a spectacular view.

Title: Don't waste your time unless you are desperate to see cows!
Text:
I am surprised at how this place got high ratings as it was the MOST uninteresting trip of our vacation!! The fee charged for foreigners is as usual higher than the locals (300 SLR if I remember right), but for this fee, there is no guide, no instructions, no signboards and no information about what goes on and what processes are followed on the farm. So we just walked around and saw a few sheds of pregnant cows, stud bulls and calves and a rather depressing shed containing rabbits in cramped cages. There are no sheds of goats or pigs. The cheese making unit wasn't functional. 
There is a small shop that serves products made there but you can get the same products at any regular grocery store in town. We witnessed the milking session which happens at various times of the day, but again, nothing spectacular - machines attached to the cows' udders to pump out the milk into large containers. 
The only beautiful part was the drive to Ambewala, and we got to see several cows grazing on vast green lands. This was pretty, but hardly worth the 3000 Sri Lankan rupees it cost to hire a vehicle to drive all the way there. 
Please skip this, unless, like I said, you just want to see cows!

Title: Interesting place to spend time at
Text: The place is located at  beautiful and scenic view area. We managed to see the cows goats and rabbits  farms inside the compound. the staff there were friendly and nice. its more or less like  a  mini New Zealand at Sri Lanka. For those who love the nature and fresh air this is the place to be at while you are at Nuwara Eliya.

Title: a must go place
Text: beautiful landscape,all photogenic,u will see windmills,drink different types of fresh milk and flavoured curd,a good place.

Title: Impressive farm with a great shop
Text:
Visited this farm with my local friends upon their suggestion. I have never been to milk farm in my country therefore it was very nice to see one.
We also loved the farm shop where the different diary products can be found. We were starving to something European and were happy to buy some gouda cheese made in Sri Lanka :) It was tasty and good quality.

Title: See Dutch cows in Sri Lanka
Text:
The New Zealand farm is located near the Horton Plains. They have a lot of Dutch Cows which they use for milk production. For a small price you can visit the farm and see the cows, the milking process and even a cheese factory.

Besides the cows they also have rabbits and goats. We felt sorry for the rabbits, they were in small cages without any hay on the floor. But besides that part of animal welfare it is nice to see the cows and how the factory works.

There are two restaurants were you can buy fresh milk and other products made of milk like cheese, butter and yoghurt.

Except for the poor conditions in which the rabbits live, this is an interesting place to visit.

Title: ambewala farms
Text: the approach to the farms is very scenic, miles and miles of green fields on either side. unfortunately when we went the factory was  closed.

Title: Relaxing and Lovely visit
Text: It was a very nice visit for my 2 kids (after many years in Europe) and very instructive one.. The sights are simply great.. and very relaxing; one feels himself not only traveling on Earth but also in Paradise; It was very nice to show my kids the Goats and their various ages, the Cows and the milk extractions, also the very little cows sitting near their mothers; we also saw the rabbits as well as the Bulls..

Title: Nice trip for families with young kids
Text: My two young children loved the trip to the farm where they saw cows, goats, rabbits in beautiful countryside surroundings.

Title: WORTH A VISIT
Text: You are in the midst of friendly set of farm hands.Do not forget to visit the factory that makes ice cream and yogurt and the wind power stations.It makes you proud of what distance Sri Lankans have travelled in setting up farms to international specifications. To me it better than the farms of New zealand and Denmark.i have seen better green only in Ireland.Visit either ambewela or New zealand farms under one management and enjoy the beauty of the highlands

Title: NIce
Text: The most I loved is the nature, surroundings and beauties of this area, more than the farm, which is of course a good one. Spending time around, breathe natural air, the breeze, the greenery, landscape around this are is just amazing. A most to visit place.

Title: Very Good
Text: The milk products for sale are really good. The curd which is a yoghurt is outstanding. Lots of really good cows and well maintained. Great place

Title: Good Day Out
Text: Visited on a very dull grey day but that did not spoil the outing.  Lovely to see the animals out in the fields.  Lots to see with milking, baby calves, goats, rabbits.   The have an "interesting" café where we sampled hot milk, yogart and various fried snacks. Take an umbrella and a jacket just in case

Title: Nice
Text: Nice place. Good fresh milk. i was visit with my family. and also nice location. kids are like very much. But Cheese factory was close.

Title: A unique experience
Text:
We visited Blue Field as part of our tour. This is one of the smaller factories in the area and offered a far more personalised experience as a result. 

Our host was only on her 2nd day of working there but was extremely knowledgeable and invited us to pluck some tea leaves, before a tour of the factory, and a tea tasting (R.s. 1,300). 

We thoroughly  enjoyed our visit and would highly recommend this estate.

Title: Unique and fascinating experience
Text: Great tour guide and tea tasting at a factory with a lot of history. Try the Blue Moon tea, I brought so much home with me!

Title: Bluefield tea gardens,Nuwara eliya
Text: Nice demonstration of processing of tea & welcome tea afterwards. First time came to know about the varieties of Ceylon tea.

Title: Breathtaking Beauty and a Cup of Tea
Text:
Visited on 20th February 2020

On our way to Nuwara Eliya from Kandy, we had a stopover at this Tea Estate to have a look at the tea manufacturing process and a hot cup of tea.

The place is beautiful and the process is knowledgeable. The Cafeteria is very well appointed and takes you back to English Imperial Ruling days.

Maintained in its original form this place is a welcome break from the long journey over a cup of tea.

You can also buy milk-tea at SLR 120/- and there are pastries and snacks to choose from ranging about SLR 150 to 300/-.

Products of the Tea estate are on sale at the souvenir shop. You may have  a look and decide accordingly.

Do not miss this place on your way to Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Free tour in old tea factory from 1921
Text: Guided by one of the nice workers we had a great tour trough the factory. The tours here are free. You can see the workers in the factory and take pictures, its nice if you give them something afterwards cause they only earn 750rs a day

Title: My cuppa tea
Text: Not my first tea factory walkabout but I still enjoyed hearing about it from our knowledgeable guide and the tea scent was heavenly. It was a nice, informative walk in the factory, before we were given some tasters in their tea room and offered to make a visit to their shop. Enjoyed the tea cake they sold too.

Title: Interesting
Text: This wasn't my first tea plantation but they explained everything very well while also entertaining and well worth the visit. There was the usual shop with a good range of teas with staff that were attentive and not intrusive.

Title: Great Tour. Recommended
Text:
As part of our tour of Sri Lanka we visited this fascinating tee plantation & factory. 
We were so fortunate to have Rasaq as our guide. What a friendly and knowledgable person. He told us he had been a guide for many years yet due to his boundless enthusiasm it seemed like we were his first ever tour. 
The factory is a trip back in time with 100 year old machinery and so much done by hand. So wonderful that the owners treated their staff like a big family.

Title: Real Tea Taste 
Text:
Blue Field Tea Gardens is an old factory established in 1921 during the British Clooney. They provide free tour and complementary cup of tea after the tour. 
Quick tour with one to one guide but useful to know enough about the tea plantation and processing. 

I liked the tour and their products. The price is normal as their brands not available in the market and you can only find it in their factory. 

Highly recommended for visiting.

Title: Generic like any other tea museum
Text: It was ok ok museum. I have seen better versions in Munnar. They hardly show you the processing of tea or green tea. Give you 5 min brief and give you come complimentary tea and lead you to tore for buying variety of teas packed fancily.

Title: Highly recommend!
Text: Good tour at Bluefield with their factory guide- very informative. Must try the tasting experience and tea cakes!

Title: Nice but overrated
Text:
If you have ever been to tea gardens or tea factory then you may choose to skip this. It is a decent place but the tea factory tour or view isn't worth it coz there are definitely much much prettier/ gorgeous tea gardens, in India at least. 
If you are around the area and have nothing much to do then no harm in giving it a try coz it is free and wouldn't take more than 30 minutes. 

I would rather sit and gorge at any of the valleys at nuwara eliya than recommend this place to anyone. Btw the cake is tasty and inexpensive!

Title: Very Informative Tour
Text:
We stopped by on our way to Ella as we wanted to understand further the unique, historical tea making process.

Our tour guide was great, spoke great English with our private tour going for approximately 20 minutes. We walked throughout the entire factory at our own pace, see all processes. The tour was free, with a free cup of tea at the end. 

Even when buying some tea at the end we were never pushed or forced into anything. The entire team was great and its well worth it.

On a side note you will notice the numerous signs for dumro tea factory. We stopped here for the view which was amazing, but didnt do the tour here, read the reviews before deciding to stop at this place...

Title: Tasting delicious tea in Nuwara Eliya.
Text:
There is a nice teahouse to try tea or other drinks. 

Guided presentation of tea preparation at the Pedro Tea factory.

Title: A true tea field experience. Much better than other tea fields.
Text:
A true tea field experience. Much better than other tea fields.

You can visit this one on your trip down from Nuwara to Kandy. Spread across huge expanse of land, this tea factory, its tour and the showroom was setup much better than Handunugoda Tea Estate.

The factory tour was given by their manager, who was well versed with the subject. He didn't rush into the presentation either. 

You will get a fair idea of the types of teas and how they are cultivated. The tea sample is served for free, sans the cake! The shop for purchase of tea is well laid out and you can get some real good packaging for gifting once you return to your home town.

If you are an India, be watchful as the tea is quite expensive to buy here, just like elsewhere in SL.

Date of Experience : March 2019.

Title: Blue Field tea Garden
Text: Blue field Tea Factory is situated near Ramboda on the way to Nuwara Eliya. This tea factory is oldest (more than 90 years old) in Sri Lanka and they are manufacturing Black Tea only. Raw materials Tea leaves are plucked from surrounding Tea Garden. Staff members explained the manner in which tea dust are prepared and we have seen all equipments which are very old. Tea is prepared in a natural way without adding any chemical or other substances. Entrance is free.

Title: Tea for 3
Text:
Loved the experience 
Had a very enjoyable tour of the facilities @ Bluefield Tea Gardens which unfortunately only had minimal workings on our day .
Loved the old machinery & seeing staff bag the tea .
Our guide a young girl spoke brilliant English & was very informative.
We enjoyed tea & cake @ a very reasonable price & also purchased some tea from the shop .

Title: So worth a visit!
Text: First of all, entrance is free! The factory is massive and full of history! The tea plantation covers a vast area too!!! Our guide was so knowledgeable that he explained very patiently and clearly everything we need to know about tea! Also treated to a complimentary tea tasting and of course we paid to try the best tea in the world- the golden tips! This is a must visit!

Title: In my opinion it's the best
Text:
In my opinion it's the best tea factory i visit in Srilanka ,
Good launch , very good tour in the factory,  dont forget to take gifts for your friends

Title: Excellent factory
Text:
Factory visit is quite detailed and to the point. Here you will know about the different variety of teas. I never heard about the white tea before. 

Neat and clean tea cafe. And a very good tea shop.

Title: Tea Factory once to be visited
Text: Visited this tea factory on way to Nuwara Eliya.  Saw the tea leaves drying . The sorting and fermentation processes were closed. Finally departed. We couldn't get guide as all were busy with whites.

Title: Amazing Factory
Text: Factory is fantastic and surrounded by breath taking view. Our tour guide Mr. Mohammad Sideeq was very friendly and professional. He provided us a lot of information about tea manufacturing process. The only negative thing is the overpriced tea products.

Title: Blue Field Tea Gardens
Text: Blue Field Tea Gardens is such an interesting place.  You learn all about the picking of tea leaves and all the machinery that is involved with the sorting of the tea.  Then, you get to taste the tea!

Title: Interesting and enjoyable, but feel sorry for the workers
Text:
You can't visit Sri Lanka without going to see a Tea Plantation, right ?!

So we were really pleased that our trip included a stop over here. Obviously there are lots of tea factories all over Sri Lanka, and we only visited this one, so cannot compare to any others, but I assume they are all very similar.

The tour takes you round the tea processing factory, as they explain the various stages of processing and different types of tea, and includes a cup of tea afterwards in the nice looking restaurant.

There is also the obligatory shop to purchase the vast number of teas from, much of which seemed a little high in price considering they made it on the premises (?). The teas in the fancy packaging seemed quite expensive and we felt it was a bit of a tourist rip-off, so we bought some of the cheaper variety to take home as a souvenir !

The whole thing took approximately one hour, which is just about right.

I was a bit disappointed that this  didn't  include a tour of the actual tea fields which surround and rise up into the hills around the tea factory.

However....  If you ask nicely then the tour guide will let you take a sneaky detour round the back into the plantation fields, where you can take photos of the tea and also some of the tea pickers - who will gladly pose for the photos if you give them some Sri Lanken Rupees (LRK) tips !

Whilst we enjoyed the experience, we felt saddened and astonished when we saw and found out about the quality of life and working conditions the workers were still enduring in the 21st Century.

None of them seemed to have any protective equipment, ear defenders, goggles, hard hats... despite working around noisy, fast moving and potentially dangerous looking machinery. Many of them were not even wearing shoes !!!!

Apparently the tea pickers earn something like just 500 rupees, which is just over £2, per day. And in return for this, they get very hard and rough skin on their hands from picking the leaves all day. Not the best life to live, is it ?!

So if you visit here and they do pose for photos, please be generous and give them a tip !  If just 2 tourists give them just  £1  tip for some photos, then that doubles their daily wage !

Title: lovely tour and tea
Text: A tour of the facility was worthwhile and gave a good understanding of the processes.  We then went to the cafe and enjoyed a cup of tea and the opportunity to taste some different teas.

Title: Great tour and shop
Text: Would definitely recommend the free tour if youre in the area. The cup of tea afterwards is a lovely treat and we also enjoyed some cake from the cafe! Lovely shop too.

Title: Nice Tea Factory, reasonable prices
Text: I liked this tea factory, many variety of teas, they make six type of teas. You can buy teas directly from this place with acceptable prices compared (I was told) with Colombo.

Title: Great visit
Text: Really enjoyed our visit to Bluefields, our guide was excellent. Tour was finished off with a lovely cup of tea.

Title: A Good Place to See Tea Processing
Text: Easier to reach, since this is roadside. They have built a path, so that you can walk along it and view the tea making process in steps. Clean factory. They also have a tea boutique where you can buy tea or drink a cup

Title: Great visit
Text: The tour was really interesting. We got shown step by step the processes of making tea. The guide spoke perfect English. The tea was nice to taste in the restaurant after.

Title: Informative tour of producing tea
Text:
We took a short tour with an english guide, He took us in a tea factory, while the production didn't worked. The tour was short and very informative. I missed some information about tea picking (how it is picked,...). At the end they show you the variety of teas, but you don't get the tea tasting. This is a big mistake. You must buy the tea, to taste it. It is not so expensive, but still, at the end of tours like that, you always expect some tasting, so that you know what to buy. It is the whole purpose of it. So at the end they lead you to the shop, but still, you didn't try it, so it is hard to buy. The prices here are OK, but for our taste there could be some basic black tea for cheaper price. Try to smell the Blue Moon tea, it is really great. Unfortunatelly we didn't buy it here, because we hoped to get it somewhere else, but we didn't. So buy it here, if you want to have it.
There is also a restaurant in the facilities, but we didn't try it. You can also have a lunch there.

Title: Saw the factory and bought some tea
Text: A lovely young lady showed us through the tea factory, which smelled wonderful. She was able to answer some questions but couldn't answer when I started talking tea grading and first flush tips etc. Sadly there was no tour of the plantation. Then it was a complimentary cup of their lowest grade tea and a shop. The tea is quite expensive and I bought some here and then discovered much better prices at the supermarket. However I was very happy that I did splurge and bought the evening tea - OPA - as it is truly delicious. Good quality, big leaves and doesn't require any milk or sugar as it's that good. I bought it in the cheapest container they had as the prices start to skyrocket when the packaging gets fancy. It's a nice setup they have here.

Title: Tour good
Text: The tour was quite good and we learned a lot about the process of how tea is made. It is something to do in Sri Lanka and why not? All part of the experience of such a beautiful country.

Title: Nothing very exciting
Text: It is just a hault on the way to Nuwara Elliya. The short tour is not very informative. It is slightly aromatic though. They take you to those parts which arent operational at that time, so we get to see only stationary machines. Tea tasting is also a long wait procedure. Tea i felt is expensive but the variety in packing is huge.

Title: Informative tour
Text: This was a relaxed & participatory tour of a tea plantation following the process from picking through to brewing and enjoying a cup of tea. Women are extensively employed from picking through the processing of a very hands on production. We started with trying our hand at picking the leaves. Staff in the shop were helpful with information about the different teas available.

Title: Tea factory & sales outlet
Text: The factory was closed since it was sunday, but a guide took us around and explained the process how tea is made from the leaves. The explanation could have been slightly more detailed & covered things like ft flush etc. It is basically a sales outlet for the world famous Sri Lankan tea & has a very good collection.

Title: Enjoyable and informative tour
Text: Enjoyed my short trip to the tea factory. Got to see some action in the factory ; the smell of the leaves being crushed was great. There were quite a few women working in there and I learned a lot about production and the selling at action. The shop is probably quite over priced but theres a nice cafe area to try the tea and get some food. A cup of silver tip tea was 170 rupees and was a new experience. Worth visiting if you want somewhere that isnt too busy with tourists.

Title: Nice walk through the tea bushes
Text: The format here is the same as other tea factories around the area where you get a free tour and tasting n the hope that you spend money n their shop. As this was our third scheduled tea factory on our day tuk-tuk tour of the area so we elected not to go in but took a walk through an area of the plantation behind the factory. It was really enjoyable to get up close to the tea shrubs and take in the scenery.

Title: Interesting and educating
Text: So, we actually learned a lot. We were met by Rasaq, a guide to the plantation and the factory. I guess that he gives the stort numerous times during a normal day, but nevertheless he was fun, vivid and clearly excited on the story of this old, still manually operated tea-factory. We liked the story, too. And we liked it so much, that we bouft more-than-normal quantities of tea. Which we enjoy today, back home, not least due to the fantastic story. Go visit, andenjoy

Title: Outstanding. An amazing experience
Text: We had booked onto a "Highlights Tour" with Viator, whom I would not recommend, as a tour operator, but the actual trip to the tea gardens was an excellent experience. We were taken around by a very knowledgeable lady and given a history and understanding of how tea is made, which was fascinating. The machinery used, was amazing, and the whole place gives you a real insight. We saw tea pickers, and learnt of their dedication to their job. The cafe and shop are both well worth a visit - prices very competitive, and of course, we had more understanding of what tea to buy, according to our own tastes. I would thoroughly recommend a visit here, but not through Viator!.  Get yourselves there by local transport, for a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

Title: Tea factory and plantation
Text: The guide was very informative and was very patient when answering our many questions.  We learned a great deal!

Title: Quality tea field experience
Text:
This is a great place.

Its in a beautiful setting, the factory surrounded by tea fields and when the sunshines, it looks fabulous.

A great little tour of the factory  just the right length with the right amount of information - and then a complimentary cup of tea

You can then browse the tea for sale in the shop without any pressure to buy. Of course, because there is no pressure and you take your time, you buy a lot more than if someone is looking over your shoulder all the time.

A great place to stop en route from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Good tea place on the way to nuwaraeliya
Text: Nice and clean place to stop for a tea on the way to nuwaraeliya. I like the milk tea its hot and delicious. I went with my foriegn friends as they have a good quality tea shop. There are many varieties of tea available with a good price. If you like to go to see the tea factory just a walking distance. We were there abouy 30 minutes to get relax and to buy tea.

Title: Interesting
Text: An old British era tea factory.  Since our visit was on the day after National, they didnt have fresh plucked leaves for processing. Only finishing section was working.  You can get a free cup of black tea.  You can also buy different varieties of teas which are sold in the outlet attached to it.

Title: Tea garden
Text:
Very informative.must see enroute to Nuwara eliya.lot of tea plantations.
Learnt about entire process, different types of teas .no entry fees. They offer complimentary tea 1 cup.the special teas green,gold,silver are chargeable.
Theres also a shop to buy the different types of teas ,nicely packed as gifts .prices vary

Title: Lovely
Text: If visiting a tea factory then there is no better, good to see the tea making process and then to visit the on site tea room for tea and in our case we visited in afternoon so we had cake. Also bought a box of tea to bring home all at good prices. Very helpful staff

Title: TEA TEA TEA
Text: A great place to go and learn about tea . Black white & green . You start with a tour of the factory and learn about the process from picking all the way threw to packing for distribution. A very knowledgeable tour we learn a lot about tea. You are then of too the cafe for a free tea or samples (at a cost ) Then the gift shop for tea sales and purchase . A great hour or so whilst on the way thru . Definitely worth a stop in .

Title: An insightful tour but rushed!
Text:
It was a friendly tour and a cup of tea given at the end but wouldnt return here. Would prefer more of a personal experience and taken to see tea growing, more interactive exhibits to view in own time rather than being rushed through. We were paired with another family who were french and struggled to translate quickly enough so one lady walked off mid your after being told we had a time limit of 20 mins to get around the factory and see the whole tour. I think it was actually quicker than that! 

It was great to see machinery working and the factory workers. Wouldnt liked to have a more personal experience, perhaps to do a bit of our own tea picking and the process ourselves- would be happy to pay more to do this.

Title: How tea is produced
Text:
This is one of the few places where you are taken through the entire tea leaf making process free of charge.
We were assigned a young guide Aushika who spoke good English and took us through the entire process.
We learnt about the various types of tea.
At the end of the tour we were asked to choose a tea that wed like to taste  at the tea room nearby.
The BOPF tea was free but we had to pay to try the other tea which were reasonably priced.
The chocolate cake was delicious.

Title: Great tour and food
Text: We were guided around by a lovely guide at no cost and sampled their tea at the cafe. You must try their pastries since they are fresh and exquisite. In comparison to the other tea factories I strongly recommend that you visit this ones

Title: A proper working factory, interesting and varied items in shop
Text: This was a great visit. In November, as low season, it was not at all busy and we had an interesting and informed guide. There is a very pleasant cafe and attractive, well stocked shop but maybe it is just me - I don't like being followed around by someone on my shoulder as I browse.

Title: If you are here for Tea factory process, it's good. Tea plantation garden view is pretty average.
Text: We came to visit Blue field just because our driver said it's one of the few places where they don't charge an entrance fee and explain the process well (though you are expected to pay a few hundreds of rupees as tips). We met our guide who knows a few Chinese and explained the process pretty clearly, though the whole visit lasted no longer than 15min. They then take you to a tea tasting section which you can enjoy a free cup of BOPF (kind of 2nd-but-last grade for tea bags. Noted we we to Damro later for tea and they claimed to use BOP which is 1 grade higher). The price of tea there is indeed 3 times more than what you can find in the supermarket or central markets (like in Nuwara Eliya and Kandy). Strangely they will tell you within the same grade the tea inside the packages are the same, but prices do varies a lot with different packages... What I learnt is that bigger brands like Lipton, Dimah, Mackswood are all sourcing teas from this tea garden partially so you can say what you buy out in the market also have no big difference in quality. What we don't really like about the place though, is the garden. We took a walk around and 1 old man approached us with a bunch of freshly picked tea leaves. Right next to him was another woman. They were not actually working, no sack no tools... They just ask you to take pictures of them and expect you to pay. Worst of all, after we gave them each 20Rs they are not happy with the amount and asked for more. If you really want to see the working tea puckers go to Pedro or Damro where you have better views and real puckers. Maybe because nowadays fewer people visit Pedro , I found the tea puckers so much more authentic and friendly than this one. They don't ask for tips. And when they receive some, I can see the real appreciation in their eyes. We ended up shooting nothing of the tea puckers in BlueField. Maybe also ask your guide or driver to see if they know that which parts of gardens have finished tea picking.

Title: Simply Tea
Text: Its all about knowing how tea is made. They have 100 year old equipment, robust time tested process & limited modernisation to give out great tea. A must place for tea lovers : Green, black, flavoured, white : you name it. Accepts all major cards. The Lunch organised by our tour Operator - Veena World was also of good quality.

Title: Family vacation
Text:
The tea factory was closed when we visited so could not see the functioning 
But the guide gave us a tour nevertheless 
Had complimentary tea which was yummy 
Go for it

Title: Very interesting
Text: Well, I never realised what went into making a cup of tea!  A very worthwhile hour spent visiting the factory and learning the various processes, followed by a much appreciated tasting.  Beautiful terraces of tea bushes - the surrounding countryside is stunning.

Title: Blue Fields Tea
Text: Nice cool place. Informative tour of tea process n a nice place to chill for tea n some cakes. Food available at 2nd level. Prayer place available for Muslims. Finally the highlight, shopping for various kind of teas from healthy white tea to fruity flavored teas.

Title: Ordinary
Text: The tour may be more interesting during an actual workday but we visited on Sunday. Still, one problem with tours lies with their organization--considering the small space with multiple groups and the resulting verbal competition of their guides. I have experienced better presentations at other plantations.

Title: Very informative and good views
Text:
The guide for The tea factory Mr. Abdullah was very good and proficient. He covered all the details related to tea processing 
Later we took some snaps of spectacular views from tea estate 
On return they provide a complementary black tea and restaurant is good with few simple eateries 
Overall a not to be missed experience

Title: Something new... tea picking on your own
Text:
100% run an managed by women... great!!

Tip: go into the fields and pick some tea on your own. Just ask your guide, its fun!!

Title: Interesting tea tour
Text: We did a brief tea tour here in October 2018.  It was very interesting seeing how tea is made, and what's involved.  Staff were very friendly.

Title: Tea Factory
Text: The property is spread in acres. Janu, our tour guide showed us around well. She explained well in English. The tea was delicious. The ambience of the restaurant and cozy private shacks were welcoming. They had olden style machines in display and some of the active machinery were still operational since the inception of the factory.

Title: Great cafe and tea gift shop
Text: Enjoyed our visit here and the tour of the process we received. The gift shop is extensive and allows you to get your gifts for your return home. The staff are warm and welcoming and the cafe very good. A nice place to visit.

Title: Auto pilot visitor handling
Text:
Maybe we just ran into a bad guide, but this was very uninspiring. I think even a audio cassette could impress me more. Also, when taking a look at the tea garden.. You get swamped by old ladies asking for money (for a picture) and not willing you to take any pictures without them on it. Really looked forward to see this interesting site but it all resulted in pretty much a deception. 
To improve: get those ladies out of the garden and organize paid tours and make it worth the money.

Title: One of the best
Text: Worthwhile visiting.  Variety of tea leaves.  The whole process of tea making is marvellous, efficient and perfectly carried out.  Our guide Ms. Prasadi is one of the best guides they can ever hire.  She was so genuine, polite, respectful and her explanation was crystal clear.  The tea gift shop is excellent.  The tea plantation view is wonderful.

Title: Paradise of Greenery
Text:
On our way from Kandy, we dropped by Bluefields. Upon reaching the estate we went to the tea fields behind the factory, where the tea pickers were working. 
P.S: You will find  tea pickers requesting for a a photograph/video & then asking for donation. Paying them is an individual choice & is not compulsory. 

At the tea factory we were greeted by our guide, Dinusha Maduwanthi. She was superb at her job! She took us around the factory, while giving us an insight to the tea making process. Dinusha then walked us through the plantations. For city dwellers like ourselves, this was a totally  different experience!

Post the tour, visitors are treated to free tea. P. S. only the black tea is free. I tried the Silvertips Tea, which they refer to as "White Tea". Unfortunately it didn't taste any different, from regular tea & was not worth LKR 180.

Otherwise our visit at Bluefields was lovely! 

Entry Fee: Nil

Best time to visit: Morning - as you get a chance to see the tea pickers work

P. S. Wear sport shoes

Title: Good, yet not for the dedicated tea drinkers
Text: Efficient quick and painless. Quick overview of the process, the mearly 100 years old processing machines are impressive and still operate well. It is a co-operative mainly producing white label for big brands. Simple plain experience. In case you are a serious tea person select another estate.

Title: Informative
Text:
First appearances are that the site is a bit tired looking but we were greeted by our guide called Razar. He was obviously very passionate about the factory and how its still running unchanged since it was first opened nearly 100 years ago. 

He took us through the full process of how tea is made from the plucking to the fermentation and end product.

There are better tea factories to visit in the area but our driver recommended it to us on our way to our next destination. A nice enough stop off for a free cuppa...well nearly free ??

Title: Interesting tour in nice surroundings. Tasty tea!
Text: Stopped off here on our way from Kandy to Ella. We arrived on a Sunday when the factory wasn't active but still got an informative, free tour from a very helpful guide (tip recommended). After the tour we received a free cup on Blue Field tea, and bought some cake to go with it. At no point were we pressured into buying anything, but decided to pick up some tea from their shop, which we thought was quite good value. After our tea and cakes, we wandered around the tea fields behind the factory, where we were again provided with a free guided walk by one of the tea pickers. A nice experience, and worth a visit.

Title: Very informative trip
Text:
Our driver recommend a stop here over the other tea plantations, and for what it was worth, he made a good choice. 

Unfortunately for us, we visited the tea factory on the weekend of "poga" which is a buddhist/hindu holiday so the factory was not functional that weekend. However, our guide was extremely knowledgeable and informative, who took time to understand and answer any questions we had about the tea and the tea making process.

The tour then ended by us being offered a cup of tea for free to try - any cake/pastry purchase is optional and at no point did our guide try to make a sale. The tea shop beside the restaurant was being mobbed by everyone who visited and us as well.

Now that we are home and i've tried their teas, I can definitely say that the tea tastes divine.

Do stop by to learn and sample a cuppa.

Title: Worth the visit
Text:
We dropped into Bluefield tea gardens on our way to Ella from Kandy. 
We ended up having lunch at their buffet - I think it was towards the end of their service, so some of the dishes may have suffered a little from being out for a while. It was adequate but certainly nothing to write home about. It was free for our driver. 
We got an informative tour of the tea factory and learnt a lot from our very informative guide Razaq. I kind of did not realise green tea was just a different harvested leaf from which black tea was from. In their tea cafe we tied their most prized type of tea - a white tea called golden tips - I had never had this before but it is from the very young leaf buds of the the tea tree. It was so good we ended up buying 4 tins in their shop to take home with us! A new taste experience which we were excited about. 
The factory is one of the more traditional types and well worth the visit.

Title: Worthwhile stop
Text: We made a pit stop to the Blue Field Tea Gardens on our way to Kandy. Our guide Adhil gave us a quick, yet detailed tour of the factory and explained the intricate tea making process. We got to taste the different varieties of delicious tea and explore the gift shop. Definitely recommend!

Title: Old school tea plantations visit
Text: We had a lovely tour around the plantation and factory. Very educational and we purchased some of the expensive tea because it seemed very nice quality and all hand made.

Title: Great tour & delicious teas.
Text:
It was great to learn about the tea plantations in Sri Lanka. Your staff are very knowledgeable and friendly. Muhammad answered all of our questions. 

You have a great range of teas for a good price at your gift shop and I loved exploring the factory and seeing how the tea is processed. 

Thank you

Title: One of the old tea factories on the road to Nuwara Eliya
Text: The visit to the tea factory is very artificial, the demonstrator didn't had any passion, he was also not aware of many things that we asked him.

Title: Amazing tour and tasty tea
Text: Great tour around the tea factory - very interesting.  Afternoon tea was served and tasty cakes!!  We bought several packets of tea to bring home.

Title: One of the best Tea Brand
Text:
This is one of the best brand. They show us how the Tea is manufactured.  We can buy tea ...we are given tea for tasting also. 

OPA is the best....

Title: Very nice factory
Text: Nice factory with very friendly staff. Short introduction about the tea process and small tea tasting at the end. Recommended.

Title: Free factory visit and complementary tea
Text:
We stopped here on a tuk tuk tour out of Nuwara Eliya. The tour of the tea factory was very good showing all the stages of the processes to make tea. The chap was very knowledgeable and answered all of our questions. 

We then were shown to the tea room and given a complementary cup of BOP tea. There is cake also on offer. 

The shop was rammed with chinese tourists buying up loads of tea. Funny to see as you would almost think they cant get it there! 

You have to pay extra to do a tea tasting. 

Toilets were clean.

Title: Interesting Visit
Text: I have been to other tea estates/factories, but the tour here was the best; instructional and interesting, learning about the different grades of tea. Topped off with a nice cup of tea and the opportunity to buy tea to take back home

Title: Great setting good tour
Text: Lovely tour with enthusiastic guide. Photos allowed. Lovely seating outdoors to sample the tea. Would recommend.

Title: Interesting insight into how tea is processed
Text: Interesting tour of the processing plant to see the different stages that the leaves of tea go through in order to be tea leaves!  Don't think the process or the machines have changed in donkeys years.  Good explanation of the different teas they produce, followed by a complimentary cup of tea!  Worth visiting

Title: A nice place to Have a Break on the way To Nuwaraliya
Text:
On the Way To Nuwaraliya From Kandy, We Stopped here for a Break

  This Place has Different types of Tea and Fresh tea with Fresh Smell.

 The restaurant offers some Good food as Well, But more than the food a Piece of Cake and fresh Tea would make the day

Title: Interesting but not the best tour
Text: The tour in the bluefield tea gardens was all right but not as good as other tours Ive done in Sri Lanka. Their tea is very good though and I recommend you taste their chocolate cake.

Title: Ideal tea visit
Text: We were not set on any single tea plantation and went to this one at the recommendation of the driver who had picked us up at the train station. A free cup of tea is given before or after your tour, and the factory is small enough that you can get pretty close to the equipment and really understand the process. You can walk the fields behind the factory too, and there is an AMAZING view of the valley if you make it over the first hill.

Title: Good stopover
Text: This place is good to stop over when you are travelling from or to Kandy. Worth of doing a tour and pure tea

Title: Lovely tour and tea!
Text:
We had a great tour of the factory, just the right length for us and the kids. Interesting learning about the different teas and how they are produced. We saw most of the machinery working, our tour was in the morning.

We bought quite a bit of tea in the shop,  thought the price was fine.  The cafe was great with lovely free tea and reasonably priced silver tip tea.  The cakes and samosas were superb and the staff were all very friendly

Title: A good place to stop
Text: We got a tour of the tea factory which was educational.  There is a restaurant and gift shop.  The food in the restaurant was inexpensive and generous portions.

Title: Nice place to enjoy a cup of Tea
Text: Definitely one of my tops 5 things to do in Sri-Lanka. We have enjoyed our visit to the factory and learning so much thing regarding the history of tea. As a Tea lover is was nice seeing and learning about the process of creation, not forgetting all Womens and mans hands behind the process, because its not something easy. Please dont forget to be respectful and nice with those hard-working people ( a tip will be much appreciated )s

Title: Nice place for a break
Text: You will see this place on the way to Nuwara-Eliya, so it is a good place to take a break from the long drive. They have a nice restaurant with delicious food and clean washrooms.

Title: Tea tasting in cafe.
Text:
As we had already done a plantation tour elsewhere we just went to the cafe.  

It was lovely sitting out in the garden enjoying tea and cake.  I ordered a tea tasting session,  600rs for about 10 different full cups of tea.  It gives you a chance to work out which ones you actually like.  

The tea in the shop is expensive ($35aud for 500g of orange pokoe - can buy it in Australia for $18 per kilo).  

Come here to taste all varieties of tea,  but buy tea's elsewhere.

Title: Short but informative tour
Text: The tour was just the right length for me - brief but informative. Despite the signs prohibiting photography, I was allowed to take photos. Be aware though, that as soon as I snapped a pic including one of the factory ladies, the hands came out for donations - oops. At the end of the tour I was dropped off at the cafe/gift shop for a free cup of lower grade tea. Higher grade teas are available for a reasonable fee. No pressure, no sales pitch.

Title: Definitely worth a visit
Text: Informative free tour. Can wander the tea plantations afterwards on own. Couldn't find any tea pickers in the plantation when we went. Complimentary tea - tried the strongest tea (Dust No 1), which was a great cuppa. Great and cheap cakes in the tea shop.

Title: Just a side of tea education
Text:
The bluefield tea factory is on the way towards the hotel which we chose in Nuwara Eliya. On arrival there a tour guide gives you a very small talk around the factory and then you get a complimentary tea to taste. Also there is a plantation for you to have a look at and walk through. 

They do explain well the tea process and also the grading of the tea. There is also a shop which you can buy the teas as well. However do have a look at the pricing in some cases for a little bit more money you get much more tea. Also the gift sets are a bit pricey. There is food available but where the food is there is also some flies there...

Title: Great tour, great tea
Text: My husband and I visited Bluefield as part of a day trip around Nuwara Eliya, and it was the highlight of the day. We started with a really informative tour of the tea factory itself, followed by a tea tasting. We could have had a free cup of tea each, but opted to pay a small amount (600 rupees, about £3) to try all the different types of tea - we were pleasantly surprised to find that this even included both types of the famous white tea, golden tips and silver tips (delicious!). We were so impressed that we bought quite a lot of tea in their shop - which was much more reasonably priced than the other tea factory we had visited earlier on that day. Altogether a great experience.

Title: Amazing experience
Text: It was a very interesting tour for us. This was the very first time I got to know about the tea plantation. Finally we know the process, it was very educational. We went to the around the factory with a really knowledgeable guide. It was actually exciting to study how the tea is made. There is small restaurant inside the factory our friend Ilham bought some cakes for us and waiter gave a free plan-tea for us. There are many of tea estates and tea factories on the way to Nuwara-eliya but our tour guide and  our friend Mr.Ilham Rameez recommend this place absolutely its an amazing experience in my life .At the end we would like to thank everyone.

Title: Tea estates...
Text: Nuwara eliya weather is apt for tea farming and you will find many tea estates here. Great to view how they make tea

Title: The Tea Factory
Text: We had a personalized tour of the Tea Factory and how it operates and this was recommended to us by our driver. It was a very interesting tour for all of us. This was the very first time i got to know and all these days i was wondering how tea is looking black in color while all plantations are fully green. Now that i know the process, it was very educational.

Title: Not as good as Damro Tea Plantation
Text:
We first visited Damro and it was great. Great view, silver service tea (free) and tour of the working factory.
BUT then we went to Blue Fields and were disappointed by the tea (we paid for) and poor service.
Not recommended.

Title: Great tour
Text:
We sampled the various tea and were shown around the factory with a really good guide. It was really interesting to learn how the tea is made and the different process to arrive at the various teas.

We tipped the guide at the end.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: This was the first time we visited a tea factory and it was interesting to learn about the lengthy process to make tea. Our guide was excellent, no charge for the tour, but we gave our guide a small tip. We would have loved to go into the fields where they were picking leaves, but it was raining so didn't, so not sure this would usually be part of the your.

Title: Where do we get our tea from
Text: Fabulous experience visiting the tea plantations and seeing the lady tea pluckers in the fields working very hard for very little.  Long days and minimal pay, but happy and polite and only too willing to let you have a photograph with them. They start work early and work until late and for this they get an approximate payment of £4/£5 per day. There is a minimum amount of tea leaves that have to be stored in their back packs in order for them to get paid. However, they do get cups of tea and have a short break.

Title: have food will travel
Text:
I was not expecting much but the free guide of the oldest tea factory in Sri Lanka was actually very informative
Seeing how they dry the leaves such a tedious process. all hand picked!! the tea tasing was also fun I hadn't rallied that all tea comes from the one plant 
cakes were ok but it was a nice thing to do in the heart of tea country

Title: Informative but beware the tea pluckers and leaches.
Text:
An interesting insight into a working tea factory. It could be a really good tour. It is free but actually I would rather have paid something and got a tea tasting or something as well.

The factory is dimly lit and has no real soul- very odd feeling inside.

Shop is ok and plenty of stock.

Be very careful if the tea ladies usher you out to the fields, they will let you take their picture but agressively demand money afterwards. 

This is awkward for you and if they are caught can be sacked so don't do it.

Title: Good way to learn about tea
Text:
Situated around 20km outside Nuwara Eliya Bluefields Tea is well worth the drive to get there. You can have a free tour of the factory where you will learn about how tea is grown, harvested, and processed into the product tea drinkers know and love. At the end of the tour you can choose to have a free cup of tea. The shop has a lovely selection of cakes (you pay for these).
The Tea Shop has quite a collection of different teas from the Estate for purchase for a reasonable amount - price varies depending on the type of tea you buy and how much. My biggest challenge was choosing.
It takes 45 minutes to 1 hour to get there by Tuk Tuk - the road winds up and down hills and valleys. It's a picturesque drive - you can see tea plantations and workers; and spectacular scenery. 
Allow 2-3 hours, it's worth it.

Title: Great Tea Estate to visit, tour and taste
Text:
Find out which is your favourite tea flavour.
Great tour of the estate followed by tea tasting. I did a great shop of teas in the shop for my tea crazy family at home!
Really enjoyed the visit.
thank you
Samantha

Title: Good place
Text: We went to Bluefield Tea Gardens on our way to Nuwara Eliya. As soon as we entered a representative took us to the factory and explained us the process of tea making, after which they served us a cup of black tea which was complimentary. You can also order from the coffee shop menu if you want anything else. They have a store where you can buy different types of tea. You can also visit the tea garden to take pictures, but unfortunately we were not able to go there as it was raining heavily.

Title: good visit
Text: would visit if in the area and after a genuine / old school experience. there are other factories in the area too

Title: Watch how the tea is processed then have your quality cupp of tea
Text:
We stopped on our way to the Forest View Lodge at the Bluefield tea gardens.The Factory staff was courteous,informative and helped the members of our group to understand how tea is processed.The Tea pluckers pose with tourists.They earn a meager salary for many hours of hard work.
The Tea was good quality.The staff at the sales outlet was knowledgeable and promoted the value of tea as a health drink.They have good PR skills..The best quality tea is out of this world

Title: Must visit tea plantation in Nuwara Eliya!
Text: We came across this beautiful tea plantation on our way to Kandy. We were walking to the entrance and were instantly greeted by a friendly tour guide, Mursheey. This was very different to our experience at Damro Tea, where we were waiting for about 20-30 minutes with no one acknowledging that we were there or anyone offering a guide. The tours here are free and the guides will take you around the whole factory providing information about the tea making process as well as history of the plantation. It was great! There was plenty of opportunities for photos and to ask questions. At the end of the tour, you are given a free black tea. There is no obligation to tip or pay any fee, we decided to tip our tour guide as he was excellent :) would definitely recommend this visit as part of your trip in Nuwara Eliya if you get an opportunity :)

Title: Beautiful tea garden
Text:
This area is very clean. They provide a free tour how tea is manufactured. There is also a shop where you will find different kinds of teas. 
It can be tour of one to two hours mostly but do try the tea at the shop.
It's one the of biggest tea supplier in Sri Lanka and I totally enjoyed the view, taste and beautiful landscape there

Title: Tourist stop !!
Text: Too many tourists, free tour is informative , geared towards selling tea after free tour. Café was okay. All staff quite friendly

Title: Good for a quick visit
Text:
The factory was not operating when we visited as it was a holiday. The guide gave a good explanation of the process. You did not seem to be able to wander through the plantation. There was a childrens play area.

The tea seemed rather expensive so we did not buy any although there were many different grades available. We had a cup of tea but it was not served in a pot and was rather too strong for our taste. There are cakes available to buy at the counter too.

Title: Nice tour and shop
Text:
Nice tour of the tea processing facility with a knowledgeable guide who spoke very good English. Not so impressed with the way the guide said we could/should tip her afterwards then walked away as soon as she got some money.
The free tea was not as good as I expected from a tea plantation, seemed to have been brewed too long. 
The shop was good - every kind of tea and no pressure to buy anything.

Title: great visit
Text: We had a tour of this tea factory and it was so interesting to see all the process the tea goes through to give us a good brew. The shop is good and has reasonably priced tea to take home

Title: Very nice tea
Text:
Had about a 20 minute private tour around the tea factory where you get to see how tea goes from the plants in the plantations to the tea you drink - was great to see all the old machinery still being used as well.
The lady that showed us round was very nice, spoke slow and very pronounced English which was easy to understand.
Im never sure how this kind of thing works regarding payment as it was part of the tour. I gave a 500 tip which seems fair to me, she seemed happy enough.
We also got a free cup of tea each at the end, you can order more of different types but the one just to try was enough for us.

Title: Highly Recommended
Text:
We came here instead of Mackwood (now rebranded) and had a fabulous time.

Met by a guide, Adil, who showed us around the plantation and explained the process. We watched pickers, took loads of photos and were impressed by the scale and organisation of the place.

Back in the factory, they let us gets hands on with loading of leaves into the various hoppers.

If you take a pic of a person working, please do remember to give them some rupees, its only polite - 50 should do it!

Loved the processing plant and tea sampling - came away from the shop with various ones to try at home.

All in it took about 90 minutes and was not expensive. We tipped our guide 500 which our driver said was the going rate.

Too Tip: Go early morning before the school tours come!

Title: Good tour with no pestering on buying products
Text: The best part is that they do not pester you to buy products from their store and all the while give you proper attention while giving a tour of the factory. The tour is short but detailed enough to know the nitty-gritty of the tea process.

Title: Interesting but too short
Text: It was very interesting and nice to see the when the factory was running. The "tour" was a bit too short and rushed (like 5 min). Our guide was nice but it sounded like a recorded text from a book. After the tour you get a free cup of tea. It's a nice visit of you stop by on the way but it's not worth a daytrip.

Title: Short stop on our way
Text:
Stopped here on our way to Nuwara Eliya. Unfortunately for us it was a national holiday so there was no tea picking going on.

We had a tour of the factory though which was still interesting and a cuppa in the cafe. Should really have gone back the following week when it was a normal working day as I imagine there would be more to see.

The tour is free and the cafe is cheap. Should have bought more tea as well as it is so good and so much cheaper than home.

Title: good tour and visit
Text: we were offered a place on a tour as soon as we arrived. Our guide spoke in English and had a Chinese couple and Japanese couple in addition to us. He was very knowledgeable and spoke very clearly. Tour was 15 minutes and then we went into the cafe for a nice & cheap cup of tea from the various selections on offer. Then there is a tea shop to buy your choice of teas if you wish. No pressure to buy anything. An enjoyable break on the journey to Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Now I know more about tea!
Text:
Interesting visit to a tea factory. I drink so much of the stuff that its nice to see how its produced. We saw the whole process and then were treated to a cuppa. 
As we drove away we saw the women working in the plantations. It was very interesting and a good photo opportunity.

Title: Interesting free tour
Text: I wasn't that keen but it actually was really interesting to see how it all works! We enjoyed tea and samosa afterwards. There's a great shop but no pressure to buy anything

Title: Bluefield Tea Gardens Ramboda, Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka
Text: The Blue Field Tea Garden cum Factory was establish in 1921 here we see the procedure of manufacture of tea in factory. We see various kind of tea and test one of them after we go to their outlet and purchase some Srilankan tea. The cost of tea was just double with Indian tea but the cost in Indian currency is near about same.

Title: Learn about your cuppa
Text: Stopped here on a tour of tea country and had a nice tour of the factory.  Saw all the old machines, some almost 100 years old and still working.  After the tour, went to the tasting room and had a nice BOP (gotta come here to learn what that is).  I'm not a tea drinker, but I could be one if all the tea was good.  No pressure to buy tea at the shop, they just left us on our own.  I like that!

Title: Fantastic and informative guided tour of tea facoty
Text:
My father and I stopped in to Blue Fielda Tea Gardens for a guided tour of the factory and to sample the tea that they produce. We were very impressed with Mirshad who was very knowledgable and communicated the process of how the tea was processed. We were able to talk through the factory and got to explore the tea fields as well. 

After the tour we had a tea tasting of the 2 white teas, 1 green tea and 6 black teas.

Beautiful and highly recommend this experience! 

Victoria and Brett

Title: Good Tea Tour
Text: Good start on the types of tea , production, packaging then to the external tea terraces where you can mingle with the tea pickers. Avoid the around mid day as it can be hot. As usual there is a tea shop for you to you type of tea.

Title: Interesting experience with some history
Text:
Im not sure why, but all of he locals want to take you to one of the more modern plantations. We did blue fields and another.

This one was by far the better tour and experience. It was working, with machines processing the leaves etc.

There are others with better scenery... but the other one we visited was more like a tourist trap rather than a plantation.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Went here today and was very happy with the tour, the guide, the little cafe and the tea shop. The grounds were lovely, well kept and so colourful. While this is not the biggest tea plantation in Nuwara Elia it is Sri Lankan  owned and well worth the visit. Best of all there was no pressure to buy and no one hovered over you like we have experienced in other places.

Title: Excellent overview of tea growing and production
Text: I really enjoyed the hour here looking at the tea plantation and then being given a tour through the factory and seeing the process. Also learnt a lot about the types of tea produced in Sri Lanka and bought some tasty Orange Pekoe(OP) as a souvenir.

Title: Good variety in tea store
Text: We did not take the free garden/factory tour but we shopped at the tea store. It was very well attended by tourists, and the parking lot was quite full.  Attendants advised and helped people buy tea. We were surprised that the cashier refused to take credit cards without giving us a reason.  Perhaps the phone lines were unreliable due to the rains, but in any event we had to reduce the number of items and pay cash for our purchase. They have a good variety of teas, and the prices were competitive.

Title: Excellent tour, highly informative
Text: Our tour guide, Razar, was enthusiastic and knowledgeable! The factory was actually in operation when we visited so we could the machinery in action. Highly recommend - tea shop had reasonably priced teas and the tour comes with a complimentary cup of English breakfast tea. This was one of the highlights of the trip.

Title: Impressive Factory but Expensive Tea Shop
Text:
We visited this factory located in beautiful hilly surroundings ,with manually operated machines in a 100 years old building and came out impressed with its focus on giving large employment to locals.They only process black tea here.The guide was a knowledgeable fellow,an employee of the factory.
The tour was completed with a complimentary cup of tea offered in the cafe located beside the factory.The cafe is a bare minimum joint,having select food items.

An adjoining factory shop was selling all kinds of tea processed by the company.They had all kinds of varieties of tea,some gift packed too. 

We purchased 200 grams boxes of masala chai flavored black tea at SriLankan Rupees 1600 each,which was expensive compared to buying beautifully packed 40 pcs Dilmah tea bags at Odel, Colombo for SLR 1100. Dilmah being a premium brand is a better gifting option at this price range.

Most of the tea factory and estates follow the same business practice,and I would suggest to check other brands tea prices at local superstores before buying from these factory shops-they charge a premium for their teas.

Title: Very informative
Text: It was good to learn how much of work goes into that cup of tea you drink. Mohammed was our guide for the day and explained every bit of the process in detail.   We were even given the opportunity to pluck some tea leaves. The whole tour was free including nice cup of tea at the end of it. You can buy cakes with your tea.
