And then your taken to a shop where you can purchase the different types of tea leaves and tea powders. They even have a restaurant there with traditional srilankan food

Title: Nice tour
Text: Its been an interesting tour. Doesnt take much time. The guide was proffesional and nice. Weve visited several factories while in Sri Lanka and we found this one to have the best tea shop.

Title: Interesting little tour
Text: Came here in April with my partner and our three youngest children.  Our guide was very friendly and knowledgeable and explained everything within the factory, giving a clear explanation of how the different teas were made and explaining each stage of production.  We were allowed to take photos and we were also encouraged to help on the production line (which the children really enjoyed).  At the end of the tour you are served with a cup of tea and you can have a browse in the tea shop (but you do not feel under pressure to buy anything - we did not make any purchases).

Title: Very friendly
Text: Very friendly guides who will show you around the factory and serve you with hot piping black tea. All of this is free and no cost. You can choose to buy tea from their store, but no compulsions. A must try place.

Title: Enjoyable and education tour
Text: We really enjoyed the tour to this tea factory.  Very informative and a great experience for the whole family.

Title: Good tour guide
Text: We got a tour by Razaq. Friendly man who gave us a very good and clear explanation of the working process of producing tea. Afterwards we could taste the tea and buy some in the shop. Prices were very ok (paid around 500-600Rs for 200-250gr). There is no entry fee but tips are always accepted.

Title: Great experience
Text: It was an unforgettable experience, we learned very interesting information about the tea production process, the lady who was guiding us was very polite and informative, she made sure that everything we see in the factory is well explained and understood.

Title: Place to know about how tea is made
Text: This is on the way from Kandy to Newura Eliya and is a good place to stop over not only to stretch legs but also to learn during the stop over. We got a good insight into how the tea is produced and knowledge regarding different types of tea. It has a coffee shop where you get complimentary tea. There is a pastry shop where one can buy pastries. There is a shop where they sell different varieties of tea. No need to go there exclusively to see but can be used as a good stopover.

Title: Educating tea tour
Text: Take 15 min time to learn about the tea production and sip a cup of fresh tea. Free of charge, while the tea in the shop is definitely overrated. Well, these guys need to get the money somehow...

Title: Tea is exorbitantly priced.
Text: Nothing exciting about the tea estate. Tea is so highly priced that it is advisable to purchase in Colombo

Title: Good place to learn more about the tea production
Text:
A good place to learn more about tea production. Every group / couple gets its onw guide who will tell you all about the tea production. Make sure you keep up, as the tour is very fast. Don't mind to ask them to explain again, as they do try to get you in & out within 10 minutes.
There is no activity in the factory at Sundays. So it is best to visit an other day of the week. 
After the (free) tour, you get a free cup of tea. 
There is also a restaurant if you like.
The tea shop has all kinds of tea from this estate. 
No one was pushing us to buy anything, so you can take the tour and tea for free.

Title: Excellent tour without the tourist hype
Text: Set in a beautiful location, there is no cost attached to the very professionally conducted, informative factory tour that including a cup of tea at the end.  It also appeared to be less crowded than some of the other better known places so we had our guide to ourselves. Her English was excellent and her knowledge vast, from information re the history of the tea growing area, the development of the processing and current marketing strategies. I learned that Dilmah is just another wholesaler like Liptons so no need to pay extra - very important information.  Naturally, we purchased some of their "free-of-additives" tea and it is delicious. If you would like a relaxed hype-free tea plantation tour, this is the place ??

Title: Family vacation
Text:
Visited this tea estate in nuwara eliya. Great location. Brought some tea for friends. Place even has kids play area
They served freshly brewed black tea

Title: Nice even in the rain
Text: Good guide worth the stop nice tea and cake.  Makes one appreciate tea more when you realise how hard tea puckers work plus the machine operators doing their bit

Title: Short tour and not very authentic
Text: The tour was short and did not seem very authentic, the tour was less than half an hour and it did not seem like we saw the whole actual factory. The guide was good. The factory was full with touring cars with big groups of people. There is also a shop and buffet lunch restaurant.

Title: tour in less than 10minutes
Text: we were thrilled to learn about tea from the history to consumer, however we were guided through the factory in a very expeditive course which lasted no more than 10minutes. we were offered a complementary tea cup at the end and left there "to enjoy"

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Very helpful guide was provided and took us round the factory and gave an explanatory the different types and grades of tea. The tour was free. We could take pictures. Some history of the plantation would have been useful, eg some display boards to read. We were taken to the café and could buy tea and we also had tasty chocolate cake. It would have been even better if we could have had a tasting of the different teas, which we could have paid for as an extra. We were able to buy tea from the well presented and stocked shop.

Title: A place of learning how to make "Tea".
Text: Nice place to learn how to make tea from a leaf. New experience. Beautiful surrounding views. Well English speaking in house guide. Great hospitality with a fresh cup of tea.

Title: Good place to see how tea is made.
Text: We were given a guide to take us around to show the factory. This was free of charge. The guide was very informative and patient with all our questions. At the end of the tour we were offered free tea to taste.

Title: Our visit Bluefield tea gardens.
Text: On the way from nuwara Eliya to Kandy we visited Bluefield tea gardens. The tea factory situated in a beautiful area, surrounding with green tea plantations, streams, valleys. They invited with hot tasty tea with a friendly smile. We visited the factory with a instructor who explain all the way of tea process and types of tea. That's good but the instructor(guide) explain like audio display. Need little deep explanation. Any how that was a great experiences. They have a store with many verity of teas. Feel little expensive but worth.

Title: Free guide
Text:
We'd been to tea plantations in the past in Malaysia but this offered a free guide, which made the whole thing a lot more interesting. She was very pleasant and gave us a nice insight into the process. There was even a free cuppa at the end.

We just gave her a tip for her troubles.

Title: A quick and interesting stop off the main road
Text: Stopped here on the road from Kandy to Nuwara Eilya and had a tour this only lasts about 15-20mins and it's free although we tipped the lady who took us round a small amount. Interesting to see the tea making process and to learn about the different types of tea, we purchased some ta after the tour but there was no pressure to buy anything. At the end of the tour they give you a free cuppa which is a nice touch.

Title: A good road side stop serving Bluefield brand tea with cakes, muffins etc,
Text: Good tea available, can buy various Blueiled tea products, may watch Bluefield Factory for tea making process, can enjoy the scenic view;

Title: Nice visit
Text: Its a nice visit to do. The guide was friendly and showed us the tea plantation and afterwarfs showed us all the process to manufacture the tea. Afterwars they invite us to a cup of tea that was very good.

Title: Best roundtrip to Udawalawe National Park, arranged by Mr.Indika Dissanayaka
Text:
We are a german couple, visiting Sri Lanka as we met Mr. Indika Dissanayaka on the beach near our hotel Pandanus Beach Resort & Spa. He is speaking german really excellent, so we decided to go on a tour to Udawalawe Nationalpark. But I don`t like to travel with a lot of other guests, because if we could take this guided tour on ourselves, we can stop where we want, stay as long as we want :-).
Mr. Indika Dissanayaka arranged an extraordinary tour for us, with taxi transfer, guided tour through Udawalawe Nationalpark with orphaned Elefants Residence and after all a short visit in Fort Galle.
This has been an exciting, interesting tour with a lot of comfort (the Taxidriver understands German Language) because we could pause and stop at the interesting places as we want.
Thanks a lot, I`ll tell all my friends to get this tour via I.D.Tours Mr. Indika Dissanayaka

Title: Short tour followed by FABULOUS pot of tea.
Text: The title says it all.  The free tour was basic but interesting and the follow up free pot of tea was to die for

Title: fantastic hill view
Text: tea gardens surrounding with hills....absolutely amazing view. tea was nice as well. this is a must stop place on the way to Nuawara Eliya

Title: Awesome teas
Text:
A great place to explore and see how Sri Lanka produces their world famous tea..
You can take guided tours at no cost but I can guarantee you will purchase something from their well fitted out shop on site.
Great little cafe with amazing views of the area.
Well worth the stop to experience and take some great photos..
The tea brings it all back when you arrive home..

Title: Wah chai !! Refreshing tea !
Text:
Visit to bluefield tea garden was a great experience ! On arrival we got Nishanti taking us on a tour of the tea factory. Her clear explanation of tea - White, black and green tea making made it so clear as to why some tea brews light, some strong. My daughter said I never knew this ! - At the end of the tour and insisted we buy some tea to take back. 

The factory had distinct aroma of tea leaves being dried and roasted - did not smell damp despite the rain ! Must visit and buy !

Title: Interesting tour of a working plantation
Text: Large factory in operation which fully explains the process of tea making. There is also a shop for tea sales( expensive) and a café to try the tea

Title: A nice insight into tea processing
Text:
I stopped off here on the advice of my driver on my way out of Nuwaru Eliya. It is set amongst an expanse of tea fields (which is useful!) and they provide a free tour around the factory. I went on a Sunday so the factory wasn't processing but it was very interesting to walk around and learn about how tea is processed from being picked all the way to being bagged up for auction. It's simple and educational, at the end of the day it's a working factory and you're learning about how it works. It's followed by a cup of tea (and cake if you like) in the cafe, and you can walk through to the shop and buy tea at their factory prices. There are staff in the shop (who do the tours) who will talk you through the differences of the types of tea leaves and how best to drink them. 
I was there about an hour for the whole thing. The getting to and from the factory will probably take most of your time but it's a nice site to visit and learn about Sri Lanka's tea production and export.

Title: A bit over assuming
Text:
A visit to the factory is short and has little to no action taking place. Just a detail of the process minus seeing too much happening..... for me that was a downer.
The sales centre is well stocked but no deals here , which was also disappointing.
One does get a feel of what tea is all about, however.

Title: Recomended
Text:
This was a stop on our way to Nuwara and after seeing all the beatifull tea plantations we learned about making tea process. The lady spoke a good english and was very nice, we tipped her 300 rp.
We also enjoyed a tea and bought some for home.

Title: Small Tea Factory with a good Restaurant
Text: This is a scheduled stop for many tourist operators. The officials explain the process very well.They have a very good restaurant with decent spread and obviously a sales counter to promote the tea sales

Title: Great Explaination from Guide
Text:
Once you arrived this Bluefield Tea Garden, you will be assigned a guide for free. They will explain to you the process of tea making. An eye opening experience and place to learn about green, white and black teas!.

Souvenir Shop selling tea as well. But slightly expensive.

Title: Lovely little place
Text: What great, friendly service we received, though we did not have to pay one cent!  Our tour guide was incredibly hospitable and knowledgeable, and the complementary tea at the conclusion of our tour was delicious.  Good quality food in the restaurant, too.  Would highly recommend.

Title: Tea experience
Text: Interesting experience, particularly when our group got to pick tea leaves like the pickers. The tour was excellent followed by the tasting. The downside was being hassled by people wanting to be tipped for everything!

User_Location: Prague, Hlavni Mesto Praha, Czech Republic
Title: Nice visit
Text: 20 minute visit to the working factory. No entry fee just tip to your guide and you have a free cup of tea afterwards and bought extra some nice cakes. Taken photos in the factory allowed. We bought some tea in the shop. It hot really busy around noon when buses with tourists came. You can have a walk to tea plantations just behind factory bulding.

Title: AN WONDERFUL AROMA OF TEA
Text: I am a real tea drinker and taking the tour at the Bluefield Tea Gardens with one of their professional guides was ''an education''.   There was so much information to digest about the different types of tea, the processes it went through before arriving at our shops and watching the various machinery process the leaves.  My tea will never taste quite the same again!

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Had a guided tour of the plantation and factory and it was quite fascinating and educational to learn how the leaves are picked and then turned into the various types of tea. Well worth a visit and our guide Suria was excellent.

Title: A greta opportunity to see tea production
Text:
Visited the Bluefield Estate during our trip to the hill country, which is in itself, both beautiful and enchanting.  The tour guides are very knowledgeable and the workers, pleasant and friendly.

Most of us drink tea but I suspect that few of us know the picking and production process, so the tour was both informative and interesting.

Naturally, we finished up with a cup of the local brew in the adjoining cafe and needless to say, Ceylon tea is very good.

Title: Good place
Text:
The Tea factory was closed when we visited the place.
The restaurant is costly...also the tea shop is very expensive

Title: Passed through here on way to Yala, so nextra cost just a bigger tip
Text:
Well you do learn something but In my opinion it was not a working factory it was an old historic factory. Still interesting and no cost to visit but you make up for it in the shop afterwards.
So all in all worth a visit if you are passing by and do end up knowing a lot about Tea,
( although still prefer Morrisons Earl Grey ! ) We visited as a couple but good for teens to make a break in the journey Loos and and cafe there as well.

Title: Quite far away. Nice tea garden with a good souvenir shop !
Text: It took us about one and half hour to get there by tuk tuk. It's quite far away. The facilities are a bit old. It depends on your luck if the guide is patient to explain every steps. Our guide went quite fast. After visiting the factory, you can walk around the tea field and have a cup of tea for free. The souvenir shop is nice. There are many varieties of tea and they are nicely packed. They are not cheap though. We found that it's even cheaper to buy tea from shops in Ella.

Title: Nice tea experience
Text:
Immediately after arrival we got 10 minutes free walk around factory. There is only black tea production. 
Tea shop is really good, we visited Mackwoods and Pedro tea plantation and here is not such a big nicely packed variety of tea. Cannot say whether it is overpriced as in local stores we didn't see nothing like these.
A bit disappointed about degustation as it is just a one cup of usual tea. 
Much more worse is a plantation itself as there are lots of poor women and children asking for money and views itself is not best of the best in comparison with others.

Title: Visit to Tea Gardens
Text: We all enjoyed the brief but informative factory tour regarding tea leaf processing. Also enjoyed the tea tastings after this tour and purchased some tea. Lovely setting and all is clean and organised.  A great place to stop in.

Title: Expensive Tea Shop
Text: The tea factory and its tour is very informative but tea being sold here was expensive in my opinion.

Title: free tea and tour - good views for photos
Text: The free factory tour was good - the cafe had good selection of cakes and patties - I like the Veg Puff - Free tea was icing on cake - We bought some green tea as souvenir which is high quality tea. Overall very happy with the visit.

Title: A must visit place in Nuwara Eliya
Text: Tea Garden with team factory is an awesome place to visit. The staff there explains every aspect of tea making with right set of detailing. The live demonstration of making white/ black & brown tea is fabulous. Bought couple of different team packs from the shopping store.

Title: Short guided tour of tea factory
Text: The guided tour of tea factory was brief as it seems the main focus is to get you inside the shop to sample the tea and of course get you to buy the tea in their shop.

Title: Great educational experience
Text: We had a very nice explanation about the tea production process from A-Z, which was very interesting and free. I finally understood the actual process tea goes through, from the picking of the leaves and up to the tea bag in my cup...  nice

Title: Good tour
Text: Lovely scenic drive to plantation. Plantation guide was excellent. Really interesting to see how tea is produced and to see the inside of the building which is in original condition and bar one modern machine the process of making the tea hasn't changed. Free entry and tour and cup of tea at end of tour. Nice to have a walk around plantation to see the tea bushes and the workers picking them.

Title: Mackwood is better for pictures but Bluefield has better tour
Text: We visited Mackwood (now knows as Damro) straight after visiting Blue Field, as it was on the way to our hotel in Nuwara Eliya. The tour at Blue Field is much better, as the process of tea making was explianed in detail in 10-15 minutes where as it only took 5 minutes at Mackwood. However, the setting at Mackwood is much nicer and for pictures. The tea from the shop is also cheaper at Blue Field. If time allows it, try both as it takes 15-20 minutes to travel between both.

Title: A good half day trip
Text:
We hired a van and the trip down the winding roads amidst the tea farms are a great view itself. The area is a little warmer than central. The factory location itself has a great view of the surrounding mountains and tea patches. 

You will know almost everything about Srilankan teas if you take the tour through. All then processes, varieties of teas etc. The guide there do it passion, for zero charge. But better give her some tips. Out in the field tea leave pickers work for a lesser daily rate. If you inquire a photo with them it would be nice to tip them. 

Theres a restaurant, souvenir shop and tea cafe. The lunch at the restaurant was of good quality.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: Nice place to.sit and relax . They have variety of tea to explore and drink. You will.love this place

Title: The best Tea factory in Sri Lanka
Text:
This tea factory was recommended by our driver. 

So glad we made the trip here. The tea pickers have been located here for centuries and I believe this is one oft he oldest tea factories around with machinery going back over 100 years. 

Our guide was very informative and gave us a thorough walk through and explained the tea making process. 

The tea tasting at the end was Devine and for less then £10 you get to sample all the tea which is made. 

A must visit, if you are in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: okie
Text: this is tea factory en route to elliay , they concentrate only for the people who buy the tea products there. i bought a tea packet its not good

Title: Very nice!!
Text: One of the best tea factories in Nuwar Eliya!! We had a tour of the factory, later we were guided to the tea lounge and were given complementary tea. They have a tea shop were you can buy different types of tea and souvenirs for family and friends. ???? ???? ???? ??? ?? ?? ??????? ??? ????? ????? ?????? ???? ??????? ????? ??? ???? ????? ??? ?????? ???? ????? ????? ???? ???????

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: The location is delightful, surrounded by hills covered in tea plants. We had a personal tour from a young woman who took a lot of pride in what she did. She gave an interesting tour explaining the history and tea making process of the factory. She also explained about the different grades of tea and what constitutes "quality". As we are tea lovers we found this fascinating. Afterwards we drank tea in the cafe and bought some to take home as gifts. I do not exagerate when I say that this was the best tea I have ever had.  A real treat. I might go back there just to stock up.

Title: Mr Debesh Sengupta
Text:
Nice tea factory on the way to Nuwara Eliya 
They take you round the factory and offer free cup of tea 
Black tea and Green tea available for Sale

Title: Beautiful
Text: Great intro to tea making.  The tea smell was amazing in the factory,  like the tea had perfumed the wood !  Tea and cakes were delicious;  you pay for the cups of tea and cake rather than the tour and unlike other places I read of there was no pressure to buy tea to take home (although we did)

Title: An Excellent insight into Tea Production
Text:
Stumbled upon this Plantation whilst travelling from Kandy to Yala. This place is definable worth visiting.
Free Guided Tour which really explained just how much goes into making and processing tea.
Really nice Tea room offering a free cup of Black Sample Tea.
Also a shop selling all the different teas produced by the Grower.
As I said there is no entry charge so its customary to thank the Guide with a small tip.
Definitely worth a Visit

Title: Great free tour!
Text:
Lovely tea field/ factory. They offered a very informative tour of the factory and how the tea is collected and produced. 
No tip is expected at the end unlike some free tours. 
We received a free cup of black tea at the end of the tour in the cafe.
We also ate he buffet lunch for 800 rupee per person, which was great. Offered lovely views in the restaurant. 
Highly recommend

Title: One of the best tea tours I have been on
Text: Went to Bluefield after recommendations from my SL cousins. The factory tours was really nice, with the guide and the factory workers explaining us the different stages of the process. The smell of toasted tea leaves that hits you the moment you step into the building is welcoming and soothing. I really enjoyed the tea tasting afterwards and bought a couple of teas at the shop! It is definitely worth a visit! Bonus: tea factory tour and sampling of one variety is free!

Title: Great visit
Text:
As mentioned by many - much better than the rather touristic Damra factory - they do take time to go through the tea manufacturing process and allow questions / pictures. Close by you can also take pictures of ladies picking tea.

Tour is free of charge so please leave tip for the good quality guide or for ladies picking tea if you take pictures

Title: Excellent no stress experience
Text: Our driver took us into the tea factory for a free tour. Our guide was exceptionally pleasant and helpful throughout, and provided no pressure for sales (a rare quality in sri lanka). We went as a couple but the experience can be great for all types. Unfortunately there is one component of the tea factory that is not wheelchair accessible, should you need it. However, the rest of the tour is accessible from what I could tell.

Title: Beautiful Tea Plantation
Text:
We had a lovely time in the Blue Fields Tea Gardens. They offered a free tour around the tea factory (first opened in the 1920s) which provided a lot of details on how the tea leaves are picked and processed. 

The tea gardens are behind the factory where you can roam around and interact with the tea pickers. They also have a restaurant where they serve buffet meals and a tea centre where you can taste and buy fresh tea.

Title: Amazing Experience - Quality Tea
Text: What a wonderful experience to visit Blue Field Tea Gardens & Factory. It is considered to be one of the best tea factories in the world. When we reached they gave us a guided tour as to how the tea is prepared in the factory which was very unique and informative. Kids enjoyed the most. After the tour they took us to their restaurant for fresh tea tasting which was so rich in taste. Some of the hot teas were free to taste and some had a price. There is a big shop within the factory where one can buy tea for self or families. Highly recommend and clean place.

Title: Good place to experience the tea growing and process
Text: This was a good place to experience the tea growing and process.  We were shown around by a knowledgable local guide and her English was excellent.  We tipped her a few hundred rupees at the end.  You can see the basic leaves and how they are turned into different varieties of orange pekoe black tea.  There is a shop where you can by the tea leaves and also you get to try a cup of the basic black tea for free.  Cakes and milk is also available at an extra charge.  Do walk around the gardens too where you can see all of the tea bushes where ladies picks average of.20 kg of tea leaves every day.  We were hassled a bit in the gardens which was annoying by an old lady who wanted us to take her photo for money and also a guy who wanted to 'escort' us around d the gardens for money.  Again we give him a couple of hundred rupees even though his English was terrible and he added no value to our visit whatsoever but he was persistent and I just wanted him to go away!

Title: Nice stop on the way
Text:
Nice place to visit for lunch (get stuck in the buffet and you will need an hour to recover after!) 

The tea factory is still working - the many "no picture" boards are hilarious when the guide tells you to take pictures. 

A nice tea shop - great view amongst the hill tops. What more does one need.

Title: Nice little visit
Text:
Yes it is touristic. But not a tourist trap.

The girl gave a nice tour which indeed does not take more than 10minutes. But in this time everything was said. So no complaints there.

They didn't push us into buying stuff. They gave us tea for free at the end of tge tour and let us be.

We had a 2nd tea (paying) and some cake. All at good prices if you ask me.

The store itself seems to have acceptable prices as well.

Title: Good experience of tea process making
Text:
Good place to go if on your way. Don't go out of your way to go there though as not worth a detour. 

Friendly place that explains the full process of tea making from moment leaves are picked. Good education for a basic product we take for granted and use everyday. Tour of factory and good knowledge by guides. 

It's a basic free tour . Nothing more to it than that.

Title: Tony estate in middle of Hills
Text: A nice little experience that starts from Tea making factory tour. It is situated in the middle of tea estate. The tea is highly expensive.

Title: Informative tour & great tea
Text: The tea factory tour was very informative,from picking up the tea leaves till packing... our tour guide was very helpful , he helped us pick up gifts from the shop... and not to forget the tasty tea in the restaurant.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: We were taken on a tour of the factory from processing of raw tea leaves to finished product. It was very interesting. All of the loading of tea leaves is done manually by women who I suspect are paid little as is the case with pickers. It is a remarkably and surprisingly labour intensive process. I don't think I will drink a cup of tea again without thinking of the workers I saw labouring away. Anyway, so much for my left leaning tendencies - one would hope fair trade might occur as it has in the coffee trade. Well worth a visit, and the tea on sale is quite cheap.

Title: It's a interesting stop en route to somewhere
Text: It was a good and informative rest and pit stop. The guided tour included explanations on how the raw tea gets turned into the end product and our guide was knowledgeable enough.

Title: Interesting visit
Text: We had a guide explain the process of tea growing and processing which was alot more interesting than I thought it would be.  We enjoyed morning tea in the very pleasant cafe.

Title: Bluefield Tea Gardens
Text:
A trip to Sri Lanka would not be complete without a visit to a Tea Garden.
And Bluefield Tea Gardens is a great example of why Sr Lanka tea is most flavorful and sought after by tea lovers the world over.
They have great tour of processing of the tea leaves which was very enjoyable. The factory and it's surrounding areas form a great backdrop for pictures. A tea shop with free tea servings are an added attraction. Attractive packaging of tea leaves for sale - at the time we visited - the only drawback was we had to pay with cash - no credit card transactions were accepted - not very convenient for the international traveler.

Title: Authentic Tea
Text: Blue Field Tea Garden an authentic place to purchase original Sri Lankan tea with different types and taste.

Title: Learn about tea!!
Text: There are many tea estates and factories near Nuwara Eliya, but Blue Fields seems to be one that is better set up for visitors.  Informative tours of the 100-year old factory are provided and visitors are allowed wander throughout the tea plantations.  Good opportunities for photos. End the tour with a nice cup of complimentary tea and chance to buy overpriced tea in their shop.  Blue Fields is about 20 kilometers from Nuwara Eliya (farther than many other tea factories), but it's a nicer experience than many others.

Title: the best BOP tea and cakes
Text: we had an enjoyable stop over here. The tour was highly educational with regards the tea process. The complimentary tea was divine and the cakes very tasty and inexpensive. Well worth the stop. I would recommend this.

Title: Its a tea plantation that is all.
Text:
A slight disappointment in that the guide, just fired us through all this and the plant was not working due to a funeral.

Interesting all the same and then you get some bad service at the end in the tearoom to make up for the 10 mins getting shown around.

I would not recommend this as we found it to be 'oh I cant be bothered", 'what more tourists", not for us wish we had not bothered.

Title: Tea at Reasonable Prices
Text:
We went there to take photos of the tea-leaf pickers and visited their factory and shop too.  

The factory visit was short, but still interesting, picking up some knowledge of the different types of tea.  

Their shop offers a variety of teas that they produce, all of reasonable prices, nothing that is exorbitant.  I bought the golden tip and silver tip tea leaf.  It is good.

Title: Great Tea Plantation
Text:
This is our First visit to a Tea Plantation, it was High up in the Mountains in a most spectacular setting, our tour around the factory albeit brief was very informative and interesting, but be aware that as soon as you get your camera out the plantation staff will soon pop-up wanting money to be in your pictures!

After our tour we was taken to the Teas Shop to sample the tea and was given an opportunity to buy some tea, this wasn't expensive nor was there a hard sell.

A lovely trip!

Title: Best Cup of Tea
Text: Stopped at Bluefield Tea gardens for a free 15 minute tour on our way to Ella. Very informative guide  and afterwards given a excellent cup of black tea. Cake or biscuits are extra and were reasonably priced so we indulged. We are now drinking a pot of tea very day which is so much better for us. Best cuppa.

Title: A good knowledge of tea production
Text:
Here we got nice experience of how tea is produced. Explanation was given point to point in a very nice way. Staff of the factory is very helpful in explaining the process of tea. Along with explanation we got a chance to taste nice cup of tea. First time I got to know that there is white tea as well along with black tea. If time permits then this tea factory is worth a visit. 
We bought tea packs, our relatives liked it very much ??

Title: Good to spend a few hours around a tea plantation and factory
Text: I went there on a day trip and the place is good to see the process that goes into making tea and also to walk around the plantation for some time.

Title: Interesting tour - not too long!
Text: It was busy the day we went as it was the weekend. If you go on a Sunday you don't see the factory working but there is no noise of machinery. You get a free tour which is really interesting and then you are shown back to the cafe for a free cup of strong tea! The toilets are ok. The shop is quite small and a bit pricey. No pressure though. The shop at the St Clair's plantation (Mlesna Tea Castle) is way better, bigger and better staffed. Worth going to both.

Title: very interesting
Text: Bluefield is the first tea plantation we have ever visited. They offer a free guided tour and tea degustation. The guide shows the factory and explains everything about tea. You can also visit their shop and purchase some tea. Prices are OK.

Title: Well maintained factory with a nice view for tea tasting
Text: Visited the factory and was given a tour with explanation on the tea making process. Later on we were given a chance to have free tea tasting.The cafe that served the tea had a nice viewing area. Only minus point, felt the tea pricing was a bit steep. But then they don't force u to buy the products.

Title: Nico to learn more
Text:
We had a tour at the factory.
The nice gentlemen showed us how they make tea.
It is nice to hear. After that we were offered a cup of tea. The tea was good.

Title: Well worth a vist
Text: We were given a tour of the tea factory by a friendly guide. Very impressive and noted the aged nature of much of the machinery. There was no pressure to buy stuff from the adjoining shop and café. Definitely worth a visit

Title: Wonderful Tea Plantation
Text:
Bluefield Tea Gardens is a beautiful tea plantation that to visit while in Ramboda or Nuwar Eliya area. The staff are very friendly and the tour is informative on the process of making tea. I wished that the tour was a bit longer and more detailed but to accommodate the large amount of people I think it's a bit difficult for them. The factory is clean and let me walk around to the back to get some pictures of the tea plantations and the workers. 

We arrived at the end of the work day (make sure to manage to go ahead of time to see all machines in operation) so we missed some of the machines however, we got the chance to talk to some of the workers before they checked out. 
The quality of the tea from this garden was some of the best we bought in all of Sri Lanka. I def recommend to buy your gifts and as much tea options as you can. Once you arrive, you also get the chance to sample the tea and enjoy some desserts (rather dry but good enough). 

Tips: 
- Arrive early so you get the chance to see everything in process. I believe the work day ends at 4pm. 
- Tip some of the workers if you can as working in the tea fields is one of the lowest paid jobs in Sri Lanka. 
- Sample and buy tea!

Title: excellent quality tea to take back home
Text:
Nice tour ... an eye opener , it explains a lot about the tea we drink .

The gift shop is loaded with all sorts of different high quality tea to take back home either for your own consumption or as gifts to your loved ones.
 I personally recommend The Blue Moon tea , the smell and taste is simply amazing.

Title: Stop for tea
Text: We stopped at Blue Field for tea. Enjoyed a nice chocolate cake. Great cup of tea. Nice restaurant upstairs but we didnt stop for lunch

Title: Short but interesting visit
Text:
We stopped at these gardens to obtain a visit, we had our own guide, the visit of the factory took about 15 minutes. Afterwards we had a free cup of tea in the restaurant.
They have a shop when you like to buy tea, as coffee drinkers we don't know if prices are high.
We also had a small lunch which was nice.

Title: We had a free cuppa and a factory visit!
Text: We went to the tea factory there and one of the staff took us to the factory and explained how we get our cuppa to our table! Sadly they were not working on Sunday but we could see the machinery and the rest and also have a cuppa after the little tour. Interesting and informative to my 10 year old.

Title: Intresting palce with good guided tours
Text:
The guided tour to team factory was very good and guide was very informative and explained the whole process patiently. The factory is very clean and allows visitors to view the process from up close. 
The tea shop was also very good and offered a wide range of products. Nice place to buy some premium tea. Use this opportunity to buy good tea as the tea sold in these factories is not available outside. Though ordinary tea in Nuruwa eliya etc. shops are cheaper, the quality here is far better and hence worth the cost.

Title: Informative tour
Text: We really enjoyed our tour at the Bluefield tea gardens. Our tour guide gave a thorough explanation of what happens at the factory and we were offered a free cup of tea at the end of the tour.

Title: Very interesting place and exceptional customer service
Text: Very clean and professional tea factory with a friendly and informative tour guide to show you around.  After the tour, a courtesy cup of tea in the lounge.  Of course, they have a shop so you can buy gifts and stock up, which we did.  Unfortunately I managed to forget and leave belongings behind on a couch in the lounge...  Their customer service was impressive - they found my belongings before I even realized I had lost them, put them safely aside, and then sent them on to me by courier.  Could not have asked for more - thank you to staff and management at Blue Field Tea Gardens!!

Title: Great tour, well priced  high quality Tea
Text:
A local friend  organised a tour here and explained that you get to buy your Tea at a fair price
We foundd this to be true

Title: Nice one hour stop
Text: Our guide was clear and took us through the entire process. The tour obviously ends at the shop which offers a wide selection of tea.

Title: One of the best Tea factory
Text: Majorly women are employed in this factory and mainly manual process is undertaken for producing the tea product. All the tea plucking staff are women. As soon as you reach, staff guides you and explains you the process of tea produce in the factory. Types of tea and the benefits from each tea type is explained very well. Very informative and enthusiastic staff. Complimentary tea is served after the explanation. Natural tea products are available in powder as well as tea bag form. The staff also explains the cost for packaging involved and suggests you the right pack as per your budget. Enjoyed.

Title: Great stop on the Kandy to Nuwara Elisa road.
Text: Do not drive past this! Short personal walk through the tea making process in the 100 year old factory, from a very personable & interesting guide.  Followed by tea, all at no charge!

Title: Exemplary
Text: Very nice place with lots of ftes firlds around. Simply honoured to take a tour in bluefield. Hope for the best

Title: Nice factory and good visit
Text: We really enjoyed the visit, our guide was very pleasant and he spent time with us, he was easy to understand and answered all our questions.

Title: Fascinating place to visit
Text: Had a very interesting tour around this tea factory. Our excellent guide explained all about the way the tea is grown, harvested and then produced within the factory. Had a first-rate cup of the tea as the tour finished.

Title: Nice original place
Text: Had a tour by a lovely Sri Lankan girl. Very interesting facts around tea. The place have a decent place yo have tea and pastry and a good shop as well. Beautiful surrounfin6.

Title: Good place to visit
Text:
Several types of teas are prepared here! A guided tour explains the differences clearly the process of making tea! 
Tea tasting is possible before you want to buy or choose your favorite tea! 

The English spoken by guide may not be clear but if you ask question, you get answers! ??

Title: Informative visit
Text:
We had a guide with good English and she explained very clearly the processes involved in tea production. Not rushes.
Had a nice cup of tea afterwards and bought lots of tea to come home. Countryside round about is lovely.

Title: Fascinating, and well worth the visit
Text: We were on an organised tour of Sri Lanka and this was one of our scheduled stops. The tour around the factory was very interesting and the old British machinery still is in working condition. The ladies were then encouraged to try picking the tea out in the field for themselves, it was a great laugh watching them working so competitively in the field. Then as a reward, we were all treated to a wonderful cup of tea followed by, as usual a tea store visit.

Title: Good tea factory
Text:
Nice tea factory, although we did not see it working as it was sunday, it is free too! But the gift shop
Probably makes up for it!

Title: Everything good but abysmal state of toilets
Text:
Short, crisp and informative tour of the showcase tea processing facility.  The area around the center offers a delightful view of tea gardens interspersed with small brooks and quaint bridges.
A winding road takes you up the hill for a birds-eye view of the mesmerizing valley studded with lakes.
Inside the outlet, there is plenty to choose from - variety, flavours, quantity, and packaging.  Staff is efficient and helpful.
There is a nice cafe where you can sample different kinds of tea and complete the experience with a choice of cake on the side.
Wish the owners lay as much importance to the availablity of enough and clean toilets.

Title: Great factory guide informative but the lunch buffet could have been a little better
Text:
Found this place informative and did purchase quite a bit of tea to take back home as well as distribute among friends.  They serve a free cup of black tea per person. I wish they had the option of milk tea and if not liquid milk at least milk powder as I do not fancy black tea.

We had lunch here but the lunch buffet was just okay, nothing great. Dessert options were very limited. I was hoping to see more of Srilankan food.

Title: Good tea factory
Text: A very good tea factory, offering free tours of the facilities and complimentary cup of tea afterwards.

Title: Good place to visit
Text: Good information about the tea plantation...the whole process of how tea is made and the machinery used to process the tea...the people involved in it was explained in detailed...good experience..we bought different varieties of tea from there too..loved it...

Title: Great place to stop
Text:
I stopped here for a break and had tea and cake followed by a free tour of the tea factory.  My guide had a lot of knowledge and took me through the entire tea making process.  It was interesting an informative.

She then showed me all of the different teas on sale in the shop and explained why some were much more expensive than others.  The good thing is that you can walk into the tea room and taste the teas before you buy any.  It is not the cheapest place to get a cup of tea but quite unique.

Title: Interesting to see a tea factory, not too special though
Text:
Somehow we did not find a guide, even though most other tourists did walk through the factory with a guide. A worker sent us in on our own, so we explored the factory by ourselves. There was just half a band of fresh tea leaves currently being dried and no worker (or anyone else) was around on that floor, but in the lower floor the rest of the tea processing was happening on a seemingly normal scale. It was indeed interesting to see the individual steps from the leaves up to the various tea types.

The tea store was well stocked and overcrowded, with a lot of tourist buses buying huge amounts of tea. Our apartment hosts already recommended us (and were right) only to buy small amounts of tea for presents, as the price was indeed extraordinarily high and the quality the same as you find in normal shops. Afterwards, we ate a little and enjoyed a cup of tea in the Cafe. Overall a nice visit and definitely great to walk a bit among the tea fields that are so common in this area of Sri Lanka.

Title: Short and sweet
Text: The tour was short and simple and well done even though we didnt see much in action.  The tea tasting consisted of one tea which was nice but made it difficult to understand the difference between the tea they made and sold...the others are available for a cost but I didnt have space for 5 full cups of tea :) We bought some tea from the wide selection on offer and then afterward went to the local village and found the same tea much cheaper in the shops! The selection was a lot smaller so I am still glad I bought what I did but it was disappointing to feel that they were taking full advantage of the captive market of tourists :(

Title: Good explanation of the process
Text:
The factory tour was good and the process was explained well. As we went on a Sunday, we missed out on the opportunity to the see the machines running.

The tea shop had many varities of tea but the pricing was high. Tourist factor.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: A good way to see how tea is processed. Was met by an English speaking guide (tip only payment) he took us though the factory and explained the process of how tea is made. We then got a free cup of tea, and then left to browse the shop, which was reasonable price.

Title: Very interesting, educational and so helpful
Text:
I have not visited a tea factory for years and was a bit skeptical about what I was going to see and learn.
I have never been so wrong.
In my early days there was no such thing as tea bags, and i thought tea bags was for grounded twigs!  
Now i know ground tea can give different strengths.
The factory was so clean and the tour was excellent.
Shop was very good.
We bought some tea to take home.
Best part of my story was we left a jacket/coat there and were miles away before we realised this. We gave them a call, and they were so helpful. They sent us a picture to confirm, and then sent the jacket to their store in Colombo, for us to collect before leaving Sri Lanka.
Thank you, Mr. Irshad, you showed us not just how good Blue Field Tea Gardens is, but how helpful and kind Sri Lankan people are.

Title: Nothing more than a tea shop
Text:
Our driver took us here as he said the Tea was good. It was merely a tea shop. Very busy and crowded, more expensive than the other tea factories.
Not worth the price or the effort to visit.

Title: Great lunch and shop
Text: We came here having already visited the Labookellie tea factory, and I preferred the Labookellie tour to Bluefield - it just seemed a bit more polished. That said, Bluefield is still good for a run-down of the tea-making process. We also had lunch here, which was 990 rupees/person for a buffet. The food was lovely, particularly the eggplant curry. We also saved our shopping for Bluefield as our hotel owner had told us it was cheaper, and we weren't disappointed. Beautiful 150g decorated canisters of tea were 800-950 rupees, and there was a huge range. On the whole, Bluefield was a great place to finish a day trip through the tea fields.

Title: Best tea factory tour in Sri Lanka
Text: Probably the best tea tour and factory experience you'll find in Sri Lanka. Friendly guides, interesting tour, and - of course - great tea. If you're looking for a place to visit to lean more about tea in Sri Lanka, then this is the place to go!

Title: Really enjoyable and lovely tea
Text:
I really, really enjoyed the Bluefield Tea Garden's factory tour.  Make sure you take the time and do this because you will appreciate the tea and the process involved so much more.  The plantations are free to wander (so lovely, although if you visited in the heat of the day like me you're wander will be brief) and there is a cafe and retail store.  I didn't sample at the cafe however I did bring home three boxes of different teas to enjoy at home.  For those coming back to Australia, I ensured I bought fully sealed bags and didn't have any issues with customs upon arriving in Perth (make sure you declare them though).  The toilets here aren't the cleanest I will say that, however not to the point you should find somewhere else.  Definitely worth a visit and I'm certainly
Enjoying my tea!

Title: Good place to know the tea production, but expensive to buy tea there
Text:
We dropped by there on the way back to Negombo. They have a tea production line there. It's a good place to understand the whole black tea diversification and production processes. The guide explained everything clearly.

They provided a free cup of tea for every tourist dropping by. And they have a shop there to do some shopping. Next to the shop, there is a quite big play ground for the kids to kill time while parents do shopping. 

However, the tea there is not cheap comparing with Negombo. 

Overall, it's a pleasant experience.

Title: Free tea tasting !
Text: We stopped here to buy tea as souvenirs back home to our friends and relatives. The cafe was crowded as it had just finished raining and there was a bus full of tourist awaiting for the rain to stop. As we had finished buying our tea, the crowd had already left with the bus and it was quite peaceful to enjoy a cup of black tea with the tea plantation as the back drop. We didnt mind paying extra for some milk and some cakes as we just enjoyed the hot cup of steaming tea in the post rain weather. Its was a perfect time and place for hot tea. Please do try the free tea, nothing to loose. And if you like it, buy it !

Title: Tea was good
Text: The view of factory was ok. I enjoyed the tea, was definitely good quality, but as is in Sri Lanka, was very over priced.

Title: nice pit stop, recommended for tea education!
Text: Nice introduction to the processes and steps from harvesting tea up to packaging. 1 of the well known tea estate. Complimentary cup of tea drink and you can shop in the many assortment of teas ready for purchase. Do try to walk pass the factory building to the tea path so that you can have a gorgeous view of the tea plantation valleys and lady workers. Friendly staff.

Title: A must visit place for a different tea experience!
Text: A should and must visit place on the way to Nuwara Eliya. It's a traditional and old tea factory which is still operational and produced "N" number of flavours of tea. There is a tea tour taken by the staff where they explain about different process of tea making until packing. The tea leaf smell welcomes you which is raw and the final stage of packing gives you best aroma of tea. Post the tour, you are offered hot piping tea which makes you warm in the cold atmosphere. Post sipping it.. you are then guided to buy their best tea which had several flavours. A must visit place which takes approximately 1 hour.

Title: Short tour and a shop
Text: In this tea farm, you can quite easily get a tour.  You just go to the shop counter and somebody will take you on a tour.  The tour is free, but tip I think is expected (we gave a small one anyway).  The tour is just around the factory and is maybe 15 minutes where they explain the production process.  At this farm you can't see the tea plants or do any picking.  The shop has a wide range of teas and I the main restaurant area gives free tea (well we got some free tea after our tour anyway).

Title: Excellent Marketing
Text: They do teach you what the real tea dust means and how it's produced. The way they accept you as a tourist and explains things without reservations is way to learn. Great way and excellent hospitality. Thanks for the tea too...

Title: Nice place
Text: Good place to understand the tea making process and a quaint little tea shop serving pastries and tea.You may also purchase branded tea from the shop.

Title: Very interesting place
Text: They took us through the tea manufacturing process and we were surprised to know the different grades of tea mainly white tea. The tea boxes available in their shops are slightly on the higher side, but the purity is guaranteed. It was raining when we went there and it made the place even more fragrant.

Title: Informative Tour
Text:
The guide who took us around the bluefield tea factory was a wonderful person.  She explained us all the steps in details, of how the tea is processed.  She also gave us details of the different kind of tea, i.e., black, green and white tea.

However, their tea shop is toooooo expensive.  Although my son bought some green tea from there but I would suggest to explore the market first.

Title: Tea Plantation
Text: Stopped here to see how the tea is processed depending on the type. It was very interesting to learn the process and to actually see it as it is still done today. You even get to have a gratis cuppa before making your way to the shop ??

Title: Tour of the factory, shop and plantation
Text:
The staff who took us around was very informative and taught us quite a lot about tea production in general, as well as how it is done in Bluefield.

He also explained about the various types of tea that are produced here as well as in other plantations, the differences as well as how best to drink them.

Title: Nice plce
Text:
Nice place yo visit and learn about tea industry.
Worth to drink a coup of tea there and to countinue ur journy...

Title: Great tour and wonderful tea
Text: Really nice tour of a tea factory. Not too modernised so you get to see so much more of the process. Great guide who took us through all the different steps. The tea is good too. Well worth stopping here.

Title: Very informative tour
Text: The tour was very informative with a knowledgeable guide..  They gave us a free cup of tea.. We could understand various steps of tea making and different types of tea.

Title: Free Tour And Free Tea.. Worth The Visit
Text:
Wow... what a beautiful area and tea plantation. We got a free tour of the factory from a knowledgeable guide and learned a lot about tea in the process. 

Afterwards we received a free cup of tea which I complimented with two small slices of a tasty "Butter" and "Fruit" cake.

Grand total for the tour, tea and two slices of cake, LKR 360 including a LKR 200 tour guide tip.

A "Tea & Souvenir Shop" along with a Cafe is also on the property. However, there was no pressure to make a purchase as Tea Shop is in a separate room from Cafe.

Feel free to roam the ground after you are done enjoying your free cup of tea.

Title: beautiful countryside and nice tour
Text: We visited on a Sunday when the factory was not running, but the tour was still interesting. Our guide was knowledgeable and answered all of our questions very clearly. Lots of options for tea purchase in the shop afterwards.

Title: Good Tea Factory
Text: The location is simply superb and there is ample parking place and after your visit to the tea factory you can relax at the cozy restaurant where you are served complimentary tea . There are many varieties of ceylon tea being sold here which is quite expensive. This place is worth a visit.

Title: A Far Better Tea Estate
Text: For tea factory tour, or to purchase teas, or to have lunch, this place is overall really great. Must visit. The gardens are charming, and what a breath taking view of the mountains and rolling mist. The restaurant is cozy, with good selection of food. I loved the Iced Tea here, one of the best I've had anywhere.

Title: See the Greens, take the factory tour & Sip Free Tea
Text: few moments before this on all 4 sides you see Lush Green Tea Plantations. The Blue Fields Tea Factory is Big & you can see more details in the photos attached. The Tea Factory tour is approx 30 mins, where they show u the making & complete process how Ceylon Tea is made !! after the tour they drop you to it's restaurant, check the Blue Fields Restaurant review for this

Title: Short & Interesting
Text:
First of all - it´s free of charge - big plus!
You´ll get a guide who explains every step of the tea manufacturing - from collecting leaves to drying & shredding, different tea types etc - quite interesting!
After that you can go into the restaurant and have a gratis tea and you can tip your guide - or not, however you like.
The whole procedure did take only about 30 minutes, but it was worth the time!
Would recommend to anyone near this area.

Title: Take the tour
Text:
A guide will show you through the manufacturing stages of the tea.  The tour is less than 30 mins and there's a free brew afterwards.  It's customary to give a small tip and well appreciated.

Tea is expensive in all the factories - but it's excellent quality.

Title: tour and buying tea!
Text:
A kind lady gave us a tour, she spoke fluent english and showed us from stage 1 all the way to the packaging stage of their tea factory! we then went to the gift shop area for a cuppa free tea and bought some teabags home too.

Tour was fairly short though.

Title: Tour of Tea Factory
Text: This was an excellent choice by our guide As usual in Sri Lanka everyone is friendly and our guide ,a young girl dressed impeccably in a Sari was informative and articulate we learnt a lot about Tea we hadn't known before and then a complimentary cup of tea and cake at the end Totally recommended

Title: Good tea to drink and purchase
Text: Unfortunately they were closed by the time we arrived - don't travel over Sri Lankan New Year (April 13-15) as most people close the factories due to the holidays, however the coffee shop and tea store was open and the guy inside explains the variations of tea. The store was also inexpensive when compared to mackwood (now called browns) so fret spot to buy tea to take back home to family and friends.

Title: Good variety of teas
Text: One can taste different varieties of teas here in payment basis. There are many types of teas on sale here in different packings. The staff is quite helpful in explaining the difference in varieties. We bought OP & OPA grades. Pl bear in mind that the drivers get a cut, as they bring the customers to the factory.

Title: Tea Factory : Not that Great
Text:
This factory is few KM before Nuwara Eliya on way. Not that great, when we visited it was closed so couldnt get much information about their processes. Got one last to explain us reasonably.

It has got one small children park with swings and slides but in poor condition.

They have Tea Cafe where they serve one particular type of tea as complimentary and you can buy other types of Tea.

Title: Good collection of teas
Text: A must visit for tea lovers. Blue field has a wide range of tea flavors to select from. Confirm whether the factory is operational for a better experience.

Title: Good, free visit to tea factory
Text:
Lovely young lady gave us a good explanation and tour of the tea process .. though I wish the factory was actually working when we visited.. 

It was nice to walk through the plantation after the tour. We tipped many of the women labourers we saw as we felt terrible when we learnt how miserably little they are paid for their hard long hours of work. 

There is small PLAYGROUND which the kids enjoyed after we had our free tea sample and also had some snacks at their coffee shop.  We also bought some tea for gifts.

Title: Wonderful visit
Text:
Upon arrival I was greeted by Muhammed and off we went to the plantation.  Here I had my first introduction to tea leaves and bushes.  The factory workers were on breakfast break and it was lovely to see the super clean and tidy century old factory in its glory. 
The tour ended with a delicious cup of tea (skip the milk and sugar this time to taste authenticity)!!

Title: The best tea tour in Nuwara Eliya
Text:
It's definitely worth dropping off at this tea factory, even if you've been to others. For a start, it's much small - the company only employs about 200 people and the place has a bit of a family feel about it.

Second, we could all around the factory and watch tea being processed, which wasn't the case at the other tea factory we tried (we went on a Monday morning and they don't pick on a Sunday, so you've got to make sure they are working in the factory or you get a trip round a silent building).

Our guide was friendly and informative and didn't hang around for a tip - in fact, we sought him out to give him a tip and and couldn't find him. And the tea was complimentary.

Title: Beautiful grounds, great tea and informative tour
Text:
Of all the tea factories I've visited on my travels this would probably be my favourite. The actual tour of the factory is extremely informative and the lady explained the entire process of making tea in great detail.

We were allowed to take photos of the factory's insides and then given a complimentary cup of tea.

After having our free cuppa and free tour we proceeded to the gift shop which wasn't cheap but also wasn't expensive, moderately priced is what I would say best fits it.

Finally we were allowed to take a stroll around the plantation completely unassisted which was lovely.

The plantation and grounds are beautiful and the fact that we could go where we wanted on our own really made it special. A definitely must do in this tea lovers opinion.

Title: Beautiful tea
Text: gardens we visited SriLanka in Dec 2017. On our way from Nuwara to Kandy , we visited this beautiful tea garden and tea factory,. The gardens are beautiful but we were a bit disappointed as the tea factory was closed since it was Sunday. We were offered a cup of tea at the end of tour which was very good. I would recommend a visit to this garden on a weekday.

Title: Nice but too expensive
Text:
This place is there to please the tourists
We wanted milk tea after the excursion, but we had to pay for it

Title: Interesting/annoying old woman
Text: Good tour but we were never taken into the fields. Also an old women who basically jumped in front of the camera and demanded money was pretty off putting, as Im happy to pay if I wanted a photo of one of the women working but i didnt ask for a mug shot in front of the fermenting block!

Title: Ok nothing great
Text:
I cant compare this place to any other tea factory because i only went to one.
The minute you enter you are taken.on a tour of the factory. It was quite obvious that the information provided was scripted. When we asked a couple of questions the guide couldnt give proper answers.
The tour ends with a complimentary cup of tea.
I was told that this place has more choices of tea in its souveneir shop.
The plus point is on our own we decided to  walk to the tea plantation.(not part of the tour)  The view is amazing. Great photo opportunities. The highlight of the visit!

Title: Nothing special
Text: Tea factory looks rather like place for guiding tourists than really working factory. Guide said about the tip for him at the beginning on the tour. Tea shop is recommended as they have tea in different kinds of packages and very reasonable price. If you want to buy tea you may visit the shop only and for the tea factory tour go to other place.

Title: Great tour
Text: Great to visit as part of the tour, was fascinating to see how the tea is produced and to be shown round the factory. Opportunities to taste tea and have food in the cafe, and buy products in the shop.

Title: A must-visit Tea Factory in Nuwara
Text:
We stopped by at this factory on our way to the city of Nuwara Eliya. The place was surrounded with tea plantations and beautiful landscapes. There's a mini a waterfall right above it. Blue Field Tea Gardens is not just a tea factory but they offer more than that. As soon as you arrive, they will provide a tour guide (for free) who will accompany you inside the factory and explain the process of producing a world class tea product.   

Once the tour is over, they will serve a free cup of tea. They also have cakes, muffins, pastries, & bread for a very reasonable price. Cheap  tea products were also available onsite.

Title: Fantastic place and Nishanthi was an excellent guide
Text:
We went to this farm (over dozens of others) based on the personal recommendation of a friend + trip advisor reviews. This was well worth a morning drive out from our accommodation. Nishanthi our guide was very knowledgeable and explained the process answering our questions. At the end of the tour of the factory she guided us to the cafe where hot tea was served and where we even got explanation about the type of tea being served. The restaurant had some very tasty and piping hot snacks as well as yummy cakes and pastries for us to enjoy with our tea all with very attentive, prompt and friendly service. Clean bathrooms manned by attendants was a huge plus. It even has a small playground for children to enjoy. After enjoying the tea and the snacks we bought the many different varieties of reasonably priced tea they sell. Someone was at hand to help us select and explain the different teas that we wanted to buy. 
To finish off the experience we went for a nice relaxing stroll among the tea plantation enjoying the lovely vistas from high up in the mountains. 

Thanks blue fields for the lovely experience and many thanks Nishanthi!!!

Title: Great little tour
Text: Our tour guy was fantastic. Her English was exceptional and took the time to answer our questions as we went. Well worth it.

Title: Tea factory tour
Text: Interesting tour and nice people showing us around. Opportunity to taste teas and of course visit their shop.

Title: Informative visit
Text: We had a short tour around here. The girl who showed us the stages of tea production was a fountain of knowledge & was able to answer questions we asked & we learnt some interesting facts. We did buy some tea at the end because it isn't available at home.

Title: Tea Factory with Good Explanatiaon
Text: I visited on a Sunday. The facory was not operative but one assistant showed us around the factory and showed us the processes involved in making tea. We were also given an explanantion of the different types of tea. Then we were given a cupof tea to drink.Nice visit.

Title: Short visit in the tea plantation. Double prices in the shop.
Text: We had a very short visit in the tea plantaion, a longer and interesting visit in the factory. The tea shop had about double prices compared to the normal in shops and hotels.

Title: Fun experience
Text: Informative tour. Unfortunately, we were there on a Sunday, so we didn't get to see the factory "in action." Provided with tea after the tour. Tea Prices very reasonable. Must do when visiting Sri Lanka!

Title: Ancient Factory
Text: Quaint factory with a short tour where you see the tea being dried and fermented. At the end of the tour you have an opportunity to sample different types of tea and purchase.

Title: Beautiful factory with nice tea tasting
Text:
We chose to come to this Tea factory because its blue colour looked very beautiful. In fact, even inside the factory, unexpectedly, many parts are in blue too. Nice colour. 

There is no fee for the tour. A guide explained the tea and differences between different kind of tea. And, showed us around the operation. We visited on Sunday and no one worked and so we could not see the real operation in the factory and tea fields. But, we could walk over to tea fields to take few photos. After the tour, a free tea was given and we could relax a bit. We did some shopping here, though not sure if it was reasonable price or not. 

But, at least, we took some good photos.

Title: nice and cheap black tea buying
Text: very good quanlity of tea,most important is the price you can't imaging!so maybe the ladies' salary who pick leaves are far low beyond we know,I guess.

Title: Great tour & factory
Text: We loved this tea factory tour. Very informative & the shop is good at the end and reasonably priced. The cafe is great. We preferred this tea factory over Mackwood's.

Title: Excellent orange pekoe and good explanation of how tea was made.
Text: The tour lasted for around 10 minutes. We were shown the fresh tea leaf, which was then dehydrated, grounded, fermented and     sorted. The factory had a lovely aroma. The small restaurant served free black tea but milk tea would be charged. The tea was very smooth and had a sweet after taste which lasted for an hour.

Title: Touristy but worth
Text:
Free to enter, short 15minutes individual guide through the factory by friendly guides of Bluefield factory. 
Good first impression how tea is being made, informative. 

Then you receive a cup of tea in the restaurant area (few dessert options to buy if one wants) 

And there is a tea shop with great selection of locally produced tea. 
The guides are there to help you, tea samples available. 
Depends what kind you want, it starts 4usd onwards.

Title: Interesting
Text: We had just tea, but it was an amazing experience in the hils on a tea estate. Tea was refreshing with many choices

Title: A nice break on the way to Nuwara Eliya
Text:
The Bluefield Tea Gardens and factory is a great way to stretch your legs when on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya. The tour of the factory was informative although very dusty. The cup of tea provided after the tour was lovely. The toilet facilities were very clean. There was food available, but we did not consume any, so cannot inform you of its quality.

The price of the tea however was quite high and as such we did not purchase any.

Title: Visiting a tea garden is a must if you go to Nuwara Ellya
Text:
And this was a very good tea garden with a nice guided tour of the tea factory- the tour is free along with a cuppa to sample post tour.
Most visitors buy some fresh tea and so did we... not cheap tea but good quality I presume as I have not yet tasted it.
Worth a visit.

Title: Lovely Tea
Text: Unfortunately as we visited on the weekend we couldn't see anything working but we had a really excellent tour and explanation of how everything worked. Afterwards we had a lovely cup of tea and opportunity to buy some local tea.

Title: aroma experience
Text: You visit this place not to see but to smell. Smelling the interior is an epic experience which makes you realise how much the manufacturing process can change the taste and flavour of the raw tea leafs. Yes, a little too expensive as benchmarked agains other attractions on the island. The guide was harsh but okay - you need to remember that tourists are differend and his job is priceless.

Title: Nice place, BUT terrible and unfriendly guide
Text: The place has a history and the building is nice. But it is the last nice thing. Ticket is expensive and the guide WAS MOST UNFRIENDLY PERSON within 3 weeks in Sri Lanka. He do not explain you anything, just read the paper which he gave you, bullying you with instructions (come!, stay here!). No tasting tea. Guide did not even say goodbye to us. Do not go there and save money for friendly people in Sri Lanka.

Title: Kinda worth it, kinda not
Text: This place was weird yet fun. We got a taxi from ella for $40USD (there and back) to go out to see this factory and liptons seat. When we arrived, we had to wait a bit for the last tour to be done and then we were given a 20-30 min tour.  Joseph aka tour guide that barks orders at you, was actually very enjoyable if you dont take him too seriously. We asked lots of questions and sometimes he answered them and sometimes he didnt lol. It wasnt the most expansive tour ive ever been on but it was food learning. After, the views up to liptons seat were amazing however the ride is rough (road is terrible).

Title: Nice experience
Text:
Nice but bit surreal. 
First of all the factory is quite hard to get to. We self drove and got there from Nuwara Eliya. Last 8km were tough, especially due to buses. The views along the way were magnificent though. 
After parking which is easy to get we were immediately surrounded by guys offering us a tuktuk to Liptons Seat. We declined and went for factory only. It costed 1000lkr per person. You get a covers for your shoes and must leave your bags outside (guarded). Also its forbidden to take a pictures inside.
The guide was appearing really strict which looked very funny to us. But obviously he was into his job. At the beginning he read us some safety rules, gave us a brochure and the tour proceeded. We were firstly afraid that he will just read from the brochure he gave us, but eventually he started adding more information and the tour turned out to be pleasant. It took around 30 minutes.
In the end you can buy local produced tea. We got 250g of leafs for mere 350lkr.
Worth the visit if you have a way nearby.

Title: good tour
Text: About one hour tour wit shopping the tea products. tour was nice and too much long.. you can smell the aroma from tea leaves whole the time.

Title: Old and cool!
Text: Amazing to see how the tea is made! It costs 250rs per person and you get a guide! (You cant take photos inside) The Factory is connected with Rain Forrest Alliance, they had built hospitals and schools. According to our tuktuk driver they where also building new houses for the workers!

Title: Expeditive visit... not worth your money
Text:
Despite its great location, Dambetenne does very little to attract tourists. Though the history behind the factory is great (founded by sir Lipton in 1890) the tour itself isnt worth it. They charge you 250 rupees per person for an expeditive tour that lasted 10 min, yet they tell you the fee is for management. No pictures allowed, the guide, which seems to be the plant manager, does not look like he wants you there. Broken english. 

On the upside, he did answer all our questions and we got a good understanding of tea processing. It was simply done in a very bland, dry way. No tea tasting afterwards either.

Title: Expensive in comparison
Text:
First nothing going on, no tours, no processing. And if there was there is 250$ charge. Other factory tours are free.
Tough driving up narrow road, limited parking, etc. But the best spot to get a tuk tuk to lipton seat

Title: Do not bother
Text:
The previous comments are positive.
Maybe there is a new guide who doesnt speak much English , therefore it was a waste of time and money , 250 R per person .
We were hoping to taste a cup of tea, they give you nothing. No photos allowed .

Title: Not worth it
Text: The tour charges a fee, its rushed, bad explanations from the guide, no photos allowed, no tea to drink, it's a dirty factory, try to sell u expensive tea at the end, had a better tea tour in Kandy with samples and explanations

Title: Whistle stop tour of the factory
Text: This tour is very very quick but I did enjoy walking round the factory. No tea tasting at the end, just a run through of all the teas you could purchase. We were made to wait a long time for our tour to begin whilst he tried to sell tea to a couple on the previous tour...

Title: Waste of time
Text: We were so excited to visit this place but left so disappointed. The tour was so fast. We were finished in 15 minutes with no tea tasting even when we enquired. The tour guide seemed more interested in selling overpriced green tea after showing us around a black tea making factory. Veey disappointed. Go to the tea factory in Ella instead.

Title: Quick tour
Text: Worth a couple bucks to get a quick tour of how tea is made, in the factory where Lipton started his mass commercialization (by the looks of it, nothing much has changed in the process). Guide spoke pretty good English and answered all questions. Then take a tuk tuk up to Liptons Seat for panoramic views.

Title: Waste of time
Text: The Dambatenne Tea Factory tour at the bottom of Lipton's Seat was a complete was of time - uninterested guide who was clearly more interested in trying to sell the tea than anything else.

Title: 30 minute tour. Very interesting and worth the visit
Text: Costs around 250 rupees. The factory is open every day. Although it says no photos, we were allowed to photograph and video. The smell inside is amazing. The guide speaks fast so get close to him and try to keep up. Paid 450 for some great tea.

Title: Another tea factory to visit
Text: The only reason to visit Dambatenne would be to take a tour of the tea factory, but as in most of them photography is forbidden. the factory was constructed in 1890 by Sir Thomas Lipton. I had already visited a tea factory so i did not bother taking a tour here but i noticed many visitors here. The tea factory stands at 1560 m above sea level.

Title: Average experience
Text: Lipton's Seat itself is so beautiful but after visiting the factory we got little disappointed. The tour is VERY brief and quick (in 20 mins you are out). They show you the machines and in a very simple basic way explain preparation of tea. Employes don't really care whether you understand or not. They just want to do they part and be done with you quickly. No tea tasting has been already mentioned. It was not that bad, but you just expect more from original Lipton factory.

Title: Tourist trap
Text:
You have to pay 250 per person. We had to wait to get the tour start. You pay 20 for the toilet. We asked if we could get at least a cup of tea during the waiting. That was not possible. 
Also they mentioned that after the tour it is not possible to taste the tea.
Because we also read a lot of reviews about the ultra fast tour and the poor speaking English guide we decide to move on. We will do a tour in Ella.

Title: Feeble 'tour' after hiking Lipton's Seat
Text:
The only pleasant aspects about this 'tour' were the smells and sights.
The guide himself was offhand, didn't care if you could hear what was said, spoke fast and hurried through. This was after being told to wait for indefinite period of time in the front. There was no photographs allowed inside and no tasting, not even a sip!
I guess it is deceptive because the room you are defrauded of 250 rupees has a sign saying 'Tasting Room'. Haha

Title: No tasting of the tea :(
Text: Its a very nice factory to visit! U can understand the all process of making Tea! The only bad about this is that u pay but u dont have a testing of the tea making there ,which I do real think that such a big factory with such a great name should give a tasting of the tea ..... in the area there are others tea factory also very nice and the give u a tasting :)

Title: Would visit somewhere else
