Text: I am sure there are better tea factories to visit in the region. I visited here because it was on my way back from Lipton's Seat and because it is the "Lipton's" factory. Sticking at the factory to me it didn't write feel like they were terribly interested to run the tours. Upon entering there was no one to ask about buying a ticket or times for the tours. Then someone appeared and said the next tour would be in 5 minutes and to take a seat on some chairs. 15-20 minutes later the tour finally started, after having been sold a ticked in a rather unfriendly (bordering on rude) manner. The tour itself was quite informative but felt rushed and photos were not allowed inside at all, which was very disappointing because the factory building and machinery are still mostly original. There was no tea tasting at the end. There was some cups and tea on a counter together with a kettle, but it liked rather dirty/messy and I wouldn't have wanted to taste anything there anyways.

Title: Don't give it a miss!
Text: Well worth a visit! You get a good idea how the tea making process works and also what the working conditions are like both in the factory and in the fields. They are frankly less than enviable. A must see when in Sri Lanka. Beautiful area too!

Title: Disgusting
Text: We were charged 500 rupees per person entrance and told to join a group that was already in progress. The guide was unhelpful, unfriendly and raced us around the tour and at the end tried to sell us overpriced tea without even the chance to sample the teas on offer. The workers having appalling dirty and unsafe working conditions and are paid substance wages with no pensions or sick leave. A total disgrace. We have visited many tea factories in Sri Lanka over the years and this one is by far the worst. They do not want visitors only your money. If this tea factory were the only one a tourist visited they would get a totally false impression  of the beautiful land that is Sri Lanka

Title: Only after your money
Text: We visited this tea factory after our walk to Lipton's Seat. It was very disappointing because although they charge an entrance fee they rush you through the factory as quickly as possible in order to sell you overpriced tea at the end of the tour.

Title: Rude, rushed, dirty...
Text: We were extremely disappointed. When we arrived they were very quick to take our money (250 Rs per person) but no-one wanted to give us the tour. One guide was finally forced to show us around. He was very rude and his English was poor. The place is dirty and will make you think twice about drinking tea again. Would you put in your cup some dirt swept off the floor of a factory and on which people have walked? Maybe thats why they do not allow photos... The reputation of the Lipton company would not benefit... After a very short / rushed and uninformative tour, the guide tried to force us to buy some tea. We were surprised that there would be no tasting. The guide announced this rudely. The tone and manner were all wrong. Try another tea factory. This one is a terrible disappointment. Go to Lipton Seat but do not stop in this factory.

Title: Interesting to see how tea is made
Text: We were at Lipton's seat so stopped of on the way back to our lodging. Interesting to see the tea making process. No pressure at the end to buy stuff if you don't want to. Actual highlight was having a fresh roti and cup of tea in a local place opposite the factory while we waited for it to open

Title: Not worth a Rupie
Text:
Without exaggerating it was the worst guided tour I have ever taken part in. It took like 5 minutes and no tasting or anything. Guide was not to eager to explain the tea factory and the processing. A total rip-off. Dont waste your money,time and efforts on that. I have done better tea factories for no fees and with a proper guide and tasting.
However, bus trip up and down the hills was nice.

Title: Disappointing!
Text: We toured the factory on a Sunday and there was not much to see. Many sections were shut and the guide was difficult to understand. After a rush look through they brought out four lots of tea you could buy. It would have been nice to have been offered some samples, maybe have tastings like a winery in Australia does. Would not waste my time going back

Title: Very interesting
Text: We stopped at the Dambatenne Tra Factor on the way back from the Limpton seat! Very interesting and informative visit!

Title: Enjoyable little tour
Text: After Liptons Seat we had a look around - a nice break from the walk. Its fairly cheap and the tour is around a working factory. The whole place smells of tea and it feels like you have stepped into the past. We had some tea to taste at the end. 75% of their product is still sold to Liptons.

Title: Please don't go..
Text:
... you will save yourself time and the rupees. 
You will have more question when you leave than answers
You need to fit as well because the speed of the tour 
As a person who worked in hospitality it has to be one of the worst.
I know the factory don't look at this review but it's for someone who ideally would like to see how their tea is make.

Title: An interesting stop in tea country
Text: Had such a good visit to the factory and learnt so much about the history of the area and the intensive process of tea farming - Ill never quite look at a cup of tea the same and nothing has tasted quite as good since. A fairly short trip and tour is all you need and its a nice excursion if you are staying at a nearby hotel. The man leading our tour was friendly and showed us around and we bought some lovely tea as gifts for friends back home.

Title: Great
Text: Wonderful experience and the guide is friendly. Recommend buying some of the tea given how cheap it is!

Title: Great tour and beautiful views
Text: Visited Dambatenne Tea plantation, factory and Liptons Seat, the favourite spot of Thomas Lipton (founder of Liptons tea). As tea drinking Brits we found the factory tour fascinating and you can buy tea at the end which is unblended (better than we get in the UK). We were lucky to also see tea weighing with the tea pickers on our way round the beautiful estate. I thoroughly recommend taking a tuk tuk to the top of the estate (walking not for the faint hearted!) to see Liptons Seat where he liked to entertain guests, which commands staggering views across the beautiful hills of Ella. Our guide told us that on a clear day you can see all four corners of Sri Lanka from here. Couple of things to note - go on a clear day and not on a cloudy or misty one, and other reviews on here have commented on how the factory isnt health and safety friendly and has tea around the place. Its a working factory in Asia rather than the cool air conditioned world of Europe, which is part of what makes it so interesting, still relying on old methods. This was one of the best days of our trip and Id happily recommend it.

Title: What did you say?
Text:
In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka.
We visited also Orange Fields Tea factory before, so this visit became as a disapointment: rushing through the factory with limited information and almost impossible to understand the guide.
The safety and cleaniness on the workfloor was not in order: you could see the treadmarks of an animal on the fermenting beds of the tea, teadust everywhere (which made the floors slippery).
Nice to hear Lipton built this factory, but not really worth the visit.

Title: Quite interesting short tour
Text: Quite interesting short tour . The factory doesn't seem to have changed its methods too much since it opened

Title: Dambatenne Tea Factory Disappointment
Text: We waited too long for the tour of machinery. The Guide was a one size fits all variety, so boring. At the end of the tour he asked us to buy tea without tasting. I asked for tasting which he organised begrudgingly. I also asked to use the toilet and a female member of staff walked me there then demanded 20 Rp which I didn't have, so she refused to let me in. I did return later, located it myself, and found the filthiest toilet ever, which didn't flush. Not worth going to this tea factory!

Title: Average tour - could have been better
Text: I had been looking forward to this tour, but what a disappointment this was. It is an average tour, and the person guiding us around the factory, kept on reprimanding us for taking photographs. AFTER we finished the tour, he showed us a sign on the door, which read that we cannot take photographs!

Title: Informative and enjoyable tour!
Text: The tour takes about 15-20 minutes and runs 2-3 times an hour, I assume basing on demand. Or guide explained the tea making process very well, taking us through the steps from leaf picking to tea cup. He demonstrated the machinery used and offered tasting and an opportunity to purchase the finished article at the end.

Title: Due to poor reviews we did not go in...however.....
Text: We did go up to the Tea Factory.  We spoke with a gentleman at the door who did not understand a word of what we were talking about.  We turned around and walked back to Haputale.  The walk back was stunning, it is 9 km along a well-paved road and with the mists drifting in and out the walk back was OH WOW around every corner.

Title: Completely ignored!
Text:
Arrived at the Tea Factory to find there was no one to advise us about a tour. No notices up other than the cost! No one showed up at all so we decided to go on up to Liptons Seat. 
On our return to the Factory to purchase some tea we went into the tasting room; there were two men counting money in there who ignored us initially...we said we wanted to buy some tea...they continued to ignore us so we left! No purchase ...no sale for them...appalling customer service.

Title: Interesting!
Text: Process of tea production very interesting, especially since method is similar to that of a century ago. Well worth the visit.

Title: Really great to find out how our tea is processed
Text: A very interesting tour of a working tea factory to see all the stages of tea production.  Our guide was very informative and friendly.

Title: Disappointing
Text:
This is a classic factory, founded by Sir Thomas Lipton in 1890. Our Lonely Planet guide had written up this tour so we came with high expectations. They were not met. The tour lasted about 20 minutes, and the guide seemed eager to get it over with. His English was fine, but often drowned out by the noisy machinery.

There was no tasting after the tour. There was a lame effort at marketing tea on site, but no effort had been put into appetizing display or information about prices.

The gents' rest room was terrible.  Dirty, dysfunctional, no soap, no running water, just a little lady who poured cold water from a bottle and then immediately stretched out her hand for a tip.

Foreign guests would--in my view--gladly pay much more than the paltry Rs.250 now charged, if they got a good tasting and decent rest rooms. They already do without protest at other tea factories that are in better shape. Having traveled for about 45 minutes on the narrow road out from Haputale, people will not back off when faced with a higher entrance fee.

You can continue another 7 km from the factory to Lipton's seat. Tuk-tuks were available to take people there. The one-way fee quoted to us was Rs. 800.

Title: Tea as never seen before
Text: Finally leanrt out sonething about tea production. Interesting knowledge acquired here for only 250 Rp. Unfortunatelly taking pictures is forbidden within the factory interior but you can understand the know-how protection.

Title: short and sweet
Text: This tour of the tea factory was only about 15 minutes, but informative and we enjoyed it. The did the tour in English and another language, and we likely missed about 40% of the information, but still learned something new.

Title: Disorganised and left us feeling empty
Text: Although it was good to see the factory in operation, there is no tea room facility here, no tastings on offer and the tour was curt and disorganised.  We even had to pay to go to the toilet.  Unless this is your only opportunity, I'd suggest going elsewhere.

Title: After reading the reviews.........
Text: I really enjoyed the tour, yes the guide had a really pronounced accent (we are in Sri Lanka). He was informative and funny.  During the tour we looked at the tea process (and helped with the drying and rolling part).  He allowed us to take a couple of pictures and we sampled the tea afterwards.  A good tour, not long, but neither is the tea making process.

Title: Disappointing tea factory tour
Text:
Rather short though informative tour through the factory. 250 Rs entrance fee. No tea tasting available. No fotos.
Wash room facilites were very dirty!
Not worth the 20 min drive form Haputale.

Title: Nice to see a working Tea Factory
Text: We had a beautiful drive to the Dambatenne Tea Factory from Ella; tea and tea plantations all around. The factory visit is not very long but it is a working tea factory and very interesting to see. Nothing much seems to have changed since Sir Thomas Lipton was there. After the tour, we went up through the tea plantation to visit Lipton's Seat but it was very foggy so we didn't have a nice view.

Title: Interesting Tour
Text: Our tour guide was very good and it was fascinating to learn how tea is made and to see the factory in action. Set amongst the tea plantations, the views on the walk up the road amongst the tea fields to Liptons Seat are amazing.

Title: Short but very informative.
Text: Dambatene Tea factory was our planned stop on the way to Lipton's seat. We took a local bus from Haputale, very cheap 80 rupees. The tour in the factory was short but the guy told us all the important information and answered all our questions. We bought their tea there for 350 rupees. However there is not a tea tasting afterwards which is a pitty. Over all I think it is good to see it.

Title: Average but don't expect much
Text:
After our visit to Lipton Seat, we decided to have a look at the tea factory. We read reviews before we went so did not expect much from the 250 rupee tour.

It was a quick 15 minute tour, the guide spoke very fast (and in a noisy environment) - note if your English is not fluent then you may have no chance of understanding him.

Like others said, there is no tea tasting but it is cheap. In a way it is a shame as they are keen to sell you their tea (only one type however) and there is no opportunity to smell or taste before buying. 

It was a quick insight into a tea factory but I wouldn't make a special trip for it and if you like tea then you can buy more types of tea elsewhere like in Haputale town, Ella or Kandy or Colombo (pretty much everywhere else...)

Title: Not really worthing it
Text:
It's interesting to visit the factory but the guy was really in a hurry and did not take enough time to explain us! not even a cup of tea at the end :( 
It's better to climb to the Lipton Seat and enjoy the view on the tea plants! much better

Title: Nice visit - bit too short
Text: We went to visit Dambatenne as it was a must according to our guidebooks. The visit was good - lots of information and friendly. However it was a bit short (30 minutes max) and there was no possibility to taste the tea ! But it's a fun thing to do and relatively easy to access (bus from Haputale every 30 minutes, tuk tuk 500-600 Rs)

Title: Dry spiel
Text: We waited 30mins in the waiting room. Our 250 rupees each was collected and we were lead into the factory and stood in front of various stages of tea making. The employee gave a very hurried, rehearsed spiel on the process. Some of the machines were working but not many. We asked about tasting the tea and were told to go to the shops down in the street. Toilets had no running water to flush or wash hands. The doors didn't close. A lady wanted money for cleaning.

Title: Interesting visit. Too bad we could not taste tea...
Text: The visit was really interesting and the guide showed us the making process with much detail. Considering you have to pay for your visit there, we would have appreciated a cup of tea at the end of the visit.

Title: great insight into how tea is made
Text: A must visit if you are in the tea country. Fabulous insight into how tea is made and brought to us. We had no idea there were so many types of tea or what they did to get it!

Title: Insite into tea production
Text: A fascinating first hand look at how tea is produced. A proper factory, with no tourist shop, tea room or other tourist facility, this place is the real thing - focused on tea production and bulk selling.

Title: that is ok
Text: that is ok after visited lipton seat and know more about the tea factory process. although the tuktuk driver is more informative than the guide but that is ok if you never visit tea factory before

Title: Fascinating, a must for your tour of the hilly country
Text:
We took in the tea factory as part of a day out with a local tuk tuk driver and guide and found the production process fascinating.  I work as a business transformation consultant, my husband in quality and this factory was mind blowing.  How on earth this production process was awarded ISO 9001 I've no idea but they have an excellent process which has been working successfully for hundreds of years and if it isn't broken don't try to fix it! 

I've read other reviews that say that the factory was "dirty".  It's a tea production plant full of tea particles but it was a clean environment and very authentic.

I'm writing this review as a tourist not a manufacturing consultant and I believe that if you don't experience this then you are missing out on your hilly country experience.  Start your day plucking your own leaves in the plantations, visit Lipton's Seat with its amazing views and finish off with a visit to this tea factory.

The factory manager who gave us our tour was highly intelligent and didn't miss a beat throughout the tour keeping an eye on the production process.  In response to the "rip off" review posted earlier.  250 rupees is only GBP1.50.  Where can you get a factory tour and a cup of tea in Europe for £1.50?

Title: Interesting but a little worrying
Text: We learnt quite a lot during our visit despite my having been to a tea factory in Kenya previously. What was worrying however was that the strict notices about wearing protective clothing and not touching the tea were all ignored by the staff who showed us around. In addition there was no water in the staff toilets (which we had to use) - not the most wonderful situation for a beverage preparation plant.

Title: Authentic processes in wonderful location.
Text: There are numerous tea estates in Sri Lanka that give guided tours and provide the opportunity to see traditional methods of tea production - this one is authentic and is situated in a wonderful location. So as well as seeing at first hand the tea production process one can enjoy spectacular views over the heart of Sri Lanka's extensive 'hill country'. It is not expensive to take a tour and one can get a very good feel of the atmosphere of tea plantations by simply visiting the area and seeing the tea pluckers in the plantations and appreciate the scale of the factory and its estate.

Title: Friendly Staff
Text: There are scheduled guided tours around the tea factory. You have to buy a ticket which is not expensive. The staff is friendly and the tour is very informative.

Title: A great place to see the historic production of tea
Text:
We took an hour's drive from Ella to visit this factory. You don't need to pro-book a tour and can turn up, with an option to purchase tea in boxes at the factory. 

The scenery is incredible and you can see staff on the factory line processing the tea.

We had a great guide that walked us through the whole process before we then visited Lipton's seat.  The views from Lipton's seat are stunning.

Title: Could make it more better
Text: They have the potential to make this a better experience. It was neat walk around and see all the machines and process of hoe they make the tea before shipping to Lipton's but they have an area for tea sampling that they do not use.

Title: Tour interesting but short, no tea for sale
Text: The factory and the whole tea making process is interesting, but the tour itself is very short and the guide seemed quite bored. Another downside is that they don't offer any tea for tasting. They don't sell tea either.

Title: All about tea
Text:
Nice place to see where you're tea comes from, but the tour felt a bit rushed. Also there's no possibility to try the tea they make. 
The plus side is that the views to the factory are really nice.

Title: Yes worth a visit
Text:
Located on a hill near Haputale. This factory was founded in 19th century by Sir Thomas Lipton, and machines look like from that time. Tours around the factory with explanation of the production process. Fee 250 LKR, opened from 8am.  They also sell local black tea, but no tasting. It is not allowed to take photos inside. Its definitely worth a visit.
You will probably also see people working at tea plantations around.

Title: Lovely way to find out how tea is made
Text: We really enjoyed our visit and learnt how tea is made - fascinating.  I don't think I will look at a cup of tea in the same way again.  We learnt about the different teas and how to make a perfect cup.  We didn't feel rushed like some have said but then we went on a tour organised by our hotel.  We also had time for tasting.

Title: Sad
Text: We were on our way down the mountain and our driver suggested we stop in and have a look - it costs 250 LKR and 20 LKR if you want to use the toilets. This was a very basic tour not like some of the more commercial operations who dont charge a fee to go through and they also offer tastings.

Title: Fun little tour
Text: Short but concise little tour about tea. Learned some things I clearly didn't know, you can purchase tea at the end too. No tastings though (or at least not when we were there?). I definitely recommend it after walking down from Lipton's sear.

Title: Quite rushed, no tasting
Text: We visited the tea factory after going down from Lipton's seat, mostly because of the handy location but it was quite disappointing. The visit is very short, we felt a little rushed. Also there was no tasting in the end. I guess it's not too bad for the price but we were expecting more. There are probably plenty of better tea factories to visit throughout the country!

Title: Good to see how Tea made
Text: It's nice to see the tea you drink everyday how it take to much time to be ready, all process is explaining by factory guy, photo in most places is not allowed, you may buy some tea also after the tour, entrance fee is 250 LKR...

Title: The visit is worthy
Text:
Very interesting visit to the tea factory... it smells amazing and you quick learn the production process of the tea. 
It's the original building that Mr. Lipton built!

Title: Interesting for Tea Buffs
Text: A stop off on the way to Liptons Seat the factory has organised tours for visitors showing in detail how tea is produced. Entrance fee and charge for using toilets. Tours are in groups and when we were there was quite a wait for the tour to commence

Title: Nice but nothing extraordinary
Text:
We visited the factory within our descent from Lipton´s Seat and, at least, it warmed us up as we were quite cold that time. You need to wait for a guide to show you around and pay a small fee. There were up to 10 people in our group and you´ll be lead to different zones of the tea production. You can smell a nice tea smell there, though I expected it would be stronger as I was in a similar factory in the Azores couple of years ago and it was much stronger there. You cannot take pictures in the factory.
After the tour you can buy some tea there but we found the packages too big and bought some tea in a much smaller packages later in Ella tea shops.

Title: Not worth the effort other than for scenery
Text:
Quick review. Long way up in tuk tuk. Very bumpy road. Super speedy tour. Lasted 10 minutes. Interesting insight into how tea is made but I think the guide could win first prize at the international speed speaking contest!
Very disappointed there was absolutely no history about Thomas Lipton. No opportunity to taste tea and no purchases to be made. No cafe.

Title: Super speeded factory tour
Text: It's a great opportunity to be able to see a tea factory and the processes leading up to the final tea. We read through the rules before entering - I then learned that no one else might have done this. Kids were everywhere. Some people were photographing/filming even though it was forbidden. Everyone were digging with their hands in the tea all through the process even though it clearly said to not touch anything. I felt like we were in a group of toddlers and seriously doubt the hygienic aspect of having these plant tours. I did not follow most of what was said during the tour either due to the noise level and because the guide was rushing through everything. However, to be able to experience all the smells and the atmosphere in there was amazing.

Title: Informative and Interesting
Text: A lovely tour of the tea factory while staying at Thotalagala.  Walked back to our accomodation and was met with sensational views and lovely interactions with the locals.

Title: Interesting to see how they make tea
Text: Poor conditions in the firm but exciting to see the methods. Lot of manual work is needed here yet which creates jobs the people who live here.

Title: Interesting factory, poor guidance
Text:
This is a tea factory you can see in actual production.
Entrance fee is 250 R pp but the guide was not so willing to give us many details on the job, he was afraid we were spies I think...
;-)

Title: Very interesting
Text:
We stopped here after having visited Lipton's Seat. The walk down to the factory (2 hours, slow pace) was very enjoyable. 

Entrance fee (guided visit) to the factory was 250rs. No pictures can be taken inside. The visit was a bit rushed but interesting and worthy. I highly recommend it.

Bus from outside the factory to Haputale cost 30rs.

Title: Good learning experience
Text: We got a great tour of the factory.  It was eye-opening; I had no idea how tea was made prior to our tour.  The staff was friendly and the guide was knowledgeable.  Cost was a few USD/person.

Title: Worth doing but could be improved with minimal effort
Text: This tea factory knows it has a captive market and no competition in the form of people visiting Lipton's Seat. It charges for entrance (unlike many) and doesn't include a tasting. That having been said, it is worth doing. A brusk but informative tour takes you up close with every stage of the tea making process. A good way to finish off a morning up Lipton's Seat but with a little effort could be much more memorable.

Title: A peak into tea factory
Text: It was a weekend when we were there. So, it was just a verbal introduction and a basic tour of the factory. We were then ushered to their cafe/shop. Paid to try some tea and bought some with us.

Title: Almost complete waste of time
Text: The visit to the factory was interesting solely thanks to the actual production process going on. The guide made no effort whatsoever to show or explain anything (or to speak clearly enough for that matter). Of course there was no tea tasting in the end ("we can buy it and try at home" the guide said). Don't waste your time. There are other factories offering much more for the price of a tip for the guide.

Title: Very interesting, well worth a visit
Text:
From Living Heritage we took an early morning trip to Liptons Seat and the Dambatenne Tea Factory - visit Liptons Seat first for the best light and views - we left at about 6/6:30 and arrived around 9 for stunningly vivid colours and far reaching views, then stopped at the factory on the way back.
The factory tour was not too long, it felt quite scripted but was very interesting covering the whole tea production process.  At the end there is an opportunity to taste different types / grades of tea - and you can buy too, though only tea bags rather than leaf tea.

Title: Interesting experience
Text:
You should visit the factory on the way back from Lipton's seat to see how is the tea from local fields actually manufactured. 
It was not long, but interesting,  however we were able to understand every 4th word from our guide, cause of the noise and quite bad English.
They also sell one product, box with 100 tea bags for 600lkr.

Title: There are better tea factory tours
Text: The guide on our tour had already warned us that this was rubbish, but because it was on our itinerary he had to take us!  The tea factory guide was just going through the motions, the factory was non operational when we saw it, the tourist toilets were disgusting, we were banned from taking photographs and we were invited to buy packets of tea yet they refused to let us try any!

Title: Interesting but much potential...!
Text: During a 15-20 mins tour you get to see the whole process from the fresh leaves coming in to the final product, being processed on what looks like machinery equipment from the 1950-60s. Very interesting, yet many questions left open and as other reviewers have written: no chance for tasting, e.g. the different quality levels that are being produced.

Title: Like a Pearl in Sri Lankas Mountains
Text:
When arriving in Haputale by motorbike (we did a couple of 1000s kilometers in Lanka) it is just like a pearl in the mountains, truely beautiful between mountains full with green tea plantations, blue skies and an amazing view over Sri Lanka. Haputale lies about 1600m above SeaLevel and it could be a bit cold in the evening. 
:
There are some nice small temples around and the teaplantations are always worth a visit...most of them wont let you in. LiptonFactory has guided tours we heard but we did not go there, we been in Dhambatenne Factory. 
:
There is also a trainstation in Haputale, so you dont have to go by motorbike, if you do, be carefull, SriLankan drivers are ChaosKids, always too fast and even for money I would not hop into one of this busses to Haputale, its just rediculous how they ride ;) 
:
all in all Haputale is Phantastic, we came from Arugam bay and our next stop after 3 days in Haputale was Ratnapura

Title: Time For Tea
Text: Did the tour on a quiet Saturday morning. Can't quite believe this Sixties-style factory was still in operation. Tour was rather swift, hard to hear the helpful guide over the noise of the machines. No tea tasting which was rather odd as there were tea pots and cups on the side. Guide was keen to sell the tea.

Title: NO Tea Tasting
Text:
Dambatenne Tea Factory Walk Back to Haputale
I took a local bus (RS 30) UP to the tea factory at 9 AM. The tour was 20. It costs RS 250. Short & sweet with NO tea tasting or even a cup of tea. By 10:17 I was slowly caning my way DOWN to Haputale. Gorgeous & a pleasant walk with incredible viewpoints. See the pictures.

Title: Disappontment in tea factory
Text:
Not sure if the guy was already on his way home or what, but I did not enjoy visiting this factory.
We paid full price, guide has strange English and on top to this he always explained things next to noise machine. Whole tour was just running through the factory. In the end also no tea tasting happen.
I believe that with better guide it is more interesting place to visit - all the machines, tea plants and their smell.

Title: Interesting factory visit
Text: Interesting to see a working tea factory in action. Due to the noise it is difficult to hear the guide, so posters or a leaflet would help understanding.

Title: Comprehensive tour
Text:
This was our second tea factory tour. Unlike our first (free but cursory) tour, this was a comprehensive tour covering all aspects of the tea manufacturing process, conducted within a functioning tea factory. We got to walk inside the factory and observe people and machines at work. The only downside is that there is no place to grab a cuppa post the tour. There is tea for sale post the completion of the tour. 
If you're looking for a tour that lets you see the process in action, this is the tour for you. Highly recommend.

Title: Fascinating with original Victorian machinery still in use
Text: Really interesting even on a Sunday with no leaves being picked - Saturday's leaves were still being dried and processed howerver. Probably not much to see on a Monday!

Title: Tea on the floor
Text: The tour inside the factory is interesting, especially for someone who hasn't visited any tea factory yet. It doesn't take long to see the process and the best part is to see the tea being fermented on the floor. This is what we drink :-) Quite disappointing is that you don't get any tea to taste... I expected more for 250 RPS.

Title: Short but interesting
Text:
This brief tour around the tea factory was interesting to see the whole sorting and sifting process. The machines that shake and rattle sift the tea into different grades. The barefooted ladies that are tiny then carry these huge bags around the factory with incredible ease.
I wasn't too keen to hear about the barracks in which they live. Most live in a very tired shed/out building with up to 20 people living in one room. A toilet block consisting of one toilet for about 50 people and these poor people get paid approx £3 per day!!   These people work so hard for their money and groups like ours pay to visit and leave tips . I refused to leave a tip to go to the big wigs. 
Pay your workers more I say. Stop being greedy.

Title: Tea is still made the same way as more than 100 years ago
Text: Very interesting tour which only takes about 30 minutes.  They take you through the whole production sequence.  Make sure you go during working hours and take the tour. Do explore the web site given below. Very informative.

Title: Brief but interesting tour of an historic tea factory
Text: This factory was actually built by Thomas Lipton in 1890 and it's got some quaint charm. The office manager will take you round on a quick (10-15 mins) tour to see the different stages of tea production. Unlike some other reviewers, we weren't offered a tasting - perhaps because it was a quiet day with few visitors. If you've not seen a tea factory before, it's definitely worth popping in on your way to/from Lipton's Seat but I wouldn't make the trek up there just to see it.

Title: Really interesting
Text: Informative tour of the whole factory explaining the tea making process and lovely to see the historic equipment in action.  Tours are daily, but there is no processing on a Monday morning since the tea pickets dont work on Sunday.

Title: Interesting but shallow
Text: I found interesting having a tour around the tea  processing factory, seeing the machines, but it was on a rush taking us from one station to the other in a hurry and at the end I thought there was a tea tasting but they only sell tea. The tour it's 250 and the teas are 350.

Title: Short tour was informative but a cup of tea needed!
Text:
The tour (250 Rs each) was well rehearsed and informative but a cup of tea or a tea tasting at end could really simply enhance the experience.
We'd just finished the walk to Lipton Seat from the Tea Factory.

Title: Amazing step back in time
Text:
For 250 rupees you get a quick 20-30 minutes tour of the factory, seeing how fresh tea leaves are converted to tea. 
* Avoid Mondays and Sundays when there is no production. 
* You get to touch and smell the tea in its various stages. 
* You can't take photos inside the factory
* I didn't have to wear a protective coat (they were available though, but I didn't think anyone would need them)
* There is no tea tasting. 
* I got the tour straight away when I arrived (I hadn't booked). If someone is getting a tour when you arrive, you'll have to wait for the guide to finish that tour before it is your turn (which shouldn't be long).

Having been to beer breweries in developed countries, I expected a modern highly mechanized process, involving maybe a few operators in a control room. Instead this place looked right out of the 1890s, with people shoveling tea and antiquated machinery. To me that made this tour a real eye opener.

To get there, I took a tuk tuk arranged by my hotel in Haputale. It cost 900 rupees out and back with waiting. A local would have gotten it for less I'm sure, but who cares. Didn't go to Lipton's seat. I went 7:30am in the morning, and saw the tea pluckers walking along the road on their way to work. The tea fields are on steep hills, and you can see them go down steps to go to the fields. Note that there is no bus, tuk tuk seems to be the only option.
  
Overall an interesting insight into how those Lipton tea bags from the supermarket are really made.

Title: Rushed tour, but still worth a stop
Text: The guide just shoots out his memorized spiel and it's pretty easy to tune him out.  However, it was pretty cool walking through the small factory for the 20-30 minutes.  It would've been nice to include a cup of tea with the tour price.  It's worth a stop if staying in Haputale.

Title: Interesting to learn about tea production
Text: We found the visit to Dambatenna tea factory very informative although the guide was quite difficult to understand. Don't go on Mondays where there will be no production.

Title: Interesting
Text: The visit is interesting and you can really see, touch and smell the leafs in the production line. It takes around 30 min and costs 250 rps.

Title: Liptons
Text:
Great cheap visit in a superb location. 
Proper working factory and a really interesting tour from a knowledgable guide. Try to go into the drivers' caff opposite; great short eats and, natch, tea.

Title: Amazing how they produce tea nowadays!
Text: Great experience. You will finally understand how and why you Lipton's tea bag is filled with powder :) worth to take a guide.

Title: A functional and rushed tour
Text: Reputed to the world's longest factory, the building looks nice and gracious from outside but leave your expectations at the door. Inside it is a sterile factory manned by efficient but not very friendly people. For LKR250 rupees you get a rushed but informative tour and a good understanding of tea production with no nice cuppa waiting for you at the end of the tour. But come for the glorious view - from any cliff along the road, you can see magnificent sea of clouds, even better than world's end and best thing of all, it is free and you don't need a long hike through Horton's plain to see it :D

Title: Working tea factory
Text: I combined this factory tour with a visit to Liptons Seat.  The good part of this tour is you only have to wait a few minutes before the guide picks you up.   The tour itself was very rushed,  I hardly could keep up with the guide, I was in and out in 15 minutes. It is interesting to see a working tea factory, but it went so fast that I hadnt the time to register what I was seeing.    There is no a tea sampling session at the end, fortunately there is a little tea shop in front of the factory.  You can have a nice cup here for a few rupees while you wait for the bus to bring you back to Haputale.  Practical info : entrance fee = 250 LKR, you have to wear a coat and a cap during your visit, and you are not allowed to take photos inside th factory.

Title: Weak tour
Text: The factory was in full swing which was great. However, the guide spoke poor English and was barely audible, even to the point where I leant uncomfortably close to try and hear him. Just following him around was enough to give the gist of how the process works. 250 rupees isn't a great amount but I still felt shortchanged. At the end of the tour, we were shown some mugs of tea. I expected the opportunity to taste the different teas but instead we were offered boxes of tea to buy. At which point I said goodbye!

Title: Surprisingly interesting
Text:
I wasn't expecting much going into the tour, but it turned out to be quite interesting. We might have been lucky that the plant was in full operation when there, but in any case it was enlightening to know exactly what all the tea pickers we'd just seen in the fields were doing, how much they got paid, and how the leaves they plucked ended up in teacups around the world. 
Our guide was informative and helpful with all of our questions, and contrary to some other reviews I just read, we were given tea at the start. 
On the downside, we did have to wait at least 45mins for somebody to show up and guide us, but we were in no rush and had just hiked quite a ways down from Lipton's Seat, so sitting on some leather couches was no big deal.

Title: Nice drive to the factory
Text: The drive is scenic for sure but that's it, management is very bad they don't know how to welcome visitors, they don't even offer a cup of tea... The tour is quick, everyone walks on tea leaves.. No idea why it's a lonely planet "top choice"

Title: Some people really are just peevish.
Text:
I'm a little annoyed with the slagging off of this place. It shows exactly how they make and produce the tea. What more do you lot want?

Saying this, I visited on my way to Lipton's seat and felt this place had good a good history which was worth the one pound entrance fee. Obviously, as some people have pointed out, they're are other factories that seem to offer visits of which are free, these may be better, but for the scenic drive around the mountains, great views for photos, en-route to Lipton's seat and being the factory that Sir Thomas J Lipton founded, I found the enter fee not enough to deter. 

Yes, a little cafe would be lovely to try the tea ( I was lucky and had a tour when the main guy was doing he tasting rounds and so had plenty to drink) but this factory is there to produce tea, not keep whiney tourists happy, if anything it shows what an old fashioned tea factory should look like. I'm sure the fermentation process which happens on the clean tea infested floor isn't just endemic to this place especially when the phrase 'dust off the floor' has been used for a very long time. By all means your welcome to start abstaining from drinking tea. I'm sure they won't change what they have been doing since long before any of you were even thought about. I must ad, photos were said to be not allowed, though i wasn't exactly subtle with my SLR and received no comments.

My review of 3 stars, I do feel is fair though. Toilets weren't great and the guide/manager wasn't completely coherent when explaining things to us although this isn't his fault that he is Sri Lankan. We did actually have our own guide who spoke very good english and so this didn't exactly faze us. The tea at the end I feel was on the expensive side, but if this is the last straw on the camels back which pushes you to make a snidey review then may i suggest you don't buy it?

It is exactly what it says on the tin.

Title: Who are you and where do you travel?
Text:
I was appalled when I read these reviews on returning from Sri Lanka! We visited this factory in March 2014. We have visited tea factories before which have not been working factories or had large groups touring including coaches. The drive was amazing through tea plantations including their schools, hospitals, clincs etc which were all in better condition than when we first visited 16 years ago.
We had an individual 30 minute tour for 500/= which is less than £2.30 2.80 euros for two! There was real working factory with no tea for sale except opposite at a tea stall which sold delicious spiced tea and short eats for 60p for us and our driver. The whole trip cost less than £3 plus driver and petrol which we had paid for anyway and was one of my best experience on this visit.

Sri Lanka is still a poor but developing country. Ifyou can afford to travel to a country as beautiful as it you should be prepared to paid a reasonable price for what you do to contribute to the economy. What can you buy in your home country for this? Do you live on 500/= which what the tea pickers get?

Title: Dambatenne Tea Factory
Text:
This factory was built by Sir Thomas J Lipton and he started his tea business from here and finally built an empire.
We have now tried to modernize this factory to a 2014 model but it is not at all easy.
Having read some reviews we find that people are stating about charging Rs. 250/= per soul and saying it is two expensive. This is less than 2 dollars. Sad when we go to foreign countries what exorbitant prices they charge and at times it is over 50 dollars just to see something.
This is essentially a tea manufacturing estate and we permit our guest that come to this area to have a look at the factory and if required to purchase some teas. It may be highly priced but definitely cheaper than what you purchase in the shelves of supper markets. We have people who comes regularly and buy large quantities of them obviously due to the quality of the product.
We pack top quality Uva Tea and they are fresh. There is a saying that " Cheap this no good and good things no cheap" we follow that principal.
If anyone cannot afford it then it is up to you we will not force you to do so but I am sure if you do buy you will always come back and buy more since we have so many who purchase up to 50 to 60 packs at a time.
Note- Photography is not permitted due to government regulations.
However thanks for the constructive critisism and whatever possible has been rectified.
 This reply is from the Manager of this Plantation.

Title: Frustrating visit
Text:
We went by tuk-tuk from Haputale (30 min).

:) To discover the process of tea manufacturing.

:( The visit is too short (20 min) and suffers from a lack a explanation (hopefully we read our lonely planet book just before...).
:( No tea tasting.
:( The tea for sale is highly expensive.
:( No photography are allowed.

Title: A quick view into the world of tea produce!
Text: A quick tour for an equivalent of 2 euros gives you within half an hour a good idea of the tea production process and different tea qualities. This also shows you how hard it is to trace 'fair' produce: their tea ends up in all sorts of branded teas, known and unknown labels.

Title: First Lipton Tea Factory
Text: Nothing much to say about the simple tea factory.. On the way from Lipton Seat so drop by and see the tea proccess.. If you have visited other factory then  you can forget this but if not, it is still a very good place to gain knowledge

Title: Deeply saddened and embarrassed
Text: I have not been to this Factory but had been planning to do so in a week or so. I went to the estate and no further.  I am a Grand Son of one of the earliest Managers of this estate, and others in the Lipton's Group.  My Grand father was George Thain-Davidson who was the Manager and Visiting Agent of Lipton's Tea Estates from 1907 until his retirement in1922 and he resided at the Bambatenne Estate.  Sadly he died suddenly at the Anuradhapura Grand Hotel in 1927 and was laid to rest at the Tissawave General Cemetery.  In researching his life and times I had planned to visit this factory but I am deeply embarrassed and saddened to read the dreadful reviews of this one time great Lipton institution.  Maybe someone will take note, and act to bring this great historic institution into prominence and be in the forefront of tourism in the tea industry.

Title: Uninviting, filthy, unfriendly and with a door price too!
Text: That was my first stop before heading to Lipton's seat, which was a lovely 30 minutes ride on a tuk tuk. It was hard to believe that was the factory where Lipton tea was produced?! They charge everyone LKR250 for the "pleasure" of seeing it inside, no shop to sell their product but just a small cabinet selling 2 products with inflated price. No photos allowed, and at the end of such tour, not a cuppa to sample even! You could see from the entrance, the condition of the factory is not the best, nor was it even hygienic. I did not bother with the visit, because I had done with Blue leaf (free) and Mackwood (the best of them all, also free). Give this one a miss, use their free toilet if necessary and that's it.

Title: Go to another one!
Text: We had (luckily!) already been to another excellent tea factory so weren't left disappointed.  The factory wasn't in operation the day we went but they were still charging people to take tours of....non working equipment! The info centre offers really no info and after traveling all over the world in a lot of third world countries I'm yet to ever see filthier more disgusting toilets....gross!! If you can go to Blue Fields Tea FActory do so instead - ok its busier/more touristy but you get free tours, tea and its immaculate throughout.

Title: Tea factory visit, but no cup of tea!
Text:
Visited Dambateene Tea factory in mid August 2013. Very interesting to see the tea production process but got the impression that visitors (who pay a fee) are an unwelcome intrusion. No you can't take any photos. No we do not have any tea shop, or serve any tea to drink! In a famous tea factory built by Sir Thomas Lipton I would have at least expected a cuppa. And would have been happy to pay for the pleasure. But like many of the fantastic sights in Sri Lanka the standard of 'tourist experience' leaves much to be desired. 
You can however buy some packets of leaf tea to take away, but I still wanted to sample the product in-situ! The owners should instead be pushing this place as major visitor attraction, and need only install some minimal facilities to make it a much more worth while place to visit. Despite my moans its still a must-see when coming back down from viewing Lipton's Seat. When you finish the short tour ask for some tea and maybe if enough of us complain my next visit just might see some tea pots and boiling water in place! And of course I ignored the 'no photos' rule!

Title: A tea factory with history, a great stopover after Lipton's seat
Text:
It's right at the bottom of Lipton's seat, so like most people, we went on the way back from Lipton's seat, recommended if you don't want to waste resources finding other tea factory to visit, just like us.   

The entrance fee is Rs.250 per person. We were brought around to see how tea leaves are processed, from drying to cutting and etc. I would say it's quite informative and I think I could still tell the processes even after a while. The guide (I think he is manager or some officer in the factory) was helpful enough. His accent is a bit thick but he was able to answer all the queries that we have, provided you get his accent. He is not exactly the super friendly type but is definitely not hostile at all. We were not pushed to buy anything at the end of the tour. We willingly bought their own (Dambatenne brand) loose BOPF tea at Rs.300, reasonable.    

The factory doesn't have fancy deco nor high-tech machine, but I like how it feels very vintage somehow. It's a medium and modest tea factory with real work going on, real people working inside, unlike some places where people were hired to put up a 'show' of working when there's visitors.  

The tour is approx 20 to 30 minutes. No tea tasting session at the end of the tour. We enjoyed the tour and I think I've learned something about teas that I would otherwise wouldn't know.

Title: A large tea factory with history
Text: The entry fee for this tea factory is quite steep. There was a longish wait whilst they found a guide and the tour was quite interesting, if fairly quick. It is disappointing that they will not allow photos - it is not cutting edge technology and whilst flash may disturb the workers, what's wrong with natural light. As we were leaving they were setting up a tea tasting for buyers - that was interesting to watch. We did not get offered a "cuppa" but they were selling their expensive blends. It would have been interesting to compare the different types of tea from the same area.

Title: Interesting, but. .
Text: Good for an informative break on the walk down from sunrise on Liptons Seat. (The walk is highly recommended) I don't think it would hurt them to let you taste some tea though.

Title: Informative and you get to see inside
Text: The tour was very informative, and I enjoyed it thoroughly. The guide taking us around spoke English perfectly, and he was always ready to answer any questions we had. The types of tea and machinery were very interesting to know about, and I bought some souvenirs at the end of the tour. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you're going to Lipton's peak. It is closed on some days though, so do be sure to check before making the journey there from Haputale.

Title: Less Plus and More Minus
Text: I really appreciate the idea of showing the tea processing methodology to visitors but I hate to say that this is not a type of processing that we should show to anybody as the process is so unhygienic and disgrace to other tea processors trading Ceylon Tea. I want to say to anyone who visits a tea factory for the first time, take only the process from this place but not the other aspects like hygiene. Visitors will be charged Rs. 250 to the factory tour which seems reasonable but give a small sample of tea as a souvenir as the entry ticket nd cover the cost from the ticket. It promotes Ceylon tea. I highly encourage the  award winning Manager to analyse the situation very carefully and rectify the minuses.

Title: don't expect a cup of tea
Text: this is a very informative tour especially for someone like me who knows nothing about tea. the person who showed us around spoke good english. if you don't expect tea tasting at the end of the tour, surely you won't be disappointed.

Title: Really interresting
Text: I liked this visit, really interresting to see how people transform the black tea using tools coming from two centuries ago.

Title: I loved this!
Text: Yes, this may be touristy, but honestly I loved it.  It is set amid the lush tea plantations, and the tour was super informative.  Since I really knew nothing about tea planting and harvesting, I learned a lot.  And the aromas are intoxicating.  And there are authentic workers there, so you are able to see the factory in real motion.

Title: Good tour and scenic journey
Text:
The tuk tuk ride to the factory was possibly the best bit. The views are stunning and a good place to view Lipton's seat.

The tour of the factory was interesting, but it was just a little hard to understand the guide at times. Also, there was no tea tasting.

Still worth a visit.

Title: Very interesting!
Text: Lovely to see this old factory! It doesn't seem to have changed since it was built and was really interesting. Definitely worth a visit

Title: Great Tea plantation and location
Text: Lovely for panoramic views of the south and east coast of Sri Lanka provided one is not here on a misty day. Lush tea bushes and well maintained tea estate.

Title: Excellent cup of tea opposite the factory
Text: Really interesting tour of the tea house, built in 1890 as part of the Lipton empire. Although no photos were permitted inside it was fascinating to see the processes involved and the guide was well-spoken and informative. The walk up there from Haputale was absolutely stunning (most people take a tuk-tuk I think as the walk is around 10km) with incredible views all acorss the mist-shrouded hills and tea fields. To those concerned you don't get a cup of tea on the tour fear not! Just opposite the facotry there is a little shop where you can have a brew and a lovely chat with the owner Raj, we spent over an hour there chatting (his Englsh is good) and meeting his family whilst eating oranges from his garden tree, a true gent.

Title: Well guided tour - no photos - no tea house!
Text: I really loved to visit this place. The tour was well done. I could see all the processes. Good time to visit are the morning hours. Wish I could make some photos but permitted. Also no tea house there. Would be nice to try some of teas.

Title: 14 days adventures in SriLanka
Text:
Interesting introduction of the guide regarding the factory history, about the period when Sir Thomas Lipton was the owner for over 40 years from the late 1800s to 1930, and to see how well functioning the old machines and methods still works.
Besides, the factory is surrounded by beautiful tea plantations and homes for the approximately 1600 employees

Title: Informative Tour
Text:
What a lovely drive up to the factory, and a good tour.  So glad they continue to welcome visitors.  The tour is a good introduction to tea processing.  Not long or overly detailed, but enough.  The machinery is worth seeing.  I will look at my tea with new respect.

The factory is well organized, as are the tea fields and the scenery on the way up to Lipton's Seat is fabulous.  You can drive (car, van, or tuktuk) up to 1.4km (possibly further?) from the top on well-maintained, if narrow, roads.  Plenty of signs, if you follow the roads.  It's a nice walk the rest of the way.  Consider bringing pens to give the children you may meet.

Title: Short and sweet . . .
Text: Stopped here like most people do- on the way back from Liptons seat. Entrance was 250 rupees each, although there was a longish awkward wait before anyone greeted us, once did went went straight off on a 20 minute tour of the factory with a man whose English was pretty good although far from perfect,  there was NO pressure whatsoever to buy any tea.

Title: Disappointing
Text: We were really excited to do the tour of the tea factory originally founded by Sir Thomas Lipton. The drive there in a three-wheeler is bumpy but the views are breathtaking. Lonely Planet describes this tea plantation as welcoming visitors but this is not the feeling we got at all. Walking through the factory and gaining even a little knowledge of the process was great but the guide seemed bothered by having to take us around and rushed through everything (whole tour did not take longer than 15 minutes). We were led to a sad looking display unit and were told that we could buy tea at what seemed a pretty extravagant price). When we said that we would not be buying anything (considering that we had paid the 250 rupees each for the tour) the guide became hostile and we left with a bad taste in our mouths. The drive is beautiful and the tea factory would be a great place to stop on the way to Lipton's Seat, if they could find a guide who is passionate and keen on showing tourists around - a variety of tea options would probably also encourage a purchase.

Title: Superbly maintained, lots to see on the way.
Text:
The lush green tea plantations are worth a visit (a small entrance fee is asked to go to Lipton's Seat on its grounds'. Lots of well meant plaques on nature and ecosystem adorn the main road (in a charming old fashioned lingo), you will see spectacular flowers everywhere.
As in other tea factories, in Dambetenna you will learn a lot on real tea - the picking, fermenting, rolling... (and 'dust nr 1 or 2' which is the bleak leftover powder  used in lots of our western teas). The smell coming from the factory is already tempting!

Title: Comprehensive tour
Text: A well presented factual tour about the production of tea with a chance to see all the ancient machinery in action. It is probably all the same as it was over 100 years ago. You can buy a box of excellent tea at the end of the tour for about £1.75. The guide we had was knowledgeable when asked questions. Takes about 30 minutes to go round.

Title: Terrible. Very disappointed.
Text: First you have to pay 500 roupies after the visit is very short we can t drink ,no dégustation !we can t take picture or video !!it s a tourist trap !????

Title: Try another tea factory!
Text: The process of making tea was interesting although the tour felt rushed and no tea tasting after paying to get in. Try another tea factory.

Title: Tea tour
Text: We visited the factory after a visit to Liptons seat with our 2 children aged 10 and 11. We enjoyed the tour and found it very interesting to see the process of tea.

Title: Avarage
Text:
It was fine, they explained to us how the tea making starting from planting and going through all steps.
Since we paid for tickets we just hoped that they would offer us a cup of tea !

Title: A Tea Factory with a Unique History
Text:
On route to Lipton Seat. Always adviced to view this on the way back from Lipton Seat. The Building is built by Charles Lipton back in 1890s and it is still functional and standing.
The factory has been modernised over the years. Has producing tea to the SL market. There is an Entrance ticket. We were taken on a very informative tour by Mr. Nihal Palansuriya. Can buy tea from the factory as well.

Title: factory by Lipton seat
Text:
What kind of tea drinker wouldn't visit the very first Lipton factory of the island ?!
Tour is average in the sense that the guide will tell you his speech as learnt by heart and can not answer some specific questions.
Tea estate visit up to Lipton seat is great.
Overall a must do.

Title: The most Scenic Tea Factory
Text:
It was a great pleasure to visit this oldest tea factory built in 1890 by Sir Thomas Lipton. How scenic can be any tea plantation!!!! This factory will lead you to Lipton's Seat, another picturesque destination in Haputale, Sri Lanka. 
A must-visit tea factory in Sri Lanka, the 4th largest quality tea provider in the world.

Title: Great place to visit after liptons seat
Text: We went on the factory tour on our way down from Liptons Seat. It was very interesting to see a real working tea factory and the tour guide was very informative and happy to answer questions. You can buy loose leaf tea after for 350rupees per box or tea bags for around 1300 rupees per box.

Title: Interesting
Text: This was the first tea factory I toured.  I found it really interesting.  I had no idea how tea was made.  This factory only produces black tea.  We spent about 45 minutes touring and that was ample.

Title: Amazing
Text:
Fully operating tea factory. Great tour through each stage of the process. Clothes smelled of tea after visit! 

Must visit if checking out Lipton seat

Title: Interesting tour and very informative
Text: If you have an interest in how tea is made, this is a good basic tour. It's about 20 minutes long and it was very informative. The tour leader spoke excellent English. There wasn't a tasting after, which is a shame, and the tour was a bit hurried. However, I have a new appreciation for each cup I drink!

Title: I did NOT go to tea factory as there is NO tea tasting. Walk back to town, man.
Text: Again, I take the bus UPHILL (RS 28 now) to the Dambatenne Tea Factory & I walking sticked my way back DOWNHILL to Haputale. It takes about 4 hours, as I deliberately sauntered & moseyed back DOWNHILL to town. I woke up at dawn I was surprised how clear, for Haputale, it was but as the morning wore on it became mistier & foggier until I couldn't see 20 meters in front of me. IF you look at the photos you will see as the day goes on the foggier it gets.

Title: DO NOT BOTHER WITH THIS TEA FACTORY!
Text: After such an amazing drive to Liptons Seat I was really looking forward to visiting the tea factory and buying some tea to take back home.  How wrong was I!  There was NO shop to buy any tea let alone taste any tea!!  The staff were rude, rushed and VERY offhand!  Don't bother :)

Title: A very Nice one to visit after Lipton seat
Text: This is a very Nice factory and they gave a very good  explanation About  the process. Entrance is 250r. A pitty  they you can't taste the tea.

Title: Interesting Tour
Text: We stopped here on our walk down from Lipton's Seat. Unfortunately because of a public holiday the factory was not in operation but we were still able to do the tour. It was interesting to find out how the tea is processed from bush to dried leaf. The drying, the rolling and the cutting using machinery that looked as though it had been there since Lipton's time. It was a bit like visiting a museum rather than a working factory. Well worth a visit if you are in the area.

Title: Tea Industry at Work
Text: Interesting to see the production of tea from picking to packaging. Hard yakka put in by an industrious group.

Title: Average. There are better & they don't cost a penny.
Text: As a standalone visit this tea tour just about hit the average bar. Group size was quite large and engagement with guide was little. I visited at least 10 tea factories during this trip to Sri Lanka and although this wasn't the worst it was at best average, it was also one of the few I had to pay for so expectations were a little higher. You get the basics and it's a nice follow up after the walk to Lipton's Seat. I wouldn't go out of my way to visit specially and will not return. It's a whistle stop tour. Being a huge tea fan ( not Lipton's admittedly) I was hoping for a little more Q&A. They don't really have anything (machinery etc.) above that found in the other big black tea producing factories around Sri Lanka. The walk to Lipton's Seat (& view from top) is the pull to this area, it's marvellous.

Title: Not convincing
Text: We have  visited the factory when machines were working. With all the noise it was almost impossible to understand the explanations. Machines are very old which is not a problem, but the security and hygienic measures are inexistant. People and visitors walk right where the tea is produced and fermented (directly on the floor) without clean shoes or caps. That is maybe the reason why pictures are not allowed. I wouldn't drink tea produced here.

Title: Nice walk up to Lipton Seat
Text:
the walk up to Lipton Seat (and the view) through the tea plantation and the visit afterwards at the tea factory are really nice. You can easily take the regular bus from Haputale to the tea plantation, cost 25 lkr pp.
From the bottom of the tea plantation you can then take a tuktuk up to Lipton Seat, were you can walk the last part, from the barrier where you must pay the entrance fee (100 lkr pp)
Try doing this early morning before the mist sets in. But later in the day it is still worth your while.

Title: Holiday visit
Text: A little disappointed that on the day of our visit the factory was in shut down for maintenance. We did have a guided tour and it was interesting to see and learn about the technology introduced  in the late 1800's by Sit Thomas Lipton which still produces very high quality black teas. The guide was not always easy to understand and he did have problems developing rapport with the large group we were asked to join. We only  did one other tea factory tour and that was a relatively new green tea factory near Ella which we found more professional and engaging. OK to do especially if you continue to walk up to Liptons Seat. This was one of the highlights of our visit to Sri Lanka.

Title: Good to see inside, uninspiring tour guide
Text: The guide was pretty disappointing, very quietly spoken, and without much interest in questions or the tour. Seeing inside was pretty good, and we could figure out the process ourselves. He didn't have much interest in selling the tea at the end of the tour or any change!!

Title: Weak Tea Tour
Text: Only the sorting area of the factory was in operation. Our guide spoke very limited English. At the end of the tour, the guide offered tea for sale, but did not offer tea tasting. Friends on the tour before us had a totally opposite experience with a good English speaking guide who offered extensive tea tasting and expert Q&A. Public toilets were dirty with no running water.

Title: Not very usefulness.
Text:
Could learn how they make black tea and white tea. No more. 
I hope they prefer have a good shop for sell to visiter. Price is 250Rs per person, and children are free.

Title: Educational
Text: Fascinating tour of victorian tea factory still using original equipment. Very active factory rather than a tourist trap. Well worth a visit.

Title: Needs a Trained Guide
Text:
We arrived at the Tea Factory after visiting the Lipton Seat summit. Admittedly, it was the day after a major festival, so no tea had been picked the day prior, meaning the most of the machinery wasn't operating. Anyway, because we were already pre booked, a man took us on a tour of the factory. Maybe it's not his usual job and he was filling in for someone else, but it seemed our guide didn't really want to be there. No photos were allowed inside the production area, so that there was no evidence of OHS laws being broken I guess! 
The factory itself looked really old, with heaps of character. We got to feel how heavy the bags of leaves are (approx 9kgs) and see how they are sorted and dried etc. Later we tasted a couple of grades of tea & made some purchases. With the right guide and a bit of theatre, this could've been a very interesting tour.

Title: Fascinating to see how tea is made
Text:
We visited as part of our stay at the Thotalagala hotel. Being avid tea drinkers it was fascinating to see the process of how tea is made from beginning to end and we couldn't help but buy some before we left.

The tour doesn't take long so even if you're someone who doesn't like to go on tours of things (my attention span often isn't the longest) this one is worth doing. 

The only slight downside was the beginning started at the top of the factory where it is very noisy, so we struggled to hear everything we were being told initially. 

Overall, given Sri Lanka's famed tea production, we're glad we visited but will be sad when the tea we purchased at the end of the tour runs out, as it is delicious!

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Shopping experience
Text: Lovely excursion but bought 100gms of tea for £35. The price was in Sri Lanka Tupperware so was confused but think the cost of the tea was excessive

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Excellent tea room
Text: Lovely stop off to Nuwara Eliya with excellent tea service and the opportunity to buy tea gifts. Well worth visiting

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Loved this place
Text:
Found this was more enjoyable than I thought. The factory tour was really interesting to see the processes. Our guide was so lovely and very informative. Were from England so love tea and this was the best we ever tasted!
We know now all the stuff at home is blended but the single origin premium quality they produce is so good. 
Definitely recommend this place and the tea they sell there is reasonably priced so we bought some to bring home

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea amazing taste and beautiful
Text:
Stopped her for overview of tea making process which began here 1928 by James Taylor didnt realize everything picked by hand by imported Indian people 
The tea tasted amazing much better than what we get in the states and the air around plantations smell of tea

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Don't miss the tea factory tour
Text: We enjoyed our factory tour and tea tasting very much. Our guide was delightful, and the surrounding scenery was gorgeous. There is a large shop where you can purchase tea in various containers but no pressure to buy. Tour is free although we tipped our guide generously.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Worth a visit
Text: Very interesting and a very knowledgeable guide. We loved hearing and seeing the process followed by nice cup of tea in the guest room. Even the shop is very well priced and it even makes the royal familys personal tea.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Great Tour!
Text: We visited Damro as it was recommended by our driver and it was a great tour, incredibly informative! We were driven into the plantation, where there are some wonderful viewpoints and picture opportunities and then got to pick tea ourselves, with our guide also explaining which leaves were used for what tea. Afterwards a lovely employee showed us around the factory, whilst quite a brief tour it was informative and interesting and she was very nice! We were served some tea to try for free and I also had the tea cake (400 lkr = 1.10$) which was very nice!

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Waste of time, they don't care and won't tell you anything
Text:
I don't know, what happend to the place, but it was ABSOLUTE waste of time.. A company guide rushed a group of us through the factory (like 5' tour)

Then we were shown the area where all different teas were available for sale.

I asked the guide nicely, if we can get some more information and even see the plantation and other staff, she told us they are busy, but she can give us the tour again, we saw they are not busy, so we told her, we can see they are not busy, so she told us it is not safe to go to the field, it was raining and it's not safe (it was not raining for a week).

So we got the feeling they don't care about anything else then sales, so we left very dissapointed. It's not worth of visit at all!

There is a large decking viewing area at this establishment..
Where you can look at the rows of tea bushes, under it you will find the poor locals, begging for you to throw a few notes over the handrail of the decking.

You only find out information once you actually leave and the guide explains more.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Well organised tour
Text: Well organised tour. We were picked up from our hotel and driven to the factory for the tour. The tour was really interesting and enjoyable. Highly recommended

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Beautiful tea plantation
Text:
Stopped here on our tour.
I have to say this was an exceptional tour with a very knowledgeable guide.
Very informative.
We have visited tea plantations in India, Kerala, China and Nepal and I have to say this was by far the best experience 
The staff in the shop were very helpful. Purchased some beautiful teas at a very good price.
Would highly recommend stopping off here.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Quality single estate tea from Damro, Labookellie, Sri Lanka.
Text:
For centuries known as Mackwood Labookellie Tea Estate, the name of the tea estate has been changed to Damro Tea Estate recently on transfer of the estate to the Damro business group.

The showroom is located in situ at Labookellie Tea Estate right on the main road from Kandy to Newerelia.

The huge bill boards near the entrance are helpful to easily  locate the show room.

The showroom has been extensively renovated with ample parking space and comfortable seating area.

The top quality of the original Mackwood Labookellie Tea Estate is still maintained.

The visitors are given free tea tasting of the single estate tea from the estate.

The quality of tea is very good and the prices are quite reasonable.

Visitors from India can consider taking many packets of Indian sweets like Son Papdi which is in huge demand by the sales executives at the showroom.

The sales executives are polite, smiling and neatly dressed in traditional Sri Lankan attire.

Highly recommended for the conoseuers of authentic single estate Sri Lankan tea.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Pleasant even in the rain
Text: Stopped for a tour and to b sold local tea, but it was a pleasant stop. There was a short interesting tour of the factory and then a tea tasting. Unfortunately we were only offered English Breakfast Tea when there was an opportunity to sample some of the more exotic teas on sale.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Informative tour but very busy.
Text: Our driver chose this particular tea factory to visit, this was the only one we had time to visit so have nothing to compare it with in regards to having a better experience elsewhere.  We went on a Sunday which is the only day of the week where the factory is not running so you dont get to see any of the processes or ladies out in the plantations picking tea.  The tour through the factory was very informative but somewhat rushed and difficult to hear as this is a very popular tour spot, so other groups are hot on your heels as you make your way around the factory.  The tour is free and you are given a complimentary cup of tea on completion, your guide will also try and upsell you in to purchasing an overpriced piece of cake to go with your cuppa.  You are not pressured into purchasing tea however if you wish to buy tea the shop was extremely busy and understaffed so hard to get any info on any tea that you want to purchase as well as pricing.  We did find out why our driver took us to visit this particular factory as we noticed as soon as we purchased he disappeared and came back with his free packet of tea. The outlook of all the tea plants for as far as the eye could see was stunning and we did gain useful info regarding the process from the tour, would have preferred to visit when the factory was working.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Insightful and Pleasant
Text: We visited on a Saturday morning and the drive from Nuwara Eliya to Damro is not far but the views was absolutely breathtaking as it was a clear morning and seeing the people working in the plantations was an amazing sight. At the tea factory we were taken on a tour by a very knowledgeable guide and we truly enjoyed it and learned a lot. We then had a very nice cup of tea to finish off the tour. They do offer tours (safari) into the tea plantations but we did not do that. Would recommend a visit. We did find the shop a bit expensive.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: " a sales push exercise. "
Text:
Having visited this establishment on a Sunday...
( CLOSED...), which the guide we used didn't know..

ABSOLUTE waste of time..
A company guide literally rushed a group of us through the factory..
It was empty of employees, and so we saw nothing of how the process works...
It took no more than 10mins to go through to the area where we Began the tour..
Then we were shown the the area where all different teas were available for sale..
So for me it's purely a 'sales push..'
Total waste of time in my opinion 
There is a large decking viewing area at this establishment..
Where you can look at the rows of tea bushes..
Under this decking you will find the very very poor locals, who have no income or jobs..
Begging for you to throw a few notes over the handrail of the decking..

The tea pluckers earn around 2,000 rupees per day.( aprox £5.)
They have to pluck 20kgs per day for that pay..
So sad ..

Would never return..
You only find out information once you actually leave and the guide explains more...

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Authentic tea experience - a great stop off to Ella
Text:
Learnt so much about how different types of tea are manufactured. 
Guide was brilliant and extremely knowledgable, answering all of the questions we had about the process at the plantation. 
Tour lasted about 30 minutes, showing the different processes that the tea passed through, followed by a nice cup of black tea in the café. 
We bought a few different types of tea that are produced by Damro - definitely worth trying! 
Highly recommend if you have an hour on the route from Kandy to Ella.
