Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: It is the best tea factory ever
Text:
My favourite part was the tour and how they really explained it 

Tips for future Travellers get the tea cake and the chocolate cake it is amazing the tea is absolutely awesome ??

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea for Two Or Twenty-Two
Text:
Lovely place to visit, especially if you are a tea afficinato!
Many varieties of tea on display and for your putchase.  Frankly I found the tea prices quite high and overpriced....not sure why Silver and Golden tips were about $40 USD for a small box!!!

Staff on site to answer questions and help you select our purchase.

There is also an indoor and outdoor tea garden.  You are served 1 cup of black tea each person for free and can additionally ourchase a slice of chocolate cake to go along with your tea.  It was an ideal and pleasant experience.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Worth a short visit
Text: There is no charge for the short 15 minute very professional description of the tea harvesting and factory processes while walking through the factory. For safety reasons, unlike some where you walk past moving machinery, this was conducted on walkways behind glazed views. And then into the tea rooms for a complimentary cup, very pleasant. Perhaps the whole structure and operation is a little too modern and clinically presented for some, and while there are hills of tea bushes around the factory and a modern tea room they are not the most photogenic.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea Factory Tour
Text:
After a drive up the steep mountain road, there is plenty of parking at the factory tour. 
Welcome with sanitation station and then around the factory & building with our personal tour guide. 
At the end of tour a big seating area inside or outside, where tea is provided and cake of course! 
Well worth a visit

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: A welcom cup of tea
Text: We were driving from Peradeniya to Nuwara Eliya and our driver guide suggested we stop at the Damo Tea Centre for a break and a cup of tea. In the prevailing damp weather, it was a good idea and the cup of tea was very welcome. It was also our first glimpse of the return of some tourism to the country.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: BAD experience! Unprofessional in their service. Saving grace is the security guy that shelters you from our car!
Text:
Damro Tea Plantation

BAD Experience! Too touristy and staff are not interested and not personal. Biggest regret as Sri Lanka are filled with many nice places and people. Damro staff are more interested in selling than service. In Dec 2019 before the onset of Covid19, I was personally guided around the tea plantation by a fair local girl that gave me the impression very blankly that she did NOT want to be there at all. I asked for permission to take picture of the tea process and accidentally had a picture of her looking nonchalant and sulky inside my picture! A picture paints a thousand word! have since submitted my feedback to my travel agent who checks in on my mum and I everyday. This same girls face only lighted up very slightly when my mum and I started purchasing many teas. Another incident that disappoints me was the complimentary black tea which we declined as it was already mid afternoon and we were afraid that the caffeine will affect our sleep when we arrive at Nuwara Eliya. Thus we requested for chamomile or peppermint tea that they said coat Sri Lankan Rupees 700  (USD3.80) which was not expensive but the tea arrived COLD! This is an abomination to a lovely country that prides itself as a top tea country! It was a rainy day in the hills and that was the last thing my poor old mum needed. Very disappointed with the entire experience! I would avoid all the touristy restaurants with big tour buses as we were on a private tour as the guide will have a tendency to bring the tourists there for reasons we all know why... so do your homework and have your travel agent give you a detailed itinery as to where to eat etc..we had a wonderful travel agent and I shall visit Sri Lanka again just NEVER to return to DAMRO!

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea plantation
Text: This is a tea plantation with great views onto the hills at Nuwara Eliya. On arrival, you'll be offered a pot of tea for free, and you can buy a slice of rather nice cake to accompany it. After that, you'll be shown around the factory floors where you can see the process of grading, drying and conditioning the tea leaves. It's a short tour, perhaps 20 minutes, but very interesting. After the tour, you can browse in the shop if you wish to buy any of the products. Very good.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Out Tea Plantation Excursion
Text:
This was on our schedules list of places to visit in SL. Very interesting to see how the tea is picked and prepared in the factory. Great experience to see the manufacture of tea.
The tasting at the end was great as there were many different teas to taste.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: It is only trying to sell expensive tea as a souvenir.
Text:
You get a brief insight into tea production. All of this is kept fairly simple. Then you can try a tea and will then be brought directly to the shop.
We can recommend the buffet and the beautiful view. Otherwise we were disappointed.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Really lovely tasting tea.
Text: Tour was not long but very informative. Beautiful views from the car park. Bought a lot of tea but beware the White tea is very expensive. I asked the price of several boxes and they were no more than 790 rupees. When I got to the till I discovered the Gold white tea was 8500 rupees. Bought it anyway but just so people know there is a big difference in the price of some of the tea. Now back home and it all tastes amazing- drinking the ginger tea just now and it is beautiful. Well worth the money.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Excellent tour & Lovely Tea
Text:
We had a very informative tour - unfortunately it was on a Monday morning, so there was not much going on in the Factory as the pickers did not work on the Sunday. The guides are all provided by the factory, so are very knowledgable

The tea lounge serves an excellent cup of tea (as you would expect) and the cake is scrummy and very reasonably priced. 

Well worth a visit

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Stopped off here on our way to Nuwara Eliy, even though I do not drink tea, the tour was informative of all the processess needed to make tea. Had a cup of tea and slice of cake delicious

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Well worth it!
Text: Really beautiful setting and modern building. The staff are super friendly and well organised. We had a great tour guide who was very knowledgable and happy to answer all our questions. After the tour we got to sit down and relax and drink delicious complimentary tea and yummy cake (at a very good price). We would highly recommend this place!! (We also went to Pedro, and Damro is 100 times better)

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Excellent tour
Text: Really enjoyed the tour and tea at Damro. Our guide was very helpful in explaining the many steps involved in making tea. After the tour, we were treated with some quality tea and delicious cake. The estate itself is very scenic and has some walking trails.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Much better than Pedro Estates, complimentary guided tour.
Text:
We left Nuwara Eliya after having breakfast at our hotel. After 30 minutes of driving towards Kandy, we arrived at Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea garden.

The tea factory here is actually running and the management offers complimentary 15 minute guided tour around the factory. We learned about various stages of processing of tea as well as about different varieties of tea. Finally we were treated with a variety of fine Ceylon tea. We ended up buying a good amount of tea from the gift shop to take for folks back home.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea and cake
Text: Beautiful place with a Nice view. You Get the feeling they have done the tour a lot of times and they rushed it a little. After the tour you Get some tea and a cake Which were Nice. Have nothing bad to say about the place, just Didnt find it very interesting.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea lover? You'll adore this!
Text:
I love tea, so the opportunity to see how the leaves are picked, dried and packaged was genuinely wonderful.

Great views, an informative and friendly tour followed by the opportunity to drink and buy the product was perfect for this tea addict. 

Highly recommended.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Nice Tour and Even Better Tea
Text:
We visited this tea centre as part of a G Adventures tour.  The first part of the visit consists of a tour of their factory to show us how the tea is produced.  This was very interesting with a lot of the equipment in the factory being last century equipment.  Before we went into the center, we saw the older ladies that pick the tea leaves.  Apparently, Sri Lanka has lost tea market share in the world as younger people do not wish to pick tea leaves as it doesn't pay well.  

After the tour, we had a cup of Orange Pekoe tea which I greatly enjoyed (even more than the tour).  I also bought a piece of chocolate cake which I also enjoyed.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Nice tea, views and tours
Text: Great place if you want to see how tea is made. You get a free tour and free tea sample. Very nice staff and tasty tea. The views make for some good photos too.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Good place for tea Tasting
Text: This place had a good selection of teas for tasting. I had a good experience with the different teas. The unfortunate part of my stop over at this place was the service by staff manning the tea tasting. Service was non existent.  I would even venture to state that there is a preference for Caucasians. I tried several times to attract the attention of the staff as it would have been nice to get some explanation on the teas. Well I agree with Simroch...Too busy to care and that too with the Caucasian visitors. Well if non for the opportunity to sample the teas and the wonderful Chocolate and tea cakes I would have rated this place as Poor.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Now we know where our tea comes from
Text:
The tea factory is well worth a visit .The processes are not particularly complicated but interesting to see,The guide speaks excellent English and there is a tea break at the end.
TOP TIP: Do check the infrequent festival dates (eg Jan) as the factory is closed or open but not running on those dates

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Excellent tour and tea
Text: Great informative tour to learn about the tea processes. Lovely views of the plantation and the tea picking ladies and a great taste of the tea after with an option of cake.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Too busy to care
Text: The place was absolutely crowded so the staff rushed people to try and get through the number of people that were there. They joined two tour groups together and then rushed through the tour. The tour guide had excellent English and she ended it by seating us at a table and asking if we wanted a cup of tea and piece of cake (the cake would cost extra) and pointing out the shop. When we went to the shop and asked to taste the tea, we were pointed to the tea tasting area. Apparently this should all have been explained during the tour. However, she was too busy trying to rush through the tour to bother. With so any tea plantations in the area, choose a smaller one which will give more personalised service.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Excellent
Text: Amazing tea garden nice view and good quality natural tea good testy good staff everything perfect..

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Wonderful
Text: We had a lovely guide called Shiroma, she was lovely and had great English. We enjoyed the tea and cake afterwards

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Less informative and more of sales promotion
Text: Located near Nuwara eliya, damro is a national tea brand that makes a lot of variations of tea. This one is located amongst the tea estates and offers a great view of the valley. The staff takes you for a guided tour of the tea estate which hardly runs for 10 minutes and then offer you a complimentary cup of tea. The focus here is on selling lose tea and tea bags which are highly priced. Overall a good place if you have never visited tea estate of plantation. They also have a  cafe where you can have some good stuff though priced heavily.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Very informative
Text:
We very much appreciated the very informative factory tour, led by our knowledgeable guide, Bosco.

Developed a much better understanding of tea production and varieties.

The tea room and shop are also excellent. Prices are reasonable for the high end products.

Picturesque setting for one of Sri Lankas largest tea estates, with glorious views of the hills and valleys it occupies.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Beautiful spot for a cuppa
Text: We really enjoyed the tour of the factory and tasting the tea.  The smell inside the factory is lovely!  Also enjoyed the beautiful views and purchased several boxes of tea.  We didn't stop at any other factories but we thoroughly enjoyed Damro.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Interesting
Text: Never knew there were soo many varieties of tea. Was nice to see inside a working tea factory. The complimentary tea at the end was nice too. Shop is a little pricey though.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Pleasant and Informative
Text: If you want to visit a tea factory, this one has it all. Clean restrooms, informative tour, tea room and ability to buy great teas.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: My Tour of Srilanka (Dec 2019)
Text: Nice place.  We were take tour of the tea manufacturing life cycle.  Followed by tea.  Amazing place.  We purchased ginger tea which was really good compared to what I had earlier.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Educational visit with a complimentary tea to finish
Text:
The tour of the factory and walk through of tea making and distribution process was fascinating, but it was anticlimactic to see that their smallest box of white tea starts at £65!!
Better off looking elsewhere for your purchases, but would recommend for the tour and photo taking opportunity of the vast plantations!

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Nice tour
Text: The factory tour was informative and the sample tea was good, but the even if it's a tasty tea is still very pricey. Mostly because drivers take the tourists there and they get gifts depending on how much the torurists spend.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Damro Tea
Text: Nice  views  on hillside  they have  a  free  entrance  and  the  host  welcome you  with a  big  smile. Worth visiting but if  you have  already taken a  tea  factory  tour  I wont recommend  that.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Breathing views/So-so Tour
Text: Arriving at the end of the day, my tour felt rushed. No samples of the high end tea were available. I opted not to buy tea. Found better deals elsewhere.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Loved the Cakes here
Text: On our way to Nuwara Eliya we stopped at the Damro Tea Factory. As u enter, u r approached with a warm smile. One staff member takes u around d factory explaining every process of tea manufacturing. Damro Tea is one of the most popular brands. All through our road journey we could only see their tea estates. After the factory tour is done. U can chill at their cafe area. Tea is on d house. But dont forget to try their Tea cake and Chocolate Cake. Both were too delicious. And quite reasonable. We saw lotbof foreigners buying bags full of tea. Overall a good visit

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Over priced tea factory
Text:
Damro Tea plantation has a big tea estate that caters to local and export needs.  We had a brief 20 minutes tour of the factory.  Picking of the tea leaves is once a week.

The picked leaves are placed in huge belts to dry where huge air blowers blow air to aid in the drying process.  This takes about 14 hours of drying. It takes 5 kg fresh leaves to make 1 kg of black tea.

Once the leaves are dried they are sent down to the machine where it's rolled and cut as per the requirements.  Then they are placed on the table for fermentation where the process of oxidation changes the colour of the tea leaves. No fermentation for green and white tear.  Then the leaves are sent to the Dryer machine to stop fermentation to turn to black colour.  After this they are sent to the Grading machine for different quality of grading - strong, medium, light.  The tour ends with complimentary light black tea.

For the huge acres of tea estate and the fact that it's a factory the rates should've been cheaper than the markets. Was very surprised to see such expensive rates.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Free tour, free tea!
Text: Entrance is free, they give free tours of the factory which also includes tea at end. The tour was very informative and interesting, you'll learn about the tea making process of white tea, oolong tea, green tea, and black tea. The view from the factory overlooks the tea plantations.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea, tea and more tea! With some breath-taking views!
Text:
This is a lovely set up. Earlier this was the Mackwoods Tea Factory, but now it seems that the owners have changed and the entire place has seen an upgrade.
Once you arrive, you have the option of going in for a free tour of the factory (15 minutes approx) where you will learn how tea is made. The guide patiently briefs you about the most important details of the tea making business and in the end show the different varieties of tea as well. You can taste the tea as well.
Once the tour is over, you are welcomed into the tea lounge, where you can drink unlimited cups of tea as you want. Whilst the tea and sugar are provided, there is a minimal charge if you want milk. They also sell chocolate and tea cakes, both simply done and lovely. 
The views are SPECTACULAR, no other word can describe it. They have a nice viewing platform that doubles up for outdoor seating (if the weather permits and its not raining) and the experience is very nice and pleasant.
Overall, very enjoyable and relaxing, and a special mention to the friendly, respectful staff that are hired there.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: A must stop in Nuwera Eliya
Text: This was our first time to see a tea factory. Max 45 min you can finish the free guided tour and then have free cup of tea. I recommend you buy hot tea cake for 1 usd. Very nice. They have excellent tea shop, a restaurant and clean toilets. Staff are efficient. The best place to take tea plantation pictures.  A MUST STOP

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: delicious sri lanka tea
Text:
Its just beside the kandy nuwaraeliya road. One of a best place to taste and buy god sri lanken tea.
Price for a tea for sri lanken is 80 with milk. i always buy tea from here to home. Very big tea shop also for foriegners.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Damro tea lounge
Text: Excellent tea tour, very informative. Great to sample tea after the tour. Asked for High tea which started at 3pm until 5pm - waited for half hour to start only to then be be told there would be a 45 min wait. Left a little disappointed.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Good experience of tea factory
Text: We took a tour around the tea factory, good guide and lots of information given, great cup of tea and a must in Nuwara Eliya

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: A must!!
Text: Best Tea Factory by far, the fee tour and tea tasting was amazing. Set in a perfect location! Definitely order the cake with your tea at the end!!! Amazing!!

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: A god place to learn about tea in Sri Lanka
Text: Enjoyed visiting this tea factory and had a very informative tour of the tea processing sytem and sampled some excellent teas.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Great Tea
Text: I had a tour of the tea centre which was interesting, then had tea and cake.  The tea was really good.  Good range of teas to purchase.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea quality very low especially the best available Golden Tips
Text:
Being tea lover, thought of buying some best tea from a very big tea estate and as promoted by them, I bought both Golden tips and Silver Tips tea.
There is no aroma in it and though looks good but taste is not there. So without flavour and aroma, I don't see anything special in their best of the best teas.

For people visiting first time in tea estate, will be good experience but suggest not to buy expensive teas from here

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Good location in the heart of the tea country
Text:
This appears to be a purpose built tourist attraction, but never the less is worth a visit. Pickers work on the tea terraces around the location and the tea making process is well demonstrated within a "mini" factory environment.

Tea is served free of charge after the tour, a cake is available at a very small charge. There is a gift shop selling tea, but you are perfectly free to exit the facility without visiting the shop, which is on the opposite side of the building from the exit.

Our tour guide spoke excellent English and was very knowledgeable when asked questions. We definitely learned something about the different kinds and grades of tea.

It is what it is, 

It is what it is, but if you want to know how tea is made, then this a free attraction worth visiting.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: An informative and nice experience to do
Text: As we wanted to visit a tea plantation, our driver suggested we stop off here en route from Nuwara Eliya to Kandy. On arrival, we were met by one of the guides who took us for a tour of the tea factory and explained to us the process of how tea is produced and ends up in our cups. As my husband and I are key tea drinkers, we found it very informative to listen and see the process happen. At the end of the tour, we enjoyed a cup of Damro tea and bought our favourites from the shop; a nice take home for us and the family.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Average with pathetic customer service
Text: We liked the scenery of tea gardens, but the thing which ruined our visit was the tour of the tea factory, the lady was explaining things in a way as she was doing on a gunpoint, we feel she was tired or bored of repeating the same information to people again and again. We had a bad experience at their tea shop too, my wife was very excited and picked every type of tea available at the shop as we are living in the Middle East and are quite fond of tea, but the attendants at shop were not willing to answer our few questions as they were more interested in tourists with white skins even they weren't buying a fraction of stuff which my wife and I was holding , we tried last time at the payment counter to ask again but the lady at payment counter was also busy with our european ,American friends, finally due to of this continuous neglection in anger my wife dumped all of her stuff at the counter and left without buying anything.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Beautiful view and amazing tea factory
Text: Very traditional tea factory with amazing view over the tea gardens. Tea we bought is excellent quality, prices are not low but worth the quality. Only remark is that the tasting area was not refreshed so we couldn't really taste for choosing the tea we preferred, we bought by type instead.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: nice experience
Text: A nice experience at one of the biggest tea plantations and factories in Sri Lanka. We saw all the tea process and how it`s made and we tasted a very good tea and eat a delicious chicolate cake.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Good way to learn about tea
Text:
This is a working tea factory, which offers free tours of how they manufacture the variety of teas - and it's worth the 20-30 minutes it takes. 

The Damro factory is buzzing with tour groups and families delivered by tuk-tuks and taxis. The tour through the factory is interesting, and you can learn a lot about the process. You get a cup of tea at the end (you don't choose which type), and you'll be offered a slice of chocolate cake to go with it. The tea is free, the cake isn't. They won't divulge that until later. 

It seems pretty likely that tuk tuk and taxi drivers get commissions from the tea shop inside, since the drivers strongly encourage you to buy some tea before you leave. And they hang out in the store to make sure you get that purchase through.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Shrouded in Mystery
Text:
Damro was the first tea factory we visited in Sri Lanka. It was recommended by several tuktuk drivers and our homestay host. 

The tour was complimentary and lasted about 20 minutes, as we walked through the factory. We visited on New Year so there were no leaves being blow-dried. Our guide looked tired and recited off a script. She did nonetheless entertain our pesky questions well. After the tour we got to taste a cup each of FF1 tea in the lounge, but sadly we werent particularly impressed. Strangely, there wasnt the option to try other types of tea - we would have wanted to try the loose leaf types like OP and BOP which we later discovered were more to our liking. We were, funnily enough, allowed to buy cakes, which admittedly were cheap and decent. Ultimately, as we had liked our hosts tea, which was from damro, we proceeded to make the mistake of buying too much tea on our first stop.

It was only after visiting the Mackwoods museum in Nuwara Eliyas city centre that we found out more about the history of Damro - it was a furniture company that had just (as of 2016) ventured into the plantation business, acquiring great swathes of land, including the Labookellie tea lounge, and a significant stake in the Mackwoods brand (the second oldest tea company after the parent company of Lipton). 

Make what you will of our experience - we still cant figure out if we are happy with our purchases 4 days later. But the experience as a whole was somewhat uncanny. The price of tea in the gift shop we found to be average - higher than the Zesta / Lipton types in supermarkets but lower than most single-estate tea companies we visited elsewhere in Sri Lanka. Our advice would be to stay off the teabags (which we tasted and found to be quite ordinary) and stick to the loose leaf teas.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Interesting
Text:
This is a free and basic tour of a tea factory with a free cup of tea afterwards.

It's great Damro does this. I learnt a lot about the tea process.

It will take 30 minutes.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Worth the trip!
Text: Would definitely recommend the free tour if youre in the area. The cup of tea afterwards is a lovely treat and we also enjoyed some cake from the cafe! Lovely shop too.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Nice place for short break
Text: Nice place to have a cup of tea (complimentary) and cake. You can buy good quality tea. Fantastic view.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Oasis in a tea garden
Text: The place on the way to Nuwara elliya is a perfect stop over for a nice complimentary tea with a visit to factory as well. The place provides good photo shoot location amidst the tea garden surroundings. A must visit.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Highly Recommend
Text: We visited Damro Teas as part of our tour with Dinesh from the wonderful D S Tours (see seperate  review).  We had a guided tour of the factory from Siroma which was very informative.  Afterwards we opted for a vehicle tour of the tea plantation (extra cost).  We are so glad we did, we had numerous photo opportunities with the driver taking many photos of us??.  We also got you meet some of the lady tea pickers who were lovely.  Thank you to all staff involved in our factory tour and plantation tour.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Informative and attractive
Text: We enjoyed our visit to this tea plantation. We had personalised service of a guide who showed us around and explained the process well. He also answered the hundreds of questions in a friendly manner and had a nice sense of humour. We drank complimentary tea and had cake (purchased) and was attended by friendly waiters and shop staff. The view was lovely. Worth a visit

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Lovely place
Text: We had a tour first. Then we some tea. It was free. Piece of cake was less than a euro. Good cake, really nice Tea.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Taste Ceylon Tea
Text:
beautiful tea plantation and offered free pure Ceylon 
Tea. option to buy in different flavors. Thank you

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Amazing place
Text: We have visited this while we were heading from colombo to nuwara eliya.. view is simply  awesome and amazing... worth a visit

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: An interesting visit on the way to Kandy
Text: The plantation offers a free pot of tea and you can buy some cakes and enjoy the wonderful views. A quick tour through the factory was interesting and we purchased some tea (at about 750Rps which is not that different to the UK, but it is single source).  There was an  option of a drive through the plantation (which we did not do). Some fantastic scenery on the drive to the plantation too.  Well worth a visit.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: STOP....
Text:
..here. Easy access off the main highway. Its a walk-in operation. You are meet at the door by one of the hostesses.  She walks you through the process and through a tight security viewing areas. Very good English. At the end there is a short presentation on the varieties of tea. Ending with a free cup of tea ..cake costs. ... and a gift shop...(why not?)
The price is right and it is worth it for the education.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: PROFESSIONAL TOUR
Text: It was fascinating seeing the tea making process from plucking to pot. I must admit sadness learning pluckers are $AUD5 daily and white tea sells for $AUD125 for 50 grams.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea Plantation for Two (or more)
Text: Interesting place and you are in Sri Lanka so you have to go to a tea plantation. A working plantation and 24 hour factory with a visitors centre set up for tourists. The whole thing is well done but of course the gift shop is more expensive than in the town. You can also do a 4 wheel drive tour which we did not do but according to people staying at our accommodation it was well worth it.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea plantation visit
Text: Demonstration of tea processing very interesting. Tea and chocolate cake to follow was a nice way to end our visit.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Interesting place!
Text:
Here you can know a bit about tea, how they make them. They have also some activities like tea garden safari.

You will get a free tea and a very small tea factory tour when you visit the place. here you can find good quality tea but is bit pricey as it is a tourist center.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Good for a visit but avoid buying the tea leaves
Text:
A short tour around the factory and tea will be served free of charge in the lobby. Cake can be purchased with your tea.

Tea leaves cost more than double of what you could find in nuwara eliya. I guess the tuk tuk and taxi drivers get a good cut from your purchase.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Great tour and tea experience
Text:
Stopped in for our last tea factory visit and was pleasantly surprised. The tour is brief but they allow you to take photos which most of the other plantations do not. The fields are lovely and the setting is pretty. 

The cursory offering of a fine cup of tea ends the tour and the shop is there for you to purchase, without too much pressure. 

Try to arrive earlier in the morning to avoid any tourist masses that come by bus or van.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Inside the tea factory
Text: It was great to see the inside of a tea factory and learn about the process of tea making. Unfortunately we arrived on. asunder so much of the factory was not in action. I would have liked to have learnt some more about the history of tea in Sri Lanka though. A nice experience having tea and cake at the end of the tour.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Everyone's cup of tea?
Text:
This is one of several factories owned by Damro Labookellie and the largest. However, it's still not a huge operation and the walk-through therefore does not take a lot of time - about 30 minutes gets it done. You peer at the operations through glas walls.

Nevertheless, i learned quite a bit about tea. The Twining's Orange Pekoe I drink is a milder form of English breakfast black tea etc. This tea factory sends its product to the merchants in Colombo for distribution and export. The capital is also where flavours, such as peppermint are added. The factory does not do any of the flavouring that is the basis for all the options we see in our supermarkets.

Of course, the tour inevitably stops in the shop, which is the only place in which you can buy Damro Labookellie tea under its own label. Of course, we bought samples - BOP and BOPF. It's all orange pekoe, but of different strengths. I won't do all the work for you, so check out what these letters mean. It will put you ahead of the game before you visit this attraction.

Location_Name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
Title: Tea Plantation, tea factory and tea Tasting
Text:
This is a very nice stop in Sri Lanka, which produces the highest quality tea in the world. Firt you can admire the tea plantation, its beautiful and amazing for good pictures. Then tehre is a tour thrgouh the factoory, where they explain every step of the tea production. Very interesting, I did not know that the green tea and the blacj tea come from the same plant. And finally,, you can try a a tea and cake. The tea cake is delicious!
please follow us at @mapamunditravel , and if you find it helpful,please give me a vote! Thanks in advance =)

Title: Disappointing
Text: Lovely spot, but it might depend which guide you get at this place. Mine was smiley and pleasant but rushed me through the tea factory, hardly explained anything, had no opportunity to pick tea, and was overly eager to "help" me purchase tea in the shop. I had to speak quite firmly to her to get her to back off. Also, why doesn't anyone mention the tea pickers themselves? They are the backbone of the industry, as I understand it. Generally low income Tamil women. The guide acted as though they didn't exist and failed to point out the tip box in the factory for the pickers. But she was certainly angling for her own tip. I'd try another place next time.

Title: GLENLOCH EXPERIENCE
Text:
We had an amazing stay in GLENLOCH we book online and they provided a very nice accommodation, very clean and the staff was super kind. The tea experience and factory was a pleasant experience thanks to Shiva that explained us every single step. We bought some tea directly from their shop and I can not wait to taste it. We will be back for sure.
Thank you guys for this experience Ill hope to be back soon.

Title: The better of the plantations and factories to visit.
Text:
This plantation and factory is worth visiting. It is not overly commercial and still has much of the original machinery.  As an avid tea drinker I learnt a lot, especially about tea dust. 

The ladies who looked after us were warm, friendly and a little wicked, in a nice way. 

A tip: there is no picking on Sunday thus the machinery does not operate on Monday. That is when the factory is cleaned.

Title: Very Interesting visit
Text: Very interesting visit .  We were welcomed and shown around by Sasi .  She told us about the history of the tea factory and plantation .  She also informed us of the different types of tea and process of making and plucking  the tea too.  Before trying the differing types.  A good experience

Title: Fantastic tour with excellent guide
Text:
Second Tea Factory visit and arguably the better one, our guide was superb, very informative, showed us all around and explained very well the different processes.
We sampled the different teas in their tea shop and purchased some of the blends to take home. We were also put to work picking tea on their plantation which was an experience - Im not very good!

Title: Shiwa is a best guide!
Text: Nice tea factory. We came in the evening, stayed in a hotel right on the factory. In the morning right after breakfast we had very interesting excursion on factory and tea plants with guide Shiwa. She told us a story about a factory, tea history, showed us all the technological process of tea factoring, explained a difference between white, green and black tea, all the black tea types and qualities and many other interesting things about tea, people, who produce it, about Sri-Lanka and  all around.

Title: Tea for two
Text: Lovely tour guide Gung and smashing teas to taste afterwards. And a very beautiful setting. Definitely worth stopping by.

Title: Amazing tour with Divya
Text:
A must stop on the way to Ella. 

The tour is completely free, with samples of tea at the end. 

We had the amazing Divya give us the tour. Her English was impeccable and she was so knowledgeable, having worked there for 10 years! 

Their tea is so delicious, we couldn't resist buying some in the lovely shop at the end.

Title: Delicious teas
Text: We received a fun tour at the tea plantation where we picked some tea and saw how it was processed in the factory. Afterwards we had a sampling of the various tea blends. They have a nice tea shop where you can buy the Tea that you liked.

Title: Best brightest flavour- love it
Text:
I dear friend visited Sri Lanka and brought back a tin of Glenloch orange pekoe
Best brightest flavourI have found in a lifetime of tea sampling

Title: Lovely tea tour
Text: A short but informative trip round this small tea factory. Some of the machinery processing the tea was very old (not operational when we visited) An opportunity to learn about the variety of teas and how they are produced. A good taster session. We bought a load and I am still enjoying it. Many thanks.

Title: How tea is made
Text: An informative visit to a tea factory which explained the production process from picking to the tea cup. Informative but short. You do get a pleasant cup of tea however at the end.

Title: Relatively Pleasant Experience...
Text: We had bad experience at Store Field Tea Factory with pushy sales girl and guide who spoke like bullet train speed. Comparatively, the experience here was relatively better. Guide spoke with reasonable speed and informative yet not too much information overload. We got to experience the tea pluckers hardship, using the rattan basket, holding with a strap over the forehead. Then, we proceed to the cafe for tea tasting. There were cakes and chocolates available for sales while tasting the tea. We purchased a packet of tea that cost LKR2,000 as souvenirs which was not really cheap. Good thing is that the guide wasnt as pushy as the previous tea factory we visited at Store Field Tea Factory. There are also shop selling other souvenirs, soap , perfumes and toiletries products, etc. We told our driver that this would be our last tea factory to visit since we are not really a tea connoisseur who is particular about the tea quality. Having said that, visit 1 or 2 tea factory is a must in Sri Lanka especially within Nuwara Eliya region since Ceylon (old name for Sri Lanka) Tea is one of the world famous tea.

Title: Good Tea Factory Tour
Text: My wife and I enjoyed this free tour of the Tea factory.  Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and we were shown how the tea leaves were brought into the factory and allowed to dry out.  There were many aspects of the tea leaves going through the various machinery.  We were also shown how the tea leaves were graded and packed.  Finally, we bought some tea and a lovely tea pot in the shop which were reasonably priced.

Title: Good tea
Text: Big factory. Good tea. Nice terrace. But guide was so... not very interesting. Plus they had some floor renovation so there was glue smell all over the place

Title: Kingdom of tea ??
Text:
Very interesting and cognitively ???
We saw the process of working with tea. 

We walked near tea plantation , tried different tipes of tea. 

Very cool ??

Title: Tea Tasting to Factory Tour
Text: Fairly attractive premises externally and a nice balcony area to sit and sample the various teas produced on the estate while listening to a commentary on their origins and production. Then it as off to the factory where the guide took us through the various stages from picking, drying, fermenting, etc. Interesting talk but difficult to hear with the noise of the machinery. No noise reduction earmuffs being worn or evident anywhere. From there we progressed to the shop where the finished product in all it's varieties awaited us in assorted packets, containers, tins, presentation boxes, etc. I enjoyed the tastings when we arrived but considered the priced product way higher than I expected and did not make a purchase despite the best endeavors and entreaties of the fashionable sales ladies.  Interesting visit and we left with a greater appreciation of the conditions that are experienced by the workforce before our favourite brands reach the shelves.

Title: Big disappointment
Text:
We must have had a bad tour guide, because everyone else seems to have had a good experience here. Our tour guide spent less than 10 minutes with us. She rushed us through the processing rooms, didn't speak loud enough to hear her over the machinery and only seemed interested in getting us into the gift shop -- and it wasn't even a busy day!
This would have been an ideal location for a full tour. We would have loved to walk through the fields to see the workers picking the tea, and to take the time to understand how the tea is processed. But we learned very little with our whirlwind tour.
It was nice to have a complimentary cup of tea at the end of the tour, however.
We had such wonderful experiences all over Sri Lanka. The locals could not be more accommodating and friendly. This was the only sour note in our entire visit to this lovely, welcoming country. Perhaps the tour guide was just having a bad day...

Title: Organic Tea
Text: We have visited several tea factories. This one may not have the most informative guided tours but they sell organic tea. I dont mind paying some Rupees more for superior quality.

Title: Interesting.
Text:
Glenloch tea tree plantation was a lovely and  peaceful.
The scenic view was  breathtaking, lush and full of tea plants and other greenery.

Title: Surprisingly refreshing
Text: We were on the road from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya and took an hour to stop at the Glenloch Tea Factory. We were invited to pick tea leaves in the fields and so began our first lessons in the art of tea making. So many things to learn but our guide Ganga, made our tour really enjoyable. We then entered the main processing part of the tour, learning how the tea leaves are dried, ground, filtered and crushed before being roasted. The kids and adults had a great experience, finished off by tea tasting. The atmosphere was relaxed and there was no pressure to purchase along the way...however by the time we had finished everyone wanted to buy some tea. Thanks again to Ganga for making the tour so much fun.

Title: Unplanned but interesting
Text: Unplanned visit. we were short on time for going towards nuwara eliya from kandy. I dont drink tea in fact never tasted. Our driver recommended so decided to take a small stop. Interesting and informative tour and follow up with a free cup of tea (if you like to). We ended up buying lot of tea for family and friends :)

Title: Very interesting
Text: An excellent tour, well organised and led by a lovely guide who explained the processes well. Finished with tea tastings and a visit to the shop, but we did not feel pressured to buy. (but we did buy several boxes!)

Title: Fascinating insight into tea processing
Text:
We decided to stop at Glenloch for our tea experience rather than the many other processers around Nuwara Eliya as photos of the factory are permitted, as well as due to the fact it was on the way to the town from Kandy. 

We arrived to be welcomed by a member of staff who would take us around the factory. Tours are free but visitors are invited to give tips at the end which are distrubuted among all staff. We started our tour seeing the picked leaves being sorted. You are then taken through the whole processing process, from drying, through to cutting, to packing. It was a fascinating insight into a product that so many people enjoy. None of it is staged (although there is some now redundant equipment around to help explain how things were done before some parts of the process were mechanised) so you are seeing tea which well end up in your tea back home being processed.

At the end of the tour you are invited to try some of the teas and of course purchase some if you wish.  You can also wander around outside and see people picking tea. 

Definitely worth a stop if you are travelling between Kandy and Nuwara Eliya: its a good way to stretch the legs.

Title: Very Interesting
Text: I quite liked the visit to Glenloch Tea Factory where I gathered so much more than just information on Tea leaves. It was quite an experience. Make sure when u visit them there is no power cut or else you wont get to see the working factory model. They even give you to taste different flavour's of tea. I loved the Vanilla one highly recommended for people who prefer black tea.

Title: Quite interesting
Text: Quite informative tour, demonstrating how tea is produced.  It was quite short and curt and lacked real detail.  The opportunity to try tea picking was good.  Tasting was just of one brew - which was disappointing.  The shop had a decent range of products available

Title: Good insight into tea production
Text: We are independent travelers and decided to try this plantation to break up our trip between Kandy and NUwara Eliya. It turned out to be a good choice as it was  quite a good tour we were guided through by an English speaking guide. This tour is free of charge. There is a free tasting of all the different types of tea varieties.  There is a sales room and they also sell fine chocolates. Well worth a visit.

Title: Tour & Tasting
Text: We visited as part of a Tour group en route from Kandy to the Hill Country. We did the Factory tour with full process explanations from an English speaking employee. Then a tasting experience and on to the shop, with innumerable tea offerings. Good stop off.

Title: Good tea
Text:
A big drawback for us was that it was the Full-Moon holiday and the workers were not in the fields or in the factory.  The tour still showed the tea drying and where the workers would be.
We had a tea tasting. Be sure to ask for milk and sugar if you want it, because it is not automatically offered. 
It is easy to spend lots of money on tea to take home.  Caveat Emptor

Title: Great tour-pity about the specialty teas
Text:
This tea factory makes a great pit-stop when travelling between Kandy and Ella. We arrived just as a coach tour was leaving and although crowded we had an English speaking guide to ourselves. The tour took us through the full sequence of preparing tea and we learnt about the difference between the varieties ( Strong, Pekoe, Green  etc.)  The restrooms were clean.
the tour ended with a tasting of several varieties of teas, after which we bought some for ourselves and as gifts for friends. 
The only downside was that  Livingston Harvest Green Tea with Raspberry and Strawberry we brought home  expecting a tasty fruit tea turned out to be a coarse green tea with no additives that is undrinkable. It tasted and looked like a cabbage leaf tea...not at all what is to be expected of any sri lankan tea.

Title: An interesting tour of the factory
Text:
As an avid tea drinker,a visit to a major factory was always on the cards. 
The guided tour of the factory was conducted at a reasonably slow pace, with full descriptions of all the processes. The guide spoke very good English and took her time without hurrying us along. All questions were answered clearly so we understood everything.
At the end, we were all treated to a tea tasting - different types of tea - at a slow pace.
There is also a well-stocked gift shop (expected), but there was absolutely no pressure at all to buy anything - well done!
Importantly, the on-site toilets have been really well refurbished much to everyone's surprise - another well done!
So, to sum up - this is well worth the effort to visit.

Title: Interesting but not a must do
Text: I love tea, so I was always going to visit A tea factory.  I understand they're all pretty much of a muchness, all similarly styled from the colonial days of past.  The walk around with an attractive and good English speaking female talked us through the tea making process from the leaf picking to the sorting, drying, crushing, dividing, bagging of the leaves. All looks archaic but it seems to do the trick and they produce and export an enormous quantity per day, so very impressive.  You then get a taste of 3 teas, black, green & white - all good then you can buy loose or bags.  I must say we did buy some green tea and now home can taste the difference to what I've bought in supermarkets.  What they don't show you are the fields and pickers, but you do have the benefit of seeing these lush fields on steep hills on the route into the plantations.  Looks like incredibly hard work but the Sri Lankan people are generous with their smiles so go ahead and visit if you have time.

Title: Factory Tour
Text: We stopped here to visit the tea factory and the plantation. The tea pickers demonstrated their skills and the factory workers the process of producing tea. This was followed by a tea tasting session of various strengths and types before visiting the onsite shop.

Title: Great place to visit
Text:
We had a great tour of the tea factory and the guide showed us and told us of each process, a tea picking competition was held after the tour with a box of tea as a prize.
we sampled the tea afterwards. well worth the visit enjoyed our time here and there was a well stocked shop to browse and buy tea too.

Title: Ceylon tea factory
Text: Visited here on Jan 22nd,2019. This Ceylon tea factory uses equipment from India & Japan to process tea. You can also climb the tea plantation and photo op with a tea picking basket. An employee explained us the process and lead us through the factory and you can also shop for different flavors of tea in the shop like Orange-grapefruit,black earl grey, cherry & mangoosteen etc. Sample tea drink also served here. Eatery is also attached for pastry/snacks.

Title: One of the best tours!!
Text: As tea lovers we were looking forward to a few hours at Glenloch and we werent disappointed. Our guide was very knowledgable and explained the whole process of the tea manufacturing from start to finish. We were given a tour throughput the factory, took photos and asked questions. It was fascinating to see and so incredible what goes into it all. We got a chance to puck some tea leaves which was great fun! Afterwards we got to try some of the different varieties and purchase some from their well stocked shop. Brilliant tour and highly recommend.

Title: Traditional tea factory
Text:
The factory offers a SHORT tour on their grounds where they will show you the tree plants. You are likely to meet Tamil ladies (who pluck an average 30kg of tea leaves per day)  along the way, who will offer to pose with you for a photo for some money (50-100rs should be sufficient "reward")
Factory tour shows you the traditional and modern way of tea making , and at the end you'll be offered black tea with some cookies in their shop where you can then buy some tea. TIP: Try the coconut sweetener & cookie with your tea, its a local replacement for sugar ;)

Title: Ceylon Tea
Text: We made a brief stop here to visit the tea factory. The staff explained the process of tea manufacturing and then we were taken to there cafe for tasting tea. You can also buy different types of tea to take back home. This place has nice views of the valley.

Title: Tea factory visit and lunch
Text:
We dropped into Glenloch for a quick look at tea production and some lunch.  We noticed other visitors receiving guided tours but nobody approached us so we just took a look around ourselves.  It's a bit like stepping back in time for anyone who works in modern manufacturing with a lot of manual labour interspersed with some very old machines.

Lunch was quite good although our waiter didn't seem all that interested in serving us.  I recommend the Nasi Goreng.

We bought some tea from the extensive range in their tourist shop which is worth a visit as you can smell and/or taste most of the teas available.

Title: Tea factory tour
Text: This was scheduled by our guide. The tour was well done and explained thoroughly. Different parts of tea leaf and stem create different tasting teas. This was informative. Afterwards offered free samples to taste in beautiful lounge area and  onto to gift shop to purchase. I drink a lot of tea and I wasnt blown away by taste of tea although we liked the white and silver tea and purchased. I noticed our guide received free tea. There are many tea factories in this area. I dont know why guide picked this particular place.

Title: Interesting tour of the tea factory
Text:
We had an interest and informative tour of the tea factory followed by a tea tasting and the opportunity to buy some tea from the gift shop.
Good activity for all ages.

Title: High Tea!....
Text:
We made a brief stop at the Glenloch Tea Factory as part of our visit to the Nuwara Eliya tea highlands. We had a very informative tour and explanation of the tea production process, and saw some interesting old machinery from the colonial days still in use! 
The different types and gradings of tea were explained (i now know exactly what is meant by broken orange pekoe) and then we sat down to taste some free samples (NB: cake costs extra). Afterwards, it was on to the gift shop which sold the finished product at reasonable prices.
As I had always suspected (and the visit confirmed) the tea we use in the West in our teabags really is called "dust"!....

Title: Great insight and some good information.
Text: A quick and free tour it was good to see and learn more about the tea and different types and sizes giving different flavours. Free tea tasting and cup of tea.  The tea shop is how they make their money but it was not madly over priced and did not feel pressured. The views are worth the stop alone.

Title: Interesting Visit
Text: When you do the must-visit tea factory tour I guess it depends a lot on the guide. Our guide was pleasant and knowledgeable and answered our questions competently and politely.This factory has some quite old machinery which is fascinating in its own right.You can also visit the plantation itself but we seemed to be left alone to do that if we wished. You are given five varieties of tea to taste, which was served with a smile and was nicely hot. Then of course the shop - and what seemed expensive packets of tea. But we did follow the notice saying no tips - which is probably the only one you will see in Sri Lanka!

Title: Enjoyed good tea
Text: Our driver made a stop here on the our way up to our hotel. enjoyed good tea. staff were informative. Made some purchases of green and black tea. enjoying it.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: We were taken around the factory, and the whole process explained to us. Our guide was knowledgeable and answered our questions, but rather unenthusiastic. He whisked us past the sign which said "Do not give tips", and hovered pointedly at the end, as we were trying the different teas. (We resisted). There is a large shop, but as soon as you show any interest the sales lady is unrelenting, so browsing is difficult.

Title: Unhelpful guide
Text:
Visiting a tea factory is a must when visiting SriLanka.   The amazing fresh tea smell permeates the air, and the landscape of Nuwara Eliya is beautiful.   Glenloch is no exception. 

Our guide to the tea factory spouted many dodgy facts about tea.  For example, she seemed to think black tea was high in vitamin C and had more vitamin C than green tea.   She did not know what fermentation or oxidation were.  When I asked questions to clarify her knowledge, she hit back by asking my travel partner whether I could understand English. Ouch!  She then treated me like a retard who couldn't understand what she was saying, which was totally fine with me, because I knew she didn't know even the basics of the tea making process.   I have attached a picture of the dodgy guide.   Surely it takes only 10minutes of reading Wikipedia to pass some basic facts on and she couldn't even do that. I've attached a pic of the guide. 

We didn't get a tour of the plantation outside.  We were told we could wander down the path/road to take a better look outside.  We weren't allowed to walk on the plantation slopes as a safety precaution. 

Once inside, we tasted just one type of tea. It was OK.   The shop was a bit overpriced.  I bought BOP tea in the cheapest packaging, it was 1000rupees. No discounts, no haggling.   Our driver was pretty happy because he got some free tea from the ladies there once we had made our purchases.  I think drivers who bring visitors to Glenloch obviously get perks which depend on how much their visitors spend -  that's enough incentive for them to choose this tea factory over others.  The tea itself tastes great.   Heaps better than the Dilmah you get in Australia. 

In this factory, the same tea gets packaged as different brands.  The price point is just determined by how fancy the brand is, which is mainly comes down to how beautiful the packaging is.   So you might as well buy the no frills packaging.

Title: One of the best activities to do do on your tour of Sri Lanka
Text:
This short your was amazing ! The guide was incredible and taking us through the factory was an eye opener ! 
The shop was a little expensive to be fair but I cannot deny the Sri Lankan people trying to make a little money
Ive just arrived home and had my first cup of tea of the Royal- wow- seriously wow ! Fresh tea and first class quality- if you could buy this tea as fresh and as beautiful as it is youd do it all day everyday- wish I had not been so frugal and bought more not just for ourselves but to share with friends.great tour and well worth the stop by. Thank you for your hospitality expertly included in our itinerary by Blue  Lanka Tours and our. Guide Mr Prakash Keerthy

Title: The tour is nice but the shop is too expensive
Text: We liked the tour very much and was interesting to see how tea is being made. At the end you go through a shop. We wanted to buy white tea and we were told that it is not possible to buy it at the supermarket or local shop other than this shop. This was not true. We paid 4 time the cost in the supermarket!

Title: What i did not know about tea
Text:
Having been driven up into the highlands of sri lanka by ranjan we stopped at glenloch .this is where there are more than just black and green tea silver and gold are now added to the list.all are made from the top leaves silver and gold are from the youngest and smallest leaves and along with green are not fermemted
Tea came to sri lanka when a scots man borrowed some tea plants from china the rest is history

Title: Ok visit
Text: Stopped here and had a tour of the factory. Quite interesting particularily some of the victorian machinery still being used but the tour is brief. Then it is into the cafe and shop where you can try a varirty of teas and purchase different teas and souvenirs. Typical tourist type place.

Title: Great tour
Text:
Visited this factory as part of a tour group and it was very interesting. (Just would have been better if our group of 18 had been split into 2 smaller groups so it was easier to hear). 
After the tour got the opportunity to test the various teas before looking round the shop.
There was a nice handmade chocolate counter - a few free samples might have encouraged people to buy as they looked delicious.
Lovely views from the car park

Title: Not up to expectations
Text: This tour was recomended by our driver but the tour itself was perfunctory, around 10 minutes and they seemed more keen to get us into the shop. The guide herself did not seem overly interested.

Title: Interesting visit-its a tea factory!
Text: We were recommended by our driver ( whose mother is a tea leaf picker)who we have for the week.its a working tea factory,our guide explained the process involved from tree to teacup and we found it fascinating.We both enjoy working factory experiences and the guide was fine.At the end we went into the shop and had some tea buying some rather nice chocolates to have with our teas -I dont normally drink the stuff!

Title: Not worth getting out of the car for
Text: We visited the tea factory in August.  The whole tour in my opinion was rushed , we didn't get any time to ask the guide any questions about the tea making process.  We were hurriedly rushed outside to try the tea which was nice (thinking this was the tea that we would eventually end up buying from their shop).  We finished our tea and were told we could purchase the tea from the shop.  The shop was overcrowded very poor customer service,  the staff did not explain fully when we asked about a particular tea .  We eventually did buy 5 packets of their flavoured tea.     Back home we tried the cardamom tea, to our disappointment the tea was flavourless very very weak ( I left my teabag in my mug for an hour) no flavour and tasted like water .  Waste of money would not recommend going there ever.

Title: Interesting visit
Text: Well organized and informative. Our guide was well informed, friendly and helpful. If you're a tea drinker/lover I'd definitely recommend a visit

Title: Not what we expected.
Text: Having spent 4 days in the beautiful Ella and Nuwara Eliya areas we were disappointed by this factory tour. Short and non motivational followed by pressure to buy what we discovered  later was expensive tea.

Title: Nice, but there are better places
Text: The lady showing us around was nice, and the factory itself is cool. The tour is free, but the tour itself lasts maybe 10 minutes, afterwards they rush you to the shop where they walk after you like hawks pressuring you to buy something. There was variety of tea, with nice packaging, but it was only later (after visiting other factories) we realised that it was overpriced! Wish a bought my tea elsewhere. Afterwards we went to Damro tea factory, which had professional staff and a beautiful place with awesome view to drink tea, I'd recommend that place instead

Title: Interesting tour and good shop
Text: The tour of the tea factory was very interesting with incredible smells. Refreshingly, we werent pestered or rushed into the shop at the end as one usually is at the end of such tours. Even so, the shop was very busy as the prices are good and the quality of the tea is high. They also offer free tastings of the different teas they make.

Title: Unfriendly and rushed
Text:
Of all the tea estates to visit do not choose this one. Our driver insisted we come here because it is one of the estates that is 100% Sri Lankan owned. Whilst I wanted to support local business the way we were treated here was disappointing. The lady provided a very rushed tour, she had no expression on her face and often yawned.
When we asked any questions she was reluctant to answer. Of course at the end she wanted her tip and when we were browsing the shop she suddenly became interested in helping us (perhaps she gets a commission). We were so excited to visit this beautiful part of Sri Lanka but being treated like we were just $$ took the pleasure out of our experience. I have heard other estates provide more customer service training to their staff and might be better to visit. I hope the owners of the Glenloch estate read this and review their service levels.

Title: Buy your tea here rather than in town
Text: The tour was short and informative, and the friendly staff promptly provided tea of all sorts for tasting. There are plenty of places to buy your Sri Lankan tea, but when you buy it from here you know it directly benefits the factory workers.

Title: Visit at Tea factory
Text: Nice visit at Glenloch tea factory. We had a english speaking guide who showed us the tea factory. She told us all about the process. We could ask questions and she gave us good answers. Afterwards we got to taste black, white, green tea. Nice store where you could buy tea. Good experience!

Title: Great experience
Text: Apparently one of the few tea factories that let you take photos. We really enjoyed our experience with our informative guide - learning about the processing of tea. We watched it being dried, sorted, roasted and packaged. We then got to try a number of types... our favourites were the OP and white tea. Chocolates are delicious and a great accompaniment to the tea. I suggest giving lunch a miss though. It was very average for a high price for Sri Lanka.

Title: Tour Stop Off.
Text: Called in here for the factory tour and was amazed at how genuinely historically it has been kept. Very noisy so it was difficult to hear what the charming guide was saying but even so very worthwhile. Nice cup of tea at the end and no pressure to buy any products.

Title: Educational visit... and a good cuppa too
Text:
Glenloch is certainly worth a visit. 

We had a a great tour which showed us exactly how the leaf is turned into a lovely cup of tea. It also explained how different kinds of tea are made.

After the tour we headed down to try four different types of tea, each of which were delicious. Before leaving we made sure we purchased some tea, however I must add that we were not pressured into doing so.

Breathtaking views of the surrounding hills and a lovely cuppa. What more could you want.

Title: A good cuppa
Text: I really enjoyed the visit to this tea factory. It was really interesting to see the process from beginning to end. This is still a thriving and active tea factory. Very informative and great to see the various stages of production. Enjoyed the smells too. Good tasting experience at the end and of course, we bought some!

Title: From the field to the cup!
Text:
From the field to the cup Glenloch Tea Factory is worth a visit. So much more to tea than what youre drinking.  

We joined tea pluckers in the field.  There is an art in picking the leaves.  We had the baskets balanced on our back with rope tethered to our head to put the picked leaves in.  

Then the next step was to take the picked leaves to the factory for processing.  

Different fields for growing different teas.  

People attending this event then get a chance to taste the different teas.  I bought a couple of tins of The Royal Tea!  Yes the Royal family purchase this tea from Glenloch. 

We spent about 2hrs here on our road trip with Pledge Holidays Sri Lanka.

Title: Interesting and informative
Text:
We had earlier on visited a tea museum in a former tea factory so it was very interesting to visit an active tea factory to see the different processes and all the different kinds of tea made from the same plant. 
We had a free cup of tea and also had the chance to taste and compare green tea, white tea and brown tea. (We can recommend the brownie cake in the cafe, it didnt look as fancy as the other cakes in the display but it had a good taste)

Title: A Very Interesting Stop
Text: Along the winding drive through the mountains and tea plantations, we stopped at Glenloch Tea Factory. It was really interesting and our guide was knowledgeable and to the point which we liked. After the tour we enjoyed a cup of tea on the balcony and took in the beautiful views before hitting the road again.

Title: The real deal
Text: Most tea factories have become just for tourists and are there for show, however Glenloch was different. This factory was a lot less busy, so the guide we had didnt need to rush us through. We was able to see all the staff at work and also were able to take pictures (most of the factories dont allow this.) It was fascinating to see the process of tea making! At the end we was able to taste 5 different types of tea with gorgeous views of the tea fields. Whats best is all of this is free! Theres a huge selection of teas to buy afterwards, some that come in beautiful wodden boxes, which make great gifts! Would recommend this trip to any tea lover!

Title: Don't buy their breakfast tea bags!
Text:
Most of the bags are either split or they split when stirring in the cup.
You end up with a heap of tea leaf bits at the bottom of your cuppa.
A complete waste of money and so disappointing after an enjoyable tour.

Title: Interesting stop
Text:
On our trip around Sri Lanka we stop among many places here, our guide set us up with a guide a the factory that went trough all the steps of tea making. It was really interesting, and more so if we actually could hear what she said all the time. The noice was a bit to load as the tour was in the actual factory. But maybe she could have spoken up a bit, we had to stay really close and pay attention to hear the main parts at least.

After we tasted the different teas and bought quite much to family and friends.

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
This was an interesting view of how tea is made, and it was free!

Our guide was very good, we were tagged onto a large group who kept taking ages to move on.

After tour got our samples of the different types of tea. Restaurant was nice with a beautiful view.

Was slightly pressured by not buying something, which we didnt. Shop very busy and small.

Title: Organized factory with a scenic view
Text:
Beautiful landscaping, friendly staff, all tourists are made into small groups for a tour of the factory. A particular staff that speaks your preferred language is dedicated for the tour which was amazing.
After the tour you can buy glenloch products to take home. We bought a gift pack of 4 different flavoured teabags and they are all very flavorful.

Title: Interesting but....
Text: The tour was interesting in what it was, though we had a very disinterested, dry tour guide not only that a couple of cheeky factory workers tricked us into paying for a photo of the station they where working in (we hadn't seen the no tipping factory workers sign at that stage).

Title: How to make a cup of tea
Text:
A nice stop to find out how English breakfast tea comes to pass. As ever very nice people and  short tour followed by tea (and cake).
A beautiful area....

Title: Worth a visit.
Text: Short visit, quick tour from informative guide, interesting. Quick tasting and visit to the shop. Toilets clean. Enough said.

Title: Terrible tea
Text:
The worst tea in srilanka 
Taste is nothing of srilanka 
Visiting the factory is interesting but the tea itself for sure the worst tea ever

Title: Very nice and tasteful
Text:
I didn't know this place. The driver took me there and I've loved the place.
The explanation  is very clear and illuminance. Leads you step by step into the creation of tea; white,green,black,strong and delicate.
At the end they serve you a taste of all the  qualities and of course the tour ends in their shop where you can buy every kind of tea. 
After that it is mendetory to step into the tea plants to take some picture with their basket on the shoulders.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We attended on recommendation of our driver. It was worth a visit. Tour was free, quick but informative. Disappointed that the tour didn't include anything in the fields and focused only on the factory side but that was very informative. Free samples at the end was great and a first for us to taste several varieties side by side and learn the differences. I was so disappointed that there was no field tour component that I struck out in my own and walked amongst the tea bushes. Nobody stopped me and I enjoyed the foray, albeit with my wife scorning me all the way. Suggest you do likewise if you want the full experience. We bought some tea to take home which was pricey, but we felt assured of the decision later as our driver also bought a kilo for his own use (or so he said - see my review of Red Dot tours)

Title: Short tour but beautiful scenery
Text: We enjoyed the tour of the factory and we ate lunch at the onsite restaurant (average and expensive for Sri Lanka). We had a nice lady taking us around but felt the tour was very short, we were then led to a room to sample the tea's on offer (had really bad heartburn after) and were then let into the shop to try and sell us some tea. We didn't buy anything but got some nice photos with the staff.

Title: Ok
Text: Visited this tea plantation,factory interesting how they produce the tea .Restaurant meal they seemed to be in a hurry asking me before I'd finished if I wanted anything else .Toasted ham & cheese sandwich disappointing.

Title: A History Lesson...
Text: Glenloch Tea was established 150 years ago and that in its self is quite remarkable to still be processing tea for export around the world. The tour was interesting to watch the process from start to finish and enjoy several tasting cups of tea at the end. The staff were friendly and we felt no pressure to make a purchase....but we did however and my family now wish me to track down were I can purchase it in Australia!

Title: pick another place, trap for tourist
Text: Tour and tea tasting are free.  tour is ok but not view of plantation, and not testing except one cup of tea so  tea tasting is a disappointment. If you want to buy tea, this is the place to be ripped off. A total no go.. it's a surprise how they are still on business. If your tour is taking you there, avoid shopping! after visit they send you directly to the shop... there is better place to go.

Title: Pick another place
Text: Tour and tea tasting are free. However, the tea tasting is a disappointment. If you want to buy tea, this is the place to be ripped off. A total no go.. it's a surprise how they are still on business. If your tour is taking you there, avoid shopping!

Title: An average tea factory
Text: We took some friends to the Glenloch Tea Factory as they had never been to a tea factory. A lady spent 30 minutes showing us around the factory after which we were offered a selection of four different teas to taste. I would describe the overall experience as being 'average', with a bonus perhaps being that we were not charged for the tour. Instead, we gave a tip to the lady who showed us around.

Title: Unsure
Text: The day we went there it was public holiday so had to see machines all at rest. In a way I think was good coz no noise of them. The guide who explained everything was a bit bore. She narrated everything like machine. Looked like she was tired coz they were running on skeleton staff.

Title: A quick tour and some tea
Text:
We were given a quick tour of the factory. It was interesting to find out how tea is processed. We saw all the machines,etc. 
Tried only 2 different types of tea, they were ok. They have a shop where you're u can purchase tea. 
It would have been nice to go and see the workers picking the tea in the fields.

Title: Fascinating and Well Worth a Visit
Text: Glenloch is 2 or 3 hours drive from Kandy but it is well worth the journey if, like me, you have never seen a tea plantation before.  En route you pass through interesting countryside including tea growing areas as you get closer, and there are great views as you get higher.  The factory tour and the tasting are really interesting and I am very glad I went.  One point: tea pickers are very poor indeed so they are very persistent if given a chance to beg: you should take quite a few small banknotes with which to thank them if you photograph them.

Title: Old building has charm; ok tea
Text:
Original corrugated plate tea factory along the road to Nuwara Elia. Easy access with parking. Tour of the old building is automatic, with a young lady taking you on a fairly quick tour. She did her best, and answered questions with some interest. Other than that the tour is mainly designed to get you into the small shop. Sad to say, no effort has been made to make the shop appealing and to give it some charm. You need to buy something or no commission for the guide...
To taste you get 4 types of tea, all quite decent, but not my favorite types.
Small restaurant on site, with good quick bites at decent price.
Bathrooms are at our own risk, although the mens has a nice view...

Title: New information!
Text:
The information during the walkthrough was nice and was good to learn about the process of tea.

Very interesting to see the amount of old and new technology used in this tea factory.
