I ended up being offered the same tea for ten times the price at several places in Mirissa. So the second time, I made sre to stock up. Our driver came in to check on us as we were checking out. He did a doubletake at the size of the stack of tea boxes we were buying. But the price cannot be beat, even elsewhere in country. They have both bags and loose leaf available. 

I really enjoy the factory tour. As others have noted, the tour is the factory side only. I also wish they would take us out in the plantation. But the factory tour is really interesting. It is amazing to see how much they produce in a relatively small place and learn about just how the tea is sold. (Hint: it is sold in international auctions held in Colombo). 

The tea here is really good. My friend bought some black tea and gave it to her son who promptly made a cup. He came in saying "Oh my god, you have to try this tea!" She responded "Yes, yes. I have had black tea." And he answered, "Oh no you haven't! Not like this!" I understand the tea did not last long and now my friend regrets not buying more. I too am completely spoiled by the quality. I tend to only drink Glenloch Sri Lanka tea.

I never felt pressured to buy anything here. In fact, the first time I came, I sat in their tasting room for hours just enjoying the gorgeous views and the excellent tea. On cup of white, one of black, one of green, and one of the golden flush (they won't tell you how they make that one). It was the first moment I truly relaxed and felt like I was on vacation.

Next time I am in Sri Lanka, I will definitely stop by for more tea!

Title: Beautiful location, nice tea
Text: The tea factory is like any other you will visit, however, the taste of the their brew was superb. After a round of the factory, they will give you taste of their popular (not their best) brew, which most will abviously like.  I had to ask for tasting their different teas, which my host readily agreed to.  I must confess I am a tea lover and have a weak point for Silver Tips which I found was up to mark and readily purchased two packs - one for myself and one for a friend who too is a tea connoisseur.  Worth a visit I will say.

Title: Beautiful Tea Plantation
Text: Glenloch Tea Plantation in Nuwara Eliya is beautiful. The tea factory is spotless clean and the guides give good tours with simple explanations. Visitors get to drink their prized teas and there is variety of caked you can buy. A good stop as this area is filled with tea plantation and tea factories.

Title: Great place to stop at
Text:
We stopped on our way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya as part of our tour plan. This is such a great place. Scenic views all around - everywhere you look you just see lush greenery and all round beauty!

The tea making process  tour itself was brief but the cafe stop was fabulous. We pickedup quite a few bakes (cookies, brownies etc) and also tasted some of their green and white teas. Also bought some Cinnnamon (which we later found to be almost 40% more expensive in Colombo) and their best teas to take home for family.

My younger was nauseous and had thrown up earlier so we wanted him to eat something. He refused to have anything except chocolate cake. One of the staff in the restaurant actually went in to the kitchen and got him a cake (although it was not on the shelf for sale) and refused to even let us pay for it! 

All in all, a great stop!!

Title: Part of Tour
Text: Visit is worth the stop in house guide has her talk down to a tea gift shop is well stocked.Take time to walk the tea garden the views around are amazing

Title: Worth The Visit
Text:
My husband and I were originally going to go to another plantation which we found online but our driver recommend Glenloch Tea factory and we are pleased he did take us here !

We were given a free tour into the factory by a lovely woman who spoke perfect English . She was friendly and knowledgeable about tea . The factory was very interesting as you saw first hand the process of the tea . Very interesting . Afterwards my husband had lunch there with the free tea they served us . Good tea , mediocre lunch but you do not expect great food at a plantation . Good tea ! We bought some tea as. souvenir. We did not need to go see other tea plantations after we had seen this one . Worth a visit if you are in the area !

Title: Great cup of tea
Text: We had a great time at Glenloch. It was very interesting to see how the tea is processed and even better to enjoy a nice cup afterwards. The view is breathtaking and the Tea is excellent. You will find a great cup here.

Title: So that's how they make tea!
Text: It's always interesting to see how stuff is made (and not just on Discovery Channel)... They show you the   Very basic and traditional way tea is made!  And then you can try it all... And buy whatever you want.  Best gifts you can take out of Sri Lanka.

Title: Health & Safety!!
Text:
Our driver took us here as an unexpected "treat". Very interesting to see what it take to make something that we wll take for granted. The process is very dusty and noisy, but not a sign of masks or ear defenders - a union would have a field day here!
Well worth a visit with camera to capture the various stages and look forward to a free cup of tea at the end of the tour.

Title: An intended break
Text: Being Indian (now living in america) we know the importance of Tea. A cup of tea in the morning gives a kick start to the life. We had detailed view of the Factory and could see how tea is processed from leaf to packed bags. It was interesting and the factory staff was eager to explain whatever we asked for. The restaurant of the Factory was updated with all variety of tea manufactured here. I bought two packs for the house in USA.We visited this factory during our visit to Sri Lanka in Dec.2012.We were on our way to Nuwara Eliya when we took a break here.

Title: Nice place for a break
Text: It is very quite place where you can get information about tea fabrication and its history. Also you can have a lucnh or dinner in the reataurant. Prices is not high and quality of foods is very good. I you are not the maniac of tea don't buy tea in this place. Because it is expencive, but not the best. Just enjoy history, nature and meal :)

Title: Honeymoon June 2013
Text: We visited the tea factory in June 2013 as part of honeymoon. As it was raining we were mat by very friendly staff from our car with umbrellas!! The tour was extremely informative and interesting. The staff were very friendly, they took photos of us let us touch the tea etc. There was no admission fee so we tipped our guide and bought some tea!! We were given tea to taste too. A great place to visit!!

Title: Very informative
Text: We didn't know anything about tea so found this was very informative and fascinating. Felt like our tour girl was in a huge hurry to finish the tour though. Disappointing that the tour was only the factory not the fields too. Haven't tried it yet but bought the strongest tea at 1200 LKR for 400 grams.

Title: First hand experience of Tea making process.
Text:
We really enjoyed the tour of Glenloch handles by a lady named Mrs.Uma. She showed us all the basics explaining how tea is processed from leaves to final dust.

Nice process views. Also enjoyed a Hot cup of Black tea at the end.

Worth visiting and buying a pack of Export quality fresh tea. and there are many varieties of tea ranging from green tea to golden tea.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: It was great to see tea leafs be produced into tea. The guide we had was informative and eager to answer any questions about the tea they produced.  We say down for a glass of tea after the visit, and yeah bought a little bit too, but hey why not the tasted good and the tour was fun.

Title: Fascinating insight, well presented, not too touristy
Text: A cup of tea will never be the same, now that I have understood and seen the complex process involved!

Title: Finelly saw how tea is made
Text: Beautiful nice girl guided us through the whole process of making tea. Very interesting experience to see and smell. Not any easy from the harvest to the final product. And although I am not a particular tea lover I have to say that the taste of the provided sample was simply great and definitely from time to time I have tea instead of coffee.

Title: Not an Attraction. Its simply a typical tourist setup.
Text:
This is a typical stop arrange by the taxi drivers and tour operators to put tourist in commercially tourist shops. They sell it as a "tea factory tour" but is basically a show around the factory to end in the factory souvenir shop to be force either to tip the tour guide or to buy a very expensive selection of tea's. 

This is very common in this part of the world. You would see this kind of stops in Thailand, Indonesia and even in India. The Spice Garden is something very similar and its around the corner. You might buy something that you like but at a very expensive price (for Sri Lanka). But don't allow to be push around with this methodology. If you don't wanna stop or buy, nobody can force you.

Title: Great place to see
Text:
As I have only ever visited one( this) tea factory I really can't say how good it is in comparison to others. What I can say is that we really enjoyed it. Didn't take too long, say the process from start to finish, saw the the classic scene of the tea pickers at work, old but functioning machines drying sorting and rolling the leaves. Very informative guide and a great cuppa to finish it off overlooking the amazing hills. 
Really recommend this place for a visit

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
On our trip towards Nuwara Eliya we stopped off for a visit at the Glenloch Tea Factory. The Guide shows you upstairs in the tea sorting room and explains the process involved in tea production. The machinery is very old but obviously still does the job. Workers seemed used to having tourists watch them work. You can take photos. Even thou there is a clear sign not to tip the Guide you are put in a position to discreetly pass him something. I did not see the Tip Box. After the tour a very nice hot cuppa is provided. No idea what type we were given as we were left in peace to enjoy it.
No pressure made to purchase any tea as the shop was busy with a bus of tourists. We did not have the opportunity to walk amongst the tea bushes but our driver very kindly offered a stop further down the road.

Title: Well Established Tea Factory
Text:
My taxi driver took me from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya to visit the Glenloch tea plantations which has a 150 years old Tea factory.  I enjoyed some beautiful scenery on the way with waterfalls and lush green tea estates on the hills. The tour of the factory was very interesting.  It is amazing to see how the green leaves are taken through various stages to turn it into the black tea we all enjoy.  The tour is free, but visitors are expected to put some money in the Tip box in the cafe, where everyone is offered a complimentary cup of tea.
I as well as a few other visitors had picked up a leaflet on this tea factory from a tourist office and it had an offer of a free mug on it.  But unfortunately all of us were disappointed as the cafe did not honour it.

Title: Interesting place, nice tea
Text: We found the Heritage Tea Plantations beautiful as we were driving through the tea country from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya. Our driver stopped at Glenloch Tea Factory to show us how tea is being dried and packed to be ready for a drink. We visited the tea factory late afternoon, so we could not see the whole process. In spite of this, our guide was very nice and he explained everything while he was taking us round. It was so interesting! We got a sample cup of tea to taste their product and then we could buy tea in the shop. We enjoyed our visit here and brought a few boxes of their nice tea home!

Title: Rude Tour Guide Ruined Our Experience
Text:
We were very excited to visit the Tea plantations and drove three hours out of our way to do so. Our driver took us to Glenloch Tea Factory. The grounds were lovely and it was fascinating to see the process that goes into tea. I certainly will never drink tea without thinking of it again. 
However, our guide was very rude. We felt very rushed the whole time, he never fully answered our questions, and even though we tipped him more than we thought we should have, he asked for more. 
I was also very interested to try the different types of tea that they have (similar to wine tasting), yet they only gave us one complimentary cup of tea and did not even tell us which variety it was. 

The best part about our visit here was the restaurant down the road which had just opened up. It is called the "Oak & Ray Tea Bush, Ramboda". It has a stunning view, great buffet, and will be beautiful when it is finished being built.

Title: Really interesting but rude guide!
Text:
Our driver took us here on the way to the Heritance Tea Factory hotel.  It was a really interesting visit.  We never realised just how many processes went into making tea.  We really do take it for granted with our tea bags back home!!!  A gentleman took us round who was the amanger, showing us the full process, we could take pictures and the staff were smiling whilst working away non stop.  After the factory tour he took us to see the tea plantation next to the factory so we could see and touch the tea bushes.  Once the tour was finished, he took us to the shop where we had a complimentary cup of tea which was delicious.  My husband gave him what we thought was a reasonable tip, considering there is a tip box in the shop, we shouldn't be expected to give twice.  He was the manager, was certainly on a better wage than the tea factory workers.  He mumbled something under his breath about the tip not being big enough.  We just politely smiled and walked away!!!
We bought a box of various fruit teas for us to enjoy at home.  Worth a visit but make sure you don't have the greedy manager show you round!!!!

Title: Interesting and worth going
Text: We really enjoyed our tour of this tea factory and learning how tea is made. We had no idea it is such a long process. You are given some tea to sample in the cafe at the end and then inevitably we bought a fair amount to bring home. The only irritant was the lady in the shop who followed us round as we were browsing the teas almost hassling us to buy!

Title: A very enjoyable place to stop
Text: My family and I went on a succinct interesting and varied tour which we all enjoyed and learnt something from. The guide was very pleasant, informative and genuine. The tour is free however there is a staff tip box at the end. Finished with a magnificent complimentary cuppa not surprisingly but splash out and buy cake. Surrounded by stunning scenery

Title: Excellent visit, exquisite tea
Text: Visit on recommendation of my guide. Tour of the factory, well explained, nothing in a hurry, though I went solo. Bought some Gold Tea, White Tea, Golden Pekoe and Silver Tips after the tasting. Decent lunch with stunning views over the mountain and the lake. Maybe there are better tea factories, but I was quite happy to have visited Glenloch.

Title: No EXP date, No Batch number, No MFD date
Text: The company sticks hand written stickers over the Tea Packages. These can be easily removed and a new sticker attached. So when ever you visit, you would probably see a Tea package that was manufactured very recently. It only occurred to me after returning home because the sticker came off easily by the time I returned home to Singapore !  ZERO star for hand written labels ! and certainly overpriced ! Scottish name with Sri Lankan standards of labeling. I used their bathroom, so its 3200 LKR for bathroom usage and cheap Tea from a company with unprofessional labeling. God only knows if it was packed several years ago or just recently !

Title: Interesting and informative tour of the tea factory
Text: We had a very interesting and informative tour of this tea factory and we really enjoyed it! I was a little skeptical before we got there, thinking that it might be dull or rigged for tourists but it was great learning about all of the different teas. The tour guide was very knowledgeable and was able to answer all of our questions, and we had the chance to try some of the teas after the tour too. Highly recommended if you're looking to visit a tea factory in Sri Lanka.

Title: Interesting Place!
Text: It's a must to visit a tea factory during travelling through Sri Lanka. We had a short guided tour in the factory which was interesting. Good for buying some gifts for people at home,

User_Location: Vila Nova de Santo Andre, Portugal
Title: Holidays in Sri Lanka
Text: Beautiful landscape and very interesting tour inside the factory with a very friendly lady explaining all the tea processes! Once more we learn something and enjoyed a cup of delicious tea! As usual people in the tea shop were very kind and professional. We bought some tea and we were very pleased to be there.

Title: Interesting factory visit.
Text:
Even though there were tour buses, the two of us got our own private tour.  The girl did a good job explaining things, and was able to answer our questions.  

It's in a beautiful area, and you can see beautiful views while you sit and enjoy the free cup of tea after the tour.

There is a lot of tea to purchase, and your guide will help you but won't be pushy.

Title: Factory visit
Text: Very interesting... A lot of work goes into producing that perfect "cup" of tea! They have a well stocked shop where various blends of loose tea can be purchased!

Title: I think there are better places to see
Text: We visited this tea factory in october this year. It is'nt very much. The total tour takes about 10 minutes and for me it was'nt interesting at all. The lady that guided us was not very friendly. We were only with 3 persons and I think she rather had a busload of tourists. In the factory is not very much to see.

Title: wonderful! - an eye opening tea experience!
Text:
One of the few experiences in Sri Lanka that felt incredibly genuine and honest.
Our helpful guide walked us through the inner workings of the tea factory explaining very clearly each part of the process of how is tea is made - from leaves to your tea cup! Walking through the factory you see the ladies working on the machines big smiles on their faces eager to have you come touch and smell each part of the tea leaves experience.
It all ends with a chance to have a lovely cup of tea or two with the hospitable people at the factory and perhaps walk away with a packet of tea or two if you'd like to - but no pressure is put on you to buy anything.

I'd highly recommend this experience to anyone with an interest in tea or even just to see the inner workings of a quaint place like Nuwara Eliya!

Title: It's good to see know how to differentiate between good and bad tea
Text: It's interesting to see the stages tea goes through to become from a leaf to tea pack. There was a guide explaining and going through the old style machinery in the factory. good Information to know about tea so you can know the difference between good and bad tea and the variety. Tour ends up by tea tasting and you can buy from their shop. Personally i felt it's a bit over priced. We had a chance to take some pics in the field where the ladies were picking the tea leafs

Title: Interesting but overpriced tea shop and poor selection
Text: Interesting old style tea processing factory and equipment.  Some old equipment is preserved for historical interest.  Our free tour guide was mechanical and perfunctory but as there were only two of us, I think she was keen to get to the next (hopefully larger) group of tourists.  Free cup of tea in the tea shop was OK but limited choice to select from.  The limited selection of tea packs on sale were ridiculously priced. If you want to buy tea in Sri Lanka I recommend you visit the markets where the locals buy.  We got some lovely silver tip tea in a small spice shop in Galle at very reasonable price.

Title: Loved this!
Text:
If you're interested in the tea making process then you should stop here. Not the largest but very informative. Friendly and knowledgable tour guide, cup of tea at the end, beautiful views from factory and a shop to buy the various teas afterwards! 
Tea pickers stop picking at 3pm so if you want to see that, time it accordingly- although not a must because if you're driving in the area you will see this happening as the tea factories cover the mountain!! Hire a driver- the views are gorgeous! The sun drops quickly and it looked quite bleak around 5pm when we were leaving but at 10am the following morning, the sun was shining and it looked spectacular! I loved this!!

Title: White Tea....wow
Text:
What a fantastic place this is.  So full of history and demonstration of the hard working people who patiently pick the tea leaves that we all enjoy around the world.  We did a short tour that is free but there is a box to place tips for the staff.  They share these which is a good and fair system.  Then you are able to do tea tasting and select tea for purchase.

I got carried away shopping again but it is so fresh how can you revisit.

I would buy more of the exotic white and silver tea next time.

Title: Pleasant & Informative
Text:
Myself and 16 travel companions dropped in at this Tea Plantation and Factory on the way from Kandy to Yala. It proved a welcome and informative rest stop.

A young woman showed us around the factory floors, providing us with valuable descriptions of the tea manufacturing process from cultivation and picking to how teas are selected and packaged. It was actually quite absorbing.

We finally enjoyed cups of Broken Orange Peko Fannings tea, about the best, and made our purchases. The views from the tea house and shop are quite stunning!

This was one if those felicitous stops we were glad to have made; I recommend this Tea Factory heartily.

Title: Nice Place
Text: Its a nice place to stop-by on your way. They serve you good tea and take you around the factory showing the whole tea making process. It has a nice lobby and I feel the tea options they had were also not overpriced.

Title: Nice tea lobby
Text: The factory is the same as others, but the tea lobby is very nice. Good to look and have a tea. I thing, their tea was the most expensive of all, where I been, but try the lobby, the shopping is not the must.

Title: A nice place to stop
Text: We stopped here between Kandy, en route to the Heritance tea factory hotel. Beautiful scenery surrounds this working factory. A polite young lady took us on a short tour of the factory teaching us the processes in which tea is made, White, Green & Black. We were allowed to take lots of pictures and at the end were offered a fresh cup of Ceylon tea....perfect. It was served in the little shop. There was no pressure to purchase anything, but we did. Overall a nice stop off.

Title: Glenloch Tea Factory...a sip of Srilankan black tea..
Text:
Visit to the Glenloch Tea Factory on the way to Nuwara Eliya was my second visit to a tea factory after the one i visited in Munnar. We were taken around and introduced to the process of tea making starting from plucking to the final product which makes its way to our home. The factory is very neat and it takes about 15 mins to see all the process involved in making some of the finest black tea in the world in terms of its distinct flavor, aroma, and strength.
We were treated to a cup of black tea and what stood out was the wonderful aroma. There is a shop from where you can purchase a variety of tea. 
If you happen to visit Nuwara Eliya, do visit any of the tea factories. It hardly takes a hour and it is not every day you can see your favorite tea processed in front of your eye.

Title: Tea county and smiling faces!
Text:
A must go place!  We were greeted with traditional Namesty, and lots of smiling faces.
A lady named Kamaleshawari took us around and guided us thru the factory. It is quite a neat place. They also have a very nice tea lounge and shopping places.
The tea made there is not of very high quality maybe. The blend wasn't of our liking!
We stayed in a place just above the factory. The Glenloch villa, very nice place!
I am really thankful to the tea factory Incharge for making it possible for my package to reach Colombo airport before we left Srilanka.
Really nice people!!

Title: Mesmerised with the flavour of Srilankan tea
Text: On the way to Nuwareliya from Kandy, this factory is located near pussawella. Nice place situated amidst the tea estates. Lot of tamil women working in this tea factory. A person named mrs.sasikala explained us about various types of tea and tea leaves processing. They also offered us a cup of aromatic sri lankan tea free of cost. It tastes excellent. Nice place to relax and sip a good tea.

Title: Glenloch Tea Factory ........... A good place to visit
Text:
The Tea factory is located in a natural scenic backdrop.A cup of hot and tasty Ceylon tea is served to us.I had a factory tour.Very good explanation about the production of tea was given by one the Glenloch staff.
Excellent place to tour.

Title: Interesting tour with shop there too
Text: I think there are probably more "up market" tourist-y tea factories in the area but we enjoyed being shown around the whole process and seeing some of the very old machinery as well as the more modern processes,  We had some tea afterwards and although no-one pushed it we did buy quite a lot to take home with some decent knowledge of what type is what.  I would definitely go to the toilet somewhere else though, grim....

Title: Great place to visit
Text: I visited glen loch on my recent tour of srilanka . We had a free tour of the factory, by a very polite young man and then taken for a taste of the tea. There was no pressure to buy any tea, though  when you see the shop you can't help but buy some! All in all a good stop off on our journey.

Title: A Working Museum....
Text:
OK, having read the previous reviews, lets try and give some balance.... The tea factory is a wonderful relic to the belief, that if it isn't broken, don't mend it and in common with other factories, the process has not changed throughout the centuries. Similarly, some of the machinery is well over a hundred years old and in fact the tea factory is in effect a working museum. Yes the tea in the shop is overpriced, we we found this to be true at other similar establishments and as for the taste...don't forget that the tea drunk in England is blended tea, a concoction very often of teas from a number of countries. Pure tea is often drunk without milk and can be an acquired taste.
You cannot visit Sri Lanka without visiting a tea factory and Glenloch set in the uplands in Nuwara Eliya is a typical set up. People wanting tips is typical of the culture and tourists should not be surprised; wages are very low, so If you feel a service has been carried out, then a small reward could be given, but if not, keep your hands in your pockets. The same applies to overpriced tea !

Title: Disappointingly poor!!
Text:
En route to The Heritance Tea Factory we stopped off here. It was awful!! And the toilets even worse, with a man wanting a tip, absolutely ludicrious!!!
We were showed round the tea processing factory by a young women who was quite obviously exhausted and sick to death of saying the same thing!!
The shop was good with plenty too offer but no change and  I was forced to ask around the room if someone could help. It wasn't until our driver intervened and protested on my behalf that all of a sudden change was found......the whole place was in a terrible state. The carpark was being altered, but not finished, the same with the extension.

Something is definitely going wrong here??!! Such a shame!!!

Title: Got a box of bad tea as gift from trip
Text: I didn't visit this place. A friend did and bought a box of tea for us back home as gift. It had a suspicious smell and tasted awful, sour, kind of reminded me of the smell of peel of lychee. It appeared to us that it wasn't just some cheap tea; instead, something was really wrong with it. One of us started to feel weird in the stomach after drinking it. So you can probably visit this place again, but we don't recommend buying tea from them.

Title: Nice Museum but sadly a hard sell at the end
Text:
I would have given this 4 stars if it wasn't for the relatively hard sell at the end of our tour with tea prices which are ridiculously high.  £4.00 for a small box of loose Earl Grey Tea when it costs less than £1.00 at Cargills is simply too steep.

As to the museum, our whole family enjoyed learning about tea and seeing the old British machinery from the 19th century.  It was easy to imagine the workings of the factory and it was an informative trip down memory lane.  I think the factory tour is free but the museum cost £2.50 to get in.  As Tea is part of the Sri Lankan culture now, a visit to some kind of museum should really be on your agenda.  Not sure if this is the best one but it certainly gives you a good insight into the differences of green/black teas and what manufacturing processes are used.

Title: Buyer beware!
Text:
Naturally the Tea factory is one of the highlights of a visit to Sri Lanka and the Glenloch has many original features and makes a great photo call as you pass through the various production stages.  The guide was good and was seriously looking for a gratuity from the moment the tour started. We were offered a luke warm cuppa at the end of the tour in the visitor centre so beware.
This is a great retail opportunity and the visitor centre is poorly laid out with a limited selection of teas to buy as gifts to take home  when compared with others we saw on the up Newara Eliya and compared with tea gardens we had visited in Southern India and Malaysia.  If fact I bought most of my tea later in my trip from a Tea merchant in Galle.  The difficulty with this venue is that it was selected by the tour company so we just turned up in the car park.  If you read this and have a choice make sure you check out some of the other tea gardens, yes they all have Scottish names.

Title: A real gem
Text:
This was an unexpectedly interesting stop off on our journey from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.

We were given a free tour of the factory by a sweet young lady and it was very informative and interesting to see how the tea is processed and to see how antiquated it all was.

We felt no pressure to tip or particularly to buy anything in the shop - although we did pick up some slightly overpriced but fresh tea in the shop following a cuppa.

Title: Terrible Tea!
Text:
I visited The Glenloch Tea factory with my family. The tour was very interesting and the guide excellent. We bought 8 packs of three kinds of tea to take back to The UK with uswhat an idea gift we thought! We also bought some tea for ourselves.
However, when we tried to drink the tea after returning home it was unpalatable. The Ginger tea for instance tasted of dish-water, quite disgusting. The friends who we gave the tea as gifts were, without exception, in agreement. I apologised to them.
Maybe we bought a bad batch? So I emailed The Glenloch Tea Company and reported what, when and how it tasted. They didnt answer let alone acknowledge. I checked the email address on their site several times and it was correct. I waited. Two weeks later I wrote again. No response. Two weeks again and I wrote now three weeks on and not even the courtesy of acknowledgement, a reply or even better an apology!
I now believe that they must have so many complaints that they just dont bother to answer.
Therefore I would most certainly choose one of the other plantations to visit but if your guide insists that you visit The Glenloch Tea Factory enjoy the tour but be strongly advised NOT to purchase any tea in their shop.

Title: Interesting place and good tour
Text:
Stopped here on the way to Nuwara Eliya - in the middle of fantastic countryside - and was a fascinating insight into how tea is made. Something we take for granted. The factory and machinery is quite old and it felt like a real working place which we were fortunate enough to see - the whole process was very well explained too. The tour was free and the guide was very nice and informative and there was none of the 'hard sell' that you get at some of these places. Complimentary tea at the end and some nice tea products in the shop. 

We really enjoyed our visit and it was one of the highlights of our holiday.

Title: Loved it!
Text:
It tools us 2:30 hours drive from our hotel in kandy to this place.
The view on the way was spectacular, where u get to see the tea estates, it's all green around you, and if you were lucky as we were, it will rain on the way there.
Once we reached the place, we were greeted by a lovely lady who works there named Ganga.
She took us upstairs and started t explain to us about the entire process taken make tea.
I taped the whole process and it was very interesting to learn about the types of tea that actually exist. Some I never heard of until my visit to the factory, and just before our tour ends, we get into the room, and we're told about the different tea levels, the tea sold in the local market and the tea that is exported.
At the end of the tour we were complimented by a hot cup of tea. That was very yummy. And Im not even a tea drinker.
My husband and I bought some tea gift packages for our loved ones.
They also have a restaurant, in case you were hungry and wanted to have lunch or something. We didn't try it, but the smell of the food was delicious.
You will not be asked to pay for the tour, nor for the tour guide, but we felt that it will be nice to give our tour guide a nice tip, for her friendly way of explaining things to us.

Title: A first time experience in the process of manufacturing tea
Text:
The trip from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya takes you through beautiful water falls and hills where the tea estates are located.
We stoped at Glenloch tea factory, where the guide explained us thoroughly the process of tea manufacturing and how the tea is graded.
Then we were invited to taste a cup of pure tea.
You can buy many varieties of tea, but they are a bit overpriced.
You can enjoy your cup of tea on a beautiful terrace overlooking the tea plantation.
A useful and enjoyable stop on your trip.

Title: Nixe informative tour
Text: Our friendly and knowledgeable guide Rajha gave a great tour of the factory, explaining very well the tea process and giving us a good insight into the types and flavour profiles of the various tea grades.

Title: Engineering tea
Text: Excellent tour to tea factory guided by Siva! We learned alot how tea gets to our cups from the beautiful hills of caylon! Siva was the best guide one could want

Title: Nice
Text: It was interesting tour made by Sallay for us as we are into teas. Very nice little shop where you can purchase amazing teas for reasonable prices. Spent there about 60$ and still think I could purchase more teas for my friends :))) only after this tour I realized how hard it is to pick the tea... i wish it wouldnt be cleaning day only, otherwise it is nice place to visit.

Title: Learn a lot about tea here
Text: This factory is out of town, a tuk-tuk ride of about 1000LKR, but worth it.  The guide is very knowledgeable, and you get to see all the steps of production and learn the different kinds of teas. There is a tasting afterward of the different kinds, and a shop to buy your favorite.  Stay to have another cup and relax and look at the lovely view! Your tuk-tuk driver can be convinced to wait for you!

Title: Awesome
Text: As a tea lover I thoroughly enjoyed this. A special thank you to Raja for his expertise and knowledge he shared. I came with my partner (we are visiting from NZ) and his family who are locals and we all had a really nice time. Recommend this.

Title: Must visit for tea lovers.
Text:
If you are a tea lover or simply interested in the process of making tea, you had better visit. The tour is quite informative and gives you the knowledge for choosing what tea to drink. Also, you can purchase the highest grade tea leaves at a reasonable price. It cost around 1500Rs from and going back to the center of the town of Ella by a tuk-tuk.

Title: Beautiful views
Text: This tea factory was very big and the top floor had an exquisite view. Our tour guide was super informative, had a great sense of humour and the overall experience was more than enjoyable. Would recommend :) !

Title: A must!
Text:
Great informative tour, well presented and so so interesting!  A must when visiting Ella... 
thanks rajhf we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves... 
Mike and Su

Title: Authentic working tea factory
Text: You can just show up and get a 30 minute tour, no need to book in advance from what I could tell. The tea factory is operational, your tour brings you past the workers in all the different stages of processing. Our guide Sallay was extremely knowledgeable and friendly. I learned way more than I ever expected. Of course there are samples as well.

Title: Tea Tea more Tea
Text: An excellent informative trip. How is tea made, how they sort the tea, what leaf do they pick. Mr Siva our tour guide and teacher was excellent. He was the factory manager and had so much knowledge.

Title: Great visit!
Text:
Thank you Rajhn!
I have been to soo many teafactories but this was the first time I understood the differences between qualities, morning, evening teas and also the differences in taste between the parts of the country!
And much more! Thanks to the fact the factory was not working on mondays we got to know much more! You are a super teacher! Thanks!
Brigitte and Eva from Sweden

Title: Very interesting
Text: We had a late evening tour, so the factory was not producing at that time. But our tour guide was very good at explaining everything so accurate that we could imagine the rest. Definitely a great stay through some of the more rainier days in Ella. If you want to see the running factory Phone them first to ask the times.

Title: Guided tour with Mr.Siva - interesting and funny!
Text: We came late in the afternoon and had a private tour with with Mr. Siva. He is super knowledgeable since he has about 40 years of experience in tea production as a technician. Tee was not produced that day, however it was a great experienced and we learned a lot about all aspects of making tee and the pillars of it  (quality, flavor, color and strength :-) ) Tee tasting afterwards with an amazing view into the tee plantations and mountains of Ella.

Title: Worth the visit
Text: My wife and I took the tour with Sallay the guide. It was very educating and interesting. Sallay spoke good English and had a lot of knowledge about the whole tea making proces. Price was around 600 rupees per person if I recall it well.

Title: Visit to Halpewatte Tea Factory today.
Text: I went to Halpewatte Tea Factory this morning for a guided tour and I was very impressed. Our guide was Rajha, who first gave us an introductory talk about the tea plant, how it is picked and how it is processed, before taking us round the factory to show us each stage of the process. He is a very knowledgeable and entertaining guy. The views from the large balcony outside the tea shop part of the factory were just stunning!

Title: Mixed feelings... worker exploitation vs. great tour
Text:
We visited this place during our honeymoon and we have very mixed feelings about it, including how the tea pickers are treated... 

On one hand, our guide Salley - who used to be an employee himself - was informative, accommodating, and took us on a fascinating 30-40 minute tour of the tea factory, ending in a short tea tasting session. 

On the flip side, we were horrified to learn (we only found this out by asking the question) that the tea pickers who are so often glamourised by Halpewatte (and indeed other tea plantations and factories as well, not to mention on the tea packaging itself) earn just +/- $4 a day. $4 to start work every day at 7:30am in the scorching sun, barefoot, picking tea leaves and throwing them into a sack they carry on their backs. The drying room is also so hot and dark that we could not spend more than 1 minute in there - it had to have been the same temperature as a steam room with NO AIR CON. How do the workers survive day in and day out in these conditions?? Plus, the tea pickers will only earn their daily wage if they pick 15kgs of leaves that day. If you put that into perspective, $4 is the approximate price for a small box of Halpe tea in the factory shop. It doesnt add up and its certainly not a fair distribution of the companys clearly massive turnover. We also learned that the local guy who owns Halpewatte also owns the £600-a-night 98 Acres resort where we stayed and the zip line and activity pad nearby. And he cant give his tea pickers more than $4 a day? We were batted down by the reassurance that the government is looking to increase the daily wage to 1000 rupees. Thats approximately $5 a day. Shame on him.

Title: A Must Visit
Text: Mr Siva gave us a comprehensive and informative talk about this Estate and the Sri Lankan Tea industry. We have been on quite a few tea factory tours with various groups, but this was definitely one of the better ones. The factory shop has a good range of teas for sale at reasonable prices. One word of warning if going in wet weather: the driveway to the factory is fairly steep in parts, but the view is lovely from the top!

Title: Great tour, money well spent
Text: I did the tour here & it surpassed my expectations. Siva the tour guide was very passionate & knowledgeable about all aspects of making tea. I walked out much better for it. Well worth the time & effort.

Title: Wonderful and Interesting Tea Factory Tour
Text:
Really wanted to visit a tea factory during my solo trip through Sri Lanka and I heard about this facility.  It was very easy to reach them, especially if youre already in the Ella area.
The tour is really well done because it combines the history of the tea growing industry, and shares with you the practices of how tea is grown, harvested, and processed.  I enjoyed learning how teas are differentiated and classified but by far the best part of the tour was our guide Sallay ... a very knowledgeable and dignified gentleman who made the tour interesting for all the people in the tour, the sweet little children included.  The next best part of the tour for me was just being in the factory watching the dignified workers processing the leaves throughout the entire process.  

The tour took about an hour and you will climb and descend a few flights of stairs so please be sure youre able to climb stairs safely.  Theres a nice gift shop that takes all credit cards and offers some of the most majestic panoramic views imaginable.

Title: Informed tour
Text:
We went on a morning tour and enjoyed it thoroughly.
Planned trip on the Sunday could not go ahead as it was  a poya day.
On the day we went (Mon), tours were taking place, but not as a full working facility. In hindsight that's was better, as it would be very noisy.

After the tour, we sampled tea and could buy at factory prices. Much cheaper than anywhere else we visited to  buy here.

Our guide had very good English and good humour

Title: Tea factory
Text: We were advised to go, and it was definitely worth it. A really great tour by Sallay, could not recommend him highly enough.

Title: Very insightful and Interesting
Text: We thoroughly enjoyed our tour. Very insightful and interesting but to see the working factory in such detail was really great. Siva was our guide and very thorough explaining every detail and also passionate about high quality tea making - he was able to answer every question. Would suggest this tour if youre in Ella and can fit it in, great view from the cafe at the top and lots of products to purchase with absolutely no pressure to buy.

Title: Great tour - learnt loads about tea!
Text: Silva was a fantastic tour guide, very knowledgeable and interesting. Great to see all the different processes of tea making and learn the different types of tea. Cost £2.50 each inc tea tasting at the end. Great shop and cafe at the end without any pressure to buy anything. Would recommend whilst in Ella - particularly good activity for when its raining!

Title: Very informative tour
Text: We took a very informative tour around the tea factory - Siva really knows his stuff and was engaging and friendly! Thanks!

Title: Lovely views
Text: I went out of tea season so the factory was not producing tea. However they still run regular tours of the factory. Tea tasting of the 4 types of black tea they produce and all good quality. The shop sells its tea at really good prices. The drive up was interesting but the view was really lovely so worth a visit

Title: Positeav review
Text: Our host SIVA was very knowledgeable. Had a great tour with him today at the tea factory. Learned a lot of tea and the science behind it. Also, great gift shop at the end of the tour and AHMAZING view.

Title: Sallay was a Wonderful Tour Guide
Text: I had a choice to visit a number of tea factories during my visit in Sri Lanka, however, I chose to visit the Halpewatte Tea Factory and I'm so glad I did.  The factory tour was very impressive ... I had no idea how much effort was put into making tea Sallay, the group's guide was was informative and gave us all a wonderful tour.  He ensured we understood the steps the tea leaves went through in order to become the beverages we enjoy and his explanations were detailed but easy to follow.  It was obvious he enjoys his job at this tea factory and that made me feel especially good to support this facility.

Title: Sensational tour
Text: We visited the factory around midday following our hike up Ella Rock. I was expecting the factory to be non-operational at that time as all the processing happens early in the morning/night (for temperature reasons). We paid 1050 rupee for 2 x adults for an education only tour. Our guide was Siva & he is hands down the best tour guide we have come across. His English is perfect, and his knowledge is incredible. He explains the whole process very clearly & makes you think about how much engineering & production goes into your humble morning cuppa! There is a gift shop at the end but the prices are very reasonable & there is certainly no hard sale. Our Tuk-Tuk cost us 1300 rupee from Ella & included wait time - we felt this was very reasonable as the whole trip probably took about 1.5-2hrs. I would highly recommend this tour to anyone visiting Ella!

Title: Amazing expirience!
Text:
The tour was very interesting with lots of new information. The guide  Salley was so nice, funny, polite, has exellant english and we could feel it was important for him that we will have great time there. 
After this tour we much more  appreciatee our good cup of tea :)
Thank you salley!

Title: Great informative tour
Text:
Great fun tour with Sallay! He really knew his stuff about tea and as went at 9am we saw the production line still going which was so cool!
Learnt about how they make each tea, growing and picking process and of course export to Europe info!
Finished with tasting 4 teas - yummy! 
Would recommend! 
Takes about an hour, not suitable for anyone with a physical disability as very steep stairs and access points.

Title: Great fun!
Text: We visited the Halpewatte Tea Factory on our way to Nuwara Eliya. We took the tea tour - lead by a passionate and insightful expert who took the time to explain the intricacies of tea picking and production, taking in the massive - skillfully engineered - machines and culminating with a tea tasting session. Good fun all round and highly recommended!

Title: Great tour and tea and views
Text:
Go in the morning when the factory is working to see the full production process. The tours go every half hour and finish with a tasting of 4 teas, ending in the shop. The factory is high up so also has great views. Well worth the climb for an informative insight into how your daily cuppa is made. 
Charge for the tour is around 500 rupees.

Title: Great morning tour
Text: We had a great time seeing how they make the tea. We got to see how the machines work then got to try the different types of tea at the end. We did buy some tea :)

Title: Site à visiter absolument
Text:
We visited the factory on a Saturday afternoon. Unfortunately there was no production. The Sivanathan guide was there and he make to us a truly exceptional visit. He knows his subject, he shows us everything and explains it in detail.
Thanks to him we are aware of the whole process of making black tea. Thanks to Sivanathan for the work you do.

Title: Not on a weekend
Text: We visited here on a Saturday as we were passing, which was a bit disappointing as while their website says they were open, no actual staff apart from presentations or the shop, are working. Therefore any descriptions of the process would not be accompanied with action, which we had seen earlier in our trip at Damro Labookellie Tea Lounge, and for free, whereas here they wanted 600 rupees each for the presentation. To be honest being empty on a Saturday it looked a little abandoned and there were not good photo opportunities around the factory for rolling hills of tea bushes.

Title: Great explanations with enthusiastic guide
Text: We had a great visit with a guide from Halpewatte tea factory. Best choice is to grab a tuk tuk and get yourself a ticket inside with a guide from the building. We had a very enthusiastic one that knew all the details about production as well as the engineering behind the machines. You could see the passion of the guide regarding his job while he talked about the factory. They will give you different teas in the end for you to taste the difference of the several types of extractions.

Title: Very interesting, new facts about tea manufacturing
Text: Was there with my mother. Interesting place, very funny and nice guide. We enjoyed and found lot of new information about tea manufacturing.

Title: Tea for two year old
Text:
We were apprehensive that this tour would be a step too far for our two year old granddaughter but she actually got very excited by the tea being produced and was a big hit with the workers.
The guide was very informative and answered questions well. Good value!

Title: Fine dining
Text: Quite a stylish restaurant which serves fab tea and eats. A little pricey compared to others nearby but worth it

Title: Thank you Siv?
Text: Our guide Siv? speaks very good english so we could hear a very interesting story about tea production. He did his best to give us all the necessary information. I recommend this place to visit.

Title: Good tour
Text: 1300rp tuk tuk return from ella. 480 for tour which consisted of talk, tour of the plantation and tea tasting. Was a good thing to do in Ella.

Title: Great tea tour
Text:
We did the tour with Mister Rajha and was very interesting, we learn about all the tea procces in a interactive way.
I highly recommend to do it.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text: Very informative and engaging tour of the tea factory by our knowledgeable guide Rajha. We learnt about how tea is made and were able to see three steps of the process happening within the factory during our 3pm tour. If you wish to see the entire process happening, it is recommended you arrive at 8am.

Title: Great factory tour with Mr. Sallay
Text: We had the best afternoon with Mr.Sallay at this tea factory where he in a vivid and colorful way and with much enthusiasm took us thru the whole process of tea production. We highly recommend having a guided tour with him and to visit this authentic and beautifully located factory.

Title: Visit to the tea factory
Text:
LOVED Siva's intelligent way of explaining the world of tea to us. Would absolutely recommend a visit.
 We walked all the way from Ella to the tea factory which was quite a nice stroll with lovely views.

Title: Siva most amazing tour guide, the best story teller there is
Text:
We had a great tour, Siva was our guide made the tour very interesting.
We asked some of the workers in the fields how much they make and they said that they are supposed to make 1000 rupees a day but that the owners only pay 700. Maybe one day the government will protect those who need it most.

Title: Tour in the Factory
Text: Excellent factory tour in a massive tea factory. Whole process was well explained. At the end of the tour we were given different qualities of tea to taste.

Title: Well worth the trip
Text:
Very interesting to see and hear the tour information. Great views from the top as well. 
Great presentation by the guide.

Title: A great tourguide
Text: We had a great time at this tea factory. The tourguide named Sallah gave us a very good explanation on the proces of teamaking. His english is very good and he really wants to share his great knowledge on tea with you. Afterwards he lets you taste the different types of tea and you can enjoy the view from their balcony overlooking the fields.

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
It's a bit confusing when you arrive here but watch for a vistors sign and head through the factory and up to the top floor to get on a tour
Cost was 500 rupees per person
Interesting tour with a guide who spoke good English and was knowledgeable about the factory 
Great seeing the tea actually being processed 
A nice way to spend an hour or 2.
Get a tuk tuk from Ella- the driver will wait for you

Title: Informative.
Text:
Expect to pay a tuk tuk driver in downtown Ella between LKR 1300-1500 to take you up there, wait for you, then bring you back into town. Round trip about 2 hours including the very informative tour. Entertaining tour guide. A bit like an over-enthusiastic headmaster :)
Naturally, you exit through the gift shop but not before they give you a taste of what youve just seen being made. Prices not bad at all. 
Just a pity we didnt actually get out into the plantation and closer to the beautiful scenery but theres another tea plantation en route and your tuk tuk driver will be only too happy to stop to let you take pics of tea being picked. Worth your time.

Title: Very Informative
Text:
Visited today and was thoroughly entertained and informed by this tour.  Provided an excellent insight into the process.  Much like a wine tasting tour we learned of the different tastes and processes done to reach it.

Bought up in the shop afterwards too for gifts.

Title: Great tea tasting and shop!
Text: This was our second and the better tea factory visit while in Ella, as it ended with a very informative tea tasting session. In addition, they have a tea shop and while the prices may be a litte higher than in supermarkets, they have every immaginable tea variety and grade, freshly packed. The factory is worth a visit for the shop alone.

Title: great tour
Text: We took a tuk-tuk from 98 acres, and visited around 9 as recommended to catch the entire process. Raja was a great guide and talked us through the whole process, answering all our questions. The machinery and production is fascinating, the only machinery that originated in the 20th century was one of the laser sorting machines. And you can up close to all of it. I loved the little office with the guys stamping the product information by hand on the large sacks before dispatch. Much better than the free tour we took at another factory where they whisked us through in 10 minutes to deposit us in the 'cafeteria' (iced donuts) and shop - we didn't buy anything there but were happy to buy our tea at Halpe.

Title: Fascinating afternoon education
Text: This was a fascinating tour with a really interesting and knowledgeable guide. He was able to explain the complex chemical reactions in an accessible way, really felt like wed learnt something ! You also get to taste the different teas afterwards and can buy from the shop

Title: Interesting tour for all the family
Text: We all really enjoyed our visit to the tea factory today. Our guide Raja was really informative and took time to explain all the stages of tea production to our 4 year old daughter - she is now quite the tea expert! The tour starts with a presentation and then you get right up close to the various machines used and are able to touch and smell the tea at the various stages and then taste it too at the end.

Title: Disappointing service
Text: We wanted to get some teas but we being coffee drinkers we needed some help in this area. This was also our only tea factory stop. The staff was not helpful and told us to take the tea tour to get recommendations of the teas that we should buy. As it was a public holiday, the tea factory was not operating and it would not be meaningful for us to take the tea tour.  We relied on whatever information on the back of the tea packaging to decide on our selected tea gifts.  We wanted to shop more but decided to limit our purchase here as the service was a let down,

Title: Extremely interesting tour!
Text:
We did our tour with Sallay who was extremely knowledgeable about the tea-making process.

The tour was very close to the action and you were in an amongst the workers and factory machines as they went about their daily routine.

By the end of the tour we far more knowledgeable about how tea is made and it was great to have this information before the tea tasting and purchase of products from the factory store.

I would definitely recommend this if you are staying in Ella!

Title: Fascinating- a must for tea lovers!
Text: This tour is so interesting, you learn about the process of making tea from picking the tea leaves to exportation in a 1960s factory. Our guide was so entertaining, very passionate about tea and you get to taste different varieties at the end and buy your favourite from the gift shop. Cost 1050 Sri Lankan rupee for 2, tuk tuk from Ella centre return journey 1500. Great afternoon thank you Halpe! ??

Title: Visit at the tea factory
Text: Decided to visit Halpewatte Tea Factory, 10 minutes tuktuk ride from Ella railway station. It was absolutely worth it! Mr. Sallay at the factory gave a professional and thorough presentation of the different steps in the making of tea. You walk around in the production facilities and at the end you can taste and buy some of their products. Visit if you have time!

Title: Eye opening
Text:
I thought I knew how tea was made. I was wrong - the guided tour at the factory was informative and really interesting with it.

This is no antiseptic tour behind glass separated from the action. You actually walk among the workers and see, smell and touch the product all the way from picked tea tips to bagged tea ready to leave the factory.

Each stage was explained and we were even encouraged to put our hands into the fermenting tea to feel how much heat was been given off as the tea oxidised and became the black tea that we are familiar with.

They have equipment in use as old as the hills as well as modern laser sorting machines, so something for all the geeks out there too!

I highly recommend this to anyone who has ever had a cuppa and enjoyed it.

Title: Simple Family Factory
Text: It was very nice. the guide knows his stuff.  excursion is small, about 40 minutes. And after have some tea testing.

Title: "BOPF" for ever! :)
Text:
Now I've got it, with teaspoon, for ever :)
It's the tea leaf grading - and it's the "main grad" for Sri Lanka tea - but also for a lot of other tea producing countries
The meaning for "BOPF":  Broken Orange Pekoe Fannings and I love this tea!
I'm drinking my tea for breakfast only and drinking with milk - therefor it's ok with a strong tea. My lady liked the blend with ginger very much. After tea tasting we went out on the terrace, wow a fantastic view over Ella and right in front of the factory there are the tea plantations. Beautiful, beautiful - and thank you so much for your hospitality, Halpé tea !

Title: Professional Tour
Text: Probably the best put-together tea factory tour in Sri Lanka.  You have to pay (not too much), but you get a knowledgeable guide who takes you through a functioning, operating factory that is pervaded by the heavy scent of tea.  At the end, you get to try 4 varietals.  Incredible views from the balcony off the tasting/waiting room.  A little hard to hear with all the machinery going, so stay close to the guide.  Tours leave every half hour...sort of....

Title: Tea factory tour
Text:
Sallay was super cool guide - best Tea factory in Ella ? so put it on your tick list ?? 

You don't need Discovery Channel to find out HOW IT'S MADE ??

Title: So that's how tea is made!
Text: This tour is really informative. We learned how tea is made and how one factory can produce different strengths of tea all from the same tea bushes (it's all in the grind!). At the end, you get to taste the different teas from the lightest to the strongest. We bought some in the shop and it tastes every bit as good back home as in Sri Lanka. If you like tea, visit this factory. You'll learn a lot! Thanks also to our guide, Sallay. He was friendly and very patient as we asked a lot of questions.

Title: Worth the visit
Text: Tuk tuk cost 700lkr one way from Ella centre. Tour of the factory cost 1050lkr for 2 people. We went on a Saturday and managed to catch the second last tour with active production of tea for the day at 10.30am. There have been mixed reviews of the guides, so we were lucky to have an older gentleman who was interesting and spoke well to be our guide. Detailed explanation of the process, interesting walk through the production areas, and we came away with a greater appreciation of different qualities of tea. There were tastings of 4 tea types at the end. Also worth paying $1/ 180lkr (prices in USD here but you can pay in lkr) to have a cup of tea and enjoy the wonderful views at the cooling balcony after the tour. The higher grades of tea in the foil wrapping are worth a buy at $5 for 250g.

Title: Friendly team and informative tour
Text: We went early around 8am as we wanted to tour the factory while production was still ongoing. Tours continue throughout the day but production ends around 10:30am. We first met one of the guides Raja who was welcoming and entertaining but later were assigned another guide Salley whom we felt equally fortunate to have. He was very patient and generous in sharing about the entire process and operation and kept checking in on whether we understood him or if he was conducting the tour well enough. He did so wonderfully. We learned a lot. We tasted 5 different teas and there was quite a variety to purchase ranging from affordable to the more expensive ones.

Title: Is this place a scam? Is it ever operational?
Text:
We hired a tuktuk driver to take us to Uva Halpewatte tea factory about 6km from Ella. It was a tortuous steep route on poor quality roads. Upon arrival the factory looked odd; there was no tea aroma and all was quiet. We followed semi permanent signs to an upper floor where packaged tea was for sale. We were approached by a lady who stated that no production was taking place on the day. Not at all.uncommon from other reviews!!!

A noticed read that you had to pay the tour fee....even when there was no production. Again odd? She advised that the power was off and this later proved to be true in other locations.

Expensive tea priced in U.S. $ was for sale, but as we discovered later, Sri Lankan tea is a blend and the fancy packaging and prices are just for us gullible tourists.

Western visitors  were ambling about quite aimlessly waiting for a tour to commence. Clearly this factory was no longer operating. The process takes several days and there was no evidence of on going or disrupted production.

Even our tuktuk driver was embarrassed! 

Upon discovering that the Uva Halpewatte tes factory was noy operational, our tuktuk driver took an alternative route back to Ella and brought us to the small Kinellen tea factory. Here for 500rps each the two of us were given a very detailed and interesting tour of the entire process....

Don't waste your time and money visiting the (former?) Tea factory at Halpewatte.

Title: Tourist trap with little substance!
Text:
The factory felt really dead with not much happening, the guide had very strong accent and was extremely difficult to understand, they rush you through the factory so you get to the shop quicker. You get to try 4 teas all of which tasted very similar and little explanation is given as to what the difference it. It was also a huge group which meant you don't get to hear everything being said.
I went for another tea factory tour in the south of Sri Lanka, which was free, much more informative and got to try about 30 types of tea!
Wouldn't recommend it at all

Title: Worth to visit, very well organized and informative tour
Text:
We have visited this factory in January, did not see drying processes, but we saw production line and had tasting of 4 different teas. Introduction was very informative and the speaker was so proud of their product and spoke with passion. Tuk tuk cost 1500 both ways including waiting time and ticket was 525 rupees per person. Lovely tea shop, many different product to choose from.

You can smell tea from the distance, never  imagined flavour is so strong its literally in the air

Title: Great experience
Text: We had a tour of the tea factory around 9.30am with our two little boys. Its started with a small talk about tea which I found very interesting. You then get a tour around the different areas of the factory and the guide explains all the stages in the process of making tea, and even gives you handfuls to smell and feel. You then go and do some tea tasting and are then left to buy any tea. I found the whole tour really interesting and a great way to spend a morning in Sri Lanka.

Title: Wasnt for us
Text: We arrived on a Monday and were advised it was a non production day. The website unfortunately does not indicate days that are scheduled for non production. We found the staff to be somewhat rude and the experience to be disappointing. We did walk here though, and the walk was thoroughly enjoyable- even the last 1.7km which was all uphill.

Title: Probably worth a visit
Text: This is a pretty popular trip out from Ella - it's maybe about 7km by road, and around 1500LKR for return tuktuk ride (you can hike it if you're keen, but it's mostly along relatively busy roads!)  The factory wasn't operational on the day we visited, which was a shame as I can imagine the noise and smell would be incredible!  Instead we were given an interesting and informative lecture about tea from a local worker, then shown round the factory with demonstrations of how the different bits of plant (that manage each part of the process) work.  It was pretty interesting, and probably worth the $3 entry, but would have been a lot better when operational.  It was also very busy with tourists when we visited, so it might be worth planning your timings - we arrived for a 10.30 tour and there must have been 50 people in our group, which was way too many - the tour 1.5 hours later was much quieter, and in retrospect we'd have been better waiting.

Title: Very informative
Text: This tea factory charged us 3US per person but it was definitely worth it. A few days prior we went to Bluefields which was free. There is no comparison Halpewatte tour was so much more informative, we learnt a lot and even had our questions understood and answered. You need to go early in the morning though if you want to see the tea being processed.If you are more interested in drinking tea in pretty surrounds and not learning much Bluefields is probably better option.

Title: Excellent visit and Tour
Text: When you are in Sri Lanka this is a must particularly if you want to know about tea. Mr Siva presented our tour, he was engaging, knowledgeable and was able to share the delights of Sri Lankan grown tea with a worldwide audience. I loved it and wished i could have seen some production. Well worth a visit.

Title: Fun and informative
Text: It is quite a trip through quite small roads to get from Ella. Trip should cost no more than 600 Rupees. The tour cost 525 but was worth it. Our guide gave us an extended explanation of how the tea was picked and processed. After this we were shown inside the factory, which was very interesting. I really understand a lot more about tea now.

Title: Great for a visit, good shop to buy tea
Text: Really enjoyed my visit here, the view is amazing, I just sat and looked at the view and relaxed for ages. Also enjoyed browsing the shop, lots of teas to choose from, taste and buy. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Informative, interesting
Text: We arrived and had to wait upstairs until enough visitors justified a guided tour. The gentleman that then briefed us and escorted us around the working tea factory did so with enthusiasm and knowledge. It takes maybe 40 mins, and then you return to the shop area for free samples and an opportunity to buy selected teas. It was very worthwhile and I learned much about how Tea is produced - you see every stage from freshly picked leaf through to packaging for wholesale.

Title: Under maintenance
Text: My partner and I were looking forward to see a tea factory and unfortunately at that time it was under maintenance.... We managed to talk to the manager and had a chat and some tea with him instead..he was friendly and super helpful with information .... He was informative and gave us the process of tea making in theory... We managed to get some delicious affordable green tea.

Title: A must when in Ella
Text: We visited on a non production day but it was still extremely interesting and informative. The tour takes about 1 hour and they explain in detail the process from picking the tea leaves till it's ready for export. Entrance was 1050 rupees for 2 people.

Title: Enthusiastic guide, interesting behind the scenes tour
Text:
We really enjoyed our tour of Uva Halpewatte tea factory.

There is a narrow, steep concrete track up to the factory, so I would strongly recommend a vehicle to get up there.
Once at the top you are rewarded with excellent views across the surrounding hills.

There are several flights of stairs to ascend up to the ticket office and tea shop.
Our ticket fee was 1050LKR for two people. We waited around 10 minutes for the next tour. Us and a group of about 10 were greeted by our tour guide at 10.30, the whole tour took about an hour.

We had arrived on a production day, so were able to see all the stages of tea production in action.
The guide was very informative and enthusiastic, talking and walking us through the whole process from freshly plucked leaf to packaging.
Once the tour was complete we were taken back through to the shop area where we tasted samples of the 4 stages of tea produced, from light green through to strong black.

Would definitely recommend a visit here.

Title: Disappointing
Text: As others have mentioned it is difficult to find out if te production is happening on the day and time you want to visit. We went in the morning as we were told this was the best time to see the tea production. We arrived to be told production had finished so in reality it was just an expensive tuk tuk ride. They do have a website but it doesn't have any information regarding production days and times.

Title: Great tour!
Text:
It's not so easy to get a lot of information before you arrive. We ended up showing up on a non-operational day unfortunately as there was a random public holiday we didn't know about, the only negative.

However, Rajha was a very informative tour guide, and manged to joke around with the group as well which was much appreciated! The tour was very thorough and insightful and we got to see parts of the factory I hadn't expected to. We then combined our new found knowledge with some tea tasting at the end in the beautiful tea shop. The views are worth it alone! Overpriced tea in the shop, but expected for a major tourist attraction.

Title: Informative Tour
Text:
My wife and I needed to do a tea tour whilst in Ella and a tuk tuk driver brought us here! Great choice!
The man leading the tour was clearly passionate about tea and had the expertise to get across all the information in an easy to understand format.
Unfortunately for him, he was the only tour guide working that day which meant he had larger tour groups, making it difficult for everyone to hear when there were machines running on certain parts of the tour. But he battled on and we felt we got a good deal of information about the tea making process from him.

Title: History of Tea
Text: We thoroughly enjoyed being guided through the tea making process with inside knowledge of what just goes into making that perfect afternoon sip.

Title: Learn something new each day
Text:
This was a great tour. To understand how tea is produced, the process of it and understanding the different flavours that Sri Lanka produces.

A great host and very good tour

Title: Interesting to hear about the science of tea
Text:
We came to Ella to visit tea plantation country. Although we enjoyed our visit to tea factory I am glad that this was not the main event. 

The tour is done in groups. It starts off with a talk about tea which we really enjoyed, however do be aware it is enirely focused on the tea production (very little on the history of the tea plantations). The talk was around 20 minutes, and after that we got to see the factory production process. I wasnt expecting it all to be in operation, but just in case you are, do be aware that a lot of the tea production you see happens in very small pockets. I suspect it is mostly used for tourism now rather than real, large scale tea production.

Unfortunately we didnt get to go out to the fields. I think that is okay as for one thing you are surrounded by tea in Ella anyway, and it is the factory rather than the plantations that is advertised.

For 500 or so rupees this place is worth a visit. However, I think they coud happily charge a bit more and tell you more about the history of tea production there, including the economic and social history. I am sure it is really very interesting and must have transformed that part of Sri Lanka.

Title: False information!
Text:
Disappointed to write this, but people need to be informed.
I was looking forward to seeing the tea plantation, as we'd been to Vietnam, and visited a coffee plantation.
Our homestay owner actually rang the factory to see if production was on, and they said yes. But, on getting a tuk tuk and travelling to here, we arrived and there was no production, but you could still pay to look round. A pointless payment as no explanation for the machines or how tea was produced. A real shame!

Title: Super interesting and authentic
Text: We enjoyed the tour with Rajha a lot! He has been working for the factory for 40 years and knows everything about plantation, harvesting, sells, quality.. No question was unanswered. The shop is really cute and the view great.

Title: Good tour
Text: Did a tour here, interesting to hear how the tea is being produced. I expected to also go through the plantations (don't know why) but that's not the case, just the factory. Beautiful view from the tasting area. The tour was 900 for 2 people I think.

Title: Excellent tea factory tour
Text: Came here in a group of 5 adults today for a tea factory tour. Rajha was an excellent guide - very informative and engaging. Able to tour all of the factory - hands on experience. Would highly recommend.

Title: Informative tour
Text: For 480 SLR you can join a group tour which will bring you through the factory and explain the art of making tea. Unfortunately, we had quite issues with understanding our guide but were able to translate under each other in the group. All in all it was a nice experience, the only pity was that we didn't go into the tea fields it self but if you really want to do this you probably can do so on your way to the factory.

Title: Interesting - even for a non tea drinker
Text: Ok, so I think tea tastes like a handful of grass in hot water, but I drank tea in Sri Lanka, just like coffee in Colombia. It was good, with sugar, but the tour and lecture was very interesting. Worth going but check it is a production day. I didnt feel comfortable to ask about the environmental impact and the chap lecturing us mentioned how they keep the workers happy...by allowing 25% bad leaves in there bags. Hmmmmm.

Title: Highly recommended!
Text: Of the two tea factories I visited in Sri Lanka, I can definitely say that this one was the best. We had a very knowledgeable guide who took us on a very informative tour, and was able to answer our many questions. All in all, it was a good experience, especially for someone who loves tea!

Title: Interesting
Text:
If you haven't already done a tour in Nuwara Eliya, this will be a good opportunity to do so. The tour guides are very friendly and explain the process clearly. Although you probably won't be able to see the whole process during the tour, it will give you a good idea how it works. Afterwards you can taste the different teas and there's a little shop as well. 
The road to the factory is beautiful, so enjoy!

Title: Informative tour with stunning views
Text:
Took a tuk tuk from Ella town centre up a very steep hill to get to this factory. It wasn't production day (due to them not picking on a Sunday) but it was still very interesting. Entry was $3 per person. Our guide explained the whole process, showing us the machinery and taking us around the factory. It ended with a tea tasting session which helped to understand how the process effects the taste. 

Shop is great for presents and they accept credit card.

P.s if you're getting a tuk tuk pay for a return journey, they will wait for you. Otherwise you're not getting back! Return was 1400 rupees

Title: Really enjoyable tour - made by the guide
Text: We visited this factory by Tuk Tuk from Ella. The factory is in a beautiful setting and had a really nice shop/viewing point at the very top of the factory. Tour was reasonably priced and very informative. Our guide was an absolute legend, engaging, informative and funny. He took us through the whole process over about 40mins. Only thing it was missing was a visit out to the fields. Loads of fun.

Title: Fun and interesting visit
Text:
We visited the factory on a Tuesday morning at 10 am to make sure that we were on a production day.
I indeed read that one should avoid Sundays as well as Mondays (the machines dont operate on Mondays since no tea leaves are picked on Sundays). Furthermore, its a good idea to go in the morning to make sure visits are interesting (according to some reviews, sometimes the machines dont operate anymore in the afternoon).
The guided tour was fun with some interesting explanations in the beginning of the tour, classroom style. The English accent of the guide wasnt always easy to grasp, but he was passionate and nice with the kids.
A special mention to the view of the surroundings from the top of the factory.

Title: An interesting commercial-tea factory tour
Text:
Halpewatte Tea Factory is one of the big players in the Uva region.  It is not the easiest place to get to (about 35 minutes from Ella, largely up-hill) but the views from the factory and the tea shop/café are stunning.

As guests staying at 98 Acres, we did not have to pay for the hour long tour and on the day we visited, the factory was in full operation.
