Our tour guide was well-versed in the manufacturing process and was able to step us through the different qualities of tea produced.  The day before, we had visited Amba Estate (a small, organic plantations; check out my separate review) so it was fascinating to see the other end of the industry on such a large commercial scale.

The tour ended with a tea tasting and there was a huge range of product available to purchase.  Very worthwhile, but make sure the factory is running before you visit.

Title: Interesting despite no production day
Text:
No production day meant most of the machines weren't working. However, I still found the hour-long tour (480 per adult ticket regardless of whether production or non-production day) really interesting. 
The views across are very impressive, and yes it is about an hour to walk there. Athough a little steep, I found myself wandering past farms growing vegetables and could more easily see tea-pickers which would all fly by if you took a tuk tuk. Walk there if you can!

Title: Informative tour and tea tasting
Text:
This was surprisingly one of our favorite activities during our trip in Sri Lanka. We learned about all aspects of the tea processing within the factory and what distinguishes the quality of different teas. We were allowed to visit the production areas while in progress.
Afterwards we got to try examples of the teas.
The tasting room also features stunning views of the valley.
Getting there was very easy by public bus, we just took the bus towards Kumbalwela. We asked a local selling fruit where to catch the bus. The bus will drop you off right at the bottom of the driveway, just tell the ticket information guy you're going to the tea factory, they'll tell you where to get off. It's a 1km scenic walk up the hill, but there are also plenty of tuk tuks around if you don't wish to walk.

Title: Interesting tea factory tour
Text: Visited Uva Halpewatte Tea Factory, Badulla Road, Hela Halpe, Ella, Sri Lanka in July. You pay for the tour whilst many other Factories offer free tours (1000rps) no need to book just turn up and get on next tour the tour guide knows his stuff but does speak incredibly fast so hard to catch everything. You get a really good understanding of the tea process and its interesting to see the whole thing. Thoroughly enjoyed the tour and tasting. You can buy lots of tea (in $or Rps) probably cheaper than in the local shops. One disappointment, I was expecting to see tea pickers working on the pristine slopes around the factory almost like a Boudreaux style winery visit but there isnt much tea around the factory so youll have to get those pics elsewhere.

Title: Informative well organised tour
Text:
The introductory talk was very interesting, we learnt a lot about different types of tea, and the history of tea production. The walk through the factory was fascinating, seeing quite old machinery as well as very modern equipment.
The tea tasting afterwards was delicious and the view from the cafe was beautiful.

Title: Decent tea tour
Text: We did a morning tour on an off production day, so the operation itself was nothing too  impressive to see. That said, our host was very knowledgeable, great with kids, and we all left with a bit more tea savvy then we arrived with. Would recommend this as an activity to do if youre in Ella for more then a few days. Otherwise, we found the tour in Nuwara Eliya more interesting (up close with insanely beautiful deck views) and some waterfalls to boot.

Title: A typical tea factory with nice view
Text:
Nice tea factory as many in Sri Lanka. Positive very nice people and relatively inexpensive tea, but a longer tour uphill. 
Take a cup of tea, you have to pay for it, and enjoy the view from the balcony.

Title: Old historical tea factory
Text:
A tea factory is a must visit while in Srilanka! They produced a black tea, so after all the explanation about how the tea was made we had a tea tasting. Interesting experience and youll have a bit of knowledge about tea. 
They have a small cafe where you can order tea and snacks with a beautiful view of the mountain. Some people came to this place with the kids, some are couples. Everyone enjoyed the session I think. I just dont remember how much it cost.

Title: Amazing experience well worth the journey
Text: Rajha gave us the most interesting and informative tour of the whole factory even parts not currently being used for production and a great overview if everything we could want to know about tea. Would highly recommend and the views from the factory are stunning

Title: Fascinating
Text: We really enjoyed our visit to this tea factory. Its in a very picturesque setting, and the tour itself is great. The guide had a great sense of humour, and we learned about all the stages of making tea, seeing each step along the way. It takes about an hour to do the tour plus tasting and theres a shop if youd like to purchase some tea at the end. Its possible to walk there but worth taking a tuk tuk as its very steep to get there and quite a few kms.

Title: Guided tea tour
Text: We walked to the tea plantation from Ella, last 1.7 km was strap climbing. I recommend to take a tuk-tuk. Good side was that views where beautiful. I didn't mind the walk. Tour was interesting, lot of new information. Factory was running, you could see how everything is done. Finally we also got to taste four different teas. You can also buy tea from the factory.

Title: Intresting tour!
Text:
Came on a Monday so no production going on, but the tour was super interesting anyway. They go through all the steps from picking the leaves to shipping it off to the market.
the factory itself is old and really beautifully situated on top of a hill.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Uva Halpawatte Tea Factory was about a 4-5 km hike from my guest house and i had decided that this would be the one that i would be taking the guided tour. I hiked up the hill on a Monday as the guidebook informed me that it was not in production in Sundays, but i was disappointed as there was no production today either as it was some sort of holiday. However i took the tour and the guide explained about the process. Afterwards i sampled 4 different teas and was allowed to choose one and sat on the terrace outside on the top floor where there was a terrific view of the surrounding area.

Title: Very informative tour
Text: We arrived at Halpewatte tea factory by tuk tuk from Ella and followed the footprints upstairs to the start of the tour. The tour cost 600 rupees each and was well worth it. Our group had a very informative guide who explained the process clearly. We were able to see each process in action except the initial drying process. Tour lasted about half an hour and then there was a chance to taste 4 different types of tea and of course a chance to purchase.  We walked back down the drive and caught a bus back to Ella for 20 rupees-cheaper than a round trip in a tuk tuk and the walk through the farm lands was enjoyable and interesting.

Title: Much better than expected!
Text:
After reading pretty average reviews of most tea factory tours we finally gathered courage and went to this one. And we were really happy we did. The tour was not rushed, it was informative and we were even allowed to take quite a few pics despite the many no-photo signs. The tea tasting at the end was informative as well - and the tea tasty. 
The shop was nice, too and the staff not pushy at all. 
It's not the rainy season yet so they don't pick tea every day which means that the factory doesn't produce every day. We were informed of this by a very pleasant woman on arrival. We still did the tour and at the end tea bags did arrive so we did end up seeing a bit of production. I'm giving it five stars which might be a tad high but it was just such a positive surprise.

Title: A bit boring if truth be told
Text:
It was okayish and we enjoyed the tuk tuk ride from Ella but the tour was a bit of an anticlimax. Bottom line is tea isnt really that interesting but I guess one feels when in Rome etc etc. Our guide was knowledgeable but it was hard work understanding what he was saying above the noise but it was ( quite) interesting tasting the different types from one plant.
Tea was expensive to buy as a souvenir in the shop...far better to buy from Ella.
If you really want to visit a tea factory and love tea..enjoy...I guess its just not my sort of thing.

Title: Great visit
Text: Just what we wanted. Easy access 1500r tuk-tuk (duff knees, we couldnt have walked) from Ella. Great (approx 40min) 9.30am tour, excellent guide, great to see the machines in use, with factory women actually working as we were taken through. Felt and smelled the tea at various production stages. Understand the four principles now (no spoiler), as we had the four tastings. Bought two packs Rose Tea. The main reason we went to Ella: bucket list tick.

Title: disappointing
Text: No production on the monday we visited which means no tour as we were informed by the none too pleasant lady in charge. We wandered off by ourselves and looked at the fields, bought a cup of tea then went to visit a green tea plantation which was much nicer. Good views from the cafe/gift shop.

Title: Most interesting
Text: Surprisingly engrossing, normally not my cup of tea (ha) but a very interesting tour. Make sure you stand close to the guide when he's talking, can be difficult to hear

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
Our group of 4 had some trouble getting tuk tuks here from Ella for some reason - must have picked a quiet time of day - but eventually found a couple that wanted 1500 each. More than previous reviewers had suggested but we werent in a position to negotiate. Trip is shorter than expected - walkable though steep - but fun in the tuk tuk.

Bit strange when we arrived as you have to walk up lots of steps through a seemingly deserted factory, but checked in and paid at reception on the top floor and didnt have to wait long for the tour. We were there at 9am on a production say so there was a lot of activity and the tour was very informative and clear. Ive been to a few tea factories and plantations in carious countries but still enjoyed it. The tour, including a quick tasting at the end, took about an hour.

I was disappointed that a walk though the plantation wasnt included or an option, hence the four stars, but otherwise highly recommended.

Title: PG Tip-top
Text:
Such a good way to spend a couple of hours in the morning in Ella. The tour was cheap and ran every half an hour, we had to wait around 10 minutes when we arrived and spent this on the breath taking viewing platform.
The tour guide was incredibly knowledgeable, and we really took away a lot of facts about tea production! The factory was in full use which was great to see and walk around. The tea tasting at the end was a nice touch. 
Highly recommend this tour.

Title: Interesting and informative!
Text:
Tours left every 30mins. Tour guide spoke good English and clearly passionate about tea. 
Were able to see most of the tea machines in action. 
Would recomment getting tuk tuk from Ella and for a return trip for 1200 rather than one way (we did this way and more expensive).

Title: Informative
Text: I went on a guided tour in this factory. Unfortunately the production of the day was already finished when we got there (11:30). We were told that this varies between the days. We still decided to get an information tour. The guide explained the different steps of tea production in a nice way. Luckily for us there was still some production going on in some parts of the factory. At the end we got to taste some tea. The factory is located in a really nice area with a great view. We took a tuctuc to get there. The price for the tour was 450 rupees. The tea sold at the plantation is more expensive than the ones you can buy in the city center.

Title: Really interesting -   Even if non-production day!
Text:
We visited late on a Saturday, when production had already stopped for the week. Initially a bit disappointed, we decided to take the tour anyway and were glad we did. Our guide was hugely informative and we learnt loads about tea production and were given an opportunity to taste the different blends at the end of the tour.

If you can go early on a weekday, make an effort to do so and youll catch the factory in full flow :)

Title: Really interesting
Text: Very nice lady took us through the whole tea processing procedure.  Seeing the workers in the fields reminded you of how famous Ceylon tea is and how we all take it for granted when you realise how hard it must be for the workers to pick their 30 kilos!  Quite iconic when you see them in their working gear including baskets strapped to their forehead.

Title: Interesting with right expectations
Text:
The guide Siva was really a tea enthusiast and well experienced and it was interesting to learn about the tea process. 
The factory was partly in operation which we knew. Tour ended with tea tasting. 

If you go, take the guided tour, otherwise it will be useless to go there. Guide 450 rps p/p and tuktuk 2x600.

Title: wonderful and very informative visit.
Text: Make sure you pay a visit to this factory. the tour is so informative and entertaining and absolutely worth the trip.

Title: Good and Very informative !
Text:
The tour was very good and only cost 450lrs pp. however try and make sure you go on a day when production is up and running. 

Great views from the factory! 

A Tuk Tuk will be 1500LRS for a a wait and return.

Title: Disappointing
Text: Unfortunately we went on a Monday when there was no production going on as no picking on a Sunday . It is a bit of an expensive tuk tuk ride for not a lot to see. Maybe better when in operation, but dont have to purchase ticket to go in and buy some tea if you dont want to listen to the talk, which we didnt as there wasnt much to see .

Title: Fascinating tour
Text: We enjoyed a fascinating tour of this tea factory, learning how the different types of tea are made and tasting the difference. We bought some tea to take home and have loved drinking it and reminiscing about our holiday.

Title: Nice tour!
Text: Would definetly recommend taking the tour while visiting Ella. We paid 700 rs to get there and 600 to get back with tuktuk. The tour itself was 450 rs. You can buy freshly made tea for a really good price!

Title: This is a scam
Text: I don't understand the reviews of these other people here. This place feels like a scam. The tour costs 450 rupees and the factory was only in half operation(?). Do yourself a favour and not come here. Visit the tea plantations in Nuwara Eliya instead, where tea is really made. Tour there is free and it is authentic.

Title: Too late for seeing production but it was worth it anyway
Text: We ended up getting there too late to see actual production bit the tour we had was brilliant. He explained everything and took us around the factory even turning on some machines to demonstrate. Yes it would have been better to see it in action but can't fault them for that. Shop is cute and reasonably priced and the staff are all lovely. A little out of the way so watch you aren't ripped off for tuk tuks as they can get thin on the ground when you're leaving. Overall very good.

Title: Awesome and detailed tour
Text: Our tour guide was very thorough and passionate about the tea making process and spent a good amount of time explaining the purpose of each step through the factory.  The view from the tasting room balcony was just incredible, as the factory sits at the top of a hill.  The tea is cheap to purchase in their small store as well.  It is amazing to think that this factory has been making tea for 100+ years!

Title: Very educational!
Text: My husband and I enjoyed our tour very much. The guide was friendly, knowledgeable, and enthusiastic. Tea tasting at the end was nice. You can purchase tea at a very cheap price in the little shop. It's also a beautiful area to walk through.

Title: Is that a joke?
Text:
We arrived after a 600 rupees drive by Tuktuk. We asked the driver before getting in if the factory was open, he said yes. Dont ever ever believe what they tell you, its all about the money!
The factory was empty and no production becauseit was Christmas...okay...actually it was Sunday and they never work on Sunday, I mean, thats totally normal, everyone deserves to rest one/two days in the week..but why do they say its because of Christmas and why dont they do nothing against these lying Tuktuk drivers! Soon, nobody will come up there anymore!
There was nothing, only a tiny shop. No chairs, no decoration, no sign of recent activity...nothing! A tour was buyable for 500 rupees per person..in an abandoned factory, with some very old tea leaves (smelt like straw..)? no thanks! Dont go!

Title: Great visit with great guide
Text: A small and winding road leads up to this pretty big tea factory just outside Ella. We came in the afternoon just before closing time so part of the factory was not running. We still took the tour which was really interesting. Our guide explained the full process of making tea and we saw all the different machines. We tried some tea at the end and visited their small shop. Only the view is worth the ride.

Title: Great tour
Text:
Enthusiastic and knowledgable guide took us around a tour of this tea factory. Interesting and cool to see how freshly picked leaves become tea. Somewhat dated but spotless factory added some character.

We visited on December 26 - one day after a public holiday - which meant production was very limited so unfortunately limited activity in the factory (in the already low season for tea harvest) - nonetheless still absolutely worth the visit.

Title: Very informative and enriching
Text:
My guide was very knowledgeable, and he was very detailed in his explanation about the history and whole tea making process which I found to be a delightful experience. He also showed us around the factory, they were having production that day (i went on a Tuesday).

I took a bus from Ella to hela halpe (bus direction towards Badulla), which cost 20lkr. The walk up the slope took about 20mins but if you've conquered Ella rock and mini adam's peak this will be nothing. Return trip was any bus towards Ella in the opposite direction for the same fare.

Title: Amazing
Text:
Factory not running on a Monday, can still have a tour and visit the shop. We were glad to go when it was quiet, we were still.shown all the machines etc. 
Just 300lkr each! Definitely tip the guides as they're super knowledgeable and really make the trip! Tasting at the end was good and the shop was cheap to take away your fave!

Title: Very informative
Text: Rajha is very knowledgeable and was able to answer any questions any of our tour group had. The stairs are the reason for my 4 star review as I visited with my parents who are in their seventies and they aren't as nimble or as fit as they once were. With the tour starting on the top level, going down 3 floor levels and then having to climb back to the top to end was hard going. Also the level of lighting made it difficult. We did enjoy our visit however and having to only pick one or two teas to take home was very difficult!

Title: Good tea factory tour, even on non production day
Text:
Really enjoyed visiting this tea factory. However when we arrived we were told it was a non production day (before we bought tickets). This was a Monday-because no tea is picked on a Sunday so there is nothing to process on a Monday. We decided to do the information tour anyway, as the tuk tuk was 1100 rps return, from just outside Ella town. We were pleased we did-don't think it made much difference, as he turned machines on anyway to show us, and they were still packaging and sorting some tea so we got to see part of it in action. And I think it would have been very noisy to hear the tour anyway if all the machines had been on!! 

Good explanations and tasting at the end, for only 300rps each!

Title: Best tour guide in factory
Text:
It was our 3rd factory that we visited, but this trip was the most informative off all.
Special thanks to our tour guide - Rajha, who has big knowledge and explained us everything, answering all our additional question. He has long experience in tea producing market so he freely tell you all the details connected with it. 
You can reach tea factory by walking, just take the shortcut, not use the main road. 300lkr per person or 2$

Title: Great tour for understanding tea production
Text:
Really enjoyed the tour round the tea factory. They take you through the whole process from where the leaves come in to packaging it up in sacks. Guide was really informative with excellent English, views from the balcony at the top were beautiful. 
Tour is excellent value at 300 rupees and there is no pressure to buy tea at the end, although they have a huge choice.
I got a tuktuk to the factory (it's up a huge hill) then walked down to get the bus back to Ella.

Title: Interesting tea factory tour
Text: Try to go there early in the morning (we went at 8.30am) on a weekday when the factory is up and running and you can see the tea manufacturing in progress. It is a really interesting tour, tea making involves more than we thought. At the end of the tour you can taste the different teas.

Title: Fascinating Tour, Amazing Views
Text:
Having read the reviews I went to Halpewatte with quite low expectations, which is perhaps why I thought it was so good.  

We took a tour at 2.15pm - it lasted a full hour and we got to see a lot of the factory floors still in operation which was really interesting.  The guide was extremely knowledgeable and clearly enjoyed taking people around.  The views from the top balcony where the tour starts and ends are simply incredible.

Title: Worth it
Text:
Takes one hour. Quaint factory. Stunning scenery. 
Very good tour and informative about the tea process. 
15 mins from Ella just do it...

Title: Great views
Text: The views were so nice from the top floor. Tour was ok. Bit confusing when you arrive as to where to park and where to go. Tea was ok but much cheaper in town

Title: The best the factory
Text:
We visited several tea factories on Sri Lanka. If you really want to know everything about tea process, the Halpe is the best one. Is it the most informative guide. They take you into the inside (no just step in front of the line), you can touch and smell tea in different stages of preparation.

But not so good, if you want just to buy tea.

Title: Interesting tour - well worth a visit
Text: Siva, the very knowledgeable tour guide, gave us an in depth explanation about how tea is farmed and made, and about the different types of tea. His talk was very informative and he also showed us round the factory so we could see the process of how the tea is made. At the end we had the chance to taste different varieties of tea. Beware though, this tour may increase your tea drinking habit when you are back home!

Title: Ella highlight!!
Text: Highly recommend this place. About a 10-15 minute drive out of the main town of Ella. We drove our own tuk tuk so we don't know the cost. The factory tour was only 300 LKR and the guy taking it was very friendly and happy to answer questions. Tours run every 30 minutes between 8am and 4pm but make sure you go early to see the factory in full swing as the tea production is finishing around 1pm.

Title: Learned a lot!
Text: More interesting than I expected and quite well done. I would go in the morning so you can see them processing and packing the tea. We went at 11, and they were still going strong. Reasonably priced and I'm glad we went.

Title: Fab tour very informative! Highly recommend!
Text: Visited with a friend, very friendly staff, excellent informative tour given by Siva! Lovely shop with stunning views over Ella landscape, would highly recommend when visiting Ella, very reasonably priced! ?? thanks again Siva!

Title: Interesting learning experience
Text: We enjoyed our tour of the tea factory and learned a lot about the process of making tea. We went on a Monday and it was not running at the time but it was still a good tour. Our guide, Siva, knew everything about tea!

Title: Awesome tour
Text: My mom, sister, and I had an awesome tour at the Halpewatte Uva Tea Factory. Rajah was funny, informative, energetic, and made the tour truly memorable! He really is a king of tour guides. Definitely worth the visit, even though we weren't there during production time!

Title: A must when in Ella!
Text: After visiting a green tea factory directly in Ella, I didnt expect much. BUT: only the view from the top floor of the factory is breathtaking, the tour was funny and interesting, tea tasting as well - not only that I broadened my horizons, I got completely into tea now! Maybe it is thanks to the best guide in Sri Lanka - Siva - his English is fluent, you will have a lot of fun and he will even prologue the tour if you have too many questions (like I had...). So overall: you have to go there and ask for Siva!

Title: Interesting
Text: We came just around closing time - but a nice guy gave us a tour anyway. He explained the different teas and you can taste them and then we saw the production. He also explained some of the history. It was a nice visit, so stop by if you are in the area.

Title: Interesting
Text: We took the opportunity to enjoy a tour around the tea factory and sample some of the tea. It was a good insight into how the tea is made from leaf to shop and a good hour or two spent.

Title: Good time
Text: The tour was very nice. The guide spoke quite fast but was very knowledgable and could answer any question. The tea factory was quiet as it was the slow season but it was still really interesting to see the machinery and processes. The tea itself is much cheaper in stores so save a buck and don't buy it there. I had a great time!

Title: Worth a visit!
Text:
Tour itself lasts approx 45mins. Started with guide explaining the tea making process,dif types of tea etc and then brought us through the 3 floors of the factory.
I was in a group of about 15 so it was difficult to hear anything with the machines working but still very interesting to see it in operation.
We arrived at 915am and it was busy enough with tours already ended. 
You then get to sample some teas at the end overlooking some beautiful views. Be warned,the smell of tea is quite overpowering!
Nice,cheap,simple tour. Worth an visit.

Title: Informative
Text: It was an informative visit and worth the detour. The guy who presented knew his stuff. It starts by sitting you classroom style, giving you samples of tea leaves at different stages and then he walks you through the factory. At the end they take you back to where you started and there is a gift shop 9they are no pushy about you buying their tea).

Title: Interesting information about tea processing
Text: Unfortunately we arrived in dry season July until September and missed the mashines running. But the very versatile guide explained every detail about tea and tea drying, rolling and so on  in undestandable words. He let the machines start to show each part of the whole process. Very helpful and interesting tea manufacturing.

Title: Not a tourist trap. Genuine tour by people truly proud of their factory
Text:
If you want to do a tea factory tour- Halpewatte has to be it. The tour guide was enthused by tea and despite the huge number of tours he must of conducted he has lost no enthusiasm. It was a genuine pleasure to be part of the Halpewatte tour. You get to see everything and walk amongst a working factory. The guide is more than happy to answer any question and is vastly knowledgable. 

I would caution you to check that the factory is operational on the day you visit to get the most out of it. The tour was fascinating and as a big tea drinker i left ashamed of how little i had known about the tea making process.

A local school were visiting Halpewatte at the same time which gives you an indication as to what high esteem the place is held in. Many factory tours you are treated as an additional revenue stream- not here.

Title: Highly informative, and guide was entertaining!
Text:
We were brought to this tea factory by our host. Initially I was expecting to be ripped off, and be given a really lousy tour.. BUT that all changed when Rajha introduced himself to us. Rajha was educational, and lively in his presentation!

I loved it when he took a bunch of teas en route to processing and tosses it back in like a boss. Overall, i'd highly recommend going to this seeing that it's only 3USD per person, well worth it!

Title: Really good! Rajha was great!
Text:
We are not the biggest connoisseurs and we went to the tour with people that had had a bad experience in a tea plantation tour.

However, Rajha was great! He did a great job of explaining how tea plants are farmed , picked, the different variations of tea in Sri Lanka, a good tour of the processing of tea leaves and generally a very good hands on experience!

He was more than happy to asnwer questions and help us buy tea from the shop. You can sense he is passionate about tea and loves to share his passion with people

Title: Informative and Entertaining
Text: Not being a tea enthusiast, I had no set expectations of this tour, however, I was very pleasantly surprised.  I had no idea about how much there was to know about the process of growing, harvesting and selling (so many varieties) tea.  A big thanks to our guide Rajha who made the experience such a joy. His passion was infectious and  entertaining and his knowledge unquestionable.  I would recommend this tour to all as a great way to spend an hour or so.

Title: Great tour
Text: An excellent tour run by a very knowledgable man. Engaging for both ourselves and our 3 young children. We now have a far greater appreciation of the complexity of tea making and the tea tasting at the end was interesting and enjoyable. Worth the trip out of Ella, the road is narrow and steep!

Title: Hidden Gem
Text: We went to the Halpe Tea Factory whilst we were in Ella and we're pleasantly surprised with how good the tour was! When we arrived we were informed that the production had stopped and it seemed like the factory was deserted with not much action taking place. We decided to go on the tour as we were there and costs 300 rupees per person. There is a tour every 30 minutes and they try and keep the groups small (we were in a group of 5). Our tour guide was Chandra and he had worked in the tea industry for 40 years and decided to do tours after he retired- and now we know why! He was the tea master and had so much knowledge about the whole process, he made the 30 minute tour very interesting with lots of history and practical aspects of the tour (we had to smell every stage!). We highly recommend having him as a guide and when we actually started the tour the factory wasn't shut as the tea making process is 24 hours, there was only 1 section that wasn't working but we go to see everything else and the staff busying away. We were very impressed with the factory and bought some of the local tea made on site- 500 rupees per box. We heard this tour is better than most others by the information you are told and how it is delivered- definitely worth a visit!

Title: Fascinating tour and well worth a visit!
Text: Small group (8-10 people) tours run every half hour and are led by experienced and knowledgeable guides.  The tour takes you through the full tea making process and explores the whole factory.  Avoid going on a Monday as there is no tea picking on Sundays and so no production on Mondays.  The tour ends with a free tasting session of about 6 different teas.

Title: Informative and friendly!
Text: We went to the Uva Halpewatte Tea Factory during our stay in Ella. It is a short tuk tuk ride (or a long walk!) away and was well worth the trip out of town. A beautiful setting and a cheap entrance fee. We had a fantastic guide named Rajha who explained to us each stage of tea production alongside the working machines. After the tour we were able to taste each strength of tea produced at the factory. We went in the afternoon and were still able to see the factory in action but the staff advised that its best to visit in the morning as there is higher chance of seeing the factory in full working order as the staff start to wind down by the end of the afternoon. A trip with thoroughly enjoyed and would recommend to anyone!

Title: interesting + cheap
Text:
the entrance fee was quite cheap but I would not recommend buying tea at the factory which was very expensive! go to Ella town or to the other factory if you want to buy Ceylon.
the tour was interesting and the tour guide enthusiastic, so def worth a quick visit (~ 1-2 hours). And make sure to be there on a production day, to see the workers

Title: Great experience!!
Text: Such a great experience to learn about the tea plantation process. The staff was extremely knowledgeable, explained everything very well, and took us throughout the whole factory. Apart from that, the scenery around the factory itself is just beautiful.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Visited Halpewatte Tea Factory today, but due to the New Years holidays there weren't any ongoing production today. We still got a guided tour and learnt about how they make their tea. Very interesting! Next time I visit Ella, I'll visit again on a day when I'm sure the production is happening!

Title: Unexpected highlight of trip to Ella
Text:
All the reviews we'd read said that the factory only works in the morning, and we assumed it would be closed on the Full Moon Monday (the other tea factory was closed) so we were delighted after the tiring 45 min walk down then up from Ella to see people getting dropped off from tuk tuks and going in. After climbing to the top of the factory we were told the factory wasn't working, so it would just be a talk. We were just happy it wasn't shut, so paid our 300LKR each (which is very cheap compared to lots of other places we've visited).
We couldn't believe our luck when the machinery started up and we were able to see the whole production line from start to finish - really up close. The guide was knowledgeable and helpful, and at the end we got to try 4 different types of tea. A wonderful hour or so, and a pleasant (if a little tiring) walk from Ella.

Title: Nice visit
Text: Nice tea plantation. They had already finished production by 10.30 but still got a 45 min tour with a great and amusing guide. Learnt all about the differences in tea types, why they are priced differently and why loose leaf is preferable! Nice tea tasting at the end. Pretty views from the shop floor. FYI: there are lots of steep steps up small staircases.

Title: Interesting hour
Text:
Wasn't sure what to expect from this tour but it was definitely worth the hour or so even if just for the views from the factory and the owners house next door which is a stunning piece of modern architecture!
Tour starts with a talk on how the tea is picked, sorted and graded and then you get to see the processes. Ends with tastings. You can buy teas if you wish.

Title: Informative and enjoyable
Text: Really enjoyed this informative tour today. Worth stopping by! The guide has 40 years of experience and his factory tour goes right into the heart of the production area. Fantastic experience.

Title: Excellent tea tour
Text:
We arrived later in the afternoon, at around 4 pm. Unfortunately the production stoppes around midday, so the factory was not in full use, however the guide, Rajha was very well prepared and gave us a lovely and very informative presentation on the process of producing black tea. We went around the factory as well, so even though we could not see everything in working, it was one of our best experiences in Sri Lanka. The trip ended with tea tasting, which was included in the price. Well worth the money.
Thank you Rajha!

Title: Authentic tour!
Text:
We were positively surprised by Halpewatte Tea Factory. It's located on the top of a hill accessible by car or TukTuk with a fantastic view. The tour through the factory is very authentic and gives a very good insight into the tea production process (ca 30 min). Guide was very friendly and open. Worth a visit.

As in most factories, tea is overpriced. Recommend to buy in local supermarket.

Title: So much fun! A must see
Text: This was brilliant! Go in the morning, before 10am so that you can see the factory when it's alive with activity. It was so interesting to see all the stages a teal leaf goes through on it journey from plant to cup.

Title: Superb Factory Tour
Text:
We visited Halpewatte keen to learn how tea is made and it did not disappoint. Siva was our guide and his passion and experience of the tea industry really shone through. The tour was very informative and Siva was able to answer all of our questions (we are chemical engineers so touring the factory brought our engineering questions out!) 

The tour showed all areas of the factory and was done at a leisurely pace. 

It finished with tasting the tea we had just witnessed being produced. 

Overall it was a great tour and we would recommend it. It gives a real feel to the tea industry that you see all around you when in Sri Lanka.

Title: Excellent tea with an amazing view
Text: The Halpewatte Tea Factory is a short drive from Ella up a windy road, which should not be a challenge for a passenger car but would be impossible for a coach for example. I'd recommend visiting in the morning because that's when the factory is in operation after the morning harvest (many reviews said that the tea factory was not in operation on the day of their visit but in my opinion this is probably because they visited quite late). The view from there is truly amazing over all the tea growing hills. Once you've arrived, follow the signs all the way up the wooden stairs until you arrive on the top floor. The insightful tour by a professional guide lets you discover the various areas of the factory associated to different states of the tea production, explains the different qualities of tea and the influence of market demand. After the tour, you may taste the locally produced tea on a balcony with an amazing view on the plantations. You may also buy the locally produced tea (a big plus for the staff NOT being pushy at all!) which really comes at a bargain, especially for pure Orange Pekoe and its vanilla or jasmine flavoured version. In fact, we've loved their tea so much that we've ordered their tea online for home delivery since!?

Title: Interesting visit
Text: Perhaps a little pricy (480 Rs), but the visit was very informative and well done. It was interesting to see the employees at work and understand as well as taste the different varieties of tea.

Title: Interesting enough, difficult to understand guide!
Text: Good insight into the tea making process from start to finish! However, really struggled to understand the guide due to a very thick accent (our fault, trying his best). The tour was just a little bit dull! More of a show and tell except for the tea tasting at the end which was good fun! Bonus - very nice views from the top of the factory overlooking endless green tea fields!!

Title: Excellent tour and very informativr
Text: Our guide Rajha gave us a very informative tour with detailed explanations and he was ready to answer all our additional questions. You will be shown every step of the production and get a tasting of 4 different teas at the end. Dont go there on weekends, when there is no production.

Title: Nice visit
Text: We visited the factory on a Saturday and that meant that no one was working in the factory. We were only in Ella for two days on the weekend, so we had no opportunity to see the factory working. The tour was interesting though and we learned a lot. Such a shame its fully directed to tourists, even the prices of the tea was written in dollars instead of rupees. The view from the factory is amazing and tasting the different types of tea was a nice touch.

Title: Informative and hilarious tour!
Text:
RAJHA is very passionate about tea and this is clearly shown in his tour. It was very funny and interesting!

Ask for Rajha!!!

Title: To-tea-ly worth a visit
Text:
Really informative talk and tour of the factory. It was great to see the production of the tea in action and all staff were welcoming and friendly. There is a tea tasting after the tour where you can try small samples of four different black teas. 
Tickets are 480lkr each and free for children under 10. Lots of tea sold in the shop, but understandably it was expensive.

Title: A surprise hit....
Text:
My family and I were reminiscing after we got back from our trip to Sri Lanka about the highlights and this place was one of the top two or three things we did in the whole country we all agreed.

It is up in the hills quite a way out of town but the tour was so interesting, and immersive that we really loved it. 

We had no idea that Tea production was so involved (a lot of similarities to wine- partially why I enjoyed it). They take you on a half hour tour around the factory which was brilliant I have to say and you really get into the guts of the place and witness the people making the tea. the heat and the smell and sound really is very evocative.... 

You obviously get to try some tea and but what you want at the end (no pressure at all).... but I think the overall experience really gave the whole tea country some context and was really fascinating.

Highly recommended.

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
We arrived at just gone 9.30 on a Friday so just missed the half 9 tour (they run every half hour) and was told that on the factory tour wed only see half production. Which was fine with us. 
The older man running the tour was very passionate about tea which was lovely and was very informative, after the talky bit he showed us around the factory and we got to see a few machines running and some staff doing the last bits before finishing. It was very interesting and would recommend going, although maybe aim for the half 9 tour!

Title: Wouldnt have missed it. Lovely walk back
Text:
For some reason I really enjoyed this tour. Given in English by a man retired after 42 years in tea who had a very strong accent, i do not know how non-native English speakers could fillow the initial lecture.
The tour of the factory allowed everything wed been told  to fall into place. 
We thought it was expensive - why charge in dollars then convert into rupees? Ridiculous.
Expect at least one processung machine not to work
Tea tastung fun
Lovely views.

Title: Tip: a lot to translate for young children
Text: Its very interesting but sometimes hard to onderstand dit young children. A lot of bio chemical stuff an info about the plant. Again, interesting. The tour was a bit disappointing cause half of the factory was not in work die to the fact that they didnt have enough plant to process.

Title: Time for some tea!
Text: Being something of a professional tea drinker back home in England, I was desperate to look around a tea factory as part of our honeymoon. Both of us enjoyed the informative and insightful tour immensely; Sivanathan is a man who is clearly passionate about tea and this is evident in his guides tour, which takes you from the top of the factory, where the leaves are dried, through the rolling, fermentation, roasting and grading until finally it is sealed within bags for auction. Then to top it all off there is a cafe in which you can sample the product itself. Excellent tour all round.

Title: Worth a visit!
Text: We visited they factory on a production day which was great as we got to see all the machines working. Our guide gave us a good overview of the tea production process before showing us each step in action. At the end we were able to sample some of the teas as well. The overall tour was very interesting particularly because we had visited Amba Estate, a much smaller tea factory, the day before. We did the 11:30am tour and our group was a bit too big, it made it hard to follow what the guide was saying and to keep up at points.

Title: Loved it
Text: The factory is situated at the top of a mountain so there's an amazing view while you wait for the tour. Then it started and our guide was immediately friendly and happy. He was very knowledgeable, very good at English and very passionate about tea. Then you taste different tea strengths at the end! Definitely worth a visit. I think it was only 300-400 rupees each.

Title: Interesting tour well worth it
Text: The tour was very informative and took about 1 hour. You don't go to a tea plantation but just stay in the factory though. You get to taste the tea and can then buy your favorite kind. I would recommend it as we realised we knew nothing about tea production which is general knowledge though. It's a nice 20min drive from Ella city centre.

Title: Large Factory, Comprehensive Tour!
Text: As the factory was relatively large, the tour was very enjoyable as we were taken step-by-step through the entire production line from start to finish and was able to get a very interesting and comprehensive view of the tea factory! Our guide Siva, having almost 40 years experience was also very knowledgeable about tea production and was able to provide a fascinating tour, the place also smells heavenly and the tea tasting session at the end of was the perfect finish!

Title: Fascinating & impressive tour!
Text: We have a new appreciation for each cup of tea we now drink. Rajha gave a very informative & enjoyable tour. The process is amazing. We admire how hard everyone works to create a beautiful cup of tea.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: I really enjoyed this having been rather resistant to going. Well structured and informative visit with Siva as our guide. Short, well put together visit and a chance to try some delicious teas with much greater knowledge about their production.

Title: Tea tour
Text: Most informative and reasonably priced tour $3/person of one of the larger tea producers in this area. Very good views of the workings in the factory  and a tea tasting to finish. Recommended

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
Interesting tour and worth doing if you have a couple of days in Ella. Our guide had a good sense of humour (although sometimes difficult to understand)... only $3 for the tour. 

It took about 10 minutes to get there in a tuk tuk from Ella.

Title: Worth a chai
Text:
If you are to visit only one tea factory in Ella, this should be the one despite some flaws. It is certainly better than our experience at the green tea factory. The actual tour around this tea factory was excellent. Our charismatic guide shoved and shouted his way through. At first I thought that this would be very perturbing but it was clear that he was actually just very passionate about tea. 
On the downside, the tasters at the end were literally shots of chai and we were very disappointed to have to wait an hour for the tour to commence.
The guide won't be everyone's cup of tea but we felt that he saved the experience, especially considering we'd had to wait so long. However, a trip here would be worth it alone for the spectacular views provided by the long balcony.

Title: Passionate tour by Siva
Text: We've had a very interesting tour from the passionate Siva. It's wonderful to see such an old tradition come to life. If you want to see the production process make sure to come in the early morning but even in the afternoon it's definitely worth a trip. Last tour starts around 4.

Title: Interesting!
Text:
A guide will show you around the whole production process and provide a lot of information.
Do not expect any high-tech. 
Great to see.

Title: Great factory tour with a very knowledgable guide
Text:
Just back from a great tour at the Halpewatte Tea Factory and a really poor one at the Newburgh Tea factory (avoid at all costs). The Halpewatte tour cost 450rps (USD 3), runs every half hour and was well worth the trek that it took to get there. The staff were happy for us to be there and enjoyed showing off the process that they were in charge of. The tour gave a fantastic insight into the whole process from start to finish and at the end there were 4 teas to try which linked to the tour. The guide we had, a small older gentleman whose name I didn't catch, was amazing. His spoken English was great and he had an impressive knowledge of the Chemistry behind the processing of creating black tea. A very engaging guide whose passion for tea and the Halpewatte company shown through.

My only suggestions for improvements is to give the guide a microphone as in some of the rooms it was hard to hear him over the machinery (he's apparently asked the management for one). Also, have a better tea tasting area as it was in a corner with no time or seats to savour each of the four teas offered. A great tour deserves a suitable tasting area!

Title: Ok but nothing special
Text:
We had a very enjoyable tour of a coffee plantation in Panama where we could walk around the grounds, see the beans drying etc. I didn't expect that here as others had said that the factory only processes the tea leaves, but I really missed not seeing that part of it. We wanted to go to AMBA estate for their tour, but the tuktuk trip was  going to be 4000 and we would have possibly missed the tour as we were setting out late - didn't want to miss it.
We arrived a couple minutes after 10:30 and were sent to join a class that had just started. The guide spoke very quickly and I as a native English speaker had some trouble understanding everything he said. He explained a bit about why different regions produce different types of tea from the same plants, the 6 stages of tea production, then took us on a tour of the factory. Only part of it was in operation as it was the dry season. 
I was quite disappointed that photos were forbidden. The tour ended after about 45min with a very quick tasting of small amounts of 5 different teas. Views from the balcony of the tea tasting area and shop were beautiful.
We were quoted 1500 rupees to have a tuktuk take us there and back from Ella by 3 different drivers - none would bargain for less.

Title: Must do!!!
Text:
If you are in Ella and you want to go and visit a tea factory this is the right place!
They first explain you all the different type of tea, then the process of making it followed by a tour in the actual factory. If you have to tour with Mr Raja then you are in very good hands...he is very good and will tell you everything you need to know and more. 
This is not the first tea factory we visited but is definitely the best one.

Title: Well worth the visit!
Text:
After hearing about some pretty expensive tea factory tours around Ella, we opted for this one as it had mainly positive reviews. 

Firstly, don't let the taxi and tuktuk drivers in Ella trick you into believing there are no buses that go there! It is possible to get relatively close by bus. First get on a bus leaving to Kumbalwela junction (eg. direction Bandarawela). At the junction change to a bus heading towards Badulla. When you get on the bus say you're heading to Halpewatte. The journey will cost you less than 0.50 GBP (much cheaper than a taxi or tuktuk). The downside is that you've then got a 1.7 km walk uphill to the factory. So if you plan on taking the bus, make sure to plan well to avoid trekking in the midday heat, and bring lots of water!

The tea factory tour was 300 rupees each, a really good price. Only guided tours available, but we only had to wait 10 minutes for one to start. It was really informative, our guide was pretty funny and spoke decent English, and we got to try a few teas afterwards too! Limited photography allowed inside,

Title: Beautiful and clean
Text:
We only had tea here but the kitchen looked so clean and the service was so good that we had hoped to return for dinner but didnt make it.
So worth a try though.

Title: Very informative!!
Text:
This is a real working factory and would recommend going on a production day! Very informative tour from entertaining guide. He spoke excellent English and was very funny in trying to translate into German/French words like wilting. the tour was a walkthrough of the process as it was happening and finished with tea tasting. All the teas were delicious and we bought some leaves and the shop at the end! We also walked there through the tea plantation from Ella that took around 45mins and a tuk tuk back cost 200 rupees. The walk was signposted from the village. 

Would highly recommend!

Title: Fun and very informative tour
Text: Worth the ride from Ella! Really interesting tour with a short lecture on tea, tour of the factory and tea-tasting. Great guide! I think it cost 450rs.

Title: Unforgettable smells, sights, guide
Text: One of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka! Ragtha was a fantastic tour guide who explained the whole tea making process in detail and spoke from his decades of experience in the industry. The smells in the factory are enticing and unforgettable (earthy, smoky, lush) and the views from the hillside factory are impressive. Must-do in Ella. They are currently remodeling the upper levels and I can already tell it will be a beautiful location once they finish.

Title: Nice attraction
Text: Nice attraction in a less touristic tea factory. You learn all about the process of making tea. Get to taste and buy some as well. Nice gifts for your friends and family back home.

Title: Not boring
Text: We went during a national holiday so the factory wasnt operating. Even so, the tour was very interesting, much more interesting than I had expected. The guy who took us around was a real character. I now know enough about tea to bore friends and family.

Title: Guide was a character
Text: An informative, interesting tour run by an informative, interesting dude! Learned a lot about tea, enjoyed the tasting at the end & only wish you could take photos in the factory.

Title: Good enthusiastic tour
Text:
We visited the day after Diwali so most of the factory was closed however, the tour itself was very good and informative. Our guide explained everything about the process in great detail and was very enthusiastic which made it pretty fun. You can also sample 4 types of tea at the end of the tour. 
The tour is Rs:450 per person which is fairly reasonable. 

There is also a small shop where you can buy all different types and flavours of tea.

Title: OK, buy not amazing.
Text: An OK tour, interesting to see the process of how we get our brews back home.  gift shop very expensive.  Tour was cheap tho.  Worth a visit if you have a few hours spare.  600rs tuk tuk from Ella centre

Title: Siva is brilliant!!
Text:
Loved this tour, Siva our guide was so passionate and knowledgeable about tea and just made us appreciate it so much more.
We were able to learn all the process of making tea and do some tasting before buying some of the factorys own product.

Title: As if I could have loved tea any more!
Text: I have loved tea since I can remember, yet I didn't really have any clue about it. Rajha gave us a wonderful tour and explained the whole tea-making process. We visited in the afternoon so the factory wasn't actually in full swing, but we were taken to every area and it was really enjo

Title: Great guide
Text: Good explanation of the tea making process and a very enthusiastic guide. We went on a Poya day, so most of the factory was closed, would probably be a bit more exciting if we hadn't visited on a national holiday!

Title: Fascinating
Text: this really was quite a drive, so if yuk tuk driver recommends they wait for you to finish tour say yes! There are no tuk tuks waiting for pick ups and we were very grateful knowing we didn't have to walk balk down the hill! The tour itself was absolutely fascinating, in fact the highlight of our trip in Ella. Our guide was very knowledgeable and extremely passionate about the tea making process. We were lucky to be shown around while the machines were still in operation - this definitely added to our experience ( I believe machines are operated at different times of the day in different seasons- work a check before visiting).

Title: Uva tea time!
Text:
What a drive, but what a view! The road heading up is pretty much a single-lane country dirt road and as you head up you're hoping that you don't have to face on-coming traffic.
Once you get up there to the top, you'll realize that the view here is pretty amazing. 

The guard at the door directed us up a flight of stairs which led to more flights of stairs that led up to the top of the factory building. For a minute it seemed like there was no tour to be offered and we were just walking to the top where the sales shop happened to be. 
But as we reached the top of the final set of stairs, a woman at a register greeted us and asked for 450 rs ;-) (The tour price per person). 
So this is where the tour starts! I thought it seemed a bit odd, to have guests have to walk up the flight twice (to get to the tour which takes place after you head back down and then again to finish the tour). 

Anyway, my friend and I paid and waited for the tour to start. It didn't take long. There was already a sizeable group standing by.
 
When you arrive walk up multiple flights of stairs to get to the sales/tasting floor. This is where you pay for your tour and wait for it to start. I arrived with a decent sized group already waiting. 
Then it was back down the stairs, grab a seat and listen to a lecture about the process of tea picking, selecting, sorting, etc. Our tour leader was enthusiastic and very informative as well as open to questions all about tea and the various types of tea produced in the country. 
Afterwards, everyone got up and followed him through the factory to see the men and machines at work (and women too). My one complaint is that the group is so large it's difficult to hear the information when our tour leader spoke. 
No photos allowed here! 
Once back upstairs we were offered a sampling of 4 different levels of tea strengths/types. If only I had more room in my suitcase! I would've purchased more.
(If they took credit cards then I probably would have bought more too).
If you like tea then definitely stop by. They produce tea from the Uva area of Sri Lanka.
There's a sampler box of tea featuring the various regions' tea for purchase as well!

Title: Worth a trip for tea lovers
Text: For only a few dollars you can see the whole tea factory and tea making process. And the place smells amazing, so much tea! The tour includes tea sampling which completes the tour nicely. There is a shop where you can buy what you just sampled and some other varieties.

Title: Learned so much about tea!
Text: This visit was super informative, and you get to go up close and personally see the tea processing. Make sure to call ahead and ensure they're processing tea that day so you can see all the action!

Title: Interesting and enthusiastic tour guide
Text:
We visited the factory on a Sunday when there is no production. However, they still ran a tour lasting about 20-30 minutes explaining tea production and ended with sampling 5 different teas, varying in strength. It was informative and the guide used good English and answered all our questions.
I'd imagine if the factory was operational and all staff in, it would've been a 5 star experience.

Title: Great to be able to see the production in process
Text: Very good guide with 40+ years of experience in the tea business. Great to see the large bags of tea leaves coming in and going through the various stages of the production while being on the tour. Enhanced our understanding of tea!

Title: No production sunday, monday
Text: If you want to see the factory at work apparently the best time to come is around 8-8:30 on any day except sunday and monday (monday is picking day). Friendly person at factory explained this to us. The tuk tuk drivers won't tell you this beforehand - they make easy money.

Title: Great tour! Recommend
Text: We walked from Ella centre and it took about 45 minutes - quite a steep climb at the end. Views are worth it when you get to the top. We then got a tuk tuk back for 500rp. We went on a Tuesday and arrived around 11am. By this time production was almost over, but we were in time to see some of the factory still operating, showing the final steps in production. The tour lasted about 45 minutes and the tour guide was excellent, very knowledgable and entertaining too. Tea tasting at the end. Value for money!

Title: best money we ever spent
Text:
We went here on a saturday- the factory was not working but it was nontheless very interesting and informative!!
Our tour guide explained everything really well, knew all the answers to our questions. He was the greatest <3
Tea degustation at the end was really nice too, I didn't even know there were different types of black tea :D
There is also a shop wehere you can buy tea.
Go here with tuk tuk from Ella town centre (1200 rupees to go there and back- its really OK price since it is a bit far)

Title: Our own personal guided tour!
Text:
We turned up here in the afternoon, and had missed the day's production. The place was deserted, but we were asked if we would like the tour anyway, and after paying our entrance fees (they let the kids in for free!), we were given a highly entertaining and educational private tour by one of the guides there. 

After giving us the theory of tea lesson, he took us around the factory, and showed us all the various stages of tea production. 

The kids found it very interesting, and even tried all the different teas at the end of the tour! 

The location is stunning. To fully appreciate it, we walked there from Ella then took a tuk-tuk back into town afterwards.

Highly recommended for all!

Title: Enthusiastic black tea guided tour
Text:
Black tea is good. Green tea is bad. And the tour is highly entertaining with much detail, good tea tasting afterwards, nice tea souvenir shop. The "slight" bias towards black tea was very entertaining. Also the q&a that felt a lot like in school. You better have s.o. ask questions. 
Overall clearly the best tea factory tour by far.

Title: Fantastic introduction to the world of tea!
Text:
We arrived at the tea factory around 13 and it was already too late to see the production, HOWEVER, please stay for the tour, it is really worth it (also, since there is no factory noise, it is better to hear the detailed explanation  of how the tea is made)! Our guide was Rajha, who is an absolute star! Very warm and friendly, he knows all the secrets of tea making and brewing ;-) the tour starts with a class and all the production steps are explained, and then we went to see where each of them takes place. Rajha shows you everything and explains it in a very interesting way. There is a tea tasting in the end and once you are educated you can really distinguish the different kinds of tea. 
All in all, the tour is a great way to spend an hour or so :-) highly recommend!!

Title: Great Tour, simple no frills but very informative! Lovely view!!!
Text: We really enjoyed our tour here and I actually went back again to bring my mom a second time. Rajha was our guide and he was passionate about tea and was an amazing guide! Just know that production is early in the morning (first tour at 8 am) and it's so good to see the whole place in action. We rented our own scooter and drove up (although the road is a bit windy and steep) but it's a gorgeous view from the top (and on the way!). For 300 rsp, it's a bargain tour. We visited other tea factories in Sri Lanka and this was by far our favourite!

Title: You must go!
Text:
We visited the tea factory and it was great. It was about 10 mins in a tuktuk from Ella, and it's a bargain at only 300SRP for the tour. 

We were there on a non production day, but this didn't make any difference to how enjoyable it was and we still saw lots of the tea making process and they turned the machines on. 

Siva the guide was excellent, very knowledgeable and funny, he made the tour. At the end you get to try the tea and there's a little shop.

Title: I finally understand tea!
Text:
Best 300 rps I've spent in Sri Lanka. I learned so much about tea in a way I will never forget.

We arrived at 2:15 pm and although most of the factory was not in production, what I really missed was hot noisy machines at work. Instead the factory was quiet and unrealistically serene, which felt nice for its location. 

Throughout the sit down explanation portion of the tour we had the time to calmly ask questions and we never felt rushed. The tour was peaceful and the quiet factory machinery were strangely perfumed with the aroma of orange pekoe.

After the tour we had a chance to sample several different types of teas, and pick our favorite. The gift shop was also open, which allowed us to purchase the exact tea we sampled.

A must "tea" for tea lovers and everyone alike.

On a side note. Hire a tuk tuk to the factory. Save your energy for nicer hikes in and around Ella.

Title: Rajha superbe guide!
Text: We were advised by our guesthouse to go to this factory and we were really pleased! Not only it it one of the biggest producer of tea in Sri Lanka, we also had the privilege to have rajha as our guide! A very knowledgeable guide! Thanks! And thumbs up for the view on the terrasse!

Title: Tea-riffic
Text: Siva's tour was spirited, in depth, and he provided great tea recommendations after the tour. Make sure you get there very very early if you want to see the production, but the explanation tour is quite nice as well.

Title: Good low key attraction
Text: We visited the green tea factory. It is quite small.Very reasonable and low key. We went onto the factory floor and saw the processes. The visit lasted about 20 minutes.

Title: Very Interesting
Text:
A very interesting tour - learnt a lot about tea and the production line. Most of the production had finished for the day so might be better to visit in the morning but still got to see the final stages which were still great to see. Tours seem to go every hour and cost 300rs and last between 40mins and an hour so well worth the money. you get to sample the different strengths of tea produced here so you have an idea of what youre buying is you get some from the little shop. the views from the top are great even though it was pretty misty when we went.
Got a tuttut from Ella 1000rs return as it was poring with rain - you can walk but there is some steep hills.

Title: Informative and scenic - we walked there from Ella
Text:
Worth seeing even if they are not producing tea at the time (when we went, they stopped producing tea at 8am).  The guide was very informative and VERY passionate about the quality of tea (woe to low land tea and flavoured teas).  We had lots of fun and learned a lot.

We walked from Ella town. The walk took around 1 hr 10 mins and was very straightforward.  The walk is quite scenic, among tea plantatinos and with some nice views.  You can catch a tuk tuk of course very reasonably.  Or even flag one down halfway if you get tired.

Title: Must do in Ella!
Text: We cannot rave enough about this tour! They run hourly (not usually in production though as that happens during the night) and it is super interesting and informative for only 300 lkr. Our guide Rajah was fabulous! Very knowledgeable and a funny personality. At the end they do make a deal of buying tea but we did because it was a great gift and good quality tea. It's about 6ks out from Ella. We paid 500 lkr for a Tuktuk as it's completely up hill. Don't miss this factory while in Ella! Beautiful views as well form the top

Title: Informative visit to Halpewatte Tea Factory
Text:
Had a nice visit to the tea factory. Although people were not producing tea at the time of visit. We were still able to see the whole factory and how everything worked. Our guide Rajha was great, easy to understand and informative. Answered all questions with great knowledge and enthusiasm. 

Got to taste some different teas also. 
Great views from the top we're you start the tour. 

All in all a nice way to spend a few hours and learn abit more about tea. 

Short ride from Ella on a tuk-tuk and they will wait for you and take your back for 1200-1500

Title: Great short tour to learn so many things!!
Text:
We arrived around 8:30am to the factory and our visit with Rajha started very shortly after that. He first made us sit around a table (we were 2 couples in total!) and made us smell, touch and feel the different tea leaves. We then walked around the factory where workers were actively sorting, fanning ... Rajha who worked all his life from bottom to management of a tea factory explained us carefully all the different steps of the production, as well as the distribution (Colombo tea exchange! ).
We eventually finished the visit with some tasting! 
Loved it, definitely recommend going there and more especially Rajha if you can have a hold of him!

Title: Great way to spend the morning
Text:
Our tour was very informative and unhurried.
Rajah really loves his job and gave us a good insight into tea production.
We saw all the processes and the place was rich tapestry of sound and smells, also great for kids as there is a lot to hold there attention.

Title: Great morning out
Text:
We went to visit the factory on the 2nd January when there was no production, but our guide explained it very well how they produce the tea. 
It's very interesting and educational. 
The guide even turned on some of the machines, so he could better demonstrate the processes. 
I wish we visited on a day when there was production, but it was still really interesting. 
I think they run guided tours hourly, so you just turn up and can get on the next tour. 
It's a long way from the center, so you will need a tuktuk driver who is willing to wait for you. Our driver was called by our guesthouse, so we knew how much it will cost up front. 
All in all, a good trip.

Title: Don't miss it
Text: Well worth a visit! The normal tour lasts about 3 hours but we asked for a condensed version and were out in less than an hour. I have a lot more respect for tea now! Very knowledgeable guide and really interesting to see the whole process.

Title: Fascinating, & stunning views!
Text:
We went here on a Wednesday (day after Poya day as we had heard the factory would be shut then). 

We walked here all the way from the bottom of the winding road up - a good 30 min walk but some stunning scenery to look at on the way!

We arrived and found the factory wasn't operating at that time (around 3pm) but we were in time for a tour, costing 300R per person.

Our tour was conducted by Siva who was so knowledgeable and passionate about tea! It made it all the better having him as our guide. He took us to the first floor to learn about the different parts of the tea plant, how the plants are dealt with after picking, and ultimately what ends up making its way into your cup of tea - be it loose leaf or teabags. 

We were fortunate that after this informative session on the tea plant, a number of tea pickers arrived with freshly picked tea leaves and the factory seemed to spring into life - so we were able to see some of the machines in action. Overall, there is a lot to take in, but the tour was done so well by Siva and he was able to answer any question you could throw at him!

We finished the tour by sampling the four main types of tea produced and sold from the factory. We also bought some tea (500R for 100g). 

Overall, would highly recommend this factory, and thanks to Siva for a great tour!

Title: A fascinating tour
Text:
Six of us turned up on a Sunday without realising there is no tea production or tours that day, but the lovely knowledgeable tour guide Siva gave us a brilliant private tour anyway. 

It actually helped having no production as we had a free run of the place and we probably saw things we wouldn't on an ordinary day. 

Our guide Siva worked in the industry for 40 years and really does know all there is to know about tea; how it's grown, produced and marketed and all about the history, which for a group of tea-drinking Brits was fascinating to learn about.

We were taken through all areas of the factory and shown every aspect of the production line. It helps that Siva speaks perfect English. 

There's a lovely tea shop on the top floor and we even got a 15% off voucher for a new local restaurant called Ceylon Tea Factory. 

One tip - make sure you get a tuk tuk or taxi from Ella as it's a 1.7km uphill walk to the factory if you get the bus. 

All in all it would be criminal to visit tea country and not find out what's made it famous; this is a great place to learn! And at less than £2 for a tour it's well worth it.

Title: Make sure you get here before 4pm
Text:
Unfortunately my visit here was a bit disappointing.
Be warned that the drive up along the winding path was a bit hairy. Upwards steep and winding.

I think this place has the potential to be a nice visit but we arrived after 4pm.
The last factory tour is at 4pm and they don't serve tea or anything after 4pm despite the fact that they closed at 5pm. We couldn't even order a pot of tea.
The tea store was rather small and very limited.
The views from the balcony are spectacular though.

Title: One of our favourite tours!!
Text:
We were shown around by Siva he was an amazing tour guide who was so passionate and knowledgeable about his job making us so much more appreciative of the work that goes into a cup of tea!

We went on a Sunday so there was no production but he showed us all the machines in action.

Highly recommended :)

Plus the view is stunning!

Title: Well worth the trip
Text: I took a tuk tuk from Ella - 1500lkr return incl waiting- its a long uphill walk otherwise from Halpe. The tour was super interesting - I never knew how complex tea-making was! Got to walk around the working factory and try tea at the end. It cost 550lkr. Well worth it!

Title: Guided tour
Text: Great tour. Our guide explained whole tea process clearly and was also passionated about it. Would recommend to everyone! Only annoying thing here was some ignorant tourists who didn't follow the rules like no smoking in the area or take pictures inside factory.

Title: Super interesting
Text: We really enjoyed our informative tour at this factory. Shiva, the tour leader, was very engaging, has worked there a long time and emphasized the importance of tea and the history of tea. He also explained the tea making process in depth as well as all the different grades of tea. We also had a little taster at the end. Kudos to Shiva, we really enjoyed him!

Title: Excellent thing to do in Ella
Text:
A very informative and interesting tour. They give you a lecture first about the teas and the tea making process. Then they show you the factory thorougly. Tuktuk from Ella 20 minutes, tour about 1 hour. Tuktuk driver will wait for you at the factory to get you back. Easy road to go by your self too if you want to rent a scooter or a tuktuk for you to drive!

At times quite hard to understand the guides english.

Title: Frustrating
Text:
There were 40 (I counted) people in our tour group. The guide was nice but spoke with a very heavy accent and we could only make out about 20% of what he was saying. But that didnt matter as when we were at the back of the group we couldnt hear anything anyway. The snippets of information we got were quite interesting and it was nice to see the inner workings of the factory. Not sure why they couldnt split us into 2 or 3 groups and stagger the visits to start at 10 minute intervals.

Tea in the gift shop is horrendously overpriced, but having said that we bought some and so did everyone else. 

Overall got the feeling no one cared that visitors had a good experience, just that they made the maximum profit possible. With a few tweaks this could be a lovely experience as all the basic ingredients are there, but that would mean management and staff attitudes have to change.

Title: TO BIG GROUP
Text: They have a group every half an hour no matter how big it is.. So our group was over 40 people big. In the classroom somehow we still understood the guide, between the machines was not possible. 10 people should be maximum for a group. With 500 rp entry they earn with visitors more than with tea...

Title: Hire a scooter to get here - cheaper than the tuk tuks
Text: Worth the effort to visit, to see the process and enjoy the stunning views.  We hired a scooter for the afternoon that gave us freedom and came in at half the price of the tuk tuks - surely more expensive in Ella than anywhere else in Sri Lanka.  One useful tip - dont buy the tea at the factory, buy it from the Ceylon Tea Factory Restaurant (also part of their empire and serving great food) in Town where it is 40% cheaper - the scallywags.  Lost a star from us for that.

Title: Informative to the brim
Text: The title says it all. The gentleman that guided us first introduced the picking, separating and thedifferences between teas after which we got to see the facilities. Unfortunately it was Saturday, close to national holiday, which meant that the factory wasn't working. Still, it was a visit well worth making.

Title: Informative tour
Text:
We headed up there just before ten oclock. We only had a short wait for the next available tour. 
We are a family with children aged 9, 7 and 3yo.   Although the children werent exactly thrilled to do a tea plantation tour, they all got progressively more and more interested as the tour went along and they got involved by the guide, who although has a strong Sri Lankan accent when spoke English (which was sometimes difficult to understand) is a real character and keep us all interested. 
The tour starts with a short lecture about tea types and processes methods than it continues along the various stages and machinery in the actual working factory. The factory is operational only in the mornings, due to favourable climate conditions, so we imagine morning tours get a much better grasp into tea processing.

The tour end with tea tasting on the top floor, where there is a balcony from which one can enjoy sweeping views.

The shop only sells a good variety of packaged tea. There is no cafe where one can enjoy a cuppa with biscuits or cake. It seems a shame we were looking forward to going to the tea factory also to sit back and enjoy a proper cup of tea.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: The guy who did the tour kind of seemed like he hated his job, he was very serious. He got a bit better as the tour went on though. We thought the tour was free but it is 525 R. Overall it was interesting to hear about how the tea is produced. It was quite hard to find the entrance though, I think they should have someone out the front to greet you. There are tuk tuks waiting to take you back which was good.

Title: Interesting tea facts for those with an interest
Text:
An interesting visit and I learnt a lot about tea, though I did find my guid a bit difficult to understand through his very strong Sri Lankan accent. 

On the tour you have a short lesson on some interesting tea facts followed by a tour through the factory. The tour is finished off with some tea tasting and an opportunity to purchase some of their tea. The tour costs 525rp but I found it was reasonable value as I learnt some interesting things I didnt know. The tea for purchase is also a reasonable price and all in USD.
