I felt this factory being in such a splendid location was missing a prime opportunity to provide a cafe setting for patrons. I hope in the future they consider adding tea and scones and a small menu for guests to really enjoy their tea and the view.

Title: Explains a lot about tea what you probably didn't know
Text: The Tuk Tuk drive to the factory is already nice. The tour takes about an hour. Unfortunately, they won't take you on the tea field itself. But you will see the machines and the testing at the end is nice. Worth the money.

Title: Excellent tour with Rajha, highly recommended especially if you enjoy tea
Text: Great tour, very happy I went. Rajha was very knowledgeable and really educated us on tea. He was very easy to understand and explained everything at the right level of detail.

Title: Nice factory production closed on Sunday, difficult to use Cards
Text: We went with a tuktuk all the way up. The small roads up in the mountain brought nice scenarios. Unfortunately factory closed on Sunday but they do educational trainings on Tea and Tea sizes plus a walk through inside the factory. After education Tea tastings. Very nice education on Tea, size and tastes. All tea sale in USD, and hard to use credit as they did hide the cardterminal. After request and insisting I was able to use the card to buy Tea. They were not keen to provide card sales and the guidning tour was only accepted in cash. Would recommend to go here and try to do it on week days. Very great learning.

Title: Very informative tour
Text: The tour in this tea factory was very good ; the guide gave us a lot of information and we saw every phase of the process of producing tea. The tea tasting at the end was also nice, their tea is very good.

Title: Nice experience!
Text: Nice experience but it will not be the same with the best guide ever! Istouti so much Sellamuthu !!!

Title: Intersting
Text: Really interesting to learn a little about the history and techniques used within the tea plantation. Even 40 different teas to try - the Masala Chai flavoured tea was my favourite!

Title: Don't waste your time
Text: Well I cant believe all the good reviews of this place, I will tell you how it was for us. We arrived around 8.20 am no one was around. Our driver went off to find someone we were then told quite curtly by an older gentleman guide that we were too early and would have to wait ( your website clearly says tours start at 8am) We were asked to sit in the shop on damp cushions and given a tatty dog eared sheet explaining all the teas they manufacture. About 15 mins later we summoned by the guide just the two of us as no one else had arrived who fleetingly told us about the virgin tea, peppercorns and cinnamon. He told us that 100 people worked on the estate. He then walked us up to the bungalow at record speed passing just 2 x pickers. I had to be quick to take photos as he was desperate to keep going. Tea and cake was served at the bungalow...might be a heathen but tea was awful prefer my Yorkshire blend. We were taken to the so called factory, not one machine was in operation or staff working when do they manufacture all this tea? my doubts are not here looking  at the ancient machinery. We also entered there with no hair nets strategically  placed were pots of tea leaves of which he put some into my sweaty hand for me to pour it back...yuck !!!We were then had to trudge back down to the shop to sample all the teas. Cant say I was enthralled with any of them bar one. We decided to buy one box you could tell the guide was upset that's all we were spending so tried to get us to buy cinnamon sticks, we have our own catering business back home and have buckets of cinnamon. Disappointed with what we were going to buy he walked off..no goodbyes etc etc  Came away with little knowledge  the place is run down, glad we only stopped here enroute to National park would have been miffed if we had paid a taxi or tour guide to take us here. Whilst this is free run by volunteers this place is just a ploy to sell tea.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Taken by tuk tuk. Enjoyed the tour. Interesting way they use a symbiotic relationship between the various tea plants and other vegetation

Title: A working Tea Estate Museum
Text:
A beautiful frozen in time Tea Estate, we arrived and where greeted by a guide that walked us along the White Tea plantation and showed us the Rubber trees and Cinnamon trees.
We saw women harvesting the tea leaves by hand and heard various explanations.
Then we arrived at a beautiful colonial style villa at the top of the hill where we got a peace of cake and cup of delicious tea, after relaxing in the cool breeze we toured the villa saw a Mongoose crossing the path and went down to the tea factory witnessing the same 150 year old machines still working today drying and separating the tea leaves.
And finally ended up at the shop where we tasted all of the tea varieties and bought some tea to take with us.

Title: Add it to your list, go early morning
Text: We came here early in the morning and there was only a couple of people in our group, the guide was friendly and informative, the tea tasting and cake was in a lush garden setting, the factories that still use the original machinery in excess of 100 years old makes the product so much more authentic in my opinion

Title: Great place to go
Text:
We went here with our young children on the recommendation of some locals, more in hope than expectation.

Anyway we arrived and had a guided tour of how the tea leafs are grown, tried a few local teas in a nice sat down area.

Followed by a tour of the factory where the leafs are dried out and made into the tea we drink.

There is no charge for this service, and its made quite clear not to tip any individual, if you want to tip there is a box at the end.

There is a store at the end, which sells various tea related items, there is absolutely no hard sell what so ever, really enjoyable due to this.

We brought some tea to take, would definitely recommend this as a way to spend a few hours.

Title: Best Tea Plantation in the area
Text: Perfect for a guided tour with a quick look on how tea is manufactured and great souvenir shop to buy some tea for the family

Title: Great tea tour (though not during season)
Text:
We had been to the tea plantation on a number of occasions. Right off the bat - it is a great and insightful tour, that is also complimentary and will take about 60-120 minutes. The tea selection that is produced on-site is grand and the facilities are nice to explore.

Generally there are no set times (its upon arrival and tour guide availability). The first time we went was during off-season (as a couple) - this meant that there were fewer tourists. This was also reflected in the tour (with the same guide mind you). He was more thorough (more informative) and took his time - then it lasted close to 2 hours. The second time we went was in December (beginning of the season) and it was completely different. We went as a group (of 8 incl a 3 and 4 year old). We arrived simultaneously with a larger tourist group. This time the tour was rushed (a bit more challenging when you have 2 little ones). When we made it up to the house for the tea tasting and cake, part of the porch was covered off and there was some noisy construction work going on - wonder why they couldnt have done it during off-season? The porch got crowded as the other tour group caught up and we had to hurry through the facilities and back as there was another group coming.

I did see that they had a kids camp under construction - I think that is a great idea and will make this a more well-rounded family experience, something we lacked on our 2nd visit. Nonetheless, good experience and would recommend it (if they more guides during peak times).

Title: Ver Interesting plantation
Text: Fascinating tea plantation with free tours by employees. It was great to walk around the estate and find out how they planted, harvested and maintained the tea and associated crops. It was quite a place to visit.

Title: Perfect visit
Text:
We had an excellent visit
Tea explainations
Spycies also (pepper, coffee, cinnamon...)
Living Museum with how to dry, crush and sieve
It was very interesting and adapted for children

Title: Free tour!
Text: This is something I love to do with all friends and family who come and visit us. It's a working tea factory and it's really cool to see how it all works.

Title: Insightful
Text: We had a great time touring this wonderful plantation despite the overcast weather. Our guide, Meril, was patient with our many questions and very informative in his responses. We stopped and watched the rain past whilst having a cup of nice hot - you guessed it - oolong tea and chocolate cake. We loved the many varieties of tea. Be warned: the shop wasn't cheap (!) but there was no pressure to buy. Overall, we recommend it.

Title: Amazing Experience
Text: We had an amazing experience at the Herman Tea Factory. We were lucky enough to be shown around the plantation by Meril, a knowledgeable gentleman who spoke wonderful English. He knew all about the process and the local flora and had a great sense of humour. It was a private quiet tour and we went at our own pace and asked as many wuestoins as we wanted. The tea tasting as very interesting and the shop had a wide variety of teas for purchase. The tour was truly made wonderful by Meril however. Beautiful location, highly recommended.

Title: Coffee drinker converted
Text:
We went to a tea plantation in Sri Lanka,never realising what an amazing experience this would be.
We got there just as they were closing,and a most characteristic man told us,he would take us round.
The tale of the white tea was fascinating,the guide was so informative,and eventually,it transpired,he owned the plantation,though was modest enough not to tell us.
We had tea and cake at his house,he showed us the BBC clip of the background if his exclusive tea,it was a most special experience.
I can't tell you if it will be Herman that gives you the tour,but if it is,you have won the golden ticket!!
Most interesting, well worth seeing.

Title: Great, informative visit.
Text: We received a very informative tour of the grounds and factory, which still has some of the original machines! At the start we were given some delicious tea and cake, and then had the opportunity to try all the teas available at the end. Would highly recommend as a day trip from Galle or nearby.

Title: Excellent tour about tea growing...and excellent teas for purchase
Text: Handunugoda Tea Estate is a great afternoon activity for anyone who slightly likes tea (by the end of the tour, you'll LOVE tea).  The grounds are beautiful, with a variety of different tea plants for demonstrations.  Inside the processing facility, you can watch as the teas are dried, sorted and prepared for distribution using both modern machines (able to measure the size of the leaves) and antique mechanics.  It's all exceptionally interesting and positive as this is the source of livelihood for a great number of locals.  In the shop, one can smell and taste various types of teas and actually purchase some of the Herman teas to take home...which I did and they're amazing.  Can't wait to order more!!

Title: Pleasant outdoor activity
Text:
We had a lovely stroll in the tea plantation with a very knowledgeable guide. At the end of the walk you are treated for a cup of tea and a slice of cake at the owners house. From here you continue to the tea factory where the whole process is explained. Its amazing! They work with 145 years old machines!!! At the end of the tour you can taste at least 20 different kind of teas and buy your souvenirs.
The tour used to be free, but due to the difficult economical situation they have introduced a nominal entrance fee of 2 USD.

Title: Large variety of teas to taste
Text:
A great trip, information guide was great
Free tea and cake was an added extra
I especially liked the fact you could taste all the different varieties of tea grown
A nice shop at the end to by the unique tea's

Title: Blown away
Text:
We absolutely loved our visit to this very special plantation. Had a great tour which was just the right length for our hot kids who at 8 and 11 didnt exactly have a tea plantation on their list of to-dos!

Plantation is extremely beautiful and on our little walk we saw lots of tea plants and also wildlife and herbs. Factory was really interesting too. The tea and amazing cake on the verandah was really welcome (kids loved it!) and the tea tasting was incredibly well done too with all the different teas available for tasting - again something the kids really enjoyed.

Others have said the teas are expensive. All I can say is that in the UK they would cost a lot more so we certainly bought quite a few.

A really fun visit for the whole family and easy to fit into the day if youre in the Galle area.

Title: An absolutely hidden gem!  Well worth the visit!
Text: Never ever did we have any idea about tea and just what was required! This was an absolutely hidden gem and was just amazing.  Thoroughly recommend this as a visit.  Actually got to see tea being sorted and then tasted the product you just cant ask for more!!!

Title: Awesome Virgin White tea plantation
Text: Driving through small local villages and communities describe closely how's life on Sri Lanka. Plantation is beautiful and peaceful place you should visit and learn more about tea. Delicious tasing (cake and tea), guided tour through the plantation were very educative and interesting. You'll se the factory inside and on the end - you may taste tea samples to choose which one is the best for you. It's not about the one - you should buy more. All are delicious planted with love.

Title: Very Informative
Text:
We spent a lovely morning here guided around by the Manager David. He gave us a so much information and clearly loves the place, more than just a job. We saw lots of spices and wild life during our walk. 

Fascinating story of the history of Tea and the White Silver Tips.

A beautiful cup of tea with excellent cake was enjoyed @ the owners residence, followed by a tour of the factory which was also extremely interesting. This followed a venture into the Tea Shop where the many teas manufactured were available for tasting and purchase. Which naturally did.

Title: Really interesting experience
Text: The place is beautiful and the tour they offer for free is extremely interesting: it covers info from planting to processing, showing breathtaking antique machinery that is still in use nowadays. They even offer a tasting with a slice of cake in the patio of a beatiful cottage, everything is organised with love and care. The shop is full of temptations (gorgeous products) and if you are lucky, as we were, you will meet the founder of this perfect place. A must go if you are in Galle or Unawatuna, we went by motorbike and it was really worth it!

Title: Amazing family tea estate!
Text: This was an amazing visit of this family tea estate - we came without previous notice (in the Covid era - we were there completely alone) and the manager showed us around, explained the tea planting and tea making process...he spoke a good English. The tour, which was free of charge (tip if you liked it), was finished by tea tasting - we could taste every single tea they sell and then buy what we liked. :))

Title: A great place to visit
Text: Another tea estate we thought but we were really glad we decided to come here.  You are taken by tuk tuk and given an individual tour of the plantation and given a great cup of tea along the way. You then go tothe factory where you can see, touch and smell the tea making process which was fascinating.  You also learn about the Virgin White Tea which this estate is famous for.  There was a shop at the end but there was nopressure to buy anything.  There were numerous teas available for taste testing, which we did, and ended up buying some , including the Virgin White Tea.  We also bought a great souvenir inthe form of a book called The Suicide Club which is the story of the founder, and thattoo was very enjoyable.

Title: We speak your language!
Text: This was a unique experience! The gentleman who welcomed us asked where are we from and then greeted us and told us to follow him in our own language! Such a nice man, he was making an effort to learn words in all kind of languages. The estate is so beautiful, besides the tea we saw rubber tree, pepper plant. They served us with tea and cookies, showed old equipment,  it was relaxing and educational.

Title: Very nice visit
Text:
We arrived early (no booking) in the morning and was welcomed and informed of the specialty of the plantage the White Virgin. Then another guide took us around the plantage telling us about the different teas, how they grow and are picked. Me and my husband were the only guests.
On the terrace to a beautiful house we were served oolong tea and cake for free.
We were introduced to the manufacturing in the factory and then the tea tasting of 40 different types! Very interesting! You dont have to buy the tea from the shop they have shipping through their website.
Before you leave you donate a voluntary sum, no individual tip is allowed. 
It was a great experience- lot to see and learn, so nice breathing fresh air and walking in the lush plantation. Recommended!

Title: Good insight into Tea Plantation. Expensive Sri Lankan Tea though.
Text:
This was a detour visit during our SL vacation. As we dropped out the Whale Watching, we googled this place and asked our cab buddy to take us there. 

The plantation is well kept, just like others, as it is a major source of revenue generation in SL.

The plantation tour takes about 45 mins. includes a free tea and cake serving also. After this, they take you through the tea factory, which for me was done in a quite haphazard manner. 

Later, as expected, they take you to their main shop where there are about 50 samples kept for tasting. 50! Seriously???? After the entire tour and smells around, I bet your taste bud would not be able to differentiate between more than 3-5 samples.

Anyways, if you are on a long tour in SL, visit the Blue Field Tea factory [between Nuwara and Kandy].... it is much better there. you also get to pluck the leaves and is very decently explained by the factory's person.

Title: Lovely tour and tasting
Text: The tour of the plantation was fantastic. We saw the tea crops and the ladies hand picking the tips to make beautiful tea. We learnt about the production and was able to taste a variety of tea. They have a very expensive white tip tea that is only sold in an exclusive cafe in Paris. The tea was delicious. An enjoyable experience.

Title: Amazing experience
Text:
This estate is 200 acres and they produce white tea, black tea, natural rubber & cinnamon. 

The machines they use is from UK, quite old but still functioning. 

Our tour guid was Meril, nice, knowledgable person with a smile on his face. Meril took us everywhere in that estate showing and explaining all the trees there and how the grow, pick and produce tea; how they collect rubber from trees; the process of cinnamon making and invited us for a nice cup of tea, which was his favorite. 

We finished our tour with drinking maybe 20 (if not more) cups of different teas and bought some to take back with us. 

Its a feee entrance place but they appreciate a donation which shouldnt be to individuals but to put into the box in the shop which will be contributed equally to the staff. 

Peaceful green place with a lot of birds, peacocks, flowers and heavenly beautiful view. Loved every minute of spending there.

Title: A complete experience
Text: Visited this tea plantation during our stay in Galle and it was fabulous. The tour guide walked us through all aspects of tea processing and took us through the plantation where there were lots of photo opportunities. Afternoon tea was served with a delicious choc cake and lastly we given a full tea tasting experience. There was no charge for the tour, but donations were encouraged.

Title: Excellent tour, friendly guide!
Text: We visited this tea plantation in March 2018.  We were in Sri Lanka during a time of torrential rain, so our guided tour was aided by umbrellas!  We were greeted with warmth and care, and set off to discover the plantation and all that it has to offer.  We were shown how the tea was picked and made in the factory.  After the tour, we were able to visit the shop.  We were under no pressure to buy, but we were amazed at the number of teas available to taste, and purchase.  It was a far better tea plantation and tour than several others we visited.  I would recommend Handunugoda Tea Estate to anyone wanting to learn from people who have a passion for tea.

Title: Fabulous tour
Text:
We went here by tuk tuk from Galle.   The guide was informative, funny and showed
us many thinks. we saw the tea pickers which were fascinating to watch.  We then enjoyed a cup of tea and chocolate cake before looking in the small factory.  We all enjoyed this trip even our 15 year old granddaughter.
thank you all.

Title: Tea factory ;friendly people and nice tase of teas
Text:
My friends and I get here from center of Ahangama around 20mins by tuktuk, the local guide is so nice and friendly, he can speak many languages which he made guest who visit here were more comfortable.

Gave many important information on differents kinds of tea in plantation area, including pepper, rubber, hibicus,etc. 

And last part is about tea shop, good to taste many cups of tea. End up buy the combination of many taste which called "TEA Flirt"

Recommend to visit to see local plantation and relaxing nature

Prair B from Thailand

Title: Tea for Two
Text: We made this a part of our day touring between Galle and Weligama and in the first instance we were surprised that tipping was discouraged, a donation was promoted at the conclusion of the tour but no pressure. The estate is a working property so you see people going about their business while learning how white & black tea is made. After walking through the plantation we were treated to a cup of oolong tea and a piece of chocolate cake, very appreciated. Afterwards we were given a tour of the factory with machines still operational after a hundred years. There was the mandatory visit to a tasting room and shop but I reiterate, we never felt under any pressure to buy or donate, although we did. An hour or so well spent.

Title: Factory with old colonial flair. Great tea tasting
Text:
The stroll through the tea bushes is not as striking as in an altitude plantation, but you can see several spice trees and plants on the way. The factory machines are more than a century old and still in use. The tea shop is a treat for any quality tea lover.

It's all free, and there's a tip jar by the cashier, split among the staff, if you are happy.

Title: Just a taster!
Text:
We visited the Tea Estate at the end of a one day tour of Galle and its surroundings.  It was just a flying visit but we saw the plants, the drying houses and machinery used in making the tea. 
At the end of the tour we had the chance to taste the teas and buy the product. 
Sri Lanka is famous for its tea and so a visit to a plantation is essential. It was interesting and I do not think we would have got anymore from the the visit if we had been there longer.

Title: I had no Idea
Text: I never knew how we got tea!! What an experience! I was disappointed that we didn't get to taste the different teas.  I would have given 5 stars for the opportunity to tase a variety.  Perhaps for a fee you could taste 5 different teas. Like a flight of beer! We bought several teas and were not disappointed at all.

Title: Interesting tour and very knowledgeable guide!!
Text: We came here as recommended in the lonely planet guide and by friends! We had Xavier as our guide and he was incredibly knowledgeable about all of the trees and teas and we were astonished by his ability to fluently speak so many different languages! We were given a choice about whether we wanted to go on a short or long tour - our group chose the long tour and it was interesting to learn about all of the products that this plantation grows. Tea and cake at the bungalow was a nice touch but the real highlight was the factory! We were able to see the old machines working and the different processes were explained in detail to us. We were then taken to the shop where we were able to taste all of the teas that we could buy, I didn't feel pressured to buy anything, however I am extremely happy with what I did buy! The bags that are given to you are lovely souvenirs and you are also given several information sheets about the plantation and their teas! Definitely recommend a visit!

Title: Worth a visit - complimentary tour and tea tasting.
Text: While in the former Ceylon, must get to a Tea Plantation. The very basic tour is free and so is the tea tasting, which was fantastic. The plantation is approximately 20km from Galle and easy to get there by tuk tuk.

Title: Nice Visit - Great vodka Tea
Text:
We called here after a recommendation by a tuk tuk driver. It was a very pleasant and informative visit. Our guide took great pride in his knowledge and use of many languages. We stopped half way round for a cup of oolong tea which we both enjoyed. Next, a visit to the factory where we were shown many various machines for the production of the tea from drying leaves to the finished product. The next part was tea tasting and there was many to choose from including vodka tea. 

Very interesting. Free to visit here and no pressure at all to buy anything.

Title: Fun (free!) tour
Text: An interesting tour of the plantation and little factory, with a cup of tea and cake thrown in, ending in a nice shop with opportunity to taste lots of teas and tea-related gifts.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: We had a wet afternoon in Unawatuna so took a tuktuk to handunugoda. Thoroughly enjoyed it. A free tour that lasted an hour or so including being served tea and cake and having a guide explain the process of tea making and show us the plants and machinery used, as well as coffee plants, cinnamon trees and rubber trees. At the end we were able to taste 30 different types of tea and could buy any ones we liked. Some of the teas were pricey to buy but we bought a box of one we liked the taste of which cost us 750rupees, we considered it a donation for the tour that we enjoyed. There was no pressure to buy or tip

Title: Interesting & nice visit.
Text: We enjoyed our tour of this Tea Estate. It is small so it doesn't take very long but it was very pleasant. We loved seeing the 150 year machiniery still working. We did buy some tea but never felt under any pressure to do so.

Title: Enjoyable and educational
Text:
Our family enjoyed the complimentary tour of the plantation and factory, it was very interesting to see the process and was of course great to try the different teas at the end of the tour! Also thought it was a nice touch that they gave us chocolate cake and sapphire oolong tea on the porch.

Also worth mentioning there wasn't any pressure to buy any tea or other merchandise at the end of the tour.

Title: Nice tea but a bit of a tourist trap
Text: Great teas but expensive and a bit of a tourist trap where drivers drop busloads of people off and encourage purchases for commission.

Title: Lovely trip for afternoon tea, village mini-tour and beautiful tea plantation
Text: Traveled out with tuc tuc from Fortress Resort for couple of hours. (1500-1800 rupees)Very interesting and enjoyable explanation of tea process and reasonably priced, good quality tea selection to buy.

Title: Very informative
Text: I had no idea there were so many different types of tea.  The factory was very interesting.  It was quite educational to see how they process the tea.  They have a little store where you can taste all the teas and buy the ones  you like.  It was a very beautiful tea plantation.  I also liked seeing the rubber trees and feel the sap.

Title: Morning Trip
Text: This is a free guide around a tea plantation. They take you around in groups and explain the processes. We had a cup of tea and chocolate cake which was Devine. The factory was very interesting and informative. The tea tasting and shop was great with no pressure to buy or leave a voluntary tip which goes into a box to be shared by all who work there. Well worth a visit.

Title: Lovely Stuff!
Text:
Informative and funny guide.
No entrance fee and no pressure to buy.
Cool little gift shop with loads of teas lined up.
Also, the tuk tuk driver who took us waited for us.

Title: Informative and free!
Text: This was a great place to learn about the tea industry and sample the goods.  We were treated respectfully and got all of our questions answered.  The tour itself was free, as were the samples and some delicious chocolate cake, and we spent a bunch on amazing teas to take home.  Highly recommend!

User_Location: Prague, Hlavni Mesto Praha, Czech Republic
Title: Best tea tasting
Text: We rent scooters in Unawatuna for a day and visited this factory in the morning. Short walk with an experienced quide who takes you through the plantation to have a nice cup of tea and cake on the porch of an old house at the top of plantation. But don't expect any spectacular views. For those you must visit the central highlands (Nuwara Eliya, Haputale, Ella). Machines in the factory weren't working. Production of white tea is shown just on tv on the tea center. In the tea center we finally had very nice tea tasting (around 30 samples) and that was what were were looking for. Prices for the tea are much higher than in the north. Worth visit if you haven't been to any other plantation.

Title: Super tour guide!
Text: We had an excellent tour of the estate with a very friendly and funny guide! He was super knowledgeable and always brought the information back to us with a personal connection--like tea's importance to America's independence etc. he even had a little book with common phrases in various languages so he could make all of his guests feel at home/comfortable! I was shocked that there wasn't more pressure to buy things at the end of the tour considering they gave us free tea and cake in the middle of it! Wish they had more small packets of tea or even a sampler pack in the shop to buy instead of the larger quantities of a single type of tea! Overall this was an awesome relaxing and informative little half day trip from Mirissa and I would recommend it to anyone in the area looking for something other than beach related activities to fill a day!

Title: Family day out with parents
Text: Great short day trip if you are staying in the Ahangama area.. a brief tour through then plantation a complementary cup of tea and cake, quick peek at the machinery,  then the opportunity to sample countless varieties of tea and select your favourites if you wish to buy.

Title: Great visit
Text: Knowledgeable guide explains the tea plantation and how its collected. You get served a free tea an piece of cake. You proceed to the factory where you are shown how to get from fresh cut plants/leaves to the tea as you know it. You see the old machin while they work, its really interesting. You finish at a shop were you can taste the different varieties and get no pressure to buy though you most definitely want to get some !

Title: Tea explained, also sipped, sampled and sold at Handunugoda Tea Estate
Text: An experienced guide tells the story of tea planting, cultivation and harvesting with humor and detail on a walk through the plantings.  He graciously answers questions as you sip a cup on the garden terrace.  Next a second guide narrates the process of withering, rolling, fermenting, grading and selling.  Employees are operating the machines as you walk through the factory.  Finally you enter the tasting room for an opportunity to sample teas grown in many areas of Sri Lanka.  Shelves are stocked with attractively packaged boxes of all the teas so you can purchase your favorites.

Title: Tea and spice tour
Text: Very well run tour with obvious emphasis on tea, but also on spices that grow on the property. They also have a nice store where you can buy a large variety of teas as well as books on the history and cultivation of tea leaves.

Title: Lovely tea plantation
Text: Great tour, entertaining guide, beautiful tea plantation. Free of charge and includes tea and cake at the house. Fabulous!

Title: Wonderful tour of the tea estate and factory
Text: We were only at the beach in Sri Lanka on holiday with the family but I really wanted to visit a tea estate.  Fortunately our villa manager organised a visit for us to the Handugoda Tea Estate and this proved to be excellent.  We were taken on a nice short walking tour through the tea plantations and then served tea and cake in a beautiful old colonial house in the estate.  This was followed by a guided visit to the factory and then to the shop.  There was no charge for the visit other than a request for a tip for the staff and the opportunity to shop int he store.  It was a wonderful visit which we really enjoyed.

Title: The Ceylon Tea
Text: This is a small holding tea estate, but has Variety of other plants and spices. The Manager David has Depth knowledge of tea Industry and Productions, This Place easy to visit from Your Coastal hotel. The owner Herman Gunaratne a legendary tea planter, who started his planting days during the British Raj. A visit will make you to realise Sri Lanka is  a  different country.

Title: A fun outing
Text: This is a lovely way to see a tea plantation. Our guide was knowledgeable and friendly. He showed us the different types of leaves and described the different ways to make tea as well as how their specialty tea was created and its health benefits. There is a tea and cake stop halfway through which is nice. You are then able to try a large variety of teas with no pressure to buy. A nice morning out.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Was given a tour of the Virgin White Tea Plantation by Meril, who was very friendly and knowledgeable.  Did not realise they made so many varieties of tea on the estate, also the numerous other flowers and trees they had growing.  Tour is free but a request is to leave a tip in the jar of the shop at the end; it gets divided between all staff.  Loved how they have a dedicated carer for a lame ex-racehorse that lives on site, and enjoyed tea and cake with Lara the Golden Lab.  Beautiful site and location. Found it really interesting that they use mostly the same technology for processing the tea as when they first started over a hundred years ago.  A great finish is the tasting session at the end of the tour.  Would recommend a visit by anyone wanting to see a working tea plantation.

Title: So interesting
Text: Our local guide stopped us as something interesting to do and he was so right. It's entrance free and the guide showed us everything, tea, rubber trees, flowers, coffee you name it! He offered is a free cup of a spectacular oolong tea and some cake before they took us to the factory where you very to see how the tea is made. Loved every second!

Title: Interesting tour, tea tasting and beautiful grounds
Text:
There is something for everyone on this tour. Whether you are interested in the full process of plant to packet tea manufacture, tasting and comparing many different teas, hearing the history of tea in Sri Lanka or enjoying the wildlife that thrives here - you'll find it on this plantation. Our guide Meril was a wealth of knowledge and very friendly and you could see that he was very proud of what this tea company has accomplished. 

We were staying in Galle and it was a short drive through the beautiful countryside to the plantation. Some chose to go there by tuk-tuk, so it's not too far. You'll see some wild life getting there but so much more in the plantation - particularly birds. Monkeys were also there during our visit. Comfortable walking shoes would be wise

Although you are encouraged to taste test around 30 different teas (for free) there is no pressure to by anything, although you can. We brought home some of the tastiest tea we have ever had. We met a Sri Lankan man in Koggala who has lived in England for many years. He travels to Sri Lanka every year to visit family and buys a years supply of tea from this plantation before returning home. Yes it's that good.

Title: History, culture and refined taste
Text: At Handunugoda you can learn the history of the White Tea, understand the special care that is needed to harvest the leafs. stroll through the entire manufacturing process of the tea, taste different kinds of teas and take home a remarkable souvenir of the country. A complete experience

Title: Long ride from Colombo
Text: Unfortunately we were sold a "bill of goods" by tour agency that we could visit both tea plantation and The Dutch Fortress in 6 hours from Colombo.  The plantation is easily 2 to 2 1/2 hours from the city (we left port area at 6:30 am).   I agree with another reviewers that staff is incredible friendly and that the tea served was excellent (if not pricey compared to shops in the city).  Also disappointed that we did not see workers actually in fields with famed "virgin white tea".  Supposedly never touched by human hands.

Title: Nice free educational tour
Text:
Very close to Ahangama this tea estate is situated, where we dropped by unannounced.
A guide was readily available and showed us for free, what is growing at their estate, which was more than only tea. Something I did not expected.
He showed us the black pepper, coffee bean plant, rubber trees and cinnamon tree. And explained how it was harvested in good English.
Then we got some tea with chocolate cake, which my kids loved. I bearly managed to eat my own piece...
A shame that they do not sell it!
The small factory looked authentic en clean. 
Off course the free tour ended in a little shop where one could taste all the blends available. Even though the prices were high (higher than back home), we bought one package of tea and cinnamon to clear our guilt of enjoying a free tour.

Title: Lovely tour and beautiful grounds
Text: A really nice way to spend a morning or afternoon.  Take the kids, they will have a blast picking flowers and running through the grounds.

Title: Wonderful tea plantation!
Text:
We loved this place. Peaceful and beautiful, lovely staff and great tasting tea. The courteous staff give you a tour of the estate, tea bushes and manufacturing; you then taste some tea and eat some chocolate cake. The surroundings are really beautiful and the story of Virgin White Tea really is a lovely one.

There is a lovely shop with all of the teas and there is no pressure to buy at all. Of course you do though.

We arranged a private driver to take us here from Ahungalla area which was perfect as it would be a little tricky finding this place alone.

Wonderful day though, wonderful place.

Title: Excellent free tour
Text:
Our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and friendly.

The tour is free and includes a short walk around the plantation to see the variety of tea growing on site, a delicious tea and chocolate cake break, visit to the production factory and ends with a tasting session of each tea produced. The tour isnt very long in duration but gives you a detailed overview of the tea production process 

In the shop you can buy all the teas produced on site including the very rare Virgin White tea

Title: A wonderful experience in the tea plantation
Text: My and my girlfriend were impressed by the tour. With all the interesting information, the cake and the tea tasting it was an outstanding experience. The tour is tip based wich we were more than happy to give!

Title: Definitely worth a visit
Text: This is a very picturesque family run plantation. The guy running the tours is a real character! It was very interesting to see the process of tea being made, and the antique machines.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Lovely place. The guide is very cheerful and also ready to give any explanation. After you have a brief tea information and get a taste of many different tea! They also have tea available for selling and Id suggest you to leave a tip in their tea room box. As this attraction is free of charge and they do make a good effort to serve you.

Title: A trip back in time
Text:
We loved this place.
We were lucky enough to get a very personal tour and insight into the estate as well as the tea making process.
Felt very colonial to be sipping tea and eating chocolate cake outside a planters bungalow in an absolute downpour.
The guide sorted out brollies for us and then we explored the very real delights of the original tea factory which due to its age is more like a working museum.it was great especially with the pouring rain teeming down on the corrugated roof felt very atmospheric.
Great tour really interesting and learned a lot while getting drenched.

Title: Interesting
Text: We had a stop here on our way back to the airport. It was really a nice stop.  Tour with a guide around the tea plantation was interesting. We also got to see the tea factory and also the taste different types of tea. The best of all: everything for free!

Title: Wonderfull Tea as it should be
Text: We spent the morning at the tea plantation loved the tea and learning about tea growing and processing

Title: An incredible few hours on route to Columbo
Text: A visit on route from Hambantota to Columbo and well worth it. Fascinating insights into tea and lots of other lovely delights - including pepper! Superb guide who knows everything about the tea and factory and a cup of tea and lovely piece of cake. A must see trip if you've in Sri Lanka.

Title: Tea Party
Text:
Enjoyed the tour of the tea plantation and came away knowing more about the topic and having sampled a range of interesting types. 
The tour is free and includes a guided trip round the property with well informed guide, tea and cake in the garden (they had me at "cake") and a tasting session of products available in the shop. Very nice low key and no hard selling.

Title: Great Tea Experience
Text: Very friendly staff on arrival. Free tour through the plantation with chocolate cake and tea in the garden halfway through the tour. The factory section is impressive as they turn the machines on to demonstrate if they arent running. The end of the tour involves a tasting of over 30 different teas including the expensive white tea. Very well organized and informative. Define recommend.

Title: wow!
Text: good place to visit. the manager was excellent and explained the whole process. we had a lovely time. Thank You.

Title: Very enjoyable
Text:
This is a lovely experience. Free tour of plantation and traditional tea processing with informative guide (ours was Meril). Very interesting to see tea but I also really enjoyed seeing peppercorns, cinnamon, rubber, jackfruit, cashew nut and starfruit trees plus lots of birds, butterflies and lizards!

Lovely cup of tea and chocolate cake. They ask for a donation to be shared amongst staff which we were more than happy to provide along with buying some tea. Thoroughly recommend.

Title: Best tea estate!
Text:
We have been to many tea plantations in Sri Lanka and also Malaysia. This was one of the best! We not only learnt about tea, but also cinnamon, pepper and rubber! After a lovely walk, we sat down and enjoyed a cup of tea and a piece of cake (we had not paid for anything thing yet!). The tea tasting was fantastic- could sample all the teas for sale, and there was an information sheet to help you too. 
It was a welcomed change for this area to find somewhere so lovely, few people and no pressure to buy. 
Highly recommended.

Title: Enjoyable
Text: Visited in 2013 and enjoyed it so much we visited again. Unfortunately, the tour is shorter than in the past and tea is no longer provided at the Gunaratne bungalow (Herman Gunaratne has written books about Sri Lanka that are well worth reading). However, the tea and cake (free) and the brief but informative tour still worth doing. Its a very different experience from the tea plantations in the higher tea country so a must do activity to compare with Ella and Nuwara Eliya experiences. They are the only manufacturer of Virgin White tea which can be tasted along with many other varieties in their shop. They also sell Herman Gunaratnes books along with other thoughtful souvenirs. The tour of the manufacturing process was excellent.

Title: Interesting and stunning location, tea heaven!
Text: If you are a tea drinker, then this is the place to go, with over 50 different types of tea, a truly wonderful interesting place, with great chocolate cake!

Title: Tea Tasting Supreme....
Text:
Just back from Sri Lanka and visited Handunugoda Tea Plantation, so interesting to see the process from start to finish and taste some of the many offerings.                                       Of particular note here is the Virgin White Tea - untouched by human hands from the harvesting through production to the caddy, produced at this estate and highly sought around the world. 
Our tour of the planation finished with a welcomed cup of Ruby Oolong tea and a chunky slice of delicious chocolate cake .... yum!
Highly Recommended.

Title: A must do if you're in Galle
Text: Really wanted to get to a tea plantation while I was here in Sri Lanka. Handunugoda was raved about in town. It's about 40 minutes from Galle Fort. Free tour, hot tea and cake. You can sample up to 60 varieties and there are plenty to purchase.

Title: An authentic tea factory that is unique.
Text:
Having initially been quoted anything from 20 to 30 American dollars, which they said included the entrance fee we opted to be taken there by our trusted tuk tuk driver Isuru.
On our arrival, having been driven through beautiful countryside and rice paddy fields we arrived at the estate to be met by a charming elderly Sinalese gentleman whose first words were,  I am going to take you on a tour of the estate, it is completely free of charge. The speciality tea is white tea. He walked us through the estate giving a running commentary on tea production, rubber and cinnamon production before we went to the plantation house where we sat down on the veranda to be served Ruby Oolong tea with milk accompanied by one of the nicest pieces of cake we have ever eaten. We went round the working factory with machines over 145 years old. I will not reveal further as the tour guide explains everything. After this we went to the shop and tasted 20 or more teas and purchased those we liked.

Title: Very interesting tour of a very old tea estate
Text:
We visited this unique tea estate on our recent visit to Sri Lanka and would recommend it highly. I did not realise ho little I knew about the tea making process! The guides are well informed and friendly, and give a full tour of the estate, including the tea plantations, the tea processing factory and also include a stop at a quaint tea room on the estate (the chocolate cake was delicious!) You get the chance to sample over 20 different teas, and also to purchase them. 
A very educational and informative half day trip.

Title: Tea for Seven
Text: I had no idea I would enjoy a tea tour so much! We had a group of seven - went on the early bird tour- and everyone thoroughly enjoyed it. Merle, our guide, spoiled us with his plethora of knowledge...he was so very kind! We also saw some great wild life- a peacock in a tree- wild monkeys... The variety of tea is amazing - you will definitely find one of your liking. A definite must if you have a leisurely day to spend in Sri Lanka.

Title: Tea and more tea
Text: I thought I knew tea, until I came here!  A short walk through the gardens to see how tea is grown, and peppercorns,  and cinnamon, and jackfruit, and hibiscus, to sit down for a cuppa and some cake.  Then a tour of the fascinating factory and a chance to taste so many different teas. The guides are very entertaining.  Of course you will want to buy some to take home.  We did.

Title: Day trip
Text: It was very informative & beautiful scenery. Personal guide to show you around with taste testing of all the varieties. Had a great time

Title: A highlight of our trip
Text: We were shown around the plantation by an informative guide, served tea and cake at the homestead which was relaxing, then shown through the tea factory and to the gift shop at the end where you could try all sorts of teas. The whole thing was free but they have a donation box at the end and tips are shared between all the guides, which was a nice way to do it. We thoroughly enjoyed it, even our daughter who does not like tea. Beautiful part of the world but a bit tricky to find.

Title: A jewel of Sri Lanka
Text: Really wanted to visit a tea plantation not too far from Bentota.  Far exceeded my expectations.  The people were so kind, patient, informative - and not obviously interested in your money, so unlike the culture I am used to.  The guide showed us through the plantation, the tea, rubber, herbs, explaining key points.  We were given ta and cake!  The factory, comprising of British Empire imported machinery, still in use, was so interesting. The shop was a final stop with a huge selection of tea tasting set out for us.  There was really no expectation of us to buy, but what we did buy was the best tea I have tasted.  Wish I had bought more.  The highlight of my holiday.

Title: Fascinating
Text: We recently visited this tea plantation. We had a tour of the plants, then we had a cup of tea with chocolate cake before seeing the factory process. Very interesting and there was no hard sell or pressure to buy the tea.  Worth a visit if your in the area.

Title: Picturesque tea estate
Text: A short tea tour around this beautiful estate is a nice attraction. The degustation of tea with the cake is probably the best part. It is comfortable to taste various teas in the selling room. Prices are quite high even for ordinary brands.

Title: see how tea is made
Text: An interesting hour or so at the tea factory learning about how tea is produced. Free entry and no hard sell at the gift shop so a pleasant experience overall.

Title: Beautiful setting and good way to fill an hour or so
Text: We found this trip via trip advisor and glad we did! From kottawa we took a tuktuk to the plantation. We were welcomed by the guide who gave us a tour of the tea growing and the production plant. We also could try some tea and cake in the lovely tea house. In addition to tea, he also showed us the rubber, cinnamon, coffee and peppercorn plants growing on the plantation. Everything was free and the tipping is restricted to a box at the end which is shared between all staff. The shop at the end sells tea produced at the plantation

Title: good tour
Text:
This place seems to be set up for tourists, which doesn't make it worthless, just predictable. 
You can see the different tea plants, rubber plants, cinnamon, and many other types of plants.
Tour guide was good, got to walk around the plants, then the factory, drink some tea and then the shop at the end. 
Honestly an enjoyable 1+ hours.
If you're in the area, go.
BTW, white tea is expensive!

Title: Quirky little tea factory
Text:
We stopped into to this estate on the drive through to Galle, and were pleasantly surprised at this quirky little establishment. 
While we were never really sure what was going on, we were served a lovely afternoon tea (tea and cake, at no cost), followed by a tour of the gardens and tea factory, and then a tasting of over 20 different house-made teas.

We had the most unique tour guide, whose school-master type persona somehow led to us having a great time throughout the tour.

While its a little off the main drag, and not as entirely informative as other more generic plantation tours, it was certainly a worthwhile detour.

Title: Beautiful. Friendly staff. Variety of teas.
Text:
Meril our tour guide was very kind and knowledgable.

Herman was the plantation owner and mentioned its been in the family for 120 years as cocunut and rubber plantation. They still produce rubber. It comes as a sap from a tree in white colour. Herman turned this into tea plantation for only last 25 years.

Its the only tea plantation that produces virgin white tea. 

I did notice cheaper priced teas in hikkaduwa stores. About half the price so maybe 900SLR for 100grs. Vs 300 SLR for 100grs. Not sure what the shop qualities were as I'm not a tea conisure but buying at the plantation ensures direct pay for the staffs hard work.

Definitely a must do while in Sri Lanka. Plenty of plantations around but avoid the touristic ones. Note that they all have early closing times so be sure to arrange based on the hours of operation for the plantation you chose to go to.

Title: Average
Text: The drive there was the most interesting bit. We got there and were told to join a group that had done most of the tour. We saw rubber trees, coffee trees and pepper trees, little to none explanation, then got taken to a tea terrace to taste their sapphire tea and choc cake which was ok. Then we asked to join another group to actually hear about the tea plants themselves, this lasted for about 7 minutes, to which then we joined yet another group to go to the final stage of seeing the machinery which was interesting and then off to the shop. Relatively overpriced tea although it does look quite labour intensive. All in all you need 30 minutes and good luck to get a good guide. I would recommend it only if you are really into tea or maybe try another plantation, not much effort put into this. I know this is a free service and thats great, however I wouldnt mind paying for a more organised and insightful tour.

Title: Very informative and interesting tour
Text:
Our driver was a bit surprised we wanted to go here. He had never heard of the place and was very curious how we learned about it (thanks tripadvisor). 

The whole experience was great.  Our guide spoke very good English and was very knowledgable. We got to see not only tea plants but also coffee, rubber, pepper and hibiscus. After walking a bit through the estate we stop at a tea house for a free sample of tea and chocolate cake. Both were very good.  We then headed to the manufacturing area. It was really interesting to see how they dry the leaves, separate and grade the leaves. Most of the machines seemed to be very old machines from colonial times.  Finally our tour ended at the store. There was no pressure to buy tea (but we did). The store had samples available for tasting of all the different varieties. Overall it was a great experience that both kids and adults found interesting.

Title: Fantastic and unexpected delight hidden in the lush countryside!
Text: As we had planned a trip to Nuwara Eliya for later in our travel itinerary, we were uncertain about whether to also visit this tea plantation.  We are so pleased that we did go!  It was fantastic!! The tour guide was very knowledgeable and friendly and we were shown all the plants grown on the plantation including white tea, cinnamon, pepper and coffee.  The tour included a complimentary tasting of sapphire Oolong tea and chocolate  cake on the beautiful verandah.  The tour culminated in the tea processing factory and we were shown the drying, sorting and processing of the res leaves.  The highlight of this visit was the colourful tropical plants and lush scenery as well as the serenity of the countryside.  I would highly recommend a visit.

Title: Rewarding tour of established tea estate with high tea in colonial setting
Text: Knowledgable guides and exquisite setting (esp. the quaint manor house on the hill which we visited for a slice of cold cake and a cup of white tea). Groves of tea hemmed by colourful flowering bushes and trees. Both the tour of the estate and the tea tasting is free (a welcome touch). We bought the book 'The suicide club' written by the plantation-owner and are finding it an enjoyable read. He is quite a card. We also purchased some of the tea after the tasting, for gifting. A tuk tuk driver was willing to take us to the plantation from Ahangama for 600 rupees return. A highlight for us.

Title: Now we know how tea is made, well done!
Text:
We enjoyed our visit, very well done. Of course it is geared towards tourists, but you don't feel scammed, there is true pride in the people who show you around.
Asides from tea you also see rubber, cinnamon and pepper trees.
The tea tasting is fun as well. Ok, the prices at the shop are anything but bargain, but we didn't mind paying a little more for the experience, also, there was no pressure.

Title: Informative, friendly and well worth a visit
Text: A great option for experiencing a tea plantation close to Galle. You get a tour of the plantation and to see how tea, rubber and cinnamon are grown and harvested. Theres also a chance to sample a wide range of teas in a lovely tasting room at the end.

Title: Tea tour
Text:
What a great informative visit. It takes you through history it the tea story and how it started out in Sri Lanka. Very very informative guides who spoke really good English. 

An opportunity to taste all the different teas produced at the plantation so you can take one home to your liking rather than guess. 

I will definitely recommend a visit to here.

Title: Informative and Interesting
Text: It was a great experience. I went with my family (there are 8 of us) and we were provided with a brilliant tour from Romesh, our guide. We received a cup of tea grown at the plantation and a slice of cake. You are also able to buy some of the teas and the signature 'white tea' at the shop at the end of the tour. We all had a good time.

Title: Informative tour
Text:
We arrived here via tuk tuk from Unawatuna - easy journey took about 30 minutes. 

We were ushered straight into a small group for a tour around the tea plantation by a local
guide who spoke great English. Complimentary Oolong tea and chocolate cake were served before moving onto the factory to see how the tea is produced. 

Finished at their on site shop where a variety of teas and products are available. Absolutely no pressure to buy and no fee for the tour - a communal tip jar is available. 

An interesting couple of hours overall!

Title: Interesting & surprising.
Text:
Really interesting tour.
Not only tea but rubber, cinnamon & coffee.
Never realised there were so many tea flavours.
The factory still used the original machinery over 145 years old.
The tasting is fantastic.

Title: Informative Tea Tour
Text: This is huge plantation where they harvest tea, rubber, pepper and cinnamon.  There is no cost for the tour.  There is a shop where you can taste all the different types of tea.  There is no pressure to buy.  Our guide Xavier explained in detail the process of how tea is made.  Along the tour he showed us how rubber is extracted from the trees and showed us the cinnamon trees and pepper vines.  The explanation of how white tea is harvested is fascinating.

Title: Brilliant and a bloody good laugh!
Text: We had ventured out from our hotel on a tuc tuc tour and our driver took us to this tea plantation and factory as one stop on our mornings ride. We were mixed with a number of other Europeans and guided by a wizened Sri Lankan gentleman with a wicked sense of humour. My understanding of tea and how it is grown and prepared for sale is almost 100 per cent greater for this tour. There is plenty of time to look around the plantation and not just at tea plants. There is a lovely stop for tea and cake before visiting the factory. It is astonishing to see some of the old equipment still working today. You finish off with a great tea tasting and the chance to buy some home grown and produced tea and there is no pressure to buy. The tour was made memorable by the banter between our guide and the members of our group. Expect to take 1.5 hours for the whole experience. Brilliant!!

Title: Surprising and interesting
Text:
It is a free tour although you have the option to leave a small token in the tea tasting room. It is a very pleasant stroll to the tea house, where along the way they also show you collecting sap from rubber trees. The view from the tea house is pretty special and you are served cake and your choice of teas.
The walk through the tea processing building is very interesting with some of the machinery being 148 years old and having manufactured by the same company that built the Titanic. 
You also get the opportunity to taste a range of teas at the end of the tour. Well worth a visit as the tuktuk ride up there takes you through the country side but is not very far from the toen.

Title: Tea Tasting
Text:
On a private Tuk-Tuk tour our driver took us to the Handunugoda Tea Estate. The tour guide was very informative and showed us around the estate showing us the various plants, and how they make tea. 

We were then served chocolate cake and tea which were both really nice. We then tasted around 40 different teas in the visitors centre. Id recommend the masala tea. 

Overall a good experience.

Title: Great tour
Text: We had a very knowledgeable guide who explained all about the different types of tea and we had a slice of chocolate cake and cup of Saphire Pekoe on the owners verandah before going to the factory and then tasting all 50 varieties of tea they produce. Of course there is a shop to buy if you want but no high pressure sales. Highly recommended.

Title: So many teas to taste
Text: Loved the personal tour. The authentic tea estate and factory. Very well organised and friendly. Complimentary cup of tea and cake.

Title: If you in the area.........
Text:
I was interested to read the comments in these pages from the Poor and Average  contributors.They may have a point. It seemed to be a long way to go for little reward. On arrival a quick walk up the hill for a cup of tea and chocolate cake with a brief explanation of the Estate's purpose on the way. Down again to the factory  (impressive machinery by the way). Taste something cold and wet  and leave avoid paying LKR800 (£3.60 or thereabouts) for a few grams of tea leaves. I suppose first time visitors to a plantation may be impressed.

If you really want to be impressed,  travel to the Kandy/Newara Eliya regions in Central Province. Camellia Sinesis as far as the eye can see.

Title: Very Nice Working Tea Estate
Text: Ive been to a number of tea estates as a child during visits to Sri Lanka and assumes they were all in the hill country in the centre of the island; so I was very surprised to find the Handunugoda Tea Estate near Galle. Upon arriving we were greeted by one of the team who showed us around the grounds where tea, coffee, cinnamon and even rubber are grown. The staff were accommodating and friendly, even giving our family a sample of tea and chocolate cake before we were shown around the factory and then into the purchasing area where you can sample just about all the teas that are grown here. Really interesting visit and  great tea! Recommended

Title: Great experience
Text:
We were staying in Galle and took a taxi which took about 40 minutes. Xavier led our tour and was very knowledgeable about all aspects of the plantation. We had a few different nationalities in our group and Xavier was able to communicate with all of them. The tea and cake on the veranda was a lovely touch and a chance to chat to others in the group. 

The whole process of getting the tea from picking to packaging was fascinating and the 140 year old machinery still being used daily was a sight to behold. 

After a tour of about an hour we were led to the gift shop for a chance to taste many different teas and purchase if we wanted. This was so helpful and meant we didn't buy the ones we didn't like the taste of. Most of the teas were reasonably priced although some of the more specialised were a bit more expensive. And really, if you're getting a free tour why wouldn't you want to buy something as a thank you. As for the tip jar, well this is shared by all the employees on the plantation so why not give generously and help these lovely people to have a little extra for their families. I don't understand why some people complain about being pressured - there was absolutely no obligation to buy anything. We had very memorable couple of hours - thank you Handungoda.

Title: Only visit if no time for the Hill country
Text: Not very informative. Pushy guide. We had a much more interesting tour in Ella. Nice tea and cake though. Expensive tea in the shop.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
The tour of this tea plantation was recommended to us and we found it to be very informative.  The guide was able to speak a large number of languages and initially showed us around the plantation, teaching us about the history, the cultivation of virgin tea, various other plants and trees in the area.  During this tour we went to a plantation bungalow where we were given tea (to drink) and cake.  The tour continued in the buildings, where the British equipment was still working and ended in watching  a short video, sampling the numerous teas and checking out the teas on sale.
We thought the teas were quite expensive, if they had been a more reasonable price I think more tourists would have purchased them for gifts.  (This was the same in other tea plantation shops).

Title: Interesting and fun
Text: Very interesting tour around the Handunugoda Tea Estate. Not only learnt about their unique tea but also saw coffee plants, teak and rubber trees, pepper plants and cinnamon. Our guide was excellent, informative and friendly. Tea and delicious cake at the plantation house was lovely. A vast selection of teas were available to taste following the tour of the tea processing. So glad we went- couldnt believe it was free! Dont hesitate to go.

Title: Great place
Text: We stopped here on part of a tour and it was excellent. Our guide was great and explained all about the tea. It was a nice touch to get to try the tea and have some cake before looking at the actual factory and then the shop. You also get to try lots of teas. Definitely worth a visit!

Title: Visit with kids
Text: Been to this place multiple times over the years and it is always a lovely experience. Herman, the owner, is a real character too. Well worth putting on your itinerary if you are in the Southern Province.

Title: Excellent Informative Afternoon
Text: We visited the tea estate for an afternoon with the family. Perfect way to spend an afternoon. Very helpful guide explained the process of tea production, from the tea pluckers to the drying room. Tea and delicious cake in the very pretty garden, with flowers and birds. Finally tea tasting and the opportunity to purchase. We even had an extra tour round the estate looking for peacocks! A really lovely afternoon.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: I use trip advisor all the time but rarely write posts. This however is worth writing. The tea factory & plantation are well worth a visit, its very uncrowded unlike some of the bigger places and the tour guides are exceptionally knowledgable. All the staff were extremely friendly and even though obviously a business and the tour is free, we didnt pressure to buy anything! We bought & tipped because both the tea & tour were very good quality.

Title: Fascinating and free!
Text: Well worth a visit. Our guide (Meril) was very knowledgable and there was no pressure to buy tea at the end of the tour (although of course we did!) Just to taste over 20 teas was a great experience but the chocolate cake at the owner's house was perfect!

Title: A Gem Of The Trip
Text: Great place to stop off for a couple of hours and to meet the staff and to learn about the production of tea. We were guided around the facility by Xavier - thoroughly knowledgable and a source of information throughout. The opportunity to sit and to eat cake and drink tea in such beautiful and stunning scenery after a long drive was extremely welcome. The location itself is completely isolated - surrounded by the most idyllic and enchanting scenery. The shop itself is not overpriced and you continue to have the opportunity whilst in there to try all different types of tea. No pressure to purchase.

Title: Tea Plantation Tour
Text:
We thoroughly enjoyed the free tour with our guide Xavier. He was very knowledgeable about the whole process and particularly proud of their traditional methods, particularly the virgin 
white tea.
The tea and chocolate cake were delicious and the tasting session was enjoyable too. There was no pressure to buy in the shop, but of course we did! Im looking forward to trying my Suicide Club tea!

Title: FREE AND AMAZING
Text: Please, please visit! The tour is free and they take you on the most charming tour through the estate, you get to see cinnamon trees, rubber trees, cocoa trees, etc! They have beautiful gardens with flowers, and with tea of course! It's a lovely way to spend an afternoon!

Title: Great tour
Text:
Virgin white tea plantation 
Here they harvest rubber, tea and cinnamon 
No charge for entry you give a donation on exit 
A guide took us round explaining about the teas showed us how the tea was picked, harvested and manufactured into tea 
Very interesting 
We tried different teas to help us choose what we wanted to buy 
They take visa, that have toilets and we we're given a cup of tea and  a piece of cake 

Worth looking around and very interesting

Title: Great insight into the work that goes into a simple cup of tea.
Text:
Our guide Xavier was well informed and spoke several languages.

He provided us with an insightful tour of the tea estate, interspersed with some humour.  We learned a great deal more than expected about the making of tea and the resilience of the machinery still operating today to sort the tea. Some fascinating information.  The white tea did taste wonderful. 

The hard sell at the end was a little overwhelming and did dampen the overall experience. Still worth while and we bought a few spices to use on our return home.

Title: Wide variety of plants
Text:
It was interesting to see coffee, cinnamon, pepper and several types of tea growing. Our tour guide was very informative. We hiked up a hill looking at plants all the way and were served a cup of tea at the top. We went back down and saw how different types of tea are processed. Some of the equipment is about 150 years old and still functioning!
At the end of the tour you could taste all the teas they produce there. There was a short film too.
The tour was free. While there is no pressure to buy tea, the cost of the tea was not known until checkout and seems to have the cost of the tour built into it.

Title: Really enjoyable trip
Text: We spent a few hours here as part of a bigger tour and really enjoyed, the plantation itself is beautiful with lots more to see than just tea , there is a lovely house where they serve you tea and cake on the veranda , a tour of the factory and then a museum , all in all a very interesting and enjoyable few hours

Title: Good overview of tea process
Text:
This was a educational tour- got to learn a lot about the tea process from picking to processing. The visit is free of charge.
Its free to go to & the guide we had was excellent & really knowledgeable.
There is tea tasting & cake to enjoy.
There is a tea shop - which to be honest I thought was overpriced given you are buying from the source.
There is also a tip box in the shop - but this is at your discretion & there is no pressure to buy the tea or to tip

Title: A fun and informative visit
Text:
I wanted to visit a tea plantation but was worried about being in the south and not finding a good one...oh I was wrong! This place is wonderful. I was met by a smiling funny guide who walked me round the different tea areas and explained how the infusion process worked. He showed me the virgin white tea bushes (no touching) and then we sat and went through all the types of tea they produce whilst supping a lovely cuppa with a nice slice of chocolate cake made by a very shy lady. I then was shown the still working machines in the factory (some from the late 1800s) and learnt about the way the tips/leaves are turned into loose and bagged tea. I liked how they use both heavy old industrial methods alongside modern tech and the good old human hand! The shop is brilliant, a tea drinkers paradise with at least 40 to try and buy. 
I must mention my guides sense of humour! When, in my usual fashion, I questioned whether the ladies who worked on the virgin white section of the plantation still had to follow the Chinese tradition of remaining virgins whilst trimming the bushes he laughed...no sir, I dont think we would be able to harvest the tips if that was still the case Legend ! 
Lovely place, thoroughly recommended!

Title: Fantastic visit!
Text:
We planned to make quick stop, to at least have seen it. So wrong we planned...
It started with the background and the story behind the virgin white tea. Very interesting and honest. Then we went for a short walk; smelled fresh cinnamon, saw rubber, pepper before we ended up in a little cute tea house. Here we were served delicious tea with chocolate cake! We continued to walk to the tea factory where our guide explained the manufacturing process to produce tea, so interesting! Machines still working for 145 years, its like walking in a live museum.
After the factory we stopped at the gift shop in which we could taste all different kind of teas, so nice!
All this for no cost! We put a tip in the gift shop as that was the option given to us.
Highly recommend to make visit here!

Title: Highly recommend
Text: I searched tea plantations around Sri Lanka before I went and this place caught my eye due to the reviews so I waited until we got to Hikkaduwa and we decided to make a trip up as it would be very un Sri Lankan to not visit a tea plantation.  Our expectations were certainly met.  We were greeted with a pot of tea and some cake surrounded by the most lush green surroundings in the middle of tea fields this was for free.  It was amazing.  We did the tea tour as well which was also for free and very informative.  After the tour we went into the tea museum and tried all their teas.  I ended up purchasing quite a few teas and gave them a well deserved tip for their incredible hospitality.  I highly recommend holding off on other tea plantations which are more commercialized as this was well worth it.

Title: Interesting tour/ tea tasting
Text:
This is a small, multi-crop estate with rubber, cinnamon, black-pepper and the black and white teas.

Great tour guides who do a fair job of explaining the tea cultivation and manufacturing process.

The tasting eliminates the need for a hard-sell.  The quality of the product ensures that you end up buying your favorite teas from here

Title: Great visit
Text: Really enjoyable visit! Saw tea, coffee, peppercorns, rubber and pineapples growing. Guide was friendly and explained everything well. Free cup of tea and chocolate cake was very nice. Then visited the factory and saw the process the tea goes through before tea tasting in the shop. There was no pressure to buy anything in the shop and the guides don't accept tips, there is a box in the shop if you want to tip but you don't have to - we did as the guide was great and as a thank you for the tea and cake. Well worth visiting, highly recommended!!

Title: Very nice Tea Plantation
Text: If you're wanting to visit a tea plantation in the south this is worth a trip. They were very informative, had a country feel, tea and cake. Make sure you too though as you leave to help them as there is no cover charge for the entry. I love tea so I purchased my favourites. It's good understanding he process and seeing the different plants and trees here in Sri Lanka. Beware of tuk-tuk drivers taking you elsewhere.....avoid the herb gardens as they are a scam!

Title: Best Tea Estate in SRI LANKA
Text: Absolute must visit. Takes about an hour to do a tour. They do not accept individual tipping which is nice. A good tour, full of historic information. Beautiful scenery. The factory tour was exceptional. Up close to the machinery. Get to touch the tea. At the end there are all 40 teas to taste. They use the lemongrass, ginger and cinnamon  on the property to make their teas. Nothing goes to waste. I'm a beer drinker and this tour of tea was excellent. Of the 3 tea factories we visited this was by far the best and the cheapest!!! The others were way to busy (even in off season) and take advantage of tourists / customers. Handunugoda is genuine great tea and a great tour experience. Loved it.!

Title: Hot day at the tea estate
Text: We wanted to see how they produce the tea here in Sri Lanka, we were recommended to go fram Galle to Handunugoda Tea Estate, and we were not disappointed. A nice tuktuk ride to get there with lovely scenery and a hord of water buffalos in the middle of the road. At the estate we were greeted by our very knowledgable guide who showed us around the different plants and specifically the virgin white plan that is what they are most famous for. mid-tour we were served cake and tea and after the tour we got to try the whole range of teas, including the very exclusive "virgin white tea" all free of charge. I would highly recommend a visit to this lovely little place!

Title: Tea time!
Text:
We visited this small tea plantation as we had read good reviews about it. It was a three quarters of an hour tuk-tuk ride from Galle and the journey itself was interesting as we took the Matara Road which follows the coast. En route you are able to see the stilt fishermen at Welligama as well as the beautiful beach Mirissa.
The tea plantation was really interesting. We were shown around by a member of staff who pointed out the different teas as well as different trees (cinnamon for example). We were served tea and cake. At the end of the tour you are given a short talk by the owner and encouraged to sample as many of the teas on display as you would like.
You do not need to book for this tour which is completely free. It passes a very nice hour or two, particularly if like us you are in the middle of a tropical downpour. Go! You won't be disappointed

Title: Informative free tour and tea tasting
Text: This is definitely worth a visit. We learned about so many of the different plants growing on the state, including rubber trees and breadfruit. There is no hassle to buy anything, just a comfortable, enjoyable free tour with tea and coffee included. Well worth a visit!

Title: Hard sell
Text: We really enjoyed the tour looking at different plants but once we got to the shop the man got the hump because we wouldn't buy anything.

Title: Excellent Tea Estate
Text:
Fabulous tea plantation & factory and off the beaten track so even better as you see even more of very rural Sri Lanka.
Super tour of the estate, explanations of the different tea plants, also rubber, black pepper, coffee, lemongrass, jackfruit... 
Tea and cake on the terrace at the owner's villa felt very special followed by an incredibly interesting tour of the working factory and then tea tasting of 40 amazingly different varieties including Silver Tips, Golden Tips and Hundungoda's exclusive and exquisite Virgin White Tea. 
Highly recommend this Tea Plantation !

Title: Excellent day at Herman Teas in Handunugoda
Text:
