The tea plantation is the lowest lying tea plantation and the tea grown here offers richer deeper tastes. You need to know where you are going as it is not that easy to find it but it is worth it. The visit does not cost anything but you are expected ( but not obligated or pressured at all ) to leave a tip in the general tip box to be shared among all staff. It is a working plantation so you will see people in action from pickinng silver tips to sorting tea in the drying room. We had the pleasure of being shown how all the machines work - some of them are over 100 years old and in good working order. The pace is unhurried, you can take as much time as you want to stay on the property. There is a lovely tea verandah at the top of the hill - it is the owner's house after all - but they serve tea there to taste in a lovely plantation setting. The tasting room at the end of the tour is impressive and I think there are over 40 teas to try - they have a spitton luckily as otherwise you would end up hyper after trying just a few. 

While you stroll around the fields, you will see they also grow pepper here and sime rubber trees and it is fascinating to see how teas and spices grow side by side.

I highly recommend a visit here. It is equally interesting for adults as for kids.

Title: Very interesting, especially for tea lovers
Text: It is a little bit dificult to arrive there, so i recommend to take a tuk tuk. We found one that took us there and waited for us to finish the tour and took us back for 1200rp. I drink tea every day instead of coffee, but I never knew how diferent types of tea are made, that blac, white and green tea is the same plant! Our guide explained us the whole procedure, from a plant to a cup of tea. On this plantation you can see grow also hibiscus, lemon grass, pepper, coffee... In the end you can taste more than 30 different teas and decide which one you prefer the most. You can taste also the most expensive tea, virgin white tea which is picked very carefully and only 25g per day. The tour is free, but you can give tips in the end.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: We had a great tour guide who explained the whole process from picking the tea leaves to sampling many varieties. The tour starts with seeing and the guide explaining the tea plants & others like cinnamon and lemongrass. We then enjoyed tea and cake before seeing the factory and the whole process from start to finish.  We then tasted so many varieties I lost count.  The tour is free but they ask you to tip the lady who serves tea and cake (we left 200 LKR) and there's a donation box split amongst all staff at the end (we tipped 500 LKR).  They ask you not to tip individuals

Title: Tea heaven, but watch out for the 'sour grapes'! ;)
Text:
As the plantation is a little way inland you will need private transport or catch a Tuk Tuk from the main coast road (I paid 800Rs return including waiting time, negotiate before travelling)

My guide was a lovely friendly man who spoke very good english. He invited me to taste a rare sour grape, turned out to be peppercorns! He was very patient as I took photos and answered my many questions. The tea and cake were delicious, don't forget to leave a tip under the plate for the maid. The factory was fascinating, my mobile phone is 3yrs old and rubbish, these machines are over 100yrs old and still going strong! 

The tea tasting was amazing, although I felt I needed a glass of water to cleanse my mouth after a few tastes. Be aware that the tea is cold so tastes slightly different. Taste the famously expensive Virgin White Tea and the favourite tipple of HRH Queen Elizabeth (little nod to colonialism)

There was no pressure to buy after the tasting but the shop guide was very helpful in selecting a particular tea blend that you will enjoy.

Title: Lovely little detour
Text:
Firstly it's a free guided tour around something genuinely interesting and worth looking at.

Secondly from a world of tourism and hustle and bustle which are prominent on the south coast, it's a step in to a bit of calm and quiet.

It's obviously quite a "historical colonial" set up, but that period and the tea industry are both very important to the development of modern Sri Lanka.

Our guide, an older gentleman was very knowledgable and had a twinkle in his eye. He spoke with knowledge and a genuine interest in the topic. 

We tried some free tea (the lovely Sapphire Oolong) and cake (Chocolate) before a tour of the still operating factory involving machines over 100 years old.

The whole tour maybe takes about an hour and ends in a tasting/purchasing room. 

Obviously the tour is aimed at a purchase, but there is no hard sell and the product is genuinely worth buying at a reasonable price.

I'd highly recommend any tea drinker, lover of history or someone just wanting to unwind to go and treat yourself to a decent brew. 

Recommended

Title: Very special tea visit
Text:
first we start walking in the beautiful garden which all the trees have a special story. 
Then we went in the home to try a tea with a delicious chocolate cake. 

Then the factory tour, very instructive. The guide took all the time for explaining and answering the question. 

We finish the tour with tea testing and possibility to buy them. Definitively a must to do.

Title: Peacefully quiet and very informative
Text:
Definitely rely vista's here and walk around the plantation with the knowledgeable guides. Rest for a cup of tea and peace of cake at the house then you visit the machinery and see the process.
The tea tasting room with around 50 twas to sip was great.
Recommended as this is not one of the tea plantations on the major tourist guide route.

Title: Interesting
Text: We really enjoyed our free private tour through the estate that includes walking throughout the entire plantation, seeing the processing plant where they were actively working to process tea. The tea tasting of ALL of the varieties of tea was awesome!

Title: An unexpected delight
Text: I hadn't intended to visit this tea estate but went on the suggestion of my tuk tuk driver and it was a real highlight. The tour was very thorough and informative and included a tasting of 65 teas including the rare and valuable white tea.

Title: Fantastic
Text:
I visited the Handunugoda tea estate with my daughter today and found the whole experience fabulous. 

It was the complete opposite of the commercialism of the highland estates where there were tour buses.

This estate makes you feel very welcomed, the scenery is beautiful, the pickers looked happy, the tea factory tour is educational, and the tea & cake at the bungalow followed by tasting of around 25 wonderful teas made it a very memorable experience. 

We got a tuk tuk for Unawatuna area and it took approx. 40 mins.

Title: A Tea lovers paridise
Text:
This is the home of Virgin White tea. Years ago that meant that even the pickers of the tea, who wore gloves so no human hand touches the tea, were virgins. That virgin pickers have disappeared, but the method of picking remains the same. It is the most expensive tea, but you get e chance to taste it in there showroom, along with tens of other tea varieties. I am not a tea drinker, so I skimmed over that part, but thoroughly enjoyed the free tour that happened before the tea tasting. We learned a lot about the differences between the various types of teas. We walked with the guide through parts of the estate, with him pointing out various plants as well as the types of tea being grown. There was a stop for tea and cake on a nice porch, which was great. The servers there took the babies and played with them while we enjoyed this stop.We watched how they process tea. It was an enjoyable experience
This is off the beaten track, but if you like tea or are just interested in the process , it is definetly worth looking for

Title: Excellent tour!
Text: Although a little hard to find, this is a must to visit. Our tour guide was excellent showing us the different types of tea and collection methods. We also got to see cinnamon,pepper and rubber trees. After a  slice of cake and a cup of tea to revive us, we were led to the processing area with machinery that is over a hundred years old!. Then back to taste all their teas. As a bonus we observed a small colorful parade outside the plantation.

Title: Quiet journey
Text:
Free of charge excursion around the tea estate. You can see where the tea, cinnamon, pepper grow, how they are collected and packed. Afterwards visit the museum to try out different types of tea. Prices are above average, 1000-1500 per box,  but they claim it is one of the finest. 
Total time at the estate: 1,5 hour

Title: Informative and fun!
Text:
An informative and interesting visit to a working Tea plantation/tea production facility where we learned the process of tea-making from bud to cup. Really fascinating, and finished with a tasting session of over 20 teas!!

The tour and tasting are free but you finish up with the tasting in the shop - be warned that you will probably be tempted to buy a LOT of tea as it tastes so good!

Really fun tour, highly recommended.

Title: Enjoyable visit to this small estate
Text: You don't need more than a couple of hours to visit this small tea estate (it also grows pepper, Cinnamon and rubber) and can give you a flavour of Sri Lanka.  After a short walk up the hill, where we were given a short talk, we stopped for a cup of tea and cake.  We then had a tour around the factory before trying an buying some of the teas of the manufacturer.  A restful way to spend the time

Title: A working tea museum/factory
Text:
The source of the world's Virgin White tea. We had a very informative tour of the estate and factory with Shirley, who also has a great sense of humour. This is really a working museum - the same equipment from 145 years ago is being used to dry, crush and sort the tea.

It's amazing how many different types of plants, herbs and teas are grown on this plantation - rubber trees, pepper, cinnamon, jasmine, aloe, etc. Shirley played a game with us and asked us to guess each plant that he would pluck a leaf from, based on the taste or smell. I got 0 out of 10..

The tea and cake on the veranda was nice, and then we went into the tea tasting room. It's great to be able to taste before you buy and I loved all the colours of the tea - yellow, deep orange, red, green, etc..

Donations are welcome in the shop and it's well worth it as the staff are very knowledgeable and friendly. Highly recommended stop for a couple of hours, about 30-40 mins from Galle.

Title: Quaint little place
Text:
We came here with Ransiri our Tuk Tuk driver (+94 71 636 2135) who was a great guide and a lovely guy.

We arrived about 4pm and were a little rushed through the tour of the grounds. The complimentary tea was very nice and the factory tour was very interesting. Though, if you want to see the factory in action you will need to arrive before 2pm when work stops.

Tasting the teas before buying was helpful and buying a few is recommended as the tour and tasting is free.

Title: Teas and lots of Teas
Text: Short ride from Galle, it is an all-in-one tea experience. From plantation to factory; teas tastings to tea shopping, we did it all in one place. Thanks to the tour guide at Handunugoda Tea Museum for this lovely experience.

Title: Great place to visit near Galle
Text: Been to this working tea estate many times over the years and it never disappoints. Well worth the trip out from Galle.

Title: Beautifull visit but exoensive teas
Text:
We enjoyed the small roads from our house to the plantation. We were met by Joseph, a local guide, who spend lot of time explaining the tea processing. We had a wonderful tour across one part of the plantation. We enjoyed very much the offered tea and the chocolate cake!!
The factory and old machines visit were quiet informative as well.

The downside of the visit was the overpriced teas at the plantation shop. We bought few items as a support for the people working there but decided to buy our teas once in Kandy and the mountains area.
Nice informative visit for adults and kids but expensive teas if you want to buy some.

Title: Beautiful location, and informative tour
Text: Interesting trip through rural area to reach the plantation, and good views of monkeys as we got out of the coach. Wildlife theme continued with quite a few birds/ a snake and huge variety of plants, many in flower. Informative tour followed by tea and cake, then a visit to the processing rooms followed by the gift shop. Our group all bought some teas having had the opportunity to taste first.

Title: Good tour of the grounds, lots of free tea tasting, but tea from shop expensive which is sad.
Text: Met by a guide on arrival for a walk around the grounds.   Explained lots of things and spent a long time taking us to all the machines used for tea making, and to see staff using them   Enjoyed that very much including the free tea tasting and chocolate cake!  Interesting plantation house where shop is located, but I was very disappointed to see the cost of their tea was far more expensive than standard tea from Sri Lanka in UK supermarkets.   Call me cynical but I don't believe that tea produced right in front of you justifies the prices they were charging in the shop to buy.   (upwards of £5 a box to nearly £25 a box of their most expensive virgin tea) - Give yourself about 2 hours for a full visit and you don't need to prebook just show up as there are always guides ready to take you around free.

Title: Nice experience
Text:
Was a great experience, was nice to walk through the estate and see the tea pickers. Friendly informative guides that provide lots of history. The kids got to ride a horse around the estate.  
We met Mr Herman and had a lovely chat.

Title: Very informative
Text: Had a wonderful informative tour at my first tea factory. First shown around part of the grounds to see all the different plants (cinnamon, lemongrass, pepper, etc and of course teas). Then had tea and chocolate  cake (really good cake) and meet Lara ( 6 month friendly dog). Then got shown around the tea factory and all the machinery. Next stop is to sample all the teas and procure teas, books, cinnamon incense, etc.

Title: Nice calm experience
Text: Very nice tea estate. You can see 145 years old machines. They offered us their tea and a cake on the terrace of the owners house. Very nice experience.

Title: Go here. You won't regret it.
Text:
We took the local bus and then a short tuk tuk ride to get to the tea plantation, and it was really fun. The guided tour was informative, entertaining (thanks Xavier), and free! You get to taste some tasty teas along the way and get a full understanding of the workings of this estate. At the end, there is an opportunity to buy any of their teas, but it is not a situation where you'll feel pressured to make a purchase. 
It's a nice change of pace from the beach activities. 
Not sure if it's perfect for kids, but the tour isn't too long, so even if they don't love it, it's over after 30/40 minutes or so.

Title: Excellent plantation tour and tea tasting!
Text:
Visited in July and had a great couple of hours at the plantation. The tour is free and you are taken for about half and hour through the plantation to see the plants, then to the house for tea and cake. You then visit the factory and can watch 150 year old machinery in action.
The last stop is the tea and gift shop where ladies will prepare over 40 different teas for you to try. All teas are for sale but there is no pressure to buy any. There is also a donation box as you leave because the whole tour is free!! 
Definitely worth the journey from town.

Title: Fantastic Tea Tour
Text: My friends and I wanted to learn more about the virgin White tea so we thought we'd head by the Estate. We were pleasantly surprised by the free tour of the plantations and factory, and even more so of the tea tasting (from which we left light-headed from all the side-effects).

Title: Informative visit - lovely place
Text:
Not too far off the main highway heading south from Colombo. 
Informative tour of the plantation that focuses not just on tea. 
Complimentary tea on the verandah of the homestead and of course a tour of the factory - wow!!

Massive selection of teas to try at the shop. 

Worthwhile visit

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Getting to this plantation alone is an experience. We encountered a herd of water buffalo, which was really fun. Our host, David, was great and met us at our car. He explained everything that they grow there in addition to the tea. It was a really fascinating and it was a nice and tranquil walk around the grounds. The tea and cakes at the house were memorable including meeting their two dogs. Seeing the old original machinery in action was really neat. I had no idea what went in to creating tea from start to finish and it was really fun to learn. Of course, we couldn't leave without some cinnamon, pepper, and tea. This was definitely a highlight of my time in Galle.

Title: Interesting Tour
Text:
The tour is free and the guide gives you a good overview of the different plants and the tea making process.  You are given a cup of tea and a piece of cake and the guide tells you to tip the lady who serves it.  Although there is a notice at the beginning of the tour telling you not to tip individuals, but to leave a tip in the box to be shared.  
There is plenty of tea for sale, although it is not cheap.

Title: Very Interesting
Text: Really interesting, see how the tea is made in the factory, hear about how they make cinnamon, rubber, coffee and black pepper. You stop for a taste of tea and cake which they politely ask you to tip for so as a warning be ready for that. It was a very quiet time of year and we felt that they pressured us quite a bit to buy more tea, we bought some and they seemed disappointed. Still we found it very interesting.

Title: One of the highlights of our Sri Lanka holiday!
Text:
Our family is very passionate about tea and this is one of the reasons why we chose Sri Lanka as our family holiday destination. The visit to this lovely tea plantation is worth it... seeing everything from tea cultivation all the way to the harvest and production. The tea plantation in itself is not postcard pretty and the whole estate could benefit from a series of renovations here and there but take away the facade and you are embraced by a unique tea heritage that will blow you away and give you a much higher respect to every sip that you take out of any tea they produce.

The white tea of course was the star of the show. It is the most expensive they have and worth every drop and sip. You are given a free tasting of their 40+ tea variations so you will have an afternoon of beating your head if you should buy half of the estate or not. But if you have but one tea to choose, let it be the white tea... Very subtle and poignant and poetic in every layer you can savor.

We also loved the Suicide Club blend, which is a unique blend with hints of brandy and also has an interesting story behind its rather unusual name!

Do yourself a favor and find this little treasure.

Title: Hidden Gem
Text: You must visit this place for tea and cake, lovely area quite deep in the jungle. Joseph our guide was very good, funny and great english.

Title: Beautiful Tea Estate
Text: Gorgeous and calm tea estate where the staff gives you a free tour of the factory and the whole estate. The machines are almost 150 years old but it's very intricate how they separate the leaves etc. Also, a great way to take a break from all the beach activities.

Title: Great way to spend an afternoon
Text: It was a rainy afternoon so we decided to venture to the Tea Estate, we didn't really know what to expect, but it was a fantastic afternoon. Free to enter and just need to tip at the end.

Title: Short and sweet
Text:
A short wander through the plants with a guide showing and explaining how they farm.  We saw peppercorns, coffee, latex, hibiscus, mango, parakeets, a Labrador and a Golden Retriever, beautiful flowers I can't name and many many tea bushes. Then tea with chocolate cake before a short stroll to the 'machineries' where the tea making process was underway.  Final stop was the museum, the room you see in their photo where you are able to taste as many or few teas as you like.  We bought their namesake the White Tea which was simply delicious.  Take cash, no cards accepted. 
Our excursion was organised through our hotel Tri, on Lake Koggala which was a jolly 20 minute Tuk Tuk ride away.  A fun outing - even the teens liked it.

Title: Good visit
Text: Well worth a visit! Great getting to have a little cup to sample! Really good guides although 40mins is another to view it

Title: A lush tea plantation
Text: We visited the plantation on the Sri Lankan new year's eve so the factory wasn't open because of the holidays. Still got a nice tour with a expert guide, nice tea tasting with cake and in the shop we tasted about 40 different teas. It was nice to see where the tea is grown and that it is produced in ecological and ethical way.

Title: Different kind of tea plantation
Text: We have visited several tea plantations in Elle region but this place is absolutelly different. The guided tours are interesting  and tea degustation is for free. Perfect oportunity to taste more than 20 kinds of tea and to buy some unique. Highly recommended.

Title: Worth visiting
Text:
Its nice to learn something about the virgin white tea, taste it and have a piece of cake. After visit you can buy some tea if interested. 
But its all for free - not a common thing at Srí Lanka.

Title: Compulsory for visitors to Galle
Text: Just take a tuk-tuk from downtown Galle and 40min later - after travelling thru some local rural sights - you will reach the Estate. What an excellent visit. The guide makes the visit, explaining all there is to know about growing and producing all sorts of tea, rubber, different woods.... Before sampling a suggested tea and cake. Great to see the ladies also working, to get a real sense of how tough it is. Touring the factory and seeing the production line in action was also a highlight. Free sampling of around 30 different types of tea, and as others have said, no compulsory purchase. But how could you not? After such a great experience. So if you want to learn about tea production in Sri Lanka and you have a couple of hours, make sure you put this on the itinerary. It's not like the bustling tea plantations elsewhere, where coaches are unloading bus loads of tourists. It's local, intimate and a lot of fun too.

Title: A cup of tea and a slice of cake - Sri Lankan style
Text:
My tea drinking habits have been converted since visiting this tea factory. Joseph the guide showed us around the plantation and the factory and this was followed by a free cup of tea and a slice of cake. 
Then into the factory to see the old machines clanking away sorting the tea. Then a visit to the shop (of course!) for a tea tasting session. 
No hard sales so not obliged to buy anything, but we did and still drinking it at home as it's much better than some of the better known UK brands! 
A lovely place to visit, away from the crowds and the traffic and the heat. Would definitely recommend.

Title: Good tea.
Text: The tour is well worth it forvthe trip. Nice tea and cake served and working museum tour. Very nice place.

Title: Great place! Must see!
Text: The entrance is FREE! The plantation is really great. They grow tea, coffee, pepper, rubber tree, teak and cinnamon. They give you a guide that walks you through the plantation and tells everything about it. Then the give you delicious cake with their tea. After that they take you to the factory and show you the whole process of tea production.  Then you go to the museum, where you can try more than 25 different sorts of tea and buy what you like! Great place! Must see if you come to Shri Lanka

Title: Excellent tea experience
Text:
We visited the museum/factory in March and were inspired by a walk through the plantation, and the story of the guide.
Wonderful experience.

Title: Go early for tea and cake
Text: Beautiful setting with knowledgeable staff, to ensure you are in line for tea and cake arrive early as do not offer it half an hour before closing time.  There are lots of teas to try and buy and a good explanation by the local guide.

Title: Its definitely worth it!
Text: The tea plantation is worth a visit! The guides are really nice and really try to tell you the idea of making a good tea. You can see all the plants and products like pepper, cinnamon and tea you normally only buy in plastic bags in the supermarkets. Beside that this place is giving work to a lot of local people. So tip well....

Title: Interesting Stop Off
Text: More of a museum than a working tea estate, but an interesting story and nice teas, if not a little touristy.

Title: Excellent Tour of the Tea Estate
Text: This was certainly an experience not to be missed.  We were shown around the estate, had a very nice cup of tea and cake, then we were shown around the factory to see how the tea is made (37 different types) and some of the oldest machines that are still working.  They don't only grow tea, they grow coffee, Peppercorns and they have rubber trees.  To the tasting, there were some very good teas, but also some very expensive teas especially the virgin white tea.  But an extremely beautiful place and well recommended.

Title: Nice visit! And lots of Tea to taste!
Text: The Tea Factory is a great and learning experience. At the end of the tour one gets to taste over 40 varieties of tea! And also buy some. Should do.

Title: Such a nice afternoon
Text: A lovely peaceful setting, very interesting tour, delicious complementary tea and cake, a chance to taste over 30 teas and to buy some of our favourites. A must go to place if stay in Galle

Title: Great tour for the whole family
Text: A great tour of a fantastic small lowland tea plantation, particularly if you do not have the opportunity to visit the tea plantations in the north of the country.  Even enjoyed a warm cuppa sitting on the balcony of the plantation homestead despite the fact it was about 35 degrees with 90% humidity. The tour was followed by a tasting session of all the teas on offer including the signature white tea.  We were able to wander around the shop and there was certainly no pressure to purchase, although we did. On the recommendation of a fellow tourist I also purchased a copy of the Suicide Club  a virgin tea planters journey. The book describes the history of the plantation during the British Raj. An interesting read that compliments the tour of the plantation. Highly recommended by the whole family and a great half day tour from Hikkaduwa in a tuk tuk.

Title: Good place to understand how tea is manufactured
Text:
Visited this tea plantation during our stay in Fortress koggala.
The guide explained various types of tea .
And took us into the factory where tea is manufactured . It  is 150 yr old machinery which is still working , it was interesting to understand the whole process.We get to taste different varieties of tea .
You can buy them from the store if you like.

Title: Small with a storied past
Text:
From Galle, it's not too far a journey to get to Handunugoda where entrance is free, the tour is free, the information is free, you get a pre-selected round of tea free (with a little cake). The only thing you pay for is if you want to buy some flavoured tea at the end of your visit.

It's fascinating to hear the story behind the golden scissors used by virgins to cut special leaves for the Chinese emperor. And the plantation's ownership through the years throws up another telling tale. 

The factory uses machines that are 145 years old, and they're in pristine condition. It's hard to imagine the place ever using all modern day machinery in the future. Our guide had a screw loose, definitely, but he was also informative, dad-joke funny, and appeared fluent in Russian (which worked out well for the few "Ruskies" who were there the same time as us. 

Seeing a tea plantation in action is a must if you're in Sri Lanka. If you're in the area (we visited en route to Tangalle), this place is worth the visit. It's charming, welcoming, and has more personality than many other plantations around.

Title: Beautiful
Text: We hired Driver in SL Tours (see my other review) to take us from the port in Colombo to Handunugoda Tea Estate and Galle, for a long day trip. We had found this estate on Tripadvisor. The excellent reviews proved to be correct. An employee gave us a thorough tour, with included seeing the virgin, white tea plants, black tea, rubber tree (with rubber dripping into a coconut collection shell), cinnamon bark and many flowers. We were given a lovely cup of tea on the porch of the owner's private home and even allowed to see his house, which felt like a trip back into British colonial times. We were then given the chance to taste at least 30-40 different teas. We happily bought a few teas we liked. We also left a tip in the tip box because the tour was terrific and he experience a wonderful memory.

Title: Lovely way to spend a couple of hours
Text: We visited the tea estate a couple of days ago and it was lovely. Such a peaceful and beautiful setting. It's pretty hot but the walk between each part is short. We didn't have to pay anything and we were treated so well with tea and cake plus tea tasting. It was really informative and we ended up buying lots of different varietiess of tea. It's worth a visit if you fancy doing something a bit different for an hour or two.

Title: Brilliant and interesting
Text:
Loved our trip to this small but perfectly formed tea plantation.

Very laid back and easy going tour. The staff were knowledgable and very happy to chat and give information. The layout is compact so in the heat there are no long treks between factory, shop and plantation as it is all within a couple of hundred meters of each other.

The tasting room and gift shop are cool and airy and there's no hard sell or pressure.

The delightful bungalow at the end of the tour where you get free tea and cake is a lovely touch and adds to the whole fleeced sensation of the place.

Fascinating, pretty and all well organised. The whole family loved it.

Title: Very interesting!
Text: We enjoyed the information tour in the plantation. They show the way of making tea and the time-consuming and hard work. Sure you can buy tea afterwards. We bought the Saphire Oloong Tea. Preparing the tea at home it tasted fantastic!

Title: A nice tea factory... too bad the person in charge of the visit was not speaking a great english
Text:
That's the only tea plantation and factory we visited in Sri Lanka and we were quite happy about it. Only thing to mention is the guy that took us on the tour, he was trying to be helpful but the communication was not easy as he mostly didn't understand our questions. 
The visit is free, it ends with a tour of the shop, prices are not too bad.

Title: A gem!
Text: There are many tea factories in Sri Lanka that offer guided tours. This one was special partly because of the incredible commitment of our guide. He led us through the romantic estate and the unique historic tea processing factory as if it were his personal property. And, rare in Sri Lanka, he wouldn't even accept a tip. A real gentleman. The lowland tea at Handunugoda is classy, especially the outrageously rare and expensive virgin white tea. Great place off the beaten track.

Title: Small, but very interesting
Text:
Amazing that some of the equipment here dates back 145 years.
This is a great way to while away 2 or 3 hours and sample a number of types of tea at the end. Don't miss ir

Title: A welcoming place, very charming and informative
Text:
Starts off with a walk up a short hill path to a bungalow, stopping to illustrate the various plants and uses on this estate. Leisurely and relaxed, with lovely scenery. At the bungalow a cup of tea or two and some cake with a chance to sit and chat. Our guide was charming and really knowledgeable.

Then back down the hill and a tour and explanation of how the tea is sorted and processed followed by the chance to sample around 80 different types. 

You can buy some if you want, but there is no expectation or hard sell. A brilliant change from most other places who are looking to maximise their take from any tourist.

Highly recommend this for all ages.

Title: So Informative
Text: Best of all the tea tours. Learned about loads of other vegetation from seeing black pepper grow to the finale of tea and cake!

Title: Great visit
Text: Really good trip, great hospitality, mostly about tea but coffee cinnamon and rubber too... Factory museum remarkable... Machines seen working... Very impressive.... Relaxing tea and cake with other visitors... No pressure to buy despite the visit being free ??

Title: Amazing Little Gem
Text:
We visited here based on reviews on TA.
The visit and tour is absolutely free.
You walk through the plantation and sit for tea and cake and then see the processing plant and then you can taste 30 types of tea and purchase teas if you so choose but there is no pressure to buy a thing.
The staff is friendly and knowledgeable. 
The entire visit is about one hour. This place is also know as the Virgin White Tea Estate.

Title: A hidden gem - what a lovely tea estate!
Text:
One of the few tea estates in the low land of Sri Lanka - and what a great one!
It is easy to find the estate if you stay in the south on the island - we took a tuk-tuk from Mirissa, a 30 minutes drive in very nice surroundings. 

When we arrived we were met by a great guide - he spoke all the languages of the visitors during our stay! - and he gave us the very interesting history about both the famous Virgin White Tea, the Suicide Club and the tea estate and tea in general.

The estate has a great history - make sure to get hold of a copy of the book "The suicide Club - a virgin the planters journey" written by the owner Herman Gunaratne. They sell it in the teashop at the estate.

The tour around the estate is all free, it lasted for 1 hour and we were served cake and one of the estates special tea, The Sapphire Oolong. 
Before tea tasting we visited the factory - one of the machines they still use, was build by the same company that build the Titanic! 
Many of the machines in use was over 145 years old!

It was a perfect way to end the tour with great tea tasting and the opportunity to get some of their great tea to bring back home! 

The whole visit was relaxed and quite and no pressure to buy in the shop - 
a visit to this estate is highly recommended!

Title: Lovely Tea Plantation
Text:
Just visited the plantation this morning and it was really interesting. The background story is pretty interesting and guide did a good job of explaining everything we were interested in. Part about how Chinese used gold bowls and scissoirs to cut white tea that was never touched by human hands and only Emperor was allowed to touch it was amazing. Virgin white tea has most antyoxydants in any beverage known and is incredibly healthy. Nowdays they use gloves but it's supposedly the only plantation that still uses this way of picking tea leaves. We were also presented with a cup of Sapphire Oolong tea and slice of cake and later we could taste every one of more than 20 teas they have. Everything was free of charge. During the walk we saw Ficus Elastica (india rubber) tree, cinnamon, hibiscus and several other plants species.
We really love tea so it was a great experience overall.

Title: Teatime will never be the same
Text: The history of this plantation is very interesting as is the owner who acted as our guide.It started life some 150 yrs age covering 2200 acres but much was gambled away by an ancestor. It is the closest plantation in Sri Lanka to the sea and the only one producing certified WHITE tea.          The machinery is 150 years old ( installed 2nd hand) and some 60 people work the estate.  The extensive tea sampling is the best part of the tour, with so many variations on offer to buy.

Title: Quaint
Text: Great little trip out with fantastic choice of tea , we had a tour of the plantation and finished off with a choice of 32 cups of tea.

Title: Amazing
Text:
We were lucky to have the owner of the plantation showing us around. He was not only a fascinating character, but also avery skilled storyteller and an  endless source of imformation on his subject. One hour in his company, and all of a sudden I, who normally is more of a coffee-person, am deeply moved by the world of tea. We walked around in the plantation, got to see the machinery and had a tea tasting in the end. All of this was for free, but we ended up buying quit a lot of tea since it was sooo delicious! At all times we were surrounded by exotic smells and friendly people. 

I recommend this activity. It might be good to bring a sun hat and a bottle of water on the guided tour, since it involves a lot of standing around in the sun listening.... :-) and bring a camera!

Title: Beautiful tour and excellent tea
Text: You will get a very interesting tour for free trough the estate and the production of tea. It ends with a tea testing and the opportunity to buy some of the excellent teas, but there is never the feeling that you have to be forced to buy anything.

Title: Informative and super fun experience
Text: We enjoyed the Tuk Tuk journey to find this tea plantation from our base in Weligama.  The gentleman who toured us around was informative and well paced.  We had a complimentary cup of tea (and my husband and the Tuk Tuk driver had cake).  The tea tasting of the many types of tea was a highlight.  It was free and we purchased some very good quality tea in the shop.

Title: A great tour guide, awesome teas!
Text:
We really enjoyed the few hours we spent at this tea estate. It was a good 30 minutes away from Galle and half of it on back roads, but they boast producing the ancient Chinese method of virgin tea meaning it does not ever get handled by human hands and the process is painstakingly careful. 
I am generally not a tea fan, but the teas I tried were very good with lots of variety. Their famous tea, Suicide Club, has such an interesting history! The tour guide was extremely knowledgable and we learned a ton from him. The machinery that is still used is ancient, but clearly seems to still do the trick!
Before our tour (which is all free) we were treated to a free cup of tea and piece of cake in their guest house up the hill. The area is beautiful and they even have a race horse on the premises! 
I highly recommend this location, but seeing as we never visited any of the main tea plantations in the hill country, I can't compare to visiting those behemoths... we did drive by though.

Title: Flying Visit - out of the way but worth finding
Text:
We hired a car and driver from Columbo for the day and wound our way down the coast to Galle. Only in the country for the day I chose this plantation from trip advisor. The driver hadn't heard of it but rang and eventually after winding through the hills just out of Galle we found it.
Basic - it's really a working plantation and visitors seemed a bother on the day we went. But none the less the teas are amazing and great value. It's definitely well worth the effort.

Title: Very informative guide and tea plantation with gorgeous location
Text: We very much enjoyed the guide showing us around at the tea estate who is a living encyclopaedia and speaks more than 7 languages. If you are in the Galle/Kahanda area, well worth a visit

Title: Beautiful
Text: We had a lovely tour on the tea estate, the guide was a lovely senior gentleman who could speak more than 7 languages and knew absolutely everything about tea and plants in general. We got complimentary cakes and tea tasting at the end. Left with a bag full of wonderful southern teas! Highly recommended!!

Title: Great tea experience
Text: While we were rushed during our visit due to grumpy toddlers, the tea plantation was very nice and what we heard from the tour was very good and informative.  We had the owner of the plantation and he was full of interesting stories.  The tea store was very well stocked and beautifully displayed with tasters.

Title: Interesting trip
Text: we spent about 2 hours at the tea estate and had a pleasant time. tour of the plantation is informative and nice to have tea and cake half way through. tour of the small factory was good and nice to see 145 year old machines in use - my wife was happy to see they were made in Belfast. tour ends with the opportunity to taste teas in the shop but there is no hard sell and they also operate a central tip box so all tips are divided equally among the staff which is nice to see.

Title: Bit of a disappointment
Text:
Having read such positive feedback regarding the Tea Estate we were somewhat disappointed at what we found. To be perfectly frank we gained more information from Wikipedia although perhaps we just had a poor guide.(in all events we both found him irritating with his puerile questions). It cost us 1500 Sri Lankan Rupees to visit by Tuk-Tuk from Mirissa South (return) and one positive of this was that we stopped at the Fish Market in Weligama for photos, then the Stilt Fishermen 300 (what a scam-but they waved), saw a mongoose and a large monitor and photos of a Buddhist shrine.
Returning to the plantation the restaurant is now closed so no chance of lunch. The level of instruction was mediocre although the cake was OK. The tea (without milk and unsweetened was not to our taste) and it was 'suggested' that we might want to tip the waitress! Finally arriving at the 'factory' again it was difficult to believe that the machinery was actually constantly in daily use, as it wasn't. In fact the Japanese separator patently wasn't. 
On to the tea tasting and I guess at 68 my taste-buds and those of my wife have retired along with us. We tried a variety of the cold, samples but of 20+ we found none to our liking. In fact my buccal membranes dried up I think from shock. Even the blended teas were awful-just so disappointing but who would ever drink cold, stale tea???? Who drinks tea cold, unsweetened and without milk or lemon? OK, I guess lots do but not us.
We left without purchasing anything which seemed to disappoint our guide who had mentioned that their only income comes from selling to visitors and some boutique in France. Not sure I can credit this either.
It was free but there was a modicum of pressure to buy.
Go by all means but don't raise your hopes too high.

Title: One of my favourite experiences in Sri Lanka
Text:
This tea plantation was such a fantastically beautiful experience, I cannot recommend it enough. The staff were delightful and extremely passionate about the plantation. The history surrounding Handunugoda Tea Estate is extraordinary and so interesting.

You're first taken to the tea house for a cup of speciality tea and a slice of chocolate cake (at no cost), here you sit in the sunshine, admire the views and read about the plantation. Herman, the planation owner made the effort to say hello to us and welcome us which was a lovely touch. David was our tour guide and was passionate and interesting to listen to, he has exceptional english and was happy to answer any questions. He didn't rush us and made sure that everyone (5 of us) was ready to move on before continuing with his explanations. After the tea house we were taken for a walk around the plantation and the factory, it blew my mind. We then ended the tour in the gift shop were you had the opportunity to do some tea tasting and browse the gifts.

At no point during the tour were we obliged to make any payment, donation, purchase or tip which was such a nice quality about the whole experience considering you're constantly asked for it wherever you go in Sri Lanka. We bought some sapphire oolong tea and Hermans book "The Suicide Club" (excellent read). I'd 100% recommend visiting here during your stay in Sri Lanka, you will not be disappointed.

Title: Must see and different travel experience
Text: This is a very interesting place to visit and we were lucky to be taken around by the owner who told us that he is also a director of Dilmah Tea Company. It was so interesting listening to his story of how he created and sold the Virgin White tea. We toured the plantation and saw the tea harvesting (although in small volume for us tourists), then we had tea and cake at the top of the plantation in the home and tea room, before heading down to the manufacturing area with its 150 year old machinery clacking away. As others have said, the shope has a wonderful collection of teas for tasting and we bought some nice teas and souvenirs for family at home. A must see attraction in Sri Lanka.

Title: Nice day, beautiful walk
Text:
We went there in September 2014.
It wasn't the high season. We had a personal guide around the plantation and factory.  It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend an afternoon. The guide was very polite and pleasant, we were not rushed around, and were never pressured to buy anything. 
We enjoyed the complementary virgin tea and cakes half way round.

We bought different teas.  The shop is incredible, with samples of all of the teas to taste.  Our favourite was the lemon grass tea mix, and also the silver tips.

Highly recommended.

Title: What an interesting history
Text:
We were pleased that our tuktuk tour from Galle included this place. We had previously been on a tea trail in the hill country, but this time we were able to visit a lowland plantation. 

We were met by a guide who told us the story of the Virgin White Tea (nothing to do with Mr. Bransom!) and the fact that the present owner's grandfather had lost 1,000 acres of the estate on the roll of dice.

The estate is interesting in the variety of produce involved. We were very interested to see the rubber plantation and the spice plants. Before seeing the old machinery and the museum, we were treated to a cup of tea and a slice of cake. At the museum, we had a chance to taste a whole variety of teas. We treated ourselves to some more teas from the shop.

Our guide was very interesting and informative so we really enjoyed the visit. There is no charge for the tour, and you are not obliged to buy anything. There is a box for tips which is well worth contributing to.

Title: Fantastic Activity
Text:
Could not recommend more highly. We got a personal tour by Xavier of the plantation, which consisted of not only tea but several spices and fruits. Sampled peppercorns right off the plant! Once the outside tour was complete, he showed us around the tea processing facility. Heavy machines from colonial times are still in use. The tour finishes with a tasting of around 50 teas, and an opportunity to purchase. 

Sri Lanka has quite a few tourist traps - This is not one of them.

Title: Fascinating and friendly
Text:
This place is fascinating, made more interesting by the fact that it is a low altitude tea plantation. David, who showed us around, was very interesting and helpful. The fact that we were given tea and cake on the owner's terrace really showed how focussed they were in ensuring visitors had a good visit.

The fact that this place is the only one in Sri Lanka to produce white tea is an added bonus and the story behind it is very interesting.

The tour of the factory area followed by tea tasting was very informative.

Would certainly recommend this place if in the Galle area.

Title: The best tea experience, great history
Text: Hidden away in a beautiful stretch of green, this plantation showcases all you need to know about tea and tea making. Beautiful old machinery, well maintained and a very hospitable reception. No push, no pressure, just enjoy the tea plantation and the friendly tour. The little tea shop offers beautiful teas, even some you may not have tried before. You can taste each tea at leisure.

Title: Interesting, fun and beautiful
Text: We took a tuktuk here not knowing what to expect. As soon as we got there we were greeted. After a couple of minutes some more giests arrived. The owner came outside and introduced himslef. This guy was without a doubt a fountain of information. He told us about his plantation, the growth and handling of tea in a very interesting and funny way. He kept his tour light but answered questions in amazing detail. After a while walking outside we sat down in a cozy house and were served an amazing oolong tea. Continuing to his factory afterwards. The tour ended in his small museum where you could taste all tea's made. The highlight being the virgin white tea, untouched by human hands and cut with golden scissors. I'm not a tea freak. I like tea but am not a worshipper. This was still a highlight on our trip so far. Interesting and a fantastic way to spend some time outdoors and away from the beach! Tour was free of charge. You can purchase tea in the museum after the tour. Easy to get there with a tuktuk from Galle/Unawantuna/Talpe/Koggala.

Title: Great experience
Text:
In this factory we got our own guide, who told us about all the process. People so kind and ready to share.

There is also a very nice buildidng for tourist were You can see an ineresting film. But what is important You can try over 40 kind of tea there! And all that for free. Only pay tuk tuk to get You there (from Unawatuna and back, about 2000 rupies).

This is really worth seeing. It's location is among beautiful te plantation. Getting there is an adventure too. Through the small villages, rice fields, jungle and cinnamon gardens.

Title: Wonderful Experience
Text: This was our third tea factory tour during our short stay in Sri Lanka. This tour was the best. They allowed you to sample all 32 teas that they produce. Our tour guide spoke excellent English. We had a private tour. Also, the majority of the plant does not run during the day so you were able to hear the guides explanation of each machine. The factory runs overnight during the cooler hours. There was no pressure to buy their tea and it was not heavily populated with tourists. I believe this is also the only factory in Sri Lanka which produces white tea. There is also no admission charge. The only negative is that it is difficult to find.

Title: Amazing!
Text: We were extremely lucky to meet the owner who kindly showed us round , he is full of the most amazing and interesting stories about his business ( Sri Lanka is the second highest exporter of tea in the world ) Had a wonderful time many thanks!!

Title: The journey there was the high light
Text:
This tea plantation is in a lovely area and the winding journey to get there is certainly very picturesque.
Loved the local homes, vegetation and smiles along the way.
The Virgin Tea Plantation was run down with very little effort put into interesting information with regards to the plant itself, stages of growth, picking and processing (even though we know this tea  is not processed by machinery). It would have been nice to see the difference of the varied tea varieties and get a thorough tour of where the tea is grown i.e, like vineyards. After all, visitors to this destination must surely love tea or at least have some sort of interest in the product? 100% slack.
Items for sale are again tourist driven with no creativity in display.
We found the tea tasting bland - I much prefer Twinings Teas - sorry!

Title: A surprise and delight
Text:
If you get the chance to visit any tea plantation in Sri Lanka you must go to this one and if you have a choice of a guide make sure that you get Herman (the owner). He gives the tour a real sparkle of star dust and gravity!
The best part of the tour is when you actually see the ladies in their latex gloves with tiny scissors cutting the Virgin White Tea leaves from the bushes that eventually will become the famous tea, which has the highest anti-oxidant content of any tea in the world! It will make more sense when you hear the story! By the way, don't speak when Herman is speaking and be prepared for several stops for him to light up

Title: Tea tasting at its best
Text: Definitely worth a visit if you're in the Koggala area. Very well-organised tour of the plantation and factory (which is more like a working museum). The staff are very friendly and will show you around and then take you to have some Sapphire Oolong tea (exclusive to Handunugoda) and a piece of cake outside in the terrace of the owner's property. Feels very colonial. Lastly you can taste (and then purchase) any of the 31 varieties of teas produced. If you're interested in health properties of the different teas, you can read all about this in a leaflet they give you.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
Great day out for all ages, you get to see how the tea is processed and how it reaches the form that you see in your everyday tea bag!
We were very lucky to have been introduced to the estate by Herman himself who gave us a brief introduction to the way in which the plantation works and a brief history into the tea export system.
You get to taste the tea along with a piece of cake, at no charge also. 
There is a chance to buy the tea at the end and it is all very well priced (bag of white virgin tea being 2500LKR)

Title: The best
Text:
I have visited 3 different tea factories and this one is the best. You are allowed to take photos of anything, your guide is patiently explaining everything, you can touch, smell all the outputs....what can I say?! 

One word PERFECT!

Title: inters-teaing
Text: Its a nice place to stop by on the way to NE if you're not familiar with tea and the process.  The tour guides who show you around do a nice job of it.

Title: A fine experience
Text: Ive visited other tea factories in the hill country and these tours were fairly rushed.  But in this estate, a charming older gentleman will be your guide. And he will explain you the ins and outs of the tea making process, no rush at all. After you visited the tea plantation, it is time for tea and cake outside a nice bungalow in a pretty garden.  Then the tour continues with the tea factory and finally the tea tasting of 30 different teas !  This tour is completely free, but you can leave a tip for the staff. A tea shop is attached to the estate where you can buy all the different teas. Including the famous Virgin White Tea, the speciality tea of this estate. It is harvested by tea pickers wearing gloves. For every tea you buy, you receive a leaflet of how to drink this particular tea and the health benefits.  Recommended.

Title: A great cup of tea in a beautiful plantation.
Text: We took a tuk tuk from Galle to the plantation which is about an hours journey. Great views along the coast and a chance to see Sri Lankan daily life. We read about the tea plantation in our travel guide and knew that it was on a smaller scale than he larger more commercial ones in the north but this was to it's advantage. It's a very successfully run business but has not lost that personal touch. There is no charge and our guide greeted us in perfect English asking if we would mind sharing our visit with a small group of Russian women. We all started off walking up a slight slope and viewing the spice garden stopping at various plants where our guide then broke into fluent Russian before repeating in English. In total he could speak seven languages and was extremely knowledgable. This combination proved to be extremely entertaining for all of us and a really enjoyable afternoon visit. Barriers came down and we had so many laughs together. After the spice garden we tasted some tea (Sapphire Oolong) which is only manufactured here and cake before taking a walk through the manufacturing plant. Some of the machines were built by the same engineering firm as the Titanic and still working. The visit ends up in the tea tasting and gift shop. Here the full range of teas, over 40 can be sampled and of course bought. Handunugoda is a great find and well worth a visit. Intimate in it's scale, professional in it's presentation and delicious teas. Thoroughly enjoyed our time here.

Title: Interesting worth a diversion
Text: We have visited tea plantations before but were persuaded by our driver to come here. A tour of the spice gardens was OK. This was followed by tea and chocolate cake on the plantation bungalows veranda. The interesting part of the visit was the factory - still using 150 year old machines  from the British. We finished in the shop where you could taste and buy tea. We didn't buy the virgin tea that the estate is famous for - very expensive but labour intensive.

Title: So unexpected
Text: We went to the tea plantation the 2nd day we were here and we are so glad we did as this was a hidden gem. The plantation is beautiful and the tea and tour guides are great too! We really enjoyed it here and would recommend it to anybody! :)

Title: The best tea factory in Sri Lanka!
Text:
The best tea factory in Sri Lanka. The rest of them are soo comercial and need to buy a ticket, which is not expensive but they will gave you just a basic staff about the factory and you will be not allow to take any photo! 

This lovely tea factory is a family business running by fantastic staff. A fabulouse FREE tea tour inside and out side where you can see from beginning the all process - from bush to bag. 
First part is outside and on the way to 'home house' nice tour guide tells many interesting news not just about the tea but coffe beans or caoutchouc process as well. There you can read some information book about all tea and they gave you tea and chocolate cake - the best one which you can find in Sri Lanka, because they do not have great chocolate like in Europe. After tea time you will see the all proces in the factory. At the end is there museum/shop where you can taste the all 30 type of tea which they have and buy the best which you like. Really recomend the Saphire Olong Tea which you can find only in Sri Lanka!

I been there last year with my another friend too. Atractive and worth trip!

Title: UnbeLEAFable tea tour!
Text: Great place, beautiful location. Our  Guide was awesome and  showed us all the ins and outs of the tea making process and the surrounding area. The little tea house at the top of the hill is stunning, and you can even take home some proper tea in the shop at the end of the tour. Well worth a visit.

Title: Perfect half-day experience
Text:
Very nice and peaceful experience with tasting, cake, good information and history.
The guide was very calm and nice - had good information about the plantation and loved his job - therefore very funny to be around

Title: £35 for a box of tea is a bit harsh.
Text:
Visited December 2015, Only cost is if you decide to purchase one of the many teas or knick knacks.

Free cup of tea with a slice of cake half way round.

The old machinery operated by women and a token native whittling some Cinnamon sticks added to the acme experience.
Mostly I thought the costs for the tea were reasonable considering I was in a tourist environment.
But Virgin White Tea at almost £35 a box was a bit too much, even if as they say it's picked with gloves on hand , scissors used and even the slightest human contact would make it unworthy, I still felt a liberty being taken :)
Still, we purchased the chamomile tea and a cinnamon one, plus a couple of nick nacks :)

Title: Very interesting visit lots learned.
Text:
This is a must if you are interested about tea. 
I'm not talking about your PG Tips or any other household brand of tea I'm talking about tea whether a single varietal or a blend these teas strived for quality and passion.

Upon arriving we were escorted around the property and given the low down on white, silver, black and green tea.

We could see the rows upon rows of tea plants and the pickers diligently filling their baskets with the leaves.

A refreshment break of Oolong on the veranda with some cake oozed of a colonial time of long ago, a pause before moving on to the processing of the tea.

 The plantation is using machinary and techniques dated from 145 years ago a working museum. 

After the tour of the processing plant, a tasting of all the teas were offered. You could compare and contrast and buy if desired.

I enjoyed the visit and the knowledge of the guides.

A worthwhile hour spent.

Title: Tea, rubber, cinnamon and more
Text:
Not only a tea estate but also rubber trees, coffee plants, cinnamon production and more to be seen! If the machines are working it is great to gain insight in the daily routine. 
There is an old Indian racing horse for the kids to ride around.

Title: Good tour, expensive buy
Text: It's a great place to experience a tea estate, tea factory and tasting if you haven't been to Kandy, NE etc. This one is also unique cos they grow the white tea.. However at the end of the tour n tasting, the tea you can buy is pretty expensive! Overall it's a good learning experience..

Title: it was just an amazing tour
Text: i guess we had the best tourguide, speaking 7 languages :-) he showed us the faboulus plantation. it was very interesting and we were able to taste, touch, look and listen. the plantation is extremely well maintained and it's far away from mass tourism handling. it's so interesting to see all the ingredients such as cinnamon and lemon grass growing inbetween the tea. they also show you the whole way from green leaves to ready-to-use tea. at the end you can taste all different teas they offer on the plantation.  it's highly recommendable! takes you about 1 hour - perfectly spent time!

Title: Interesting but rushed
Text:
It was raining on the day we visited the estate and this may have contributed to the slightly rushed pace of the tour.

We were greeted, on arrival, by an umbrella wielding guide who then proceeded to whisk us round the outside area. He was very knowledgeable, and pointed out many things of interest, but didn't really give us time to enjoy the sights. Also, at one point he did subtly request a tip. You are specifically requested by management not to tip the guides and to report such behavior. Obviously we didn't report him but was a little disappointing, nonetheless, and something to watch out for.

The hot tea and cake part of the tour was lovely. Really great tea, made on site, and served in a beautiful and tranquil seating area, overlooking a gorgeous tropical garden.

The factory tour is also reasonably brief but very interesting and impressive. Our guide for this section was also very knowledgeable and proud of the factory. And rightly so-the machinery, still in use and in good condition, is over a hundred years old. It's great seeing the tea making process from start to finish and leads nicely into the tasting session.

The tasting session is held in the shop, with a view to trying before you buy. There's a short informative film, and then you're given a clean spoon and glass, a description of all the teas and you're free to taste test as you please. There are over twenty teas to try, including the virgin white tea and the famous 'suicide blend'.

The purchasable  teas are, understandably, expensive for the most part, however there a few reasonable ones and you aren't made to feel pressured into buying anything.

Short but enjoyable tour, and as it's entirely free and quite interesting, I'd definitely recommend if you're in the area.

Title: Tea plantation
Text: I was here with my girlfriend. It was very infromative trip, because we saw how grow tea, cinnamon, black pepper, caoutchouc, papaya, ... We received a good pice of cake and it is possible to buy here some gifts. Of course very good tea too.

Title: Tea Plantation Tour
Text: The ride is very nice from Galle in a tuk tuk to get to the plantation, stopping along the way for a coconut juice and bananas.  The tea estate tour was an amazing place to visit, especially for someone like me who had never been on a tea plantation before.  We got to see so many types of trees, plants, herb and flowers along the way.  We took a short walk to the estate where we were served a cup of tea and has a square of cake.  After the tour we were taken to the factory to see the processing of the tea that was fantastic and still being done on machines that are more than 145 years old!  The tea store was a bit expensive, but you are allowed to taste more than 30 types of teas that are sold.  I would recommend to sneak upstairs to see the great paintings and photographs on the walls and there is a great photo opp from the top floor of the plantation.  We very much enjoyed and bought a few teas as well as left a donation.

Title: Wonderful and extraordinarily interesting
Text: Wonderful experience of seeing the plantation. They Crow everything there including cinnamon, Black pepper, rubber trees, coffee and many other. It is a truly beautiful place and i enjoyed a great Tour including a beautiful cup of tea and a peace of cake at the tea House on the erstate. The Tour on the factory was really quiet extraordinary as the machines are 145 years old and in perfect working condition. One machine is made by the Company who made the titanic. The tea is extremely good and all are very freshly made. Nice shop allows for great buys and bringing the taste of ceylon back home. Well worth a visit.

Title: Charming and interesting place to visit
Text: The Handunugoda Tea Estate is unusual in the area being a tea plantation rather than just a tea factory (most of the plantations are quite a distance away).  It is well worth a visit - you will be taken on a short walk through the beautiful plantation and shown not only tea plants but other interesting crops too.  The walk takes you to the plantation owners bungalow where you will be served tea and cake on the lovely verandah overlooking the gardens, with beautiful views and echoing to the sound of birdsong.  You will also visit the tea factory with its fascinating old machinery and then to the "Tea Museum" where you can taste all sorts of teas and of course purchase some.  There is absolutely no pressure to buy though and you are left to peacefully browse.  I'm a confirmed coffee drinker and even I thought this was a really charming place to visit - it would have seemed wrong to visit Sri Lanka and not gain some experience of tea - this is the perfect place to do that.

Title: History, Tea tasting, A nice walk and Lovely People
Text:
We visited this Ancient Tea Estate as part of our Resort's City tour. 
Long drive from where we stayed but totally worth it. 
Get here before the day gets too hot since there is a nice long walk in the beginning. 
With this walk there is a lot of history attached.
I do not want to spoil your trip so will not give too many details.
Also included is a factory visit and then the amazing tea tasting. 
10 on 10 for them. Hats off.

Title: Tea farm with 140years history
Text: Great excursion for everybody, you will get tour what you never visited and the infromation from the old guy is also very interesting.I thought that I knew almost everything about tea but this tour fill me up to 100%.Very interesting with so nice people.They are selling to all over the world. Best for me is Saphire Oolong tea and virgin white tea.

Title: Tea-rrific!
Text:
The Handunugoda Tea Plantation is about much more than tea.
The guides are multi-lingual and able to explain in detail about all aspects of the tea making process, specifically they produce the Virgin tea that uses the very young leaves from the tea plant.
You are treated to a detailed demonstration that includes working machines that have been used for over 145 years and are still used daily. The tea and cake are enjoyable plus the tea tasting includes about 30 varieties and you are not rushed or pressured at any stage. 
Additionally there are rubber trees that are producing rubber extract, Teak and Mahogany trees, cinnamon and lemongrass plants and wonderful flora and fauna to take in as you are guided around.
There are teas and related-products to buy in the shop but everything else is free.
We took a tuk tuk from Bentota to Handunugoda (Dennis Tours) and it was well worth it. A day out to Handunugoda provides lots of photo opportunities and places to visit en-route and is a lot more fun than a taxi!

Title: Worth the visit.
Text: This made an enjoyable and interesting hour or two.  We had a brief tour of a small area of the estate, tea and (very nice!) chocolate cake before being shown round the small factory.  We learnt much more about the process here than we did at the big Mackwoods estate in Nuwara Eliya. We tasted different tea varieties and made a modest purchase.  The teas are quite expensive but there was no pressure to buy. We were based near Galle and driving ourselves round and it was easy to find once we located the right turning.  By the way, don't believe all the horror stories about self-driving in Sri Lanka. We has no problems at all, including driving through Kandy and Colombo - the roads were generally good although you do need a good navigator as signs are difficult to spot, and reasonable nerves when surrounded on all sides by tuk tuks.

Title: Great place and no hassle
Text: The drive up is as magical as the place itself. Our tour guide knew everything about the tea, and the herbs they grow in the beautiful gardens. After a nice cup of tea with a lovely treat we left for the factory. After the factory we went into the shop. Really nice as you can taste all the different flavours of tea the have. When we bought some tea, and wanted to tip the tour guide he declined and asked to make a donation in the pot. Which is divided under all the employees. Absolutely worth going to !

Title: Interesting tea tasting experience
Text: This is a small privately owned tea factory and plantation.  The tour, including the guide, is free.  After walking around the gardens for a while looking not just at tea but also coffee, pepper and cinnamon you are given a free cup of tea with cake.  Next to the factory where the entire drying and preparation process is explained.  Most of the machinery which is used is 145 years old and so it is like a working museum.  Then to the tasting room where you have the opportunity to taste 29 different teas.  Tasting notes are available in many different languages.  At this stage you have the opportunity to buy some of the teas. Our guide did not have good English and the tour would have rated top marks if we had been able to get better answers to questions.

Title: Informative
Text: It was interesting to hear about the different teas and spices they use in tea, but the most interesting was about white tea. The tour is not too long and you finish off see how the tea is dried and cleaned followed by a tea tasting of all the varieties they produce.

Title: Nice diversion from the beach
Text: We had a nice visit here.   The tour of the grounds was pleasant and the tour of the plant was very educational.   Prices in the salon were a bit pricey but it was great to try different teas.  We had a very nice host.

Title: Low land tea estate
Text: Enjoyed the rural drive up there by tuktuk. Entrance free and you can taste lots of teas and have a slice of cake! The tour was interesting , seeing and hearing all about the process. We also visited the factory, where some of the machinery is 150 years old.Finished with a visit to the shop (!) but no real pressure to buy.

Title: A beautiful place
Text: After seeing the highland plantations near Nuwara Eliya, we wanted to see a lowland plantation. Handunogoda was more beautiful and we were given much more information about the tea processes and about other plants. Joseph, our guide was full of information and ttpook time to explain things and answer our questions. The tea and chocolate cake were delicious and we had a tea tasting session after visiting the factory. We met Herman Guneratne, the famous tea planter and were pleased to buy his book, The Suicide Club. The visit was one of the highlights of our trip.

Title: Lovely place
Text: Lovely place with lots of history. Well worth a visit, never realised there were so many teas and to see the process from leaf to tea was very interesting

Title: Very informative guide tour
Text:
1. Free of charges. 
2. Offer free tasting of tea, including luxury white tea and a small piece of cake. 
3. The guide did explain the tea plants, type of leaves, the factory operations in very details. 

Recommend anyone to go. 

We bought some tea box, including Virgin white tea. It was quite expensive. 

in some shops in Galle, we could find white tea as well. They were of much lower price. But, of course, they are of different brands.

Title: Fascinating
Text: So many samples to try after a gentle stroll through the tea plantation with a humorous guide who was also very knowledgeable. Tea and cake supplied for just a donation. We  were taken around the factory and the whole process of making tea was described. Low key, simple, wonderful trip in the sunshine.

Title: Enchanting tea plantation
Text:
Wonderful estate providing tea to luxury European tea brands.
The visit started with a walk among the incredibly rich collection of bubbles plants of the plantation and explanations for each tea/tree variety.
We were then welcomed at the owner's house for tea and homemade cake (both delicious) before following the visit of the factory and finally the tea shop (where tea is considerably less expensive than the same one sold in Europe!).
Note: tea factory museum wasn't open yet but should open at some point in 2017.
Highly recommended.

Title: Nice tour, nice people, nice teas
Text:
Arrived at the plantation around 10 am, just in time to join the tour with a small family. Our guide was friendly and informative, the complimentary tea and cake were nice, though I would perhaps have preferred a more extensive walk around the plantation.
The tour of the tea factory was very nice and interesting, learned a lot about making tea. The supervisor leading the tour knew his stuff, the old machines looked cool, even more so in action. 
The tea tasting was very nice as well. You get a small glass and a big spoon and then you can just scoop to your hearts delight from the 30 or so different teas that are available. Small thing, I realise it may be impractical, but it would be nice if the teas were served hot to better taste them. 
You can buy each tea in the shop, but they can get a bit expensive, think at least 1000 slr for 75 grams of tea, more for the more interesting teas. Haven't visited any other tea factories yet, so can't compare prices. 
If you don't want to buy tea, leaving a small tip in the box by the exit is also fine.

Title: A good short visit on a lazy day
Text: Nice place. The gentleman giving us the tour was the Estate Manager of the property. He explained us nicely the tea-plantation and the tea-making process. Being an avid tea-drinker & lover, i really liked the whole tour and was excited to see the old British era machines still being used. To taste the Virgin White tea was really exciting and i loved the smooth and aromatic profile of the tea. You can also buy other tea-leaves or tea-bags of different quality from the estate/factory, though these are a bit expensive compared to outside market.

Title: Interesting excursion and plesant staff
Text: They offered a free excursion about how the tea, cinnamon, pepper grow and are collected. Then you will be offered tea tasting with cake. You can see the process of collecting tea and buy some tea.

Title: A must see!
Text: This is a must see if you are in the area. Give it about 2 hours. This is free, but do accept (non pressured) donations. We had an excellent tour guide who was very informative. We had a scooter and made our trip from Marissa up the coast which was scenic for a good few miles! Lots of tea  and some cake to try also!

Title: worth to see
Text: If you like tea- must see. My girlfriend and I enjoied it a lot. Very nice guide- an old man, talking very very slow, but he's very friendly, and has a grate knowledge not just about tea, but general. Estate is very nice, you can try different types of tea, and Virgin White tea.

Title: Great experience!!
Text: Loved the drive to the estate through small winding roads and quaint villages. After parking we walked through the tea estate to the tea museum. The staff received us warmly and a guide took us on a small tour of the estate. He explained everything in a most knowledgeable and friendly way. The guide then took us to the tea estate owner's bungalow where we were given cake and tea, free of charge. We were taken to the tea museum where we watched a film on tea making and tasted different types of tea. There was no pressure to buy anything and the guide refused to accept any tips. We bought some nice cinnamon tea. It was a nice experience overall. Very much recommended.

Title: So that's how tea is made! - note my TIPS!
Text:
We went here one day as part of a day trip to Galle. 

On arrival, we were promptly introduced to the owner of the Estate and then a guide took us through a small section of the plantation and up to the owner's house. On the way he explained the various types of produce they grow including tea, coffee, and rubber. At the house we were offered some cake and tea. 

The history of the tea estate is fascinating - refer "The Suicide Club". 

Afterwards, we were shown through the factory where tea is manufactured by some old but fully functional machinery, which was very interesting.

We finished at the small shop where we tasted some tea and bought some of their specialties. 

TIPS:

- There is no entrance fee. The tour is free.
- There is no expectation that you tip or purchase any of their products. 
- The tour takes about an hour. 
- Wear a hat and take some water. Walking through the plantation is hot work!

Title: Beautiful Tea Estate
Text: Had a fascinating tour of the estate and tea production area. Tea tasting afterwards was amazing too.

Title: Amazing!!!
Text: On a rainy day took a tuk tuk from Unawatuna to check out the estate. Free tour that shows 150 year old British machinery at work. Followed by a tour of the owners house with a free cake and tea! Woohooo!!! And finally a tasting of all the teas they produce. You are not pressured into buying anything but the tea was great and I picked up some tea. definitely worth a visit.

Title: Paradise
Text: This was one of the best things we did in Sri Lanka. You become used to being constantly hassled and cajoled into parting with your money,  so to visit somewhere so peaceful and beautiful, and to be given it for free,  with no obligation to buy anything,  is a unique experience.  The tour is very interesting,  giving you a real understanding of the process of making tea.  The free tea and cake on the veranda is shady and restful.  There is a shop with  dozens of free samples you can try. We didn't buy anything and there was no pressure to do so.  A thoroughly enjoyable and commendable trip out.

Title: beautiful tea plantation
Text:
We had a delightful visit here. We learned so much from our host David. We sampled over 20 types of tea and began to appreciate the differences in harvesting and production. Watching gloved women harvest the delicate Virgin White Tea was an experience. 
The gardens and  grounds on the plantation make for great stroll. 
A surprise for us was seeing the processing of the tea using antique machines, themselves works of art

Title: Wonderful!
Text:
