This was one of my favorite activities on our journey. The tour is thorough and free. It includes the plantation and factory. You get a cup of tea and bit of cake halfway through. Rubber trees, a variety of teas and black pepper are just a few of the items grown here. The tasting room was fantastic. There was no pressure to buy (though I did buy a lot because it was all so good!) and a sign is posted asking you not to tip your tour guide but to put funds in a general bin if you liked your tour. They don't use pesticides so there are a lot of red ants about, watch for them, just keep moving and you will be fine. 
Find them online at http://www.virginwhitetea.com/

Title: great tea plantation visit without the long drive to the hills!
Text: perfect add-on to other tours in the area. We combined our visit with a beach trip to Mirissa. Short enough not to bore our 8-year old son. Horse ride also available but we didn't opt for it in the end. Interesting and well-presented introduction to the process of making the virgin white tea and the other varieties of black and green tea, and of course a tasting at the end. Try the Suicide Blend! Nice gifts to purchase in the shop after sampling the numerous tea varieties. Lovely spot for photos. Feel lucky to have found this excursion which we found easily manageable by road from our base in Unawatuna.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
I'm not a particularly big tea drinker but I was curious to see a plantation and my girlfriend really wanted to buy some good Ceylon teas whilst we were visiting. It is quite a way from the main roads, but when we arrived we were met by a guide (Xavier) who first showed us the various tea leaves and rubber trees, before taking us up to a bungalow on the hill, where we were served some cake and a cup of their own tea.

Following this we walked down to the factory buildings, where we saw the entire process from drying the fresh leaves to bagging the finished products for shipping. At no point was money/tipping mentioned, which was a refreshing change from other attractions we had been to in Sri Lanka. When the factory tour was over it was suggested that we have a look in the shop, where we could buy the different varieties of teas they produce. All the different flavours were laid out for you to try, and we left with a few boxes of not inexpensive (about the same price as good quality tea in a US/European supermarket) teas. Others who didn't wish to buy anything were allowed to leave without hassle.

All in all it's well worth a visit. It is an interesting and well explained tour of the tea making process, and it was nice to be allowed to wander at your leisure without being given a hard sell. Plus, if you like tea, they have an endless list of varieties and all of it produced on the estate.

Title: Best Tea plantation in Sri Lanka
Text: Peaceful and no pressure to buy like most tea plantations in Sri Lanka. It is in the south not far from Galle and no where near the traditional tea areas visited by tourists. The owner is an author and has written a book The Suicide Club, a book about the heydays of tea production in Sri Lanka. Highly recommend a visit.

Title: Well worth a vist.
Text: Don't miss this excellent free tour with chance to sample and buy the tea at the end. You get to see the tea and rubber plantation the the leaf drying and tea making processes followed by a chance to sample the products and make a purchase.

Title: Authentic non touristy feel, detailed explanation, little to no pressure to buy, phenomenal tea
Text:
Went to a couple tea plantations / factories in Sri Lanka - this one was definitely a highlight. 
Appreciated the time the staff took to explain the production process and also to sample the teas (approx 20 teas), including complimentary cake. 

Highly recommend.

Title: Informative trip for all ages
Text:
We visited this tea plantation with kids age 5 upwards and all of us enjoyed the tour.It was hidden away and we drove through the beautiful Sri Lanka countryside to reach it.  The guide managed to keep the children interested all the way around.  Our kids were particularly interested in the rubber tree and how they harvested it. The guide then gave us tea and cakes at the plantation owners house. it was like stepping back in time. 
The factory and museum were all equally fascinating and it was great to taste all the teas at the end.

Title: Very educational and inspiring re. tea's detoxifying properties!
Text: A large group of us ranging from 2 to 50 years old visited the Handunugoda Tea Estate a few weeks ago. We had a great afternoon being shown around the estate, drinking tea and eating cake up on the hill, admiring the owner's former race horse and all the classic original giant British machinery still churning reliably away in the factory before descending to the tea museum where we sampled - and my wife went on to buy - practically every tea under the sun, as well as a colourful range of historic Ceylon postcards and posters. This is a serene and informative place, quite a winding road to get to it but one of the best outings in the South of Sri Lanka without a doubt. Highly recommended.

Title: Great place and its free
Text: We were a bit sceptical when our Tuk-Tuk driver suggested this place but as we were able to trust him agreed that we should go. So glad we did. We had one of our best trips in all our holiday. We were very lucky to be shown around by the owner Herman and as we were not part of a group we felt very privileged. We could have listened to this gentleman for hours. His passion was tea but had a full repertoire of interesting and amusing anecdotes. We had tea and chocolate cake on his veranda and were taken on a very interesting tour of the plantation and factory.The tasting room was very good but at no time were we pushed to buy any tea, and after wards were left to decide whether we would buy or not . We did. A great day out and FREE, a sad rarity in Sri Lanka.

Title: Wonderful afternoon!
Text: I'm really pleased we took the time to visit this Virgin White Tea plantation. It was in a beautifully scenic location and we started with a free guided tour. It was so interesting, really informative and educational. The children loved it and had lots of questions. It was really intriguing to see the old machinery, which they still use, made by the same company that supplied parts for the Titanic! We then went for tea tasting, which we all loved, and decided on a few purchases of some exceptional teas that were new to us! The whole visit was very enlightening and pleasurable and the friendly people at the plantation make it a must-do excursion!

Title: A fun visit - well explained and fun. Highly recommended
Text: I've been to many tea estates but to date this has been the pick especially with Herman Gunaratne as an enthusiastic & entertaining raconteur. The estate is scenically positioned in the low country & the process well explained including a short break for tea before visiting the factory, a tea tasting and opportunity to purchase not just tea but one of Herman's entertaining books. The whole visit is very well done & is great fun.

Title: Must see if you like Tea
Text: We have really enjoyed our visit at Handunugoda Tea Estate. These people really do what's their passion, they make excellent tea and take good care of the visitors. It's interesting to see how the tea is grown and processed. The cake & tasting was a nice surprise...I'm enjoying the teas from this tea estate now back in the office :) I would say for us this was the most enjoyable attraction in Sri Lanka.

Title: Must see in southern Sri Lanka
Text: We had a great visit to the tea factory & plantation, much thanks to our great guide. Good place to learn more about tea and its history. Take money with you so you can buy the excellent teas from their teashop.

Title: Fantastic place!
Text: Fantastic place! It was a great experience to be able to see a tea plantation. Fantastic photography opportunity as well. People as typical for Srilanka very friendly. There also are couple of cinnamon peelers over there to give you an idea how cinnamon is harvested. Beautiful experience!

Title: What an experience!
Text:
One of our friends in Sri Lanka suggested visiting the Handunugoda Tea Estate, and we followed his suggestion.  

We were greeted by The General Manager of the Property Mr. David Manickam, who gave us unforgettable tour of the plantation, explained how they cultivate the famous Virgin White Tea, how the tea is produced, packaged, etc.  The cup of Sapphire Oolong and then a Rainforest tea accompanied by the delicious homemade chocolate cake was the delightful break during the hot day.  

Then we visited the museum and tasted all teas produced in the Estate, including the Virgin White Tea. What an experience! The visit to the Tea Estate cant be completed without the purchase of the Virgin White Tea!  

Dont miss the opportunity to visit the Handunugoda Tea Estate!  It is free learning experience!

Title: Learn more about tea and taste some varietes
Text:
This tea factory is located in the South-West of Sri Lanka near Galle. Ask a TukTuk driver to take you there. Either select a vehicle with taxameter or one of a licensed driver. This can be identified by a corresponding license number on the windscreen. Both assure, that you pay for each driven km and not for the fantasie of the driver. Our driver knew the Tea Estate were allowed to be our guide. He brought us to the owner's house, where we got a piece of cake and two cups of tea, one without and one with cinnamon.
The driver showed us green pepper, cinnamon and - needless to say - the tea bushes, a small factory and the tasting house, where we could taste about 20 different teas.

Title: Very interesting
Text:
I would have never thought that a visit to a tea plantation can be so interesting. I really enjoyed my visit there.
The tea factory itself is, as written on a plate, is a working, living museum. I was fascinated by the old machines (over 145 years old!), and the whole process was described with lots of details by the guide (Chris?). After a week, I visited another tea plantation, so I could see the difference. The experience at Handunugoda Tea Estate was much better.
Beside the museum-like factory (that was similar to the other one I have seen), here I have also visited the plantation, I have been shown different types of trees and plants (rubber tree, mahogany, ebony, bread tree, sugar cane, pepper...), and I also had two complimentary cups of tea and a cake on a very nice porch. Also, the tea shop was very nice: 27 types of tea to taste and/or buy.
Very pleasant and interesting visit!

Title: Maybe not the best factory tour.
Text:
This tour is quite dull. 
It only took about 10 minutes, and no photos are allowed. If it was a free tour, it would be fine, but I'm not sure it's worth paying for.
We saw the tea factory at the Heritance Tea Factory hotel- it was free, and much better.

Title: Can be avoided as other options are better
Text:
Nice tea estate and one of the oldest. Tour of the factory is not free. There are other 2 tea factories in Nuwara Eliya , which I believe are better in terms of service.
Staff seemed to be least interested in selling the products, which is unusual for Sri Lanka.

Title: No explanation
Text: We intended to go on a factory tour, but they told us the factory wasnt running at the moment. We decided to do a tea tasting instead. 6 cups of tea were put in front of us without any explanation.. I then asked someone for an explanation, she just told me which cup was which tea, no further explanation.

Title: Beautiful tea estate
Text: Impressive to see all the tea plantations in Nuwara eliya, which are very big. We had a very good tour guide who showed us the factory and explained the process of making tea very clear. Also very impressive to see under which circumstances the employees live.

Title: Lovely old tea factory
Text: Lovely old tea factory in the hills.  we were given a tour of the factory and shown  how the leaves are processed. At the end we got to taste 2 kinds of tea. The tea is brewed for exactly 5 minutes.

Title: An average factory tour
Text:
We were supposed to go to Damro but went here instead as land slides had blocked the road.

A very average factory tour: the attendant walked us through the entire tea-manufacturing process in their factory. Nothing spectacular, just an average tour. 

They didn't have a lot of varieties of tea for sale either.

Title: Really disappointing
Text: We were really disappointed with our visit to Pedro Tea Factory. Firstly when we arrived noone greeted us, the staff all ignored us and it was really unclear where we were supposed to go. We figured out we had to buy tickets and were then told to wait 10 minutes until the tour started. We waited 30 minutes without any further communication about the tour. Another staff member did give us a cup of tea but with no explanation, we weren't really sure if it was actually supposed to be for us. We chose a table to sit at, but they were all very dirty with bits of food and flies and dishes unclear from previous guests. Finally our tour guide came to get us for our tour, she was very unenthusiastic and came across as in a hurry and disinterested. During the tour, our guide was very rude to other guests in our group. The guide's accent was a bit hard to understand at the best of times (not her fault as English is her second language), but she told two members of our tour group (who English was also not their first language for) that taking photos was not allowed. They clearly did not hear her/understand what was being said, and instead of gently making sure they understood, she yelled at them "do you even speak English?!". After the tour was finished she just walked off without saying goodbye or thanks or anything. Such a bad experience from start to finish! The previous day we did a tour at Damro and it was amazing! I'd definitely recommend avoiding Pedro and going to Damro instead.

Title: Damro factory is much better. If you are going to visit just one, go there. If you have time, can see both
Text:
Nuwara Eliya is a hill-station and we were not going to leave without seeing at least a couple of tea gardens and tea factories. Two of the most famous tea gardens in this town are the Pedro Tea Factory and Damro Labookellie Tea Factory.

We drove to the Pedro Tea Factory. This is NOT a working factory and therefore we decided to skip the factory tour and instead walked part of the tea garden.

Title: Average
Text: The guide tried her best, but she is average and her explanations were very general and not insightful. The factory is in operation only at night hence the instruction given to us on the process was  more or less in theory. The factory has a good view but still not worth the price you pay and the time spent.

Title: Informative tour
Text: The tour we did was informative and reasonably priced. There was a very large group with no options for a smaller group. Overall glad we went but would maybe check out a different tea factory if we were to come again.

Title: Amazing amazing memories
Text: Amazing tour , almost overwhelming with the gorgeous scenery and staff , the smell of the tea is stunning , the staff that work there are dedicated and passionate. Hard to believe that the traditional processes end up in our tea all round the world . The tasting process is an art passed through familys . It also goes into our favourite Ahmad tea and helped us understand why it tastes so wonderful

Title: tour was a let down
Text: this is apparently a working factory hence was expecting a lot from the tour. although the staff was friendly they seemed to be disinterested in conducting an informative tour. the shop has limited options in terms of packaging but was well priced. Yet to taste the tea!

Title: Learning about tea production
Text: One of our highlights to tea country was our trip to Pedro tea factory. The tour was amazing. The process was explained and we saw the machines and every step of tea production our guide was lovely and guided us with expertise and passion I was particularly impressed how they included a man on our tour who had an impairment. They were considerate of his needs and he wasnt left out. Tea tasting st the end was great and we purchased tea to take home. Highly recommend if you love tea.

Title: EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING
Text: This was one of the main reasons for our trip to Sri Lanka and this was such a disappointment. The tour when it got underway was taken by a lady guide who seemed so un-interested in her job and the customers were an inconvenience. It was so rushed and a large group whereby it was difficult to hear what was being said. This lady did not appear to want to be there and her body language exuded this. It was so rushed. Very very disappointing, don't waste your money, a small as the fee is, or more importantly your time you will be under whelmed

Title: Not Much Happening
Text: We visited Pedro Factory on Monday but there was nothing happening.  We were told that the factory does not function on Mondays - very strange.  According to our driver/tour guide, each time he visited this factory the equipment was not functioning.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Nice setting especially combined with a walk to Lovers Leap Waterfall 
Factory tour is 250rp - we went on a Sunday and not much was happening so better to try another day.  It was nice walking around the tea plantation.  Staff were friendly and the cup of tea great.

Title: excellent tour
Text: very informative tour and a lovely setting well worth visiting and trying the teas - the tea is for sale also

Title: A beautiful tea plantation and factory outside N.E.
Text: It wasn't a production day, no ladies in the plantation picking pekoe leafs, only a open day to have a stroll trough the plantation slopes, but this was beautiful. The shop was open for tea tasting and a lot of different types of Ceylon Black Tea for sale :)  (it was february)

Title: Go on a production day
Text:
It was a Sunday so the factory wasnt working. We decided not to pay for a tour as wed already seen one tea factory on a non-production day. They do let you wander the plantation which was nice, although there were no pickers working either.
Free tea tasting - just one tea, and a very small shop.
If youre going, go on a production day.

Title: It was oké.
Text:
Not very special but it was fine. The view was very nice and
the free tea and a good price for the cake.

Title: Tour around eco friendly tea factory, not far from Nuwara Eliya
Text: Interesting tour following the process from fresh tea leaves to tea packets.... with cuppa at the end. Great views. Not allowed photos in the factory. There were a lot of  initiatives to look after their workforce.

Title: Really interesting tour of the tea factory and walk in the grounds
Text: We really enjoyed our morning tour of the Pedro Tea Factory just out of Nuwara Eliya. We got to see all the stages of tea production and sample a lovely cuppa overlooking the plantation. A great way to spend an hour or so and very informative, especially if you're a tea drinker. It's got a special gentle vibe, tucked away in the hills.

Title: Really fascinating tour
Text: We had a fascinating guided tour of the factory and learned all about the tea picking, withering and packing process. We then had a cup of tea and wandered through the plantation itself. Highly recommended.

Title: Interesting tour with a great view
Text: If youre a tea lover and have time to kill its a good place to go to. The tour was nice and the views were great. Very interesting.

Title: Waste of time
Text: Went on tour of factory, could hardly understand the guide, nothing happening in the factory. Very little explanation of the picking process or tea varieties, offered a cup of tea at end of visit. Im sure there are better places to visit.

Title: Amazing view but not much explanation
Text:
We arrived at the tea boutique just when a group started the factory tour. They told us the next tour would start in 20 minutes and asked us to take a walk around the tea plantation first. The view was truly amazing. 

After the walk, we went back to the tea boutique and waited. The group we saw earlier finished their tour and was given tea to drink. We continued to wait but nothing happened. Then a staff asked us if we wanted tea. We asked if the tour would start soon and was told that it would not start for another 15 minutes. 

We ended up waiting for around 40 minutes before the tour finally started. We were given aprons and shower caps to wear. The tour guide was soft-spoken and we could only hear part of the explanations. 

After the tour, we wanted to buy some tea to take home. There were many different types of teas and we had no idea about differences. When we asked the staff, she only gave us some half-hearted attention. It would have been better if they could put up signs next to the teas to explain the differences.

Title: You paid for what u get.
Text: Potential not exploded. Could be amazing, stays on average. Good tea and views at the end. Nothing special. What a pity. The explanation is made while they dont have much going on. Hard to see it in action. Mainly cos they work at night. Hope to come back in the future and see it shining.

Title: Sullen guide
Text: Went to this factory to see the tea process.  As others have said, nothing working on the day.  We got a guide who was very quietly spoken and difficult to hear.  She told me off for having my camera open and when I asked her a question she told me to ask one of the tourists and flounced off in a huff, bringing our tour to an end.  Nice location but staffer was rude.  She was the only rude Sri Lankan we came across in our 1 month holiday, so it really left an impression (not a good one).

Title: Fabulous location
Text: This tea factory offers a tour of key production processes.  It is unfortunate that the factory is not actually operational during the daytime.  Explanations were clear and concise.  Refreshment is available and a small shop selling their products

Title: The plantation in factory  Tour
Text: many varieties of tea and The tour was wonderful  The guide was explained everything nicely also price is cheap

Title: An interesting visit to a plantation and working tea factory
Text: We had a visit to the Pedro tea factory , the factory is an excellent example of the processing required to convert the picked tea to the delicious end product. The tour is not long but showed the processes they went through. It was fascinating to see the old processing equipment still in use. Though it was disappointing the factory was not in use during our visit as it was a Monday and no fresh tea was being processed.

Title: So much tea!!
Text:
This tour gives a good insight to how tea is manufactured and is located in a very picturesque setting. 

The tour is not too long at 30 minutes and only costs R250 pp which we felt was reasonable.

Title: Tea Factory
Text: The tour at the factory was kinda short but also cheap. And it was so nice to stroll on the tea plantations after the tour. Also cup of tea was offered.

Title: Fine tour
Text: We got a fine tour through the factory. Be aware that they work during night, so most machines are turned off. Got a nice cup of tea after the tour. The tea they sell is quite overpriced so buy elsewhere.

Title: Worth a visit if the tea pluckers are working
Text: A three wheeler from Nuwara Eliya centre to the Pedro costs 350-400 rupees. The estate is in a picturesque setting and the tour is very reasonably priced at 250 rupees per person. Pedro cares about its staff and the environment - both important factors when considering which plantation to visit. The workers were off and the cleaners were in when we went round, that was fine as they warned us. The best part was talking to the tea pluckers at the end. And the cup of orange pekoe!

Title: Great place to learn a little and then enjoy the view
Text: We arrived at Pedro Tea Factory via tuk tuk (we paid 500rupees from the city centre, negotiating it from an original 1000 rupee 'tourist rate') and were ushered to join a tour (250 rupees each for foreigners). What i couldn't really find information on, was if the tour timings were adhoc or at certain times in the day. When we arrived, everything seemed more adhoc - and it appears the tours run frequently enough  and there aren't any minimum tour sizes for them to start (our tour group was 4, whereas others were 10+ people).... so arrive when you can and I'm sure the waiting time will be limited. Tour guide was friendly enough, communication was good and she was happy to take questions. You do get a free tea at the end of the tour and then we actually spent sometime just sitting and enjoying the view. There are plenty of tuk tuks waiting to take you home just outside of the gates or as many did to us on our walk down, offered to take us home.

Title: Ok experience.
Text: This was interesting if youve never been to a tea factory before, but on the day we visited the machines were not working which was a little disappointing. Also the guide who was very pleasant spoke in a quiet voice and was incomprehensible for most of the people in our group.  Also we didnt see the actual T plucking and all exactly how this was done which was disappointing and couldve been explained in more detail. However the building and machinery was interesting to look at.

Title: Ethical Tea Factory with excellent tea
Text: We went to this factory because it has been awarded with multiple certificates for treating their worker ethically. They tour of the factory was only 250 rs. The tour is rather quick and the machines are not operating (they work at night) which for us was okay. It gave us a good enough idea about the production of the tea. Afterwards you get a tea and also can buy tea if you want to. I really liked to browse the little shop, since there was no hassle and nobody was pushing us to buy something. We could even try different teas and take our time to make a decision which tea we want in the end.

Title: The free tea they give is great
Text: All tea factories in Sri Lanka is same, we went to tea factory in Lipton seat, this one is also similar to that one, but the free tea they give after tour, is amazing ;) you have to pay 250 rupee per person...

Title: Very interesting
Text:
We went on a Sunday so no picking or processing happening but lovely staff showed us around .Certainly puts a different perspective on a simple cup of tea ! Such hard physical work for the ladies picking .
Great tea samples after the tour.

Title: A Tea plantation visit is part of the Hill Country experience
Text:
Our group visited the Perdro Tea Plantation & factory as part of our tour of the Hill country. They produce Lovers Leap ethical tea.
We were shown around the factory by a local plantation worker who explained the tea production process & showed us the various steps from picking to drying & quality control. She was very interesting in describing a very labour intensive process.
We also saw tea pickers & had a cuppa in the factory tea shop. Very enjoyable & informative.

Title: Pretty uninspiring tour
Text:
The price of the tour is not much, but the commentary was pretty uninspiring. The only two sections of the factory working at the time was the sorting of the finished tea into its various grades from the top grade orange pekoe to the tea dust.  We did see the first process but I didn't hear the name where the leaves are initially dumped in big bays to be dried with wood fire heat to remove enough moisture from the leaves to make them rubbery and then allow the rolling process. But there was no machine on to show the rolling, the fermentation, or the cutting etc. After seeing the sorting, we saw the packaged product ready for auction, then  it was back to the shop for a cup of their tea but no explanation of what we were drinking etc. So a pretty short and basic tour of the factory with a commentary that hard to hear at the best of times, but was inaudible when the sorting machine was on. We didn't see any tea pickers.  I think by the afternoon they were all clocking off.

The tea fields were nice to look at.  The tea in the cafe was nice.

Title: Very disappointing
Text: Everything about the visit was bad. Not sure if we got a particularly unmotivated guide, but she just repeated what she memorized and explained what each machine does. We asked several follow up questions, but her answer was not insightful. Also, we all get free tea but honestly the tea tasted worst than the cheapest tea I drink back home. They provide third grade tea. After drinking that tea, I definitely didnt want to buy any tea from the factory. Lastly, now the tour fee is 250 lak. Overall, it was a waste of time. I could google and drink better tea at home.

Title: Underwhelming.
Text: The tour was short and underwhelming. I came out with as little knowledge as I went in.  Far nicer is the Hertance tea hotel.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Factory tour with the guide was very interesting and informative. They charge a  nominal fee of LKR250 for adults and my kids were allowed without a charge. 

They run the factory during the night shift only so couldn't see most machines working but despite that one would get a good sense of how tea is produced.

We also walk down the tea bushes but didn't see any plucking activity in that part unfortunately.

I would recommend this place to people who have not been to a tea factory before.

Title: Nice tour and delicious tea!
Text:
Since this tea factory was very close to our Nuwara Eliya hotel, we decided to take a tour.  It was a bit disorganized at the beginning, as we purchased our ticket and were then told to sit in a waiting area.  Meanwhile, we saw people gathering and being handed aprons, and turns out this was our group, but no one told us.  So we joined in and had an informative walk through the factory.  Most of the work is done at night, as the tea picked during the day has to dry, so only a couple of machines were actually running.  No problem, and they were nice enough to let us know this when we purchased the tour ticket.

Our favorite part was the cup of tea provided at the end.  We enjoyed sitting outside on the balcony with a lovely view of the plantation.  We hope you enjoy the tour as much as we did!

Title: Not a rounded tour
Text:
While the guide was fine, it wasn't a very rounded tour. They should start with showing tea plucking, through the factory with showcasing the old wood burners and letting people see the different grades. It should end with a tea tasting where ppl can try to taste the differences. Great location and definitely worth taking the walk to the waterfall as well.

The guides (I overheard a few while we were there) should try to introduce themselves and give a little personal story of their relationship to the estate. I would assume our guide was the daughter of a estate worker who has learned english and is now guiding groups which is nice to see.

Title: Historical tea factory
Text: This is a smaller, more historical tea factory, built in 1885. The entrance costs 250 rupee ($1.40) and the tour lasts about 20 minutes. The tour is very interesting and it includes a cup of tea. You can walk around the tea plantations afterwards. You'll see women working, they allow photos, but a small donation is expected.

Title: Interesting if you enjoy tea
Text: Interesting tour which shows you from start to finish how tea is produced. The machinery wasnt working the day we went but the tea tour was still worth it. Free cuppa at the end.

Title: Interesting
Text: Really worth the 20 minutes that the tour takes.   Great to get an insight into how tea is produced as well

Title: proper working lesson on tea making
Text: It was a Sunday they were washing down the machinery and finishing production, fascinating. Like stepping back in time.

Title: Tea culture
Text:
This is a great place to go with kids.
They have tea factory tour.u need to pay for that.But its worth for the cost and affordable.

Title: A waste of time.
Text: The tour took 15mins at most including the walk from the boutique to the factory and back. We were provided only very basic information about the manufacturing process,none about tea fields, tea bushes or plucking. We didn't have an opportunity to ask questions,as the guide simply told us (at what seemed like a random point of the tour) to take a seat in order enjoy a cup of tea, without saying goodbye or in any other way suggesting that the tour had come to an end. Expecting her to at least tell us what kind of tea we would be served (to this moment we do not know) or asking us whether we had any questions was apparently too much to ask. We would have at least partially understood this kind of attitude had the factory been busy,but we only came across three other guests in the facilities who had already been taken care of. Definitely not worth 250 rupees. We ended up finding out a lot more about tea production from blogs written by tourists who visited other factories,which I find very sad. Honestly I fail to understand the added value of taking the tour. You can simply stroll through the countless tea fields above the factory (with better views) and later enjoy a nice cup of tea at a restaurant while reading about tea production on wikipedia. I sure hope that the tours at other factories are more worthwhile.

Title: Interesting place
Text:
Excursions to the factory goes every half an hour. (Till 16.30, as I remember)
If you want to see working machines, you need to come in early mornings (may be not all days)
But its not necessary to see  exactly working process. Its interesting anyway.
Guides speaks English, so all information is understandable.
You could see old machines and know many interesting facts about tea manufacture. 
The smell of tea is amazing.
And also you could walk among tea trees on tea plantations behind the factory.
Its very beautiful.
You could see the process of picking tea leaves into special baskets. 
Working women could show you tea leaves and you could taste it. So also they suggest you to take a photo with them, but they also wants you to pay for photos. And its strange.
Also you could but very good tea in a factory shop. In the shop you could ask about process of brewing tea.
Its a good gift.

Title: a scenic place. Their prime intention is to make you purchase their products. the climate is very soothing.
Text: Their prime intention is to make you purchase their products. the climate is very soothing. can visit.

Title: Nice place
Text: Overall the place is very nice. However, we did not receive a fair treatment. After purchasing the ticket they told us that the factory was not working that day and therefore the machines were off... The girl who guided us through the tour was just repeating phrases that she clearly memorized few days before... also the level of English was quite poor. On the other hand, you get the chance to walk around the plantation and to drink a nice cup of tea at the end.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We went to this on our way to Heritance Tea Factory. Unfortunately it was a Sunday so the factory wasnt working but we saw a tea factory and got a good explanation of its working. Worth the hour stop. They dont allow photos. No idea why not.

Title: A nice cup of tea
Text: Excellent tour followed by a lovely cup of Pekoe. No better place to find out what makes a good cuppa and - see photos- a bit of a looker!

Title: Lots of steps
Text: Interesting tour but two groups merged to one as they were short staffed so over 35 people walking around the factory together was not ideal. Some of the group were elderly and the many steps and metal staircases were a bit challenging which also slowed down the tour. Free cup of tea at the end and the views from the cafe are fabulous.

Title: Nice
Text:
Went here to have a look at the lounge .. its beautiful surrounded and overlooking the tea estate !! A cup of tea here just to sit and watch the view is great .. went venturing out in the tea estate itself plucking tea leaves !! 

The tea cake wasnt the most delicious ones Ive had but it was okie !!

Title: Come for the tea, not the tour
Text: Tea factory with factory tour and shop plus nice views. We had a brief group tour which cost 250LKR each for approx 30min tour. The tour guide was arguing with workers for a long period of time and I got the sense we were not welcome to watch the workers load up tea. That said we had a rudimentary tour of the factory and I left with more knowledge about tea than I came with. At the end we all had a complimentary cup of tea which was very nice and were encouraged to buy some tea at the shop. I think the tea here is better than other places but a bit disappointed by the tour.

Title: Well conducted tour
Text: The factory tour is extremely well presented and any questions from the visitors were well dealt with.  Not to be missed if one has the opportunity to go

Title: Nice
Text:
The visit was nice but a little bit short. We had a free tea cup at the end of the visit. 

The views are beautiful from the factory.

Title: How tea leaves processed for consumption
Text: Entry to the factory is free. but if you want to enter inside the processing unit and see the different stages of tea leaves processing you will have to pay SLR 250 per head. The entire factory visit will take around 30 minutes time. You will be served complementary tea at the end of the factory visit. there are a lot of places around for clicks. Must visit place in Nuwra Eliya. Preferred time of visit morning till 12 noon.

Title: Couldn't get a cup of tea!
Text: We went straight to the Tea Boutique and separately ask two staff members for a cup of tea. They each told us to sit and wait then disappeared. Waste of time.

Title: Interesting process
Text: Worth a visit and the guide answered all the questions although I do not know why photos were not allowed to be taken. No pressure was put on us to buy the tea.

Title: Quite Interesting, nice tea
Text: The tea factory is an interesting place which provides a tour which is informative. There is a lot of talk about how little the tea pickers earn (~800lkr per day) which seemed like a ploy to get tips, which probably dont find their way to the tea pickers.

Title: Don't dare to take photos!
Text: Interesting tour round tea factory but the over-zealous guide was obsessed by telling us not to take photos! Accused one young lady of taking them when she hadn't. Must have though we were all competitor spies although there was hardly state-of-the-art innovative machinery to spy on!

Title: Better tea factories
Text: There were 2 options - 250 rupees for tea factory or 1000 for tea factory and tea picking. We opted for the latter and picked tea first. The lady took us down and we got dressed in the tea picking clothing, and she only said how to pick tea leaves and then left us to it for 20 mins. She didnt explain anything about tea picking or the process. We then walked round the tea factory which wasnt active with another uninspired lady who was on autopilot when explaining things. At the end we were given a lovely cup of tea but were not told anything about it. Visited another tea factory in our trip and had a much better experience and learnt so much from an enthisiastic guide who turned on the machine where the factory wasnt active for us to help visualise the process, and then we bought tea from there!

Title: Disappointing visit - not worth the time or money
Text:
On arrival we were given the option of tea factory tour for Rs 250 or tea picking for Rs1000. We went for the latter which turned out to be a huge mistake. We were shown how to pick one tea leaf then left to our own divides for 20 minutes, whilst the guide was preoccupied with her phone. We were not told anything about the tea plantation or the tea picking process. 

After this we were taken on a tour of the factory, but all the machinery was off as they only use the factory at night. During the tour the guide was more interested with her friends, giggling and waving at them, than giving us any real information about the factory. She also spoke in autopilot and was inspiring. 

Overall a very disappointing visit and not worth the money. This trip was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons.

Title: An Essential Part of a Sri Lankan trip - visit a tea factory, so we went to the Pedro Tea Factory.Guide spoke very quick
Text: Disappointing tour of the tea factory as the guide had a poor English accent and spoke very quickly. Amazingly they did not sell the lovely green smocks which they insisted all visitors had to wear on the tour. BIG missed opportunity.

Title: Excellent
Text:
We visited a number of tea factories and got tired of the hard sell. 
Pedro tea factory was different. It had a lovely feel. The lady who showed us around was really lovely. There tea is delicious and there was no hard sell at all. 
Highly recommend

Title: Not bad if youre interested in seeing tea factory
Text: I wasnt really into this, but my lady was and the tuk tuk driver recommended it... youll take a 15 minute walk through the factory and see how tea is made... they let you have a tasting and hope youll buy something.

Title: Best tea factory in NE
Text: Honestly we visited 2 tea factories and found this one the best . It was nice , the tour was really nicely done and the estates were soooo pretty and secluded. Totally worth the visit

Title: No tours
Text: We went out of our way to visit this tea factory due to a write up in the Lonely Planet.  They did tours, but they were at a cost, and the factory is not in operation during the day, so there is not much to see.  The tea room and gift shop was pretty uninspiring, so we spent about 5 minutes there and left.  Waste of a tuk tuk fare.

Title: Worth a visit!
Text:
Interesting place to visit. We came at about 8:30 AM (visiting hours are 8:00-11:00 AM and also in the afternoon, but I cant remember exact hours). 
We immediately got a guide (entrance fee - 250 rupees per person, but guide is for free, you can leave tips, if you want). The guide was kind and told us everything about the factory clearly and we went through all the steps: from picking leaves to packing a tea. 
In the end of the tour we could taste a cup of their tea while enjoying the tea fields view from the big windows. 
You can buy some tea in their shop and have a walk trough tea fields, even talk with the workers. 
Really nice time we had! It took us ~ 1 hour.

Title: What a great way to learn about tea
Text:
We were only staying about 3 mins down the road from this factory so it was the natural place to visit. Maybe not as grand or as big as some of the other factories, but our experience was excellent. Some days the factory is not in full production and this is due to the weather. When it is full and raining the tea leafs are not growing and therefore are not being picked.

It was in half operation when we were there, and the lady who escorted us around for almost an hour was excellent. She advised she was the daughter of parents who had also worked at this factory for many years. She had been there for more than 8 years working also, and had climbed the ladder to a tour guide supervisor.

There is a 250lkr  entry fee and that covers the tour and a cup of tea at the end. The lady clearly explained in very good English the full process while taking us through the different drying, rolling, and sorting rooms of the factory. She welcomed our many questions.

A worker at the factory or in the field does an 8 hour shift and gets paid 850lkrs for that shift. All workers at this factory live in company provided housing, so while the pay is very low in comparison to most western countries, the workers we spoke to are very happy to have steady work and a roof over their heads. 

So a great thank you to the senior tour guide at Pedro, well done! We are far more educated now.

Title: Very Interesting Tour
Text: When we visited the Pedro Tea Factory the weather was too wet for tea picking so the factory was not operational. Nonetheless we had an excellent guide and it was fascinating to see the equipment and learn about all the different teas and how they process the tea leaves

Title: Visit the factory and enjoy a cup of tea with a great view
Text: Interesting to see the factory and get a better understanding of all the process steps for making tea. Unfortunately the factory is running during nighttime, so you do not get to see the process in working, but you get to see all the Machines and get an explenation of all the steps. The tour is finished by getting to try a cup of the from the factory, and you can buy a lot of differnet tea sorts as a souvernier

Title: Tea factory vis
Text: We visit Pedro tea factory in August 2018. It is only 10 minutes to Nuwara Eliya the factory is working only nights. They made a quick tea factory tour and served a cup of tea at the end of the tour. They are selling also their own tea. You are paying 250 rupies ( less than 2usd)  for person. You may find another place which is free on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Interesting and helpful guide
Text:
Visited early in the morning as an alternative activity to our trip to Horton Plains being cancelled. They were extremely helpful, despite the electricity being off, they managed to make us a hot and welcome cup of tea and a tour of the factory. The tour is free and there is a small shop to purchase the estate Tea from. It is useful to offer the factory guide a small tip of 100/200 rupees.
The factory is full of the most original machinery much of which is still in operation today, so if you are a lover of this sort of thing, you would definitely enjoy a visit.
I was surprised at how quickly tea leaves are turned into tea, within 24 hours and that the aluminium lined bags they pack the tea into at the end of the process can keep the tea for upto 2 years.
The estate announces that it is an ethical company with some opportunity for the workers to be involved and would appear to offer more medical care and education than some others do.
I wasn't sure about this place as there were some remarks about the speed of the tour and the guides accent, but we did not feel rushed at all and the guide was clear, helpful and very friendly.

Title: Little bit disappointed
Text:
Our guide was a very poor English speaking lady. The tour was very fast. You do not visit the tea plantation itself, only the factory. 

Afterwards you might get a cup of tea.

Title: Tea leaf picking
Text:
Actually got the chance to go amongst the tea bushes and pick tea leaves if you. I believe not many tea factories allow you to do this but this one does and it is near the town of nuwara eliya so it is very convenient if youre staying around town. 

Didnt go for the tour though as we went for another tour at another factory previously and i dont see how the process would be much different.

Title: A little bit disappointing
Text:
We went for a tour to this factory. Our guide was a lady that spoke very unclear english. She guided us at a high speed through the production facility where nobody was working. Only during the night there is production. So after the tour we have seen all the machines but still do not know exactly how the production is being done.
Afterwards you receive a cup of tea.

Title: TEA FACTORY
Text: This is an excellent Tea factory experience. The guide Kalai vani was excellent. The view is beautiful. Tea very good. A good experience.

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
We went here for the tour and tea picking experience. Tour was very informative but you werent allowed to take photos. I was impressed some of the machines were installed in 1950s- built to last in those days! Tea from here is wholesale sold on to big companies who blend it to their own specifications. There were 65kg bags in the packing area!
At the end you get a cup of tea to try.
Being a photographer I really wanted to get some photos of the tea pickers but it seemed they werent working the Monday we went. We managed to see some further out of town so got some pictures then. Worth a visit!

Title: Factory tour
Text: We had a short but informative tour of the factory in a small group and learnt heaps about tea making. This dispelled some of the mystery and myth. Highly recommend to anyone with an hour to spare

Title: Excellent Tour
Text:
We enjoyed a very interesting and informative tour of the tea plantation at the Lovers Leap Pedro Tea Factory.
The tour is quite short and takes you through the factory, explaining the various stages in tea production from harvest to drying, to grading and to packaging. The guide spoke English and was very well informed about the process and the history of the plant.
Afterwards you are given compkimentary delicious tea on the balcony overlooking the plantation where there are lovely views and you are able to go for a walk down among the tea plants which was something we really enjoyed.
They have a small shop selling their tea if you want to buy presents, absolutely no hassle or pressure though. A great morning or afternoon out; highly recommended.

Title: Interesting but lacking
Text: We learnt more from our guide before we got to this place. It was interesting but missing parts of information regarding the growing of tea. It would have been more interesting if the factory was actually working the afternoon we visited. We were told they only function at night due to the correct temperature for processing tea.

Title: love the scenery
Text: nice loving scenery and the weather was really good. the factory is very traditional as they are still using very basic machinery and process to product tea

Title: Tea factory
Text: A nice tea factory where they make primarily black tea. Staff is nice which takes you through the factory and explain the process.

Title: Tearrific!!
Text: Having read mixed reviews we were pleasantly surprised with our visit. Well signposted, easy booking, 250LKR pp, lovely guide, interesting tour and great cup of tea. Good value for money.

Title: A charming visit
Text: A charming tea factory. We did a factory tour followed by a cup of tea then we were able to wander through the nearby slopes watching the women pick tea. The factory was very interesting and so clean.

Title: Nice Place to Visit
Text: Ive been at Pedro Tea Factory to times and it was very interesting both times. It was a friendly guide, who showed us that old and very traditional factory. After the tour you will be invited for a nice cup of tea. Also you can buy tea with a high quality for a reasonable price.

Title: Nice staff and tea room
Text: Pedro Tea Factory is not quite as fancy as others in the area but definitely worth a visit. The staff was friendly and helpful. There is a outside area where you can have a cup of tea and enjoy the beautiful view.

Title: Quick tour, full of information and a great cup of tea.
Text:
A good tour, although rather quick (roughly 20-30 mins). We came on a Sunday so only one machine was working, and no tea picking - not to mention torrential rains. 

Our tour guide was really informative, giving us plenty of info although it wouldve been nice to hear about more about the founding of the estate and the fermentation process. But for 250lkr and a great cup of tea at the end (which we then purchased for a great price) its definitely worth the trip from Nuwara Eliya.  

The views are beautiful and Im sure during the week when the pickers are out and the weather is more pleasant a stroll around the fields would be worth it. 

Id recommend getting a list of questions you want to ask, as theyre happy to answer any questions if you find you havent had one answered.

Title: Informative tour of tea production in the home of tea
Text:
Youre shown around the processing factory. The tour finishes off in the tea shop where you can then stroll around plantation. Were big tea drinkers so we enjoyed it. We even chatted with some of the tea ladies in the fields. 
Fun fact: their collection bags are attached to their hats (not their backs)

Title: Good tour but not much happening
Text: We took this tour and another on the same day, this tour was educational and we learnt a lot about the tea making process which is good however there was no option to walk around the plantation after the tour, it seemed as though it was more effort and nobody came to show us the gift shop either which was strange. The tour cost 250LKR pp. It was a rather hurried trip and we only stayed for around 30 mins from arrival time to leaving. Other plantations offer a more relaxed welcome.

Title: Poor service, poor tea
Text:
We visited this factory on 4th October and were looking forward to a tour around their site. Unfortunately we didnt make it to this point. 

After buying our ticket for the tour we spent almost 40 minutes sat waiting for it to start, after being told it was a 10 minute wait. After around 30 mins we were told it would be another 5 minutes and waited another 10 before leaving. It was very disappointing to see that they had chosen to prioritise the bus tours over our custom. It also did not help that the waiting area was completely infested with flies. 

We were given a cup of tea to try whilst we waited, with one of the cups arriving with the previous users lipstick on which is always very appetising. The tea was weak and not particularly enjoyable.

All of this mounted together helped our decision to leave without the tour starting. We would recommend there are plenty of other tea factories in the Nuwara Eliya area where they treat all customers with respect.

Title: Interesting easy tour
Text: This place is close to Nuwara Eliya. Its a 40 min walk or a quick Auto-rickshaw. Our guy took us there from town, waited for us and took us back to the hotel for 600 rupees. We did a tour which was as only 20 min and really quite interesting. It was 250 rupees each and the woman taking the tour was quite engaging and interesting. Nice cuppa tea at the end. An easy and relatively quick way to see a good tea plantation.

Title: A tour of the actual factory is comprehensive and interesting
Text: This very old original tea estate offers tours to visitors of the main factory during the day as the tea is actually made at night when it is cooler. Clear explanations of the various levels of tea and a beautiful cup of tea at the end. Stunning location close to town.

Title: Interesting and great setting
Text:
Well worth a visit, very informative and interesting.

All staff were friendly and no sales pitch at the end too

Title: Interesting tour of tea factory
Text: once completed tour go to the tea house to enjoy a full flavoured tea. staff friendly and helpful. You can purchase tea there.

Title: Interesting But Not That Great
Text:
To be fair, it was interesting and was set in stunning Countryside. We learned about the tea making process and that was an enjoyable experience - but because they make light tea most of the really interesting work and processing is done overnight, meaning the tour was primarily around an empty and quiet factory - more like a museum tour, which is not what it was billed as. Worth it ifyou have time to kill and are in the area, but would not go out of your way. 

Plus, as always, the shop is very overpriced.

Title: Good tea factory experience.
Text:
Visited Pedro having been left wanting on a trip to Stone Gate the previous day. 

Pedro is actually based on the plantation and you can see the tea plants and pickers in action. 

Good tour and explanation, but machines arent working as the quality of tea they produce is made at night (when cooler to slow down the the fermentation process) and I guess it would be dangerous anyway to walk around a factory in production anyway. 

Nice cup of tea afterwards, and a very soft sell in the shop, with really good prices. 

Afterwards had a wander through the tea plants and then walked up to Lovers Leap. 

Well worth a visit.

Title: Waste of Time !!
Text: One of the reasons we went to Sri Lanka was to see a tea factory in production.  Owing to the type of tea they produce here the production only takes place at night.   We were given a quick tour around looking at inactive machines which made us none the wiser.   You are then left in the reception area to watch a marketing video about how wonderful Pedro is and how they are helping the community etc (and given a cup of tea!).   Given the lack of tea production you see on this waste of time tour, it would be far more useful to show a video of the tea production, at least then you would not feel you were leaving as badly informed as you were when you arrived!   There are tea factories where you can see tea being produced and I suggest you visit one of those!!

Title: Very interesting and free tea at the end
Text: We had a tour of this tea factopry during our 6 day tour of Sri Lanka. The two, of us were taken round by a very knowledgeable young lady who was able to answer all of our questions. Unfortunately photography isn't allowed inside the factory but I did manage to get one picture which gives you an idea of what it's like

Title: Interesting tea factory tour
Text: Had a nice 20 minute tour round the factory (note: machinery operates only at night). The tea house could do with having a larger outside terrace to enjoy the plantation views whilst sampling the different teas. Also had a wander through the plantation for some good photo ops with/of the tea pickers.

Title: Nice short tour
Text: Dropped by on the way from the Horton plains and weren't disappointed. A nice short tour in the plant with a cup of tea afterwards made the end of the day. One can crop the tea leaves as well but we were unlucky - it started to rain once we set off.

Title: Pleasant Experience; Great views
Text: We all had to have a picture of us in our green aprons you have to wear for the tour. The tour was nice - some very old equipment. Interesting how the different teas are made. Nice cup of tea on the deck overlooking a great view.

Title: Fast and short
Text: Its a short briefing on the flow of making tea. Factory have its specialty as i read in google. It was interesting and fun. A cup of tea as a complimentary before visit the factory. The view of tea estate was awesome! We met an estate worker while taking picture. Worker are so friendly but someone take for granted asked us to paid the worker because we taking their picture.

Title: No photos please!
Text:
Pleasant enough guided tour although not so much to see unless you come after 11.30 when the first tea comes in from the fields. 
Photography not permitted! Why not? Management policy apparently. Seriously? Whats the secret. 
A visit to a tea plantation last year in Kerala was much more animated and entertaining because they made sure to have a small batch of tea being crushed, rolled and dried specially for the fee paying visitors. 
Tea shop not impressive but maybe theyre more interested in selling by the sack at market than by the packet to tourists. I missed opportunity alas

Title: Better option abound
Text: The guide could not have cared less. Shortest tour possible. Couldn't even be bothered giving us a cup of tea. AND had to pay for the "privilege". Much better options elsewhere - and no charge!

Title: Informatory and interesting tour
Text: Visited this tea plantation, whist staying at Nuwara Eliya, during our recent tour of Sri Lanka.  Sited in old buildings with old machinery, built in the 50s, we were taken on an interesting 30 minute tour,which gave us a good insight into the basic process of what happens from the time the leaves are brought in from the fields, til they are graded and bagged up to be sent to the tea auctions in Columbo.  For some unknown reason, not allowed to take photos during the tour.  At the end of the tour there are photo opportunities outside and a chance to sample one of their products.  There is a shop where you can purchase their tea, but only in large bags, so not worth the bother.  Company could do with a PR overhaul, but a pleasant morning nevertheless.

Title: Lovely estate
Text:
Enjoyable tour of the factory with an informative guide.
The ticket for 200r was very reasonable as it also included cup of tea at the end.
I wanted to buy some tea however they only came in large boxes so would be great if they had smaller packaging.

Title: good insight into the production of tea
Text: An interesting guided tour of the factory followed by a cup of their tea.  Only one of their products was available to sample as part of the price.  It would have been good to sample other blends as we had done at other tea fctories.  Price was 200 Rupees, which was reasonable

Title: Excellent English with unreal tea
Text: The tour was excellent throughly explained how the tea was made from start to finish. Would recommend

Title: Interesting well worth while
Text: Good tour and an interesting insight into how tea is picked and prepared for packaging. Also has great views of the tea estate and a nice place to relax and drink tea (what else)

Title: Beautiful but are they really ethical?
Text:
We visited the factory with a group and there is no doubt the surrounding area is stunning and everyone is very pleasant
I was struck by the emphasis their signs made about how ethical they are
I am reliably informed that the pickers are paid only 500 SLR a day - the equivalent of A$5 and not paid if they are sick
Our guide was so ill she had not have sit down breaks so she would not collapse
This same multi national company still has its office workers using a typewriter with carbons and a manual ledger!

User_Location: Prague, Hlavni Mesto Praha, Czech Republic
Title: Short visit
Text: Short (15 min) visit to the factory for 200 LKR per person with a free cup of tea afterwards on a terrace with beautiful view. Our guide looked little bit annoyed. Not allowed to take pictures inside. It is easily reachable by public bus from the city centre (around 25 LKR per person, 15min). You can also take a walk from here to the Lover's Leap watterfall.

Title: A great visit but a huge rip off by the tour company!
Text: We paid £26.71 per person for 6 people for a private tour.  The tour company didn't realise it was a public holiday and so there were no pickers on site and the factory wasn't working.  There were people on site who greeted us and actually did give us a tour but, not realising we had pre-booked the visit, they said it would cost us SLR200 each - i.e. approximately £1!  So - in essence, we paid £25 for a very expensive taxi ride from our hotel to the tea plantation approximately 3 km away!  You can turn up at the Pedro Tea Plantation at any time and be given a tour for SLR 200 and the price of a Tuk Tuk from town.  Having said that, the tour was very interesting.

Title: Lovely plantation, but some room for improvements
Text:
There is no signage to this effect, but you buy your ticket (Rs. 200) in the nicely located tea shop.  It took a while to get to it, as people line up to ask for prices of the various tea packages.  Apparently, management does not want to put the prices on the shelves, but rather have each customer approach the cashier to ask. 

The entrance ticket is amusing. There's a list of admonishments about proper behavior in the factory, including "Do not waste time inside the Factory."

After a short wait we got an apron to put on, and joined a large group on the tour.  We were about 20 visitors, too many to always hear the guide.  She spoke good English, but sometimes her voice was drowned out by the machinery.

The best part of the visit was the nice cup of tea on the terrace overlooking the lovely plantation

Title: Fascinating insight into tea production.
Text: We took the factory tour with a knowledgeable guide. The process really is visible and makes you start to think twice about what goes into our staple cups of tea. The tea pickers have back-breaking work, nevertheless they are happy to welcome you to their world. You can get a nice selection of teas from the shop - without any pressure selling.

Title: Nice but too short visit
Text: The plantation is very beautiful and you can also visit by your own walking through the fields. The visit at the factory does not cost so much but it's really too short and at the end we had just a cup of tea (same for everybody, you cannot choose). You can buy tea, but the prices are a little bit higher than in other stores.

Title: Nice facilities but hard to understand the guide
Text: The tour guide from the tea factory has strong accent. It's very hard to understand what she said. The facilities inside the factory are good though. However, the souvenir shop was disappointing. Very few options and no price tag there. Also they use special names for different types of tea so even harder to know what types of tea they are. The only advantage is this tea factory is not too far. We have been to Bluefield tea garden and ceylon tea museum in Kandy. Those are much better places to buy tea in terms of varieties and prices.

Title: interesting tour and good tea
Text:
The guided tour is about 40 minutes and it costs 200 rp per person. At the end you can have a cup of tea.
It's interesting if you haven't visited one already. The area all around it's very nice and you can walk around the tea plantations!

Title: Very beautiful
Text: We didn't try excursion there as it costs 300 rupees and we visitrd Bluefield earlier for free. But we really enjoyed the tea plantation view downhill (not such impressive like Lipton's seat but also good).

Title: Interesting but avoid a large tour group
Text: Unfortunately the size of the tour group (about 20) was too large for the factory tour guide to manage However, the tour was still interesting in terms of the process of making tea from growing to packaging for the market Tea can be purchased at very reasonable prices.

Title: Very lovely tour!
Text: Lovely tour of a tea factory with beautiful views and excellent service... and you get to wear a super sexy outfit to boot!

Title: Worthwhile
Text: Really interesting and informative tour is very workwhile. Explains a lot about the industry how tea is made and the history

Title: Lovely little tour
Text: It's not a big thing, give yourself an hour or two max. But it's a lovely little trip very informative of tea production and cup of tea thrown into the mix for 200 rupees. So can't complain.

Title: Informative tour and lovely plantation
Text: Even though the factory was not working (tea production occurs at night here) the guided tour was very informative.  The tea rooms are quite nice and offer great views out over a picturesque section of the plantation.  The cup of tea was lovely also!

Title: Average - busy and hard to hear guide
Text:
Its a pity that the group sizes are so big.
We were shown around by a very sweet lady but unfortunately we couldnt hear a word she said, due to the noise of the machinery. 
the gardens are pretty, and it was interesting to look around the factory but overall we felt that they should have more but small tour groups.

Title: Great to see Tea production and put IT in its conceptual reference
Text: To learn how to produce Tea, to understand the work environment in a Tea factory, to understand a little bit more about the plucking of Tea as Well the value chain to the end-consumer. Great and interesting. Pedro seems to be a small and regular production unit, extending with guided Tours, show room, and Tea testing, offering a small range of its products.

Title: Don't bother visiting!
Text: Paid 200 LKR for the factory tour which the staff told us would take 20 minutes. The machines weren't operating during our visit and we were completely fine with it. The tour took only 10 minutes and the guide wasn't knowledgeable at all. Everyone who left good reviews must have gotten a different guide. When I asked questions, she seemed very annoyed and was just hurrying us to get out of the tea factory to quickly end the tour. The guide is a local woman who is quite short and skinny (if you must know to avoid her). After the tour, they will serve you a cup of tea and it took them 20 minutes and after asking multiple times to serve us our tea. Very bad experience overall! Teas on sale are overpriced too. Other travellers we met who visited blue fields said that was really nice so perhaps check that out instead of Pedro. Bluefields offer free tour too I think! Avoid Pedro at all cost!

Title: Interesting to Visit
Text: The half hour tour costs 200 rupees and takes you through the workings of the factory. The guide was very honest and answered all questions including what wages the workers received. Interesting to learn that the grades of tea are sold at auction in Colombo to companies that then add flavours to the basic tea. You are served a good cup of tea either before or after the tour - no milk provided! Great you can walk through the tea plantations which are lovely.

Title: A Lesson In Tea
Text: The friendly guides at the tea factory give you a reasonably comprehensive tour of the tea drying and preparation process. You end up with, what else, a nice cup of tea and it was actually one of the nicest cups of tea I've ever had. A good learning experience.

Title: Beautifully located nice tea café with a great view
Text: Nice tea shop. Offers guided tours in the tea factory. At the end of the tour you are served a cup of tea in the café with a nice view. You can take walk in the hills.

Title: Interesting demonstration on how tea is made.
Text: Guide was very knowledgeable and was focused on explaining the tea making process rather than selling tea!

Title: Pretty view, disappointing tour
Text:
There are nice views of the tea plantation but they can be had for free from the side of any road in the region. 
Our half hour 200 rupee pp tour took about 10 minutes and our guide clearly didnt want to be there. I also found the tea at the end to be weak. 
Not a highlight for the trip.

Title: Good to visit
Text: We were greeted with a hot cup of team (no milk or cookies) but it was refreshing. It requires a small fee to enter inside the factory. Unfortunately we visited it on Sunday so we could not see if live but we still received a guided tour of the factory inside and how tea is made .

Title: Closest Factory to Town
Text: Its a small factory and when i visited, it was not operational. They showed us around and offered us a cup of tea at the end. Costed 200. It was OK trip and only thing working for it was that this was the closest factory to the city. Many people come by tuk tuk (400-500 Rs) but one can easily find bus from city center which drops you just outside the factory and cost you like 20 rs. The path leading to lovers leap is just opposite to factory (passing through tea plantation of pedro estate) and both activities can be coupled together.

Title: Interesting little tour
Text: Wasnt a high cost for this tour and you get to have a roam afterwards. Our tour guide doesnt seem to get that much enjoyment from the job and it felt a little underwhelming but it was still informative and I learnt stuff about tea- which was the point. Its good to combine with a loop walk up to lovers leap and then get a tuk tuk back to town

Title: Nice place to enjoy a cup of tea
Text: I had already visited two tea factories so i did not bother taking the tour, but i rested in the cafe where i watched a documentary about Pedro Tea Estate and then enjoyed a free cup of tea. However there were quite a few people taking the tour and they seemed satisfied. I hiked here after passing by Lover'sLeap waterfall, but the last kilometer is along a busy road which was not too enjoyable.

Title: A nice hour spent looking at tea plantation
Text:
A tuk tuk from town should cost about 500 each way.
This is a nice tea factory. It's interesting to look around how it all works.

Title: Disappointing
Text: We travelled from Kandy to Pedro tea plantation by train which took us about 4 hours which was great. When we arrived at the tea plantation we were given a cup of tea and a tour of the factory which was rushed and took us twenty minutes. A total waste of time and a waste of my holiday. I was excited that I booked this tour prior to my holiday and I feel totally let down

Title: Closed on Sundays
Text: We dint know this and ended up just taking a stroll at the tea gardens. You can also buy the tea at the factory.

Title: Small and forceful
Text: The people try to force you to do the tour. The place is small and not as beautiful as other tea locations such as Talawakelle Tea Estate and Edinburgh Tea Estate. I would personally avoid and go to the above.

Title: Beautiful location
Text: Went there by Tuk-tuk, paid 200 rp per person for a guided tour around and a cup of tea afterwards. The tour takes no longer than 20 minutes and gives you the basic information about the tea making process. Smaller place compared to the big tea factorys in the area. I would guess also less tourists. Which we love. After the tour we walked into the plantation and talk to the working ladies. A nice anc cheap experience.

Title: OK
Text: Our guide was friendly and the factory interesting. It did feel like we learnt the rudiments of the process and given we only had a limited time, this worked for us. If you want a more in depth bus-to-cup tour, you'll have to look elsewhere.

Title: Enlightening experience
Text:
I have visited the Pedro factory twice now, once with my partner and a second time with my Mum. It is very reasonably priced at just 200rs for a 20-30 minute guided tour and cup of tea.
Our guide Kalaivane was superb! Friendly, informative and the daughter of a tea picker so able to gave a very personal and honest account of the tea industry. An enlightening experience I would definitely recommend!

Title: Cool Experience!
Text: Visited this factory... they give you a tour inside the factory where you can see how tea is made and you can enjoy different types of tasty teas.

Title: Traditional tea factory
Text: Lovely, quaint, old tea factory. Tour was very informative and views were fantastic. Tea quite expensive.

Title: Great experience
Text: I visited with my friends and family from Norway,Serbia,China, Cambodia and Vietnam. It's very beautiful place with different varieties of tea. They explain about use and benefits of different types of tea.

Title: Interesting - worth a visit
Text:
Good tour with a guide explaining the processes. Interesting to see how old the machinery was and still working. Strangely no photography allowed.
Nice views outside of the reception area but not impressed with shop.

Title: A well-organized tour of a factory in an attractive estate
Text: This was our first of two tours of tea factories. It was inexpensive (about $2US) and well organized with an attractive display area and I would recommend it if you have a mild interest in the tea making process. However, we were hoping for a longer, more in-depth tour but our guide was hard to understand and her lack of English meant that she was unable to answer questions so we left a little disappointed.

Title: Wonderful example of a tea plantation!
Text: We came here in the afternoon of our day trip to Nuwara Eliya after riding the scenic train. Blue Lanka, our tour agency, recommended it so we thought we would give it a try. The factory is wonderful and the guide of the factory spoke great english. It was great to see the tea making in progress and smell the tea in its rawest form. Then, there was the tea tasting. The first couple teas come free while the others cost money to taste. All the teas are great and they bring out an additional rare (we don't know if it actually was) tea for us to try. This tea was 150 USD per kilo....the tea plantation was wide, beautiful and spacious. The tea ladies always beckon you over for photos (and tips). Overall, a wonderful tea plantation and I would recommend coming here.

Title: Interesting tea factory in beautiful surroundings
Text: Stunning nature surrounds this old tea factory, which is still in full activity. The tours around the factory gives you a good insight in the process of tea making, and makes you humble to every glass of tea you drink thereafter. Also, seeing the hard work of the tea picking ladies, makes you wonder why the tea are not more expensive, and you really wish someone would increase their income a bit. If you take a picture with them, be wise enough to give them a few hundred rupees - they will appreciate the added income

Title: Interesting short visit with a cup of tee afterwards
Text: We had a very short, but still interesting tour in the fabric with the basic information about the producing of tee. Afterwards you get a couple of tee (no need to pay extra).

Title: Nice visit
Text: Nice guided visit to understand the process of making tea. After the visit you can walk in the plantations. It would have been nice to have a tea tasting at the end, as the visit is not free.

Title: Beautiful view
Text: Since we arrived together with the westerner groups we, can see the favoritism in entertaining guests by the staff.

Title: Avoid it.
Text: We got to the tea plantation and the ladies at the counter told us that the machines were off, so if we wanted to, we could still pay to enter but no tour was going to be offered because the production had finished. We hung out at the lounge and had a cup of tea but it's a level of poverty tourism that I am not comfortable with. All you can see are the tea plantations and the women that work there. If you read a little bit about it, you'll realize that these women are very underpaid. So you end up sipping a cup of tea looking down on the workers from a viewing deck. Not really my kind of thing to do, so I'll just advice you to avoid it altogether. The tea plantations in themselves are beautiful-ish. They're green trees... there are only so many pictures you can take of green trees.

Title: Learn the history of tea growing
Text:
Good place to visit, you are taken round the factory to see the process. You get to try some tea on the verandah.
Good little shop to buy the different teas.
Staff were lovely

Title: Nice short tour.
Text: The tour is short and I would have wanted a bit more info about the history and cultivating of the tea.

Title: Amazing View, Pictorial
Text:
Non operational in the morning. 
Opening Hours: 8.30 AM
Ticket: LKR 200/- with one cup of tea

If you don't want to visit the factory, you can still visit the tea plantation without any charges. You can tip the workers in the plantation if you like. The hike in the fields in amazing.

Title: Average
Text:
Should only visit this place if you have never been on a tea factory tour before. 

The guide was not very enthusiastic and could not communicate very well in English/answer questions that were not in the part of her script. The factory tour itself was very short and not very informative. Since the factory operates only at night we couldn't see any machine working or the end product from a particular machine. Maybe they should have kept samples from each stage for visitors to understand the various processes better. 

Nonetheless the view from their tasting area balcony was really nice and you were welcome to walk amongst the tree bushes

Title: Just my cup of tea !
Text:
I really enjoyed a brief but informative visit and was happy to see a working factory and the tea making process in action.
