Title: No wonder it is a secret in a beautiful location
Text: Former Plantation bungalow and gardens named after Bevis Bava's father a well known lawyer of Sri Lanka. It is located inland off Dharga town, no wonder it is secret as there are hardly any signs shown on this very narrow village road. All you need to do is ask any of the locals around here as they all know it. Once you get to the main front gates you have to ring a makeshift bell and an attendant will welcome you. Beautiful gardens with an incredible amount of tropical flowers and trees on narrow footpaths with statues dotted around. You need to spend at least half a day here to soak up the atmosphere. The entrance ticket price includes a pot of tea laid outside in the lawns of the bungalow. Inside the bungalow walls are littered with photographs of some Holywood legends and royalty who have visited the place over the years.

Title: DISAPPOINTING
Text: There can be little doubt that, in its prime, this house and garden was once very impressive and well-worth a visit. However, it is now very run down and only a short step from becoming ramshackle and overgrown. Still of interest for those who wish to see something of the former colonial lifestyle, but nothing more.

Title: Only requires Brief Visit
Text:
Gardens were a bit disappointing, didn't take long to look around.

The house itself is very pretty, had loads of questions but the local tour guide only knew how to say "Mr Bawa 2 metres tall!" And that was it. Our tuk tuk driver knew more.

Well over priced at 1000 each.

Title: Fascinating visit.
Text: We took a Tuk Tuk from the Cinnamon Bey Hotel in Beruwala, 1000rps including a stop at the magnificent Buddist temple en route.  Would be very difficult finding this garden without a guide.  Attractive gardens with lovely views but the highlight is the bungalow tour with the resident owner explaining everything.  Well worth the visit just to see all the artwork and artefacts of a recently decadent by-gone age.  Probably a bit boring for youngsters.  Well worth the 1000Rp entrance fee.

Title: Off the beaten trail
Text:
On my last visit to Sri Lanka in October 2015 I had visited the Geoffrey Bawa Garden at Lunuganga (see my separate review) but had no time to visit his brother Bevis's place. So I was able to rectify this on my latest tour

Access is along badly made roads and signage is not great. The garden and house would prove difficult to visit for anyone with mobility problems. The attraction would not be suitable for large groups

Not as expansive as Lunuganga, Brief is more intimate and to my mind contained more colourful and lush  planting with some exotic specimens. Within the grounds some impressive stone and art work. The house is also more interesting with an eclectic collection of works (some homo erotic) giving an impression of the bohemian and privileged lifestyle once enjoyed by its occupants

Although off the usual tourist trail this was well worth a visit

Title: Interesting
Text: Lovely gardens to wander through with sculptures dotted around then guided through the house, ending with a cup of tea! Great views

Title: A lovely surprise
Text: We visited the Brief Garden just a short distance from hubbub of Bentota. It is a little slice of tranquility. Although the garden is smaller than Lunuganga it is still well worth a visit. We arrived there just as it started to rain but umbrellas were quickly provided. At the end of the tour of the garden before we looked around the house we had an excellent cup of tea with the owner who had inherited the house from Bevis Bawa. Take the chance if you can to make the time for this chat as it is full of interesting information about the history of the house and garden and its creator. Do go along if you have the time.

Title: Bevis Bawa's retreat in a gloriously decadent and stylish house and garden
Text: If you are going to Lunagunga (brother Geoffrey Bawa's weekend retreat) I recommend that you visit Brief in the morning, then have lunch at Lunagunga and go round that garden afterwards.  I completely endorse the review by Romeboy which says it all much better than I can.  Watch out for the photo of Larry Olivier and Peter Finch, who stayed when they were filming Elephant Walk (wonderful old poster at the Empire Hotel in Kandy!).  Very tricky to find - take a driver or a tuk-tuk.

Title: A real garden in the tropics, a bit of history too
Text: We went by  tut tut which cost approx 1500 rupees, entrance was 1000 rupees, a very interesting place, lovely gardens with little secret corners, all very tropical , ending with a tour of the house with its paintings and artworks, what a time they must have had !!!

Title: Decadence, Myth, Eros, Art, Still Hang in Colonial House and Grounds - beware of steps
Text:
We recommend taking a tuk-tuk there as the directions to the house are minimal. Also, there are many steps (some of them high) and uneven terrain in the grounds and garden, which could be challenging for the elderly or differently-abled. 

This is were Bevis Bawa retired after his brief career in the army and where he surrounded himself with a bevy of boys, young men, gentlemen and similar masculine companions. While the grounds are nice, we liked the house the most. Beautifully designed, decorated and furnished, it truly reflects Bawa's taste and upbringing. The Picassos, Gauguins and Cocteaus - despite being copies - reminisce of the atmosphere and the erotic fauna that the house enjoyed in the 50s and 60s. Walking in the open-air Roman-style baths in one of the room's private courtyard, we wondered what the darkened and foggy mirror would say if it were ever allowed to tell what it saw!

The current resident, the former head gardener to whom Bawa donated the house (!), is doing a good job preserving the house as it was when Bawa died: simple, elegant, decadent, and yet ready for a pool party and music and boys, should the former ghosts decide to visit one night. A magical place indeed.

Title: a paradise
Text: Found the location in Lonely Planet guide book. We stopped there on our way from Colombo to Galle. Our driver had difficulty to find the place. Finally we arrived and paid the 1000Rs/p fee. Worth the price! The garden and house are very well maintained. Garden and house are so beautiful and quiet, 1-2 hours visit in this enchanted place

Title: Nothing great, simple home garden, Nice colonial bungalow
Text: Difficult to find the place as no directions are  given. Entrance fee is Rs 1000. Garden is not at all great. Plenty of greenery and quite vast. The colonial bungalow is the highlight. Boring for children. It can be seen within an hour.

Title: Breathtaking
Text:
We visited the Brief Gardens on the recommendations of the owner of Diya Sisila last January but didn't get a chance to go last year so made a point of going this year.

Well it was certainly worth the wait, it was such a tranquil peaceful place to be and it just transported us back to the 1930's. We could just imagine what life would have been like living there in that era.  It obviously isn't as it should be as they don't have the money for the upkeep but they are certainly trying to maintain it as best they can with limited funds.

Following the many meandering paths lead you to the house which is awash with beautiful works of art and furniture that is now looked after by a wonderful Sri Lankan gentleman and his family.  He very kindly gave us a history of Bevis and Geoffrey Bawa and the house and gardens that they created followed by a lovely cup of tea.

We absolutely loved this place and will definitely visit again next time we are in Sri Lanka.

I understand that the price advertised on Trip Advisor for the entrance fee is 370 rupees however it is now 1000 rupees (£5) but well worth it.......Fabulous.

Title: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style  garden
Text: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style  garden. Well worth a visit if gardens interest you.The guided tour of the house and information about Bevis Bawa was fascinating and cup of tea very welcome. Apparently the road has recently been improved ,we had no problems visiting by tuk tuk.

Title: Beautiful garden and the best lunch.
Text: The tour around the garden was beautiful if you like to see typical Sri Lankan trees, flowers and buildings. But the most wonderful thing about this visit was the lunch in the garden. We got served twelve different curries, all of them very tasty. We would recommend a trip here, mostly to taste the food.

Title: Worthwhile and captivating
Text: Our driver offered to bring us to this garden. We are eternally grateful for this suggestion. The guide seemed a little "annoyed" with the visitors but after showing genuine interest in the house and the life of the Bawa's, he appeared to be a very funny, thoughtful and knowledgeable guide. Loved it!!!

Title: Short visit
Text: We quite enjoyed our visit here - there isn't a huge amount to see .It cost 1000LKR. A tea room would be a bonus. We were taken there by our Tuk tuk driver from Suranga Tours - who i cant recommend enough. We much preferred Lunuganga gardens.

Title: Emperor's new clothes
Text: We felt this was a waste of time. Not much to see either in the garden or house. 500 rupees would have been better value.  Very unwelcoming. No cafe or drinks, unlike guidebook. Would advise against visiting unless desperate for something to do!

Title: Great place
Text: We enjoyed visiting this beautiful property together with the history of this Aristocrratic Family in the Times of the British colony. A great artist and architect of gardens design. Definitely recommendable. Pity that the foundations of Sri Lanka do not invest to keep it nicer. Renovations works are needed because it is falling a liitle bit apart in the gardens.

Title: off the beaten track
Text: This was a really cool thing to do. The Tuk Tuk ride is fun, it takes you off the beaten track into the jungle. Upon arrival you ring on a big gong bell. A man lets you in on the side gate and allows you to walk around the gardens yourself and when you are ready to enter the house. You can see it was probably once a beautiful garden but don't expect the botanical gardens with gorgeous flowers and lush grass. It is more rustic. Upon entering the house, it reeks up hedonistic decadent parties once upon a time. It is a great house for entertaining. Bevis apparently loved to party. The art and antiques are beautiful. It is worth the trip. Something different - hard to explain.

Title: Amazing gardens, place has a quaint old world queer feel  - hope those boys did well from the estate
Text: Loved strolling around the gardens and through the house. Fascinating to see how it has been maintained and to reflect on that era, good and not so good. Appreciated the gay art.

Title: what an interesting place to visit
Text: did not know much about this place ,but three people in one day recommended,and was very pleased to have gone.look it up first to see if its what you like.

Title: Fascinating garden and house
Text: This was one of the highlights of our time in Sri Lanka.  If you enjoy gardens, art and architecture you should not miss this.  Brief is hidden away inland of busy Bentota and is a tranquil oasis created by Bevis Bawa, brother of well known architect, Geoffrey Bawa.  Previously a rubber plantation, the gardens have been beautifully designed and the house is full of beautiful art works by Bawa and his friends, including Donald Friend from Australia.  You need to ring the bell when you arrive and time your visit so that you can then go to Geoffrey Bawa's country house at Lunuganga which is also well worth a visit.

Title: Tranquil Garden
Text: The Brief Garden is a must to visit.  It is tranquil and yet totally alive with bird song. At the villa we were met by a guide who informed us about the history of the house and garden. The gardens are beautiful however, we would have lingered longer in the garden if there had been a tea room or refreshments to buy then we could have just sat and taken in the full experience.

Title: An absolute gem
Text:
What a hidden gem! One of the most impressive, calm and beautiful places we have visited. We visited as a family with adult children. Walked around the garden - perfect for pictures. We also saw some monkeys! 

Off the beaten path, especially from Kalutara, but we had a driver with us who knew the way. Fascinating scenery and a must stop if you are in Bentota.

Guide was very polite and informative. Only suggestion is to consider opening a gift shop. Lots of potential to sell tasteful postcards of garden views or reproductions from some of the art in the house.

Title: Amazing!
Text: A visit to the Brief Garden and bungalow is a must if you are in the Aluthgama area. Fascinating history, imaginative landscaping, lovely building, I could have moved in immediately!

Title: An amazing and eclectic house and garden
Text:
The gardens and house are really lovely. You're free to explore the large garden then a guide will take you around the house. 
The gardens are filled with sections of tropical plants and features which are truly peaceful. The house sits at the top of a hill with calming views and is filled with personal objects and photos of interest depicting Bevis Bawa's relationships with many famous individuals such as Prince Edward (later Edward VIII) Lawrence Olivier and Agatha Christie. 
The house and garden contain interesting pieces of art as well as phalic statues. Those with with a less open mind or narrow thinking of the world may wish to avoid

Title: Beautiful gardens, really interesting history
Text: We felt this was well worth visiting and the entrance fee of 1000 LKR per person was reasonable. Very peaceful gardens that you can wander through and explore at your own pace. After visiting the gardens a friendly guide showed us the house and explained the history. Having read some other reviews on TripAdvisor I would suggest that if you are homophobic then don't visit - if you aren't, then enjoy the beauty and serenity of the garden and finding out about the interesting history of the house and the Bawa brothers.

Title: Loverly walk
Text: A lovely walk through the grounds around the winding paths was had, followed by a walk around the house which had some querky items like the outdoor bath and statue ( see if you can find it) ideally take mosque spray with you as we got a number of bites whilst in the gardens.

Title: Really nice place
Text: We spent about an hour or so here. It was nice, but the weather was really humid that day and our kids were getting a bit cranky. The gardens are well kept and we would love to live in this house, it's lovely. It's 1000 rupees per adult but overall I thought it was worth it

Title: it is worth a visit - hidden secret
Text:
Already the way to brief garden is a little adventure and makes lot of fun. You pass little village(s), get the feeling driving though jungle.
Brief garden itself is an oasis of silence. It is designed/arranged very well with nice trees, flowers, tiny lakes. The house itself a gem, with artistic paintings, a wonderful view. Interior is arranged very well.

First we were skeptic about the idea going there but it is more than worth.

Title: Peaceful paradise garden and house
Text: I have nothing to add to comments and pictures of earlier visitors.  An adorable place, away from mass tourism. I would stay there forever...

Title: A surprise
Text: The road to this place is really challenging - and it will make you wonder where on earth are you - but once you reach the place; every bump on the way is well worth it. It charges 3000 LKR for entry. The gardens are beautiful. The house tour will take you to days of glory of the european influence - its a must visit. I would love to visit again.

Title: Peace in the jungle
Text: Interesting jungle garden which is very peaceful and not busy. You can walk around the garden and then the house which has works of art created by Bevis Bawa . Saw a large monkey in the trees and also a minitor lizard. Take a picnic and enjoy the experience.

Title: Interesting Story
Text: Take a tuk tuk ride to the Bawa house and garden. Although garden needs some maintenance it's a lovely retreat with pathways through the tropical gardens. Aspects of the house are interesting as is the story of the talented Bawa brothers.

Title: A must-go place but a bit too pricey !
Text:
I love the Bawa family history and went there as a kind of trip to the intimacy of Bewis. In fact, this is what you get... a good insight to yesteryear artistic life. Quite a good collection of artistic objects that remind you of Jean Cocteau.
The garden is less enchanting except for the cascade and the century-old frangipan tree. 
I found the entry price of 1000 LKR too expensive, especially when there is no special fee for children under 18. Maybe, the fact that I am a regular visitor to the island makes me a bit more sensitive to this detail??!!!

Title: A mountain side feeling near to beach area
Text: A wonderful garden built by Captain Bawa and it is well kept until now. Nice old photos remind the old days of Sri Lanka (Ceylon).

Title: Sad to see the Bawa name tarnished
Text:
As a fan of Bawa's work, it was disappointing that our entrance to the property began with a bad start, firstly because the caretaker was not happy with our arrival at 2:30pm. Then sadly a member of our party was falsely accused of potential wrong-doing (I.e walking into an entry and bending to look at a painting whilst we used an outside restroom) -this was made by a female who lived on the property, not the caretaker. The caretaker' excuse for the yelling was thinly veiled by an explanation of previous trouble they had experienced with past visitors. The visit had now kicked off to a bad start and the caretaker did not offer to take us around the gardens and describe the beauty and landscape architecture. We were left to wander aimlessly through the overgrown gardens before having a tour of the house. 
It is clear that the caretaker is very knowledgeable, and he provided curt and limited explanations of the beautiful works inside the home itself.
This was not what we expected especially with our comparison visit to Lunuganga, and some previous internet reviews prior to our visit to Brief Gardens. So you may need to piece together your own reading and research prior to visiting this tranquil acreage. It is clearly a magnificent property with alarmingly priceless artworks out in open display and unprotected from the elements. 
The property is in a hidden location along an unkept road that all but disappears at the gate. This journey itself is an adventure! The road is only just big enough for a 10 seater van. 

So sadly, our 1000 rupee entry fee pp was seen as very expensive for our party of 5, and it is a quandary because the property needs the funds from entry fees to maintain the property. Perhaps some better management and direction is required to preserve such a beautiful history.

Title: Beautiful gardens and gracious house guide
Text: A very enjoyable hour exploring this lovely japanese inspired garden. Touring the house afterwards was interesting and the guide was knowledgable and passionate about the home.

Title: A must for those who love a splendid garden. Bevis was the brother of renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa
Text: The late Bevis Bawa created a botanical garden on his own private plot. And woaw, what a nice and cosy place it is. Now it is the trusted caretaker of the house who still maintains the magic, with its cherished botanical species. I sat with him and my then still very young daughter on the verandah, sipping a cup of tea. And it was an unforgettable experience. the luxury of a simple but tranquil haven. Good to forget the stress from home!

Title: Brief gardens not worth the £10 entry price !
Text: Beautiful setting with great views taken there by driver. Very overgrown and in need of serious maintenance. You could glimps the beauty that was once there when the gardens were maintained but they have been taken over by weed. The house although interesting was very dark which made it impossible to really see the art work. Most of the art work was of naked men in various poses although there was one of Sri  Lanka with prominent sights depicted as one large Mural. I don't think it was worth the hefty entry price.

Title: Nothing to be seen.
Text: We spent some strange time in the garden and were surprised not to see anything interesting. Were surprise d to lots of Homosexual paintings and sculptures. The garden and house are a little bit old fashioned and outdated. If you have a spare 1000 and you saw everything on the island than you are welcome.

Title: Tropical Not a British Stately Home, but that is the charm.
Text:
Our driver recommended this garden & house and we were not disappointed. 

The gardens, started in 1928, have a huge variety of tropical plants and trees. They are presented in formal & non-formal settings and provide a beautiful walk, shaded by these huge natural structures. It's not an immaculately kept stately home in Britain, this is Sri Lanka and not enough gardeners to keep up, but that is part of the charm of this place. 

The house and it's history are fascinating and has been visited by many famous people including Edward VII, Vivienne Lee and the Danish Queen Mother. 

We were treated to a lovely cup of local tea in the garden by the house. 

We were the only visitors at the time and enjoyed the tranquility of this hidden gem.

Title: Lovely peaceful garden and home
Text: Really enjoyed this experience, the artwork, library and sculptures were interesting. The garden was lovely and peaceful. Looking back I wish we had spent more time exploring both the house and gardens.

Title: interesting style
Text: a long ride. expected much..maybe that was the problem. i liked the location and the spread of the land..a large place with a fine vantage view, well utilised to build the bungalow there. the house itself is very spacious. stark and spartan though.

Title: Tranquil
Text: Lots of grounds to cover. Tour not as good as we hoped. The pet dog knew the tour blindfolded so we followed him.

Title: slightly odd place
Text:
well, its interesting - so if you are around do visit, but dont build your day around it

the original owner had special interest hence strange pieces of art, see the picture

Title: Must Do !
Text: Loved Bevis Bawa's gardens and house, full of art history and faded glamour. The hospitality we received was simply wonderful, tea and biscuits chatting to the current owner was a real highlight.

Title: The secret garden
Text: Definitely worth leaving the beach for a couple of hours to visit this hidden gem. Bevis Bawa's garden and house are stunning and incredibly well kept. One could spend hours inspecting the garden alone. The house has been left as it was when he lived there. One can't help wandering about the crazy parties which must have gone on there!

Title: Tea in paradise
Text: This house and garden is lovely, though the prudish might be taken aback by some of the sculptures. We were offered tea - nothing could be more perfect.

Title: An amazing oasis of beauty
Text: Of all the experiences in Sri Lanka this was our number one. Our party of four took 2 tuk tuks to the house of this larger than life Sri Lankan [6ft 7 inches} The house id s full of artwork and treasures and our guide worked for Bevis so new so much. The gardens are beautifully landscaped, Tea on the lawn mad the vist perfect.

Title: Design
Text: Very interesting garden and house, well worth a visit and not crowded.Intereting to compare eith other Bawa buildings such as The Gsllery cafe in Colombo.

Title: Peaceful birdsong
Text: What a beautiful place to visit its a short tuk tuk ride to these lovely gardens and house with a interesting story now left to the staff who cared for the owner until his death you can then visit a nearby temple and see the everyday life of Sri Lanka people en-route

Title: Tucked away gem
Text: Down some very narrow rough roads (with no signs pointing the way), this is a great way to spend an hour or so away from the beach.  The house and grounds are beautiful  and an inspiration for landscaping back at home.  Dont expect formal gardens or placards identifying plants  but rather just a nice place to explore and fantasize about escaping everyday world and moving to a garden paradise in the middle of no where yourself.

Title: House and garden designed by Geoffrey Bawa for his brother
Text: Geoffrey Bawa was a very important architect in Sri Lanka. This house and garden developed some of his ideas on light space and shape and vistas (and his sense of humour) as well as displaying some of the art he collected or commissioned by a range of artists and sculptors

Title: Not worth the effort
Text: It is located way too much in the interiors . If you are in self drive with gps then I will not suggest going there. After much meandering I found a rickshaw who asked me to follow him to the gardens otherwise I would have got lost . The entry charges are thousand rupees

Title: Beautiful
Text: Unspoilt full of birds. A guided tour around the villa with a very interesting history. Well worth a visit

Title: Lovely Garden , a must see if your close to Beruwela!
Text:
We really enjoyed the Bevis Bawa Garden, it is stunning and beautiful, we were amazed by ist varaiety of plants and stautes/figures. 

A must see see if you like nature.

Title: Nice garden and house
Text:
Beautiful garden and house with unusual plants, especially black flower is wonderful.
For a relatively short period of time and small fee we saw a delightful garden and house created by Sri Lankan landscape architect Bevis Bawa.
Enjoyment and relaxation in melt of nature and human mind.

Title: Don't miss it!
Text: Very atmospheric and well worth a visit.  The gardens are well cared for and very interesting.  Watch out for the mongoose,......

Title: Lovely house and gardens
Text: Just a short ride in a tuk-tuk from our hotel and well worth it..a couple of hours is enough to take in the beautiful gardens and house. Lots of flowers and birds and a free cuppa at the end of the tour.

Title: Disapointing
Text: Disapointed with the gardens. Not enough information or even a map. House was interesting but the whole thing was not worth the entry fee.

Title: Inspiring
Text: Lovely place to visit and stroll through the garden but most interesting part is the house. Fascinating for people interested in architecture and design.

Title: Absolutely Must Do
Text:
I can't believe when people below have written that they think the gardens and home have not been maintained.

I strongly recommend you organize seeing this estate.  We did Lunuganga too and organized a meal there but didnt organize in enough advance at Brief to dine there but I wish I did.  Email on info@briefgarden.com a few days before to do so.

We took a proper car / driver to this location as the reviews say it is a rural once you get off the main road.  I wouldn't like the idea of rattling around on a tuktuk to get there.  It is LKR 1000 (7$USD) and our tour was unguided but at the end, the man who Brief was left to spoke to us a bit about the history so I think you can get more of a proper guided tour and info if you want.

The gardens and sculptures are fascinating and I would love to live in the home myself - all the interesting furniture, art work, antiques and books.  The Bawa's bohemian sanctuary properties are not to missed if you are near by.

Title: Left dissapointed
Text: Visited here on the strength of reviews but left extremely dissapointed. After arriving by Tuk Tuk over some rough terrain which was nice to be out of the hustle of the main roads it cost 1000 rubes to enter. I thought I was in for seeing spectacular gardens but it was generally over grown and the house was a dissapointment too. I have to say in its defence I am not a tourist who is a lover of historical land marks and a couple who were in English who were there at the same time were raving about it - so not for everyone but some yes.

Title: Not to be missed when in the Bentota area
Text: Beautiful gardens and residence with an interesting history. The Brief Garden is a bit off the beaten track, so arrange round-trip transportation. This site is not to be missed if in the Bentota area.

Title: Interesting history lesson
Text:
An interesting place to visit and hear the history surrounding the house and gardens .
maybe not the best place when it's raining . The road is a bit on the rough side but a bit of fun .

Title: Brief visit to Brief
Text: Brief Gardens are a real treat for anyone that loves a bit of horticulture. Simple masculine layout to the house and gardens alike. I love the fact that the gardens are not manicured to within an inch of there lives and certain areas have a real feel of the wild. Then of course there are the various statues dotted about, that present a real sense of mischief, you will see for yourselves. We had a lovely pot of tea up at the house, but I understand that this is not always available, so we counted ourselves as lucky. A lovely place to wander and soak up the beauty for a couple of hours, maybe longer if you really take time to enjoy it all.

Title: Intriguing
Text: I did not know a lot about Bevis Bawa before visiting this place and probably would have appreciated it more if I had done more research. The gardens give a hint of the magical place they once were. There was a guide in the house who explained all of the features and the stories behind the artwork. Lovely, but out-of-the-way place to visit.

Title: Charming curiosity!
Text: The gardens and house are a fascinating insight to Bevis Bawa's life and Sri Lankan culture in general. Some of it unexpected and a delight. The grounds are immaculately kept and full of flowers and birds, whilst the house is preserved in a 'shabby' charm!

Title: Delightful
Text: This is a treat of a place if you love gardens.  You enter through the bungalow which is a lovely place in itself with its collection of art and wonderful old photographs of Bevis Bawa and some of the famous visitors to the Brief.  The garden has quite a mysterious quality to it as you wander along winding paths surrounded by lush plants and occasionally happen upon a seating area in a clearing, or a pool or statue.  We visited after a rainstorm which had left the garden a vibrant green and a dripping jungle like atmosphere.  The drive there takes you through some beautiful countryside too.  Well worth a visit.  There is an entrance fee which at the time of writing works about to about £5.

Title: A beautiful secret garden.
Text: A beautiful and historic garden with an aristocratic story attached to it . An extraordinary secret garden in an unexpected location . well worth a look .

Title: See how the other half lived.
Text: Pleasant,verdant garden. Enjoyed a one hour ramble amongst unexpected water features and overgrown paths;even saw two mongooses at close quarters big colonial house with a bit of history.

Title: Worth the drive.
Text: A green and ordered oasis behind an impressive hedge.  The walk leads one through the tropical gardens with some interesting plantings of tropical vegetation interspersed with landscaping reminiscent of an Italian garden. The house itself is also of interest and had an unexpected treasure trove of art on the walls.  Worth the drive to get there.

Title: Tranquil setting
Text: We took a TukTuk for a day visiting these gardens as part of our excursion. What a beautiful and tranquil place. We were able to wander around at leisure and when visiting inside the house a guide gave us an interesting insight into the history of the owner and his family. I would strongly recommend this place for gardeners and non gardeners alike. Not too expensive either.

Title: Architectural place
Text: Architectural place, nice to visit for relaxation and studying architecture. you will see some endemic plants too.

Title: Lovely garden with nice collection of statues
Text: A nice garden to stroll around in. The grounds are rather big and there is lots to see. The visit ends with a tour of the house and the art collection of Bevis Bawa. Nice and gives some insight in his life. Loved all the stautues and little ponds and features.

Title: Fantastic
Text: This was a highlight, what a magnificent short day trip. What was created here is just fantastic, and what a great time it must have been to live in Sri Lanka.

Title: Beautiful gardens and house.
Text: Make the time to come and see this beautiful garden. Easy to get to and in some ways much more beautiful than Lunaganga. A real treat.

Title: Still as gorgeous as ever.
Text: This really is a wonderful garden and house now owned and run by the previous gardener and his family, who used to tend to the gardens for Mr bevis and his partner. It looks simply sumptuous in the rain and still has that wonderful charm and magic about it. Well done Dan and the de Silva family for continuing to uphold Bevis's legacy.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Beautiful grounds to wander through followed by a tour of the house with an informative guide, but wear mosquito repellant otherwise you'll have loads of itchy bites!

Title: Interesting garden with unrealized potential
Text: The biggest problem with Brief Garden is the lack of directions both to get to the gardens and once their around the garden itself. Constructed in 1929 and opened to the public 40 years later, not a lot has been done to assist the visitor. Even the toilet located in the garden is a health hazard, certainly not there to be used!

Title: Peace from a bygone era
Text: Personal tour of the gardens and beautiful house. Entry 1000 rupees which goes towards upkeep. Take a picnic.

Title: Horrible access with absolutely no signs to guide you
Text: It was a nightmare to get to the garden. There are no signs and the road is almost non-existent. After a long search we reached the place to find it desolate. We returned utterly disappointed.

User_Location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
Title: Afternoon tea in a quaint setting
Text: We spent a lovely afternoon here wandering round the neat lawns. An English garden with spectacular exotic flowers. The house is beautiful and the lovely gentleman who showed us round and made our tea brought the house to life with stories of the past. Magical

Title: neglected
Text: hard to find. no signs of indication. charging visitors but unable to see any maintenance. very neglected. Was greeted by a very rude, unfriendly man. visitors are locked in the garden once entered. to get out must ring a bell and wait for him to open gate.Not worth seeing. Waste of money.

Title: Need of maintenance
Text: This garden is in serious need of maintenance. This is a smaller property compared to its bigger cousin Lunaganga, but there are weeds everywhere, the trails are unmarked and the paths slippery with mosses. The guide seemed uninterested and rude. Like Lunaganga, this place has potential to be major tourists attraction, but in serious need of care. Unlike Lungaganga, this is in private hands. The Government should take over this to promote tourism.

Title: A controlled jungle garden
Text: Bevis Bawa may not have had the fame and talent of his brother Geoffrey, but his garden at The Brief is a wonderful exercise of trying to keep the jungle under some control, while letting it be part of it at the same time. Mass plantings of one plant on various locations creates a calmness next to the riot of growth nearby. Good fun to see, lots of work for the maintenance workers!

Title: perfect clearing in the jungle.
Text: Hidden away inland it is not the easiest of places to find. But it is worth it, not a huge garden but lovely views and interesting house. Peaceful. Bevis bawa was an interesting chap.

Title: Artistic treasure
Text:
Brief House is approximately 10 kilometres inland with no public transport so got a tuk tuk  ride. The journey after turning off the main road was great, passing through small villages in the countryside as I ventured further inland. Not well signposted but the locals happy to give directions. The entrance is like coming through a secret door into a tropical paradise. The gardens are extensive with large stands of trees and tropical vegetation in a wild layout with artistic follies scattered throughout. Brevis Bawa's house appears to be as he left it, full of amazing artwork with murals on the walls and a splendid one by Donald Friend a renowned Australian artist who came for a week and stayed 5 years. Don' t miss the collection of photos giving an insight into the lifestyle
of Bawa and his famous visitors. It was a privilege to chat with the current owner, who was a long term manager for Bawa. He shared so much fascinating information about artwork, history and gardens that enriched my visit. Can only imagine the grand parties!

Title: Designers and architects home
Text: Lovely large  tranquil gardens but the house is very interesting. it belonged to the architect and designer Bevis Bawa, a homosexual who was the darling of the Hollywood crowd in the 50's. Beautifully deigned spacious rooms, he died without children and left the house and over 24 acres to his staff,The Butler, who now owns the house will show you around.

Title: Well worth making a trip
Text: We took a tuk tuk from our guest house in Bentota - approx. 25 mins drive each way - paid rps 1200.  The drive was interesting in itself, but then the gardens and house was amazing.  We were left to wander alone around the gardens then given a guided tour of the house and its' history. Bevis Bawa had the most incredible life and this is portrayed in his former home.  Make sure you see the outdoor shower and the moon gate too.

Title: Steeped in History
Text: The present owner explained how the house and gardens came about, they form a quiet and tranquil setting. Was used as a emergency shelter for 200 tourist in 2004 after the Tsunami. Owner refused a large compensation sum from the tourist industry but donated it to the town to pay for scholarship for local students.

Title: Tranquility guaranteed
Text: Beautiful gardens with many lovely flowers and plants. We even got to see a group of monkeys high in the trees feeding on fruits. It is well worth a visit if you like gardens and tranquil surroundings.

Title: What a delightful place
Text:
Worth the trip to see this amazing estate and house. The gardens and paths are charming and the house a perfect setting in the climate. Entry is 1000 Sri Lankan Rupees per person and worth it. 

We took a Tuk-Tuk there and that is the best way to get around.

Title: Beautiful garden but not enough details for visitors
Text: It's a beautifully laid out garden, though the entrance fee is steep (SLR 1000 per person). And for the price one doesn't even get a guide to walk along and point out the sights or even give some history of the garden. Visitors are left to figure things out for themselves.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: Beautiful and interesting place,filled with amazing works of art of the Bawa and his friends. The house itself is an architectural pearl. The gardens are inspiring.  we all loved the place. Worth a visit if you stay in Bentota or Beruwela area. A half an hour with a three wheeler which in itself is a lovely experience. Only downside is the high entrance fee, in sri-lankan terms of course. 100 rup. Per person.

Title: A must!
Text: The garden and the house are very nice and the guide gives you a great introduction to the life of Bevis Bawa and the estate. He was perfectly speaking english and german and made the tour very interesting. We love the estate!

Title: Did not want to leave Brief Garden!
Text: The beautiful expanse of greenery... Garden is manicured yet so wild in places to keep the natural charm alive.. We fell in love with this romantic garden and the family who welcomed us there. A must visit for all nature gazing lovers.

Title: Garden of delights
Text: We really enjoyed our two hour visit, especially as we shared tea with the charming owner. He could not have been more patient and informative about the house, garden and the Bawa family. The garden in a carefully choreographed "jungle" with some beautiful (and sometimes quirky) architectural features and ornaments. The collection of photographs and paintings in the house - which is light and spacious - helped turn the clock back to its heyday. A really memorable trip, just 1000 rupees waiting tuk tuk from the coast.

Title: Well worthwhile.  Fantastic for birds.
Text:
I found the house and garden moderately interesting, but the real "wow" was the range of birds that could be seen (and photographed).  This is a "must" for bird enthusiasts: allow a half day and bring your binoculars and long lens!

One of the best locations for birds that I visited during my entire tour.

Title: first visit to brief garden
Text:
I had read about these gardens and had a half day to spare so went along.
The garden is beautiful. The flowers and exotic plants were fascinating. I heard a variety of birds and enjoyed searching for sight of them.
I must say however. The house gave me the creeps and I couldn't applaud the statues and paintings. I would not have wanted my son to go there as a child or young man shall we say.
Definitely worth a visit though.

Title: hmm
Text: might be an interesting walk around the gardens if you have company and fancy a change of scene .. interesting take on colonisation and creating a space where you can live as you please .. surreally, there is a Picasso in the somewhat indiscriminate art collection

Title: Such a Green & Peaceful Place
Text:
An unexpected garden. Full of quirky ideas. So lush and green. The wife of the owner is a lovely lady and knows so much about the history of the house and the family that formerly owned it. The photos on the walls show many film stars from bygone times. 

Sit and look at the view from the terrace. It is hard to leave it. In the garden are colourful birds and monkeys. At every twist and turn in the garden there is something new to look at.

Don't miss this garden!

Title: shangrila
Text: this was the best thing we did on our visit, the house and gardens are such a pleasant surprise and very interesting too, not very big so you can do it all in an hour but you wouldnt want to eave the cool and beautiful house once youre there

Title: Walk through Brief Garden
Text: Was a lovely experience. Every turn, every bend in the path was interesting - so many many plants. Very beautifully laid out garden. You can spend ages in this place without getting tired - if you are a nature lover. Sitting down to have some tea and biscuits in the Bawa home was also a treat. If they do up this house and let out the rooms, then this is a must stay place.

Title: Brief Gardens
Text: What a fantastic look into the past. The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. Though the house was modest, one can only imagine  heady lifestyle enjoyed by the Bawa clan. Well worth a visit

Title: Divine Decadence
Text:
If you are open minded, like something truly out of the ordinary and off the beaten tourist track, then this is definitely for you. Take a tuk tuk for a magic ride into the past and visit the Brief Garden to discover how it was to live a decidedly debauched lifestyle in the colonial days leading up to Ceylon's independance.
In the middle of a forest you come upon stunning landscaped gardens supporting a myriad of trees,plants,flowers and wildlife to soak in. You then arrive at the sparse but beautiful house, full of impressive paintings and photographs of a bygone age. To cap it all there is some pretty dubious but nevertheless eye catching sculptures to be studied!  
The 1000 rupee entrance fee is quite high for Sri lanka but certainly, from our point of view, worth every rupee.
Before going it is worth looking up the history of Bevis & Geoffrey Bawa to give you some idea of what there is in store for you. A wonderful experience.

Title: Interesitng but strange
Text: Small gardens with weird history and plenty of artwork. Staff were lovely. p.s WEAR LOTS OF BITE CREAM

Title: Umm....
Text: Beautiful gardens but research the owner and his past first!? The atmosphere and artwork in the house were strange.

Title: Likely not worth your trouble
Text: Make no mistake, Brief Garden is off the beaten path.  You will want to investigate whether it is worth the trouble to get there.  Garden aficionados might want to visit, but don't take a rickshaw.  Too, the pedophilia element surrounding Bevis Bawa adds another dimension to the question of visiting.  The Rs 1000 admission fee is a bit over priced.

Title: Hidden treasure
Text: Wasn't expecting such magical gardens hidden away.  Well worth visiting to take in the gardens and architecture, even if you're not a buff.

Title: Brief Garden
Text: Interesting way to spend a couple of hours wandering around the lovely grounds and viewing the house.

Title: Lovely
Text:
Excellent and lovely garden, great welcome from Dooland and his wife. Well manicured garden in a peaceful location!
Must see if you are around Beruwala area.

Title: Worth a visit for lovers of good and timeless design.
Text: Bevis Bawa had a great eye for design as did his boyfriend Donald. The garden and house make an interesting tour with lots of take home ideas. Yes the man was gay and young Sri Lankan males were involved but to downgrade this place because of the sexual orientation of the owner somewhat misses the point. The whole area reflects his sensitivity, sensuality and imagination and unlike his brother's property, Lunaganga, you can see inside the house as well. You may not admire the man but you must admire his talent.

Title: Nice garden, shameful history
Text:
OK, so the house and gardens are presentable.  The moon gate is interesting, but that's where it stops.

Make no mistake, this place reeks of paedophilia.  Everything about it, from the "special" places and hidey-holes in the gardens where young boys where taken, to the phallic statues and sad photographic portraits of young boys.

Bawa, Donald Friend and their cronies should be remembered for what they were.

Title: A must for Bawa fans
Text: Wonderful garden and house is full of interesting art work. Fascinating contrast to Lunagunga. A must for Bawa fans.

Title: pretty garden and very comfortable experience
Pretty gardens, but a very uncomfortable experience overall
Text: The garden was beautiful and we had a very pleasant stroll through the jungle like growth. The tour of the house spoiled the experience for us, however, as the hallway exiting the house showcased paintings and photographs that implied that Bawa's boy servants were victims of pedophilia. These acts should never be condoned, let alone celebrated, and we remain shocked that this hasn't come up in previous reviews or guidebook write-ups about the place. While the gardens were quite pretty, we struggle to recommend visiting Brief Gardens for these reasons and the chilling atmosphere that burdens many areas of the property.

Title: Below our expectations
Text:
We chose this place based on Tripadvisor number 1 rating, when we arrived we had to ask to know our way there.
entrance fee is 1000 LRS
the attraction is composed of Bevis Bawa's ( a Srilankan Artist) garden which he desined himself and his home, he died in 1993 hi house has some of his paintings and a lot of other artists contributions
if you are an artist then this is a place for you.
if you aren't into art then I think you will get a bit bored like we did.

Title: Shows what great planning can do with little
Text: This was a very relaxing spot. It shows you dont need fancy flowers or exotic ornaments. The placement of trees and the care taken with the garden planning shows what a talented person Bevis was

Title: A Garden for Connoisseurs - a Work of Art
Text: Brief Gardens is a masterpiece of landscaping. I could have spent all day here, observing the play of light and shadow in the changing daylight. It is also a wonderful opportunity for photography. A single visit will hardly do it justice. This was my second visit and I shall certainly return in another season.

Title: A brief visit!
Text: We were taken by tuk tuk from our hotel by a driver who obviously knew his way, but I could easily see why it might be difficult to find - as other reviewers have stated. Having read previous reviews, I doused myself in deet before arriving! However, within minutes of getting there, I had been bitten numerous times. I reapplied copious amounts of repellent whilst there, which appeared to stop further bites. I liked the serenity of the garden, but felt I was hurrying through, to ensure I didn't get bitten again. There wasn't much in bloom, but I managed a few interesting photos. The house was spartan, but had a rather nice, colonial feel about it. Normally, apparently, there is a gentle breeze wafting through, but on the day we were there it was stifling. I enjoyed the photo collection and in particular, the lovely, natural photo of Vivien Leigh and Laurence Olivier. The history of some of the artefacts in the house was explained, however, nothing was mentioned of the garden. We were not offered any refreshments and if I'm honest, I wasn't disappointed to leave.

Title: Interesting garden
Text: Very cool and almost like an English garden - we particularly liked the cascade run of water down the lawn from the top by the house. Tea and lemon puff biscuits were provided after the tour of the garden - a nice touch. Interesting to hear the history of the house and gardens and see the old photos of past visitors.

Title: Brief Garden
Text:
Interesting but slightly disappointing...
We expected it to be more colourful from what we'd read about it.

Title: A place full of atmosphere
Text:
This was a great visit! Our driver took us there early in the day. It is not very easy to find, it is a hidden gem in the middle of lash trees and plantations. The tour guide is great! We got to know that the place is full of charm and stories to share. The paintings on the wall are really touching. The one of Bevis Bawa in his very late days with the boy with his arm around him is breath-taking, and leaves you with so much to think about. So much charm and so many stories in the house. The building itself is not a palace, but the garden is something to tell about.  
We set in the garden at the end of the tour, and enjoyed a cup of tea, and let the whole place sink in with us. It is an experience not to be missed! A very moving experience...

Title: Normal Garden.
Text: The worst part is they charge Rs 1000 from foreigners as entry fees, wheras local Sri Lankan has to pay Rs 50 only.

Title: Artistic history
Text: It's wonderful to see the work of Sri Lankan artists in situ...to see where they lived and retreated, their artistic legacy and the lovely gardens. If you are interested in the artists of the mid 20th century, including Donald Friend, this is a delightful place. But a warning...the road is windy and bumpy and long. Phone to see if it is open before you arrive.

Title: Quaint slightly eccentric place but worth a visit
Text:
Water moniter lizards and range of plants/trees/nice landscape.
A nice place to spend a couple of hours.

Title: Bawa's best creation
Text: we were so luck to have quick visit before we catch our light to London. it was amazing design of the garden. i really like the view.

Title: Excellent
Text: I loved every bit of this garden and house. It was pouring hard with rain which simply added to the atmosphere. Lovely Family who now oversee the running of this special idyll. We were the only visitore when we went- would willingly go again- and again,.

Title: Brief Garden
Text: Amazing garden and house in the middle of the jungle with wonderful views lovely sculptures and lots of interesting little nooks and crannies to explore , great place to spend a morning.Interesting library and [hotographs in the house

Title: Persistence rewarded, multifold
Text: Finding Brief is not easy, as testified by other reviewers, but every uncertain turn on the ever narrowing roads is rewarded from the moment you walk through the arched gate. The 1000 rupee entrance fee (which helps to maintain the gardens to the traditional standard established under Bevis Bawa) is a tourist bargain. We were free to roam at our leisure and spent nearly 3 hours exploring the gardens and house. The tea spontaneously provided was an unexpected and lovely bonus, as was the tour of the house and historic features. As Australians, we were especially interested in the sculptures and art work of  Donald Friend who lived at Brief for several years. His mural of Sri Lankan life, painted on the wall of the main room, was fascinating. The wonderful hospitality of the current owners, the de Silva family, who have enjoyed a long connection to Brief dating back to the Bawa era, the extraordinary beauty and layoutvof the gardens and the tranquility of the setting made Brief the most memorable experience of our Sri Lankan trip. Better signposting and promotion would encourage more visitors I am sure.

Title: BRIEF rather too brief
Text:
As an antidote to the hedonistic beaches of southern Sri Lanka, we decided to go inland and explore the attractions that lay within. A visit to the Brief Garden associated with Bevis Bawa (1909-1992) older brother of the more famous Geoffrey Bawa, the renowned architecht,seemed to be just what the doctor ordered. The road trip to the location once one left the main Galle Road at Bentota and traversing narrow rural roads and ups and downs was itself a challenge as there was virtually no signposting. When we finally reached it, the imposing entrance to Brief ( named after the association with lawyers holding briefs)with its ivy covered walls and cement sculptures standing guard over the iron gate was startling.Another shock was the steep entrance fees - Rs 1000SLK per head - which was collected at the door after which we were sheperded into the gardens to find our way about while an earlier Sunday meeting of a local association concluded its tea party.
The gardens are the real star of the show, and despite the size having been reduced to just five acres, one could visualise the arboreal grandeur that must have existed in its full majesty.
A botanist-guide who knew the trees and the manner in which they came to be would have been appreciated. We finally were admitted to the main house - just about a hour to closing time - and got a rather canned conducted tour where the guide repeated himself several times. 
The architecture and the imprint of Barbara Sansoni and Donald Friend,the Australian artist during his five-year stay there in the 1950s are absorbing to explore,The sculptures , paintings, courtyards, open air showers and fountains all made their own quiet statements.
One could have lingered more but closing hour beckoned  and a cuppatea - which sadly never came - would have befitted the admission ticket and the host.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Being an architect loved visiting the house and the gardens. Well designed.Worth a visiting to see both the residence and the landscape.A unique view of the house of an architect himself.

Title: Unexpected paradise
Text:
One does not expect to see anything like this in a Sri Lankian village. It's stunning from the entrance gate till the last step, a magical mix of tropical nature, Ancient Greece, South Asia, a song to life, beauty, love and loss.. 
And the park's manager deserves special mention for his intelligent tour through the park and museum with respect and devotion to the beautiful place and its great creator.

Title: Brief
Text:
This place "Brief" was undoubtedly good but i wish there were more indicators on the road to find it. We had to struggle to get to place. 

Once we reached with lot of struggle, it was difficult to find the access. One of the care takers took us around. I wish this part was also better organised since the took LKR 1000 per person including the child.

Since I am an architect, i would have loved to have more relevant and genuine information about the work than personal information about Bawas.

They can have a more organised /aunthentic audio tour. Its a one time expenditure - audio/head phone tours. That will do justice to the purpose of visiting the place. 

Wish somebody connected to  "Brief" notes the suggestions.

Thanks

Title: Wonderful visit
Text:
The Brief Garden was the house of the writer/artist Bewis Bawa,brother of the architect Geoffrey Bawa,a visit  is a full immersion into a silent,beautiful paradise, lovely trees,flowers,well kept lawns,walled gardens.The house is full of old fashoned,colonial charme,nice drawings,statues by Geoffrey and a beautiful murale by Donald Friend,an Australian artist,nice collection of old photographs as well.The manager is gentle and invites you for tea when you visit the house.
They offer also accomodation which must be a wonderful experience!

Title: A Dream Garden
Text: Brief Garden is beautiful - if you are staying in or near Bentota you should try and make a visit.  Created by Bevis Bawa, the celebrated landscape artist - it is like entering paradise with beautiful lawns, walled gardens and a pond.  There is also an intresting house to visit with an art gallery and photographs of celebrities. Make sure you put on lots of insect repellant otherwise you may get bitten as you walk round the garden.  The staff are very welcoming.

Title: all about good taste
Text:
One of the Bewis brothers has created this house and garden. Both house and garden are an example of a perfect taste, mix of colonial and modern architecture, well kept and deserted. In the garden you walk alone buth the house visit is guided.
Entrance is 1000 Rupees. It's impossible to find the place without a local driver. And i's a pity that they have no merch like postcards, books etc. I'd love to buy something in this style.

Title: jeffrey bawas garden
Text: took a tuk tuk ride here and walked around for two hours in beautiful well kept gardens,really is a solitary place we were the only visitors at that time,wonderful!!!!

Title: Worth a trip
Text: The gardens are not large, but they are interesting.

Title: Fantastic
Text:
All great!!!!!!
Enjoyed very much
The gardens are spectacular & the house is amazing

Title: beautiful gardens and scenery
Text: Had a nice afternoon here. The tuk tuk ride to the gardens is beautiful in itself. The gardens are obviously well cared for and really relaxing. Little guided tour at the end, of the house. There seemed to be a little cafe for tea outside but i didnt bother with this. All in all a nice place to pass an hour or two.

Title: If you stay at Lunuganga you will be interested in seeing GHeoffrey Bawa's older brother's garden  a taxi ride away.
Text: It is another of the great gardens of Sri Lanka.

Title: A little more greenery outside of the resort
Text: I decided to take a little excursion on my own, and the Brief Gardens was recommended by the hotel. So off I went with a personal driver. Once at the Gardens you will get a personal escort to take you around. I didn't know much about the garden itself ... apparently it was designed by a famous Sri Lankan architect. The grounds were extensive and I even managed to see a little wildlife in the form of a monitor lizard! Apparently if you go in the morning opportunities to see birds and other wildlife would be a better bet. I enjoyed the few hours excursion.

Title: Amazing nature all around
Text: It is a trip into the wild, with lovely views in every corner. Worth a visit for the price, and the way from bentota to the brief garden by tuk tuk is simply great!

Title: Fabulous study on living space, abc character.
Text: Visited this preserved house and garden today, recommended by my tour guide. The walk around the garden leading to the house, was amazing. The layout and design of the portion of the house open to the public was most interesting, achieving comfort, many places to rest and enjoy the SriLamkan weather, and muse, yes of windows and busy areas to cool and filll with light. Recommended, historic, nice old photos.

Title: What a wonderful tropical garden!
Text: Lush, wonderful tropical garden designed by Bevis Bawa. Unfortunally, he got under marvelous shadow of his older brother Geoffrey  Bawa. Love the artworks, some furniture designs and the weird statues in his garden. It works a long way to go from Negombo. Must see if you are around Bentota and Galle.

Title: Tropical Garden
Text: The road up to Brief gardens is narrow and winding so don't go in a minivan. It was definately a hideaway for old Bevis and his young men, and it's a fab spot. There are lots of secret seating areas and amazing views. Watch out for the leeches, they'll get you if you wear open-toed sandals, but are easy enough to get rid of (google!)

Title: Not the must
Text: First of all it's just place where original person lived. He had got interesting garden and house. Now it seams that not too much is invested to maintaine the garden. At the same time entrance fee is pretty expensive. It's also not so easy to get here. For our children it was boring and to hot to walk through the garden

Title: Relaxing in a beautiful tropical garden
Text: The garden is a lush greenery and as specialty features some fine statues honoring the male genital (one male face in a phalluslike stele, one statue of a boy enjoying to caress his love organ and one stone Phallus with pubes of tiny green plantleaves growing on it, very crative). It is wonderful sensible art, no offense.

Title: Lovely find
Text: Whilst not the main event (apparently that is Lungana) this is a lovely find (although it is very hard to find) and a lovely example of tropical living in a bygone era. I arrived late in the day, had I planned better I'd have seen both and booked the lunch, but Brief (and you learn why it's called that), brief as it was, was a delight.

Title: a lovely estate
Text: although not at the same level of the Luluganga estate this is quite a find, lovely details and momentos from the friends and visitors of the Bawa brothers

Title: Overhyped Place
Text: We went to visit the place on the basis of earlier reviews. The Gardens were nice but the entry cost is prohibitive and definately not worth the effort.

Title: Stunning gardens
Text: Beautiful gardens, great day spent there and a very interesting guide who told us all about the house and about Bevis Bawa (including some... interesting details!)

Title: Hard to find but worth the effort
Text: Having visited his brother's property of Lunuganga we were curious to see Bevis Bawa's home and garden. Once again there is a bell to ring, and an entrance fee of 1000 Rupees to pay. We were left to tour the grounds on our own, which was a bit daunting but  since it is a relatively small area we did not get lost. It is not particularly well kept but still charming and relaxing. We had a guided tour of the house, which we found very interesting and are pleased we made the effort.

Title: Tranquil Gardens
Text: Worth the 3000 Rupee taxi fair from our hotel to visit these gardens in Bentota .The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. The house was modest but brought to life by the man who guided us round.  Bevis Bawa was certainly and interesting man. 1000 Rupee entrance fee.

Title: Interesting gardens and house
Text:
Charming gardens, with a variety of plants, and many interesting birds to watch.
House also worth a visit, with helpful guide.

Title: Unmissable and not just for the planting
Text: We knew nothing about Bevis Bawa, although knew about his brother Geoffrey the architect.  His garden reflects his life and is fantastic - lots of paths leading to secluded areas where you'll find odd and interesting sculptures (some more interesting than others!).  The house is preserved and filled with his possessions.  His story is fascinating and Brief Garden gives a glimpse into his hedonistic and self indulgent life.  The only problem is finding the place and you are best with a tuk tuk as they know where they're going.  Ring the bell and you might even get the current owner to give you the tour.

Title: Beautiful!
Text: It's not easy to find Brief Garden as the signs have disappeared recently so suggest that you take a tuk-tuk. It was the home of the artist Bevis Bawa, the very well connected younger brother of Geoffrey Bawa who was a renowned architect. The extensive gardens are truly wonderful and beautifully kept. It's a real tropical paradise with so much to see - all types of trees, shrubs, flowers, water features, pathways, statues, pots etc - and a real pleasure to amble around. Included in the entrance fee is a guided tour of the house, which is very interesting. It is rumoured locally that Bevis Bawa was a well endowed gentleman and there are a number of images and sculptures possibly based on him, of naked men with large attributes, which may make some visitors blush!

Title: Serenity
Text: This is a beautiful and serene place to visit.  Set amid a coconut plantation, Brief Garden is lush and aesthetically pleasing.  The caretaker is knowledgeable and offers insights into the history of the garden and house.  The gardens are divided into outdoor rooms  revealing Bawa's sense of style and sense of humor.We found the place with difficulty but felt the trek was worth it.

Title: Beautiful Garden
Text: It was clean and always well kept, pool was clear and lovely and the whole thing was private and safe

Title: A hidden Gem in the Jungle
Text:
Brief Gardens are a 'must see' for anybody visiting the Beruwela - Aluthgama - Bentota area. Although somewhat overgrown now, the gardens still show traces of their original grandeur, and the bird life is wonderful. 
The bungalow and it's associated art works are splendid, and give some impression of the colonial lifestyle in Sri Lanka fourty or more years ago.
Overall, don't miss it!

Title: Well worth a look
Text:
The garden is relatively small, but divided into different 'rooms' by screens of shrubbery and trees, as well as by stone steps and a series of different levels. There is a barbecue area, several ponds, a cascade (which was dry during our visit) and shady benches to sit on and chill out. The owner of the house welcomed us personally and gave us tea and biscuits in the courtyard, followed by a tour of the house, with its amazing collection of art (particularly gay art) and comic pieces, as well as its fascinating history. 

It's a quirky, unique attraction and you are either going to love it or hate it. It's also a long way from the main road, and the only practical way to get there is by tuc-tuc or motorbike. I think you'll find it worth the effort though. I suggest you take a picnic and a good book and make a laid back day of it.

Title: A beautiful legacy!
Text: I had a few hours to kill in Bentota, waiting for a train back to Colombo, after a trip around the South coast. A Tuk Tuk driver helped me at the station with my enquiry, and then tried to persuade me to visit the gardens. By this time in my trip I was tired, and to say the least, rather jaded in my dealings with Tuk Tuk drivers. Because of his appearance and manner (very smart and polite) I decided to go. I had three hours to wait for the train and this would be an unexpected adventure. Sugath was a very good driver, and a Karate Master (0776070246) He turned out to be a gem, just like the garden! It is a wonderful, beautiful place! I can't wait to go back. The entrance fee of R1000 is a very reasonable price to pay, to walk in such beauty and tranquility. I loved the house and the stories that were told about Mr. Bawa. What a remarkable man he must have been. There is some stunning artwork in the house, and controversial statues in the garden, which Sugath kept apologising for! Not necessary, but very sweet. :) Go. If you like gardens you will love it!

Title: Nothing special
Text:
We lived not far away from the garden, therefore decided to visit it. 
The garden itself didn't meet our expectations. There were almost no flowers in there, only trees and bushes. It took us 15 min to walk in the garden, it was not much to see. It was interesting to see the house, even though the guide didn't give us a lot of information. Only a few phrases about Bawa and his life. I wouldn't bother to go there if you need to drive far and the entrance fee is expensive as well.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
We had been here a few years ago and thoroughly enjoyed the experience, so, since we were staying in the Bentota area, we used the opportunity for a return visit. It only takes 20 minutes or so by tuk-tuk from Aluthgama. The entrance fee of 1000 rupees might seem steep, but if you are interested in gardens you will consider it money well spent.
You can walk around the grounds at your leisure and there is plenty to see, from interesting trees and plantings to colourful birds and even monkeys. When you are ready, simply walk up to the house where the guide will show you around and explain the history of the place and the background to the various works of art on view. When we went, we had the place to ourselves for most of our time there. It is truly a haven of tranquility, with beautiful views of the surrounding countryside.
The return tuk-tuk ride from Aluthgama (or thereabouts) should not cost you more than 1000 rupees (including the driver's waiting time).

Title: Hidden jem
Text: Amazing discovery seemingly out the back of nowhere.  Donald Friend's life was fascinating and finding this house in Bentota was a really special experience.

Title: beautiful garden with river
Text: this brief garden situated at bentota. very closed to the bentota town .from main road only three kilometers far..in side the garden you can watch very demand and rare flowers.valuable and beautiful scence too.so when you sri lanka you should visit this brief garden very nice journey.

Title: peaceful
Text: Amazing gardens, so peaceful. We had a slow walk around and enjoyed tea in the garden too. Cover yourself in bug spray though- the mosquitoes are everywhere.

Title: Don't miss this magnificent place!
Text: The grounds and home are a true delight. It is not easy to get there independently by walking or bus, so hire a tuktuk driver, who will wait for you while you are inside. Cost should be somewhere around 1,000 LKR for a return trip to Bentota.

Title: Erotic garden
Text:
Beautiful & interesting garden. Around every corner is a surprise. Bevis obviously enjoyed himself. Good that you can wander the gardens at your own pace. We appreciated that we were able to take our driver free of charge on the tour with us. He had never been before & he was not allowed to look at the gardens or buildings at Lunuganga (Geoffrey Bawa's property).
Interesting to see Donald Friend's input in some of the garden design & also his works in the house.

Title: Wort to visit
Text: it was a nice garden we were see in bentota area. They have interesting house inside the garden. One of guy he explained us architecture value of that home. It has created by bawa.

Title: Chilled with a teaspoon of History
Text: If you are feeling a bit cynical about the turtle sanctuaries, check this place out, Bevis Bawa was an interesting chap. There is a rather melancholy gentleman (he cared for the dying Bawa) who might see you after you have wandered around the gardens and offer you a very nice cup of tea and biscuits, who will show you the house and tells some interesting stories..

Title: worth the effort to go
Text:
Wonderful private gardens - you'd struggle to find on your own. Let in by one of the staff you are free to wander at leisure the gardens with all the nature all around - before being given a guided tour of the house along with the history that went with it.
£5.00 Entry and around £4 return from Bentota in a tuk tuk - it was excellent value for money.

Title: worth a trip
Text: beautiful gardens and an interesting tour of the house offering interesting insights into the life of the Bawa brothers.

Title: A paradise garden
Text: Well worth an hour or so to stroll around the stunning gardens. There are wonderful views out across the surrounding area - lush green hills with a huge variety of plants and trees. The house is the centre piece of the gardens and there was a very knowledgable guide who showed us around and pointed out all the different paintings and sculptures. We paid just under 500rs to get here in a Tuk Tuk from Bentota.

Title: Exlent and butiful garden...
Text: Very great place to visit and must to see the bungalow Mr: Bave. Me and my friend are very happy to see it. We were with tuk-tuk was great travel for a day.

Title: Serene
Text: A must visit - the estate of bawis bawa is a sight to see -

Title: a peek into the decadent indulgence of Bevis Bawa
Text: this is a beautiful garden that allows you to explore at your pace and ponder the goings on of a by gone era + the life of the indulgent Bevis Bawa

Title: Brief by name, long on beauty.
Text:
A most lovely garden to wonder through, with small garden rooms, rambling walks and lovely steps through the centre of the garden.
Different to Lunaganga, which is more architectural in design.
The present owner of the garden was a genial and knowledgeable host, and afternoon teas were included.
It was a delight to walk through the home, and we both travelled from Australia to see this garden, and it was well worth it.

Title: If you like gardens then make the effort to see this.
Text: This was a little out of the way but the driver got us there eventually and after wandering around the gardens we had a little tour of the house followed by morning tea.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: I'd never heard of Bawa before this trip, but staying in a property he designed I was interested to see where he used to live. This is well worth a visit to get further into the mind of an extremelly talented artist. He has many properties around Sri Lanka and i could quite happily say i am now a big fan of his style.  Ask for a cup of tea before you leave!

Title: Excellent tour
Text: Very long unmade track to get to the gardens - giving suspension a hard time. Beautiful planting and house design/setting and a very well-informed guide who provided much colour about Bevis' life and interests....

Title: "worth to visit"
Text:
we went to brief garden by tuk tuk from bentota. we could reach that place within 15 minutes.
Garden and home wort to visit. There is many antique goods and fascinating old photographs and some important artworks.

Title: tropic treasure
Text: beautiful, like paradise, amazing collection, bawa must have been a very cool guy.

Title: Quirky Hideaway
Text: An amazing house and garden well away from the main attractions. The approach road was VERY poor - you'll get shaken up quite badly. However, the walk around the gardens (mainly jungle plants rather than flowers) and the tour of the house are great. Entrance fee was 1000 Rupees (about £6)

Title: Great excursion from Bentota
Text: If staying in Bentota for any length of time then this is a very pleasant half day excursion. You enter the grounds and are told to wander around the gardens. These are extensive and rather wild but very interesting with lots of shade and pleasant places to sit and enjoy. When you are ready you are taken for a tour of part of the house. Again very interesting and being served tea on the veranda by the owner is quite entertaining. Several erotic statues around the gardens add interest - most unusual.

Title: A lovely way to spend a morning in Bentota
Text: A 20 minute drive in a three wheeler takes you to the Brief Garden. The drive itself is interesting as it takes you off the beaten track. The Brief Garden and House are fascinating, and we were served a lovely cup of tea at the end of our tour.

Title: A Brief and memorable diversion
Text:
We had already visited Lunuganga, the nearby gardens and home of Geoffrey Bawa, before we came to Brief, the home and gardens of his older brother, Bevis.
Whilst not as famous, nor as vast as Lunuganga, Brief is an interesting place to visit if you wish to get an insight of the lifestyle of the well-heeled Sri Lankan demi-monde.
The home itself is a beautiful old plantation house that Bevis Bawa improved and still contains beautiful antiques, fascinating old photographs and some important artworks - most particularly a wonderful (albeit somewhat time ravaged) mural by the Australian artist Donald Friend, who came to visit Brief for a week and stayed for 5 years. When you see the gardens you can understand why. Brief may not be as grand as Lunuganga, but it is equally as likeable and the staff member who showed us around the house was extremely knowledgable and generous with his time.

Title: you should see there..
Text: It is the best place I saw in Sri Lanka...It is an old house belong to Bewis Bawa..I did not know who he was before I went...His house and especially garden worth to see..

Title: Quirky, wonderful place in Bentota
Text: This garden built by Bevis Bawa in 1926 is simply wonderful. Bevis was the brother of famous architect, Geoffrey Bawa. The garden is fully of secret places, cascading pathways, magnificent plants and the house is in the middle of it all. A short tour of the house and surrounds was so interesting and the guide will serve a lovely cup of tea at the end. Definitely do this. It is a real highlight in any visit to Sri Lanka.

Title: Beautiful garden and a great private talk and tour of the house.
Text: Was't as hard to get to as some reviewers had said nor was the state of the road to bad.  We had a very reliable tuk tuk driver take us out there and wait for us.  The tour over the house at our own pace was also good and very informative.  Also enjoyed looking at all the old family photos on the walls.  The gardens were beautiful and it was very relaxing just wandering around.

Title: fabulous
Text:
you dont need to be an artist to appreciate art. the brief garden is one such place. walk around this fabulously landscapped garden and see for yourself how much nature can actually be captivating.

had a cup of tea which was served by the caretaker. there is an entry fee for this place. dont miss this place and lunaganga when you are in bentota

Title: Very Interesting
Text: Loved the gardens and variety of flowers and plants. The house and history was also very interesting, very informative guide. Quite pricey entrance fee 1,000 rupees.

Title: LOVED IT !
Text: We were the only ones there and it was gorgeous.  Felt like we were trapped in time .  Magical .  We got some delicious tea and sat on a bench outside .  I will always remember that place .

Title: Garden
Text:
The gardens were a  bit neglected but still interesting, the house
told you more about the man , art work was good and we had a nice cup of tea at the overlooking the gardens

Title: Interesting visit
Text: Half hour Tuk Tuk ride from the Taj. Nice gardens with tropical plants and interesting tour of the house which was lead by a guide. We were offered tea and biscuits which we took outside on the patio and it was lovely looking down into a green area. House contained a nice library ornaments paintings etc and lots of history on Bevis and Geoffrey Bawa. Cost about 1000 rupees to enter but worth it, could spend a couple hours here and get some good photos. The tea was the best I have ever tasted in Sri lanka.

Title: Fascinating place and great art surprises
