Text: Warmer welcome than at Geoffrey Bawa's house and gardens. We loved the garden and the guided tour of the house, which had a surprising array of art. Cup of tea in the garden was the finishing touch. Take a tuk tuk for an adventure.

Title: Take the time to see it
Text: It's worth heading down the bumpy road/path to Brief Garden. Just when you think you're being taken the long way by your driver or tuk-tuk the road turns sharply up a hill and the landscape changes just enough so you'll know you're in for a treat. Up the drive you go-- if you're tired of the car, go ahead and get out and walk here-- and soon you'll arrive in a circular drive with two doors. Ring the bell and the caretaker will greet you. I think it was a nominal 30,000 ($3USD) to enter but you'd gladly pay double. This rather large garden feels incredibly intimate. Little living vignettes are strewn together with grand gestures here and there. A unique balance like I've never seen before. Exotic plants grow naturally and abundantly. When you're done filling up your photo memory card walk towards the house to be met by the caretaker who will share tea and a tour of the house and immediate gardens. He has stories to tell if you listen closely. The art and sculpture in and around the house let's you truly invision the lives that were lived there.

Title: Interesting Visit
Text: A lovely afternoon spent enjoying the gardens and drinking tea on the terrace enjoying the views. Not much to see inside the house.

Title: Almost a Secret Garden
Text: The challenge of locating the Brief Garden set the mood nicely.  I had read about it in a gardening magazine and was delighted to be able to wander about the gardens & tour some of the house.  Even though time has taken its toll on the condition of the house & the layout of the gardens, one can see what a lively place this was in its heyday.  I was grateful for my insect-repellant shirt & my sturdy shoes as I peered over, under, around & through it all!

Title: Tropical paridise
Text:
Beautiful gardens to wander through and admire vistas both near and far.  One has to wonder at the time and effort that must have gone into the planning and planting.  The juxtaposition of textures is delightful.

The house itself is of little note but the interiors contain interesting artifacts and artwork

Title: A tropical oasis
Text: A truly delightful vision of paradise distilled with vision by a highly gifted individual. In a secluded, and very remote setting, it really is well worth making the effort to find it.

Title: Hardly Worth the Trouble
Text: It takes quite a bit of time to get here.  What one finds is a nice, if somewhat neglected garden, a pleasant house and tales of the fairly sordid lifestyle of an old paedophile.  I'm just not sure it's worth the time and trouble.

Title: Well worth a side trip from Bentota
Text: A delightful place to spend an afternoon and an interesting comparison to the garden at Lunaganga by Bevis' more famous brother Geoffrey. Brief garden sprinkles camp humour among its elegant vistas and the art contains many homoerotic jokes - there's a real sense of fun about the place. As well as having a good sense of humour, Bevis was a talented gardener and designer and this is truly one of the great gardens of Asia.

Title: Wish it was my home
Text:
At Brief garden you get the kindness and the welcome totally lacking at Lunuganga.

Brief is smaller and less experimental than Lunuganga and was the private home of Bevis Bawa. You enter by a sidedoor and are free to roam the garden with interesting perspectives and ecclectic (some may say tacky) artwork until you arrive at the main house where the charming caretaker (who not only speaks English, but fluent German) will offer you tea and give you all explanations you may need.

Bevis Bawa obviously had a good time at Brief and some of the exposed pieces might amuse or even slightly shock you. Discover yourself!

Worth a visit but difficult to find.

Title: Tranquil house and garden
Text: Brief garden is quite tucked away in the jungle, and it took us a while to find, but it was worth it! The garden is quite compact compared to Lunuganga - we visited both in the same day, and it was interesting to compare the two - I think I preferred the smaller scale of the Brief Garden, it felt more like a home than a country estate. I found the house to be just as interesting as the actual garden, it's filled with antique furniture and artwork from a range of local and international artists. Lovely place to visit and explore if you're in the area or interested in the Bawas!

Title: Beautiful house and Gardens
Text: Loved this place and a must to see if you are staying in any of Geooffrey Bawa's hotels. The staff there was so friendly and they made us the best cup of tea ever

Title: bawa brothers and brief gardens
Text: stayed at Sri-Lancashire guest house and had done my homework on the area and visited Brief Gardens. Small and manageable to walk roound in a few hours. Very well maintained and the guide was very informative with his knowledge, cheap entrance fee though people would find this hard to find if they didnt know the area, would visit again with a better camera as fantastic photo opportunities are there.

Title: A hidden gem"
Text: Lovely visit around the garden then a private tour around the house followed by tea and biscuits on the patio.  A lovely way to spend a couple of hours.  Very interesting and a lovely tuk tuk ride there.

Title: Breathtakingly beautiful
Text: Words and even photographs cannot describe the tranquility and beauty of these gardens. The owner is a genial and welcoming host. I would say that if you are in the area and are in the least bit interested in gardens or just the beauty of nature, then this place is a must to visit.

Title: Overt suggestiveness?
Text:
We visited Brief Garden while staying at Lunuganga. If you can swing it, I would say it is worth seeing both (Lunuganga should be reserved well in advance, phone ahead for Brief). Either one is a welcome reprieve if you've been spending too much time on Bentota's beaches. (I know, not possible for some.)

If you do manage to see both gardens, the comparisons will be inevitable. As you may hear, both Bawa brothers were talented but with differences in their approach. It should be noted that (the older) Bevis' Brief Garden was first and was the precursor to inspire Geoffrey's Lunuganga, if not eventually spurring Geoffrey's entire architectural career. And the two properties are very different to begin with. Brief is inbound within the jungle, while Lunuganga is larger with a lake bordering its opposite ends. 

The experience of Brief is intimate in size, the garden is organized by designated paths with lushly dense tropical foliage. Following these paths, you happen upon sudden openings and clearances that are humanly scaled - almost like garden "rooms". Some of these open spaces might have a water feature, formal stairs, or spaces sized for activities. The feeling of the garden as "rooms" is more clearly evident in the garden spaces behind the house (such as the outdoor shower area) that the tour guide will take you through. 

Lunuganga is more pastoral in comparison. Indeed, Geoffrey kept cows on it (still there) that maintained its legal status as agricultural land. There is a spatial flow to the rolling hills and stepped plateaus that contrast to the jungle walkways of Brief. Lunuganga is often cited as one of the factors that ultimately led Geoffrey to get formal architectural training. This may add to the sense that Lunuganga is the work of someone more concerned with space. As far as I can tell, Bevis designed his garden primarily as an enthusiast.

I am surprised that few if any comments on TA thus far make mention of what appeared to be Bevis' undeniably overt orientation. In one sense, it should not matter. Yet, I think it provides a fascinating angle from which one can reflect on the brothers and their relationships to their gardens and the world. There are records which suggest Geoffrey may have also veered this way, although they are only inferences, as he did not openly project this image as his brother did.

Entering Brief Garden, you feel like you are allowed into Bevis' private world. Homo-eroticism abounds - some blatantly obvious, some quite suggestive, some with a touch of cheeky humour. It reads as a place where he was free to let loose and enjoy life on his own terms without abandon. Viewed in this light, outdoor spaces which are "intimately scaled" take on a further dimension. (Something happening behind those moving bushes?)

Likewise, Lunuganga is an interesting documentation of Geoffrey's world. You could almost chart his career as an architect in parallel to its evolution. While Brief seemed somewhat of an inner sanctum, Lunuganga had an expansiveness to it where one did not necessarily "hide" so-to-speak. (There are plenty of physical hiding "spots" but I'm referring more to the mentality.) For example, the male sculptures on display at Lunuganga are significantly more demure in posture - classical rather than wildly expressive. Was this the influence of English propriety alongside English landscape design? Was he acting in accordance with the etiquette expected of someone of his growing renown? Or was Bevis so forwardly extravagant it makes us pale in our moralities?

Title: Relaxing Gardens
Text: We decided on a late afternoon trip to Brief Gardens, a sort of gentrified English Garden with the tropical touch. To see the exquisite birds you will either need to visit first thing in the morning or late afternoon. There are a myriad of colourful birds - I have no idea what they are and the garden also offers sitings of Squirrel, Chipmunks and we were also lucky enough to see a mongoose whilst having a cup of tea after our tour sitting on the veranda. The drive up from Bentota through the small villages and up through the rice fields and jungle is in itself a small tour of how life in Sri Lanka goes by day by day. If at a loose end it is worth the trip and Rp1000 entrance fee.

Title: Peace and tranquility
Text: Beautifully designed, but not overkemped - I liked the fact the fountains don't work anymore and it all has a weathered feel - working in harmony with nature, not against it.

Title: "Really architect Bungalow"
Text:
I was interested only bungalow because there are real architect design and guide explain everything very well.  Garden was not interested to me because when i visit that place i already visited peradeniya botanical garden and Hakgala garden. 

entrance fees for per person : 1000 LKR

Distance to from bentota : About 8km

Title: Fascinating house & enchanting jungle garden
Text: Created by Bevis Bawa, brother of celebrated architect Geoffrey.  Its an eccentric combination of Italianate landscaped areas and meandering paths through lush semi-jungle. Atmospheric rather than spectacular, and on a relatively intimate scale.  The garden is enchanting and in combination with the house it gives an insight into the life and times of an unusual individual. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring it. However, whilst you can appreciate it for what it is, I felt a few notes on the gardens history and how Bevis set about creating it would have been helpful.  The current owner was padding about and amiably chatting to visitors but after he had generously spent quite a bit of time talking with me about the photos of Bevis and his family I didnt want to monopolise him by quizzing him about the garden. The garden doesnt advertise itself, which is probably just as well. Crowds of visitors would overwhelm it and destroy the atmosphere. There are no directions and it is not easy to find unaided but all the locals know it and can point you in the right direction.

Title: Brief
Text: Lovely garden with some good views , slightly disappointing house , although there were some interesting old photographs

Title: Lovely spot
Text: Although it isn't easy to find, this place is really worth a visit. The gardens are lovely, a sort of English landscape style made of tropical plants with lots of shady corners to explore. The house is also interesting, with pictures of Bevis Bawa and other family members and lots of artwork to admire. I wish I'd known more about the Bawas before I visited, I've done some reading since and they were a fascinating family. I'd highly recommend this place as a change from the usual tourist stuff. The trust who now run it are clearly doing their best to maintain it as it was, and I didn't grudge the 1000 rupee entry cost at all.

Title: tranquil and fascinating history
Text:
loved being given an unexpected cup of tea and lemon biscuits on the terrace!
Not too demanding -  a gentle stroll around the house and grounds with some interesting specimen plants and the erotic sculptures were points of interest!

Title: not worth 1000 rupies
Text: nice park and house, but I think 1000 rupies are to much - locals pay only 300. the house is nice, but not super special

Title: Nice story
Text: The garden is nice and the house is nicer, I wish I was more informed ( so do before you go ) about Bevis and had more time at the house for a cup of tea and o let it all sink in.....

Title: Great Garden!
Text:
We loved our morning visit to Brief Garden. We went by tuk tuk from Bentota, the tuk tuk driver was very familiar with the place, he charged 1,200 SLR return which we felt was very reasonable.
The garden was really interesting, we loved the secret corners, pathways lined with lush plants and landscape garden features including steps, water ponds and curved concrete garden seats. Lots of ideas to take home! 
The house was open the morning we went and the very friendly and knowledgeable caretaker gave us a guided tour, including giving details of the artwork on display. We were then treated to a cup of tea and biscuit outside on the terrace. 
All in all a great visit and we felt well worth the 1,000 rupees each

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Beautiful tranquil gardens.  Wonderfully quiet but for the bird sounds finished off by a tea and biscuit at the house all of which you can do at tour pace.  Few tourists even at high season.  Very much worth the Rps1000

Title: Disappointed
Text: Decayed garden and a couple of rooms in the house open to the public. There are better ways to spend your tourist pounds in Sri Lanka.

Title: Very nice
Text: I spent 2 hours inside the garden and this was a very different experience for me because i was mostly into dry areas in my first 2 weeks and this was very lush and green and wonderful. I can not imagine the effort put into create this masterpiece but surely worth checking out if you are heading this way.

Title: Interesting garden in the jungle
Text: Bevis Bawa was the brother of Geoffrey Bawa famous architect in Sri Lanka.  The house is tucked away in thick vegetation and farms, (rice etc) about half an hour from the main road, maybe more.  It is very interesting with different themes such as Italian garden english lawn and so on.  If you book to go make sure the house is open, Bevis had an interesting collection of art and photos of famous visitors such as Vivien Leigh, Laurence Olivier Peter Finch.

Title: Beautiful English flowers
Text: We went in to kill time prior to going on the train and we were delighted that we did! Relatively small but very nicely laid out with classic English flowers that were in full bloom - sweet peas, sweet william, busy lizzies, holly hocks, dahlias etc it was a true delight and very relaxing

Title: A Pleasant Place to Spend Time with Nature
Text: Enjoy a pleasant place, beauty, brilliance and intelligent nature.  I loved it and sat there for a long time and breathed a lot of fresh air..

Title: Dont See This if you have seen Perediniya Garden Kandy
Text: This is a much smaller garden with the same 2000LKR per foreign adult entry ticket. Paredenia Botanical Garden ,Kandy is 100 times better and worth the entry ticket

Title: Worth a visit if you are into nature and gardening
Text: WE had the advantage of a lovely day at these gardens. I suggest a buggy which is cheap to cover the entire gardens. We stopped by a number of attractions here. There was the cactus and succulents gardens which was worth. It was not rose season as we were told it blooms in April. albeit was worth spending half a day here. thia is also a bird watchers paradise

Title: Well maintained and plenty of shady areas
Text: A nice way to spend an hour or so strolling the park  , indoor and outdoor plants and  cheap to enter !

Title: Good park with a lot of Roses
Text: Must visit for people who Love Roses and Flowers - we had a good day out at the park but it started to rain after we entered - had lunch and then left as it was raining heavily

Title: Never Seen like it 
Text:
HAKGALA Botanic Gardens in Sir Lanka is not like other botanical gardens I visited before. The variety and organization of the garden is something noticeable. Although I  visited during December and its not a preferable seasons. Im very impressed about it and number of plants planted and the size of the garden. If I will suggest something it will be about the signage of direction that can be improved and enhanced. 
Also if you had a chance to visit during April - July will be even better since it is spring and will see the flowers totally different.

Title: Nice to walk around
Text:
It is a very good garden but hilly and you have to be physically fit to spend 2.5 hrs walking around to admire the garden. Alternative you can rent a golf cart with driver for 2 person total 1000 rupees for 1hr. Entrance fee for foreigners is 2500 per person some usd 15. First time to see green roses. 
Recommended

Title: Good botanical garden
Text: Nice and best beautiful garden in nuwaraeliya. 50 rupees for local. Need 2-3 hours. Well maintain. lots of nice places to get photos. Must go if you visit nuwaraeliya.

Title: A bit disappointed
Text: We went to the Botanic gardens on a rainy day. If you walk up a distance to the office you could get a golf cart to take you around. We had to wait quite a while as there were only 3 golf carts. Charges are 1000 or 2000 depending on size of the cart. The gardens do not have lots of flowers. The major part are trees a Fernery,rock garden,arboretum.  There is a small rose garden and glass house with begonias and orchids and cacti.

Title: Foreigners are charged 20 times more than the Locals
Text: Noting to rave about.  Not worth the Rs. 2000 one has to fork out.  In other countries entrance fees for parks/gardens like this are very much lower or even free.

Title: Amazing Rose garden
Text: There were lots of winding paths that led to beautiful gardens. The rose garden was amazing. Roses with colors that I had never seen before.

Title: Big big roses & variety of flowers
Text: It charged foreigner 2k Rupee, it is pricey I must say, do it if you are really free. It is not particularly impressive, I had a leisure walked around and taking pictures of the flowers. There are lots of tall trees around, I am not a fan of plants /trees, so it is just an average garden for me. Perhaps I went to others in other countries that charge lesser or even free.

Title: Relaxing amble
Text: relaxing walk through well maintained gardens. A very pleasant way to see lots of local plants and features.

Title: Close to Nuwara Eliya
Text: Situated at 16km from Nuwara Eliya on Nuwara Eliya - Badulla Road. Well maintained with an attractive rose garden.  Disposable plastic bottles not allowed to be taken inside.   Some pathways are steep and may be difficult for the elderly.  Electric golf cart (4-7 passenger) may be available with driver/guide for hire. Parking only along the main road, entry and exit at two different locations.

Title: Huge. Huge. Huge. Keep strolling! Keep strolling!
Text:
Huge. Huge. Huge. Keep strolling! Keep strolling!

Visited this garden during SL trip with family. The garden truly amazed me in the way it was kept amidst the lap of nature. 

It is surrounded by hills on almost all sides and being located @ 5000+ ft above MSL, provides the right type of cold climate required for the garden to blossom.

You will just be surprised on how many varieties of flowers & trees, our nature can provide us.

The garden houses thousands of varieties of plants, trees, flowers, ferns, cactus etc.

It is spread over, minimum 25 acres of land, I presume.

 The garden charges same entrance fee to all SAARC and non-SAARC visitors. It opens @ 0800hrs and winds up @ 1730hrs.

The nursery - for shopping - shall close by 1500hrs.

You can spent a lot of time in the well laid out sections of the garden like Bulb garden, Rose Garden, Glass House, Fernery, Rock Garden etc.

Date of Experience : March 2019.

Title: Hakgala Garden
Text: Hakgala Botanical Garden is nearer to Nuwara Eliya and it is one of big botanical garden in Sri Lanka. Various types of Plants and trees are there in this garden.It is one of the tourist attraction place in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Fantastic place!
Text: A perfect place for gardens as its so nice to walk in the windy n chilly temperature! Flowers were blooming so beautiful, wind brushing against our hair and faces, trees were green, gardens were nicely sculpted. We love this place!

Title: Great range of flowers and shrubs
Text:
A huge number and range of flowers, trees and shrubs, many of which we are familiar with in UK, but somehow these were bigger and brighter.
Also saw a large troop of monkeys both large and small babies. They come down to eat the foliage and are shooed away by the staff. However, they came very close to us and ran across the paths in front of us.

Title: Past its best
Text: The gardens are quite different to what you will see at Peridiniya due to the cooler climate. It is still very much based around the traditional English style with elements of a cottage garden feel with the flowers on display. For heritage gardens such as these the management of the plant material as it ages is critical to maintaining its integrity. Unfortunately these gardens are really passed their best with the Cyprus trees in varying stages of decline as with the large rhododendron plantings towards the back of the property. The Japanese garden is not a good example and the roses if in bloom when you visit add colour but with no real design. There are some interesting endemic species that can be seen with the history behind gardens establishment of greater interest. Entrance cost for foreign visitors is 1500Rps which is a little in the expensive side for what you really see. As something to do while visiting a few days you might want to consider visiting, otherwise give it a miss.

Title: I love this garden
Text: A super cool garden. I love this garden just because it has many subtropical and tropical plants. Garden is spread across 68 acres with a huge variety of trees, plants and pretty flowers and more.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Large botanic garden established in 19th century, with impressive old trees and many plants from all over the world. Worth a visit when you are around Nuwara Eliya. 
Adult foreigners pay 1500 LKR, foreign kids 750 LKR.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: Good park with lots of photo ops. However, lack of sitting areas, access to water and food makes things bitter for those carrying along kids. Booking of ekarts is not transparent.

Title: Visit to Hakgala Gardens
Text: A walk in the park is the best you could do in this area; it is 68 acres in area and established during the British regime in 1838. We used a Golf Cart to accomplish to cover the area.

Title: Enjoyable stroll
Text: Large site that is being carefully and sympathetically developed.  Lots of beautiful trees, and plenty of flower planting going on.  By April I think it will look very attractive, when the plants have grown and are in flower.  We were very happy to follow the paths and stretch our legs after being in the car for some time.

Title: Brilliant for nature lovers
Text:
As the park is big and we had limited time, we chose to do the tour with the large 6 seater buggy. We were fortunate that our driver had an intricate knowledge of the history , plants and trees.
There is so much to see and nature lovers could spend days exploring this wonderful garden

Title: One of the Nice Nature Attractions
Text:
The First Issue I had Here was, At the Ticket Counter they said me that there is a Shuttle inside to go Around the Garden, But when I went in up the Officers said that the Shuttle's battery is down so for the day there is no More shuttle.. When I complained Saying that At the Ticket Counter they promised me for the Shuttle but when I come there is no shuttle, One of the Officers were very Kind and He gave the Permission to Take my Own Car in to go around the Garden .

That was Really Appreciated, because it was So Raining as well..

  In my Point of view, More than the shuttle or the Car I prefer Walking..

Title: must visit
Text: excellent and huge garden with variety of plants and flowers.nice place for photography and roam around for 3-4 hours.

Title: Beautiful Park
Text: It is a lovely place, especially for botanics. Otherwise nice place to take pictures among beautiful flower

Title: Definitely get a golf buggy
Text: The gardens cover a wide area and it is quite steep if you walk all of it. Unfortunately, this time of the year, the gardens were not seen at their best. We still enjoyed an hour or so being driven around in the golf buggy, which we shared the cost with two strangers. It is pretty cheap. Some lovely views to the mountains make for good photo opportunities.

Title: Variety of green
Text: Great place to spend a day. But we had to wait for more than an hour for the golf car to come around for us.

Title: Nice botanical garden,I love this
Text: I love this garden because it has many subtropical and tropical plants, pretty flowers, centuries-old trees, and more. It's such a great place to be in contact with nature!

Title: It is such a gorgeous landscape with beautiful sceneries
Text: Those gardens are extremely famed for their beautiful plants and flowers, especially the roses and orchids. In fact, I can totally understand why so many people enjoy it. It is such a gorgeous landscape with beautiful sceneries! I definitely recommend it to anyone.

Title: Nothing special.. but a good botanical garden
Text: May be this garden is sold telling as Ashok Vatika or some other important place where events occurred during Ramayana. It is a simple garden and nothing else. Charges are very high for foreigners.. so can be avoided.

Title: Nice botanical garden
Text:
Worth a visit if in Nuwara Eliya area. Parking was a bit difficult. 

Tickets need to be purchased for entry. 

Some areas are in regeneration phase, the tropical garden section was excellent - even saw ~3m snake, not sure if it was  venomous or not.

Title: Overpriced for tourists
Text:
Is this botanical garden nice? Yes, it is. Is it amazing? No, definitely not. You park along the road (can be long walk if you're unlucky) and then at the gate you're welcomed by hefty 1500 LKR "tourist price" where "local" price is 20 times lower... Is it worth the price? NO! 
Nice collection of flowers, but being very honest, some hotel gardens on our trip were as nice (or maybe even better) thank this botanic garden. Hill walk, so not for those with walking problems.

Title: Amazing
Text: This is a must see. Golf carts are available & must be used because the driver is also a good guide who can educate you about the flora & fauna. Neatly labled garden with local, international species surviving. Supposed to be associated with great Indian epic Ramayana.

Title: Nature
Text: This botonical garden is not as great as one in Colombo however good for relaxing and evening walk..

Title: Not worth it
Text: The botanical garden is rather a bigger garden however not too many attractions. Not worth the time nor the money.

Title: Beautifully maintained gardens
Text: These beautifully maintained gardens are only a short drive from Nuwara Eliya. They feature any extensive array of flora from all over the globe. Lawns and flower beds are all well cared for. Towards the back of the park, near the Japanese Gardens a group os resident monkeys provide some entertainment for visitors. Easy walking trails packed with beautiful scenery. A great place to relax and enjoy a well maintained garden.

Title: Great experience
Text: Had great morning visiting gardens, well laid out and organised and exceptional variety on show !TIP.   Although we walked round there were golf buggy tours available at a reasonable cost that we would have used if we had known about them.

Title: Informative and enjoyable tour
Text: Long walking was not convenient for my family so we chose to visit this garden for their golf cart service/ tour. For an additional 1,000 Rs. (we were a group of 6 persons) we had an actual botanist (Dr. Herath?) drive and guide us around, sharing and explaining about the different plants, native and non-native to Sri Lanka/ Asia. Ask and he'll give you both scientific and common names of any plant you point to. He also demonstrated how parts of certain plants could be used for health and/ or beauty purpose. There is a little nursery where you can buy plants and seeds at a reasonable price. A small and very well-maintained botanical garden. We went during planting season yet still left impressed. Blooming/ flowering season from April to December would be perfect timing.

Title: Very pleasant location
Text:
My wife and I spent the morning here during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka ????. Our visit coincided with a major planting exercise for the forthcoming holiday season, so we didnt see the gardens at their finest, this didnt bother us as our main for visiting was the 'Bird' the Gardens. What we did see of them was impressive, theyre very well laid out and beautifully maintained. 
We managed to see several of the more common local species including Dull-blue Flycatcher and Purple-faced Leaf Monkey (Langur) and the rare Chestnut-backed Owlet. A Black Eagle flew over the escarpment as we arrived. A very enjoyable visit and well maintained paths. Highly Recommended.

Title: Few blooms in February
Text: A nice peaceful botanical garden with lots is cedar trees and tree ferns, but something of an anti-climax after having visited the Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya. It maybe that February is not a good month to visit because there was little colour to be seen even though there were many plants that must flower at other times of the year (there were, for example, a number of well set-out rose gardens but not a rose flower in sight).

Title: Nicely maintained garden
Text: We enjoyed the trip of botanical garden but unfortunately flowers were not there because of season . In different locations we found chairs for sitting so that one can relax in between

Title: Seen Better!!
Text: Maybe it was the time of year but, we were not impressed. From looking at the other reviews we expected more. The price did not help either!! Seems like being a tourist in Sri Lanka sometimes feels like your being taken advantage of. I paid 1500 rupees, my Sri Lankan wife paid 60.. Oh well

Title: Must see place in nuwaraeliya
Text:
If you go nuwaraeliya,this is must see place. No need to take a taxi. Every minute there is a bus to go and and back. Within 15 minutes you can reach to the park entrance. A ticket for a foriegner is 1500LKR, but its really worth. Full tour inside the park is around 2-3 hours.

If you go march-July there are a lots of flowers can see. Thise are amazing. Otherthan flowers there are more than 5000 trees, plants and insects can be seen. 

Garden is cold throughout the year. If you wany you can hire a cart to go around the garden but my recommendation is do walk.

Title: Fabulous Gardens
Text: If you like your gardens then this is a must, entry fee is 1500 rupees and will take around 2 to 3 hours to walk the grounds, there are golf buggy type carts you can hire to take you round, 500 rupees for a couple, monkeys are all over and funny to watch, only thing lacking is a real cafe, there is a cafe but very limited food available. We visited in January and this is planting time so limited flowers to see but the grounds are incredible to walk

Title: Nice garden
Text: We went to see the garden in eaely februari. That is the time for planting. There were few flowers. But we can see that in March/April  there will be lots of flowers. The Arboretum is very impressive with many species and well marked. Entry fee us 1500 rupies which is on the high side. Easy to reach by bus. Certainly back towards Nuwara Eliya there is a bus every  minutes.

Title: Ashok Vatika
Text: Visited here on Jan 23rd,2019. As per folklore, the Sri Lankan demon King Ravana after abducting Sita, kept her hidden in this area and this area was offered to Sita as a pleasure garden, the place finds mention in the Ramayana as Ashok Vatika. This place is of special cultural significance to Indians!

Title: Nice way to spend a few serene hours!
Text: Get the public bus from the station and for 40 rupees you will arrive! The gardens are well kept and its nice to see house plants in the UK growing outside! Its definitely worth the visit..

Title: Park
Text: This is a very good park. A good place to spend time with your friends and family. You can just walk about and enjoy.

Title: Poor condition
Text: You have to pay to enter this park. Its poorly maintained and needs a lot of work. Dont bother going. The hotel gardens are much nicer and dont cost anything.

Title: Botanical Garden
Text: Being a flower enthusiast, I was quite disappointed with the place as the only flower in season were roses and they only sold three types of seeds at the time of our visit. The entrance fee was also quite expensive for foreigners when compared to the entrance fee of other attractions in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Beautiful and well-maintained
Text:
Though it offers golf-carts for elders, the entrance is too steep for most elders to climb and the slope is too steep to walk till the cart is available. One has to wait in the office room to get a cart-ride. 
The Garden is well-maintained with wide range of trees and floral plants.

Title: In the lap of nature
Text:
If you love plants, trees and greenery, you have to visits this Botanical Garden. Situated about half hour from Nuwara eliya and on the mountains, the view from this place is majestic.
There are various kinds of trees and plants to see. The garden is huge and I would suggest you wear a good pair of shoes.
A nice place to take kids and family to enjoy nature.

Title: A complete waste of Time !
Text:
Looking at 79% of the reviewers giving it a 'EXCELLENT' & "VERY GOOD" rating , we were inspired to allocate time to visit the garden.

All we can say is ...its a terrible terrible waste of money . Yes ticket cost is LKR 1500 and if you choose to avail the services of battery operated car to guide you through the park - add another LKR 500. 

Well not sure about April ( touted to be the main flowering season), on 17th June , it was nothing less than a disaster. Except for the rose garden (very ordinary) , there was nothing else to really appreciate.

One can never compare this with the Royal Botanical garden (Peradeniya), which also have similar entry fee, with lot more to see and appreciate.

Title: An Well maintained Botanical Garden
Text:
A super cool garden, just a 15mins drive from Nuwera Eliya town, crossing the scenic Gregory Lake. The garden is spread across 68 acres with a huge variety of trees and plants. The place is well maintained with a golf car service to take you around which you have to pay in extra. Loved the time that we spend. There is a fernery with in the garden which looks awesome and scenic.

Despite the strong winds and continuous drizzle we had a soothing experience here.

Title: Another Nature paradise
Text: A beautifully maintained botanical garden, a heaven , wonderful climate , lots of different flowers and plants build in the jungle, sight and sounds are excellent , a good place for a day outing with friends and families.

Title: Very very beautiful and mesmerising for all plant lovers
Text: It is an extremely beautiful garden that is situated on a height. If you love spending time with flowers and greenery then this is the place you must visit. But try and go there during flower season time. In May, there are fewer flowers but they are still there. Can be difficult for senior citizens to go upto the garden as its on a slope that you need to climb up and on your way down. Thought I have seen a golf cart there which is available on chargeable basis. But the drop off point seems to be upstairs only near exit point. So people who have difficulty in walking may find it a bit challenging navigating their way up and down. Otherwise its a great place to visit and spend time.

Title: Dissapointing Visit
Text:
We had heard so many good things about this garden. But when we visited we were very deeply disappointed with what we saw.
There was hardly any flowers and the whole place looked as if it had been taken down for maintanence.
The least that the managers could do was inform the visitors and  ticket counter staff to forewarn before selling the tickets - which are quite expensive for foreign visitors.

Title: Not to be missed!
Text:
We just couldnt make ourselves leave these gardens. Very few people visit so its very quiet and peaceful plus the gardens are maintained such they look and are more natural than cultivated.
A great place for meditation.

Title: We enjoyed seeing the monkeys
Text: There was a lot of greenery but not many flowers in bloom. The highlight of our viit were the monkeys an the top of the gardens

Title: Beautiful nature
Text: Great Place and nature , the weather is amazing, well organised, clean and easy to walk around, no need for a guide.

Title: Do not visit during March/April
Text: If you are planning to visit srilanka in march then i would suggest to skip this place as march is the season when they plant new flowers. so there wont be much to see during that time. Also you can find a board outside displaying the same, I would suggest to visit pinnawala botanical garden instead

Title: Breathtakingly beautiful with the blooms in the season but still amazing without
Text: I visited the Hakgala gardens with family and friends during a visit to N'Eliya.The flowers well be ready for the May -September season.The back drop reminds me of the Yosemite park at times.The fern forests with the small waterfalls were a photographers delight as were the orchids.The monkey species that roam around are unique to Sri Lanka..The gardens are well cared for.It will be a kaleidoscope of colours during the season especially the roses.

Title: Attractive hillside gardens
Text: We realised that the best displays of annuals would be in April but there was still lots to enjoy, especially the extensive hillside fernery and the general ambience.

Title: Green and natural
Text:
It was solo visit in a morning. 
Its a green and natural park. Very well laid, planned, clean with wide variety of flowers, gardens, trees. Its a place to be for one to two hours. 
If you have visited the kandy botanical garden you can skip it, because kandy botanical garden is very big.

Title: Beautiful gardens & so peaceful.
Text: Stopped here on our onward journey from Nuwara Eliya. These gardens are a must for the plants and different sections of the gardens. Also getting to see more of the monkeys of Sri Lanka !

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Extremely well laid out with a variety of themes all presented in a very natural setting. Our visit did not give us the best of the gardens because of the time of year i.e February. We expect that the gardens would be best viewed between May and July  and September to November to really get an appreciation of the variety of plants and flowers in bloom

Title: Paradise!
Text: I visited Hakgala Garden last year May 2017, it was really a nice place! A green scenery and has a lot to offer! Will be back there for sure!

Title: A green lung
Text: This garden is a run of the mill affair. Laid out over a large area, it has many plants and green house. It seems t hat  flower season is November onwards so did not see any flowers. Green house is ok and nothing exotic about it.

Title: Pretty rubbish
Text:
We went in Feb when there was nothing to see. Later in the year when the planting had taken effect it may well be different.

It's £7.50 each to enter. The map is ok as a basic check where you are guide but not accurate - just have a wander if you go.

We managed to stretch out to 90 mins, not sure how.

Title: Fabulous
Text: We visited the gardens on a fine sunny day.  Although this is the middle of the planting season we loved the layout of the gardens; the peace and quiet; and the views beyond to the distant mountains.  Our two hour stroll was fabulous although like everybody else who mentions it, the price differential for 'foreigners' is annoying.

Title: Disappointed!
Text: Confused about this one. We were in two minds - whether to see this since we had already done the Royal Gardens in Kandy that were massive!! Not only is this garden smaller, has lesser variety but also priced the same - 1500 LKR for foreigners. Huge disparity between locals and foreigners regarding entry tickets. We took the cart and managed it faster but not even half as appealing as the Royal gardens. Definitely not maintained well so dont feel the price was justified!

Title: Poorly maintained gardens
Text: We just visited the Hakgala gardens and were disappointed that after paying 1500LKR to enter each the gardens were poorly maintained. The Rose garden was off limits, some of the ponds were empty and the paths were poorly maintained. After paying a hefty entrance fee this was a disappointing experience.

Title: Too much disparity on the entry fee between locals and foreigners
Text:
The entry fee for a local is LKR 60 and that for a foreign national is LKR 1500. Not sure if the 25x price difference is justified 

One possible explanation for the fact we didn't see too many foreign nationals in the park.  may be the authorities just dont want anyone else around here.

Reasonably maintained but again too pricey for the what you get to see,

Title: Great find
Text:
Our driver suggested we stop here on route to haptule and I was thrilled we did - its huge and we could have spent more time
Wondering around the beautiful diverse gardens and enjoying the impressive views. Lots of local holiday makers but not crowded

Title: Green park, good one to stroll around
Text:
This park has various treks and sections so if you love to stroll around and spend time in some greenary, do visit.

We enjoyed the walk across various sections of garden

Title: The ertwhile Ashok Vatika
Text: Hakgala garden is atop a vast amount of land and though it is a charming place , Id rate the KANDY  Royal botanical garden way more in terms of plant diversity and placements

Title: Excellent place to visit
Text: Lovely place to visit......vast areas filled with delightful flowers and foliage.....orchid garden and cactus house worth mentioning....places to sit and rest at regular intervals...must visit

Title: A green oasis
Text: Come early and you can easily lose yourself in this wonderfully well maintained sanctuary. As the mist rolls across the mountains, you can easily see what drew the English here in droves. The gardens are lovingly maintained and in particular we loved the fernery. The signage can be improved - we got lost trying to get to the exit - but it just meant we spent more time here. No plastics allowed although they are ok with water bottles.

Title: Beautiful botanic garden
Text:
The Hakgala Botanic Garden, just outside of Nuwara Eliya, is definitely worth a visit. As some have noted, the entry fee for foreigners (LKR1500) may seem a little expensive, but as a visitor, you can see where the entrance fee is going. An army of gardeners keeps this place very well tended. 

The garden is at an altitude of around 1700 metres, and features a lot of temperate plants and trees. Monterrey Cypresses features prominently here, but there are also Bunya Bunya Pines and Norfolk Island Pine Trees from Australia. There's a rose garden, several greenhouses, a rock garden, and also a Japanese garden. I thought the Japanese garden was lovely, but struggled to see much relation to traditional Japanese gardens. There is also a section of the garden that was part of a tea plantation, where camellia sinensis trees have been allowed to grow out. I was fascinated to see them, as they grow to 10 - 13 metres once they're no longer pruned tightly. 

I'd recommend getting to the gardens early, as they are pretty popular. There's a small canteen inside, but there are a lots of small shops immediately outside the gates. 

I'll let the photos of this place speak for themselves...

Title: Very good variety but steep entrance fee
Text: The garden has some nice walks and a variety of trees and clolourful plants that one does not usually see. We spotted trees from Australia, Mexico and a few more countries. The rose garden and the glass house are quite good. Overall a nice experience but the entrance fee is a bit steep.

Title: Beautiful Botanical Garden
Text:
This is nice botanical Garden with lots of flowers and nice landscape and many perfect locations for taking photograph. 

It has got cart service but mostly it is fully booked.

Toilets are not very clean

You will enjoy visiting this place.

Title: Nothing special about this place not worth visiting
Text:
Well we paid the entrance fees (foreigners get special price) and saw a few flowers here and there. The highlight was the Rose garden with different colored roses. We took a buggy ride (extra charges) which was supposed to be 30 mins but with the various stops to take pictures and see some plantations it was done well within 15-20 mins. By way of explanation we were offered that due to heavy rains most of the area was closed. 

You would expect this to be told upfront before they make you part with your hard earned money. Or maybe they just think money grows on trees for foreigners and it is okay. 

Best avoided as this is a complete waste of time.

Title: Fine gardens but expensive
Text: The entrance to the gardens is impressive and they are extensive and seem to be well laid out. There was quite a lot of renovation/maintenance taking place.  We visited on a very rainy day so some areas were too wet, slippery or muddy to get to. It is not the best time of the year for many of the flowers but the trees are magnificent. At 1500 SLR per person it is much more expensive than the beautiful gardens in Kandy.

Title: Wonderful
Text: Our tuk tuk driver took us there and came inside. He was better than a guide! Several type of flowers and trees. Rose garden and Japanese garden are awesome

Title: Perfect getaway
Text: Not the biggest botanical garden, but enough to loose yourself in the maze of swirling paths. Lots of locals.

Title: One of the best botanical gardens in the world
Text: Hakgala Gardens located in the hill country of Sri Lanka is well worth a visit. It is a not only a horticulturalists haven but a lovely way to start a day. Some very very old and rare trees nicely showcased, Lots of flowers and well laud out garden layout. Truly worth a morning. Needs about half a day to see the entire garden if you really want to get the best experience. Walking is the best way of course as in any garden. The only drawback we found were the crowds of local tourists who visit. This we are told is during the school holiday season. So make it there at opening time (check with your hotel). Even though its its up on the hills the summer days can get rather hot. Take a hat and sunscreen.

Title: Go early and hike up
Text: One of my favorite places for birds and trees. Entry fee is 1500 for foreign guests. Walk in the front gate and turn up to the right past the ponds. Keep going to the upper trails where the thick brush grows. Many endemic birds can be found if you are patient. Avoid public holidays because of crowds and noise.

Title: A great  garden with a mythological story attached
Text:
One  of the biggest botanical gardens of Srilanka, Hakgala gardens is famous otherwise too. It is said to be over the are where Ravana kept Sita in captive in the epic Ramayana. This place is also called Sita Vatika.
The vast garden has over 10000 varieties of plants , beautifully landscaped. The small water bodies here and there and pleasantness to the atmosphere. The wash rooms are in place but could be more. There should be more sign boards to direct the tourists to different areas.
There is an entry fee, which is a must to generate funds to maintain and develop the gardens. But I feel the cost of the ticket is very high atleast for the foreign tourists, which makes people think twice before they get the ticket. 
A real treat to the eye and a is a delight to the serious  researchers in the field of botany .

Title: good place but difficult to cover
Text:
Popular place and scenic views....very long and would take couple of hours if one takes a van inside...however, getting a van is a challenge.....one may have to wait for 1 hour to get a van,,,,,without van, one may barely cover 1/3 of the area...saw rose garden ...it s beautiful...japanese garden is utter waste of time...complete avoid....
going to this place if its raining is a challenge as the winds are likely to be strong out here

Title: Beautiful gardens broken into seperate areas
Text:
This is a large area to walk and quite steep in places, but you can get a guide to take you round for 15/20 mins in a golf cart. Don't think you can book this before and they don't have many of them. The driver explained each area you walked though some and he met you at the end of that area. Would recommend this way to see the gardens, well worth the price he also pointed out animals we passed. Really enjoyed the visit.
Keep your water bottle in your bag as there is a sign that say doesn't allow plastic bottles into the park and people were just leaving there's at the entrance. Must be to stop the rubbish in the park as I couldn't see you could buy water or anything in the park. Understand the logic but would recommend a small bottle in the heat

Title: Lovely gardens a real gem
Text: The entrance is just off the side of the road. Lots of people trying to sell us stuff.but once we were in then what an amazing array of plants and flowers. We hired a golf buggy and the driver took us around and explained the various trees etc. Make sure you get to see all the different tree types. Simply stunning.gardens set against amazing views

Title: Better to avoid it
Text:
This place is poorly maintained and for the price they charge (1500 LRS) there is nothing to see here.
There roses in the rose garden were non existent, only good thing was the greenery in the fern gardens.

Title: Great place for Flower lovers
Text: The best season to visit here is month of April ,during other months there're only flower buds ,if you want to have the real experience you should visit during April.

Title: A beautiful garden in a unique location
Text:
Hakgala Botanical Garden is uniquely located at the base of the Hakgala Mountain range. The land itself is at a slope, and as you go up, the view also becomes great. 

If you don't want to walk, they now offer golf carts for hire that takes you around the park, with a knowledgeable guide who does a wonderful explanation. 

The management had implemented a strict no plastics policy, so they check and remove and plastic bottles and bags at the entrance. Personally I think it's a very good policy. Inside the park, there is a small cafe, where you can get snacks and drinks. There is also a small outlet where you can buy plants. 

One major drawback is the lack of parking. You have to park on the side of the main road, which in itself is narrow and bendy. There is a parking charge and attendants who look after the vehicles. It is also very crowded as it is a popular place to visit if you are in Nuwara Eliya. Don't expect to find peace and quite.

Title: Good garden to visit
Text: Exceptional garden and worth every penny for the entrance as a tourist. Easily spend 1/2 day there. Lots of walking inside and things to see. Some great views from certain locations in the garden,

Title: Gorgeous and peaceful gardens
Text: This botanical garden is certainly worth visiting. It is quite large, so be prepared to do some walking. Many different sections to enjoy and we really loved the Japanese garden and the fernery. The cost for foreign tourists is a bit expensive, but when you see how beautifully the garden is maintained you won't be upset to have contributed. They do not allow plastic water bottles inside.

Title: Nice place
Text: Beautiful place with lots of colourful flowers. But the entrance fee is way too expensive for tourists. Compared to Peradiniya botanical park, this is smaller but fee is higher.

Title: Absolutely Spectacular Botanic Garden
Text: This is probably the most beautiful botanic garden Ive seen, anywhere in the world. The massed displays of flowers just went on and on! There is also an arboretum section that is atmospheric, if not as stunning. Really worth a visit!

Title: Very expensive for foreign travelers
Text: Rs300 for travelers, Rs400 for locals. I understand it is a means to help travelers subsidise the upkeep of the gardens but that seemed a little much of a difference to me. Gardens could be stunning though they do hark back to the British times with many European flowers (roses, etc) and little that is native to the Nuwara Eliya region.

Title: Quite good
Text:
It is quite a nice garden. There are nice streams in the park. 
I like Peradeniya Garden (near Kandy) better.

Title: Amazing place
Text: A lovely amazing garden.. trees are 150 years old with the origin of each documented.. Japanese gardenis wonderful

Title: Great chance to walk
Text: It is big park. The ticket price reasonable. It's great place to walk between trees and flowers. Some areas are closed due to maintenance. We spent more than two and half hour and never get bored.

Title: Scenic Garden with wide range of Flowers & Plants
Text: A very scenic garden on a hill; one of the 5 botanical gardens in Srilanka, and this place is just 1 km from Sita temple. A good hang out place for family and kids. This park has a wide range of flowers and plants, it also has categories like Rose garden, Japanese garden,etc. It was like an Amazon forest kind of place, it also has some cute bridges and small waterfalls running all over the park.

Title: Flower paradise
Text: Haggala botanical garden located in Nuwaraeliya district. So many beautiful flowers and beautiful trees. For aged people can take golf car to visit entire garden. best is walking and covering entire garden. Place to relax. Ideal for half day activity. Cafeteria available inside the garden. well maintained garden. Whoever visiting to Nuweraliya they will obviously visit Haggala garden. Tourist location and need to get ticket for enter the garden.

Title: Foreigners will be ripped off. Best place to see funny policies and flowers.
Text:
Best - Good botanical collection and seems best in April/May. Good places to relax and nice walking paths. Could have done better. 

Worst - Few thugs like people will scavenge for plastics at the gate and remove all before you enter saying need to be environment friendly. But they provide paper bags to use. When you go inside there are no litter bins at all in the places they are needed. Why don't they provide litter bins and avoid hassle at the gate to tourists ? May be because that's their own way. Staff at the entrance and ticket hall are all with see it or leave it attitude.  

If you are foreigner, they will strip you with Rs 2500 ticket compared to Rs 60 locals ticket. But there are even no basic facilities like usable toilets [so don't expect toilets with tissues]. However being a foreigner has advantage that you can carry plastics without interrogation at the gate. So that's the plus point for a foreigner. 

Travellers Tip for Foreigners - If any issues, just keep on talking in your language. So the staff will indeed back-off. Tested successfully. Beware of monkeys in some places are bit aggressive when they see food.

Title: Worth a Visit
Text: Beautifully laid out gardens and the bird life is amazing. The layout though is really good no strenuous walking and prices in the park are reasonable.

Title: Once a beautiful garden.
Text: During the time I visited, due to a bad drought & pruning of the rose garden, there were not many flowers in the garden. The best time to visit is June to August. Can spend almost a half a day. Nursery was excellent, even in December.

Title: OK, but very big and spread out
Text: The setting of this Park is probably a bigger reason to visit than the Park itself. Sitting under the rock cliffs above, the park is very pretty. If you love trees, this is the place. However, this is a very large place, and very much up and down. Otherwise a typical British style Park. Only go if you really enjoy arboretum type areas.

Title: Cool & Calm
Text: Worth a visit in the morning. Garden is not much big like Peradeniya Botanical Garden. Flowers are less in some seasons.

Title: Completely waste of time and money
Text: A very expensive ticket gets you an entry to massive garden which is usually littered with newly weds taking photos. It also is not very laid out making it even more uninteresting

Title: Peaceful and cool
Text: I loved the hakgala gardens almost as much as Paradynia Gardens. It's cool, calm, and mystical. While it does not have as many prehistoric looking trees like the Paradynia Gardens, it's worth a visit in the early morning hours.

Title: Some great trees - literally!
Text: A lovely place. We were guided round which is a good idea. Lots of lovely nooks and crannies with different themes and some massive trees well worth a look. Nice calm session to cheer anybody up.

Title: Hakgala Botanic Garden in Nuwara Elyah, Sri Lanka
Text: It's a vast botanic gargen having many types of trees & plants. Need a guide if you're interested in botany. Garden has a histroric spot that goes bak to Hindu Ramayan days. It's beleived that "Ravana" kept "Sita" under guard in this garden after kidnapping "Sita" from "Rama" in India.

Title: Green green every where
Text: The botanical garden is a great oxygen pool. The distance to be covered is more than 4 kms so be prepared with good shoes. The trees are really good. I found all sections similar. The terrain is good for a fast walk with green beauty around.

Title: Nice Visit with Misty Views
Text:
The Hakgala Botanic Gardens are more modest than its counterpart in Kandy, but it offers wonderful views of Nuwara Eliya's ever-present shroud of mist, both in the surrounding hills and the garden itself. Mist descended and lifted over the garden a couple of times during our two-hour visit in late December. It was beautiful (see photos).

Hakgala has a couple of rose gardens, which probably makes up for the orchid house in its Kandy counterpart.

Hakgala offers much better views of the surprising hills, many of which are green with tea plants.

Title: Nice garden
Text:
It's located on main road and entry fee to foreigners is ?1500/- which looks high. 
Spreaded in a vast area has lot to learn if it interests you..

Title: Very peaceful and educational
Text: It's always crowded specially during school holidays but still you can find peaceful places as it's a huge place. You can even buy plants at there. Try to get a buggy ride and if you are lucky enough to get Person who drove us, you will get to know more about trees. Unfortunately there are no guides. I hope they stop letting public to have lunch inside the garden as they will liter the place.

Title: Charming & relaxing
Text: We found this a really enjoyable & relaxing visit - took a good 2 hours made more interesting by the intertwining pathways you can take to meander through the gardens. It's not anything like the scale of the Botanical Gardens at Peridineya, but worth a visit if you are in NE for a day or two

Title: Hindu religious name "Dronagiri Mountain" (Hakgala) that Hanuman brought from Himalayas
Text: Hindu religious name "Dronagiri Mountain" (Hakgala) that Hanuman brought from Himalayas for Sanjeevani Booti for treatment of Lord Ram's brother Laxman during Lanka war. Beautiful Hindu temple of Sita nearby at Sita Eliya 1 km away

Title: A Beautiful Garden
Text: A Big beautiful garden near the Gregory lake, but need to pay a hefty entrance fee. Beautiful species of plants and birds. An exotic Sri -Lankan garden. Quite refreshing to have a garnden walk but too big for senior citizens. Some facility for senior citizens should be thought of.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text:
Lovely place to visit & walk around, the trees, flowers and fauna are lovely. 

In certain areas you can see the monkeys too. Nice to just walk around and stretch the legs if you've been cooped up for a while.

Title: Beautiful but unguided
Text: A beautiful garden with many varieties of flowers and plants. A guide to the garden or a map would have been a huge help. The paths are unmarked and one wanders around asking for directions. Toilets are widely spaced so best use them when you see em! A golf cart is available but is severely inadequate to cater to the needs of visitors. There is no consideration for elderly visitors who have quite a long walk to the carts and then to find that a two hour wait was required to use the next. The Japanese garden was an utter disappointment. The Rose gardens were beautiful

Title: Beautiful Garden
Text: The Garden is maintained very neatly and I being a Botony student really felt  very Happy to see so many varieties of plants  in this garden. It is very big garden on a small hillock like area and there is a battery car to take you around and it is worth going around as it needs a lot of time to walk around and one should be fit to cover the full garden on foot. The entry fee for foreigners is Rs. 1500 per person and battery car for 6 people is Rs 1000 in sri lankan rupees

Title: The roses were the best we have seen them
Text: This was the first time we have been to the Hakgala Botanic Gardens in April and it is possibly the best time to go there. The flowers in general and the roses in particular were the best we have ever seen them. The majority of the visitors were Sri Lankans and their children - this being the school holidays.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Was beautiful and well maintained. Lots of varieties. More labeling of the names of the flora and fauna would have been helpful. Kept us occupied for about 2 hours.

Title: for nature lovers
Text:
superb garden once I visited during my stay in Sri lanka.
ticket price little bit more. but recommended

Title: Nice place to visit.
Text: One of the nice places to visit and take pictures. Quite and nice place. Highly recommended. Take pictures as many as you can.

Title: Worth a stop off
Text: We stopped off on our way into Nuwara Eliya. It's 10km south of the city so convenient on the way in. Can be done in 1-2 hours.

Title: Foreigners get ripped off
Text: The entry price of Rs. 1100 for foreigners, but they only charge Rs. 50 Sri Lankans. So if you are foreigner you pay 22 times more than what locals pay. I feel so bad that foreign tourists are being ripped off.

Title: Way overpriced
Text: When you have seen Kandy Botanical gardens don't come here, way to expensive for what you will get. Some flowers you also see everywhere else around the world.

Title: Well manicured gardens with lots of shade
Text: Memories for my wife and her mother strolling through these lovely gardens. Many varieties of plants and trees and a superb fern garden. Really cheap food cafe with Sri Lankan fare. If you are tired try the golf cart.

Title: Gorgeous Place
Text: Hakgala gardens actually feels like it is in another country. The weather is so cool and at times cold and the plants are also not the normal tropical plants one finds in the hotter parts of Sri lanka. The garden has rhodedendrond and other European plants as well as local flora all beaufitully laid out. An excellent way to spend an afternoon.

Title: Beautifully Landscaped
Text: You need at least an hour and a half to explore these beautiful gardens. Its quite a walk albeit a lovely one. Buggies too are available to take you around if you don't feel unto the walk

Title: botanical garden
Text: This garden is nearby to Sita Aman temple. It is believed that Sita was kept captive by Ravana  at this place. We did not go inside the botanical garden but saw it from outside only.  If you visit the Siat Aman temple then you can also go to this place since it is nearby.

Title: Treat for Botanists
Text: Amazing number of botanical specimens to be found in a small area at the foothill of a peak. There are golf carts for those who do not or cannot walk for long.

Title: Extensive botanic gardens with beautiful views out to forested mountains
Text: Extensive botanical gardens with winding pathways making for easy strolls around the various themed areas from around the world. Some of the gardens are in need of tidying up and repair/re-planting, although some of this work seems to be going on. The featured rose garden, although containing many varieties is not particularly well maintained. From the gardens there are distant views of wooded mountainsides and distant villages.

Title: A good photo spot... but over priced tickets
Text: We visited this spot on our way from nuwara eliya to bentota... the entry fee was 1100 lkr per person ... which I thought was a little too much for a botanical garden but hoped that the place would match the price... the place is filled with a variety of trees and plants... really makes for a good spot if you are planning to take a photo shoot or on your honeymoon.. The area is vast so it gets pretty tiring to see the entire place also after some time the plants and tress look pretty monotonous... If you would lie to see each and every spot then it is better that you spend a little more and make use of the internal transport system. They have a good variety of orchids which was the highlight of that place atleast for me.. I would suggest that you visit this place only if you have extra money or are a botanical fan.. overall a little too overpriced for the place...

Title: Could be better
Text: Greenery, flowers, some good views and a leisurely stroll through the park would sum up our visit here. There is a entry fee for foreigners. Also available is a 3 seater and a 7 seater golf buggy, if you don't want to walk.

Title: Nice but not spectacular garden.
Text:
We decided to give this garden a visit on our first Sri Lanka trip. It is located about 30minutes from Nuwara Eliya town. This botanical garden is spread across hectres of hilly terrains and beautifully maintained. The entering price is quite steep for tourist (1100Lakhs per person) as compared to locals (50Lakhs). It is not as magnificent as those botanical garden in some part of the world that I have been but it has numerous type of plants, ranging from medicinal plants, cold climate colorful flowers and very old aged mature trees. Due to its large area, the stroll can be quite tiring especially when we walked along the small rocky paths. If you need to get a buggy however, it is available at 1000Lakhs per hour but the number of buggy is very limited. My mom and her friend waited almost 1 hour for any available buggy but failed.

There are upper gardens and lower gardens. We lost track of our whereabouts but we first encountered Rose Garden. Since it is May and it is spring, there are many blossom colourful roses. Red (definitely), pink, white, blue, yellow etc.

The Japanese garden is nothing to shout about with its water features and some unimpressive bonsai. Probably can skip it if you are not up for a long uphill stroll.

This place is a good diversion of the busy Nuwara Eliya town but it comes with high price and the garden is not really spectacular. It is still a good place for relaxing stroll with family, but definitely not for those with weak knees or legs. Unless you are lucky and there is available buggy for you to rent.

Title: A huge well maintained place. Must Visit for nature lovers
Text: We loved walking around the place and exploring it at our own pace. However, battery-operated carts are available for a fee.

Title: Beautiful landscape
Text: The garden built on the foot of a huge rocky mountain. Very nice place to walk and enjoy the nature, it is clean and well arranged. There are signs all around the garden to  read informations about plants and their place of origin. It was an educational trip and for relaxation.

Title: Good in december
Text: good in december, but very attractive time is Aprill.All the flowers belongs to cold climate as well,as,attractive location after Nuwaraeliya town.

Title: Nothing much to offer if you are not a botanist
Text:
While the gardens, per se, were good with great varieties of trees, flowers and fauna; if you are not a botanist of a flower and trees lover, you may get bored after some time like we were. 

Definitely not worth the entry ticket cost.

Title: Nice but a bit expensive
Text: It's a huge botanical garden but the entrance fee is a bit high (LKR 1100 for foreigners). The map was a bit confusing so we couldn't cover the whole place. But the garden is full of flowers of vibrant colors. When we went it was a bit crowded.

Title: Good for a visit early morning or late evening. Dont waste your time in Nuwara Eliya here
Text: A decent botanical garden; with some nice Japanese plants and a good cactus house. Nothing else about it was special. Fees entry for foreigners is also a bit on the higher side. Didnt like it too much; not recommended unless you have a lot of time in Nuwara Eliya

Title: A quiet afternoon walk
Text: These gardens are nice for an afternoon stroll in the shade. The gardens aren't as good as those in Kandy but very pleasant. We took the bus from Nuwara Eliya which was very easy.

Title: Nice Botanical garden
Text: This is a nice botanical garden. It is pretty well maintained. clean with lots of rare plants and trees. I liked a palm tree with fruits which looked like coconuts.The orchid garden was very nice.

Title: I LOVE Botanical Gardens.
Text:
Hakgala Botanical Gardens
I also went to see Hakgala Gardens via bus (RS 30). Its 10kms from Nuwara Eliya. What a BEAutiful place. Yes, I know its Saturday but its the day I had to go. Avoid weekends. Its less crowded. I tried to avoid the hordes. Foreigner fee is RS 1100. Local fee is RS 50. See some of the pictures. Nuwara Eliya is VERY crowded in April which is Sri Lankan New Year. I purposely avoided April when prices triple and planned to come in March. The annual flowers would be blooming then, of course, but I couldnt stand the crowds. Still the gardens are pleasant.

Title: wonderful day out
Text: Well worth the trip out of town. These gardens are very natural unlike Peradiniya  formal ones. Taking in the rock massive backdrop the setting is fantastic.

Title: Beautifully maintained gardens
Text: There was little colour when we visited in February but the beds were newly planted and will no doubt be stunning in a few weeks time. Beautifully maintained and with enough space to wander and escape from other people and admire the fauna as well as flora. About a 20 minute (frequent) bus ride from Nuwara Eliya. 1100 rupee entrance fee for foreigners.

Title: Beautiful place and surely worth visit
Text: This botanic garden is really nice and with so many types of flora. Somehow its not marketed well. There ate plants and trees from round the world and place itself is beutiful. There are so many types of flower formations. By chance we visited this place and felt so lucky that we did. If ur visiting eliya then dont miss these gardens.

Title: Blossoming flowers added an extra flavour to the garden.
Text: It is a botanical garden with full of flowers blossoming throughout. You must see this place if you visit Nuwara Eliya in Sri Lanka.

Title: Take enough time to visit this beautiful garden
Text:
Wonderful garden. The small orchid collection is not special but take about 2 hrs to walk through the garden. The palm lanes are impressive and an absolute must are the bizarre (witch) trees in the area around the suspended bridge.
Coming back from this bridge you walk on a real "bat" avenue with thousands of big fruit bats. Don't miss it!

Title: Nice but no flowers when we went
Text: It was a nice experience but we were disappointed to see no flowers blooming during this part of the season. Must be worth visiting during full season

Title: Superb
Text: Really nice Botanic Gardens, well kept, nice variety of plants, trees and flowers. Kids climbed the trees and enjoyed it!

Title: A must for nature lovers when in Nuwara Eliya.
Text:
spell binding aged cypresses with countless trees and bushes.
fascinating walkways if a bit scary in the misty foggy silence with only the trickle of water for music.
The occasional cry from a macaque monkey or a bird call wafting on the cool fresh breeze may be soothing to some and alarming to others, i felt distinctly unsafe and vulnerable, although i may be totally out on  a limb and the place may be very very safe.i felt like walking through a spooky movie.
the upper gardens and theme areas are neglected and need more attention.
A thoroughly enjoyable and engrossing visit which is also a trek through local history.

Title: Love the Electric Cars.
Text: The Electric cars that shuttled us around these gardens were the best thing about the botanical experience. I loved the Fern corner with their luscious green leaves, but other than this, and the old trees and bushes that looked gnarled and calcified, we felt that Hakgala can offer a more authentic experience. It is no World's End.

Title: Beautiful botanical garden
Text: Hakgala botanical garden located a few kms away from Seetha Eliya  is a place not to miss when in Nuwara Eliya. Beautifully designed and layed out into various categories of plants ,flowers ,vegetables n trees.The garden has windings walking tracks spread through out the garden ,some portion of the garden are on the slope which require climbing steep slopes

Title: Nice and calm place
Text: Beautiful place. Nice and calm environment. Plenty of flowers (Good for fans of flowers). Nice weather. Nicely maintained. For foreigners Rs. 1500 (about $11.00) so it's very worthy. Must visit place in Nuwaraeliya.

Title: Nice garden; way too expensive
Text: This is a really nice botanical garden. Beautiful flowers, layout is fantastic, the guys in yesteryear did a great job. Alas, today money is the object an the entrance fees are just crazy. The gardens should be renamed "Sponsored by Foreigners". Too expensive and not worth the money if you are on a budget. If money no object, check out he rose garden ...lovely.

Title: A good nature for who needs
Text: Coming from Dubai (a desert with fake greens), visiting the botanical garden was so relaxing and exciting (especially for young kids). I recommend to go end of the park to see more natural environment with big trees and small waterfalls... Kid loved it...

Title: Outstanding
Text: We spent a whole afternoon in these botanic gardens and had a wonderful experience.  They are beautifully landscaped and maintained with a rich balance of internal and external plant displays.  The trees are particularly special.  My biggest surprise - and delight - was the discovery of a colony of thousands of fruit bats at the rear left of the gardens by the river - noisy but spectacular.  I highly recommend a visit if you like this sort of stuff.

Title: Great Botanic Garden
Text: Large and nicely laid out, a beautiful place for a walk, with many of the huge old trees labelled as to species, a classic piece of Victoriania really.

Title: Nice garden; good way to spend an afternoon for nature lovers
Text:
If you love nature, this garden is definitely worth the trip.

ENTRANCE: The line for the tickets can be a bit unruly - crowds just hanging in front of the window to collect tickets.  Tickets can be a little pricey, especially if you are not a local.  Having said that, it may be worth what you pay for.

TRANSPORTATION: Since the garden is quite extensive, you can hire a buggy to take you around the park.  This may be a good option if you are a family with elders or toddlers who may tend to get tired with long walks.  They are priced reasonable and can be hired from near the entrance.

PARK: You are provided with a map of the garden.  Definitely recommended as some of the areas you might miss out on if you are not referring to the map.  Some areas of the park give you a good view of the city from up above - definite photo opportunity.  When we visited, the flowers and plants were still blooming, so colors were a little limited.  Nevertheless, it was still a fulfilling experience.

You may also see family of monkeys - just be careful if you are holding any edible items - they may come and grab it.  But for the most part, they keep to themselves.

FOOD: There was a small canteen that served drinks, crisps and other food items.  Nice spot to catch your breath a little, view the surroundings.

OVERALL: A good visit if you have an hour or two to spare.

Title: Over priced for nothing
Text:
I've visited it to day almost end of March. The garden is not ready a lot of maintenance work. 
Very expensive entrance ticket 1500 rupes for tourist and only 10 rupes for locals.
The orchid house is only 4 × 4 meters approximately with around 5 kinds of orchids most of them need repotting badly. 
The rose garden is closed for pruning the sign say but all the roses are  starting to blom and nothing in need of pruning. They should wrote closed for other reasons. 
The garden is hilly it is not accessible for handicapped people and old folks; but I sow a golf cart touring some people. Only third of the garden is accessible by it.
I had a good quite time under the big trees and walking around discovering the garden it's signs are confusing. 
No services inside other than one dirty place selling snacks and drinks.

Title: Interesting
Text:
Interesting tour and close to town. However, they only process at night so not much happening in the factory. Still educational and have complimentary cup of tea. 

Closed from 11am to 2pm

Title: very old garden with beautiful flowers & trees
Text: This place now well maintained & can view very beautiful roses , flowers & trees. very relaxing place for even large groups. cheap entrance.

Title: Nice place for relaxing.
Text: Hakgala Botanical Garden is one of the five botanical gardens in Sri Lanka. It is the second largest garden in Sri Lanka. The garden is contiguous to Hakgala Strict Nature Reserve. Hakgala Botanical Garden is situated on the Nuwara Eliya-Badulla main road, 16 km from Nuwara Eliya. Hakgala Botanic Gardens, about 28 hectares in extent, lie under the shadow of the Hakgala Rock. The garden was established in 1861, under George Henry Kendrick  as an experimental cultivation of Cinchona, a comercial crop thriving at the time. Once after the Tea replaced the Cinchona, it was turned into an experimental Tea cultivation. In 1884 it transformed to a garden.
