Since then many sub tropical and some temperate plants were planted in the gardens. The Botanic Gardens are locally reputed for their collection, the rose garden, Magnificent trees, indoor plants, flowers. The climate of the Gardens is subtropical, cool and freshThere are over 10,000 species of flora planted here. However USD 12.5 for SARC coumtries and USD 25.00 per person for a foreigner is bit expensive.

Title: A walk amid nature
Text:
We got here a half hour before the ticket booth closes (the park remains open for another hour, if I remember correctly) and noticed that people were leaving in huge numbers. We thought we had come at the wrong time but instead we really enjoyed walking with almost nobody around. It was planting season so it wasn't as colorful as it should be but still it was wonderful going through the various gardens.

Several paths lead to different areas and all are worth exploring. We really loved walking through one particular narrow path that went through trees and felt as if we were in a forest. With nobody else around, we just had so much fun.

As the light faded we started looking for the way back but got lost. We didn't panic though and enjoyed our search for the exit. The management should add exit signs in some of the remote places to guide visitors because there is only one entrance/exit and these Botanic Gardens are spread over an enormous area.

Title: Nice stop
Text: We visited these gardens en route to our next stop on our tour. It was a pleasant and peaceful walk around these gardens but unfortunately we did not catch them at their best as it was planting season. We would imagine that they look beautiful when all the flowers and shrubs are in bloom.

Title: stroll around
Text: The local trees walking around gardens are the most interesting part of the gardens.  Best early morning as it can get hot.

Title: Beautiful Gardens
Text: Even though it wasn't the season for flowers in the gardens the hot houses had some really beautiful orchids. At the right time of the year the whole garden would be a mass of colour. We still enjoyed our visit looking at the ferns, Japanese Garden and much more. Definitely worth a few hours of peaceful time.

Title: Overpriced
Text: They charge LKR 1500 per person for foreigners which is too much. The garden is nice. Has lot of variety of trees & plant. We hired golf car for LKR 500 hoping that the driver explain something about the plant we see. But he just gave brief information & was rushing us as the car tour was for 1 hour only. If this huge amount is charged for ticket they should also provide group tour guide so that it is informative. Most of Trees & plants found there are found all across Nuwara Eliya...so nothing special.

Title: Awe inspiring trees, woth the uphill walk
Text: Beautiful old trees. we loved the camphor trees - the fallen leaves have a strong & delightful camphor fragrance. lot of uphill walking required on a paved path but worth the effort if you have the energy

Title: Beautiful misty garden
Text: I really loved this garden. They have such beautiful trees and there was a mist in the background. We went on a weekday afternoon so there was hardly anyone. U can see monkeys running across the path and there's a stream. I didn't get to explore the entire garden but I really loved it. My only complaint is that there are no sitting toilets which may be difficult for the elderly.

Title: Not a great place and costly for foreigners
Text:
This is nice and calm garden with some big trees, flower nursery and offers a good walk of 1.5 hrs.
However the place offers nothing special and its unnecessarily costly for foreign tourists.

Title: A walk in the woods
Text:
It's okay if you don't mind the steep price of 1500.- p.p. 
Lots of big trees a nice fern garden and a slightly neglected Japanese garden.
Some trash here and there since it was a Sunday.  Almost no flowers because of the time of the year. December.

Title: Beautiful and very Natural........
Text: The gardens are tended to very well...This garden is definitely worth a visit. The flowers are beautiful and we took lots of great photographs.Must see place in Nuwara Eliya. Garden was huge and interesting with many varieties of plants.

Title: Beautiful Botanical Garden with a rich history attached
Text:
Hakgala gardens are both beautiful and rich in hostory. It is the place where Ashok Vatika was present . This place was later on converted in a beautiful botanical garden with a wide variety of exotic trees and plants. The best way to see the entire garden is  walking although there are golf cars available at the gate which charge LKR 200 per person and covers the entire garden in around 45 minutes.
There is an Ashoka tree which is said to be from the lineage of the original ashoka trees of the Ashok Vatika.

Overall , its a beautiful garden with an  amazing array of flowers. Its a must see place in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: beautiful
Text: Hakgala Botanical Garden is very beautiful and it make you feel really relaxed because all you can see is green mountains the sky and flowers. all you can smell is fresh air.

Title: Beautiful Botanic Garden
Text: The ticket room is a little bit messy when full of people, but it's ok. It is a beatiful place to go if you have extra time on your schedulle or if you are with children.

Title: Serene gardens

Title: Not a place to visit

Text: Learnt that face foundation was obtained from tree barks. "Karpoor" used in medicine , essence and for " Arti'  is also extracted from trees. The guide was good and did his best to pass on information of the different trees planted there and their age. They have maintained the place well.

Text: It was beautiful and colorful but after visiting the botanical gardens in Kandy, it seemed very small and boring..

Title: Best garden in Nuwara Eliya
Text: This is the best botanical garden in Nuwara Eliya if not in the whole island. Best time to visit is Spring (April) when most of the flowers are in full bloom.

Title: Pretty flowers
Text:
Definitely You have to visit it.
Colorful pretty flowers and beautiful green spaces also you can see some birds and monkeys.

Title: Expensive & overpriced

Title: Smaller than 'big brother' Peradeniya gardnes', still really worth while.
Text: Sri Lanka can boast some superior parks (the Kandy Royal Udawattekele, the amazing nearby Peradeniya), and Hakgala is one of the smaller once, less crowded (lots of locals) and not as expensive. These are also scientific research stations on indigenous plants, including the worlds finest tea shrubs...

Title: Cozy , medium size botanic heaven
Text:
This is a medium size garden , not too much detailed information labeling plants or scientific organization , however it is definitely an elaborate work which started in 1861 , has surprising collection of well organized trees and flowers arranged in a very beautiful and creative manner which made my 2 hours walk an ultimate joy.
Must visit

Title: Relaxing
Text: A nice Botanical Garden with lots of trees, shrubs, flowers, bushes on hilly terrain. For foreigners, it is a bit expensive, Rs.1500 (USD =10). Those who can not walk on hilly areas, are discouraged. Lots of ups and downs. I was getting tired. On my way took lots of pictures of flowers and trees. Nice place to relax. The area is quite huge and takes lots of time. I walked for about an hour and then started to get down. My husband decided to stay on the road and have tea as it was difficult for him to walk up hill. Walking shoes, raincoat, or umbrella for sudden rains, Caps and camera will be helpful. Many places are not very even, so walk carefully. I went there alone but did not feel scared. Many local tourists were there. Part of the park was quiet and had a deserted look.

Title: Wonderful view of Native Plants & Local Visitors
Text: Really nice botanical gardens primarily frequented by locals (a young couple asked to take a selfie with me so Westerners not all that common apparently). Not too large, great for a couple of hours seeing some really beautiful flowers, trees & shrubs (greenhouse and rose gardens, Japanese gardens and other specialty areas and waterfalls abound). Not world class or anything but a great local find.

Title: Nice & lot of walking!
Text: Beautiful Botanical gardens, you will see lot of flowers, trees, birds, monkeys, open spaces for kids to play, you will walk along the river, do check out the suspension bridge.

Title: Amazing place
Text: Way more interested by the ferns and the lush tropical part than the rose garden. This part is very impressive.

Title: Nice garden
Text:
Lots of different flowers and trees, nice view of the surrounding mountains.
Spacious setup, so very relaxing.
Only a bit on the expensive side, 1500 roepie ($10) per person, where the locals get in for 60 roepie ($0,40)

Title: Good
Text: Was veru nice to see that plants and trees from all over the world could be found in Nuwar Eliya. Could walk throughout, but got a feel of the place.

Title: Great place to learn

Title: Worst
Text: This is totally wastage of Money LKR 1500/- per head. I personally don't recommend this if you don't know much about the plants. As they charge such a high entrance I suggest sending one guide along so that they can explain.

Title: Amazing diversity ! Great way to spend a few hours!
Text:
About 5 Km away from Nuwara Eliya town, the Hakgala Botanical Gardens is a must-see.

The variety of trees and plants is stunning.
Orchid and rose gardens are at treat to the eyes.

Some the trees were so huge - some with  trunks spanning nearly  2 metres.

Fabulous place for  the nature photographer. And even if you  not are one, you will become one here!

After a long and leisurely round of the garden, one can nice to sit and relax on a sloping glade . Divine !!

Nature lovers - set aside minimum 2-3 hours at the minimum for a visit here.

Title: Nice garden
Text: Nice garden, who is worth a visit. plan for 2-3 hours.  some of the garden vere under re-Construction, but no signs, so it was a bit tricky to find out where to go.

Text: Avoid this tourist trap for foreigners at all cost. They charge 1500 LKR for foreigner entry compared to 60 for locals. Entry fee aside, the place is tepid. Title: Nice place
Text: Nice botanical garden although the entry fee seems to be overpriced for foreigners. Nevertheless with Nuwara Eliya's pleasant weather, this is a wonderful place to visit. You also see locals going to the gardens on Sunday :)

Title: A part of Ashok Vatika
Text: a place which a nature lover shouldn't miss.... beautiful landscape... well maintained parks... some of the plants are unique.....rose garden is awesome.... a must visit when in Nuwara Eliya.

Text: try to get away from the interlocked pathways and climb higher on trails so that you avoid the noise from hordes of families who descend on this garden on the weekend. it's really beautiful and amazing if you find a quiet spot and there are many. the entrance fee is also pretty high: SKR 1000 for an adult and like everywhere else in Sri Lanka, the entrance fee for foreigners is way higher than for locals!

Title: Not crowded, refreshing and beautiful.
Text: The Park is small, well contained,with amazing flora, beauty and peace. I visited it 5 years ago. I would have revisited it on this recent visit in March '16, but I did not have the time, and I think the entrance charge was quite high

Title: Overpriced.
Text: Turned up expecting to pay 600 rupees admission only to find that it had gone up to 1100 rupees for foreigners. Together with tuk tuk fares, 3000 + rupees (for 2) was a very expensive visit to pleasant but not spectacular gardens. I think that the main attraction of the place is a respite from the chaos and rubbish of central Nuwara Eliya (Little England!!!). OK. I understand that they need to raise funds and that the local people can't/don't pay more than the 50 rupee (?) locals' fee but this is just a rip-off. But then again, that's the story all over Sri Lanka.

Title: Flowers in a Misty Mountain
Text: Located in one of the highest spots in Sri Lanka, thus covered with mist during the evening hours (usually). It is a pleasant surprise to find some rare species of plants and flowers in the mist. The foot path may be muddy if rain disturbs you, but you can simply turn back to the main walk ways which are properly built. You can further take the assistance of a guide if you wish. Best time to visit is March / April & May, during morning hours.

Title: Beuatiful Garden
Text: a beautiful collection of many species of trees and flowers and a must visit for the botanical stream student. A better one is at Peradeniya Kandy but here there is better

Title: Best Botanical Garden in Sri Lanka !
Text: This place is the best botanical garden in Sri Lanka. You can see thousands of varieties of flowers bloomed in rich little England. Very good for relaxation with family and for nature lovers. Special minicab service also available for little extra payment !

Title: Beautiful, well worth it
Text:
Incredibly well-tended gardens in the centre of Nuwara Eliya. Big enough to spend some time in, small enough to cover pretty quickly.

Good kids' playground although much was under maintenance when we visited.

Title: This is how to chase tourists away!
Text:
With an entry price of 1100 rupees for tourists but 50 rupees for the locals,  it is impossible not to feel that tourists are being ripped off.
The locals use it for noisy picnics or school trips (can they ever not be noisy).
The gardens themselves are actually quite a delight with various easily demarcated sections.  eg rose garden, Japanese garden etc.
Overall it is a haven for garden enthusiasts who look back to time of the British colonial past for inspiration.
Get full value by bringing your own picnic lunch and not getting caught in a monsoon thunderstorm!  (What fun).  There are some tacky tourist shops near the entrance.

Title: Kandy one is better
Text: I heard the botanic garden in Kandy is bigger and better than this one and prices of entry is same (LKR 1100).

Title: Must to visit
Text: Might not be that value if you don't have a guide with you to describe some truly amazing facts and information! I don't know if you can hire a guide, but we rent a golf car and the driver was the guid! It is very big so the car was a nice idea. One of the plants closes its leaves once you touch it! Many others have great smell once you squeeze the leaves! The monkeys there was a great added value! Be careful, we saw a snack!

Title: Beautiful and historical place
Text: We wanted to go to these gardens because our grandfather visted them in1897 and wrote about them in his journal. We loved the huge trees aind were impressed with how well it is being looked after. We were told they have a staff of 60. We used one of the little electric buggies so we had the added advantage of a knowledgable driver who pointed out the most interesting items. We could also stop and walk for a bit of we wanted. There were good smooth paths, but some of the steps were a little hazardous. Hakgala was where the first tea was planted in Ceylon and we saw some of those bushes. Also a Cinchona bush which was also trailed here. A bush used in treating Malaria. The exhibits were identified well with their names and where they came from. In January the bedding plants were not in flower. It must be a blaze of colour in a month or two.

Title: 2 hour visit to hakgala gardens.
Text:
We stopped to visit here as this is supposedly the area of Ashok vatika. 
The gardens are beautiful with variety of plants. There is a interesting rock garden and barren area in the garden. Langoors roam in the gardens and are harmless .

Title: Nice place to spend an hour or 2
Text: Not very different from the rest of Nuwara Eliya. But may be a nice place for a stroll with the kids. Some maintenance activities going on at some places.

Title: One of the best
Text:
A beautiful garden full of roses and huge old trees through the misty hill country of sri lanka. If you happen to go to nuwara eliya, it would be in vain if not pay a visit for this place.
Do a little bit of walking in this place situated above 2000 meters above see level. When it's sunny 30 degrees Celsius in colombo,expect this place to be 8 - 12 degrees.

Title: Absolutely loved it!!!
Text:
This gardens didn't get enough credit on trip advisor. We spent 1.5 - 2 hours there but could have stayed much longer. Take a blanket and just relax amoungst nature's beauty. There's many different sections and quiet the mixture from open areas, jungle, rose gardens and more. 

Would definately visit again! Must see if in Nuwara Eliya!!

Title: Not so interesting
Text: The high price for this place because a few interesting flora growing there. But if you like flowers and trees it can be interesting for the rest.

Title: Enjoyable location
Text: Only spent one hour at these gardens which isn't enough. We walked around the fernery and Japanese garden, nice but not as impressive as the Royal Botanic Gardens. If I was in the area again I may visit but only if it was flower blooming season

Title: Lovely Place to stretch and enjoy
Text: Lovely garden full of a huge variety of trees, flowers and ferns. Plants from all over the world layer out in a beautiful park. Could walk around in this park for hours. It's excellent for strolling and away from crowds. Chinese garden is peaceful and fern garden enchanting. If you get as far as Nuwara Eliya, this is a "must see and enjoy"

Title: Absolutely worth to visit!
Text: This garden was actually a big surprise. It is much bigger than Victoria Park in Nuwara Eliya and as plentiful of different species. There are many trees from all over the planet. Sometimes you run into monkeys. A pitty is that visitors feed them with chips and other food. Hopefully the management will end such things soon.

Title: Visit during flowering season (April)
Text: It's a nice garden and reputed as one of the 'must visit' places in Nuwara Eliya. However, the gardens which used to flourish with flowers during all seasons is more of a rain forest nowadays. December visits can get crowed and the entry fee of 200 Rs is  an unwelcome addition.

Title: Peaceful gardens
Text: Ask to book the golf cart if raining or difficulty walking long periods.  The cart drivers are very knowledgable so worth the commentary.

Title: Large botanical garden
Text: this large garden supposedly the ashok vatika described in the Ramayana, is a large botanical garden. Good for stroll. has large rose garden and fern garden.

Title: Most educational and enjoyable experience!
Text:
My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Sri Lanka and whilst travelling from Sigiriya to Kandy earlier today we stopped at Ranweli Spice Garden.

This proved a most enjoyable experience as our visit started off with a guided tour around the extensive spice garden. We were then given a thorough explanation of all the various products followed by a choice of short massages (I went for the neck & shoulders option which was professionally delivered).

This was followed by a visit the Product outlet where - without any undue pressure - my wife made a few purchases.

All in all, this was a most enjoyable experience and - although there is no shortage of choice - I would have no problem in recommending Ranweli Spice Garden to others.

Title: Interesting
Text: We stopped here for lunch and had a lovely curry buffet. Opportunity to tour the spice garden and make purchases at the shop.

Title: When knowledge meets humor
Text:
We wanted to visit one of the spice gardens while we were in Sri Lanka and during our day in Kandy we decided to give this one a try. Boy were we lucky. We had a wonderful experience. Our guide Asanka showed us around even though it was pouring rain. We ended up under the roof where we chated old friends, while enjoying some black-cinnamon-vanilla tea. Asankas humor might not be for the ones that are quickly offended, but we had a blast listening to his stories. In the end we were shocked to hear that the whole tour was free of charge!  
Also the shop in the end is definitely worth a visit! They sell high quality products which would be way more expensive in Europe and of poorer quality. We bought some ceylon cinnamon sticks, nutmeg, curry powder and vanilla extract. Cant wait to start cooking with this at home. 

Thanks for bringing sunshine into our rainy day in Kandy!

Title: Very Good Experience
Text: On the way from Kandy to Colombo we visited the herb garden. Great tour and very informative.  If you want to know something more about spices; it would be really pleasure to recommend it for you. Nice atmosphere and nice people. Just a very good experience. Thank you!.

Title: Knowledgable Guide/Great Experience
Text: Our guide was very helpful and knowledgeable.  I learn so many cool things.  We were able to see cinnamon, nutmeg, cocoa, coffee, turmeric, chili, pepper, citronella, aloe vera, curry leaves, cloves, and cardamon.

Title: Entertaining Experience!
Text:
First, make sure you go to the CORRECT New Ranweli Spice Garden.  Then enjoy the charismatic Asanka as he leads you around an attractive and informative spice garden.  No hard sell, products are reasonably priced.  Best cinnamon I've ever had in my life. 
Come back and enjoy his responses to incorrect TA reviews.  Don't forget to ask how they keep the monkeys away!

Title: Organic
Text: I loved it because everything is organic. The tour guides are well informed and share valuable information. The tour is free but believe me, youre going to be spending a tidy sum on products after unless you have a tight hold on your wallet. The tea is refreshing and delicious

Title: Great find
Text: We visited here yesterday and were enthralled by the chap that took us around. We were guessing what the plants were from the look and smell and were told what healing powers each plant has. Its free to walk around and you give a tip. I had a head massage whilst there too. Would recommend

Title: Good experience
Text: Such a good place to visit .Guide explained us in details about all the trees and plants and there uses in life

Title: Interesting garden...go in a group though
Text:
We were really looking forward to visit a spice garden whilst we were in Sri Lanka as weve heard so many good things about the wonderful spices that grow here.
Although we werent disappointed by the spices themselves, we were disappointed by the lack of professionalism on the guides behalf. He seemed very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the spices, but completely ignore our personal space by shoving various spices in our faces to taste and smell. When we were in the shop, he was really pushy in trying to get us to buy the products and followed us all around the shop.
I also think he took advantage of the fact that it was just the two of us there (my friend and I, two girls) and was rather inappropriate. When he showed us the citronella spray he offered to put a bit on our ankles, but after doing so he started massaging it into my calf and carried on higher to my keen. I think he would have carried on if I wouldnt have stopped him. At the end of the tour he wanted to have a selfie with us and when he took the picture he touched my friends behind. We both felt anxious and couldnt wait for the tour to finish so we could go.
If you do visit the garden, I would recommend you go in a group as the above is probably less likely to happen. Safe travels!

Title: Excellent tour
Text:
This is the best thing we did in Kandy. 

Joshua gave us a very informed tour of the spice garden. It was really interesting to see spices that we use daily in their natural state. 

Afterward he explained the medical uses for each spices. 

The tour is completely free, and the shop at the end is filled with very well presented spices, cosmetics and remedies. 

Its a twenty minute tuk-tuk from the lake, and is very close to the Royal Botanical Gardens.

Title: Its a shame about this place.
Text:
I definitely was up for listening to someone tell me about all the spices they grow in Sri Lanka. I was definitely up for someone telling me about how they are used in medicines, creams and beauty products. I was not up for someone following me around in the shop as I browsed.

In fact, the worst thing you can do to a European, is to follow them around in a shop encouraging/advising/pressurising  not sure what it was but it made me uncomfortable  them to buy things.

I would change things. Give people a card with the name of the guide that has taken them around the gardens, they can then browse at leisure and present their card when they make their purchases.

Everyone can then get their cut and the customer has a much better experience and may even buy more as a result.

Title: The best spice garden
Text: Lots of drivers stop here as this is the best spice garden .A guide will show you how the spices grow and show you examples of their raw state and when they have been dried .I had an excellent knee massage but others  were offered  a shoulder massage .

Title: Not to be missed
Text:
We have had the loveliest morning at the spice garden. Our guide was delightful and very passionate. He taught us a tremendous amount too.
 At the end of the tour, we were given examples of the remedies available along with a tea. Which was delicious.

Title: Quality time at New Ranweli Spice Garden
Text: My husband and I visited New Ranweli Spice Garden in January. It was a very relaxing and pleasant tour. We learned about spices and a lot of different herbs. I wasn't feeling very well when we arrived because  we had a 5 hours drive and I got car sickness, but a nice gentleman gave me a neck and head massage and made me feel better in a couple of minutes. At the end of our visit, we stopped to the shop. We did not bought anything at that day, but came back the next day after our two days Kandy city tour was finished and bought some good quality local products for us, our family and our friends.

Title: Very good moment
Text: Very good moment in the spice garden. Our guide was very passionate by the spices and we learn a lot of things.I really recommended and it's very near the botanical garden

Title: Interesting
Text: Nice tour and something different to do. Tour guide was knowledgable. There is an expectation to buy after the tour, but its all affordable so we didnt mind. Got some nice cinnamon and citronella

Title: Great experiecne
Text: Very friendly and honest guide who showed us interesting things we never knew about plant. Very much recommend this spice garden

Title: Excellent Service
Text: I ordered product from the New Ranwelli Spice Garden earlier in the year and have just reordered. They are very professional and helpful plus very quickly processed the order. I paid by PayPal and the bottles arrived within a few weeks. I have no hesitation in recommending this company with the quality of their products and safe reliable service

Title: Email ahead and get the pick up
Text: We visited new ranweli spice garden as part of our kandy tour. After Having misled by a couple of tuk tuk guys we decided to email the staff at the spice garden and we received a quick reply from a person named Asanka. We emailed spicegardencli@gmail.com. We arranged a place to meet in kandy and Asanka came on time and picked us up and gave us an amazing tour. For my money this was the best thing we did in kandy. The tour didn't stop at the spice garden he even took us to a place where traditional masks are made this was a bonus. Anyone  who plans to visit this place I suggest you email them and get their free pick up from The town.

Title: The ONLY Spice Garden that isn't BS or pushy around Kandy, Sri Lanka
Text: We researched which spice garden was the best and found most/many were extremely pushy and sold lower quality items that "took" tourists. So we found this place and went. Our tour guide was Asanka and he was great! He was very funny and knew his stuff. He seemed to really care about the quality of the items and knew his stuff. He was NOT pushy and we bought what we wanted. The tour is as slow or fast as you want, it's not crowded there and is very natural. We were fascinated and loved it all. Looking forward to using or spices - this is the ONLY place to go!

Title: Traditional medicine
Text: An amazing place. Peace, perfect peace. Had a head massage with oils. Fell asleep. Bought lots of things to take home. Wouldn't hesitate to go again

Title: Educational
Text: Even if you know what some plants benefits do, it is well worth the trip to find out more interesting facts about different spices etc that can benefit us humans.

Title: Only interested in hard sell
Text: Rushed around guide reeling of rehearsed bored script. hard sell at the end, shop prices extortionate. commission stop for tour guides, avoid if you can

Title: Most enjoyable and relaxing stop.  Highly recommend.  Four months after our visit I sent email about recording products.
Text:
Four American professional women from 34 to 70 enjoyed the tour of botanical specimens and learning their health properties.  The guide was knowledgeable and well spoken.  Our individual questions were answered about various 
treatments, and we received short botanical applications and mini facial massages.  We bought aloe and sandalwood.  In fact I am ordering more to be shipped.  

The aloe vera arrived well packaged and very well picked.. the service was really exceptional!

Title: Informative
Text:
This spice garden was visited after being recommended by a friend who made mention of Asanka.
We were fortunate that Asanka was working and he gave us a very informative tour of the garden including an explanation of the various spices and their uses.
There is an opportunity to purchase at the end but it certainly wasn't a hard sell.
Asanka speaks great English and enjoys good humour.

Title: Staff more interested in sales
Text: The garden appeared very big with plenty of herbs and plants. We were anxious to learn more about the plants and the uses as we have not seen most of them. But the guide that showed us around appeared to be more interested in selling the products than explaining about the herbs. So we left early.

Title: waste of time
Text:
I visit there last month.very bad expiriance.They pushing to buy something from there products and then when you buy they charge you like you buy a gold.There creams are not really working like they said.
But biggest problem with them is because they see the tourist only for money.

Title: Could not recommend this place more!
Text: Very accommodating with arranging pickup and drop off transportation. Asanka was very knowledgeable about the spices and we received great service with no pressure to buy at the end. Prices are very reasonable and quality of spices is fantastic. It is a real shame that a lot of people confuse these guys with the other Spice Garden that is in fact a tourist trap. We can assure you that they are not a tourist trap and would highly encourage that you contact them direct to avoid the tuk tuk drivers that take you to the other one. We nearly fell into that trap too with our tuk tuk driver when we first arrived in Kandy. We left this place with having learnt a lot about the spices and we willingly purchased some teas and spices without feeling like we needed to. Highly recommend!

Title: Worthwhile for me!  Found a Eczema medicine
Text: Interesting spice tour and found a eczema herb that cured my rash.   I actually visited the No.99 Ranweli but sure they all the same.  Except this one had a nice restaurant buffet, delicious in Kawdupelella, Matale, Sri Lanka.  Nice, complimentary tea and pamphlet describing all the spices and herbal medicines.  Overall, good but expensive herbal medicine.

Title: Very much designed to sell you products!
Text: You are offered a tour of the spice gardens - which could be interesting if there wasn't such a feel of being pressure sold creams and lotions of the products whilst being told how efficacious they are to everything from health to skin tone to correcting erectile disfunction ! There are very small bits of plants which are pointed out to you, as the medicinal properties are extolled to you. Trees are also grown for their uses - quite interesting  - but I wasn't keen on the man who showed us around daubing me with dollops of greasy creams that I had no way of keeping off clothes etc. I had to ask him not to do so - personal space is rather ignored here! so, all in all, limited appeal - more along the lines of the obligatory 'carpet factory' tour etc.

Title: Do not bother to hire tuk tuks
Text: This is my second visit to this place, this time I brought all my kids with me as this is really an educational stop. we visited the peradenia botanical garden first and exited through the suspension bridge and switched on maps.me .so could easily locate the place. Using maps and walking will save both money and the time bargaining with tuk tuk guys near the botanical garden. only thing is you need to find the suspension bridge and exit the botanical gardens and then switch on maps. but it is worth the effort.

Title: If you don't expect - you get more!
Text: So it was one of those stories where a tuk-tuk driver starts to sell to us all the excursions he had. But we were prepared and we've got everything planned beforehand. We were craving to see only Royal Botanical Garden, but our driver promised to drop us there right after we visit Herbal Garden (or Spices Garden). So it was opposite the Royal and same price for trip, we agreed. My amusement was hard to keep cuz it was nice decision. In all meanings! We were greeted by very nice guy who politely with extremely good English explained us everything what was held in his garden. Now we know how ginger grows, how it is gathered, what's its use and so on. We could smell/touch/wonder on everything : best cinnamon, carnation, citronella, aloe, cacao. Now I know what a hard work it is to grow and look after all that. I won't tell you all the secrets, but one thing you should know: now I'm super excited to come back home and cook using all those lifehacks. And by the way there is a nice boutique of super useful things such as cremes and sprays, spices, tea, perfumes etc. don't miss!

Title: An authentic delight!
Text:
We were shown around by an Ayurvedic doctor who was very knowledgeable and the tour was free. We would happily have paid for it.
   Walking in the garden, smelling all the oils and samples, and drinking our free delicious spice tea at the end - was very relaxing and a great way to spend the an hour or two away from the crowds. 
    The products in the shop were lovely. Beautiful wooden and woven boxes containing essential oils and spices...creams, perfumes, balms...We only bought a small bag of turmeric as we have 3 months left of our travel and small backpacks...But I wanted to buy it all for friends back home.
Take mozzy repellent!

Title: Very unpleasant!
Text:
Went there couple of days ago together with my girlfriend.. All i can say very bad experience with very bed storyline. Do you know that feel when you feel under pressure, when someone owns and spreads a very bad energy.. Looking you only as a person with dollar over your head. Feel when you are already dissapointed but must buy something.
This morning visited herbal/spice garden in Ella. Uncomparable...
Beautiful tour, garden, learnt a lot... Bought beautiful stuff and left with smile. 
DO it in Ella and not here or just go and write another review similar to mine. Cheers

Title: Spice garden with hard sell
Text: The tour of the garden was good and informative. We were then taken upstairs and handed a piece of paper with all the natural potions they made for different 'conditions' along with a pen to mark the things that may interest you.  We then were given a 'complimentary' massage ( head, neck and arms) and then taken to the shop.  We did bargain for the items we chose but didn't achieve very much of a reduction.  Felt slightly ripped off. Another holiday sales pitch unfortunately.

Title: Nice gardens
Text: We got there at opening and the medicinal herbologist wasn't there yet so we missed out on some educational points of interest. However it is a nice garden where you learn about medicinal properties of plants and some ancient recipes for teas, infusions, creams, and oils. Bring bug spray.

Title: Hidden gem
Text: Our driver took us here and I was wary of overpriced nonsense. Turned out to be a highlight. Who knew turmeric was a natural hair remover? I spent far too much money here willingly and with no pressure. Tipped the masseuse as was needing a massage anyway, enjoyed the little outing and got a lovely fresh coconut! Very much recommend!

Title: Excellent tour
Text:
As suggested multiple times in the forum by the management of this garden, please do take their tuk tuk pick up service. It is indeed very affectionate and kind of them to arrange this especially when it comes to tuk tuk scams. We emailed them a day before and Asanka, the guide, came right on time the next day morning. We were greeted and showed around this magnificent privately maintained spice garden by Asanka as he explained each product they make and how naturally the spices are grown, with live examples like smelling and tasting cinnamon, cocoa, aloe vera and others. We were given a free herbal tea and shown their products which was for sale in their store. No pressure in selling and we never felt we were being cheated or forced to pay for the tuk tuk or tour or anything. We willingly on our own purchased some of their products. They accept credit cards as well apart from Srilankan rupees. 
We inquired about a tea garden which we can visit next, to which Asanka suggested the Geragama Tea Factory and he offered us a tuk tuk ride to that place and introducing us to their tour guides. 
Overall, a very personal touch and a great tour, worth the trip and a must thing to do in Kandy. Appreciate the special initiative by Asanka who treated us extremely well.

Title: Informative and fun!
Text: First thing to say is that you should definitely email and arrange free pick up from kandy Town. Email spicegardencli@gmail.com. We arranged this the evening before and as promised pradeep picked us up from the arranged location. After a short walk up a dirt track the tour began and we really did learn a lot about all the different plants and spices. Pradeep was an excellent guide with a great sense of humour. We could have bought everything in the shop at the end but had to settle for our favourite fragrances. We also got a lovely herbal tea at the end. Pradeep then jumped in a tuktuk with us and dropped us (for free) at a tea factory for a tour which was also great. This should definitely be on your list of things to do in kandy! But definitely email! Highly recommended!

Title: Not worth a penny
Text: Basically a classical tuk tuk driver forced stop rip off. I found the same products (different brand, same containers) at the Kandy market for a 10th of the price. I totally discourage to buy.

Title: Interesting and informative
Text: Very informative tour, seeing plants and trees in their original state. However we did get bit a few times from bugs (despite wearing repellent)

Title: Good stop to see spices in their natural state (not in a bottle).
Text: There are a number of spice farms/gardens along the highway.  They all show a multitude of spices in natural plant form and treat you to a wide variety of amazing concoctions prepared from plants on site.  A fascinating educational experience if you like spices but don't often see them growing wild.  No fee to enter but they like to sell you something on the way out.  Very low pressure sales pitch.

Title: Amazing garden!
Text:
It was a great visit! It is a small garden with family atmosphere. Our guide explained and showed us plenty of spices and we were able to taste all of them directly from tree/bush.
After that he tought us about Sri Lankan curry and other products they are selling but in any momemt we didn't feel like we have to buy sth.
Prices are fair. Not cheap, not to expensive. In my opinion absolutely good value for the quality.

My suggestion to owners is to change the name to be easily recognised and reached. It is a shame that people are confused and then you're getting bed reviews.

Title: Scam
Text:
Attention all travellers Please avoid this place ! It is scam ! Outrageous prices for all products We only realised after we converted the cost of a packet of black pepper. This was about 20 x normal cost After we realised the ridiculous inflated price of that product I question the validity of all their products 
I will be writing to the government to complain as these places give the good Sri Lankan businesses a bad name

Title: Great free tour
Text: Had a great free tour by a girl whos first say it was and really interesting if your in the botanical gardens

Title: Great place to learn about spices!
Text: GREAT tour, very informative - I'd really RECCOMEND it if you want to know something more about spices. It looks like it is run by a family - NOT "commercialised", NOT 'touristy'. Nice atmosphere, nice people. There is no admission fee so buying something from their shop is a good idea to pay the people for their hard work

Title: Email ahead for the tuk-tuk pick-up and get the authentic(ally wonderful) experience
Text: Asanka is a knowledgeable and personable host, from arranging a tuk-tuk pick-up to explaining all about the spices around the small garden that he manages. We had a fantastic time learning, and exchanging our own experiences on medicinal uses of spices and beyond. A highlight of our time in Kandy indeed.

Title: LOVELY GUIDE
Text: We were taken here by our driver on the way to Nurawa Eliya - interesting spot and amazing what spices can be used for medicinal purposes.   Don't drive too much out of your way but if you are in the area go visit

Title: Asanka picked us up and gave us a wonderful tour of the spice garden
Text:
First of all: there are other spice gardens with similar names - this is the only good one. You should _ONLY_ visit the garden by contacting them directly and getting a tuktuk ride directly to the garden because it's easy to make a mistake and visit one where the people running the place will pressure you into buying things - which does not make for a fun trip!

So, on to the spice garden: Asanka was very helpful in picking us up near the tourist information centre in Kandy, we went via tuktuk and he showed us around the gardens explaining a lot about each spice we saw. I especially enjoyed seeing the pepper plant as I'd never really considered where all that pepper I eat comes from, and eating them fresh was amazing! We learnt a lot about the spices, and in particular we saw a cinnamon tree and learnt how different it is from the Indian version.

There was no pressure to buy, but we ended up getting more than 2kg of spices as we're big fans of cooking - the prices are not cheap but they felt reasonable.

I fully recommend visiting, but advise you to be very careful in making sure you do indeed arrive at the right place as apparently lots of people are visiting nasty places whose only aim is to exploit tourists, so for your own benefit make sure you contact them directly from their facebook page.

Title: Excellent after service when ordering once you get home
Text: The staff were so helpful and efficient when I called from Australia to order more of their Medanashi herbal tablets.  The tablets arrived within two weeks with no problem and they only charged $10 US for postage.  The product is designed to help lower cholesterol and it definitely works!  I will definitely be ordering more product from them in the future.  I cannot recommend them highly enough

Title: Thoroughly Intersting
Text: This was a great place to visit and learn about all the spices I use at home. Our guide was so informative.

Title: Interesting with a hidden extra!
Text: Visited this garden as part of a day out to other attractions. Small but interesting but there was an obvious drive to get you to the end to sell you products! Accepting cultural ways but also acknowledging the facts, ageing creams do not work! (None of us would look old if this was the case!). Note: the garden was riddled with mosquitoes and my wife received at least 20 bites in 15-20 mins. Apply your repellant before entering. Enjoy.

Title: Spice of life
Text:
A real interesting visit here ,a guide around the spice plants with informative information in relation to how natural plants can be substituted for other chemist medicines and food preparation.
So much explained it was hard to take it all in ,complimentary head and back massage which was very good .
At the end of tour talk a lot of people including myself visited the shop and purchased some of the items .I bought a oil rub and paste for arthritis in my shoulder and it still is providing some relief and benefit .
Overall a interesting experience.

Title: Get up to speed on natural remedies
Text: Lovely guy who took us around and explained the herbs, plants etc. which was very interesting and informative.  We found the experience uplifting to see alternatives to western medicine.

Title: The simplicity without pretence!
Text:
As thetitle of this review states: they don't have any false pretences here. But they simply show what they have on offer, and that is great. All spices which we generally use in the kitchen are grown here, Interesting.
They have as well a shop. But are not pressing you to buy. Which is nice.Such people deserve support.

Title: Interesting and informative
Text:
We were very pleased with to see the variety of plants at the the Ranweli spice garden, and our guide was very informative and entertaining in his tour. 

I would happily recommend this to anyone looking to see traditional Sri Lankan spices growing in their natural surroundings.

Also the tour is completely FREE!

Title: Authentic and informative visit
Text:
We found this spice garden at Tripadvisor and were very satisfied. There is no entrance fee and the visit takes apx. 1 hour.
The guide was very nice and funny, really knowledgable. Answered all our questions.
There is a small shop, where you can buy their products (spices, cosmetics, etc.)
We recommend.

Title: Friendly and interesting!
Text:
We visited the New Ranweli Spice Garden yesterday and loved it! The guys that show you around the garden are very knowledgable and we found it all really interesting. 

It is a small place just like their back garden but this was preferable to us.

There is no pressure to buy the products but to be honest with the enthusiasm they show and the friendly, warm atmosphere you are welcomed, these guys deserve it. 

A really good stop when visiting Kandy, we recommend!

Title: Interesting
Text: AN ok tour,saw lots of interesting things,guide good,passed a few hours.Had a pot of tea on arrival.Interesting plants and trees

Title: Worth a small detour
Text: Even though there is no signage (that  I could see) it's not difficult to find this little gem.  You'll see nutmeg, cinnamon and clove trees, vanilla and pepper vines and aloe Vera plants. Lots of packaged spices and products to purchase at very reasonable prices. Our guide was really knowledgeable and a very pleasant fellow.

Title: Small authentic spice garden
Text:
I'm not the kind of person who would go to a place and complain about small things but thought I would share this story. We all had originally planned to visit new ranweli spice garden kandy as part of our kandy tour. But my driver a nice guy ( at least we thought so ) recommended another spice garden that was a bit far away from kandy town. According to our driver the place he was going to take us was way better than any other spice garden in the city. We visited the spice garden  which I don't like to mention the name. and we were greeted by a guy at the entrance and the whole tour didn't even take 10 minutes. And then he took us to his shop. Good gosh the products were so expensive 200 USD for a small bottle of oil. ( where is the exit we were wondering) almost had a fight with our driver and We insisted to go to new ranweli spice garden. And we did after a big argument with our driver.
The tour in New ranweli was about one hour and the young man who guided us was very knowledgeable and answered all our questions. Also the products were much cheaper than the previous garden. If you want to visit a place in Sri Lanka never listen to the recommendations of your guide or driver do some research and read previous reviews follow the map and get to tour destination. Never be manipulated by your driver or the guide. Leave him at the vehicle never let guides or drivers handle your visits.

Title: Can be Better
Text:
While in Kandy we wanted to see Spice garden and happen to come across this. A difficult place to locate though in city . Narrow roads to reach. The person giving tour is very humble and knowledgeable.A small sample garden is there,the tress we saw there are-black pepper,Nutmeg,Clove,Rose Apple,Jack fruit,cinemon,cardamom,ginger,turmeric,Avacondo,star fruit.
They have small shop to sell spices and oil..

Title: An honest take on Sri Lankas spices
Text: Asanka the guide was a funny guy who led us through the spice garden - it looks like the backyard of someone's house but the authentic village setting of it all made it much more real and we enjoyed seeing firsthand what a cinnamon tree looked like, smell fresh nutmeg and learn how cloves and cardamom are processed. Very educational and a fun stop for a family with kids. As for buying the spices, they are of a superior quality and would cost more than those found at regular shops in town. It is a worthwhile trip all the same and the things sold in there are packaged well for gifts to take home.

Title: Wonderful visit
Text: Excellent visit. The tour guide was  clever helpful and very funny. 100% NO hard sell. They have a shop to buy spice ...but it's up to you if you want to buy anything. Highly recommended . thanks

Title: interesting place
Text:
It was interesting to visit this garden with my kids and having the chance to see everything growing in its natural state.
Monira, one of the garden employees guided us in the garden and showed us the different spices trees that grow in sri lanka in a very nice manner.

Title: Quiet, serene place
Text:
My husband and I went there in around afternoon time..

It was very empty and quiet..

However there were so many colours and interesting smells..

Got a view of many unsual plants..

However, the products they sell there were slightly highly priced...

Title: Smells are divine
Text: Lovely to see everything growing in its natural state, the smells of Sandalwood, Jasmine etc are really great and you can buy products in the shop which is a little on the pricey side but there is no obligation to buy.

Title: Interesting place to visit
Text:
Though the garden is not very big, the manager is very enterprising and took us through the various spices grown within the small garden in a very nice manner. They have a small boutique shop wherein you can buy the herbs/ spices. If you are in the area and don't have much to do, visit this place...
Ps . You might not be able to locate the garden on your own, hence call the number available on Google, response is good

Title: Money Making mind set
Text: Its like privately owned Spice Garden. From the onset your guide will start pitching for buying their products. Take a tour since it is well built and maintained but products are exorbitantly priced.

Title: Nice stop off
Text:
Actually surprised me how interesting the tour was. It was also fairly quick and covering a large amount of information, then you can get a free massage and see some products. 

Admittedly it is overpriced. The best bargains are for the large packets of spices rather than buying creams and ointments. 50p for a large pack of hot chilli is very good. However, we saw some creams for near enough £20 which is ridiculous. 

There is also a cheap restaurant which does a good buffet. Think it was only 500lkr each and food quality was a lot better than some hotel buffets we tried.

Title: Informative
Text: Any one interested in herbs and plants should visit this place to see how herbs and spices are grown and what are their benefits.

Title: Nice to visit but take care when you buy
Text:
It was nice place to learn and understand many facts about spice planets .. The local guide was nice we take a tour around and at the end of the tour they take you to the shop.
You have to avoid buying anything you will not use .. I end with few things but mostly I didn't use.
But I is wonderful place you should not miss.

Title: Great tour
Text: We had a great experience in the small garden. A guide with great humor, explained about the spices. Thank you Asanka for a great and informative tour.

Title: Interesting
Text: This was a very interesting tour and guide. I learned about the medicinal qualities of the different herbs and spices. The shop at the end of the tour however, was overpriced in my opinion.

Title: Highly recommend this special garden with great guide.
Text:
After a false start with a driver taking us to a different spice garden and then telling me the Ranwali was closed - and me insisting that we be taken to the Ranweli (I had been there years ago and knew it was the wrong garden) we arrived later than expected. 
Our guide was knowledgeable and interesting, with good English and a good sense of humour. 
2nd visit and it was as good as I remembered. 
Nice range of products for sale - but no pressure to buy.
Good Job guys.

Title: A gem of a place tucked away like someone's back garden
Text: As Sri Lanka is renowned for its cinnamon we wanted to see it growing and also buy some cinnamon oil. Our guide took us to Ranweli, which appeared like a an allotment in the centre of a residential area. However we were handed on to a guide who was very good, he was eloquent and amusing and showed us all of the spices growing on their plot (cinnamon, black pepper, nutmeg, mace, cardamom, vanilla etc). A small 'shack' was the shop which we managed to purchase far more than we set out to, whilst he prepared a herbal tea.

Title: Must see in your Kandy trip
Text: The place offered a nice variety of herbs and spices, and they also explained and gave us massages with different oils which was very soothing. The caveat is that they take you to their shop which sells very overpriced stuff, and you're kinda obliged to buy something. So better to enjoy the experience and not buy stuff from there

Title: A definite must do in Kandy!
Text:
This was one of the highlights of our Sri Lankan trip! 

It was amazing to see how these spices are all grown and getting to try them fresh was just amazing. Our tour guide Joshua was so informative and answered all our questions really well. 

We found the spice garden easy to find. We were at the Royal botanical gardens and exited through the suspension bridge (the suspension bridge said no entry on the gate to get through but you can go through there) once out of the park you cross the road and go up that street (it looks like a driveway). Just follow the google maps directions. It only took us 10 minutes to get there. 

We couldn't believe that it was free. We learnt so much and really want to grow our own spices now.
They had cinnamon, vanilla, cacao, cardamom, citronella, cloves, pepper, nutmeg, tumeric and many more!

We were given a try of their spiced tea which was amazing! We bought some to bring home and it made it through Australian customs no problems. 

I highly recommend checking this place out.

Don't let tuk tuk drivers take you anywhere else as apparently there is some sort of scam where they take you to another one. 

Thanks so much guys! Keep up the amazing work!

Title: You need a car or tuk tuk for this visit.
Text: Everyone we asked for directions thought we were talking about the Botannical Gardens, even though we showed them New Ranweli Spice Garden with the address written down. The bus driver nodded confidently and told us it was our stop at the Botannical Gardens . No one we asked knew where the spice garden was. We rang the Spice Gardens and were told to look on Google Maps, but the directions were through the Botannical Gardens. We almost gave up until a tuk tuk driver took us there. It is quite a way from the entry gate of the Botannical Gardens as it is behind it and certainly well hidden. We thought the spice garden grew spices in commercial quantities and processed them but you are shown individual plants of ginger, turmeric, vanilla, curry leaf plant, cacao, cloves , pepper, aloe Vera, citronella and cinnamon. Then you are taken to a table with all the packaged products for sale and a printed sheet with over 20 uses of herbal treatments. We were then shown into the sales room with the products for sale. The young man who told us about the spices was very pleasant and informative. The time taken there was a little over an hour.

Title: Well worth a trip
Text: We found it so interesting to see and understand how all the spices grow. The owner is extremely interesting. It's only a short walk from the botanical garden and easy to get by bus from Kandy. We were offered a sample of the tea and it was delicious so had to purchase.

Title: Great tour with welcoming guides
Text: We really enjoyed our visit to the spice garden. One of the spice garden tour guides personall met us in kandy city center and we were able to experience both public buses to get there and a nice walk through nature. When we first arrived it was raining a lot so they postponed the tour until it stopped and never seemed in any rush to complete the tour or have us buy anything. The tour was super informative, our guides spoke fluent english, and he answered all of our questions. We got to see and hold the actual parts of the plant used to make spices and even try some to eat. He also mentioned health benefits of each spice. After tour, they showed us many aruvedic products made from the herbs but never pressured us to buy anything. They then sat and chatted with us about just life in Sri Lanka which was really awesome. Overall, very welcoming guides who were very excited to share with us their knowledge In a very pretty part of Sri Lanka. Also prices were reasonable for spices.

Title: Amazing herbals
Text:
If You are here it's important to try They herbal balm. My whole famili just love it :)
It was great experience

Title: Top thing to do in Kandy
Text:
Very interesting visit in a nice spice garden. There is a lot of different plants to see. The guide is very friendly and interesting. He speaks a perfect english and even some french. We spend one hour in this garden and it was amazing.
And all of this is free !! Of course, they show you their shop at the end with very interesting products. I strongly recommend you to do it (just give the number to the tuk tuk driver because it's a bit hard to find)

Title: Avoid - Another tourist trap
Text: The garden is interesting with a guide taking you around and handling leaflet on different types of herbs available for sale. You better off buying the herbs and spices in normal supermarket. The sandalwood oil was exorbitant, the sales person was trying very hard to push it to us. Not worth a visit .

Title: Good for a visit but don't buy
Text:
We went as part of a Kandy tour. It was quite an interesting half an hour and although they say you are not pressured to buy anything we did feel this way. We bought some items but then found them also in Kandy market at about a tenth of the price.

All in all, not a bad way to spend half an hour, but save your money and buy the products at the market.

Title: IS JUST A SCAM, CLASSIC CABLE TV SELLERS PITCH TO SELL YOU CHEAP OIL WITH GOLD PRICE
Text:
GOOD: Nothing, is not a serious place like a real spice factory or something. The guys there they don´t know anything about herbs or ayudervic stuff. They play with the fact we western know even less about it. hahaha. But you can spend a great time playing you are a innocent western with them. 

BAD: Everything. 

We went because the tuk tuk driver they all are connected so basically they don´t push you to go but.. since there is not too much to do there you accept. The truth is nothing more than a tourist trap to try to sell you miracles. 

The guides are locals who tells you they are ayurveda students. You don´t need to be super smart to realize the huge amount of crazy facts they say. They just focus in try to sell solutions to all (what they think)  the western people problems: grey hair, old skin, fatness, neck pain... 

If you feel like having a good time I strongly recommend to play with them for example saying: oh really? I´m also studiying Ayurveda!! and then see their expresions.. hahaha. They don´t have a clue about Ayurveda is, they just want to make some money taking benefits of our western approaching to alternative medicine. I remember when he tolds me: how old are you? 37? you hace some grey hair, you know.. is because the stress...you have 2 layers in the head skin.. so one layer is dead.. blablablabla . And I say him: Damn I want to keep my grey hair, I totally love my grey hair!! Was funny his face afterwards. 

So, everything is focused to the shop they have selling super expensive oils (I bet the same oil solution in every bottle but differents tags). They are not aggresive or something but they will try you to buy some stuff and pay 50 $ for cheap oil which contain more than 200 herbs and.. blablabla

Title: Beautiful place, informative guides
Text: We had a great time here - finding out about all the different herbs and spices and their uses was amazing and our guide had been studying herbal medicine for 12 years so was an expert on the subject. We got to try out some of the lotions and potions like the hair removal cream which was amazing! Ended up buying some of the King coconut oil and having used it now, it works really well - my hair is so soft! A really good experience and not something we would've usually done so worth a visit even if you're not into plants!

Title: A good sales pitch
Text: If the focus had been more on explaining how the spices work, what they were useful for and so on it would have been a good way to pass an hour or so. As it was there was a cursory trip to look at the spices growing, 10 minutes, then a ten minute sales pitch/demonstration resulting in the hair remover actually removing a large patch of hair from my leg. I would not rush back.

Title: Interesting hour of your time
Text: We found the spice garden tour very enjoyable and informative, very nice cup of herbal tea and had a nice massage and it was lovely and of course into the shop and yes we did succumb and buy some products, which were very expensive, but you know you need them ?

Title: This trip was very educational to my children and to myself.  The tour guide was brillant.
Text: This experience will always linger in our hearts for many many years to come.  The knowledge and expertise shared was just amazing.  It was a truly educational journey through the roots and stems and trunks and leaves and flowers.  The divine smells and taste ...the aroma will linger deep in our hearts forever..

Title: Pleasant enough visit and interesting to learn about the plants, but so expensive.
Text:
Our driver stopped here, and we were taken on a tour by a 'doctor'. 

The talk was very interesting and it was nice to see all the different plants, learning the source of some common spices that we use in cooking. 

The claims made were at best spurious, at worst dangerous, but as long as you take them with a pinch of salt you should be ok. 

Avoid the free massage, as its not free, and before you let them fill your shopping basket in the shop,  ask the price and do the conversion. The oils are extremely expensive.

Title: Happy and interesting visit
Text:
We found our visit to the Spice Garden very enjoyable  yes it is tourist orientated and yes you are expected to buy the products but we still saw how the spices grew and we loved the products we purchased. 

First of all you are taken on a short meandering walk through a cross-section of spices and at designated points are shown products made from the different plants. After the short walk you are taken to an open air theatre area where, whilst enjoying a herbal tea, you are given an explanation of all the different products available to buy. The offer of a free massage is then made  excellent but it is expected that you give the masseurs a small tip. Its then on to the shop to make your purchases.

Title: Informative and enjoyable
Text: We found the spice garden tour very informative and we enjoyed our small cup of herbal tea and sampling the jackfruit. Had a small massage and it was lovely and of course into the shop and yes we did succumb and buy some products. Purchased the hair removal cream and now my legs are smooth and hairless, products were expensive.

Title: Nice garden
Text: This is a nice garden to see how all the spices are grown. You might not be able to get to see some plants like Cocoa etc else where so easily. But totally commercialized and you are made to buy not so quality products at a high price.

Title: Interesting but be prepared for hard sell technique
Text: We had a lovely lunch at the restaurant across the road before touring the spice gardens. The guide was very nice and it was interesting to view the spices in their natural state. The talk on the benefits of their products and getting you to circle the ones that relate to your ailments is a precursor to pushing those products on to you at the shop. We bought some cough syrup and a herbal balm. The cough syrup did not live up to the claims given but the balm is very good for a natural product. Their products are very expensive. It was good to see the coconut husks used for creating retaining walls.

Title: Spice garden
Text: We as Indians were very much aware of the spices around, but it was informative on which spices are to be used for what, a nice head & hand massage & a coco drink was very much nice. The entry is free, but the guide would expect a tip for whatever he would explain. The products sold are a bit expensive & is not worth paying.

Title: Pushing to sell their creams
Text:
A few things to say here. Entrance was for free. We were taken here as part of our Kandy tour (which we booked).
We got a tour through half the garden. It was interesting to see how the spices really look like and what you can do with them. Because the guide will explain which natural medicines they make out of them. 

All seemed ok, until the end. Then we were brought into a little room with some benches, and we were given a form with all of their creams and where they are good for. 
The guide would explain some things again on all medicines. After which you could mark on your form what you found interesting.
After that, the couples / people in our group were escorted one by one into their shop (why  I do not know) where they tried to push the creams onto us. 
We bought nothing though. They pushed too much, and the prices were way too high (compared to super market, or the little shop in our hotel). They would give no discount either. 

Fun fact, all of their creams works 100% guaranteed. 
They can even help you of your gout, osteoporosis, and all kinds of stuff.

All in all: 
a) If you have seen one spice garden, you have seen them all. And this one here is no difference - just different spices. 
b) In this specific one, all is focuses on selling. Where I wonder if they can live up to their promises.

Title: RECOMMEND A VISIT TO THE SPICE GARDEN
Text:
The guide was excellent explaining all about the herbal trees and 
how we can use it on daily use and the use also for holistic medicine.

Title: Interesting but........
Text: Interesting with regard to seeing / hearing about the various spices but, far too much accent on selling various "wonderful" treatments that make use of these products.

Title: Good sample of local spices, explained
Text: The spice garden visit fit in well with my schedule, as I visited the excellent botanical gardens nearby. The spice plants are a very realistic sampling of  local spices for  foodd and herbal medicine, and the explanations given were an appropriate length with some good info-- as I was familiar with some of it, and I was alone, I was able to discuss some aspects, and the person showing me the garden turned out to be quite knowledgable -- he was not just giving me a memorized spiel. Also samples of the fruits to taste and spices to smell were worthwhile. Of curse I expected that products were sold -- in fact, Iam the one who asked. The presentation of the herbal medicinal products was very brief although sufficient to give a quick idea that was supplemented by a sheet with fuller explanations, and I was not pressed or rushed into buying. I bought a couple of things that I had been meaning to get anyway. I am usually quite skeptical of such attempts to get me to buy, but this time I was pleasantly surprised, enjoyed the little tour, learned some stuff, and overall found it a worthwhile addition to my visit to the botanical gardens.

Title: Great impromptu massage - for a £2 tip
Text: Not quite as good as the one we visited in Goa India, however still worth the visit and went as part of an organised tour with Mercury Direct.

Title: Visit to the Herb & Spice Garden - April 2017
Text:
Our driver, friend and guide Hetti of Hetti Tours Kandy took us to New Ranwell Spice Garden during our Sri Lankan holiday

Ranwell was a wonderful tranquil oasis and we had a guide who was extremely knowledgeable. I would highly recommend a visit. We were there for less than an hour but could easily have spent 1-2 hours.

I purchased some oil and herbs for an arm injury and using it over a period of about a month has virtually healed this arm. Expensive but very very well worth it.

Title: highly recommended
Text: i sent them an e-mail before going and the reply was quite prompt and very helpful! The place is a bit hard to find but once you get there, they are most informative and respectful. Their siddhartha oil is THE BEST!!! Will definitely be going back! :)

Title: interesting place
Text: We enjoyed the walk through the garden and the education on the plants and trees growing there. Did not particularly enjoy the time spent after the walk while our tour guide pitched all of the stuff they sell.

Title: Interesting visit to this small spice garden
Text:
The tour around the garden was free. But of course it was somewhat encouraged to visit the small shop - the encouragement was however very subtle. 
It was quite interesting to hear more about some of the spices from the local kitchen. And to learn that apparently many of the spices can cure you from whatever ... diabetes, arthritis, grey hair, diabetes etc. The staff and the guide was very friendly and eager to tell about the spices. 

We took a tuktuk from the city center of Kandy for the price of 600 LKR (one way). The driver offered to stay there and wait for us and drive us back to Kandy for 1.500 LKR in total - I'm pretty sure the last offer was a very good deal for him...

Title: Just a sales pitch
Text:
It would be nice to wander the garden and learn about the spices.   But this is a sales pitch to sell herbal remedies.  These remedies can apparently cure everything and have no side effects.  The guide kept wanting to tell us his CV.  How clever and trained he was in natural therapies.  -  Well not trained enough to know that no treatment - No treatment is free of side effects.  
Eventually I had heard enough of this insult to my intelligence and returned to our car.

Title: Interesting and Informative.
Text: Saw a lot of spices as well as Coffee and Cocoa grown. The guide explained all the different bushes and trees growing there.Found it quite interesting and informative. At the end we were asked if we wanted to go to their shop. There was no compulsion for us to buy anything.

Title: Same old thing
Text: Nothing special. Guided through the various spices etc. and then, not surprisingly, through into their shop. The items I looked at, seem similar to that Which could be bought in town for less.

Title: Very informative visit
Text:
Went to this place as it's near the hotel and based on the positive tripadvisor reviews.

Well worth the visit and I concur  good reviews and also with the management replies to some of the bad ones (perhaps reviewing the wrong place).

Our driver had trouble finding the place as it is tucked out of the way.  When we arrived I thought we were going to be wasting our time as it was quite a small place.

However, it was very enjoyable.   The guide was very friendly, knowledgable and helpful.  We learnt a lot. For instance mace is the covering around a nutmeg nut.  Loads of different spices to see, touch and smell.

There was an opportunity to buy, which we did, but there was no hard sell. 

A great way to spend an hour.

I was told by our driver that there are much bigger places that we will see later in our tour but this is worth a visit if you like cooking and want to learn more about the many spices we use all the time, e.g. Pepper, cocoa, cardamom, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and mace.

Title: Awesome Spice Garden
Text: We were brought to the spice garden on a whim and we couldn't believe everything growing! I had no idea what many spices looked like before they were put into jars; it was very interesting and eye opening. Of course, afterwards, you are explained the health benefits of each spice in great detail, and then given the opportunity to buy products, straight from ground to bottle. I now have the best vanilla and cinnamon ever, thank you!

Title: Charming and informative visit
Text:
It's worth a visit to this enchanted spice garden. You receive a personal and interesting guided tour through the small family run garden which showcases spices and herbal medicinal plants. Lots of interesting points made on the uses and benefits of each one. We enjoyed our free tour with Asanka who obviously loves working with nature. Afterwards we were shown a range of products for purchase. The dark roasted curry powder is an authentic Sri Lankan mix which comes with a recipe and it's delicious! Also hand made incense, various ointments and essential oil. 
This is not a big commercial venture so it has a much more friendly and uniquely Sri Lankan feel to it. Very enjoyable!

Title: A really interesting visit
Text:
The Ranweli Spice Garden is a little off the beaten path and is a real garden, no a tourist trap. Our guide showed the two of us around discussing each of the various types of trees, their spices and uses. He was very informative, extremely pleasant and appreciated the fact we already knew quite a bit about some of the spices because we
cook with many of them. There is no admission charge. Our driver/guide took us their at our request. There is a boutique where you can buy various spices and products but we were not pressured to purchase.  We spent about an hour there.

Title: Best unprompted massage ever
Text: Not as long a visit as I'd expected, thats not to say it wasn't interesting and informative, it was all of that, worth a visit

Title: A must!
Text: The tour is interesting and the staff are well informed and did a great job in informing us about every plant, spices, oils and many remedies. At the end of the tour, they offer you a free massage using natural oils and you can taste a selection of tea and hot chocolate, and then you can go to the store to purchase spices, oils, lotions and other things.

Title: awesome place
Text: it was really nice. we had a very polite and professional guide who took us in a very rich tour and we had massages for few minutes and then went to their drug store and bought some  oil for back pain and some diet supplements and we had the best spice tea ever.

Title: Nice  place can be visited once
Text: We  can see spice plants  and  variety of  herbs here. This is a  good place  for nature lovers  as well.  The attendents/guides   will explain  the name of the plant  and their uses.

Title: Tourist Trap
Text:
Our driver brought us to this place although it wasnt included earlier.

I could feel it was a trap especially the guy when he knew I was Arab, he started to speak with Gulf accent thinking I'm coming with the Oil.

I didnt believe anything of what he said and tried to control my wife from buying stuff but still we spend some money there.

Then we were taken around the garden while there was a close way to our car but this was to give a chance for the driver to go grab his commission.

Please don't go to that place ever as they are ripping tourists.

Title: Enchanting Aroma of Fresh Spice & Aroma
Text: Got to touch & feel the different spices, the benefits of the spices, herbs. Got a goods massage which was a lot of relief to the tiring trips of walking around seeing places. We had an excellent Orator Mr. Chaminda who briefed us on the various herbs, the benefits of each herb & their medicinal properties. We bought a few of the Natural medicines from the store. Will review them when we get back & if required will definitely order more for our use.

Title: spice garden or a shop
Text: These people will take around the spice garden and show different type of spices. Then there will be a demonstration of their products for different kinds of health problems. I do not know whether they are effective or not but these products are really costly.

Title: Its a grocery
Text: We get there and expected to see a national spice garden made by foreign affairs but once we reach there we recognize that the driver and the person who work there 55 years old and he was arabic speaker. 5 min after the tour once he recognized that we will not buy there products he stopped the tout are became angry. And at the end he asked us to give him money as a gift. Come On!!!!

Title: Natural spices and herbal treatments
Text: This was a great place. It's free to get in. And a guide takes you through the the garden and educates on all the spices for healing,and eating etc. The have a huge variety of plants. All gown right there in Sri Lanka. Then the uses for each was great. After a walk through there is a sit down and the guide explains the mixes and their benefits. There is an instructional sheet. Also a 10 minute massage of the neck and shoulders with the oil and balm. This took me back to the olden days where everyone made their own types of meds, cures etc. The tour ends with the shop/ pharmacy to purchase any of their products. We enjoyed this place so much. You won't regret it.

Title: Spice Garden - A trail of knowledge and fragrances
Text:
The spice garden is a treasure trove of knowledge and spice fragrances. The guide at the garden explains each of the spices and gives a detailed encounter of how each of these spices were introduced in the island country. The garden is very well laid out and covered with dense vegetation. The surroundings are calm and ocassionally intercepted by the calls of some local birds.
There garden offers a complementary Green tea drink and they also have a medicine shop / souvenier shop selling many herbal medicines, spices, tea etc.

Title: Fresh smell of spices!
Text: If you have time, then visiting the spice garden is a good option. You can see different spices, smell them and even buy them! Its all organic.
