Title: Spice garden
Text: There are many  spice gardens in Sri Lanka .they have all spice trees growing and they have their oils extracted for sale .but I don't know why they sell it very expensive .

Title: A fleeting vision our tour
Text: Would have loved to have had more time to see more of this fascinating garden, what we saw and were told was amazing

Title: A SCAM and a tourist trap!!!
Text:
It' was our first day in Sri Lanka we made a mistake converting the currency we didn't realize on the spot how bad it was!!!! After a visit in the garden, quite informative, you get a  "free" massage and then they take you to the shop where everything is 10-20 times overpriced!
Our driver took us there saying it's a short and free visit. It took for ever to get out of there and I learned later the driver get 20% commissions on what you buy...

Title: A spice world
Text: Nice visit and as usually a touristic place but worth visiting and to learn unknown facts about spice and some items are only available here only.

Title: Informative
Text:
An informative experience, nothing to write home about though, I didn't feel pressured to buy anything and we gave the guy a couple of hundred rupees for his time. 

It was ok

Title: Beware the shop
Text: Charming man Moses told us all about the different plants and what they are used for, proceeded to covered hut for more talk, massage and given sheets with recipes. Proceeded to shop, beware, debit/credit card machine here, very very expensive, a fool and his money could easily be parted here

Title: A tour through the magic of spices
Text:
Guided by a very wise and enthusiastic gentleman, we saw and heard about spices we had not previously encountered.
The shop was very interesting too.

Title: Just say no
Text: Yes my wife and did do tour which was nice and they gave her a back rub after buying over $150 of two items which were taken by customs.  Buyer beware. Buyer beware.  Shame shame shame.

Title: Very expensive with pressure to buy
Text: thought it would be some huge garden but turned out its a few trees. the tour was informative however not sure how true it was. They pressure you to buy at the end however everything is over priced. i ended up buying a few things which i regret now. highly not recommended.

Title: watch out, tourist scam!
Text:
You get a so called "free" guide. At the end he gives a "suggestion" how much you can tip him were they use the classical 'anchoring' trick (mention a very high rate; even if you pay half, you are still overpaying).

But by far, you are being scammed in the shop at the end of the tour. You pay here for "special" homepathic a insane high price; EXACTLY the same products can be bought for one fifth of the price in the city market.

This is nothing short of a full-blow tourist scam. The tuktuk driver receives 30% of anything you buy.

Title: Informative and a nice stop off.
Text: Stopped here as part of our two day tour with Asda Tours. Both myself and my mum, who I was travelling with, really enjoyed it. It was great seeing how different spices grow naturally and the tea and massage went down a treat. Of course they try and sell you their products. They are a business in a struggling economy and we did overspend....A LOT! This was our fault though, everything was priced clearly but our naff calculations worked out terribly and it wasn't until we had left we realised how much we had spent! My hubby will kill me when I get home....all I can say is work out the exchange properly...currently 199.00 rupees to £1.

Title: Fabulous
Text: To see and smell all of the spices for example cinnamon bark and all the different coloured pepper seeds growing naturally.....AWESOME....Again a must see.......SRI LANKA is my favourite holiday destination with so much culture......So don't miss out...

Title: Nice place, lots to learn
Text: This is a nice place, seeing all the plants and learning about their health properties. They are looking to sell their products which are great but quite expensive... free massage and tea though

Title: Auervedic spices
Text: Nice small spice garden near Kandy. Simple introduction to the compounding of auervedic medicines. Worth a stop if you are passing by but not worth going out of the way for.

Title: Mildly amusing and plants interesting
Text:
We stopped here en route to Kandy. It was ok; I enjoyed looking at the plants and the guy showing us around clearly knew his stuff. I enjoyed the spiced Ceylon tea we were given in a mini mug. I also enjoyed the awkwardness of my husband being given a massage with citronella rub!

They will try to run all sorts on you as you go round. I didn't appreciate being told that I should get the sandalwood cream because of my face (adult acne).

They do try a very hard sell in their shop. Just be polite and firm. It was a nice little stop and quite interesting. 
The buffet lunch place across the road was fairly reasonable too.

Title: too expensive, Not recommended !
Text:
We went there thinking it would be a real spice garden but they only have a few trees. They have a product made from every tree which they want to sell. We got interested in purchasing a few things but when we got into their shop - the prices were extraordinarily high - just a rip off. They even said we'll give you discount since you are from a SAARC country but even then the price were a rip-off. 
Not recommended !

Title: Beautiful garden with a variety of plants.
Text: The spice guide was very knowledgeable. We got a free massage at the end by students learning Ayurveda. We just gave them a nominal tip. The garden is beautiful, lush, and it is amazing to know that they make oils out of pineapples, cinnamon, sandalwood etc. and combos of various things. We did not buy any oils as it was very expensive. (For eg. Hair oil was SL Rs. 5000 for 150 ml.)

Title: If you've nothing better to do.
Text: It was ok, but the end result is they want you to part with your hard earned cash. Sure it is a poor country and you may wish to help out, but things are over priced...

Title: Everyone has a cut, even the driver who brought you there
Text:
The concept of taking the passengers to these gardens is not good in itself. They might make good products BUT they are soooper expensive so actually not worth it.

The tour itself is entertaining.. though

Title: Interesting and engaging
Text: Stopped here en route to Kandy. We were not expecting too much but actually enjoyed the tour, even the herbal tea tasting. We did buy, but with care. Surprisingly both our boys enjoyed it too.

Title: Interesting but don't feel pressurised to buy anything
Text: We stooped off here on the way to Kandy. The guide was informative as to how certain spices are used for ailments etc. we were given a cup of tea while walking around which tasted lovely.  Towards the end we were taken to a seating area and given a list all the things we had seen and we were then asked to tick each one we wanted to see a demonstration of.  This actually didn't happen and really a way of seeing what you would buy in the shop.  The shop is totally overpriced and the people did bag the items quickly and asked for money.  We were careful though and once we worked it out in sterling we said no.  THey did try to get us to buy other things but we stood our ground and actually they were ok with it.  WE did have a lovely massage by some lads who were apparently studying massage ((which we took with a pinch of salt). Overall good trip but more like a sales pitch.

Title: Interesting and Informative
Text: I found our tour of the spice garden to be very interesting and informative.  Being a gardener, I very much enjoyed seeing actual spice trees, vines, bushes.  I would have liked to have had a more in-depth lecture on the medicinal uses of many of the plants.  I experienced absolutely no pressure what so ever to buy anything!  I am now using some of my spice purchases and their aromas are to die for.

Title: Well oiled sales machine
Text:
We came here as part of a tour. It seems the tour company insisted we be delivered to them.
Tour of the garden was very interesting and there were a lot of plants we would not otherwise have seen. However, it was a short impatient tour where questions were clearly unwelcome. 
Main purpose was to get us in for a big sales talk and wheel us into the shop. I bristle at this type of business but the shop was busy. Buyer beware. I suspect your tour company got paid for bringing you so don't expect bargains.

Title: Spice Garden & Herbal Plants--Interesting to visit
Text:
New Ranweli Spice Garden is full of Spices and Ayurvedic Herbal Medicinal Plants. This is being well maintained. As a part of our itinerary, we visited this Garden and we were happy to be hear. The staff here explained in detail about the spices and their growth and also about the Herbal and Medicinal plants.

It is said that these plants are precious costume of Beautiful Nature. We came across some of the Ayurvedic medicines which is useful in relieving aches or pains such as severe Rheumatism, Arthritis, Knee pain, Spondilosis and pain in the backbone etc.

Apart from the above medicines, Cosmetic Combinations such as Aloevera Cream which can be used daily for Replenishes skin health restoring. The other items are Herbal Tooth Powder, Citronella,etc.

Many items, which were explained, were available for sale at the counter. Though appeared a bit costly, some of our people took it for their usage.

Title: Very interesting clip joint but worth visiting anyway
Text: Spent much longer here than intended, and despite being a clip joint it was quite fun and the guide was charming. We did buy one thing which was expensive but it seems to work, but we declined everything else. Quite educational, so worth a visit.

Title: fun and yes, overpriced
Text: The tour was sweet and we enjoyed the tour, however did buy a basket full of stuff that was very overpriced and we knew this but was our last stop. Even the airport has cheaper stuff and the nutmeg we got home appeared to not even be fresh. So it goes! Cute little place though. Enjoy.

Title: Nice Place
Text: An exciting and knowledgable experience to touch and feel spices ,nice garden but we did not buy things.

Title: Very nice and very informative
Text: We spent like an hour there, escorted by a nice expert. He gave fair explanation about everything there. Also I had a free short shoulders and nick massage. We bought many items from them.

Title: Don't buy anything
Text:
A local professor showed us around the garden and told us how each of the products was good for the body. Honestly he was really impatient and quite rude and he kept asking us to 'shhh' when he heard even a whisper from our group.
They provided a small cup of hot chocolate and 3-5 min massage for the head shoulder arms and palms.
We had lunch there ( i would not recommend) limited choices of food.
lastly they brought us to the store where they are overpriced. If you really want to buy visit pharmacies in colombo they sell it at a much cheaper price.

User_Location: Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: What spices?
Text: I'm not sure this place is really worth a visit. It was nice to walk around and smell the herbs, but often times it just looked like signs in the ground and you had no idea what you were actually looking at. For all we knew, they could have just been putting the signs anywhere and we would have believed it. After the tour, we sat down for an introduction to some of the remedies made from the herbs and spices. It was interesting but I felt like I was watching an infomercial. "This will cur your diabetes." "This eliminates cellulite." "You'll lose 10 kg if you take this 2 weeks straight." While I believe in the medicinal benefits of spices and herbs, it was a little frustrating to watch the crowd be so duped by the false promises. Later they take you to the shop where they try to sell you on all of those promises. The quality definitely seemed to be there, but I recommend doing your own research before assuming you'll grow back a full head of hair after 30 days using their sandalwood oil.

Title: Don't buy any thing
Text: Although place seems to be attractive and little bit of learning is their. But Don't  Buy Any Medicean from them, nothing works.

Title: Good experience
Text: We were here last week. Nice place to learn about spices and plants like cinnamon,cardamom,aloe vera etc.During the demo on uses of each plant we were given ginger tea. It was amazing!The guide takes u around an explains about the plants and how it is grown. U get to learn a lot in such a short time.At the end of the tour, they take u to a shop where there are plenty of medicinal ayurvedic medicines for treatment of joint pains,headaches,cholesterol etc. We bought some from here and also some spices.

Title: Appeals to the senses
Text: This was a pleasant place to stop off, wander and take in the aromatic herbs and spices. It wasn't, for us, a major attraction but is certainly worth a visit.

Title: Its free to get in but costs to get out.
Text: I actually enjoyed the tour and took lots of photos. Ok the guide was stressed but just don't let them stress you, take your time and enjoy. they have most of the plants and trees for spices that we recognise as powder, so it's quite educational if you enjoy botany. At the end of the trip is the shop. you know that when they tell you the tour is for free. I am a hardened traveller so it takes more than sweet talk and pleasant smells for me to open my money belt. A good trip and for my part it was free.

Title: Informative
Text: Pretty little place, talk from local expert quite informative if not a little rushed...at the end of the day, quite literally, it was nothing more than a selling game - pity really, but we all need to make a living! Don't purchase anything, just leave a donation or tip.

Title: Informative,  commercial and tourist alert
Text:
Of course no trip to Sri Lanka would be complete without a trip to the spice area north of Kandy.
I noticed a beautiful venue so immediately I knew what I was getting into. Tourist Alert! 
I was immediately approached at my car by a so called Salesperson.i asked up front the cost to enter and was told no cost, purchases are the commission they make.
The quick tour was informative and they had a man hike hi way up a coconut tree to fetch for a sample for the small audience he had. ( very touristy). We then sat in a hut and we're explained with a paper all the products to purchase. Short tour included a sampling go chocolate milk, spice tea and coconut water. 
Last stop was the store. Prices very inflated for European travellers. I did buy cardamon pods for 400 rupees which I know was expensive however I stopped intentionally for that purpose. 
I did see the disappointment on our salespersons face when I did not buy much. 
As I step into my car he approached and ask for 500 rupees. This was not shared at entry when I specifically ask so this was a turn off. 
So just be aware. Bottom line, Tour was informative and if you buy  there expect to overpay

Title: A decent stop without too much sales pressure.
Text:
Our driver suggested this place en-route from Habarana to Kandy and, though we were dubious (anticipating some kind of hard sell), we were getting bored and sleepy with the long drive so we figured we would just treat it as a rest break.

Once out of the car, we were offered the use of the restrooms and then a guide was assigned to us and he then spent the next hour taking us around the garden showing us some of the spices and other plants growing in the grounds.  There was plenty of te usual stuff you;d expect - cinnamon, nutmeg, aloe vera etc and it was actually kind of interesting.  At two points in the tour, we were offered tea which had various spices in it (e.g. cinnamon tea) which was nice and the guide obviously knew his plants.

At the end of the tour, they tried selling us a head and shoulders massage using some of their home-made ointments to which we declined (was thinking about lunch and heading onwards to Kandy) so we were then directed to the shop which was obviously always going to happen.  However, to my surprise, once in the store, there was no hard sell  - the guide did point  a few things out and hovered around but there didn;t feel like any real pressure to buy (although we bought a spice box as a gift for family).

After exiting the shop, we had lunch with our driver who recommended the fish curry (not a huge surprise as that seems to be the staple in Sri Lanka) but I was up for it so agreed and out came a multitude of dishes including curries, rice and other accompaniments.  The food was a really good and we all enjoyed it although I wasn;t massive happy about all the damned flies crawling over everything - at one stage the bowl of rice looked like a dessert with currants..  but anyway, there's probably not an awful lot they can do about it in the open.  we are also surprised to see the total food bill which worked out at around £12.. which, for so much food that three of us couldn't eat it all, plus drinks, was a steal.

So in the end, it was actually a decent stop.  There's approximately two million and forty spice gardens in Sri Lanka (made-up number obviously) so I daresay there's some good ones and some bad ones but this one seemed pretty good.

+ Interesting collection
+ Knowledable guide
+ Nice food and good value

- Bit of a soft sell
- Flies

Title: Unexpectedly good
Text: We dropped in here as we passed by, not expecting much...I really didn't have any interest in the place....however the guide started explaining all the different plants and it was really interesting! There is a bit of a push to buy at the end, and the guide will expect a tip...but the tour round is free and informative. We were offered head massages, which we refused, and am sure they would probably have charged you for after! All in all a good stop off on our tour.

Title: interesting insight into spices and your wallet
Text: we were tired when we were dropped here by our driver. We were shown around the small spice garden by a very informative guide. It wasnt busy and he spent time explaining the benefits and uses of all the spices. There were cures for everything and the concoctions tasted quite pleasant. There was an opportunity for a massage from a waiting Masseur but we were so tired the thought of one had not crossed our minds. After explaining all the spices there was a subtle attempt of waiting for a well deserved tip. Unfortunately we didnt realise what he was after until a few days later when we had finally come to our senses. The products were expensive in relation to Sri Lankan terms. We did purchase two items the hair removal cream he put on my hairy legs remained hair free for the entire holiday. The number six energy potion the equivalent of the verbal viagra we reluctantly purchased. We both took a teaspoon every day of the holiday and it may have been expensive but we thought it certainly had medicinal properties. Must get some more. Another opportunity at these places to extract the tourist of their cash but we were aware of that and only bought what we thought was fair.

Title: Buyer beware: Same spices cost far less in the local supermarkets!
Text:
Definitely a "tourist trap" where a short tour about spices is followed by a visit to the spice shop! On the day we visited there were more than 10 drivers/guides are waiting for their tourists (and kickbacks??) outside of the Spice Garden.   

A package of cinnamon sticks cost 150 rupees in the supermarket; it cost more than 10 times that at the Spice Garden (albeit the packaging is prettier).  

Something is wrong when the guide is selling spice-based tooth whitener and his teeth are yellow!

Title: Interesting to see Where our Spices Come From
Text:
Speedy tour of the growing area led us to a sales pitch for the spices used in medicine which was very expensive. 

We bought the cooking items but that was low on the guide's list of priorities.

Title: Not impressive
Text: In India it's more popular and widely available , so I was not impressed . Products they sell is also not worth they charge. I feel it was more like typical to visit

Title: Educational, worth doing
Text: This was a little tour of some of the spices grown in Sri Lanka.  It's not a sales tour: they don't try to pressure you into buying their products.  i live in NY, so all this stuff is available anyway.  But you will definitely learn about the spices.

Title: Not worth a visit
Text: As others have previously stated, its a nice enough small garden tour with some interesting information but how much of it is true.  The tour guides actually call themselves doctors and profess to offer all sorts of cures for all sorts of ailments.  But at the end of the day its all about selling.  I confess to buying but regretted it once I converted the rupees into £'s.  The spices are extremely expensive and you  could do better buying in a sri lankan supermarket.  As these places are government run why are the products so dear?  So I would say by all mean visit but we wary of buying.

Title: nice walk but do not buy
Text: we went to one of the spice gardens. The tour was nice and informative. the massage was also nice. of course in the end there is a lot of pressure to buy. just avoid this pressure and buy something if you feel like paying for the tour. there is ayurvedic shop in town on kandy street that sells all the products in a much better price.

Title: Very Interesting spice garden
Text: We were met by a guide at the entrance of the Spice Garden. He showed us the many species of differnt plants, vanilla, Jasmine, Aloe, Tumerick, Cardomon, Cloves, peppercorn and so many  many more. A truly must go place..Lots to learn and see.

Title: Very interesting and helpful
Text: My local tour guide, Hemantha, brought me to the Ranwell Spice Garden. I hadn't heard of it and I wouldn't have gone myself - I was even a little dubious when I got there. However, I was very pleasantly surprised. I got a great tour by a young gentleman - really informative and quite fun. I kept guessing the spices wrong but he was really nice and pointed out many more uses for each item than I knew (Tumeric is good as a cleaning product? Sandalwood whitens the skin etc). I was really interested in all the products that they offered at the end and I do think the actual spices were good value given that they are pure and produced onsite but the oils etc were quite expensive. In the end I bought two spices (spent approx LKR1000 which isn't much in the scheme of things). I would definitely recommend this place, particularly if you are interested in plants or cooking.

Title: just a tourist stop
Text: I would have wanted to see more of the plants etc. We skipped lots of boards and when you ask they just quickely say the name and that is it. Then you get the workshop... And they say several rimes the massage is free. but who will walk without tipping, so yes, you pay. I was with locals, and thay say that for the locals behind the tourists back they give it for halfprice, but the tourist board has fixed the prices. I couldnt afford anything. I just bought curry powder.

Title: Aromatic time to be had by all who visit
Text: Had a wonderful couple of hours learning all about the alternative uses of herbs and spices in well being. Had a fab facial massage

Title: The equivalent of a timeshare selling effort
Text: Pretty much all Spice Gardens (and there is quite a few of them, especially on the road between Kandy and Sigirya) seem to operate along the same lines: a quick / hasty visit of the gardens, followed by some "workshop" to demonstrate the virtues of their Ayurvedic gear and finally the mandatory visit of the shop where they'll make sure you buy some of their their grossly overpriced merchandise, i.e. not the cooking spices that are too cheap but the Ayurvedic rubs, ointments and else. They might also throw in a "free" massage at the end of which you'll be reminded not to forget to tip the guy who delivered it + the guy who gave the visit + pretty much half of the staff on deck. My advice, just STAY AWAY from any and all of them, especially if they are commended by you car or tuk-tuk driver (who will get commisioned wherever he takes you)

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
Although very touristy we find this very interesting.  A bit of explanation and trials of different products for about 40 mins. You could then sample some tea and a head massage if you wanted - we didn't have head massage but others there said very good. 
There is of course a shop on way out to buy products.  It is expensive but didn't feel we had to buy anything.

Title: Money making trap
Text: The tour in the garden was very quick. the main thing was a hard sell session with "demonstrations" of the products. There was a lot of pressure on us the buy the products from which I bought a few. Don't know yet if they are effective...

Title: Quick visit
Text: Our driver for the day took us here, enjoyed the walk around and was interesting to here the chat from our guide.  We were then given a free massage - would recommend this.  No obligation to buy anything - although the exit was through the shop and you can sometimes feel a bit embarrassed just passing through - however we didn't buy anything!  Lovely clean toilet facilities!

Title: Interesting but quite simple
Text: This small garden has quite a few spices in it but clearly the production and true growing area is elsewhere. The young man that took us around was very knowledgeable and friendly.

Title: Amazingly effective products!
Text: After a very informative tour of the garden we were given refreshments (tea or hot chocolate) while various products were demonstrated. Our scepticism was quickly overcome when my husband had a knee massage using some of the herbal balm. Whether it was the balm or the massage itself may be open to dispute but his recovery was almost biblical as after the 10 minute massage he was able to walk with more ease than he had done for months!

Title: Do not buy
Text: I fall on buying trap and spent more than $364. It is very expensive products and no warranty results.

Title: Free Head and Shoulder Massage
Text:
We were taken through the compound and shown a wide variety of spices and natural remedies.
The best part was the head and shoulder massage given generously by the on site masseurs.
I must admit that this was a bit of a softening up process hoping that we would be relaxed and would buy on the way out at the spice shop. 
We were and we did!
However, the tooth cleaning powder was excellent and we are still using it. Our teeth seem to be whiter and our gums healthier. Great stuff.

Title: Very informative - great visit, but don't be pressured to buy
Text:
We visited here at our request and were amazed to see the variety of spices and herbs grown and interested to hear the variety of remedies that can be be created from them.  At the end of the tour we were given a quick free head and neck massage - brilliant. 
On way out they take you to the shop and encourage you to buy the various remedies - prices are very high and they are quite high pressure salesmen, however if you like a bargain you can find these remedies in the central town areas at lower prices, if you can be bothered to search them out.  Saying that we did buy a couple :-)

Title: What a ripe off  very deceiving products at an expensive price
Text:
We where there on march 2013 the guide make a quick visit and after take is time to show us the product so he can make a profit on the sale.The product are very expensive for what they contain.We bought santal oil when we arrive home  the oil is like glue the same  with there hair remover and the container so cheap that it is impossible  to close container We went in a market and we saw the price at least 90% less .Yuo will say but it is not real product, but  at least it is a small riped of than paying a huge price for bad products.

Pleas avoid at all cost

Title: no, thanks, we are backpackers.
Text:
i do not consider it's worthy to visit, especially if you consider yourself as a backpacker or to seek for an authentic traveling experience in sri lanka, yet, if you love free things, that 's another story.

The case is, our driver unfortunately bought us there, and the products are relatively expensive, so i definitely recommend people to shop in local markets.

Title: Watch out for those wandering hands...
Text: I enjoyed the tour of the gardens (even in the rain) but got more than I bargained for when my '5 minute neck, head and shoulder massage' came with a bonus grope!  The products are overpriced but I was well impressed with the natural hair removal cream.  Avoid if you're on a serious budget!

Title: high knowlegde guide and fun experience
Text: i c ame home with ab 200 usa$ products because they have fresh what u need. one product label fell off,so thy helped me once i was in ISRAEL.gUIDE KNEW ALL ABOUT PLANTS AND TEAS,LOTIONS,ETC. Excellent complexion cream and honey

Title: Seeing red
Text: I've now had a week of applying red oil every night to my arthritic hip, but if anything it's got worse. We were shocked by the prices at the time, but had quite enjoyed our visit and felt we ought to repay them by buying something. Now I refuse to believe their claims that former purchasers write from abroad to eulogise about their products and order more. The garden tour is pleasant enough and you can give them whatever you think it's worth for the ten-minute massage. Just don't buy anything in the shop - you'll regret it.

Title: Great Massage
Text: Our visit was part of a very long day out. The Gardens were not that large but the guides were very knowledgeable and the sudden massage although unrequested or expected made the rest of our day out that much more acceptable. The massage was really good. As 1 of 2 blokes with hairy legs I received the organic hair removal treatment. Only a strip mind you. I wonder if it's going to grow back !!!!!!!!! ( 3 months later )   As another reviewer stated, a bit of a hard product sell as you leave.  Worth a visit as part of a day out however

Title: Interesting- beware strong sales pitch
Text: We were interested in the visit, very knowable guide. After a shoulder massage it was a sales pitch, we did buy a few things but very over priced. Just beware.

Title: Fun place to discover various spices . . .
Text: An exciting and knowledgable experience to touch and feel spices of all varieties we've been consuming all our lives. Must experience this place!

Title: not worth the visit
Text: as other experienced...they treat you very nicely, they explain the plants properties and don't force you to buy..untill the end when you're forced into the shop...and maybe you can escape the buying but I wasn't strong enough...and everything is way over priced...please don't fall in the net

Title: Good
Text:
Been to the spice garden on our way to candy. The presentation given by the students out here was very informative.

Did buy a few basic things....

Title: Interesting visit
Text: We had bad feelings while reading reviews of spice gardens located nearby. Despite all our visit at Ranweli 99 spice garden was very nice and interesting. The tour took about 20 minutes and was free, and of course there is a small boutique where you can buy all the spices and products. Although there is no obligation to buy anything.

Title: beware, they will rip you off
Text: If you have visited any spice garden before, this one is going to be a bore. The guide may go on harping about how he is just telling you about the properties of the spices and not trying to sell, however, the truth comes out at the end. Their products are way too expensive. Beware, especially if you are a foreign tourist. They looked greedily at first and almost accusingly even after my friend bought stuff worth 10k Sri Lankan Rupees. Not worth a visit.

Title: interesting but...
Text: Bought some Ayurvedic stuff, very expensive.  All natural ingredient  but I came out in a rash almost immediately - beware!

Title: intense
Text: interesting but intense tour. I remain sceptic on at the healing power of spices. I'm sure it works on milder issues.

Title: Really interesting
Text: Our guide was informative and knowledgeable about the spices and herbs grown there. A massage was available for a small tip as well as a short cookery demonstration There was a shop there but no pressure to buy. They were extremely concerned about our son who was ill with food poisoning and gave him some herbal remedy to help him. Lovely people and worth a visit.

Title: we felt like ripped off
Text:
nice explanations, but we took off with mixed feelings about the genuine intent of the guides.
Afterwards, we learned that the prices of the spices they sell are exaggerated.

Title: They are very good at spices
Text: We found that the spice and gem places in Kandy were the most interesting placed around because of their great knowledge and good presentations, they also have good prices compared to other places

Title: Enjoyable and informative
Text: We went here today and had a nice experience. The garden tour was really interesting and we learnt loads. The massages were great also but we werent asked before hand if we wanted a massage. The shop was great but also felt quite pushy and over priced. It would be much better if they had an entrance  fee with less hidden costs.

Title: Great experience
Text: You can get knowledge of sri lankan spices and medicinal plants it is worth trip for you around the village garden.

Title: Spicy Break
Text:
Quite a precarious spot on the corner of a fast mental road. Make sure you get help to cross the road. It is available. 

Good thorough guide, although maybe a little over the top on benefits of each spice.

So many different spices to discuss. 

Shop well stocked with lots of spices and add ons. 

Free massages offered to all. Decent restaurant too.

Well worth a visit.

Thank You Team Spice Farm.

Title: Arrogant cheaters pushy scammers
Text:
This place is a scam. Avoid at all cost!
Prices are like 10x what the product should cost.
Plus they push you into buying they product after taking you for a tour of a small garden.
I left without buying anything and they started to act pissed off.
This people are a shame to Sri Lanka. Nothing to do with all the other honest people I met during my trip.
They should run out of business.
Dont be tricked by your tuk tuk driver and if they propose you to go there dont

Title: Do not go!
Text: Nothing interesting to be seen. Just a few trees, is way exaggerated to say this is a spice garden. Everything is just a tourist trap, oriented over robbing the tourists. All the taxis or the tuk-tuk will tell you fairytales about how interesting it is. The true is that they got a big commission from what tourists spend. Is absolutely not important what spice garden youll see. All are the same oriented, have the same concept. Free massage at the beginning, tipping is an absolutely must, then the theatre from the shop. You will be pushed and suffocated by a couple of knowledgeable sellers and left without your money for buying the most useless dirty liquids you can ever imagine. I personally spent 200 for some stupid liquids. When I got home I realised how stupid I was. So, do yourself a favour and go away of any of this dubious businesses. Doesnt matter if is this one or the other one!

Title: Quick Education in Medicinal Plants
Text: The garden itself is small, but well kept and sports diverse medicinal plants. The guide was very informed and fun, and there is a demonstration and review of the many health products and spices sold there. There is even a free massage (for men... its shirt off) though a tip is expected. A full visit is an hour, if that. If you seek a quick lesson in Ayurvedic medicine and the plants used, this is a good spot. Clean toilets.

Title: The massage!
Text: We spent an enjoyable hour here and our guide was very informative. We first saw the plants and then had a demo about the various products that come from the plants. It included a lovely head and shoulder massage.  The tour costs you nothing but we were so convinced about the properties of the products we spent quite a bit of money!

Title: Fabulous visit
Text: An unexpected, wonderful stop in Kandy!! Highly recommend it!! We had a local professor show us around and explain all the different herbs and spices!! Make sure you add this place on your stops in Kandy!

Title: Interesting
Text: We walked around the well ordered garden in which there were many examples of different herbs and spices growing in their natural habitat.  Our guide was very  informative and after a massage and cup of herbal tea we finished in the shop where there was an extensive range of herbs and spices and well presented products.  There was no pressure to buy but we thought the prices were reasonable and we selected some spices to take home.

Title: Do not fall into this trap
Text: We went here as tourists do, had a walk round a few plants and a demonstration on how the products are used. Very small spice garden. We were then taken into the shop where we brought a couple of things, we were so shocked of the price when we got to the till $60 for 2 oils. Very extremely expensive when you can buy the same product at shop for a fraction of the price. So be careful!

Title: BIG BUSINESS
Text: This is a slick operation with informative guides explaining how numerous spices grow and an in depth synopsis the uses of spices as the locals to it. This culminates in a cup of tea, potion and lotion sampling and a shop. There is no pressure to purchase, but most did.

Title: Informative
Text: Well presented garden and informative guide with products available at the end of tour. Herbal remedies and of course the inevitable please could you donate to the poor children for school assistance

Title: Check the signboard before entering!
Text: We had a horrible experience with a Tuk Tuk driver who wanted to take us to a different spice garden. We wanted to visit this spice garden because it had good reviews and we gave our driver clear instructions/ directions , but still we were taken to a different spice garden also located near the botanical gardens. Had a very bad experience in this spice garden which I do not want to mention here. If you want to visit an attraction , book a hotel never listen to these drivers /guides they will take you to places where they are paid a big commission not to authentic places. Do your own research online and visit places and book hotels .

Title: Beautiful and very relaxing
Text: I recently visited the Royal Botanical Gardens. What a great experience w. The gardens are extensive and was so relaxing to walk around.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Really beautiful gardens and reasonable entry fee. Easy to spend a couple of hours wandering around the beautiful place and plenty of shady benches to relax. Down the top end there are trees full of huge bags too which was amazing to see.

Title: A pretty park
Text: We hired a tuk-tuk to take us on the three-temple-loop and then to the Botanical Gardens:  It took much longer than we expected to drive out to the temples however 2 of the 3 were quite worthwhile: Ancient and interesting.  The Botanical Gardens however was a disappointment:  It is a large, well-tended park.  A nice park, but just a park that has some name signs on trees and shrubs.

Title: Beautiful and calm
Text:
We loved the botanical gardens. It's beautiful, lots of open space as well as different themed houses. The orchid house was really nice. There's monkeys towards to back near the bamboo which were really cute to see. 
There's a little shop just outside for snacks and drinks. We spent 1.5 hours in the gardens but could have easily done longer. Lots of shaded areas to get out the sun.

Title: Definitely spend some time here ..
Text: A well maintained garden , this place was a pleasure to visit and a nice break from the hustle and bustle of town. We spent only 2 hours there but you could easily wander around longer. Plenty of paths and open space, information boards etc. The Plant House and Orchid House were the favourites as they were of interests to us; with many similar plants in our home. Another big tick for this garden is the section where world leaders had planted a tree and we could see how much the tree has grown from then.... A recommended visit !

Title: Worth the visit.
Text:
You don't have to be a dedicated gardener to enjoy these gardens. Trees are labelled according to whether they're native, imports, even poisonous- so don't lick these ones!
We had our guide with us, and he had a lot of knowledge about some of the plants and trees, that we may have missed if we'd been by ourselves.
The mahogany trees are spectacular- the root system is about a metre high. The Cannonball tree looks like it has coconuts, but they weigh about 4kg. The palm trees lining one path are huge, and the little ones in between them are the same type, but look different when they're younger.
We saw flying foxes, a water monitor, birdlife, and there's an orchid house, and a small suspension bridge.
We were here a few hours, and it was a very pleasant visit. Well recommended.

Title: superb gardens
Text: superb gardens. very neat and clean and lots of walking paths. the views are pictuesque and the feel is very good. must visit place

Title: A well maintained botanical garden on par with the best in the world.
Text:
This centuries old botanical garden planned by the British in the centre of the hill station Kandy, Sri Lanka is huge.

There are a number of covered exhibits category wise like seasonal flowers, cactus, perennial et al.,
The place is well maintained and the pathways are clean.

A number of families picnicking in the park are also mindful of the trash they generate and are meticulous in keeping the area clean.

There are a number of species of plants and trees which are imported from across the world and are thriving in the botanical garden.

One needs atleast a couple of hours to walk around the garden and enjoy the nature.

The entry fee to the garden is reasonable and the park is secured fully by barbed wire fencing.

The security checks at the entrance are robust.

 Take your camera along.

Recommended.

Title: Spend a few hours walking around all the gardens.
Text: The nicest and most relaxing thing to do I Kandy. So many trees, plants and fauna from all around the world. Some very large trees and bamboo. Fruit bats roosting in the tree tops, monkeys and birds to see.

Title: Absolutely loved this place!
Text: We stopped for a quick visit on our way to Nuwara Eliya but ended up staying for two hours in there because it is so beautiful and enormous. It is very relaxing to walk around or sit for a picnic. Huge collection of plants from all over the world and large trees that are more than 50 years old. Highly recommended if you are staying in Kandy or just passing by!

Title: Most nice place in Kandy
Text: Actually in Kandy no more places to visit, this Park is the main place in the to, so if you are tourist you have to visit it. It has all kind of plan

Title: Beautiful
Text: Amazing to see all the different types of trees and plants. Nice walk, plenty of shade to keep you cool

Title: A must see in Kandy
Text:
Fabulous botanical gardens, very well maintained and a must see when visiting Kandy. 
The variety of trees, plants and fauna are amazing, we followed the path along the river and came to the suspension bridge at the top, then made our way back towards the orchid house. Approx an hour and a half.

Title: Beautiful....
Text: These gardens are a must see in Kandy - they are absolutely beautiful...the flying fox bats by the river were spectacular...

Title: A must-do in Kandy
Text: If you're travelling to Kandy, visiting these gardens is a must. They are beautiful. A nature-lovers dream.

Title: Close To Nature
Text: Great place to explore with kids. Nature at its best. Well maintained park with lush green park for children to play and explore different plants.

Title: Tree Heaven
Text:
Went at 9am to avoid the crowds although the temperature was low 30's.

Great shaded walkways.

Well laid out, easy to follow on the given map.

Tree signage brilliant with signage making you aware of the
poisoness trees and who planted what. Don't miss it if you visit Kandy.

Title: Very impressive gardens
Text: Went to the gardens with mixed emotions, wasn't too sure I would enjoy it. Wow was I surprised. They are stunning with loads to see. Loved Royal Palm avenue, loved watching the bats flying around in the large fir trees and the orchids were magnificent. Well worth a visit

Title: Fantastic gardens
Text: Beautiful gardens and extensive grounds all immaculately kept .Easy to follow route around main sights and we particularly enjoyed the beautiful orchid house.

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Peaceful haven to visit and take time out to walk around all the lovely trees and and plants. Make sure to go into the Orchid House.place of vibrant colours and peace

Title: Excellent site
Text: This is an excellent botanical site. I would suggest allowing a morning or afternoon to undertake a full visit. We benefited from a guide who could tell you about the various trees etc. A visit to the orchid house is a must.

Title: Massive Garden with Exorbitant Fee
Text: This is a massive garden that is well-maintained with more than 4,000 species of plants, range from humongous trees to herbs, flora, palm trees, orchids, etc. It was built since 14th century as royal  garden, but was destroyed during British occupation and was made as garden for coffee and cinnamons in 19th century. It was then under the administration of Department of Agriculture since 1912 when it was established. Beautiful place to spend for half a day especially for plants lovers. Many sitting benches, people also doing picnic on the lawns. Toilets are available within the park. Many different sections, such as palm tree sections, giant trees, orchid garden, cacti section, flowerbed section, etc. There is a section with interesting sights of lots of visible hanging bats on the tree branches. Overall it was a pleasant and therapeutic session to walk around the garden. Brochure indicates various species of birds can be found in the garden, but we could hardly see any. Also, the entrance fee is rather steep for foreigners at LKR2,000 per person per entry whereas locals only pay a small fraction.

Title: Very nice
Text: Very nice gardens and very big, they have a lot of different species of plants and flowers. Also a chance to see a lot of birds and other animals. In the trees you can see hundreds of flying foxes

Title: Another visit to the excellent gardens
Text: Four of us enjoyed another visit to the excellent gardens but noted that, due to the current Covid-19 problems, the number of visitors were greatly reduced. This made our visit even more personal.

Title: Peaceful.
Text: A tranquil place after all the noise from traffic. Lovely gardens, especially the number of different trees. Orchids were good, but a small display, we are used to the orchid garden in Singapore, which I reckon must be the best in the world.

Title: Tranquil surroundings in a busy town
Text: Visited for an afternoon and was a very pleasant stroll through lovely grounds. Tourists pay 2000rupees and you can hire a golf cart for an extra 2000 if you feel too hot too walk. They have a fantastic selection of trees which are nice and shady to sit under and there is a lovely cool cafeteria where you can sit and have lunch and soft drinks at reasonable prices.

Title: Relaxing walk in the gardens
Text: Loved this place! Great relaxing few hours spent here wandering around in theses fabulous gardens. There was lots of wildlife too including peacocks, monkeys and bats! Lots of areas of shade providing a welcome relief from the heat. Do check out the suspension beige too.

Title: A must visit in Kandy
Text: Large botanical gardens that are doing great work alongside Kew gardens amongst others. Some great tree species to see from around the world , as well as beautiful flowering plants. Loved the avenue of palms, the large , old mahogony tree and the Madagascan 'canon ball tree' with its beautiful fruits shaped like cannon balls and its beautiful flowers. Well laid out, well sign posted and very well maintained. You will probably need 3 hours plus to see it all. Although there is shade , it was hot walking around so take plenty of water. There is a cafe , ideally located by the large lawn if you want to stay longer/ are in need of refreshments.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text: Wonderful gardens with all sorts of birds monkeys and large fruit bats. The tour in the golf buggy was wonderful and very welcome if you're a bit dodgy on your pins. The driver was also knowledgeable friendly and amusing. They don't have enough 3 seater buggies so you have to be lucky or pushy to get one. A pity they don't have more benches so that you can just and ponder. Lots of history.

Title: A highlight in  Kandy
Text: It was a very pleasant and relaxing walk through this large botanical garden seeing so many different species of flowers and trees, as well as endemic vegetation. In hot day you can really enjoy the shade and the tour through alleys of palm trees. Give yourself 3-4 hours.

Title: Don't Bother
Text:
What a total waste of space and time. 
The Orchid House and the Rose Garden were totally pointless and disappointing. The local Garden Centre in the UK has a better range of both Orchids and Roses. So we gave up and went to the cafe in the middle was a welcome spot to sit and have a drink.
There are virtually no seats in the garden to look and relax.

Title: Beautiful Gardens
Text: We didnt spend enough time here as our driver was picking us up so we didnt see all the gardens but what we saw was beautiful.  we were amazed at the bats in the trees there were hundreds of them and very noisy! When you come here make sure you bring enough water as its very hot work walking around. Well worth a visit!!

Title: Fruit bats and monkeys
Text: Easy to spend a full afternoon here. Beautiful well kept gardens with lots of interesting trees and plants. There is an orchid house, suspension bridge and fruit bats along with cheeky monkeys who will take  food from your hand. But be warned, they can be slightly aggressive. The cafe is welcoming on a hot day.

Title: Stunning.
Text: FABULOUS. I had a great few hours here. Amazing. The trees etc were spectacular. The cheeky monkeys roaming around watching for an opportunity. Magical place. Well worth a visit. Very well maintained. Sch a variety of things to see. Camera fanatics would love this.

Title: Good place where to spend some hours
Text: Beautiful gardens, very well kept, not cheap tickets, but worth the price if you are interested in trees, that are the main attraction. The orchid glasshouse was a bit of a delusion because there werent any particular varieties.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text: Excellently maintained gardens and Orchid House. Leisurely stroll around the stunning flora. Helps to have a knowledgeable guide but not a necessity. Must see when visiting the area.

Title: An enjoyable restful few hours
Text: Quite expensive to enter for a Sri Lankan attraction, 2000 rupees per person for foreigners. But it is worth it. The grounds are extensive with beautiful trees, palms, shrubs, flowers, a lake etc. You will spend several hours walking around the various paths, sit down and appreciate some views, a very restful relaxing place contrasting with the hustle and bustle of Kandy itself.

Title: Good walking tour
Text:
Had a good walk through the gardens. There are several unique plants in the garden. 
The orchids were OK but there were not as many that I heard about.

Title: Delightful garden
Text: This is a very large, well maintained garden with lots to see as you wander around. Youll need at least a couple of hours for a quick tour. There is quite a bit of renovation going on so some places are closed. It costs 2000 rupees for foreigners to get in. Street vendors arent allowed in so your visit will be relaxed and hassle free. We didnt visit at the best time of year in terms of flowers, but it was lovely nonetheless.

Title: Wide variety of plants.
Text: One of the oldest botanical gardens in the world.  Our guide around the gardens was the botanist Bandara Palipana and he made it a most interesting tour.  We saw many trees and shrubs which were new to us and the stories behind some of the plantings was interesting.  The orchis collection has over 300 varieties on show.  The Cook pine (introduced from New Caledonia by Captain Cook) is unusual as always leans towards the equator.   HM Queen Elizabeth II, Lord Mountbatten, King George IV, Yuri Gagarin and others have planted trees there.  Lord Mountbatten used the old residence in the centre f the park as his headquarters as Supreme Allied Commander of South East Asia Command during WWII.  The gardens are kept in a pristine condition.  Many Bollywood films have used it for location shooting.

Title: A Tranquil Setting
Text: We arrived early in the morning and were lucky to get a golf buggy and guide for an additional 1000rps. This helped us cover more than 5km of the beautiful gardens and ensured that we managed to see all the highlights within about an hour. Our guide was lovely! super friendly and informative and gave us good insight into the gardens history and fauna and flora. The entrance fee is 2000rps per person which is very reasonable considering the immaculate condition the garden is kept in. This is a must for nature lovers, photographers and artists!

Title: Ridiculous price for foreigners! Is Sri Lanka racist to whites? Yes!
Text: Lots of plants to see and big walks but a ridiculous price!! 4000 rupees for two British people. Come off it guys! We were so shocked at the price that we even tried to pretend we were both students (I actually am but my partner is not) and they said they wouldnt accept that and had to pay full price! 4000 for a walk around the garden. It took all the cash we had so we had to get out more. 250 for locals or something. In the UK that would be called racism my friends!!

Title: A green heaven
Text: These gardens were a highlight of our time in candy. The gardens where a peaceful haven from a bustling city centre. There were many distinct areas and a huge variety of different types of trees. We couldve spent hours and hours there

Title: Wonderful
Text: This garden is wonderful. Due to my healthy situation, I hired a caddy and it was so pleasant and quite to hang out, discovering all those amazing scenographies: the Royal Palm Avenue, the Orchid House, a rubber thee creating a forest all alone (like in the Jungle Book!), a huge selection of different grass samples, a noisy colony of flying foxes (big bats)Do not miss these garden, walk around and discover yourself your coup de cur!!

Title: Awesome botanical garden!
Text: You can easily spend the half day there. The exhibition has a high variety of local and global plants. We absolutely recommend to go there if you have time.

Title: Amazing green
Text:
We were there with my family and they were enjoying a lot by playing here and there on the grass. 
There were lots of historical trees around it and all most every single tree you can find in Sri Lanka you can find a sample here. 
Ticket will be around $10 and its really worth it. There were lots of tourists there and I guess everybody was enjoying there. 
Loved to return to be back.

Title: Great visit
Text:
We stopped at the botanical gardens after visiting the Temple of the Tooth and it was a lovely way to end the day. The gardens are extensive so be prepared for a lot of walking (in the heat!)! Our guide arranged for a tour of the gardens for us and it was great, we got to see the whole area and the different varieties of plants, learn a little about the history of the gardens, and all without breaking a sweat!

Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.

Title: Extensive and impressive gardens
Text: This is a really attractive large park in the town of Kandy, full of wonderful trees, shrubs and plants, many from different parts of the world. Entry is relatively cheap and I would suggest paying a little extra to tour the park with a driver on one of the electric buggies (it is very hot to walk around and explore the whole park - there's a lot to see and the drivers are quite knowledgeable). Most of the trees etc. have descriptive plaques, and you'll notice from the information that many were planted by famous people, some over a hundred years ago. In one area in some fir trees, you'll almost certainly see roosting bats, which was quite a surprise. The Royal Palm avenue is very nice too. Don't miss the Orchid House near the entrance before you leave. Very good.

Title: Peaceful area.
Text: We arrived at about 2 p m and our driver waited about 2 hours. We could have stayed longer. It was peaceful and relaxing. All plants and trees had explanation labels attached. Theres a cafe, toilets and a good souvenir shop. We could have stayed longer in this beautiful area. It closes at 6 p m with last visits at 5 p m.

Title: A Morning in the Gardens.
Text:
Although my wife and are lovers of all things historical, occasionally we need to refresh the mind and relax. The Gardens were included on our tour itinerary and provided a welcome interlude from the intensity of the UNESCO sites. 
The origins of the Gardens date to 1371 and they were declared a Royal Garden during the reign of King Kirti Sri Rajasinghe between 1747 - 1780. The Gardens on their present site were established in 1821 and cover an area of 60ha. showcasing over 4,000 species. The informative guide map that we received on entry contained a detailed legend and history of the Gardens. We spent approx. three hours strolling the walkways and admiring the beauty of the flora and it's diversity. The Orchid House held a marvelous display and variety of exotic blooms. We enjoyed the Flower garden with many annuals and perennials in bloom. The Palm Avenues are spectacular and include Royal, Cabbage and  Palmyrah, not to be ignored and great for photos, especially the Coco de Mer of Seychelles notoriety. We saw some of the tallest grasses in the world, stands of bamboos on River Drive, including the giant bamboo of Burma. We enjoyed the Fernery, Spice Garden, Cacti and the Arboretum. 
Interesting plaques recognizing world leaders and renowned visitors who planted trees there. Lovely way to spend a morning and then adjourn to the pleasant café near the entrance.

Title: Beautiful well kept Gardens
Text: I'm not a huge fan of gardens and so forth however I found the Botanical gardens really interesting, trees planted by various Presidents and Prime Ministers from round the world, some dating back to the 60s. Trees that are a hundred years old, lots of wildlife like kingfishers and monkeys. We would have stayed longer but we were running out of time. Worth a visit if you like this sort of thing.

Title: Charming
Text: One of the must visit destinations in Kandy. The garden is very big & needs enough time to get a good tour. There are hundreds types of plants & many trees were planted more than 100 years ago. They are really giving special care to the place. Its very clean, neat & well maintained. The suspension bridge is having very nice view to the river. Nice photos could be taken on it. The garden is a very good destination for relaxation.

Title: Expensive and not very impressive
Text:
For tourist who have visited similar parks in other parts of the world can avoid this.  The entry fee of LKR 2,000 for foreigners is not at all justified.  Its a waste of time and energy.  The only impressive part was the Orchid collection which had a few beautiful flowers.  The part is anyways well laid out and well kept.  You will find a lot of local couples romancing at secluded placed.

If you do not get time to visit this location or avoid, you do not loose out on anything..  This is a very personal opinion.  Travelers who have lot of free time and money can definitely spend time here.  May be impressive for tourist from places with sparse vegetation.

Title: Massive garden
Text:
We spent hours in this garden and if I had more time, I'd stay much longer. I loved this garden. It must have been the biggest I have been to in all my travels. The huge trees were extra special because of the history and their age. It is nice to find something like this at the heart of the city.

Aside from plants, there are many animals roaming the garden so watch your belongings in case there are monkeys. They usually would not bother you but it's better to be sure.

Wear comfortable footwear and clothes so you can cover the whole grounds.

Title: Trees
Text: This is an excellent botanical garden here in Sri Lanka. The garden is well maintained.  A good place to go for a walk.

Title: Visit in the pouring rain
Text: Our guide took us here - it is wonderful - sadly the rain was fierce and we went round in a golf cart so only were there for about 90 minutes - wonderful trees and plants and the orchid house was special -it would be great to walk and fully understand the background and history - really peaceful

Title: Amazing !
Text: We don't want to go home after we visited the Royal Botanic Gardens. She is very impressed by the color of the flowers in the garden. She cant stop taking pictures of her with such a lovely place. I truly loved this place.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text:
The garden is very big. You could spend half a day for sure just walking around. It's a really nice place to visit. Unfortunately we didn't had enough time available to see the whole garden. I think we saw about half and we still spent about 2 hours or even more in there.
The price is about 11$ per person. it's a really nice place to see.

Title: Nice place to visit
Text: Nice place to spend a day. Better go when it is not too hot. A lot of things to do - can spend even whole day in there.

Title: Lovely gardens with beautiful old trees
Text: The gardens have many trees that were planted nearly 200 years ago and they are stunning. The walkways and general surrounds are peaceful and well interpreted. There are a number of fantastic vistas within the grounds. We noticed you could get a buggy to take you around, although we decided to walk. The variety of plants is amazing and numerous birds were seen. Bit disappointed with the orchid displays...needs to be curated and rearranged. But all in all a beautiful place to visit.

Title: Tired, neglected and over-priced
Text: Around 6km to the west of Kandy.  Overall these gardens are somewhat tired and neglected.  We have visited a number of botanical gardens around the world including in the tropics and these are typically free to enter or the entry price is reasonable.  The entry price for foreigners at Peradeniya is LKR2,000 per person, which is not far off what you would pay for far superior gardens in Europe.  I have no problem with foreigners being charged more than locals but the price charged should be reasonable and it would be good to see the money generated being invested in the site.

Title: Wish we'd had more time...
Text:
One of the main attractions in Kandy.  Entrance fees are 2000 Rps per person.

If, like us your time is more limited you can hire a golf buggy for another 2000 Rps (although unfortunately you can't drive it yourself!!).  The guide will point out trees planted by various celebrities and royalty.  Although, I don't think this does the gardens justice and, in retrospect, would have preferred to wander through the pathways and enjoy them at a more sedate pace.

As well as all the interesting trees, plants and orchids you can see monkeys and fruit bats.

Title: Rest and enjoy the place
Text: A quiet spot in Kandy, with hundreds of plants, trees ... and monkeys. Many Orchids in gorgeous colours. A great way to spend time is a slow stroll through the entire grounds. Nice to find a seat and just enjoy the beauty and quiet. Another must-do when in Kandy.

Title: Nice walk through the gardens. Not that many flowers though
Text:
We were initially hesitant about a visit to the royal botanical gardens but overall it is a pleasant visit. 

We were focussing on a few displays that we were interested in. Firstly we went to see the giant bamboo forest which was amazing. We also went to take a look at the fig tree and the orchid house. 

It is well maintained but having more flowers would be good.

Title: Beautiful Gardens
Text:
This is a must see in Kandy.

There is a big variety of plants and what impressed me the most was that not only is the names of the plants/trees shown, but also the country of origin.  

We spend about 3 hours there but if you have time you can spend the whole day.

The layout is also good and interesting in some instances.

Title: Beautiful and well laid out gardens
Text: We loved walking through these gardens. They are beautifully landscaped with more than 4000 species of plants. They have a big collection of orchids too. The cannon ball tree was very fascinating. One can easily spend a couple of hours here without getting bored. But you have to be prepared to walk. The gardens are spread over a huge area.

Title: Spectacular gardens!
Text:
I am not usually a botanical gardens fan, but our innkeeper and many guide books recommended this, so we decided to give it a try (especially since it was Monday and the Tea Museum was closed).  What a pleasant surprise!  The various avenues of palms are striking and you can enjoy many areas of shade as you explore the grounds.  The gift shop is excellent as well.

You could easily spend hours here, but 90 minutes was enough for us.

Enjoy!

Title: Good place to spend a day with kids
Text:
Needless to say it was a massive spread of various plants and trees from around the world. Well maintained and clean with information on some of them which we found to be useful. Many tourists around due to its popularity though it could never get congested. A huge grassland in the middle gave our kids unimaginable space to play. Alongside was a cafe where I could only spot tourists,the locals were seated down on the grass with their modest meals.
We sat around them too and couldnt have enough of the fresh air that is usually missing in gulf counties.

At 2000 LKR per adult it was worth our time and effort.

Title: Very disappointed that it is a rip off
Text: I have visited the garden as a teenager many times while living in Sri Lanka. After more than 30 years living abroad, I decided to take my teenagers to show this amazing place. It is very disappointing that they charge more than $40usd while the locals pay less than $1. Dont get me wrong, this a very beautiful place but a steep cost for a family.

Title: Nice well maintained garden
Text: Tip - use a buggy for covering this in an hour. Very well maintained botanic garden. Entry fees is on the higher side but still highly recommended to visit

Title: A Nice Garden
Text: It is indeed a nice botanical garden to spend hours. The garden has wide space and plenty to enjoy. It well maintained. Different section of the garden fills heart with different types of feeling. A must visit place.

Title: Beautiful and well maintained botanical garden
Text:
If you really want to do full justice to this place you need 2-3 hours as it's a huge botanical garden with variety of trees, flowers and birds.

The garden is well maintained and there's also a buggy service if you don't want to walk the entire garden area.

What i loved most is the orchid garden, the cactii garden, the Rose garden, lovely trees in various natural shapes and the way different plants are laid to bring our the beauty.

Title: Great Guided tour
Text:
We had the choice of walking the gardens ourselves - or taking a tour on an electric buggy.
We took the buggy - with some 6 other folk, and in a little over an hour saw as much as 3 hours of walking ( in the heat).

The time saving was only one advantage - the buggy driver was an excellent guide that helped appreciate the various plants - and the historic connection of the gardens.

The ride cost us LKR500 each.

Title: Well worth it
Text: The gardens are really worth the visit, I was shocked how much I enjoyed it. You need at least an hour

Title: second visit and even more interesting than the first time
Text: If you're visiting Kandy, spending a bit of time in the Botanical Garden is a must.  Reading about the history, seeing the beautiful displays, walking among the trees or even walking on the suspension bridge will interest all. We especially appreciated the flower displays along with the historical plaques commemorating the people who planted trees at the garden.  It's well worth the time.

Title: Just beautiful
Text: Plan 2-3 hours for your stay. Otherwise you'll either have to hurry or can't see everything. Can recommend the gift shop. The selection is quite good and the prices are low (e.g. 100-200 RS for a magnet).

Title: another view of sydney opera
Text: In Royal Botanical Gardens, you can see another view of Sydney Opera and Sydney Bridge. The view is good, air is flash, you can see sydney people relax life style. Also, Mrs Macquaries Chair is in it and worth to see.

Title: Do not recommend going, especially in December
Text: May be we were just unlucky, but almost none of the flowers were blooming at that time + they are making some renovations, so the little lake was empty, covered in mud with lots of workers, rose garden leafless and empty, the map was outdated, some roads and items were not marked there. Only the trees are gorgeous and impressive. But, surely, its not worth spending LKR 2,000 per person.

Title: A beautiful garden
Text: This is a beautiful garden and a welcome haven from the busy centre of Kandy. There are so many interesting and unusual plants and it is a real joy to wander around for a few hours - I definitely recommend visiting if you are in or near Kandy. The photos on here and elsewhere online didnt really do it justice, it is more impressive in real life!

Title: Peaceful place to relax
Text:
Located about 10-15 kms away from kandy city. Its a huge botanical garden thats been developing from the last 100 years or so. Its beautiful and its huge. U can just keep walking for hours. Theres so much to observe here. Though i have no idea about trees/plants, it was quite fascinating to see the variety of flora n fauna. The botanical garden is really well maintained.  I found d entrance fee of 2000 LKR for foreigners too much though. Thats a big hole in d pocket. 
So if ur ok to spend on d entrance ticket then its surely worth a visit. We spent an hour n half just enjoying d greenery n pleasant weather.

Title: Pleasant day in this beautiful garden
Text: We felt like we were in paradise. This garden is simply beautiful! Take your time to walk around and take in the beauty of the trees, flowers, and all sort of plants. Enjoy the peacefulness!

Title: Beautiful
Text: Beautiful gardens loved the orchids a truely peaceful place to spend some time . A lot of shady places to get out of the hot sun .

Title: Worth visiting
Text:
These gardens are well presented and a must see in Kandy.  From the established trees and palm walks to various hot houses and green houses displaying orchids, cacti, flowering plants and many others o the trees full of resting fruit bats its a great way to fill in a few hours. The gift shop at the end also has a good range of reasonably priced items for those that like to shop. 

Just be sure to take a hat and sunscreen.

Title: Beautiful
Text: We enjoyed these gardens, as keen gardeners we found the gardens absolutely beautiful, I wish my garden could look as good as this! They give you a map, we still didn't manage to see it all. A lot of information on the different sort of trees and plants. The cactus/succulent house wasn't that impressive. It cost 1500 rs each to get in, worth a visit if you're in to plants.

Title: Fabulous garden to visit
Text: Well worth a visit.  Huge garden to wander around and admire the vast and varied trees and plants in the garden all of which are well maintained.  Particularly impressed by the orchid house.  Added bonus are the monkeys and bats to add life to the garden.

Title: WELL MAINTAINED
Text: These extensive gardens provide lush lawns on which children play, heaven in a crowded city. The maintenance and layout are quite good, but the plants and trees are not labeled which is a shame.

Title: orchid lover
Text: this botanical garden is said to be the garden used by the last king of kandy to meet his queen and stroll which was later improved by the British. a highlight of this garden is the orchid museum which has many varieties of orchid flowers.

Title: Royal Botanical Garden, Peradeniya, Kandy
Text: Botanical Garden area is vast about 60ha and various types of tress, plants are there. Orchid, Herbal, flower, etc are in separate wings. Entrance for foreigners is LKR2000. Big lawn, tress in rows, Double coconut are speciality of this garden. Garden is well maintained and battery car facility is available to visit entire garden.

Title: Beautiful gardens and area
Text:
Loved our visit here especially seeing the bats hanging from the tress in one area of the gardens. 
Gardens are extremely well kept and beautiful to see especially the orchid house.
Lots of walking to cover the vast area so recommend taking a bottle of water with you.

Title: Enchanting
Text:
We easily got a tuk tuk from our hotel to take us to the gardens. Entry fee is about $15 CDN each person. There is a coffee/gift shop at what is the entrance and the exit area. Public washrooms, which are very clean, are at the entrance and throughout the gardens. 

Can easily cover the gardens in 3 hours or less depending on what you wish to see and how fast you walk. 

Well maintained and a treat for any nature lover. We also saw a troop of monkeys and many beautiful birds.

Title: 5 stars if it werent for the price...
Text: This place really is a gem and oh so beautiful but again foreigners will pay for the fact that they are foreigners. Effective August, 5 (we visited on the 6th??) the entrance fee was increased to 2000 Rupies. Still this place is worth a visit. Make sure to bring some time and enjoy the beauty of the park. There is lots to see and also enough spaces to rest. If this is not convincing you, just take a look at the pictures.

Title: A must see
Text: When you are in Kandy, you should definitely visit the gardens. You can easily spend a couple of hours there and see the amazing collection of trees, plants, etc. The kids also loved it!

Title: Fascinating.
Text: It is unbelievable unless u read the pamphalet and check the dates...it is about 600+ years old garden and still maintained so well. Though they have Holf carts to take you around on nominal charges but the best way to explore this garden is buy walking around. Its not even difficult as there are benches arou d everywhere to sit and relax when u get tired. The river and the shaky bridge on it is really a great attraction in the park. A must visit site when in Srilanka.

Title: Well maintained garden
Text:
Its is a huge botanical garden in the middle of Kandy city. Those with an inclination towards plant studies will have a great time exploring the garden as it has a lot of variety of plantation.
We loved the greenery and beautiful flower garden.
To my surprise we have seen a double coconut tree inside the garden and same dried one is for display in a museum inside premises.
You can spend entire day if you wish to in a calm and beautiful garden. Please note it has an entry fee.
I'll suggest to improve on the direction maps so people can explore their interest due to limited time being a tourist.

Title: Nature at its best
Text:
We loved exploring the beautiful grounds of the garden and only wish we'd had longer there.
We arrived mid afternoon with our young children who adored the space to runaround and explore. They spent time looking at the different flora and fauna and admiring sights and sounds of the birds and numerous bats.
We had been told there was a chance of seeing monkeys but were overwhelmed to observe them closely on the suspension ('dancing bridge'). 
We had a truly fabulous time visiting and would recommend it to everyone.

Title: Must Go!
Text:
Actually "Kandy" sounds so much nicer than it is, BUT: on our second day we visited the botanical garden and it was far beyond our expections. 
Its a huge areal to plan at least 3 hours for the visit. Surprised by amazing garden planning and well cared...
One of the best botanical gardens I ever visited.

Title: Outstanding Gardens full of lovely flowers, trees and Flying Foxes!!
Text:
My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Sri Lanka and this afternoon we visited the lovely Royal Botanical Gardens of Peradeniya in Kandy.

After paying our SLR 1,500 (£7 approx) non-resident adult entrance fees, we spent a couple of hours exploring the extensive Gardens which will shortly (2021) be celebrating their 200th Anniversary. When I say extensive, we barely scratched the service but still had time to visit the impressive Orchard House.

I also much enjoyed - particularly, as many of these had involved various members of the British Royal Family - seeing the number of trees planted by VIPs over the years. My personal highlight, however, was not Botanical by nature but seeing the literally thousands of Fruit Bats (Flying Foxes) that were certainly making their presence felt!

All in all, a most enjoyable visit to what - by any standards - are first-rate Botanical Gardens.

Title: Spectacular botantical gardens
Text:
We went back and forth on whether to stop here on our way into Kandy, since we only had one night in the city and it's pretty hot to walk around the gardens in the middle of the day. In the end we did stop, and we're very glad we did. You don't need that long in Kandy, and Peradeniya was certainly more interesting than anything in Kandy.

It takes 2 or 3 hours to wander around. There's a lot of great plants and trees, but also birds and a large number of bats towards the back of the gardens.

Title: Real gem
Text: It's located at a distance of about 30km from Kandy. I spent well over 3 hours in the gardens and absolutely enjoyed it. Its home to many native plants of Sri Lanka and the entire place is clean and very well looked after.

Title: A beautiful garden is a work of art - Jun 22
Text: The garden includes many species of plants, This garden is home to trees from every corner of the tropical atmosphere.it's a massive garden and would take few hours for site seen. electric buggies were available, inside the garden average price cafeteria serving Western and Sri Lankan food for hungry tunnies. washroom facilities were available in many locations,  if you want to purchase plants, there is a plant centre near to the main gate ( Open at 0830 ). Barista and Laksala anchored near to exit.dont missed this man-made piece of art, it is a haven in the haven.

Title: Amazing, Soothing and Beautiful
Text: WOW. What a place. Beauty everywhere. Superb arrangements. Nice walking experience. Bridge is a little bit adventurous too. Very soothing. We luckily had a very good weather as well.

Title: Garden in the city
