Text: Beautifully maintained botanical gardens with various zones for types of plants. We especially enjoyed the orchid house and palm tree avenues. Surrounded by the river on most sides, it was an ideal place for local families as well as tourists and enthusiasts. Highly recommended on a sunny day.

Title: Good
Text: Good.......Long walking ... Peacefully life ....Greenery.......Fresh air......Peace of mind......green....... atmosphere....... Heaven.....Like Forest....  Double coconut trees ....... Bamboo trees..... squarels sound.....Monkeys.....

Title: Nice walk
Text:
Peaceful park with lots of extremely unusual trees from around the world.
Also there are quite a few monkeys about which make good viewing.

Title: Sprawling gardens with diverse flora in a peaceful environment
Text: Acres and acres of gardens but way better maintained than most botanical gardens in India. The collection is quite diverse and rare as the signboards suggest. The whole area is very peaceful and calm - not much rush of tourists. Must visit for plant lovers but even otherwise a nice spot.

Title: A must see
Text: If you are going to kandy than u must visit this beautiful garden. The views were mind blowing and soo many trees to learn about and beautiful nature.

Title: Big Enough
Text: Its big enough that you can feel you are in a hollywood movie where you are sent to a new planet and you have special house for each flowers species. No word and describe the beauty nor pictures can show you how beautiful this planet is.

Title: 10 STARS!
Text: Wow...what a collection of plants.I've never been to Kews Garden but believe that this botanical gardens is on par.We were very much overwhelmed the collection here.We spent 5 hours but suggest to spend the day here.Long walks to experience the beauty of this place. It was very eye opening.A must visit place for all botanist!

Title: Beautiful garden
Text: This lush quiet oasis in the middle of busy Kandy was an eye-opener. It was hot (as is usual in Sri Lanka) but when you got under the shade of the many trees the coolness was amazing. The highlight though is the orchid house. It isn't all that big but the number, variety and colours of the orchids is just simply stunning. We walked around a lot if the garden but didn't see all of it by any stretch of the imagination. The Palm Grove is so regal you can just see the maharajahs in procession on their elephants!! Don't miss this.

Title: A beautiful botanical garden
Text: We had a relaxing time at the Botanical Gardens in Kandy. This is a must visit place if you love Orchid flowers.

Title: Good place to walk
Text: The Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya, near Kandy, is worth a visit if you have the time and fancy an interesting walk. There are some majestic old trees and a good orchid house.

Title: Dont eat at the cafeteria
Text:
Nice gardens even in the rain. However DO NOT let your guide persuade you to eat at the cafeteria.
Its really bad and the service is worse.

Title: Peaceful
Text: Got to the gardens went in back way over the bridge great fun. The different types of trees  and plant's are just amazing.loads of birds flying round and saw the only snake on the whole trip a rat snake just before the wonderful orchid house.with tortoises in the ponds .a great place to visit

Title: A blooming marvel...
Text: The botanical gardens, just outside Kandy, are spectacular. A mix of colourful tropical flora and quiet strolls. Very reminiscent of wandering around Kew gardens in SW London.

Title: Huge open spaces- interesting and well worth it
Text: Beautiful location... nice stroll around in this beautiful garden- interesting watching the monkeys interacting.... nice time filler

Title: Sri L:anka vacation
Text: A lot plant houses (eg cactus) were not open to the public.Toilets in the grounds are primitive although thoss in the cafe were clean and western,

Title: Beautiful gardens and walk
Text:
The Gardens are probably 5km from Kandy, a short Tuk tuk ride. We spent around 3 hours walking around the Gardens. They are beautifully kept and the Trees are spectacular. The clumps of bamboos add to beauty of the Park as do the plants and the river. In one corner of the Gardens 20 plus thousand fruit bats roost which is a spectacular sight.
There are places to take refreshments. 
I would highly recommend a visit.

Title: Stunning Gardens
Text: We had a one hour guided tour of the gardens. Our guide was very informative and we loved the beautiful surrounds; magnificent trees and avenues, flowers and lawned areas all beautiful set out. Loved the history and the trees planted by notables such as King George V. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Gorgeous gardens!
Text: We spent a couple of hours here en route elsewhere, but we could have spent far longer! Lots to see and many fascinating and unusual plants, all clearly labelled. The orchid house was stunning, so many different colours and shapes. Wonderful palm walk, and a fascinating cannon ball tree! Tranquil areas for wandering, but also lots of grassy spaces for family games and local wedding photos - as it was the weeeknd when we visited, there was lots happening which gave a lovely insight to Sri Lankan everyday life! Theres also ponds, lakes and even a rope style suspension bridge, which gives great views over the river. Sadly the fruit bats wed hoped to see werent in evidence, but it was a very enjoyable visit indeed!

Title: Spent a great morning here
Text:
Visited here whilst in Kandy for the day and loved the place. We took a leisurely stroll down the main path to the green, down palm avenue to the suspension bridge, taken in the orchid house on route. Suspension bridge was fun to walk across but not quite sure why there is a gate in the middle with a sign that states stop. We saw some people get to the gate and turn round and then some people got to the gate and opened it and walked all the way across! Then walked along the side of the river and back round to the main entrance. At a leisurely pace this took about an hour.
Nice little cafe by the entrance where I enjoyed a great milkshake.
Great gift shop with some lovely items reasonably priced.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text: Enter the gardens by the back entrance, if possible, so that you can cross the river by rope bridge which makes the experience all the more memorable. The gardens are beautiful and are a lovely place to spend a few hours. In addition to the multitude of plant species there are hundreds of fruit bats hanging from the trees in certain areas. A really pleasant afternoon.

Title: Beautiful and Serene place
Text: Spent a couple of hours wandering around the gardens, really quiet even though its in the city, Beautiful flowers and even if you are not a natural gardener it is worth a visit and go for a little walk over the suspension bridge. Also worth watching the monkeys raiding the rubbish bins !

Title: Peaceful in noisy Kandy
Text: A large botanical gardens given near the centre of Kandy. Would recommend as a way to get some peace in Kandy! It was even possible not to hear the horns when in the middle of the park! There are impressive plants particularly the wild bamboo. Can easily spend a couple of hours.

Title: Great place
Text:
Simply one of the nicest gardens we have been to. The area is so well covered and the gardens are very big. Lots of wildlife. 

Take your time just walking around such a great area with fantastic scenery.

Title: Good but not Excellent
Text: It is a big garden but the collection we expected was not there. The orchid section was excellent, rest portion not properly maintained. Entry fee is excessive, for srilankan it 60LKR but for others it 1500LKR which looked high in compare to the  collection of varieties but you can pass few hours there because the area is large. Cactus section is small. I can say just nice.

Title: Amazing, wonderful
Text: Even if you are not into gardening, this is an amazing place. It's a huge site with some amazing plants and trees. It really is worth spending an afternoon here. Well worth the money.

Title: Absolutely beautiful! Dont miss it.
Text: An absolutely gorgeous garden. Cafes inside with food and drink. You can rent a golf cart to travel around if you want to avoid walking.

Title: Superbly maintained, one of the best
Text: This is a few km out of Kandy but well worth a couple of hours. Its quite large but is beautifully kept, very well laid our and plants well signed. A family of monkeys can be seen near the palm trees beyond the lake; many beautiful birds also. The northern part is an arboretum with many tress planted by heads of state and other famous figures, starting with the Prince of Wales in 1887. The orchid house is absolutely beautiful. Nice cafe overlooking the Great Lawn. One of the highlights of our Sri Lanka tour

Title: For Flower Lovers and Lovers
Text:
Botanists will love this vast garden paradise, as it's filled with a diverse and well organized garden. 

Most of the locals visiting here come as couples, seeking benches and shade for romance.

So if you're a tourist with deep interest in plants, you'll find a wealth of resources. More casual visitors can enjoy the beauty of the flowers and a beautiful and peaceful setting. I highly recommend the orchid house for its exotic beauty.

Title: A botanist's dream and also very beautiful
Text: Our (Sri Lankan) tour guide used these gardens as a lunch stop: unbelievable ignorance. I went hungry and went on a very fast hour's walk around the periphery and wow, was it worth every minute. Their map plus frequent helpful signposts reassured me that I'd find the way back to the entrance, which I did in exactly the hour, most of which time the rest of the party spent waiting for and eating their sandwiches. Around the gardens I met the unbelievable rainbow Eucalyptus tree with its trunk of many colours; cannon ball trees with their scented pink flowers and hard ball fruits; tall fat conifers, Durians, giant bamboos and so on.  Most plants have labels and the whole gardens are curated equal to anything in the UK.

Title: Just a nice, quiet park, not much else..
Text: We were not much impressed by the Botanical Gardens, which we found to be not much more than just a nice, quiet park. We spent no more than half an hour there, then a bit more time in a cute Laksala shop and a surprisingly good coffee shop (both of the with good ac) located inside the park, close to the entrance.

Title: Nature in its abundance
Text:
Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya are about 5.5 km to the west of the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka. It attracts 2 million visitors annually.The garden includes more than 4000 species of plants, including orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees.Attached to it is the National Herbarium of Sri Lanka. The total area of the botanical garden is 147 acres (0.59 km2), at 460 meters above sea level, and with a 200-day annual rainfall.
One needs at least half a day to trek the whole area. The weather was good. For people, who cant walk, battery operated car is run for a fee.

Title: Amazing!
Text: It's a really great place to get away from the busyness  of Kandy. We jumped on a local bus (20lkr ok.) And got dropped off right at the gate. Great walk through the gardens, palm avenues made the biggest impression on me :) watch out for the restaurant, check your bill very thoroughly!

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text: The gardens cover a large area so you could easily spend several hours here looking at the plants and trees. The highlight for us was the wild monkeys who we watched for ages playing in the trees. There is also a suspension bridge over the river which is worth a crossing

Title: Remarkable Botanic Gardens
Text:
Having lived opposite Kew Gardens in London we are used to a high standard, Peradeniya was up to this standard.
Well organised, an interesting selection exhibits, orchid house, fernery,bamboos, plant house and my favourite the palm avenues.
Towards the end of the day, as usual, there was a thunderstorm...

Title: Peaceful n beautiful gardens
Text:
Friendly guide from staff of visitor centre 
Peaceful walk 
Heaven in the centre of the city centre 
I visited in late Nov 
Guess the gardens will be more beautiful in 2 weeks time and in autumn

Title: Amazing garden
Text: We could of stayed here for the rest of the day, so so much to see, we kept getting lost which we found funny, we came across a blind dog, which brought tears to our eyes. The gardens were amazing for all to see. There are so many different varietys of plants to see here.  You must not leave Sri Lanka without seeing this place.

Title: Relaxing place for a stroll
Text: These are beautiful gardens with a wide variety of plants. Its a great place for a stroll with lots of shady areas to escape some of the heat.

Title: Variety of flora
Text: Good lung space to relax and exercise. Wide variety of plants and trees. But the entry fee is too high, especially for foreigners.

Title: Very relaxing enviroment
Text: A large expansive park in the heart of Nuwara Eliya, with extensive lawns, flower bed and a large cascading pond. A great place to relax and spend an afternoon. While i didn't visit the park at its most colourful ( Apparently this is April/ May time when all the bedding plants are in full bloom) At the point of my visit these were still being planted up.....however there's still much to see and admire. Also good for the soul.

Title: Botanical and other garden in Nuwara Eliya
Text:
Botanical Garden - Since this is located a few miles out of town, it does not attract a large number of visitors like Gregory Lake, Victoria Park etc.  However, it is a beautiful park with old trees, a nice Japanese and other landscaped gardens.  Well worth a visit to have a walk in the midst of these trees and fresh air.

A brief word on the other park/lake with which Nuwara Eliya is blessed.  Gregory lake is beautiful, but getting to be overcrowded, particularly the entrance where there are pony rides, roadside vendors and car park  all rolled into one.

Title: NOT IN FULL BLOOM BUT NICE
Text: Visited here in Jan/20, likely a couple of months before the park would be seen in its best light. It was not unexpectedly named in 1897 to commemorate the diamond jubilee of Queen Victoria. One of the gardeners gave us a tour for the better part of a half hour, clearly loving to show off the park. The birders are not forgotten nor the ophiophilists. The backside of a cobra was seen, resting among dead leaves! It is a nice spot to chill. There is a kiddies' area. The entry fee for foreigners was 300 rupees.

Title: Dead cat in the filthy river ??
Text: Very disappointing. Out of season for flowers (Feb) - I understand that, but the river in particular was full of trash and A DEAD CAT! Seriously, this is supposed to be a well manicured garden. Awful!

Title: Bird Watchers Paradise
Text: I was not very impressed with this garden. it had pretty much the same flora and fauna as in the Botanical gardens. What I was taken aback was the number of birds in this place. Certainly worth if you are into bird watching

Title: Beautiful park to spend time
Text: Located in the centre of the city, this one is a lovely park to spend some in Nuwara eliya. The entry tickets are around 200 LKR which are justified. The park has a lot of green spaces which are very well maintained. There are some rides for small kids which they would enjoy. They also have a kids train which runs within the park. The park is very well maintained. Though not a major tourist attraction, the park can surely be visited.

Title: Great play park
Text: Took the children to play before a long trip on the train. They loved running and climbing. The miniature train  ride was fun and was 50lkr   We spent about an hour here but you could bring a picnic and explore the rest of the beautiful gardens. Toilets are in the main park are very clean

Title: Pleasant to stroll through
Text: This is quite a nice park but not a 'must do'. Just make sure you pay for entry - the ticket counter is tucked away behind the gate we came through and it's not well signed to say you have to pay. We walked through on our exploration of Nuwara Eliya and it was a nice respite from the busy streets.

Title: Beautiful calm park
Text: Beautiful park and location, several local plants and fauna. Great place to spend the day or even for a picnic.

Title: Nice Park to walk
Text:
Victoria Park in Nuwara Eliya is a Nice Park to visit and have a little walk with the family. They have a children corner with a good number of games. 
Good to visit if have plenty of time in the city.

Title: Lovely park
Text: Very nice spot to spend an hour or so! There is a childrens park which is quite big but a bit knackered, still quite pleasant (if spoilt by the surly guards).

Title: Victoria Park
Text:
This park is a nicely laid out English style garden. When we visited many of the areas in the park were being renovated and so the floral displays were not fantastic.
The Public Toilets within the park were dreadful and not really fit to use, which was very disappointing.

Its worth the visit, but considerable improvement is warranted from Park Management.

Title: Victoria Park
Text: This was in our plan and a very beautiful park with a number of variety of flowers.  The park is well maintained.

Title: Nice but under constant renovation
Text: This was a nice and peaceful place to take  stroll but since it was under so much renovation, it was difficult to really get a full sense of it. It looked as if they had done a lot of projects in the past, but failed to maintain them while starting on further new projects. So it was a bit of a shame as it could have done with some TLC.

Title: Enjoying the cooler climes of..........
Text: A beautiful green space located in the very busy town of Nuwara Eliya, it was so nice to walk/stroll around amongst the greenery, we loved little england as it is known, for its colonial settlement

Title: Beautiful Park for walk
Text: Well maintained park in the heart of Nuwara Eliya. You will be able see different types of flowers. Really beautiful.

Title: Lovely urban park
Text: This park lies in the centre of the town and offers respite from its hussle.  Parts have been replanted recently, most notably the rose garden.  The herb garden is in need of similar attention.  It provides lovely space of quiet and colour

Title: a parks a park
Text: Definitely nothing to go out of your way to see. But if you do go, don't miss the museum, it's worth a visit.

Title: Green Paradise
Text: Lovely way to relax after traveling to town.  Ee spent about an hour walking through the gardens and chatting to many people

Title: Compact summary of nuwara elya
Text: The park was , small filled with green areas and photographable spots. It is a very quick tour send nice place for a memorable journey

Title: It was ok
Text: The park charges and entrance fee and that is absolutely ok however once you are inside its not amazing.  I guess Im England we are spoilt with parks and so it didnt give me a wow factor but it was a pleasant stroll to get to our restaurant across the town

Title: Tranquillity in the heart of a busy town
Text: This is a beautiful garden to visit. It costs only a nominal amount to go in and is a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

Title: Small and busy
Text: Green place with some flowers not special ones.the trees are so talk and beautiful.full of local people and at the bridge end of the park a very bad smelling pond.calm and relaxing place . I saw 3 teenage boy who were bothering 2 teenage girls and it was so sad to see such this acts on public . Walking is enjoyable at the park and it takes about 45 min to visit all the park.

Title: Needs work
Text: This park was close to out accommodation so we had some free time and thought wed take a look - 300LKR for foreigners. It looks as though there are works going on which is well overdue by the look of things. They should also look at the creek flowing through the park as it does not look or smell good. That being said it has some very good looking displays to look at.

Title: Beautifully maintained garden in the heart of the city
Text: Centrally located, this garden is very well utilized by visitors and local folk. An excellent selection of flora and fauna can be seen and appreciated in this park. Garden beds and walking tracks are well maintained. An excellent variety and colorfully flowers can be enjoyed in this park

Title: Nice park to meet locals
Text: Us foreign adults are charged 300 rupees each to enter the park, which is a bit steep in context with other Sri Lankan sites, however, hopefully the money goes towards maintaining the park. We strolled around most of the 26 acre site and enjoyed the birds and flowers. Best of all was chatting to the gardener and school children on a day trip who were keen to practice their English on us.

Title: Fun time with friendly locals
Text: There was a small entrance fee to this park, 300 Rs. It was planting season so there were some ongoing maintenance works but otherwise it was a neat little place to stroll and relax. We happened to visit when bus loads of school children were there for a field trip. They and their teachers were extremely friendly so we ended up spending our time interacting and playing with them.

Title: Great Birding Location
Text: My wife and I visited here during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka. This park as well as being beautiful is also International renowned as a must visit Birding location. The park is well laid out with easy to follow paths. Our timing wasnt perfect as many of the flowers had gone over. However, it was easy to imagine how impressive it would look in its prime. Several of the beds were already being replanted. Around the perimeter of the park there is a very smelly river, this was a magnet for many of the birds including some really sought after species - Kashmir Flycatcher, Pied Thrush, Forest Wagtail, Dusky Warbler and Sri Lanka Bush Warbler. We were so impressed were planning a second visit during our stay in Nuwara Eliya. Highly Recommended

Title: Lovely walk in Nuwara Eliya (Little England)
Text:
The overall location is worth a visit. Very interesting English style buildings throughout the town and lots of interesting things to do and see. Restaurants and cafes too.
There is a lovely park and an extensive lake, boat hire available.

Title: Lovely park
Text: Take a stroll in this park and appreciate the botany. Vegetation is aged and lush. An expanse park and a nice place for a picnic.

Title: Smells like sewage with litter in the river
Text: The park is okay and pretty in parts. However, if they are going to charge for it the park needs to be maintained. There was loads of litter in the river and all around the park. You are better off paying for a cup of tea in the Grand Hotel and wandering around their gardens, which are absolutely beautiful.

Title: No Bad
Text:
Not great but worth a look around. Still improvement work going on but a pleasant stroll. 
Places to sit and shade if you want it. 
Not a must see but good way to chill out.

Title: Take a gentle stroll
Text: It probably wasnt the most colourful time to visit. There was evidence of newly planted beds of plants, but it was too early to see them in all their splendour. There are established trees and grass and you can stroll or find somewhere to sit away from the bustle of the shopping streets. Its not a huge park, but you can enjoy the peace and watch the locals on a family visit.

Title: Lovely spot to relax
Text: If you go here do visit the little museum at the entrance on the east side (non town centre side). Its great!

Title: Beautiful park
Text: Located right in the middle of the city it is hard to miss this small and beautiful park.  Highly recommended for a short visit.  There are lots of great treats and flowers and spots to look out over the hills.

Title: not much to see in December
Text: The entry fee for foreigners is 300 rupees. December is not the best time to visit, as there was almost nothing blooming. I saw a lot of wide open green space, and local families having picnics.

Title: Not bad
Text: You can have couple of hours there, also pass on museum for few minutes if nothing else to do on the city.

Title: Lots of TLC needed
Text: Interesting that a few recent reviews mention how well maintained this park is. I had the exact opposite impression. Loads of dead or dying plants, gardens filled with weeds, shuttered toilets. It was still a nice place to kill an hour or so, sitting on a bench and enjoying the scenery and people watching. Foreigners pay an entry fee of 300 LKR. I'm not sure how they can justify charging a fee of any amount, as there are tens of thousands of parks like this around the world that are open to the public with no charge.

Title: Some areas are neglected
Text: We spent a pleasant hour walking through the park. It is a very pleasant place for families to spend time together and there is plenty of lawn area for running around. Some great specimen trees in the park. Some side areas, such as the herbal garden, need some improvement and interest taken.

Title: Lovely park
Text: Nice park for a family time.Good for picnic.There is kids playground as well.Very green and peaceful although can get a bit busy.It's beautiful but not worth a visit if you have a short time in Nuwara Eliya.It's just a park at the end of the day ??

Title: Beautiful place and nice playground
Text:
After Long car Travel the playground did the work for our 3y. 
The park is very Beautiful and nice to visit

Title: Not worth paying for....
Text: Sri Lanka likes to extract money from tourists whenever possible and to charge nearly USD2 for this poorly maintained park is scandalous. It is good for birds early morning but that's not unusual for Sri Lanka. It is a little bit of peace from the traffic (but runs along the main road) . Otherwise it is not very large and has little of interest plants wise . We were staying nearby but do not make a special trip to see it!

Title: Very poor park
Text: In one word I can say it has put the name victoria to bad name. Very poorly maintained small park. Moreover, entrance fee is very high for foreigners 300LKR which is injustice in compare to the park condition. I think this quality park can be available in every nook & corner without any entry fees. It is wastage of time, better to sit quite in any stupa. I can't recommend anybody to go there. Srilankan Govt should think what for they are taking this money?

Title: Mundane
Text: Unlike the botanical garden in the Kandy area, this is more limited and less organized. Tourists are charged a 300 rupee fee to visit, and it's a pleasant enough walk Just don't expect too much.

Title: Park with old playing area
Text: Since we were looking for a place to let our 3 years old son to play we decide to have awalk till there as we can see the playing area from the main street it was obvious that its not a time to visit and pay for nothing .swings slides .. etc were not well maintained adding to that we went after a rainy day so ground of playing area was wet and water all over the area so we did not enter the park

Title: Wrong time of year
Text: We have visited at the wrong time of year! Beds filled with just sprouting plants.  Some renovation been done. Food and drink unavailable (of basic coffee et cetera) in both kiosks.  Not worth the expensive entry fee.

Title: Well maintained Public Park
Text:
The park is located in the center of Nuwara Eliya. It is relatively a small park, which is well laid out and very well maintained. The park dates back to colonial era and is named after a British Monarch.
The park provides nesting place for many rare species of birds. A section of the park has been made into a Children Park. Overall, a good place to spend some leisurely time.

Title: Tourist trap
Text: The park is very small and you will have to pay entrance for it. 40rs for locals and 300rs (!) For foreigners. I hate this racism!

Title: A nice stroll
Text: For a Sunday aftenoon stroll in Nuwara Eliya this is a great place. The garden is very well kept and the entrance fee is just rs.300 for overseas visitors. There is a good cafe just by the entrance as well.

Title: A gentle reminder of our colonial past
Text:
For no.monely at all (£1.50 or so) you can enjoy the peace and beauty of this lovely calm park. Well maintained plants and beds and an wide range of mature trees and shaded walkways. 
Renovated in 2008, the park is reminiscent of everything English which the Victorians tried to recreate in their colonies. We met one of the garden supervisors who talked to us about the local plants and their properties. Some families were having a picnic on the grass. The garden employs 32 people who take a pride in its maintenance. A relaxed and calm place for an easy meander and reflect on our colonial past perhaps.

Title: Lovely Park
Text:
I had a couple of hours to spare in Nuwara Eliya so decided to visit Victoria Park. It was a lovely afternoon and I thought I might have a walk round and then sit on a bench to read a book. No problem there except as I entered the park I was accosted by an attendant wanting to see my ticket. I gathered I needed to pay SLR 300 to visit the park.  This is about £1.25 so I willingly paid for a ticket but it seems a lot to pay when a tea worker is only paid SLR for a day picking 20 kilos of tea leaves. 
The park is lovely and I believe the charge is only levied on foreigners but I am far from convinced that the money will go to help the plight of the underpaid workers.

Title: Beautiful and unexpected park
Text: This park is cared for fantastically by the locals. It was a relaxing and warm place to escape the usual hustle and bustle of travelling. A little bit of Victorian England saved for everyone!

Title: City Park
Text: Its a beautiful petite park in the city. Very well maintained and clean. Good a stroll early in the morning.

Title: Nice spot in the town
Text: It is in the core part of the town offering a place for relaxation, exercise and entertainment. The children's section adds value.

Title: Nice
Text: This is nice big park in nuwara eliya, looks stunning due to the weather of the place and great for evening walk

Title: Small lovely park
Text: We visited this park on a rainy day. There were few people only. They apply strict monitoring that someone inside the park approached us and asked to see our tickets. The scenery inside is just lovely! The park isnt as big as Candy Botanical Garden for example, but good for having a two- hour picnic.

Title: Good park
Text:
It is a pleasant park to visit with young kids.

The play area is good but in need of upgrade. 

It is slightly expensive for foreign tourists to visit.

Title: Stunning gardens and park
Text: We really enjoyed visiting Victoria Park. This is partly due to the fact that the grounds manager, Tony, gave us a fantastic and impromptu tour. Lots to see here and a good walk on a nice day. There isn't much cover, so it might not be much fun if it is raining. Wonderful to see families out and about enjoying the park.

Title: Pay to get into the park?
Text: Not sure why Sri Lanka, the most beautiful country , who already charge tourists a fortune feel the need to charge us to walk a few hundred metres in a park .. surely it's a public space ? Found it ridiculous. Looked nice from the outside but seriously nothing special. Very disappointed in the tourist industry for this charge.

Title: Worth a wander
Text: Dont expect the full botanical garden experience but a wander around Victoria Park is a pleasant way to pass the time. Plantings are a bit mixed but they are trying hard and the wide open lawns are well used by couples and families.

Title: A good place for a relaxed walk
Text:
We went here on a sunny morning in Nuwara Eliya. We were looking for a place to have a walk around after a day of touring in a Tuk Tuk.
It costs 300LKR per adult to enter the park.
First stop was the small museum. It's mostly photos grouped in categories. It's interesting how Nuwara Eliya was essentially developed around the tea industry.
Walking around the park is a pleasant way to spend time. It's a mix of a typical British park with tropical overtones - the locals work hard to keep the park neat and tidy and keep vegetation from taking over. Some parts were clearly a work in progress, other areas trimmed and manicured.
The colonial roots of the park are obvious.
Worth a visit

Title: Busy Little Park in Nuwara Eliya
Text: I visited this park along with the rest of our bird watching group on one afternoon after doing Horton Plains Natl. Park that morning.  We stopped for a few hours primarily to find a few unusual birds that were tough to locate anywhere else.  This park was very busy (people everywhere), but we managed to find our own space for the most part away from the crowds.  Lots of flowers and for the most part good landscaping - just ignore some of the waterways as they are full of trash (and rats running around).  This could be a top notch little park if it was cleaned up a bit; just too much garbage laying around.

Title: Pleasant Small Park
Text:
The park is very close to the Grand Hotel so you can easily combine visiting both.

It is a small park which seemed to be very popular with Sri Lankans. It is well maintained but cant be compared to the gardens in Kandy.

Title: Good Park
Text: Very good garden on the top of the Mountain with chilled whether good activity place with ample plain surface

Title: Bit disappointing
Text:
Maybe it was the time of year we were there ( February) however Victoria Gardens was very disappointing! I would not pay to see gardens like this in February. 
Not too pleased at having to pay a lot more than the locals for entry! Surely the entrance price should be the same for everyone!

Title: Nice place to relax
Text: I didnt come in the right season to see the flowers in bloom but if youre looking for a quiet place that could be in England, this is the place. Theres a small museum with photos from the 1940s which show how different life was under English rule. Theres also a cafe with Italian coffee and Sri Lankan food at the north end of the park

Title: Pleasant, but could be so much better!
Text: We decided to spend an hour wandering in the park and at first sight it looked very attractive . However, I don't think much of the 300 rupee entrance fee is spent on litter collection, as the place is filthy.

Title: Victoria park
Text: Bit early as planting just starting. Would imagine beautiful in the Spring . Felt sorry for ladies raking the grass. Bet on only few rupees.

Title: Neatness, unexploited and well maintained are the USP
Text: Has lots of varieties of flowers, shrubs and also very ancient trees preserved and taken care of. A nice stroll makes it very refreshing and soothing.

Title: Disappointing
Text: I think it must be the wrong time of year to visit this park as it wasnt very pretty as expected! Nevertheless an ok walk.

Title: More charging of foreigners
Text: Costs 300 rupees for foreigners to enter, so we didnt. We only wanted to take a short cut from our accommodation to town so went the long way instead. Looks an ok park from what we saw but its just a park for goodness sake.

Title: Nice park for family and friends
Text: Good park to be fun and relax with family and friends. For foriegners ticket is 300LKR. 30 min to 1 hour is good to be there. But this park is not same beauty all the year. April to July us great. Very good place for especially children because it has good children park. For adults there isnt much..

Title: Nice Park
Text: If in this area then a walk around the park is a good time to spend, in the central town area by the market and local shops.

Title: Out of season
Text: Victoria Park is nice for a stroll, we were there a bit too early in the growing season as no roses or other English flowers were in flower.  Lots of gardeners working away so guess it is better later in the year.

Title: Good looking park
Text: If you like to walk through a botanical garden than you will like the park. It is a small version of a botanical garden. Pleasent environment with an entry fee of 300 rupies.

Title: Pleasent place to walk around
Text: A nice and pleasent walk at Victoria Park. Not well maintained but still have nature beauty. Just to spend 15-30 mins.

Title: Pleasant City Park
Text: This is quite a nice park, in the center of Nuwara Eliya. Most of the visitors are Sri Lankan, either locals or tourists. Victoria Park is overshadowed, however, by the truly spectacular Hakgala Botanical Garden a short drive away. If you only have time for one garden Hakgala is your choice.

Title: Beautiful Park but not well maintained
Text: It is a beautiful park in Nuwara Eliya have a good collection of flowers and plants. I loved the colonial feel of the park and the vast collection of flowers. The maintenance was not proper.  The water in the ponds look dirty and stinky.  The children play area is not clean at all.  All the play equipment are rusted and no maintenance. I loved the colonial feel of the park and the vast collection of flowers.

Title: Pleasant park.
Text: This is a pleasant park with some interesting trees and plants. Also some interesting features such as a japanese garden and various ponds and buildings. It also has a childrens play area. We enjoyed a pleasant 90 minutes   wandering in here after paying the small entry fee.

Title: Ridiculous you have to pay to enter
Text: This is merely a standard park with flowers etc like anywhere in the U.K. or world. We walked down not realising you had to pay per person to enter. We didnt bother as all its done is rain since we arrived and we certainly werent paying to walk round what is a standard park...not great tbh. This should be free to all public.

Title: Nice enough
Text: This is a nice, well manicured park and worth a short walk around. It didn't blow my socks off, and it wasn't particularly more special than other parks you might have seen, but it was a pleasant stroll.

Title: Nice
Text: A very nice large park.. wonderful view.. sunny with good weather.. a nice place to spend a day .. small fine museum there

Title: Lovely little park
Text:
Its not quite like the Royal Botanical outside of Kandy, but its still a lovely little park to have lunch or chill for an hour.
There is a charge for foreigners but its not expensive and I presume it will go to the upkeep of the park.
There are toilets either side men and women respectively but these are the hole in the floor type.

Title: Nice park to hangout
Text: Really nice park close to where we were staying, there is an entrance fee but did not bother us too much (300 rupees).

Title: Very poor maintenance
Text: Once this used to be a lovely park, but now its not maintained properly. Also there should be arrows guiding people where to head next.

Title: Dissapointing
Text: Nothing to see, It was a waste of time. My advice is, go to the botanical garden in Kandy instead id rate it 1/10. I managed to take some good shots of the park.

Title: Beautiful park in Nuwaraeliya town
Text: Fascinating park in nuwaraeliya town. Lovely landscaping. Need to pay entrance fee. but its worth to pay and hangout in this beautiful garden.

Title: Poor
Text: This is just an area in the city centre called a Park it's in a negelected state.They charge you to enter.Just skip it not worth.

Title: Healthy shrubs throughout.
Text: If you are in the area, this park is well worth a short visit.  Huge pride and care has been taken with the overall layout and it is ideal place to relax and spend some quiet time during your stay.  It is basically a place to sit or take photographs or go for a walk.

Title: Nice gardens
Text: I spent about an hr here , cost 500 rupees, I would consider it a botanical garden not just a park. Theres a greenhouse as well but was locked, all the flowers are well kept. I enjoyed.

Title: A mix of style and kitsch
Text:
This is the first time in my life that I paid an entrance fee to get to a park. Not that much, but it's there. As everywhere at Sri Lanka, foreigners have different rates than locals. 
The park is interesting, I would say, reminds me somehow Great Britain. The trees and plants are taken good care of. You can find also some statues at the place. Some of them are nice, some of them are straightforward kitsch.  
There are also toilets at the park, but at the time that I visited the park, the particular toilet building that I was passing was not working at the time, so you can't totally count with that.

Title: Pay to enter
Text: The initial surprise here was paying 400 rupees per person to enter. I don't think I've encountered a city or town park in the UK or Europe you pay to enter. But it is only £1.40 and the park is very nice. Small, only 800 metres if you enter through one gate and go straight to exit the other but with other paths within the park and pretty arrays of flowers, shrubs and trees it is a quiet respite from the busy town.

Title: Dirty and expensive!
Text:
I arrived at the eastern gate at 7.10 am.  The park is supposed to be open at 7 am. There was no one at the ticket window. The security man said come back at 7.30. I said  but it should be open now. He then demanded to see my ID! Whatever for?
      I left and went to the main gate, which was open. The entrance fee for foreigners is 400lkr!
        I have an interest in birds so walked slowly around the park. I didnt see many birds.. but piles of rubbish and litter everywhere!

Title: Pleasant place to chill out
Text: Well maintained gardens.  Pleasant to walk around. Good to see so many locals enjoying this facility.  Good variety of lovely flowers

Title: Well Laid Out : Feast to the eyes
Text: Victoria Park is a small but well laid out botanical park that is home to a large number of flora. Good place for photographs.

Title: Poorly managed. Not worth the entrance fee.
Text:
Victoria Park, Nuwara Eliya

First thing to note, although this is common, foreigners (you) get charged 300 rupees to enter. Locals are free. 

We paid our fee to the lady behind the counter. As I turned around a male guard asked to check my ticket. Hed just seen me buy it but never mind. 
We saw signs stating no plastic bottles or bags were allowed as they become litter. 

The place was filthy with litter of all types but mostly plastic bottles. In one of the free flowing water areas there were several old tyres which had clearly been there for ages.  It was obvious the bottles were not all from the day before due to the condition or grubbiness  of them. We picked some up and gave them to one of the many guards and staff but there was too much for us to manage. 
No one appeared to be proactively litter picking when our perception was that a person could have been tasked with this.  

There was clearly ongoing work judging by the piles of garden debris but again our perception, this appeared to an effort to tidy the place up when it had been neglected over time. 

We noticed some of the plants were covered in graffiti scratched into their leaves. Some people eh! But then we saw what appeared to be locals rather than foreigners doing exactly that. Despite the wealth of staff and uniformed guards this behaviour was unchallenged so we did, loudly.
These plants surrounded a water feature which was not in operation. There was a wooden jetty into the feature which looked 20 years past its prime, basically derelict and in need of removal. 

I know this is not main season so the gardens would not be at their best but the overall impression was of poor and overdue management. 

Overall we were disappointed and would not recommend this unless you have nothing else to do. 

So we left and walked up to the nearby lake which was even worse! Again we were asked to buy a ticket, from where we were we could see rubbish floating everywhere.  Dont bother unless you want to see a few horses tethered. 

Nuwara Eliya is grossly overrated and was a shame to waste two booked nights there.

Title: Great place to spend the weekend
Text: A beautiful place for picnics or just spending the day. A lot of people come here on the weekends. There are lots of activities such as jet ski rides,  paddle boats or speed boats. Scenery is just stunning . Centrally located and well worth a visit or a picnic with the family.  Plenty of parking areas and long foot paths for walking.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Simply amazing ?? it was so beautifully arranged and greener. Really enjoyed. Just like a little England !!

Title: Interesting garden
Text: We had a lovely walk around the gardens. One of the gardeners took us around for awhile until he realised we were happy to amble on our own. Its well laid out although there was way too much litter around. Very interesting selection of plants. The little museum in the grounds was well worth popping into.

Title: Victoria Park
Text: Very well maintained park. If you staying in the city, it is within walking distance. Good place to take a stroll.

Title: Cute and nice
Text: An easy stroll in the park. Flowers were blooming, weather was so cool and nice- a simple park which was easy to walk in and get closer to nature in an easy way!

Title: Good place for a stroll
Text: Just in the middle of the city, well maintained clean and green. In a Victorian design. If you have some free time to spend.

Title: Nice oasis
Text: A pleasant place to wander around, in the nice fresh temperatures of Nuwara Eliya. We weren't that impressed with the town overall, but this, along with a couple of the hotels, was the highlight.

Title: A breath of fresh air
Text: Pay a small entry fee. Lovely space for the children to enjoy and the gardens are well maintained. A highlight in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Nice Place for a stroll
Text: Nurses Elita is a place for families of Sri Lanka to gather. The park is no exception. Lovely to see so many families enjoying the beautiful grounds.  Some spectacular trees including a flowering bouganvillia arch.  A little expensive for tourists but still a worthwhile place to spend a few hours.

Title: Beautiful gardens
Text: Lovely peaceful gardens, lawn and flowers worth a visit , we enjoyed relaxing after a big hike . Stop after for a refreshing cup of tea with local products.

Title: Himalayan migrants
Text:
I visited this delightful park on a sunny afternoon with the main aim of birdwatching  . The park was buzzing with families , couples and groups of schoolchildren enjoying themselves . The planted beds were attractive and a few neglected areas were being worked on . 
  My main focus was along a stream inside the park boundary where I had close views of a variety of birds including two scarce Himalayan migrants ; Pied Ground Thrush and Kashmiri Flycatcher .

Title: Disappointing
Text: This was the only place in Sri Lanka which disappointed us. It should be lovely but it seems neglected and in a poor state. It is apparently under renovation but is not worth visiting at present. I even heard of someone who demanded a refund because they were so disappointed.

Title: So much potential but full of litter
Text:
We visited Victoria Park twice during our time in Nuwara Eliya. The first time to just explore and the second time for a nature walk organised through the hotel.

There is an entrace fee for the park, which would be fine if the park was actually maintained with the fee. We were incredibly dismayed by the sheer amount of litter in the park. Surely someone or a community group could organise some clean ups (if I had had a spare bag and gloves during our visit I would have happily removed some of the plastic waste myself).

Rubbish aside, the park is a pleasant place to spend some time. There were plenty of flowers out when we visited (albeit the same as the ones we frequently see in the UK) and different areas to explore. Many local children come to play games as well as couples and larger families just enjoying the surrounds.

From a nature perspective there were a few bird species and squirrels but not the rich levels elsewhere in Sri Lanka.

Title: Small park with vast greenery
Text: The park has to see some proper family entertainment facilities. I understand it is kept green for a reason but it has to go beyond its current state of boredom.

Title: Pretty and well maintained park
Text: This park is very pretty and well maintained. It is like most European parks so to see in sri Lanka is something. Nice for a leisurely walk - but not a must see.

Title: Lush Green & Eye Soothing
Text: What a wonderful lush green this place is. You see a variety of beautiful and unique trees and plantation all around the park. Truly an unforgettable scenery. We are photographers and went with kids and captured some wonderful scenes and kids really enjoyed it. Entry ticket price was reasonable. Highly recommended.

Title: Bird Watch
Text:
This is an attractive park, well maintained and serene. Its a good place for bird watching. The well manicured lawns and originality will take you down the British era.

The town is just around it and so is the golf course, a functional bygone era post office throngs the small town center with a trade mark clock tower..a so obvious British trade mark :)

Title: The mighty park
Text: A huge and massive park located in the City with lot of places to roam around. completely green and a good place for taking a lot of photographs

Title: Great Park for a stroll and a picnic
Text:
We stopped in town and picked up some lunch and then wandered over to Victoria Park for a stroll and to have a picnic. 

There is an small entrance fee for non residents but we found it was worth it as the gardens are maintained and we had a lovely spot in the grass away from the hustle and bustle of town.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Just in the city centre itself, good enough for walks and for enjoying the trees... reasonably maintained

Title: Very nice Victoria ganesh garden  of British legacy
Text: Nice garden in the heart of town , next to bus station.  Beautiful CALIFORNIA trees 100 years old nicely maintained

Title: Lovely Park
Text: This english style park is really lovely and you dont expect to see that kind of place in the middle of the mountains of Sri Lanka.  Many flowers and very well maintained garden. Worth a visit.

Title: Ok
Text: Payment to walk through gardens a surprise, not extensive plantings,no labelling.Further out by racecourse a lovely hotel with quaint English garden in front with  full descriptions.

Title: Pleasant
Text: Not much to say, set in middle of town, nice walk through, parts could do with a spruce up but generally well maintained. Surprised to have to pay to go into park. Split into different sections. Whilst your in town, take a look at the post office, very quaint.

Title: A small garden..
Text: A small and beautiful garden in the middle of the city .. nothing is a special .. it took us 15 minutes to finish the tour inside the garden.. if you have something else  to do in nuwara eliya go for it.

Title: A lovely park
Text: Obviously the adverse weather over January had delayed the plantings but this is still a lovely park and was being worked on and well maintained. Still worth a visit.

Title: Well maintained city park
Text: For foreigners there's an entry fee, and to be honest nothing great about this park, its just like any other city park. The rose garden was disappointing.

Title: A nice place to walk
Text: Lots of visitors and a great place to walk. Downside is the smell of the river near by. There's a small kids park as a plus.

Title: Just any other park
Text:
Is it a nice Park?
Yes
Is it worth 200 (for foreigners)?
NOOO!
Very basic park which one can find in every city.

Title: Ok park but great for twitchers!
Text: Seemed a bit steep to pay R300 to get in for what is just an ordinary, park with a few small gardens. However its a haven for birdwatching where we saw a pied thrush as well as a number of endemic Sri Lankan birds. Loads of twitchers in the park actually and some very helpful local ones too.

Title: Stunningly beautiful
Text: We visited here in the early morning looking for birds and it was SO peaceful just strolling around amongst an immaculately kept garden full of amazing trees, shrubs and plants.

Title: A nice walk, but nothing special for the entrance fee
Text: Its just the local park, not intended as a tourist destination, but as there is not much to do in Nuwara Eliya, if you have spare time you could go for a pleasant walk there. There is nowhere much to shelter if it is raining though, so better on a nice day. It has a large pond, a rose garden, lots of trees and a fountain.

Title: Supremely average tourist trap
Text:
I would not recommend this place for non-Sri Lankans. If you want well kept gardens in Nuwara Eliya you should visit some of the hotel gardens nearby; The Grand, The Hill Club or St Andrews Jetwings. These are all free and much, much better.
Victoria gardens is a baffling 300rs for tourists and 10-15rs for locals. Definitely more of a park than gardens. I would not visit again.

Title: Ok
Text: Pleasant enough place to wander around for an hour or two. Some interesting trees and plants and a good play area for kids. 300 rupees entry for foreigners. Small museum but not much in it. Lots of well dressed school kids who are always interested in talking to you in their rather shy and naive manner.

Title: A place where local couples meet
Text: It is definitely not a highlight. Average - unless you want to walk to relax. If you lack time, you will not miss much.

Title: Is this a park???
Text: The park is not well maintained at all! Its cheap to enter but still not worth the money. Maybe you will find some intressting birds as we saw a lot of photorgraphers but the park is not nice at all.

Title: Could be so much nicer
Text: The park is quite large and a peaceful enclave away from the bustle of the town, even though it's a very short walk from the bus station. The biggest issue is litter. There is a SLR300 charge for foreigners - it wouldn't take much to employ some litter pickers from this.

Title: Small entrance fee
Text: As usual a small foreign tourist entrance fee but not expensive , Lots of flowers and a Japanese Garden . Really its best because its very noisy once you exit the park to the shops and bus station.

Title: One of the worst ever
Text:
At the gate after buying entry tickets you are guided towards the museum, big sign Silence, black and white photos the latest 1940.
The park no flowers at this time of year, scruffy with big signs saying No Playing in the Park, and Behave with decorum.
Enjoy at your peril!

Title: A reasonable oasis near the hectic town/bus station
Text: This is a modest sized park with a lot of history. It`s  busy, well used ,safe for all. the audience is mainly the young kids plus 25-40`s.  No loud music,has a cafe and little areas with attractions that make a stroll worthwhile. You could do it all in no more than 30 minutes

Title: Not bad... Not bad.
Text:
Nice to stretch the legs. 
Have a look at the post office slightly down the road in Swiss? Architecture. 

I would not go out of my way just for the park but it is nice if you are passing by. through.

Title: Average park
Text: It is just an ordinary park but a tourist attraction of this area. Good for families but not a park for full day activity. There is a children play area inside as well but on rainy day it is very messy.

Title: Out of season in January
Text:
This is probably a nice park in season, but in January it has little to offer except green lawns populated by pick-nicking groups and--unfortunately--feral dogs.

The park was mostly clean, and there are three types of bins set up to encourage recycling.  No signs in English on those, so you will have to open them up to gauge what is appropriate.  However, there are some signs in English: one of them admonishing us to "Behave Decently."  I did my best.

It is only Rs. 300 to get in.

Title: Beautifully maintained park
Text:
Lovely park to spend an hour or two.

Everything is very well maintained and the flowers are beautiful.

I walked around for about an hour, then sat and read a book.

Very British feel to it.

Title: A very nice English style park
Text: Victoria Park is quite large and beautifully green.  Well worth a stroll around, especially the herb garden.

Title: January visit not worth the entry fee
Text: Its only 300 rupees each but nothing was in flower etc so not worth a visit in my view. Other times of year may be better of course.

Title: Tiny and litter
Text: This is nice and in the middle of town - but its very small and lots of litter which really makes it unpleasant in parts - expensive for what it is

Title: Can be skipped, nothing great
Text:
It's an ordinary garden, nothing great about it.
We just walked around and we're out in less than an hour.
Don't spend money and time on this location.

Title: Not as nice as we had been led to understand
Text: Having paid the entry fee we were disappointed with the state of the gardens.  Maintenance seemed to be lacking in many places and the children's play area didn't offer much more than 10mins worth of distraction for our two.  The miniature train is cute, but it didn't entice our kids to wait in line.

Title: Nice place to relax
Text: This is a very large park, very well maintened grassland and trees. Together with other neighboring public parks and lake makes this Nuwara Eliza looks like a very nice European or a new world town. A good place to relax or take your kids to ride on a pony.

Title: Dont miss the faris wheel!
Text: The pack is really nice (except for requiring to pay entrance fee!) - there's a kids corner, where you can find the unique attraction. Diesel-engine powered faris wheel! You may even see the staff climbing up to the top and hanging on the cart to get it spinning. It's quite surreal to see... :)

Title: Ok for a quick look- see
Text: Not quite sure why you have to pay to walk around a park but there you go - pleasant enough 30 - 45mins unless you have kids maybe longer.

Title: Very pretty park
Text: Lovely park to wander around or relax in. A small fee for foreign guests of 300 rupees. Worth a visit.

Title: Relax or Fun
Text: Its a good place to be with kids families friends or with your partner. Either you want to relax on the grassy ground and benches or walk in between huge flower beds. Huge  botanical variation of flowers and plants. Decorated with water fountains and nice little paths. Recommend for families and this is one of the must see locations in Nuwara Eliya..

Title: Nice place to while away half an hour or so
Text:
We strolled through the park after having been cooped up in our room due to cxld program and rain.
A nice park. Not big, not fancy, but clean.
For us it was a breath of fresh air (in both meanings) as Nurawa Eliya was such a disappointment for us.

Title: Something to do
Text: Victoria park is quite nice and well kept - you have to pay to enter but it's a nice activity as Nuwara Eliya offers few things to do. The park is quite big and has a lot of places to sit. There is a play area for children.

Title: Very pretty
Text: Lovely, well manicured garden with huge variety of flowers all of which were in bloom in August. Very relaxed environment and pleasant place to take a walk. Seems popular with tourists and locals alike.

Title: A victorian park that needs a bit of TLC in the gardening department
Text: Victoria park is a fairly typical Victorian style park, only in Sri Lanka. The gardens are not particularly well maintained and there are signs that say you cannot play in the park. With an entry fee that is a little on the hefty side, I felt it was not good value.

Title: Small garden
Text: Perhaps the time of the year isn't right as we didn't see many flowers blooming. Small garden for evening walks. Completed it less then an hour.

Title: Great place for nature lover
Text:
This is some wonderful green experience. It has Lilly garden very well maintained. 
You can complete the park within 2 hours very easily by walking.

Title: Average park you pay to enter
Text:
We had a nice walk around the park but it's really nothing special, especially having been to Kandy Botanical Gardens and walking through the beautiful country side around Nuwara Eliya. 
We did see a lot of bird watchers so presumably its good for that.  
Maybe it has more going on at other times of the year....

Title: Pay for nothing to see
Text: 15 minutes max in this park, not much to see, and you have to pay for the visit... Go to the botanical garden instead!!!

Title: Very nice park in the middle of a busy city
Text: We really enjoyed walking around Victoria Park.  Very nice trees, well manicured lawn and plants and it's just fun to people watch here.  Everyone was having a good time, including three Buddhist monks who were constantly taking selfies of each other.  In tis busy, crowded and noisy city, it's a nice refuge from the craziness.

Title: Typical park
Text: Really odd to have to pay to walk around a park. Nothing special about it really.  It is quiet and has some lovely areas of flowers fairly typical of a park.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: The atmosphere and the views were amazing, the trees and the flowers were well engineered and the weather was super pleasant, I would recommend this place for everyone looking for a quiet place and fresh air.

Title: Ho hum.Not Worth the Entrance Fee
Text: Our guest stay looked over the park and we thought we would have a look.Entrance was 500rp if I remember correctly and it wasnt worth it.The Park wasnt as nice as it could be and needed a lot of work.To give it credit we were there just after the planting of the annuals so in 3 months it could be a different story.Lots of locals enjoying the gardens and met the gardeners who were very proud of their garden.Needs work to honour the entrance fee.Not Missing much if you walk around it

Title: Big and Old but beautifully designed and kept
Text:
Victoria Park is very beautiful with thousands  of years old trees,  many different types of plant species. Where i have hardly seen any ehere else. It is well maintained and designed in such a way. That every one can relax and spend time here. 
Children were playing in their own areas. Couples were relaxing and enjoying the peaceful environment. Chatting and sitting care free on the green velveteen grass spread all over the garden.  Elderly people were walking around with their grand children. Happily chatting and moving in different areas. We spend almost two hours there then also some parts were left to explore, it's big and  

Must visit in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Smaller than Peradenya Botanical Gardens
Text: Good place to walk. Garden is not well maintained and a number of flower beds were found to be barren. However, the older trees were beautiful as were the green lawns.

Title: nice for a stroll, killing time
Text: When you need killing some time in Nuwara Eliya, and have checked-out already the various quirky old English style buildings (Post Office, Office of the Police Superintendent, etc.), and when you're tired of the hussle and bussle of the shopping street, this park offers an oasis pf quietness.  For a small entrance fee it's nice to have a quiet stroll, and look at old palm trees or check-out some manicured planted area's (for example in the Japanese garden).

Title: A park
Text: For 300LKR you can enter this park. It has everything a park usually has. And having that said, it is nothing special. There is an area specially made for children where they can play.

Title: Good place to spend time
Text: A good variety of plants and flowers, well maintained park, serene atmosphere. Not a very large place though

Title: Trees ??!
Text: The beauty of this park catch my attention to see whats the true meaning of natural nature. Im very thankful because Ive been in this beautiful place. Thank you for all the people here in Sri Lanka!

Title: Lovely place and cool
Text: This was a nice garden situated in Nuwara Eliya .We had lunch siting here during our visit to Kandy while on our Sri Lanka tour organized by Arooha tours. This place has nice flowers near by stalls and pony rides as well

Title: Boring and another foreigners fee to enter
Text: Only went in to kill some time. Nothing much to see - took 10 minutes to walk through it. As usual,  an entrance fee vigourously enforced - not much in the scheme of things -  but annoying anyway.

Title: Well worth the money
Text: Spent a long time here looking at the wonderful trees and a few flowers as not the best season for blooms. Met Tony the head gardener we think very knowledgeable & gave us a few blooms to hold camphor leaves to smell fantastic man

Title: Needs better maintenance
Text: Not much to see in January in the gardens. The little stream was full of rubbish and the lawns needed mowing. OK for a quick visit on a nice day.

Title: Very sweet spot - a perk in the city
Text:
Well maintained, clean, calm. A good break from the more energetic surroundings and a nice path through the city. A small shop in the middle serve tea etc.
Entry fee LKR 300.

Title: Slightly neglected - maybe better in the spring!
Text:
Foreigners are charged 300 rupees to visit and that is fine if the park was kept in good condition. In December it all looks a bit 'tatty' - a park gardener was happy to tell us how lovely it looks in April. 
So for now, just a place to stroll for 20 minutes!

Title: A quaint little park
Text: Definitely a must see in Nuwara Eliya, but please be mindful that this is a very small park.  One could finish walking around in 30 minutes or less.  We took our time and just enjoy walking inside of the park.

Title: Well kept town park and appreciated by birds too
Text:
This is a lovely open space in the middle of the town. We visited for the birdlife that can be seen there. Early morning is the best time before there is too much disturbance from human visitors. As well as the obvious egrets in the open areas there are different birds all along the stream and vegetation on the opposite side of the park. This is a site for wintering Pied Thrush

At the time of one of our visits see saw two wedding parties having photographs taken.

There are small kiosks for buying drinks and snacks.

Odd quirk - mens and womens toilets are at opposite sides of the park.

Title: Ok place for an afternoon
Text: Nice relaxing park - crazily English except the fact that you have to pay to get in! Well maintained and very clean. Well policed and very safe. Ok children's area which gave our kids some space to run around. Ok for a spare relaxing afternoon if you have one.

Title: A taste of Little England
Text: Loved the place and the endless array of trees and flowers.  Nice place for a stroll with a loved one. Quiet and serene. Be sure to bring a sweater

Title: Try to catch the gardener for a tour
Text:
By chance we bumped into the head gardener who gave us a very good tour. I suspect he does this for a few tourists and we did give him a tip.  We left with a much better knowledge of plants in Sri lanka. 
At 300 LKA to enter its only a couple of UK £ so we did not begrudge that . And compared with the nearby town bustle and fumes its a place of peace and quiet. It was also close to our hotel so a pleasant walk.

Title: Worth a visit I guess
Text: Not being used to having to pay to visit a public park I guess one feels a little hard done by when all our parks are free to all. At 300 LKR I guess it is not a lot but the standard then one would expect to be higher. A asmall variety of colour was on display. Apart from the odd tree label none of the flower beds gave any description. Obviously popular to the locals on a Sunday with a children's area also. Really only an average garden good for a stroll.

Title: City garden
Text:
Nice city garden in the middle of city. Have children play area. Good for walk for elders. 
I feel entry tickets should not be there at morning times for elder tourist who go there for morning walks.

Title: Its expensive but must visit if you like Nature
Text: The Victoria Park is much like a botanical garden with varied trees and flowering plants. It also has sprawling green lawns and a play area for kids. The entry fee is LKR 300 and is open from 7am to 7pm on all days.  The park was christened in 1897 to commemorate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.

Title: It's just fine, not as good as the Botanical Garden in Kandy
Text: It's just fine, not as good as the Botanical Garden in Kandy but great if you want to walk around and see Srilankan families relaxing.

Title: Excellent tour by head gardener
Text:
Head gardener gave us a special tour through "his" park. He was very knowledgeable having studied 2 years in Kandy, owning many books of German botanical gardens and working already 16 years in this park. Many flowers and trees were presented by their German name. 
Although I have to agree with another feedback that there is waste laying around, the excellent tour outweighed this fact by far!

Title: Sri Lanka with friends
Text: Beautifully kept gardens, we spent about an hour here just meandering around, I was taken aback by the size and number of the Bamboo and also some of the huge old trees.

Title: Garden visit
Text: We went there with three kids. Nice and calm place. There is a small park for younger kids to play in.

Title: Beautiful and Green
Text: Beautiful green park that all enjoys. Groups, kids, all. Also a golf course nearby. A nice stroll, a nice place.

Title: Great birding stop
Text: Classic Victorian-era Botanic Garden, with some wonderful notices " All clergys get free entry"  "Behave decently"; also a great birding spot, with Indian Pitta, Pied Thrush and Kashmir Flycatcher on our short late afternoon visit.

Title: Small park in the middle of the city
Text:
The park in the middle of the city just next to the main bus station. Nicely kept but too much noise from the roads around the park. Small green house about 10 meter square with nothing worthy to see. 
They have a small play ground for children with a horse ride.
Nice stroll for people who like to walk away from the busy streets with good paved walking path. 
Good roses display and they have some benches for resting or reading. 
The charge to enter is 300 rupes for tourist and much less for locals.

Title: Nice gardens but surreal!
Text: Almost feels like bring in London, but not quite. Pretty gardens and make for a relaxing stroll but the hills and tea plantations outweigh it in beauty.

Title: Green spot in the heart of Nuwara Eliya!
Text: Excellent green spot in the heart of Nuwara Eliya.  Pleasant place for a stroll, picnic, or for kids to play.

Title: Stroll in the park
Text: We visited the park twice during this years stay in Nuwara Eliya. It being February the whole place was in its Landscape maintenance phase, and since we had frost in the mornings, many of the new plantings were under protective covers, but it was still well worth the entrance fee.

Title: Very nice park
Text: Very nice park in the middle of Nuwara Elyia. Very nice to see the local people and the school children. Everybody was talking to us, we enjoyed it.

Title: Interact with the locals
Text: Visited this park just before a rainy shower - beautiful variety of shrubs, flowers and trees, well maintained and thoughtfully designed. Heavy rainfall led to us taking shelter in the park's central shelter where we found many families enjoying their day out; we ended up making lots of new friends, young and old. There is a reasonably priced restaurant at the entrance with an adequate, if very limited menu, as well as a cafe inside the park serving drinks and snacks. Staff are friendly and helpful and the park was a welcome change from the frantic pace of the surrounding area. Stray dogs abound but pose no problem as they peacefully coexist with park goers and simply sit watching the world go by - I recommend you do the same in this beautiful park.

Title: A pleasant stroll
Text:
Any place should be evaluated based on what it offers, not for what we hope to find there. Victoria Park was not meant to be a tourist attraction. It's a local public park with some interesting history.

We visited in February and it seemed some of the beauty had faded away in the winter months and some planting and gardening works were going on. I bet it looks much more beautiful in Spring and Summer. We still found it to be a lovely park for a pleasant stroll while also exploring some of its historic areas and trees. The playground had lots of fun rides and our daughter enjoyed them a lot. Like most places we visited in Sri Lanka, mornings and evenings seem to be the best times to visit the park.

Ticket prices are very reasonable and should be appreciated because the money goes into the maintenance and upkeep of the park. I recommend it for tourists who appreciate leisurely walks in relaxing settings.

Title: Pleasant "English" park
Text: This is not terribly exciting but a pleasant place to spend an hour or 2. Several interesting birds and one of the gardeners took us under his wing, so to speak and showed us birds we would not have seen by ourselves.

Title: Very disappointing
Text: Just a park like any other Victoria park in the world apart that it is paying... old playarea, tacky train ride...

Title: Not the real Sri Lanka but still part of history
Text: The road from Kandy to Nuwara is a must see in Sri Lanka. The nature is remarkable. Then you get in Nuwara and oops, well, this is not Sri Lanka. This is a colonial British style, but still the town with its green scenery and Victoria park is a pleasure for the eyes. The park itself is not something you cannot miss (it just look like a park) but the whole Nuwara is something different to feel in Sri Lanka.

Title: Interesting gardens
Text: The garden supervisor took us around the gardens and showed us lots of plants, extremely knowledgeable and friendly. They had lost a lot of plants to frost the week before and I believe these gardens are at their best in the spring.

Title: Expensive municipal park
Text: A small park in the centre of the city, with a very steep entrance fee for foreigners (as elsewhere, locals get almost for free). Not worth the money or the time wasted.

Title: Brilliant gardener
Text: We visited one morning and spent a couple of hours wandering about looking at the flowers.  The thing which made thus such a brilliant experience was only that the Gardener Tony started chatting to us and basically gave us a free guided tour telling us about each flower.  I'm not that into flowers personally but his enthusiasm was so infectious that you couldn't help but enjoy it!

Title: A park for walk
Text:
It is a normal park where you can go for a walk and spend some time.
Not a must go place but if you have leisure time then you can go for a walk.

Title: Very beautiful park and well maintained
Text: This is pretty ancient part with lush green grass and variety of flowers. I am sure you gonna like it. The park also have a connectivity to children park with lots of swings options for kids. Park has entrance fees of 300 LKR per person. But a must go place.

Title: Not much
Text:
Park entry is 300 roepies for a foreigner, 40 for a local.
For Sri Lanka standards, that is pretty high.
So I was very dissapointed to see all the plastic rubbish lying in the park in the ditches, all the grass groing out of the pavement, and some buildings needing a make over 10 years ago already....

Title: This is a children's park can't walk freely as a couple
Text: Before we arrived here we think this park to be nice place to visit. But when we entered the park it was nice but as a couple we can't sitting,hanging hands together or a doing a funny things.. because one of the security lady coming and scolding us "don't doing this and this,this is a children's park" so after this stuff we are went out the park. I really hate this place and I'm not recommended this place to anyone.

Title: Fantastic experience
Text:
As a keen horticulturalist we took a walk through the park and met the head gardener . Never caught his name , but a great guy with a passion for plants. We spent an hour together walking around sharing our knowledge , and he gave us a personal tour of the parks special plants .
Great that you can go half way around the world and meet someone with a very similar passion and interest.

Title: Beware entry fee rip-off
Text:
I was deeply shocked to be asked for 300 rupees to enter this park. Whether this is the official foreigner rate or a scam I don't know. In England parks are free. I have no objection, as an overseas visitor, to making a reasonable contribution to Sri Lankan parks such as this but excessive demands will result in NO revenue. I just walked away.

If an individual was trying to make a dishonest charge, he should be sacked. If not the authorities need to review their charges. It would be sensible if charges were advertised at the entrance. A tax rate of 0% or 100% will yield nothing. An excessive park charge will yield nothing.

I love Sri Lanka and especially the people but beware of greed. Foreigners are not silly and news of bad experiences travels fast.

Title: A family Treasure
Text: It is the onle place which will be guarnteed to hold a spot a soft place in our hearts! The romantic walks before tying the knot and later the visit with a kid and then with two! A place to make memories forever. Has an adequately well maintained Children park with makeshift (and safe) ferry's wheel, a small motored train with its own track and passenger carriages - Adults too can use it!! ;)

Title: Nice park
Text: Nice Park,  we'll maintained,  good trees and greenery nice place to CHILL and relax good place to take pics

Title: Small but nice
Text:
Good to see well maintained. Nice flowers and trees. 
A bit small but there is an old small bridge where can catch good picture.

Title: A NICE EVENING STROLL
Text: A  beautiful garden in Nuwara Eliya. There is a small entry fee. Good for a nice evening stroll. The flowers are beautiful though they are also seen in other parts of the Indian subcontinent. A few beautioful birds and monkeys also can be seen.

Title: Attractive public gardens
Text: ...like this are uncommon in South Asia but they are an integral part of this very pleasant town. Well worth a stroll after the hectic tours in Kandy.

Title: Pretty scenery
Text:
Absolutely gorgeous greens with plenty of flora and fauna.
Loved walking around in the park. Children loved playing in the grassy fields.

Title: Relaxing Park
Text: Neatly kept park for peaceful enjoyment. The flowers weren't out as it was the wrong season but the park is well maintained and a pleasant area for a rest. The children's area looks like a lot of fun incorporating a Ferris wheel and a little train. The museum is very interesting with many photos of years gone by.  Well worth a visit.

Title: Nice park, but beware ticket scam if entering with children.
Text:
We visited the park with our two children, aged 9 & 10. You have to buy tickets to enter the park. There seems to be a scam going at the ticket office, where the posted price does not match the ticket price. The price for foreign adults is R300 each, but the children's admission price is not indicated. We gave R1200 and got four tickets and no change. Off we went to visit the park, however a short while later, on examining the tickets, we noticed that the children are charged at half price, i.e. R150!
