We went back to the ticket office to inquire and immediately the R300 change appeared, as if by magic...

As for the park, it's quite pleasant but definitely overrated.

Title: Could be better
Text: All this park needs is some TLC and a work crew to clean it. Since foreigners pay for entry that does not seem too difficult.

Title: A great welcome!
Text: As we were showing interest in the plants we were approached by the Superintendent who gave us a personal tour for three quarters of an hour, showing us things we never would have spotted for ourselves. An enthusiast for the Royal Horticultural Society he was delighted to share his expertise.

Title: A nice park to relax in
Text: Not a big park, but it is very nice to walk around and relax while you read a book/the newspaper. Every is 300 rupees for an adult (foreigner) which includes every to a small museum at the entrance gates showing historic photos of the town and tea plantations.

Title: Victoria Park
Text: A nice piece of English gardening with local plants. You have to pay and indeed a lot more than the locals. I prefer to see that as a little contribution to the maintenance of the park. After all, it's only 300 RS (20 SEK/about 2).

Title: Pretty Park
Text: Well maintained and pretty park to walk around. Also has security guards. Lovely in the sunshine. Foreigners cost is 300 lkr to enter. Nice place to take children.

Title: A must visit in Nuwaria Eliya
Text:
The Park is beautiful, and well organized. Perfect for picnics, walking or even if you just wanna chill on the grass.

It has so many different type of planets and tree and even a small Japanese Garden inside

There are spots for bird watching too.

There is an entrée fee for the Park but its for full day

Title: Victoria Park
Text: Nice park, but there is really not that much to see. You can come there for a walk, make some people watching but the place is not special.

Title: Nothing spectacular
Text: As usual foreigners pay about ten times as much as locals to see this attraction. The park is well laid out but needs time and money spent on it. We also visited at a time of year whe the roses had been pruned and most flower beds cleared and recently re-planted so there was little colour to be seen.

Title: Cafe in the park
Text: Lovely coffee lovely staff and service. Food looked good too. Delightful little place to stop and chill out.

Title: Beautiful park
Text:
It was a Festival Day in Nuwara Eliya and the park was full of local families out in the sunshine enjoying themselves.
We were lucky to get chatting with the head gardener who had a wealth of knowledge of all the trees and flowers in the park. He showed us many beautiful smelling flowers. He explained that now is the season for them to be planting and tending new seedlings. Many were covered to protect from frost. He said in another couple of months the park will be full of flowers and look very pretty.
It was lovely to walk around anyway. There is a very large playground for younger children.

Title: Calm place in the city center
Text: The call it botanical garden but actually it's not a real botanical, you'll find some kind of plants there but not endemic ones,anyway a calm and beautiful park for morning or afternoon walk.

Title: Nice park
Text: Nice park- as non Sri Lankan you pay 300 rupees to get in. It's not as big as we thought and you could do this park in 15-30 mins. Lovely flowers. Some stray dogs around but not an issue.

Title: A nice park among many others!
Text: The park was well maitained with a lot of  people working for the great tourist season,which would start for the weekend,saturday 1/4.We went there for a couple of hours and realised that many of the flowers are common potted plants in Sweden.

Title: Interesting for people watching
Text: An easy if not that inspiring option if you're looking for something to do in Nuwara Eliya, especially with young children. There is an entrance fee for foreigners of a few pounds. It's a pleasant place to take some short eats for a picnic but we preferred Gregory Lake as a child-friendly destination.

Title: Nice park
Text: It was nice to visit this park as the town was very busy. It is a well kept space for a pleasant walk.

Title: Good greenery
Text: This park is well maintained and one feels really refreshed walking around . It is a good quiet place to spend the evening.

Title: Snakes, rides and fun
Text:
There was a festival on at the time, so not sure if it happens every week, but it was great fun. We saw a man with a huge Python AND 3 Cobras!! 
Great experience with these amazing animals.
There's a fun kids park with swings, monkey bars etc., and large manicured lawn areas for relaxing.
Good for few hours to let kids run around.

Title: Good little walk
Text: Not the best park in Sri Lanka and probably best to avoid on national holidays if you're looking for serenity but it helps in escaping the heat.

Title: Nice park in the centre of town
Text: Really enjoyed these gardens, financially much cheaper than Hakgala.  Good to visit early in the morning when the dew is still on the flowers.  Bigger than I thought at first, it stretches for quite a way.  Happily spent a couple of hours here, along with a few tourists, locals and the odd group of school children.  Options to purchase food and drinks also available.  A nice spot.

Title: Good option
Text:
Good place to visit and enjoy the greenery. 
Hakgala Botanic Gardens are much better to visit and this place can be as a second option.

Title: Excellent  little park
Text: A lovely park, wonderful green, with flowers, birds and trees, really pleasant hideout for families. We also visited the small,  informative museum explaining the history of Nuwara Eliya and the surrounding areas, particularly exciting to learn more about how the railways were built and the plantations. Recommended!

Title: Very pretty park
Text: Charming park which is not as big as the Hakgale Botanical Gardens. The entrance fee is cheap and they have lovely flowers and trees.  I really enjoyed ambling through the park and because the weather is so lovely, u don't sweat or feel tired. They have huge roses too. Worth visiting with children.

Title: Good place to unwind
Text: Good place to unwind. They have a separate place for kids activities. Neat and clean and have good varieties of plants.

Title: Went there in a Morning...
Text: Small park situated in the middle of Nuwara Eliya city... But the place is very natural and have different varieties of plants and huge  flower collection. You can sit anywhere and read a book or may be you can have a nap if you want... there's that  cafe outside of this park,and nice place to have a meal....

Title: Very beautiful place specially for families
Text:
Nice park with beautiful landscaping and huge tees and plants 
Memorial trees since the occupation times
Entry fees 300 SLK R per person which almost 2.5 dollars 
The park is closing by 18:00

Title: Good for a evening stroll
Text: The park is located right next to the bus stand and is relatively small  but looks amazing. It should be noted that foreigner have to pay LKR 300 as entrance fee. You should also try the restaurant on the premises

Title: If you have kids and want to relax for sometime this can be your hide out
Text: This is a very huge garden with children play areas. It is well maintained and again if you are foreigners you pay 300 SLR and locals pay 60 SLR. Again the ticket you might get will be used by someone already ;) In Srilanka tourist places are full of frauds and you have no choice and government is least bothered.

Title: Nice park but should be free entry
Text: It's a really nice entry with a 300rp entry fee for foreigners (locals pay 60rp). It's not that much but I believe the entry to a park should be free. It's not even that clean because there are some plastic bottles lying around. Regardless it's a nice park and worth the visit for a quick stroll or reading a book at a bank.

Title: Unkept Beauty
Text: Lack of proper maintenance mars the beauty and charm of this historic garden. A sign board inside reads "Please behave decently".Interpretation is not difficult to fathom with young couples around.

Title: Wonderful place
Text: Wonderful place with birds chirping , very clean & wonderful trees , we could easily spot , nightingale, koyal, sparrow

Title: After visiting Kenya somewhat  worn off, but stiil was interesting.
Text: We saw a leopard, elephants, many buffalo, deers, crocodiles, peacocks and other. Safari takes 3 hours.

Title: English park amidst of tropic
Text: We visited this park as it was just few steps from the Gand Hotel were stayed in. Very clean and well maintained place to relax. Vide variety of plants.

Title: Beautiful park
Text: Nice park to take an easy walk or relax on one of the lawns. The childrens playground was nice, but little outdated.

Title: nice garden
Text: nice garden to spend couple of hours with little kids especially as there is a nice play area and train rides. well kept garden with beautiful flowers, trees and bushes as one would expect in Nuwaraeliya.

Title: Well maintained. Lovely walks in the chilly climate of Nuwara Eliya.
Text: Right in the heart of the city. Well maintained. Do not miss the small museum at the entrance with lots of old photographs and a charming curator.

Title: The parj worth to enter
Text: If you want to see a small well (see the picture) that is moved by power generator and use some artificial playground facilities you need to visit this park. The entrance fee is 300 LKR per person (tickets only for adults) and the ride on the well is additional 100 LKR per persons

Title: Top class park
Text: We make it a point to visit parks in all the cities we visit as we have young kids. Given that experience, I would rate this as one of the best parks we have visited. The layout and trees make it a good park. It has a children's park tucked away in one corner and a pond with an island, fishes, birds - it is packed.

Title: "The best play ground ever!" My 7 year old daugtet
Text: My kids and their cousins loved this place so much, they went back twice. "My favorite things to do were some of the spinny things," ten year old daughter.

Title: Great spot for picnics!
Text: We went twice in one weekend as we had a very active child with us. He could run around on the grass while we had a great picnic. There is also a amusement park where we spend many hours.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
What a lovely park to walk in. The place is tended by numerous gardens all eager to share their knowledge with you. Plus practice their English!! 

Their are many very old trees in the park and plants I had not heard of before. We were also able to see many different birds. 

The down side, you have to pay an entrance fee.

Title: Victori Park in Nuwara Eliyh
Text: A very big natural green park (entry fee LRK 300) in the heart of city. It'll remind you of Hyde Park or the vast ground in front of Washington Memorial. You can take a good walk for unwinding.

Title: Nice park
Text: Nice to take a walk in. A lot of Sri Lankan people. Nice and calm. 300 rm in entrance free for foreginers.

Title: Pleasant gardens, but a little small
Text:
Worth having a quick look through the gardens if you're staying In Nuwara Eliya. It's a nice place to sit on a sunny day and it seems most days in Sri Lanka are warm and sunny. 

The bathrooms inside the grounds are very poor so ensure you visit one before you enter. I recommend avoiding using them if you can.

Title: Beautiful park
Text: Beautiful park with great kids playground, nice for a stroll among lakes and trees. Take one hour relax. Entrance is 300 rupees for foreigners.

Title: The kiddies playground was the attraction.
Text: The gardens were very nice and spacious but at this time we were there they had building materials lying around as they must have been doing renovations or something. Also, there was not many flowers blooming and a lot of stray dogs all around the park. However, the kiddies park, which is hidden through some trees, is absolutely great. There is plenty of awesome playground equipment for the kids to play on and there is some cheap rides (Ferris wheel, bouncy castle, train, pony). I think, at the moment, it's only really worth it to go there if you have young children because the rest of the park is a bit underwhelming.

Title: Not maintained
Text: I had planned to visit this park after reading about it online, but when I arrived in Nuwara Eliya, my guide told me that other tourists had complained that it was poorly maintained and that I'd be wasting my money paying the entrance fee, thus I didn't bother.

Title: Nice Park
Text: Worth the v modest entrance fee to have a stroll around this v pleasant park. Well kept with a nice variety of planting & ponds. Like a lot of NE it makes for a welcome change in pace if you recently arrived via Colombo & Kandy. Seems to be popular with locals as well which is always a good sign.

Title: Not as good as described in lonely planet
Text: Very disappointing, quite small not very clean and updated... 2 entrances. Price for tourist is 300rs. Doesn't worth 2euros.

Title: Nothing more than any big park in your town
Text: It was an okayish place with lots of trees, shrubs and flowers. There is a childrens park with swings. There is a clean pathway for a happy morning walk. But nothing very special about it

Title: Was Ok
Text: Visited it. They had special price for foreigners like 300 Lkr and park is maintained nicely but nothing much to do. You can just sit for sometime and thats it

Title: A massive fortress in its day
Text:
Came here as part of an island tour, this was obviously a very big fort in its day and you can still make out most of the features. Here you can witness crazy divers/jumpers who for a few will jump off the fortress walls into a very narrow stretch of water 5ft deep.
When the tsunami hit the area in 1998 the fort was one of the few places to be safe.

Title: Overrated
Text: We did a day trip to Galle Fort and did a visit to Old Town and The Fort.  Parts of the Fort is dirty and neglected and other areas better but not great. We walked through some of the small shopping streets and expected more. Many shops were closed and no real vibe - appreciate it is probably the current environment and economic climate but think twice before you go. Think there are much better options and day trips around.

Title: Stunning
Text: If you visit the World Heritage site of Galle spend time to walk round the walls, the views are stunning. Very safe.

Title: Amazing place, with a lovely ambiance!
Text:
We visited this as part of our sightseeing trip down to Unawatuna.
Arriving here we were impressed with how neat and clean and well kept the place was. The old buildings and the ambiance was so nice! (made me think of HoiAn). 
Walking around and visiting the small shops and having lunch in a little restaurant was the perfect start to our stay in Unawatuna.

Title: Precious History Within The Walls
Text:
This a quant little town from the Durch era in Sri Lanka.

Easy to walk around, so much history within these walls.

The cannons explain a troubled past.

Not to be missed.

Title: A must see
Text: Loved it. A cozy plaze with many small shops and restaurants. Beautiful view. Absolutely worth a visit when you visit Galle

Title: A lovely historic area
Text: The fort consists of the surrounding wall with many stronghold bastions that would have been armed with canon, both in older times and up to the Second World War. Pleasant to walk around the walls and view the old colonial town from many viewpoints.

Title: Place of high historical interest
Text: Learn about the history and understand the cultural mix of Sri Lanka. The structure of Portuguese, Dutch and British  influence is particularly interesting.

Title: Grand Day Out to Galle
Text: We did a day trip to Galle in the south of Sri Lanka with Freddy Tours of Kalutara. Freddy drove us 81 km in his Tuk Tuk which was a happy and fun experience. He arranged quite a few visits for us on the way there and on the way back. Our trip took in Buddhist Temple in the Southern Provence, The Tsunami Museum and a mask museum. Galle was beautiful and I recommend you take time to walk about inside the fort. The views from the fort are amazing and the little streets within the fort were fascinating to explore. We stopped by some beaches and the fish harbour on our return. This was a great day out put together by Freddy who we would strongly recommend. He is based in Kalutara and provides great trips to the guests of the Avani hotel where we were staying. He is contactable on + 94 77 63 49248.

Title: Gorgeous European colonial corner
Text:
Unic part of colonial city in the middle of Asian island. If your tired of  loud colorize local you definitely should visit this European  city. Architecture, Cousine, people - everything is different and impressive!
Recommend to visit!

Title: Gorgeous
Text: There isnt anything that is wrong with this place, not even the slight touristic vibe, since it hasnt touched its identity, but boosted it, seen the perfect maintaince and the redecoration of units that might have gone lost. The atmosphere is magic, its full of gorgeous buildings, a temple, a church, a mosque and a tiny local beach that becomes very quaint at the sunset. Its also gorgeous watching the sunset from flagrock, where you will meet young boys diving into the sea for some money in exchange. The atmosphere is great because many locals will be around strolling with their family, so the vibe is cool and interesting.

Title: Nice experience staying / being in the Fort
Text:
Centuries-old Dutch Fort, in parts still carrying the legacy.

Quite a nice experience to be in this Fort. We were staying within the Fort so it was lovely to just walk around across Peddler St, Hospital St, Rampart St. and visit the restaurants along the way.

The Light House, Rampart, Hospital and the bastions are some of the attractions; you get stunning views of the ocean, and Galle cricket stadium. 

There are a lot of restaurants in the area, and some shops and ice-cream shops. 

It is a lovely place to stay within the Fort so you can soak in the experience.

Title: Nice spot in SL
Text: Must visit spot in Sri Lanka. The vibe is very nice in the area and the restaurants and spots there are nicely done - touristic area in general. Nice walk in the afternoon after lunch. More reviews @myra.recommends

Title: Stunning views
Text: The view were amazing we took loads of photos and going around 5 pm was a great time to visit as it is a lot cooler although the museums are closed at that time.

Title: Nice fort
Text: Nice fort and some views around Galle coast. Sadly our guide didnt give us too much information about it. But we enjoyed the walk around and there are stones with information on for you to read.

Title: A True Living Heritage Experience
Text: A genuine experience, not a contrived tourism attraction. There are still people living, worshipping and going about their daily business in this truly worthy world heritage site.

Title: Worth the visit.
Text:
The fort is an amazing place to walk around. 
It has signs here and there with information about the fort, which was built and added to by different countries.
 While it's not all there anymore, what is left is quite impressive. Look for the coral in the wall and ground of one part, and the view over the ocean is very pretty, so I'm sure it's a good sunset place.
There are a lot of markets and restaurants around, so while we didn't, it would be easy to fill in most of a day around here.

Title: Relieving History
Text: Galle fort is an amazing and quaint place which literally transports you back in time. well preserved ancient heritage. Lots of interesting things to see n do. great dining options

Title: Perfect end to an incredible trip
Text:
Lovely mix of traditional and western. Great for shopping at the end of my tour. 
Fantastic choice of restaurants.
Will be back.

Title: Nice historical fort
Text: Lovely fort complex with lots of small streets, shops, restaurants. The architecture is amazing, go inside some of the larger shops and restaurants as some have lovely courtyards. Nice to just wander around.

Title: Great atmosphere
Text:
The history of the area and the old buildings make thIs an excellent place to visit and it is free as well. Not what I expected but well worth an hour to explore by walking the ramparts as well as the narrow streets.

I thought it was an actual fort but it is the area enclosed by the walkable walls and is full of shops, restaurants and homes. Just wander the street to get a feel of the European occupation of Sri Lanka in the past.

Title: Schedule this into any visit
Text:
Galle fort in a very good example of the different ways the various kingdoms thought, from the Portuguese then Dutch then English and also what the security concerns were in the different centuries.

The walks on the ramparts and views are great then the history which seems very Dutch orientated as is shown by the names and descriptions.
The Portuguese get very little other than they started it then the Dutch get the most then it is an almost afterthought, oh yes then the British took over.

Title: A must do in Galle
Text: This a must do in Galle, but please use a knowledgeable guide otherwise you will miss so many places of interest and the stories behind them. The old fort also has a number of quaint little shops and restaurants.

Title: Where you can enjoy history
Text:
Had a lovely few hours at Galle Fort,  a World Heritage site.

You can walk all they around on the fort walls,  lots of information on the Portuguese, Dutch and British history.

Lovely streets to meaner in and some excellent cafes.

Loved the green space (think called ramparts green) and all the local school children running around. Seems to be a place for young, courting couples and its stunning watching the sun gone down. Great view of the Galle cricket ground from the north side of the fort.

Title: Worth to visit this historical place
Text: Interesting to see Portuguese and Dutch forts difference. For us more interesting was to learn the history of this place. It makes sense to go there with a good guide!

Title: Great historic site
Text: Very impressive historical site, built by the Dutch in the 17th century. It was actually so strongly built, that even with the horrible tsunami in 2004, inside the fortress they kept it dry. Lots of stuff to see, including nice bars, shops and restaurants.

Title: Well preserved Fort
Text: The layers of British Dutch and Portugese fortifications will appeal to military buffs.It is fiercely hot at mid day so a good start to a morning walk and then do the museums and churches later in the day

Title: Walk back in time
Text:
Thanks to painstaking efforts of some people you can see this Dutch fort in its original manner. Though the fortress was not damaged All other equipment such as lighting was changed. But now all fittings are in the original shape. Even the buildings are now reinstated to original glory. One of the photos shared show a restaurant. This was a government Office around 40- 50 years ago. 
Most interesting places would be the dungeon near to the light house. There are ample restaurants serving all types of food. You can even taste Gellato in Galle Fort. I am sure you would love that as Sri Lanka is a tropical country. 
Galle is also a favourite destination for many Yachts. Windsor's are the best Yacht agents. They are really helpful people.

Title: Must-go place near Hikkaduwa!
Text: Must-go place near Hikkaduwa! Went here extempore and was pleasantly surprised. Very nice historical fortress build by europeans. Nice way to change the scenery for awhile.

Title: So much to walk so avoid afternoons
Text:
You go there, take walks on the fort. See the scenery around and you come back. 

While nothing extraordinary about it, it is also a place that you should not missing out. There are no entry fees and so much history behind the fort you sure want to visit and learn more about it.

Title: Extreme South of SRILANKA - Galle Fort
Text: a must place to visit esp drive from Bentota to Galle not the Expressway but adjacent to seashore. it has clean and clear green beach which is just awesome. You can see Indian Ocean from the fort and also go down to the beach. has light house. no charges to visit.

Title: Colonial architecture one beautiful coast
Text:
A great half day excursion. Beautiful colonial architecture as well as a living / working local town with good options for food, a local market (souvenir as opposed to food).

It is a short walk from the train station. Would recommend getting the train through the jungle / along the coast if you can. But check the travel times and best in mind it won' be air conditioned.

Title: Passing Visit
Text: My wife and I had a passing visit to Galle Fort en route to Hikkaduwa we stopped here for lunch and a walk around. You can really see the western influence has had on this town its very different to anywhere else in Sri Lanka. Worth the visit if in the area but it would not be top of my list.

Title: Quaint
Text: Can walk around on the ramparts or stroll along the shops. Beautiful view form the ramparts especially at sunset.Some pricey boutiques as well as more reasonably priced tourist shops. Places to sit and relax or enjoy a gelati on a hot day.

Title: Must see in Galle
Text: After a long trip in Sri Lanka triangle,if you can come Galle it feels so much different to you with ?ts fort also

Title: Worth a look.
Text: Great place to while away a few hours and wander the streets. Lots of cafes, restaurants, shops etc. The prices here are higher than you'll find elsewhere in Galle though. We saw snakecharmers, monitor lizards and, in the evenings, fruit bats.

Title: Unique experiences
Text:
We very much enjoyed touring Galle Fort, appreciating the old fortifications, the mix of architectural styles, and opportunities to learn more about the history.

Lots of great shops and restaurants within.

Our driver made the brilliant suggestion of going later in the day to avoid the heat, and take in a stunning sunset. Highly encouraged to do the same.

Title: Galle Fort
Text: I had a fantastic visit to the historic Galle Fort amazing views fantastic choice of restaurants and wonderful shopping in the quaint boutique shops in the small streets within the Huge Ramparts a must visit is recommended by me

Title: An old fort with a prison below
Text:
An old fort with a clock tower and an old prison at the bottom of the fort. 

I found the prison quite interesting as it has no roof. With one access door, the prison is exposed to rain or shine. 

From the top it has a great view of Galle and also the cricket ground. 

Highly recommended.

Title: Lunch at Galle courtesy of out Tok Tok driver
Text: After lunch we undertook a walking tour of Galle. Our problem was we had to call it off due to heavy rain. Well worth the visit and next time i hope we dont get rained out

Title: Nice walk
Text: This was a nice walk along the tops of the fortifications. It was not spectacular but pleasant. Make sure that you go out onto the main bastion to get the best views.

Title: A little Dutch fortress
Text: The views are amazing.  Its a tourist trap though, so expect that when walking around the area.  I completely loved it.

Title: Well worth seeing
Text:
An interesting history and it was great to wander around the streets and buidings.
Also some great views over the city and the Galle Cricket Ground.
Even the "Crazy" cliff divers were worth seeing.

Title: Excellent
Text:
Well worth a couple of hours of anyone's time. A wide selection of shops & bars with some fascinating architecture to enjoy.
Don't miss the opportunity to see a more refined area of Sri Lanka.

Title: Must Visit
Text: This is a place one must definitely visit. Right in the city with one side bordered by sea this is a wonderful place. It offers beautiful views of the sea and is a wonderful location to click photos. One can also watch a cricket match in the Galle stadium from here. Overall dont miss the Galle Fort in your visit to Srilanka. While u can drive inside some parts will need you to walk as well.

Title: Galle Fort
Text: This is very unique to have such place in Sri Lanka. there are certainly lots of things you can try in Sri Lanka., but this is must.

Title: Pleasant 1/2 day out
Text: Galle fort is a fortified town within ancient walls. There is an old lighthouse, various dutch colonial architecture and several churches and a maritime museum. The rest of the town is filled with numerous eateries, jewelers and craft/souvenir shops. It is a pleasant way to amble away an afternoon.

Title: A charming place
Text: Delightful walk along/adjacent to the fort walls. Lots of places of interest along the walls or nearby streets, lots of cafes and bars, shops, museums etc. Really enjoyed my time in Galle, its a charming place within the old city walls.

Title: Those walls witnessed history
Text: It is really amazing to see the fortifications that you usually see in Europe in Asia. Thick walls, hospitals, gardens, towers, splendid artifacts of the Portuguese occupation.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: beautiful place. suggest visiting by early evening. That way you can enjoy the fort, the sunset and the night sights and sounds.

Title: 17th Century Dutch Fortress walls
Text: If you come from Europe with thousands of years of history and cultural heritage the fortress walls will not impress you. The town itself is not older than that and there was really nothing which caught my eye. Some old buildings, nice restaurants, shops with gifts, jewellery Thats it. Ignoring time spent in restaurant it didnt took us more than 2-3 hours to walk all what was worth seeing there.

Title: Quaint Little Town
Text:
An UNESCO Heritage Site, a once upon Dutch Town. There are many old houses left behind during the Portuguese, Dutch & British. Many houses are reconstructed, converted to shops, hotel, restaurants, museums and yet there are some still in ruin.
The popular functional Lighthouse is the place every tourist will snap a photo with. 
The town is quiet with the Fort Wall surrounding the town. We can stroll around the wall of the round. Enjoy the sound of the sea. At the click Tower side, we can see overlook the exterior of the city wall, the cricket club.
The best time to stroll around is during evening and early morning. Look out for the sunset and sunrise. Listen to the roaring, bellowed sea.
Things are more expensive within this wall.

Title: Dutch Fort Full of Tourists  Still Nice
Text: Galle Fort is the entire old part of Galle  a peninsula with Dutch-built walls and other fortifications. You can walk on most of the walls, and the Fort itself is bursting with restaurants, cafes and hotels. It is Tourist Central. The Fort has a distinct Olde World feel to it as most of the buildings are Dutch or early British and, despite the traffic and tourists, is quite something to see. Its not a large place, so if you walk briskly you can easily go up and down every street, and walk the walls, in 3 hours.

Title: Nice views
Text: Nice views from old fort. Interesting history. Worth a visit and the back streets are a nice place to wander

Title: Galle fort one night enough
Text: The fort is nice but small. Enough to spend one afternoon plus evening there. Everything is overpriced. We found nice accommodation for reasonable price inside the fort. Check Nisala guest.

Title: A really atmospheric and picturesque place.
Text: A place with vivid memories from all european occupiers. Interesting buildings, unbelievable sceneries. I wish I had planned to stay longer.

Title: Pleasant trail and beautiful view
Text:
we visited the Galle Fort and walked around the place. It is a beautiful place and there are other attractions nearby like the Galle International Cricket Stadium. the view is very serene and it is a wonderful experience to walk along the trail.
there is a clock tower also present from where you can see the cricket stadium.
we were also shown the place where the tsunami had struck.

this fort is steeped in history and worth the visit

Title: Lovely trip
Text:
Did it as a day trip. Amazing scenery.

Its getting hot in the afternoon as there is no wind. But if you have a cold drink soon enough - its all fine

Title: A Quick Stop
Text: We had a bit of miscommunication about what exactly the fort part of Galle was. All of the part of Galle that you (as a tourist) are visiting is the fort. The more photogenic bits down by the water are lovely, but the enclosure runs around the entire old city. As a few photos is all that is really needed to have checkboxed the site, 20-30 minutes should be sufficient. The lighthouse is lovely.

Title: Interesting Fort
Text:
We visited this fort as part of a G Adventures tour of Sri Lanka.  This fort is a UNESCO site and is also where the 2004 tsunami occurred.  

The remaining parts of the fort were built by the Dutch.  This is a nice area to visit as the fort itself is pleasant to walk around and there are lots of shops and restaurants to visit.  I enjoyed checking out the numerous jewelery shops in the area.

Title: Spend a day here if not more!
Text: Really amazing historical area. There are so many cafes, bars, restaurants and galleries that you can spend a lot of time here. There is a little beach too and a few little lookouts. We really enjoyed this area a lot. Close to Unawatuna Beach too.

Title: Good place
Text: Good place for all day visiting, have historical buildings, museums. Cafe and restaurants. Jewelry shops. More better if you will visit with local tour guide, for more information.

Title: HISTORY ON EVERY STREET
Text: One of eight World Heritage Sites in the country, the fort area allows you to explore influences from Portuguese, Dutch and English perspectives. The fort area is largely on a grid pattern. Many old buildings have been put to modern uses [shops and restaurants] while others are in a state of decay. You can walk the ramparts around more than half of the fort. Sites to see include churches and several museums. There are many cafes to have a cool drink to escape [somewhat] the heat of the day. It is a nice spot to meander, hearkening back to the days of European imperial designs, realizing the range of influences also extended east to China. The forts role in commerce was the impetus to its status as a crossroad for civilizations.

Title: Nice piece of history
Text: Very nice place, where you can find a lot of europian architecture. Many restaurants, hotels, cafe etc. You can go for running around for 3km. The truth is the forth is bit expensive.

Title: Huge Fort
Text:
The fort is big in length and you can visit lot of other things besides the fort. There are churches, markets etc. 

Time to complete full trip would be around 2-3 hours. The market is expensive compared to other markets in SL.

You can also have a quick tour from the car itself if not interested in walking.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Had a morning visit which was lovely on a sunny day, a great walk around the old streets and churches and Mosque

Title: Quaint old town.
Text:
A very pleasant few hours walking around the quaint streets, discovering shops, market stall, restaurants & cafes. 
Do not miss out on a lovely ice cream from 1 of the many gelatos cafes. 
There is also the fort structure with ramparts, tower & lighthouse. 
Its not as well maintained as many old structures but it looks like they are doing something about it. 
There are many Tuk Tuk drivers that will offer you a 1 hour tour for £2 or £3. In the heat it many save you some sweat. 
There is also a small fish market on the way in, which we found interesting.

Title: Great place to spend a day
Text: We stayed within the fort and spent an afternoon walking around but could easily spend a week here visiting all the amazing cafes, shops and restaurants.  If you visit Galle then you really should make the time to visit the fort and allocate at least half a day.

Title: A memorable visit to famous fort at Galle
Text: It was a dream came true. I have heard about it for a long time. The place is preserved well. Views are excellent. Walking around it was a great experience. The watch tower and the light house gives nice view. The surrounding sea as well as buildings inside can give a lot of good memories.

Title: Great history
Text:
The Fort area is not what i expected but was a lovely surprise to find an old walled city with many buildings and cafes. There is an old world charm enhanced by the Portugese and Dutch Architecture. 
It is a little spoiled by the number of Tuk Tuks hanging around although they are all very modern and comfortable. If you take a Tuk Tuk to the Fort you will be dropped off at the Wall. If walking to the lighthouse is a problem for you, then catch another Tuk Tuk.

Title: Lovely walk across the fort overlooking the ocean
Text:
We had a lovely walk around sunset time which added to the magic of the site. Overlooking the rooftops of the old city is spectacular as it combines Dutch, Portuguese, SriLankan and English touches. You can easily spend a half day or more walking around, shopping and grabbing a bite.

I wish we had planned a short stay within the old city... I can imagine the morning walks would be equally spectacular.

Title: Awesome history
Text:
Thoroughly enjoyed my time at Galle Fort.
I spent an afternoon walking the old perimeter wall and going into places of interest along the way i.e. Dutch hospital, Dutch church, Old Dutch Governors mansion, old warehouse etc. etc.
I used a guide book as I walked around and found it fascinating talking to some of the teams doing the refurb work at various areas around the perimeter.
Some great eateries and shops particularly on Peddlar St.
Great vibe within the fort and its narrow, grid-like street layout.
Highly reccomend.

Title: Easily done in a day trip
Text: I can say you can easily walk around, see all the sights in less than 1/2 a day. So easy day trip from nearby beach towns. We stayed the night inside the fort and was great to watch the sunset. The town closes down by 9pm

Title: Interesting place
Text: Galle is a great place to visit if a little touristy in places but with the narrow street good place to eat and lots of history a day at Gale Fort s certainly a must do when in Sri Lanka. There is a lot of rock going on to the walls at the moment which limits access but wench this is complete it will be a real bonus.

Title: A lovely walk
Text: The old fort is lovely to walk round on the ramparts. It is well looked after and parts are being upgraded at present. Lovely views of the coast from many points of the outer walls.

Title: Nicely maintained fort on the sea...
Text: We did a day trip from Beruwala(near Bentota) to see the Galle Fort as it was highly recommended and we were not disappointed. The fort itself is quite well maintained. Lot of nice cafes, bars, restaurants, ATMs, souvenir & gelato shops etc within the fort. The lighthouse was really nice and there are quite a few good spots to click pictures from overlooking the sea. We travelled to and fro in an AC bus which was good and super cheap.

Title: Great Historic Site
Text: Fascinating historic site that has been reasonably cared for. Lots of little shops and restaurants, old churches and other buildings, nice views of the ocean. Must see if you are in the vicinity.

Title: Watch sunset and have lunch at The Bungalow.
Text:
Watching sunset from the wall near the light house is mesmerising. 
The Galle Fort is world heritage site which contains the Dutch period buildings and constructions. It is a historical, archaeological and architectural heritage monument. When Ptolemy made the map of Ceylon in 139 AD  he indicated Galle as Cetum Proments The port was in use in Pre-Christian times because of its strategic location from the east and west of the world. 
Today Galle fort covers an area of 36 hectares and encloses several museums, clock tower, Churches, mosques, a light house and about 473 private dwellings

Title: Must see
Text: If you visit Sri Lanka, you must visit Gale. The picturesque Galle Dutch fort and the several shopping opportunitys must stand on  your plan.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Galle is beautiful. It looks lovelyboth at night and during the day, when it's white walls look shiny in the sun. It's a necessary place to visit when traveling through Sri Lanka. It's enough to be here for just one full day, because it's small, but it nevertheless should be a part of any travel itinerary.

Title: Recomendable
Text: Beautiful fortress. Compulsory visit. Well-preserved walls and towers. Even you can walk on the top surrounding almost the whole fort.

Title: Expansive and impressive fort
Text: The dutch built fort is relatively well preserved and worth a photo op and short was to see its impressive design from centuries before. The dutch hosptial is another iconic building by the colonists still standing and in use!

Title: Beautiful fort
Text: A visit to galle surely means you are visiting the ancient Fort. The Fort though has only the remains of a huge structure, what attracts you here is the view of the town your get. The sunset, Clock tower and beach looks absolutely stunning. You surely love to spend the evenings here.

Title: Lovely views and interesting visit
Text: We came as part of a Kuoni excursion. We enjoyed being shown around by our guide who was also our driver.  Is worth a visit is you are in the area.

Title: Worth it!
Text:
A wonderful, compact historical fort city located along the sea. What we liked:

- compact, can be explored at your own pace and can spend a couple hour or all day if desired
- accessible. Very easy to get to. Bus, taxi, tuktuk, Uber
- beautiful location. Magnificent views of the sea and waves crashing. 

Its easy to navigate so easy to with small children. Bring a hat and sunscreen. There is almost always wind so its quite cool but the sun can be very strong so burns can happen quickly.

The cafes and restaurants are priced higher than outside the fort. There are hits and misses so scout for locations before sitting down. You can look at prices from outside in most places. Many places are quite expensive.

Highly recommend.

Title: Afternoon sightseeing
Text:
Its a check of the bucket list of things to do in Galle by visiting here. 
Interesting to see however it is literally for us a 15min stop.  
The views from top are lovely however in Galle their are so many beautiful view points.  

The fort was a old prison located in amazing location.  No charge to enter  

Their a people touting to make money for example a man with a cobra snake and monkey on a rope.  Pay him and he will get the animals to entertain you.  No thanks! We found this wrong but you will see this place to place.  
Or a man offering a free foot massage as your feet may be tired from walking.  Obviously he wants a fee at the end.  But again no thanks!

Title: An amazing historic site
Text: A wonderful place to explore on foot frequented by locals an tourists. You can walk the walls and if your lucky watch the cricket on the oval down below. There are many shops, restaurants and a market inside. You can also view churches and the lighthouse. Well worth the visit.

Title: Nice Relax Walk Around
Text: Nice sea views, easy walking around. Nice to take in all the old buildings. Lots of influence by the Dutch.

Title: Disappointed
Text:
I love history and visiting historical locations, but this UNESCO site left me disappointed. The fort is lovely, but it is lacking the components that made it. Where are the guns? Where are the historical locations in the fort? What is there here to tell someone that a battle was fought?

Reality is, this is a tourist trap with nothing but hoky poky stunts and trinkets. It has been inundated with Chinese culture so much that with all the Chinese flags, youd think you were in China!

Title: Funky
Text: We loved the fort so much so that we were thinking the next time we're in Sri Lanka we'd like to spend a couple of nights there. We stayed outside the fort this trip but stopped to have a drink at a hotel, walked around and explored the streets and the shops, whose prices weren't too unreasonable. Definitely well worth a visit.

Title: Beautiful fort
Text:
Spent 2 nights in the fort
Went into town one morning to the market
Rest of time walked around the fort
Enjoyed shopping and the great resturants

Title: Best location of Galle
Text: While visiting this place please try to walk as much as possible to cover all bylanes. The street are very beautiful fully loaded with shops and small cafes. Also from fort you get full 180° view of the Indian Ocean

Title: DELIGHTFULLY DUTCH.
Text: Dont let the fact that this is very touristy put you off, this historical site is fascinating and its architecture original and maintained. A walk through the narrow streets, and the Fort walls is a must.

Title: A morning of culture and History
Text: If you love history, then this is a must place to visit. Steeped in local current culture, and past history you can lose yourself with a vivid imagination of what once was an amazing fort for Dutch and British colloquial settlers. Now a recognised National Heritage Site, it's great for the local community. If you have a good hunt on the beach you might even find yourself some old relics.

Title: Huge fort
Text:
This is located right next to the Galle bus station and train station and hence very easy to find. 

Overall nice place reminding you of colonial history,  probably a better option if you study the history before you visit. 

Many good food and drink options nearby,  a bit expensive as well.  Best time to visit would be just before the sunset. 

Sri Lankan govt should do something to stop plastic usage in this area to keep this place clean.

Title: Lovely shops & restaurants
Text: Besides the history of the this old Dutch fort, which has withstood numerous attacks over hundreds of years as well as the more recent tsunami, the area within the fort is filled with narrow streets full of interesting shops and numerous restaurants. It is a good half day outing.

Title: Fort with a cricket stadium
Text: Enjoyed the walk around the Fort periphery. It is a living Fort with people living in it. It has European style shopping streets built to attract tourist. The best part was the view of the cricket stadium from the Fort. You can literally watch a match from the walls of the Fort!

Title: Please checkout my Youtube channel " Jair Canada "  for Sri Lanka videos . Budget travel advice .
Text:
I made a video riding a train from Colombo to Galle for $1 . Cheap lion lagers and exploring fort Galle as well . Fort Galle is beautiful , right on the Indian ocean . Be sure to eat some of the streetfood at the nearby vendors . 

I would greatly appreciate some subscribers and views on my channel . thank you

Title: an old city with amazing relics
Text: This Fort is a relic of this ancient city, we stayed in this city for 3 nights, bought real gems, enjoyed, however, be alert once you buy Gems, there are so many roadside shops, get a bigger one which looks old and an established shop which must have some trustworthy photos of  having dignitaries buying gems from the respective shop, we enjoyed sea bath and beaches, too good and serene and calm, not like beaches in Thailand, hover around the city , take an auto rickshaw and enjoy. from Colombo try to take the express way by taxi to reach Galle, regular road is too busy and take 3/4 hours to reach Galle from Colombo. Express was shorten the road by 2 hours, it was a good experience of visiting innumerable beaches in this beautiful sea city.

Title: Worth walking around
Text:
It is a nice walk around the old city. The feeling is like you are in Portugal but in a poorer version :p (with some effort from the authorities it would be awesome :) )
Beautiful waves crushing on the rocks.

Title: Nice relaxing place
Text:
The fort is not really the fort i thought of, its just fort walls. But the city around the fort walls is amazing. Every city in the world has a old city or city inside the city so this is one of them. 
Loved being there. Its clean, quite, nice and relaxing. You can spend there half day walking and looking around with a plenty of coffee shops and eateries. 

Its not a very good time for SL with almost no tourists but it is still lovely to be here and the Fort area had few tourists around, honestly we saw more tourists here than anywhere else during our stay. 

We took a nice walk starting from the entrance till the end of the Fort area, including Light House which is closed for visitors, Old Dutch Hospital which is converted to little shops and we have been escorted by locals asking for money as they have not enough to feed their family, lost family during tsunami. It was really uncomfortable feeling. But honestly we havent seen these anywhere else but in Galle as weve been around in SL. Not a nice feeling when someone is following you for 15 min and you are trying to be polite... 

There are a lot of souvenir shops, gold shops around that area and everyone can find something nice to take back home.

Title: a must see in Sri Lanka
Text:
This place is truly beautiful. walk the streets of the forte. there are shops and eaterys throughout.
walk the extremes of the forte with your guide map and see and learn the forts history.

Title: A walk around mind the rubbish look at the veiw and leave
Text:
Just a few walls
Don't see why people give this place good reviews   maybe they havnt been many places
As for the shops and food it's a total rip off 
This place is a overpriced dump

Title: Just a dilapidated fort with scenice sea view
Text:
Visited in March 2019 with family. The fort is just a bunch of walls pulled in different directions. But, yes, it is spread  out over a big parcel of land. 

You can enjoy watching the sea waves. That's it. Nothing more. 

The premises also covers shopping centres, a museum and is hustling with lots of local vendors. Nothing interesting about it. 

As we had changed our entire route map to be here, we were wuite disappointed.

Title: The Fort !
Text: This place like an open museum, old buildings, old strees, canons, etc... it's perfect for walking, biking,...  a lot of bars, restaurants,  toilets etc... available in the area, also the view of the ocean totally worth it, it's good to chill out somewhere with ur drinks.

Title: nice walk
Text: nice walking area with Seafront. Fair number of restaurants and coffee shops are available. Shopping experience could be enhanced as most of the shops selling the same stuff.

Title: Must if into history
Text: We had a good guided tour around this fort.  Very cool, even though it was raining.  The shops nearby were excellent, even though the town was nearly deserted due to the recent church bombings.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
Had gone with family.. Lovely place on the beach. Old buildings which stands long and says a lot about the history. The light house itself is a Landmark in galle fort. The small streets all along the fort with so many outlets just superb.
Though majority of the shops and restaurants were closed... May be off season or may be due to the unfortunate events earlier... Not many tourists though. But worth spending a nice and quite evening with family and friends...
Do visit once esp in the evenings where the sunset is spectacular.

Title: History..
Text: I as in Cartagena Colombia recently and visited the fort there. These two places are a good history lesson as they were close in design.. history of the far reach/scope of the 16th century and up explorers. Within the fort walls is a large village. Lots of jewelry stores, etc on the side streets. Wonderful walk along the fort walls and up to the lighthouse.. a must do even if  it needs a lot of attention/maintenance.

Title: A nice area with a great history
Text: This historical place holds beautiful stories around every corner. From the okd Dutch church to the Black fort, to the streets with little cafes, it's a great place for your evening walks and for kids to learn a little more about the ewrly Dutch rule

Title: Galle Fort
Text: Galle Fort is situated on the south west coast of Sri Lanka. Fort is more than 400 years old and Dutch people ruled this area. It is a heritage monument. Still some dutch people are holding the properties inside the fort. One can have a free walk behind thd Indian Ocean. Many official buildings, restaurants are there. We travelled by our vehicle and visited round the fort.

Title: A must do in Galle
Text: This is a beautiful old Dutch fort built around 1640.  It takes about a day to wander around.  The fort has lots of restaurants, shops & historical buildings to visit.

Title: Good for a day trip
Text: Galle fort is beautiful. It is a great idea to make a day trip of it. You can walk next to the ocean and follow the pathway easily. Go eat and a great selection of restaurants and cafes. Also, you can buy a lot of gifts, clothes, tea and coffee at the shops.

Title: Nice walk
Text: Visiting the fort and the lighthouse is a must, great place to walk with very nice sea view.close proximity to our hotel

Title: A beautiful living fort city
Text: Spent marvelous few hours at galle fort and in the surrounding area on our way to Colombo from mirissa. Galle fort is a great piece of work during the Dutch colonial period. If you are a history and architecture fan, it will be a paradise for you. Apart from that we visited galle temple, dutch reformed Church and took a walk around the area enjoying some street food. Great place to visit if you are around.

Title: Beautiful view
Text:
A very European area to be in! 

The tuk tuk drops you at a point from where one has to walk to the fort. There are hotels, restaurants in this area. We recommend staying in the fort if you come to Galle. Its convenient and everything is just around there.

Title: Day out
Text:
We took the train from Hikkaduwa to Galle.Train runs every 2 hours from Hikkaduwa Station journey to Galle take around 20/30 minutes and it would cost you 80 rupees return (40p ) 
Galle Fort is about 10 minutes walk from the Galle rain station.  

Fort it self is built and conquered by the Portuguese later on Dutch invaded the fort and the city it self and used it as their main trading port, end of the 18th century the British invaded Sri Lanka took control of the fort. 

Theres lot of mixed colonial architectural buildings to see around the galle fort area, 
busy narrow streets with loads of small boutique coffee shops and hotels. We spend few hours exploring on the fort walls, beautiful sea views. Magical little city so please do visit enjoy. 

To check train times, search services railway gov lk

Title: Shopping and food!!
Text:
This place is great for shopping and amazing food! Its a must see as it doesnt look like anything you have seen before. Safe to walk around day or night. 

The number one thing you want to do is get a good driver! Not be cheap and try to make a better deal a Driver is everything thing in Sri Lanka and finding a good one is almost impossible to find. 

My driver Priyanga I found when I booked him at the Marriott hotel. He was a great driver very safe and really cared about what he was doing. He spoke great English and respect our privacy but was also very helpful about the local news and country. He was as good as a tour guide. He knew all the best places and even kept an umbrella in the car for us. He texted us updates on his location and was so helpful when we needed him. How did not do anything weird or ever ask for money or a tip. He went where we asked with no weird driving or taking us to where he thought we wanted to go. No funny business with trying to take us to a place where tourist get over charged. He was the best! We even asked for him to take us to the airport because he was better then the airport driver. 

If your at the Marriott ask for him! I also have him a nice tip each day he drove us he never asked for one but trust me hes worth a tip.

Title: Highlight of Srilanka trip
Text: We went to Galle Fort on a day trip but wish we had stayed in the fort area for a night or 2.  The place is really cool and very well maintained.  I would recommend this place to everyone who visits Srilanka. This place has been the highlight of our family trip.  It is only a 2 hour drive from Colombo.

Title: Missable
Text: As this is a UNESCO world heritage site I thought it would be spectacular but i was throughly underwhelmed and bored. The Fort is nothing special in my opinion and definitely an activity to by pass on a short schedule!

Title: A browsers paradise.
Text: Stunning old town surrounded on three sides by ocean and the foreboding walls of the old Portuguese/Dutch/British fort. A myriad of simply laid out streets, jam packed with cafes, boutiques and bric-a-brac. A photographers paradise too with oodles of atmospheric buildings to capture. One of the most charming places weve ever seen. Not to be missed. And you can spend as little as an hour here or a full day.

Title: Good walk
Text: We stayed in galle on our last day was in the fort and had a lovely walk to see the sunset with our guide. It was very pleasant and we are happy and we had a good dinner. Recommende

Title: It's only a wall
Text: The so called Galle Fort is only a wall. If it had any fortifications in the past, they are now nowhere to be seen. All you see is a very wide long wall with a light house at one end. That's it. Call it a fort if you wish. The town, to protect which the wall was built is charming. Parts of the town date back to Dutch era. It is a nicely laid out town and one would love to live here. The beach is good and the sea beautiful.

Title: good but very hot
Text: the fort is well worth a visit but prices inside the fort are 30% higher than just outside the wall so beware of purchases, lots of souvenier shops and bars which you will need to get out of the blazing sun as the fort locks the heat in and it gets very very hot

Title: Nice hangout place for shopping and food
Text: Nice place to hangout during the day . They have lovely shops and restaurants. Must visit is Ceylon Spa shop here .

Title: weLL preserved
Text: Nicely preserved set of ramparts but little else. Nice to walk the perimeter but it gets a bit repetitive.

Title: Each section is different
Text:
During the early afternoon, we explored the Old Dutch Hospital and Lighthouse side of the Fort.  At sunset, we visited the side that was at a much higher elevation near the clock tower, hotels, restaurants and shops.

The Galle Fort sections that we visited were more like wide grassy or stone covered walkways.  It did not feel like a fort such as the Halifax Citadel or some of the forts in Oman.

Still, it is a notable part of Galle's history and should be explored if you are in town.

Title: A historical come pleasure outing
Text: Well this is the old time Portuguese fort which has now been developed into a nice tourist spot ...you can roam around the ramparts of the fort which is sea facing and an evening outing can really be very enjoyable ..there are a lot of Street food stalls all around the outer Periphery and as you venture into the by lanes you will be greeted with small cafes souvenir shops and shops selling clothes and nice parlours for massage ...There are tuk tuk rides available in case you do not wish to walk around the fort... you can also see the light house. An evening outing is highly recommended so that you can beat the Sun also and soak into the atmosphere also which revs up in the evening time

Title: Trip to the Galle Fort!
Text: I visited a few days ago and found that it was very beautiful! It was a cool, sunny day as everyone was walking along the beachs boardwalk next to the fort. It wasnt very crowded and busy, but well worth it. I enjoyed the views and the architecture in which the fort was built! A visit here is worth it for any trip to Galle!

Title: A lovely walk along the Fort Wall
Text: Make sure you walk early in the morning, or later afternoon for sunset.   Its a very hot stroll at any other time.

Title: Must see!
Text: The fort and clocktower (next to the Gall Cricket Ground) is a great place to start exploring the old town. We walked the whole Old Town in a morning and finished with some cold beers at "A minute by tuk tuk" - great view of the bay.

Title: A fabulous old town with great cafes and restaurants.
Text: A fabulous evening wandering around the old town. We stopped for great coffee at  Pedlars then a meal at the Pasta factory which was delicious and an ice cream from one of the many ice cream shops. Definite a place to be visited

Title: A little disappointing for a UNESCO heritage site
Text: Half a day spent here walking around the ramparts and nosing in the overpriced shops would probably be enough.

Title: The vast Indian Ocean view!!!
Text: As you enter its a different world all together . It transport you to that Dutch era. Beautifully preserved most converted into hotels and cafes,boutiques. Its wonderful to walk in those narrow lanes and by lanes.As you reach the edge yo climb up the steps and the fantastic view of Indian Ocean lies in front. Must visit.

Title: Best view
Text:
All around the fort 300degree view of Beaches. it will take half a day to complete even more time if you want to spent some more time. why not - you will found great view which will definitely catch your eyes. its so beautiful. this is the main tourist attraction. Tuktuk is available at 1-2 dollers from any places in galle.
There is no entry ticket for the fort.

Title: Galle Fort
Text: We had a half walking around the walls of Galle Fort and thoroughly enjoyed it and understand why it's a world heritage site. There are lots of good views over the natural harbour, Galle international cricket ground and old colonial buildings, there are the usual sellers and snake charmers at various parts of the walls as well. Had a good lunch overlooking the sea, and if time permitted we would of explored some of the smaller streets with its little cafes and restaurants.

Title: Amazing!
Text: Walking around the fort was an amazing experience. Such a large area, and we could clearly see the history and heritage left by the dutch and the portugese, and were amazed that such a lot was so intact. It was great to be able to wander along the walls, and soak up the atmosphere, and I would recommend  a visit here to anyone, whether interested in history or not, as the setting was sublime, and the atmosphere superb.

Title: Great place to spend hours walking around and exploring.
Text:
Galle Fort area is really charming and historical for the area.  The Dutch influence is still prevalent today.  Buildings and cobble-stone streets still maintain the Dutch look and feel. Many streets in the area are far to narrow for cars, only motorbikes and pedistrians.  I believe this is what elevated the charm of this area.  It's clean, quaint and deliberate in it's design. The Fort area is avery large land mass (not indoors) and could potentially take all day to see, if you are walking at a leisurely pace.  I recommend seeing it more than one day in order to spend time relaxing and taking in all of the majestic, panoramic views.  An added bonus is the Galle Cricket Club is directly across the street and you get these amazing views of cricket practice and games....at no additional cost. Tuk Tuks are plentiful in this area and their prices are extremely reasonable.  Lots of great variety in cuisine at reasonable/low prices.  I even stopped to have the most delicious scope of pineapple gelato on my walk around.  There is an ATM in the area at the centrally located round-about (it's bit harder to find an ATM for Union Pay, but if you leave the Fort area and head less the 600 meters across the street, you will find banks that take Union Pay).
All in all, a great place to hang out.

Title: Interesting to walk along the ramparts & imagine how it was in its heyday.
Text:
The walls of the fort dominate the centre of Galle.
Some lovely shops , hotels, & restaurants inside the fort itself + of course the Dutch reform Church.

Title: nice place to visit
Text:
well worth a look 
big place to walk around 
great view of cricket ground over the road 
many shops bars etc here 

we came back on a night for a meal and loved it

Title: Gorgeous Galle
Text: Galle Fort was a lot of fun.  It was much bigger than I anticipated.  Tip:  Find a Tuk Tuk whose driver acts as a guide.  They will show you all the places to see in a very efficient manner.  If you want to stop for food and drink, they will wait for you too.  There are many gorgeous places to see!

Title: Old world charm!
Text: What an interesting afternoon I had at Galle Fort, Sri Lanka where the taste of Ceylon tea, exotic spices and good beer is never far away! We were staying at Bentota so came during the lunch time and spent our time wandering around and enjoying the piece of history. So strolltaround the fort we plonked ourselves at Sugar Bistro and just chilled!

Title: Tiny town within a town!
Text:
Our accommodation was within the fort walls so exploring the fort was a lot easier as we could pop back to our room for cold drinks etc.

When walking along the wall bordering the sea ?? you can see because of the height why the Tsunami in 2004 didnt do much damage to the fort area. The streets are of course full of restaurants and shops for tourists but you are not put under too much pressure which is refreshing.

We spent the best part of a day just wandering around and enjoying the piece of history.

Well worth the visit.

Title: A fascinating place.
Text: A living fort.. an important history preserved yet still offering shops, restaurants, places to stay. Beautifully kept.

Title: Good place to visit when you  in Galle
Text:
we spent our time in this place several days. it was very beautiful . so enjoyed lot. hope to come back 
Thank you

Title: A disappointing experience for a UNESCO site
Text: Galle is held up as one of the best must see places in Sri Lanka, mostly due to the UNESCO status of its Fort. Im sorry to say this, I was there yesterday, but I wouldnt recommend a visit for those wanting to see the best of Sri Lanka. The Fort has piles of rubbish lining its beaches and down small side alleys, not just the odd plastic bottle. No one seemed to care. It is expensive to stay and eat. While shop owners and restauranteurs where accommodating and welcoming, the overall atmosphere was one of complacency. I think we may have been scammed into donating to a childrens nursery too - its seemed genuine but it was hard to tell because of the way it was done. I left Galle rather depressed and hoping the rest of my time in Sri Lanka would be much better. Ive only ever heard good things about the country.

Title: Galle fort
Text: Galle is nice place, worth visiting as a day trip from  Bentota/Ahunglia. One should spend 3-4 hours, preferably in the evening roaming around and soaking in the architecture, sea, streets, shops

Title: great place for sunset
Text:
was there for the sunset
beautiful place overlooking the sea
a nice sunset walk for tourists also 
can be crowded

Title: Picturesque historic fort
Text: The area around the fort is both historic and very scenic, with many small shops and restaurants to choose from while exploring the area.  The views of the ocean are also amazing. This is a must see attraction if you're in the area. Plan on spending the better part if the day visiting and exploring. I was there as part of a Gate1 tour stop.

Title: Nice walk
Text: Nice to walk around the walls. You probably need 2 hours to walk all the way around including stops. Definitely do this in the late afternoon or early evening as it can be very hot otherwise. Quite a lot of rubbish on the beaches / on the wall which we were not expecting and spoilt the walk some what.

Title: Great place to visit.
Text: Its almost compulsory to visit Galle. We only spent a few hours but its a lovely place to wonder around and get a sense of the fantastic history of the area. Its certainly very touristy but its also very historic and quite honestly, its nice. We had lunch and then wandered around. There is plenty to see and its all well presented and clean. I liked it.

Title: Surprisingly good!!
Text: It is such a popular place but it is really worth visiting - very clean, slightly more crowded on weekends. There are lot of local people as well. The place is very popular for snorkeling. Would recommend visiting during morning hours since it gets very hot. Not much of tree cover around.

Title: Cute and rich history
Text: Galle fort is really a piece of living history. The streets are well organized and reflect most of the history from the Dutch and Portuguese presence. There are also nice shops, restaurants, hotels, bars, and everything looks great. Well worth a detour and a short stay to explore

Title: Stunning location
Text:
Make sure you have a good, knowledgeable guide when you visit Galle Fort. 
As it's had such an interesting history.
Overlooking Galle, the cricket grounds and some wonderful architecture - it's an interesting place.
Can get quite busy at times- So worth taking advice from a guide as to best time of day to visit.

Title: History
Text: Visited in the afternoon seen great views of the Indian Ocean, this place is very historical & you get the best view of Galle international cricket stadium.

Title: So pretty
Text: Galle Fort is so pretty, sitting above crystal clear water.  Its a nice walk along the wall and there is a lovely swimming spot.

Title: Unexpected food, shopping and views
Text: Galle Fort is well worth at least half a day, if not longer.  The walls themselves are very much intact and afford beautiful views of the ocean.  There are a few historic sites to see, but we focused more on the restaurants, spas, and shops, which offered a wide variety of tourist gear as well as more upscale interpretations of Sri Lankan fabrics and crafts.  We ate at two different restaurants while we were there, and also had tea at Amangalla hotel.  All were delicious.

Title: History at its best.
Text: Beautiful weather and day to explore 95 acre Forte built by the Portuguese and taken over by the Dutch in 1640. Good facilities, restaurants and amenities onsite. Great view of the Galle International Cricket Stadium and many other attractions inside and outside the Forte to explore.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
Galle was on my to-do list as its pretty unique and only a slight detour on our route. We planned to spend a few hours here to walk around, take it in and grab some lunch. 

Its a protected site so residents must maintain their property but cannot redevelop it outside of keeping which gives the place some charm. You can walk around the fort wall which offers some great sights and the inner streets are nice too. 

There are a lot of Italian restaurants and samey shops (a lot of gem sellers) which was a little disappointing but this is one of the main tourist attractions in the South so is expected. There are still good and reasonably priced places to eat if you check trip advisor so this was a massive positive for such an area. 

Well worth the visit, I wouldnt stay here personally as a few hours was all that was needed.

Title: A nice walk of 2-3 hours rich of history and amazing landscape
Text: I would suggest to undertake the walk on the fort wall. It requires two or three hours and the west side is perfect for watching amazing sunset in the sea

Title: Excellent
Text: It was great to actually stay inside the Fort, mind you we could have chosen better accommodation. To avoid the heat we did half of the Fort walk late in the afternoon and completed it early the following morning. It does get very hot inside the Fort and the beach area does not look very pleasant, but we found a lovely place to swim possibly only during low tide. If you go to the end of lighthouse rd and climb up to the Fort you will find a wooden staircase down to a small sandy area, the water was lovely and clean and a welcome relief from the heat. Beware of hidden taxes on menus, a few have taxes included in price, some have 10% which is expected, but beware of the ones that charge a whopping 18% or more. We also saw turtles here, but not up close unfortunately.

Title: A REMNANT OF TIMES PAST.....
Text: A must when you visit Galle, it's essential to seek out a destinations history to understand its present.... a walk in Galle Fort bears all the remnants of times past and will give a true appreciation of it as it is today.... delightful.

Title: If in a Galle then fort is must!!
Text: We went to the fort in the evening around sunset and the place was really beautiful. Put on proper comfortable shoes as you will need to walk all around the place. Also from the top , on one side,you will see the sea surrounding Galle and other side you will be able to see the town. The Dutch architecture was really beautiful

Title: A world away but watch out for scammers on the way there
Text:
Lovely place to walk around and enjoy international high quality restaurants.  While expensive for Sri Lanka, these high end restaurants are half the price of any western. 
Modern stores located within beautiful restored and maintained buildings. 

If you arrive by train watch out for well dressed men claiming to work for the government/railways saying the fort is closed (due government official visiting) and recommending an official metered tuk-tuk to take you to other sites before the Fort opens.  This is a scam and they drive you to places attempting to force you to purchase various things or pay for walking around sites of little interest. 

Plan your trip head, straight to the Fort, its only 1km away from the train station and well worth a visit or overnight stay in one of the beautiful, historic buildings within the Fort.

Title: History and style
Text: Galle Fort is a world heritage listed walled town begun in the15th century by the Portuguese and added to by subsequent Dutch and British invaders. There are so many fabulous old buildings it is hard to pick a favourite. A great number have become hotels, shops, restaurants etc, but there are still plenty of beautiful private homes. Walking the fort wall at sunset is the thing to do, and just walking the streets at anytime is lovely, particularly first thing in the morning before the crowds. Beware- it is very difficult to walk around the fort without buying wonderful gemstone jewellery!

Title: 5 Days for wanfering and eating
Text: A perfect location to launch into other day trips. Fabulous beaches surround Galle Fort. Only 500 rupees will get you to most. The Fort is brimming with tea shops, cafes, restaurants, bars and shopping.

Title: Must do at least Once!
Text:
You don't have to pay any entrance fee to enjoy Galle Fort :)
It's a nice walk along the wall, and it's all connected. You can walk from one end all the way to the beach and viewpoint area. 

It's amazing how the fort is standing for so long through history.
There's an area where there is a huge drop, sadly there are a lot of rubbish thrown down there. It's a pity how people can fail to help maintain things.

There's a small beach but crowded with people. Walk further up and you will see sort of like a Viewpoint, also crowded with people. Before the viewpoint there is an area not too big almost nobody (think it's opposite the white mosque). We sat there with our legs hanging over the cliff while waiting for the sunset. It's a very high fall but doesn't seem like it in the picture I attached. 

It was amazing, peaceful and windy. Our enjoyment was short-lived as people began flocking to the spot we were at and started taking pictures. 
Do make sure u check out the fort at least once, I think it's worth taking the time.

Title: Galle on a tour
Text: We visit the galle fort on a tour with Passion tours.The fort is impressive and must stand on your list if you visiting the South coast!

Title: Must
Text: Who had enough from the ugly new buildings along the roadside with all the eyehurting publicity, will feel in heaven here! So far the nicest town and a absolute must go there!!! At least two or more nights.

Title: Great
Text: Great place but becareful of touts. Loads of nice things to eat and see. From fine dining to cheap eats.

Title: Amazing Viewa
Text: The Fort had amazing views of the harbor.  I was fascinated walking around the fort and enjoying all the views.

Title: Throwback in time and history
Text: We visited the fort today and it was a nice and hot day. We visited by tuk tuk from Hikkaduwa which was good and accurate. The driver dropped us at the beginning and we walk all the way to the walls and fortifications having feelings of how was the time and what was going on those times back in the past. It is a very well preserved monument with lighthouse and old clock. Inside the fort there is a whole city with hotels, restaurants and shops. Some f them have good prices some others definitely very expensive. One bad spot for us was that cars and any other vehicle must not be allowed to enter the fort or at least till one point cause all the nice paths that you can walk and explore are full of them which also drive fast and you need to be careful on every step. Another bad spot is that some drivers of transfers and tuk tuk are so pressing and annoying even if you say, no thank you.

Title: Enjoyable walk  and views along the fort wall
Text:
Definitely worth doing. We were dropped at one end and we walked along, enjoying the view of  beautiful clean water of the Indian Ocean. Very picturesque. There is a viewing point as well. Some cafes and restaurant along the way. (tourist prices) We stopped for an icy cold fresh lime juice in one of the restaurants. 
We were not interested in the touristy prices in the artefacts and gem shops. Many locals selling souvenirs too if you are interested. Offer 1/4 price which is still more than the locals pay
Very historic area, interesting churches, court houses and a mosques
 Full community in the Fort, schools etc We enjoyed a couple of hours there and visited St Marys Cathedral too which is outside the Fort

Title: Must visit
Text: This is one of the most beautiful places i have seen in Srilanka. One side beach , a light house and other side a city. Reminded me of Phi Phi of Thailand .  Lot of good restaurants , beautiful view , light house and you can walk hours in here. Better to travel in morning and evening. In the day you need to have goggles as it could be extremely hot but still worth.

Title: Well preserved
Text: It is interesting to see the fortification and explore the fort area built by the Dutch on this beautiful rugged coastline. We walked round the walls, saw the lighthouse, walked through a parade of high end shops in an old restored Dutch building, passed the High Court building and watched groups of young boys playing cricket in the square. Here an amazing banyan tree provided shade. Next we explored the maze of narrow streets with their shops, cafes and restaurants before watching the sun set into the sea while drinking the local beer.

Title: Something southern you can think of.
Text:
Loved at first sight with this place! Second time visit to Sri Lanka and I am so happy I choose this itinerary. Went on the afternoon between 4 pm. Its windy and breezy, lively with all the locals and foreigners crowding around.
