You can take as much photos as you can as the view is just beautiful with the ocean beach  overlooking the lovely lighthouse what else can I ask for. To think of it's just not the lighthouse, but as a solo explorer, your feet will just take you around the fort, to get a view of the city area if you walk all throughout the end.  This place is nice to see by afternoon evening time to see the sunset, in the night to have a snap of the lighthouse and seeing stars on the sky, and also in the early morning between before 6 am to have a walk or jog around while seeing the Sunrise! It's just amazing. Early morning vibes in this place is quite, not so crowd, you can see locals and few foreign walking exercising, jogging, photo shooting. Locals are friendly, got some small talks in between. I am lucky not to be scammed.
Tips: See the place by sunset and sunrise and night time
Bring a small bottle of water while walking around and a folded umbrella, evening time may rain with few rain showers.
Bring some snacks while enjoying the view it's like picnic in the fort. Bring a selfie stick or a small tripod if your on solo.
Early morning activities recommended. 
Can never forget this place.

Title: Good way to spend an afternoon
Text:
We walked along the wall of the fort from the lighthouse to the clock tower, which I believe is almost a km long. Views were great. It was cloudy and rainy, but the sunset sky still looked great, and would probably be even better on a clear day. 

There looked to be a pretty happening area with hotels and restaurants, all in old colonial style buildings. Had we had more time we probably would've liked to have dinner there.

Title: Galle fort and galle timepiece
Text: Galle fort and galle clock was too good. And the scenery from the the fort also was great. And the fort and architecture was too good to ignore. No wonder the place is in the UNESCO land of heritage.

Title: Nice free walk
Text: I was really surprised they dont charge for a walk around the fort walls. I think that is what may be missing though! A very cheap entrance fee would allow them to keep the walls better maintained and the rubbish cleared

Title: Beautiful
Text: Really nice place to see the history of Galle. It is definitely worth it to visit when you are interested in seeing older buildings. Especially the sunset is nice!

Title: History of occupation.
Text: The fort dates to 1588, constructed by the Portuguese and, later, when defeated by the Dutch, underwent extensive additions to it's fortifications from 1649  onwards, until captured by the British in 1796. Today it is a UNESCO site and the Dutch influence on the architecture of the area is clearly evident. Some of the building that still exist include  the Dutch Reformed Church, Government House,  National Maritime Museum, Old Dutch Hospital and, of course, the fortified walls and bastions of the town, A good guide will point our the few landmarks from the Portuguese and the later British occupations. There has been extensive restoration of houses and commercial premises but still much to do. Lovely walking area with assorted shops, restaurants and accommodation.

Title: Lovely town.
Text: We were travelling from Mirissa to Colombo with our driver as part of a Citrus Holiday tour of the country. Its a great place to stop and visit and was recommended by our driver. Its a great place to photograph and has a great history being occupied by Portuguese, Dutch and British. The different influences are everywhere. It showed another aspect of the country.

Title: A lot of history in this place
Text:
A great visit for history buffs. There is a quaint little village with the history of the dutch showing through. 

Some fantastic shopping options for gems and clothes though priced for the tourists. 

It tends to get very warm along the fort wall with not too many options for a drink/rest and hence would recommend that you carry a lot of water/drinks with you.

Not suggested for young kids as it gets too warm and they don't seem to be able to take the heat well.

With the combination of the heat, it is nice to find a place to sit down for a lunch topped by a gelato that you will find in the cafes/shops that line the village.

Title: Fabulously preserved fort/ rampart
Text: The impressive old Dutch fort/ rampart is in great condition. You can walk most of the way around, although you'd probably be best wearing sneakers because there are some parts that require a big step or a bit of a jump across a hastily-made wooden plank bridge. It's a very hot area, and there's very little shade along the rampart, so I'd suggest going early morning or late afternoon, rather than trying to do it in the heat of the day. There are also a few nice swimming areas, so bring your swimming things!

Title: A piece of history
Text: The UNESCO listed Galle Fort was on the list of places to visit. The walls of the fort are in tact and provide an amazing view of the sea. The surrounding area is. It well maintained and is very hot. I would suggest sunscreen, a hat and plenty of water. Try visiting in the evening near sunset fir great views or bring swimmers for a dip near the lighthouse

Title: A great snapshot of history
Text:
Worth a visit. The walls, ruins and fort are across the town, so you need to be prepared to walk and will certainly need sun cream as theres limited shade. 

There are restaurants dotted around with small areas of beach to chill out and rest. 

The only thing I didnt like were the men walking round with very clearly abused and traumatised monkeys on the end of ropes. To see tourists actually having pictures with them was heart breaking.

Title: interesting
Text: On a hot day we walked around the walls with an occasional look into the town.  It is an interesting site, good views of the sea and of the cricket ground. Need a hat sunscreen and water if you intend walking as there is little shade on the ramparts

Title: Wonderful experience
Text:
The mixture of cultures is very absorbing, with local stores mixed with western type stores.
Lovely places to eat, and the walk round the walls was very stimulating. The views over the sea are magnificent.
You can't visit Sri Lanka without going there!

Title: Amazing, unique and boutique
Text:
I have travelled a lot but Galle Fort is out of this world. It is a feast of unique things to see. The architecture, the ambience, the restaurants, the shops, the history. 
Its a must for ones life bucket list.

Title: Could have skipped it
Text: We came to Galle just for one night and stayed inside the fort. Our hotel was amazing (Le Jardin du Fort) and the town pleasant. All the shops sell the the same gimcracks and really inflated prices compared to most other parts of Sri Lanka. The views from the fort walls are beautiful and like all over Sri Lanka the people are really nice, friendly and helpful. If you are coming and not planning any excursions outside the fort 1 night is plenty.

Title: Walled City
Text: This UNESCO site is beautiful and accessible.  Freely circumambulate the walls, popping in to enjoy the colonial decor.  Some of the city is still rebuilding/refurbishing, but most of it is in great shape.

Title: Historic fortification
Text:
Galle Fort is a UNESCO site first built by Portuguese and then expanded by the Dutch to protect the natural deep water harbour of Galle.  Much of the walled ramparts that encircle the inner city remain and are able to be walked upon, offering views across the harbour or back into the inner city. 

We were taken around by a Sri Lankan local and expected to learn more about the fort's purpose, operations and maybe visiting one of the museums. Rather despite it being quite hot and humid, we basically walked the ramparts. 
It is such a significant feature in Galle so it's worthy visiting.

Title: Warm & lively place
Text: Historicall place full of life ,lots of restaurants & cafe & handicrafts shops that you buy some souvenirs. Church & mosque located inside that you should walk hours to enjoy the place .if you book le grand Galle hotel is close to old Galleh.

Title: Really interesting site of history
Text: As part of a group tour we visited Galle Fort and learned about its history. It was good to be able to compare it to Jaffna Forte which is a ruin. We were able to take pictures of the cricket oval and of course sunset. Also had a nice stop for some refreshments in AC. The Church was also very interesting.

Title: Really cool walk through time...
Text: I really enjoyed walking along the fort as it felt like walking through history. The structure is still pretty much intact and well preserved. Well worth the stop.

Title: Scam to watch for at fort
Text:
Galle fort was extremely interesting to visit and I enjoyed my day there.One scam to watch for is people selling old coins purported to come from ship wrecks.It is against the law in Sri Lanka to remove artifacts from wrecks that are 100 years or more old. This alone should make you wary.
The coins are nicely corroded to look like they are from the sea but in the days when anyone can look up the value of coins on the internet why would anyone sell a 1641 Dutch silver dallaar worth over $300US for $20-$27.
The coins are fake so don't get caught.

Title: Quaint old Dutch Fort town
Text:
The fort area of Galle very historic and definitely worth a trip.
The whole area oozes charm, with lots of historic things to see and do.
There are plenty of beautiful shops, galleries and restaurants to help you wind your way through the small pretty streets.
It does however all seem to close quite early and most places close by about 9pm and lots of the restaurant are full by 7pm to factor that I when looking for something to eat.   A lot of restaurant do not serve alcohol either, so be sure to check that out before you choose a table.

Title: Walk around the ramparts
Text: You can walk around most of the ramparts which allow you stunning views across the coast and town. It is fairly exposed so it would be best to do it during the coolest parts of the day.

Title: Lovely old town
Text:
We traveled by train from Bentota a journey of 50 minutes on the fast train about £1.20 return 
Just be very careful at the train station at Galle  as out side there is a few tuk tuk drivers and a few other con artist trying to scam you 
So be aware!!  the fort is open all day with loads of interesting Dutch, English and Sri Lankan buildings 
Try the local chai its well worth the visit

Title: History
Text: This area offers a little bit of something for everyone. I recommend you do a little bit of research before you come so you can better understand about the fort and its history, or take a guided tour. There are plenty of souvenir shops, cafes, restaurants and antique shops to while away the hours or you can do what we did and found our accommodation in the fort. A must see for anyone visiting Sri Lanka but remember it gets very hot inside the fort.

Title: Vibrant
Text:
We spent the last 3 nights of our Sri Lanka tour at Galle, with time to wander round the old area near the lighthouse. Despite it being busy with tourists it's well worth a visit.
There are many old buildings such as the lighthouse, police station, magistrates court, Dutch Reformed Church, Great Warehouse and the Dutch Hospital to name but a few.
The local fish market and fishing boats are also worth seeing as well as the street market. Find a courtyard for a cool drink in the shade.

Title: Wonderful experience at this world heritage
Text: Spectacular view and marvellous architecture. Finest restaurants and shopping options. I love peaceful environment.

Title: Beautiful place
Text: Huge amount of history here in the Dutch fort. Such an amazing place to explore and wander around. The place is well looked after and its still very beautiful. Great spot to visit and spend a few hours.

Title: Stunning piece of History
Text: My wife and I visited here during our recent tour of Sri Lanka ????. We spent several hours exploring the walls and the little side streets inside the fort walls. Lots to see and do, plenty of places to enjoy a cold drink or a relaxing meal. Also lots of tourist souvenir shops, the only ones we saw during our whole trip. Well worth spending a few hours wandering around, thoroughly enjoyable. Highly Recommended

Title: Well worth looking around
Text: Had a great time discovering all the nooks of Galle Fort! Many great eateries to visit and try and you could spend a day just discovering and the scenery.

Title: Dutch Colonialism
Text: Wander the cobblestone streets inside this well preserved Colonial Dutch Fort and witness living history surrounding you. You can see the Tsunami water level marked by the harbour, which was devastating. Plenty of shops, cafes and restaurants nearby to satisfy any tourists appetite.

Title: A Fascinating Place
Text: A magnificent place to walk and relax. Very well preserved and far from the noise of the vehicles. Walking through the walls of Galle at sunset is one of the most beautiful views you can have in Sri Lanka. It also has a small beach that is not worth much. Children play with kites, the wind "refreshes" your face. It's a feeling of calm and peace as you watch the red disc disappear into the sea.

Title: a site with rich history and until recent times serve its purpose
Text: Nice fort which kept those within alive during the tsunami. got a really good background of the history through the guide we engaged and a nice walk along the fort walls. Grand and filled with historical buildings.

Title: Intrepid tour
Text: A beautiful place to visit and wander the streets, soak up the history and visit historical monuments including the Dutch Church where plaques are located in memory of those that died of malaria.

Title: Must stop by
Text: Good idea to stop here...this place had significant historical significance.  Different kinds of architecture, interesting to see.  Easy to walk around but make sure to get a guide or read up before you get there.

Title: Interesting ....
Text:
Worth a wander around and guess what the various buildings were used for. Good views of the surrounding area and famous cricket ground.

Would recommend walking along the extensive fort walls too keeping an eye open for monitors, sharks, crabs and lots of birds.

Title: Beautiful cobbled streets
Text: Had a lovely time walking around Galle fort area. The cobbled streets, few boutique stores contributed to a good few hours in Galle.

Title: Colonial Dutch charm
Text:
We were staying at the Amari Galle, which is a 10min tuk tuk ride away from the fort. It cost us 500Sr each way (£2). Our first driver offered to wait for us but there really is no need. Theres loads of tuk tuks around and it was easy getting back to our hotel. We had a leisurely walk around the walls which took about 40 mins at a slow pace. Along the way there was a very picturesque lighthouse and for cricket fans; a cracking view of the Galle Stadium. We also wandered the streets inside the walls, which had a very chilled out vibe and bags of colonial Dutch charm. Loads of restaurants around if you fancy a refreshment break. This was definitely worth seeing and would recommend. 

Iain, London

Title: Culturally interesting Fortified Old Town
Text: We visited Galle Fort for a few hours.  It is a complete walled town dating back to the Dutch origins with interesting and intact buildings from that time.  The walls are grassy park areas where games and general relaxation takes place.  Within the walls there are a lot of touristy shops in addition to thriving business.  For greatest enjoyment at this time of year, head there early in the day or later as it is very hot.

Title: Nice Experience
Text:
Love to see that historical place recommend to visit in the evening to catch the best sunset experience on the fortification. 
There are nice cafes, restaurants & boutique shops as well. nice footpaths and you could travel all around the fort by following those, very friendly people and neighborhood. there's a museum, clock tower, light house also to discover. 
Love to visit again.!

Title: Wonderful
Text: A wonderful historical place to spend your evenings. The sunset view is extraordinary with the relaxing sea breeze.

Title: Fortified town
Text: This is a really nice fortress complex on the sea front at Galle. Entry is via an arched opening in the walls, and once inside the peaceful ambience is quite different from the hustle bustle of the main town. You'll find little lanes lined with shops, restaurants, bars, and the occasional museum. There are also small guest houses, hotels and lanes with attractive private residential properties. Walk up to the lighthouse and you'll get good views out to sea. Also make sure to find the clock tower. This was a real town back in the 17th century and still retains that feel. Really nice.

Title: History Awaits
Text: Galle Fort is a wonderful example of 17th Century fortifications. The Fort was improved over the years by both the Dutch & lastly the English.  The Fort in its heyday was a bastion of the Dutch East Indies Company and is still in remarkable good condition. The old town is mostly a mixture today of shops & accommodation with private residences as well. Stroll the ramparts & look out to sea to repel all invaders like days of old !

Title: Interesting piece of history
Text: You could easily spend a day here. Within the walls is the historical town, where a lot of the old buildings have been made into shops and restaurants (some very high end) but still retain a lot of their historical attributes.  There are also museums, the famous lighthouse, and wonderful sea views. A must-see while in Sri Lanka.

Title: Day out to Galle Fort for a change of scene
Text:
Short trip from hotel by tuk tuk. Great views out to sea from the fortress walls with a cooling breeze. Excellent photo opportunity.
Like a small town built within the fort, lots of little boutique shops (particularly jewellers) to browse around. Very little traffic so able to walk round without danger. It was nice to be able to stroll without the craziness of the tuk tuks on the main street.

Bought some relatively inexpensive clothes in a couple of the stores and some more expensive earrings in a jewellers but I was glad to put some money into the economy of the hard working and patient shop holders.

There is a bar there where we enjoyed cooling drinks (twice) and they provide you with a token which allows you to use nice clean toilets across the square.

We both enjoyed our time at the fort and would recommend this trip.

Title: Historical Landmark
Text: Fortification built by Portuguese in 16th century and extended by Dutch in 18th during the colonial era. Nice place to enjoy the sea Breeze with good sea view, but should do it during morning or evening time since afternoon sun can be scorching visiting at this place. Some of the highlights are the clock tower, the lighthouse, etc.

Title: A place to go
Text: The galle is one of the good and laid back twon of  Srilanka . nice Road and shopping area . the fort is worth a visit for the lover of the History.little warm during the month of Feburary

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Interesting history of the Fort which was in the hands of the Portugese, English and Dutch. It now  houses museums, shops, restaurants, and coffee shops. Well worth a visit

Title: Wonderful history
Text: This area is great to walk around & wonderful history. Such  diverse events in this neighborhood- you really need a guide to explain the significant history bits. It is well looked after & a working village so tou ferl a part of the  day. I love all the public servants in the Saris so go about 4pm to see them finish work ?

Title: Experience the Fort with Shanjei
Text:
My husband and I recently did a one and a-half hour experience with Shanjei. The whole process of communication was very easy via WhatsApp. He met us at the pre-arranged meeting spot, gave us some great history under the shade of trees. He asked us our preferences and then our experience began. 
Following Shanjei through little backstreets and corridors of the inner sanctuary of the Fort was very interesting. He had some wonderful tales of history and cheeky gossip that was both amusing and educational. 
We finished our tour by offering him a beverage and he found a beautiful place with a rooftop bar for us to finish on. 
After our time together we felt very confident walking around the Fort and we stayed and had a lovely massage at one of the spa salons in the old town. We had lunch at another of Shenjeis recommendations,  a rooftop restaurant with amazing views.
We highly recommend this wonderful experience because Shanjei has a way of bringing the old fort to life.
Shanjei also offered for us to contact him any time during our stay in Sri Lanka should we require advice or suggestions... local knowledge is invaluable.

Title: Pleasant stroll
Text: The old fort town is a pleasant place to stroll, you can walk the wide ramparts with nice views of the ocean and amble through the narrow streets, with lots of colonial era buildings

Title: Visit to the Dutch fort at Galle
Text: A lovely place to wander round for an afternoon, the fort is very well kept and great to have a walk along the sea walls. Watching around the shopping area is just my cup of tea, lots of little shops selling curiosities, tea, art shops, clothing, food and general Sri Lankan souvenirs. So many places to eat and drink, lovely ice cream and coffee shops.

Title: Beautiful and scenic.
Text: Must visit place if you are a tourist. Loads of selfie points and a taste of history. Great for an evening stroll.

Title: A beautiful piece of Ceylon's history with the "old city" inside the Fort
Text:
The beginning of the forts history, which was built by the Portuguese, along with a Franciscan chapel (now mostly in ruins) inside the fort started  in 1541. 100 years later the Dutch, with a force of some 2,500 men under Koster, captured the fort from the Portuguese in 1640. They started building the fort as seen in its present form in the Dutch architectural style. Fortifications were added up to the early 18th century. The British took over the fort on 23 February 1796, one week after Colombo was captured. Sri Lanka remained a British colony formally from 1815 till it became an independent island nation in 1948. The importance of Galle also declined after the British developed Colombo as their capital and main port in the mid nineteenth century. 
Today the Sri Lankan government and many Dutch people who still own some of the properties inside the fort are looking at making this one of the modern wonders of the world!  This work is going on still very slowly, I guess there is not enough money yet to build up the Fort to this modern wonder. Maybe the next generation!?

Title: Worth A Visit
Text:
We enjoyed a splendid three days in the Galle Fort and dont regret it. It was the highlight of our trip around Sri Lanka that included Kandy and Ella and surrounds. We were here in October, where the sunsets on the fort were just amazing after a summer storm swept through. This was by far the most western catered part of Sri Lanka we visited and there was a magnificent variety of sea food restaurants, gelato and shopping all at affordable prices.

We stayed at 20 Middle Street and I would highly recommend this as an amazing place to stay (further details in a separate review ??)

Title: Must see!
Text: The place is steeped in history and most of the battlements of the fort still survive. The place definitely is a must see if you are in Sri Lanka

Title: Great few days for family of 4
Text: This is our first time to Sri Lanka.  Our friends recommended we stay inside the Galle fort. We ( 2 adults 2 boys aged 8 &10) had 3 nights here. We loved it. Bats, money's, people, Gelato, shops and the fort itself were fantastic especially for people who like quaint old villages. We used this as a base to go on safari and to the local tea plantations too. We will come again

Title: Very interesting
Text: Fascinating structure with lots to see and explore. Lovely views from the ramparts. Plenty of space so wasn't too crowded. Vendors at intervals so you could stop and have a refreshment.A must visit.

Title: Day trip
Text: It was very interesting to visit the fort and see the village inside it. We walked along the outer wall next to the the sea which was fantastic. We also stopped at the lighthouse which was very busy with a number of other visitors viewing it too.

Title: The City of Gale
Text:
The horrendous rain simply would not stop all morning. The moment it became a drizzle, we grabbed our guide and off we went for our planned Fort tour. 

The drizzle then became a small storm. We were not dressed properly to take in the relentless wind and poodle of water, with our umbrellas threatening to fly away during our walk around the walls for defensive purposes.

It was the most speculator sea ever. Gazing out, I could imagine how the four metres high waves swept over the train station and bus station located right next to the Fort, and those inhabitants in houses on that Boxing Day. 

Our Tuk Tuk driver told us his then fiancé had an urgent need to pray at the temple really early that morning.  Everything and everyone in her family was gone upon her return. He then took her in and gave her a home. Id told him to treasure her - what immense luck to be the sole survivor.

We entered the Fort from the old main gate. The walls were erected by the Portuguese in the 1500s and later added on by the Dutch and the English. During the walk, the guide pointed out the Fort Lighthouse and the many Bastions. The UNESCO Fort was truly a fusion of fantastic European architecture with Asian influence. 

The 300 year-old Dutch Reform Church was a humble establishment. No one was in there during our visit. The stained glass panels were worth looking at. We ended our tour at our hotel. 

I so named the City of Galle as the City of Gale right after our eventful walk that day.

Title: Nice way to spend half a day
Text: We went to Galle when staying in Unawatuna. A tuk tuk was 800rs return (we didn't bother negotiating for a price). Galle was listed as a must see and while it was a nice way to spend a day, I wouldn't call it a must see - if you're limited for time and have good weather go to jungle beach. Wandering Galle was nice and there are many decent boutiques and cafes or gelato stalls. The clock tower and lighthouse etc are ok but don't go too far out of your way.

Title: Significant landmark in Galle
Text: It is a very nice place to take a walk, the tourists and locals especially those love birds are everywhere at the fort. I took a walk along the fort by the seaside, it was breezing and relaxing, it was a cloudy afternoon Jensen not that hot. Not much shelter around as it is pretty empty surface. The main attraction should be the white light house. I enjoyed walking around and gazing at the sunset by the sea.

Title: Something romantic about this Dutch Fort
Text: We stayed at the fort and walked the main bastions.  There is something very romantic about this place.  Go around twilight.

Title: Beautiful Fort
Text: The white lighthouse, coconut trees and the blue sky  make this place is so special. Sunny day is a perfect day to visit this place.

Title: WONDERFUL
Text: This is a wonderful place to spend an evening with so many nice restaurants all around the fort. Had an excellent walk over there.

Title: Very nice
Text: It is a Dutch architect marvel at seashore with the famous galle cricket stadium within its premise. It is truly a very unique and beautiful place.

Title: Nice view
Text: It is a nice walk, the sunset and views are nice. Be prepared to the crowd in high season. Go early in the morning or late afternoon because there are no shades though the wind often blows.

Title: Ruined by the pressure to buy gifts
Text: This was something we all was looking forward to but was ruined by a persistant person wanting us to buy fridge magnets. I have been to places where you get hounded but never this bad, he ruined.  Don't let this put you off as it is great walk and sunset area I would expect.

Title: MUST VISIT
Text:
This place is a must visit and its a lovely place to spend your evenings. During the day its useless to come here as its very hot so one cannot see anything. Post 4 Pm its good here.

This place has a lot of shopping and good food. nice bars.

also has a nice beach if you want to use it.

Title: Old Dutch fort
Text: Took a tuk-tuk from our hotel and he took us around the fort and to various shops in Galle for 2000 SLR (3 hours). Fort was closed after Easter bombing and lots of security. Interesting to see around quickly. Went to Silk shop and tea shop, Douglas & Sons manufacturing jewellers had great selection at prices half that of Colombo - recommended for sapphires.

Title: Great place to spend a couple of hours
Text: Galle fort is very accessible by foot, you can walk through most of the inner streets within an hour or so. By walking up on to the ramparts you get a great view of both the interior and the bay and surroundings outside. There is also a good view of the International Cricket ground from the rampart adjacent to the main gate. Within the fort there are many cafes and boutiques, some of which are quite expensive but if you wander you will find pretty much a place to suit your tastes or your budget. There are lots of gelato stores and tuk tuk son every corner, also banks and ATMs, absolutely worth a visit and there are also high end hotels and restaurants within the fort

Title: Lovely  afternoon walk
Text: Went by local bus from Ahungalla, no 2, 40 pence each, we were on the bus just over a hour, arrived at Galle, we got a Tuk Tuk  which took us all around Galle this was 90 rupee  per kl, he took us to the stilt fisherman, good Karma hospital,  spice garden showed us lots of things you just dont get on a tour bus, it was definitely an experience, the fort is huge we managed to walk 3/4 round as it was so hot and there is no shade, lovely views over the ocean, unfortunately the day we went the museum wasnt open, but was lovely to see and well worth going, on the way back we went to the bus station and got no2 a/c bus which was 80 rupees each and didnt stop as often and got us back in about 40 mins

Title: Interesting
Text: We visited Galle Fort by train from Bentota. The railway station is very near the fort so it is easy to do this. The area can get very hot so it is advisable to pace yourself when walking around. We were not overly impressed by the various attractions such as the Dutch church and the Maritime museum but it was nice just to walk along the walls and sample some of the characteristic street food in a cafe.

Title: Unmissable
Text:
First conquered by the Portuguese in 1588, Galle was later overtaken by the Dutch that fortified the city, also because under their government it became Sri Lankas main spices trading port.
When the British arrived at the end of the 18th century, they applied their own touch too, with the odd lighthouse.

As a consequence, today, the Galle Fort area is unlike any other place in Sri Lanka: a European/colonial feeling in the deliciously salty tropics.

The old beautiful buildings of Galle Fort today house chic boutiques, trendy shops, cafes  restaurants and design hotels.

Unmissable destination on every Sri Lankan itinerary.

Title: Great place!
Text:
Galle Fort in the Bay of Galle was built in 1588 by the Portuguese. The British took over the fort on 23 February 1796. It is currently restored. 
Today the fort is inhabited. There are several hotels, residences, shops and restaurants. It has a multi-ethnic and multi-religious population. There is a Christian church, a mosque, and a Buddhist Temple.

Title: Nothing great
Text: Didn't find anything great about this fort.The location is good, by the sea.It has some restaurants and souvenir shops. Went to a lot of restaurants, but most of them didn't have much to choose from. Been to a lot better forts in India.

Title: Must see!
Text: Old district called Fort is probably the nicest city in Sri Lanka, at least from Europeans point of view, its also UNESCO heritage. Its full of historical buildings, museums, boutiques, shops, restaurants and galleries, for Sri Lanka surprisingly clean and tidy. For sure worth a visit for half a day or a full day.

Title: important landmark
Text: This is most important landmark in Galle.Spread over a large area it provides a good view of city .There are colonial era buildings around as well as a light house.Worth a visit.

Title: Galle Fort Walking Tour with Madawa
Text: Only one way to describe this walking tour - excellent. We thoroughly enjoyed this tour booked through Viator. Madawa's knowledge & English are excellent, the content hit our requirements to perfection. All the history of the fort,it's development through the ages, its occupiers & more recently the tsunami impacts. Madawa even returned the next morning to complete the tour as a torrential rain pour made the late pm tour impossible. He then provided us with good information ,like train times etc. after he left us by whatsapp,to assist our travel plans. First class all round, don't miss it, great guide and more.

Title: Well preserved walls
Text: Well worth a walk round the walls as it gives you good views over the bay. There are also a good selection of shops and eating establishments within the walls

Title: You only need one day in Galle
Text:
I think a day in galle is enough (unless you are watching the cricket) to soak up the atmosphere, walk the wall, look at some shops, visit the churches, and have a good meal. 
Otherwise you will find its quite hot and stuffy in the town. 
But its worth a trip to see the stark difference - its like an oasis (all be it a strange one) in Sri Lanka.

Title: Well preserved
Text: Considering the battering the tsunami inflicted on the Sri Lankan coastline the fort was relatively unscathed.  It's possible to walk around the walls and through the magnificent old gates, as well as view it from the beach.  Stuning area.

Title: Good to see and great views
Text: A short visit and lunch for us on route back to Columbo but a nice stop. Great views out to sea and a nice evening walk.

Title: Relaxing
Text: Took the very cheap train to galle and visited the fort area. Interesting walk around ancient history. Really worth visiting

Title: Beautiful place, a must visit when in Galle
Text: Whilst staying in Unawatuna this week we decided to take a Tuk Tuk over to see the Fort in Galle. Safe to say we are glad we did, what a beautiful place with some stunning scenery to experience. Would definitely recommend going before 11am or after 3pm as we went in the middle of the day and it was sweltering heat with very little shade around the outer wall itself. Also there are a lot of people trying to sell you Gem's, wooden elephants and the usual Sri Lankan gifts which at times is a little bit annoying.

Title: Historic Galle Fort
Text:
Loved Galle Fort, Loved learning the history behind this place, from the ancient spice merchants to learning how the Fort was constructed.
The cobblestone streets with their interesting names housing many sophisticated cafes, restaurants and beautiful boutique hotels, spice shops to the original little hole in the wall shops.
I hope in the future it still retains some of its original old charm. We totally loved Galle Fort, was one of our highlights, especially early morning walking the streets in relatively cooler conditions in search of caffeine!! Was peaceful and lovely to see the fort slowly waking with early tuk tuk bread deliveries, cats still asleep front of house, locals going about their early mornings, and the call to prayer breaking early morning silence.

Title: Sri Lankan historic Place
Text: An old Dutch and/or Portuguese styled fort at the coastline. Idle for people who wish to click photos because of the background.

Title: Its nice but too many shops
Text:
Its really nice location in galle. Unesco and historical place. Structure quite old Europian style.
Too many shops. Its very expensive

Title: Dutch built Galle Fort and World Heritage Site
Text: Must see the Dutch Fort in Galle. You can walk along the walls and climb to the gates above the town entrance. The views of the shoreline are amazing and thick stone walls are a magnificent depiction of labor, time and probably lots of pain.

Title: Absolutely beautiful
Text:
The fort is a must for any tourist to Galle. As you meander through the fort you have breathtaking views of the ocean on the one side, and the city and cricket stadium on the other side.
It is worth exploring with a guide

NB : As it is extremely hot I would suggest that you carry a hat and or umbrella for protection from the sun

Title: A MUST SEE
Text: From the views of the Indian Ocean to Watching the local Children play cricket on a makeshift pitch. Galle Fort history oozing out of it. It is a very easy walk along its length. Another highlights was stopping for a while and watching the cricketers in their whites playing a match at The Galle International Cricket Ground.

Title: Fabulouso
Text: Fabulous with a good atmosphere. Lots of lovely shops restaurants and cafes  Gem prices very reasonable.

Title: A little gem
Text:
Like Paris, no high rise buildings. Utterly cute peninsula, completely surrounded by ramparts. Great walking. Tiny streets and 5 star low rise hotels with beautifully plated and elegant meals. There are also tiny eateries, look for the A rating for cleanliness.  The Jewellers LAKSANA, is a very reliable dealer; always bargain for a 20% discount..I often get more. Before getting into a tuktuk get the charge for the ride.
Antique shops, elegant interiors in hotels and inns are worth looking into; staff are always friendly and English speaking.
I stayed at Villa Aurora; I have lived in the US for nearly 50 years and speak all the SL languages. Look for small gems run by, usually European couples, who have fallen in love with the island and are above the political fray. Great locations to visit outside the Fort.

Title: A Solid Defensive Construction.
Text: We visited this fort from Unawatuna a short distance away. Formerly a very solid fort it now encompasses a number of hotels, coffee houses, restaurants and souvenir shops to cater for tourists. A very popular location it has fine views across the bay and plenty of open space to move around.

Title: Family walk around the fortress
Text: Nice walk around the old fortifications, fine breeze from the sea :-) i do reccomend in the morning or evening :-)

Title: Amazing Fort
Text: One of the best old time built forts in the world. It looks still very strog and it has lots of histroy. Lur driver took us all around the fort and we came across a guy who jump in  to the sea from top. Must visit place in Sri Lanka

Title: Impressive
Text: Impressive but be sure to walk the ramparts early morning or late afternoon as it is to hot during the day. Agreat view overlooking the Galle Test Cricket Ground!

Title: The views are worth it
Text: This is a stone wall enclosed city.  Walking along the ramparts makes the visit worthwhile.  The town is full of shops and restaurants.  You can walk it all in a few hours.  There are also some museums.  At 1:30 the kids get out of school and that can be fun to watch.

Title: Nice historical place
Text: Nice historical place, with really nice nature and cool buildings in fort. Great view to the ocean from fort walls

Title: History
Text: Nice to walk along the walls, lots of history in Galle with Dutch, Portuguese and English invaders over the years. Nice mixture.  The fort is the attraction and well worth a visit.  Make sure you have a hat on a hot day - little or no cover from the searing sun.

Title: wall walk
Text: As you walk on top of the walls, all the way around you can see most of what the fort offers. Hotels, shops, and restaurants. You can also see a mosque, a church, and a Buddhist temple.

Title: Fantastic Fort
Text:
Galle Fort is a must see for anyone travelling in southern provinces. Full of history- Portuguese, Dutch and English.
Churches , mosques  and temples. Beautiful early Dutch colonial houses many sympathetically restored. A walk on ramparts highly recommended especially around sunset. Plenty of places for eats and refreshments.

Title: don't miss now, very soon it will be another one of those places that the sheer number of tourists will spoil the place
Text: Galle Fort is just one of those places you have to have been. just relax and enjoy. There are still corners that are not overrun by tourists and there is always the seawall to watch the ocean

Title: Nice day out
Text: Nice day out. A bit of a drive with traffic if taking the costal road From Colombo. Taking the expressway home was half the time. Lots of tourists when you arrive. Bring water and sun protection as there is nowhere to take cover.  Nice pictures of the water along the coastline. Lots of historical buildings along the streets if you are adventurous. Plenty of restaurants and touristy shops as well. Good for a day trip.

Title: Nice place to watch the sunset
Text: The fort walls have a really great view of the sunset and with pedlar street running off it makes for a nice few hours of shopping and grappling a bite to eat!!

Title: A really genuine Heritage site
Text:
Just love the Fort. It really is a world class heritage location.
Where else can one find a living piece of history that is real and not like a theme park or a movie set. 
The small cobble stone streets  have so much character. There's a great choice of restaurants and cafes, little shops, boutiques and houses.
It's nice to really walk all the streets and explore the fort on foot. 
Really has a charming atmosphere.

Title: Interestng
Text: Nice to walk around the ramparts or watch people playing cricket, would be awesome if they banned motor vehicles.  Across the road from the international cricket stadium

Title: Interesting
Text: Worth a visit, I think if you get a guide it will make the experience better as there are no free information boards.

Title: Jaffna fort
Text:
This fort is rich in history and remains after being built around 1616. Built by the Portuguese and then later own by the British. The remains show the architectural skill of the times. The queens room is still partially intact. The church is only a pile of stones however photos show what it once looked like so I am wondering if it had recent damage in the civil war. The pentagon sharp of the fort is amazing and one could spend quite some time exploring the ruins 
Photos arent really allowed so I snapped a quick few on my phone.

Title: Historical Delight!!!
Text:
Beautiful Historical Place. Loved walking through it at dusk.Was fascinated by the 'corals' in the walls. 
I didn't have much time to explore and just scratched the surface only as we arrived late. So I guess i have to go back ... :)
The place was rather deserted when we got there so basically we had the entire place to ourselves which was very nice.
Took many photos and walked around.
I feel it would be more productive if there were guides. we didn't come across any sadly.
I highly recommend a visit and don't forget to look for the corals in the wall.... still fascinated by it!!!

Title: Fort built by the Dutch around 16th century.
Text: It is sorounded by water with bridge conecting to the main entrance. It is well designed to keep enemies out. You can wander around inside. You can see the gallows which was used to hang.

Title: Famous Jaffna Fort
Text: First place which we explored it was Jaffna Fort.  So good that Sri Lanka has peace long time and it's possible to visit.  It's old and  famous fort, which was build by Portuguese in 1618. We took a  local guide with us, which explained all important information. It was  hot and windy,  so I reccomend to take umbrellas,  sun protection cream and water. It's great place to visit.

Title: Lovely site and views
Text: This fort is huge.  It is the classic star layout with moats and drawbridges and so forth.  Do notice that it was built from dead coral.  Very pretty

Title: Worth seeing and its still being restored
Text: A site to see but still is being restored.I walked from my hotel and it was a rather warm walk. You can see some views of city etc. It was good to contrast with Galle forte that i saw late in my tour.

Title: Good views and needs restoration
Text: Weve explored a fair bit of Sri Lankan during our stay and its good to have visited its three main forts. However, Jaffna Fort needs to be restored and cleaned up, after its recent turbulent history, and a museum, to pull the crowds like Galle. The views from Jaffna Fort are better than its cousin down south!

Title: Worth the visit
Text: We were impressed by the remaining structures regardless of 28 years of Civil War. Well worth the early morning visit.

Title: Worth a short visit but not a lot to see
Text: Our guide rather mismanaged our expectations for this visit to the Jaffna hill fort . The fault itself was built in the early 17th century by Dutch colonialists and there is evidence of solid walls, ramparts, I rather for bidding looking jail and a four person gallows. Inside of the Fort much of the remaining buildings have been bombed to rubble by the Sri Lankan air force during the Civil War and all that remains is rubble and a few statues that were untouched. As others have remarked, this is worth a visit if you are in Jaffna and is not far from the celebrated ice cream parlour which we visited afterwards and which is a must-visit restaurant. You should visit the hillfort but don't be tempted to stay too long.

Title: Interesting, must- see if you're in Jafna
Text:
The fort was built by the Dutch and later used by the English. It was damaged in the war between the Tamil tigers and the SLA. From the buildings inside remain only ruins, some overgrown with trees.
The walls, ramparts and moat are beatifully restored.
Must-see if you are in Jafna.

Title: Nice for an evening stroll
Text: Entrance is free and it's big enough for a stroll, particularly along the walls, but there isn't much to see inside.  Everything, including the church, was destroyed in the war.

Title: Like a lot of forts in SL, good for half an hour
Text: Just a few walls, a few views and not a ot of information. The views over the water were good, but this is not a must-see.

Title: Incredible site!
Text: Very serene environment. 20 LKR entry fee for the locals. A tiny museum with not much to offer. Clean grounds. Lots of derelict buildings and rubble kept on display. Half an hour here would certainly be enough and it is definitely worth a visit.

Title: Environmental, worries. Egypt and Jafna on par.
Text:
Fort at Jaffa is nice, well .. some care could be taken for this place. 
I feel for the people who live here. This fort could be a great draw card for tourists, but we didnt know about it at all. 
The township is only Two blocks away, and the waterways under the township are disgusting. Why? Sanitation , education and services need to be reinstated. Please.
I wouldnt come back up here to this part of Sri Lanka because of a chance of sickness.
Army has picked up some rubbish, but what about the rest.? The ocean can only take so much,like us!

Title: Sunsets
Text: A resemblance of dutch architecture. Played a pivotal role during the civil war as well as per history. Despite not being much to do as such if you do enjoy beautiful sunsets int he evenings do come here.

Title: Not worth the visit
Text: Not worth visiting. The fort is poorly maintained, overpriced and lacks information about the fort. There are also random shacks that have been put up in the grounds of the fort.

Title: NOTHING SPECIAL
Text: Dont waste your money for this ticket, nothing interesting to see inside the walls. Tourists pay a higher price than locals and the fare is totally overpriced and exaggerate. it was a no no for us.

Title: Hotspot
Text: Must visit place. Historic and maintained really well for the public to visit as well as for tourist to come by. Make sure you take some sun cream with you as it can get very hot.

Title: Great sunset stroll
Text: Lovely Fort, worth spending an hour touring, with pleasant views over the sea (and sunsets). Whilst we paid for a tourist ticket to enter the place one could still get a good impression of the place by walking around the outside.

Title: Interesting historical fort
Text: I enjoyed the different parts of the fort but especially the high bastion and its views of Jaffna. The ancient boat was also fascinating.  I found it  a little difficult to try to match the ruins with the brochure. The brochure was interesting though explaining the influences of the Dutch and Portuguese.

Title: Fort that has been played with.
Text: A fort not to be visited in the hot afternoons! Nothing too special but curious to see what the Portugese did and then the Dutch changed. Not that expensive .

Title: Amazing place with wonderful restoration in progress
Text: We were here 5 years ago , in the interim the body of work undertaken to restore the historical site and preserve the integrity of the site is of the highest order. Congratulations to the responsible historians and archeological staff . Keep up the good work, the next few generations will have a better understanding of history  because of your dedicated work

Title: Fort Jaffna - well preserved and presented
Text:
Seeing the Jaffna Fort 'as it is' gives real insight into a fort's hostile purpose and the sombre consequences for anyone inside who lost ground. Whilst the walls are beautifully solid, the internal buildings have been reduced to rubble.
There is a lot to take in. 
When we visited an archaeologist on duty at the site told us about a joint Jaffna Uni Archeological Department/UK Durham University initiative. This has only recently revealed "...if Jaffna's history was condensed in a day, the colonial era would only start at just 3 minutes before midnight..'' Using ground penetrating radar (GPR) surveying they know that below the current site sits another preceding the colonial period, and finds show activity well prior to the Portugese, Dutch and British: finds include Roman coins and Chinese porcelain. What a blast?! Some of these finds are on display in cases in a separate chamber in the fort wall, just to the right, if you are facing the entrance from inside the fort. Allow about 1-2 hours to walk around and take in the views, contemplate the past hostilities, the sea birds and the remoteness of it all, and come in the morning if you can. 
There are WC (traditional). BYO tissues. BYO hat and drinking water. It's about the 30 minute walk from the Jaffna RS or Jetwing Northgate, you can get a tuk tuk there. It was still free when we went (6 August).

Title: visit
Text: nice place to visit and see the Fort and how it was built with and the history of the Fort is very interesting. beautiful place and a must see.

Title: A fort is a fort
Text: I have seen several forts in several countries and its not as huge as the other forts that I have been but still it is a fort. Some reconstruction is quite obvious to maintain its looks.

Title: Walk around to see the glory it once was!
Text: Unfortunately most  of the fort structures were destroyed during the civil war. Mum and I were particularly sorry to see the beautiful church in total ruins . There is a small museum inside that you can visit - the staff are keen to show you around . The fort walls are in tact as is the moat. Great views of the backwaters and fish farms

Title: Restoration just started but it all ruins
Text: Quite a magnificent place, compared to Galle Fort, this one is not maintained, may be it was destroyed more during the war time.

Title: Place has a great deal of history
Text: The area is worth seeing as one can walk around and enjoy the surroundings. We did not have a guide so I am certain we missed out on a lot of details. Not certain if guides provided

Title: A very interesting place, steeped in layers of history.
Text: At first sight, you may think there is little to see here. But if you look carefully, you will see so many stages in the fort's history. Sadly, much of the inside of the fort is in ruins from the recent, bloody civil war. But much can be gleaned from the ruins. It's good to see that chunks of ruined masonry have been aligned and numbered, presumably with a view to eventual reconstruction, to some extent.

Title: A short visit recommended
Text: It is an interesting structure with its star shaped architecture. It may be as well appreciated from the outside without having to enter in the heat of the day. The surrounding of the fort also give a good view of the town layout and water front.

Title: Superb remains
Text: It really is a must to visit with the remains of coral walls and past evidence of the destruction - sad

Title: Fascinating
Text: The Fort has an interesting history and has been the site of different groups' occupying the fort. Its brilliant to walk along the ramparts in the evening. There is room for vast improvement in the museum.

Title: Interestung
Text:
Lovely to walk around the old fort. It is possible to see the buildings which were damaged in the war and also how they are revamping the area. 
A chipmunk was hopping round the walls and we came across a charming cow too

Title: Fabulous piece of sri lankan history
Text:
A fabulous piece of history, well worth the visit, id recommend setting aside a good couple of hours to take it all in. This fort was originally built by the Portuguese centuries ago, one can only imagine the battles and bloodshed here, also evident is the extensively damaged parts due to the Tamil tigers taking over the fort, last decade, which was eventually recaptured by the sri Lankan military.

The Dutch are donating to have it all repaired.. its an ongoing labor of love.. there is also a moat around the fort, a great day out exploring the ruins and reading the history.

Title: Impressive fort and moat
Text: Free entry and we could just wander around inside the fort and up and along the walls. Wonderful views out over the sea. Just walk over from the town.

Title: Surreal
Text: If you are interested in colonial history, I highly recommend you visit this Fort. Much of the Fort has been refurbished by the Dutch government, however, there is still restoration efforts that need to be done in order for the entire Fort to be fully refurbished. That's all dependent on how much the Dutch government is willing to donate.

Title: Nice look into culture
Text: The Fort was wonderful to see because with a vivid imagination you could imagine the defense system and how  the crocodiles would be swarming to catch intruders in the water

Title: OK Place
Text: Jaffna fort has been refurbished recently hence it looks new and has lost it's traditional old look.

Title: Better care please
Text: Great place to see what is left over of portugal colonization. Not very well kept. It could be a great tourist attraction

Title: Intact until recent times
Text:
Built in 1618-19 by the Portuguese before going into Dutch hands in 1658. The British held it till independence in 1948. It remained intact till destroyed in the more recent civil war. Some sections are now damaged beyond repair.
Woth a walk around but it can be very hot in the sun. There is a small area of displays.

Title: great views at sunset...
Text: great views at sunset. a must visit if in Jaffna. Close to the city, parking may be an issue during peak times and be mindful of opening and closing times.

Title: Morning run
Text: Had a good run around the ford . Its fresh air with gravel path. Its out seeing the sea and bridge. Its not spectacular as the ruins are not maintained well . Recommend just See while going for a walk .

Title: nice enough views
Text: after seeing Galle, you will be disappointed at the condition of this fort. Some interesting views, but no big deal if you miss it

Title: Very little to see
Text: Unfortunately the fort has suffered a lot during the long-lasting conflict. The fort itself is enormous in size. From the Southern tip you can see the sea-side.

Title: Nothing special
Text: It's an impressive size but other than that it is just ruins. It wasn't for me, however a sit by the lagoon watching the sunset was worth the walk.

Title: Large Dutch Fort
Text: Free entry. The outer walls and moat are mostly intact. Sadly the inside buildings fell casualty to the civil war. Well worth a visit. Allow about 30 to 45 minutes

Title: Walk around the Dutch Fort
Text: Well worth a quick visit, free to get in and interesting to walk around, not a huge amount to see inside but nice views from the walls. There are ice cream vans outside for a cool down after. Some high steps and uneven ground.

Title: ??????????? ?????? "Jaffna Fort"
Text: Limestone and black coral structure was build in 1618 by portuguese and rebuilt by Dutch later. During our visit, Hindu God Pillaiyar at the entrance is welcoming the guest. History of hindu Tamil books at the sourvenier was lacking.

Title: Nice
Text: An interesting fort, which plays on the mix of stone & water, it offers you interesting options for clicks, and is a good example of the rich cultural heritage of the place.

Title: Ruined
Text: This  famous old Dutch fort is in a state of ruin. Most of the structures are damaged. Now the Army is here. You can visit to  say you visited.

Title: Sightseeing
Text:
Worth to go and see.
Sad that this place was intact before the civil war. 
The fort was bombed by Sri Lankan and Indian forces.

Title: Nothing much there....
Text: If need to kill some time, this is a decent location. Its mostly remains from the old fort. Peaceful to walk about and read the signs explaining the location. There is a small museum, which is free to enter. A few ice cream carts around to keep you sugared up.

Title: Great
Text: It is a must to see, wonderful experience and one to enjoy with the family including toddlers.  The locals are very helpful and great sunshine 28C.

Title: Old fort with history but not easy to park or get around if handicapped
Text: I enjoyed driving around it but not able to climb its stairs or park. The drive around showed areas of boating, jogging, bicycling, picknicking so could be a great outing for a family or group of pals.

Title: Most informative
Text: A visit to the fort should be done early as it was very hot and it offered very little shade. The fort is a beautiful representation of the various periods of Jaffna's history.

Title: Disappointing
Text: Disappointing  why are there so many good reviews to make the fort number 2 of things to do? Still undergoing restoration and has lots of rubbish.  Reads well in guide books. If you have run out of things to see in Jaffna you can might as well visit the Fort.

Title: Worth visiting if in Jaffna
Text:
The fort is one of the main attractions in the area and worth a visit if youre in the vicinity. 

The external structure is largely in place, but the interior reflects the results of the civil war with significant damage. This having been noted, its totally safe to wander and the damage actually makes the place seem very real. Much restoration work is underway. Only place I can recall seeing coral blocks being used as a major building material, both in the original structure and the rebuilding.

Title: Impressive walls and moat but not a lot else
Text:
For anyone who has visited the fort in Galle this is a very poor relation, but it is probably unfair to make the comparison. 

The entrance is interesting with a moat topped up by the sea. It is worth walking round the walls giving a good view of the causeway to the offshore islands. The fort must have been impressive in its heyday but is now little more than a large empty space.

If you are in Jaffna it is worth a visit but that is about all.

Title: Worth it
Text: At evening hours enjoy the cool breeze on top of the fort. The fort houses a government run exhibition which takes you through the history of the fort. There is government outlet selling souvenir at very attractive rates. Some of the things are found only here which you will regret if not bought.

Title: An incredible history
Text: Although damaged in the recent war this was very impressive. The tales of construction and the use of the dungeons were frightening.

Title: Dutch legacy as part of Jaffna's history.
Text: I recently visited the Jaffna Fort for the first time in 38 years.  Years ago the Fort was used as a prison and my uncle was the Prison Superintendent.  Thus, I used to visit and stayed at his residence at the Fort as a child.  It is sad to see the ruins of this once grand facility.  Fortunately, my memory enabled me to visualize where various buildings once stood.  I am glad that the Sri Lanka Historical Society is restoring this once majestic facility to as close to its original condition.  I highly recommend visiting this attraction to truly understand its significance in Jaffna's rich history.  Keep in mind that it closes at 6:00pm.

Title: Bit disappointing
Text: I read a bit about Jaffna Fort before arriving but was a bit disappointed when I got there - there really isn't much to see and there are loads of interesting buildings in and around the neighbouring islands

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Spent an hour walking around the Fort. It's free entry. There's a very small gift shop.  Yes the place is dilapidated restoration - but I suppose that's history (it can't all be perfect).  It's nowhere near on the scale of Galle - but we really enjoyed just walking around these ruins

Title: Historical site
Text: This was quite interesting with good views around. We did go on a very hot day and it's pretty exposed so bring a hat and lots of water

Title: Colonial art...
Text: This is a good example of the colonial military art, a big fort over Jaffna lagoon. Jump to the walls and try to go around the fort (it is not possible to go around all the wall, but almost all) for the great views and wind!!

Title: A reminder of history
Text:
The Dutch fort in Jaffna is a masterpiece of old building technique,still preserved
Worth looking at

Title: Great to wander around in the late afternoon
Text:
Amazing to see the fort before anything has been built inside (especially compared to Galle in the South). Really not much standing except for the outer walls. It's best to walk around in the late afternoon so you can see the sun going down over the water. 

It could really do with a bit more tourist infrastructure - some more signs, information and history would be great.

Title: Just saved from total decay
Text: A lot of work needed and for the visitor, imagination as this place was heavily bombed. Grumpy shop and information staff. No facilities. Quite nice to perambulate the ramparts. Hopefully over the years a bit of care and thought will be spent on restoring this important site

Title: Sunsets and pick up cricket
Text: The restoration is in progress but the scale and importance of the Fort in Jaffna's history is evident and it makes for an interesting stroll. Give yourself about 30-45 minutes to wander before strolling to whatever location you've chosen for sunset which is the best time to visit. You can combine the Fort with a visit to the Library which is close by and both are a short walk from the City center. in the areas around the park locals play pick up cricket - it's a very peaceful scene and the views are wonderful.

Title: Military take over
Text: Good experience in that this placed is steeped in history but the authorities have made no real effort to showcase it post the 2009 conservation effort. Annoyingly the military has unofficially taken over the old Governors House and chosen to live there within the ruined fort and consequently move visiting tourists on (with armed soldiers). Although you don't pay to go in the fort, this is the best kept area which you can't see...

Title: Wonderfull fort
Text:
Beautyfull restoration in progress.

It is already nice to have a look at but after the reconstruction of the old church it must be even more wonderfull.

More than nice fort !

Restaurationers did a hell of a job to preserve it for future generations. And its a nice one / two hour walk in and outside the fort.

Magnificent solid architecture. Impressive and that for the year 1640.

Title: I have visited Jaffna Fort on numerous occasions
Text: What an outstandingly beautiful ancient place is this fort built in 1916 by the Portuguese occupiers of Sri Lanka then known as Ceylon was. As a very young medical representative of the local branch of Pfizer Ceylon Limited in the 1970s I used to travel once a month to Jaffna. Having numerous friends in the Sri Lanka Airforce ( SLAF), Army and Police I was thrilled that the late Chandra Jayawardene later to become a senior Head of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) and another senior Police Officer Percy Ekanayake were residing in official quarters in the Jaffna Fort and they immediately invited me to drop in for a drink at this magnificent  Jaffna Fort. Unforgettable. Later a childhood friend of mine the late Air Vice Marshall Anslem Pieris became a hero in the 30 year Civil War in Sri Lanka piloted and conducted one of the most daring Helicopter Rescues of seriously wounded Sri Lankan Army personnel from this beautiful fort steeped in history. This fort was destroyed totally during the Sri Lanka Forces War with the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Elam).

Title: Must have been grand before it was destroyed
Text: Built by the Portuguese, occupied by the Dutch and British spread over 62 acres, must have been a stunning piece of architecture with 40 feet wide walls, a moat etc...it's all in ruins unfortunately. Nearly completely destroyed in the civil war, the restoration seems to have begun just a few years ago

Title: Wow- great history
Text: Go early, gets quite hot. Walk the walls, close your eyes and try and imagine the magnitude of it. Not much left but the outer walls. Looks like a decent effort is being made to rehabilitate some areas. See it now while its still true.

Title: Really impressed with this fort
Text: The fort was visible and within walking distance from our hotel.We wandered down and spent an hour walking around and inside the Fort.The walls and moats are really well preserved.Free entry in with is always a bonus too.Worth the visit.Great views from the abutments in the walls over the sea and moats

Title: Fort at Jaffna
Text: The  Dutch fort Is an experience but saddened by the look and appearance of the vast destruction. Walked around the whole fort and wondered how all that coral was brought from the sea and used to build the walls????????????

Title: A slice of history
Text:
This was a revisit after 4 years.
Little progress has been made on the governor's house, which was disappointing. There was also no one in attendance who could speak English so our questions went unanswered. The fort itself is a truly magnificent testement to its builders.

Title: Interesting History
Text: Jaffna Fort was built by the Portuguese on late 1600s and then e tended into present star shape by the Dutch. It was used. Y the Sri Lankan Army against the Tamil Tigers and the church was destroyed by shell fire. There are many visible bullet holes on the stones, many if which are cut from dead coral.

Title: Fascinating site
Text:
Jaffna fortress is worth seeing. Its a must if you visit Jaffna. Built in by Portuguese in 1619 and then rebuilt by the Dutch. 
They say that the Dutch used stones from the kovils to build the fort. And the curse fell upon it hence the troubles. 
You will see the lagoon(kalapuwawa) with the  prawn farming and beautiful sunsets in this area. 
In the fort the ponds are amazing to look at specially at sunset. 
Hope this helps anyone traveling to Jaffna. Please read upon before visiting .

Title: Hot in the sun
Text: Very interesting but too hot to really enjoy. The archaeological department  staff were very friendly and knowledgable.

Title: Make it as afternoon city tour
Text:
All what you can see is ruins of fort. Damaged from both LTTE attackers n SL army. 
Will be a nice place to be in the afternoon, can cover Jaffna Library ?? in the same short visit

Title: Impressive howver not much detail saved.
Text: As Dutch citizen  it was very impressive. A pitty not much detail is saved over time. Mannar fort in the south gives some grave plates.

Title: A pleasant stroll in the late afternoon
Text: Great views and interesting restoration work, this is a must see. Afterwards walk around the outside on the new seaside walk and then back into the city through the markets for a real taste of modern day Tamil-Sri Lanka... it's like being in India but without the hassle... magic. BTW don't expect the tuktuk drivers to have the faintest idea what you're talking about.

Title: Will be first class when finished
Text: This fort will be outstanding when they have finished the restoration work.It must of been magnificent in its hey day.Not far from the centre of town,no need for a taxi or Tuk Tuk.Jaffna feels very real,not many tourists so has a nice feel to it.

Title: Dutch Fort
Text:
The Fort at Jaffna was built by the Dutch to protect their interests. Great architecture still there to be seen and the ramparts are a great walk with an amazing view of the ocean.
The fort has World Heritage listing and there is evidence of rehabilitation of the site. Inside the fort is a small museum showing the work being done. 
Well worth a visit and a donation to the museum.

Title: Regal fort in need of renovation
Text: You can see how this Fort must have once stood. but right now it is in need of urgent renovations. the sprawling grounds and the massive ramparts make for nice walks, but there is very little else you can do just now. renovation efforts are beginning.

Title: under refurb
Text:
At the moment not much to look at and nothing like the one in Galle.
Still very dirty as is with the rest of Jaffna, lot of rubbish and plastic bags and a dirty mote around the fort but with a clean up and a bit of passion defiantly has the possibility of being a very special place.

Title: Impressive fort from the Dutch colonial period
Text: The fort is in an amazingly good state of repair, considering its recent turbulent history. There is a small exhibition on the history of northern Sri Lanka, just inside the entrance tunnel. It is easy to spend a least an hour, strolling along the ramparts and admiring the views across the causeway and the nearby islands.

Title: Not really worth walking inside
Text: The fort walls are nice from the outside but there's really no need to walk inside. Be careful where you park your bike if you have one, I had mine stolen at the entrance of the fort in less than 10 minutes. And it was locked.

Title: fish
Text: amazing old 360 degree lookout / fort featuring cannon turrets all the way around. has a moat strangely full of fish

Title: Impressive structure but lacking info
Text: Impressive Dutch colonial fort. Definitely worth wandering round at sunset. But it has been much damaged during the civil war and is yet to have decent signage added to elucidate the history.

Title: Disappointing
Text: The outer walls of the fort look stunning and give no indication of the shabby interior. The fort is undergoing massive regeneration with a large grant from the Dutch government, but that is no excuse for the messy conditions once inside the fort with rubbish strew around and piles of rubble everywhere.

Title: Morning visit.
Text:
This place was knocked about quite a bit in the recent war as clearly modern weapons are more than a match for ancient fortifications.
We went very early in the morning while it was still cool and had the place to ourselves. Although the notices all said it didn't open till later the guards left us alone and we were able to walk the walls with no interuptions.

Title: Get what you expect
Text: Just lovely scenery but not the most amazing thing. Needs more books or scriptures so we can learn the heritage

Title: Good day out.
Text: This fort is accessible from a road running by the sea which can be a little tricky to find, the place has a post war feel to it with obvious old army temporary buildings and bullet holes in the walls of the buildings (was the last stand of the tamil tigers) it has a lot of character and archeology is going on one of the buildings that were hit by bombs. Lots of character and full of history.

Title: Historical site
Text: It was interesting to see the old fort, which had beautiful views of the ocean. You could imagine it centuries ago. Worth a return visit in a couple of years.

Title: A fort under renovation
Text: Undoubtedly, this fort built by the Portuguese needs serious renovation (work is currently being done ) before it can become a real attraction in Jaffna. It is a huge structure that offers nice views over the surroundings. Worth a visit if you have the time.

Title: worth visiting
Text: this is one place thats really worth visiting.  they do ask that no video is taken, photos is okay. there was a beggar inside. its right next to a playing field and the day i was there, a game was going on. :-)

Title: Poor conservation efforts
Text:
The Tourist Board should do more to preserve this site by having more signs for visitors to help maintain the cleanliness of the place. I did not 
observe any rubbish bins in the site, thus the rubbish that is strewn around. The site in itself is amazing but there are no detailed descriptions of the fort and what it was used for, when it was built, etc. This is generally what's lacking in all tourists attractions in Sri Lanka. It's time the government put more effort into this, to attract tourists even more.

Title: Interesting, but a lot got destroyed
Text:
Unfortunately a big part of the Fort was destroyed and only the main walls remain. There is a small exhibition about the history of the Fort. 
The good news is that they are in the process of trying to preserve what's there and restore it. 
There is very little shade - so be prepared!

Title: Worth a Visit
Text: Worth a visit. You do need a guide to explain the history behind the fort. We enjoyed walking around the ruins.

Title: Could be more maintained
Text: You only get to see ruins and the place is not maintained at all. Some cows, crows and wild grass everywhere. The fort in Galles is much nicer.

Title: Moat needs work
Text: We traveled here by local bus 6 of us, not much to see here ramparts are there no buildings inside the fort, needs tidying up, also the moat has all sorts of rubbish in it plastic bottles paper and weeds growing in it.

Title: Some interesting bits
Text: There's not a lot to see here. When you enter, there's a room that describes what they did to renovate and rebuild the fort, and that's worth a visit. Walking around, you get some nice views from the top, but there really was a lot fo damage done during the war, and that's sad to see.

Title: Nice wall but not much to see inside
Text: While the outer wall looks intact sadly there's not much to see inside. The ruins are in bad condition. The atmosphere is quite eerie and interesting at the same time.

Title: Glimpses Of The Past!
Text: It provided a narrative on the historical clashes with the Portuguese and then the Dutch! The fort despite in ruins in certain parts and getting the attention it needs at rebuilding says enough and gives visitors an insight. It is a place one should stay longer and just walk about. It is a pity that there are no government or tourism board staff to provide an historical narrative on this site neither were there a place where we could pick up any leaflets for the same! But definitely despite the two observations a must for visitors here! As a footnote: It is important that officials control the presence of cows in the area and the mess they create. Not a good sight for a tourist site!

Title: Interesting ruins
Text: Very interesting ruins from the Portuguese and then Dutch occupation of Sri Lanka.  Good to have a guide to explain ti to you.

Title: pleasant walk around
Text: strolled down from Jetwing Jaffna; amazingly no charge to get in ! had a stroll around the ramparts etc, probs should got a hand book or something about the place beforehand ! worth a look

Title: Lovely serene place for a late afternoon stroll
Text: By no means a tourist hub like Galle Fort, Jaffna Fort is obviously in a period of restoration with new walls evident but tastefully reconstructed. Cows, crows and goats roam the area and the grass is lush. The unique star shape makes walking along the walls a pleasant experience. Found the setting of a place being rebuilt but still wild and not that frequented a happy mix. Peaceful and would definitely stroll the walls again

Title: Visit
Text:
I booked this hotel 2 months in advance to visit with my friends. Last minute booking was cancelled by the hotel staff giving various reasons. 

For tourist I advise your booking might get cancelled if a senior politician wants to visit here. It is better to confirm before getting there. 

We visited the hotel for dinner and after ordering food, 40mins later we were told some items we requested were not available. Some dishes were far below the standards. Waiters attitude was disappointing. 

This is far from the city but a fantastic historic place to visit. Worth going there again

Title: Must visit - Jaffna
Text:
It was badly damaged due to civic war in late 20th century. They are trying to restore the fort at the moment. Unlike other forts in Sri Lanka, We can clearly see many bullets marks in Jaffna Fort. 

Unfortunately, there aren't much information about the history provided on the site. Information can only be gained by asking local people.

Title: Modern history
Text: It is amazing to think that this fort survived a three month siege in the 1990s. The construction by the Dutch is staggeringly well engineered. Loved the views of the moat and the causeway from the fort. Huge destruction of the interior during the siege but the walls remained intact. A worthwhile monument to visit.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
Incredibly for Sri Lanka it's free for foreign visitors.
Main entrance is near the football stadium facing south.
The Dutch Sri Lankan restoration project has restored the outer walls and moat.
Unfortunately inside the fort is mostly rubble except for a small exhibition space and shop.
Open to visitors from 8.30 - 6.00pm every day.

Title: History
Text: You will see the remnants of the Portuguese Fort. Interesting site if you are interested in History.

Title: Very old...demolished look
Text: Good to place to see and understand the history. Worth a visit. You will also get a good view of City and back water from the fort. Also you can take some good pics.

Title: The most beautiful sunset
Text: Its centrally located and not hard to find. Pay a visit in the evening when the sun is about to set. Magnificant view of sunset over the fort and then Kaytes causeway.

Title: Jaffna Fort
Text: There was a guide who gave us the history of the fort and was very knowledgeable. It was very old with lot of ruins. Interesting to visit.

User_Location: York, U.K  but sometimes India and sometimes Austria and soon to be Germany!
Title: So anti-climatic!
Text: I have no idea why this is rated number 2 for things to do in Jaffna.
