It might be that it was just undergoing restoration, but the ancient ruins are difficult to enjoy when they look like they have become the town's rubbish dump. Really unpleasant, not really anything of note. While I loved visiting Iaffna, tourist attractions are yet to become a big thing. They have only just started to cater for tourism and as such a lot of it is fairly naff by the rest of Sri Lanka's standards. I would definitely recommend going to Jaffna, but I suggest just walking around and taking in the city instead of trying to tick off 'must sees'.

Title: Interesting, not spectacular
Text: It's interesting to see, but there's not a whole lot of info on site. It's good for a half hour wander around but I wouldn't want to waste much more time than that, there's plenty else to see in Jaffna which is more interesting

Title: Historic fort in center of city
Text: This was not a high-light of our trip to Jaffna, but our group enjoyed visiting the fort and looking around the ruins. They have interesting displays of the excavation of fort and its fun to roam and see how they used coral for many of the bricks when building the fort.

Title: not a lot left of the old
Text: Walked around this place but it is not as interesting as the other forts to visit,they have done a lot of repair plus a small display of other interesting places to visit in Jaffna.

Title: Great place
Text: Travelers please come to this part of Sri Lanka ,Jaffna is a lovely place and the trip to the island just delightful.This place is very safe and there is lots to see.We loved it and would return again soon.

Title: Old Fort
Text: It is good to see with the wide walls that enabled carts to transport army, moat, and  the beautiful scenic experience on the sea side.

Title: Nothing much to see
Text: Nothing much to see, it's dirty and rundown...maybe once they do the reconstruction, it might be a place to go in Jaffna...not now though. ..

Title: A place of battle
Text: It was a place a intense battles and there was and eerie feeling when we walked around. I cant imagine the battles which would have raged on both within and without the fort. The fort stands tall in spite of all the battering it would have endured.

Title: History
Text: A visit to the Jaffna Fort is recommended. The construction is amazing considering it would all be done by hand. An information display gives an insight into the history of the area. Amazingly there is no admission charge??  Great views from the battlements.

Title: Nice fort, but not done yet
Text: If you are Dutch and appreciate the history and Dutch way of building forts this is a nice visit, but the fort has been mostly destroyed and reconstruction has been started, but far from showing any complete fort and furthermore, the use of new bricks does give a weird mixture with the original bricks... The visit is fee though, so why not give it a try? :)

Title: Nothing special
Text: Not kept well so litter around. A little section where you can read up on some history. But it's not really worth a visit. But once there, you can have a casual walk around, sit by the beach over the road and visit the Public Library nearby.

Title: Second Largest Fort in Sri Lanka.
Text: Jaffna fort is the second Largest Fort in Sri Lanka. Now a days a major tourist attraction.Must visit.

Title: Interesting history, super sunsets.
Text: Always enjoy visiting the Fort, walking and exploring here, especially in time for the gorgeous sunsets. Take your camera!

Title: large, partly renovated fort
Text: This nice piece of historical art is worth visiting. It is one of the largest well kept forts in Sri Lanka. they have a small exposition which tells enough of its history, including interesting photographs.You can walk all along the fort, partly also up the ramparts which give you fantastic views.

Title: Dripping with several hundred years of history
Text: You can see the levels of history, from the early colonial invaders to the more recent civil-conflict.

Title: Not amazing,  not bad
Text: Fairly nicely preserved ruins,  nice moat. Not worth a trip to jaffna just to see,  but a good place for a daytime walk if in town.

Title: Not much to see
Text:
We took a Tuk Tuk here, for somewhere to visit whilst in Jaffna.
It's work in progress, so there isn't really much to see other than the walls.
The views on top of the walls weren't spectacular, so I would suggest this as a minor attraction which requires little expectation.

Title: A fine old fort ashort walk from town.
Text:
As you arrive, you can see the coral blocks that make up some of the "stone".
the entrance area has restored post the troubles as have parts of the external walls. As you go in there are photographs in the guard house showing the fort's development. The internal buildings are missing (unlike Galle) and the major damage caused during the recent fighting is clear to see. The walk around the walls is easy and the wind off the sea helps with cooling!

Title: Old Dutch Fort undergoing restoration
Text: Old Dutch Fort undergoing restoration by the archeological dept. Despite this a walk on the ramparts ( defensive fortifications) give one   sense of scale and beautiful views of the water and surroundings. Near the entrance is photographic exhibit of the ongoing work.  It can be very hot during the day , take water and a hat.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We spent a short while walking around this old ruin and learning of its history. It is good to see renovation works being carried out.

Title: Lots of history
Text: We walked around the Jaffna fort area, which is quite large. It was good to see that some restoration works are going on. It would be a pity if this huge monument to construction were allowed to fall into disrepair. It is pretty impressive and interesting to see that coral blocks were also used in the original construction. Several of the workers spoke good English and were happy to talk to us about the fort and what different parts had been used for over time. It was raining at one point during our walk and we were standing undercover with a couple of workers. It tuned out that where we were all taking cover had actually also been used as a gallows at one point.

Title: Excellent!
Text: A site of historic significance. Sadly, the place has been badly damaged during the civil wars. A beautiful and quiet place to visit with your families and friends. The site is still under repair and conservation while I visited in November 2015. Most importantly, the visit is free-of-charge.

Title: Little to see
Text: It appears from the outside that there's lots of see. In reality, the outside walls are all that's left and there's not much to see inside the fort. No building or other structures have survived and there's no information around.  The visit would last all of 15 minutes.

Title: Worth seeing ...... Just a great shame the war left so little to see
Text: Once was a massive fort that has been through Portguese hands, Dutch hands and then for 400 years British hands ..... Before being wrecked by Sri Lankan Government troops at the end of the civil war.    The walls are there and being repaired but all the churches and cells have gone ....... Should be seen, all 22 acres of it, as it is an easy trip and with a bit of imagination it would have been a great trip.

Title: Huge and beautiful views
Text: You do not need to spend long at the fort (unless you want to stroll around more of it). There is a small museum (free) and if you go up the first set of stairs on your left as you enter, walk around the front section (looking out to see) and down the next set of stairs you will see plenty of what remains of this site. It is the sheer size of the site and the walls that are the most impressive part - sadly the rest was lost in the civil war

Title: rebuilt stone wall and that is all there is to it
Text: My title is sufficient to describe it. Don't bother to get off your transport. You can see it from the bus or car.

Title: interesting spot in Jaffna
Text: this is interesting because of the walls that remain in spite of damage inflicted in the 90s because of the war in the area. There are few remaining ruins from what is said to have been an enormous Dutch church in the middle of the fort. The views are OK.

Title: The Dutch Fort of Jaffna (Yazhpanam) - on its way for revival!
Text:
I visited this Fort after over 30 years - having heard of  its partial destruction by the Sri  Lankan Army during the ethnic conflict.
This is being renovated and cleaned by the current regime of Sri Lanka and very well worth a visit (although the resurrection in still incomplete).

there are resoring the old fort and work is going on there , well worth an hour or so walking round very interesting

Title: Impressive fort

Title: A must visit of Jaffna!
Text: This place is more or less well kept piece of Jaffna history. Easy to access, and great place to spend the evening! You can also see damage done to it during the civil war, as this was a famous LTTE lair. Do visit if in Jaffna!

Title: Good
Text: Historical fort. The fort is several hundred years old and was built by the Dutch. Not much other than the walls, but plenty of history.

Title: Historical
Text: There is not many thing to see in Jaffna but at least this fort among few other. Nowadays rennovation going on and becoming one of the tourist attraction for all. I visited couple of time and its refreshing to sit on the fort wall and over look at sea. This is an old fort made during Dutch time but was destroyed partly during the conflict. Must visit

Title: History worth Exploring
Text: We were taken back with the history of Jaffna and how strong the walls were. They are still renovating, but great to see Sri Lanka retaining their history for future generations. Inside the walls we were lucky to have come across a local with tremendous knowledge and who was appy to share with us tourists. After we strolled along the waterfront, spoke to some local prawn fisherman and of course sampled their catch the following day.

Title: wandering on the fort walls at sunset
Text: A great place to explore in the evening as the sun sets and it's cooler. Great views from the wall, and good fun wandering around the crumbled remains. Think there might be a museum there, but we missed it!

Title: Nothing much to see
Text:
The fort is beiing renovated but there is till a lot of work to be done.
At this moment you can walk along the fort walls but that's about it.  Within the fort is nothing to be seen exept for some ruins.
But... when your in Jaffna you probably want to go and have a quick look anyway. But you'll have seen it within an hour.

Title: Nice view of the water
Text: Good little place to visit if you have some time. Not a lot to see inside the fort, but it does have very nice views from the walls. There are a lot of animals inside the courtyard, so watch where you step! And sadly a lot of trash is lying around the place. But overall its an interesting  way to spend an hour of your day.

Title: Past its glory days
Text:
Nothing much to say here except that it's past its usefulness. This place was said have been heavily bombarded during the civil war. 

People interested in old Dutch forts may find this interesting with its moats, curtain wall, watch tower and coastal location etc. It's generally is a state of decay.

Title: Jaffna
Text: We hadn't known what to expect of the Jaffna Fort but was pleasantly surprised by what we found. It was quite large and had good views of the surrounding area. When we visited there was a photography exhibition of the restoration of the Fort following the civil war and various archealogical finds during this restoration. A definite place to visit when visiting Jaffna.

Title: Average
Text: Not impressive compared to other forts in Sri Lanka and India. You can step by but overall we found it a bit boring.

Title: Pressed for time? ... skip it.
Text: There was trash everywhere and the whole coast and fort area had a feel as if there had been a big festival and no one cleaned up afterwards. I thought the scenery was dull for the most part.

Title: Run down but very real
Text: Jaffna Fort near the center of the town must be a standard visit for all visitors.  It is partially restored and partially still a mess.  Overall, an impressive structure and a very pleasant walk around a good part of the wall.  There is no admission charge and hardly any visitors when we were there.

Title: Fort at Jaffna
Text: Very hot unless you go early in the morning or late in the evening....a solid edifice although iside you can see the rubble where the Tigers blasted the barracks of the Sri Lanka army..note the scratched names or numbers of the soldiers kept there including Sinhalese soldiers who waited there while the Tigers bulldozed their way inside, knowing that they would all be killed -- no help would be coming from Colombo!

Title: The Dutch Fort the Dutch repair today
Text:
It's not something you'll never see In Sri Lanka. But it gives you the feeling of history. Try to imagine the past of this place, surrounded by very friendly locals.
The fort is in reconstruction. What I saw, didn't make me very happy. They try to restore it, but my idea is to use the stones that are left over, not new ones. But again, this is my idea.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:

Make sure to visit the morning or evening or pick a cloudy time. We visited during the day and breeze did very little to bring temperature down.

Title: Pretty basic.
Text: Not sure what all the hype is about ... it's basically a bunch of walls, with a lot of destruction inside.  The Army is living in the bombed out buildings towards the back - so you can't go near it.  All you can really do is walk around on the top portions of the walls ... not much to see here really.  There is an 'exhibit' in one of the rooms at the entrance (free) but ... they are in a dark and unlit room making it hard to see.  Figure on 1/2 an hour here in the blazing sun.

Title: Interesting!
Text: Great to find out all about the history and also filming was taking place so enjoyed watching the dancing.

Title: The history
Text: This fort is stil in renovation with de donation from Netherlands. The old glory from the Dutch VOC period.

Title: Great tour
Text: We went to Jaffna fort on a two day tour with slimline tours , a very interesting place to go , the fort is an 18th century fort , amazing place to learn about Jaffna , we went with a great family , the history of Jaffna is mind blowing , I could have listened to the guide all day , I learned some amazing history about the place thank you to slimlinetours for a great very interesting tour , learning about the history of your wonderful country

User_Location: Layer de la Haye, United Kingdom
Title: Free, breezy and an interesting slice of history
Text:
Very easy to find and free to enter.    The fort is primarily a ruin, with some renovation to arrest further decay.  Much of the destruction happened during the civil war and in the entrance portal you can see photo's of some of the reconstruction and what it looked like at the end of the war in 2009.

The fort is huge and you can walk around much of the remaining exterior walls, with a pleasant breeze off the ocean.   The custodian is helpful and will point you to the right direction and answer questions.  

You could spend perhaps as little as an hour and tour most of the site, or stay a few more hours.  The renovation works are interesting and you can see how they're making bricks and using volcanic rock in the centre of the fort.

Don't forget to get an ice cream from the ice cream tuk tuk on your way out :-)

Title: Interesting site to visit
Text: This is a large area which has seated bench in shade of tree to take in surroundings. Worth walking up to from centre to get understanding of city's history.

Title: Very moving
Text: Seeing all the damage caused by the war that carried on for ages being tastefully restored was good.

Title: Interesting for archeological and history lovers
Text: Lots of interesting old ruins to see.  One of us really liked it, I at this point was hot, as we are outside the whole time and found it so so.  I found other things in Sri Lanki more exciting.  If you do it, do it in the early morning.

Title: Best fort to visit in Sri Lanka
Text:
I was impressed by the massive building. Of all the forts I saw in Sri Lanka, this was by far the largest one. We strolled around in the ruins and climbed the thick walls. Above, there's an amazing view across the sea with the magical kayts-islands on the horizont.

Jaffna's Dutch Fort was built by the Portuguese in 1619, rebuilt by the Dutch in the second half of the 18th Century and finally felt under British rule, you can read about the whole history in the nice little museum inside. next to the entrance.
The entrance is free and If you have questions, the english speaking staff at the "tourist information" will be eager to answer them.

Title: Reasonably interesting and free entry
Text: The walls and ramparts are really the only thing left intact here with all the fort interior largely ruined. Still, whats there is pretty good and is worth a visit. There are good views out over the sea towards the islands from the ramparts. Entry is free which is a plus.

Title: Fort For You
Text: I liked the fort in Jaffna better than the one in Galle. In Jaffna, one can pretty much walk the whole fort walls without having to straddle portions off it (like in Galle). Plus, it was a lot quieter in Jaffna and I could easily find areas to be by myself and take in the views. Well worth a couple hours of your time!

Title: An interesting place to explore
Text: It's much grander than I had been led to expect by the guide books.  We really enjoyed wandering around the extensive space.

Title: Massively impressive colonial relic
Text: This is a stupendous monument with its ancient ramparts and moats still complete.  Unfortunately many of the buildings it once contained were destroyed in the civil war but the sense of power and importance here is still palpable.  Some efforts are being made to interpret what one sees, but a lot of work needs to be done in this respect, to make it truly interesting and memorable.

Title: Wish it wasnt that destroyed
Text: A very good reminder of the carnage during the war and how badly jaffna was affected. Would love to see this when it is restored.

Title: Not much to see
Text: The fort is nice to visit because its free, but there is nothing much to see there. Its only the outside walls that still exist ; inside there is nothing.

Title: Impressive large fort
Text: Easy to find and free to enter. You can explore all round the fort and the walk along the walls gives great views over the city and lagoon.

Title: Not to be missed
Text: The fort has a very interesting history, the information at the entrace of the fort gives a good overview if you have not previously read up on it.  The best time to visit is early morning or later in the afternoon, it gets very hot and there is not a lot of shade to be had.  Take your water bottle, hat and sun screen.

Title: Very interesting
Text:
Well worth going.
They now have plenty of information boards and artefacts to see as well as the fort itself which is beautifully maintained.
One of the boards told us that this structure that the fort was built on was formed by the Jaffna Kingdom, and its timeline is such that 99.7% of its existence predates the colonial era.
A hugely historic site indeed.

Title: Waste of time
Text: Not worth seeing this place. Nothing much here to see. Just a waste of time here. So hot the place.Long walk to the fort. Just nothing worth to visit. Just learning about this fort is enough.

Title: The lost city!!
Text:

Please do visit, its worth it!!

Title: Bit of History

There is hardly anything inside but it looks beautiful from the outside.  The outer walls (limestone) of The Dutch church could be seen  but the church is destroyed. There is lots of litter left   near the entrance to the Fort, which will need ongoing maintenance.

Title: Recent history
Text: Due to recent history this fort is worth a look. There is not much inside. Some restoration is in progress.

Title: Extensive fort with little to see
Text: The former formidable Dutch Fort is of little interest today, although you can visit (free) for history's sake.

Title: Steeped in history
Text: I travelled for half a day ,thrown all over the observation coach on the train,due to very old worn rail sleepers,but it was worth it to see the Fort.The fort is approaching 400 years old and the history is written in English and Jaffna was the hub of Ceylon,DEFINATELY A MUST if you are in the North of Sri Lanka.

Title: Touring round Sri Lanka
Text: Nice for a walk around the walls and taking a few photos. Nothing there to see yet. They are restoring the fort though. Worth a quick look in the room by the entrance to see some details of the fort.

Title: Tourism
Text: A bit rough and ready but worth seeing for the obviously once amazing defences. The place suffers from a blight of plastic bags which Sri Lanka is trying to deal with, as yet unsuccessfully.

Title: Outside walls complete, not much inside.
Text: It looks impressive from the outside but there is not much to see on the inside.  The view from the ramparts are good overlooking the sea and there are plenty of different birds to see both inside and across the moat.  There is no charge to enter so worth it for the view

Title: Great
Text: Great place to visit and understand how big a feat it would be to build something like this in the 1600s. Amazing cultural experience.

Title: Step back in time
Text: This a fort that had a bad time during the recent troubles, but all is not lost. Extensive work has been carried out to put the walls back to their original state - still more to go. A wall round the outside and from the inner walls gives an excellent view of military architecture. Need to have more displays to put fort life in context.

Title: A lovely place to spend an hour wandering and exploring
Text: We visited both the fort t Jaffna and Galle - Galle was far busier with tourists and locals so it was lovely to be able to wander around this fort in near isolation. There is a huge amount of restoration work going on and it was good to see the care and attention that is being taken to restore the fort. You can walk almost a complete circuit of the fort walls and we had a great sunset the day we visited. A couple of rooms near the entrance takes you through the history of the fort which is a great idea as that does not occur much in many places in Sri Lanka.

Title: Another Historical place in Jaffna
Text: A recently restored place and a good place to visit when in Jaffna. Gives a good view of the Dutch fort and history behind it. Quite a busy place too.

Title: Historical Fort
Text: Good place to visit in Jaffna to understand the history of this place. I liked the fact that the place is kept clean to attract visitors.

Title: Interesting experience
Text: Major restoration works have been taking place and in a few years this fort will be awesome. It is interesting as its set around a pentagon shape. You can walk around the walls and there are a few rooms with pictures showing the renovations. The lady in there was very friendly and informative. If you are in Jaffna it is worth spending an hour or two here.

Title: Jaffna Fort - A Beautiful Historic fortress
Text: Had the pleasure of visiting the Jaffna Fort in August 2017.  I had not had a chance to previously enter the fort but the city has done a commendable job of making it very presentable and clean for visits by locals and tourists. The fort itself represents the great architecture that was present in the earlier Ceylon.A must visit either in the morning or evening (as it gets very hot in the afternoons). There are ice cream / soft drink vendors at the site if you need a snack and parking if you have a vehicle to drive you around.

Title: One of the forts the Dutch built alongside  Sri Lanka's coast line
Text: In our opinion the former Dutch fort in Jaffna gives a far better idea of a fort than the one in Galle. One needs his imagination though how things were centuries ago. Nice views from the fort.

Title: Well worth a look
Text:
This is the only place that I can recommend in Jaffna

Really interesting and given the age of the place it has stood up well, although my understanding is there have been many restoration attempts here. A very helpful lady at the front desk and the entry was free which surprised us as this Sri Lankan government seems to want to part as many tourist dollars from every unsuspecting foreigner they can.

Apparently during the war, the Fort sustained considerable damage by both sides of the argument. It was not clear to me whether the large amount of rubble were part of the damage but appear to be being assessed for further archaeological investigation.

Walking around the top ramparts of the fort it is easy to imagine how many people lived and worked here and how much effort went into constructing the fort.

If your spend a couple of hours imagining yourself a Jack Sparrow

Title: Stunning fortress
Text: Great example of Dutch style of fortification, loved it! Make sure to see fort, you can climb on walls and have beautiful walk tour on it.

Title: Nice walk around
Text: It is a nice environment to walk around at the end of the day. You can see nice views over the sea, lots of locals and a partly damaged and restored fort. It is not the best fort ever, but interesting to visit.

Title: A Must See!
Text:
The second largest Portuguese /  Dutch period Forts on the island, extensively damaged during the civil war it is now being restored although sadly, the Dutch Reformed Church that resided within these walls and said to be the oldest and best on the island is now a pile of rubble that will never be restored.
It is a large fort and one is able to wander freely unlike the forts at Kalpitiya and Trincomallee that still carry a military presence. Spend some time wandering along the Cannon Paths and gaze down into the old Armoury, Dining Hall and Church complete with lectern and gravestones! You may even see a donkey or two.
Look out for the Hangman's Tower, which was also damaged but is being restored
There are some areas that you cannot take photos so keep an eye out for the signs.

Title: it was a long hot walk lots of stepds but the views were cool
Text: worth the walk, it was hot dusty but we went after a day trip to Delft Island so I amy have been tired

Title: They are working on it

Title: A crumbling piece of Jaffna's past

Title: Historical place, but still needs a lot of work

Title: Bit of History

Title: An historic fort of which much more can be made

Title: Beautiful sight a must see!

Title: Historical place in Jaffna
Text: This is a fort located near the border of the land. spreading to a vast area & very interesting place. The building were now ruined & reshaped by the government.

Title: Nice history.

Title: Historic fort, slowly being reconstructed
Text:
Jaffna fort is an amazing masterpiece of colonial building and from the outside, it decides the eye, as it is quite low lying and being built of limestone and coral rock, it merges into the landscape. Located close to the causeway to the islands and walkable from the city centre, it is a huge edifice which is worth a visit. Occupied by the SRi Lankan forces for a chunk of the civil war, the huge Dutch Church in the centre of the massive site was sadly destroyed. However it is apparent that much effort has been made in the last few years to repair and reconstruct much of the inner walls and there is some archeological work going on.
There appears to be no charge for this historical setting although information was being collected on the country of origin of visitors. There is a small shop and also a small exhibition explaining some of the work and the findings. More information would be welcomed I am sure especially of the internal buildings that used to make up a seemingly impregnable setting.

Title: historical place in jaffna
Text: a lot of history about Jaffna can be learn. must visit place . well kept and popular for tourist. Good view.

Title: Interesting, but in bad shape

Title: Must Visit
Text: The Fort is one of the main attractions in Jaffna. Definitely worth a visit. There is a guide offering an insight into the history of the Fort.

Title: A glimpse of history.
