Title: Interesting!
Text:
Staff at the fort was very helpful in educating us and explaining the history behind three nations contribution over years when they were ruling the Island in building the great fort. 
Just be watchful for Mango sellers by the entrance who would quote Colombo prices for mangos!!

Title: Still under construction
Text: This fort is still under construction, but promises to become quite a building again. Part of it is already renovated, but unfortunately most of it is still a pile of rubble...

Title: Fantastic place that dates back to the dutch period
Text: Major damage during the war years, lot of re-construction work has been done, but lot more to be done. A must for all visitors.

Title: A typical fort.
Text: This is one of the sightseeing spots in Jaffna, however there is nothing extravagant other than a fort and a mini museum inside the fort explaining the history behind the fort.

Title: Not worth a visit
Text: Although I'm Dutch this Fort is not worth visiting. There's basically nothing to see except the Fort walls. The rest is just piles of stones. It's a waste of time

Title: A history of batles
Text: Portuguese built fort renovated by Dutch, a significant battleground during the war where occupancy sea sawed between the Sri Lankan army and the LTTE, is being restored. There is small gallery at the entrance to view photographs of yester year.

Title: Windy and Cool
Text: A nice fort with ruins of a church and other walls during the war. You could have a good view of Jaffna from this place.

Title: see it as soon as you can
Text: Currently undergoing some serious renovation, it is great to see it now in a state where some remedial work has been done but to a large extent it is still a relic of the past, untouched for many, maybe a 100 years. Only a small display but itself providing some great photos of what the site was like when work started. At time of our visit, there is no entrance fee and little restriction on where you can go. An absolutely amazing historical site where you need to spend at least an hour to take it all in. Minimal facilities at present.

Title: Impresive fort
Text: I saw many fort in Sri Lanka and this one is different because it has not real marks of old life inside. So you can enjoy to imagine and feel more the military use of it.

Title: Large, crumbling fort to explore
Text: Very cool place to walk around and explore for 90 minutes or so. It's a sprawling complex with some interesting nooks and crannies.

Title: Panoramic view
Text: The view from the top by Lipton's statue is pretty and shows off tea plantations in every direction. There are places along the way (walking or riding) where you can look around and wander a bit through the rows of tea plants.

Title: Spectacular view ! Must visit !
Text:
Advisable to travel up and down by tuktuk. (RS1500 for to and fro trip). 

Wonderful sunrise at mid of the mountain , whereby tuktuk driver stop by to allow me to take a photo.

Title: Not there
Text:
Lipton statute has been sent away for repairs. Return date unknown. Trip up here is nerve wracking ... it is wise to take a tuk tuk from the tea factory. (800$) Roads are really very narrow cliff hanging single goat tracks but sort of paved. The number of idiots driving up in cars and suv and blocking the road because they cannot make the bend is unreal..watching them backup is exciting.. will he drop over the cliff or not... take up a pool.
The view from the top is a gamble...mist is the prominent weather.. but worth the gamble. Little tea shop with black tea and samosas. You pass hundreds of tea workers on the fields.
If you can stop and try and communicate..they have stories to tell. Then tip ...for their time.
I gave it a higher rating solely for the adventure factor.

Title: Dambatenne Tea Plantation: Walk From The Factory to Lipton Seat and Back
Text:
This is one of my favorite places in SE Asia. We only spent one morning there, but I would be happy to return for multiple consecutive days just to walk around and enjoy the views.

Many people only speak of Lipton Seat as a place to go in this area, but I was unimpressed by the actual Lipton Seat. It essentially is just a view-point of the land looking off the mountain at the land below, not a view of the rolling hills patterned with tea trees. The true beauty of this area is the entire tea estate you go through en route to Lipton Seat. The best time to go is the morningthe earlier the better. It started to get clouded over by 10 AM, so if you are walking, arrive early. I would recommend arriving to the Dambetenne Tea Factory between 7:00 - 8:00 AM (or earlier). Then, just start walking up to road, which is about 7km to the top. There are tuk-tuks which can take you up or down, either for a round trip quick ride to the top or by walking one way and riding the other. However, you would likely miss a lot of the wonderful views in a tuk-tuk. We leisurely walked up and walked down in about 4 hours, and stopped for tea and appetizers at the top (which were delicious). Along the way down, we decided to get off the road and walk down the same paths as many of the workers picking the leaves and it was absolutely wonderful to interact with them. They were so friendly and welcoming and wanted to chat with us, encouraging us to come with them as they continued to walk and work. 

Its one of the most beautiful place in SL, in my opinionand the women working in the fields are equally beautiful and filled with generosity and love. Its the true embodiment of Sri Lanka.

Title: Tea and view
Text: The road to up is one of the most beautifull what i have ever seen, its about 10 km between Tea plantations and workers houses. On the top is restaurant and you can enjoy tea and beautifull view.

Title: Certainly worth visiting
Text: Very good views. We took a Tuk Tuk up and then walked down. Despite being relatively high up it is quite hot, but well worth doing the walk through the tea fields in at least one direction. Tuk Tuk ride up felt quite expensive.

Title: A must see in Haputale!
Text:
While the Lipton's Seat itself is a fantastic location,  there are a number of equally gorgeous viewpoints along the winding estate road to stop and enjoy. 

From Lipton's Seat,  you can observe the southern plains of the island as well as Nuwara Eliya and Namunukula mountain ranges,  offering a near 360 degree views.

You should ideally catch the sun rise,  which needs an early start, or should be there before the mist sets in. 

Don't forget to visit the  Dambethenna Tea factory on the way back and also enjoy a cup of tea and local snacks from the small shop right in front.

Title: Fantastic
Text: It's heaven of the world, we went there at 5:30 for sunrise, we had our car, wait their for sunrise and took a time laps video, view and everything is great, after sunrise, we drunk tea, something you have to do after sunrise, the road to top is also very nice, you have to pay 100 rupee/person for entrance... thank you Thomas j. Lipton for this great innovation...

Title: Nice sunrise
Text: Nice view and if you are trained walk through the fields (not the road) to the tea factory of Dambethenna. You basically take the ways clockwise around lipton seat. At the factory  is a bus going back to Haputale.

Title: Nice
Text: Epic place to visit! We rented bikes in Ella, and drove to Liptons seat. There was beautiful old tea road with stunning view and endless tea plantations. Recommend for everyone. At the end of the road you will get tea and cookies from locals. Recommend for couples and families.

Title: Historic monument
Text: Must see where the famous Lipton daily rode his horse to the top of the hill to oversee his tea estate. The plantation has probably not changed that much since it was first founded.

Title: Sensation Panorama in the Clouds
Text:
My Kulansa Tours driver wisely opted to park our vehicle at the Dambatenne Tea factory so that I could take a 20 minute tuk tuk ride up the long, perilously steep, hair pin bend, narrow and winding road to Liptons Seat

Passing acres of blindingly green tea plantations with pickers toiling away the journey to the Seat is unforgettable

There is now a small charge to reach the summit. Here there is a statue of Colonial tea planter Sir Thomas Lipton on a seat but also a most wonderful panoramic viewing point with 360 degree views of the surrounding countryside. The experience made very special by the prevailing meteorological conditions with us sometimes above the clouds and within a few minutes clear blue skies

A little off the usual tourist path but well worth the effort getting there

Title: Wonderful vistas
Text: This is a lookout/vantage point located in Dambathenne at the summit of a mountain surrounded by tea plantations. The drive up to Lipton Seat is an experience in itself. Narrow winding roads with steep precipices on one side leading up to hairpin bends on the last stretch where the road is so narrow that descending vehicles have right of way and we had to reverse back downhill to the last curve in order to let the oncoming vehicle proceed back down. We had a very good driver. Many people leave there vehicle and hire a tuk-tuk for this final bit of the road. Be aware that there are limited toilet facilities at the top. Come prepared. There is a little tea shop at the summit and a seat with a statue of Sir Lipton where you can get a picture of yourself with the old planter. Because of its situation. Lipton Seat offers vistas in three directions simultaneously. A wonderful opportunity for panorama photography.

Title: Scenic tuk tuk safari not to be missed!
Text:
My family and I were lucky enough to visit on a cool, clear day in February. Everything was arranged by Mai Globe Travels and we had a great time! 

You get to roam around the tea plantations and see the ladies plucking the leaves. My children had fun running around too. We enjoyed a nice snack and a delightful pot of tea while enjoying the view.

The only thing... well... is that we feel the toilet facilities can be improved.

Title: Spectacular outlook
Text: Well worth doing the slightly nerve wracking drive up - the road is very very narrow and steep - but the view on the way up, and at the top, is breathtaking

Title: Great sun rise.. You can do it from Ella or Haputale!!
Text: We slept in Haputale, next morning at 5:00 am we took a tuk-tuk 1200Rs to the top!! One way and walked down!! Superbe sun-rise and tea plantation!! At the base you can grab the public bus to get back 60Rs

Title: Fun hike
Text: It's a 2.5 hour round trip hike through tea plantations and occasionally along the road to a nice peak with great views. Take the train from Ella and from there a bus or tuktuk to the start of the hike. Not a "must-see" experience but great views and pleasant hiking through tea plantations.

Title: Great view
Text: Supposed to be where Lipton surveyed his 'kingdom's.. the view is excellent although misty. The biggest challenge was the vehicles that were heading up... congestion was frustrating. Almost wanted to turn back. The season would be intolerable. Tuk tuk is ideal access. The wild flowers en route were also beautiful.

Title: Go if you love tea
Text:
It's a loooong drive to see a tea factory. We were in a tuktuk and had no idea how far it was from Ella - it's almost an hour and a half to see tea fields and a statue of Mr Lipton. Not really my thing but if you like tea go for it.

My favourite part of the trip was that all the way along the road they have deep, thought provoking signs.

Title: Great Tea plantations views
Text: We went to there in Octomber 2018. it was clear every side of the panaromic view. We stayed there while driving to Ella. We could see the wind mills in  very clearly though. The care taker informed us that the best time to visit.

Title: Great views even better walk
Text: The views are impressive however the real joy was walking down. So much to take in and see. We got a tuk tuk (ask for Farouk or his son they are good value - mob 0729545324) from Haputale to the entrance, walked up to top and then all the way back down through the tea plantation, small holdings and villages ending up at the tea factory. Worth mentioning is the little short eats shack opposite the tea factory where we had the best snacks.

Title: Fog can spoil it for you
Text: We visited the Liptons Seat during a visit to Ella area. Although it is famous for its breathtaking views, we were not so lucky due to heavy fog. If you are driving a car or van to all the way to the top, avoid public holidays as the road is very narrow with many elbow bends and our van had to reverse several times to allow vehicles coming from the opposite direction to pass. Many prefer a tuk tuk ride or a hike. We were disappointed after a difficult drive, we could see nothing but heavy fog. So timing is the key.

Title: Beautiful view!
Text: The view point at the top is great and you can get a cup of tea at any price you think it's worth it. The paved road to the top and back is less interesting. It's more adventurous if you follow the trails through the tea plantations and some of the hidden unpaved roads.

Title: Viewpoint and great hike
Text: We took a tuk tuk from Haputale and got dropped off at the ticket booth under the top of the viewpoint. We walked up the last 1,5 km and enjoyed the splendid view. Drink tea on the top and the guys will ask you to pay whatever you think is reasonable. No set prices. We hiked the 8 km back through the tea plantations going east around the south side of the peak back to west where the tea factory is. Hopped on the bus back to Haputale (40 lkr) and looked back ona great day.

Title: Our favorite walk
Text:
This was our favorite place and walking during our 6-day hill country stay. We started Ella by train, it's an hour scenic journey to Haputale. Then we got a tuktuk almost to the top (20 min); for the last km there's an entrance fee and by tuktuk+driver you pay more. Even there were clouds and vapor the views are just stunning. There is a cafe where you got local snacks and tea automatically just as you sit down. It's a cheap place.
We walked all the way down until the tea factory. It's a pleasant 8km walk with incredible scenery; we could stop every minute to watch the unbelievably green fields. At the tea factory there are a lot of tuktuks but there is also a bus which goes until Bandarawela (40min) where you can switch to bus going through Ella (20min).

Title: So pretty
Text: We went at sunrise and it was lovely.  We hiked down.  I think it would have been a hell of a hike up.  I would have needed the whole day.  My super fit boyfriend was glad we decided to just walk down.   Samosas and chili paste are the best thing at the cafe.  Roti is probably better later in the day when its fresh.  I think that early in the am we got the leftovers from the night before.   Still it was an exceedingly lovely morning

Title: Worth a visit
Text: A great visit. We got a large tuk tuk to the top for 1,500 rupees (a normal tuk tuk is 1,000 one way) and then walked back down to the tea factory through beautifully manicured tea plantations. You can either walk on the road or down the steps amungst the tea. Once at the factory we got a bus (40rupees) back to haputale. We had a lovely time but due to our late arrival the mist had set in. Therefore I'd recommend doing this visit early morning so you can see the great views at the top.

Title: Not busy at all - absolute must do
Text:
Liptons seat, views and surrounding tea plantations were AMAZING - nothing short of some of the most breathtaking scenery in Sri Lanka.

We got a TukTuk from Haputale all the way up to Liptons Seat) one way flat fee of $1000 rupee). Our driver stopped at a couple of stunning view points on the way - view of Haputale Town and Eagle Rock notable mentions.

We left at 6am and the drive is around 45 minutes - beautiful country side - but take a few layers as its cold in the morning!!

Arrived at Liptons seat around 7am, or just after with a few stops. At one stay we were the only people up there, with a few other tourists floating around.

Its $250 rupee for two people and a tuktuk to get up to the top - ticket gate is 1.5km from top. Go all the way.

At the top we had a cuppa tea $50 rupee, and some snacks - wade, samosa and chapati - all $50 rupee each. **Tip for the cafe at the top - just get a tea, and when you walk down to the Lipton Tea Factory at the bottom (7km and 1-1.5 hr leisurely stroll) there is a very tasty local vendor selling wade and alike which are packed full of herbs and flavour - so yummy and only $20 rupee each (see photo!)

Tour of the factory was $250 rupee per person - and very interesting. Same building and some machines that Sir Thomas created in the late 1890s. Im not a history buff, but found it interesting to see the process.

We caught the local bus back to Haputale $36 rupee per person. Took around 30-40 mins. Enjoyable ride and gets very busy with the locals.

Title: Liptons Seat Amazing
Text: Visited Liptons Seat and the journey towards it was amazing. On arrival at the top the views were breathtaking. I would say that this has to be in your top ten places to visit on your itinerary.

Title: View Disappointing
Text: We came from Ella in a tuk - tuk and surprised I made it. This was some trip as the road was terrible. Other people went there by walking (good luck to them), vans and motor bike. The view was disappointing as there was mist rolling in making it hard to see into the distance. This is just pot luck I am told. The views on the way up were good though.

Title: Beautiful place!
Text: This is a must-see if youre staying in Haputale, not just because of the views but also because of the beautiful tea plantations all along the way. I highly recommend walking at least for part of the waywe took a tuk tuk up and then walked down. From Haputale, its quite easy and cheap to get to: theres a local bus to the Dambatenne tea factory for only 35 rupees (it leaves from the bus station in Haputale). From the tea factory, you can either walk or take a tuk tuk up to Liptons seat for 500 rupees (you can probably even bargain for less) to the top, and then walk down. Just be aware: the ticket booth is 1.5 km before Liptons seat, and some tuk tuk drivers will tell you to get off at that point. Just insist that they drive you all the way to the top and you should be fine.

Title: Oh my God ...
Text:
What a disappointment ... 
I have to say, first, that the view is incredible. Definitely ... if you know how to forget that they destroyed the whole Nature to build this.

But, the worst is to see the whole pollution of the site ... Lipton's tea grows on plastic. Check my pictures ... what you drink when you buy Lipton tea is plastic. That's depressing.

And you have to know that the women you can see that harvest the tea leafs are modern slaves.They are paid 4 per day and are watched 24/7 by "men" so that they work hard to be considered as worse than human beings (they don't even have water in their toilets). 

Please, don't participate to that. I bitterly regret it now.

Title: One of my favorite spots in Sri Lanka.
Text: Amazing. I would recommend getting a tuktuk to drive you to the top as it is a decent walk, and then to walk down to the tea factory at a leisurely pace. It's 4 or 5 km but it's all downhill if done this way. I also suggest doing it early-ish in the morning (we left haputale at 9) as the fog rolls in later in the afternoon. Again, AMAZING views. A must.

Title: nice view
Text:
very beautiful view
tuktuk up is around 2000LKR round trip
we had luck to get there quite early and be the only tourists on top

Title: Charming area
Text: We had a fantastic driver who took us all the way up to the top of the lipton's hill. Lipton's seat isn't any special but the views there are spectacular (provided that there isn't mist).

Title: Cloudy but worth the visit
Text: It is a very interesting journey up to the summit to get to Lipton's seat.  Driving through the tea plantains along tiny roads to Lipton's Seat is an experience in itself.  Unfortunately, the day that we went, it was cloudy in the valley below and we didn't get the wonderful views.  However, we enjoyed seeing Mr Lipton and what we could see of the countryside.  Even though it was cloudy at altitude, it was worth the visit.

Title: Not worth the trip, you can enjoy the views from many places Haputhale
Text:
It was about an hour bumpy tuk tuk ride up and another hour bumpy tuk tuk ride down. The view is ok if you are lucky not to have a hazy / grey / rainy day. Not worth the trip or the view. Many places in Haputhale to get a better view without the bumpy ride.

Note: I am writing this review after completing 15 days holiday in Sri Lanka; therefore, I have considered all pro and cons.

Title: AVOID THE SCAM TEA SELLERS
Text:
You are led to believe the "cups of tea" at the viewpoint are part of the Lipton Seat viewpoint. They are not. This is just a scam where they will offer you tea and then charge you a ridiculous price for it. Many many dollars for a pot of tea... And then become confrontational. 

These scammers are not part of Lipton and its amazing that they are let inside to scam people each day. 

DO NOT FALL FOR IT

Secondly. Need the toilet? There is a guy stood outside and only white people must pay. 

This place was a joke and made the entirely of Sri Lanka look bad. Shame on you!

Title: brilliant view..
Text: nice panoramic view rough road but good journey. better if you have 4*4 not ideal if raining. interesting.

Title: Fantastic views
Text: This is a great place to visit on a clear day with stunning views. The journey up is best by tuc-tuc as the road is very narrow - it's a great scenic journey up and well worth the visit.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
A must see attraction if you're in the area.  The Victorian tea making factory is still working and is a great example of colonial investment (whether you agree or not with the historical context).
It's in a working plantation and there are fabulous views of the surrounding area from its mountain-top location.

Title: Sunrise visit
Text: Tuk tuk was 1500LKR return. Would advise getting up and watching the stars before waiting for the sunrise. Lots of monkeys around - don't be a Pino and feed them. This encourages aggressive behaviour and they were already trying to snatch food and bags.

Title: tea plantation
Text:
We hired a tuk-tuk driver to take us to Liptons Seat from Ella. 

About 1-1/5 hours away from Ella, this was by far the most scenic tea plantation we have seen in our trip. We were stunned by the view of the tea all over the hills around us, the tea pickers, the blue skies or sometimes the fog around us.

We didnt get to see the view from Liptons Seat due to the fog  still, the trip was worth every minute.

Title: nice hike
Text: so we were choosing between horton plains and here and chose this cos it was closer to our hotel. we took a tuk tuk 3/4's of the way up and hiked the rest. at the top the view was really nice! we were happy with the luck we had. the clouds parted and the view was great. then we hiked down from the hill

Title: You are here, so see it!
Text: Well, you made it to Sri Lanka so may as well go up.  You can take the Dambatenna bus up to the Dambatenna Tea Factory then hire a tuk tuk for 400 rupees to the "almost" top, a surprise as it is almost 2 km straight up...NEGOTIATE and make sure the tuk tuk driver takes you all the way up!  Once there it's fine but the day we went it was cloudy...go in the morning , early morning to catch the view.  We walked back to Haputale a total of about 12 km (downhill) and it was beautiful.  Don't forget to bring water with you.

Title: Pretty average
Text: If youre staying in Haputale or passing by then you may as well stop by but we made the day trip from Ella and I probably wouldnt do it again. The walk is easy to navigate and the landscape is very lush but it was a bit boring to be honest.

Title: Very nice
Text: Tuk tuk ride from haputale to Lipton seat paid 800 roupies (only 1 way) to a driver met in the street the day before (my guesthouse proposed me 1500 roupies for the same service...). Arrived at the top around 7:30 am. Very clear view that changed dramatically in 10 minutes time, around 7:40. The views are actually the best from a curve on the road 5min walk before Lipton seat. Nice to walk back down across the tea plantations. Very few tourists when I was there. At Lipton seat, child trying to get money or food...

Title: Unforgettable walk!
Text: One of the most amazing walks i had in my life and I believe it will be always the best one! Unforgettable views all the way down from Liptons seat, dont take TukTuk when you are going down, just enjoy the tea plantation and talk to the tea planters . For the view on Liptons seat, sadly i arrived at 9:30 so the view was not clear however i love Lipton ?? so i was happy to take photos there. The experience itself is absolutely amazing !

Title: Great view point
Text:
Plan your visit before 10AM to reach there. Because after that mist might cover the view. Amazing view at the top of the mountains.

Best part is drive through to the top inside the tea estates. Amazing drive through as its green all over. We drove through in car but the roads are too narrow so recommend to take tuk tuk from down the tea factory to Lipton seat top.

Spend quality time up as the view is amazing.

Title: A great walk through the tea plantations
Text: Try to get there before the mist comes in, say 10 am. Dont follow the road unless you have to and look for the short cuts that the tea pickers use to get around

Title: Phenomenal !!!
Text: I took tuk tuk from Ella to get to Lipton seat - was 1,5 hours ride but when you get there you totally rewarded !!! The view and the scenery are absolutely phenomenal - you literally can touch the clouds. There is a small simple cafe serving some tea and roti , just in case you need a bite before heading back.

Title: Fun ride up to a gorgeous view
Text: Tour the tea factory then take a tuk tuk (800-1000 rupees rt) up to to enjoy a panoramic view of the gorgeous tea country.

Title: Great View Point
Text:
A rough road up to the place from Haputhale Town passing Dambetenna Tea Factory.
However worthy visit to have a great view of Tea Plantations 360°

Title: Amazing drive to get there!
Text:
We visited Liptons Seat on a day trip on a scooter from Ella. 

The drive to get to Liptons Seat is what was the most amazing for us as we had left it too late and it was cloudy by the time we arrived at the top. The drive up the windy road through the tea fields was just amazing. 

We were cheered on by local school kids and saw the women in the fields picking the tea. We arrived at Lipton's seat around lunchtime the tea pickers were having their break and congregating at the view point. They asked if we wanted to take their picture for a fee. We declined. We were disappointed with ourselves for forgetting to take biros/pens with us as loads of the kids were asking for school pens. 

Lipton's Seat is ticketed and you have to pay per person and vehicle to access the view point. There is a local cafe at the top. 

Beware that at the moment there are construction works at the seat where he is sat. 

Top tip: Get there at sunrise to get clear views! 

We didn't ask if there were or used toilets.

Title: Nice walk - views ok
Text: We took a tuk tuk up to Lipton's Seat at around 8:30am on a relatively nice day.  The views at the top were ok but not spectacular - it might have been better to arrive a little earlier.  What was very beautiful was the walk back down as we could see people picking the tea leaves and were surrounded by beautiful green scenery in every direction. As we got closer to the bottom we could see the fog/clouds rolling in so we were lucky we got there relatively early. The Dambatenne Tea Factory tour at the bottom was a complete was of time - uninterested guide who was clearly more interesting in trying to sell the tea than anything else.

Title: Spectacular views
Text: The view from Lipton's seat and many other points from the hills of Haputale are spectacular. Not to be missed.

Title: Worth the early start
Text: We came up by tuktuk and got there just after 6.00 am. Worth the early start for the view. We then had the driver take us half   way down and walked the rest of the way to the tea factory.

Title: Sunrise tuk tuk ride!
Text: Picked up at 0500am got there 0545am. Views were amazing, definitely recommend the early get up as it was clear and the clouds started rolling in 9ish. 1000 for a tuk tuk up to the Seat. Lovely walk to the tea factory on the way down and he will wait there and return journey 500 to Haputale! And the rotis and tea are a big plus from the cafe at the top.

Title: Lovely downhill walk, visited from Ella
Text: Because of the reviews we decided to also visit Liptons seat from Ella. Took the 0640 train to Haputale and a tuktuk up for 1200 rupees. A beautiful windy road. We walked back from the top to the tea factory through all the tea plantation fields. So lush, so green, so amazing! Really enjoyed the walk, maybe also because it was downhill ;) just missed the train back to Ella so took the bus. Bus 99 will take you to Bandarawela and change there to bus to Ella, not hard to find. It was only 150 rupees for the two of us and took us 45 minutes. The alternative was taking the reserved train but that was 2000... So definitely do this trip and no worries if you miss the train back! Bus is easy!

Title: A good days walk with great views
Text: We toured Liptons Seat from Thotalagala, walking up and down during the day.  The walk is beautiful, taking you through a few villages and tea-picking fields where the workers are very welcoming and polite.  The views from Liptons Seat itself are beautiful, but its difficult to know when the cloud will roll in, so sometimes you are lucky and other times its a white-out up there!

Title: On top of the world
Text: We took a tuk tuk up from the tea factory and walked the 7k back.. a must do! The view from the top is 360 and was amazing! As per other posts , this is some of the most beautiful scenery in Sri Lanka. Walking down enables you to really appreciate the scenery, the tea plantations, the villages and their carefully tended allotments, the lady in red doing mountains of washing in the stream. Do it!

Title: A must in Sri Lanka
Text: We didnt expect much from this visit and we were positively surprised from the view going up to the top!!! Just amazing!!

Title: One of the most beautiful spots in hill country!
Text: Took a tuktuk up for sunrise, enjoyed a packed breakfast up there then walked down a couple of kilometers before catching our tuktuk back to Haputale. Ride from Haputale took maybe 40 minutes? Its not far but definitely a steep and windy road up! Gorgeous ride up, stunning views, and highly recommend walking at least part way down the road to fully enjoy the peacefulness and beauty of the tea fields. We thought it was one of the most beautiful places on our whole Sri Lanka trip. Highly recommend!!

Title: Great view even at 11am
Text: We were staying in Ella and got the train to Haputale (100 Rs) then a tuk tuk from there to about 2km from the top (1200 Rs), there is a small entry fee. The hike is uphill through the plantation and beautiful. When we got there it wasnt completely clear but we still had a great view - theres a cafe that sells tea and Sri Lankan food which is very tasty and not overly priced. Walk down through the tea estate down to the tea factory was a pleasure.

Title: Amazing view and tasty breakfast
Text: I recommend going there by bus as it's the most convenient and adventures way. If you are traveling from Haputale (stay at White Monkey!), it will take you approximately 20min by bus and then another 20min of walking so that you've really earned the view. Go early in the morning to assure that no clouds block your view. And treat yourself with the delicious breakfast for a cheap price.

Title: Feel like youre on top of the world!
Text:
Our review focuses on the natural landscapes surrounding Liptons Seat. We spent about 30 seconds at the statue itself (after driving up there by Tuk Tuk). 

The real magic comes from walking down the mountain and taking in the breathtaking scenery. The tree plantations, the farms the women working on the plantations are just too amazing for words. Our photos dont do the view justice. 

We have seen a myriad of stunning scenes since being in Sri Lanka, but this walk is not to be missed. Get there early morning (around 9:30am) so that you can do the walk before it gets too hot.

Title: Stunning views
Text:
We took a tuk-tuk from Haputale to Liptons seat which is a very scenic drive up in the mountains and round hairpin bends. The view from Liptons seat is amazing but it's best to arrive early before the clouds obscure the views. It gets pretty chilly up there but there's a tea shop where you can get a warm drink and something to eat.
It's just over 7km walk down to the Dambatanne tea factory where you can pick up a bus to Haputale, or carry on and walk back all the way to Haputale which we did, takes about 3 hours but it's all downhill through the tea plantations and is a lovely walk. Don't take a taxi/tuk-tuk there and back as you'll miss out on the splendour of the place.

Title: Visit at sunrise
Text: Visit at sunrise to get a great view - i's worth the early start.  Coming back down you get to see what you missed on the way up - the tea plantations and the workers

Title: Go for sunrise!
Text: We went up there for sunrise from Haputale. We left at 5AM from Haputale for the sunrise at 6AM but that was a bit short because the entrance was still closed so our taxi stopped us there which is 1,4km before the summit. So at 6AM we were halfway up from the entrance to the summit and we actually found the perfect spot to watch the sunrise :) we then finished the climb up to the Lipton Seat and finally went back all the way down to the tea factory while walking through the tea plantations. The sunrise, the view from the top but, even more, the tea plantation landscape all around us on the way down was absolutely gorgeous! Then it was super easy to find a tuktuk driver at the tea factory to get us back to Haputale. A must do!

Title: Tea lessons
Text: A must do, knowing how tea is being made is great. It helped and leaned me also a lot about what influences government, shareholders and in the end customers have on local circumstances. It did not change for the better, and other tea sites are really a lot worse off. A pity big companies are watched through western eyes only.

Title: Surounding area very beautiful, seat not interesting
Text:
In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka.
We visited Liptons Seat during a daytrip with a minivan. The road on the tea estate (where you have to pay for entering) was very bad, but the vista's on the teafields were great!
When we reached Liptons Seat it turned oud to be a polyester statue-bench under an ugly sort of steel and concrete parasol.

Title: If you can organise a walk do it
Text: This region of Sri Lanka is absolutely stunning. I cannot recommend a walk thru these mountains highly enough. Grab a guide if you can and even g a bit further into the high mountain villages..

Title: Go for the tuk tuk ride on the way up!
Text:
Staying in Ella and decided to do trip up to Liptons Seat. Its a good 1.5 hour drive up mountain twisty roads to get there so bear that in mind if you want to go. Not a great route if you get car sick. 

Driver suggested we leave at 5.30-6 am in order to get there and make assent before mist rolled in and obscured the views. However, we are not early risers (family with teenagers!) and we hate missing our nice hotel breakfasts (a packed one is never the same!) especially when you pay a premium to stay somewhere. 

We were staying at 98 Acres and views from the restaurant there are amazing in themselves and probably the best breakfast weve had on our trip to Sri Lanka to date so not to be missed! 

We ended up leaving hotel around 9.30 and got up to the tea factory around 11.15. We then opted to take the rest of the route by tuk tuk. We needed 2 and they were SLR1000 each for the round trip. 

I did a bit of research beforehand and the average price is somewhere between 800-1500 rupees for a return tuk tuk depending on your negotiating skills and how busy it is.    

Some people were walking up but my guess is it would take you 45-60 mins to walk up. Its not a difficult walk, you just follow the road as it winds up the mountain. Tuk tuk was much more fun though! It took about 15-20 mins to get to the top. It was a great way to make the assent and look out at the landscape and beautiful views. 

Once near the top you need to lay a further fee at a gate of 100 rupees per person to go right to the top. 

Im sure the views are great but it was heavy with mist at the top, we couldnt see much if the views. It was still nice up there though and we had a cup of tea and a few snacks that were brought out by a few plantation workers whilst we were up there (tbh I wasnt keen on drinking or eating anything due to hygiene but we thought we should  just go with it.....Im glad we did as in end it was only 400 rupees and it doesnt really matter if you drink or eat any of it). 

The best thing about the trip was the fun tuk tuk ride which the kids loved. It doesnt matter what time of the day you go for that, but if youre desperate for views the go early. The most interesting ting for me was seeing the workers village and the tea plantation itself, and thats all around where you pick up the tuk tuk to go up to the top viewing point.

Title: Truly the journey not as much the destination
Text:
the roads are narrow and wind through the tea estate. you'll see tea pickers busily pluck away and maybe smile at a nosy tourist every now and then. As you go higher, the views are breathtaking. We went up in a small car, so it was perfect. especially the roads are very narrow at the top with hardly any parking. 
I really think the tourisim department needs to develop this a lot further, as the place on top could use better management. but the view. that's what you really go there for.

Title: Spectacular views on a clear day
Text: Fascinating view where Sir Lipton could keep an eye on his tea plantations. Cute simple little cafe serving delicious rottis and red tea,

Title: Amazing view
Text: Went here yesterday with my local friend and i couldn't stop taking videos and photos to stay with me forever and show to my friends. It's one of the reasons i wanted to vidit Sri Lanka.

Title: Wonderful countryside
Text: The view from the top could have been better due to the weather. The real highlight was the walk back from the seat to Haputale. Quiet road with superb views. This was recommended by the Nature View guest house in Haputale. We took the bus from Haputale to the tea factory and then a tuk tuk to 1.5 km from the top

Title: Weather dependant
Text:
It makes for a nice walk in the tea plantation from the factory nearby. You can get a bus from the town to a point just 2km from the main attraction if you prefer. The cost is Rs100 for foreign visitors. 

It has a nice view if the weather is clear and some good photo opportunities with the statue of Lipton too. 

It's a famous spot in the area so could be busy at peak times but it's worth the walk.

Title: Nice view
Text: Lots of driving in a tuk tuk for a good view of tea plantation. There is a tea room up top and a viewing tower, both a waste of time.

Title: The journey is the reward
Text: I started from Ella with a train to Haputale. From there I took the bus to the Tea factory. I can't understand why people take the journey to the top with a tuktuk or a minivan. The hike through the tea plantations was exhausting but totally worth it. The liptons seat itself is quite nice, but not that special (to many people, to many tuktuks)

Title: Fantastic
Text: Lipton's seat is situated in the Hill country East of Haputale. The views on a clear day from the top are absolutely stunning beautiful. It is possible to walk or take a Tuktuk. We enjoyed very much the views and a nice cup of tea from the small friendly restaurant at the top. Well worth a visit.

Title: Definitely worthy visiting
Text:
Fantastic experience with great views.
Lovely walk through the tea plantations to get there, but you can also hire a tuk-tuk.

Title: Worth the effort. Nice view of tea plantations
Text:
We enjoyed visiting Liptons Seat.
The area has great views of lovely tea plantations and a lot of history. You can get nice tea and breakfast at the little restaurant next to Liptons Seat. Dont pay more than 50 rupees for a cup of tea

Title: Not worth it!
Text:
Don't go unless it's a perfectly clear day - which you can't guarantee.
To get here takes a very, very long, uncomfortable, winding drive along very poor roads - our driver got stuck several times. There had been a lot of hype so we were very excited about this stop...what a massive disappointment!!
The weather was poor so when we finally reached the top all we could see was cloud.
Added to that, the promise of refreshment at the top was met by a tiny shack selling only local tea (incredibly sweet) and snacks (exceptionally spicy) with questionable hygiene - fine if you are a backpacker perhaps, but with two small children in tow this was a depressing and stressful end to a very tough day of travelling...with only the promise of the same horrible journey back down. 
Not worth it.

Title: This is the place to go! Do it!
Text:
I went to many attractions in Sri Lanka, but this was exceptional.

One of my top things to have done in Sri Lanka.

I got a tuktuk from the tea factory, and the ride up the mountain is great fun by itself, with plenty of photo opportunities of tea pickers and their homes. And when you reach the top, the view is stunning. I was told it can vary with mist and cloud, but it was fine the morning we were there (around 11am).

I rank this so highly, as it is accessible to anyone who can get in a tuktuk, the ride is an experience, and it is such a spectacular view at the top.

Title: Tough ride to the top
Text: You need to brave the long winding ride of about 8km up the tea slopes. If you manage to reach the top the views are stunning. Other than that there really isn't much else about this place. A bit ambivalent regarding whether it was really worth the effort. But all in all if you are near the Haputale area, I think you should consider giving this place a visit.

Title: Excellent views with incredible history!
Text:
On our trip to the Uva region, which we allocated about 2.5 days, Liptons Seat was one of the few things we had planned for and we are glad we did. 

Liptons Seat has tremendous views of the surrounding tea plantations. I recommend going early in the morning (7am to 10am) as thats when its most clear. We had a driver take us up as the walk is quite long (5.5km+). If a driver is not an option, a tuk tuk can take you up. 

Beyond the views, keep an eye out for the local plantation workers - a true indication of the regions culture and economic livelihood.

Title: Amazing
Text: After about one hour journey i reached to the place. At that time full of misty in afternoon. But after certain time i could see the view. It was very beautiful. Good place for nature lover.

Title: Stunning, a highlight of our trip, an absolute must!
Text: We had arranged to be picked-up at our hotel by tuktuk at 5.30 h in the morning, so that we could experience the sunrise at Lipton's Seat.  It's an approx. 29 kilometres tuktuk ride.  Truly spectacular up there.  It was so peaceful and quiet!   But do it early in the morning, as the daily clouds will start rolling-in later in the morning, blocking the fantastic mountain views from this hill top.  Tea and a snack can be served at the top.  It can be chilly early in the morning, dress well.  It's absolutely worth getting up for this early in the morning!!  Around the hill-top, just stroll down a bit along the road, amids the tea plantations.

Title: Best view over the tea plantations!
Text:
The best view over the tea plantations. You can take the care halfway up.Walk the rest or take a tuk-tuk (300 Rds). 
Be amazed by the magnificent views over the tea plantations. Views are even better than on Worlds End. And you can drive there. 
Enjoy the ride through the fields and take your time to soak in the views. 
It is the best view point we visited in Sri Lanka. You might feel like you are on top of the world.

Title: Fabulous views
Text: You can walk up to Liptons seat, but we took a tuktuk both ways and were glad we did seeing a number of very hot and bothered people struggling up the very steep hills!

Title: Great drive but no view!
Text: Great drive up to Lipton Seat through tea plantations and past tea factories. However it was very misty and damp at the top with no view at all. Also no toilet and a very basic 'cafe'. We waited two hours with no sign of the view appearing before returning to Haputale. Our only miss in an otherwise terrific trip to Sri Lanka.

Title: Go early
Text: Definitely worth a look. Fun Tuk Tuk ride up from the tea factory. Great photo opportunities on the way. Early is the best time but be prepared for mist at the top. It does break and the view is wonderful.

Title: Wonderful day trip activity
Text: We made an excursion to visit the tea plantation from Ella (train to Hapatule, bus to Dambutenne) - it's easy without a guide. Well-worth it, but advise you to leave early (for best chance at getting good view at top, and to miss the hot afternoon sun). We just made it to the top in time to get a decent view before the fog closed in, but we had to tuk-tuk up to the gate. Unless you're starting from Hapatule in the early morning I would recommend the tuk-tuk up and walk down (the walk down is plenty to take in the magnificent and tranquil scenery of the plantation - and the walk up could be tough in the heat unless reasonably fit). Highly recommended (even if you don't get good views at the top; the highlight is walking through the tea fields - the view at the seat is just a bonus). Remember to take small change (I think it was 100Rs each for entry at the gate) - we forgot to take enough to cover the tuk-tuk as well and had difficulty exchanging a 5000 note...

Title: Lipton's peak
Text:
The trip to Lipton's started with an inspection of the tea factory which was interesting. We then proceeded to Lipton's seat. 
We enjoyed the vista and then walked had way down the mountain!
We will fondly remember that trip!

Title: Beautiful walk up to the hill and great view
Text: "We took the local bus from Haputale to Dambatenne tea factory for 80 rupees but they can take you by bus straight to Lipton's seat. We walked from the factory 7 km up to the hill, the walk is beautiful, surrounded by small willages and tea plantations. Be aware that weather can change rapidly and be ready for a cloud burst. The view is amazing from the seat if not foggy. You can get a pot of tea in a kind of restaurant teher for 350 ruppes.

Title: Stunning views but go early!
Text: A beautiful place with incredible views across south Sri Lanka.  The view is best at sunrise, which is also the time where Lipton's Seat and the view is least likely to be covered in cloud. We started the walk at 5.30am and reached the top about 6.00am. Take something warm to wear. There is a cafe at the top that opens around this time, it serves great tea and fresh roti and other breakfast food. It's worth a visit for breakfast. They will keep bringing you food until you say stop!

Title: Beautiful walk!
Text: Perfect half day trip! Just go up by tuk tuk and then walk down approx. 8 kilometres down to the tea factory. Even if we were up at Lipton's Seat quite early, there were clouds, so no view... But nonetheless, it was worth to go there, since the scenery is beautiful and it is so nice to walk down through the tea plantation. Even our teenage kids liked it; not only the selfies with the Sir Lipton statue...!

Title: Wow!
Text: The view at this point is amazing!! It is really beautiful to walk back from this point in the direction of the Dambatenne Tea Factory (if this is too far for you, you can aks a tuk tuk driver to pick you up halfway).

Title: Amazing view of tea plantations on your way to the top
Text: Just going up to Lipton's seat will bring you through amazing green tea plantations. This itself is already definitely worth going up there. Going to Lipton's seat you need to get there early, as it will become misty in the afternoon. On top there is a small place where they provide you tea and some Sri Lankan snacks, which is quite nice. I don't know what they base the bill on, but expect to pay somewhere between 600 and 800 LKR.

Title: Need to be there very early
Text:
We went at Lipton's seat at 11 am ad it was already too late because the weather was cloudy. The entrance is 50 LKR p.p. + 100 LKR if you come with a tuktuk. 
Even with clouds, the landscape is amazing. In my opinion, the best tea plantations I saw in Sri Lanka.

Title: A must!
Text: Lipton's seat was amazing ! We climbed all the way up (about 2hrs walk), quite strenuous but completely worth it when you get to the top. The view is amazing (we went around sunset time) and the surroundings are pittoresque. This is definitely an unmissable walk

Title: Beware of shonky tuk tuk drivers!
Text: We, like most people went by a tuk tuk to Liptons Seat. The trouble was when we got to the entry gate where you pay for your ticket the tuk tuk driver let us out. We thought we were there but there was another 1 and a half km walk up steep hillside to get to the viewpoint. We had not been well and this was the last thing we needed. We met other people who had been cheated by tuk tuk drivers in the same way. By the time we got to the top the fog had closed in and there was no view. Others said it had been clear 10 mins earlier . This was at 8.30am so go early. The statue is of fibreglass, not bronze. The surrounding tea plantation scenery is worth the trip.

Title: Best at Sunrise
Text: You can arrange a tuk tuk at the city centre the day before to pick you up at your hotel the next morning for a ride up to Lipton's Seat to watch the sun rise. There will be others there but it was not too crowded.

Title: Great tour
Text:
Get a feeling for tea, by making this tour. 
I would recommend to go up by TukTuk and to walk back down.  I would recommend an early tour in order to avoid to see the mist. 
The area is sensitve to quickly changin weather conditions. 
Would also recommend to take the short cuts by walking straight downhill through the tea fields.

Title: Great view and great road to get there
Text:
I think the road to get there is almost as great as the view itself. Indeed, you will drive across many tea plantings and the road is impressive with some great views in between.
Once there you can enjoy the view if it is not fogy. I really recommend it, but you will need some time to drive there and so you should plan some hours to do this place.

Title: Outstanding view
Text: Outstanding panoramic view and great 2 hours walk back to the tea factory among the tea plantations with beautiful lively green colours and tamil women pickers.

Title: Charming, tranquil in the morning. Ideal selfie spot on the bench wit 'Sir' Lipton
Text:
I took a tuktuk as it is a really long and sometimes steep walk. Really enjoyable and tranquil trip...
I should even have gone earlier than the official sunrise... to get the most of the superb early morning light.
But... surprise, Sir Lipton is not made of bronze but of fiberglass, superbly painted with a nice patina ;-)
I hope he will be repaired soon as some *** broke off the famous cup of Lipton tea ;-(.

Up there a friendly team even offers a big SL breakfast, a pot of tea or hot food at nice prices. A small fee is asked to pass through the well kept Dambetenna tea plantations. Lots to see on the way - including everyday life of the Tamil tea pickers.

Title: Wonderful half- or whole- day trip
Text: Stunning drive through steep tea gardens to reach this stunning viewpoint, especially that to the South. Could be the objective of excellent hikes also.  Nice simple cafe nearby.

Title: Worth the walk
Text: Our group of four 50+ women decided to walk up to Liptons Seat from Dambatenne tea factory. Despite many tuk tuk drivers telling us it was very steep and far, we wanted to slowly take in the sights. It was a 2 hour walk up a gently winding road through glorious tea plantations. The views were sublime and we loved seeing the workers and tea pickers going through their daily tasks en route. Unfortunately it was clouded in at the top at Liptons seat. In hindsight we should have taken tuk tuk up to top early and then just walked down while still clear. But despite that we all loved this walk.

Title: Magnificent views
Text:
We visited all the landmarks placed under Mr. Thomas J. Liptons seat like Dambetenne tea planations and factory but this place makes it worth. We took a tuktuk from Ella and he was with us whole trip, stopped for pictures and waited everytime we went for a walk. With the way back it cost us 4200 Rp. 

The entry fee is 100 Rp. for a person and 50 Rp. fot a vehicle if you are lazy to walk up the hill ( as we were). The statue of Mr. Lipton is made from plastic but...you know...Sri Lanka style. Up there is a small cabin that offers a tea and breakfast (we arrived around 9:00 a.m.) but it lookd like its a gift. It is not.

Title: good view if you are lucky
Text: We weren't lucky.  You can allegedly see multiple provinces, we saw a wall of fog.  Our guide didn't tell us to get there early, so it was a long ride for nothing.  When you are driving around tea country in Sri Lanka you will see miles and miles of beautiful views and overlooks.  Not sure this is worth the time.

Title: Spectacular panoramic views
Text:
Liptons Seat is the famous viewpoint where Sir Thomas Lipton used to sit and contemplate his plantation with its stony landscape and green tea bushes. Located in misty Haputale, on your way to Dambethenna Estate. 

Once you are at the summit, to say the view is spectacular would be an understatement. The climb is worth it, just for this.

How to get here

Take the signed narrow paved road from the Dambetenna tea factory and climb about 7km through lush tea plantations to the lookout. From the tea factory, the ascent should take about 2½ hours. The earliest bus leaves Haputale at 6.30am. You will enjoy the talk with tea pluckers going off to work as you walk uphill to Liptons Seat.

Alternatively, you can hire a tuk-tuk from the viewpoint too. but recommend the walk to get the full use of your journey.

Title: Chilly weather and fantastic views!
Text:
Our driver got us a tuk tuk to take us up to the attraction. Unfortunately when we reached up it was too misty to see anything. We were a group of 3 tamil speaking girls and we got a very warm welcome from the local tamilians there which was very heartwarming. 

Although we couldnt see the 5 states, the views and misty fresh air up there was worth the visit.

Title: Fantastic biews
Text: Fantastic views make sure you are there for sunrise. We paid a tuk tuk driver to take us there and back, to home yourself would take a long time

Title: Nice place.
Text: Can see 5 provinces in Sri Lanka. The place could be covered from mist. So better get locals advice. We could not see much. Heard we should come in the morning before 8 am or after 4pm.

Title: Fantastic view
Text:
We could see panoramic views all around.  The day we went was cloudy.  Because of that we couldn't see all the way to the southern coastline.  But according to people who live around there a person can see the southern coast.  

Walking up to the observation point from the gate was a good exercise and it was pleasant walk because the road was between tea grown areas.

Title: What a Beauty
Text: The most beautiful destination to visit in Sri Lanka. You'll just to view the amazing beauty of the tea plantation on the way to Lipton's Seat. How picturesque can be any destination from 1970 meter above the sea level! You must got to visit and see.

Title: Lovely Walk
Text:
Took the 6.40 AM train out of Ella and was in Haputhale about an hour later. Took a tuk tuk from the train station for Rs 1000. Dropped off at the entrance where we paid Rs 50 and walked the rest of the way up to Liptons Seat. Wasn't very misty so the view was pretty great. 

We then walked back down all the way to the Dambethenne Tea Factory. My parents, who are in their early 70s had no issues with this walk down. On the way we bumped into a young family and made our way back with them. We took our time to savor the views, take pictures and talk to the plantation workers as we weaved down.

Title: Great walk and view
Text: You can get a car to the top but we walked from the tea factory up through the tea plantations to the Liptons seat.  It is 3hr return but well worth it for the views on the way and the friendly locals who live on the hills.  Take plenty of water although there is a shop at the top to restock. The route is easy and you don't need a guide.  Our kids of 11 and 13 were easily able to make the walk.

Title: Lipton has a pretty spectacular seat!
Text: Apparently you can see 5 provinces from the same spot. Perched high above spectacular tea gardens overlooking patchwork valleys and mountains is Lipton's Seat and didn't Sir Thomas Lipton have the best view. The road is narrow, winding around the hills with too many hairpin turns to count but without a doubt it is worth the drive. It is 100 rupees per car plus 50 rupees per person weather you drive or walk to the summit. Get some beautiful panoramic photographs plus some selfies with Sir Thomas Lipton's statue likeness. There is a small cafe serving tea and Sri Lankan treats which is affordable and the staff are friendly. Highly highly recommend.

Title: Absolutely amazing views!
Text:
Worth making the trip to Haputale just to do Liptons Seat! We stayed at a guesthouse in Haputale and got a tuk tuk at 6am to the Dambatenne tea factory (700 rupees around 30min journey). From there we followed the winding road up to liptons seat. It's a very easy 7km walk up and I would definitely recommend walking rather than getting a tuk tuk to the top if you have time! A tuk tuk straight to the top costs around 1000rupees apparently. 
For the way up we followed the gentle winding road but on the way down we took the steeper routes straight down the tea plantation which is definitely faster (would make for a very strenuous hike up hill though). It's a 50 rupees entrance fee to enter the last part of the walk to get to liptons seat. 
The views through the tea plantation are absolutely stunning, we were lucky to go on a sunny day. It took us about an hour and a half to get to the top and we stopped for a cup of tea, there's a hut selling tea and rottis with lots of local Sri Lankan guys trying to get you to eat there. Views at the top are also amazing but make sure to get there early as the fog rolls in mid morning. 
The way down is pretty fast if you take the steps down the tea plantation (you'll see them on the side of the road). 
We went to the tea factory for a tour then got the local bus back to Haputale and were back in town by around 11:30am.

Title: Breathtaking views
Text: Whether you walk the 7.5km uphill or get a tuk tuk the views are incredible.  Many sure you arrive early and stay and grab some rotti at the top.  Walking back down through the plantations is truly stunning.

Title: Incredible place
Text: Amazing way from Dambatene to Lipton Seat between tea plant with workers like from 19th century. Unbelievable. On the top is small lovely restaurant  with tea and simple Sri Lanka food. The biggest experince in Sri Lanka.

Title: Swathed in mist
Text:
The trip up is by Tuk-tuk but a few hardy souls walked through the tea plantation to get there and saved themselves the fare (3000R). We were forewarned on the day that we visited that we would be lucky to get a good view from the toil and sure enough it was swathed in low cloud when we arrived with only the briefest glimpse throughout the cloud after about 40 minutes. 
Local Macaques abound and raid the bins of a nearby refreshment shop, which also supplies tasty curry at not-too-exorbitant prices, given the transporting costs!  
A bronze statue of Sir Thomas Lipton on a board seat invites you to be photo'd there.
Despite the briefest glimpse through the mist, it was worth seeing.

Title: Amazing
Text: This turned out to be a much better site than we expected.  We were amazed at the beauty of the area with the vista from the top of the valleys and the surrounding tea plantations.  Early morning is the best time to visit.  We were there by 8am, and the clouds moved in and obscured the view about 8:45am.  The little cafe at the site is OK, but not great.  We recommend taking a tuk tuk to the top (beautiful ride) and walking down, taking a few shortcuts through the tea fields on established paths.

Title: Amazing view
Text: This must be at your to do list in central Srilanka. Amazing view. We take tuk tuk from Haputale to the top for 1000 R. On the top is nice tea shop and you can enjoy cup of tea and the view.

Title: Nice hike with great view!
Text: We loved hiking through the tea fields! When you reach the top, you'll be at Lipton's seat. There's a small tea house where you can sit, have a tea and enjoy the view. View was awesome, the tea was the worst tea of whole Sri Lanka!! But it was a funny experience.

Title: Great 360 degrees view
Text:
Incredible views over the plantations and several mountain ranges all around you. Breathtaking, but be sure to be there before 10am before the fog hits the peaks and visibility decreases or becomes non-existent ;) The way up and the scenery is definitely worth setting your alarm clock. The Dambatenne tea plantation is very well-kept and beautiful, and it's worth taking shortcuts through it and walk around (as opposed to only driving up and down).
There are many ways you can reach the Lipton Seat panorama, from Haputale : bus to dambatenne tea factory (about 10km) + another small bus or tuktuk to the lipton seat gate (or hike but mind the heat) (about 5km) + uphill hike or tuktuk to the top (1 km). At the Haputale tuktuk stand, drivers will be happy to negociate a cheap fee up to the very top, as there are few tourists.
There is a small entrance fee (50 rps ?) at the Lipton Seat gate (1km from the top) (+vehicle fee so you might also want to ride a tuktuk to that point and walk up)

Title: Spectacular!
Text: It took us along time by scooter to find this. We travelled from Ella! Worth it in the end! It was very misty up there and the views all the way up by scooter were incredible!

Title: Great walk through tea plantation
Text: We were based in Ella and decided to get the train to Haputale (roughly 1 hour)  then a tuk tuk up to the Dambetenne tea factory. From there it is a lovely 7.5km walk up the road to Lipton's seat. The route winds through the tea fields and the little districts where the workers live and every person greets you with a friendly smile and a wave. It took us about 1.5hr to get to the top at a leisurely pace and were met with some incredible views. We had to pay 50lkr each to proceed to the top and it looked like any vehicles required 100lkr. We then decided to walk all the way back to Haputale which was about 9-10km from the tea factory. This walk is not too arduous as it's fairly flat but can be tiring in the afternoon sun. NOTE: There are a lot of local kids on the way to Liptons seat and walk to Haputale who ask for the obligatory sweet/cookie etc.but also ask for school pens. Unfortunately we did not have a single pen between us but I'd recommend stocking up before visiting so you can become the local hero!

Title: Amidst the clouds
Text: A short ride into the hills and the Lipton Tea plantation surrounds you. This place can be either reached by a quick hike or a tuk tuk ride. There is a small toll fee to be paid but its totally worth it. You get a chance to jump between the tea shrubs.

Title: Hike, don't tuk-tuk
Text: You can easily hike from the Dambatenne Tea Factory to the top and back (it's two hours to the top and hour and a half back). On your beautiful, refreshing and not-at-all demanding way up, you'll be passed by old people in tuk-tuks (understandable), handicapped people in tuk-tuks (also understandable) and able-bodied lazy loosers in tuk-tuks (not understandable at all). Please, make fun of them. Also, hike. The view is much more rewarding if you walked it up. On the top, you can get some food, water and tea as well (the tea on Lipton's Seat is highly recommended and it costs only 200 rupees for the whole pot!). Entrance fee is 50 rupees for foreign visitors.

Title: Spectacular View
Text: It's worth watching this spectacular view. Nice drive through tea plantations. Shouldn't miss this wonderful place.

Title: Worth the trek
Text: Even though we had some fog, the trek up here was totally worthwhile.  Take the tuk-tuk - too far to walk.  Beautiful tea gardens and hills, and view from the top is exceptional.  Early in the day is best.

Title: Focal Point of Sri Lanka
Text:
On a clear day, you can see 5 provinces and 2 seas. Just thinking of that can be baffling, and I'm certain it'll be an awe-inspiring and humbling experience.
If the day is misty, then you won't see much but it's still a magical, mystical experience to be amongst the clouds.

If you do choose to come here, you can avoid staying in Haputale as there isn't no much to do there. Also, you can go up to Lipton's Seat by van, tuk-tuk, or spend quite a bit of time climbing up and down.

Title: A must see if you're in Haputale
Text: We highly recommend a tuk tuk ride early in the morning to reach the Lipton seat. The view is dramatic and the hike downhill is unforgettable.

Title: Great lookout on a clear day
Text: Bit of a drive to get there, but really great lookout across the whole area on a clear day. Beware of foggy weather though. A lot of beautiful tea plantations on the way.

Title: Great viewpoint!
Text: If you are lucky with a sunny day, this is an excellent place for stunning photos of this beautiful countryside and the smiling ladies picking tea in the hills below!

Title: Must Do
Text: Instead of hiking we were driven up, first in a car and the last stretch in a tuk tuk. The views were breathtakingly beautiful along the way too. We made a stop at the tea leaves weighing station. It was on their first working day of the year, it felt very festive and all the tea pickers were chatty and happy. Quite an experience to see the mass quantity of rice and curry being prepared.

Title: Great views on d way and from d top.
Text:
We went there by scouter. Don't be discouraged by clouds- they come and go making the trip even more picturesque. 
On d way I see local people, children, tea plantation workers. Very nice day exploring local area.

Title: Incredible view. ....!!!!
Text: It's important land mark in haputale. good observation point. around 15-17km from haputhale drive to the top. good experience drive to top on small road. we are very lucky sunny day.spot up to hambantota sea.you can see all the provinces of sri lanka. I think it's belong to dabethenna tea factory. i can imagine how enjoy mr.thomas lipton in the evening with this amazing view.

Title: A beautiful site
Text: A very touristic place but, nonetheless a beautiful view over the tea plantations.  A nice climb to arrive to the Seat

Title: Tips for Tourists
Text: If you are on a vehicle with a reasonable ground clearance you can drive to the place by yourself. A Normal car with 14", 15" rim size wheels will do. There are lot of Tuktuk drivers in Haputale Rail station, but they may charge ~1500LKR for the trip. Negotiate the price BEFORE YOU GET IN. Another good choice is you can drive up to the tea factory (Dambetenna Tea factory), visit the factory, leave the car there, and take a tuk-tuk to the Lipton's Seat. Don't forget two things; first, go early, earlier the better; second stop at local vegetable selling places go to their back yard with them; you can pick up vegetables by yourself, amazing experience !!!

Title: Stunning View
Text: We opted to go to Lipton's Seat over World's End as it was on our way to Ella and that it is significantly cheaperl. We got into Haputale late, got up early and took a tuk tuk in the morning to Lipton's Seat. If you get dropped off at the gate it's about a 1.2 km walk with a beautiful view. If you walk from the tea factory at the base it's about 7-9km. The entrance fee is 100lkr per person.

Title: Enjoyable walk in lush green
Text: It's the best to get there before 7am by a threewheeler. The view on top is great but what's better is the walk downhill. There are tea plantations all over the mountain, and everywhere looks like a painting. You could see workers going to work and picking tea leaves starting around 9am. Finish off the walk with a visit to the tea factory and learn about how tea leaves are made.

Title: Seat's that close to heaven
Text: A 360 view of a hill top Lipton seat was the worlds famous historical place located in dambatene, a place that every foreign people must visit.  A few steps to heaven that how tired you may walk to reach it, it's a stress reliever and pain relief once you reach the top.  Fresh air,  Amazing view,  feels like you are in heaven.  Just a reminder before going,  just bring enough water and food as there's no foreign food available once you reach on the top

Title: Must see??
Text: This I such a beautiful hike, especially with the sunset! It' s best to leave at 4.45 (yes I know, very early...but so worth it!) a tuktuk Will cost you around 1000r to be there in time. You Will walk your way back through the theeplantations until you reachbthe Lipton teafactory, wich is deffinately worth a visit (250r) as well! From there you can take a bus of tuktuk back to Haputale.

Title: Stunning Views
Text: As there were 4 of us we took a pair of tuk tuks from our guest house to the top of Lipton's Seat which is about 5,000 feet in elevation. The road wound its way up and up through the tea plantations round countless hairpin bends (not dangerous) before reaching the entrance gate where there is a small entrance fee to be paid. The views from the top are almost 360 degrees and are stunning. We were possibly lucky with the weather as it was a cloudless deep blue sky and we could see for miles in all directions.The vivid green of the tea plantations set against the sky was very photogenic......lots of photos to be taken here!! At the top there is a fine statue of Mr Lipton himself and a small cafe where we sat and enjoyed the views. The air was cooler here and although it was hot when we were there I can imagine on a cloudier day it could be pretty chilly! Instead of taking the tuk tuk back down we decided to walk back down through the tea plantations. This was superb, we took it at a leisurely pace and just enjoyed the scenery, the friendliness of the locals particularly the smiling schoolchildren who make their way up and down this steep hill every day! We walked as far as the Dambatenne Tea Factory and then took a tuk tuk back to town from there. This was yet another highlight of our trip and one i highly recommend.....away from the crowds too!

Title: Magnificent Views
Text: Beautiful views from the top of the hill. The scenery getting there is through tea estate, with tea pluckers and workers going about their jobs.

Title: Wake up early to be there early
Text: It is worth the stress to put an alarm clock even on holiday. But when you will be there, almost yourself, looking at the hills pointed out by the trees...you will understand. The walk can be long, so if you are not really willing to enjoy also the trekking to reach the seat, book a tuk tuk or rent a scooter.

Title: Superb View
Text: Visit with my friends. Must visit place where you can see three provinces together. cool climate. loved very much. Its better to go by your own feet. i did it. amazing experience.

Title: View from above
Text:
The Lipton Seat hillstop is like any other viewpoint in Sri Lanka. You can see 5 diatricts from above and the view is beautiful.  

The tea plantations etched beautifully across the mountain side is just gorgeous. 

We took a car up and it was slightly difficult as the road was rather narrow. But if you are willing to pay a Tuk Tuk driver about 1000 rupees, he will take you there and back. It will be a unique experience indeed.

Title: Fantastic morning. Amazing views. Loved it!
Text:
Left Haputale around 4.30am. Took about an hour for the winding drive to the start of the walk up to Liptons Seat. The walk itself is uphill on good paths/roads, took about 2 hrs to reach Liptons seat, it's a lovely walk, thoroughly recommend it. Arrived just after sunrise, should of left Haputale a bit earlier, say 4am. Rewarded with truly stunning views, would do it again for sure. There is a small place at the top where you can get a cuppa tea and a rotti - absolutely lovely and with that view - a breakfast to remember!

You can of course drive all the way to the top and then walk down, this should guarantee you sunrise and you get the beautiful views on walk down. I walked up and down as I had the time. I would definitely walk up or down as it's just beautiful through the tea plantations. 

A fantastic way to spend the morning! Can finish off at the tea factory when you come down.

Title: Stunning views
Text: Long way up, but worth it. Stunning views all the way to the top. We took a Tuk Tuk which was a good decision. The road is narrow and not really suitable for anything bigger. Some people walked, but it's a long way.

Title: Srilanka-Maldives Tour!
Text: One of the best hiking point through tea planted mountains. It's good to be there early in the morning to capture sun rise scene. Point is very good for those who loves photography. Pleasant views all around at top.

Title: Very nice place and walk over to Worlds End
Text:
Make sure to get there early and arrive before the fog sets in. We drove in from Haputale which is a one and a half hour drive. Leave at least at 4.45 h. 
It's a 3-4 hours walk and if you want to move on afterwards to Ella for example, you can take your luggage and ask to be dropped at the nearest train station. (in between Nuwara Eliya and Haputale.
Take breakfast with you and enjoy it at World's End.
You don't have to pay for toilets on arrival, although a guy will certainly try you for it :)
Don't leave youre garbage in the park!!!

Title: Nice long walk but it's likely to be cloudy at the view
Text: The walk through the plan at ions is nice enough but we found the best view was actually off the beaten track pretty early in the walk.  From liptons seat it was too misty to see anything and it seems this is common. Perhaps arriving very early morning would have been worthwhile (we arrived around 10.30am).

Title: Great walk down
Text: The view was obscured by cloud, but the walk back to the tea factory through the plantations is scenic and a fascinaing insight into the area.

Title: The views are stunning, even more is the way.
Text: The views from the seat are beautiful, great valley under, and beautiful tea plantations. I'd advice to go up with a tuk-tuk and take the 5 km road down. Walking through the plantation, some local villages, see the tea pickers at their work, and enjoy the changing scenery

Title: Magical
Text: Magical views, the way there is also stunning. Go from Haputale by small bus to Dambetenne factory, from there by tuk tuk to the top of Liptons seat. Get a breakfast there (there is a small place up there which serves tea and some rotti) and make your way back down.

Title: A must see around Haputhale
Text:
If you only have limited time here, this is The  place to go.
Reach the top of the hill before 10am as it is said that the stunning view is quickly obstructed by clouds coming up from the valley.
You can reach the top of the hill (and actually the Seat itself) by car or tuk-yuk, but one should enjoy walking at least from the gate (less than 2 km).
Also, walking down across tea fields is a must.

Title: Must go
Text: Nice view especially in the morning.  Serene and refreshing tea plantations all under your eyes.  Treat yourself a nice morning here.

Title: Fantastic walk
Text: Fascinating walk up through the village, past the tea-pickers, and up to the top of the hill where the views are stunning. I implore you to walk - it's uphill but not strenuous. If you take a tuk-tuk you will breeze past fantastic photo opportunities, and miss any interaction with the lovely children and workers! Easy to get to the tea factory by bus from Haputale.

Title: Marvelous view
Text:
It is a steep and curvy road up to Lipton's seat.
But it is worth it. You travel through hundreds of tea fields, enjoying all shades of green. And when You reach the top, the view is marvelous.
But it is a pity that Mr. Lipton lost his tea cup :(

Title: walk to Liptons seat
Text: i'd recommend tuktuk up and walking back down. Don't be afraid of the shortcuts through the tea flields that the tea workers use as they cut out a lot of switchbacks on the road.

Title: Stunning View
Text:
Liptons Seat is a must see if you are in Sri Lanka we took the train from Ella back to Happatale. We left early around 7 or 8 am and boarded the train when we arrived at the station we were, as usual in southeast Asia, hit upon by the local rickshaw cartel. I never really see this as a bad thing it's just business. Like any other business it has pros and cons. They will always go ridiculously expensive you go RIDICULOUSLY cheap and meat somewhere closer to ridiculously cheap side of things rememember to walk away and convict to your walk aim at a shop say your gonna go for a coffee you've changed your mind completely etc etc. Unless of course you are not on a budget then you have the option of taking a tough job and making it a little easier for them. Rickshaw can take you right to the entrance gate of Liptons seat which will require another 15/20 min walk up hill. Or you could get left off at the tea factory below and walk 1-1/2 or 2 hours depending on your fitness. We went straight to the gate and walked back it was a glorious walk go early so hits nice and sunny and clear. The views at the top and the walk back down are just fantastic

Title: Great Views
Text: Great spot to see sunrise. Nice, leisurely walk down the paved road through the tea plantation and village with vegetable gardens and on to the tea factory. Some people use the tea picker paths as shortcuts down the mountain.

Title: Amazing heeling point. No needs any words.
Text:
Amazing beautiful point, have to go there. It's not just top of the mountain, there is more than something, feeling. 
We took the tuktuk from the station to here.(return 1400rs) this nice driver stopped several times for take photos.

Title: Amazing view of tea plantation
Text: Lipton's seat is definitely one of the must visit places in Sri Lanka. Recommended to reach there before 6am in order to catch the sunrise. Along the way to Lipton's seat, we were surrounded by tea plantations and the view is stunning.
