Title: Amazing view and a nice cup of tea
Text: An amazing view and well worth the walk from the gate. I wouldn't start climbing up from the tea factory unless it's a cool day. However, did walk all the way back down to the factory. Lovely walk and the tea pickers are just so kind. There is a very funky little tea hut at the top and it's well worth having a cup and chatting with the host, narayanan.

Title: The views are BEA-utiful.
Text: I'm up early, eat breakfast at hotel & off to Lipton's Seat. I take a local bus UPHILL  to Dambatenne Tea Factory (RS 30). It takes 30. It's 9 kms. On the spur of the moment I take a tuk-tuk (RS 500) UPHILL to Lipton's Seat. I don't bargain, first he says RS 600 but I say too much, then he says RS 500 & I go okay. It's 7-8 kms & takes 20. I'm glad I did that. It is foggy & blusterous up there. I stay a few minutes and saunter & mosey DOWNHILL back to Dambatenne Tea Factory. That takes 3+ hours. It's splendiferous scenery. I take tooooooooooo many pictures (Sorry) but the views are BEA-utiful.

Title: Enjoy the Journey (as well as the view)
Text:
While it's recommended to go early in the morning for clear views, we decided to take a more leisurely trip later.  We took a tuk tuk from Haputale to the Dambatenne Tea Factory and walked the road and some shorts cuts to the top - Lipton's seat.

We much enjoyed the views on the way and seeing the tea pickers at work.  I received many looks of amusement and perhaps disapproval on account of my walking sticks and hiking boots, which surely seemed way over the top, but I also exchanged a good number of smiles.

When we reached the top at least half of the view was covered in mist, but we really didn't mind.  It was the journey for us that mattered more than the "prize".  And, the restaurant at the top had surprisingly good food and perhaps the best tea I tasted on our entire trip.

We walked back down to the tea factory and were lucky enough to catch a local bus back to Haputale which was a super fun experience -- devotional tchotchkes on the dashboard and popular Hindi music playing all the way for a cheap price.  

Definitely worth the visit.

Title: An enjoyable walk in the tea plantations
Text: Count 1h20 to go up and 45 min to go down. Beautiful walk in the middle of the tea plantations. View there is amazing. Try to get there early in the morning as the clouds go up at around 9:30-10am.

Title: The early bird catches the worm ... in this case the view weather permitting!
Text:
We visited Lipton's Seat while staying at Haputale. The advice was to get a taxi to drop us off at the top, walk the 7 kilometres downhill through the tea plantations and catch a bus back to Haputale from Dambatenne which we duly did; we were not disappointed. 

We got to the top by 06.00 which was plenty of time to settle down and wait for the sun to rise. At that time of the morning, and at that height, it gets pretty cold so I definitely recommend a fleece and windproof. The views are stunning but of course are totally dependant on the weather. We were lucky and had great 360 degree panoramic views; absolutely stunning and an experience that will stay with us forever.

At the top you can get hot tea and roti freshly cooked over a wood fire which was very welcome after our early morning start.

The walk downhill (I note some reviewers walked up as well as down - I consider myself to be a strong walker and I wouldn't have liked to have done that so hats off to them!) is equally enjoyable. The incredible views of the summit are gradually replaced by rolling tea plantations and tea planters villages until finally the tea factory at Dambatenna comes into view.

All in all a wonderful experience although, of course, totally dependant on the weather. Here's wishing you good luck on the weather front when you get the chance to visit Lipton's Seat.

Title: A morning walk
Text: We parked at Dambattene tea factory and walked up to Liptons Seat and back down. The return trip took us about 3 hours and was well worth the effort. It is recommended that you get to the top before 11am as after this time the mist increases and the views are not as good. On the way up and down you don't have to follow the road put can use the paths through the tea plantations as short cuts.

Title: Great views of mist
Text: A perilous journey that our hotel driver handled safely and well. Stunning scenery. Well with the trip.

Title: Go in the morning
Text: Be careful of the local taxi-drivers who know that they have you by the short & curlies. It is worth persevering, get a good price and get a lift up to Lipton's seat and then you can walk down to the Tea Factory and they will pick you up from there. It is a brilliant walk and all downhill. Make sure you are down by midday though as it starts to get misty and the views become limited and it seems that you are walking over the Yorkshire Moors and not the Sri Lankan Uplands.

Title: stunning view
Text: since rainy before so that not so many people at there when i reached lipton's seat around 9am something. weather was varied every moment but i got stunning view finally.

Title: The views are worth the effort!
Text: We considered walking but opted for a tuk tuk ride which I would seriously recommend.  It's a big hike otherwise but the views are spectacular and you can't help but wonder about Thomas and his royal parties in that spot a hundred years ago.  Sunrise is a great time to visit, you'll get some awesome photographs.

Title: Wonderful view
Text: We took the easy way up but many walk up or down or both - a great way to meet the locals in the tea plantations. It is quite a climb even in a car but the views are well worth it and it was not crowded at the top despite the numbers seen making their way up and down.

Title: Amazing views over tea plantations all the way to Udawalawe National Park.
Text: Interesting drive and then walk through an active tea plantation to the spot were Thomas Lipton came on a regular basis to commune with nature and survey his plantation.  Great views.  Can be combined with a visit to the original Lipton Tea Factory, still in operation and producing tea much as it would have been done decades ago.

Title: Breathtaking experience
Text: This place literally took my breath away. Definitely one of the most gorgeous places of Sri Lanka. We got there by tuk-tuk from Haputale (for 1000lkr). It is approx. 45 minutes ascend by serpentine in tea plantations to height of 2200m. Whole route is jaw-dropping. Our driver stopped several times for us to let us enjoy various views. On the very top there is a platform from where 360 degree panoramic view opens in front of you and you can watch countless plantation hills disappearing in clouds below you and if weather is opportune you can even see ocean in the distance. We arrived in the afternoon and due to locals we were very lucky about weather conditions that day, cause usually people visit in the early morning to have the best visibility possible. I would recommend to do so, apparently it is not unusual thing to not be able to see further than 10 meters around you. Only thing apart from platform on top is small restaurant that will offer you one type of food that they made that day and delicious fresh local tea. There is some small fee for entering the seat, the experience is unforgettable and priceless though. This place is a must see!

Title: Great Views But Nothing Unique If You've Seen Other Tea Plantations
Text:
Main Tip: If you've been to tea plantations in Nuwara Eliya you can skip Lipton's Seat. If not, I would make the trek out to visit. 

It was about a 1.5 hour tuk tuk ride from Ella on some scary roads once you get closer to Lipton's Seat. If you have a fear of heights - this is not the drive for you. I'd highly recommend taking a tuk tuk over a car if you can, the roads are extremely narrow  and I saw multiple cars have a difficult time getting through. If you are self-driving (as we were) I would absolutely discourage self-driving here because there is very little room for error. You can also take a bus to Liptons Seat (get off at Haputale) and take a tuk tuk from there.

The view from the top by Lipton's statue is pretty and shows off tea plantations in every direction. You can either walk back down to the entrance (about 8km) to catch the bus or meet your ride or simply ride back in your tuk tuk once you are done looking around. There are places along the way (walking or riding) where you can look around and wander a bit through the rows of tea plants.

Go early - the fog/mist rolled in around 9:30 am and I was told it can get bad enough later in the day that driving is difficult. Given those roads that is not a risk I'd ever want to take! Also people often take pictures of the tea ladies working but remember - they are paid the equivalent of less than $3 usd a day and they are not animals in a zoo who are performing for your entertainment.

Title: Budget trip from Ella
Text:
We were based in Ella and having read a few reviews about going to liptons seat we decided we would try and do it as cheap as possible and here's what we did. Below prices are 1 person.

First train from Ella to Haputale (6.40am) -  60Rp 

Local bus from Haputale to Dambatenne (5mins walk from station) - 32Rp

We ate at a local "Hotel" 
Dahl curry, rotti, sweet tea 100Rp

Entrance fee into Liptons seat - 100Rp

Tea at the top - 50 rp

Toilets at the tea factory 20Rp

Dambatenne to Haputale - 32Rp

Haputale - Ella train 60Rp

We then did the hike from the bottom to liptons seat you can get the tuk tuk and saw lots of people doing this. I would defiantley reccomend doing the hike if you've got time it took us about 2 hrs up and 90 mins down. It made the views so much worth it!
We got up there just before 11am a little bit misty but still had some clear breaks to take in the amazing views.

We arrvived back in Ella around 4pm as we had just missed the 12.30pm train back to Ella and waited for the 14.15pm train. You can also do a tour of tea factory but we skipped this.

So all in all the cost of the day excursion was 352rp per person. Pretty good I thought for about £1.50.

Title: One of the best experience in Sri Lanka
Text:
This one made our trip! We came to Haputale by train from Ella before 10 am and took a tuk-tuk (I believe 1000 LKR one way) all the way up to Lipton´s Seat. It took about 45 minutes so it was already almost 11 am but still the sceneries were beautiful. Some mist tossing about but still with good views. Take a sit in a small restaurant up there with only 4-5 tables and enjoy simple but delicious tea and roti.
There were about 20-30 people up there strolling around at our arrival which absolutely didn´t make it crowdy and as we started our descent by walk, we left all the people up there and remained all alone on our way down. Sometimes we cut through tea fields and we also passed through a unique village observing their local Hindu ceremony for a while. Incredible experience!
At Dambatenna factory we took a tuk-tuk for, I believe, 800 LKR (they didn´t want to bargain at all) for Haputale but we could have easily taken a bus from there as well which, unfortunately, wasn´t a preffered way of travelling to Haputale for the rest of our group.

Title: Shame it was cloudy
Text: Long way up. Nice sights. No long distance scenery due to clouds. And now I add words to make up to 100 character as specified by Trip Advisor

Title: The walk from the seat was awesome.
Text: The top is mediocre at best. But the walk down from the seat was amazing. We walked until the thee factory. Taking most short cuts along the way. Good walk, just becarefull of some wildlife.

Title: Amazing and serene view
Text: It's an incredible place with an amazing view. Take a tuk-tuk to Lipton's seat and enjoy different tea plantation and villages along the way.

Title: Most scenic and serene view with clouds passing by and gazing over lush green tea estates !
Text:
In the small tea town of Haputale, this point was simply worth all the pain ( waking up early and catching first train from Ella), reason being after 11/12 in the morning it becomes too cloudy and misty and you don't get to witness the amazing view. So, better to reach here around 8-9 to have best of the experience. About 15 km from Haputale  railway station, we took a tuk/tuk for 1000 LKR (round trip) - bargain . In between, you can have a tea factory tour as well. One out of three tea factories on the way, lets you experience the tea factory process. There is local bus service as well which drops you till tea factory, but from there also you will have to take tuk-tuk, if not you can be up for a uphill hike as well of about 7-8 km.
Trust me, this is not a place to skip during your Sri Lanka trip !

Title: If you only do one thing in Hill Country do this
Text: Incredible place with some of the best views in Sri Lanka. Get up early and take a tuk-tuk to Lipton's seat then walk down to the tea factory afterwards.

Title: Amazing viewpoint
Text: 360 Views across hills, tea plantations and a good walk down to the tea factory below. There is a little cafe right at the top serving team and pastries. Well worth the climb (or drive up).

Title: Astonishing scenery
Text: If you're wondering whether the rather long (1 hour) scooter drive from Ella to Lipton's Seat is worth it: it totally is! It's one of those things where the ride is even more beautiful than the destination. Driving by acres of tea plantations actively being worked gives amazing scenery, and along the way there's a tea factory you van visit with a guide for a cheap price (thinking about 200 Rs p.p.). Tip: don't go on a Monday, as the factory isn't operational then (no harvest on Sundays). You can still visit the factory though.

Title: Go for sunrise!
Text: We took a tuk tuk one way to get up to Lipton's Seat for sunrise - we were not disappointed with the early morning rise! We had the whole place to ourselves and it was magical watching the sun rise over the tea plantations. Be sure to pack some decent warmies as it was very chilly and windy. We had a fantastic, warming breakfast up at the cafe overlooking what Sir Lipton would've back in the day. With full bellies, we walked down to Dambutene Tea Factory which was a nice gentle stroll down and through the tea fields in the rain ?? (approx. 1.5 - 2 hours down).

Title: Nice view we didn't see :)
Text: We arrived on the Lipton's Seat after lunch, which was too late and the view was already covered in clouds. However, we were able to admire the view on the other side - on the tea plantation, which was absolutely worth it too.

Title: Sunrise
Text: The view from Liptons seat really is impressive. We decided to hire a driver to take us there from the center of Haputale as i suffer from vertigo and was unsure id make the climb. Most of the road is through the tea plantations although certain parts are a little on the edge, however travelling before dawn meant i couldn't see the drops! The top is really safe and there is even a small cafe although we didn't go in. We then walked back down through the tea  plantation which is a real pleasure.

Title: 360 view
Text: Amazing place and if you go there you may see 6 Districts if there is no fog. Try to go there early morning and amazing weather climate as well. If you take tuk tuk from Haputhale Railway station just 1200LKR with return. Don't forget to have a tea with pol Roti for that place shop and kind peoples.

Title: Great view and interesting history
Text:
We went a bit further up the hills to visit Lipton's seat after seeing the Dembele tea factory.

There is a lovely collection of chairs and tables where you can buy snacks and tea. 

The view is well worth climbing the steep hills to reach.

Title: The way there is as beautiful as the top
Text: We rented a little scooter and made our way up in the morning. The view along the way is absolutely stunning and peaceful. At the top you can have a cup of tea and snacks watching an amazing view. Also you can visit a tea factory on the way down. Absolutely worth the visit! My girlfriend and I actually went there again on our way back to Colombo, just a few days after!

Title: View None Can Beat
Text:
The only location in Sri Lanka where 5 Provinces can be seen. On a clear day, the sea is visible from the Hambantota side and the Mattala Airport. Also on another day Adams peak is visible.
Place founded by Charles Lipton. Now it is been ran by a plantation company. Roads leading up to the place is narrow. A 4x4 ideal however having a small vehicle is also fine.
A place which is a must see. Go ask for Narayan, a good character with local knowledge

Title: Unique views
Text:
We were staying at White Monkey - Dias rest, around 12km from lipton's seat (4km out from Haputale town). Some of the other guests advised we take a tuktuk or a car up to Lipton's seat, as the walk would be too long and strenuous. However, we had our hearts set on the walk - the pivotal reason we were visiting Haputale - and so decided to hike up the next morning anyway.

We left the guesthouse around 6am and had a beautiful two and a half hour hike to Lipton's seat. We passed a small lake, walked through cloud forest and past lush tea plantations. There are signs along the way with words of wisdom about environmental issues and protecting the planet as well as a count down towards lipton's seat. The views going up were different to any that we have ever encountered and it has been our favourite hike in Sri Lanka so far.

The walk can be strenuous at times, but it is mainly a gradual incline on a good path with plenty of places to rest or get snacks or water.

At the top we were greeted with tea, toffee, rotti and corn cakes: so delicious and just what we fancied after the hike. The views are stunning, however the mist and clouds surround the view point from around 8:30am onwards, so try aim to be there before. At the top you can get a tuktuk back down, or walk to the tea factory where there are plenty more tuktuks willing to take you back into town.

Title: Interesting tour of plantation
Text:
get a tuck tuck to drive you up to the top of the hill where lucky ones will see breathtaking views of the estate. If fog is surrounding just get a tea and enjoy the warmth of the cup. Walk back to the estate if weather allows it.
Tour of factory is basic but nice anyway.

Title: A must for a visit when you are in SriLanka
Text:
It's one of the most impressive places in all respects
The way to get there best by tuktuk from Haputale and do stop as the views on this long drive are fascinating but so are the tea plucked villages and you have many opportunities to see them close and experience theyre friendly contacts 
Visit also the Hindu temple and the people in the enclosed village around it the top is an ultimate view place in all directions but mainly to the south and west so go there early as it can get misty from noon and then the famous view has gone
If you are good in walking do it from the entrance port it's a great walk and visit the shady cafe for lunch or?whatever you need

Title: Some tip for the tourists
Text:
Take a tuktuk from Railway station and offer the guy 1200 or 1300 LKR to visit both Lipton Seat and Tea Factory. Pay him 100 for every additional time you want to stay at either of the place.

If you are not strong enough at hiking, then you may consider visiting this place or Little Adam's Peak instead of going to the Adam's Peak at Hatton.

Title: Really gorgeous views
Text: You take a risk with the clouds but even though our view was limited once we reached the top our journey up was great if a little sad seeing all the hard working tea puckers.

Title: Hike on a road
Text: We went to Lipton Seat with a tuck-tuck (800 roupies from Haputale to the entrance). Unfortunately at the top it was foggy by the time we arrived. Nevertheless we hiked all the way down. We were a bit disappointed that the path was just the way back on the concrete road. Still a nice walk trough the tea plantations.

Title: Worth a visit ????
Text:
Car can only reach Dambatenne Tea Factory and from there we changed tuktuk. 
It was a 6~7 km ride to the top and I am glad we did go there.
The Lipton's seat location is private property so you'll have to pay by entrance (forgot how much but it's cheap).And if you wanna enjoy tea farm view all the way up it's about 30~40 mins walk (~2 km). There's no toilet inside so be prepared. On the top you may see Lipton's (Sir. Thomas.J.Lipton) statue and a beautiful view from top of the hill. You can also enjoy a fresh cup of tea from the tea plantation and some snacks there. Our driver was surprised (he'd never been there) and said he'd definitely recommend this place to his customer in the future.

Title: Amazing views and beautiful tea plantations.
Text:
We had a Tuk-tuk take us up to Lipton's seat. The road is tight hairpin bends all the way up through the tea plantations, so not easy by car and it is a long way on foot. All along the way the views just get better and better. Once on the top the panoramic view is breathtaking. Oh.. and you can get a nice cup of tea while you admire the view.
Go early in the day or you might be sharing it with too many people.

Title: Must go
Text:
From Haputale, get the local bus to dambatenne (rs30/pers), it is only 15 minutes ride. And from there you can start to walk to the Lipton seat. 6 km through the tea plantation and local village to get to the top. It is a easy walk and not so many cars.
You will be charge rs50 when you get close to the top.

Probably the best and most enjoyable think I've done here in Sri Lanka, landescape are breathtaking, people along the road are so nice, and nobody is trying to sell you anything.
There is a fews school on the road, if you go there, take some pen with you to give out to the kids you met on your way up, they will be more than happy!

On the top, there is a little shop, selling tea coffee soda.. they even cook some very good samosa! Please do not miss them, the 2 gentlemens are very kind, and the price is more than reasonable.
Be aware that some monkey will try to rob your food.

A must do in Sri Lanka, and by walk!! Don't wast your money with a tuktuk.

Title: best walk on sri lanka
Text: Best walk on vacation. Go early morning with the bus to the tea factory.than take a tuktuk 7km up to the lipton seat. Enjoy the view and than take a walk down. Use the shorter ways and get lost in green color everywhere. Just beautyful place.

Title: A must see!
Text: The drive from Ella through the tea plantations to Liptons Seat are gorgeous.  We walked part of the way but I would recommend you walk the whole way if you're up to it.  The scenery is spectacular.

Title: The walk to or from is the real fun!
Text: Liptons seat itself is hit or miss as there can often be mist or clouds blocking the view from the top...but walking through the tea plantations either to or from Liptons seat is spectacular! Dont miss the beauty and fun of the journey.

Title: What a view. We were so lucky
Text: Our driver took us up to the entrance to Lipton Seat. You have to walk another 1.4km up the hill. It's a good hike but you can negotiate a tuk tuk. Try paying 300 for the lift up, wait and then lift back. It's worth it. The walk down to the tea factory is long, but also worth it.

Title: Nice Hike, okay view.
Text:
A lot of fog even though we made it up there early. 
Dont take a tuktuk all the way up, walk from the tea factory (2h up, same down).
If you ride, youll miss the best part of the landscape.

Title: Fab
Text: We hired a scooter and went from Ella. Have to be confident to drive though and nerves of steel lol. If not hire a tuk tuk from Haputale. The views on the way up are fantastic and so worth the drive. We got to the top a bit late so it had clouded over on one side. Had a cuppa and a snack at the top before we ventured back down. Had a chat with some of the locals and really enjoyed ??

Title: Excellent but tiring day of hiking
Text: From Haputale i caught the bus 9 kms  to Dambatenne  where the bus stops and returns to town. However there is another smaller bus that takes you much further towards Lipton's Seat, but i decided to hike the last 8 kms up the hill. I walked through the village of Dambatenne and the road led uphill for the next 5 kms, sometimes quite steep. Eventually i crossed a ridge and the road leveled out until it reached the ticket office where i purchased an entrance ticket for Lipton's Seat. The last kilometer was all uphill. There were a few other people there and there was a statue of Lipton, himself sitting on a bench (where most of the visitors sat with him for a photo). The view was quite good and on a clear day you could see the coastline. This is where Sir Lipton used to come and sit. I decided to walk back all the way to Haputale (16kms) and it was well worth doing.

Title: Get there for the sunrise!
Text: From Haputale, we took tuk-tuk at 5 mp to get there for a sunrise and we were very happy with the decision. Don't go to the very top where the Lipton is seated, stay about 300 m below where the road curves and enjoy the splendid view of the valley. Take a tripod for better pictures! The way down is very easy and enjoyable 7km long walk, but it feels much shorter. You can observe ladies picking tea leaves, they are very sweet and even keen to pose you! Take some pens and other school supplies as you will meet many local kids.

Title: Cracking experience.
Text: Certain worth it, we took a tuk tuk (recently done Adams Peak and didn't fancy the trek!) up and down and stopped at various breath taking view points on the way. Recommend doing it as early as possible in the day to get the best views before the cloud rolls in. The tea at the top is both cheap and best way to relax and enjoy the scenery!

Title: Beautiful, easy hike. Take the short cuts!
Text:
You can arrive by bus to Dambatenne factory or take a tuk-tuk to the top at Lipton's seat. We recommend taking the short cuts to be immersed in the nature and say hello to the tea pickers. 
We also went through the Tamil villages and saw the lovely kids coming back from school.
We don't recommend to visit Dambatenne factory though. 250 Rs and not even a tasting experience.

Title: The view's great but the ride 's even better!
Text: What a tuk-tuk ride! A convey of tuk-tuk snake their way up the mountain to the penultimate view of Sri Lanka. Ask your hotel to book Safran. He'll give you a hoot of a tour with plenty of honks to boot- he seems to know everyone in Haputale.

Title: Fantastic views
Text:
We skipped the factory as we had only just been to another one. 
We did use the wash room which cost 20 rupee each, not sure what the money went towards as they were horrific. 
We then took a tuk tuk to meet Mr Lipton. When we arrived it was misty but it soon cleared. 
The views and the journey were spectacular. 
We had tea and rotti at the top. Food was delicious but the workers were trying to get as much money out of you as possible by giving you more without asking

Title: Nice view and trail
Text:
At first we wanted to take a walk to Lipton's Seat, but our driver arranged a couple of tuk tuks to take us up hill. From the last village to the seat wouldn't have been too much to walk, but we got the tuk tuks from far away, so it seemed like too much to walk. 
The guys were nice enough to stop at every nice view in order for us to take pictures. The view was amazing all the way up.
Sadly when we got to the chair, there was a lot of mist on one side of the cliff and we couldn't admire everything, but the view that we had was amazing!

Title: Breathtaking Views
Text: The highest point in the area with distant views of five of the provinces of Sri Lanka. We were told that on a clear day one can see the ocean from here.  It was a little too hazy when we were up there.

Title: Walk up at sunrise - grand way to spend morning!
Text:
The walk up from the entrance gate is about 1.3 km according to my tuktuk driver. It took a very leisurely hour, stopping to take pictures and marvel at misty mountain views and ghostly tree silhouettes. Walk it if you have two legs, it's worth it. The trail itself is glorious and at the top you can get some nice strong hot tea and/or coconut roti and wadi. I walked the 8km down but loved wandering through the terraces so much it was more like 15. I would totally recommend spending an entire morning, if not day, doing just that. The people are super sweet and will even invite you into their house for tea. Take 'school pens' or stickers along to give the children living there, it makes them so excited!
You can grab the bus back to Haputale for 16 rupees.

Title: Magnificent Sunrise at Liptons seat
Text:
We started our journey from a hotel in Ella at 455am and arrived the peak after a short transit to board a tuk tuk in order to get all the way up to the Liptons seat.

The temperature was cold, around 8 degrees celsius so please be prepared.

At the peak, its just a viewpoint to take a great sunrise shot, there is a local cafe which serves some local savouries and hot cups of tea and coffee, nothing fancy.

Be warned, there are no restrooms at this point and the closest one is at the tea factory 30min drive away that only opens at 8am, and you will need 20 sri lankan rupees for that.

Title: Walk through the tea plantation
Text: A wonderful place to go down from the Lipton Seat to the Tea factory. It will take you a couple of hours, but it's worth it!  The views are unforgettable.

Title: Like from fairytale
Text: Stunning view from this point. you can go by foot but by tuk tuks i better option i guess. up on the hill is small restaurant where you can enjoy your cup of tea.

Title: Liptons tea factory
Text:
Stunning views over huge area of tea plants . Liptons height is on 1900 meters. You can see the picking of the tea leaves by women. They earn 40 rupees per kilo. They pic up to19 Kilo a day. You can se the very old fashion factory following how the tea is dried cut and fermented.
It was really worthwhile to go there.

Title: Tea Tea Tea
Text: Really recommend a trip to Liptons Seat, and from there walk down through the fields to the Tea Factory to catch the bus back to Haputale.

Title: Very nice view. Less nice Café
Text: Very nice view even though it was cloudy, the way up was absolutely amazing.  However we could gave skipped the café. The workers lured us in which was expected but it was unnecessarily expensive for a cup of tea and some small portion of Rotti. When we paid the waiter refused to give me the change because I'm a woman and insisted on waiting for my fiancé which i found upsetting, and then he expected a tip.

Title: Amazing views
Text:
We did this the lazy way with a bone rattling tuk-tuk ride to the top and then back down.
Beautiful views, absolutely breath-taking, photographs dont do it justice you need to see it to believe. With a morning visit, with bright sun and clear skies you can see all the way to the southern beaches of Sri Lanka from here.
It actually got a bit cold when we visited and we were glad that the lookout at the top asked us if we wanted some team & rottis ??
Some hot food and drink was most welcome!
Thoroughly recommend.

Title: Stunning views
Text: We did Liptons Seat the lazy way which was to take a Turk-Tuk up and then walk down.  It is so worth it to stay at Haputale to do this walk and see the views which are spectacular. The walk down is a breeze and is a wonderful experience.

Title: Incredible views!
Text: Go early in the morning, such a beautiful spot and very peaceful. We were lucky enough to experience a perfectly clear sunny morning. The small cafe/hut at the top also serves good roti, samosa and of course tea. We traveled by Tuk Tuk from our home-stay in Ella.

Title: Beautiful
Text: We had our driver take us all the way up to Liptons Seat. No need for a tuk tuk if you have a car. Unfortunately for us it was super misty so we didnt have the amazing view we had heard of.  The locals told us the mornings are much better than the afternoons so I would advise you to go early. The drive up was completely beautiful so we still enjoyed some amazing views and there is a cute tea shop at the top with really good samosas!

Title: Stunning view of surrounding mountains and reservoirs
Text: The place was named after Sir Thomas Lipton who has loved to come to this lookout point and for whom a memorial has been erected there. It shows the British founder of the trademark Lipton sitting while holding a cup of tea. From Liptons seat you can have a stunning view of surrounding mountains and reservoirs. Clouds might fog the views at times. We advice to ask the locals about the expected weather conditions. They´ll know better than the well known weather websites. There is a basic tea stall which serves breakfast, with tea of course. A final advice: bring some extra warm clothes, it gets quite chilly in the morning.

Title: Great view but drive better
Text: The drive up was amazing, the actual look out was overated but the drive up through all the tea plants was really special

Title: an amazing place designating a piece of history
Text: Many people come to see the views and to experience either sunrise or sunset.  We arrived a bit later than sunrise but had the tremendous experience of taking a tuk tuk from the Dambatenne Estate Factory and office to the top -- not to be missed.  We then experienced the incredible fog which came and went (mostly came) but appreciated the views when they were available.  Don't miss the dosas and somasas (along with the super coffee) served in the little shop right at the parking lot....all were terrific.

Title: Ancient ruins
Text: You buy a ticket that allows you to access all the ancient spots of Polonnaruwa and they stamp it at each site. The tour from one spot to another should be done by tuktuk or car or on a scooter as it is not walkable, and you need a good 3.5-5 hours to finish it all if you want to take pictures and check out each site. It got a bit redundant at the end and it was hot by mid-day, but it's always nice to explore the ancient side and ruins of a country. More reviews @myra.recommends

Title: Amazing whole day trip for everyone that enjoys building ruins
Text:
I liked the tour through the historical sights of Pollonaruwa a lot. The places are visited by tourists, but also by locals, since the temples are still active. 
This is definitely a whole day trip as the places are far away from each other. You will need to get tuk tuk or taxi to manage everything. I recommend to have 1 driver that will go with you through all the sights, as the locals know the town and an arranged tuk tuk/car makes it very convenient and comfortable to move around. 
The tickets need to be purchased at the ticket office of Archeological museum in Polonnaruwa, where you will also start your tour and get the most basic information about the place.

Title: So rich in history!
Text: A day is hardly sufficient to see and learn it all. There is so much to see with its colourful history going back many centuries. Fascinating city. Loved it.

Title: Ancient City,
Text:
Lovely heritage city. You can find a lot of ancient monuments. Second oldest kingdom of Sri Lanka You cost only $ 25.00 USD to enter . . There is a modest dress code for visiting temples in Sri Lanka. Knees and shoulders must be covered. It's very humid so if you do wear shorts, pack a sarong for when you enter the temples.
Sarong will be nice experience for you

Title: Add the experience to your travels.
Text:
Oh my goodness. This whole site is absolutely amazing.
Look at the photos- they will show much better than I can describe what it is like.
Most attractions in Sri Lanka have quite a steep entry fee for foreigners, but this is worth the cost.
You can spend a whole day here, wandering to different sites all in the same area.
Highly recommend having a guide, so you can learn all the history available. If you are not with a guide for your whole time, find a way to hire one. It will be worth it.
I won't forget our visit here- it was stunning.

Title: Great Day Out
Text:
Third trip to this site since 2018. What an incredible job they have done with this place. Remarkable the care and attention bestowed and over the years we can see how this has developed 
We really enjoyed the experience but our negative experience against the hawkers would certainly make me think about going again. We almost got told off by one for not buying his wares and why as tourist we should. Sadly it did put a damper on the day having to constantly say No Thank You
Word of caution be very aware of the monkeys as they are incredibly brave and up for a free lunch

Title: Royal palace quadrangle, pulanaruva, Sri Lanka
Text:
The ancient ruins of hatadage of vijayabahu empire are still in excellent condition.
The moonstone depicting various phases of life are beautiful work of art.
The royal palace quadrangle with more than thousand years old ruins give a glimpse of the flourishing art and culture of the bygone era.
The bathing ghat, the round Buddha vihara with the statues of Lord Buddha in various postures facing the cardinal directions glimmer even today.
The place is still a pilgrimage place for Buddhists.
There are a number of stalls selling refreshing tender coconut for the thirsty tourists.

Worth visiting.

Title: True Ancient City
Text: Very good place to visit to see how all the cultural things mixed up with Buddhism.intresting place and you will never get bored.

Title: Inspiring and
Text: a really great visit that had me thinking about just how sophisticated ancient civilisations were and how their societies worked and relaxed together and how important their religious traditions were in shaping how their community operates

Title: Ideal half day tour
Text: Our hotel arranged for a guide and bikes to allow us tour tour this site. Our tour lasted approximately who hours and enabled us to visit most of the key locations. Definitely worth visiting the area - remember to get your ticket validated on leaving the site if you want to visit again later in the day.

Title: A nice experience
Text:
We visited the 3 points of attraction in the area. It took around 2hs ( max) by car, and it was fairly pleasant. 

You defiantly need a guide to get a better understanding of the area and its importance to Buddhist. 

It doesn't feel as grand as some of the other sites we have visited and here I feel like you really someone to guide you otherwise it feels like its just ruins and a few Buddha statues

Title: An amazing site
Text:
An amazing site! and i believe this is one of the must-see places in Sri Lanka, highly recommended for those who like to explore history or architecture. And also definitely you need a guide, Mr Kaan was our guide throughout the tour and he has very good knowledge about the history of Sri Lanka. The information he gave were fantastic!

We started our visit at the archaeological museum and you can learn some interesting facts about the history from the archaeological museum before you go to the ruins. We started early morning 8.00 am and leave 1.30pm, we spent there at more than 5 hours.

Title: Good ancient site
Text: For me, much better than Anuradhapura. Its easier to get between the sites, but still needs a tuk-tuk, and the ruins are more impressive. The high spot for us was the sleeping Buddha carved out of the rock face.

Title: Excellent Historical site
Text: I really enjoyed visiting the museum and the various sites. This is a must see when visiting Sri Lanka. The structures give a glimpse of life during the 8-9 century. I particularly liked the Galviharaya Site that had the 4 Buddha's carved into the stone. Absolutely a beautiful religious area.

Title: The ancient city
Text: Definitely wort a visit. You need a whole day, its a huge area. We where there as some of the first visitors after covid close down, so we where there almost alone. There is not many places to hide from the sun, so bring water or buy from many of the small shops there.

Title: Archeological and natural site
Text: Polonnaruwa is in the meantime an archeological and a natural site. Do not expect ruins like you will have around the Mediterranean Sea or in Central America, but the monuments are suggestive, especially in the holy area. All along the visit, you will encounter bonnet macaques, which are very funny. At the entrance, you can rent some bicycles to enjoy the visit at a pleasant rhythm.

Title: A historic site that showcases life in those bygone days
Text:
Its a nice place with rich history. Since the areas are spread quite a bit, maybe a good idea to hire a tuk-tuk (we travelled by car). A local guide could be very helpful, else you may not understand the significance of the artifacts or end up spending time less efficiently. 

If youre from South India, youd be amazed by the historical connections between Srilanka and India.

Title: Amazing!
Text:
We were staying in Dambulla as part of our tour and made the trip to visit this fantastic site - not to be missed! We went in the morning and were meant to be using bicycles to get around - it was very very hot so we opted to stick with our driver and use the car to move between the various sites.

Shorts below the knee and shoulders to be covered at many places here if you want to properly explore! Vendors selling drinks too (very welcome as there isn't much shade around!!!).

So much to learn about this site - definitely grateful to have our driver with us to explain everything!

Well worth a visit.

Title: Need Time to do it Justice
Text: What a fantastic site. We caught Tuk Tuk's to cover as much area as possible but still had to hurry. There are 4 major sections with the  Citadel, Royal Palace, Sacred Quadrangle & Galviharaya plus lots of other sights. Being time poor we covered as mush as we could. Our guide was pretty useless so I gleaned as much as I could from the signage which was poor mostly. This is a World Heritage Site & an ancient capital of Sri Lanka & home to many kings in its day.

Title: wow
Text:
we visited polonnaruwa site in the morning time.
our driver reccomended us to hire a bicycles it was great idea but not in the afternoon.
the ruines are old and beautifull.
best place in the site was three  budda statues carved from the rock

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Museum and ruins well worth the visit. undiscovered for 700 years. The Kings Palace with a huge slice off  rock on which 4000 rules are engraved, truly amazing

Title: Peaceful cycle through lovely ruins
Text: Brought ticket at museum entrance to visit the ruins. Do the museum first because once youve done the ruins, they keep your ticket so you cant pass to anyone else, and you then cant get into the museum later. We cycled through the ruins and it was a really great way to see them. There are places within the ruins to buy cold drinks and snacks and sit for a while. One word of warning, a lot of the ruin buildings ask for shoes to be removed before you enter, and the ground is gritty and boiling hot, so take a pair of socks with you to save your soles. Also shoulders and legs need to be covered in certain areas so dress modestly or carry a shawl

Title: Great Cultural sites
Text: We visited here with a party of seven tourists. We had a guide with us who was knowledgeable and clearly a great help. Some great sites to see but only enhanced by local knowledge and understanding. It will take you all day to see most of the sites so plan accordingly.

Title: Intriguing History & Amazing Heritage!!!
Text:
Another UNESCO World Heritage Site that worth a visit especially for history buff. An interesting history where the kingdom was built during Chola Dynasty since invasion from South India to the capital city of Anuradhapura, then Polonnaruwa since 10th century. It is said to be a systematic destruction of Buddhism civilisation from the north in Anuradhapura and built Shiva Temple with Hinduism influence. Polonnaruwa was then established with various significant architecture including more superior water irrigation system that flourished agriculture and trade. Both metropolises were then destroyed and burnt after the war and invasion by Kalinga Magha  (founder of Jaffna Kingdom) in 13th century. There are many remnants of the ruins with intriguing stone carvings. Some of the checklist for places to visit at this site include the below: 

a. Thivanka Image House**
b. Polonnaruwa Nelum Pokuna - Lotus**
c. Gal Vihara (Rock Temple)**
Kiri Vihara - 91**
Lankatilaha Viraya - 90**
d. Alahana Pirivena - 73**
Rankot Vihara**
Pabalu Vehera - 52**
Sheva Devale - 2-54**
e. Hetadage
f. Nissankalata Mandapa - 43**
g. Vatadage - 39**
h. Dalada Maluva - Polonnaruwa**
i. Hindu Temple God Shiva Devalaya**
j. Palace of King Nishshanka Malla**
k. Deepa Uyana
l. Palace of King Parakramabahu**
j. Council of Chamber**
k. Pothgul Viharaya

Well worth the steep entrance fee of USD25 and take your time to enjoy the site at your own pace with half to full day tour. Hiring a driver is essential when visiting this site. We used BLUE HAVEN TOURS with an excellent driver Mr Sugath. Drinking water  is essential too.

Title: Interesting
Text: Came here on our bikes which I think is the best way to visit the site. Loved the ruïnes and the history

Title: Too much to see
Text: Spent a good part of a day walking round the ruins of temples and other buildings. Quite crowded, and by time we had finished I felt that I didnt want to see another temple!

Title: Words cannot describe it
Text: This is a huge, huge site. We had a private bus tour and we used it to move between the sites, otherwise I don;t know how we would have done it. All the sites are amazing, take at least half a day to see them.

Title: Yet another wonder of Sri Lanka
Text:
Lots to see in this ancient and well preserved city which is rightly a UNESCO world heritage site. Shamefully, we spent less than two hours here when at least three would've given us the opportunity to see even more. 

The Buddhas at Gal Vihara are an magnificent site and we were lucky enough to witness a Religious ceremony during our visit.

The Rankot Vihara dagoba was extremely impressive and is still used by pilgrims to leave offerings, most of which were snaffled up by the ubiquitous and fast moving monkeys!

Thoroughly recommended.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: I visited Polonnaruwa on the way from Negombo to Sigriya. It requires atleast 2-3 hours and is worth the visit. Entrance fee for SAARC citizens (includes India) is USD 12.5 and  you need to produce the passport at the counter. At the museam office they handout a one page guide / map with major attractions, you can go from one place to another in car and visit as many as interest you. Reading the reviews of the key places to visit and keeping a note of them before arriving there is helpful, so as not to waste time there figuring out what to see. There are quite a few to choose from. Given the pleasant weather and the lovely greenery it was more than just visiting some historical place with ruins, the greenery added to the pleasant vibes and overall it was a wonderful experience.

Title: If you like ancient archaeology, this is the place for you....
Text: We were due to be taken to Sigiriya by our tour guide, but it wasn't really suitable for my post op knee, so he suggested going to the Polonnaruwa archaeological sites... It was a great experience. He drove us between each site and left us to explore the archaeology. It was a really amazing place to explore with each site having old ruined temples which are still considered holy places  and hence no shoes and respectful clothing.. We really enjoyed our time there although it would have been better for us to have gone earlier in the day, as we had to give up on the last temple because it was too hot with our shoes off !... We could see on many of the sites conservation work was going on which was very good , these important historical sites need to be preserved. We saw many people touring on bikes which looked fun and some people were using Tuk-Tuks to travel between the sites... If you like ancient archaeology I highly recommend this place to you.

Title: Fab day out
Text: A must do day out whilst in this region. Really interesting and awe inspiring. Few things to try to do. Visit the museum first which will make the whole place more understandable. If you want to book a guide it is worthwhile but if you struggle with hearing it may be better not to as they dont all speak good English. Take a scarf for the sights require ladies to cover legs and shoulders. Wear shoes you can slip on or off as you need to remove them to go up close. There is a number of pedlars at every site. Unless you want to buy anything just say No Thank You. You can go round by car or hire a bike depending on your fitness and heat tolerance level. The toilets for foreigners are very clean and good. Take some small change to tip the attendants. A worthwhile and enjoyable day and leaves you in wonder and awe on how it must of look when in its full glory.

Title: Worth It
Text: So far in our trip, this is the premier historical site. I can't image being in Sri Lanka and not visiting here.

Title: A STUNNING SITE
Text: Polonnawura richly deserves its status as a World Heritage Site. It can be visited over the course of a day. While a ruin, there are enough tantalizing remains to interest any traveler. The area ruled Sri Lanka from the 11th through 13th centuries. Several buildings here likely held the Tooth Relic. There are other unique structures like the circular Vatadage and the oddly shaped Satmahal Prasada, the purpose of the latter unclear. Places like the Lankatilaka Vihara, stretching to the heavens, will catch any photographer's eye. The sublime sculptures at Gal Vihara represent the best of Sinhalese craftsmanship, the artistry of the Kumara Pokuna, the royal baths, not far behind. It is a more impressive site overall than Anuradhapura.

Title: Amazingly rich historical site
Text:
Fabulous historical site. The remaining ruins are of a medieval kingdom that flourished for a short period in the 11-12th centuries. Many amazing bits of architecture 

The site is huge so if you are not up for a 12 km walk take a Tuk Tuk or rent a bike.  Bike rental is 400 rupees.  

We walked it and spent the day there.  Enjoyed the archeology and the wildlife. Saw monkey deer and an amazing range of birds including woolly necked stalks and hornbills

Title: Amazing variety of temples
Text: Our guide took us to the small museum first, to put everything in context.  It was useful.  Then we hired bikes (ropey and old but functional!) and went into the Polonnaruwa complex.  It spreads over a quite a large area so is well worth hiring the bikes in order to see everything.  I lost count of the amount of buildings - quite a lot of temples still intact and not just ruins.  Everything is labelled in English too, so you can get some background information at each individual site.  It took us a good 3 hours to go round the whole site on bikes - there are various vendors around the site selling snacks, drinks and souvenirs.  The whole experience was very pleasant and a relatively easy ride with only a few slight inclines.  It was interesting to find out more about the ancient civilisations and learn about the culture. A good trip

Title: Nice but...
Text: very nice and old city but the systém of tickets and entrance is terrible and crazy.. no marks and signs ticket office is almost 2 km far away from entrance.

Title: Interesting and well kept
Text:
The site is on a big area and is recommended to have a tuk tuk driver or to rent a bike in order to explore the whole area. 
Very interesting ruins and I am positively impressed how everything is well maintained and clean, which is a sign that the money of the ticket goes into the preservation, as it should.
The museum is also well made and contains some artifacts found on the site.
Definitely worth a visit!

Title: Gal Viharaya was amazing but the monkeys stole the show
Text: I don't want to come across as too much of a Philistine because we came to see the ruins and they were very interesting, our guide gave a nice explanation and Gal Viharaya was particularly impressive in its scale and preservation. It must be said though, the monkeys stole my attention for all but GV, they were everywhere and I could have watched them fighting and playing all day. Apologies to our guide Dan because he probably got fed up of me looking at the monkeys instead of what he was pointing at.

Title: Huge site
Text: Polonnaruwa covers a huge  area so it is handy having a car that can drive you from one archaeological ruin to another. There are many ruins to explore and learn about. Well maintained areas. Handy to have a guide to explain things but it is not essential. There are many areas to see that are not so popular with tourists so are less crowded so need to make sure you have enough time to explore it all.

Title: Full of beauties
Text: It has a lot of beauties about ancient but its very different from the other ancients. I visited for a 2 hour,so i had to skip some points but i think it deserves 3 hours if you want to catch to everypoint

Title: Better with a guide
Text: Vast area  with museum and archeological sites. It really is worth spending the 20USD on a guide for 2 hours to get the most out of it.

Title: Amazing
Text: Polonnaruwa is a must on any visit of the country. The amazing statues of Lord Buddha, rock carvings and ancient moments are all simply beautiful!

Title: Ancient city ruins of the Chola dynasty
Text:
It is not a large area and the ruins arent as intact as in Angkor Wat, if a comparison needs to be made. But it is a good introduction to the history of Sri Lanka. 

The second most ancient of Sri Lanka's kingdoms, Polonnaruwa was first established by the Chola dynasty after their successful invasion of the country's then capital, Anuradhapura, in the 10th century. The Ancient City of Polonnaruwa has been declared a World Heritage Site. 

Polonnaruwa is the second largest city in North Central Province, but it is known as one of the cleanest and more beautiful cities in the country.

Polonnaruwa was ruled by the Kings Vijayabahu I, Parakramabahu the Great and Nissanka Malla  all 3 of these rulers devoted themselves to fostering agriculture, religion and social development and the kingdom prospered under their reign during this era.

Title: Rich history
Text:
From the museum to the many sites throughout the ancient city, Polonnaruwa was probably our favourite stop in the Cultural Triangle. 

Not as old as Anuradhapura, or as well preserved, it is better organized and you can more easily develop an understanding of the different eras and constructions. 

Youll need a few hours to see it all, but youll want to spend time checking out the different sections and appreciate the artistry evident in many of the ruins.

The only drawback are the numerous, persistent vendors at nearly every stop (something that isnt condoned at Anuradhapura), but be firm, polite and keep moving and they will leave you be (eventually).

Title: Amazing
Text: Such a good glimpse back in time. Well worth the trip. Unfortunately we only had half a day, as  the site is so big could easily spend the day here roaming around. Was a great experience.

Title: Incredible Ruins!
Text: We loved the fact that we had our lovely guide travelling with us who was able to give us just enough information about the history without overwhelming us. These ruins are incredibly breathtaking - the magnitude of them, and we enjoyed biking around the vast area in between the ruins. Don't miss the Buddha carved into the rock. Stunning!!

Title: Vestiges of the great history of Sri Lanka
Text:
The ruins and artefacts of Polonnaruwa, the centre of Sri Lanka's second most ancient kingdom established by the Chola dynasty in the 10th Century, are widespread and impressive.
Given the time we had, our tour took in the most significant of the ancient ruins, but you could spend several days covering the entire World Heritage area of around 100 sq km.
The royal palace and citadel area is a good place to start, as the centre of this ancient kingdom, then fan out to nearby attractions. Water was gravity fed to the royal bath, captured on the slightly higher ground of the palace itself. 
You must ensure your tour includes Gal Vihara, to see what are considered the best rock sculptures in Sri Lanka.

Title: Great half day
Text:
Hired bikes and cycled round the pleasant site over a 3 hour period. 
You will need to have covered shoulders and knees, take off shoes etc to visit the temple sites. 
Plenty to see over a large area.

Title: Hot but worth it
Text: We toured the many historical sites , in this ancient city . It was a little tiring and hot with kids but well worth the effort . Finished at Gal Vihara at 4 pm which was perfect with the sun a little less intense

Title: A absolute must see
Text: We visited this ancient round and had a guide, Polo, who was fantastic ($35) but well worth it as his knowledge was superb and as the site is so huge invaluable... the history and wonderment is outstanding

Title: So much to see in a week let alone a day!
Text:
My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Sri Lanka and earlier today we visited the old Capital of Polonnaruwa.

We began our visit at the Archeological Museum (see separate Review) which gave a sense of what lay in store but the scale and size of the main site has to be seen to be believed. It is also hard to believe that barely 5% of the site has so far been excavated so you can imagine what treasures will be unearthed in years to come!

As such, to get the most out of ones day visitors are strongly advised to plan their visit well in advance. We all have our own preferences but my selection would include the Royal Palace Grouping, Quadrangle, Northern Group (particularly the Rankot Vihara & especially the Buddha Seema Prasada & Lankatilaka) and - even though I wasnt personally over impressed - Gal Vihara.

Believe me, to see everything would take the best part of a week but plan ahead and you should have a most enjoyable day out!

Title: Good, but not great
Text:
Very interesting place to visit, with a large number of stopping points. This was probably the day when our driver guide was most helpful. 

It is of course hot work, even with a car to get between places. Must be really hard on a bike. It's also very expensive and there are lots of hawkers selling junk everywhere.

If you have time it's a nice place to visit, but I wouldn't say it's a must.

Title: Polonnaruwa sacred city
Text: Great place to visit but definitely not worth $25. The museum felt like an oven turned on full. I couldnt stay inside because I was feeling uncomfortable from the heat, and the lettering on plaques explaining the various ruins is wearing off. This site needs much more maintenance work. And the locals pay 100LKR entrance fee...

Title: Grossly overpriced and filled with tack sellers
Text:
This site is used to take money from tourists. It is that simple. 4500Rs for an adult "foreigner" to enter.

On arrival at the museum to buy your ticket you will be surrounded by local tour guides trying to be employed. They do not take no for an answer. Ignore them; walk the site yourself. They will tell you it is too big to be walked, trust me, it does not require a tuk-tuk. Walk.

The museum was worth one trip round, but better to get to the ruins themselves. Once there, they are lovely to see. Amazing history. All of which can be walked around. The Temple to the north was really special and well kept.

It is the local tack sellers and temple "life guards" blowing their whistles which ruined the day for me. They walk around in shoes whilst barking at tourists to remove theirs - it's ridiculous - especially given how hot the sand is in the sun.

It's all a money making scheme, which is such a shame. Worth the trip, but be stern with the vulture-like salesmen and take lots of water on a hot day.

Title: Wastly overpriced and filled with annoying salesmen
Text: Just normal ruins with nothing to see really. Museum was poor and really hot because they used only domestic A/C machines. Definitely nowere near worth the 25 $ pp it costs. Typical Sri Lankan touristscam...

Title: Relaxing tour with  very few tourists.
Text: This place is really huge and our driver cum tourist guide Mr Suranga is very good and knowledgeable in the history and stories about this place. We are able to take as many pictures as we want without having people in the background. It feel like we are on a very private tour to this place.  The place is clean and there are many toilets and it is very clean too.

Title: Cycling round temple ruins
Text:
Collected bike and started our ride around the site of old temple. Built by King Vijayabahu 1070. Interesting place to see amazing pagodas built so long ago.
Worth an hour or so of your day.

Title: Amazing Cycle through the Ruins
Text: This was such a good experience! I highly recommned the cycle option. Our driver offered to take us round as it was hot but there are plenty of stalls along the way to get water or better yet, a cold king coconut!

Title: Impressive ruins but HORRENDOUS museum
Text:
We visited Polonnaruwa on a typically hot, humid day, which would've been no big deal except for the fact that we did a tour of their "museum" too.

I mean, knowing it's hot and humid, I can accept that it will be tiring under the sun while viewing the ancient ruins. 
But I really, really thought it was downright pathetic of them to call their museum a "museum", because that's indoors, and it was a literal oven cooking everyone inside alive.

We visited the museum prior to actually viewing the ruins, and there, the ventilation is not poor, it's NON-EXISTENT. It's so damn stuffy you have difficulties breathing, and while there are these industrial air-conditioners fixed from the wall, they are not in use at all. Instead, they put fans and those coolers around, expecting these little machines to provide the ventilation and cool air the place actually needs.

It was an epic fail. Unless you stood right in front of a cooler, you'd feel like you're burning from inside out, all the time. The moment you step way from a fan or a cooler, the heat literally engulfs you. 

The museum content is actually quite interesting. The ruins themselves were also impressive. But the ventilation and air-conditioning of the museum is worse than crap. If I could I would just visit the ruins and skip the oven they call their museum.

Title: Ancient city of Polonnaruwa
Text:
If you go to Sri Lanka, Pollonaruwa is a must go place 
Large tanks ruins of the palace, temples and also the worlds best stone carved Buddha statues

Title: Awesome if you start at the right end
Text:
World Heritage for sure.
Start with the 4 Buddhas (Northern group) and work your way south. Its a fairly big area to visit. 
Bikes for rent are mostly in a sad condition and not fun to ride. I would rather suggest to be dropped off by a tuktuk at the northern end/the 4 Buddhas and walk back to the entrance area. Theres at least 2 simple coconut cafes on the way back, too.
The worst part of the area is the Island/Mausoleum near the museum. 
The museum is hot like a sauna with mainly before-after pictures and models with only some interesting original exhibits.

Title: ANCIENT CITY
Text: We started with a visit to the on site museum which gave us a good idea of this civilisation, rediscovered by the British Archaeologist H C Bell who spent 20 years in Sri Lanka.  There are remains of the palace and the usual temples.  There is a reclining Buddha and one some 24 feet tall.  This is the second most ancient capital and World Heritage Site.  Monkeys abound  One thing to remember you have to take your shoes off in the temples and must never turn your back on Buddha  !Wear socks, dark ones!

Title: Well worth a half-day visit
Text:
Spent half a day exploring the ruins of Polonnaruwa and very much enjoyed this UNESCO World Heritage site.

It was a hot day and we'd thought about cycling around, but ended up having our taxi driver take us around. The sites are quite spread out, so its definitely worth having transport to get around.

Bring a pair of socks for the sites that require shoes to be removed (e.g. at the vatadage). Must sees within the compound, if you are short on time, are the Gal Vahara (for buddha statues) and vatadage. Personally found the Lankatilaka Viharaya of most interest - its a large site and there was hardly anyone there - it was a very atmospheric as a result.

Polonnaruwa is a fascinating site which can't be missed if in the area. Try come early before it gets too hot and the big tour groups. Food and snacks are readily available around the site.

Title: It is no wonder it's a UNESCO site.
Text: This ancient city covers a large area you need to allow several hours to walk around the many temple ruins and statues  and you better need a bike to get around (bicycles are available at the entrance). Most important archaeological site in Sri Lanka that is still being discovered today. I recommend this site to visit. Truly amazing ruins!

Title: What a history!
Text: Our guide, (young man of history!!) first took us to the museum and he described almost everything in there with ancient city models, statues, and other ruins. Then he took us to see the ancient city ruins. It was a clever move. So we got a really good idea. It is a really amazing place with a unbelievable creativity and stunning architectural skills nearly 1000 years ago. we were walking through huge green trees and with the fresh air without getting exhausted. Drank coconut water which was really tasty. we saw so many monkeys who were very familiar with people. Even though place is really nice and has a ancient value, authorities should pay more attention to keep the place and ruins safe for next generations.

Title: Fascinating history
Text:
We were on a private guided tour and so glad as there is so much history and without someone giving you a bit of the background to the area it would be very difficult to understand this.  The area is massive so I would suggest if you don't have a guide, read up on the area and have a very good map in hand. 

If you are in Sri Lanka I would put it on my itinerary.

Title: Glad we went
Text: Wasnt sure if this would make the itinerary.  But glad we (accidentally) made it there. A little bit expensive for tourists, and almost no info/maps etc available, so do some reading online first to really enjoy.

Title: Definitely a must to any itinerary........however
Text:
We have to be honest we did not know much about this ancient site before our visit, as we were with a large tour group and just tagged along.

This was once the capital of Sril Lanka (or Ceylon in those days).  Its now a UNESCO World Heritage site.  Certainly interesting and sometimes referred to as the Angkor Wat of Sri Lanka. We wouldnt go quite that far, but the day was dragging on a bit and we didnt visit all the possible sites within. We did a down a dirty visit for about 3 hours, being shuttled to each site/sight, it was a really hoy day and the ground was cooking, (the shoes off rule when visiting scared sites was a challenge), so we weren't keen to hang around.

Eight hundred years ago this was the place to be, now just ruins are left of its former glory, we hit the high points as directed by our guide.

The Quadrangle - a concentration of important monuments ie, temple of the tooth of Buddha.

Rankoth Vehara dagoba - a  massive stupor, at 54 metres high 

And Gal Vihara - beautiful rock carvings, Buddha, and some others

As we were with a group the tickets were just part of the package, however, the  entrance fee for Foreigners is 4500 LKR (or 25 USD), seems a bit much, as independent travellers we might have thought twice.

Title: Great historical park
Text:
A very large park with ruins of the medieval capital city of the kingdom. UNESCO heritage. Entrance fee for foreigners is expensive - 25 USD for adults and 12.50 USD for kids 6-12 years. But its worth a visit - the stone and brick ruins are really interesting. You can see the key places in half a day, but you can also spend here a day or two.
If I compare it with other heritages in Asia, it impressed us more than e.g. Ayuthaya in Thailand, but for sure less than Siem Reap in Cambodia. 
All in all worth a visit.

Title: large historical site
Text: This site comprises of quite a number of interesting ruins. A guide is worthwhile to get an understanding of this ancient site. As portion of the buildings are temples it is necessary to remove shoes and so a good pair of socks is worth it as the ground is uneven and it can be very hot underfoot.

Title: Worth having a tour guide to visit these ancient city
Text:
The main town of Polonnaruwa is in North Central Province of Sri Lanka. The second most ancient of Sri Lanka's kingdoms, Polonnaruwa was first established by the Chola dynasty as their capital in the 10th century. The Ancient City of Polonnaruwa has been declared a World Heritage Site.
Get a guide to inform you of the history... definitely worth it.

Title: Sri Lankan History
Text: Certainly worth a trip if you are in the region. The advice regarding visiting early morning or late afternoon is worth considering if the heat is a problem for you. I went in the afternoon and while it was very hot the place was more or less devoid of the tourist bus loads that flock these sights. Note that if you have a driver it is possible to drive to each of the major sites rather than walk through the extensive reserve. There are bikes for hire which would be a great way to take in each site at a leisurely pace when it is a bit cooler. The museum where you buy your ticket is well worth seeing as there are some magnificent artefacts that have been collected from the site. If you plan to go later in the day be aware that some parts of the site require you to remove your shoes. Suggest you have a pair of socks to provide some protection as the ground gets quite hot.

Title: Amazing Ruins
Text: The ancient city is incredible and quite spread out. There is a lot of fascinating sites to visit. Make sure to allot a fair amount of time to trek through each location.

Title: Photographers Delight.
Text: These ruins are beautiful. The area is huge. There really is a lot to admire. Must have been amazing in its day. Visitors must be respectful and remove shoes in certain locations. Also do as the signs request and don't climb on the walls.

Title: An ancient site - so much to see
Text:
The former medieval capital city of Polonnaruwa covers a very large area and you need to allow several hours to walk around the many temple ruins and statues. It is arguably the most important archaeological site in Sri Lanka that is still being discovered today. It is no wonder it's a UNESCO site. At times you will need to remove your shoes to enter some off the temples. Beware that their are plenty of mischievous monkeys here that may charge at you if you get too close and please do not feed them. You will also experience many locals trying to sell you postcard, wood or other souvenirs.
I thoroughly recommend this site to visit and it sits comfortably as a major attraction with nearby Sigiriya Rock Fortress (Lion's Rock).

Title: Fascinating
Text: Although it's full of tourists in bus loads it's a World Heritage Site and worthy of the appellation. The museum is being fitted with aircon (April 2019) and, so, is somewhat humid. It has good written explanations but is, otherwise, just OK. The ruins are interesting, but if you want to visit the 'sacred' areas bring sodding thick socks as the ground is burning!

Title: Huge, diverse
Text: This site is extensive and contains many relics.  Some are dramatic; some beautiful; some impressive and some historically very important

Title: This site is amazing
Text:
This is a huge site with very many ruins and complexes: citadels and temples.  It is hugely significant to Sri Lankan history.  Parts are very old and very impressive.  There is some - but little - interpretation on site.  A guide (or guidebook) would be useful

It is popular - but can absorb many visitors.  Toilets are only available in carparks, so quite remote from some parts of the site

Title: Nice!
Text: If you go to this area , it is better to visit all the places. I myself just love some parts of that but if you go to srilanka you have to visit this places just for once.

Title: An amazing site
Text: Such wonderful history at the Ancient sites in Sri Lanka. Visited the temples here and statues. Well worth visiting.

Title: Substantial ruins, some strikingly well preserved
Text: Polonnaruwa is a pleasant town with an incredible 12-14c history. We went to 4 out of the 5 main sights including all of the Lonely Plant must sees. Tuktuk drivers have a set tour and its best to just go with it, easier for everyone. The early sites were ruins but they got better, some with stunning stone buddhas and intricate frescos and paintings. Its so hot, cycling wasnt an option for me. I know people lasted two hours on bikes. An added bonus around the ruins wildlife is everywhere!

Title: Impressive and fascinating ruins!
Text:
This is a fascinating place to wander around for a few hours. But these ancient ruins are spread over a vast area, so youll need a car to get around. We were told it takes around 3 days to see it all (not that you need to) but our Trailfinders guide showed us the highlights in a morning. A lot of it is quite similar and can easily be skipped. Sections of it are impressive to say the least and some of it less so. My girlfriend thought parts of it reminded her of Angkor Watt. 

This is a religious site so make sure you cover shoulders and knees, this isnt just a suggestion. We saw one lady having a right tantrum when they refused to let her in one of the temples, because she wasnt dressed appropriately. Even when another member of the public offered to lend her a scarf she carried on screaming at the guards, which had no effect whatsoever. 

Also make sure you dont pose for photos with your back to Budda, its a big no no. There are monkeys everywhere, so avoid carrying food or drink and theyll totally ignore you. We saw what happens if you have food and its not pleasant. Pollonaruwa Ruins are impressive, intriguing and well worth seeing. It was definitely one of my highlights of our Sri Lanka trip. 

Iain, London

Title: Ancient Royal City
Text:
Ruins of the aniient capital, a world heritage site. Really interesting.
There are magnificent statues of Buddha carved into the living rock.  The reclining Buddha is about 40 feet long.
Whatever you do do not take a photo of yourself with your back to the Buddha. It is not allowed and we saw several people being yelled at because they were not showing respect.

Title: Super Stupas
Text:
This whole area is another World Heritage Site, and extensive needing transport to see it all. There is so much to see and explore, and it is worth starting at the museum to see the scale model of how it all looked in its heyday.
We enjoyed the Kings palace, the baths, the Rankot Vihara stupa which is the fourth largest in Sri Lanka, but most of all the rock carvings.
You need time to visit this site - dont forget your socks as shoes off whilst visiting , and it was hot underfoot!

Title: Very interesting
Text: spent half a day here looking at all the ruins and enjoyed it very much. Our tour guide met up with his mentor who taught him his history of the site to pass on to us.

Title: Go on a sunny day without a guide
Text: As per my own schedule, this visit was done on a rainy day. I had a private driver and upon arrival at the building where one is supposed to buy a ticket, the entrance is crowded with people trying to seek shelter from the rain. The parking area has no proper pathment so prepare to dirty your shoes since it's wet and sandy. Got myself an official guide which cost 3000lkr for 2 hours and I deeply regretted it.   Not only the guide has bad breath and I find that my movement were very retricted as he wanted to move fast and was quite impatient to wait for me or help me to take photo. The Audience Hall was ponding with water. I also did not go into the The Vatadage, Rankot Vihara and Gal Vihara as these places requires removing of shoes to walk in the wet sandy ground. And in the end, I gave 5000lkr to the guide expecting him to give me the change of 2000lkr but he just keep the money and feigned ignorance. I had to demand from him to give me back 2000lkr in change which he did upon my insistence. He also trying to sold me some private spa and dining contact places he had which I refused.  Overall I like the sites but due to the various factors, I did not really enjoy my experience there.  My advice, read up on the various locations, go on a sunny day and go around casually at your own timing without the annoying guide.

Title: Vacation
Text: Acres of beautiful old buildings and Temples and Palace make up what used to be the second oldest kingdom in Sri Lanka. This really is a must see. You could spend an entire day here. Dress for very hot weather. Temple sites have a no shoe policy.

Title: Vacation
Text: The council chamber of the king of the second oldest kingdom in Sri Lanka. Some beautiful carved rock  and stone make up what remains of what must have been an amazing building.

Title: Ancient ruins
Text: Beautiful ancient ruins, simply stunning and well preserved, definitely worth a visit, close to Sigria Rock, both can be seen in a day.

Title: Worth the drive
Text: We were staying at a distance but much of fascination to be seen so glad we made the trip. Allow a couple of hours minimum but easy to spend all day there.

Title: Lots to see spread over a wide area
Text: Fascinating place to visit and see the history of this area. The remaining buildings have been preserved/rebuilt and give a great indication of the civilisation that existed here. But the most impressive part are the carvings in the rock and must not be missed.

Title: At least mum and dad loved it!
Text: We arrived at about 10.30am and the ticket office was rammed. A guide talked us into using his services (we had a driver already) and this proved to be a fabulous last minute decision. Hema was able to answer all our questions and made sure we saw all the highlights. We covered everything we wanted to see in about 2 and a half hours. Just as well as the teenagers didnt totally love it. Saw a few families there and it really is very hot and humid and of more interest to adults so think about whether it is right for your family before going.

Title: A little bit of ancient history
Text: One of the ancient capitals of Sri Lanka the site is made up of three main parts, the museum, city ruins and the carved rock. The services of a good guide will greatly enhance the visit experience. Be aware that in parts of Polonnaruwa shoes will need to be removed and respectful dress is required ie no knees or shoulders on show.

Title: Great Afternoon Cycling the Ruins
Text:
We hired a bike and cycled around the ruins on a fantastic Sunday afternoon. 

Some fascinating sites and some busier than others but just hire a bike and give yourself 4 hours to enjoy the sites, make sure you take your camera!
