Its also worth checking out the museum but do this after seeing the ruins, its quieter and you can get a greater appreciation of what must have been an unbelievable city.

Title: A very large site
Text: This was an interesting visit to see a site that had remained lost in the forest for many years. Well worth thevtrip.

Title: A great ancient city
Text: This ancient city covers a large area and you need a car or a bike to get around. Highlight are the large stone carvings of the Buddha in the rocks

Title: Absolutely amazing
Text: It was very interesting to learn about the ancient culture that created these monuments. We hired a guide which was $15 I think and we had a private driver for the duration of our trip so we drove in between monuments. Highly recommended!

Title: Amazing piece of ancient history
Text: What an interesting place! I mean, its vast and we were fortunate to have our driver who ferried us between sights and our guide taking us to the best bits. It covers a huge area, you could explore for a couple of days. So interesting to see all the ruins, especially the huge Buddha statues. Just remember to remove shoes and hafs, cover shoulders and not turn your back to the Buddha statues! Take socks if youre going in the heat of the day - ouch!

Title: One of the best ancient cities.
Text: Polonnaruwa is one of the best ancient cities I have been to. It is amazing to see how they built all the Sthupas, buildings, statues.... etc. thank to those who try to protect and maintain the ancient city.

Title: Day visit
Text: Our guide took us here as part of a cultural triangle tour - medieval capital of Sri lanka - wonderful history going back 1000 years and very well presented - the history is quite superb and whilst it is quite spread (so allow plenty of time) it is well worth a long visit - ignore traders who approach you - as others have said not too busy

Title: Historical
Text:
Polonnaruwa was enlisted 1972 in UNESCO!
It was the capital of Sri Lanka from 1059-1207, it was the golden era of the time under two kings ruling! N it was most prosperity time!

Title: So many items in one place
Text: I cant do hundreds of stairs so this location was easy for me to access walk around. There are many different designs and it was very interesting to see them. Make sure you have someone with you like a guide who can explain it all to you. Just be firm snd say no to anyone who offers you help because the men at the bottom of the stairs know who to target. Prob one of my fav locations on the trip.

Title: Awe-inspiring. Must visit.
Text:
This is one of the ancient capitals of Sri Lanka, centuries old and with a number of sites contained therein. Entry is USD 25 for foreigners and USD 12.5 for children (half rate for nationals of SAARC countries). Payment can be made in USD or LKR, but change is returned in LKR only. Paying in USD is every so slightly cheaper when you do the reverse forex rate calculations. 
Upon paying the entry fee, you can enter the area and see all the various attractions. There is not a lot of information available on-site, so hiring a guide can be worthwhile. There is a museum in the building where you buy tickets, entry to which is complimentary with the Polonnaruwa tickets. However if running short of time, can skip this (which is what we did).
Since there are around 26 sites within the premises (all spread apart), it can easily take upwards of 1 whole day to see the place in its entirety and enjoy its beauty. If running short of time, you need to plan in advance and shortlist the places you want to see and first finish those (and then, time permitting see as much of the rest as possible). The Golden Quadrangle, Palace Complex and Gul Vihara are some of the places that i would recommend as must-see.
Suggest carrying a lot of water, wearing hats and covering knees.
As with most historic ruins, children and people without a sense of history will find this dull, so i would suggest they opt out (instead of paying 25 USD and then realising that they didnt appreciate the beauty of the ruins).

Title: Impressive ancient Capital
Text:
A very impressive ancient capital, definitely worth a visit.If you are in the hot season, try to avoid getting there as early as you can, because the hit was almost unbearable. Plus, since it's a sacred site, you are needed to take off you're shoes and hat so in the pick hours of the hit it can even be dangerous.
I also recommend to go there with a guide, if you can. It will add to your experience.

Title: If you are not specialist, don t go !
Text:
My girlfriend and Me paid 25$ each to see some ruines without any good explanations/pictures, who are informative and interactive. We are not specialist and it was complicated for us to visualize places and to understand the history. For an excessive price, it is a shame. 
I recommend you to walk around the site and the city and looked around ruine, it is same. With a ticket, you will only gets closer but without entertainment.

Title: TAKE A GUIDE
Text: There are many beautifull place to visit, the site is quite big and you can get lost and miss places. It can easily visited with a tuk tuk, a car is not a must.

Title: Wow... so many ruins to see
Text:
We arranged for our driver to take us to Polonnaruwa. We were going to hire bikes but as it was a scorching hot day, we opted for our driver to drop us at the key sites along the way.. perhaps a little lazy but we did get to see a lot. Drivers are allowed into the site, but not to act as guides without paying extra I think. 
The site is huge and amazing! Definitely a highlight.

Title: Nice ruins
Text: A nice place to visit, there are various different bits to see that are dotted over the site. We visited them all by car with our guide, there is the option to do it by bike but we decided against this in the heat! We saw all the main sites in a morning. Be sure to wear trousers, cover your shoulders and take off your shoes at some of the ruins. There were a lot of people trying to sell you things at certain areas.

Title: Stunning historic site
Text:
We were pleased we hired bikes - from Polo at the Cafeteria in the museum car park - to explore this interesting site. A relatively quick trip around the museum allowed us to orientate ourselves as well as get an idea how the site originally looked before we set off  along the main road before taking the turn into the site itself. 

We immediately headed north and enjoyed the less crowded Gal Vihara - awe inspiring- and Monastery area before joining the crowds at the Quadrangle and Royal Palace group. The latter was rather disappointing- we had previously strolled around the (free entry) Island Park group of ruins near the museum and found them to be more informative and certainly more comfortable. 

Allow 3-4 hours - on bikes - to explore the main site and be prepared to observe standard temple visit practices - remove shoes, hats and cover shoulders and knees - at multiple stages of the visit. Water very welcome although there are multiple vendors en route. 

We visited in August - Sri Lankan school holidays and ahead of the apparently imminent rainy season - so many parts of the site were crowded. An early start might be wise.

Title: Hard to imagine this year's ago!
Text: There is a tonne on ancient ruins along this stretch! It seems to never end! We had a guide and vehicle where we stopped and then moved further on. If you like history this is well worth a visit, our guide was very informative and it adds to the ruins to understand what was what!

Title: Amazing architecture and history
Text: We visited the major Polonnaruwa sites in a a few hours but could definitely have taken a whole day or more to see all of it. We had a driver to take us from one place to the next which was so worth it as it was very hot. The ruins were a massive culture shock to see - simply knowing they were over 1000 years old was mind blowing. Some sites you need to wear appropriate clothing (shoulders and knees covered) and you also needed to remove shoes to enter some - I recommend wearing socks when taking shoes off as the ground was very hot. A must do if youre into culture.

Title: Absolutely stunning.
Text:
Approximately $25 to get in but worth every last cent. 
Unlike places such as Angkor Wat, Polunnaruwas sites are all completely different making for a stunning day out. Ideally, do it over two days. We crammed all the top sites into one day and it was exhausting. 
We were staying in Sigiriya and negotiated a LKR5000 fee with our tuk tuk driver to pick us up from the hotel, take us to all the main sights and then drop us off back at the hotel. A great deal, considering it was a round trip of about 6 hours. 
You need to dress appropriately for Polunnaruwa. Knees and shoulders covered. And theres a lot of shoes off. Good tip to wear ankle socks as the bare stones do heat up as the day goes on. 
We saw a lot of people biking the ruins, but theres no overstating just how hot it gets out here, so I wouldnt recommend it. Youre better off in a tuk tuk. Enjoy!

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The world heritage ruins at Polonnaruwa appear to be on the list of every tour that passes through Sri Lanka's cultural triangle.  We were staying locally so could get a head start on most of the tours before they poured in.  Most people seem to cycle around the ruins and I could see why this would be attractive - it's cheap, easy and safe, and you can move between the different sites fairly quickly.  However, we were advised by a local to head to the top of the site by tuktuk then walk back to town, and I'd highly recommend this approach too - you'll get to see a lot more wildlife when you're walking, and trust me there's a lot to see if you keep your eyes open!  Saying that, you'll probably be fairly tired by the end, and make sure you take plenty of water.  The ruins comprise of a number of main sites interspersed by smaller, less-visited sites.  Be prepared for crowds at the main sites, with far fewer tourists at the smaller ones.  All are worth a visit though.  OK, this is not Angkor or Bagan, so don't expect it to be - I've been to both those and still reckon this is worth a visit if you're up in the cultural triangle.  However, I wouldn't bother staying in Polonnaruwa, I'd probably stay somewhere else - such as Dambulla - and get a tuktuk across for the day.

Title: Disappointing
Text: Having visited several similar sites in India, Cambodia etc. We found this site disappointing, but if this is your first ancient city site then you will enjoy it and then maybe visit Hampi, SiamReep, etc.

Title: Hauntingly beautiful and mysterious!....
Text:
Once an ancient capital of Sri Lanka, Polonnaruwa is a must-see on any visit to this beautiful island.  The site itself is vast, with lots of ruins of ancient stupas, temples, water gardens, monk's lodgings, moats, etc  dotted around. it must have looked somewhat like Angkor Wat in its heyday. It is also hauntingly beautiful now, and although one of the more popular tourist sites, never seems crowded because of its vast size.  Towards the end of the site are exceptional and magnificent representations of the Buddha carved in stone - standing, seated and laying down. Definitely not to be missed!... 
For me however, the most intriguing building of all at this ancient site is a very odd and out- of- place (i.e.not buddhist nor hindu ) temple that has puzzled even eminent archaeologists which bears remarkable similarity to the architecture of the pyramids of the ancient Maya.  How can that be possible?......  A real mystery!

Title: Disappointed
Text:
I expected more. The area doesn´t seem to be that large and I definitely didn´t find it as a lost city in the jungle. Main attractions were full of visitors and souvenir sellers. On the other hand I also have to admit that my disappointment arose from Polonnaruwa city itself which is very dusty, noisy and hard to find good local restaurants here.
We rented bikes just in front of the entrance for 500 LKR/pc (they didn´t want to lower their price at all). Got flat tire twice which was embarassing.

Title: Enlightening
Text: We had a guided tour around the multiple sites that was informative and interesting. Well worth a visit.

Title: Beautiful peaceful historical location
Text:
We took a tuk tuk here to take us from one area to the next, he waited between each place dropping us right by the entrance paths, it was well worth it as the area is quite large and the ruins clustered together.  Bikes were available to hire as well. Beautiful ruins, with lots of details quite different from Anurashapura.  
It was not a hectic here and you felt you had more time to absorb the atmosphere of the place

Title: Interesting experience
Text:
I visited here with a your group and we hired bikes to get between each of the ruins. This was a great experience and was much better than the lengthy walk would have been! That said check your bike over before you leave the rental area. My first bike had a flat tire so I wouldn't have got too far, so I was glad to have spotted when I did. Wear loose clothes as it was hot work under the sun.
There is lots to see and plenty of history to keen most people interested. It does get busy with tour groups and if cycling be careful on the roads as buses don't think twice about bikes!

Title: worth visiting
Text: This a very vast archeological site with many nice ruines.If you do not want to drve by car, you can rent a bike near the entrance and take your bicycle from the start to the end, a very nice way to travel and be able to go to some more remote sites, with less people around.

Title: Gorgeous!
Text: Magnificent! Past signs situated into a wonderful landscape. Our guide (from Sri Lanka) was kindly And very clever. Beautiful day between past And nature!

Title: Walk along the ruins
Text: Went for a morning stroll along the ruins. It was a pretty nice expierence. Because I went quite early it was not so crowed.but you could see the bulk of the people come in by the time I moved out of the ruins. I is worth getting up early for this one.

Title: Beautiful, recommend cycling
Text:
Many beautiful ruins, recommend using a guide though- our driver came with us and gave so many interesting facts and explanations about the ruins, carvings, history etc. (Some buildings are so destroyed, makes it easier to understand what you're looking at). 
We hired bicycles for 500Rs each, fun and easy to get around, don't have to worry about locking bikes in the complex.
 Be very careful not to take photos with your back to the Buddha statues, they are very strict!
Recommend having a quick walk through the museum where you buy your tickets, gives a good overview of what you're a out to see.

Title: Wonderful place
Text: Even though Polonaruwa is amongst the most visited places, the vastness of the coplete area disperses the masses to an extent that it is possible to feel nearly alone sometimes. We liked it very much.

Title: Definitely worth visiting
Text: We spent hours exploring the site by bicycle which is easily done and very accessible.  We thoroughly enjoyed our day here and exploring all the ruins.  Pricey entrance fee but I thought it was still worth it (US$25).  Be sure to cover your shoulders and knees.  Lots of dogs too, not that they bother you.  Wear flips flops for ease as you regularly need to remove your footwear.  Plenty of places to pick up trinkets and drinks onsite too.

Title: Fascinating and awe inspiring
Text:
Absolutely loved the ruins of this ancient city - from the monks quarters and medical block to the temple and royal palace, the stone carving is spectacular. 

Wandering around soaking up the atmosphere was spiritually invigorating.

Title: A very interesting ancient city, well worth a visit
Text: The ancient city of polonaruwa was facinating. It had many ancient stone buildings that you could walk around and many temples to go in. My tips for visiting Polonaruwa is to bring a scarf of garment to cover your bare legs as in certain areas and temples it is mandatory to cover bare legs a matter of respect.

Title: Historic World Heritage Site
Text:
Vast and overwhelming, this ancient site is best visited with an experienced guide who will give you enough information to appreciate it before blowing your mind with too many details. That is ....unless, you're an archeological geek who could spend weeks exploring this site.

Many stupas and remnants of communities abound, and one detail you can trace is the elaborate water system throughout. There is a reason that the entire area is now part of UNESCO's World Heritage sites.

Title: Great ancient ruins
Text:
Terrific for a day, only an enthusiast would need longer. 

I had pre-arranged a scooty rental with the same company doing cycle near the entrance. It was delivered to the hotel and for LKR 1,500 thought it was worth not having to pedal in heat and humidity. 

The area is well spread out and fairly busy the day I went. The strategy I used, which worked well, was to do the north then head south towards the main entrance. It seemed to beat the worst of the crowd - most buy the ticket at the musuem, use the nearby entrance and head north.

Many sites are sacred so hats and shoes off. Due to the heat I did wear shorts and really many did and it was not an issue.

Title: Interesting and atmospheric
Text: We'd missed out Polonnaruwa on previous visits to Sri Lanka because most tours don't include it in their itineraries.  I am so glad we made the effort this time.  The museum was excellent and set the scene well for our leisurely tour around the ruins.  Everything is so well kept and well organised - we bought an English guide book and our driver helped fill in the important historical background.  The park is lush and green and in many areas the jungle was just waiting to reclaim the ruins - makes for great photos!. But it was also wonderful to visit somewhere so culturally important without hordes of other tourists.  Highly recommended.  Remember that because of the number of temples visitors have to be dressed respectfully so take a sarong with you.

Title: Great historical place
Text: We started our tour from museum and ended it from Gal viharaya. Walking is not possible as the ruins are well away from each other. Cycling possible. There are plenty of cycle hire places.

Title: Fascinating visit
Text: This is a large site with the ruins spread across a wide area and so we werent sure how best to visit it, given the heat. As luck would have it our driver asked someone who turned out to be an official guide (not a scam) and told us we could drive around in our van between the main sites and walk from the car parks. Which we did and it was the best thing...also the guide was excellent (Sunil...he was involved in the restoration of the site and now does guiding in his retirement). We spent about 4 hours visiting the various sites with our guide giving very good explanations (his knowledge was vast...get him talking about the technical details of the restoration). He was also excellent at getting his timings right to avoid crowds (peak holiday season for locals). On his recommendation we visited the sites first and then as the heat really ramped up we headed into the AC cooled museum where we were wowed by the pre-restoration photos and the models of key buildings. Definitely the best order to visit and the way to travel around in the heat!

Title: A not to miss experience
Text: Towards the beginning of the 12th century AD, Polonnaruwa became the second capital of the Sinhalese. Little is left nowadays from the old capital and visiting the Archeological Park would give you an idea of the beauty and the size of the place. One can easily spend half a day just walking around, looking at the different ruins and wondering how the city must have looked like back then...

Title: Impressive remains of an ancient glory, not to be missed...
Text: In our opinion and alongside the marvelous Dambulla caves and the Sigiriya Rock Fortress/Palace, the ruins of Pollonaruwa Archeological Park are one of the most interesting remains of the island's glorious past and one of the main reasons for us coming to Sri Lanka. The park is large and you can easily spend half a day here, just walking around, looking at some beautiful remains and wonder how life must have been like and how the city must have looked like back then, in the 12th century AD. Very much worth your time..

Title: Fantastic place
Text: I really like the ruins in Polonnaruwa. It takes a about 4 hours to explore all the park and its best to go by bike. The museum is really good and all the important buildings in the park have explanation signs in English. In my eyes, its much more worth the money than the ruins in Anuradhapura.

Title: Alright
Text: It was alright but not as astonishing as expected. Good for a one-day trip, either on foot or by bike.

Title: Vast expanse of a bygone era ...
Text:
Spread over a vast expanse this archaeological park holds many wonders of a time thats lost in history. 
Not a whole lot of known about these ruins but what it has left behind are some stunning stupas and temples housing Buddha. 
We chose to walk and drive around instead of renting a bicycle and cycling around the ruins. I would visit again just to immerse in the space surrounded by lush green space.

Title: Interesting & brilliant Buddhas
Text:
Its a large site and well worth a visit although its $25 each and they DONT take cards - cash only. Lots of walking or take a bike.

Demure dress code - clothing below knees and covered shoulders. No selfies allowed!!!! Honestly. 

Quite ruined but some interesting remnants and statues. Lots of history.

The highlight is the four varying size Buddhas carved side by side  out of the same granite rock face (one is about 17m long, another 7m tall). The granite looks like it was carved yesterday not in the 12th century.

Title: Fascinating ancient city
Text: You start in the museum which gives you some perspective of the overall site and how it might have been 1000 years ago. Moving between the ruins you can imagine how the place functioned as capital and get some idea of how the people lived their lives. The four Buddha carvings in the rock are simply fantastic.

Title: Ancient city
Text: The ancient city is def worth a trip. Very very warm. Wear loose fitting clothes that cover your shoulders. Beware of the monkeys thet are easily irritated & gave my husband a stern warning by hissing at him. I would advise renting bikes it makes travelling between each ruin easier. We came across a cobra snake charmer, it just added to the atmpsphere of the area. The local sellers gently encourage you to buy postcards etc. We did not find them too aggressive. Its a great day & I would recommend a visit!

Title: Impressive ruins, worth visiting
Text:
The Archaeological Ruins date back to the time when the Capital of Sri Lankan kingdom was located there in Polonnaruwa, few centuries ago. The ruins are mostly of Buddhist and some of Hindu structures. The ruins are scattered within a area of few square Kms and are difficult to cover on foot. Tuk Tuks are available for moving between the ruins and cycles are available for hire. Entrance fee has to be paid to enter the area of the ruins. Though the structures are in ruined state, they are still impressive and indicate their glorious past. The area of the ruins are well maintained with proper passages and greenery all around.
We had hired a Tuk Tuk on the Main Road, from where the side road leads to the Ticket counter and driver, Mahinda, acted as our guide. He was quiet informative and entertaining.

Title: Erstwhile Capital of the Kingdom of Sri Lanka
Text: Second Capital of Sri Lanka was known to be located in Polonnaruwa. The remnants of the erstwhile Capital are currently existing in ruined state. Most of the ruins are located in relatively close proximity, however, a visiting all of them on foot may not be easy. The place is worth a visit and provides great opportunity for photography enthusiasts. There is ample greenery around the sites, which is quite soothing to the senses.

Title: very very impressive
Text:
a beautiful and very impressive cultural site which you should visit either with enough pre-praparation or a guide as there is tons of important and valuable information ...
go to the museum first and then visit the sites ... ENJOY!

Title: Polonnaruwa ancient city
Text:
Polonnaruwa was the 2nd capital city of Sri Lanka, built in the 11th and 12th centuries AD and is a world heritage site. There was so much to see. So much we wanted to find out. It's gets extremely hot here and there is nowhere to get shade and as you have to take your shoes off when entering the temples your feet get burnt. you can see the ruins of the Royal Palace, the Gal Viharaya  where four splendid statues of the Buddha can be seen in the Upright, Sedentary and Recumbent postures carved out of rock.
Polonnaruwa as you may be able to see the site scenes of Ancient city which can be considered as a Kingdom well run or managed with improved ways of irrigation, cultivation and the ruins denotes the spacious living of Kings with loads of entertainment in an Environmentally friendly way which is not possible now a days. One can understand the level of Engineering.

Socks are recommended when entering the temples as it can be very hot underfoot. About half way round there are toilets  those for foreigners were clean & in a reasonably good condition. There were also the aforemen-tioned refreshment stalls. There are similar facilities (albeit less clean toilets) just before the exit. Dont forget sun cream, water, and bear in mind the need to cover shoulders and knees. No sleeveless shirts or shorts.

Title: Another Historical Place
Text: Great place to be. One should visit the museum before visiting the ground location to get a clear picture how far it is spread and what is what. P.S  Be careful of the snake charmers etc.

Title: A Fascinating Site
Text: We spent about 3 hours here with an excellent guide.I normally refuse a guide but it is almost essential here.The museum at the start is a must as you see models of the site as it used to look. It is a huge site and our driver took us from place to place. Be prepared to take your shoes off endlessly which was a bit annoying as the surface was rocky at times and it was pouring with rain so we were paddling through mud as well!

Title: Interesting ancient city ruins
Text: Luckily our driver/guide was very knowledgeable about this ancient city and made the visit fascinating. Polonnaruwa covers several square kilometers and on the day we visited it was sweltering. Remember to have plenty of sunscreen, water, hats etc as there is no cover from the sun. Shoulders and knees need to be covered at some of the sites.

Title: Full of ruins... worth visiting once
Text: Ruins tell the history of that place. May be it was a planned city at once. The charges to visit this is extraorbitant. It's $15 per head if you are from SAARC countries and $30 for other people but for srilankans it's free. That too we have to go to the other side of the ruins (around 2kms) to get the tickets from the museum which in the archeological department building.

Title: Exploring the history of Sri Lanka
Text:
Start off in the museum and take in all the models that have been created and it helps your imagination when you explore the ruins. 
Would definitely recommend a guide to help explain what everything means to you.
Lots of locals desperate to sell their tourist goods to you. Make sure you barter and the nearer you get to the end the more chance you have of a lower price.
Watch out for the monkeys - dont put anything down or it will be gone. 
Spent an interested couple of hours here. Am sure you could have spent longer but this was enough for us!

Title: Lots of history.
Text: Rather impressive site and a history buff could spend days here. We had a guide which was worthwhile. Half day was enough for us with our kids in tow.

Title: Very old city but should see
Text: There are so many things to see in polonnaruwa. So many tourists are there.lots of rice plains and 2 large national parks

Title: Very best city to visit in srilanka
Text: It's very beautiful city in srilanka rounding big lake.it's rich city than anuradhapura.Very big area to visit.galvihara is wonderful and elephant safari is amazing

Title: Very important place in srilanka
Text: Amazing place to visit in polonnaruwa .don't miss this site when you are arriving in polonnaruwa you. If we can take a bike we can see all very nicely

Title: Cycling tour
Text:
My family (2 adults and 10 and 6 year old) went to visit in a very hot day 34c and strong sun. We went around the rather hot museum first which was interesting as our guide explained much to us. If you just looked without info I  not sure it would have been so greAt.

We all got bikes and were then guided on a cycle tour. It was a great way to see the sights. At times the kids got overly hot and got a bit templed  out but we enjoyed it all.  Seeing all the ancient sites was great and the the giant buddhas!

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Full of amazing ruins and lots of history.You will definitely need a guide to enjoy it at full and make sense of it.
 It's definitely worth seeing if you are interested in history and culture of Great Sri Lanka.
ou are supposed to have cover shoulders and knees, and ideally wear white or light colours(out of respect) but a lot of tourists didn't, and it was ok.

Title: A morning's pleasure
Text: Many of the sites require visitors to remove hats and shoes, so don't go in the heat of the afternoon. The palace, government and walled city are a joy to visit if you like any of the following: history, religion, architecture, geology, tradition, communal activities.

Title: Amazing Historical Area
Text:
Polonnaruwa was the former royal capital and religious center of Sri Lanka about 800 years ago. The area is an amazing array ruins from ancient temples, palaces, bathing ponds and religious buildings. 

You need to go to the museum first to purchase your entry tickets and then you can drive into the grounds and around all the historical locations.
We spent a couple of hours here just visiting all the different places and found it absolutely fascinating.

Title: Very Beautiful Peaceful City
Text:
We visited Polonnaruwa on our December vacation, 
Great place to visit. Very interesting place, and would definitely go into the museum before hand. Probably the best historic site of whole Sri Lanka,and ,by far, most popular.
We hired a tuk tuk and it took us almost 3 h to go through the whole thing.

Title: Amazing ruins
Text: Great place to visit. Lots of ruins and information. You really need some sort of transport to get around, tuk-tuk is fine. Also preferably wear socks as you will need to take off your shoes to enter some areas and the ground can be very hot and/or stony

Title: Not worth going out of your way
Text:
If youre nearby then do this, but otherwise I wouldnt bother. Its a huge site, lots to take in and a very detailed museum - if you love ruins and Buddha statues then youll love it but by this stage wed already seen plenty of both so werent that impressed. 
Avoid going in the heat of the afternoon.

Title: Very interesting place
Text:
We really loved it! A lot of history and scale for imagination! 
Great to see how civilization was developed in 4-12th century already!
Worth to take a local guide, they all speak good English.

Title: Just Wow!
Text: In almost 6 months of travel through Asia, cycling through the impressive ruins at Polonnaruwa was by far one of the best days weve had on our trip.  There was so much to see, and it was not only interesting but also really pretty.  We didnt know what to expect, but were blown away by the size and scale of this site.  Another bonus was that it wasnt particularly busy either, so we werent fighting for space with other travelers like weve experienced elsewhere.  Traveling with 3 kids under 5, its not often we are out and about for hours on end (especially in the heat), but we spent around 6 hours at this site, on and off our bikes, enjoying the ruins, laughing at monkeys and just having a great, interesting, relaxing day.  Highly recommended!

Title: Amazing day trip
Text: Rent bicycles and cycle around this amazing ancient city. So much history, beautiful temples and a vast array of wildlife. Worth stopping for a fresh coconut on route at one of the local stalls, and visiting the very furthest site if you can make it - 'Thivanka Image House'. Definite highlight of our trip so far.

Title: Intersesting relics, nice surroundings
Text: Pleasant day trip from our base in Habarana. You can get tickets from the museum, don't lose them as they are checked at various sites. The relics themselves are impressive without being spectacular. The sites are spread out over a wide area, hiring a bike is a good way to get around, there are several places in town where you can rent one, don't attempt walking. There are a few places in the park where you can get something to drink.

Title: History
Text: If you love History and to know about the ancient culture of Sri lanka, it s good to see, i did it wit ha bike in 3 and half hours. you can take all your day if you want to go by details.

Title: EXTORTIONIST SECURITY GUARDS AT THE ENTARACE, FULL OF VULTURES
Text:
The Polonnaruwa Ruins traumatised my children as they tried to cut us a foreigner price eventhough we were locals.

This discrimination between prices for foreigners and locals is already distressing, however when they terrorise my children and wife by claiming they were foreigners despite seeing our identity cards as proof of our nationality and then assualt them with personal questions even Immigration doesn't ask; this disgusting behaviour shouldn't be tolerated in 2018.

In the end they ruined my childrens holiday as they were uncomfortable with this experience due to the security guards enforcing their bigotry opinions on them; they were prejudice to judge us based on our looks than the proof shown on my identity card. They even asked for our passports (which they are not entitled to ask) and continued to try to stubbornly extort money from us. We do not reccommend this site for a good experience.

Title: Great Fun to Ride a Bike between the Ruins
Text: Amazing and fascinating place, and it was great fun to ride a bike around the area.  The bikes are outside the main entrance and are in pretty poor repair, but they got us around and we had a great time feeling like kids again (an added benefit of junky bikes is we did not have to worry about them being stolen).  The ruins themselves are amazing.  Make sure you bring along some information about what you're seeing along with a map.  If you rent bikes, make sure you remember what yours looks like (!) and hold on to your ticket - they will ask for it again when you leave.

Title: Enjoyed the history
Text:
This site covers a large area and includes a museum which you need to visit first if possible. There are various models and information that will make the visits to the actuals ruins far more informative. We visited on a Saturday which was also a religious festival so were unable to get to one area due to very large numbers of people attending the festival. Try to plan visit for a weekday as the festivals tend to be on the weekends.
Having a guide with us helped explain much more of what we were seeing and details we would have missed were explained helping to understand the history of the place. This site was 90 minutes from our hotel in Sigiriya and you need to allow at least 3 hours to travel around the different locations. As there are various temple buildings you will need to cover up and remove footwear if you want to enter those buildings .

Title: Wonderful History
Text: This site is spread over a large area and takes some time to explore fully. Walking is not really an option if you wish to see as much as possible. For this reason as well as avoiding some of the crowds it is worth arriving early.  Tickets are expensive, but given the number and quality of the many sites and to understand the history it is worth it. Hiring an informative Guide is also worth the cost to increase understanding and make the best of your time.

Title: So much to see
Text: The Polonnaruva World Heritage Site is a former royal city spread over a vast area beside the Sea of Parakrama. A mind-boggling array of shrines, temples, palace and bathing sites, some in near-perfect condition, are scattered throughout the ancient city and nearby sites. Good interpretation signs are sited at the entry points to the most significant features. Overwhelming, but definitely worth the visit. Once tickets have been purchased at the museum, cars can drive into the grounds.

Title: Well worth it
Text:
Spent 4 hours cycling the main sections of the Ancient City, but found it wasn't enough to really appreciate it in full. At least another 2 hours would have given enough time to wander the gardens and visit the museum.
 Definitely go early - the Palace and Citadel before the crowds were very evocative. Best done with sandals as many of the temples require no shoes and appropriate dress. 
Highly recommended day outing.

Title: Beautiful history
Text:
Make sure you have a guide! 

Our group-guide told very much about the history of this place. He arranged bikes to go from point to point, and told a lot.

Make sure you wear or are prepared for proper clothing

Title: Take your time to visit and start early .
Text: We loved Polonnaruwa,but wish we had more time. It is spread over few miles so take your time to visit and start early.

Title: Disappointing Pricing Yet Again
Text:
Beautiful ancient temples and city, spread over a wide area. We opted to walk but really we should have hired bikes or a tuk tuk to move around. We didnt really have long enough to do this site justice. 

Again our experience in Sri Lanka was marred by the very high prices charged for tourists. Also children are glassed as 11 and under, so with three teenage children we are forced to pay for 5 adults. Very unfair its more expensive than London. We visited Angkor Wat 2 yeas ago and it was nowhere near the price we have had to pay in Sri Lanka. The Sri Lankan Government really need to rethink their pricing system otherwise people will stop coming and that would be a shame.

Title: If you like your tourist sights ancient ...
Text: We only had three hours here; it wasnt enough time for me but it was for my husband and six year old.   We arrived at 3pm and did as much as we could -  although short it meant we avoided the worst of the heat.  The image house was a highlight not to be missed.

Title: If there is no tour guide, it would be just look a some broken rocks
Text: Suggested to pay some money for a tour guide as you should know the story behind the temples in the park. I thought it was beautiful to see the temples and this absolutely one of the  must go place when you visit Sri Lanka.

Title: Very interesting site - guide recommended
Text: We spent a day in the ruins of this ancient site, it was a fascinating experience given I had very little knowledge about the history of Sri Lanka 1,000 years ago. Our experience was definitely enhanced by an extremely knowledgable guide - without his input it would have been less of an experience as we would not have understood the different uses of the buildings and been able to visualise how this formerly thriving city would have looked in the past. Of course, this information is probably available on guide books as well but our guide was so enthusiastic and expert that he brought the city to life for us, as well as answering any other questions we had.

Title: Loved it
Text:
Keep in mind that the ticket office and the entrance are not in the same place! The tickets are a bit pricey, 4000 rupees per person (aprox 25 US$ per person). Where the ticket office is, is also the small museum where you can read about the site. Dont forget to take a map from the ticket office (it is free)! No way of getting around otherwise.
It is a huge place, and my advice is to hire a tuk tuk to drive you around from one ruin to another. I think it is the best way to explore this amazing ancient site! We hired a tuktuk from Sigiriya to take us to Polonnaruwa and around Polonnaruwa. It took us 1:45 minutes to get there from Sigiriya, and we spent another 2-3 hours exploring the ruins of the site (with a tuktuk, walking would take us the whole day). That half a day trip with a tuktuk cost us 5000 rupees. (Use your bargaining skills)
I saw you can hire a bike to explore around the ruins, but considering the sun above us, not the best option (if you want this option, take some hats and sun protection)
Most places there you will have to take you shoes off, so if your feet cannot handle heat, bring socks with you! The sand and the stone can get really hot. Also, like all buddhist holy places, keep you shoulders covered and wear longer pants.
There are a lot of vendors there where you can buy cold drinks, but a bit exspensive.
I think it is a nice trip for families, couples, friends - everyone.
You can buy nice suvenirs there like wooden elephants and Buddhas. But remember, always bargain! We bought a small wooden carved elephant- the original price was 4500 rupees, and we bought it for 1000 rupees. (Walking away after not agreeing on the price is the best method)

Title: Well worthwhile ruins
Text: We hired bikes and biked around. First get your tickets at the museum down by the canal and then walk up to the main entrance and hire bikes right outside. They are pretty old but it's mainly all flat. Entry USD25 and they were happy to take USD. Go early as it gets hot looking around. Biking helped with a breeze and places to purchase drinks along the way. Do your homework prior to your visit and have an understanding of the ruins. Also helps with knowing where you want to go. So we went in the entrance gate and looked at the ruins to the right. Then went to the far end Gal Vihara etc and worked our way back. They checked our tickets in a couple of places so keep tickets handy. Also remember to bring something to cover up and easy to remove shoes. Socks were required on the hot stones. It's definitely achievable in a half to 3/4 day depending upon how interested you are.

Title: Amazing ruins, certainly worth visiting
Text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our visit here, and the ruins are amazing. Our favourites were the Image House next to the freshly painted white stupa, and the temple with four huge carved Buddhas (including the reclining one).
Some tips to make your visit more enjoyable are:-
If you have a driver, use them to take you around the site. There is a lot of walking at each of the sites anyway, but it is so spread out that it is not possible to see everything, and even with the bicycles available for hire it would be exhausting just getting between the various ruins.
Make a priority list of what you want to see as you cant do it all.
There is very little information available at each of the ruins, so take a guidebook or print out information from the internet before you go.
Make sure to wear clothes that cover the shoulders and knees or you wont be allowed to enter some parts.
Wear shoes that are easy to get on and off as you will need to do that continuously.
Take old socks to wear as the rocks can be very hot.
Use plenty of sunscreen and take a hat and water as it can be very hot indeed.
Enjoy - an amazing place.

Title: Guide and prior interest essential
Text:
A rough rule of thumb for me in Sri Lanka is that if something is priced in rupees it will be good value, if its in US$ it will be expensive - and this is true here. This place is exceptional for what it was, not what it is - so the fact that descriptions/info/signs/directions are all absent is poor. For teenagers its only intermittently interesting and without a guide it would have been hopeless.
Worth a trip if you are keen, but if time is limited and you had to choose between, say, this and Lion Rock, Sigiriya wins hands down.

Title: History Culture
Text: Wow. This establishment is hust fascinating. All the more so if experienced by bicycle. You get the gist of the size of the place. Walking around in the history of this place is just fantastic. GO!!

Title: Definitely worth a visit
Text:
A better place to visit than Anuradhapura, if you needed to choose.

Polonnaruwa is a huge site with some well-preserved ruins scattered throughout.  You can walk, bike, tuk tuk or if you have a car and driver, you can be driven from site to site.

You will need to remove shoes at many sites and on many occasions, there is a lot of walking across hot stones dirt; take socks.

Title: Amazing ruins
Text: Was in awe of how well preserved many of the ruins are, although it seems not everyone can read the signs telling you not to walk on the walls. Definitely start early as it will take 3-4 hours and you cannot leave for a break and come back. I didnt get a guide and found that between starting at the museum, reading the signs at each location, and doing a bit of online research before hand, I got a comprehensive understanding of what everything was. I also did use a bike and think if youre used to riding and/or are reasonably fit, you will be fine. Just cover up with sun protection!

Title: One of the best thing to do when in Srilanka
Text:
I travelled here solo...from dambulla i took a bus for 1.5 hours....dont worry the scenic view is amazing.....

As a design professional this is heaven to me....others might find this boring but i find this very interesting...although all you can find here are ruins. After your tour here better finished that up with a visit in their museum before you go.

I travelled solo here and these are the tips i can give,
1. You can just rent a bike instead of tuktuk....i should have done this if only i knew that the road is good..i thought it will be just like in Bagan so i took a tuktuk.
For a bike you an rent it for 500 rupees
For a tuktuk service for 3 hours you an pay 1300-1500 good for 3

2. Much better if you carry with you snacks and a bottle of water food inside is very expensive specially if youre a tourist theres always a mark up hahha

3. Better start from the farthest to the nearest to the main gate.

4. Overall, this is recommended.

Title: Beautiful and hot
Text:
We got there as early as we could and hired bikes to get around.
It was really beautiful and I would recommend it. We loved cycling from one site to the next, seeing monkeys on the way. Definitely a must see.

Title: Lots of history!
Text:
This was an ancient capital of Sri Lanka and this vast site covers a wide area! You do need to remove your footwear in places so have a think on your footwear. Some people hired a bike, or tuk tuk to take them around or our guide dropped us off at different ones and parked. It would take you a long time to walk this site!
Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Large area to cover with amazing history
Text: Our guide told me I would need below knee shorts and a scarf to cover my shoulders to visit here. We went to the museum first and then got driven around as there is parking near collections of areas to visit. There are information boards near each site to give you the history. There are places you can buy drinks and souvenirs as you go round. It was very hot when we went but there is shade in some bits. Definitely worth a visit!

Title: Wonderous Place
Text:
Polonnaruwa is an amazing place and the obvious attraction is it's stunning archaeological site with the kings palace, library, baths, council house etc. The site is dominated by the Sacred Quadrangle with the stone book, Vatadage and Hatadage as well as numerous temples.
The site is busy in places but delightfully quiet in others and thoygh absolutely huge if you  do it all on foot, especially in the heat we experienced, it's still small enough to do in a day if you hire a bike or a guide with a car as we did. A guide is vital as you just won't get the same level of knowledge of the place  from books or display boards and you get the personal touch and knowledge of an expert.
One of the best days out I've had in many a long year. Loved the place.

Title: Absolutely Fantastic
Text:
I dont realky know where to start in trying to even sum up how fantastic and amazing this archaeological and historical gem is.
We had the most wonderful day exploring as much of the site as we could. A guide is vital as you just won't get the same level of knowledge of the place from books or display boards and the personal touch makes all the difference.
The Sacred Quadrangle is the highlight with the stunning Vatadage where the Buddha Tooth was kept, the Hatadage, the stone book and other temples.
The Royal Palace and Baths are beautiful too and we particularly loved the Royal Library and the Kings Council chamber.
The Gal Vihara statuary complex is just jaw dropping with the reclining and standing Buddha's carved into the granite rock.
As I said, the place is an absolute wonder and it's been a long, long time since alive had a more enjoyable day on holiday. 
Utterly amazing, captivating and unmissable.

Title: Go early cause of extreme heat
Text: It s a very interesting site to visit. The monuments are widespread and you can hire bikes or tuk tuk. Go early because its extremely hot during the day. Esspecially for young children

Title: Better with guide
Text: The ruins are beautiful and interesting. However I feel it would have been better if I visited with a guide who can tell more about the significance of the different places.

Title: Takes more than 3 hours
Text: Very interesting historic site. Try to go as early as you can to finish before the sun is too strong. I would not advise you go walking through the whole site because it is way too big. Our tuk-tuk driver took us through the site and kept stopping for us so we can look around. Start at the museum (where you can buy the ticket) so you get an idea of what to expect. Make sure you have lots of drinking water. I saw some people cycling through the site but I am sure it is not easy given that the roads are not paved and the site is too big and the sun is too strong. At the Buddha temple I was asked not to enter because I had bare shoulders.

Title: Really Beautiful site
Text: The site is really beautiful, well maintained, with clean surroundings. Its quite large so you better do the visit with a car or by bicycle if you are courageous because the outside temperature can be very hot. Its worth staying in Polonnaruva to discover this ancient capital.

Title: Ancient and Amazing!
Text: I was not aware of the wonderful ancient history and cultural / engineering achievements of the Sri Lankan people until I spent 3 days in the cultural triangle. One site that is a must see in the triangle is the Ancient City -- Polonnaruwa.  You will see and learn of the 1) irrigation advancements that enabled a large city and rich culture, 2) amazing ancient architecture and landscaping, 3) beautiful Buddhist statues, relics and temples, (along with some minor Hindu sites).  Would recommend 1) Hiring a UNESCO World Heritage site trained guide, 2) Biking it, 3) Wear comfy shoes, 4) Bring water, and lastly, 5) Don't skp the museum.

Title: Only if youre really bored!
Text: Visited the ancient city but all I can say that we were really disappointed, first of all they charge you almost 30 USD, for a walk in this ancient city, which I think is a ridiculously high price. There are some old ruins and statues, maybe if youre into ancient stuff you are likely to enjoy it. We were disappointed and regretted that we went there. I suggest going there if you have nothing to do with your time..and money.

Title: Second Ancient capital
Text: You should not miss the great Buddha statues and the beautiful archeological remains here. Best way to enjoy is to walk around the site. Important to wear long attire as you may not be able to enter the religious sites. Beware of doggy people saying they are from archaeology department- they tried to con us.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
The entrance is not clearly signed from the museum meaning we spent about an hour cycling around looking for it!! Worth it when we got there as the place is quite fantastic!!

Went on bikes which was a great experience, however we went in the heat of the day so perhaps a tuk tuk would have been better at this time.

Expensive entrance fee but well worth it as it is so well looked after and well preserved.

Title: Museum and ruins of secon kingdom of Srilanka
Text: All at all this is a very  big complex of one Acheological museum and ruins on three (or more) locations. It was hot and sunny day so don forget to take enough water and hut. As we are speaking of temples you must walking around them without shoes and hut/cap - good luck with that! What borought me is the fact that foreginers pay a lot-lot more for entrance than domestic.

Title: 90 of Sri Lanka history
Text:
Go straight to the museum and pay for the entrance fee on the archeological site + USD20 for the tour guide (look for Sunil). 

You start at the beginning by visiting the museum where all the statues are kept and you will have a chance to understand the whole picture of the site you are about to visit. 

We saw people riding bicycles (in hot weather!) however we went by car so if you are doing this by bike it will take longer. 

Make sure you use a Saron to cover up to your knees and ideally flip flops as in some temples you are requested to remove your shoes. Ladies may be requested to bring an scarf to cover their shoulders. 

The place is full of history and the guide takes you into that journey as he walks you through the different locations. He reminds you of some of the important learning you take from the museum visit. 

That helps to get the whole picture of it and its significance for the Sri Lanka nation in the XII century (just about the end of our Middle Age).

Title: Impressive but beware of scams
Text:
The ruins are really impressive and only really need a day. The most impressive are "Gal Vihara" or rock monastery and "Lankatilaka". We went in the afternoon/early evening and so this meant it was much cooler and probably slightly more enjoyable.

We decided to go by tuk-tuk and our driver tried to make us go with his "special price". This entailed not buying the official ticket and paying him the cash instead which he could use to "bribe" the guards. Overall he tried to convince us this would save us approximately Rs 2000. We felt really uneasy about this and declined, deciding to buy an official ticket. He then got really angry and then refused to drive us to the north site. 

We spoke to a local about this and apparently it is a really common scam and those that have gone with the "bribery" option haven't been able to get in to see some sites, particularly Gal Vihara. Our advice would be to be very clear before getting in the tuk-tuk about what is going to happen.

Title: Enjoyable and interesting day out
Text: We had a tour of the Polonnaruwa Ruins.  I would highly recommend a small vehicle taking you around so that you have relief from the heat.  There were people walking and bike riding, however my family would have struggled with the heat and distance.   My 11 year old enjoyed this tour however my 8 year found it difficult to understand and was less engaged.  As adults, we appreciated the history and were amazed at the ruins.  Recommend thongs as shoes come on and off all day and both male and female must cover up.

Title: Big site
Text: As a World Heritage site in the heat and crowded with school groups I was a bit underwhelmed. You need good info to bring this one to life a bit.

Title: As Fascinating and important as many of the more famous sites in Asia
Text: It will take time to walk around this site to take in all that is to be seen. Watch out for cars and buses and troops of school kids but patience and care will repay as there is so much to see.

Title: Spectacular ....
Text:
Oh wow ... this is truly spectacular and well worth the visit. Many temples to visit so take your time. The workmanship and skill to build these amazing structures is truly spectacular.
I strongly recommend spending at least a half a day visiting these

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Came here for the day with my partner and our three youngest.  Our guide drove us between each site but there was still a lot of walking and it was very hot - so make sure you take plenty of water and a parasol/umberella for children to shade themselves (whilst we were there we saw 2 local children faint due to the heat).  There is plenty to see and the ruins and architecture provide plenty of photo opportunities - although there was some confusion as to what you could include in your photos - we knew from visiting other areas that you must not take selfies or pictures that show you or your party with your backs to any buddas, however our guide (who was a local Sri Lankan) told us that if you stood next to a budda - ie at its side and not with your back to it  then that was fine.  However when we did this we were told off and made to delete the photos - our guide did not understand this and spoke to the man who made us delete the photos at some length and told us that this had never been an issue before - however, best advice is do not have any people in your photos wherever they are standing!! In addition, please dress respectfully. Also, there are parts where you must remove your shoes so we always carried a little pair of socks with us when visiting any of these type of places so we could pop them on as the ground was not only stony but extremely hot!  We saw a lot of people who simply had to miss out some of the areas as they could not walk on the ground in bare feet due to the heat.

Title: Historical place.
Text: This is a historical place with lots of religious and ancient architectures. Some of the precious old works unimaginable. The area was so big we had to walk everywhere and get tired. Better spend more hours to see things otherwise dry weather may make you feel exhausted.

Title: 5-star ruins but 1 star off for the cheats in the ticket office
Text: The Polonnaruwa site is as magnificent as the reviews say it is and it is a must do on your Sri Lanka trip. Don't just do the big name buildings, Royal Palace, Quadrangle and Gal Vihara though. Take the time to stroll through the huge monastery ruins between the Quadrangle and Gal Vihara and make sure you check out Lankathilaka. Make a detour too to see the only frescoes remaining on the whole site at the Tivanka Image House in the far north. The only small downside of our day was right at the beginning when we went to the museum to buy our tickets. The tickets were LKR 7950 for two. We paid with 2 x LKR 5000 notes. The tickets were handed over with an LKR 1000 note and a LKR 50 note. I waited. The ticket lady put her hand in the drawer and pulled out a stack of LKR 100 bills and started talking to me. As the conversation continued, she put her hand and the notes back in the drawer. Chat over, there was a pause."You have to give me more money," I said. She pulled her hand out of the drawer, counted out some LKR 100 bills and pushed them over. I picked them up. There were nine. "One more please", I said. She peeled one more off and laid it down. Not a word. I counted everything out again, said thank you and walked away, making a mental note to include this in my review to warn future travellers. That's it. It's still a terrific place to visit, just watch out for the short-changers at the ticket office.

Title: Excellent historical site of ancient kingdom in Sri Lanka
Text:
We stayed at Sigiri and travelled out each day to Polonnurawa and Anuradhaphura. 
Polonnurawa is certainly worth a visit. There is really a lot of history here. We came with a tour guide so we got the low down on the history.  
Again expect to pay for the admission which is around 3500 LKR ( pls check before going ) each.  This is about the same price as for Anuradhaphura . The majority of the  entrance fees go towards maintaining the site and further excavations, so you are funding a good cause.  After paying for the admission do go round the museum which is where you get the admission tickets.   The visit to the museum is worthwhile especially if you dont have a guide. It explains each monument and the history behind it.  And also the history as to why the Kings moved from   Anuradhaphura to Polonnurawa to start a second kingdom.
All the places are concentrated in one small area so walking from one to another is quite straightforward.
Polonnurawa  started in the 10th Century as the capital city  and ended around the 12th Century . 
Apparently it had lain undiscovered until British archeologists began probing in the late 19th century when the whole area was covered in forests.  When you look at the buildings do look at the surrounding trees. Their bases are about 1.5 m to 2 m above the ground of the excavations. It will have taken some serious excavations to get to the monuments.
Some places are just spectacular.  The Royal palace for one, the second is the lake or a tank as they call it.  This huge lake of 25 sq km was manually excavated in the 12th century by people and elephants.  It really is quite an awesome task. 
There are some temples which are in ruins and previously held the Scared Relic of the Tooth ( now housed in Kandy).  Just do note that the dress code applies to temple ruins as to living temples. No shorts, or crop tops and no slippers on the temple grounds ( even abandoned ones).  A few visitors were caught out and not allowed in. 
Having visited both Polonnurawa and Anuradhaphura I think if you dont have enough time then Polonnurawa is the better choice.  But if you have the time and inclination then do visit both places .

Title: too many visitors
Text: The ruins are part of the middle ages period, and in a not too terrible state of conservation, but there is just too much visitor pressure and the heat and the religious requirements -walking without shoes and not wearing hats- make it a very unpleasant experience. I happened to visit coinciding with a large tour sponsored by an insurance company (6 or 7 buses), which didn't help but this seems to be more the rule than the exception as there is no control on the number of visitors. What would have been a pleasant visit in very early morning or late in the afternoon was a pain in the late morning. I gladly endured it and would go back to Anuradhapura, which is well worth the visit -so much more to see, and so lively-, but would not come back here ever.

Title: Amazing old civilization ruins
Text: Polonnaruwa is a must visit place in Sri Lanka. It has so many ruins to visit and some of them are really huge and amazing. I suggest you have a car or tuk tuk as there is a lot to see

Title: Bogus guides
Text: Make sure you get a guide from the ticket desk or ask for id - they wear cream shirts. There are bogus guides lurking in the car park who will charge double and offer no information. Mine had a smart red shirt and drove a tuk tuk. You have been warned!

Title: Not bad but certainly not breathtaking
Text: Its not bad but a little underwhelming, particularly by comparison to places like Bagan (Myanmar) and Siem Reap (Cambodia). I was incredulous how little care seems to be taken to clear up trash - bottles and other rubbish are pervasive. As with all the ancient site museums, the Polonnaruwa one is pretty dull and not very well executed. Make sure you cycle rather than drive between spots - hot but not strenuous. Suggest wearing socks - the ground becomes quite uncomfortable to walk on during searing hot days where you have to remove your shoes.

Title: A vast area of ancient sacred places
Text: Our knowledgeable driver was our guide to this fascinating area. On the day we visited it was popular with Sri Lankan school visitors who arrived in lots of coaches. The pupils were dressed in the common white school uniforms and dresses. It was very very hot but cold drinks could be obtained from stalls near the entrances. In the sacred areas you must remove footwear so remember to wear socks to protect your feet otherwise you could be dancing on the hot stones.

Title: Bike it on a two day visit
Text: Polonaruwa is interesting only if you read about the place beforehand or maybe have a guide.  The site is big and the must see bits are scattered around.  We had car and managed to see the main attractions only.  If Im to do this differently then Id stay the whole day and do it on bike or maybe biking it two days would do better justice.

Title: So much to see
Text: The city covers such a huge area you may wish to pick and choose the bits you see. You can drive between the areas of interest or hire bikes... the latter our driver thought was hilarious due to the heat and the area we would need to cover.

Title: Structural masterpieces & True Treasures of Plonnaruwa
Text:
Polonnaruwa archaeological well preserved ruins show us grandeur of that period & artistry of that period craftsmen. It is a Unesco  world heritage site & medieval capital built by King Vijayabahu1. 
 You can visit this as a part of cultural triangle covering Anuradhapura, Mihintale, Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya & Dambulla.
It has many ruins, 
1 Entrence ticket area having museum also
2 Area near Sea of Parakrama, statue of Parakramabahu area
3 Main area having citadel ( Kings palace, Kings council chamber)
4 Quadrangle area adjacent to citadel having Atadage,Vatadage, Hatadage, Stone book, Shiva temple,Vishnu temple, Satmahal Prasada, Lankathilaka image house etc
5 Another area having Gal Vihara, Lotus pond.
Tickets- For SAARC nationals $ 12.5 or LKR 1937.5
              For other tourists $ 25 or LKR 3850.
Qualified guide is must to visit these ruins ,Charges approx LKR 1500 to 2000
Bargaining possible.
Must visit place

Title: Medieval capital & Heritage city
Text:
Polonnaruwa was royal ancient city of Kingdom of Polonnaruwa in north central province of Sri Lanka. It was first declared capital city by King Vijayabahu 1 in 1070 AD. It flourished under King Parakramabahu 1(Golden age). Its irrigation systems were superb till date supplying water to paddy fields. He built a arteficial lake called Sea of Parakrama. Nissankamalla was another great king who established matrimonial relations with south India kings leading to Hindu influence on archaeological ruins. One can experience grandeur of that period after seeing its ruins.
Guide is must to see this city.

Title: Fantastic place
Text:
This is definitely one of the places not to miss. The site is huge and you might not manage to see it all. Once you arrange your guide, you can agree which parts you will see. You can hire bikes to go round the place of course...
What stories this wonderful place can tell.

Title: A must if you stay close
Text:
You first go to the museum site to purchase your ticket, a lovely bit of history there, if you can read and love to take your time I would suggest NOT to get the guide who will hustle you and try to convince you into using him and go as far as to say dont pay me if you are dissatisfied. Dont fall for it.  Its nice to just go around read the descriptions yourself.  The whole experience will take you upto 3 hours.  Make sure to take socks, cover shoulders and legs.  You wont be allowed to wear hats and sunglasses either.  I loved it and highly recommend this to anyone! Its an ancient city and the architecture is fascinating.

Watch out for the monkeys as they will try to be cheeky and steal where they can. Loads of monkeys, wild cows and dogs live here!

Title: Huge World Heritage Site
Text: Having visited the museum first, we couldn't believe the scale of the site. We luckily had a driver to act as our guide and a nice air conditioned ride to the next place! We easily spent the entire day visiting the various sites, stopping off for lots of king coconuts and other refreshments as we went to not rush around. Some sites do ask for you to cover up and remove hats/shoes but these are clearly signed.

Title: Culture vultures
Text: Dripping with history and very well interpreted on site in English.  Cycles are useful as the sites are quite spread out.  Plentiful cold drink sellers

Title: A must see
Text: Excellent museum, great ruins pleasant gardens. Don't miss the three Buddha statues - highlight of the visit. Poured with rain so when you go take a brollie.

Title: Kings of 800 years ago
Text:
Polonnaruwa was ruled by Kings 800 years ago, when it was a thriving commercial and religious centre. Explore hundreds of ancient structures, tombs and temples, statues and stupas.  

We had our local driver drive us through these archeological monuments - stopping at sites to explore everything in detail.  We also picked up a local tour guide who gave us in-depth stories on the history of each site.  Polonnaruwa is a World Heritage Site.  

We then dropped our guide back and gave him lots of donations that I had collected from my local community at The Gap for his young family.  

You could even ride a bike through these ruins.  Especially on a hot day I wouldnt recommend walking the big area. Either local driver or bicycle.

Title: Buddhist Heritage
Text: The second buddhist kingdom in ancient sri lanka. Many intersting things to see here. Moonstones guardstones and many archiological ruins. Amaizing tour.

Title: An amazing World Heritage site - former capital of Sri Lanka
Text: Went here as part of our trip to Sri Lanka and fortunately had an excellent guide with us as this really helped when visiting this site.   The museum was an interesting start followed by a trip around the whole site.  It was truly amazing place and our guide information and explanation brought the place alive.  Clearly one has to dress appropriately and remove one's shoes in places but this shows respect and therefore is clearly not an issue.   A worthwhile place to visit and very well maintained.

Title: Stunning, serene site
Text: The many ruins are spread over a large area so our coach took us from site to site.  The moonstones and guardstones were in an excellent condition.  I stood in quiet contemplation in front of the large stone Buddhas at our last stop.  Very impressive.

Title: Suprisingly very good - recommended
Text: I was a bit sceptical to start with visiting Polonnuruwa ruins after previously been to Siem Reap (Angkor Wat) 2 yrs ago. I didnt really know what to expect probably due to my own ignorance but upon visiting with my wife & 2 young kids (8&10), I was very impressed. There are plenty of well retained ruins steeped in history. Its a really interesting bit of history. The ruins are over a large area, you can cycle around or get a guide & transport or if you have a driver use your vehicle. It would be hard to walk around due to the heat. My two daughters struggled a bit with the heat but in their defence they climbed Lion Rock earlier in the morning. I highly recommend visiting the museum to gain a little knowledge before browsing the ruins. Highly recommend visiting this site whilst in the Cultural Triangle.

Title: A city out of time
Text: Best advice is to use a bicycle to visit the area. The place is big but easy with bike and there are plenty for rent around. If you're travelling in a small group my best advice would be to do it ahead of the buses that are all going the same place at the same time. Be smart and observe first where they're going. Then you could be almost alone on the various sites. Half a day is definitely not too much for it and the beauty and peacefuness of the site is really amazing.

Title: History and Heritage at its Best!
Text:
We visited this site in early February on a fairly warm day i.e. temperature about 23 degrees. We had guide with us. The advantage of a guide is that they can help you make the most of your visit by selecting out what to see and more importantly they have the knowledge of what is inter-connected and in close proximity too. 
This is massive heritage site and you cannot explore all of it in one day so selecting out points of interest and finding them is a challenge. Best to read up about it before you arrive as that may help you select out what you think suits you best. Alternatively just meander and explore. 
There is an option to hire cycles and that could be a good way to explore the site. Whether walking or cycling or with a driver guide you will almost certainly come across structures which will amaze you. The architecture is a delight if you have not previously seen buddhist or hindu heritage sites before. One of the joys was seeing carved granite carvings in the structures which convey stories. Hindu architecture is very different from Buddhist architecture. One revers the Buddha without much reference to the animal kingdom and the other is prolific in carving animals, 'grotesque' masks and moonstones with story telling symbolisms threaded throughout the buildings and statues. One is also relatively simplistic in design while the  other is over complicated, yet they are in harmony too.
So this a site where you can marvel at the size and shapes of early structures, whether they be structures like a giant wedding cake or stupa's which are round and dome like. Another joy of visiting this place is the sense of freedom you have to explore it. However there is an obligation that visitors show extra respect for those sites with a special religious significance. This presents no problems if your address is appropriate i.e. no knees (men and women) showing and the female head is covered. However this applies only to certain special places here not all of them. This is also a site that has grass and avenues of trees to contrast with the massive  brick structures. 
Until I visited this place I never realised that bricks were being made in the 12 century and were being used to build multi storey buildings and places of worship. 
If you are not keen on heritage ruins and history you will probable not rate these sites very much. For me it was interesting, enjoyable, varied and wonderful because of it heritage. I have not previously seen a nothing quite like it on this scale despite travelling to over 20 countries.

Title: well maintained ruins
Text: the ruins are in 3 or 4 separate blocks. definitely hire a bike. a guide would be nice to unstandardised intricacies.

Title: lovely if one likes history and old architecture
Text:
hiring a cycle was interesting and probably a must and quite inexpensive. entrance fees are a little steep. you visit an old large city. English signs help in understanding some history though in retrospect a guide would have been a better option. we missed the highlight.. the sleeping buddha.
there are options of coconut water and ice lollies and water everywhere.
do wear a large hat as the sun even in February was scorching. its about an hours drive from sigriya

Title: Great place to understand the history and power of Sri Lanka
Text: Its not cheap to get in but you can easily spend hours here. We hired some functional, but quaint, bicycles to get around and needed them. Its a big site, on a par with Angkor Wat and loads to see. Lots of history, well signed buildings, be aware that many are religious relics and can only be visited in appropriate clothing and barefoot. As its so hot, socks helped. Huge number of separate sites, refreshments available around the park and decent toilets at the midpoint. Quiet and a time for reflection, worth checking muse out first.

Title: Staggering but HUGE
Text: Really give yourself a day to slowly go round this enormous range of monuments. Also wear SOCKSas in hot weather barefoot on the stones is painfully hot

Title: Stunning buildings relics
Text:
I always love seeing historical buildings. When its about religion and royalty, more is expected. This town shows great culture and history with its huge palace buildings and temple relics. You can see temples with Buddha inside and Hindu on the outside wall. 

Its temples, though only relics, you still need to remove shoes and hats before you enter the building. Walking on crude sands on bare foot on a sunny day can be torturing. Be prepared for it. Wearing socks and slip-on is a good idea.

Be careful with the locals who approach you and start to talk about the buildings and history. They will ask for tips once finishes. If you dont want this service, please dont let them talk. Cos they will not ask you if you want his service or not but just start it!

Title: Worth visiting!
Text: Must see in Sri Lanka if you wanna taste the breeze of ancient times. You will feel like in the middle of the jungle, surrounded by monkeys, deer, lizards and flocks of various species of birds. The site is huge and the best way to see it is from a bike. On our way from Dambulla, we just hopped off the bus and there was the guy, lending bikes for 800 Rupies right on the side of the main road. It took us approx. 3 hours to see the whole place and we would have spent there much more time if we were not in hurry.

Title: Really fabulous Ruined Complex.
Text:
This is a must do on any trip up into the cultural quarter of Sri Lanka.  This is a UNESO World Heritage site which in its hey day was in the 11th/12th century and was one of the most important cities in Sri Lanka.Overall it is not bad shape! There is so much to see that you should plan on spending 1/2 a day here. You can walk it but it could be quite exhausting and extremely hot and there are no shops for water etc. Hire a bike or better still an A/C car. You should hire a guide as they have a wealth of knowledge  and it will avoid you missing out on stuff. 
I suggest that you start in the museum (next to where you pay), the head  south to Potugal Hihara, then do the Royal Palace Complex, then the Quadrangle and then work you way up the site to Gal Vihara (the star of the whole show) then head a tad further north to the "Lotus Pond" and finally the Tivanka-Patamaghara ( a hidden gem).
Doing the Complex properly makes a great day!

Title: Nice and large historic site
Text:
We where guided trough most of the area and is was so large, but also interesting about the history. It was almost too much in the short time we where here so we got a bit exhausted. But wouldn't liked to missed it. The problem was our tour guide tried to squeeze to hurry up due to the bad wheater it was really poring and he didn't like the rain so much.
It would have been nice to take the time we needed but we where on a schedule unfortunatley. Nice area but I recommend you plan to spend at least 3 hours here to be able to take everything in. Museum was not that interesting.

Title: Ruins galore
Text: This was a huge area to visit and we were lucky to have a car and chauffeur to move us around and to explain a bit about the ruined temples. Some areas were difficult to walk about on and there was some confusion about where one should take off ones shoes. Sometimes the rough rocky surface deterred shoe removal anyway. A bit of information of the exhibits would have been useful but it left one with an overall impression of past greatness.

Title: A UNESCO world heritage site!
Text: This is a truly impressive site with many buildings which have been rebuilt as far as possible.  When found the site was covered in jungle and over many years has been reconstructed.
