Certain artefacts are in the museum, where there are scale models of the original buildings.  Visit this either before or after you visit the site to get a true perspective on what the site was like originally.  A guide is recommended to avoid missing the most important buildings and temples.  Socks are recommended on hot days, if you want to visit the temples!

Title: Huge site full of temples
Text: You could easily spend all day here- i'd be hiring a bike next time. We had a whistle stop tour courtesy of our guide Sampath Maragoda- superb guide from our travel company Diethelm Tours. The site is very extensive and worth spending some time exploring

Title: Angkor of Sri Lanka
Text: Probably the best historic site of whole Sri Lanka,and ,by far, most popular. It is pretty crowded but it cant spoil the beautiful ruins of this ancient city. We hired a tuk tuk and it took us almost 3 h to go through the whole thing. Highly recommended

Title: One of the major sites of historic interest in Sri Lanka
Text: This is an important UNESCO world heritage site and has been extensively rebuilt.  It is best visited with a guide.  We spent a couple of hours here, but it would have been easy spend longer.  There are several temples, where shoes have to be removed to enter - a bit of a problem on very hot days, so socks are recommended.  The buildings are quite spaced out so a car is useful.  Tickets are obtainable from the museum further down the main road.

Title: Beautiful Polonnarawu
Text:
We would highly recommend Polonnarawu (people staying at our guest house who visited both Polonnarawu and Anaradhapura found the latter disappointing in comparison).  Entry is not cheap -  25$ per person  but it is an impressive site, with well-preserved monuments and good landscaping.  It is a generally peaceful site, with a prevailing air of calm and respect.  The one exception was the completely inappropriate loud music blaring from the refreshments area half way round.  We spent around four hours there which enabled us to visit all the temples and monuments.  We spent a further 30 mins in the museum adjoining the ticket office.
Practicalities:
Polonnarawu covers a large area, so walking the whole site, which covers a large area, might be a challenge - particularly in the 30 degrees heat.  We had hired a driver for the day so he came with us into the site (entry is free for locals) and dropped us off at each of the main areas to wander around at leisure  the car a/c in between stops was very welcome!  Another option is to hire a bike outside the site, which a number of people did ( depending on where you hire bikes from the downside is that you may have to cycle for a stretch on the main road  contending with all the usual crazy Sri Lankan traffic- either at the start of the tour or end).   Socks are recommended when entering the temples as it can be very hot underfoot.  About half way round there are toilets  those for foreigners were clean & in a reasonably good condition.  There were also the aforementioned refreshment stalls.   There are similar facilities (albeit less clean toilets) just before the exit.

Title: Ruins of the country's second capital
Text: This is a World Heritage site and a must if you are in the area.  The place is large, but it is easy to walk the ground to the various sights that are all open to the public.  In some one must remove shoes.  I would suggest that one reads up about this site in advance since there is a lot to absorb.  Also you would be well prepared to ask questions to your guide as you go from one to another.

Title: Discovering Polonnaruwa
Text:
We visted this archeological site during the morning and the visit took us about 2,5 hours. 
Our driver was picking us up to transfer us from one place to another and then let the visit quicker.
This site, as any other in Sri Lanka, is definitely very expensive if compared with more important and monumental sites in other countries (Angkor Wat, Bagan, Sukothai..). Morover, no comulative ticket is possible. In many cases archeological sites or temples only accept dollars from turists and no credit card.
It was our first visit in Sri Lanka, so we decied to enrol a guide we met in front of the museum entry: 1500 rupees.
It was interesting to start the visit from the museum, where we could understand some info about the history and see pieces of stones, statues we would recall diring the visit in the outside area.
Weather wasn't good despite the dry season.

Title: Great architecture super history
Text: If there is one place you visit in Central Province this it it. The whole complex covers a vast area, wear good shoes and take plenty of water. The museum is very interesting and each of the various site have jewels in each of them. The highlight for us were the  Weijantha Prasada, Kumara Pukona and Kiri Vehera.

Title: Fascinating introduction to the area
Text:
You can go around by car or by bike & (it was raining, so we opted for the former!) as the sights are quite spread out. Its worth getting a guide here (2,000 LKRs approx at time of writing) as there is quite a bit of ground to cover & as its mostly ruins its good to have someone to bring it alive for you.
An interesting introduction to early Sri Lankan culture & Buddhism.

Title: Must See
Text: If you are into history, ancient ruins or into archaeological ruins this site is a must see and not to be missed.

Title: Amazing Ruins
Text: One of the most important ancient sites within Sri Lanka and without a doubt the most attractive place for history fans. Getting a local guide to explain the history and the ruins.

Title: Palace and Temple ruins
Text: The size and scale of these ancient ruins is immense. Suggest you use a guide for the background history and significance of this site. If you start at the museum, the archeological sites youll visit will follow the path taken through the museum. There is still a lot of work to do to uncover much of what is buried. It took us a whole morning to visit. Beware the monkeys - they are not shy in attempting to take your icy pole! The palace precinct is separate to the temple precinct and yes temple protocol is expected.

Title: Great historic kingdom ruins
Text: We visited the historic ruins of the polonnaruwa  and were not disappointed.  Although it rained throughout the day we managed to see the ruins of the former kingdom and very old Buddhist and hindu temple ruins. This area was the 2nd kingdom in Sri Lanka thousands of years ago and the ruins were discovered by the British. There is also a museum which is worth visiting.  There is an entry fee to see the ruins and its more expensive for tourists but worth it.  Allow to spend at least half a day to see everything.  A lot of the structures is still in very good condition. A must see to appreciate the rich history of Sri Lanka

Title: Great - Even in a Downpour
Text: There were unseasonably heavy rains the day we visited this site.  We recommend visiting the museum first, to get a good overview, and then the ruins.  The history and ruins were fascinating.  We enjoyed it despite walking through ankle deep water at a few points!  We went with a local guide organized by our driver and he had great information and spoke very good English.  We may have enjoyed biking the area had the weather been a bit better!

Title: A forgotten City
Text: We stumbled upon this ancient city almost by mistake. It is one of the best preserved ancient cities I have visited and I have been to a few including Pompei and Herculaneum! It is a huge layout and will need the best part of the day to visit but it is well worth it. Make sure you wear a hat as it is hot. The building and the sculptures are well preserved. The city was founded in the 10th century by thee invading Cholas but was kept as capital for future dynasties as well. The Royal Palace, the Swimming Pool, the various Veharas particularly the Gal Vihara is magnificent!

Title: Heat
Text: Great to learn about the various aspects of ancient history in Sri lanka. You can bike, walk, drive a car or hire a tuk tuk. Make sure to cover up though as it is roasting out there!! Im told by my Sri Lankan in laws that this part of Sri Lanka rarely sees rain hence the intense heat. For me the heat started to take away from it a bit cause It was so intense but I did still enjoy the historic side of it and cycling!! Cool to see but definitely recommend to go earlier in the day before heat rises too much! Also be prepared to take off shoes, hats and have your shoulders and knees covered to be able to enter and walk around the amazing temples whose infrastructure have remained largely preserved. Recommend. Three stars only because of the heat and humidity (which I know cant be helped).

Title: Fascinating history, ruins and places of worship
Text: An all-in-one stop to understand the history of early Sri Lanka. Buddhist, Sinhalese, Tamil, Hindu buildings that housed local kings and queens, their people and all that accompanied them. Sophisticated irrigation and water systems, palaces, council chambers, bathhouses and places of worship and learning. Helps to understand the traditions and cultures that shaped the country. If youre a pale skinned visitor wear hat, sunscreen and consider long sleeves.

Title: You see the real deal
Text:
I think the vibes here are a tad nicer than Anuradhapura's, but if you have time of cos go for both :)

The place is not too crowded but very hot. Most places you need to remove your shoes, so try to not go when it is scorching ... :D

Title: Must see
Text:
We really enjoyed this archeological site and spent a good few hours here. Its very impressive. Its in the jungle there are lots of monkeys, so dont bring food inside. We hired a motorcycle from Sigiriya, from Wew Thawulla Restaurant, and saw all the sites via motorcycle. Because the site is very big, some people hire a bicycle to see the place. You can also go by tuk tuk. Some drivers will try to get you to pay all fees to them, instead of the paying the park entrance fee, but know that if you do this, the money does not go towards the park for restorations, so please make the right decision and pay the entrance fee to help the conservation and maintenance for this beautiful site. 

You can park at the entrances, but when you enter each area, you must take off your shoesyou will be taking them off a lot. From Sigiriya, its a one hour drive. Costs $30 to enter site. Ticket office is not at the entrance, its around the corner.

Title: Good park - but very big
Text: The ancient town of Polinnaruwa is quiet big and u need to take car or bicycle (also hard ) - the distance between the monuments are big and need time . There are very interesting and different . At some of them its not allow for photos . Any how is good experience and history of Sri Lanka . If u dont have much time u can skip the museum on the cashier place and go direct to the park . Park is full with friendly monkeys.

Title: Amazing history
Text: For sure you need to go with a guide as the place is so spread out, we had a driver for the entire thing and it was definitely worth it. There are some information boards but not a lot and as some places are temples you need to take your shoes off and cover up. We went when it was raining heavily but it was still amazing to see the ruins

Title: Must see
Text:
Polonnaruwa was the thriving commercial and religious centre of Sri Lanka some 800 years ago. It consists of a lot of temples and religious buildings. It is UNECSO world heritage site. Before we went into the ruins of the Ancient City, we visited the Archaeological Museum (next to the ticket office). I am recommending this museum for all of tourists, after that no need for a tourist guide in to the Ancient City ( you will recognize all main buildings and tourist sites from the photos and stories in the museum). You can walk, rent a bike or go by car depends of your time and interesting. The enter ticket price is 25$/person and you can pay with US dollars. 
The best time to visit Polonnaruwa is in the morning, to avoid high temperatures and hot weather. The opening time is 7am-6:30pm daily. We spent more then 4 hours there and we really had a nice time. After touring we took a lunch in The Lake House, which is so nice place for a rest. Built in 1870 as a circuit bungalow for British Government Agents, the Old Polonnaruwa Rest House and once the Queen of Englands holiday destination in the 1960s, has now been restored and renamed as EKHO Lake House. 
Go and enjoy on this amazing place!

Title: World heritage ruins should not be missed
Text: This is an extensive world heritage classified archaeological site with a large range of very impressive ruins over a wide and carefully tended area, including ancient sunken gardens with sophisticated irrigation systems, and many remains of temples, palaces, monasteries, stupas, tombs and fortifications.  This must have been a truly glorious place in ancient times.

Title: Spectacular 10th century ruins in lush jungle setting
Text:
This is a must see UNESCO world heritage site. Well worth the price of admission, and you could spend several hours here. Fascinating history and impressive architecture for the times.  We had a car to shuttle us between locations, but the distances are not too great for walking, or rent a bicycle outside if it's not raining (it was on our visit).
We STRONGLY recommend spending 30-60 minutes at the museum where you purchase tickets to the architectural ruins. If you do this, you do not need a private guide when you are walking through the ruins, because you will recognize the main sites and there are brief placard descriptions (including in English) at the main entrance to each site.

Title: Marvellous journey and sites
Text:
You could easily spend hours upon hours here.  There is so much to see and walk around.  We travelled by car, however, you could easily get around walking.  

The sites are very well preserved for such ancient buildings.  The details are still there and in some places you can still see the white faces that would have covered the buildings.

It was a pleasure to go around with my guide and work out what everything was and try to imagine how everything would have looked in the past.

Definitely needs to be done and in great detail while here

Remember to take your shoes and hats off during all the visits to the temples, as well as covering shoulders and knees! They get very angry if you do not.

Title: Royal Ancient City, a remarkable site
Text: This archaeological site is extensive: impressive ruins, remnants of ramparts, sunken gardens, remains of temples, the Royal palace and Council Chambers, stupas, impressive tombs of varying size, a monastic hospital  site, and many steps. The site covers 35ha. and is the largest monastery complex in Polonnaruwa. Parts of the Lankatilaka Vihara still stand; two 17m high walls, each 4m thickness and adorned with impressive murals, form an aisle to a headless 14m high Buddha statue in this ancient temple. We had the services of a terrific guide, he had an encyclopedic knowledge of each structure and ruin and made our visit a rich and rewarding experience.

Title: Beautifully preserved ancient grounds
Text:
These ancient structures are so intricately made and so well preserved. For many years, nature has reclaimed the structures in Polonnaruwa. Today, only less than 40% of the old structures and artifacts have been unearthed.

We started at the museum to get a glimpse of what we can see inside. 

You can rent a bike to go around. I personally would not do it because it can get too hot and there is a lot of grounds to cover. 

Wear cool, comfortable clothes and footwear. For the footwear, aside from comfortable, wear thise that are easy to remove because you will need to remove it to enter some of the sites.

There are many animals around just walking and monding their own business - monkeys, monitor lizzards, squirrels and more. The highlight in terms of wildlife was seeing a huge herd of deers eating grass on our way to the big stupa.

Title: I loved this ancient city
Text:
I spent near on 6hrs wondering around this ancient temple city & enjoyed, no I loved every minute of it. I found it small enough to be able to walk, an opportunity to get some exercise in, and so was able to follow paths to areas that no one else considered. Most people had drivers or tuk tuks and pretty much stayed on the beaten track. The site was also quite serene & tranquil & had that air of sacredness. Thankfully there werent a whole lot of tourists about.

Polonnaruwa is apparently the best preserved & I felt rewarded & by the end felt happy enough to have paid the exorbitantly high entry fee. After touring around this site & reading forums I decided to cancel Anuradhapura, again another extremely high entry fee & a site not as well preserved. Doing both would be an overkill.

I highly recommend.

Title: An unbelievable medieval city
Text: I and My wife didnt expect our Polonnaruwa trip to be this awesome. We visited a lot of places before we returned to our hotel. From the Palace of King and Shiva Devale to our favorite Stone Book, everything was memorable. I would love to come back again!

Title: Fascinating
Text:
We visited here with a tour guide and spent approximately 4 hours exploring the temples and museum. I would definitely recommend a guide as we would have missed most of it! He was a fountain of knowledge and really added to our visit.

On the day we visited it's was 38C and I was not dressed appropriately. I would suggest light trousers, flip flops and cooling spray, and not thick trousers and trainers. The ground was also very hot on bear feet when visiting the temples, but I don't think there is any way around this!

Title: Delicious Sri Lankan buffet lunch at Maha Kithula!
Text:
Nestled in a rustic home setting in North Central Sri Lanka in the Polonnaruwa region is a gem of a restaurant called Maha Kithula. The food is not too spicy and its very hard to resist a second helping. The oh-so-hospitable owner Nadeeka offers a very delicious lunch buffet of organically farmed regional vegetables which the ever affable chef Kusuma serves with lashings of motherly love and pride. Staff with broad smiles are ever ready to help. Buffet lunch LKR950 includes as much you can eat, dessert, coffee / tea. Drinks not included. 

Opening hours:
Lunch 12pm - 4pm Buffet lunch
Dinner 6:30pm - 9:30pm A-la-Carte menu

Title: Lovely ruins
Text: Such a lovely large area with many ruins of old temples.  Take lots of water as it is extremely hot and sunny.

Title: The Pompei of Sri Lanka
Text: The site is huge. You can even hire a bike just to get round it. The city was abandoned and its location was lost n history. It got covered in jungle was wasnt rediscovered until Colonial times. Now it has been excavated, is being restored and is a UNESCO world heritage site. The best place to start is the museum which gives you an overview of the site including the huge reservoirs. It is an all day excursion,

Title: Surreal Place
Text:
We initially purchased the tickets and spent about 20 minutes inside the museum. We had our own private driver who dropped us off to each of the historical sites although I saw quite a few people cycling between the sites. I am so glad I visited the ancient city of Polonnaruwa. It was just over an hour drive from our Sigirya hotel (Aliya Resort).

The ancient buildings are not that large in scale, but they looked incredible. Some were more broken down, whereas others still maintained their structure. Personally I love history, so all this really interested me, there were quite a few tourists about but it still felt really open and relaxed. You have to cover your knees in a few places, along with taking off your shoes.

All in all, it was a really good day out, we spent about 3-4 hours in total there and dont regret a single minute.

Title: Seat of the Sinhalese Kings
Text: After the demise of Anuradhapura this City was the ancient Capital for a while in about the 12th Century. Quite a scattered site with monumental ruins in the woodland. Crazy King Parakramabahu 1 built most of it.

Title: Culture on a bike
Text:
We visited The ancient city of Polonnaruwa in early March. 

We arrived around 11am and it was not busy. We started off with the museum which we found extremely informative. We then went to start our tour. 

We hired a couple of bikes from the man across the road from the entrance. I strongly suggest any abled person do so. The ruins are spread over a reasonable distance and moving between all on a bike is not only a pleasant experience but also saves a lot of time. 

We loved our time here and spent roughly around 3.5 hours exploring. You could however take all day exploring every nook and cranny should you wish. We found some amazing locations and ruins with no other tourist around just by walking a different path to others and the main walked paths. 

So glad we took the time to visit this location.

Title: Impressive medieval city ruins
Text: Polonnaruwa was the capital of Sri Lanka from the 11th to 13th centuries. This is a large sprawling complex of city ruins and ancient temples. A bicycle or vehicle is recommended for visiting the site since it is so expansive. The ancient palace is highly impressive as is the area with the temples. Longer sleeved clothing is recommended for the temples and shoes need to be left at the entrances. There is also a section with an elegant statue of Buddha and a pond full of lotus flowers. Hydrate well and bring sun block as most sites are fully exposed to the sun.

Title: Biking
Text:
Very interesting, lots of beautiful ruins in a wooded landscape. We visited the south, central and northern part on a bicycle. 
Most locations are very busy, but Lankatilaka was quiet, which was nice.
A location you must see!

Title: Ancient Capital City
Text: Polonnaruwa was one of the past capital cities of Sri Lanka in olden days. Now it has one of the best archaeological sites in Sri Lanka which is a World Heritage listed site, which wold make other cities envious.

Title: World Heritage Site
Text:
We visited the site today independently. To enter you must first purchase your ticket through the museum $50 US which also entitles you entry to the museum. The entry to the site is about a kilometre away, you can traverse the site by a number of options - walk, bicycle or tuk-tuk. You can hire a guide to explain all of the different areas for a price if you like. Because of the distances around the site we chose to use a tuk-tuk we negotiated a price with the driver (dont pay over 2000 LKR) as we wanted him for over 4 hours. You will be overwhelmed by the history dating from the 10th century I believe. Most of the structures are in a state of disrepair but it looks as if the government is taking steps to rectify this. You may wear hats and footwear and take photographs in all places except religious shrines and monuments but this is signed to make you aware. Be aware this site can get extremely hot but there are plenty of stalls selling cold drinks as well as the usual trinkets, souvenirs,post cards etc.

There is a place just past the museum behind the Ekho Lake House called Island Park which is free to the public and contains some sites.

This World Heritage Site should not be missed.

Title: Sprawling site of Ancient Capital City
Text: One of the primary tourist sights on the Island with lots to see, plus a Museum. We were part of a tour group & had an excellent guide to talk us through our visit here. You must follow the religious site rules - no hat, covered knees & shoes off - compulsory. It would be easy to spend a full day here, but read up prior to your visit & be selective. Intriguing place.

Title: A good day trip
Text:
I hired a Tuk tuk for 5000R for a return journey from Sigiriya including waiting time. The ancient ruins which were abandoned over 700 years ago cover around 4km north to south, and there are about 6 or 7 main sites spread short distances apart from each other, but too far to walk in the baking heat, so having the Tuk Tuk was ideal. I did however see some people who had hired cycles, but it was too hot for me! It was 4525R entrance fee with the ticket office next to the museum, but there wasnt much to see and the information and presentation was quite dated. Fortunately my driver ordered the sites so I started with the smaller less impressive sites first, followed by the more impressive ones late on, including the 55 metre high red brick Rankot Vihara Dagoba and the quadrangle of Dalada Maluwa which at one point housed the Buddha tooth relic. Remember many of the sites are holy so you need to remove shoes when entering, so bring socks as walking bare foot on the stones gets hot! Also a real no no is taking pictures posing with your back to any Buddhas. 
If youve been to some of the major Buddhist archaeological sites like Ankor Wat, Bagan, Borobudur etc. you wont be blown away, but still this was very enjoyable, and you can easily spend a day seeing the full city. This was one of my favourite attractions in Sri Lanka.

Title: Exploring the ancient city by bike
Text: We enjoyed a very nice morning in the ancient city of Polonnaruwa. We rented some bikes and were able to move through the ancient city pretty quickly (unlike bus tourists). The buildings are very well preserved and very interesting. Incredible what people were able to build back in the day!

Title: Extensive
Text: What is not explained at the museum is where to go and the distances one needs to cover to see all the main ares.  The Island Gardens are just behind the museum at the back of the car park (sign says road closed).  The more extensive site is over the road and about half a mile away.  So basically if you arrive with transport make sure they stay.  Pay for your tickets ($25 / head), spend 30 minutes or so at the museum, walk to back of the car park to do first section, then take your transport to the main site and again keep them with you to drive between sites.  Do not attempt to walk the site, it's enormous and in the heat I would not recommend.  Each site is fascinating  but unless you are an architectural boffin, pace yourself and consider reading up before you go and picking areas of particular interest.  We spent over 4 hours here and were completely exhausted.

Title: Exceeded expectations
Text: The site is big. You will need to hire a car/tuk tuk/bike to go around. Be ready to spend at least a couple of hours there.  The ruins are amazingly, on par with those in Petra and Machu Picchu. Make sure you wear sandals as you will need to take off your shoes a lot to go into the sites and walk on dirt road.

Title: A lot to see in the heat
Text:
We stayed in Pol in order to see the Archaeological ruins. On our arrival day we walked round the small site  directly beside Ekho Lake side hotel where we are staying, this appears to be free of charge and was a useful introduction. The next day we bought a ticket from the main ticket centre/Museum and hired a guide. Hiring a Guide 'on-the-street' as it were is always a gamble, the first person who latched on to me appeared to speak OK English, but after asking him a few questions it was apparent that his English was not really much good. The second person who approached me claimed to have been an english language teacher and was much better - but far from perfect. I'm not sure that a guide  you pick up on the street is really worth the hassle. Ours was quite useful in the Museum, but his interest waned during the next few hours and having made enough money from me  was keen to get back to his family for the rest of Poya Day. I thought we had agreed a price, his reccollection was slightly different ( take a piece of paper, write down the agreed price and each kepe a copy!) and when it came to tips, it was OK, then he suggested I also give him something for his lunch, then he spotted that my wife had £'s in her purse and so suggested  £10 towards his air fares fund! So altogether cost about double what I thought we  had agreed - but at the end of the day wasnt really much in European Terms. You would probably be better off with a good guide book and research printed off before you went. 
The sites are fairly spread out and the entrance is about 2-3Km's from the ticket office. So you need transport (we already had a van and driver for this part of our trip), I guess that visiting all the central sites and then back to the Museum was about 5-10kms, so it's not surprising that the further you travel the less busy the sites become - and actually they are the best parts, Tivanka Image House in particular. Some hire cycles to go round the sites - I would not reccomend it in 30+ degrees unless you are very fit.
I would like to have spent more time there but  3-4 hours seemed to be the expectation of the guide and our driver. If I had wanted to visit for even 30 minutes the next day it would have cost another $50 for two of us. 
Having been to the Angkor Wat archaeological sites the previous year, there is no comparison, Angkor is much larger, much busier, much more interesting but also more expensive, but you can buy 3-day non consecutive tickets.

Title: Fossils of great kingdom
Text: Polonnaruwa is the dilapidated fossils of an old fortress with ruins of palace, residential structures, pillars and alike in a vast area of greenery. It is worth visiting to have a peed into the pages of history.

Title: Rich historical site, to travel with a guide
Text: all ruins now through the years of wear and tear. can still vaguely see the base structure the palace, it was a huge site with historical temples in place, definitely will need someone who knows the history of the place to explain, otherwise most likely you are only looking at stones and ruins which one would not understand. the site has been ruthlessly plundered and destroyed by the invaders.

Title: Lots of ruins to see
Text: You will need transport to see all parts of the site and it will take you approximately three hours to see it all. Lots of history and a guide will help. There are lots of ruins to see.

Title: Interesting and reasonably informative - useful to have a guide
Text: Interesting to explore and take in the culture. Not at all crowd and everything was very accessible. we were lucky enough to be escorted by our Guide who proved to be very informative. Various ruins do have visitor information boards in English. We were lucky enough to be accompanied by a huge Monitor Lizard roaming the grounds. A fascinating distraction from the ruins!

Title: Really interesting remains
Text: All this area is really interesting, learning about the history of Buddism and how the kings built their palaces. Learning all about cultures was well worth visiting this historical site.

Title: Very large complex
Text:
It is impossible to see all the archeological ruins on foot.  You can either hire a driver, rent a tuk tuk, or borrow a bicycle (not recommended unless you are in good shape).  The complex is very large.  Many of the roads are dusty and unpaved.  

Some of the ruins are close to the parking lots, some require a short walk.  Some of the sites require that the visitor remove their shoes and be dressed appropriately.

Do a little bit of research before your visit.

Title: Ruins but history
Text: Yes ruins, but plenty to see and undesrstand. Guide was knowledgeable and made the visit come alive.

Title: History
Text: Some great ruins accompanied by te whole story of the royal palace and parliament style building. well worth a visit, get a guide if you can for better perspective and details. fascinating place, shame it was damaged in the civil war

Title: Take your own car in
Text:
Unlike Anuradhapura where the ancient sites are dotted around the town, Polonnaruwa is contained in a fenced area several kilometres long. Weirdly the ticket office, not far from the clock tower, is tucked away in a commercial area one kilometre from the entrance gate. Why, who knows?. The site itself is too much to walk. Rent a bicycle or a tuktuk driver for the duration, about 2000rupees for 3 hours. Or for self drivers just go into the area in your car. At each of the four groupings of monuments there is a car park so its well set up for using a car. Lots of people are there with tour company drivers in cars and tuktuks, for obvious reasons to utilise tour companies, they don't publish advice that you can use your own car.
Further reviews of the different structures themselves are listed separately.

Title: Amazing Polonnaruwa!...
Text:
Polonnaruwa is amazing! My husband and I spent more then 4 hours walking around the ruins of this ancient city. We started our visit with Polonnaruwa museum and ended it with the area where was located the lying Buddha.

We had a driver who helped us because Polonnaruwa covers several square kilometers. It was a good choice considering outside was very hot and at the end we both  were exhausted... 

Dress code: shoulders and knees need to be covered.

Title: Fascinating, huge and quite spiritually moving
Text: WEAR CLOTHES THAT COVER YOUR KNEES AND SHOULDERS, particularly ladies. They will not let you in to see the temples otherwise.

Title: Enjoyment Depends on Experience With Similar Sites
Text:
Polonnaruwa is a well maintained and well enough run ancient city/archaeological site in the cultural triangle. Its very easy to get around via tuk tuk (and fairly inexpensive too) or you can go the bike route if you don't mind the heat. There are a number of sites to see but it can all be done in about three hours if you have a tuk tuk.

Visitors should be prepared for crowds of people, many of whom will ignore well placed and easy to read signs about taking off shoes and not climbing on crumbling walls. There will be people in all of your pictures as well.

Ultimately I have two different recommendations re: whether to visit:

(1) If you have never seen a similar site I would recommend going - you will be interested the whole way through. 

(2) If you have been to  multiple other sites as I have, including in Cambodia, throughout Thailand and Burma this is ok to skip. I grew bored pretty quickly and didn't see anything new/different that made it worth a special trip. If you are in the area with an afternoon to kill (as I was) there are way worse ways to spend your time but be prepared to be underwhelmed.

Title: Interesting Place - More tourist information needed
Text:
We generally enjoyed what we saw here but we found that the support provided fo tourists is very poor. We were only provided a very basic map and were then largely left to the mercy of all the local touts, tuk tuk drivers, etc.

After several 'bum steers' we eventually worked out what to do and where to go and saw some quite interesting ruins. Information provided at the ruins is generally very limited - our LP travel guide helped us to plug a few information gaps.

Overall we felt that the site management is not really well tuned into the needs of tourists and is missing out on optimising the site's tourism potential.

Title: Wonderful
Text: As a family we walked around the entire site during an afternoon, not bothering with bike hire or tuktuk, it is flat so shaded by lots of trees.  We did hire a guide who was with us for 3 hours and cost 3000 rupee - we thought it worth it.  Get your tickets at the museum first.

Title: Rent a bicycle at least
Text: Worth to see. Just note, that one object from another is far from each other, so at least rent a bicycle (app 3 eur per bike), so you can easily see all ruins. We noticed people were going by cars or busses, not sure how many costs this.

Title: Great to do on a bike
Text: Such a lovely area with lots of history! We done this on a bike. Bike rentals are outside the entrance to the park for a small fee. Recommend taking lots of water as it gets very hot.

Title: Can't be compared to other historical sites in Asia
Text:
We decided to visit to Polonnaruwa after great experiences visiting similar historical sites in Cambodia (Angkor), Indonesia (Borobudur / Prambanan) and Thailand (Sukhothai).
Polonnaruwa can't stand the comparison against any of these other sites. It's not specially nice, it's not very well conserved.
The entrance fee of $15 is very expensive compared to the other sites. Overall, disappointing.

Title: UNESCO site
Text:
We had this visit booked by our tour company and they had arranged a UNESCO guide.  Our guide was very knowledgeable and we started at the small museum before progressing to other sites.  The whole site is vast and we travelled by car between the various areas of ruins.  There are areas where you have to remove your shoes as they are religious parts but this is very much the normal at all religious sites in Sri Lanka.  I would firmly recommend having a UNESCO guide otherwise you'll miss bits and it certainly enhanced our experience here.  The ruins are very well cared for with ornate and elaborate carving of rock showing fantastic craftmanshp.

This is a a must do when visiting Sri Lanka as it helps you gain a perspective and understanding of the ancient history of a beautiful country.
Huge site well worth a visit. We had a guide and a car but people were using tuk Tula to cover the area.

Title: Interesting - make sure you do the lotus pond
Text:
Huge expense and very interesting to see.   However, after a wee while a broken brick fence/house is a broken brick fence/house (no matter how astounding).

However, don't miss the Lotus pond - as I thought it was amazing and so pretty (not full).     Near the end and you need to drive to it.

Title: Impressive site
Text: A must see tour . Beware you have to be courteous and remove shoes so make sure you are wearing easy shoes to get on and off ! But you cant randomly walk all over the ruins which seems odd. Females must cove4 shoulders and wear suitable attire to go below the knee

Title: Very Interesting
Text: Great place to visit. Very interesting place, and would definitely go into the museum before hand to explain all the details about it - make sure you cover your shoulders and knees as some ares are sacred

Title: impressive
Text: A amazing place. An UNESCO site with amazing temples in an enormous area of park land. Its worth visiting this archaeological site. This area is declared a world heritage site, well worth the visit.

Title: Another World Heritage Site?
Text:
We had a 3 hour guided tour of this ancient city provided by Walkers Tours who are the largest suppliers of Tours in SL.  Our guide and driver was extremely knowledgeable and understandable. 

The city is spread over a vast site. We saw some people using push bikes to travel between the various areas which looked hard work. An air conditioned car was much preferable!

The history here is amazing if not a little repetitive.  The highlight without doubt is the Gal Vihara - a group of 4 massive Buddha rock carvings in fantastic condition. Our favourite was the reclining Buddy although the 7m standing one was also great.

The rock carvings throughout the site are mind blowing considering the period when they were made.

Were not particularly keen on museums but the one here is worth a visit. Although you cant take photos, you can touch many of the ancient exhibits which somehow makes you feel closer to the history than our sanitised western museums!

Well worth its status as a UNESCO world heritage site

Title: Must see in Srilanka
Text:
You should stay at least one day in this city, worth it :)
The old palace of king's area is too big. The ticket office is inside archaeological museum, go there and visit museum early in the morning for about 1 hour then come back to the parking area outside the museum then on the canal road there is an entrance for palace, the whole area takes 4 hour to visit and amazing ... enjoy it :)

Title: Amazingly extensive and impressive ruins.
Text: This is is well worth seeing. There are at least 3 dynasties who erected larger and more elaborate Buddhist temples in this second capital of Sri Lanka.

Title: Vast world heritage ancient city
Text: Built in 1200 the city has so many well preserved buildings, and temples in a lovely park like surrounding. The site is enormous, and in the sultry weather is too big to see in one day. Parking is difficult. However, the history is fascinating, as are the very special features.

Title: Polonnaruwa- amazing place
Text: Polonnaruwa if your interested in history is amazing a city from 600-1300 AD then abandoned to the jungle then uncovered in the early 1900s the site is huge 2-3 miles across. I would aim to go early morning as the temple areas are no shoes and the stone floors result in fire walking the areas round the palace ,council chambers and the vatadage are amazing. The sites are so far apart we drove in between and you see loads of mounds which you know cover things but haven't been excavated yet.A An amazing place to visit.

Title: Alot of history to take in
Text:
We visited yesterday and started by visiting the museum, think you pretty much need to as there is not much info at each building on the site.
We had a tour guide who showed us the bits worth seeing and in the heat getting in and out of the air conditioned car was greatly appreciated.
The site is not used for worship anymore and some buildings have been salvaged as the site was abondoned. If you are big on history then worth a visit, not recommended to take young children

Title: Huge archeological site
Text:
The ancient capital city of Sri Lanka, it is a huge archeological site. You will need a car to visit, cause it is stretching on many kilometres. 
I recommend to have a spare pair of socks, as you will need to leave your shoes outside of the temples and the ground can be hot and with small pebbles.
The site is really well preserved and the museum is very interesting.
This was the most impressive attraction from this trip. I totally recommend!

Title: Second-class site, plus how to get there from Dambulla
Text:
As I was staying in Dambulla, I had to take a bus to visit Polonnaruwas sights. From the main street of Dambulla, there are regular buses heading towards Kaduruwela  which is an adjacent part of Polonnaruwa where the train and bus stations are located. Hopping onto any bus that is heading to Kaduruwela will get you into Polonnaruwa. 

However, it is best to tell the bus conductor to drop you off in the Old Town, which is (I think) the first main drop-off as you enter Polonnaruwa (from the direction of Dambulla). The bus journey took about 90  100 minutes, and cost 100 rupees.

After getting off the bus in the Old Town, ask around to get to the Museum -- just short walk away along a canal -- where you can buy a combined ticket for the museum and the archaeological sights. It cost 3975 rupees but is valid only for one day.

The museum gives a so-so introduction to the history of the Sri Lankan kingdoms, putting the ruins of Polonnaruwa into a larger context. Curation has room for improvement. Moreover, the airconditioning was weak and it was warm and humid inside the place.

The ticket comes with a pretty useless map. The staff know that the map is useless. So the lady advised me to take a photo of the wall-mounted map which gives clearer directions of where the ruins are situated. What's so difficult about designing and printing a new map? The fact that no one has yet done so gives you a clue about shoddy management standards.

From the museums exit, walk northwest through a small garden to the group of ruins on the shore of the lake known as Parakramabahu Samudera. Then walk east and cross the main road, to the entrance to the other section of the ruins. Your ticket will be checked again.

The ruins are in three main clusters: the lakeshore cluster (also known as the island group), the royal palace cluster and the quadrangle cluster, each about 500m from each other. But there are plenty more sites scattered a few kilometres around. Some ruins are in bad shape; the ones in the sacred quadrangle are perhaps in the best condition.

It wasnt possible to cover much more than the three main clusters in the time (a daytrip) that I had. Based on my experience, Id say that if you want to examine most of the ruins, I think you will need a much earlier start, which means staying in Polonnaruwa the night before and the night after.

I am rating his site as merely "average". Even allowing for the fact that ruins that are 800 - 1100 years old can't possibly be in good condition, when I compare it with other archaeological sites of similar vintage around the world, Polonnaruwa is not outstanding. The stone construction does not look to have been built to a high standard; the sculpture works were relatively few and not particularly good aesthetically. The fundamental reason, I suppose, is that the kingdom over which Polonnaruwa controlled was probably a smallish one (by world standards) and it might never have had the resources to build a truly great capital city. As a second-class city, today we have second-class ruins. Add to that sub-par management, lack of cafes and toilets in the sites despite the heat and great distances... and my feeling at the end of the day was a degree of dissatisfaction.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Area is very large and some quite similar so it may be wise to decide beforehand which bits you want to see. Take a sarong to cover your ankles. Our guide was very keen to quote dates and  but had a nationalist Buddhist view of the history which was inaccurate and one sided. We paid him off and finished the tour on our own. Would recommend reading a bit about the history from an impartial source before you go to get a better idea of the context.

Title: Interesting ancient city
Text:
We spent an enjoyable few hours exploring this ancient site.  We were on a bit of a tight time deadline and were torn between Polonnaruwa or Anuradhapuda, am glad we chose the former as it's a fairly compact, self contained site, with good access to all the ruins.  Yes it's not as glamorous as other countries' ancient sites, but it is of great historical and cultural significance in Sri Lanka and several of the buildings are well preserved to say they were buried beneath jungle for centuries!

There is ample parking and good visitor facilities (toilets, wash facilities, food and drink)
We travelled around by car, which was straightforward enough.  There are several services hiring out push bikes, which seemed a pleasant way of getting around.

We had a very informative guide book, which we used to navigate and inform our route round.  There are some information boards dotted around, but they don't give particularly detailed descriptions.  As with any historic site visit, there are several 'guides' hanging around offering their services, if you are without a guidebook and find a good guide I would recommend it as you will miss out on a lot of information and even miss some of the well hidden sites altogether!

You do need to remove headwear and footwear to enter a large number of the sites, so come prepared and maybe bring something to dust the gravel off your feet after.

I would highly recommend a visit here during a tour of Sri Lanka's 'cultural triangle'.

Title: do it with a guide
Text: It may not be as well known as angkor wat, but it is one of the kind in Sri Lanka. The ruins may not be very huge or majestic but with the guide explanation, you will appreciate it better.

Title: Nice ancient city
Text: A nice place to visit full of ruins of the ancient city. Due to size of the site with ruins scattered throughout the area it's advisable to rent bicycles and allow for 3 hours visit.

Title: Heavily overpriced ruins
Text:
If you been to maccu pichu, bagan and angkor wat then this will be the most disappointing site. 80% are just ruin foundation with a few poorly maintained buddist temples in place. At 25 USD for foreigers a ridiculous price. With bicycle you are done in 2.5 hr. 
Remember to wear easy to take off shoes mandatory before entering the temples. At various times you are chased down by guards wanting to see your ticket over and over or by sales guys selling some 'handicraft'. If you travel on a budget avoid.

Title: Worth a visit half day with a guide
Text: Entrance to all sites was about 18000 for 5. We had a private guide for 3000 and it was worth it as the explanations were very informative and the kids enjoyed it very much.

Title: An ancient city with a guide recommended
Text: We started of at the museum which I would recommend as we could see what the ruins once looked like with a private guide. The entrance cost 18000 for a family of 5 and takes a good several hours to go through all the inner cities, outer cities and northern cities. Great for kids to learns about civilization back in the 9th century

Title: Sprawling, fascinating series of ruins
Text: Polonnaruwa used to be the capital of Sri Lanka, for long enough that a major series of temples, palaces and other buildings were built there.  There's a decent museum summarising the history, and then you tour the site.  It's all spread over rather a large area, so you either want to do it by car, or possibly bike if you're feeling energetic.  There's a lot to see; it takes several hours to do all the main bits even quickly, and could take longer if you wanted.  But once you're in amongst the buildings, they're largely partly ruined, and there isn't a lot more than them to go around.  Whatever you do, take a pair of socks.  You can't go into the Buddhist temples with shoes on, and the paving gets scorching hot in the sun,  Definitely go to see this if you're in reach.

Title: Sri Lankan and Buddhist History
Text: This place is quite large, so you may want to hire a tuk tuk or bikes to explore the area. Many different parts to see and much history to take in. Much of it is in direct sun and you must remove your footwear, so remember your socks! Also, there is a temple there where you will need to have knees and shoulders covered. The museum is just okay.

Title: Beautiful historic site
Text:
We spent quite a number of hours with our guide here exploring the site and the magnificent monuments. 
Though not of the spectacle of Siem Riep much of it did remind me of that site and they are doing a continuing job of restoring many of the monuments.
Its well worth a visit and of walking around the museum first which gives a good insight into the broader historical context.

Title: Fascinating Sri Lankan history (remember your socks)
Text:
We did this with a guide and I think that's a must if you want to get the most from the experience. It is worth visiting the museum before walking around the ruins. It's a large site so there's a lot of walking and it probably needs at least half a day to do it justice.
Socks are essential if walking around the temples because you must remove shoes to go around/enter some of the temples and the ground is burning hot.

Title: A must see place in Polonnaruwa, Sri Lanka
Text:
A world heritage city of Polnnaruwa and nearby museum are places to visit 
The museum Is open daily from 7 am to 5.30 pm and there are tickets 
Taking photos is not permitted especially if one has ilhis back facing the Buddha. It shows disrespect.
When in the religious shrines, one should be dressed decently. 
The museum has a great collection of pottery and 
Artifacts.

Title: Don't miss
Text: Full of amazing ruins and lots of history.You will definitely need the expertise of a guide to fully marvel  make sense of the interesting  in history and culture of Sri Lanka.

Title: Must visit
Text: This ancient ruin is one of the highlights of out visit to Sri Lanka. Wandering this sacred site it is still possible to imagine what a magnificent structure this had once been. A must visit destination.

Title: GREAT RUINS TO SEE
Text: Went here as part of our tour & it was great to see this Unesco World Heritage Site which is still in very good condition considering it was built so very long ago, amazing to wonder how they built this!!!

Title: Burn your feet for 25$!
Text: The temples are okay but honestly they are way overprised when you compare them to other more significant ruins from that time. For that reason, I think, the Sri Lankan government is not doing a great job asking these exorbitant prices.

Title: Historically interesting
Text: We saw a lot (and we mean a lot) of temples plus the ruins of the Royal Palace and Chamber Council in Polonnaruwa. They were all very interesting but the 4 statues at Gal Viharaya were our favorite.

Title: Secluded site, with a pleasant walk up through the forest
Text:
We enjoyed our visit here, even in the rain!  You are free to walk up and around the forest site at your leisure.  We had a guide book with a reasonable amount of information about the site, without this we would have been lost as there are no information boards about what you are looking at and a pretty basic map at the entry lodge.

The car park and visitor facilities are rudimentary, but functional.

Worth a visit if you want to see an untouched, ancient site.

Title: Lovely way to spend an hour or two
Text: We enjoyed this place so much more than polonnaruwa - so much more relaxed, calm and much less busy. With it being in a forest, it is nice and shady too so much more comfortable walking around. Highly recommend exploring this place!

Title: Off the beaten track but worth the detour
Text:
We drove for some twenty minutes on what could have been the quietest road in Sri Lanka and the road itself became more and more narrow.  We had not seen another vehicle in ages and I was at the point of wondering "where the hell are we?" when the road jungle opened up and suddenly we were in a carpark with several other cars and about eight big buses.  Hello, Ritigala.

The site is a located in a beautiful piece of jungle, with ruined sites (foundations of ancient buildings) connected by roughly-hewn stairs.  It's a lovely walk, most uphill.  There is the most spectacular tree almost at the very top, don't miss it.

You walk back down the same stairs to return to the carpark.

Wear good walking shoes and take water.

Title: Old Buddhist Monastry
Text: We visited Ritigala in the afternoon. We were able to purchase the tickets, but we felt that we were tired and so decided to spend some time at the entrance and go back. Whilst we were driving back, we saw a huge elephant standing in our way. We stopped the car and waited as we had no other options except reversing back, but reversing all the way would have been extremely difficult as the road was not a smooth/straight one. But to our surprise, the elephant took its trunk and brought it up and down twice  (as though it was blessing us!!) and then went back into the jungle again. We waited for a bit longer to make sure that the elephant had gone inside the jungle and then drove back. This was one of the exciting moments of our trip in SriLanka.

Title: A great hike ...
Text:
Visited Ritigala today and was very impressed. It is the remains of an old forest monastry. They are no Buddha statues, merely remnants of pillars and basement but well worth a visit.
It is a pretty steep hike with most of the pathway laid with stone. There are however areas unlaid.
Strongly suggest wearing sensible walking shoes and not flipflops like me. Also be mindful that as you under the forest canopy it gets extremely hot and humid.

Title: Enjoyable forest walk & learning about Buddhist monastery
Text: Our family of five had a tour of Ritigala.  This was not as exhausting as Sigiriya.  A pleasant, easy walk with informative guide.  The children enjoyed learning about the legend of Ritigala and the guardian spirits of the mountain.

Title: Beautiful silence
Text: Off the beaten track but worth a visit. Wonderful local guide who was a wealth of information. Great viewing point from the library.

Title: Fascinating place with a guide
Text:
A little off the normal tourist track, and not that easy to get to.  We thoroughly enjoyed our visit here, it wouldn't have been quite as good without the excellent guide we had.  He was very enthusiastic and told us all about the monks and how they lived.  

I would recommend walking shoes, as at the beginning the path is uneven.  It's a lovely cool and quiet spot away from the main attractions.  

It used to be free, but now has a small charge - much less than the other government owned attractions.

Title: Cool and itrresting walk. Top notch!
Text:
Very easy walk.
Cool as its in the rainforest.
Tuk tuk is easy to get to from Habarana.
Dont need guide.
Cost us 310 rupees to get in and took photo of map.

Was getting around for about 2 hours.
Not too many tourists.

Title: Great Cooler Place
Text:
We went there in the afternoon as per hotel staff recommendation. It was a hot day but when we arrived climate changed massively, very cooler like a rain forest. Huge trees and lots of greenery.
Nice walk up to the rock/mountain through ancient Buddhist monastery. Lots of old trees and some of them are very rare. 
Little water falls and beautiful nature, kids enjoyed a lot.
The old ruins were great and surprised by the work, hospital, library and bridges. 
We have been warned by locals to take care of snakes and spiders.
If you are lucky you can buy Wood-apple on the way.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Always looking for a slightly different experience to the main touristy things and this one is perfect.  Very interesting, picturesque and quiet.  We only passed one other tourist. It seems mainly Sri Lankans frequent this place, possibly for spiritual reasons.  If you are staying in the area it does not take long to get there and expect to spend no more than 90 minutes.  Basic facilities but you really dont need much else - it speaks for itself.  Minimal entrance fee.

Title: Little gem of the area
Text: During my stay in this area, my driver told us he hadnt taken any one to Ritigala in 5 years (!) I wasnt sure what to expect however I found the place devoid of tourists (which was great). The ruins are spread over a large area that continues via a path up into the forest. Make sure you wear appropriate hiking footwear. Its really quiet unlike the other places and I thoroughly enjoyed it and would recommend it to any one who enjoys exploring tomb raider type ruins.

Title: Very Peaceful
Text: Our driver suggested visiting this place and we are so pleased he did.  It has been recently restored and is not a major attraction at the moment so go soon as it will get much busier when word gets around!  Ruins of an ancient monastery set in the hillside.  Lots of climbing initially over rocks until you get to restored pathways so not for the elderly/unfit.  The entry fee is very cheap compared to most other attractions in Sri Lanka - expect this is because it is not quite finished and facilities are very basic at the entrance.  No food or drinks and really basic toilet.  BUT well worth going!

Title: Amazing
Text:
Off the beaten track and can be overlooked by tourists but well worth going Bush to see this gem. 

It just keeps going and going and artifacts remain sprinkled around the site so you can see the functionality of each space.  

Do yourself a favour and hire a local guide.  Not only will they explain to you,  they will also show you so much more than you would find on your own. Especially the toilet system!!!

Title: Not many tourists at this place yet!
Text: You need to know where to go to find this place. You are walking through the jungle stepping up to the monastery ruins. It is different to usual temples in Sri Lanka.

Title: A mysterious, tranquil must see site in the forest
Text:
Our family visited this site after a recommendation by our driver and it proved to be one of the highlights of our month long trip around Sri Lanka. We arrived at the site around 330pm and despite being one of the hottest Aprils on record, the forest provides natural shade, so you can always head to Sigiriya early in the morning as we did and then Ritigala in the afternoon once you've had lunch and a rest.

You are provided a plan of the site when you buy your tickets, but a guide is recommended as several paths are quite hidden and there's a point at which you are forbidden to stumble into without prior permission and protection. The higher forest contains leopards, bears and elephants are never far away. That said we were still treated to plenty of wildlife around the ruins with the monkeys being our kids favourite.

We heard this site is like your own personal Indiana Jones adventure and we could see why as we had the forest all to ourselves away from the tourists. There is a tranquility about Ritigala, which we simply didn't experience anywhere else in Sri Lanka as the mysterious ruins emerge in hidden pockets around the forest. A fantastic experience, we hope to one day revisit.

Title: worth visiting
Text:
very close to where we stayed and hotel arranged our visit,.
a lot of climbing till the top but it was very comfortable climb and 
worth visiting,.

Title: Peaceful journey
Text:
We visited this place in early afternoon. This mountain range consists of four peaks of which the main one is called Ritigala Kanda.
Monks used to pray at various levels based on the degree of meditation they carried out. There are four courtyards.
It's a good walk of 1 1/2 hrs and people must wear decent walking shoes. Be prepared for occasional shower.

Title: Peaceful
Text: We visited here after walking all day in Anuradhapura which was probably a mistake as there is quite a climb.  We arrived an hour before closing and were amazed to see how many people were still there, having heard it's off the tourist trail.  However, after 10 minutes the school parties had cleared and we had the forest much to ourselves. Previous reviews basically say it all, however, on reaching the top ruin keep walking about 50 metres an there is the most beautiful tree.  Wish we had longer to explore the woods.

Title: Nice place to hike a little in the forest
Text: It is a little hard to get there because the road is not good, but is is worth it. Its a very peaceful forrest with a not too lang path through it. You don't see much animals there except monkeys, but some ruins and a nice forrest. The entry was 400 rupees, but we read about staff tryibg to trick you, so be careful.

Title: A beautiful walk in serene environment
Text: This wander through the ruins of Ritigala Monastery was a real highlight . We went quite early in the day with no one else about and this added to the serene atmosphere. Our guide was able to give us information on the various sites we came across and we really appreciated both the historical nature of the place along with its natural beauty.

Title: A leisurely walk
Text: Pleasant walk through the forest, very quiet and sadly we did not see any orchids and heard very few birds that the tour operator had promised! The history of the monastery was interesting although we were allowed to see the monks in their current environment

Title: Little visited ancient site -- why is no one here
Text: After visiting the  crowded Lion Rock the next day we came to this site - 5 visiting cars vs 500 - why? this is a magnificent well restored very historical ruin on a massive scale out in the jungle. I think one reason it's not visited is that too many people want to  "Do" S-L in 2 weeks and therefore haven't got time to visit the lesser know sites. But if you have got time you should visit. Lion rock wont take you all day, and you can come here in the afternoon rather than visiting the Tourist Trap shops

Title: Stroll through the magnificent ancient ruins like Indiana Jones.
Text:
For less than 2000/= we rented a scooter at Habarana and followed the directions to Ritigala (bascilly the A11). Right at the 14km mark, you have to turn right. It's a scenic ride along sunlit meadows of lush rice fields and through dark patches of jungle where the road is lined with giant trees.

We strolled through the magnificent ancient ruins, climbed the roughly-hewn stairs just to discover a small waterfall. We really enjoyed the spectacular feeling of a sunken city secluded in the jungle.

Don't miss the old library, there is a stunning view across the jungle. We sat down and listened to the sounds of the monkeys and elephants while the sun slowly went down and the sky turned into an flaming orange. Magical.

It's a lovely, easy 1,5 hours uphill walk. Ditch the flip-flops in favor of comfortable shoes, pack a bottle of water and jump right into this adventure.

The fee is 2$. For 10$ you can hire a guide at the entrance. Beware of the monkeys, they might look cute - but they will steal your food!

Title: Good option; good guide
Text: We spent a very interesting half day hiking up the mountain through the monastery ruins.  The hike was great and getting history of the monestaries gave us better insight inot other aspects of what we were seeing in the Cultural Triangle.  We used a guide, Manjoo provided by Sri Lanka in Style tours, who was excellent and also offers tours of neighboring ruins by bicycle.  We highly recommend him.

Title: Charming place
Text:
As we drove towards Ritigala we were flagged down by a man wanting to be our guide he offered a good price, 1200rs, so we agreed and were very pleased with him.  He spoke good English, the children liked him, and we walked us round at a comfortable place and was happy to allow us to linger.  Heaps of history here that had been hidden by the jungle.  Lovely to see and imagine what it would have been like as a monastery.

We had a really good visit and think it was well worth coming.

Title: Lovely little archaeological site/hike
Text:
Nice little hike in the jungle, with monkeys overhead, looking at archaeological ruins. The walk is not tough, and the path is well maintained. Definitely look for the side path that takes you to the ruined library, which has excellent views.

You don't need a guide, as the path is clearly defined, however there are no information boards to tell you what the ruins are, although the ticket office has a guide book I think- our tuk tuk driver kindly leant us one, so we knew what we were looking at.

The entrance price is currently LKR 300, and we got a tuk tuk to/from Habarana with waiting time for LKR1800.

Title: Ancient Buddhist monastery
Text: No need for guide. Many local people ask you to be your guide because you might get lost, but the road is very clearly indicated and there is no way you loose your track unless you want. Local visitors never take guide.

Title: Must see
Text: One of the best places to go in Sri Lanka. No people, quiet place with mystery atmosphere. Beautiful. Strongly recommended!

Title: Interesting hill hike in the cool forest land
Text: Worth a trip to visit this ancient monument.  Uneven ground, so full shoes / trainers advised.  A guide is not required.  Atmospheric walk and interesting ruins to view.

Title: Enjoyed the jungle walk
Text: Not far from Habarana. We got a jeep for 2500 rupees between 4 people. An interesting walk through the forest. The ruins are not very extensive, but worth a morning trip.

Title: Walk in the forrest
Text: We walked about 1km before we were confronted by some aggressive monkeys and we had to turn back. We then got at guide (1000lkr) to take us all the way to the top. The monkeys were gone by then but the guide told os many interesting facts and took us a bit off road. The guard told os that only around 5 foreigners entered these woods during the off season which meant that we were all alone for 2 hours.

Title: Worth seeing
Text: Lovely forest walk, if you are lucky you can see monks in their traditional orange outfits. Very calming

Title: Loved this place!
Text: This is a special place---a group of ruins with a "jungle feel."  It is off the beaten path and does not receive the volume of visitors other sites experience.  The entry fee is much less than other cultural sites (~300 rps), and the site, itself, is not as well restored.  However, if you want an experience that feels more remote and "in the jungle," check out this hidden jewel.  It is a short hike, mostly on a rock sewn pathway, but I would still recommend that light hikers or tennis shoes be worn to access the ruins.  Be sure to continue off the rock path at the end to see the huge old tree.  It is amazing!

Title: Amazing!
Text: Me and my girlfriend did this beautiful walk solo without a guide, it was one of the most breathtaking treks I did my whole time in Sri Lanka. Lush jungle, not too tiring but with some exciting elements. Easy and very memorable.

Title: Religious Mystery
Text: Ritigala is the site of the ruins of a Buddhist sect of which not a great deal is known except that they lived a strict meditative lifestyle. One can imagine how it must have looked hidden on the side of a remote mountain and dream of what life must have been like then.

Title: Ancient place with great history
Text:
Carrying a history of thousands of years.... some sources said that goes back to the era of great king RAWANA who mentioned in Ramayana....

Once a monastery and once a natural fortress.....

Title: Buddhism, Ramayanaya, Nature, Yakkhas (Devils), Medicinal herbs
Text:
One of the must see nature reserves in Sri Lanka located just 50 kms away from Historic Dambulla. This place is mentioned in both Mahawamsa (one of the oldest and sacred books in Sri Lanka) and in Ramayana trail of Walmiki (India). If you hire a local guide he will tell you the story of the fight between two tribal leaders (Gotaimbara & Jayasena) and how Jayasena became Mahasona (a Devil) after beheaded by Gotaimbara.
Most importantly, although Ritigala is located in the Dry Zone in Sri Lanka, it has a unique climatic pattern that changes when you hike further and further.
Excellent for bird watching during the morning hours.

Title: Special place
Text:
This monastery in the middle of the jungle is special. All are ruins, but with some imagination it is easy to imagine monks lived there. Like in Sigiriya, the irrigation engineering and various tanks are interesting.

It is basically one path uphill, with various buildings around it.

Tip: Visit the library, great views from there.

Title: Beautiful, serene, ancient site
Text:
Our driver had no knowledge of Ritigala, so when a local rice farmer flagged our car down at the crossroads near the mountain and offered his services as a guide, we said yes. He turned out to be the most brilliant guide - full of facts and information about the ruins and beautiful, unusual trees, and able to describe in vivid detail how the community of monks would have lived, meditated and operated an ayurvedic hospital at Ritigala. When they came to establish Sri Lanka's first monastery there, the monks apparently brought plant species from the Himalayas and some of these still grow on the mountain, uniquely for SL. 

The road approaching Ritigala is stunning, and there were only a couple of other visitors when we were there. Our children, who experienced extreme temple fatigue at various other sites, loved Ritigala for its Indiana Jonesy atmosphere. 

It's an extraordinary place: 2000-year-old Ebony trees, rare types of monkey, an ancient library overlooking spectacular views, and an extremely well preserved system of walk ways, pools, and peaceful prayer places... well worth a visit.

Give a donation - there's no ticket charge.

Title: No tourists, very Raiders of the Lost Ark
Text: Great experience wandering along the old pavement through the ruined temples in the jungle - when we visited there was not another soul there bar the monkeys.

Title: excellent de tour from habarana
Text: this a fantastic place,i have been many time there in the rainy season you can see small water fall also,calm relax place , the ruins are belongs to 3rd century bc,as its monastery old days ,even yuu go now, you still feel the same atmospherics situation

Title: Solitude in the forest.
Text: We visited this place during the afternoon so it was a bit hot, but it's mostly shady. The paths are charming and the ruins pretty cool. They aren't super super impressive but it is a good walk through the forest, although our tuk tuk driver went with us, his English was not good so a proper guide would be better if you're really into the history of the area.

Title: A work in progress
Text: Undergoing excavation,it is still disclosing its secrets,albeit slowly.A guide helps explain the site and puts things in perspective.A little esoteric but worth a small detour to visit

Title: Trek through forest
Text:
I was totally confused before we embarked to ritigala from Habarna. It was a half hour drive. There are two areas there meditation center and ruins.

The meditation center falls before and there is a 2 km drive through dirt road. We didn't do that.

We went ahead and went past the information center to the car park area. From there we started our trek. The path is well defined. There are steps which can be easily climbed.

Walking with nature around was lovely. Yoy can see ruins of various sites in between. There are hardly anyone there.

We didn't find any streams as others have mentioned. We weren't sure how far we are supposed to go. Nevertheless we enjoyed.

The entire walk took us 1.5 hours both ways.

Title: History in the jungle
Text: A wonderful place to explore. We had a local guide organised by our driver who was very informative about the monastery and its history. It is a wonderful, quiet place to walk in but it does require a reasonable level of agility to deal with the uneven surfaces which are probably also slippery after rain.  The old majestic trees are splendid and the birdsong delightful. It is easy to imagine that this was a suitable place for the contemplative life.

Title: Great get away from the crowds
Text:
We took at Tuk Tuk from Sigiriya and what a find. It was quiet seen deer, monkies.

It was one best days out we enjoyed the place do yourself a favour go and explore

Title: Hidden gem
Text:
Hidden treasure in the jungle - amazing ancient ruins. 

Steep terrain but worth the trek into the jungle, amazing amount of the ruins in tact. 

A guide is an must for the formidable area and also to explain the ruins too you. 

Decent walking shoes advised - water and hat.

Title: Great trip
Text: A great morning out. A hidden gem hardly visited by tourists. Very peaceful place to visit. No crowds. Free entry. An absolutely magical experience

Title: You might even find yourselves there alone!
Text: A remote temple in the middle of the forest/jungle. Not many visitors. Fantastic jungle ruins well worht seeing

Title: Totally Worth It!
Text:
Rittigala was one of the most memorable historical sites we visited in the country thanks largely to its feeling of isolation and peace that swells from the history of this monastery that was left to the jungle some 1,000 years ago and the fact that it is well removed from the tourist hordes as my wife and I only ran into another 5 travelers during our time exploring this amazing place.

Much of the ruins are simply the foundations, columns, and pathways that led around this once massive monastery, but for those people who have an imagination, love nature, and want to get off the beaten path this place is perfect.

Be advised, you will need to have your own car or hire a tuk tuk to reach this place as the site is located on a dirt track 8 km north of the Habanara Highway. It is generally open from 7:30-18h with no fee, but they can ask for donations at times.

Aside from the paved walkways, visitors should be advised that it is possible to bathe in the waterfalls and if you find the dirt path just downhill from there, be sure to visit the remains of the library, which in our minds was one of the best highlights of our trip

Title: It worth the visit
Text: I really like this place hide in the forest. We were alone visiting it!. Even though we had our own car and driver we took one of the tuk-tuks down in the main road. The tuk-tuk driver Sukat knows very well the ruins and the surroundings as he lives nearby. He is a nice guy.

Title: beautifully unkempt
Text: Old carvings, ancient rock caves, flowering cacti, along with pheasants, kingfishers, turtles and skinks, this was just heavenly. We didn't see another person the whole time we wandered (but then we also didn't see the etching of the headless man we read about). No maps and very few signboards added to the feeling of emptiness and mystery. Worth a pit stop between Colombo and Anuradhapura.

Title: Your own discovery adventure in the forest
Text: Not many other tourists. We liked it a lot. Beautiful walk through the forest with all these huge finds from the past. Highly recommended when in the area

Title: Great place to explore , off the beaten track, so you will have a peaceful day.
Text: Most ancient sites in Sri Lanka are known to everybody so tend to be crowded during the tourist season.  Ritigala site is off the main tourist route, so its quiet and peaceful.  Its a two Km long path slowly rising up the Ritigala mountains so one need at least half a day to explore.  Views are fantastic from the top and the ruins all along the track.

Title: Wear stout shoes or boots
Text:
This is a magical experience, the partial restoration tells stories and the mysteries still remain. It is almost unvisited which makes discovering it all the better. It is an extraordinary achievement to have built in stone such a complex which was home to so many. You can really appreciate how the jungle took over whilst it was abandoned, even some of the restoration is being encroached upon by the jungle. Find the library, it is a sublimely peaceful place with a breathtaking view.

This is not a suitable visit for small children or the very unfit, but it was one of our best and most alone moments in Sri Lanka. If you do it without a guide then get some good information about it to understand it better. Also if you are self-driving as we were, be aware that your GPS may take you to the current Ritigala monastery, a fascinating place and not at all easily accessible. A lot of apologetic smiling and bowing later we found the ruins on the other side of the mountain.

Title: Unspoilt
Text:
A new road makes access easier than it was a few years ago now a 15 minute tuk tuk ride from the main road.
Entry is free, guide essential. With guide we rambled through the forest visiting the King's bathing pool, one of the monk's caves, a 3rd century BC toilet and a 1,000 year old tree amongst the ruins.
We were there about 2.5 hours.
Most interesting. Suggest you wear long trousers (a few mosquitoes) and stout footwear.

Title: Magical walk through the forest
Text: Really enjoyed climbing through the jungle to access Ritigala site - very beautiful and hardly anyone else.

Title: Total beauty
Text: This place just resonates peace and tranquility. The walk is picturesque and when you reach the top there is a beautiful little steam to cool your feet off in. Which is ideal because it is pretty hot and humid. One little warning, beware of the little leeches, wear insect repellant...

Title: Amazing!
Text:
Great place, nature and ruins are incredible, you can easily spent half a day exploring the ruins in the jungle ! (... in theory, you do not have to exit the patch. In theory...)

Transport to this place is complicated, you can get closer but bus, but you will have to take a tuktuk for the last km.

Title: Could be better
