Text: Difficult to get to - We arrived with our driver at the faded and unused 'visitor centre' where we had to transfer to a tuk-tuk as the track was too muddy for vehicles. We came here as it sounded interesting in the lonely planet description but it wasn't that great. The part you can access (the rest is a protected area) has been part restored and there are some paths relaid. There is a fair bit of scrambling to do though which makes it more exciting but there is little to see here really and even the 'carved urinal' was a bit disappointing. Visit if you are passing but don't go out of your way.

Title: well worth it if you have time
Text: We arranged to visit here with our tour guide, so was driven in a jeep there.  We visited on a Sunday and there was no one else there.  It is govt run and a donation is asked for, we gave 500 each, which was incredibly good value for money.  We spent around 2 hours wandering about, at a nice steady pace.  Some of it is uphill but not too taxing.  There is a tank, ruins, arches, a blood tree, queens toilet, executioners block - all in a jungle setting.  It is tranquil, you can hear the birds singing, waterfalls, frogs etc.  Lots of unusual rock formations and large trees.  The hills surrounding were swathed in clouds.  Lots of photo opps and by the time we had left we saw 3 other tourists.  Shame about the scabby dogs but they were everywhere in SL.  Would definitely recommend if you have time to visit.

Title: Peace and Tranquility
Text:
We arrived after the monks had their meal and was offered food, but we declined. Loads of village people were coming in to enjoy a free meal.
We walked up the 200 steps or I walked up the path which ran next to the steps. At the top in this forest setting was a peacful stupa area. You can just sit or do a meditation in this tranquil setting.

Title: Excellent Countryside
Text: Must visit. Lovely countryside. You have to see visit as to see the true nature of Sri Lanka. It is very important if you a Buddhist too.

Title: Mysterious
Text: Amazing atmospheric temple complex, buried into some truly deep jungle, get a local Tuk Tuk driver to take you there.

Title: Nice track although not too long
Text:
You'll have to conquer a bit of bad road to get there. 
Our visit however was quite nice. It's a short track, climbing smoothly and it's a nice place in general. According to our travel book, in the past you could climb to the top and there was an entrance fee, but this is old information as you are not allowed anymore to climb further into the jungle.
Visit is free and you are expected to give something. The guy at the entrance did not seem that happy with our 1000 rupees, although in my opinion it's enough.

Title: Unique experience in the jungle
Text: As others have said, Ritigala does have a bit of an Indiana Jones feel to it, although pretty much all that's left is the foundations of buildings and walk paths. I was the first one there in the morning (at 9am), so I had the whole place free to myself to walk around. A couple of groups came after me, but I only saw them on the way out. I was able to get a tuk tuk driver to take me there and back for 1,000 LKR, which also included him walking me around the site. The staff informed me right away that it was a donation to enter, and did not try to trick me into paying anything as others experienced. I spent a couple of hours there, and really enjoyed it. I would definitely recommend it for anyone who is interested in getting away from the crowds for a bit and seeing some decent ruins and massive trees.

Title: Great jungle treck a la Indiana Jones
Text:
Practical info: you can GET HERE from Habarana by bus, get off at Ritigala. You will see a sing pointing the direction to the ruins. According to tthe sign it's 9 km. Away. That's why there will be tuk tuk drivers waiting there. They want 1500 LKR (after Bargaining) two ways. The only thing is that They want you to do the treck in an hour while you can easily spend 3 hours there.
The ENTRANCE FEE is an obligatory donation, you will pay it in a small office at the entrance . Don't let the tuk tuk driver see how much you donate. 
After that you can enjoy yourself exploring the area. Don't be afraid to leave the path and explore also sideways. That's how we found a lookout called the Fort. A nice place to have breakfast. 
If you sit there for some time you will see rare birds which come there to drink water.
When you will get to the top of the path after seeing a few ruins you will see the sign of a restricted reserve area. Big rare langurs live there. They are called "bear monkeys". We were able to See two of them close to the border of their area.
Don't forget to bring mosquito repellent.

Title: Hidden Ruins
Text:
Having been intrigued by pictures of this place we decided to make the trip out here to see the ruins.  We took a bus bound for Anuradhapura and got off at the Ritigala Junction.  From there we took a tuk-tuk.  This felt like a rip-off as the driver ended up charging us 1300 rs.  I could tell we were paying a good rate as he was smiling for the whole trip.  Anyhow once you start up the trail to the ruins you will forget about any tuk-tuk negotiations.  At the site we were told there was an entrance fee of (I want to say) 1300 rs. each, which we balked at.  We were then asked to make a donation of 500 rs. each which seemed more reasonable. 

There was no one else on the trails and we had plenty of time to explore the various ruins.  There were small offshoots at some of the trails where there were some significant additional ruins.  Make sure you've got an hour or two to explore everything.  Highly recommended if you are down with photography.

Title: Hidden wonder
Text: While the climb was a bit gruelling in the heat, Ritigala was well worth it. We chanced upon a guide, which was a good thing, as he could tell us what each ruin was. The water tank and stairs are remarkably well-preserved. Be sure to wear good shoes and carry mosquito repellent.

Title: You might be the only tourist there!
Text:
Me and my girlfriend went there on our motorbike. It was personally one of my best visits in 4 weeks in Sri Lanka. Unlike ancient ruins like Polonnawura where theres a lot to see but also so many tourists and you feel like in a museum, this place lets you explore as you are ALL BY YOURSELF. All we saw was the guy at the entrance, 4 dogs and another couple.

Theres a main track that you can follow up and down and see a few site, but the fun begins when you look around, in the forest, and try to look for ruins.

Look in the jungle for the faint tracks leading to sites or the big stone sticks, hinting that something cool is around. On our way down we realize there was so much to discover outside the beaten track. Everytime I went deeper in the forest I found another cool thing, remains of a praying site, mysterious grottos, name it.

Sites arent as impressive as the other touristic ruins, but the fact that youre discovering them yourselves and that youre all alone really adds to the experience.

You really do feel like Indiana Jones! The entrance is free (but a volontary donation is asked) and a bit hard to find.

Title: almost indiana jones!
Text:
Great jungle ruins, quiet with few visitors adding to the experience as monkeys scream in the tree tops, and lizards scuttle across the ruins.  A bit too dry to feel really Indiana Jones, children had been hoping for king Louis from the jungle book!  But they still described it as awesome.
Entrance was donations, no guide pushed on us so we were free to wander for a couple of hours.
Amazing granite blocks, how did they do it?  Worth detouring of the paved path to find the lookout fort, which was the highlight for us.
Very basic toilets.  Take water.

Title: Nice hidden site
Text:
Ritigala is a nice site, quite different from Polonawura and Adurnarhupa. The site is in the jungle, with a few temple ruins to visit, and deserves a trip if you're around.
However, the site should should be free, but the people of archeological department asked us to pay 10$/person to come in (of course without any receipt...). Our guide even went at the end to take his commission.

Title: Nice forest few tourists
Text: Went to Pidurangala rock and Ritigala ruins by tuc tuc from Habarana, was a nice trip. The forest was nice, some big impressive trees making for nice photos, not many or really amazing ruins, there is no official entrance fee, leave a donation at your own discretion. Nice walk, worth the hour or so stop if you go to Lion Rock or Pidurangala rock.

Title: Quiet and peaceful walk in the jungle
Text: The ruins are not particularly breat taking, but it was enjoyable walk through the jungle. I also foun the ruins intriguing even though they were not very massive or spectacular. There were only a couple of tourists so itwas possible to explore the ruins in peace and silence and spot lizards and monkeys. Felt a little like Indiana Jones :). It was very clean, no trash around. There is no admission fee but a donation is expected, we donated 1000 rupees each.

Title: Quite a route march in the heat!
Text: This was a lovely - if somewhat demanding - climb through the jungle to see ancient monastic ruins. Very enjoyable however, with knowledgable guide.

Title: Great walk
Text: This was a great walk up through rainforest to ancient Buddhist monastic ruins. The forest was lovely and we got to see plenty of wildlife. The walk up is reasonably strenuous but worth the effort. The ruins themselves are not extensive and there is a lot to see but they are very interesting in their own right.

Title: Pleasant walk in the forest, that's about it.
Text:
On reading some of the reviews of Ritigala on TripAdvisor, I was expecting some kind of Indiana Jones-esque ancient ruin in the jungle.  It's not.  

As we had already used half a day in a Sigiriya visit, my partner and I decided to take a trip to nearby Ritigala during our final day in the Habarana area.  Our driver took us as far as he dared and we then clambered aboard the the tuk tuk that had followed us from Habarana (on reflection, we should have just got the tuk tuk from there).   After a short ride along a bumpy dirt track, we arrived at a few scruffy buildings and were ushered inside one to sign the visitor book and also pay the 'donation' fee of 500Rs each.   can't complain about the 500Rs as that is pretty much pocket change to most westerners.  From there we were offered a tour guide to which we declined as we preferred just to explore ourselves.  

The ruins are not impressive at all - they don't seem particularly ancient.  If you've been anywhere there are some impressive ruins  - e.g. Pompeii, Athens or Latin America, you might even walk past the Ritigala ruins assuming that the real ruins are further on.  Well, they aren't.   When you reach a point where there's a square with some old building foundations, the rest of the path is blocked off - apparently it's because of the risk from dangerous wildlife (snakes, scorpions etc)..   I'd actually have been quite interested in seeing some of those but safety first, I suppose.

On the positive side, it's a reasonably pleasant walk in the forest with all the Sri Lanka forest noises that you'd expect - we didn't see much in the way of wildlife -  a few interesting bright red bugs and a couple of monkeys in the trees but it's more of a walk in the park than a walk on the wild side.

Truthfully, I'd skip Ritigala unless you have a lot of time to kill and have run out of other things to do.

+ Fairly secluded/not very busy
+ free/donation
+ pleasant forest walk

- ruins distinctly unimpressive
- top is blocked off

Title: Monastery
Text: This is very beautiful. There is a small parade of huts before entering the park. Do take time to have a drink called "orange" even though it is green. Really refreshing. The park is beautiful with a very old Buddha stature. Be respectful and cover your shoulders and legs from the knees up when entering the park.

Title: Very pleasant morning trip
Text: Nice walk and interesting remains of old monastery .  The road there is in very bad condition making it difficult for cars. Tuk tuk drivers offer trips to the site. They charge 1500 rupees.  The driver we ad ave a very good tour for tge price and was very knowledgeable about the area.

Title: Alone in the jungle
Text: Well worth the walk up to the site. Our car couldn't drive the last 2km, so we walked, not after been warned to be very carefully, staying on the track and turning back immediately should we meet wild elephants. Well we did not them and arrived at the site which is completely forlorn in the jungle. I've never seen trees of this size and age - it's simply amazing. Even the tiny rests of the monastery are impressive. A visit absolutely to do if you are near!

Title: Worthwhile the little detour
Text:
Don't expect mayor ruins or heavily restored temples, but, as one guide book described it, it is a bit of an Indiana Jones experience. I loved the fact that we were the only visitors and the fact that it is a nice walk through a lush forest. The site itself is fairly small and one can cover it easily in 1 hour.  
Despite what some guide books say, entrance is free. 
The only negative thing is that, should you have a driver, he will likely refuse to drive the  last 1.5km of dirt road. The only tuktuk driver around demands Rs 1300, which is far too much. You can even walk there really. 
Recommended

Title: Tranquil setting
Text: Set deep in the forest, a very peaceful place.  We went early morning arriving 8.30 and were the first visitors of the day.  We got a real sense of the peace and tranquility of the place  helped by our excellent driver and guide.  Even with the rough guide, we felt it was very helpful to have a guide to lead us around. A truly magical place

Title: Forest Scramble
Text: This is seldom visited but is real forest scrambling up a clear trail across huge boulders beside a stream to a hidden ruined monastery. Beautiful, trees were full of monkeys telling us to go away crashing through the branches. magical. So glad we added it to our itinerary.

Title: All to ourselves
Text: Went here yesterday. Jeep ride to the entrance was fun. Cool breeze a relief. The site is  Truly beautiful and amazing in terms of the ruins, the history and the jungle setting. The view from the monk library was fantastic too. Walk is totally do able and worth it.

Title: take a good antimoskito lotion with you...
Text: Ancient monastery around 30 min walking from the parking lot in the jungle,spotting termiten,kameleons,eagles and huge beautiful trees..

Title: Beautiful and peaceful.
Text: Definitely recommend a trip to the beautiful and peaceful Ritigala. Although we chose not to hire a guide in most places we visited, a guide is helpful at Ritigala to make the most out of your visit. Lots of wildlife to see. A bit of a hike to see all the ruins but the walk is under the cover of a canopy of trees.

Title: Great hiking
Text: Bit tied to hike but it was so good to did that hiking. once you climb up to the mountain you can see whole area which was amazing. On  the way to the top of the mountain we saw some old monetary ruins. I heard that it was a old castle. Great adventure to do if you hanging around dambulla.

Title: another super place full of good energy
Text:
It is told that Budda during his visiting Sri Lanka visited that place I mean Ritigala Monastery.
This is beautifull place full of positive energy, calm and green.
You can walk and find the ruins of old  monastery .
really nice place.

Title: Off beaten track
Text: Very few tourists come here which is a good respite from the crowds at other major attractions . Peaceful n serene .

Title: Very enjoyable walk
Text: Ritigala is about 30 minutes drive from Habarana, there is a small entrance fee but the area is very quiet and we'll worth a visit. The walk around the ruins is not difficult, we spent about an hour there and could have stayed longer. Do read about the history before you go so that you can fully appreciate the area.

Title: Nice walk full of suprises
Text: We drove from Habarana and it was about 30 minutes drive. The walk itself is 90 minutes return with easy to moderately difficult due to granite steps. However it is far easier than other hikes as Seegiriya or Mihintale due to ancient paved footpaths. The vegetation is different to surrounding dry zone and takes you to another world. The real star is the ruines of a monastery with a hospital and a massive pool all made of granite. Pay attention to precisely 'joined' gapless granite paving stones. A guide is highly recommended if you didn't know the details. It is less visited than other main sites in the cultural triangle, I think mainly because Sri Lankan history books/school curriculum seems to give it enough respect, hence not hugely popular with locals. Thoroughly enjoyed the visit with large group of people including small kids (5y+)

Title: It's just a pile of stones in the jungle....
Text: However if you pause to consider how these stones were cut and placed in the area, it's pretty mind blowing!   Not too difficult an ascent and we arrived at 12.30 today. Mostly visited by the "off the beaten track" tourist and we spoke to a lovely English couple who had years on us and still climbed to the top!  A lot of Sri Lankans come here and it certainly wasn't crowded.   We loved it, shame I was suffering from the after effects of dodgy belly and by the time we reached the last sunken garden I had barely enough strength to drag myself up the path to view the enormous tree roots that form the "fort". Was it so worth it to go, absolutely. Get there before the word gets out!! Cost for two tourists LKR 600

Title: Great if you have the time and like Ruins.
Text: I personally liked this experience but I could see people being disappointed if they expecting a lot. Its ruins after all. But I enjoy the slight hike and especially the "hospital" of these ruins. Do yourself the favor and either research it before, or get a cheap guide to get more out of the experience.

Title: Worth visiting
Text:
Went with our guide. Quite a hike up rocky paths but manageable if moderately able.
Mostly through rain forest. My husband picked up a tick. No leeches though and it was a drizzly day. Hard to get your head around how ancient this place is. Guide recommended

Title: Hike in the jungle
Text: Very nice hike through the ruins of a Buddhist monastery. Lost in the jungle. Very few (if any) tourists. Most of the walk is in the shade.

Title: Retreat in the forest
Text: What an amazingly beautiful and serene spot in the middle of the forest. A long drive to get there but such a welcome  from the locals who had just finished serving lunch to the monks and offered us a meal.

Title: Relaxing walk in the jungle
Text: Nice, failry short walk in the jungle and interesting ruins. Easy to climb and lots of beautiful trees.

Title: definitely worth the visit!
Text:
This was probably my favourite activity so far this trip. We went in the morning, by tuk tuk, and luckily we had the mountain to ourselves. The peace and serenity, only interupted by the sounds of the jungle, was so nice compared to the noise and hustle of tourists at the other ancient sites. If I was short of time, I would go here instead of Dambulla Rock, unless you are really interested in more statues of Buda. Gamini, out tuk tuk driver walked with us and explained some of the interesting features, as well as telling us about the different trees and creatures we encountered. It must have been a massive feat of engineering 1500 years ago to get the massive granite slabs up the mountain and in place. Great.
P.S. free of charge, just a small donation required.;

Title: don't go out of your way
Text:
A good place to wander around the ruins, bit of a hike, take lots of water. Not much about the history of the place though. I wouldn't go out your way to visit, but do if just passing. Free to go in, though a donation is asked for.
Only wildlife we saw were loads of butterflies! And an elephant poo!

Title: WOW - another gemstone in Sri Lanka's archeological heritage.
Text: Amazing.  Ritigala has only recently opened for tourists, it is an ancient Buddhist monastery and the highest mountain in Northern Sri Lanka. The ruins and rock inscriptions date back to 1st century BC.  I recommend combining a trip to Ritigala with a stay at the Forest Rock Garden Hotel which is magnificent and won Green Hotel of the Year 2015

Title: A nice place to visit if you have nothing better to do !
Text:
Although not as impressive as Sigirya, Ritigala is worth a visit !
This place used to be a Monastery where some monks, originally educated in Anuradhapura, established to help local people.
Unfortunately, there is absolutely nothing to be found in English and this is a pretty remote area.

Title: Another perfect day in Sri Lanka
Text: We went by tuk tuk to Ritigala from Haberana with a great guy called Minda (probably spelt wrongly). Minda was an expert bird spotter and took us on a side trip to a lake where we saw an alligator, frogs, and eagles. We didn't bother with a guide at Ritigala, Minda came with us and pointed out various things of interest. The place is really atmospheric and although the buildings are in ruins, it is amazing to imagine the civilisation that created the monastery. On the way back we diverted to Habarana Lake where Minda showed us a monitor lizard - a great day out.

Title: a walk in the jungle
Text: great place to visit, not a lot of tourists, you can hear and maybe see the monkeys and you see lots of abes. Remember to bring something to drink. The walk takes around 2 hours.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
Great place to visit. Not many do it but it is worth the effort. You can now drive up to the site - apparently this was not possible before. 
You have to sign in (name ,passport details etc) for the site and a donation is requested. 
There are a lot of steps up to the top but there are lots of places to stop and see different parts of the temple. Some of the paths are through the forest which is good.
The ancient monastery is inside a national park but we did not see any animals only monkeys though we did see elephant droppings.

Title: Treasure hunt
Text: We went here with a local guide, who, if you ignore the requests for doubling his fee due to a 'sick child', is a good guy. Our children (6 & 4) were fascinated by the stories of cobra houses, elephant attacks and special medicine trees. They were playing 'Tomb Raider', looking for clues to find the lost treasure (magic medicine) of the Buddhist monks who once lived in this beautiful forest location. Just make sure you stay on the trails

Title: Amazing mouton hard to access - By Serendib Traveller
Text: Ritigala consist an ancient Buddhist monastery and mountain in Sri Lanka. Amazing geography so unusual located in the dry zone. Still no proper directions to reach up to the mouton. At the peak that weather almost similar to central hill country. But still open up to the monastery and archaeological sight. some times need to use a hard drive car or a jeep to drive through humph road. Im only recommend this to people like to take feel the real trekking experience in this non residential forest with a better organization.

Title: fascinating ruins; horrible access road
Text: highly recommended if you are interested in Sri Lankan flora and fauna, early Buddhism or a pleasant but steamy 2-hour hike

Title: Nothing really special
Text:
I was expecting more of this place as I have read all the previous reviews. The place is in the middle of the forrest indeed, but there is really not much to see and the landscape is not breathtaking either. There are mostly conserved floor plans with some original stones... and lots of mosquitoes. You can see much more lush and green forrest with "Indiana Jones feel to it" in other parts of Sri Lanka (Pidurangala or Knuckles range for instance). 

Lonely planet description is also idyllic but don't get your hopes up. There is also one disinformation in the 2015 guide - there is no admission to this place. The guide says 10 USD. In fact you're only asked for a donation (so it's up to you how much you're willing to give). 

All in all it's a good place to kill some time but nothing really special. Personally I'd skip this place if I ever came back.

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Unesco Site an ongoing archaelogical dig. Very interesting. Bit of a clinb to get to main building over rocks and streams but worth the effort. The viewes for the Library was great.plenty of trees and plants, very restful place.

Title: Lovely forest walk
Text: A fantastic walk through unspoiled forest with lots of wildlife. The remains of a nearly two thousand year old monastery dot the hillside. Beautiful environment and very peaceful. Walk tales about 1.5 hrs.  Ensure you have mosquito spray if bites trouble you

Title: Almost undiscovered
Text:
This site is perfect for travellers who wants a non-touristic experience. There are no signs and it's not all that easy to find the right way on your own. We almost missed out on most of the fun, because we couldn't seem to find the track, but luckily a guide saw us and guided us around, which included a exciting walk in the forest. The trees there are so beautiful!
Don't miss out on this!

Title: Awesome
Text: This is an awesome historical monastery the hike up was fantastic. The hike is mostly on the rock bad cut when the monastery was active. There are steps and most of the time it is at upward in Klein which is mild in natureThe hike I must say it was pretty easy other than for the incline. There are areas of the monastery still intact which would include areas of meditation and also completely intact bathrooms that were used 1000 years ago. It has a fantastic view from the top of the mountain. There is also a 3 acre lake at the bottom which is in disrepair but it is been rehabilitated by the Department of archaeology. I  used  the services of a guide and he was A fountain of knowledge as he knew the history of the monastery and also combined it with the history of Buddhism in that area. I have never met a guide  who so enjoyed his job and knew so much so I decided to include his name and telephone number if anyone is interested. His name is Asanka 0719560633. I would strongly recommend this hike.

Title: Peace and quiet and cool
Text:
A nice walk through the forest exploring the old monastery. We were the only ones there - apart from a small group of buddhist monks, and the monkeys.
There is restoration going on at the beginning of the walk and there is a small charge to enter.

Title: A walk though the old ruins in the forest of the Ritigala monastery
Text:
This place was a rare experience of our trip in Sri Lanka.
If you had enough of overcrowded spots and noise, add this monastery to your visit.
It is an easy walk on the path through the forest. Silence and mistery will accompany you.
It takes approx 1 hour. 
Go over the last ruins for few meters and you will also see a giant and spectacular tree.
From the main road, you have to driver for approx 15 min to reach by car.

Title: Shhh! It's a hidden gem; don't tell everyone.
Text:
Hidden away up a 3 km dirt road, Ritigala Forest Monastery is a fascinating, beautiful and stimulating place to visit.
Make sure you get an official guide - Daya was ours - who charge around 1500SLR on top of the 350SLR entrance fee, as he'll give you insights into the rich history of this area, with its incredibly developed culture and brilliant design. It makes you re-think the uniqueness of the Romans, although most of Ritigala is 8th century, so a little later than the best of the Roman empire in Europe. Their skill in building and the beautiful little details - the feet carved in the stone marking where to stand on the urinal, for instance - reveal a deep and rich Buddhist culture which was fed by the beauty and rhythms of nature all around.
Fabulous visit, totally worthwhile; I'm afraid I found Dambulla commercial and disappointing, but Ritigala helped me to forget!

Title: Tranquil monastery
Text:
Such a great find and so happy that we visited. The walks through the jungle are peaceful and like something out of an explorers adventure. We followed the paths and saw ruins from 200 BC and a few monkeys too!
Would be useful to have more signs and explanations of sites.

Title: Such an amazing place!
Text: We are on a tour and our driver suggested this ancient monastery as a place worth visiting - it was fantastic - the history is incredible.  Our driver also suggest that we should get a local guide - we paid 1000rp for 4 of us - its a tip.  So worth it his knowledge of the area and the wonderful things he told us.  I highly recommend getting off the main road and visiting this place.

Title: Isolated
Text: A ruined monastery in the middle of nowhere. Well worth the trek, not another western tourist to be found. I fell for the "reduced" entrance price thing. More fool me, however my tuk tuk driver didn't let me fall for the guide scam. He asked for 2500rps but my driver gave him 200. The place was amazing.

Title: Be transported to another era!
Text: My mum's been wanting to visit the Ritigala Monastery for a quite awhile now and finally, on one of our many trips to see the usual Cultural Triangle sites (e.g. Sigiriya), we decided to visit Ritigala. I highly recommend it to everyone; it's kind of in the middle of nowhere but that promotes its peaceful factor. It is a site to be seen and experienced with your eyes, ears and heart. My mum and I walked through the paved stone path and among tree roots in total silence, breathing in the fresh air and keeping a reflective mindset. For the short time we spent there, we forgot all about the hustle and bustle of city life and other such materialism. A wonderful part of Sri Lankan heritage and well-worth a visit. The only sour note for us were the pesky bureaucratic "officials" who were in charge of the place - they pestered us for money for a personal tour and offered a cheaper entry ticket - but stand your ground and stay firm in your refusal. Once you leave behind the entrance, you will soon forget about bureaucracy and everything else and just only be entranced by nature!

Title: What a treat
Text: Our visit to Ritigala was an off the cuff decision based on the fact we read about it in the rough guide and it was near to us. What a great decision it was - a highlight of our short tour of SL. The nature reserve is 5km up a very bumpy, muddy and pot holed track. There were only four other tourists there and the hour or so walk through the jungle to view the ruins was exceptional. You'll need to hire a guide to show you where to go (R1000) and the entrance seems to depend on what the manager wants you to pay. It said R500 in the guide, but we had to pay R1000... That said, it was a beautiful, tranquil treat to wander through the jungle. My wife and I loved it. Head away from the crowd and go here. We enjoyed this much more than some of the other more well known attractions.

Title: A wonderful to build a monastery
Text: Very peaceful,but it is in the middle of nowhere in fact we go lost trying to find it!It was worth the journey .Sitting by the pool enjoying the site

Title: Stunning, very atmospheric ruined monastery in a mountain forest
Text:
This is one of the loveliest and most atmospheric places I have ever been to. 

There are miles of ancient stone paths and steps though the forest, some of which have been restored. There are ruined refectories and enigmatic 'roundabouts' (apparently for walking meditation). The trees and wildlife are beautiful and there is the sound of waterfalls all around you. It's quite cool, but like many sites in Sri Lanka involves many hundred rock steps and a bit of a scramble at times. The atmosphere is out of this world. It is not visited all that much, which adds to its charm.

It's on a rough track from the main road (our driver booked a jeep). When we got to the ticket office, still several kilometres from the entrance, a huge tree had fallen across the road and nothing had been done about it (it falls between the Forestry Department and another), so we paid a local lad to take us down the track on his motorbike! Clouds of butterflies rose up as we went along the track and I heard load roaring and crashing noises from the forest (wild elephants). There was birdsong everywhere.

Title: Ritigala
Text:
We decided to go to Ritigala only 14 km from Habarabana to try to get a bit of the beaten track. It was very much a success. 

The park is an old monastery with surprisingly well conserved ruins. Tourists have obviously not truly spotted this place (yet!) and the artefacts are not covered in glas etc. but appears to be as they were left by the monks a few thousand years ago. 

At the entrance about 2 km from the actual park there is a visitor centre which is quickly overseen. We did not see any official staff but were met by 3-4 men with a jeep who adviced us that an ordinary car could not make it the last 2km to the park as the road was damaged. Instead they proposed to take us by jeep and give us a tour for 4000 rupees. We took it for a scam (of which there are many in Sri Lanka) but when we decided to walk the last bit one of them insisted on following us at least to park. To make a long story short the truth was that the road WAS impassable by ordinary car and the elephant danger was in fact very real. The elephant stories were later validated by pictures and other locals. As elephants are present all year nobody should try to walk, but in dry seasons (we visited in January) any car can do the trip.

We ended up asking the "guide" to follow with us the entire trip which was a good decision as - his poor English aside - was very knowlegable about the site and show us stuff we would never have found by ourselves. 

The trip includes a approx 4km hike up a mountain side (medium intensity) and lasts about 2-3hours. There is an entrance fee of 1500 rupees pr person (be aware that the staff might try to persuade you to a lower price which they will then keep to them selves - if possible pay full and ask for a receipt).

After the trip the guide was so nice as to invite us for lunch with his family. Best experience so far! He lives in a small house on the corner right in front of the visitor centre. If you pass by and want a guide be sure to ask him.

Title: Indiana Jones at its best
Text: Lost in a forest, you'll need a 4x4 -or in our case a Tuktuk - to get down the road here, but it's worth it to find one of the most armospheric ruins in Sril Lanka tucked into the hillside jungle

Title: A pleasant change from the over-visited cultural triangle sites
Text: Allow plenty of time to visit this site (1/2 day) as if you rush there and back you will miss the wildlife and atmosphere of this remote place. Look out for peacocks on the surfaced access road. When we went (early Nov 2012) the last track (unsurfaced) was badly rutted and it was tricky getting to the car park in our hired car.  We arrived mid afternoon and the custodians had "run out of tickets" - so we paid nothing. You don't need a guide - just follow the main path and use the guides available on the internet. But we had someone to help spot the abundant wild life and plants - that was very good. As others have said it is a bit of a clamber round the old tank and up the slope on the opposite side of the stream - but after that it is a well made (original) pathway to the top.

Title: Ruins in the forest
Text:
We made the mistake of walking the 6 km from the main road - don't.  Take a tuk-tuk!  The "officials" at the site offered to give us access at less than the official ticket price - and pocketing the money themselves.  I would strongly advise that you pay the official price and get an official ticket - that way there is some chance that the site is looked after.  I would also recommend that you get a guide.  Ours was not expensive - R500 and did not speak that much English, but he did show us a lot of places we would not have found by walking on our own.  He was also able to communicate some of what the various places were.

The real joy of the place is the vast array of mostly unrestored ruins and the pathways between them.  Ritigala is not a major attraction and is all the better for it. Exploring the ruins amongst the forest is a great experience and for me one of the best!

Title: A Real Life Indiana Jones Movie Set
Text: A step back in time. This was a wonderful place to wander around and see what ruins you can find in the woods. Some wonderful viewpoints, and sitting quietly listening to the sounds of the forest, contemplating life here as a monk many centuries ago, was fantastic.

Title: Ritigala ruins.
Text: We get to Ritigala and find there few people, of some archeological office , they speak just very basic English ,but our driver also don;t have good English knowledge, so after long talks between driver and local people we paid them 500 LKR ,they give us guy that would our guide with just few English words. But we enjoyed of forest cooler then outside environment,and our guide may explain us about ruins, we went on paved road to ruins, of what was before some 1500 years ,monastery facilities, bath,"cleared" circles( monks have to go 30 times around these circles to be cleared),double platform. I recommend visit this place, to people that like antiques.

Title: Ritigala
Text: Quite a treck for not too much to see. Nice forest though

Title: An oasis of mountain walks!
Text: Not on the main tourist route, a great advantage in the popular Cultural Triangle.  Sadly access to the top is restricted to protect the valuable plants but there are still many birds to catch sight of and, if you are lucky, the shy bear monkeys.

Title: Amazing to see
Text: Amazing to see these paths and structures in the middle of nowhere halfway up a mountain. Needed an English Speaking guide and could do with some means of access to allow the less fit and able to see this amazing site.

Title: Extraordinary - a must-go
Text:
This was spectacular, and a must-do for anyone visiting Sri Lanka.

We managed it in a day-trip from Kandy, but were up at 6.30am to make it work. Wed recommend staying nearby and combining it with Pidurangala (another absolute must), Kaludiya Pokuna, and perhaps Polonnaruwa.

We climbed without a guide  the route is clear, and we were happier by ourselves. The climb took us about 35 minutes, and was at times quite steep, but there are plenty of places to rest.

The view at the top is spectacular  make sure you leave plenty of time to explore Royal Gardens at the bottom, Boulder Gardens at the end, and the archaeological remains at the top. We had a wonderful time.

Title: Definitely worth visiting
Text: Definitely go there if you can. Parking is easy and free for those who self drive and the climb is not so hard. About 150m of elevation but on good steps. The view from the top on surrounding jungle is amazing.

Title: Worth the climb!
Text:
Definitely a must-visit if you are in center-north Sri Lanka. The views from the bottom/garden are already great, but from the top it looks amazing.
Not recommended for people with vertigo (due to the last round of steps) or impaired mobility.
Climbing is easy even for elder people as long as you make a few stops on the way up (I went with my father 65+ Yo, that has some problems doing long walks / climbing, but stopping a few times worked out very well for him. Managed to go up and down in a total time of 57 minutes).

The history of this place is also very interesting. You can get leaflets at entrance. Expect lots of locals trying to guide you up (I think its totally unnecessary to hire one specially considering the very poor English skills..but it's up to you. They will try hard).

The only bad thing is families that don't respect the wasp warning signs resulting in incidents. Wasps can be triggered by sound - as advertised everywhere. Unfortunately we saw families with kids screaming, loud music and others crying out loud precisely in the designated "Wasp attack zone". Avoid going with kids to keep this place safe for everyone or at least take them to non-attack zones.

Title: Well worth the climb!
Text:
Fabulous views from the top, energetic climb but its worth it, extensive site at ground level too, plenty to see in terms of views, ruins and wildlife.

Watch out for the guides who try to attach themselves to you at every opportunity - you dont need them.

Title: Hard climb but worth it
Text:
Had a great experience climbing to the top of the fortress. 
It is not an easy climb. It has about 1200 steps to reach the top of the mountain. 
Great frescoes and great views.

Title: Beautiful frescoes
Text: Be prepared to climb about 1200 atep steps to get to the top of the rock. It takes about 2.5 hours to go up and down.  About half way up you will the frescoes of woman from the Harem. At the top you will get a view of the area and the distant mountain.  Take comfortable shoes, a hat and a bottle of water. It is hot and sunny. We started the walk very early in the morning to beat some of the heat.

Title: Passable
Text:
Firstly it's a ruin. So you don't get to see walls or actual structure. It's left to your imagination. 

It's for people who love to trek, climb, walk in the hot sun. 

I would suggest you to not go by the Ariel view or drone shots. You won't find the place like that unless you are flying. So once you reach the top after walking, climbing, sweating it's entirely left to your imagination. 

Price is high. Do it if you like sweating it out. The view is nice from the top. You can just feel WOW and think how someone would have built a palace on this huge rock. That's about it.

Title: LOVE THIS PLACE! This is MUST visit.
Text:
I LOVE LOVE Sigiriya! One of the best places I have visited. Lion's Rock (ancient rock fortress) mesmerising to see and can't wait to visit again.

Note: I am writing this review is after completing 15 days holiday in Sri Lanka; therefore, I have considered all pro and cons.

Title: Must visit - heritage site
Text: We had a great experience around this rock fortress. The Tickets for SAARC nations are at a discounted rate of 15USD. you need to provide your actual passport to avail the discount. For non saarc nations the tickets are 30 USD. We hired a local guide who asked for 5K LKR but we bargained and got him to agree for 3K. He explained all relevant details right from the start. Great site to visit.. The climb is a little strenuous and become overcrowded sometimes. Overall we completed the climb and descend in around 2 to 2.5 hours (along with my kid - 7 year old). View from the top is great . you can see a huge buddha statue a little far away and also the pidirangula rock. Overall i recommend a visit to this heritage site.

Title: Ravana connection or just Mythology?
Text: Amazing destination for those who like to explore heritage sites. Climb to the lion rock top is a bit strenuous. Best time to start the climbing is in the morning, avoid climbing in hot sun. The museum has some splendidly preserved artefacts dating back to 2 century A.C. This also houses 5000 (claims) year old human remains. Tools and Furnaces dating back to 2nd to 5th Century A.C. Amazingly preserved earring.

Title: Hardly anyone there
Text: Had a lovely time wondering around with hardly anyone else there! People were working on the gardens and doing maintenance ready to welcome people back. The frescos were incredible, luckily our guide knew a lot about them as there wasn't any information around.

Title: Overrated
Text: Overrated and over priced. I understand this is to protect the ruins, but the opposite hike of pidurangala is much more challenging and beautiful, and you get the view of the sigiriya rock.

Title: do this at 4pm it is cooler and breezy on the top
Text:
We were thinking of doing this at 8 am but kids did not wake up so decided to reschedule it to 3 30 pm. we started the climb around 3 45 to 4pm after buying tickets and I felt it was much easier to do than we expected as as it was not as hot and had a good breeze on the top. I felt morning would have been more hotter.
overall not much structure on top just a nice gorgeous view. there is no water or food being sold on top so carry your own snack and water. just treat it like a nice trek with steps and enjoy the view on the top.

Title: Don't look down
Text: You can see the rock for miles around and it does look a little daunting when it comes to climbing up to the top.  In fact, although it is 1200 steps up and the same down, taking a steady pace, it wasn't too bad.  If you don't like heights - just keep going and don't look down.  The metal walkway takes you up the last few metres and it's worth it when you get up for the view (and sense of achievement).  Don't miss the side walk across the front of the rock and the spiral staircase to visit the caves.

Title: MUST MUST VISIT!
Text: A must visit in Sri Lanka, a hidden jewel. A must see for people who like history and culture. A special mention to Priyanthe who was our guide for the tour. He was very helpful and had deep knowledge of the Rock Fortress. Note - if you are from SAARC countries, carry your passport, you will get a 50%discount. And would definitely recommend a guide. It takes approx. 2 hrs to complete the climb and come down. The view from the top is just breathtaking.

Title: definitely recommend this historic site
Text:
If you are looking to break a sweat and get some steps in.. I definitely recommend this historic site.
You will be rewarded with a nice view! I would recommend bringing a water bottle and wear comfortable shoes.

Title: Offers stunning views of the region
Text:
Offers lovely views of the region.

There are about 600 steps to climb, the first few are steps in rock and later on steel steps bolted on rocks. The climb is steep but doable. Contrary to earlier reviews, all the steps now are in perfect condition and it is safe to climb. There are railings throughout so you have something for support. There is a lush green garden before you begin the climb and a small musuem.

While on top, you can see the remains of the foundation of the erstwhile palace, and the pond (/swimming pool). 

There are only about a few trees so make sure you carry sun protection and plenty water and some snacks. There are no shops / shacks en route or on top. 

On the way down, you can climb up a few stairs again for paintings in the cave.

PS: if you're from SAARC countries, do NOT forget your passport. The ticket prices are significantly lower for SAARC citizens but you'll get that rate only if you're carrying the passport, soft copy is not accepted.

Title: Breathtaking Views
Text:
Do not visit Sri Lanka without visiting here. The views once on top are breath taking, you can see for miles and its beautiful. Also you get the benefit of learning all about the history during the stop, the grounds surrounding the rock are just as beautiful.
Just be aware there are a lot of steps to get up! But you do have a break about half way up.

Title: Must see in Sri Lanka
Text: The rock fortress is a must to visit in Sri Lanka. When we where there in the beginning of november 2021, we was almost the only visitors, due to covid. But it is clear they are used to many many visits every day. We bought a guide at the gate to show is around, it was worth all the money. We spend 9 days in total travelleling around to turists sites, but this one is a clear no 1.

Title: Amazing natural feature, but expected a more structured experience
Text: It is an impressive natural feature which we enjoyed exploring. However, there are many good aspects to the area but it could be executed slightly better. If you want to find out more about the history, it would be better to do research before coming to the attraction. We would have expected a lot more pomp, but it seems to be more low-key. It was relatively expensive to get in, but worth it overall. It took around 30 minutes to get to top, but overall spent around two hours in the area.

Title: Spectacular
Text: From walking through the water gardens and seeing the spectacular rock to actually walking around on top of it this is a wonderful experience. I would go as far to say one of my top 3 archaeological experiences. We took it nice and steady and took between 3-4 hours to complete the site. Wonderful photo opportunities at every point. You can't take pictures of the frescos, but there are copies in the museum where you can. One day later still in awe of the place and should be on everyone's 'bucket list' in my opinion. Cost at the current time LKR6000, but worth every Rupee.

Title: Fabulous fortress!
Text:
Loved our trip here, we went in the morning arriving by 9am and it wasn't too busy at all. 
The museum part at the start is a bit rubbish of the old photos but it was nice to see the jewellery and things uncovered from the site. 
The walk along the flat to the rock just brings home the scale of the place its just incredible. 
The climb up is all even steps and in different sections, the first part is steady wide stone steps with places to stop on the way. Once at the top of that you can see the stone lions feet as the entrance of the fortress itself. There are some dogs/ monkeys about so be careful of having food and drink out here but they were very calm and I never saw them trying to get anything from people. 
From here its tight metal steps and no places to stop but not as bad as it looks from the bottom. 
Once at the top of the fortress there is beautiful views over Sri Lanka. Easy to spend and hour or so wandering around and some places to sit and enjoy the views too. 
Definitely worth the money. Not sure how anyone can moan about the difference for tourists and locals - is their country of course they should enjoy it cheaper and tourists who can afford to travel should pay more to upkeep this beautiful place.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
What can I say, this is one of the highlights of my 13 day trip to sri lanka!
There are govt approved guides at base if you want to have a little history lesson and guide all the way to the top. I declined because I wanted to experience without alot of talk. Obviously  I went when  tourism was down in sri lanka so there were only about maybe 25 people or so I got to enjoy to myself. I took over a 100 photos and had all developed. There is photo opportunities at every step. The hike up and down took me about 3 hrs but I took my time, its steep but I'm used to hiking uphill. I can say it's safe but I would recommend being fit. The cost as I saw some complaining is NOT expensive of what you get to see. This is on the same scale as Machu picchu or chichennitza in cancun. So ignore those posts. $30is nothing to someone who comes from the west and travels that far!!. 

On a historical note this fortress dates 500 yrs before Christ. There's only one place at the top which you cannot take photos and a man sits there so you don't and thats ancient Buddhist frescos which very colorful. 

Once again, this fortress is an incredible place

Title: Amazing experience
Text: One of the highlights of our holiday in Sri Lanka. This is an amazing experience. This must have looked fantastic when it was first completed. You can still see some of the Lions claws and there are still some of the original fresco paintings.you need to visit this place definitly.

Title: Amazing view
Text: Amazing view and one if the must visit places in Sri Lanka, but it's so hot during the day time, avoid weekend crowded and difficult to climb.

Title: Morning sunrise at Lion Rock Sigiriya
Text:
We went as part of our Walkers tour so included in our paid for itinerary. Our guide suggested going early so we started the climb at around 6 am and was at the top in 30-40 minutes. It is exhausting if like me you are not as fit as you though you were but the views on the way up and at the top are worth the effort. To see the sunrise and the forest jungle landscape below is literally breath taking. We sat for a while taking in the panoramic view then explored the fortress. Marvelled at how they would have built it in 400ad and then took the descent past the cave fresco and mirror wall. 
Its a must do experience if you come to Sri Lanka.

Title: Great climb
Text:
Going up is a bit exhausting but coming down is scaryat the end you dont feel disappointed as the journey is both rewarding and exciting

View from the top is amazing its a protected site so lot of history is available avoid taking a guide as you dont need one and you will be a lot happier doing this on your own instead of being heckled by a guide

Title: Please Avoid
Text: Locals paying 100 rupees, foreigners paying 10.000 rupees, its like 30 cents for locals, 30 dollars for foreigners ???? most shocking thing i have ever seen in my whole life.

Title: Exceptional and integral but very expensive
Text:
This is a mind blowing experience, almost an 8th wonder of the world but I just cant help but feel taken advantage of by the astronomical expense of entry - where does this money go? The upkeep of the site? Paying of guides to help you (no it cant be as you have to pay extra for them)? It just feels like a bit of a low blow to be ripped off like this.

Pidurangula was much cheaper and tbh more mind blowing of a view though with less historical importance

Title: Especially enjoyable on a rainy day
Text:
I and my boyfriend are a living proof that this place is manageable even on a rainy day. Actually, the experience is amazing! There were almost no people, shorter or none queues. Just bring a raincoat or an umbrella, and open sandals, and you will be fine. 
The complex consists from the rock that you will climb using the famous stairs. In the second half of this journey, there is something called Mirror Wall and then frescoes, which is a small cave with very old pictures with still vivid colors. 
The place is full of self-employed tour guides - locals that will follow you around, saying that they are tour guides and that you definitely need one. Then they will walk with you, talk with you, and expect money at the end. We were warned that there is no need for a tour guide and that the place is mostly about walking the stairs and the view afterwards. 
Lion's Paws is the stairway where are normally those long lines of people that are trying to get to the top of the rock. At t the base of the stairs, there are statues in a form of lion's paws, so hence the name. This place is what you want to experience when someone talks about Sigiriya Rock. And form my experience, it's the biggest fun!
The Mirror Wall itself is not that wow, I would say. It's not shiny anymore, you can't touch it, it's just therein its not shiny form. 
Frescoes that are waiting for you at the end of the line are much more interesting, since it's something to look at. The line leading to the frescoes is heading among the Mirror Wall. It's not possible to take pictures of frescoes, thought, there is a lot of staff watching everyone so nobody does it. 
I didn't see any toilets on the way, just those at the ticket office. So count with that, if you want to spend few hours of wondering at the place, or if the queues on the particular day are too long.

Title: Definitely worth the visit and cost.
Text:
Its a well known rock on the tourist trail of Sri Lanka , but dont let the crowds put you off, but go early to catch the morning light.
This is a strenuous climb of stairs, metal staircases, and clambering of the ruins on the top, and anyone with vertigo might be advised not to do this, or those with weak stamina. That said its a fabulous view, and a great ruin with a nice history to it. 
You will be pestered by guides offering to take you up there, but really theyre not necessary, and they want a tip of rupees for it. Basically you climb up the stairs ( over 1000!).

Title: The Ultimate Challenge: Conquering Sigiriya Rock
Text:
Sigiriya Rock, also known as Lion Rock, is an impressive landmark located just 30 minutes away from Dambulla village in Sri Lanka. The rock can be reached by tuk-tuk or bus and is a must-see destination for any traveler to the country.

It's recommended to arrive early to avoid the crowds and make the most of your visit. The entrance fee is $30, but it's worth it for the breathtaking views from the top. The climb is of moderate difficulty, so make sure to wear comfortable sneakers and bring a bottle of water to stay hydrated along the way.

As you make your way to the top, you'll pass by ancient ruins and intricate frescoes, all while taking in the stunning scenery around you. Once you reach the summit, you'll be rewarded with a panoramic view of the surrounding jungle and countryside. Don't miss out on the opportunity to experience this incredible piece of Sri Lankan history and culture.

Title: Epic,
Text: Dont go on a Full Moon holiday as crowds are huge!  But other than that expect to climb lots and lots of steps but well worth it for the view and to learn about the despot king who was carried around there and had 500 concubines too!

Title: Watch out for the guides and helpers!
Text:
Beautiful ancient rock fortress! Easy climb. We really enjoyed the views. Only reason Im giving it a 2 starts is because of our guide. We actually had a great time once he left us alone. 
Be careful with tour guides and helpers 
We had a man following us from the start and he was talking about the Sigiriya Rock. After approximately 5 minutes he stated that he was a freelance guide and offered to accompany us to the top while telling us about the history of this rock fortress. He stated that he didnt have a price and we could decide at the end what to pay him depending on how we liked his services. We agreed. About 5 minutes after that he brought us to a man selling magic boxes and insisted we try to open them. We were not interested in buying any boxes. A few minutes after that his friend arrived and started helping me up the stairs. I did not ask for help nor was it needed.  He insisted on holding onto my hand however it was very awkward and opposite of helpful. It quickly became hazardous as none of the steps are the same size and walking with a stranger like that out of the blue was weird. This helping up the steps became annoying and I tried numerous times to stop it but he kept holding his hand out. My husband was actually walking behind us and thought it was the funniest thing.  Its funny now looking back at it. He even snapped some photos. After a few more sets of steps I had to tell my husband that I am not climbing 1200 steps and up the rock like this. Luckily we were still in the beginning. My husband told our guide who translated to the helper that his assistance was not needed. We were then told he doesnt work for free! Our guide then told us that his services were $40-$50! We paid less for a taxi drive with all our luggage from the airport to our hotel! Be careful! We told both of them to have a nice day however the guide still wanted money for his services thus far   Ruins the experience!

Title: Worth the climb
Text: An amazing place to visit & whilst the climb is steep the views from the top could be amazing (sadly a bit overcast when we went). The gardens you walk through to get to the rock are beautiful. Whilst there dont appear to have been any accidents the steps dont fill you with confidence as they look old & rusty

Title: A Must-Visit Destination with Stunning Views and Historical Significance
Text: we recently visited Sigiriya and would highly recommend it as a must-visit destination. The climb to the top of the rock is around 1200 steps, but it's well worth the effort for the incredible views across the forest. I would recommend visiting in the morning to avoid the heat and crowds, and to take advantage of the stunning sunrise views (start 5:30). While the entry fee is $30, I believe it's a reasonable price given the historical significance and beauty of the site. One thing to be aware of is that there are often many guides at the site who may hassle tourists, so it's best to be prepared for this and set clear boundaries. Overall, I found Sigiriya to be an amazing place to visit and would highly recommend it to others

Title: Good Place to visit
Text: best place to visit. around 1200 steps to climb. the entry is 30$.  climb in the morning is amazing.  hot during the day time

Title: Worth the climb
Text: An amazing place to visit. Well worth the climb. It is easier then it looks to climb to. The views across the forest are amazing

Title: Fantastic Experience
Text:
Extremely good experience and this place is incredibly well maintained. Beautiful gardens and the extremely well looked after. 
They have altered to route now so you go up to the Lions Feet on what used to be the exit before ascending to the top via the metal steps. Returning to the bottom along the side of the rock. Much better and somewhat quicker. 
Views are amazing and worth the effort. 
Only negative is there are so many hawkers that want you to buy from them and the number of guides that want to help you. This was our third visit to the lion rock and we didnt need help. My husband needed to use the toilet and a guide showed him the way back. He demanded $10.00 which is just outrageous. 
Well worth the effort. Be careful of the guides who what a fortune for helping you

Title: A terrific site, needing a head for heights
Text:
One of our party dithered about taking part in the climb because of a fear of heights. The steps are uneven up until the Paws, where, if you don't have a head for heights you can wait whilst others ascend the slightly rickety staircase to the top. I wore Merrell sandals with grip soles and they were great. If you are nervous about following the route, or needing a little help, you can hire a guide.

The views at the top are stunning and it is worth the climb, popping on the way back down, up to see some lusty murals. Again the cage, circular staircase, isn't for everyone.

At the top the world and his wife seem to have assembled, but it is worth it.

Title: " Responsible service and heartfelt friends "
Text:
My Sigiriya tours provided the best service for us :) Chandu helped us a lot and he showed a little bit of his village beauty. He cares about us all the time. Like our fathers. But he is a young father. He recommended us a place to stay for a month. It was the perfect place. We really had fun there. We followed the Chandu. He made our plans. They are really good plans.

The best thing was to spend the night camping in the jungle. We had a lot of experiences that we had never experienced before. At once we felt like fish living in the water. That's because we're camping in the most beautiful lake in Sigiriya.

We climbed the Pidurangala rock, we climbed the Sigiriya rock and went swimming in the Thalkote lake. Chandu took us to see the hidden beauty of Sigiriya.  " Mapagala Fortress, Galkanda Temple, Kaludiya Pokuna, Ritigala, and jungle safari ". If you want, you can help Chandu get a guide to study history or the past in depth. There is a lot to write but I will stop here. Chandu's service is excellent and I highly recommend him to you.

Title: amazing view from top
Text: this place is great for people interested in history. It is safe though it is a long hike to the top. People scared of height should not climb as well as those with physical ailments as there are a lot of steps. has caves with beautiful paintings right in the middle of the climb. The place is very crowded and need to be careful as there is only some room to climb. this place is associated richly with sri lanka's history. The climb is steady. The best part of it is the view from the top though there are incredible views throughout the climb. it is enchanting and fills one with amazement. it is covered with forests on all sides.A must see when in sigiriya.

Title: Always a great visit
Text:
Two trips to Sri Lanka in a year and two visits to the rock fortress!

Definitely a highlight of the area, a great experience!

Title: Amazing views!
Text:
Beautiful place full of history - we had our driver with us who told us all about it which was fascinating!

There are a lot of steps but lots of places to catch your breath if you need to. Take your time - absolutely worth it to the top! Railings all the way and a comfrtable walk (compared to Pidurangala!). 

We went mid afternoon - very hot but not many people at all which was great. Would absolutely recommend to anyone visiting the area.

Title: Worth the Climb
Text:
The climb up Sigiriya is well worth it! Take your time and you will get there :)
It's best to start the climb early if possible around 6.30-7.00am. It is also worth getting a guide as they can explain the history of the  rock as you go. If you go early there  are far less people and it is much cooler for climbing. It can get very hot from about 9.30am on, and those 1,200 steps can become challenging. It will take about 2-3 hours to climb up and back down, but the view from the top is well worth the effort.

Title: definitely worth the climb but also take the time to explore the surrounding
Text:
We had limited time so we focused on climbing to the top.  However, our tour guide showed us the amazing water/irrigation system that could only be seen during rainy season.  It was quite amazing given it was built so long ago.  So if you have time, don't miss exploring the grounds.  

Also, if it is an option, go on a cloudy day.  We lucked out - we went on a cloudy day and the climb was so much easier.

Title: Stunning and a little scary but well worth it
Text:
My vertigo has got worse with age. It was put to the test getting up the stairs to the top of the rock, but thankfully one of the local guides put his hands on my waist and guided me up. It gave me a little bit of security that I needed to finish the trek.
The fact there was one of Sri Lanka's many cute stray dogs at the top of the rock just rubbed salt into the wound and made me realise I should have been a little more robust.

Sigiriya is one of Sri Lanka's best-known sites to see and it easy to understand. It is an incredible archaeological site, and the mind boggles when you reach the top passing the ancient steps people clambered up, and you realise a whole civilisation lived here. The views from the top are truly breathtaking and well worth the wobbly legs on the way up. Monkeys and butterflies and fortunately no hornets were enough distraction from the rocky drop below. 

The walk-up is a workout, and I was dripping with sweat when I reached the top but having said that it was over 30 degrees, so dripping with sweat was just the norm. 

If you go to Sigiriya and don't think you will make it to the top, then I would recommend not going. Getting to the top is what this excursion is about, and once there, the sense of achievement is tremendous but more significant is the experience of what you see all around. 

There are plenty off guides around if you want one. I would have got one personally, but my partner is a little more frugal and not as free-tipping as I. But when a man is willing to hold the waist of another grown man with wobbly legs to get him to the top - he deserves a tip.

Sigiriya is the kind of place that now lives in my dreams, and for that, I am grateful.

Title: Lion Rock
Text: A fabulous experience as only 4 of our group made it to the top. As a fairly fit 60+ I thought it was pretty tough in places. Maybe i had too many Lion Beers ?? Either way, this 5th Century marvel was created by King Kassapa 1 and was used up till the 12th C. The moats & ramparts and the steep climb kept the invaders at bay. The frescoes paintings are worth the effort and the ladies are nice !  The terraced gardens & the water movements were all before their time ! A wonderful trip & glad we decided to do it. Anyone can get to the top if they just pace themselves, it is worth it !

Title: Stunning
Text: This is a must-see for any traveller to Sri Lanka.  We were lucky that because of the coronavirus outbreak, there were very few people there, so we were able to rest at frequent intervals on the the climb: there are plateaus on the way up.  I think it would be very hard if crowded, but the views are spectacular and the Lion's Gate is amazing: I stopped there but it's well over halfway up.  You just have to see it to believe it!  Take lots of water and sensible shoes, and arrange a reputable guide before you get there (there is a lot of history to be explained) - there are lots of men at the entrance who offer to take you up but expect a lot of money.

Title: Pretty amazing
Text: This rock is doable, provided you go in the morning. Luckily when we went, there weren't  many people climbing, so we could take our time climbing up, and coming down. There are resting areas, so you could have a breather. Carry water and wear comfortable shoes though.

Title: Awesome experience
Text: We arrived on a wet morning and started to climb with some trepidation, wondering if we would be able to see anything.  The climb was not as bad as we feared as there were plenty of places to have a break and when we arrived at the top, the rain had stopped and views were magnificent.  Well worth the early start and the many steps to the top.

Title: Excellent adventure
Text: We climbed the rock very early in the morning to avoid the worst of the heat but it still gets very hot, take lots of water with you. Lovely walk through the gardens and moat to the bottom of the rock. Lots of steps and even a spiral staircase, some parts one way. Our guide was very informative about the history of the rock. Amazing views from the top, there are remains of the swimming pool and throne area. Quicker coming down with a few stalls and water/ice cream at the bottom. Highly recommended, tough climb but worth it, take your time!

Title: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
Text: A climb up to the ruins on top of this amazing rock is a bit strenuous, but for reasonably fit people very gratifying because of the fantastic view from top

Title: Climbed
Text:
My trip to Sri Lanka had only one item which was to get to the top of Sigiriya and I succeeded.

The site is very well maintained with it very well set up to show the site and its history. Getting to the top was hard due to the temperature but the crowds are the only problem.
The site is very important to Buddhists who wanted to see the painting but I didn't and there was no easy way to bypass it.
It was well worth the climb

Title: Worth the climb
Text: This is a beautiful place and definitely worth the climb. Take a guide with you it was worth it. The climb was difficult for my mom but she made it with breaks.

Title: Awesome!
Text: This is a must visit place. Views from the top are stunning. Climbing the Lion's rock is not easy, but worth it.

Title: Too busy.
Text: We never managed to climb to the top as it was far too busy. We got some lovely camera shots but really wanted to climb it. Make sure you don't go on Buddhist day. Schools etc come out. There is a museum which was interesting. Beware of the guys offering help. Don't offer any money. They are like vultures preying on the weak. I had to be stern and tell them to go away. They did cos I am quite fit and strong. The weaker are not so lucky.

Title: God, its a long way up.
Text:
I am in my early sixties, with a lung condition. Was very hesitant to climb the zillion or so steps, so climbing this was , for me, a trial of resolve. I managed it, but took my time. Sri Lanka, right now, is sparsely touristed-but not at Sigiriya. I would dread to think what it is like when the overseas visitors arrive back en masse, once the memory of the 2019 bombings and Coronavirus are ancient history. This place gets crowded and people taking it slow like me tend to get in the way of the more fit individuals. Mind you, I was not the slowest by far. Unfortunately, however, being slow attracts the attention of helpers. Fit young Sri Lankans standing like hungry carrion, scanning for prey and constantly picking at the perceived weak ones and assisting up each flight of stairs, whether that attention was requested , required or not. Their keen eye for a sucker is uncanny and they latch onto a potential monetary catch like seagulls on a chip, regardless of whether you are struggling or not. If you are not quick with a kind hearted rebuke, then they claim their prize and the hassling for large tips starts. They have a hide like an elephant and nothing short of an angry expletive will shake them off.  Be aware. These guys get aggressive and persistent  if you dont make it absolutely clear that you do not wish their assistance. However, you are not out of the woods, as a couple more of these vultures wanting an easy kill will be at the next flight and the process starts again. I hated that and my patience and initial good natured banter was retired in short order. This spoiled things for me, but that is just my personality. Being honest, Sri Lankans are a good natured and, largely, well mannered bunch, but I set my standards for other peoples behaviours at, possibly, unrealistic levels. This is a dirt poor country trying to provide for its peoples and the population have grown to act in a certain way to feed their families. Their behaviours are borne from a need to earn money and, as a result, they can be a bit pushy bordering on exasperation at times.
Did I enjoy the Sigiriya experience? Well, besides the huffing , puffing and wanting to turn back at every step, I guess I did. Was that enjoyment because I was using the      climb as a yardstick for my failing fitness and a small mental personal victory was my just reward? Probably. Would I do it again? - Not a chance!

Title: Dont look down, look up!
Text: A must do in Sri Lanka. The climb is tough work but we recommend going early - we arrived at 6.45am to make the most of the cool weather. The final climb feels a little hairy but the views and the experience and worth every leg wobble!! Make sure you do the extra walk to see the ancient paintings about half way up.

Title: Excellent and Highly Recommended!
Text: We arrived at Sigiriya at around 7:15am and there were already people ahead of us. Buy your ticket in the museum near the car park. Because this is not a sacred area, you do not need to cover your shoulders or knees. I recommend sneakers and dressing for a hot sweaty walk up many stairs. It took us approximately 35 minutes to walk up with very little in the way of crowds. We looked at the murals and mirror wall quickly on the way up and then went straight to the top and explored for about an hour. On the way back down, we went more slowly and looked at the lion paws, octagonal pool, caves, and gardens. This is an incredible place and is famous and a major tourist destination for a reason. Highly recommend going and getting there as early as possible to avoid heat and lines. I would say youd want to be in reasonably good shape to make it up without too much suffering. Bring water and a hat too!

Title: Amazing
Text: It is amazing to hear how ancient Sri Lanka was so advanced to provide water up to the hill and draw those beautiful faces in the rock wall. So many people climbed all the way to the top and must go after the sun down.

Title: Well worth the climb
Text: Thought it might be too challenging but in the end it was fine. A series of steep steps but you can go at your own pace and it took under an hour to get to the top.

Title: You can manage this even if you are older!  Views are worth it!
Text: Myself and my husband are in our 50's and managed the climb up this in around 50 minutes.  There were a few points where we stopped and took a break and some water.  We did not find any of the steps too steep and the views at the top were breathtaking.  It's maybe close to being as good as Ayers Rock but then we are biased!

Title: Well Worth the Effort
Text: This was our second time of climbing the rock having done it two years ago. Amazing place and every step is worth the effort. This attraction is vastly improved from our last visit however there was a few things that could of been clearer. Guides now are registered and have to be engaged before you enter the ticket site. They should cost no more than 2000 rupees but some folks where charged 5000. The car parks are different than before and you are dropped off outside the ticket office however your car or Tuk Tuk then collects you after your climb in the foreigner car park in a different area. No issues as such but this means you must do the museum before you climb. Some guides just want you to commence your climb and dont give you this choice. Also it is not clear when you buy your ticket. The friends of Sigiriya are still at the bottom to assist you up if you require and this can cost 2000 rupees or more. The ticket price is $30 each and when you now exit there is a little market selling what you would expect at variously different prices depending on which one you would chose. The toilets in the Foreigner Car Park are extremely good. This attraction is worth a 5 star review but the lack of information regarding the museum and the car parking arrangements just made it a four.

Title: Stunning place but be prepared to climb and climb and climb.....
Text: What a climb but well worth it! The views from the top are amazing although when we were there it was cloudy and a bit misty. Queues can be quite long so get there early if you can. Amazing cave art to be seen on the way up.

Title: Awesome but chaotic
Text:
The story of Sigiriya is fascinating and to say that youve climbed to the top is one of the must-dos in Sri Lanka. The views are amazing and the remains at the top are interesting. 

However, it was a chaotic ascent with no staff, no decent signage and a complete free for all with ignorant, impatient people pushing in and ignoring the queues that the rest of us were patiently observing. One of the few places we visited that didnt reflect well on the people of this wonderful country. A shame and therefore not recommended.

Title: Heritage site !
Text: Amazing ancient kingdom with nice sunset and green view around. Wall paintings and nice garden with monkeys. Must visit place !

Title: One of must see in Sri Lanka
Text: Sigiriya shows us how developed technology could be used in a fortress built 1600 years ago...After defeating 1200 steps you can admire a wonderful view. There are a lot of tourists there but not so many to spoil the joy of visiting the place. You can meet a lot of monkeys there.

Title: Worth the Climb
Text: This was a one of the greatest adventures for your life. If your plan to go Sri Lanka for your next tour, definitely add Sigiriya to the list. The view is magnificent! Definitely worth the climb!

Title: Definitely worth the climb but go early in the morning before it gets too hot and crowded.
Text: Tough work getting to the top but really worth it. One of our group was afraid of heights and so paid a special guide to get her to the top and she said he was great at helping her to the top and really understood her fear.

Title: One of must see in Sri Lanka
Text: A must do in Sri Lanka. The climb is tough work but we recommend going early in the morning or in the evening. The final climb feels a little hairy but the views and the experience is worth it. Make sure you do the extra walk to see the ancient paintings about half way up. It was a great experience

Title: Worth the steep climb
Text:
