An amazing place that you must visit, if you're in Sri Lanka. Most package or guided tours will take you here (or get a taxi/tuk-tuk), and if they have any sense, you'll arrive early in the morning, That way you not only miss the queues at the entrance, but you can be up, down, and gone before the hot sun makes it even more difficult! There are a lot of steps (1200), and some of them are steep/high, and some of them are a little bit scary - especially if you have a poor head for heights. There are no facilities for wheelchairs. In fact, you probably need be pretty able bodied to do this one.
We had a guide who took us slowly from the top to the bottom, stopping to show us the small details we might otherwise have missed, and also to give us a breather! There are plenty of things to see before you reach the upper staircase. But once you are at the top, it provides a spectacular view (though early morning mist can limit this), and there are some extensive ruins. You'll be scratching your head trying to figure out how they got all the bricks up there. Get there early to beat the queues (the stairs are very narrow), or get there later for a clear view. 
Take your pick. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip to Sri Lanka. There's nowhere else like it.
Tips - wear sensible shoes, carry water, and although a hat is useful, it can get pretty windy up the top, so hang on to it.

Title: Worthwhile the climb
Text: The walk up to the foot of the rock, looking at the restored pools, birdlife and rocks was interesting. I was a bit wary as I do not like heights, but I made it to the top. Well worthwhile the effort. The paintings on the way up were fascinating, the view from the top was great. Be wary of being offered help to climb the steps (at an exorbitant price !), also some of the sellers of souvenirs, we could have bought them cheaper elsewhere! We had a guide who was good.

Title: Now that was tough!
Text: Was on a tour with G Adventures and this climb was one of the activities. So glad that I climbed it but it was hard going! Some 1300 steps! Steep stairs. The view from up top was spectacular! A must do!

Title: My personal highlight.
Text: A stunning location, immaculately maintained and clean.  The climb up looked daunting but we took our time and paced ourselves, enjoying the views as we ascended.  My own personal highlight of a wonderful trip to Sri Lanka.

Title: Impressive
Text: A very popular place to visit so advice would be to get there as early as possible to miss the crowds and the heat. Very tranquil and fascinating.

Title: Worth it
Text: This is an exhausted trip with two small kids, specially one carrying in hand since stroller cannot make up there. It worth the visit to see those but avoid noon and use always early morning or evening to climb, glad I read reviews before I climbed.

Title: Excellent
Text: Nice place to see it, amazing view how building this rock ......? Riyal place to srilanka dont miss it

Title: Sigiriya rock
Text: Been there, done that, avoid if scared of heights, otherwise it is well controlled area, little can go wrong. Frank tip, start the ascent early, the earliest the better, i.e. 8AM

Title: Great view
Text: Well worth a visit if you go to this part of Sri Lanka. Its a lot of steps up but worth it for the view from the top.

Title: Vertiginous Views
Text: Quick review to say that this site is not to be missed. But I found no reviews on how vertiginous the climb up might be.  Clearly it wld be steep climb but for those    who have a slight fear of heights the issue is whether you felt safe making the climb. We asked a few of our fellow hotel guests the night before and had a mixed response.  So we gave it a try. However I only got one third of the way up via means of a broad staircase which reached a platform with some terrific views over the countryside. But then onwards it became more challenging as I saw a steel caged spiral staircase built into the rock face. I knew straight away I wld freeze half way up and not be able to come down!  So I agreed that my partner would carry on up and I would meet him an hour later down in the visitors car park. I had an enjoyable hour watching everyone come and go for an hour and the wonderful vistas knowing I had made the right decision. This was confirmed by my partner when he got back to say it only got worse going up and he witnessed a number of people being vertiginously challenged on the way down. Phew! But it sounds worth the challenge if you know you can get back down. I was happy with my own 1/3 way up kind of achievement! Later found out that the steel spiral walkway (to see some cave paintings)is not obligatory and can be bypassed as you make your way further up. But you still faced further open and steep staircases built into the rock face.  But not me!

Title: Fantastic view, but be early
Text: 1200 steps to the top is a a small challenge but we met people from 3 to 80 on our way up. Start early before it get to hot, bring Lots of water

Title: Breathtaking, one of a kind
Text: When we got there the queue was huge. We decided not to take the central spiral stairs, we used the ones on the lest, where there are the Lions. We were able to climb in less than 1h, despite the crowd.

Title: Worth the climb
Text: There is a rich history in this rock and decently climb if you are in good physical shape. It is not an easy climb we stopped at many places to take a rest and must bring water since the sun can dehydrate you very fast.

Title: 100% recommended!
Text:
Definitely a must do! Amazing views at the top. Not too tough a climb really, as do in stages and can take your time.

Tips: Wear good shoes and bring water and hats as its pretty exposed up top. Watch out for the guides wholl charge you if they accompany you. Go early to avoid being busy. Recommend as early as 7am! 

Cost: about roughly $30 per person for international visitors.

Title: Worth the climb
Text: Even though I didn't claimed the rock I regret that for not going when the kids returned with dad after climbing the rock. They had taken bunch of pictures and they looked amazing. During the day time sun is too much so use a sun screen otherwise you'll get sun burn.

Title: Outrageously expensive
Text:
30$ entry fee.... I seem like the government is not thinking of tourists only about money. 
It is a great place to visit but the prices everywhere are accumulate to a small fortune ... many people around me give up and leave without seeing anything of the country....

Title: A truel Marvel!!!
Text: This place really got me so well. What an unbelievable place. I am so fascinated by Sigiriya.  One of most iconic places i ever visited. Honestly number one place in my list. It shows how rich and advance our ancient people were.A truly remarkable place. Must visit. Worth for $30!

Title: Amazing Place
Text: Best place to visit every one. Amazing view from summit sigiriya rock. It is most beautiful place in sri lanka. See you again sigiriya

Title: Amazing views from top.
Text: Over 1,200 steps to get to the top, very strenuous but worth it. Avoid the so-called guides who say they will help you up but demand money at end. Visit on a weekday as weekends are very busy and the steps get crowded.

Title: Hot, tired but well worth it!
Text:
Due to the recent events in Sri Lanka, we were lucky to have the fortress and the climb mainly to ourselves. I believe it can have to 3000 per day in more calmer times. This enabled us to enjoy the area mainly to the 20 in our tour group and meant we could meander at leisure and also take our time climbing to the top without being pressured to move on, or be held up. 

The climb itself is very steep in parts and with over 1200 steps to climb, you would need a moderate level of fitness to make to the top. There are plenty of places to rest on the way though if needed. 

If they want any improvement, it would be a zip-line to get back to the start! We could see our bus waiting for us below and what fun it would be to have a buzz on the way down!

Entry fees were included in our tour, so not sure how much they charge. From reading other comments, I feel it was well worth it and money goes to preserving this historical site.

Title: Amazing site.
Text: One of the highlights of our holiday in Sri Lanka. This is an amazing experience, the climb is not for the faint hearted but worth it. This must have looked fantastic when it was first completed. You can still see some of the Lions claws and there are still some of the original fresco paintings. Beware the naughty macaques, they will grab any food or drink you have.

Title: Sensational
Text:
What a great and unusual place to visit. This was my main interest in Sri Lanka and it didnt disappoint.

There are about 1200 steps to the top which not only provides a great view but also a challenge to get to the top and back down again.

The gardens at the base are interesting and the rock formations are an added bonus.

Title: What a view!
Text:
I am no fan of hiking and steep patch, but this experience is absolutely worth it! If you suffer from vertigo it will be challenging, a steep small stair to go up and do not look down. But the view of the rock both from the ground and the panorama will leave you without words!
Travel light and get up those stairs! Absolutely beautiful.

Title: Great views worth the climb
Text:
Definitely worth a visit when in Sri Lanka as it was an enjoyable couple of hours and the views were amazing from the top . Because there are stairs the climb is not to strenuous  but you do need a breather now and again because of the heat .
The historical aspect is well worth a visit to the museum to have a read up on the culture and ancient times surrounding the rock

Title: Amazing palace on top with an amazing view
Text: Me and my brother climbed this rock, after the pidurangala rock. We climbed the Sigiriya rock around 2pm. It was not too hot, we brought a lot of water. The climb is really easy because its only stairs. The ancient palace on top is amazing to walk around. The view is also really incredible. We didnt see any wasps. Only be careful with some dogs, because some can be a little aggressive.

Title: Must see on your Sri Lankan itinerary
Text: Well worth a visit.  Recommend that you take one of the numerous guides who are at the entrance waiting for tourists to roll up.  They all wear a uniform polo shirt so you know that they are offical guides, however as like anywhere you need to be prepared to negotiate a price.  We paid $20 US for a guide for 3 hours, our guide was excellent giving you a lot of background to the fortress which you would not get from reading the information pamphlet you get given with your ticket.  There are toilets located just by the ticket office, very clean but no toilet paper so make sure you take tissues.  There is also a water station before you enter with purified drinking water where you can fill up your water bottle.  Be prepared to climb up narrow stairs to get to the top, the view is amazing and worth the climb.  When we went in Feb there were no hornets which we had read about however we were told that it was the wrong season.  Beware of monkeys everywhere which is all part of the Sri Lankan experience.  When you exit the fortress there are numerous toilet blocks which were all clean and well maintained, again take your tissues.  Make sure you wear comfortable walking clothes, shoes, hat and take water, there is nowhere to purchase water along the way until the exit.  We arrived about 9.30ish which we found to be fine, the heat was bearable, the timing of your visit will all be dependent on the time of year you go.

Title: Telling it how it is
Text:
My Husband and I were here 4 weeks ago and decided to go early in the morning at 7am as the heat and humidity was just horrid anyway and thought it would be less then, but it really wasn't. Anyway we went shortly after opening time which is at 7am. Now, we are both nearly 60 years old and totally unfit fatties and both of us have bad hearts, bad knees and ankles, plus me with an already sprained ankle from a collapsing bridge a week earlier, but hey, I wasn't going to come all this way from Australia and not climb this Sigiriya Rock right?. Anyway we climbed to the very top in 50 minutes from the very start to the very top, including a few stops in between to catch our breath and trying to stop out hearts from exploding, but just quietly were were so very proud of ourselves, so kudos to us. Now just a word of warning, for those of you who have really bad knees or ankles this climb is not for you, and if you have even the slightest fear of heights, this climb is definitely not for you. I'd say go as far as the Lions feet and that's it as it is really frightening after that especially if people are trying to get past you and your clinging to the edge of the rock for grim death while letting them pass. For those of you who are not scared of heights then go on up to the very top, the 360 degree view you will love and you get to see all the ruins also. I must say watch out for the scammers too who will approach you along the way up at different points, they will make conversation with you and try and help you get up rocks etc and they will start to tell you all about the rock and the history and then they will become your guide without you even knowing about it and it will cost you money, but if you want to use them then go ahead, these locals are desperate for money. Also when you get there, there is no signage, well in English anyway, to where you buy the entry tickets from, we found it a bit confusing where to go to get the tickets, and that's a walk in itself too. There are plenty of Tuk Tuks at the bottom when you come back down that will take you back to your Hotels at a reasonable price. Just be aware that where the Tuk Tuks will drop you off at the start where you buy your tickets from is not the same place where you finish up when you come back down from the rock, you seem to get rail roaded out a different exit to an other side of the rock so you end up having to go past all the souvenir stalls. Our rooky mistake was telling our Tuk Tuk driver to pick us up here where he dropped us off, and he failed to tell us this was not the spot you finish up at when you come down from the rock, so once we came down and realised this was not where we started from, we then had to figure out how to get back around to the other side of the rock where the entrance was to meet our tuk tuk driver who was waiting so patiently for us, it was a long walk in the heat.
 All in all, we were both glad we did it and didn't drop dead from heat exposure and blown heart valves. We never want to see another step again as long as we live, our knees and ankles were aching for days afterwards. But done it now and so a big TICK off our bucket list.

Title: Sweaty but happy
Text: A lot of irregular steps make this climb a bit difficult and exhausting, but it is nonetheless worthy when you reach the top.

Title: Nice sunset on the top of Sigiriya
Text: Absolutely nice and wonderful world heritage place in Sri Lanka. Ancient technology is amazing here. Its very hard to identified how they bring water to the top of the rock.

Title: I overcame my fear of climbing heights!
Text: Nothing prepared me for this and I was glad I was wearing sturdy trainers.  The climb is quite steep for the uninitiated!  It's a combination of stone steps, some rickety and on occasions nothing to hold onto and metal open stairs, with railings.  You really have to look where you're going!  There are various stopping points on the way so you don't have to do it in one go. A good tip - our guide took us up early, as it opened - about 7.30 I think.  We were at the top by 9.  It's quite a steep climb in parts and not for the fainthearted, but I didn't see anyone turning back.  When you get to the top it's a stunning 360 degree vista and well worth the climb.  How they ever built a palace up there several hundred years ago, I can't imagine.  There are various interesting features on the way up and down, one being the wall paintings, hundreds of years old.  You have to climb up a metal spiral staircase on the side of the rock, but you are caged in.  As with many things in Sri Lanka, its very ad hoc!  What an amazing morning!

Title: Beware: Dont hire a guide!
Text: Not all guides created equal! Beware! You really dont need a guide! Buy the ticket pick up a brochure before bargaining for a guide. Go to the museum first and read the brochure. I ended up with a guide that was clearly drunk and kept talking about naked women pictures and swimming naked for the king to watch. He pointed to things and said their name that was clearly on the sign. Knowledge was abysmal. Then said the court was a night club. Seriously an idiot. I said it wasnt and he said same thing. I fired him on the spot. Ugh. Felt safer as a single female and more relaxed once he was gone

Title: Amazing sight
Text:
The only thing to do in Sigiriya, but an absolutely amazing must do thing. Due to the Sun and heat, do not start the tour later than 9AM in the morning.

The Way to the top is quite demanding and absolutely not for people who are not in decent or good shape. 3000 stairs up and down. No lift, no shadow but very rewarding when you are at the top.

Title: An Unique Rock Fortress
Text: It is one of those must visit places. The feeling is surprising and pleasing. Climbing is a bit hard for me. But the experience was worthy. Ancient paintings were thought provoking. It is almost believable how so many years ago human could achieve such rock structures. It will be ever fresh in my mind.

Title: Sigiriya Rock
Text: Awesome views . Tough climb for some . The views are spectacular. Take a local guide to understand the history

Title: Amazing
Text: Very nice... amazing rock in the very nice park. On the top is old city with a magnificent view...  must see in sri lanka

Title: Great morning, loved it all.
Text: I loved my trip to the rock. We got there around 0930 and it was not as hot as I expected or as busy. There were lots of people but not enough to stop it being enjoyable. My partner stayed at the base of the lions paws and I went all the way up. Both were spectacular. I didnt struggle with the walk as much as I anticipated, those gym classes must be paying off! I thought it was hilarious to find dogs at the very top!

Title: Lovely visit, would highly recommend
Text:
Very busy and over priced, watch out for the scammers, dont bother to climb it.
view of it is just as good

Title: Busy and over priced!!
Text: I wish more people were honest with their reviews as we would have never visited. It wasted half of our morning and didn't make it to the top as the que was so slow. Complete waste of money. I would recommend to climb Pidurangala instead and its free.

Title: Climbing Sigiriya Rock in Sri Lanka
Text:
We decided to venture to Sigiriya Rock, to climb to the top in order to see its famous views.  

On the way to the Rock itself, we were surrounded by beautiful manicured grounds, gardens, and pools.

As I have a fear of heights, I wasnt sure what to expect.  I will say that I struggled on the the way up and going down, as my anxiety took over.  My other half had no issues, but I found the narrow and very open stairs difficult to traverse.  Having to stop a few times, not due to the physical activity, but for me to be able to control my vertigo.

The trek, and shaky legs, were worth it as the views were worth it.  From the top, you can view a 360 degree view that Sri Lanka has to offer.  One view was reminiscent of a Jurassic period of a beautiful lake leading to a distant mountain.  You will also see remnants of a fortress, as well as some wildlife (mind the cheeky monkeys, as they will steal what they can).

I would highly recommend it, as the adrenaline rush is great.  Those with a paralysing fear of heights... dont go.  

Note:  Go early, bring water and sunscreen, as there is very little shade on the top.  Also, go to the bathroom before heading up, as there are no facilities on the the way up and on top (a poor gentleman learned the hard way ??).

Title: Sigiriya Rock Fortress well worth the climb.
Text: Looking up at the 200 meter climb along the outside of the rock was a little daunting but onnce on the way up it was much easier than expected especially after having biked 75km that day. The 360 degree views of the area were breathtaking.

Title: Special place!
Text: We hiked up very early in the morning to avoid the intense heat and the anticipated crowds as it was a holiday in Sri Lanka.  We were a group of ten women with a private  guide and all different fitness levels. Lots of places to stop and have a drink of water as you sure need it with the heat and the sweat from the heat.  There are many willing helpers wanting to help the tourist make it to the top and one lady In our group needed that little extra support. They negotiated a price for the help and it was more then reasonable .  He carried her pack and helped her by supporting her elbow over steeper stairs. He was great.  So glad we did it! Beautiful and peaceful and the views spectacular. We were fortunate to have a private guide with us  in our group (not our helper) who explained the history of this amazing site!

Title: Impressive site
Text: Very nice sacred site. 30$ the entrance but worth the money. If u have vertigo it may be an issue to reach the top. Safe, clean and well organized unless you end up with big groups and have to queue on the staircase...i went there at 10am and it was not too crowded so not sure early morning is a good idea as recommended as many people are doing that.

Title: A wonder of the world
Text:
Took me by surpise how magnific it is. I can hardly imagine what a wonder it was when everything worked and people lived in it.
The rock itself is a very special, add to that the ingenuity how they used it. 

1200 steps, worth every one of them. Sound frighteningly high but you will manage. There are sections where you are almost alone, but you are gonna cue especially on the iron steps and there you can catch your breath.

It is good to have a guide. There are several licensed ones and I suggest that you take one of them ( you can hardly avoid). They show you detailes you could very easily miss.

The view upstairs is stunning as you can expect.

Title: A must see in Sri Lanka
Text:
Visiting the ruins at the top of this incredible rock formation requires a bit of effort, but the view once up will pay back with interests!
Definitely worth to go late afternoon for the sunset, and to avoid the hottest hours.
The whole site is well maintained.

Title: Really great thing
Text: A unique fortress with surrounding gardens. Everything built in and used for only some 10 years. They did it without modern technology. Shame on us

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: WOW. Awsome sight driving up to the site. 1222 steps to summit, not a trip for the faint hearted, but well worth the strenuous effort needed.300 meters above sea level. Wall paintings in excellent condition considering the age of them. Be careful of the monkeys trying to steal anything.

Title: Amazing UNESCO heritage site
Text: Fascinating insight into Sri Lankan history so well preserved and presented! The museum and grounds are extremely interesting but do be aware the walk to the top is not suitable for those of us with mobility issues!

Title: about 1200 steps to the top
Text: Magnificent views from the top and an amazing climb with 100's of others, Best to start around 7 AM while its cooler. Great history and a must do in Sri Lanka. Coming down is very easy.

Title: Great historic site - Must Visit
Text: This is a great historic site. It is well worth the effort of climbing up to see the various points of interest but the bit is the actual views when you get to the top of the rock. This is a must visit site when you are in Sri Lanka. Make it a full day trip to get the best out of your visit.

Title: The climb
Text:
Took me some time to decide scaling Sigiriya due to one bad knee but am glad I attempted it upon hearing the story behind it and reached the top after much huffing and puffing.  Having done it, I must say the stairs are manageable if you pace yourself and keep hydrated as the temperatures can go up as the day progresses. There are also many locals who would offer to help for a fee, but I found that saying no thanks decisively holds them at bay. 

After reaching the Lion's Staircase, the climb u the metal stairs are a little more steep with less resting platforms but once you reach the top, one can appreciate the ruins of this architectural monument. Hard to imagine how one can build a palace on the rock until you see the remnants of ancient urban planning for yourself.

Title: Breathtaking Heritage!!!
Text: This is one of the impressive UNESCO World Heritage Sites we have visited. Steep entrance fee LKR5,460 per person, but it is well worth it! Since 5th century, this place was built by the King Kashyapa who killed his father, King Dhatusena, usurping the throne of his father. He eventually fled to Sigiriya from Anuradhapura to avoid the retaliation of his half-brother, Moggallana who was the rightful heir of the throne. Kashyapa ordered to build fortress and palace on top of Sigiriya Rock. Eventually, Moggallana came to Sigiriya for revenge and war was declared between the brothers. Kashyapa lost the battle and committed suicide, and Moggallana returned to Anuradhapura after winning the battle, and Sigiriya Rock was converted to a monastery. Four parts to appreciate this site: First, the fortress at the foot of the rock with viewing site of Sirigiya Rock from far after passing by the main entrance surrounded by moat. Some of the highlights are the Summer Palace, Cobra Hood Cave, etc. Second, the decoration of the authentic fresco half way up to the rock, reachable by spiral staircase. Third, the small plateau half way up the rock with massive gateway of Lion Rock with gigantic rock carvings of Lion Paw as entrance to the palace to the top of the rock. Fourth, where is the last part at top of rock where the ruins of the palace is located. The idea of building a Palace on top of a massive rock is already very incredible! 360 degree panoramic views from the top is amazing with sunset view in the evening. In summary, this heritage consists of intriguing historical background, plus the incredible architecture back then in 5th century. It is one of the highlights of our Sri Lanka trip!

Title: Fantastic
Text: You have to start your trip at 5am to beat the heat, 32 degrees when I visited, but worth it. Stunning views from the top

Title: Out of this world
Text: Took us by surprise how magnificent it is. I can hardly imagine what a wonder it was when everything worked and people lived in it. Definitely worth to go late afternoon for the sunset, or early in the morning for the sunrise and to avoid the hottest hours. The whole site is well maintained

Title: Stunning
Text:
The view of the rock from ground level is inspiring, the views from the top make every step & bead of sweat worth it. 
Its £25 to get in, so not cheap. 
The gardens are immaculate & then the reality sets in. 
In fairness its not too hard of a climb if your averagely fit. First the stone steps up to a kind of balcony. Up a tight spiral staircase to see the cave paintings, then back down to the balcony. This staircase is optional. Then up a few more stone steps to a rest point, were you can top up your water bottles for no charge. 
Then the slightly scary metal steps. There are around 7 flights of 25ish steps. You dont need to go straight up them all in 1 go. 
Then the impact of the view hits you. 
There is shade at the top which is very welcome. 
Ps there are monkeys everywhere including up all the staircases.

Title: Make sure you are fit!!
Text:
Awesome 5th Century palace split into 2 sections. One palace is at the bottom of the rock and the other at the top. Many many many steps, even on the lower section and they can be uneven and worn in places. A lot of the steps still have their original white marble coverings and when the are wet are extremely slippy. Get a Guide, the whole history of the place is brought alive. The guides don't have a set cost, you just tip them what you think their service was worth. The frescoes are incredible. I would say that getting here (halfway up) is a must, even if you can't make it to the top. The rock formations and the construction techniques used to build the place are quite awe inspiring. The views from the top are simply stunning, but it rained the day that we were there and was somewhat misty. You may want think about if the climb is worth it on a rainy day. Slight downer was that you had to run the gauntlet of the looky looky men on the way out and the attendants in the Free public toilets practically hold you to ransom for toilet paper and a tip. 
Very long journey by private car to get there (about 4.5 hrs) from the Bentota area south of Colombo.

Title: Stunning when you get to the top
Text: It is a long hike to the top with a lot of stairs, some rock hewn others metal spiral staircases and its quite hard work though they do provide helpers if you need them. The view from the top is stunning but even if you only get to the frescos or the lions paw its worth it. You can always turn round if it gets too much.

Title: Lots of steps but well worth it!
Text: If youre visiting, I recommend you get a guide. We were told about the history of sigiriya rock, the king and his 500 some concubines. It was all very interesting. There are lots of places to stop and rest if needed. The view at the top is amazing!

Title: EXCELLENT IN SO MANY WAYS
Text: This is a fine World Heritage Site best visited in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid as much as possible the heat. From passing through the various gardens to the physical exercise involved, it is not to be missed. The Sigiriya Damsels are superb frescoes. The Lion's Paws is its own 'wow factor'. The views from above, quite apart from the cool breezes, are great. There are other areas of great interest on the way down to the parking lot like the Audience Hall and the Cobra Hood Cave. If you have the time to wander both below and above, so much the better.

Title: YOUR REWARD AFTER THE SLOG
Text: There is no T-shirt to proclaim your success of making it to the palace area but you will be rewarded with cool breezes and an excellent  360 degree panorama of the region. Little is left of the royal palace but it is amazing to think about the labour it took to get all the materials to the top, quite apart from any construction. The area is terraced. You can find some nice pools. If you have the time, an hour will allow you to give the entire area a good examination.

Title: Interesting World Heritage Site not to be Missed
Text: We enjoyed our visit and hike to the top of the rock.  It is amazing that so many years ago a king could build a palace and city so high up.  This visit was one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka.  We could see our hotel's pool in the distance.

Title: What an amazing place!
Text: This is one of the "must visit" sites in Sri Lanka. We climbed it many years ago when we were much younger and this time just wandered around the lovely water gardens and rocks around the base enjoying the views and the serenity. The place never fails to enchant!

Title: so beautiful
Text: very nice place nice view sunset so beautiful tickets little high but amazing place great time there

Title: Fantastic - a must do
Text: Truly spectacular this place. Not only the climb itself with 1200 stair steps to take, but definitely also the ancient frescos and the views at the top are breath taking !!! Easily spend here 3 hours to fully enjoy all there is to see.

Title: Advice for people with a fear of heights.
Text:
Trip advisor Sigiriya 

I am writing this mainly for people who, like me, have a fear of heights. 

Most reviews focus on the effort of getting up the rock. I am moderately fit and found it hardly taxing at all. My Apple Watch said I had climbed 48 flights of stairs but it did not feel anywhere near that much. 

More of a challenge for me was the height and especially the two separate  flights of iron stairs. 

I had debated whether to do the climb at all and was pretty apprehensive. Having done it, my advice would be to do it if you have a mild fear of heights or a moderate fear that is under control ie not subject to serious panic attacks. It also helps to have a supportive companion. I would suggest not doing it if your fear is more severe. 

Most stairs are stone with balustrades but there are two iron sections:-
One that leads up from the mirror wall via a caged-in iron spiral staircase to the cave paintings. (You go up to the paintings but then have to come down again to continue.) The steps are solid so one cannot see the drop below but of course you can look out as you go round. I managed this by focussing on the central post of the staircase and talking encouragingly to myself! if you are anxious about this you can probably bypass the cave paintings and head straight for the Lions Claw platform, although the paintings are interesting. 

Another section leads up from the Lions Claws level to the top. This has iron sections crossing the rock, again with solid steps, but is more exposed. Going up was easier as one faces the rock. I was more anxious about coming down but my husband went in front of me so I could hold on to his back with one hand and the railing with the other. The walkway gets quite crowded which slows the descent but means you are surrounded by people. This made me feel less exposed. I was nervous but it was very manageable. I have found other places more challenging like going up a tower in San Giminiano and inside the dome of St Pauls. 

I would make two other points:-
There are guides along the way who look out for people who look anxious and are quite insistent about holding your hand. Kind but probably better declined. 
The remains at the top and the views are very impressive - well worth the effort - and if you get there with your fear of heights, a real achievement. 

I hope this is helpful - it would have helped me if I had been able to read this before I went.

Title: Breathtaking views
Text: Popular location. On the day we went it was extremely busy and it was a slow step by step climb in single file. This made it an easier climb as there was no rushing or having to stop for a rest on the way up. For those who want to go half way, there is a option to stop at the lion's foot and then head . Be aware that, as with many tourist attractions, it is free or very minimal cost for the locals but there is a hefty entrance fee for tourists. View from the top and from the lookouts on the way are breathtakig.

Title: Great Heritage
Text: Truly a wonder of Asia. Huge rock fortress reflecting a great culture and heritage standing high touching the blue sky showing spectacular views all around from the top of the rock.

Title: Cracking panoramic views
Text: Large rock near dambulla in North Central Sri Lanka showing ruins of former civilisation.  Not huge amount of remains remain but the real pull is the rock climb. This consists of a number of sections of steps up to the summit. Some of the metal staircases hammered into the rock feel a bit hairy if you have the fear of heights but worth the climb and visit. I was more concerned at the numerous signs warning you to be quiet less you get stung by a swarm of wasps of hornets. Apparently its happened a few times over the years and I wasn't keen on joining the ranks. I purposely kept well clear of the loud and. excitable Italian group at the time of my visit. Cost was pretty high at about 20 each. There is another peak of a similar height that also holds some lesser ruins nearby which is visible from Siguryi and only costs $5 for a more natural climb.

Title: Absolutely stunning!!
Text:
We went really early in the morning to avoid the crowds and so glad we did. The climb we easy to access with nonstop views and photo opportunities. It can be a challenge for some, but well worth the effort. The top is breathtaking and so peaceful (without all the people). This is a MUST see! Highlight of our trip so far...

When we got down there were thousands of people, so get up there first to appreciate it more!

Title: Fantastic Experience
Text: We hired a local guide and hiked up the rock.  It was crowded, especially because we went on a local full moon holiday, but it didn't detract from the experience and we loved seeing the grounds and ruins.

Title: Not to be missed
Text: Sigiriya rock looks imposing. At first, we were scared we might be too unfit to climb it. Such fears proved to be baseless, however. The climb is very easy. Anyone in good health should be able to make it, and they should! This castle is something out of a medieval fairy tale. It's absolutely stunning. Its history is fascinating, too! Go and see it!

Title: Disappointed
Text: Too crowded that you don't enjoy. And very expensive around 30$ and for locals only 5Rupis. The place is amazing to see but to be hours of waiting lines for achieve the highest points is really disappointing.

Title: Sigiriya Lion Rock fortress...well worth the climb!
Text: Had a fun day at Lion Rock! This is a serious rock with a fascinating history but the climb is not for the faint-hearted or the unfit. As a 65yr old in decent condition it was still a reasonable challenge. There seemed to be some doing the climbing who may have under-estimated it. Its 1-way up and 1-way down so turning back might be an issue. There are places to take a breather along the way. You should have good non-slip footwear, enough water, camera and as little to carry as possible. You will get hot and sweaty! Having said all that....go for it! The view is spectacular! For others who dont feel up to the climb there is a museum and interesting parklands to walk thru. Be warned of spruikers claiming to be official guides and who wont take no for an answer but I suppose can be helpful to assist the less agile.

Title: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
Text: 2000 years old and with a history going back before that, the climb up to the top of the rock fortress Sigiriya is a must do. Take time to check out the museum - it has some basic information but is helpful in understanding the history of this place. There is so much yet to uncover. 2400ish steps will get you to the top but the half way mark at the lions paws offers great views too. Wall frescos are a little detour on the way. As a foreigner, if you have a guide youll learn a lot more about the place.

Title: The ancient Sigiriya fortress.
Text: This was an amazing fortress set upon a massive rock that towers over the forest. The climb is a little scary if you are not good with heights. But the view is amazing. The crowds do make the climb up and down are little long as you have to wait in a line.  Remember to bring ID

Title: Remarkable Heritage Point
Text:
Firstly, this point should be covered either early morning or later afternoon unless the weather is good. 
If it is hot, then you might not enjoy this place that much.

Coming to the place now. Entry Fee is 15 USD for SAARC nations and 30 USD for others. I paid 2760 LKR per person. 

You have to walk for about 10 minutes to reach the point from where the climb begins. 
However, the place is extremely well managed and surpassed my expectations. 

It is a world heritage site and known as the eighth wonder. 

There are gardens and mini water bodies on both the sides. 
There is a very small bridge with water on both the sides just after the ticket checkpoint and one can have nice clicks standing on that.

Please DO NOT THROW away your tickets after this point since it is again checked midway into the ascent.

Coming to the climb, there are about 1200 steps. The difficulty is moderate. It surely tests your stamina.

But if the weather is good, it is all worth it.

As you keep on climbing, the view of entire surrounding just keeps on getting better. I doubt if you can get better views from any other place.

It took us about 30-40 minutes to complete the climb. Do not recollect noticing any restrooms on the way so be mindful of that.

Once you reach the top, you truly appreciate the work that has been done at such a height. It is a refreshing feeling at the top.

You can easily spend an hour at the top, just sitting and roaming around.

While climbing down, check with someone the way to Tourist Car Parking area since that is different from the original place where your driver might have dropped you.

It is must visit place. If the weather is on your side, then you will have an Unforgettable time.

This was the best sightseeing point for us on our entire Sri Lanka trip.

Title: Beautiful landmark with amazing views
Text:
Sigiriya is one of the eight World Heritage Sites of Sri Lanka. It is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning worldwide. There are remains of an extensive network of gardens and reservoirs. Some structures like fountains are still intact today.
The monolithic rock itself is a lava plug left over from an ancient long extinct volcano. It rises 200 m from the green scrub jungle surrounding it. Today on top the visitor finds the ruins of what was once a king´s fortress in the sky.  
While climbing up the steps there was a lady before us who got in the middle of a fight between a monkey and a dog. She got bitten by the dog and needed to go down to get treated by the red cross at the lions gate. This is nothing that you would like to happen to you. So be aware of stray dogs and over-curious monkeys. If they approach you too boldly you might want to try out a self defense technique Marcell has discovered to be effective. He has successfully kept monkeys distant by using insect repellent.

Title: Amazing rock.
Text: Is a must see thing here. The rock is so amazing. Have to walk a short distance to reach the bottom then climb the stairs up. Can be scary for those weak hearts as the stairs are along the rock. After the lions paw the stairs are much steeper and narrow so walk with caution. On top is flat, able to view the surroundings and capture nice pictures. Beware of the monkeys too as they are everywhere.

Title: Mammoth structure
Text: World heritage venue worth the effort and surrounding views. Lots of history albeit this should have been presented in a better way. Museum is ordinary. Steep climbing recommended only for super-fit genre. $30 entry fee is relatively expensive.

Title: Must see
Text: This is a must see! Make sure you get here early to beat the crowds. When we came it was raining so there wasnt many people which made it great

Title: No words to describe!!!
Text:
This sightseeing was always in mu bucket list. When i visited i felt amazed by the view of the rock fortress, by the area and the views and remains on the top. I can write for hours for this marvellous world herittage. Everyone must visit it at least once.
It makes you wonder who made this at those ages and how a single rock can be there in the middle of the jungle.
We strongly recommend it to visit it around 11 in the morning when there are not so many crowds and wear trainers which will help you climp up all those stairs.
The dissadvantages and the points that should be mentioned is the high entrance fee especially when you have to spend hundreds of dollars till you reach that point, some locals were to noisy and annoying,not respecting their own sightseing moreover other people that tried to enjoy it and take photos by pushing them or standing in front of them. Local people are so nice and kind but there are some among them that ruin everything, this need to change...we saw even one of them spitting inside the monument.
The activity is not recommended for elder,young kids and disabled although we see many of these categories which you can guess...causing problems. Sad for such a place.

Title: A must do in Sri Lanka!
Text: Did this hike 7am - the ideal time. Just before the crowds and the temperature increased. Loved it! Its about 30USD to get in. They offer you a tour guide for extra fee, we didnt bother. The views at the top are fab! Lots of steps, but nothing too drastic. Some people were wearing flip flops, we wore trainers and Id definitely advise that!

Title: Over 1200 steps!
Text:
Beautiful ancient site, well worth the visit. Cost is $30 USD or 5460 rupees at todays exchange rate.

Stairs are an easy climb and there are many "rest" areas (straight stretches).

Wonderful to be a part of a this history, and to see the ryins of the ancient fortress

Title: Exhillarating climb to the top
Text:
For me it was an achievement as I had had surgery a couple of weeks prior and was nervous about the climb especially as our driver mentioned that we would be 4 hours or so. It was a challenge but doable and a great feeling when you reach the top. 
We only took one bottle of water each (contrary to others advise, which Im glad I didn't take) and only had a drink when we got to the top (or it will weigh you down). Also visit the washroom before you start. We arrived at 830 after breakfast and had a very comfortable climb without to many people, however on our way down, there were heaps of people crawling single file up the stairs.... you can go for sunrise if you choose and its quiet but dark.
Spectacular views 360 degrees

Title: Spectacular
Text:
I climbed the other rock the day before, and was told by many that sigirya wasn't worth the money, same view, same experience. This is not the case the view from the top is so different and the rock is full of history.

Steep stairs, but a quick climb for the height of the rock.

Don't be overwhelmed, I was concerned about my fear of heights, just don't over think it, 1 step at a time and look into the rock.

Title: Not too hard a climb, and quite touristy
Text:
The mood at the top is not bad, even though there are many tourists, if you wait a while and walk to other areas, you are able to find a silent spot. 

There are handlebars to accompany you all the way, I think this is a good thing, but made the area less ''authentic".

Not sure about the museum, maybe I can go again.

Title: Utterly impressive
Text: Awe inspiring and it never ceases to impress.  I hope that the US$30 entry fee for tourists really goes back into the conservation of such an important archaeological titan.  Interesting visiting the museum to see the reconstructed superstructure of palace buildings on top of the rock.

Title: Perfect for travel goers
Text: Sigiriya is surely a wonderful place to visit, with its title as the most vital place of the Cultural Triangle in Sri Lanka. We had a nice stroll in the location with some of my family members. this is one of the wonders of the ancient world. I would recommend to visit early morning or evening to skip the strong sunlight.

Title: Just amazing
Text: Just amazing. So many steps (more then 2300) by fantastic view and spirit there . Spectacular view from the top of all valley. In the top is like Machu Picchu .Get strong rain in the top and same time in the valley was sunny . Really recommend, but take good shoes and have enough power to go top

Title: A Climb to Remember
Text: Meander through narrow rock passageway and steep stairs to the summit of Sigiriya's Ancient Fortress, also known as the Lion's Rock. This charming site was once the palace ground for the ancient king and his 500 wives. Do check out the oldwall paintings and climb the 1200 steps to the summit for the breathtaking views of the surrounding atmosphere.

Title: Amazing views
Text: As the most popular attraction in the area it wasn't ridiculous the amount of people there, not helped by arriving at the same time as 3 coaches of tourists. I strongly suggest to wear decent footwear and avoid sandals or flip-flops as the steps can be wet and dusty from the dirt around. The walk up is a bit steep but all steps and once you reach the main part of the rock you get a lovely breeze. The stairs are the busy bit, once you're at the top it fans out over the ruins and there is plenty of exploring to do. Head for the far corner with the royal pool and see the balcony for a great pano shot. I'm sure if your visiting Sigiriya you wouldn't miss this but just to say it's a must do. If you're feeling a bit fit and energetic head to the other rock that over looks Sigiriya for some amazing photos (be warned it's a bit of rock climbing(

Title: Honeymoon
Text: We stayed in Sigiriya for a few days and this was a must for us. It certainly didnt disappoint. At over 200m high the views over Sigiriya are spectacular. We were told to visit early in the morning before it gets to hot and busy, this certainly pays off.

Title: Historic wonder !
Text: This fort is really amazing and one of the best places we visited in Sri Lanka. The views from top are amazing.

Title: Super Hard work, but well worth it
Text: This place is stunning, Take it slow and you'll get to the top. Carry as little as possible but make sure you have water. Make sure you have a good pair of trainers. Oh and dont forget your camera, the views are amazing.

Title: Well worth the effort
Text: There is really no need for a guide, with the good information plaques throughout and the free pamphlet with a map you will be will equipped information wise. Take as little to carry as possible, it is a tough climb but there are plenty of places you can rest. I hate heights but took it slowly and did not look until I was right at the top,  there is plenty of space there so felt safe. Go as early in the day as possible.

Title: Take it slow and easy
Text:
A very interesting attraction, I got to the murals only as it was hot and very humid, I was amazed at the views across the land and how flat it was. I loved seeing all the gardens, cave shrines and the workmanship of the stonework.
Definitley a place to visit.

Title: Spectacular view and ancient city
Text:
A visit to this UN World Heritage Site is a must. It's an exhilarating climb and amazing remnants of the ancient civilization that built this fortress city centuries ago.  We recommend staying at one of the great hotels just walking distance from the site, so you can get an early start before the crowds and the heat increase.
We were fortunate to have a break in the rain for the morning, and were treated to fantastic views from the top. It's a steep climb but all stairs with handrails, so even those with aversion to heights should be able to stomach this.
Carry as little as possible other than camera and plenty of drinking water. No need to hire a guide as there is signage throughout, and if you read up even a little in advance you will have a good understanding of what you are seeing.

Title: Great, great, great!!!!!!
Text:
The way up is a bit difficult if you are not fit. But it's worth it! 
The view of the valley through and from the top is beautiful. You are standing on a rock, on the ruins of a former city surrounded by jungle! Fantastically!

Title: Extraordinary views!
Text:
It will well worth the journey up to the very top if you can.  The views from up there see unforgettable.  You can see everything.  It is tough to imagine from the bottom how many buildings could have been up there during it time, however,  when you reach the summit, you can see how vast an area it really is.  If would have been a truly magnificent site when all the buildings are temples were standing!

The walk is quite tough, especially on a hot day.  There are lots of different heights steps so.e of which are steep.  You must also take a metal staircase up to the top via the side of the rock, which could be scary fot those afraid of heights.

On the way up, the frecos on the ceilings are worth looking at. Remember no pictures, but it is amazing to see how vivid and detailed the paintings are still, and unbelievable to think the whole area would have been covered in such figures.

The gardens at the bottom are equally majestic.  They are vast and very well preserved. you could easily walk around these and not do anything else.  There is also an ebony tree in the gardens which is worth looking out for.

A must if staying in Sigiriya.  It is a once in a lifetime experience

Title: Hard climb, busy and $30 is too much
Text: I realise it's a main attraction, but 30 USD pp is pretty ridiculous. Especially when locals pay about 50 cents!. Its a hard climb up thousands of steps and can get really crowded. View is nice and good to say have done it. Sri Lanka tourism/government really need to rethink how much they gouge tourists.

Title: Wonders of man and nature combined
Text:
My first time climbing a rock fortress. I have climbed many mountains, visited dozens of temples and ancient sites to. However this one is awe inspiring and majestic both in its simplicity and 'remote' location. Located a few hundred kilometers (and miles) from Colombo, you can book several tours that will get you there in a few hours from any part of Sri Lanka. It is an island after all. 

We spent a few hours here after going to Dambulla and I'm glad we did, as this was scenic yet serene. A tour guide is not necessary as the place speaks for itself and large group tours can be rushed to get from A to B. We were in a small group and allowed to take our time. Even though we did this, I could easily have spent more time exploring the place and taking in the setting. Its not an arduous climb, although the spiral metal staircase about halfway to the top can leave one feeling a bit dizzy. However, if you have vertigo you would not be climbing this rock. One of my favorite places in Sri Lanka, which is a beautiful country. Definitely would recommend a visit if in Sri Lanka.

Title: Wet but Still Worth It.
Text:
We deliberated on whether we would visit and climb the rock as we had a 2.5hr drive from Kandy to Sigiriya and the weather was poor (as it is in October). We made the journey, and we didnt regret it. It was a good experience, it essentially rained the entire climb which meant just taking it easy to avoid slipping. It is over priced like everyone else has mentioned (but so is stone henge, and that was far more disappointing!). When it isnt wet, its very quickly very hot (so bring water!). 

On reflection I would consider not climbing the rock when it is wet. It becomes seriously slippery, the stairs become the run off for water and you are exposed to the elements when at height. If something was to go wrong, youd be in a bit of strife. 

We went on a Monday at approx 10:30am and it wasnt busy and we were back in our car by 12:30pm.

A guide could be handy next time to give you context on the history (we overheard one guide for a couple and he was very informative). But make sure they are wearing a white guise top

Title: Amazing place
Text: Very nice location special for sunrise, nedt time visit 6:30 morning afternoon very hot and busy....

Title: Worth the climb, but watch out for so-called guides
Text:
At  USD 25 per person, not a cheap day out for a family  But that is true of most sights in Sri Lanka.

There are over 2000 steps, but its not as bad as it sounds as they are quite well spaced out into various sections (2 main ones).  And the view at the top is definitely worth the effort.  

If you are a little wary of heights watch out for the official looking guides (in matching T shirts) who will rush to help you (or may help even if you don't need it).  In particular they can be found on the last steep section (as you go through the lion paws). Once you are at the top they will demand money for their services!  And not small amounts at 1000 Rps.

Luckily we had our own real guide for our tour of Sri Lanka.  And there are a lot of details that he relayed that made our visit all the more interesting.  For example, how did they get water to the top of the rock?  And pointing out  the fountains fed from pools at the top of the rock.

If you are lucky you may spot a crocodile in the pools at the base.

I highly recommend getting there in the morning before the sun rises over the rock and beats down onto the steps.  We arrived around 0930 and were back down within a couple of hours and were in the shade whilst climbing.

Title: Very impressive. Must visit
Text:
This ancient attraction is just as impressive and awe-inspiring as websites and other reviewers have said. The site is a massive one and other than the rock fortress (for which there is an entry fee), there are other places which visitors can roam for free. As you get down, you will be approached by numerous guides who will try to dissuade you from buying tickets to the rock fortress by mentioning the arduous 1200 step climb and instead offer you a tuk-tuk ride covering the places which are free. They arent aggressive but can be pushy, so you need to firmly tell them off.
Foreigners need to but tickets from the museum (entry to which is USD 5 if brought separately and complimentary if you purchase the rock fortress tickets). The museum is a good place to start off your visit.
The tickets to the rock fortress are USD 30 for adults and USD 15 for children. SAARC country nationals are entitled to a 50% discount on the adult price but no further discounts for children (so USD 15 for both adults and children). Payment can be made in USD or LKR but change, if any, is returned in LKR.
The climb itself is actually quite difficult, especially if you go in the afternoon. The place is also crowded on weekends because of lots of locals coming for a picnic.
My suggestion would be to go early morning to beat the heat and the crowds. Carry lots of water and snacks as well, as there werent any outlets selling food or water.
The way up is different from the way down, so take pictures as you go up, because you wont get the same view on the way down.
A lot of people have suggested the recommended length as being 3-4 hours but from my experience, it takes a lot longer, especially if you have young children and also explore the whole place. So in my opinion, take your time and enjoy the whole place in all its splendour and beauty. Dont try to rush things through and combine this with another attraction (like Dambulla, Anuradhapura etc) because those places too require more than 3-4 hours and it would be better to comprehensively cover both places rather than do a bit of both.

Title: Cool ruins and an epic climb
Text: We had a great day climbing up to the ancient ruins. Strenuous but worth the views and sense of accomplishment!

Title: Cairo city and giza pyramids
Text: Thanks to Mohamed Elshaer for bringing us around pyramids and Cairo.its good to know about ancient history of Egypt in details.

Title: Awe inspiring and a great workout!
Text:
It's hard to beleive that this was man made so many years ago on top of this rock without modern technology and tools. It's a tough climb up the stairs but if you start early in the morning just when the park is opening it will be easier. We also went in October where the weather was not so hot and cooled down by the rain showers.
Sigiriya refuses to reveal its secrets easily, and you'll have to climb a series of very narrow steps. The staircases attached to sheer walls to reach the top. On the way you'll pass a series of quite remarkable frescoes and a pair of colossal lion's paws carved into the bedrock. The surrounding landscape  lily-pad-covered moats, water gardens and cave shrines  only add to Sigiriya's rock-star appeal.

Title: Just WoW....
Text:
The effort to climb all the way up 70 floors is worth every drop of sweat. Try to visit on a working day in order to avoid the rush. carry enough drinking water, wear good shoes with grip and do not miss to carry a CAMERA....believe me you will not regret the climb. 

For those who have excuses this being steep...Our group had a 3 & 4 Year Old who were very enthusiastic to climb all the way :).

MUST Experience...for Sri Lanka, THE View, History, Art, Adventurous climb.

Title: Not worth the money
Text: Honestly this tourist attraction is really overpriced. I guess that everyone just wants to say that they climbed Sigiraya, but I don't think it's worth the hype. Sure it's cool, but climbing the small rock (nearby) was actually more fun.

Title: Beautiful view
Text:
So many stairs!!! But so worth it. We went in the afternoon and encountered only few tourists. Make sure you take a bottle of water with you as the climb is exhausting. 
The view for the top is amazing, so beautiful.
The ticket is a bit expensive - 30$ per pers.

Title: Very impressive. Must visit
Text:
This ancient attraction is just as impressive and awe-inspiring as websites and other reviewers have said. The site is a massive one and other than the rock fortress (for which there is an entry fee), there are other places which visitors can roam for free. As you get down, you will be approached by numerous guides who will try to dissuade you from buying tickets to the rock fortress by mentioning the arduous 1200 step climb and instead offer you a tuk-tuk ride covering the places which are free. They arent aggressive but can be pushy, so you need to firmly tell them off.
Foreigners need to but tickets from the museum (entry to which is USD 5 if brought separately and complimentary if you purchase the rock fortress tickets). The museum is a good place to start off your visit.
The tickets to the rock fortress are USD 30 for adults and USD 15 for children. SAARC country nationals are entitled to a 50% discount on the adult price but no further discounts for children (so USD 15 for both adults and children). Payment can be made in USD or LKR but change, if any, is returned in LKR.
The climb itself is actually quite difficult, especially if you go in the afternoon. The place is also crowded on weekends because of lots of locals coming for a picnic.
My suggestion would be to go early morning to beat the heat and the crowds. Carry lots of water and snacks as well, as there werent any outlets selling food or water.
The way up is different from the way down, so take pictures as you go up, because you wont get the same view on the way down.
A lot of people have suggested the recommended length as being 3-4 hours but from my experience, it takes a lot longer, especially if you have young children and also explore the whole place. So in my opinion, take your time and enjoy the whole place in all its splendour and beauty. Dont try to rush things through and combine this with another attraction (like Dambulla, Anuradhapura etc) because those places too require more than 3-4 hours and it would be better to comprehensively cover both places rather than do a bit of both.

Title: Well worth the climb to the top.
Text: An amazing place and well worth the clinb to the top( 2202 steps ). we had a guide and this was very worthwhile as history of this site is exstensive and interesting.

Title: Beautiful cave and story
Text: First you go through the place where the palace was build, you can still see remains of baths and lodges, once you pass this you start a small hike in combination with a lot of stairs which go up and bring you to where the king of Sigiriya lived. It's so cool to see the paws of the lion, eventhough no one actually knows for sure that the head was ever there.. Somewhere in between you can see the cloudy-women which is also nice to see. The view from the lionsrock is pretty cool and you could see many types of land, its truely amazing!

Title: A Must
Text: A long climb, but worth it for the view.  I climbed on a very hot humid day.  Beware of the cheeky monkeys though.

Title: Accomplishment
Text: The rock was a difficult climb but worth it when you get to the top to see the amazing views. The jungle all around. The top was nothing but but ruins and parts of walls here and there but it represented history. Make sure you have water with you and recommended to climb early in morning before the sun is at its strongest point. The monkeys halfway up were posing for the camera however be careful, they tend to steal items they can grab when you are not looking for from your bags.

Title: Lion Rock
Text: Magnificent location and wonderful history. Worth the climb to the top. Go early in the morning to avoid crowds and the heat as the climb up 1200 steps can be a challenge.

Title: Worth the Climb in the Rain
Text: The rock itself was amazing and worth the climb even in the rain. Please be wary though when raining it is very slippery and bring wipes as you will get rust all over your hands. Lots of tourists stalls after but still a must see stop in Sri Lanka. Great views.

Title: Can do with children and elderly
Text: Set out early in the morning so you avoid the sun. Do carry umbrellas. It rains on and off. We left at 6. My six year old was ahead of us the whole time urging us on :-) We met really old people making their way down so you can do it if your knees arent bad. The view from the top is totally worth it. Watch out for the dogs at the very top before you open your snack boxes. Sometimes dogs and monkeys can cause some trouble. A monkey reached for my back pack... fancy that...

Title: Great historical site spoiled by insistent local guides.
Text: While we enjoyed the historical site, the insistence of young local guides to man handle you up and down the many sets of stairs and then argue about how much they should be paid spoilt the experience. Be sure to clearly indicate you don't want help or negotiate your price before you begin your experience.

Title: The Painting and the view worth the climb
Text:
Well, the climb itself is a challenge and quite rewarding. I, personally enjoyed the exercise. You don't have to be in great shape to do it, since one can take his time and climb slowly. I've seen elderly women in their late 60's or even 70's, with walking canes, that climbed it all the way to the top (very slowly, though). So I guess that any healthy person can do it!
The view was spectacular and the frescoes are beautiful and intriguing. definitely worth the effort. 
DON'T FORGET TO TAKE A LOT OF WATER AND A SNACK! You don't want to find yourself with no water on the top of the stares.

Title: Amazing view of the plain
Text: Climbing up to the Rock Palace is a good exercise, need to be careful of the wasps.  There were first aid tent set up on site in case any tourist got stung by the wasps. Amazing view when you reach the top and get to see the ancient palace on top of the rock.

Title: Nice Historical Site
Text:
You cannot visit Sri Lanka without going here and climbing the famous rock.
 It would have been quicker had there not been so many people.
Make sure you go first thing in the morning to avoid the intense afternoon heat.
The views at the top are simply stunning and when you reach the top.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text: This amazing ancient palace has not been completely excavated, but even what you can see now is amazing and an indication of how grand it once was.  The entrance cost for local and foreigners are different.  It is advisable to get one of the Sigiriya guides that works at the site.  There are many around.  There are also quite a number of steps to climb up to the top.  There were guides who helps you up the stairs, but be aware, if they keep helping you, a tip is expected and our family unwittingly fell into this tourist trap and paid USD10 per person for this unnecessary service.  Other than this little annoyance, the rest of the sightseeing was absolutely fantastic.  Expect to spend 2-3 hours there and be aware there are no toilets after the park entrance.

Title: Beautiful historical site
Text: It is a beautiful place, and if you imagine it was built in the 6th century, it gets even more amazing! It's expensive for tourists, that is true, but to us it was worth it. If you go outside the main season there will be no lines or crowds. The ticket office closes at 17h/5pm and the stairs to the top close at 17h30/5:30pm, so if your planning on an evening visit, get there before this.

Title: Incredible!
Text: What an amazing place! Probably the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka, definitely a must do. The climb was easier than I anticipated when we first saw "the rock" and could be done at your own pace. You can experience the magic of it without going all the way to the top but it was definitely worth the little bit of extra effort. Most challenging ( also the most rewarding) was from the lion's paws to the top.

Title: Lovely view
Text: The view from the top was lovely but a long way up. Take lots of water and sunscreen! If youre interested in the history then get a guide as there's limited signage.

Title: Well worth the climb lion rock
Text:
It is incredible to see an ancient palace/city on the top of a giant rock. The climb is really straightforward- many steps but they are short steps and the climb to the summit is via narrow metal
stairs. Climb down is super easy and shorter! I think you can take this way up too - we saw many locals do it, but then you miss Mirror Wall and the Wall Fresco.

Title: The view up there is better than the 'ROCK' itself
Text: It is a must do "tourist thing" in Sri Lanka although it isn't that 'impressive' in real. It is USD30 for the tourist to get in. A very well maintain site, clean, easy to walk around and climb up. It is not that tough to climb the stairs, just need to be careful as it is quite steep at some point. If you don't have knee/leg problems, you don't need to worry about it. It is a ruined ancient city up there back in thousands of years ago. Therefore, it is pretty empty on top of the rock. But the view is great. It is literally 360' degree of view for you to see what's surrounding the rock. The wind was strong when I was there but I rather it was windy than hot, there will be no shelter on top of the rock. So, it is good to go in the morning than mid day.

Title: Easily one of the highlights of our holiday.
Text:
Wow this is just spectacular, walking through the grounds, past the fountains the rock of Sigiriya looms large in front.

You then reach the foot of the rock at the entrance of the Lions Feet you start to climb the steps, and there are many, if you dont have a good head for heights this may unnerve you a little, when you eventually get to the top the 360 degree views are awe inspiring. As you start to make your way down you climb up some spiral stairs to the see the paintings which are 2500 years old, the colours still vibrant today.

Title: Excellent awe inspiring
Text: Incredible place, really well maintained, the highlight of the trip so far. Stunning views. Go early because of how hot it gets during the day, we arrived at 7, were back downstairs around 9am.

Title: Hard work but worth it!
Text:
This is a trip best done early morning...it is a gentle walk through the lower gardens but then it is a sheer climb...there is a first aid station at the feet of the lion carvings and then the hard work comes as you go up the final ladders...but the views from the top are unmissable!
Just a little surprised at the cost compared to other sites...

Title: Great view
Text: More than two thousand stairs to climb. But totally worth it for the view at the top and the signs of ancient culture

Title: Significant 'Wow' factor...
Text:
Well worth the climb, go early, with a guide and have your breath taken away.
very well taken care of and maintained
Huge surprise just how big the five acres are on top, no sense of that from below...
gets very busy from 10am

Title: Worth visiting
Text: The top view is breathtaking! However, to get that view, you need to climb more than 1000 steps! Yet it is worth doing :) Its a lifetime memory to visit this place

Title: Pidurangala is a better option.
Text: Over priced and not worth the cost. Pidurangala near the Sigiriya rock is better choice if you want one of them or need a better experience.

Title: Sublime views from the top!
Text:
The climb to the top of Sigiriya Rock is challenging but the view from the top is incredible. Definitely take lots of water and try to visit in the early morning as the sun is quite unforgiving at the top, with little to no shade. It took about 20 minutes to walk up the rock, 

Definitely explore the surrounding gardens, as there are lots of hidden treasures. We enjoyed looking at the caves, which were carefully created to protect from the rain, as well as the surrounding pools. Also, visiting the museum before entering the grounds definitely gave us a lot more insight into what we were about to see.

Title: Worth it
Text:
Very beautiful, worth the trip. We did a day trip from Kandyhired a driver for $50 round trip (he was awesome, contact info below). Left Kandy at 0600 and took about 2.5hrs to get to the rock. $30 USD per person (cash only). There are guides waiting for you if you want, we went without. Its not as hard as everyone makes it seem. Yes, there are a lot of steps, but many places to take breaks and look around. Id say there is maybe 20 mins of step climbing. We saw small children and a pregnant woman at the top.  Also, we never saw any wasps and signs are EVERYWHERE. 
Driver Shan (for hire) Whatsapp: +94776919000

Title: Wasps!!!!!
Text: Admission to hospital after wasp attack on the staircase with no possibility to hide. Super dangerous! Worst day ever.

Title: Amazing place but beware of scammers
Text:
Definately worth visiting. This is my 4th time here and I learn something new every time. I would recommend going all the way up as the views are amazing!  I would also recommend getting a guide who will explain the history. 
**The only issue here is the scammers. Beware of the guys 'helping' you up the steps beforebyou get to the rock. If you accept their 'assistance' they will follow you to the top and back down then they tell you that you will have to pay them. 

Apart from that this place and the views are amazing!

Title: Great view for the fit and fearless
Text:
An amazing place to visit - the old city / palace complex built on top of and around a sheer sided rock pillar.

Be prepared for a strenuous climb - its about 250m vertically - a lot of it on metal steps built out from the cliff face - the rest on narrow / irregular stone steps often without hand rails.  Going up is definitely easier than coming down!

The views from the top are spectacular; although perhaps the most amazing thing are the ancient ladders carved into the rock face!

There are limited information boards with a few snippets, so a local guide would be of benefit - but check their ability to explain before hiring them.

Title: Great climbing experience
Text: A lovely approach to the Rock helped by having a knowledgeable guide. 600 feet high the 1200 steps to the top were a challenge but well worth it. Great views throughout. Definitely must do.

Title: Gentle walk with some history
Text:
The views are incredible, defiantly would recommend you go all the way up. Especially if its a good day with a clear view of most of Sri Lanka!

We were fortunate enough to have a guide who shared the history with us, but for anyone who is going without a guide you may have an issue. ( WARNING - there is a few scams of local guides in the area - ignore them as you can end up in deep trouble)

The walk took us from ground to to the top around 20 mins or so with a stop of two along the way.

Title: Awesome experience just how old and sophisticated everything is - but get here early in the day
Text:
An awe inspiring place with sights thousands of years old so extensive and sophisticated. Good to have a guide or take half a day to read the signs explaining everything.
The steps are steep and many so get there early or you will get very hot indeed.
Its not cheap to get in @ nearly 5000R each but worth it many times over

Title: Amazing views......
Text:
My third climb this time with a 9 year old in tow.

Left the hotel a bit behind schedule which meant were were at the car park around 9am.

While driving I spotted a board mentioning local car park. So I drove towards that. Car park to entrance ticket counter is about 01 +KM walk. I didn't measure, alternatively you can take a tuk for a few hundred rupees.

Due to the pandemic the crowds were less and it was nice to have space and less crowd to e joy the climb up. It was a lot g climb. Walk past the garden to the base and then comes the first set of steps to reach the lions paw area.

Onwards are the rest of the steps via a iron staircase and a narrow one to the top. The last bit of stairs and you are at the top. Exhausted!

Amazing views all around and my son enjoyed exploring the area while I caught my breath!

It took as about two hours from car park to the summit. With plenty of breaks in between. Coming back down was a far more pleasant experience, we didn't walk up to see the frescoes as my son had enough and wanted to get back to the hotel. It took about 45 mins coming down. 

Like another reviewer has suggested I do recommend purchasing drinks or other items from the vendors below on your way down as they are most impacted by the decline of tourism in that area.

entrance tickets for locals are 100 rupees.

Title: Breathtaking views
Text: It was sad to see how empty this place because of the COVID-19 pandemic. But Ive enjoyed this time as Ive spend few extra hours just to relax myself as not many people around. If you are planning to visit Sigiriya make sure you are on your walking and outdoor gears. Approximately 8000 steps . I would suggest that you would buy something from the street sellers just help for the local communities as they have suffered heavily in this pandemic time

Title: Impressive ruins in the middle of the forest
Text: The rock is very impressive, standing quite alone in the middle of the forest. At the beginning, you will cross the former gardens with some water basins; one of them is in form of octagon. Then you begin to climb the stair, about 1.600 steps! However, you will find several terraces and belvedere where you can stop and take advantage of the view. I stopped at the platform where the ruins of the Lion Gate are because I had crutches for walking and it was impossible for me to go ahead. Pay attention you must not have vertigos to climb the last part, the stairs are actually in the void! More or less at mi-walk you will find wonderful paintings, unfortunately, there is not a lot of place and you cannot stay long time. Pictures are strictly forbidden. It is suggested to visit the rock in the morning or in the late afternoon, you will find less tourists and less humidity. Take some water with you there are no kiosks inside the site.

Title: Long strenuous trek but astounding view
Text:
It took us several hours to reach there. A long, tiring climb, surrounded by a huge crowd. Of course, youre treated with an amazingly beautiful view from the top. Just be prepared to be jostled a bit by the locals during the climb.

The frescos themselves took just a few minutes to see - suddenly you feel hey, did I trek so long to see these few meters of frescos?. Of course, they are beautiful and of historic significance.

Maybe a good idea to start in the early morning to avoid the midday heat.

Title: Not worth the ridiculous price
Text: Like all sites in Sri Lanka, this is very, very overpriced. The best part of the sight is the view, so I recommend climbing the neighbouring rock for the view at a fraction on the cost.
