The rock paintings are sparse and just tiny segments. There is a pair of carved lion claws at the base of some stairs. That is it for things to see on the rock. Does not come close to justifying $30 US or $40 Canadian a person. I felt rather ripped off.

Title: Great
Text:
Worth the climb to the top. 

Start as early as possible. We went at 7.30am. We would not have wanted to start much later.

Title: The Crowds!
Text: Imagine an amusement park without the fast track. Well, apparently there actually is a (mini) fast track which we realized after about our first hour of waiting. Its not really a hike to the top - more like a queue to the top. And a crowded one. If you are going to hand over the money for the steep entrance fee and hike to the top then do it as early as possible. Otherwise, the experience is one that you might want to skip.

Title: Worth the climb and high entrance fee
Text: This giant, ancient rock fortress has an impressive view of the surrounding area.  A 30 minute to hour vertical climb to the top, but it's sure footed with stone steps and some metal stairs.  Bring water and a camera!  It's UNESCO too.

Title: Absolute joy and scenic view once you reach the top of the fortress
Text:
we had heard about this place and had always wanted to visit. there is a beautiful garden as you approach the fortress.the climb is around 1000+ steps.so be sure you are properly hydrated and ready with spring in your step.
on the way there are painting on the wall which we can see.
from there on, we have to keep climbing till we reach the base where we could take a break and chill for some time.the last part of the climb is absolutely bonkers.
but it is well worth it. Once you reach the top,the view from the top is simply brilliant. and we spent time just feeling the cool breeze and the picturesque view from the rock fortress.
it is a must visit  attraction,if you are in sri lanka. highly recommend to others.

Title: must go see and climb to the top!
Text: Begin at the Persian-style gardens, then walk up the face of the rock-- on the way see the beautiful paintings on the rock (this rock was once all plastered and painted)-- then arrive at the lion's paws where you continue to climb until you reach the very top. The most spectacular view!

Title: It was a great experience
Text: It was a great experience, view from top was amazing. Try to avoid visit on weekends, you may find much of crowd. There is another rock nearby, you can go in that too. You will get the good view of Sigiriya rock.

Title: Nice Looking Rock but Expensive to Climb
Text:
While I was on a trip of Sri Lanka with G Adventures, I hired a driver to take me out to see the Sigiriya Rock as it is #191 on the Lonely Planet's ultimate travelist.

Since the entrance fee into the area of the rock is $30 USD, I did not climb the rock as it has 1200 steps to get to the top.  There are also many tuk tuk drivers that try to get you to pay $30 USD to take a tuk tuk around the base of the rock.  I did not take them up on their offer as you can walk around the base of the rock and see the moats without their services, and you do not need to pay anything to do this.   

I think that $30 USD is way overpriced as the locals pay only a fraction of this cost. Sri Lanka is not the only country that charges too much for foreigners.  I found that this was true in India and Nepal as well.

Title: A highlight of Sri Lanka
Text: A must see if travelling to Sri Lanka. Our guide took us to the rock about 6.30-7am which was the best decision...barely any other tourists there and before the heat. The climb up, which is a combination of flat areas, stairs and sights, took about an hour going easy. Views and ruins at the top are amazing and worth it.

Title: Worth the visit
Text: Prepare for the day. We first climbed a mountain to get the view of sigiriya rock and then climbed the sigiriya rock. The first treck was hard but the view was breathtaking and totally worth it. Then we climbed sigiriya rock. Its better to take a guide outside. They help you to climb and tell you stories which makes the experience better. The guide costed us 2000lkr.

Title: We did it
Text:
I was looking forward to Sigiriya and also dreading the climb up as im unfit. We got there around 9am and it was quite busy but not crowded. It was hot but we walked up in about 45 mins with a few stops. Beware of the 'helpers'. One helper grabbed my arm and pulled me up about 10 steps while i was saying not to help and that i was fine, at the top of the 10 steps he made some conversation then asked for the equivalent of £3. We said no as he had been told that I didn't want help, he then came out with a story about his child being in hospital and he needed money, i suspect this isn't true. 
We loved the views from the top and also on the way up. Beware of the cheeky monkeys.

Title: Simply stunning
Text:
Stunning place and must see. 
There are over 1000 steps to get to the top, but all ages are able to enjoy and well worth the views from the top. 
Highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka

Title: Well worth it
Text: Well worth the climb, not going to lie was dreading it a little, it was hard at times, but so glad that I made the effort and got to the top. Get there early to avoid the crowds and the heat. Take a camera for the fantastic views.

Title: 8th world Wonder
Text: A very beautiful place to visit when in Sri Lanka. A UNESCO Word Heritage site.  Definitely a must visit location.  Large rock with a castle carved into it with natural water pools and frescos that have lasted 100s of years.  Everything there was built by human hands and has amazing architecture.  The best view is all the way on the top.

Title: Impressive
Text: The work involved in build the fortress on an impenetrable rock is amazing. Well worth the climb. Just be wary of the thieving monkeys

Title: Don't be scared of heights
Text:
This is an extremely large and impressive area. It is quite a climb to the top but very doable as long as you have a bit of patience with the crowds. The views from the top are spectacular.
You need to be wary of the resident monkeys who are very keen to steal thing out of back packs even if they are closed. Also hornets apparently can be an issue.

Title: An awesome experience
Text: This is a complete must to do experience. I am a not very fit 54 yr old and even in the heat at 8am managed to get to the top with no  problems. And it was worth every step of the climb. The view is jaw droppingly beautiful and the remains of the palace incredible. We didn't have enough time to really explore everything and next time would put aside a whole morning,

Title: Strenuous To the Legs but Worth
Text:
Set off at 4pm, a short drive from my villa. When reaching there, we had a site guide. He explained as we move along towards the Lion Rock. The excavation, moats, lower compounds, caves, even the steps has its reason why it was coated. 1200 stairs up. 1/2 of the journey to the frescoes and wall mirror (no photos & videos allowed). 3/4 to the base of the lion 's paw entrance to the Palace up on top of the rock. By now, my legs almost gave way. I stayed at the lion's paws. But my hubby & site guide went all the way up to the top. He explained that the highest is not 1200 stairs but 1202. There are 2 steps of stone right in the centre of the Palace!
Worth participating in this UNESCO site. Entrance fee USD30 each. They accept USD.

Title: Incomparable Ancient Engineering Marvel
Text: When youre climbing the 1000 steps (like a 60 storey building) to the top, where the fortress and palace were (after walking 2km from the car park to get to those very uneven steps) you will marvel at the engineering and sheer audacity behind such a place. Millions of bricks. A massive swimming pool. (How did the water get there?) And on and on. Greater views, including that of a nearby mountaintop Buddhist temple. Bring water and be sure to stop at the toilet before your ascent. Wow.

Title: Best experiment
Text: I really have problem with heights and climbing up. We have a 4 year old boy, that's why we skip to go Adam's peak. I know there's a little climbing up in that rock but i didnt know it would hard for me,so it was full of suprise to me. It bagan with awesome views and gardens with normal steps but after than it was hard to climb for me. I had to face with my insight power and some scared. When i scared every moment and decide to go back,i saw my little 4 years old hero boy that climbing up without fear, i renewed myself and climbed up, so it was a nervous moment for me, but i tried and completed such a best experiment in the end.

Title: Well worth the climb, awesome views!
Text: WOW! If you're visiting Sri Lanka you really should consider putting this on your itinerary.... It's like nothing I've ever experienced or seen and is such a unique 'rock' and ancient kingdom. There are approximately 2000 stairs which wind their way up the face of the rock, arriving at the summit which is where the ancient kingdom was. It requires a moderate level of fitness, although you can take your time and do it at your own pace. Be sure to go earlier if possible as it does get quite warm.... also wear shorts or loose fitting light clothing (particularly for the ladies) as you do work up quite a sweat. Also make sure you explore the entire area at the top as there are some resident guides who will show you some interesting aspects.... and don't worry, they are not your typical money hungry types.... a donation once you're finished will suffice. Incredible experience and one for the bucket list!

Title: You climb up and see stuff around.
Text:
We went on a Friday which was a full moon day which is a holiday in SL. So we had lot of locals visiting the place and climbing up was pain as there was a huge queue. 

The view from the top is great and as you climb up its windy so you dont really feel the heat. 

If you are from one of the SAARC countries then you get 50% discount on tickets which is a great thing.

Title: Great view
Text: This is a must do in Sri Lanka but be warned it cost the most and has a lot of people doing this , get there by 8am to do so you beat the heat and people its amazing

Title: Amazing views
Text: As soon as you reach the entry point you have to pay entrance ticket and also their will be the option for a guided tour that he will explain all the way the story of this place. I opted to have a solo walk. There are good signs everywere to follow the path. Then stairs will be awaiting you around 1000 steps to reach the top of the rock. Somewhere in the middle there is like a cave with   wall paintings were i couldn't take any pictures. Once you reach the top a magnificent view will be waiting for you and also you can see the kings palace ruins. Worth all the effort, please take plenty of water with you ??

Title: beautiful view
Text: mowgli style sunset what a pity for garbage...getting up is long and tiring not for anyone...still would redo it

Title: Holiday
Text:
Great place to visit with amazing views.
Must be fairly fit to climb the steps
Better on a slightly cooler day 
Can be very busy.

Title: Nice place with great views
Text: One of the historic places to visit in Sri Lanka. Also known as the lion rock, sigriya is at a distance of around 3 hours from Kandy. We had not stayed in sigriya and hence we started early from Kandy and reached the rock around 10.30 am.  The climb takes around 1 hour and you can expect too much rush. It is advisable to stay here previous night as start climbing early since the rock opens at 6.30 am. There is a huge entry fee of 30 dollars which seemed a bit in reasonable. You also have an option to take an tuk tuk and visit the nearby places from where you get good views of both the rocks and a few farm too however you don't get to climb the rock in that case. Overall a nice place to visit barring the high ticket cost.

Title: must visit
Text: This is  the leading romantic destinations in the whole world surrounded by gardens, ponds and other structures. The gardens are amongst the oldest landscaped gardens in the world. love this place??

Title: Nice
Text: When you reach the top, apart from the sheer satisfaction of the climb, you feel the beauty of the greenery around, along with the pools, gardens etc of the summit.

Title: Impressive
Text: The trek is steep and the crowds are huge. Nevertheless, Sigiriya offers you a wonderful mix of man & nature - carvings, monuments, views, history et al.

Title: Spectacular
Text:
Its not until you get to the summit that you are able to appreciate the sight and effort the place must have needed 
There can be a queue but it is worth it and feels calm at the top and you can find your own space

Title: History at its best
Text: Although the climb was steep, all the family enjoyed the climb. The trip.up and down lasted about 1hr 30mins. Our guide was very good at telling us the history of Sigiriya rock.

Title: Amazing climb and view on the top
Text:
This is the reason I came to Sri Lanka. We were lucky that the crowd was manageable. 

Got to be relative fit to hike up at ease but its possible to climb at your own pace. It could be daunting for some at the final steps as the staircases are narrow and got to walk in a line. Total steps depending on which way you start - 1362 steps. 

Its also an amazing story of what Sigiriya is - it was a kingdom from a self proclaimed king that ruled for 18 years. He committed suicide due to the loss in a battle.

Title: amazing srilanka
Text: Also known as the Lion Rock in Sri Lanka. Climbing up the rock does not take long and it worths to be close to the eighth Wonder of the World. Frescoes, ancient art can be seen midway up the rock.

Title: Nice breeze at the top and a 360 degree view from the top
Text: Lots of stairs to the top., almost an hour long climb, but beautiful views and breeze at the top. Go for Sunset view and spend some time at the top once you are there. Not much to do at the top just feel the vibes and the wind blowing.

Title: Get Ready to burn some calories !
Text: Too good, I must admit. Beautiful ancient place a must visit. Be prepared to spend half a day or more for this Rock visit. Requires stamina to climb 1000+ steps so may be challenging for senior citizens. Well maintained too. Carry water bottles and light snacks. Dont forget your sun glasses and hat!

Title: We Climber the rock!
Text: Nice view from the rock. Not to hard to Climber even with small children. We had a good time. Come early

Title: Majestic
Text:
Entrance ticket for SAARC country citizens is at 50%discount,so comes upto 15 dollars per person. Make sure u carry ur passport with u. 
Right at the entrance is the Museum,do visit it before starting ur climb,itll put in perspective a lot of things.
Make sure ur carrying water,wearing comfortable clothes and shoes. Its not that its a hard climb, even then u get tired n sweat a lot coz its a 1200 step climb. 
Click a lot of pics from d view point and the entrance garden. Half way through the climb is the grand lion paw entrance,its really fascinating that this was built thousands of years ago. 
Once u reach the top,ur blown away by the view. Spend enough time on the top,click loads of pics. Luckily it wasnt too crowded for us. But ive heard it gets crowded quite often. We started our climb at 9.30, took us an hour to go up,spent an hour on top and then another hour to come back down.

Title: The view is worth the climb
Text:
A huge rock dominating the surrounding landscape as you approach.  The surrounding grounds are beautifully kept and the ruins are impressive but the highlight is the climb up and the view from the top.  Well worth the effort and a significant historical site.

It's best to avoid or refuse assistance from the "helpers" who keep trying to assist you (for a fee) if you can.

Title: Made it to the top
Text: Start as early as possible to allow for the humidity and take your time. Expect to find lots and lots of tourists, incredibly popular and busy. The climb to the Lions paws is long, but there are plenty of places to stop and rest. While from here the ascent to the top took about 15 to 20 minutes, we walked slowly, its steep and no where to rest, but doable. The view is amazing, especially the remnants of the Palace and old swimming pool

Title: Fantastic ancient buildings and gardens
Text: The climb up to the top of this ancient castle/fortress was daunting (to a person with fear of heights. (But what a view on top!) And the history of this place - first buddhist temple, then castle and grounds laid out in the 5th century by King Kashyapa, including two moats and the rock citadel. Most memorable: wall paintings half way up of the Cloud maidens!

Title: Empire over the rock
Text: The Sigiriya Rock Fortess is a must do item for every traveller visiting Sri Lanka. This is beautiful emperor built on the rock. The climb is steep but the arrangements using a stairway is very neatly done and well co-ordinated. It is mesmerising feeling once you are at the top. Beware of monkeys on the way and try to climb up with minimal stuff in your hands.

Title: Sigiriya
Text: Really enjoyed the walk to the top, not a good idea if you don't like heights. Also far to many locals who pretend to be friendly and helpful,  however they are just looking to fleece as much cash out of you as they can. My advice ignore them and do your own research into the historical aspects of the ancient palace grounds. Visit the museum before you climb, you get some useful information. Some historians also believe this was the Palace of Ravana, the epic story of Ram and Sita. Highly recommended if you like history and seeing some fantastic views from the top of Sigiriya.

Title: Lion Rock dominates
Text:
The ancient city of Sigiriya is an archaeological site whose ruins point to the opulence and architectural wonders of this ancient city. The Rock dominates the area with the ruined fortress on top, a 1247 step climb for the energetic. We wished that we had visited years ago as old legs were unable to obey the spirit. 11 of our group of 34 made it to the top, the remainder were in awe at the photographs that captured snapshots of the ruins and views of the surrounding district. 
Those of us left at ground level enjoyed the hours viewing the ruins, ramparts, moats, miniature water gardens, fountain garden, octagonal pond and so much more of the area surrounding the base of the Rock before heading to the interesting museum.

Title: Cool hike
Text: Reading the reviews had me worried and nervous for this climb. But actually it was totally fine. I would advise getting there early to avoid the crowds. I got there at 8am and left as the tour buses and queues were building up. The rock entrance opens at 7am and closes at 5.30pm but get there early to avoid the afternoon heat. The climb itself only took 45 mins up - and I took my time. I got to the top and walked around for 30 mins before coming back down. I would say the whole experience took under 3 hours. There are a lot of steps but it's totally manageable if you just take your time and wear sensible shoes. I had my hiking sandals on. Some locals wore flip flops which I personally wouldn't recommend.

Title: Quite a hike but worth every step
Text:
This World Heritage site shows the ancient Sri Lankans' ingenuity in construction, architecture, design and engineering.

It took us several thousand steps to get to the top. This place is full of interesting stories of the past ancient king. 

If not for the history, come for the view. You might think many times if you're afraid of heights but the view from the top is gorgeous and definitely worth it.

Bring sun protection because there's very little shade. Wear comfortable clothes and footwear. Bring a cold bottle of water and some trail food if you get hungry easily.

Title: Very demanding and hard but beautiful
Text: We went with our toddler to Sigiriya. It was quite hard. But we did it! Our toddler enjoyed it! And we did as well! That feeling, when you climb all the way up - amazing! And the view - beautiful. Bring your raincoat in rainy season. We had un umbrella, but it is difficult to manage it. Raincoat would be better choice. And bring some food for the dogs.

Title: Nice place, not sure about the price.
Text: The area around the rock and the walk up was beautiful, as was the view. A little too expensive though.

Title: Great visit
Text:
We visited as part of a tour. There are a lot of steps and if you need help, there are some men who will drag you up the steps and give you some info about the site. The negative is that I repeatedly told one of these men I did not need his help and he just kept grabbing my arm, then had the cheek to tell me I must pay 20 dollars for the help, which he said he had negotiated with our tour guide! We did not pay it, so he got in a real strop.
The views are pretty amazing, and what remains of the ancient city after so many centuries is intersting.
I would recommend a visit, but leave plenty of time as there is a lot to see. I know the helpers have to make a living, but either make it clear what you will pay from the start or send them away. Take a hat and water. There are some facilities about half way up. The climb is about 200 meters of steps.

Title: Hard Climb! Wonderful view!
Text:
Climbing this huge massive rock was attached in our Itinerary which we got from our Local Tour Operator and we did not hestitate to skip this because of the Arts. Its highly recommended to climb in the morning as it get heated at afternoon which will be hard and also recommend to take plenty of Water. The panoramic view at the top was amazing.
Thank you Kingfisher Tours Sri Lanka and our guide Aswar to take us here.

Highly Recommended!

Title: What an experience!
Text: If you suffer from vertigo, then you will need to take a very deep breath before embarking on the climb to the top of Sigiriya, which rises 200 metres straight up out of the surrounding countryside.  The steps up the mountain are universally steep and often hang from the side of the mountain out over the space below and to see the magnificent painted Sigiriya Damsels it is necessary to scale and then descend two winding spiral staircases attached to there rock and with nothing but air below.  While all the steps are quite secure, you sometimes feel as if you are suspended in space! The climb is quite a hard slog and there is little shelter so it is best to go early in the morning.  The remnants of the water gardens and other construction at the base of the mountains, the painted ladies, the extensive remains at the top of the mountain and the spectacular views are well worth the effort.  It seems absolutely amazing that such a construction could have been built with minimal equipment in such difficult terrain 1500 years ago and that the King responsible for the works then rashly decided to leave his impregnable fortress and fight his enemy at ground level only to be defeated and commit suicide.  Such incredible folly!

Title: Best tip: go early!
Text:
We were counting on the climb to the Sigiriya ancient rock fortress to be one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka.  And it certainly was!  The best piece of advice we can give you is to go early.  This will help with the heat and with the crowds.  The rock opens at 6:30 am, which is when we arrived.  However, it appears that the ticket office opens earlier, so I suggest arriving around 6:15 and being among the first to go through the gate.

Be warned that the price is hefty: around $30.  At the gate, a guard will take any label off your water bottle, so you can save time by doing this in advance.  Then, you will proceed on a straight path for about 10 minutes just to reach the beginning of the stairs to climb.  We were pleasantly surprised that the climb, while strenuous and very sweaty, was not as difficult as we expected.  We were not hurrying, and made it to the top in about 20 minutes.  I do feel this is primarily because there was no one else in our way on the stairs.  I can see how this would easily become a bottleneck and slow down your progress.

Once at the top, you will be rewarded with beautiful views of the surrounding area.  The ruins are peaceful to explore when crowds are light.  On our way down at 7:30 am, the crowds were now rolling in, so even 8 am is too late to embark.

Do go early, do take water, and enjoy the experience!

Title: Sigiriya, one of the highlights of our Sri Lanka trip
Text: We loved this place. We got an English speaking guide who gave us a full history of the place. We were glad that we started quite early in the morning. One has to be fresh to climb 1332 steps to reach the top of the fortress. It was hot and humid, but the intermittent clouds gave us some respite from the sun. Wet wipes came in handy. We marveled at the water management system and the gardens and the ponds of various proportions that were  in place so many years ago. The entire area has been maintained really well.

Title: Incredible Ancient Palace with views!
Text: An absolute must in Sri Lanka. Such incredible scenery and views. Not the easiest walk to the top and maybe not perfect for anyone with a fear of heights! But the views are worth the sweat. To avoid the crowds go just after lunch but be careful of the hot sun.

Title: WOW!!
Text: Well what an experience. Morning is much better as the stair climb is shaded. Highly recommend a personal guide who can give you much insight into the history behind this amazing place.

Title: Cool one but...
Text:
So... if you visit SriLanka this is must. 
But... there are several buts:
Come early in the morning. Its open even before 7. I came there at 6.30 and it worked.
It is crowded. Event that early there were lot of people. I can imagine how it looks at 8.
Its really easy touristic climb. Like climbing 40 floor building.
And its a bit pricy for tourists.
I went to Pidurangala as well and if you are not arhitectural oriented person than Pidurangala is much better choice.

Title: Nice place & views, but waaay overpriced
Text:
As you can see in the photos posted by many travelers, the views are scenic here with lots of macacs around. 
However, I find it a pure insult to tourists since the price is 60x higher than what locals pay ($30 vs $0.5).

Title: Go early, must visit place.
Text:
Sigiriya is ancient rock citadel located in Sri Lankas cultural triangle. The enormous rock towers above the surrounding jungle offering extensive views. I will suggest to stay nearby and start the hike as early as 06:30AM as the temperatures rises to 100 degrees Fahrenheit and humidity around 80%. You have to climb about 1200 steep steps with elevation gain of about 650 feet. My advice is to start early, drink water regularly, wear hat, use sunscreen and go slow. If you are from SAARC countries then carry your passport to get 50% discount on admission ticket. 
Sigiriya is a world heritage site declared by UNESCO in 1982. It is a unique combination of 5th century urban planning, architecture, engineering, hydraulics, garden design, painting and poetry. 
The city is designed in a square module 2750 meter east to west and 925 north to south. 
1. Royal Gardens- This is massive water gardens. 
2. Three water gardens. 
3. Boulder Garden- It begins at slope of hill at base of the rock. 
4. Cistern Rock- Huge stone that has been split. 
5. Audience Hall Rock
6. Preaching Rock
7. Painted maidens- These frescos  are preserved in a cave pocket about 40 feet above walkway. 
8. Mirror Wall- Highly polished surface is original stucco. Most poetic verses had been written in praise of maidens on cliff face. 
9. Lion Terrace. 
10. Palace- It is located on summit but none of superstructure remains.

Title: Stunning
Text:
An absolute must do for anyone who is able to make the ascent, Sigiriya Rock is stunning! 

Seen from below, the massive granite outcrop looks daunting. Its a  challenge to climb, but mainly because of the heat and crowds. (Go early enough and you can mostly avoid both.)

We made it to the top in 30 minutes, with two young kids, and two adults with bad knees! We arrived around 800 and were glad we had because it was incredibly crowded as we descended. 

The water gardens viewable on the approach are impressive. Incredible feats of ancient ingenuity and engineering prowess. 

The climb is well organized and with the $30 US for adults (kids 6-12 are half price). Most of the way you go up metal stairs the are secured to the rock face. These are narrow, and a bit unnerving when the wind gusts, but we saw people of all ages and fitness levels work their way up.

It is worth the sweat and sore legs when you reach the top!

The palace ruins are incredible, but it is the 360 degree vistas that are the real payoff. We spent close to an hour roaming around and snapping breathtaking pics.

The descent retraces the final section of the climb, at first, before reaching a much easier exit pathway. Again, it took roughly half an hour.

One of the coolest, and most singular, experiences Ive ever had!

Title: Sigiriya Rock
Text:
My wife an I climbed to the summit in approximately 40 minutes with a few small rests along the way.
The spectacular view from the summit is worth the effort, as well as the beautiful grounds and fort below. 
This site is a must see in Sri Lanka !

Title: Amazing fortress, great wonder of ancient architecture and history
Text: Great place, enjoyable climb need good energy and stamina to climb up to top, amazing garden (ruins), unique place of history and wonder. There was huge crowd on Sunday which was bit not so pleasant to climb, many times we had to wait for place to climb.  It took about 2 hrs for climbing & back, carry lots of water as it will be very humid while climbing. The place is maintained very well with control on plastic & clean, spectacular view of forest when you reach at top. Recommend to go early as place gets crowded & you will have to wait to get ticket, good if you take guide.

Title: Inspired by families climbing the Rock Fortress
Text: Climbing the Rock Fortress is not for the feint of heart or weak limbs. I was daunted looking at the fortress from afar. But what gave me strength was the sight of families, grandparents, parents, and children--barefooted, in flipflops, sandals--climbing to the top. With digestive cookies and water and rest stops, I was able to climb to the very top in around 2 hours! People were waited patiently for the slower climbers. And what a view! 360 degree view of the sunset! We waded in the ancient swimming pool and enjoyed the cool breeze. I was immensely glad I had the courage and strength to complete the climb. A midafternoon climb after the Dumballa caves culminated my day.

Title: Nice view on top of the rock but concerned about safety
Text:
It is a major tourist attraction in this area.  The place is very crowded with 95% locals.  They pay only R50 but the foreigners pay R5000.  

You have to walk through a huge garden and walk up many steps to see the Lion Rock and to climb up to the top to see the view.  You need good shoes as the stairs are not even.

The day we visited the place, it was very crowded.  We could only move a couple of steps at a time and waited for the next step.  We had to walk through some walkways which were built on the side of the rock.  The narrow walkways were made of metal and with metal support welded into the rock.  It has to support a lot of people at anytime.  I was a little concerned about the safety at that time. 

It took us a long time to go to the top of the rock because there were a lot of people.  It was extremely unpleasant under such hot weather to be stuck with hundreds of people.

The top of the rock is not really big but the view is stunning.  Unfortunately, there is no sign and no brochure about anything of the rock.  We spent about 15 mins there taking pictures.  Going downhill was easier but it was also very crowded.  

Before we walked to the foreigner parking lot, we walked through a few stores and bought a couple souvenirs.  I am not sure if there is any washroom at all.

Title: Beautiful palace on an ancient rock!
Text:
It was a tiring climb but worth it. Took us 45 minutes to get up there.
It is extremely clean and did not find plastic waste anywhere.
Was a little crowded so had to go up slowly, but am not complaining!

Title: Magnificient !!!
Text: what a great culture this island has , loved the view from the top and the history which it tells , mirror wall , how they took watwer up the rock simply amazing , tickets are bit pricey .. but worth it

Title: I preferred Pidurangala but Sigirya was also an amazing experience
Text:
We visited sigirya during our trip to Sri Lanka. I was already knackered from waking up at 7 am to get there early (trust me - don't do this later than 10 am)

Having said that climbing Sigirya is 100% the most fun activity my wife and I did during our trip to Sri Lanka. It costs $20 or $30 to enter (expensive compared to the $2 entrance fee at Pidurangala).

It's a steep climb easier than Pidurangala and there are stairs for most of the way up but everyone can do it. I saw people with babies doing it with one hand and old people with sticks getting pushed up the hill. 

Apart from the fun way up you get 360 views of Pidurangala, Dambulla and the nearby parks. 

I left with major aches in my legs but I can't stop thinking about that day . I would do it again on a heartbeat.

If someone asks to help just refuse politely. I was scammed again and some "helpful" employee extracted 3000 rupees from me for grabbing my wife's hand to "help her up" . He wouldn't let go. For this behavior alone I am not willing to give 5/5

Title: Mask Shop and Museum..
Text: You get to see different type of mask, very unique to Srilankan Culture. The guide at the museum is not very knowledgeable. However, the museum is well designed and maintained. However, this museum is not for a group, if you are going there as a part of a group, I suggest break the group in smaller unit not more than 5-6 pax. The shop has good collection of mask and other artifacts. Best part is to see the making of the mask.. dont forget to notice the tree in the compound..Balsa tree, which basically used to make these masks

Title: Lovely unique mask museum
Text: This is a mask museum worth visiting.Several beautiful masks of different size are displayed.you can purchase a few,reasonably priced masks from here as Sri lankan memento

Title: Good stop
Text:
We stopped here during a trip the museum was good with a guide who explained all the difference masks to us this lasted about 30 minutes. Taken to the workshop where we able to watch them carve and paint the masks. We asked if we could take pictures that was ok.
About is the shop prices are good 
Well worthy of a visit

Title: Could have been interesting
Text:
Part of a tour group (22 people) but the museum not designed for a group of that size and the lack of space, speed of presentation & the guides accent made interpreting the various masks on display very difficult.  There are story boards with the masks but not given the time to view/read them.

The masks that were on display were very colourfu, unique and interesting - lots of detail on carving & painting.

After leaving the downstairs museum there is a chance to view the actual carving and painting of the masks and this was quite interesting seeing them omoving from a single block of wood to the end product.

Could have been much more interesting if group size wa slimited to 10 or so guests.

Title: Masks Galore
Text:
Makers of Masks.... so many different shapes, sizes, colors, types.
Had a quick look in the museum and then a wander through the shop. If you are looking for a mask then this is the place to buy one.
There is a lot of meaning and culture behind these masks and they are happy to explain this to you.

Title: Makers of masks!
Text: Our group was a little too big for all of us to hear what our guide was saying whilst touring through the museum but nonetheless it was interesting to see the history of the mask in Sri Lanka.  What we found fascinating was to watch the men carving and putting the masks together then to see the mask come alive with the painting of it.  The shop was filled with heaps of masks and other interesting souvenirs - it was a good place to stop for a visit - would recommend it mostly for interest in the manufacture of the masks.

Title: Beautiful masks
Text:
The exhibition is ok. A bit tired. But watching the craftsmen is very interesting and the shop is excellent.
They sell all types of masks with both the usual colourful decoration but also more muted colours. They also know the meaning behind them, which is helpful.
For artists and children you can buy plain masks to decorate yourself, not something weve seen anywhere else.
After shopping around we went back here to buy the mask we wanted. The price was on a par with other shops but the quality much better.
They also sell puppets, musical instruments, key rings etc.

Well worth a visit for the shop alone

Title: nice place to visit
Text:
This is a lovely place to visit while driving from Bentota to Galle. There is no entry fee and a lady from the museum takes you around to explain the various facets. Quite interesting and somewhere intertwined with Indian mythology, too. It's interesting to see the workers in the factory busy with their artistic hands. The gift shop, though, is quite exorbitant and prices much higher than the souvenir shop in Bentota. Difference of approx. LKR 1000 for the medium sized face masks!! 
Nevertheless, still worth a visit.

Title: Bored guide
Text: Altbough the tour of the mask museum could have been interesting it was spoiled by the attitude of the female guide. Her explanations were delivered with such a bored and monitone voice tbat it was almost comical. No smile. No entnusiasm. Information on the walls was wortj reading. Worth a visit but only with the right guide!

Title: Well worth the visit
Text:
The Ariyapala Mask Museum is a short Tuk Tuk journey south from Balapitya in Ahungala. The tour itself in the museum on the ground floor takes about 30 minutes and is very interesting. 

You can actually see the masks being made to the side of museum and a shop above has many you can buy for a holiday souvenir to take home. Prices can vary depending on the size and complexity of the design. We bought 4 small ones which relate to different ailments, illnesses, conditions.

Title: Interesting, worth a visit
Text: The mask museum does not have an entry fee, however you can give donation as per your wish. Sri Lanka has lots of fables which are performed using these masks and you will learn some stories behind several different masks which are made of wood. You can visit their store and pick up a mask as a souvenir.

Title: ideal for gifts
Text: Excellent to see the vast array of masks ,colours and sizes to suite everyones budget.Also plenty of gift ideas well worth a visit.

Title: Miserable museum staff
Text: The shop is lovely and the staff friendly, the prices are alot higher like everyone says , however you can see a lot of work and time goes into their products . I have left with 3 masks that look will super in my home when I get back . Like you might also have read, the woman in the shop are two miserable , despondent women , who should concentrate on welcoming visitors rather then rolling their eyes back at the sight of guests and playing with their phones . They are the face of that brand and need to represent it.

Title: God explanations in English give background to culture
Text: Demonstration of carving balsa wood. Painting of masks. Then museum shows a wide range of masks with explanation.

Title: Don't expect good prices
Text:
I thought it's a good idea to stop on the way from Hikkaduwa to the airport at this mask museum to understand the story behind the masks, see how are they produced and buy them directly at the factory.

Don't expect something big and I ended up with a much higher price than in other touristic places like Hikkaduwa or Mirissa.

Please click helpful, if you liked my review. Thanks.

Title: Very interesting
Text:
You can go by bus to the museum as it is very close. The museum is small but you can ask for an explanation of the different masks and the work behind them. There is no entrance fee but you can make a donation, both in the museum and in the work area where you can see how they produce and paint the masks. In the shop upstairs you can find a lot of different masks at different prices. Prices are higher than the other places, but you get what you pay: the difference from the others is very clear. 
You won't be disappointed

Title: Interesting
Text: A small museum which gives a very interesting story about the history of the masks and the storytelling that goes along with it

Title: Really worth it
Text: I went around looking for Masks all over Ambalangoda. While they are all really intriguing, the music has some of the bestest ones! The quality is just better, although it is more expensive too.

Title: Mask my enthusiasm
Text: Worth the visit except it would be better if they didn't rush you through the creation stages. The museum, whilst very small, is very interesting and informative with a few 200 year old exhibits. The shop has lots of goodies and not really that expensive. I would have bought but with the restrictions placed on tourist baggage it really does now become unfesible to buy large souvenirs. Good place though.

Title: Interesting museum and great to see the pieces being made and painted
Text: Interesting visit to the small museum to find out a little more about the history of these Sri Lankan masks.  The staff will talk you through the exhibits which brings the stories to life a little more.  Enjoyed seeing the production process from the initial carving of the balsa wood through to the hand painting.  The shop contains many pieces with something for most budgets - visit this after you've been through the museum as it puts a different perspective and understanding on the pieces you'll see. Well priced, and good quality.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Gives an idea of how the masks you see everywhere are part of the life of rural folk. The staff are not helpful so you need to read the information, spend some time and do some thinking.

Title: Excellent masks
Text: I stopped here on my way from Colombo to Galle.  The museum was very interesting and informative about the history of masks in Sri Lanka.  The masks are so beautiful and intricately carved.  Staff is available to offer a short guided tour and/or answer any questions that you may have.  I thought that the staff was very friendly and helpful.  There is also a small workshop where you can watch the masks being carved and painted.  The gift shop is well stocked and most prices are reasonable.  The masks are a bit pricey, but worth the cost considering the effort to make them.  Definitely an interesting place to stop for a few minutes.

Title: Nice Place
Text: It is worth a visit if you want to know about different masks, Nice place as I was able to purchase some souvenir for my son and he loved it.

Title: Worth a visit, certainly seemed informative about the history of the masks.
Text: Worth a visit, certainly seemed informative about the history of the masks when compared to when I asked other so-called mask experts. Of course, ends with a mask shop. Decided to buy one here in preference to some of the other places I visited.

Title: Interesting history of masks
Text:
An interesting place and compact. The museum is small, but does contain a good number of exhibits of masks across history. If possible take the time to read the plaques listing the stories after the narrative by the guide.

The workshop round the back is also worth a visit to see masks being made.

Title: Beautifully handpainted masks
Text:
Very nice little shop with beautifully handpainted traditonal masks and other (wooden) souvenirs.
Small family business, friendly owner, fair prices.

Title: Worth a quick stop
Text:
Fun place to learn a little bit about Sri Lankan cultural history through their usage of masks and puppets used in plays dealing with gods and demons.  It's a bit of a stretch to call it a 'museum' though, as it's really centered around the shop which sells replicas of the masks.  Friendly staff gave a mini guided tour and you were free to browse around at your own pace if you liked.

Fun diversion if you're looking for something to do in Ambalangoda.

Title: Worth a visit on the way to Colombo
Text:
We stopped at the Mask Museum on our way to Colombo. It was an easy 45 mins bus ride from Unawatuna. 
The little museum is quite interesting and the ladies providing the description run through the different masks fairly quickly. They do like it if you ask questions, and spend a bit more time if you are interested. We did the tour with them to get a quick orientation, and then went around once again to get a better look at the masks. Worth making a small donation as the museum was set up with funding from the German govt and not sure it gets any more funding now. 
The workshop was interesting but nothing special - felt like the workers were placed there for the sake of the tourists. The shop is pretty good, but feels too commercial after hearing about the history of the original mask-maker and his family. Nevertheless a good place to pick up a special souvenir especially as the price and quality are good.

Title: An ok experience
Text:
We stopped by this museum en-route to Galle. While the name is very catchy, it is not really a museum but more of a workshop and shop where once can see how masks are prepared. There are a few puppets also in the shop.

There is quite a variety at the shop but the prices are very touristy, to be honest. Total time taken by us to see everything was 15 min.

Title: Excellent Museum
Text: This was an excellent museum, which I wish they would have charged for rather than expecting us to visit the shop. The moment we arrived we were being hurried to visit the shop. It was as if the shop was a compulsory part of the experience. The masks in the museum were great and rightfully recognised for this by a number of anthropological institutions in Europe. The visit to the workshop where masks were being made was a disappointment. Clearly the skill and craft of making masks is probably dying out. The tourists just want to buy the cheaply made masks.

Title: A small but informative museum cum workshop
Text: On our way to Galle, we stopped over at the museum by the roadside and visited the workshop downstairs and the museum cum souvenir shop upstairs.  We learnt a lot about the history and development of the masks here which were mainly used in functions and festival times.  You can buy some gifts at the shop prior to departure.  Worth to come.

Title: Ariyapala Mask Museum
Text:
I had read about this museum on Tripadvisor, and decided to stop in.  I am ever so glad that I did!  The museum actually sits in a small building-with the museum and the workshop downstairs, and (a few steps outside) the store is located upstairs.  The museum was fascinating.  The young lady that gave me the tour could not have been kinder.  She spoke English, and took time to explain and answer all of my questions.  The tour was short-no more than 15 minutes, but very informative.
There is no fee for the tour, however donations (of any amount) are gratefully accepted. Following the tour, I was able to observe the mask carvers at work.  It's amazing to watch these artisans at work-- from the hand carving to the hand painting--incredible. And yes, photos are allowed.
Next I went upstairs to the store.  What an array of masks !  All in various sizes, shapes and colors.  The shop owner was very knowledgable, and extremely patient.  I was able to bargain with him for a simply beautiful mask (which is symbolic of good health).  My mask was wrapped so carefully, that even going through customs, overhead compartment, and taxi ride, it was still in perfect condition when I unwrapped once I arrived back home.
Al in all, Ariyapala is a wonderful little shop/ museum filled with treasures.  A must do ! !

Title: wow
Text: wow it was great amazing masks on display and they were truly amazing

Title: Interesting Museum!
Text: We visited this delightful museum on the advise of our guide. It was a highly entertaining and informative visit. We saw the whole process of mask making from scratch. The museum educated the kids about the various forms of masks and their significance in the Sri Lankan lives.

Title: Small but Nice Museum
Text: The museum was very nice, though small, and provided an interesting look at masks in Sri Lankan culture. We felt forced to give a donation (though we did not, as we bought masks upstairs). There is a small workshop downstairs where you can see the men carving and the women painting. I was told this place has the best quality in the area.

Title: An Expensive Tourist trap. Avoid
Text:
Mostly a store, the Ariyapala Mask Museum has a tiny gallery featuring a handful of masks decaying and gathering dust. With close to no labeling and poor organization it's a challenge to comprehend anything except the disjointed anecdotes narrated by the guide (one of the shop employees). After a ten minute tour covering all of three rooms, I was hustled for a tip in the guise of a donation before getting led up to the real business - the store. The wares were ridiculously overpriced (even the souvenir shops in the upmarket corners of Galle and Colombo are cheaper). I ran for cover once it became apparent that the staff saw me as a cash cow. 

A complete tourist trap that offers very little and sells stuff at inflated prices. Don't waste your time here, try the Nandana store across the road.

Title: Worth a visit if you are in Ambalangoda
Text:
This is one of the best place to see traditional masks in Sri Lanka. Next to the museum is small workshop were you can witnesses the mask come into life. On the first floor is a souvenir shop. Product here are bit costly, quality is of top notch. Employee in the shop are not well trained, they couldn't give a detailed explanation of the masks.

Masks in Srilanka are originated in South of Sri Lanka, usually made using Kaduru wood in the mask capital of Ambalangoda.

Title: interesting stop
Text: we like masks so our driver brought us here on our way back to the airport from Weligama.  the museum took us about 15 minutes and unfortunately there wasn't much going on in the workshop/

Title: Must do in Ambalangoda
Text:
A very different experience from the rest of Sri Lanka. It was a pleasure to see the craftsmen at work making the beautiful, bright masks.

We ended up buying many as gifts for ourselves and friends and family back home.

Title: Workshop interesting
Text: Workshop great to see and very informative. Museum itself masks were good but you feel a bit rushed around with the guide. Donations only to visit

Title: Thoroughly enjoyed it
Text: Weather a bit changeable so came here. Was wary about reviews Re prices in gift shop but thought wed give it a go. Its really small but interesting. You get guided round first then its worth walking round by yourself to read the detail, reads like a play. The workshop was brilliant, the artists and sculptors are super talented. Boys (aged 12) loved the gift shop, yes there are super expensive things in there but actually keepsakes for every budget. We did treat ourselves to a mask that was mid priced but something we really wanted. Can buy smaller masks and carved ornaments for just a few hundred Rupees if you want. Had good lunch and a dip in the pool at Hotel J Ambalangoda which made it a worthwhile day out!

Title: fascinating masks
Text: the masks and history are amazing and fascinating.  Sri Lanka is an amazing place.  The museum had a workshop and a gift shop connected to it.  The fellows doing the carving were generous with their time and made us feel welcome.

Title: Interesting
Text: Took about 15 minutes with a short guided tour. Small donation. Workshop out the back although nobody working whilst we were there. It was ok if in the area.

Title: Interesting
Text: The museum itself was moderately interesting, but more interesting to me was watching the men in the next room carve and paint new masks.  A nice piece of local culture.

Title: Okay Museum, but great masks
Text: We went round the small museum, which had a limited selection of exhibits, we also visited the workshop which had about 4 persons working, this was also quite small and offered limited interest. However the shop had some excellent masks, of better quality than we had seen elsewhere. We purchased one.

Title: Cool if you passing by
Text: Its free of charge but donations are welcomed, we got a tour from one of the workers it was good that she explained the meaning of each mask, there some mask original from 200 years old, for me lot of the masks were creepy lol, you can see the work area as well, but the big surprise is the shop, no picture are allowed and I wasnt expecting to buy anything but I bought 5 pieces

Title: Short Visit
Text: Short visit with family, tour of museum with museum guide giving explanations.  Watched the carvers.  Were warned off buying masks here due to prices.

Title: Get an insight on handicraft, but beware of being ripped off when buying masks
Text:
There a two parts, one where you can see and experience the various steps how masks are designed and crafted. Very interesting, and the skills of some of the workers are worth watching it.
Second part is the showroom, where you could buy the masks. Although the masks are nice and well made, the price is about much too expensive,  maybe the commission paid to drivers and guides prevent reasonable pricing. But 150 meter, down the R.E de Silva Rd  opposite of the museum - you get same style, quality for half the price, just avoid to go there with your driver on your coat-tails

Title: Interesting history
Text: Many beautiful masks from almost ancient times in the lower level museum and new ones for sale at the street level show room. The owner ( ? ) a good guide.

Title: One of the highlights
Text: We stopped off here en route, and didn't expect much. However the museum was wonderful with so many vibrant masks and a great explanation. We saw masked dancing in Kandy but seeing so many masks together was a real treat.

Title: Stop worth making
Text: Good museum with explanations in english and guide taking visitors through. Helps understand some of the cultural roots of sri lanka and the masks themselves can be amazing. Shop is very expensive- has a wide selection.

Title: Small museum of masks
Text: Stop here as part of a tour, very small but quite interesting. The masks are sold throughout the country

Title: Cultural insight in mask history and meaning
Text: Tour stop on route to Galle at this attraction. Whilst not something of personal interest, it was informative with a short whistle-stop museum tour, followed by a workshop tour when you can see the effort involved in carving and painting, before the usual "up sell" opportunity to purchase the wares at the well stocked shop. There seemed to be all sizes and prices catered for although i had not "benchmarked" with local on street stores to establish if this was another Spice Garden type tourist rip off. Worth the stop off...

Title: Nice Museum
Text: Very nice Museum ti visit. I went few times over the past years. Mask are bit over priced. But it is good.

Title: One room, with about 20 historic masks - but it is free!
Text: The shop contains a wide variety of masks to buy, decent quality and not bad prices. The museum downstairs is free, which is good as it's basically just one room with four tableaux, which the host explains and which are interesting and worth seeing. I dropped 100LKR each into the Donations box, I think it was worth 33 centimes each!

Title: Just okay
Text: I would not travel specifically to Ambalangoda to see a mask factory, whilst it was interesting for a minute or two to watch the painters copy from a page that was all. Then the must do shop visit, a huge array of masks in natural colours and lacquer, all sizes. But they were expensive, just made us all the more pleased with the price we paid for a mask at Laksala in Kandy.

Title: Scary faces
Text: Fascinating insights into the provision of masks according to a formatted pattern and characters for a Sri Lankan folk story. We got to see the museum and the actual manufacture of the masks and browsed a very interesting collection in the museum. Again well worth a visit.

Title: Good memories
Text:
My husband and i first visited this place 17 and a half years ago and bought our first mask , we have visited  4 times altogether, it never changes, great place and great craftsmanship!! Wouldn't buy a mask from anywhere else the quality is far superior to anywhere else!! 
Will definitely return when we visit Sri Lanka in the future !!

Title: Mask Museum
Text:
Really worth a visit while in Sri Lanka
History about different types of masks for various reasons will be explained in detail - they have a vast collection of traditional masks used in traditional dances
Not worth buying any as their shop has fixed prices & too expensive keeping in mind the tourists

Title: the best masks museum and shop in sri lanka - nothing comes close
Text:
this is the best place to see, study about and even purchase authentic hand made masks.

it was obviously more expensive than the masks some other local shops sold, but this was the real deal.

would highly recommend this place -- very very immersive experience - dont visit the free tour guide who describes some of the more interesting masks on display

Title: Interesting
Text: Very small museum with really beautiful traditional masks. We enjoyed the brief tour. The shop selling masks above is great and we found the prices very reasonable.

Title: Interesting experience
Text:
The masks is one of the symbols you often seen in Sri Lanka. This museum (also a factory) has great information on the masks.  A guide explains the various kinds of masks and the story behind each mask.  One can also see the various artisans working on the masks. Photography is allowed. The entire process of the mask making can be seen here.  Its an interesting experience as mask making is not often found in many countries.

It also has a shop were you can buy the masks as well as other souvenirs. Prices are reasonable and quality is good.

Title: Interesting and informative workshop with small 'museum'
Text:
This is not so much a museum as a workshop with a sales area and a small museum attached.

Our visit lasted about 20 minutes and it was an interesting experience. The lady who showed us round explained the symbolism and purpose of the various masks (there are hundreds), and it was also interesting to see the carving and painting of balsa-wood masks in the workshop.

I wouldn't recommend anyone to go out of his way to visit this museum (even if it has the largest collection on the island), as you can see much the same thing in handicraft shops in other towns - but if you are passing through Ambalangoda on the Galle road it is definitely worth a stop.

Title: Masks are made of light balsa wood, so buy away!
Text:
We read the reviews and were wary of pushy sales, but when we got there we didn't experience any more than any other place.
Before we went into the shop we were taken round the small museum and made a voluntary donation afterwards.  The guide explained the masks and drama of the displays and she did a very good job.  When we went into the mask shop we knew which were the ones we wanted to buy for health and posterity! 
We bought three masks and a carved elephant ashtray.  We bartered a little bit and got a good price. The side 'ears' of the masks come off for packaging and the wood is very light balsa, so will not make a real impact on your luggage allowance.
There is a toilet in there, but I'd recommend you 'go' before you go.
Our masks are a great colourful reminder of our Sri Lankan holiday.

Title: Interesting ...
Text: & worth a visit.  We had a good look around at the many masks & took pics but we didn't buy.  Imagine trying to get through customs in your mask!  I asked to have a look at the elephant  fridge magnets & I bought 1, they appeared shocked that I only wanted the one but I have no use for any more.

Title: Worth a short stop only
Text: The mask museum is touted as Sri Lanka's original/oldest by most people. It's located on the Galle Road and is a fairly small joint. A garage type workshop where one can do a very quick walk through seeing the artisans at work is the primary feature. The museum is a very small gallery depicting the culture and details on masks (nothing much to write home about). The staff make a very hesitant request for donations (albeit the large signboard that clearly specifies that the museum has been sponsored by a german agency). They are not pushy though. There is no entry fee (some places in Sri Lanka can hit you with a very high fee is you dont ask upfront).

Title: Interesting experience
Text: We bought a lot of boxes and a wooden mask that makes our day now in the house :) The place has also a museum and the lady there is very helpful in offering details and explaining all about masks. They have a lovely shop, very well provided and on its right side you can see the real-time work of children and people overthere. A lot of work though...

Title: Interesting if staying nearby
Text: Our guide appeared rather bored by the whole thing but there were some interesting masks and the shop was good with no pushy sales pitch.

Title: Intersting Stop in Sri Lanka
Text: As we headed out of Colombo south along the coastline to the Galle Fort, we stopped at the Ariyapala Mask Museum. As you enter the shop, a docent will take you on a very quick tour of the museum's collection of antique masks, explaining what they represent, and then, as always in Sri Lanka, you're asked for a donation.  Next is the gift shop, which was filled with all sorts of masks and baskets and trinkets.  I just loved this gift shop and found the prices were ok -- no bargaining though!!  I am pleased with my purchase of a colorful peacock God mask (the God of good humor, good look and harmony ... good choice!) and two beautiful masks of a Sri Lankan antique king and queen made from balsa wood. In Sri Lanka you're are constantly bombarded with hard core sales people, many seemingly untrustworthy, but this gift shop was not bad and I enjoyed my visit.

Title: Wood masks in the Sri Lankan tradition
Text: On your way to Galle, you may make a quick stop at Ambalangoda, visiting the Ariyapala Mask Museum. Well, calling it a museum may be too much ... There, you will be able to see the woodshop with a few artisans working on future masks; the so called Museum itself, with a nice collection of masks, all related to Srin Lankan folklore; and, of course, the Museum Shop. Avoid it! Prices are extremely high and you may be tempted to buy a mask that will be a burden to carry during the rest of your vacations. The entrance is free but you won't escape of being asked to make a small contribution to the Museum maintenance. Enjoy!

Title: Faces, faces everywhere
Text:
Liked:  makes possible a successful bank heist.

Disliked:  The thoughts of conducting a bank heist :)
Use of masks is ingrained in local culture.  One is exposed to the real as well as surreal when browsing the factory.

Title: These are the real masks
Text: It was interesting to find the history of the masks and to see real artisans making them. These are the real mckoy, not the flat, factory made ones you see all over Sri Lanka

Title: Mask Mania
Text:
This was not on our itinerary but our guide offered to stop for us to have a look and I am so glad she did. The museum is free and the lady in charge will provide you with information on the history of each exhibition in English. It was very interesting to learn about the masks and the history and cultural significance attached to different ones in the collection. i particularly liked the ones associated with medicine and "cures" for certain diseases!!

There is a shop attached to the museum but this is a very expensive place to purchase masks so I would advise giving this a miss. There are plenty of places throughout Sri Lanka where you can buy the same masks for about half the cost.

Title: worth a visit
Text:
This is one of the places that if you're passing by it is worth visiting but isn't a destination on its own. We were passing through Ambalangoda on our way back to Galle and the driver asked if we wanted to visit the museum (glad he did - certainly was a welcome break). 
The premises has a museum, a shop and a workshop. The museum is downstairs and worth visiting first. Admission is free and they have english speakers who can guide you through the displays and provide you with a more detailed explanation than necessarily contained on the boards next to the displays. There are a number of historical masks and dioramas (showing how they are used in performances). It gives a good appreciation of the culural significance that masks play. They do ask for a donation on the way out but as we got a guided tour it something we were happy to do. Upstairs is the shop (which is larger than the museum). Prices for the masks (dpendent upon the size) range from $40 - $150 US. Which are relatively expensive but you are paying for the quality and authenticity. For me the real bonus was the workshop at the side of the building, where you can watch the craftsman (& women) at work making the actual masks.

Title: Nice collection, but shop elsewhere
Text: Ariyapala is both a museum and shop. The museum was free and definitely interesting, but basically a gimmick to get you to go to their shop and buy their masks. I found a large selection of masks, which were very beautiful, but extremely expensive. I think since they got a good write up in the Lonely Planet, they have decided to charge as much as they can. If you have time, walk up and down the road leading to their store and look for smaller shops. I found a very nice shop albeit with a smaller selection at 1/3 of the cost. The quality of the craftsmanship was as good as Ariyapala if not better. I ended up buying 5 masks!!! Yeah, I know I went a bit overboard, but I couldn't resist. My advice is to check out L.A.R Nandana at No. 17 Sriniketharama Road.  Definitely worth a visit!!!

Title: HISTORY OF SRI LANKAN MASKS
Text: Admission is free and while there are small signs in the display cases, it is difficult to understand the history of masks and the cultural association without a guide.

Title: Everykind of mask there
Text: Unbeliveable collection of masks not to be seen elsewhere

Title: Very interesting
Text: Dont be put off by some reviewers...this is a very interesting museum.Dont spend too much time with the old machinery apart from noting its age and where it was made but do read the informative posters about the history of tea in Ceylon and its production.

Title: Interesting educational trip
Text: this is a great place to learn the production of tea before heading to a working tea factory worth the cost of the entrance if you like... no loveeee tea!

Title: Great visit
Text:
Very interesting and lots to see.  We had been to a working tea factory so it was good to see it without the mess!
Quite tricky to find, even with google maps.

Title: Expensive
Text: Our 2016 Lonely Planet showed this as costing 500 Rupees but it has gone up to 800 Rupees. The displays are reasonable as are the descriptions so providing a guide was unnecessary. It was also disappointing that the complimentary cup of tea was just a standard tea with no offer of milk. There were also no snacks.

Title: A private tour comes with your entrance fee, then you can wander back through at your leisure
Text:
I like that they have a complete compliment of the machines that are used to make black tea and they a guide leads you around and tells you how they work. Although, the guide can't go far beyond their trained texts.
I really enjoyed the artifacts on the upper floors of the factory. I really liked that the building is a preserved original in which manufacturing took place. I liked all the odd bits of history and the stories about James Taylor and Sir Thomas Lipton.
The drive up the hill to the museum is interesting, with pretty views.
I thought the museum missed a major opportunity serving such poor quality tea at the end of the guided tour.

Title: Much declined and poorly managed
Text:
Being a long resident and visitor to Kandy for over thirty years I have taken many guests to this museum over the years but not for a few years until recently. 

I was shocked to see the decline of this museum and the poor visitor experience it now offers. The museum itself is tired and dilapidated with no sign of any real care being taken to maintain it. A lot of areas are just empty spaces, dingy and dusty in the main.

Worst of all is standard of welcome, with staff simply going through the motions, indifferent to visitors to the point of rudeness. This attraction clearly needs to be much better managed to reflect the fine heritage of tea growing in Sri Lanka.

It is definitely not worth the time and expense involved in a visit. My advice is to find a working tea factory that is open to visitors. You will see and learn much more and certainly receive a better welcome than at the Tea Museum.

A real disgrace to Sri Lankan tourism to have let this place go to such ruin.

Title: Okay to visit
Text:
A must for tea lovers, but is a bit run down and is in need of some tender loving care and upgrade.
Great insight into the history of Ceylon tea

Title: Needs to be better
Text: This has the potential to be something. But as it stands its not good enough to be a proper tourist attraction. It needs to work harder in delivering a good tourist experience but the location is good, some of the info is great and the guide was informative but more by rote...didnt really bring the location to life. There is great potential for it...but as it stands its not good enough.

Title: Perfect place for a Tea Lover
Text:
As an avid tea drinker this was a must on my to do list in Sri Lanka.  We had our own guide for our family, who took as through all the floors of the old factory. Machines were explained and how they worked and the whole process was explained to us from picking to packing. The guide had excellent English so we had no trouble understanding and answered lots of our questions.  At the end we were given a free cup of very nice tea to enjoy. Different teas were available to try which you could purchase if you were still thirsty:).

There was an excellent shop to purchase to tea which we felt had a good selection and was reasonably priced. It took about an hour and half for us to complete which was a very comfortable pace.
This isn't something you can see in the UIK so a great opportunity to see something different, also the free tea at the end was very welcome something other similar places don't offer.

Title: Great insight to the origin of Ceylon Tea
Text: This is a great place to get an insight in to the origin of Ceylon tea. It is a bit away from main attractions. Still worth the visit.

Title: Seems a bit run down
Text:
From the approach it looks uninteresting, but once inside it has been well done. 
The building has been well restored and the machinery looks as if it could work today. 
We found it amazing the fortunes which were made and the role of Sir Thomas Lipton with James Taylor in creating a world industry in the late 1800s.
They must paint at least the sign at the entrance.
An explanatory video would be good.

Title: Ceylon tea museum
Text: Unique place.Worth visiting this place,especially for tea lovers.The whole process of tea preparation from tea plantation to a cup of excellent tea is nicely demonstrated here.

Title: Interesting
Text:
This was my first visit to a tea museum and it was interesting to learn all about different teas and the process of them.
Worth a visit if you know nothing about the process/history of tea.

Title: Culture
Text: As this is my favour drink it seems right that I spend time learning about it. Was very interesting learning about the process, Bush to cup. Than if course, the sampling, gotta ge done.

Title: Tea lovers
Text: Sri Lankan tea is one of the most famous one in world and here you can see the history of the same... Old machines and stories are great for a tea lover...

Title: Good little tour
Text: Bit of a dated place with a slight musky smell but still worth a visit. You get a walk through tour with a very informative guide and a cup of tea at the end. Learnt lots and really enjoyed the short visit here

Title: Good for a brief history
Text:
Being a big coffee drinker, didn't know much about tea and it's different processes, so this museum to me was quite fascinating.
Our guide was very detailed in her presentation of all the different steps taken for tea to become drinkable as we know it.
Was a true eye opener for me, but being in the food game, wasn't overly surprised at the procedure and the different steps to the final product.

Yeah sure the place was old, and smelt a touch, but surely that's what you'd expect from visiting such a place, so if you can block that out you'll be just fine.

Know that after you walk out of here, you'll look at tea in a different but refreshing light.

Title: Holiday
Text: Beautiful scenery, interesting museum,followed by a great cup of tea .  Would recommend a visit. Lots of tea plantations to visit in the area'all WIth breathtaking scenery.

Title: Strong tea fragrance
Text: The museum is for hardcore tea lovers or people who just want to go for the sake of it. Inside there's a horrible tea smell which can cause a suffocating feeling, especially to people with breathing issues. Skip it if you can. Nothing here for families or honeymoon couples.

Title: Okay but not a 'must-see'
Text:
It is just a small museum which is a bit interesting but probably not worth the money if I was honest.

We were hoping for working tea factories, however as the closest ones were quite far from Kandy, we had to resort to the Ceylon Tea Museum instead.

It includes a guided talk through the machinery but you can tell they only really stick to the core bits as the tour didn't last too long and we walked past a lot of the machinery on display.

The building has some cool history, and it was good to see the machinery, but as it's not a working factory you just walk around looking at old machines.

The best part was being able to try a cup of tea which was good, but even then you are only offered the basic black tea, with anything else being extra.

I probably wouldn't recommend it unless you don't have the time to travel a bit further to a working tea plantation, but if like us you really want to see tea related things and don't have the time, then it's probably a good visit.

Title: Nice insights on the origin and production of tea
Text: Entrance fee is 800 roepies per person but worth it. Access is possible via Tuktuk from Kandy. We started the descent by foot and jumped on a bus to take us back to Kandy for 20 roepies per person. We had an excellent explanation as a starter and, after a cup of tea, we could further explore the museum. A nice way to go, in my opinion... very interesting! Nice place!

Title: if you haven't been to any Tea factory.. then you should visit
Text: its like a normal tea factory., where is see the tea making process starting from plucking the leaves from plants to making it edible etc. you also get to buy Tea from the shop-- where you get a varied range of teas available. they also serve you a cup of tea on complementary basis

Title: Very enjoyable
Text: Interesting, informative and well presented tour. Well worth a visit and good value for money. AAA+++
Interesting place. Pleasant visit and glad we went.  There are lots of other tea museums Im sure so not sure if this is a must over any of the others.

Title: A great way to understand the process of tea production.
Text:
We grabbed a tuk tuk from Kandy, and was impressed by the wonderful scenery on the way. We were greeted by pleasant staff and our guide was so proficient in explaining the long process the tea goes through for us to enjoy the end product. The history of this factory was also explained with photos and paraphernalia There was a working model of the plant at the end of the presentation, a great touch! Upstairs you are given a complimentary cup of tea with your entrance fee, and other information boards regarding health benefits of drinking tea..
By visiting this Museum we were able to utilise this information, when we visited a working tea factory. The working tea factory was loud and we couldnt quite hear the guide. So, it didnt really matter as we already had that understanding of the process before visiting.

Title: You can do this for free in tea country !
Text: We went to the museum whilst in kandy only to regret it later! We paid 500rps for a tour of the old factory (now not working) to see old machines and get an idea of the tea making process. At the end you get a free cup of tea too. As we visited nuwara Eliya later and many other tea factories we realised we could actually do this for free! So for those visiting tea country avoid this museum - youll experience this tour many times without paying. Those who however Wont get the chance to do that then it is worth a visit to learn about the tea making process.

Title: The history of TEA - well packed!
Text: A lovely place to visit if you are really into tea and the history behind one of our absolute most popular drinks all over the world!

Title: Ravishing tour
Text: Truly superb visit to this well preserved gem. Hardly ten minutes from kandy by tuktuk, making it an excellent and insightful activity.

Title: Interesting historical visit
Text: We enjoyed learning about the early tea industry in Sri Lanka. The biggest drawback was the number of stairs that we had to climb.

Title: Superb in every way!
Text:
The museum is about 10km away from downtown Kandy, so we took a tuk-tuk, which was not expensive. Without being asked, the driver waited for us, while we were inside, so we volunteered a small waiting fee. 
I cannot over-emphasise how wonderful the museum is. My companion and I had a guide just for us (we were the only guests present for most of the time) and she was totally brilliant. My pal has an engineering background, and I'm a chemist, so we had some pretty deep questions for her, which she answered terrifically. I learned a heck of a lot about tea, which is good, cos being a Brit, I've drunk it all my life!
Speaking of Britishness, we were fascinated by how much of the antique processing equipment had been brought in from the UK, including some hydro-electric turbines made in the English Lake District! 
I enjoyed the quality control laboratory, as I once worked in QC.
The cup of tea at the end of the visit was very welcome, and most enjoyable.
This museum was one of the highlights of our entire trip.
I bought a small amount of tea (not expensive), and I'm sipping it as I write this. Delicious!

Title: Visit the tea museum
Text: Here you can learn everything bout tea making but the entrance fee was about 1000 rupees so it may be better to hold off until you are in a different area where admission charges are cheaper.
