The museum is located in the hillside outside Kandy and is surrounded by tea plantations. There are four floors and the upper floor is a tea shop/cafe.

Title: Very informative
Text: You can taste the tea with amazing flavor, good place to visit and see how tea is produced with so many varieties. Information are quite helpful for kids to understand the process.

Title: interesting and worth seeing
Text: After a lot of Temples and relics it was interesting to see the history of tea and the way it is dried and sorted and graded - worth visiting and fun to have tea in their shop and of course buy tea!

Title: Not to be missed!
Text: This quiet museum is a hidden gem!! Absolutely underrated by guide books!  It was fascinating to see traditional tea making equipment, and learn the history. Our entrance fee included a complementary guide who was professional and spoke excellent English. We finished with a delicious cup of tea in the café overlooking great views, and buying different types of tea from the shop for our friends and family.

Title: Tea factory in Kandy
Text:
Must visit if you want to see tea plantations in Kandy. the factory , musuem is about okay but the surrounding tea fields are very picturesque.

good photography point if you would just go down couple of bends from  the factory

Title: Must visit museum in Kandy
Text:
Just 3km from kandy city..This musium is all about tea history in Sri Lanka. Old tea factory has converted in to the musium. Totaly this is a 5 story building. LKR 100 for local and LKR 800 for foriegners. 
In these you can see many exhibits related to tea industry. You can see many  belonginess of the father of the tea Mr. James Tayler toi. There is a good simulation which showes how the tea factory works. The first tea bag, first tea drying machine, first tea rollimg machine  also exhibit.
Top of the museum there is a tea cafe and they will offer you free Sri  lankan tea.. its delicious. Next to it there is a big tea sales shop with various tea types in sri lanka.

Title: What it says on the tin
Text:
Probably not the most exciting excursion but still interesting. 

We found our tour guide to be very good and thorough in showing us how the tea making process used to work. 

It's worth noting that this is no longer a working factory and all machinery is just available for show. The information provided is a good foundation for our experiences to come in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Old-Timey Tea Factory
Text: This museum illustrates the history of tea in Sri Lanka in the building of a former tea factory.  Lots of old machinery, the tour is brief but informative.  Our weaker score is in relation to visiting an actual working factory where everything is clearer and in use (and free).  Bathrooms outside had no soap or TP.  You get a cup of tea at the end.

Title: All you wanted to know about the history of tea
Text: This tour takes you back in time to the infancy of tea - John Taylors time. It also has some very good early machinery in the whole tea production process. There is a tasting and tea to purchase to take home. It is over 4 levels and made up like an old production factory which it was.

Title: Interesting visit
Text:
Visited here recently. A very interesting place to visit. Its free to enter and you are shown around by a guide then given a cup of tea and offered the chance to buy some sea leaves. Friendly staff and not pushy with the sales so that was good. 
Beware of the ladies washrooms - I was nearly sick, they were BAD!

Title: The best introduction you will find to tea in Sri Lanka
Text:
The museum tour was excellent - the guide was amazingly good and knew all there was to know about the machinery, the processes, the history and the part it played, and is still playing, in Sri Lankan history.
This tour is better than anything you will get in the Nuwara Eliya area.
Well laid out and very informative - I've been to tea estates many times before but this museum was still up there with the best.
Highly recommend a visit.

Title: Very interesting tour
Text:
My wife and I really enjoyed this visit. We were given a guided tour of the old tea factory. Don't  spend too much time with the old machinery, year of manufacture will give you the right perspective.
Cost of tour is LKR800. If Lonely Planet has it wrong that is not a matter for discussion in this forum.
At the end of the tour we were offered tea. The large pot was a reasonable BOP, milk and sugar were included.
Would recommend this tour to anyone visiting Kandy.

Title: Greata stop...better than other "tea museums"
Text: Great stop that was not originally on our trip route. We asked the driver to detour there and it was much better than the tea factory we had seen the day before. Very well laid out and informative tour.

Title: Interesting and not pushy!
Text:
Really interesting site. Because it's not operational you can look closer at the machines than you can in the working ones. 
The guide was clear friendly and knowledgeable. A welcome free tea at the end with no pressure at all to buy anything.

Title: Surpisingly interesting!
Text: We visited this museum not sure it would be worth bothering about. But it is worth the visit as it puts the whole tea planting history into context.

Title: Low key but informative
Text:
The museum is well set out with lots of original machinery and explanations about the history of tea making and processing. There is really good video presentation on the top floor next to the cafe where you get your free tea to drink

Its low key but worth the trip up into the hills

Title: Fascinating stories of tea and tea workers but needs modernising intepretation
Text: This has all the makings of a good museum but it needs to emloy far better intepretation techniques - it's rather dated and dead but could be fantastic if enlivened by, say, oral history recordings, and the machinery not set out in straight rows but put more into context and with a video of production adjacent. But still worth the visit! and you get a free cup of tea!

Title: not worth the time
Text: we learnt nothing here, as when we got here it was a busy day with some school kids from colombo, all 16 busloads of them. the guides were busy briefing the kids, so we had to figure out the machines on our own (its written in english) but that's about it. upon reaching to the top floor (5 floors in total), we were allow to taste 1 cup of tea (which they had like 6 different kinds of teas - we thought you could try them all before deciding what to buy later at the gift shop). but nope, the rude staff were like, 'no we only have this one'. So....... it's quite unfortunate the experience was so bleah. How do i know which tea to buy later at the gift shop? So we left after that one cup amidst all the screaming school children :/

Title: Almost to ourselves.
Text: After the hordes of visitors in the 'cultural triangle', many locals, it was pleasant surprise to be one of only three couples at this informative place. Short but sufficiently detailed guided tour to see how a tea factory worked. Free cup of tea. Shop, but almost all tea! vey worthwhile.

Title: History of the Tea industry
Text: A most interesting collection of equipment, maps and photos plus an excellent cup of tea.An insight into the probelsm faced by our Victorian ancestors

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The guide was very informative and it was very interesting to hear and see the original equipment. However be prepared for a tortuous journey up the mountain to reach the Museum.

Title: Great visit
Text:
was a little worried thatb it would be boring (sorry) but the young lady showing us round was engaging and informative... the tour lasts 15 minutes and as really interesting - and finished with... a great cup of tea!
gifts overpriced but ....hey ho
worth a visit

Title: The history of tea.
Text: This museum really tells the story of tea in what was originally called Ceylon. It's a fascinating story from how tea is picked to how it is brewed. And at the end of the story you get to taste different types of tea as well as the opportunity to purchase tea packets to bring home.

Title: Interesting, but could be better
Text: Tuk Tuk ride to the top of a hill outside Kandy. You're given a guide to take you round the museum, which is helpful. The guide was decent, but could have been a bit more enthusiastic. There are three floors and a cafe on top where you get a complimentary cup of tea. After that you can take your time going back through the displays, with more time to read the exhibits or buy some tea. We found the history very interesting, particularly the links to our home country of Scotland. The women working in the café were almost rude, which was completely unnecessary.

Title: december holiday
Text: Good experience given tea to drink with jaggery it like sugar you first have to take a bite of the sugar and then sip the tea

Title: Informative and nice designed place
Text:
In former tea factory, this museum has tours included in (budget) ticket and cup of tea at the end. There's a small garden where one can see tea plant and pick a leaves. Also degustation of the different kinds of tea and free cup.
Just at the begining the staff was anyoing forsing me several times to stop reading and join the tour. It's my choice what will I do, ladies...

Title: Interesting history - and a pleasant cup of tea!
Text: A pleasant way to spend a morning.  Your ticket for entry includes a guided tour of the museum along with a cup of delicious Ceylon tea at the end of the tour.  Interesting history of this factory which is no longer in operation.  Negotiate no more than 1000LKR for a round-trip tuk-tuk to the tea factory.

Title: Very informative
Text:
I went to four tea factories in Sri Lanka in a short period of time, and this was the most informative one. We were lucky to have a knowledgeable guide who spoke clear English. The fact that this is a quiet "museum factory" also made it a lot easier to actually take in the information.

The oral guiding is complemented by a good video shown in the tea room, where you can enjoy a good cup after the tour.  There are also additional displays there for those who remain intellectually curious.

There is a small tea store, but no hard sell at all.

Title: Historical place.
Text: There are many old machines. Books,documents books and pictures are displayed.there.Nice visit it is worth to visit.It explains about Srilanka Ceylon tea history,

Title: Informative tour
Text: Want to know more about tea then be sure to visit this place and follow it with a cup of tea like you have never tasted before . Sales people but NOT pushy

Title: Quite interesting
Text: We were shown all the old machines and the process the tea leaves went through to end up in our cup. Floors 2 and 3 didnt have much and the top floor was where you got your cup of tea

Title: Excellent shopping worth the stopover
Text: The shop has an extensive range of teas with the chance to sample some of the blends. The prices are average for Sri Lanka. The factory tour will give those with no knowledge enough to ponder when they sip their tea back home. The hard labour that goes into making one cup of tea is not always known let alone appreciated.

Title: You have to see the home of tea
Text: Quite a small factory tour of the tea process. A must do while in Sri Lanka but not an impressive overview of the tea world. Good to try the different teas.

Title: Very intristing- not impresive
Text: We liked the place, it isnt perfect , but it can be very good background before visiting the tea factory

Title: Tea museum
Text: The title says it all, and it left much to the imagination. We were the only pair in the museum when we visited and this made our visit very quiet and seem strange. The entrance fee also includes a pot of tea at the end of the tour. Alternative drinks were offered, but those had to be paid for. Our guide told us about the various machines, but it was much more interesting (and free) when we went to a working tea factory.

Title: Somewhat Interesting
Text: The museum is filled with old tea making machines. It is interesting for the first room or two, but then it becomes a bit tedious. Our guide droned on about these machines in a monotone like she had given this presentation a thousand times before. The best thing of all was the tea tasting at the end of the tour. Overall, meh.

Title: This is how they make tea
Text: We enjoyed our visit to the tea museum. It was made that much more informative with the help of our guide. Worth the time to visit.

Title: Tea Museum
Text:
We stopped here on our way to the botanical gardens.

I don't drink tea and my husband didn't before we went to Sri Lanka. However it was very interesting to learn about tea production.

We bought a few teas which we took home and my husband subsequently enjoyed.

Our guide was pleasant, I felt a bit for her like she had said the same thing over and over again.

It's an interesting way to spend an hour and learn about the islands tea industry.

Title: Tea plantation
Text: We got to do our own tea picking and stay in this lovely Converted factory. It's at the very top of a lovely quaint village.

Title: An insight into tea production  in years gone by
Text:
This was a guided tour by a very informative pleasant friendly guide.wellworthwhile if you are interested in bygone days.Once the tour has finished you are able to continue and look without the guide.A free cup of tea is available after the completion of the tour.
Lovely views from the top floor.
Cannot remember exactly how much the entrance fee was but it was not exorbitant.
We took a tuk tuk to the museum which cost 600 rupees

Title: Worth a visit.
Text: We arrived just in time to join a small guided tour of the old tea factory, which  has 5 floors and is well maintained. The short tour gave us a good overview of how tea is made, and all the machinery was really interesting and in good condition. After the brief tour, we had a free cup of tea and were then left to browse through the whole building again at our leisure. Well worth the 400 rupees (£2) entry fee.

Title: Fascinating insight into the history of tea in Sri Lanka and how it went from field to packet!
Text: There is a guided tour and the guide explains all the machines etc but once finished you can wander around at leisure. Tour finished with a free cup of tea though you had to pay for the iced tea.....it was very informative if a bit lacking in atmosphere.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Our informative and pleasant guide explained the process of producing tea leaves very well. The old machinery is very interesting. The included cup of tea at the end of the tour was very much appreciated. Well worth a visit.

Title: Interesting tea introduction
Text: An interesting introduction to any tea tours on the way to Hill Country, in an old tea factory. However, the same information more or less you can get for free in the working factories, so you can avoid the steep ticket or the detour.

Title: Maybe worth a trip but better go to one that is not a museum.
Text: I had two plans arriving in Kandy, since I have been here many times; visit the Ceylon Tea Museum & for the 2nd time travel to Peradeniya Botanical Gardens since I haven't been there since 2010. I KNOW it's +/- 4 kms from Kandy & I thought I could take a bus BUT my hotel manager said there are NO buses to  Ceylon Tea Museum. (WRONG!) anyway, he arranged a tuk-tuk for RS 600/RS 800. I got two different prices. Since I have NO clue how long it will take to see it the tuk-tuk driver was SUPPOSED to wait & drive me back to Kandy. Once there he follows me (I can tell time IS money) & he wants to get back. I'm in the middle of the tour and haven't even had a pot of tea. I give him RS 500, since he was  SUPPOSED to wait but he wants MORE! Give me RS 800, he says. I give him RS 800 & tell him to take off, I'll walk back. Creep!!!! I finish the tour, look around the old paintings/posters and have a pot of tea. Then I walk outside to cane to Kandy. I see a bus going up the hill & hope one will go back down to Kandy later on. Lucky me, bus # 655 comes by 30 later and for a whole RS 16 I get a ride to the bus station. FYI; IF you go to a tea plantation it's better than here as there is NO actual tea. There are tea plants outside but it is just a museum.  It's only $5+ dollars, man. It is better you go where they are in reality processing tea.

Title: Good but heavily scrpited
Text: The museum and displays are good and the guide taking us around was good, but the descriptions and process seemed to be a scripted without much time to ask questions. Felt like it was a way of getting us around a s quickly as possible so hopefully we would buy something at the shop.

Title: Did learn a thing or two
Text: I did learn a thing or two at the tea museum, however, I found it overpriced for such a short tour that ended with a mediocre cup of tea.

Title: Interesting, superb guide but a little overpriced
Text:
As previous reviewers have mentioned this is a great place to come if:
- you want to learn more about the tea industry and history of tea in Sri Lanka
- you want something to do to stay cool during the heat of Kandy 

I enjoyed it as I have quite an interest in colonial history and the tea industry. My wife was not so keen and preferred our experience at a working factory. The price of entry has risen and I feel is pushing it slightly for what is on offer. You will also need to outlay for a three wheeler to get here and back.

Having been to a working tea factory the machinery and process section wasnt overly impressive. However our guide was wonderful, very knowledgeable and with great English. Also the working model of a factory was great though! In contrast the collection of historical artefacts was really interesting and nicely displayed.

The cup of tea at the end was delicious and as ever service was excellent. If you are interested in tea its well worth a visit.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The museum very quiet when visited (there were more staff present than visitors). We found the tour interesting and enjoyed learning about the history of tea. You get s free cup of tea included and there are several stores selling tea which makes ideal souveniers

Title: Highly recommend
Text: We went to the Tea Museum based on reviews on TA and th expectations were not very high. To our pleasant surprise, it turned out to be a good visit. The guide was very knowledgeable and patient. She explained various steps involved in tea making. The tea tasting experience was also good. My daughter enjoyed the ice tea available at a nominal price, while I sipped BOP tea.

Title: Great experience
Text: Must  to visit this place, where you can learn how tea was made and see the varieties of tea  with  a cup of tea for free.

Title: All you need to know about tea!
Text:
Based in the hills above Kandy, the Ceylon Tea Museum is a short tuk tuk journey away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre.  The museum is based in a former tea factory but it retains all the equipment used in early tea production and paints a clear picture of the tea production process and how it evolved.  

Included in the cheap entry cost is an informative guided tour and a cup of tea.  There are also a number of shops in the building selling tea at the end of the tour.  The whole visit takes less than a couple of hours and is a good chance to escape the midday heat.

Title: Interesting trip with a free cup of tea
Text:
This is a good trip to take if you have a spare hour or two whilst in Kandy. The museum is about 20 -30 mins in a tuk tuk from Kandy city centre (depending on the traffic getting out of Kandy!) And the free  guided tour at the museum takes around 20 minutes also.

Interesting collection  of old tea factory items as well as some good information on the history of tea. There is a free cup of tea at the end of the tour and also some shops where you can buy different types of tea.

Title: Great experience
Text: This is a gem of a museum, hidden away outside Kandy. It features very personalized tours including a nice cup of tea through an original old tea factory. The guided tour is included in the ticket price and is very friendly and informative. The gift shop has a wide selection of local tea to take home. A must see in Kandy!

Title: A great experience.
Text:
A nice educating museum located in an old tea factory just few km out of Kandy. We received an English tour, which was very interesting. Entrance fee was reasonable and the staff was very friendly. Gave us a lot of information and interesting details about tea growing in general and about Sri-Lanka's tea production and plantations.
definitely worth a visit (with a complimentary cup of tea at the end of the tour).

Title: worthy of your visit
Text: Located in old tea factory among the teagardens, the museum provides an informative insight into development of the tea industry that make Sri Lanka famous

Title: We loved it!
Text: A great visit. It was so interesting and the guide was extremely informative. It was great to see and understand the history of Ceylon tea. Definitely recommend!!

Title: Pop in for a Cuppa!
Text: We got a great insight into the process of making tea with our guided tour around the museum. The guide was very friendly and a free cup of tea was provided at the end of the tour. All in all, a pleasant place to visit.

Title: Buzz of history in a lovely setting
Text: Very interesting to see the process of preparing tea leaves. The museum is worth visiting to see and read about some of the history. The guided tour was appreciative to see what processes occur in the preparation of tea. The surrounds are lovely, and you can see tea leaves being picked.

Title: Pleasant staff with tour and shops
Text:
We stopped here on our way to Kandy for an hour or so. It was quiet when we arrived, although a tour group turned up just as we were heading out.

After paying the entrance fee we had a whistle stop tour of the machinery and process, before heading upstairs for the complementary tea. You are encouraged to have a look round the different vendors located the floor down from the cafe, but it is not required. We bought a few gifts from one of the shops though, as there is a reasonable selection.

Worth visiting if you're in the area, and you're interested in tea and the tea making process (my partner enjoyed it!).

Title: If you like tea...
Text: My husband was more interested than me... They show how the tea was made years  ago. I am not sure I would go if he did not ask for it.

Title: Not worth it - Unless this is your only time in the hill country
Text: Nothing special given the outrageous entry fees; one can visit other tea factories in and around the hill country much more cheaply (if not free) - and see the production process to boot. If one has no time and only in Kandy, fair enough; otherwise, give it a miss!

Title: Underwhelming
Text:
We took a tuk tuk up to the museum expecting an engaging experience. My expectations were not met. We were shown around the museum by a lovely hostess after paying our admission fees. We saw machinery used in the tea making process from the C19. We were then entitled to a 'free' tea, included in the admission fee. There was no description of which tea it was ie which region. I can only assume that it wasn't Kandy as apparently tea from Kandy is best consumed with milk. I'm not a tea drinker so wasn't overly concerned. There was a video in the tea room outlining the history of tea in Sri Lanka. I found the video the most engaging part; until it stopped short of the end. 
We ventured into an area that was part of the tea plantation and again this was underwhelming as it appears that the area in close proximity, where we were advised to go, is no longer part of a plantation. The insight into the 'human element' of the tea plantation was best observed from the tuk tuk where we observed the shacks the tea pickers lived in, from the road. Very rudimentary conditions. 
Maybe I didn't do enough research in advance of heading up the hill. Unless you're a tea lover fascinated by the historical presence an processes involved in the tea making process, I'd give this a skip. I'm interested in the human element and the landscape of tea plantations and I clearly went to the wrong spot.

Title: Well Worth Visiting
Text: Having seen enough temples, my wife and I decided to visit the Tea Museum instead. Although they levy a charge, you are given value for money, unlike many other things and sights we experienced in Sri Lanka. A guide goes along with you to explain the use of all the displayed machines and the processing of tea leaves. It is very informative. At the end, you are also given a very nice cup of tea!

Title: A Lovely Place...
Text: A lovely tea museum situated atop Hantana. The weather is different and you will feel like you are in a much colder clime than Kandy. Tea is tasty. They have small boutiques to sell them as well. You can read a lot of history here. A wonderful place to visit.

Title: Surprisingly amazing
Text:
Guides so knowledgable and friendly, definitely worth the 800Rs entry fee. 
There were no negatives about this visit - it was amazing to learn so much about tea. Much better value than temple of the tooth

Title: Very serene environment, good tea!
Text: I really enjoyed coming to this place. I did not expect much as it was located in such rural area. There was a guided tour, free tea, and tea market where I could get some discount to get tea!

Title: Educational
Text:
Arriving at the Tea Museum seemed it had not much to offer but as one walks it way through the various levels one can appreciate the educational Tea history this museum has to add to ones knowledge.
It wonderful to note how Tea originated and the equipment used to process tea for everyday consumption.
The complimentary tea is refreshing while watching the tea documentary on the TV.

Title: A bit of a tourist trap
Text: A bit of an overpriced tourist trap aimed at selling you teas from boutiques on the top floor. However they did educate us about the different types of Ceylon tea and James Taylor so the trip wasn't totally wasted. I would say though buy your tea from the supermarket not the tourist shops.

Title: Must do for tea enthusiasts !
Text:
Old factory turned into a museum with refurbished production equipment. Guides are so knowledgable and patient that they won't let any questions unanswered.
I would likely recommend the visit to anybody, tea enthusiast or not !
Stay for the tea tasting on upper floor and watch the documentary, highly instructive too.

Title: Hidden place with a lot of history
Text: Ask your guide to take you there. For 800rupees you get a guided tour and a tasty ceylon tea. Staff was nice and smilling all the time

Title: Hard to find the museum but worth the visit
Text: We struggled to find this place, arrived an hour before closing time and wish we had longer. Entrance fee 800 rupee per adult includes a cup of fresh tea which is particularly delicious. The museum guides are very engaging and eager to share their knowledge of the tea production process. We learnt lots, it is not as straight forward as one may assume. There is much hard work in gruelling temperatures to create the tea for a cuppa. It is humbling to learn of the history.

Title: "Good Attraction "
Text: We couldnt see the functioning  factor as it was Holiday time and people were out of the city with their family. But we did visit the factory and saw the machinery. Its a must to visit place and very nicely preserved. Also different types of tea that is been made there. Its worth going. And if you are a Tea Lover to buy some Ceylon Tea you would love it..

Title: A good museum but poor guiding inside
Text:
This is nice museum and has some really interesting exhibits.  What spoilt it for me was that lady guide, that just whisked us around, without really giving any information, other than a rehersed speech.  Maybe it was the English barrier, but I felt that she was only interested in getting the tour over.  You can go around after and have another look properly, and I would definately encourage you to do just that.  There are alot of interesting exhibhits that really do require you to read the plaques.
Questions that I asked were not answered fully and did not invite further discussion.
There is a tea room at the top, where you can sample some tea (although you can't choose which one).  They offer no edibles with the tea, and I feel if they offered light bites, they would certainly do well.  I suggested this to them.
The plaques are all in English, and this seemed rather strange.  I would have thought it would have been in both languages.  
Worth a visit, but don't expect too much from your guide

Title: Nicely preserved; helpful docent; no sense of factory
Text: Housed in a formed tea processing factory, the museum has very well preserved machinery, good labeling, a nice working miniature model, and a pleasant tasting cafe.  We got a very nice tour from one of the museum's docents (whom we tipped but were not charged additional beyond high admission fee).  It's a classy and pleasant place to spend some time.  However, without any machines running or workers running around, you will not get a sense of what a working factory feels like.  (I've been to one elsewhere.)  It's also up a long and winding road from Kandy so while the views are nice, the drive takes some time and is a bit jarring.

Title: Might be a museum but not much has changed!
Text:
If you visit a working tea factory add this to the itinerary as it gives an idea of the early days.  That said a lot of the machinery was still in use in the actual tea factory we visited,  mostly British dating from 1950.
A well presented museum and the tour ends with a cup of tea!
Guide was clearly knowledgeable but at times her diction was difficult to understand.She had another tour waiting so preliminary guided tour was rather too pacy, but wandering around on your own is easy because everything has a written explanation.  Pictures of tea pioneers and how they got machinery in and tea out were priceless.

Title: Pleasant few hours looking at and old factory and learning about tea
Text: This is a great little museum, dealing mostly with the processing of tea once it's been picked, and the history of tea cultivation in Sri Lanka. It's very clean and very well laid out. A guide showed us around first, and then left us to explore things in more detail. One disappointment was that there weren't any tea plants around, so it's not terribly scenic; it really is just the factory. (Location: A few kilometers out of Kandy, up in the hills. We paid 500 LKR in taxi fair one-way from the center of Kandy.)

Title: Interesting!
Text: What a great little museum. The ticket price includes a quick guided tour by one of the guides. They explain the tea making  process and the different machines and then point out a few interesting things on each floor then leave you alone to browse and read in detail anything that takes your interest. The view from the top floor where you drink a lovely cup of Ceylon tea is also worth your time!

Title: History of Tea
Text: Having been to Nuwara Eliya and spent the whole day passing through and stopping on different tea plantations to drink a cup of tea and go around and listen to a lady dressed in their national costume and explain to you how tea is being processed, you would want to give this place a visit. The Ceylon Tea Museum in Hantana is a bit of a climb (well, I haven't literally climbed it as I was riding in a car, but the road's a bit steep and its recommended to get a tuktuk because its a bit far from the main road of Kandy), but worth the visit if you're truly interested in the history of Ceylon Tea. There were only a few visitors when I visited the place. Not very crowded compared to the tea plantations I've visited in Nuwara Eliya. Here, you'll find the very first tea packet, the first machinery used to produce tea in the land, the story on how Sir James Taylor started the tea industry in Sri Lanka and even one of the first tea shrubs ever. The experience was overwhelming as you could see how the tea industry in the country has evolved from manually grinding and drying the tea leaves to the modern way used in tea plantations nowadays. It's definitely a must-go place for tea lovers like me. There's a pot of tea that awaits you at the end of the tour.

Title: Tea story
Text: IF you're interested in a bit of the history of the British in Sri Lanka, how the tea business was set up and operated, in having a nice tuk tuk ride out of town and in buying some tea from source, this nice old wooden factory on a hillside ticks all the boxes. Clean and nicely presented museum with plenty of original tea processing machinery and storage facilities etc, plus a decent selection of historical imagery, documents, posters, tea pots, you name it....to stare it, and a decent cuppa too. There is an entry charge.

Title: Worth the trip! Make this part of your trip onto other destinations (e.g airport)
Text:
Save yourself the tuk tuk fare by doing the travel this way. It is definitely worth a trip and although it is hard to appreciate the machinery without seeing an active factory, it definitely provides you with an overview of the process and some insightful history about the origins of tea planting in Sri Lanka.

It's also a good spot to buy some tea, but be prepared to hustle!

Title: Really interesting and informative
Text: Make sure you try and visit this museum, housed in an old tea factory. The exhibits are in a good state and you do come away much better informed about everything to do with tea.  You even get a free cup of delicious tea afterwards and there are a few nice little shops on the upper floor.

Title: A bit boring and very overpriced
Text: Compared to other tea factories in the central highlands, this one was very average. At 800rp per person it was several times more pricey than other places, and it's more of a historical place than anything else. It is just an old building with traditional machines inside. The tour is ok but quite brief and the tea they give you afterwards isn't very nice... you don't get to choose what tea you get, and if you ask for milk they give you milk powder. The tea factories we visited in Ella and Nuwara Eliya are so much more informative and interesting, and way cheaper.

Title: A great museum
Text: Well worth the tuk tuk ride out of Kandy. A beautiful spot and real insight into the history of tea and how it is made.

Title: Nice visit - see key info below
Text:
It was a nice visit. Nothing too spectacular but still worthwhile. Website and travel book info is slightly outdated:
Admission: Rs 800
Opening hrs: Tue-Sat 8:30 to 15:30h
Good 10min Tuk Tuk drive from center

Title: Worth the effort
Text:
Took about an hour and was worth the trip.  We felt the tour could have included more info on the history, this was a little sparse.  The setting is lovely and is great to see how tea is produced.  The staff are friendly and laid back.  
Is a short ride up from kandy town.  You can catch a tuk tuk,  but note that a bus is just as easy going up and back and will save you a bit of money

Title: Great place to learn about tea!
Text: Set high in the hills of a working tea plantation, this massive former tea factory preserves historic processing equipment and is full of exhibits and stories about tea. A visit begins with a tour, then you can wander around on your own. Ticket cost of Rs. 800 also includes a pot of good tea. The 3-kilometer drive up Hantane Road is very scenic as it twists through hills up to the tea plantation and museum. I did it on a bicycle, slowly and with low gears!

Title: Would be average but for the price its poor
Text:
This seems to contradict other reviews but to be honest its not that great. Yes, you can get a cheap bus up there and the trip up there alone is of course worth the SLR15 each but the climax is just a bit disappointing. 

The museum tour is literally 10 minutes and focuses only on the machines stored within museum, at the expense of the history behind the industry which when is addressed seems to ignore colonialism...bit odd. 

Go if you have an extra day in Kandy otherwise I would just stay in town, get some short eats and drink a cup of Ceylon tea in the real world.

Title: Must visit with little kids.
Text:
My husband planned it because he wished both kids to see how actually tea was originated. We loved the guide and we loved the British era building very well kept too. 

The tea they offer actually opens your eyes that what crap actually multinational companies are serving you in the name of finest tea.

We bought loads of tea from there.

Must visit if you believe in the quality of life.

Title: A must visit for the complimentary cuppa if nothing else!
Text:
If you drink tea and would like to see the process of drying and machinery involved, this one is a must visit. They have a decent variety of tea leaves and they are happy to answer your questions. The tour begins from the ground floor and when you reach the top floor, you are served a complimentary cup of tea. 

They also have a small shop for people to buy tea samples and accessories. I did buy some flavoured and Ceylon tea packets from the place and they were good. However I did find later that you could buy it cheaper elsewhere! Not sure why the price difference when the factory should be the cheapest; but overall it was worth the visit. A must do in Kandy.

Title: Best place for tea in Kandy
Text: Avoid the other tea shops that all the tour buses go to. This working factory gives you a tour guide, teaches you about tea and gives you a nice cup of tea at the end of the short and simple tour. The shop has many teas to buy and take home and there is no need for asking for a discount. Great experience for tea lovers and non -tea lovers alike.

Title: Kandy is a town based of plantation industry
Text: there are different tea factories and make sure the tuk tuk takes you to the correct location , tell them it is the government tea museum

Title: a tea factory
Text: This is a Ceylon tea factory. Take a round to see  that the tea is made from the leaves. They make different quality of tea and the same is offered to buy.

Title: want to know about TEA then this is the place
Text: it was actually a tea factory which was turned in to a museum. its the factory which has James Taylor's (first person to plant tea in Sri Lanka) equipments and things he used. you can see the machines there. it will cost you 750 LKR ($15) if you are not a local.  its well worth it. the ladies who are there will explain how you make tea and you really can learn a lot from them. you can even to tea tasting and buy tea and enjoy a cup as well. many tour operators or guides will not take you to this place cause they will not get a commission out of your purchases. just 5km away from Temple tooth and easy to find.

Title: Fun museum
Text: We walked up from our guesthouse to this museum and it was a pleasant guided tour. Unfortunately the museum closes at 4:30pm and we therefore did not have enough time to see all of it.

Title: fabulous
Text: a fabulous afternoon seeing from the tree the leaves being picked and how it is processed to the end and then a lovely cup of tea, in my top 3 for places to visit

Title: Quaint
Text: To understand the tea in your teacup you must come here Lthough they no longer process tea. The young lady was informative and showed and explained all the machinery involved in the process from bush to your cup. The museum is a bit quaint but if you embrace the tour it is interesting. On 4 levels, there is no lift, so only the ground floor is suitable for the physically challenged! 5$ p.p. this includes a pot/cup of tea at the end on the 4th where there is a very interesting film of the whole process - history to benefits of tea drinking today. 3rd floor a no "pressure to buy" area. The staff are charming, happy for you to look, not feel obligated to buy. Well done.

Title: Ceylon tea museum
Text: There are many tea states in Ceylon . Ceylon was the name of Sri Lanka .here they have a collection of all the different type and Flavours of tea .

Title: interesting and informative
Text: this is a must visit place.   it is a really nice museum with lots to see. pros :  the museum building is nice.  the equipment used during the era are interesting.  there was a tour guide who brought us around.  there were a few shops selling tea. there was a cafe which offered free tea. the different types of teas are very interesting.  the history of tea is interesting. cons : the tour guide was not as interactive as we would have liked.  she just recited  what she had to. infact, she did not allow us time to look at the stuff and ask questions. she was more interested in keeping to the time.  the free tea offered at the cafe was just given to us in a pot and 2 cups. there was no one to explain what kind of tea it was.  there was a video playing but to us, first timers there, it was kinda boring.  the shops close at 330pm as the official closing time of the museum is 345pm.  you need to have sufficient to look at the articles, and spend some time in the shops. on the whole, it was rather informative.  there is a entrance fee.

Title: Another part of our tour of Sri Lanka
Text: This was very interesting to see from start to finish where our cup of  tea comes from, we had a guided tour of the factory and then a nice cuppa before we did the gift shop and went on our travels

Title: Insight to tea processing
Text: The tea museum showcases the history of tea production in Sri Lanka and variety of tea available. Along with the entrance ticket (which is over-priced), you get to taste a complimentary tea in museum.

Title: Tea museum, Kandy
Text: well organised and presented in a lovely building, with superb views from its windows. Enjoyed  reading about the history of the tea plantations of Sri Lanka.

Title: Excellent visit to Ceylon Tea Museum
Text: We visited the Ceylon Tea Museum in the afternoon, following the hectic hustle and bustle of Kandy-life and it proved a fantastic getaway for an hour or two. The museum is a converted tea factory, which is gorgeous in itself, and the display of machinery is just amazing. The guided tour was great - the guide such a lovely lady and with excellent English to answer all our questions. The history of tea in Sri Lanka was presented very well with all sorts of tea-related paraphernalia throughout the ages on display. The building and exhibits are maintained extremely well (nice to see the displays and building being taken care of compared to some other museums in the country). The tea shops and tasting on the top two floors are worth visiting. We spent over an hour here. It was very quiet when we went at 1pm, only a handful of visitors, but beware, the museum closes earlier than other Kandian site (3pm that day I think). Great views of Kandy from the road up there too!

Title: Tea Trip
Text: Great museum- with a full working model of the factory- They have a very friendly staff to give you a full tour of the machinery and you get a free cup of tea at the end. Really enjoyed seeing the factory.

Title: Old timey tea factory
Text: 800rp to get it but it's well worth it. We had a great tour which is included in the cost. The woman's English was very good and she explained how the tea was produced, something which wouldn't have been apparent without her explanation. The second top floor is the gift shop. They take you to the floor briefly to say you are welcome to buy something afterwards but don't pressure you at all. On the top floor you get a complimentary pot of tea. You can then go back down and look at all the stuff that was missed during the tour. I highly recommend. Lots of antique tea equipment and the building itself is beautiful.

Title: Interesting place for learning tea
Text: This museum gives me history of tea in sri lanka, how to process tea leaf into our mug, and ended with a cup of tea. Clean place but the toilet. Has some tea souvenir shop in it. With Lkr 800 entrance fee, they also guide us into the museum and also for a cup of tea. I also spent 800Lkr for tuktuk from kandy station to this museum and the tuktuk driver wait for me while I'm in it and return to kandy station.

Title: Very interesting.
Text:
Really enjoyed it here, good info provided
Nice to see all this old machines and methods, and after the tour a nice cup of tea.
Pathway to Tea museum needs to be renewed.

Title: Enjoyable.  Expectations that you will purchase!
Text: This was a brief but interesting tour followed by the big sell in the tea shop.  The tea is hugely, hugely overpriced but the little tour was informative.

Title: Enjoyable and informative visit
Text: We visited a tea plantation south of Kandy, but were pleased that we'd visited here (Ceylon Tea Museum) first.  It was informative and our guide (provided by the venue) was helpful.  Nice free cuppa at the end of the trip, too.

Title: Seen the plantations? Now see what happens to it
Text: There are several tea factories in and around Kandy, however the tea museum is more than a factory.  It follows the introduction of tea to Sri Lanka, the history of its production, giants in the tea industry who have influenced the name of Ceylon tea.  After the tour, you get to have a nice cuppa too.

Title: Full History of Tea Making
Text: This museum gives you a really good history and background to how tea came to Sri Lanka. As well as housing the machines that they used to use to process the tea. Interesting visit. We were the only ones there when we went which made for more of a private tour.

Title: A Eye opener to the history of tea
Text: The Ceylon Tea Museum is one of it kind and is a must visit in kandy, it gives the history of tea and also about the different type of tea in the region

Title: nicely detailed tour of tea manufacturing
Text: nice beautifully restored machines, clean and personal tour guide provided, tea and tea paraphernalia for sale.

Title: Worth a visit but lacking tea!!!
Text: We spent an hour or so visiting the Museum and found it really interesting, BUT .... our Guide (who was very sweet) whisked us through the tea process and surprise surprise ended up in the shop!! We actually then went back through the museum and found some lovely facts, artefacts and memorabilia. What was lacking was a tea bush, real tea leaves, how they grow etc ... it's all based on what happens when they arrive at the processing plant. This could be so much better - instead we felt that the aim was to get you in to buy (second rate?) tea.

Title: Good visit but room for inprovement
Text: Myself and a friend visited on a Sunday morning-it was quiet with only a handful of other visitors. It closes on Sundays at 3pm. The guide was warm and friendly but we felt that the site could do a lot more to improve the experience by showing machinery actually working with tea leaves being sifted, dried and roasted etc in front of us. An interactive experience, if you will. At the end of the 15 minute tour over 3 floors(not suitable for people with a physical disability as a lot of stairs to climb) we went for our free cup of tea on the top floor. This was a huge disappointment. The cups and saucers had obviously just been hand washed from the previous visitor as they were still wet and not dried. The tea itself was not boiled. Note ;water for tea is meant to be boiled!

Title: Interesting to visit
Text:
Your visit to SriLanka cannot be complete without a visit to a tea plantation or tea factory.
However, I dont urge you to buy anything from these places because products are extremely overpriced!! Be sure that the guide and tour organizing company who take you there get a percentage of whatever you buy!!!!

Title: We stayed there for one night.
Text: Buffet dinner was very expensive it was for 75 US Dollars per person. Breakfast was very good and have several items.

Title: visited as part of tour of the island
Text: The tour takes place in an original old building with old machinery etc present. It is a little 'dry' as an experience but still didn't regret going as the guide was excellent and enhanced the experience. Very quiet at the tine of our visit - only 2 couples including us! Had tea afterwards as part of the tour - probably the best tea I had the whole holiday. All staff extremely warm and friendly. There are reasonably priced teas to buy if desired but absolutely no pressure.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: You get a shirt free guided tour through the factory. Afterwards, you can enjoy a complimentary tea and buy souvenirs.

Title: Interesting visit
Text:
We were looking forward to coming here to see the tea being picked and how it is sold to everywhere in the world from being picked to the different processes to making tea,we found it very interesting to watch the pickers and the process of the tea harvest.
Amazing scenery of the tea plantations and of the river valley from a view point.
Take a warm jumper or jacket as it does get quite cold as very high up.
And if you are lucky your visit will coincide with a slice of cake and a free tea tasting.
Well worth going.

Title: excellent intro to the history of tea in England
Text: before this visit, i knew absolutely nothing about tea.  I'm a coffee drinker.  Who know that pekoe is the size of the tea flakes after they are ground?  This place runs thru the entire process from picking thru sorting/packaging.  there is a tea tasting, a good video, and interesting old machines.

Title: Taking you back to another era
Text: In the old factory, with original machinery and structures and old photos the museum created a chance to imagine the past without the interference of modernity

Title: Learnt a lot.
Text: Vaguely knew about collecting tea but had little idea how much goes into selecting the different parts of the bush for the various grades of tea. The knowledgeable guides here explain it well and the tour is fascinating. You will be presented with a variety of teas to sample and then (of course) have an opportunity to purchase them. Not exactly bargain prices but worth investing and the views from the factory are outstanding.

Title: something different
Text:
the tea museum is a great place to spend an hour. the guides are really knowledgeable
and the artefacts and machinery are very interesting. great brew at the tea shop which is included in the price.

Title: Loved this place
Text: For anyone who's a connoisseur of small specialist museums, this is a must see. The process of making tea from raw green leaves is explained carefully as you're taken from one great victorian machine to the next. The process hasn't changed much in 160 years, but it will change the way you drink tea. Interesting to learn (not at the museum) that the women who pick the leaves earn 250 rupees a day (about £1.25) while the men work for half days only and make twice as much.

Title: worth a visit
Text: Very interesting and enjoyable visit. Good guide , excellent old machines with an interesting history plus various TEA orientated memorabilia

Title: Nice Museum
Text: This is a nice museum to see how tea was made earlier and now. good for a family visit once during your visit here.

Title: Interesting
Text: Quite interesting, but the tour is too short. You get the same information by visiting a tea plantation. The views from the top floor where you get a free cup of tea is great. The entrance fee is quite high (750 rupees per person).

Title: Good if you are not traveling to NE
Text: Nice place to see the tea making process if you are not visiting the nuwara eliya. however, tea prices are on higher side.

Title: Fascinating little museum of the tea industry in Sri Lanka
Text: Interesting old tea factory giving a brief overview of the tea industry in Sri Lanka. Beautiful views from top floor.

Title: Go and have a cuppa
Text: Enjoyed this tour and learned more about tea and the quality of it. Nice complimentary tea too,  very enjoyable couple of hours with fellow backpackers.

Title: Accessibility is a challenge
Text: Not very accessible. You should visit only if you have nothing much to do. Requires extensive travel on a hilly road to reach this destination which is only half good.

Title: Humm
Text: I was expecting something else. I was disappointed. The guide was just doing her job, talking quickly, almost not listening to my questions.

Title: Tea Museum
Text: Quite a long drive to get there - as it is at 8,000 feet  Views are stunning and climate is cool - with nice fires in the evening.   The conversion is well done and rooms are adequate - but the hotel lacks real charm.  Greater attention needed to cleanliness overall.  Extensive buffet - but food unfortunately tepid/cold; best to focus on food cooked to order.   Chef responded to complaint and provided hot food.  Staff pleasant and willing.

Title: A step back in time
Text:
Interesting visit to the tea museum. We purchased our tickets and were sent straight to the restaurant for a pot of tea. I am not a great tea drinker myself, but that may change after my visit.
After the tea we were briskly shown around the bottom floor of the museum.
I would have preferred seeing the museum first and then the tea - which was what everyone else seemed to do.
The views of the tea plantation were worth the visit.

Title: The best museum in Kandy
Text: Without any doubts this museum is the best in town. You can understand a lot about the most British drink, tea. A guide will bring you through the old factory. The building is very old and interesting. It's possible to visit some plantation outside

Title: Overpriced
Text: The museum now charges 750p (not 500) for entry. You get 15mins tour and a complimentary cup of tea. All the machines are not operational. A few more exhibits related to tea making (e.g.  some of the belongings of the founders of the tea business on the island) and some info panels. The toilets there are disgusting. I'd recommend visiting Pedro Tea Factory in Nuwara Elya instead (which is for 200rp and much nicer, also not operating during visiting hours, but there is at least some actual tea there) or other tea factories where you can actually see the process of making tea.

Title: Interesting historically
Text:
Excellent tour guide explanation of the old, mostly English machinery used in the tea process. Husband loved it as he knew many of the manufactuners.  
Perhaps just as good to see the machines here, still mostly the same used in working factories now, rather than go to a working one.
Enjoyable and not thronged with people like the "major factories". Lots of historical info and lovely old photos displayed, oh yes - and you get a cup of tea too!

Title: interesting and educational trip
Text: if you are in kandy, this is worth visiting. its not a tea factory so dont expect to see real time tea production. this is all about tea and its history in sri lanka. they do sell tea there and we never found it being sold any where else. good to try

Title: Well worth the effort
Text: An amazing trip to the beginnings and later history of tea growing amd making in Sri Lanka. The facilitie are a little sparse and the road access road from the main road is in extremely poor condition. However, with a guided toor and free cuppa at the end, it is a very interesting and worthwhile trip.

Title: Interesting historical tea museum
Text: Set up in the hills outside Kandy, this tea museum is well worth a visit. Not big on tea tasting, this gives more of a historical view and a greater understanding of the processes involved in tea making and production.

Title: Interesting glimpse of the tea industry
Text: Well maintained old factory site with original equipment in place to provide an interesting insight into the development of the tea industry in Sri Lanka. Provides some understandings about the tea we buy, and provides a tasting, and the  opportunity to buy some souvenir teas on site. The guide had a good understanding of the site, and the tour was well organised. There is a small charge for the tour.

Title: Very nice visit
Text: The Ceylon Tea Museum is a very authentic museum to understand how tea is made and distinguish between the different kinds of tea. The tour was ok. The shops are a good place to buy some tea as a souvenir as they offer a great selection for descent prices.

Title: Good
Text: I liked this place because you can get some knowledge about machines and techniques which were used for producing tea. The guide was very nice, but she was rather in a hurry. We enjoyed the cups of tea we got at the top of the museum and bought some packets of tea in the shops. There were several different shopes in the middle floor so you can compare the prices and kinds of tea before you choose some which is good.

Title: Map location in Lonely Planet is wrong
Text:
We are not the only ones to discover that the location of this museum is wrong in the Lonely Planet guide 13th ed, page 159. There Ceylon Tea Museum is marked with #1 close to Sarasav Uvana railway station. That is wrong, see google maps It is close to Hantana D2-D3 on the map. If you are wrong a and have ended up in Peradeniya a tuktuk driver will  bring you to the real spot for 1000 lkr. 
Another issue is that this museum is close to Ceylon Tea Estates which have received a better rating in Tripadvisor , has a different address yet Google maps places them close together. 
The tour through the museum is Okish, but rather I would have seen the real works instead of old machines.

Title: Great tea house with good explanation!
Text:
Very detailed overview of tea making process. 
Each step is clearly explained and the staff is eager to share their knowledge and show the machines and how they work.

Title: Interesting with Great Views
Text:
We arrived after a hairy ride up on a tuk tuk and were immediately given a very knowledgeable tour guide with amazing English skills. She showed us around and explained the tea making process. Whilst it was a little rushed, she answered our questions and we had time at the end to go back and revisit the things we didn't have time to peruse the first time around. 

On the top floor there's a room where they serve you a cup of tea (included in the price) and you can look out over the mountains. It really is incredible and, even if you're not that interested in tea, it makes a nice jaunt outside of the centre of Kandy. 

There is a floor dedicated to the selling of tea - you can wander around or miss it entirely. There's no hard sell.

Title: informative
Text:
Elegantly clad in saris, the ladies at the museum run the show....
Entrance fee keeps increasing, but there is only that much to the factory and the tea. Lots of info about machinery as well as documents and valuable items belonging to the long gone past. The many stairs to walk up during tour are worth climbing, as on the top floor you are rewarded with a free cup of fresh Ceylon tea and an audio-visual presentation about - tea. And then there are tea boutiques set up on the floor just below top floor. Mesmerizing!   But one thing to remember: the museum closes at 4 pm!

Title: was not really impressed
Text: They will charge you a ticket which is expensive. you can enjoy the same experience actually even better with real tea leaves at Glenloch for free on your way back from elephant bath towards Colombo. the tea shops are interesting in the museum but Glenloch also have good collection of tea with free tasting of different tea.

Title: Back in time with tea.
Text: One of the well organized informative mesuem about origin story of Sri Lanka tea (Ceylon tea). The staff was friendly and we'll educated to provide a great history lesson from James Taylor to tea brewing.

Title: If you like tea and history, this place is ace!
Text: What a peaceful, welcome respite from being treated like a walking ATM in Sri Lanka! The staff here are so lovely and welcoming and it's set in a beautiful location about a 20 minute tuk tuk ride from Kandy's centre. The tour was very informative and interesting and the guide equally so. The museum holds some impressive tea history, including the first tea drier in Sri Lanka. The complimentary pot of tea is lovely (we could have done with some milk though). The view from the top of the museum is also stunning and there's some nice tea shops located at the top also, if you're a tea enthusiast.

Title: Lovely museum.. a bit out of the way, but worth the visit.
Text: This museum was very nice, but if you have the opportunity to visit an actual tea processing facility first, I recommend that! Friends and I had visited a tea plantation the day before and had received an excellent tour of the facility while people were working so we had a strong understanding of the machines in use.

Title: Interesting site. Not happy with the staff.
Text: Very interesting site with valuable pieces of equipment initially used in the production of tea. Pity that the staff are not very enthusiastic in their tour guiding and very much in a hurry to finish their job. Not a good sight to also see staff in the office sleeping at their desk in full view of guests. Those in charge need to look at a better promotion of the Musuem.

Title: Tea Museum with a beautiful background.
Text:
Everything to know about a tea factory is here. You will wonder to see a machine from Culcutta, India here.
Enjoy a tea from here. Available different flavors of tea.

Title: Immense
Text: I'm not a tea lover however I had to visit this place...Although again extremely humid and the workers in the factory how do they survive and still smile like all the Sri Lankan people....If you don't go you'll miss out......

Title: Tea history - up in the hills
Text: Up in the hills is the tea museum- real interesting place capturing the history of  tea evolution from early  1800s till now. Bought some wonderful tasting refined tea from here- must visit for tea lovers

Title: A not to be missed for tea lovers
Text: The is a guided tour of the facilty for Rs 650 per person and it gives you an idea when the first tea was planted by James Taylor and the museum has all the machinery used during the times and the fuide wzplains you the whole process..There is a museum and shops selling teas at reasonable prices on the 2nd and 3rd floor and you get a pot of hot tea on the 4th floor which is included in the entrance ticket. One can see the tea plantations around and the scenic view of Kandy along the way..I have a better perspective of my favorite drink after the visit..

Title: Average
Text: I feel like there wasn't much to the tour we did and since its not a working factory you don't get to see the machines work. The tour lasts around 15 minutes and the tea tasting takes up most of the time. Specially if it's a hot day. You're free to walk along the tea plantations but there isn't really much to see. Perhaps the tea factories down south offer something more to see!

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Learn about the history of tea production in Sri Lanka. Entrance fee is reasonable and comes with a pot of tea in the restaurant. However, some of the tea sold in the shops can also be found at supermarkets for a better price. I paid 215 for a packet of tea and found the exact same thing in a supermarket going for 150.

Title: relaxed, informative, no hard sell, very good morning visit
Text:
It's a short ride out of town on a tuc-tuc for R400. As you get near to the museum there are actual tea bushes growing in the fields although they are not processed at the factory as its just a museum. Its R650 for an adult R300 for U18. You get a guided tour when you arrive as they have a team of ladies doing the tours. Ours was knowledgeable and able to articulate the finer detail of some of the exhibits and processes.

The machinery on the first floor which states of the tour is a bit 'dry' but it gets better. After your been shown round 20 mins ish you are left of the top floor to have a free cup served  and at one side there was a demo / tasking of six different types.

There are about six or so mini shops selling different types and brands of Sri Lankan tea and some other souvenirs but there was no pressure whatsoever. The prices appeared very of reasonable.

There was also a scrolling video in English showing a factory at work the planting, weeding, pruning and gardening to keep a plantation healthy and producing.

Finally there was quite a bit on James Taylor as the father of tea in Sri Lanka how he started commercial production 2 years before the coffee blight decimated coffee production on the island some of his relationship with Sir Thomas Lipton and other historical stuff.

Definitely worth a visit and much much much better than the other tea factory tour we were encouraged to go on.

Title: Who doesnt love the smell and old machinery in a tea museum?
Text: Old machinery, the smell of tea, great for all ages. This is the one thing that you must do in Sri Lanka. Visit the museum and then visit a factory. The tea is just amazing.

Title: Definitely go and have a cup of tea
Text: I have no idea why this place has indifferent reviews. It is excellent, great informative guides, wonderful building and views back to Kandy and the white Buddha. Its only minutes up the hill from Kandy and tells the story of Tea in Ceylon really well. Go further up the hill for more tea plantations and views too.

Title: love the history
Text: It was a lovely experience to get the knowledge of the inception of tea. They could actually improve the standards to make the tour more worthwhile. It was a very educational experience.

Title: Must Visit Place
Text: This place is bit away from main down town but worth visiting. They have guide to show entire process of making tea from raw leaves to finish form what we get in the market. Tickets are for adults with 400 SR / person and child below 8 to 10 are free and they don't charge upon request. Tea tasting is included in the tickets and one can by pure Ceylon tea from this place. This places closes at 4 PM in the evening, so make it sure to reach early at-least 1 hr. before closing time.

Title: Go and take a look you will not be disappointed
Text:
Wow this place is brilliant - heaped in history you simply must go and visit.

You will find out everything there is to know about tea - remember it used to be called Ceylon!!!

Title: TEA EXPERIENCE
Text: Excellent selection of teas that tea lovers would enjoy anytime, and would never forget! Recommended for every visitor to Sri Lanka

Title: Nice museum shame there's no plantation to see
Text:
The museum is very nice, lots of old machinery and a model to show what the factory would have looked like when operating. The free tour guide was very good and spoke very good English.  The free Cup of tea was good too and there was a good video explaining about the whole process from growing tea to selling.  
The only let down is there is no tea plantation to visit.
We took a tuk tuk there for 400SR, but we got the bus back from the main road which cost 15Sr each, the bus comes just before the hour (between quarter to and o'clock) for heading back to Kandy. I think it's around 700SR for a round trip in a tuk tuk.

Title: short and boring
Text:
Trip starts with a guide who leads you trough the 1sth floor. The rest 4 floors you visit by yourself .
The most interesting is the movie that is shown when you drink the tea. 
Recomendation- ask the Tuktuk driver to wait for you, because its rather empty place with no communication

Title: Mixed feelings, definitely worth considering if you're interested in tea but could be improved.
Text:
Went here as a couple.

Location 4/5
Up on the hill side, a bit out of the way.

Atmosphere 4/5
Very quiet the day we visited. Building itself is immaculate and historic.

Overall 4/5
Mixed feelings, definitely worth considering if you're interested in tea but could be improved.

Title: Only if you are interested in tea
Text: It was nothing special only the different variety of teas that are offered for sale is a good deal, but the tour was ok.

Title: Tea Museum
Text:
You want to know how tea is made, well this is the place to be!!
One of the absolutely must visit places in Kandy!  
Staff is very helpful

Title: Do not miss it if you like drinking tea.
Text: I loved the whole experience of visiting old factory but not liked the rushed tour provided by the museum.The tea sold upstairs definetly nice quality and reasonable compare to other  places on your drives.

Title: Good tea!
Text: Our driver took us to this factory, which we found very interesting.  A good insight into the history and the making of tea.  Lots of informations and a very good shop at the top of the building.  Fair amount of steps looking at the machinery and the processes of making and choosing the different types of tea. Very interesting.

Title: INSPIRING
Text: A small insight into how our humble cuppa comes to life...from picking to drinking.   Makes you appreciate your breakfast cup of tea a little more.

Title: An interesting step back in time
Text: An interesting visit being shown the old equipment used in the factory and an explanation of how all the various processes of tea making occur.  There are a few floors with lots of posters to read providing information from the initial tea plantations to modern research and the benefits of tea. If you are not going to a working tea plantation this gives the perfect opportunity to gain an understanding of the process. Your ticket also entitles you to a free cuppa at the end of your visit!!

Title: An interesting morning visit, high up above Kandy
Text: This was listed in my Lonely Planet guide and my experienced driver and guide had not visited. We had a very knowledgeable lady who showed us around and explained all the machinery. This was  a good preview before seeing the actual machines working at Mackwoods Tea factory. I enjoyed all the little historical facts and machines made in Lincolnshire etc . There were some great photos of the Scottish man who first planted Tea in Ceylon( as it was then). One floor has lots of teapots and other tea making equipment. There are some very clear story boards which tell you the history of Tea growing and how Sri Lanka came to be such an important tea growing area. The museum is a quiet place , with a nice pot of tea at the end and a chance to buy tea and mugs etc at not extortionate prices and from pleasant staff who are not pushy. Clean loos too ! What more can you want ?

Title: if you are highly intersted in tea
Text: The museum is for people who have time, and are highly interested in the tea scene in sri-lanka. a pleasant place. not more

Title: Intersting
Text: Some lovely old relics, made to last machines from the late 1800's and some laughingly dated 60s and 7s machines. The t a is very competitively priced and you get a free pot

Title: opening hours are not as advertized
Text: Great advice comes from our group's misery : find a way to call and confirm the day and time of your visit. Otherwise you will face a friendly guard telling you he is sorry but it's  closed now.

Title: nice museum
Text: We preferred visiting the museum rather than the tea plantation we visited. The building is interesting, you understand the different stages of tea making and see lots of historic machinery.

Title: The best tea museum in Sri Lanka. A must if visiting Kandy
Text: A total overview of the tea industry in Sri Lanka.    Machinery, processes, culture, the people who brought tea to Sri Lanka.    No need to travel further in a bus for hours to see the processing of tea and the growing of the bushes in the fields.. Everything is here and know one op seems to visit. While we were there only 4 other couples.  Even had a film show and a cup of tea.  Should be the number one attraction in Kandy.

Title: Excellent
Text:
Brilliant displays, knowledgeable local guide, who was charm personified.

Not busy, which was good for us, not necessarily for the museum

Title: Pop in for a cup.
Text: Excellent tour of the building. Much original machinery and expert guides. Very interesting history with many delightful photographs. Tea shop was well stocked, but slightly more expensive than in town. Tasting was an excellent experience. Recommended.

Title: Learned a Lot
Text: I love tea and so going to a museum about it seemed like it was a great idea, which it was.  I never knew the process for making tea and now I do.  My guide was very nice as was the structure and of course you get a free cup of tea at the end.  Plus there are 6-7 tea vendors on one of the floors selling different varieties of tea.

Title: Money worth place
Text: If you travel to Kandy. do not forget to visit this place.  Guides at museum. help me and my foreign friends very much.  we hand nice tea.

Title: Not worth the price
Text: 4 KM out of town on a windy road you come to Tea museum, which is only an old tea factory, closed for 50 yrs. You see their old machinery & enjoy a good pot of tea, but the price of Tuktuk & entry free is not worth what you get.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
A little bit of haggling wih a tuk tuk driver to get there as they have to wait for the return (1000 rupees). A fair trip up the hill which would not havd been good for kids but easy for any walkers out there.
500 rupees per person  included a guide who explained the basic facts and a cup of tea at the end. 
A little dry but as an avid tea drinker who knew nothing it was informative and explained a lot about the history and developmdnt of tea in Sri Lanka as a whole.

Title: Quite interesting but only if you are passing.
Text: Tour consisted of showing lots of ancient machinery which wasn't working. Surely even on workdays they don't use this? Quite interesting though, with a free cup of tea, and as it only takes about 15 minutes you don't lose much going there and might enjoy it.

Title: Nice Place
Text: Tea Museum was located on the hill near tea plantations. The building was nice, museum consists of four floors of tea manufacturing machinery, information about the process of making tea, and the history of tea making in Sri Lanka..a worth visit place,

Title: NOT QUITE WHAT WE EXPECTED
Text: Worth a visit but we were expecting to see the plantation, pickers etc.  This felt like a tourist location to earn money.  If you have never been then of course go, drink and buy the tea.

Title: Very good staff and a lot of tea facts :)
Text: Got to see this place and enjoy a hot cuppa ! Blooming tea to white tea to green tea to malsala one. they have it all and you will get to know how it is made.. good visit. Excellent staff.

Title: Ceylon Tea at its best
Text:
An interesting insight into how tea is grown and processed.  It is back breaking work picking the tea on the mountainsides, and most of it is done by Tamil women imported from India.

Bought some prime grade Ceylon tea to give as presents on my return home.

Title: Stubborn staff refuses our visit
Text: A friend and I went to the museum during opening hours but they had decided to close the place without giving a reason. The whole staff seemed to be inside but refused to open. We tried to talk to the boss but he was impolite and sent us away.  We had hesitated to go because the place gets mixed reviews in guidebooks. We wasted our time and money going there. I would recommend you don't waste yours.

Title: The Blue Plantation
Text: The tea plantations are set in the north of Kandy in the mountain area. We travelled from Mahaweli Reach Hotel, Kandy,  to the mountain about 60km away in a tut tut which took about 2-3 hours. ....Beware to warm warm clothes as cooler in this area and rainy. The scenary was awesome Enroute especially the waterfalls. The weather was changeable, sunny at bottom, mountain mist in middle, then rain at top.mThe Blue Plantation is free admittance and a guide takes you around the working factory on a tour, where you come out very educated on the cup of tea you drink. There is a shop to buy the fresh tea, a cafe and restaurant.

Title: The heritage of tea
Text: This is a beautiful building, beautifully kept in a magnificent setting. The tour of the factory is interesting and informative with commentary given by knowledgeable guides. Considering the resources available they have done a good job. Room for improvement but they will get there. For now, enjoy the old world charm and peace of the place.

Title: Original machinery still in use.
Text: This is a small tea plantation with all the original machinery still in use. We saw where the tea is picked, dried and cut, also where it is packed in sacks for export.  We were able to buy some tea to bring home.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Worth a trip for a few hours, interesting history of tea in Ceylon. A guide shows you around & gives a general overview of systems involved in processing tea in the early days and the early founders of the area. Free cuppa at the end. Beautiful old building

Title: A must for vintage machinery enthusiasts
Text: If you are really interested in the tea business or an aficionado of beautifully restored vintage British agricultural machinery, this museum is well worth the effort. We found it to be a worthwhile complement to a visit to a working tea estate up in the mountains. It is very much a static museum, with no processing going on, but our lady guide was charming and informative. Unfortunately, a power cut meant that we didn't get our cup of tea after the visit, but we were glad we went.

Title: History Lesson on Tea Making
Text:
A short drive out of Kandy the museum is well worth a visit. When we were there a guide accompanied us around the exhibitions telling us about the history of the tea industry in Sri Lanka and provided information on the manufacturing process
Included in the admission price is a cup of tea

Title: Interesting, with lots of potential
Text:
First, I should identify myself as a museum professional. As such, I couldn't help but see the Ceylon Tea Museum as a facility that could so easily be made excellent. As it is, it's pretty good and a pleasant and enlightening trip from Kandy. 
Their tour guides are wonderful and enthusiastic, but the tour is strangely out of order. The tea bushes come after seeing the machinery. The miniature factory would have worked better at the beginning or end where it could be used to sum up the tea process. The tea service on the top floor was pleasant, but if you are there with a school group, as we were, you could be waiting forty minutes for a cup - with only an old and overly laudatory video for company. 
It must be hard to gain buy-in from the museum backers, but I feel like a more critical look into the history of the plantation tamils or even a more in-depth discussion of the work they do would have improved the experience.

Title: A lot to read and discover
Text: This museum is well done and is in an old tea factory. Downstairs we could see machines and a nice lady explained us how to produce black tea. Upstairs you can read a lot about the history, it is very interesting. Take time to visit and enjoy.

Title: Nice visit
Text: The guide took her job with more speed than depth but when we started asking questions she answered thoroughly and probably realized we were interested. There are lots of machines and stuff to see. The shops were very different with a couple of them selling mostly gift packs. We found a very good one and the prices were really low.
