We have more than 2 kgs in our luggade. The tea served at the end of the visit was really good and there was a film about tea. Enjoyed it!

Title: Nothing to get excited about
Text: Presented in an ex tea factory this tells the story of tea production after picking the leaf. Old machinery can be seen and a range of artefacts from the early period of tea production under British control. Quite interesting but not exciting. There is a range of small units selling tea on the upper floor and a small tea bar on the top floor.

Title: Good visit
Text: Good experience to see how the tea is processed. Good explanations and a not too long visit. Can arrive there by tuk-tuk.

Title: Museum worth a visit
Text: Everything you need to know for the tea in Sri Lanka. You can discover the production of tea with all the machines, archives, old photos and few different shops where you can buy locally produced tea. The guide tour is included in the entrance fee of 700 rupees and it's very useful for the tea production area.

Title: The land of good Tea..
Text: Ceylon the old charming name of the now called "Sri Lanka" is maintained by the good old "Ceylon Tea Museum".The charming Kandy adds dynamism to the Museum, once a tea factory and later redone as a Tea Museum could be one of a kind in the world and allows Tea lovers to experience and walk through their Tea feel..don't miss if you are around in Kandy or Nuwereliyya....

Title: Surprisingly interesting
Text: You'll never drink a cup of tea the same way again! It's incredible how many stages it goes through. Happy tour guides, lovely views (of course... it's Sri Lanka after all) and a nice cup of the local brew of your choice. I didn't like the sign by management asking not to tip the staff... Don't tell me what to do and also... why? Anyway, it was altogether lovely and I tipped anyway.

Title: Overpriced
Text: This place is crazily overpriced. Do not buy anything from here. They lure the customers. It is not worth it.

Title: Good cheap tea on sale
Text: The factory is quite interesting and informative. They offer a nice fresh tea after the show around of the factory. Then there are around 7-8 tea shops on the 1st floor. At first we were not going to buy any tea powder but after seeing the rates we ended up buying 5 boxes!

Title: WOW feeling
Text:
Our driver drove us at the Ceylon Tea Museum on our way to Nuwara Ellaye.
It was a nice experience seeing how tea leaves gets converted into tea. The company member had shown n explained us the whole process of tea making n how to differentiate between good n average quality, export products, type of tea. 
Though the staff doesn't forces you to buy there tea. If you like it then you can buy that or else you can go back after viewing the process..
I bought different types  of tea..

Title: It's okay
Text:
It's okay. Adequate but for what you pay its pretty boring, the tours are quite rushed. 
The equipment on show is interesting, yet this tour compares badly in content and detail to those available in Taiwan for example.
Around 800r for Tuk-tuk return.
The tea served on the top floor and video shown a highlight.

Title: interesting and informative
Text: This is another free of cost tourist attraction which I found very interesting! The staff takes you through all the stages of tea manufacturing starting with the freshly plucked green leaves! Very informative and they wrap up the session with a free cuppa of freshly brewed Sri Lankan tea!

Title: Long journey, short tour
Text:
The best thing was the journey up to the museum.
The tour was fine, but we didn't know the basics about Tea growing/making and she didn't explain any of it to us, and therefore we struggled to understand what she did tell us (3 Doctors, we aren't stupid!)
I subsequently went to two different working tea factories and they were miles better, the tour at the others was really informative and seeing the machines working gave a much better idea of what it was all about. 
At Mackwoods they also take you to a tea bush and explain there which helps.

I wouldn't go, go to a working tea factory, there are so many choice of places to explore the tea industry, no need to go to  a sub-optimal one.

Tour is about 5-10 mins and there are then 3 floors to look around and on the top floor is a cafe for you to have a complimentary taste of tea. 
3rd floor is shops but they were mostly closed as we went out of season.

Title: Fascinating insight into Tea
Text: You need to take transport upto the Tea Museum which sits high up just outside Kandy. The original building is still standing and is quite a few stories high. Each level leads you through some of the history of tea in Sri Lanka and we were fascinated to find out it started with a young 17 year old Englishman sent out to run a coffee plantation. On the top level you can drink some tea and compare the different types. informative and fun.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Very interesting to see the museum and how tea is made and how the different kinds of teas are produced. Well worth a visit.

Title: Very lazy staff; unfortunately a tourist destination
Text:
I have been to tea museum twice, once recently and the staffs were useless. They were doing nothing other than chatting each other. I have been to Loolkondura, the first commercial tea plantation and the James Taylors museum also before. Now, everything has been transferred to this location.  Why? I was told it was convenient but no use of having any of the displays without a proper guide.
It seems everyone in the museum assumes that the people who are coming to this place are tea experts. There is no one to explain the tea processing methodology or how to categories tea as BOP, BOPF etc..
I strongly feel that this museum should be used to educate visitors and promote tea by letting people know almost everything about tea. Frankly, its a shame to say, this is a useless place unless the management take a U turn soon.

Title: Decent insights into tea production
Text:
Showcasing a lot of machines used for tea production and some background information, the museum does give a decent insight "into tea".
As the machines are not in use and the explaining signs could be more informative, it sometimes was a little difficult to imagine the process thoroughly.

The museum closed rather before the official time of 4:30 pm and so I missed the last floor of the museum as well as the sometimes cited cup of tea. There are 4 floors to the museum and the basic overview of tea production on the upper floor is better than the cut off newspaper clippings on the ground floor.

I also visited "Pedro Tea Estate", an active tea factory in Nuwara Eliya, afterwards and feel like that was visit over there was giving me similar, yet a little more lively insights. I would maybe skip this Tea museum when visiting a factory but otherwise this gives a nice enough insight.

Title: long way
Text: a long way up the hil to this tea meuseum. if you are hoping to go to nuwaraeliya or where the tea plantations are, this would seem unimpressive. a tourist trap.

Title: Learn things about tea you didn't know before
Text: The guided tour gives you a good understanding of how tea is produced after plucking the light green leaves. After the tour in the factory you have the opportunity to have some fresh tea. We enjoyed the tour a lot.

Title: great museum
Text: this museum is good if you also get to see an old fashioned factory/ plantation. it pulls all of the information together. its still worth visiting if you dont go to both. good selection of machinery and articles. there is not too much to overwhelm you or too little that its not worth going to. 150 rps tuk tuk they may wait if you agree a price, we walked back down. 400rps entrance.

Title: ANY interest in Sri Lanka's tea culture and history? Go there!
Text:
If you don't like tea this is still a good place to be... If you like tea then this place is awesome!

This old tea factory 4km up from Kandy in the hillside now serves as a tea museum with detailed insight as well as quite some real exhibits from the days of good ol' tea production (which is in many ways the same still as today anyway;-)

Seeing this place was, for us, only part of some exploration on Sri Lanka's past, it's tea production and all about tea in general, beginner's level, that is... (The other part being at an operational tea estate - in our case Pedro in Nuwara Eliya) What you get to see in the museum will set you right to learn a good deal on the subject and how it had an impact on Sri Lanka on many levels.

However, it should be mentioned that the manner in which all is explained and depicted is also a bit of the old-fashioned way. This said, don't expect too much from the museum as someone who has very little interest in the topic.

Title: Fab Education
Text: our driver took us here and we were well impressed with the guides telling/showing how our tea we drink is processed from field to tea bag well worth a visit

Title: Simple yet interesting.
Text: We took a tuk tuk to the museum which is a great drive up into the tea plantations. The museum is very basic and has a very relaxed atmosphere. A guide shows you around the museum and explains a little about the processes and equipment. You can read about the history of the tea makers and enjoy a cup of tea at the end. There are a couple of little stall type tea shops also, we bought some local teas to take home with us. A very relaxing couple of hours.

Title: educational
Text: Learning about the Scot Lipton and how hard pickers have to work so hard for our cuppa were eyeopeners

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: We took a tuktuk to the Tea Museum in the hills outside Kandy in January.  The museum is based on several floors and shows all the machines which have been used in the processing of tea.  You have a chance to try the teas and can also purchase them but they are not at all pushy.  Very good short visit and recommended stop

Title: Interesting
Text:
The museum is of course something to visite when in Kandy. But do not have too high expectations; it is rather basic.
There is a guide presenting if you want to with good knowledge, but rather uninspiring. Surprisingly our guide did not know how green tea is processed.
A the end you get the opportunity to taste some tea, this is also very basic and no guidance on what tea to try.
This could be so much more, but any way worth visiting.

Title: Dont miss it
Text: Very informative about the history of tea in Sri Lanka, and you also get a nice cuppa on the top floor cafe!Had a lovely guide who gave a very knowledgable explanation of all the machinery. As we are involved in the tea business it was great to learn about the tea history of Sri Lanka.

Title: tea paradise
Text: beautiful mackwood tea factory, over 170 years old. very friendly staff and beautiful scenic place. I enjoyed meditating by the river beside the factory

Title: They could have made it so much better
Text:
its a very ordinary place which you can give a miss
You only wonder at the potential this thing holds...
they show you the process of making tea and even have access to tea plantation to get pics taken. Then there is a 10 minute lecture from someone who would remind you of your grumpy professor. He said all the right stuff which was worth hearing and to his defense.. he has to put up with unruly and rude visitors every day :)

Title: Watching how tea is made
Text:
While we were visiting friends in Sri Lanka , the pereras  ,we went on a very nice tour in 
a lovely old tea factory, coupled with a complimentary cup of tea. Can also buy tea from the 3 shops in the building.
We visited this factory as part of a tour with slimline tours , amount some other great places , we watched how they draw sap from the trees to make medicines , other places was were they made cream for all different kinds of things , , we went a pine apple plant , were we could taste fresh pine apples straight from the trees , amazing , Sri Lanka is an amazing place love the tea factory very interesting to watch ,

Title: good
Text: Good, nice staff. lots of information. shame we ran out of time to do a long tour. Tuk tuk man brought us and stayed with us until we had to go back. quite helpful.

Title: Fascinating
Text: Definitely worth a visit, beautifully put together, very interesting and lovely cuppa afterwards. There is a delightful miniature tea factory model that the staff will activate for visitors

Title: Charming factory
Text: Very nice tour in a lovely old tea factory, coupled with a complimentary cup of tea. Can also buy tea from the 3 shops in the building.

Title: Interesting, no more Tea Bags
Text: This was really interesting and the tea taste at the end was good, can't believe there are so many different types and the processes they go through. Don't have tea bags as it's just the dust would you believe.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The journey there was lovely and great view from the top.  Interesting old machinery and information about tea and planters in an old tea factory. A guide will show you around but we decided to look round the 5 floors ourselves with a free cup of tea on the 5th floor.

Title: Well Organized
Text: The Tea Museum was very interesting, you can look at in a short time is really interesting! At closing you could look at the different varieties as they were made.

Title: For those genuinely interested in tea
Text:
So this museum is a very quiet place but well maintained and holds all the traditional machinery used to manufacture tea leaves. Even machines dating back to colonial times. You even get a chance to sample different types of tea.

So if you're really interested then go otherwise this place might come across as quiet and boring.

Title: Under appreciated - well worth
Text:
We spend a few enjoyable hours here. It is around 4km fro the city centre of Kandy. The ride to the museum is already quite nice as it takes you away from the hustle and bustle of Kandy. The last few 100s of meters you actually pass some tea plantations already to get you in the mood.

We did call in advance to make sure they were up and running on a Saturday. Upon arrival it looked like we were the only guests though more people followed. Still not busy anyway. Reading some of the other reviews we sort of expected information not to be readily and easily available. 

Guides are available, though we did not bother using one nor checking prices. There is a fair bit of information available in the museum but you do need to make the effort to read it. Lots of old stuff including equipment but also newspaper clippings that describe what went on in the old days. Some of it supported by extra boards with information.

Nice write ups on how Taylor and Lipton started and expanded their business. 

The top floor has a sort of summary display that explain the benefits of tea, what happened in the industry as well as the process. It would have made sense to put that first and then go into the details of machines and the process.

There is one floor with some shops that sell tea. Interestingly no real hard sales going on there. We went to the Tea Board shop to get some teas as gifts. Good variation and decent prices.

Although not all is super clear laid out for one, our visit was enjoyable and we did learn a fair bit about tea and the industry development so worth the visit.

We paid just over 600rps entrance fee at 9 august 2014.

Title: Lots of history but quiet
Text:
We visited in July, which isn't really tourist season as it's pretty hot. The museum was very quiet but we learnt a lot about the 2 main tea companies we know, Lipton's and Taylor's. You need to be able to walk up the stairs to the 5 floors of the museum, showing you how a factory would've worked. 
It was very interesting but would've been better if everything was open (the cafe was closed as off season) so we could try the tea.

Title: The best
Text: I cant believe we had this place to ourselves, The tea shops are quite cheap and the free tour guide makes this place. Not on the beaten track but its worth the small detour

Title: Nice insight into tea production
Text: Learned a lot about early tea production and saw excellent machinery. Tour guides available if needed.

Title: Must visit museum in Kandy-Revisit the rich tea heritage
Text:
The Ceylon Tea museum was incorporated on 9th January 1998 under Section 21 of the Companies act no 17 of 1982 and declared open to the public on 1st December, 2001. It is housed in the 1925 established Hanthana tea factory, 4kms from Kandy and at a height of 2499 feet. The museum consists of four floors. The ground floor has the Engine room and Rolling room where old machinery connected with the tea industry are displayed. The first floor has Drier room and furnace room and related machinery displayed. The second floor has sifting room and related equipments. The James Taylor museum and the archive room is also located on this floor. The third floor is allocated to Tea sales outlets where one can buy the finest selection of Ceylon Tea.

The entire fourth floor area is a restaurant where visitors are served complimentary tea. They can also take part in Tea tasting session. A panoramic view of the Kandy town surrounded by beautiful Hunnasgiriya Knuckles range and the Matale range of hills can be viewed through a telescope here. This floor also has the original cat walk platform which was used by the superintendent and the tea maker of the tea factory for monthly inspection of the roof and removal of any tea fluff.

Title: Very Interesting
Text:
Spent about an hour at The Mackwoods Plantation and it brought back school day memories of learning about where tea comes from!
Very interesting to go into the factory where the smell of tea was quite overpowering-glad I don't have to work there!
Most of the pickets are still women and still get paid according to how much they pick
Worth a vist

Title: A shame is not well run
Text:
A leaflet explaining each numbered machinery as we went through would be good.  There is very little information on the making of tea.
I would pass on this one until such time as this place is set up properly for tourists

Title: Nice
Text: Take a tuktuk up the hill to this converted tea factory for soem insights in the Sri Lankan tea culture, nice views and a good cuppa.

Title: must see
Text: We were taken on a tour of the tea museum..Showed how the different teas were sorted and graded.  Afterwards we were given different tea to sample. Now we know exactly what to look for when we buy our teas in the shops.

Title: Closed
Text: It was Monday, it was closed, and tuk tuk driver knew 2 days before we wanted to go there, but didn't tell us. Very disappointed.

Title: A History of Tea
Text: To get there takes a long drive with congested roads on the way up.We hopped on a 20-year old taxi which was driven by a very friendly driver who said that he used to be the head of the Taxi Drivers Association.Spent our time at the museum in the cool morning.The tour guide was good and also friendly.Even the people in the museum tea shop were helpful in explaining and answering all our questions regarding tea. They weren't just about selling off their products.Overall,it is a place worth a visit when you're in Kandy.

Title: Great value for money
Text:
One of the few museums in Sri Lanka where you can view displays at your own leisure without some obnoxious guide rushing you through the museum. At the end a well deserved cup of tea awaits you. 
Learn hear about the history of tea in Sri Lanka. If the scale model of the museum is switched off, ask someone to switch it on. Truly amazing!

Title: Wunderful building, interesting old machinery
Text:
worth visiting, only some minutes with the tuctuc from Kandy city center
atmospheric building, the ancient machinery is visible and in good state, additional model of whole factory
individual guide and included cup of tea in the highest floor

Title: Interesting Museum
Text: The Tea Museum is located on the hill near tea plantations. The building is simple but well maintained. because I had an early start for my Kandy City Tour from Hanthana Hills, iIt was still closed when I visited so really did not have the chance to see what was on display.

Title: Interesting visit
Text: though not an active plantation, the museum is a good place to understand the history of Ceylan tea without focusing on one type of producers only - as is the case in classic tea plantations tours promoting their own products. I had a guide introducing me to the history of tea plantations, providing a bit of background on technical history of the tea industry. You can see original machines used in the early 1880s until more recent periods which is quite interesting. You can see also other antiques and objects belonging to the period.The other floor show exhibits related to tea production and history themselves. 3rd floor holds small shops with no attractive sets of products - last floor is a large tea room where you are offered a cup of tea and where you can enjoy a nice view.

Title: The secret of tea......
Text: We had a tea musuem on our list of places we wanted to visit but we werent sure we would have chance to visit one.  This was on the way from Pinnawela to Kandy.  We were given a tour (no fee) of how the leaves become tea which was really interesting.  We were also shown different types of tea inc. BFPM which is English Breakfast Tea type and BFP which we then tried and you drink without milk.  It tasted lovely and very refreshing.  We bought a pot of leaves for 1100 (£5.69).

Title: Informative
Text: Had a lovely guide who gave a very knowledgable explanation of all the machinery. As we are involved in the tea business it was great to learn about the tea history of Sri Lanka

Title: Tea haven!
Text: It was very quiet when we visited - but the guide was friendly and knowledgable and we learnt lots about the process of making tea. She didn't make the tour too long or too detailed - and we got a free cup of tea at the end upstairs! Well worth the Tuk Tuk ride. Its about 10 minutes from the centre of Kandy.

Title: Interesting
Text: Interesting to see all the equipment as it would have been back a few years ago. It can be an expensive tuk tuk ride out there but we inadvertently only got the tuk tuk one way and was happy to find a bus stop on the main road which cost us 16 rupees to get back into Kandy. The tea they sell there is much cheaper than the tea factory prices in the way to botanical gardens

Title: Kind of Interesting
Text: I enjoyed the tour of this now-defunct manufacturing facility, even if it wasn't anything amazing. It gives you an idea how things worked and how tea is made, which I didn't know much about prior to our visit.  More interesting, though, is a drive along the road outside to explore the tea plantation itself and see pickers in action.

Title: Unexpected jewel ...
Text: We didn't have high expectations of the Tea Museum, but it was excellent - very informative about the history of tea in Sri Lanka, and you also get a nice cuppa on the top floor café!

Title: Travel back in TeaTime.
Text: Well worth visiting this Tea museum, to travel back in Tea Time and learn lots about the Tea industry and its establishment in Sri Lanka, complete with examples of the original equipment used and the way tea was manufactured in the entirety of the process.  We found it most interesting, and have visited multiple times, whenever in Kandy. I think it is a credit to whoever has collected all the equipment and set this up for all to learn from. There is a small entry fee, and free tea is served once one reaches the highest level of this original old tea factory.  Guides are provided if required.

Title: Phenomenal museum
Text: The Ceylon Tea Museum was such a treat. It is located in a beautiful setting in the hills of Kandy. There is a very informative guided tour of the museum included in the ticket price. Some of the manufacturing equipment dates from the 19th century and has been perfectly restored. There's even a delicious cup of tea included at the end of the tour. Quite remarkable and unmissable if you're passing through the area.

Title: #1 Tea Museum
Text: Awesome Tea Museum I ever See like this with all types of tea making facilities in front of us good experience Must Visit

Title: Great place to discover more about tea
Text: Very nice place, everybody is very helpful to learn something about tea manufacturing. In the top of the building you can buy postcards or other souvenirs and try different types of tea, which is included in the price ticket.

Title: Vintage building, authentic machinery and a cup of tea
Text:
An old tea factory turned into a tea museum.  Everything is kept authentic, which makes the building an attraction on itself.   In the museum you get a rather quick tour with a guide, but I found the old machinery pretty cool.   After the tour you can have a free cup of tea on the top floor and have a look around the museum on your own.  I found it very interesting to learn about the production of tea. 
Upstairs are also shops where you can buy tea and accessories.   Entrance price is 650 LKR

Title: I learned a lot
Text:
A very well run and informative museum about something I drink every day. Never before thought about how I get my daily cup of tea, but now I know. The visit involves an obligatory guided tour after which you can get a free pot of tea and a walk around the museum at your leisure. The guide spoke excellent english and is very well informed. There's lots of information around the museum, although a few of the exhibits could have done with more information. The cafeteria has an excellent video documentary on tea.

Overall, a very good museum.

Title: Free tour, free tea, no hard sell!
Text:
Great tour by one of the local producers then taken up to the tea room and given the tea of your choice and then left alone.

We purchased some gifts from the shop but did not feel obliged to.  Was a really great way to spend a couple of hours in the afternoon.

A little bit out of the way, about a 15 min drive.

Title: Very interesting visit, tells you all about tea
Text: A place very professionally managed for tourists, they have guides who can speak most of the foreign languages. The walk in the museum explains the complete process of tea manufacturing right from plucking leaves. You can enjoy free tea freshly prepared or paid golden n silver tip teas. Also there is an outlet to purchase tea if you are interested.

Title: Everything you need to know about tea
Text: This museum is a must see in Kandy, even if you're not a tea enthusiast. It is as well a technical museum as a very educational site to learn about tea growing and processing. They also give a real tribute to James Taylor and sir Thomas Lipton who started the tea industry in Sri Lanka. The displays and a guided tour give you everything you need to know before you visit a plantation and a working tea factory. Everything in the museum is displayed really well and in real size as the site once was a tea factory. If you hire a transport in Kandy ask for Ceylon Tea Museum and don't let them take you to some tea factory around the city, where they get commission.

Title: Great Museum
Text: The museum is housed in an old tea factory, the building itself is very beautiful and the exhibits are very quaint / interesting. We were given a guided tour by a very friendly staff member and a cup of tea is included in the admission price.

Title: Interesting tour
Text: Was more interesting than I had anticipated. I learned quite a lot about the production of tea in Sri Lanka. It is worth a visit.

Title: Great Museum!!!
Text: During a one-day tuk-tuk tour of the area with my family, this was one of our stops. We started by sitting down and enjoying some complimentary tea and sweets. Then a local guide gave us the tour of the museum. I love tea, and it was great to learn about the different types there and how it is made. Afterwards, you have a chance to buy tea downstairs.

Title: Worth stopping
Text: Very interesting to see how the tea is processed from the time picked from the plants until is bagged and sent to auction.

Title: Not bad...
Text:
I visited the tea museum as something to do whilst in Kandy. I enjoyed the free cup of tea at the top and the views from the restaurant floor. There were some interesting bits of information about James Taylor and Mr Lipton's. 

However the rest of the museum was not appealing to me, being a collection of machines used during the manufacturing process. I imagine this would be more interesting for the mechanically minded. 

I was shown around by a tour guide who was pleasant but just gave me basic facts about each machine, I would have been interested in a more detailed explanation of the process at each stage.

Nonetheless I enjoyed my visit. Entry is SLR 650.

Title: I have visited this Museum on at least three occasions starting in 2003
Text:
This is an excellent idea which has had measured progress from the first time I visited it in 2003 when Mr Madugalle was the Manager.  I knew him as a quiet conscientious person when he was Manager, Thotulagalla Estate, Haputale. He has now retired but left a great legacy on which some great opportunities await.
I last visited this place in August 2015 and questioned the ladies there as to whether there had been new developments in the past three years.  Sadly, they confirmed that there were no developments so I didn't make the effort to spend more time here.

However for the first time visitor it does give a glimpse of the tea manufacture processes of the past and they can make up their minds as to how this place can be made to capture the imagination of a greater number of visitors.  The tea industry of Ceylon is in rapid decline because there is a lack of vision for its future.  The British gave this country a wonderful legacy upon which a significant future was squandered away.  The country has lost its European markets and this industry is mired in practices which are known to most people through their own media in the country as totally inappropriate. The sad thing is that most people who can do something about it lack the energy, courage and ability to do anything about it.  Still the Museum as it stands is an effective monument to the creative effort of many good people to provide an opportunity for an outstanding character to take this industry to a better place.

It calls for hard work, courage, fortitude and capability to turn it around. The rewards will be substantial but  the inheritors have taken a long time-about 45 years.

Title: it's what Ceylon about.
Text: excellent experience in how ceylon tea is made. after the tour you get to enjoy a complementary cup of black tea. on the top floor there is a great variety of tea selections from different tea factories.

Title: A must do in Kandy
Text:
We toured this whilst in Kandy  it was quiet cheap and you got a cup of pot tea after the tour
The tour was very informative and we did not realise how involved tea production is so it was fantastic and very well done !

Title: An interesting walk.
Text:
Ive always thought you should visit a countys National Museum if you get the chance. Its worth it. A beautiful building depicting the history of Sri Lanka. Stroll through the rooms at your own pace and try to take it all in. 
Lots and lots to see and learn. It is quite warm in the museum as there is no ac. Not a big deal. Bring some water. Youll be glad you went.

Title: Superb Museum and lovely lunch
Text: We visited the national museum in January and were very impressed, not only by the exhibitions which were carefully presented, but also by the beautiful building and the lovely Sri Lankan cafeteria. A must do for those who appreciate Sri Lankan history and culture.

Title: Wonderful museum in a beautiful building
Text: This was a genuinely pleasant surprise - a beautiful 19th century building, overflowing with treasures from Sri Lanka's past from prehistory to the present day. Our kids (4 and 7) loved wandering the halls looking at the exhibits. (Don't forget to pop into the park next door afterwards to rest your weary legs and watch the world / squirrels / parkeets / fruitbats go by!)

Title: Exceptional museum
Text: This is a great museum of the history of the country, with a great collection of artifacts and replicas. The preserved skeletons and the art were my favourite parts. Some of the dioramas need to be touched up but overall a great collection well worth the visit. Compared with some of the museums we have visited, 1000 rupees for admission is cheap, considering that to do this museum justice you will need to spend the whole day here.

Title: Best Museum at this Location
Text: When I needed a museum to visit, I was so happy to standing in the lobby of this museum.  It gives an excellent history of the creation of Sri Lanka.    Ive never realized that Sri Lanka was a country till I went here.  You should attend.

Title: Colonial building housing national collection
Text: A traditional style of national museum starting with mans early history up to recent time. It was started by a British colonial. Some interesting exhibits, one which I enjoyed was seeing the colonial period clothing of the Burghers. Worth a visit, but it was a hot day, and there arent A/C or good fans. The museum store has many handcrafted items with good prices.

Title: Interesting insight into local history
Text:
This is great for history students and who have passion to study history of places. 

The museum building itself is great but the lighting is not very effective but I enjoyed seeing so many new items showcasing history dating back to centuries.

Title: Good to know more about Sri Lankas history
Text: It was our first time in Sri Lanka and I thought it would be a good way to get to know this little but complex country before we left Colombo to explore. The museum is small and well organized, and although the expositions are not new and do not count with technological improvements, the pieces in the expositions are great and worth the visit. Every information is translated to English in the boards with short and clear explanations. We learned a lot by this visit, specially about the different eras of the mighty empires of Anuradhapura, Pollonaruwa and the more recent Kandean period. Worth the visit ! Take 2-3 hours to explore the museum without haste.

Title: Great place to know your heritage
Text:
The museum has artifacts that are dated and old yet well preserved.  There are descriptions written that make it easy to understand the artifacts.  It's amazing to know how old the history of Sri Lanka is.

It was extremely humid with fans placed at some places. Either there should be AC or fans as our can get pretty claustrophobic.

Title: 1000 lkr for foreigners. Didnt bother
Text: After being sick of paying lots extra for Sri Lanka tourist sights, I would have at least expected a museum in the capital to be free, or cheap. 1000Lkr for foreigners and basically nothing for locals. Didnt bother going in as I refuse to pay for this stuff that should be the same price for all. Or at least not 10 times more expensive.

Title: Gives info about the Lankan history
Text: Its located in the heart of the city and has a detailed information about the heritage and history of the lankan island.

Title: National Treasures
Text:
I'm still trying to understand how our tour only allowed us one hour at this museum to view eleven galleries of national treasures. We managed to view five galleries and enjoyed the experience albeit disappointed that we could not visit the remainder.
The displays could be better curated but that's just my viewpoint; there is substantial information on many of the exhibits while very brief on others. The galleries visited display artefacts belonging to the Pre and Proto Historic, Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa, Kandy and Transitional periods. From among all these treasures I selected the Goddess Tara, the Elephant Lamp, Siva-Nataraja, the Royal Seat and the stunning Samadhi Buddha statue under the Makara Arch as my favourite displays. 
The museum is housed in an impressive building dating to 1877 and founded by Sir William Henry Gregory, the British Governor at the time. A statue in his honour stands in the lawned area fronting the main entrance with notation, "erected by the inhabitants of this island to commemorate the many benefits conferred by him upon the colony during his administration of the government 1872 - 1877". This museum is a fitting legacy

Title: Drearily and not user friendly
Text:
A real throwback to the past, in all senses.  Has not been done up for ages and whilst there are some nice artefacts they are poorly displayed with little information.  The whole place is dreary and dim.   Two floors but no lift and although they say they close the second floor at 4pm it was closed by 3.15 today and we couldnt go up. It is in a complex of government buildings and there are only limited ways out of the compound so I had to walk a long way round to get to a road. 

I am mildly disabled and need to sit from time to time but no chairs except for the room attendants.  No free info. A small printed guide  was 10 rupees but we didnt have small enough change so couldnt have one. Wouldnt go back

Title: Magnificent colonial building
Text: We did not visit the Museum but a look at this building is not to be missed on a visit to Colombo.  It is a magnificent example of British colonial architecture set in lovely expansive lawns.

Title: A Must Do Venue
Text: I would strongly urge all visitors to Sri Lanka to visit this museum. It offers a comprehensive history of the country, it's traditions and it's people from prehistoric times through to the present day. We visited at the beginning of our tour and I felt it gave us a better perspective and understanding of the country before we visited other sites.

Title: Histroy of the Island
Text: The National Museum of Colombo was 100% worth it! Our entire visit allows us to understand the entire story of Sri Lanka. It showcases the culture of the country, along with documents and antiques displayed inside. The establishment was very clean too.

Title: Nicely done museum
Text: There are lots of artifacts here and archaeological specimens. I was hoping for more information on the civil war but the museum is impressive enough as is. The section on masks is very interesting.

Title: Great perspectives on Sri Lankan history
Text:
We did this at the end of a two week trip around Sri Lanka and it puts all that we saw into perspective and joined the dots for us (where we were confused about who ruled when and where)!

Many examples of the country's cultural achievements as well as it's historical roots.
Definitely wotrth visiting for a couple of hours or so.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Both the beautiful building as well as the amazing artifacts make that visit a great experience while you are in Colombo. There are a fare amount of explanation in English, so one can learn quite a lot on Sri Lankan history from a visit there. 
And, again, the artifacts are amazing!
I could only wish that there were toilets inside the building, and not only in the exterior.

Title: A bit of local history
Text: We learnt a lot from our visit to the museum as it shows the whole story of Sri Lanka as a country. There were clearly demarcated sections on different points of interest.

Title: VERY INTERESTING
Text: This museum is worth the visit. It shows the whole story of Sri Lanka with documents and antiques displayed. All is clean, well explained and well displayed. There is a large variety of goods displayes (antiques, statues, ivory, paints, fabrics...). Take your time to go around there are many rooms to visit including "live" scenery of the agricultural world.

Title: must visit
Text: One of the best national museums weve seen in Asia. Not only a comprehensive history of Sri Lanka but an insightful history of mankind. The museum is well laid out and easy to navigate. Its definitely date, and the dioramas a bit terrifying...but overall, I walked out learning more about Sri Lanka.

Title: Fascinating visit
Text:
The Staff were very obliging and the exhibitions very well done 
Worth a visit Its easy to get to and getting a Uber or taxi simple

Title: Incredible
Text:
I loved this Museum. The statues and sculptures from the Buddhist sites are simply incredible. I found it very interesting and surprisingly well arranged and laid out. The Buddhist history was the best thing for me and I realised there are still places I want to see in Sri Lanka related to this. The Kandy section was very interesting too. The Throne was worth a visit all by itself. I was also surprisingly moved by some of the murals. It was a shame the Masks were at the very end as I was tired by then and needing a drink and did not fully concentrate on them which I might have done had they been earlier in the trail, as once on it you are not able to exit.
So, excellent on the exhibits and history front but really lacking on the cafe front. I could not get any information about where the gift shop was. I ended up in a branch of Laksala to use the Toilet there. So, it was a little haphazard on the cafe and toilet front which after 2 hours in the heat was really needed. However, a minor inconvenience really for such a historical and cultural treat!

Title: full of information
Text: Very important place to visit if you have enough time during the the trip. I got many information from the museum here as well as a huge information from my tour guide and the friend

Title: My visit
Text: Ok museum not my cup of tea but good for a quick visit, no air con at all baked inside they only have fans and should have air con installed other wise not worth going people were leaving quickly coz of how hot it was inside

Title: The best place to learn about Sri Lanka
Text:
The museum is a comprehensive place to know about Sri Lanka from geography, economy to history.

I quite enjoyed roaming around. There were not so many visitors then. 

In the middle of summer, one should be ready to bear heat as it is not air conditioned.

Title: National Museum -An historical experience !!!
Text:
We had been to the national museum,several old artifacts,stones,idols,coins,pillars,pots  were very well preserved.Very well maintained museum neat and clean.
HSBC bank were one of the main sponsors of this museum.A lot about the sri lankan history was available in this museum.It even had a place where the old life style of the ancient sri lankan people was.
Overall time well spent.

Title: Must visit
Text: Learned a lot about Sri Lankas culture. Saw a lot to historical artifacts and scriptures which were fascinating. Should visit once if youre in colombo

Title: Finding Sri Lanka history and culture in a day
Text: In this museum you can find history of Sri Lanka, from pre historical times to modern days, Culture, religion, history all toghether in the same place. There's also a gift shop but, unfortunatly the staff of the gift shop is not so helpfull and nice as staff in the museum...There is also a beatifull garden with a fantastic giant tree. A must! On the nearby there paintings and art work available , from students of an Art School. Very friendly people!

Title: Worth a visit if only out of interest...........
Text:
We found that the museum of natural history a waste of time, however it was interesting to see the Beautiful colonial style building that showcased the British opulence of the time. 
There is NO Air Conditioning, and very poor lighting over the images.
Foreigners are charged more than the locals.
They do need to update and make this Museum more modern to keep it inline with the growth of the city.
The Artifacts need to be showcased to preserve.
There were NO toilets in the building.

Title: No AC inside
Text: The museum is big and very interesting. However, make sure you have enough water before you get in because you cannot re-enter again. There is no AC inside so it is hot and dehydrated.

Title: The recreations of early civilisations are excellent
Text: Our concierge told us: "There's nothing to do in Colombo".  But we took a Tuk Tuk to the museum and spent a happy two hours looking at all the displays. The information was available in English and we had no trouble understanding any of the material.  The dioramas recreating early Sri Lankan village life were excellent - very lifelike and convincing and very educational.

Title: Wonderful building and excellent exhibits
Text:
If you want a quick overview of the history, culture & religion of Sri Lanka, this is your place. Beautiful exhibits with explanations in three languages made for a fascinating couple of hours.
Our only beef? They shut the upper floor at 4pm (and this was not mentioned in any guide book we read or any review online) and they do not reduce the price.

Title: beautiful building
Text:
The museum is nice place to go to especially if you intend afterwards to travel to other cities as you will understand the story behind what you see.
It is not huge so you get to see everything quite easily and the collection of objects is nice.
From the outside the building is really beautiful.

Title: A quick summary about Sri Lanka history
Text: The museum exhibits brief history of the Anaradhapura, Polonnaruwa and Kandy period which provides a good start or conclusion for visiting Sri Lanka.

Title: Informative displays help visualise Sri Lankan heritage and culture.
Text: Although our visit was in effect a whistestop tour of the museum, I feel that we got a lot from it. We had visited the Square of Independence and it's museum shortly before, and some of the information was repeated in both.  The museum celebrates Sri Lanka's vast cultural past, the influences that came from outside, to include the Dutch,Portugese and British Colonial times, along with showing traditional farming methods and tools, traditional craft etc. Well laid out, we spent only an hour and  a quarter here but could have stayed a lot longer. Worth a visit at rs 300 per person.

Title: Worth to see while in Colombo
Text: National museum is the largest museum in Sri Lanka. The museum holds contains a collections of much importance to Sri Lanka such as the regalia of the country, including the throne and crown of the Kandyan monarchs as well as many other exhibits telling the story of ancient Sri Lanka. It was established in 1877. Generally it is open from 9 am to 5 pm

Title: Great Day Trip to the National Museum!!!
Text: Great learning experience for those into art, antiques and artifacts! Very well designed museum with great displays and information regarding Sri Lankan history. For those with walking disabilities and limitations, there are a lot of walking and stairwells thoughout. Many display rooms do not allow photography or camera use. However, there is a great deal of information to be learned from this place - from history to wars to cultural ideologies and politics. This place is a great half day trip for museum lovers!!

Title: Amazing
Text: Visited this place with no expectations and it was a wonderful suprise. Leave plenty of time, well over an hour to see all the section of the museum.

Title: Mostly religious artifacts.  No air conditioning
Text: This large museum is in a beautiful building.  Although it stretches over several floors, the second floor is closed off a half hour before the museum closes so we did not get there.  There are certainly some interesting exhibits and works of art, but it was packed with school children and the fans in every room were not enough to keep the building comfortable.  Note that there is a very nice (air-conditioned!) gift shop in a separate building.  I would not call this a must-see.

Title: One of the World's Great Civilizations on Display
Text:
Sri Lanka has an incredible civilization at the intersection of major sea routes, and the Colombo Museum is the storehouse of that greatness.
It i an old fashioned museum in an incredibly beautiful building built in the day when museum visitors were expected to be educated and not need to be spoon-fed every morsel of desired information.  The exhibits offer each visitor a chance to see, to think, to question, and to learn.  It is a classic museum devoted to a classic culture, and therefore it is for education more than entertainment.

Title: Interesting Museum
Text: Great colonial building housing some great exhibits from days gone by. Worth a visit when in Colombo, small entrance fee.

Title: Very well displayed collection
Text:
The museum building is superb but it is 'naturally ventilated' so it does get a bit hot and humid. The galleries take you through the various different kingdoms ruling Ceylon and then move on to look at topics such as painting, sculpture etc..  There is a lot of material but the explanatory notes are comprehensive and clear.
We found it very interesting

Title: beautiful grounds
Text: The museum is set in a huge, old and grand colonial style building. The grounds around are kept very neatly landscaped. The museum is well worth checking out, there are a variety of displays.

Title: First rate attraction
Text:
The National Museum was purposefully built as a museum in 1877. It is as the picture shows a graceful colonial building, with spacious galleries, half themed, half periodic. Its collection is part original, part copies (because they are still in situ for example in Sigiriya).

I was captivated by the bronze gilt Avalokiteshsvara Bodhisattva and despite my best efforts unable to find a replica anywhere. 

This is well worth a visit. The only downside is that the Museum shop has very limited stock.

Title: One stop history and cultural centre
Text: An enormous and elegant building which houses, displays and explains over a dozen aspects of Sri Lankan pre-history through periods of social and political evolution. Plenty of themes to choose from and choose you must if only to keep a tour down to 2-3 hours.

Title: Neoclassical vibes
Text: I visited today it was beautiful buildings and many things to see inside the museum, it's recommended to visit for the traveller to knows more about Sri Lanka history.

Title: Impressive
Text: It's hard to guess from the outside, but this museum is huge. We spent an easy three hours there (both my friend and I liked to read everything), but even then we were rushing through some of the final rooms because we were hungry. The history is well displayed, but there is a distinct hop over the period between the Kingdom of Kandy and Sri Lanka's independence. Since I hadn't read any other sources before the museum, I had been hoping to learn what that period was like for this country and how the transition from colony to nation had gone, but if it was in the museum then I missed it. Overall though, this place was incredible.

Title: Not to be missed!!!!
Text: This is one of the best museums anywhere. Be well rested and bring water. Expect to spend at least 4 hours. there is so much history to see. The museum is divided into time eras and there were many in Sri Lanka.

Title: So much to see.
Text:
I will preface this review that I visited have just got off my flight so was probably too tired to take it all in...

The grounds are lovely and the building itself spectacular. 

On the ground floor there are a huge range of artifacts covering the whole of Sri Lankas history. The labeling is good and there are clear informative descriptions of each room.

Upstairs there are several galleries with paintings, textiles and mask displays. It is worth noting that they close the upstairs areas earlier than the main exhibits downstairs.

Title: Great insight into Sri Lankan History
Text: This museum is a great way to spend a morning or an afternoon while in Colombo. It is 1000 LKR for entry but you can buy a joint ticket for this and the Museum of Natural History for 1200 LKR so if you intend to visit both this is worth it. There is no air conditioning in the museum. I went in January and it was fine. If this is a worry then go when it opens at 9am and it should be cooler. There is a cafe on site with a clean toilet. Well worth having a little wander around the park opposite as well.

Title: Mrs
Text: Interesting exhibition of Sri Lanka s history, very informative. Beautiful building and relaxing garden tea house

Title: Interesting!!!
Text: A very interesting collection of historical artifacts. The museum is a must visit to understand and appreciate the history of Sri Lanka. A recommended visit

Title: Worth a visit
Text: This is a large museum with many different rooms featuring different aspects of life, art and culture of Sri Lanka.

Title: Very interesting
Text: If you are doing a stop in Colombo on your way to the cultural triangle the National Museum is definitely worth a visit. You will find many antiquities here that have been removed from Polonuwara and Anuradhapura. Entry is cheap and there is plenty to see. Though carry water as it was very hot inside.

Title: If you enjoy history, museums - go see it
Text: There are 15 rooms so allow a couple of hours.  Some rooms are more interesting than others and they give a great insight into the Sri Lanka history and influences. We felt Rps 1000 per person was justified by the explanation, quality of display and quantity of items.  There are many fans in each room to cool you down and while there were a numner of people visiting on a Saturday it never felt crowded.  If you have any interest in what made the island as it is today then its worth a visit, time permitting.

Title: Good experience
Text: The self tour was good. The numbered stalls give additional information so that anyone can get the required information.

Title: Short visit
Text: Interesting place with some great artefacts and information about the history of Sri Lanka. Be prepared for the usual high prices for foreigners to visit local attractions, I think it was overpriced for the time we spent there (our visit was made shorter by the lack of air conditioning).

Title: Just Don't
Text: There's no AC! There is absolutely nothing in this museum of any value or interest and the tickets are WAY over priced.

Title: Its such a great place to visit
Text: Colombo National Museum is a glorious colonial building full of beautiful historical artefacts. From textiles to jewellery, this museum has everything you need in order to understand their city. Its such a great place to visit if you want to know more about Sri Lankan culture!

Title: This should be your first stop
Text: If youre going on a trip through Colombo, this should be your first stop since it teaches the historical context of the city. It not only provides a great understanding of the things you will see in your visit, English and other local languages are also used in their exhibits! Therefore, its really easy to understand everything!

Title: Good place to learn about Sri Lanka's History and Culture
Text: I went there in the afternoon. At the entrance, they offered to place my heavy bagpack at a place for free. A tag is passed to you. For an adult who does not have Sri Lankan citizenship, the entrance fee is LKR1000 which is around SGD7.50. There was no air-conditioned room for most of the exhibits. However, there are fans to keep you cool from the hot sun. The staff there was nice as I got lost for one part and then he guided me by telling me to go upstairs. There are various beautiful exhibits like the throne and the Sword of King Bhuwanekabhaju, which have a dragon face. It reminded me of the parrot umbrella of Mary Poppins. All in all, it was a good visit and one can spend 2-3 hours there.

Title: Must see place
Text:
The building was constructed around 1870.it is one of the very beautiful building of srilanka.It has around 13 gallery displaying art and culture of srilanka.
The exhibits are displayed in very planned and organized manner.you can start from one place and end in last gallery.
It has large collection of old sculptures particularly related to buddha.paintings are also very old.
Every one must spent atleast half day to visit and learn about srilanka.
Viddyapati chaudhary 
Lucknow

Title: Poorly maintained!
Text: They charge a lot but dont care of the exhibits; nor provide a good experience for the amount they charge!

Title: Huge building; lots to see
Text: I'm not really a museum person, I get bored easily, but I did enjoy wandering around this one. Vast area with lots on display and in a beautiful green setting, including a fantastic fig tree.

Title: Worth stopping for
Text: Interesting artifacts from Sri Lanka's history. Beautiful building  that could need some repairs though. Lovely cafe in the back that has a nice gift shop.

Title: Very well organised displays
Text: The National Museum is a fine example of curation. All information provided is well informed and available in English as well as local languages. We visited from 2.30 until 4.15 and will return for the national history museum. The building is cooled by fan and there is a small cafe where you can purchase cold water if you wish.

Title: Vast building with much to see
Text:
We came in the late morning and although the traffic driving to the museum was really heavy the queue to enter was reasonable. We were on a coach tour and this was our first stop and there must of been half a dozen other coaches there too. 
The museum is spread out over a number of floors and in different wings. there are collections from times go by and so waxwork type displays of life as it was in different areas and eras. The building with its high ceilings and open planning is cool and an inviting relief from the outside heat of the day. 
There is plenty for people of all ages to see and of course there is a gift shop and cafe on the site as well as public toilets. There are many steps inside the building and therefore it could be difficult for people with mobility issues but they may have lift we did not see one but then we had no need to look. Well worth a visit.

Title: A must visit !
Text: Having been a several museums across different countries , the colombo national museum is one the best I've seen in terms of the depth of details offered,  the displays of historic things,  statues, art gallery etc.  Be ready to spend at least 3 hours because there's just so much to see and learn. Words alone will not do justice so I've added some pictures of the amazing displays at the museum. Good place to bring the kids and teenagers for an educational tour!

Title: Brilliantly done - totally worthwhile
Text:
One of the best national museums weve seen in Asia. Not only a comprehensive history of Sri Lanka but an insightful history of mankind.
It covers everything with vast quantities of historical items and artefacts. Multiple dioramas were exceptionally well done & great for kids.
The colonial style building is also stunning.
We could have spent a full day here. 
Lots of staff around & its well mapped out. Exceptional.

Title: very interesting
Text: Colombo national museum very interesting thousands of antiquities as well as cultural and historical exhibits, paintings and manuscripts are on display in the galleries of a grand, italian-architectural-style building opened in 1877.

Title: Good place to start
Text: The museum is definitely worth a visit, I would suggest that if you are starting your trip in Colombo it should be the first place to visit, sets the context of what you are about to see.  Unfortunately for us it was at the end of our trip but was still very worthwhile, gave us a good understanding of a lot of things and places we saw and visited.  It was well laid out, albeit sometimes the lighting was not the best, the signage was good and all translated into English.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text:
Highly recommended, well laid out and curated collection showing the history of Sri Lanka.  All the signs had English translations.

Took about 2 hours to get round (Im a museum geek and take my time).  It can easily be done in a hour.

Title: Worth a visit, certainly helped me better understand the history
Text: There's a lot to walk through! And so much to read.  The museum is well laid out and easy to navigate.  Its definitely date, and the dioramas a bit terrifying...but overall, I walked out learning more about Sri Lanka. Stop by and enjoy a few hours of the afternoon.

Title: The museum of natural history  is a waste of time , but the Museum itself is worthwhile,
Text: Worth the time for a look at Sri Lankas history, the ticket office  was a con , said he did not have any change so we paid 2000 rp rather than 1200 rp.

Title: Interesting but needs updating
Text: I love visiting museums.  I think this one needs a little bit more work to bring it up to standard and in a city that is rapidly updating a lot its surprising that they havent a more modern museum.  Theres way too much repetitive artifacts and not enough explanation.  Theres also very little seating and after an hour, you need to be able to rest your feet.  It feels like the exhibits need to be updated, and the flow more useful for travelers to understand the story of Sri Lanka.  Its has no air conditioning either, so avoid on hot days.  There is also no decent cafe on site.

Title: My visit to Colombo National Museum
Text:
A gem of a museum, going by the priceless exhibits in it. 

If anyone wants to know about the amazingly close civlisational, cultural, artistic and spiritual bonds between Sri Lanka and India during the various eras of history, there is no better place to discover it than in this museum. It will surprise and disappoint those who believe Hinduism and Buddhism are dissimilar or mutually antagonistic. The museum has relatively less focus on Sri Lanka's Islamic heritage.

I had gone to see the trilingual (Chinese, Tamil, Persian) stone inscription about the voyage of the great Chinese explorer Zheng He (1371-1433), who visited both Sri Lanka and India. The inscription shows that he offered prayers to Allah, Buddha and Shiva (a Hindu deity) for his own safety and for peace in the world. A good historical example of Sri Lanka-India-China affinity.

My two big complaints about the museum: 1) The Museum Shop is hopelessly small and short of material on sale; and 2) The museum guides should be proficient in English and know more about the history of the museum and its exhibits.

If you are a visitor to Colombo, don't miss it.

Title: Worthwhile visit
Text:
Found this glorious colonial building so much better than expected.well laid out with explanatory boards alongside exhibits in English as well as local languages. Some excellent examples of textiles, jewellery and weapons as well as history, archeology examples from the many of the sites we had visited during our holiday in SriLanka.
It was hot but fans were placed around all the rooms so you could cool off.
Shop with lots of resealable priced souvenirs and a cafe. Lots to like, definitely recommend a visit we spent 2 hours and could have spent longer.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Excellent museum highlighting the history of Sri Lanka and all visitors to the country should spend some time learning about the country. Worth an hour or so during ones time in Colombo

Title: History and Artifacts
Text:
Visited on 22/February/2020

Entry Fee applicable

This place was one of the visit places in the Colombo tour itinerary and this place gives you a understanding of the history of Colombo, its establishment and so on.
Displays are interesting and of interest for all those who love to know in-depth about the place of visit.

If this makes you interested then do visit.

Title: Diverse Interesting artefacts
Text:
A large number of diverse artefacts, from many eras, all labelled. Sculpture, paintings, fabric, jewellery, pottery, currency, etc 
The building itself is beautiful.

Title: Large and interesting museum
Text: Easy to find your way through the exhibition as there are clear signposts throughout guiding you to each gallery. The exhibits and information provided give a good insight into centuries of Sri Lankan history. We visited after a 2 week trip around Sri Lanka and our visit helped to cement and make sense of what we had seen on our trip. Worth visiting.

Title: Extremely nice - For museum lovers
Text:
A huge collection of very nice artefacts - lots of  statues, paintings, bric-a-brac, etc.  Good explanations of all material displayed.

Some the paintings on cloth are immense.

Very imposing building.  Everything kept in very good condition in a neat and clean environment.  Definitely a pride of Sri Lanka!

Wear comfortable walking shoes.

The canteen adjacent is a bit grubby.  I suspect used by all museum staff.

Title: Overall interesting
Text: We werent blown away, but its a nice museum. It is located in a nice, old House built 150 years ago by the British. You can see the items from the prehistoric age, the iron a age, lots of Buddha skulptures, old paintings, stone sculptures, Ganesha sculptures, old clothes and jewelrys, agriculture from the past and coins for example. We missed exhibits from the last 100 years. But overall it was interesting. No air-condition is available, only fans.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Spent all morning wandering around the very informative museum. It was good to revisit information about the places wed visited during our three week stay. Good value for money with the combined ticket for the Natural History museum too.

Title: Nice place to visit
Text: It was nice to spend an hour here all very informative on life in Sri Lanka a very well  laid out display as we was on a coach tour it was not long enough to appreciate all this museum had to offer but what we did see would make us come back to have a longer stay.

Title: its huge
Text:
The museum has 15 major displays over two floors of a series of interconnected colonial buildings.  We got through the lot but took a break at the cafe next door - you can exit and return at no extra charge. The toilets are located there, too.

We enjoyed the visit - the coins and early trade discussions were particularly interesting. The throne was impressive, too.

It seemed odd that there was not more attention given to the colonial period. Yes, it was mentioned in places but there was not a specific section.

As others have  mentioned, it is not air conditioned and the odd tourist group distrupted the otherwise peace and quiet.

It is certainly a grand building from the outside and it is good that it has been retained

Title: Very interesting building and displays
Text:
Wonderful exhibits and hopefully one day SL with have the resources available to keep them in pristine condition for future generations.

A great place to spend a couple of hours.

Title: If you have time and money, then yes...
Text: We came to the National Museum towards the end of the day, in hopes of finding out a little more about the country and to see some of the artifacts illustrating the history. The space itself is vast and quite old. It is a cavernous series of connected rooms cooled only by standing fans, filled with objects and art kept in old cases with glass panes. We saw lovely original pieces and some reproductions with the originals held by the colonist countries still (very sad). The larger general descriptions were well written and helpful, but the objects themselves were only labeled with no identifying facts, which I found frustrating. There were also a number of displays that were dated (lifesized dioramas of jungle scenes with sound effects, etc...). We walked and walked (quickly to get upstairs before the 4pm closing time for upper floors) and were stuck behind a large tour group part of the time, which was very frustrating as they stood in front of important pieces, not moving to let others in to see. I think this is an important landmark and tourist destination that would benefit with major updates to the displays. There is also a sense that the objects are not benefiting from the spaces they are kept in (wondering how they are damaged by the heat/light/etc...). If you have time and the entrance fee, it is worth a visit.

Title: Nice Museum Housed in A Colonial Building
Text:
We visited this museum as part of a shore excursion from our cruise ship that was docked in Colombo.  

This is a large extensive historical museum housed in beautiful colonial buildings that has quite extensive collections in it.  Most of displays did have English explanations.  It also has a film at the entrance of the museum that covers some of the history of Sri Lanka. This room has air conditioning and seating.

Since this is a colonial building it does not have air conditioning but I found the temperature was comfortable due to cross breezes.  There are no toilets in the museum building itself.  However, there are western toilets in the gift shop building and in annex to the main toilet building located outside of the main museum buildings.  

The gift shop is quite extensive with lots of various types of souvenirs in it.  I would recommend that you spend 2 to 3 hours to fully enjoy this museum.

Title: A must see in Colombo!
Text: We were fascinated by the extensive and breathtaking artifacts displayed in the National Museum. A large colonial style building houses the national collection of Sri Lankan history. Cannot say enough about the quality and the layout of the museum. It was beautiful. The whole of Sri Lankan history (and prehistoric history as well) was presented over many floors and large galleries. We were blown away with the artistry and evolution of the island. A great first stop in Colombo and a must see location.

Title: beautiful building interesting ehxhibits.
Text: The building is certainly impressive. We found plenty to interest us for the couple of hours we spent there. Some of the paintings were in very poor condition but were nevertheless worth seeing for their historical value. We did rush through some of the rooms as we were short on time and wished to see as much as possible.

Title: Excellent experience
Text: Simple museum but outstanding basic educational experience of Sri Lanka. I would recommend a visit to get an understanding of the general history of Sri Lanka particular from the 9-10 century onwards

Title: Worth a visit
Text: On an off travel day, not a bad idea to visit to see the cultural early days of SriLanka. Takes about 2 hrs for a complete visit, very interesting

Title: Extensive, well displayed exhibits in a beautiful building
Text:
The museum is in a gorgeous building set in large. well maintained gardens.
Allow a few hours for your visit and be aware that, at the time of our visit (October 2018) access to the upper floors was only possible until 4pm.
The various exhibits are well displayed and some have good description cards attached.  As is often the case with many museums, this information is often lacking at other displays and you have to rely on guess work or prior knowledge!
There is a lovely café by the museum gift shop, with seating outside in the courtyard, which had a very European feel.
A visit to the museum leaves you well placed for a stroll around the very pleasant Victoria Park (which we did) and also the adjacent Natural History Museum and art gallery (which we didn't leave time for!)

Title: Uninspiring displays
Text: Museum needs a makeover in terms of how exhibits are displayed and explained. There is no air-conditioning. And no guides or tours to explain. There is an interesting display of tourist /sidewalk art outside the museum along the road. More colours and much more lively.

Title: An excellent museum that ashames the country due to its employees.
Text:
The museum it's very interesting and gives a very compreensive view from the history, culture, society of Ceylon/Sri Lanka. Unfortunately the assistants close some of the upper rooms 40!!! minutes before ending time, interrupting abruptly the visit, without any justification except a stupid, nervous smile. They were eager to go on weekend, as some five minutes later, half an hour before 17H00, most of them were on the run.
Bad service to Sri Lanka, that is a warm welcoming and interesting country.
Therefore my evalaution reflects  the service and not the museum contents .... what is a shame.

Title: Old, older, oldest
Text:
The National Museum should be a mandatory visit for every single student in Sri Lanka, in order for them not to forget where they come from and not to forget their origins, which they should be proud of. It gives a nice overview and comprehensive summary of the entire history, through colonisation and independence. However, the building itself could certainly do with some urgent refurbishments, because otherwise the picture of the museum building might end up in a museum.
Indications are easy to follow, but the staff in every single hall should be a bit more energetic. They all were either seated on their little chair (I do understand that standing up the entire day is not easy), or they were on their personal phones or they were chatting with a colleague from the hall next to them.
The poorest part was definitely the little museum shop, where some books were available, as well as some post cards. But it was so small that within a minute you know if you want to buy something or not. Definitely to be changed.

Title: Beautiful museum
Text: Colombo National museum was built by the British governor of Sri Lanka in 1876. Its building is beautiful. Surrounding its building there is beautiful and greenery park. Inside the museum you will find the ancient story of Sri Lanka. You will also find the gun, swords, carvings, masks etc from the Sri Lanka's ancient past.

Title: GREAT MUSEUM
Text: Plenty of interesting items & history to see in this Museum, very well planned out & easy to navigate through, well priced souvenir shop just outside Museum & coffee shop with an interesting sign ?? well worth a visit & allow about 2 - 3 hrs.

Title: Worth visiting
Text:
The National Museum is much improved from our last visit 5 years ago when I called it a national disgrace. Most of the ground floor rooms have been improved with many exhibits standing out much better now. 

The upstairs section and the adjacent Natural History Museum need more TLC but there is good information on Sri Lanka, albeit poorly presented. 

You can get a combined ticket to both museums. It is easy to miss the Natural History Museum which is in an adjacent building.

Title: Worth visiting before you travel in Sri Lanka
Text: Relatively easy to locate and with a small adjacent cafe you can spend a few hours here getting a comprehensive background prior to a country visit. Starting from the bottom floor you work your way up to the top which has a series of dioramas depicting early agricultural life. The section on the Sigiriya paintings is perhaps the highlight. Tip : if you want you can stop and exit for the adjacent Barista cafe, and reenter with the same ticket.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Good place to visit if you are in Colombo. It has 15 rooms and takes around 1.5-2 hours to visit all the rooms. Very well maintained and you will come to know the bit of history of SriLanka culture.

Title: Make the time to visit the National Museum
Text: Unequivocally worth the visit to the National Museum. Beautifully presented items covering all districts, and topics such as language and literature, health and sanitation, jewelry, textiles. Worth the 1200lkr.

Title: Must go to this museum
Text: Must go to this museum, it is incredible antiques, and not guide, so you can ask to some taxi drivers (toc toc also) known very well this awesome items. It is hot, very hot, take water with you, no AC.

Title: Opportunity to catch up on Sri Lankan history and background
Text:
This iconic museum is easy to locate on all the maps and the taxis and Tuk tuks know how to get round the back where the entrance way is, somewhat against intuition. It's a big museum, and we only managed the ground floor in just over an hour, as the first floor gets closed off at 4pm - although it was already shut when we got there at 3.30. Having said that there was plenty to keep us occupied, with a thorough grounding in Sri Lanka's pre history and the development of its people's and culture. There was sadly very little about the indigenous forest/aboriginal people's. 
Masses of info about the various kingdoms and their development and it helped put some of our visits to Polonaruwa and Anadrahapura in context. Masses of stone and statue archeology and the most curious exhibit was a slab of stone which had been the base for an urinal/toilet at one of the Buddhist monasteries about 2,000 years ago. Quite a few local families were enjoying themselves on this late Saturday afternoon. The Lanka tourist shop is next door too!

Title: Interesting..
Text:
It is a pity that we were the only 2 visitors to this museum when we visited.
The museum has a number of bursts of freedom fighters in chronological order explaining the struggle the country had gone through to finally achieve freedom.
In talks of inclusivity by depicting pictures with captions like Towards freedom through Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, cultural revolution etc.
It has a clean wash room too.
They charge 300 SLR for a foreigner and 10 SLR for a Srilankan adult and 5SLR for Lankan kids.
Ganesh J

Title: An Important Tribute to the People of Sri Lanka
Text: This important place is the largest museum in Sri Lanka and it will help you understand the ancient story of this serendipity island! It contains, for example, the thrown of the great Kandyan Kongs and many other splendid artifacts!

Title: A must-see place in Colombo
Text: A serene, cool and informative museum with plenty of artefacts related to the history of Sri Lanka. Well layed out in a wonderful colonial building complex. Cheap entry (around 7 euros per adult) for around 2 to 3 hours of browsing, reading, taking photos, educating, strolling, enjoyment.

Title: Very nice
Text: A very nice review of srilankan history.. items are really good and well presented.. it worths a visit indeed

Title: Excellent museum
Text: Very nice overview of Sri Lankan history.  Some very fine pieces in a beautiful building.  I particularly like the old stone facades with scenes of elephants and other animals.  Also had some excellent stone carvings of Ganesha the Hindu god with an elephant head.

Title: Visited after renovation and it was good
Text: It was under renovation for a long time and visited the museum during the school holidays. It was very good and new additions were there. You can take photos inside the premises and the ticket price for a local was very cheap.It included Sri Lankan history and my daughter was amused to see lot of the things she learnt at school in the museum. Cannot highly recommend the lav-oratory facilities. But you can go to Barista in the same compound to have a coffee and a snack and use their rest rooms which is better. For that you will have to walk about 200m as the coffee shop is located in a side. The exhibits are detailed in Sinhala and also in English which makes easiar for travelers.

Title: A very good museum
Text: There are lots of interesting things to see here and it is worth a visit. Descriptions of the exhibits could be a bit better, it is also a shame that people insist on shouting and not using their indoors voices. It would be good if the security people could remind visitors that it is a museum and not a playground!

Title: History
