Text: One of the oldest museum in Sri Lanka. This place is house of some great artifacts and worth a visit.

Title: Okay, but
Text: Lots of interesting artefacts on display here, separated into the various significant historic periods. Interpretation could be better; and there is a lot of repetition. Definitely worth a visit. The cafe and gift shop are poorly signposted, the cafe is small and mostly western foods, the gift shop quite comprehensive.

Title: Intriguing
Text: The staff was friendly, the exhibits were impressive and informative. Would certainly recommend a visit.

Title: A rainy day
Text:
Very simple museum in a nice building
Good for a rainy day in Colombo
Beside there is no much to do in colombo

Title: The Only Museum to Visit in Colombo
Text:
Only pay to visit this one Museum dont go to Natural History its terrible terrible terrible I have seen year 5 school projects better displayed then the Colombo Natural History Museum with all its stuffed dead animals, did I say its TERRIBLE!

However the actual Colombo Museum is worth the visit in its amazing old Colonial building. 

Retired restorers of the world need to save many of these precious artifacts before they rot on display from the humidity. 

But there is so much to see and learn about Sr Lanka here so do visit.

Title: Worth to visit for school childrens
Text: I have visited when I was on 12years. It was almost 20years back. Now lot of renovation has been done for the museum building. Among bus conductor this place known as Glass house. Located on colombo 7. Must visit place for all school children.

Title: A quick history lesson
Text: Columbo national Museum is full of interesting pictures stories and artifacts which tells the history of Sri Lanka from ancient days to the present day. We were visiting just for a few days and this was a great way to help us understand the context of the country we are visiting. It is quite a lot of walking and it set up in 15 areas. One warning its not air-conditioned in there. Even though it was interesting in many ways it was exhausting also.

Title: Fantastic artifacts
Text: The building itself is gorgeous as are the many statues and paintings depicting different periods of Sri Lankan history. The curation itself is lacking in contemporary creativity, with rather bland and minimally descriptive placardsin particular the early settlements of the island.

Title: Nice Historic Place
Text: We went there with family and place is nice and well maintained. There is some renovation work going on.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: We spent a few hours looking around. It was interesting and the displays were informative. Entry cost Rs1000.

Title: Good introduction
Text:
I went to the museum when I first came to Sri Lanka and found it a good way to get an overview of the country and its history and culture.  Ended up in a fine discussion with two of the young attendants who were interested in my observations and clarified some of my questions about religions. 
Not air conditioned-- an early time might be best.

Title: International standard with great artifacts.
Text:
This museum was much bigger than I was expecting and had a lot of really interesting artifacts from ancient times and more modern times. It touches on colonial times, rural living, currency, costume and the traditional monarchy of Sri Lanka. I visited on the end of my trip so it was wonderful to see more artifacts from places like Sigiriya and other places I had visited in previous weeks. It was a great extension to my holiday and very good value for only about 10AUD for foreign adults. 

It gets a little hot in places so be sure to take advantage of the spots that have fans and seats.

Title: Ok, but not spectacular
Text: This place is probably best visited on the beginning of your trip in Sri Lanka as opposed to at the end. You get to see artefacts from Sri Lanka glory times, but I had al ready seen the real deal when visiting Kandy, Anuradhapura etc. However it gives a decent insight into this wonderful country

Title: Nice collection of Sri Lanka artefacts
Text: On a beautiful colonial building, theyre gather a large collection of stone and bronze statues, ancien coins, various artefacts, clothes, etc. Its quite busy and hot but worth the effort.

Title: Loved this quirky place!
Text: Go there. Its all great, especially the death masks! A rambling building of different rooms dedicated to Sri Lankan history.

Title: Great museum full of history and artefacts
Text:
Great selection of artifacts and historic items throughout Sri Lankas history.
I would suggest going on the weekend as school groups visit during the week so it can be quite crowded.
It is set in a beautiful building and feels very calm and you can take your time through the exhibits.
I loved the jewellery and clothing sections!

Title: known for it culture
Text: National Museum of Colombo is the largest museum in colombo where it shows history with full of knowledge.worth visiting.

Title: Archeological Attraction in Colombo
Text:
This museum building seems old palace. It had around 16 rooms to visit. Archeology lover must watch once.
A nice garden outside the museum building.
An idol of Lord Buddha under a tree in garden is peaceful!
There is a small canteen on backside of the museum building.

Title: Worthy of a few hours
Text: Absolutely stunning building and was originally built to be a museum. Inside, museum covers entire history of Sri Lanka from prehistoric times and then groups through different government/city capital periods. Amazing range of artefacts and the museum is well curated and signposted as you are led through galleries in order.

Title: History and culture
Text:
If u need to know srilankan culture and history this is the best place must do in Colombo.
The place is full of knowledgeable things mostly the old ones u can learn history of srilanka while u reading the captions wrote on each stories.

Title: Very good experience
Text: A must visit for history buff, we thoroughly enjoyed the experience. It was amazing journey with very polite non obstructive  attendents in all halls. A person needs atleat 6 hours to thoroughly enjoy it.

Title: Give yourself time
Text:
If you are interested in the history and culture of Sri Lanka, the Colombo National Museum is a must. The displays are carefully curated with short but interesting detail and context provided. Its a pity there is not an illustrated catalogue, though this would need a monetary investment and like so many museums throughout the world, budgets are tight.
Visiting the museum subtly reminds one of the fallacy of colonial assumptions. Sri Lanka has a civilization stretching centuries BC.

Title: NEEDS A MAJOR OVERHAUL
Text: Well, we arrived early had to wait until 10.00 when it opened. Went in with high hopes, should have known better! Paying a whopping Rs.1000 Aud $10 each we were expecting a lot & were utterly disappointed. With the automated dummies that were new in the 60s, ( and even then wouldnt have impressed ) to the stifling heat, that had us running from fan to fan in each huge room, we couldnt wait to get to the exit. The building is impressive, save yourself some money & see it from the outside, you can also take a photo of the 9th century Buddha from the entrance way. Bodhisattva Sandals were cool, and the wooden masks ok.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Bit surprised by some of the negative reviews of this museum.  There are lots of different exhibits, covering the country's history, including the changing locations of the capital and why.  There are fans in each room but no air conditioning so if you're planning to go to get out of the heat, you might need to re think.  That said, it's not particularly somewhere I'd take children as there is a lot of reading to understand the exhibits.

Title: not bad
Text: reasonable visit. grand architecture from the British colonial era which makes it impressive. worth a quick visit although at 1200 for both visits it is a bit steep for SL

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Beautiful colonial building which houses some very interesting artifacts. Really like the fact that many things were not behind glass and could be seen very clearly. 

No ac so it is quite warm but there are lots of fans in every room. 

Well laid out. Some interesting water colours upstairs and a great textile section.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Best way to find out about the Sinhalese culture and history! Highly recommend for everyone visiting the capital for more than a day!

Title: An excellent snapshot into Sri Lankan culture and history
Text:
We visited the Natural history and main museum. The national history (science) museum was ok. It seems like it needs a renovation. The blue whale skeleton was very impressive. 
The main museum which houses the cultural history was a standout. It had a vast collection of artefacts, art and other cultural history items. 
What would be awesome though is having live shows and demonstrations of devil dancing. There is an air conditioned cafe outside the museum with a gift shop. 
Im very glad to have visited.

Title: Huge Museum, but don't expect european quality
Text: When we visited the museum was crowded with Sri Lankan students and it was great to see how excited they got from the exhibition. There are some interesting pieces and stories, however, there are some irrelevant objects on display as well (like a simple glass with no story whatsoever that looks like you can purchase anywhere). The museum is huge, and you can buy connected tickets to the Natural Museum, so this can be a whole day program. It is worth to visit once, just to understand more the Sri Lankan history and heritage, but I wouldn't go back for a second round. Make sure to bring water with you, as there is only option to purchase once you come out of the building.

Title: Interesting!
Text:
The Colombo National Museum can be found opposite Viharamahadevi Park and you will need a couple of hours to look around both buildings. The main part of the museum is a grand colonial style building which was built in 1877.

There is an entrance fee and you get shown into the first building which is all about nature and how things grow etc in Sri Lanka. There is also a large dinosaur skeleton to see at the end of this building before you are shown to the main building.

This building is full of artefacts such as art, weapons, furniture , paintings etc. to see and plenty of staff about to answer your questions , if you have any.

There is a café and gift shop in the grounds and the gardens are which are well kept by the staff. An enjoyable visit which takes about a couple of hours and gets one away from the humidity and heat!

Title: Whole story in one building
Text:
The Best out of many museums in Lanka. Extended collection of art, textile, arms, money etc. Helpful staff! 

By the way, the building was found in 1877 and it is still in a perfect condition.

Title: Nice visit
Text:
Nice visit in the afternoon when it's very hot.
It takes around 90 min,2 floors, then there is a coffee shop

Title: National Museum
Text: Founded in 1877 is the national museum which houses artifacts spanning the history of Sri Lanka.  The two story structure is houses a rich history of covering a period of 2500 years and includes important collections including the throne and crown of the Kandyan monarchs.  There are three main sections including natural science, cultural and a library.  Signs direct you through the maze of rooms which are cooled with large fans--ther is no air conditioning.  Guards sit at the entrance of many of the rooms.  The museum opens at 9am and closes at 6pm.  There is a small fee for entrance.  Next door is the Laksala Government Gift Shop which houses a huge variety of Sea Lankan art work and souvenirs and the prices are very reasonable.  Plan on spending about 1-2 hours if you visit all of the rooms.

Title: Nice museum
Text: The museum is accomodated in a great white house. They have plenty of rooms with a lot of differented topics. It's specially nice if you bring a visit after you made your roundtrip. You will recognize more. Definitely worth a visit!

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
Housed in a beautiful old mansion, the Colombo National Museum is definitely worth a visit. Each room has a different collection of artifacts, beginning with pre-history and ending with a farming/agricultural models. These two are probably the least interesting, although the models are quite lifelike compared to some we've encountered in other countries. The weapons, clothing and costumes, jewellery, pottery, ivory, stone statuary and a fine collection of stone urinals kept us engaged for some time.

The chitty system at the entrance was in full sub-continental swing. It is non-air conditioned, but is not too hot due to high ceilings, fans and open doors.

Title: Magnificent building and world class art.
Text: I loved my afternoon at the National Museum. There was a tremendous amount of information, and everything was beautifully displayed. I especially enjoyed the bronzes and sculptures from the 8th and 9th centuries and the traditional Sri Lankan masks. I have to say that its pretty hot though - there are fans but not air conditioning. Take plenty of water!

Title: More than a bit dusty, Kandy is better
Text:
Once you get past the pre-historic displays (skip) and past the hordes of school children, there is some good stuff here, but it is limited in my view. Enjoy the Buddha statues and related stuff, but it goes downhill from there in my view. Yes it is the national museum in the capital so it has an encyclopedic collection, but unless you want to see every old farm tool in often not very well lit displays, you can really speed up. I was time-limited anyway, but seriously an hour was enough for a visit. Yes it is an old building, so lacks a/c, and route is one way to upstairs then out on side of building.

The price had gone up from guidebook 600r. to 1000r. and as it is a national museum that sounds OK, as likely all tourists will go. However the museum in Kandy is much better value in my view- a much more compact and curated collection. The highlights of this one really, and very presented and lit, despite guidebook comments that it was like Colombo, dusty, unlit etc.

Title: I should visit it again
Text: Unfortunately, when I arrived around 5 pm, this place was closed but I liked the souvenir shop which was open. The architecture of the place is really nice....Next time I will try to go early to be able to enter the museum.

Title: History History and more History.
Text:
Well first off the building has no AC.   Dress appropriately.    The building contains statues, art, coins, and facades from centuries ago.    

You will be immersed in what it meant to in the area long ago.   

The Natural History Museum is behind the main building and in my opinion not worth the entry fee and could be overlooked.

You will pay more than the locals but still the price was not awful.    My biggest fear in seeing all the antiquities was that the unmitigated heat and humidity will denature the quality of the artifacts contained inside the museum.

Title: Interesting tour
Text:
We did a city tour by tuktuk and this was one of the places the driver took us to.
It was a really interesting visit with lots of facts throughout the ages of Sri Lanka including masks, clothing, jewellery, coins, artefacts and the different countries to have ruled. Well worth a visit to find out the background and history of Sri Lanka.

Title: Colonial building but socialistic service
Text: Good choice to visit this Museum, nice colonial building, but inside is hot hot and hot, exponates are chaotic collected on many places, many "Educative" models are without reality. Bookstore is poor and not interesting, cofee/tee is far and by the exit is the "restoran" for local people only with higher prices for foregners. Totaly full joke is the Museum of Nature, only the whale skeleton is remarcable, other exhibitions (except geology) are poor full of mistakes and Mme Tussaud Animals... No more frineds.

Title: Amazing Architecture, lacks delivery
Text:
The museum is a lovely old building with a nice coffee shop out back to relax after walking round the mueseum. There are plently of things on display.
Im giving it an average overall because there is zero effort from the museum to explain anything or try create an educational experience to learn about the country and history. 
Everything is there to see, and there is loads of it. Its just my opinion is should be presented to visitors better.

Title: no good official guide but worth a visit
Text: This is a beautiful place. The museum has a good collection of historical artifacts, however without a good guided tour, sometimes it is difficult to understand much.  We tried asking for an official guide of the museum, but the lady was not much keen on telling us about the things on display. Basically she only walked with us through the halls.

Title: A Great Museum
Text: The National Museum has a great collection of historical items, well displayed in a purpose-built colonial building. Exhibits are well described in Sinhala, Tamil and English. There is an excellent cafe.

Title: Check it out
Text: Interesting old colonial type building with lots of artefacts and informative displays depicting Sri Lankan history and culture. It wont take long to take this in, maybe just as well, no a/c

Title: a beautiful colonial building with a wonderfully collated exhibition
Text: With a spare afternoon we visited the museum and spent an interesting and worthwhile time. The building itself is worth the visit but the exhibits cover everything from early history, religious artifacts and art, Royal regalia costumes, jewelry , China glassware and all manner of fascinating items from the countrys historical and colonial past. A great museum shop and cafe for a midway refreshment.

Title: Good museum depicting Sri Lankan culture and hostory
Text:
Well signposted once inside. Foreigners pay 1000 rupees for visit. Exhibits are on two floors. No lift. My elderly mother struggled to go upstairs . Many chairs scattered around so that she could sit when tired. Lots of Buddhist items from Pollannaruwa  and Anuradhapura bronze statues stone items paintings . Museum
Not air conditioned and toilet facilities in another block. Small basic canteen serving rice and curries drinks and snacks

Title: The museum is nice but old
Text: You can enjoy new information yet it feels more like a school field trip. Its a Rich culture and a must see

Title: Beautiful museum
Text: Beautiful museum with good layout of displays-  in time order then upstairs is grouped by artefact type. You can get a ticket for just this museum or also the natural history one, which is more like a school biology level.

Title: Beautiful old building and worth the visit
Text: I'm not one who generally enjoys museums but this one I did.The buildings themselves were beautiful and well maintained.Each room held a different collection so you walked from one to another not getting bored.Plenty to see and more to see outside.Worth the visit just to see the buildings

Title: Interesting museum
Text: This museum has no air conditioning, only fans.  It was quite hot.  Some of the exhibits seemed a little tired and needed refurbishing.  There are no restrooms in the museum.  The ones on the grounds are only squat toilets.  There were some nice artifacts in here, and also some nice paintings.  Not the best museum I was ever in.

Title: Good museum?
Text: Very elegant building with 15 rooms displaying history and development of Sri Lanka. Good signage and information. Only disappointment was lack of 19th and 20th century information unless I missed it.

Title: Good museum!
Text:
I wasn't sure if I should invest time there because of the mixed reviews here. 

I really enjoyed the exhibits, the setup and the explanations. Most museums in Asia are not as informative or well done as people from the West are used to. So, the exhibits and everything needs to be seen in context. Overall, it a very good museum that gives an insight into the history, culture, tradition and people of Sri Lanka. As this was my first visit in the country and since I know India very well as I live(d) there for years, I truly appreciated the museum and recommend it.

Title: Intetesting insight into Sri Lankan history and culture
Text: Intetesting insight into Sri Lankan history and culture. Lovely building and some interesting well layed out exhibits. Expensive as all tourist attractions are in Sri Lanka to foreigners but worth a visit. Colombo is not filled with attractions so this rates highly.

Title: Helpful for context
Text: As with all museums, the exhibitions for local information help with understanding the country. Not overly busy ( Sunday visit). Lunch at the little canteen was affordable and  tasty.

Title: Serendipitous visit Colombo Museum
Text:
In May 2018, I visited the museum with  my husband Radha and Bhante Sujato, who has deep interest in Buddhist texts, a scholar of Early Buddhism and the project lead for suttacentral.net, a website dedicated to Buddhist scripture in 40 languages. There were not many people or school groups, so we had the place to ourselves. 
In room two we found a well preserved manuscript of the Cullavagga written during King Parakkamabahu II who was the King of Dambadeniya in the 13th century, he ruled from 1234 to 1269. 
Bhante Sujato recognised this to be the oldest original manuscript in the world. Like this there were so many unique and little known treasures scattered across the place. If you are in Sri Lanka dont miss the national museum

Title: Not bad
Text: This museum was not the worst we have been to. It is large with a lot of stone relics to see. It is very structured and tourists are expected to follow a pre destined route. There are often school children here which can make for a very loud experience. The tourist price is 1200 rupees for both museums (natural and historical)  and 1000 rupees for just the history museum.

Title: Best collection of hand painted masks
Text: Well preserved and tastefully renovated with a small cafeteria and a nice laksala store close by, worth a visit for history and culture buffs. I loved the stories that came with the traditional srilankan masks, clothes , weapons and utensils

Title: Exceptional recording and display of Sri Lankan hostory
Text:
Firstly a warning : you need at least 2 or 3 hours to do it justice!
The history of SL is recorded with in meticulous detail with a room/hall representing the various eras. Information is presented clearly and thoroughly in each room and for each section. Well preserved artifacts are on display and some stunning artwork and crafts. 
When you come from a country which only really has well -recorded history going back less than 400 years, it is humbling to literally walk through 3000 years of social, economic and spiritual development. 
I left feeling I was visiting a proud nation.

Title: Rip off prices for tourists
Text:
Like every temle, museum, library, park and national monument in Sri Lanka...there is a cost for tourists and a cost for locals. The prices charged for tourists, with no discounts for say a family of four...makes about $100++ for everything you want to see. The disparity makes you feel like a walking ATM...even a roti shop..our tuk tuk driver took us insidemhis favorite shop...the cashier asked who the food was for..for us? ...the foreigner? Yes! So then the store owner recalculated the cost of roti...a small simple local filled bread..and charged us triple the amount! So from museum to roti shop...to a hamburger at the airport on your way out..$18.95 USD!
Be prepared to feel ripped off...your travel $ wont take you far...as for this museum..we viewed it from the outside...we spent the money with cocktails in a famous hotel surrounded by antiques instead. Until the Sri Lanka government changes this disparity of tourists paying more and the locals charging more ..even of bananas...it all adds up to people leaving the island feeling ripped off..or as another tourist told me..the feeling of sadness in the heart to be treated like that NATIONWIDE!

Title: Nice museum
Text: We visited the Colombo National Museum on a recent cruise call to Colombo. The museum is housed in a very attractive building but unfortunately there is no air conditioning. We enjoyed seeing the murals from the Citadel of Sigiriya (I would have loved to have visited Sigiriya). There are some very interesting and attractive exhibits - worth a visit if you have time.

Title: Very interesting.
Text: Very interesting.  Not airconditioned so a little uncomfortable and we wondered how they would preserve the artworks in the humid temperatures. However, the timeline for Sri Lanka was fascinating.

Title: Worth the Trip
Text: With so much else to do in Colombo, you might think the National Museum should be skipped. You would be wrong. The free WiFi at the Museum Cafe had me sold. Plus, the haggle free gift shop, next door, had almost everything I needed.  The museum itself can be done quickly or you can read everything and take a much longer time.  If you know very little about Sri Lanka and its history, start here!

Title: Extensive
Text: Covers all aspects of Sri Lankan history with art, sculpture and artifacts in a very large collection. Well worth a visit.

Title: Needs modernization
Text: Beautiful colonial style building showcasing the british opulence of the time but nothing has been upgraded for many decades. Artifacts need to be better showcased and lighting improved. No toilets in the whole building.

Title: Bit dry
Text: We visited here one afternoon and only stayed for less than an hour (We didn't go round the whole mueseum). There are some interesting statues/artefacts but the captions etc are all a bit dry and uninteresting.

Title: Very fine.
Text:
Huge colonial building in imposing grounds.
The huge reception rooms make a good museum space and some of the countries treasures should not be missed. A super throne etc etc
Pity there is little history available of this splendid building.

Title: superb Must see
Text: A good 1.5 hour is useful for this very rich museum presenting collections form the whole island, with paintings, scuptures and many photos of places to be later visited. entrance 1000 rupees, no photo fee.

Title: An amazing museum that should not be missed
Text: Not only is the building spectacular, but the museum has an amazing selection of Sri Lankan historic artifacts and artwork.  It is not airconditioned but many fans help in hot weather.  There are a couple of coffee shops, one in front of the tourist shop which is also worth a visit.

Title: Historic museum well laid out
Text:
Designed and built as a museum and expanded several times to house the growing collections of antiquities this place is a must visit.  The building itself is a great example of colonial Dutch architecture and each of the expansions carries the same feel.

The collection is vast and is well displayed and curated. Well worth the 1000 LKR entry.

Title: Gateway to History
Text: This place acts as a gateway to Sri Lanka's history. There are lot of artifacts to see, all divided by sections. Must visit!

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Visited here recently on a tour of the country. The place is filled with interesting artifacts and was pleasantly cool which was a bonus given the temperatures outside. Allow about an hour for your visit.

Title: disappointingly old fashioned
Text:
The museum is in a beautiful building that has recently been renovated. The layout is very old fashioned - you can not just go to the rooms that interest you,
 you need to follow the trail IKEA style - but unlike IKEA there are no short cuts! You are going to see prehistoric rock formations whether you want to or not. 
The entry fee for tourists is high and does not represent value of any kind. As other reviewers have said - the written descriptions either don't exist are so long winded and are so poorly written you give up the will to live. The one interactive display (of paddy field irrigation) was not working. There is no air conditioning only fans - pointed firmly at the exhibition staff - so the whole experience is quite draining. 

The textiles area has beautiful embroideries and historic costumes - delightful if under explained. We would have enjoyed looking at the crafts and jewelry more thoroughly (they have a fabulous collection) but these were housed in one of the later rooms and by that stage we were too exhausted. 

At the end of your visit you are rewarded with 2 restaurants. One is very much for the locals the other for 'pigeons' - this is what tourists are called.

Title: Excellent
Text:
This museum is full of well presented treasures offering an interesting insight to Sri Lankas history. 
A wonderful building kept in excellent condition
Well worth a visit

Title: Interesting exhibits
Text: Much more than what we expected - many galleries with interesting exhibits. Had to rush through as it closed at 5pm.

Title: A great overview of Sri Lankan history
Text:
Worth a visit, but allow sufficient time to meander through the two stories of galleries.  It's hot, cooled only by odd fans turned towards the attendants' chairs, but the displays are fascinating.

Chairs for the hot and weary would be a great improvement!

Title: Mixed fare, but a must see
Text: It's a large museum, so needs time and energy. You have to go there if you have gone to SL for more than the beaches and the food! We noted some very interesting displays,and also, of course, one or two dreary sections

Title: very knowledgeable  place
Text: very knowledgeable  place , special for all school children .. in this place we can learn about sri lankan culture

Title: Overpriced
Text: As is the case for many tourist destinations in Sri Lanka, tourists get charged an extortionate fee compared to locals (1000lkr V 100). I personally didn't think it was worth it; considering you can go to far more high tech and interactive museums for free in the UK. I did learn some things especially about Sri Lankan history, but there was often just far too much writing that you just gave up. Wouldn't recommend for children as is not interactive at all. Definitely not a must do.

Title: Great museum
Text: Well worth a visit. We spent 3 hours there. So much to see on several floors.Excellent. It was very informative and enlightening.

Title: Impressive!
Text: Impressive and beautiful collection, definitely worth the price and visit. Bought a joint ticket with which you can visit the museum of natural history as well.

Title: Can skip
Text:
I love visiting museums around the world and maybe this is what I am comparing to so have traveled to over 70 counties around the world so I usually will go to the national museum 

This unfortunately was one that actually is done quite poor and not fun at all 

It was not done well at all , not informative the collection was not displayed well , not very informative not interesting at all in my opinion 

So my verdict is there is so much more to do in this beautiful country like going to Galle . kandy , visiting tea plantations

Title: Very good intro to the rich history of Sri Lanka
Text: For those who don't know much about this South Asian country, the Museum is a great place to start getting acquainted with its people, history, and culture and to be awed by its enchanting arts and crafts.  The only drawback, especially for seniors, is the absence of lifts.  An introductory leaflet would be useful, too.

Title: Informative museum
Text: Was very impressed with the range of exhibits and the quality of the information at the museum. Would recommend at the beginning or end of a Sri lankian trip. The museum building itself is beautiful.

Title: Whole history in one place
Text: History of Sri Lanka from ancient times. Each hall presents different periods. Many exhibits and descriptions. All descriptions are in English. Museum is on 2 floors. Entrance ticket is 1200 rupees.

Title: Colombo museum
Text:
You must experience this place. Under funded third world and run down. Some of the artifacts are amazing and ancient. The museum consists of multiple buildings surrounded by old trees. Some displays have never been updated and some children would find the paintings and displays laughable. Other buildings house some absolutely ancient artifacts. Admission is minimal and photography is an extra 40cents. Well worth a visit to see early history.
In the street on the South side are framed paintings of local artists if you want some original work to take home. On display 10am till 4pm. Check the pencil figure on the back for the local price.

Title: Some lovely examples of history, art and craft.
Text:
I went to this museum today and was immediately impressed by the presentation of exhibits in this huge old building of many beautiful objects from Sri Lanka history.  Most foreigners visiting here will learn something and the locals I met while walking through the exhibits were also impressed. Buddhists and art lovers are well catered for but If you are part of the instant information generation [google style] you may find it a bit of an effort so best you stay away. If you can appreciate a culture through it's artifacts and visual history then this museum will not disappoint you.     
I would like to say to Tripadvisor that the questions at the end of this review[ and others I have filled out lately] do not make sense - surely you have data that enables you to ask more relevant questions?

Title: A great introduction to Sri Lanka
Text: As museums go in developing countries this is a great one! Lots of exhibits with English explanations. Some lovely dioramas on the upper floor. Cool and roomy. And a great shop and cafe outside with decent toilets. The gifts in the shop were very reasonably priced.i bought a sunhat for £2!

Title: Masks and more...
Text: The collection includes murals from Sigiriya, traditional masks, a coin collection, and Buddhist artifacts.  Surprisingly the museum is not climate controlled.  Check with your hotel when they are open, the hours posted are well shall we say aspirational.  Worth an hour or two to visit.

Title: Good to do a rainy day
Text: We were just outside of the museum. Looks nice, didn't had enough time to visit it unfortunately. The security was good. If it rains maybe come here?

Title: Comprehensive summary of preindependence history of SriLanka
Text: It is a very well stocked museum displaying various artifacts of preindependece history of SriLanka. It takes us through various ages, kingdoms and civilisations. It is very good start point for exploring SriLanka. Based on the information gathered here, one should select and then visit original places in different parts of SriLanka.

Title: This country has a wonderful history, but so much is not told here
Text: Having visited this city many times. I now ( with my husband) visited this museum. It was great to find out what happened up until Sri Lanka becme a British Colony, but then ver little. I would have wanted to know a lot more about the what happened then!!!!

Title: Well maintained!
Text: Quite well maintained! Sections well organised. Gets a bit warm suggest carrying water bottles & a hand fan.

Title: Quite interesting
Text: For those interested in museums, this one offers quite an array of historic and cultural displays. Just a word for the wise, it's not air conditioned but has some fans in place!

Title: One of the best developing nation national museums I've ever seen.
Text: The National Museum building could use a little TLC but it's contents and presentation are amazing under the circumstances.  Well maintained and curated.  All signage in 3 languages (including English).  SLR1000 for foreigners to get in.  The history and culture of Sri Lanka/Ceylon from 5/6th century BC to today on display.  Strong recommendation as a Must See.

Title: Colombo at it's best
Text:
The Colombo National Museum is well worth a visit, takes you for about 2hrs back in time and away from hustle and bustle of Colombo City
the museum is huge and I think it is necessary to focus on the Hightlights, a audioguide is available but I preferred to walk just through and stop at fascinating exhibits....I came during morning and the place was full of school classes, so maybe afternoons are better
leave time for a walk through the well tended grounds

Title: Colombo National Museum
Text: Well presented tour of the artefacts through the ages relating to Sri Lanka, starting with prehistoric periods. Housed in former Governor's mansion which in itself is interesting to visit.

Title: Excellent
Text: Hi good evening friends, look great, u cant help but I think we should do eating in like crab and dinner.

Title: knowing culture of Sri lanka
Text: This museum has complete all aspects of Sri Lanka's culture and heritage. The local guide is so friendly. Good for foreigner who has limited time staying in Colombo

Title: Beautiful Place
Text:
It reflects Sri Lanka history...
Its a must see place in Colombo...
You might take some photos, have some coffee or enjoy a walk around...

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
I have visited many museums in India and UK, and this one was worth a visit.

Located in the heart of Colombo, in the busy streets, spread across acres of land. Has a great banyan tree at the entrance atleast 500 year old.
It will take half a day to complete the museum, entrance fee for locals is 30 lkr and for foreigners it's 1000 lkr. 
Has a wide varieties of collection from paleolithic age to Mesolithic age to neolithic age till modern era. Articrafts and works of Srilankan native can be seen. 

Neatly maintained and very informative. Stored in a magnificent and vast building. 

Worth a visit. If u are staying at Colombo on your tour plan then definitely visit this place. And it ll make your day.

Title: A Grand Olde Building
Text: A wonderful building and the displays and exhibits are for the most part good and the descriptions good. The cultural exhibits need replacing.  I was there in May and is very hot and humid and you are soaked to the skin in 5 minutes. No way to AC a building like this. Did have a dreadful time with the police and army guards they are abusive and nasty. They wanted us to leave all our belongings after inspecting thoroughly and had no place to lock them up so my wife didn't enter the museum. They did not even offer her a chair telling her to leave as she waited for me.

Title: Great Place
Text: It is a great place to know about the history of the island. Although it takes time to go through all the period sections  yet it is interesting.

Title: History
Text: The biggest museum in island country is located in down town and have lot to offer. Specially their history of their colonial days and freedom struggle.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
Really puts you in the picture of where Sri Lanka was placed within the world, over the centuries. It has lots of amazing architectural remnants which have commonalities with other parts of the world. There are pottery, jewellery and money from places as far away as ancient Greece, Rome, China and old Arabia showing how paths crossed.

If you are into ancient weapons you may notice influences of ancient Greek Kopis and Indonesian Pistol grip daggers.

There is also quite  bit of the Portuguese, Dutch and British colonial stuff here, as well.

Theres lots of technological displays for example and ancient burner that uses hydraulic principles to control burn and also some stuff on how the ancient lakes were built and why the majority are still functional without suffering erosion.

What threw me was that Sri Lanka was producing STEEL in the iron age!! 

Expect nearly a full day here if you are a museum geek like me.

Title: lots to see but ancient style museum!
Text: A modern curator would shudder at the lack of any environmental control and/or explication in this museum.  You will feel you have traveled back to the time of Victoria.  Dust, heat, smoke drifting through the halls, but a treasure trove of neat stuff.  Worth a visit but bring a guidebook that will give you some context for what you will see

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Excellent range of exhibits tracing Sri Lankan history and I strongly recommend a visit for an appreciation of the growth and development of Sri Lanka.  Generally well maintained but very disappointing to see that metalic exhibits have not been preserved with Museum Wax. Iron and steel exhibits in particular e.g weaponry are rusting to oblivion before the curator's eyes.

Title: Stunning
Text: A look into the past of srilanka and its many culture and religions. The museum is well maintained with a small cafe . The museum wont ket you visit the second floor after 4 pm so plan accordingly.

Title: Excellent
Text:
Impressive building. Well kept. Clean. 
Lots of history. Worth visiting. At the heart of the city 
It takes about three hours to tour the Museum

Title: Solid National Museum
Text: This is a good place to go for an overview of Sri Lankan history.  Lots of the better artifacts from the main sites like Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa are actually here.  Not too pricey and in a beautiful colonial building to explore.

Title: Absolute gem of Sri Lanka
Text: So many beautiful antiquities, artworks and important historical artefacts on display.  Please allow at least 90 minutes as there is so much to see there.  The museum building itself is stunning.  An absolute must to visit in Colombo.  So glad I visited the museum.

Title: So-so experience
Text: Being a museum fan and having been to museums in several parts of the world this one fails to impress. Also the entry tickets aren't exactly cheap and there's no place to stop and ponder on the collections by sitting anywhere. Some of the paintings seem worn out and badly maintained.

Title: Hot, humid and shadowy but deserves better!
Text: This museum  deserves better. The priceless exhibits deserve better lighting and conditions for those visiting. A few floor fans aimed at attendants is understandable but to the visitor is typically unable to concentrate on exhibits in comfort and so move on without gaining a full appreciation of the displays. Needs a refurbishment to demonstrate the history and culture of Sri Lanka in the style it deserves.

Title: Pretty good museum
Text: I was surprised to see the way they have maintained this museum. It is a must visit place for any visitors, easily it would take 3 to 5 hours to see the place, depending on your interest level. The collections were awesome.

Title: An Exposure to the History and Culture of Sri Lanka
Text: This for us The National Museum is a must visit.  It is a well laid out museum that takes the visitor through various epochs in the history of the country.

Title: Sri Lanka History - all in one place. A must see.
Text: Time well-spent here. A marvellous collection of ancient Sri Lankan culture and history. The Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa sections were superb. Ancient collections of jewellery, pottery, costumes, masks, etc were insightful. Reserve an entire morning or afternoon for the museum. We missed the natural museum as we ran out of time.

Title: Historically fascinating place!
Text: The Colombo National Museum building is historically fascinating, its a huge white colonial mansion with well-maintained large courtyard and balconies. The place is quite big and allowed plenty time to explore and enjoy. Inside of it contains all manner of art, carvings and statuary from ancient past of Sri Lanka, and swords, guns and other paraphernalia from the colonial period as well. The collection is well presented and of course impressive. This is one of perfect places in Colombo to visit for the tourist.

Title: Worth a visit.
Text:
This is worth a visit. It's well signed inside and takes the tourist through the ages of Sri Lankan history. There are some interesting pieces to see. Take your time and sit down when you can. You can take photos.

Great value, the revered tree outside is astonishing. This is ideal for children as well .

Title: Very interesting and well laid out
Text: Have spent 10 days in Sri Lanka we decided to visit the national museum on our final day in the country. The museum is very well laid out and details the history of the country over time from ancient civilisations to British rule and the return to Sri Lankan independence. This should be a must see site for any tourist visiting Colombo

Title: Sri Lankan history
Text:
Dear all if you're going to visit sri lanaka you must visit Colombo national museum 
Because you can see all Sri Lankan historical things and ancient things there
You need to take a ticket to enter 
You have nice parking space as well 
This is one of perfect places in Colombo

Title: comprehensive history
Text: Housed in a lovely building surrounded by well maintained grounds. This museum offered a concise but comprehensive history of the country. Displays and artefacts are easily viewed and accompanied in 3 languages. Outside is a cafe and a large,air con, well stocked gift store which surprisingly is not way over priced.

Title: Well curated collection within a nostalgic colonial building
Text: The collection is well presented and range is impressive. The building itself is historically fascinating: huge white colonial mansion with courtyard (unfortunately not accessible for visitors) and balconies. The place is quite big and follows a oneway system, allow generous time to explore and enjoy.

Title: A bit of disappointment
Text: The place Looks promising from a distance but hardly anything inside. Disorganized and messy. Construction and painting works restricts the smooth movement of tourists. Appeared like the museum of a zoology department of a science degree college. Highly priced entry tickets for visitors as well as their vehicles.

Title: Beautiful museum
Text: An impressive collection covering millennia of Sri Lankan history.  Well laid out and easy to wander through,  trilingual text panels make for an easy read for English speakers.  Upper floor can get quite warm in the afternoon, so be prepared and hydrate.

Title: Great museum
Text: Very good museum, spacious, clean and very informative for all things SL. Would definitely visit again

Title: Perfect place to learn Ceylon history
Text: The museum contain lots of artifice and descriptions is clear in English.  Worth the visit but natural museum? Please pass it. Unless the open the sperm whale bone to public.

Title: Great insight into Sri Lankan history and culture
Text: One of the best museums I've seen in the country. The exposition is perfectly arranged a clear path through the rooms and all texts in multiple languages. Pictures are allowed and the staff is very friendly. I have learned a great deal about the country, it's history and culture. Nevertheless, I was missing an overview with the countries timeline and more intimation about the recent times.

Title: An interesting collection worth a visit
Text: We enjoyed a slow wander around the collection in this fine colonial building that houses artifacts and treasures from Sri Lanka's long history and archeology. Most items are displayed reasonably well with descriptions that help. Most certainly worth a visit.

Title: It's ok
Text: The organisation of the artefacts could be better as you can see the potential for it to become great.  It lacks information and a sense of history.  Curators would add to create a sense of history and enthusiasm for Sri Lankan history in all its contexts.  The rich and diverse aspects of Sri Lankan history is yet to be a wow factor in the museum

Title: Oldschool but very nice museum
Text:
This museum woke up my schooltime memories. It looks like from 80s. But I liked it a lot. 
For entrance fee 1000 ruppies you will actualy get access to 2 museums. One is full of historical artefacts, second is more focus on natural treasures. See photos- one picture worths thousand words

Title: Ok place
Text:
Visited this museum on 1st May 2018,
This museum has all interesting details about the evolution of mankind and lots of details of how the early generations moved across the continents.

They play a short movie at the entrance right side.

The entry ticket is 1200 LKR for foreigners.

Title: City tour
Text:
Very knowledgeable thing you can see there in Museum 
Many historical things you can see there 
Very helpful staff on duty there to assist you

Title: Too hot to enjoy
Text:
This museum is gorgeous the building is magnificent and the artifacts are interesting however it is so hot inside it is hard to stay long enough to enjoy anything .
They have pedestal fans but are generally pointed at the staff that work there and not enough to cool you down.
They had also recently painted some fixtures and it was still wet but no wet paint signs were put up and I had black paint on my legs.

Disappointed that I couldnt enjoy the history here as it was just too hot to bare.

Title: Mixed bag of exhibitions worth a visit
Text: The National Museum is housed in a massive building with huge halls and you really need a couple of hours to see everything. Some of the displays are dusty and dated, but numerous exhibition areas were refurbished just a few years ago  lots of English language display descriptions that helped us put the artifacts into historical context, from the earliest human settlements, rule by kings, various invasions and occupations, and eventually independence. Huge collections of coins, pottery, religious items, Stone sculpture, and everyday items from across the ages. If you heading for any of the historic/cultural sites across Sri Lanka, this is a good orientation to when the sites were in use and why they were important at the time Just a minor complaint, very little signage to help visitors move from gallery to gallery, its not always clear where to go. Fortunately, there is a guard in almost every hall who can point the way.

Title: Interesting Architecture
Text: It is worth visiting the building to see the 1877 architecture, even if you don't specifically tour the museum. There is a statue of the museum founder, Sir William Gregory, in the grounds and a spectacular banyan tree. There is also an excellent state-run gift and jewellery shop and a cafe, which are all worth a visit. 30-45 minutes without a museum tour.

Title: Interesting history
Text: We enjoyed a day sightseeing, as part of our cruise. Vibrant place with some great buildings. Hot and humid walking around, so take a towel.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Visited here as part on our Colombo tour and enjoy it, well worth a visit . Well laid out with plenty to see.

Title: If you have time, it will be good to see
Text: National museum in every country should be one of the best point of attraction to visit. this museum is to visit by every one. some part of it is even interesting for children

Title: Wow tack some time out
Text:
This is a great museum and worthy of your time to explore and gain an in depth understanding of the Sri Lankan history and culture.  What a wonderful country.

Oh there is a decent coffee shop close to the exit for those like me love coffee.

Title: History buffs haven!
Text:
Two storeys of 1877 colonial style huge building houses the Museum which has elaborate displays ranging from natural sciences, history and culture. Innumerable artefacts  are indeed enthralling... prehistoric to Kandyan exhibits Ate great. Remember it is a heritage structure so devoid of modern air-con facilities.

A huge outlet called the Souvenir and gift shops has very reasonably priced local stuff. The coffee shop near the billing counter offers discounts on edibles and coffee over the Museum purchases bills.

Title: Educational for visitors
Text:
Located in an imposing colonial building the museum traces the history of Sri Lanka/Celyon from pre-history to recent times.  An excellent collection of artefacts, a very well organised walk through time with an emphasis of the kingdoms up to colonial times.
i was somewhat disappointed that little was said of British colonial times and the following independence and recent history.
Visitors do need to be aware that there is a big difference in entry fees for tourists and locals (fair enough given the wealth difference).  Travel by tuk-tuk is easy from any of the major hotels

Title: Hot but a great introduction to the cultural heritage.
Text:
You can get a ticket for the National museum and the Natural History museum (hidden behind the main museum with no signage!
Wouldn't recommend the Natural History museum as it has very tired looking exhibits in an even hotter environment than the main museum!??.

You need a few hours to take in everything in the National museum. Pause in front of the fans to read the info.

2 minutes is too long in the Natural History museum. Little signage to help you navigate the maze.

Title: History revisited
Text: It should be on the top of your go-to places if you love history. There are various sections in the museum that keep you intrigued and wanting for more.

Title: Must visit if you like history
Text: The place is huge so take some time with you if you plan to visit. Lots to see from different periods of Sri Lankan history.

Title: Can visit if you want some time out of the hot summer weather
Text: The Museum might not have anything special, but its worth a look if you are a museum person, looking at historical artifact. The route and rooms are very well organised and the staff there will direct you in the right direction if you are lost. Well-maintained museum.

Title: If limited on time, skip this!
Text: If you have a full itinerary, I would probably skip this museum. Cost was $8 and I didn't think it was worth it. I spent about an hour inside. The artifacts and paintings were beautiful. It provided a nice history of Sri Lanka but I was really bored for most of it. If you have lots of time in Colombo and LOVE history then you will enjoy it. If you are limited on time, definitely skip it. Bring your camera because the outside is beautiful.

Title: Excellent museum
Text: This museum is very comprehensive in giving a good insight into the development of Sri Lanka. There are a wide range of exhibits with generally good labelling in English. We recommend spending at least 30 minutes each in the first two rooms as this sets the scene for the rest of the exhibition.

Title: Great museum
Text: Well worth a visit and if you have a few hours take your time. There are a huge amount of exhibits but nothing from the 20th century

Title: Visit on Sunday 28th Jan
Text:
This is a large museum on two floors with excellent pieces of ancient and more modern items too. The labelling is generally very good if you speak English. The museum has none of the interactive displays that a modern museum would have but it is still very interesting and well worth a visit.

The authorities need to invest in better facilities.the toilets are appalling and the cafe is poor. Considering the high standard of cafes nearby such as The Commons, I was disappointed.

As an introduction to the culture of the country I think a visit to this place is essential. It is open every day except public holidays. If you buy a ticket you are allowed to exit and return on the same day.

Highlights are the prehistoric tombs, carved stone statues and columns, ceremonial throne and weapons, textiles.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: The Colombo National Museum details Sri Lanka ancient past and it's colonial periods - although it seeks to create the impression was the island was uninhabited before the arrival of the Sinhalese. It is well worth visiting the museum as a prelude to visiting the ancient cities of Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa .

Title: Excellent museum in wonderful colonial building
Text: This was beautifully set up and well worth a trip.  English translation very good and exhibits very interesting.

Title: Give tourself plenty of time here
Text: Amazing. Collection. We did a lot of touring around Sri Lanka and saw plenty of ancient, architectural and archaeological sites. So we went here on our last day in Sri Lanka to help tie everything together. However, people say it's a great intro cultural  collection to the country. But also a nice farewell.

Title: Brief history of Sri Lanka and some nice items on display
Text: If you are interested in the history of Sri Lanka, you should go the this museum. It will provide you with a brief introduction on the country and her history. Note: the recent history is not really added to the collection (yet). Beautiful building and gardens around the museum. Note: entrance ticket: price seems to be flexible.

Title: Large museum in old building
Text: Large museum in impressive old building with nice grounds. Displays were well laid out and sign posted to walk around in order. Was hot inside the museum and the toilets were outside.

Title: Average; foreigners, beware!
Text:
Visited this place when I had a few hours to kill in Colombo.

The entrance fee of Rs.1000 was too high in my opinion.

The collections of the museum vary from very average to somewhat interesting.  Some more contemporary displays would have been nice.

Foreigners: beware of the cafeteria.  I asked for a chocolate drink that I was told cost Rs.150.  Paid 500, but was shortchanged by 100.  I had to ask for this extra money. Moreover, upon finishing the drink, I noticed it was labelled 50, not 150.  Again, I had to request that I be given an extra 100 back that I was duly owed.  The two apologies from the cashier were very insincere, and it is therefore regrettable to experience the extent to which they went to try and rip me, a foreign tourist, off.  This is from a government owned museum.  Shameful.

Upon leaving, I was asked to complete a survey.  Apparently staff members within the exhibitions are meant to chat to you about their various displays, however, I can only say this was the case with 1 single staff member!

Nevertheless, the woman conducting the survey was very friendly, and provided me with very detailed instructions on taking the bus back to my hotel.  This was a very positive note to end on.

Title: Interesting ride through history
Text: The museum is in an impressive old building and grounds. Inexpensive entry. Linear walk round well presented displays, with some interesting items. Well worth a visit if you arrive in Colombo and before you head out to explore the country and its historical sites. Was quiet when we toured.

Title: Rich collection
Text: Rs. 1000 per person will get you into this stately building and its well organized halls containing a vast collection of artifacts from ancient and colonial history. Unfortunately, it does stop there, and you do not learn about contemporary Sri Lanka. Thankfully, the collection is neatly partitioned thematically and chronologically, so that you can pick and choose--and choose you must!

Title: Lots of history
Text: The Colombo National Museum is a treasure worth visiting. Allow enough time if you like history. 2 stories of treasures about Sri Lanka. The National Museum houses 4,000 palm leaf manuscripts, coins, guns and weapons, art and the history of early man. Worth a visit.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Plenty of historical artefacts to see aswell as beautiful sculptures. The museum has a lot of view and read about.

Title: Start of Sri Lanka Tour
Text:
This was only our 2nd day in Sri Lanka and before we made our way up country it was a chance to understand the early history of Sri Lanka and how some of the places we planned to visit fit together. It was housed in lovely building and was set out with 15 different rooms. It was easy to understand the different periods Sri Lanka has gone through and as we were going to Anuradhapura the next day gave us some ideas what to see including  the early method of irrigation by building 3 tanks.
We spent over 2 hours and really enjoyed it. It cost LKR 1000 for an adult.

Title: Learn the history of Sri Lanka
Text: This is the best place to learn the Sri Lankan history. There are lot of things to read and see over here. I really liked the new room dedicated to the Silk Road and the Chinese Shi dynasty who were originally Sri Lankan who went to to China and settled in. The tour takes around 3 hours and parking is available.

Title: Sri Lankan history
Text: I did enjoy learning more about Sri Lanka by visiting this museum. There's no air conditioner, but fans inside kept the air flowing. Exhibits give a good window into life and culture from prehistoric to near modern times. Scale models also demonstrate the advanced engineering they used centuries ago.

Title: Very average
Text:
By world standards, a very average museum.
We paid 1000 rupee each to visit (tourists pay, locals dont). It's almost an Ikea experience where once you start, you can't get out until you have past everything.
There are 2 buildings in the complex and I would have thought an entrance ticket to the "museum" would have been to both buildings, but no, you then have to pay another 400 rupee to get into the second building.
At the original ticket office, this was not explained where we could have purchased a multi ticket for 1200.
The money was not an issue, basically just a tourist rip-off and we will not be part of it.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Good place to learn more about the history of Sri Lanka. Huge collection of Buddha statues and artefacts with English explanation, house in a beautiful Colonial Style building. Need at least one hour. LKR1000 for one museum and LKR1200 for combination of 2 museums. Really worth a visit.

Title: Lovely building
Text: Quite interesting to see some of the artefacts in the museum. Well layed out and easy to navigate. They have an app you can down load on the museum (but I could only get the begining to work but that is probably my fault as I am not very tech savvy). Wouldn't say it is a must see but we had two days in Colombo so was good to do for 1-2 hours and then visit beautiful Viharamahadevi park.

Title: Definitely worth a visit!!! Beautiful artifacts on display!
Text: Though Colombo is far from the most attractive location in Sri Lanka to visit, don't skip it or at least reserve half a day to visit the National Museum there. There are hardly any museums in the country and those which are there have a limited collection (which isn't always best preserved). Those artifacts which didn't end up in a foreign museum are more or less assembled in the National Museum in Colombo. Therefore one gets the best impression of Sri Lanka's ancient history in Colombo.

Title: Traditional Old-School Museum
Text: The exhibits are quite good in this very traditional museum.  It's not really kid friendly, but history buffs will find it well worth a visit.

Title: Colombo Museum Bemuses Visitors!
Text:
Colombo National Museum is a good start point for knowing Sri Lanka and its history. The Museum is full of artifacts from different Lankan eras. Although I spent 6-7 hours in the Museum and tried to read as many posted placards on history as possible, yet I couldn't get enough of this beautiful country's glorious past and ups & downs over the centuries!!!

Despite the fact that Museum wasn't air conditioned and Sri Lankan sultry weather couldn't be tamed by those old colonial pedestal fans being used inside the museum we still enjoyed the visit and learned a fair deal about Sri Lanka.

Huge collection of Buddha statues, coins, ceramic, daggers, bows & arrows, swords, guns, silverware, jewelry etc lie in wait for admirers and history buffs & students. 

The entry fee SL Rupee 1000/- seem a bit high for one Museum (2nd one is small and not much to see). Museum building is spread over great acreage with its magnificent white color. Lot needs to be done to add beauty and prestige that this Museum deserves. More detail on each item will definitely benefit, and interactive touch screen will help visitors to learn more about Sri Lanka and its history.

However, as it is, it's worth visiting if one is in Colombo! 

?????????????????????????

Title: Interesting exhibits
Text:
We had a couple of hours to spend in Colombo and decided to visit the national museum.   Overall the exhibits are organised well, with good explanations of the different artefacts.  We only had time to cover the ground floor, visiting the Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa era galleries, but there was more than enough here to keep our kids engaged for the time we visited.  We had to promise a return trip to see the rest to get them to leave when our time was up!

Only minor gripe was that the galleries could be better ventilated with more fans.  It could get quite hot in places. 

The museum is convenient to drive to, with good parking on site that was easy to access.

Title: Great Heritage
Text: Great place to learn about Sri Lankan heritage, I highly recommend a visit here. You can learn a lot about Sri Lankan culture and heritage.

Title: nice place to visit but don't regret if u miss it
Text: colombo national museum located in albert crescent road . vast area and has a good collection . to know about country's culture and history - museum is best place .its good , but i don't find it interesting - so i won't regret if i would have skip it .

Title: Hoping for something different - but worth a visit.
Text:
I was keen to learn more about this fascinating country but much of the history on display is about Budda which is pretty much the same story as in all the other Asian Buddhist countries.

Saying this it is still worth a visit as the museum building is beautiful and there are some interesting snippets of Sri Lankan history I enjoyed learning about - cost is very reasonable around $7.

Title: Unexpectedly informative
Text: We arrived at the National Museum from the rear and bought the combined entry tickets at the Natural History Museum. A short walk around that museum made us wonder if we had wasted our money with tired displays of stuffed animals and half the museum seemingly closed off so it was a degree of trepidation that we walked around to the National Museum. However we were pleasantly surprised to find a really good and informative museum. Most of the galleries had been refurbished over the last 10 years and the exhibits and information filled in a lot of gaps from our earlier visits to historic sights in Sri Lanka. Clearly there is a bit more to go though as the final three rooms were back to the Natural History Museum standard, with almost no information on the interesting items in the rooms.  All in all though worth a visit.

Title: Gives a nice overview of Sri lanka's history
Text:
You can find different displays in this musea, statues from all over the country and from different centuries, but also paintings, coins, battle equipment, agriculture equipment, masks.
Done with child who also enjoyed the different rooms

Title: Very good
Text: Nice place that you have to visit when you are in Colombo. It might be a bit boring but it's gives you a better understanding of Sri Lanka and it's history.

Title: Very informative as interesting
Text: The exhibits here provide an insight into more than 2000 years of Sri Lankan history. This provides a great context to understand the country but also displays some incredible objects in every gallery. A rare treat at approx $10.

Title: Interesting for kids and adults
Text:
We passed a fun few hours here with 3 kids (6, 5 and 1). It is a grand building, worth seeing in itself. Tickets were inexpensive (1000 per adult, 500 per child above 6 I think as we only paid for our eldest). Some stairs, not certain if access is easy for wheelchair users on that basis but perhaps there is a lift we missed. 

I loved the textiles and specifically came to view them. The kids were astounded by the stone statuary and we now have a whole new set of bed time questions (are Buddha and God good pals? Who is the eldest? Why do goddesses have 6 arms but I dont?). They had some interesting ceramics but the level of information was frustrating at points. Many items had no age, origin, description etc and it would have been great to know more about how the different pieces of china came to sri lanka. Who used them? Where were the items found? You see lots of more modern copies of the same designs in Sri Lanka...what are the differences in ages and which nationality made the copies?? 
Although, in general, thr museum could provide a lot more information and context for the exhibitions, we still really enjoyed it. There is even a good cafe for sustenance afterwards. Dont miss the rickshaw/cart display outside by the cafe.

Title: Great Variety of Amazing Artefacts
Text: Loved the variety of historical, painting and costume artefacts. Not too busy and lots of information about each area.

Title: Window Into the Past
Text: This a well laid-out display of important parts of  Srilankan history. The display starts from the Paleolithic era and ends at the recent past (1930-1940). The most impressive part for me as a visitor was from the 12th century until colonisation by Portugal. If I remember correctly, there are some stone works in section 3. This area gives a good overview of how and why stone works were important at that time. They has been used largely to store information, for example land ownership, taxation rights, demarcation points and etc. Also, in day to day live (example toilets, baths) .The details, the precision, the tools available and the material used gives an idea about the knowledge level at that time. The adjacent display was based on craft, jewellery,  weaponry and artefacts. There is a small section dedicated for jewellery worn by kings and queens. It is truly breathtaking. The artists have taken extraordinary care to preserve the original structure of gems embedded, they have handmade minute links connected in multiple dimensions. Some of those jewels are currently in fashion but they are nowhere near what was achieved at that time. You have to see it to understand. This whole room contains the Srilankan craft heritage. Since craft and artistic excellence is a demonstration of how advanced the society is, the ordinary population seems to have lived in a sophisticated healthy society during this time. You will have to allocate three hours to view this complete display.

Title: Nice place to visit
Text: Nice place to take some photos and visit the Sri Lanka history... A big big tree live there for more than 100 years.

Title: Beautiful Heritage building and Interesting displays
Text: We enjoyed it here, the museum is very large and extensive with some lovely displays and Interesting history write ups etc. The museum is very well maintained and clean throughout. Lots of school children which was cute but got a bit crowded in particular areas. I would however recommend going to the restroom in your hotel as the public facilities are very poor and very unhygienic and you have to walk all the way outside near the main entrance to access them (so don't lose your entrance ticket). Despite that we enjoyed our time here and would recommend if museums are your thing.

Title: Great stop on tour
Text:
An eclectic mix of things to learn about Sri Lanka. Some great stuff along with the more mundane. Some of the masks were amazing!
Definitely worth a stop.

Title: Interesting building
Text: Interesting building however attractiveness of exhibition can't compete with museums in other places (Europe, US & Canada, Japan).

Title: Lovely renovation of this beautiful building
Text:
Lots of absolutely fascinating artifacts packed into one building. This is a good place to start before touring Sri Lanka, since it will provide some basic information regarding the different empires and their geographies.

As a agricultural geek i was particularly impressed with the working mock-up of the ancient tank system and the sacred harvesting circle, which i was lucky enough to experience in real life during my trip.

Definitely helps to situate some of the sites that you will probably come across during your trip, and even enables us outsiders to consider how history has shaped contemporary Sri Lankan culture. 

Amazing to see the Roman coins and Viking artifacts. Evidence that ancient cultures were strongly interconnected through the Silk Road!

Title: Maze
Text: This is a wonderful museum with a great many artefacts. The only downside is that once you start you have to complete the circuit. There is no way out from the middle. We had a melt down with a child with no way to exit and so had to keep going. With smaller children be sure to carry snacks and water definitely not stroller friendly

Title: Good for history/culture/religion buffs
Text:
We took a tuktuk to the museum, they are quite well-known. Then after that we got on another tuktuk and went to Odel department store which was about 900m-1km away.

There are some exhibits that are more well-maintained and well-lit than others - the weapons/pottery/tools exhibit is renovated and looks good, the rest of the museum is more old but i love the colonial vibe of the building. 

Note that there is no airconditioning, we went on a rainy day so it was alright. 

Im not a history-inclined person so i didnt really enjoy it but those who are will as there is so much explanation to read. Not really kids-friendly though.

I like how the museum flows - they label each exhibit area with numbers and you just follow them, each exhibit has an exit that leads to another (eg. 1- history, 2- culture etc.) and in the end you wind up at the exit which has a nice air conditioned large souvenir shop with benches you can sit and some drinks or light snacks you can order. the toilets at the shop are also not too shabby!!!

Title: Not worth it
Text: I do not recommend visiting the museum. It is very hot there (no AC). The poster are very basic (elementary school science project level in the smaller building). The explanations in the nicer building are not very clear. It takes quite a long time to go around and once you start there is no short cut to finish the visit earlier so you have to go through the whole thing. I did not really learn anything there. Only go there if you do not have anything else to do. On the positive side, the big white building is very pretty.

Title: Avoid - until discriminatory / prejudicial pricing is eliminated!
Text: Excellent collections of art and artifacts depicting the richness of Sri Lankan history and culture, but the discriminatory / prejudicial pricing was horrific! Seeing local students allowed to enter at decent (and fair) prices while foreign students were forced to pay multiples more was a souring experience! Adding insult to injury, wealthy Sri Lankans were afforded entry at small fractions of what foreigners from developing countries (and backpackers on small budgets) were required to pay. This prejudicial - and highly discriminatory -approach to pricing must be discarded in the interest of fairness. Either charge everyone the same price -- or charge nobody anything at all. And if one wishes to discriminate, then do so on the basis of one's ability to pay, allowing individuals to self-report and give what they can. This would be the most fair.

Title: A true yet a sad memory
Text:
The tsunami museum was a great place to visit. But a very sad place. The place had pictures of different incidents during the tsunami and the guide gave us a full detailed explanation as well. 

A sad but a must visit place.

Title: Definately a must do.....bring a tissue  and prepare to tear up!
Text:
A chance to talk to some people who were there.
We had no idea what it was like back home. The media could not possibly portray the terror, grief and sadness.

Title: very moving
Text: worth a visit the man running this should be applauded for his on going determination in making sure the victims are not forgotten

Title: Informative, emotional and a must
Text:
When visiting Hikkaduwa a visit here I simply a must.
Great info about tsunamis and why, how they occur.
Of course also a lot of pictures from the 2004 tsunami, first wave and the devastation that followed after the second.
Don't miss!

Title: A brave and moving attempt to illustrate the causes and effects of the tsunami
Text:
This small museum contains pictures of the disaster, the aftermath and the beginnings of the recovery work. There is a very full account of the causes of tsunamis and much geographical information . There is also some amazing artwork done by children as part of art therapy treatment and education.

We would have liked more information about the government, NGO and international response and the local and national economic aftermath. However this is a small project started by a remarkable woman who survived the disaster with her 2 year old son
by climbing a  tree. She is a good source of information. 

It is rather extraordinary given the scale of the disaster that the SL government has not established an official museum/ information centre

Title: Excellent exhibition ....well worth a visit
Text: We took a tuk tuk from Coral Sands Hotel return trip driver offered to wait for us 1000 rupee return was about a 5km trip each way, the museum was definitely worth the trip. Manager and staff passionate in sharing the impact of the disaster and the recovery. Lots of photos ( some disturbingly graphic) but they are behind a curtain and staff make sure you are ok with viewing as they are confronting images. Other rooms old explanation re tsunami and pics of the aftermath . Definitely worth a visit if you are in Hikkadua. Will cost 509 rupee entry. They used to just have free entry and a donation box but many Russians never  paid so now they have to have an entry fee.   A really worthwhile visit

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The staff here were so nice and talked to us about the sad event that was the tsunami. Lots of photos and information. We liked that you can donate to the victims who are still suffering now - children who were orphaned etc. Highly worth a visit. There are some horrific photos of the victims but they are covered by a curtain so you can opt not to see.

Title: Big recommendation!
Text: At first the place seemed like a little boring but as we continued, the lovely guide started to tell us the history and stories about the Tsunami. It was super intresting. Big recommendation!

Title: Eye Opening Experience
Text: This is a very sobering and humbling experience. The pictures are very graphic so its definitely not for the faint hearted. The very graphic pictures are behing a curtain so you do not have to look at them if you find it too much. We got a lot of info on what happened and how and what they have in place if it ever happens again. Worth going here to bring you back to earth.

Title: Excellent museum
Text: A must visit to get to know how Tsunamis occur and what devastation they cause.    Very comprehensive insight in to how Hikkaduwa suffered on 26/12/2004.   Very sad,  but the warnings in place now should prevent such a disaster occurring in the future.

Title: Museum
Text:
I found it moving and educational. The staff we great at answering questions. Worth a visit. 
The only thing negative is cost 500 rupees to get in which was fine, she showed us a ticket but you are not given a ticket so I dont know how the money is accounted for as my husband said she put the money straight into her purse and another couples.

Title: Heart wrenching
Text: A simple but powerful museum in memory of all those lives lost during the Tsunami.  Many testimonials and vivid photos.
