Title: A thought provoking display.
Text: This is a really well organized display with good scientific diagrams to explain how a tsunami occurs. The two young guides were  good at telling some of the stories connected to the photos.  The hand-drawn pictures done by the children were, at times touching and also devastating, showing the effect it had on them.... how their lives changed forever, that day.   The Sri Lankans are strong resilient people.

Title: Good collection and stunning images
Text: The tsunami museum has a large collection of photos and stories. It shows what the impact has been on Sri Lanka. The guide told me that she lost family members and that it took a long while to rebuild everything. The images that tend to be shocking are covered with a curtain. So if you do not prefer to see dead bodies, you can refrain from it. In the end you can give a small donation for tsunami awareness. The guide and the museum itself are for free.

Title: A must do when in Sri Lanka
Text:
Heart breaking but incredible. 
Get the tissues ready but also learn how Sri Lanka have recovered and feel inspired.

Title: Highly recommended
Text: When in Galle area, this is a must. You learn so much about the tragedy, how it affected the area and the people here, plus it teaches you what to do in case it happens again. The staff is super friendly and theyll explain everything to you, from how tsunamis form to what to do in case of one. Its heartbreaking but very educational.

Title: Very moving but educational
Text: A very moving display of photos giving you a real insight to the destruction and pain caused by the tsunami. Very sad and somber experience but well worth visiting.

Title: In memory of a tragedy
Text: A stunning photo museum which shows the destructive power of nature. A must visit when you are in the area. Also great additional information by the guide.

Title: Heart breaking, but must see
Text: This education centre teaches you about earth quakes to start with. Then as you travel around the museum you automatically feel fear of what you are about to see next... And what you learn is the great misfortunes these towns have endured and even though there is such positivity here, your heart will be wrenched by the realism of what these families have been through

Title: Informative and emotional
Text: This is a free museum to see the photos of the devastation that the Tsunami caused to the whole country, with informative facts on the causes of the tsunami and how they pulled together to rebuild what had been lost. They do ask for an entrance fee, but we were told by our accommodation that is free but we tipped the equivilant.

Title: Sobering visit
Text: The man who talked us through each room had lost 2 brothers in the tsunami and many friends. The pictures alone were incredible. This organisation does a lot for those victims affected by the tsunami. Entry is 500 per person which is well worth it.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Loads of facts about the tsunami and many photos some graphic of the aftermath. Very sad and very humbling. Was the best experience of the day. Absolutely worth a visit if in the area.

Title: Must visit for respectful travelers
Text: Solemn experience for travelers who want to know how the locals are expressing their grief and recovery.

Title: Humbling
Text: We stopped here on our trip down to Galle and it was most memorable and important part of the day. Very informative and shocking. I was so appalled to see the true figures of the day, the scale of loss in countries other than Thailand and hear how little help they received from outside aid in comparison. The photos really do give you a picture of the devastation caused, especially the covered wall. Both my partner and I was stunned into silence. Absolutely worth the visit and will not take up so much if your day that you cant fit it in along with everything else.

Title: Very informative and emotional
Text: We visited this small museum thinking we knew about the Tsunami of 2014 from the British press. How wrong we were, everything in the UK mainly related to Thailand not the many more thousands of lives lost in Sri Lanka. The young man that talked us through the geology of what occurred and then the human aftermath was very informative and sensitive. The photographs in one room, which are difficult to look at without feeling very emotional, are sensitively covered so you dont just come across them. Very well worth the visit.

Title: A shrine to the lives lost
Text: A small moving museum filled with harrowing images of that day. The owner has rebuilt her home into a small photo gallery and she can explain the day as she recalls.

Title: Really Good but Sad
Text: Amazing photos showing what happened - until you see it you just don't understand the devastation that took place.  so many people lost their lives and homes.  Just hope it never happens again.

Title: Great learning
Text:
Good reminder of that disaster. Made my kids pay attention to the devastation of such a natural disaster. Some photos, esp of corpses, were an awakening to them. 

Use to depend on donations but now they charge 500 rupees per person.

Title: Heartbreaking
Text: We came here in a tuk tuk and arrived at an old worn out building. Inside was full of images and messages from the locals about their missing loved ones. The devistation of the tsunami was truly heartbreaking and touched us emotionally.  Must see.

Title: A must
Text: This place really makes any worries or problems you might have seem childish and insignificant. Very emotional proof that life is so precious.

Title: Sobering
Text:
A small museum with an explanation of Tsunamis and a selection of photographs of the aftermath of the Tsunami that hit Sri Lanka in 2004.

I found chatting to the staff particularly informative

Title: Holiday
Text: Incredibly moving and humbling, so important to recognise how this area is still rebuilding after loosing so much. We are simply guests in this beautiful place and the people entertain visitors every day but still have ghosts at their doors, we must treat with care and respect

Title: A must stop on your trip
Text: We visited the museum early in the morning and were the only people there so we were shown around and given a one on one talk with the lady and gentlemen who run the museum. The pictures don't hold any punches but we didn't expect anything else. We both walked out with a tear in our eye. Please go and see this museum and see for yourself just how the Tsunami devastated this wonderful island.

Title: Very Moving
Text: This is a very small museum but the efforts gone to help people and children be educated is truly admirable. The lady was very informative and was clearly affected with her own experience and I was completely floored by what I saw in the pictures displayed. Sri Lankan people suffered horribly and their resilience is beyond comprehension. Definitely worth visiting and donating to.

Title: Very Humbling
Text:
We visite dhere with 2 of our Sri Lankan friends who remember the tsunami.  It is very well put together and upsetting to remember the devestation and lives lost.  Having said that, it is good to be reminded and pay repect to those affected.   
You must remember to dress properly, remove your shoes and not take photos.  You do not have to view the terrible scenes of dead bodies, this is optional and covered by a curtain so not to upset people.

Title: Thought provoking
Text:
The museum is well laid out and informative but be prepared for the shocking images of the unlucky ones who lost their lives. Hopefully the knowledge gained from this harrowing experience will ensure that if another tsunami were to strike then the people of Sri Lanka will know what to do to save themselves.
The large Buddha shows just how high the wave was and that particular site has a very calm atmosphere.

Title: Terrifying and moving
Text: Perhaps it was because of the western media, or perhaps I was so young, that I missed the devastation on Sri Lanka when the waves hit. I didn't understand the magnitude of the disaster. The museum shows a no holes barred snapshot of that day, the cause, the moment it hit and the aftermath. Moving and saddening, but I feel we should all visit if not only to support the work that the organisation continues to do.

Title: Informative and moving
Text: Saw as part of a tour from New Berlin tours. Left one member of our party in tears. Understated with heartbreaking photographs as well as plenty of information

Title: Very sad but worth visiting
Text: Worth visiting museum with real photos from tsunami affected areas. Very touching and sad but also interesting. Lady which showed us around was able to answer all of our questions in very good English. Excellent. Tickets are around £2 each and also you can make a donation.

Title: So sad.
Text: I have visited SriLanka 13 times, first time 2 years after the Tsunami, and it was only last year I decided to visit the museum because I was afraid of what I would see. The photos are very graphic, as I expected, but it certainly brings it home to you, the  horror of what they went through.   There is also a memorial ( over the road ) to the many who died on the train when it was hit by the huge second wave. Also along the road is the tall Buddha given by the Japanese.  Also not far off the main road, are the new homes built and donated by various countries for those who survived, and did not want to rebuild so close to the ocean.  All very moving and heart wrenching to see.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Its a small museum and packs a punch. The staff are very friendly and on hand to answer any questions (with very impressive English). Its incredibly sad, but educational at the same time. It lays it all out for you in a way that you just dont always see in the media. Definitely worth seeing if you are nearby.

Title: A must see!!
Text:
I bring all of my friends here as I believe it is important for holidaying visitors to understand a little of the areas recent history.
There is no entrance fee but donations help to keep this museum running & help to preserve the information inside.
On the day we visited two very helpful women explained the story behind this tsunami which killed over 35,000 Sri Lankans.

Title: Reality
Text:
This centre an museum brought us back to December 2004 where so many locals and foreigners lost their lives as there was no warning of the impending Tsunami. Thankfully in later times there are now warning buoys placed at sea which are monitored by stations around the world.
This is a sad place as many of the photographs are graphic, as well as the stark reminders of memorials placed upon the beach heads all along the beaches around this area. Many in Sri Lanka have had some relatives lost and never found.

Title: Informative and with dedicated staff
Text: My husband and I visited here two weeks ago. Our young guide was very informative and seemed to really care about the conservation of these wonderful creatures.  The eggs hatch out, and the hatchlings are released back into the sea. Injured giant turtles are also cared for here, by staff that seem genuinely caring and kind.  Well worth a visit.

Title: Just Go - You Really Have To - Show Some Solidarity.
Text:
So, you're on holiday, having an amazing time and there are many reminders of the tragedy that occurred 0n 26th December 2004, but it's fairly easy to skip by and carry on enjoying yourselves; it's hard not to in Sri Lanka.
You really do need the context of what the people who look after you went through and the Museum is an excellent effort to inform and remind us.
Reading the comments from other reviews, yes, there might be underlying issues around the funding and income from the museum, but in the great scheme of things, giving a few £ is well worth doing.
Our understanding is that the government provide very little - the community and various foreign aid agencies have done it all themselves, with a huge emphasis on helping children and families in the aftermath. Sri Lanka was a war zone at the time.
The lady and a young guy who were there for us have to bear the reminders of this traumatic time and explain it, repeatedly, to us as we visit - that must be incredibly tough. She said that she lost 2 close relatives and she clearly had been involved in this project since its inception; she could explain everything there, in great detail.
Everyone will take away different but abiding memories. For me, there were 3:
There's a photo of a Western looking lady running towards her husband and kids, who seem to have gone exploring on the beach when the tide initially ran way out. They are now facing a massive wall of water and I would imagine that within seconds these people would have drowned. It could have been almost any of us.
The second was that the railway line runs along the beachside. It was holiday time. An 8 carriage train was packed with well over 1,500 people and it was caught as the wave came 2.5kms inland. They all drowned. It remains the largest loss of life in a rail accident, in the world and it happened right there. How you can you begin to comprehend it?
Lastly, as you walk nearby, there's a superb Buddha memorial. It's about 50-60 feet high  the height of the wave as it came over. That puts everything into perspective.
You really should go, just to try and help to show solidarity with the wonderful people you've met on your fantastic holiday.

Title: Very Moving
Text:
A very moving and worthwhile experience. We got a tuk tuk to the Museum and he waited whilst we entered the exhibition. 

The Museum had informative posters in multiple languages (including English) around the building. The posters included: geographical information, causes, effects, statistics and preventative methods. The Museum then consisted of local photographs taken during the aftermath of the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. This also included a display of photographs showing the deceased that was covered with a curtain and opened if you gave your consent. 
The Museum cost a donation of 500 rupees each and I encourage all tourists to visit!

Title: Another very sad visit
Text: This was our fourth or fifth visit to the Tsunami Museum and it is always a very sad visit - extremely sad. It is hard to imagine the power of water - the fact that it could and did push a whole train hundreds of metres inland, with more than 1,200 deaths - just on the train.

Title: Such a poignant place
Text: This was not a museum in the traditional sense as in a brick building with rooms. It is one room with so much information and pictures. They day we went there was a monk making bracelets. You can walk up to the huge buddah which was donated by the Japanese. As always its barefeet so if its hot take socks!.You can also walk up to the railway line, its literally a two minute walk.What a shocking disaster for this lovely town.

Title: Haunting
Text: We visited today and this place is an amazing record of a truly horrific natural disaster. There was a gentleman there taking us into each room and explaining the pictures. Some deeply disturbing but a true representation of what happened. We had passed the memorial on the way and didnt realise that this was the site of a mass grave of  people whos bodies were not claimed for burial - maybe whole families were lost and therefore no one left to claim them. This place is upsetting but on a positive note, the donations are used to help local children many of whom were left with literally nothing. I felt quite emotional which I thought I was prepared for, but still had tears in my eyes at some of the sights.

Title: Graphic Photos, lack of actual information.
Text: We visited this 'photo museum', which is one of 4 community 'museums' all situated close together. It's not a museum, but a collection of photos, quite a few extremely graphic of dead people and decaying corpses. We expected more information about the tsunami, what caused it, what the aid effort was, how the rebuilding has happened, what alarm system is now in place. There was none of this. We were also a little dubious what percentage of the donations actually went to the community, and what were retained by the 'museum' owner? There needs to be a proper community museum set up by the Sri Lankan government, with clear information to inform about this tragic disaster and evidence of where entrance fees and donations actually get used.

Title: Not easily forgotten
Text: This is a harrowing account of the event that hit this coastline on 26th December 2004. You would be quite heartless if you left here without being moved.

Title: A must visit
Text: A very good place to visit while in hikkaduwa. Such a tragedy with so many people losing their lives.

Title: Tsunami museum
Text: This museum explains well this big catastrophe which hit this area 2004. We were silent after coming out from this museum. Very sad to see the entire damage and thousands of lost lives in this area.

Title: I felt so sad what happen to this beautiful country and lovely people
Text: It is really sad moment for us to learn what happen in tsunami. Thanks for keeping this place open to visit people

Title: Emotional and Educational
Text:
This is a must see. The building itself is unimpressive but the lady who runs this has personal experience of the Tsunami. There are lots of photographs depicting the stories of many people on the day and thereafter and if you have the chance speak with the lady in charge, she will really help you to understand.
A small donation is expected, but not demanded. I'm sure anyone visiting will be glad to donate.
It really makes you aware of the power of the seas and you may look at it differently after your visit. I know I did.

Title: Absolutely must see
Text:
Brought most of the memories back from the Tsunami we had seen on the news.
Well presented and very sobering.

We chatted to many locals during the week and they all have their story to tell.

No entry fee but donations help maintain it.

Title: Powerful experience
Text: This primitive exhibition in small house of local teacher is one of the most powerful museums I have ever visited. Remember that there is another small house museum just few meters next to this one. Visit both of them. They are free and it is worth it.

Title: Heart wrenching and eye opening
Text: This is really worth a visit. I never knew how bad Sri Lanka was hot by the tsunami, the museum runs on donations and helps the generations of the people and families and orphans affected l. I would highly recommend the visit to here

Title: Very moving
Text: A short tuktuk ride from where we were staying and incredibly moving. I cannot imagine the tragedy of this event in 2004.

Title: Great place
Text: Learned so much about the tsunami- my children aged 13 and 8 were fascinated well worth a visit . Its walking distance to the turtle hatchery so it can be done in time be trip

Title: If you are in the area you must go here
Text:
We visited the museums last week and I have to say it was both moving and informative. We learnt a lot about the tsunami and how the area was affected - certainly opened my eyes and I was amazed by how the community has bounced back since the 2004
Event.

Title: Reality check
Text:
So you're having a great time in Hikkaduwa. The sun is warm, the beach is breezy, the drinks are cool and the ocean is a gem. Stuff is really cheap and the service is amazing. Awesome, isn't it? 

And then you go to this photographic museum and you see in graphic, uncensored detail a little bit of the horror people faced on Boxing Day in 2004. It's frozen in time; it can't really hurt you, but the people of Sri Lanka are still hurting from it. You might cry a little. You'll probably leave a donation. You'll look out the window as you're driving away, and you'll see all the graves by the road and you'll realise why they're there. You'll also realise that you might be having a fun holiday, but people here are still, in some ways, rebuilding, and you'll tip your waiter more, or not bother with change from the tuk-tuk. Basically, you'll understand a little more how damn lucky you are, because you are. All from one little visit to a concrete house with photos and hand written signs stuck to the walls. Not too many other museums in the world can give you that. Go there. Seriously.

Title: A hidden gem
Text: We only stopped here because it was raining so hard it was making driving dangerous (as if driving isn't dangerous enough in Sri Lanka).  This place is a must see if you want to understand the real Sri Lanka.  We stayed here for about 30 mins but the memory of this place will stay with us for a long long time.  We were able to get a real insight into the impact of the 2004 tsunami and the devastation that it reeked on the island.  Moreover, you can't help being emotionally engaged with the human effect of the disaster which is rounded off by hearing the stories of how the world came to the aid of the island to help rebuild.  If you are passing this way, please stop here.

Title: Worth the visit
Text: Share in the locals history and pain. I learnt so much there. I didnt even know Sri Lanka had the 2nd largest Tsunami death rate. And I learned all about the train full of passengers that was swept away.

Title: Very Informative, Sad but so true and so informative
Text:
It was off season when I went to Hikkaduwa. Often, I spent my days lazing by the beach, but just like others may have commented,  I was kinda disturbed a lot by the "beach boys" like they would wake me in my sleep which was a bit annoying,.  

Anyway, to give me a break, I went to this one. The manager at Kai Hotel suggested it.  I loved it a lot. There is no entrance fee but there is a donation box. I spent around 30 minutes there. Others maybe less but I really wanted to read all the details of the event. It was so shocking how documented it was. The Tsunami felt so long ago but  this museum reminds us how nature can be beautiful but it also has its wrath so we better take better care of it. 

I loved this museum a lot.

Title: Worth knowing the horrors ppl went through
Text: As an Indian i have seen lots of TV coverage and photos of the horrors caused by Tsunami. Wanted to see how badly it hit Srilanka. Saw some heart wrenching photos of that time. They have a collection of photos of troubled times during and after Tsunami in Hikkaduwa. It's a small place, which has a room and a shed in the back which has these photo's hanged. Worth a visit to experience what ppl went through n talk to the lady who's running it to know, how she survived. They run the place on donations. No entry fee. Hope government can help, as so many tourists visit this place.

Title: Very sobering visit
Text: Definitely something I would recommend anyone visiting Hikkaduwa to go and see. Some of the photos could be upsetting to some people but it shows you the real effects to some families and homes

Title: A Must Visit
Text:
This museum is the work of one woman who survived the disaster and is located where her house once stood.  It is not in any way a professional display but that adds to the authenticity of the stories.  
The very lovely lady running it is very happy to talk to you about her personal experience during and after the tragedy. There are some graphic photos which are in a book so be wary about looking through it if the content may upset you.
A great experience that will remain in my memories.

Title: Small but interesting
Text:
Small place with three or four rooms. The first one had lots of interesting info about the earth, plate tectonics and how the tsunami happened, the others are photos of the aftermath. 
There are very interesting guides who show you around and explain the pictures. 
There is one wall of photos that were quite distressing but they warned the children and pulled a curtain across when they were there. 
It is mostly pictures but the knowledge from the guides makes it interesting and the stories are very powerful. 
It is free to go in but they were a little insistent on donations - we were planning on donating but I'd rather they charge an entrance fee than be hassled while looking round. 
An interesting hour to visit and good information for kids.

Title: Photos of Tsunami
Text: a little museum with a lot of pictures of the destruction in Tsunami. place is quiet and calm. no photos allowed inside.

Title: A very sobering reminder
Text:
Humans have short memories and we should never under estimate the power of natural disasters and be prepared for them, including Tsunami's. 

Thanks for putting the Museum together with such awesome photos, even though very graphic, because that is the truth of the matter. Just a shame photos are restricted because this way visitors can help share with the world.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Great photographic presentation. Also staff told about their experience. No Entrance fee but a donation towards the orphan children.

Title: An excellent source of local information about the Tsunami
Text:
I wanted to visit this community Centre for a long time based on my research on Hikkaduwa and its efforts to both commemorate, educate and most importantly rehabilitate. I was greeted by the founder of the museum. I explained to her that I was a geography teacher and we went through all the science and geography section of the museum together. The small Centre has a room dedicated to understanding the science behind a Tsunami, a room dedicated to physical damage to the surrounding area, a section devoted to the train disaster and a section dedicated to the volunteers and charity workers that helped in the short and long term. 
Hidden behind a curtain (to avoid distressing children) are many images of the reality of the human disaster. I was so impressed that she had included this section as many would have avoided displaying such images but in our conversations we agreed that to exclude the people who lost their lives would contribute to the focus on only the damage to buildings that was so prevalent in the local media. 
The Centre also has a classroom in which school children learn about the disaster and what to do if  the sea goes out again. We spent a while talking about the long term psychological impact on those who were there during and after 2004. I was pleased to find out that those who were children then are now returning (many from University) to educate the next generation. 
I could have talked to her all day!!! 
Well worth a visit and if she reads this (I hope the speech went well) x

Title: A must to see and understand the earths power and the devastation it caused in Sri Lanka
Text: After seeing the graves and building ruins along the Galle Road we decided to visit to get a better understanding of what happened to almost the whole of Sri Lanka in the 2004 tsunami!  You will be stunned to silence as you learn about the sheer power of this earth and seeing the photographs of the what was left.  The lady who runs it was very friendly and the museum is in what was her parents house after being rebuilt afterwards.  A must visit, free but I am sure you wont leave without making a donation!

Title: Inspiring
Text: Just a quick tuk tuk from the main part of town, this is a quick visit to understand what happened to Sri Lanka and this town back in 2004. Utter devastation. The photos and faces tell such sad stories. Nonetheless, resilience is an amazing trait and the generous spirit of volunteers helped to rebuild the structures but also the mindset of the people. I highly recommend visiting this sight with your children and discussing emergency plans for when a potential tragedy could occur.

Title: Very impressive
Text: A must see in Hikkaduwa. The setting is typical for Sri Lanka. The Lady explaining everything to us was very nice and it is very impressive to see what a disaster struck the country back then.

Title: Humbling
Text: This museum will leave you speechless at what the people here had to go through. Please visit, an incredible couple run this and it being a small humble house makes it all the more worth going to.

Title: Okay...
Text: We went to this museum as part of a day tour. We were told it was free but when we left we were asked if we bought tickets. We replied saying that we made a donation (even though this is voluntary) and then she said it was fine we don't need to buy tickets. I understand they need to pay rent and upkeep the building but I don't think it's fair trying to sell tickets to get a donation. That being said the lady who explains everything is very informative and it is very sad and thought provoking.

Title: Little Gem
Text:
This museum is very small but very educational. My friend and I visited for free however obviously there is a donation box which you're isn't compulsory but considering the cause, it's a no brainer! 

We were walked around by a lovely young woman who educated us on earthquakes and tsunamis before going into other rooms where there were real pictures of the aftermath. Learning about the impact to hikkaduwa, Sri Lanka and surrounding countries was harrowing and a must see if in hikkaduwa!

Also they had the most adorable little dashund puppy which I got to play with!

Title: Thought provoking.
Text:
Shows the real tragedy, loss and stories of those consumed by the tsunami and its after-effects.

Very emotional and not for the feint-hearted due to some photos.

Lest we forget.

Title: Heartbreaking!
Text: Our visit was heartbreaking and inspiring. The museum consists of three sections - One describing the physics and prediction of a Tsunami, as well as the areas affected in Sri Lanka in 2004. The second showing pictures of the destruction caused (emotional, not for the faint-hearted) and the final section showing the relief efforts and the resilience of the people of Sri Lanka. The lady that runs the museum is a credit to her country - there wasn't a dry eye in our group by the end of the tour! Free entry, with a donation box at the end.

Title: Emotional
Text: When I was listening to the stories of the 2 women, I get emotional! We all saw it on the television and note You can hear the story of the people who survive that terrible day in 2004! It is a must see thing if you are in Sri Lanka, where a lot of people died!

Title: A TRIBUTE
Text:
Community tsunami museum at Hikkaduwa stands out as a fine tribute to the unfortunate victims and their relatives and is a place worth visit. The pictures displayed succeed in taking the visitors through the travails and agonious moments of the devastating tsunami which hit this village.Display snaps also show the extent of damage caused and also the relief work undertaken and also efforts taken to rehabilitate the survivors and the relatives.
Pictures exhibited really bring out the gravity of the disaster and the pain and anguish and anxiety underwent by the victims, their relatives and that of the relief team.
Noteworthy are the photo of the train which was hit by the tsunami and the photo of the tidal waves  hitting the shore.
The donation box kept in the museum certainly needs support of the visitors.
The person who explains the exhibits is herself a survivor.

Title: Very moving
Text:
Driving to the museum you see the remains of homes that were washed away on that fateful day, just the remains of foundations and walls. This alone is moving to see the devistation that nature can throw upon us.
The museum itself is extremely moving showing pictures of the aftermath and how much damage and loss of life was caused. The explanation of how a tsunami is caused and the affect at sea from deep water  the shallows of the coastal areas is informative.
I personally would be wary of young children going inside the museum due to the graphic pictures of bodies etc within the museum.
In all a humbling experience to see how much damage and death was caused and how the local community has recovered.

Title: Very moving
Text: Visiting the tsunami was one of the most important and poignant things we did on our trip. It put the whole visit to Sri Lanka into perspective and , having seen the tragic events unfold on TV at the time, brought the magnitude of it home. The museum is small and runs on donations. There are many photos and testaments from survivors to read .

Title: Very informative- must see if you are in the area
Text:
The lady who runs the museum has first hand knowledge of the tsunami, she showed us around and talked us through the whole tragedy. 

The lady is very passionate about spreading the message and educating children - all in all a very sobering experience. It's nice to know there are now warning systems in place which may give people a chance if this was ever to happen again

Title: An emotional experience
Text:
Theres two tsunami museum close to each other, so your experience might differ depending on which you enter. 

We love the one housed in an old shack where theres a man selling drinks next to the entrance.

It was a very moving experience. The lady owner guided us from picture to picture narrating what happened on that fateful day. The arrangements and displays in the museum really touched our hearts and we highly recommend everyone to come visit here.

Title: Very Informative and Sobering
Text: A small museum manned by volunteers who are only too happy to show you round and talk you through the exhibits which are mostly photographs.(some of the photos are very graphic and show dead bodies). you dont really understand the full force of the Tsunami and its devastation until you have visited this place. Take 20 minutes out of your holiday to see this place and give a small donation as they didn't get a penny from the government. We visited with an 11 year old and i wouldnt really recommend viewing the photos with younger children.

Title: Make a Trip to this Place
Text: You have to See this Place. You can See a lot of pictures from Tsunami at hikkaduwa. Its very hard to See this all.

Title: Informative and uipsetting
Text:
A must for travellers in this region to get a real understanding of the effects of the Tsunami in 2004. A colossal impact on the local community with indescribable suffering and stress. Very graphic display - can be upsetting for some.
The information provided is very helpful and informative.
you definitely leave with a desire to do something however small to help the local community

Title: Very informative
Text: Really interesting small museum. Sections on geography, geology & formation of tsunamis. Photos displayed were heart wrenching but brought the tragedy home.

Title: Sadness with a glimpse of happiness
Text:
Only a small photo tour but a real eye opener the lovely lady explained the history of the tsunami and then the destruction of 2004. There is a section behind curtains that is you are emotional please be careful as these pictures are graphic.
But the last part shows the kids in a happier place and educated for in the event of another tsunami good for bid.

Title: Small but informative museum
Text: A couple of small buildings with photos depicting the devastation of the 2004 tsunami. The first room includes thorough description of the geological aspects of tsunamis, which is quite educational. The next rooms are dedicated to the history of the 2004 catastrophe, with some very GRAPHIC images of dead bodies etc. Be aware if you bring young kids, as some of the photos are rather disturbing.

Title: Very moving
Text:
There is a lot of information on tsunamis and how they are created followed by a series of traumatic and moving photographs of 26th December 2004 - deeply moving. 

We were surprised to have been handed a small piece of paper saying welcome to the museum and the cost was Rs 250 per person as we were already half way through our visit. We read a review posted on the 4th nov that the museum entry was free and a donation was encouraged, so an entrance fee must of been added since then. 

You must visit the museum to comprehend the sheer destruction the 2004 tsunami had on Sri Lanka. Heartbreaking.

Title: Interesting
Text: It was very interesting. But quite upsetting as well. I was not prepared for the pictures of all the dead bodies. But I suppose this part just belongs to the whole very dramatic incident, too.

Title: Very informative
Text:
This is a small education centre & Museum about the devasting 2004 Tsunami. It's a place that really makes you think about what happened.
It starts off informing you about earthquakes and what causes tsunamis and then gives you the statistics of the impacts of the Tsunami which were shocking. You then enter another room to a gallery of photos showing the total devastation. Please be warned there's some graphic photos showing the dead so you might not want to take small children into that section. These photos are truly shocking but a necessary part of the museum. The tour ends showing photos of how the Community is rebuilding.
A must do visit - please be respectful and please give generously into the donation box.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: The photos gallery of Tsunami devastated Sri Lanka. Simple but concussing. Need to see to understand power of earth and tragedy of Sri Lanka.

Title: Humbling
Text: I think this is more of an information centre than museum. It consists of 4 rooms , first Tsunami information, second the devastation caused to property and land, third is quite graphic showing the human suffering, not nice to see but it brings home the enormity of what happened and lastly how things moved on from the tragic incident. It is well worth a visit, it is free to enter but nice to leave a donation.

Title: Don't miss this one
Text: The museum/memorial documents exactly what happened when the tsunami hit and the impact that it had on the local village. Interestingly, the guide there told us that not one animal or bird body was found - all had fled before the tsunami arrived. The photos of the bodies are confronting, which is why they are initially covered by a curtain. It is great to see the international help that went into rebuilding. Today, only a few ruined houses where whole families perished remain as a reminder of the power of nature. The beachfront near the museum is clear of buildings as no one is permitted to build anything up against the beach at this location any more.

Title: Sombre
Text:
It is exactly what you would expect from a place like this. Harrowing and sombre. The lady was extremely helpful and knowledgeable. There is also a room dedicated to information about tsunamis which we found very educational. 

The reviews on here with one star I find laughable. What did they expect from a tsunami museum!!!

Title: A must visit place if you're there
Text: Took a tuk tuk to see what the impact the tsunami had on this place.Didnt realise the severity.Well documented, lovely people taking you and showing things,answering any questions.Please give generously in donation box, no pressure whatsoever to leave anything and free entry

Title: Very moving
Text: Well worth a visit, bring your tissues and learn about the power of nature and see how lives can be rebuilt.

Title: A tsunami of emotion.
Text: Right, this is a little building just outside Hikkaduwa. All it holds is information about how Tsunami's happen, photographs of the horrors that hit here on Boxing day 2004, and survivors of the event as your host. That's it......but if you don't go, you will be the poorer for it. Not a pleasant experience, but if you have taken the time to travel to Sri Lanka, spare an hour to see this. They ask for 250Rs contribution. Give more and be thankful you didn't experience it.

Title: Very interesting, but a little upsetting.
Text: A must to visit whilst in Hikkaduwa as it documents the local tragedy of the Tsunasmi from the villagers aspect & the continued effect that it has had on the community. There is no entry fee, so please donate generously to help the community.

Title: Important to remind yourself
Text: We felt we need to see the reality of the devastation caused by the Tsunami. It was a somber and sobering experience, particularly when they draw back the net curtain to reveal photos of the human catastrophe. No entry fee, but give generously to help the continuing recovery particularly those orphaned.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: This place is a must if you come to Hikkaduwa. Its important to understand how people still live with this in their memory and how it still affect them. Very informative and nice people who worked there

Title: Very Emotional
Text: A visit to the Tsunami museum will engulf you in the feeling of sorrow, pity and a normal human being is bound to have tears rolling down his cheeks. There are numerous photographs of the Tsunami period displayed here. We went to the one near Hikkaduwa and the visit was worth it.

Title: Photo gallery
Text: There are a couple 'museums' we went to the newer one. It's a 4 room building filled with tsunami literature and photos. This place has some excellent and moving photos. The support of community and volunteers makes all one.

Title: A visit makes you realise how lucky one is.
Text:
We hired a driver for the day and on talking to him about his way of life, he suggested a stop at the museum. A very grand word for 4 small rooms - but the impact those 4 rooms have is incredible.

Museum is not really the right word to describe this place - it is more of a memorial to the 34,000 Sri Lankan people who lost their lives due to the 2004 Tsunami. And sadly it highlights how the world forgot Sri Lanka at the time (probably due to the civil war in the country at the time).

We heard heart breaking first hand accounts from those that lived through that awful time.

Being on Holiday, this visit made us realize just how lucky we are.

Title: Educational, emotional and essential
Text:
This is a very unassuming place, within a small building located a couple of kilometers north of Hikkaduwa. We walked a little from the beach then grabbed a tuk tuk which cost 300 rupees. 

The exhibition itself is a very factual journey through the story of the tsunami with geological information, earthquake information then the tsunami itself, its impact, aftermath and subsequent response. The staff who work there all have personal accounts of that day and are all extremely knowledgeable and friendly. Be warned there are some graphic photos of the aftermath, but we both agreed that these are a necessary part of the story and really hit home the scale of destruction. 

All in all this was an educational and emotional visit and we think it is important to see it, both to pay respect and to donate to the ongoing regeneration of the area and its people. 

After our visit we walked a short way back towards Hikkaduwa and visited the Tsunami memorial statue to get a true understanding of the size of the wave (the Buddha is as tall as the second wave).

Title: Moving
Text: Id read reviews that people had said it was too graphic and therefore I was a little concerned.  However I am so glad I went to the museum, yes the photos are shocking but that is the reality of the situation. We were shown round by a young man who had been through the tsunami. He spoke very eloquently about what happened and whats been done since. We are a family with two teenage boys, we were all visibly moved by what we saw.  Im so glad we went, you see things in the media not appreciating the reality of the situation. By visiting the museum you fully appreciate the human suffering that the Sri Lankans experienced that day and how people from all walks of life have helped to repair the physical and human suffering.

Title: Must visit
Text: Museum is run by lovely volunteers from the village who experienced the devastating tsunami first hand. Very emotional and emotive but great to hear stories of hope for the future. A donation box is located in the second room - be generous.

Title: Probably my 8th visit here.
Text: I myself was in Tsunami 13 years ago in Sri Lanka. Almost very time Ive come back to the amazing country Ive visited here. Mainly taken friends and family who have come out to see Sri Lanka and have wanted to come here. It breaks my heart every time I visit as it brings it all back but it is an amazing thing they have done and donations go towards a good cause so I like to go give something. Thank you

Title: WOW - CONFRONTING BUT ALL PART OF THE STORY
Text: We wanted to visit this museum because it is very much part of the story of this beautiful country.    The museum leads you on a journey about the story of the Tsumani - images of the aftermath, the sadness of dead bodies and the amazing images of the rebuild and the people who made a difference to an event that changed the lives of so many.   Well worth visiting.

Title: Really informative and interesting, sad but real
Text:
Very real visit to the Tsunami Museum with many photos on the walls about their village and how it was affected.  We found the guide exceptionally friendly and informative.  Is certainly worth visiting and honoring in your travels to Sri Lanka.

There is one room that is for adult viewing only, but the rest of the photos were suitable for my children and they enjoyed the discussions.

Title: A worthwhile visit
Text:
Obviously one visits in a sombre and respectful way.

The museum is very small and feels somewhat haphazard, but there are some interesting insights to be gained.there.

Some of the photos may be considered gruesome to some, but they do reflect the harsh / ugly side to life too, so accept it and take it in,( in a non ghoulish way)

Entry Fee ? 
I read somewhere that entry was free, therefore I made sure I put a substantial donation into the donation box towards the end of our visit.
Almost as soon as I had done this the guy that was running the place stated he had forgotten to charge and give us our entry ticket ( at 250 rupees each). 
I paid up of course but it did make me  feel a bit awkward. ( never mind).

Title: Must see
Text: It make you feel for the people living  in Sri Lanka. This was huge tragedy for all and you can see a small piece of it. Be greatfull for what you have because it can be gone in a flash. Thank you

Title: Take some tissues
Text: Small but effective display of photos and quotes. Very moving, considering youre right where it occurred. Definitely worth seeing.

Title: Great, dont miss
Text:
This was a very humbling experience and well worth the walk from Hikkaduwa.  If your in the area don't miss this, the photographs in the museum are incredible and so sad.

Women are provided with material to cover up so no problem with what you are wearing.

Title: A must visit!
Text: Very knowledgable staff at this small photo museum. A very touching experience. Well worth a visit. There is a curtain screen if viewers find some of the images upsetting. There is a donation box, but visitors are not pressurised to put anything in it....unlike some places.

Title: worth a visit
Text: very confronting to see all the images from the damage. would recommend visiting and donating if In area

Title: A must visit. Terribly sad. Graphic images not for young kids perhaps.
Text:
Terribly terribly sad but we feel a must visit.
Awful and tragic images , memories and letters from the event.
There are some photos of turn limbs and dead bodies that were too much for my young children aged 9 and 12.

Title: Moving and Beautiful - not your typical museum.
Text: I went with my husband and three children to this museum and it was a memorable experience.  It is easy when you see the beauty of Sri Lanka to forget the tragedy that it faced not so long ago.  This museum is in the former home of the woman who runs it - the home was nearly destroyed by the tsunami.  There are photos and art work about the day that changed the island forever.   The first building is more factual, explaining about the wave and the other aspects of the tsunami.  The second building has more graphic images.  Our older daughter and my husband went through that part and our younger two children and I hung behind.  It isn't a museum like most you are used to - there is no dramatic lighting, no air conditioning, no gift shop.  It is a dirt floored home full of true artifacts.  You come out feeling a combination of absolute devastation for what the people faced and extreme hope for all the has happened since that.  A truly beautiful and moving experience.

Title: A good place to visit
Text: The museum is not far from Hikkaduwa, so it's worth a visit. Located in a house close to the road, it takes you through the moments before and after the tsunami that hit Sri Lanka back in 2004. You can not take pictures inside, there is no visiting fee but we recommend you leave a small amount for the donation. Although I have read reviews where the museum owners ask for money from the tourists, we have not experienced this, and  the two people who presented us the rooms and pictures were very kind and provided all the details, answering to our questions.

Title: Educational
Text: We had no idea how many lives had been lost in the tsunami here in Sri Lanka.   The staff here were so humble, being victims themselves and all having lost people ...Friends and or family.   The information and photos are to educate everyone and they regularly have childrens groups here to educate and I nform them.   Sri Lanka had not experienced a tsunami before in modern times and so many people simply did not understand.   A complete tragedy.   Very emotional yet I think a must as this is part of the history of this country.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The community tsunami museum is well worth a visit if you are in Hikkaduwa. A short tuk tuk drive from the Main Street. The museum is very informative and is run by locals who want to education people on the impact the 2004 tsunami had on Sri Lanka. Visiting the museum gives you a huge insight into what the local people have had to go through. The museum is free but you can donate to local charities trying to rebuild the lives of people effected by the tsunami whilst there.

Title: Everyone will learn something and be very touched by visiting
Text:
Take your shoes off before you go in and you will stay in that respectful perspective throughout. 
I thought I knew a lot about tsunamis and about this disaster, but I learned a few very interesting facts about both.
There is a really good explanation about tsunamis and what happened then a load of pictures showing before, during and after the disaster 
The staff are very informative and most experienced the disaster itself and give a harrowing account of what happened
It is free to get in and highly educational for all so do please donate generously

Title: Good to know the History
Text: Worth the visit. It is sad to see the photos of the victims. A ticket of Rs 500 to be given. Near to the beach.

Title: Educational and confronting
Text: Very informative museum. First part focuses on how tsunamis are caused and gives you some facts and figures on tsunamis in the past. Second part is a photo collection of the devestation the 2004 tsunami caused in the area. Would not take young children into this bit. Museum relies solely on donations.

Title: Beautifully Done
Text: The pictures are moving and difficult to see, as they'd should be. But it is presented very well and is possible to miss the hardest bits though I wouldn't advice it. There is a lovely but at the end showing the positive way the community is dealing with it and moving on. Donation box, I put all my money in so be warned, not that I regret it.

Title: Several Tsunami museums in Hikkaduwa, the one on the north entrance is utterly moving and not commercial.
Text:
I came out with tears in my eyes.
My tuktuk driver too me to the very first Tsunami museum when entering town from Kosgoda. I, liked that there was a a free gift box (for the Cancer society), the other ones do charge an entrance fee - which may be no problem if the quality is related to the price.
It is basically two simple shacks, every explanation carefully and lovingly written by hand. Lots of pix, statistics, a moving kids suitcase, a bit of beach full of plastic debris.
Some bits of critical notes on certain kinds of rather unpleasant actions by so called helpers looking for Western bodies.
This is just the simple, uncommercial place that is suited to inform us on the tragedy.. Hikkaduwa was the last place on the west coast to be so severely hit by the Tsunami

Title: Important place to visit
Text: A very moving place to visit. Listening to our guide had me in tears, hearing about the mothers grieving for their children about families ripped apart. A very moving place that I will always remember. It's easy to hear about tragedy's on the news but it's hard to relate. Here you are on literally where such sadness occurred, it really hit home for me. Be warned there are a lot of graphic images, and our guide did not hold back with explanations. We had our 9 year old and 7 year old sons and I sent them away in this room, the guide guided them to a kids activity table away from the images in the next room which as the images aren't suitable for young children. I feel this is a very important place to visit.

Title: Good collection
Text: Wide collection of photos and science behind the ill fated Tsunami which hit Sri Lanka and India. Graphic description of the destruction, loss and rescue makes the visitor realize the extent of the tragedy. Sensitive people can best avoid.

Title: Tsunami history in Sri Lanka
Text: This place had good information on the history of the 2004 tsunami. How it happens and what the impact was for the local region. The lady that was the host was very informative and is willing to answer all of your questions. This is more of a converted house that has pictures and charts explaining it all as well as the gruesome details that you may not want to witness. Very informative for the children to see something like this first hand.

Title: An ode to the communities struggle post tsunami.
Text: The tsunami museum is a quiet, small building right opposite the sea that caused so much devastation. The pictures are quite shocking, somber and sad. There are survivors who will tell you the harrowing story of the tragedy that occurred that day. We were glad we went as we also saw how the community strived to pick themselves up post tsunami. That was the uplifting take away message from this place.

Title: Touching
Text: Tsunami Museum has a collection of pictures of Tsunami disaster. You need a lot of courage to look at them. I came out with a very heavy heart and tearful eyes. Go, if you can handle it.

Title: A Must-visit site
Text:
This place is not your typical marble-floored, double-storied museum, instead it's a rather small, open hut, with posters hanging on the mud lined walls. Posters of devastation and desparation. It's hard not o cry when you see some of the pictures of the tsunami that hit Sri Lanka in 2004. There is so much detail and information here. Details of the deatht toll not just in Sri Lanka, but also elsewhere in Asia where the tsunami hit. A detailed map of the regions affected, first-hand accounts of what happened, survival accounts but also of what they saw of the people who weren't so lucky. The before and after pictures of the areas were heart-wrenching. There are also personal items that I believe were recovered from the tsunami aftermath. It's worth a visit to contemplate just how profound and devastating the tsunami was for Sri Lankans. 

There are actually two tsunami museum places a few minutes walk from each other. Both are filled with heart breaking pictures of the tsunami and it's aftermath but one of them also contains some science behind the formation of tsunamis, brief details of how to survive/prepare emergency flood bags and it is run by a lady who was present on that fateful day. You can ask her for her account which somehow makes the whole experience even more real and profound.

There are donation boxes at both sites and as it's maintained by volunteers using the money from donation, there is an expectation that you leave a donation. It can be of any amount and they don't actually watch you while you leave the money in the box so it's not as awkward.

Title: So Sad....
Text:
This was near to our hotel so we went by Tuk tuk
There are lots of photos depicting the story of the 2004 tsunami.... we heard lots of stories about Thailand at the time and didn't realise how badly affected Sri Lanka was. They have not been able to rebuild all of the houses etc and lots stand derelict 
Some of the photos are quite graphic so bear this in mind if visiting with children...
Definitely an eye opener that makes you grateful for the life we have

Title: so hard but necessary
Text: it's a small museum. You can go with tuk tuk. It's a place for remember and everybody should go. It explain what a tsunami is, and there is a lot of pictures about the tsunami in Hikkaduwa. The owner explains a lot of things about her experience there. It's so hard to visit, but it's necessary.

Title: Sad but thoughtfull place to visit
Text: Very quaint and basic very thought provoking, very sad a rush of emotions. This place makes you realise just how lucky we are in this country.

Title: So sad , you will not forget this visit
Text: we stopped here as part of a tour , didnt really know what to expect , but so moving , it was very upsetting , there is a lady there who surivived but tells you the full story , the one the papers didnt tell you and the photos are heartbreaking , be prepared there are some that you might wish to avoid .   we had no idea that this area had lost so many of its people ,  you will leave feeling very humbled .  please leave them a donation its for the children who survived ,  left a lasting effect on myself

Title: A place for remembering!
Text: A small shed with lots of photos and newspaper clippings and children`s drawings of the catastrophe.This is cloose to the place where the train overturned,and ca 1500 people died.Do not go long ways for a visit,if you don`t have a special reason,but if you are cloose,we recommend it.There is also a memory place cloose,where you can lay a flower.

Title: Interesting and very sad
Text: We had a very interesting trip to this museum. So sad but really informative. Definitely worth a visit!

Title: A real eye-opener
Text: We didn't realise Sri Lanka was affected by the tsunami in 2004 and it was heartbreaking to see the effects.  Photos were very graphic and our tuk tuk driver also became our guide and explained all about the tsunami and what happened after it to us.

Title: Interesting and moving, makes you appreciate life more.
Text: This is a must see if you're around this area, its really moving and you really see what people were left to deal with after the tsunami.

Title: You have to visit this place
Text: Here you Can se, what happened in Sri Lanka under the tsunami. Very sad, but also interesting to see.

Title: Touching
Text: The visit here was very informative. Also the visit was very sad. The museum gives you a good idea of what happened when the tsunami hit the area.

Title: Informative and Touching visit!
Text: Can recommend to visit if you want a glimpse of what happened in Sri Lanka during the Tsunami. Especially touching to see the drawings of children.

Title: Sad
Text: Had to visit a great set up with lots of information and helpful staff very sad but need to see what they have been through

Title: Sad pictures
Text: This is actually only a small kiosk, but something you should not want to miss. So many sad stories and pictures and children drawings telling us about this horrible day you should never forget. Hopefully this happens never again. Don't forget to give a small donation, it helps those families who actually lost everything.

Title: Good to see
Text: Good/sad to see what the community went through. Friendly people working there - telling there first hand stories. Free to enter and makes money off donations. Must visit.

Title: Many photos
Text: Breath-taking photograps. The woman there told us interesting notes about this incident. Its really good to see that

Title: Visit to the Tsunami Museum
Text: Excellent and well worth a visit.  Unbelievable destruction and loss of life.  Very hard to comprehend.

Title: Very moving and educational.
Text:
I felt that I should go and visit this place. Only 6km form my hotel. I was guided by the lady who looks after the place. She is a survivor and lost three relatives in the disaster. The place is well laid out and carefully built. It came across very well - the power and scale of nature. The suffering of the victims.The kindness and skills of the volunteers who came to help. 
If you visit please leave a donation.

Title: Heartbreaking
Text: Gradually taking shape, needs a bit of investment and planning, a big undertaking but worth a visit,

Title: Thought provoking
Text: Many of the photographs and the stories written by children brings home to you the heartbreak and suffering that this area like many others went through

Title: Sobering visit
Text: A sobering visit however very interesting . Assistant shared her personal experiences and local stories.

Title: Nicecollection but sad to see the disaster
Text: It was really sad to see the photos, how tsunami took lives. They have good collection but you will not feel happy seeing people died in such a horrible way. Must visit though.

Title: Very Moving
Text:
Not a big place but crammed with loads of photos showing the complete destruction of the area and some very heart rendering photos.
 The building is built on the area that was most affected. 
There is no entry fee but a donation box, well worth a visit and a donation.

Title: A good local museum about tsunami
Text:
Nice visiting when in Hikkaduwa, you really get a good idea how big the impact of the tsunami had and still has. Free entry but you can leave a donation.

One room has pictures of dead people so if you have children with you, you can as them to close the curtains on that wall.

Good place also for locals to get knowledge of tsunami and how can one prepare for another, which hopefully will never come.

Title: Moving, a must do
Text: Small photo museum about the horrific natural disaster that happened on boxing day in 2004. Very informative and explains many things about how the community has coped with the event and aftermath.

Title: Totally moving
Text: Went here and it was moving and amazing to see. I'd definitely recommend it as a site to visits if you are staying or traveling into hikkaduwa.

Title: A must see
Text: This isn't the happiest, most fun thing you'll do or see on a trip to Sri Lanka but I felt compelled to visit.  It's graphic, informative, heartbreaking and inspiring.  You have the opportunity to donate to the ongoing support still needed (completely voluntary, just a donation box inside).  I was very glad I visited and gained a very small but important insight into what happened on that fateful day.

Title: Must see
Text: Our tuk-tuk driver insisted we see it and told us about his family's experience. Seeing the photos and reading about the 2004 tsunami gave us a better understanding and appreciation for the area.

Title: Interesting sad and rather graphic
Text: Small museum with free entry and no pressure to donate. COntains a lot of information and some very graphic photos in the second room which can be hidden behind a curtain. I would recommend if you are travelling with young children that you go first and take a view on whether you should ask for the curtains to be drawn. It appears the government did little or nothing to help and many houses are still in ruins. The tsunami early warning system seems inadequate compared to that installed in Thailand for instance.

Title: Informative
Text: This is a small museum, it has a lots of photo's of the aftermath caused by the tsunami, some are quite graphic.

Title: Definitely worth visiting
Text: This is a very good museum to visit. It is very informative about the tsunami. There is no cost to visit must donations are welcomed.

Title: Very moving
Text:
Nice quick stop to the museum. The pictures really paint a very graphic picture in your mind what Sri Lanka went through during the tsunami and aftermath. 
The amazing people that helped the injured and rebuilt to what it is today.

Title: Graphic reminder
Text: Hikkaduwa was one of the worse hit areas from the tsunami. It's free to enter. Only small. It's tells you how tsunamis are created and then has a gallery of photos which are very graphic. Devastating but uplifting as well. No pressure to donate but donations are welcome

Title: Tsunami Museum
Text: Hikkaduwa area was badly hit by Tsunami and a statue and museum has come up in memory of the affected. Its really sad to learn how the families of a lovely seashore place have suffered

Title: Really fascinating
Text: This hatchery gave us a real insight into the life of turtles and how important their preservation is , we found it hugely educational and to see them and even touch them , a real privilege, then we saw one up close in the sea at Hikkadawa !

Title: Sad
Text:
Found our visit here a very emotional one.
The Photo Museum is run from the home of a local family who had their house destroyed by the disaster. 
The exhibits are very basic but all the more powerful because of this and the the fact that there are many very personal stories on display.
Incredibly moving and highly recommended.
Entry is free but please make a donation in the box.

Title: Very powerful photos
Text: Although this is a very small place, the photos and information were very interesting. Afterwards, I was very aware of the fact that many of the locals I met were directly impacted by the tsunami.

Title: Very emotive
Text: Very raw and authentic photo memoir of the 2004 tsunami; family and children stories, anecdotes, and messages of hope. Run within the old home of a local family (they also manage the museum) who had their house destroyed by the disaster.  Incredibly moving and highly recommended.

Title: just a memorial
Text: nothing much .. and more deeper you look  might generate a fear of beaches.... just avoid... not that it s not having any importance but not a worth visiting place

Title: Very moving place to visit
Text: This is only small but it brings home the scale of the disaster. The people who run the museum are worth talking to as they have first hand stories to tell. Very sad but it's somewhere you should visit. Afterwards you see the area in a different light

Title: A real shock
Text: About a 200 rupee tuk tuk ride from town and a real eye opener. Worthwhile visit and make sure you leave a donation, as its free to enter. A real insight into the devastation this event caused!

Title: Very informative and very sad place
Text:
This museum is set up so there is an educational room for school kids at the front and then rooms of pictures of the disaster behind. Don't let kids in the back where the pictures are because they are very graphic and done are very disturbing. The museum is very respectful and the people who run it are very informative and in our case, were there living there when the tsunami happened. 35 000 people dead in Sri Lanka alone.
Would highly recommend going just to get an appreciation of how devistating this event was to the people.

Title: Very moving
Text: A very interesting and moving hour spent at this tiny museum in a location near the eye of the tsunami. Well worth a visit if in the area.

Title: An emotional experience
Text: A tiny bungalow of 3 rooms rebuilt after this terrible natural event. Informative, harrowing and uplifting. A must visit, it puts life into perspective. In future if I am having a bad day, I will remember 1 picture in particular and realise that nothing is really 'that bad' and count my blessings. The 2 local guides were knowledgeable, and very willing to explain and talk.

Title: Must see if staying near Hikkaduwa
Text: Knowledgeable guide showed the family around this small museum, takes about 30 minutes to view, explaining what happened geographically and geology wise. One wall, covered by a curtain, has many harrowing pictures of human suffering and the devastation caused. Very moving.

Title: A humbling experience
Text: A tiny little house that was rebuilt after the tsunami...sad but very emotional and well worth taking a little time our to understand exactly what happened to this beautiful place x

Title: To the point
Text: It consists of one room that is info posters which seem a copy and paste from the internet. The second room is a bit heavy with many of the pics consisting of dead bodies. The final room is many happy pictures of aid and children. No charge in but donation given.

Title: Moving
Text: This very small but moving Tsunami Museum displays photos of the devastation caused by the Boxing Day Tsunami.  I was met at the museum by a young Buddhist monk who explained the photos, some of which were very graphic.  There is no cost to visit the museum though there is a donation box where you can leave money to help maintain the museum.

Title: A very informative display regarding the 2004 Tsunami in Sri Lanka
Text: An educational and deeply moving experience detailing the Tsunami and it's effects, an emotional account of photography displayed.

Title: Hmm...Questionable Practices
Text: We went here not because we asked to, but because a tuk tuk driver insisted that we stop by. The ticket was 200 rs, and I was later told that the tuk tuk driver will get a commission from it. It's a small place. The first room is a basic presentation of what an earthquake and tsunami is, and how it affected Sri Lanka. The next room is very graphic photos of the victims, and the final room is pictures of happy children that are said to be the survivors. Overall, it is a very brief display of a horrible event that changed hundreds of thousands of lives. Walk down any street nearby and you can talk to survivors and hear their own story. It is heartbreaking. That being said, I kind of get the feeling that this place is taking advantage of a really bad tragedy which is why I've given it a poor rating. While I certainly encourage people to help tsunami survivors, I'm not sure that this place is the best way to do so.

Title: Impressive
Text: A small museum close to hikkaduwa beach where you can see the impact of the 2004  tsunami in pictures. Would definitely recommend to visit this place. No entrance fee but you can give a donation at the end. Hard to see what happened here in 2004.

Title: Can't help but be moved
Text:
Despite it being many years since the Tsunami struck Asia including Sri Lanka, visiting this museum is incredibly moving.  Whilst very basic, the free museum displays very interesting facts & photos around the tsunami impacts.

Close to the big Buddha that now stands close to the location where the train was washed away killing over 1000 people which is still the worlds worst train disaster.

The fact that over 1000 people were buried in a large pit grave brings the immensity of this disaster into rela terms.

Title: Moving time
Text:
Worth a visit has quite a few moving photos about the tsunami that devastated here and the greater Asia area.
Certainly tugs on the heart strings.
Not sure what the purpose of the private museum is about as there is also another museum down the road about 200 m with the giant standing Buddha outside.
I just hope its not tsunami inc.

Title: Tsunami community museum
Text: The Tsunami community museum is run by an amazing woman, who is a survivor of the 2004 tsunami herself. The museum has an informative section and a photos section (some are hard to watch) so it is very powerful and gives a wide picture of the disaster

Title: Small museum but wow
Text: Small museum but worth the visit. Three rooms and a very impressive. Plenty of pictures and tells the story of the natural disaster. Moving at times and definitely a must to go see

Title: Wow... makes you think
Text: Eye opening somber view of the tsunami impact. Spoke with a lady that lived out the natural disaster. Good to go and see what happened, the impact and how sri Lanka have grown stronger.

Title: Must See
Text:
This is one of those places that you need to visit while in Sri Lanka.
Just a few little rooms with lots and lots of photos  and information all about the Tsunami that destroyed Sri Lanka back in 2004.
It really is an emotional experience seeing all the photos and reading all the information first hand in this little place, on the beach area where so much devastation and loss of life occurred.
Museum is run by one lady who is in attendance and happy to talk all about it.
Entry is free but donations are welcomed.

Title: Small museum but must watch
Text: This is a very small 3 room museum depicting the situations of Tsunami that hit Sri Lanka. A lady is present who will let you see and explain each photos present there.

Title: Eye openinn - every one should visit
Text: A very informative small museum that only take 30mins to visit. It is completely shocking to see what the poor people of Sri Lanka were subjected to 13 years ago. However - WORD OF CAUTION - I took my 8 and 10 year old children and while the first room was very interesting and informative, the photography in the second room is not suitable for younger children. It is very graphic with many scenes of dead bodies, drowned people and mass graves, it gave my daughter night mares for a few nights. I think it is extremely important that they understood more about Sri Lanka than just the beaches but would question how this material is displayed or at least offer a warning.

Title: Very moving
Text:
All done by volunteers and donations. History of Tsunamis as well as the tragic one in Sri Lanka. Guides explain the pictures and posters.
A must see

Title: A place of remembrance
Text: I have been to tsunami museums in other countries but this was the most evocative. Unlike other places, this one pulls no punches and the photos are distressing but then in the next room you have smiling faces showing how the community has moved on and supported each other. A worthy cause

Title: really worth visiting
Text: it is a very simple museum but gives a very good impression on what the tsunami must have been like for the people in Sri Lanka. there is also an interesting educational piece upfront to explain where a tsunami comes from. there is no entrance fee but you can leave a donation to support the museum and tsunami fund.

Title: Worth a visit - the stories should be kept alive
Text: The museum is divided into 3 parts - educational, SL tsunami and train disaster. There are loads of photos of the trategy and the victims which which are very difficult to process - I couldn't see these and quickly walked through these. This is a donation run organisation and whilst we tend to enjoy the beautiful ocean and the surrounding beaches I think visits to these places keeps the stories of those who helped re-build and plight of the SL people alive. Please do visit - it only takes 15-20 mins.

Title: Sad, moving and worth a visit
Text: The Tsunami museum is located just a short tuktuk ride outside of Hikkaduwa. Entrance is free, you are asked to leave a donation though. The museums consists of 3 small rooms. The pictures you get to see are sad and moving. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Sad, moving!
Text: There are some experiences that can't be described in words. To see the community Tsunami museum and relive the tragic experience of so many who were affected by the unfortunate event is surreal, sad and extremely emotional. God bless the families and amen to the ones who lost their lives. This place is a must-visit for anyone visiting Hikkaduwa.

Title: Emotional
Text: This place is a must if in Hikkaduwa. It's a house with photos of the damage of the tsunami and how the area has recovered. It's a truly touching place and very emotional. The lady there gave us more information about the tsunami and was great in answering our questions. There is no charge for entry and you can give a donation at the end if you wish.

Title: Tsunami photo museum
Text:
Good place to visit to see what the destruction was of the tsunami. It's just a small house with photo's and stories of the local people but defenetly worth a visit. You can make a donation in the box if you want. 
The photos are getting old and damage but I didn't mind.

Title: Surreal and sad but a must
Text: This museum really hits home just how badly this area of Sri Lanka was hit by the tsunami. All of the stories from the different contributors to the museum are incredibly sad and moving. Speaking to the owner about his experience you really are left speechless at their strength and resilience. Even speaking to others on our way back to Hikkaduwa, their stories just blew us away - our tuk tuk driver in particular was a police officer at the time and I couldn't believe what he was telling us. Poignant, moving, sad but a definite eye opener. An absolute must!!!

Title: Really sad
Text: It was so sad to see the effects og the tsunami, really Nice museum. But Many sad pictures and stories

Title: Very sad and moving but an essential visit
Text: Some of the photographs are truly shocking but the whole museum helps you understand how badly hit this region of Sri Lanka was.  This stretch of coastline is littered with ruined houses left behind by the tsunami and the pictures paint a scene of the true devastation that took place.  It doesn't take long to look around but you come away with a profound feeling of sadness and a degree of understanding of what actually happened that day

Title: Essential visit.
Text: Very moving indeed and an essential visit to help understand this region. Some of it is quite gut wrenching but the admirable lady who runs it has dedicated herself to creating good from the disaster.

Title: Very good summary, but disturbing
Text: Been there last month. In just 30 minutes, you will be able to live the moments that shook the Island nation of Sri Lanka. Very informative and for a great cause. One wall particularly where you would notice the corpses lying around - on the fields, hospital beds, of children, young men, old people - is very disturbing.

Title: intersting but very sad
Text: its not for the faint hearted , there are some photos that maybe children should not see but its interesting and gives a local approach to a very sad day

Title: Very emotional visit
Text: Our guide stopped us here to give us a better idea of the devastating aftermath of the tsunami. It's free entrance but you can donate if you like. The lady showed us around and answered some questions. It was very hard to see how badly this area was hit by the tsunami. The last room has many photos of dead bodies so he mindful if you have kids with you. I personally couldn't see all of these photos after 3 seconds. Worth a visit and a good donation.

Title: Very moving
Text: If you are traveling to or through Hikkaduwa, take some time to stop at this little 'museum'. There is not a lot more that I could add that has been already said. This is a very personal experiences, which I found to be very moving.this is a good experience to understand how Tsunamis happen and what Srilanka went through in the Tsunami of 2004.

Title: Sobering stuff
Text: Some of the photographs on show here are not the faint hearted. Or faint stomached. However, the grisly images do bring home the true horror of the tsunami which devastated this stretch of coastline. Well worth a visit - for the brave amongst you.
