Title: Important place to visit to understand Sri Lanka
Text:
The museum has two sections - one explaining where tsunamis come from, the other one showing the damage from the 2004 tsunami. While we all have seen similar pictures on the internet and tv, you gain a different understanding of the situation once you realise these victims have lived within kilometers of where you're standing now, and that most Sri Lankans on the south coast have lost their loved ones.

Most importantly of all, the museum is led by local people, tsunami survivors. It is a rare opportunity to be able to talk to someone who survived this tragedy and be able to ask them difficult questions.

Title: informative
Text: The Museum has lots of pictures of Tsunami 2004 and very informative too. some pictures are very disturbing and not suitable for kids and light hearted people and they have taken good care of it too

Title: Informative and emotional
Text:
This is one of two tsunami
Museums in Telwatta. See them both - there are a few photos you may see twice but they both offer a lot of different material and different perspectives from
local residents. 

This one emphasises explaining the science behind tsunamis, as well as showing many before and after photos and stories specific to this town. Note that there are photos of the dead, and the photos at this museum a bit more graphic than the other museum. Not for children or those who do not wish to view that aspect. 

Donations of 500 rupee + helps maintain the museum. The local museum host will answer any questions. 

If you are staying in Galle you can get to  Telwatte by train for 20 rupee. There is a tsunami memorial and a turtle hatchery in easy walking distance.le you can easily get

Title: Very moving
Text: Great insight into the terrible events of the Tsunami in 2004.  Very informative by lovely guides showing photo footage and facts & figures.  Only a small building free of charge with donations if you wish to.

Title: Small and basic info - and suddenly an entrance fee
Text: Our guide book recommended this small place also because it was supposed to be free. When we entered, they informed us that there was a fee which we did not think was appropriate for what was offered.

Title: Barely held it together
Text: There are two photograph museums quite close together so I hope this is the right one. The museum is where the owner lived when the tsunami came through and she tells everyone what happened. It is heart-breaking but so so important to hear. It's not fancy, the english explanations are a bit rough, but it's really about the photos that show the devastation of the area and especially the train that was swept off the tracks causing the worst train accident in history.

Title: A must see.. though quite graphic
Text:
Blink and you will miss it, the Community Tsunami Museum we visited on the way to Galle from Balapitya.

It is run and maintained by a local family, and remembers the Tsunami disaster that befell the area in 2004 where many thousands died.

We did not take any photos inside the museum out of respect, and i would warn people that there are some extremely graphic photos on display which could be upsetting to some, of the aftermath and victims of the tsunami.

Well worthwhile visiting and worth leaving a generous donation afterwards to help the family maintain the museum

Title: Short but interesting
Text: We just visited this on the way to a beach it was very interesting with some harrowing pictures showing what it was like worth a visit.

Title: Breath taking
Text: When you are in Hikkaduwa you have to visit this museum. Its an overview in pictures and together with the stories of the survivors it is an emotional experience. Makes you humble and gives you an idea of what is important in live.

Title: Harsh Reality
Text: This place shows the harsh realities that the people of Sri Lanka had to face in the midst and aftermath of this horrible natural disaster. Some of the photos are heavy and very somber to see but you are warned first so you dont have to see these.

Title: Very informative
Text: We went here as part of a tour and it was good to be able to contribute to the charity fund. However it is very sad to see and some very graphic pictures.

Title: Important and moving.
Text:
The museum is situated by the main road, opposite the beach in what is left of what once was the curators family home, ripped apart by the tsunami. 
It is free to enter and the lady who runs it gives ALL donations to local education and a cancer charity. 
As others have already mentioned, there are some photographs I didnt want my youngest (age 6) to see, and its upsetting to see the damage that was inflicted upon people, particularly when you see the streets and some of the building you know in the area youre staying. However, this is a very important memorial to those who lost their lives and their loved ones. Please go, take a moment and make a donation.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: This is a small place north of Hikkaduwa that has a educational display about earthquakes and Tsunamis. It also has a poignant and moving display of photographs taken at and after the Indian Ocean Tsunami. The entrance was free but there is a box for offerings. No photography is allowed and visitors are asked to remove footwear before entering.

Title: 2004 boxing Day
Text: It was a very sad day in 2004 when this tragedy occured. The photos are very graphic and sad. Good models etc to explain how it all happened, very helpful staff who also lost loved ones.

Title: A definite must do. Plan time after to contemplate
Text: This place rocked me. After a few days in Hikka you realise everyone lost someone or something. A must do destination to understand the impact at that time and of course the lasting effects. So sad. Humbling and deep. Gave me a true appreciation of the human experience.

Title: Touching
Text: We went there with our two grown up children (probably a bit distressing for young children as really graphic photos).  They did try to keep the graphic photos separate behind a curtain though.  The family who run it were severely affected by the Tsunami. They were really very knowledgeable and very sweet. It was really moving. I would definitely recommend a visit. You can't really go to Sri Lanka without embracing this bit of of history since the island was so badly affected. This museum feels intimate and homegrown and personal.

Title: the power of nature reveiled
Text: Two small buildings full of real photos and comments from real people who did or did not survive the drastic tsunami on that boxing day. Moving, disturbing, and so real. A must to see, to make us realise that nature is so strong. A very humbling experience. Basic but so real.....

Title: Dramatic insights to tragic event - some drastic images
Text: This is a so called community run museum that gives deep insights to the terrible devastation and human tragedy that unfolded during and after the great tsunami. It also relates the efforts made by locals and volunteers to bring recovery to the area. The museum is set-up in what is a very basic building, the walls of which are covered in photos and handwritten information cards/posters. There are also a number of artefacts from that time. There is no fee although one can give donations. Whilst this museum is a worthy effort by people with few resources and little (if any) funding, it raises key questions in my mind. As this tsunami had a such a massive impact on Sri Lanka, and the lives of its people and so many visitors, why has the government not taken on this project to create better conditions and a more professional structure for visitors? Also visitors should be warned that there are drastic graphic images that will shock and upset. Whilst these scenes were of course an inevitable result of the tsunami and may have a place here, I question whether the relatives of the dead are aware there loved ones are displayed in public. Apart from this, everyone should get closer to what happened here and this place does that in massive measure.

Title: Over-whelming.
Text: Such an eye-opening, over-whelming experience. The tsunami holds a very tense atmosphere, but is very informative and touching.

Title: Must visit! Very humblng
Text: This museum was run by a really sweet lady who had lost her house to the tsunami and has converted a part of her new home into this photo museum. She took us around all the photos and shared first hand stories. Very humbling experience and I would suggest that anyone who is visiting hikkaduwa should go and see this place.

Title: Humbling
Text:
This fascinating pictorial museum really brought home the devastation of the Boxing Day Tsunami. It is stunning to consider the power of the tsunami so far away from it's epicentre. Our guide was informative and had personal experience which is clearly still raw as she showed us the rubble of her home.
This free to visit museum is well worth a visit to truly understand what happened in a country that had never seen a tsunami before........

Title: An important part of recent history
Text:
We arriver that small museum on our way from Galle north.Stoppeed for 20-30 minutes, it can take longer than that, still it made us understand the great dissaster od 2004 tsunami.  
The exhibition is simple, only 4 rooms. The first explain about tsunami and hoe it happens. two more rooms show pictures of the ruins it lefet behind, some of them are hard to watch (dead bodies) and another shows the rescue teams and there work.All have english explantions, and there is a mon working there and explains all about the pictures.
You go out somone else from this small simple museum

Title: Very informative
Text: This was free to visit. It was very informative about the devastation of the tsunami. There is lots of information and pictures. There is a donation box where you can leave a donation which we were happy to.

Title: Educational, very upsetting in parts
Text: A little house of photos which show the terrible impact of a natural disaster. Some photos were quite upsetting and not for the sensitive Educational if a little basic but worth a visit if you're passing by. Free entrance but a donation in the box is encouraged

Title: Inspirational
Text: We visited the museum with our 3 children aged 18, 15 and 8 and were truly humbled by the courage and determination of the people affected by this tragedy. We shed a few tears whilst in there but wouldn't have missed this experience as the people who run it are so special. This is such an important place to visit and a donation will help so much with all their work.

Title: One Word - Moving
Text:
Stopped here on the way to Galle. I remember this disaster, and whilst our driver talked about this on the way, it was not until we visited the museum, that you get a true sense of the scale of the devastation the country faced.
Agree the building could do with some modernisation, but it is almost a reflection of the destruction the coastline suffered

Title: Very Moving Experience
Text: If you are in this area you must take time out and visit this photo museum. We were shown round by a lovely lady whose family survived but who lost friends and extended family. It is a stark reminder of the power of nature and a testament to the very many lives that were lost all over Sri Lanka and especially in this are on that fateful day. Slightly run down and disorganised and photos could do with renewing but well worth the visit and the donations given  are well spent.

Title: A must in Hikkaduwa!
Text:
Regardless if you are on holiday, travelling solo, or in Sri Lanka for a business purpose - this is something worth visiting. If you do not fully understand what a tsunami is nor what the effects were when it happened, you will after taking a look round the museum. It hits every emotion you have but again you then fully understand what this country experienced and with that, you can empathise with the place and people. 

The women who showed us around is incredible for having strength to look at these photographs and talk to individuals about this everyday. 

This is a free event although you can donate at the end of your time there.

Title: impressive yet under developed
Text: The content of the museum is impressive , the package leaves some room for improvement. The museum is literally a collection of laminated photo's that mostly show the aftermath of the Xmas 2004 tsunami here. Devastating outcome with the destroyed train that left 1270 people dead. How to improve ( i I may offer some advice) create a story line (one of the inhabitants or a virtual train  traveler) and have a small scale 3D model (maquette) of the area/ That would impress.

Title: So sad
Text: A must  when in Hikkaduwa.  Very informative - excellent at creating awareness - so sad to learn what happened.  Please note that one of the rooms (about the 3rd room you go into) has a wall that is covered with a veil - behind this veil are photos of dead bodies.  Not very nice but is there to bring awareness.  be aware of this room if with young children as they do not need to see those photos.  Lucky we were warned before hand so we knew not to let our 7 yr old see that wall x

Title: A real insight into the devastation of the tsunami that hit Sri Lanka
Text:
Before we arrived in Sri Lanka I had heard about this museum. I wanted to go to visit and try to get more of a understanding of what happened during this sad time. 
I was over whelmed with heart ache at the destruction and loss this community had suffered. The photos told a heart breaking story of the events that took place. There was a lovely man there that will talk you through the pictures and you can offer a donation if you like. I wish I could do more but if you gone to hikkaduwa please visit and give a little help. The people here are so wonderful and despite going through this horrific time they stay positive, strong and very determined to build there town back together.

Title: impossible to be un-moved
Text: Don't go past this museum, the photos and stories are jaw-dropping.   It is an authentic and captivating experience.

Title: Amazing must see
Text:
This is a must visit for everyone how goes to Hikkaduwa. To see the devastation caused by the tsunami and hear and read first hand stories from the people that actually lived through such a traumatic experience was both harrowing and moving. This is a free museum but there is a donation box by the exit which goes to a local charity every month. 

NB: Some of the pictures may not be suitable for small children

Title: Very interesting
Text: The visit at tsunami museum was very informative! The lady told me about everything that happened in Hikkaduwa during the tsunami and showed me pictures! Thank you for received me friendly!

Title: A worthwhile visit
Text: Whilst entry is free, a donation is expected and if just a small amount can buy something for an orphaned child, then it is worthwhile.  Some of the photos were pretty harrowing but the staff at the Museum were highly knowledgeable and the first room is very educational.

Title: A reminder of what this area has been through!
Text: Take a few mins in a tuktuk to check this very moving place out. It's nothing flash, just a couple of rooms with picture lined walls..however these pictures are very real and a stark reminder just how bad that day was for these people who lost everything

Title: Tsunami community museum visit
Text: An extremely moving experience. The museum is run by an amazing couple that together with their children survived the tsunami. They have an amazing story to tell so please speak to them. There are 4 rooms. The first one details the science of how tsunamis happen. The second has tragic pictures of the train disaster. The back room has pictures drawn by child survivors of the tsunami. The other room has some very graphic pictures which may not be suitable for children but is important as it gives an accurate account of the horror of what happened. The museum is free to enter but we left a donation in the box. The couple who run it are amazing people and it's worth going in to speak to them.

Title: Very informative
Text: Seeing all of the photos really brought it home to you what these people went through...very though provoking and it was lovely to get first accounts of their awful tragedy from the mouth of the lady who lost everything, but has  gathered all of the photos and memorabilia of that awful Boxing Day  so that  those lost will never be forgotten.

Title: Tsunami Museum - Hikkaduwa
Text:
The tsunami museum at Hikkaduwa is a community museum and is a remembrance of the devastating tsunami that had hit the island nation in 2004.  The museum has many heart moving photographs of the aftermath of the tsunami. Some of the phots are very graphic but depict the harsh reality of the wreck, the tsunami had caused.

The museum also provides basic information regarding a tsunami and is a place of developing tsunami awareness. Do visit this place as a mark of respect to the victims of the tsunami.

Title: Worth Visiting.
Text:
The museum is a run by a lady who survived the Tsunami, she can tell you about her story. There are many pictures showing the effects of the natural disaster in the local area.

There is a comments book and donation book.

The museum is about 3KM from Hikkaduwa Beach.

Title: Very moving
Text:
The lady who ran the museum was amazing to listen to. Her stories as a survivor were gut wrenching. 

The images left me an emotional wreck but worth every moment. 

Thank you for preserving such memories, to give us an insight of what you went through. 

I loved our visit.

Title: Eye opening and harrowing but a must visit
Text:
I was quite shocked at how much effort and work had gone into creating what from the outside looks like someone's house. The museum itself is very informative starting by educating those that are not aware of how Tsunamis occur, how they are measured, the warning systems now in place etc. The museum then goes onto focus on the specific disaster in Sri Lanka, the effects, the clean-up and the continued efforts to try and repair the extensively damaged communities across the Island.

I would say prepare yourself for the pictures which are truly harrowing and bring to life what really happened in Sri Lanka. It was very very sad but then again what do you expect.

The museum asked for a donation to be put towards the upkeep of the museum and to support affected communities both of which I consider to be very worthwhile causes.

Title: Very informative - a must visit
Text: As reviewed by others this is a must visit if you are in the area as it is extremely informative for a very small museum.  Some of the pictures are very harrowing but it does convey the real effect of the tsunami.  The community volunteers that staff the museum were wonderful and were keen to explain the facts and figures as well as related real stories. No entry fee but donations encouraged.

Title: Informative but harrowing
Text: This is nothing more than a three room bungalow with pictures of the tsunami disaster. The first room has charts (and some images) and models - like a young kids classroom - breaking down the science of a tsunami, with the next few rooms floor to ceiling lamented pictures of before, after, and grim pictures of mass graves or washed up dead. You'll be in and out pretty quickly, though you'll inevitably leave a donation (it's free entry)... probably in the thousands of rupees.

Title: Tsunami Museum
Text: Real pictures of the death, agony and pain of the people of Sri Lanka displayed in the museum, visit and donate for a good cause.

Title: Heartbreaking
Text: This museum is small with lots of photos from the disaster on the walls. I feel that even though it lacks in size it is an important visit because acknowledgement of a tragedy helps with community healing. It is a museum that will leave you feeling incredibly sad. On the drive there you will also see the monument where the train was swept of the tracks that took at least 1700 lives. Just a warning for those with children or those affected by trauma that there are many photos of bodies of the deceased as they were found, which could be disturbing.

Title: Very sad but educational
Text: It is important to not let the tragedy be forgotten and learn from it.  Just be a bit careful since some rooms have graphic photos not appropriate for kids.

Title: Utterly moving
Text:
A really raw and emotional experience to visit this museum, talk to the owner who clearly still sees the horror of that day in her eyes, and read the stories that bring home what happened that day.  

There is no entrance fee, but a donation box to support the upkeep of the simple museum and also she told us towards cancer medicine for the local community.

Both my wife and I found it a truly moving experience and would recommend everyone in the area to visit.

Title: Thought provoking
Text: Well worth a visit to this simple yet poignant collection. The photos and stories made us all reflect on what must have been an utterly terrifying time for anyone caught up in the tsunami.

Title: A must visit museum if you are staying close to Galle
Text: Not what we were expecting, but even better for it. The exhibition is really well put together, the photos are hard hitting but communicate the devastation caused by the tsunami. The stories are heart rending, and we all left the museum in quiet reflection.

Title: Gives a good impression of the terrible tsunami
Text: It's a relatively small museum with a lot of photo's taken after the tsunami take place. Some really moving pictures. It was one of the stops of our Daytour. If you pass this place a stop is recommended to see it yourself.

Title: informative
Text: We are glad that we took the time to visit this museum . lots of of photographs (some may be disturbing) of the havoc created by the Tsunami. The lady in charge is a survivor and told us her story .

Title: Glad we stopped off....
Text:
Whilst our trip around Sri Lanka our children where made more aware of the Tsunami in 2004, and they both asked a lot of questions throughout our stay. We tried to explain as much as we could without too much information for their little minds, but as children the questions kept coming....

We visited the Tsunami Museum on passing, we travelled with our 3 children 22 month old, 6&7 year old, I'm really glad we stopped off, we where able to explain in more detail what happened in 2004,  there are lots of pictures and information here to help children understand.

Visiting the museum and surrounding area really made them understand more as to what happened when the terrible Tsunami hit in 2004, This Museum is a lovely way to raise awareness and also remember those who sadlylost their lives and homes.

NOTE: In one of the rooms in the Museum, there are many photos showing dead bodies, we didnt let our children see these photos so be prepared and ask one of the volunteers to close the netted curtains if taking children..

Its is an emotional place but very glad we stopped off. There is no fee to enter, there is a donation box.

Title: Lots of info and photos.. Well worth the visit
Text: We visited here after the turtle hatchery as it was not far.. It was full of information and the photos followed the journey from just before the tsunami struck, to the people helping to rehabilitate children who lost their parents and families. It's a very emotional place and if in Hikkaduwa I think this is one not to miss. There is no fee to look but there is a donation box, and a lovely lady showed and explained everything to us.

Title: must visit location
Text: it is very sad to hear about the tsunami that happend 12 years ago, in the museum you can visualize all the horror the people went trough, you can't stay nonshlant to the pictures , the museum is free of charge but a donation will be appriciated.

Title: Lest we Forget
Text:
Having visited Sri Lanka the year before this disaster, I just had to go to comprehend
the magnitude of what happened when the Tsunami struck.
The exhibition is a testament to those who suffered the loss of loved ones, and somehow have managed to move on.

Title: Memories
Text: This small museum is informative and the lady in charged who had lost her home in the tsunami was glad to answer any questions I had. It all seemed so recent not over 12 years ago. We must never forget the power of nature and remember the people whose lives were lost.

Title: A real eye opener
Text:
This place gives a real insight of what effect the Tsunami had on the local area and the local people.  Lots of images of before, during and after the Tsunami along with accounts of people who were involved.  A must see if in the area.  
(Some of the images are not suitable for young children)

Title: Eye-opening
Text: Before going to the museum, I was not very familiar with the details of the 2004 tsunami. The exhibit provides you with information about tsunamis and how they're formed before you view photos of the tsunami. Just beware that some of the photos are graphic. Overall, I recommend that anyone who visits Hikkaduwa stops by here.

Title: Heartbreaking but a must see if in area
Text: Stayed in Hikkaduwa for 2 weeks and travelled via tuk tuk to this museum.  Absolutely heartbreaking and it brought tears to my eyes within minutes of entering as I read personal accounts of that dreadful day.  The strength these people have shown in the aftermath is truly amazing. Please show your support and visit this little museum - just remember to take a tissue or two!

Title: Good for a visit, museum is run by people who were affected by the Tsunami
Text: This is a small family run museum, full of photos and newpaper cuttings from the day the Tsunami hit and the aftermath is caused. Very moving visit and pics of our hotel under water really brought it home to us how badly damaged the area was and in some places still is. 10,000 still missing 40,000 dead just  in Sri Lanka.. No charge to go in, just donations if you want to that they sent to support local cancer treatments

Title: Very moving
Text: The lady who runs the museum is lovely it's a collection of pictures photos and drawings that tell the story of the Tsunami and its aftermath well worth a visit although some of the pictures are a bit graphic. Free to enter but there's a donation box.

Title: Gud Place to visit
Text: Gud Place to visit and help us know the how god controls  us not we control our future . and helps to know the what is Tsunami and how it actually divested human lifes in a such huge manner

Title: Good photographic coverage of the disaster
Text: Set in the home of a tsunami victim. Not what you would expect a museum to look like but well worth a visit. Good photographic coverage and written experiences of local area

Title: Take the short Tuk Tuk ride here!
Text:
A visit here was a solemn reminder of the volatility of Mother Nature. 

The museum is very informative, the first room basically explains the cause and effects of a Tsunami while the next rooms have pictures of the destruction the beautiful ocean across the road caused.

The pictures are very graphic but still somewhere I would recommend to take children depending on their sensitivity levels. The pictures tell a story of disaster but also of the people coming together.

It is worth a moment of your time, and although it is free to visit they do have a donation box for visitors.

Title: An absolute must
Text: This is an incredibly raw museum of pictures and stories. Completely heart breaking but something everyone should do.

Title: Don't pass this by ... heartbreaking but everyone should see the efftects of Tsunami 2004
Text: It's impossible not to be moved by the pictures shown  here !  The sense of loss and helplessness is huge. We couldn't think how we would have reacted in such circumstances.

Title: Moving and informative - worth a visit
Text:
Visited this museum after the turtle sanctuary, it's free to look around but they do have a donation box I recommend you contribute to. 

The lady managing the place was caught in the tsunami and had to run from it with her two year old son and ten year old daughter, she spoke freely about how terrifying it was and explained she couldn't find her daughter for four days afterwards. It was so interesting to get a first hand account of what happened that day, I had no idea Sri Lanka had been so badly affected by the tsunami.

Just a warning to those with small children, the third room has some graphic photographs of bodies piled up waiting for burial etc but it definitely makes you realise how tsunami has touched everyone's lives here.

Make time for this place, you only need an hour but it makes it all the more humbling that people in southern province are so hospitable when they've spent the last 12 years rebuilding everything from the ground up.

Title: Once visited never forgotten
Text:
we visited the museum after a day trip to galle I'm glad we didn't visit first as this museum has very graphic images of the destruction  caused by tsunami the train with 1200 people on board was hit just behind the museum and the devastation of the local area is all visible through photographs,
very informative on how the tsunami happened with models showing different stages and the final room with the childrens pictures and ther interpretation of things, 
this was a very moving place

Title: A Very Touching Experience
Text: Avery graphic and moving experience or the 2004 Tsunami and descriptions of how it was caused, and photos and narrative of the effect it had on the coast and up to 3 KM inland. Also how the coast recovered from it.

Title: Touching
Text: Our tuk-tukdriver took us to this museum. So glad that he did, though it was a heartbreaking experience. It gave us a deeper insight in the tragedy.

Title: heart wrenching
Text: never knew how badly this affected so many people we had tears in our eyes from reading the stories mmmmmm

Title: Very Moving Experience
Text:
There is not a lot more that I could add that has been already said. 

This is a very personal experiences, which I found to be very moving....A period of reflection and respect. A tragedy I hope we have learned the lessons from.

Title: Heartfelt experience
Text:
Based in the shell of the house of one of the tsunami survivors in hikkaduwa is this very real and sobering experience of many survivors, from mothers that lost their children, children that were orphaned as well as people that are still looking for loved ones as their bodies were never found. The photos, stories and even pictures drawn by small children all help to piece together the tragic events that took place.
A really humbling experience.

Title: Very moving
Text: If you are travelling to or through Hikkaduwa, take some time to stop at this little 'museum'. It houses a collection of photographs, from truly harrowing scenes to those of hope and camaraderie, together with information following the Tsunami which hit the west coast on 26/12/2004.

Title: Harrowing experience
Text: We happened upon this museum by accident. It was set up in someone's house and was a truly raw experience. Well worth a visit and a great lady to support.

Title: a short visit
Text: it is a small building with three rooms. the first room is geographically informative, but as you progress through the rooms - the photos become much more harrowing and intense. it is worth stopping by if you are in the area, and nice to leave a donation.

Title: A very humbling and moving experience.
Text: This was a 'must see' for us as we were in Sri Lanka just one month before the tsunami hit in 2004. It was a very moving experience to see the photographs and read the firsthand experiences of the local people. Their resilience and fortitude in the face of such a disaster is an example to us all.

Title: Very moving - its her own home
Text: Entering the place we were welcomed by the woman running the place. Its was her home. She told her story, and the pictures of her and her lost family form before the tzunami. "We did not have a word for it, most people ran into the countryside when the water withdrew after the first wave". Yes, and unfortunately many fled to the train standing on the rails just behind the city. 1.700 drowned when the train was hit by the second wave. The museum holds a lot of heartbreaking pictures, and some very tough pictures of bodies scattered all over. Grab your young children by the hand, when visiting. And hold tight.

Title: Very moving
Text: Some of the photos in this museum documenting the tsunami are shockingly graphic but important if you want to try to understand what the poor local community went through and it's nice that the tour ends with stories of rehabilitation and the warning system they now have in place.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We found it really interesting learning about tsunamis. It was also quite harrowing and very sad seeing the true picture and hearing the stories of what happened and peoples lives who survived. Really worth a visit.

Title: Great explanation, friendly
Text: Very friendly guide who gave us a good explanation about the whole theme. Emotional photos to show how dramatic the Tsunami was.

Title: Very informative and moving
Text: A great little museum that provides an excellent explanation of what happened and how it happened. Some harrowing photos - but important to see these so you can actually get some small idea of what things were actually like. Highly recommended for all.

Title: Poignant and ultimately uplifting...
Text:
Both fascinating and horrifying to get at least some sense of the awfulness of the 2004 tsunami and its impact.  
And, at the same time, how the local people have risen to the challenge of dealing with future potential natural disasters given the place that they live in.
Poignant and disturbing and ultimately uplifting.  make sure you spend time to understand 
the geology of what happened
impact on the people
how they recovered and
what they have done to remember those who died...

Title: Sad but worthwhile visit
Text: This a truly humbling experience into the terrible day the Tsunami hit Sri Lanka. The lady who tells the story lost family members to the disaster. She explains how the Tsunami happened. There are some graphic pictures at the end but she does tell you and if you would prefer not to see them then that's OK. I would recommend this as it makes you be thankful for your life ??

Title: Recommended to understand their history
Text: Very touching place to know the story of the tsunami in Sri Lanka. You first get information about how a tsunami arises and then based on photos and the stories of the owner you get a clear picture of how it went down that day en the days after. Very recommended if you are in the neighbourhood. It is part of their history now.

Title: very informative museum
Text:
a place to visit and respect.
 It tells the entire story of the Tsunami with lots of pictures and a thourough explanation by a very friendly lady. The most impressive pictures hang on a wall that can be closed off with a curtain in case children come to visit too. 
They do a great job by teaching the tsunami victimes as well as their children to open themselves up by drawing, painting and talking about it. 
Really worth visiting.

Title: Nice museum with good info
Text: It's a small museum located next to the Galle Road just past the 'city center'. Its a harsh but necessary reality check with the horrors of the tsunami disaster. The way this museum contributes to the historical preservation of the events surrounding the disaster, but also the beautiful examples of humanitarian aid and help from everybody in the world regardless of skin color or religious believes are worth the visit. You'll be humbled and deeply touched in one visit. The guides do their best to explain the details of the pictures and the artifacts to you.

Title: Emotion and impactful
Text: I would highly recommend visiting the museum if you are in the area. The staff are helpful and give plenty of information to you. Its heartbreaking to revisit how this has impacted people in Sri Lanka and a truly important experience.

Title: Ok, a bit more modernity re didactics needed
Text: Gives a brief overview what happened in 2004. A bit more interaction would be needed in order to give here a clearer view what desaster struck the costal area then.

Title: Folk Museum
Text: Located in Koggala, Sri Lanka, is a large museum complex that dipicts the culture and life of rural Sri Lanka.  The artifacts exhibited related o the arts and crafts, folk art and folk life of locals.  Clothing, jewelry, folk games, medical devices, transport (wagons, canoes and carts) religious artifacts and education tools are displayed in the many different buildings.  The house where Martin Wickramasinghe was born is an important part of the complex and is a home typical of the headman, teacher, and the native physician during the 19th century. A library containing the works of the writer is located at the entrance.  Plan on 1-2 hours if you slowly browse--1 hours if you hurry through.  Not much of interest for children in my opinion.

Title: Inspirational experience
Text: If you want to get a glimpse into Sri Lankan literature and charm of life in Sri Lanka, this is a place to visit.

Title: So much to see
Text: We thought it was a small place but it was huge! Lots of different sections in many different buildings. Thought wed be an hour - 3 hours later we had nearly finished! Really interesting.

Title: Very Good
Text: We have stayed close to here many times but never visited so our friend to us. It worth a visit to see the old traditions and how people lived. Plus of course the birth place and house of Martin Wickramasinghe. Really enjoyed it.

Title: A good guide really helps
Text:
We visited twice a few weeks apart.  On the second occasion our guide was totally disinterested and explained very little, totally unlike that of our first visit.   

This place is a combination of the first homeplace of Wickramasinghe and has exhibits relating to his life and work.  It is also an interesting folk museum with exhibits relating to local life, work, crafts and culture over the centuries.

Title: A bit run down
Text: Some interesting artefacts and the staff are helpful with explanations. The garden is pretty. Unfortunately it all feels a bit run down. No photos of exhibits allowed.

Title: A very interesting place to visit.
Text: Martin Wickramainghe is a very important writer and person in the development of the modern Sri Lanka. Most of the museum is display of Sri Lankan folklore, but the house he was born in is very interesting. Most of his books, translated into English can be purchased at the museum.

Title: A good guide is important
Text: We visited this place with a group. Its a lovely place, great historical artefacts and fantastic flora. It was a nice stay however I missed a little bit the background information. Our guide was (in my view) average and I wounder if another guide could have made more out of it.

Title: No A/C, rather hot and no fresh air in the rooms, historically interesting
Text: We participated in a hotel excursion combined with a river road trip to local people harvesting and selling cinnamon. The museum has a nice collection but the items are rather dusty. So I did not take pics. Bring your own water bottle. The garden is also nice but some trees are affected by mushrooms.

Title: A wonderful overview of Sri Lankan life and history.
Text:
2000 or so LKR got us a return tuk tuk trip from Unawatuna to the museum and lake on a rainy morning. We spent an hour and half guided around the place by a knowledgeable elderly gentleman who really brought the exhibits to life. Set in a garden with many specimen trees, most of the place is undercover so perfect for us that day.
I would thoroughly recommend it- I know so much more now about the country and the remarkable man who created it. Beats sitting in a bar all day!

Title: A good look at traditional crafts
Text: We were unprepared for how large this complex is--it's really practically a whole village with multiple displays in multiple buildings.  A very nice guide attached himself to us but unfortunately he really wanted to show us everything and we were tired and eager to move on to our next stop.  I really appreciated all the labels on things, even the trees.

Title: Fantastic overview of Sri Lankan cultural history
Text: I had never heard of this prolific author when our driver suggested this place. We very much enjoyed the museum's artifacts, as well as learning about Wickramasinghe's story and seeing his birthplace.Well worth an hour or so of your time.

Title: Window into the culture of the past
Text:
An interesting place with many artifacts from colonial and pre-colonial Ceylon. It commemorates the life and times of one of Sri Lanka's best and prolific authors and contains many souvenirs and photos of his life. He wanted the culture to be remembered and collected much of the contents.
Presentation is quite good and the exhibits well displayed; although the whole place is a little tired. 
We were assisted by a guide who helped a little. We did not ask for him but he sort of latched on to us as we arrived. No commercial arrangement was discussed until the end, and inevitably he was not totally happy with my tip. I had to explain the essence of contract law.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: An interesting collection of both Sri Lankan life and the life of Martin Wickramasinghe, worth an hour or so of your time, a minute's walk from the main road, lovely gardens.

Title: A nice history lesson
Text: We spent a little over an hour at this museum, and it was a good way to learn about the history and culture of Sri Lanka. I found it especially interesting how this one house has survived only because a British officer's wife had decided to use it as her personal quarters. The amount of effort that has gone into putting the museum together and keeping it running is commendable, but the place could do with a little bit of a clean up now. Overall, a good thing to do if you're keen on understanding a little more about the folk history of the area.

Title: History
Text: A old house and surroundings converted into museum and maintained beautifully. You will get sense of true Lankan culture here

Title: Fascinating trip back in time but needs a bit of a polish!
Text: A really interesting collection of artefacts which really help to illustrate Sri Lankan culture and folk history. Some items could do with a bit of a clean and polish, but nevertheless this museum is well worth a stop-off on your way along the south coast, or as a half-day excursion from Galle.

Title: A  must visit place
Text: A very historic place of an exceptional man who lead the Sri Lankan literature to the international level. A very educational place for people of all ages. The extended museum carries many different varieties of history. Do pay a visit when you visit Galle or when you pass by further towards the Southern side of Sri Lanka.

Title: Rustic Museum
Text: Great little museum with some cool rustic artifacts and a good deal on the author himself. Just up the road is the airfield/strip where the Catalinas used to fly out of in WW2. Theres a DC3 aircraft which you can explore in the resturant just up the road.

Title: Must Visit Place (if you are around)
Text: The museum complex is an excellent place to know more about folk culture and history of Sri Lanka. Surely a place to spend 2-3 hours soaking in all the information you can get from artifacts there. We were lucky to meet with a very helpful employee of the museum who gave us detailed knowledge about various part of the museum and gave us enough time on each of the exhibitions.

Title: Great place for school children
Text: This is the place where one of prominent Sri Lankan novelist & creative writer Martin Wickramasinghe spent his life. Folk museum located in Koggala around 15-20kms from Galle towards to Matara. Every Sri Lankan school children must visit place.

Title: Leonardfamilyvacay
Text: Excellent cultural experience. Well worth the visit to learn more of such a scholar and books he authored.

Title: Local writer
Text:
Martin Wickramasinghe" delved into the life and culture of our people from their early beginning to the present day and through his writings, he identified our folk culture as a resilient bonding substance which has not only prevented our social disintegration and alienation, despite assimilation of elements from a multitude of eastern and western cultures, but also moulded our collective identity and values as a people. Wickramasinghes unceasing intellectual exploration and his creative and critical writings relating to the life and culture of the people of Sri Lanka continued for a period of over 70 years.
The Folk museum is an ideal place to get to know the author better, to understand a little of what Koggala and its people meant to him. Wickramasinghes writings vividly recall the carefree days of his childhood, exploring the marine life in the Koggala reef, playing with his friends from the village and enjoying the rural solitude of his beloved Koggala. Seated on the steps of Wickramasinghes ancestral home, and enjoying the blessed charm of this seven acre piece of rural paradise, it is easy to understand why this piece of earth nurtured and set ablaze the imagination of one of this countrys greatest writers.

Title: A small insight in Sri Lankas history
Text: The museum is based on the life of one of Sri Lankas most famous writers; their so called Shakespeare. The museum consists of his original house and many items and photos from his life. However most interesting part for us was the collection of historical items from the Portugese, Dutch and English periods. One of the guides told us, very proudly, about the history of his country. It was definitely worth visiting If you are in this area (visiting time approx. 2-3 hours).

Title: Great place to learn about Sri Lankan traditions
Text: We really had a good time at this museum.  We had a guide take us all the way through, showing us the collection of the Sri Lankan writer, Milton Wickramasinghe, who wrote over 100 books about life in Sri Lanka.  He was an avid collector of all things Sri Lankan and this museum houses that collection.  Jewelry, kitchen implements, vehicles, everything under the sun.  If you have time and have an interest in the culture of Sri Lanka, please go here.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: This museum is well worth a visit if you're staying in or around Koggala. Not expensive at time of our visit 200 rupees approx £1.00. It is housed in a number of buildings and features various objects showing the life and styles of the local people including various carts, boats, dress etc. Interestingly this area was covered by many dwellings which during the 2nd world war was evacuated within 24 hours to built an airfield and only the Martin Wickramasinghe house remains..

Title: Martin Wickramasinghe's collection of masks, artifacts of village life are lovingly maintained and displayed.
Text: Martin Wickramasinghe was an author and leading intellectual in early 20th century Sri Lanka.  He and his wife created a trust museum to protect his collections, and the house in which he was born.  Religious objects, as well as farming implements, musical instruments, masks & puppets, medical tools, canoes and fishing traps and vehicles pulled by animals are among the artifacts displayed in cases.  Some rooms and furnishings and a coconut oil mill are also on the grounds.  We visited the Wickramasinghe Museum of Folk Culture on a day tour that also included the Handunugoda Tea Factory.  We traveled by tuk tuk from Galle Fort.

Title: A surprising and interesting find
Text:
We found this a fascinating place and knowing nothing about this man was surprised at his life.
It is not a normal experience for overseas visitors we surmise but the old buildings and gardens are a haven from all the other busy things that are now are going on all around. Great for seeing the old ways of life in Sri Lanka and lots of interesting birds all around in the garden.
Very good value and so pleased we made the effort.

Title: An unexpected surprise
Text: This museum was a pleasant surprise. I was staying in a hotel in Koggala in 3 minute walking distance from the museum but postponed the visit until the end of my vacation as I didn't think the museum was really worthy. It was a mistake. I really liked the collection of traditional Sri Lankan masks, the wooden statue of the demon king Ravana and lots of other exhibits. The territory of the museum compex is also quite extensive and very pleasant to walk. Photography inside the buildings is prohibited, but you can take pictures outside in the park. The entrance fee is 200 LKR (about 1,3 USD).

Title: Wonderful exhibits and very informative
Text: This museum has a partially renovated home where the Sri Lankan author was born in 1890, as well as his burial site.  Today, the museum contains various folk artifacts from throughout Sri Lanka's history, including costumes, musical instruments, giant puppets (my favorite), masks and kitchen utensils.

Title: Excellent folk art museum
Text: This museum is dedicated to Sri Lanka folk arts. Well thought out and offers qa lot of long lost games, traditions etc. Superb collection of 19 century masks. lovely garden... well worth the visit if you are in koggala area.

Title: Folk museum
Text: We visited  museum  on April  2016. It's  nice and  small  museum  in folk style.  As for a foreigner  it was  interesting to  see  old money, dishes, clothes, religious things, old village  houses, transportation. I  recommend to visit.

Title: Excellent small museum
Text:
It costs next to nothing to go in, the grounds of MW's house are extensive, cool and tranquil, the folk museum is beautifully presented and fascinating, and was improved by the guide who adopted us and explained the exhibits. The house with all MW's mementos is also interesting as the displays are so personal.

So for a bite sized insight into Sri Lankan history, culture and life this museum can hardly be faulted. It's all on the flat, so no problems there, we were there for about an hour and a half, and came away with change from 1000 rupees, having paid the entrance fee, a tip for the guide and bought a book. Take a bottle of water, no refreshments there, and no photos inside the exhibitions.

So, it's cheap, pleasant and informative, go there!

Title: Great museum
Text: This is a beautifully curated museum, full of interesting artefacts and information in English as well as Sinhala. I was drawn to it because of Martin Wickramsinghe's role in authoring many books in Sinhala and enjoyed reading his most popular children's book, Madol Doova (translated into English!)

Title: Fantastic little place; rich with nostalgia and atmosphere in beautiful gardens
Text: We loved this place and would have stayed longer than 1 hour if we hadn't come so late as they close at 5pm. The artefacts are displayed really well with lots of descriptions in a English. An older gentleman led us round and explained things to us at no extra charge to the entrance fee, he is obviously proud of his heritage and of the museum. He was very informative. Lots of fishing and farming implements, lace making, gem cutting tools, jewellery, some clothes and a fabulous room full of masks and puppets which was really impressive. You can also wander around the famous Sri Lankan writer's home and see the old bedrooms and his writing desk and many photographs of Wickramasinghe, his family and visiting dignitaries, a selection of old books on display. A genuinely charming place with loads of character and a lot of atmosphere in his old house. We really enjoyed it; not a stuffy museum experience at all. The gardens are beautiful and shy grey langur monkeys were watching us from high in the palm trees. Definitely visit this place, it's like being taken back in time to old Sri Lanka....loved it.

Title: Well worth visiting even if not heavy into literature
Text:
Visited the museum with 40 girls from the Anula Girls Orphanage and everyone thoroughly enjoyed the morning out. 
Museum has loads of interesting items and gives an excellent history of Sri Lankan life and its development over the years. Was particularly impressed with the boats and the monsoon wind furnace!.
Nice seating area if you fancy a rest in the shade, and Martin W. original house was a great representation of what life must have been like many years ago.
All in all, a real hidden gem I would say as not that widely publicised as worth a visit. Not as grand as the Galle Museum, but definitely worth a look for anyone looking for something to do for a morning or afternoon.

Title: very interesting place
Text: interesting museum wqith large collection of old dancing masks and carts and forms of transport from the 19 century. I loved the elephant drawn cart which is like the trucks of a hundred years ago!

Title: Great museum in a beautiful setting..worth a visit
Text: Our group toured the museum and it was an insight to the folk life of the Sri Lanka people as written by Martin Wickramasinghe.  Nicely layed out with many artifacts....we had our own guide but there was a local gentleman who was very eager to show and tell us about this place...he was very proud.  The gounds are beautiful and the huge trees provided welcome shade.

Title: Absolute must visit.
Text: One of the most important writers that Sri Lanka has ever produced lived here in this very house. His writing was of highest order and depicted the reality of Sri Lankan folk life and its contrast to upcoming Sri Lankan elite capitalist class. His knowledge of society and common wisdom is unmatched. This place showcases the real Martin Wickramasinghe. The land surrounding the house was much bigger in 1980's. Now the Koggala trade zone has taken over some part of it.

Title: Eclectic but fascinating
Text: This museum in Koggola near Unawatuna is a fascinating collection of Sri Lankan culture: great artifacts housed in Wickramasinghe's property.  There is a particularly good collection of  masks, some of which show old colonials, and jewelry.   The exhibits are poorly dated with little information, but a guide approached us and filled us in on the details.  There was a good model of an ancient Sri Lankan tank, used for irrigation; it did explain why some national parks are based round a 'tank'.  It was the only time we saw a snake: its tail was hanging from the coconut palm roof of a model house!  Lovely grounds - peaceful despite the large number of school visits.

Title: Lovely museum in beautiful surroundings
Text:
This museum is built around Martin Wickramasinghe's house - you can visit his house and pause to reflect on where this far-sighted Sri Lankan legend and his family lived.

The museum itself is informative with a variety of displays.  You can learn about the engineering feat that established the 'tanks' that serviced irrigation in the dry central zone of Sri Lanka 4 centuries BC as well as enjoying a vivid display of masks ranging from the old and traditional to the modern and current.  Archeological explorations are revealing the nature of Sri Lankan culture from prehistoric times.

We were helped to understand aspects of Buddhism and Sinhalese culture by a knowledgeable gentleman - the exhibits are not comprehensively labelled in English (but then the British Museum doesn't label all its displays in Sinhala does it?).  He didn't expect payment either!

The grounds are lovely too, beautifully tended with many of the trees labelled with their scientific names.  A thoroughly fulfilling visit which I would recommend without hesitation!

Title: A Must Visit
Text: If you are interested in The Folk Lore of Sri Lanka then this is a must visit Museum.Martin Wickramasinghe left a legacy of knowledge for the people of Sri Lanka to enjoy forever.

Title: Must Visit in the South
Text: Incredible collection of Sri Lankan folk art. The collection of 19 century masks, especially those of various communities, British officials etc. are very rare and fascinating. So is the collection of the carts and various forms of transport. Set in a huge garden, the museum is a treasure trove of folk art . It is also interesting to see how they have preserved everything of Sri Lanka's foremost author including his old house.

Title: Interesting if you know of him
Text: Unless you are familiar with his work, it will only give you an insight into the tools/culture during his era. Even a slight bit of familiarity with his subject will provide greater context to the exhibits

Title: don't miss this most interesting folk museum
Text: it's a delightful and interesting place that just goes on and on. You should have a guide with you to explain what you see or you will probably miss out. Lots of trees that are well marked shade the walk ways (it's HOT). the museum does a good job of depicting the medieval and ancient cultures, etc. Loved the masks and displays of old boats, carriages, etc. in particular. Don't miss the birth place and living place of Martin Wickramasinghe - a little house. You have to take off your shoes but if you don't want to do that you can walk around the house and peer inside the windows to get a little glimpse.

Title: very interesting
Text: sadly you do get an individual tour guide which may be more thorough than you'd like, but there is an awful lot of interesting stuff here. The guide did not want a tip! refreshing.

Title: Nice little exibit from late Martin Wickramasinghe
Text: That is a great place to visit if you want to get an idea of life in Sri Lanka 100 years ago. One of the best writers, SrI lanka was ever gifted. The place is really beautiful. Please do not visit this palce if you do not want to see southern Sri Lankan village 100 years ago.

Title: Fascinating
Text:
We enjoyed the simplicity and sincerity of this lovely Museum.
It is such a fascinating place to visit. 
The museum comprises an extensive and rich collection of Sri Lankan artefacts, beautifully curated and housed in an interesting variety of buildings all scattered through a charming garden.
Highly recommended.

Title: Cool Museum
Text: We took the local bus from Galle bus station to Koggalla since it was a bit far for tuk tuk. The trip took about 25 min. It was a short 15 min walk after we got off the bus. Straight ahead till we saw the Fortress Hotel then make a left, cross the little train track and there it is.  Really enjoyed learning about the culture and life of rural Sri Lanka. Some really cool artifacts. I think the entrance fee was 200 rs. Well worth the visit. We stopped by the Fortress hotel for some cold beverages and amazing ocean views before heading back to Galle.

Title: Amazing place
Text: Very large collection of historic Sri Lankan clothing, weapons, transport vehicles and boats... too much to mention and a big surprise as we only intended spending an hour there.

Title: Wonderful artefacts of this great man
Text: Martin Wickramasinghe was one of the greatest authors and intellectuals of Sri Lanka and how good it is that the Wicjramasinghe Trust decided to set up this museum in the house and its surroundings in which he was born. The folk museum had been a wish of Wickramasinghe himself who desired to preserve the artefacts and rural culture of his childhood. Visitors can enjoy many personal items including some of the authors writings, furniture and possessions but much more besides - the museum contains many exhibits depicting the development of agriculture, fishing, pottery, crafts and Sri Lankan culture and rural technology in general. Items are very well displayed with many details written in English. The museum is in peaceful garden surroundings so one can enjoy both indoors and outdoors and happily spend a couple of hours here learning much about the history of the locality and Sri Lankan folk history in general.

Title: So Interesting...
Text:
This was such a fascinating visit which was enhanced by the obvious pride and pleasure of our guide who showed us round. The entrance fee is minimal and the escorted tour was free.

Unfortunately it was very very hot and we ran out of time which prevented us from seeing everything. What we saw was a rich collection of artefacts and heritage, assembled really well in buildings scattered throughout  a beautiful tropical garden.

If you'd like to know more about Sri Lankan history and its colonial rulers, this museum is a must see. There were even tribes people who were cannibals!

I will definitely return to complete the tour on my next trip.

Highly recommended.

Title: Interesting Stop to Galle
Text: I took a bus from the Southeast to Galle aware of this museum. I had planned of going there but transportation seemed hard due to Kogalla being on the way to Galle. When I was on the bus I decided to just get off at the town and a guy took me on his scooter there. It was very pleasant! The guy whose office was in the canteen area was really nice! He was a former teacher and found a job at the museum. He helped me take care of my heavy rucksack when the guys at the entrance refused to take it in as I look around. His in-depth knowledge was very helpful and gave more insights about Sri Lankan folk history.

Title: Attractive and interesting.
Text: This museum was just a short walk from my hotel and had been well reviewed in my guidebook, and I wasn't disappointed.  The museum is set in a large park with beautiful trees, each labelled with its name.  The main thing to see is the Folk Museum, which has 3 rooms all about Sri Lankan history and culture.  It's a bit dingy and old-fashioned in its layout, but the exhibits were really interesting, particularly the dance masks and life-size traditional puppets.  I was also interested to find out about the ancient iron and steel industry, with excellent diagrams and model, thanks to research by Exeter University.  There was also a museum of costumes which was well worth seeing.  In a large covered area outside was a display of carts, coaches and carriages from the past, though most of these were in a bad state of repair and could do with some restoration.  Finally I went to the small traditional bungalow which had been the home of Martin Wickramainghe, who was one of the foremost Sri Lankan writers of the 20th century.  The simple house was very evocative of times past, and the exhibition room at the back, full of old documents and photographs, really told the story of the author's life and personality.  I enjoyed my visit very much, and it's a great place to go if the weather's bad!

Title: Fascinating insight
Text: This is a great place for an insight into Sri Lankan life, as the museum contains wonderful displays showing all aspects of life. There were some school visits while I was there, and it was nice to see the place being well used and appreciated.  I wish the management had spent a little bit of the admission fee on cooling the air.  There were fans, but they weren't switched on, so everyone was very hot and sweaty.

Title: Great museum
Text: Large collection reflecting local costumes, masks, local trades; enthusiastic staff keen to provide explanations and point out things you might have missed.  What's not to like?

Title: A good stopping place
Text: We were travelling from Galle to Mirissa and popped into the museum for an hour along the way.  There's enought to keep you amused for an hour.

Title: Extremely interesting
Text: Opened up a new world of Sri Lankan culture for us. Martin W.'s delightful house like a little cottage was a highlight.

Title: Great author's home
Text: It has been change to museum. IN the past time it was ancestral home of Hon;martin wickramasingha's. You must have to go there. Good experience about fisherman's culture in past time also

Title: Step back in time.
Text: Martin Wickramasinghe's writing evoked a village life when he was growning up, which was already changing, if not dying out, when his novels were published. Visiting the museum is akin to revisiting that time. It's easy to imagine barefoot boys running around Koggala Lake, when strolling around this complex.

Title: A CULTURAL MEMORIAL
Text:
If the hedonistic delights of the turquoise beaches of southern Sri Lanka can get a bit overwhleming, there is a peaceful getaway in the town of Koggala just off the A2 (Galle Road),beyond Galle and directly opposite the spa hotel intimidatingly called The Fortress.
Titled the Martin Wickramasinghe Museum of Folk Culture,the attraction, to visit which there is a small admission fee, is spread over several acres around his birthplace and has been visualised as a memorial to this doyen of Sri Lankan writers and a man of letters. Such a
initiative was close to his heart and therefore the Trust in his name has built a museum depicting folk arts and crafts and folk technology,and re-creates the work of craftsmen and their role in rural society.
Following entry,one traverses a path through several interesting botanical specimens of trees,
Walking Pine tree,Golden Shower pudding pipe tree,Beauty Leaf Alexandrian laurel and other unique varieties before reaching the small house where Martin Wickramasinghe was born.It was designed as a home typical of the headman,the tacher,and the native physician, the rural village gentry of the early 19th century.A samadhi (grave)where his ashes were interred in 1976  and later his wife's in 2001 are nearby. The samadhi and the house of his birth are symbols that span over seven decades of continuous intellectual exploration and creative writing.
The high-roofed,spacious halls of the Folk Museum house a vast array of artifacts of Sri Lankan folk culture and life.
Traditional vehicles used for travel and transport such as carriages and canoes are displayed in separate sheds.
One can easily spend 2-3 hours in this memorial absorbing the many facets of Sri Lankan culture before being rejuvenated to experience the modern way of life in this beautiful country.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Medium sized exhibit of Sri Lankan history, well done. Masks and story on iron smelting (really) were the highlights.

Title: Interesting Experience
Text: This is the childhood home of Martin Wickramasinghe a Sri Lankan author with whom I was admittedly unfamiliar.  Admission is very minimal.  The property contains a good folk museum with historical items related to various periods of Sri Lankan history.  The grounds are large and peaceful.  Visitors can walk through the author's small house.  While there, we were approached by a gentleman who identified himself as the author's son, Ranga.  He autographed copies of his father's books, which he had translated into English, and discussed a current political situation.  I have enjoyed reading the books he signed.  Although the chance meeting made the visit more memorable, this folk museum provides an good opportunity to experience Sri Lankan history and culture in a peaceful setting.

Title: Interesting Encounter
Text: The Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum has very nice and interesting artifacts showing Sri Lanka's folk culture.  I had no idea who Martin Wickramashinghe was before going there but while strolling the premises we were approached by this very nice older gentleman.  It turned out that he was actually the son of Martin Wickramasinghe himself (Ranga Wickramashinghe)!  He engaged us in a very interesting conversation and gave us hand-signed copies of two of his fathers books that he translated from Sinhalese to English.  He also called us over to enjoy fresh coconut harvested from one of the trees on the estate.  This is really something we did not expect from visiting this place!  It was a very lucky coincidence but the place is well worth seeing ... even without this interesting encounter

Title: Excellent historical place - Like Shakespeare Country In Sri Lanka
Text: This is the birthplace of the famous author Martin Wickramasinghe. It has a folk arts centre, with museum and his birth home. Rich in detail, very well maintained and an oasis in midst of galle. A must to visit

Title: Very interesting
Text: Interesting and eye opening. The Masks and puppets are great. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Well worth the short trip
Text: Very Interesting Museum, 200rup in, take some an hour or two away from the beach and visit this place.  Great for kids too

Title: Really excellent visit
Text:
We were not expecting too much from this visit but what pleasant surprise??
We had our own guide who was very knowledgable and a good communicator.
The story of this Author's life and the insight into the Sri Lankan way of life was simply outstanding.
A must do visit fir anyone who wants to learn more about Sri Lanka

Title: Must visit
Text:
If you are interested In srilankan history and culture you should visit this place.
Very peaceful and lovely environment.Definitely worth the effort going to see it.

Title: Sri Lankan Culture
Text: This place takes you back in time, with the memories of Martin Wickramasinghe belongings and other displays at the museum. If you want to learn about Sri Lanka and its culture make sure to visit. The only thing I found bad was the toilet which was not clean and not maintained. The place offers greenery and peace with rich culture.

Title: LenR
Text: The  place of a great writer, and now a museum. The museum displays a wonderful collection of artefacts and memorabilia. Which includes traditional dress through the ages, farm and fishing implements. You walk through the grounds from building to building in a tranquil setting. Very user friendly as the grounds are on a flat serface. Well worth a visit if in the area.

Title: Very interesting though not publicised
Text: Our driver asked if we would like to stop in and glad we did this was really interesting and great museum.we also ended up buying a couple of books which is not something we would usually do, worth spending an hour having a look through.

Title: good museum for sri lankan culture and history
Text: This museum is skiped by many tourists, but it is well worth a visit. You can combine it with a visit to the turtle farm and hatchery (3km apart). You can go by bus or tuk tuk. The entrance fee is only 200rs and the museum is well maintained. There are even free guides a your service. There are 4 buildings with a variety of objects and everything is also written in english. The trees in the garden have have their names written on little signs.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
Really enjoyed the variety this museum has to offer.
Very easy to get to just jump on a local bus. 200 rupees entrance fee.
This would be a great museum for all ages, lots to keep kids interested too. A guide showed us around for ages which was included in the price.
12km out of Galle but deffo worth going to see.

Title: Well worth an afternoon or an hour or two.
Text: Interesting exhibit, nice place. He was an important man. The collection of artifacts is extensive.Beware of hords of well behaved schoolkids days before Holidays though. They tend to pay more attention to you than to the exhibits. But nice and friendly as usual.

Title: Sweet Piece of History
Text: We rented a tuk one day to take us from Galle  to Mirissa so we could stop as we chose along the way, the was one of the places we stopped. The museum is actually quite  large, a fair amount of history, one of   the few remaining houses since the British occupation,  the  grounds are serene and peaceful, a pleasant surprise.

Title: A place you must visit once..!
Text:
The museum and the authors old house is a must see place in Koggala (Galle). It is not a place you feel you can visit again. 

**SPOILER ALERT*** 

The Museum has nothing to do with author or his life. The things in that museum reflects the ancient Sri Lankan culture and some of the items relates to the events in authors books.

Title: If a history lover its good to visit
Text: The famouse sri lankan author's museum. If around good to pay a visit. Its a small museum doesnt need hours to look around

Title: Holiday in sri lanka
Text: Fabulous way to spend a couple of hours on our tour of sti lanka we had a very knowledgeable guide who told us about each exhibit.When you look at some of the artifacts you realise things haven"t changed that much over the centuries in sti lanka.Visit if you have the time.

Title: Visited at the 20th time.
Text: You mustn't miss this wonderful museum if you travel from Colombo to Matara. Can cover up in 2-3 hours and the museum has almost every icon related to the Sri Lankan history.  There's a nice excursion with Lotus Holidays and Events we tried.

Title: A journey back in time
Text: This museum complex houses a number of historical artifacts, implements and photographs which are very rare to find nowadays even in Sri Lankan homes. A must see for the kids to appreciate what life was like in olden days.

Title: History unveils...
Text: If you happen to know the greatest writer of Sri Lanka, or if you have no idea about him, this is the place you must visit. Mr. Wickramasinghe was one of the most honoured writers of Sri Lanka,  by both western and eastern world. His writing style depicted the simplicity inherited by our ancestors. This is his birth place. There are a lot of photographs and almost all his books and there is a bookshop to buy his work. On a higher ground, his and his beloved wife's tombs can be seen.

Title: A glimpse of the past
Text: This museum is definitely worth a visit if you are in the Galle area. The grounds are shady and well kept with named specimen trees and lily ponds. The exhibition buildings whilst a little hot and stuffy are full of fascinating exhibits and photographs and the guides are helpful and well informed. There is a bookshop with a limited selection of English translations of Mr. Wickramasinghe's books. After visiting the museum we crossed the road to The Fortress Hotel for a light lunch and a touch of luxe.

Title: Fascinating and beautiful.
Text: This museum is a beautiful place to visit if you want to get an idea of life in Sri Lanka in a previous era. Martin Wickramasinghe has left us an amazing collection and educational resource - SrI Lanka is rightfully proud of their most famous author. The place is really beautiful. Highly recommend.

Title: Intriguing place
Text: The museum is an intriguing place. It is quite run down but contains a vast array of historic gems, including the guides, some of whom will delight in explaining in detail every single item on display!

Title: probably the best 'museum' in Sri Lanka
Text: if you are interested in craft and craft heritage this is a must see in Sri Lanka. a fantastic selection of household and everyday handmade objects as well as some slightly more industrial and ceremonial. Some wonderful massive catamaran hulls. Slightly frustrating that the information on objects remains a little vague but highly recommended none the less. I believe that the museum is currently entirely privately funded so you support is really valuable.

Title: Educational
Text: worth a visit if you are planing on visiting or climbing the rock it is very educational which gives great background info

Title: Slightly tired
Text: The museum has a great open air style to it, but sadly looking dilapidated in places. Nevertheless, worth a visit to obtain background information on the history of the rock and the archaeological finds. Interesting photos of late 19 century archaeological expeditions. Also you there are copies of the frescos which you are not allowed to take photos of on the rock itself, but the museum allowed us to take pictures of the copies.

Title: great place
Text: this museum house ancient objects such as water pipes and other items found during excavations at sigiriya rock fortress. it also has a depiction of how sigiriya would be looking in olden times. great place to visit as it has a lot of objects associated with history of sigiriya.

Title: Disappointed
Text: We were a bit disappointed by the museum and pieces of art maintenance . Bad smell and need a good refreshment

Title: Well worth the visit
Text:
If you visit Sigiriya, we strongly recommend that you also visit the Museum which is very good. The first room contains old photos of the early days when it was found by Colonial researcher Bell. 

However, the real highlight is in the second part of the museum which is extensive and very explanatory. 

If you find yourself at Sirigiya in bad weather than dont miss this opportunity.

Title: Good overview of Sigiriya
Text: The museum has an impressive display of artefacts dating to prehistoric times and the period to the establishment of the fortress. Enjoy the brief video introduction in the reception area as a precursor. There are various galleries showcasing the prehistoric period, Buddhism, literary history, the royal city and golden age of Sigiriya and archaeological history of the site. Climb the spiral staircase or take the ramp to the Frescoes Gallery. Impressive building built with Japanese funding. Shame that the attendants on reception are not a little more proactive in handing over the informative brochure or displaying more enthusiasm about the museum. No photos, no videos. A couple of souvenir outlets as you exit.

Title: Average in itself but free entry with Sigiriya tickets
Text: The museum is where foreigners buy tickets to the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. The museum entrance is included in the rock fortress entrance fee, so if you are anyway going to buy tickets to see the rock fortress, then the museum is a good starting point to gain some perspective and information about the rock fortress. If not, then you will have to pay USD 5 to see the museum, which honestly speaking is not at all worth the price and you are better off just seeing all the free locations in the premises.

Title: Visit to the Rocj
Text:
Visited the Rock, such an amazing place, would definitely recommend getting a guide for 20USD! Our guide was very knowledgeable and told us all about the history and the King! We went right to the top, its quite a hike but the view is spectacular from up there!
A must do visit whilst in Sri Lanka!

Title: interesting history
Text: You can visit Sigiriya museum at the ticket counter and it`s worth to visit before climb the Sigiriya Rock. You can get some idea about the history of Sigiriya and some other things. You can visit the museum with the same Sigiriya Entrance ticket.

Title: Good to learn about the history of Sigiriya Kingdom.
Text: me & my wife learned everything about Sigiriya Kingdom from Museum. there are lot of things to learn.

Title: Under repair
Text: When we visited the building was under some sort of restoration. The displays although small were quite interesting. You cannot take photographs of the exhibits

Title: Disappointing interior
Text: Obviously a huge sum of money went into building the museum, however, the exhibitions are very outdated.  The first room is essentially photos of the history of the rock but there is no explanation in English.  The video sound system is so bad even as an English speaker I could barely understand and lots of people gave up trying to make head or tail of the dialogue.  The exhibition to the right of the front door was much more professional and hopefully people won't be put of by room 1.  It seemed a huge waste of a great space.
