I presume people climb the rock and don't bother with the museum.

Title: Go for the history
Text: Really basic museaum that you can visit in 30 minutes but help you to understand the history of the lion rock as has all the information and artefacts from this place.

Title: Informative
Text:
One of the attractions within the sigiriya world Heritage site. Ticket price for the entire site which includes - museum, mirror wall and the entire premise is $30 per person ($15 for Indians).
Very informative museum where you will get the see the ancient technologies used in srilanka.

Title: Great insight
Text: Well worth going to the museum before climbing the rock. Although not large the information given gave an insight into the building of the palace on top of the rock.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: This is a limited museum with some interesting exhibits.  Definitely worth the time it takes to walk through.

Title: good overview of the rock development
Text: Before starting your climb of Lion Rock, the museum gives you background on the history of this site.   There's are historical photos, artifacts, and site plans.  Worth the brief time.

Title: Prelude to the Sigiriya fortress exploration
Text: Visited here on Jan 20th,2019. This museum basically displays the artifacts found near the Sigiriya area by the archaeological excavation such as the Sigiriya frescoes, paintings & weapons used by those people.It also has scale models of the rock fortress and maps/books/post cards that you can buy. It also has photo op areas like man in cave with fire, women drawing water from the well etc. The museum itself is surrounded by trees and ponds. This museum provides context before your actual exploration and should be treated as such.

Title: Primitive and old-school exhibition
Text: It is somehow interested and few details are worth to see and understand. The history of the archaeological site is interested. Simulation of old time settles is very poor.

Title: Sigiriya
Text: As a foreigner I was shocked at the price of this museum, and heritage sight. On the day I visited, the foreigner price in rupees was 5430. Locals paid only 50 rupees. The stairs were packed, the queues moved very slowly

Title: Very Pleasant
Text: The museum is included in the ticket price and worth a walk around to give some idea of the place. Could do with an update / upgrade

Title: Museum
Text: An interesting museum with a lot of information. However building and exhibition need a good makeover and technology update.

Title: Only the pictures are worth it.
Text: So the museum is a bit crap. The explanations of the things in the museum are lacklustre at best. They miss the point most of the time. Only the old pictures of the excavations where awesome.

Title: Awesome museum
Text: It's a great museum in Sigiriya so can take lots of idea about Sigiriya heritage site... Reccomend to visit when you come to Sri Lanka

Title: Ok, but needs work
Text: We have visited Sigiriya 3 times now and the museum is new this time.  Its good, but not worth the astronomical price tag Sigiriya is now asking for entry.  Given the money generated from tourists my expectation would be a museum of higher quality

Title: Nice Collection
Text: One should visit it as you would come to know about the history of the place and will be able to relate to the location when you are at the top.

Title: An interesting exhibition
Text: Photographs of the early exploration and models of the rock are great for those who do not get to the top.  A few hours well spent

Title: History..
Text: Lions rock ticket of USD 30 covers museum as well which has some nice ruins of lions rock displayed for public

Title: Actually a nice museum
Text: It covers well the historic relevance of the Sigiriya Citadel and the remains they have unearthed. My advise would be to plan the visit to the museum keeping in mind that there are long lines to climbing to the Citadel, while the museum is quite empty.

Title: Not great...
Text: But the actual rock is fab. There were more guides than tourists and the photos of the history showed various dignitaries visiting the site. Meh!

Title: Museum
Text: Interesting and fun, staff helpful and ready to assist if you should need it. Mindful if a tourist to be respectful as we witnessed some very inconsiderate behaviour.

Title: Well worth visiting before going to the rock
Text: A good idea to spend an hour or so here before visiting the rock, as it explains a lot about the area so you actually understand what you are seeing later on. Hire a guide to explain things and you will then recognize it all later

Title: Useful background and context before climbing Sigiriya
Text:
Included with your admission price to the rock, this is a useful place to go prior to climbing the rock as it gives some of the background and history. 
What was useful to know is that the rock had been used as a Buddhist monastery prior to becoming a palace and a fortress and there are some extremely old rock carvings, and that there were some really ingenious irrigation and water management during the time of its occupation. Given how quickly the fortress was built and occupied by the errant king Kashyapa, there was surprisingly little about its construction. I mean how did they get all that stuff to the top, tonnes and tonnes of it!
The museum is also set in lovely gardens and has some interesting architectural features such as trees growing out of it! The toilets were good enough, given this is not one of Sri Lanksa's strongest points!

Title: Skip It
Text: The museum is old, hot, not much to see.  Bathrooms are gross, go to the bathroom up by the entrance to the rock.

Title: Simple but informative...
Text: Before climbing the rock fortress pop in here and learn about the history of the place. They have some really interesting exhibits demonstrating what the fortress would have looked like at its height.

Title: Great intro to the history of the rock
Text: We spent a good 30 minutes in here before climbing the rock and it was definitely worthwhile understanding the history of the region and to see some of the artefacts discovered in the area.

Title: An excellent museum
Text: This is a very well put museum. For someone like me who was not able to climb Sigirya rock, it gives a very good idea of the place. I particularly enjoyed seeing reproductions of the paintings.

Title: Self-Guided Tour of Sigiriya
Text: Interesting exhibits showing the past and how the place the transformed over time. The recreation of village life is an interesting place for photo moments.

Title: Lots of information
Text:
There's quite a bit of stuff to look at here. 
My friend got bored quickly and left but I was determined to stay and absorb as much as possible. 

It would be easy to spend a couple of hours here. It's not necessary if you really want to just get up that rock. 
If you want to shove a lot of history into your brain then stop in here. 
There's also a lot of information about the creation, industry, and culture of the place too.

Some of the displays could use a little bit of work but there's a recreation of the mural of the ladies that you can't take a photo of on the citadel. 

There are easy to walk ramps and  it's also cooler in here in case you wanted to escape the heat.

Title: Worth a look
Text: Our entrance tickets to Sigiriya covered here as well and there were some interesting exhibits worth seeing so it is worth looking here first. There were some figures, metal implements, a replica of an amazing necklace and a mock village.  Visit the toilets here before you head to the Citadel as no toilets there!

Title: Little museum
Text: As part of the ticket price for Sigriya Rock you get entrance to museum. The actual museum building is very nice and modern with ramps that make it easy to take strollers and wheelchairs. It is a shame that the museum is not being taken care of properly cause you see the paintwork peeling off. In any case, it is nice to walk through the building.

Title: Nice For A Quick Visit
Text:
The museum at Lion Rock Sigiriya is worth a quick stop on your way to the climb. It's no great shakes or anything but it does have a short film about the rock, sone nice models of the area and some rather tired and jaded faded pictures.
If you have the time call in, it's not bad. But let's be honest, who goes to Lion Rock to do anything but wander it's lovely gardens and clunb the rock itself? 
An interesting way to start your time here or do it after the climb but if you are stuck for time head straight for the climb.

Title: Do it
Text:
So worth it - amazing view of Lion rock
Nice to hang out at the top and soak up the view . Must do.....

Title: Good little museum
Text:
We visited the museum after climbing the Lion Rock, definitely the best order to see the two.

Museum has some good historical background and also recreation of the frescoes.

We can recommend a visit.

Title: Review
Text: Nice museum to see before or after climb! If you can not make the climb you must visit the museum. The section of relics does not permit photographs

Title: Interesting
Text: The museum is interesting place because you can see very old things and really nice map of the whole city. It takes no more than 20 min..

Title: Too ordinary!
Text: Located near the lion rock. Entry to museum fee is included in the sigiriya lion rock entrance ticket. Museum gives an insight about the history of the place and making of the structure with well illustrated maps and diagrams but all that is not needed in case if you are going for a guided tour. Advise not to spend too much time here and move on to climb the rock early in the day before it gets sunny as there a substantial number of stairs to climb!

Title: Worth a visit
Text: For an over view of the history of the area, this is a tourist must. Make sure you get a guide to show you around and explain the history.

Title: Visit to know more about the Sigiriya rock
Text: The ticket of museum is included in the ticket price. The museum is a must visit if you do not have a guide with you. The museum gives you a good insight about the history of the rock, the whole palace/fortress, its surrounding in a well maintained way.

Title: Not worth a visit
Text:
I came to Sigiriya with a tour and our guide visited the museum with us before going to the entrance of the heritage site.
In my eyes the exhibition was very poor and boring. Not only that it's presented in a very old fashioned way, there's not air condition, it's dusty and you know the main facts already if you have read a good guide book before. 
I recommend that you go directly to the entrance and try to climb the Lion's Rock before it gets to hot. It's also not worth going back to the museum when leaving the area.

Title: Interesting museum
Text:
Entry to this museum is included in the ticket for Sigiriya. 
We visited after visiting the rock and I wished we had gone to it first. It explained about the rock and had reconstructions of it when it was a palace. 
Our guide had tried to dissuade us from visiting the museum but we found it very interesting and informative. 
I would recommend visiting this museum

Title: Go after the walk up
Text:
Having walked up and down the Rock , its good to go to the museum- its included in the ticket price  . The first part is a three minute film in English and some photos on the wall .This room though is rather dirty and one of the pictures of the Queen and Prince Phillip is falling out of the frame . 
Luckily upstairs is a lot better and was gifted by the Japanese in 2009 I believe .

Title: Can understand the history of Sigiriya rock
Text:
No photo is allowed inside the museum. We could only take some photos in outside display and shops.

It helped us to understand the history of this ancient palace and how people lived at that time. It's worth visiting it.

Remember to climb the rock first then visit the museum to enjoy the air conditioning after the hardship of climbing.

Title: Excellent exhibits
Text: This was our third visit to SIGIRIYA, the first two when we were young, with strong knees!!! This time, after a knee surgery we decided not to climb up the daunting slopes of SIGIRIYA. The museum offered us a revisit, to remember the beautiful place again. The frescoes are recreated and give a good idea of what it used to be. The other old artifacts are excellently preserved and exhibited. It is truly worth visiting. The ticket price is included in the entrance fee for the rock outcrop (SIGIRIYA). So, if you are well and active and go up the rock, still make some time to visit the museum as well. As an added extra, there are many birds in the ramparts... We did some bird photography as well!

Title: Worth a look
Text: We stopped in here in a visit to see the rock. Its worth a visit if you're here for the rock anyway - very interesting and loads of info about the place. Oh, nice clean loos too!

Title: Worth a quick visit - included in your entrance ticket
Text: There's a few artefact displays to wander through, but the highlight is the small scale-model of the Sigiriya complex.

Title: nice exposure to the basics of Sigiriya
Text: This is a fairly sophisticated museum for SL. Has exhibits on various phases of the citadel's existence. Like most tropical museums the artifacts are either stone or metal. I came away with a better understanding of the various cultures who occupied this place, but don't expect a major museum experience.

Title: Decent brief background
Text: Gives decent background to Sigiriya but not extensive. To be honest was what we were after as main attraction is the walk up and views. Took around 20-30 mins to look at the displays.

Title: Excellent museum and display !
Text: For those who are unable to climb the Sigriya rock structure, this museum gives a very clear display of the lay out of the ancient gardens and town on top of the rock. It also has an exact  to size replica of the murals in the cave so one feels that she has seen the original. Excellent for those who cannot go to the top of the rock !

Title: Do it, spend a short half hour
Text: It's nothing fancy.  But it's relatively short walk through the museum, and it will give you some nice insights on what used to be on the rock, and what you might see on your way up.  And an idea of what it used to look like.  Do consider stopping here before you go up, as I think it will give you a better experience of the visit to the rock later.

Title: Not bad but leave it for the end
Text: Its a little museum built by the Japanese (if I recall correctly) with a video about Sygiriya that you can watch in several languages and some artefacts from the site. Intended as an introduction to your visit, it wont necessarily teach you something you cant read online before going to Sri Lanka so youll be fine if you left it for the end or even if you had to skip it because youre tired or have a tight schedule. Dont spend time there before your climb though as the earlier you go up the rock, the better.

Title: Backpacking Asia
Text: Pretty basic museum but does a good job of detailing the history of Lion Rock. Well worth checking out while you're there.

Title: Only after the rock climb
Text: The Sigiriya museum is included in the price of your ticket. It is worth a visit after climbing the rock to provide context and perspective, but don't expect a state of the art display.

Title: Shame
Text:
Its a shame as it could be something great but it just isnt. 

The bit i dont mind is spending the exspencive amount on knowing it goes to the trust. However I question this as very little is looked after which is such a shame as so much history.

Title: included in your ticket to sigiriya rock
Text: this museum actually blew my expectations. you should go as it's included in your ticket up to sigiriya rock. the first floor displays photographs through the years and also a interesting video. as you walk to the other side you get more information with lots of displays and artefacts. there are fans and air conditioning so it's comfortable to walk around too.

Title: Part of the Lion Rock Experience
Text: A great way to finish off a visit to Lion Rock and included in the ticket price anyway. Some interesting artefacts and a great overview model of Lion Rock.

Title: Better than expected
Text: After the walk up the Lion Rock we went to the museum. Our expectations werent that high because of our experience, but after the section with photos of different stages of the mountain there was actually a pretty nice section with al sorts of pottery, statues, a nice 3D miniature map of the gardens and rock and some paintings. Its included in the ticket price, so give it a try!

Title: Beautiful collection, terrible display
Text:
There are some really beautiful pieces and interesting photos, but the building is crumbling, the lighting is terrible, plates are barely there and there's no explanation. 
All in all it is worth 20 minutes of your time as you come down from the rock.

Title: Its included and whilst not to Uk or US standards wortha visit for background info
Text: There is a lot here, but as others have said, it is a little dated and needs a review. However despite the large entrance fee for the rock itself, I cannot imagine much funds comes the museum way, which is a shame for what it is covering. Recommend a visit prior to the stresses of the rock.

Title: Bit dated but good nonetheless
Text: Sadly this is a bit dated but a must visit nonetheless if you are visiting sigiriya rock. This place provides graphical views of what the sigiriya rock actually looked like in the ancient days. This located near the entrance so visiting can only help you understand the details better. Recommended

Title: outdated
Text:
probably only for die-hard history lovers.
The museum is rather outdated. it contains some artefacts, but it's quite hot inside so it is a challenge.
For those who are unable to climb the rock: there is a replica of the wall paintings. But in real life this is way better.

Title: visit takes 15 minutes
Text:
Enormous building, but finally nearly nothing inside.
It could be an eyecatcher but it isn't. People are demotivated.
The entrance is included in your ticket.

Title: horrible ugly concrete building
Text: looks like a car park, whoever thought this was a good idea should be shot and the building needs demolition.

Title: Top up your knowledge
Text: Go first this place to top up you knoeledge oh sigiriya area and lion rock. Ole can wonder why in Egypt at pyramids and here in sigiriya at the lion rocks you walk between lions legs to main site. Our guide told us that in the historical time there were connections between India and Egypt. That will explain the similarity.

Title: For those who cant make he climb.
Text: A worthwhile journey through time. The rock old have been a magnificent sight in its time. This Museum shows Videos of the complete structure and art if acts of the time.

Title: Part of the Whole Visit to the Lion Rock.
Text: Nothing special, but its a part of your Lion Rock Site...At the entry point where u buy tickets for the World Heritage Site - Museum is included in the same ticket so spend some time here before your climb up the Lion Rock.

Title: Worth the walk through
Text: This was a small but tidy museum that contained a lot of history and relics from the region and explained the story of Sigiriya Rock. Seeing as you pay to climb the rock and this also gets you museum entry, I would highly recommend going through this museum after you have been up the rock. It would also be a good pace for people who are unable to climb the rock to visit as it has a miniature of the whole complex inside.

Title: A museum that is well arranged and displayed.
Text: Sigiriya is a fascinating historic site well worth a visit and the museum displays the site and its long history well utilising video and artifacts from the archeological digs.

Title: interesting but nothing special
Text: Well worth a visit when at the Rock. The museum provides interesting history to the Rock bug it is nothing special. You could give it a miss. Definitely climb the Rock though ... that is a must

Title: A bit underwhelming
Text:
Included as part of your ticket price into the ancient city but let down by the organisation and management of the museum. I suspect this is just created for the sake of 'adding an additional piece to the site'.

However, since its part of the tour, its worth just swinging by. Some people may find it particularly interesting. For myself, however, it was a 10 minute blitz to get a slight perspective on the sites that lie ahead.

Title: A nice reprieve from the heat
Text: The museum is worth a visit as it goes into the history of the rock. It explains the archaeological finds and their relevance. Their are beautiful gardens to walk in but be aware of crocodiles in the water.

Title: Potential to be wonderful, let down by staff & poor maintenance
Text: Engaging collection of artifacts, set out chronologically. There is also a replica of the frescoes and a scale model of the site. Unique architecture and attractive landscaping. Interesting collection of historic photographs as an introduction. Worth seeing and included in the price of admission. Unfortunately it all appears to have just been left as is since it opened. The building seems poorly maintained and is dank and dingy; the grounds fare not much better.  A sad state for a UNESCO World Heritage site. Could be a fantastic small museum, and one could overlook some issues - but the experience is negatively affected by the unwelcoming, often rude, and completely disinterested attitude of the staff (from the ticket desk, to the information desk, to the to those in the galleries). I saw one staff person flopped over asleep at her desk, and another with his foot on a stool, clipping his toenails - !  So many staff about, yet not engaging with visitors, doing the bare minimum. Such an important site deserves better care - especially given the price of admission.

Title: Waste of time
Text: A children's school project. Poorly done and poorly maintained. A complete waste of time, as such you will finish it in 10 mins. Rather read about the place in wikipedia before your travel

Title: Worth the visit
Text: This is included in the ticket price to climb the Lion rock, so would definitly say to make the most out of this. It isn't very big, but includes lovely picutres of the site over the years. Just have a little look around before you leave.

Title: Interesting history
Text: When you pay to enter the site, this is included, and it is so worth a look. You might be tired, but you can relax in the quiet.

Title: Fantastic place
Text: Very interesting place to visit. Hard for small kids  because of stairs but a very good view form the top of the rock. The stairs are impressive and the story is fantastic. Please read before on the internet about this place !!!

This museum has lots of different artefacts from periods of this area's history , unfortunately the exterior of the building and the internal has not been maintained and the toilet area is very poor .

Title: Most interesting and informative
Text: This is a must see if visiting the rock the displays are informative and show a history of the area the people and why Sigiriya rock came to be

Title: Not a lot here
Text: Not much to see but as the entry price is included in the ticket for Lion Rock do not miss it out, some bits are worth the time

Title: Lovely museum, shame it's overlooked
Text: This museum donated by the Japanese is not often visited, it's well laid out and informative. Architecturally I think it's quite interesting too with the water running below and trees growing through it.

Title: A great little museum
Text:
It is best to visit the rock as early as possible. It opens at 7am, and if you start the climb then, you climb in the shade and with fewer people. Visit the museum afterwards. 
Tip: if you have a driver, ask them to guide you. It will keep the local guides at bay. Also do your research in advance as there is not much information at the top.
The views from the top are astounding and when you look down onto th water gardens and consider the level of plumbing expertise that was emoted, you can't help but be impressed. 
The museum is relatively basic. Lots of photos from the late 19th century, which are interesting and show the rock when climbers went up with ropes. There is a very good copy of the paintings, including some that are now out of view. There is also a mock up of a cottage from the Iron Age which you can walk through and some video.

Title: Visit is worthy
Text: Visiting the museum is worthy, but the exhibition may be better arranged. New colour on the walls might look the museum quite better. No really competiveness to European historical museums.

Title: A must
Text:
This is a bit out of the way from the rock, and not well publicised, but provides lots of information on local culture and the rock itself.
There is also a faithful reproduction of the cave paintings which can be photographed and appreciated as long as wished.

Title: Nice museum
Text: It is worth the visit but don't expect anything spectacular. A good way to learn more about this important historical site.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Lots to see. The building is modern and well layed out. We didn't climb the rock because of all the crowds (a holiday weekend), so this made a very acceptable substitute.

Title: Interesting museum
Text: But you still have to pay a lot - Rs 2250 for non climbing foreigners- to visit this museum, a gift from the people of Japan to the people of Sri Lanka. 1 hr max recommended time.

Title: Dissapointing
Text:
Poorly maintained, dirty displays, definitely not worth the time. 
As it is included in the ticket price for Sigiriya rock, we were walking through it, but is really is a waste of time.

Title: Early start needed
Text: Quite a climb but really worth it, wonderful views and cooler on top. Whatever your guide says go as early as possible, he might not think it gets hot but we do. It will be interesting to see the water gardens when they have been restored.

Title: Needs to be developed
Text: Just to one side of the entrance. A ramp takes you on a route to the top where the trees poke through the open roof and monkeys abound. Apart from one cultural static display of life a lot more needs to be added. Pictures, photographs, maps, local animals etc to cover the bare walls. Perhaps I went at the wrong time. Only saviour was the last toilet before engaging Sigiriya Rock and the extensive grounds

Title: nothing much to watch
Text: this is a part of the lion rock fort site... those who cannot take the effort to climb all the way  can have a look .. but its not worth the fees as there are nothing much to see except some paintings and writeups

Title: Informative
Text: This is a great place to start before visiting the sites as it give good context. The ticket also then gives you access to the other sites. All descriptions are in English too.

Title: Better then I expected it to be
Text: The review it gets in the rough guide is not exactely jubilant. But since the admission is included in the general 30$ admission for the World Heritage Site. So I went trough there anyways and was pleasantly surpised. It gives a very good overview of the history and préhistory of the surroundings with good photo's and exhibits. Also a very intricate live size rendering of the apsara paintings on the rock for those not able to make it up the stairs to the actual paintings.

Title: Interesting; No photos allowed
Text: Interesting museum about Sigiriya and deities including Danesa; contains mummies, models, and artifacts. Some artifacts don't have descriptions so read the pamphlet, research in advance,  or hire a guide.

Title: An Average Experience
Text:
After climbing Lion Rock the visit to Sigiriya Museum was somewhat underwhelming. Photography is not permitted.

The entrance ticket also covers the Museum but there not too many other visitors when I was there.

Perhaps my exertions in climbing the rock had dulled the senses but reading the narrative provided with the exhibits etc. was onerous and I cut short the visit.

The Museum was opened in 2009 with financial support from Japan.

Title: Nice place
Text: This museum takes you through the history of the restoration of the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. How the excavations were done and how it was restored.

Title: Probably the best museum in Srilanka
Text: Considering what I have seen all over Srilanka, this is probably the best museum and fulfills in engaging and informing the visitor.

Title: Dated but excellent account of Sigiriya and its history
Text: Went to Sigiriya Museum before doing the wonderful climb up the rock. The building itself could use a bit of a clean up but the exhibit on the geology and history of Sigiriya was truly fascinating. Definitely recommend that you start your journey here to get some context into the wonders of Sigiriya

Title: Interesting Museum
Text: The archeologists have done a decent job on supplying the museum with relics and findings. They also have a video explaining the site's history with a few details.

Title: Very Good Museum in Sigiriya
Text: This is a very informative museum that offers excellent knowledge of Sigiriya and surrounding areas.

Title: Well laid out museum!
Text: We were greeted by a guide and agreed to have him show us around, the museum was very well laid out with historical dates and eras for the artifacts. Was interesting seeing some of the more practical traps and hardware used in that era. Don't skip this one if you are on the way up to the top as your entry ticket to the top also covers the museum and water garden! No photos are allowed in the museum!

Title: Ignorable.
Text: There's not much to see here but it worked ok as a 20-minute diversion whilst the rains eased off outside. There is a fair bit of information about the site yet it's presented in a strange way and the building itself is just odd. I'd say just head straight for the rock

Title: Eh. Go straight for the hill
Text: As far as museums go, this is just a collection of photographs and replicas. I would skip and go straight for the climb.

Title: Interesting museum
Text: Interesting museum in the heart of Sigiriya beautiful site. The entrance fee is integrated with the hole Sigiriya package. You can have a look upon the history and culture of Sri Lanka, through many historical objects. A detailed history ods Sigiriya is also proposed.

Title: very informative
Text: we visited the museum as it was part of the paid package. was very informative as lots of explaination and details available. a must see if there is extra time

Title: not worth visiting
Text: visited this building as part of the tour of the rock. A featureless concrete nuclear bunker built by the Chinese or the Japanese, not sure which, in which blck and white A4 size photographs adorn the featureless concrete walls. There is a model of the rock in a glass display case showing the top of the rock, which, as I didn't manage to climb to the top, was my only view of the layout. There were sevral members of staff who's sole employment appeared to be collecting leaves that fell from the trees into a water trough which ran the length of the building, a job that appeared to be for life. A complete waste of several tons of concrete that could have been used to build some houses for the population.

Title: Go in before you climb the rock!
Text: The museum price is included in your entry to the site. After heading in it is over to the right hand side. A large building but it is not filled to the rafters. There is lots of information though and nice to read up on this before you go and do the climb.

Title: Okay experience
Text:
Houses a huge collection of photographs describing the states of the ruins at the time of discovery and subsequent restoration processes.
Collection of artefacts are very few. But the replica of the wall paintings of original rock fortress is worth mentioning. Overall an okay experience.

Title: very informative
Text: the museum is near the ticket counter and even though not a must-visit, its worth-visit as you can gather information about Sigiriya.

Title: Happy
Text: Enjoyed  the museum's all the smallest details and  I will record every body to visit  atleast once to this place.it was very informative

Title: Depressingly run down
Text:
I dont know how this place can be so run down after opening less than 10 years ago!

Clearly none of the $30 sigiriya entrance fee invested here. Gloomy throughout and no aircon. Water features (presumably replicating the grand water gardens) left to clog up with algae. Dogs and monkeys roaming free

However, some useful bits of info to be found and the scale model of the citadel is worth seeing. Might as well look in if its included with your ticket to the rock

Title: History told
Text:
This small museum tells you the history behind the rock, the King, his brother and the battles.
Also shows some of the items found - included in the price of the full ticket

Title: Interesting displays as well as the overview of Sigiriya history
Text: Visited this museum and found lots of interesting piece of arts as well as ancient historical items. Worth a visit if you are into those things. No pictures allowed to be taken inside the museum. We also found out the that souvenir shop sells various items at decent prices.

Title: Visit is included in your fee but do it after the climb
Text: As it was already getting busy and hot, we decided to do the climb first - good move as the rock gets even busier/ hotter and the museum is (relatively) cool to relax in afterwards. But not that interesting! Worth a quick look round as it's included in the entrance fee but we didn't think the layout was that great or the exhibits that well explained.

Title: Ok
Text: It is only a formality and boring one, since ticket contains three portions.  That is why we are forced to visit.

Title: Good introduction to the history of Sigiriya
Text: I really liked the bitesize approach to this museum. It made it easy to piece together an overview of the incredible history of sigiriya. The model of the site was very cool and the artefacts amazing.

Title: Nicely display

Title: Worth a visit
Text: After climbing the rock (which can be crowded and a bit touch) this is the place you go to learn some more. It is a modern building that provides background information and artifacts. It doesn't take very long to walk through but it sure is worth a visit.

Title: Interesting Museum
Text: It can be visited when you go to Sigiriya rock, the entrance fee is included in the same ticket. The pictures in the museum inform you more about the history of the Lion Rock. it is better to visit the museum after climbing the Lion Rock

Title: Slightly interesting -needs better/more explanations

Title: very well presented museum
Text: had a good look in here while the boys climbed the 1200 steps up and then 1200 steps again back down lion rock. got dressed in a local outfit,had a walk around the gardens and saw some monkeys as well

Title: Not a must
Text: I found the museum pretty average. I only went there to kill some time. There are some ancient artefacts but not much. a quick visit was enough.

Title: Expensive

Title: Trip to Museum whilst visiting Siirya Rock

It tells you how the treasurers of the rock were re found by a British General whilst the country was under British colonial rule in the 18th century, it also gives valuable information on the era that the king who built the palaces at this fascinating site.

Title: Good but not much

Title: great

good view of monitior lizards and cheeky monkeys

Title: Very infromative

If you had the desire to read the information, you would come out with a wealth of information about the Sigiriya historical area. Luckily for us, we had a guide who explained a lot of things to us without our having to scrutinize the artifacts and posters. The price includes the museum visit.

Title: Do the Climb

Title: Interesting & good for more information

Title: A good alternative for those who can't make the climb

Some rooms were obviously more modern than others and the only really interesting room didn't really explain anything terribly well.

Title: Very good museum

Title: Good exhibits, unfriendly facilities
Text:
This museum has been built by the Japanese as a gift to the people of Sri Lanka. I particularly like the section where they describe how the citadel of Sigiriya would have looked like in its hey days. The story of the history of the place has been woven nicely in another section. 

The lack of air-conditioning in the museum is a huge negative. I could not spend time inside even though I was liking the place. The signage are are not very user-friendly and there is no commentary during the video. These things can enhance the user experience.

Title: Dive into the history of Sigiriya Rock before climbing
Text: The ticket covers the museum and the Rock climbing. Our tour guide Malinga walked us through the museum explaining the history and marvel of Sigiriya. We spent several days with him exploring the cultural triangle in Sri Lanka. I would recommend him for tours, he's a nice, licensed, and knowledgeable English speaking guide and driver. You can contact him directly for various tours: mwimalinga@gmail.com +94773609202

Title: Could use some tidying and painting
Text: This museum is included in the Sigiriya ticket. We went after visiting the rock as we didn't want to delay an early morning climb.  The building is interesting architecturally with a tree built I to it. The building is not well maintained. Of interest: photos of Sigiriya from the late 1800s, ancient models or the busty ladies in the murals sold as souvenirs (there is a photo of this in the brochure given at the ticket counter).  They have a replica of the frescos but you cannot photograph these replicas either! Actually you cannot photograph anything.  I was disappointed there was not a diarama showing what the rock may have  looked like 1500 years ago. Title: Stop by to get insight on Sigiriya

Would be worth seeing before visiting but we came after our visit and while it was stil interesting we would have gained more doing it the other way round.

Title: A real museum

Title: A preview before you embark on the actual site visit
Text:
At first, I thought the museum is free. But no. It is not free. You can enter if you bought the main ticket to the Sigiriya Citadel. For foreigners, the counter to purchase the entrance ticket is also located inside the museum. 

I could have go in for a preview before the actual landing but I came after visiting the actual site. There were photographs taken of the Lion Rock during the colonial days and before the actual restoration works commenced. There is also a video showing a helicopter view of the citadel at the summit of the rock and the other attractions way up the steel ladder. The sound effect of the video was not very good. The volume should be turned on louder.  

The museum also showcased how the restoration and preservation works on the cave frescoes were carried out. It is great laborious preservation work. I was sorry to take a photo of the frescoes earlier at the actual site which could have caused damage to the preserved frescoes. I was lucky to be let off with a reprimand from the staff of the archaeology department. 

The last time I saw such cave frescoes was at the Mogao Caves in Dunhuang, China. The monks who traveled along the old Silk Road and resided in the Mogao Caves left behind such beautiful masterpieces. At that time, I was also advised not to take photos at the frescoes. But when I came here I really forgot about the advice. I should have seen the painstaking effort of the archaeology experts shown in the museum and reminded myself before proceeding to the actual site. 

The frescoes shown at the museum were impressive, colorful and sharper than those actual images at the site. The female figures look voluptuously gorgeous and beautiful. 

Other than those I mentioned, there is nothing much in the museum. I left the museum in less than an hour. It is more a preview before visiting the actual site.

Text:

Title: Must be seen
Text: This is a beautiful museum. Allow at least thirty minutes. I went twice as I really enjoyed the moonstone Buddha statutes and the very old frescos and other paintings. Don't go at four pm as they want to go home!!!

Title: Don't skip
Text:
Highly recommend it after your climb up and down the Lion Mountain. Go straight to the gallery and follow the layout. Stop at the scale model and look at the animations to see how the completed buildings once looked. Don't forget to put your phone and camera away as there is a lot of security. There is an official gift shop on the way out, which sells some of the handicrafts at reasonable prices.

People will tell you, you can't get there by foot from the Foreign Tourist Car park and try to hustle you into a tuk tuk fare. Just walk right through the food stalls, back to the main boulevard and you will be there in under 3 mins.

Title: Underwhelming
Text: After the exhilaration of climbing the Rock at Sigiriya, the museum is underwhelming. The exhibits are well set out and this is the highlight of the visit. But the building is shabby, poorly signposted and its cavernous spaces are poorly utilised! The facilities are poor- the bathrooms are untidy and lack in basic provisions, the souvenir shop is hidden away and doesn't offer much, and every wall needs a coat of paint. Having an attendant asleep in the temporary exhibit sort of captured the vibe! There is a cafeteria about 200m away in another building but the poor hygiene is a turn off.

Title: Needs freshening up
Text: The buildings design is cool indoor/outdoor combined but really needs freshening up and the exhibition not a must see.

Title: A bit small, but provides good insight in the rock and its history
Text:
The museum is just behind the ticket office from where you buy your entrance tickets to climb the rock. The museum entrance is included in the ticket. The museum itself is rather small but provides some interesting insights in the rock and the history around it. Also you find some statues and a replica of the paintings you find on the rock.
Not super special, but ok for a 15 minute stroll.

Title: More Broken pots
Text: Museums around the world seem to like to show their visitors broken pots and this one is no exception, although to be fair, it does have less of them than other museums I have been to. It id quite a small muesum so it doesn t take long to complete. At the start of the tour is an exhibition of childrens drawrings from around, oh, 2014-2016, there are some fantastic pictures, especially the ones of half naked women. This exhibition was the highlight of the museum as I am getting bored of broken pots and arrow heads.

Title: One of Sri Lanka's better museums
Text:
We'd recommend visiting this museum after climbing Sigiriya. It has a suprisingly modern design and is built around a lake and some trees.

The museum has a rather good diorama of Sigiriya and the surrounding grounds aong with a short film showing a computer image of how it would have looked like in its day.

Although it's one of the better museums that we visited in Sri Lanka, there are still spaces that are under-utilised and staff who look bored.

Given that entry to the museum is included in the extortionate Sigiriya ticket price (4,200 SLR for European visitors) then it's certainly worth a visit.

Title: Rather Dull actually
Text: It was a monsoon when we arrived so opted for Museum trip. The size of the Museum suggested some fantastic exhibits but rather disappointing. The children's paintings of life on the rock and various Buddhist artefacts were interesting. Some Public interaction with taped 'talks' in different languages would create a better experience. Rather boring actually with some good bits !

Title: Nice touch
Text:
Good place to finish off your trip after doing the Rock climb very informative 
Set in a nice location

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The museum gives a excellent overview of the history of the Lion Rock and has a nice collection of artefacts found at Sigiriya.  Look out for the replica of an exquisite golden earring similar to those of the ladies on the frescos. The original earring is kept in Colombo.  But the building itself is poorly maintained. There are empty rooms and the walls can use a new coat of paint.  A pity, because I like the modern design of the building. Especially how the museum was built around the trees on site

Title: it's Ok
Text:
The museum is not beautiful, but the visit is included in the ticket price, so why not go? 
We refresh ourselves around in the park where there are services.

Title: Excelent info, entrance included in ticket price
Text: The best museum we visited in Sri Lanka. A wide range of exhibits with loads of info presented very clearly. A must visit when at Sigiriya - especially as entrance to the museum is included in the ticket price.

Title: Fantastic, but sadly ignored by tourists
Text:
This museum has an excellent collection of artefacts from Sigiriya. There's a natural flow through the museum exhibits explaining everything from the historical timeline of the site and Sri Lanka. The museum also touches on the archeology, geography and geology. The labels have all been written to a high (if rather academic) standard.

Sadly, most tourists make a bee line for the rocks. Visit this and it helps put everything in context.

Title: A good addition after climbing the rock
Text: My guide told me the museum was intended for those wanting an imitation and not wanting to climb the rock.  I insisted on visiting and was pleased I did.  What I especially enjoyed were the drawings by children depicting their "take" on Sigiriya.

Title: Very Good - International Standard
Text: This is a must see before you start your climb. It gives and in-depth understanding on the history of Sigiriya. Interactive resources are good and helpful for the young. Do not forget to get the museum brochure from the shop that you can keep for a price which has all the illustrations of the exhibits.

Title: Visit if you can
Text: This is often forgotten at the start of the site- we came back the next day to visit  . It only takes 30 mins or so and is included in the ticket price. It taught me a lot about the city and brought it all to life. The building it is in is also an interesting design

Title: Not bad if you have the time
Text: The museum at Sigiriah is OK but not worth going out of your way for. Some artifacts but mostly replicas. The scale model of lion rock is good though.

Title: Good place, worth visiting
Text:
This is situated just inside the rock fortress area as soon as you cross the entrance fee counter. The entrance fee is part of the fees that you paid for the rock fortress which must be 30$.

This museum replicates what is there in store once you walk towards the rock fortress and has some beautiful representation of the Sigiriya rock. Also has lot of artifacts dated to BC. Photography not allowed.

Mostly this place is not crowded as people tend to walk towards the rock area bypassing this museum.

Just visit as you walk towards the rock. But in case if you have some time constraint you may skip as well.

Title: Worth a visit as it is included in ticket price
Text: If you have some time before climbing the big rock then go visit the museum for some interesting background as to the history of the area. The museum has a great potential that it doesn't quite fulfill but it is still well done and you can get through it in about 10 mins. One dislike was all the male staff who just sit around by the bottom of the stairs, can be a bit intimidating and you wonder why they need 6 staff for a place that is pretty deserted of visitos

Title: Very well display.
Text: Nicely arranged & display all things with all details.Need not take a guide to see the Museum because display information near every item .

Title: nothing important
Text: it was nice , but really i don't like museums , so if you like museums its good .The place is quit and there was no one there to guide me .

Title: interesting display
Text: we were told that it is better to see the museum first before going up the rock to have better appreciation of sigiriya. but we wanted an early climb to avoid the heat and besides, the staff didn't know the exact time the museum would open. when we visited the museum later, there was a power outage and they didn't seem to have a back-up power supply. we ended up rushing through the display which was somehow impressive because it was so hot inside.

Title: Amazing building, not an interesting museum
Text:
The building is spectacular! 
It is brutalist architecture at its finest, it was designed by Chandana Ellepola and built in 2009, however due to poor maintenance it feels much much older than this, it bought to mind some of the styles of Le Corbusier and Bauhaus design. It is a beautiful building worth exploring. It is open to the elements and feels light.
However, the exhibition design feels even older than the building. very dated design with no technology used, the style of the museum building is of the 60/70s but the exhibition feels from the 80s with no improvements.
Come for the building and the monkeys!

Title: Useful introduction to Sigiriya rock, great architecture but poorly maintained
Text:
The museum provides a good introduction to the history and architecture of Sigiriya rock. Although a good guide will explain most of this while walking up the rock, the museum also has a diorama and animated video that give a good visual image of what the site looked like in its prime. The museum was recently donated by Japan, and we loved its open architecture. However, maintenance is not great, staff do not look interested, and the souvenir shop was closed ( or maybe out of business?). 

As the entrance fee is included in the overall ticket price for the site, I would recommend the half-hour visit.

Title: Not bad, takes about 20-30 minutes.
Text: Some lovely relics and history on the rock. Sadly you can't take photos. Worth checking out to give you good context of the Sigiriya rock and the ages through which it passed.

Title: Sigiriya is a must visit in Sri Lanka
Text: Highly recommend - Sigiriya is one of my favourite places in Sri Lanka. Natural beauty. And of course, you should not miss the museum too while you are there.

Title: s short stop before we climbed sigiriya
Text: i'm not really a fan of museums, but this one was interesting...the museum is relatively new.. they had a lot of space which was used well. we could see langoors on a tree that was growing in the middle of the museum...you had to walk on steps around the tree to exit. the museum had a lot of artifacts that were interesting to see and a model of what the sigiriya rock palace used to be. its better to go to the museum before you climb the rock (since its close to the ticket counter and your entrance fee covers the entrance to the museum as well) you may not spend too much of time in the museum as there seems to be a lot that they need to do to it. there is a whole wall of children's drawings in the museum.as you walk down the slopes of the museum, you walk alongside lotus ponds-beautiful! also, if you need to use the toilet before you start the climb it is advisable to do so here-very clean and well kept.

Title: Fairly modern but a little disappointing after visiting Lion Rock
Text:
Sigirya Museum lies just off the main path from the Entrance to the Lion Rock and is probably best visited after climbing the Rock itself, especially if you are visiting early to beat the crowds and the heat.

It's a fairly modern building and sits unobtrusively on the site but the charge of $5 to enter it seems a little much after already paying $30 at the main entrance to visit the Lion Rock.

After passing through a reconstructed angular brick entranceway copying originals found elsewhere on the site there is a fairly obvious route to follow with a series of cased artifacts mainly from Sigirya, along with a fairly nice model of the Lion Rock in it's landscape that helps to put things in perspective.

There is also a full size replica of of the rock overhang and the Apsara Paintings to be found high up on the Lion Rock. Surprisingly, because photography is banned in the museum that means you can take photographs of the original paintings high up on the Lion Rock but you cannot take photographs of the copies down in the museum. Surely this is short sighted especially for visitors who can't make it to the top of the rock due to mobility problems and who would benefit from being able to visit the museum alone. Approaching the exit there is a diorama with an indigenous structure and examples of some traps that seem out of place somehow, almost as though they were put here because no-one quite knew where else to put them because they don't fit in with the rest of the exhibits, though given the museum's size there is plenty of room for more to be added.

If you want a souvenir don't expect to find it or a guide book in the museum itself. There is an official looking store nearby if you turn to the left on leaving with a limited range of reasonably nice but sometimes quite expensive items. There is also a slim but well illustrated guide book in several languages, but if you want a guide book you would do better to keep your eyes open for one elsewhere in Sri Lanka before your visit to Sigirya. Surprisingly one of the best ones I saw was in a shop in the airport.  There is also a smaller independent store nearby on the same block but it too had little to offer and the same guidebook was on sale there as in the larger shop but no cheaper when we visited.

The museum isn't really bad and it's nicely laid out, but I found it  a bit disappointing after the sights and the experience offered by an ascent of the Lion Rock and an exploration of the grounds. Being charged again to go in, instead of being allowed in with the same ticket purchased at the main entrance to the site was also unwelcome. Our visit probably lasted around 20-25 minutes and I in hindsight I don't think we would have been left with regrets had we not gone in. It's ok but nothing special.

Title: Must See
Text: The museum is well planned, the various exhibits explained clearly and the whole museum is well maintained. This is a must see before visiting Polunnawarra and Sigirya.  It explains the history, the various aspects of each site and helps to create a context in which to place the sites.

Title: Worth the visit
Text: Well set up and interesting. the diorama was very useful. The main problem was they will not let you split the ticket, and visit the museum on one day and then the rock the next day. This would help with understanding the site, before climbing the rock.

Title: Good Museum
Text:
Artefacts are arranged nicely and well maintained. Ticket is part of the rock entrance ticket.
Photography is not allowed. 
Museum gives the history of Sri Lanka, Iron production, History of Budhism and the history of Sigiriya.
It may take around 45min to 1 hour to see.

Title: An excellent introduction to the Sigiriya complex
Text: It's very informative without forcing you to wade through too much detail.  I highly recommend it as a precursor to the climb up the rock.

Title: Not much visited!
Text: Hardly anyone seems to visit the museum after climbing the rock. It has some interesting details about the rock including geological, anthropological and historical data. However it is not very well maintained. The lights were not working properly and no one was bothered to explain the exhibits to us although we tried asking questions.

Title: Don't miss this
Text:
Pay a visit to this museum before you start your climb . It's very informative as it gives an overview of what lies ahead at the top . It's next to the ticket counter . 
The cost is inclusive if you purchase the ticket for the climb .

Title: Happy to visit
Text: Your ticket include visit to this Museum. so many articles are displayed and properly arranged. Need much more time to see and understand. our visit was just running one.

Title: Beautiful building
Text: The exhibits aren't particularly memorable but the building is very interesting, worth a look as entrance is included in lion rock ticket price.

Title: worth for quick stop after the climb
Text: ask your driver to stop after the climb of the rock, then you can better understand what you have seen, you can relate to it easier. i would recommend to climb rock first and then enjoy whatever else ( if you have energy left). museum was nice you could see some relics,statues,which have been found and by looking at exploration pictures you see history of sigiriya which was lovely

Title: GIves a very good context of the Sigiriya Rock
Text:
We visited this place on our way to Sigiriya Rock. Its a good small museum which gives a good account of the historic rulers of SriLanka. 

A word of advice, its better to visit this place after actually visiting the rock. Good place to rest your feet and gives a lot of context to what you've seen.

Title: Worth a look but not much else
Text: You pay the same money to see the museum once you've paid to visit the rock but the museum itself is pretty tatty and lousy. Worth having a look while you're there but the place needs to be taken care of as it seems neglected.

Title: Somewhat interesting
Text: Includes some interesting information and a really good visual representation of what the site looked like in ancient times.

Title: Museum with Mixed Theme
Text: The Sigiriya Museum should be the first thing to do after paying the entrance ticket to the site. It will give you a good insight on what to see and expect at the Sigiriya Lion Rock. I was surprised to see coins and currencies on display here which in my opinion has nothing to do with the theme of the attractions on site. The cave paintings are close representations of what I saw up in the mountain.

Title: My first time
Text: This so interesting to see and this my first time to visit museum so happy to see this things and well plan

Title: Boring
Text:
Nothing much to see. Got bored halfway and left.
Its not air conditioned inside just small rotating fans.

Title: Time Pass
Text:
Not that impressive.  But a quiet walk in the museum might relax your legs and mind.  There is also a review at the end of the visit.

You can review it!

Title: Learn your past how thing were made.
Text: It was wonderful the visit we made to this Museum and lot of things to see inside the museum. It is close to the ticket office and after climbing the rock do not forget to go there.

Title: Interesting
Text: This museum is worth it if you want to get a short history of the area.  I found it pretty interesting and it doesn't take too long to go through.

Title: Nice museum
Text: Nice museum. Entry ticket included with lion rock entry ticket which cost LKR 3,900 ( US$30) . Well maintained. Takes less than 30 minutes to cover this one. Museum is inside of lion rock compound.

Title: Well maintained
Text: This museum at the entrance of the complex gives us a birds eye view of what we are going to see in the sigiriya rock fortress. Better to visit this place to know the historical aspects, especially if you are NOT engaging a guide.

Title: nothing special
Text: It could be much better than this , the only intresting item is fortess  small  maquette . It is a2 story building  near the fortess do this after your climb

Title: Worth a visit
Text: I didn't climb the rock so I found the museum very useful. The history of the rock was very clear with a number of artifacts on display.

Title: Informative
Text: This is not the best museum, very sparsely laid out and not many antiquities to view, but of what there is to see, the objects give a good idea of the beautiful objects and artisanal work that would have been part of the Palace that once stood.

Title: Informatiive
Text: The museum was very well made, informative and the artifacts were well preserved. It was worth the time we spent there

Title: Fairly small but effective
Text:
I generally don't love museums but this one was very well laid out. Good background as well as images and models of how it would have looked. Also had reproduction of the cave paintings and translation of some of the ancient graffiti which was curious.
There were also more recent exhibits of rural life with monkey traps and household effects. Very hands on and we were encouraged to take photos with the exhibits.
Small can be beautiful.

Title: Interesting museum, with added value as shelter for heavy rain or burning sun
Text:
The museum features a well documented exhibition that is organized by 5 periods Sigiriya has known. I'm not much of a museum-goer but I liked this one.

If you arrive early on the site and weather is good, visit the rock first and museum after.
If raining, visit the museum first and hope for sunshine when you walk out of it :-)

Title: Basic and not very interesting
Text: The museum is at the entrance of the Sigiriya complex. There is short video about the rock and the history and quite a few artifacts from the area, but the whole museum does not feel interesting enough considering the potential...

Title: Great architecture dissapointing context
Text: I would recommend just going up the rock.  The building has nice architecture but it so much more could be done with such a great space.

Title: Great little museum
Text: Everything is very well set out and described in English (also Tamil and Sinhalese).  My husband didn't want to climb the rock; he likes museums and found this to be an excellent example of its kind.  He didn't feel he had missed out on anything by not climbing up to the top!

Title: Oh dear
Text: It looks as if no one has done any maintenance on this place since it was built. Some architect probably thought he had produced a masterpiece but he forgot that a) this is Sri Lanka where it is hot and rains a lot which produces mould which needs to be accessed to be cleaned and b) people tend to use museums. The layout was bizarre and a spiral staircase might look good but it doesn't suit everybody. The exhibits are informative if you are not able to climb all the way up the rock. Unfortunately the staff are totally disinterested and spend the whole time playing with their phones. The shop was particularly bad with very poor quality stock that was badly displayed and the staff spent the whole time playing a noisy game on their computer. This place needs a new manager fast.

Title: Don't miss if you can't get to the top of the rock
Text: If you can't get to the top of the rock, you don't need to as a life size replica of the cave paintings is here, as well as a model of the site on the top. I met people who didn't go to the top and missed the museum as well as they weren't informed. If you did get to the top it is optional, but there is a decent toilet there so that's worth knowing!

Title: visit before the rock
Text: The museum provides useful information and models of the site.  This is necessary as there is no signage at the site itself.

Title: Skip It
Text: Skip this part of the attraction and pay a local 1000 LKR to guide you around the site because the museum is just full of poor quality replicas. You will learn much more about Sigiriya Rock Fortress and the young kings by using a guide as you ascend.

Title: Interesting and quick guide to the area
Text: The museum shows interesting historical findings and gives good information of the area around the Sigiriya rock. It doesn't guide you in depth of the subject but gives a breef understanding of the area. Does not take more than 30 minutes to go through. Worth visiting though.

Title: So pathetic
Text: The muséum is old and the walls black and mouldy. There is a strong smell of humidity as there is no air con. You pay too much to see... Too few artifacts almost ..nothing ! Really disappointing. Some men are there doing nothing the place is really small it takes 15 minutes to visit. I don t know why at the counter there is a poster trip advisor 4,5 rate in 2012 ..'.'''!...!!!!!

Title: Imagine - if u can't conquer the Summit
Text: If one cant climb the Rocky Heritage site, walk towards the museum & see the heritage site thru a hawk eye view. finely mentioned details on the site, the utensils used, the cutlery used, the fighters choice of weapon then & go thru the video show on the site ....very useful. Can be managed better for the Fee they are charging.

Title: just so so.
Text:
The approach and entrance are pathetic
not much of an attraction. The building and architecture is nice.
only limited number and variety of artifacts are displayed.
needs some serious attention and maybe cash injection.

Title: Good showpiece...
Text: Nice architecture (set in the middle of trees and water stream) and lovely atmosphere to enjoy the artifacts. However, there are signs of decay at places. A coat of paint on the walls and and better use of wall poster spaces (some pictures have been removed and the patches show) can improve it further.

Title: Great museum with attention to detail in curation
Text:
The curators at the Sigiriya Museum have done a great job. Including preshistoric details as well as exhibits that tell the interesting story of how Matale and Sigiriya came to be made for a wonderful visit. 

It's also great that the price of admission to the museum is included in the ticket to go to the Sigiriya rock.

Title: Worth a quick stroll if you have 30 minutes
Text: The museum itself was nothing special. I went after I had finished walking around the site, as it is positioned in the opposite direction of the rock from the ticket counter. The exhibits tracing Sigiriya's use over time had a few interesting nuggets of information and were decently designed. I spent about 30 minutes walking through and reading most of what was there. If you happen to have extra time after finishing visiting the rock, then it's worth a brief walk through, although if you are pressed for time, I would skip it and save more of your time for the rock.

Title: Brilliant
Text: The set out was fantastic and the content very interesting.  It is a huge modern building with many interesting artefacts.   Would have loved more time there.

Title: Nothing special
Text: Museum partly justifies the extortionate price charged for climbing the rock fortress. You can visit it, but you will not walk out more knowledgeable than when you walked in...

Title: nothing to see
Text:
Just nothing to see over there.
Only replicas,very dirty place, no explanations about the site and ruins.
Definitely a waste of time.

Title: Don't bother
Text: I think that the title says it all. There is really not much here to see. If you have paid to get in it is probably not so bad, but if this is only what you have paid to do at this site, save your money.

Title: Just alright...!
Text:
Since it was included in the price of the whole Sigiriya experience, it wasn't bad in anyway but as a standalone museum, it's not great. There are a lot of empty spaces, strange layout and quite small.

Worth doing if you have time on your hands whilst at Sigiriya but not essential by any means.

Title: Not amazing
Text: This came as part of our tickets to the rock so we had a quick look through but it was pretty basic. Lots of replicas of things that you can see in person at the Rock.

Title: A WELL THOUGHT OUT MUSEUM, FULL OF HISTORY..!
Text:
And this was the first thing we did after arriving, as it's next to the main entrance and is part of your ticket . Upon entering I noticed the open planed theme of the place which made it look bigger than it actually was, walking through the displays takes you from the very beginning of this palace which has a ton of ancient artefacts to behold and anyone with a sense of history will find this very interesting as it builds up to the construction of the rock fortress itself . Just be aware there is also a ban on cameras / videos in here and is strictly enforced as they follow you around at times, just to make sure I suppose.?  There are also two levels which are easily accessed and wheel chair friendly and on one of them there is a large brilliant reconstruction of the "Naked Ladies" frescos and are identical to the ones up on the rock. Which gives anyone who is unable to climb the rock a great chance to see what's up there and the people who recreated these frescos deserve great credit too, for the painstaking work involved , they've even got the entire rock face copied too. This let my wife see them as she wasn't going climbing with me and is the highlight of this museum, also in here there is a small cafe, plus shops which are slightly over priced as one would expect, and as you walk around there are many walk ways with nice views of the ponds and are ideal photo opportunity's, the only down side here were a group of American female teenagers who were squealing and giggling loudly down a phone which was on speaker and one wonders just why the hell they would visit a place like this and behave like imbeciles.? 
I would certainly recommend a visit here before you climb the fortress rock , as you'll have a better understanding of the history involved in this unique UNESCO site..!

Title: Get ready for a day of climbing and history!
Text: Awesome site. The museum is so well thought out and set out that you really get your imagination working by the time you walk through the ruins and up the rock. A really great day out.

Title: Decent little museum
Text:
Small museum about the history of Sigiriya with plenty of artefacts etc. 
Worth a look if you've already got your Sigiriya ticket and are not too tired after the rock climb.

Title: not like a museum
Text: Maybe not too much thing there with minimum description...not interesting to see that museum..it is good if they put story year by year with updated news....the only interesting there is see one gemstone :)

User_Location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
Title: Very interesting
Text: Very interesting but do the climb first to beat the crowds. The museum was virtually empty when we went.

Title: Helpful context for the Heritage Site
Text: The museum is one of those old fashioned look don't touch museums with no interactive elements, but the trilingual labelling is very helpful and sets a good context for the heritage site.

Title: Climbing the rock was the greatest
Text:
The museum area is ok, not more than that. It's not worth to hire a guide!
Climbing the rock was the greatest experience!
We used about one and a half hours up and down. They told us that it is 1200 steps up. 
The wall paintings were really good. Enjoy the sight!
Also a great view from the top. 
And; don't forget to bring water with you! They don't sell it on the way up.

Title: Worth a quick visit
Text: Not a huge museum but some interesting information and artefacts. Worth a quick visit, especially when entrance is included in your Lion Rock ticket!

Title: Plain Joe
Text:
My attention span in amusuem is as this one is low
It will give u a quick summary of what you've seen or going to see
What I appreciated was a 3D rendering or visual played to understand the structure that was

Title: Interesting!
Text:
The museum contains the story of Sigiriya and some replicas or even real stuffs. Don't expect any air-cons inside LOL
And you are not allowed to take pictures inside the museum.

Title: Just OK not mind blowing
Text: This was just OK. I wasn't fully blown away. I do recommend just browsing through. However, be mindful of the stuffy smell inside. If you have mold allergy, this may  bother you a bit.

Title: Come here to complete the visit to Sigiriya
Text: We didn't know the ticket to the site includes the entrance to the museum. We came back the next day anyways and paid again to go in. It's worth coming back because I got to learn more about this place and see the story of the amazing discovery and excavation. Coming here completed our visit to Sigiriya.

Title: Visit it as it comes with the ticket price.
Text:
We actually missed the museum as its just at the right of the ticket counter and we were too excited to ascend the citadel rock. When we did realize that we had indeed missed it, we back tracked when we descended and took a much leisurely walk, appreciating the lotus ponds and landscape. The museum itself is a quiet building with not much visitors in it. I remember sitting down to watch a short documentary about the discovery and restoration of the citadel rock. We  also spotted a small crocodile as we were exiting the museum. 
Since it comes with the ticket price, why not ? Plus its an escape from the sun outside.

Title: Worth a quick visit but only before the rock
Text: This museum is reasonable, but I would recommend a quick visit first to the museum then do the rock, otherwise it would be underwhelming the other way round.  It is located not far from the main ticket office of the main site.  The multi-level museum has some interesting information, but sadly no photography allowed, which reduces the museum rating.

Title: ok ok. can do better..
Text: museum ticket price is included in the sigiriya rock ticket price. it houses a miniature model of the sigiriya rock, multiple historic pictures of the rock fortress and assorted artefacts, tools and jewellery found on site. includes a short film played in  3 different languages - english, sinhalese and tamil about the sigiirya rock. not air conditioned. no photography allowed. at the exit is a miniature mirror wall for tourist to make graffiti while the children get to complete the picture of the sigiriya rock with just the lion paws and you have to imagine how the top lion head would have looked. can see the whole museum in less than 30 minutes.

Title: Replica of Sigiriya attractions
Text:
It was an interesting museum with information in English.  Lots of good Sigiriya artifacts.  Good information for people who could not climb the Lion Rock.  

However, I found it very hot inside.  No air-conditioning.  Few fans here and there which are shut off most of the time.  But this absolutely does not mean that the museum is not worth a tour :). This is just an information so that the travelers are prepared accordingly.

Title: No photos allowed
Text: The fresco and the photos are good replica than the rock. since in the rock most of the things are damaged.

Title: Gem
Text: A really interesting museum, with lots of good Sigiriya artefacts, photos etc well labelled in English. It really added to our experience (and was already included in the exorbitant ticket price). We spent about an hour there but only saw one other couple.  Such a pity.

Title: Great Museum
Text: This museum has a diorama of the site which gives an excellent overview and explanation of Sigiriya's cultural importance.  It was originally a Buddhist monastery and established as a fortress.  It was important for the trade routes with the Gulf, China, India and the Roman Empire. No photos are permitted here.

Title: Good insight to Sigiriya
Text: Museum opens at0830,so if you are early do climb first, but check it out as good background knowledge to area and the rock,and makes you think how they built palace on top and lived thete

Title: complete your visit to the rock
Text: Don't miss the museum's animated recreation of the palace/fort on top of the mountain! The old photos of the British discovery of this site are also fascinating.

Title: Basic musuem but is on the way and included in the ticket price
Text: The musuem is free (within the cost of the ticket for Sigiriya) which is good.  Well worth visiting given that it is on the way but it is a little tired to say the least.  It is basic and gives a pretty cursory explanation of the history of the site in general.  In short it does the job of setting the scene but little more.  This said you have to walk through it on the way and the price is included in the ticket so you may as well.  Further when we visited it was the least crowded part of the heritage site, which may well be telling in itself.  In the event that you wish to know more about the site you would be better served going online the night before or if you have a guide asking them.  We had a guide/driver for our tour and he was far more informative than the musuem.

Title: Nice to get to know the history behind the Lion Rock but nothing more
Text: Free of entrance when you paid the 4000 rupiees for the Rock. In there you cancer get to know a bit of the history of the Lion Rock. However, Wikipedia would work just as fine ??

Title: Good
Text: Museum gives good background information on the rock. I liked the model of the rock and the surrounding area. Puts it into perspective.

Title: Visited after climbing
Text:
This museum, located adjacent to the rock, is included with the ticket for the climb.
We found it interesting and it added more information about Sigiriya.

Title: Great 3D fly-through CGI movie of how this place used to be.
Text: The Museum was all we needed to absorb the essence of the place. That and a walk around the water gardens.

Title: So-so Sigi Museum
Text:
Not a particularly inspirational museum. Ticked the boxes but not a lot more. I suppose it is useful perhaps to go there before climbing the rock. Looks rather tired and needs some up-dating.
Rather dark and gloomy.

Title: Perfect if you dont want the climb
Text: As two of our group didn't want the climb we visited this museum instead. Worked out well. Gave a fair insight to what it was all about and a flavour of what we missed by not doing the climb.

Title: great to visit prior to making the climb....we didnt
Text: This museum is a little sweet and a little in need a spruce but tells the fascinating story of this site with brothers killing fathers and each other - after creating a magnificent slice of history that we can enjoy years later....

Title: Well worth the visit
Text: The museum is included in the price of the exorbitantly priced ticket, which is something. It has interesting artifacts discovered on site, a superb scale model of what the original site would have looked like funded by the Jpanaese government and also computer-generated images, as well as facsimiles of the "topless lady paintings". Once again, no leaflet or plan is provided and photos are not allowed, so a really good memory is required!

Title: Interesting little archaeological museum
Text: Interesting museum! Entrance to the museum is included in the citadel-Rock ticket price (£ 20.00pp). It gives background of the history of the citadel, showcasing archaeological finds.

Title: Short stop before the climb
Text: In-case you are not hiring a guide or you want to under the history behind Sigiriya then this is a good place to spend your 15-20 minutes. They play a short video and also have detailed exhibits about key characters, cultural significances and layout of the erstwhile lower and upper palaces,

Title: An uninspiring museum
Text: The story of the Fort is so rich but not at all well represented in this museum. The entrance area has artwork and drawings by local kids- which gives it an amateurish feel.

Title: Great museum
Text: Not too big but a great museum with beautiful pictures and old pieces. Worth the visit when you're around.

Title: Go, but with low expectations.
