Text: Considering how much the ticket is to the Heritage site the Museum  should be excellent. Unfortunately it's run down and has rather basic exhibits. Worth going into because it's part of the over-priced ticket but do so with low expectations.

Title: Too many spaces, but not too many monuments
Text:
The museum is included in the price of entry to Sigiriya, so I suggest you visit it. You will learn some historical facts and see a few artifacts.
Visit the museum first, it immediately at the entrance to the complex.

Title: Worth knowing..
Text: After our climb,  we went to this museum. It was good to see ages old stuff so closely.  I enjoyed a walk around, reading , noting and experiencing sigriya rock's history..  Recommended post visit to Sigriya rock ..

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The museum has lots of objects to view and is certainly worth visiting. they have  relics centuries old

Title: Beautiful modern building - must to see it if you are an architect
Text: I am not a museum lover person, but love the nice modern buildings, than I was more interested in the building than the exhibition. Must see, if you are an architect or modern building lover :) Unfortunaly, a little bit in bad condition beacause of weather conditions. Good joke from the side of the museum management - has exhibition room without  exhibited stock, only their messy place :)

Title: a great introduction to the place
Text: a great introduction to the rock, why it was built and what they found at the place - probably should be done before climbing the rock

Title: Spend bit more time and visit the museum, Its worth..
Text: This museum organized and arranged very professionally.. its worth to see it.. there are gift and souvenir shop inside the museum if you want buy some..  they do not allow you to take any pictures inside the museum. I recommend to visit the museum before you climb the rock. that way you really have a idea what are you looking at..enjoy it...

Title: Climb the rock, buy a book and don't bother with the museum
Text: The building is large and the amount of information is small. The most interesting thing was to see the poor state of repair of what is a relatively new building.  Obviously the funding of the building did not include any money for maintenance, for removing rubbsih from the grounds or for the actual museum collection.

Title: well-worth visiting
Text: My spouse and I are over 65 and decided not to climb the rock. This museum provided less-strenuous exposure to history of citadel, palace, monastery and apsara frescoes. It is in a beautiful new building offering contemporary museum amenities and displays.

Title: very small museum
Text: Mostly just empty rooms, not much to see. It is included in the ticket, though, so you can have a quick look. Don't worry though if you are too tired after the climb - you won't miss much.

Title: Try not to miss this, very informative & modern displays
Text: We went here after climbing Sigiriya & then Pidurangala early in the morning, the cool was very welcome! It looks a huge building but it doesn't have much in it - however what is there is very well presented, including a large diorama of the site. It's definitely worth spending at least 30 minutes having a quick look round if you have the time.

Title: Big boring building with little info
Text:
I went there after I climbed the rock. I did not want to go but I went anyway because the ticket comes together with the entrance ticket. I really hoped it will be worth it, but boy it was terrible. For something so great as Sigiriya, this museum was downgrading. The building was so huge but they are mostly empty & boring.

I would say you can skip this if you are too tired.

Title: Just empty building
Text: I think positive comments are referring to Sigiriya rock, because this is just big empty building. Forget the museum, climb the rock.

Title: wonderful ancient place
Text: This place breathes all with ancient times. The staircase, the constructions, the nature... All around you brings you back to the past. U see almost untouched place. But be careful - it is better to come there only in the morning when the sun is not so killing. Take a water with you - the climbing up could be hard for people with health problems. U can also bargain with guides there and agreeon the price BEFORE you go there, they always cheat.

Title: Worth the climb
Text:
Hard work in the heat of the day but its worth the effort.
You must have a head for heights as the view of the drop from the metal stairs
is not for the faint hearted.You can stop half way at the lion entrance.Tip NO flip flops trainers and a hat recomended. Take a bottle of water you will need it at the top.

Title: A good complement to your visit
Text: This well laid out, unmanageably sized museum was a refreshing break after our climb up (and down) from rock. Good perspective added to visual experience.

Title: Impressive, modern museum
Text: One of the most modern museums I came across in Sri Lanka. Not only is it air conditioned and well lit, the items on display were detailed well. Very informative.

Title: Superbly presented history of site
Text: Well laid out and thoroughly described. Fascinating insight into this world heritage site with ancient artefacts and detailed explanation. All the exhibits were carefully presented and labelled in Sinhala, Tamil and English.

Title: Sums everything together
Text: good place to get a clearer picture of the journey of Buddhism through the ages and how it has taken shape in different cultures.

Title: World Buddhism under one roof
Text: An absolutely amazing experience where one can immerse themselves to learn more of Buddhism. It is in my opinion a great facility and a definite to do for any traveller

Title: Really interesting
Text: Museum for anyone interested to find out more on Buddhism and the history of the temple. Definitely reccomend

Title: Must see
Text: Glimpses of World Buddhism under one roof. Need about an hour to read / see how Buddhism has spread & now a largely global religion.

Title: A Must See Museum
Text: The Museum has Budhist exhibits from India, Japan, China, Korea, Thailand, Pakistan, Afganistan, Laos and many other Asian countries which are well maintained and are a must see.

Title: Should be #2 place to visit
Text: At the time of writing,  this museum is #6 of places to visit in Kandy. But, having visited the temple, we considered this place the next 'must see'. Free admission if you have your temple receipt or a 500 rupees if not, but still a modest fee for a broad oversight of Buddhist lands. Only criticism is that Buddhism in the west, especially in the USA, is completely missing!

Title: Showcases World History of Buddhism
Text:
The Museum is located behind the Temple of Sacred Tooth Relic. The Museum, as the name suggests, showcases the history of Buddhism around the world and the artifacts associated with the Buddhism from around the world. Although it is not a very big museum, the displays have been very well laid out and maintained. There are sections and galleries dedicated to various countries associated with Buddhism, down the ages.
Overall, a good place to spend some time, to get to know about history of Buddhism. No photography is allowed inside the Museum.

Title: Buddha..
Text: A totally different kind of collection of art and history. You can see replicas of most famous pagodas across the world at one place..

Title: The Best Buddhist Museum I have Visited
Text: often called as IBM (International Buddhist Museum) is claimed as the world first IBM which created with contribution of 17 countries. for foreigners, the ticket is included with the entry of Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic. the museum is really good where lots of information provided showcasing the expand of Buddhism around the world, especially in Asia. each country has separate showcase area which makes it easy to cluster the information. photographing is not allowed, but I asked special permission just to take the section of my country. it is really worth of visit.

Title: Inside the temple complex
Text: This place is within the periphery of the tooth relic. The complex is extremely well maintained and beautifully ornated.

Title: Interesting and well laid out museum
Text: This museum is a must visit for anyone interested in understanding the differences in Buddhist art, architecture and practice from one country to the next. The museum is made up of numerous statues, pictures, models and texts explaining Buddhism as it applies to different countries in Asia. Having travelled to four countries with large Buddhist populations it was nice seeing detailing of many of the sites our family had visited.

Title: One of a kind
Text: It was really nice to see the differences of Buddhism across the world and the importance of it in Sri Lanka. With the modest entry fee I would recommend it for all non Buddhist visitors to Sri Lanka

Title: Must visit with kids to get a glimpse of world buddhist sites
Text: Very good place to visit with kids. You get a glimpse of all world Buddhist sites. This is within the sacred temple complex and could easily take an hour to see

Title: Unexpected world class museum
Text: We were pleasantly caught off guard by the caliber of this museum. A very patient and highly informative docent walked us through the entire exhibit, detailing us with knowledge while graciously accepting our 3 children and their prone to hide and seek ways. As lovers of history and art, this was a highlight of our time in Kandy, and Sri Lanka as a whole for that matter.

Title: World Class
Text: We had only a short time, but were very impressed with the artistry and quality of the presentations. It appeals to international tourists as well as locals; English explations abound.

Title: Really detailed and interesting museum
Text: Included in price of Temple of Tooth. You could easily spend 2 hours here reading everything, even if you rush through its still an hour. Dont skip it, its really cool and the museum is unique and well maintained.

Title: Great place if you're interested in the variations of Buddhism in the world
Text: ticket included in temple of the sacred tooth relic - foreign countries were given rooms to display their specific Buddhism so you will see the Pakistan way - the Japanese way - the Tibetan way etc.

Title: Interesting but needed more explanation
Text:
The World Buddhist Museum is a bit hard to find.  It claims to be on the grounds of the Temple of the Sacred Tooth, but you actually go through a gate with a guard to access the right area.  No good signage to get you there.

Upon arrival, you will need to remove your shoes.  We thought the design was interesting: the museum featured a room highlighting how Buddhism is practiced in various Buddhist countries, such as India, Cambodia, Laos, and Sri Lanka.  Very nice displays but I was not able to learn why there are differences among the countries' practices.  

Entrance to this museum is included in your Temple of the Sacred Tooth ticket, so worth a look when you are there.

Title: A great Museum near temple
Text: The museum is adjacent to the temple. So, visitors can just spent some time inside the museum. It is a good museum to learn.

Title: Beautifully Designed. Experience the spread of Buddhism globally.
Text:
This is one place which gives you a 360 degrees perspective on how the concept of Buddhism spread globally, how it is practiced differently in various geographies etc.

The museum is designed in a manner that between the entrance and exit points, all the blocks are kept and you have to - by default - pass through them. Each block showcases the details of Buddhism in a different country and its practices inbuilt over there. 

There is no photography allowed inside. The souvenir shop - run by the trust/ government - provides the best priced items to shop for. This is my experience after staying in different parts of this country for 12 days.

Date of Experience : March 2019.

Title: International Buddhist Museum
Text: International Buddhist Museum is the world's first International Buddhist Museum. The International Buddhist Museum (IBM) was established to showcase the expand of the Buddhism throughout the Asia. It is located next to  Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, Sri Lanka.

Title: Well worth a look
Text: Entry to the World Buddhist Museum is included in the Temple of Tooth Relic ticket price. It is home to loads of displays and interesting items dedicated to Buddhism, providing a great insight and understanding of the religion and its influence on different cultures and countries.

Title: Good insight into Buddhist world
Text: The museum is adjacent to the temple of the tooth relic and can be accessed from the temple. The museum has two floors and you will get great insight into the Buddhist world. I really enjoyed the part where each country had a special chamber where relics and ceremonies.related to that country were shown.

Title: Very informative
Text: There is an extensive collection of historical artifacts and documents from across asia. You dont need a guide as the entire museum is well laid out and marked

Title: Really interesting history of buddhism
Text:
I absolutely loved my trip to the world buddhism museum. It was really informative and covers buddhism from across Asia. 

Definitely get a guide to show you around - mine was able to pass on so much knowledge and more than happy to answer any questions I had. 

I didn't go thi the temple of the tooth so the entry was 500 rupees but totally worth it if you ate interested in knowing more about buddhism

Title: Can visit
Text: Not many people and good to visit when you're at this place.  There have been presented the historical Buddhist information so beautifully inside.

Title: must see
Text: It was a beautiful visit to the museum and all the historical Buddhist facts that have been presented so beautifully inside.

Title: Most Interesting Museum
Text: Well worth a visit and a little quieter than the Temple itself. The history of the spread and development of Buddhism across Asia was fascinating and enlightening.

Title: Very inetresting
Text: Worth taking time to walk around the museum after visiting the Temple of the Tooth.  Nicely presented.

Title: Excellent depiction of History of Buddhism
Text: Housing the artifacts and various depictions of the Highs and Lows of Buddhism over the years in all the Buddhist countries. Gives a great insight into the religion and its History.

Title: Educational and good for rainy days
Text:
Summary:  Your relative happiness with this museum relates to expectations and how much 500LKR means to you. I got what I wanted out of it, but removing a star only because I think that I don't represent everyone.

WHAT THE MUSEUM IS:  The museum is a collection curated by each contributing country around the world that has a long history of Buddhism. The first floor is split with a general overview of Buddha and a number of Central Asia's booths. Upstairs you get SE and East Asia.  The museum gives a brief history of Buddhism for each contributing nation and shows you the sites that are particularly famous in each country's landscape.

WHAT THE MUSEUM IS NOT: Low rating reviews can be divided into 3 groups.  The first, takes issue that the museum is not indepth enough. I would recommend these people just use this museum as an overview and then actual go and visit these countries if you're that passionate.  The second group, feels that there is some misrepresentation that has happened for a given country, for example China. I would remind individuals that Buddhism is not about forcing others to their will. I'm glad they did not use this museum to become political and thus alienate, only to educate. The third group feels that there is some sort of agenda that was espoused.  I did not see it. Mostly, I saw a great exhibit that added places to my travel list. 

THE VIBE:  I thought everyone was pleasant. The museum is requires quiet. Most people adhered to this. Likely for this reason there isn't a lot of talking/guides/etc. Buddhism is about self- contemplation and this museum adheres to that.  Shoes off is very buddhist as is no pictures.  I think those that cringed on all these things, likely have too little experience with this religion.

LANGUAGES:  Most stuff is in English, Tamil, and Sinhalese.  There is SOOO Much reading. There are also videos in the C. Asia exhibits were a nice touch, but other than the one from India, I found them hard to follow. I think perhaps the Buddhist orgs of these two countries might want to work on what they are trying to present and maybe update these videos in the future. 

COST:  Given the nation's average income and that it's only been at peace for 10 years, this is a great museum. Yes, the foreigners pay more, but I didn't find 500LKR outrageous for what it must cost to keep the lights on and staff paid, particularly in low season.  That said, it would be good for the museum to continue to work with other buddhist groups to raise private funding and continue to upgrade the exhibits. 

SUGGESTED UPGRADES:  Since each nation is contributing, possibly Samsung (one of the main sponsors) can provide an app or some device for which all of the different countries can translate a guided tour of the place.  Also, I would love to see them get more artifacts, particularly for C. Asia and China. The rooms were a bit too much text.  China in particularly, could modify the way it presents all the text toward more visual demonstration of the way Buddhism has advanced over time.  I think the best example of a buddhist museum for this place to draw inspiration might be the Angkor Wat Museum in Cambodia. Also, it would be great, if there was an area outside of the museum that could answer questions that individuals had afterwards. I'm not sure how much funding that would cost... maybe they could partner with a university or something. 

FINAL NOTES:  I really enjoyed seeing this overview of Buddhism across countries. I don't think people really appreciate what it might even mean to begin to collect an over 5000 year history of the religion and it's variation across such a ridiculously large land mass. The manner in which some of the leaders were able to blend Buddhism with other religions and cultures is truly remarkable, particularly relative to the other major global sects.  Great start to a museum. Keep going.

Title: Great museum!
Text: This place is beautifully done, and has the history and artifacts of Buddhism from all the countries where is it practiced with any significance. Lots to read so take your time and enjoy. All signs and commentary is in English and clearly written.

Title: Nice museum
Text:
We visited after visiting the temple of the tooth as it is adjoining. 

We enjoyed the museum. It was particularly interesting seeing how Bhuddism has evolved around the world. There were some beautiful statues and exhibits.

Some of the captions were a little dry so we didn't spend too much reading through it all and most of the video displays weren't working. You can't take any photos inside.

Entrance price was 500 rupees when we visited (may 2018).

Title: lot info
Text: We spend around 4 hours in this museum. There is a lot to read, videos, pictures and artefacts. It was very informative if you are interested in Buddhism. Bring some time!

Title: Worth a specific visit !
Text: I visited the museum during my visit of the sacred tooth temple in Kandy and I wished I had more time to spend discovering the history of Budism and its various national specificities. Special mention to the very friendly and knowledgeable staff always willing to help and advise the visitors.

Title: Loved it! History of Buddhism
Text: Loved this Museum! It's located near the Temple of Tooth. The museum teaches you about the birth of Buddhism and how it has grown and practiced throughout Asia. A must for history lovers.

Title: Wonderfully organized
Text: The world buddhist museum is a wonderful museum that has great organization. It splits the buddhist studies and unique depictions and customs between all the countries where buddhism is considered a religion in. There are two floors and the museum is covered in half an hour to an hour. Now, the beginning will interest most, but eventually, some may consider it repetitive and get bored. I would recommend, but only for someone who finds an interest in the buddhist religion

Title: Interesting if eclectic
Text:
A museum of Buddhist artefacts and reproductions from round Asia

A good introduction to the Buddhist world and to the religious beliefs of Buddhist culture 

Ticket is free with visit to temple of the Tooth

Title: Great information, beautiful exhibition
Text: Right behind the temple of the tooth, very interesting exhibition about Buddhism in different asian countries. Fulfills international standards. Great place to go and spens some time

Title: Great museum
Text: I loved this place. The museum was great and I get to learn the history of buddhism throughout the entire continent.

Title: Buddhism across the world
Text: The exhibits are sectioned off into different countries.  Interesting though, that whilst Tibet was included in the 'China' room, I saw no reference anywhere in the museum to the Dali Lama

Title: Realy great museum!
Text: The museum presents the budhism through the countries and each part is excellent decorated and informativ.

Title: On your way out of the temple of the tooth.
Text: Not a particularly engaging museum. It's a very brief overview of all countries in which Buddhism is widely practiced. I didn't find it particularly interesting.

Title: Enlightening place
Text: Fantastic overview of Buddhism and its many faces around the world. Different pavilions for each Buddhist country, explaining traditions and customs. Great gift shop at the exit, as usual. Must see!

Title: One of the best!
Text:
Probably one of the best museum I ever visited. Lots of Buddhism artifacts and statues from various countries. It provides lots of valuable information how Buddhism being spread to all over countries during the century! 

Entrance is free as it is part of the 1.5k rupees paid earlier on at the Temple of Tooth. Otherwise, Just pay 500 for entrance.

Title: Enlightening museum
Text: Highly informative about Buddha,s life history. May be we also get enlightened by a visit. Do not miss if you get an opportunity to visit

Title: museum visit
Text: Very informative and interesting, got to know a lot about Buddha & Buddhism.  There were many facts I didn't know.

Title: must visit place in Kandy
Text: This is located inside the Temple of the tooth relic and you can access entry by purchasing a ticket. If you are a cultural lover this place would add you some precious details to your collection. You will find the stories, some structures, and lot of information that is related to the Buddhism.

Title: Could be interesting
Text: This museum could be interesting.  However it is eclipsed by the Temple of the Tooth and the whole of Royal Palace complex.  It is interesting to know the different teachings of Buddhism but the exhibits were not as captivating.

User_Location: National Capital Territory of Delhi, India
Title: worth a visit
Text: before entering one is greeted by shops selling beautiful flowers for worship. a short walk takes one into the temple .The atmosphere inside is serene ...even though there was a big crowd of worshippers there was no shoving and jostling.Dont miss the carvings on the 200 year old wooden pillars...

Title: Inside the temple of tooth area
Text: Was interesting to see the different types of Buddhism around the world coming from someone who knows nothing about it.

Title: a good place for the buddhist-centric.
Text: a place to learn more wide perspective of Buddhism is geopolitical regions of the world and very educational too.

Title: Really liked ir
Text: Accidentally came into the museum, entrance is included with Tooth Relic Temple ticket. We usually don't like to have guides but this young man had the best attitude, a great smile and just the right information (not too much, not too little) to have a spectrum of what the museum has and Buddhism in the world in about 20 minutes. Nice visit.

Title: Inside the Temple of the Tooth - quite extensive
Text: If you are deeply interested in the minutia of Buddhism, you may find this museum very interesting. There are separate wings for the different styles and geographic areas of traditional Buddhism.

Title: Lazy staff close whenever they want
Text: We went there on 12 April. They were closed stating on the notice that they close from 13-16 April for new year. Guard said thats how it is.

Title: Buddhismorama
Text:
Curious about buddhism history and its development in asia? This is the place for you.

Nice and well arrangered. Interesting to see how different countries try to portray buddhism in their country - i liked how the japanease did their room - less is more sort of style.

Had my share of buddhist museum for a while after this one :)

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Your ticket to the Temple of the Tooth gets you in here for free, and the place is worth taking time to visit. There is a large amount of information about Buddhism around the world, from which I learned quite a lot, and some interesting items on display

Title: Interesting collection of artifacts
Text: You can enter the museum for free with a ticket to the Temple of the Tooth. It is a well laid-out and well presented collection of Buddhist artifacts grouped by country. We spent more time in here that at the temple! Worth a visit.

Title: Quirky and unexpectedly enjoyable museum
Text: It was the Rough Guide to Sri Lanka that enticed us into this museum. Thank you! It is an overview of Buddhism country by country, enabling one to appreciate the differences in style and iconography in each of the Asian countries in which Buddhism has prevailed in the past or present. It is not crowded, nor so large that you would get tired.

Title: History of Buddhist religion
Text: The Museum is the best place in find the history of buddhist religion and the role it played in srilnaka. do visit in afternoon to avoid the heat outside

Title: Buddhist variety that must be seen
Text:
it was fascinating how each country portrayed Buddha just to resemble their race :) 
The contributions of so many countries in one place and the nice presentation made the visit really spectacular.
I'd definitely recommend the visit

Title: Right next to the Temple
Text: Visited this Museum along with our visit to the Temple of Tooth and found very attractive with good layout and highly informative. The Indian section is particularly very educative. Must visit their souvenir shop.

Title: We visited in September 2016
Text: A must see for Buddhist religion. Guide explain every thing to us very well. A ood collection of Buddhist culture.

Title: A cultural highlight
Text: This museum is fascinating and provides a real insight into the Buddhist religion across the world. Set in a lovely old building, there are hundreds of fascinating exhibits, which are displayed very well with english signage. Easy to lose a couple of hours here. The museum is on the sight of the Temple of the Tooth and entry is free on production of your ticket.

Title: A Hidden Gem
Text: The world Buddhist Museum is tucked away, behind the Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth) in a newly restored light grey building. To get to it, you have to walk either through the main temple and out through the rear exit or around the back and through a rear gate with no signpost. No one seems to be aware of the existence of this place. It consists of Buddhist exhibits from all countries where Buddhism once flourished or is currently alive including: Sri Lanka, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Tibet and China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Korea, Vietnam and Cambodia. Each country has presented exhibits that make you want to visit those countries and the visitor can gain some insights into some of the general influences that created the artistic elements such as the sculptures, tapestries and statues from each country. I live near the museum and I've now visited it four times with visitors, and each time, I see something new. For anyone interested in Buddhist art - this is not to be missed.

Title: short study of different buddhist countries
Text: Good overview of different buddhist countries in the world, next to the tooth temple. Takes about one hour.

Title: All artifacts under one roof!
Text: Very interesting place to visit - everything you want to know about buddhism is all here in 20 rooms over 5 levels unfortunately no photography so one could only remember the exhibits on the entire visit.  Don't forget to finish off the museum at their shop.

Title: Interesting yet all over thevplace
Text: Good place to take a stroll and learn a bit more about buddism. It is a bit all over the place, especially the rooms dedicated to specific countries. They are seemingly filled with random artifacts (mostly replica's) and some kitchy stuff. Still, it has its charm and I enjoyed the visit.

Title: Mixed bag
Text:
This place is said to provide an overview of buddhism and it does deliver to some extent 
In fact the building contains a number of country specific rooms that highlight the religion and possible ties with sri lanka buddhism. As far as i could see countries were given their free hand in design of the rooms and this results in an unbalaced exhibit. Highlights are rooms of Bhutan Thailand Burma and Japan but Indonesia did disappoint. Not much explaining and the red line was buddhism but that was it
I would have preferred a much more focused exhibition really telling along a storyline. As it stands it may be seen as a collection of philosophical/religious artefacts

Title: Whole Buddhist world at one place
Text: A must visit for every buddhist and those who are interested in Buddhism. Situated at Sri Daladaa Maaligaawa premises. The museum has dedicated areas for every country which has had a Buddhist history. Amazingly presents how Buddhism was spread throughout asia and people molded their lives through it. Tickets 500LKR for foreigners and 50LKR for locals.

Title: Good for passing some time after temple of tooth
Text: It has Buddha statues from across the world. And shows the history of buddhism, how it reached those countries.

Title: World Buddhist museum
Text: A good sized museum broken out country by country and talking about their Buddhist connections.  I learned of a few more places I need to visit.

Title: Worth visiting!
Text: A must if you interested in Buddhism....very well set out and lots of information in very airy surroundings.

Title: Extremely impressive exhibition
Text: The World Buddhist Museum is adjacent to the Temple of the Tooth and is an extremely impressive museum indeed. It is beautifully laid out so the walk through begins with Buddhism in Sri Lanka, then you enter rooms dedicated to Buddhism in other countries, for example, India, Bangladesh, Thailand, Japan, Nepal, China and many more. There are some truly amazing exhibits from around the Buddhist world. If you wish to take in the whole museum in one visit, allow plenty of time as there is a lot of really interesting and educational material to read as you go along. It costs 500 rupees for entrance for non-Sri Lankans and this is well worthwhile. There is an adjacent souvenir shop. We regard this as a 'must see' for anyone interested in the history and nature of Buddhism.

Title: A pleasant surprise
Text: Right next to Temple of the Tooth, this museum could easily be missed. The story of Buddhism and its spread  across Asia is recorded through items and images that are labelled in English, making the museum very user friendly. The gift shop is worth checking out for inexpensive batik and nice postcards.

Title: Learning
Text: Interesting to learn something about Buddha but an awful lot of reading from the displays around the walls.

Title: Very informative
Text: Not a "must see," but was really informative and would be helpful for those less familiar with Buddism.We enjoyed it.

Title: Just loved it
Text: The was my favourite museum in the whole Temple of the Tooth complex as it was very informative and well set out. I certainly felt that every effort had been made to collect the very best artefacts of each country that was represented, in either actual, photograph or replica format. It is truly amazing how far Buddhism has reached: China, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos and of course many more all faithfully represented.

Title: Awesome collection
Text: Wonderful collection of Buddhist artifacts from all over the Asian, South Asian & SE Asian regions. Very educational throughout. Don't visit if you are watching time - easy to spend many hours slowly ... A great thing to do after visiting the Temple of the Tooth. Photography not allowed.

Title: Interesting and versatile
Text:
This is a museum right next to the temple of the tooth. It is made of two floors with sections displaying Buddhist-related objects and gifts from many countries of East Asia where Buddhism is a major religion.

The museum also has boards with information about Buddhism and quotes from Buddha. I found the Indian, Thai, and Chinese sections most impressive.

If you have bought a ticket to the temple of the tooth, museum entrance is included in the price. Otherwise, a separate entry fee of 500 rupee is charged.

No photography allowed inside.

Well worth a visit. It widens horizons, and teaches about a religion that managed to find its way across many countries and to the heart of millions.

Title: Interesting geographical journey around Asia
Text: We came here after visiting the temples and audience hall. The museum is really informative and the gift shop sells touristic holiday gifts for family and budget prices.

Title: For enthusiasts only
Text:
Despite the fact that the usual racist policy applies: foreigners pay Rs 500, anyone with a stronger tan enters for free, we found this rather boring. It would have been a good opportunity to clearly indicate the differences in buddhism in various countries but they missed that/ made it not visitor friendly.
The most frequently used English label for the replica artifacts is "Do not touch" although they are all in glass boxes...

Title: Very informative but long!
Text: An elaborate history of Buddhism culture and architecture, it covers so many specific countries. We got lazy and tired towards the end.

Title: Great overview of world Buddhism.
Text: This museum provides a detailed, visually stimulating intro and overview to how Buddhists across Asia worship and what kinds of temples and monuments can be found in each country. The Indonesia, Bhutan and China galleries in particular are fantastic.

Title: History of Buddhism
Text:
Within the premises of the Temple of the Tooth, is situated the World Buddhist Museum. It has a beautiful display of the Buddhism history and how it is in various countries that follows Buddhism.
If you are interested in Buddhism, this is a must visit place.

Title: Part of our day tour of Kandy
Text: Veyr nicely done museum- the first floor is a bit odd and seemed disconnected, but then the different exhibits of different countries and how they worship Buddhism was great and very well done.

Title: An Interesting Buddhist  Museum
Text: I enjoyed this museum as it held contributions from 17 countries. It was informative and easy to follow along if you took your time to read each exhibition. Some of the artifacts were reproductions. Some were not. it was not crowded unless a large group of school student are visiting. They do not allow photos without flash, which is a curiosity. The fee for entering is $3.40 pp.

Title: Fascinating insight into Buddhism
Text: well thought out, an exploration of Buddhism around the world. Take your time to read and open your heart as well as your mind can be enjoyed without a guide as it naturally flows from country to country. You will see the familiar and bizarre

Title: very informative museum on Buddhism
Text: very good museum which gives information on Buddhism and the contribution of different countries on buddhism. my personal opinion is must visit.

Title: The historical information
Text: A very detailed museum of Buddhist history and information. It was good to learn the routes of the religions progress around the world and see examples of the temples from different Countries.

Title: Superb museum
Text: Really interesting to see to see. The only downside was that the Tibetan display was written by the Chinese Government so it was a propaganda piece. However, still well worth it. Best museum of its kind that we have seen.

Title: Comprehensive History of Buddhism in Sri Lanka
Text: Excellent museum that documents the history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Also has a shop that sells beautiful souvenirs.

Title: A Great Deal of Information to Digest!
Text:
We quickly became saturated by the displays, photographs, long descriptions and such as this rich museum. The entrance fee was worth it (We didn't pay to get into the Temple of the Tooth, so paid for this separately.) Could have spent longer in here but we just were overwhelmed. 
Please remember that religion in his country, particular Buddhism, cannot be easily separated from ideology or politics, so know that the history you read inside the museum may reflect a particular pro-Sinhalese bias. 
Having said that,  I found the information informative, even though I'm not sure how much I retained.

Title: Informative
Text: This was informative and interesting. I enjoyed it. I did not do everything in it however and skipped the upstairs. The shop has some nice cards and there was a fixed price which is always a relief.

Title: Needs a revamp but interesting.
Text: Interesting but dated and not a modern style of museum. Felt like something from 30 years ago or more.

Title: Interesting Place
Text: Learned a lot - worth the 1000rupees to get in and have a look around.  Marred by the number of schoolkids stomping around the place, but i guess it is an educational venue!

Title: INNER PEACE
Text: Not only for religious pilgrims, but for inner peace and motivation. Loads of history on how buddhism started

Title: Not many exhibits
Text:
Museum of Buddhism doesn't tell a lot about the Buddhism itself neither does it tell a lot about history of the religion. Mostly, the exhibition consists of photos of various temples in different parts of Asia, and an interesting, but rather small collection of statuettes from different Buddhist countries. The exposition is divided into country-dedicated sections, and it's interesting to see how the face of Buddha and deities change when depicted by different nations. The surprising part is that it's prohibited to take pictures inside the museum, given that I didn't see anything that would suffer even from flash photography. 
For me, the main value of the museum was that it helped me make a list of the places in Asia I'd like to visit next.

Title: Nice insight into buddhism
Text: The museum nice idea of the origins and spread of Buddhism. However the entry fee of 1000 LKR for foreign tourists was very high. There were very few tourist visiting this place.

Title: Learned a lot!
Text: Very interesting, lots of history and information.  Helped to understand buddhism more profoundly. It gives an overview of how buddhism is in each buddhist country, we loved that. Make sure you have enough time to spend there.

Title: ok if you are intrested in history
Text: The museum is built in two story  filled with items related to Buddhism  history.  photography is not allowed

Title: If you have an interest in Buddhism you must stop here...
Text:
A huge museum about the world of Buddhism, taking you all around the world and going into great detail about the global history of it.

We were impressed!

Title: Informative museum
Text:
The museum shows the way buddhism spread over asia and gives good insight information how the different branches of buddhism developed. Every buddhist country has a special exhibition.
Fee is 500rs

Title: BRILLIANT MUSEUM
Text:
Well worth a visit. This museum traces the story of how Buddhism migrated from India to the rest of the world and it's interesting to see the slight differences in Buddha's image from country to country. A very peaceful museum with lots of artefacts and interesting displays. 
This museum is situated in the same grounds as the tooth temple and the Bodhi tree where Buddha sat and gave sermons. Today it's enshrined and you'll find locals placing offerings and praying.

Title: A well laid out, informative museum.
Text: this was an interesting museum, divided into different countries to demonstrate the way Buddhism has developed in different Asian countries.

Title: Really well done!
Text: I really enjoyed this museum. Loads of information on a variety of Buddhist cultures and traditions worldwide. I spent a few hours here but could have stayed longer.  Quiet and not too busy when I went and the staff were readily available to answer questions etc. Some of the displays are a bit much, one looks like a Chinese restaurant but overall really interesting.  I liked how each country had their own display room.  Highly recommended.

Title: Cool and comprehensive
Text: Air conditioned, very quiet, exhibits are shown by country- it was fascinating to see the different interpretations

Title: Not a good museum, but definitely a good experience.
Text:
From a museums perspective, this museum is not good. Each exhibit is based on one of the participating Buddhist countries and varies widely in quality and perspective. Each overly dense word panel seems written by a bureaucratic functionary from the embassy with overly careful attention to lauding that country's buddhist tradition. Biases are laid bare: the Thailand exhibit suggests that their King is a Bhoddisatva (a kind of Buddhist saint) and calls him the "King of Kings"; the Tibetan exhibit is a part of the Chinese exhibit and *never once mentions the Dali Lama.* Did you catch that? The "World Buddhist Museum" *does not mention the Dali Lama!
So no, this is not a good museum. it is a terrible museum. 
But it is a great experience! As long as you approach it knowing that each exhibit is a state-sponsored piece of propoganda written by people with understanding of museum principles, it becomes an unintentional museum of buddhist propaganda! 
The the main entryway's exhibit on the Buddha's teachings was really quite moving - powerful and simple moral messages to live by - which, like Western tradition's Ten Commandment, none of the countries espousing them follow them particularly well.

Title: Very enlightening
Text:
Would be a favorite place for museum and history lover while you in Kandy.

You can learn everything about Buddhism from the old to modern age.

Title: SUPERB!!!!
Text: We thoroughly loved this museum!!!! Situated behind the Tooth Temple, it covers all Asian countries were Buddhism is practised. The Museum is well organised: visitors have to follow a fixed route - indications are very clear!! The exhibits which include models of sacred buildings, maps, photographs as well as sacred objects and sacred texts are well presented and accompanied by detailed information!! What is more: it is not full with tourists :-) !!! Allow yourself at least 1.5 hour!!! A MUST!!!!

Title: Interesting
Text: Gives a good overview, which is worthwhile for someone like me, who knows next to nothing on the subject.

Title: Great Little Museum
Text: I am taking a course in Buddhism in Hong Kong and really wanted to visit this museum.  It didn't get a favorable review in a guide book, so I didn't have high expectation. I visited with my young adult daughter, her friend, and my husband.  We were all favorably impressed.  The museum does a good job capturing the "flavor" of Buddhism in all the various countries with displays.  So glad we visited.  Wish I had had longer time to linger.  In and our in an hour.  Great Buddhist souvenir shops next door with the best (local!) prices we found in the country.

Title: Great.
Text: Such a great museum! It was filled with so much information about Buddhism not only in Sri Lanka but all throughout Asia. In order to soak up all the information you would need at least two days.

Title: Great history of kandy and maligawa
Text: It felt sorel to go through the history of the maligawa and also to see the ruthless damages suffered in recent past. Reading through materials of imperial age provided gret history lesson and information on our forefathers and their works.

Title: Very Interesting
Text:
Great place to understand the history of Buddhism and the contribution given from each country to Sri Lanka.
Has lots of pictorials and old relics and early Buddhist statues.

Title: Buddhism around the world
Text: An excellent run through Buddhism around the world. A chance to see some of the world's greatest sites in one place with the all of the labels thoroughly informative and in excellent English

Title: Very interesting
Text: ....but it can takes days to go through it. So much to see and read. Special rooms for each of the South East Asian countries to show their special version of Buddhism. Also information about how the different 'branches' of buddhism have spread over Asia.

Title: Awesome, This place is worth every penny
Text: Most of the people in any city avoid giving a visit to a museum because of old things but i am found of Ancient things and i like to visit such places. this place is worth visiting every penny. The best ever museum i have seen in my life. Tip:- If you are travelling to Kandy and you have time, Dont miss the opportunity to visit this place.

Title: Nothing special?
Text: I really liked the idea of the museum as the comparison of the Buddhist countries always seemed interesting to me. But.. Well... Could have done better and more interactive. Like this, I was unfortunately almost asleep when I got upstairs...

Title: packed with statues
Text: there is trillion statues of buddhas, two floors in which you got to see tons of artifacts, divided in sections according to itself origin, well maintained museum, worth going.

Title: Great educational museum !
Text:
This museum , located within the Sri Dalada Maligawa complex , and you should find the museum with no problem.
A lot of artifacts , history from 17 countries are exhibited, including murals, paintings ,scrolls , documents, instruments.An English speaking guide usually at service.
A lot of Buddha statues of all shape and sizes are exhibited.
Worth a visit , great educational museum for learning the journeys and history of Buddha.
Phototaking and video recording are prohibited inside the museum.

Title: Revisit the Buddhist culture and heritage
Text: Nearby the Temple of the Tooth is the International Museum of World Buddhism. Housed in the former High Court building, this comprehensive study of Buddhism throughout Asia opened in May, 2011, and has rooms dedicated to sixteen nations, from China to the Maldives. From recreations of famous temples Angkor Wat to Javas amazing Borobudur, gifts of relics, paintings and Buddha statues , the museum has rich collection of artefacts from all major Buddhist countries, Countries represented here are China, Korea, Japan, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos, Indonesia , Bhutan, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Nepal Bangladesh and India.

Title: Get to know buddhist culture of 16 countries in one place
Text: Nearby the Temple of the Tooth is the International Museum of World Buddhism. Housed in the former High Court building, this comprehensive study of Buddhism throughout Asia opened in May, 2011, and has rooms dedicated to sixteen nations, from China to the Maldives. From recreations of famous temples Angkor Wat to Javas amazing Borobudur, gifts of relics, paintings and Buddha statues from nations like Laos and Japan, the museum has rich collection of artefacts from all major Buddhist countries. Photography is strictly prohibited

Title: Loads of information on Buddhism all around
Text:
If you want to get some deeper understanding than the 5 minutes knowledge of a guide in the temple, this museum really pays of. Loads of information about symbols, buildings, art, history, ... of Buddhism. The museum takes you through all countries with important connection to Buddhism showcasing their style of Buddhism and can keep busy for quite some time.
I found it very well worth a visit and took my deepest insights into Buddhism during my Sri Lanka trip from here.

The museum is on the grounds of the Temple of the Sacred Tooth so you will need a ticket for that (?) and additionally pay the entry fee to the museum itself (500 LKR)

its a small museum about Buddhism in various south eastern countries  like Cambodia Thailand china Tibet Pakistan India etc... 

entrance fee  was 500 rs

only go if you are very much interested in Buddhism ,

cant take pictures inside.

Title: Interesting!
Text: Really recommended for Kandy, the exhibitions are well described in English. Each room is fashioned by a different country representing different aspects of Buddhism.

Title: An excellent museum

It is also overwhelming because there is just soooooo much in there.  After about an hour and a half, my brain couldn't take any more information. Like me, you might not be able to do it all justice.  However, it's well worth the entrance fee however much you choose to see.

Title: Dull

worth to go there !  We had a guide at the entrance , should be a manager there, who was exrtemly nice, funny and interesting.

Title: Don't miss when in Tooth Temple

Title: Very Interesting

Title: Exceptional
Text: Superb museum retracing the history of world Buddhism. There is also a section dedicated to the Buddhist countries. Each country has his own room. Take your time to visit.

Title: A must see - but make sure you have enough time to take it all in
Text: This is a quite remarkable museum. It has every imaginable piece of information on each Buddhist country's slant on Buddhism. Yet, remarkably, I was unable to find a single mention anywhere of His Holiness the Dali Lama - a great pity and a huge gap in the knowledge therein. The museum has so much material that it would be impossible to take it all in during a single visit. So either use your first visit as a recce, or pick out just a few countries of interest to visit in detail - naturally, these should include India and Sri Lanka. Do be aware that it can get very hot and oppressive in this building, so choose a time to visit when it is cool

Title: Historic information & artifacts

Title: An insightful Visit

Title: Worth the visit
Text: We had an early morning visit to Bundala. The landscape, in parts, is really quite beautiful. We were lucky that there was a bi of water around, and the birds and wildlife very active. We saw plenty of bird life including painted storks, spoonbills, ducks, toucans, hawks, water hens, peacocks etc. Quite a site to look over a small lake and see a tree denuded of leaves, but  full of cormorants drying their outstretched wings. Wildlife included crocodiles, several troupes of grey langurs, wild boar, domestic cattle, water buffalo (a lot of them) and land monitors. The biggest surprise was driving to the coast and pulling up on a rocky outcrop at the Indian ocean. This particular spot also overlooks a fishing village. Having been to Yala, Minneriya and Udawalawe as well - Bundala deserves a place on the must do list for it's contrast to the others.

Title: It's worth it!
Text: Despite the weather,, our safari in Bundala was great. The place is very peaceful: beautiful landscapes and not crowded at all (we saw just one jeep!). We saw many birds but also buffalos, monkeys, crocodiles, a mangoose and a big elephant. We made our safari with Srimal (really recommended). He knows the park very well and he spots animals that a "normal" eye would never catch! His contacts are khsrimal@yahoo.com +94779599397

Title: Interesting contrast to Yala
Text:
Very scenic national park. Much smaller area than Yala. Less interesting in terms of wildlife, although still some great birds and crocs. So much less vehicle traffic is a benefit though. Much less scope for a full day trip than Yala. 

Overall, if I had 1 day I would do Yala, but with a second day Bundala is worth the trip.

You need to take the park appointed guide with you, in addition to your driver guide.

Title: Great day on safari
Text: Birds are the major attraction here, but also monkeys, mongoose, crocodiles, monitor lizards, water buffalo. No elephants, unfortunately. We had a great day.

Title: best place for birding and camping
Text: BundalaNP is a great place. not so many tourist and you will see plenty of wildlife. also you can drive with an open jeep and camp out!

Title: Wonderful Wetlands
Text:
No wonder this is a World RAMSAR site it is full of a wide variety of interesting wetland birds . Arriving just after dawn we drove slowly around the area and surrounding salt pans all morning . Birds seen included : Watercock , Pacific Golden Plover , Rosy Starling , Pin-tailed Snipe , Changeable Hawk-Eagle , Jerdons Bushlark , Hoopoo , Grey-headed Fish Eagle, Indian and Greater Thick-knees , Clamorous Reed Warbler , Jacobin Cuckoo , White-winged Tern , Kentish Plover , Small Pratincole and Red-necked Phalarope .
 This is a must visit if you are looking for water birds and want close views  . The salt pans are spectacular in their own right .

Title: Siri
Text: We booked a morning tour of Bundala park with Siri he picked us up around 5.30am, on entry to the park we seen elephants, Siri was very knowledgeable and has a real passion for bird watching, we also managed to see a family of jackals, we really enjoyed our safari with Siri so much so we booked him for a full day at yala the next morning.

Title: Great safari with Srimal
Text:
I recently visited Bundala National Park on Safari with Srimal. He was very knowledgeable and friendly. We saw lots of crocodiles, monkeys, water buffalo, peacocks, turtles and many other species of birds. The park is also home to a herd of elephants but we were unable to find them that day. 
I would highly recommend a safari with Srimal, he is an excellent guide! Contact him via email or whatsapp to book. 
Khsrimal@yahoo.com
0094779599397

Title: All about the birds
Text:
My husband is a bit of a birder so we planned a morning (3h) safari at Bundala National Park having booked with the fantastic Ceylon Safari Tours. We wanted an extra pair of eyes so hired a bird guide at the gate and we were so glad we did as he was brilliant at identifying some of the more obscure birds.

While Bundala is very much about the birds there are a few elephants here too.  There are a number of different parts of Bundala to explore, with different terrain and water salinity meaning that you get a range of different birdlife.

It most definitely is worth coming early as one of the lakes we visited at sunrise, which was full of birds at the time, was practically empty when we came back that way at the end of our safari about 2 hours later.

We saw a large number of birds - my favourite being the pied Kingfisher, the Eurasian Spoonbill and the purple swamphen.

I'm not a birder at all, but I still enjoyed being out and about enjoying the wildlife and scenery. 

A 3 hour tour from Tissa was plenty of time to explore the park. It's way less crowded than nearby Yala so much more relaxed.

Title: Bundala and Yala with Siri
Text:
Siri is a knowledgable guide, who has a keen eye for wildlife. He was very attentive, knew a lot about the wildlife and hot spots to find them in both Yala and Bundala National Park. 

Bundala was more for reptiles and bird life, and Yala for mammals (elephants, buffalo and a sloth nosed bear and leopard if youre lucky) 

Each tour was roughly 4 hours and started at 5:30am to ensure we saw the best of the wildlife! Siri even took us on our return home to a local lake to see a large family bats - was amazing to see. 

Was offered a very reasonable price for both tours and would recommend

Title: Wonderful birds and much more
Text: Having visited parks in Africa, we were keeping our expectations in check about Bundala.  But, we were pleasantly surprised.The variety of birds is outstanding and we also saw elephants, crocodiles, mongooses, monkeys, wild pigs, spotted deer....The park itself is beautiful with its numerous wetlands sections and gorgeous coastline. When we were there on a late afternoon in March there were few visitors making it a very pleasant experience. We used the services of local guide Siri who is friendly and very knowledgable about the animals in the park. He is great at spotting things. We appreciated that he had several pairs of binoculars for us to use. You can find him on Facebook at Bundala safari with Siri.

Title: Jeep Tour
Text:
Today we went on a private Jeep Tour for 3 hours with Siri. He was a great driver and knowledgeable guide who we were put in touch with through our accommodations owner. He works independently and would be a good option for anyone considering a private tour at a reasonable price.

Title: Great safari with Srimal
Text: We went on an afternoon safari with Srimal who was friendly and enthusiastic. He lead us to storcks, water buffalo, lizards, jungle foul, parakeets peacocks, elephants and other exciting stuff. Bundala is a quiet place to go safari. We booked Srimal at khsrimal@yahoo.com or +94 77 95 99 397

Title: Bird Paradise
Text:
Did an early morning trip from 6 am-9am. It was perfect. 
There were so many birds most of them I had never heard of. My driver organized a Jeep. He accompanied me with his bird book. It was peaceful and enjoyable. 
There were some other animals like water buffalo and crocs. Magnificent lakes too. 
Also stopped at this beautiful beach and fishing area. 
Highly recommend.

Title: A wonderful experience
Text:
Another 5* review for Srimal.

Spent yesterday afternoon in the Jeep with Srimal and my wife and had a really relaxing and enjoyable time. Srimal has great knowledge and seems to have charmed the birds and animals out of the bush for us.

The one thing my wife wanted to see was elephants, particularly baby elephants, and although the parks is not known for this took a change with Srimal. 

3 bull elephants were seen separately and then to round it off, a group of 3 ladies together with 2 babys (3 months old) which we watched to for ages. We also saw lots of peacocks displaying, 2 golden jackels, and countless other wildlife.

We only saw 2 other jeeps in 4 hours.

Finally, the large groups of monkeys were great fun to watch and it was incredible to see the Mothers carrying babies as young as a week old.

Highly recommended.

We got into contact with Srimal directly by email (Khsrimal@yahoo.com) and he also has WhatsApp (0094779599397). Booking was really easy.

Title: Morning Safari
Text: We did a morning safari drive in this park. We saw lots of birds, crocodiles and elephants on the access road to the park and then after entry we saw lots more birds, a mongoose, monkeys, monitor lizards, crocodiles and buffalo. The park was much quieter than Yala and the scenery was beautiful.

Title: Best national park in Sri Lanka!
Text: We visited Bundala, Yala and Uda Walawe and this was by far our favourite. Amazing scenery, teeming with a variety of bird species, crocodiles, buffalo, many many monkeys and we even saw 3 elephants up close. The lack of Jeeps makes it so much more special and you are able to have a real intimate encounter with the wildlife.

Title: Interesting
Text:
We saw a variety of birds at Bundala National Park, which had a very different landscape compared to the other NPs we were at - Udawalawe and Wilpattu. 

Srimal was knowledgeable and readily shared what he knew about the birds, and his driver drove at a delightful pace that allowed us to observe the birds for an extended length. He took photos of the birds too, but hasn't been able to send all of them over.

Title: Beautiful park. The provided guide was amazing!
Text: Wetland park only accessable by jeep, although you are joined by a guide on the way into the park. A lot of birds and other animals, like turtles, monkeys and crocodiles, all of different species. We were sad to hear about the problems with the extremely invasive accacia and cacti that threaten to take over the grasslands needed by elephants etc. We enjoyed it very much!

Title: Not a very big park but to see all that birds and elephants is amazing
Text:
Not a very big park but to see all that birds and elephants is amazing
We visit in the morning the park and spot a lot of different birds, elephants, crocodiles, apes and wild pigs.
It is beautiful nature and because of all the wed lands a good place for the birds. Nice park.

Title: Wonderful early morning bird watching
Text:
We very much enjoyed our 6am sunrise trip to Bundala NP.  We saw a large number of beautiful birds, including a stork enjoying an eel for breakfast, as well as Asian water buffalo, monkeys, monitor lizards, and crocodiles.  The wetlands are truly stunning first thing in the morning. 

Our guide (Srimal) was very friendly and knowledgable, picking us up from our accommodation in Tissa at 5.30am to ensure we were amongst the first in the park.  Here are his details:

Title: Great, quiet place for birdwatching
Text: We visited Bundala park with Srimal (tel or whatsapp 0094779599397) thanks to a recommendation from Tripadvisor. The park is the best place we visited in Sri Lanka. No crowds, a lot of different animals, mostly birds, but we spotted also crocodiles, lizards, monkeys and elephants. Title: GREAT Safari in Bundala with Srimal

Title: Birdspotting safari in Sri Lanka
Text:
We really loved our safari in Bundala with Srimal as a guide! It was very relaxed and quiet, so we could enjoy the nature and animals peacefully. We saw a lot of pretty birds and learned much about them. There were also lots of crocodiles, monkeys and even wild boar, deer and 2 elephants. The park itself is a very beautiful peace of landscape with a still untouched beach.
We would definitely recommend to go on this safari with Srimal. He's a really nice guy who knows a lot about the animals living in the park. His WhatsApp is +94 77 959 9397.

Title: Bundala park tour with Srimal
Text: Had the best time with Srimal in Bundala national park. We were lucky - elephant came 1m from our jeep. It was terrifying and beautiful at the same time. Also saw plenty of crocodiles, wild buffalo, monkeys, birds! Definitely worth visiting - there are no jeep wars, you during 3h trip we saw just few jeeps, and we didn't disturb each other or the animals. Really great experience and Srimal was a professional and knowledgeable guide!

Title: Wonderful park, Chaminda is an excellent guide
Text:
Wonderful national park!
We went with our guide Chaminda, who we found here on tripadvisor, and would definitely recommend him!
He is a friendly guy who knows a lot about the species and has an eagle eye to spot them, we even saw the shikra!
He picks you up at your hotel, and stops frequently to let you observe the animals.
You can find him on whatsapp: 0713095115

Title: An unforgettable experience
Text: We just returned from bundala safari with Srimal.  The trip was amazing.  Srimal is a good man who respects animals, knows every nook and cranny of the park.  Srimal easily spots animals and allows you to calmly look at it and photograph it.  During our trip we saw mostly crocodiles, monkeys, iguanas, bufallos, deers and of course a lot of different kind of birda but we wanted to see elephants the most.  Due to the Srimal knowledge and determination, we managed to see them and enjoy their beauty in peace.  During the 4 hour trip we only saw a couple of other jeeps.  We came to Srimal on recommendation and we highly recommend him to everyone.  Thank you Srimal! Hope to see You again sometime my friend!

Title: Memorable safari with Srimal
Text:
We had previously visited Yala and found it so busy and not what we expect as a safari with 30 jeeps speeding through the park and surrounding a herd of elephants.
As we enjoy spotting birds we decided to try Bundala hoping this would be a somewhat calmer wildlife experience. What a great decision this was, providing a totally different and memorable experience.
Having spent some time searching for a guide, I came across Srimal. Srimal lives immediately outside the park and is so knowledgeable and passionate about the birds and other animals. He provided and great tour, spotting many different birds and animals for us, from the many wading birds to the amazing eagles and falcons (including the beautiful Shaheen falcon).
Near the end of our safari we found about 15 elephants close to the track and we were able to stop extremely close to them. Rather than a short stop to finish on time, we sat watching these amazing animals for about 30 minutes wih Srimal explaining the group dynamics such as the tusker stopping any other males approaching the 1 female.
Such a memorable ending to a great afternoon.
Thank you Srimal.
With only a few jeeps in the park, the safari was far more what one would hope for

Title: Lots of Animals, Very Few Jeeps
Text:
We decided to hire Srimal based on good reviews on TA.  His driver showed up on time (actually earlier) to pick us up.  Srimal lives right across from the park. He grew up there and has intimate knowledge of the park and all the animals there. 

The owner of the Unawatuna hotel we stayed at said, "Budala is a bird park and there aren't even birds now."  He was SO WRONG!  We saw 4 elephants at 3 different locations, a bunch of crocodiles, monkeys, a wild pig, a monitor lizard, deer, buffaloes, peacocks, fresh water turtles and even a cobra, which is rarely seen at the park.  And we saw only 4 other jeeps while we were there for 3 hours.  We decided to skip Yala b/c we read that too many jeeps are distressing the elephants.

Sirmal is very responsive via WhatsApp (+94779599397)  and email (Khsrimal@yahoo.com)

Title: Great for birdwatching
Text:
We just did a 3 hour safari in Bundala national Park, which was well worth it. We are low level amateur bird watchers from Australia and have our own binoculars and bird book (binoculars are highly recommended). 

 We used Srimal as a guide, based on the reviews we had read here on Trip Advisor, and were not disappointed. 

We contacted him through WhatsApp and he replied immediately. He was easy to communicate with, was punctual and came with a driver. The vehicle was fine.

Inside the park Srimal sat at the back with us and was great at spotting birds and identifying them. He lives on the edge of the park and does know his birds. 

Apart from birds we saw a few crocodiles, lots of monkeys, a small monitor lizard , an elephant and two small spotted deers. 

Srimal's contact details are:

0094779599397

He charged us 15000 LKR and we recommend him as a guide.

Title: Magnificent for birding
Text: Coming from Africa, we were not so interested in the elephants and leopards of nearby Yala, but the wetlands that make up this park have a great variety of birds, and by our count, only five other jeeps full of tourists (people just like us!)! We saw spotted deer and wild water buffalo, but if birds are your thing, this is the place to come. A government guide joined us (free of charge) and he knew his birds well! A very enjoyable morning!

Title: Great Birding Spot
Text:
This is little gem of a park, not very busy and the opportunity to see some great birdlife
The driver along with our guide were both experienced birders and know the park well
We also seen a few animals as well as a number of bird species
Great half day tour & well worth doing

Title: great bird watching/pay your entry fee
Text:
great little 1/2 day safari, relaxing, no crowds
magnificent sunrise- great bird watching
be sure to pay your own way at the front gate
our jeep driver/guide offered to do it for us and he wanted close to double the actual price

Title: Fantastic Tour
Text:
After reading the great reviews about Srimal and his expert knowledge of Bundall Park. We booked a early morning safari with him. We were picked up on time from hotel and greeted with a smile from Srimal. We spent the next 3 hours gently touring the park seeing wonderful bird life, elephants, monkeys, mongoose, tortoise and much more. Srimal is kind and gentle and has a passion for all wildlife which is obvious with his approach. We would highly reccomend  his company for a private Safari in Bundala National Park. Title: Probably the single best Birding Location in Sri Lanka ????
Text:
My wife and I visited here twice during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka ????. The park itself isnt particularly large and can be quite easily covered in a day. Tour with an experienced guide is essential to get the best out of a visit. The bird life can be somewhat overwhelming to the experienced Birders never mine the less experienced. The park consists mainly of wetlands, scrub and the added bonus of Salt Pans. During our visit were saw a spectacular array of Birds and even managed to find a couple of very rare winter visitors in the form of - Bay-backed Shrike and Black-capped Kingfisher. 
A lovely well maintained park and should be top of anyones must visit site. Highly Recommended.

Title: An unexpected surprise
Text: We were driving from Hambantota to Kirinda and took a short cut, which turned out to be part of the perimeter road of the Bundala National Wildlife Park. The drive along this road did not cost anything and we saw as much wildlife here as we did in the Yala National Park, which cost Rs.7,000 each to visit. The shortcut is highly recommended.

Title: Srimal. The king of Bundala NP
Text:
We arrived in Bundala after an early and full morning searching for the elusive leopard in Yala. Consequently we were quite tried before our afternoon safari in Bundala. We are also not really bird people so despite the good reviews our expectations were low for the afternoon.

Srimal has a driver with him so he concentrates on spotting wildlife. Yes there are some lovely birds but he also managed to spot a Python, star tortoise and some carefully camouflaged crocs.

We were also lucky to see the Elephants.
There is also a nice cliff overlooking the rugged sealine. This and numerous pretty watering holes adds to ambience.

The park is relatively small but overall a very pleasant way to spend an afternoon.

Title: Wonderful birdwatching experience
Text: Went on an early morning trip to Bundala and saw many interesting birds in the lovely dawn light.  The beauty of the landscape and the tranquillity would appeal to people not so interested in birds.  If you are more interested in animals, the afternoon is the best time to visit.  Few other vehicles there: not like Yala.  Our guide was Srimal, who was very knowledgeable: khsrimal@yahoo.com

Title: Great Visit if you like birdlife
Text: Fantastic variety of Birdlife, from Pelicans to Bee Eaters, Kingfishers, Eagles. Also saw Elephants and Monkeys. Did an organised trip through Sam's Travels near Hambantota. Sam and the guide from Bundala very knowledgeable.

Title: Great visit. Worth the time.
Text: This park was full of wildlife. All types of birds, monkeys, crocodiles and small animals. There was so much to see, we loved it. We did this instead of the wildlife which was supposed to be very crowded. We werent disappointed.

Title: Bundala Wildlife
Text: Great  birding trip with SameeraSampath (+94792 64692 or sameeraatyala@gmail.com) at Bundala National Park in February.  Amazing variety of birds and also Elephants and Water Buffalo doing what they enjoy most rolling in the water.  Various habitat and even very worthwhile trip to the beach.

Title: Safari to Bundala
Text:
We went on an early morning safari as we wanted to see as many birds as possible, we used Shrimal as our guide and he was excellent, he found lots of good birds for us including a black bittern  very good views of this. He speaks good English and can be contacted on +94779599397 he uses what's app and replies very quickly. He charged us SLR 5000 each inc all fees and we were the only two in the vehicle,so we stayed as long as we wanted at each sighting. He also arranged our taxi to Tangalle.

You can actually walk to the park entrance and see loads of birds we did this the evening we arrived, from the Lagoon Inn turn right, walk along maybe 100 meters then right again I think there is a Park Sign there,walk  along the dirt track there are birds everywhere.

For non birders don't expect too much an elephant if you are lucky, crocodiles, mongoose, monitor lizards and water buffalo that's about it. The trip stops at a headland above a beach to give you a break.

A must for birders

Title: Wonderful varied landscape and wildlife
Text: We saw so many different birds and animals during an afternoon safari. The landscapes are beautiful and very varied with lagoons, bushland and coast.

Title: Get the right guide
Text: Arrived before dawn and had a wonderful tour. We were so lucky to have a brilliant guide Pemadasa Safari Service (Lokka). Whilst most went straight to the park entrance we spent at least 30 minutes at the wetlands before the entrance looking at birds. In the park the paths are rough but not to bumpy with a good driver. There are a host of fascinating birds, not always easy to see which is where you need help. Even spotted a chameleon on a tree whilst driving. We struggled to see it when pointed out and with binoculars. This a lesser known park but well worth the 13500 R for safari

Title: Some of the best birding you will find
Text:
This is a real hidden gem for birding and scenery.
The terrain is varied and beautiful.
You should see a vast variety depending when you visit. We saw two types of eagle close up, as well as osprey and many other species. We also saw elephant, mongoose,deer and a jackal.
We could spend all day there but a morning was a treat.
We suggest the excellent Sam tours. A guide/ranger joins the vehicles at the gate and they are good spotters.
Hope to return soon.

Title: Nice day-trip as we had a nice guide
Text:
I was bringing my parents along in this trip to Sri Lanka. We were staying in Galle for 4 nights. We picked this national park because it's driving distance to Galle is acceptable.

Lucky for us, we had a very good guide. The name of his company is Srimal Safari.
Email address is  khsrimal@yahoo.com; Whatsapp is  +94779599397.

His team came to our villa to pick us up. A little extra transportation fee was charged. They managed to find a decent restaurant for us to have lunch near the national park. The food's not everything-spicy. The coca-cola's cold enough. The toilet's very clean.

The park is mainly for elephants, monkeys and many kinds of birds. It's peaceful, not crowded. Staying quiet is very important, not to disturb the normal life of the animals.

Our guide has very sharp eyes and he knows every inch of the park. With his guidance, we saw many kinds of birds, a huge family of monkey, a couple of elephants, a crocodile and a turtle. 

At the edge of the park, there is a stunning cliff overseeing the Indian Ocean. It's so windy up the cliff, my girlfriend's hat was almost blown away.

Recommended to go there near dusk. The lower the sun, the more appearance of animals.

Title: Bird park
Text: Lots of birds n different breeds  clean well kept grounds  but theres many many birds you can see in natural habitat in Sri Lanka

Title: Excellent birding at Bundala National Park
Text:
Had an excellent safari with Sameera Sampath as a guide on 24 February 2018.  His knowledge of both the park and the birds is first class and I cannot recommend him highly enough to other birders - he even knows where to find 6 photogeinc Little Pratincoles - a real treat!

If you want good birding I suggest you go to Bundala and not Yala.

Title: Brilliant bird park
Text: This was a really enjoyable visit the birds, the crocodiles. The guide made it a great experience. We organised through them hotel and chose an early morning safari I would definitely recommend.

Title: Excellent safari with elephants & birds
Text: I had a great 3 hour safari at this park in the afternoon. We saw lots of colourful birds both on the water & on land. I was also lucky & saw 2 elephants up close, a crocodile, tortoise & monkeys. I really enjoyed the landscape, a mixture of lakes, trees and the beach. It was also nice that there was only a few jeeps there in the afternoon & often we were driving round on our own. I did the trip with Srimal, he was a great guide and he also had a driver. Definitely recommended to contact him & he can offer a trip. Contact him on 0094779599397, khsrimal@yahoo.com.

Title: Smaller than Yala but a jewel
Text: Last year we visited Yala and took part in chasing the poor leopard. This year we went to Bundala and found a jewel full of birds, monkeys, buffalos and warans. Great and only a few other jeeps. We love it and avoid the big parks from now on.

Title: Beware - so badly organised
Text: We visited the park as independent travellers, with our own car. After being encouraged to pay the entrance fee of £12 each, we were told we couldnt go in the park without paying a big fee for a guide and it was ok to use our car as the roads inside were fine. This was not right. We reluctantly paid for a guide as there we no maps at the visitor centre but wildlife was scarce and the roads so bad we damaged the car. We probably chose our time poorly as we visited in the day not at dawn but nevertheless a dreadful experience. We felt exploited by the staff rather than helped with advice.

Title: Wonderful birds
Text: Sadly this little gem of a national park is often overlooked by tourists. We had a super morning's safari with our guide Pandika, who was a volunteer guide and passionate about birds. Our driver Lanesu was equally enthusiastic. Variety of terrain and habitats, including salt pans. We also saw an elephant!

Title: A paradise for bird watchers
Text: We visited this National Park as opposed to Yala National Park to avoid the crowds and it was an excellent decision. Excellent bird life and viewing, quiet roads and really special. Some animals - deer, buffalo, monitor lizards but we did not see the elusive elephants. A good idea to hire a local guid from the Park who knows all the birds and roads. Well worth the trip

Title: Great park with abundance of wildlife
Text: Bundala National Park offers a great abundance of wild animals without being too crowded with jeeps. Most of the time we were alone, only from time to time we met other jeeps so we could really enjoy the atmosphere. We saw a lot of beautiful birds, deers, monkeys, crocodiles, mungos, a python... and even one elephant! We can definitely recommend to make the tour with Srimal. You can just contact him via whatsapp or e-mail, he will come back to you very quickly: 0094779599397 or Khsrimal@yahoo.com

Title: See crocodiles and birdlife up close on an afternoon Safari drive in Bundala NP.
Text: We chose Ajith Safari for an afternoon drive through the lagoons of Bundala National Park, based on our great experience with that company in Yala NP  Surprisingly Bundala surpassed our drive in Yala.
