Elephants, crocodiles galore, diverse birds of all sizes, including water fowl, raptors and song birds, monitor lizards, even a tortoise came into view.  Of course water buffalo lolled in the pools.

Title: Half Day Safari
Text:
We visited Bundala for a half day Safari with a local guide. We were staying in a hotel just outside Hambantota, our guide collected us there and drove us the 30 mins ( we saw wild elephants en route to the Safari) 

During the Safari we saw lots of water bird ( Heron, crane, stork, pelican, egret, kingfisher, spoonbill cormorant, etc) and dancing peacock, eagle, owl, bee catchers and then Elephants, Water buffalo, Crocodile, mongoose, Monkeys, monitor lizard and a whole lot more. Our guide had great eyes, could see things everywhere and was extremely knowledgeable. 

We enjoyed this trip so much we discussed other local visits that our guide could arrange - and we ended up visiting the local Elephant Transit at Udawalawe, the Yala Safari and also a days Whale Watching out of Mirissa.  

Our guide was Srimal( khsrimal@yahoo.com, +94 779599397) who was a great communicator and accommodated all our trips with great flexibility. ( he virtually lives on the National Park, we passed his house on the way in) 

He is a very friendly and knowledgeable guide who can arrange most things and is very reliable. I would recommend you email him before going and sort out your trips,

Title: Your up with the sunrise!
Text: This is definetly a worthwhile  activity to do especially as it's early in the morning and the birds are all there before they move on for the day. We got the hotel to organise it for us but you can contact the safari people yourself.  It's not too expensive and the guides are very helpful.

Title: Elephants, Elephants, Elephants!!
Text:
Only came to Bundala as our planned camping and safari at Udawalawe was cancelled due to flooding. 

We took an afternoon safari from our accommodation - this was the perfect time for elephants.

The landscape is stunning.

We saw a full herd of elephants (inc. 2 calfs) as well as monkeys, monitor lizards, crocodiles and many beautiful bird species.

Both our guide and driver were amazing.

So many elephants!! 

Such a beautiful place and we had a perfect up-close encounter. 

Shorter afternoon safari is the perfect length for younger children. Went to Yala afterwards and found it over-crowded, disappointing and too long to be comfortable for young kids.

Title: Great excursion for birds. Srimal is an excellent guide
Text:
We booked Srimal for an exclusive morning safari in Bundala, and we were not disappointed. Srimal proved to be very knowledgeable and very keen on showing us the different species in the park.

We were fortunate enough to see an elephant bull as well, which apparently is very rare. But the main theme of this morning was birds. If you are into birds, book a trip with Srimal. 

Bundala is much less crowded than Yala, so this park is a completely different experience.

Title: Must see for bird watchers!
Text:
I have read in the guide this place is mandatory for bird lovers, so it really is! The birds are mostly on the ground what is perfect for observing and taking photos, they don't fly away while you are there and the guide mostly offers you binocular.
The perfect place to stay both for Yala and Bundala is town Tissamaharama.
I took full day tour (don't regret!) and my driver identified all species, provided me two guide-books had binocular etc. Unlikely the one (actualy two) in Yala - didn't talk almost nothing.
You can take half day tour, but full day is also good. 
We also saw several crocodiles and elephants - from few meters, much closer than in Yala.
You have 20 minutes driving from Tissamaharama to there.

Title: Awesome!
Text: A beautiful trip with magnificent views of tropical birds. Oh and elephants of course. Our driver and guide were great and helped us to identify lots of birds that we had never seen before.

Title: Lovely way to spend half a day
Text: This was a great place to visit, much quieter than Yala National Park. We saw some fabulous birdlife, quite a lot of mammals and reptiles too. You have to have a guide and the roads are interestingly bumpy.

Title: So many birds! And more...
Text: It starts even before the ticket office of Bundala park. In half an hour on the way to park entrance we saw more birds than during a day trip to Yala. We got a great guide Mr. Karu from Tissa, he used a illustrated book on Sri Lanka birds to explain what birds we were watching.

Title: Birdwatcher's paradise
Text:
Different kind of birds to see and also animals (crocodile, elephant, large lizard, deer). A must visit while in Sri Lanka.
Stay at a nearby hotel: Lagoon Inn to take advantage of their good and resaonably priced safari tour.

Title: An excellent place to view the rich diversity of Sri Lankan flora and fauna
Text: An excellent visit - uncrowded and peaceful with just the sound of birds and the breeze (and the engine of the jeep as it negotiates the ruts and gullies); lots to see, particularly rich in birdlife but we also spotted a mongoose, numerous crocodiles and monkeys and deer. A great alternative to the traffic jams in Yala!

Title: Great Safari, great guide
Text:
Only came to Bundala as our planned camping and safari at Udawalawe was canceled due to flooding. 

So many elephants!! Such a beautiful place and stick a prefect and up-close encounter.

Shorter afternoon safari is the perfect length for younger children.

Title: Half a day with the birds!
Text: Primarily a bird reserve, but we also saw groups of monkeys, monitor lizards and elephant. Compared with Yala and Udawalawe, reserves, this was a pleasure. It was uncrowded and it was very peaceful. We saw many bird species.

Title: Bundala National Park tour with Srimal
Text: It was a super nice tour in the park! I would deffo recommend it if you like animals and some wildlife experience. We saw lots of different birds, two types of monkeys, waterbuffalos, crocodiles and some more small animals. Unfortunately we did not see the elephants, but its very rare and you have to be lucky! Srimal is a very nice guide and convenient to go with through the park. You can just call, whatsapp or email him directly. He replies super fast! Email: khsrimal@yahoo.com and 0094779599397.

Title: Wildlife tour in Bundala with local guide Srimal
Text:
We had an amazing time here. Saw lots of macaques, langurs, and loads of birds. Quite a lot of crocodiles as well and a mongoose. We asked Srimal (a local guide) to take us, who was excellent. He knew where all the best spots were and knew the name of every animal we saw. Contact details for Srimal: Khsrimal@yahoo.com
0094779599397. Highly recommended.

Title: Siri makes this a great experience
Text:
If you are thinking about going on the safari, we could definitely recommend this. Lovely birds, monkeys, alligators and elephants. The wildlife at Bundala is astonishing.

We went a guide called Siri, as mentioned by many here he is really good. Knows and spots the bird before you are even close and is extremely friendly. His email is piyasiriubewarna@gmail.com and phone 0770232577.

Really easy to book and great value for money

Title: Fabulous
Text: Fantastic Birds, lovely wetland environment, amazing dunes and a thoroughly fabulous experience which pleased us all. Great young guide too.

Title: Wonderful
Text: Our previous two safaris at Hurulu Eco park and Yala National Park had seen swarms of jeeps chasing wildlife. This was a completely different experience. We only saw one other jeep during our two hour safari. Following other favourable reviews we booked Srimal 009477 9599397 and he sat in the back with us pointing out things we would never have seen on our own. Although billed as a bird safari there are elephants here too and we saw three of them including a 55 year old male at a water hole  a special moment.

Title: Beautiful place
Text:
We saw lots of wildlife and our guide was very informative. A beautiful place, not as crowded with jeeps as Yala.
On the negative side some of the entranc3 money would be well spent on improving the toilet facilities, Only one available and it was broken, smelly and the walls covered in frogs. Also one of the jeeps that some of our group was in seemed old and unreliable, several times it didnt start straight away and then broke down completely.

Title: A real surprise
Text:
Bundala National Park is very unspoilt,uncommercialized and far less touristy than its neighbouring parks such as Yala
During our three hour safari with Srimal we only saw three other jeeps so it gave the sense of a pioneer adventure
We saw elephants,crocodiles,buffaloes,pelicans,storks and a diverse range of other smaller birds
There were many monkeys including a large group with many females carry their young on front of their bodies
Srimal was very knowledgeable of the animals and birds 
The price of SLR13500 covered the cost of the jeep,driver and park entry fees and  all in  all very reasonable
Srimal is very calm discrete and engaging and passionate about his work
You pay for the jeep rather than per person so we were able to bring our taxi driver

Title: Email or call Siri
Text: After going over prices I found Siri to have the best price.  Picked us up from hotel did safari and returned to hotel.  Also for a little extra took us up to Yala for our next hotel.  He knows his birds and stopped on the road because there was a wild elephant even before we got to park.  What a great experience. we email him in the early evening and set up for the next morning.

Title: Amazing safari with Srimal
Text: We have just finished our afternoon safari with Srimal and his excellent driver. He is an excellent guide as all the other reviews say. He was easy to communicate with when booking - responded quickly. He arrived on time at our hotel. He lives right near the park - its like his back garden, and has been guiding for 10 years. He sits with you not in the cab and so he is able to explain everything, identify the birds and wildlife and answer questions. He is alert - using both his eyes and ears. We saw crocodiles, monkeys, land monitors and loads and loads of birds. Then, because of his excellent guiding skills he heard then saw an elephant hidden to us in the trees. A large older male, who walked in front us before disappearing again. Srimal thought he was going to a nearby water hole and we waited there lo and behold the elephant came to drink and cool down. What a treat.  Yes its hard to see elephant in this park but..... the whole experience is peaceful and quiet, fewer jeeps and calm when viewing. It was a great afternoon Thanks Srimal and good luck  WhatsApp 94779599397 khsrimal@yahoo.com book him in advance if possible to be sure to get him

Title: Evening safari with Wasanta
Text: Stayed at Bundala Flamingo Cotteges. Amazing location overlooking wetlands. Booked a safari through the property and we were introduced to Wasanta our driver and guide. He was brilliant! He told us so much about the local area and the life of the villagers as well as having a superb knowledge of the birds. We saw so many new things and were incredibly privileged to see elephants in 3 different locations. I am sure this mostly due to Wasantas knowledge and understanding of the animals in the reserve.

Title: Amazing Eye Opening Safari at Bundala National Park
Text:
Our fellow cruise passenger organised safari at Bundala National Park. Our ship docked at Hambantota. Srimal provided us with a convoy of 7 jeeps. He himself was in command, in one of the jeeps. The park is  beautiful,
with diversities of landscapes, plants and abundance of birds, animals and reptiles. We passed ponds, lagoons, salt pans, wetlands. The drivers had sharp eyes for spotting birds, animals etc. They stopped for us to take photos from the jeeps. Birds were in abundance, peacocks roamed about, water buffaloes in herds, red face and black face monkeys, crocodiles and elephants etc. It was indeed eye opening for most of us, the change of sceneries, the species of birds, animals, reptiles in their natural habitats. The convoy of jeeps wrapped up the safari at a view point, overlooking white sand beach, blue waves. Srimal and his colleagues delivered and we had an amazing experience.

Title: Wetland Kamal safari, Bundala Park.
Text:
We stayed at Lagoon Inn, chosen because of its proximity to Bundala park, and bird Tower. The owner Kamal, runs his own safari firm, contact lagooninn@yahoo.com / 94716310173, and organised for us to be picked up following morning at 6am for a half day safari. Driver was prompt, and we headed out in a comfy vehicle. And a couple of minutes later, we were snapping away! We photograph birds, and driver Siri had sharp eyes, and knew them all.....he stopped when he spotted anything, or when wer tapped on roof. And although we mainly wanted to just see birds we also saw a few elephants for good measure!
And then back for a good breakfast .....and a trip to the loo!!!

Title: Relaxing safari with lots to see
Text: After a hectic morning rushing about Yala chasing leopards, Bundala was a great change of pace. I was lucky to have one of the park rangers join me, and he pointed out all kinds of birds and animals I wouldn't have seen by myself. The park is huge and there are a number of different landscapes from marshes, to slat flats, forest areas, tall grass, the longest sand dune in Sri Lanka and a beautiful coastline viewed from a rocky cliff, which kept things interesting.

Title: Tremendous safari with srimal
Text: Our family had a terrific safari with srimal at bundala national park. He is very knowledgeable about the area and all that Bundala has to offer. Our wonderful experience of the park was largely due to the way he went about his work. He uses a driver which allows him to focus on spotting, unlike our experience at Udawalawe. We would highly recommend seeing bundala and using srimal. This is a beautiful place - and we only saw 5-6 other deeps in the park.

User_Location: New Forest National Park Hampshire, United Kingdom
Title: Great little National Park for a half day safari
Text: Elephants, mongoose, monkeys and 50 species of birds a great way to spend an afternoon. Entrance price to the park is not bad compared to other parks and much quieter than Yala. Its well known for its bird life so Id ask your guide to point them out, helps break up the journey round too! We used Piyasiri Ubewarna (Siri) as our guide, excellent knowledge on every species.

Title: Very nice for birds and not crowded
Text: We did a half day safari in the morning and enjoyed it very much. We saw many birds including Elephants and Crocodiles. This National Park is still quiet and that is a plus.

Title: Birds birds birds! Ih and some monkirs and mongoose and crocs and elephants
Text: Bundala is a great place better that Yala by miles just no leopards (which we didnt see anyway in Yala)

Title: a pleasant and interesting experience
Text: We took off from the hotel in Tissa before sunrise just in time to arrive Bundala when the sun rose. Srimal and his jeep driver are both very good at spotting birds and animals, and they work great as a pair. We were in Yala before and Bundala is definitely a better experience, with fewer jeeps and many more animals and birds.

Title: peaceful and great for bird watchers
Text:
we booked a jeep for an afternoon tour from Tissa with an independent driver from the car park near the lake. The park was very quiet compared to Yala and most of the time there were no other jeeps in sight. Our driver was excellent at spotting and identifying birds and had a bird guide in English. There was lots of other wildlife to see including crocodiles, water buffalo, deer, a mongoose, monitor lizards, tortoise and an elephant.
We are not experienced bird watchers but enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere here.

Title: very nice and interesting
Text: park too undervalued due to the nearby yala national park. here you live a real atmosphere without being with dozens of jeeps circling around. famous for birdwatching but there are also very varied fauna. a place not to be missed. among the various birds we have also managed to spot rare and other very large and colorful specimens.

Title: Birds and Elephants
Text:
We enjoyed a fabulous afternoon safari at Bundala. The wetlands provides the opportunity to view a wide variety of birdlife. We also saw a turtle/tortoise laying eggs in its shallow hole and covering them up before returning to the water. 
There was the opportunity to stretch our legs at a headland overlooking a fishing camp on a beautiful beach on the Indian Ocean.
Whilst there arent a large number of elephants we were fortunate to see several small groups out in the open and on the fringe of the forest. The behaviour of the elephants was different to those in the larger parks, presumably theyd see fewer people, and are quick to trumpet and feign a charge if they consider your Jeep is getting too close.

Title: Amazing place for birding
Text: I have seen almost 40 species of birds during the safari on that afternoon,along with 2 species of monkeys and several other mammals.Highly recommended!

Title: Excellent for RSPB members or bird watchers
Text: This was our second year visiting Bundala national park with Ceylon Safari a member of the independent drivers association and Chamara an experience Sri Lankan bird watcher. This year we were able to visit the new tanks that are attracting diverse birds in large numbers- Purple necked heron, Pelicans and on land we watched an Osprey and black necked stork as well as a yellow Bitten. Fantastic day and without the crowds of 4WD in Yalla.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Unlike the busy Yala park block 1, this is a quiet and beautiful park. It is unlikely you will see large mammals, although we did see a bull elephant. However we saw 50 species of birds. Quite wonderful.

Title: Birds, birds and still more birds
Text: Waking up at 04:30 in the morning and after one hour´s travelling when the sun was raising we arrived to Bundala. It was so fantastic to see hundreds and hundreds birds there. Sam the Man is the king of the guides!

Title: So many birds!
Text: Enjoyed the visit. Saw so many Birds and even some crocodiles. Our Driver/guide did an amazing job. Pradeep Was top notch. https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g1027209-d9738923-Reviews-Safari_in_Sri_Lanka-Hambantota_Tangalle_Southern_Province.html

Title: Worth the visit
Text: We decided to do Bundala instead of Yala as we had read so many stories about how crowded & chaotic it can be. We ticked everything off our bucket list from an up close and personal encounter with a male elephant to crocodiles, water buffalo, mongoose, heaps of monkeys, birds ,monitor lizards & a wild boar. We went at sunrise & saw the water buffalo taking a morning bath. Our driver was quite knowledgeable & knew the different types of birds. The safari was arranged by our hotel, Gaga Bees, who also made sure we had a packed breakfast.

Title: Safari at 2 pm but still saw many bird species
Text: Went to Tissa on business and on the was back visited the park. It was past 2 pm and not an ideal time for bird watching. However we were blessed to see many species such as storks, thick knees, snake birds, purple herons, bird eaters, parrots etc. It was a fun and fascinating experience. We even saw a lone elephant, few crocs, lots of monkeys and peacocks. It was a rough ride in some places but I thoroughly enjoyed it. We had a short stop on a cliff overlooking the sea and the view was gorgeous. We ended by going around the salt lake.

Title: Great morning safari
Text: We had a great guide, Asila, and a tracker from the park service, both of whom really made the experience. They set expectations low early - mostly birds, and maybe it typically is - but we saw elephant, crocodiles, deer, mongoose, monkeys, and a host of bird varieties. They were laser-eyed, pointing out the tiniest birds, and patiently waited while we ogled and snapped photos. They also broke for leg-stretching at the most picturesque seaside cliff. We did the 2-hour tour and it was perfect; any longer would have become repetitive/boring.

Title: Very few birds in the park, the driver did his best!   Srimal from bundala tours
Text:
This bird park definitely has on and off seasons.
Our driver and guide, srimal knew his birds and pointed them out to us. He had a good eye and made our time an enjoyable one, even though the number of birds was quite low, being the dry season.

Title: Safari with Srimal
Text:
With all the good reviews for Srimal, we contacted him to arrange a safari in Bundala. For 11 000 rp we were supposed to have a private jeep with a driver and Srimal as a guide with us. We were disappointed when we saw that Srimal was driving because it was difficult to interact with him. He was nice and gave some informations about the park but it was limited. We had the same service in Udawalawe (jeep and driver who give info for 9000 rp). In his message, he told us that the afternoon was a good time to see animals but once we were in the jeep, he told us it was to dry and hot at this time of the year to see animals. He did not make a discount when we told him we were paying for guide and driver but had only the driver. 

Bundala is a nice national park, very quiet. We saw only 5 jeeps during our safari. We visited in dry season so it was not good for animals and birds but we saw 2 elephants. If you have only one safari to do, choose Udawalawe instead, it was perfect!

Title: Incredible safari
Text:
Best safari we've ever been on, and we've been to South Africa! Our safari, which was arranged by Kamal at the Lagoon Inn, situated right next to the park (0716310173) and a wonderful place to stay, was absolutely fantastic. We had everything explained in perfect English and the guide had eagle eyes and spotted wildlife that we would never have otherwise seen. We saw about 30 huge crocodiles going about their business and watched one catch a fish! The birds are amazing, so many different varieties and incredible colours. It was like being on the set of a BBC wildlife documentary! There are elephants,  lizards, monkeys plus loads more. 

The fantastic thing about Bundala is that there are no crowds, it's a hidden gem that means that the wildlife is totally undisturbed, unlike other more 'popular' and touristy nature reserves. Highly recommended and our best experience from our 3 week trip to Sri Lanka.

Title: If you like birds...
Text: This little gem is often passed by. It's a wetland on the south coast and boasts a wide range of birds. We were there for a few hours out of the really busy bird season but still had a great time photographing herons, langurs, crocodiles, and a wide range of birds. Pretty. Not a place for people who like their attractions on a plate. You get around by jeep.

Title: Famous for migratory birds
Text: We visited this park with friends straight after our visit to Yala National Park and what a contrast.   We were told that this is a park that is an internationally important wintering ground for migratory water birds in Sri Lanka with 197 species of birds. It is also a Ramsar wetland. We spent a very pleasant four hours meandering around and found a few species we hadn't photographed before. It was a very pleasant experience after the frantic pace of Yala.

Title: A different safari park, with focus on bird spotting
Text: Good, even in the off-season lots and lots of birds. The guide was very knowledgeable and good spotter

Title: Amazing
Text:
Ours was a 'last minute' booking as we initially did not intend to go for a Safari. But we are extremely glad we did go for it! We contacted Srimal (found him thru Tripadvisor reviews) 3 days before the Safari date we wanted and everything went smoothly. He practically arranged everything for us.

It was a very, very good experience for our family and it is fair to say that it is the highlight of our Sri Lanka trip. We thank God that we are able to experience this wonderful Safari as a family.

Highly recommended family activity. We also recommend Srimal as he is very knowledgeable, friendly and trustworthy guy.

User_Location: Emirate of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
Title: natural habitants
Text: This is a place you'd hire a 4x4 to see different animals where they live in their natural home. different animals from elephants to crocodiles and animals on top and above. it takes almost 4 hours with full of "waoooss" and surprises. you'd love it. don't miss if you'd visit to this are area this truly heaven on earth.

Title: Brilliant national park
Text:
In an effort to avoid the circus of Yala we chose to come to Bundala instead. We arrived at 6.00 when it opened and were immediately rewarded by seeing a group of elephants emerging from the morning mist! We spent about 3 hours in the park (including having a break on a viewpoint overlooking the amazing coastline) and saw so many different types of birds (indigenous and migratory), crocodiles, mongoose, monitor lizards, monkeys, macaques, and another herd of elephants (there are only 25 in the park so we were very lucky!)  In all that time we only saw 1 other jeep, the rest of the time we were alone in nature. The landscape is spectacular, especially as is the wet season and so very verdant!

The tickets for two cost 6150 rupees. This includes a tracker who joins the jeep at the ticket office. Ours was called Kapila, and his knowledge especially of the different birds was impressive. Avoid the toilets if you can!!

Title: Absolutely spectacular!
Text: Serene. Calm. Plenty of birds to see and hear. They provide a guide who knows them all by name! Well worth a visit if you are a bird lover.

Title: Lovely Bird Sanctuary
Text: We took an afternoon safari to Bundala. We only saw 2 other vehicles & had a very relaxed & interesting trip. We saw a large variety of lovely birds, also crocodiles & elephants. Our guide was Nissanka & we also had a tracker, both were excellent at sporting the wildlife.

Title: Wonderful for birds
Text: A great place if youre into birds. Arriving early, we saw kingfisher, heron, Indian roller, jungle hen and more before entering the park proper. In the park, there are birds at every turn, from bee eaters to pelicans to birds of prey. Im not a birdcwatcher, but this was probably my favourite of the 4 parks I visited in Sri Lanka

Title: Afternoon Bird Watching
Text: Had a nice afternoon in the Bundala National Park. Three hours in the park is enough to get around. We spotted lots of birds, mongoose, crocodile, Elephants, monkeys, rabbits, iguana, Monitor lizards. Great guides not sure how they spotted some of the animals but every credit to them.  Even if your not a bird watcher well worth a trip just for the scenery.

Title: Nice Parc, good ranger
Text:
The Bundala is a very nice and around this time at least also a quiet Parc. You can see lots of animals here and explore the Sri Lankan wetlands.
Our guide there was Srimal. He was great with spotting animals and very knowledgeable. So all in all a great guide to have with you.

Title: What a day
Text:
After visiting section 5 in yarla the day before hopes where high ranjan our driver had arranged everything he did not disapoint just on the drive up to the office 13 new birds for list .ranjan acted as spotter translator we never miss a think elephants crocs 8 feet plus even some underwater birds just kept coming .no leapard but sloth bear great bonus and tje total bird spotted 112 for day 5 eagles,3 storks.
Thanks to ranjan for a great two days

Title: More monkeys than birds
Text: Best time to visit this place either first thing in the morning or after 3pm, recommend to take a guide to this place as you will see different types of birds, doesnt need a safari jeep as roads are not bad to drive on a normal vehicle but you are not allowed to get down at anytime, you can see lots of my monkeys than birds, if you are lucky you may also see some crocodiles and elephants.

Title: Stunning half day tour to watch birds
Text:
This park is beautiful and quiet. We saw another 5 jeeps the entire morning. We didn't visit Yala as we're really put off by the reviews of the number of jeeps. 

We saw so many birds, wild boar, monkeys, mongoose and wild deer. Would highly recommended. 

We used Ceylon Tours and they were fantastic.

Title: Better than Yala
Text:
In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka.
We visited Bundala National Park with a jeep and driver/"guide", and found that it is
A) much closer to Tissamaharama than Yala (the teenagers could sleep 20 minutes longer..)
B) the roads in the park are much better (so less bumping in the jeep compared to Yala)
C) there were only 2 jeeps at the entrance at 06:00, so much more quiet and we could enjoy the animals better without distrubance. At the entrance of Yala were about 60 jeeps.
D) small park: 4 hours is enough (but our driver/guide left already after 2 hours.
E) last but not least: we saw a lot of animals, besides birds a group of elephants and some lone bull, a group of crocodiles and a lot of deer (at Yala we saw birds, a couple of crocodiles and for 5 seconds a bear)

Title: Very quiet - but out of season
Text:
We went here very much out of season (but still quite a lot of birdlife!). It was exceptionally quiet (only 2 jeeps in the park) which meant it was slightly odd visiting - but we got to see quite a few birds, mongoose, the remains of a porcupine (the guide thought it was probably killed by dogs). We also - inexplicably - came upon a ginger domestic cat near the shore...... hopefully they will catch and re-home it.
Slightly odd going out of season (a bit unfair to criticise the place for not having much birdlife!), but an interesting place that will have flocks of birders in high season.

Title: Comfortable Jeep - Great adventure.
Text: I booked this trip from Unawatuna with Vision Lanka Tours and was very impressed. The jeep we picked up in Tissa was superb with high seats for perfect viewing. We arrived in Tissa at 2 pm in time for lunch before setting off to the Park at 2.30 pm. We saw 44 bird species in the afternoon along with crocodiles, monitor lizards, elephants and a single individual deer. White-bellied Sea Eagles should be seen and lots of large water birds such as Painted Stork, Spoonbill, Ibis, Egrets and Herons. Even if you don't see very much the journey itself into the bush is very memorable.

Title: Small park, max 3hours needed
Text: This is not a big park.  The most interesting part of our visit was seeing a male elephant doing his number 1 and 2 and spraying himself in a close distance to our Jeep.  We probably spent 30 mins on him.  The rest of the park has some colorful birds, but small kind and most were viewed in distance.  There are a lot of water buffalos, crocodiles, monkeys and peacocks.  We drove by a hilltop to have a nice lookout of the coast which was beautiful.  All in all, if you are not interested in birds, you can skip the park. We paid 70 usd for our private jeep with a park ranger and a driver.   Ask your private driver to arrange the tour to save money.  These tours are like commodity, all the same.

Title: Bird paradise
Text: A paradise for birdwatching! We went in the morning (started at 5 am from the hotel) and could catch the period when all waterbirds are feeding on fish. Contrary to Yala, it is a very calm place; we only occasionally met with other jeeps. We had enough time to observe and photograph all the birds, enjoy the view of the wonderful landscape. The ocean is also wonderful here. We could see an elephant calmly walking next to our jeep. There were hundreds of monkeys and peacocks. Our fantastic guide recommended us an experienced jeep driver, who knew the English name of all the birds. Most interesting species included Lesser Adjutant, Indian Darter, Painted Stork, Green and Blue-tailed Bee-eater, Pied Kingfisher, Purple Coot, Great Thick-knee, Great Coucal, Open-billed Stork, Whistling Duck, Pheasant-tailed Jackana, Sri Lanka Junglefowl, Glossy Ibis and Black-headed Ibis. There were many birds which are wintering there, e.g. Egrets, Spoonbills, Herons and Ducks.

Title: Stunning safari
Text:
We spent 3 hours in Bundala, it was amazing ! We saw elephants, crocodiles and many beautiful birds. At the sunset, landscapes are wonderful. 
We made a safari with Khsrimal, a very nice guy, very friendly. Don't hesitate to contact him, he is the best ! Khsrimal@yahoo.com and 0094779599397.

Title: Tranquil nature reserve
Text: After visiting Yala Game Park we wanted something different. Bundala National Park ticked all the boxes. We hired a jeep in Tissa for 3hrs for 6000 SLK on the understanding a tip would be forthcoming if we had a good time. We paid at the entrance, including the drivers fee and picked up a guide who proved very helpful. Bundala does not have the amount of game that Yala does, and is mainly a bird reserve, and they are beautiful. There are a lot of lagoons and wetlands teeming with life. As well as the birds we saw deer, crocodiles, mongoose, tortoises and monitors. We were able to turn the engine off and enjoy the serenity of the place as we did not see another jeep during our whole visit. The paths were smoother than Yala. When we exited the park we met two bull elephants on the road in two different places. Amazing.

Title: Lovely morning safari
Text: My friends and I stayed at the Lagoon Inn and arranged a safari with Srimal whose number we got from TripAdvisor reviews left previously. Srimal recommended we do an afternoon safari so we would see elephants but unfortunately our itinerary didn't allow this. Early start at 6am meant a quiet trip and watching the sun rise - a peaceful way to see plenty of bird species, monkeys, crocodiles and a land monitor. No elephants seen (as expected) but really enjoyed the trip nevertheless - Srimal was knowledgeable about the birds which was great.

Title: Bundalla
Text: Today we had another safari with Ceylon Safari Tours but this time we were off to Bundala with Chamara again. We had the same prompt pick up in the jeep just for the two of us. After Yala yesterday's Safari which is manic with many vehicles. Bundala  is the total opposite with only a few vehicles a day and the whole tour taken at a more leisurely pace. Another bonus is that you also get a park ranger to accompany you within the jeep and his name was Randika which means we had two experienced knowledgeable guides spotting the beautiful birds. We had a wonderful experience and spotted many birds and a couple of wild animals (elephants and crocodiles). The tour included a picnic spot in an absolutely beautiful spot on the coastline before we carried on with the tour. A wonderful trip made special with Chamara and Randika , many thanks to them both for a highly recommendable trip.

Title: 'Wetland Safari'
Text: Trip in jeep to the park (arranged quickly and easily by the Lagoon Inn +94(0)716310173) Saw loads of wildlife including close-up elephants, crocodiles, monkeys and huge variety of birds. The guide spoke excellent English, was very knowledgeable and frequently stopped the vehicle so we could have good look at everything, and only continued when we were ready to move onat a pace that suited us. We went on an afternoon trip which lasted til sunset when the park closed, which was a good time as birds/animals getting ready to roost/gather for drinking/night. Can highly recommend this trip.  Also as it's based right by the park at the Lagoon Inn, don't have to spend lot of time travelling to and from the park.

Title: Good for early morning tours
Text: a lot of birds, less bigger animals compared to Yala. However nice beach side and lagunes. So I liked it.

Title: Wonderful natural environment
Text:
We were initially unsure as to whether to do this safari or not, as there had been quite a lot of rain during the day. At around 2pm we decided to go for it, and took the afternoon safari run by our hotel, the Coconut Garden Hotel & Restaurant. The cost of the safari was 11500 LRP, all-inclusive for 2 people. We had the jeep to ourselves.

The drive from our hotel to Bundala National Park was pleasant and we stopped several times to view birds and monkeys. The park itself is quite small in comparison to Yala National Park. The procedure of getting into the park was much smoother than at Yala National Park as there was only one other jeep waiting with us to get into the park.

During our entire two hours of Safari at the park, we saw just one other jeep in the park. As a result we found the animals to be far less acclimatised to safari jeeps and to be more relaxed and wild in their behaviour.

While we were at the park, we saw lots of peacocks one displaying his tail feathers to a group of females; two male elephants - the first 10 to 15 years old, eating vegetation by the side of the lake; the second around 30 to 40 years old having a drink at a waterhole, then covering himself with mud, before heading back into the forest. We also saw several jungle fowl, lots of blue-tailed bee-eaters, many painted storks, Indian darters, many egrets & cormorants, many red-billed lapwings, Ibis, open-billed Ibis, storks, fishing eagles & a large sea eagle in flight and several green parrots. There were also many water buffalo, several medium sized crocodiles basking beside waterholes, and many monkeys, both Macaques and the black-faced variety. Even the monkeys seemed far less stressed at this national park than the ones we have previously encountered throughout Sri Lanka. There were many tiny monkey babies, some only just a couple of days old.

Other animals we saw included several mongoose including a large and rare king mongoose, which we were told, is rarely seen. There were many land monitors, including a large one, sleeping high up on a tree branch. On the way out of the park, we spotted a large hare sitting by a waterhole.

We stopped at a lovely vantage point on a cliff-top to view the rocks below with large waves crashing against them. From there we could see a lovely beach below with fishermen shacks and fishing vessels waiting to go to sea. We also saw a large sea turtle coming up to breathe down below.

One the way back from the national park, we stopped to see the fruit bats rousing from their sleep for their nightly feed. The on these same trees, many of the other birds after a day of foraging, were coming to roost for the night.

Finally, if you wish to see birds and other animals in a truly wild and natural environment, without all of the thousands of jeeps that fight for vantage point in Yala; then this is the national park for you.

Title: The beauty of tranquility
Text: Wow - an early morning safari at Bundala was such an unexpected treat. It is so beautiful and so tranquil and if you love the beauty of birds it's heaven. We saw so many species .. we had a guide too, who could spot so many more. It's much calmer than Yala but equal in splendour. Elephants wander, and the crocs lurk and the birds gather. You also get to stop at the seas edge, with its blue clear water and incredible red sand, if you're lucky there are fisherman and of course the amazing fish eagle (if you're lucky, and we were). It has a very different feel to Yala, much more gentle and less touristy which makes for a superb experience..

Title: A fantastic morning's birding
Text: I wasn't sure if this park would add much to what Yala offers, but it really did.  If you are a birder, definitely spend a morning here.  The key finds for me here were yellow bittern (very common), black bittern (2 seen), watercock, pacific golden plover and glossy ibis.  There was also a wide selection of waders, terns, etc and also a turtle seen close to the beach.  The pace is slower than Yala and the guides are quite good.

Title: Forget Yala- go here!
Text: Beautiful national park! We had 3 hours here and it was such a special experience, we spent a full day in Yala the next day and it was nowhere near as good and was jam-packed. Must see

Title: Amazing Safari Experience
Text:
Our guide Srimal gave us a fantastic tour through Bundala National Park. 
We spontaneously arranged the tour with him, since our hostel did not really offer tours to Bundala (and we definitely wanted to go to Bundala instead of the apparently over crowded Yala National Park) - and it was the best choice we could have made. Srimal is such an openminded and friendly person. He knew all the good spots and took his time to show us around. It was so relaxed and nice to drive around with him. He could explain a lot about the wildlife and did not speed from one spot to the next. Thanks to him, we saw four elephants from up close and also many peacocks, crocodiles, buffalos, turtles, and many many birds. We highly recommend him as a guide and thank him for this absolutely beautiful and exciting day. His contacts details are Khsrimal@yahoo.com and 0094779599397.

Title: Great fot Bird life
Text:
This reserve is predominantly bird life, the wet lands allow plenty of opportunities to view.

The park is not busy so plenty of time to see the birdlife, which is to numerous  to mention.

Well worth a visit, especially after Yala, which is overcrowded with Jeeps.

Title: Must visit
Text:
It was a fantastic safari.. Plenty of birds for bird watcher,few migratory birds,deer's,lot of peacocks.
Elephant,tortoises were there.
Worth a visit.
Must  for a photography enthusiasts

Title: Incredible!!
Text:
We cam on early morning there, and were lucky.
We saw wild elephant, leopard, bear, bore, crocodiles, dear, ...
All in only just two hours. 
What a natural park!

Title: Beautiful Quiet Park with Excellent Bird Watching
Text:
My partner and I have had our share of safari experiences in the Motherland and so decided to go to Bundala instead of Yala. For us this was the right decision. We later realized that we had avoided the masses at Yala and basically felt like we were in the park alone. We drove up looking for a guide and found Shrimal on the spot. He was friendly and quite knowledgeable about the birds who have migrated to the park. We recommend a ride with him (contact info: email - khsrimal@yahoo.com mobile/whatsapp -  0094779599397). 

Just some advice: If you also would like to see elephants best time is in the early afternoon when the weather is cooler.

Title: Amazing Bundala
Text: Even if you're not into bird watching it's well worth doing a half day safari in Bundala simply to have a relaxing drive through what is a beautiful wetland park. We were lucky and had elephants cross one of the lakes and walk right in front of our jeep. We also stopped to eat our breakfast looking down at the beach, which was simply stunning. We briefly saw three other jeeps but other than that it felt like we had the park to ourselves. Srimal was our driver/guide and did a good job of pointing out the various birds and animals to us, and expertly kept a close but safe distance from the elephants as they came towards our jeep. Khsrimal@yahoo.com, 0779599397.

Title: Beautiful Bird Watching with Guide Shrimal
Text: Wow.. what a beautiful National Park with so many species and timing was right for me in December 1st week. Went with Shrimal a local guide . He came to Hotel to pick me up sharp on time 5.30 AM and drove straight to Bundala in the high raised Jeep Safari. Very knowledgeable about the park and I had my own target species and managed to see 68 species out of which 22 are Lifers to me. Being from a foreign country without a local cellphone but managed to hook up with this guide in whatsapp and all deals done previous night and he did a great job for the money we paid. I strongly recommend Shrimal incase you need a guide . His email Khsrimal@yahoo.com ( Mobile 0094779599397 ) ..

Title: Jeep Safari
Text:
Yesterday we did the Jeepsafari at Bundala national Park.
We came there by bus. The bus stops in front of the entry of the national Park, when you tell the bus driver. The way from there is arround 6 km. At the busstop there was already drivers waiting for the tour, so we could go to the park with them. We went with Chaminda. 

Chaminda weerasooroya
94713095115
Bundala jeep safari

He was a really nice driver and his jeep was comfortable. The entry was 5160 Rs for two of us plus the jeep and guid for 5000 Rs.

We saw a lot of animals in the park - A lot af beautiful birds - the guid knewd all names of the birds, crocodiles, elephant, and a lot of monkeys.
So we really liked and enjoyed it.
Chaminda had a good camera with and sent us nice pictures he took of us.
Thanks Chaminda for the nice tour:)

Title: Wonderful Wildlife
Text: A great tour with wonderful wildlife, Birds, Monkeys, Crocodiles, Buffalo, Deer, Boar and much more. The bird watching in particular was superb.

Title: Great visit to beautiful Bundala
Text: We visited Bundala national park from Tangalla. Srimal safari helped us reaching the place by bus. We did the afternoon tour with him and we have seen plenty of birds, monkeys, crocodiles etc... beatifull! I recommend it. I leave here the contact of Srimal, an excellent guide: +94779599397, khsrimal@yahoo.it

Title: A very pleasant and quiet park with amazing lagoons
Text: Beautiful bird life and both fresh water and salt water crocodiles. The high point for me was the layout of the park with many lagoons where we could drive through. And the stillness of the place with many peacocks all around -  either majestically perched on trees or dancing in the forest - a lovely sight indeed! You must take a guide (available at no extra cost) along with the jeep who has good knowledge of the park and can speak English as the experience is enhanced by the knowledge shared by him. Serious or even amateur birders should carry a bird book.

Title: Crocodiles in salt water lagoons, Eagles, Peacocks, trip ending by the Sea.
Text: It was a lovely experience. We took the early morning trip and could identify about 35 species of birds ranging from painted storks, darters, ibis, bee eaters to eagles, spoonbill and dancing peacocks. Unfortunately, the migratory flamingos hadn't come into the park yet. The park is quite extensive with lagoons and the highlights for us were getting to watch sea water crocodiles (muggers) at close quarters and ending the trip by the sea. You get an experienced tracker alongwith your entry ticket (ask for one).

Title: Great for birds - go early!
Text: Were recommended to go to Bundula as the best place to see birds at this time of the year (early December) as some of the parks further West had suffered from recent bad weather and numbers were low. Its worth checking with the park authorities on this before you set of on the visits we discovered! We travelled over from Galle (took 3 hours and we stayed at hotel nearby). Went into park at 6 in morning - excellent numbers of species. We specifically requested a good bird guide after previous experience at Uda Walawa where if it ain't an Elephant or a Peacock most birds are surprisingly 'pigeons'! Anyway the guide was excellent, as was the driver and we had an very good 3+ hours for an overall cost of about £40. The driver also took is around some of the lakes outside the park, which was a bonus - tip required!

Title: Surprisingly good
Text: After a visit to Yala Park the previous day where we saw plenty of animals... and even more humans and jeeps we went for a morning safari in Bundala. This is a wetland area full of birds. I suspect I'm like many in that a few feathered creatures don't excite as much as the prospect of a leopard or a herd of giant elephants but I was glad to be proved wrong. The sheer number of birds is amazing, both in their density and diversity and this differs from Yala as you see one creature after another rather driving through the bush to get to one animal. Watching the Peacocks fly was special. There's more than birds though with the usual monkeys, mongoose and some very large crocodiles. It was also very quiet, we only saw two other vehicles in the park the whole time.

Title: Bundada for birds and best on a morning visit
Text:
We arrived just as the sun came up and were there for the birds. For hardcore birders, this site gave us a lot of the species that we knew we may miss - our list here included Watercock, Pacific Golden Plover, Greater Thick-knee, Indian Thick-knee, Yellow-Wattled Plover, Jerdon's Bushlark and Bar.d-button Quail.

It's much better to go in the morning. When checking the salt pans it's best to drive the length then check birds as you drive back, so avoiding viewing in to the sun at this time of year.

There are toilets at the entrance - but NOT once in the park.

Title: Amazing trip in Bundala
Text:
We did both Bundala and Yala and we both agreed that we much preferred the Bundala safari. It was much less crowded and the views and animals we spotted were very similar 

We were very lucky to see 3 elephants and plenty of other animals but that was mainly down to the experience of our guide Prasanna from Araliya tours, who I'd recommend 100%!

Also the total pricing seems a bit confusing on all the sites but a good private jeep and driver should cost 6000 rupees and entrance to the park is about 2600 rupees per person, including your driver

Title: Really nice afternoon
Text: We went there to avoid the crowded yala National Park. And we were not disappointed . Its mainly birds (so it makes it not as sensational for some people) but the atmosphere in the park was really special - with no one around (we saw 2 cars in the 5 hors we spent there) - you just have the sound of birds and monkeys. It was nice to see a family of elephants , with their babies, near the lagoon and we spotted crocodiles, eagles and peacocks, it was one of the highlight of our trip !

Title: Birds Birds Birds
Text:
A very knowledgeable guide ,Damit made our trip to Bundala worthwhile 
Saw 37 species mostly shorebirds and a few huge crocodiles

Title: Birds and Elephants!
Text:
We went to Bundala because the drivers at Yala were on strike, but we feel like it was better touring Bundala. 
We got an early start with a driver with a 4-wheel drive jeep and watched the sunrise as we got to the park. We were joined by a park ranger and were off on our adventure. We saw a wide variety of birds which the ranger identified for us. Then we saw  nine elephants, uncountable monkeys, a few mongoose, four jackals, lots of crocodiles and a 4-5 foot python. 
We felt as if we had the park to ourselves and were able to spend as long as we wanted watching the animals.
Near the end, we drove over a sand dune to see the ocean. It was a gorgeous location and we took a break there.
We had a great time watching animals and our driver helped us take some up close pictures.

Title: Solo
Text: This park was the alternative to Yala due to the Jeep drivers strike. Ok if you like birds but no leopards, bears and only one elephant. Plus we had a park guide that was not very knowledgeable and was difficult to understand. Save your money if Yala is still closed.

Title: Beautiful, Natural Park - Salt Water Crocodiles, Wild Monkeys & Birds
Text:
Yala was closed for our supposed-Safari due to strike of Safari Jeepney owners. We were looking for good options so as not to waste our time staying in Tissahamarama. Our villa host (who happened to be a local tribe from Yala) called up his driver and asked if he can bring us to Bundala.
We woke up around 450am and our driver arrived exactly 0500am. With our packed breakfast, we went through Bundala.
We saw the following : salt lake (where salt are produced / grow), different kinds of birds, a bull elephant (at a far sight), wild boar, spotted deers, wild cows, water buffalo, tortoise, parrots, and crocodiles. Had to watch crocodile fight which was really great.
Would recommend this to people who are not afraid to watch crocodiles and love monkeys.

Title: Croc's & Elephants
Text: Bundala National Park is a great place to see Elephants and Crocodiles. Also have good camping sites. As this park has a long beach you may get a chance of seeing and Elephants on the beach. We had a late evening bath at the canal next to our  camping site and while we having bath crocodiles swam away It was a lucky escape and never recommend this to anybody

Title: Great Safari with srimal
Text: As recommended by many on here I used Srimal for my safari- he was really knowledgeable about the birds and animals and was helpful at suggestions as to how to get to bundala. We were going to use a taxi from tangalle and srimal knew that (and I dare say could have made a bit by organising that for us) but he suggested we got the bus and told us which bus to get etc which was of course very cheap and probably took not much longer at all. Tour was really good - we saw lots of animals including elephants and crocodiles and loads of birds. Also the scenery itself is beautiful regardless of what animals you see. I would definitely recommend Srimal for this tour. He provided binoculars and the jeep was comfy.

Title: Not for the young
Text: We visited hear whilst on a 4 night stay in Sri Lanka, whilst the park was beautiful with lots of animals to see and the jeep comfortable, I think it was too much for our two young children it was a good two hour tour with 15 minutes travelling time to and from the national park. By the end of which both had become tired, hot and miserable. So whist I would highly recommend I would say the minimum age for children would be 5 if not slightly older to appreciate it fully.

Title: Birdwatching, but also many animals.
Text:
We were there 6am, and there were nearly no other cars. Lots of birds, but we also met elephants, crocodile, mungoes, deer, water buffaloes, water monitor and monkeys.
I liked this place better than Yala, because it was less others. We could stop and take photos without thinking of the cars behind, and I felt we got closer to the animals.

Title: Wonderful bird park
Text:
A brilliant park, far less packed than the nearby wildlife safari parks.
You need a knowledgeable guide, a pair of binoculars and a camera, then just enjoy a couple of hours seeing the wonders of nature.
Breathtaking

Title: Simply Amazing!
Text:
The Lake View Cottage in Tissa (review to follow) organised my half day safari starting at 5.30am. I was the only person going and although I had read that it was quieter than Yala, what I didn't expect was to have the park more less to myself (with driver) until another jeep arrived about an hour later. Only 2 jeeps there all morning.
I am a complete bird watching novice spurred on by a recent visit to Thailand and by watching the birds in my garden. Although my guide lacked English speaking skills, he certainly made up for it with his wild-life knowledge to the extent that I sometimes couldn't keep up with what he pointing out to me. A wonderful experience and I was more than happy with the half day visit. Be prepared to be jostled about as the roads in the park are not maintained in any way.

Title: Highly Recommend!
Text:
We booked Srimal for a Bundala NP tour & were very happy with our choice. He is a very friendly guy who grew up near this park and so has great knowledge of all the birds and animals we saw. Currently he is studying the names of the birds in German so seems to go that extra mile to help all tourists.

We really liked that srimal sat in the back of the truck with us. He has an excellent eye for nature spotting and this allowed us to chat & ask questions as needed. The morning is best at the park for birds, the afternoon for animals. However we were there in the afternoon & saw plenty of birds. We even had the thrill of a male elephant chase our jeep! 

As we were so happy with our experience we also booked him for Yala NP the following day. He is a very relaxed guy sitting in back of jeep as you enter the park as tour also includes a driver. We really liked this & noticed in other jeeps there was just 1 person as a driver/guide, therefore concentrating on the roads which in Yala NP are terrible.

In our experience of Yala, there are so many companies out there which can make a very confusing and impersonal experience. We found ALL jeeps to be of similar quality, despite other companies being more expensive. Also there are no government or tourist board companies running safaris, and we did not see any exceptionally eco friendly tours, all this info is just sales tactics. 

Overall, we recommend a tour with Srimal who is a very relaxed and trustworthy guy. He can be contacted via :

Khsrimal@yahoo. com

Mobile number 0094779599397

Facebook - Bundala safari Srimal

Title: Superb birds, peaceful, pretty
Text: After the chaos and poor behaviour of Yala NP, we visited Bundala the next morning.  Stretched along the coast to the West of Yala, it lies between the sea and lagoons.  It is a beautiful small park and very peaceful, with a small number of visitors compared to Yala.  The bird life was outstanding and it was possible to approach the birds in a vehicle to quite close quarters, giving great viewing and photographs.  There are also many smaller mammals, the monkeys being the most entertaining to watch.  In the South, the views along the sea coast are also lovely.  Highly recommended for bird lovers.

Title: Hidden Gem
Text: Bundala National Park is lesser known that Yala but offers a great safari opportunity. Although there are some elephants, Bundala's main attraction is the bird life with over 400 species in the park

Title: Quieter than Yala and well worth the visit
Text:
This is an old established National Park like Yala but has fewer visitors. The NP provides a guide for each Jeep who are well trained and knowledgeable. It is a wetlands park with a very wide range of migratory birds and at the right time of year Flamingoes. No Leopards (which you may see at Yala from a great distance with a 100 other jeeps) but elephants, monkeys, boars etc.
So may be a morning safari in Yala and afternoon safari in Bundala is the best balance

Title: Mecca for birdwatching
Text: This place was paradise- an optional trip on my tour I paid for up front - but so glad I did - it's an early start to catch the birds but what birds - I saw over forty types whilst there from kingfisher to fish eagle plus buffalo,crocs and other animals but this park is primarily known for its birds. The highlight of my trip without a doubt.

Title: Picturesque... Scenic... Try to go there.
Text:
We went there in Dec 2016. We went to Yala the morning before, and decided to visit Bundala the following morning. As we were staying at Cinnamon Yala (which is very close to Yala), the jeep ride is about 45 mins to Bundala.

This is a very different park to Yala. This looks much more scenic and this is a bird paradise. You might see Elephants here (we didn't) but the main attraction here is Birds and the park landscape itself. As most people (like us) are not much knowledgeable about the birds, it's better to have a good guide (or knowledgeable Jeep driver/guide). We had 2 keeps and both the drivers were excellent (through Shehan Jeep Safari), and an official guide also joined us at the park entrance. Our driver had a Birds of Srilanka book with us and he gave us very good commentary and showed the details of the birds in the book. That way, we had a much present and more educational experience than simply looking at the birds. 

We had our morning tea break (you need to bring your own snacks) at the sand dune area which is on top of the cliff overlooking the beach). You can see turtles in the water (if you can spot them). 

Overall, I would highly recommend the visitors to this area to visit Bundala park.

Title: Excelent for birds, guide Srimal is the best
Text:
We went to Bundala park with our guide Srimal which we found on Trip advisor comments. His contact: khsrimal@yahoo.com +94779599397.

We contacted him on short notice and amidiately arrange everything. He showed us a lot of birds (he know the names, which I can say for many SL guides), crocodilles, mangoose, varans, apes etc. Really recomend to go to the park with Srimal if you are planning to go. Compering with other jeeps visiting at the same time, we event went on some other roads to be alone and better observe birds. "programe" in the park is similar with all the companies, so its really worth to have a good guide. You dont need fancy companies with serving coffe on this 4 hour tour, you need to gain knowledge, experience and of course to see as much as possible. With Srimal this is what we get! As we are dragonflies enthusiast after the tour he took us for longer time to some nearby lake and around a village where we observed even more (free of charge), so he really puts an effort in costumer service. You can see his a young independant guy.

I suggest you go in early morning, starting at 6.

Title: Safari
Text: We had book just Yala and paid a hefty price prior to arrival , We met Srimal here 0779599397 Khsrimal@yahoo.com who offered a much more of an competitive price with local knowledge ! We visited three parks on Srimal's advice and saw a massive range of animals from a Water snake to Elephants! We also got to see the elusive Leopard, that was in Yala. I would fully recommend him as he was very reliable and flexible and even found a ratchet strap to hold my Three year old nieces car seat !

Title: Beautiful small wetland reserve
Text: Great for bird watching, crocodiles, a few elephants. Major plus point, not many safaris, feels much more relaxed and natural than Yala.

Title: Very good
Text: We chose to do Bundala instead of Yala or Udawalawe due to it being quieter, we didn't want loads of other jeeps and tourists disrupting the experience. Apparently Yala is notorious for loads and loads of jeeps/tourists. We really enjoyed Bundala. It's a bird watchers haven and along with birds you get to see monkeys, peacocks, wild boar, a couple of elephants, alligators, snakes, mongoose, cows, eagles and plenty of other animals! It really was a fantastic experience. We only saw 5 other jeeps all day. I think a half day tour would be enough (5-6 hours or so.) We did a full day and felt like we did a bit of backtracking. We saw loads of animals within the first few hours and then it seemed to dry up as the day went on. Loads of hotels do packages where the jeep will pick you up, give you breakfast and lunch, do the tour and then drop you back at the hotel. To give you an estimate I paid 9000 rupees per person. Would highly recommend if you want a quiet, more intimate experience.

Title: Birds!
Text: Bundala National Park is easily accessible from Tissa, so that if you are visitng the Yala National Park and staying in Tissa, you should plan on visiting Bundala Park also.  This park is very different from Yala, in terms of flora and fauna: Bundala is a network of waterways and pools teeming with birds, but you wont see large mammals here.  The park is fairly small, a half day safari is all youll need.

Title: A physical challenge!
Text: We arrived early (circa 6am) for a walk. 4 1/2 hours later our group had completed to walk via Worlds End and including both waterfalls. Toilets on route were a bonus. However conditions were extremely challenging in parts and 22000 steps later many of us were exhausted. We were advised not to take plastics into the National Park so were without water which was a mistake. DO take water with you. Lovely scenery although most of the walk/climb you look down to check your feet placing.

Title: Fantastic scenery
Text: A great mornings hike in the park , the terrain can get slippy and challenging with high steps but shouldnt worry any person is in reasonable shape and take your time . A couple of toilets along the route but not a western standard so be prepared . Bring plenty of water and start early , Worlds end is a great stopping point with awesome views , lots of wildlife to be on the look out for.

Title: Beautiful hike through the misty terrains
Text:
We started our hike through Horton Plains early in the morning to catch a sunrise over the misty hills and terrains. What can I say, it was definitely worth waking up so early. We saw plenty of deers eating fresh grass even before we entered the main gate of the park, and then had an enjoyable walk along the route towards Baker's Falls. 

There are two options: you can start with the Falls and finish by the Little World's End or vice versa. We chose the first option and did not regret it. After we saw the sunrise, the sun quickly disappeared behind the clouds and we did not see it much until we reached the falls and the skies became blue. We took wonderful photos and had our packed breakfast right there on a bench, which was so romantic and enjoyable.

When we continued our route towards the World's End, we realized how right we were in taking that path - we almost always hiked down rather than climbing up and it made our trekking way more comfortable and less tiring. The day before we hiked the Adam's Peak, so we could not feel our legs and feet after that and this path we chose turned out to be helpful :) 

Unfortunately, when we reached the World's End, a big cloud hung on top and covered all the view. We waited for 30 minutes and the situation remained the same. We still were pleased with the hike and the World's End because there was a certain mystery in this endless mist over the edge. You can literally feel you are on the edge of nowhere.

P.S. In my opinion, you won't need a guide to hike Horton Plains. It is super easy and it is impossible to get lost on the way. There is literally only one path and it is a round journey, so whatever way you choose - you will end up in the same place. Only if a lady is solo and scared of being attacked or something??? But generally, for me it seemed peaceful and safe. And if a leopard comes out from a bush, I don't think that having a guide will be helpful right??)))

Also the time you will spend there will be at least 4-5 hrs if you do not want to run along the whole route and wish to take nice pictures and just enjoy the nature around you. So don't listen to people who tell it is like a 3-hour hike. Maybe, if you don't complete the whole circle..)

Title: Great hike - hire a guide!
Text: Lovely hike with amazing views. Took us about 4 hours total while carrying our 9 month old baby in a sling. We saw fluffy purple bear monkeys, reptiles, deer and even signs of leopards. It was chilly so bring layers! Make sure you hire a proper guide with a 4 wheel drive or a van to take you up - we saw some hair raising scenes of small cars struggling to drive up the mountain. I would highly recommend hiring a guide for the hike - you don't need one but you will learn so much more about the local wildlife and see so much that would otherwise miss! Can highly recommend!

Title: Beautiful but Expensive!
Text: The National Park is beautiful however the entrance ticket is expensive at 3000rps per person (tourist price). Locals pay a whopping rate of 60rps p/p!! This price disparity made us feel slightly exploited! You will need to pay an additional fee of 2100rps for tax and 100rps for a paper pamphlet! The park seems to be badly managed in general and overpriced for what it is. If you have an abundance of time in Nuwara Eliya and feel like a hike in nature then this could be worth jt.

Title: Lovely  walk .
Text: However not for infirm walkers . Start early as its very hot in middle of day. Lovely views . Not always a good path a little bit of climbing over boulders.

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: Very Very rough terrain up to Mini World End then upwards to Worlds End viewing area over 2000m high views stunning. Then went onto Bakers Falls which is a large waterfall. 10k clambering scrambling sometime steep terrain. But if going need to set off when the gates open at 6am after that too hot and clouds roll in and obscure the views.Worth the effort

Title: Great trek to Worlds End
Text: Good to be able to walk in a National Park but very few wildlife apart from samba deer. Nice waterfall and a few steep climbs.

Title: Lovely Mother Nature!!!
Text:
This is a lovely trekking place with fresh air and beautiful scenery along the trekking paths. Some beautiful stops worth to check out are: 
1. Little Worlds End view point 
2. Great Worlds End view point 
3. Bakers Waterfalls 
We were so lucky to be able to see a wild Sambar Deer right in front of us up close before the starting point of the trek. Entrance fee is quite steep at LKR3,850 per person. Suggest to go early in the morning as we departed from our hotel at Nuwara Eliya at 5am. On the way up to Horton Plains, before reaching the ticket booth, we stopped at the roadside to watch the sunrise above the sea clouds. Horton Plains is a UNESCO World Heritage Site where is protected areas for its nature beauty. It is a plateau at 2100-2300 meters above sea level. Hence, be prepared for the warm clothing since it can be very chilly early in the morning. A complete route of hiking require at least half day time (4-5 hours depends on individual fitness level) and the trekking path is relatively easy for all age, but good walking shoes are necessary, plus adequate drinking water. Packing breakfast is advisable for people who do morning trek. Tight security check of the bag/ haversack at the entrance of trekking and no plastics allowed at the park. We were so glad that we did morning trek as the weather was cool and pleasant and completed our trek slightly before noon. Hence, most people do morning trek and be there early as there will be long queue for security check. An afternoon trekking would be warm and sweaty due to warmer weather in the day. We simply love this place and the beauty of Mother Nature!!!

Title: Ok but......
Text: The world's end was an anti climax. We were sold the story it was an awe inspiring site, and sight,  perhaps it is if you haven't traveled anywhere else. The park does show the diversity of the terrain and is a nice 10km walk but it is not for anyone seeking diversity of wildlife. It was disappointing to see the disrespect of some tourists who could not control their bodily needs until they reached the toilets provided. Perhaps more guides walking along the tracks or more signs showing where the toilets are may help ?

Title: Fantastic place
Text: After witnessing the litter problem in Sri Lanka it was very pleasant to visit such a clean litter free environment. Bags were searched on entry to make sure you weren't carrying any possible litter. The whole trek was very well marked and gave lots of opportunities for sight seeing.

Title: Just dont
Text:
We were searched bottom to top upon entry of the park to avoid any plastics, tobacco, lighters etc to enter the park, despite being nature respecting people ourselves.
After entry, we saw groups of locals carrying gas bottles and tents around a random place they decided to camp inside the park. While we were robbed of our breakfast, they were cooking it in the park, while washing their hair and brushing their teeth in the river. 
The park is expensive (3500 rupees per person) for two viewpoints and a meagre waterfall. 
On top, we saw quite some wildlife, but all on the outside of the park. 
Theres no need to pay this fee, be searched and go through the hassle. The views, the ecosystem can be better just outside of the park.

Title: Interesting but not spectacular
Text: Not quite as spectacular as Id been led to believe. We got there early and it was cold , need to wrap up, and the cafe was not open so no breakfast option available. Nice enough walk and views, spent about three hours going to Mini Worlds End, Worlds End and Bakers Falls.

Title: Well worth it .. but be prepared
Text: We left our hotel at 5:30 AM to get there in time to see Worlds end before the mist comes in.  It is cold at this time but it gets warm quickly so dress in layers.  The trek is long (9 km) and the walking challenging at times (lots of rocks and roots to watch for) but it was worth it to see the view.  But be aware that the trail is a loop and that it requires some degree of fitness

Title: Worth the early start
Text: So good to see this beautiful natural habitat kept in pristine condition. Many thanks to all those involved.

Title: Ancient landscape
Text: An unusual place to find on a tropical island. It rains a lot so pack sensibly and wear descent gripping footwear as the path down the circuit is difficult. The trees and fauna are lovely. You will recognise a few in your garden. The waterfall is beautiful and worth the detour down the hill. We had low visibility as in the clouds even at 6.00am so not such good views. Well worth a visit.

Title: Beautiful worthwhile visit
Text:
This was a beautiful place to walk in, especially if you starting the cooler part of the day as it really gets hot from midmorning onwards. The terrain is quite difficult in sections. One needs considerable concentration and good balance not to twist an ankle. It requires a moderate level of fitness and good footwear.
We were initially ambivalent regarding how dangerous some of the areas might be, but if people are sensible and do not attempt selfies near the edge, we could not see a problem. Take a hat and plenty of water, enjoy the walk.

Title: Unusual scenery
Text:
I had an sunny afternoon trek through this park, the scenery is not like what we call plains in the US but more interesting. The rhododendron trees weren't blooming but the shape of them was unusual , a mix of a bonsai and an acacia. I took the trek from the visitor center through hills and a waterfall and then you see lakes then you will run into bakers falls. I didn't go to lands end , a lady said it wasn't worth it and the scenery wasn't much different, so I passed.  

If you have 2 days in nuwiyra eliya,  visit here, but its about 30 miles away, but interesting scenery on the way to the park.

Title: Worth the effort.
Text:
We did the early start- here around 6.30am., and as it was part of our tour, we didn't pay for it individually. 
It's quite a hike here- smooth paths one minute, rocky paths the next. I found it a bit hard, especially as the air is quite thin from the altitude- we couldn't chew our sandwich and breathe easily at the same time!
But despite the effort we had to put in, it was SO worthwhile. 
Bakers Falls was lovely, and it wasn't crowded when we were there, so some lovely photos to take.
World's End and Mini World's End have the most stunning view- it really feels like you're on top of the world.
It's a real photo opportunity while hiking, so we really enjoyed it, despite the hard slog we had to put in!

Title: An amazing expensive experience
Text: The reservation is gorgeous don't  miss.  Entrance fee is $25!! 10 km walk through beautiful landscape

Title: Foreigners skip. Pretty but a rip off
Text:
My friend and I visited in January 2023. Overall, I would recommend choosing antoher of the many attractions in the hill country over Horton Plains.

Why go: it's a pretty and clean walk through a high-altitute plateau to a wide outlook down to the plains. We saw some deer in the open fields and interesting descriptions of the cloud forest. The walk is comparable in enjoyment to many temperate walks elsewhere. Easy to hire a return car trip from Nuwara Eliya (10,000 LKR). You can easily do the circular walk in 2-3hrw. Take sturdy shoes and a warm top layer. Start early: be at the park centre for 6:30am to get the best chance of the views before the clouds come in. If money is no question, then you will enjoy the park.

Why skip: regretfully the park management seem to have taken to an extortion racket. A single person ticket for a foreigner will cost you around USD40 with the ticket price and the 'service charge', and even more if you actually want to pay in dollars (the clerk at the entrance will happily exchange to rupees for a hefty fee). That's probably about 40 times the price for locals. That is absurdly expensive for Sri Lankan standards and it's very expensive for what you get by Western standards, as it is just an unguided walk through the nature.

Title: Hike Through Nature
Text:
Got there just after 6.30am. Had an amazing walk round the trail with some stunning views at World's End and Bakers Falls, pretty much had the whole thing to ourselves... Get there early, we finished just before 9.30am. on the way back down the road it was a constant stream of cars coming up to the trail, so  would imagine it's extremely busy the later you leave it.

Tips
Get there early
Wear comfortable walking shoes or trainers.
Take your time, and listen to nature on the way round. So many people are in such a hurry to go round, they miss the beauty of it all

Title: Hortons Plains is spectacular
Text:
Horton's Plains is an amazing walk taking you to Bakers Falls and Worlds End

Recommend getting there for 6AM and going right first to The Falls and thereby going anti clockwise. We did both before anyone else was there so had to ourselves. We saw spotted deer, falcon and other wildlife before the crowds arrived.

You cannot take single use plastics into the park, yet amazingly some local tourists managed to leave litter behind. Cost should have been $66USD but this magically got rounded up to $80. You can pay in rupees which I would recommend

Title: Horton Plains via Rickshaw
Text: I went early in the morning and was first at the gate at 6 am. The rickshaw ride in the dark from Nuwara Eliya took exactly an hour. And I walked the route without seeing anyone until just after Bakers Falls at the end. A magical hike. I was back in Nuwara Eliya at 10:30 am.

Title: Not so plain for a walk, walk and walk experience!!
Text:
Get ready for a walk, walk and walk for approximately 9.4 kms !! (Pheww)

Undoubtedly this hike will give you a beautiful experience of walking in sweat, clouds, mist, rain and breeze ! One can experience all of them in the total hike !
To consider for people who are not so adventurous and who prefer less walking. The plains may mislead you about the difficulty level !
There are levels of walking and they are easy, difficult and more difficult!!
And there are definitely the same the way they are listed. In the rains the rocks, the waking passage can be slippery making your hike really challenging. Till you reach bakers fall you will get an insight of your journey anyways !! One should be with very good quality hiking shoes with good grip which will be helpful while waking. Rain Coats, cap and some food stuffs are very important along with you. Remember to carry them in a paper bag as no plastics are allowed inside. They will remove the plastic covering of the water bottle too ( a good initiative though)
Do try to start your journey maximum by 7:30 am to see a clear view near the world end ( if you fortunate). Else the clouds will cover you well and give another experience for photography only ??
You will enjoy the named places called and mini worlds end and worlds end. They are the places where you can have a breathtaking views if there are no clouds.
Be very careful of the steep elevation of the worlds end while doing some photography.
This may take a minimum of 3 to 4 hours depending on the walking speed and time.
Apart from this: undoubtedly this will give an amazing feeling once you finally see the finish gate ??
# leaving your foot prints behind ??
# mythological: In the story, Hanuman set fire to Horton plains and that fire lasted for a long time. The original name, Maha Eliya Thenna carries the meaning, 'The hugely lighten ground'.
