Recommend good walking shoes or sandals. But nothing too bad if reasonable fitness.
Mini World's End was good but World's End was spectacular.  Getting there as early as possible seems to be better before it gets too misty.  Standing on the edge of a 4,000 ft vertical drop is not good for your vertigo!!!
The walk back via the Baker's Falls was also great.
In the end was a loop of about 9KMs.
Be aware that as you enter the walk they search your bags for any plastics and take them away from you.  For example we had a couple of water bottled with plastic labels and they cut off the labels before we were allowed to take them in.

Title: Proof of the Continental Drift Theory
Text:
It is a beautiful place, good for trekkers especially because you have to go walking long distances to view the park. Not advisable for small children, it is simply too tiring.

The Horton Plains are proof of the continental drift theory and the museum in the park has details on this. I found it very interesting.

Title: Excellent Walk
Text: We were picked up from our hotel at 5am and driven to the entrance of the National Park to begin our walk at sunrise.  It gets very busy especially on weekends, holidays etc. so go early to beat the crowds.  We walked the circuit to Bakers Fall first and then onto Worlds End and mini Worlds End.  Not a difficult 9kms but wear good walking shoes.  Worth the time as the scenery is beautiful.

Title: Nice tour but overpriced
Text: The landscape at Hortons Plains is really beatiful and different from what you see in  other parts of sri lanka. However the entrance fee is relatively high (we paid a bit above 7000 rupees for 2 persons and a shared van for up to 4 people costs you another 4000-5000 rupees) - a bit pricey for a 3 hours walk. We left nuwara eliya at 5:15 and arrived at the park entrance at 6:15, then we had to queue for tickets for around 30 min (better leave before 5 if you decide to go). We did little world's end first which was free of clouds, but wirlds end was already covered in clouds when we git there 8:30/8:45.  Try to not take any plastic  bags / Joghurts etc since there is a backpack check after the park entrance where you need to remove those anyhow.

Title: Horrific for 5 minutes late
Text: Horrible adventure which makes me dissapointed by this country on my last day of Sri Lanka... We wanted to go through there and visit it to go Nuwara Eliya, we arrived there at 4H05PM after 3hours of driving into the mountains, the staff didnt want us to go through cause it says Tickets counter close at 4pm but the park himself closes at 6pm !!! When you check on their website it says close at 6pm... After 45 min to ask them to understand our position that if they can not let us go we will have to drive 2h30 more hours to reach our arrival.. we were about 30 min to reach our destination from horton plains !! The girl in duty call her Officer, 7 people came for us and talk to us like if we were just a piece of s**** and tell us baddly and angry to move the hell from here !!! We were basicly begging them and they were using their power against us in a way I never experienced before. I am not the guy who  used to put bad reviews at all but this one needed to be known for everyone ! Make sure if you go nuwara eliya from Ella in car, that you take the right timing. Don't waste your time and money, the suroundings are much more nicer for free. The price fee is also super high for that short parc and foggy place.

Title: Very disappointing
Text: Dont bother. Ridiculous entrance fee (40 euro for two foreigners, of which only 60 roepen for our tuktuk driver) for an average walk in an avarage environment. When you go very early you have to walk in a crowd, when you go later in the morning the Sri lankans scare away every animal with their chatter.

Title: Nice stroll in the park
Text: Horton Plains with Worlds End is one of the "musts" when visiting Nuwara Eliya, and it´s worth the effort. Worlds End cliff is enchanting with the drop of +800 meters, but you have to be there before the mist sets in (before 9.00am.?) or else you will meet the white wall instead of the magnificent views.

Title: Well worth the early start
Text: We hadn't planned to head up to the Horton Plains before we got to Nuwara Eliya, but decided to on arrival and arranged an early pickup (5am) with our tuktuk driver.  Nuwara Eliya is cold at that time of day,and we were very grateful for our padded jackets - make sure you prep well for a cold morning!  The journey over in the dark was, well, interesting - low-lying mist on the unlit roads, speeding drivers trying to overtake at all opportunities (it is Sri Lanka after all!) and low powered tuktuk lights all made for a memorable trip!  After buying our entry tickets ($45 for two people including all fees and taxes) we headed up to the trail head as the sun was coming up, with a few scattered deer out on the plains - fairly magical!  The hike itself is a circular, so you can head either clockwise or anticlockwise - most guides say to go anticlockwise, as you reach Little World's End before World's End but we opted for the latter and didn't regret it at all - it's slightly easier as you get a flattish finish, and you also avoid most of the crowds - once we'd headed out the only people we saw for the first 4km or so were the quicker hikers heading past us (not sure why, this is the sort of place that deserves you take your time to soak in the atmosphere!)  The early start was a killer at 4.30am, but seemed like a great idea now - the light is beautiful at that time of day and there's still the early morning frost on the ground and low-lying mist in the valleys.  Baker Falls are nice (but no Iguazu!) and the views from World's End and it's little brother are great, but for me the real winner was the hike and the scenery - just magical at that time of day, and we felt at times we were no longer in Sri Lanka but maybe south America!  While we didn't see much wildlife on the outward part of the hike we saw quite a bit when heading back after Little World's End - a couple of giant squirrels and a few purple-faced leaf monkeys enjoying a feed in the early morning sun - plus quite a few birds.  The round trip is around 9km or so, but we took our time enjoying the journey.  Very highly recommended if you're in Nuwara Eliya - indeed, probably the best thing you can do here IMO!

Title: Nice walk early in the morning.
Text: This place is good to go early in the morning, then we saw the most animals and it was not so hot yet. I left with a group from the Laughing leopard Hostel in Nuwara Eliya. The only downside was that we had to wait on one of the slower walkers.

Title: One of the best things we've done in Sri Lanka!
Text:
Living here for two years I can't believe we have never done this before! It HAS TO be on your bucket list of you're outdoorsy, adventurous or just enjoy beauty in nature. 

We left Newara Eliya at 5am and paid and entered the park by 7am. The entire walk took us 3 hours and was stunning. You walk through so many different terrains and get to see stunning sights. I even saw families with young children managing the walk. 

You can choose to go right or left at the Y-bend after entering on the walk. We went left, which takes you to little world's end, then on to world's end and finally the falls. But you can go right and switch the order. I think we choose well as returning by the left route may be more difficult than via the right. Look out for the clouds covering the valley as you drive up the mountain. Magnificent!

Title: Superb Morning Trail
Text: Try to go early morning as you get good clear view of vally. Just carry suffcient water to keep yourself hydrated and where good pair of shoes. Once you are on Horton plains I dont think you need warm cloths as you get warm up as you keep on trailing. A must place to vist in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Challenging but worth it!
Text:
Im not a morning person so the thought of setting off at 5am for a hike filled me with dread. A compromise was reached with my guide and we set out at 7am instead. My guide told me that the walk had to be done before 9am otherwise I wouldnt be able to see anything due to the mists. Judging by the number of people walking back when I started the trek, their guides had told them the same thing! 

The walk itself was challenging but totally worth it for the views. The mists had indeed settled when I reached worlds end but a bit of patience and I was able to get the amazing views. Theres lots of native fauna to be seen on the way, keep an ear out for the monkeys. 

Tip: most people turn left to reach little worlds end first, I went straight to get to bakers falls first. This meant the walk back, when absolutely shattered, was way easier and mostly downhill.

Title: Pretty, but overpriced
Text: The place is beautiful, with a few hidden gems around, worthwhile. But we felt that the entrance ticket was a bit overpriced.

Title: Nothing special compared to National Parks elsewhere in the world and expensive
Text: Worlds End was an anticlimax, and we had good weather there. It is a good 9 km walk with varied terrain, scenery and views but nothing special compared with many walks in the UKs National Parks and elsewhere in the world.  Not worth the early start and high fees and getting there is not simple.  We were travelling from Nuwara Eliya to Ella, so did the Worlds End walk on the way. We hired a car and driver for LRK10,000.  The Horton Plains NP fee for two people, plus the car and driver was LKR8,100.  Apart from the first kilometre or so there is no sign of the money raised from foreign tourists being used to maintain the route.  In places the path would become a watercourse after rain, luckily it was dry when we were there. I have no problem with foreigners being charged more than locals but the price charged should be reasonable and it would be good to see the money generated being invested in the site.

Title: Wish we hadnt bothered...
Text:
We should have heeded those who advised against doing this walk, particularly agree with all that Aaron and other gentleman below has said on this site.  Its a lot of money to get in, an hours drive to get there, and in fact we only saw deer outside the park.
Guess it depends where you are from but we felt we could be doing a walk in one of our National Parks that is just as beautiful and free to all.  SL needs to seriously rethink about some of these out of proportion fees for foreign visitors if they want to build tourism numbers.

Title: Horton plains
Text:
We did the walk along Horton Plains to see Worlds end and bakers falls . 
It is worth getting there when the park opens at 6am as the walk can take a while and the clouds come in during the day. 
Wear sensible shoes as some of the walk is along a rocky path and it is not easy to walk along. 
You can see deer and lots of birds 
Well worth a visit

Title: Wonderful scenery !
Text: It was a very cool and windy place ! Required to bring wind breaker for the trek. Nice trekking. Nice scenery at the world end. Suggest to bring breakfast box and have it when you arrive at world end view point and continue to trek for waterfall.

Title: Overpriced hike
Text:
40euro for 2 persons is way to expensive for this.
It is just a normal hike, Worlds end could be nice if your lucky, we had only clouds...
I don't get where all this money goes to.
There is only few staff at entrance and a worthless museum.
No wildlife to be seen. Only saw some deer outside the national park area.....
Better hiking to do in Ella for free.

Title: Great views!
Text: Wear comfy clothing and be prepared for rain! This place is a great place to walk, we walked up to World's End with it's amazing views and then around to Baker's Falls. Such a beautiful waterfall. This is an amazing part of Sri Lanka, the climate here is so different from the rest of the country. I can see why they call it Little England! We only saw some deer but still enjoyed the day and the fresh air.

Title: One of the most awesome places in Sri Lanka
Text: Youcan experience a different type of climate up there with different flora and fauna compared to other places in the coutry. World's end drop is just one thing visit within this amazing area.

Title: deer spotting at horton plains
Text: we arrived early morning to avoid the afternoon mist. we had to walk about 01 to 02 km from the entrance to get to the famous viewpoint where you could see an entire town from the top. it is advisable to stay of the edge of the cliff and avoid having any accidents as many people have fallen off this cliff.

Title: Memorable Hike to the top
Text: the best hiking experience in sri lanka. we visited nuwara eliya and then took the hike the day after. we started off early morning and it was amazing. we were able to spot deer, a leopard and migrating birds. wonderful experience.

Title: A Trip we can never forget
Text:
We were in Nuwara Eliya, Small England of Sri Lanka (elevation 2000+ meters above sea level, average temp 12 degrees). We Started our trip early morning at 5.00 am which will take around 1 hour due to foggy road.
It is 30 kms south of Nuwara Eliya lies the famous Horton Plains (2,100 m) sorrounded by mountain ranges.
It starts about 400 meters from the Entrance Gate. Start off early and aim to get there before 6.30am for the best views over World's End, before the mist & cloud cover the area. 
Take the route that goes to mini World's End first from left. The hike takes about 3 to 4 hours, do not forget to bring water, snack, umbrella (in case if it rains) and wear proper hiking shoes. 
You will first reach to Mini World's End ( 2 Kms from Entrance). 
From Mini worlds Ends to Greater World's End is further 3 Kms. 
Further to reach Baker's Falls you need to Walk 2 Kms. 
On the way you will get a Public Toilet which is not very clean & hygienic with no water tap in it. 
Returning back to gate you will get to see Chimney Pool (1.5 Kms from Greater World's End.
And at last to reach the Gate its 2 Kms 
In rain get muddy and slippery, especially when you go towards Baker's Falls. 
There is only one toilet in entire route inside the Park, so try to use one before you leave your hotel, or else at the entrance of the national park, there is a toilet.
Ticket price is well worth it. Grassland plains, mangrove forests.
There is a restaurant outside the gate were you can refresh yourself .
We paid LKR 7,950.00 for 2 person incl all. for the entrance ticket.

Title: High plains drifter
Text: You need to set off early in the day to avoid the noonday sun and also find a parking space in this popular national park. The views are stunning but if you suffer from vertigo, I would give this a miss. Ground is quite uneven so ware good quality walking boots and be prepared for a workout!

Title: One of the most fulfilling experience!
Text:
Park is easily accessible from Nuwara Eliya, you can choose from different kind of transports. On the way back you can also visit dairy firms.

Park is one of the most pristine and serene natural parks i have visited till now. Took the worlds end and & bakers fall trek,which is about 9km hiking. Surprisingly they have well maintained washroom facilities inside the park too.

Tips would be bring  raincoats and a spare pair of cloths.

Title: We enjoyed it alot, but get there EARLY!!!
Text: we are two fit 20 some / 30 something year olds, in good physical shape, so this hike was a breez, a little tricky a a few points, near the Worlds End, but in general its mellow, and can be done by most. We saw small children, old people, fat people, and hundreds of locals in flip flops. So its not too difficult of a hike. We saw some deer, and alot of birds, but thats about it. Alot of good photos and if you sneak off the paths here and there you can find some even better ones.

Title: Very beautiful trail
Text: We were told to be there early, so we were at the park at 6 am (!). Still, the queue was long to buy tickets and entering the park. However, the effort was totally worth it, hikikg the 7km nature trail. The plains offered lovely views and so did the hot spots Worlds End and Bakers Falls.

Title: Best guide for Horton Plains exploring - worth every cent
Text:
Mr Kaneel Rajanayeka is recommended in the Lonely Planet Guide and we were lucky our hotel's recommended guide turned out to be the man himself. While we could have walked the 9 km circuit by ourselves, Raja's expert knowledge of creatures, birds and medicinal plants made our day memorable and we learned so much. Plants used in Ayurvedic healing of arthritis, depression, even cancer, and ones which are still sometimes the basis of our western medicines, were frequently spotted. While the famous view at Worlds End was obscured by cloud, we finished the day feeling privileged to have experienced some of the Sri Lankan forest and plains. In addition he answered many of our questions about the wierd half of Nuwara Eliya town known as Little England".  Raja can be contacted independently on E: 
nuwaraeliyatrekkingclub@hotmail.com

Title: A not-too-strenuous hike, with plenty of wildlife and animals along the way
Text:
We enjoyed our trip to the horton plains and after completing the hike we did an afternoon trip to Ella from the Nuwara Eliya train station. The hike was stepo at some points (we did the "long hike" to world's end) but nothing that children couldn't manage. We saw a pair of chameleons and a lot of playful monkeys which was lovely and the whole hike took about 2 and a bit hours (we didn't walk to fast).

However when we got to world's end there was nothing to see as the views were barred by clouds, so I would recommend if it was a noticeably cloudy day take the shorter route to save time if you would be disappointed if you did the hike and there wasn't any views (whihc wasn't the case for us as we loved all of the wildlife and scenery).

Title: So many different reviews on this - yes its hard, but its worth it
Text:
Ok, so Ill start out by saying Im a pretty fit person (triathlete, trail runner). I read all the reviews before going and noticed so many different views from nice flat and easy to really tough. 

I ran the route, taking about 1hr 30 (Im not a quick runner). For someone who doesnt exercise regularly this would be really tough. But definitely give it a crack. Just know its not going to be easy and you need comfortable shoes. Saw so many people out there today in completely inappropriate shoes. 

I ran clockwise. Ive read that anticlockwise is easier. Without having run anticlockwise, I think that would probably be right. But I guess its a loop. So theres as much up as there is down, whichever way you go. 

But its so beautiful. I didnt go with the intent of getting to Worlds End before the fog came. Which is good, because I got there at about 10:15 and you couldnt see a thing. But its still well worth doing as there are so many other views.

Title: If tghey tell you there are inclines but no steep climbs - don't believe them
Text: Disappointing. We are reasonably fit but were misled by being told there were no steep inclines. In particular there are stony areas where you have to climb up and down the rocks - harder going down in fact as it jars the knees badly. The view isn't great because you are on the top of a steep cliff and therefore can't see the cliff itself. Absolutely no guardrails or safety features before the sheer drop - in fact somebody had fallen to their death a few days earlier and, while w were there, a party of climbers came to recover the body.

Title: Hike in the mountains
Text: We did the round trip to see the waterfall and the worlds end. The entrance fee is a bit pricey for foreigners but thats the way it is in Sri Lanka. You get some nice views and a glimpse of the nature here. If you are lucky and walk with open eyes you will see some animals.

Title: must stay a night
Text: you will must reserve a cottage in advance from forest department. there are cottages according to your capacity. great opportunity to see some wild animal next to your window. some of them friendly too..if walk thru the park will take five hour to complete. don't forget your water bottle.

Title: Long Walk
Text:
If you're lucky, you may see wildlife....but there's no guarantee. We did see a rather rare buffalo during our ride (30 minutes before the park) but didn't see much once we began our hike. 

The path is well defined, and you'll see nice waterfalls. But I didn't find much that was appealing, evidenced by the fact that I didn't take many photos and was glad when the walk ended.

Title: Get there early
Text: We set off from Nuwara Eliya at 5am. We arrived at 6am and there was a que to buy tickets to enter. Tickets are relatively expensive but worth it. The whole walk takes about 2-3 hours including a stop for a snack. Please dont wear flip flops! You will struggle without decent shoes as its not a pristine beautiful path the whole way. Views from worlds end are stunning but you need to get to that point before 10 or 11am when everything clouds up.

Title: A nice hike in the morning
Text: Nothing special or unique about the park. It's just a park, fresh air, nice views, nice hike, after many days spent mostly in the car, going from one place to another.

Title: You need to be surefooted
Text: I didn't find this particularly taxing in terms of fitness, but there is a lot of picking your way over rocky and muddy paths, some quite steep. As advised we got there really early - make sure you allow about half an hour to queue for tickets, then drive the couple of miles more to the actual start of the trail (where there is a toilet and small cafe). You need to make sure you don't have any plastic bags, as they will be taken away at the gate, but plastic bottles are OK if the label is removed. It will be cold when you start (15 degrees when we left Nuwara Eliya at 5am, 12 degrees at the gate to Horton Plains at 6am), but once you start walking you will soon warm up, so only one extra layer is fine, and shorts would have been OK. We actually set off walking at 6.45. Shortly after the start you have a choice of which way round you go. We chose anticlockwise, but with hindsight, I think the clockwise route would have got us to World's End quicker. There is a map at the start, but few signs on the way. The terrain was tricky, with rocky paths to start, and a couple of streams to cross. It then got steeper, and much muddier, which slowed us up. Unless you've never seen a waterfall, don't waste time by diverting to Bakers Falls. It's good, but very much the supporting act, and you can always go back after you've been to World's End. We finally got to World's End at about 5 to 9, and were very fortunate indeed - literally within 5 minutes, the view had disappeared, the mist just rolling up the whole valley - quite a sight to see. So disappointing for anyone arriving after that, as there was nothing to see. The rest of the park is pleasant, but not spectacular. Further along the valley there is Mini World's End, but I can't tell you what the view would have been like! Once past these, the terrain becomes much flatter, apart from one fairly steep rocky path, and the mist doesn't encroach on the rest of the park. There's a toilet on the way back, on the edge of the hillside, open sided with a pretty decent view. I had walking shoes on, but on the way back we passed locals in flip flops!

Title: A manageable walk!
Text:
As an obese person with a bad right knee and a recovering strained left upper thigh muscle, I was worried that I could not tak÷ on the challenge that was Horton's Plains, especially after reading horrifying reviews about it. Fortunately, all my fears were unfounded!

Walking at a moderate pace, I found the walk entirely manageable though there were some tricky parts such as the rocky sections of the trail. On this note, do make sure to wear good shoes! 

We were also blessed as the weather conditions were in our favour. It did not rain the day before and neither did it on our hiking day. As a result, the paths were not very muddy and therefore easier to traverse. My friend and I, however, could see why the trail might be challenging should the weather be poor. 

A note on safety precautions to take, do not go too close to the edge of the cliff at World's End. According to our guide, a tourist had plunged to her death just a few weeks before our trip in an attempt to take a selfie.

Some tips: 
1. Check the weather forecast
2. It is preferable to have a guide since some paths may not be clear to the inexperienced
3. Bring some food and water
4. Do not bring plastic bags as there are thorough bagchecks before one enters the park
5. It is okay to bring bottled water into the park. However, do remove the plastic seal and label around the bottle before entering the park. 
6. There are rubbish bins in the park. DO NOT LITTER. 
7. Do not make too much noise as that might scare away wildlife. We had an unpleasant encounter with a group of noisy and rude tourists and had to ask them to tone it down. Do respect the environment and be comsiderate to others. That way, the walk will be pleasant for everyone! :)

Overall, I enjoyed the trail as the views were lovely and it was certainly good exercise!

Title: Excellent tour. Good value for money.
Text:
This was an amazing tour for the money charged the tour lasted 3.5 hours. We saw so much wild life in this park including wild boar, peacocks and rare birds. We got up close to elephants and a herd family.

We had an excellent guide who pointed out animals and rare species.

Title: Well worth a visit.
Text: Good variety of animals for a small park. Plenty of elephants and excellent bird life near lake. Guide was reasonable and did not chase the animals. Roads were bad but it was after the rains,

Title: Shocked as cash only
Text:
With Sri Lanka in a such financial crisis how is the Kaudula national park allowed to handle cash only
I was supriced when they said cash only.
National Park it self was great.

Title: 2 Hour Safari
Text: Went here was we had some time and the 2 hour trip was great. We have done a safari in Africa  previous to this trip.  Great view of elephants in the wild

Title: Amazing
Text: Once in a lifetime experience , stayed local in the go go green hotel (highly recommend) the guided tour was amazing ?? saw loads

Title: Elephant visit
Text: We were a small group of people travelling together.  We were all looking forward to seeing the elephants.  We saw many and they were beautiful creatures but unfortunately it was a bad day to view elephants and they were all in the same area. All the jeeps congregated in one area to make  sure their paying customer got the best view buy cutting in front of other vehicles.  I know the Sri Lankan Economy has been suffering and everyone wants that big tourist tip but not at the cost of the elephants health and safety.  I understand that this was unusual practice but it was only because the elephants were all in the same area.

Title: Exciting safari seeing so many elephants
Text: Experienced a wonderful safari here with Ceylon Wild Trails Safari. Sanjay was an excellent driver with a comprehensive knowledge of the birds and animals in the park. Even saw an elephant on the road as we left the park. i

Title: Fantastic to see so many elephants in the wild
Text:
We did an afternoon safari to see the elephants. A fantastic experience, particularly seeing the weeks old babies with the herd and the protection they are given. 

Then there was all the birdlife.

An experience youll never forget

Title: Elephants
Text: This is a wild life park you can see elephants. There are many safari jeeps around to hire. The fare had to be negotiated.

Title: Safari trip around Kaudulla
Text:
Worth a visit to this national park if youre in the area.

Had the opportunity to see a vast array of wildlife including some beautiful elephants. 

There are a fair few safaris operating in the park so it would be nice if the authorities cap the number of safaris so it was less busy but I think compared to some of the other national parks, its pretty quiet! 

Most safari drivers are considerate but there are a couple who feel the need to go that little bit closer to the animals or drive a little bit more dangerously so just pick your tour guide carefully!

Title: Elephants everywhere
Text: A great place to watch these gentle giants feeding and interacting. We saw lots of play and while the grassland was full of jeeps, the 100 or so elephants seemed like they were counting us as much as we were counting them! A lovely afternoon and evening. Plenty of other wildlife as well.

Title: Tour with Kamatha safaris
Text: Warner took the 'slow route' and his local experience and knowledge of the wildlife made this a highlight of our Sri Lanka holiday. The driver was very careful both driving to the park and during the off-road drive in the park itself. Plenty of time was given for photo opportunities of birds and the elephants which were numerous. Elephant watching has become a very popular tourist experience and the park had a number of other tour operators who just seemed to be racing to the final destination. The Kamatha safari was done at just the right pace.

Title: Kandulla national park
Text:
What a fabulous place - I visited in October and saw hundreds of elephants.
Many had babies which was extra special,
The vehicles were covered over - I was in a jeep. Brilliant afternoon out ??

Title: Hundreds of elephants!
Text:
Honest review. Before visiting Kaudulla, I had said that I would be happy to see three elephants! I had done quite a bit of research regarding the safari's and elephant sanctuaries in Sri Lanka and both Minneriya and Kaudulla were the ones that came up as the most ethical while others just seemed a bit sketchy or disrespectful in terms of the space given between the jeeps and elephants.
Sometimes you just have to go and see it for yourself and so we did. The national park is a big land and the elephants are entirely free to wander through Kaudulla and Minneriya without direct interaction with people. If you have a good camera, you're in for a treat. We saw hundreds of elephants! 
Yes, there are a lot of jeeps but I felt like the drivers kept a respectful distance at all times and even to one another so as not to hog all of the space. We were often quite far away from the elephants and only close if the elephants were coming toward us or passing by us so I'd recommend buying a good zoom lens if you don't have one. My camera had an unfortunate accident in some torrential rain in Ella so I had to make do with my phone but I still got some really great pictures and even better memories.
All in all, this was a major highlight of a full-on trip and I would definitely recommend it.
I think it cost us around $60 USD each and I felt like we got our money's worth.

Title: Nice but muddy
Text: When we go there its heavy rain but we see so many elephants. We enjoyed it. If rain dont go to see the elephants. Because its muddy.

Title: Safari of Jeeps not Elephants - Higher Entrance Fee for Foreigners
Text:
Though at the time we did enjoy the sight of elephants at the waterhole, in hindsight I feel that there were way too many jeeps.  They were blocking the path of the elephants.  

Foreigners are charged a higher price than the locals.  This was our experience right throughout our 10 day tour of Sri Lanka.  Every attraction we visited, foreigners had to fork out between 20 times to 100 times more than the locals.

Title: Rainy Day / Lucky day
Text:
For the first time in my life, I was able to see an wild elefant. In fact we were able about 150 of them in small groups. 

We are wet to our Bones because of the rain but very grateful. 

We called this little fellow: Stampfi! Luckely we had been there early enought! 

Driver needed! If you love elefants this is the way to go. Also if you are Lucky you might be able to see snakes and crocodiles aswell.

Title: Majestic
Text: Enjoyed a Safari in this park about an hour away from Cinnamon Lodge Habarana. It was exciting to see the elephants roaming free along with birds, mongoose, deer, cattle and monkeys.

Title: Hundreds of elephants in a beautiful setting
Text:
An afternoon visit was recommended as having the best chance of seeing elephants.  So enough time to visit Polonnaruwa the morning have lunch and head to the National Park.

Whether Kaudulla or Minneriya will probably depend on where the elephants have been sighted recently.  Minneriya was deserted as we drove past as the elephants had been favouring Kaudulla.

The cost of the park entry was around US$100 for 4 of us.  Then there is the jeep and driver which our guide organised.  A total of about US$150.  So an expensive 3 hours, but we did see lots of elephants with the lovely backdrop of the lake.  And although there were many in the distance around the lake we were also able to get very close to some.

By the way, there are probably as many people and jeeps as elephants!  It is a popular activity, so you certainly won't be alone (see photo)

Title: Afternoon safari
Text: Visited for an afternoon safari as we were advised not to visit Minneriya which was our first choice as we'd been before. We saw approximately 250 elephants which was more than we'd seen on previous visits to Minneriya so good advise. It was a little longer from Cinnamon Lodge but would advise anyone to visit.

Title: Excellent
Text: An afternoon experience not  to be missed.  Saw hundreds of elephants in their natural setting.  Memorable!

Title: Just as good as Minneriya
Text: We were told to visit this national park as elephants migrated a few days before from Minneriya, which was our original target. This national park is just as good, with plenty of things to see

Title: Amazing experience seeing so many elephants
Text: We did an afternoon safari here and it was brilliant - we saw easily over 100 elephants including 1 month old babies! The driver stopped still and allowed the elephants to come close to the jeep. Highly recommend a trip to this beautiful park.

Title: Elephants ??
Text:
We joined a safari through the park. We were told that there are up to 200 elephants in a group at the water hole. Because of rain there was "just" round 100. 
We've also seen water buffaloes, monkeys and lots of  birds. 
Today we feel blessed. It was amazing.

Title: Evening Safari
Text: Wow wow wow. There are no words for this beautiful place, elephants are my favourite animal so the opportunity to see them in the wild, left alone was incredible. You can get so close to them without disturbing them and it was unbelievable how many there were! Easily over 200 and lots of babies!! 100% recommend.

Title: excelant
Text: beautiful wildlife tour very nice many elephant and birds elephant bathing with baby amazing special thank for jeep driver

Title: Elephant hot spot
Text: What a fabulous place, went on safari and saw around 200 elephants, incredible, including baby ones, I took so many photos I ran out of battery, elephants are relative close to the jeeps. You do a one way circuit, we saw the elephants near a giant water hole, stay as long as possible here, further along there were buffalos, we saw jackals and peacocks

Title: Amazing natural reserve
Text: Beautiful national park that is left almost untouched by humans. We went during mating season, and we saw almost 100 elephants! You can hire a Jeep safari and get your own private tour of the place for a reasonable price.

Title: Wow
Text: We booked a 3 hour tour to Kaudulla National Park, but were a little bit frustrated at the entrance gate, as many jeeps with tourist were waiting to get in. We thought that would be a tourist trap, but it ended up to be one of our best experiences by visiting Elefants. We strongly can recommend to do his tour

Title: Elephants and elephants... everywhere
Text:
Kaudulla or Minneriya is the obvious question when one is in Sigiriya area. Guides and jeep drivers decide on know positions of elephant herds and water level in the area. Our Jeep safari suggested Kaudulla, so off we went. 
We did have a few sighting of peacocks, deer, birds, monitor lizards, but these parks are for the majestic Asian elephant the largest mammal on land. 
After a bumpy ride through the greens we came across a vast expanse of grassland and so many elephants. There were everywhere, near us, ahead of us & everywhere we could see.
This was a large gathering of approx 350 wild elephants. Our driver said that there are more baby elephants this year than last. 
This is the best place in Sri Lanka to see wild elephants in such a large number.

Park ticket costed us LKR 14800 for a group of 6 and jeep charges were LKR7500

Title: OMG!!!! This place is the paradise for elephant lovers!
Text:
we planned to visit other park but the guide recommended this park as it was cheaper and better! And it was true!!!
Lots of elephants and you will be next to them!!

Title: A great place to see elephants in the wild.
Text: A great place to see elephants in the wild and was amazed at how many are roaming around this reserve. Only issue was the fumes from the vehicle as it is open topped.

Title: Highly recommended
Text:
There are 3 national parks in the vicinity (Minneriya,Kaudulla and Eco), with elephants travelling across all 3 of them, which is why it is best to check with locals (hotel owner/ tour operator) to confirm which park the elephants are in.
We checked with Rana's information counter and were informed that the elephants were in Kaudulla, so booked a safari here.
We booked the afternoon slot and entered the park around 3.00 P.M. We saw a lot of elephants and big herds of wild buffaloes soon after entering the park. At the lake, we saw a big herd of elephants, including some cute baby elephants. 
Overall, this was a great experience and we thoroughly enjoyed watching elephants so close and in their natural surroundings.
On the cost - we checked with a few operators and ones we approached through the hotel and our driver quoted prices around 30,000 LKR (inclusive of tickets and the jeep). We then went to the main road and checked with a  few tour operators who had their offices there, where we found Rana's information agency, and booked the safari for LKR 19,000 (inclusive of tickets and the jeep). 
An alternative would be to check the prices of the jeep only and book tickets yourself. This will allow you to negotiate the price of the jeep (the tickets will cost the same as they are issued by the government). The only issue with this is that you will spend quite sometime in talking to various people and negotiating rates, while you potentially save 1 - 2,000 LKR, so the savings might not be worth the time spent).

Title: Loads of elephants!
Text:
Was not disappointed. Saw loads of elephants, monitor lizard, peacocks. 

Fantastic experience! 

Would highly recommend.

Title: Where the elephants roam amid the traffic
Text:
I've never seen so many elephants. Nor have I seen so many people in 4WD vehicles clamouring to watch them. Kaudulla National Park is pachyderm central and the place to go to see elephants in Sri Lanka as far as I can tell. Our visits to other parks - Yala, Horton Plains and Wilpattu resulted in few elephant sightings. On this trip, we saw large elephant herds, totalling at least 200 animals. 

You can spend hours watching them, particularly as there were many youngsters on show during out visit. Our only concern was that some animals appeared anxious, angry or both at the 60 or so vehicles full of local and international tourists lined bumper to bumper to see them. However, most appeared to accept it as part of life and just did what elephants do at a respectful distance.

Thanks to the number that hung around, this was a great opportunity to see lots of interaction between the animals, including youngsters and their mothers. 

Kaudulla is well worth a visit and let's hope all remain respectful of the animals' space.

Title: Exellent safari experience
Text: We were enchanted to get up close to a herd of more than 70 elephants and see a wide array of birds on the safari. Nonetheless, you need to be aware that the roads are a bit unbearable. But its worth the experience. After that, you will be relieved by the majestic herd of animals in the park.

Title: Elephant spotting
Text: Had an amazing safari! You have a certainty to see elephants in their natural habitat which is a very nice experience.

Title: Sir Lanka
Text: The car cost 60 USD . It take about 20 min from car site to the park . It take about 2 hour in the park

Title: Nice park for july-october
Text: Ask the jeep drivers where the herds of elephants are! they are or in Minneriya, or in Kaudulla or in Eco park.

Title: Elephants, of course
Text: We were on an 18 day tour with LankaTracker visiting many national parks .. to avoid the crowds in Minneriya we opted for Kaudulla. It was just as our guide said it would be .. there will be fewer elephants but you will have them all to yourself :)

Title: Wild elephants at Kaudulla
Text: One of the best national Parks where you can observe large elephant herds. You can enjoy an exciting safari ride with local guides.

Title: What an Experience
Text:
We used a company called Akita village and lake adventure for this trip which included a village tour. Our Jeep on the safari was in good condition and the driver careful when driving around the park.

After about an hour into the visit we had only experienced one lone male grazing. The rainy season had just finished so the tracks were badly rutted making it a bumpy ride, along with the heat and humidity we were about to ask to finish the tour.

Im so pleased we left it a few minutes as we rounded a corner and in front of us were a herd of 20+ elephants of all ages. Luckily we were one of the first jeeps to arrive so had a prime spot very close to the herd. We spent about 45 minutes watching this incredible scene unfold before us, a couple of the calves were only a 2/3 weeks old...so cute.

I do hope you experience the same when you come here as this was one of those Never to be Forgotten moments in life.

Title: Bad!- More jeeps than animals
Text:
I went  in February. I think what I experienced there happens in most of the other parks close by like Minneriya or Kaudulla. Anyways he driver decided in which park the most elephants were expected. 
The few elephants there were surrounded by eight jeeps or more. The problem is that they dont fill up the jeeps with people so there is mostly one Jeep per person or per couple. I understand that people need jobs here, but this is not a sustainable way and there are better systems in other National Parks. 
Jeeps crowd chaoticly around an elephant and sometimes the driver couldnt get through or just drives by because there is no space to stop. Fumes and noise from the jeeps were constantly around me. 
I saw more animals outside in the country than in this NP. 
Not sustainable activity, no animals or nice nature observed, dusty, hot, polluted and crowded with people and Jeeps. Not recommended at all.

Title: Lots of Elephants
Text: Did a safari trip to Kaudulla Park.  We had a driver and a jeep, as did many other people.  We all headed out at the same time.  Very crowed.  But we were thrilled to see elephants and got some fantastic pictures.  Was a little long.  Our driver was awesome and helped us find some fresh elephant dung for pictures for our grandsons.  Had a good time, but did get very hot.

Title: Excellent birdwatching.
Text: The previous day we had visited Eco park on an elephant safari, which was great, it did what it said.  Kaudulla, however, was magical! It made a huge difference that we only saw one other jeep in 3 hrs instead of being in a convoy of 30, but even so, it is a stunning place - enormous lakes teeming with wildlife and so many different sorts of birds. The elephant we saw washing in the lake was somehow more magical than all the ones we saw yesterday.  (The weather had been pretty bad which may explain the lack of jeeps, we dont know).

Title: Safari Elephant experience
Text: Quite simply the primary reason for visit Sri Lanka was to see elephants in their natural surrounding. For our trip we hired a driver with 4x4 transport who guided us through the jungle terrain, photographing water buffalo and crocs but the main attraction was the sheer number of elephants. For us, this was a once in a lifetime opportunity to see hundreds of elephants in the natural environment. Highly recommended

Title: Amazing
Text:
Spent 4 hours here watching the elephants 
We had our own jeep and our diver was excellent and very knowledgeable about the park and didnt get tangled up with the other jeeps 
Found mother and baby elephants in packs 
Crocodiles 
Monkeys and some amazing bird life

Title: Humbling
Text:
We spotted several types of animals and birds and of course the star attraction, elephants. They were a little hard to find in mass early on but closer to sunset, out they came. Probably 120+ elephants in several locations. 
There are quite a few jeeps but nowhere near the amount I was expecting from what I'd read of other parks. The drivers respected the elephants and stuck to the tracks which looks after the ground so there is enough food for the animals.

Must do in Sri Lanka.

Title: Bumpy trip to see amazing elephants
Text:
To be honest, its not so much the park as the safari driver that makes this a good experience. Our driver knew ( as did all other drivers) that the majority of elephants were in Kaudulla on the day we went. 
The park itself does have a lot of wildlife but we were rapt to see about 200 elephants in the wild, so left having had our expectations exceeded. 
Apparently afternoon is best, you pay an entry fee to the park as well as a fee for your Jeep. 
Amazing experience.

Title: Simply amazing experience
Text: Visited in late August 2019. It was an amazing day! Saw so many animals like monkeys, crocodile and the main attraction the elephant. Was an amazing sight seeing so many elephants together in the wild. Truly a once in a life time experience and I would highly recommend to anyone travelling to Sri Lanka. It appears the elephants move between kaudulla and Minneriya national park, so I am sure whoever you book a safari through they will know where the elephants are.

Title: Deep Forest
Text: Drive to Minneriya National park was an awesome experience we had. We were taken into the park on an open jeep and we could even go close to around 30 to 35 wild elephant. I presume we were so lucky to have that sighting of them. The 3 hour drive was really memorable and could see a lot of wild inmates of the area

Title: Kaudulla National Park
Text: We had a great jeep and driver organised by Habarana Inn at Habarana. Saw over 100 elephants! So amazing. Driver happy to stay as long as we wanted too and was respectful to the animals. He was very observant and was always pointing out things for us to see. He even bought us some watermelon on the way back to our accomodation, the Jasmin Villa, run  by Habarana Inn. Great little cottage.

Title: Great place to see elephants
Text:
Was a wonderful experience to see so many wild elephants in one place and the fact you can get so close to them was amazing.

Was fortunate enough to see one of the 30 odd tuskers roaming there ( Sumedha as they call him).

Title: superbly protected and exciting park
Text:
Don't make too many safari plans before coming to Sri Lanka - the animals move around and local people will be best able to tell you where to go. We were planning on two other parks, but our accommodation host in Habarana recommended Kaudulla and we weren't disappointed. After a bumpy and challenging drive into the heart of the park, encountering a crocodile, countless monkeys, several eagles and a couple of chameleons on the way - our path led us to a wide and open scrubland, where the elephants were clearly visible, in groups of up to 20 or so. We were able to get as close as 5-10 metres, although the guide/drivers are careful and respectful of these lovely but dangerous creatures, so when they walked towards us, we were ready to drive away. 
The drought this year had made the elephants even more eager to congregate near water and this enabled our safari to be a memorable experience indeed.

Title: awesome experience - no crowded (august 2019)
Text:
I took a morning jeep safari in august 2019, and the two things I wanted were:
- spot elephants
- not have a thousand jeeps following mine

both were accomplished. 
We arrived slightly late at the park a bit after sunrise, and there were few elephants here and there, I think we could have spotted more, but to be honnest i was already enough to make me feel happy

Also we saw only 4 other jeeps in the whole park, felt pretty private. Might be due to the fact we took the morning jeep safari (organized by my driver, 45 USD/ pax),  and also because of the unfortunate terrorist attacks that happened three months ago... not many tourists.

Title: Amazing!
Text:
Seeing elephants in the wild was an incredible experience, especially the baby elephants. It was a bit surreal as the elephants observed all the tourists filming them from their SUV open air vehicles. 

Perhaps we were just lucky that day, but we observed almost one hundred elephants on our trip. The only drawback (besides too many tourists) is the chaotic traffic jams in and out of the park. Please note the special vehicles into the park are very bumpy (think amusement park ride) and may not appeal to some visitors.

Title: Great Ride
Text: Went to visit the place with friends & used 2 safari jeeps.they came and pick us from the place.the ladies and kids enjoyed the roofles  ride.there were few deers,  foxes, birds & lots of elephants. For my liking as it's a designated place for elephants could have been more.but nevertheless enjoyed the place

Title: Elephants and More!
Text: We visited this park as part of our wildlife tour of Sri Lanka and saw 60 elephants many with young calves and the parks biggest Tusker. An amazing place with plenty of bird life including eagles and wading birds.

Title: Potentially but not always a great elephant experience.
Text: Minneriya is renowned as a park in which to see elephant.  We were lucky in seeing a large number around the open grassy shores of the eponymous lake.  But beware!  Do your local research before falling into the arms of the first jeep driver!  The elephants move between three parks and are sometimes never here.  Wonderful if you're lucky, but the large number of jeeps does not enhance the experience.

Title: What a great experience, but like a jeep rally at times
Text:
We went in mid November, and were advised locally to change our plan to visit Minneriya National Park and come here instead, for the best chance of seeing lots of elephants. What good advice! We had a guide in an ancient jeep, which rattled along the road from Habarana, but it was to prove its worth later on, as we saw lots of fancy modern ones stuck in the mud. 
It takes a while to get into the park itself, but the scenery is good, and as you enter you start to see lots of birds - my favourites were the painted storks. Although the day was dry, it was still extremely muddy in places, and there are not really proper tracks. Each driver picks a line and goes for it, which resulted in us seeing 3 or 4 jeeps being pulled out of the mud by other drivers. We were beginning to think it wasn't our day for elephants, when we saw a group ahead, surrounded by jeeps. The elephants were clearly used to this, and didn't seem phased by it, but were careful to protect the two youngsters with them. It improved as we moved further on, and the jeeps spread out a bit. It was incredible to see so many elephants (probably in excess of 50) in one place, and in such beautiful surroundings beside the lake. I'm not really bothered about seeing birds, but there were quite a few to interest those that are, including an eagle.
On our way out of the park at dusk, we were still seeing more elephants, walking through the edges of the forest. Absolutely a day to remember.

Title: Mixed feelings: plenty of elephants but too many jeeps
Text:
We organized an afternoon safari to view the elephants through our homestay ( ortunna guest house) For 4 people all included driver, Jeep, national park entry fees cost was 21900.we saw about 60 elephants including 10 calves in 2 main groups. We also heard the roars of other elephants from deep in the jungle.

Our driver, like the majority of drivers, was respectful to the wildlife and kept a reasonable berth while ensuring good views. However a small number of elephants would drive to within 5 meters of the foraging elephants and / or directly block their direction of travel.

There were more Jeeps than elephants and the grasslands around the lakes were being trashed by so many jeeps. Jeeps getting bogged was a common sight. 

We would probably not go to Miniyera or Kaudulla again unless the wildlife viewing was better regulated to protect the environment and animals.

Other unexpected highlights included good views of a giant squirrel, water buffalo, painted storks, peacocks, various lizards.

Title: "Cute Baby Eliphant,"
Text: Lots of Eliphant & baby Eliphant good to see. Very green every were. The Geep Driver great driving. Lake was amazing. At evining Nice Environment looked to see.

Title: Safari
Text: Just brilliant!! Only problems were the number of other jeeps and the mud.  At one point we were with a family of 30 elephants, and I counted 65 jeeps!! But seeing the elephants close up, eating and the way the family cared for a baby was facinating.

Title: An elephant festival
Text: We loved seeing the elephants in their natural habitat and so many young ones as well, we probably saw several hundred elephants. We also saw plenty of birds, buffalo and monkeys and the countryside was beautiful. There were lots of jeeps but in general the drivers were respectful. The elephants walked towards the jeeps on several occasions and we were able to see them quite close up, including elephants mating. We arranged a driver by the roadside in Habarana and paid USD35 per person for 3 of us, significantly cheaper than what we would have paid booking through our hotel. The driver will take you to Kaudulla or Minneriya, wherever you are more likely to see the elephants at the time. A highlight of our trip.

Title: Best Day ever
Text: Just increadible - we see in the region of 200 elephants in the natual environment. It was the best day of our visit to Sri Lanka, and the whole family loved it

Title: Saw over 250 elephants
Text:
Originally we were going to go to the other park but our tour guide informed us the elephants had moved to kaudulla

We were not disappointed. we saw around 250. we got to the park around 1pm, we left around 4, it was getting really busy after 3pm. Don't go in the morning as the elephants rest then!

Title: Elephants, Elephants and more elephants!
Text: I thought we would see elephants but wow so many.  An amazing safari saw so many lovely birds, monkeys, monitors, elephants and lots of jeeps.  The only thing that spoilt it was there are two many jeeps and some of them got too close to the elephants which really distressed one of the large female ones who you could tell was stressed.  Our driver said she does this when there are too many jeeps it was like she was protecting her herd.  The lake and surrounds are beautiful.  Throughly enjoyed our Safari and our driver was very informative and tried really hard to find us other animals which he did.

Title: Wonderful Elephant Safari
Text: I visited the park on October 17. We saw over 100 wild elephants. Thanks herds included Bulls, Pregnant Females and Families with baby elephants ??. We also observed a Jackl, Peacocks, Wild Water Buffalo herds and many birds. I highly recommend this park when the elephants are there.

Title: Mesmerising elephants in large family groups
Text:
We visited the park during late afternoon/early evening, which meant the temperature was more bearable and more chance of seeing animals.  There were just the two of us and the driver in our jeep, so no jostling for position to get a good view!
Once off the forested entry track the park opens up into a vast grassland around a large lake.

Obviously the main draw here is the elephants and we saw hundreds of them in large family groups, feeding, interacting and playing naturally, and it seems undisturbed by the jeeps travelling around.
There is also an interesting array of birdlife plus water buffalo and deer.

As the only route into the park is via a jeep excursion there were quite a lot of vehicles, but they do all split off in different directions around the park and once positioned with a view of the animals the engines are turned off so you can have a more peaceful view.
We instructed our driver whenever we were ready to move to another spot and in total spent around two hours on the park, which was sufficient time to take in the scenery and wildlife and capture some memorable moments on camera.

Well worth a visit, good value (5800 LKR for our jeep) and by all accounts less congested with vehicles than some of the other big hitting National Parks.

Title: Elephants!
Text: We took a Jeep safari into this national park. Its absolutely gorgeous scenery, with a beautiful lake, and hills. We saw elephants, water buffalo, painted storks, pelicans, eagles, a monitor lizard... would thoroughly recommend.

Title: Respecting the elephants
Text:
Great and learning experience where the elephants gathered near the lake. We saw baby elephants, different groups, as well as peacocks and smaller birds.

Highly recommended with an experienced driver. We were lucky as ours saw the best places to see the elephants in advance, reducing the impact of the jeep onto the elephants.

However, it later got overcrowded and some groups got upset because there were between 15 or 20 vehicles around them.

Locals recommended visiting the park in the afternoon, which turned out to be better.

Title: What a fantastic experience
Text: This elephant safari was fantastic. Our personal guide arranged a pick up from our hotel and then the safari guide took us to this fantastic National Park. We saw so many elephants and babies as well. Its truly magical to see them in the natural habitat. Our guide and our safari guide realised we liked birds and made so much effort to stop and point out the most beautiful birds including magnificent eagles. This was a most truly memorable experience that we will always remember

Title: Safari on a private jeep ,lots of elephants to view
Text:
Cost for family of 5 was 10,500 for entrance and jeep/guide hire was 6500.
We left from Habarana and took us another 30minutes to get to Kaudulla park.the kids had a fab time riding on the jeep as it was very very bouncy. there were mainly elephants to view in different sites, some peacocks, cows, birds but it's really the elephants jeeps are gathering around . There were quite a few jeeps around each elephant groups but our guide was great and got really close up. Great adventure for kids

Title: Elephants galore
Text:
During our stay in Habarana at Elephant Watch Hut we used the in-house safari to take us to this National Park.
We saw heaps of elephants up close. 
There was as many tourists as elephants but everyone was respectful. 
A very beautiful location.

Title: Start early and avoid the crowds
Text:
Ask your hotel to start early. When arriving at the plateau, stay left as to the right you find later in the afternoon a share of 1:2 (jeeps : elephants).
Absolutely stunning to see these huge animals from a close but respectful distance. Very peaceful!

Title: Amazing
Text: We saw many elephants of all sizes grazing on grass as well as some birds and butterflies. The Safari drivers are skilled at navigating the sometimes rough and boggy terrain

Title: Holiday 2018
Text: The jeep Safari was excellent loads of potholes in the roads for the off road vehicle. But once near the elephants it was amazing, there was a cute baby elephant there and one elephant came near one of the jeeps.  There must have been 100 elephant there if not more. Saw them drinking water and good close up to the elephants in the jeeps. U get good pics if u have a decent phone. I would definitely  recommend this trip in Sri Lanka. A good price aswell.

Title: Elephants, Elephants, Elephants
Text: Amazing, we were planning to go to Minneriya NP, but our driver recommended Kaudulla as more elephants present (I believe they move between the two parks). We saw over 150 elephants. It was magnificent to see them emerge from the jungle and than congregate at the waterhole. Lots of babies too. Heaps of jeeps, but still peaceful when all the engines are off. A must do in Sri Lanka.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: The main reason we chose to go to Sri Lanka is that my wife loves elephants. This was the best way to see them and we saw way more than we were expecting too.

Title: Kaudulla safari
Text: We had a wonderful time. Our driver Asela got us close to 3 separate herds so we saw about 150 elephants. Very impressive. Also good 4 wheel drive skills crossing the river. A great trip.

Title: More Jeeps than Elephants
Text: I love the landscape.  I would've been just as happy even without spotting any elephants.  It was magical just being there.

Title: Amazing view of elephants
Text:
We had an amazing view of elephants here. We rented a jeep and driver outside that drove us in.

The entrance process is a circus, ironic for an elephant viewing place. You will be surprised at how many jeeps go in at once; I think maybe 20 or so all drive around a set track.

You WILL see elephants and the views are stunning. We were treated to a storm on the horizon which made it spectacular.

I don't wish to be overly negative but the park rangers should have more of a presence. At one point other jeeps coralled the elephants in and they became distressed protecting their young, trumping and huddling around. Could have been avoided by the driver keeping clear for 30 seconds more.

All in all though some amazing sights and a smoother entrance process would make it excellent.

Title: Special experience
Text:
Fun to get on the back of a safari vehicle and come close to so many beautiful elephants! We saw plenty including babies that were feeding, very special. 

Be prepared though there are far more humans in jeeps than elephants!

Title: Stunning 180 wild elephants
Text: We saw around 180 wild Asian elephants as well as chameleons, eagles, pelicans and peacocks. A great experience. Shame about the growing number of jeeps and some of them encroaching too much on the Wildlife.

Title: Great experience
Text:
The private Jeep safari tour considering what it cost the operator to run such a tour. They should make it more affordable. 

But other than this, we saw over 50 elephants on the day of our tour. Some came really close to the jeeps so you can take great photos. The ride was quite bumpy throughout but it was still worth it. There were not that many other animals about.

Title: Mi experiencia
Text:
The park is beautiful. We did not like that the number of jeeps was very large. They should control the flow. And above all we did not like that the elephants were cut off from the wooded area to the water. We believe that this should be managed by animal welfare
The sunset in the park is very very beautifull

Title: The Gathering was amazing...but jeeps can get in the way
Text:
We went to Kaudulla in mid August and saw the most amazing site of families of elephant coming out of the bush...along trodden paths, to eat the fresh grass that surrounds the water tanque....as we waited, the numbers grew to over 250 elephant of all ages, including young tuskers, matriarchs and babies...with solitary older male elephants circling round the edges.
We noticed that jeeps stopped on what were clearly "paths" for the elephant and caused them distress as they couldn't easily reach the grass and water
I'm not sure how you could get the balance right between the needs of the elephants and the desire of visitors to see the amazing sight...but this isn't right yet.

Title: Great to see wild elephants, but becoming overcrowded
Text: Hadn't heard of this place before, but our host took us there to see elephants in the wild. We saw about 10p elephants, which was fantastic. Aside from elephants we saw many birds, water buffalo, deer and a jackal. Whilst it was lovely to do, it did feel that it was starting to become quite overcrowded, with jeeps everywhere.  Not really sure it's sustainable if numbers aren't capped.

Title: Not really a safari
Text: This is a good place to see elephants, though minimal other wildlife. Id call this more of a elephant watch drive rather than a safari. Also, as we were leaving it looked like it was getting very busy (5pm). We were lucky enough to be on our own before then.

Title: WATCH OUT FOR YOUR HEAD WHEN YOU STEP OUT OF THE JEEP!!
Text: Kaudulla National Park is amazing and good on you for choosing to see elephants in their natural habitat instead of the poor captive elephants in Sri Lanka. People who drive the jeeps don't say anything to prevent very common head slamming that happens when safari-goers are stepping out of the jeeps. Please remember to take off your sun hats and watch out for the led pipes of the jeep roof. At least 5 in our group of 10 in two seperate jeeps accidentally slammed their heads. I ended up with a concussion. If this was in the US, several companies would have already been sued, so precautions would have been made! Here, no ones warns, there are no signs and yet, we heard from many who made the same mistake and ended up with very painful heads. So watch out. Please take a safari jeep into a park like this instead of riding elephants or seeing them in festivals and pageants and temples or hotels. We went in August and saw at least a 100 amazing elephants and baby elephants!

Title: Awesome experience!
Text:
We were lucky enough to be here at the time of year when all the elephants congregate The Gathering. We saw over 100 elephants on the plains by the water hole. It was an awesome sight! In the herds were babies only about a week old and a big male tusker elephant. You really do get close up with them. 
There are lots of jeeps; too many as it seemed to stress the elephants. We werent expecting that after the less busy Udewalawe National Park. 
The terrain is very rough; be prepared for a very bumpy ride!

Title: Lots of elephants!
Text:
We saw at least 90/100 elephants. It is quite expensive but totally worth it. My only recommendation will be to choose a time when there are not many cars. 
It gets really busy and there are far too many jeeps but it is incredible to see the elephants in the wild.

Title: Plenty of elephants and traffic jams
Text: Surprised by the large number of jeeps in the park at the same time. Does not appear to be any road rules or driver courtesies and is a free for all when passing/overtaking. Plenty of elephants to see but roads/paths are well worn with dips and pot holes. Good viewing from open air roof when standing up in the jeep. Not the most exciting safari but OK if you can tolerate the hustle and bustle of all the traffic.

Title: More jeeps than elephants
Text: This is all down to timing. The elephants had migrated to here, an minneriya, so this is where the action was.  There must have been 100 jeeps swarmed around a similar number of elephants.  Still a worthwhile safari, although the scenery is not as stunning as at minneriya.  There also appeared to be fewer birds of note.

Title: What a RIP off
Text:
A $100 US dollars was paid for this safari. It wasn't so much an animal safari, as a jeep safari.  There were hundreds of them, and  all we saw was about 6 elephants, and even that was hard jostling with the other vehicles to get to see them. There was nothing that we hadn't seen before.  Our driver thought a peacock or a lizard was something we hadn't seen before. 
The majority of animals we saw were cows, we didn't even see a deer. And when we got back to our hotel our driver wanted a tip!!
Do not waste your money 
One of the elephants we saw could hardly stand up and walk.

Title: Great experience but overcrowded.
Text: I had been looking forward to the safari but my heart sank when we spent nigh on an hour queing up with loads of other jeeps and buses just to enter the park. However things did improve once we got inside the park and the traffic thinned out. The highlight off course was the elephants and their babies but we also saw water buffalo and a few birds, don't expect to see much other wildlife tho'. Great experience but would be much better if the number of jeeps were limited to a certain number at any one time, think the wildlife would appreciate it too.

Title: Great safari
Text: Great safari saw lots of elephants and some monkeys on the way out of the park.  There are many jeeps and some are less considerate than others where respecting the animals is concerned.

Title: THE place to see Elephants
Text:
We were luck and felt privileged to see the annual "gathering" where literally hundreds of elephants make their way to the lake in the centre of the park. It is a truly amazing experience to see so many and so close up
The only downside was that there were at least 100 jeeps doing the same thing and we really felt for the elephants, trying to make their way to the water, but often blocked by the jeeps. 
It didn't spoil an amazing sight though

Title: Mixed feelings
Text: Probably wish we had not gone now. Yes, the hundreds of elephants were amazing to see, but the experience was marred by literally over 100 jeeps surrounding them. The elephants must have been so stressed. I feel Sri Lanka is going to lose its amazing assets by complete lack of eco tourism. We stayed for only 30 minutes as I felt so guilty. Paid $110 for two in own jeep, but would happily have joined others if there had been that option.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: Our driver arranged the safari. He told that the elephants are not in mineriya Park today. We visited Kaudulla park near Habarana. We saw minimum 100 elephants in the nature. We paid 100 usd for two adult and 1 child for private Jeep. We started at 13.30 and turned back at 17.30 when we said it is enough.

Title: Great experience
Text:
OK there are many jeeps in the park  as mentionned in many comments but you cannot expect to have this gem all for yourself... However many jeeps with 2 and sometimes 1 person, the park should force jeep operators to pool together more passengers, it would reduce the flow and increase their margin (but decrease revenues of drivers as they are paid a fixed amount per jeep, whatever the number of people in it).

Beautiful park with lots of elephants at this time of the year, we saw one group with >30 elephants and another with >100 elephants, plus eagles, deers, foxes, peacocks.
Great day with the kids !

User_Location: Bay of Plenty Region, New Zealand
Title: It's all about the Elephants
Text:
Fabulous. Every August the elephants start their migration. Our driver knew his job and introduced us to 4 large herds meandering through the Kaudulla National Park. At one stage we were the only vehicle in our guide's secret spot and we're surrounded by about 70 elephants including 1 month old babies suckling on their mothers. Late afternoon with an experienced driver. Our day in the park was our highlight of our Sri Lankan holiday. A truely remarkable and humbling experience.

One elephant up close and personal makes my heart jump. Three hundred sets my soul on fire.

Title: Brilliant trip
Text: Absolutely amazing trip, it was breathtaking to see the elephants in the wild. Our guide was brilliant and knew the correct times and places to go to. There were a lot of cars but knew the areas and places to go to. It was my favourite day of the whole trip- memorable for all the family

Title: Overcrowded with jeeps spurting exhaust fumes
Text:
Ok so there are a lot of elephants but really so what if they are so numerous if jeeps by the dozens block the roads .
I liked Udawalawe where it was more sensitively managed with a greater range of terrain and wild life
This was a low pount of my holiday

Title: Mixed Feelings about the Park
Text:
We had a great afternoon in the park and saw lots of elephants.

However The place was far too crowded. There were dozens of Jeeps everywhere, this cannot be good for the wildlife.
The driver seemed to be wanting to rush through the track as fast as possible to take on his next batch of tourists. The noise of the engine going at 40MPH is enough to drive animals away by the time you turn up to a good spot, so what is the point! When asking questions, he seemed to have little knowledge about animals.

As for other natural parks in Sri Lanka, the financial interest is greater than the animals' interest it appears.

We did take some nice pictures and the children were happy to see so many elephants but a quieter, closer to nature experience would have felt a lot better.

Title: Go Early
Text:
It's amazing elephant gathering. Lot of babies near the lake ground of Kaudulla.
They eat , walk ,palm and bath.
Thank you Kalum safari for wonderfully experience

Title: Plenty of elephants and even a croc!
Text:
Enjoyed seeing the lovely majestic elephants at Kaudulla National Park!

We were told by a few local people that Minneriya National Park didn't have as many animals as it often does this time of the year so we took the recommendation to go to Kaudulla instead.

We weren't disappointed with the park! It was slightly cheaper than Minneriya (although I can predict the prices may go up as they are even doing up the roads leading up to the park probably for more tourists).

It's also not as busy as Minneriya can get which is nice but the main reason I can't give five stars is due to the level of tourism now at all these national parks. It's lovely to see these beautiful animals in their wild habitats, however I can't help but begin to see these national parks as a zoo or large tourist safari park like you get in western countries. There are so many jeeps that at times it looks as though the elephants are closed into spaces due to the jeeps all around them.

This isn't all the time which is fortunate and seeing elephants (around 60 on the day), monkeys, plenty of birds and even a crocodile was amazing!

I would definitely recommend Kaudulla National Park and it's worth taking local advice as many people work in tours and can recommend what the animals are doing at that particular time of the year (they are likely to charge you the same jeep hire price regardless of if you go Minneriya or Kaudulla).

Enjoy the amazing animals but let's hope they begin to limit the number of jeeps allowed in at any time, otherwise this incredible national park will look more and more like a cruel zoo.

Recommend:
Doing your research on credible touring companies and jeep hire before you go. Otherwise you may end up booking a firm who over charge or try to squeeze more money from you through pressure sales or tips at the end. Otherwise enjoy!! :)!!

Title: Impressive encounter with elephants
Text: Yes, Kaudulla is busy with safari jeeps. But for a good reason: there are lots of elephant herds to be seen at close range. Definitely worth an afternoon safari! We appreciated it even more than our visit to Udawalawe.

Title: Awesome Elephant Viewing
Text: We came with Kalum Jeep Safari on their recommendation. We saw lots and lots of elephants. Our driver also pointed out smaller animals and birds. There were plenty of vantage points. The day we went there were lots of jeeps but our driver got us away from them and our photos were just elephants. If it is elephants you want to see then this park will reward you with excellent viewing.

Title: So many elephants!
Text:
We did the afternoon tour for 11,000 rupee for a Jeep with 4 people.
We saw hundreds of elephants who all seemed so relaxed and not bothered by the fact there were also hundreds of jeeps in the park. 
We also saw crocodiles, birds, buffalos, deer and monkeys. 
The elephants were definitely the highlight! We couldnt believe how many there were. 
Highly recommend the National Park.

Title: Unbelievable busy park - mixed feelings
Text:
This is the most hideous excursion we had. The way into the park it was crowded we thought. There were approximately 50 jeeps waiting to get into the park. When we left, it was rush hour London never had! 
The Safari is just a visit to the zoo in a Jeep. No question you are going to see elephants, they are there in herd of 50 together. We saw three of those herds. Magnificent animals and easy to photograph, but what a shame we are doing this to them.

Title: Lovely!
Text: Not sure what to expect - but it turned out to be one of the high points of our 3 month South Asia trek! Elephants and lots of em - very up close and personal - simply spectacular!

Title: Elephants
Text: An exciting journey with around 150-200 elephants that come near our Jeep. We also saw some buffaloes and different kinds of birds. The only thing is it was a crowded and dust coming from other cars so at the end everyone was tired on the way back. Will recommend to anyone.

Title: Great trip in afternoon
Text: Great way to see tje wil elephants migrating from the forest to the water. Go in the afternoon from 2 o clock on. Avoid late afternoon or early evening for reason of extreme business with 4 wheel drives and jeeps

Title: Elephants everywhere!
Text: Kaudulla national park is a great place to see elephants grazing near the lake in the afternoon. We had a large safari vehicle which was perfect for 5 of us and we left our guest house in Habarana shortly after 2 pm. It was nice to get to the park before 3:30 pm because by 4 pm it was crowded with other jeeps, with everyone keen on seeing the elephants. We had about 2 hours of elephant watching here...really cool to see them in the wild and undisturbed by our presence.

Title: Elephants galore
Text: Having visited Minneriya Wildlife park the day before this was further away from the hotel in Habarana & there are major roadworks along the way. However the park was a lot quieter and there are plenty of elephants to see at close range including a few only weeks old that were having a mud bath. If you like elephants this is a great trip.

Title: More humans than elephants
Text: Really beautiful National Park but completely spoiled by the amount of Jeeps visiting. The elephants were, for the most part, unphased by the volume of traffic going past. On the plus side, there was loads of wildlife to see!! Aside from the majestic herds of elephants we saw a wild fox, peacocks, monkeys, buffalo, cows, stalks (and lots of other birds I cant remember the names of), and to my delight I caught sight of a huge kabaragoya (Asian water monitor lizard) having a paddle in the river. I would definitely recommend going to Kaudulla (or any of the national parks) for a wildlife safari not just an elephant safari.

Title: Good elephant safari
Text: Had a safari to see elephants in early July. We left all the organising to our car driver from SLD tours (Sri Lankan driver tours) and he talked to locals about where the elephants were best at the moment.
