We went with driver/vehicle 45 from United Jeep Safari Association. (Not sure if every operator or driver is registered with this or not, you can see the yellow stickers on some but not all jeeps. Our driver was friendly and happy to point out things along the way, we ended up in Kaudulla while most tours seem to go to Minneriya. Total cost 5500Rps per person and that included the park entry fee. We saw elephants, eagles, crocodile, water buffaloes, cranes, Ibis and lots of smaller birds. In total around fifty mostly female elephants and young, they seemed not too bothered to see us. There were a variety of other Jeeps around at the same time and all went pretty close to the herd, the elephants were well able to say if we were too close and all the jeeps backed off. Elephants are why must people come to this area and the tour was a good one. Looks like there are so many tours drivers hanging round Habarana that you dont really need to book in advance. Its 4x4 city and everyone wants to offer a tour. We were happy with our driver and United Jeep Safari Association. Got to do a safari if your in Habarana or anywhere near these parks. We have also passed wild elephants on the roads this week too.

Title: Elephants!!
Text: Saw lots of wildlife - birds, hawks, eagles, cows and of course elephants. We were really lucky and saw lots, and some young ones. Definitely worth it. Our driver was really nice and patient, he stayed until we were completely satisfied. We must have been a few hours.

Title: Just Amazing....
Text:
We were on a tour of Sri Lanka as part of a Trip A Deal group tour and our guide, Lakmal, suggested we go into the Kaudulla National Park and try and find wild elephants, which are now protected and roam freely in the National Park. This tour was an extra, to fill in a few hours of free time we had one afternoon. 

What an excellent suggestion as this turned out to be probably the best highlight of the trip. All of our group of 10 elected to do the tour and we met up with our safari guides and were transferred into 4WDs. It was a bit of a trek to get to the National Park, taking about 40 minutes to get there. Once we arrived, the safari guide opened up the roof of the 4WD allowing us to stand and take in all the sights. We entered the park and had our eyes peeled in search of the elephants. We saw many birds, even a crocodile sunning itself on a rock but no elephants. There were traces of them (elephant poo), but no elephants. We drove around for about 30 minutes along the road through the forest and then we came out onto the open fields to a huge lake. We drove along the dirt tracks adjacent to the lake and turned a corner and WHAM...straight into a heard of about 30 elephants roaming freely eating the grass and foilage. It was a sight we will always remember. There was a big bull, who when he saw us became a little spooked and began to charge at us. Our driver reversed up quickly and the bull backed off. He eventually moved and we were able to pass by. To cut a long story short, for the next 90 minutes or so, we drove around this part of the National Park seeing 5-6 herds totaling more than 100 elephants. We would just stop, turn the engine off and watch these huge majestic animals in the natural habitat. It was a great experience.

There were many other tours doing this as well, with up 10 4WDs parked at one or two locations. But the elephants didnt seem to care at all..in fact, they often roamed by within a few metres of the vehicles. 

If you get the opportunity, make sure you do this.you wont be disappointed.

Title: Wow
Text: Our tour company had originally rranged for us to visit Minneriya national park but following local intelligence our guide informed us we were better visitng here to see the elephants.  Boy we were not dissappointed.  Our guide had arranged a 1968 jeep to take us round.  Our driver was excellent and obviously new the park vry well and pointed animals out to us as did our guide.  There are lots of jeeps queing to get in as the entry and exit times are restricted.  This was a very enjoyable visit and certainly gave us a taste of what we could expct when visiting Yala later on during our tour.

Title: Elephants Galore
Text:
If your back can handle the rough ride there and back its well worth it. 
Probably saw 100 Elephants of all sizes in the wild feeding and having fun. 
We took a video of them charging us in protection of a one month old baby. Its the most exciting footage I have ever taken.

Title: You Know This Is Going To Be Good, But You Never Expected Anything That Great
Text:
We had been searching for these marvellous creatures for more than 3 hours. The scenery was a-maz-ing and the anticipation & excitement would grow more and more with every sighting of fresh poo, every footprint, every track into and out of the jungle and every broken branch or tree pushed over BUT there is nothing NOTHING that can top seeing a creature happy and safe, free in an environment it's so perfectly suited to whilst being surrounded by creatures of it's own kind. I have seen a few elephants in my time but I have never been so blessed to see them in a National Park and see them visibly happy.  And then when we went to another place in the park we got to see them come out of the jungle in numbers so vast I had never expected such a sight.  I could have watched them for hours.   Brought to tears I was.

A valid mention also goes to the water buffalo and bird life a-plenty.

Title: Must visit....
Text: Place was teeming with wildlife... went late afternoon around 3pm.. we were driven in a Jeep. 3 hours just roaming around... be careful when u book. We knew we overpaid by at least 3 times. But the wildlife made up for it..

Title: Wild Elephants
Text:
Got to see lot many elephants.  It was raining heavily and many safari jeeps around. we saw many elephants from close range.

a very memorable elephant safari.  Enjoyed.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: Very nice trip to national park, almost four hours. I saw elephants, pickkoks, Egels, wild cows a lot of different birds. Yes it was very crowded almost 100 Jeeps was the same time in the park.

Title: Most uncomfortable rough ride ever
Text: Went on an evening safari to this National Park & had  the ost uncomfortable rough ride ever & saw very little wild life except elephants. We see more bird life on our balcony in Sydney! Not worth the money & discomfort.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text:
If you want to see lots of elephants and do not mind being surround by 50 other jeeps, you will be happy there.
Dont expect a real safari though where you rather discover animals, it is more that you are taken to main spot where most elephants are and that is it.
If you want to discover other animals you should tell the safari guide beforehand and choose one that decently speaks English and knows the animals and where to find them.
We also saw elephants bathing in the jungle river, axis dear, buffalo, monkeys, a lot of birds.

Title: elephants
Text: this wasnt really what we expected there were an awful lot of jeeps in this park and all converged on the lake to see lots of elephants , i counted 30 jeeps all surrounding the elephants ,we thought udawalawe was a more natural experience ,

Title: Adventurous tour
Text: Mainly there were elephants and few peacock and buffalos but going in a Jeep to see them and the view was a great experience

Title: Close up to the elephants
Text: Good jeep safari amongst the elephants. Really interesting with lots of photo opportunities. Buffalo and birds in the national park too. Really enjoyed the experience

Title: Be prepared for a lot of jeeps chaseing a herd of elephants
Text:
We collected our jeep at Cinnamon Lodge and were told iit was over 50 years old - well it felt that way driving around the park. You will see the occasional elephant whilst driving around and many birds but at the end all the jeeps converge on the lake to spot the herd of elephants. Almost 100 grazing along the banks unlike Africa where you will see smaller groups. Tour lasted almost 3 hours so good value for  money. Took so may photos, need to review on our return.

.
.

Title: Brilliant
Text:
Spent three hours one evening on safari.

The evening was well worth while because we saw lots of hers of elephants making their way to the lake. Amazing experience and not to be forgotten.

Title: great to see elephants relaxing in a natural environment
Text: wonderful opportunity to see herds of elephants behaving naturally, youngsters playing, adults supervising . fantastic photo opportunities

Title: Great safari!
Text: Quick and lots to see. Very manageable in a couple hrs. Good guides and lots of elephants, birds and sun!

Title: Absolutely incredible and the best place to see elephants in Sri lanka
Text:
We chose Kaudulla National Park because we met people a few days ealier that had a fantastic expereince.  

We arrived in Habanara by bus with our 3 children at about 2.30pm and a helpful tuk-tuk driver found us a cheap room then helped us find a jeep driver.

We paid 21,000 LKR for a 3-hour jeep ride from town.  We left at 3.30pm and arrived at the perfect time to see about 80 elephants grassing and bathing.  We also watched as they walked between all the jeeps to get to the fresh grass on the other side of us.  Utterly spectacular!

I know that some people have complained about all the jeeps, but there were a lot less here than at other parks that we considered.  We also know plenty of people who spent a lot of money at other parks and never saw Elephants at all.  So I think it's important to keep a perspective about the popularity of this park unless you have loads of money and can arrange a private tour somewhere else.

Title: Perhaps the best place to see elephants.
Text: We went on the jeep safari you couldn't really do it any other way it pretty rough tracks. You get to see so many elephants its so moving plus a raft of other birds, animals etc.  The guides choose the best park for the time of year and in Jnauary this was clearly the best. Watch out for the hoards of other jeeps though.

Title: Very crowded...
Text:
Before visiting Sri Lanka i made some research about where you can see the elephants in a natural enviroment. I found a lot of posts about Kaudulla and how it wasnt as crowded as the other places.

Man was i dissapointed, this was like a mayhem of jeeps. Perhaps 50-100 in a very small park stressing the elepgants out totally. It was like a safari in a zoo.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: An amazing afternoon spent in a jeep watching large herds of elephants going about their business of washing, eating and dusting themselves with their young, in the wild. At times they were as close as 3m away, it was very special.

Title: Fun jeep ride for the elephants
Text:
Great ride to see the elephants. The tracks are bumpy so hold onto your phones and don't place them in your lap! Very dusty with all the other jeeps driving around so wear sunnies and be prepared to get dirt on your face. 

I loved seeing the elephants around the lake but there are so so many other jeeps around it's a bit of a circus to get through. 

We saw beautiful elephants, peacocks, monkeys and some wildebeasts. Fun experience. 

The cars are jeeps with car seats welded onto the back ute, no seat belts required. Hilarious but fun!

Title: Just great for seeing the elephants
Text:
We had a two hour jeep safari, which actually lasted an extra 30 minutes. It is the elephants you come to see. Our tour started at 1.15pm and we were a little concerned that this was the wrong time to do this. There were only 4/5 other jeeps out with us so it was not crowded in the vast plains. 

We were not disappointed as the elephants were there in large numbers, including a baby elephant only a week old. There must have been 30/40 elephants together.
It was fascinating and we were able to get pretty close, which was good as we had left our binoculars behind at the hotel!

When we finished and returned back to base at 3.45pm there were loads and loads of jeeps and tourists getting ready to leave. Far far too many. We were so pleased that we had gone out at 1.15pm.

We also saw some birdlife, including some eagles which were very impressive.  But it is all about the elephants.

Title: Nice gathering of elephants
Text: We went on a safari jeep to this park because the jeep owners all said they elephants could be sighted only at Kaudulla and not at Minneriya this time of the year - probably they already saw them. The road was extremely bumpy and we did spot a crocodile, a peacock and an eagle on our way. Very close to a water body, in a large open space there were about a hundred elephants, including little ones. they were busy grazing; not sure if they were bothered by the presence of so many jeeps. A little distance from them was a herd of water buffalos, also grazing. NIce to see the animals in the wild.

Title: Wonderful experience
Text: Elephants by the hundred lots of rare birds and a safari experience do die for. Good for couples or families. See nature at ease

Title: Wonderful Safari
Text: It was amazing safari in kaudulla national park. We saw many wild elephants and many wild animals. Memorable experience in sri lanka

Title: Too many elephants to count
Text: There are 2 national parks in the area.  At the time of our visit this was the best to visit to see elephants as the other park had too much water therefore not enough grassland for grazing.  Worth the trip.. absolutely.  Yes there are a lot of jeep safaris doing the same thing, but they all seemed to be doing the right thing. We got excited at the sight of the first single elephant only to go around the corner to see herd after herd, probably in excess of 300.

Title: Jeep safari for enthusiastic family
Text:
We took a jeep from a company I wouldnt recommend - Atika.....comfortable jeep but the driver did not engage with us at all, was on his phone at times, and when we made a request to stay longer than 90 mins he had a paddy. He drove fast and returned to same group of elephants we had just seen.
I have been on some African Safaris and there is much more respect shown the animals. I wonder if there is any control on the number of jeeps at any one time.
We enjoyed the animals and birds and hope the NP put in something to respect the animals.

Title: Lots of Elephants indeed
Text: But also lots of people (jeeps) so dont expect africa safari style. But surely nice to see the elephants, specially during sundown with the whole family.

Title: So many elephants
Text: Wow! We loved our safari here, we saw so many elephants and the park wasnt busy. Our driver Chandla was fantastic with our son. An extremely memorable afternoon.

Title: An elephant heaven
Text: What a fabulous afternoon. Best to book a tour early afternoon as when we were leaving around 4.30, there was a massive queue of jeeps coming the other way, evidently to miss the heat. We did this through our hotel, the Vaana Resort and were picked up from there. Around 200 elephants out and about wallowing in the lake with 2 tusked and lots of babies. Boy, theyve really got their work/life balance sorted!

Title: Hundreds of elephants!!
Text: Just breathtaking! Elephants of every size as far as the eye could see.  The journey by jeep isnt all that comfortable as the track leaves a certain amount to be desired but our jeep was skilfully and carefully driven and our backs survived the ordeal! What s memorable afternoon.

Title: elephant capital of Sri Lanka
Text: Kaudulla was the first safari of our Sri Lanka trip. we met our driver and started the safari. the moment we started our jeep to leave, i saw 3 Malabar pied hornbills fly. the hornbills landed and we ran out of our jeep. the hornbills jumped around until they sat for a minute before flying. we made our way into the park. we arrived at the park and heard a call. we looked on a tree and found a juvenile crested hawk eagle. soon after that we saw a nest of Asian predatory wasps. we went to a lake and saw an Indian roller at the top of a tree. we we saw many painted storks and even many of the rare lesser adjutant stork. after that right next to the lake we saw another jeep that had broken down for 2 hours. we helped them but they couldn't do anything. our driver was  about to give up and turned right and saw an elephant at the lake. we immediately drove there. we looked at the elephant for 30 minutes. we drove away and saw a peacock dancing until an elephant chased it away. after that we saw 2 elephants fighting from far away. after that that we saw a male elephant that pooped and peed before walking away. after that we drove to an area where many jeeps were. then we saw gray big rocks there from fa. we went close and saw 30 elephants. our driver was good, however, another jeep got in between a mother and a 5 day old calf. the elephants started trumpeting. we were late as the park closes at 5 pm. we got out of the park at 5:30 pm. on the way back we saw our elephants cross the road.

Title: So many elphants
Text: We did an afternoon safari here and yes there were an awful lot of other jeeps, and it didn't feel like you were out exploring the world on your own or anything but seeing so many elephants in their own environment was amazing really great experience.

Title: top for elephants
Text: we have been in this park because it is very easy to watch free elephants. we were satisfied as we saw 50 elephants busy in their daily chores. even families with children. depending on the season you could be diverted to the nearby minneriya nation park. the opposite happened to us but there are no problems as the elephants move freely between the two parks depending on the rains. your guide will suggest you the best.

Title: An excellent experience ..
Text:
Yes it indeed was....
Bumpy roads,offroad driven trips being soo closer to hundreds of ginormous friends is not a very common experience and must add it was a very pleasant one for my family and me
If you go in the everything you can see almost all the elephants around the lake..
And the chances are high to find nice peacocks and very many birds too

Title: Plenty of Elephants - Recommended
Text: My two young daughters wanted to see Elephants and plenty of Elephants they saw. We saw 3 seperate herds near the lakes edge including baby Elephants. We entered the park at about 1.45pm and within 10mins came across the first herd. Had a big bull come pretty close to the jeep we had to get out fast. We drove about 5mins more and came across another herd approx 40-50 Elephants. At that time I counted 12 jeeps. After 45mins of watching various groups within the herd we moved off. There were more jeeps arriving. We found the third herd approx 30 Elephants not far away and we were the only jeep at that time. Some of the bigger Elephants came up to the jeep only 10ft away, a little scary but wandered past, then more jeeps arrived. We also saw Water Buffalo, Eagles, Monkeys & a snake in a tree. We spent approx 2hrs in the park, well worth it and saw more Elephants than expected.

Title: brilliant
Text:
Practical tips:-
- the elephants migrate between different parks so hopefully your driver will find out which park will have the best viewings 
- our driver organised the tour with a local company. we were charged 55 US  dollars each which includes the entrance fee and jeep 
- we went at approximately 3.30pm. There was a bit of a queue to go in but it wasn't too bad. It did start raining heavily at the start.
- it is very bumpy. We found it easier to stand.
- there is a toilet at the beginning. Obviously you can't use the toilet once the safari has started. 
- we saw around 400 elephants. We were so close to them, it was amazing. They seemed really calm and undisturbed by us. Saw a group of them going to cool down in the water. 
-it does get very hot so take plenty of drinks and also cover your head to protect from the sun.

Title: Worth a visit !
Text: Amazing safari !  Really enjoy the trip - to be  surrounded by elephants and managed to see them pretty close up.  Real experience in Sri Lanka :)

Title: 200+ wild elephants.
Text: We paid 5000 for our driver and jeep and 2500 each to go into the park. Best time to go is after 2pm. There may have been a lot of other jeeps but it didn't detract from the elephants. You easily got loads of photos without jeeps and there were even a few jeeps making a rapid get away as elephants charged them (no real danger though). Check out the photos.

Title: Absolutely amazing with lots to see ..
Text:
Yes the drive is bumpy but this adds to the fun. We loved it.
Saw loads of elephants as well as many other animals including water buffalo, eagles, egrets, painted storms, peligan, elephant stork and loads more.

Strongly recommend.

Title: Dont get too excited
Text:
OK so they call these rough vehicle trips SAFARI, but they are not great.
You do have a good chance to see a large group of Elephants, if little else.
Worth your money...not really.

Title: A very bumpy ride, lots of birds and lots of elephants
Text: Our 4x4 drive jeep was VERY bumpy as the roads are very, very rutted but in the end I felt it was worthwhile just to see a very large herd of elephants of all ages including a couple of males facing up to each other over a female with he big lad chasing away the younger male. The winner's wee offspring seemed very pleased with his, I presume, dad when the latter returned. We were surrounded by 4x4 jeeps so it is hardly a quiet safari. lots of birds but little other mammal wildlife apart from the odd monkey. A few goanas by the side of the "road" ignored us. We did see some impressive sea eagles.

Title: More Elephants than I Could Count
Text: I was a bit skeptical of the safari beforehand, particularly given the number of vehicles all heading the same way. However, once we got through the first 10 mins to get to the lake we saw loads and loads of elephants all making their way through the park. There were a lot of other tourists but our driver was good at getting us to a position so that we were close enough to take pictures and feel away from the crowd. He also managed to take us around the lake to an area with no other vehicles where we saw a group of 6 elephants by themselves. There were plenty of other animals and birds to see but the elephants are the main attraction.

Title: Just Elephants & a lot of Rain!
Text: We had to book a jeep for the national park safari, as cabs are not allowed inside the park. The jeep was open roof and we enjoyed the ride. There were no animals in sight and we started wondering if it was a right decision to pay that amount of entrance fees and come here. Unexpectedly it started raining and we hastened to pull up the waterproof cover over the jeep and got completely drenched in the process. It was fun. Soon we came up to a place which was crowded by other jeeps, only to discover a herd of elephants ahead. The rain soon started coming down in full force. Even though we were enjoying the sight of elephants, I am not totally sure how much the elephants were actually enjoying. The jeeps seems to have surrounded them from all possible directions and they seemed to be stuck between the river and the jeeps. They seemed to be confused in which direction to move, because they kept changing directions. But soon their leader got them going and the heard soon disappeared from sight.

Title: Many elephants
Text: Instead of visiting elephant orphanage I decided to take a jeep safari to this place. A unique experience to observe elephants in their natural habitats, you can feel that they are at home there and we were just visiting. Quite crowded with many jeeps.

Title: So many wild elephants !
Text: We paid 5000 rps for a 2 hour keep safari of the park. This included the entrance price and also a guide. We mainly saw many types of birds and very soon came across a whole herd of elephants - around 30 of them! What a beautiful site it was. There were quite a few other jeeps around but only really noticeable when we reached the elephants- they were otherwise pretty distant. I preferred this safari over yala as its not so busy and I much prefer elephants to leopards.

User_Location: New Forest National Park Hampshire, United Kingdom
Title: A jeep car park...
Text: We were really looking forward to seeing the elephants again after a great experience in Uda walawe NP. We were told Kaudulla NP was the place to go over Minneriya NP as this was where the elephants were. So we went off in a jeep and basically joined everyone else... the poor elephants were so encroached upon. It felt more like a zoo car park than a safari. The kids loved riding in the open top jeeps but thats about as good as it got. Something has got to be done to manage the NP. Its only a small area for a NP and we left feeling a little sad for the elephants. Not sure we could recommend especially if you have a chance to see elephants elsewhere.

Title: Elephant Spotting
Text: We went here one afternoon to see some elephants in their natural habitat. We got picked up from our hotel, had a good few hours driving around the park and then got dropped back to our hotel. We only saw three elephants, however that is no criticism of the park. Anyway, we did see a lot of other interesting wildlife as well. We would rather risk not seeing any elephants in their natural surroundings than go to an elephant sanctuary where they are chained up for the majority of their lives. Seemed to be a lot of jeeps there, many more than we were expecting. That was the only issue we had as it spoilt the views of the park.

Title: Very nice safari
Text: Good alternative to mineriya where there are less jeeps and more elephants to see per tourist. Long loop with good trails. Lots of elephants plus peacocks kingfisher monkey etc

Title: Excellent place to see elephants in their natural habitat
Text: We went in a jeep safari and saw many animals and even babies with their mothers. It is must visit in Sri lanka.

Title: Elephants Galore
Text: A game drive in Kaudulla proved to be one of the highlights of my trip to Sri Lanka. Arrival at the park did not look promising, with countless safari vehicles and heaps of people coming and going. Once inside the park, the mayhem ceased and we could enjoy the nature. After a pleasant drive through woodland, the road emerged to a huge grassy plain with a lake in to distance. It turns out, the entire plain is underwater during the wet season, which explained the muddy tracks we had to negotiate. At first, all we saw were birds and domestic cows but that quickly changed. Over the course of our game drive, we saw over 200 elephants in several herds, including a number of calves. Despite all the vehicles, there wasn't any crowding, with each vehicle allowing ample time for observation, often at very close range. Even in four trips to Africa, I have never seen so many elephants in one place. Don't miss it!

Title: Fun Elephant-spotting Safari
Text:
Animal lover that I am, this was my favourite experience of our trip to Sri Lanka, despite being very unlucky and only actually spotting a pair of distant elephants in the park. 

We arrived at the park from Polonnaruwa for the afternoon safari starting at 2.30 pm.
We were a little overwhelmed by the swarm of jeeps (apparently up to 400 are allowed in the park at any point), but as soon as he could, our driver turned away from the pack, took the roof off and set off into the trees. It was amazing fun to drive along standing on the seats looking out over the roof of the jeep. 

Our guide and the driver were experts at spotting all sorts of birds (including a pair of lesser adjutant stork which are quite rare, and a pair of eagles) and wildlife. He was extremely patient, stopping and approaching as close as he could for us to take pictures. 

When it became clear that we would not spot any elephants inside the park, our driver took us out onto the main road to track down a family of elephants at their regular spot. I wish he hadn't in the end as my heart broke when I saw mama elephant eating paper litter :( :(

Title: Elephant safari
Text:
This was the best trip for us (me especially as elephants are my favourite animal!). We were picked up from our hotel in the jeep and it didn't take long to get there. 

When we arrived our driver put the hood down on the jeep and pointed out various things of interest along the way......wasps nest (huge!)/monkeys/deer/birds until we reached a family of elephants. What an amazing privilege to see them in their natural habitat. I thought that was it but we carried on through the park and met up with a herd of at least 50. Some of the babies were only a few weeks old. How protective they are their young shielding them from our prying cameras. It was quite emotional. We did not feel rushed and stayed for about an hour just mesmerised by the herd. 
If you get a chance to visit this part I would definitely recommend it. We also visited an elephant orphanage earlier in the week and there were stark differences in both but equally fabulous.

Title: Incredible pachyderms
Text:
The visit to Kaudulla was sensational. Our driver and guide superb. Driving to the grass plain took us along a winding road, and during that time we came upon a protective mother. She instinctively charged our vehicle, however it was more show than anything. We weren't to know that - cowering in the back of the truck. When we entered the main grass plain we were surprised with close to two hundred elephants all hanging around chomping on grasses. We were told that three herds usually come together just before dusk, but we were very lucky in the fact that it was only midday. How majestic and calm they all were. Amazing!

So much wildlife in this park. Water buffalo, eagles, monkeys, painted storks...

We were a little horrified when departing the national park, as there were over one hundred vehicles in or driving into the park. The young lads I was with counted them!

Please make sure that if you get the chance to get out of your vehicle, to pick up at least three pieces of plastic. I made a quick pick-up of about fifty pieces in a ten by five metre area at the edge of the lake.

Title: Jumbos and Jumbos.
Text:
Perfect place to get closer to elephants. 
You ll see a herd of 50-60 jumbos. 

On the other hand I felt the jeeps are going too close, violating territory of wild life.

Title: Great nature
Text: We reallt wanted to see elephants in the wild. We have seen the lot, but always ik capture. We din't get dissapointed. Go arround 14.00 hour and you see big groups of elephants at the lake. Go earlyer and you dont die by the heat. So make your choice. We seen more then just the elephant and i think a trip to this park is big add on your vacation.

Title: Wow!
Text: Kaudulla greatly exceeded expectations !  It was a bumpy but lovely ride in from the highway through forests where we spotted many birds, deer and a small crocodile on the way to the park .  When we got to an open grassy plain with a large lake nearby -in a steady drizzle - we spotted a few elephants at the edge of the dense forest. Once the rain quit ..... the elephants came out to eat, wander and goof around!  We counted two groups of about 40 animals and a third group of 20 and various strays . There were many Other Jeeps present but everybody stood off a bit and let these majestic animals attend to their business if eating drinking and socializing .  It was a day that will be with me the rest of my life!

Title: Lovely day
Text: Even though it was cold and raining torrentially, I really enjoyed the safari. There were groups of elephants strolling about and even more jeeps clustered around the elephant families. Don't expect to see more than elephants on a jeep off-road ride and you'll leave satisfied.

Title: Safari
Text:
Just a short ride from Habanara this is an easy 4 hour package where you'll get lots of close encounters with elephants. The driver knew where to find them and constantly positioned us in perfect spots to watch and photograph. It's a bumpy ride in the jeeps so be warned! 

Visit Rana's Travel shop in Habarana to arrange it rather than use your hotel as it will be much cheaper. See reviews of his services.

Title: Elephants!
Text: Went on this Jeep Safari. Was our first time on a safari! Was exciting.. would have been happy if we saw more than just elephants. But nevertheless it was a memorable experience! Such peaceful animals! Until one actually started chasing the keeps away!

Title: Such an amazing experience
Text: Our trip to Kaudulla was wonderful! After searching for about half an hour we stumbled across a group of approx 100 elephants, including lots of little ones some only a few days old. We were able to watch them from our jeep, as they moved around us and ate. We then moved on to another group, again of more than 100. This was so special seeing them in a natural environment, and all the jeep drivers and tourists seemed very respectful of the elephants too. Make sure you check with a local which national park they'll be in as they move freely between this and Minneriya park.

Title: Oodles of Elephants!
Text: We visited Kaudulla yesterday and it was amazing seeing all the elephants!  There were a herd of about 50 and we were able to observe them from very close.  It was amazing to be able to see them graze and interact.  There was a pregnant female in the herd as well as a tiny baby elephant!  We were absolutely awed by their beauty.  We did the evening safari, after 3 pm when we saw them.  We also see peacocks, crocodiles, a hornets nest and eagles!

Title: Amazing herds of elephants with babies
Text:
Fabulous trip organised from guesthouse.
Picked up and taken to where the herds had migrated to in the parks.

Spent a couple hours just watching the elephants.

Jeeps kept to the roads and are only supposed to park on sode of road to preserve the grass.

The elephants seem to like grazing near the roads instead of at a distance which was great.

Baby elephants everywhere!

We tipped the drivers at the end for a good job done.

Title: Wonderful, just what we hoped
Text: My wife Julie had said before that all she wanted to do was to see an elephant up close & in the wild. Well we saw 2 different herds and her day was made when the huge bull elephant in charge of the first herd turned and walked past our jeep at a distance of less than 30 yards.... lots of pictures. Saw some buffalo and birds, but its the elephants that you go for. Apparently there are crocodiles and rumoured to be leopards, but I think you would be exceptionally lucky to see these. Dont be put off that there are dozens of jeeps as the animals ignore them.  Great couple of hours

Title: Jeep safari
Text: We did a Jeep safari with Akita safari.  The Jeep was comfortable and the driver was an excellent animal spotter.  The elephants were amazing about 100 of them at the water hole.  The only draw back was there were at least 40 jeeps all watching the elephants.  Some of them people were noisy and not respectful of the animals.  We went at 2 oclock and it was very crowded.  Our driver did a good job of anticipating which way the elephants were going to move.  Takes three to four hours and the road is very bumpy.

Title: great experience wonderful to see elephants in their natural habitat
Text: We travelled with a fellow called Asana in a real 4 wheel drive vehicle (unlike most others which were regular 2 wheel drive jeeps) - just the two of us. Asana knew exactly where the elephants were. We left early - 1.30 -  2.00 pm found the elephants a herd of over 80, watched them emerging from the jungle for their afternoon feed. We were there with one other jeep - it was magical and then, completely spoiled after jeep after jeep arrived - there would have been over 30 jeeps there in the end. We had had enough left early too to go and look at different birds in the park and spot a crocodile.  Our guide Asana knew so much about the elephants and wildlife - he was respectful in his approach and not a cowboy as we drove through the plains to get to the elephants.  He was also very knowledgable and told a lot about elephants, how to identify then as a male and female, breeding etc. I don't think Asana advertises widely - our driver organised for him to take us - I do have a photo of his phone number which i can send on request.

Title: ELEPHANTS
Text: I was staying in Polonnaruwa and through my hostel did a jeep tour here to see the elephant gathering. I visited in late August which is a good time from what I gather. I saw a ton of elephants, more than the rest of my life combined. I wasn't the only one as there was a few dozen jeeps here but it all still worked out to have great views of the elephants while not really interfering with them. If you want to see lots of elephants I'd recommend a tour of here.

Title: Great day out
Text: We went on this trip with our guide we had for the week ( feb 18) .we went out in a jeep with a local guide , jeep sizes vary we were only 2 in back of ours .The tracks are abit rough so be prepared to bounce around abit , but thats part of it ! We did see alot of widelife , crocodiles in the river at the start , varity of birds , monkeys , water buffalo but the best bit was seeing all the Elephants, we sat for couple hours watching them swim , fight and play there was around 150  Elephants it was lovely to see. If your in this area put this on the list .

Title: Elephant safari - plenty of them
Text:
This was a spur of the moment safari and glad we did.

Cost of this was £55 for 2 people and we were told that in Feb this was a good park to visit for the elephants.

We had a great guide, new all about the wildlife and birds names and seemed to really care about the animals. He came from United Jeep Safari in Habarana (0773155044). All vehicles here are 4 wheel drive

Word of caution - you have to shut out of your mind the number of jeeps around literally dozens, all doing the same thing in the same direction.

There are lots of elephants and when you see them all of the jeeps congregate around. We were fortunate to get a great view of them crossing the river.

Title: Expect lots of elephants and a bumpy ride!
Text:
Our driver recommended us this national park as we are on the way from Negombo to Sigiriya. And true enough, yes, there are many elephants and baby elephants in this national park. There were also peacocks, eagles, many types of birds, crocodile and some monkeys. 

We got a guide who helped us spot many animals amongst the bushes. It costs us USD 60 each (not sure if we got ripped off as this was not part of our itinerary). We also managed to get up close to some elephants and baby elephants. They didnt seem to be bothered by our presence - could be because they are used to humans. 

Overall, really good visit and worthwhile! Expect a really bumpy ride as there are many potholes on the road. 

(All photos taken by iPhone)

Title: Lots of beautiful elephants
Text:
Took an afternoon safari here after our guide told us that the safari guides said they were seeing more elephants here than Minneriya NP. Reading online it appears that the elephants mi e along corridors between parks. 
We reached the first group and counted about 60, including some babies.
Also spotted some beautiful birds! 
Moved along and another group came in to view! A similar number and we got closer!  Wonderful afternoon, leaving the park at 6pm with so many photographs!

Title: Great wildlife, terrible roads
Text: We were delighted to get up close to a herd,of,over seventy elephants and see a wide range of birds on our safari. However, be aware that the roads are horrendous and the journey to and from the wildlife is an ordeal particularly for anyone with a bad back.

Title: Massive herd of Elephants
Text: We had a fabulous guide who pointed out many different birds and stopped numerous times to let us take pictured and also very informative. The highlight was a herd of 100+ elephants which we watched with fascination. There were a few bull elephants and some very young calves. Great afternoon and first visit to a wild life park.

Title: More safari jeeps than elephants
Text: There was a herd of about 80 elephants (only about 5% of SriLankan elephants have tusks) at the lake, with about 120 head of cattle grazing next to them but what was the most amazing sight was the 100 odd safari vehicles lined up in a straight line watching the elephant. The roads in the park are attrocious but there are other animals such as water buffalo, and peacocks abound showing off their plumage.

Title: So many elephants
Text:
We visited the park with a local safari company 'kalum jeep safari hababara' 
He timed our visit so we got to see a huge group of elephants close to before other trucks heard about them. The park is full of wildlife.  Lots of birds, gekos, even spotted an alligator. 
Roads are bumpy as you'd expect. 
Great place to see elephants.

Title: Wonderful elephant viewing
Text: Amazing trip here by jeep.  We saw hundreds of elephants that were close enough to really enjoy.  Definitely worth coming.

Title: Elephants
Text: Brilliant afternoon. Elephants in abundance as well as birds, monkeys, crocodiles, Jackals to name a few. We had a truly magical trip and to see the babies was a utter joy.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: Many elephants to see mainly around the lake area.  The number of bird species was well worth investing in some binoculars.

Title: Loads of elephants.....loads of jeeps
Text:
Went in to the park despite misgivings about numbers of people in jeeps in a massive queue. Enjoyed it overall, saw 100+ elephants in our late afternoon trip starting about 15:00. That's your reason to go, right there. Didn't see that much else, but there are some good birds there, even for the casual twitcher (big eagles, brightly coloured bee-eaters, etc).

Downside? Absolutely wacky races. I jest not, at one point we saw 60+ elephants in a group, and there were 30+ jeeps in a group watching them, jostling for position. The good news is that the wildlife ignored us completely, but it feels "odd" to me. The only safari I've done before was in Tanzania which was empty of other vehicles. All the drivers want their clients to have the best photo (= bigger tip for them), which doesn't help. If you can ignore this, it's good fun.

The tracks were hard and massively bumpy, so expect to get thrown around a lot and pick up a few bruises - all part of the experience, (unless you're frail!)

Title: A wonderful sight to behold
Text: Lovely to see so many elephants in the wild , enjoying "family" getogethers by the lake.  Baby elephants running round playing and making a nuisnce of themselves with the adults

Title: For elephants lovers
Text: it was my first time on a jeep safari to wildlife park, the area is huge!Great experience to embrace the nature. Not a wide variety of animals to spot though, main highlight is the big herd of elephants. If you're a big fan of these jungle jumbo, this is the place for you.

Title: Great for elephants
Text: A great place to see elephants but lot of vehicles. Lots of bird life and small mammals. Big area so you can get away from the majority of other vehicles. Beware of charging elephants!!!

Title: Best place to see wild Elephants in their natural habitat
Text: We had a very good safari in Kaudulla National Park. Saw nearly 100 odd elephants in 5 groups. This looks like a sure shot place to see these majestic creatures in their habitat. Worth a visit if you have time.

Title: Great park for a safari
Text: Nice park with lots of animals, but not many tourists. Plenty of buffalos, wild pigs, deer, we also saw foxes, mongoose and an elephant. Myriad of birds, any bird lover will be thrilled.

Title: A beautiful little gem and oh so peaceful!
Text: This is one of the hidden delights of Sri Lanka - a very special place with lots of wildlife and gorgeous scenery!

Title: Beautiful park with a lot of wildlife
Text: Kumana national park is also called Yala East. It is a lot smaller than Yala and much less crowdy. We booked in Arugam Bay and paied 5000 LKR each, which included everything: entrance fee, 4x4 and driver/guide. You stay in the park for about 4 hours. We were lucky and saw all kinds of animals among which elephants and even a leopard.

Title: Amazing!
Text:
Did an afternoon safari (seems more common than morning).  Left at 1:30pm and came back at 7:30pm.  We saw too many animals to list here!  The only one we didn't see is the leopard.  The road to the park was very dusty.  Bring binoculars.
July 15th 2019, the standard price was 4300-4500SRL per person for shared safari or 16000SRL if you want to hire a private vehicule(both peice include everything: guide, entrance fee, etc).

Title: Grate place for family trip
Text: We visited the park one week ago, and I can tell you that it was great. We are luckly enough to take our road, and we travel through the park along with our friendly ranger. The animals were so cute and amazing.

Title: Collected indelible amazing experience
Text: This is a bounty of nature indeed! Wonderful place where you can collect lots of experience with respect to extremely rare  types of colorful birds, animals reptiles etc.  Compare to other national parks in Sri Lanka, Kumana is a calm and quiet place where you can enjoy the unique fascinating beauty of the nature intact till now. The safari guide provide by the wild life office had also done his best to make us understand the nature of the place, birds, animals, and its persistence under the thorough control of the wild life department.

Title: Visit to Kumana National Park
Text: Such a beautiful scenic jungle with a variety of animals, birds and reptiles. One can enjoy the park as it is not spoilt with too many visitors and vehicles. Roaming animals have their freedom and we can enjoy the viewimg them in their Marital habitat. People of the country has to value these without dumping their rubbish out of their vehicles as plastics can be seen around and feel sorry. Authorities must take more care about the people who stay overnight in those rented bungalows with stringent rules requesting them to take their own rubbish out as they dump their alcohol empty bottles out in the beach and under the trees. Animals have left their foot prints only on the sand, beach and its so admirable while people leave their rubbish in a vergin jungle having a brain to think that it does not decay for centuries. Enjoy the view of the nature and leave nothing other than the type marks.

Title: Jungle Safari
Text: We took a Jeep Safari with Terrel Berenger  (Terrel Residences in Ampara) to the park with hopes of seeing elephants.  We were at the right place (we saw feesh signs), but the timing was not right on that day.  Regardless, we had an interesting ride in the jungle and saw birds, monkeys, and a beautiful lake.

Title: Touted to be better than Yala
Text: We Visited kumana national park on recommendation by the owners at Hideaway resort. Paid about SGD 40 per person for the jeep(shared with a british couple) and abit more for the entrance fee at the park. There is a concentration of wildlife at the park entrance and then on its mostly birds. Left for the park at arnd 1pm from arugam bay and it seemed abit disappointing at first as it was mostly birds and buffalos. However in the short period of time (probably the last hour before sundown, there is a burst of wildlife around the waterholes. We were lucky, saw spotted deer crocodiles, jackals, elephants, a sloth bear walking alongside the jeep, and the elusive leopard which seemed to be stalking peacocks until the jeep approached to near and scared it away. a really fantastic experience for me and my girlfriend.

Title: "Lions and Tigers and .... -- Oh My!" Not in Sri Lanka, but here's what we did find...
Text: I pleasant, late afternoon adventure by safari jeep (operated by Dulip Kokuhannadige for Surf n Sun in Arugam Bay) meant that we saw more wildlife than most safari experiences. We took along our 6 year old granddaughter to view the event and we were delightfully rewarded with sighting elephants, crocodiles, iguanas, monkeys, a fox, a civet and Junglefowl (the national bird), Spoonbills and eagles abound. Sadly, the leopard alluded us this visit as did the bear. Next time....

Title: I have had trip jungle of yala and arugambay and they will support us bot safari and see plain also.
Text: I wold like all of my trip with them,and also always arrange my food in side the kumana national park,also had good way back to monty hotel.

Title: Beautiful wildlife park
Text: We made a 6-hours safari in the national park in a jeep with a Sri Lankan driver. We saw all we wanted to see (elephants, leopard, deers...) even if there was a pilgrimage crossing the park. Really great moment!

Title: We we unlucky
Text:
I think we were the unlucky ones that didn't get to see groups of elephants which is all we wanted to see. We saw one elephant in the far distance and then one elephant in the bushes and one outside the park heading to the beach. Everyone else I spoke to that had done this tour said they saw loads of elephants.
There were lots of water buffulo and deers plus we saw some crocodiles towards the end. Oh and lots of peacocks plus monkeys at one stop.  Need to take a good camera. Prices to vary a bit we paid 5,500 LKR per person  including jeep and entry.

Title: A great safari with EcoWave Travels
Text: We went on safari with Ecowave (based in Arugam Bay). It was so good!! We went in the morning and saw elephants, water buffalo, deer etc. There's lots of birds because of the lagoons. Such a gorgeous place and we were the only visitors - didn't see any other jeeps at all. Our guide was able to answer the endless questions I had about the animals and the park. We had breakfast by the birds information centre.

Title: Loved it!
Text: We went in the afternoon and saw tons of wildlife and no other jeeps! The scenery was stunning too. Would definitely recommend. Just make sure to bring food and water with you and wear comfortable clothes; it's a long time in a car!

Title: Worth talking about
Text: They are the best camping outfit in SL and their understanding of the National Parks, the flora and fauna within is fantastic. Highly recommend them

Title: A place to go
Text: We spent a day inside Kumana national park with a safari driver. It was not that dry due to wet days in the previous days. We were lucky enough to watch lot of birds. There were few elephants close to the road. We enjoyed watching dancing peacocks everywhere. Thanks to safari driver and park guide, we had a wonderful day.

Title: Amazing bird life at Kumana
Text: We spent the day with by brothers and a friend of ours. It was a pretty dry time of the year and we were lucky enough to see a couple of elephants and lots of Bird life.

Title: Great camping experiance
Text:
We did camping in Kumana last year. There are several camping sites inside the park. You need to reserve in advance through the Department of Wild Life.

You have a great chance to see leopard and lot of elephants. Kumana is popular for bird watching. There are hundreds of varieties of birds. Safari Jeeps need to be booked form private suppliers. But not mandatory to book in advance. There are lot available in Panama area. It is difficult to reach park entrance by a car because road is not in good conditions. Vehicle with high ground clearance recommended.

Title: Wow!!! Do not miss this park
Text: This park is amazing. We did 3 safaris while in Sri Lanka, they were all great but and this was our favourite. The park was so quiet, we only saw one other jeep the whole afternoon, which was so refreshing after our busy safari at Kaudulla NP. The animals were abundant and so much variety. We saw elephants, buffalo, spotted deer, mongoose, countless birds, crocodiles. The only thing we weren't lucky to see was a leopard, maybe next time. The park itself is well kept and had a variety of environments. We just loved it. Our guide had a good eye and pointed out lots of animals, unfortunately we didnt get his name, but his picture is below, he was lovely and tried really hard to spot a leopard for us. If your in the area and love animals do this safari.

Title: Impressive landscape and a variety of wildlife
Text:
I liked the park more than expected. We visited mid/end of September and saw lots of water buffaloes, deer, some elephants (one was really close and we could watch it for a while), crocodiles, monkeys, mungos and many colourful birds. Other groups even seemed to have spotted a leopard.
Also there were not too many Jeeps, at times it felt as if we were the only ones there.
Furthermore the landscape alone is just stunning and varies a lot throughout the park.
In my opinion Kumana is a great option for people who want to avoid the crowds and want to see some local fauna in their natural habitat, but do not necessarily need to see huge herds of elephants and see spotting leopards as a nice bonus and not as the main reason to visit the park.

Title: Incredible and exceeded all expectations
Text: I was expecting this to be mainly birds but we were about 5 metres from a leopard, saw crocodiles and such an excellent range of birds. Really quiet when we went, around 6am, with hardly another car in sight.Highly, highly recommended.

Title: Thrilling Safari
Text:
Started our safari around 1.30 pm and main target was to see leopard & bear. From Panama to park entrance is about 45 min as the roads are bumpy and unsealed.
After paying entrance fee we were joined by a tracker - Chanaka who had a good knowledge and an eagle eye to look for animals. Within half an hour we were thrilled to see a leopard under a tree. In two seconds he slowly disappeared into bushes.
Guaranteed sight in KNP is water buffaloes, Spotted deer, wild fox and wild pigs. Saw a crocodile resting on the bank.
Bird information centre  where there is a tower overlooks the lagoon is the best place to watch birds. Fantastic info about different kind of birds on the walls at lookout point. Even though KNP is rich in bird life and most popular bird sanctuary in SL, we saw only few of them. Green bee eaters are commonly seen.
Road conditions inside the park is much better than Yala NP. Better to start early morning or mid afternoon. 
On our way back saw a leopard in the treetop. As it was getting dark, didn't see him clearly. 
Well worth 4.5 hrs drive. Will be back to see bears and more birds later !!

Title: Great park! Arugam Bay Khan safari overpriced
Text:
The park: Had a great variety of animals. We saw jungle fowl, mongoose, wild boars, peacocks galore, samba and spotted deer, buffallo, monkeys, crocodiles and elephants. It wasn't very crowded, maybe 4 other jeeps were spotted. Gorgeous mangrove area with lookout point. Very interesting trees and birds. Best safari we had in Sri Lanka for variety of animals and sparsity of humans!
The tour: Our tour was organized through our accommodation and it was definitely overpriced! 160 000 LAKs for 2 people. I would have really loved seat belts for the drive to and from the park, the driver was speeding through the local streets and it was bumpy, was quite nervous at times. Once in the park, he respected the speed limits. Their was no guide included, and he was not able to answer any questions in english about the animals or park. He went outside of the jeep at one point and picked up large mushrooms and peacock feathers until a local park ranger caught him and he had to put them back. He kept intimidating the elephants, even after we repeatedly asked to keep moving as we didn't want to scare them (we understand when it's for our safety if a lone male elephant shows signs of aggressivity, but this one was not). Finally at the end he asked for a tip which we said was included in the price of the tour.

Title: Excellent place for bird watching and safari
Text: Lovely place to visit during the season. Can see thousands of different variety of non natiove birds flown from thousands of kilometers to have their summer holiday here in Kumana marshy lands. Do not forget to carry a binoculars if you want to watch the birds seriously. Beautiful drive in a 4 wheel drive through waterways. Lots of Elephants,Lepords, deer, Elk,Water Buffolows. It was a fantastic journey with a very good tracker and the park office you get loads of information about its habitat. Can visit the "Kuda Kabilittha", devalaya too on this visit.

Title: Beautiful and quiet park
Text: Kumana National Park is well worth a visit if you are in Arugam Bay. The park is about one hour drive from Arugam Bay. We saw elephants even before we entered the park and the drive to the park was really beautiful. We saw many big crocodiles, deer, water buffalo, birds, elephants, rabbit and in the end we also saw a leopard crossing the road in front of us! That made the safari. The nature in the park is very beautiful and quiet, we only saw three other jeeps so we pretty much felt we were alone in the park. Well worth the money it costs (and you can make good deals in Arguam Bay)!

Title: Full with wildlife
Text: Beautiful park with a lot of wildlife. The road to the park is already beautiful. You can do this strech with a scooter (though there are big elephants present!) or tuktuk and can see everything except maybe the leopard. But the park is worth the extra money. Scenery is very nice. Many birds, eliphants, crocodiles, fox, deer and many more. We saw within 10 minutes a big leopard.

Title: A pleasant afternoon
Text: We found a budget friendly jeep and drove to the park. Before we entered we already saw monkeys and crocs. At the entrance we paid additional 2000 rupees each (4 persons). Inside we saw jackals, birds, deer, buffalos, wild boar, more crocodiles and a huge elephant. We drove pretty close to it, i would say at about 50 meters. Of course we didn't see any leopards or bears, as they are really hard to spot. You can also see marshes, lagoons and a dry zone vegetation. That was something for the eye. The road is extremely bad, so prepare for a bumpy ride.

Title: Awesome road trip to the remote areas
Text: Visited the national park after the arugam bay trip!! The entire stretch of gravel road is filled with rare flowers and birds !! We were lucky to spot 4 big crocodiles waiting for their prey !!! Different kinds of crane with different colors!! Recommend to go on a jeep since the road is bumpy all the way !! We stopped at kudumbigala Rock where you could get a sky view of national park !!! Overall awesome place to have a road trip !!!!

Title: Many monkey and 4 leopards spotted
Text:
We went to Kumana on a morning drive from Arugam bay.
we were with only 4 people in the car so we had plenty of room.
Already when we arrived at the entrance we were greeted by 10-30 monkeys.
Inside the park we saw a few elephants, some deer and 4 leopards.
Our guide heard the couple of leopards from the watch tower near the wetlands so we rushed to the car and found the leopards where he expected to find them.
Very worthwhile trip.

Title: great unspoiled park
Text: we were almost alone at the park. Though we did not see any leopards, we had the opportunity to watch crocodiles, elephants, special birds, water buffalos, pickocs and more. this is a different safari, at least at this time of the year (late september) because the park is almost empty from visitors. Very special opportunity to enjoy nature.

Title: Less tourists, lots of birds, very attractive scenery
Text:
We camped in the park which was great and although we did not see any Leopards we did see 3 sets of prints and narrowly missed seeing a bear (people in other car saw only minutes before).  The birds were amazing and a number of elephants, deer, boar, hare, buffalo etc.  
Could have spent much more time at the large waterhole than we had.  Well worth the visit if you are also going to other parks

Title: Leopard!
Text:
We came with a jeep from Arugam Bay which was pretty close and easy to arrange. 

We ended up seeing almost "all" the animals: even a leopard. The guide form the national park was great at spotting animals and pointing them out to us.

Great experience and very convenient.

Title: Don't go during July's pilgrimage
Text: We went on three game drives in Yala, and saw lots of animals and even a Leopard for a few seconds. We saw practically nothing in Kumana. My advice is don't even think about wasting your money during July/early August when the pilgrims are all marching right through the national park on their pilgrimage. They walk from Okanda through the park to Kataragama. All of the animals go into hiding. When we visited the park it was a few days after this, and all of the animals were still in hiding. We didn't even see an elephant grazing around. The mandatory guide they send along basically slept the while time and didn't bother looking for animals, so I added a photo of him sleeping. The safari's to Kumana from Arugam's Bay are far more expensive than the ones in Yala. However, we were the only jeep we saw all day, so it was much quieter than Yala. I would give it a go any other time of year though. We paid $100 for two people for a jeep. But we were quoted as much as $200.

Title: Kumana is the best but don't tell anyone!
Text: Oh my. We went here for Sloth bear and Leopard and were not disappointed. Its a bit of a drive to get here as we stayed at Arugum Bay so the drive is about 50 minutes but when we got here there was no one in the park and we hardly saw another vehicle in the whole of three days with six drives. One morning we spend 72 minutes with a leopard walking/sitting on rocks before it decided to get somewhere cooler to rest. No other vehicles! If you had been to Yala you would be lucky to get three minutes before another vehicles turns up. Did I mention the birds? Fantastic lagoons with wildlife everywhere. Owls, raptures etc.

Title: Very nice exploring the wild life
Text: Very good for kids, to see elephants on closeup view,  we chased the elephants and their babies, very nice to watch how they eat living in the wild free .the  provided car is fine you can stand and watch animals from car top .

Title: A great national park!
Text: Another great national park with more fantastic wildlife elephants, buffalo and monkeys and plenty of birds.

Title: Brilliant experience
Text:
We booked a driver through our hotel costing 5000Lkr, he took us to the ticket office and for the two of us i think it was around 10,000 Lkr.

It was around 3pm we got there and the park was very quiet, only two other jeeps going round which was brilliant as there were so many elephants around and we could all watch them without disturbance.

So hard to describe how amazing it is to see so many elephants in their natural habitat.

Definitely worth visiting

Title: Close and amazing encounter with large gathering of wild elephants - at Minneriya National Park
Text:
The best place to view the largest gathering of Asian elephants anywhere in the world. During our visit there were around 150+ elephants near the tank and this can increase to 300+ Elephants in the dry season to drink, bath and feed on the fresh grass from the lake bed. And also to socialize and to find mates. Cost of safari jeeps is around Rs3000-5000 plus park entry fees.   ( we hired our Jeep through the Aliya resort and it cost us Rs 5000 to pick up from the hotel (which includes 20 minutes drive to the park entry)) 
Jeep can accomodate up to 7-8 adults. 
Safari will take around 3-4 hours and start around 1-2pm. 
It was an amazing experience for all ages and you can get a very close encounter with these giants. This one of the must do in your Visit in Sri Lanka.

Title: lovely place
Text: lovely place, nature lovers should go there. you can see so many groups of elephants there it s pleasure to see real wild elephant in there natural environment

Title: Awesome experience
Text: We were hesitating wether to go or not as we read different reviews with diverging experiences.  I can definitely say it was worth the money and the time. We could see many herds of elephants including babies.  I'm sure we saw more than 150. The place is also very nice.

Title: Minneriya National Park Safari - Elephants are Beautiful but Tourists beware of SCAMS!
Text:
We came to Sigiriya during our roundtrip through Sri Lanka and stayed for two nights at a local homestay. Our plans were to climb Pidurangala Rock for sunrise and for the afternoon of our arrival we had hoped to do a kayaking trip on the nearby river. However, despite mentioned in Lonely Planet's guide, Rasta Rant does not offer those trips anymore.

So, we decided to return to our accommodation and since we are quite new to Sri Lanka and it is our first time here, relied on the help of our hosts to arrange the Safari on short-notice, instead of booking an offer we had found on Air BnB. The trip for two people was quickly scheduled and a driver showed up in his jeep an hour later. After driving for a while, he pulled on to a gas station, where he asked us whether we were going to Minneriya or some other park. We quickly said Minneriya, as this was what we had asked for from our hosts.

Once we got to the park, the driver (whom we had paid beforehand - 13,000 Rupees for 2 people as agreed with our hosts), went to the ticket counter. While he was gone, a man in what appeared to us as a park ranger uniform approached us and told us that today was a great day to see the elephants. When our driver returned, him and the "ranger" quickly exchanged some words, followed by him also getting into our car, shaking our hands and introducing himself.

During the drive he seemed very knowledgable in terms of the different animals and birds, told us he has been working at the park for over 10 years and that he would know all the best spots to see the elephants. Every now and then he hammered against the side of the jeep to make the driver stop and show us something. Everything seemed fine, until at the end of the drive the "ranger" got up to ask us if we were "very happy" and mumbled something about "I really need the tips." That's when we realised that this man is as far away from an official ranger as possible. 

We passed him some money so he would leave us alone and after again exchanging some words with the jeep driver, disappeared into the woods. We already felt quite embarrassed that we had mistaken him for an official ranger, when our driver made us stop at a local vegetable plantation and encouraged us to buy corn. We kindly refused and were relieved when finally returning to our accommodation. Then, when we got out of the car, he claimed that Minneriya was more expensive than the initial quote and demanded an extra 2000 Rupees from us. We were completely confused, but ended up refusing and walking away from his vehicle.

If you're planning on visiting the park - please make sure to compare prices, and don't make our mistake and fall for the false rangers.

BUT: The park itself is beautiful, we had lots of close encounters with elephants and other wildlife, saw different kinds of eagles, water buffalos and jackals - which overall, was worth the hassle - so overall - we absolutely recommend visiting the park.

Title: Great Park!
Text: Park with many beautiful elephants that we can see in their natural habitat very closely, in addition to other innumerable animal species.

Title: Asian elephants and more
Text: Fantastic experience to see so many elephants and youngsters up close.  Bumpy jeep tide adds to the enjoyment!

Title: Elephant safari
Text:
We visited the park as part of a tour package and while visits to other parks in other countries have largely been disappointing, this exceeded expectations. I cannot say if we were just lucky but in the space of 2 hours saw close to 200 elephants. They were feeding and walking close to our Jeep. 

A very surprising and enjoyable experience

Title: Beautiful experience
Text:
We went during the wet season so it wasn't super overran with Elephants, but we saw some herds. Overall, a lovely experience but beware: at the start, a tour guide will hop into your vehicle and you might not want that. We didn't and he still came along. We didn't ask him for anything and he was not very knowledgeable about the park. I spotted the monitor lizards before he did and pointed them out to my friend. As a person who is a nature enthusiast, I already knew quite a bit about the animal inhabitants.

 We also didn't know that the tour guide was coming and didn't bring any money to tip him - only enough to pay and tip our driver. It didn't help that at the end he was asking for a tip and neither of us had the money for him since we did not account for his company. 

A definite must see.

Title: Peaceful afternoon with Elephants and more
Text: We had a beautiful afternoon in our private Jeep to Minneriya. We saw well over 40 elephants, water buffalo, monkeys, birds of prey and other exotic birds, deer, lizards, you name it.  The guide/ranger was excellent.  Do it!

Title: Elephants in the wild
Text: If you wish to observe wild elephants in a beautiful natural lakeside setting, then this elephant reserve is the place to go. It was a wonderful experience. Touring the park in the back of an old 4WD on some pretty rough tracks adds to the excitement and sense of adventure. You are able to get quite close to herds of elephants grazing along the lake side as well as individuals hiding in the thick scrub only metres off the road. Water buffalo herds are also aplenty and were interesting to watch frolicking in the shallow waters of the lake. A storm blew up suddenly while we were out in the parklands requiring the roof of the 4WD to be quickly drawn over us. Then we discovered the mouse living in the rolled up roof and shared the ride with him/her for the rest of the trip. This visit was a truly memorable thing to do and is highly recommended as a must do for anybody whether wildlife enthusiasts or not.

Title: Excellent birding
Text:
Visited in a private safari Jeep and collected our guide at the gate. He was excellent and had a great knowledge of the birds as well as excellent spotting ability and he pointed out many species we would have missed without his assistance.

We spent four hours in the park and sited 42 species so an excellent result.

Title: Wow- lots to see
Text: Enjoyed my jeep trip around this park. Saw lots of animals and birds. I was taken to a lot areas and felt I saw the park to its full advantage

Title: Fantastic safari
Text: We were taken to our jeep and driven to the park,,,we drove about a bit and saw some elephants but they were quite far from us and couldnt really take any photos but our driver was very good and carried on driving about and it was worth it as we came across about 10 elephants it was an amazing sight... There was even a little baby one hiding by his mother. This was the highlight of our holiday we loved it so if your in the area you have to go!!!

Title: Distressing experience
Text:
We have been on many safaris, albeit in Africa, and this is the first time we felt uncomfortable viewing wild animals.  The park is small and has limited wildlife (we saw 2 small herds of elephants, a peacock, one empty eagle nest and a wasp nest). On the day of our visit there were upwards of 40 jeeps surrounding a small group of elephants.  One of them, "Broken Ear" was known to dislike jeeps due to one killing her baby elephant in the past.  Despite this the convoy of jeeps surrounded her, and after two roaring past she became increasingly angry. Our jeep was stuck - due to other jeeps blocking exit paths and despite being one of the furtherest away we were in her line of vision and she charged us, hitting the jeep twice.  It was very upsetting to see an animal so distressed and angry, she obviously felt she need to protect her herd which included a baby. It felt so cruel having so many jeeps invading her personal space

It is a beautiful area but I really would caution anyone thinking of visiting

Title: Elephants safari !
Text: A beautiful national park in sigiriya. Hundreds of elephants, deers and wildanimals. The largest elephants group I have ever seen. Baby elephants are so cute. I will visit again and again.

Title: Elephants!!
Text: Took a jeep tour around this Park with a small group. You find out on the day if the elephants are more prominent here or over the road at the other National Park. We were worried because it started to rain just as we started but luckily it stopped pretty quickly. I thought we'd get very little in the way of sightings and only from a distance but it must be said I was very wrong. We got very close to multiple groups and even though it was Jeep city they didn't seem to mind, they mostly kept eating, which was amazing to see and exactly why we came. Such peaceful creatures (so long as you don't do anything stupid). The driver got us very close. We also saw a couple of peacocks and parrots but it was mostly about the elephants. I enjoyed seeing this more than the Elephant Orphanage as it seemed like less of a display.

Title: A DIFFERENT ELEPHANT
Text: We drove through this park en route to Girithale for the night. Our guide described it as'an elephant infested jungle'. It was a great and pleasant surprise to see an Asian elephant eating roadside, traffic giving it a wide berth. I was struck by its colours with a pale orange/pink colour above its trunk, behind its eyes, the trim of the ears, etc. This type of elephant is decidedly smaller than its African counterpart.

Title: Great drive but no sighting of elephants !
Text: We visited on 28 December at about 11 pm with out two children aged 5 and 2. The safari drivers did mention that due to rains only a few elephants were sighted the previous day. After much discussion they still urged that we take the ride which lasted about 2.5 hours. The cost was about 13,000 LKR (5000 for the driver and 8000 for entry with taxes and rental for car.). Peacocks and butterflies were more commonly visible while an eagle and some other exotic birds in smaller numbers. Going one way (about an hour)  was exciting though while coming back the same route was taken and kind of felt dull because we knew the elephants arent going to show up anymore. Initially I was upset for spending that amount and not having achieved our objective of seeing elephants but then their movement cant be controlled by the authorities whatsoever. Its part of nature and luck. Very unfortunate though we will try again some other time in a season which is more suitable.

Title: Minneriya....Pachyderm paradise!
Text: My wife and I visited the Minneriya National Park in late November 2019 as part of a Webjet package tour of Sri Lanka. The day included a morning visit to Sigiriyas Lion Rock (which is impressive) followed by a 4wd tour of the park in the afternoon. We were in luck and came across several hundred elephants (guide said 300-400.... maybe) in about 4 or 5 large herds around the edge of the lake. Many babies were seen in different herds. We got within 50m of a few herds as they grazed and moved around the lake edge. Absolutely amazing! Apart from the elephants we saw a lot of bird life and a herd of water buffalo. There were probably 20-30 other 4wds sharing the experience so it can get a bit hectic. The elephants generally seemed to ignore the visitors. The only criticism is that our personal guide and the 4wd driver/guide didnt exactly overwhelm us with information and stayed fairly quiet thru out. Overall a great day!

Title: Many elephants with babies
Text: Was sceptical about this, as I usually am with all things elephants, but actually found it a great experience to see so many elephants.  Im still not convinced « in the wild » is the right turn of phrase as the elephants are clearly very used to vehicles, a shame most of them have grown up with this, but they seemed healthy with as much space as allotted for wildlife nowadays and they were thriving! Many babies so lovely to see their interaction!  If youve done safari in South Africa etc and are used to that, I would say the jeeps get very close (too close) to the elephants but I think this is because the elephants know these jeeps (in SA we would stay a lot further away and not get ourselves in situations where we couldnt reverse quickly out of a situation, but here the drivers didnt seemed worried at all.

Title: Jeep safari
Text:
Had a Jeep safari through this lovely park which was very enjoyable. Arrived a few hours earlier than planned and really it was for the better. After lunch the amount of jeeps going through this area was extreme, bumper to bumper with
 lots of people taking photos. We were lucky enough to see at least 50 elephants with baby ones too. There was also lots of painted storks and cattle. Lovely place to visit

Title: So Many elephants, beautiful and
Text:
At the Beginning the tour I was a little apprehensive as to whether we would be fortunate enough to see any elephants - this wasn't a problem! 

Although the drive through the woodland area was exciting in the jeeps and we spotted some wonderful trees and birds. Once we reached the open plains We saw upwards of 50 wild elephants, ranging from 6 weeks old to fully grow males which we were told was quite rare to see. 

Definitely a must if you are in the area. We were also lucky enough to have a really knowledgeable driver who had got used to the elephants from a young age and took us on some short cuts to avoid all the busy jeeps around.

Title: Terrific elephant viewing in the wild
Text: We had a terrific afternoon drive to the Park where we saw a number of elephant bulls, usually alone, and many larger groups of up to about 50 mothers with babies of various ages. Some were only a few weeks old and it was interesting how the herd protected the little ones. So the elephants were definitely a highlight. Also we saw many interesting birds, some spotted deer, mongooses, monitors, water buffalo and a variety of small animals. If you are staying in the area this is a definite tour not to be missed. We were due to do a village tour, but cancelled that to do this, and were so glad we did

Title: Amazing
Text: The elephants were amazing! So many jeeps lined up but it was incredible to see them in their element. Kids liked the jeep ride too. A highly of our trip to sri lanka!

Title: Great experience  up close to Elephants
Text: We did a half day Jeep tour through the park to view the elephants roaming the park. We were not disappointed and saw an amazing number of elephants roaming the area and were able to get up close and get some incredible pictures of these magnificent beasts. Our driver was able to get us very close and highlighted aspects of the habitat and other wildlife in the park. A definite must do.

Title: Lovely to see the Gathering
Text: Very lucky to go to this park when the annual gathering was taking place.  The elephants live in Clans, and they all meet and form a herd at the lake.  We were in Sri Lanka when this was going on, and we saw them coming out of the forest to head there.  Quite a few jeeps, so it was a bit busy, but they give the animals space.

Title: Saw so many elephants!
Text: I took this tour with a specific tour company and highly recommend! I had my own private jeep (albeit a little uncomfortable) but I saw so many elephants I could not have asked for more!  The tour guide was very informative and excited for me that I had this experience with him on this day!
