Title: Super and Amazing Safari! It's a must to do
Text: On our trip back from Sigiriya Rock to our hotel, our guide recommended this National Park to go to, We drove here and it was really an amazing and unique experience. We arrived here at the end of the midday at a big parking. This was the departure point for the jeeps. Here we were seated in the back of an 4x4 jeep. First we thought there will be more people in our jeep, but we got our own private tour. Only the 2 of us. haha. The driver drove into the woods, it's about a 15 minutes drive thru the thick woods before you reach the park area. It's really beautiful and breathtaking. The drivers have their route around the park, and off course there were more jeeps driving around. We were lucky that we were late in the midday, so we had only a few jeeps around us. The driver took us around the water and at some point he stops and shutdown the engine so you really can enjoy the beautiful and silence in the park. When your driver sees an animal, he will point at it so you can take a photo of it. In the beginning we saw a group of elephants in the distance  and this was really amazing to see in real life (not in a zoo). At some point we drove thru a bushed area and when we reached back in the open again we were surrounded by many elephants and other animals, In 1 word.... WOW!! Really amazing and unique, I recommend everybody who is in the Area or is on Sri Lanka, to go to this National Park.

Title: Lots of Elephants
Text: If you go here for a safari make sure its in the afternoon, our tour guide changed it from the morning and well worth it. You will see far more elephants in the afternoon. If you are booked for in the morning, change it.  The only downside is there are a lot of jeeps doing the safari, they could do with restricting the numbers.

Title: Gathering of elephants... and 4x4's :)
Text:
I have never seen so many elephants grouped up in my life. Stunning spectacle which you can watch for hours! At the same time another spectactle to behold is the neverending horde of 4x4's pushing and grinding past each other to give their passengers the best viewpoint.

We came for the elephants, we saw the elephants, but we will never return due to the amount of 4x4's. I would recommend to all that you visit this park (at the time of the gathering) but also visit a smaller park in another piece of Sri Lanka to actually feel emerged in to nature.

Title: Great afternoon safari
Text:
Spent an afternoon in the park
Saw soo many elephants
With many calfs playing
A special experience not to be missed during the gathering

Title: Must Visit
Text:
This park has the largest group of wild Asian elephants and we didnt have to drive far before we saw lots of them.

While there are lots of elephants and water buffelo there really is not much else but you cant beat the joy of seeing these wonderful creatures in their natural habitat.

Title: Brilliant Experience
Text: Brilliant experience. Very good driver - felt safe and he took us to sights where we saw loads of elephants. As there was a language barrier it might be a good idea to have a book in jeep about facts and figures about the elephants. We were delighted to see that the elephants are in huge areas and that there were many babies.

Title: Elephant city
Text:
This is a great park if you want to view elephants.  Expect it to be crowded with safari jeeps and therefore not a personal, peaceful experience though. 

If you can cope with that, expect to be treated to views of herds of up to 100 elephants and even turkeys if youre lucky. 

Definitely worth the half day trip.

Title: Great safari
Text: Great to see a lot of wild elefants and the jeeps keep a respectful distance from the animals. We saw a lot of baby elefants and many birds, it is hot and dusty so a little protection is recomended.

Title: Top attraction in Sri Lanka
Text:
Best season is August. We had a wonderful afternoon on a good open jeep and saw 100 elephants female and baby eating grass near a lake. You can't miss elephants ( they have 600 on the park).
If you are lucky you can see a big male that usually eats within the forest. 
All the animals are on the wild but you can see them very close.

Title: Beautiful view of the elephants in the lap of Mother Nature
Text:
We did the jeep safari and saw hers of elephants during the entire tour. It was a very peaceful experience and I would highly recommend everyone to do it. 

Some tips would be to respect the wildlife and stay within your jeep. Getting out of your vehicle is strictly prohibited. Carry plenty of water, a scarf as the mud can fly at certain points and be prepared for some jerks and bumps as the road is uneven at certain points.

Title: Trumpet! So many elephants
Text:
We had an amazing tour in here as part of an overall tour group to SL. The jeep was respectful and stayed a good distance away from the animals... we saw so many gorgeous elephants, birds, monkeys and even a giant squirrel! 
It was thrilling to see elephants on a savannah and not behind bars. 
Thank you so much!

Title: Elephant Safari
Text: Definitely definitely definitely recommend if you are in the area to visit this wonderful gem.  You get to see 200-300 elephants in their natural habitat. You are not allowed to interact with them, call them or feed them. They are used to the safari cars (loads of them) however the idea is that you are the observer you are not to disturb them. We loved every minute of it (2,5h) and we saw baby seagulls, peacocks monkeys and catle of cows. Awesome experience.

Title: Check with locals first
Text:
Sooo we went to Minneriya based on Trip Advisor reviews not the advice of locals. Locals told us the elephants were at Ecopark not Minneriya ( the elephants travel between the two parks). We ignored that advice based on reviews here. At Minneriya we saw 7 elephants in total at a distance. We later heard that most elephants were at Ecopark. The drivers at Minneriya knew the elephants were mostly at ecopark, but need an income so dont tell people this. The next day we went to Ecopark, and saw more than 7 herds of elephants. 
The elephants do frequent ecopark and Minneriya but check with  a local before you go,, to see which park the elephants are currently in. We used ceylon wild trails safari at Ecopark the following day, and were amazed at what we saw

Title: So many elephants
Text:
This park is stunning. It is all around the most beautiful lake. Our tour guide arranged a jeep for us and he was very good.We saw a couple of female elephants with their babies in the river and then saw a herd of over 20 with very young babies that came by the track right past our vehicle. I was in elephant heaven.
A big tip is to go at lunch time. In the mornings the elephants don't tend to come to the lake but as it heats up they come and the park is quiet at lunch time. We arrived there at 12.30 and we only saw 3 other jeeps. We came out at about 2.30 and there was jeep after jeep coming in - they were queuing to get in right back to the car park. We had a job getting out due to all the jeeps. It was manic and awful. We were so glad we were early.

Title: Elefants yes but once you are on one of the 2 loops your driver will just rush you through
Text: We saw a herd of elephants (21 individuals) and a few bird species. After that the driver had to drive a one-way loop. To get out of the park at 6 pm he went so fast we didn't see any animals in the forest part of the park. There are 2 loop options. The jeeps have to drive in line, sometimes overtaking each other but there is no way to slow it down and spend more time. Once you are on the loop the distance is so big, the driver has to hurry up.

Title: ELEPHANTS GALORE
Text: This is a beautiful park.  Once you have experienced the jolting ride through the rutted drive way, it opens up into a lake experience with plenty of elephants and water buffalo.  Along the way we had to ford a river and one of the jeeps got stuck!  Lots of wading birds, egrets, pelicans, cranes, ibis.  We also saw a family of monkeys in a tree close up cradling a baby.  We also saw eagles in trees.  This is a very lively experience.  Make sure you are in a jeep with the tarpaulin 'roof' off so that you can stand up.

Title: Wow! Go with @specialsafari01
Text:
We hired a jeep and driver from Habanera, their company name was Special Safari, the driver was Giayan Kaluarachchi and their number is 0763101482. They are situated in Habanera, near Cinnamon Lodge. 

We looked on here and took advice to not book in advance, but to go to Habanara and hire a local guide and keep. This was excellent advice. Hire Special Safari as they were fantastic! I read that older jeeps are better as they can go through the water in the park and not get stuck - this was true. We sailed through whilst other newer jeeps became stuck. Our driver was an excellent guide, he knew exactly where to go to see a multitude of animals. We saw: elephants, mongoose, snake, jackals, eagles, deer, herds of water buffaloes, monkeys, peacocks, herons, bee eater, monitor lizards to name but a few. Our driver Giayan was patient, there was never a rush. We set off at at 2.10pm and returned at 6.30pm, giving us 3.5 hours in the park (it's about 30 mins from Special Safari in the middle of Habanara to the middle of the park). We were one of the last jeeps to leave the park as we were having such a great time and our guide was so busy showing us all the animals we could think of!
I can't recommend Special Safari highly enough to do the safari in Minneriya. The other thing to note is that the elephants move between parks, so hiring locally meant that Giayan knew exactly where the elephants were and took us straight to them.

Title: Good but the elephants were distant...
Text: This was good for seeing a high number of  elephants together but we had a better safari experience in Uda Walawe. We saw a grey hooded eagle, painted storks, elephants and lots of monkeys here.

Title: Most amazing experience
Text: We spent the afternoon here is was the best day seeing the elephants roam free as photography is my hobby the photo opportunities are unreal a must trip

Title: Enjoyable afternoon jeep ride
Text:
Yes there are a lot of jeeps, but I felt this park was more open and avoided a lot of the crush I felt with Yala National Park (the highlight being to try and spot an elusive Sri Lankan leopard or Sloth Bear).  The jeeps on this occasion had room to manoeuvre and the elephants were all very obliging and all jeeps kept their distance and even waited if elephants approached to let them have their way.  So I did enjoy this park much more - seeing elephant families doing their own thing without being hassled by the jeeps was most enjoyable.  Birdlife was the only other wildlife but there were large and small herds everywhere in this park and I didn't feel the jostling of jeeps too much.  Most drove up slowly, found a position and parked to allow us to take photographs or just enjoy their antics.  On our safari I didn't feel that the jeep drivers were encroaching on the elephants as all the jeeps seem to follow the track, parked off to the side and allowed us to just watch the elephants - yes mothers put their babies on the other side of the jeeps, but continued feeding, and the babies of course continued playing.

I actually quite enjoyed the afternoon safari as instead of getting hotter, it cooled as the afternoon sun began to set.  

We were a private group with our own guide so we had a pre-arranged driver for this attraction, so it was just us in a slightly newer and more comfortable jeep - open topped and a little dusty, but allowed you to stand and take photos when the jeep stopped.

Have an open mind here - Sri Lankan is a developing country and has a long way to go so don't expect the same level of eco-tourism you would get in other countries.

Title: Bad experience !!!!!
Text:
We felt something wrong going on when we reached to the location between our taxi driver and the jeep driver ,Then we figured out that they were manipulate. The jeep driver was asking for double amount.He asked for 220 USD for the couple included the car while the actual price should be around 100 USD Only or even less.Therefore,You have to make sure to get the ticket by yourself OR to receive the receipt of paid amount.

In addition to the above, we read that the safari should take about 3 hours to 3 and half while our tour was less about an hour only after the above incident, we havent seen anything just two elephants!!

Title: Dont miss it
Text: A great safari with a lot of elephants and water buffaloes which we saw from a very short distance. On top of the tickets you pay 7000 LKR for a jeep. We had a good luck and saw dozens of elephants and even more water buffaloes. There were  more jeeps than I would prefer, which makes it too busy, but it was still an amazing experience.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: This is a good place to see elephants in the wild. Depending on your luck you may see 20 or more elephants in groups. It is a busy place. Lots of jeeps. Just make sure to be careful of low hanging branches and narrow passages through thick vegetation, especially on the way back once the safari is over. We saw one of the visitors got a cut on face after getting hit by a tree branch on the way back from safari. And it is an open top safari. So apply plenty of sun screen and wear good sun protection. Also it can be dusty and so bring a mask if you have dust allergies.

Title: Evening drive
Text: This is the perfect drive in the evening, even though we didn't have any plan of visiting this park, our guide suggested to do this, so we went ahead and we were not disappointed. It's an 2-3 hour long Safari in the park and they take you near the lake where elephants come there to eat. It's the perfect time to visit as you would end up seeing so many so close. I think they are used to so many jeeps coming close everyday so they were busy eating and we were ignored most of the time by them. So we closely watched how they eat the grass, the way they pull out, dust it out and then eat. It was an amazing experience to watch them so close. We were taken another side of the lake for a nice view which you can climb few stairs to watch and if you are keen just to get the legs dirty after. The surprising visitors were variety of birds, they were awesome. I wish I had more time to spot them more.

Title: Bet the rush to see the elephants!
Text:
Went at about 1:30pm; yes it was hot! But it was outstanding plenty of elephants, Monkeys, Deer, water buffalo, monitor lizards, Turtles and plenty of beautiful birds. 
Going on the earlier tour there were only a maximum of 5 Jeeps at once  stopped looking at the elephants and felt like we saw the animals in their natural habitat and when we were leaving the park at around 3:30 there must have been around 50 odd Jeeps lining up to see a heard of elephants in which we saw earlier and plenty more entering the park as we left. 
Was a truly wonderful experience!

Title: Afternoon drive
Text: Were not sure how good this was going to be when we saw the number of vehicles heading into the park. Initially saw a couple but then as se went around the lakeside there were 40/50 elephants quietly grazing.  Although there are lots of vehicles they seem to stick to the tracks and everyone has got the opportunity to see the elephants and get some good photos.  Very enjoyable.

Title: Take the evening safari
Text:
We went on a morning safari and made it to the elephant herd just before they went into the jungle. It was nice, but I think you'll have more chances to see them on a night safari when they come to the lake to drink. The park itself is amazingly beautiful. 
Safaris don't provide you with anything and you have to pay the entrance fee yourself so bring water and money. 
Expect to pay around 4000 LKR for 2 people. It's worth your time and money.

Title: Not for the purist
Text: If you are looking for an exclusive observation of elephants grazing in herds by the lake edge you are going to be disappointed. This is a popular tourist attraction and the convoy of vehicles winding their way along the dirt roads to find elephants is at times intrusive. Having said that you are likely to have the opportunity to see groups of elephants as we did. There were many with young, one or two month old babies and they genuinely seemed unconcerned with the vehicles nearby. For the most part drivers showed some respect for the elephants welfare and maintained a good distance. In many instances the elephants ambled slowly closer to the vehicles. If you decide to go my suggestion would be to go late afternoon, say from 3.00pm onwards. This way you escape the heat of the day. There are dozens of drivers outside the park entrance ready to take you.

Title: Nice place
Text:
We went to Minneriya national park and booked a 
Private Jeep and driver recommended by one of our Colombo friend his name is jayalath and can be contacted on 0771278352. He charged us 3500 srilankan rupees . Usually hotel charge 5000 . So its was a good deal driver was very informative and explained us about most of the animals . As it was too early in morning so was little difficult to see elephants but he did his best to show us and finally we saw a few , it tools around 3 hours altogether and the entry fees was seperate which was around 8000 srilanka rupees for two foreigners two locals and taxes included . So basically we paid $100 au dollars all together including Jeep hiring. But it was soo beautiful and lovely to see wild animals without any animal cruelty. Worth every cent. Thankyou jayalath .

Title: Wonderful heard of elephants.
Text: Had a half day visit to Minneriya. Highlight was around 30-40 elephants emerging from forest to 'take the waters'. An awful lot of trucks vying for best position, but got a good long view of several heards around the park. Lots of birdlife and buffalo also. A 'must see'.

Title: Highlight on our trip!
Text: Minneriya National Park was an incredible place and experience. The park is beautiful and we saw hundreds of elephants on our loop through the park. The drivers were careful and respectful of the animals.

Title: Elephants galore!
Text: This was our first (of 3) safari experiences in Sri Lanka.  The jeep was in average condition,  3 rows of seats,  with open roofs where you could stand up.  All the jeeps follow the same track,  up to 2 abreast at a time. You go through bush, then through a river (3 jeeps got stuck - fortunately not ours) and then it opens out to large areas surrounding the lake.   We saw a couple of hundred elephants (best to go on an afternoon safari as they come to the lake for water). Unfortunately there were almost as many jeeps as elephants and at first we sat in a huge queue (the jeeps at the front of the line didn't move on in a timely manner).  After a while the jeeps spread out and there were plenty more elephants to see,  with less crowded jeep conditions. Our driver didn't really talk to us,  but it was pretty obvious what we were looking at! If you're into elephants this is the safari for you.

Title: Pick right!
Text: Make sure that you pick the right guide. Some clearly just roar around as fast as possible in unsuitable vehicles. Others are great and gives you a detailed view of what's going on and get you really close.

Title: Visit to Park
Text: We were left slightly underwhelmed. The park was very busy and there was a lot of jostling to get into positions. The variety of animals was disappointing, and every bird of prey was an eagle...... the elephants are in abundance and very docile so you get up close to them.

Title: Excellent safari we saw so many elephants
Text: Great way to see elephants and lots of bird life. The driver was great, making sure we had seen enough before moving on again. Highly recommended

Title: Too many jeeps
Text:
Sadly this wildlife park is being over-exploited, with convoys of jeeps in search of a limited number of elephants. When a herd was spotted, the dirt track turned into a 4x4 sales forecourt, with jeeps jostling for space and the best view.

We also saw a few larger birds (egrets, eagles, herons and pelicans), and a mongoose. 

Ironically, we saw two elephants (one of them with tasks, quite rare) by the side of the road on our drive back to the hotel. Our driver was quick to spot them in the semi-darkness, and we were much closer to them than in the wildlife park.

Our expectations may have been too high, as we had already visited Yala National Park earlier in our holiday. I would give Minneriya a miss and spend the extra time at Yala. A more diverse range of animals and birds, with less jeeps!!

Title: Amazing to see Elephant
Text:
Great park , you see Elephant really clearly. On my visit there was a herd with a 3 week old calf who was feeding. In another area another herd with a young calf who was trumpetting, I also saw Giant Squirrel and 6 times The Jungle Fowl Sri Lankas national bird. 
My driver arranged an earlier visit than planned to avoid the many jeeps on our way out there were many many jeeps. So if your goings get some good advice and go a little earlier.

Title: Elephants, elephants, elephants.
Text: Loved this adventure. Our safari had a fun start with one jeep bogged in the river. Then there was great excitement when we spotted our first wild elephant, then another and another. Then there were dozens of them gathering near the lake, one only a month old. Very special indeed.

Title: It's All About The Elephants
Text: I had no high expectations prior to our jeep safari but maybe by luck or chance we had a great experience. We did see a lot of elephants but more significantly was the fact that we saw them in herds of at least 40-50 with babies! The park is very open so we were able to get quite close, many photo opportunities. Also saw an abundance of bird life, water buffaloes, monitors etc. The safaris seem to take about 2 hours. Wear sunscreen as the jeeps are open top and plan to have a good long shower back at your accommodation to wash of all the dust! Great experience.

Title: Nellys Everywhere!
Text:
Beginning the tour we were apprehensive as to whether we would be fortunate enough to see any elephants - this wasn't a problem! 

We saw upwards of 50 wild elephants, ranging from 6 weeks old to fully grow males which we were told was quite rare to see. 

Definitely a must if you are in the area.

Title: Choose the wrong time of year
Text: I really wanted to see the Sri Lankan wild elephants, so I just ignored the experts opinion. Eventually I realised the consequence of my arbitrary decision. The best time to watch these wild elephant is July to end of September. But I went there in last December. But I was lucky enough to see dozen of elephants instead of hundreds. These Asian  elephants are more beutiful than the African ones. Safari started early as 7am. The guide and park ranger was very knowledgeable and know exactly where can find the elephants. also we saw few peacocks, pelicans, some other birds. After all it was really remarkable safari, enjoyed the dry zone wild life in Sri Lanka.

Title: Fantastic, dozens and dozens of elephants
Text:
Starting of with the negative, dozens of jeeps!
Otherwise, beautiful area and elephants, elephants, elephants.
Youll get very close! So, must see when in the area, just dont get bothered too much by the other jeeps.

Title: Nose to tail
Text: No, not the elephants - the jeeps. I imagined a jeep safari would be a quiet affair, little did I know that all the jeeps set off at the same time, so we were virtually nose to tail the whole way round, unless we spotted some elephants and then we were 3 deep trying to take photos of them. Still, it was worth doing.

Title: Good Elephant Sightings.  Nothing More and Too Crowded.
Text:
Yes, we saw a lot of elephants.  and more elephants.  and nothing else, unless you want to count the egrets and storks...

But... there were TOO MANY JEEPS. Easily 50 deep at every sighting watering hole.  Way too many for any decent viewing or photographing.  More than I have ever seen at any other game drive we have taken in the last 40 years. :(

Title: Too Crowded and nothing beyond elephants
Text:
Yes, we saw a lot of elephants.  and nothing else, unless you want to count the egrets and storks...

But... there were TOO MANY JEEPS. Easily 50 deep at every sighting watering hole.  Way too many for any decent viewing or photographing.  More than I have ever seen at any other game drive we have taken in the last 40 years.

Title: Excited
Text: Amazing, amazing - was so excited to be able to see the elephants and other wildlife.   Tip...make sure you get a jeep that has proper tyres and that it is a 4x4......we saw two jeeps that couldnt make it up the hill!  There are various companies out there that offer a trip and all look pretty decent jeeps and the really good thing is that they respect the elephants space and keep to the track.

Title: Great to see animals in their own environment.
Text:
We visited the park whilst on an organised tour.  I love to see animals in their own environment, they look so much happier.  There are loads of elephants to see, water buffaloes and a variety of birds.

The park is extremely busy with visitors and you can lose count of the jeeps.

It is good there are tourists and especially if the money goes towards the upkeep and conservation.

Title: Very nice elephants safari
Text: A very nice safari to see elephants. We went around 2:30 pm as its the time for elephants to come to the lake for drinking water. Our hotel was 50 minutes away from Safari point and cost us 60 US$ to pay the local jeep to take us around.

Title: No, this is not Jurassic Park!
Text: But it's worth the visit.  The plains are beautiful and made more beautiful by the wild life.  We saw herds of elephants, lots of peacocks (including one doing a dance and 2 others fighting), pelicans, etc.  Amazing place

Title: Very nice park
Text: We were very early, at sunrise. We were the only ones in the park. We could see many birds, quite a few quadrupedes including elephants. No leopard and the like.

Title: Amazing trip to see elephants
Text: We went there around 2 pm and saw heaps of elephants - it was the best experience ever! I never saw elephants before in the wild life and it was amazing to see them. We went from Sigiriya and paid 5.000 Rupiah for our cheap but could divided it through 4. The entry fee for a group of 4 is 14.400 Rupiah but it is totally worth the money

Title: Overcrowded
Text: Overcrowded but nice elephants to see near water with young ones. MANY jeeps rushing all over the place to position themselves for best position!

Title: So many elephants!
Text: We saw so many elephants on this trip.  Unfortunately there are way too many jeeps too and some of the drivers hog their space if there is a good view.

Title: Fantastic afternoon tour
Text:
We did a jeep safari tour as part of our Sri Lankan tour and we had the most fantastic day we say hundreds of elephants in their natural environment just doing what elephants do,  there were several herds and we also saw some babies  that were only a week or so old, we also saw water buffalo, and pelicans, deer and lots of other birds. 

It was a spectacular afternoon made all the better by our guides.

Title: Simply Stunning
Text: My wife and I visited here during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka ????. We chose to take an afternoon Safari Drive as wed heard that it wasnt so busy then, hmm Id hate to see how busy it was in the mornings ??. Most people visit the park for the wild Asian Elephants ?? and they were impressive. However, our main interest was the bird life, which was extensive and impressive. Several rare and sought after species are easy to see here, Lesser Adjutant, Spot-billed Spoonbill, Paddyfield Pipit and Jerdon's Bush lark to name a few. The Asian Elephants ?? did steal the show. The place is a must for anyone visiting the area. Highly Recommended

Title: Elephants, elephants and more elephants!
Text: Fantastic afternoon with the wife on a safari trip. Saw all sorts of birds, monkeys, lizards etc. But the highlight by far was seeing 200+ elephants all playing, eating and washing in the reservoir. Amazing experience!!!

Title: An Elephant paradise
Text: Minneriya national park is a great place to see hundreds of elephants in a single place. This is where I saw the most number of elephants at a time in a single place. Best time to go is the evening as elephants come to the lake. Apart from the elephants you can see some other species like deer, wild boar, buffalo, etc. Be alert and get some information from your guide or any other local in the area about the crowd in the park as lots of crowd will ruin your experience.

Title: Lalith Jeep Safari Dambulla
Text: We Saw very special places.Great Tour and very friendly Guide. We can highly recommend Lalith Safari Dambulla

Title: Great Elephant safari
Text: We spent a couple of hours in a large 4 wheel drive viewing many elephants of all ages here. The terrain was interesting if a little boggy (it rained overnight).

Title: Elephants Elephants Elephants
Text:
mostly elephants can be seen although there are quite a few herds of migratory birds nearyby,
I hope they have more species to be seen for a change,

Title: Safari
Text: Don't go expecting to see loads of different types of animals. We saw plenty of elephants and this was amazing seeing them in the wild.

Title: Amazing safari with lots of elephants
Text: We did an evening safari at Minneriya national park, and there were an abundance of elephants. There were quite a few trucks in the park but it didn't detract from the elephants.

Title: A place with a very large number of jeeps and a few elephants
Text:
It is no so much of a safari as it is a large bunch of tourists loaded jeeps rushing to see the elephants. At some point there were twice or tree times as may jeeps as the elephants they surrounded for the benefit of their clients. If you've ever been on an African safari forget about this one, or you will be sorely disappointed... 
Bear in mind that you can actually ride an elephant in Sigiriya, if you so desire.

Title: Amazing Site
Text: Its wonderful to see all the elephants. I arrived early afternoon, around 2pm. There were maybe 50 elephants, by 4pm there were 200. They just kept arriving in various family groups, walking out of the forest for kilometres along the lake. Ive been to Africa and have not seen this many elephants together at one time. Really was something Ill never forget.

Title: Make sure you use a 4 wheel drive jeep company
Text:
We were lucky to see many elephants and not get stuck in the mud in the park because our touring driver knew an excellent company who use 4 wheel drive jeeps. The company is part of the Mihini hotel on the main Polonnaruwa road at Habarana. 
Our jeep driver was Nimal and he was excellent at navigating the rough and very muddy terrain . We saw two other much swankier jeeps stuck in the mud waiting for rescue because they are not 4WD. Don't be fooled into getting one of those. Nimal is a local guy and knows a lot about elephants. He also managed to get us away from the other jeeps so a lot of the time when we saw elephants we were on our own which was a much better experience than being in a traffic jam of 8 of them. Highly recommended and seeing elephants in the wild and beautiful setting was very special.

User_Location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
Title: Elephants........
Text: Large convey of Jeeps/ Land cruisers etc explore the park in search of Elephants. Very rough terrain particularly after heavy rains. A joy to see a herd of 12+ Elephants just eating and roaming.

Title: Absolute Rubbish - Avoid!!!
Text:
The "Ecco Park" is supposedly a sanctuary for wild elephants but it has now become completely over-commercialized by greedy Tours firms all congesting parts of the park in their diesel polluting vehicles.

We were on an organised trip that lasted several hours much of which was spent in traffic jams of vehicles all travelling along the same track but often several lines abreast and in different directions as individual drivers each sought to outdo the numerous other vehicles. Some broke down or attempted ridiculous "three-point turns" in the track only to become stuck in the mud thus causing various blockages. At one point we didn't move for nearly an hour. Imagine a crowded street full of tuck tuks all vying to get to the same spot and not caring about the chaos created and the effect on the elephants. 

Most importantly the Elephants' space isn't respected so they were sometimes chased by selfish drivers. It was an appalling experience for the animals and the far too numerous visitors alll congested into very tight areas. 

Website photos suggest large open spaces and numerous elephants enjoying the peaceful sanctuary but instead we saw a mere handful and on each occasion they were quickly approached from various directions by numerous jeeps. It's just become a commercial rip off for greedy firms. 

Overall it was chaotic, disrespectful of the elephants and an appalling excursion. Avoid!!!!

Title: Love love loved it
Text: We came to the park to see the elephants which we saw, they were in a pack witch was lovely to see, it was a beautiful day for us just being with them in there nature setting. Would love to come back.

Title: Yup, you'll see elephants, but if they are calving they will be pissed off...
Text: Sri Lankan safaris are perhaps the cheapest on the planet compared to Africa, but do understand, you will be in a queue of vehicles, the drivers will all be communicating with each other to get their convoys close to any animals spotted. On our safari the Elephants were clearly upset with being intruded upon. One of the vehicles got bogged and the Elephants were being quite aggressive. The interpretation from our guide was little more than "look - there's and elephant" He certainly was no naturalist. The national park was certainly beautiful, and it was nice to be out in the bush, but I would not describe this as an "eco" experience. Sri Lanka has a way to go to offer true eco tourism experiences.

Title: elephants galore
Text: great place to go in November when not so many jeeps. lots of flooding so we accessed from the Kaudulla side. Elephants, jackal, wild hare and lots of birds. Nice to see them behaving naturally in the wild

Title: Minneriya National Park
Text:
It is the largest concentration and gathering of Asian elephants that can be seen anywhere in the world. We did an open top Jeep safari, watching baby elephants playing with each other, bull elephants tussling for dominance and the great matriarchs surveying the scene is not a sight you are likely to forget in a hurry. Inside the park you will also come across some wild boar, peacocks, deer and many more animals roaming freely as nature intended them to live. 
Aside from the elephant, Minneriya is also home to some 23 other species of mammals a paradise for many species of Lizard and you will see them here in all their colour if you look carefully enough. the views are stunning. You'll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. There are also spotted deers roaming around. The driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species.  as well as snakes like the Indian Python and the Mugger Crocodile. Above all, of course, are Sri Lankas wonderfully varied bird population.
 We drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deers and when we thought viewings were over, we saw a young grey leopard. It was just breath-taking. Then more Stunning scenery and you will also encounter deer, buffalo, pelicans and peacocks. Despite the heat it was a great afternoon at the park. The drivers are constantly in contact with each other and updating where the elephants are to be seen. I highly recommend this to everyone.

Title: Impressive, but ....
Text: ... too many jeeps around the elephants which can be seen in very large numbers , but unfortunately the park has not been limiting the number of tourists so far ...

Title: Elephants and Buffalo
Text: Lovely setting and one of the best parks in the region to see the wildlife. The wildlife do travel between the two main parks so ensure you know which park to visit

Title: Elephants
Text: Lots of elephants. No predators. A couple of different wetlands which attract elephants, buffalo, bird life and the occasional mongoose. If you want to see elephants, this is the national park to visit. We had a driver/ tour guide Sangeeth Gayan who organised our safari for us.

Title: Beautiful elephants but busy park
Text:
If you want to see lots of elephants this is definitely the place to go!

We say a few herds in a variety of places and seeing them playing in the water and enjoying themselves was truly spectacular. There were some baby elephants who were only a few weeks old which was amazing.

The downside was the hordes of other safari vans and people in them. There was lots of congestion at the points were the elephants were and it did impede the experience slightly.  Some of the behaviour of other vans and the people in them left a lot to be desired and at times got to close and upset elephants.

Nevertheless it was a lovely site and one I wanted to see and would say dont miss the experience!

Title: Too many jeeps
Text: Went on a jeep safari as part of our Sri Lanka tour. Wonderful to see so many Asian elephants but it felt like the drivers were chasing down the elephants! There was nearly as many jeeps as elephants and it didnt seem much consideration was given to the wildlife, elephants especially. We have been on safari in Africa where there is a 2 vehicle limit to protect the animals from over exposure, this was certainly not the case here. Concerned how much of the money raised from the safari actually goes to the protection and conservation of these endangered animals, I believe it probably goes to purchasing more jeeps!! Would not give them my money again until I was convinced a large percentage was being used for conservation purposes. Their tactics and approach should be monitored by animal welfare groups to ensure it is in the animals interests.

Title: Wild elephants awesome
Text: Tough off road trail but well worth the effort. Elephants ,crocodile,Monkeys plus much more all in their natural habitat. This is a must do

Title: Really good experience
Text: Definitely go if you love elephants. Make sure you tip your guide a little so they take you good spots as well.

Title: Absolutely Incredible Wild Elephants
Text:
We knew that the herd flitted between Minneriya and Kaudulla but heard there where elephants at the former.

There are literally hundreds of operators out of Habarana and I think most hotels guest houses either run or know someone who does.

We went with our stay Sagiriya Water Gardens and the guy was excellent, we even saw a single elephant on the way to the park.
Once at the entrance you have to pay for each individual in the jeep and there is a discount for jeeps with more people in so a couple will pay slightly more than a jeep with four and so on.

Once in the park it takes a while to reach the lake but we saw multiple elephants on the way, then two herds of about 30 elephants at the lake ranging in age and size from cute little ones to one of the largest who was only one of two with tusks.

What an incredible day, and our guide held right back and kept a good distance, where we saw others too close.

Title: Highlight of our Sri Lankan tour
Text:
We were almost bitterly disappointed as the park was closed on the day we wished to visit due to an employee strike, however it was resolved on our last day - worth checking that there are no such issues when you are planning to go.

The elephants gather early morning and during the evening, so going in the middle of the day will end in disappointment as the elephants head into the jungle. Worth booking in advance to make sure you get a good time slot.

The gathering is a daily ritual, so seeing elephants is highly likely.

The round trip is approx 2 hours, including about 30 minutes to get into the jungle lake where the elephants gather, so you can spend around an hour watching the various herds/families gather.

It was a great experience, and a "must do".

The elephants are not confined to the park. When returning to our hotel after dark, we saw an elephant on the road side, eating, so keep your eyes open!!!

We were lucky enough to get our own jeep, and they are comfortable. Drivers are knowledgeable and enthusiastic.

Title: In the midst of nature
Text:
You can book the safari in advance online or ask your local resort to assist you. Special jeeps for the park. Seats 5-6 each .

Awesome views of the elephants as well as the other wild animals. Don't miss their evening congregation by the waterbody.

Title: Best of the parks we visited in Sri lanka
Text:
There are 3 parks in haberanan we visited this one and kaldoulla.  The elephants had migrated to the latter which, therefore attracted all the traffic.
Minneriya was peaceful and the more attractive with a wealth of bird life alongside a herd of 30 elephants and beautiful scenery.  Youre in the park for around 2.5 hours. Terrific.

Title: Captivating experience
Text:
My wife and I enjoyed the visit to the Minneriya National Park with the exposure to nature and her habitats.

We took the afternoon session. While we didn't see as many elephants as others had experienced there were also fewer jeeps. It could be the timing and day or how thirsty the elephants were. We had also spotted monkeys, peacocks, eagles, and buffalos. 

Note that one cannot get off the jeep once inside the park, so please make sure you have your toilet break beforehand, and bring your sunglasses, sunscreen, and some water to hydrate.

It's an unique experience.

Title: Not to be missed
Text:
This was mind blowing seeing the Elephants in the wild
I would recommend this to anyone kids and adults
It is very safe 
We went in jeeps with heaps of opportunity to take lots of photos
There are around one hundred or more elephants and to just see them in their natural habitat was awesome

Title: For such large animals, they tread very softly
Text:
Minneriya is reputed to be the home of the largest herd of Asian Elephants, and our experience in April 2017 would seem to bear that out. Despite the commercialisation of the trip - there must have been 50+ Land Cruisers around the reservoir - the park is big enough to give one a good view of the herd, especially as it gathers in late afternoon before going into the forest to sleep. They came from all around, to drink, wash and play in the shallow waters, before setting off in a column and heading back into the forest - and they were so quiet. No squealing from the baby elephants, nor thudding of feet from the adults, but simply an inexorable susuration as they walked past us.

The area is also home to many other species, and we saw many types of bird, including the omni-present egrets, ibis and other water fowl. There are also crocodiles, and we saw a couple basking on the banks. A great experience.

Title: Elephant heaven
Text: The highlight of our trip to Sr Lanka. Too many elephants to count. We went for the afternoon safari and it was far superior to both Bundalla and Yala safaris.

Title: Fantastic experience
Text: We visited here during our visit to Sri Lanka and it was the highlight of our holiday. The whole experience was fantastic, we saw lots of animals on our trip especially lots of herds of elephants including baby elephants which were all really close to us in our jeep. Fantastic experience We also had a brilliant guide who talked to us about all the animals and provided us with binoculars. ??

Title: Amazing
Text: We had an amazing afternoon at this National Park.  We arrived mid afternoon.  Could not believe how many elephants we saw.  Herds and herds by the lake.  So great to get so close to families with their babies and to sit and watch them in their natural habitat.  Yes lots of jeeps but plenty of room to experience these beautiful animals in the park.  A highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka.

Title: Too Many Elephants to Count!
Text: This was a highlight of our holiday. This is a very large National Park.  The number of elephants of all ages strolling across the grassland around the huge lake was incredible.  We felt very privileged to see such amazing sights and at very close quarters too.  On the advice of our guide we entered the park in mid afternoon and the number of visitors was much lower than at other times of the day.

Title: Elephant in wild
Text:
My sister and I went to this park in mid Oct. Before setting off, we were told by the tour guide aka jeep driver that we might see peacock, buffalo, many species of bird, etc in the journey. Eventually we could only see big group of wild elephants. It was impressive to witness a crowd of 80+ giants in wild which totally opened my eye.

This was my first safari experience so I found it eye-opening. However it was the second safari visit of my sister and it disappointed her a bit comparing with her last visit in Udawalawa national park in the South of Sri Lanka. She saw a lot of peacock on tree, buffaloes, many birds in beautiful colors on top of elephants and to her the Udawalawa visit was more a memorable experience than Minneriya. 

For those who are planning a visit around the country, would recommend to visit other sizable national park where may have higher chance to see more wild animal instead of just elephants. If your trip cover just the middle part, this safari is still a must-go!

Title: 200+ Elephants with 30+ babies! Amazing!!
Text: We were lucky enough to visit Minneriya National Park during The Gathering. This is a natural event that happens between June and October when elephants migrate to Minneriya for the protected area and large lake. It still depends on the day you visit but we saw over 200 elephants and a magnificent tusker who gave us a show bathing in the lake. Many new babies that were so enchanting to watch. Don't expect to be the only person in a safari jeep in the park... there will likely be many. We spent over 3 hours there with our driver and saw so much. We also encountered a water buffalo stampede with hundreds of them running right across our path! It was an unforgettable experience and one that I will treasure for years to come.

Title: So many elephants!
Text:
We saw more elephants here and nearby outside than anywhere else in Sri Lanka. The elephants were really relaxed and were mooching around indifferent to us. 

I would however share the concerns about the number of jeeps and their proximity to the animals. They really need to introduce some daily limits to the jeeps.

Title: A safari to remember
Text: A two hour jeep safari. A wide range of wildlife but the highlight was, of course, the free roaming elephants. The drivers are constantly in contact with each other and updating where the elephants are to be seen. Absolutely amazing to be sitting looking an elephant in the face from 10 ft!

Title: Felt like I was in a different world
Text: I loved Minneriya because the animals were unharmed and were in their natural habitat. It felt like a different world during the safari. I highly recommend this to everyone.

Title: interesting place
Text:
It will be interesting to see what happens in future as they are building a tarmac road just about up to the national park.
It was great to see the elephants up close but they really need to educate the drivers more they formed a whole line blocking the groups of elephants actually getting over to the water hole at one point and one elephant was getting agitated and moving towards the jeeps to protect the small baby elephants which is completely understandable.
Our guide told us in the peak period there are over a 1,000 jeeps in the park- more jeeps than elephants.They really need to get the balance right-
It was interesting to see some groups of elephants waiting in the trees for the jeeps to go at sunset before starting to come out down to the water hole.
Good experience but they need to get the balance right otherwise the elephants will withdraw.
Interesting to also see cattle grazing and eating grass in the national park- the elephants food too....

Title: The Gathering
Text: I visited in September when the elephant herds gather in this region. On our safari we saw approx 150 elephants which was an amazing sight. One of the highlights of my visit to Sri Lanka.

Title: Largest known meeting place for Asian elephants in the wild
Text:
We went in open jeeps to a place where there were a large number of elephants of all ages - it is said that there are over 200 elephants in this park. The jeep ride is bumpy and those who have back trouble will be advised to sit on a front seat 
An afternoon well spent!

Title: FANTASTIC TO SEE
Text: Booked a Jeep Safari to see the Elephants & we saw sooo many Big & Small, the Jeep ride was fun & the Elephants were sooo close, we have been to Africa before but saw a lot more Elephants here in their natural habitat, it was really nice to see all the different terrain as well.

Title: Elephant paradise!
Text: if you like elephants than this is a must! We were lucky to see hundreds of elephants of varying ages and it was an absolutely brilliant. Would highly recommend.

Title: Wow an amazing place
Text: Did a safri here and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. We travelled in open top jeep so you could stand up and really take in the sights. Big open areas and lakes where the elephants go to play and drink in the water. The elephants wander around ignoring all the jeeps so seems quite natural instead of seeing them in a captive situation. Before We went there, I just thought we would see a few elephants and it would be no big deal but I was wrong. we seen about 150 and quite a few Calves as well. One of the high lights of our SL holiday. Saw lots of birdlife as well .

Title: Too many jeeps but still excellent
Text:
Well worth a visit. We visited both Udawalawe and Minneriya and if youre only able to do one then 100% do Udawalawe as its way less tourist crowded and you get more up close to the elephants without actually disturbing them. 

At Minneriya we were lucky enough to see loads of elephants, probably 100 in total but there was easily 100 jeeps all vying for the best view and its gets really chaotic. The elephants just want to get to the water and with the jeeps all in a line they almost block the elephants which doesnt seem very animal-centric. We didnt pressure our driver but you could see other tourists pushing their driver to get in front of others for a better photo. 
Dont get me wrong, a beautiful place and the elephants are magnificent.

Title: Fantastic
Text:
A must do on our agenda!

Piled into the back of jeeps (5 seats) & headed into the national park on a fine day with the roof open & no side wall giving great views. The driver was great driving along & spotting various animals in the bush and grass.

The highlight took a little time with us seeing various monkeys, birds & water buffalo before finding the elephants (a couple of large herds). The elephants were amazing - probably 50 to 80 in total & they were so carefree despite our close attendance.  At the busiest time there must have been 50 jeeps & 4wd's parked up with cameras clicking amongst many excited people. The elephants mainly ate grass however a few entered the lake.

We also ascended a small tower for better views over the countryside & lake - be careful as no handrails. Nothing special but part of the tour.

Took a bit of a drive back to the bus/car park where we met numerous monkeys & a couple of relatively tame deer.  Great fun even for the older less mobile folk in our group.

Title: Elephants
Text: Much smaller than Yala, this park is home to large herds of elephants and we managed to see lots of them as well as buffalo and several peacocks. I was surprised by the large number of jeeps in the park, but luckily we had arrived a little later in the afternoon and most were heading back to the park entrance enabling us to have a relaxing 20 minutes observing the elephants with only one other jeep in attendance. A beautiful experience.

Title: Go here if you love elephants
Text:
Don't go to other "sanctuaries", visit Minneriya if you want to see elephants in their natural environment, thriving, playing and reproducing in a healthy setting. We did a 3 hour "safari". There's not a huge amount to see apart from elephants, but there are lots of then and you can get close to them (closest was about 10 metres from the jeep). The safari is basic but fun, you park in the car park, climb in the back of a jeep and get driven around the park to seek out the elephants. We went in the afternoon as that's when they are most likely to congregate at the lake. Our jeep driver was very good, the two of us bounced around in the back - just two side benches, three padded cross bars to hold onto if you want to stand up. No Health & Safety here - hold on tight to avoid bashing your bits against the side of the jeep, and if standing, duck to avoid branches thwacking you in the face! Remember sun cream as there's no cover, and a hat is risky to blow off if there's wind. 

We saw loads of elephants - noisy, playful, muddy, but and small. There was one suckling it's mother, still a bit pink, that our driver said was about ten days old. 

We did this as part of a four day tour which originally had the elephant sanctuary in its itinerary, but switched to Minneriya before we travelled. We are so pleased, as people concerned with animal welfare, opposed to elephant tricks and rides and tethering, but still wanting to be close to the magnificent beasts.

Title: Far too many jeeps
Text: In short, yes you can see elephants as long as you enjoy being in a traffic jam of at least 30 jeeps with diesel engines on and completely stuck with alpha male drivers not giving way to anyone. They cut across the elephant herd who were left on either side calling to each other. One hopeless safari member of staff. Think twice about going. Went to Ude Walawe which was a  much better experience.

Title: Yes lots of jeeps but still a wonderful park
Text: We saw plenty of elephants, although probably there were a few more jeeps than elephants! Our driver was really good and didn't get too close or follow them if they chose to walk away. Some elephants especially the young males seemed quite keen to come and look at us. Watching them was fascinating and a very special experience.  We also saw hundreds of water buffalo and loads of birds. In particular the storks, pelicans and spoonbills in very large flocks were spectacular and a fish eagle hunting was entertaining.  The Jungle Fowl was cool too, very pretty. If its a clear evening, get your driver to stay as long as possible because the golden light is amazing just before sunset.

Title: Very exciting to see such large family groups
Text:
It was great to see such large numbers of elephants in the family groups - matriarch, babies, youngsters, teenagers. Then with the young males who had been kicked out from the herd just feeding a short way from the main herd.  Interesting to watch the antics of some larger males finding their way into the smaller herds to check out the females.   

Yes there are a lot of safari jeeps but it did not seem as chaotic as in the Yala National Park and I think this is due to the fact that this park has a rather large open area of grass around lakes that allow for the army of jeeps to park by the road and allow for viewing by everyone as there were elephants everywhere.  In Yala once an elusive leopard is found, it's a race on for ever driver to get their clients a sighting and the tracks are narrow and not as open as in Minneriya.

I loved watching the babies, and yes the protective mothers keeping their bodies to the jeep side, but both continued grazing whilst we looked on. Watching elephant behaviour was interesting -  a mother comin out from a bamboo thicket as we approached in the jeep.  We stopped. She stopped. She waited - we didn't move.  Then obviously when she thought it was safe, she signalled to the two younger elephants and one by one out of the thicket they came and crossed the track.

I didn't feel the driver of our safari jeep hassled the elephants at all.  All the jeeps seemed to give them the space. If the elephant came behind the jeep, the driver stopped, waited for the elephant to pass or do what it wanted, before the driver proceeded along the track   The park appears to have designated trails that the vehicles can use and the jeeps generally stated on this track or to the side if they needed to pass.

Its main purpose for this park I think is for wild elephant viewing, but we also saw lots of birdlife around the lake.

We did an afternoon safari from 3pm and I found the seats were very nicely padded in our vehicle but seatbelts I think are optional, but then I was standing up a lot when the vehicle was parked or moving slowly along.

It's not for everyone as it's hot, it's bumpy, but I enjoyed it.

Title: Elephant safari
Text:
Did afternoon/ evening safari here. Over 250 elephant which we were able to get quite close to. Lots of young one too.
Long queue to get tickets but our driver did the hard work for us 
Recommend for families as well as groups.  All the children we saw seemed to be really enjoying it.

Title: The Elephants were amazing
Text: I went on an afternoon Safari as part of a Gate1 tour. The jeep guides knew the best places to see the elephants and we were not disappointed, seeing several herds both at a distance and close up. The park was extremely crowded though with a lot of jeeps, so if possible check with the locals first and try to go during a less crowded time. That aside, it was amazing to see all the elements in their natural habitat

Title: Elephant Commute
Text: We were staying in the park in order to reach sites within the cultural triangle, Sigiriya, Dambulla and Polonoruwa, it was amazing  to see elephants in the wild even just walking down the highway great authentic experience.

Title: "JUST ELEPHANTS & MORE ELEPHANTS"
Text:
"Very Unique Experience "  plenty of wild life Elephants aplenty. Take plenty of water, caps, umbrella, binoculars,  if possible. Beautiful scenery & birds. Booked our tour through Minihini Hotel. Thissa & his staff were FANTASTIC. Thank you  guys.
Cheers Glen W Melbourne Australia

Title: Bad!- More jeeps than animals
Text:
I went  in February. I think what I experienced there happens in most of the other parks close by like Minneriya or Kaudulla. Anyways he driver decided in which park the most elephants were expected. 
The few elephants there were surrounded by eight jeeps or more. The problem is that they dont fill up the jeeps with people so there is mostly one Jeep per person or per couple. I understand that people need jobs here, but this is not a sustainable way and there are better systems in other National Parks. 
Jeeps crowd chaoticly around an elephant and sometimes the driver couldnt get through or just drives by because there is no space to stop. Fumes and noise from the jeeps were constantly around me. 
I saw more animals outside in the country than in this NP. 
Not sustainable activity, no animals or nice nature observed, dusty, hot, polluted and crowded with people and Jeeps. Not recommended at all.

Title: No so big, almost cute !
Text: Our grand'children were delighted to see wild elephants, buffaloes, peacoks, big monitors and cameleons  ...But the adults became annoyed by the traffic jam !  So many jeeps!...Better to be there at the low season....Anyway a bit of rain and mist made the scenery  dreamy, beautiful.  I suppose that we are a bit spoilt by many safaries in Africa.

Title: Vacation
Text: Wow what a great after noon. Set off for a three hour safari and when we were finished we had seen approx 45 elephants in total. Many mothers with thier babies and a few old Tuskers. Very enjoyable and a must do.

Title: So many elephants -
Text: really remarkable.  Take the evening visit - starts at 130 pm.  Not too crowded and so many animals. Take you camera but you dont even need a long lens!

Title: Fantastic meeting with the elephants
Text: Had a private safari tour of the park and we were not disappointed. There were Peacocks and Eagles in abundance and we also saw lots of small groups of elephants. Definitely worth a visit if you want to get up close to the elephants.

Title: Great small national park
Text: We saw a number of Elephants, Crocodile and Buffalo as well as some very rare birdlife. We had an afternoon and early morning safaris. Both worth while

Title: Excellent elephant viewing
Text: We decided to add it to our trip on the way from Polonnaruwa to Sigiryia and did an afternoon safari. There were a ton of elephants and it was a fantastic experience. I think a jeep tour in a private jeep was $100

Title: Poor
Text:
This experience was poor. Inexperienced drivers drived too fast to the elephants along with around forty other jeep drivers. 
 I can tell here safari service is bad.

Title: Don't support this - elephant chasing/ destroying nature
Text:
This was the worst safari I have ever experienced! Thousends of jeeps - in every jeep only two people. The jeeps don't stay on the roads. If they see elephants they drive wherever they want - without worries to destroy the National Park or if there might be nests of other animals. When they spotted elephants they regularly chase them and made circles with the jeeps around them. We saw lot of elephants, but the way we did so made me hardly cry. 

Please go to Udalawale to do a safari and not here - there they stay on the roads and respect the animals and nature! 

Please people in Sri Lanka - stop the way you treat the National Park and the animals - otherwise there won't be any tourists anymore

Title: Not worth it
Text: Cost a lot of money and not worth it. Far too many vehicles with drivers driving like mad men. Hardly saw and Elephant only in distance. In the morning driving on the highway one was right on side of road. No other animals either. Waste of US$100

Title: Good but could be better
Text:
We saw lots of elephants, and the park is a nice setting. I agree with some other reviews that, if it's busy, there are a number of jeeps, and you can smell the pollution from them, which made me feel bad about doing the safari. 

I used fasttur to book in advance. I am not sure whether they are overcharging or whether they charge the standard rate for entrance+jeep hire. But there is no visible benefit from their service, as you still have to wait for the driver to purchase the tickets. If there is a queue, that can be a while. But still, it guarantees you a jeep. They did say an English-language guide would be included, but that was not the case at all. In the end, you don't need one anyway, but I feel they should have given a discount for something they did not provide.

Title: Visit in the morning
Text:
We visited at 8am and only saw a few other jeeps in the park so completely contrary to some of the other reviews here. It took around 90 minutes to find an elephant. Apparently it usually takes only 10 minutes so we were unlucky. Once we found some the driver parked up around 50ft away whilst we watched them.

We paid USD 90 for a private  jeep for 2 people which our driver arranged. I suspect you could get it cheaper if you organised it yourself.

Title: Awful experience
Text: This experience was terrible. Inexperienced jeep drivers driving too quickly to the elephants along with around forty other jeep drivers. Avoid this not least to give the elephants some peace.

Title: The place to see elephants in the wild
Text:
Thoroughly enjoyed our visit. We must have seen between 80 -90 elephants, often in groups of 8 to 10, all females with young. The males are only around in June/July at mating time. 

We did get really close up to them and they did not seem in the least bit bothered by the jeeps and the elephants were not chased at all by the jeeps. The jeep ride is like a bucking bronco. We did not see nearly as many elephants in Yala. 

Don't bother with distant photos with half hidden elephants as you will see plenty up close.

Title: Potentially a fantastic elephant experience.
Text: Minneriya is renowned as a park in which to see elephant.  We were lucky in seeing a large number around the open grassy shores of the eponymous lake.  But beware!  Do your local research before falling into the arms of the first jeep driver!  The elephants move between three parks and are sometimes never here.  Wonderful if you're lucky, but the large number of jeeps does not enhance the experience.

Title: Nice but not excellent
Text: It's nice to see elephants here, in natural habitat and not in "prison" but apart from elephants one can see very limited number of other species (not only for our trip, but generally that's what we have heard).

Title: convoy of 4x4's
Text: This was the most disappointing part of our Sri Lankan tour so far. Scores of jeeps kicking out fumes chasing  the Elephant. No information given had no idea where we were going other than following other 4x4's .

Title: Awesome experience!
Text: Convoys of jeeps travel into the park in the search for wild elephants.  Even though we were out of the gathering season, we saw several groups of elephants, including young babies, at very close range.  It was fantastic.

Title: Great fun!
Text: Took a safari from our hotel. Most of the vehicles have up to four seats, and there are loads in the park all it appeared searching for the same herd of elephants. Its quite a physical experience as the dirt roads are bumpy, but well worth it. We had multiple encounters with single and herds of elephants. Its a must do if you are in the area.

Title: Nice but nothing on Yala
Text: We got see elephants close up but, in hindsight, would have passed this up and just done the safari at Yala National Park. Yala has a lot more to offer.

Title: Amazing afternoon
Text:
We had pre-booked our safari and met the driver at 3pm.  It was busy going into the park but the jeeps soon dispersed.  We saw loads of elephants, peacocks and monkeys.

At times we met up with other jeeps and there seemed to be  a lot of us but everybody needed to see the wildlife  so naturally congregated.  The elephants with babies crossed the road in front of us it was awesome.
Kids loved the jeep and racing with some of the other drivers in some parts.  Really great highly recommended afternoon

Title: Wouldn't recommend
Text: This is one of three 'safaris' we did in Sri Lanka, and was by far the least enjoyable. It seems that there is little regard for the environment or the wildlife as a large number of vehicles thrash around a relatively small area. I had the feeling that the tour was not about the wildlife at all, but about giving tourists a four wheel drive experience - not what we signed up for. The park itself appears to be in a sad state with many invasive weed species; the roads are overused by the heavy vehicle traffic and poorly maintained. We saw a few elephants, but the experience was marred by the volume of jeeps jostling for position. We got much more enjoyment out of seeing wild elephants by the side of the road than we did on this tour - save your money.

Title: Wonderful!!!
Text: So cute! We run And run into The jungle to find elephant... And thanks to our guide, we saw Them!!!! To do!

Title: Safari trip
Text:
So upset with the Safari this afternoon I agree with the man that lives in Kania it was a shambles. Youll go in the same way all 20 to 30 James drive the ages see you feel youre very distant into the park are you actually not gone that far when you get to see the elephants the James entrap the elephants so march its very upsetting. The tourists are revolting and do not respects the wildlife or nature. It was like being in a safari zoo back home Hone. 

On the way out we took a shortcut and ended up on the main road within five minutes so its all a con very disappointing and I feel sorry for the elephant.

 On the way out we took a shortcut and ended up on the main road within five minutes so its all a con very disappointing and I feel sorry for the elephant. I have been on proper Safari is in Africa where they look after the animals and do not have so many jeeps surrounding a wild animal. 

 This is for tourists not for wildlife lovers

Title: lots of elephants
Text: Most enjoyable part of the 14 day trip to Sri Lanka. Had bit of excitement with an elephant. Everyone should go on an elephant safari.

Title: A Great Safari Experience
Text:
This is one Safari experience you shouldnt miss. If youre in the region, then make it a point to keep aside a half-day for the tour. Do get a good guide-cum-Driver to take you around the park.
The park doesnt have many big animals, but the Elephants makes up for everything. They are practically everywhere & easily spotted.
A great experience ??

Title: Overated.....dont waste your money
Text:
The whole experience is very staged and disappointing. The problem is that the vegetation is very high and dense in the park, so while you do see elephants and other animals, they are usually far in the distance and you can only see them through lenses or binoculars. Also the variety of what we saw was very limited. After about 2 hours, all of the jeeps then take you to a large look out point high on a hill. While it was beautiful, again you can only see animals far in the distance unless you get lucky. 

It all seemed very stage like a Disney-world, andino in the final scene. Dont waste your money! We later went to Udawalawe National Park in the south and it was spectacular. we saw numerous animals and birds very close up. It also cost us far less...$30 per person compared to $50 in Minneriya.

Title: Elephants galore
Text:
Although we hired a private Jeep it wasn't quite the intimate experience you imagine. Transfer to the park from the hotel was swift, I'm fairly certain our driver was trained by Lewis Hamilton. Entry to the park is chaotic with the car park heaving with other vehicles waiting to get in followed by a long wait to start moving along a dusty track bumper to bumper. I never imagined eyes watering with dust & exhaust fumes that you would see anything but our expert tracker seemed to know that if there were 30 or so jeeps huddled together there might be something worth seeing.
Once you see the elephants and there are plenty including some only weeks old, all you can do is focus on  them. They switch off the engines and you can watch at close range as they go about eating with their young rolling in the mud.We even saw some tuskers that the guide said are quite rare.
It was a good afternoon & although they probably allow too many vehicles in I wanted to go as much as the next person & enjoyed being so close to the elephants.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: We hired a jeep through our driver (Ceylon insider tours) and decided to do the safari late afternoon as he advised that is the best time to see elephants as they come to the water just before sunset. As soon as we entered the park we saw an elephant at the side of the road. The paths are very bumpy and dusty and there were many other Jeeps, making it quite an exhilarating experience. We spotted a few elephants on our way through to the water, then we were absolutely delighted when we saw several groups gathering by the lake. Some bathed but most grazed. A couple of elephants walked right in front of our jeep. As the sun set we saw two large elephants with tusks. It was a brilliant experience. Highly recommend it.

Title: Breathtaking elephants!
Text: I made the trip to the National Park in July 2018 and saw more than 100 elephants combined all together! Other than elephants I saw some water buffaloes as well. I managed to get a Jeep for 4000 LKR from Sigiriya. I also paid 4500 LKR for the entrance fee for one person. The system works in a way that you pay lesser if you have more people entering the park in a single Jeep. So going solo into the park is the most expensive option. Try to get a few fellow travellers to share the Jeep, if they dont mind, to bring down the price of the entrance fees.

Title: Great Elephant Safari
Text: A must visit, not to miss is you are going to Sri Lanka. Being among literally hordes of elephants, up close.

Title: Amazing afternoon full of elephants ??
Text: I went her in a group of three one afternoon. We were told by our hotel owner than the afternoon is better than the morning for seeing animals. We paid 16,000 for the jeep rental and guide. This was for hotel collection and the whole tour. We saw so many elephants, even a baby one that was only a week old! We also saw water buffalo, eagles, cows some birds like a peacock and some monkeys. The afternoon was brilliant. There were lots of other jeeps but they all seem to be really respectful of each other so you move around them and they move around you. Overall a really great day

Title: Minneriya National Park
Text: Nice park to go for safari early morning 6 am we loved because of only 2 jeeps in the park and rherefpre it was a really good expieroence of the  ature of Sri Lanka.

Title: Massive herd of elephants
Text: Great safari for a couple of hours in the afternoon. Our excellent driver Dilee from Louis tours organizeda driver and took us for a ride. We saw over 250 elephants in great big herds. Wow what a thing! Recommended!

Title: Herds of Wild Elephants around your Jeep.
Text: We booked a Jeep Safari into Minneriya Wild Life Sanctuary in the afternoon, where we saw herds and herds of Sri Lankan wild elephants in their natural habitat. Inside the park you will also come across some wild boar, peacocks,  deer and many more animals roaming freely as nature intended them to live, The elephants gather at the waterholes for drinking and bathing their young and immersing themselves in the river. It is incredible how close these wild elephants come to the jeeps with people aboard, They are very interesting to watch as they wander right pass you and go about their business.

Title: Great elephant safari
Text: There are a huge number of elephants and you can get very close. We saw a baby that was only a month old, and it was amazing to see how protective the females are. Plenty of other wildlife int the park as well make this a really worthwhile visit.

Title: Elephants!
Text: What a beautiful place.  We saw many elephants.  They were close and playing in the water.  Really nice safari.  Was not too crowded either which made it even nicer.

Title: Safari tips
Text: National park with safaris. You can book a safari in advance but you dont have to. At the entrance you find a number of jeeps waiting. We paid 3000 LKR for the jeep, 7500 LKR entrance fee for two persons and 1000 for the guide (english speaking). Compare this to the prices of organized tours and decide yourself. The guide told us the morning tours have higher chances for smaller animals (deers, monkeys etc - the leopard is only very seldomly seen) and some elephants, in the afternoon rides are for elephant sightings. We started at 1 pm. Be prepared for adventures, our jeep got attacked by an angry male elephant!

Title: Breathtaking
Text: Its been one of the best , most beautiful experiences I have ever had ! Nishantha, our guide and driver was amazing and also very thoughtful towards the wild life in the park, always being mindful not to disturb but also offering us a wonderful experience. Its been great being able to see the animals in their natural habitat, I would always recommend that you visit the park in the afternoon, it is the best time!

Title: Great safari
Text: We went just wanting to see elephants in their natural habitat and we were not disappointed. Saw small groups, larger groups, in the forest and in the open lake area. Our jeep driver was very respectful of the elephants and their space, some srivers were not. We also saw a lot of other animals, many different birds (a nesting  flycatcher much to our guide's delight!). Was a great sfternoon.

Title: Good
Text: Safari was a good place to visit and seeing the elephants was nice. Its amazing how the national park is managed.

Title: Beautiful park
Text: So many very cute elephants in one place. Worth seeing it !!!  Its an adventure with four wheel drive!

Title: MADE MY WIFES HOLIDAY
Text:
My wife planned to ensure we visited the elephant reserve whilst in Sri lanka. We were not dissapointed with the 4x4 jeep drive into this great reserve. IOur guide estimated we saw approx 150 elephants ranging from raging bulls to 1 week old baby .
We also saw babies buffalo, Jackals, Sea Eagles, Fish Owls and Peacocks to name but a few.

Great experience, Great day 10 out 10.

Doug and Julie

Title: Amazing, Memorable and so many elephants
Text: We had an amazing experience on our tour of the Wildlife Park.  There were hundreds of elephants to see and admire.  Our family loved it.  We enjoyed the open jeep ride and thoroughly took in the expereience

Title: Tons of elephants
Text:
We were staying at Habarana and its a 15 min drive to the entrance of the National park. The ticket price calculation is a bit weird as all price lists are displayed in the local language only . Three of us in a JEEP cost me SL Rupees 9840 as entrance fees for us and jeep driver  plus SLR 5000 for the jeep rental . Wish the prices were better explained in English as is done at other places. We were lucky to have the services of Kavinda Thushan (kavindathushan888@gmail.com) who ensured that we moved in at the appropriate time ie 3pm and saw atleast 3 large groups of wild elephants , including a solo rogue tusker. All in all we would have seen 70-80 elephants. It is a bit tricky as there is another national park , across the road (name starting with K) . Elephants keep on moving and there are times when sighting wud be nil in Minneriya as all elephant herds would have moved across the road to the other park. 
We spent time till 5:30 pm in the park and saw elephants of all sizes from very small babies to large tuskers. Water buffaloes also inhabit this park and so do peacocks , monkeys and other animals. There is a huge lake inside the park called Habarana lake which attracts all wild animals.
Definitely worth a visit. Take your camera and binocs as they would be handy.

Title: Great if you love elephants
Text: Came on this safari with my partner and our 3 youngest - who absolutely loved it.  We saw plenty of elephants - both on the grass and in and around the water and managed to get some great photographs.  We also saw plenty of birds and our guide was able to spot where everything was and drive us as close as he could.  Had a really enjoyable time.

Title: Elephants, Elephants & Elephants!!!
Text: If you intend to see a lot of elephants enjoying in their natural habitat, eating, drinking and having fun, this is the place for you. Our driver had a contact for the jeep safari and thus we didnt book in advance. The park is vast, full of greenery and spread across nearly 9000 hectares. As it was a weekday, there were not much people, just a few jeeps doing the safari. The site of more than 60-70 elephants at one place, enjoying their time, was really beautiful and satisfying. Plenty of playful baby elephants seen!! There are a lot of bird species as well in the park.
