Our safari driver was sharp-eyed and knowledgeable, spotting and identifying birds at a distance and stopping to let us take photos. The safari took nearly 2.5 hours to complete. All in all, it was worth the price paid for!!

Title: Awesome!
Text: This is a great national park if you're interested in seeing Elephants in their natural habitat. From memory, the price was reasonable and totally worth it, because during our 3-4 hour stint, we managed to see circa 50 Elephants. The Jeep used was very comfortable, and the tour guide was helpful. Definitely one to recommend.

Title: Elephants in the wild!!!!
Text: We saw lots of elephants, monitor lizards, peacocks, wild chickens and loads of birds. There is lots of other visitors but the park itself is beautiful. It surrounds a large lake with hills in the back ground.

Title: A privilege!
Text: There are monkeys, various species of birds and water buffalo a plenty to get you excited but we were very fortunate to see two different elephant herds at close range. The first was a reasonably large herd which were by the waters edge. This herd had many adult elephants and three young tuskers. The second herd crossed the road directly, and very close to, the rear of our stationary jeep. They were almost in touching distance, amazing animals to get so close to. Again we were lucky enough to see yet another mid aged tusker. It is advisable to cover yourself up well and to use plenty of sun cream as the jeep is open top and the sun is unrelenting. A must do activity for anyone lucky enough to get the opportunity to do so.

Title: Elephants, elephants, elephants
Text: When we visited late afternoon in late March there were dozens of elephants making their way from the forest to  the lake and we were quite close to them. In addition there is a lot of spectacular bird life around. The park has leopards but are rarely seen so do not expect a viewing.

Title: A great afternoon safari
Text: Our Jeep driver with five of us aboard took us along some very bumpy tracks but knew where to find the elephants which were plentiful including many babies, either in the scrub or by the water. We were able to go quite close to the various herds which was exciting. Only saw a few deer but its the luck of the draw. Birdlife too was prolific and so colourful especially the Indian Rollers with magnificent blue wings seen as they flew away. Painted storks, herons, kingfishers and cormorants were also spotted. Despite the heat it was a great afternoon at the park.

Title: Jeep safari
Text: We did an open top Jeep safari, pre-arranged by our travel agent so no idea what we paid. It was a great experience, far quieter than some of the other reserves that we went around on our trip which made it feel very authentic. The downside was that we didn't actually see many animals! We were realistic to understand that's the nature of safaris so didn't let it spoil our day and we enjoyed the beautiful park anyway. On the drive back to Dambulla, a wild elephant walked across the road in front of us which made up for it!

Title: Wow, AMAZING
Text: We love wildlife, especially elephants. Have experienced encounters with them in many countries, for us seeing them tied up, & taking tourists for rides doesnt sit well. So.......if you want to see elephants being elephants this is a must do. Words cant describe the exhilaration when you see these majestic creatures appear. MAGICAL. For 4 of us Rs 15000 AUD $120, the majority going to the government! Our guide truly loved his job & was so enthusiastic at showing us every animal in the park. Including big monitor lizards, eagles , peacocks, monkeys, hornets nests, fantastic, didnt see any leopards but over 200 elephants was good enough!

Title: Just jaw droppingly wow
Text:
Weve been on one safari in india to see tigers and have left dismayed and poorer because it of course is down to luck and on on both occasions saw nothing more than a bird or monkey. So the thought of doing a safari to possibly see elephants was not top of our list in Sri Lanka. 

But our driver said we wouldnt be disappointed so we gave it a go. 

First impressions great - we had our own jerk and driver. None of the group squeezing into one huge jeep for twenty with limited views. 

As we entered the National Park and drove around for 15mins I started to recognise in myself that desperation you feel looking for anything, something to make you think you just MIGHT see an animal. After another five minutes we slowed down and poking its head through some palms was a huge elephant munching on some food. 

That alone left us happy and content as it had already surpassed expectations. Amazing 

We then drove around the corner and found ourselves surrounded - literally surrounded by a herd of about 300 elephants. All slowly eating and gradually edging toward a lake for water. 

We saw families, babies and even rare tusked elephants (apparently only about 6% have tusks here). Words cannot describe the experience. We slowly drive around with them for an hour finding it hard to pull ourselves away. We eventually did to drive around another corner of the lake only to have another herd of about 200 doing the same. 

There is nothing more amazing than watching the sunset and these amazing animals calmly go about their business with no fear of humans or the Jeep and most importantly in their natural habitat living wild. 

Make sure you do this. It was an experience of a lifetime and the highlight of two weeks in Sri Lanka

Title: Heaven
Text: Loved this tour. Lots of guides and cars exploring at once but was fine. Hopefully elephants weren't bothered by our intrusion. There were dozens and good to see them in their own habitat

Title: Great Safari to see the elephants
Text:
Great, smaller safari to get up close and personal with the elephants. 

There were tons of Elephants to see and we were able to get really close to them, as there weren't too many jeeps in the safari. 

We also saw water buffalo... but naturally we cared more about the Elephants.

Title: Well Organized
Text:
Overall jeep quality and driver awareness and friendliness were just nice. You have to be prepared to get a bit too deep inside the park to see herds of elephants. Don't be disappointed to see the loners at the start of the safari and get too anxious way too early. :-)

I should say the safari drivers who don't seem well educated were far more cordial and courteous.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: Our driver Chathu from Sri Lanka Wide Tours arranged this at short notice with his friend Amila, a jeep driver at the park. The 2 of them really made this a great experience but you really have to get over the sheer volume of other jeeps at the waters edge where all the elephants congregate to get the most out of this. There were alot of elephants to see including a family with a week old baby. You could watch them all for hours and its a great setting with the lake as a backdrop. Amila managed to get us off the beaten track and away from the masses for most of the trip where we were able to see a variety of birds, monkeys, lizards and deer. There were no bears or leopards to be seen but elephants are what you come to see here for the most part. We came across a wounded elephant alone in the bush on the way back. Apparently the park was aware of it but inter-departmental politics and red tape was preventing something being done about it. The elephant was clearly in pain. Chathu and Amila both called the ministers office in Colombo while we were there and ended up getting something done about it. The calls were flying back and forward to Amila. We were very impressed by his tenacity in trying to get something done about it.

Title: Lots of Elephants
Text: Amazing to see so many elephants in one place, but it was so busy when we were there with other tourists. Jeeps everywhere which did spoil it. We visited some other safari parks later on in the holiday that were much quieter, and for us, a much more authentic experience

Title: Stunning scenery with wild elephants
Text: Amazing jeep tour in this national park full of water buffaloes, grazing elephant families, many species of birds, lizards, etc.

Title: Suprisingly good!
Text:
This park is just off the main road from Habarana to Polynaruwa. We took a jeep "safari" ............. which means you stand up in the back of a jeep, holding on to the roll bars.
Nothing much to see as you enter down a dusty track - but then it opens out to a flat area by the lake, where there are a lot of elephants ..................and a LOT of jeeps!
Some of the jeep drivers could do with better training, as they get too close and spook the animals - but its still goo and there are plenty of birds to see by the lake.
Not really a safari, but quite an interesting drive around for around 2-3 hours.
The good news is that they only allow the jeeps in between 6am and 6pm - no night time drives .................but there are a LOT of jeeps. They need to be careful or they'll spoil this by unregulated commercialism.

Title: Elephant gathering
Text: This NP is interesting from july to october. At that time you Will encounter group of elephant. Next to elephant you wont find too many different species of animals

Title: Definitely worth a visit
Text:
We had a great jeep safari there and our aim was really to see elephants. We managed to see about 100 elephants including quite a few baby elephants. The park also has a variety of birds should you be interested but it was not our top priority. 
We went for safari around 1:30pm which was quite unusual time (normally either 9am or 3pm) but that meant that there were not many jeeps around which was great- perhaps a bit hot but wear appropriate clothes and sun cream and it will be worth it! The tour was organised by our hotel and we paid Rs16,000 from Dambulla hotel pick up

Title: National Park on Speed!!
Text: We were staying in Habarana and had pre-booked a safari in this National Park with Walkers Tours. In short, this was a fabulous experience. The jeep picked us up at the hotel then took us about 20 mins down the road to the park. After a short delay where the driver bought the tickets, he drove us into the park. Pretty much immediately we saw spotted deer then we drove through the jungle for about 20 minutes down to Minnerya Tank and saw roughly 80 elephants in abou 10 different groups (or some were alone). We also saw a huge variety of birds. Our Walkers Tours guide was hugely knowledgable about the bird names, elephant ages etc. We never expected to see so many elephants in a 2.5 hour trip. Brilliant!!

Title: Nice National Park to view Elephants
Text:
Minneriya National Park is on the way to Polonruwa, just around 10 Kms from Habarana town. You have lot of options from jeep drivers and hotels, guest house who can organize the safari into the national park. 

Its best to visit the park in the afternoon at 3 pm as you have better chance of sighting elephants & other animals, birds in the park. The Jeep safari should not cost more than LKR (Srilankan Rupees) 3500-4000 for the entire jeep. The entrance tickets to the park is steep but worth the price.

The jeep can seat easily 6 persons. Check out the jeep before you agree on confirming the same. Go for Jeep which is more open type with good space to stand and view the wildlife. Some jeeps have 2-3 rows of seats which makes the jeep cramped and no space to stand for viewing animals.

The Park has dense population of elephants. You are sure to sight elephants at close proximity specially near the lake within the park. Apart from Elephants there are quite a few birds you can sight near the lake and water bodies within the park. 

The safari is for 2 hours and almost all the Jeep Drivers are knowledgeable about the route within the park and places to sight elephants. The Jeep safari has a pit stop at lake where you can get down and take pictures. There is tower near the pit stop to get views of lake and park.

Overall a must visit place if you are staying in Habarana or near by place.

Title: Elephants in the wild!
Text: Finally managed a life-long dream of seeing elephants in the wild with a visit to this National Park. It is an amazing site however they do get crowded & surrounded with many safari jeeps which seems unfair on the animals. The park is a huge wild expanse and a great experience.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Great 2 hours saw around 50 elephants from 3 days old, infants, juveniles male and female. We were very close so lots of pics. Yes pricey at $70 aus but so is everything.  Driver was good and overall a great adventure

Title: Minneriya National Park
Text: I would recommend to go to this park early morning or late afternoon. Animals are more active. Great place :)

Title: Great safari to enjoy wildlife
Text:
While visiting Sirigiya, we decided to visit Minneriya National Park and it was the best decision we could make.
I have seen but reviews of people saying it was crowded. It must have been we went late during the day, but we just came across 2 more jeeps in the whole safari
We arrived just after 3pm. We were travelling with locals who arranged a safari driver that was at the entrance for only Rs3000 (bear in mind that you may be overcharged if you don't have someone to negotiate it). The entrance fee is almost none for locals and quite higher for foreigners, but still quite reasonable. 
We started the safari and were able stand up on the jeep and get amazing views. The first part of the route is a dense forest, but when you reach the opening, the views are stunning. You'll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. There are also spotted deers roaming around. The driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species. We saw elephants far away, then, a lonely one 50 meters away and then we came close to three, i.e. a mum with the two kids. We were totally amazed at seeing wild animals at less than 30 meters away and suddenly the protective and caring mother charged at us. It was terrifying yet astounding. The mum just wanted to ensure that we didn't hurt her kids. 
We drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deers and when we thought viewings were over we saw a young grey leopard. It was just breathtaking, but the young fellow disappeared before we got our cameras out so it only got imprinted in our memories.
Overall, we spent 2 hours enjoying beautiful views and spotting some of Sri Lankan amazing wild life. Highly recommended.

Title: Wild elephants!
Text:
We did an afternoon jeep tour and it was amazing. We saw two whole herds of wild elephants including a number of babies. Was so magical to see them so close but also in the wild rather than tied up/being ridden.

We also saw lots of monkeys and birds. The reservoir area is beautiful.

Title: Better than Yala!
Text:
For us, this was better than our trip to Yala national park. 
We saw 70 elephants gathering as opposed to 2 lone Male elephants at Yala. And we got lucky, we saw a leopard, we didnt at Yala. I understand that Yala is a huge area in comparison. 
Our guide was very professional, caring for the ecosystem here and extremely knowledgable - the guide joins your jeep and is included in the entrance fee to the park. Enjoy!

Title: Fabulous elephant safari
Text: Loads of elephants - more than we could count.  Shame that there were loads of jeeps too.. Pick up a jeep safari from nearby Habarana

Title: Amazing
Text:
Here you have the chance to get up really close and personal to the wild elephants. We saw a family of 5 and it was amazing, as well as seeing other elephants along the way. We were under the impression beforehand that we would see hundreds of elephants but unfortunately this was not the case, so don't get your hopes up. This did not ruin the experience as it is really amazing to see wild elephants so closely in their natural habitat. We saw about 11 in total.

There are also other animals here to see such as lizards, iguanas, monkeys, water buffalos etc. 

We spent over 3 hours in the safari but the time flew by. A must do if you are in the area.

Title: Excellent
Text:
We organised our own jeep and transport to the park. We arrived earlier than we initially thought we would which worked in our favour. It took a while for our guide to find any elephants but when he did find them there were only about 5 other jeeps around giving us exclusive viewing of these beautiful creatures. When it was time for us to leave the park we came across another herd of elephants but they were surrounded but a huge number of jeeps - I would say more than 50. If Im honest, Im not sure if this is very ethical, I know everyone wants to see the wildlife but I think the amount of people entering the park needs to be limited.

We also saw lots of different birds and lizards. All in all a very nice trip.

Title: So many wild elephants !
Text:
Even with the large number of jeeps, it was a very special experience to see so many wild elephants.  It really impresses on you how social elephants are and how lonely those single  working elephants you see around must be. 

Best moment was seeing a two month old baby and its mum with a security detail of older females.

Title: Excellent Photo Opportunities!
Text:
We went in the late afternoon and saw herds of elephants by the lake.  A fantastic photo opportunity, as we didn't want to visit any of the elephant orphanages having heard about the way some of the elephants are kept.  
It is a shame to see so many jeeps all speeding round to find the elephants, but to be fair they are only doing what we as tourists want, which is to find us a good view of the elephants!
As we were leaving the park we came across a small herd completely by themselves and with no other jeeps around, our driver switched off the engine and we sat for a while watching them, it was the highlight of the afternoon.

Title: Excellent!
Text: My wife and I arrived at Sigiriya and saw the crowds and cost to climb it and decided we would go to Meenniriya instead. Definitely a good call! We saw around 25 elephants, countless buffalo, a samba dear and a chameleon. Best to go in the afternoon. A great experience.

Title: One of its Kind
Text: One can rarely get to see this gathering of Asain elephants else where. It is one of the largest in Asia. the safari can be quite dusty. One needs to have a hat, sunglasses & something to save yourself from the muddy dust.

Title: Brilliant safari
Text: Simply a must. Ensure you get s tour guide that has local knowledge and speaks good English. Gets very busy and a shame you can't pre book tickets. Take something to keep the dust out of your eyes/mouth. Gets very busy which kind of ruins the whole experience as all you see is about another 100 jeeps all racing to the same spot when wildlife is seen.

Title: An absolute highlight, an absolute must-do
Text:
I am not an elephant person.  Never have been.  I would see an elephant or two at the zoo and be ..... meh.  But Minneriya ... ROCKED. MY. WORLD.

It starts with a 30 minute ride in a jeep from the entrance into the heart of the national park.  The roads are good, you can stand up in the back of the jeep and you are racing through the jungle with the wind in your hair; exhilarating!  And we hadn't seen our first elephant yet!

During the next three hours, we encountered lone male elephants (who challenged our small jeep for dominance), a young mum with babies in tow (who was determined to chase us away to protect her babies) and then a herd by the lake.  The herd must have been close to 200 elephants; the sight was mesmerising.  Groups of elephants bathing, males warily standing apart watching the jeeps and each other, baby elephants running excitedly from group to group tooting their little trunks.  It was the most gorgeous experience.

And it is not just elephants, we also saw flocks of birds, a herd of water buffalo and one crocodile sub-bathing.

A brilliant afternoon, we loved this experience so much that we almost considered going back a second time!

Title: Highlight of my Srilanka trip
Text:
This is the highlight of my Srilanka trip....timely in their annual The Gathering......and being able to see more than 100 elephants in the wild.....
I travelled solo and was a joiner on a safari tour.

Title: Minneria National Park
Text:
Worth to see,Luckily we were able to see group of elephants including baby elephants too:-),peacock,buck.
Best time to visit after 3.30 noon,it will take around 2 hrs for full coverage.

Title: Up close with elephants!
Text:
I have been so looking forward to this and it exceeded my expectations! We were picked up from our accommodation and had a 20 minute drive to the park entrance. The roads inside are bumpy and dusty but we were by ourselves for quite a while and it did take a while to find a family group. We stopped and just watched in awe as they ate and move a bit and are some more. We moved on and saw some deer, monkeys and a turtle sunning itself then turned around and the group of elephants had trebled in number. A lot of other jeeps did join us and it got rather crowded but everyone switched their engines off and just enjoyed the view!
I felt really privileged to have had this experience and definitely recommend!

Title: Do not go mid-day!
Text:
We made the huge mistake of starting our safari at 12.  We thought the park was quiet.  We ended up understanding why!  We saw ONE single elephant in our 3 hours tour, and we saw him about 100m from the exit!   None of the other jeeps we passed had seen elephants either.  Talk about a major disappointment, for our 3 kids and us!  I know its nature and you cant control it,  but I wouldve appreciated if they could have mentioned the best hours to visit, at the entrance of the park.  When we got out of the park, there were many, many jeeps that were coming in .  Hopefully for them, and they saw more elephants than we did during the day. 

The entrance fee was 11,000 roupies for the 5 of us (2 adults + 3 children) + 5,000 roupies for the jeep/driver, so this was a very expensive outing. 

We got to see monkeys, birds and buffalos, and the scenery was memorable.  But the lack of elephants was too.

Title: Elephants in their Natural Habitat.
Text: The safari was a wonderful. To see so many elephants in their natural habitat was a real treat. Bring sunglasses and a scarf to cover your nose, and be prepared to be filthy when you are done, as the trails are dusty. The kids absolutely loved it.

Title: Not like the best bits of Africa
Text: Weve been lucky enough to travel extensively and go on safari across Africa (and have avoided private reserves), and whilst there is a great opportunity to see Elephants (Peacocks, monkeys and buffalo). The limited road/track system and volume of vehicles (at one point on our visit there were 40 trucks watching a herd of 20 elephants) means this is more theme park than wildlife experience. However, saying that, the context and countryside is beautiful - but we couldnt help feel that the herd were slightly penned in.....

Title: Like Africa.
Text: You can enjoy the beautiful landscape, it reminded me of Africa, there is a lot of wildlife, specially elephants bt you can also see buffaloes, peacocks, crocodiles, monkeys and more!

Title: Wow!
Text:
Wow, wow and wow!

I have been on safari in South Africa before but never have I seen herds of elephants congregating NATURALLY in their hundreds. So close you could almost touch them but there of their own accord and not through force or any sort of zoo/conservation set up. 

Nature at its absolute best. I highly recommend this nature reserve to all! 

You could sit there all day just staring and would never get bored. Such majestic animals without humans on their backs or chains around their feet. Playing in the water, eating grass and just being elephants!

Title: Lovely national park!
Text: A great safari trip! Saw lots of Elephants and other animals close up and from a far. The park was very environmentally aware and are doing a good job to help wild animal populations.

Title: expensive
Text: we were diving and went to Pidgeon island between dives. it was an expensive ticket at $60 for the 2 of us for 90 min snorkling. If we had not seen a turtle and followed it for 20 min and some reef sharks then i would have felt unhappy with the entrance fee. One other issue was that it would be wise not to get sick on the island as they do not have any emergency first aid - we saw a near drowning where the guy needed CPR and they had nothing, he was lucky one of the dive boats had oxygen to allow him to be eventually shipped off

Title: Pigeon Island National Park
Text:
Pigeon Island National Park is near the Nilaveli Beach in Sri Lanka. This National Park is amongst the 17 national parks in the country, but amongst the only two marine national parks in the entire region. This area is protected due to the aftermath of the 2004 Tsunami, which caused a lot of damage to the marine and coral life. This national park is also known to have the best coral reefs in the entire country! The rocky island is also home to rock pigeons, based on which the national park gets its name.

Diving and snorkeling are two everyday activities done here, apart from safari and hike.

Title: Heaven
Text: Our experience at Pigeon Island was marvellous .It was like heaven all the colourful brightening fish were glistening through the googles .This is a must go destination.WOAHH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Title: Must Visit
Text: A must visit on your trip to Lanka. Its very well organised and snorkeling in the corals is a fantastic experience.

Title: Whether Scuba or snorkling: a must visit
Text:
I was there doing scuba with Nilaveli Diving Centre and my wife joined for snorkling. We both had great time and an amazing experience. We saw a lot of different fishes, also turtles and sharks. Don't miss!
One important point: we did go in the beginning of October, so it was almost off season. Therefore it wasn't really crowded. I recommend to do so if you can.

Title: Snorkelling Heaven
Text: About one kilometre away from Nilaveli Beach, Pigeon Island is perfect for snorkeliing with intact, colourful corals and lots of fish. We saw four sharks and two turtles in the first 15 minutes.

Title: Snorkling adventure
Text: The boat picked us up from the shores of our accommodation and whizzed us up the beach to pay for our trip to Pigeon island - although perhaps they should rename it Crow Island!   I think it was approx 2400 Rupees for a family of 4 ( £20 cheaper than our previous driver quoted too), and 250Rps for a jacket or two. We are novice, so the eperince was fine with us. The people working on the island and our boat driver were very helpful and friendly. Its a shame we couldn't get out further than the immediate area because of the tide but was a nice taster of seeing some colourful fish. A lot of sri lankans seem to just hang out in the shallow parts chatting. Saw lots of jelly fish but this small ones don't appear to sting and a baby shark - probably approaching from the blood from scratching ourslelves on the rocks and coral. The coral is very damaged now since the Tsunami.

Title: The best thing you can do: Avoid it!
Text:
That sounds rude, I know.

It is my first time, that I would have liked to give less than one point, but that's not possible....

I have already been there in 2013. Even six years ago it was not the "hidden gem" anymore but it was not too crowded and one could believe that the guards of the national park might be there to protect the enviorment.

But now it's 2019. 

Masses of tourists were brought to Pigeon Island and it's a challenge to get into the deep water, fighting against arms and legs, paddeling like mad, you can see that there much to much people that doesn't know how to behave in the water or just how to move in the water. We got away from the entrance point as quick as possible and in the deeper water it got better.

Yes, you might see fish. We saw at leat 7 black-tipped-Reef Sharks one Turtle...nothing to complain, one could say.

And we saw tourists that entdered the inner, strictly protected part of the reef, went on swimming while guards were yelling at them, finally climbing the top of the reef and walking on the reef top.

Yes, I complained. I complained why there are no guards that really take care, complained why there are signpostings indicating the fee that is to be payed when someone destroys parts of the reef....but the guards of the so called national park are here to get the entrance fee and to organise the landings of the ships, not to disturb the paying tourists.

No, there are no regulations you have to obey (of course there are, but nobody cares about it).

Yes, there are certain tourists that didn't know how to behave, not really able to control themselves, needing life vests to be protected from drowning, well equipped with long sleeves and gloves that made it easy to touch and finally to walk on the reef.

I really felt angry and disappointed when leaving that island. You might feel the same, if you would go there. Better stay somwhere else...at the beach, at a bar, in the bed....it's your choice...but better avoid a ttrip to Pigeon Island!

Title: Pricey but nice if you can swim
Text:
We didn't understand the contradictory reports, but getting to the tiny island we understood. The two bays are way too crowded with people. However, most locals don't venture out more than 50 meters and if you do, you see quite a lot of fish and some coral. 

It is really overpriced for foreigners. 75$ Park Fees are ridiculous for a family of 4. Charging adult pricing for a 12 year old and the captain of boat #5 on 25 August 2019 decided to drive off with his boat without giving me my change... such ugly behavior for 300 Rps on top of that.

Title: Lucky to see turtles & sharks
Text:
Its an excellent place for novice snorkelers, lots of colourful fish ?? and coral to see. We were lucky to see two turtles ?? whilst snorkelling and as we sat by the water a small reef shark ?? passed by. 
I would recommend persons visiting to have good footwear as there is a lot of dead coral and its spiky. 
With the cost of visiting this island they should provide better facilities.
Will definitely recommend this place and visit again

Title: Amazing experience!
Text:
Snorkeling was very interesting. Not cheap (around $65), but its worth it. 
First, we did snorkeling ourselves, it was very interesting. Fish were very close to my nose)) 
With the help of the guide I have seen a turtle, reef shark and different fish. It was on the other side of the island

Title: Wonderful sealife
Text: I have limited experience of snorkelling but felt very safe in this environment. There are many different types of fish, the coral was magical and we also saw turtles and reef sharks.

Title: Overpriced, but worth the visit once.
Text:
Beautiful yet dying. The coral is on its last legs, theres litter around the beach and its hugely expensive for tourists. 5800lkr for two people + 2000lkr for a boat over and back. The prices seems to vary day by day, we were told one price from people visiting recently and paid more on the day. I think its pretty much up to the ticket office to pick a number daily.

It is beautiful, dont let it dishearten you from visiting. When the sun is shining, youll see plenty of life. Sharks, fish, turtles.  

Its worth a visit, but only once. And soon. The coral will be gone before you know it.

Title: Beautiful island
Text:
Pigeon Island National Park in Sri Lanka

Beautiful island

Pigeon island, is located one km from the coast and the marvelous hotel in which we have stayed: Jungle Beach. It is a national park and a coral reef. Lots of coral dyed in the 2004 tsunami. The place is very beautiful and a destination that attracts local people and tourists. Some people may not like it because it can be crowded and difficult to snorkel in peace, but truly enjoyed. I loved seeing the families having fun, going into the water fully dressed. Mothers, daughters and grandmothers in their saris, so happy. It may not be the best place to snorkel, but is truly beautiful. My daughter saw six sharks and a sea turtles, besides lots of beautiful fishes.

Title: Some snorkeling success at Pigeon Island
Text: Get there early! We were on the first boat there at 8am and the crowd didn't show up for another hour or more. There is a snorkeling area that has a protected reef roped off. The water on this side of the island was a bit rough and there were many jellyfish in the water. You may be able to see reef sharks and turtles if you can brave the waves and jellys. We went to the other side of the island where there is a bit of a cove and were able to do some really relaxing snorkeling. There was no current and quite a few fish to see. Good area for beginners. Be sure to have water, towels, suncream, and snacks (if you want them). There is a bit of cover with some seating but the vast majority of the island is in direct sun.

Title: Amazing snorkeling experience
Text: I have never enjoyed snorkelling or imagined seeing the creatures we were able to see until this trip.  We saw sharks, jelly fish, squid, starfish, sea turtles and many tropical fish.  This was an amazing experience and I highly recommend it when in Sri Lanka!

Title: Nice animals, but entry fee excessive
Text:
Even without a guide it was easy to spot reef sharks and turtles as well as interesting fish.
However the entry fee for foreigners just seems a bit high. We paid 5600, way more than for Kumana. Also the officials explained the fee was higher if you were fewer people which doesn't make any sense to me. Why should one person pay more for entering a protected area than two people? 
In the end we did enjoy our stay though and we didn't regret going.

Title: Swim with sharks & turtles
Text: I have read a lot of negative comments about Pigeon island, and I do agree that it is really sad that the coral very close to the shore has been damaged. We spent 4 hours on Pigeon Island and most of that time was spent snorkelling, first we went to the far side of the Island, if you are prepared to swim out away from the shore and the people then you will be rewarded with coral, shoals of fish of all shapes, colours and varieties, we also swam with 2 large turtles and watched them being cleaned by fish. On the side where the boats stop there is an area sectioned off for snorkelling, there were no people on this side, the coral is not damaged and we swam with a turtle and snorkelled on the surface while 5 sharks (4- 5 feet long) darted beneath us, for me it was a great few hours and an experience I will never forget.

Title: Snorkeling spot
Text: Nice half day trip. Easy 10 minutes boat ride from our hotel Anilana. Beautiful water with a lot of fish. Couldn't find turtle. If you stay this area, worth to visit. Though it's a pretty island, it is pitty to see that many tourists stepping on coral that damages them.

Title: Lots of amazing sea life
Text: We went in August and the ocean was full of jelly fish.  I was stung a few times - nothing serious that wasn't gone within 10 minutes of applying vinegar but it was a bit off-putting.  There is lots of beautiful sealife within easy reach of the beach, so it's well worth a visit.  Go early as it gets crowded in the afternoon.

Title: Over priced and over crowded
Text: Nice to see some tropical fishes, sharks and turtles but I had seen better in other places and frankly speaking it was over rated/over priced and over crowded (like many other turist attractions in Sri Lanka). Paid around 6,000 Rs or 40 USD for two of us for boat/entrance fee (we had our own equipments).

Title: Very sad experience- not worth going!!
Text:
Please save your time, energy and money for something else! 

We are a family of 4 who did a few snorkeling trips in south east Asia as we live in Singapore since 5 years.

Was informed by two diving sites at Uppeveli beach that it was a much better option to visit other diving sites instead of Pigeon island itself as the coral was much damaged and the area overcrowded. I really should have listened to them!!! Really don't understand what's all the hype about this snorkeling site!!! 

A few nice fish on the other side of the island but were not lucky enough to see sharks and turtles... but one thing we saw was the very sad ongoing coral destruction!!!!

Please just don't go and give this island a chance to survive!

Title: Horrible over rated place
Text:
Over crowded / All corals are dead 
Business over boats (only way to get there) make the journey expensive and with few service.

Title: Beatifull fish but corals are mainly gone
Text: The place wasnt that crowdy as expected (we went on the 4th of September). We were a little bit dissapointed by the snorkling (2 spots for snorkling on two sides of the islands). The area fot snorkling is quite small and most of the corals are gone. We were not lucky enouhh to see turtles, but some in our group have seen a big one. There are small sharks (1m) as well but those we only spotted from the beach.

Title: Overcrowded but we still got to see a lot if fish
Text: It's easy to get to and we did see a good amount of fish including a small Blacktip Reef Shark.  Go early to try and get there a bit before the crowds.  They really should try a better system such as time slots to limit numbers. 2 hours was enough for us.  The Sun was intense and there is very little shelter.

Title: They should limit numbers
Text:
Weve just returned from an early morning snorkelling trip to Pigeon Island and we were horrified at the numbers of tourists able to visit at the same time. We got about 15 mins on our own then suddenly the hoards arrived!
There were no patrols to stop people standing on coral at the far side of the island. As a result most of the coral is dead. The side where one is supposed to see reef sharks was tourist soup.
Whilst we understand many people need to make their living from taking boat loads of tourists to this park, if we keep disrespecting nature this way therell be nothing left to see soon.

Title: a turtle and lots of colorful fish
Text: we went snorkeling with the kids, one first timer. the fish were fascinating, getting there was easy. make sure you bring water and snacks for a break in-between.

Title: Completely overcrowded
Text: Sorry but this little island is unfortunately overcrowded. I counted 30 boats and each of them drove several times both directions. 2 places indicated for snorkeling, more people than fishes. The entrance fee for 1 person is 3900 rupies. So the government gets more money out of such a trip than the sevice providers!

Title: Small but very beautiful place for snorkeling
Text:
Not far away by boat, simply beautiful half-day trip, worth for money.
We saw many various fishes, also big ones and maily sharks and a turtle.

Title: Nice day outing
Text: If youre staying In Trincomalee its worth taking a short boat trip ( 1/2 hour) . Gentle waves and with fish , coral and turtles to be seen . Ideal snorkelling spot with young kids or beginners

Title: Must visit excursion in Trincomalee, Sri Lanka
Text: Usually hotels in Trincomalee provide day/half day trip to this Island. You should be prepared for snorkeling with a guide. Deep sea diving also possible. Sea is going to be deep about 50 - 70 meters away and you can see small sharks and turtles there. But the corrals and colorful fish can be seen near to the coast as well. It can be very hot in a sunny day and sun cream/sun glasses, hats and enough water is recommended.

Title: Snorkeling
Text: Having dived around the world, and once having snorkeled with dolphins, this has to be the second best snorkeling ever! The preserved coral (inside the white buoys- where you must NOT go) is wonderful, and yes the rest is a bit damaged, but we saw multiple black-tipped shqrks from a few meters and highlight were several turtles 1.5m directly below us feeding on the coral just at the boundary of the buoys. Amazing sight.... and even sound! Entrance to park for 4 wqs 10,000 Rps (go to counter ob beach), cooperative boat (fixed price) of 2000 Rps and full snorkel gear 600 Rps each (a bit worn but did the job fine). No haggling - all fixed. Thoroughly recommend - unforgettable for us!

Title: Snorkelling experience
Text:
A very quick boat ride from the mainland and you find yourself in a beautiful natural park. The snorkelling has different options.  A sheltered lagoon area withckoads of fish and coloured coral or brave it in the open water and see turtles and reef sharks.  Either way lots of options. 

Don't worry if you haven't packed a snorkel.  You can rent for a few dollars from the boat crew.  

Do everyone a favour and follow the instructions to stay off the coral and let it live another day.... Saw a number too people standing on coral....

Title: Overhyped
Text: Visited in early July after several recommendations that this was the place to snorkel in Trincomalee but was pretty disappointed. Have snorkeled at various locations around the world and the coral here was the worst Ive seen, dying off and a lack of aquatic life made it quite underwhelming and sad. Would not recommend other than nice boat ride out to the island itself.

Title: Good snorkeling
Text: We had a good time. Not too many tourists.  We got thete early. Saw lots of fishes and corals. You have to go a bit farther. We did nit see sharks...

Title: Nice snorkling trip
Text:
We took the boat with several other tourists in the morning and arrived there around 9am. We were provided with the gear by the organisation.
There are two main sides to the island. The side closer to the mainland which had more coral and was a bit rougher, especially closer to noon. We saw a lot of different kinds and sizes of fish but also a sea turtle and at least 2 blacktip reef  sharks. They we're not interested in us are all;)
The calmer side has also a lot of different fish but no fields of coral but patches on the rocks.
Definitly a to do in Trinco. 
Don't overpay and try to share the boat. Around 4000pp for boat, gear and bottle of water is fine. Other tourists we met, paid double pp

Title: HOW TO TRASH A PLACE
Text: We hired the very over priced boat to take us the 10 minutes out to Pigeon Island National Park. Once there on the unshaded Island we put on our snorkel gear and hit the water, well what a disappointment this was as the place was trashed by so many people over time standing on the coral and killing it. If you went out further it improved but seeing we were only using snorkelling equipment it was too deep but I am sure if we had used SCUBA we could have gone to other areas that were not frequented by the Coral Trashers.

Title: Poor efforts by island staff
Text:
The conservation staff joined us on our boat ride to the island. We Snorkeled on both sides of the island .. saw sharks, a turtle and plenty of fish. Much better examples of coral when on a dive trip the previous day. 
Island staff did not speak any English however our guide did. The staff sat at their desk and supervised which I guess is part of their job description. There is still however plenty of trash on the island being a reserve, very surprising.

Title: Good reef experience
Text:
We visited Pigeon island on the 27th May and overall very satisfied with the snorkeling experience. 
However, I would say the experience completely depends on the guide. As mentioned in many reviews, you need to pay for a boat ride and entry ticket for the island. Prices of both are very variable and all of it is bit chaotic, so my recommendation would be to offer what is within your budget. We paid 35$ each including boat ride, guide, snorkeling gear and entrance fee. But we were happy to pay higher price to have a private boat and guide just for 2 of us. Our guide was knowledgeable and showed us turtles, sharks and other fishes. From our past experience in Great Barrier Reef, this reef is small but having a guide to show you the main parts of the reef was the highlight. Much of the reef is damaged/ dead however was also good to see some new corals growing albeit bleached. Overall 1.5 hrs of snorkeling is enough time and tiring in the Sri Lankan heat.

Title: Amazing!
Text: This is a must go to if you are in the area. We saw so much beautiful marine life including sharks, sea turtles, coral and many different fish species.

Title: Lovely Island
Text: Superb spot but in danger of over tourism. We visited on a public holiday and hundreds were packed onto the small beaches and in the water. Despite this one can see the beauty of the place and ideal for beginner snorkellers. There are only certain areas you can snorkel in an effort to protect the reefs. No amenities here so pack your food and drink. Two to three hours is probably long enough for a visit. Remember: take nothing but photographs and leave nothing but footprints in this National Park.

Title: Beautiful
Text: The island is a perfect spot to snorkeling! Lots of fishes, turtles, corals and ... sharks!! Impressive!! The sea is very clean and the environment seems to be very well treated. Certain periods of the day the island can be a bit overpacked with people. Better to go early in the morning.

Title: Plenty of reef sharks to spot
Text:
Went snorkelling on Pigeon island a few days ago and had a great experience.

We went early in the morning (arrived around 8:45am) and whilst it was still quite empty my boyfriend and I began snorkelling and saw three huge black tip reef sharks swimming aimlessly in the shallow water. It was an incredible experience!

To be honest, we didnt stay much longer than an hour because after the sharks, we knew we wouldnt see much to rival them. But both sides of the small island were nice to snorkel in - mainly shallow warm water all around. Definitely recommend.

Title: Amazing
Text: I was a bit skeptical before visiting Pigeon Island as people always claim you can see all these animals and most of the time youre lucky to get a glimpse. Not here! In 1 hour we managed to see 3 turtles, a handful of sharks and many different fish. Some of the coral is damaged from bleaching but I did also see some careless visitors standing on it. Please help protect these places and be mindful!

Title: very nice place for snorkeling
Text:
Very nice place for snorkeling and  relaxing also have nice beach many sharks and Turtles
Boat ride 20 minutes from Nilaveli  even the boat ride also very nice

Title: Pigeon Island Visit
Text: We had a great morning visiting Pigeon island and snorkeling both sides of the island off the small beaches. There is good coral and wildlife to be seen if you are happy to swim 10m out off the beach. Definitely worth a trip if you are in the area. We were there for 3 hours but could have stayed another hour to relax after our snorkeling in the shade and had some lunch. We also got to Nilaveli beach at 830am getting the first boat across to the island beating the crowds into the water.

Title: Amazing snorkeling
Text: Just a short boat ride to a completely different world. We saw sharks, swam with turtles, enjoyed the pretty coral and saw many many coloured fish. The highlight of our holidays!

Title: Pretty island with trash
Text: The island is pretty with beautiful corals, fish, sharks, we even spotted a turtle. However, the back of the island is filled with trash and on the way we saved a turtle entangled in a plastic bag. Part of corals are already destroyed and bleached. Unfortunately we suspect this beautiful island will no longer have corals left in the near future.

Title: Amazing snorkeling; expect sharks
Text: Negative reviews are likely by people who stayed in the dead zone near the beach. Pigeon is one of the best spots on Earth for beginner/intermediate snorkelers to see fish variety. I counted 87 species including Napoleon wrasse, triggerfish Moorish idols, parrotfish and black tip sharks (at one point six around me.) The sharks dont bite (unless theyre hungry). Actually theyre under 2 meters and not aggressive, but dont get close. The wildlife is tame, bad for the ecosystem but great for close fish encounters. A turtle felt comfortable coming within one meter. Coral is returning, especially antler and blue. A few more years without a bad El Nino (warming sea event) would be great. Dont go unless you can snorkel and swim for 15 minutes or longer without touching bottom; you cant stand up beyond 10 meters or so (it kills coral.) No food or plastic is allowed (eat, hydrate and apply sunblock beforehand.) The main beach is best for fish. Swim out between the buoys in the center of the beach  then turn right after the big rock. The bay on the other side has more rocky terrain.

Title: Great experience
Text:
We spend 2 hours doing snorkel and it was amazing, we could see sharks and a lot of different kind of fishes! 

Reccomended to every age and every one whi is visiting trincomalee.

Title: Lovely little island
Text:
The island is just off of Nilaveli Beach and is a 5 minute boat ride. You buy your ticket on Nilaveli Beach from the coast guard and then use one of the guys on the beach to take you across. We paid LKR 6000 for both of us for the boat there and back and the entrance. 
There is nothing on the island (no toilets etc) so be prepared! You cannot take food or plastic onto the island. The island has two places to snorkel off of. One seems to be more predominantly used by locals and was busy but there were a few foreign snorkellers. The other side had a sandy beach bit you could relax on and was nice and quiet. 
When you arrive they will explain to you where to swim. Its a bit complicated but to put it simply: there is an area cordoned off with buoys and you cannot swim in this area. You have to swim straight out, and then on the opposite side of the buoys. We were told that they move this every now and then so that they can try and preserve as much of the coral as possible. 
There is lots of dead coral but thats because of the Tsunami. There are still lots of fish to see and the water is nice and safe for not confident swimmers. We saw sharks too!

Title: Simply Awful stay clear!
Text: This is a truly awful place to visit. The coral is dead and the area you are allowed to snorkel in, is about the size of a tennis court. As a foreigner you pay a premium to visit this site, which looks nothing like the posters that advertise it, which show it as secluded, with swimmers enjoying the company of turtles etc. Its a bland monochrome experience that is over crowded and greedy local hotels are still trying to punt it to unwary tourists. My sons were massively disappointed.

Title: A beautiful island
Text: I WENT TO VISIT IN juin and the time was good for that... In November you can't go as the see is too rough.. Lots of kinds of see corals, beautiful fish.... See weeds,.... Etc

Title: Great Snorkelling, but at a price!
Text:
My friend and I spent a morning out on the island. I went diving and she snorkelled. I got to snorkel a little between dives and was some of the better snorkelling I have done, ever! Lots of healthy corals and many hawksbill sea turtles, black tip reef sharks and many different fish species. The white sand beaches are gorgeous, and crowded! It's sad to see the many plastic straws, bottles, bottle caps and pieces lining the shoreline, even some bags and strings floating in the water. Perhaps more could be done to clean up the area to keep this island beautiful for years to come.
I would bring water shoes as some entry and exit points are full of dead coral, not pleasant on the feet!
It was about 5000 rupees/person to enter. Considering you are only there for about 3 hours and have to pay extra to snorkel, equipment and transport it makes for a very expensive excursion.

Title: Grossly overrated
Text: The corals are average. The fees very high. Okay if you have nothing to do and few dollars to spare. I rather spend time in the beautiful beaches of Nilaveli

Title: One of the best in Srilana
Text: This is a best plave to snorkel and diving. You can see many things. Reef sharks, lot of fishes, sea turtles, corals. For the snorkelling morning time is the best. Unfortunately now most of the corals are destroying. Authorized government organizations are not much aware of it. Specially in weekends they do not limit the boats because island is limited. Think if it is 100 boats per day what will happen ????

Title: Abundance of fish & snokel with sharks & turtles
Text: We spent 2 1/2 hours here which was ample time. Wasn't too busy on a Monday morning. An abundance of tropical fish, schools etc....Saw plenty of reef sharks out near where the boats drop people off. Saw 2 turtles close up and a few others in a distance. Yes there is dead coral but expected at a tourist site, but plenty of no go zones to keep people away from the coral. It was crystal clear ( Apr 2nd). Like swimming in a stocked fish tank. The local guides are helpful telling you where best to see sharks and turtles. The sharks can sometimes just appear from no where as my 10yr old daughter found with one swimming along side her. Dont worry though it wasnt dangerous or anything it was minding its own business. I highly recommend a visit & dont read too much into the knockers who have negative comments.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Unfortunately a lot of the coral has died due to tourism but they are now cordoning off big areas to protect the rest. Lovely to snorkel in, saw sharks, turtles, octopuses, eels, and lots of tropical fish.

Title: Extortionate prices for foreigners - dont bother
Text:
Foreigners are charged 2000 to 3000 rupees for a park pass, on top of 600 rupees per person for snorkelling gear, plus the price of the boat (2000 to 3000 rupees per boat).

Not sure where all the money goes, its an absolute scam.

Title: Don't go there!
Text:
There is absolutely no coral. A least not the coral that is alive... Damn..... So sad to snorkle around a graveyard of dead corals.
No matter what the locals tell you (they really just want to make money after all) there is NO CORAL. Many retards write reviews about how pretty the snorkeling was, are you blind?
For the uneducated ones: What you see there are some rocks, dead coral, homeless fish and tons of plastic waste.
At the ticket office they hardly speak English so very little explanation about the situation. Parkrangers at the island itself also do not speak a word of English (very handy for a tourist spot) so why the hell sell this place as a coralhaven?
A conservation disaster we call this. I hope they close it down and protect it so it can perhaps one day recover. 
Please do not go there. Don't support this.  You'll see more plastic waste then fish.

Title: Snorkling paradise?
Text: Small island, where they do ship out everyone for snorkeling. Okay in low season, but it will be definitely overcrowded in high season.

Title: Snorkeling at Pigeon Island
Text:
Great morning's trip to Pigeon Island to snorkel, about ten minutes by boat from the shore.

Some beautiful fish, a small group of sharks (no more than a meter long) and a great guide in Rihan.  A few small jelly fish to avoid at the end, so good to take some anti-hystemen just in case.

Make sure to wear a tea shirt, or you will get sun burnt.  

Good hotel back at the beach to get a drink / have a seafood lunch.

Rihan then picked us up a couple of days later to take us round the Mangrove Swamps and then back to his mother's house for honest simple local cooking in their village, with a great baked mullet!

Title: Amazing island
Text:
This is a beautiful island with clean water and perfect for snorkel, lots of beautiful fish, star fish and amazing coral. The island is stunning with white sand. Highly recommend it for a day trip. 
PS bring your own snack because theres no food there to buy, normally the resort around makes a take way box with fruits etc. Have fun

Title: Great snorkelling
Text:
Easier to bullet point
1) Price. We paid 4000Rs each for a boat with 5 in it. That included everything
2) Boat out took an hour back 1/2 hour, snorkelling time 2 hours
3) Talk of damaged coral. Yes very true the beach is full of fragmented coral but about 1/2 people there don't know how to snorkel. You DON'T sit upright in the water waving your flippers about, that damages the coral, I saw at least 3 people doing this. Lie flat and flipper gently. If you need to adjust your mask, go deeper and do it there.
4) No litter on the seafloor
5) They restrict you to a narrow area, the rest I hope is pristine
6) Loads of fish. After many years of snorkelling, first turtle and black tipped shark, amazing.

Title: Amazing experience
Text: I visited with my cousins. Wow what an experience. We ware 4 and we got a boat for about RS2000 each, to pigeon island and return.We spend about 2 hours in the island. I suggest u to take a guide for snorkeling, our guide was an ex navy soldier. And he was super guide. It was my first time i dis snorkeling, i was even afraid for a bit coz of the experienced person with us. And u can see much more amazing things with the guide than by ur own. We also got lucky to see 3-4 reef sharks as well. I felt like i was in a paradise for a while, what a feeling inside the water. It is a must in ur bucket list if u r visiting nilaveli.

Title: Amazing snorkeling with reef sharks
Text: Took a morning visit over to Pigeon island, and it was definitely worth a visit. Its well worth getting a guide to take you out for a snorkel, as we saw so much more than we would have on our own. We saw about 6 or 7 big reef sharks, and a huge sea turtle. An unforgettable experience! One thing is to watch out for jellyfish though. We saw quite a few, and did get stung, but it wasnt a major issue (one of the guides got us some aloe Vera to put on it)

Title: Beautiful island
Text: There were 9 of us so we split in two boats and each of them charged Rs.2000. After dropping us, they even asked us for the return trip time for them to come back. In addition a permit needs to be obtained too before travelling. Pigeon island was maintained clean with white sandy beaches and clear blue water. It was just so natural. We enjoyed snorkelling here seeing beautiful fish and corals. But some of us got wounded by the corals. Spent like 1-2 hours on this island. Nice place for some good pictures.

Title: Great Snorkeling!!!
Text: Wow!! What a beautiful place! Fish everywhere in all colours of the rainbow!! Turtles, black tip reef sharks, coral reef, it was fabulous!! Well worth doing on your Sri Lankan adventures!!

Title: Snorkelling experience
Text: We started out early, 8am, as we were informed the island becomes crowded later. The boat took us across to the island, about 10 mins ride. We were given life jackets to wear. On arriving we were kitted out with masks and snorkels and fins. The bay to the front was marked off with bouys to show where it was safe to snorkel without damaging the coral. We saw a lot of beautiful fish but sadly no turtles. We went over to the bay at the rear, which was by now very crowded. We saw similar fish especially if we swam out but felt we preferred the bay to the front so went back. We stayed till midday and caught the boat back. A really pleasant morning with underwater beauty all around us. If you have aqua shoes, I suggest you wear them as the beach is made up of broken coral which is sharp underfoot. You can leave your back packs at a desk at your own risk. Ours were ok. Cost including boat 11.000 rupees for 2 of us.

Title: Great Snorkeling and Pristine Coral/Marine Life
Text:
Excellent clarity of water
Great variety of Marine Life
Excellent and Supportive Ground staff
Superb location which is pristine
Only, get your own snorkeling gear if you can

Title: Worth visiting!
Text: Paid around 30 usd / person for the boat to the island and the entry fee but I can say that it is really worth visiting the island. Is a really great place for snorkeling, the water is clean and you can see a lot of beautiful, colorful fishes. If you go a bit deeper and get lucky you can see sharks also, no worry there arent dangerous. Be prepared as there are no shops, toilets, changing rooms on the island. Most probably there will be lots of tourists, but even so the island is really enjoyable.

Title: Beautiful
Text: A short boat ride takes you to amazing snorkeling.  They take care of your rental equipment and guide you to see sharks and turtles and colorful fish.

Title: Great snorkling in calm waters with children
Text:
Only 15 min (speed) boat ride from Nilavelli Beach Hotel. We took the hotels boat even if we were not guests to the hotel. They leave you at the island and come back to pick you up when you want (national park calls hotel boatsmen and 15min later they are there). 
Nice snorkling with kids! Loads of very different colourful fish. If you want to avoid big crowds: Go early: leave at 8.30 at the hotel so you are one of the first people there.

Title: Beautiful place for snorkelling
Text:
Recommend go here for beautiful snorkelling. Go early in the morning as it gets crowded throughout the day. About 2 hours on the island is plentiful. 

A lot of beautiful fish, and a good chance to see turtles and harmless blacktip reef sharks. Stunning.

Protected coral reef area is very well marked with floating buoyances. Route for snorkel is easy to understand, just snorkel outside all the buoyances - and there is a lot to see. 

We did not see turtles, but a one blacktip reef shark. Other people saw both turtles and shark. When booking boattrip, ask for a guide and price, it might help you find the best spots. But you can very well do without one, or maybe boat driver will do the guiding.

The beach is made of a lot coral stones etc which is a bit sharp, can recommend having slippers for walking on the beach. You can get in water without the need of shoes.

Title: Amazing
Text: The people who ran ran the business were very punctual and made sure we made it to the island safely. We then went snorkelling and saw the most amazing fish and corral. I highly recommend you do this if you are on the east coast of Sri Lanka.

Title: Corals are coming back
Text:
It takes short boat trip (5000 lkr for one person) to island for snorkling. Many local people there at sunday. Its nice to see that coral is coming back in some places. Some area at beach was prohibited. 
Some corals and many fishes. No white sharks.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
It is a beautiful little island, very scenic with clear water.
As previous reviews pointed out, it can get very crowded and I was torn about going to not add to the issues raised.

Title: Great snorkelling place
Text: A short boat ride here from the main land . You will come to this beautiful island for snorkelling! Water is so clear and you can see the coral, fishes and shark even within 100m radius ! Be careful of the coral rocks that may hurt your bare footed feet. Prepare your own towels and water is actually warmth that you can spend time with .

Title: Driving with the sharks
Text:
We visited Pigeon Island National Park recently (boat over to the island was 8100 rupees, 3000 rupees for the ticket for the National park) as we were staying close to it and it was definitely worth heading over to see. 

We got there around 8.30am and were one of the first people to arrive (it got quite busy after 9am with boats constantly coming into the beach) which meant going out to see the wildlife was much easier without loads of people around. 

What we saw when snorkelling was a large array of tropical fish, quite a few black tip reef sharks and we were lucky enough to see a turtle too. 

There are two areas to snorkel in which are both quite different but both had a lot of things to see. 

When entering the water there is a lot of broken coral around so I would recommend bringing some form of footwear to enter the water. 

Unfortunately the coral around the island is totally destroyed over time but some of it is coming back but its still not nice to see. 

I would suggest that its best to stay over there for about 4hrs (the boat captain will ask when you want to be picked up) as time does fly while you are snorkelling. 

Overall though definitely worth heading over for.

Title: Dead corals
Text:
We saw so many beautiful fish, a green turtle and even a shark.
However, we were surprised in a bad way by the condition of the reef. It is deteriorating and they should protect the area more. Too many tourists are coming here. The number should be reduced and bigger area protected from snorkeling and boating.

Title: A total waste of time
Text:
I was one of the first people to visit this place from my family holiday home in front of it in the 1950s
It was pristine  with many colourful Carls teeming with reef fish and spiny lobsters 
IT IS NOW WASTELAND mismanaged ravaged and raped by greedy boatmen and the Dept

Title: Great diving / snorkelling
Text: It's a Heritage site and the snorkelling (reef sharks) is amazing as are the dives (we did two), in one case simply walking off the beach

Title: Snorkeling
Text:
We went to pigeon island to see
Some turtles and black tipped reef sharks. Unfortanetly we didnt see both of them. Sea was rough, corals were beautifull as were the many fish. It was crowded with people and i think it is more experienced snorkle spot because of the waves and at a few points the sea is very undeep. This makes less experienced swimmers damage the corals.

Title: Good Snorkeling experience
Text:
We went as a large family party arranging boat ride, park entry fees and equipment rental in advance.

Pick up was from beach directly outside hotel around 08.30, and then across to the island. Traveling time was around 45 minutes including a stop to collect snorkels etc. 

Island was fairly quiet when we arrived so we were soon out snorkling. We saw a great multitude of different fish, as well as octopus, small shark and some saw a turtle.

As the mornig went on there were more people arriving, croweding into the shallow waters near the island which were quite congested as it was clear that some people did not have much confidence in the water. This ment that the waters were cloudy and visability not so good but for us we swam past to  more open water that was clear with the abundance of sealife clear to be seen.

There are comments on these reviews regarding condition of corral and yes there is a lot that appears dead but i was advised that this was a consequence from the last tragic Tsunarmi and i note beautiful new corrals are now growing, showing off there abundance of colours.

My essential tip fornthis trip is to have some beach shoes that you can keep on in the water as large parts of the beach are blanketed in dead corral pieces that are sharp and uncomfortable to walk upon. 

All in all a great morning trip enjoyed by out whole party

Title: Must visit for the experience, for snorkelling and scuba diving!
Text: Will literally come back only to this Island if I really have to. Amazing Small little gem with beautiful corals.

Title: must see
Text:
you should do that for sure. costs around 10$ -7000 RLK per person to get in there. 

sharks and turtles are always there. plus all fishes you want and lobsters 
we swam for 2,5 hours and thats why were than burnt :( so do use some protection or t-shirt 
no food or water on the island
do not forget to take underwater camera as we did :)

Title: Excellent!
Text: This is a brilliant place to go and I would highly recommend this. If you are 50/50 with your swimming they give you a life jacket to help you. We booked through sea view beach hotel and the price per person was $30 (£22.61) with equipment included and and a speedboat to take us there too. You see all kinds of fish, turtles and baby sharks. Its an amazing experience.

Title: Good experiences for the early bird !
Text:
Pigion Island is understandably a popular spot, both for locals and tourists. It's a small island, situated approximately 20 minutes with motor boat from Nilaveli (more from Trincomale).
It's a nice spot with good snorkling and a lot of colourful fish, sharks (harmless) and turtles. And as a good thing The Preservation Council has guarded parts of the coral reef with floating fences to protect it. Bravo !
The sea was qite calm without strong currents. 
But ! If you decide to go there, do yourself a favour by going early in the morning !!! Around 10.30 the island will be swarming with people which might spoil your experience of the beautiful nature. People were behaving very well, bat again; it's a small place ;)
Have a nice swim :)

Title: Awesome variety of fish
Text: We booked our snorkelling trip from our hotel itself including a guide. None of us are good swimmers, so a guide was a must. Even though we did not see any turtles, we did see a baby shark and an immense variety of colourful fishes. It was enchanting.

Title: Good snorkeling but a bit pricey...
Text: A good one day outing if you are staying at Nilavelli for longer than a day. Black tip reef sharks and turtles guaranteed as long as you arrive early (8:30am departure)

Title: Amazing snorkelling
Text: A bit expensive to get there but well worth it. Amazing snorkelling with sharks turtles etc. Sometimes turtles come to you to play around. Magical.

Title: One of the top experiences in Sri Lanka
Text: Pigeon island has been one of the best experiences in Sri Lanka. Do not forget to have your diving mask and enjoy hours of snorkelling. Dozens of fishes of different colour, sea turtles even sharks &they don't harm swim around you. I will never forget it . It was amazing

Title: Yes!!! With the sharks!!!
Text: First time in my life i was snorkeling with sharks! Unbelievable. So peaceful animals... many colorful fishes, few turtles, clear water. Go for it!

Title: An abundance of sea life!
Text:
We are a family of 5 with children aged 13, 19 and 20. 
Initially we were out off doing this trip as there were reports of overcrowding and reef damage. But on our last day we decided to give it a go. And we were so glad we did! 
Its a beautiful spot, just 20 mins boat ride from Uppuveli beach. Its a national reserve so permits have to be obtained by the boat man en route; a quick job. 
You need to visit both sides of the island to get the most out of it. The boat moors on the side viewed from onshore and u then walk across (a couple of mins) to the back side. The sea life is very different on both sides. The back side of the island has better visibility. Be warned there is a lot of broken coral and it is painful on the feet; if you have beach shoes or wetsuit boots bring them! Short fins which you can hire also work.
We have done a lot of snorkelling/ diving all over the world and based on reports werent expecting much; well what a surprise! The abundance of different varieties of sea life was huge. So many different species of fish, squid, turtles and sharks. We saw 3 (think black tip sharks) at very close quarters on the shore side of the island. On the other side we saw turtles, incl a large hawksbill turtle who we swam with for some time. They have 2 types of turtle in Sri Lanka. 
At the time of our visit there were quite a few jellyfish but then it was just after a storm so its probably not always an issue. They arent poisonous but u may get a mild sting which soon goes. At some times of the year they have the red jellyfish which is poisonous so check before u do the trip. The rangers hut on the island has vinegar which will relieve a sting. 
We really enjoyed this trip which was about 3 hours duration (though you can stay longer; we felt this was about enough). It was good value and well Worth it. ??

Title: Overcrowded
Text: Coral and snorkelling was nice but when we went it was very overcrowded - you could see damage to the coral was fairly severe and ongoing while we were there which was sad to see.

Title: Mixed feelings
Text:
Two friends, my wife, litte son and I went on a snorkeling trip to Pigeon Island. We did the trip from Uppuveli and it last from 8.30 am to 12.30 pm. Deducting the travelling time and waiting time for the national park tickets, only 2 hours were left for snorkeling. After the trip all of us had mixed feelings. On the one hand we were excited, because we saw sea turtles and sharks. On the other hand we were very sad, because due to the mass tourism the nature in and arround Pigeon Island really suffers. The coral reef around Pigeon Island is almost completely destroyed. Apart from watching sharks and turtles the submarine world offers a sad picture. Furthermore most of boats are quite old, i.e. many boats loose petrol and pollute the sea.
All in all we can only partially recommend snorkeling on Pigeon Island. Although, the probability to see sharks and turtles is quite high, the impacts on the nature are terrible. Therefore we wouldn't do the trip again.

Title: Do not go here
Text:
If I could give this place less than 1 star I would. It was heartwrenching to see how they treat the marine life in Sri Lanka. This is a national park and nothing is done to conserve the corals or fish. They had one small plot where you were not aloud to swim because they were preserving corals there.
The whole trip was extremely badly organised. Noone spoke any English. Noone told people not to touch or step on the corals. The locals were standing on coral, shouting and screaming the whole time. I'm not sure if this is because of lack of knowledge and education? If it is this is really something the government should consider teaching if they don't want the whole sea to be ruined. I realize that this is a business opportunity for people who do not have much else, but this is not an honorable way to earn a buck. 

We got there at 8.30 and were one of the first boats. 30 minutes later you could hardly move around it was that crowded. The boats kept coming and going all trough the time we were there, crashing into each other at the beach. No safety whatsoever. The boat drivers didn't speak English and we were just given a broken snorkel and they told us they would come back for us three hours later.
After five minutes in the water fending for your space we gave up and went to the beach. We saw a few fish, clearly distressed from all the commotion and people. This place is dying under water and it is all because of people.
It was so sad to see... Most of the other western tourists we meet had the same feeling.

There were a bunch of jelly fish in the water that sting. Badly. They did not give us any information about this and one girl had an allergic reaction after being stung on the neck. There are also some extremely dangerous jelly fish abit further out... Which we found out after being in the water.

Turtles had laid eggs on the island the previous night and the locals kept running over the eggs, sitting on them and really not giving a f***

It was terrible to see the condition the corals were in and how the locals treated the place. Most of the locals can't swim and walked from coral to coral. The water was extremely murky due to the amount of people.

This trip made me wonder what the conservation area are doing with all the money they get from arranging the snorkling trips. They had one trash can and it was filthy. No place to leave your things. No food or water. It was a mess.

Do not go, for the sake of the corals and marine life please consider not going.

We left two hours early because we were all so saddened by the experience!

Title: Very crowed experience
Text: There is plenty of marine life to be seen here. I saw 1 turtle, 1 black tip reef shark and a multitude of fish. Our issue is with how it is being run. There does not appear to be any control over the numbers. We thought it was crowded on our visit but our guide advised that you can get times where there are 1000 people on the tiny island. Yes there are ropes that cordon off coral reef located within shallow water but people are ignoring the rope and standing on the coral. The first time I saw the turtle people were pushing each other to get pictures of themselves with the turtle, to the point where they were grabbing the shell of the turtle. Yet all this time there is a ranger sat in his hut doing nothing. We have snorkelled in various parts of the world but this was our worst experience. Sri Lanka has a very important marine park here but it is going to be ruined as the numbers visiting are only going to increase as more and more hotels spring up on this coastline.

Title: Half day snorkeling
Text: Get there early in the day and its great. Heaps of fish and coral to see. Go to the leeward side of the island for best snorkeling.

Title: Nice visit although crowded
Text: A nice visit but there isnt that much to see if you are expecting world class snorkeling. Still nice clean beach. Take your own food and drinks though. We spent 2hours there and that was plenty.

Title: Disappointing - not worth the effort
Text:
Set just off the beach - around a 15 minute boat ride away - is this VERY small island, which you can only get to 2 places. Most of it is barred - so don't expect to be able to wander all over it.
We arrived very early on (boat no. 3) and by the time we left there were 15 lined up in a very small bay - so be warned, it gets very busy. There are no facilities there whatsoever either. 
The snorkelling such as it is, was good, BUT the reef has been destroyed by the Tsunami

Title: Fabulous but no lifeguard or first aider.
Text:
Great snorkelling. Safe cove. Water was clear. Very clean beaches. 
The coral is being preserved by areas being cordoned off. Outside of this area you can see cuttlefush and basking sharks and a fellow traveller saw a turtle.

There doesnt appear to be a lifeguard anywhere which is worrying and they have no first aid on island. I thought that if I got into difficulty, that would be it
Good to take suntan lotion and water and towel for sunbathing

Title: So is it a 1 or a 5?
Text:
I was puzzled by the contradicting reviews of Pigeon Island with some rating it 1 and others 5.  So here's the explanation:
1. The bay where everyone heads to is small, massively overcrowded (00's of people) and any coral within 20 metres of the shore has been destroyed.  Anyone who doesn't past here will rate it 1 out of 5
2.  However, once you get past this there is some pretty decent snorkelling. The best coral was to the right as you face the sea so head over there and go out a bit further and there is plenty to see.  I've done plenty of diving and wouldn't be unhappy to see this on a dive.
3.  There is also good fish life here, we saw a Black Tip Reef Shark close up as well as the usual mix of tropical fish.
4. On the side where the boats come in there is a cordoned off area where they are trying to re-grow the coral and you can see an entire bed of new coral.  There is a rope surrounding the area that you can use as a guide - there were very few people here compared to the main bay.  It's good to see what the Sri Lankian authorities are trying to do here.

Title: Close encounter with sealife
Text: All visitors to Pigeon Island go there to admire the sealife on the coral reef. Although we went there during the low season, the place was very crowded; no coffeeshop or bar on the island - bring your own snacks and drinks.

Title: ok snorkelling, crowded
Text:
I agree with both the good and bad comments on here:
