it is crowded, but if you're an ok swimmer you can swim beyond the hordes and there's a wide range of fish, some of the coral retains its colour and it's really lovely snorkelling, albeit in a small area. (By ok swimmer I mean a very strong 8-year-old or average young teen would be fine.) 
There are lots of jellyfish where the boats land, but a guide with a different group said they were harmless. One brushed against my son's arm with no ill effects, one lady was picking them up to photograph (!) However, the sight of so many of them is off putting.

People do trample the coral, and the stamping about does cloud the water near to shore, but to be fair the coral starts at the beach so it's difficult not to stand on any. There were two roped off protected areas. One tourist, the first thing he did was swim to the rope, and duck under it into the protected area, so obviously the rules didn't apply to him.

The boats pull up on one side of the island, this bit is very crowded and the sea a bit choppy, which could put off under-confident swimmers/ young kids struggling to master their snorkels. Walk over the spit of sand to the other side and there are even more people and more kids, but the water is far calmer and lots of people just stand in the water and don't swim, so once you're past them it's lovely and there are lots of fish - whole shoals swimming by. You can apparently hire a guide for an extra SLR 2,000 (about £10) to 'show you the reef sharks, where the turtles are', and I can imagine if he took you to different areas the snorkelling would be amazing. But the standard trip is a good way to spend a couple of hours if you're holidaying in the area - I wouldn't deliberately travel there specifically for this though.

Title: Too crowded
Text:
If you have tried snorkling already, then nothing will impress you here. The reef is practically dead and the visibility is far from perfect. Maybe you'll see a shark or a turtle, but nothing more than that.
Place is definitely overcrowded, which kills the pleasure a bit.
From Nilaveli beach I paid 3.850 rupees to get there.

Title: Don't waste your time, nothing to see
Text: Such a disappointment. We paid 3500 rupees per person (children too) which was a complete waste of money. But more importantly, this island is being destroyed by tourists. There is dead coral everywhere- all over the beach and in the sea. (If you do go, take swim shoes or your feet will end up scratched and cut. I cut my foot in the water). The island is tiny, it has two tiny areas to snorkel from. In both we saw nothing but a few odd fish, -after expecting reef sharks etc. So do not get your hopes up. No one saw anything it wasn't just us. Swimming is awful, everyone kicks you with their flippers and the constant stream of boats coming in creates large waves meaning your snorkel fills up with water. Please don't visit.

Title: Another paradise we are loosing
Text: The island is the target of too many turist and too many boats. Almost all the corals are dead and the island itself looks like a crowd in a city centre. You get the ticket (is a huge paper) at the jetty point and the skipper ask you when he could pick you up and he is there at the exact time. You can't stay overnight and remeber to bring with you water as no shop are there. You may find some tiny jelly fish as well. You have to bring with you rockshoes absolutly. Swimming is nice to see big variety of fish but at the same tiem the large ammount of corals destroyed by the anchors and turist stepping on them. They try to say that the ammount of dead coral is due to the tsunamy, but is evident it is not. I strongly belive that Pigeon Island should be more preserved as it is a clear victim of the travel guides and tryp advisor. The volume of turism there is not sustainable at all in my point of view.

Title: What could have been an amazing experience...
Text:
Visited the island on 01/08 with my family.

I was aware the place is overcrowded and that we had to arrive early. We only made it to the island at 10AM and my first thought was the placed looked more like Picadilly Circus than a natural reserve!

As many others have reported, the water is far too crowded to enjoy. We managed to see a couple of Black tip sharks, a green turtle and some nice tropical fish. The constant noise, splashing and banging will drive all fishes away over time I am sure. Let alone the poor coral being destroyed by careless swimmers.
I experienced the bumping into other "swimmers" like others too.

Authorities should really limit the numbers of visitors in a day if they really have Conservation in mind. Money obviously comes first sadly. Considering the entrance fee and the boating co-operative charges, someone out there is making a lot of money.

I would not go back there again unless I hear some drastic changes had been made.

Title: Another Few Years There Will Be Nothing Left
Text: A 15 minute boat ride from Nilaveli beach brings you to Pigeon Island. We arrived around 8.45 on a Saturday morning. My family went off with their snorkels round an area cordoned off with ropes and bouys (a protected area) there were only a few other people around when the started, it took around 40 minutes for them to snorkel round the whole thing. By time they returned to the beach it was rammed. There were about 30 boats all waiting in the shoreline and there wasnt enough space to put a pin between all the people on this tiny island. It was just getting busier and busier. There were so many people it was almost impossible to snorkel on the other side of the island. Lots of people were ignoring the cordoned off area and were oblivious to the rangers blowing whistles and shouting for them to get out. My family were lucky enough to see a turtle and a couple of reef sharks I saw some brightly coloured fish which was a highlight. There needs to be some sort of limit to the amount of people allowed on the island at anyone time otherwise soon here will be nothing left for anyone to see. Pretty disappointing. My pictures show what it was like before the hoards arrived.

Title: Coral graveyard
Text:
Overcrowded with people, you cant even swim without bumping into another snorkeler. 
The 90% of the corals are dead, you wont see much more than their stoned carcasses, except for a few of them that still have a touch of color. Even though the few fishes to be seen are beautiful and very exotic, it was a mistake of us to go there in the first place and disturb the nature of this tiny island, that must have been an absolute paradise before humans set foot on it. 
For the people that have never snorkeled before, it is for sure pretty much of a great experience. But every footprint has an impact and before going, make sure to know the consequences of it. 
Having been there and regretting afterwards I would advise you not to go.

Title: Overrated and overcrowded
Text:
It's absolutely a nice spot, but not as good as many places in south-east Asia. It will definetely impress someone who has snorkelled only a coulple of times in their life, but if you plan your every holidays focusing on some fantastic places to see the underwater world, it may disappoint you. 

No matter what you're able to see underwater if every now and then you get hit by someone's fin. The place is so overcrowded that it's difficult to enjoy snorkeling. What's more, on one side on the island corals are terribly damaged by people who can't swim and just step on them. I saw one turtle and some fish. Nothing special in terms of snorkelling comparing with the Philippines and Indonesia. 

What I have never seen before was such a huge crowd of people and a complete chaos in the water. It took most of the pleasure of  me. My tip is, if you've seen a lot of good snorkelling spots in your life skip this place or at least don't expect a peaceful underwater paradise, it's not there.

Title: Surprisingly stunning!
Text: An amazing array of beautiful fish - surprises around every corner. Boat hire simple and efficient. Best to explore a little off the beach where there is less foot damage.

Title: Not worth your time and money
Text: The island is sooo crowded you can barely get in the water. All the corals are dead. You can se about 5 different types of fish, but that is it. Don't waste your time.

Title: Snorkeling
Text: Nice place for snorkeling although there were too many people on the island simultaneously. Saw a lot if coral reef fish as well as a couple of reef sharks which was exciting!

Title: Living Aquarium
Text: Fantastic fish - gets crowded so come early! 10minutes from the mainland. Great mix of locals and tourists!

Title: More fish than expected
Text: We took a boat to pigeon island, snorkeling gear was provided. Although still rather crowded (apparently weekends tend to get even busier) we could easily get some space to snorkel and see some really nice fish. The coral unfortunately is nit that spectacular. You do have to take for granted that in the island there is not much place to hide or get some private area

Title: snorkeling
Text: Very nice snorkeling. Wonderful coral gardens with a lot of colored fishes. Possibilities to see Blacktip sharks, turtles and others bigger fishes. Amazing!

Title:  Marine Wonderland slowly but surely vanishing 
Text: We visited this so called magical place and was shocked to see the total neglect of the Nature of which these locals make money. The Island it self  is located short distance away from Nilaveli Town, which is renowned for its pristine beaches. This activity is totally mismanaged and boat service is run by a local Co-op Society . This place is totally overcrowded and to my amaze some local people get into these boats in their Traditional Clothes and totally unaware about the activity ahead. They go like on a Pilgrimage. It is so heart breaking to see that their total disrespect to the Nature . In my mind this is a total waste of money and time for a Western Tourist as some Tour Operators charge exorbitant prices for a non satisfactory experience with the local mass. Government intervention is badly needed for this unregulated operation , I will rather take a walk in these Pristine Beaches and not waste my money .

Title: Beautiful island but overcrowded
Text: Went to the island with a really good dive company, very early in the morning. Got there at 9am and it was already crowded. There are only some spots of shade and no lockers or toilets or places to buy water so make sure to bring lots with you and be prepared to leave things on the beach unattended if you do go snorkelling. It's shocking to see the amount of tourism and what it has done to the island and it's coral reefs. The dive centre may be more money but with that we had a safe place to store our belongings, a guide who looked after us the entire time and showed us sites away from the crowds. He was also very strict about touching coral and keeping away from areas which were cordoned off to preserve the sites. Many tourists were ignoring these though. The coral a bit further out is amazing with an abundance of wildlife. We saw many sharks and turtles. Be sure to go early if you want to see these.

Title: Nice little island
Text:
Nice little island not far from Nilaveli beach. Lots of colorful fish in the water. Please remember to keep this little wonder clean.
You can easily spend 2-3 hours here.

Title: Nice but too crowded snorkeling place
Text:
Very easy to go to Pigeon Island from the main land. We could directly from hotel walk to the beach and book our boat and leave. The boat takes you in 10 minutes to the island and has snorkeling gear for you. It is a lovely place but once we arrived we were quite shocked about the place being already fully crowded at 9.45 am. Simply too many people on the island and in the water. Weird experience since the beaches on the mainland were empty. The snorkeling experience is nice once you pass the dead coral and swim a little more outside of the reef and other snorkeling people. We saw many beautiful colored fish (small and medium size) and even a black tip reed shark. 
We strongly feel that the rules of protecting the coral should be made clear and mandotary to every visitor: do not stand on the ground/coral and do not touch the coral. Else this whole place is dead within a year, given the number of visitors being not instructed well how to treat the coral.

Title: nice small island for snorkelling, but crowded!
Text: We went there as a family, on a rather windy day. Many others were there as well, so many that you were kind of snorkelling in a queue. The tiny beaches were full too.  The coral is nice some places, but quite broken other places. We saw the traditional Indian Ocean fish including smaller sharks, but it was not a spectacular snorkelling experience. And given the crowds I worry for the sustainability of the national park....

Title: Too busy
Text: Just too many people - avoid if you don't like a crush.  Sadly most didn't seem able to swim and many were standing on the coral!

Title: Far too many people on a tiny island
Text: Snorkelling was okay, but way too many people are let on the island so the water was murky around the easy to snorkel parts. And one big toilet too, there being no facilities on the island. The coral was damaged in a lot of places, some nice bits though here and there. Saw a number of different tropical fish species.

Title: Crowded but great fun snorkelling here!
Text: Be prepared for a crazy amount of people: we saw more people on the reef around the island than in the rest of our time in nilaveli altogether, but well worth a visit.  Sadly most of the corals were wiped out by the tsunami, but some are slowly growing back and there are a good range of colourful fish along with the two real highlights: black tipped reef sharks and sea turtles; we got to see loads of sharks, and several large turtles up close! Be warned: it's quite deep out on the reef, and the water can get very choppy, so you might want to take flotation aids for younger children, or a guide to show you around - I strongly recommend Ravi, from the Pigeon Island PADI centre, who speaks excellent English and helped my kids so nicely, and took some fab photos for us, too!

Title: Good snorkelling with reef sharks and turtles
Text: We snorkelled here with our three children age 13,11 and 8. The 8 year old is a strong swimmer but found it quite hard as there was quite a swell in the water. We wished we had taken a life vest from the boat for her to use as it would have helped with her buoyancy. Everyone follows the same path out - here the coral has been totally destroyed. There is not enough advice about not walking on or touching the coral and consequently, many people destroy it. Once you are further away from shore and away from the masses, you can see lots of beautiful reef fish, reef sharks and Green Back Turtles. We really enjoyed it. Getting back to shore is more challenging as you have to go back along a roped area with broken coral underfoot. Go early in the morning - once we got back on shore after snorkelling, it was packed with people. You can snorkel on both sides of the island. There is some shade in the middle of the island but this was very crowded at the weekend.

Title: Ecotourism? Must try harder
Text:
What a shame! It must have been beautiful once but it has been over visited, destroying what makes it special. Yes there are some pretty fish and a few live corals but it is so crowded, I have been in less crowded public swimming baths.
If Sri Lanka want to make eco tourism part of its offer, they have to do better than this.  See the pictures

Title: You must be joking
Text: I went with Shanker of Pigeon Island Dive Centre.  Cost was 5000rps (about $A45 but I suspect locals get there much cheaper).  He insisted I confirm my booking by SMS, then forgot to pick me up the next morning.  This made us late so Shanker got me a place on a later boat (with a defective engine)  from Coconut Beach in Nilaveli.  I had to pay for the Tuk Tuk to Nilaveli although Shanker came too and it was his fault he missed me.  The new organisers were surly and kept asking us to hurry up (for reasons I cannot understand).  We changed boats in mid trip.  I am an experienced diver (400+ dives) and I have rarely snorkelled in worse conditions.  Crowded, few fish, baking sun, poor beach access.  A hugely overused site and most disappointing.  To cap it off the boat to pick us up forgot to do so (he said he had problems with petrol but I don't believe him).  We had to ask another boat to take us and again change boats mid-trip.  What a shambles and lousy swimming too.

Title: Good snorkelling
Text: We booked through our hotel and were picked up by boat from the beach. The hotel supplied the snorkelling equipment. There was a wide variety of fish to see and although it was busy you could swim away from the crowds. The water is clear. We couldn't remember the number of our boat for our return pick up and it was a bit chaotic on the shoreline for dropping off and picking up. Our driver did eventually pick us up and was very apologetic for being late. Enjoyed the boat trip to and from the island.

Title: Beautiful place that's being destroyed, sadly
Text:
Positive points first: we saw some beautiful coral, many colored fish, turtles and reef sharks, very awesome to see! Ideal for snorkeling.

But, the way this island and reef is treated, all the beauty will soon be gone :(

Hundreds of people, 20+ boats. People are walking on the corals constantly. Near the coast the coral is already completely destroyed. But farther out we also saw people constantly hitting the corals and standing on them. 

It's a matter of time before all the corals will die. Then the small fish can't live there anymore. Then medium fish can't feed anymore. Then the turtles and sharks will go away because there will be no food for them. This is basic ecosystem logic. 

If the organizations around pidgeon island don't start to do some serious conservation actions, then they can soon all close their businesses because there will be nothing to see underwater.

Right now pidgeon island is a money machine. It should be about the beautiful underwater world that us humans are allowed to respectfully visit and observe.

Title: Best place ever for snorkelling
Text:
If you are on the east cost of Sri Lanka you should definitely go and enjoy a snorkelling session in Pigeon island! 
The departure will be from Trincomalee by speed boat for 10 to 15mn. There are basically two snorkelling spots but careful because there are a lot of jelly fishes. 
Good point if that we saw some sharks (not dangerous ones) - apparently possible to see some turtles as well... 
Fees entrance (+boat ride) are quite expensive as the rest of the touristic places  in Sri Lanka!

Title: Worth a few hours for great snorkeling
Text: If you are in the area it is definitely worth getting a boat out to this tiny island for some great snorkeling. We saw a huge turtle, lots of reef sharks which we had never seen before and which swam right by us, as well as countless other hugely colourful tropical fish. It is only about a 10 minute boat ride from Nilaveli beach and you can hire the snorkeling gear from lots of outfits in Nilaveli or on the beach

Title: A lot of fish, but boat service was poor
Text:
We went there from Uppuveli beach. We arrived by tuktuk in time. We had to wait for 45 minutes. Then they want to split us over different boats. We told them we did not want that. Then we had to wait for half an hour they told us. We ended up going directly, but with too many people in 1 boat. On the way back we had to switch boat on the middle of the see. Annoying, especially because the boat people were not communicating well. They only have us orders: 'help ', 'quick', 'out, etc.. .
The snorkling was fine, especially at the other side of the island. We did not see sharks or turtles, but a lot of beautiful fish.

Title: Nice snorkeling
Text: A lot of tourists you must arrive at 9:00 when it opens. If you are a good (I mean a really good swimmer) ask your guide to show you the real thing. It is sad that people are walking on corals, how can they do not know it's alive and take so long to grow!!! Please if you go there be careful not to walk on corals....we saw sharks and fishes it was nice...

Title: Early in the morning is best to avoid the crowds
Text: We went early in the morning - leaving Nilaveli at 8:30 am - and managed to avoid a fair bit of the crowds as well as arrive when the water was clear. You can snorkel both sides of the island. The side you arrive on has turtle and black tipped sharks but the other side has a greater diversity of fish particularly if you snorkel out around the little rocks/islands. There is some damage/die off of the coral, particularly close in. However, I was expecting this to be much worse based on the reviews I had read. I really tossed up whether to actually bother going, but it was well worthwhile - saw some amazing reef fish with. a lot of diversity.

Title: Avoid weekends
Text: We have just come back from a trip to Pigeon Island from our hotel Uga Jungle Beach. The hotel wanted 50$ per person to take us 9km down the road to Nivalli beach and to buy our tickets for the boat ride and entrance fee. We called our driver who took us for free!  Anyway the costs are 9000 RS for 2 of us for the boat and the island. The island is a 10 minute boat ride away. There are no facilities on the island - no toilets or shop and the ground is quite stony so take some water shoes if you have them. Our driver advised us to take only our towels and snorkelling kit as you basically leave everything on the shore whilst you swim. We also took some bottled water which was useful. One thing I would say is AVOID WEEKENDS.  It was heaving over there particularly with locals who were all swimming in their clothes and underpants -it was like a Sunday afternoon at the local swimming pool at home!  Unfortunately the water was not very clear - not sure if this was due to the amount of people in it or the recent rains, and it was also quite choppy and difficult to swim the further away from the shore you got. We only saw the normal types of tropical fish and no turtles or sharks unfortunately. We have seen videos from others where the water was much clearer and they definitely saw turtles and more, so the moral is don't go at weekends or when's it's too windy/choppy.

Title: nice snorkling
Text: I was snorkling with my 7 year old son and he loved it. We saw sharks, seaturtles and many different coloured fish.

Title: Love it, but small
Text: I loved it too visit this national Parc, but it is a small island and full with tourists, the coral was also not beautiful, I saw other places with very beautiful coral, a lot is destroyed here, very sad actually! There is not a lot of fish, but I saw a shark, that was amazing!

Title: Pigeon Island alternative
Text: We heard this was an alternative to the busy pigeon island. The spot is a few km's north of Nilaveli beach. First we were taken on a boat trip up the relatively uninteresting river, later snorkling off the coast. Both were mediocre, especially for the price asked (18$ pp). Would not recommend.

Title: Good for snorkeliing with black tip reef sharks
Text: Good for snorkeling. The place is very very crowded. It would be a good idea to reach there early in the morning - around 7am. But we booked the trip through our Airbnb host and they delayed the trip so we were waiting around at the Dutch Bay Harbour till 11am. Also, the boats that carried us there waited only for 2 hours. So, it was a bit short. I believe some people hire a boat for the full day and that would be a better thing to do. We did see lots of black tip sharks. Sadly, the marine life is getting destroyed due to the hordes of people coming in each day, stepping on the coral and damaging it. Also, while in a boat with other tourists, the boat driver was ready to leave without doing a full count and if we hadnt alerted him, he would have left one of the people who came with us behind. So, recommend that you stay with the group once the 2 hours are over.

Title: A sad conservation marine park
Text: If you want to snorkel it is not really worth it. People throw their rubbish anywhere. Most of the corals are dead. We were disappointed especially the price was shocking, for 4 people 16.000 rupees. Absolutely not worth it.

Title: Pigeon?
Text: This is a really nice trip if you love snorkling. It is better to go early morning, a lot of people want to visit this Island. It is wise to bring water shoes as there are a lot of stones. Unfortunately we only saw 1 shark and 1 turtle but we had a blast. We paid in total $70 for the four of us.

Title: Sharks
Text: Some of the best snorkelling we've done and seeing 3 large black tipped reef sharks was amazing. We were glad to see coral protection areas as a lot of the coral has been badly damaged.

Title: crowded
Text: Really nice little island. We were the first tourists that day, therefore had the advantage of seeing three sharks and a very tall turtle at the beginning. And some nice fish as well... - That is on the side where the boats arrive. The other side of the island is unfortunately almost dead. There is not much left to see as a lot of tourist just stumble over the corals and don't pay attention to where they are going with their fins... Very sad. It get's really crowded with lots of boats, but you really have the opportunity to see very nice sea life.

Title: snorkeling is at best
Text: This is a must do thing if you are going to Trinco. You will be able see colorful corals and many varieties of fish. Saw a sea turtle and shark as well. One of my best experiences.

Title: Go early!!!!!
Text:
We recently read the reviews on Trip advisor and decided we couldn't miss this trip so we were the first people on the island!  We arrived on the beach at 8am before the island boats depart (8:15) and ended up being the first two people there.  It is pretty and a very quick boat ride away.  There are two places to snorkel = one out front where it is a bit windy though you can see sharks (we saw about 13) and also a LOT of jellyfish which felt really weird - like swimming in a bowl of jello or jelly!  They don't sting though so all good.
The other side of the island is quiet and calm and you can do some nice snorkelling and swimming.
Other people and boats start arriving pretty much on the dot at 8:30 and the masses hit at 10.  Then it was actually crowded and not comfortable at all/  If you are a diver or have snorkelled in other places you might not see much but it is still a lovely experience and worth the trip if you have no expectations.
There is nothing to buy on the island so bring some water and take your rubbish back with you.  They are doing their best to start protecting the site which is a good thing.

Title: Excellent snorkelling!
Text: We loved the snorkelling on Pigeon Island! We saw sharks, turtles, tropical fish, sea cucumbers, coral, translucent with autoluminescense jellyfish and poisonous yellow jellyfish. You could tell a lot of coral was already degraded but quite a lot of the sea was now protected with very active wildlife guards on duty! Keep up the good work! You have to get a ticket from the beach to go to the Island and book a boat that will take you there and back.

Title: Great Snorkeling!
Text:
We visited on a rather choppy day, but the snorkeling was still great. We saw with both sharks and turtles. Lot of amazing fish to see as well.

There are two snorkeling areas. The sharks are in the front area. If you are in the area and love snorkeling, I would recommend.

Title: Pigeon Island snorkel trip!
Text:
Booked the snorkelling trip through our hotel, who arranged with a diving school to take us on a 4hour morning trip at Pigeon island.

3500 Sri lankan ruphees per person (includes boat ride & gear hire)

This small island is beautiful and the snorkeling experience was amazing.

Wide range of fish, sea turtles, sharks, blue water with fair visibility.

No alcohol is allowed on the island.

Pigeon island is one of the cleanest places in Sri Lanka. 

Was not over crowded

Great sorkelling experience!

Title: Pigeon Island
Text:
Beautiful and Devine island if you like snorkelling.
Rough ground and corals but nice experience.
Sun, warm water, short boat trip from the hotel.
You need to take sun protection with you.

Title: Snorkelling for everyone
Text:
Fantastic experience, worth paying for the guide.  Up close with fish, turtles, sharks, and amazing sea creatures.   Best snorkelling experience yet ! 
Ohhh, don't stand on the coral and wreck it for everyone else.

Title: These sharks are safe, but still scary!
Text:
This trip is definitely worth it, if you can manage to get out of bed early.

To get there you need to do the following:

1. Get to Nilaveli beach in front of the Anilana hotel.
2. Buy tickets for pigeon island as early as possible (opens at 8AM and costs $10 per person and $8 per group)
3. The people there will show you to your boat which should cost no more than 2000 LKR (can be shared with up to 6 people)
4. Your boat will have snorkeling gear on it (mask, snorkel, flippers) which costs 600 LKR a day per person.
5. Your boat will drop you off in about 15 minutes but will NOT wait for you at the island. It will be busy bringing people to and from the island the whole day.
6. Agree on a time your boat will take you back, and it will be there.

Following these steps we were first to enter the water. There is an area marked by buoys which you are asked to swim outside of to preserve the beautiful reef.

Within the first 50 meters I saw a shark and a turtle having breakfast! It was absolutely stunning, and the reef was very beautiful. I have diving experience in the Caribbean and this place is definitely on par. I saw a bunch of amazing fish here! After about two hours of snorkeling I left the water and went to the other side of the island which is literally 50 meters away. Here you can also swim and snorkel. I spoke to someone who saw a giant eel! The island is very hot and you are quite likely to get a sunburn or overexposed to the sun. There is some shade but take caution. 

This is a must do activity in an otherwise quite simple town (Nilaveli).

Title: Sad Situation
Text: Destroyed coral reefs, as hundreds of people snorkel here on top of one another, clambering over the reef. Not an experience I wish to have again.  Make sure to take a towel and drinking water as there is nothing on the island, other than swimming with a lot of people.

Title: Sharks & Turtles
Text:
We arrived early at Pigeon island & were lucky to snorkel before the crowds arrived. This way we were able to spot a few turtles & sharks. Afterwards, the place became very crowded & the sight became very ppor. In fact, in our opinion there were too many people in the sea which will certainly have a negative effect on the corals.
Morepver, the boat drivers drive like crazy on & off.
Bring some kind of sandalls or swiming shoes when going to this place. The beach is difficult to walk on.

Title: Fantastic for snorkelling.
Text: A little over crowded at certain times of the day, the swimming and snorkelling area is away from the boating channels and parking on the beach. Expect to pay rs2,500 each for your visit. There are a couple of benches to sit on in shade but no facilities or kiosk so take your own water and food. The snorkelling is amazing with lots of beautiful fish to see. Please take care not to damage the coral.

Title: Lots of reef fish & turtles but the reef is bleached or dead.
Text: We saw many beautiful fish, turtles and a reef shark but this reef needs some love and care and no visitors would help. Very overcrowded conditions for snorkelling with many people standing on the reef. Some sections are roped off to protect it but more needs to be done. We went on the advise of a friend who had been there 6 years before, said it was quiet and stunning snorkelling, a lot has changed in 6 years, not the place we had imagined.

Title: Snorkling
Text: We went at the end of the day. Nice place for snorkling. We saw many different fish, even sharks! Nice boatride.

Title: Nice reef
Text:
We have snorkled and dived many places around the world so actually we didn't have the highest expectations. However we were positively surprised. There was a nice reef and we saw many black tip reef sharks, a few turtles and a lot of other fish. 
We paid 25 usd for the boat and the same per person for entrance since it's a national park. 
I can't give 5 stars. Too many people on the island and no snorkeling instructions. I saw several people standing on the live reef which is sad. 
The reef is completely dead in the area where people enter the water.

Title: wow
Text: go there it really worth it, too many tourist but if you go on the opther side of the island it's another thing. lots of sightseeing of any kind of marine life, also reef sharks.

Title: Dead Corral National Park
Text: If you are after seeing lots of dead corral, and people standing on rocks in the water, perilously close to the last of the remaining corral, and seeing a few colorful fish, all the while with a good chance of encountering lots of jellyfish, well then this is the place for you. What this theoretically beautiful place really needs is an end to the steady stream of careless tourists. I try to avoid places like these, but didn't today. A very sad mistake.

Title: Lovey Sunday Morning trim to do some Snorkling.
Text: We went to Pigeon Island as part of our tour of Sri Lanka with our private tour guide who also came with us to the island. The island is a 10 minute boat ride from the beach. Our guide was able to negotiate a deal for the boat crossing there and back, the tickets for access, hire of snorkels, flippers and flotation jackets for about £35 each, so we paid £70 for the two of us. Well worth the money as when we got there it was busy but not too quiet, lots of locals go there on a Sunday to enjoy the water and to snorkel. If you plan on going then a few musts to remember, the beach is a coral beach so take sometime to lay on, on the Island itself there are no facilities AT ALL. No toilets, apart from the sea, no sun beds, seats or any place to get water. So take what ever you need with you, make sure you take water, sun tan location, any food you want etc. The island itself is small and there are two small beaches, one where the boats all pull onto and the other side just a minutes walk away where you can snorkel. The coral reef is about 80% dead but there are some stunning fish in the sea and still signs of life on the coral. Great place to relax for a few hours to snorkel, lay in the sun and read a book. Place can get busy so go early and work on having a good half day there just to chill and relax. Just remember to take what you need with you as there is NOTHING on the island.

Title: Excellent snorkelling experience
Text: A short boat trip from the beach at The Nilaveli Beach resort, the Island has two snorkelling areas only metres apart on each side of the island.  The snorkelling is better on the southern side. We saw heaps of reef fish and turtles.

Title: A bit disappointing...
Text: When we booked to go snorkelling at Pigeon Island and after reading the reviews, I was expecting to see a huge number of fish. In reality it felt like there were more people than fish. I was expecting to be able to snorkel off the boat (for the price) but everyone walked In from the beach - thus damaging more of the coral. I have snorkelled many places around the world and we went to Nivaveli just to do this but I wouldn't have bothered if I knew now what I knew then. It was quite expensive-park fees alone were more than $10 and for 3 of us it added up to more than $100. The boat trip (only about 10 minutes) was the most exciting part - and meeting people from many different countries.

Title: Amazing coral,sea turtles,reefsharks, beautiful fish (snorkel). UNMISSABLE!
Text:
We travelled to Pigeon Island twice over two days because it was so beautiful. Perhaps this was the best time of year (bit hot! but water clear), and we saw sea turtles, reef sharks, lots and lots (tons) of colourful fish, and of course the coral! Truly a OMG experience for all of us - family friendly.

We ended up renting snorkels and masks and flippers from the boatman, but better if you already have your own (hygience etc at least for the snorkels and masks). Renting snorklels / flippers / masks is 600 LKR per item rented.

There is a great chap on the island, Sujji, who helped our kids and us to really enjoy the snorkelling (we are utter novices). He is v v kind and a real asset for the island.

The first time we went to the island it was around 1200, and the place was pretty crowded. However this didnt dilute our experience - the wildlife totally ignores humans.

The second time we visited at 1400, and stayed till 1730 - as Sujji told us, the afternoon is best for seeing the elusive turtles (and we saw 2!!). Also, the heat means that the human crush is less. This was June so may be different at other times of the year.

What can I say - the singular experience - apart from seeing bottle nosed dolphins at 0630 on a morning shipride - for us all in Trinco! NOT TO BE MISSED!

Title: "Best Tourist Attraction in Nilaveli"
Text:
In all honesty this place is not the best tourist attraction in the area, far from it. 

The island is made up of dead coral which was very sad to see. It is also sad when you consider the measures in place in other countries to save their coral which Sri Lanka have ignored - and are paying the price. Amongst the dead coral there's plenty of plastic waste for you to see.

Cost 6700 rupees for the boat and tickets for 2 and went early to beat the crowds. After about half an hour (9:30am) it got very busy with flippers in everyone's faces and low visibility. There were so many boats that they wouldn't all fit in their designated area! 

All of this coupled with very high winds and low visibility meant we saw plenty of fish but no turtles or Reef sharks.

All in all it was something to do and something to see but it will never compete with other countries.

Title: Please don't stand on the coral!
Text:
A great (half) day trip by boat from Nilaveli beach, about 10 minutes away.  Don't overpay by going with your hotel, you can do it for a fraction of the price - there's no difference in what you get!  We went with Ashok based at Coral Bay Hotel, our dive centre next door told us about him.

The snorkelling is great at Pigeon Island, plenty of fish especially a myriad of different parrot fish, there are corals too, but sadly much of it is dead and damaged.  We were shocked at the way a lot of visitors were standing all over it - do they not realise the damage they are doing?!  It's good that you can swim and snorkel in any areas but really there should be some control/guidance to help preserve what's left of this precious site.  It was also very busy, perhaps again numbers of visitors should be controlled, You can snorkel on two sides of the island - we saw some impressive reef sharks who swim really close.

Take suitable footwear (we used our wetsuit socks) as the dead coral on the beach is hard/sharp to walk on barefoot when you get off the boat especially with the heat of the sun.

Title: Heartbreaking. Ashamed i went here
Text:
Terrible tourist trap. Overpriced at 3500 rupees. To make it worse, they even dare to ask tips after the tour (coconut beach lodge).
But worst of all is of course we re destroying beautiful coral reef, unknowing tourists stepping on the fragile nature. You can just see the coral dying. 
Disgusting commerce.

Title: Great snorkeling
Text: We saw some black tip sharks, loads of coral fish and nice reef. Other visitors saw a couple of turtles too. It's better to go early in the morning, it gets dusty  underwater with poor visibility due to crowd afterwards. I think in general people is damaging the coral reef, we should be very careful and respectful with it.

Title: Overcrowded and dead coral
Text: An unbelievable and unmanageable amount of tourists. The guides and hotels need to tell tourists about stepping on the coral, a lot of it is dead but it is heartbreaking to see everyone trampling over it.

Title: Great place to watch coral life
Text:
Very clean
Nice beach 
Great boat ride to Island 
Travelers need to be careful with broad drivers they might cheat the riders

Title: Blue skies, white sand and tropical fish!
Text: I really enjoyed the snorkling here at Pigeon Island I saw many fish and coral sadly there were  lots of people so watch out for fins in your face. The guys driving the boats are keen to get to the next fare which is why I think they drove so hard and dangerously I seriously thought I would injure myself.

Title: Very busy but maybe worth the trip
Text:
We visited Pigeon Island and did a bit of snorkelling there. 

If you go please make sure you take everything that you need especially a towel and water as there is nothing available in the island. 

The island is only accessible by boat and is about a 15 minute trip from the mainland. There is a charge for the boat and a permit to go to the park. 

It is an immensely popular destination and it's good to get there early. Snorkelling is not bad although where the snorkelling happens is on a lot of dead and damaged coral. The first thing we saw was a Black Tip Reef Shark which was pretty cool. 

As it gets busier snorkelling isn't quite so nice as people are rude and barge past you, kick you with their fins etc. Too many people in a pretty small place. 

It is worth the trip but go early to avoid the crowds.

Title: Beautiful island, not great for snorkeling
Text: The island is beautiful with white sand beaches and blue sea. After 11AM it is very busy. The snorkeling is not that great: you see some colored fishes and coral, but nothing special.

Title: Good snorkelling
Text: Nice little island but not much to do apart from snorkelling. The snorkelling was awesome tho, with plenty of different fish, black tip reef sharks and turtles! Beach is fairly clean but mostly coral so not great from sunbathing on.

Title: Overrated
Text:
Nice place to snurkling. We paid on the beachr 8.250 rupees for entrance, boat transfer an snurkling goggles.

It is very very very very crowded

Title: Snorkeling a must see
Text: We went early in the morning  we arranged everything at our stay Sea Zone Hotel. The boat and snorkeling set was included. You can stay as long If you want. 3 hours was enough. You first start at the back of the island in a bay. A lot of colorful fish and the water is easy. In front of the island is the current strong and you have to be a Good swimmer If you want to swim around the Riff. Your not allowed to swim in the riff. A guard Will whistle you back. We saw a turtle and a shark. Amazing. It is getting crowded later on the day.

Title: Worrying for the future
Text: Pigeon Island is clearly a naturally beautiful place but it won't be soon if development continues to be unsustainable. It was sad to see so much broken coral on the beach. The instructions are very amateur- everyone is just dumped on the island by boat and then told that one side is full of fish and coral and another has sharks and turtles. The fish side is overly busy and difficult to navigate due to slippy, dangerous rocks. People consequently stamp all  over the coral. The other side is cornered off to show some attempt to save the coral. On the fish and coral side, the coral was damaged but I did get to see an abundance of beautiful fish, such as puffer fish and jellyfish. The shark side was extremely rough to navigate and would only be for experienced snorkelers and good swimmers. I did get to witness a big reef shark which was very exciting. Due to the poor clarity of the water I felt like it was just me and the shark, which was really exhilarating. I was glad to visit but am genuinely worried about the future. It was nothing like the coral I've seen in Belize and Australia and the instructions were far less rigorous. With stricter guidelines, the reef will be protected better.

Title: Beautiful place but damaged by careless tourists
Text:
Please be careful to avoid touching corals with your fins !!! No prevention is done to avoid it, that's a pity. Snorkeling is beautiful here but if nothing is done to protect corals it won't last forever!
Don't forget to bring water because there's no shop in the island.

Title: One of the best place
Text:
Best place to do snokerin

We went to Pegion island on 14th August... 

We paid LKR 3500 per person which includes boat ride and light snacks.. you can spend 5-6 hours at this place... Best place to do snokerning and get to see under water colour full fishes, sea turtle, corals and is you lucky then shark also.

Title: Good snorkling
Text: We saw sharks and turtles. We booked the boat on the beach and spend around 3-4 hours on the island and in the water. Beautiful place.

Title: Nice place for snorkeling
Text: A motor boat picked us up from the hotel and brought us to the island for a 3h snorkeling trip (4'000 rupees per person). Even though there are lots of people and the place gets easily crowded we enjoyed a great snorkeling. There's lots of fish to see on both sides of the island. Bring sun protection!

Title: Amazing white sand beach
Text:
Our objective was not snorkeling, so we went inside trekking to see the whole island. The island has a hillock where the pigeons throng 
The water is deep sea green against the white sand which look beautiful.
Best time to reach nilaveli beach is 8am to purchase the tickets for 2 reasons: Beat the heat before the sun is scorching & before the crowd makes the island a fish market.

Title: Best Snorkelling Ever!!
Text: Fabulous place to snorkel cannot recommend highly enough. Black-tipped sharks, turtles and wonderfully colourful parrot fish. Don't miss Pigeon Island!!

Title: Natures Gift
Text: This is one of the best Island Park in Trincomalee  of Sri Lanka. You can go by any of those boats which take you up and down. Worth the visit

Title: Amazing
Text:
This is a must visit place. Great if you can swim and have snorkelling experience. 

Need to buy tickets and then you ll have to pay 2000 LKR for the return boat trip.

You can rent snorkelling gear from the boat people but those are dirty and low quality so bring your own if possible.

I want to thank Police life guards in the island. They are very helpful. Gave us a free lesson and help us to have great time there.

Dont take valuables as there is no lockers and please dont leave any rubbish.

Title: Another Tourist Trap
Text:
It seems easy: just call s/t a National Park and you can ask 25-fold the entrance fee from so called foreigners than from locals. Ad some 2000Rs. for transfer and get shipped to a small nice Island with lots of dead corals and some fish. 

Listen to crying babies an loud locals. 

Snorkeling really is nit worth it. 

I can not recommend this place.

Title: An amazing trip
Text: This an amazing place to visit. It's crystal clear water and beautiful natural surroundings makes to relax.

Title: Snorkeling with turtles and reef sharks
Text:
We organised a trip to Pigeon Island through our hotel from Coconut Beach Lodges for 3,500 rupees. Price included the boat, entry to Pigeon Island ($10), snorkels and flippers (make sure you try the flippers on to ensure they aren't broken), bananas and water. We spent 2 hours snorkeling around the island and saw turtles, a couple of reef sharks and lots of beautiful fish. The coral is sadly not in great condition. Our boat driver minded our belongings on the beach but there are no secure areas so maybe don't bring money or valuables just to be sure. 

We really enjoyed the trip and it definitely wasn't as busy as we were expecting it to be. We snorkeled around the side of the island and were the only ones there. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Snorkelling with sharks and turtles
Text:
Going to pigeon island is a great half day trip! 
We paid 3500 rupees per person - started at 8:45 at uppeveli beach to get our snorkels and flippers then it's a 30 minute boat ride out to the island. You are provided water and biscuits/bananas by the company. 
Once there, there are two sites that they recommend you snorkel in though technically you could probably snorkel around the whole island. 
Underwater it is really beautiful and we saw so many fish, reef sharks and two turtles! Unfortunately there is a lot of dead coral as you swim around however there didn't seem to be the hoards of tourists as described in previous reviews. 
It would have been nice to get a bit longer on the island, we had two hours in the water then spent around half an hour taking photos on the rope swings. 
Overall a great activity to do!

Title: Good coral ...
Text: Got to see a few turtles, sharks and heaps of coral fish... it cost us 10,000lkr for two people which included tickets to the national park, boat ride,snorkelling equipment and guide. Worth the visit ...

Title: Great Snorkeling
Text:
We visted on a rather choppy day, but the snorkeling was still great.  We saw with both sharks and turtles.  Tons of amazing fish to see as well.  

There are two snorkeling areas.  The sharks are in the front area. If you are in the area and love snorkeling, I would recommend.

Title: Amazing... I have no words...
Text:
Pigeon Island is amazing. If you want to do snorkeling in Sri Lanka this is the best place. There are plenty of corrals, fish and other sea creatures. Because of the war took place in the country this was not accessible so probably thats why its so protected. 
i really hope people will look after this site. 
I can see that precautions are taken. Like you cannot go in your private boats as you want, you have to take tickets and then permission. There is a wild life representative at the site so look after. 

Well there are private companies who take you to the island and you can borrow snorkeling equipments from them. they take you to see the corals. 
I have gone with the hotel (Jungle beach). Wella who took care of us is really great. he made sure that we see the creatures. I could not believe i swam with a shark and a turtle in their natural environment. i saw pretty amazing beautiful fish and corrals. 

this is absolute must do things in Sri Lanka

Title: Wondeful day!
Text: We swam with sharks, turtles and fish in all colors - over beautiful coral reefs!  Highly recommended!

Title: Great snorkelling!
Text: Definitely worth a trip if you're in the area. The fish and the coral were amazing to see. Unfortunately I wasn't lucky (or unlucky) enough to spot any sharks or turtles which was a shame, but thing some other people did that morning.

Title: Wow wow wee wa
Text: What an awesome place! I am a bit "snorkel level basic" but even so managed to have a great time snorkelling with sharks, turtles and cheeky looking fish! The corals looked untouched and even though there were many people there was still a great experience! If I could only do one thing near trinco it would be this!!!

Title: Worth the money!
Text: Great experience, worth the money. We arranged with two other people staying in our hotel and shared a boat. We paid around 3200lkr, including snorkeling gear...Boat costs 2000 lkr (the whole boat, not per person) regardless how many people, ticket is 2000 lkr per person, snorkeling gear (fins and mask) is 600. Make sure you go on a sunny day, to have better view in the water. We saw sarks, turtles, corals and loads of colorful fish. Very nice, little island. You can also find some shades on the island to rest.

Title: Crowded....
Text: Nice place, but definively too expensive and over-crowded. It's a pity, while snorkelling, to be surrounded by more humans than fishes....

Title: Snorkeling with sharks and turtles
Text: We saw baby sharks, turtles and all kinds of other fish, felt like in a middle of an aquarium. Never experienced snorkeling like this before. Just amazing!

Title: 'too much corals'
Text: we went pigeon island on may that was amazing moment for us there too much different corals and we snookering there

Title: Lots of Reef Sharks
Text: Very nice trip with a lot of people though. I have seen something between 5-8 sharks including babies from a very close distance. It was really really nice and I recommend it to everybody.

Title: Beautiful young corals
Text:
Lovely to see so many healthy young corals growing and I esp enjoyed seeing the sharks.
I half dived half snorkelled during my trip. Pigeon island gets really busy for a more interesting experience you might want to consider scuba diving with Nilaveli Diving Centre at nearby Crow island - some great coral & lots of underwater life.

Title: Swimming with turtles & sharks!
Text: Amazing experience of swimming with turtles and sharks although the coral is very damaged. Sharks were circling around us and the turtles were right next to us. Worth the experience to see them and go early. We were the first there and it was nice to swim for a bit on our own before the masses of boats arrive.

Title: Snorkelling around pigeon island
Text:
We had a very nice trip with a boat we rented from our hotel(cardamon nilaveli) and a super nice guide who showed us around the island, we were able to go out further the sea because he knew where to go and we saw turtles, sharks and many fishes, after we walked around the island. There might be better spots to dive because of the high damage of the corals but for snorkelling it's fine. 
For sure a really nice trip If you go in the morning before all the tourist groups come

Title: Pigeon Island - no pigeons here!
Text: Rather barren island, so take whatever you need when you visit. Great snorkelling, 2 resident black-tip reef sharks, lots of marine life, some beautiful corals, well worth a trip for the non-diver.

Title: Nice snorkeling
Text:
It nice coral reef. You can see here turtles, sharks, lobsters and more than 300 types of fishes.
Best time to come 8 at the morning on first boat. Only till 9 at the morning possible to see turtles and sharks

Title: There are more tourists than animals
Text: The entrance is very expensive comparing to sri lankan entrance prices and to the experience. We saw elephants. The crocodiles were too far in the  water the birds are little and there were too many jeeps. I expected to see more species

Title: Elephants...
Text: This is a fairly large park within which several companies offer game drives. We booked with Niluka Safari, who were very good. Once in the park, the terrain is quite open, with small plains and the occasional watering hole where animals will congregate. Mainly, you'll see elephants, lots of them which is great, and they'll get quite close too. There are also lots of birds that your guide will spot and point out to you. Others to look out for - the occasional crocodile, land monitors, wild boars and some deer. Altogether, you'll get a good safari experience.

Title: Excellent Safai with Lahiru
Text: We found Lahiru's details from Trip advisor and booked a private safari with him via Whats App (+94762726799), we were not disappointed and saw lots of elephants. He was a great guide offering a private tour in spacious raised jeep. The tour was not rushed or limited on time, we finished when we wanted to rather than set time. Went off the beaten track away from other jeeps. We had time to view a family of elephants (with babies) on our own without 5 other jeeps fighting for the best spot for pics. Arranged pick up and drop off (this is extra to the safari, ask p for a quote).

Title: Udawalawa National Park
Text: A game drive in the afternoon is very exciting. Lots of elephants and many other animals and birds to see.

Title: Humbling experience
Text: This was a great park and to see elephants,crocodiles,lots of different species of birds was just amazing. Baby elephants being protected by the adults. This is a good conservation park and well worth a visit. Our guid was great and we had a vehicle to ourselves.

Title: Awesome time in national park with Lahiru
Text: I found Lahiru via his numerous good reviews on TripAdvisor. We paid 100 for me, my wife and my son for a tour. I can see why Lahiru has lots of good reviews. He was an excellent guide and really made the effort to make sure we went to places where there were not so many other jeeps (couldnt believe how many Jeeps there were on the day!). He was polite and answered all our questions and also gave expert advice on the animals we observed. Highly recommend ??

Title: Great Safari
Text: This is an excellent park. Our driver was well informed and a good communicator. We saw many wildlife from exotic birds to crocodiles. The best however were the single elephants to the large heard. This is a must do trip.

Title: Well managed national park
Text: The big draw here is the abundance of elephants. However there is so much more to see, not least crocodiles, monkeys, birds and if you are lucky leopards. Only downside is the number of tours in operation which can at times lead to congestion which makes you question why you are there at all as it feels like we humans are intruding.

Title: Natural setting to see magnificent creatures
Text:
Apart from having to get up at 3am for the drive there the day was well worth the effort.
The guides were all very friendly but driving around the bumpy roads of the reserve in the back of a pickup truck safari car was uncomfortable.
We saw all the animals from families of Elephants to Monkeys crocodiles water buffalo wild bore and many more.
The visit to the Elephant orphanage at feeding time was my highlight.
About 6 babies at a time let in running grabbing the pipes of the feeding tubes in their mouths to get their funnels of milk was magnificent to witness.
Highly recommended.

Title: Amazing safari with Lahiru
Text:
We enjoyed an amazing safari experience with a private guide called Lahiru. He organised everything for us- our transfer from Ella to the National Park, where we had our fantastic 4-hour safari, and our transfer on to Mirissa. During the safari Lahiru was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic- it was great to have a guide who clearly loved and respected the animals, while making sure we had an incredible safari experience- it was clear he wanted to give us the best experience possible! There are quite a lot of jeeps in the park but Lahiru managed to bring us places to see animals in secluded areas with no one else around where we got closer than we could ever have imagined to lot of animals including elephants- our highlight!! We got some amazing photos and memories to last a lifetime.

We would recommend booking Lahiru if you are looking for a guide for the safari. (We contacted him directly on +94 76 272 6799)

Title: what a park
Text: i had an amazing day at this park...if i may recommend an early morning trip, not only to enjoy a beautiful sunrise in there but also to avoid the queue at the entrance. from what i understood from the driver, they allow only 30 cars per hour...excellent idea actually and it works really well...good variety of wildlife from kingfisher birds to elephants...highly higly highly recommended

Title: Fabulous
Text: This is a well organised and very enjoyable location to visit. The vehicles that take you around are extremely well maintained and comfortable, giving you an extremely excellent view of the park and all its wildlife. Amazing sites, like seeing a nature documentary from the TV. Drivers are helpful & knowledgeable, stopping at locations that will provide all you would need to see. Cannot recommend this place highly enough, a fantastic day out. Absolutely stunning.

Title: Very beautiful park
Text: We had a 3 hour tour booked for 3500 one way a other at the arrival point we got a tour guide in our Jeep . Its low season so was not to busy with the jeeps only 50 in front of us before we went into the park a bit of a problem is there are only one person selling the tickets that a bit of a hold up , if you can take a tour guide with you they have a lot of power to get traffic going again when you see elephants. We saw a lot of animals and birds in that short period

Title: Amazing Elephants
Text:
We had a great day out driving around the park.  There are a variety of birds and other animals to see but the elephants are the star attraction.  We went around 3 PM and spend around 3 hours.  There were plenty of elephants on the lake side and it was possible to get a good view of them.  
We had a private driver take us from Unawatuna and back again on the same day.  The drive each way was around 2.5hours.  I would suggest staying overnight closer to the park and avoid driving as much.

Title: Take this safari, not the Yala one...
Text: This was our first safari in Sri Lanka...our driver was very good..he stopped as long as we wanted to see the sights and animals...he never rushed and we hardly saw any other jeeps. It was an amazing trip and loved it....we went to Yala after and were so disgusted byt the actions of the drivers, and surrounding the elephants ( one with a small baby) not giving them any space...definitely go to a smaller known park as there are hundreds of jeeps at Yala ...Uda walawe was fantastic,,!

Title: Loved the morning safari
Text: It was wonderful to see so much wildlife in its natural environment. We didnt see many elephants but the ones we did were very close so it was really special. Our driver and guide was great in pointing out bird life and other wildlife.

Title: Lahiru Jeep Safari Tour
Text:
We had a perfect day in Udawalawe National Park, thanks to Lahiru who organized everything from A to Z: he sent a driver who picked us up at our hotel near Tangalle, drove us to Ella afterwards and then back to our hotel.
The safari was the most incredible experience in Sri Lanka so far! We saw a teenage male elephant bathing himself and were only a few metres away, four female elephants and one adult male elephant... Besides the elephants, we saw crocodiles, hyenas, different kinds of birds and chameleons, mungos, deers, wild boars and probably more. Almost everytime we were completely alone, not one other jeep was there besides us. When we arrived at the lake, we were the only ones seeing about ten crocodiles, elephants, birds and hyenas at once. Lahiru knows all the roads and places and seems to suspect which animals will be where and when. This made this trip so special. He is also a very funny guy and cares a lot about the park and the animals. Thank you a lot for this unforgettable trip. See you in Cologne... Katja + Halil
You can reach Lahiru via Whatsapp or phone: +94 762726799

Title: Beautiful safari, but also a lot of plastic rubbish
Text:
A beautiful park with a big (men made) lake. Around the lake are many kind of animals. Mainly birds and elephants. 
We had a afternoon drive and have seen lots of elephants, birds, crocodiles and many more. 
I would recommend going here and there are several places to stay close to the entrance of the park. You can arrange your safari right at the entrance by hiring a driver, car and guide and pay for the entrance fee separately. Or you can arrange a package via your hotel. 

The downside of the park is the plastic rubbish people leave in the park. I really cant believe this is happening and not be cleaned by the authorities in a national park. I hope the local people will understand some day the importance of a clean environment for nature.

Title: Great Safari
Text: Great Safari, we saw family of baby elephants, monitor lizards, peacocks, pelicans, water buffalo, two types of monkeys.  Well organised through Kalus Hideaway.  Definitely recommend.

Title: Fun place to Safari.
Text: My wife and I just did a Safari here and it was pretty amazing! We had a great driver that our guest house booked for us (Mansala safari resort), which I highly recommend. The view from the small private Jeeps cant be beat! Youre mostly going to see lots of elephants and some very close up. We saw a ton of wildlife on our 4 hour evening Safari. No lines to get in for the evening safaris so thats a plus and the sunset doesnt disappoint either. Yes, theres lots of other Jeeps around as well. Yes, once theres elephants spotted there will be other Jeeps around, especially at the bigger watering holes. We also got to see plenty of elephants and other wildlife with nobody else around as well along the drive. There are some leopards in the Park, but we did not see any on our outing. Id definitely recommend this to anyone interested in the wildlife of Sri Lanka. It was a super cool experience. We saw, elephants, crocodiles, buffalo, peacocks, tons of birds, monkeys, a few monitor lizards etc...

Title: Safari with young children
Text:
Left our accommodation at 5.30 in the morning and had to queue to buy a ticket for our group. Children up to six are free.
Initially felt a bit like a traffic jam of jeeps but they go different ways and it then got much better.
Had a wonderful moment with a group of female elephants with three babies arriving at a water hole to wash and throw dust on themselves. 
Lots of buffalo, birds, and several crocs. Spent over three hours driving around the bumpy tracks which was enough for the 2 year old.
Worth a visit!

Title: Lots of Elephants
Text:
We visited this park as part of a G adventures tour of Sri Lanka.  We used Mahoora to provide us with an afternoon drive to see the animals.  This park is known for its large number of elephants (approximately 600).

We saw about 40 different elephants, some water buffalos, peacocks, a jackal and some other types of birds.  It was nice to see the elephants because I didn't get to see them in Ghana.

Title: Awesome safari with Lahiru!  +94762726799
Text: Today we had a safari with Lahiru which was really excellent, he sorted everything out, including picking us up & dropping us off after the safari, with no extra costs on the day. We saw so much wildlife, Lahiru has super powers to spot even the smallest animals and excellent local knowledge so you see the most. It seemed we were always in the right place at the right time and mostly away from all the other safari jeeps. We saw so many elephants, including some babies, crocodiles, monkeys, water buffalo, spotted deer, and many birds. Lahiru speaks excellent English and is very knowledgeable and friendly. So glad we did our safari with him! Highly recommend, his WhatsApp is +94762726799

Title: Fantastic safari with Lahiru!
Text: My husband and I booked an early morning Safari with Lahiru, a guide we had read a lot about and he really was excellent. His knowledge of the bird life was superb and we came away having seen so many new species of birds we were amazed! He also helped us with the photography of the birds. We also saw wonderful wildlife and the whole experience was just amazing.  Lahiru is a very knowledgable guide and a lovely person and you can contact him through WhatsApp. + 94 76 272 6799 - you wont be disappointed!

Title: Uda-wowed-me!
Text:
We had a great morning on safari at Udawalale National Park. We got picked up from our homestay (Falcons Nest) at 5am and waited in the queue. Lots of drivers like to go nice and early to get in quickly - the animals are better in the morning & you usually see more.

The sun rising as we travelled through the park was amazing. 

We saw so many elephants - one came so close that our guide had to reverse! We also saw crocodiles, water buffalo, wildcats, jeckalls, peacocks (hundreds of them!) and lots of other birds. Unfortunately no leopards for us but as there are only approx 15 in the whole park, its very unusual to see them!

We barely saw any other jeeps throughout our 3.5 hours in the park and were able to watch the elephants so peacefully with only one other jeep. 

Highly recommend Udawalale if youre wanting to see elephants :) Booking through your hotel/homestay is the best option as they tend to have a guide they use. You can also visit the Elephant Transit Home after and see the elephants being fed!

Title: Wonderful evening safari in Udawalawe National Park with Lahiru.
Text: Great evening safari with Lahiru- if you would like to experience a safari away from the crowds this one is for you. We managed to see about 9 baby elephants and clocked 38 different bird species. We were collected from our accomodation in a timely manner, our group of 3 had a wonderful time after booking a private safari on WhatsApp  94762726799. Our group has been on safari before in Africa and were slightly worried about the crowds but Lahiru managed to position us away from other jeeps, also of concern was animal welfare as a veterinarian but was most impressed by him  saying it is their place not our place and respecting the space of the elephants.

Title: Great experience with Lahiru
Text: We spent this morning at Udawalawa National Park with Lahiru as our guide. Myself, husband and young daughter (nearly 3), we had the jeep to ourselves. We saw more than we could have hoped,  various types of birds, deer, mongoose, monkeys,  crocodile, water buffalo and elephants up close. The best part was when we were by a small pond and waiting for a herd of elephant to come over, including 2 babies - we were the only ones there, it was very special. Lahiru is very knowledgable and can spot all types of animals from far away, he knows the park very well which meant we were never close to other jeeps. Hes also great at getting photos!  It was very special ,  and our daughter loved it. It was perfectly safe for her. highly recommend Lahiru. I organised our tour very easily through WhatsApp +9476 272 6799

Title: Not to miss; beautiful experience and very nice place to sleep
Text:
.The national park was so much more then we wouldve expected! Lots of encounters with elephants, up close!, jungle cats, fat crocodiles, monkeys etc. 
The safari in an open jeep was arranged by our accommodation; Mansala Safari House. Speaking of which. Do yourselves a favour and stay at this place. Close to the park in an elegant house. The comfort level was super high. Beautiful room, quiet airco!!! and the bathroom... shower outside, boutique-style, looking up seeing the palmtrees. 
In the morning, sitting on the veranda and being spoiled with a lovely breakfast served by the owner Tiron. 
Tiron deserves a medal, by the way. My husband forgot his sunglasses in Hiriketya and Tiron was sort of in the area and made the effort to drive there just to pick up the sunglasses. What a hero.

Long story short. Do the safari? Yes! Stay at Mansala? Very yes!!!

Title: Wonderful elephants in their natural surroundings
Text: It was a lovely day out in the Udawalawe National Park.  We toured with park in a jeep with a driver and English speaking guide who was great at spotting eagles, other birds, animals and of course the elephants which were wonderful to see so close up.  It was a great experience and I would highly recommend a visit.

Title: Safari
Text: Lovely area with lots of elephants, plenty of rare and exotic birds. Best time early morning before the heat comes.

Title: Elephants galore
Text:
After reading reviews on TA we decided to take a safari. We simply WhatsApp Lahiru, who has been mentioned many times & he made all the arrangements. 
A driver picked us up from our Villa, we switched into Lahirus jeep at the entrance, did a 4 hour ride around & then back home. It was quite a long day with lots of traveling. 
We found him very informative & had a keen eye to spot thing we could never have seen. 
We seemed lucky in that we saw so many elephants all over the park, including 1 week old calves who could barely walk in a straight line without falling over. 
Also plenty of birds, buffalo, lizards, a few crocodile, red spotted deer, monkeys & giant squirrels. 
The tracks around were rutted in places but thats to be expected. The jeeps everybody seems to use are clearly up to job & make for a great experience.

Title: Magical Safari with a superb English speaking guide Lakshan
Text:
We were staying at a fairly newly opened local hotel: Royal Reach Family Resort (1/2hr drive from the National Park) and their lovely staff helped us organise this unforgettable 3 hour long safari in their hotel jeep. They also promised to get us an English speaking guide who turned out to be an absolute expert on all the wonderful creatures (and plants!) to be seen there. We picked him up at the entrance of the National Park and with our guide on board our safari was off to a great start. 
Lakshan is a volunteer guide and he turned out to be a real expert. He worked closely with the driver to take us away from the crowds into the heart of the park, spotting herd after herd of elephants, filling us with exciting facts and anecdotes about each animal encountered along the way: peacocks perched on top of tall trees, gorgeous birds of all shapes and colours, lizards and buffaloes. Lakshan has a very extensive knowledge of the fauna and flora of Udawalawe Park and he is a skilled educator, too, He taught us how to recognise different species, how to tell the age and sex of the elephants, His enthusiasm for this place was contagious. Lakshan is also very patient so throughout the trip we had plenty of time to take fantastic pictures without being rushed. The three hours we spent with him exploring the national park were the highlight of our Sri Lankan trip. The whole safari for two people was about $60 including the jeep, entrance fees and a voluntary contribution to our guide! I cannot recommend him highly enough. 
If you would like to contact Lakshan - you can find him on Facebook: Lakshan Geeganaarachchi (he was the guide for Prince Edward- Earl of Essex and his wife when they visited Udawalawe last year!). He is brilliant!

Title: Fantastic trip with Lahiru
Text: Just came back from a really great trip to Udawalawe National Park with ace guide Lahiru (WhatsApp +94 76 272 6799). It was our first Safari, so perhaps a little inexperienced but we felt blessed to see a variety of wildlife and have an amazing up-close encounter with several Elephants. Lahiru was a friendly, knowledgable and considerate driver who took extra care ensuring the safety and comfort of my pregnant wife and two year old daughter. Highly recommended!

Title: Overhyped and unorganised
Text: Highly unorganised. The information centre is so further away from the check point that people are easily fooled by the safari guides standing before the check point. The guided tour are very bad we constantly asked the driver for information. Pro tip- the real rates are given inside the information centre which is further inside the check point. There are only a few elephants, buffalos, crocodiles and very few birds. Dont waste your time and money on this.

Title: nice to see
Text:
the Jeep was comfortable but when we arrived at the entrance, around 30 other Jeeps where waiting and when the Gate opens all go at the same time and you need to be at the beginning... otherwise its a big cloud of sand :-)

we saw not that many animals but it was quiet ok. it might be that 10 Jeeps are standing around 2 elefants and the nearest Jeep remains there for a long time so you often can't see them nearer. It's peoples egoism :-)

i think best to go there would be in the morning maybe you can then see more animals, but the landscape is nice too

Title: GREAT PHOTOGRAPHIC OPPORTUNITIES
Text: This is not like a safari in Africa as predators are few. Many of the park's secrets were revealed over a 3H safari. The birding is very good, bee eaters posing for you. The elephants steal the show. We had herds eating grass and crossing the road. At the end of the day there were three elephants, one a baby, drinking at a waterhole; epic stuff. The water areas produced their own attractions, from crocodiles with open mouths to cormorants drying their open wings to lounging water buffaloes. The roads are in fair condition with just a bit of dust to be expected. The park is largely forested with areas of bush. Any number of companies will take you for hopefully what will be as good a day there as I had.

Title: Travel from afar it is worth it
Text:
A well run game park where your driver knows the terrain and will find you much to enjoy and photograph.
Top Tip: If visiting in the afternoon make sure you have a cap or bush hat to shade the eyes

Title: Well worth the visit plenty of wild life
Text: We really enjoyed our visit to Udawalawe Reserve. We had a good guide and driver and we saw lots of wild life.

Title: Safari with Lahiru Prasad
Text: We had a fabulous safari in Udawalawe with Lahiru. He picked us up early from our accommodation in a van to avoid the bugs in the Jeep on the way to the national park. The Jeep he took us in was very comfortable and he provided us with snacks for the ride. His eyes were amazing and he was able to spot animals from far away! We had a great day and saw everything and more than what we came for! Thanks Lahiru. His number is +94762726799

Title: Amazing place just pick your tour well
Text:
Our first safari experience and we really enjoyed it. 
I would say to make sure your guides are good as ours was awful, we got no information other than pointing to the animals and naming them- wow. (Don't know the name but booked through capital lanka/ BH lanka). But this didn't ruin the experience and seeing the elephants in the wild was wonderful. 
The first hour was quiet we maybe only saw 2-3 elephants, peacock and a land monitor. But when we went to the clearing by the lake there was 10s of elephants, birds, spotted deer, water buffalo, a crocodile in the distance, painted stork, and a mongoose. 
Make sure you take water and suncream with you and maybe a snack too as a large part is of course waiting around to find the animals. (Most of the cars we saw are covered but depending on time of day the sun still comes through the sides).
The timing was right for us at about 3 hours, we knew a day tour or several days wouldn't interest us so great taster and amazing to see these animals in the wild.

Title: To save
Text: When I went to visit the Udawalawa National Park, they blocked the road at a place where Udawalawa safari vehicles were and forced me to pay 300 dollars for the safari.  I got rid of them and went to my accommodation and then they provided a car for a very reasonable price.  Don't be fooled by those who block the road as you go

Title: Lahiru - the best safari and guide in Uduwalawe
Text:
We had the most amazing couple of days in Uduwalawe in February, mostly because of our amazing guide Lahiru!! We managed to see Elephants, Monkeys, Crocodiles, Buffalo, Peacocks and even Golden Jackals, Land Monitors, Chameleons, Eagles, Kites and much more! He was so good at finding lots of different animals and wanted to make the Safari as amazing as possible, even letting us use his binoculars! He also helped us find accommodation for the tour at Wild River Side, which was very clean and comfortable and the host made lovely food! 

We would 100% recommended Lahiru for a tour as he is extremely knowledgeable, kind, funny and helpful! 

Lahirus number is +94762726799

Title: Highly recommend Lahirus Safari! Best experience
Text:
We had a safari with Lahiru (+94 76 272 6799 - WhatsApp) as a group of friends and cant recommend it enough! We saw so many animals and he really took us away from the other jeeps and off the beaten path to find them, making it feel so much more special!
