Advise you all to go to minneriya and remove yala park fom your list, as we wait around 3 hours to start our safari there, and was not worth it.

Title: Elephants in zoos VS elephants in the wild - no competition.
Text: The Jeeps bring you up to almost touching distance of the female and baby elephants in this wonderful park. Great way to spend an afternoon and have the camera ready.

Title: Sure to see elrphants
Text: We went to see elephants and saw many. In addition there were wild birds, eagles and monkeys as well as other animals. A very commercial national park overridden with 4 wheel drive vehicles carrying tourists. Very different to Safaris in South Africa. In Africa one sees maybe another one or two jeeps. Here it is in excess of twenty clustering in one place to look at the animals. However this does not seem to disturb anyone and it is nature a usual that continues as well as humans joining the next group of vehicles.

Title: great place to see many elephants
Text: Definitely worth a visit - if you are lucky (which most seems to be), you will see hundreds of elephants gathering around the water holes every afternoon around 2-4 pm. LOADS of safari jeeps, but still worth a visit.

Title: Love Elephants
Text: There were so many elephants and lots of baby elephants.  They were playing in the water and spraying one another.  They Mommas were very protective of their babies.  They were close to the road, so you got plenty of good photos.

Title: Only elephants
Text:
We came here for a safari but, apart from elephants, there is nothing else. Some birds - but none that you cant see out of the park. 
The safari guide/driver was non-communicative and didnt tell us where we were going, what we were seeing or any other type of info. 
We expected the drive to last from 14:30 tp 18:00 but we headed back at 16:30 and never stopped again, even when we saw some deer in the distance. 
Also worrying was the attitude of the multitude of jeeps towards the herds of elephants. Although the animals were extremely calm, a very short security distance was kept (with cars pulling up at 4-5 m from a female) and the jeeps blocked a herds way when they were obviously trying to get to the bushed area. 

On the whole:
- drivers should be trained in pr skills and told to be communicative
- it should be clearer that the safari is home only to elephants
- an ethical guide should be implemented so that there arent so many jeeps crowding the animals and a respectful distance must be kept

Title: Rustic elephant watching
Text: This is not a luxury well run park, but it has its charm. You organize a guide with an open jeep outside of the park. You travel with a convey of other open jeeps down bump roads through the jungle to large open water bodies where you are going to see ALOT of elephants. They don't go extremely close to the elephants,its good that they give them space.There were lots of babies there too.I would recommend going at 4pm as the elephants are active then and you might have a chance of spotting a leopard too.

Title: Amazing ride to the elephants
Text:
This is a crazy fast ride to the national park to see the elephants and other animals and birds. We had to hand on in the back of the jeep but it was a lot of fun. You drive on dirt tracks and through water and lots of mud. Some jeeps were getting bogged,Mobutu luckily our driver was great and we didn't have any problems. It was all worth it to see the many hearts of elephants with babies also. We would have seen over 50 elephants and also saw 2 young male elephants having a fight which was very interesting.
I would definately recommend this attraction.

Title: Ticket item elephants roaming
Text: Well apart from the traffic jam of jeeps this is an amazing experience. Our guide explained the bird life as well as getting us close to a group of elephants with their young. We just watched as they grazed and played it was fantastic and something with doing. This park is one of the smaller ones with no leopards but evert pythons else. If you want a close experience with elephants in the free this should be added to your wish list. Thank you to our driver and team.

Title: Wow!
Text: If you want to see elephants in the wild then please visit this place a not an orphanage in which they are fenced and caged. It was truly amazing to see and remember.

Title: Get your safari on
Text: Our driver recommended this. We were going to wait until we got to another location in Sri Lanka but were glad we didnt. Great fun standing in the Jeep and seeing an abundance of wildlife in their natural habitat.

Title: Really enjoyable safari
Text: Lovely safari. Would recommend going early morning or late afternoon due to the heat though. Saw lots of elephants, monkeys, water buffalo and wild birds. Was a lovely afternoon out.

Title: a great trip
Text:
you cannot go to Sri Lanka and not see the elephants.
good trip in jeeps with open tops. each jeep seated four and there was plenty f room to stand up and take photos.
some real close ups of the elephants
about 2 hours cost about £35 each

Title: A bit disappointed
Text:
Was really looking forward to this safari but all we saw are PELICANS, ELEPHANTS, INGRIDS and some BUFFALOS

After all those.crazy bumpy rides, that's.all we saw... at some point we got bored looking at the same animals and.wished we were just heading back .

It must be the draught season so most animals are Hiding but crap! This isn't the safari I was expecting. Might as well I visit the zoo

Title: Lots and lots of elephants
Text: After a rickety rackety jeep ride we saw lots if elephants and quite a few birds too. These though were out numbered by jeeps.

Title: Fab time, saw lots of elephants.
Text: This trip was one of the highlights of our Sri-Lanka trip and well worth a visit.  We arrived just after lunch so there were plenty of jeeps available, being only 3 people I was please we didnt have to share.  We saw a variety of wildlife including lots of elephants in different areas of the park, as with all parks the drivers keep others informed so you are assured of seeing something, the most jeeps at one time was about 6 which didnt seem too crowded. The park and roadside was the only place in Sri Lanka that we saw picking us rubbish!  The only downside is as with other attractions in Sigiriya it doesnt take credit cards so bring plenty of cash!

Title: Amazing elephant park
Text: We've seen elephants in India but this was something else, they were so close and in such a brilliant setting. Beautiful, we saw about 170 elephants in all! Standing up in an open air jeep, fantastic!

Title: So many elephants!
Text: I don't know if it's because we were so lucky or if it's the time of the year that helped us, but we saw so many elephants there!!! Just awesome for everyone! Our guide was charming and very respectful to the environment and animals.  Just loved this experience! (I've been in Serengeti, Ngorongoro Tanzania and Ethosha in Namibia).

Title: Fabulous experience of animals in their natural surroundings
Text: Very good fun trip, beautiful surroundings, saw loads of elephants it was amazing but be prepared for a bumpy ride

Title: Best place to see elephants
Text: It was a great experience! It's the perfect place to see plenty of elephants in the wild! We were there in the afternoon and it was amazing because there were so many elephants and they came out of the woods to drink water. Also our driver was patient and waited for us to make photos and he drove us to some great spots to have good visibility.

Title: HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE !
Text:
We payed 120$ for a 2h30 tour safari to see elephants. Our driver was a crazy driver, he was driving in the water and got stuck in the mud. We tried all afternoon to get the jeep out of the mud but we didn't manage to do it. Then after 5hours of waiting in the sun, a friend of the driver came to pick us up as the jeep was still stuck in the mud. We didn't see any elephants. We lost our day (we left at 10 in the morning and came back at 5.30 in the afternoon). We asked for a refund and the responsible for this tour told us that it wasn't possible... 
I wouldn't recommand this tour at all (the one with the reservation in front of the cinnamon hotel). DON'T DO IT !!!!!!!!!!

Title: Elephant sanctuary. Animals in the wild. Real thrill
Text: The drivers usually charge Rs 6000 for a hotel pickup and about three hours of driving round the National Park. There is a further fee to enter the park. It's an amazing sanctuary and we saw over 100 elephants sometimes up close. It's not overrun with tourists like some of the other larger national parks. Definitely worth a visit. About 20k out of Sigiriya.

Title: Respectfully done
Text: Great opp to see plenty of elephants in the wild including lots of baby ones. Given some of the reviews I have read was expecting jeeps all over each other and the elephants but the drivers kept to the paths and were respectful of each other. One suggestion is either go early morning or after 3pm given there are more at dawn or dusk. The Jeeps can also be very comfy or rough as guts with the seat quality so suggest checking out what u are expected in yours.

Title: Elephants up close
Text:
Our jeep driver took time to locate as many elephants as possible. Yes, we saw quite a few, and it was quite memorable.
At times, jeeps become very crowded and chaotic in one spot, but it all worked well.
My only concern seems to be many jeep companies are located along the road outside the park, so you need to ride in them for some distance without seatbelts. Perhaps, the jeeps can be rented inside the park instead.

Title: Fantastic excursion, highly recommended
Text:
We took a private jeep, (we were very lucky and were one of the few people to get a Land Rover!). At first we struggled to see much, and so did all of the other drivers, to the extend that our driver took us deep into the jungle for best endeavours to see something. 

Eventually as if our of no where we saw the most amazing site of several elephant groups. In the end we saw 7 instances of either individual elephants or groups of elephants. 

We went at about 1 and stayed in the park until about 4.30, this was plenty of time. Our driver also took us to the viewing tower where you can walk and get some amazing views. 

Highly recommended.

Title: Too much money for that!
Text: In the last day of our trip we decided to go there , it was completely wast of time and momey , we just saw 1 elephant after searching about 1and half hoar, we got so tired for nothing, They told us today is hot and elephant goes to bushes , and I think they take too much money for that!

Title: Exciting end to the day
Text: The national park was flooded by recent heavy rain but the eco park across the road was full of elephants who had moved in to escape the floods and search for food. There are far too many over enthusiastic jeep drivers careering around trying to get the best positions for their clients but we were fortunate to get an old hand who knew the best tricks and who got us within touching distance of a small family of 3 plus mother without raising any alarms. It was a most moving experience to be so close while they were not in the least disturbed by our presence. We almost wore out the camera!

Title: Great day at Minneriya
Text:
Was picked up from my guest house exactly on time and taken to this beautiful park. We managed to get really quite close and saw lots of elephants at various spots. My guide was really friendly and made me feel at ease being a woman alone. He was able to answer all my questions and never rushed. He was also so good stopping on the way home to help me get a new SIM card because mine had broken, it was quite late at this point and I really appreciate his time and help. I would definitely recommend booking a trip with them, professional, good drivers not like some of the touts you get that drive bad and scare the elephants... Saw some of that and it was upsetting. These guys very good and respectful.
Thank you for a wonderful day.

Title: Safari in jeeps
Text: Safari absolutely brilliant with teenagers and infants. Knowledgeable, careful driver. Saw an abundance of elephants up close including babies. Countryside so beautiful. Well worth a visit.

Title: Rain ,mud,No elephants
Text:
We had booked to go here or so we thought . However we were taken to the Eco park at Habarana .There must have been a hundred vehicles which set off in a massive convoy .After a couple of miles the jeeps with bald tyres got stuck in the mud - there was no way to turn back , the whole convoy had to sit in the mud for an hour . The Forestry Dept were still selling gate tickets despite the terrible conditions.
No animals.
If you really want to go check , check and check again on conditions at the site.

Title: almost unbelievable
Text: Our "safari" was booked for us by the driver we had contracted for our week in Sri Lanka.  Although we have no way of knowing what options might have been available, it is hard to imagine that we could have done much better.  A number of species are represented in the Kauoulla National Park, but elephants are the obvious draw.  We had heard that sightings earlier in the day were plentiful, but that doesn't really prepare you for the experience of encountering large (at least 50+ animals?) herds.  Knowing that you are seeing them in what is their natural habitat  is an incredible experience.  We rode in a "jeep" with a raised passenger compartment, so at times it felt like we were almost "face-to-face" with the elephants.

Title: The highlight of our sri lancan visit
Text: To get as close as we did to a heard of over fifty elephants and watch them for well over 45 minutes was sensational. One had a one week old baby that was great.

Title: Elephant Safari
Text: We have seen herds of elephants on this safari. Most of the action is around the water body. There are too many vehicles , bothering animals . Overall , a good experience

Title: must see
Text: it is must see if you are going to sri lanka, just find driver with good price, nothing to add more .

Title: Breathtaking
Text: Well worth a visit....  the elephant population is huge and you will see all sizes from small babies to fully grown bulls...  the park also hosts many more animals and got to see a lot of eagles, buffalo, crocodiles to name but a few.  try and get an early sunset one otherwise there can be a lot of jeeps on the safari.

Title: Wow! Wow! Wow!
Text: This was a great experience. We probably saw about 200 elephants plus a number of other animals including deer. There were babies, heavily pregnant elephants and everything in between. Some of them came up quite close to the open jeeps we were travelling in. Our jeep driver and guide was fantastic and told us lots of interesting details. However others I spoke to said this was not the case with their driver. Nether the less a very rewarding experience.

Title: More jeeps than elephants
Text: We had heard about the elephant gathering on a nature documentary and were looking forward to this experience, however it when we arrived the reality was quite disappointing. We did see quite a number of elephants, which was great, however, this was marred by the hundreds of jeeps descending on them. At times the jeeps even blocked their access to the water and  cut off their path. It was awful. Our fantastic guide told us that the gathering has not happened for the past 3 years due to the water levels being kept artificially high, stopping fresh new grass growth from water receding, which is what the elephants are attracted to. Considering the amount of money brought in by the entry fee, the government needs to manage this resource much more sustainably.

Title: Elephants!
Text: We took the afternoon safari which starts at 1.30 pm from Sigiriya. It took around 40 mins to reach the national park. Tickets are 3000 LKR per person. The jeep took us inside the reserve and slowly you will leave behind the city and enter a jungle. The experience is one of its kinds. Highlights of this safari is ofcourse the elephants which come right at the end. You can see the entire herd walking together. We almost had one elephant moving towards the entire group of jeeps which was a little scary. But thrilling too.

Title: Elephants..
Text: One of the best safari to see large groups of elephants. Best time is noon safari of 2 pm when these elephants groups come to lake.

Title: Elephant safari
Text: Seems there are many companies doing safari from Sigiriya. My experience with one company who took us to this safari was such a fun. Saw many elephants, very close. It was an amazing experience. It was a private jeep trip and the driver was very nice and eager to show us a lot. Trip was 3pm to about 7pm which was perfect time to see elephants dinner time and nice sunset.

Title: I was blown away
Text: This was one of the most wonderful holiday moments in my life - to see elephants in the wild. Although there were a lot of other vehicles, the drivers are skilled in stopping for photos where you feel you are the only one. The elephants really don't seem to mind and carry on as they have been doing for thousands of years before we showed up!

Title: Not many animals
Text: We traveled on a very bumpy road on an old jeep to arrive at the water hole. There were not too many elephants around and we could only view them from quite a distance. Other animals include some buffaloes and a few types of birds. The driver of the jeep was rather surprised that we were not impressed. If one wishes to see more animals, one should go to South Africa.

Title: AMAZING
Text: It's so great to see how lives elephants in wild.  The biggest population in Sri Lanka, around 300.  Price 6000 per Jeep(5-6 people) and 2500 entrance fee.

Title: Great experience
Text: Called up the day before and was able to arrange a Jeep no problems. Had a fantastic time, saw easily 100+ elephants, our driver was very helpful and courteous. Highly recommend !

Title: Safari
Text: A must do to see a lot of elephants, beautiful peacocks, some black bulls, even a jackal, crows and white egrets.

Title: elies galore
Text:
I haven't seen such herds in the wild in Asia. The eleis are a joy to watch. We spotted a few jackals and a horn bill. The lake is stunning towards sun down and the sight of the herds against the lake is a photographers delight.
Don't expect too much of the park other than the elephants.

Title: If I hadn't been to Africa...
Text:
OK so this "safari" is OK and we did see a LOT of elephants (about 120) as we were there at the right time.  We also saw a pack of jackal and a Leopard (VERY lucky spotting on our part) BUT... You are there with a hell of a lot of other jeeps and people and they stop midway through so you can "stretch your legs" which meant people smoked ??????? and then we drove back the way we came.  
If you have never been on a safari then definitely go as it is wonderful to be out in an open jeep.

Title: A more ethical way to admire these beautiful creatures
Text: We hadn't planned this into our itinerary and like many spontaneous outings, this was hugely rewarding. We were delighted when we saw just one elephant. 10 minutes later we saw 75. In their own habitat unmolested by tourists climbing them - quite wonderful.

Title: Great place
Text: This is one of the most beautiful place I visited. New experience with elephants life. The green and mountais view are remarkable. Kids and families will enjoy such place. You can feed elephants old and young. You can watch the bath time at the river.

Title: Satisfying first time safari experience
Text: This was my first safari experience and it was just satisfying. The entire goal of the trip is to see elephants on a pretty close distance. Our driver pointed out few other animals such as monkeys for example, but we could see monkeys everywhere else outside of the park. After around 2 hours we finally spotted a group of elephants and took some nice pictures. We didn't run across any other animals unfortunately.

Title: Elephants - Elephants and more Elephants!!!!
Text: Was getting a bit worried we may not see any however saw over 100 in the end - along with other wildlife. This was the highlight of our visit and really is a must do !

Title: Fantastic Safari
Text:
After staying at Holiday Cottage in Sigiriya with Roshan and his family, my tour guide from Sri Lankan Nisha Tours arranged this Safari with Roshan to Minneriya National Park.  I had read reviews about the amount of elephants that you are able to see here but did not expect to see such a large gathering of them.
Roshan's service from being taken to the National Park to his patience while I spent time in awe of the herd that we stumbled across was fantastic, very comfortable transport and Roshan's engish is brilliant making this a really memerable afternoon.  Thanks so much Roshan if anytime I return to Sri Lanka I will most definately pay you another visit.

Title: You're guaranteed to see elephants
Text:
Unlike most Kenyan safaris (the only comparison I could make) you are taken around in a 4X4 jeep, rather than a minibus, so that's a good start.
The park is not that big so you will definitely see elephants but, be aware, you will also see every other jeep in town!  As they flock to the herds for a better view for their guests. So much so, that they intrude on the elephants path causing some nervous reversing when faced off by three great beasts!

A great trip but a little more respect for the animals wouldn't go amiss.

Title: Great visit with a great guide
Text:
Wonderful area with a lot of elephants.
Our guide and chauffeur searched explicit for the non crowded places.
We saw a lot of elephants but also a lot of jeeps.
It's how it works..he explained that even wild ill elephants are being treated from the money tourists pay for a visit.
However, he really tried and managed to spot elephants without a lot of jeeps around them.
We spotted also a lot of beautiful birds.
Really worth to join this company.

Title: Wild elephant watching
Text:
It is very beautiful experience, that is one of its kind.
Those who like to get an experience of being in between the heard of elephants (daddy elephant, mummy elephants and the cute little baby elephants) grazing the lush green grass on the bed of a man made lake. Also a guide who is well explaining the facts about the elephants and their behaviour.
It is one of the most do thing in Sigiriya.

Title: 150 elephants
Text: The best afternoon you can imagine, casually roam in the countryside and forest with elephants, big and small.

Title: Far too many Jeeps in the park
Text: Minneriya National Park is where you can see wild elephants roaming from a Jeep. There are a LOT of Jeeps though. Hundreds of Jeeps which all converge on any Elephant they can find. I'm not overly convinced it is in any way ecologically sensitive

Title: Great if you've never seen a wild elephant before, but dull if you have
Text: Your opinion of this place will depend on your previous travel experiences. Having done safaris in other countries, we found this little more than a jeep drive around lake to see some elephants and several varieties of birds, but other members of our party who had not travelled much before, thought it was the best things ever. We saw about 30 or so elephants at fairly close range. Many jeeps jockey for the best position. Bumpy ride. Advised to tip driver at least 500 rupees per couple.

Title: Good ride after long time
Text: The elephant back ride in Sri Lanka is one of the To Do activities depending on your interests. Our little boy of 3yrs just loved it and kept singing his elephant rhymes. The elephant took us by the lake and we fed some cucumbers too. It is quite expensive compared to the elephant safaris in India. It costed 20$ per person for the 20min ride on the elephant.

Title: It is Nice to Be the Captive Animal Every Now & Then!
Text:
As someone who has seen elephants mostly in captivity and, not always enjoying a high standard of life (for example, some Thai elephants), I was ecstatic to be the "caged animal" for a few hours and to observe elephants roaming freely & happily at Minneriya.

Though there was other wildlife, the reason for spending AUD$120 as a couple was because of the elephants. The money spent was petty cash on that basis. No offence to the other wildlife but, were it not for the elephants, I could not say the experience is well worth the investment. The array of birds, monkeys, deer & buffalo should, however, not go without mention. A set of binoculars would be an advantage in better observing some of these other animals. We didn't have a pair and, our driver didn't either.

Though I do not consider the experience to be age restrictive, I do warn that the ride is not always smooth. Be prepared to bump around a bit!

Title: Amazing
Text: A must on anyone's list. The park is fantastic and the elephants are in abundance. Loved every minute of it.

Title: Perfect....
Text:
This is the way to see elephants, not in a zoo or circus, but live and free.
This was the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. 
One slight issue.... maybe too many jeeps on the track at one time.

Title: Elephants Move Freely and well Protected
Text: This park is a must see if in the area. Bumpy and dusty road to reach n need 4WD vehicle. Many are available for rent plus a guide for around $40 plus entrance fee. Ask yr tour guide. Elephants by the hundreds with babies r there. Freely moving, feeding without fear and near the lake. U can get very close without getting them upset. Safaris r starting afternoon and u get to see them going to the lake almost by sunset. Monkeys, peacocks, monkeys, birds r available.

Title: Elephant reserve
Text: this was such a treat the girls loved it and so did we!!! the elephants were going for their afternoon dip in the lagoon as the sun was setting it was just magical!!

Title: Elephant Safari
Text: You need to avoid rainy seasons. I could see only one elephant crossing the road during a four hour trip. Most Jeeps are not four wheel driven cabs. Two vehicles got stuck in the mud. We had to wait for a real 4X4 cab. Some cab drives might mislead you. they some times pretend as there are no more cabs. and demands you to pay more. Get your hotel to arrange one for you.

Title: Amazing Safari
Text: We went there in the afternoon, the safari in a private jeep lasted for two n half hour. we saw hundreds of elephants grassing just by meters away from us. There are lots of other animals like bulls, jackals and bird also there.

Title: AMAZING!!
Text: We had a fantastic jeep safari with driver Johan. Encountered more than 100 elephants, really close. Also saw beautiful birds. Unfortunately we had to share the space with lots of other jeeps, but still an amazing experience. An absolute must do excursion!

Title: ELEPHANT HAVEN
Text:
I suggest you come early in the morning or late afternoon. We went in the aftenoon as waited for the sun to set in a safari -- feels like the African Safari that we see on movies. Really breathtaking place! A whole new experience to do a safari ride.

A must go and do when you are in Sri Lanka.

Title: Real thing
Text:
Even if the area is crowded the experience is amazing.

Many wild animals and in particular elephants - but also birds and other species made this an unforgettable experience.

We wanted to avoid the tourist elephant traps in pinnavala so to see the free animals in minniriya was a true privilege 

Of course there are (too) many jeeps, but it was all with respect to the animal 

From what we later experienced this was the best animal experience In Sri Lanka

Title: Wonderful to see all the elephants
Text: Very good t our but pretty much all centred around the elephants ad not many other animals. Rather too many jeeps though at time s crowding the elephants. Our driver was really thoughtful and kept a respectful distance from the wonderful elephants. Butt others were less caring and at one point got in the way of a family that were trying to reach the water hole. That's a shame. We went in the late afternoon, perhaps early morning is less crowded

Title: Elephant Heaven!
Text: We took a jeep safari to watch for animals & birds.  The main goal was to see the elephants--which we saw in abundance--from the oldest bull elephant to a tiny 2-week old baby.  We watched several herds for a couple of hours because it was so interesting to see them interact with each other in the wild.  We were happy that Sri Lanka has chosen to develop their national park system to protect these magnificent animals!

Title: A day I will never forget
Text:
Wild elephants up close.... do I need to say anything else! Bucket list tick! 

Take a good camera and enjoy these beautiful animals

Title: More jeeps than animals
Text:
My personal experience in this safari was not that great. To begin with I think its overpriced. The enrty fee to the park is around LKR 3500 per head. After that you have to book/ rent a jeep separately. As in most cases you have to bargain to get a good deal with the jeep rental - We got one for LKR3000. So we ended up spending LKR 10000 (2 of us) for this safari and we got we got to see was - a few peacocks; Langur monkeys and domesticated cows and buffaloes! 
I know it depends on your luck if you get to see certain animals in a safari - its always a chance you have to take.
There were many jeeps and they all follow a fixed path. Overall it was a bumpy 3 hour ride up and down the national park and we were quite disappointed with the safari. I think a safari at Udawalawe or Yala would be a better option.
We actually spotted to elephants right after we left the safari! They had strayed onto the roads from the jungle!

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We booked a 3h jeep safari and saw lots of elephants. Even though there are more jeeps than elephants in the park the drivers generally kept their distance to the animals. I was rarely under the impression that the elephants were disturbed or stressed by our presence- they seemed used to the jeeps and didn't show any reaction. Better than I expected having read other comments before the tour.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: Lots and lots of jeeps at the same time. However, we managed to see lots of elephants - and also buffalos, monkeys and different birds. A really nice safari - though there were a lot of waiting before it started.

Title: Ask the homestay owner for a better deal
Text: 100% worth a visit, we saw 30+ elephants in their natural habitat! Definately ask your homestay owner to look into though- our owner managed to find another couple to share the Jeep with, halving the cost to hire it for the afternoon and also reducing the price you pay for entry in the park (each group pays a fixed amount extra to enter the park on top of the price per person and the price of the Jeep). Altogether it only cost us less than 10,000 Rs for an unforgettable experience.

Title: Great experience! Recommended!
Text: We visited Minneriya National Park the first day of our trip in Sri Lanka and it was really unique experience, because we had never seen elephants from that close and in their natural habitat! Our guide, who was really good suggested that we had this safari, since it was not arranged by the travel agency, and it was really worth visiting. We enjoyed the beautiful route inside the park with an open jeep. Except for elephants the residents of that park are buffalos and birds. Since anyone visits Sri Lanka I would recommend this activity for sure!

Title: Beautiful park, lots of elephants
Text: The jeep was uncomfortable and the road extremely bumpy. We saw tons of elephants, but no other animals aside from monkeys and a few pelicans. Oh, and a crocodile in the distance ;)

Title: Limited wildlife.
Text: This place worked out quite expensive I felt. It is also a long and very rough ride into the park before you see anything. The only animals here are elephant and water buffalo. We did see lots of elephants in large groups but that was it.

Title: Calling All Ellie Lovers :)
Text:
At first I thought I could see a lot of animals here but in fact only elephants in this National Park.
You got to go there by renting a jeep car, just prepare your butts for the crazy bumpy roads LOL

The price ticket for foreigners is about LKR 2,200/pax, while for local is about LKR1,250/pax (USD 1 = LKR 152).

Don't forget to apply sunblock all over your body! :D

Title: Elephant Lovers Paradise!
Text: There isn't much variety  here int his park, but if you love elephants, you're in heaven. To those who've been on African safari, do NOT place your expectation here. This is a very simple almost sanctuary feel and no other big game are present. When you come know that the elephant is here to enchant and show you true simplicity of another safari life.

Title: Family of five
Text:
This National Park is great for viewing elephants and we saw a herd of over 100.
At one stage we were so close we could almost touch the elephant, while in the protection of a jeep.
When vehicles are turned off you can feel the calm tranquil atmosphere when the herd was feeding.
Baby elephants are always a good sign and we saw plenty of them.
Something special and definitely worth a visit.
Only negative would be the amount of jeeps.

Title: Elephants Galore!
Text: We were fortunate to see a lot of wild elephants at this park, family groups with calves as young as two weeks protected by their Aunts, and lone large males wandering about.  The bird life was also very good.

Title: Elephant gathering
Text:
a 3 hour experience to watch the gathering late afternoon. 
Saw other animals along the way- kingfishers, spotted deer, monkeys, peacocks to name a few. Watching the elephants in their natural habitat was a wonderful sight and a holiday highlight.

Title: Hundreds of elephants
Text:
Going inside the bush for 30 40 minutes to see some elephant behind a tree doesn't let you understand immediately what are you going to discover! Just few minutes later you're going to meet groups of elephants just eating and walking with no stress by the human being. The drivers (most of them)know how far have to stay from the babies to not be attacked by the elephant. We have seen one attacked by the elephant because his jeep was too close to the crossing path of the elephant..
Be careful. 
It must be on your to do list!!!

Title: 100+ Elephants
Text: We arrived for an afternoon/early evening drive through the park. Our driver was friendly and knowledgeable. He pointed out other wildlife on the drive towards the lake. The elephants gather there to feed. I counted over 100 elephants by the water. It was a busy day to go as it was a local holiday. There were almost as many jeeps watching the elephants. Unlike African Safari the drivers stick to the tracks so the elephants could decide how close they wanted to come to the jeeps. We saw a number of tuskers and enjoyed watching them. Slightly disappointing we didn't see much other wildlife in the park. But we had seen the elephants which was the main purpose of visit.

Title: Outstanding experience so close to the fascinating land giants
Text:
Elephants are always a great watch. For someone who enjoyed them in some zoos earlier- this was a phenomenal experience. The sheer number of elephants was a delight and to be so close to the wild was enchanting and trilling at the same time.
Special thanks to our guide/tours (Kanota tours) who recommended this attraction over an alternate safari plan we had and we loved every second of this !
An unforgettable experience.

Title: As good as Africa?
Text:
I was truly touched by the sights. I saw a lot of elephants and many of them very close. Once you get through the forest with the jeeps the area opens up in a lake-side savannah, I felt it was breathtaking. I saw heards, individuals, pregnant cows and small babies.
I feel like my expectations are really high now for any African safari (at least when it comes to elephants)

Title: Safari to Minneriya National Park.
Text:
First we did not want to visit the park, but our driver Nuwan Sameraa said that there were many elefants to see and he arranged the driver. The safari was very good and we saw lots of elefants, birds and even crocodils.
We enyoid the Safari.

Title: Lovely safari for elephants
Text: The park has an incredible amount of elephants.  We also saw snakes, monkeys, crocodiles, water buffalo and various birds.  Our homestay organised a visit for 11,500 rupees.  It was however extremely busy with other safari tours and did get extremely dusty at points.

Title: Hundreds of elephants
Text: Quite touristy attraction and there is not much of animal spotting but you get to seen hundreds of elephants by the lake (together with hundreds of fellow tourists and dozens of other jeeps). Still worth a visit.

Title: Our Small Safari
Text: We were told to reach the premises by 1 pm, landed there well on time & we entered Mineriya National Park. Did not see much crowd whilst we entered, thought we would not get to see a lot but we were delighted to see quite a few herds of elephants, wild buffalo's, different species of birds, monkeys. We enjoyed our drive & by the time we returned there were around 100 jeeps entering the safari. As per our Driver, we were on time to visit the place, any later we could not have seen the animals as they would all go back into the forest.

Title: mother elephants protecting a baby
Text: we had an excellent experience witnessing 2 elephants protecting a baby.  We saw about 20 elephants in total. We went at 12 and the park was empty, as we were leaving at 3, we passed at least 30 trucks going in. I can't imagine how crowded that would have been.

Title: Elephant heaven
Text: This was a good trip, we saw hundreds of elephants around the lake, although they can be quite aggressive if the jeeps get too close.

Title: a lot of elephants
Text: We hired an external jeep so to bargain a much better price. Our visit was roughly 3,5 hours an we enjoyed many elephants from few meters distance. Even a mother with the child.

Title: Lovely gathering of wild elephants
Text:
So glad we chose this over the elephant orphanage as it offered us a chance to enjoy the elephants in a natural setting. We started out at about 4pm and spent a good 2 hours around the National Park.
There were monkeys, crocodiles, birds etc and the setting was just lovely

Title: Safari for elephant and nature lovers
Text: Spent 5000 rupees ppl for the safari in this national park we enjoyed the scenery and view of elephant herds quite a lot.  There's one thing for sure   is that you will be satisfied if your target is only enjoying the ride on Jeep & elephants instead of expecting to varieties of wild animals. Again, you can enjoy the ride in the park with natural scenery just don't expect it to be like a wild land with thousands of animals on it.

Title: Great safair
Text: saw 80 elephants, a jackal, boar loads of birds eagles and crocodiles what more could you want for £35. Loads of great photo ops

Title: One of my best days ever
Text: saw over 200 elephants on a  hot sunny day. loved it but take a hat and drinks it gets hot in the back of the trucks

Title: Viewing Elephant herds in nature is a MUST in Sri-Lanka
Text: We stayed in Dambulla and from there did all our trips in this area. Elephant Safari was definitely breathtaking, not too difficult. We had a Jeep pick us up, and drove to the reserve, in the reserve we saw Elephant herds, buffalo herd crossing the water, wild peacocks dancing with their full plumage in display, really wonderful. Can be done in the afternoon time.

Title: A highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka
Text: We loved this! Saw tons of female elephants and baby elephants and a couple of tuskers (males). Dozens of water buffalo nearly submerged in the lake. So may birds, and monkeys too. We enjoyed that the jeeps would drive up and cut the engine so we could watch the animals in their natural habitat in silence. We've visited an elephant sanctuary in Chiang Mai Thailand, and this was a much better experience. Highly recommend.

Title: For the price, it's ookaaay
Text: Set governmental price are the same for every national park and additionally you have to pay for a jeep. But the prices are still expensive. I won't undermine the nature however, it's beautiful, water buffaloes, elephants, crocodiles, jackals and birds of every kind. It's a must see if you love elephants. Plus, try and go in the afternoon!

Title: A surprising safari
Text:
When we planned to visit Sigiriya, jungle safari was not an option in our list. Our tour operator suggested it and so we decided to go. He arranged a jeep and the first view into the jungle was not very impressive

But then the moment we reached near the lake, it was really mesmerising. Herds and herds of elephants were seen. The best part was how the adults were protecting the little ones. The numbers were so huge that after a point we lost track on how many elephants we had seen.There were also many different variety of birds. Would say that this is a must visit place for bird watchers

Overall a surprising safari which we really enjoyed!!

Title: good
Text: We went with chanaka adventure. Saw loads of elephants, birds, crocodiles and peacocks. Driver helped to spot animals. 4x4 was clean and spacious. We had to pay for chanaka adventure , entrance tickets and entrance for the vehicle also, so make sure what you pay for.

Title: Won't do this again.
Text: Lots of elephants here, but be prepared to get a "dust bath". The driver's seem to take great delight in out manuvering their associates. The result is that no one wants to leave much space between themselves and the car ahead so the driver in the cab is protected, but the his unlucky passengers are constantly enveloped in a cloud of dust.

Title: Too Many Jeeps
Text: It was amazing to see the elephants at Minneriya, but it was incredible busy. More jeeps that elephants, but we've ticked the box.

Title: Amazing!
Text: Great afternoon looking for elephants in the national park. We saw lots of other wildlife as well which has ignited our idea of possibly doing a safari in Africa as one of our next holidays

Title: Elephants, Elephants & Elephants
Text:
They are in their natural habitat and can be seen while traveling in a 4x4 accompanied by a Park Ranger. It is home to other wild life species as well. 
A must visit!! 
The entry fee for foreigners - RS. 2,500/- +/-   There is a park ranger fee too.  
Locals free.

Title: Highlight of the day
Text:
We quickly decided to visit Minneriya national park. Unexpectedly we saw approx. 30+x elefants eating grass. We were close up to 10 meters. A baby elefant approx 3 weeks old, we felt touching him. The driver was very experienced, showing us this unique view. And we had really luck to this unique situation.
 Highly recommended

Title: Great way to see elephants in the wild
Text: This was a very interesting experience enhanced by the fact that we had an excellent ecological guide and skilful driver. Driving off road to see the elephants after relatively heavy rains meant that the tracks were very slippy and it was difficult to cross the river. Some of the jeeps (2 wheel drives) got stuck in the river. It was fun to see the mothers with their babies near the river. No leopard sightings though!

Title: beautiful park but too much noise
Text: this national park is very beautiful with loads of elephants and many other animals to see from the jeeps. But for an animal loving person the safari jeeps are too many and too noisy and too near to the irritated animals than one can really enjoy it.

Title: Amazing
Text: The main attraction is the elephants, however there is an abundance of interesting bird life as well as a herd of wild buffaloes

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: Go in pm, from 1:30 to catch the sunset. Can be organised with your guesthouse in Sigiriya and is totally worthy, tho the main attraction is elephants. The surrounding is amazingly beautiful and the experience is nice. Not much tourist, we saw only few jeeps but at least over 50 elephants. Cost was 4500 all inclusive per person from Sigiriya in a jeep of 4.

Title: Amazing
Text: Have done a lot of safaris in Africa but this was a very good experience to see so many elephants so near in a open jeep.

Title: Nice but not great...
Text: The elephant safari is nice and interesting. Just too many vehicles going around the park. Limiting the number of vehicles might be a good idea, or imposing at least 4 pax per vehicle, as many jeeps carry only couples + driver. But overall a good experience as we didn't want a "zoo like" thing

Title: Elephants everywhere
Text: Just about 40 mins drive and you enter a huge clearing like nowhere.  Herds of elephants keep coming and it's a delight to see them eating , and the baby elephants playing . The drivers are well experienced and there are many jeeps around you. I

Title: Amazing sights, beautiful animals
Text: Apart from all the beautiful birds (herons, peacocks, pelicans, eagles etc) who saw three different herds of elephants amounting to over 200 individuals, including many calves.  We were able to get close in the 4x4 we were in and were able to get great photos.  Minneriya is beautiful - particular forested and then large wet plains near the lake.  Definitely worth doing.

Title: An close encounter with the elephantts
Text: A very interesting experience to visit and watch the elephants.  There are very old jeeps to take you into the park and it was very rough ride, so be prepared.  The jeeps are really good so don't expect to be comfortable.  However, you can really see the elephants in a very close distance.

Title: Wacky races meets Mad Max
Text: We arrived as part of a party on an organised holiday tour having spent the morning at Sigiria rock. We climbed aboard our Mihranda Jeeps (don't forget to tip the driver !) and drove into the jungle in search of elephants. After about half an hour of driving and seeing absolutely nothing we came upon a herd of about 30 elephants near to a dried up lake (or tank as they call lakes ) we followed them around for some time, the jeeps kept overtaking each other and jockeying for position to get the best views of the elephants that came up close to our convoy. Not relly much else to see other than the elephants, apparently Sri Lanka has experienced a drought this year and most of the lakes have dried up, we then endured another half hour trip back to base, not seeing anything else exciting. However on a safari trip a few days later, which began in the early morning darkness, literally hundreds of jeeps took part in a race worthy of the title of the review looking for elephants and stuff, we actually saw a leopard who was rather nonplussed at being surrounded by about 100 mihranda jeeps full of tourists taking photo's of him, he was on top of a rock, got up, stretched and promptly went back to sleep. Epic !

Title: "Big Elephants, Medium Elephants, Baby, Oh! Baby Elephants!"
Text: I did the safari in the afternoon. My tour guide/driver was excellent. The bumpy road was really bumpy, so dress comfortably, bring your camera and excitement as it is truly a galore of Elephants. Many people came, all riding the safari jeep. Seen most of the people standing up and enjoying the view of the plethora of amazing elephants, big, medium and small. The best part of the safari is seeing the baby elephants and feeding at that time. One elephants was on the defense because one jeep got too close. I think that parking the jeep and just viewing the elephants is the best part of the safari.

Title: Short Safari. Total excitement
Text:
So you cannot compare it to any Indian or African safari, buts a good quick and dirty ride into the wild! 

The experience of moving about in an open UV and the feeling of getting close to wild elephants is what one enjoys. Evenings are the best times and there is a sure shot view of Elephants in huge droves 

You will get to see a variety of birds but beyond that there is not much to see. 

This isn't a very expensive safari ...so for a group you will be paying around 8-10000 LKR. For a total time of about 2-2.5 hours.

Title: A good place to see some elephant
Text: Its a place where you can see some elephant at a very close distance and best to visit in the evening

Title: ELEPHANTS !!
Text: We have travelled to the Kandalla National Park before but nothing can prepare you for a herd of wild elephants grazing quite happily with 100s of people clicking away.  Mums and their babies and teenager, aunts and the matriarch.  It is a truly amazing experience.  Cost including jeep and safari and entrance fee 10,000 LKR.

Title: Elephants place
Text: we hired a local jeep for 5-6k and we roamed aroudn the park for about 2-3 hours we could get a close look at the grazing elephants 3- 4 herds each having 3-7 elephants including calf's we had a look at water buffaloes from the far.. yala was closed so we opted for this . mainly elephants , a few birds int he water

Title: Animal abuse!!!
Text: This place abuses animals!!  Elephants are chained and beaten please do not support this horrible establishment

Title: Great way to interact with native Asian elephants
Text: Great place to interact with native Asian elephants. We ate in the fully glassed restaurant where you can see them bathing in the river. You also see them interacting with each other: eating, nursing, frolicking. You may even pet them. I saw no evidence of maltreatment as some posters have said. Quite the contrary. They seemed very healthy and happy to live in peace!

Title: Day trip
Text:
Its great to see the place looking after the elephants from the temples or injured from taking care of them feeding them and then letting back in .

As many reviews say they are caged , they arent .

The idea of elephant care is definitely explained well and every step in detail is shown to you .

Its a wonderful experience, I recommend to go volunteer for a day or two ,

Its worth it !

Title: Disappointed in the staff
Text: The orphanage itself was amazing and we didnt see any elephants being harmed however, the workers at the elephant orphanage were rude and are only there to make tips off you. At first, they are very helpful wanting to take your photo and show us more elephants but then took us to a remote part of the orphanage were no other guests could see us and asked for a tip. My partner gave them a tip of nearly 1000 after already tipping another staff member 1000 and 500 and bought fruits for feeding the elephants with came to 1500 ( this is after paying a $15 entrance per person). When they took us to do remote parts of the orphanage, which was behind a building away from other guests and cameras they asked for a higher tip whilst one of the staff members were sharpening his massive knife. This obviously made us feel very uncomfortable and we ended up leaving the orphanage look out area after being there only 10 minutes. If you was to go, I would suggest that you go and watch the elephants down at elephant Bay hotel and dont enter the zoo its self. Saying this we did have a lovely time and got some really lovely photos but just felt very unsettled by the whole experience.

Title: Unique experience but at what cost
Text:
At first I was extremely excited to be able to feed & bathe and elephant and it is a very unique experience. But it does seem like the elephants are made to act a certain way for turists on command which is awful. They were showing us an elephant carrying logs as if it was impressive, while it clearly is making them do labour they shouldn't do. I saw an elephant trying to break off the chain and it broke my heart.

I'm quite confused about the 'orphanage' naming, I don't think it's that. They do take care of the elephants but I feel like there could definietly be a better way of doing that.

Title: A sanctuary for the Orphaned Elephants as well as some of the offspring.
Text:
Contrary to some of the negative reviews, the actual Pinnawala Orphanage depicted here treats the elephants much better than some of the  other places in Pinnawala where elephant rides are offered with no freedom for the working elephants. 
While here  the elephants are taken twice a day to the river to play and bathe, unchained to enjoy their meals on the premises except for an occasional male who is  aggressive during musth.

There are no rides offered unlike in other places  operated by private owners. 
 The mahoots treated them kindness and care when I visited most recently in February 2023, during which I spent  5 full days staying at the Pinnalanda Hotel. I took the photos from the balcony when they were brought to bathe in the river.

Title: Elephant orphanage Pinnawala
Text:
Was an eye opening experience with regards to the anatomy of the elephant and comparison with the African elephant.
We had the opportunity of i teracting with Pooja ( the first elephant to be born in captivity?) Gave hr a bath and fed her. We also agreed to having an elephant ride but was sad when we realised that the elephant ride went against all the principles they claimed they stood for.  Sad

Title: AVOID!!
Text:
Really did NOT enjoy our time here. This place masquerades as a 'sanctuary' but it's pretty much a circus. Elephants are made to lie down (clearly against their will) to take photos with the tourists and the Mahouts (elephant handlers) are awful to them. I witnessed elephants being prodded with metal sticks and whipped across the face with a whip. Both cried out in pain. 
This could have been something special but it made me sick to my stomach.

Title: Good place but mahouts are not good to elephants
Text: I had visited this place in 2007 and saw maimed elephants herehurt by landmines during the civil strife. This time around the elephants looked healthy. I went to see the elephants taking a bath in the Ma Oya river. Some frolicked while two were held down in the waters so that visitors could touch them and sit on them for a photo opportunity. The mahouts would not let the elephants stand up if they wanted to. For an orphanage that claims to be the worlds largest, this certainly is not nice to watch. Would I recommend visitors to go there? I am an eternal optimist. If the fees paid by visitors to watch the elephants can in any way improve the treatment meted out to them, it should be encouraged.

Title: Elephants All Over
Text: Best place to see elephants. We can see them bathing eating chilling. It is mesmerising to see them coming to river for daily bathing. Must visit if u coming to sri lanka.

Title: A great experience to see these majestic animals
Text:
Ive read the negative comments and cant agree. These animals would, if left in the wild, die quickly. Many are rescued due to injury many are cast out from the heards. 
Most of the elephants do not have chains but some of the bull elephants do especially when some of the other elephants are in season. 
The place itself is well laid out and the elephants look well cared for. To see the elephants in the river is quite something. 
Captivity should be a last resort but the alternative is worse.

Title: Visit worth the education. Learn the true facts about this place!
Text: I so enjoyed this visit. I asked many questions before and during my visit. Education is the key to understanding this place. Remember each visit is what you make it. It was so fun to meet the 'twins' born in 2021. So fun. Staff are pleasant and  will allow you being up close but will also protect your safety. These are wild animals. While a few are controlled with chains, the majority are not. My guide did everything possible to ensure I had the best experience with these animals. Watching them play. Understanding the controlled freedom they have. Learn more why some are chained. Educate yourself. Blessed to have had the opportunity to visit. Every creature loves a play in the river.

Title: ABUSIVE PLACE FOR ELEPHANTS!
Text:
Such a SAD experience watching chained elephants at the river. The keepers ALL OF THEM WERE COMPLETELY DRUNK!  They were pushing tourists to make photos with elephants & then tempting to get money out if it. We saw so much of bad behaviour with the elephants: shouting on them, not letting then go out of the river when they wanted & pushing elephants to make tricks and fun to tourists.

After seeing such abuse of elephants, we decided not to visit Elephant orphanage, which is norhing more than tourist attraction place and an elephant zoo with their abuse.

PLEASE DO NOT SUPPORT SUCH PLACE - better visit honest ELEPHANT FREEDOM PROJECT NEARBY, where you will be able to spend half of the day with well treated elephants and great sincere people, trully looking after their beloved Elephants: Kumar&Manicha.

Title: With elephants in open
Text: Pinnewala elephant orphanage is meant for old and sick animals. They say total 80 elephants live there fed by caretakers food of peeple leaves and taken to bath in a nearby river. It is feast to see elephants roaming freely. Some are chained as well. We are told that is one of it's kind in world to have elephant twins, two she elephants. Place is neat souvenir shop and clean toilets. Nice warm staff.

Title: Pinnawala Elephant town
Text: We planned a one day stay at Pinnawala as we heard that the kids can enjoy bottle feeding the baby animals and also bathing them in the river. We visited the orphanage and were disappointed that there is no bottle feeding , just simple zoo like feeding and you had to pay to get some food to feed the elephants. It was sporadically raining during the visit and thus again we were disappointed that on rainy days the elephants do not make the trip to the river for bathing as the water level rises.

Title: A remarkable orphanage for injured and orphaned elephants.
Text:
The elephant sanctuary in Sri Lanka's pinnawala town is a major sanctuary for orphaned and injured elephants.
The road to the orphanage is perhaps one of the most scenic drive you may come across in Sri Lanka.
The star attraction of the sanctuary was an elephant which has given birth to twins, a rarity.
We were also able to see a few elephants in search of a mate.
Away from the orphanage across the road the elephants were given a cool bath in the river.
There are also a number of souvenir shops near the elephant bathing ghat.
The parking space is spacious and the western style toilets were clean and well maintained.
There is also an ATM near the entrance where the newly arrived foreign tourists can convert their home currency into Sri Lankan rupees.
A fun place for kids to see elephants of all ages at close proximity.
The entry fee is nominal and the place well maintained.
We could not locate a restaurant in the premises.
We could also see a number of birds in the surroundings.
A good place to visit with the kids for a picnic.
Recommended.

Title: Amazing!
Text: A great place to see many elephants at one place. They look healthy and well cared for. Entry fee is higher for non-nationals as compared to nationals.

Title: A mixed review
Text:
A bit of a mixed review. I do agree with lots of the reviews here, its not an elephant orphanage, its a tourist attraction. Its clear the Elephants are trained , some of them are chained to rocks in order to tame them around people, we did see some not so nice treatment of elephants, which at times was uncomfortable. On the flip side to this, as someone who has never been close to Elephants before it was amazing to see so many in the river playing. It was definitely an experience and to be honest I don't regret going but Im not 100% sure if I would go again just because of the animal treatment. Also be aware - this is 100% a money making tourist attraction. We stayed in the hotel right on the water (thats another review in itself..) but when we arrived if we wanted to go to our hotel we had to pay an entry fee to the 'park' then if you want a photo or to touch or feed the elephants, its made out this is fine but you're then demanded to pay the staff , and they want more than you give them. 

A tough one to review, as a brit it did seem a little odd and hard to tell what treatment the animals get, but it was an experience we wont forget - so I think you have to make your mind up based on the reviews.

Title: just awful
Text:
The cruelty that goes on at this place is appalling.  Visiting and promoting this so called sanctuary only makes the problem worse with more elephants being tortured and put into chains 

Do not visit here or it will ruin your wonderful trip to such a beautiful country with the friendliest people

Title: River walk is worth the visit
Text: We landed in Colombo around 7.30am and headed straight up to  the  Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage which was around 2.5/3 hour drive.  Be sure to time your visit when the elephants do their walk from the park down to the river, which happens twice a day, this is an amazing sight seeing a herd of elephants bathing and wandering around in the river area.  As close to them being in the wild and their natural habitat as you can get.  This experience alone is well worth the visit, the rest of the park is average with elephants grazing in different areas.  One highlight was seeing the twin baby elephants with their mother.  There are a few informational boards scattered around the park but apart from this information was lacking.  Wear a hat and cover yourself in sunblock, take water, as there is nowhere to escape the sun.  Be aware of people trying to sell you fruits to feed the elephants on their walk which is frowned upon and of course they can be quite persistent.  Maximum two hours is all you will need here.

Title: I would never visit, if id know before
Text: So sad that this place is not a sanctuary nor a orphanage, IT IS LITERALLY A ZOO. Elephants are chained as they claim to protect the babies. They are even chained under the water of Pinnawala river. You better read some blogs b4 visiting if you do not want to contribute animal cruelty.

Title: Don't go.
Text: Not recommended. Sadly the elephants are so distressed and chained up. They are taught to paint for the tourists.

Title: Mistreating the elephants!
Text: unfortunately the elephants looked very sad and stressed and they were in chains, being poked with sharp metal sticks and hooks most of the time. do not go and support this shady business.

Title: Don't miss the opportunity to admire the majestic elephants- in the heart of nature!
Text:
We reached the Pinnawala Elephant orphanage around 11am- picked up tickets & headed straight to the elephant bath area. Spent the next 30+ minutes watching them in the water- one herd left & another herd of 25 elephants just reached the area. Stunning experience to watch so many elephants up close, enjoying the water & almost natural environment. 
Took some great photos & left to the orphanage area. It was like a pleasant park where you can watch the elephants, read the boards with interesting facts about elephants in general & the Pinnawala orphanage. 
We found a mother & 2 little ones- sat next to their enclosure, watching them for good 10mins. Very calming experience. 

Would recommend to spend atleast 1-1.5hrs between the bathing area & the actual orphanage premises. Elephants are just too majestic to be missed- especially in their own space in nature!

Title: Worth to visit
Text: Real nice project, protecting the elephants. You´ll be able to see and touch the elephants and get to know in more detail this fantastic project to protect orphan and disable elephants. If you have the opportunity don´t miss how they made paper and other objects from elephant poo...really interesting.

Title: Not so good
Text: The orphanage is located in pinnawala which falls in the route from Colombo to Kandy. The place is a major tourist destination as you can see a lot of elephants, take rides and watch them being fed and bath. As you find it everywhere the place is fully commercial and you feel the elephants are being used to earn some hefty money. While you surely love watching them bath and feed, there is not much humanity around. The elephants are often I'll treated in front of the tourists. The entry tickets have different rates for SAARC nationals, do carry your passport as a proof of it.

Title: Best Volunteer Experience!
Text:
You have also the chance to enjoy the volunteer project available all year round. 
You can choose your own start and finish dates.
Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is an orphanage and breeding sanctuary for rescued, injured or abused wild elephants which is situated northwest of the town of Kegalle, Sri Lanka. It shelters for over 88 orphaned elephants include about 15 baby elephants that volunteer can gain a wonderful opportunity with the largest land mammal on the earth. This institution caters not only for the abandoned babies but also for those injured and maimed within the jungle. We employ the expertise of both modern veterinary and traditional indigenous medical treatment to cater to these elephants needs. Orphanage provides all foods, medicines, milk for the baby elephants itself. It cost a lot. One elephant usually eats over 150 kilograms a day. Of course this orphanage need volunteers and their donations. That is why we charge a project fee(donation fee) from the volunteers. All these donations are used to take care of these elephants.

Title: Felt good to watch elephants without chains
Text: This orphanage was the first place we visited on our Srilanka tour. It was a pleasure watching them moving around without any chains on their legs. Some of them were busy having a mud bath. We spent an hour just watching them.It is heartening to know that orphaned baby elephants are taken care of, here. Hats off to the dedicated staff and care takers.

Title: Don't go if you love elephants
Text: I went here last week under the illusion that there were no chains . No hooks and just a orphanage . When we arrive I had suspicions but gave them the benefit of the doubt. At first things seemed ok. We went to the waterfront area to see them bathing. Then another group of elephants walked with mahoots down through a shopping street. This is when I was horrified. As they approached I went closer for a look. Mahoots forced an elephant(with hooks) to take my photo with them . I said no no Hari Hari but a mahoots grabbed my camera while they hooked the elephant. I said no no.no stop..but he kept going. I was in shock. I said to my guide I wanted to go home immediately ND didn't want to see them being fed.i cried and cried and cried all the way back to hotel. This is a desperate place and NOT an orphanage..please do not.suppprt this place in any way !!!!!! It's is cruel and inhumane !!

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
Text: A worth visiting place  before  you head  to  Kandy. You can see  plenty of  Elephants even feed  them with banana/watermelons( to be  bought separately). You can see  them bathing at particular time  when they reach the  river, Different entrance    fees  for  foreigner  adult, foreigner  child  , SAARC nations  adult and  child are  different. They have dry  restrooms  for  foreigner ticket  holders  for  free. Elephant  rides  which  is  organized  by different agents  are quite  expensive 30  mins  rides  is  5000 rs  while  45  mins  ride  is 8000  rupees

Title: Good place to visit en route to Dambulla or Sigiriya
Text: We visited this place enroute to Dambulla, good to see many elephants & baby elephants. Reach this place by 1 pm so that you can watch 20-30 elephants taking bath in the river which is great to see. You can have pictures with elephants while taking bath. There are places who makes paper from elephants dung, you can watch this and buy paper. There is good restaurant at bank of river where you can take lunch while elephants taking bath.

Title: Rip off tourist trap - give it a miss
Text:
Let me start by saying I have visited the Pinnewala Elephant Orphanage many times dating back to 1985. The spirit of the place has certainly changed and unfortunately I now cannot recommend this place to ethically or fair-minded tourists. 

I wont comment on the treatment of the animals - there is a lot of info in other reviews about this. My main issue is the price - it costs approximately  $16.50 for a foreigners ticket. Bearing in mind that this is approximately what you would pay for an adults entry to a large, well-kept urban zoo with adequate facilities in Europe or the United States, the experience falls far short of that. There are far better ways to see elephants in Sri Lanka than to support this racket. Give it a miss and go to one of the national parks instead if you can.

Title: Wonderful
Text: We visited this place enroute Dambulla from Colombo. It has close to 85+ elephants and children feel very excited to watch baby elephants and large elephants. One can see them take a bath in the river and can click pictures with these mighty animals as well. A good activity with kids for an hour. You also get to see, in shops nearby,  how paper is made from elephant dung !

Title: Not sure
Text:
I was left feeling slightly sceptical on the nature of this orphanage, I cant help but feel the animals welfare might not be the main priority.
I know they do good work but the handlers seem happy to make the elephants interact with customers as long as theres a tip involved. I thought it was a place elephants could go so they didn't have to perform!

Title: A better way to encounter elephants
Text: As a volunteer at an elephant hospital in Thailand I was very sceptical of coming here and looked at previous reviews.  But in my experience this is one of the better lives that elephants can be offered in todays world.  The way the park is planned with the rotation of the elephants (some bathing, some eating fruit, some in the free land), was planned with the elephants in mind.  The control measures are there but not over the top and it is one of the better places for elephants to be that can no longer be integrated into the wild.  Im not sure how far « orphanage » has been stretched, but if you take it for what it is, they do a good job to sustain this business so that the elephants can live, when it is not feasible for them to be in the wild.

Title: Ship's shore ex to the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
Text:
We ventured to this Orphanage on a ship's shore ex ... it's about a 2 - 2.5 hour drive from the port on a coach.

I think if you can get here with a local guide you would be better off as you can spend as much or as little time as you like at the orphanage, whereas on a ship's tour the time is shorter.

This orphanage is a government run orphanage and at least paying guests are aware of this when they enter and hopefully all money raised goes towards the elephant's upkeep and setting them free back into the jungle.

I found all the public areas where we went and the enclosures we saw were very clean and tidy.

Take Sri Lankan money with you - although you can use CC at the Orphanage shop and other shops in the town, generally speaking they don't take cash unless it's Sri Lankan money.

There is an opportunity to feed the elephants by hand in one areas of the orphanage however Rupees are required - no USD or other currency and definitely no CC there !!  Luckily our guide exchanged some USD for Rupees but the fruit was gone very quickly.

Yes there were a few elephants chained up in another enclosure but of the three enclosures we saw, this was the only one where they were chained.  The reason we were given for this was because they are wild animals... let's face it ... if they are males and are maturing, they could get annoyed about something and cause injuries to other elephants if not their handlers and / or the public if they crashed through the fence.

Indeed at the elephant feeding area I saw one elephant get grumpy with another one for muscling in on the food I was feeding it - the elephant turned around and head butted the second elephant in its side to show it's displeasure at eating its food.

The third area where we saw elephants at this Orphanage, the elephants were roaming free in a large treed area ... I wondered if this was the first stage of getting them used to fending for themselves before setting them free in the jungle.

We had lunch included in our ship's shore excursion at a hotel by the river and luckily for us, they had quite a few elephants bathing there - a lovely thing to see.

IMO, this excursion is not suitable for mobility impaired people because the terrain to get to the elephant enclosures is not paved and the surface is uneven.  There's also a few steps to negotiate within the elephant orphanage area.  Also, the "road" to the hotel where we went for lunch was not paved either.

Title: Elephants galore
Text: If you are in Sri Lanka and want to see lots of elephants and get up close and feed them, look no further than Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage. About 2 to 2 1/2 hours drive from Colombo is this nice, quiet area where they care for orphaned elephants. We could count more than two dozen elephants there. Reach early (I recommend leaving Colombo by 6.30) if you want to capture it all when it's not hot, and get tickets. As is with most places in Sri Lanka - entry ticket prices depend on your nationality. You walk in and the elephants come out and you can get close to the, feed them fruits etc. Then they take the elephants for a shower at a nearby river. I thought it was going to be all natural, but then they opened a powerful hose and started showering the elephants. Oh well.. Sip a cup of coffee or get some juice while watching that at one of the few restaurants there (watch out for those flies!). There are several shops that sell pooper (paper made out of elephant poop) and other trinkets there. I found them exorbitantly priced, so I skipped. But overall a very pleasant place to go outside of colombo.

Title: Elephants friendly to people
Text:
The orphanage is located some 1 hr from kandy or 2 hrs from colombo. They charge rupees 3500 per person which is roughly usd 20. The best time to go is when they are taken for bath (10am to 12pm noon) parading through a 250m street of souvenir shops. 
At the sanctuary you can feed them and watch them. Overall good experience

Title: Bad place
Text: Sad place, the people that work with the elephants are agresive and bad people. Everything is just about the money. I wouldnt go there never again. Ticket is 3.000 SLR ..

Title: Big number of elephants that you can observe all their daily activities in a natural habitat
Text:
Big number of elephants that you can observe all their daily activities in a natural habitat 
The elephants are taken to the river twice daily for bathing for 2 hours each time.
The fees is 3000 rupies per person

Title: Awesome
Text: must see for all Elephant lovers. Breathtaking watching these beautiful  creatures in a natural environment.

Title: Visit the site for yourself & make up your own mind!
Text:
I visited Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage on 15 February 2020 from Australia. 

This was my first holiday to Sri Lanka even though my parents are Sri Lankan. 

I had heard many stories from my relatives about the elephants at Pinnawala and had always wanted to visit. 

In saying that, making the decision to go was a tough one as I am aware that currently Pinnawala is classed as slightly controversial & I am an extreme animal lover!

Nevertheless after reading many reviews (some from people whom havent even visited the site!?), I decided that I needed to see it for myself & make up my own mind. 

My honest opinion was that I was pleasantly surprised and I believe that they are genuinely trying to improve the operations of the park. 

Out of the 90 odd elephants I saw there, the majority were free roaming and appeared to enjoy their free time and bathing in the river. 
The only elephants I saw had chains were some of the males which is more for everyones protection so as not to cause a stampede. There were also 2 that were in pens apparently under veterinary care. 

The only tourist interaction that I saw was the fruit feeding which I avidly took part in - i bought like 4 baskets of fruit to give to 2 beautiful elephants. 

(**And for those people complaining about having to pay for the fruit baskets- get over it! 
It only costs like $2 aud for a basket of fruit! You pay way more than that for animal encounters in western countries and thats not included in your ticket price either!)

No tourists (that I saw) were allowed to bathe with the elephants etc at the park and I didnt really see any exploitation as such. Ie, I did not see any elephant rides being provided.

It was just a joy to see them down at the river with many elephants enjoying the water or their mud bath. 

At the end of the day people will need to make up their own minds as to what theyre comfortable with. 

I personally am happy I went there and I dont believe it is as bad as some people are making it out to be.

Title: Breakfast with the elephants
Text: This place is very interesting, I would highly recommend visiting and having breakfast around 10 am when the elephants come down to the river to take a bath. That was the highlight of our visit.

Title: what fun to watch the elephants
Text:
we spent a happy hour watching the elephants feed, scratch themselves on huge posts and then amble down to the river for a thorough brushing from their Mahoots .
the look of sheer bliss on their faces was really amazing .

Title: A lovely day.
Text: A lovely day watching the Elephants playing. We only saw 1 elephant chained and apparently he was being aggressive. Others were having a great time. They have a small museum where they re cycle the dung to make paper etc....I didn't want to go at first but I'm glad i did.

Title: Grat jeep safari
Text: You cannot miss it. It is worth every penny and minute spend to get there! I would recommend to go there very early in the morning before animals hide from heat to the forest. As the jeeps have no windows it is wise to take a hat or something protecting your ears from wind diving along the dam on the lake. I would also suggest to take good camera, binoculars with you as well as something to drink and eat as the trip takes 4 hours. There are so many animals to see that you will enjoy every minute you spend there. As the animals got used to the jeeps they dont escape  we had to stop few times to let elephants, warans, lizards cross the dirt road in peace.

Title: Disappointed experience
Text:
we were expecting to give the elephant a bath and give some food to elephants.
but we were left disappointed.
we were taken around the orphanage where the orphan elephants are kept.
then on the other side of the road,our guide took us to see elephants being given a bath and fed.

but over there,the people started asking money if we wanted to feed guava fruits to the elephants.or even to give bath,they were charging money.

we neither gave bath to the elephant,nor we fed the elephant.

we thought it was part of the ticket which we had purchased.

overall my kids were left very disappointed.

Title: Elephant Orphan
Text:
