Well arrived at around 1430 hours, just to be told as the Grand hotel which we were booked in, cant be accessed until 1600 hours, as the elephants are still out there, we must pay an entry, or wait till 4pm, although check in starts at 3pm, what a drama, so are in a local restaurant which was incidentally amazing, later meeting another tourist from uk, we sat down had few cups of tea, but we were virtually the only ones there, progressing to dinner, which were not so good,  it was like the taste ran away from the food in boardum.

tomorrow we will see the elephants,
so it was amazing seeing the elephants, they are literally walked passed the road which is in front of our hotel, the sight is amazing, I had a clear shot of it, until some t*** moved into my shot, thanks mann!! I cursed at him with outrage, but clearly whilst having a ignorant mannerism, he also had a lack of understanding of simple english too, never mind.
the elephants were amazing to look at bathing themselves, putting dry soil all over them using their trunks, then they roll around in the water to wash off.
some of the elephants were chained up and separated from the the rest, in observation, I could only see the older problematic and younger rascal are chained and separated, presuming to prevent them from harm.
the journey was amazing shame we had to leave, then again the hotel was not very welcoming the food was absolutely rubbish a lot of improvement nee

Title: Very pleasant
Text: We went here because we had some spare time. Its cheap to get in and didnt need to book before our visit. We went to the 9am feed, you dont get to feed or touch the elephants just view, plenty of seating. Its funny watching the young elephants race towards the milk station which is done with a few at a time, its not very long maybe 1.30 hours but a pleasant experience. No one tells you what or why they do it but there is a information building that you can walk through.

Title: Sad
Text:
I love elephants and was very excited to see, interact, feed and bath them. Pinnawala was a as disappointing as it could be. elephants ill treated, hurt, scared, chained. they were literally poking the elephants with metal rods to make them do things. 

For visitors to be able to bathe the elephants, the elephants must lay down in the water. To make them do this, the handler pokes and chains the elephants. You can hear the elephants crying in pain. All this because visitors want to experience something. 

There are cafes like Elephant bay and others that offer a view of the bathing elephants. 
Strongly urge you to not participate in these activities, which in turn will encourage brutality to animals!

One thing you can consider is buying Poo Paper. it sounds weird but is eco friendly as it is made of elephants poop. The have great shops to buy stationary and painting made from poo paper in Pinnawala

Title: Sad + mistreat elephants
Text:
If you want to see sad elephants which are mistreated with scars on their body + if you want to support this sad place you can go there but it has nothing to do with a safe place for this beautiful animals. 
Some of them are on chains and the babies are separated from their moms to be more attractive for the tourists. 
Dont spend a single coin to support this system! The animals will thank you!!!

Title: Seemed to be Exploiting elephants for profit
Text: Walked in and saw how the elephants were kept and treated - walked out nearly in tears?????? .i felt uncomfortable and the elephants looked very unhappy and stressed- the staff were also very un-accomodating ! They only accept cash which doesnt sit right for a tourist attraction - more like a tourist trap

Title: Very disappointing
Text: Today we travelled a long way especially to visit the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage and we were so disappointed. It was 3,000lhr to enter and we specifically went for 1pm as between 12pm-2pm that you can supposedly feed the elephants fruit and see milking time. We walked in and the place was deserted, there was no one to help direct you or advise you, only some signs. There were a few elephants you could see in a small grass area with a couple of trees which you could see from a viewing point at least 15 metres away from the elephants themselves. We moved along to another area where there were 6 males chained up to a tiny concrete area with nothing but a couple of coconuts on the floor and men clearing up the ground around them. They were clearly very distressed and not happy in their environment and it was extremely sad to see this especially as we had believed this was somewhere they look after the animals well. There was no elephants in the fruit feeding enclosure (we also saw this was an extra charge even if there was) all in all we were there for about 15 minutes before we decided we should leave. If you love animals and want to see elephants being treated well in a safe environment do not bother wasting your time.

Title: More animal torture and rip-off than anything else
Text:
I was more than shocked. On the one hand we only wanted to watch the animals bathing and we were told that we need a ticket for 3000 LKR each (there is a ticket office for tourists and locals. I doubt that they are the same prices) which is not correct. You can just walk down to the river between 10am and 12pm or 2pm and 4 pm and watch the elephants bathing. You need the ticket to see the "orphanage", which was one of the saddest things I have ever seen. The animals have far too little space and no things to play with. 
When we asked why two elephants were chained and kept circling their heads, we were told "their will first has to be broken". 
There was also an enclosure with 3 baby elephants inside, which were made to pose for photos. There were men standing in front of it offering to take photos of us and the elephants. However, this is not a nice gesture (even if the locals are otherwise very nice and helpful), but afterwards the hand is held out again for money. 

 Also the small elephants which are "rescued" are not let back into freedom. Once an elephant is in Pinnawala, it never leaves again. Some of the elephants were chained to the river and many men with very sharp sticks were also on guard. Of course: safety is a must. But I didnt have a good feeling.
 
Better to go to the Udawalawe National Park and see elephants without chains and men with pointed lances. 

Later we also talked to a very good English speaking local, who told us that only a small part of the income goes to the animals

Title: A Gross Zoo
Text: Awful, awful and then some!  Not as expected!  Elephants chained and in distress.  The mother of twins the first born in captivity, put in an arena so small, mother showing signs of distress.  Most upsetting

Title: Watch elephants freely roaming around
Text:
Quite a nice place to visit to see elephants free to roam around and do their thing without being chained.

There are about 70 elephants here and most of them are free to roam around the property (there are tied only when under medical care or preparing to mate). Visitors have a gallery from where they can watch the elephants, and also walk around their bathing area. There is a small souvenir shop as well.

They take the elephants at designated times to the river for bathing, but that was not done when we went because the river water level was very high. 

This can be fun for kids.

Title: Sad
Text: Billed as a sanctuary for orphaned elephants, commercialism has taken over and it is no more than a glorified tourist attraction zoo. Not a pleasant site to see these majestic creatures chained up and being proded with spiked staffs.

Title: Happy elephants being bathed in a lake
Text:
Entry charges were LKR 800 (for SAARC adults), LKR 3500 (foreign adults). We enjoyed the place a lot because it lets you be quite close to the elephants. It's not every day that you see elephants being bathed in a river. In fact, there were more than 20. There were elephants of all sizes. While some elephants were returning to the orphanage, we witnessed them passing on the road leading to the river. We were less than 6 feet away from them! It was amazing! Make sure you check the timings before you go. You don't want to miss the bathing time. 

There was a small little street with some elephant themed handicraft and boutique shops as well. Mainly for souvenirs. One of the shops was particularly interesting because they made products out of dried elephant dung. They had a little processing plant in the back of their shop.

Title: Worth to visit pinnawala.
Text: Amazing place. Hundred of elephants. Was interest to see how they are taking the bath. And feeding is the main attraction.

Title: Second visit
Text: This time we visit was 4 of Us and 2nd visit for my daughter and first for the Son.. The place is so quiet and peaceful with very few local visitors..Best time to visit the place is now..kids enjoyed the elephant shower...

Title: Good
Text: Must visit attraction in Sri Lanka...it is the place where you can feed ,bath and play with elephants ....must must visit

Title: An amazing spectacle
Text: I was initially worried about going to this place. A lot of reports talk about the elephants being chained up which seriously could prevent any form of enjoyment. We did not actually go into the actual orphanage but merely paid (the full admission price) and watched them crossing the road and bathing at the bottom. Yes, the bull elephants were chained I guess for their and my safety. These were big animals that you would not wish to charge you. The younger and better behaved marched down the road and seemed well looked after and showed no discomfort that I could see. Ok far better that they are free totally in the wild and this would really be the way I would like to see them. They seemed to enjoy their trip and bathe and we did not see any rough handling by any of the Mahoots . All in all a wonderful morning. I would return if I ever get back to Sri Lanka.

Title: Terrible
Text: All elephant chained at night. Most show strong stereotypic behaviours. Many elephants are fat - saw a mahout feeding ice cream to one elephant. Many have chain scars on their legs and must stand in their own faeces all night. The bulls are almost always chained, some not even having shelter. They also sell their elephants to many first and second world zoos. DO NOT SUPPORT!

Title: A Must Visit: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is understanding the balance of Wildlife and Nature
Text:
Visited on 17th Feb 2020

Entry Fee : SLR 800/- per Adult and SLR 400/- per Child of SAARC countries
Timing : 8.30am till 5.30pm (ticket window closes)

Ideal time to visit are 10.00am or 2.00pm respectively when the Elephant herds are taken for bathing to the river in batches, and 12.00noon or 4.00pm when teh elephant herds are brought back after bathing.

We got a chance to see the Elephant herds being brought back from bathing and the walking of the herd in the sandy path is amazing.

Watch towers and pathways are created in the venue for proper movements of the tourists. Also few installations and information boards are provided to inform all about the history of the place and its evolution through years. It also talks about the mahouts or elephant keepers and tools used by them to control the pachyderms.

Duration of visit will be about 1 hour.
Laksala and souvenir shop is available at this attraction. Outside the attraction there are few small shops selling fresh cut fruits and cold drinks and snacks. 

It can be hot on sunny day so please carry umbrella or caps.

Go and Enjoy!

Title: WONDERFUL TO SEE ELEPHANTS
Text: Up close and personal with he elephants, my wife was absolutely star struck with them and had the time of her life, some were chained when in certain areas but plenty roaming free, walked down to the river for play time and bath time and did not see any bad handling of them. feeding the elephants was a treat and the price of a basket of food very reasonable. well worth the visit

Title: Some parts were great but there was a little disquiet about it.
Text: I'm not too sure what I thought about this place.  The elephants have been 'rescued' and they appear happy enough but I had the vague feeling thye were like peforming elephants in a zoo.  It is a geat expeirence to being down a thoroughfre and suddenly a small herd of elephants (with their handlers) wlk past you.  It was great too to see them behaving quite natrally in the water.  But there were some moments of disquiet.  Some of the elephants are chained, and I accept and understand why, but it does leave an impression.  A couple of the elephants are also forced to lie down in the water for the benefit of the crowd which I was not sure of either.  Still, it was an experience althougha bit expensive, 3000 rupees per foreigner.  If you want the experience of feeding a quiet elephant, you can also do that for 250 rupees.  There are no elephant rides and I was pleased about that.  Finally watch out for a scam with the mahouts (handlers).  They will try to isolate you away from the crowd and lead you up into an area by yourself.  They then offer to photograph you with an elephant by yourself but won't return your camera/iphone until you pay them money.  I was offered this a couple of times but did not do it.  I did see a family forking out a few thousand rupees to one of them so watch out for it.

Title: An average only visit this time
Text: At the moment, feeding of the orphaned elephants has been stopped, which detracts from the overall visit. Bathing of the elephants is still taking place but the water level in the river is currently very low.

Title: Elephants beaten
Text: All looks wonderful, but Mahouts have bull hooks and they use them.... they have no respect for the elephants.

Title: Really lovely experience
Text: My 2 year old son loved washing the elephants, and there was the opportunity to ride and feed them also. Elephants appeared well cared for.

Title: Foreigners are charged 10 times more than locals
Text:
The price for locals is Rs.100 and price for foreigners is Rs.3000.  Where is the sense in this?  Do other countries charge Sri Lankans 10 times more when they visit attractions?  

Though most of the elephants roamed free there were some elephants who were chained.

Title: Nice Time
Text: This place is a government owned elephant orphanage. They have loads of elephants here. Activities you can do are feeding the baby elephants and bathing elephants. There is no riding elephants here. Overall it's a nice place to spend an hour or so. Elephants looked well taken care of. Exciting place for kids.

Title: Pinnawala
Text: The elephants were great but be very careful of scams like elephant rides,  agents take foreigners and try to charge them 6000 rupees for a 10 min ride which is a rip off, we got ours for 2000 which is still very expensive, small place you only need an hour there and not very good elephants are prisoners and its all a money making scam,  foreigners get charged 10 times more for entrance in Sri Lanka compared to locals why should they pay more its all a rip off

Title: A MUST DO !
Text: The highlight of our Sri Lanka trip. It is worthwhile to pay the additional charge and go beyond the crowd and rope to wash a 3 tonne elephant in the river. We all found it very very special washing an elephant and getting sprayed with the elephants trunk in the process. An experience I will never forget.

Title: A must visit
Text: It is a beautiful place where you get to see elephants from a closer distance. We had an awesome time with the kids there. They loved it as they got to bathe the elephant and the elephant later on bathes them. You also get to see the baby elephants. Time spent there will always be etched in our minds. Do keep spare clothes with you when you visit the Pinnawala Elephant orphanage.

Title: Elephants are amazing
Text: You can watch the elephants bath in the local river. Once you look into the reason why and how, you need to make up your own mind on the scenario. I took up the option to wash the matriarch of the herd. She is a beautiful animal and I am thankful to get close and wash her, she made sure I was wet as well! Having been to other countries where orphaned animals are left to die, I am glad these gentle giants do have an option here. Yes, it is a tourist attraction, but feed needs to come from somewhere. (You can decide) If you are in the area I would go. BTW, we have travelling Sri Lanka very safe! There have been some great sites!

Title: not the best place to see elephants
Text: the orphanage is just a tourist attraction to make money. if you want to see elephants its best to ask your tour guide to take you to a national park were the elephants roam freely and you get to see them in their natural habitat.

Title: Too touristic
Text: It's lovely to see bunch of  \elephants so close. But everything here is almost too much touristic. Tickets are expensive. It is nice to see them while they are in the water. But it's a bit of a trap for tourist to steal from your pockets. People around here charged too much to take just one photo with an elephant.

Title: Pinnawala elephant orphanage
Text: Great experience and we can see more number of elephants at one single place. Baby elephants and female elephants are roaming freely and tourists can enjoy the site. We are informed that milk feeding is not there since elephants are now more than 5 years old. We can feed elephants (at specific timings ). Male elephants are kept separately. More than 10 elephants are moved to Kandy to participate in temple festival. Entrance fee (LKR 110) for local, SAARC countries (LKR 800) and other foreign countries (LKR 3000) are different.

Title: First time see the Elephants Bathing
Text:
great experience, by visiting the orphanage, you also sponsor the survival of the species! the best part of the visit are the bathing elephants in the river, we could have stayed there for hours!
good tip from our tour guide: while watching the elephants at the river, enjoy a dring on the terrace at the right side of the river, it will give you access to an amazing and clear overview over the bathing elephants.

Date of experience: August 2019

Title: Not an Elephant orphanage but a tourist attraction!
Text:
Not an elephant orphanage at all! More that 80 elephants in distress are kept there just to amuse the ignorant tourists. Most of the beast are chained and follow a routine programme just to entertain the crowd, so sad. all the time they are are being beaten and frightened to obey.
It was nice to be near them but not pleasant to see all this circus.

Title: So many elephants in one place
Text: If you love elephants this is the place. So many elephants in one place. You can feed them( at a particular time) and see them roam freely. Overall a fun park.

Title: Elephants are so cute
Text: This place was not originally on our iternary  but our driver suggested it and it was on our way (almost) to Dambulla. Im glad we stopped here. It is sad to see them in chains but this is a treatment centre for injured elephants. We got to feed Meenachi, the elephant. I should confess this is the first time I actually touched an elephant. After the feeding, the elephants were taken to a river across to bathe. How is elephants bathing in a river not a viral video on YouTube is beyond me. Its was an absolute delight to watch these elephants frolic in the river. We couldnt sit and watch for hours to keep up with our iternary. On our way out we stopped buy to pick-up Poo-poo paper. Yes its paper made out of elephant dung. Dont worry it doesnt smell. I suggest to bargain before buying or wait till Kandy to purchase. We found poo-poo paper cheaper in Galle (Dutch fort) and Kandy.

Title: Just OK
Text:
We didnt find anything great there. Few activities around elephants. Kids might like it. 
Nothing much for adults. Tickets for SAARC COUNTRY is 800 lkr and golf cart is 1200 lkr
Can be avoided definitely

Title: Few Hours with Living Monsters
Text: This is first time we saw the Asian Elephants. We are scared first time when we saw them. We dont agreed hurting them. They need freedom we thing. But government doing good job keeping take care of them. There are some disabled. Tickets little bit expensive we think. there are big gap with local tickets. But its nice visit.

Title: Biggest herd of elephants
Text: Theres a big herd of elephants probably arround 100 and all are taken to river twice a day. That the best times to visit this wonderful place where you can see so many of this magnificent creature.

Title: Strange place
Text:
We went here wanting to make up our own minds from reading reviews and have very mixed feelings. On one hand, the elephants were healthy looking (no bones showing) and majority allowed to roam around the river free.

However, around 8 elephants were chained to various spots around the river...the signs say this is to stop harm/danger of the Male elephants. From the looks of things, these elephants were chained for tourists photos as they were dotted around the hotel points and only need the front (of the viewing platform). The elephants are also clearly scared of the mahouts & when one of them began to ride the elephant he was nearly kicked off.

We went up to the relaxing zone which didnt look that way for the elephants at all. It sort of looks like an elephant zoo enclosure, however yet again all elephants there were chained up and visibly distressed. A better idea would be to let the elephants freely roam and invite tourists to visit safari style - no touching or contact. 

What we couldnt understand is if this was an orphanage...why arent they let out into the wild, given they are well enough/old enough.

Title: Interesting..
Text: Lots of elephants were bathing in the river at the time when we arrived to this elephant orphanage and  there were few activities including elephant parade and feeding baby elephants. You are allowed to feed lovely, little cute baby elephants under their supervision which was great.

Title: A shriking elephant orphanage
Text: Our second visit to this orphanage, which has shrunk to just viewing elephants going down to the river for their daily dip!

Title: UNETHICAL do no go there
Text: The elephants are beaten up before the tourists arrive and chained up. Any place that allows elephants bathing and riding has had to beat them up at some point in life. The elephants do not actually live in the river but they are brought there every morning in a chain and beaten with a stick that gets into their skin for them not to move. It was horrible to see. Never go there.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Although seeing animals in captivity is never fun, but it seems like they take good care of the elephants in this sanctuary. When I arrived, the elephants were bathing in the river, which could be fun to watch. The interior of the sanctuary is not yet big and you may just spend less than an hour three

Title: Life For Elephants  -  JUNE 22
Text: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is an orphanage located at Pinnawala village approximately  13km from Kegalle town on the Colombo Kandy Road (A1 turn to left near the 82km post). This orphanage provides a lifeline to the orphaned baby elephants and orphaned elephants lost in the wilderness. You can see them having a bath in the river then crossed the road back to the orphanage where they are feed and roam the ground. The orphanage will be open from 08.30 hrs to 18.00 hrs daily. Normally herd of elephants bathing in the river from 10.00 to 12.00 again from 14.00 to 16.00. Milk feeding starts in morning 09.15, 13.15 and 17.00 hrs. It is the place that gives us unforgettable experience. Elephant caretakers must care with love and respect without being cruel to the elephants will help them grow up with nature.

Title: Interesting and Memorable
Text: Surely a memorable trip. Elephant feeding and bath. Kind of an Elephants parade as well. We missed the kids. They wouldve loved it.

Title: Avoid if you care about animals.
Text:
I hadn't done any research on this place before visiting which was a huge mistake.

The young elephants are tamed by being chained up and beaten and shouted at. They were visibly very distressed and making a lot of noise. 
I felt extremely upset when I saw this and angry at myself for visiting. Our guide then took us down to the river where the elephants are taken to bathe. Some are chained up and forced to lie down in the water. There is no need to treat these poor elephants this way. 
Go and visit Minneriya National Park instead to see happy elephants roaming free in the wild.

Title: Disappointed- sad
Text:
So disappointed with Pinnawala Elephant orphanage. They advertise saying elephants are semi wild but reality is, elephants are not well treated, elephants have mahouts to be trained and unfortunately they dont have a proper semiwild life. Elephants will end working for temples and going to Parahera in some point which makes me really sad. Pinnawala orphanage says there are 84 elephants but visible you can only see a group of 27 elephants + other group of 10 sick elephants. Where are the others? I would say, chained, because they refuse to be domesticated* I paid 3k rupees for the entrance expecting to see elephants having a better care. I am the person who would pay more if elephants are well treated. Elephants only eat once per day (kindly note elephants of Pinnawala are well fitted), but still, the nature of elephants is to eat several times per day. Sri Lanka government, please do something to improve the programs for elephants, I understand your mindset, culture and religion and most important I respect it, I understand the value and meaning of Parahera, but dont advertise lies. Please give a better care for them. Elephants are humble and loyal animals we should be better for them. 
*Note: some elephants are on their Musth period, is understandable that they remain separated from the group, but, are 50 elephants on their Musth? Dont think so. 
Note 2: tourism is an income that Pinnawala orphanage needs to give elephants a better life. I wont say dont visit the place, I will say: go and see for yourself, raise the voice and ask Sri Lanka Government to improve the programs.

Title: An Awsome Place.. A Must Visit
Text:
This is an awsome place, one must visit while in Coorg or rather in Karnataka,,,,
A sort of Island where these elephants are looed after was just too good!
They were fed with hey balls that were wrapped around some seeds and cereals that were required by the animals.
Oil was applied on their body to avoid any wounds.
Their bathing was also very interesting in the river ... viewers are given a chance to take a pert in the activities.
Most inmportantly, the animals were almost in the open and were very closed to the viewers.
The only problem was the approach... the walk through the river was a  bit dangerous, as the path was slippery and many people were seen falling int he water and getting injured. There is no good arrangements for parking the vehicles also. This part must be looked after.

Title: Elephant viewing
Text:
On the way to Kandy from Colombo take a visit to see the Elephants. If your timing is right you see them having a bath in the river then cross the road back to the orphanage where they are feed and roam the grounds

They appear well cared for and are checked for illness and treated. A lot are injured or former working Elephants who retire there or orphans who need looking after. 

Having read the bad reviews I didnt see any mistreatment and to me it looks like they were caring for the animals, the handlers do heard the elephants with sticks or a hand slap on the legs but it didnt seem to bother them and the 4 or 5 tonne elephant has the size and weight advantage if it did hurt, they could easily kill the handler

Title: Lots of Elephants - Watch Your Step
Text: We arrived in the late morning and found most of the elephants down at the river bathing.  As we walked down the street to see them, we passed several shops selling souvenirs and then suddenly were treated to a few elephants being ridden back to the orphanage from the river.  It was a bit scary, but also exciting as they walked right past us.  We got down to the river and there was the rest of the group bathing and playing.  We took a few pictures and then went to the orphanage where after a short walk inside we came to an area where one can feed the elephants.  I didn't see any mistreatment while we were there, but our experience was limited to about an hour and a half.  It's a long drive to get here, but if you like elephants, it's worth the drive.  We also passed a few wild elephants crossing the road on the way from Colombo, so keep an eye out if this is your route too.

Title: Elephants in a pen
Text:
Supposedly elephants roam naturally through the 24 acre park. Nope. Penned elephants trained to lay their trunks out so you can feed them fruit you have to buy. One can tell the elephants didnt like their handlers. 

Nice to feed and touch elephants though

Title: Huge disappointment
Text:
If you short of time and/or money, you can easily avoid this place. This is basically a zoo (even worse than a zoo) than an orphanage. How often do you see children in orphanage tied up with chains and made to walk a long alleyway just so that a few tourists who paid exorbitant prices for tickets can watch them walk and feed them coconuts?

The elephants take bath in the pond which is at the opposite side of the road from the orphanage, twice a day. We were very excited that we reached just in time when the elephants were getting ready to walk through that alley to go to the pond to take bath. What we saw was very disappointing. Almost all the elephants were chained to their teeth. Most of them were missing their tusks (don't know when it happened) and almost all of them just sat in the pond and did nothing.

Inside the orphanage, it was the same story. You can see them grazing or can give them bananas or other fruits (there are extra charges for that as you can only buy the fruits from one of the shops inside the orphanage).

We were from the SAARC country so we paid 750 LKR per person for entry but I think for foreign tourists from other countries the fees is around 3000 LKR. It is highly overpriced and it's better to actually go to Marissa and watch whales in their natural habitat instead of seeing chained Elephants sitting in water.

You can do all the things you can do here at Dehiwala zoo in Colombo, including seeing Elephants taking bath.

Title: Basically an elephant prison
Text:
We visited this place in February as part of a tour with Mercury Holidays.  We were hoping it would be the highlight of our trip, sadly it left us with bad memories for this part of the trip.  
We started watching the elephants in the water from an adjacent hotel veranda, the elephants certainly didn't appear to want to be there, they were corralled to stay close to the hotels so that visitors could see them.  We then went to the land site on the opposite side of the road, again elephants are corralled for the entertainment of the viewing public. A very heavily pregnant elephant was trying to get to a water hole at the top of the paddock with some other elephants following, however the mahouts would not let her rest and drove her and her followers to the part of the paddock closest to the tourists.  In another part of the paddock one of the mahouts was repeatedly hitting an elephant in the leg making it squeal, a sound I don't want to hear again.  One of the staff stood near me kept saying 'happy elephant'. I'm not David Attenborough but I would say that the elephant was not squealing with delight.  There were also other elephants under shelter which clearly had mental issues and were heavily chained, I do however appreciate that where they have been rescued from may be the cause of their problems and not the place they have come to. 
I have read through some of the reviews and they do vary widely and of course they're all personal assessments, some cultures approach animal care differently, for instance some have referred to being able to ride the elephants which I personally don't agree with.  I would strongly recommend you think seriously about visiting this place, yes there are a lot of elephants here which is great, but the evident lack of care for them is distressing if you are an animal lover.

Title: Beautiful Baby Elephants
Text:
A must visit if you like elephants, there must be around 50. From the age of around 2 months old, they get released in pairs from the main pound towards the milking station, its fantastic to see them realise theres food, and its a race.
Its a vey cheap entrance fee, around 500 slr which is approx £2.50. But get there early as it gets packed. Great entertainment for the whole family.
They are well looked after.

Title: Not what we expected!
Text: Despite all the positive recommendations for this elephant 'orphanage', it seemed more like an elephant medium security prison. There are many captive elephants that are kept in large fields. In some areas the visitors can come close and even touch the tamer elephants. Around mid morning (10:30 to be precise), the elephants are paraded down to  the nearby river and encouraged (or in the case of some of the young male bulls, forced) to bathe. The male elephants are chained up and pushed and prodded, and appear and sound unhappy. The females and children though are allowed to roam and appear less anxious. In comparison to elephant sanctuaries in Thailand or free roaming African elephants, many of these Asian elephants appeared to be distinctly unhappy and uncomfortable. We went with two teenage girls and they were distinctly unhappy with the elephants' circumstances, as was I.

Title: Loved the elephants!!
Text:
This place has alot of elephants which range in age.
They also offer you to ride on one of them..
There was a baby elephant who was dancing for us..it was lovely!
There are separate entry tickets according to your prefrence..we took the 3000/-  SL rupees pre person ticket for half hour!

Title: SRILANKA TOUR
Text: we visited on our way to kandy.we did colombo city tour on arrival in the morning so reached there late afternoon-bathing time at the river.to make most of it,you need to be there in the morning,but we had limited time on the tour.good sovenier shops.few hours is enough.

Title: One of the best experiences !
Text:
It is definitely one of the best experiences in Sri Lanka.
I personally love elephants, and it is so nice to see them have a shelter and people who care about them, it was a lot of fun to watch them walk by us, to see them enjoy a bath in the river, and there is always a naughty one in the group. you should go and experience it for yourself, every ticket counts for those elephant orphans.

Title: Abandon sentimentality
Text:
You cannot view this with western eyes, some of the elephants need to be chained because they can be dangerous. The alternative would be to put the elephant down. These are orphan animals that are being prepared to be released to the wild at Yala
It is a wonderful sight to see these magnificent animals bathing in the river.

Title: Big disappointment
Text: I know they explain why they chain elephants, but its always hard to see elephant chained and think its for their own good - at an orphanage at that. Then, the price to go in and see the elephants is just ridiculous when all you get is to walkthrough shops, sit a restaurants, and watch the elephants from a distance. On the other side you have to buy the food if you want to feed them. I mean, it was a waste of my time. I had a better experience with elephants in Thailand. If you had never seen elephants, I would just wait around the area because they walk them from one side to the other - take your picture and keep it moving. Oh and if you had s driver like me, they will take you to an Herb Garden as part of the ticket price to get a tour: TOTAL SCAM. Go for the tour, but dont buy anything.

Title: Good and Bad
Text:
We were a bit disturbed that the first elephants were chained up! We were told that the animals were a bit "frisky" and needed protection from each other. Perhaps we were overly sentimental but it just didn't seem right.
The elephants cooling down in the river was good to watch.
We eat in the Elephant Bay Restaurant and the food was terrible. Worst we have had on our trip.

Title: Not what we thought
Text:
I found this place distressing. So many of the elephants were chained up and swaying from side to side. I think the whole 'orphanage' title is questionable.I witnessed some of the kahoots hooking and poking the elephants alot. One kahoots wouldn't stop poking and hooking his elephant and when he walked away the elephant went crazy trying to break her chains.
It was terrible to watch. I wish I never went there.

Title: Variety of Interaction
Text: This was an interesting experience with many elephants roaming unchained. It was good to see them in that environment, however there were also a number of chained elephants that looked quite forelorn. I expect there is a good reason but it seemed unfortunate. There was also feeding of the elephants by tourists and both parties clearly liked it. There was washing in the river which the elephants seem to like - some of the elephants received a body scrub by the handlers. We also did a seperate elephant safari in the wild and it was much better to see the elephants roaming free.

Title: Its how you perceive it
Text:
We visited this elephant orphanage and quite honestly didn't see any ill treatment of the animals.  It was lovely to see the elephants walking to the river for  a bathe. We got quite close to a few of the cheeky ones who came up to the chain where we could stand. 
Yes a few of the males have a chain to a leg but we were told they were the "frisky" ones and it was to help keep them under control. 
The older  males are separated from the females as in the wild . They even have a "murderer" male which is kept apart from all the others and needs a few members of staff around when cleaning his area. He apparently has killed humans when he was in the wildlife reserves-  so nice to see he has been given a chance to life as his rages were probably instigated by humans  who didn't behave appropriately around him. 
We were told not to buy fruit from the street sellers and were always reminded to behave appropriately. 
Such a joy to see these huge creatures.

Title: Elephants bathing a must see
Text:
Some negative reviews on here and comments concerning the treatment of the elephants.
Some are in chains but these are male elephants and are to control their natural aggression to other males.
The mahmoods use sticks to encourage understanding of commands - again for the safety of the elephants and surrounding people. They use the sticks to apply pressure to vital points ( acupuncture points) which do not harm the elephants - if youve ever been struck in a pressure point you will know a slight jab doesnt hurt but does encourage the body to move in a certain way. This is what they do with the Sticks. You couldnt move an elephant with a shove or a little stick otherwise.

If youre concerned with the treatment suggest research first before judging. 

Many of the elephants come from farmland where theyve been trapped in holes dug by farmers to collect water. They often have broken limbs when they come to the sanctuary. 

Once recovered, most are returned to the forests. Some pictures attached of the time we watched them bathing.

One thing to note - from wherever you are you will likely take some time to get there. For us it was worth the journey.

Title: It is what it is!
Text: If the tourists help pay for their food it is ethically OK(ish). It was great to get close to the elephants, from a cafe, and the vast majority of elephants were free to wander. Three were chained and one looked unhappy. Some seemed to really enjoy their back scrubs and it was a memorable experience. There were a series of shops on the way down and one tried to shortchange us 1000 rupees so be careful.

Title: Incredible!!!!
Text: Time your visit to see them either go down the road to the watering hole or back up!!! You can feed them and bath them all for extra cost!!

Title: Heartwarming
Text: This orphanage is amazing. It supports the weaker elephants in the Jungle. It seems the mothers bring their young to be given milk and we watch them been let in through  the gates to be fed. There was even an old elephant with a prosthetic boot.....really heartwarming.

Title: Elephant Orphanage
Text:
I strongly recommend skipping this experience. 
There are so many great opportunities to see elephants in their natural habitat in Sri Lanka. This was not an orphanage, more like a zoo. The staff did not appear to care about the animals. The animals are not treated well. They dont seem to have the freedom to roam that I hoped they would. They are chained up at times. Standing in the river, they were made to stand in a tight group.
The website advertises bottle feeding but this is no longer happening.
We were approached by an employee who offered to take a photo. He then led us behind a building (we thought he was leading us to more elephants) and demanded a tip. 
Our kids did enjoy feeding fruit to the elephants. Still, not the experience we were hoping for.

Title: Not an Orphanage, Better Avoid
Text: We were grossly disappointed to see elephants in chains, many of them visibly distressed, forced to pose for tourists. It felt like a zoo/circus. Don't do the same mistake as we did and don't financially support this animal hell. However when we visited I was sad to see these poor animals in such distress. Better Avoid.

Title: Up close and personal with elephants
Text: If you want to see elephants in their natural habitat, this is not the place for you. If you want to get up close and personal to elephants who are being well taken care of, come here. Yes, some of the (male) elephants are in chains but you leash your dog, right? Same concept only you're trying to leash a 2-ton semi-wild animal.  I never saw one hit or its chain pulled on. They seemed to listen well to voice commands. Elephants were in social groups. Was fun to see them walking through the street from the river back to the sanctuary.  Got to feed one. Loved it.

Title: Elephant Paradise in Paradise!!!
Text:
The whole concept, location, facilities  are fabulous and fantastic. Best such in the world!

Been to many such facilities around the world, nothing comes even close when it comes to being close to the Indian elephants.!

Title: Disappointed & Upsetting
Text:
Having been to an Elephant sanctuary in Phuket, Thailand where the elephants were free to roam and were very well looked after, this was a considerable disappointment.

Elephants penned in and chained by the neck and feet is what you can expect to see here. Added to this, the wardens hold long spear like tools with curved ends in order to control the animals, this creates a very circus-esque atmosphere where you just feel sorry these beautiful animals. 

Bottle feeding is advertised but was not happening on our day of visit - dont get too excited, you yourself dont get to bottle feed elephants as the orphanage implies, you watch an employee do it (just to save you some time).

All in all, save your money and pay more elsewhere for a more natural, less zoo-like experience where the elephants are treated better.

T

Title: So much Improvement needed
Text:
There was huge property where raising up, taking care and protecting Elephants, but i think they did not run it properly. There was nothing to do except for going around in the bright sun-meeting elephan randomly , feeding them and taking pics with them. 
No shows, no entertainment at all...

User_Location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
Title: ELEPHANT HELL
Text:
We visited this tour part of what Mercury Holidays offer, I did at the time question the rep about the chains on the  elephannts as I had read about this, and aware this is a cultural difference, but at the end of the day it should be about the elephant not a zoo or making the elephant perform for you.  The Rep advised the chains were required as the Bulls do get aggressive.  What I dont understand is elephants should be able to roam freely, however when we visited I was sad to see these poor animals in such distress.

When you approach the orphanage you are advised not to purchase any fruit but to buy inside, the place was heaving with local school children coach loads - not sure if this is part of their school curriculum but vast amount visiting.  The elephants in the watering hole seemed dazed and when one elephant approach the handler who has a stick with a hook to control the elephants came close she quickly reacted and walked away - the elephants seemed lifeless and bored.  One elephant was showing signs of distress side to side shaking her head and body - not nice to see.  We then visited the feeding stations and walked passed where the elephants are seen my the public - makes you wonder how much space do these elephants have to roam - not a great deal.  I saw the bull elephants chained and what was so shocking was the behaviour again rocking back and forth - this is where he remains all day - and the phrase for the wealth and safety of all elephants was the reason - this was utterly sad, such a beautiful animal chained. Again aware the cultural differences but, somehow human instinct should kick in for anyone to see these elephants are anything but happy. We then visited the feeding station once again for the elephants to perform - one of the man handlers asked if I wanted a picture of the elephant raising its trunk - he called the elephant over and used this stick to control her - just like a circus act, and she had chains around her neck.

Please think twice about contributing to this orphanage in hindsight I regret contributing, and my advice would be be go on the safari - this is where you see elephants roaming freely and happy but the choice is yours.

Title: Overrated.
Text:
We visited this place on our way to Kandy. The price of Rs3000 is way to much to see some elephants bathing in the river. And when you visit the otherside, the park where they stay, there is not much to see.
I do understand you have to chain these semi wild animals but I really thought they will roam around freely. It is nice to see them thaking a bath i  the river and then walk over the street back to the park. I have to admit that it is not worth the price.

Title: Wonderfull experience with this beautiful animals.
Text:
Spent 2 hours at Millennium Elephant orphanage. The pre walk information sessions was really informative and revealing!  Walked with the first elephant born there "Rani" - just a wonderful experience as she accepted food and gently walked around with us. Her mahout was gentle and you could see the intense relationship. The helped washed her in the stream and scrubbed her with coconut shell.  I swear she winked at me!  She lay there as we all had turns. Then she showered us with water from her trunk. These are just beautiful and serene creatures.
Next door is the only elephant poo paper factory in the world. It's free and fascinating how the elephant dung is used to make paper in a very simple and environmentally friendly way. Nice gift shop as well with the final products for sale, all reasonably priced.

Title: Pinnawala elephant orphanage
Text: While going from Colombo, the tour operators have this on their itinerary.Only Sri Lankan currency accepted for purchasing the tickets. Elephants can be seen chained, eating leaves, taking a bath.In case one has already seen elephants, the trip is not worth the effort. Better is to go straight from Colombo to Kandy

Title: Good day
Text:
We went to this place to see some elephants of the orphanage which are there like 60-70. They have specifc time to take them to bath to the river. 
Ticket for 1 person is Rs 3000 which is quite expensive. Nice to visit for a shot time.

Title: Not wonderful
Text: The elephants were lovely but I hated seeing them in chains Have visited an orphanage in Kenya and there were no chains I realise the male elephants can be aggressive but wondered why they have not been released to the wild again also they let them breed? Site is attractive lovely by the river watching the elephants until you see the chains Had meal in restaurant and it was very good personally I would not visit again but maybe our attitudes are different to theirs

Title: Average
Text:
I have mixed feelings about my visit to Pinnawala. Having read some disturbing reports I was nervous about what we would see. We visited early in the morning and saw the elephants bathing and then went back to the reserve and saw some elephant there in the enclosures. Did we see cruelty? No. Did we see chains? Yes. Was I impressed? I don't think so.

Now, I have to confess to not being a fan of zoos on the whole but I can really appreciate a zoo that has a conservation ethos (Twycross for instance) Pinnawala felt like a poor zoo to me. A few elephants paraded for public entertainment. Thats ok I guess if there is a greater good but I'm not sure there is. 

Overall this was an ok experience but I wouldn't go again.

Title: Very suprised
Text:
After reading reviews about the treatment of these elephants I was very anxious to see for myself.
When we arrived early in the morning the elephants were having there feed and the keepers cleaning out the poo and water troughs and refilling them, they were all playing around and having such fun, not one elephant was pacing up and down or looked stressed, one elephant was spraying the keeper with water whilst he was trying to clean out the trough, after about 1/2 hour of watching these beautiful animals, they were let out and started walking down the road to the river the traffic is stopped whilst they cross the road it was so lovely to see them being washed and playing in the river spraying water over each other this happens twice a day, whilst we were we had the opportunity to feed a elephant with some fruit which was amazing and we really enjoyed this and so did the elephants.
The bull elephants were chained on the way to the river for safety, these male elephants are enormous about 8feet high and its a way of controlling them whilst going down to the river, we looked at there feet there was no sores cuts or callous the male and females are separated when they go down the river because the males can get very aggressive at no point did we see any keepers use sticks on the elephants, we had a lovely time and glad we went, at least being at this place they are not poached and left to die.

Title: Not the bad place some people write about.
Text:
I visited Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage just over a week ago and I must say that I was on high alert after a few derogatory articles I had seen written about the facility and its treatment of the elephants. Happily, I found nothing worthy of a complaint.

The elephants parade down to the river and anyone who knows animals can see that they are intelligent beings who are used to the routine and are not at all stressed by the watching crowds - in fact, some clearly loved it and were happy to participate and be patted or fed a morsel along the way.  Once in the river they splash, roll around in the water and clearly enjoy themselves.

Yes, some did have a loose chain around their necks, but this didn't bother them. When you consider the size of an elephant and the general havoc they could cause to a community when aggressive, it's not difficult to understand that there are times when they must be prudently restrained or separated. 
As for returning them all to the wild; these elephants no longer have a place in the wild as they have formed new family bonds within their new herd. Many have already been rescued from the wild where they were close to death and others are on medication or special food.

So if you want to truly help elephants and not just have a pompous rant about turning them loose, visit Pinnawala, spend a few dollars towards their support and watch them happily splash about in safety.

Title: Elephant Orphanage
Text: the Elephant Orphanage is such an interesting place to visit.  At certain times the elephants (ages 1 to 5 years) are fed.  There are viewing stands so you can watch while the elephants are given milk and also greens to eat.

Title: Awesome experience
Text: Long drive from Colombo, but you will not regret it when you get there. Try to reach early to see the elephants taking their bath. You will get the opportunity to ride or feed one. Thrilling experience just to be near to watch them move freely and safely.

Title: Skip it
Text:
Expensive at 3,000 rupees. Locals pay just 110 rupees. I'm happy to pay more as a foreign tourist but not 30 times more. There is no guide nor any information. You can see an elephant chained up swaying from side to side up close. You can see 20 odd elephants in an open area about 30m away. That's it. Very ordinary. 2 stars only because you can go across the road and see some elephants bath in the river and then walk back up to the orphanage. They walk straight past you and across the road. Pretty cool. The traffic is stopped by the police each time. I think you need the ticket to get to the river, our driver organized that.

Overall pretty poor. Save your money and time.

Title: Loved this place
Text: These Huge but loving animals keep you amazed through out your visit to this orphange. Don t miss the elephant bathing experience you will left in awe expression. Here they allow you to feed the elephants.

Title: Sceptical but pleasantly surprised.
Text:
Reviews of Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage praise and condemn so our only choice was to see it for ourselves. The stamp of the countrys Department of Wildlife Conservation on the park was the deciding factor.

Over a twenty year period, Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage hand raised abandoned babies, treated the injured and integrated displaced elephants into a growing herd.

Currently, 88 elephants are part of the Pinnawala family on their 30-acre property, making it one of Sri Lankas largest tourist attractions.

At Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage you will see chains. This is precautionary for large males while bathing, wandering the park  river path, and when a females seductive pheromones spike.

A full grown male can stand more than 2.5 metres weighing  5.5 tonnes. A force to be reckoned with when they want to get down to business.

You will also see mahouts rounding the elephants to keep them in one spot. This is also precautionary to keep them from getting too close to punters.

A disappointing observation was people paying some entrepreneurial mahouts to bathe the elephants. The elephant is chained and made to lie on its side during the encounter. This is not approved and is something the orphanage is trying to eliminate.

Elephants eat an average of 250kg of food per day, multiply that by 88 of them and you have an expensive grocery bill. Modern veterinary equipment and traditional indigenous medicine come at a price and the gallons of milk required to raise a baby elephant is also exorbitant.

Sponsorship programs, donations and your ticket price all contribute to the cost of feeding and caring for these adorable creatures.

Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is not perfect, but the care for these elephants is obvious.

This is a heavily tourist-trafficked attraction. Vendors take advantage of the captive audience and sell everything from elephant poo paper products (quite an interesting process) to every form of elephant printed clothing you can imagine.

Away from this retail madness, however, is picturesque countryside, a meandering river and comfortable accommodation.

Title: Disappointing
Text: Elephants are chained up and poked with sticks. Do yourself a favour and visit the open elephant safari where they roam free.

Title: Spend at least 2-3 hours
Text: I loved every bit of this place. You need to spend at least 2-3 hours in this place and play with the elephants.

Title: Its easy to judge
Text: Having read some of the reviews on here I approached this visit with caution. But I was pleasantly surprised. Sure, it no longer operates as an orphanage but a controlled breeding zoo. That said, the elephants seemed well cared for and minimally managed by the mahouts. I never saw any being mistreated. Yes some are temporarily chained for the safety of the herd and human safety. So long as they control the matriarch and/or bull the rest will generally follow. Its easy to judge but the govt agency has a big elephant population to manage throughout the country with very little funding, all in various states, wild & working, and in different relationships with humans.

Title: Amazing experience with kids
Text:
The orphanage is located in Pinnawala town, near Kandy. It took us by car 2:30 hrs.
The orphanage is huge and you can see loads of elephants in land being look after eating and walking. Then you can go to see them bath along the river and is just wonderful. Breath taking to be in contact with these huge animals, kids can come close to them touch them and help to bath them a life time experience.

Title: Perfect view
Text: It was really nice to visit this place as we love elephants. Time of bathing and feeding was nice. But of course it is not good to see the bad behavior to them . I heard a lot of bad thing about this place but i did not see something bad.

Title: Wonderful Experience
Text: Wonderful experience. I fed the elephants which costs 250 rupees a plate of fruit pieces. Entrance ticket about 800 if SAARC country and 750 to wash the elephant. But worth it. Up close to see and touch n feed the animal! Loved it.

Title: A Wonderful Excursion
Text:
Watching these beautiful animals enjoying the river and then walking up the shopping street back to their home is just a lovely experience. The orphanage is a fantastic achievement supporting these orphans - now of all ages. 
You have the chance to feed them as well and we would certainly recommend that you do not miss this on your travels.

Title: Nice to be withnthenelefant, but to expensive
Text:
There was promissed also a visit at the river with the elefants, but they wont do that after paying
Overall to shot, to expansive and agreemsts, they dont care

Title: They really take care of Elephants
Text:
This place was first in our itinerary in a 10 day Sri Lanka tour and were very happy to see how the Elephants are treated. We were on time to witness the elephant bathing session on river close to main entrance gate. I mean accross the road. Local seller sell food stuff to be fed to elephants and it was really great experience. There are more than 40 elephants taken care at this place and whatever I saw I felt they are really taken care by staff.
If you have time you can also plan to give bath to elephant at extra charges.
Do visit elephant poo paper factory to experience the making if paper from poo.
Overall a great experience

Title: Elephant welfare residence
Text: Visited here on 19th Jan,2019. This orphanage established by the Sri Lanka Department of Wildlife Conservation is home to around 80 elephants. They have fruit feeding activities.The elephants bathe and frolic in the Maha Oya stream. Plenty of British tourists sitting in the viewing areas of the restaurants here. The road near the entrance also has plenty of elephant themed souvenirs from t-shirts & paintings to magnets and puzzle piece toys for kids.

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage Visit
Text: It was a great experience to watch the elephants bathe in the river, though some of the larger elephants have been chained. The orphanage does display a board stating why they chain the elephants - as measure of precaution to the public due to the size of the animals and other reasons. I was not entirely convinced mainly because the handlers had sharp objects which they use to direct the elephants. The place is great to visit and the local shops produce paper using elephant dung which was quite intriguing.  You can also bathe the elephants for an additional cost. The shops have great souvenirs.

Title: Only for one time
Text: It was a good experience at Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage. Because it is on the way to Kandy it can be visited else coming from Colombo or any other place specially for this is not the worth.

Title: Different to expectations
Text:
It is easy to judge and come to conclusions, yes on our visit there were a few elephants feeding and loose but the majority were chained for some reason and some were pacing and looked stressed. But we have to wonder what would happen to these magnificent beasts if they had not been rescued and left too fend for themselves.
We did see some of them in the river walking freely.
Before we went we did expext the elephants to be free and not chained, it would have been a good idea if we had been given the reasons as to why they were chained.

Title: Elephants appearing to enjoy life
Text:
The orphanage is great and the vast majority of the Elephants appear to be enjoying life.

They have various areas and pens and so some are chanied. But without knowing why, you cannot really judge on it being cruel, given that so many are roaming free.

If you go mid morning around 1030 or at 1430 in the afternoon you can see the elephants walked down to the river to bathe. It really is a beautiful sight and they appear to be thoroughly enjoying themselves.

We enjoyed our visit and these elephants appear happy.

Unlike the elephant tourist spots before or after Pinnawala which offer close ups and rides with the elephants. They are nothing but a rip off and it's distressing to see the elephants. We did stop off at the advice of our guide and wish we hadn't. A complete rip off. 

DO - Visit Pinnawala Elephant Orphange 

DONT - Visit any other tourist elephant spot before or after

Title: Conservation at its Best.
Text:
It's not often that we get to see wild animals close up - least of all endangered  species  like the Asian elephant. But to see 75 of them in one place is incredibly privileged. 
This is the largest herd of Asian elephants in the world today in controlled ,protected surroundings.
The orphanage  has been running since 1975 and the work it is doing is helping  to keep the species alive and all monies raised goes towards the continued  work of looking after these magnificent beasts.
A MUST SER. Very highly recommended.

Title: Mixed feelings
Text: The actual sanctuary area is a bit of a letdown, not much to see, Elephants are semi wild and are orphaned or injured. Guests can watch the elephants bathing and playing in the nearby river and can also feed elephants if they are there at certain times.  This is a great opportunity to see elephants up close in an open, relaxed and somewhat natural environment.

Title: Commercialised venture - heartbreaking.
Text: I have been to an elephant sanctuary in Thailand a couple of years ago this was an exact opposite of that. I have seen elephants on the roads of Jaipur  treated with love too. This was drenched in economic greed and maximizing profit irrespective of the mental health of the elephants. No matter what they say about the chains around their feet it's wrong and enslaving. The handlers very-very rough. It was heart breaking to see

Title: Disappointing and utter neglect of animal welfare
Text:
Apart from providing photo opportunities, this place is best forgotten. Firstly, if the exorbitant entry fees were put to good use, there would be improvement in the animal welfare. More to the point, the so called mahouts could be provided with some training and the two pronged metal implement confiscated. Pronging these majestic creatures  is utterly cruel and there are places overseas, where the metal prong has been discarded.
When the animals are taken across back to their glorified cage, often a 'senior' mahout and an elephant lag behind providing close photo and feeding opportunities---at a cost of course

Title: Very nice experience
Text:
Whilst I am not a fan of animals being kept in captivity I was very pleasantly surprised by my visit.
We were fortunate as the elephants were "bathing" in the fast flowing river, and it was amazing to see them frolic in the water. Thereafter we followed the elephants back to the enclosed arena.

Definitely worth visiting

NB -- there is a very big difference in the fee entrance for locals and foreigners

Title: Rethink this as a venue please
Text: I was hoping that this would be a happy place but instead I left feeling very, very disappointed. One entry price for locals and an over-inflated price for foreign tourists, and I struggled to find anywhere which showed rehabilitation in action for these magnificent creatures. Elephants get a trip to the river (when tides allow) and this is what appears in the site photos, however this is misleading, and the actual reserve is bleak. I would not go there again and would encourage others to do the same. Elephants were heavily chained and there is little to stimulate them here, and many seemed anxious and distressed. We left (my wife in tears) after 15 minutes.

Title: good chance to see elephants up close
Text: a really good gesture to set up an orphanage to rescue the orphan elephants. chance to see the elephants up close, u can get to feed the elephants too.

Title: 2 Weeks Volunteering
Text:
Spent 2 weeks volunteering here as a family so gained some insight into the orphanage.
The orphanage would love to see all elephants in the wild, unfortunately this is impossible with pressures on land use by a growing population.  They cant introduce elephants to an existing wild herd as they would not be accepted.  All elephants in the orphanage have been raised in captivity so would seek out people if released and this would in turn create conflict risking the elephants life.
The mahouts do shout and use ashoks with elephants to ensure public safety.  To see behind the public face and watch them tenderly go over the elephants skin for 2 hours looking for problems shows their true feelings towards the animals.  They shout at the cleaners if the elephant houses are not sufficiently cleaned.
The prices are fair for tourists and cheaper for locals to encourage locals to visit, learn and take an interest in their own wildlife.  This is a government run organisation so the prices are set in Colombo, not by the orphanage.  The extra fee for feeding or bathing 
elephants is likewise set by the politicians.
The Elephant in the Room - chains.  These are necessary to manage the herd in a small area to keep public, staff and elephants safe.  Injured, sick and pregnant elephants are kept separate, but still taken for free time at the river away from the main herd. There are 19 elephants housed here which have been seized from illegal owners and are awaiting court cases so can't be put with the herd.  
In all we really enjoyed our 2 weeks here giving us an insight not gained during a short visit.  Volunteering is hard work and not for everybody.  We learnt about the politics behind a lot of decisions and saw the love held for these wonderful creatures by all the staff at the orphanage.

Title: Do not go!!!
Text:
I wish I had done my research before going to the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage because it was honestly more like a prison than an orphanage. The second we got there we were bombarded by a man who said after we see the elephants eat we need to get in a tuk tuk to see the elephants bathe and then go to the spice factory. You do not have to do this! All you need to do is cross the street to see the elephants bathe. 

Now back to this horrible place.... once we entered everything just seemed like an amusement park. It seems this place is more for making money than helping animals. Most of the animals were chained up not able to roam free. There was also an area for I guess the elephants that could not be with the rest of the population and they were chained in an area that was dark and smellyand they were weaving back and forth. This is a sign of distress which many of the elephants exhibited. Once it was time for the elephants to bathe in the water they walked them down in chains while the handlers prodded them with their bull hooks. I was shocked to see how aggressive they were with the elephants. If the wanted the elephant to move or stand a certain way they would hit it with a wooden stick then take the hook part and stab the head of the elephants. You could see when the handlers came around the elephants were scared. I also saw them prodding elephants to pick things up and move them. They were using them for work abs using the hooks to get them to do what they wanted. 

It was an extremely sad and disturbing place. If you love animals do not give your money and support this torturous place. This is just a place to exploit elephants and make money. I have to give 1 star to post this but it would have been 0 stars.

Title: Horrible place. Pinnawala is a glorified zoo - or worse
Text:
I had read up about Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage before I visited Sri Lanka and from what I'd read, I was honestly considering skipping the visit due to claims of animal abuse and unnecessary confinement. But as it turned out, I was part of a group and because the group wanted to go, I had little option but to tag along.

What I saw there truly horrified me.

1. Elephant calves were confined in a circular pen and their legs tied with metal chains that left little room for manoeuvre or free movement.

2. There was a tusker displaying a classic case of depressive symptoms - head swaying incessantly and bobbing up and down. Like the calves, he was also tied with a short metal chain in a small shed. 

3. A herd of elephants we saw there was so scared of the keeper that as soon as he entered the enclosure with his bull-hook, the terrified elephants literally fled away from him. The keeper was careful not to display any aggressive behaviour in front of the tourists but it was obvious from how scared the elephants were, that terrible things go on behind the scenes. 

4. While there, we saw a keeper repeatedly strike a pregnant elephant with a huge pole that had a metal spike at its end. He poked and struck her hard despite the presence of tourists there. I cannot imagine what must be going on once tourist hours are over.

We then headed off to the river adjacent to the orphanage where they take the elephants for a bath - hoping that at least there, the elephants must be free. But they were not. Even here, the elephants were tied with short chains while tourists threw fruit at them.

I would've compared Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage to a zoo but most zoos treat their animals better than this 'orphanage' does.

Pinnawala is not a place I would ever visit again. My money isn't going into a place that has made a business out of abusing animals that should've been returned to the wild. Plus, they breed elephants in confinement at Pinnawala. Real orphanages don't typically do that.

Instead, I would strongly recommend visiting the Elephant Transit Home near Udawalawe National Park. I haven't been there but from what I've heard, they are much more responsible in caring for orphaned elephants. Plus they return the elephants to the wild once they are old enough - unlike Pinnawala.

Title: Elephants - up close!!!
Text: its such a wonderful experience - elephants real up close.  They amble along for their feed and patiently await for the keeper to come and feed them.  The elephants going for their bath is totally another level.  The keepers do warn tourists to keep out of their way, coz they are mostly semi wild with a few wild elephants. Once they get into the water, its such a pleasure to watch them enjoy their bath.  Its almost as if this is the high point in their life!  the huge pachyderms simply roll on to their sides and loll in the water, letting their keeper give them a good scrub!

Title: Awful experience - not a shelter - it's prison!
Text:
We expected more from an orphanage! This is not a shelter for elephants! This is cruelty zone prison!!
Animals are chained and beaten with long sticks with spikes! 
The worst part is that local people and tourist gides lie about how animals are sick or naughty so they have to be chained and beaten.
Also, when they bath them, most of them are chained as well. 
Due to human cruelty, number of animals in Sri Lanka has dropped from 15.000 to 3.000! And an orphanage is not a way to keep them safe! It's a way to earn money!

Title: Elephant jail
Text: We asked the rep before we booked  if any of the elephants are chained. He advised us one had been chained when it started attacking a baby elephant, they found out the elephant had tooth ache and once that was sorted it was as happy and released. He also said the keepers were sacked for poking the elephants with metal tipped rods. ALL UNTRUE. There are lots of chained elephants, clearly distressed as they rock from side to side. The keepers all carry large, metal tipped sticks. They are also chained when they go to the river. They all looked so miserable and sad.

Title: Disappointed about the treatment of the elephants
Text: I do recognize that different culture do have different way on how to treat animals. But we wouldnt recommend to any westerly tourist, to see this animals wearing chaines, which are even fixed being in the water. If you want to see wild elepfant go to other places. This is too commercial.

Title: Please dont support this place
Text:
This is NOT an ethical experience with elephants. Please spend your money on seeing happy elephants in the wild, rather than supporting places like this orphanage with your money.
The elephants are raised and kept for your entertainment, often chained to trees and coerced using bull hooks. If you care at all about elephants you wont go here.

Title: Not Disappointed mixed reviews
Text: I was again very dubious when visiting the orphanage after the reviews but we had a tour guide (not from the orphanage) and he said that the orphanage does well and helps elephants after they have been mistreated or some babies that were left abandoned in the national parks and who would definately not survive alone - the hooks are to stop them running off - and the ones we saw in river bathing looked exceptionally content - we also saw them feeding and they looked content - true you do get to see herds in the National parks but you do not get so up close and personal as the orphanage, i guess the chains are for our protection as well remember these are wild animals.. i know if they were mistreated our tour guide (who we had for over 2 weeks with us would have told us) the workers caring for the elephants seemed to have a good relationship with the elephant - just be prepared if you want a photo you will need to tip them.

Title: Dissappointed...
Text:
Pinnawala has the largest herd of captive elephants in the world. Actually one need not buy tickets to the orphanage at all. Its a waste of money to look at captive the elephants. Just visit any Hotel on Pinnalanda road or riverside Restaurant during early morning hours and watch herd or parade of Elephants walk down the road towards the river for a bath.

Sad that most of them are chained and controlled with bull hooks by mahouts. 

Elephants are safe to be near with, they could be fed and photos taken along.

Title: Once in a lifetime experience
Text:
I was dubious about this tour seeing some of the reviews. We did question why a few of the elephants were in chains which was rather distressing but we read that they are the males and were under medication as many of the elephants come from farmland where theyve been trapped in holes dug by farmers to collect water. They often have broken limbs when they come to the sanctuary. 
Once recovered, most are returned to the forests. Some pictures attached of the time we watched them bathing. The elephants are taken to the river twice a day and seem to enjoy their swim. For us, it was worth the journey. We werent interested in feeding them but more to watch them enjoy their swim.

Title: Very Disappointed that I went
Text: I heard reviews for both good and bad and I am so mad at myself for going. Half the elephants are on very small chains not allowing them to move around at all. I witness two being forced to sit in the water with bull hooks. They are never released back into the wild. While yes, they could be in worse situations do a yourself a favor and go see them in the wild during a safari. They are wild everywhere in Sri Lanka. Don't waste your time seeing somewhere where they aren't truly happy.

Title: Seems perfect home for elephant
Text: As I touring Srilanka and I am not aware of this place someone told me visit here, but being an Indian elephant is nothing new for me as we have been raised around animal like elephant so nothing new but particular here is, its a orphanage and i don't know is it required to keep them here anyway all seems prefect like elephant having quality time having food taking bath in river and may be raised here till death. But unless until not required elephant like animals should be left away from humans in jungles until being rescued from poacher or hunters. Wild animal are a thing of display there are being like human and should be left with their privacy

Title: DON'T GO!!! IT IS NOT AN ORPHANAGE!
Text: I was soo dissapointed, I was crying...they don't treat them good! It is not an orphanage! They force them to stay in the river, if they want to go out they beat them with the stick, and they are crying...turist trap

Title: Dont go here
Text: Animal abuse :( Do not go here if you like elephants! They deserve a free life, not being chained or beaten by humans.

Title: GOOD EXPERIENCE
Text: On the way from kandy to colombo this is an orphanage for elephants .One can see their bathing,feeding and other activities.the restaurent is a good spot to have lunch and see elephants from there bathing in river.

Title: Amazing place for kids and adults too
Text: We visited Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage in January 2019 and were mesmerized by the view. Scores of elephants roaming around you. You can feed the elphants, see them bathing in the river and learn a lot about them. A must visit place if you are in Sri Lanka

Title: Leaves a bad taste in the mouth
Text: We visited the Orphanage today hoping for lots to see, learn and feed the elephants.......you can do this visit in about 15-20mins. All the while seeing elephants chained up, looking stressed and swaying back and forth. It was actually distressing seeing them like that. We then went to see them bathe in the river and they were chained up again!!! The elephants were all thin and ones ribs were protruding. These poor beautiful creatures-treated like criminals on day release from prison. No life for an elephant. It isnt an Orphanage but a money making tourist spot. Elephants are treated better in our zoos than here. ??

Title: Worth visiting
Text:
The actual sanctuary area is a bit of a let down,  not much to see,  we were out within 15 mins.  The walk down to the river was easy, the road is lined with shops,  including elephant poo paper shops (the first one you encounter is much cheaper than the other one). 

We got to the river and went into the cafe on the left,  got a front view table and ordered a couple of drinks.
