It is great seeing the elephants walk through town and into the river.  We sat and watched them for over an hour.  Did not see any mistreatment at all.  

I would recommend going.

Title: Elephants galore
Text: The elephant orphanage is a place which kids would encounter lots of elephants. Since there were no baby elephants we could not see any milk feeding. There were numerous elephants which were being taken for bathing. We could see them frolick on the river bank. The kids enjoyed it thoroughly.

Title: See elephants up and close
Text:
The orphanage has three broad time slots: milk feeding to calves, fruit feeding to elephants, elephant bathing, so you should try to plan your arrival at beginning of one of these (picture has details, zoom in). You will be shuffling between hold area for feeding and river for bathing. One ticket (Rs. 700 SAARC country, Rs. 2500 for other countries, 50% for children) gets you multiple access to all events. You can easily spend 2-3 hours here watching elephants eat, play, relax, dance, and what not. They even have huge hose spraying elephants in the river, though we expected more frolicking in water it was still good experience. There are various souvenir shops and elephant poo paper shops around, and few mid-range restaurants.

Story behind orphanage is that it takes care of abandoned calves and tends them to youth, though for tourist purposes you can consider it open zoo. There is also separate zoo nearby and you can also take elephant ride.

Lot of negative reviews are from people who are aghast seeing animals in chains. It's not a jungle safari, and (some) elephants are in chains (some of the time). Go for watching elephants doing various things, as extended version of zoo. Don't go thinking it's natural habitat. It's always ironically funny to see bleeding heart of meat eaters for animal cruelity.

Title: A visit to Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
Text: Visited this place when we were on holiday tour to Srilanka. First time we had a chance to ride on an elephant and enjoyed a lot but it was scary. Also saw the bathing process of Elephants. It has a small museum also regarding elephants. It's a nice place to visit for all ages.

Title: Tourist trap. Not what the photos promise
Text: I would describe this place as a Tourist trap. The experience is not what the photos promise it to be. You can see the elephants walking to and from the river, and bathe. Getting close is not really whats on offer, apart from the occasional elephant coming close with its trunk, looking for food. All for the princely sum of Rs. 3000. (Approx £16) per person. We did get the chance to feed one elephant from the terrace of a hotel when a keeper asked us to come with him. Of course then demanding a rather generous tip for himself and his colleagues.....

Title: This is an awesome place to visit!
Text: This is an awesome place to visit! We are constantly surrounded by cute baby elephants and sumptuous older elephants! It's such an amazing experience to be that close to them! I recommend everyone to visit the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage!

Title: Nice place but missing activities
Text: I was on a family vacation and all tour operators recommended it. While it proved to be very spacious, lots of elephants but it missed key activities like elephant rides, and guests really engaging in feeding and bathing the elephants. Ended up going to a private elephant raising nearby place to give the children the true experience they wanted. I specifically would like to mention that I was impressed with the cleaness of the toilets. For such a public place, job well done.

Title: Hated seeing the elephants in chains
Text:
It's supposed to be an orphanage but very quickly you can see it's a tourist trap and money making business. 
As soon as you pay your ticket you'll find the guides encouraging to feed the elephants cucumber or take a picture with them and soon as thats done. they'll demand 500 rupees. 
Also not all elephants look happy most of them have chains and look stressed.
Do yourself a favour and visit the eco parks or the safaris instead where you can see these majestic creatures in their natural habitat

Title: Good place to see elephants
Text:
We went and saw the elephants bathing. They were bringing them back from there as well.  But other than that, there isn't much to see here. 
The elephants are chained but look well looked after. Prices to get in for foreigners are extremely high so you would be better off just watching them from the non-paying points or the hotel on top where you get to see the same things.

Title: Elephants are all chained up
Text: The elephants look stressed as they are pacing back and forth ( as far as they can go) as they are chained at the feet; Both front and back feet, which leaves them very little room to move. See photo. The entire atmosphere was a negative experience, and my family and group were very heart sick about the way these animals are treated. We did visit other elephant sanctuaries in the area, and found them to be more appealing and the animals are free range. Also, you can visit at another location, how they make elephant poop paper ( n/c), and see the entire process Pinnawala has the name, but NOT the proper treatment of animals.

Title: Elephants place ... but is it HOME???
Text:
I'm not sure about this place, generally speaking it's very nice place and seen a lot lovely elephants, those animals are beautiful and amazing, watched baby-teenagers elephants playing, and feeding time. Seen some elephants - males chained as it was heating season so they are dangerous because of the dose of hormones- it was sad picture, even if you understand the reason for it. Place kept in very good condition.
I didn't like the way some staff was treating elephants with sharp tool and pooling them over to  tourists so they could take a pictures and they were speaking very quietly about "making donations ".

Title: Great morning with elephants
Text: A good way to break the journey between Colombo and Kandy... elephants were in a natural setting and appeared to be well looked after and enjoying themselves in the river etc .... kids and adults loved it .. only need 45 mins before heading on

Title: Not a lot to see
Text: Love elephants but these creatures look tired. We wanted to see a lot of animals but had to pay high admission price to see a herd far away. Not a lot to do or see once there. We spent maybe 20 minutes to see herd and then walk back to car. Some elephants were chained up and we were told they were violent. The elephants go to nearby river and bath and cross the road around 930am. Do that instead and save admission costs.

Title: I am glad we went
Text:
Both my partner and I are animal lovers, and we deliberated long and hard whether to visit here due to some of the Trip Advisor reviews. However, after doing more research and reading some independant travel articles, we decided to visit - and I am glad we did. 

Yes, there are chains used to anchor, help control and keep the elephants safe as well as the many visitors this place has. In addition, the males - especially when in musth - need to be controlled and seperated. These elephants can never be released in to the wild, so ensuring they can not wander off when in the river is essential. I did not see any evidence of distress, and I saw some lovely interactions in the main herd with some of the younger ones playing. They genuinely seemed to enjoy their time in the river, and seeing them walk through the main street was an experience! 

This place is not perfect - however people also need to remember this is a poor country. It seems to me like they try and do the best they can with the money that is available. The only thing that stood out to me is that the Mahouts seemed to over use their hooks and shout when it did not seem necessary. This could be my ignorance of course, but it seemed over the top at times like they were showing off to the crowds.

Title: Such a great place to visit.
Text: To me, the main attraction of the orphanage is the elephant's bath time! It is amazing to watch, and my wife loved it! I have never seen anything like that before,but it was quite fun. Such a great place to visit.

Title: Having a better understanding of the Sri Lankan culture.
Text: In Sri Lanka, elephants are a big part of their culture and are considered symbolic animals. Maybe that is why it is so important for them to create a place dedicated to taking care of orphaned elephants. I would definitely enjoy seeing those majestic animals and having a better understanding of the Sri Lankan culture.

Title: Lets save the Elephants
Text: Beautiful day touring the elephant orphanage at Pinnawala in Sri Lanka. Watching and learning about elephants in a natural environment was a great learning experience for all the family. Our driver Hetti from Jet wings was a really safe driver and great tour guide for us. We loved spending some time watching the elephants. About 2 1/2 hour drive from Colombo and well worth the time and drive.

Title: A must-do
Text: Having heard so much about the place, we had to stop here on the drive to Nuwara Eliya and we were not disappointed. Seeing the elephants make their way down the street to the river to bathe was interesting and we loved to see their antics in the water. Some naughty ones kept coming up the banks to be fed until they saw their mahouts and scampered back into the water like naughty children. Glad we visited.

Title: Elephant orphanage
Text: It was fun for the kids to watch all the small elephants get feed. It was about 40 elephants. After the feesing we went into the information senter and got some information about the elephants and the orphanage. It seamed like the elephants was well taken care off, and a visit here seemed like a good way to support the orphanage.

Title: Not to expect as publised
Text:
I dont even handle an orphan baby like this.
Elephants are most brainy animals in this world and when you see elephant babies with their herd, you can figure out how they are protected by other elephants.

The initiative is very good by the government, but commercialising this Is not a fair approach to that baby elephants. Animal lovers especially those study about elephants and its emotions will understand this.

The elephants are not treated as babies or orphans. They are mainly managed to attract the tourist who visit that place. Locals who belongs to this place, including the management and staff should at least show the attitude of their loving approach to elephants.

As a human if you have never seen elephants closely or interacted with baby elephants, you may find this place interesting. 
We have lived in a culture (Southern most part of India) which is very much similar to Lanka, with elephants on day to day life. In timber depot, temple festivals, local rich guys house, but baby one is always attraction for us.

We arrived around 1030 by the time the Babies were at the river playing, some were afraid of the crowd being gathered, some are weak to even taking bath/ play.

We also saw while they were taking back to the so called orphanage from river.

Pros:- you can see herds of babies in one go.

Cons:- you wont see the feel of orphan baby elephant being well treated.
More of a commercial establishment to sell substances, gift items with elephant name or photo somewhere.

But a place one should visit at least once, best time is while they were going to river, taking bath and coming back. Timings are displayed and published in their web page.

Avoid buying souvenirs from their, as the prices are sky-rocketed for tourists. You will find same items in cheaper rates outside.

Title: Mixed emotions
Text:
I've got very mixed feelings about pinnawala. 
On the one hand - beautiful to see so many elephants together in safety. Some reviewers have stated that ALL the elephants are in chains - they are not. The information boards clearly explain that the male elephants are chained when in the public areas for the safety of everyone around them. 

However, I did see an area with two baby elephants who were chained front and back, unsupervised, surrounded by noisy tourists. I didn't stay long to see this, it was too upsetting.

Things that bothered me were - what happens to the adult male elephants? Where do they go? Are the elephants ever released back into the wild?

Regardless, this is a beautiful place, surrounded by hills, with the most elephants you're ever likely to see in one place.

Title: Truely Awful
Text:
Ive seen elephants in many different places. On safari in a reserve in Africa, in the wild in Borneo, in captivity in London Zoo. Ive never seen such hostility from keepers or such fear from animals. 

Elephants like to hold each others tails. I watched one try desperately to reach the tail of the next elephant but he couldnt because he was chained up. Eventually he held his own tail.

The keepers hit them with sticks and shout at them. The elephants just stand there. They dont try to play or bathe. They appear to scared to move.

It is definitely not an elephant orphanage as Ive not seen any baby elephants. I dont think the owners have any intention of trying to get the elephants back to the wild as they can make so much money out of them.

This is a money making scam and if Id known what it was going to be like I would never have come. .

Title: Disappointed
Text: Very short time to go and actually see things there. Or to actually see the life of elephants there. They bring them for bath in the river and take them away. That's all to see by paying a price.

Title: Chains, whips and riding
Text:
Lies. This whole place. They do not care about elephants welfare nor do the ignorant hordes of tourists clambering for a picture.
Yes the elephants have a large river for bathing. Yes the animals have a large expanse to roam. But the animals are chained and I witnessed one elephant being rode by a keeper, with a chain round it's neck and being prodded and whipped.
Stop the abuse.

Title: Tourist trap not an orphanage
Text:
Elephants on show for the tourist. If you want to see elephants close up you wont be disappointed. Just accept they will not be happy elephants because they are regularly chained up and made tame by the use of a sharpe pointed stick. 
There are so many better places in the world to see elephants that are not chained up or abused. This is not really an orphanage it is just a business.

Title: Captive & captivating elephants!...
Text:
There are clearly divided opinions about places such as these. The elephants here are either orphan elephants, those born in captivity or ex-working elephants in retirement. They are cared for at the orphanage their whole lives and are not planned for release back into the wild,  as they probably would not survive  by themselves, having become accustomed to human handling. We saw them taken to the river for their daily bathing,  and clearly they enjoyed the experience, playing and splashing around with each other (and even trying to mate!) in the water for several hours.. 
Some in our group objected to the chains the elephants wear and the actions of the mahouts prodding them to move. We learned later (contrary to appearances) the elephants are not chained up back in the orphanage - they only have the chains on for use in an emergency and for public protection if they get spooked. 
But as one commentator has already said, if you want to see elephants in a free and natural environment, visit one of the many national parks -  not the orphanage, or a sanctuary.

Title: Place of Elephant Lovers
Text: A beautiful and rare place for elephant-lovers. An awesome sight of seeing 70 plus elephants at one place. At the time of my visit to the orphanage with my wife, it was bathing time for them. Around 35 elephants were give bath in a flowing river followed by the royal walk of parading elephants one by one. An important destination in Sri Lanka. Entry fee of SLR 2500 for foreigners and SLR 700 for the visitors of SAARC countries is charged. A memorable visit indeed.

Title: DO NOT GO HERE - especially if you love elephants
Text:
Before our trip to Sri Lanka I did a lot of research online into Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage. There are lots of contrasting opinions online so in the end we decided to visit.

I regret going here and giving this company my money. The elephants are not well looked after, they are paraded around like zoo animals, and patrolled with bull hooks and chains and it is a massive money making exercise. The elephants here are not happy, and there is no program to release the orphans back into the wild.

I came away feeling really sad and sorry for the elephants at this place.

If you are thinking about visiting - please do not! Instead save your money and go on a safari at Minneriya national park, where you will see hundreds of happy elephants in their natural habitat.

Title: Terrible.how on earth the lovely
Text: People of Sri Lanka can advertise this as an elephant orphanage is a complete joke.It is just an excuse to print money. Most of the adult elephants were chained and appeared to be in distress. The elephant s were confined to a small area and the emphasis was on giving money to feed them or if one was available to give milk to a baby elephant. However because they didn't have a baby elephant they were looking to import one from a zoo. So much for an orphanage.

Title: Elephants close up
Text: The elephants were a delight and watching them splash around in the river was amazing.  3 hours from Colombo with interesting road sights and villages along the way

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
A group of us went here on an organised tour and unfortunately it was rather a disappointment. The elephants were actually quite nice to see but we were herded through in less than half an hour to make room for the next tour group. Also we didn't get to see the elephants go to the river as this was cancelled because the river was too deep due to the recent rains.
Worth a visit, but not in a group.

Title: Mixed feelings
Text:
I think its a must visit if youre with kids.
During elephant feeding you can see the elephants from a very close distance.
Elephant Bathing is good to watch. You can notice the elephants playing with each other.
Yes they keep few elephants chained, but they have also mentioned the reasons for chaining them.

Title: Elephant protection
Text: It is good to see most elephants are happy :). It is not the money machine as reviewed by other people. The elephants are well cared. All the staffs are nice and friendly. The chain on the male elephant is only a protection to tourist. One only need to pay 1 pound to have a chance to feed them with melon.

Title: Elephants seemed treated ok
Text:
We got there at bath time. Elephants seemed to enjoy being in the river. They were given reasonable room to roam, a 30m x 10m section of river. A few wandered past the handlers to forage on the far side of the river ... it seemed that they could have made a dash for freedom into the forests, but they didn't.
Of herd of 30, only 2 or 3 had chains. Handlers had hooked poles but although they were waved around, I did not see any physical abuse or contact.
We enjoyed seeing them close up and being relatively free in the river.
These are not wild elephants.
Not sure what happens at other times or the conditions in which they are kept. Would be sad if they were not treated well then.
Although we sat on the hotel balcony, there was no pressure on us to buy drinks etc.

Title: A very commercial experience
Text: Certainly one of the most avoidable experiences.. the elephants are all chained up and seem pretty afraid. There is a place inside where you can feed fruits to the elephants, provided you pay money (and can also pose with the elephant). Those tourists who decided to pose without paying for the fruits were rudely told to stop clicking photos.. later our driver took us to the hotel where the elephants come close by to bathe. Some elephants who were afraid of getting into the water were whipped so they would enter the water. Again, here, when some tourists decided to touch the elephants trunks, the mahouts immediately helped them click pics and asked for money. It is a money making business for the mahouts rather than being an orphanage.. avoid at all costs!

Title: Totally commercialised
Text: I had been here 15 years ago, so had some idea of what to expect, but still went in two minds about whether it was worthy or not. The development has been enormous, with two hotels now overlooking the bathing area, and a street lined with proper shops. No doubting where the focus is. It's still tempting to go to see the elephants close up, and their handlers will happily take photos of you with an elephant (and then expect 1000 rupees +), but the pictures are kind of spoiled by all the chains..................

Title: Sad truth
Text: So we visited the orphanage during our honeymoon Sri Lanka tour. We knew what to expect and our guide confirmed it. It has nothing to do with an orphanage. It is a pure tourist money making machine. The animals live on a fenced area with no shade to hide from the sun and no water place. A bunch of them are chained, for the safety of the tourists. Having visited previously elephants in one of the national parks, where they live freely and feed from the jungle, it is a very sad image to see the orphanage. If you are looking for a nature friendly experience, rather visit one of the national parks instead of the orphanage.

Title: Elephant  orphanage in Kandy  colombo
Text: This is a government run  orphanage for abandoned  elephants .Every day  two times they take the elephants for bathing down to a nearby river. We saw lot of elephants  of all ages walking around the park  and they are under strict control of their mahouts. We saw some cute small naughty  baby elephants also.

Title: Confusing experience
Text: When the local driver brought us here and recommended this place, it seemed to be ok at first when they feeded the elephants. But very soon after that we noticed some elephants being captured with a chain around their ankle and the animals seemed to be very stressed out. People were just trying to make money with these poor animals taking photos etc.

Title: Amazing place
Text: We stopped here on the way to Kandy and one of the highlights of our 7 days journey in Sri Lanka. We witnessed feeding milk to baby elephant and large group of elephant taken a good care.

Title: Highlight of the trip
Text: A real highlight to watch these majestic animals playing in & enjoying the water. Definitely worth the effort to get here by 10am

Title: Up close and personal
Text: When we arrived the elephants were down the road from the orphanage in the river so we went there first and it was awesome to see 30 or 40 of these magnificent creatures bathing. They were then led back to the orphanage where there is plenty of opportunity to see them up close. They appear to be well treated and not used for rides like other places

Title: Fantastic
Text: Here you get up close and personal with the elephants - an unforgettable once in a lifetime experience. You can see the feeding and touch and stroke them. Unfortinately there was heavy rain in the night so no river bathing and there are no babies to be fed right now (Nov.18). We combined this with a visit to the nearby Milennium Elephant Foundation project which made for the best day of our holiday.

Title: A place not to be missed
Text: Just go and have your own thoughts as Im overwhelmed by the closeness of these lovely animals. Sixty odd including elephant families roam free over many acres and know when to appear for food. Twice a day they take the for a walk to the local river . Its was brilliant to watch these enormous animals swimming, playing in this fast flowing river....great memory....

Title: A great way to support this herd
Text:
There are a lot of misleading reviews about Pinnawala. I've been twice - earlier this month and 21 years ago - and I've enjoyed the experience both times. The price of 2500 rupees (about £11 per person) is quite high but much lower than I've seen online where it's often stated at $20 per person.

There's not too much to do. Our driver went in with us which we thought a bit odd until we realised he knew exactly where to go and when to make sure we got the best experience. We went first to the elephant 'paddocks' where the ladies were hanging around eating and waiting for bath time. In a separate area, the boys were getting ready to go the river.

Nothing can really prepare you for seeing a massive herd of elephants on the move. The boys went first, strolling through the orphanage, out to the road and down to the river. Some are chained - for their safety and everybody else's. I don't think it's a bad thing. Once the boys were on their way, the lady elephants followed.

We watched the bath time for nearly 2 hours. Our driver urged us to a brilliant watching space in a cafe which we really appreciated. In two hours you have plenty of time to watch and observe the different personalities amongst the elephants. There are the cheeky younger boys, the stubborn old ladies, the frisky and the laid-back all hanging out together.

People have commented on the use of 'spikes' or 'guides'. We was the metal guides being used by the mahoots but always very gently and never with any violence. The love of the handlers for their pachyderm pals was clear to all.

One old lady - quite possibly the grande dame of the herd - spent an hour standing knee deep trying to avoid a wash. Her mahoot gently urged her into deeper water, taking his time and using his 'guide' to help scrape old mud off her head and back. Eventually she gave in and rolled over in the water to let him clean her properly.

Some are chained in the water but didn't seem distressed about it. A couple of young females made a jovial bid for freedom on the far banks and were laughingly chased down and returned to the herd.

If you're looking for lots of action, this may disappoint. If you have the patience to watch and wait, you'll probably love it as much as I did.

One comment. I think the management should consider rebranding this as an Elephant Home rather than an Elephant Orphanage since it seems to create elevated expectations of lots of babies and at present there really aren't many at all. The purpose of the home is to give safe haven to elephants, not to go looking for unwanted babies. Back in the days of the Civil War, a lot of babies were orphaned by their parents being killed (accidentally or intentionally) so there were more little ones to see. These days they do have a few babies but I suspect that's more an outcome of boy and girl elephants getting friendly rather than any kind of captive breeding programme.

Title: HMMMM Not sure
Text: Nice to see the elephants in the river but not so nice to see them walking with chains on and being poked with spiked sticks.

Title: Gutted
Text: Had been looking forward to seeing the elephants but on the day we went there was no bathing as the river was too high which is fair enough but there was no feeding either for reasons we couldnt find out. However both these issues paled into insignificance once we saw how the elephants were being kept. A significant number were chained by one and in some cases two ankles and two of the elephants were clearly in distress swaying from side to side. We left feeling very sorry for the elephants and wishing we hadnt gone

Title: Loved it
Text: We came her for a few hours, watching them and feeding them was fantastic.  They just love being around people yes for the treats. You need to see them its a big must.

Title: Ticket entrance paid and scam artists around
Text:
Read reviews before coming here and also heard from a friend who has volunteered here in the past.

The ticket fee of 2500rupees was apparently to feed, see and opportunity to bathe the elephants. 

Not the case. 
Some Elephants are chained in the water..
However most are Free roaming around which is great to see! 

The staff did not explain anything and no such thing as a refund. 

Beware of scam artists around trying to upsell by saying the ticket price is to only see the elephants in the water.

Title: Terrible place
Text:
if youve come to Sri Lanka looking to see beautiful happy elephants i suggest you dont come here and find a safari in one of the national parks. there are about 35 elephants at a time in the river here but also about 200+ people and hotels and restaurants on the riverside too. elephants are kept in close herds together and are absolutely petrified of the workers, but this is no surprise as they all carry large sticks with a sharp point on the end - which they use for what seemed like no reason. the sticks had a large metal point and hook at the end, the hook is used to drag the elephants around by their ears. 

i was expecting many happy elephants being helped by loving people and am absolutely gutted that i have given this place my money and come across this.

Title: Mixed feelings!
Text: I honestly have mixed feelings about Pinnawala Elephant orphanage but I want to believe they really love Elephants and that even when tourist are not around they would treat them properly. Elephants seemed a bit nervous but it was nice to have the possibility to feed them. Absolutely stunning watching them taking a bath into the river!

Title: Elephant orphanage
Text: Orphan baby elephants,old and sick elephants are housed here.They are everyday taken to a nearby river for bath.They are taken care of and fed with,milk,fruits and food.you would definitely love seeing them

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
Text:
After landing in Colombo, we headed to Kandy & this orphanage was the first stop en-route to Kandy. 
Visited with family & my 4 year Son enjoyed the elephants bathing in the river. It's fun to watch the elephant parade when all the roads are cleared of public - so the elephants can go back to the orphanage after bathing in the river. There is a restaurant overlooking the river & the entire lane has a lot of road shopping stuff in terms of clothes, souvenirs, etc. 
They have time slots reserved for the elephants to bathe, be fed, etc. One can pay & feed the elephants.

Title: Horrible and sad place
Text: Wanna pay a lot to see chained and suffering elephants? Go there! None of the other things you see here worth that horrible and sad sight...

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
Text:
We visited Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage again, the first time was 2007, certainly another highlight was According to our guide there are nearly 100 orphaned elephants here and we got to see them be playful with each other, walk through the sanctuary, saw them being fed milk (members of the public can do this but there is only a limited number of tickets available, if I recall rightly its only 30), What an unbelievable sight it is to see them walking down the street towards the river for their bathing (10-12 and 2-4).
They blow a siren warns of approaching elephants to signal that the elephants are on the way, you can stand within 2 feet or so of the procession. Once safe, make your way back to the rocks by the water. This is an excellent vantage point to enjoy the spectacle. when all merchants guided all tourists inside and took their merchandise inside as well. Then dozens of elephants marched through the 200m market street and some bags and t-shirts feel down to the ground as they had passed by so close to the shops including the poo shop. 
The keepers or mahouts also carry "guide sticks" to help direct the elephants to the bathing river etc. They never hit or hurt the elephants with these sticks, they just use them gently to guide them safely across the roads etc.  Then we positioned ourselves on the verandah of the Hotel, where to also had lunch overlooking the river & got a really good view of the Elephants being washed & playing in the water.

Title: Not value for money
Text: Has a collection of injured or orphaned elephants but the entry fee and charges for bathing, feeding and riding the elephants is very high and not worth it.

Title: Good time with giants
Text: It was really a good time spent with loveable giants. The awesomeness of place is it has river where these giants taking bath and playing with waters. You will love it when you see them. Another good experience is to feed them. I was lucky to feed these giants. Unfortunately limited days to feeb baby elephants, so i was not lucky to see them. Make sure you confirm the schedules for these guys. Go for it.. enjoy it.

Title: A mixed reaction
Text: It was very sad to see some of the elephants chained in solitary confinement. The reason that they are adults and may pose a threat to others at certain times does not seem a true statement. This as supposed to be an orphanage but it is clearly also a breeding program. We were told that the animals are never released into the wild, surely other species can be rehabilitated so that seemed so wrong. We went to see the animals bathing in the river and were disgusted to see a young elephant walked down the road heavily chained and tethered to a rock when in the water, It was clearly distressed and only settled when an older one was allowed near it. Many of the others were chained to rings embedded on the rocks. Most of them didn't seem too stressed by this but I suppose they don't know any other life.

Title: Visit to Sri Lanka
Text: I was so looking forward to seeing the elephants. At first it looks lovely when you get to the elephants, they are all in the river, but I started looking closely and noticed one elephant on his own at the back on his own, he looked very distressed swaying from side to side and chained down. I tried to ask questions but no one wanted to answer me! Then there was another one with the herd that was also chained down. The mahuttes have sticks with sharp ends on them, the elephants did not look relaxed I come away feeling very angry and upset. When you visit the orphanage across the road, there were 4 males chained down  in the park, this should not happen, again when you ask questions you get excuses, like they need to do this for safety reasons. I never got to see them feed or wash them that was at a different time, so I cannot comment. Not sure you should visit this park, there are lots of other parks where the elephants are wild, I I feel its for tourists, not sure I would call it an orphanage??

Title: Wild elephant was more worth seeing
Text:
Read a lot of extreme comments of this site beforehand. This place was highly recommended by the agent and was a midpoint from capital to Dambulla. 

We spent an hour here for a short walk with the elephant, feed with fruit, and watched it at bath in the river. Each elephant had an assigned caretaker to look after and as per the guide, the elephant would only be chained at night during sleep and no wounds or marks could be found at the elephant leg which caused by the chain. Literally there was no evident to prove if they treated the elephant in a proper manner or not in just an hour stay. 

To us, this spot could be omitted as we would visit Minneriya National Park seeing the wild elephant 2 days after this. Recommend to go for the wild elephant instead of seeing the caged.

Title: Excellent facilities
Text: Went to this orphanage couple of days back. Was a wonderful experience. There is a disclosure / notice board indicating why the elephants are chained. The animals are well maintained. You can also feed milk / fruits, subject to conditions that you have to buy the stuff at the location. Enjoyable. Overall its a good experience.

Title: Disappointed: Do not Recommend
Text: Many of the elephants were chained and appeared distressed. I am disappointed that the elephants are not being prepared to be returned to the wild. I do not recommend visiting this elephant tourist attraction.

Title: A nice outing...kids would love it!
Text: The orphanage is about 1 1/2 hrs from Kandy, it is definitely worth the visit especially if you have children because they would love it!

Title: Visited on a tour!
Text:
Great to see the elephants walk by on their way to the river and play together, the chains on some looked to be rubbing and cutting into the leg, its needed to control them but I would prefer they were not chained at all or not made to be a tourist attraction.
Im sure thatll upset some but their we are.

Title: An amazing place to visit and watch elephants in the river
Text: The place was really spacious and not crowded. We went for the 2pm river bath and the kids managed to feed the elephants fruits. The sight of the elephants walking down the road to the river was simply amazing and we spent an hour plus just watching them play in the river. There was some elephant we saw chained but we were told he was aggressive towards others..all in all the rest looked happy in their pack and the must see is the river bath time

Title: Best Animal Human Interaction
Text: The orphanage is ding a great service by taking care of those pachyderms needing external support. the bathing if elephants is a sight to behold and the opportunity to feed an elephant is too unique an experience. The centre is extremely well maintained and exceptionally customer friendly. A must experience in Sri Lanka

Title: Magnificent herd of elephants
Text:
This place is one of the most well known spots in Sri Lanka. Dont miss the elephants bathing in the lake - one of the key attractions here. Better to arrive early around 10 am - the elephants come back from bath by noon. After that u can even feed the elephants. One thing u cannot do here is ride elephants - that was little disappointing. For elephant ride u have to go outside to some privately maintained places and they rip u off.
If u r from SAARC nations u get discounted tickets - less than half than their European counterparts.

Title: So many elephants in one place kids love this
Text:
If u love elephants you will love the place as they have around 65 elephants which them .
With all ages from 10 years to 70 years.
Kids love this places.
You have to see the elephants from 10 feet distances and on a particular time you can feed the baby elephant from bottle by paying a charge of LKR 250/300
ENTRY FEE : 700 LKR / 2500 LKR
what i dont like about this place is they keep the elephants tied with iron chains.

Title: Day with Elephants
Text: I was told that this is the most visited tourist attraction in Sri Lanka so expect plenty of tourists and activity here. And as many have said, its not cheap. However if you wish to spend a day with elephants, i can't think of any better place than here. As for cleanliness, thats another story. But i guess you can't really expect much as there are many tourists and its a place where elephants are kept. I would say, yes, its a must see place for anyone visiting Sri Lanka.

Title: Cute elephants
Text: We stayed in Negombo and it was a 2 hour drive from our hotel to the elephant orphanage, along the way we visited the herbal garden and a tea factory. It was nice to see the elephants bathing in the river, the baby elephants feeding wasnt really worth it. You just see the caretaker fill a bottle with milk and then the elephant drinks it in less than 10 seconds! You cannot really pet the elephants, but they do have a feeding area, however by the time we got there the food finished. You dont get a one on one experience with the elephants as there are lots of tourists around. There are several shops around to buy souvenirs. I especially liked the shop that sold elephant poo paper they show you a quick demonstration of how its made. Very interesting and worth a quick visit and purchase! I recommend visiting the elephant orphanage.

Title: Very expensive..not worth it for an elephant ride 10 mins
Text:
Not worth it they charged 3000LKR per person for a 10 min elephant ride .. which was totally not worth it . In India you can do that for ?50 for the same experience u won't like to pay ?1500 and this is basically not even in the jungle 
Also after to complete the ride the mahavat and the other guys will come after you asking for hefty tips .. which is not supposed to be paid
Don't waste you time here

Title: Exciting to see
Text: Well worth to go and see if you are in sri lanka it was memorizing just watching the elephants would visit again

Title: Not perfect, but not awful either
Text:
First things first, I saw no evidence of any physical abuse of the elephants during my visit to Pinnewala Orphanage. The elephants look well fed, clean and have no scars from chains or sticks as far as I could see. The keepers used goads to guide the elephants and to prevent the bulls trying to mix with the main herd of females/younger elephants, but I did not see a single one being hit. The chains used on some of the bulls look unpleasant, but they seem to be loosely fitted and not particularly irritating to the animals. Keeping such large and potentially aggressive animals under control is essential when they are in such close proximity to one another (bulls generally wouldnt mix with the herd in the wild) and to humans. The animals are corralled to be fed and kept in a certain (quite large) area of the river to be washed, but otherwise roam around a large natural reserve. 

Some of the extras put on for tourists (photos with the elephants, feeding/washing them etc) arent acceptable. The elephants are wild animals, not playthings or props, and they should be treated as such. A couple of keepers rode some of the bulls back from the river, which again I dont agree with. Additionally, perhaps more effort could be made to return some of the animals back to the wild, however I dont know anything about the practicalities  and of course this runs the risk of them being killed by farmers (the main threat to wild elephants in Sri Lanka).

All in all, as far as I could tell the Pinnewala Orphanage is not abusive to the animals in its care and is no worse than Western zoos. Keeping animals in captivity is never ideal, but the fraught relationship between farmers and wildlife in Sri Lanka make it impossible for all elephants to live in the wild. Perhaps in the future with better education, people all over the world will be better able to co-exist with animals and places like Pinnewala will be unnecessary. However, for now this place is the best of a bad situation.

Title: Grate Place to see Elephants in Sri Lanka
Text: Get a pretty closer look the elephants and feed the babies ,watching them bathing in the river ,Pleasing atmosphere. best place for family's. we had a grate time.

Title: In love with the Elephants
Text: Stop the car on the road and wait till the Elephants get back to their Orphanage at 12pm and 3PM you wait them on the road and see the old and the young, the new born and their mothers, passing 2 meter away from you. the feel how these animal are loving and live in family.

Title: Wish we never visited. Ashamed we supported this.
Text: We stopped off here on the way from Kandy to Negombo in time for the 2pm bath time. Its the last thing we have done in Sri Lanka and has left a bitter taste. As this wasnt part of our planned itinerary, I did not do any research beforehand. Wish I had. Youll find plenty of articles which will dissuade you. The word orphanage is a well chosen one; it fools you into thinking this might be ecotourism. There are no success stories about these elephants being released back to the wild, only a brag about how this is the largest herd of Asian elephants handled by man. Twice a day the elephants are walked across the road down to a river where masses of people crowd around taking selfies. One man sprays them from a water cannon. If they dont want to get wet, then tough. I watched several try to avoid the spray only to be herded back into its path with shouts and the bull hook. It is sad to see them just standing there not playing at all. It is not their choice to be at the river and they look unhappy. Some of the handlers were interacting nicely with them, washing and scratching them. But others just sat on the rocks. I fail to see how the animals well-being is put first - a complete money making scheme (2500 rupees to watch at the riverside). In penance for participating in such unethical tourism I will be donating the cost of our tickets to Save the Elephants. Im hopeful my review will deter at least a few people from visiting.

Title: excellent day out
Text: had a great morning here at the orphanage - I even fed a baby elephant with a large bottle. and watched then walk down the road in to the river for their bath/fun. Amazing creatures - well worth a visit

Title: I was sceptical too - but then we visited it :)
Text: I read a whole bunch of these reviews before we travelled to Sri Lanka. I really wanted to see the elephants and it was our honeymoon after all. We visited Thailand last year and refused any elephant visits as they are so mistreated over there and we are very against elephant riding. Our experience of Pinnawala was delightfully reassuring and I felt relieved. The elephants are treated very well and no one was riding them or beating them with sticks - as some of these reviews suggest. They were free to walk around and were fed very generously. You can tell that all staff members look after them very well. Yes - there some that have some chains around them. This is unfortunate but we asked why this was and didn't just assume. As this is an orphanage, a lot of these elephants wouldn't survive the wild because they are unwell or have certain illnesses. Naturally, some are also a bit aggressive and therefore, to protect themselves and the other elephants they have some with chains. It's the best of a bad situation for them but they are bathed separately and have the same amount of love and care as the others. The keepers also carry "guide sticks" to help direct the elephants to the bathing river etc. They never hit or hurt the elephants with these sticks, they just use them gently to guide them safely across the roads etc. I think the people here are doing an amazing thing and we loved seeing them. We didn't need to ride them or anything - it was just amazing to see them. What a wonderful place for them.

Title: Nice experience
Text:
Such beautiful creatures
Take a hat
Drinking water
Camera
The feeding session was basic
The hand feeding excellent for families- do your little ones a favour and treat them
Highlight was the bathing time- it was a delight

Title: On our bucket list
Text:
Jack tours picked us up from our hotel the Turyaa, quite a long journey with another couple and two ladies. During the trip we made new friends and laughed and laughed.
On arrival at the orphanage we saw young elephants being fed by the keepers with large bottles of milk.
We crossed the road towards the river, a siren warns of approaching elephants, Jack took us up some stairs to a restaurant overlooking the river, what a view we had,and then they arrived at least 20 elephants, some to the left and these were chained as they were being trained for religious ceremonies. The rest just played in the river, washing and shooting water out of their trunks, an amazing sight and a privilege to be part this tour. Thanks to Jack and our new friends this is a trip we will never forget....

Title: Please don't participate in the abuse of elephants!!!
Text:
Maybe the intentions of this 'orphanage' were once good, they are definitely not now. 

This is a commercialized elephant breeding factory. Most of the elephants are bred in the park, for the sole purpose of entertainment for tourists. 

Caretakers are encouraging everyone to take photos and touch the elephants in exchange for tips. 

You can pay extra to feed a baby elephant, who is chained by itself in a cage surrounded by tourists. When we were there, the baby was freaking out, trying to get out of the chains and hurting herself. They get fed whenever a tourist pays, not only during feeding times.

Many elephants are chained up all day in the same spot. They get to go to the river 2 times a day (you have seen the famous photos). Even there many are chained up under water and caretakers push them underwater with a stick so they look like they are splashing around. 

Many of them are showing signs of distress, rocking back and forth for hours at the time while being chained up. This does not happen in the wild. These compulsive movements cause life-threatening damage to the feet and joints of the elephant. They are in severe distress and don't let them tell you otherwise. 

People saying that there is no other way to treat them and the elephants would not survive in the wild are wrong. There are way more humane ways to treat elephants in an orphanage and this is not one of them. Please don't participate.

Title: It could have been so much better
Text:
So sad to think that the reason why the elephants are there is because of the impact of man on their natural environment- baby elephants frightened falling down wells, electric fences, orphaned. 
When we were there there had been a train crash killing 4 elephants..
Chains and the use of elephant hooks not nice to see...
The whole area is just going to get more commercialized, lots of building work going on- 
they should be educating the locals as to how to have a balance to live with elephants

Title: Interesting but a bit sad
Text: This was an interesting experience but not quite what I expected. Most of the elephants were adults not babies, which is what I thought we would see. Whilst they looked healthy I would much have preferred them to be in the wild. Apparently it is a catch 22 situation. The elephants draw tourists and people of the area rely on this for their income. There are very few elephant orphans so the elephants are kept and not released back into the wild, so that tourists have elephants to see

Title: Chains and elephant hooks
Text: It may have started out as an orphanage but it doesnt appear like it now. Not what we expected at all. Chains and elephant hooks. This place does not appear like a refuge for elephants ?? at all. We were visiting from Australia. The elephants at the orphanage are in chains, and the keepers have elephant hooks. Really left with such a bad feeling of the elephants not being treated very well at this place.

Title: Did not enjoy this visit
Text:
The park is very touristic , some of the elephants are tied . 
It is nice to see the elephants , the staff cleaned them and fed them. I do not recommend visiting unless you have nothing else to do . It is much better to see the elephants on a national park .

Title: Not bad
Text:
Visited with the family 
Sad to see the animals in captivity 
But good experience for kids to have closer look of a giant animals
Dont eat food in high end restaurants -no much different compare to street food 
Good public transportation available even though its not its best for country like Ceylon 
Might visit again

Title: Amazing experience-a must when you are in Sri Lanka
Text: Great to experience something different and exciting. A great way to get teenagers off their phones. My son 15 years  was hard to please but enjoyed this experience the most. We stayed over a hour. You get to see elephants in their natural habitat playing and having fun.

Title: BEST EXPERIENCE
Text: What a great Experience, we arrived at 9am so I was able to feed an Elephant it only cost 250 rup, we then watched the Elephants walk down to the river, Once there we positioned ourselves on the verandah of the Hotel overlooking the river & got a really good view of the Elephants being washed & playing in the water, as you walk towards the river on the right hand side there is a guy who will take your money if you would like to wash an Elephant it is only 750 rup just be prepared to get wet, The orphanage assures everyone that the Elephants are well treated & looked after which is great, so lovely to see the Elephants having fun, we loved every minute ??????

Title: Buen lugar para conocer
Text:
Elephant Orphanage in  Pinnawala is very nice but in my opinion is more  focus on comercial side than care the nature! Rs 2500 is ok. In sept 2018

I booked a car and driver and is very comfortable. Colombo to Pinawala is 2.45 hrs

Title: Lots of Elephants!
Text: We arrived just in time to see the elephants getting their daily washing at the river.  They really seemed to enjoy being doused with the water cannon.  Afterwards we toured the actual ground where the elephants were eating and enjoying the company of other elephants in a nice peaceful setting.  The entry ticket is a bit pricey but the money goes towards the enormous costs of feeding and caring for these majestic animals so make the stop and buy the ticket.

Title: Mixed feelings
Text: Its nice for childern and special to see the elephants trekking through the villages to the river for bathing, the other actvities such as milk feeding and fruit feeding are just over commercialized (as is the whole park). Somehow did not feel right

Title: A Viking excursion
Text:
This was an all day excursion from our Viking Ocean cruise docked in Colombo. 

A three hour bus drive going and coming. But it was worth it. 

When we got there our tour guide directed us down to the river where dozens of elephants were bathing. It was incredible to watch them. 

Then after lunch we went to the sanctuary where they graze and are taken care of. 

If youre an animal lover youll enjoy it.

Title: Beautiful animals - but just on show for tourists
Text:
We went to the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage with our driver as our guide - if you didn't have someone with you who knew how the place worked you would be at a loss as you are not given any information when you purchase your tickets.
We were in time to see the elephants herded together to be fed and then followed them down to the water for them to bath.
This is 'put on' for tourists twice a day and even though it was wonderful to see these magnificent beasts it really felt like a show.
It is expensive to get into the park and we are hoping that most of the money goes to caring for the elephants.
The tourist shops on the way down to the water are fairly expensive but you can get a last minute gift if you need.
We preferred seeing the elephants in the wild on our safari tour

Title: Wow...
Text:
We were on time to see around 30 elephants bring given a bath through a high pressure pump.
After the bath, they orderly walked one behind another to the orphanage across the highway.
We saw many more elephants including one with very long tusks.
There were many curio shops near the river where they sell a lot of elephant related curios as well as stationery and other items made of elephant poop. There was a demonstration too to visitors showing the process making paper from elephant poop.
A must visit place in Srilanka.
Ganesh J

Title: So little to do or see.
Text: Not worth it. The baby feeding show is only one baby. Its really small and run down looking. Area seems much too small for 80 elephants. You can pay 1£ to feed an elephant... but he seems really overfed with people Queuing up to do so... felt a bit wrong.

Title: Not Impressive
Text: It's a large place and there are quite a few Elephants. But the premises is not well maintained. Also you are not allowed any where near the Elephants or to feed them, unlike in some other Elephant safari's. Some of the Elephants were very restless and were grunting. Everything inside the souvenir shop is exorbitantly priced and not worth the buy. The place is not very impressive and if you been to other Elephant camps, then this is a big let down, as the entrance fee for foreigners is very high.

Title: A money making, tourist trap elephant orphanage
Text: Apart from the Instagram worthy shots, this place seems like a money making attraction rather than an orphanage. There are better ways to donate your money and support these elephants. If you are looking for an alternative experience with the elephants, then I would suggest the safari.

Title: Elephant orphanage?
Text: I don't understand why it is called an orphange. It is deffinitly an elephant Zoo. The elephants are being escorted to the lake twice a day for a couple of hours. other than that they are being tied up inside the Zoo. It costs 2500 Rs per person. If you want you can pay more and touch them. I don't recommend coming to this place unless you like zoos.

Title: Herd of elephants
Text:
Its a good 3 hr drive from Colombo. This place is famous for the elephant sanctuary.

We could see the elephant bathing at the river and in the orphanage could see a lot of elephants especially the baby elephants. It was a bit hot so did not venture too much.

The fees for adults are LKR 2500 for international tourist and LKR 700 for SAARC countries tourists.

I think 1 hour is sufficient for the entire place.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
going through all the reviews I wasn't sure shall I visit it or not! I am glad I did, they take care of the elephants and we shall contribute with the ticket amount.

The baby elephants, the river and the spacious place is defiantly the highlight.
Check their timetable and plan your time accordingly 

Go for it!

Title: It was a long drive from Colombo, but worth it.
Text: It was nice to see the elephants roaming around seeming to be enjoying their space. We were only separated from them by two rows of rocks which was nice. There were plenty of trainers around watching what the young ones were up to and keeping them behind the rocks.

Title: Elephant Orphanage
Text: The first thing to note is the orphanage is more Zoo like than I expected. I was also not really prepared to see some of the elephants chained to posts, however I also didn't expect one to walk past within ten feet of me either. The park is split into three sections - there is an area where you can feed fruit to an elephant, there is a holding area where the elephants are chained and fed; and then there is a large 'paddock' where they roam free. There are keepers who patrol the perimeter of the paddock, but other than a smattering of rocks, there is nothing between you and the elephants. Whilst we were at the paddock, the elephant who had been at the fruit station, was walked back to the field in front of where we were stood. It was quite amazing. Later on a group were walked down to the feeding station and again were no more than ten foot away from us. There is a daily milk feed for the orphans, and a walk down to the river for a bath, but on the day we were there, neither took place. Unsure as to why the feeding didn't happen (although I expect the babies would have been chained too & not quite the romantic image I had), but the bathing was cancelled due to the rain causing river levels to be too high. Would recommend as an opportunity to get close to the elephants, but not as one to view them in their natural habitat.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
So we had read so many mixed reviews and were debating whether to go or not. We decided to go and see for ourselves and make our own minds up & in all honesty seeing these wonderful animals at such close proximity was amazing, would we prefer no chains - of course, but you can see in most cases it is for the Elephant & public safety as most do not have such chains when back in the ample enclosures. They seem to be well fed and love the water playing.
Bearing in mind that this place started with two elephants and takes in sick or injured as well as releases some back to the wild on balance they do a great job.
Seeing the keepers with hooked poles is not nice but we saw no ill treatment and more love than anything.
Cost for us foreigners is 2500 rupee (around £12.50) each and bearing in mind that the money goes to help I see this as good value plus I paid 750 rupee for my wife to wash an elephant in the water - clearly enjoyed by the elephant and my wife.
I do have issues with the elephants being ridden by the keepers & also on the road into the orphanage a place offering ride an elephant Service - this to me is totally wrong and should not be allowed! 

Anyway in my humble opinion it was a wonderful experience

Title: Poor Experience
Text:
The ticket is 2500 Rupees and each activity is charged separately with average 750 Rupees (Elephant Bathing / Milk Feeding).
I do not mind supporting the cause of caring for orphan elephants and I think it is good to do this initiative.It is quite amazing to see the elephants bathe and then return from the river but also quite sad and meaningless to see some inside strapped and used for tourist attraction - Milk feeding is a joke, you pay but don't really do it.

Maybe this is not the kind of place that I would like to visit, but if you have kids and want to get them up close to elephants then that could be a good option. For me, I would rather next time go to national park safari and see them in their natural habitat.

Title: To do absolutely!
Text:
A great experience: elephants come close by, you can see them being free to play in the river, they look happy and totally good.
You should definitely go to visit if you go to Sri Lanka!

Title: The Elephants were poorly treated. It was heart braking to hear their screams
Text:
We were taken to Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage by our tour guide on our way to Nuwara Eliya from Colombo. I had heard and read so much about this place that I definitely wanted to visit it.
As soon as we entered we were pleased to see so many elephants in the river  which was quite a sight. But after standing and looking at them for a bit, we realized that some of the elephants were chained up and forced to spray water from their trunks or were being forced to lie down. If they tried getting up the so called caretaker would pierce them with these long sharp and pionty spear/rods in their hand. It made the the elephants scream loud(could be heard at a distance) in pain and the care taker seemed to enjoy it. I really felt bad and we all decided to leave immediately. It dint feel as though the care taker had any kind of bond or cared even a bit for the elephants. I really hope that the government looks into it and hires people who actually want to do something for the elephants and not use them as props for tourism.

Title: Lots of elephants
Text: definitely a spectacle to see. Very nice to see them in the river and travel across the walk. Some paths are steeply slopped.  Recommend sneakers instead of flip flops.  Some were in chains during the processional as other reviews indicated. Places to eat and shop. However vendors  were pushy and annoying.

Title: Pinnawale elephant-bath and park
Text:
Elephant parks can be found at several place in Asia. They differ in offered service, exposure and elephant treatment, At the Pinnawala Orphanage in Sri Lanka you can see the herd walking to/from the river and watch them inside the the orphanage, being fed. 
Part of the herd is on the background (furtheraway from the public) and others are more upfront. The entrance ticket is also required for the riverwalk, as the authorities close off the street, to secure the elephants from traffic. Inside the park, I saw 2 elephants chained on 2 legs (according to the staff because of behavior). There are no rides possible, and no tricks/acts are presented. Mahouts offered me to take a selfie with the elephant (for money), which I declined, The mahouts are using the sticks with metal points,

Title: Up Close But Not Personal
Text:
This is a place that has many controversial reviews and so we pondered to whether we wanted to go or not. It was a tossup and I am glad we did go but it did leave some questions unanswered. 
We missed the elephants walking from the park over the road and down to the river. So we purchased our tickets from the ticket office and then headed over. You have to give your ticket to the ticket man at the start of the road so unpaid people cannot get down there to watch the elephants. We got down there and it was quite a sight. All these elephants standing in the water. The group of elephants was split and I did notice the ones that were chained in place. I also noted a small group that kept trying to get out of the water. The mahout would let them go for a while and then he would yell and wave his hook and the elephants obviously fearful of him would get back in the water. I got talking to another visitor who said she had been a number of times and that the river was really low and when it is low they seem to be lethargic. It was the first time she had seen them so disinterested. 
The mahout to me seemed to be a bully. Later on when they were prepping them to leave, this particular guy caught my eye and smiled. I gestured to him that I was not happy with his behavior and proceeded to photograph him. I believe there is a difference to being in control fairly and being a bully. Out of all of them he definitely was a bully. The elephants were swapped  around a bit and it was fascinating to be so close and to watch them for a reasonably long period. It was extremely hot that day so we sat up in the restaurants balcony and had a beer etc. to get some respite. They then moved the elephants to the water cannon by the exit to the river which they seemed to enjoy and then the main girl elephant, she led them back up the road. They knocked over a hat stand in a store which was funny and they seemed keen to get back. 
We followed them closely and when we got back they had taken them over the back of the park and they were being fed. We stood for perhaps half an hour and no one told us what was happening- we just stood and hoped there was something more. Eventually they told us we could go over which we did. 
Yes they were all chained by a foot and they all had piles of food. We stood for a period watching how they ate soft wood, palm leaves and observed what they seemed to prefer to eat, and how they manipulated the food to eat. 
We then went back to another area where they had younger elephants still on milk. We got talking to the assistant curator and it wasnt until he answered my questions about containment, feeding, punishment, medical care, that it made any sense. He said there was a lot of misunderstanding and therefore there are negative reviews. I asked why they seemed to be not enjoying themselves in the water and he said, they are just so keen to get back to eat.
The main reason for containment is to stop fighting. In the wild the elephants form packs where there is a boss and they will fight if they encroach on other elephants territory. They are working on a big open area for them but at the moment containment is the best for them. So this parks environment is not normal, but it is the best they can do and they do their best to stop the animals hurting each other. He said that the elephants do not have to work for their food there and life is quite easy and the care is excellent with medical care etc. and it is a good alternative for the orphans. I suggested they educate the visitors more. There was very little education of the visitors and when you dont know why things are being done, you come up with your own theory. The experience is not interactive enough. 
I also complained about the bully mahout and he knew who I was talking about and he has been pulled up before about this. I appreciate what this place is doing but think it is a shame that there are even orphans that need care. If they were just left to their own devices, and humans didnt interfere, there would be few orphaned anyway. 
I think they actually do really care for them and give them great care, but they need to connect with the visitors more and explain what and why and how they do what they do.

Title: Front Row Seats to 40+ Elephants Bathing and Crossing a River is Priceless
Text:
We stayed at Hotel Elephant Park. This is an excellent place to get up early, have breakfast and have some of the best seats in the house to a fantastic experience. Photographs of the experience are readily available... the actual experience is way better. From the eyes of my 8 year old granddaughter, it was magical. You want to be done with breakfast by 830am when the first group of about 7 elephants come. You can move off the balcony of the hotel down to the rocks to get really close to the elephants, If you move down early you will beat the crowds and get pics you will treasure. Once the elephants are guided away from the river, take an hour or so shopping the row of shops leading to the river. Make sure you begin to make your way back toward the river just before 1000am. You will be able to see 40+ elephants guide toward the river. You can stand within 2 feet or so of the procession. Once safe, make your way back to the rocks by the water. This is an excellent vantage point to enjoy the spectacle.

Unfortunately I don't have anything positive to say about the actual orphanage. I imagine and believe that they are doing good work, but I can't personally vouch for it. We went before the 40+ elephants were guided back to the orphanage, and I can say that within 10 min, the overwhelming impression my family got was: depression. I would NOT recommend entrance to the Elephant Orphanage. Enjoy the elephants while bathing.

BTW,if you are looking for an extremely high quality experience from a personal driver,  I had an opportunity to work with both Gamage Asanka from Gamage Tours, gamagetours.com, asankamail2@gmail.com. I reached out to him because of a good review on Trip Advisor. From the first email, it was obvious he was responsive, quite courteous and professional. We began to work on an itinerary together, and received what I thought was very reasonable pricing for what I was asking him to do. When it came down describing our vehicle needs he was quick to note that since we had 4 people in our party, his vehicle would not be the best option. I appreciated his candor. 

He recommended a personal friend and colleague, Gihan Thissera, from Sinethi Tours, sinethitours77@gmail.com.  Gihan took us on 7 day tour of central/southern Sri Lanka. He was prompt, kind, attentive, and professional at all times. His driving was safe and at no time did I feel any stress on behalf of my family. He asked him to meet us at a railroad station after a 5 hour train ride, and he was there exactly where and when he was supposed to be. He pointed out fruits in season, and bought us fruit to sample. He was especially attentive to my grand daughter. His vehicle was utterly spotless at all times. I thought I was getting a driver what I ended up getting was a guide who became an integral part of our group. My family and I could not imagine a better experience than the wha we had with Gihan.

Title: Highlight of holiday
Text: Excellent experience. The setting organises visitors appropriately ensuring safety and plenty of opportunity to see these beautiful creatures. To see approximately 40 elephants bathing freely  in the river is magnificent . Well worth visiting

Title: Wonderful experience to get so close to the elephants
Text: They have set the time for the elephants to go out to the river. It is very important to check the time in advance. Seeing the elephants having fun in the river is remarkable.

Title: Worst experience in Sri Lanka
Text:
We arrived just in time to see elephants bathing, and it was nice enough. Then tuk-tuked  to a spicegarden, although we said we didnt got the time. Staff got angry when we didnt want to buy anything. Didnt go back inside to see anymore. 

Elephants seems poorly treated, and why its called an orphanage I really dont know. Most animals borned in the park.

Title: The highlight of my trip
Text: Omg a must see. You could not go to Sri Lanka and not go the Pinnawala. This was the highlight of my trip. You must go to where the elephants live and then watch them  walk down through the street to the river to their bathing and play time. Loved this so much. Something you will never forget.

Title: Nice Place to watch elephants closely
Text: This was our first stop in Sri Lanka The scene of elephants to the river and back from the river is very impressive,You can experience milk feeding to baby elephants & feed a much older one,There are also many other elephant acrivities to see.we spent 3 hours there and and felt we could have stayed there more, A truly family friendly place to visit.

Title: Amazeballs!!
Text:
Loved, loved, loved this place. 
Experience of a lifetime! Bathed and rode elephants. You can see how much the people working there are passionate about their elephants and just adore them.
They are working hard to re educate and ethically care for these big beautiful animals.

Title: Bucket list experience
Text:
This was booked by our tour company for us.  We did not therefore have to deal with getting tickets etc as our guide did all this for us and showed us were to go.  First of all we went across the road from the main site towards the river where we watched the lephants bathing in the river.  It was a lovely sight to see, I know some had chains on them but this we were informed was for safety reasons related to the behaviour of the specific elephant. The elephant hotel is an ideal spot to having a drnk and some lunch as they have a balcony area overlooking the river.  We were fortunate to be browsing the shops down towards the river when the elephants were being brought back to the main sight.  Boy were they lively with a slight incident with one not behaving!!!

Back on the main sight we were able to see the elephants includiing a couple of tuskers (we learnt that not all elephants have tusks).  There is the chance to hand feed a elephant fruit which was 350 rupees and this was certainly memorable with the chance to touch them under the supervision of one of the keepers.  There is also the chance to bottle feed a calf again under supervision - if you're going to flim or take pictures of this be quick they drain a large bottle of milk in the blink of an eye!

It certainly was a bucket list exerience and lovely to see how they have taken them in for various reasons ad how well they are cared for.

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage: A Hope for Elephants Protection
Text: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is located on a road breaking from Colombo Highway to Kandy. There are baby elephants as well as large elephants rescued from the Jungle who have lost way from their parents. Good place to visit.

Title: We'll never forget...
Text:
This place has something quite magical about it - the elephants of course. Split across a road (really) it is a little bit complicated upon first arriving as you feel you shoud go into the actual orphanage but then a siren sounds and the elephants leave the grounds to cross the road, parade down a street full of shops (!) and into the river but this is something you must see! It's amazing to watch 40+ elephants happy, frolic and even scrubbed by some of the orphanage workers. You can enjoy the view from a cafe or just from the pavement. Proceed back up past the shops selling elephant dung toilet paper ;) to the orphanage where you can enjoy feeding them or just watch them roam about in wide open spaces. 

Some elephants are with chains which can be a little upsetting to initially see but it appears its only for those that are a bit unruly and could charge off. None are actually shackled to the ground although we did feel a bit taken advantage of by the river as a young elephant with a chain was used to pose for photos with tourists as workers pressed for money for each photo. Try to avoid this if possible as you will have many opportunities to take photos of them in the river, on the road and in the orphanage without lining the pockets of opportunists using them for a photo opportunity. Who wants a photo with chains in it anyway?

Title: Must do for kids of all ages..
Text: One of the oldest places in Sri Lanka where elephants wounded, hurt are cared for. They even breed elephants and leave them out in the open once they are ready. This is my second visit to the place, and was excited all the way through. You can see elephants up close and personal, chewing the greens, with their young ones and in their families. If its a non rainy day, you can even see the herd bathing and enjoying in the nearby river. There is a ticket for foreigners, saarc country foreigners, and locals...totally takes about 1-2 hours, and is on the way to Kandy...

Title: Great to see elephants treated well
Text:
We visited as a part of a day trip from Negombo to Kandy.

We arrived early morning, at 0930 and were able to watch the baby elephants being bottle fed. You could also give it a go yourself if you asked.

The elephants looked well treated and after  walking around the orphanage, we were pleasantly surprised to be guided across the road by our tour guide to a local restaurant overlooking the rivers. The street was full of shops and people asking us to come in, which seemed decent if your into that kind of thing.

We arrived at the restaurant and ordered some food (Western prices) and after a few minutes, saw a huge herd (50+) elephants coming down the streets into the large river to bathe. It was particular great to see they were completely free to play and wash (no chains of ropes) with a few of the handlers simply sat by on the rocks.

Absolutely fantastic to see and definitely recommended.

Title: Great for 1-2 hours with the kids.
Text:
Great experience.
Washing & feeding the elephants.
We need to pay appx 50 USD for a pack of 4 ( 2 adults 2 kids ). A way of donation.
The souvenir shop has reasonable prices compared to the ones that we saw in Bentota & Galle.
Try to be there early like 10 am. to see all the ceremony.

Title: Surprised to see a few elephants in chains
Text: I have visited a few elephant sanctuaries in Thailand, but this is the first time visiting an elephant orphanage in Sri Lanka. We were not expecting to see a few elephants chained at their hind feet and neck, but were informed that these were untamed animals. Overall the caretakers did not seem to have a bond with their charges like what we saw in Thailand. It would have been better if there was more narration on how these animals are cared for and managed.

Title: Wonderful
Text: I love elephants so had to visit the orphanage whilst on holiday in Sri Lanka. Fabulous place. Had seen mixed reviews about the place but can honestly say that I saw no signs of cruelty whatsoever.  The elephants were free. The only elephant I saw that was chained, was one that was eating. All of the other elephants were free and it was great to see. Highly recommend.

Title: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage Sri Lanka
Text: A really nice to visit especially if you have children with you... Seeing the elephants bathing in the river is such a joy...

Title: Overrated & missable
Text: Fell pray to the hype of visiting the elephant orphanage at Pinnawala. Unfortunately, we went  on a Sunday which meant that the place was extremely crowded. If you have seen elephants in safaris elsewhere in the world then theres really not much to see or do here. Most of the elephants are small & young. One can skip this place to do something better. Incase you are traveling with children then it might be fine to visit Pinnawala but rather do the private parks like Millennium elephant park close to this place to experience bathing, feeding the elephant, etc

Title: Recommended on the way from Colombo to Kandy
Text:
I am an animal lover and I think this is a good place.
