Don't understand some of the comments below, yes elephants have baths and food at set times so that tourists can see them/ feed them, yes some elephants are chained (only the very big ones from what I have seen), but the elephants seem well cared for and they do not authorize riding of elephants (not like some other places in Sri Lanka or Thailand).
Overall a very nice day with the kids

Title: Beautiful elephant gathering
Text:
It's is nice to see lot of elephants , it's orphanage. You will see milking and even you can feed. Then if you need to feed some fruit it's possible. 
Since we got very good driver he direct us. 
Then we watch them having bath while we had our lunch neara rezturant.
Overall it's nice experience

Title: Looks nice
Text: Well what to say....its an elephant attraction, but elephants looked in a good condition, taking bath every day, well feeded with big area where to be. The most important thing - riding is not available - thumbs up for this.

Title: They do a good job
Text: Being an animal lover and bit concerned about animals being used just for entertaining tourists we were a bit unsure about going. However that wasnt the case here, the elephants came first. They looked healthy, well cared for and by following them down to the river for their daily river bath, we could clearly see that they were stimulated and enjoying as much freedom as is possible. Certainly much happier than any zoo environment in any country. I would certainly recommend going

Title: Worth a visit
Text: The orphanage is famous for elephants which kept over here though the drive to Colombo is bit long it took us 3 hours to do 84 km only above that the road width is too less which makes travelling slow so if you ample time its worth a visit there!!! One can see elephants bathing and feeding of milk also happens there

Title: Animal buff? definitely a treat :)
Text: If you are an animal buff then this place is definitely worth visiting. My guide took me there on our way to kandy. We pulled over at this Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage although there are many orphanages in the way to kandy but I preferred to this one. Its a huge place with many Elephants. You can even feed them with extra charges like milk and fruits feeding, I tried both and loved it! They than take all the elephants to the canal where you can witness these giants playing and washing themselves in water. I would definitely recommend this place

Title: Disappointing
Text:
We visited this zoo-like park on a day that there was no milkfeeding. As we also missed the bathing it was just looking at some elephants. Like others have mentioned before, it doesnt add much when you have already done a safari. 
Prices are steep for foreigners. With feeding and bathing things might have been different; without it, don't visit, so look out for those times.

Title: Love elephants? This is a spectacular sight.
Text: We watched up to 50 elephants of all sizes going from their home fields through a shopping area to the river to enjoy bathing and being washed by keepers. It was quite extraordinary and we could have spent hours just watching their behaviours. We had lunch in a restaurant by the riverside so we could sit and enjoy watching the bathing ritual. Definitely worth a visit if you are a fan of wildlife. The animals appear very well treated and cared for here.

Title: Good
Text: This place was good to visit- cost 2,500 rupees (25AUD) per person which is similar to animal park prices in Australia. They have cheaper prices for locals of course. The best part was the bathing of the elephants which we already had access to anyway as our hotel was down on the waterfront. When they walk from the sanctuary to the river it is crazy- they all just storm down the street, some looking a little scared. I am unsure of how well they actually look after the Eles- lots are in chains and the keepers just kept telling us that the animals are mentally sick. I wish I'd chosen a national park with free roaming Eles rather than this sanctuary where they have hugely commercialised every aspect of caring for them. That said, some keepers did get in the water and play around/wash their Eles which was great to see.

Title: Get up close with a herd of elephants
Text:
Having read some negative reviews on here about entrance fees and paying extra to feed the elephants I was pleasantly surprised to see the entrance fee clearly displayed on arrival. RD 2500 for foreigners and RS 100 for Sri Lankans and RS 700 for SAARC nationals. 

Twice daily you get the chance to bottle feed the babies or fruit feed the adults, who clearly love the attention they get. The elephants are kept in wonderful surroundings and are looked after very well. This is a tourist attraction but it has expanded to rescue elephants injured in the jungle and offer them a safe home for the rest of their lives with medical attention when needed.  

It is an amazing sight to see the elephants being led down to the river to bathe, some are tethered in the water, this is to protect the human visitors and also to stop the males harassing the females. There are a couple of hotels/tea shops on the banks of the river from where you can sit and watch the elephants bathe and the road leasing from the river to the main park is lined with souvenir shops which are fun to browse. 

We thoroughly enjoyed our trip to the elephant orphanage, it is as close to seeing elephants in their natural environment as possible. I would recommend a visit, even for those who do not like to see animals in captivity, they are well kept and far better off here than in the places they were rescued from.

User_Location: Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates
Title: Asian Elephants
Text: This is a must stop and preferably earlier in the morning if you want to feed milk to the baby elephants.From the ticketing desk is opposite the road a less than 5 minutes walk to the river. Was lovely seeing the herd though it can get a bit crowded with the number of students and tourists. If you want to ride on the elephants its in a different location and different sanctuary. Overral experience was good

Title: Mandatory stop!
Text: we went there during the afternoon when they feed the cubs. We waited for the elephants to have the bath at the river. You can have a coke while seeing the animals having fun on the river. Top photos.

Title: 4th visit
Text: Absolutely love this place, to see the elephants here relaxing and playing in the river, and roaming in their enormous paddock is a wonderful sight.   Yes 2 or 3 animals may be tethered but they will explain that this is for the safety of the animals and the visitors.  Every day they are taken down to the river and are free to play and roam the river

Title: Elephants bathing in the river was magical
Text:
I was a little unsure of how I felt about this place upon arrival. My driver dropped me off at the foreigner ticket booth where I paid maybe l35 USD for my ticket. 

When I went in there was a spot where people were paying to feed fruit to elephants. Then an open area in the back were some elephants were just standing. It seemed like occasionally the staff were trying to corral the elephants closer to the tourists.

I wasnt feeling great about the place. I walked down to see the milk feeding and again, people were paying to hold a bottle of milk for a single elephant in a caged in area while so many people made noise and took photos. It felt so commercial and unkind for the elephants.

I left disheartened, not knowing that there was another area across the street where the elephants were taken to bath. My driver then showed me the area across the road, and for me this for me was magical. I watched maybe 30 elephants walk their usual path down to the river where a giant hose has been built to facilitate their bathing.

Ill admit, I was slightly distraught to see that some of the elephants had chains tied on their ankles that were then hung over their backs. They were not being led by chains and a near by sign explained that the chains are precautionary for the safety of the staff and tourists. I watched the elephants bath for almost an hour before deciding to have lunch at a restaurant that overlooked the bathing elephants. I did not once see the chains used.

My only qualm is that some of the staff ride the elephants. I have heard that this is very bad for the elephants spines. I am no zoologist, and I welcome any additional info on the harm this may cause to the animals as I do not like to see animals being mistreated.

Title: Awesome experience
Text: If you havent seen any elephants walk around so free or have not seen them having a bath live then this is a good family day out with the kids,youd also find slots of souvenirs of Sri Lanka at this place

Title: Elephants Relaxing in the River is an Awesome Sight to Behold
Text:
On the way to Kandy district straight after we landed in Colombo, our guide told us that the elephant orphanage was along the way and is a must-see. Indeed!

Besides the educational elements that were food for our intellectuality, there were plenty of F&B outlets to feed our tummies too. But the most memorable experience had to be seeing the multitude of elephants relaxing and enjoying themselves in the river. Yes, even for 1500 rupees per person (for foreigners like us), it is worthwhile and a very good first impression of Sri Lanka.

Title: Interesting Experience
Text: We stopped here on our way from Colombo airport to Kandy. It was almost in the mid way. They offer discount to SAARC country nationals which is a good thing and child also get some further discount. There are a lot of elephants here which are taken for bath every morning around 10 am to the river and afterwards they are fed with milk.

Title: Interesting but need to time your visit
Text:
We visited this last week with our family. Childrens love it when they see elephants so close by. However one of the fun activity here was feeding the elephants. Now for this to happen you need to 
a. Know the feeding times
b. Be a little earlier than feeding time, as there are only limited tickets available and its first come first serve. So, if you are with kids, highly recommended to plan it with your tour operator. 

Overall nice place for kids. 

You can also buy some handmade paper made out of "elephant poo" . They show you the complete process which is amazing. Then when the elephants are taken for bath, it is also amazing to see. 

Vegetarian restaurants nearby are not so much, so please be prepared to eat French fries , sandwiches only.

Overall a nice place to be. 

If you are holding passport from one of the SAARC countries, ticket is discounted. So indian have to pay only 700 Sri lankan rupees.(approx)

Title: The elephants are kept in wonderful surroundings
Text: I am not one to go to Zoos but to see these elephants being cared for in natural surroundings was quite inspiring and well worth the day's trip from Colombo

Title: Enjoyeeeeeee
Text:
Now en route from Colombo to Sigiriya one cannot... rather should not miss the Pinnawala elephant orphanage. 

These are rescued elephants and are not tame, you can see them take bath . Its more of an elephant rehab. If you are here to witness the wild and the wildlife this is it.. now there are plenty of private farms here catering to tourist needs of elephant rides and baths.. not these are exact opposite to the govt run which is a rehab and the private ones are only for tourist and making monies with elephants rides of different rate cards i.e. by the time you wanna ride them, there will be a mahout who will walk along and will take thru the mad and wild made wilderness.

there will be a place for quick bites and buy souvenirs too. So its practically ones own decision what they want and do. If you are Asian, you will not find anything amazing what you have not seen in your own home country.

Title: Really enjoyable
Text: We saw the elephants bathing and also saw them grazing in the fields. They are not tame, you cannot pet them, they have been rescued from the wild and some are released back into the wild. Sticks are used to guide them but we saw no cruelty. The guides seem to care about their elephants.

Title: Average
Text: It is a noble cause to take care of elephants that have been disabled and orphaned but the charges to enter are quite sky high... it is not value for money as you spend LKR 2500 just to enter... with that kind of money you expect to see something nice... all you see are a few elephants roaming around and there is an elephant feeding and bathing activity where you have to shell out more...

Title: Up close to Elephants
Text: The Pinnawala Elephant orphanage was first set up as a tourist spot but is now known for its rehabilitation of elephants. While there we saw herds of elephants in tranquil like conditions and free to roam with extra feed being trucked in. There is information posters explaining the difference between the Asian and African  elephants which was very interesting. There is a small gift shop which sells lovely fold up umbrella's with elephant designs for $7.50 all which helps finance the orphanage. One small elephant was chained by the leg and a bit distressed but we were told it had recently arrived and was being assessed and its feed monitored . On the way back to the bus we had to stop as did all foot traffic and auto traffic for the herd of elephants returning from the river following their bathing, There is a platform to watch them in this process

Title: Help the orphans
Text: Visited elephant orphanage with my family. Enjoyed every moment of the visit. Missed feeding the baby elephant as only 10 tickets were available.

Title: Watch the herd walking to and from the river
Text: Certainly there are many differing views on the Elephant Orphanage. It is a delight to watch them bathe (and to see how cheeky the little ones can be). Yes there are some chained and possibly the lack of communication regarding why is the issue. (Read AucklandWiz review below) Still a delight to see them in the river.

Title: Wow
Text: We visited on Boxing Day and were blown away from walking through the gates. From the surreal spectacle of the elephants walking through the middle of town to bathe in the river to bottle feeding the babies this is a once in a lifetime experience and would definately visit again.

Title: Nice... But
Text: Went to watch them bathe, you cannot bathe with them. There are men with metal prods but they use them sparingly only when they are getting too close to crowds and could be startled. Most of them really enjoyed the water, and you could tell the ones that didn't because they were so dirty still! At the end they did make the elephants go in the water, but they need to clean them somehow. I didn't like that the 3 largest ones were in chains, probably to prevent them from escaping to keep up conservation efforts, but still. If I had to do it again I would rather have gone on a safari to see them in the wild, but conservation is important and they are helping elephants that would not survive otherwise.

Title: Disgusted
Text:
So we went to pinnawala orphanage and it is a very sad sight to see this place needs closing down.
The elephants are chained in the water and forced to lay down the men or ogres that force them to do stuff
It is out and out cruelty.
The elephants are so sad.
This is no orphanage it is a money making 
I will do my utmost to get a petition going to get the elephants where they belong.
It brought tears to my eyes to see such  cruelty.
If you are an animal lover then please don't go

Title: Must visit!
Text: It was a treat to watch these majestic beasts! The sight of the bottle feeding of the calves, and the elephants all marching to the river and bathing there was spectacular! Definitely visit this place on your trip to Sri Lanka

Title: Chained and Corrupt
Text:
If youre concerned about animal welfare, please do not visit this place. 

The elephants are chained up and are being reared with pointed poles, the keepers are also riding them while their feet are chained. Not what I expected of an orphanage.

We bought a feeding ticket, but before we could feed the elephant its rearer asked us for extra money to help him out, before we could even feed. We told them no and proceeded to give the elephant some fruit. 

It was only on the way to the orphanage that a fellow tourist told us that the Sri Lankans have started to put sanctuary or orphanage in front of their Elephant enclosures to make it more attractive and seemingly less cruel towards what they are doing. It makes sense considering what we saw today.

Title: Total tourist show disguised as an orphanage
Text:
I understood from all the material that this place is an elephant orphanage where they take care of motherless elephants. But it is only one big tourist show and the animals are not treated well but moved around by a group of attendants with sharp sticks that they use to poke the elephants. The elephants are obviously scared of the sticks and try to move away only to be stuck by another attendant from the back. Horrible to watch and all done so we tourists can get the best photo opportunity. 

A huge part of the park is closed or under construction but no one tells you about that. 

Price for foreigners are 3000

Title: Animal sanctuary
Text: Great visit to see elephant rescued. No shop for merchandise which is good to see. Watched herd down at river and walking pack to park.

Title: A must see
Text: A must see and the showers of the elephants are super. Check the timing of the showers because its not done through the whole day.

Title: Difficult to view elephants in this set up
Text:
We visited the orphanage on the way round to Dambulla. We had read reviews on tripadvisor but we were undecided whether to visit. In the end we felt that perhaps our entrance fee would contribute to the elephant upkeep so we proceeded to visit.
On arrival and purchase of tickets we were taken down a small shopping street opposite to the orphanage which takes you to the river where the elephants bathe daily.
We arrived to see at least 30 elephants enjoying the water with some "snorkelling" and a couple of younger ones being a little cheeky. This part of the visit was great.
We did not wait to see all the elephants make their way back past the shops and street stalls but that might have been fun.

Back at the orphanage the pens, albeit large, just did not offer any stimulation for the elephants. Even though they are trying to make improvements the orphanage itself was not what we expected or would like to consider as acceptable for keeping what are wild elephants. We were saddened by what we saw and it left us thinking why not take them to one of the national parks and releasing them back to the wild. Probably not that simple but thats how it left us feeling.

Title: Don't visit this place for God sake.
Text:
You feel being hooked in a tourist trap. they charge a lot for nothing. it is just a so-called orphanage but nothing more than some captured and chained elephants. it also makes you sad and angry. because they misuse elephants and behave badly with them. 
don't spend a penny here. I think some organization should do something to close the place in the name of animals rights.

Title: Elephant baths
Text: A little uncomfortable to see a few of the elephants in chains although we were informed this was due to their unruly adolescent behaviour. This is very much a tourist destination rather than a pure sanctuary. For all the perceived negatives the elephants are well cared for and it is a wonderful sight to see them making the journey down the road to the river for bathing which the elephants do seem to genuinely enjoy.

Title: Playtime for elephants
Text: The elephants (there are around 80 at the orphanage) are taken to the nearby river in groups of 10 throughout the day. It's a  privilege to see them making their way past local businesses to and from the river. And of course to see them frolic and play in the water.

Title: Beautiful bathing site and Elephants crossing the road
Text:
Visited the Orphanage's bathing site at around 10.30am. The elephants are already in their natural bath. Honestly after walking through the street full of souvenir shops and suddenly this open space appear, seeing the elephant against the greenaries and blue sky is quite a sight to behold. Do look out for the men enticing you to feed the elephants with the oranges they provides, it willcost 100rupee. I next visited the Orphanage itself but only a handful of elephants are there. Do wait till 12noon when the elephants walk home from their bathing site. This is where the elephants walking by the souvenir shops and crossing the busy road to return to the orphanage. There are some reports that saying this Orphanage is ill-treating the elephants.  Yes I do see some elephants been chained at the leg but there are also signage to explain that they need to chain some of the more agressive male elephants to prevent them from attacking.
So is it ill-treating or disciplining - I guess it's up to individual to decipher.

Title: Worthwhile cause
Text:
We enjoyed our visit to the Elephant orphanage, we arrived for bathing time and watched them enjoying relaxed time in the water but watching the heard walking back to the orphanage is a sight to behold.
Unforgettable

Title: It is a zoo! Nothing else, and a small one...
Text:
You are charged 3000Rs to see 10 elephants in a enclosure, some of them chained. Today " no elephant bath" because water is to high, "no baby milking" without any other explanation. Another zone is closed to the public.
Just the explanation panels are well done and interesting, but in half an hour you have finished the visit. Really disapointing.

Title: Don't visit this so called orphanage
Text: I unfortunately ended up here while traveling through Sri Lanka and it's clear to me that this is nothing but a tourist trap of captured and chained elephants. We were approached several times by people asking for us to pay more by riding/bathing these poor elephants that are anything but "wild". Please don't encourage this place to continue the mistreatment of these poor animals.

Title: Elephants in Pinnawala
Text: Im unsure how I feel about this place...they seems to treat the elephants well but they dont give you enough information about their cause. I was nice to see the elephants play in the river and I can understand that they need to chain the males because some can be aggressive, though it was distressing to see them chained and poked at.

Title: Great to see the Elephants but would only do once!
Text: It was nice to see the Orphanage and I am pleased that the Elephants are being protected. I was a bit upset with the section for treating the 'angry' teenage elephants were they are tied up with no room to move and are basically having to dance on the spot to keep moving. That said the rest of the orphanage was big and spacious allowing the Elephants to roam. It was also nice to see them enjoying the water (in the big river) splashing around and playing. Glad we went but would not rush back again.

Title: This was a great experience.
Text: Before we came here, we did much research on the humane treatment of their elephants.  The primary objection that most people have is that male elephants have a chain on them when they are bathing.  This is to prevent them from attacking other males.  The elephants and their trainers had a grand time taking a bath and there was nothing cruel about it.  If they were released to the wild, they would die.  What other solution would you offer.  Seeing 40 plus elephants was a once in a life time experience and we would highly recommend it.

Title: A most uncomfortable experience
Text: After visiting the wonderful Elephant Nature Park in Chiang Mai a few years ago, this was a poorly executed excuse for a rescue park, where in truth the Elephants looked stressed and far from happy. At the feeding station, we declined feeding an elephant on the grounds that its keeper had a big stick with sharp end to keep the elephant in step. It may be needed, but it looks as if the elephants are are not treated nearly as well as in Chiang Mai. We then crossed the road to watch the elephants bathe, only to find that they are are chained in the water and literally unable to move, does not look like fun to me. I totally get why some people love this place as its the closest they ever get to seeing elephants in a wild setting, but I would say better to do a safari, which is close by.

Title: Unforgettable Experience
Text:
We visited Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage on our way to Kandy from Colombo. 
Initially I did not have high hopes of seeing anything extraordinary. 

After entering we had to walk for some distance in the hot sun seeing only one or two elephants chained inside their enclosure. 

But at the end of our walk, we were treated to a fascinating sight of more than 50 elephants roaming about in an open area enclosed by rocks and railings to prevent them from coming out. 

Then we watched some elephants being fed and some people were allowed to feed milk to baby elephants in bottles. 
After coming out, we were told that the elephants would come out, cross the road, walk into the street and take a bath in the river. 

We waited outside for some time and then the gates opened and more than 30 elephants came out, crossed the road and walked into the street within 5 feet of where we were standing. 

It is both awesome and scary to have 25 elephants walking right next to you, trumpeting and swaying and one elephant swerved dangerously close to where I was standing. 

After they crossed us, we followed them to the river by paying the charges and were again treated to a rare sight of so many elephants bathing together in the river. 

All in all, it was a wonderful and unforgettable experience and I am very happy that I paid a visit to this place. 
I have no hesitation in recommending this attraction to all of you who are visiting Sri Lanka.

Title: Love elephants
Text: Pinnawala had about 90 elephants ?? n are looked after very well by the people. They are the wild elephants n orphaned elephants looked after here. They are not tamed so are kept away from people. We can see them from a distance by the mud lake and by the farm. We can see them being fed at particular time n even feed the baby elephants ??. Then one can see them bathe by the river which is too adorable. Was fun n beautiful to see the grand elephants being their natural self in the pinnawala farm. Must visit.

Title: Adorable elephants
Text:
We read some dreadful reviews here and it nearly put us off but I knew a few friends who had been and they said it was worth a trip and they were right. 
I saw one elephant chained whilst feeding which I found upsetting but the rest was ok.
The highlight is definitely sitting by the river watching them bathe and have fun. 
There were only the male elephants who had chains on even walking back to the reserve, for obvious reason! There is information everywhere about what the males have chains. 

We made our own decision after visiting and I am glad I went. I got into the river to wash an elephant, it was an amazing experience, one which Ill never forget

Title: Need to love Elephants
Text: The government here is actually doing something about the elephants in a humane way. What a great experience. feeding the elephants!

Title: Elephant ride in Sri Lanka
Text: This is one must do activity in Sri Lanka. This was on our way from airport to Kandy. Will cost you SLR3000. But it is really worth doing this. The first 5 mins will be scary but gradually when you start making balance on the animal the ride becomes fun. The elephants are very gentle and well trained. The ride gives u a real feel of adventure as there is no howdah on the elephant and it bathes you also with the river water.

Title: Worth the road trip
Text: After a long 3 hour trip we got there and were the first in. our guide brought the tickets and managed to get a feeding ticket for my wife as well. This was one of the must do things there. There are plenty of elephants roaming freely which is a joy to see. Plenty of photo opportunities. the wife fed the little elephant with about a litter of milk, this went down in about 3 seconds but was definitely worth it. next we headed across the road to see them washing and playing in the river. would definitely recommend this experience as they do a lot of good work here.

Title: Great action
Text:
Went 10 am and Paid the entrance of 5000 Roupee and went thru the park to find very little but a few caged and chain tethered Elephants only to find that all of the action is down by the river as its washing time. 
40 Elephants of all sizes both male and female were having the fun of their lives. Swimming and going under. Playing together and enjoying the freedom of the running rapids. A few of the apparently naughty ones were tethered but the rest just frolicked in the river and roaming a fair distance up river. When called by the handlers they came. 
It was a great experience.

Title: Thankful for the work
Text:
Seeing these elephants makes you wonder what would happen to so many if it were not this centre. 

I am sure there could be improvements to the centre. 

I loved it. I was surprised how close we actually got to these animals. 

Thank you to all involved at this centre.

Title: Expensive for foreigners, but good
Text: The place is nice to visit. Saarc countries get a discount, so that makes up for it. The elephant feeding session was very enjoyable.

Title: Don't miss this.
Text: I don't believe in riding elephants and I know these elephants belong to an orphanage but the experience of seeing them lumber down the street two metres from your face and then being washed in the river is a sight to behold.

Title: not worthy
Text: Have to say, no worthy at all. Elephants are not treated well, looks awesome on photos but reality is different. Wouldn't go there again. Better to go for Safari tour, where u can see them in the wild.

Title: Mixed thoughts
Text:
Honestly. I thought I would write something that will help guide your decision about whether to go or not, however it isnt straight up and simple. Ive tried to bullet point my thoughts to try and help.

1. Yes there are chains on some elephants. I believe some have shown aggressive behaviours. There are some very not well looked after elephants in extremely worse situations I have seen across the island. 

2. The milk feed I am in two minds about. It is done to obviously provide money for the elephants. The two we saw were not in shackles, were boisterously playing around the site and seemed more than happy to keep drinking away, and were more teenager-ish stature.

3. The River. They seemed more than happy to splash about in the river. Some elephants were having their keepers wash them, one elephant didnt want him to stop, encouraging him when he stopped until he carried on again. Two elephants were chained on a long chain, they had enough room to play and their keepers could leave them safely there. It didnt seem any different to when you nip into the corner shop with your dog tied by its lead to the lamppost outside.

4. I did see one keeper prodding an elephant with a sharp pointed spear type implement at one point when it appeared to be going off track. This concerned me a little, however no elephant I had a good look at had any wounds, there were happy calves with their mums. They kept the bulls separate to the rest of the herd as they generally get territorial and violent.

If you do not like Zoos, do not go. Minneriya National Park is nearby and has wild herds.

Title: A different experience
Text: A different experience. The herds of elephants and their kids are very lovely. The elephants in the river are also very interesting.

Title: Unique experience yet could be distressing to some
Text:
After some initial concerns, we decided to visit Pinnawala Orphanage and we enjoyed it yet it did raise some concerns. The ticket for locals is a bargain. Foreigners pay much more, but I guess you need to maintain such a place and it's be unfair to overcharge locals. The place is indeed huge, beautiful and well-kept. It's all surrounded by the jungle. The orphanage enclosure is all done with wood and trunks and there is varied and typical vegetation (there are signs for the trees).
The fruit feeding of adult elephants and milk feeding of the young ones has a little of a show feeling, but if you try (paying a somehow reasonable price), you'll get the chance to have a unique experience, get close to the elephants and touch them. The unruly young ones were cute and insatiable. The adults seemed to enjoy the fruit and none seemed to be forced to eat.
Across the place there are lots of signs with information about elephants and their care and feeding. 
In a world where human beings are taking space from the wildness to build towns and roads, Pinnawale has a caring aim. Seeing a few unruly young ones chained was cause of concern, yet I want to believe that's the only option to keep the most unruly ones and that at some point, they are unchained and allowed to be in other open areas. 
It's a different experience from a zoo and a from a circus. I have heard otherwise yet I don't have those strong opinions. These elephants were separated by their own herds so at least they appear to be looked after and they may not have had many chances out there alone.

Title: Lot of Elephants but are they really orphaned.
Text: The elephants here are herded together and brought out to the river for bathing and you can have a view of the same. You can also feed the elephants with plantains, vegetables and the like at the orphanage. During the bathing the person herding them was noticed to use a longish  rod with a metallic pin or hook to prod the elephants to bathe thereby angering them. The Elephants belong to the Jungle and it may not right to chain some and parade them. It would have been better to look at them in the Jungle.  It is sad the 'orphanage' is one of the major attractions! for Tourist visiting Sri Lanka!

Title: Out of the World Experience !
Text:
We were simply floored with the utmost care and compassion with which Elephants are treated at this unique orphanage.It would be a misnomer to call this an orphanage,its more of a family home to all little and big ones.
The River bath of these mighty elephants is an awesome experience,not to be missed.Its a good option to have your snacks and drinks in the cafe overlooking the river bathing point,with wonderful photo opportunities too.Pls schedule your visit timings as per the bath timings.
Do remember to carry your passports,if you are from SAARC nation citizen, entry fees is only SLR 750.You can pick up paper stationary made from elephant dung from nearby shops.
Dont miss this experience,if you are visiting Kandy.

Title: not enough space
Text: the watching space needs to be bigger, really was not enough room to see the elephants. all the shops were closed, so no where to buy sovereigns

Title: This place has changed a lot for the better
Text: My mother and I visited here on our holiday to srilanka. I last visited 15 years ago. The elephants have their own section of never ending land to roam around. Large boulders are in place so the public do not enter. I loved that now these beautiful animals have their own space rather than being bombarded with people around them. They walk down to the river through shops to bath. Its truly fantastic to see. Yes the elephants are chained though which is hugely sad I believe its one leg. You cannot go into the river with the elephants which is also a nice touch I think as they have their own time to wash and do their own thing rather than pose with humans in the river.

Title: Amazing experience
Text: Came here with my partner and our three youngest.  Firstly, it was enlightening to read the information at the entrance regarding the welfare of the animals, apart from which they had such vast grounds to roam in and the wonderful river to bathe in.  We only saw two elephants with chains on their ankles, but the reason for this was explained - apart from this all the elephants seemed well cared for and had plenty of freedom.  Watching them frolicking in the river was awesome and provided excellent photo opportunities. We then all had to stand back whilst they walked back up the road the the other area.  We spent ages in awe just watching them walking around and the babies playing and then moved on to the feeding area.  We were too late to purchase a milk bottle, but, that being said we were able to purchase some fruit to feed to them - what an amazing experience for the children.  I firmly believe that this orphanage works to help elephants and I am unsure as to why some people have a different view.  A wonderful day was had by all!

Title: From Colombo 2.5hrs ride and 10 minutes of Elephant ride * Worth the travel
Text:
I have visited this Orphanage 2 weeks ago (May 2018)

The tour bus took us from our hotel in Main Colombo and ride took about 2hr-2.5hrs.

We have visited the Elephant place for 20minutes and 10min elephant riding. 

There are about 8-10 elephants and you take turns with 2 people riding the elephant at the same time. 

There is a river and you can bath the elephants in cool water. 

Also can make some shoping to donate/help the orphange.  

Once in a life time thing to do while in Colombo

Title: Well worth it
Text: The Elephant orphanage was on out list to do, but with a little nervousness due to the varying reports. However these nerves were soon dissipated, as you enter the orphanage there are education boards which clearly explain the facility, the elephants and the people, take time to read and understand them. The Elephants are clearly happy, well looked after but still a wild animal and hence the need for some control. The feeding is a true privilege and but make sure you get your ticket as obviously feeding is controlled to prevent them being over fed. A great mornings visit to visit these wonderful creatures.

Title: A Bucket List Experience
Text: Im so grateful that friends told us about the orphanage. We watched all of them lumber across the street down to the river for their afternoon romp and soak. Closely monitored by their handlers, who called to them in the water and helped bathe them in the mist of their hoses, this massive herd was thrilling to watch. We also got to ride one. If youre coming from Colombo, I recommend ordering a car to take you. Pick up some buttery cashews on the way. Theres also the very interesting Luck Uyana Herbal Medicines Garden nearby that is worthy of a visit.

Title: loved it
Text: brilliant visit, watching elephants being bottle fed and seeing them playing about , didn't have time to watch bath time

Title: See the Elephants in their habitat
Text: Get up close and personal to the Elephants, watch them bathe and if you want you can help wash them. You can follow them throughout the day if you wish. Great vantage point by the river, there is a well located cafe and its a delight to have a coffee and literally the elephants are a few feet away. Buy some food for them and they will stop and grab it from you, great fun.

Title: They really help the turtles
Text: A place where they really help turtles. You can see them hatching and even release some. You can also see some turtles recovering. Entrance is 2000 per person. See it as an donation.

Title: Avoid this place
Text: I visited with my two children. The lady seemed mostly interested in collecting the money for the entrance ticket. While she did explain about the turtles that were there, overall, I still felt that they were primarily focused on making money from tourists. Some locals also warned us that these centers are appearing all over the coast now with dubious missions.

Title: Loving family work
Text: Love this family, what they doing. They doing all just from the donations. Thank you for the perfect day. Must have to see it, have to be on the bucketlist.

Title: Place To Avoid
Text: This sea turtle hatchery centre is a worrying concept. While I accept that there will always be those turtles that require help and assistance due to injury or birth defects, this place appears to be more of a sordid tourist attraction whose primary aim is to make money.  The entrance fee is 2000 Sri Lankan rupees,  and upon entry, the poor turtles are kept in small, unclean tanks, swimming aimlessly around in circles.  Yes, they are cute and are such beautiful animals,  but I do not believe that they are truly cared for or treated with love and affection. I believe that this was once a genuine going concern,  but now has simply become a way to make human' s money at the expense of these serene animals.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS, if you genuinely care for wildlife. This is simply a zoo. DISGUSTING!

Title: Emma and Paul
Text: Brilliant work done here. New hatchlings  and rehabilitation of turtles that have been injured by boats or sharks, also by eating plastic. Go visit and donate!!

Title: A visit is warmly recommended to all turtle-lovers.
Text:
Very interesting, very friendly staff, you get a lot of information about the turtles, their behaviour, reproduction etc. and about the work of the sanctuary. Great work.
Impressive animals!
A visit is highly recommended!

Title: Great place to support when in Galle
Text: Great experience, they are doing a great job looking after the turtles! Well done to them all ??????

Title: Turtle rehabilitation
Text:
The kindest and most selfless people doing fabulous work!

PLEASE BE AWARE - If you get a TUKTUK to this place some of the drivers are less than trustworthy!!!!
Some demand the turtle charity give them cash as payment for bringing them visitors. When in actual fact it was ourselves that asked to be taken there - NOT a recommendation by them. 
PLEASE make the sanctuary aware when you arrive that you have some off your own accord from trip advisor/word of mouth/read about it etc so they do not have to believe lies from tuktuk drivers and feel forced to pay them a snip!!!!

Title: DO NOT VISIT THIS PLACE !!! GREEDY WOMAN !
Text: Hi ! This place is TERRIBLE !! these people are greedy for money and scammers, they only care about money and the woman owner is very rude and always asking me for money !! DO NOT VISIT THIS PLACE ! The daughter also making fake comments on this site and giving 5 stars, these people are greedy for money only... they dont care about the turtles and the place was very dirty.

Title: Turtle rescue
Text: This is a great little turtle rescue and hatchery about ten minutes ride by Tuk-Tuk from Galle fort. There's a small entrance fee, all of which goes to supporting the hatchery. Once inside, the owner will show you around and explain what the hatchery does - they rescue injured turtles and nurse them back to full health before being released back into the ocean, or if they are maimed they'll be homed there. Then there's the hatchery which rescues vulnerable egg nests and hatch them in a safe environment. The baby turtles are then raised and released into the sea. You'll get the opportunity to handle the baby turtles - so cute. It's a really small establishment doing great work, so visit if you can.

Title: Small but definitely worthwhile
Text:
Just a short ride (5-10 minutes in a tuk-tuk) from Galle Fortress, this hatchery is well worth a visit. It isn't big but it's a pleasant, nearby excursion and you can be sure that your entrance fee/donation is going to a good cause.

You can handle the smaller turtles, and the owner will happily show you around & tell you about the conservation work she does.

Honestly, 20-30 minutes is sufficient - our tuk-tuk driver said that he was happy to wait for us & take us back.

Title: Baldr Help
Text: Great mission. Great place. Turtle Rescue. Similar to Gumbo Limbo in Boac Raton, Florida. The work they are doing is wonderful.  They rely heavily on outside donations.  The tanks are all split between healthy ready to release on down to newly arrived with injuries.

Title: The love they give to this turtles just unbelievable
Text: Everyone need come to see this place and see how beauty this creatures are and how well they treat them before release them. Humble people!!

Title: Nice Staff
Text: Great place to visit. The staff are very friendly and knowledgeable. They're doing an amazing cause for the sea turtles.

Title: Peaceful and Relaxing Place
Text:
The owner is really well informed and has full knowledge about Turtles and their types. Has dedicated his life and soul to save these species.
If you wanna have a quiet and peaceful evening by the beach, then this is the place to be.

Title: Turtle Rescues are REAL!
Text: Such a nice thing the owner here is doing by helping the disabled turtles to heal and get back out to the sea! :) :) :)

Title: Not recommended
Text: Be careful some people may trick you. Ask to extra money unnecessarily.  Do not give money to film. Good places doesn't ask extra money.

Title: DO NOT GO !
Text: Money hungry greedy woman manage this place and all she cares about scamming people off. Do not go there. Not worth it !!!

Title: Don't go
Text:
Foreigners don't go. For locals ok i think. Still not sure though. 
The donation amount they expect hmm just don't go.

Title: This place is amazing
Text: Love the work done here. What an experience to come and check out the turtles, and learn a lot I did not know.

Title: Harald Baldr
Text: This place looks amazing! I'm looking forward to seeing the turtles released back into the ocean! Thank you!

Title: Amazing wildlife rehab center
Text: This place rehabs sea turtles. Simply amazing. They show great love and respect for these creatures. Highly recommended.

Title: love the experience
Text: thank you so much for your service it was one of my best experiences ever .. especially when I saw the first time the baby turtle swimming .. thanks again

Title: Amazing Turtle Sanctuary
Text: It is wonderful that there are people who dedicate themselves to looking after vulnerable creatures. This is an extraordinary sanctuary for baby and injured turtles. Definitely worth visiting and supporting.

Title: Amazing! Such a good deed
Text:
Incredible place. This guy helps turtles. He hatches them and returns them and also helps injured turtles.

10/10 recommend.

Title: Looks great
Text: HARALD form Youtube SENT ME ?????? I mean from the videos it seems like a pretty awesome place, good work I look forward to seeing Haralds donation

Title: Wonderful
Text: A very wonderful project by a wonderful owner! An absolute must-visit if you ask me, save the beautiful nature by donating a dollar or two??.

Title: Amazing Place
Text: The Guy there was very friendly, Great service from him. And once you go there youll get a different type of love for these creatures. Amazing place. Id go there again for sure.

Title: Very Good People
Text: These are very good people dedicating their life to saving amazing animals. This kind of work takes a special person to run and dedicate their life too.... These are some amazing creatures and this place is a great place to understand these animals!!! Superb!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Title: Thank you
Text: I saw this establishment on Harald Balbr's YouTube channel. Thank you for helping the  sea turtles and sea turtle eggs ????

Title: Recommended
Text: Very nice place cheap prices and a very infesting and entertaining place to go with family and even by yourself

Title: Worthy of your Support
Text: This guy knows his stuff and is making so much good out of so little.  Sea turtles are having a rough time in the ocean without getting help like they do here.

Title: Important work
Text: This is a very important place for turtles to have if they are hurt and need medical attention, and its very important to take care of these beautiful creatures!

Title: Support this guy and his good cause
Text: This guy saves turtle eggs from people collecting them to eat, hatches them and returns them to the wild. Also saves injured ones and nurses them back to health. Small but well worth while if you are interested in wildlife. We were able to return in the evening and return hatchlings into the sea. A memory to saver.

Title: Amazing!!
Text: Stopped by the hatchery today and it was a wonderful experience! Small place, but so unique. You can tell they really care for the turtles and its so lovely to be so close to them! Would recommend.

Title: Great short visit
Text: Lovely quick stop during visiting Galle. This place is held together by the big heart of lovely lady taking care of hurt or ill turtles (even injured monkey by the time of this review). You can get information about challenges that turtles in Sri Lanka have to go through and pet turtles. The entry fee is 1000 lark/person which is fair considering the costs of the hatchery. Be careful of some tuktuk drivers that will tell you to not go here and will want to take you elsewhere as the lady of this hatchery refuse to give them any commission for taking you there.

Title: Turtle hospital and hatchery
Text: Really nice place to visit, if you are near. The lady doctor is absolutely kind and helpful for visitors and turtles. You can see the spark in her eyes and love for turtles. You can pet some turtles and they love it! :) Majestic dinosaurs??

Title: Short visit after Galle Old Town
Text:
Excellent place for short visit to understand a bit about turtles and the challenges they face. 
Injured turtles brought in by fishermen. They are cared for and returned to the ocean if possible. 
We also saw babies only a day old.

Note: the tuk tuk drivers try to get a commission from every place they take you. The lady here refuses to.pay them so they try to take you to a bigger commercial hatchery.

Title: A good display
Text: He guys at the turtle farm actively try and help the various turtle species survive. The either rescue and look after damaged animals or gather eggs, hatch, grow and release the babies. Well worth a visit

Title: A nice visit to turtle farm
Text: We enjoyed and learned about the sea turtles. There were few turtles of different age in ponds. It was a great experience..

Title: Fascinating short visit
Text: Well worth stopping off en route . A chance to learn a bit more about turtles and to make a donation to help a worthwhile project

Title: Turtle rescue centre and hatchery, great job!
Text:
Great work done by the team here. It's a small family run place and it's can't be easy to rescue them and search for eggs.
Was sad to see the injured ones who can't be re-released into the wild, but the work these guys do releasing the healthy grown ones who've been caught in nets, etc and the hatchlings is great. They chip them too for further monitering which is good too.

Title: Good work for turtles
Text: We visited the turtle hatchery in the morning and really enjoyed it. The organisation is doing a good job taking care of turtles injured by fishing boats. We went back at 5 in the afternoon to give a hand with feeding the turtles.

Title: Baby Turtles!!
Text: Went to this on the way back from another excursion but have to say I was pleasantly surprised. They do great work helping injured turtles and have a number there that you can see. The main highlights were getting to hold one of the baby turtles and then releasing one out into the ocean. Definitely worth a trip

Title: Quick Visit
Text: Found this quite interesting as it tells you about the different species of turtles found in Sri Lanka and how they have created a safe habitat come hospital for them.

Title: small but significant
Text:
A lovely place run by a family that are clearly passionate about saving the turtle population and rescuing turtles that have been injured. 

It's quite small/basic but they do very important work and it's amazing to see turtles close up. It's a 25 min walk or a 10 min tuk tuk ride away from Galle so very easy to get to and I would recommend it to anyone staying in Galle

Title: Please, don't take a tuk to get here!
Text:
I made a mistake when took a tuk here.. It turned out that tuk driver wants a commission and occasionally started fighting with us because we didn't want to pay more!
Please, go on foot or take a bus if you want to come here.
Excellent experience besides that )

Title: Great visit
Text: We visited the turtle sanctuary in a rainy afternoon in Galle. We were so pleased to see the amazing work.being done here, looking after injured turtles and helping with breeding programmes. We had a young girl as our guide who was very helpful and knowledgeable, she happily answered all our questions. We were able to see the 5 different turtle types that live in the waters of Sri Lanka. They all seemed to be living in great conditions before their release. It seems like vets visit very frequently to check on them, plan release dates etc. I would really recommend visiting and supporting their great cause.

Title: Not happy with the way the animals are treated ..
Text:
Animals are in pens and cages far too small for them ...The large pig they have there is living a miserable existence in a pen that he cannot even turn around in ..it has no gate to allow him to be let out for exercise and they hog tie him occasionally to exercise him and it is evident with the rope imprint marks left on his legs ..poor beast.
I do Not recommend visiting this place as the more people who pay the more cruelty these poor animals will have to endure.The only food ALL of the animals eat is paw paw fruit.Really not a suitable food for all of them ..some maybe but not all of them .

Title: An Old Lady and her Tantrums!
Text:
Our tuk tuk driver took us to this turtle farm He had told us that they will charge LKR 500 per head. The lady who was in charge of the farm said she will take LKR 1000 per person. Later agreed for LKR 500! But when I took out the camera, she threw a fit and said we cannot shoot in her premises, She asked us to get out of her place. Again, she was abusing Indians!
They were no boards or signs indicating the cost of entry tickets or rules. Strange!
The lady needs serious mental treatment! Avoid this place and head towards Koggala, if you want to visit a professionally run turtle farm.

Title: interesting for a short stop
Text: The Sea Turtle Farm is on the mainroad Merissa-Galle. It shelters disabled sea turtles of all kind. Some ate plastic, some were trapped in fishermans nets and have amputated limbs. It is an edjucating short stop.

Very nice sanctuary, everything there is for the turtles, and appears to be more of a charity than a tourist trap. Before we went, we read that it was 500 rupees each, but when we arrived discovered it was 1000 rupees (around £4.50-£5.00). It was very small so seemed expensive, however, with the amount they do for these animals, medication and operations, just to get them out into the sea again, it makes it all much worth while. We were also able to hold the baby turtles, and a couple of the medium sized ones. So all in all, excellent place to visit. The girl who took us round was very knowledgable about all the turtles.

Title: Total Turtle.
Text: An excellent tour of the Sea Turtle Hatchery. With turtles living up to 120 years old there were turtles two days old and others 40 years old to see. Also many eggs still to be hatched (hopefully). Only disappointment was that we didnt release turtles into the sea. I guess that is just a timing issue. Well worth a visit for this great cause when you are in Galle.

Title: Amazing
Text: This guy is doing an amazing job! Please support him, he is protecting our nature and beautiful animals!

Title: This farm is a MUST SEE in Galle!
Text: Amazing place, the guys are going a great and important job rescuing these cute wild turtles! This place is a MUST VISIT in Galle, I highly recommend it!

Title: Relaxing time ????
Text: Best ever experience with my friends . We went there as a change of pace of our workload. Had a very relaxing time with sea turtles ??

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
I would highly recommend that you visit here while in the area of Galle. 
They do amazing work to look after injured and unwell sea turtles before releasing them back into the wild.

Title: Very nice visit
Text: from Jersey, Channel Islands. we visited the turtle hatchery and was welcomed by the friendly staff. They explained how they look after the turtles and release the babies into the sea. We saw some babies that had just been hatched last night. Definitely recommend visiting if you are in Sri Lanka.

Title: Caring for the sick turtles
Text: This place is amazing. They really seemed to care about the sick turtles they had rescued. They also have hatchlings and invited us to help set them off back into the ocean. Its right on the beach and I felt very humbled to be able to visit.

Title: Lovely sanctuary
Text: This is a small but wonderfully caring turtle sanctuary. They look after injured turtles and release them once they are recovered, some are not lucky enough to be released but they are still looked after. You can pay 500LKR and release a baby turtle into the ocean which is a lovely experience. Would highly recommend this place.

Title: Real care and concern for turtle welfare
Text:
The work they do here is amazing. With no real funding other than donations and voluntary help they care for turtles injured in nets, propeller blades even oil from ships. As well as nurturing newly laid eggs to give them a better chance of survival, the centre run an active care and release program giving as many turtles as possible a chance to be returned to their natural habitat.

I would throughly recommend stopping off and hearing their stories. Ive experienced turtle farms/sanctuaries before but not one as genuine and committed as this.

Title: Great Place to Visit
Text:
A really great place to come and see, a genuine charity/sanctuary where they are caring for ill/injured turtles and trying to nurse them back to full health. Very knowledgeable team 

Apparently on some days you can help to release babies, on the day we visited they had just hatched the day before so were in a separate little pond

Charged 1500lkr per person, and we got a tuktuk from the fort for 400lkr each way

Title: Pretty amazing experience!
Text: We enjoyed this little place ??  the stuff was really nice & friendly and delivered a lot of interesting informations. We paid 1000 rs/person to enter and we also had the chance to release some baby turtles into the ocean. (1000 rs/baby turtle). It was soooo sweeet!!

Title: Nice little place
Text: I Saw lots of turtels in differnt adges.   There where eggs in the sand and a sign on hos many eggs there were and When They wood come up and be Ready to go to the sea. There where also Big and grownup turtels.

Title: just amazing
Text: well worth a trip and dont forget to call in the gift shop as all funds go to help the centre so any help they get is appreciated as government does not support

Title: Such a good cause
Text: Its great to see that these guys are trying to do their best to protect sea turtles! They were caring for some injured turtles (through fishing and boating accidents) and also taking care of some eggs that had been laid! We all need to make sure people are educated about the importance of protecting and caring for sea turtles!! Thank you for your work!

Title: Turtle Farm
Text: Ran by volunteers to look after turtles brought to them by local fishermen. Well worth a visit. Entry was 1000SRP each and we had an informative walk round. This will only take about 30 minutes or longer if you are have to hang around. A great cause that needs support.

Title: Good conversation
Text: Good work being done to preserve these wonderful creatures but I did had a concern about some older ones that we kept and would never be released because of injury. The tanks were small.

Title: THIS PLACE HAS A BAD FEEL
Text: The woman who took our money and showed us around was strange. There was no price advertised to go in and it seems she charges different prices for people from differing parts of the world. She was keen to get people to handle the two day old babies, which seemed wrong and she invited me to put my hand into a tank without saying why and a turtle came and bit it. She thought this was hilarious and said "sorry". I said you are clearly not sorry, you enjoyed doing that. I am sure there are better places to give your money to. Our guide had the same feeling about the place and will no longer bring tourists here.

Title: Interesting
Text:
Visited a few days ago
Staff sounded knowledgeable..tanks were very small but relatively clean.
We were shown a "handicapped" turtle which basically was bobbing up and down in its tank..I personally think this is a feature and should be euthanized.

Title: So adorable !
Text:
It is such a unique experience, first time to see and hold the sea turtles, they are such beautiful animals, especially when they look at you with those adorable dark eyes. The baby ones generally 2-5days old are the cutest, it was so much fun to watch them swim , you have to see them ! Try to support the neck when you hold one.
The ticket costs 1000Rps, I think it is well-worthy, appreciate the idea of protecting and appreciate what they do.

Title: Release a baby!
Text:
Worth doing your bit for the world and nature! Released a baby turtle in to the sea and feel good about yourself! 
Interesting place

Title: Place worth a visit
Text:
I have visited this place with my husband on Sunday morning and we were the only guests. The family that owns the place seemed to be kind to the turtles. They said they take care of the ones that get injured in the sea, are attacked by the sharks, eat plastic items from the ocean... It's mainly the fishermen who bring the injured turtles to them. We felt like it was something worth seeing and reflecting upon. 
And, of course, this is not about good customer service or visitor's satisfaction, so I suggest not to expect anything extraordinary in regards to this.
The board is visible from the main road, so the place is not hard to find. The price is 1000 rupees per person.

Title: GREAT
Text: Great place to experience the lifecycle of a turtle. The guide at this place fills you up with superb information about them

Title: A must place visit
Text: If you are in the Galle area this is a must visit it is a fantastic place to come and see what these people are do for the turtles . Not sure if you should be holding some of them but i guess its all part of the experience

Title: Great work done by locals
Text:
A must visit when in Galle. Dont take a tuk tuk but go by bus or walking so all your money goes towards a good cause and isn't shared with the tuk tuk driver.

We need more rescue efforts for marine life and wildlife. They also welcome kids to volunteer and its a great experience.

Title: Place where hurt turtles gets help
Text:
Very important thing is to come here by yourself, not with tour or tuk-tuk!
Come by walk, by bus or by bike. 
Otherwise owners must pay 50% to someone who bring you there.
Such places run by money support from people and organizations so make a donation.
For 1000 rupees donation you can visit this place to know about what is happening with turtles which were hurt by boats, sharks, plastic (!) or some illness.

Title: Great hatchery
Text: Nice little hatchery. Animals are being well looked after . Good explanation of the different types of turtles they have and the process of returning them back to their natural habitat. Would recommend if in the area .

Title: Turtle rescue
Text: This turtle rescue centre is run by volunteers. Although illegal, poachers steal turtle eggs as the turtles come ashore to lay them. The rescue centre uses some of the money from visitor fees to buy these eggs, immediately rebury them in the sand in a protected area and let them hatch naturally. If they hatch after dark they can go straight out to sea, but if they hatch during daylight there are so many predators that the babies are placed in sea water tanks and released to the sea after dark. The rescue centre also houses some turtles that have been born with deformities or have lost limbs in fishing nets and would perish at sea. I have mixed feelings about the ethics of paying poachers for eggs but if poaching can not be properly policed I suppose this is the best outcome to protect the species.

Title: Amazing day  with turtles??
Text:
It was an amazing day at the turtles Farm. It is a center of saving turtles. Here you can see a small turtles that are just born and also old turtles, which was attacked by speed boats or by fisherman...also one turtle is there because of the plastic in the ocean. The stories are too sad, but we can help to this beautiful turtles.
At this farm they are support by doctors and will go in the ocean soon. 
The owners of the farm are very kind and friendly people. 
It is the place that must be visited. Please go this turtles farm , you will be full of emotions.

Title: 500 LKR per person -totally worth it
Text:
This is a nice place ..there are many ?? turtle hatchery out there in Galle , hikkadua  there are a lot of types of sea turtles ..the best thing is they are treating the handicap turtles.. which got hurt due to fishing net
It was very informative..my kids loved it.. also you can hold the turtles in your hand

Title: Turtle hospital
Text: I enjoyed the story behind the turtle sanctuary and turtles were incredible who survived injuries which as happened to them

Title: Great stop on the south coast - conservation at work
Text: Stopped here on the suggestion of our driver. We thought it was great. Some larger turtles that were being rehabilitated and lots of baby turtles. Our guide was really informative and clearly enjoyed his job. They even let you hold the turtles (the ones that dont bite!).

Title: Great little spot
Text: Lovely staff and a real passion for sea turtles and conservation - very kind and helpful. Lots of varieties of different ages being rehabilitated or prepared for release to the wild.

Title: Worth every cent
Text: It cost $10 AUD to get, this is a country with no welfare system so they have to live while do amazing conservation work with Turtles, while we were there twice a Goanna came in looking for eggs, if it wasn't for these people the Gonna would go along the beach, dig up the nest and eat the eggs, I don't understand why people would have a problem with a small entry fee for something so good.

Title: Turtles up close
Text:
The Turtle Hatchery is worth a visit. It's around a 5 minute drive from the Old Dutch Fort. 
The Hatchery collects and hatches turtle eggs - there was some freshly hatched turtles the day we went there.
The Hatchery also cares for and rehabilitates injured turtles. There was several turtles there that had been treated for a range of injuries from fish nets and hooks to swallowing plastic bags. Once well again the turtles are released back to the sea.
You can see several different breeds of turtle here. I had no idea how beautiful turtle shells could be.
We worth a visit.

Title: But long Winded but Interesting
Text: Bit pricey for entrance fee for what there is to see. Young man gave a very long detailed explanation, but we felt the length of the blurb was to make up for the fee. I tipped him so we could get going. They are doing a great job of protecting the local turtle species and good on them. Maybe weve seen too many turtle hatcheries in our lifetime already.

Title: Great place to visit
Text: We visited the turtle farm and it was great to see how they are preserving nature and the wonderful turtles. They also care for injured turtles and then release them when they have recovered. You even get to hold a baby turtle, a great experience!!

Title: Feels dodgy
Text:
When this was advertised as a conservation effort I was excited. I have had some great experiences with turtles in the wild. They are amazing, intelligent, beautiful animals. I paid the 500 rupee entrance fee and was immediately disappointed after walking in. They had large turtles alone in very small tanks (about the size of a single bed), these poor creatures were lifted out of the tank and passed around for each tour group that went through (about 5-10 mins apart).  A couple were obviously injured and I do believe that they wouldn't have survived in the wild, but I'm not convinced that their current circumstances are necessarily preferable. One (which didn't have any obvious injury) was showing signs of distress and biting the edge of the concrete tank. There were chunks missing from a few places of the tank, so she'd obviously been at it for a while despite the fact that we were told she was only there temporarily.

The baby turtles were listless, but I don't think I saw any dead ones. They have a hatchery at the back of the compound which is ostensibly the main part of the conservation effort. They pay locals to bring them eggs from the beach so that they can incubate and hatch away from predators (dogs and birds). I'm sure it has nothing to do with the 1000 rupees they can charge tourists to release a baby into the wild. 

The guide was knowledgeable and friendly enough. When asked whether the centre was involved in any conservation research or formal programs the answer was no.

Overall I was extremely disappointed and feel very guilty for giving my money to this business. I thought long and hard about writing this review because it may be that there is a genuine desire to perform some conservation efforts, however the more i think about it the more sinister it seems.

If you are genuinely interested in turtles, I'd advise you to take your chances and go on one of the may dive/snorkelling tours that are available in southern Sri Lanka. If you just want to see a turtle and have no concern for it's welfare, then this will fulfil your needs

Title: Don't go.
Text: We visited and whilst they do help some of the turtles and release, the're are ones they can't which are stuck in a tiny area all day and are lifted in and out of the water for tourists all day which is cruel.  The water is dirty u could barely see the turtles in there and they say you can part their shell etc but that's just not nice for a title. They also breed them. Ruined my day and i don't reccomend going. This was just after i saw an elephant chained to a tree too.

Title: Sea turtles of all stages of life
Text: 4 of the 7 existing species of sea turtles in the world can be found here. There are infant turtles, babies several months old, 2-3 year-olds as well as one that's close to 60 years, and of course a hatchery with 1000s of eggs. This is run by a poor family who manages everything with the donations that they receive, in addition to the entrance fee which was Rs. 200 for a local adult. A very humbling experience to see injured turtles whose flippers have been either cut-off or badly damaged after getting caught up in fishing nets. If you want to learn about turtle conservation or just like animals in general, this is a must visit if you're around Galle (it's a 10-minute drive from the city center).

Title: Lovely Experience
Text:
We really enjoyed our experience here but its not donations as some have made out, its 500 rupee per person for foreigners and then you are obliged to tip the volunteer who shows you around. So dont think its donations or free...

It was a lovely experience, we felt they were genuine and werent exploiting the turtles as some have made out in other reviews. These turtles were genuinely missing fins, injured etc and were being helped and given medicine.

It is however a very short trip, we were there about 30mins. We didnt travel far, only from Galle Fort as we are staying within the walls. But Im not sure I would have wanted to have travelled for a long time for that experience. So I recommend doing if youre passing through or close by, but otherwise find one somewhere else. Not worth travelling hours to visit.

Title: Don't go
Text: These places do not help protect turtles only to exploit tourist curiosity and cash. Don't go you help turtles more by not patronising them

Title: Very rewarding!
Text: Very touching visit to see injured and infant turtles. The carers are very inspirational. Highly recommend! And leave a donation!

Title: Excellent donation only farm
Text: Run by a young family with very little money who rely on donations or voluntary work for the upkeep of the farm. Worth every minute of the visit and please donate big

Title: small but doing good work
Text: I am happy to see that injured sea turtles and eggs are being protected here.  The farm itself is very small and would not take more than 5-10 minutes to take some photos and linger.  A good cause though to support.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Interesting and informative visit as part of tour group. Do not need to spend much time here. Suitable for children who would enjoy handling the baby turtles.

Title: Great learning experience
Text:
Our family and a large group of friends with children aged between 6 and 13 years visited the hatchery and sanctuary. 
We were warmly received by the team caring for the turtles and then had the privilege to see a number of different species. 
The team assisting us was friendly and helpful and answered all the questions patiently. We were there just before sunset and were even allowed to spend the last few minutes on their beautiful beach, watching the final rays of sunlight dipping into the ocean.

Title: A Very Worthwhile Cause
Text:
This is a small centre, but doing valuable work.  It was explained to us during our visit that unfortunately the stray dogs (you will have seen many if you have been in Sri Lanka for any length of time) dig up the turtle eggs on the beach. So collecting the eggs before this catastrophe occurs and hatching them at this centre ensures that a higher number reach the sea to take their chance at survival.

There are also a number of adult turtles of the major species found here, which are looked after having been injured in various ways.

It is good to be able to see these wonderful creatures up close and make a small contribution to their protection.

Title: Great experience
Text: We had a very lovely visit to this quaint Turtle Hatchery. Small but good hatchery whose owners are doing great work. Explanation and tour for visitors is great they were very knowledgeable and informative about the turtles,Worth a 30 min visit 1500 roupee to release baby turtles in the ocean at sunset. But it's really lovely I'll go back before I leave

Title: Keep up the good work
Text:
We were welcomed by the family and paid 500LKR for the entrance. The owner told us about the different species of turtles and showed them
If you come there around 8 a.m. And 6p.m. they get feed.
It looks like the turtles are treated very well. Some of them just had a surgery, but they were doing great.
It is not a big place, but it's nice to see little and big turtles and their eggs.

Title: Brilliant and exciting
Text: Small place but with several rescued injured turtles and active in protecting and releasing baby turtles. Good information and ability to hold a turtle

Title: Great experience
Text: At first we thought it would be your typical roam around turtle hatchery/sanctuary but it wasnt! This place is run by a very nice and hospitable family. They educated us about the different types of turtles.  They are very passionate about saving turtles that have missing fins due to shark attacks and to those who needed surgery due to swallowing plastics. They also protect the turtle eggs. Once they hatch and are ready to go back to the sea, they set them free. We waited til it was feeding time 5/5:30ish and we got the opportunity to feed them under supervision. We got to hold them and transfer them from one tank to the other. The entry fee is quite pricey for a small place but they say its for medication for the turtles and payment for surgery. The male owner showed us a photo of him on the newspaper setting the turtles free and that he has written a book about his love for turtles. He targets to educate younger children in schools. Be careful as some tuktuk drivers from galle fort told us that this place was closed due to holidays etc but what they were trying to do was to bring us to the furthest sanctuary so they get more money. The place was only few minutes away from the fort. The owner also drives a tuktuk who brought us back to our next destination charging us with local price.

Title: Fulfilling experience
Text: We traveled as a small group of 14 for a school trip from Dubai and the students spent all of their time caring for the turtles here. Our mission is to bring awareness of human impact on the decreasing population of the sea turtles and our time here was one of the most memorable experiences I've ever had. Speaking for all the adults and students involved, we couldn't have asked for a better experience. The owner and his wife are very hospitable and while I've read other reviews regarding her (Nisha's) "bad attitude", I am assuming these tourist were expecting these wonderful people to conform from their cultural norm to fit into what they think is an "acceptable attitude". Nisha (wife of the owner) is a loving mother and wife and her personality is what makes her such fun to be around. They don't expect much and considering they are running this organization out of their home and allowing strangers to visit with no government funding, I'd say a small donation box at the front of the gate is not asking too much.

Title: Turtles
Text: There are number of small turtle hutcheries bear galle. These people working on saving sea turtles. This is a nice quick stop over to enjoy with baby turtles

Title: A TURTLE HAVEN.
Text: Very informative staff who seemed passionate about the creatures in their charge. The title of turtle farm may seem a bit misleading as it is a hatchery and haven for sick and injured turtles.

Title: Fascinating and informative
Text: A brief stop on our way out of Galle was well worthwhile to see the variety of turtles and to learn of their life cycles. The injured ones were being well cared for and the knowledgable guide painstakingly answered all the questions we asked of him.

Title: A quick tour
Text: This is a small turtle sanctuary and a guide will walk you through the process of turtlevcarecand breeding in an effort to sustain turtle numbers. A great half hour and well worth the reasonableventry fee

Title: Great to see their conservation efforts
Text: The sea turtle farm is a conservation project for injured turtles and their main objective is to care the turtles back to health and release them into the ocean once they are fit. They have about 4-5 different kinds of turtles and they have guides who explain things when you visit.

Title: Children loved it
Text: A bit wary that the farm was a tourist attraction and money making exercise rather than a conservation area. A prefer to lean on the side that they genuinely care for the turtles. Most of the larges turtles were obviously injured, ie shark had bitten off limbs and other were said to have viruses, so were receiving antibiotics. When asked about releasing back into the sea they seem to have a definite programme, timescale. Would recommend.

Title: Worth visit despite guide disinterest
