(3) Seems to be very random if they open their "cafe" which is just a basic coffee tea facility (when we visited midday it was "closed" and no reason given)
(4) Guide takes you up - they really need to get this better - our guide spoke virtually no english except single words "spider" "snake" etc - if they can't speak the language a guide book in a different language saying what you see would be really beneficial to take with them.  (seems we just sadly got the wrong guide as other reviews say many are excellent)
(5) Admission fee reasonable no objection to paying.
(6) Guide didn't warn us about leeches.   The tourist "centre" if you can call it that sells leechproof socks.  Buy them and put them on.  We discovered that they don't just live in water and will drop from trees or leaves onto to the ground or you if they sense a chance at a blood meal - so put full covering on legs and top.   If you do get bitten it is harmless just a nibble pain and then you will bleed for a while but stops - you will not die :)
(7) We saw snakes, reptiles, monkeys, spiders, all sorts so very worthwhile.
(8) Suggestion bring tea, coffee, drinks, snacks etc as could find there is nothing at the tourist centre on arrival or after.   Busy time is mornings when tour buses arrive lunchtime less so.  Best time to see birds are morning trips but plenty of other stuff on view other times!

Title: Nice, if you bring leech socks
Text:
-We booked the 10h Tour to the Lions Rock directly at our hotel (Sinharaja Rain Forest View Villas) and paid $95 for 2 people including a lunch packet. From what I could find in the internet it seemed like a fair price. I think it was $65 for 2 people for the 6h Waterfall tour.
- we asked for a guide that spoke good English. Thank God we did, because I don't know who were would have gotten otherwise. Our guide "spoke English", but hardly understood anything
- we felt that our guides (we had 2, one who "talked" to us and one who did the guiding) weren't really prepared for the job. He didn't check with us, if we had enough water, the right clothes and when we came across a snake that be hadn't spotted before he got really worried and has quite a panicky look on his face. I don't want to think about what would have happened, had we been bitten!! I don't think they could have helped us. 
- leeches in abundance!!! We knew there would be leeches and we had them before, but not like this. We would have enjoyed the tour a lot more, had we had leech socks. 
-the tour was challenging and we were glad when the guiding guide offered to take our backpack (and we're both not unfit). The way was maybe too challenging to enjoy the scenery and you had to watch your every step, make sure you don't get sucked dry by the leeches when you stopped. 

In hindsight the 6h Tour might have been the nicer, if more "touristy" option. 
And it very much depends on your guide, which we couldn't really influence :-(

Title: I wish I knew the name of our guide!
Text: Shortly, we'll be uploading the photo of our guide. We can't remember his name but he was incredible. He was so sweet, friendly, helpful, knowledgeable and willing to show us the best of Sinharaja! We learnt so much along our way but I won't put too much on here as it's great to learn as you go. He asked us if we wanted to go on a long walk uphill. We was exhausted when we finished but we got to the highest point of Sinharaja on top of a mountain and the view at the top was spectatular. A once in a lifetime sort of view. Besides this, we saw so many animals, plants and insects. Our guide was very funny too as we had a little giggle as we struggled up the mountain and he hopped up as if it was the easiest thing ever! He was a little shocked to learn we didn't walk hills most of the time! It was something so normal to him. He showed us how to drink the river walk which we did (reluctantly) but don't be scared as the water was so fresh and cold and I couldn't quite believe it wasn't half frozen bottled water as it tasted so nice. This was one of our best days in Sri Lanka and I think this was definitely because of the staff as well as the beautiful things Sinharaja has to offer. You have to visit this place! You'll miss out if you don't go!

Title: Interesting 3 hours in the rain forest
Text:
A couple of previous reviewers have referred to this as 'rainforest lite' and that would probably be a fair description. However, that is not necessarily a bad thing. The paths are well made and mostly flat and make for relatively easy walking. We booked an official park guide to take us round and he was very good at spotting many small reptiles, birds and insects. Don't expect to spot much in the way of furry animals here though other than a few monkeys. We were lucky enough to see a couple of large groups of purple faced monkeys at quite close quarters which was fantastic. We had hoped to see the waterfalls we had read about but it seems we had entered the park at the wrong entrance - due to the fact that our driver had never been here before and did not know to take us to the Galle entrance. 
Doesn't compare with some more unspoilt tropical rainforests but enjoy it for what it is - an enjoyable 3 hour walk in some beautiful scenery.

Title: Disappointing visit to a wonderful place
Text: This forest is a wonderful place, a beautiful tropical forest, quite some interesting animals and a beautiful waterfall. However, it was very disappointing that there is no fixed prices, that there is motorbikes driving in the forest all the time (in order to reach a village nearby), there is dogs that the guides do not try to keep out and our guide was smoking the whole tour. It doesn't seem like they take very good care of this incredible place, and that is very sad.

Title: Interesting walk
Text: Interesting 2-4h walk, particularly if you have not walked in a tropical forest before. The paths are made partially of cement slabs and rocks, and are well market throughout. Some parts are not suitable for disabled people, but good for children. The sight of elephant tracks (and dung) make it exciting for the children. If you use a guide, dont expect great naturalist or linguistic skills, but they have a trained eye for interesting plants and invertebrates. You will struggle, however, to find a single leech or mosquito. This is the rainy season, and the most experienced guides walked in shorts and flip-flops, which is telling. Swimming is safe. The paths inside the park are crossed daily by hundreds of local people, often in motorbikes, and certainly not accompanied by guides. In addition to all the visitors, this makes it a crowded park, particularly in the paths close to the entrances. The entrance ticket to the park costs now about Rs 600. One should not have to pay more than that for a guide (per adult). This is already a bit higher than the Sri Lankan tourists in small groups pay for a guide. The best strategy is to sit in a restaurant by the park entrance, enjoy a beer or an excellent curry, and negotiate the price with one of the local villagers that are, so-called, certified guides. The first offer you get may be 5 times higher than the park fee, which is obviously a swindle. Take it easy, prices will come down. But, remember that by 17:30 it starts to get dark. Plan to arrive early.

Title: Interesting walk in the nature
Text:
It is a small rain forest and you don't get to see a lot of it if you take a three-four hour tour. But all and all it was a nice walk. We spotted some monkeys, giant squirrel, snakes, lizards, scorpion, spiders,... And we had a chance to swim in the river by one of the waterfalls, which was refreshing and fun.
It is important to have a good guide, who can spot all the animals and show them. We've had the best guide (but unfortunately I don't remember his name): He is a young guy, official forest guide. He was very into nature, wildlife, and was full of information and had a great eye for spotting animals. He really made our walk perfect.

Title: Good for Reptiles
Text: A little out of the way from most other attractions in Sri Lanka but if you are interested in wildlife its worth the trip.  The hike wasn't as long as I was hoping but we still saw three different vipers, bump nosed lizards, kangaroo lizards, giant squirrel and a few other animals.

Title: Rainforest "lite" but still really enjoyable
Text:
Yes there is a well trodden path and yes, you do get locals using this route as a cut through on motorbikes as other reviewers have said. So it's not perhaps a fully authentic rainforest experience for serious trekkers and/or nature lovers. But for most people, especially in the heat, a couple of hours "trekking" is enough and there is lots to see. You do need to take a guide, so your experience will partly depend on their skill/ English in explaining to you, but we saw quite a lot and the kids (13 and 11) really enjoyed. Our driver who is also a ranger didn't come with on this trip which was a shame as I think we would have got more out of the trip if he had. 

The path involves climbing over rocks/ tree roots so whilst some did it barefoot/ in flip flops, trainers etc are probably best. the halfway point is at a beautiful waterfall and the locals were swimming there so take swimsuits etc if you want to do the same. It's a pity the walk back is exactly the same - apparently there is a slightly longer walk that would have gone deeper in the rainforest and if we'd known, we'd have made sure we had time (we did an afternoon walk so needed to be out before sunset).

The bridge across the water was good fun (wobbly but great photo opportunity) and the waterfall was a lovely place to sit and rest and soak up the sights and sounds.

Title: Lots of small wildlife
Text:
We went to the Sinharaja Rain Forest, entering on the Deniyaya side.  You pick up a guide and a ticket near the entrance (Tickets are approx LKR 600 per person and you give the guide a tip at the end (approx LKR 1500-2000 seems the norm).  Do not get a package from your hotel as you will get ripped off. 

Yout then go for a walk for a few hours in the forest up to a waterfall, being shown the local flora and fauna by the guide.  Generally there are lots of insects, a couple of snakes, some small mammals, a few birds, and lots and lots of trees.

Everyone seems to take the same route and see the same things.  It's not very strenuous - really a 'rain forest lite' experience, but a good taster of what the rain forest is like. Overall, a very nice way to spend half a day.

Title: Excellent for Small Animals with Guide Hassun
Text:
I wanted to photograph reptiles and insects with my macrophoto lens. Thanks to Hassun the guide from Mideripitiya I saw a Greenpit viper,
Sri-Lanka kangaroo lizard and several kinds of beautifully colored lizards,  
spider wasp and more. After a four hour walk I returned with phantastic photos and a memorable rainforest experience.

Title: Nature lovers paradise
Text: This is highly green and It's hard to see sun from some places of this area. Some places are full of leachers so you have to be careful with that. Other than that, there are so many indigenous animals and plants and it's biodiversity is at the top among a lot of places in the wold. It's a world heritage and preservation is up to task by Sri Lankans.

Title: Fascinating
Text: Don't miss this experience. You could see amazing animals and plants. If you like more adventure you could jump down a 10m high waterfall in the area. Ask for Tour Guide Vini!

Title: Great intro into rainforest for children
Text:
We had one of the Rangers as guide which was really helpful to spot all the different plants and animals. 
My children, 8 and 10, were fascinated by the many millipedes, snakes (we saw 4 in total, 3 different species), fish in the river, large snails and geckos.

Title: Fantastic birdwatching
Text:
This is my second trip to Sinharaja, the first as a keen birdwatcher was 19 years' ago.

There are a number of entry points to the park but we went to the one which requires a jeep (or long walk) up to Martin's Lodge, birdwatching the trails from there.

Sinharaja is now recognised as a Unesco World Heritage site and an Endemic Bird Area by Birdlife International. The flocking behaviour of birds in Sinharaja is the most intensively studied in the world.

Indeed find a flock and you may well see a decent number of Sri Lanka's 33 (currently, will increase soon) birds, including Ceylon Crested Drongo, White-backed Starling, Sri Lankan Scimitar-babbler and Ceylon Rufous Babbler. Sinharaja also has a very good site for Ceylon Scaly Thrush which was split into a separate species after my previous visit. 

There are also a number of very good guides and rangers who can spot roosting nightbirds including Ceylon Frogmouth and most crucially Serendip Scops-owl, the latter only described to science as recently as 2003 (I think).

Sinharaja has ensured excellent birdwatching on both our two visits and we can't rate it highly enough. However, leeches are abundant so do take leech socks.

Title: Superb birding in forest reserve
Text: Finding a bird flock is essential, but when yo do the birds come thick and fast: Red-faced Malkoha, Ashy-headed Laughingthrush; White-faced Starling, Sri Lanka Scimitar-babbler, but the stars are the Sri Lanka Blue Magpie and Sri Lanka Scaly Thrush.

Title: Great rainforest area
Text: We had a bird watching and a trek in this amazing ecosystem. Make sure you have a good guide and wear good strong non slip shoes.

Title: Great trip - even better guide!
Text: We picked up our tour guide at Deniyaya bus station (look for the man in a van!) He sorted us out with salt for the leeches. provided us with extensive knowledge of the flora, fauna, insects and animals, and even lead us off the beaten track to swim in a secluded waterfall. Amazing! Everything included (ride there/back, ticket, tour) it came to £12.50 - bargain.

Title: Leech filled but beautiful
Text: This tropical rainforest has trails which are gentle for all ages, and take you deep into the forest. Here it rains most of the times, the showers were light and passing when we reached. We saw the Pitcher plant, two varieties of snakes, several green lizards and brown skinks,several varieties of trees and flowers, and ofcourse were bitten by the painloess leeches even though we wore the footcovers that are sold for 350 SR at the entrance. The guides they gave us did not know much english but were helpful.

Title: Loved it here!
Text: Worth a visit, would have stayed longer- very knowledgeable and showed us a lot. enjoyed here and reasonable price

Title: Nice walk, not many wild life spotted
Text: We had a nice walk in this wonderful park. Its really amazing to see a rain forest like this. Great nature! We were a bit disappointing since we didnt saw a lot of wild life (some monkeys, a butterfly, a centi- or millipede, one green hidden snake). Also our guide was not the best one we could have. He didnt found a lot of animals, didnt show us plants/flowers. We always need to ask ourselves if we saw something interesting. The animals he found, he was told by another guide that those animals where on that place. Visiting this place is really a must, but make sure you have a good guide.

Title: Trekking through rainforest
Text: Passing rivers , waterfalls , wildlife sinharaja offers a vast diversity of wild life. It needs about a day if you really want to explore the place. Have to go prepared to walk through the forest since the way can be rough at some point

Title: Exotic
Text:
Brillant, and totally unexpected trip.
Went out for a 2 hour walk and wanted to keep going.
Saw the most amazing animals, birds, monkeys, lizards, orchids and so many things just essentially walking up a pathway with a very experienced guide.
Took many pictures and wish we could have walked further.
A truely incredible place - and we are not usually keen on walking.
- Tip... take strong footwear and cover ankles (leeches). Tiger Balm is available to smeer on your shoes (leeches hate it).

Title: South entrance not so much of a wilderness....
Text:
We travelled to Sinharaja from Tangalle today...  About 2.5 hours so a reasonable trek to the southern entrance outside Deniyaya. The road ends and you are in a very small village where tuk Tuks are there to take you up the bumpy trail to the Forest office where you buy your tickets (560 lkr each).  Tuk tuk was 250 lkr each way.  we were told in the village that the guides all had to be hired in village, our driver seemed sceptical but nonetheless we went ahead with a "guide".   On reflection I don't believe he was a true "guide" as on the trail we noted other guys with official polo shirts, rucksacks, and binoculars...  Our guide was in tracksuit bottoms with a bottle of 7-up.  My fears were confirmed when his initial quote for the 3 hour walk was 4600 lkr, rather more than the 2000 lkr I was told  to expect.  Some haggling later we were at 2500 for 3 hour trek and set to go.   It started off promisingly ...  Tiny luminous green snake, massive millipede, rhino fly all spotted in a few minutes, then a couple of lizards...   But then things literally dried up and we diverted off to the track to the conservation centre for 10 minutes sit down, Nothing there apart from some faded pictures...  Then after a total of a 1 hour slow walking on a very, very well trodden path (avoiding locals on motorbikes as mentioned in other posts regarding this southern entrance) we arrived at a picturesque, but hardly awe inspiring waterfall, where we sat for another 10mins before a brisk walk back down the same path and back to base.. Avoiding those motorbikes again.  Luckily we saw a serpent eagle high up in a tree on the way back or else it would have been a zero spot rapid trek back - total time start to finish 2 hours 10 and we only made it to first waterfall.  Should have asked for trip to 2nd waterfall instead of stating a time.  Although, apparently, you do have to wade to get to the second.
So in summary I would have to agree with earlier posts about this southern entrance and say that it is spoiled by the motorbikes which must scare off the timid wildlife and please make sure you get a proper "guide" with binoculars and who has time and inclination to be able to look for and find whatever wildlife does stay close to the main route. To be fair and for reference we hit the trail at 9am and that may well have been too late to see the bulk of the wildlife...  So my advice would be go to the north entrance, go early, get an official guide with binoculars and spend more than 3 hours :-)

Title: All in one
Text: If you like walking around in natural forests with multiple activities this is the place. It's not easily accessible as it's at least a couple hours drive from any civilized accommodation but once you get there it's a great activity for a full day. You have to get a tuk tuk from a nearby village to get to the park. There are multiple waterfalls and interesting trees around. The water is pretty nice if you like to swim in rivers or lakes. The trek isn't very demanding and almost anyone can handle it. Since it's a rainforest there's a lot of humidity and camping in the forest could be quite a wet activity. There are various snakes and spiders around so if you are specifically interested in them this is a nice place to find many. We only spent day in the park so we had to choose among multiple alternatives to limit the trek but it's well worth the trip.

Title: Jungle trek
Text: We visited via the southern entrance. The main track follows the river that marks the southern boundary of the park. The track is much-used by local villagers, including an occasional man on a motorbike -  not my idea of a nature reserve. The only furred animals that we saw were dogs. Having said that, the forest is beautiful and swimming to a waterfall at the end of the trek was a wonderful experience. Leeches are numerous, but not problematic if one keeps moving. We enjoyed our day out, but it would be better if the park were properly protected.

Title: Beautiful place!
Text: It is a giant rainforest so there is things to see for days. We only spent maybe 3 hours in there with our guide who had so much knowledge and was able to spot all sorts of animals for us. Prepare to walk lots and drink lots of water because it's hot in there. Just beware there is no toilet facilities.

Title: Hidden gem
Text: this is definitely off the beaten track and not very popular yet with tourists. When we arrived there was a big party of school children as this is where all Sri Lankan children go for their school trips, we thought we wouldn't see much because they were a bit noisy. How wrong we were this is Virgin rain forest and we saw some amazing giant snails, large spiders and butterflies bigger than my hand, we saw loads it was simply stunning. We will definitely go again.

Title: Green green forest !
Text: We travel from Galle to the forest area by car.stayed at Deniyaya.Stayed 5 hours in the jungle wet and greenly .Walk about 8 Km.

Title: Underwhelming
Text: Let's be clear. This is a walk along a well trodden path through the rainforest. Surprisingly It is also much used by locals often on motorbikes to cross the forest. You will also meet many other groups of tourists on the trail.It is a miracle that one sees any wildlife at all, perhaps they are used to it. Pali seems to be the only guide that shows any genuine enthusiasm for the wildlife.The rest just go through the motions. The only animal they are interested in is the cash cow. The whole thing is just another money spinner. A lot of guides will get you to rush back on the return path in order to fit in a visit to the tea plantation and buy way overpriced tea. Another money spinner. My advice is make use of a full day in the forest and visit the plantation on another day if you are interested. Once you accept all that , it is still a nice walk and you will be contributing to the local economy. Just don't have too high expectations.

Title: Wonderful.
Text:
We are hiking enthusiasts and found the difficult, less traveled, off the beaten path trails amazing. The waterfalls were an absolute delight after a difficult hike and the hidden trails were pristine. The well traveled ones are good and easy going, but can get crowded very fast.
One word of caution, pay at the official entrance and hire a guide there. Pre-booking through hotels or guest houses result in dodgy hidden fees - still cheap, but as a local, I wouldn't want inappropriate tourism practices to succeed.

Title: Beautiful rainforest
Text: Wonderful trek along the neatly paved trail. Rocky trail but made it all the more interesting. Guides are available and knowledgeable. Saw some rare bird species - serendib scops owl, wood pigeon, blue naped monarch and vine snake. Beautiful opportunity for photography.

Title: Sinharaja Northern Entrance (Kudawa Road)
Text:
Note that there are 2 entrances to the forest area, North and South.
For birdwatching the Northern part seems where most people head, but it's probably more difficult getting there than the Southern entrance. 
This post is about the Northern side only.
Choices of accommodation is limited and expensive in comparison to the rest of Sri Lanka. You really need 2 days minimum or 1 overnight stay close by to make it worthwhile, a day-trip is not realistic in my opinion.
Taking a guide is compulsory Rs1000 + Rs 650 pp entrance fee. 
The road up to the Ticket Office and parking area is tarmac & accessible to any vehicle. At the Ticket Office you pay your fees, sign the foreign visitors book and get your guide. The guides are all very experienced and know their stuff so don't worry. 
You then have to walk to the actual park entrance about 2 km uphill along the Park Road (pedestrian only) that goes through forest. (Some people get ferried uphill by arranged jeep, but this is back on a completely different track - Martin's Rd - and it's not very pleasant + expensive.) See the map on my photo uploads - the one in Google maps is completely incorrect.
Once you reach the Entrance Office, they will sign you in and let you through.
The main trail is very broad and fairly flat with resting shelters and toilets along the way. You are not "trekking" through the jungle. It's more like an easy stroll really.
In March the forest was very dry with not a single leech in sight either.
The main trail from the Entrance Office leads to a Rangers Station a few kilometres further on but there are other smaller side trails too. I was very content walking the main trail at a slow pace to spot as many things as we could, finding a feeding flock of birds is brilliant and you can easily spend an hour rooted in one spot trying to pick out different species. I found the fact that none of the guides use binoculars amazing! 

Note for birders - If you have spare time walk the access road between the Ticket Office and Kudawa Bridge below. Some good birding to be had here as well as in the actual Ticket Office grounds.

Title: Amazing Wildlife at arms length!
Text:
We trekked the Sinharaja Rainforest on 2 separate mornings.  The experience was nothing short of exceptional.  We saw birds, lizards, snakes, monkeys, giant squirrels, scorpions, bats, crabs, fish, crayfish, butterflies and well as plenty of flora.  We also got to swim in a rainforest waterfall.

The guides are a wealth of knowledge and can spot the impossible.

Our trip to Sri Lanka also included jeep safaris around the more famous nature reserves, but they paled in comparison to the on foot rainforest trekking.

Advice: Wear decent walking shoes; be aware that there are leeches (easily dealt with and not dangerous); take plenty of water; take your swimming gear :)

Title: Fantastic day in the forest
Text: We had a great day out in the forest. This forest itself has a lot to offer in the way of wildlife and plants and also the river and waterfalls. But in order to really appreciate it you need a good guide.  We took Dilshan on Sinharaja Rest in Deniyaya who was terrific and really made our day.  Also the  guide from the Forestry Dept, Anura I think his name was, was a good spotter and went out of his way to find us interesting creatures and plants.

Title: Beautiful, easy, calm and full of animals.
Text:
With a very knowledgeable and friendly guide for only two of us (thanks Nimal!), we had an amazing 5 hours easy trek in the middle of a wonderful rain forest. We went for bird watching (we saw about 12 endemic species) but also saw monkeys, snakes, spiders, giant squirrels and plenty of other interesting things such a leaf ant nest and huge spider webs. There are plenty of leeches but not a problem if you wear protective socks (available at the entrance). 
There were not many tourist so the hike was calm and fun. If you like nature (responsible tourism), this is definitively a place to go. Amazing experience all in all!

Title: Wonderful mother nature
Text:
Great feeling to explore the forest. You feel so tiny in the tropical rainforest !
Made a 6-hour off-road trip in the forest (excursion done with the Deniyaya National Motel staff).

Title: Fabulous
Text: Superb experience a beautiful place and best to experience with a guide - watch out for leeches - leech socks are available and recommended.

Title: The country's premiere rainforest
Text: Flippin' awesome. For an extra adventure, enter through the parks remote northern entrance, straight into the heart of the rainforest.

Title: Disappointing
Text: We were disappointed with this trip. We decided to spend a night in the area and therefore took 2 days of our holiday. Although we saw most of the animals we were expecting the 3 hour return trip to the waterfall didn't  live up to expectations. We had expected to be on a trail in the wilderness jungle. Instead we had a pleasant walk alongside the river on a well defined path to the waterfall. The problem was that this path connects 2 villages and is used by motor bikes as a short cut. So instead of peace and quiet we were having to step aside as motor bikes sped past us. So if you fancy a nice guided walk, see some wildlife and a swim by a waterfall then this is good for you but if you're expecting wilderness it is not worth the time out of your holiday.

Title: Blue magpie, at last...
Text: Excellent guided 3 hour walk through the forest, only saw another two couples and such a varied selection of birds I have never seen before, even a group of Blue Magpies with their insane colouring.

Title: Not Worth Going Out of Your Way To See
Text: As we were staying on the coast north of Galle, the drive to Sinharaja took over two hours.  We therefore did not arrive there early enough to see any wildlife or birds.  For those who have seen a rainforest elsewhere in the world, I can only say this is not a particularly attractive or interesting one in comparison to others.  Add to that the presence of leeches and poisonous snakes.  If you go, be sure to purchase the cinnamon oil from the fellow selling it at the entrance.  We heard however he may not always be there or some visitors might not realize what he is selling and rush by him.  We took what we were told by our guide is the normal hike but he did not mention that to get to the falls we would have to wade through the stream with water evidently thigh high.  Being disappointed by then with the hike and knowing we still had over an hour to hike back followed by a two hour drive, we decided not to bother going across the stream.

Title: Fascinating glimpse into the rainforest
Text: The reserve is well worth a visit.  You are given a guide who takes you round and is very good at spotting and pointing out the wildlife.  Unfortunately, our guide's English was not the best and we wished we had had one of the other guides whose English was better.  Nevertheless, we had a very interesting visit and saw chameleons, a pit viper, a green snake (can't remember the name), pitcher plants and various birds. We were lucky to spot a group of laughing thrushes just inches from our feet and a bulbul just above our heads.  We also spotted an eagle, but it was not easy to see the birds, so a good pair of binoculars would be handy to take.  We solved the problem of leeches by applying tiger balm to our shoes before we started.  There is a small stall on the way to the reserve with general items and our own guide advised us to buy the balm.  I don't know if the leeches don't like the smell or if the smell cancels out the smell of humans - all I can say is it worked and only cost a few rupees.

Title: Take your swimming gear
Text:
We did a 6 hour walk in Sinharaja with a Forestry guide who found some lizards, snakes and birds for us to look at. 
You have to go with a guide and there were quite a few other groups there at the same time. Everyone seems to do the same route and I don't think it matters whether you do a four hour hike or a six hour one - the itinerary is the same, you just do it slower on the longer hike!
Take your swimming gear as there's a chance to swim in a water hole with waterfalls at one point, and a pool where fish clean your feet!
I was a bit disappointed with the area the tours go to as it looked as though it was regrowth not virgin rain forest.

Title: Bhattacharyya couple visited January 2015
Text: Liked Architecture moulded to huge boulders , personal attention friendly service , quite surrounding, simple food served with utmost attention , humour and gentle smile of the hosts .

Title: Wonderful forest
Text:
A fascinating place. There is long rocky drive in the back of an ancient, but well maintained jeep from the park office to the actual entrance - then you are on foot. 
There are good well-maintained tracks and a great abundance of birds etc to see - although bird spotting in the dense forest can be a challenge. There are lots of lizards and a few other creepy crawlies - notably leeches! It is worth wearing long trousers and closed footwear and purchasing the special leech socks at the entrance!
It a privilege to visit the amazing ecosystem.

Title: None existent customer service
Text: I booked and paid f$100 USD or a tour with this company called "Best of Lanka", we met another couple who wanted to join us and agreed to pay an additional amount. We were arriving on a cruise ship and were told the name and phone number of the driver and where he would meet us. When we arrived he was nowhere to be found, I borrowed a phone and called the driver who said he had no knowledge of our party and he was in another part of the port and he would phone the company and would get back to me which he did a few minutes later. When he phoned he said he did not have room for 4 passengers so I phoned the company and got no answer so we hired another vehicle. About 45 minutes after we were supposed to be met I get a phone call saying that they had a different driver waiting for us but as we were already in Colombo with limited time available so we would continue and asked the company to let the driver know. When I got back I received an email claiming falsely that I had been told by email to go to a different terminal 2 Km away as the driver was not allowed into the passenger disembarkation area and that I would be considered to be a "no show. I suggested that under the circumstances that a refund was in order and requested that $50 be returned, this suggestion caused another email to be sent and I was told that "company policy" did not allow for refunds. Moral, buyer beware. If you are looking for a city tour and are arriving by cruise ship, there are plenty of cars and vans to choose from, we finished up in a 7 seater air conditioned van with a knowledgeable driver who spoke excellent English for $20 an hour, less money less hassle. TIP, avoid this company and save your money.

Title: Great whole day trip!
Text:
We were travelling from Unawatuna to Sinharaja forrest for almost a full day trip. 
It takes 2 hours to get there, we came around 9:00 and the guide was ready for us. We had a best guide (I am really sorry i cant remember the name), he has been doing a guide there for 6 years, he was able to point at the snakes in the bushes, grab them etc. We started at the restaurant, where you can have some drinks or homemade curries. The guide asked us, how long we want to walk and based on this he planned the way. The journey to the waterfall and back was 3 hours of very slow walk. We saw all different types of animals, 3 different snakes, spiders, chameleons, monkeys, varans, multipedes etc. Do not expect too see interesting flowers, it is a jungle and it is more about the fauna. 

Practical info:
Clothes - would recommmend full shoes, high socks, long pants. There are leeches everywhere, so the guide will put you trousers to the socks, wet your shoes and cover them with a salt. If you are coming in the shorts and flip flops, the guide will put a special repelent on your feet and legs to prevent from the leeches. Even if they do this, the leeches can stick on you. 
Repelents - good to have good insect repelent
Food and drinks - there is a very nice restaurant at the beginning, you can order curries before the jungle trail and they will have it ready for you after you end it (prices are higher)
Price - we paid 11 000 rupies for the return journey from Unawatuna and 5000 rupies for the entrance and guide (for 2 people). I think we overpaid it but the guide was really worth it
What to bring with you - plasters, if the leech bite you (you will bleed a lot), repelent, camera, swimsuit if you wanna swim at the waterfall, towel (if you are swimming :-)
Toilet - there is a very very poor toilet at the beginning, many leeches outside. No toilet on the way
The track is not difficult for older people or children

Title: A Real Wilderness Experience
Text:
We liked - we walked for hours in the forest with a forestry guide who could show us the vegetation, wildlife and hidden paths.  We spotted a viper right next to the track, a snake catching fish in a pool, rare colourful birds and the purple leaf monkey.
We disliked - the leeches but wore leech repellant socks.

Title: Beautiful....
Text:
A great walk through the reserve accompanied by a local guide.

Our guide lived in the area, and knew the terrain like the back of her hand.  We chose to walk / scramble to the top of the canopy, and whilst this isn't a complex climb, a reasonable level of fitness, good footwear, and leg coverage against leeches is required.  Approx 5 hr walk, taking in some of the lower more easy access sights too.   All worth the effort

Title: excellent walk
Text: if you like getting out and about, or hot and sweaty, a visit to the Forest is for you.  We picked up a Forest guide as required and accompanied by our own excellent guide/driver Prabaht, had a delightful stroll through a patch of primary growth rain forest.  Our forest guide pointed out things of interest, a glorious bright green frog eating viper down by the creek, lizards, spiders, epiphyte orchids, native mango and olive trees as we wandered up the track passing waterfalls and lovely ferns.  We walked for about an hour on a fairly rough track before succumbing to the heat and retracing our steps.  It was a lovely, albeit brief insight into some of the original natural vegetation of Sri Lanka.

Title: Unforgettable Rain Forest walk
Text:
If you have read a few reviews you are probably wondering two things : 

- what will i see?
- what about the leeches? 

About those leeches - i went early November, it had been raining hard recently and rained on our walk back. My guide wore flip flops and bare feet and wasnt worried by the leeches. He found one to show me but they didnt seem to be an issue.  Dont let thinking about them put you off. Same with mosquitoes- according to my guide humans are not the preferred food so the mozzies dont bother you in so balanced an ecosysytem. 

What can you expect to see ? You see scorpions, a couple of snakes if your guide has keen eyes like mine, many lizards (including the kangaroo lizard) , many butterflies, a giant squirrel, some macaques and some giant millipedes.   Birds are best seen early in the morning so not great for daytrippers. Dont expect to see the leopards or elephants. They are here but you wont see them.

I saw a great variety in prices for this tour . I paid 95$ for a solo trip, pick up and drop off in Galle, including all tolls, entry fee and guide charges.  The only extra cost was lunch and a hefty tip for the guide who was an absolute legend. 

This is a lovely memory of a trip to Sri Lanka, well worth the full day required to make the trip.

Title: Lots of interesting birds and reptiles to see
Text:
We had a guided walk through the reserve for a morning. We bought the leech socks (much needed!) though the leeches just climb up your trousers and get through your T-shirt.
The walk takes a few hours and along the way you can spot a number of native birds; some interesting lizards and snakes and macaque monkeys. We also came upon elephant poo (there are two elephants in the reserve).

If you are very interested in spotting the birds youll know you need to come early in the morning but if not you can still see a decent number as we did.

As it was the rainy season we got soaked on the walk back; Ive never been so wet; but it still good to experience.

Title: Most beautifull thing i saw in my life
Text: We visited this amazing forest with a guild and it was beautifull. Reptiles, plants and trees. We toke a dip in a little lake by a waterfall it wat amazing!!

Title: So much wildlife, such excellent guides
Text: THE staff at the main entrance and at the upper gate were friendly and helpful. The guide was absolutely excellent, spotting and pointing out everything and anything.

Title: An unexplored rainforest
Text:
Reaching the entrance of the park is an experience of it's own. Had to get there by a 4X4 provided by the owner of Sinharaja Eco lodge. We booked a tour thru him and he provided a very fantastic guide Hemal who speaks good English & had a very observant while walking to show us the many kinds of indigenous Lizards,Spiders and snakes, butterflies, the century old trees etc which can be found only in Sinharaja which is very unique as Sri Lanka being such a small island it cannot be found in the rest of the world. The many waterfalls you come across are wonderful and you can have a dip in it.

Don't forget to take Leach socks during the rainy season this is a must and having a refreshing bath at the waterfalls. 

Please be careful not to litter the place and take plenty of water and some snacks if you are doing the full day trek. 

A must do trip for environment lovers and a wonderful thing to show the kids as to why we need to take care of our surroundings.

The best thing here there is no cellphone signals which makes the environment more peaceful while trekking with no phones ringing around you and not disturbing nature.

Title: Stunning walks - take a guide
Text: Easy accessible, good car park. Need license to get into the park. Must- ask a local guide to help you along the trails. They spot animals and flowers you otherwise miss. The more enthusiastic you get, the more they show you. There are also booklets on trails from their local shop: ok if you want to do the kilomets but the guides see more chamelens, snakes, monitor and stump nose lizards, bush spiders in many varieties, orchids and so on.

Title: One of the few untuched rainforests in the world
Text: Went for a walk within the forest together with one of the local guides/ park rangers that are available at the forest entrance. Amazing to walk within the forest and see all the tall trees, butterflies and flowers. You could notice that the guide was very familiar with the forest. He know where to look for specific birds, and took us of the normal big Walking paths to see some small owls sleeping Deep in the forest. Everyone should experience thise once in their Life to get an understanding of why we need to take care of the environment

Title: Be prepared!
Text:
So my family and I visited here with our guide. We paid an entrance fee which included the services of a forest guide too. He did not speak English but our guide was luckily able to translate. He pointed out wildlife; we saw a snake, monkey and various birds, pretty butterflies and others. 

The trek is 4 hours to the viewpoint at the top. Be warned though this is not a casual stroll through the forest! We rocked up with trainers and anoraks and thought we were fine. But there is a lot of climbing and clambering and it took us nearer 5 hours. It is very humid as you would expect. I struggled and didnt quite make it to the top although the rest of the family did and enjoyed the view. 

Really hiking boots are required and DEFINITELY pay for leech socks! I didnt know you could do this or I definitely would have done. We were plagued by leeches all the way round - I tucked my trousers into my socks - but the leeches ate through my (fairly robust sport socks) and my ankles / socks were bright red from the blood!! Not a pretty sight. Shocked the (well prepared) Chinese tourists! I ended up with 5 leech bites and we had to keep stopping to remove the leeches from INSIDE our shoes/ socks as well as outside. Ew. On the way back down we sprayed our shoes with mozzy repellent which seemed to help.  Do take plenty of water too - again we were ill prepared.

An interesting experience but would have been much easier with the right equipment!

There is a little shop you can buy a few welcome snacks/ drinks at the end. There are toilets but women - its just a hole in the ground :(. You make want to take an entire change of clothes if like me you sweat in the humidity!

Title: Get away from it all
Text: You can hike here and be away from people and in the presence of many animals. This is a great activity with or without kids.

Title: There Are The Rainforest Explorers & Then The Rainforest DayTrippers.  Either Way A Fabulous Experience +++
Text: We were the latter.  We saw the explorers on our three hour journey in and out of the forest.  They had the hiking boots and the gaters, the hats and the long sleeves.  They had the walking sticks and the backpacks and they had the expression when they encountered us with our sandals and shorts, short sleeves and water bottles that we too were strange and curious creatures of this forest.  Their get-up would have been of an advantage to them because it did mean they could spend longer off the beaten track before the inevitable leeches rose from the vegetation underfoot or fell from the trees above.  We had to be quick and as a result many photos were blurred because they we were taken in haste, however we saw some amazing creatures and FOR-THE-FIRST-TIME-EVER swam (fully clothed ... didn't have bathing suits with us either ... oh well) under a waterfall.  I did wonder if the explorers would have with their need to take so many items off.  Anyway the Rainforest was a FABULOUS experience that I would highly recommend it.  Our fear of leeches when we realised our inadequate clothing has been replaced with curiosity and wonder through observation of them and out of four of us we unknowingly at the time only had one bite ... and we survived to tell the tale!  We are very grateful for our guide who knew how to spot things that we would not have.

Title: Very pleasant rainforest experience with guide Chaminda
Text:
It is very difficult to find prior information on internet regarding reliable and knowledgeable forest guides and prices of a trip into Sinharaja rainforest from the south (Mederipitiya) entrance. Eventually we were advised by our taxi driver (Niron, owner of Unawatuna Tours) to hire a guide called Chaminda. Price was 5000 rp per person for our family of four, inclusive the park entrance fee of 1250 rp per person, for a full day trip (07:00 - 14:00, from our accomodation at 1 km from the park entrance). We agreed to meet Chaminda in the afternoon to discuss things further.

Our accomodation (Sinharaja Forest Sanctuary - certainly advisable for a pleasant stay!) also advsed Chaminda without being informed by us about our previous arrangements; they were very enthousiastic about his qualities. In the reviews in this Tripadvisor topic, Chamindas name appeared once, also with good judgement. A couple that had made a trip with him on our arrival day was also quite pleased with him, only a bit set back because of the price (16000 rp for the two of them including entrance fee). After meeting him, we were convinced of his quality. The price seems fair enough in comparison with tourguide costs in other Sri Lanka parks. Obviously, cost per person decreases somewhat for a group of four compared to only two persons - the guide has to spend his full day in both cases, isnt it.

The next morning Chaminda picked us up at our hotel; he had already stored the packed breakfasts and lunches in his backpack and off we went. He immediately showed to have a keen eye for all kinds of creatures, large and small, and knew their names well (as a biologist, I was very keen on that aspect of his guidance).

The first 4 km led along a track that was also used by local villagers, as this is their only way to go there. A new road is slowly being realized through difficult terrain south of the river bordering Sinharaja on the south, and hooefully will be completed in 2 years from now. The motorbikes were certainly there but kept a reasonable pace (the track hardly allows for speeding...). We then reached the park centre where we ate our breakfast and we were registered by a park ranger; entrance fees were paid. From there we went to first waterfall, and continued in easterly direction along a steep climb to a second fall. There we had lunch and had our feet being cared for by small fish (Garra or similar species: a free jungle spa experience). We returned to the park via another trail and continued along the main path back home. Total distance was 17 km (from 7 am till 2 pm).

Leeches were hardly a problem, but we were lucky with hardly any rain so this may be the explanation. Wildlife was abundant: snakes, macaques (and purple-faced langurs heard, not seen). Grey hornbills, hand-sized spiders, large millipeds and various beautiful lizards. A beautiful experience of a primary and seemingly untouched piece of rainforest!

Chaminda can be reached via his local phonenumber 041 5633209.

Title: Fantastic experience
Text: I arrived early morning, and met my guide, after putting the leech socks, off we went, I good steady climb, the smell of the forest and the noises were intoxicating. With laser vision the guide was pointing spiders the size of dinner plates in front of me, they were so well camouflaged, I saw a kangaroo gecko, and the ever so large Asian squirrel. I suppose you have to expect that these creatures are going to be tucked away, and you need to work at getting some good pictures, we climbed to about 1100 Mtrs and the humidity was reaching 90% with a temperature of about 34c. It was hard work but worth every step. The diversity of plants and insects is incredible, and the fact that a large % are endemic to Sri Lanka. If you have 4 hrs to spare don't miss this opportunity.

Title: Beautiful experience
Text: 20 classmates ventured out to take this hike. Not knowing what to expect, we had the most memorable time - seeing insects and reptiles, listening to forest sounds and bathing in the waterfall. Best part was the torrential downpour at the end with hot ginger tea awaiting us. Thank you for a lovely trip.

Title: Amazing but watch leeches
Text: We enjoyed our long walk through the forest with a local guide, but we hit lots of rain and leeches. I am an angler and no issues with leeches aside these bite through thick socks.

Title: Not what we were expecting
Text:
As everywhere in Sri Lanka, very nice people, BUT being at the beginning of their tourist development, they don't try hard and they don't always tell you the truth. Before the walk, paths and small roads were closed to vehicles, ensuring guests no car can go further. A big lie!... after we reached the beginning of the walking path we saw a jeep outside the ticket office.The Sinharaja walk started at 9 a.m. They could say, it is too late to see los of animals, they could charge less if you go later than 06-07 a.m. and they could tell you, you will only see  1 lizard, 2-3 birds and if u r  lucky 1-2 
snakes...oh yes, 2 butterflies, 1 centileg and 2 hidden monkeys. AND there was a fight with a guide who claimed that our group  was "stolen" from the other guide...a real fight. The forest was nice...NOT as nice as the rain-forest I have seen in Peru...BUT no animal watching...and I think it is not the time we went there...it is the month...DON'T go to Sinharaja AND/OR Yala in August...both are disappointing.

Title: A nice walk but if you are a keen animal watcher you'd need several visits
Text: When we were there is pelted with rain so watching animals was limited (but in a rainforest this is to be expected!) You do have to watch out for leeches after the rain which was an interesting experience! Did see a few interesting animals e.g. giant squirrel, large spiders and green pit viper but not the masses of birds that this area is known for. For the children the walk was quite long in the humidity and heat but if they like bugs etc they will enjoy.

Title: Amazing hike with knowledgeable naturalist
Text:
Sinharaja was a highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka.  We spent about 4.5 hours there and could not get there earlier than 10:30am (the full drive from Colombo took about  3.5 hours plus a half-hour stop) so we were only able to do the "short" loop of about 6km.  We took a tuk-tuk from the main road, arranged by our guide/driver, to a small cafe from whence we hiked to the ticket office and then into the rain forest. This is Sri Lanka's last remaining virgin forest and is a UNESCO world heritage site. Because we arrived in the middle of the day we did not get to see the full range of bird or animal life  because their natural activity is limited in the middle of the day; nonethless we heard their calls, which our naturalist often identified for us (hornbill, monkeys, etc.). 

One of the reasons we loved this hike was because of our naturalist (you cannot hike unaccompanied in the forest both because the government naturally wants to protect the fragile ecosystem but also likely because there are some poisonous snakes around), Sanjaya. He lives in the local village of about fifty families and has extensive knowledge of both the plants and animals at Sinharaja. He was eager to show us (at our request) many of the snakes--including a green pit viper and a bronze back--and reptiles including a couple of hump-nosed lizards and kangaroo lizards. We also saw large milipedes, a giant squirrel at close range, some large fish and a few other things. It was instantly obvious that Sanjaya knows every leaf, twig, nook and cranny of this forest and likewise knew exactly where to look for each kind of creature we wanted to see.  He also pointed out giant vines, wild cinnamon and some other unusual plants, some used for Ayurvedic medicine. Sanjaya was very conscientious and careful, always keeping an eye on our nine-year-old daughter, holding her hand at more difficult points in the hike, carrying her bag when she got too tired, warning us when we should keep our distance from a snake/riverbank/motorbike, etc.  

The hike was virtually flat and the only challenge was sometimes navigating major tree roots or uneven terrain. Some other reviews mentioned perilous leeches. We saw two miniscule ones, the size of inchworms, between four of us, but that was it the whole time. It was a dry day when we were there so it may have affected things. 

The short hike does involve crossing a river in order to get to a beautiful waterfall and swimming hole. I did not originally want to do this and ended up not swimming but it was fun to watch the others, who had a great time.

Title: A nice walk but might not be as you expect...
Text:
You can easily spend 8-9 hours in this Forest Reserve. 
We came there with the expectations of real rain forest conditions but where slightly dissapointed. 
You follow a track all the times and the animals we spotted weren't that incredible. Consider your time before going here - if you have a month in SL it might be worth it but with lesser time a would chose differently.

Title: Exotic Plants
Text: If you want to see Sri Lanka's most exotic plants all in one place, Sinharaja is the place to be!  This dense jungle is truly an experience.

Title: Walking in the forest
Text: If you are interested in lizards, snakes and general rainforest experience then this place is great.  We went in from Deniyaya (this side is more for reptiles, if you want birds you need to come in from the North).  Our guide was excellent and we saw snakes, lizards, monkeys and grey hornbills - along with other small things.  We had thought that our driver could then drive round to other entrance - but apparently it is a very very harey road and he would not go there.  I would like to visit the other side for more bird life, but this side was interesting and worth a visit.

Title: Breathtaking views and experience
Text: In the heart of the rainforest. Even a monsoon deluge did nothing to dampen the experience. A 10k trek through the forest, observing birds, butterflies, giant worms, millipedes and lush growth. Excellent trekkers who kept to our slow pace and imparted a wealth of knowledge. Dumbed down as he soon realized our knowledge was minimal, compared to bus normal bird watchers and biologists

Title: Don't let leeches stand in your way
Text: This the most unique forest in Sri Lanka - some of it is still primary forest. Several birds, butterflies, dragonflies etc.. are only found here and no where else in the world. GO!

Title: Back to nature
Text: This was an amazing experience! We walked with a guide and, while we didn't get to see any large animals, we did get to see many birds, including a Jungle Fowl and some snakes. Beware of leeches, though. Our guide had us tuck our pant legs inside our socks so that the leeches couldn't get to the skin directly, and he had some repellant made of tobacco juice and soapy water. It must have worked, because we didn't get any leeches on us!

Title: Fantastic experience
Text: A really true jungle experience with leeches trying to share your blood at every corner! Provided you wear leech socks and are vigilant you might get away without being bitten. But that's half the fun. The reserve itself is full of wildlife and the birds are spectacular.

Title: PITADENIYA ENTRANCE-a waste of Time, Money, Sleep and Perspiration
Text:
We have noted the negative comments regarding this entrance and they seem well founded as we just had the most negative Rainforest Experience in 3 decades.
A two and a half hour trip from Mirissa most in darkness to get there at dawn. At the village it was 2280 rupees for us as a couple plus 2000 for the Guide (variously Freddie or Prandi who allegedly had worked there for 5 years and was abysmal-and I am being kind), and then 800rupees for the tuk-tuk to carry you from the village to the restaurant at the edge of the Rainforest itself. In fairness it was a diabolical track but are you going to refuse have travelled for probably hours and hours to get there. You are pressed to order a meal and the indifferent breakfast for 2 was more expensive than we would pay in Spain at our coastal resort for a full English breakfast.
On to the rainforest experience and what an experience it was as we constantly had to quit the path in order to avoid being flattened by motorcycles and scooters. You see the track runs between 2 villages and is used for foot and cycle traffic. Then again there were the pedestrians although for the most part they were all smiles and 'good-mornings'  to which we replied in good part.
So what did we see-Birds-ZERO, mammals-Zero, 6 Spiders, a small snake that crawled through the leaf litter-a whole 3cm long, a 5cm green tree snake, a chameleon and a kangaroo jumping lizard. And that was it. We have seen more wildlife in our hotel garden in Weligama including a 2m Monitor, a Mongoose, and Indian Cobra (which was duly collected by the snake man), and umpteen lizards.
We arrived at the bridge some 3km on thinking we would get to the waterfall! Wrong again, you have to parallel the course of the river and then wade across. I ask you-shouldn't we have been warned. No the guide just wanted to shoot through because of course as soon as he had got rid of us he was then free to inveigle another punter to part with his/her hard earned money.
At the bridge I spent some time talking to a local villager who said that the whole thing was nothing but a scam. The local fauna is just not in evidence due to the nature of the current disturbance and that anyone wanting to see the real Sinharaja and its wildlife should enter from the north where the fauna is much more acclimated to human intrusion. I know this seems somewhat contradictory but perhaps he meant that there were no noisy 2 wheelers shrieking by every 5 minutes or so.
The pace set by the Guide was anything but conducive to studying nature and you had to keep your head down to avoid slipping and tripping. No Leeches.
In conclusion, and as a world traveller of 40 years plus a thoroughly negative experience although possibly less so to the uninitiated and ON A GOOD DAY. Whatever you do avoid this entrance and state this to your Tour Company.

Title: World heritage site!
Text: one of the rich and famous rain forests in the world. Beautiful and elegant. it is a tiring journey into the forest. Please do not try this unless you really want to see this place. The fewer the people visit this place, the much safer it is.

Title: Jungle
Text: another amazing experience Sri Lanka offered including leeches!!! Even the long socks weren't long enough...

Title: A whole new world
Text:
A must visit place for adventurists and nature lovers, You'll be able to see over 100 types fauna & flora, though we were unfortunate to spot any big mammals as most of them are deep in the jungle, however we spotted many birds,insects and snakes.

one must make sure to be fully geared with water,clothing to keep the LEACHES away along with a cake of soap another method of getting rid of leaches, snacks, good shoes etc.

According to our guide the forest reserve is approx 11,000 acres so it advisable to stick with your guide,unless you know the place at the back of your head.

Title: Average Place
Text: Really far from the city. If you plan to visit start early by 6:00 a.m and only if you are a true nature loved.

Title: Easy jungle walk, don't call it trekking
Text:
We took main, north-west entrance (nearest village- Pothupitiya). We paid 2200LKR for 2 entry tickets and a guide. 
We trailed to big tree, which was about. 6.5km one way. The trail was very easy,  more like a walk in the park than actual trekking. You can do it in flip-flops. It took us 2.5 hours to return with one stop on the way. 
We were lucky with a guide,  a guy with university degree in biology and eagle eye.  He found for us few reptiles,  birds and butterflies.  All endemic species to Sri Lanka. We also saw 2 species of monkey. The guy give us names of all the species in Sinharaja,  English and Latin and also shared some interesting facts about Park and Sri Lanka in general. 
In overall nice experience of local nature.

Title: Amazing
Text: Great primal forest . Try to book a trek with Pali from Sinharaja Rest guest house in Deniyaya , he is the best .

Title: Rainy trip
Text: We visited the forest with all our family and it was a real adventure. When we did enter the forest it started to rain havily and stopped only after two hours. NOt sure, but can be rather regular rain as we did visit it in the afternoon time. Anyway we did manage to get to the waterfall and it was very nice, however we did not bath there as were already completely wet. Problem was that before our trip we asked everybody about leaches and were assured this is the dry season and there are not there. However on the way back from the waterfall it was realy fight with leaches - they stick to your shoes and climb up, so if you have just shorts you have to count you experience them as we did. They are not dangerous and will drop off after some 5 minutes when they are full of your blood, but it is scary and when we got the first onece we could not help up not to stop and check every minute of our walk. Probably also because of the rain we saw limited number of animals, most impressive was to hear very loud screems of monekey, but we could not see them, also spiders 10 cm big and really huge trees.

Title: Wonderful place.
Text:
Sinharaja is a lovely place and we saw some exciting and uncommon birds. Sinharaja is for those who are serious about bird-watching are prepared to do a fair bit of walking and are equipped with good binoculars and leech socks. 

Our naturalist guide was very knowledgeable and was able to spot and identify birds quickly. 

I would recommend an early arrival around 7am because it seems they run out of guides and Jeeps. 

Having obtained our tickets and found the naturalist guide, we had to wait 20 minutes or so for a Jeep (even at 7am). This took us up the hill on an extremely rough road (15 minutes) and left us with the naturalist guide to walk through the reserve. It would be possible to walk up the hill but it would take a long time to get to the heart of the reserve.

After some 2 - 3 hours, the naturalist guide suggested we go to the village area in a Jeep where he reckoned we could see a number of birds not previously seen. So we waited 20 minutes or so for another Jeep and started back down the hill. Halfway down, we met the original Jeep coming up and changed vehicle. At the bottom we met our chauffeur/guide who had taken us to the reserve and he explained that if we took the Jeep to the village, which it appeared was outside the park area, it would cost extra (some 3500 rupees). He explained that what we had paid for was one Jeep trip up the hill and down again. We declined the Jeep but the chauffeur/guide took us in the car as far as he could and we agreed to walk the rest with the naturalist guide. We never really reconciled whether the naturalist guide was simply trying to get us the best bird-watching experience and see the most interesting birds, or whether he was trying to rip us off by luring us into extra charges.

I dont know what our agent in Sri Lanka expected and had paid for the package that we had but, from the contract we were sent, I had expected that the Jeep and naturalist guide would be at our disposal for the day.

However, we saw lots of exciting and uncommon birds, had a lovely day in the rain forest and came away happy and content. What more could we ask?

Title: No birds
Text:
We stayed in Talpe and we had to start from the hotel at 5:00 AM. We had a breakfast in Sri Lankan style by the entrance of the rainforest. It was interesting, we did not know what we exactly eat. :)) After the breakfast we walked into the rainforest with our guide. He was friendly and had eagle eyes, he discovered a lot of tiny insects. We saw a snake, snails, lizards, monkeys, but we did not see any birds. I wanted to take photographs about some beautiful birds, but they did not come. 
Anyway, the forest and the waterfall are beautiful, and the tour/walking was really easy.

Title: Excellent Avian and Reptile Viewing
Text:
Our group had an amazing trek with Mr. Pali (of Sinharaja Rest House). We saw birds such as the Grey Hornbill, Imperial Green Pigeon, blue Monarch bird, and Paradise Flycatcher. We observed a number of reptiles at close range, including the kangaroo lizard, pit viper, Blossom's krait, and many more. In the middle of our trek, we took a short break to swim at the waterfall. 

As it was a Sunday, it was a bit more crowded than usual and yes, there were terrestrial leaches so be prepared with proper footwear and precautions. Leaches and crowds aside, the biodiversity is incredible, and we had a great time!

Title: Mild jungle trekking for beginners!!
Text: Arrived here around 5.30-6.00am in the morning in hoping to spot some birds here. Our guide were experienced, attentive and observant enough to discover all the birds and animals in the area. We saw more than 10 different species such as as blue magpies, bukbulk bird, long tail squirrels, grey face monkey, blue face monkey, kangaroo lizard, green vine snake, green viper and so o.n ! To us, the hike was too easy and we should have gone for a 25km hike to the northwest exit. I strongly suggest experienced hikers to do that! But to sum up we enjoyed the experience and the swim in the waterfall!

Title: Take a day tour
Text: The forest is really great. I would recommend a full day tour. We took a short tour (3-4 hours). You just walk along the forest and see few animals. To see more and real jungle you need to take a day tour.

Title: rainforest for kids
Text: Easy walking paths through the jungle, you'll see a few birds, insects, the usual monkeys and the occasional snake if you're lucky. It's ok but we've seen much more exciting jungle trecks in South-East Asia and South America.

Title: Wonderful place for true nature lovers.
Text: It is true that the journey up is long and slow, the views on the way are spectacular , but the journey is worth it to stay in a rainforest and enjoy guided walks through the jungle seeing birds and small creatures, flowers and trees is a terrific experience. Rainforests are always difficult for animal spotting, bit the Black purple faced monkeys make their presence felt and some of the rare birds we saw were spectacular. Don't forget the little joys, butterflies, dragonflies, frogs and tiny lizards, waterfalls and rocky rivers and giant trees. Our guide was excellent and knowledgeable and we had a terrific couple of days there.

Title: 3 hours' walk in Sinharaja forest reserve
Text: It is always nice and interesting to walk in a rainforest. My husband and I did a 3 hours' walk with a guide. We were perhaps unlucky as we did not see much as far as animals are concerned. A few monkeys and a viper. We did not see many flowers. A bit disappointing.

Title: A nature lovers paradise!
Text: Sinharaja Forest Reserve is simply one of the best places in Sri Lanka to imerse yourself in nature. Dont take much notice of reviews from tourists complaining about the journey up. It is a bit bumpy but the 4x4's cope with this very well and it only takes about 45 minutes from the accommodations near the entrance gate at the bottom of this mountain. Full of endemic wildlife which is not all easy to see, if you love nature and are not just a moaning general tourist, then this is paradise.

Title: Underwhelming
Text: X4 of us endured a gruelling 2 1/2 hour journey to cover 52km from Koggala to Sinharaja over the bendiest roads ever. If you don't suffer with travel sickness you might after this journey! We started out at 6.30am and arrived for 9. We saw about 12 species of birds and x3 snakes with our guide. Birding was the usual difficult dense forest type. I would suggest if you are going to bother going here you need to do an overnight stay local to the forest for a dusk then dawn visit. Otherwise go to Udawalawe where the birding is easier.

Title: The only primary climax left in Sri Lanka of the type, this bit of tropical rain forest is a must visit.
Text: Sinharaja forest is the only primary climax rain forest left in Sri Lanka, with its unique and varied plant and wild life it never seizes to amaze me.

Title: A really good contrast to other places
Text:
We spent a couple of nights a Sinharaja Forest Reserve in the middle of a dry spell, so I don't know what it is like when it rains.

I really enjoyed our stay here, it's a tourist location but not touristy. The relatively small number of guests gives it a country house hotel feel as we had conversations with a number of other residents.

The accommodation is in T shaped metal buildings, they are large enough for two with good showers, bed and settee. They also have a number of UK sockets, we also had an extension lead. Interestingly we were able to sleep with the windows open as there does not seem to be any flying biting creatures at all. 

Breakfast and dinner were both good, although there is only a choice of two main courses for the 5 course dinner. Our travel agent said they do not serve alcohol which is not true.

The WIFI is a little erratic but it did not prevent me from doing everything I wanted to do online.

The high spots are the very relaxed walks with the personable and knowledgeable guides. We did 3 in one day the 6.30 am bird watching 3.3 miles along a road, the rainforest walk around 3 hours over reasonably easy ground and the waterfall walk somewhat steeper. On the latter walk one can paddle in the water and let the fish clear any dead skin of your feet. The walks are free and there is nothing to stop you going on the same one twice. There was an evening walk on offer as well. 

As others have said leech socks are provided I wore them on the second walk but not on the last one when I had shorts and crocs on.

The journey to the hotel is 'interesting' as it's pretty steep and narrow, our driver had no problems but others did especially if it was the first time they had done it.

Title: Bring snorkeling gear!  and leach proof socks
Text:
The jungle tour with the provided guide was excellent. You have a choice of  lengths and we chose the two waterfall tour which was a nice compromise between too short and exhausting. Maybe the guides vary, but ours had good English, sharp eyes, and an extensive knowledge of all the flora and fauna. We saw so many snakes that we have never wanted to put our hands or feet down on anything but the path ever again in Sri Lanka  (we love reptiles and insects) and plenty of leeches so, if possible, where longer socks so you could talk your pants in. The guy gave us all to put on her shoes and socks but my daughter and I had short socks and I had waffle fabric shoes so the salt just went into my shoes.  BTW If you do get a leech, the current science recommendation is to just pry it loose with your fingernail.

At the second waterfall you can swim and there are also lots of fish. If you have snorkeling equipment, take it! Or maybe just take a mask and snorkel or even goggles. If you do swim to the waterfall, don't just strike out for it. Facing the waterfall, go along the rocks in shallow water to your right and then swim to the back wall of the pool. Then there is not so much current and even a weaker swimmer can get under the waterfall. (Of course if they can't tread water they might then be pounded into a panic but that's another issue :-)

Title: Need a guide
Text: We went in there and yes it is jungle in the city. Not well marked unless you know Sinhala. Saw a few skittish deer and hit a bunch of dead ends and come home with multiple cuts and bruises. It is quite pretty but I thought overrated and wasted our day.

Title: Jungle in the city
Text: We went to Udawattekele for a walk to escape the busy city setting of Kandy. Its only a 10-15 min walk from the center of town, so we expected nothing more but a small forest. What we got though was a full jungle-experience with monkey, snake and barking-deer sightings. You can decide how much time you want to spend walking through as there are several loops, marked out on a big map by the entrance. Entrance fee 660 Rupees as of October 2019. Beware of the leeches. We got attacked a few times!

Title: Good walk
Text: Good walk, plenty to see.  Our guide said it was about 3km to get around. Liar liar pants on fire, it was at 6 km's.  Plenty of monkeys all over the carpark and cars when we finished.

Title: Enjoy some quiet time in the woods
Text: Kandy can be pretty noisy. If your ears need a break, come here. Once we stepped into the forrest we felt like entering a different world - a very beautiful one. Make sure to take a map since the signs wont always be a big help to you. Other than that just enjoy your time. We barely met other people and just enjoyed the hike and the beautiful viewpoint over Kandy.

Title: amazing place
Text: amazing place to travel ,,,, just for calm down your mind..... there is a bicycle driving path also there

Title: Must do in Kandy
Text:
This is seriously a must do! We went up to the forest at 3.30pm and saw so many monkeys, it was the most amazing experience as we love seeing wild animals. Bring cash to pay the lovely old lady at the entrance and she will give you a map, can be done within an hour or two but recommend allowing more time so you can stop to take photos. We also saw 4 deer and some friendly stray dogs :) Highly recommend to all, such a beautiful, peaceful and quiet place.
Tip: bring your own water bottles.

Title: Great scenery but could be better maintained
Text: Did a really nice circuit around the park which offered a great viewpoint of Kandy. However there were heaps of not so friendly monkeys hanging around. Could be better but is a cheaper alternative to botanical gardens

Title: Rainforest in the city!
Text: This rainforest just behind the Temple of the tooth is nice to have an early morning walk. As soon as the forest awakes the city also wakes!

Title: Nice for a stroll and a view over the city
Text:
We came to Udawattekele first thing in the morning, with my husband hoping to see some birds. There are plenty of trails. Unsurprisingly it was quiet at that time. While we didn't see too many birds it was still a wonderful place to walk around. While you are here be sure to track down the liana called pus wel. Its a giant vine believed to be between 200-300 years old! First thing in the morning before the morning mist had lifted, it made a weird and wonderul part of the forest. 

Also while you are here seek out the view point overlooking the city. It's lovely.

Title: Green lung of Kandy
Text: Truly called the green lung of Kandy, it's beautiful!! To know a tropical forest exists in this small town was truly mesmerising. You could walk inside without encountering another person for 30 minutes!! Tall trees give the requisite shade and the entire experience is serene and beautiful!!

Title: Quiet place to go for a hike
Text: The sanctuary was a lovely stop on our trip. A dense and beautiful forest a short drive from the town. Took us about 2 hours to hike the majority of the park. Would definitely recommend stopping.

Title: Beautiful forest close to city.
Text:
We almost didn't come here having read some negative reviews, but we were really glad we did. There are some lovely old ladies at the gate and the cost was very reasonable (about £1.50 each I think). We walked around the whole forest which took a couple of hours at a slow pace. It is such a peaceful pace and there were few other people there. An oasis of calm right next to the hustle and bustle of Kandy. The sounds of the forest were fantastic but we only saw monkeys - lots of them - and some birds on our walk. There are many other animals here but they mainly emerge at night. 

Some people complained about the state of the path but with the exception of one small section in the south I would think you could wheel a wheelchair around the rest of the forest as there are good flat dirt roads most of the way round.

Title: Wonderfully peaceful and beautiful
Text:
We walked here from town - take the first right off the main road with the Queens Hotel on the corner, takes 15 mins but last bit quite steep - and spent an idyllic couple of hours wandering around. Amazingly quiet after the noise of Kandy, and beautiful trees everywhere. Make sure you go to the lookout for great views of Kandy.
We were lucky enough to see a large troupe of monkeys go barrelling down the hill, crossing the road right in front of us.
Frustratingly the info board and leaflet tell you the main things you can see but not where they are!

Title: Lovely place for a wander
Text: Had a morning walk around the sanctuary, was a lovely start to the day! Various paths and routes to follow, with some gorgeous trees and rest spots, caves and lookout points. There's a pond there and various wildlife in the park, we saw some monkeys and a water monitor lizard! Well kept pathways and some basic toilets available as well. Watch out for leeches - best to wear shoes, not flip flops as we learned! But it was beautiful and shady, so the walk was comfortable even in the heat of Sri Lanka. Would recommend this over the botanical gardens.

Title: Quiet respite, lots of monkeys
Text: We visited in the morning and spent about 2 hours walking. The paths are fairly well maintained. The forest is full of birdsong and is a respite from the noise and bustle of Kandy. We saw lots of monkeys, some deer, but not much else. The main entrance is a bit tricky to find, and the map isn't that accurate but it's small so difficult to get lost. The map implies there is a second exit near the temple, but this isn't the case (or at least we couldn't find it). The signs are pretty useless and the attractions they send you to are oversold - the viewpoint led up a winding path and ended, with no viewpoint!
