Title: Cheapest and best way to relax and do a bit of excersise in kandy
Text:
Cheapest and best way to relax and do a bit of excersise in kandy. 
Amazes me how many people skip this when they come to Kandy, its so close to the centre of town yet once inside you wouldnt know it as its so quiet and peaceful. 
Highly recommend

Title: place for relax
Text: if you are able to visit this sanctuary you will be amaze. this place is located near to Kandy city and this place has a great history. if you are lucky enough, you will be able to get some great information about this sanctuary and ancient Kandy kingdom from one of the local person lives around here.

Title: Real forest experience a few minutes from Kandy city centre
Text:
Udawattekele is an area of natural forest on the very doorstep of Kandy city.  I visited it with my 14 year old daughter at 06.00 in the morning and we had the whole place pretty much to ourselves - we stayed for around 4 hours.  You get given a map and suggested itinerary at the entrance and the very clear paths make it just about impossible to get lost.
We saw deer, wild boar and the inevitable monkeys along with a variety of birds and insects (but absolutely no leeches!).  But the sheer variety of vegetation is enough to make it worth going it itself.

Title: A very special place in the heart of the town
Text: Superb little forest - just above the Temple of the Tooth. Take a picnic lunch and lots of water and just spend an afternoon or morning wondering around. Lots of birds, butterflies etc

Title: Best thing in kandy!
Text:
Nice and relaxing walk in kandy to get away from the hustle and bustle. 
We walked around for about 2 hours, could spend longer in there or be done a bit quicker though.
We did get some leeches on us so might be best to wear long pants and tuck them into socks.
Maps also arnt the clearest but isnt too hard to find your way.
700 rupes to enter but as it is a conservation area it goes to a goos cause

Title: The best place in Kandy! ! !
Text:
Really enjoyed our time walking around this beautiful forest, if you're keen for peace and quiet out of hectic Kandy then definitely come here. We did however get a bit lost due to the maps not being very informative. 

We made our way down a not so well trotted path and got bitten by a few leeches. Come prepared incase you happen to get lost or want to explore other trails, tuck your pants into your socks!

The entrance price is a bit steep at 700 rupees per person, but not uncommon for Sri Lanka

Title: Nature forest
Text: One of its kind in Asian, this is a uniquely preserved nature forest and you can spend the whole day in this nature forest, it is so relaxing. Entry tickets apply but less than $20.00.

Title: Beautiful Wooded Retreat In The Heart Of A Bustling City
Text: Beautiful and quiet escape from the noise and chaos of Kandy City.  Just watch out for the leeches and wild boar!

Title: NATURE AT IT'S BEST
Text: Amazing view full of nature at it's best and not polluted, and exceptionally breath taking. Any one would enjoy this!

Title: Must visit
Text: We went for a walk just right after a heavy rain. It was a bit muddy but very nice forest walk and fresh air. Lots of birds and butterflies, and monkeys were just jumping around above us.

Title: Hidden Gem
Text: It was my first ever visit to this hidden gem. I had long walks around the sanctuary and loved it all! A must visit to enjoy the nature in a bustling city area. You wont hear a thing other than singing birds.

Title: Have to see.
Text: Out friends loved it. The dancers are great and the costumes make it amazing.Great for kids and families. The fire walking was great. Fire in general is cool. Would do it again.

Title: Not worth it.
Text: We got completely lost and had to exit the sanctuary to find a tuk tuk driver to take us back to the entrance.

Title: Ubspoiled forest but watch out for the Leeches
Text: Unspoilt with some amazing wildlife, a lovely quiet place as well

Title: nice walk
Text:
We enjoyed our walk around the sanctuary .
Very shaded and not loads of birds as a little late in day for them apparenbtly but nonetheless a relaxing bit of shade on a hot day and very tranquil.

Title: Not worth the money spent
Text: Having to pay the steep entrance fees along with the safari charges and guide tips - certainly not worth just to see few elephants. Safari in some other national parks around the world are far far better. Just another commercial establishment like the many others in Srilanka.

Title: I loved my little walk through this forest!
Text: I was completely alone and in 20 minutes walk from Kandy center I felt like I was in a real jungle/forest with monkeys swinging around and peace in the air. Tip: Watch out for leeches. Little ones that will sneakily to your shoe and then to your ankle :)  Don't be scared of that. Go check it out for some fresh air, a GREAT view of Kandy at point E (I think) on the map, and a chance to watch monkeys in their habit and possible little deer that cruise through there.

Title: Forest
Text: Nice and peaceful walk in a forest. You can see many animals like monkeys, agamas, etc. You will get a map at entrance. You need about 2 hours for it.

Title: Udawattekele Sanctuary nice
Text: A breath of fresh air (so to speak in the heat) after the center of Kandy. A beautiful forest with one side a beautiful view of the city but quite noisy as close to the road. On the other you are surrounded by nature with very few visitors, damage some cars or motorcycles go through some trails. Another bad point, the plan is anything but clear to find some points of view. Anyway we enjoyed the meet monkeys, iguanas, snakes and wild boars !!

Title: kandy forest walk
Text:
Udawattekele forest is close to the centre of KANDY and very easy to reach by tuctuc taxi.
There are views toward the city  and kandy lake .
Easy broad paths that lead through the tropical forest around the pond.
A lot of rainforest birds can be heard and spiders and monkeys can be seen.
recommended.

Title: Super but watch your ankles!
Text: After three days hill walking in the tea plantation of Sri Lanka at 3000mtrs we decided to have a rest day today in Kandy. That lasted till 12noon when the hotel manager suggested that we go to the rain forest for a walk. One tuk tuk later, We headed in with our map and local emergence phone, provided by the hotel. At first it was wonderful, huge trees covered in giant vines with monkeys and snakes all over the place. Ants and millepedes the size of your largest finger. Confidently guiding my family with the map i directed them deeper and deeper into the rain forest. The canopy was so dense that it made the forest floor dark. We stopped for a drink then I felt it! I though it was an ant bite, sharpe and pin point pain. I looked down and nearly dropped with the shock. There were five or six leeches on my leg and foot. Bear Grills I am not, I flicked them off and sprinted forward hoping to leave them behind us, the kids followed in panic as there father led the way. My Wife calm and collected walked along, laughing until she too realised that if you stood still the leeches were all over you. I looked down at the ground and the forest floor was alive with leeches. Every two or three inches there was a leech stretching it's neck upward, swaying hoping to find some pale Irish skin. We ran for 3 to 4km through deep jungle as the leeches could not latch on when you ran. In the panic and noise of us all getting eaten alive I realised that i missed jogging. This was fun, soft ground, great scenery and laughs (fear). Who knew, all I missed was the correct motivation. I wondered if they used leeches on usain bolt, no? Should have, they work. Well after a 30min run we got back to the path and onto civilisation. My 10yr old son looked up at me and said "Dad you have three leeches on your face" f&@....... I shouted. I had read the map backwards and led us all into the jungle and off trail. Sorry guys! Two hours later in a super market I found the last leech in my runner, full and bloated. Kids want to move back to Eire!

Title: Elephants fun
Text: Great opportunity to get up close to an elephant, be prepared though the handlers will expect paying, but well worth the 1000 rupees I paid, excellent experience.

Title: overpriced
Text:
A beautiful forest, amazing vines, trees, Dorian fruit trees  Nice view over kandy,. Saw very little wildlife. husband attracted a couple of leeches, rest of us were fine.
Cost almost £10 for a family of 4 which I think is too much.  I know we need to pay to preserve such lovely areas, but I feel Sri Lanka is cashing in too much.
Visit if you have some spare time, makes a pleasant escape from the bustle of kandy.

Title: Leaches!
Text: I really should have listened to past reviewers.  There are serious leaches.  I ended up trail running by the end, which I never do.  Do not go here.  It was awful!

Title: greeny..
Text: The Sinharaja Rain Forest is spectacular. We saw so many endemic birds, snakes and plants to Sri Lanka. We also got to tick off the Sri Lankan Blue Magpie and Sri Lankan Frogmouth from our "to see" list, which was extremely exciting.

Title: we went here instead of the elephant orphanage.
Text: it was nice, what can you say, the elephants were rodden bareback to save chaffing, but my driver insisted we come here instead of the orphanage, I thought a mistake, if I did it again I would do both...beware these are all pricy exercises.

Title: woodland in the city
Text: this beautiful little forest is located within the city yet is a true forest with lots of birds and insects giving it a calm feel. an afternoon sroll under the large canopy and shrubs was an amazing feeling before luch.

Title: Beautiful!! An amazing experience
Text: Its a jungle walk with sound of nature all around..chirping of birds, a myna's song, woodpeckers' call, owl's gaze, wild flowers, old tree roots winding all around and sun rays peeking from the lush green thick mane of the trees! kids loved it!!

Title: A true sanctuary yet so nearby the crowded town center
Text: Do your self a favour and take a threewheeler around 6AM to the Royal Forest Park entrance. For 650 LKR (locals pay 30 rupees) you enter the quietest easy-to-access tropical forest just a stone-throw away from the overcrowded Kandy town center. After entering the forest take a left-left to follow the anti-clockwise route until you eventually reach a visitor's center (one hour walk). From there, continue 100m to exit the park left-ish towards the Kandy lake side and you are back into the city. Do not expect too much birds but clean air and quietness are kind of priceless too. Walking paths are well maintained so buggy's can be taken there (only in dry season). The reason that you can't bring any food into the park is that Sri Lankans don't understand the concept of not throwing anything away ... Only recommendation I could make is to let people enter on the other side as well. Why isn't this allowed??

Title: Enjoyable early morning walk
Text:
It was a pleasant surprise to be given a map when we paid our entrance fee to the sanctuary.  So often in Sri Lanka we have found that we have had to pay high entrance fees, then no map.  We went early, in order to enjoy the birdlife.  It was a very pleasant, slow two hour walk, as we tried to identify the wide variety of birdcalls we heard.  This was a struggle, as the sanctuary is well wooded and the birds quite elusive.  We identified and photographed a few, also saw a family of wild boar, a troop of monkeys and a deer.  Highlights for us were spotting Lesser Goldenback and Crimsonbacked Goldenbacks (woodpeckers) and seeing a Lesser Hill Mynah on its nest in a hole in a tree.

The walk is very well signposted with a number of routes.  We only did the main circuit, which is about 3km.  Very quiet, very peaceful.

Title: Don't tell everyone about this place!
Text:
A lovely area of forest sits on the hill above Kandy.  So peaceful and varied with many species of the trees and other plants which grow in the Hill Country.  Huge spiral lianas wind up into the canopy in places and birdsong fills the air.

It is a bit difficult to match the map on your ticket to the paths and signs at junctions in the forest add to the unclear advice you get from the bored person who issues the entrance tickets.

But this is an unpolluted oasis above the city and one well worth a visit - not to be missed.

Title: Stunning trees and plants...mind the leaches
Text:
Great little walk round the loop path of the Sanctuary through some awe inspiring trees and vines.

We saw very little wildlife except for a brief hint of a deer and possible turtle in the pond, but the leaches were out in force in the wet and mud, so ensure you have closed shoes - my flipflops were useless!

Title: watch out for leeches if wet
Text: we went after a lot of rain intop this rain forest. Despite the easy to walk paths being wide and free of vegetation, little leeches found us. Take a bar of soap to get them off-better still rub ankles with soap before start. Im sure if dry theyd not be a problem and wed have enjoyed it !. We saw no birds

Title: Amazing vegetation!
Text: Saw really incredible Liane plants, they look like the huge chains of ship anchors, amazing how they grow up into the air, some really high, across the paths. Can only imagine they grew over some saplings and then waited a couple of hundred years for the tree to grow and carry them up into the air. Truely asonishing to see it for the first time.

Title: Good afternoon activity
Text: I had a good weather when I ventured here. I didn't really get leeches or was sunburnt. The path was a bit confusing especially if you follow the map so it';s better to ask the person at the gate about it first. It's a refuge from the noise of the city.

Title: Nice place to stroll
Text:
very nice stroll that gives you a feeling of nature while still being in the city. Nice great trees, thick jungle, you can peer at specific animals at some point : lizards, snakes, butterflies.
It is well maintained with good pathways with clear indications so giving a chance to walk around for everyone. those who want more of an adventure feeling can go on smaller paths. Inside the park you have buddhist retreat places. Some great viewpoints to observe from a higher perspective the Kandy valley and surrounding mountains.

Title: Did see a few other tourists
Text: Enjoyed this solace in the town. We had a troop of monkeys literally cross our path. I don't think they realised we were there. They were doing something with the toilets, I don't know what exactly was happening but it is an area they need to improve on.

Title: Excellent place to walk around
Text: Fantastic place to see lots of wildlife right next to the city centre. We saw monkeys, deer, lizards, turtles in their natural habitat, it was amazing! We normally do things quickly but took a good couple of hours to walk around. Great place to visit although beware for leeches! Even though we'd read about them and covered up with closed shoes and long trousers, my husband still managed to get a bite from one, only noticed a few hours later when he took his jeans off and his leg was pouring of blood!

Title: Primeval forest located above Sri Dalada Maligawa
Text: It is also known as the forbidden forest of the kings of Kandy. A great place to hike for a couple of hours enjoying he nature and viewing some bird life. With some luck you might see wild boar, Money's, Hare, Squirrels, Porcupines, and seven some reptiles, Water monitors, Lizards, Tortise and a variety of birds,. The pond in the heart of the jungle is believed to be the the place where queens in the pas bathed and used as their player garden. The brown fish owl is a famous sighting in the forest though you have to spend a little Ike to spot it and in one visit you might not see all above... Would highly recommend this visit I anyone who has 1-2 hours o spare whilst in Kandy. During the wet season just be cautious about the leeches.

Title: Real Jungle!
Text: An amazing area of untouched tropical jungle within walking distance of the city. Don't go off-track - there's leeches, as we quickly found out! Lots of wildlife and amazing vegetation.

Title: A great hike
Text: This is a great hike - beautiful country, paths are good and plenty of monkeys. We heard a lot of birds but didnt see too many so probably best to go early morning if you can. We took about 2 hours but you could do it in an hour if you didnt have lots of time. But there are small leaches so wear shoes, socks and long pants - and after check your legs. I got back to the hotel and was lying around on the bed and noticed blood everywhere!

Title: beautiful sanctuary but beware of the leeches
Text: the scenry is just beautiful: a rainforest not far outside of Kandy - huge trees, some monkeys, dense vegetation, nice views of Kandy - a little information centre - just nice to walk. we were there in the rainy season, and then the leeches are obviously very active - unfortunatly we got lost - and so took a tiny path, the rain started - and as soon we stopped to get orientation, leeches crawled up your shoes - so many that we couldn't avoid bites. I think if we'd stayed on the swept paths there would have been less risk - so it was partly our fault of course

Title: Leopard and bear
Text: Spent one full day in Wilpattu and we were lucky to see a leopard and a bear at the end of the day. Big park less crowded than Yala and then much more easy.

Title: Amazing Trip and we saw Leoards
Text: We visited this area twice and was blessed to see a leopard on both days.  We also saw a sloth bear, which was a lucky sighting.

Title: Diverse Wildlife
Text: Early morning ride at 0630 to this park. Some wild life you can expect are Wild Water Buffalo, Monkey, Sri Lankan Flapshell Turtle, Sri Lankan Junglefowl, Peacock and Deer. Need to have their Rangers 4X4 to enter and is a separate charge for that. After nearly two hours managed to spot a Sri Lankan Leopard and of course we are not only the vehicles there at that time. A bit surprise for this excursion are no elephant were spotted however is fine with whatever was there.

Title: True Joy Like being on the Set of Bambi or the Jungle Book
Text:
This was a highlight of our trip 5 hours in a jeep with a guide who knew how to find the animals.

It was like being on the set of Bambi  and then Jungle book.  Highly recommend. 

We gave the Guide a very good tip 5000 Rupees for his very efforts .  We saw a Leopard, Elephant Sloth bears, wart hogs and a jackal plus lots of other animals and birds.

Title: Great
Text: A beautiful national park with lots of animals. We did a half day tour on a rainy and overcast day and we didn't see any leopards, other than that we had a great time. Be prepared for bumpy ride.

Title: Fantastic
Text:
Beautiful park - we had an afternoon safari and a morning safari the next day. Both roughly 4 hours in duration.

Guides were fab and we were lucky enough to see an elephant in the water, as well as a leopard! Much calmer and quieter than the other parks we visited on our tour of Sri Lanka - would definitely recommend this as the best. 

Be warned - the toilets in the picnic area of the park are interesting and i would avoid if you can! Also watch out for the monkeys in this area - they didn't both us but some people were teasing them with food and lets just say they are not shy!

Title: Good but Leopards remained elusive
Text: Wilpattu is the oldest and largest (1317 sq km) National Park in Sri Lanka and we explored it from the delightful Leopard Trails luxury tented safari camp.  The camp is only a few minutes drive from the National Parks entrance gate and our journeys to and from the park were partly taken on the wrong side of the road.   The local rice farmers have worked out that by spreading their newly harvested rice over one carriageway, the rice dries twice as quickly (using the heat attracted by the black tarmac) as traditional methods.  We took three drives (one full day and two half days) which saw us cover a good deal of the parks forested, sandy and lake side areas.  It was great to see many animals in their natural habit and spotted deer, water buffalo, jackals and wild boar made regular appearances.  An elephant entertained us by standing in the lake, ripping vast quantities of water plants up, shaking off the mud and munching them for its tea.  There were many species of birds to admire, with sea eagles catching their supper from the lake, serpent eagles and owls staring regally from their tree perches and our favourite, the brightly coloured varieties of bee eaters.  Often our drives seemed like we were driving through snow, as white butterflies settled in mud pools to collect minerals and then burst into blizzard like flight as we passed close by.  A picture postcard position beside the lake was perfect for a sumptuous lunch.  A little drama was added by monkeys watching us closely for the chance of any left overs and us keeping a careful eye on the partly submerged crocodile twenty meters out in the lake.  Further searching revealed many other sightings, even a brief glimpse of a Sloth Bear.  Sadly the key attraction (leopards) remained elusive for everyone

Title: A must you need a full day
Text:
We are staying in wilputa nature resort only 10min away from the back entrance of the park for two people its a bit more then 7800 r 
We have seen so much many different animals and birds , this park will stay in our memories we have seen 3 leopards also a leopard attack on a group of monkeys

Title: Perfect!
Text: We Saw 3 leopards... And a lot of other animals! Above that is the Parc lovely on itself! We had a refreshing pack during the break. Thank you for the perfect morning!

Title: Be prepared... and if you have done safari in Africa think twice
Text: Our guide was good - but that is about the only positive thing I can say. The "roads" and I use the term loosely - are horrible. This would be okay except that the vehicles are worse.  They put sets on a flat bed truck - no suspension at all.  Bone jarring.  The guides seem over focused on seeing a leopard and the competition between vehicles to be the first there is dangerous and crazy.  While there are some nice wet land areas here, the drive to get to these areas is quite long.  If you have a bad back .. beware

Title: Terrible safari experience
Text:
Really disappointing, saw literally nothing. Drivers all went too fast and far too noisy. At one stage they were cutting each other up and racing! 
Seemed to have no idea where the animals might be, or the best way to not scare them off. Driver barely spoke to us. 
Expensive waste of money!

Title: A wonderful park
Text: Not as famous as Yala in the south but far less crowded. And you still get to see most of the wildlife, particularly the beautiful birds and the elusive leopard.

Title: Great wildlife experience
Text: Unfortunately we arrived late and so only had two hours in the park. We were 4 of us in a Jeep, with the driver working hard to ensure we saw the best of e park, part way through a leopard was sighted and we were lucky enough to get there in time to see it - an amazing experience

Title: A NICE SETTING AND A NICE FIND
Text: My tour had less than three hours in the park but we did manage to see a range of animals. On the western side of the island, it is close to Anuradhapura. The geography of the park varied. Most of it is forested. Some of the tree species are worth looking at plus various hanging vines. The dirt roads, of an orange reddish colour, were not bad but there were numerous potholes and portions that were not level but this is a national park. The park hours are 0600 to 1800. The only animals in any abundance were the spotted deer. There were numerous peacocks. Other birds included parrots and egrets. A couple of iguana were seen and one turtle sunning itself. Water buffalo were seen in the water and grazing. The star of the afternoon was a somewhat hidden leopard. It did eventually walk off into the bush, clearly annoyed at the presence of so many jeeps and the level of noise. I was concerned with the speed the jeeps went en route to the leopard. Maybe there are no speed limits. At the gate were toilet facilities and a canteen/restaurant. The fourth star was for the leopard sighting.

Title: Park visit
Text: The park is beautiful so much to see. It did not feel like too many vehicles chasing around. You are in the centre of the park with such amazing scenery we saw a number of animals and birds. I liked how the keeps kept well away from the animals. The lunch area was great even with all the naught macaque monkeys around. Get a naturalist to go with you around park they are a source of knowledge makes the trip way more exciting.

Title: Wonderful (despite not seeing leopards!)
Text:
Fantastic place with so much beauty. Had a thoroughly enjoyable experience and saw some amazing wildlife. Loads to see and plenty of opportunities for photos!

We went just after sunrise and was still very quiet. Looked like it was getting a bit busier by 11am, however not as busy as lots of other places

Title: Beautiful Park
Text:
We did a morning safari beginning of January 2020. Park is stunning, Nature, animals, though we didn't see any leopard, worth the trip. We did our booking through Best Of Lanka company. We were very disappointed by this company, as we didn't have any naturalist with us and the driver could hardly speak English and didn't have any binoculars; so very few interactions. The jeep was in poor condition, one of the seats was broken.
The experience remains overall very good, thank to the beautiful landscapes and animals we spotted.

Title: Nice drive and lots of small animals.
Text: We enjoyed the drive through...the roads had tree canopy completely through the bush....it was so different from, say an African safari.  Not a lot of wildlife, but enough to keep one interested.

Title: Wilpattu National Park - Sri Lanka touring with G Adventures.
Text: Had the good fortune to be in Sri Lanka earlier this year on a  G Adventures tour which visited this national park on day two of the tour.  Very lucky to be in the right place at the right time to see this magnificent elusive specimen of a leopard almost at the end of the late afternoon game drive.  Kudos to a Canadien lady in our group who managed to take these shots and share them with us.  Aside from that we also saw a sloth bear, elephants, asiatic buffalo, crocodiles, a golden jackal, various mongoose, sambur and spotted dear, grey langur monkeys and more bird species than I can remember.  The animal viewing is not on a scale like Africa but in saying that, for such a small island with such a large population it punches way above it's weight. A lovely country with great weather and great people.  Hats off to G Adventures for providing a wonderful trip.

Title: Wonderful visit
Text: Had one safari ride in the park and saw such a variety of animals  - a leopard, elephant, jackal, crocodile, monitor lizards, numerous birds, deer etc. Went to 4 other parks while in Sri Lanka which were all very different but this one certainly offered the greatest variety. Brilliant!

Title: Nice park
Text: Beautiful park. We saw a leopard and a lot of birds. Monkeys and varans. Beautiful surroundings, unfortunately we did not spot any elephants.

Title: Wilpattu National Park Jeep Safari
Text:
Great half-day Jeep Safari with sightings of Leopard, Sloth Bear, Red Spotted Deer, Samba Deer, Wooly Necked Stork amongst many others. Much rain the last days so great trails on very muddy tracks and around several lakes.
Highly recommended.

Title: Great experience
Text:
We visited Wilpattu National Park in August 2019.  Although there had been little rain we were fortunate to see a multitude of wildlife.

Strangely we only saw 2 elephants, one just inside the park on entry and one some distance away when we were leaving.

We took notice of one sign regarding the leopards.  The sign says while you are looking for me I am watching you.  How true, we were lucky to see a leopard on our way out of the park only because the guide pointed in out.  It was sitting in a tree and was very well camouflaged.  

We also were lucky enough to see a Sloth Bear, Spotted Deer, Barking Deer, Buffalo, Sambar, Mongoose, Monitor Lizard, Mugger Crocodile, Serpent Eagle, Jungle Fowl, Peacocks and many other types of birdlife.

Title: National Park contains ancient ruins
Text: Many reviewers have spoken about the amazing wildlife that can be seen in this National Park. But we went there to see some ancient ruins and an Baobab tree that was planted an extremely long time ago. To see the tree, you have to travel by boat from a fishing village called "Gange Wadiya" and the return trip takes about 1 hour. The other ancient ruins lie deep within the National Park. These include the stone pillars of what is considered a palace that belonged to a queen called Kuveni. The other ruin is sadly just a foundation of a statue of a horse holding a lantern that guided vessels into the nearby harbour which no longer exists. Nearby is an 40 foot long tomb of a Muslim saint who was supposed to be extremely tall.

Title: The wild Sri Lanka
Text: Compared to othe parks in Sri Lanka, this one offered the greatest variety of animals seen so far. It all started with a sloth bear we were able to follow for about 20 minutes. Many, many wonderful birds, Bee-Eatres, Kingfisher, Owls, Eagles, sometimes that close that I was not able to shoot a photo (when a Bee-Eater flew through our car...). And, yes, we saw a leopard. Even though he was a bit far away an vanished soon after we spotted him...it's always a matter of luck.

Title: Great Wildlife experience
Text: We had a full day guided tour in this amazing national park. Our guide was well connected with other drivers and service providers so that he got right information about locations of animals. Amazing park to see variety of animals including large group of deer, lots of beautiful birds, rabbits, leopard and many more.

Title: Our great leopard experience
Text:
Wilpattu sits a little bit off the regular organised tour circuit, positioned slightly north of the central west coast of the country. It's also Sri Lanka's largest national park. These two factors mean that you'll experience less safari traffic than in Yala or even Kaudulla. Another benefit, if you're lucky enough to discover a leopard or other large animal, is that there is no mobile phone reception so safari guides cannot readily communicate sightings to stimulate a mad dash by everyone within range to share the experience.

It's a selfish view, but it paid off for us when we encountered a leopard on a lakeside trail in a more remote part of the park. Our driver slowly reversed the vehicle as our leopard followed us back down the trail for about 15 minutes before padding off into the jungle. 

We also encountered a Fishing Eagle and Crested Serpent Eagle within telephoto lens range in this park - something we had not been able to do elsewhere. Wilpattu also offers encounters with the usual suspects - water buffalo, land monitors, wild boar, spotted and barking deer, crocodiles and a wide variety of birds.

Title: Great afternoon animal spotting
Text: Unfortunately we didnt spot the elusive leopard, but we did see plenty of bird life, some deer, buffalo, heaps of monkeys and a few elephants. However the jungle is super thick so it was difficult to get good pics with just a phone. Heaps of fun bouncing round the tracks in super comfy jeeps though, and the drivers made a really great attempt retracing their steps so that we could see as much wild life as possible.

Title: Beautiful national park
Text: Wilpattu National Park is one of the most beautiful national parks in the country. We saw a huge variety of animals, including leopards, deer, rabbits, eagles, owls, king fishers and much more. Make sure to arrive early and to have a good driver with a naturalist. The entrance fee of USD 20 is reasonable.

Title: Paradise on earth
Text: If you are a nature lover or simply a wildlife photography buff such as myself, you will instantly fall in love with this place. Easy to access, compact enough to see in several days, you will amazed at the variety of wildlife this park has to offer. Elephants, leopards and bear just to name a few. If Africa is a little too far away and out of your budget, then this place comes a very close second. Totally enjoyed my stay here.

Title: Wilpattu a great leopard watching experience.
Text:
Although the area has dense vegetation, we still spotted 14+ different kinds of animals and birds. The highlight was watching a young female leopard trying to catch monkeys in the trees right beside us. Among the birds the highlights were two species of stork, a fish eagle, many sightings of peacock and the Sri Lanka national bird and Hornby last.  Animals included many deer, elephant and monkeys among others. 
Jeeps wait at the turnoff on the main Puttalam-Anuradhapura highway.

Title: Fantastic
Text: We were fortunate to see all of 'the big 3' here - elephant, leopard and sloth bear. Excellent driver and guide who know where to go and stopped frequently to point out animals and birds. A fabulous day.

Title: National Park or Highway
Text:
Having never been to a wild animal national park had me exicted expecting to see large quantitiies of free roaming  wildlife of all sorts.
Yes I did see  the odd crane/egret  some water buffalo as well.
The main stay of the park is elephants grazing with their young which is goog to see.
I was told there were crocodiles,jaguar and many species of birds alas one eagle no crocodiles one peacock .
My final impression of this park the cost of a 2 hour drive on very bumpy roads(to be expected) $100 be careful about this as the Jeep companies will take 100 aus or US whichever comes out of your wallet.
We tourists create our own problems of course and the big one for this park is the amount of traffic jams in a national park like this as it is not controlled.
You will not be alone looking at wildlife as most of the time there will be 20 jeeps behind you full of loud screeching tourists taking photos of scared elephants.
Thats why you wont see lots of wildlife , think about it and for me sad and disappointing.

Title: Sloth bears
Text: We went on a jeep safari and unluckily saw no elephants nor leopards. There were lots of exotic birds, crocs and sloth bears.  A good trip

Title: Possibly better than Yala
Text:
Amazing!!
Guided by Nuwan Deninanda of Wilpattu safaris (separate review).
Wide range of animals
Low number of jeeps
Not much commercialisation

I have been to both Wilpattu and Yala. Personal opinion is that Wilpattu has a distinctive edge.

Title: Wilpattu park
Text: A 5hour (half day) jumpy bumpy safari. Before the start of the safari my driver has said seeing animals on safari is about luck. Well luck was not with me on my visit to Wilpattu park. Thats not 100% true... I did see deer, one water buffalo, mongoose, birds and lots of butterflies. The ride itself was not an enjoyable experience and after three hours in the heat bouncing around the back of a jeep I had had enough. I wouldnt personally recommend doing a safari

Title: A fabulous jeep safari where we spotted a Sloth Bear
Text: An early morning start to visit Wilpattu for the morning. Really good fun and luckily we had the tour guide in our jeep, who pointed out all the beautiful birds and wild life including peacocks, deer, water buffalo, monkeys, elephants, crocodile and the legendary sloth bear who was eating termites. Others spotted a leopard but sadly we missed this. Enjoyable trip nevertheless.

Title: Long drive but worth it
Text:
We have done a full day safari here. Beautiful atmosphere and a nice drive. Little bit tiring but worth it. We have been to the first fleet where is thambapannee. 

We saw leopard, elephants deers and lots of birds.

Title: Amazing Wildlife Experience
Text:
A very full day in safari style jeeps over fairly rough tracks, looking for a wide range of wildlife especially leopards & elephants
The guides are very good and work hard to find animals for you to see, they also provide a lunch
We got up close to three leopards and got some amazing photos we also seen sloth bears, elephants (a fare way off), mongoose, jackal and about 45 bird species
Great place and a must do

Title: Wonderful national park to see leopards on their own environment
Text: I can highly recommend this place to visit. We saw leopards six times during our full day safari. We were told that we were very lucky. You can also see elephants, crocodiles, lizards, deers, monkeys. There is also lots of birds (rare ones too) to bee seen.

Title: Wonderful safari
Text: 11 hours of animal watching was terrific. We saw leopards and axis deer and much more. Loved watching all the birds. It wasn't just the animals the whole area is so beautiful.

Title: Amazing wildlife
Text: We did an 11 hour safari through the park. We saw leopards and axis deer and so much more. The bird watching is amazing. Watch out for the monkeys near the place where the safari trucks stop for breaks. They will steal your lunch and anything else that they can grab. Fun to watch though.

Title: Not Too busy
Text:
We went on two safaris  and were lucky enough to see 2 Sloth Bears and a leopard along with plenty of deer, birds and reptiles 
On trhe second we went through a very sandy part around a lake eventually stopping for a wonderful breakfast

Title: The best place to see exotic animals
Text: It was no doubt a memorable experience for me. The best part is when our driver calls everyone else to come to our location. We were able to see the entire movements of the animals while not disturbing them. Would come back!

Title: vast reserve though animals are not easy to see
Text:
this is the biggest of the wildlife reserves in Srilanka. tourists need to pay about £18 to get in & take note of this along with vehicle hire & guide.
we were unlucky that we saw only one elephant & just a fleeting glimpse of a leopard during our 2 visits to the reserve

Title: Not our favorite
Text: We were expecting to see elephants at least, if not a leopard!   Saw peacocks, and ....more peacocks and ... more peacocks.   One road leads in and out of the park so you're not able to really look for game.   If it's on the road as you drive past, you're lucky.   Felt our driver wasn't really paying attention and the safari vehicles were quite uncomfortable.   Having spent 4 or 5 hours in the park and only spotting birds and a few deer, I was disappointed and felt that I had wasted a morning.

Title: Highly recommend to visit
Text:
Highly recommended place to visit. This area is famous for its leopards population but unfortunately we didnt see any of them. 
We saw elephants, crocodile, lizards, deers, wild boars, monkeys and lots of different types of birds. 
The tour takes about 4 hours.

Title: Choose your guide and driver carefully!
Text: The we a half day morning safari. The park itself is beautiful and we spotted a lot of wildlife including crocodiles, peacocks, various birds, wild pigs and buffalos. Sadly no bears, elephants or leopards for which the park is famous. I think this is largely down to our jeep driver who was driving so fast through the park, I do not think we would have been able to spot a leopard even if it were right next to us. We arranged the tour through our guesthouse in Anuradhapura. If you plan to go to the park, I would advise doing your research and arranging a reputable guide and driver. Whether or not you see animals is partly down to luck but also highly dependant on the experience of them.

Title: Disappointing
Text:
Only birds to be seen, no elephants, leopards, beards. Not much to see.
Better Parks around, like Minneriya even if it is overcrowded.

Title: The Best Nature Reserve in Sri Lanka.....!!!
Text: If you like to see the wild life of Sri Lanka, then i would recommend Wilpattu as your number 1 choice. there is something magical about that place and there is something for every type of nature and wildlife lover.....make it a point to visit at least once......you will not regret it....I am sure....!!!

Title: Saw elephants and a bear
Text: We took a 2.5 hour safari starting at around 10.00 am.  We saw lots of small animals and birds but the highlight for me was a bear, ambling across the road in front of us, plus a couple of elephants in the middle distance.  No leopards but the park condition you to this with a sign at the entrance that says something like "you might not see us, but we are watching you".  I really enjoyed the park and was happy with what we saw.

Title: Disappointing.  Not worth the effort or cost.
Text: At the park gates at 6.30 am. Spent the next six hours sitting in a jeep riding through the forest but only saw a few significant birds, many monkeys, deer, 4 tigers and couple of other animals.  The park is not teeming with wildlife.

Title: Variety of animals / birds without too many jeeps
Text:
I was wary of other national parks in Sri Lanka (e.g. Yala, Minneriya) as I had heard they were very busy with jeeps and I really don't enjoy viewing wildlife when you are one of 20 jeeps crowded around - so I thought I would give Wilpattu a try.

I did one full-day safari and started at the Eluwankulama entrance - it was quiet when I went, there were no queues and the only other jeep there was carrying the other guests from my hotel. 

The biggest group of jeeps that I saw at once (aside from at the rest stop) was when a leopard had been sighted in the bushes. At that point there were maybe 6-8 jeeps in the vicinity waiting for the leopard to make an appearance. The leopard did indeed come out and crossed the road in a flash! At other times throughout the day, we passed the occasional other jeep but often went long stretches of time without seeing anyone else which was really nice.

The park is vast, a lot of it is wooded and so it felt harder to spot animals for this reason. There are several watering holes and you can see animals drinking around the perimeter. I did see a huge variety of birds, elephants (including a large group just before the entrance/exit to the park - I was the only jeep there), 2 leopards (fleeting / at a distance), monitor lizards, deer, monkeys... The wildlife is fewer and far between compared to other places perhaps, and we did go a couple of hours without seeing any animals at all. When you do spot something though, it feels extra special for this reason.

I didn't love the rest stop where I was brought for breakfast / lunch - too many monkeys which steal food and climb into the jeeps. They are afraid of the drivers but certainly not afraid of the tourists. There are basic squat toilet facilities. I would have preferred to have parked near one of the water holes in the park and eaten there instead. 

Overall, if you go with the right attitude and don't expect a zoo - you will enjoy Wilpattu.

Title: A truly wild park - not Longleat
Text:
We did 2 safaris at Wilpattu. One was an afternoon safari and one was an all day safari. 
Wilpattu is a big park and there are less roads than at Yala, but there are also a lot less jeeps, and for much of our wildlife viewing we were on our own. During our afternoon safari we watched a sloth bear feeding from a termite nest very close to the road. We were able to sit there for around 20 minutes and during that time we were joined by maybe half a dozen other jeeps - a complete contrast to Yala where around 30 jeeps were competing for a view of a sloth bear which was much further away from the road.
We saw lots of animals and birds. We didn't see a leopard but we saw plenty of evidence that they were around - lots of very recent footprints in the sand - it's down to luck whether you actually see one or not, but the chance is obviously increased by the number of safaris you undertake.
There is a place where they stop for lunch and breakfast where there is also a basic hole in the ground type toilet. Beware of all the monkeys there, who will steal your food at any opportunity!
As expected it is a very bumpy ride in the jeep and my husband suffered a bit as he has some joint problems - especially during the all day safari, which lasted from 6.15am to 6.00pm. However the advantage of the all day safari is that they can take you much further into the park, away from any other jeeps. This park is not for kids who will easily get bored - but it is a genuinely immersive wildlife experience.

Title: Absolutely loved it!
Text: We had a great trip around the great Wilpattu National Park. We saw both black bears, crocodiles, water buffalos, deer, monkeys, elephants and even a leopard, which was quite a rare sight, we were told. Perhaps we were lucky, but we chose the park for it's actual wildlife, which means you cannot be sure what you get to see during your visit. The is definitely preferred over the captive or sedated animals you may find in other countries.

Title: Underrated
Text: Lovely scenic National Park with great wildlife, and birds. We had a good driver and guide who drove us all over this lovely park over 2 days to find the animals we wanted to see. The rest stops were pretty rustic, but adequate. The roads were bumpy dirt roads and 2 days in the back of a jeep was enough.

Title: Vast but sparse
Text: A safari park in the north west of Sri Lanka. It is vast but animal life is sparce. We did see one Leopard, a couple of elephants in the distance, lots of monkeys and a several species of birds. Apart from the leopard nothing to wow.

Title: A great safari park in Puttlam. Sri Lanka
Text: We rented a Jeep and had an evening safari / game drive. Saw lots of animals and birds. The driver / tour guide was fantastic, He was very good in spotting the rare birds and other wild life.

Title: We were lucky, less crowded safari
Text: We dont like Yala as there are far too many jeeps. Here we were aware of maybe ten together when we came across a bear. Much less busy. We did see two leopards, mainly due to the experience of our driver who recognised the warning cries of the monkies.

Title: Wonderful wildlife park
Text: Recently reopened after the war, there are leopards, deer, myriad birds, mongooses, elephants and many other fascinating wild animals to see. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit though sadly did not see a leopard!

Title: Long trips
Text: We did 2 trips on the same day here and it would have been better to do one longer trip. Some interesting birdlife but did not see either the elusive leopard or a sloth bear. The last hour of each trip was wasted

Title: Leopard and elephant tracking
Text: We were told to go here because it wasn't as busy as some of the other safari adventures.  This may be because we didn't see any leopards or elephants!!  It was great roaring round in the SUV's and we did see a Sloth bear, crocodile, deer, peacocks, big lizards etc.  The drivers all seemed really disappointed that we didn't see any of the key animals!

Title: Beautiful nature and some wild animals
Text:
Reading many reviews here, I must conclude that many hotels nearby the park who organize the Jeep tours are scamming the tourists, which is really sad. We stayed at The Backwaters and organized our safari trip with them and found them to be very trustworthy. They charged us LKR 6500 (Feb 2019), for a private Jeep fitting up to 6 people with an extra guide to sit with us. The Jeep and entrance fee must be paid in the local currency. 

Seeing a leopard or a bear is up to luck, and we unfortunately didnt see these animals. We came close to spotting a leopard in the bushes but mostly the guide spotted it and could take a picture of it for us. The bushes are really dense so you have to be really lucky or early to spot a leopard walking up to you on the roads or in an open space. 

We did a half day safari starting from 6:30 to about 11am. By the end of it we were pretty beat. So maybe it's more advisable to do a morning and evening safari on two separate days if you wish. Bring a jacket and wear light long pants as the Jeep is open (windy) and the morning air gets quite cold. 

The drive in is through a long road of dense bush land which might be a bit boring if you can't spot anything. There are small ponds where you might spot crocodiles. Our favorite spots were the open spaces with a sort of marshland or watering hole / lakes which look like a dreamland. There you can spot heards of deers, and if you're lucky like us, a large elephant swimming through the water! Simply magical! We also spotted wild boars, many birds, a turtle, a ferret and monkeys. Of course we wished we'd seen more large animals but it is up to luck really. 

We would rate the park more highly if it would have had more plentiful, and better maintained washrooms which are a basic necessity for an area which invites tourists to visit it. There is no soap, the toilet is a squatting toilet which you can't even flush, so you can imagine the smell. Please bring your own toilet paper and hand soap... And of course someone has to invariably take a dump just on the side of the toilet hole itself. Why??? If you can, use the washroom near the ticketing office and avoid drinking till you're about to leave the park again.

Title: A true gem. Must see!
Text:
Wilpattu is such a beautiful place. On the huge grassy plains, between the large ponds lives the most diverse and vivid wildlife of all parks. In Minneriya & Kaudulla it's all about elephants. But in Wilpattu we saw myriads of colorful birds, lots of eagles, giant lizards, impressive crocodiles, scary snakes, cute turtles, cheeky monkeys, laughing jackals, shy flocks of deer, rare leopards and of course: elephants. In general, there are much less visitors than in the other parks (especially Yala) we barely saw any other jeeps.
If you need to choose only one park in Sri Lanka, this is the one to go.

Title: An Interesting if Tiring Experience
Text: The park is large so you need a lot of time and are not guaranteed to see specific animals given how far they can roam. It does take about 1 and a half hours down rough tracks to get from the entrance to the start of the main viewing spots which are around about 10 very scenic lakes spread over a large area. Bear in mind you have to return down the same route at the end of the day. The birdlife is great - we would have liked to remain by a lake to see what turned up but the driver obviously wants to see if he can find other animals in different sections.  We did not see any elephants on our visit but were lucky enough to see a leopard which is not apparently common.

Title: Awesome
Text: Acres of space  - immense opportunities to see the variety of wildlife both in terms of bird life and mammals. We were lucky to encounter Elephants, Monitor Lizards, Starcross Tortoise Bears Water Buffalo Deer Crocs monkeys Peacocks Eagles you name it it was there to be seen in their natural environment. Our only disappointment being the elusive leopards. I feel were were simply unlucky. An experience of a lifetime - one that we shall always remember.

Title: Worth a visit if you're up in Anuradhapura
Text: We recently visited Anuradhapura and ventured across to Wilpattu for a safari.  We decided to eschew Yala as it has a reputation of being very busy, so can't comment on that, but Wilpattu isn't as quiet as we expected - even if there are only a dozen or so vehicles, you'll still end up seeing the same cars time and again as you search endlessly for wildlife!  The bush is pretty thick in places in Wilpattu, so spotting stuff can be pretty tricky at times, particularly if your driver is driving at a quicker pace that you'd like!  We started early - we were in the park by 6.15am - and it was cold, particularly with the windchill when driving - if you go early, do yourself a favour and take some warm layers with you!  We did spot quite a few things on our day safari - lots of birdlife, and quite a few mammals and reptiles too.  We weren't lucky enough to see a leopard on this occasion, but we did see a sloth bear late in the day and there's clearly a grapevine as within 10 minutes of spotting it there were about 10 vehicles around us!  We noticed quite a few vehicles had separate guides while we just had a driver - haveing done other safaris this concerned us, as normally a separate guide is a good thing (we re-organised our safari late due to issues with our previously arranged trip so had little choice!) and while we managed OK in the end I'd suggest a separate guide would be better.  It can be a very long day though - we were in at 6.15am and left the park at about 5.30pm, having been batttered and bruised from the drive in the meantime.  Still, it was well worth it - while we seemed to spend more time driving round to find stuff than we'd have liked, we did see a decent quantity and variety of animals in the end, and came away feeling pretty happy about it (probably the sloth bear siting helped!)

Title: Silent Forest
Text: Well, best ideal time to see some animals like leopards, bears etc. is in early morning. If you got a full day ride or morning ride, it's better to enter to park by 6am. Chance of meeting elephants are bit higher in evening. And during the March & April, chance of meeting bears is quit high. Most importantly, if you want to see wildlife make sure you ask your safari driver to drive bit patiently through the park. Because some of them are racing through the park.

Title: Hidden gem of Sri Lanka
Text:
We were not sure we could fit Wilpattu National Park in as we only had one night to spare.  

We set off from Colombo and the drive took approx 3hrs to reach the Treehouse Hotel right at the NAtional PArk Entrance Gate.  

We were keen to see the elusive leopards and the trip did not disappoint.  Hidden gem of Sri Lanka and a lot less crowded than Yala.

We went on a full day safari and had 2x  leopard sightings in the morning.

Title: A Great Park!
Text: We did an all day tour arranged by the folks at Ruuk Village. The wildlife that was around and the lighting for photography was different in the morning and evening so it was worth it to do both in my opinion. Our driver was fantastic - following leopard tracks in the sand, while driving on some crazy terrain and pointing out other wildlife at the same time! It was not crowded at all and the landscape was really interesting. Go with an open mind and you'll have a great time - we saw a lot of wild life, birds, reptiles, all sorts of mammals. We went with zero expectations of seeing a leopard and were pleasantly surprised to see one at the end of the day.  Keep in mind - this isn't a zoo so you can't control what animals make an appearance. I would definitely recommend a visit to this park!

Title: Best park we visited in Sri Lanka
Text:
We did the all day tour at Wilpattu which our driver arranged for us. Lucky day for us as we saw a leopard walk right in front of our parked jeep.  Thanks to our jeep driver who knew just where to wait.  Do not get impatient if your driver decides to stop his jeep and just wait!!
We also saw lots of spotted deer, an elephant having a spa day, mongoose, many bird varieties, crocs and monkeys.
I would recommend this park over Yala. It is nowhere near as crowded and the roads not as bumpy.  But do be prepared for a bumpy ride.
We love safaris so the all day was perfect...you have the option of a half day. And remember you  are in the jungle.

Title: Good tour, if a little long
Text: Our guide arranged for us to be picked up by the safari jeep from our lunch venue for an afternoon tour. We saw a very wide variety of wildlife: leopard, deer, mongoose, hare, monkeys, crocodiles as well as peacocks and many other birds. Most of the wildlife was very close - about 10 metres to the leopard for example. We really wanted to see the sloth bear, but maybe next time! It is a very attractive park, and we did not find it too crowded compared to other parks we toured. Our driver was very experienced at spotting wildlife, and seemed to have a good idea of where various species were likely to be found. We felt the tour was about an hour longer than it needed to be.

Title: Great nature preserve park.
Text: This was my second time visiting this park, so many animals in their nature habitat. Similar to Yala, another great park. This one was in the northwest part of the country where there are many sites, ancient cities and a calm ocean.

Title: Bumpy long trip poor experience
Text: Pick your Jeep and guide carefully. We stayed just outside the park and took an early morning game drive. It could have been a good experience but the drive into the main game area is long and very bumpy. The speed made seeing the animals almost impossible ... we had to get the driver to slow down constantly to avoid permanent back injuries ... our guide was friendly but poor English... he was not able to share anything... having done many game drives in Africa, only novices would enjoy such a poor experience. Pay a little more and make sure you get quality. Or everything will be down to sheer luck. What is guaranteed is a tiring ride.

Title: Wildlife Preserve
Text:
Of course there are never guarantees when you undertake a safari, but we were very lucky.  Within 10 minutes we came across a sleeping leopard (although it was pretty well hidden behind a number of trees), so that was a huge highlight.

But we did see a number of birds, deer, and a sleeping crocodile.  The jungle terrain is varied and among the most verdant you can experience, so it's still worth checking out even if you don't spot the always elusive leopard during the journey.

Title: Great, if you love birds
Text: We saw some pretty birds, a crocodile, and deer.  But, no elephants or leopards.  We were told that there aren't any elephant in this park.  But, after we left the park we went for lunch.  There we ran into a man from UK that said he has been to a few National Parks in Sri Lanka and Wilpattu is the only one he has seen leopards in.

Title: First Sri Lanka Game experience.
Text: Spent about 4 hrs on a Jeep tour, saw elephants,deer and lucky enough to see a sloth bear. Gets a bit dusty so suggest a face mask from a chemist to reduce dust intake. Luckily our guide offered that advise. A really great experience.

Title: Exceptional jeep safari with a wide variety of wildlife
Text:
This national park and wildlife reserve is probably not as well known as some others and I understand it was only created about 6 years ago following this area being off bounds during the civil war. As a result, much wildlife has been left to its own devices, but like many others, licences jeeps and drivers are available for hire. Our cost 8,000rps each and was designed to be one of the longest trips. You can negotiate shorter trips for less cost down to about 4,000rps each.
Our Jeep driver was very happy to stop and check things out and during a 4 hour trip, we managed to see most of Sri Lanka's wildlife starting with a smaller adult bull elephant grazing on the trees about 500 metres from the park entrance.
During the trip we also saw crocodiles, Mongoose, sand deer, spotted deer, water buffalo, monkey and many birds which thankfully our quite could identify for us. 
We had begun the trip at 2pm and we're lucky enough to get a call that a leopard had been spotted - quite close to the entrance again - so we rushed for half an hour to get to this spot and were very lucky indeed to catch sight of this beautiful creature. Apparently there are 12 leopards living in this area and with 2 babies this year the population is at least steady, although pressure on space can lead to conflict with the local population.
The ride was bumpy and dusty, but the experience was wonderful and it was an inspired idea to create this further wildlife reserve. We have so enjoyed our opportunities to see the wildlife and watching as these creatures shyly come to the water holes and lakes in the late afternoon has been a real privilege. Don't miss an opportunity at some stage to get out into the countryside and the skill of the Jeep drivers both managing to traverse the tracks, know their way round the parks, work out where best to see the animals and communicate with each other, was very impressive.

Title: Very interesting - lovely wildlife
Text: Fascinating landscape full of absorbing wildlife. Not as crowded and touristy as some parks in Sri Lanka. More verdant and lush than, say, Yala, so animals harder to observe. Well worth a visit. Nice roadside stalls for food outside too, so early game drives are straightforward.

Title: Amazing
Text:
The best park in Sri Lanka!

We managed to see almost everything the park said it had in it. The only thing that we did not see was elephants but we were fine as we had seen loads of them in other parks. 
The driver was amazing, I cant remember his name but he was and old man with the eyes of a hawk, he had a white mitsubishi (the only one that colour that I could see), even when he was pointing at the animals hidden in the trees we still could not see them straight away! He could not stop telling us how lucky we were to see a leopard and a bear on the same trip. 

Great park, even if we had not seen all the animals that we did it still would of been a great afternoon. 

All was arranged by City Center Lodge guesthouse in Anuradhapura.

Title: Guide
Text:
The Park is very nice and there is a lot of animals don't use the guide with the mobile number  +94 77 3476288 is very expensive and it is not useful is sufficient call the park and book through them a visit. 
The guide is the some guide but it cost the double and probably the guide it is not the best. No comment!!! Fede

Title: More jeeps than elephants...
Text: Having time in our trip schedule, our driver / guide suggested to visit this park in light of its large number of elephants. The trip started with a long wait as there is  only one counter for tickets. After that and the associated trafic jam, we could eventually enter the park. Around the lake there were indeed a large number of wild elephants. Partly in the far distance, partly close by. But unfortunately the number of jeeps well exceeded the number of elephants, certainly at those spots where the elephants were close to the tracks.

Title: Long time for less
Text: We spend 12 hours in the park. Yes, we saw a leopard, but nothing like we saw in Tanzania. In fact, we saw lots of elephants in an other park, none in this one.  Wrong time of the year? Maybe. We saw chacals, peacocks, lots of other birds, crocodile, water buffalos, wild pigs, monkeys, deers, etc.  So, there is a lot of animals.  But maybe we were to tired of going back and forth in circles to have a look on one or another.  If it's your first, you'll sure have a great time. We had too much to see in Tanzania and Namibia and other parts of Sri Lanka to enjoy convenly.

Title: Disappointing
Text: I know that a national park is not a zoo, but in a park of this size and not seeing anything except monkeys is disappointing

Title: A beautiful find.....
Text:
The key thing about this park is that it is currently unspoilt and thus not very busy - nor commercialised.
There are some beautiful roads and avenues of trees, some interesting lakes and some very interesting (!) bumpy roads!
The fact that the park is fairly quiet means you can have undisturbed sightings without the radio crackle of everyone racing to the same point. Saying that, we did have an amazing sighting of 2 Leopards drinking, and 10 vehicles appeared to watch. Sightings are not all that common (its a huge park with few roads), so the element of luck is vital.
Well worth visiting - but dont make it too commercial or popular please as it will ruin its charm!

Title: Excellent safari
Text:
I highly recommend this to anyone traveling to Sri Lanka.
Safari took about 3 hrs  and we enjoyed it very much.
We stayed near Kalpitiya and its about 1 hr 20 mins away .
You can also do it as a day trip from Colombo.

Title: Hit and miss!
Text: So a couple of suggestions. Go early morning or late evening given more likely to see leopards and elephants etc. Its about a 3 hr drive from Colombo and then u are driving a few hours again in a Jeep in the back so again do one of the local temples and do this next day given u are sitting down way too long otherwise. Just my view........ we missed many of the animals but u may be lucky. Best of our snaps attached. Enjoy! ??

Title: New things to see
Text: Comfortable seats for a rocky ride, although I tore my trousers on a sharp edge.  As to be expected the driver had good eyes and we were introduced to bird life that we had not seen before.  Other than that it was crocs, deer and buffalo.  Apparently bears had been spotted that day but unfortunately not by us.  We didnt see leopard either but were not disappointed as we have been lucky in that respect in Africa.  On the whole our African safaris have been teeming withwildlife and therefore this was not as exciting but we are still glad that we did it.

Title: Stunning park teeming with wildlife
Text: We absolutely loved our stay at Wilpattu Treehouse and our full day safari at Wilpattu National Park. If its mandatory to see leopards this may not be the place for you...go to Yala or Botswana. Theyre hard to see and its blind luck but a lot of people spotted them and the park itself is stunning and full of other wildlife. Elephants, crocodiles, deer, mongoose, monitor lizards, turtles, peacocks and a huge variety of beautiful birds. The treehouse is right at the gate which is a great location. We stayed with people who had seen leopards with cubs and sloth bears the same day so its not something that never happens. Highly recommend.

Title: Lovely park
Text: Wherever we go on safari, I don't  like the question:' so what did you see?'. Because if I were to say: we saw amazing plants, eagles, beeeaters..., people just switch off. In Africa, they only want to hear if you have seen the big 5, here in Wilpattu, wildlife has been reduced to the Big 3. That makes me a bit sad because surely all of nature is to be appreciated? The bad reviews here baffle me: how can you review a forest? I seem to understand that if people see a leopard, they give it a high rating, otherwise not so... well Wilpattu is not a zoo but a vast and sometimes densely overgrown Wilderness. I loved the wildness of it, the lakes full of Lillies, the trees... we only saw a glimpse of a leopard and a lone elephant far away but we saw an eagle a meter away from use, colourful green bee-eaters right close, monkeys, deer, fighting lizards, storks, peacocks, a giant squirrel and many birds. Isn't that amazing? In my book, it is. We got the impression lots of people come here for the day from the beaches and they expect to have the animals shown to them on demand. Shame I guess because I think this park is lovely!

Title: Rare sighting of a leopard
Text: Great park with lots of wildlife and the most amazing range of local Sri Lankan birds; all so beautiful. I chose to come here rather than the very popular and touristy Yala national park and glad I did. It was less crowded and still had lots of amazing wildlife to see. Highlights for me was seeing a gorgeous young leopard on the roadside and a land monitor lizard eating another lizards prized eggs from a hole in the ground.

Title: Valerie Glasgow
Text: We have visited several National Parks in Sri Lanka and were slightly disappointed with this one. We drove in the jeep through the trees and couldnt see a great amount of wildlife. The driver tried hard to get us to see a leopard as two other jeeps had seen one, but we were not so lucky. There is more to see in the other parks.

Title: Thoroughly enjoyable
Text: Had an amazing safari around the park and saw lots of wildlife including - a bull elephant, baby leopard, sloth bear, turtle, monkeys, peacock and pea hens, spotted deer and samba deer, kingfishers, bee eaters, hawk eagles, serpent hawks and many other birds. The 4x4s were very good at getting around and the drivers where very talented at spotting animals deep in cover or high up in trees.

Title: Worth the 4am wake up call
Text:
Sorry to hear that others didnt see much but we really enjoyed it. On our 4 hour trip we saw a leopard, monkeys, monitor lizards, crocs, mongoose, grizzle giant squirrel, water buffalo, samba deer, spotted deer and SO many bird species. Our guide had a bird book too which we really appreciated. 

Wouldnt do it again but well worth it

Title: Amaizing
Text: I was here with two of my friends for full day safari. Start the journey at 6.30 am. It was a full of lucky day. We saw bears elephants and 3 leapords also. Other than many wild animals and lot of birds. It is better to take enough foods and water when you are in full day safari. And please take care of your safari driver too. Some of the visitors do not care of them. I think it is the best park in sri lanka to see many wild animals.

Title: Wildlife Safari
Text: Have good views/perspective from the 4 x 4 safari vehicles which bounce along the dirt tracks, stopping every now and then to show you animals of interest. Quite enjoyable and fun.

Title: Long Drives for very little
Text:
Our first wildlife trip in SL and pretty disappointed.
Once you get to the park, there is a very long drive to get anywhere with very limited wildlife. Our drive lasted 5 hours.
We are well used to African game drives and understand that animals do not perform to order! All we saw was a few bird species, monitors, spotted deer, 1 water buffalo and 1 elephant.
Pretty disappointing - sorry.

Title: A great afternoon watching beautiful wildlife in its natural environment
Text: In 3 jeeps, our group took to the tacks and how the drivers spot so many interesting birds and animals as they go is amazing!  They always stopped for us to get photos where possible and we all enjoyed the time immensely.  We did not see any elephants of leopard, but several land monitors, eagles, bee eaters, flycatchers, monkeys and so much more.

Title: Small park compared to Yala... good spotting including Sloth bear
Text: Compared to Minneriya, which is too crowded with jeeps chasing around after the elephant herds, Wilpattu is tight and compact with a great lakeside breakfast stop and plenty of birds.

Title: rise and shine if you wanna catch the birds, and leopards, and slot bears etc
Text: it can get a bit busy in the park, but if you get the morning start, say 0630 at start things are very quiet and you see lots of birds and with luck: 2 elephants, a leopard, etc

Title: Stunning scenery along with good viewings of leopard
Text: We did one late afternoon drive and a full day one meaning we got to see a lot more of the huge park, with both man made and natural lakes.

Title: Saw Leopards
Text: A very good park with lots of diversity. We were fortunate to see Leopards, but it always a great experience. The park had few Elephants while we were there as they had moved to other areas as part of the travel cycle. Saw lots of Raptors and many birds including plenty of Jungle Fowl.

Title: Experiance in 02 ways
Text:
There are 02 ways which you can visit wilpattu National park :D 
One is going inside of National park from Hunuwilgama main entrance. The other one is drive on the road going from Mannaram to Colombo through wilpattu national park. Their you just have to drive middle of wilpattu jungle near to 40km. Either way you can find many animals. It will be good to have good ground clearance vehicle for safe side. Specially if you choose second option you have to cross river going across road with shoe bridge. In dried season will have around 1Ft height water which you have to cross and drive through. But rainy time forget to cross here. Having many navy camp inside of this jungle. Be sure to fill gasoline and have spare tire before you start this journey. Be careful with elephant on road when you driving as they are not much familiar with vehicle like in other places. If you choose first option you can do camping in jungle

Title: Excellent potential for sight seeing despite hours restricted by ongoing drought
Text: In the company of a trained naturalist a short morning visit yielded verified sightings of 35 different birds, 15 mammals and 2reptiles. The coast was not visited and thus potential opportunities missed. Elephant , 4different deer(antelope) and crocodile but no leopard. Interest in a wildlife experience must be comprehensive as demonstrated above or why bother going.  Birds have far more to offer than mammals and just need a good pair of binoculars.

Title: Amazing day at the park
Text:
We spent an entire day at Wilpattu national park and enjoyed it very much.
The driver of our jeep was excellend and we saw a lot of wildlife, such as leopards, sloth bear, elephants, mongoose & many birds.
There weren't many jeeps in the park which made the experience even better.

Title: Waste of time and money
Text:
We booked our safari trip 4 days in advance, the price included hotel pick up, 6 hour safari and drop off. 
We found out that we had to make our own way to the safari as our area wasn't included in the catchment. 

After arriving and sorting out our jeep, we had to queue at the entrance to the park, at this point we were told our safari would be 3 hours not 6 hours due to 'Government rules ' and the drought. 

We continued with the safari as our guide didn't understand our complaints with the short notice. We saw no animals at all. 

We paid the full amount for no animals, half the amount of time and our own pick up and drop off. We would never have paid what we did for 3 hours safari if we had known in advance.

Title: Amazing Game
Text:
As ever we go game viewing with the expectation of seeing nothing that way we are never disappointed. The landscape reminded me of Hwange- lots of bush with small openings and then bigger vistas around the tanks 
Great bird life as you would imagine but when you turn a corner at 5 pm and come across a Sloth Bear casually drinking at a watering hole you feel like you hit the jackpot.... then the Leopard stalking wild pig at the next tank followed by watching the sun go down while an old Bull elephant stands in the middle of a lake munching gently away -awesome! 
Racing back to the park gate before it closed at 630pm we saw another bear - the kids were beaming from ear to ear as we left eagerly awaiting the next morning game drive... couldn't be as good could it.......

Title: Sloth bear viewing
Text:
We got to the park later than most (around 8:30 am) because we had already done 4 successful safaris during our Sri Lanka trip and didn't feel like getting up early.

We still saw many birds, spotted deer, barking deer. But the most interesting was a sloth bear, unafraid and right by the road. We observed him for half an hour, eating and then drinking at the water hole. 

By the large pond, we saw deer, buffaloes and crocodile. 

As a cherry on the cake, we saw a leopard in a tree (at a distance).

Title: Worth the trip
Text: Did a morning safari....always a punt with wild animals but saw a bear....elephants...an otter.... elephants an eagle really close up and plenty of birdlife, deeds and gazel.

Title: enjoy nature and solitude
Text: We went on a full day safari here and were very sad to leave afterwards. We saw so many spotted deer, monkeys and peacocks, several wild boar and crocodiles, a couple of elephants and jackals, and a great variety of birds. Sadly we couldn't see any leopards but it was the most beautiful national park we've been to. We felt like we were in Jungle Book, absolutely mesmerised by the scenery. Visit Yala National Park for leopards, Kaudulla National Park for elephants, and Wilpattu for the scenery and solitude. This was the only safari experience where we were by ourselves in the wild, we only saw five other jeeps at meal breaks but quickly lost them. By the way be careful with monkeys whilst having your food at the breakfast/lunch area, they stole my sandwich!

Title: Lovely park
Text: We visited this park for the day with our driver for the holiday and another driver/spotter.  The drivers, when we meet on the road, exchange information about sightings and of course, we were all after a leopard sighting.  We saw lots of birds, spotted deer, mongoose and had our lunch watching an elephant having his at a watering hole. We did manage to catch a brief glimpse of a leopard, which was bigger than others I'd seen in other places but still a thrill. Despite the heat we were quite comfortable in our vehicle which had a roof for shade but open sides with tiered seats so everyone could see.

Title: Spotted the leopard
Text: Yes we were lucky and we spotted a loepard and were able to watch it for quite a while. But apart from this the jungle itself is very beautiful with lots of wildlife and birds. One of the most beautiful forest area as compared to the southern national parks.

Title: Beautiful forest safari
Text: This was the most beautiful forest I saw in Sri Lanka. Other national parks have more small trees and shrubs rather than the the thick jungle experience. Teeming with wildlife and birds. Spotting a leopard is a luck and I was lucky to spot a beautiful leopard.

Title: Not all about the leopard
Text:
We have recently been on an afternoon safari to this national park and thought it was great. Be realistic and don't assume that you will see a leopard and you won't be disappointed. We employed the services of a naturalist and yes they do cost you more but as visitors to this lovely land we thought it would be money well spent. We  were very happy with that decision as he was very knowledgeable and between him and the driver they spotted lots of animals that we would've otherwise missed. We were given a good amount of time for photos and were lucky that there were not many jeeps in the park at the same time. We did not see a leopard but were still very happy with what we did see. We could tell our driver and naturalist were working very hard to give us a memorable experience and surely that is all you can ask for.
Highlights for us were seeing langur,a golden jackal, many different bird species and a sloth bear just before leaving the park. Other more common animals were also seen.

Title: Serendipity
Text: If you are there at the right place at the right time, then you see the lot.  In one afternoon safari, we were so fortunate to see leopards, sloth bear, elephants, wild boars, water buffalo's, mongoose, star tortoise, barking and spotted deer and lots of birds,  It was our lucky day, hope they will be still there for our next visit to the park and the Tree House at the Wilpattu Corridor.

Title: Sloth bear was the highlight
Text: Plenty of elephants, a tortoise and even a usually elusive sloth bear. Bird life was varied and interesting. Unfortunately guiding was poor. No leopards.

Title: Wilpattu National Park safari package
Text: We were very disappointed with Sri Lanka expeditions safari package as we paid a lot of money for a full day safari but only had a driver who spoke little English. We did not have a guide so drove around all day mostly spotting animals ourselves, and learnt nothing about the park or the wildlife. This tour company is not recommended.

Title: Leopards galore!
Text: Very good park to see leopards and sloth bears. Elephants are more difficult. Not too crowded, much less than Yala...

Title: Shaken but not that stirred
Text:
