The 4x4s were good, the location and scenery were good, the animals we saw were good.
Things here were good but nothing special. The range of animals was not vast, the illusion animals remained elusive and the common animals them being deer were around almost every corner and so used to the 4x4s that they remained really close but actually I see deer that close all the time in the UK
Some of the birds were exotic and some good pictures were had. The crocodiles were evident but not big cats as we had expected so not really a let down. Evidence of elephants was everywhere but alas not were seen. The odd lizard crossed our path but actually the experience was a tad underwhelming.

Title: Amazing experience
Text: We were lucky enough to have a driver who was great at tracking the animals. We were lucky enough to spot 4 leopards in the one day and it was overall a really lovely experience.

Title: Safari Fun
Text:
The terrain in this park is quite different to the usual jungle one would expect here.  However it was delightful to see something different.  Our driver and guide were excellent and they were quick to point out the different birds and animals.

Sadly we saw no elephants but perhaps the middle of a drought is not the best time to visit a game park!  The area is suffering badly.

Nevertheless it was a great experience and I would happily return.

Title: Great safari
Text: Our first safari experience. Booked a half day tour, which allowed us to cross through the park for about 4 hours. Due to the many small lakes the park on it's own is beautiful! We saw many birds and butterflies, many reindeers (even one at a small break time that seemed to like people, allowed us to take several pictures from just half a meter distance and even followed us when we walked back to the jeep). Unfortunately we only saw 1 elephant and no leopards, but it was still worth it.

Title: Different country side to other safaris - worth seeing
Text:
We enjoyed our safari, well worth the time. Lots of spotted deer and birds and some Elephants. 
Our tour guid recommend it rather than do two safaris at Udawalawe. Very good advise for us.The terrain was completely differently and very interesting lots of lakes. It was a very peaceful visit with not herds of other people.

Title: One of Sri Lankas best
Text:
Wilpattu National Park is a must for animal and wilderness lovers. 
Aside for the BIG ticket sites of Leopard and Sloth Bear you will see plenty of unique bird life and field game.  Of course if there is a special sighting be prepared for a crush of safari vehicles.
Choose a good company to experience the park with like Leopard Safaris or stay as close as you can to entrance to avoid the long queues first thing in the morning.

Title: Too many safari jeep, not so many wild animals
Text: This is relatively small park by USA standard. One must hire a local safari jeep to get into the park, and a park ranger must sit in the jeep too. Because it is relatively small, you will meet many other jeeps, and because your pay to the jeep driver is fixed so he will try to get back home ASAP, not try to find you the best spot to observe the animals. Again, it is a small park and very dry often so don't expect to find as many animals as in Africa or as in India where land for tiger is more futile.

Title: The biggest National Park in Sri Lanka
Text:
Is a safari, then all depends on the lucky.
We could see eagles, crocodiles, "bambi's", a very kind of birds, buffalos and a LEOPARD. The biggest than the guide has ever seen in the safari. 
The tour has been very funny and we want to give thanks to our driver by Bobby Safari Wilpattu

Title: Big park but desperate for rain
Text: This is Sri Lanka's biggest National Park which unlike Yala NP does not close in September. It boasts birds, deer and the elusive leopard and sloth bear which is what everyone wants to see. When we went they hadn't had rain for over a year and the park was parched with little water in the usual watering holes. The park authorities had stopped full day safaris to allow the animals a chance to get what water there was without the hoards of jeeps that ply the very limited tracks.... we did an evening and early morning safari and saw lots of birds, deer and crocodile noses in the evening, the highlight being a leopard viewing but nothing bar a couple of deer in the morning. There are around 150 leopards and 200 sloth bears in the park so it really is down to luck if one decides to walk out in front of you. It was good fun in the jeeps but I suspect that unless it rains l'm not sure how long the authorities will keep it open, they close evening drives for a week before we visited .

Title: Would be a great trip under better conditions
Text: Booked our trip in advance and all went well with meeting the tour guide and the vehicle supplied. Tour was in the afternoon finishing around 6 pm. The disappointment that there was little wildlife to see. Viewed what apparently was a leopard from some 400 metres away.  Saw an elephant in a waterhole.  It is deceptive to arrange tours under such severe drought conditions as there are few animals around. We were informed that the park would be closed in 2 days, but on reading recent reviews this is apparently not the case.  Beware !! make inquiries as to whether weather conditions have improved.

Title: Place full of Water holes (willus)
Text: Fantastic place to go on safari. Select the proper season when all the villu's are full of water. Unfortunately we went in the wrong time where most of the villu's were dry. Didn't see much wild life. There is a large area to cover in a good 4 wheel drive vehicle in very good condition. In the thick jungle you can visit the ruins of the Kuveni's palace and the area where King Vijaya landed (Kudiramalai). There are ruins of a monument (very large horse) situated near this place for the sea farerers to see in the olden times. Ideal to spend a day there to enjoy the fauna and flora as well. Take lot of drinking water with you.

Title: Not the best
Text: If you want the best safari experience then you need to go elsewhere. It is good if you are interested in birds but the thick vegetation provides great cover for most everything except the deer.

Title: Great - if long - trip with Sri Lanka Day Tours
Text: My wife and I were staying in Colombo on business but had one day off, so we booked a trip to Wilpattu, the only major park within a reasonable travelling distance. This was with Sri Lanka Day Tours. It was still a long drive but we had an excellent driver and she included a lunch stop on the way.  We had booked an afternoon tour and arrived a little early, but the driver phoned the guide and within 10 minutes the 4x4 truck arrived.  We had a four hour tour deep into the park, seeing two large birds of prey just a few metres away, three species of deer, a mongoose - all at close quarters - and many water birds near the lakes and pools.  At the furthest pools we saw hundreds of flying foxes - large bats - hanging from trees, giving a "different world" appearance to the area and a mugger crocodile, very still with just its snout above the water.  We started back then just as light started to fade, a leopard, just 10m away.  We watched it in the bush and walking across the track ahead, for about 15 minutes.  A brilliant round up to the day. Two small gripes - the guide could have been better at pointing out and naming some of the smaller birds - though he identified over 30 species - and the company could have been clearer at the start about what pick up time was needed to get us there in time for the tour.  The day overall was about 13 hours, which was pushing it.  Still, an excellent trip overall which we will remember for many years, and at a very reasonable price.

Title: Thoroughly Enjoyable Safari
Text: We booked this safari with Pradeep who was doing another safari with us in Bundula he couldn't come on the day so organised someone else to do the safari for us. It was a beautifully sunny day. The roads or tracks were mainly dry. We saw lots of birds, bats, deer, crocodiles, monitor lizards, water buffalo, peacocks, water hog. Sadly no leopard on the day or elephants. We had a volunteer guide who was keen on birds which helped as he was good at spotting birds.

Title: From tortoises to leopards !!
Text: An amazing day spent in the back of a jeep travelling through the rain and sun which led to us seeing a myriad of different birds, animals and insects as well as a stunning sunset over the lake. To cap it all we say a leopard getting ready for a night's hunting sat above our heads in a tree. What more does one want from a trip to Sri Lanka. We booked through See Lanka Travel near the Club Hotel Dolphin in Negombo. If your staying there do sign up for the trip through Nippon....you will not be disappointed.

Title: Fantastic
Text: Absolutely wonderful. We were lucky and saw a leopard. We also saw elephants, monkeys, bush hens, crocodile, peacocks, birds - lots of birds. We did 2 safaris here, a morning and an afternoon we just loved it.

Title: Great experience
Text: Happy to have chosen to go to Wilpattu National Park for a whole day. I saw a lot of animals like elephants, crocodile, leopard, mongoose, a lot of deer, a lot of birds. It was a lovely experience.

Title: Fantastic experience
Text: We have traveled several wild hogs and safaris. What makes this park special is that it is completely wild with very little man made influence. We started around 6 AM and it was raining heavily. We spotted a lot of spotted Adnan spotted deers. However the rich diversity of the bird life took our breath away. We spotted CORMORENTS, horn bills,common sand pipers, great thick knees, red WATTLED lapwings, black winged stilts, great eGRETS among others. We saw a herd of wild boars. We also got lucky decide three leopards who were crossing the road. They offer a tracker, who is a local native trained to spot the flora and faunaThere are also a lot of jungle fowl, the national bird of Sri Lanka and peacocks perching on high branches and chattering away nicely. A beautiful untouched experience. There is a bathroom in the middle of the park but we opted not to use it..

Title: Great place for a safari
Text: We went on a half day safari starting at dawn and were fortunate to see 2 leopards, 3 different species of deer, monkeys, wild boar, water buffalo, mongoose and 1 elephant. Also sighted were numerous birds and lizards. It was not as busy as I believe Yala is, and the jeep drivers shared sightings to get the best for everyone. I felt that the animals were not disturbed by us & it was a privilege to observe them in their natural habitat. A word of warning -don't leave belongings esp food in the jeep when you visit the rest stop area as that's what the monkeys are waiting for!

Title: The Elusive Leopard
Text:
We had two safaris in the park., One was at 2pm and the other was 6am the following day.
They are both different, but still very interesting.
The afternoon safari, we managed to get a glimpse of a leopard in the bushes and in the morning, we did not.
It is very hit and miss on whether you manage to see one, but there are other animals to see. These include crocodiles, buffalo, monkeys, kingfisher and deer.

Title: Brilliant.
Text: An early morning visit paid dividends. Birds, spotted deer, sambars, crocodiles, water monitors and leopards! Great driver who doubled as a guide. One of the highlights of our visit to SL.

Title: Not worth the effort
Text:
There supposed to be 200 elephants in this park and maybe 25 leopards.
We didn't have a good guide but with the fees and the guide I personally think it's simply not worth the time and effort to go there. It has some beautiful Weiss and lakes and plenty of peacocks and deer and some wonderful birds. If birds are your thing maybe it would be worth your time. I think Yale is the park to see.
If you happen to go forget about Thimbiriwewa EcoResort. It's in a sad state of repair and not clean to boot!

Title: Relaxing
Text:
When we were there end of april it was really quite. A extreme long dry period. The bigger animals especially the elephants were aggresive. We didn't see them fortunately. 
We have done quite some safari in thed past so our expectations were low.
The birds are sometimes really fascinating.
There are easy to spot so are the crocks and deers (impala). 
In the end we have seen a bear.  The highlight of the safari.

Title: If you are a wild life person, this is one of the best placers
Text: To enjoy more you should stay at the bungalows located within the park. This is a place where me and my husband want to visit again.

Title: Sloth bear and a large leopard sighted
Text: Worth a visit. Lots of lakes and wildlife. Birds galore. Deers. A highlife was a sloth Bear walking across the track. We also saw a large leopard in the trees but not fast enough with our camera for a photo. Aust couple traveling with Travel Lanka.

Title: Terrible!
Text: WPN is really a waste of money..the entrance fee is 10x higher for foreigners compared to locals...and u can see only few common animals...very boring safari as the roads also repeated...dissapointed

Title: Amazing wildlife
Text:
Wilpattu is a beautiful National Park in Sri Lanka. 
With a good driver and a four-wheel vehicle plus an excellent guide we saw a leopard, sloth bear, water buffaloes and elephants plus a numerous birds both endemic and migratory. Our guide had the uncanny ability to spot birds or animals from a great distance.

Title: The Largest Park in Sri Lanka
Text:
This is the largest park in Sri Lanka. So need more time to spend inside to spot animals.
I have been there over 10 times & still not seen a leopard. You need to spend whole day & need luck to see animals. I seen bear & elephants lot.

Title: Boring, unless you flip over birds
Text:
Sorry to be negative but surely the idea of a safari park conjures up images of lions, elephants, crocodiles and so forth. Well, apparently Wilpattu has leopards but they were well hidden on the day we visited. Oh well, its Sri Lanka so we are bound to see herds of elephants to make up for it, right? Nope. Not even one. So we spent all morning looking at birds. The guide got all excited over deer and even native fowls. Where I come from deer are a pest and don't start me on native chickens!
We decided against Yala as heard it was very crowded. Maybe it is but there was not an abundance of wildlife in Wilpattu. Even the monkeys were thin on the ground - and trees.

Title: Natural elephants
Text:
A great experience to see around 40 elephants in their natural environment. Make sure you ask the drivers to stop and take plenty of time to enjoy just watching. 
The drivers like to get you in and out quickly.

Title: Bad luck
Text:
We went there by ourselves , we were 3 friends, and arrive and the entrance at 6:00 in the morning (For sure they will stop stop before the entrance of the park, telling you that you can't go without a car/guide/tour and asking ridiculous amount of money don't listen and keep going) we were trying to join another tour, so that
 way it will be cheaper since you you paid the car and not per person. EverythingWas full so we hired a car right there, the office can call for you, for 4500, half day. We did see a couple of monkey, buffalos, birds, deers but no leopard or elephants, but what we could hear from
another guide no one that day had luck, most of the person we pass by we're sleeping in the car. It's beautiful but not many animals. Up to you if you want to give a try. Most of the time we were by ourself so plenty of time to watch the animals when we spotted them.

Title: I've been scamed by my guide and state employee
Text: My guide was very nice, and he gave me the feeling that I could trust him. In collaboration with the state employee at the reception, they make me pay twice the foreigner price. After paying, the state employee doesn't want to give me my ticket but only to my guide. I felt the tricky thing.  i took the paper from the hands of my guide and I saw they fraud with me. By asking my money back, the employee became agressive and told me 'You pay or you don't enter'.  The guide was recommanded by Water Garden Hôtel.  He lives 7km from the parc entrance. The vehicule plates finish by ***387. Don't trust this guide, he's a scammer. The normal price is 15usd+vat+service charge

Title: We did a full day!!
Text:
My young girls really wanted to a safari, as we were at Negombo the driver advised us to go Wilpattu, Yala is too far. Took us just about 4hrs to get there!! We wanted to do a full day, park opens at 6am, we set off at 4am!! We did the safari till 6pm. Best time to go in my opinion is early morning, be at the park for 6am and do half day safari. We saw more animals in the morning than the afternoon/evening. We never saw any Cheetah, we saw 1 elephants, lots of dears, a bear, a cobra ??, lots of lizards and lots of birds! We got to step out the vehicle and have a picnic near a lake, the lake had 6 crocodiles. 
We also saw monkeys where we had a picnic.

Title: Go back to nature at Wilpattu - Pride of Sri lanka
Text:
As Wilpattu National Park is situated nearby to my work place at north west province of Sri Lanka, taken the opportunity to visit the same during free time in first week of Feb 17.  The national park established in 1938 and is located 30 km west of Anuradhpura, the nearest city and located 26 km north of Puttalam. 

About 60 lakes and tanks spread throughout Wilpattu National Park. we spotted deer, elephant, crocodiles, peacock, leopards, rare birds, monkey etc in the huge national park. 

Visitors can currently tour and explore only 25 % of the park as 75% area  is dense forest. The best time to visit Wilpattu is during the month of Feb and October. Its recommended to visit the Wilpattu in 1st half of the day as we get to see many animals etc.  Go back to nature at Wilpattu and its worth a visit.

Title: Short leopard encounter!
Text:
We booked two half day safaris (one afternoon and one morning) and we were lucky that we did that, because the first guide was good, the second one was rather poor driving through the park rather quickly. We saw many different birds, deer, monkeys and some elephants from rather far away. We were also lucky to have a very short encounter with two leopards on the tree. Even though we didn't see so many big animals, the scenery is beautiful. One big plus is that there aren't so many cars, hence, the park isn't so crowded and you get to enjoy nature. 
Summed up: If you like birds and beautiful sceneries then it's the place for you. Of course, you can be lucky and see a leopard and elephants, but don't be disappointed if you don't get to see them.

Title: Sri lankan Sloth Bear and Swiming elephant
Text: the owner of Dill lake view resort did organise a guide for our trip to the Park and due to the experienced guide we were able to spot many many animals. The park itself is hughe and with only a few tourists. You should go if you want to see an untouched, natural habitat for elephants, leopards, many many birds and the Sri Lankan Sloth Bear.

Title: Average
Text: This safari is worth a trip, lots of different birds to see, also wild dear. Didn't see any wild boars or elephants or leopards, fabulous scenery, and lots of nature, especially environmental aromas to enhance your nasal sensors, the tour is a great experience just a little 4 hrs too long for me.

Title: Elephants & Monitors a highlight ... the treehouse, dangerous
Text: Great fun, the treehouse/observation deck aside.  The treehouse has no wall on one side, large holes in the floorboards and rotten beams.  It is in urgent need of new wood, or there will be deaths from falling in the next 3 months.  I urge any who climb to do so with caution - check the wood before climbing off the (unsecured) iron ladder.

Title: Spot the leopard
Text: It is oneof the best places to spot the leopard in Sri Lanka. A pretty big national park that has many natural lakes. Also can spot the crocodiles and Bears in some parts of the NP.

Title: Wildlife in Wilpattu National Park
Text:
We went on 3 full day safaris (6-18) in order to see as much as possible. Exotic birds were plentiful e.g. bee-eaters, kingfishers, peacocks, painted storks and various eagles and hawks. We saw several water buffalos, a few wild boars, and some elephants. Generally the elephants can only be seen on a large distance, but one male elephant was looking for water chestnuts in one of the lakes and it was great fun watching him half buried in water. 

During the 3 days we covered a lot of ground and saw practically every corner of the park. We did appreciate that generally you travel with almost no other jeeps around you. The roads are terrible, so it is really a fun ride and you have to admire the skills of your driver.

On the second day, we spotted a young leopard drinking from a small pond no more than 30 m from the road. We got great pictures before he wandered off into the wilderness. This was great luck and generally very few visitors have that luck, so do not expect it to happen.

We highly recommend the park, but it is a severe and exhausting effort to drive 12 hours for 3 days in a row. Remember to bring warm clothes, because the mornings can be very chilly.

Title: Great Nationalpark
Text:
I visited this nationalpark with my family for two days. First day we went for an exhausting 12 hours, next just a half day trip. Luckily it was possible in December, because sometimes the rains make it impossible.

It is a park with many animals and birds, and with beautiful lakes. Both days we saw a leopard (one in a tree and the other running across the road, both mid day), several elephants (evening), eagles, storks, wild fowls, deer, wild boars, monkeys, crocodiles, peacocks, mongooses, monitor lizards, giant squirrels and perhaps some more animals.

There were not many jeeps around first day, but a few more the second day which was a Saturday, so avoid weekends for the optimal experience.

Title: Interesting
Text: Wilpattu is an interesting national park to visit. It is very scenic with lots of lakes and forest. We did two safaris, one in the morning and one late afternoon. We had to stay in the park all day and our driver provided a delicious lunch made by his wife. In all we would have been driving eight hours. We did see one elephant, one bear, three varieties of deer, boar, buffalo, a tortoise, crocodiles aplenty, many mongoose and water monitors and one squirrel. There were lots and lots of birds including eagles and many peacocks displaying. However, we did not see a leopard, but we did see paw prints!

Title: A total ripoff for foreign travellers
Text:
I made the mistake of staying at Sinharagama Resort close to the park on Puttalam Rd assuming it would be easy to arrange a safari with the hotel and hookup with other safaris to split the costs. 

Instead I was quoted 7500 for a half day and 12500 for a full day by the hotel manager and told all costs were included and I was sharing with 5 other people.

When the driver picked me up I was told I had to pay an additional 3000 park entry fee and I was the only one on the safari.

Alternatively I could have tried to go directly to the park entrance and join up with a safari but I am was already fleeced just going from Anuradhapura to Sinharagama in a taxi being constantly told how far it was. 

If money is no object go, but otherwise don't bother. I reluctantly passed.

Title: A nice quiet park to visit.
Text: We spent all day in the park from first light till sunset and really enjoyed the experience. We stopped twice at the picnic place (where there are acceptable toilets) for both breakfast and lunch and both times there were about four other jeeps around. We rarely saw anothe jeep while on our travels and more or less had the place to ourselves. There are plenty of birds to see plus elephants, leopards, deer and sloth bears (yes we saw all of these) all in a quiet and sedate atmosphere that is in marked contrast to some other parks in Sri Lanka.

Title: Amazing Safari Experience
Text: This was a fantastic visit for my first ever safari experience. From our jeep with our guide we spotted elephants, leopards, bears and a whole lot more. The park is huge so there are occasionally long spells of driving (but great fun on the tracks) and being in the back of a safari jeep, the place gets HOT during the day. You have to have the attitude of being patient - the happier you are to sit and wait, the more you will see.

Title: Remember its not a zoo.
Text:
Our travel agent arranged for us to do this safari three times to maximise our chances of seeing a leopard and we werent disappointed.  We did one afternoon and two mornings and hit the jackpot on the first one (pm).  The leopard only appeared for a few minutes but as we went prepared not to see one, I was so in awe when we did that I was literally shaking trying to take photos.  The second sighting was on the second morning.  A baby leopard suddenly appeared crossing the track quickly followed by mummy.  Wow!

We saw so much more in the 2/3 hours we were there.  The bird life is amazing.  There was a crocodile hidden in the undergrowth which was a surprise as it was quite a way from water.  Only one elephant, but I dont know how many are in the park.  3/4 different kinds of deer.  Monitor lizards were in abundance (all sizes).  The only animal missing from the list was a sloth bear, but we thought we were so lucky seeing what we did.  

The jeeps tend to space themselves out so we felt we were the only ones there most of the time.  There is just one place where we were allowed out of the vehicle, which is a seating area near a lake.  Crocs can be seen in the distance! The toilets were being worked on when we were there (April) so I had to brave it and disappear into the 
undergrowth.  

As others have said before, this is not a zoo so we didnt expect to see something every few minutes, but it made it all the more exciting when we did.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: If we would have seen more animals this would have rated a 4. On the day while we did see a leopard and lots of spotted deer and birds, there were no elephants or sloth bears to be seen. The driver and guide tried very hard to track some but no luck. At a cost of $70 which was for entry and jeep this was disappointing.  All staff were very friendly and made the 4 hours pleasurable

Title: One of best
Text: We have a chance visit this national park on March. The location is fantastic. We have a chance to see the leopards and many more animals. This is one of best national parks in Sri Lanka. Highly recommend.

Title: Insightful Experience
Text: Hemal was both warm and professional as his superb knowledge of the country really gave us much insight to Sri Lanka. We had a terrific time and would highly recommend him.

Title: Photography Tour.....
Text: We had a excellent tour experience there. Our main interested was to see leopards and bears.... finally we saw 10 leopards and two bears....

Title: Like all safaries- good if you see the wildlings otherwise it can quite boring
Text:
Okay so I wanted to see the Wilpattu national park upon recommendation of a couple of friends. I didnt have anyone to go with so had to solo it. And honestly had a very mixed experience. I quite enjoy solo travelling but a safari can be PRETTY boring alone at times- especially if there are only 3-4 other jeeps around. 
I booked through my hotel- Rajratra reach resort and the owner didnt explain the price properly to me- so had some issues there (he was genuinely a nice guy and I am just giving him benefit of the doubt that he forgot to explain me that theres an entrance fee along with the Jeep hire. 

Anyway the safari part: its the biggest national park in Sri Lanka and there are numerous lakes inside (approx 42) which is responsible for the unique eco culture. We were the only ones to spot a leopard on the day- so I was pretty happy. We also saw: plenty of peacocks, Sri Lankan jungle fowl, eagles, wild buffalos, various other bird species, fox, crocodiles, deer (plenty). 

In summary: dont recommend a full day safari; would recommend going in a large group (more fun and easier on the wallet); bring binoculars; also try booking through your hotel and get a good price but make all the costs very clear at the start. Also bring plenty of food and water theres not much once you re inside the park. 

Getting to Wilpattu: 
- note the Wilpattu is closest to Anuradhapura (about 30kM) 
- how I got to Wilpattu? 
     - I was staying in a hotel in Anuradhapura 
     - I caught the 5am bus (from the Main bus station) and asked the conductor to drop me off at Wilpattu junction (Rs70) 
     - note that there are 2 buses- bus #4 and another one I cant remember (they are both heading towards Colombo) 
     - my safari driver was waiting there and took me to the entrance gate where we bought the entrance tickets.

Title: a fantastic park
Text: An amazing park that has a range of animals. Unfortunately we did not see a leopard but the safari experience was still amazing.

Title: Magnificent
Text:
A highlight of our Sri Lankan trip. A National Park without too many jeeps, and plenty of animals and birds if you are persistent and keep you eyes open. Wasn't lucky enough to see a bear and only one obscured sighting of a leopard but it is a place where there is plenty to offer anyone who really loves nature. As with all the National Parks in Sri Lanka the foreigners pay a huge premium on entry prices but that the governments policy, not each park.
If you wan't to tick a box saying you saw a particular animal maybe this isn't the place for you. For all the people who cant understand that this is a National Park full of wild animals who travel about as they wish, and complain about not seeing whatever animal they demand, go to the Pinnawala Zoo. They have leopards. Have fun there.

Title: Truly wild!
Text: The best park in Sri Lanka! Much less crowded than Yala, with a greater sightings of Leopards. In my three night stay I was fortunate to spotted 6 all together. Highly recommended!

Title: Busy safari trip
Text:
We did two safari trips at 14:00 and 06:30 the following day. The park was very busy, at numerous points we were in a convoy of 5 or 6 jeeps which doesn't make for the most enjoyable experience, especially the way the drivers jostle, reverse and drive alongside the animals to get the best views.
The park is very nice, there's a toilet station in the middle to stop and have a break.
We did see a lot of animals here which was what most people obviously go for! We saw a leopard, sloth bear and elephant (each from about 4 metres) which was a great experience. Unfortunately as mentioned, for most of those there were also 6 other noisy jeeps with us!

Title: Going wild
Text: From holy grounds of Anuradhapura we went to jeep safari to Vipaththu park. Unfortunately we missed the elephants and saw one leopard in the bush, but the rest was OK.

Title: Beautiful NP
Text: Great place to visit! Excited to experience elephants in the park. Wonderful opportunity for bird watching and enjoying the scenery too. Title: Had a great safari
Text: What a place on the earth...  this park is just wild. The best is to go early in the morning at 6 so that you can see as many as animals. We have seen about 35 different animals including a leopard sleeping on our way. The paths are narrow and branches of the trees are often covering so be careful you may hit by the branches. Title: Best place to enjoy wildlife
Text: Hi guys this is the best place to enjoy the wild life, and We took a full day safari and this place is full of nature, and excitement. For everyone who is willing to go their I would recommend  to take a full day safari because you will guarantee you will see leopards

Title: Raptors Up Close
Text:
Whilst the park's main attraction is leopards, it was the raptors that were amazing.  Many of them were simply unfazed by our jeep and we were able to get up close.  Similarly, peacocks and jungle fowl too, were easy to get close to.
There wasn't much happening in the heat of the afternoon, and we chose to do early morning and late afternoon drives each day.  Unfortunately, the park charged full fees on each entry.
The Wilpattu Tree House is right on the park's doorstep and saved a lot of time getting to and fro.

Leopards proved rather more elusive, and we got 3 good sightings in 10 consecutive days.

Title: Lovely Park
Text: We spent a half day in Wilpattu and saw many birds, crocodiles, monitors, deer and a sloth bear. We arrived with a driver from the hotel and the park called a guide/park driver for us from the gate - no problem. Plan on about 3 hours in the park. It was much less busy than the parks we visited further south and denser forest, which was nice. We didn't see a leopard, but it was clear from the guest book at the info centre that many others have better luck on this front.

Title: nice elephants
Text: nice experience with the elephants 2000 LKR per person for entrance and 100 m elephant ride. very decent souvenirs but a bit expensive. you can bathe with the elephants and feed them crackers for 200 LKR

Title: Disappointing
Text: I realise that what you see in these parks is a lot about luck! But we spent four hours hurtling around in two jeeps (driven by teenagers ?!) and saw virtually nothing! Our trip was part of an Intrepid tour and so we had no say about the organisation, but this was the worst of its kind compared to ones in India where drivers are well informed and drive well apart from other jeeps. At one point an elephant appeared and about five vehicles drove towards it at speed and by the time we got there it disappeared into the trees. Not surprisingly. Eventually our driver stopped next to a rabbit, pointed it out, and said, look it is eating 'wild grass' ! Since we are from NZ we could only laugh and wish we had a gun! Unlike Uluwallawe in the South east this park doesn't even have beautiful scenery. Cannot recommend.

Title: I wish I had passed on this one
Text:
Wilpattu Park was hit hard during the war and was subject to much poaching. It advertises the opportunity to see leopards, but unfortunately there are only about 30 in a park twice the size of Toronto.

Like other national parks in Sri Lanka you are taken around in a 6 seater safari vehicle. Unfortunately the driver sit s in a closed off cab and every now and
again will stop and point through his window at something. English is not very Common and many drivers are hard to understand. I would pass on this park and wish I had. It was 4 hours @ $25 US To see a crocodile, a handful of deer, a
few peacocks and a monitor lizard.

Title: Great for birds
Text: We had an early morning safari with a good driver and our tour driver who was brilliant at pointing out the wildlife. However the driver is only allowed to stick to certain paths and the undergrowth is quite dense so although they advertise that you may see leopards and sloth bears it is extremely unlikely. Great for birds though, deer and we saw wild boar too.

Title: Don't expect to see a leopard
Text: This is another example of how a tourist can lose the fun just by looking at at the price difference between locals and tourists. Now it makes sense that tax payers should have a good break, but the ripoff prices that we're made to pay, with false promises of seeing animals that will never appear in daylight, then the ugly bargaining with the jeep drivers. In the end we saw a bear, some elephants, whatever, this is a headache.

Title: Super for Wildlife Fans
Text:
This is a super park for variety of mammals and birds... But the pick of them is leopard, followed by Sri Lankan sloth Bear, both of which are elusive and hard to spot, with a 30%-40% chance imo. You could see Elephants, Crocodiles and Buffaloes too on most days. Park is nearly 1500 hectares, having over 40 water holes called "willus". The attraction is to spot the animals, and if you have enough time to see the dynamics between the hunter and the hunted. Here are few factors that may be handy to know
a. Park is open from 6am to 6pm
b. Entrance for locals is around LKR 800 for foreigners its more
c. Jeep fee are negotiable half day LKR 4500 and full day LKR 8000 for locals. For foreign nationals it my be 5000 and 10,000 respectively. Get a Toyota or Mistubishi jeep rather than Mahendra ones.  You may want to look at the seat too
d. There are no supermarkets, well stocked shops or restaurants close to the park. So arrange for food (breakfast and lunch) , water and any other refreshment you need prior to going in to the park. This is sad part, but true. Even after coming out of the park at 6pm you cant get a good cup of Ceylon tea, unless you have pre-arranged or travel to Nochiyagama (few km from Wilpattu Junction). Suggets you buy the following
1. Water Bottles from Cargills/ Keels Super or Arpico / American Premium or Aquafin
2. Tea : There are iced tea/ fruit juices if you like to sip in
3. Some fruits or nuts: Almonds and Guava are my favorites if I'm going for a full day. Anamaalu bananas are good too.
e. Park has different routes so you could say you want to go up to Thambapanni (Kudiraimalai Point) which is a beach where early settlers to Sri Lanka from India came. But less animals or birds here. But you could see sea eagles fishing on most days and large elephants on Periya willu or Periya uppu villu and sinna uppu willu. You can ask the jeep to go towards Pomparippu where seeing elephants is more likely though its a dusty road. 
f. There is a very basic washroom at Kumbukwillu where jeeps stop for breakfast (around 8-9) and lunch around 1pm. Better to tell him your expected lunch time so that you don't have to keep worrying
g. between 12.30 to 2pm these jeep drivers prefer not to drive and the excuse they say is that animals will be resting during this time. Only partly true imo but unless you know the driver well, you may have to stick to taking photos around Kumbuwillu. One driver to us to a church close to pomparippu but that is not a done deal it seems
h. you could stay at Anuradhapura and drive to the park early morning or stay in wilpattu itself. Rooms start at around 3000 for locals. You may have to check if the hotel/ motel provides food (breakfast and lunch) early morning at 5.30 or so before confirming the motel/ hotel.
I. During dry season lots of dust / If you are going with the kids you may want to use masks. Caps and sunglasses are must. I don't go there without my camera, or at least binoculars.

I have been there few times. I have been to other parks in Sri Lanka, but for diversity in terms of animals and landscape, no other park could beat Willpattu. However,, don't expect Leopards and Slothbear to usher you in to the park. That is only a 30-40% chance , though I'm repeating it ;-)

Title: Less tourists but also less animals
Text:
It was my third safari and it was also the most unique. We appreciated the fact there were only a few jeeps and most of times we were on our own I'm the park without fighting with other jeeps to watch animals. Our driver was also respectful and kept it's distance with wild life while also systematically turning the car off when observing animals. However we did not see many animals. A few herds of deers and buffalos. Two gigantic elephants and a few other birds and mammals but that's all. We had a full day tour for 5.5k lkr pax (4ppl in the jeep).

Recommend if you are patient and respect animals peace. If you want fast show with lots of animals everywhere like for your children, go somewhere else.

Title: Struggled to deliver what was promised but delivered something I was pleased with
Text:
As I write this I am a bit conflicted. All the talk about this park is the chance to see a leopard. The problem with that is the chance of seeing one is 50-50. So like what happened to me... there is potential to be disappointed when you fail to see one. Probably the biggest problem with this park is that it is quite thick jungle and as such the view from the Safari truck can get a bit monotonous. 

That being said the scenery opens up at some points and when it does it is majestic. I saw in Enormous Lotus Lily Ponds, beautiful lakes and a whole bunch of animals I was not expecting such as a very cool 'Sloth Bear', Buffalo, deer, crocodiles, monkeys and a lot - and I mean a lot - of birds of amazing colours and shapes.

At the end of the day I had to tell myself 'self don't be disappointed you ... might have missed out on the leopard but half the people do... but you still got to see something pretty amazing.'

So I think if the park perhaps talked down the leopard a bit and talked up the other great things They have this might be a more well known attraction. 

A half day was enough... It opens at 6am. It is about 1 hour out of Anuradhapura so it makes for an additional half day trip if you are visiting the ancient city there. The heat would make any longer in the park unbearable - and besides, the animals are all hiding and sleeping in the middle of the day. Take a lot of water and food with you as the shop was not open when the park opened.

Title: Largest National Park in Sri Lanka

Title: Wonderful experience
Text:
Entrance fee (rs 7800/ 3 adults) and we found a jeep charging rs 5000. No tracker was available but for me this just added the fun as now I get to play tracker. But our jeep driver was very good, he found crocodiles elephants spotted deer mongoose monkeys( 2 types) rabbits peacocks eagles lizards Buffaloes and many birds. Unfortunately no leopards or bears. But we did see leopard's foot prints. Was a beautiful tour non the less. Total tour took 4.5 hours. We left at 7.30am. Only one toilet half way through but it was in an AWEFUL condition. There were a few concrete cylinders lying around which altered the wildlife feel the place had going.
Bring lunch and water as there are no shops inside at all. Every payment must be done in Sri Lankan rupees , USD not accepted here. So ensure you have enough money on you ( same goes for all the national parks in Sri Lanka )
Tip bring a can or two of beer on board the jeep while driving around ( if you want to). But please do NOT litter. No dustbins in the jungle so please keep all the rubbish on board the jeep and throw it at the end of the tour.

Text:

At the same time the place looked quite artificial to me. One can see concrete pipes and rubber hoses in many places. And the animals seemed to be at exactly those places where the driver expected to find them.

Title: Great Lakes and Landscapes
Text:
Wilpattu National Park is the largest in Sri Lanka, located on the north-western coast of the island. The park's unique feature are the large lakes that attract much bird life. It is home to leopard, bear, sambar, elephant, deer, crocs, peacock, jungle fowl to name a few.
A visit to the park requires a minimum of half a day, however a full day visit (6am- 6pm) is highly recommended since the attractions to be visited are located at least 40 - 50 km from the park entrance and hence cannot be visited within half a day.
The scenery is beautiful and relaxing, if you are lucky you may be able to have a river bath in one of the limited locations visitors are permitted to alight. (Kokmote camp site)
You can hire a safari jeep at the entrance, the ride can be quite bumpy due to the terrain. 
There are no places to buy food, so be prepared with packed breakfast, lunch, snacks and lots of drinking water.

Title: A beautiful park for those who love birdlife and butterflies
Text: This is a park for those who want to experience a bit of wildlife and a taste of Sri Lankan nature. But don't have too high expectations, a safari tour in the park is not to be compared with the ones in southern Africa. You will see some different species of birds, lizards, water buffalo, spotted dear, barking dear, Asian elephants, wild pig and hundreds of butterflies. We were lucky to see one of the parks biggest draws up close - the Slot bear. You can either choose a morning drive or an evening drive. The morning drives are probably better than the evening ones. Most important though is to get a proper ranger, and not only a driver of a safari jeep. It can make a huge different to have someone that point out the animals and name them. We got unfortunately the other kind, a driver. The price of a 4 hour tour is on the high side. Make sure to bring water/snacks before you enter the park.

Title: Jackals and leopards
Text: Wilpattu is a fantastic national park.  We spent three days there staying in the Eco Team tented camp.  We had two very close encounters with leopards and saw others at a distance. We also saw a jackal dive into a thicket to pick up its baby in its mouth and run off at speed to a safer place - there was a leopard in the thicket!  Our guide - Dhanu - was extremely knowledgeable and the range of wildlife from the tiniest birds to huge elephants was amazing.  A visit which will be remembered for ever.

Title: Well Worth the Early Start
Text: From where we were staying we had a two hour drive to get here so it meant a really early start for us but well worth it. We did not see any leopards or elephants but we did see wild pigs, deer of various types, mongoose, crocodiles and any amount of birds, fowl and raptors. Amazing!!

Title: beautiful place
Text: We did both Yala and Wilpattu, and Wilpattu was the best in my opinion. While Yala is crowded, it seemed like we had Wilpattu to ourselves. We had a jeep for just the 3 of us so that was cool. We did a full day and it's quite exhausting. + we almost didn't see any wildlife in the afternoon.

Title: Uncrowded
Text: It's always a question of luck. Many people go to this northern wildlife park to see leopards, which has 38 of them, and never do. We saw 3 in one day, including one that put on a show in the road just a few meters away. Also spectacular is the birdlife; water fowl and eagles. This park straddled the former conflict zone during the civil war and was off-limits for nearly 20 years until the war ended in 2009. It is Sri Lanka's oldest and largest park. Its jungle is dense, making it a challenge to see even large animals. But to me, it is far preferable to Yala National Park in the south, which has so many visitors that its rutted roads are as jammed with traffic as central Colombo. And any leopard sighting attracts an unruly jostling of jeeps. That rarely happens in Wilpattu. The landscape changes dramatically in the northern part of the park, more open grasslands where herds of elephants roam -- though often at a distance. Keep an eye out in the treetops on this side for the magnificent hornbill.

Title: A good exposure to Sri Lankan wildlife
Text:
You need to be there before 6am to get tickets. We found this with many Sri Lankan national parks - early opening, but chaos to get the ticket to enter.

Once inside - it's a large park with many roads, so you do find yourself alone rather than in a queue of jeeps.

Good variety of terrain, ranging from wetlands, jungle and plains. As for wildlife - we didn't see the leopards, bears or elephants but bird life, deers, crocodiles, mongoose, water buffalo, still made it a great day.

Title: Guide availability
Text: When we drove up to the parks Hunuvilagama entrance in our rented Fortuner, the ticket man told us none of his ~30 trackers were left (high season!), and therefore he couldnt allow us to go in. After some begging, he kindly deputized one of his ~10 park wildlife protection officers (whose shift was about to end) to jump into our car so we could spend 3 hrs going in and out. So for you self-drivers out there, beware of this possibility, since the manager insisted guests were not allowed inside the park without escort. It appears there are no through roads because theres only one entrance--so far, although the map we were given at the entrance showed another in the south near Puttalam. Although the 18h30 park closing time is flexible (we left at 18h45 as part of a caravan of 7), park rules forbid artificial light (e.g. headlights!), which (because dark falls quickly at about 18h35) puts a natural limit on your visit. And although that map has far more detail (showing maybe 30 small roads) than Google Maps, still we saw passable tracks not on the map, so a guide would probably know places we cant. Jungle fowl, serpent eagle, herons, painted stork, wild boar, spotted and barking deer. The 25kph speed limit isnt hard to stick to, given how rutted and bumpy the roads are (if the park has any tarred roads, its not the one at the front gate!).

Title: A Wildlife Reserve between Puttalam and Anuradhapura Sri Lanka
Text:
The park itself is really lovely although we were very disappointed that we didn't see much fauna. That is of course the luck of the draw and we just hoped, but ce la vie. We took 3 safaris, but failed to see a single Leopard or a Bear. Saw a few deer, one tusker, a few peacocks, Jungle Fowl and their mates, and a crocodile. We also saw wild boar and several birds, and two magnificent Eagles, one a Serpent Eagle.  

The authorities really need to improve the condition of the tracks. Some of them have very deep gouges and others are completely water logged and impassable. 

My biggest grouse was the toilets. They are in a shocking condition and a disgrace to the whole country. I shudder to think of what visitors from overseas think of the standard of hygiene of this island. I do believe that the one near the Admin block has not been flushed or cleaned for at least a month. It must have been teeming with Bacteria and a site for air borne diseases. The odours from the one within the park reached at least a 10 meter radius around it. Yuck!!!! The Department of Wildlife Conservation obviously does not care about the awful image created or the health hazards. 

We fully intend returning when time permits, because although we did not encounter any thrilling experiences, we did prefer it to the other parks in Sri Lanka which are overcrowded with visitors where  one encounters jeeps racing around thoughtlessly. It was much quieter here and to us, a typical wildlife park and not a circus. Since it was a very large park, 13,00 ha, it was not easy to cover much ground with the rough tracks. 

The Water holes were full since this was post the rains, and were very serene to look at. There were large expanses of water, which could be a reason for the lack of sightings, as the animals probably had small pools inside the jungle to quench their thirst. 

The park opens at 6 am and closes at 6 pm. One has to allow plenty of time to get to the exit gates in time to be out at 6 pm if you are far away from it.

Title: Amazing Day spent with absolutely nature at Its best.
Text: If you are the out door out going Love to enjoy bumpy sans roads feel the sweat and smell the Green in the air, thén Its a wonderful place for family or friend to enjoy with coupled with laughter and satisfaction At the end of the Day. I enjoyed évery moment and would love to go again.

Title: The number 1 national park in Sri Lanka
Text: My love affair with Wilpattu started way back when I was in school. Back then the park was closed for visitors during the war. In 2003, during a ceasefire agreement, we managed to get permission to camp in the park. It was the most exhilarating experience, camping deep in the dense wilderness, next to the clear waters of the Moderagam Aru. Due to heavy poaching back then the sightings were few, but I will never forget the massive tusker I encountered on Percy Bendhi wewa close to the park entrance. I named the tusker "Wasantha" after the gutsy park warden back then Mr. Wasantha Pushpananda. Since then I cant count how many time I have visited the park. Maybe over 500 times. As a review what I would say is this park gives the most complete and "real" wildlife and wilderness experience out of all the parks in Sri Lanka. Don't come expecting a quick fix of wildlife, where a one day trip would result in a loads of wildlife. Remember this is not a zoo ! this is a real national park with real wild animals and they would choose to appear or disappear. I would highly recommend spending at least 2 full day safari's in the park to get a real feel of the place. Also having a great driver/guide is a must. This is the place, where if I die, I want my ashes scattered, its that special to me. Over the last 13 years of visiting the park, I have seen many amazing sighting, from 5 hour leopard sightings, to tuskers, bears, elusive and rare Forest Eagle Owls, our jeep being rammed by a wild boar and so much more. This is THE park to visit when your visiting Sri Lanka.

Title: You probably need two interests
Text: We took a Safari to Wilpattu National Park and thoroughly enjoyed the experience - we saw monkeys, jackals, spotted deer, muntjac deer, wild boar and mongeese - but the number of wild mammal sightings may not be enough to interest all. We also enjoyed seeing large numbers of birds. We suspect that most people would want to have two interests eg mammals/birds or mammals/flora to keep them fully engaged.

Title: Authorities please fix the toilets
Text:
This was my first visit Wilpattu. I was appalled by the state of the toilets near the ticket counter and also inside the park.  Almost all the comments on the Guest Book refers to the poor state of the toilets. It appears that the Department of Wildlife Conservation in Sri Lanka have turned a deaf ear to the requests to keep the toilets clean or build a new set of toilets suitable for foreigners to use.

The overall experience in the park was very good.   

We were at the park in late December which is also the tail end of the monsoon season. The park was lush and green and most of the Villus or Lakes were at full capacity. The park name Wilpattu is derived from these shallow Villus. Driving on the water filled sand banks of the Villus were a great experience

The sanctuary is located in the dry part of the country and it is the dryness of the surrounding that attracts animals to the many waterholes.  We didnt get to see too many animals because there is plenty of water inside the jungle for them to drink. We were lucky to spot a bear as we were leaving the park.

The park is very large (appox 13,00 ha) and was declared a wild life sanctuary in 1938.

We arrived at the park around 2.00 pm and were forced to leave before the gates close at 6.00 pm. Allow plenty of time if visiting this park. It located approximately 188 Kms from Colombo and will take about 4 hours to get there from Colombo.  Tickets have to be bought at the entrance and hiring a four wheel drive is highly recommended. The park is open from 6 am to 6 pm. The best time to visit the park is between 6 -10am or 3  6 pm in the evening. The entrance to the park is from Nochchiyagama and can be reached from Puttalam to Anuradhapura road. 

The animals we saw included peacocks, flamingos, serpent eagles, Ceylon jungle fowl, Green bee eater and many other species of birds. Also we saw, water buffalo, wild boar, deer, bear, rabbits and many crocodiles.

The best time to visit the park is between February to October.

Title: Not Worthy
Text:
We visited the safari with family in Dec 2015. However, we were not satisfied with the experience because of following reasons:
1. Park/Jungle is huge and very dense. May be because we visited in Dec which is rainy season in SL, the thick vegetation on sides of the road impacted the views
2. Animal sighting was poor. We understand it is not Zoo but after paying Foreign Toursit Fees with small kids we felt it was not worth the money and time spent. The kids were bored within half an hour into the ride.
3. Requested for Forest Ranger or Guide at entrance. However it was not available (Not Sure if the facility is not available or person was not available). That left us to interact with Driver of Safari vehicle who obviously was tasked to drive the safari vehicle safely rather than interact with tourists.

Title: At the end of the day it is a bet what you see
Text: We had great luck and saw a leopard sitting on a tree and afterwards walk closely to the jeep. We had a lot of rain in the last days, so the ponds were filled up with water and no animals were there. We saw a crocodile, deers, birds, leguans, etc. - but no bears, elephants. With the leopard a clear five star, without only two stars.

Title: Not worth
Text: We visited the safari with Family and it was not a great experience. We do understand that it is not zoo with certainty of animal sightings but the after paying the hefty tourist fee of foreigners it was not worth the time and money spend. In the whole tour we saw very few animals

Title: Amazing visit!
Text: We saw lots of wildlife on our safari through wilpattu: Sambar, spotted and barking deer, crocodiles, wild boars, Mongoose, monkeys, jackels, monitors, peacocks, hawk-eagle and many other birds! We did not see a leopard (only tracks!), but a few other people did see one that day :) great to know they're still around! We booked a driver through eagle safaris, which they never confirmed so it was a bit of a hassle to sort out when we arrived, but it worked out ok. Our driver did not speak any English, but was good at spotting things and it was fine as we know quite a bit about wildlife, but might have been difficult if we didn't know which species we would see. Amazing park for those who are keen to see Sri Lankan animals in their natural habitat without loads of tourists! Highly recommended!

Title: Safari in the north west, a huge and quiet park
Text:
As you probably read in any Sri Lanka travel guide this national park reopened only in 2009. It's Sri Lanka's biggest park, but in terms of wild life it's thinly spread. Our tour was however still amazing, the park is beautiful, but we didn't see what we come for... Not the park's fault of course. The number of visitors in the park is very low which is of course a big plus. 
We had a private jeep with a great driver and spotter. He was very knowledgeable about the park and all the (wild) life inside. 
The park is well laid out. I had a bit of a feeling too much was 'touched'. Maybe in a couple of years this is the best place to go again...

Title: Amazing park and wildlife!!!
Text:
This place is awesome. It's wild and 'mostly' free of tourists. During our whole day safari we only encountered two other jeeps. We had a terrible driver but being in a group of 4 wildlife biologists we were able to spot loads of wildlife including 30min with an elephant playing in the water and not a single human soul to be seen. Bliss!

It definitively gets hots and you might not see lots for some period of time but this is the essence of wildlife encounters.

All the people complaning about not seeing a leopard or about the lack of widlife do not understand the concet of a wild animals and must have a poor understanding of nature based tourism. It is not a Zoo and you might not see things, this is part of the game! If all you care about is a selfie with a Leopard than this place is not for you. If you ar enot ready to divert from wildlife and enjoy the scenery and natural aspect of i all, again, this place is not for you.

Try and avoid the rainy season November-December as you might not get to see the whole park due to the roads being flooded.

I loved it and will be back for sure.

Title: We saw a Leopard!
Text:
It is a nice park. Less visited by tourist which is good because you dont see a lot of jeeps in front of you. You feel almost alone in the park.

The only thing is that you need to rent a Jeep (4,500 rupies for 4 hours If I am not mistaken) plus the park entrance fee. 

We saw quite a few animals, but it all depends on your luck and whether it is the dry or raining season.

Title: The jewel of Sri Lankan nature expeditions
Text:
My wife and me went on a full day safari in a comfortable Japanese jeep, with a guide (extra cost) and experienced driver, through Best of Lanka Ltd. We were picked up by our hotel at 5am and dropped back at 6.30pm, with breakfast and lunch included. 

It was a FABULOUS experience, and I encourage everyone who is interested to go only for a full day, nothing less. Without the full 12 hours, we wouldn't have had the chance to see the numerous wonderful bird life in the morning. The herds of Spotted Deer hiding away during the midday languor. The bull elephant venturing out into the lake serenely for dinner. The unlucky leopard missing out on a jungle fowl meal, and eyeing us warily but majestically from a distance.

The dramatic shifts of landscape, from thick forest to sand dunes, from lakeside views to marshes, are spectacular. Ultimately it's not about the wildlife. It's the experience of communing with nature itself and it's fascinating, deep beauty and variety. If you have to choose one Park as a true believer in this philosophy, choose Wilpattu

Title: All by chance...
Text: We read online mixed reviews, some saying they had seen a variety of animals and other saying they hadn't seen anything. It's a lot of money, but if you are lucky enough to see something it's totally worth it. We saw a baby bear twice (think it was the same one) water buffalo, lizards, deer and lots of birds. Unfortunately we didn't see any leopards, but the driver we had knew where they had been and sat patiently for 15 minutes for a possibly chance to see them, the leopards weren't playing ball. We thought it was worth it, but it's all by chance and depending how hard you are looking.

Title: Wonderful nature reserve
Text:
The largest nature reserve in Sri Lanka, providing the opportunity to experience nature and see animals in their natural habitat.

We were able to see many different types of birds, crocodiles, spotted deer's, sloth bear, tortoises, hares, etc. in close proximity.

Title: Go early...
Text:
Was a real highlight of our trip. We saw all the animals except for the bear and the highlight was the leopard. We only had 5 jeeps in the whole park which is quite different to Yala where a leopard sighting can lead to massive gridlock

I think the quality of your experience really depends on your driver/spotter. Our driver Saagara was awesome- he spotted so many animals and told us a bit about their history. 

Recommend to go early 6-9 as more tourists come through for the evening session. Make sure you arrange a good guide beforehand

Title: Lovely Day out
Text: we spent about 6 hours here , had a great guide who was eagle eyed just don't know how he spotted some of the animals. yes there are lots of birds but also we did see many more animals, water buffalo, deer ,eagle , jackals , monitor lizards , monkeys , crocodiles , wild hogs and yes we did see a leopard all though it was deep in the trees taking cover. A really nice day and a park that will evolve to be even better over time.

Title: Difficult to spot beautiful animals
Text: The problem of the WNP is that it is very difficult to see leopard, bears and elephants so if you are on vacation and you value your time and money it just doesn't worth. You will spend 4 hours looking at some birds and deer and that's it.

Title: Very sereen, not a lot of tourists
Text: We saw a lot of animals, even a leopard. We spend 8 hrs there and there were only a few tourists there.

Title: Fantastic experience
Text: We took a one-day safari and had a fantastic experience. We didn't see many animals and birds but enjoyed the landscape and diversity of trees and plants.

Title: Peaceful, pristine national park in Sri Lanka
Text: The park was clean, including the common areas. The acreage is quite large and the woods are dense so it is not easy to see animals. We did not see leopards during our three, four-hour drives but the lakes are picturesque and birding is easy. We viewed spotted deer, barking deer, samba deer, wild boar, one male buffalo, land monitor, and it is not crowded with other vehicles.

Title: Great  safaris
Text:
Oh . very nice jungle and nice guy.we  are lucky people. We ask the hotel management after she will arrange it s jeep. Bird's ,bear.and lot of deers.we seen the three Eliphants and one leopard. 
      Nice area.beach is good but aloneness.

Title: Good bird spotting but nothing else
Text: So disappointed....spent four hours driving round only to see birds, a monitor lizard, jackals, monkeys...and the sighting of a leopard was on a poster to warn against dropping litter.  Furthermore, there was no opportunity to communicate with the driver who was sat in his cab and us in the back. If we saw something it was a noisy drama to get the vehicle to stop...not ideal!

Title: A National Park with disappointments
Text:
Wilpattu National Park is the biggest National Park in Sri Lanka, it is said to cover 132,00 hectares and houses many wild animals. However, our visit to the park recently is full of disappointments. Firstly, the entrance ticket is very expensive ( USD 40/person) and what we got to see were just a few animals and birds. Only one elephant was seen drinking water from a pond ; 2 serpent eagles and a few peacocks ( which are common even in countryside in Sri Lanka). After going round and round many times in the park, we finally managed to get a glimpse of a leopard which we could hardly see becasue it was so far away from our car.

That was all we had for 4 hours of so called safari trip. In conclusion, it is not worth making the trip to the park because it has nothing much to offer except the bumpy ride!

Title: Great national park
Text: Wilpattu is open again since 2009. It is a park in the wet zone which means lots of natural lakes. You can find all the special mammals here, including the leopard, elephants and sloth bear. It is a dusty road to get further inside the park so take something with you to cover your mouth and nose and your camera.

Title: Wildlife
Text:
The park is situated just a half hour before Anuradhapura if you are coming from colombo and is pretty green
There are a lot of trees and bushes and this makes spotting the animals difficult, but the rangers are pretty good and they know where to look.

The park is also less visited than for example Yala and that is a good thing, here you don't have 50 jeeps around a leopard and you have more the idea that you are in the jungle (and not like Yala where you sometimes have the idea that you are on a highway)
We visited this park in not the best weather of our tour through Sri Lanka. But although the weather was far from great we enjoyed the safari very much. We saw a lot of wildlife and also a leopard (unfortunately no bear). Maybe it is due to the weather that we saw a lot of wildlife, because when the sun is shining and it is very hot most animals will hide their self under the bushes and they will be hard to spot then. Now the animals were mere out in the open.

So if you have the time to visit I would say do.

Title: Peaceful and relaxing day
Text:
We had an early start for our safari (5:30). However it was quite a nice and relaxing day with comfortable seats in our jeep.
Not that many animals to be seen though. We did see some deer, wild pigs, sloth, monkeys, numerous birds and one elephant. The elusive leopard was not to be found even though our guide really tried, calling and conferring with other jeep drivers that have spotted him that day.

Title: Saw lots of wildlife - but no leopards!
Text: Great journey out - saw crocodiles, lizards, monkeys, deer, great birdlife, mongoose & wild boar. It was along journey back to the exit though, in a VERY uncomfortable jeep!

Title: Well managed park with lots of wildlife
Text:
Vilpaththu National Park is a newer park in the north west of the island that is growing in popularity.  I chose to come here over Yala and the more famous reserves in the south as I had heard a lot of tales from other travellers about irresponsible operators in that park, harassing the animals and behaving dangerously.  So I decided I'd prefer to visit a park that had lower chances of seeing a leopard, but at least wouldn't put the animal at any risk if I did see one.

Vilpaththu does have all sorts of animals living within its forests, including leopards, sloth bears, crocodiles, and a very small number of elephants.  You are not guaranteed to see them.  I have been lucky enough to already see leopards in Africa, so I was perhaps more relaxed about this than some travellers may be.  

The park consists of dense jungly forest, interspersed with big lakes (the name means 'many lakes').  You drive in high, open sided jeeps along well defined but bumpy red earth tracks, through the forest.  There are relatively few tracks so you tend to take the route there is.  There aren't options for vehicles to go 'off road' due to the forest, which is a good thing as it prevents the environment being degraded.

On a four hour trip, I saw lots of different wildlife, including crocodiles (huge, and really good views), spotted and barking deer, mongooses, peacocks, green bee eaters, a serpent eagle, beautiful butterflies, large monitor lizards, two types of monkey, wild boar, and wading birds.  For me, a lot of the joy of a safari is not knowing what you might see next, and its that thrill of the unknown that makes it such a great experience.  Even if you see nothing at all, I find that makes the experience worthy in itself.  Of course, I'm lucky in having done several safaris in different places, so perhaps get less anxious about seeing things that people who might have only had this chance.

If I'd had more time, I'd have been happy to stay here and do a few game drives over a couple of days.  I reckon if you went several times you'd have a pretty good chance of seeing a leopard or bear.  You are unlikely to see elephants here, but there are lots of other parks in Sri Lanka where you've got a really high chance, so factor in a trip to one of those too if you can.  It's a well managed park, with no litter and not too many jeeps, and I loved it.  If you have never seen big wildlife before and are desperate to see a leopard, you might be better off going for one of the southern parks.  But I'd highly recommend this park in addition if you can, or for those who are happy to see smaller animals.

Title: Wilpattu National Park, well worth the visit
Text: In January my daughter and I spent an afternoon in Wilpattu and it was the highlight of our 2 week trip.   Other reviewers have been disappointed that they may not have seen a leopard, something the park is famous for.  We went with the expectation that a leopard sighting would be a bonus.  The park is half the size of Rhode Island and is full of animal we did not see in Udawalewe or Bundalla.  The park itself is beautiful but the during the last hour as it was getting cooler (after 4:00) we saw a large male leopard asleep in the road.  We were far enough away that he took his time waking up and moving on.  Everyone was ecstatic as we quietly watched this amazing animal.   I was fortunate to have a large lens on my camera and I've been asked to share the photos with our driver.  If we had not seen the leopard the park would have been a wonderful success since the park has only reopened in the last few years, it still feels very special.

Title: Jeep safari in Sri Lanka's largest national park
Text:
I wanted to take my kids to see something of the Sri Lankan geography, and also various animals in their natural habitat (rather than zoos or such like).
After taking the advice of a very helpful lady at our hotel (Menuka at Jetwing Blue), I booked this trip which included transfer from/to the hotel, a naturist guide (also provided by the hotel) and the jeep safari at the park.
We were staying in Negombo, so it was a 3 hour journey to the park.  Kids feel asleep and I enjoyed seeing the various sights along the way.
Once at the park, our guide took care of everything whilst we had lunch (which was a picnic provided by our hotel) - all very nice and relaxed!
The jeep safari was excellent - basically it is a converted 4x4 pick up truck with comfy seats welded/bolted into the back.  It had a roof but open sides - so we only got a little bit wet when the rain poured down!
During our visit there were intermittent heavy downpours, but this did not in any way spoil the experience.  Our kids loved it (aged 7 and 3).
We saw many animals and birds, each explained by the naturist who had a book and binoculars (my 3 year old was so much more interested to be shown the book when looking at something in real life - it made it more understandable for him).
Highlights included there was the lone bull elephant eating reeds in one of the lakes, a leopard (which we only spotted on the way back), large land lizards, peacocks and other colourful birds.
We left as it was getting dark, and just before the gate there was an elephant crossing the path - we had to wait until it disappeared into the bush, but then it let out a loud roar which the kids thought was amazing.
Although it was a long journey from/to our hotel (because of young kids), we all thoroughly enjoyed the visit and it is a memory that we will cherish.

Title: The biggest parks of he parks and further away from the more heavily tourist populated parks of the south
Text: Well known for its leopards - but it is hit and miss if you want to see a leopard for certain go to the zoo - but you will see lots of birds, many predatory types feature along with fishing birds and parrots.  Croodiles seem to be freequently sighted from babies on small ponds to larger ones sunning themselves by their established homes at various waterholes.  Plenty of Water Buffalo and some elephants though we only saw one at dusk.

Title: Interesting...
Text:
The ride to 'Wilpattu National Park' took some hours. Once arrived, there was time for a bathroom break. After which we went into the park with our driver. 
We drove for many hours through the park on bad roads full with holes (in all sizes). This was a bit of an unpleasant ride because after some time you get enough of the shaking in the back of a truck. 

The guide sitting next to the driver pointed out various animals we saw / encountered. But that is all the two of them did. Drive and point. There were no other interactions, no additional information or anything. 
Unfortunately, this might have had more to do with the trip we booked then with the park itself. We booked a trip at a place across our hotel to the 'Wilpattu National Park'.

Ive been in South Africa before and did some safaris through several parks. Compared to them, Wilpattu seems like childsplay. But maybe mid November is not the best time?
We saw quite some things; Ill list them in order of interest:
  -- A cute small/medium sized bear was hiding in the bushes. Took some time for him to come out and he crossed the road. 
  -- Just before we left the park, we saw an elephant hidden behind bushes. 
  -- A cool green/blue bird. 
  -- Some deers.
  -- Some monkeys. 
  -- A lizard or two.
  -- Two white storks.
  -- Quite some peafowl.

Title: Fantastic Experience
Text: Lovely day out, we went during the dry season so were NEVER going to see leopards and Bears, but were treated to Monkeys, Grizzly Squirrels, Eagles aplenty, Eagle Owl, deer, baby crocodiles, water buffalo, wild dogs, mongoose, monitor lizards, peacocks and many beautiful birds and butterflies.

Title: Not a tourist destination
Text: Peaceful and unforgettable.  To say it was once an area ravaged by war, I have to say it has survived and is steadily evolving and life is returning.  If you are looking for a touristy park with lots of wildlife, this is not for you, go to Yala for that.  If you hope to see wildlife but are not really worried if you don't, then this is for you.  I only hope that the government have the sense to restrict numbers entering the park as it is best that the wildlife is left peacefully to recover.  Absolutely loved it and the views are stunning and our indebted thanks to Leopard Trails and Indika and his team who made it absolutely memorable.

Title: Beautifull park!
Text: Our guide suggested to visit Wilpattu NP instead of Yala NP, because Yala would be closed when we supposted togo there for a safari. This was a perfect alternative! Unfortinately we didn't saw a leopard during but it didn't made our experience less wonderfull. During our afternoon safari (app. 4h), we saw some elephants, deers, lizards, crocodiles and a lot of birds. We heard many stories about Yala is being popular and more crowded than Wilpattu. In the time we were on safari, we didn't saw another jeep. You can enjoy the beautifull nature, silence and animals in the wilderness!

Title: Wilpaththu naitonal Park  with Muthalif jeep safari
Text: It was a really good day. We're in raining seasons , an we can see and leopard and elephants . Thanks to de driver . He didn't stop until find de Leopard. :) . Amazing day. Thanks Muthalif jeep safari

Title: Not interesting
Text: We spend the afternoon searching for leopard, but unfortunately we couldn't find any. Concerning other breeds you can see the same animals outside the park so no need to spend 3 to 4 hrs of your life at Wilpattu National Park.

Title: Easy to book safaris
Text: We went on safari from the Big Game Camp Wilpattu - the vehicle was very comfortable and the scenery is interesting - heaps of raptors and hornbills, plus elephant. There are also landrovers at the junction - it looked very easy to go on safari even if you hadn't booked ahead.

Title: Beautiful park!
Text:
We went to Wilpattu instead of Yala for a chance to see a leopard in the wild. I had to change my group's itinerary at the last minute due to the announcement of Yala that it will be closing on the day my group was supposed to go there for a safari. I think it was the best unfortunate circumstance to happen because we managed to spot leopards on 3 different areas of Wilpattu.

The park is beautiful. We went in early September so it was the end of the drought season. Near the opening of the park, it was dry and almost arid but deeper into it you will see the lush fullness of the forest around the reservoirs. Our guide, Krishan Fernando of Triplanka Tours was a god send. If you're a bird watcher you will love the guy. He identified all the wildlife we saw, most especially the birds. He knows all the local birds of Sri Lanka by heart. He even brought binoculars with him. Had a good eye in spotting the wildlife in the bushes, better even that our hired park driver.

We paid 3300rupees each for a group of 6 people for 6 hours in the afternoon in the park. Thats 130-630pm. We opted afternoon with the thought that the animals will start appearing after the heat of midday, maybe near the watering holes. We were lucky. We saw a 2 year old adult male leopard 3-4 hours into the safari. It was just right there. Lounging beside a bush at the edge of clearing near a lake. Like a boss. The other two we saw while going back to the entrance. Along the road! One was around an 18 month old female who probably just left the care of its mum as our guides said and another was a cub, barely a year old. so the mum was also probably hiding somewhere in the bush.

We didn't spot a sloth bear, our guide said it wasn't the time of the year but the leopards alone were so worth it. Just hope for the best though, not everyone sees one. They do get scared if there are too many jeeps around. We were lucky there were only a max of maybe 15 jeeps that afternoon with us. A couple we talked to spent an entire day at the park without seeing a single leopard or bear. Just birds.
