Title: Disapointing
Text: We visited Wilpattu in August this year and drove around for 3 1/2 hours but unfortunately we didn't see anything other than lizards and monkeys that you can see anywhere in Sri Lanka. We were hoping to see sloth bears, elephants and or leopards, sadly none of them were in town the day we went.

Title: Wildlife watching at its best!
Text:
A great National park with an abundance of Bird/wildlife but without the huge numbers of tourists of other parks such as Yala.
Saw the majority of large mammals we were after including Leopard but unfortunately no Sloth Bear.
Saw over 40 different Species of Bird including Lesser Adjutant.

Title: Not much wildlife that day
Text: Unlike some other reviewers, I wasn't lucky. In the whole day, I saw lots of birds, a few deer, and one elephant. However, the marshland scenery is beautiful, but after several hours it gets old, as it's the same. At the breakfast and lunch stop, take the short walk to the lake--about 100 meters. It's relaxing and peaceful there, and there are the most interesting frogs to watch.

Title: Don't go there
Text:
We booked a safari to Wilpattu national park from Anuradhapura. The trip started in the morning at 5:15h from our hotel. The car was nice and brought us directly to the park. Hopefully we bought some breakfast before, since there was no possibility to get some (the hotel, hievet, offered to prepare us breakfast for some phantasy price extra, which we did not do).

The six hour half day trip was unfortunately very very boring. We saw dogs, chicken, several birds, frogs and as a tiny highlight two crocodiles.

That was it. No elephants nor any other interesting animals.

In total very disappointing, definitely not worth the 7000RS we paid per person.

Title: Unforgettable experience
Text: We stayed near the entrance which was great for watching birds and the locals bathing in the river. Our driver tried hard to spot the wildlife, it would have been a little better if he spoke a little English, but nevertheless it was a great day.  We spotted a Leopard,crocodiles,eagles,deer, wild boar and lots of birds. Take food and water with you as nothing in park. We did all day trip very bumpy and lasted 12.5 hours.Shame about rubbish around "toilet ". Hardly any western tourists but quite a few locals as it was a long weekend.  Exhausting day but well worth it as we spotted the leopard in the middle of the day.

Title: A wonderful wildlife reserve
Text: A top place for wildlife lovers. We visited over 3 days and saw leopards,sloth bear,jackal, lots of elephants, deer, crocodiles and mongooses, etc, and we logged over 70 different birds.

Title: Saw very little
Text: Went on an early am safari - this park is enormous, and just now beginning to come back after the civil war ended in 2009.  I didn't see any animals other than a couple water buffalo and some deer.  I think both the size of the park and the decline in animals over the years makes it very difficult to really spot any abundance.  However, the park itself looks like it is well maintained and the Sri Lankans are trying to promote awareness of the need for animal habitat.

Title: Famous for leopards
Text: Famous for leopards, elephants, many bird species.......bungalows inside the park are in great demand. Guest houses around the turn off to the park......comfortable, Airconditioned......Teal cottage best....Leopards den ok.....the guest house will arrange a jeep......ask for Bobby or Wimalasena.....enter early...6AM.....take your breakfast in the park....the guest house will pack a breakfast for you. Return to guest house for lunch and a rest......get back to the park at 3pm. On lucky days you will see many leopards. I was not lucky......this time. My friends have seen plenty in one day!

Title: Nice park - wrong time
Text:
Visited the park in March which is the end of the rainy season, therefore the lakes were very full (we were actually driving through the edges of them). Believe this is why we didn't see any elephants as the animals don't move about much when there's plenty of water about.
Despite this we saw a lot of deer, lizards, couple of jackals, peacocks and other birds. The vegetation itself was also very scenic.  

We didn't have a guide but don't think this would have helped in our situation. The drivers all stop when they pass each other to find out if anyone has spotted wildlife.

Title: wet wood without wildlife
Text: Ok, it rained, and as we passed through the entrance it poured and then flooded (rare for February), but this national park was a waste of time. It took forever to get there from the airport along the coast road North which is an endless sprawl of shabby ribbon development, and not the best introduction to Sri Lanka. After three and a half hours of a stomach-churning jolt from one pothole to another along an enclosed narrow sandy track, made worse by the jeep convoys which are obligatory, we saw a rabbit, a tortoise, a chicken, a log (which might have been a crocodile) and the backside of a water buffalo, not animals exactly known for their wild ways.Give it a miss: you'll see more wildlife in Kandy's excellent Botanical Gardens.

Title: For the Love of the Leopard
Text: When we stayed for 3 nights at Nilketha Hotel, Anuradhapura, Adrian, the manager, booked a full-day safari for us at Wilpattu National Park.  Our driver was so brilliant, making sure we didn't miss a thing - and we saw some amazing wildlife and had every opportunity to take great shots of the things we saw. And oh!  What we saw!! An elephant taking a bath in the marshes; several kingfishers and bee-eaters posing for photos on tree-branches; peacocks galore on the trails and in the bushes; an eagle glaring at us from the tree-tops with beady, hypnotic eyes; spotted deer in herds grazing in the bush - mums and dads and babies.  And then we came across a leopard, sauntering through a clearing in the jungle, looking so gorgeous.  It was so other-worldly somehow - and I still can't quite believe our luck.  Our driver was really on the ball, getting us as near as possible to this beautiful creature.  I'm sure if I'd leaned out a little more from the 4WD I'd have been able to touch him.  My husband and I were so fortunate to have the driver and the 4WD to ourselves - especially since we passed a lot of tourists packed to the hilt in their vehicles.  We felt privileged and downright spoiled!  What a wonderful day - warm and breezy - lots to see - lots of breaks to eat our packed lunches and head to the loo. WOW!

Title: Two Leopards...Score.
Text: I felt like Vilpaththu struck a good balance between reasonable regulation and flexible freedom. Our hostel arranged a driver who took us to the park and then transferred us to a park jeep in which we spent the morning hunting around for leopards. Spoiler Alert: We found two jaguars and they were magnificent to see up close. Neither they nor the peacocks, deer or other animals were particularly skittish so it made for great photos. We observed both park department jeeps as well as private vehicles but all the drivers seemed to be in touch so that when a sighting was made, the other vehicles were able to coordinate to maximize sightings. We were able to get out and stretch at a designated rest zone (with a bathroom). I wished that we had more time to spend there and we appreciated that the guides were both expeditious in their attempts to cover as much ground as possible but also stayed put as long as we felt like taking pictures at a given spot. Good times.

Title: Fairly dense jungle
Text: Did two trips into the park on successive days. As other reviews have said, there are few roads and the jungle is fairly dense. You have to work hard to find and see animals and birds and its not easy to get good photos. Few other tourists. We have visited Yala three times where its an easy tourist trip but we did enjoy Wilpattu.

Title: Worlds within worlds
Text: Though you have to get up early, it's worth it when you get to see so many different animals living in the wild plus so many different landscapes. A half-day safari is plenty though: the park is enormous and you will see a huge amount of things within 4 hours.

Title: Nice, but too long to get to center.
Text: The park is great, but there are 26km from the entrance until you get to the main area where most of the animals can be found and beautiful watering holes.  You see some in those 26km, but it normally is kind of empty and you lose some time just going in and out.

Title: Beautiful park and no other tourists!
Text: Some visitors give the park 1 star, other give the park 5 stars. How is that possible? We went to Wasgomuwa NP Udawawele NP, Yala NP and Wilpattu NP and can compare these parks. We put Wilpattu on the top position with 5* mainy because there are hardly any other tourists, the park is very big, the trackers love their park ánd they have all the wildlife! We spent the wole day in the park (from 6 am to 6 pm) and were never bored! We don't think you must give 1* or 5* because you see a lot of wildlife or you didn't see any wildlife. On our day In Yala nobody saw a leopard and the day before us 4 leopards were spotted. Spotting the wildlife is not a reason for us to give 1* or 5* because th WILDlife is unpreditable. We give Wilpattu 5* because the park really gives you the feeling of being in a wild national park. It's huge, there are many different habitats and people at the ticket office, the locals, the driver and our tracker all love the park and love to welcome tourist after 25 years of war. In Yala, it's too touristic, they just want your money... Spotting a leopard in the wet season in Wilpattu is difficult and we were lucky to be the only ca (out of the 10 in the park) that day to spot a leopard. In the dry season they spot as many as 10 leopards on 1 day. Wilpattu has a lot of elephants, 3 species of deer, crocodiles, big lizards, turtles, lots of birds etc. So the park has a friendly and relaxed atmosphere and that is something Yala doesn't have at all. So, go to Wilpattu and you wil NOT be disappointed

Title: Visiting wild animals in Wilpattu
Text:
We left Kalpitya for a day trip (started visit at 2pm, ended visit by 6:30pm) and diversify our activities from beach and kitesurfing

The park is stunning and the jeep was old-school as we love it!

Driver was really knowledgeable and had the eyes to spot living creatures from small birds to a big male elephant, including a variety of deers, crocodiles... but no leopard, who apparently do not like rain and wet grounds

One CAVEAT, lodges around are really pricey and given the lack of competition do not offer great accommodation: we visited after our day in wilderness but decided to come back by night rather than sleep over at the park

Title: Seen Better Days
Text:
I was looking forward to some great wild life photos and with a very slight chance of seeing a leopard.

It was very tired looking bush, all water holes were very low or dry. We saw a few water birds, a viper, monitor, a kingfisher, 2 close up eagles some wart hogs, a mongoose, a bear and some good shots of spotted deers. Oh we also came across two leopard footprints on sandy track.

I have probably been spoiled with excellent wild life experiences in South America and stunning experiences in Africa but even so I was disappointed. Our driver and spotter were willing workers but lacked the skills for searching and approaching wildlife. Driving too quick through tree areas and no quick response possible to driver when one of us spotted an animal/bird.

My recommendation is that it is worth going there on the chance you could be lucky but are prepared to accept that you may see very little.

Title: Morning safari ( 6 hours)
Text:
Stayed in Wilpatthu for two nights in a bungalow run by the wild life conservation group S/L,next to the national park very basic accommodation in a beautiful setting with wild animals visiting you at night.Most of the accommodation around the park are very basic.For me this was a good experience adds to the whole adventure.
The morning safari was a beautiful drive into the jungle lots of birds big and small, was not fortunate enough to see any big animals however did see a leopard in a tree covered in bushy branches just managed to get a glimpse of it, well camouflaged.A group that went that afternoon saw a leopard walking in front their jeep, they do say the afternoon trip is better for spotting big animals.Entry fee was S/L Rs 3000.00 £ 15.00 per person, safari jeep cost Rs 4500.00 (takes 6 persons) and finally Rs 1000.00 for the tracker that comes with driver.Sounds a lot but when you do your maths its not a lot.Do take a packed lunch and lots of drinks and enjoy the truly wild side of S/L. Did not see any Elephants in park but they did visit our bungalow at night.
( For ladies toilet facilities are not good once you are in the park picnic area, watch your bags and cameras  as the monkeys will get them.)

Title: Beautiful landscape, few animals
Text: I booked on the Wilpattu website. The driver and the tracker were playing more on their mobile phones than looking for animals. We saw a few birds and deer but not much more during a morning game driver. Perhaps we are too spoiled having been to fantastic African safari parks previously.

Title: Whole day safari
Text:
I had a whole day safari, but I suggest it's better to have a morning and an afternoon-safari. I believe the afternoon-safari will be longer and it's a better time to spot the animals after dusk. I was so lucky to se a Leopard sliping in the sun and jumping up in the tree. But we didn't see any elephants, even it's 200 of them. Do not expect to see as many animals as in Africa, if you have been on a safari there. But I saw quite a few birds, some land monitors, crocodiles, wild pigs, spotted deer, turtles and one buffalo. In the morning it was about 4 jeeps, but later we were all alone. 
I got a very, very simple lunch packet, but it was not sufficient, so bring some extra food if you don't get the time to eat breakfast before you leave on the early morning safari.

Title: A park you must visit
Text: This park is relatively quiet and one gets peace to view the animals. Our guide followed leopard tracks up the road until we eventually caught sight of him sitting on the verge. The leopard was not surrounded by other jeeps as in other parks. One wants to spend a whole day there so get your hotel to provide packed breakfast and lunch. Make sure you visit the park before it gets too popular

Title: Not that much wildlife
Text:
We took an afternoon game drive in the park, from 3 to 6. He heard an elephant, glimpsed a leopard behind the bush for half a second, plus common wildlife. Scenery is nice in some areas around lakes but nothing oustanding, maybe we are just too used to African game drives, nothing comparable! 
Jeep rental R5000 + entrance fee for 2 R5800 so 60 euros

Title: Great nature reserve
Text: We were there for one afternoon until dusk. The highlight was seeing two young leopards at close quartets playing & climbing into the trees. We also saw deer, a lone elephant, baby wild boar & crocodile. The were lots of exotic birds as well. The guides were fantastic. Well worth the visit.

Title: Good trip but didn't see a leopard
Text: I visited twice in 2 days and saw lots of animals including elephants and  bears but the closest I got seeing a leopard were the paw marks from the one that passed by the morning before.

Title: Modest setting, but the wildlife is astonishing
Text: Half a day jeep safari may be the best bet since sitting in the jeep even for a half day is tiring, but you forget all the difficulties when you see the animals. We saw lots of birds, crocodile, deer, jackal, mongoose and leopard to mention a few. Unforgettable experience.

Title: More enjoyable than Yala
Text:
We visited 2 national parks in Sri Lanka... Wilpattu and Yala... and they were quite different. The animals were probably further apart here, but so were the tourists! The tourist volume in Yala was crazy, especially when there was talk of a leopard sighting early on, and we did not enjoy it. In my opinion Yala was still worth visiting, but don't anticipate a relaxing tour! 

In contrast when we stopped for breakfast by the lagoon in Wilpattu we saw only 3 or 4 other jeeps (compared with maybe 30-40 in Yala), and rarely passed them on the tracks. We weren't lucky enough to see leopards in either park. But we did see plenty of birds, buffalo, deer, wild boar, crocodiles, mongoose and a fox. Plus it is a very scenic park, with lots of dense jungle as well as some open spaces and waterholes.

We also took our 2 and 4 yr old boys who loved it until they fell asleep (it's an early morning start to see the most animals). Tour was longer than expected, almost 4 hours in the park, but well worthwhile!

Title: perfect
Text: We saw more than 100 elephant at the same time it was really amazing experience .....Price is cheaper than Yala and nature is more beautiful......

Title: Master  Campers Luxury Portable tented camps in Sri Lanka Wildlife Parks
Text:
We, party of two(couple) stayed At a potable tented camp by "Master Campers" outfit inside the Wilpattu National Park, in Sri Lanka on the nights of November 29, 30 and December 1 in 2013. 
The tents are reasonably comfortable with enough cold water and barely adequate hot water. Remember that these tents are set up in a few hours time, considering that I would rate the accommodation in terms of comfort as satisfactory to good. The Master Campers own vehicles take you for game drives in the morning and afternoon. As you are already camping within the park you get more actual drive time in park game dives. The guides are well informed and very very helpful. The food is good and has reasonable choices.I was told that they arrange for within the park tents at various wild life parks in Sri Lanka; but can do only three nights maximum within one park. We were able to see leopard, crocodiles, many birds,. especially eagle species, elusive barking deer, Sambar deers, python, mongooses, jackals, the rare Purple Faced Leaf Monkey(Tachypethicus vetulus), grey Langurs, Fishing owls among others. The very agile climbing leopards being the most rewarding experience. The Game drives were excellent and accommodation good to very good.

Title: No leopard but lots of other wildlife in 3 hour ride.
Text:
Only complaint - the visibilty from the safari wagons is very limited by having a solid fixed fibreglass roof and a roll down 9" surrounding pelmet so anything in the trees (ie birds!) is impossible to see. The driver stayed in the cab, as we had no guide on board, and he pointed out of his window so no information on what we were looking for or indeed had missed.

Having said that low level birds, iguanas aplenty, jungle fowl, peacocks, crocs, turtles, mongoose, jackals, several types of deer, water buffalo, elephant, (stupidly the driver missed the best one and did not stop despite us shouting and banging on his cab roof) all seen well and many photographed.

I know that Sri Lanka and its fabulous people are recovering wonderfully well from a terrible war and tsunami and I am loathe to criticise but they need to make a few adjustments to improve the viewing experience and attract more tourists to this fantastic nature reserve.

Title: good plan for a full day tour
Text:
We did an evening, morning, and a full day tour in the park.  We used the naturalist and driver from Palpatha Resort.  They were fantastic.

I would recommend doing a full day tour.  It takes quite some time getting in and out to the center of the park.  This maximizes your time spent on sightings.  

We actually saw our 2 leopards near mid day. 

Arrive at the gates at 6 AM, and take food and plenty of water.

We did not feel crowded at all.  Most of the time we were the only vehicle around and could stay in a spot and enjoy the sounds and sights.

Title: Punisi Jeep Safari - Kelum
Text: My recent visit to Wilpattu National Park was fantastic. We had Kelum +94 718272499 organize our stay and safaris where he pesonally took care of us. The Hotel was not much to write home about, but, with what was available it was O.K. The food was fantastic though. The Safari experience with Kelum was one to remember - birds, reptiles and mamals. He has a fantastic eye and is a must have for a photographer or a tourist. We were also stuck as had an issue with our driver which we had hired out of Colombo and wanted to fire him...Kelum stayed awake till 3 am and organized another car to drive down from Colombo to pick us up at 5:30 in the morning and was back to see us off.... That's what I call service. He is genuinely a very warm and friendly chap. If you ever visit Wilpattu do call him in advance to book the Safaris with him. You could tell him you want to stay in a village setting as then he could send you a few options of hotels.... As there are a few small 2-3 room guest houses which I did not persue...

Title: Unless you're staying close,not sure it's worth it
Text:
Yes it is a beautiful serene place. However, we were told it was a "half day tour". It took 3 hours each way from our hotel in Negombo. We had about 2 1/2 hours in the park as we had to get back to our other daughter. Our guide was very knowledgable and had pretty good English. 

The facilities at the reception area were lacking to say the least. The smell from the toilets was indescribable, and a little tip, take some toilet paper with you!

We saw a lot of birds, crocodiles, deer, monitors and mongoose , but no leopards or elephants.

For US $400 (booked thru our hotel), I thought it was a bit overpriced!

Title: Awesome Experience
Text: Wilpattu is the largest National Park in Sri Lanka not yet  overrun by Tourism, as in Yala. We were fortunate enough to "research and compare " info. before our actual trip. As we had a local chauffeur throughout our holiday, our jeep and tracker was reserved in advance, please make sure that you get the offical ones recognised by the authorities.Our aim was to see an area known as Thambipani, due to the erosion of the hills by the sea winds, one can see unusual rock formations,this area was also where the first Ruler Vijaya, landed from India.We were the first vehicle to enter the park at 6am. and we left the park at +- 5pm.We were very lucky in that we saw also everything that lives here, leopards(3) 1sloth bear, land monitor(sp?) mongoose, elephants, crocodiles, soft back tortoise, hundreds of birds, including the hornbill, and many beautiful trees and plants, we were amazed!!!

Title: Great Jeep Safari
Text: We had an excellent morning's jeep safari - just the two of us, our driver and a very friendly and knowledgeable guide. Plenty to see and, hooray, that included a beautiful leopard.

Title: lovely scenery, not a huge concentration of game
Text: had two great days here with Leopard safaris - though we weren't lucky enough to spot a leopard! No herds of deer, or large numbers of any particular species here, but a great experience nonetheless

Title: A rather disapointing experience
Text:
We were rather unfortunate in that a guide was not available due to the large numbers on safari at the time. It is a large game reserve and does need an experienced guide to find animals. We were out in the afternoon,
/evening when there should have been some game around. Other members of our party persevered and went on the next mornings safari and had better luck spotting a leapord among other animals. The presence of an experienced guide made the difference. Our overnight stay at the no frills 4 bedroom "hotel" was inexpensive and quite comfortable with excellent service.

Title: Underrated park
Text: We spent an afternoon in late July in the park, enjoying every minute of it. Sightings included four sloth bears, crocodiles, two types of deers, wild boars, monkeys, wild buffaloes and lots of birds, including serpent eagles, horn bills, and jungle fowls. We did not see any leopards, but we have met lots of other travellers who had that fortune during recent weeks. The landscape is superb, with a highly varied forest being interspersed by meadows and lakes. Having read slightly less positive reviews in guidebooks and from other visitors, the experience definitely surpassed our expectations.

Title: Jeep safari
Text: Saw an elephant and crocodiles but sadly no leopards. Trip slightly marred by opaque pricing re jeep hire and accompanying guide so get all prices and clarify who is owed what up front (do not rely on being told at the end).

Title: The park is good, the town not so good
Text: Spent two days in Wilpattu. It's a pretty run down and barren town, I'd recommend staying elsewhere (Anuradapura or Puttulam) and doing the safari from there. First day in Wilpattut was spent trying to find the cheapest half day safari, none of the jeep drivers wanted to bargain everyone was charging 5000 rupees for 4 hours. We found one guy at the "Fride Rice" restaurant that offered us 4500 so we went with him. Picked us up at 5.30am as the park opened at 6, we had to buy an entrance ticket to the national park which was 5700 rupees. Only one ticket was needed per jeep not person, so would be cheaper if there was a group in the jeep. We saw lots of monkeys, spotted deer, barking deer, serpent eating eagles, a couple of snakes, wild boar....but no leopards which was unfortunate. The park itself is beautiful, the wetlands are really pretty. It gets very hot after 10am and apparently the prime time for leopard spotting is between 6-7am so a half day safari is worth it! If you stay in the town there's only two places to stay on the main road where the bus drops you off, and the cheapest is 2000 rupees a night for a non ac double (The leopard den hotel)..this was by far the worst accommodation we'd had in Sri Lanka.

Title: Great but avoid on a weekend!!
Text:
Wilpattu is a beautiful national park and a perfect place for any bird lover to visit. We were lucky to see a number of different types of birds of prey as well as the stunning kingfishers. Our driver guide recommended that we visit the park in the afternoon as he has a 100% record of seeing at least one leopard there when he has been in the afternoon and it was great advice! The ranger managed to track down a leopard for us which was lying in the middle of one of the roads. We had a great view and it was an amazing animal.

The only downside was the number of other jeeps in the park. As it was a saturday there were lots of locals who were extremely noisy and littered (the ranger kept popping out to pick out their rubbish which they just chucked out the back of their jeep). At points it did feel that we were just in a queue following 6 other jeeps around which made it hard to stop and take photos.

Title: Excellent Place to Visit
Text: Very good place to visit, day trip would be better with the option of going to beach. we were very luck to see lots of animals.

Title: large undiscoverd forest
Text: Safari in wilpattu sanctuary is really wonderfull.It is different from yala and its landscape is quite large and different diversity of animals. plenty of safari jeeps availabe cheap charges( 4500 to 6000 Rupees). Spotted animals and birds were leopard,elephants,fox,aligators,eagles,wild chicks ,monkeys,deers,toucan,peacocks.

Title: Lovely Park
Text: We had an evening drive, all day and the following morning.  The early mornings are great for birds and we saw a leopard towards the end of the day.  Sightings are possible most of the day.  The park is hot and there is only one picnic site.  No toilets, only nature!  This park has only been reopened in the last two years and building is going on which may result in better amentities.  The education building just before you enter the park has great photos, information and a toilet - worth a look.

Title: An idyllic nature setting at the Willu
Text:
My expereinces of the park was a first, and my impressions were very positive with regard to the range and scale of fauna and flora considering that the park's size meant that most shy animals could remain outside the visitors' paths with ease.

Our jeep experience was less than satisfactory as the guides allocated to us simply performed routine roles which included taking us on a designated route, with absolutely no consideration for the needs of the tourist but with a view on the "tip" only. 

This might not be noticed by foreign visitors as much as local visitors would. This seems to be a general reflection on attitudes in general throughout such operations for visitors to the country.

Our accommodation at a private bungalow owned by a friend was superb while being simple, in that it included a very enthusiastic husband and wife team who saw to all our needs with great interest.

The weather in late June was quite dry and the area had not seen rain for perhaps more than a month. The lack of toilet facilities at the park office area was felt badly, as everyone had to go to the bush area outside those premises.

Overall, the park was lovely in its variety of flora and bird life.A great expereince all told.

Lasantha Pethiyagoda
Melbourne, Australia

Title: Beautiful Park-needs making the most of
Text:
Wilpattu is beautiful and bursting with wildlife. We saw 2 bull elephants, mongoose,crocodile, jackals, monitor lizards, eagles, hornbills, peacocks....
The day felt a little spoiled by the lack of information, no visitors centre and a guide who barely spoke to us and was a bit miserable. We spend far too much time hurtling through the jungle at full speed in a jeep-not the best way to see wildlife! We would have loved to sit my one of the lakes or visit a viewing point. Instead there seemed to be a rush to get to a place we could get out and have a packed lunch by a beach.  I wish we hadn't bothered as the long journey was a bit much on the bumpy tracks and the beach was full of litter-very upsetting.
My advice to Wilpattu is to make the most of the beautiful environment, keep it clean, slow down the jeeps and employ guides who speak English and are knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the wildlife. It would then be worth the high price.

Title: A beautiful park re-emerging after the security concerns a few years ago
Text:
I have been to Wilpattu many times, but the most distinct images in my mind are from 2004 , from when I have visited this park a further 3 times. Let me put it briefly, the park is beautiful and it is a miracle that the wild life that currently exists, remains as is, given the poaching and lack of management during the LTTE era.  My most recent visit was in May this year and we stayed at the "Kokmutai" Bungalow within the park. Wildlife did not disappoint, we saw leopard every one of the four days we were there, including bear and elephant. However this bungalow, supposed to be a premium one, dissaponited very much. The location was magic, located by the Modaragam aru river with the peaceful jungle around. The maintenance of the bungalow was however sadly lacking, toliets in very poor condition, no light bulbs in many parts of the place and very limited electricity (solar power) that seem to run out way ahead of the "cut off" time.
I understand the government wants to make these bungalows similar to the game lodges in Africa, great intention, but based on the current condition and price, this vision has a lot more work involved, if it is to become a reality.

Title: Great experience..!!
Text: one of the biggest national park in Sri Lanka. Everything is easy and convenient in there. Friendly guides help us lot. They have wide knowledge about the all places in the park. It cause to see leopards, elephants and monkeys. Had a great experience.. !!!

Title: Dont be in a hurry....
Text: This is real djungle really left as it is, but please take your time and also ask the drivers to take their time as well. The entrance fee could be more reasonable of course as usual for tourists visiting Sri Lanka. But what to do ? Anyway this is attraction not made for a stop just passing on the way. You need time and stay for the night in the neighberhood if possible two nights. After the end of th civil war in Sri Lanka this attraction could finnaly be opened. Good,good !!

Title: great forest safari
Text: after long time this forest open for public i was really happy with this jeep safari ,we so lepards and ,deers,wileboand other animal hope and recomended others as well

Title: A big rip off and a very badly managed park !
Text:
This is a huge park but someone somewhere needs to wake up and sort this place out. The entry fee is high ...and what you see is very little ..There are local groups making a lot of noise inside the park and there is no control. Some were beating drums and singing in vehicles . The half way stop point is ghastly ...broken toilets full of crap ....and litter all over the place ..people urinating everywhere ..and no concern for the environment or animals at all.
The worst is that the jeep drivers and naturalists dont seem to conrol the guests ...we just about saw a leopard only to have it scared away by a howling japanese jeep load ...and the driver or guide said nothing !
The game in this park is very sparse and the dense foliage does not help ....but its the lack of discipline and the facilities which is really annoying 
A terrible experience

Title: I loved it but the government needs to bring the facilities up to international standards...
Text: Yes if is different from safaris in Kenya or South Africa but then we chose to come to Sri Lanka .It was quite a drive from our lodgings but arrived about 7.30am the toilets at the entrance were not very good.the government charge a great deal of money for tourist to visit the national parks and should insure that the facilities are up to international standards .Our spotters were very good and we saw a wide range of animals .we stopped to have our packed breakfast  at one of the picnic areas ,watching an elephant berthing and playing inthe water hole amazing and lots of other animals near the edge .So to use the toilets smelly and the  toilets were actually broken!,we had to go behind a bush!,we saw a herd of wild boar and babies running from a water hole ,lots of spotted deer .We had lunch down by a river but no toilets nearby.As were leaving the park we finally saw a leopard our spotters had been so determined to find them for us.

Title: one of the best
Text:
If you want to see many different type of animals its ideal.
Lots of elephants and we were lucky to see few leopards too.

Title: Disappointed
Text: We booked to go on this safari as we were told we would see a Hurd of elephants a gorilla and crocodiles but we might only get to see the leopards.  We left the hotel close to Colombo at 4.30 in the morning so as to get there by 7.30 to see the animals at the water.  On entering the park we saw an owl and. Lizard some birds in a swamp and three deer that ran across the road. Then we drove round for another three hours and then spotted 1 leopard in the bushes.  When we left we went to use the toilets and what a mess they were just a hole in th floor with  beetles flies and other things in the cubicle with you.  For a cost of 70.00 per person I think this should be better.  Save your money you see more wildlife on the road monkeys jumping from tree to tree fruit bats and about 30 parrots flying, cows walking the road and even saw a working elephant, when we asked the guide where they had gone he said they had not had water for months but he ddnt know where all the animals had gone.  Small shop on site but not much and with the toilets being in th state they were didn't fancy anything.

Title: Wilpattu rip-off !!!
Text:
A very mediocre experience for a lot of money !!  We paid nearly £40.00 to get in to the park and then, when we returned from the drive, had a demand from the 4WD driver for another £45.00 which we were not expecting.  After all, once you've paid your entry fee what are you supposed to do - walk !!  They even charged us to park our car.   We ended up paying a total of £60.00 to see deer, buffallo and two elephants plus birds and lizzards that you can see from the side of any road.  The jeep was dirty and uncomfortable.  The terrain is attractive but makes it hard to see anything that might be lurking.

If you want to see wildlife, go to Africa - forget Sri Lanka.  If you do go, be very sure what you're in for.  The locals pay a pittance by comparison and the fat chief warden took great pleaure in pointing that out to us.  You expect to get ripped off in Sri Lanka but you don't expect it to be Goverment sponsored (allegedly) !

Title: Beautiful but a little over crowded
Text: Baker falls is an amazing natural site, but it is a little over shadowed by the entry price and it being over crowded.

Title: Beautiful Baker Falls
Text: Baker falls come midway enroute to world's end. The falls is full all round the year which looks very scenic. One cannot go near the falls or take a dip in the water for safety reasons.

Title: Wonderful bit of nature
Text: This is in a national park and on a circular trail. It is an awe-inspiring waterfall and you can get closer to it if you are careful and brave enough to go down the slope.

Title: Worth the detour
Text: This waterfall is worth the detour to see it. There is a small platform to take pictures. Take care of your camera, the place is very humid and the fall produces a lot of mist.

Title: Pretty waterfall
Text:
The water falls are down several steep steps but are worth the walk down to them. Take your time walking back up and it's not too difficult. 
The falls have two levels of platform near them for taking good photos

Title: Beautiful Waterfall
Text:
You will get this waterfall along the Horton plains trail walk. It will be first stop if you decide the start the trail anti clockwise. In my case it was the last stop as we had started the trail clockwise. 
You have to take a small detour to reach the falls and I was surprised to read some reviews which claim this path to be difficult. There are a few steep steps, but for an average person it would take hardly 5 minutes to get down.
Near the falls you have an option of sitting down in the shade for a while and if you are adventurous enough you could get close to the water and splash around for a while.
If you are doing the Horton plains trail, you should definitely not miss this waterfall.

Title: Lovely falls
Text: These falls are very picturesque but there is quite a climb down steps to them.  Definitely not suitable for those with mobility problems.

Title: Amazing & Lovely Place to Relax, Eat, Get Wet !! 1st Stop of the Trek !!
Text:
This will be your 1st stop in the Horton Plains, if you are going anti clockwise (advisable : read my Horton Plains Review !!) 
Scenic waterfalls named after some Britisher Mr Baker who discovered it.. Do not just see this fall from a distant, but go close to it & the stream below to enjoy the most of it.. if you are hungry by the time you reach here, you can find some space for yourself in the the shade nearby & open the Breakfast which your Hotel would have given you.. the falls wasn't dry & was full of water even in the March, i believe it to be Summers for Sri Lanka.. You could just take few selfies, sit peacefully & hear the sound of Water falling.. & enjoy Nature at it's Best !!

Title: Time to relax and eat
Text:
We had a breakfast pack from the hotel.  As we walked the circuit clockwise this was about 2/3rds the way.  Time to sit and relax.  
Unfortunately the stale sandwich from Heritance tea factory was only worth a bite.  Then packed to be taken out of park.  So we had some nice fresh fruit and relaxed at falls.

Title: Amazing and peaceful
Text: It is in the middle of the 9km hike. The signs are very clear there to the waterfall and it is safe and amazing. Take your time in smelling the fresh air and let the breeze of this waterfall touch your face by getting to the lower level which is close to the waterfall

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text:
Lovely waterfall in the Horton Plains National Park.

Walk through the park, along a very easy to follow trail. The train is rocky and muddy is some places, so dress accordingly. 

The fall is off the main path, but easily found, so follow the steps down, and onto the viewing platform. Here you can feel the spray from the waterfall. Apparently there are lots of lizards in this area, but we didn't see any!

Title: Sucker for waterfalls!
Text: I can't resist a waterfalls, so was happy to make the 100 meters spur off the World's End loop trail to reach Baker's Falls, and about 3 kms from the start trek's starting point, going to the right from the fork of the trek. The falls is beautiful, albeit not spectacular. One of the three main attractions on the World's End track, along with World's End and Mini World's End viewpoints.

Title: On the Worlds End Hike
Text: It's worth swinging by Baker's Falls on the World's End hike It's a small waterfall in a beautiful setting.

Title: Beautiful 20 metre falls, surrounded by flowers and with a perma- rainbow
Text: This was for me easily the highlight of the 9km circuit walk. Accessed via about 100 steps from the path, it is serenely beautiful, with multiple cascades, surrounded by rhodendron and other flora, and a permanent rainbow. Camera's at the ready, and enjoy the beauty of nature.

Title: Water fall in the middle of the hortain planes nature trail
Text: You get to see this wide beautiful waterfall when doing the 10 kms long hortan planes nature trail. Don't be discouraged and stop your walk half way through but take your time and finish the walk where you get to see both world's end as well as this nice waterfall

Title: Part of the Horton Plains hike
Text: Part of the trek in Horton plains and possibly the most difficult to access, but doable.  Would recommend hiking shoes or sneakers.

Title: Favorite spot in Horton Plains National Park
Text: This was my favorite spot along the 10km loop at Horton Plains, although the entree fee is ridiculously overpriced.  While it's no Niagara or Iguazu, it's a good spot to take a break on the hike.

Title: Impressive waterfall
Text: You get this waterfall for free on the same trail as Worlds End. It is an impressive and large waterfall, with a platform that allows you to get right up close to the water. The steps down are quite steep, so take care with your step.

Title: Lovely and breezy small waterfall
Text: Located inside the horton plains national park , it has the most amazing breeze . When you go close to the waterfall tiny drops of water splashes over the body, baker's fall is a wonderful little piece of nature.

Title: Great view
Text: A decent waterfall to have a look. Its on the hortons trek. The place is great to take some good pics. The trek to the waterfalls is certainly worth.

Title: Thumb's down
Text:
Just a falls.  Not that impressive for a tourist visit.
I Would definitely not recommend this to a friend.
Waste of time

Title: Beautiful Falls
Text: Baker's Falls is located inside the Horton Plains National Park. Visited the falls while coming back from the World's End. Indeed a very beautiful falls. Getting down to the view point is a bit difficult.

Title: Nice
Text: Bakers falls is along the hike at Horton's plains national park. Steep climb off the trail to get here. Not a very big waterfall, but a nice place to stop when doing the trek.

Title: Splendid!
Text: It is on the way to the 'world's end'. Nature in in full boom. Lovely falls! You can sit there and take pictures,a nd enjoy the beauty of these falls

Title: Breathtaking view and moderate hike
Text:
You can reach Horton's plain by car or tuktuk. The whole route to hortons plain is  very scenic. We stopped at few places to take pictures.

There is a little cafeteria at the entry of hortons plain. We bought a packet of  jumbo salted peanuts and  ginger snaps from there to enjoy during the hike. 

We started our hike around 12.30 in the afternoon. Weather was pleasant with smattering of sunshine and chilly wind. Please do wear your trainers as the terrain is rocky and do carry a windsheater to save you from the chilly wind. 

There are three places to see - Bakers waterfall which is the shortest hike, then mini world's end and the farthest is world's end. We went upto Baker's fall and it took us 1.5 hours going and coming  back. 

The view is breathtaking! You are surrounded by nature all around you!! It feels like you are in europe. There are mountains all around covered with trees, a small waterfall leading to a pond. 

Bakers falls is really beautiful. There is an observation deck where you can sit for a little time before starting back. 

on reading some reviews i thought the hike would be difficult. But my hubby who has knee problem could do this hike easily. I think the cool weather and so much of beauty all around you keeps you mesmerised.

On our way back we stopped at cafeteria for a hot cup of tea and some biscuits.

Whenever you are in nuwara eliya it is a must do. I would love to do the whole hike upto world's end if i visit this place again.

Title: Must see, must do
Text: Must, must do! Just must do. The Baker's fall are a part of The Horton Plains National park which is one of the most beautiful locations in Sri Lanka. It is a 9km circle which has three stops along the way  Mini Worlds End, Worlds End and Bakers Fall. The trail is easy (will short patches of incline along the way which are easy to climb) and breathtakingly beautiful. Finish it off with a cup of tea and biscuits at the canteen overlooking the plains. On more practical information, the entrance to the plains is an hours drive from Nuwara Elliya (approximately) and the tickets are slightly expensive (but worth every penny). Take the route on the left (which reaches bakers fall last) since its a better way to circle the plains. Also, if you get tired halfway and feel the urge to turn back  dont, because even if you turn back youll have the same distance to cover and youll miss the trail on the other side.

Title: Small Waterfalls at Horton Plains
Text: We visited as part of our walk in the park. There is a steep but not to arduous path down to them. Perhaps, as it was out of the rainy season, the true spectacle was not evident. I however found them average and not a patch on others I have seen in the world. That said they are worth a detour on the walk.

Title: Small but beautiful
Text: This Fall is comparatively smaller but it has its own charm and uniqueness. It's beautiful and the water flow is strong. Though you can't spend a lot of time admiring it as other hikers are waiting for their turn to appreciate this natural beauty. Photos don't do justice to this beauty.

Title: Just ok
Text: Its an OK attraction. Waterfall is quite small and when we went the platform was quite crowded. Would go to HP for the trekking not so much to see this

Title: WOW
Text: Important place to visit in Horton Plains National park. most people are visit on this last of the walk. but we saw this first. that side the best.

Title: Great way to start the Horton Plains hike (if you turn right at the start)
Text: While the falls are a short hike off the trail down some rather steep steps, they are certainly worth the walk. I was there in dry season and the falls were still impressive!

Title: splash of water after a long trek
Text: it was so refreshing to see bakers fall after the long world's end trek.  though the water was too cold to take a dip, sitting besides it was equally soothing

Title: Pretty falls
Text: A lovely part of the Horton Plains experience, we enjoyed admiring the falls though watching some of the other tourists climb up and slide down gave us some anxiety. A good spot for to drink some water and relax before the last slog to the park gates.

Title: Picturesque falls
Text:
The Bakers Falls are part of a series of sights within Horton Plains. 

See my review of Horton Plains which includes hints/tips on visiting this beautiful natural sight. 

Must-see as part of a visit to Sri Lanka!

Title: Impressive
Text: My partner and I visited the falls whilst touring the country. This is a beautiful area and great if you enjoy walking. Wear comfortable walking shoes and set off early to avoid crowds. There are some good photos to take. There are toilets and free parking.

Title: Decent falls
Text: We visited in a fairly dry period and the falls were not very dramatic.  However it is evident that in wetter periods a lot more water would be falling, enhancing the drama

Title: Spectacular and beautiful reward
Text:
Located in Horton's Plains National Park as part of the 9.5km trek that also takes in World's End, Baker's falls offers a contrast in scenery after walking across the drier plains section, where we spotted some sambal deer and lovely mountain scenery. 

You hear the waterfalls before you see them. To view Baker's Falls requires descending about 50 steep steps to reach the first of several viewing areas. On a hot humid day the spray from the falls is refreshing.

Title: Wonderful Waterfall
Text: The loop around Hortons Plains National Park brings you to Bakers Falls which you hear before you see. Its a stunner with a good viewing platform. My advice is don't try and go back to the car park from here double back as its a killer otherwise!!

Title: Nice, small waterfalls, not much of a tourist atttraction....
Text: The waterfalls are part of the Horton Plains National Park, they are nice and small but, nothing special, not a tourist attraction in or view...

Title: Waterfall
Text: It was such a relaxing place to sit after 1 hour of walking.. the waterfall really changes your mood to a better one .. really loved it

Title: Like hundreds of waterfalls in SL, nothing special
Text: OK, it is nice, you get to stand on the viewing platform near the falls. But you also need to trek hours and pay lots of dollars to see what is essentially a waterfall that is no different to many others in the region that you can see and swim around for free. DO the trek for the World End's view if you must, but the Baker's falls is not special enough to do the trek.

Title: Small but beautiful waterfall in Horton Plains National Park
Text: This small and placid waterfall is only 20 metres in height and was discovered, and named after, Sir Samuel Baker, who was a British big game hunter and explorer. It is located in Horton Plains National Park, a montane and cloud forest region which is unique in Sri Lanka. Sadly, Sir Samuel Baker was one of the British colonialists that was responsible for exterminating the elephants that inhabited this region in Sri Lanka and who were apparently different from the other elephants residing in the island.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Probably the best so called activity that you can do in Hortons National Park, but still doesnt worth the entrance fee. You can see soo many beautiful waterfalls for free, people are just lazy searching for them.

Title: Bakers Falls
Text: Very pretty and refreshing after the long walk there. It always amazes me what you find at such hight's. You are unable to swim there so enjoy the spray from the falls instead.

Title: Nice but not worth it
Text: Beautiful and spectacular but really not worth the effort. In order to see this you had to pay 3,500rupees plus hike non stop over 12km in rough terrain. Definitely give this a miss.

Title: Beautyful
Text: This is a beautiful waterfall. It is a bit of steep down hill to get close to it but worth going there.

Title: We skipped it due to too many tourists
Text: There was an incredible number of other tourists the day we visited, so we didn't even bother to try to see the falls -- we walked on by.

Title: Rush of Waters
Text: Nice falls, though not as large.Do make that stop to see it. It is towards the middle of the 9 km loop.

Title: Worth a short stop at Horton Plains NP
Text:
It's a five minute walk from the round trip at Horton Plains NP to the Baker's Falls. They are not as impressive as we expected but still worth a short stop. 
There are two further ways down (off the main path) where you can get directly to the river and offers a better view of the falls.

Title: Fresh and calming checkpoint
Text: Through the sunny days was this place more calming when you can breath fresh waterfall air. You can see local people in the water and you can also try it if you have enough of courage.

Title: Just a checkpoint
Text:
If you are on the trail, you will come across with Baker's Falls.
Nothing specifically interesting, just a checkpoint for trekking.

Title: Delightful, soothing experience
Text: I've seen many waterfalls & this wasn't magnificent in any way....but ther was a thoughtfully provide bench where we could sit up close to the water fall, eat a snack after a long walk, enjoy the sound of the rushing water, watch as the water flowed through various crevices it had created for itself....

Title: nice waterfall
Text: You will see Baker's Fall while hiking the 9km Loop Trail at Horton Plain's Nat'l Park. The falls were nice with our good clear weather but not exceptional. Only recommended if you have the time and fancy waking up at 5am.

Title: Belle cascade / Nice waterfalls
Text:
Il est fort probable qu'en cette fin de parcours du Parc National de Horton Plains, vous serez fatigués. Toutefois, ne ratez pas ces chutes d'eau, elles valent le détour.

It is likely that at the end of your walk in the Horton Plains National Park, you will be tired. However, do not miss these waterfalls, they are worth seeing.

Title: Gem in Horton Plains
Text: This is inside Horton Plains National park and can be visited by following the circular trail. It is few hundred meters downhill climb from the main trail.

Title: Nice!
Text: Falls are nice to visit and walk (a good three hours to do the loop) goes through many different types of environments - all different and beautiful in their own way.   Wear good walking shoes:)

Title: Srilanka-Maldives Tour!
Text: Good Place to visit in Horton Plains Park. You should reach park early in the morning to catch full beauty of the park. You can get good photos but can't get shower at fall....

Title: Bakers Falls
Text: Whilst walking through Horton Plains you'll come across this smart water fall, so make sure you have your camera with you, as its worth a snap or two, and if your an artist, this will certainly wet your appetite...Pardon the Pun.!!....Enjoy.!!

Title: A nice waterfall during the hike in Horton's plain
Text: the fact you can get really close and on the rocks just below the waterfall make it you can really just relax it there's not too many people. Doing the hike quite early in the day really helps.

Title: Very beautiful waterfall i have seen in my life.
Text: Very beautiful waterfall i have seen in my life. Surrounding nature is very scenic! Very clean pathway!

Title: Beautiful Waterfall in a Lovely Walking / Hiking Area
Text: Bakers Falls is half hour or so from the visitors centre on Horton Plains, the walk around which is simply lovely; it was close to being the highlight of our Sri Lanka vacation, in fact. The Falls themselves have a two-tier viewing platform, and on the day we were there, in full flow. Attractive rather than spectacular, the spot is definitely worth a visit

Title: Very close view
Text: Baker's falls is a moderate sized waterfall with several streams. The viewpoint is very close in front of the waterfall, so one can see everything in every detail. From the viewpoint, one can climb down the stones almost into the waterfall itself.

Title: It was nice
Text: the fall is not extra ordinary. since there are much more nicer waterfalls in sri lanka. but when you consider the whole journey around Horton plains it really add values to the walk.

Title: Nice stop after World's End
Text: A nice and relaxing stop after World's End. The steps are manageable. Take a break before you continue your journey.

Title: Worth the walk
Text: You reach there after a long walk in Horton Plains, very relaxing place with the sound of the fall gashing down,  before continue your walk to world end.. enjoy

Title: A nice waterfall
Text: During your trip in the park you reach this waterfall. It is a nice waterfall and a perfect place to take a little rest. If you walk the whole tour it takes about 5 hours of walking.

Title: Nice waterfall
Text: A very nice waterfall at the Horton Plains National Park. You will find it when you do the complete walk of around 8-9 kilometers.

Title: Picturesque
Text: Great waterfall, a peacful place where you can only hear the sound of water. Managed to take great pictures here.

Title: A waterfall is a waterfall is a waterfall!
Text:
Waterfalls are waterfalls. No matter what the height is, or what the width is... waterfalls make you freshen up in a moment and bring back that energy the Sun sapped away!

Part of the Horton Plains 9+km trail, I went to the Baker's Falls towards the end. An easy climb down and a challenging climb up, its all worth it. 

For the more adventurous, do what I did - hop down through the back onto the rocks and touch the ice cold waters! :)

Title: Nice to see, but there are better in Sri Lanka.
Text: A nice waterfall, and part of the Horton Plains circuit walk. Good viewing platform. It can be rather slippery getting to the falls as you walk through forest, so wear good shoes.

Title: Nice part of Horton Plains visit
Text: The waterfalls are very nice...the climb down to see them requires a somewhat challenging climb up to return to the trail!

Title: Pretty waterfall
Text: Along the World's End Trail. Nice stop, nice photo op. But waterfalls are waterfalls. This isn't Vic Falls or Angel Falls.

Title: Beautiful Falls
Text:
The falls are worth visiting along the Trek in the Horton National Park 
But they clerly need to make a better access as the stairs leading down to the falls are so big even for a tall person like me 
specially when they charge you so much for the entrace fees

Title: Small falls
Text: This a not a big fall, but a nice break during your Horton Plains hike to admire the water and perhaps fuel up if you have not had the chance to do so before you continue the rest of the way. Keep your hands free to help you grip the branches as you climb up and down to get to the falls. Skip this part if it is raining and slippery. Don't attempt this carrying your child.

Title: Diyaluma falls - A must experience
Text: Ultimately good. We hiked through the forest and reached the upper and lower Diyaluma falls. There is a natural pool. When we went the water was more. Our guide helped us to find a safe place to have a bath. He took us with passion and patience . His name is Upendra. He speaks and understand English. We parked our car near the village . From there along with tuktuk to go up and down until the hiking point. He also came with us until the falls. He can be contacted at 0775474725. Our driver got a good deal by talking with him for both tuktuk and being a guide. After bath we changed our wet clothes in his house. Friendly people. I have included his photo with his shop. The falls and the forest just got imprinted into our heart. Beautiful road to the falls and extraordinary hike upto the top of the falls. A must do. But people should restrain from polluting the place with plastics.

Title: Do it !
Text: It is an amazing place to visit. A not to hard climb to the top but when you get there, the view and the waterfall are amazing.

Title: A wonderful time - just jump in!
Text:
This was one of our favourite days in Sri Lanka. Definitely worth a visit.

As others say below, you can go with or without a guide. We had a guide from Ella whose company we really enjoyed, so we went up with him  but you could definitely find your way without a guide if you wanted to, maybe with a wrong turn or two along the way.

We took the short 20-minute walk rather than the 2-hour hike, and didnt regret it.

The bottom pool is the busiest with tourists  but we found it was only really worth a short stay. The views are beautiful, and this is where everyone gets their photos  but thats pretty much it.

The second pool, a very short walk away, is good for a swim, and the view of the falls above you is pretty special. 

The third pool, directly above the second, and a short 2-3 minute hike up, features an 8m cliff jump. We did it and were perfectly safe  but I wouldnt do it without being shown by a local guide. There are plenty around the first pool who can show you. We did it a couple of times  every time, my feet hit the bottom of the pool at the end of the jump, but not hard enough to be of any concern  just a surprise first time around!

We then had a lovely time at the top of the third pool, sitting in the sun and relaxing. Well worth a trip.

Title: Don't get scammed 2000 rupees to get to tbe waterfall!
Text:
If you don't want to get scammed 2000 rupee for a 20 min walk to the waterfall then check the location in the attached photos. This place gives free parking (the rest charge) and they have steps that go straight up to the waterfall. Just follow up, wqlk along with barbed wire on right, through a small bit of woods (wear shoes or sandles). You can hear the waterfall on right and you will probably see guides walking with paying tourists along the way... once at the waterfall go left (many ways to plunge pools further up. Please up vote this so other tourists can decide to pay or not pay.

(The place on the photos also has rooms, food, snacks, cold water etc - they are very nice family).

Title: Natural swimming pools on the top of the waterfall! Amazing scenery. It is worth the hike! :)
Text:
We stopped by the waterfall and it looks stunning from the bottom. But even better was to go up with one of the local guides - they drove us by tuk tuk and then brought us to the top of the waterfall (15 minutes walking). We could swim there in lovely natural pools right above the fall! :)) It was such fun! We took many pictures, then he took us to another swimming area and showed us where is it safe to jump into the water (we didn't, it was like 8 meters jump! :D). The only thing you need to be careful of is the water quality (not pure) - you might get ear aching if you dive - clean your ears afterwards. 
The contact for our guide: Mr. Sudu, 070185255 - he speaks good English. ;)

Title: Worth the trip!!
Text:
We rented a scooter in Ella and took the 1 hour ride (1:20 to the top) to visit the magnificent waterfall. On the food of it you can take a climb to bath in the pools below the fall. After it you can take another 20 minutes on bad roads to the top. Place your scooter there (100 rupies) and walk over (40 minutes) to the pools to chill. Definitely recommended. It is a day trip.

On the food of the waterfall you can buy water. Bring your food :)

Title: Great for a swim and photo shoot
Text: Normally we like to go things alone but I suggest getting a guide who can take you to the places to swim (and jump if you desire!) and for good photo shoots.

Title: Well worth it
Text: Stunning waterfall!!  We hired a scooter from Ella and ventured here. At the base guides will try and offer services to the top. This is easily achievable without their services if you are adventurous. They said a scooter will not make it to where the climb starts, we made it with ease. The trek is somewhat difficult depending on fitness. Would allow minimum 3 hours round trip. But more would be preferable. We spent 4 or so up and down

Title: Wow.....
Text:
We took tuk tuk from haputale 3500lkr
Driver waited on us, however we came back down same way as went up, he was apparently waiting on other side... So make sure you clear this up.. 
Good 20min walk up to top of falls well worth it what a view.

You won't need a guide path is pretty obvious..

Neraby Town is quaint stop for a nosey around locals are friendly

Title: Absolutely Stunning
Text:
We drove to the bottom of the waterfall by car, its beautiful to see. Lots of people just stop there ....... not us! 

We then took a tuk tuk as far as possible as the road becomes non-drivable. The tuk tuk driver became our walking guide to the top of the fall and to another hidden waterfall you cannot see from the road. 

The hike is approx 30-40 minutes with varied difficulty. Honestly do it!!

Wow wow wow it is just simply stunning. 

There were no tourists up there, when we went, only local kids and us swimming and playing in the falls. One of my favourite experiences of Sri Lanka and travelling the world. So so lucky to have such an experience

Title: Recommended Tuk Tuk driver
Text: Amazing view and experience ! Would highly recommend to take a Tuk-Tim WITH GUIDE to reach the top of the waterfalls. Several tuk tuk drivers are trying to sell you their service but we would definitely recommend to go to the small and lonely family shop which is on the left handside when looking at the waterfall . Their son, Tharindu (0719702456) is such a lovely person . He took us to the waterfall and took great pictures . So nice and genuine person!

Title: Just wow
Text: It is worth the trek to get here both walking the and tuk tuk here. We ended up spending 3 hours here enjoying the rock pools and waterfalls. You must come here

Title: A B S O L U T E  M U S T  I N  E L L A !
Text:
Wow. Could not recommend going to Diyaluma Falls more. It was an absolute highlight for not just our trip to Ella, but Sri Lanka as a whole. Such a beautiful waterfall, amazing views, you can swim (definitely recommend as its a lot of fun!) and the hike isnt too hard to get there. 

The only thing is, you do need a guide to walk you to the spots to go. When you arrive by tuk tuk, there will be guides there that will offer their service, at first you dont think you need them but Im telling you... you definitely do. So many turns and theres no clear path in the slightest, and they take heaps of photos for you ! We went with a guy named Dennis (071 988 1825 if anyone wants to get in contact with him) and he said we decide on a price at the end depending on how happy we were with his service. We ended up paying 2,000 rupee for 3 of us which I think is very reasonable. 

Also, a tuk tuk from Ella to the falls was 4,000 rupee, they all say 6,000 only but you can definitely find someone who will do it for 4,000 just takes a bit of bartering and searching !

Title: Instructions on how to reach falls. "GUIDES NOT NEEDED!!"
Text:
Stunning multiple waterfalls and a great place to swim. 

"Guides" are not needed !! 

After thoroughly researching the falls we were confident on how to get to them with clear instructions saved on our phones. after parking our Tuk tuk at the top carpark we were asked multiple times if we would like a guide. After saying no and following our saved directions we set off to find our path only to be followed by one of the "guides" from the carpark. 

We were told we were going the wrong way and he directed us down some path in which he said was the right way. We trusted this advice as we thought he was being genuinely helpful. This path was overgrown and full of leeches (have a bottle of insect repellent and lighter ready to spray/burn them off as soon as you feel them) after eventually reaching and exploring the waterfalls we found a much much better path back. we popped out (surprise, surprise) where we were originally headed before being led astray by the guides advice. 

After returning to our Tuk Tuk and confronting the guide we asked him if the path we were going to follow was were the guides go and he laughed in our face and said yes. We expressed our disappointment at his actions and said in Australia or New zealand we would never do this to tourists or deliberately lead them astray simply because they chose to make their own way. 

Below are clear instructions how to get the falls without utilising the guides who take advantage of tourists and deliberately confuse them or make up that google maps wont work or that its extremely difficult to find the falls, both of which turned out to be lies. 

Follow this reviews instructions - however after walking past the green and white gate walk for about 50m then take a sharp right onto a wide path. From there traverse around the hillside towards the sound of rushing water and you'll find the various waterfalls.

Title: One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Sri Lanka
Text:
There are two ways to see this beautiful waterfall: 
from below - you need to overcome big high stones (of you need to wear snickers, better to have snickers for tracking), and then youll enjoy a very cool view of the waterfall from the earth, its very high and athmospheric, the sun and drops when you are inside the waterfall are amazing!
And the second way - upper view, and its absolutely unbelievable , because upstairs you have a possibility to visit all small and so small ponds connected with each other! And you can also swim inside them and enjoy a very amazing Mountain View from the very high spots.
Its one of the most beautiful waterfalls weve ever seen at the moment.
Less people. And very cool route, cause you need to go through the jungle.
Absolutely must visit. Much better and more beautiful than Rawana waterfall.

Title: Beautiful Waterfall
Text: What a remarkable place in Sri Lanka. Its just wow. Stunning waterfall. You will find a very relaxing surrounding area there as well. No words to tell about this destination and this beautiful, natural waterfall. Sri Lankans are surely one of those lucky people on Earth.

Title: Great day from Ella to Diyaluma Falls with guide!!
Text:
We are a family of 4 (2 kids age 10/13) and spent the day around the falls. We took a bus from Ella to Wellawaya (45 min, 300 rs). From there, our guide for the day (Tharindu, +94 719702456) picked us up by tuktuk. Of you have a car, you could also come straight to the falls on your own. Tharindu lives at the base of the falls.
We first spent half and hour climbing and playing on the boulders at the bottom of the falls/river.
Then Tharindu brought us with the tuktuk halfway up the mountain, from where we hiked 30 min to the falls. We recommend bringing a guide, because it saves you a lot of walking and you wont get lost (which is easy). When we got to the top of the falls, it was a bit crowded with locals because of the weekend. We hiked 10 min further up to Upper Diyaluma falls, which where even nicer! There, we swam in the pools and climbed up to the top, from where our kids jumped off from a 8 meter rock in the pool! Awesome!
Tharindu was really nice and helpful and encouraged the kids with the swimming and jumping. He also makes really nice pictures (and loves the panorama setting!). 
We had a great day all together. Dont hesitate to give Tharindu a call.

Title: Spectacular waterfall
Text: Waterfall of about 100 meters high. It's possible to go in the pool, buy only if the water level is not too high.

Title: Absolutely stunning
Text: Amazing and dreamy waterfall with a slippery hill. Worth to bring good shoes and clothes but great for a jump in the waterfall and the natural slide. A lot of locals offering tours. Very nice people but not necessarily needed.

Title: Good views from the road
Text: Impressive waterfall, with a good view from the roadside bridge. There is a walk you can do to the top of it, but it looks like hot work so we didn't bother. About a 20 minute detour off of the main road up to Ella, which we thought was worth it.

Title: magnificent views, hike and experience
Text:
My husband and I hiked the Diyaluma Falls, we hired a guide with a tuktuk, we ride the tuktuk for like 7 minutes, then we contined by foot. 
the views from the top are great, we enjoyed the pools so much. 
make sure you wear the right shoes for this hike, as it is not an easy one. 
our great guide was with us the whole time, his name is Tharindu Mihiranga, his phone number: +94719702456.

Title: Definetly worth it
Text:
Definetly worth the hike and worth the adrenaline rush when you swim in the pools up top! Don't forget to take the diyaluma short cut trail as it makes the access to the top much easier ! 

If you can go early in the morning that would be great as it gets busier as the day passes

Title: Many pools to soak at
Text:
We got a guide, but you don't absolutely need one. We didn't regret having a guide because we are quite weak, and at least the guide could.help us at some part. 

Once you reach the top, there's many "pools". There's quite some people, but it's not overly crowded. If the big "pool" is crowded, just head to behind and there are small pool with small falls. Stand under the fall and let it wash away all your tiredness. 

It's about 1 hr past drive from ella town, but I highly recommend it. As compared to ravana falls (we went past twice), diyaluma looks alot better!

Title: Best thing in sri lanka
Text: We've spent almost 3 weeks in sri lankan and this was by far the best thing. We got a tuk tuk from Ella for 5000 rupee for 3 people. The guy also guided us on foot to the actual falls (you won't find them on your own). It is amazing. The waterfall isnt touristy at all so the path is overgrown so you'll  need to watch out for leeches and ticks. Despite this it's so worth it. Don't forget your swimmers as there is lots of jumping and swimming to be had. Enjoy!

Title: Stunning views from above and below!
Text:
Diyaluma Falls is the second highest waterfall in Sri Lanka at 720ft high. Located about 6km from Koslanda in the Badulla District, and 38km from Ella, this horsetail waterfall has multiple falls and natural pools for you to dive into, refresh yourself and explore. Diyaluma Falls can be explored from both above
and below, as the base of the falls also has a pool you can dive into! The best time to visit would be for sunrise as you get to see the rising sun shine upon the waves crashing down, however, sunset isnt a bad
option either, just be weary that you may need to travel back towards the main road in total darkness.

Title: Wow
Text: It was fascinating waterfall. We had a hard time to go up , i had an injury on the way. But the view the spot was amazing. One of the most beautiful place in my life i see. But coz alot of things happen to us we perefer to come down as soon as we can. My friend fell into the lake , i sliped on the rocks. We didnt take any first aid with ourself. If i go back before i go to this place i really pack some first aid with my self and then go to this beautiful place.

Title: Stunning view, great hike !!
Text: Thia waterfall is amazing ! First, the hike to the uppermost level of the waterfall takes you through breathtaking scenery. Mind that you have to do proper research online so you find out the right way for the beautiful hike. The starting point is a fee hundred meters South from Diyaluma Falls Inn. The local tuk tuk drivers will try to sell you tours, no need to get one. Once you get to the top of the waterfall, you start to descend, following the flow of water and you go through several stages of the waterfall, each with beautiful little pools where you can take baths. The lowest level is actually the top of the waterfall that you see from the main road. From there, you descend on a dirt path and reach a point close to Naulla village. So, the start and end points are different. This is the best way to go, in my opinion. You will enjoy amazing views and a good workout ;)

Title: Nice view
Text: There is quite a bumpy road to get to these falls on the A4. They were worth it though even though there is not much water coming down. We didnt try to get to the top of the falls but our driver said it was possible.

Title: Stunning
Text: We didnt go up top which we really should have but we still really enjoyed the view from below. You can climb to the base and actually swim in the water fall while letting the water fall on you. Really beautiful place but really far from everything.

Title: Tough climb to beautiful waterfall
Text:
I gave it 4 stars because of the tough climb to get to the top. Otherwise, it is indeed a multi-level beautiful waterfall with a number of pools to sit or have fun in.
We rode a motorbike from Ella, took about 1-1.5hrs. Fairly good roads  except for the last 15min stretch which were bumpier. At the base of the waterfall (some distance away from the actual waterfall), there is a small parking area and an inn. 
There are a few local boys/ young men waiting and will offer their service as a guide. We could have bargained to 1500lkr but paid the 2000lkr asked, after hearing from other travellers at our guesthouse how they topped up 500lkr in the end after experiencing the amount of walking and the guide waiting to bring them down at the end.
The walk up starts with a fairly straightforward dirt path through rubber trees and a small cluster of houses. However, the rest of it is a climb up the mountain, on uneven, scrabbly rocks, large and small, and cut-in steps in the ground. You should be young or of moderate fitness to do this. Definitely wear proper shoes and have sunscreen and water. Preferably start early in the day and wear longer pants, as the tall grass growing towards the path for much of the climb can get itchy after a while. You will also appreciate the helping hand of the guide as you climb..
At the top there is a coconut seller, then slightly downhill to the actual waterfall. 
It is fairly easy to get to the various levels of the waterfall. Be careful stepping in and out of the pools as the rocks are slippery with moss.  
There is only a roti and coconut seller at the waterfall itself. Bring some snacks or you can buy them from the few village grocery shops on the road in. Very friendly locals, we smiled and waved to everyone.
From the bottom of the waterfall, you will need to climb back up again to the top where the coconut seller is, to go all the way down again. It takes about 1hr each way.

Title: Natural heaven
Text:
This place is behind a hike. The hike up the hill tries to kill you but when you get to natures own pools.. It is just worth it. The scenery and atmosphere is something out of this world, so beautiful. There is many pools to hang out in and we definetly recommend to start your cooling down process from the bottom pools and to work your way up the hill.
We were lucky to have our Tuktuk driver as a guide, you should really hire someone to get the most out of this place!!

Title: Wow it's fantastic
Text: This place is really amazing, maybe one of the best place to visit in Sri Lanka, you can go to the top of the fall, swim and have some great picture, it's good to go with a local guide, because you need to walk in jungle for around 2Km, and it's difficult to find the way...

Title: Diyaluma falls
Text: Lower Diyaluma falls can be seen from the roadside - a massive cascade. But the real treasure are upper Diyaluma falls, a 3/4 mile hike up. There are multiple accessible bathing waterfall pools  - each one unique. Most are easy to enter pools but one is for daredevils only -  a 5m deep pool with a 20m high edge to jump from!

Title: Great hike
Text: Beautiful waterfall. You can swim at the top so wear swimming gear. Do this with a guide as youll probably get lost otherwise. We paid 1500 LKR for ours with a group of 3. Dont believe the tuk tuk drovers who threaten you with a 3 hour walk to the top - with moderate fitness you can do it in about an hour going at a comfortable pace. Tuk tuk doesnt get you anywhere near the top and you still have the hardest part of the walk to do so dont waste your money.

Title: May be worth getting a guide
