Text: The waterfalls were lovely and definitely worth a visit however you may want to get a guide. It seems compared to other reviews we went the hard way as ours was about a hour hike or more up rocks with a steep incline. I am quite fit but it was not easy. Definitely doable but will leave you breathless. Also there are leeches in the water so bear this in mind. If you go in the pools with running water you should be ok but check yourself before you leave. This is a whole day trek so I would leave early I wouldn't want to be walking around in the dark. You can catch a bus there first to Wyallaway then another bus to the falls very cheap compared to a tuk tuk.

Title: Breathtaking views and sights
Text: Start ur hike  early morning to avoid traffic on the hiking route and less photo bombing  by others and it's less warm. Takes about 40mins ~ 1hr one way

Title: Worth the long scooter trip
Text: We hired a scooter in Ella and made our way out here during our day. We wished we had been better prepared time wise and been able to go to the top of the falls but it was still awesome from the bottom. We went for a swim under the waterfall and it was a pretty cool experience Id recommend to check it out. Took us about an hour via scooter from Ella.

Title: Great stop during our outing from Ella
Text:
We hired a scooter in Ella and stopped off at Diyaluma Falls on a bit of a round trip in the countryside. 

The road to get there was in good condition and picturesque. 

The Diyaluma Falls are easily seen from the road which makes it easy for pulling over and having a look.

Title: Really good waterfall after rain
Text:
It is a long drive along a terrible road to get to here, which is why you don't get many foreign tourists. I saw coach loads of Sri Lankans, though. Not really worth walking up the track to the foot of the waterfall -- you get a better view from the road, especially about 500m toward Wellawaya.

It is rather puny if there has been no rain, but after a decent rainstorm it is stunning.

Title: Beautiful falls, a bit of a D-tour to get here
Text:
beautiful falls, next to the road. So you don't need to hike there.
It is a bit of a D-tour to get here, as the road to/from the falls is not in good shape. We could only drive like 40 km/h the whole way.
But it is worth it!

Title: Second highest falls in Sri Lanka
Text: We returned here after a year away and the falls were not so spectacular as we have seen on previous occasions, but we were not in the heavy rainy season. At all times of year these falls are impressive being some 220m in height. They are very easily accessible on the highway from Belihul Oya to Wellawaya and one can easily park, enjoy a splash in the water and take advantage of the road-side vendors who sell water, corn, nibbles and so on. As with all falls, the rainy period is by far the best time to see them at their spectacular best.

Title: Take your swimming trunks
Text: A nice waterfall where you can take a dip.  Easy to get to and cool.  Can get quite busy mid morning so get there early.  Not sure how high you can climb, but a couple of hidden gems

Title: Quick stop
Text: This is the second highest waterfall in Sri Lanka at 220 metres but we learnt that it is far more spectacular in the wet season and when you can soaked standing on the road next to the waterfall. Local vendors sell freshly cooked corn on the cob .

Title: A Short Hike to the top of Diyaluma
Text:
So everyone can enjoy the beauty of Diyaluma easily by the Koslanda - Wellawaya road. There is a way to get to the top of Diyaluma with a short and enjoyable hike. You have to travel  bit further towards Poonagala and find the foot path by the makaldeniya bend. On the way to Poonagala also you will find several beautiful rivers. Ask a local they will show you the road. 

Then there is a hike to go to the top of Diyaluma. Go to there around 9-9:30 in the morning because a local warned me that there are elephants around 6-7 in the morning. 

 At the end of the hike, you can get down to the point where the water finally descends the 200m. You can peep over the edge the look down at the main road. Be care full. The pool created by the first cascade is good for bath. The view over the edge is amazing and worth all the steps in the hike. See the pictures.

Title: Worth the drive!
Text: Although we came from the other direction and it took 45 minutes each way, the falls were well worth the trip, even the hold-up on the way back as they were renovating a large bridge!  The falls are 220 metres high and tumble in long silvery plumes against a dark brown rock-face. There are also small refreshment places nearby.  You may do a bit of rock scrambling to get close if you wish, but the best view is from the road bridge. Of all the falls that we saw in Sri Lanka, this was probably the best.

Title: Need the rainy season
Text: The Diyaluma Falls can be seen from afar as you approach them travelling from Wellawaya to Beragala. We have seen these falls on many occasions but strongly advise, if possible, to visit during the wet season when they are spectacular. On this occasion (January) we remained impressed by the incredible height of the falls but the volume of water was very low. There are places to get water, drinks and snacks on the roadside at the foot of the falls. If travelling this road, it is worth stopping to enjoy the incredible power of nature.

Title: Hidden gem
Text:
On the way to Tissamaharama from Ella we took a slight detour (12 Kms, I believe) on a bumpy road and arrived at this gem. Despite it being a dry season and the flow of water anything but incredible, the tall waterfall was a nice sight. There were hardly any tourists. One can easily spend a good 30 minutes over here.
Highly recommended during the wet season.

Title: serene and beautiful, a good respite from backpackers of Ella
Text: after going to Rawana falls and sharing the beauty with 40-50 other backpackers, heading to Ella where we were the only people around was such a treat.  We didn't hike up to the top but jumped into the water where recent rains had the waterfalls coming down heavily.  It takes about 5-10 minutes to trek up the rocks and make sure you bring shoes not flip flops.

Title: Second highest waterfall in Sri Lanka
Text:
The majestic Diyaluma Falls drops 220 metres and is best seen during the rainy season when there is a lot of water flowing. It has been called the "waterfall of smoking water."

It is on the Beragala to Wellawaya road, a short distance from the small town of Koslanda. The road is narrow, potholed and has some mud, so be careful when driving or riding, especially in wet weather.

Title: A must visit waterfall
Text: This is just next to the main road from Beragala to Wellawaya. Can easily reach by public transportation. For adventure seekers, there is a path to climb to the top of the falls.

Title: Nice adventure, but a bit remote
Text:
We visited here on the advice of our guesthouse in Haputale. We hiked up and down Lipton's Seat in the morning and then caught the Wellawaya bus at about 2pm. Bus was mega full (it was a Sunday) and we didn't get a seat. It was hot and bumpy and we were happy to get of the bus after 1hr and a half. 

It was dry season so there wasn't much water, but the falls were impressive nonetheless. We didn't hang around too long at the bottom because it was a bit touristy. Instead we attempted the hike to the top, as described in the Lonely Planet (2012 edition). A young boy from the village volunteered to guide us along the way. To be honest we would have struggled without him, so we gave him 10Rs. ostensibly to buy school supplies. He put us on the right path and we scrambled up for 20min to the top. You should make sure to take plenty of water for the hike, and don't wear flip-flops. 

At the top we hoped to have the pools to ourselves, as we were hot and sweaty and just wanted to jump in the water. Surprisingly there were a few groups of locals (one getting a bit boozy), and some German girls attracting attention in their bikinis. We just took our boots off and cooled our feet off while chatting to the locals (apparently a family of wild elephants come here for a drink most days at around 6:30pm). 

Sadly we didn't go to the top of the actual falls, because we had to get the bus back to Haputale. It looked really cool and would probably make a great photo. 

The REAL HIGHLIGHT for me was in fact the bus ride back up to Haputale. Buses going up come approx. every 30min, and the last one is at 1830. It took us just over an hour to hike up, 20min at the top, and 45min to get back down, so we caught the bus at about 1720. There was plenty of space on the bus, and it was a magical journey through the forested hills overlooking the southern lowlands as the sun sets over the mountains. Keep your eyes peeled for macaques as you drive up!

Give yourself more time than we did if you're using public transport. Alternatively, if you have your own transport, take a torch with you, stay to see the elephants. :)

Title: GREAT WATER FALLS
Text: A beautiful sight to behold. You could actually take a bath at the foot of the falls. Great photography opportunity.

Title: A quick photo stop en route
Text: Beautiful waterfall close to where we stayed - Living Heritage, Koslanda - we stopped to enjoy the scenery and take some photos on our way.

Title: A Waterfall and pesky vendors
Text:
Again a SL attraction that I personally do not find particularly attractive. 

Yes, nice waterfall. But the approach is difficult. No stairs, lots of floating garbage and pesky vendors that try to peddle their stuff. 

I don't buy stuff out of principle, so they tried the coin scam on me. His daughter was collecting coins and only the 2 Euro coin was missing.

Title: Short stop for a photo
Text: Could watch the falling water for ages. Unfortunately waterfalls are next to the road and there is not much place to sit, relax and see time pass by.

Title: Beautiful Falls
Text: They are down a narrow bumpy road,  but worth the trip. We visited them on our way from Horton Plains to Udawalawe. Well worth  a visit.

Title: Sri Lanka's third-highest waterfall
Text: In September when I visited the waterfall, the stream was fairly small.  Probably, at the end of the rain season the falls will  be more spectacular.  It is a short walk from the road, about 200 meters.  The path and steps to the waterfall are in excellent condition. It is not the most impressive waterfall I've  seen, but worth a visit.  So if you are passing by, go and have a look.  Entrance price =150 LKR.

Title: Majestic!
Text:
It's quite the sight to take in .

There is a hidden path on to the left of the waterfall which can be used to get close to the base of the fall.

Tread carefully along this side and you will be rewarded for your attempt.

There is also a way to reach the top of the falls. Speak to the locals and they will tell you the best way to the top.

Enjoy Diyaluma !

Title: Wonderful waterfall
Text: Alongside the road you cross one of the most spectacular waterfalls in Sri Lanka and you can get ou of your car or tuktuk to make the most beautiful photographs

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text: Another lovely waterfall in the hills of Sri Lanka. You can see it from the road and viewing platform. Worth a short break when passing.

Title: Magnificent!
Text: We have gone here a couple of times and each time it is just as magical as first time! Can get a bit busy during peak season so go early and spend an hour there immersing in the beauty.

Title: dont forget your swimmers
Text: amazing hike and views are great at the top- foolishly forgot to bring our stuff for a swim which was a shame as loads of great pools for dip

Title: UPPER DIYELUMA FALLS NO GUIDE
Text:
it's about an easy 30 minute trail path walk from the car park.

directions:

Facing the car park take the road left and follow it bearing right around the corner. After about 5 minutes you will come across and green and white gate (looks like private property drive going downhill). Go through the gate, or if it's locked you can walk around it. a few metres in front is a sign and take the path that leads right. it's a clear footpath the whole way and it leads through a field of long grass, not very steep. follow this trail for about 15/20 minutes and you will hear the waterfall. you will see a hut and follow the path to the right a few hundred metres. you will see the pools and the rest is pretty simple from there! Be careful the big rock you have to walk across is quite steep, some people were sliding down on their bums. 

its totally worth it even just to swim around the upper pools, they are beautiful. some points you can jump off ledges into, they're very deep. the Sri Lankan children are dare devils and very fun to watch. we didn't go down to the actual waterfall because we didn't have time, our taxi driver gave us 2 hours. but could have easily spent half a day here.

Title: Incredible!
Text:
Natural rock pools and waterfalls. 
We first visited the bottom of the falls by tuk tuk, then he drove us another 30 minutes to reach a property at the top. From here we walked about 20-30 minutes with the help of our tuk tuk driver pointing us in the right direction. People will ask to take you on a guided tour, our driver said not to do this because its unsafe and costs a lot of money. The people offering tours are not guides and not have licenses.
You have to pay 100 rupee parking fee at the place you park your tuk tuk or scooter. After the walk we then reached the first rock pool and waterfall where you can bathe and jump down a big waterfall into a plunge pool. You can then ask some locals to direct you to a path that takes you to the edge of where the waterfall drops down 200 or so metres. 
Moderate fitness level recommended.

Title: Beautiful and 2nd highest waterfall in Sri Lanka
Text: It is situated 6-10 km away from Koslanda in Badulla District on Colombo-Badulla highway.The foot of the Diyaluma falls is quite easy to reach within an hour by tuk-tuk, car or motorbike. The last 15 minutes of the drive will be uphill and the road isnt the best from that point. At the foot of the waterfall, pass the bridge and follow the path to the waterfall. Beautiful surrounding. Very risky to bath here during rainy days. Near to waterfall you can have hot plain tea with juggery.

Title: Climb to the top with a guide and swim in the natural pools
Text: Such a beautiful waterfall and its worth climbing to the top so you can play and swim in the natural pools and then walk alongside the falls to the point where it drops. Its really good fun! We found a local kid who was offering to take us and we joined up with another couple of people and it cost us 1,500rupees between us 4- worth it to get the local perspective, walking through rubber tree factories and beautiful scenery. Be prepared for a good 20min hike uphill so wear trainers for better grip. The locals do it in flit flips no issue but us Westerners arent used to this terrain.

Title: Beautiful falls
Text: On our way to Koslanda we saw this beautiful waterfall. It is worth stopping by. The road on the highland of Sri Lanka is beautiful in general.

Title: High waterfall with little water
Text:
In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka.
It took us one hour and a half to drive from Liptons Seat to these waterfalls...
Impressive in heighth, but unfortunately not too much water coming down outside the monsoon season.
We did not have the time to walk to the top to take a swim.

Title: Amazing waterfall!
Text: We stopped in Koslanda and followed a local guide to the top of the waterfall. We swam in a pool (which we had all to ourselves) and continued the climb down. It was beautiful and well worth it.

Title: Nice place to meet people
Text: We stop by, went for a walk and a short dip inn the bottom pool. We ended up talking to people from all over the world.

Title: Cool picture in the wind
Text:
We drove here by motorbike from Ella and it took a us about 1.5 hours with photo breaks etc. There wasnt a lot of water despite visiting in rainy season but because it was so windy, it produced some awesome shapes with the water. 

If you have time and transport, Id deffo recommend a visit as its the 2nd tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka.

Title: Most beautiful waterfall I've ever seen
Text: We went to this waterfall in July 2018. To get to the top of the waterfall, you can go alone or ask a guide to take you there. You can find those guides at the bridge. We had a really awesome guide, called Sudu. You can ask after him when you're there, he's awesome and he will give a lot of extra information on the way to the top. During the hike, there's even a chance that you will spot some elephants when you're in luck. One of the best experiences of my life!

Title: Passing by
Text: It was not in full force when we passed everytime we returned to the Living Heritage hotel.  But still very beautiful.

Title: Beautiful waterfall
Text: We went to the Diyaluma falls to stay at the Inn next to the falls after seeing the beautiful pictures on the website. The views here are absolutely stunning. However after taking a look around the Inn we were so put off even the views werent enough to make us stay at the Diyaluma Falls Inn. The proprietor has to seriously consider  a makeover of the place to have any one stay there. The toilets are dripping and dirty and the rooms are dingy and musty. It was a real pity to see the place as the location is absolutely brilliant.

Title: Pretty waterfall, AWFUL resthouse
Text: Really pretty falls..but seriously dodgy rest house right beside it.

Title: I was surprised
Text: I have heard about this waterfalls, but was under the impression that this was even smaller than Dunhinda. So I was not interested in visiting this before. Last week I went there with my wife, and was surprised seeing the beauty of it. It is reasonable that people saying that this is the most beautiful waterfalls in Sri Lanka; but unfortunately there are no Cameras that could capture the real beauty of it with the wind and the mist with the real feeling when you be there for real. If you do not see any specialty when you just watch its photographs, I would recommend you to visit the place and experience it with your own eyes. I guarantee that you would agree with me then.

Title: A nice waterfall but access to closer to it difficult
Text: This is a nice waterfall in between Koslanda and Wellawaya, by the side of an undulated road. Access to this place is not convenient and not worth unless passing the area on your way to some other place.

Title: Holiday
Text:
Beautifull waterfall, very good distance from Kandy and nice walk.
The view is fantastic en great, nature of Sri Lanka is superb!

Title: Beautiful 170 m high falls
Text: We passed this waterfall at the end of the mansoon period and because of the rain more water thundered down as usual. Because of the height and the wind the water falls everytime in a different direction downwards. Enjoy the few with a nice lunch or just a drink at the closeby Diyaluma Falls Inn

Title: Beautiful waterfall!
Text: We made a detour from Wellawaya in our rental car and were not disappointed. The waterfall is beautiful! It's a quiet place, so you can enjoy a picknick without being bothered by local people or crowds of touristst. On this topic we read other comments of other people who made a walk to the top of the falls. When you have time, try it. The waterfalles are on the edge of the escparment and the views into the lowlands must be great.

Title: Very dramatic falls
Text: The Diyaluma falls are well worth seeing in all seasons but are incredibly powerful and dramatic after seasonal rains. The local environment is very beautiful and it is wonderful to watch the water crashing down on to the rocks with a backcloth of trees and mountains. A bridge at the foot of the falls is a very popular tourist stopping place and there are several places within walking distance to purchase drinks and snacks.

Title: One of the best wonders of mother nature
Text: Very beautiful waterfall that will make you go wow specially during the rainy season. Truly a marvel of mother nature. Good place to have a bath as well

Title: Great experience
Text: The waterfall offers really great views both from the bottom and the top. It's not an easy walk but it is worth it, especialy because you can take an awesome bath in the pools at the top. Definitely recommend it!

Title: Rocky climb easily done
Text: Good fun to climb to the top pool where you can take a dip with the locals. Its a bit of a scramble to the top but its worth it.

Title: Don't make a special effort
Text: We were passing and stopped for a bit. Glad we didn't make a special effort. Bandarakwela falls was much better.

Title: tall waterfall with mini falls at the top
Text: i and my family had a thoroughly enjoyable trip to this 170 m high waterfall . it is about 14 km from the hilly town of Haputale. The view moving out of the this town is captivating as it is situated on a ridge .  the bus trip from Haputale to the Diyaluma falls takes 45 minutes., going towards welawaya. The falls is  situated by the roadside with sprays falling onto the road . we took a walk thru the rubber plantation with many village homes enroute. there is a few paths leading up but one can always ask the village folks.  A young boy of 12 years became our guide and he is really well informed and fun to be with. we walked up  through temperate shrub land for about 45 minutes with many stops along the way to enjoy the views . At  the top it was pristine and gives a top of the world feeling looking down at the massive falls below.  many small falls are scattered around and provided much fun for my teenage childrem.  One can choose to explore further inland following the river but it was too tiring. there are  villagers selling coconuts and food  at the bottom of the falls.

Title: A nice waterfall!!!
Text: It was a nice walk to this small waterfall ,beautifully surrounded by tea gardens and lots of greenery with lots of early morning tourist came out for walk.

Title: Delightful walk amongst the tea plantations
Text: Actually our favourite walk in Sri Lanka. Not remarkable. Not a huge tourist attraction. Just a delightful stroll amongst the tea plantations watching the tea pickers at work to a nice waterfall at the end.  Lovely views over Nuwara Eliya and surrounding towns. Met some happy, smiling locals who wanted to have selfies with us. Finished with a tour of the Pedro Tea factory and a nice cuppa. Superb morning

Title: A little lightt on for water due to drought
Text: Worth the walk but like all of Sri Lanka we need some rain to make them grand again, pass through beautiful market gardens if you take the walk from town

Title: beautiful view
Text: quiet nice experience as we first went by tuk tuk and clicked fews pics in tea plantations then started our trail to the water fall which was very nice. Best was the view that we got from the hill point when we reached the water fall. The trail was worth walking.

Title: Beautiful small waterall
Text:
Lovely views going up to this waterfall 
We used a driver called Tharindu (0769164393) who took us to the waterfall and made the whole experience really fun. Waterfall is beautiful but obviously depends on the rains. When we went it hadn't rained for a while so was quite small but still definitely worth the trip.

Title: Great easy hike
Text: Great little waterfall to visit, and you get to wander through the Tea Plantation to get to it. Lots of locals picking tea and happy for a chat.

Title: Does not worth to go
Text: Sri Lanka is a country full of Waterfall, most of them has swimming pool, but this one is not good, it doesn't worth to hike for it, even when we came back, we lost our way and our car, need 45 min to find it, so if you visit Diyaluma fall or Ravana Ella fall, don't go to this...

Title: Good opportunity to stretch legs & see falls
Text: It was a good opportunity to stretch our legs during a long journey and there was plenty to see and buy if required.

Title: Bit of a hike but worth it
Text: The falls were quite small due to the lack of rain but fabulous views over the tea gardens .We took a tuk tuk up half way which made the last bit easier.

Title: One of the nicest waterfalls
Text: A breathtaking waterfall with an interesting legend. The legend goes that a pair of lovers took a leap to be together in the afterlife as they cant be together in real life.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: If you are pssing by do take the time to stop and take in the beauty of the falls. there's a good hotel/restaurant accross the road where you can get a fine Sri Lankan lunch of curry and rice!

Title: Average
Text: In Nuwra Eliya the two most beautiful falls are devon and st clair falls. there is nothing spacial about this falls and the roads to raach to the view point is very narrow lanes.

Title: Lovely walk through the Tea fields.
Text: Lovely steady climb up to pretty, natural waterfalls. Got chatting with a couple of tea pickers and took photos for a few rupees.

Title: Lovely stroll to the falls
Text: You can drive to within 10 minute walk of these falls. The stroll up to the falls is gentle with great views. The area of the waterfall did not live up to expectations. However it was very worth while.

Title: Pretty cool waterfall.
Text: A quick hike up the mountain after our tuk tuk driver drive us halfway. Pretty quiet, only saw a few people on the trail. Worth the effort.

Title: Another nice waterfall
Text:
We came across this waterfall shortly after we did a tea plantation view. We were intrigued with the name and stopped to enjoy the natural beauty and surroundings
Worth visiting

Title: Very nice though steep little walk
Text: Up a steep hill on a narrow road by tuk tuk, followed by a short though steep walk on the side of a tea plantation, the warter fall was  lovely and after the recent rain, quite spectacular

Title: I was missing clearer instuctions on how to get to the waterfall in the forest
Text:
Not that long hike, but count with walking a bit up to the hill. I didn't like much that it was not that clear where should a person walk to get to the waterfall. Some local was realizing that and he was guiding people up to the waterfall in exchange of some money. I didn't like that he just joined me and my boyfriend and suddenly became a part of walk, since we didn't ask him and I felt bothered.
The place is free of charge. You can either park at some parking lot a bit further away, or at the street under the hill, but then you need to walk a lot up to the hill.
What was disappointing was that right when you get to the waterfall, there is a fence that protects people from walking further and probably hurting themselves. It makes sense that it's there, but it prevents you from creating a nice picture of the waterfall. From this perspective, it's better to take pictures of the waterfall from a bit of distance.

Title: Quite a climb but well worth the effort!
Text:
Visited with a guide - doubt wed have found it otherwise!

When we arrived there wasnt much of a torrent but that made it even more spectacular.

Parts of the walk need care to negotiate. Good shoes and reasonable fitness required.

Title: Beauty waterfall just close to the city??
Text: Beautiful place to visit in 10 min drive from Nuwara Eliya centre. Small tracking to the waterfall from the parking, can be handled with kids. Exciting view to the valley. The waterfall can be seen from the main place but I also spotted people above the cliff, so somehow its possible to climb there if you in some real search for extreme)

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text: We were in the area so stopped to take a look at this waterfall. We paid for a tuktuk (long day!!) through the tea plantations to get to the area, and from there it was a short walk to the waterfall itself (few boulders etc!).  Great for a short stop on the way to Ella after lunch.

Title: A short walk from the road
Text: The waterfalls are a small walk from the road no need for Tuk Tuks walking through the tree plantation to the waterfall. Remember that to do the tea plantation get there an hour before they close we missed but 10 mins.

Title: Enjoyable trekking to the waterfalls
Text: Starting of the trek from the tea plantation opposite Pedro Tea Factory. The journey took 45mins to an hour walking along the tea plantations. Many different paths to walk to the waterfalls and we had to keep asking the locals whenever we met them. Beautiful scenery with tea plantations and met many friendly villagers. Upon reaching the waterfall, the path can be challenging having to manoeuvre between boulders. Also, beware of touts who would offer to bring you to the top of the waterfalls and pretend to get lost, then asking for money to bring you back. There is a warning sign near the waterfalls. Possibly, avoid going alone. The waterfall itself is underwhelming to me, but the journey of trekking was fun with beautiful scenery.

Title: Scenic beauty
Text: The place is scrnic and very beautiful. It is breathtakingly nice .  easliy accesible and can spend time finding your self and beauty of the nature in all the corner of the world .

Title: Great
Text: Nice waterfall close to the tea fields. Make sure you dont get bothered by one of the shady people hanging around there. Just dont accept them walking with you. Besides that its very nice

Title: Must See: Breathtaking Experience
Text: This breathtaking Waterfall is loacted in the outskirts of Nuwara Eliya and can easily be accessed by a tuk-tuk. You can also reach the foothills by a local bus and hire a Tuk Tuk to take you till half the distance ahead on a rocky track amidst tea plantations. Then one has to walk for five minutes uphill to get to the falls. There are people who do a trek from foot hills also. The water is cold, refreshing and sweet in taste.

Title: Good
Text: I had an amazing time at this place  and this place receives a big thumbs up from my side.a personal advise wear comfortable footwear

Title: Lovers leap
Text: Our tuk tuk driver showed us this falls from a distance. We had small children who could not climb far. The story of the lovers is great for our children and they then could put the story yo the water fall

Title: Beautiful
Text: We stopped off while travelling and delighted we did. Its amazing, a great photo opportunity, and a retreat from the heat of the day. It was busy, but it only added to our visit.

Title: Striking cascade
Text:
Lovers Leap Falls is a beautiful waterfall a short drive from town, near the Pedro Tea Factory.

The initial section up from the main road can be walked, but we opted to take a tuk-tuk, because e were tight for time.

You first cross through the tea plantation with excellent views of Nurawa Eliya, before reaching a forest path (where tuk-tuks will park.

Our excellent, considerate and thoughtful driver Jagan accompanied us, picking wild flowers for our daughter and explaining interesting details along the way. He also ensured our son was safe when he wanted to explore closer to the falls (where I was a bit concerned about slipping in my sandals).

We thought the ride was definitely worth the roughly $8US (1500 SKR), although it was rough and taxed the tuk-tuks lower gears. It had also drizzled all morning so it was muddy and slippery, which this option allowed us to avoid.

The path to the falls is picturesque and the view at the end is striking with the cool spray from the cascading waters misty your face. 

Took about an hour round trip, but was one of the highlights of our time in Nurawa Elyria.

Title: OK but not spectacular
Text:
We had a little time before our train departing Nuwara Eliya so decided to visit Lover's Leap Falls.  The climb to the very top looked too difficult and we were pressed for time, so we stopped at the lower level.

While very nice, these falls did not strike me as anything special.  It can be easily skipped if your itinerary is full.

Title: Lovely views and a nice hike- wear good hiking shoes and water proof jacket
Text:
It was an impromptu decision to go to this location. Our driver took us to the locality, from where we took a tuk tuk for half the ride up amidst the tea plantations. Since the path is full of stones and very narrow, normal cars cannot go up, however tuk tuks can easily access the place. For serious hikers, they can go for the climb all the way till the falls. 
En route, the view is enthralling, with team plantations all around and if the weather is on your side, there is little mist and clouds. As we went in December, we continued to experience rainfall throughout our journey.
Once the tuk tuk parked at it's last accessible spot, we took a short hike up (around a kilometre). Ensure to wear proper hiking shoes as because of the waterfall, the area is wet, with lots of small streams flowing, making the path slippery. There are also loose stones and wet ones, so shoes with a good grip will help. If you have not climbed before, be careful of your footing, however for most part, its a fairly easy climb.
Also be prepared to get wet! Needless to say, the water from the waterfall will get you soaked. Mind you, we were just on one side of the waterfall and not in its way, however the pressure sends water sprays that soak you completely. Some of us went prepared and were fine... others like me felt we jumped into the water :)
Its a fantastic view and very rejuvenating to be in the midst of nature and I really enjoyed it.
With the cold and wet weather of Nuwara Eliya, note that clothes DO NOT dry easily, unless you have heaters or fans.

Title: Lover's leap visit
Text: This place was not in our itinerary but due to availability of some time with us, our driver asked us to visit this place in a tuk tuk.  The tuk tuk driver Mr. Raju took us to this place through the tea gardens and explained about this waterfalls.  A worth visiting place.  The view from this place is awe-inspiring.

Title: Wonderful Hike to the Falls
Text: Must see if you visit Pedro Estate. We took a tuk tuk to the top and hiked on foot about 500m to the falls.  You could hike back down and enjoy the view of the tea estate and villages along the way.

Title: lovely walk to the falls
Text: we worth hiking to the falls they are excellent and you walk through tea bushes on your way great views

Title: A beautiful view
Text: A must visit and go to place. Do gear with shoes and bring along water bottle. A splendid view on the way up. You can hike up or take a tuk tuk ride cost us rs4000 with a tour. Took about 2hrs as a whole.

Title: Nice tea fields hike without too much effort
Text:
After a challenging tuk-tuk ride we hiked 15-20 minutes in to this nice waterfall. Great views all the way and the waterfall itself it really nice.

Do be aware of dodgy touts just before reaching the waterfall. IGNORE them and do not even engage them. They will try to make you pay them for being a "guide."

Title: Beautifull waterfall
Text: The way from the parking is about 1 km, so its ideal for small trip. The way is very wet, so is better take sneakers. From waterfall is good view to the Hawa Eliya

Title: Nice view for chill morning
Text: Theres not much to do here apart from sitting on a rock or filling in your water bottle but it is a good place for a chill morning or afternoon

Title: Stretch the legs and walk
Text: Easy 30 minute walk to Lovers Leap water fall. Worth it if you are looking to get the kids to do some walking. Not too far. You walk past the tea fields. When we went (July) low amount of water but still worth the walk and a good photo stop.

Title: Beautiful falls
Text: We didnt walk there because of weather but stopped at the oak ray wood shop for a view from their rooftop. Gorgeous.

Title: Scenic spot
Text: Managed to snap a picture of the fall from a distance. Due to lack of time did not trek to the fall. As usual better to go early morning where is comfortable and cooler.

Title: Didn't go close- saw from a distance
Text: Saw from a distance- didn't have time to trek up close. Looked fine from a distance- you can possibly skip unless you've lots of time to trek or very very fond of waterfalls

Title: A walk in the unknown bush until you come to it...
Text:
The road to this beautiful water fall was unique and adventurous. 
There was tea estates and lot of uneven terrain to travel and at the end it was all worth it.
I would recommend for those who go to the water fall please do not walk down the rocks to get closer unless you are with a professional tour guide as the rocks can be very slippery.

Title: your expectation falls...
Text:
...probably because like the lover, your expectations takes a jump (down) when you see this. A little underwhelming to see it - but maybe because we didn't really go up close. Yet another waterfall to see in the region.

I'd just say to stay in the car and get to your destination. Avoid this, unless you're a waterfall-phile.

Title: Superb in all directions
Text:
Beautiful waterfall in picturesque surroundings. Turn to view the falls then turn for a wonderful view of local village and villagers doing their daily chores.
A short walk out of town but very well worth the trip amoungst the cows, chickens and local houses. Unfortunately rubbish is a problem though.

Title: Pretty waterfall and nice walk
Text: Pretty waterfall. We walked up from the Pedro Tea Factory and it was a nice 20/30 minute hike through the tea plantations. On the way back we walked through the roads to town and it was nice to see all the small flower and food crops growing on people's properties.

Title: Pretty
Text: Just park up and take in the view, you can also see from the train from Kandy. Or you wish you can drive to the falls and walk up. We saw from the visitor area opposite.

Title: Pleasant pretty much sums it up.
Text: We decided to walk to the falls following the road, which proved enjoyable. The falls themselves are very nice; however we were not able to locate a clear path up to the top, which was disappointing.

Title: A cold, fresh reward for a hot hike
Text:
We cycled here form Pedro Tea Estate and then walked the last few hundred metres. It's a fun if hot walk walk (not too difficult but a little slippery on the very steep bits). We were rewarded with the beautiful falls. 

We paddled and drank the fresh clear, cold water. You can sit on the rocks and feel and feel as though you are in the falls. 

Definitely worth a visit.

Title: A lovely walk, worth it for the views
Text: There are several routes up to the falls. My driver took me to a village part of the way up the hill. From there the path was fairly steep. The falls were higher than I expected, the area clean and green. On the way down we got a bit lost - trying to take a less steep route - but found our way through the tea plantations and fields in the end.

Title: Path to Fall is whats great about this
Text: Not the fall, its the path leading to fall thats fantastic. The hike takes you through the tea plantation and some great landscape on the way. Many people were taking tuk tuk up to a point, i think hike along the way is great way to enjoy this.

Title: Nothing special
Text: I had already seen two lovely waterfalls in the hill country so i was not too impressed with Lover's Leap as it was much smaller than Ravana or Bambarakanda. It is less than an hour's walk from the town center but the final few hundred meters is up a steep path. Apparently prince found a sweetheart but his people did not like her so they committed suicide jumping from the falls.

Title: waterfall
Text: My guidebook made it sound like this waterfall is hidden, it isn't. There are signs at the beginning of the way (which starts across the main street from the tea factory,) then keep following the path. The story of how the falls got their name is sad, but the falls themselves are pretty.

Title: Tourist spot - must go
Text: Beautiful waterfalls. We took many pictures . Wear sneakers in order to climb the rocks. Grab a toasted Mielie whilst there. Stunning - please visit.

Title: Great water falls
Text:
This water fall is located in Nuwara Eliya and has two ways to reach. One is a steep way right through and the other is through adjacent tea plantation which is fairly easy to climb but a longer way.

You can expect 1.5 to 2 hours hiking and sitting beside the falls. Dont forget to ask the significance of the name these falls to the locals nearby.

Title: Worth Visiting.
Text: I allong with my family took tuk tuk to the foot steps . One can go walking also it will be good exercise. Mind your steps as you go near the falls if its raining. A worth taking efforts to way up

Title: Breathtaking views!
Text: We took tuk tuk to go up to the waterfall.It was amazing experience for kids,especially for my son who was riding on our guide's lap and  was using a steering wheel.The walk is not hard at the beginning but then you need to do a bit of hiking so it's a bit of a challenge with small kids.The tuk tuk guide was so kind though.He was even carrying my daughter to help us reach the waterfall.When you are there it's so beautiful and you can feel the water drops on your face.Really beautiful experience,pure nature.

Title: Easy Walk
Text: We took a tuk tuk up to the top of the trail for 1300 rupees. Great ride with views of the city below and tea fields. The walk from the end of the road to waterfall was about 500 m, with some rocks, but easy enough that I did it in flip flops!

Title: Nice trecking but beautiful
Text: It is on the outskirt of the Nuwarea Eliya after crossing about a kilometer between tea garden. The scenic beauty of the road is nice and can be easily reached if you are not too old or having problem in walking but wear the sports shoe ot comfortable shoe. However, auto(TukTuk) is available for this treck path with 500 LKU for both way but if you walk, you can take some beautiful snaps of tea garden and the city. Please keep some water with you. The fall is not too big but falling from a considerable height. No platform or railing not provided so it should have been developed properly. Please maintain safety because a big piece of rock is there which obstructs the spot where water if walling. Some young were riding  on that rock which looked me slippery and may be dangerous. Overall beuauti is OK.

Title: It's a hike
Text:
If you are done with other attractions of nuwara, you can explore this waterfall....

Car or taxi goes up till certain point and tuk tuk a further bit...then it's a walk of 1km to reach there ...if you want to avoid long walk, take short cuts but that's too steep 
With young children, a little challenge but i managed with my 3 and 9 yrs oldies 
I would not call.it average but above average and not very good....

Title: Nice place
Text: Best is to take a tuktuk (only one-way without waiting for us to go back) which drops you off close to the fall (then 10 min walk). We hiked back to town through tea fields and local gardens and the surrounding areas, which was nice. We were there on a Sunday and there were a lot of couples (mostly locals) so it was a nice atmosphere. Don't expect too much from the waterfall but it is definitely a nice place.

Title: Beautiful treck
Text: We had trailed along tea plucking estates. The path was rough, but worth the visit. The weather was pleasant.

Title: Waterfall hike
Text: One of the best places to visit in Nuwaraeliye .Bio diversity and the panaromic view is amazing.Walking through the tea fields and the cloud forest will take you to this lovely place.Also you can visit the Pedro tea processing center too which makes the Garden fresh lovers leap tea.

Title: Lovely fall
Text: There are so many water falls in Sri Lanka and most of them are beautiful. This one is of medium size but nice

Title: an amazing view
Text: Took a tuk tuk, walk and climb to this area. The view was amazing, the water from the water fall is cool when standing there and watching the water pour down from it. The first time i ever see a water fall at close distance

Title: An interesting activity
Text: We went to the falls after considerable heavy rain had fallen in the area so the falls were very full and fast. A worthwhile activity for anyone travelling in the area. We hired a tuk tuk to take us up to a spot 10 minutes walk from the middle platform of the falls.

Title: The highest watrfall in Sri Lanka
Text: Near Nuevara Elia ( small city in mountains) you can see magic waterfall. 30 meters. I spent 1500 ruppies fro two ways hotel-waterfall-hotel. By tuctuc, The Prince and pure girl loved each over... And... jumped together down. :((, So this name Leap Lovers. Waterfall down from ~ 2400 beters. It's the highest from Asia... And enough nice.

Title: Nice walk up for a great cuew
Text: Beautiful views up by lovers leap. A really pleasant walk up even in the pouring rain. Only spent around 30mins-1hr total. Hire a tuktuk to take you the majority of the way up and walk the final 250 metres.  Rain or shine this is worth it.

Title: Worth the effort to reach there
Text: After a small trek on difficult terrain, you will come across this gem of a place. With the waterfall on one side, and the entire city view on the other, this place has to be on your must visit list.  As the same suggests, legend has it that a royal prince jumped from this waterfall with his lover from the town when his father did not approve of their love. The water is also the only source of water for the entire city and once you reach the top, you will realize you are seeing something special.

Title: He asked & she said yes! ??
Text:
So my experience may be slightly bias as today while visiting Lovers Leap Falls my partner got down on one knee and asked me to marry him infront of it! It was just so perfect! ??????

As I am pregnant with twins we didnt walk up the very bumpy, steep road that would have easily taken 90mins at least, we got a tuk tuk from our hotel at Araliyah Green Hills which is 10 mins away by car, all the way to 5 mins walk from the Fall, the driver waited and took us back all for 2,000SR which is around £10. Very much worth paying for if you dont fancy the trek or arent fit enough. I wouldnt recommend walking the entire hill with small children or if you arent in a fit & healthy time in your life.

We only had to share the space with another group of young people for about 10mins before having it to ourselves. Its a very quiet and non touristy place.

It was a lovely waterfall and the surroundings were beautiful. Def worth a visit with or without children ??

Title: Beautiful waterfall!
Text: The waterfall is really beautiful and the walk up to the waterfall is not too difficult. Take a left at the blue water tank and keep heading straight until you see signs. Mostly dirt roads with a few steep parts at the end of the trail. Absolutely a must do!

Title: Tea-citing experience
Text: A must-do in any travel to Nuwara Eliya is the tea plantations. Learn how tea came to Sri Lanka, sip different tea,  consider a purchase and explore the landscape. Learn now the name lover's leap came about.

Title: Feel the spray in your face!
Text:
You must walk to these falls if you are only 3 - 5kms away. Dont get a car or tuk tuk or you will miss the fresh air, the spectacular views across the tea plantations to the mountains and the lake, and the sight of those working in the fields. 
If you must get a ride to the end of the track, it is only a 10min walk to the falls. Over 30 mtrs high, you can sit on a rock opposite and feel the spray in your face, but be careful, them rocks can be slippery when wet.

Title: Great for a few hour trek and views
Text:
Lovers Leap is a really nice and walkable trek from the city centre. Total walk time to the waterfall was about an hour. Tuk tuks are available but will try rip you off. Walking there you will catch some amazing views of the town and its surrounding landscapes! 

We accidentally went through an alternative route and walked through a (muddy) farmers foot trail... dont wear flip flops. The usual route is via Pedros Tea Estate, which is also an easier walk.

Overall highly recommend if you want to kill a few hours in Nuwara... tuk tuk back for ~200 rupees.

Title: Beautiful
Text: This is a another beautiful water fall around here. You have to walk a bit from the main road to get close  to the water fall.

Title: Nice Waterfall
Text:
We used a tuk tuk most of the way to the falls as it was very hot and the road was both steep and rough. Plenty walked it but I can't comment on how difficult it is. The fare was haggled down to 1200 rupees return for both of us, about 7ish. Pay when you get back, not in advance! You want him to be there waiting for you when you walk back down the path to the end of the road!!!
We walked the last 10 minutes or so as the road becomes a path. The falls are lovely but not overly massive. There's a flat rock to stand on at the base to admire the waterfall and plunge pool.
It's not going to change your life or anything but its worth it for the lovely views of Nuwara Eliya and the cool breeze you get up there.

Title: Nice story and waterfall
Text: You have to walk to the waterfall. Not far and not difficult. It is worth a visit. Such a nice story about the waterfall and You can get quite close to it.

Title: A leap of faith if ever there was one!!!
Text: Worth the visit despite the windy roads towards the leap.  The weather whilst we were visiting was not the best but we were determined to drive up the narrow road leading to the Lover's Leap.

Title: A very nice walk
Text:
This nice waterfall is just a short ride outside Nuwara Eliya by tuck tuck or bus. 
It's across the main road from Pedro Tea Estate.  There is a big sign pointing you in the  direction. You don't need a guide to find it. The walk to the fall is easy  and pretty, and takes you through tea fields on a gravel road. Shoes are better than slippers for this walk, and  almost everybody will be able do it. Most will even find the walk quite easy. The waterfall itself is fine, but you can find even bigger ones in this part of the country. All in all Lovers Leap is a fine morning or afternoon walk.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Its beautiful surrounded by tea plantation. We just stopped on the main road to have a look on our way back to Nuwara. It was beautiful.

Title: Perfect stop
Text: Our driver pulled off to the side . We had decided we didnt want to climb to the top after climbing Adams peak. Perfect photos from the bottom. Quite crowded with people swimming, but definitely worth the stop.

Title: Good for photos on the way from Nuwara to Yala
Text: On the main road, about an hours drive away from Nuwara. One can take photos and then move on. It is on the main road hence crossing the road needs attention.

Title: Make sure you go right to the top
Text: This is a terrific attraction. Free entry and sensational views. We visited the day after some rain which was good however even with little water the view would still be worth the hike. The highlight is going right up to the top of the falls, this is a very steep and slippery section and not clearly marked. It took us 1.5 hours to reach the top from the centre of Nuwara-eliya. We then got a tuk tuk back into town for just 200rs.

Title: Beautiful view.
Text: This is my first time to come in this place and it was really really great experience. Every single things here in Sri Lanka ???? I really appreciate.

Title: Easy Hike
Text: Around 10 - 20 min hike, u will be rewarded with the spectacular view of the waterfall. My muscle was not helping me to go faster to the view area due to muscle pain after hiked up the Adams Peak. After few minutes climbing.. all the pain goes away when you see the great view.

Title: Wonderful experience
Text: Well worth the walk to this waterfall and several great places to take some great photos. Nice place to simply take in the view.

Title: Pleasant and easy hike
Text:
The turn-off to the Pedro Tea Estate is better sign-posted, but the road to Lover's Leap starts just opposite. We were immediately approached by a tuk-tuk driver who declared the road impassable with a regular vehicle.  He was partially right.  Some 200 m further up the road it does get bad.  Some vehicles with higher clearance still drive up that way, as do tuk-tuks.  We walked, as the tea-landscape is pleasant and the trail makes for an easy hike.

About half-way up the trail, even tuk-tuks stop and you have to walk the last ten minutes or so.  You are rewarded by the sight of the waterfall, which is by no means massive, but a refreshing sight.

Title: Great quick hike
Text: Not too far from the town proper. We did not end up hiking all the way to the top of the waterfall - it was extremely steep and quite wet. A nice short hike to get out of town.

Title: Good waterfalls
Text: It's a small trek to the water falls. It's about a 10 mins walk towards the waterfalls. The view is good. No entrance fees. Our tuk tuk driver took us to the waterfalls. Better to go with someone to guide you through the trails to the waterfalls. Saves time.

Title: Excellence choice for a walk from Nuwara Eliya
Text:
The first part of the walk is not attractive because you have to go along the street but when you enter side street everything changes. You walk up through the village and then amazing tea fields. Final stage is through the forest. Waterfall is picturesque. 
The whole way from city centre is around 5 km. If you don't want to cover everything on your feet you may take tuktuk or local bus.   The attraction is free.

Title: Quite a trek but worth it
Text: We visited here during our stay in Nuwara Eliya. Reaching out to the base of this place is quite a challenge but its all worth it when you reach there. a Must try!

Title: Lovely view up close after a fun and bumpy tuk tuk ride
Text:
Reading some of the comments here we negotiated with a driver from the city center for a to and fro trip for 800. The ride up was bumpy and fun but also full value for money as there were lovely views along the way. There is a short 5-7 min hike over natural forest terrain before you reach the viewing point with breathtaking views of the water falls. Along the way you can dip your hands or take a sip (depending on how strong your gut it and how adventurous you are) from the numerous small streams with crystal clear cool water trickling down. 

Dont be fooled though by the tuk tuk guys who tell all sort of stories about the distance and difficulty. The distance is no more than 5 km from city center and difficulty is what you pay 750-800 rs which is far the normal tariff for such a distance. 

All in all a couple of hours well spent and well worth a trip in clear weather.

Title: Nice waterfall
Text: The point of view is nice, you can see the city. The fall is quite tall and refreshing. There are two tracks to reach it : the first one starts juste before the little bridge coming from town center on the road below the fall (steep and some climbing), the other one is easy and you walk in tea plantations and access Pedro tea factory from there.

Title: Very nice
Text: You can take the bus from Nuwara Eliya, it takes only 10 minutes. After a visit at Pedro tea factory you can have Very relaxing walk through the tea plantation. Beautiful waterfalls

Title: Excellent
Text:
Did this on our tour with our wonderful guide it is a must if your travelling this way you wont be disappointed 
And real good for some amazing pictures

Title: Graced with a story to complement the peacefull nature of the falls
Text: A pleasant early morning walk through the tea plantations with great views over the city of Nuwara Eliya. After 30 minutes or so you then have these clean water falls to view. Surrounded by lush bush and the bird song nearby adds to the drama of the visit.

Title: It is the best place in the world
Text:
But you need a guide
there are some local people can help and come with you.
Going up to the highest point of waterfall takes 3 or more hours but I recommend that don't lose it

Title: Nice small walk up the hill between tea plantations
Text: If you have planned for Pedro Tea Factory, then this is a must visit, as it is very near. A small hike up the hill and you will find the amazing views of the Fall. We were there on a rainy day, so the fall was amazing. can't comment about dry season.

Title: Doesn't worth it
Text:
I highly do not recommend this place . it is nothing but a little of water falling. see the photo I attached .

the car also cannot take you there , while you need a tuck-tuck and to pay around 2000 rubies for nothing

Title: Really worth it
Text: After the tea factory we walk to this waterfall, we had bad weather, but it was still worth it! You will have a nice view over the city and it was amazing with all the clouds! In one time is clear and all the clouds are gone, looks so amazing! Also the waterfall is amazing!

Title: Small pleasant hiking
Text:
The hiking is really pleasant and you can do it before or after you do the Pedro Tea factory visit. You can also enjoy some great views of the surroundings and the tea plantings around Nuwara Eliya.
Note that the pathways are not very well indicated, but you should find it easily.

Title: Stunning Creation Of God
Text: While many may disagree with my review, I am sticking to what I am writing here. The fall is beautiful and the walk up the fall is well worth it. Do not attempt to take the tuk tuk up the hill. Go and enjoy the nature and you will be amazed at what you see. The climb can be quite tiring but it is absolutely well worth it. Go for it folks.

Title: Well worth seeing in a town with little else to see
Text:
Anyone who gives this natural creation a poor review has no idea what they're talking about. 
Take the bus here and walk up the hill. Don't take a tuktuk. 
The walk is nice but there were loads of kids on the way up who were spread in packs... First lot tried to sell us some narcotic substances and followed us for a bit much to the discomfort of my other half. Further up there were more who would ask for money and shadow you. Have your wits about you here
 
The falls are nice. Peaceful. A nice rock.to lay on. If you're ballsy, climb higher and stand on the higher rocks.

Nice place and well worth it.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
The hike up to Lover's Leap has stunning views. You can take a tuk-tuk up to specific point though the wrong tuk-tuk will struggle to go up the hill!
The waterfall itself isn't as spectacular from close up but that's just my opinion

Title: Nice quiet place
Text: If you want to run from crowds and enjoy a piece of nature with great views over Pedro tea plantations go for it. You can come by Tuktuk very close or just walk from the main road by yourself which is better!

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Web took the bus from Nurwa Eliya station cost 50 lkr going out and 24 coming back! Still ridiculously cheap. The bus conductor will tell you where to get off to find the path which is clearly marked. We got off at Pedro tea factory where we took some great photos of the tea terraces and reservoir. Walking up to the falls is not difficult although going right up to the top may be far more challenging  (we couldn't see the way to do this and weren't equipped anyway). Lovely waterfall and well worth a couple of hours.

Title: Stunning location
Text: One of many lovely falls in the area but stands out because of the location. Popular spot for travellers to stop so it can be busy but worth the time. Stretch your legs and go for a walk in the area

Title: One hour round trip - good views of the valley and plantations
Text:
The Lonely Planet guide mentioned this walk near the Pedro tea factory.  Make sure you don't enter the factory before looking for the start of the walk.  On our first attempt we headed down the hill from the factory and ended up at a dam.  In hindsight that was pretty dumb, since you usually need to climb to see a waterfall!  The start of the walk is actually well signposted from the main road and, not surprisingly, you need to go uphill.

The walk is through plantations, and is not taxing.  When you reach a temple, you head up a small track and quickly come upon the waterfall.  It was not flowing heavily when we were there (Jan).

For us, this was a nice way to do a bit of exercise and see the view before heading off on a drive to Kandy.

Title: Nice hike to the quiet waterfall
Text:
From where the car stops, it's a 10-15 minute walk that takes you through a local neighborhood, tea plants and other plantations common in this high-altitude Sri Lankan rural community.

The fall itself is at its ebb in December, which is when we visited, but it still offers spectacular views of Nuwara Eliya.

Lovers Leap is the main source of water for the entire Nuwara Eliya valley, so visitors are asked to be considerate of the water and not contaminate it.

The name Lovers Leap kind of betrays the legend: a prince fell in love with a beautiful maiden living in the valley but his father opposed the union, so he took his beloved and together they leapt to their tragic demise, their love forever immortalized by the folly of their youth and a waterfall that is visited by many from far and wide.

Title: Reasonable falls close to Nuwara Eliya with nice surrounding views
Text: If you've got some spare time, Lovers Leap is close to Nuwara Eliya (20 min drive). It's a short but reasonablely steep, scrably climb to the waterfall. Its not too difficult to climb and quiet nice.  They're not the best falls you'll see, but worth the trip and effort. . From the base of the falls there are some nice views down the valley across the vegetable farms.

Title: amazing small adventure
Text: manageable, easy to reach, some hiking, deserve to see with coffee, nature, love, couples. you can just sit and see

Title: Beautiful hike
Text:
Such a lovely place and one of the rare things you can do for free in Sri Lanka! Theres no signposts but if you ask and walk in thw general direction on Google maps its pretty easy to get to. 

The hike is fairly easy too (but wear boots or sturdy trainers) and there are lovely views of the town, waterfall and tea plantations. 

Highly recommended when in Nuwara Eliya, especially if you're on a budget!

Title: Amazing place
Text: We just couldn't stop contemplating those falls surrounded by green areas all over, different kinds of trees and bushed, while having our lunch in a nice decent restaurant.

Title: Spectacular but slightly overrated.
Text:
On our final leg of our trip to Sri Lanka stopped here to photograph the falls,was expecting something more spectacular and awe inspiring,but just a standard waterfall with a pool at the foot of it.
People were swimming in the pool as it was a very hot afternoon,but I would not recommend it as our guide said that loads of tourist break limbs there!
Worth seeing but have seen better.

Title: Spot well worth a visit
Text: Lovely waterfall and good views of Nuwara Eliya on the way. We walked up from the main road.  The road up is quite uneven so could be a bumpy ride in a tuk tuk There were several tuk tuks waiting on the road to take us back to our hotel. Lovely waterfall and good views of Nuwara Eliya on the way.

Title: A Waterfall in Nuwara Eliya
Text: Few people has mixed up between this waterfall and the other one on the way to Ella from Nuwara Eliya. This is different waterfall and can be reach easily in Nuwara Eliya. You can either go up by Tuk Tuk or walk the unpaved road. Keep in mind walking means you will be full of dust!! On the way you will see many tea farms and locals who are working on it, beautiful! The waterfall it self its normal and it was very small. Maybe in rainy seasons will be much more better.

Title: Its nice  in way to nuwara eliya
Text: Its good watarfall and nice place for photography there are big mountains around and trees around. Dont missed it

Title: Tea everywhere
Text: We decided to walk from Nuwara Eliya to this waterfall, as it is not far away (after tuk tuk driver wanted almost 2000 rupees for the ride) and it was a nice walk, first trough the village and after trough the tea plantation (which was my favorite as we've run into tea pickers and that was opportunity for some typical Sri Lankan photos). The waterfall is nice, nothing spectacular, but we were there in the dry season, so I guess there is more water in other seasons. But the place is quiet and the view is nice.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
We got a tuk tuk most of the way up, I don't know if it was the roads of the drunk tuk tuk driver but not for the faint hearted. 

It isn't that far and due to the hike not being all that overwhelming I believe it would be easy to walk from the bottom. 

On the way up we met local women who pick tea leaves and the whole journey the views are spectacular. Once arriving at the waterfall it wasn't disappointing, absolutely beautiful with different levels able to reach even the top. 

It is free unless your paying a driver and is very chilled out. Easily fitted in as a second or third thing to cram into a day.

Recommend it to anybody in the area.

Title: I liked
Text: We were on the road from Yala to Nuwara Eliya which is very busy way and took about 5 hours with stops and in the middle was is natural wunder Be there is must!

Title: Rawana Warerfalls
Text: Drove by this scenic area on the drive from Nuwara Eliya to Yala, busy attraction. Not huge water cascades due to low rainfall, although the preceding area may be more treacherous if there was more rainfall, ie falling mountain rocks and road giveaway. Nice to see, when passing by.

Title: Water falls
Text: This waterfall is certainly worth a visit , even if the weather is not so good. Can be got to just off the Glenfall road in Nuwara Eliya. Allow a few hrs to take the views in. You'll not be disappointed. Once At the top, you can see quite a lot , from race course, Sports lake, (Gregory), Golf course, parts of town etc. Go for it. You will enjoy.!!

Title: False?
Text: May be an attraction for a deserter, way up in a private tea garden one has to take a 3 wheeler ride for about 20 minutes and then walk on rough patches for another 20 minutes to sea water fall from a tap?  Funny

Title: Nice Walk, Lovely views
Text: Worth a visit but do it en route to the milk/dairy farms of Ambewela which makes it a perfect day out and about Nuwara Eliya

Title: nice view of the city - nothing more
Text:
,The fall - at least in August - is not very impressive, but it offers some very nice views of Nuwara Eliya and it's surroundings. A nice way to spend some time at the city.
There are Tuk-Tuks wainting on the road beloow, taking one of them is recomanded, to save the long sunny way up.

Title: Get a tuk tuk here as its a bit steep up and dangerous
Text:
Great waterfall to see via tuk tuk journey
Good to do before a tea plantation
Free and always better when things are free
Good photo spot and you can walk up to a ledge bit to sit and also a good photo spot

Title: awesome spot
Text: it's awesome spot near Nuwara Eliya to take photos and enjoy the weather and the magical views. I have been there on the road after I got out of Nuwara Eliya

Title: Very nice waterfall
Text: This is a  very nice waterfall. Wonderfull view. If you have a SUV or 4X4 dont afraid to go yourself. Tuk tuk drivers will tell that you can not drive that's because of a tuk tuk mafia. You should go if your vehicle has a high ground clearance.

Title: Spectacular falls!
Text: Take a road trip from nearby Nuwara Eliya to see these beautiful falls, easily visible from some dedicated parking bays.

Title: Great hiking tour for Waterfall and great view !
Text: Excellent hike in up country with view on tea estates, Nuwara Eliya town and great countryside. I stayed on lower side of the waterfall but you can reach out further through a path in the jungle and get up to the falls. In any case it's a lovely view and great experience also for families with children as not too long or too tough/ steep.

Title: Nice fall
Text:
Its a small hike but some places it is very steep, avoid it on a rainy day.

Fall is not very high but is nice, water is clean. From there you get great view of tea gardens and city.
worth a visit is you are in Nuwara Eliya.

Title: Worth the view
Text:
You have to travel further up from Nuwara Eliya to get close this waterfall. Once there you shouldn't regret the spectacular view of tea plantations and misty city establishments. 
We were not prepared to take the cold weather of Nuwara Eliya at all. Therefore, we couldn't stay long. 
Next time, I have plans to stay in Nuwara Eliya for at least a week.

Title: Average
Text: We went towards the end of day. Tuk Tuk took us up the hill, through an uneven road. Once up, we had to trek for a while. The view was ok. Maybe we had seen a lot during the day, so view was not as great as the reviews mentioned. The falls were also average. Not a lot of flow. Overall it was ok, For senior citizens, my parents are 65+, so my mother could not make it. Father is fitter and made it. So, if parents are with you, see if you want to take them with you.

Title: Walk to the waterfall,No tuktuk
Text:
Be aware that distance between the main road to waterfall is just less than 1.5 km,when we asked about the waterfall way the drivers asked us 15000sr and told us its far far from the main road (8km) they said that's impossible to get there by walk!but I just checked the google map and ask our host!
Be careful about tuk tuks they'll cheat you if you don't have enough information!
Also the way to the waterfall was really really great we pass the tea fields and amazing views above,don't mind miss the way! 
And an other important point! Don't care about boys who will ask you money during the way just ignore them and keep walking!

Title: Fresh, Peaceful and Beautiful- that's all about Lover's Leap Falls
Text:
If you just have only one afternoon to visit around Nuwara Eliya before going to Horton Plain next morning, Lover's Leap Falls is a perfect choice. I arrived Nuwara at 1.30pm and took a rest in my hostel (Lake View Holiday Home) till 3pm. The tuktuk driver offered me a tour package for 2 people to visit Lover's Leap Falls and tea factory for 1000Rs from our hostel (after bargain).
I can tell that Lover's Leap Falls is really amazing, after tuktuk took us to the hill, we walked about 10 min to the fall. From the fall, we could see the whole picture of Nuwara Eliya and enjoyed the blowing wind, fresh air, and feel like time just stands still for a moment. This moment is memorable and priceless to me.
After that, we went to the tea factory that was not so far away. To visit around factory, we paid 200Rs/person for visiting around and for the guider. If you dont want to visit around

Title: Definitely worth seeing
Text: Beautiful views, worth the climb we took a tuktuk up and otherwise long steep walk, watch out for begging children, which is actually against theaw in Sri Lanka.

Title: Nice walk
Text: This is a worthwhile and nice walk. You can look out over the tea plantations and see the waterfall. We walked back to town and took the bus out but you can also take a tuk tuk.

Title: Amazing view
Text: The falls is very nice and looks fantastic. It is cascading from a  great height and looks very lovely..

Title: Nice walk and views
Text:
We walked to the falls from the other side of the lake which was about 5k and took about 1.5 hours.   It makes a very scenic walk and you can take a slightly different route to the taxis although some parts are fairly steep and take lots of water. The views are great and on the way back down we caught the local bus back to town which was rs 30 for both of us. 
Nice experience.

Title: Lovely lover's leap
Text: We took a tuk-tuk from Nuwara Eliya, overpriced, as it is another and easier way to visit the falls. Easy hike and nice falls, but not spectacular. We took a shortcut back and passed lovely small houses and gardens before we reached the main road and got  a tuk-tuk back to Nuwara Eliya. It is also possible to go by bus, but tuk-tuk is more convenient.

Title: Great view for pictures only
Text: Great view for pictures only. If you are in your way from Kandy to Nuwara eliya do not miss it. You have to stop and tage pictures.  GREAT VIEW

Title: Good waterfalls, but you need to walk around few hundred metres
Text: Nice waterfalls, but there is no proper road to the same.Also, the tuk-tuk will only take you to a certain point, beyond that you need to walk.Advisable to go in groups and the place is not very safe for children (safety wise)

Title: Great view
Text: We took a tuk-tuk from Pedro Tea Factory and Plantation (750 Rupees return) to get to and from the falls. The is a little walk at the top and not too strenuous to get to the falls which are not that spectacular but nice to view as is the vista from the falls across the valley. Younger people walked up and down and some took a tuk-tuk up and walked down.

Title: Nothing spectacular. But a nice walk through the tea fields.
Text:
The waterfall itself isn't too special. Not much water in the dry season.
The way to the waterfall is a quite nice walk through the tea fields. You also can combine your visit here with a tour at Pedro's tea factory.

Title: Nice waterfall
Text: A nice waterfall that actually provides drinking water to the town. Don't listen to the tuk tuk drivers on the main road, it's only about 1.8km to the waterfall (although the path is quite steep).

Title: waterfall with a view
Text:
we loved the trip to the fall , we took a tuk tuk and payed 1500 roepia for 1 tuk tuk - the small car did with us 15 minutes and then we walked for another 15 minutes to the faal.
Lovers leap is a beautifull place, nearby you can see the tea factory and the peak of the highest mountain in Sri Lanka

Title: Amazing
Text: Lovely site to see to see the water guessing down the mountain side wonderful scenery lots of people taking photos and monkeys looking for food

Title: Spectacular Waterfall and view
Text: This is a short 4.5k walk through tea plantations and tracks by a forest.  It's a quiet, non touristy walk and the waterfall at the end is beautiful.

Title: one of the water fall in Nuwara Eliya
Text: Therev are so many water falls around Nuwara Eliya. This is one of them but I will not rate this as best. There are some other water falls which are better then this one.

Title: Nice small waterfall
Text: Easy to walk up to here after a tour of the Pedro tea estate. Locals want to guide you (for a fee) but it is reasonably self explanatory so no need. Got some great views of the town and the tea estate on the way. Waterfall is nice to see. Still clean and can get very close to it. Don't dirty or swim in the water, locals still use it as drinking water downstream.

Title: you can reach the very bottom of the water keep climbing.
Text: its nice and offers nice views across the valley, late afternoon is better because when your up close the sun might hide behind the cliff, offering better images.

Title: lovers leap falls
Text: This place Nuwaraeliya is a small town surrounded by hills . It is 6200feet above sea level . It is a popular hill station . When there r rains they collect together and fall down as water falls . There are many falls in this area .

Title: it doesnt exist!!!
Text: Please stop advertising this Falls...it doesnt exist anymore. There is a dark stain on the rock where the beautiful falls used to exist but all the water has been stopped by a dam and so there is NO waterfall there!

Title: A nice walk and view of Nuwara Eliya
Text: Lover's Leap Falls for me is not that main attraction, it's actually the stunning view of Nuwara Eliya town. It's worth the walk to get there.

Title: Water Fall
Text: Romantic place to spend a few minutes with your loved ones amid the water falls though you cant get wet which is not allowed

Title: Isolated Area
Text: You walk on a narrow lane which leads to the viewing area right next to couple of buildings. Its a distant view and you can probably spend few minutes as there is no seating area.

Title: a breath of fresh air
Text: L.L. Is a well worth a bit of extra effort as you hike round the park, not everyone bothers, that's part of the attraction.

Title: Water falls
Text: This just a small water falls I saw it from a distance. I was told since it had not rained for some time there is not much water.

Title: Well worth the effort
Text:
The Lover's leap falls requires one to leave their car on the main road and take a rickshaw (tuk-tuk) for the next 15 mins before having to walk the last km. But once you get there you'll probably be the only person and can access the waterfalls after jumping over a few big rocks. It's a wonderful place to relax or even jump in and immerse yourself. 

Do visit!

Title: Cool waterfall, quite secluded
Text: Well worth a visit if you are in the area. Wesr runners/hiking shoes to get there (not flip flops!) Because getting there involves climbing over some rocks. Its walkable but we took a tuk tuk most of the way because we had just finished Adam's peak that morning!

Title: Beautiful peaceful walk up to these falls
Text:
The road to these beautiful falls is located across the street from the entrance to Pedro Tea Estate just east of the city. It can be reached easily and very cheaply by taking the bus to Borlander.
The falls are about a 2 km walk of an easy grade gradual climb. There are TukTuk for hire at the entrance to the road. However the walk up was easy and wonderful. We were able to get great views of the mountains, the plantations and some of the houses where the pickers live.
The falls themselves are large but not spectacular as we visited in the dry season.

Title: The journey to the tea plantation makes the trip
Text:
We walked from Pedro tea Plantations, the walk up through the tea plantations, watching the tea pluckers was a great cultural experience and made for some wonderful photography.

We packed a picnic lunch to eat at the waterfall. Picturesque.

Title: Lover's Leap Falls,Hawa Eliya,Nuwara,Sri Lanka.
Text: Lover's leap falls.We had a very well planned drive,by our driver to view this quite spectacular waterfall.Well worthy of a visit!!!.

Title: Walk through the Tea plants
Text: It's an easy walk through the tea plant fields, which they were harvesting at that moment. We got a peak at the weighing on our way down. The fall itself is not that impressive.

Title: Fall in the heart of town!
Text: Definitely lacks signage and is hard to locate. A couple of false trails as roads were not the best. The best trail is via a tea estate that we never found. We climbed up the hard way through the hill. The access to the fall is not easy and partially fenced by a religious shrine. Possibility of bathing in a very small 'pool'. Worth a visit and good view from the top of the town and surrounding peaks on a clear day.

Title: Superb little trip without to many tourists
Text:
I really enjoyed the Lovers Leap Waterfall.
Personally this was probably one of my most soothing hikes in whole Sri Lanka. Its just a short walk from Pedro Tea Factory, however there are little tourists and its super nice to chill on one of the big rocks just below the waterfall.

Be Advised, the water is drinking water so one are not allowed to step into the pond of fall itself. However standing on the rocks in front of the fall makes great picture opportunities

Title: Good view
