Title: Nice, but not spectacular...
Text: This was a quick stop over when we were on our way in the morning from Ella for afternoon safari tour at Yala National Park. A quick stop for 10-15 mins for photo takings from the viewing platform near the bridge. Many tourists stop by here too, hence it can be crowded at times. There are restaurants nearby with toilet available. Nice for a short stopover, but nothing wow us.

Title: Another must do in Ella.
Text: Everyone who visits Ella visits here, and it is about 6 k's out of town.  Plentyof taxis, tours and tuk tuks to choose from toet you there.  Another must do if visiting Ella.

Title: Nice but can be very crowded.  Watch out for the monkeys
Text: We visited the falls late afternoon so there were a lot of people at the base of the falls cooling off and swimming.  Watch your things as the monkeys are everywhere and love to grab and dash away if they can grab something from you.

Title: Beautiful view from the top
Text: One of the best things about our trip to Srilanka was visiting Ravana Falls. Its majestic,magnificent. Located about 15mins away from ella town centre. Since we were on a day trip to ella,we had our cab with us. U can easily go here in a tuk tuk. Spend atleast half hour here. Take lots of pics n videos. U can go near d foot of d falls. Its an amazing experience. The falls itself are so amazing. No entry fee. Its a popular destination.

Title: Travel
Text:
Wooowwwwwwwwwww
One of the most beautiful places that I ever been .
Very recomanded 
If you r in Sri Lanka don't miss this place

Title: Ok
Text: Nothing special, but others may think it was . You can get a refreshing shower under the falls if you like.

Title: Quick stop on route to Ella
Text: Pretty falls even in the dry season. Difficult to park a car. You should need more than 10 minutes to see and take photos. Dont climb them as lots of people I am told have fallen.

Title: Do not miss it!
Text: This is another amazing nature scenery in Sri Lanka. If you pass through the region is a must visit!

Title: A soothing place
Text: A well visited waterfall on the main road from Ella to yala. The place is close to the main city and can be easily accessed via bicycles or vehicles. The view is really stunning and you feel like spending some time here. A couple of small eateries help you refresh. A good visit in Ella.

Title: Very busy
Text: The lovely waterfall was somewhat spoilt by the amount of traffic and stall etc immediately surrounding it. It is worth stopping for a photo if you are passing but otherwise not really worth a detour to find it

Title: Beautiful falls, not a nice atmosphere
Text: Go somewhere to look at something from the road, accompanied by busses of tourists , is not are thing at all. Pushy venders and the water is extremely dirty, alle the waste water from uptown Ella comes down here.

Title: Pretty Waterfalls
Text: While we were staying at the Amba estate, we visited these waterfalls.  These falls are close to the road and there are a lot of vendors booths around them.  The falls themselves are pretty.

Title: A waterfall.
Text: The falls are quite big and picturesque, don't expect anything to really blow you away though - its not anything extraordinary when it comes to waterfalls. The place is quite crowded and surrounded by vendors.

Title: Water is always a refreshing sight.
Text:
The Ravana Falls is majestic in its own way and drops from a fair height. 
Not crowded like the Nine Arch Bridge and can be easily included in a half day excursion along with the nearby Ravana Caves and the previously mentioned Nine Arch bridge.
1

Title: Pretty waterfall
Text: We drove past here and our driver stopped for a photo opportunity.  The falls are not a prolific as they are sometimes as the rainfall has been poor, but it was still worth a stop and a pretty location.

Title: A WATERFALL WITH MANY FEATURES
Text: Near Ella, the waterfall can be viewed from various vantage points. It is about 85 meters high. That it is a broken up waterfall adds to its allure. It has wide and narrow areas and areas of crashing waters and relative calm. It was named after an evil king named Rawana. Some call it Bambaragama Falls. It is best seen during the rainy season. It is conveniently located beside the Wellawaya Road. The uploading speed was terrible so I could not provide some photos.

Title: Okay to see if you are passing
Text:
This large waterfall is located at the side of a main road where there are major roadworks happening. Our driver stopped to show us on our way down to Tangalle. There is a bit of a viewing platform for people to take selfies, parking payment attendants and refreshment stalls.

It was good but I would have been disappointed if I had paid specifically to go there.

Title: Photo hotspot, limited space
Text:
A few minutes from Ella town & right on the roadside is a fairly impressive waterfall. 
Space is limited so I imagine on a busy high season day access would be a problem. 
As youd expect the rocks in the water flow are slippery but once navigated you can stand on the other side for some great pictures. There is a pool that can get into for a splash around but dont see it as a swimming opportunity. 
There are a few refreshment huts around & as everywhere lots of monkeys. 
Id suggest no more than a 30 min stop off.

Title: Amazing waterfall
Text: Beautiful waterfall but it's right on a main road so not a peaceful place to visit. Worth stopping off in a tuk tuk on your way to the coast for the view. Would not recommend walking here from town as the road is not safe to walk on.

Title: Nice picturesque falls near Ella
Text: The Ravana Falls are worth seeing if you visit Ella. A twenty minute tuk tuk ride out of the town, it might cost you about 2000 rupees. We stopped on our way to Udawalawe so the stop was included in the total price. You cannot walk there from Ella as the road is pretty narrow with lots of traffic. The falls themselves are nice to see; about 25 metres high but quite wide (widest in Sri Lanka). Depending on the time of year there would be more or less water pouring down the rock face. We visited in January and there was still some water flowing.

Title: Right on the road so difficult to miss
Text: Great fall which is easily accessible for some pics. You can pick up some fruits from the close by shops. Spend 10 mins here and good to go.

Title: Quick Dip
Text: We stopped here just after we left Ella and had a quick swim too cool off under the waterfall. Nice location but we didnt spend too much time here as there was much more to explore.

Title: Ravana Falls
Text: Ravana Falls is located in Srilanka. It is in the Ella region of Srilanka. It derived its name after Ravan.

Title: Beautiful waterfalls and watch out for the monkeys
Text:
Amazing waterfalls that can be viewed from the side of the road. Due to past accidents, signs are put up to warn visitors not to climb the rocks. 

Plenty of monkeys there. So dont bring any food or drink there if you are not willing to share with them as the monkeys can get aggressive.

Title: Ravana Water falls
Text: Ravana Water fall is situated on the main road near Ella. Sceneary is very good. Water is falling in to a pool, where all can swim. It was slippery and we have to carefully reach the pool. We enjoyed the bath in the pool. All age group will enjoy the site.

Title: Cool but dirty
Text:
A cool waterfall where you can swim with Kids. Watch out for falls cause the rocks are really sliding. Dont climb the rocks around 40 deaths with this... 
The place need some cleaning there are papers every where that's disgusting.
Local People come also to take a bath so dont be surprise...

Title: Nice water full by the roadside
Text: Long waterfall that goes into a pool where locals and tourists swim and then it goes into another little waterfall.

Title: Ravana Ella Falls
Text: Worth a visit and on the main road if travelling near Ella. The immediate environs are interesting and when we visited it was holiday time for the local children so very busy but interesting none the less.

Title: A nice experience.
Text:
And no, the water is not as cold as youd think :)
Youll pay a tuk tuk driver around LKR1200 to take you down here, wait for you and then bring you back into town. The place is very popular with locals so its a good way of jumping in and mingling. Pack a towel and a dry change of clothes and enjoy the water. Its free and will take you less then half an hour. On the way back to your tuk tuk make sure you buy the chili-dusted mango from the roadside stalls. Absolutely delicious.

Title: Easily accessible
Text:
We took a tuk tuk to the falls which are seen easily from the road. A few street carts and vendors in the area and lots of people bathing in the falls. 

There is a viewing point right off the road to take pictures and you can take a quick rock along the rocks to get to the water pool. 

If you love nature and water falls they are very beautiful.

Title: Very dirty
Text: The fall was very dirty,  ots of plastic bottles/food/rubbish all around and in the water. Nice view from long distance, closer looks not so stunning.

Title: Small place and very busy
Text:
Just next to the road so lot of people go there. The pool is small.
We just had a quick swim and left. At least the water is refreshing after a hiking day.
But Ramboda Falls next to Nuwara Eliya are much better !

Title: Do stop by for just 30 minutes!!
Text:
Just the way the fall has to be amidst the roads and the cars.

Stop by for some good clicks, clean water, some "water-rock-climbing" if you want to risk your limbs and awesome views.

Not sure why is it named Ravana though yet.

Title: Great spot and not to miss out
Text: It was cool and fresh. Easy accessible and lovely place. Its a must if your in Ella, especially if youre hot and need a cold wake up call

Title: Beautiful
Text:
It is easily accessible by road. Very pr6etty.
It is few miles from Ella. people tend to bathe in it.The surrounding areas are breathtakingly beautiful.

Title: Not great.
Text: The falls are not worth viewing. They are not high, the scenery is not interesting, and the water is murky. There are lots of monkeys about that try and steal from you. Some locals were washing in the pool.

Title: Not Sri Lanka's finest
Text: Quite an average waterfall on the way into Ella. Very busy with tourists as well, given proximity to Ella. Ok for a brief stop by car, but I wouldn't waste too much time and energy walking down (and back up) from Ella.

Title: Waterfall
Text: Lovely waterfall only metres from the road.  Can have a swim in the lovely clear water or. Just marvel on such an enormous drop of water (even in the off Season it is still worth a look)

Title: Lovely
Text: Visited whilst passing, you can pull over at the side of the road, there are lots of monkeys who aren't afraid of you or phased  y you, so plenty of photo opportunities and the waterfall itself is beautiful

Title: A nice stop
Text: The waterfall is really nice for a short stop. It's a good idea to visit at the end of an eventful day. There are crowds, and monkeys waiting to steal snacks, but the waterfall is beautiful.

Title: Not as good as Diyaluma Falls
Text: I would recommend going to Diyaluma Falls instead of you can, it is much more impressive that this. But it is still very good but just busy

Title: Good fall with great history
Text: Amazing fall, coming from the rock which is again a great history of Ravana, good place to visit to explore

Title: Beautiful, quick stop
Text: This was a nice quick stop on our way out of Ella. Take a bunch of pictures and then can head out. Beautiful waterfall!!

Title: Wow
Text: Awesome! A lot of water due to monsoon weather well worth the drive not just for the waterfall but for the amazing and dramatic surrounding landscape

Title: Beautiful
Text: The waterfall is beautiful. Some locals are going for a shower there. And there is full of monkeys around it. Children were thrilled.

Title: Another Hotspot of Sri Lanka roundtrip Tour
Text: Must see when you are in/at Ella or passing. Nice big waterfal/fountain with overview point and restaurants

Title: Just another waterfall
Text:
Nothing much.

If you are an avid photographer perhaps you may take very nice and beautiful photos. As for myself, just some snaps and thats it.

Just another waterfall.

Title: Just magnificient
Text: Worth visiting. 15 min drive from Ella city centre. The most popular tourist attraction very close to Ella city centre. U only need max 30 minutes to admire and take photos. You can do easy climb to few metres

Title: Nice and Big
Text: A quick stop at this place on the way to south beaches from ella. Right in the road. Big cascading waterfall, but pretty average one with nothing special or extraordinary. Good for a stopover and photo opportunity.

Title: Cascading gently
Text: More rainfall required to see the waterfall in all it's cascading glory. It was still impressive and a nice view. Our bus was lucky to be allowed navigate the major land-slide between the falls and Ella, the road was being closed as we drove through on the 25/10/19.

Title: Not at its best
Text:
A good size waterfall, but not much water flowing when we were there. It's right beside the road so no long walks. Would have been nice to have a dip in one of the rock pools but didn't have time.
Try the freshly cooked corn whilst there.

Title: One of the famous waterfalls in the island.
Text:
It is like 10-15 mins drive from Ella town. There are public buses passing by the waterfall or one can easily get a tuk-tuk (LKR 1000 as of Oct 2019) for back & forth ride from Ella town.
This 82ft height waterfall is Sri Lanka's one of the famous & beautiful waterfalls. 
It is easily accessible by road and a perfect stop for photos.
Rocks are slippery,so be extra careful if you think of climbing on rocks at the waterfall..
There is a safe viewing deck and no entrance chargers here.

Title: So much fun!
Text:
Wait for the train to go across the bridge / usually 8:30am 

Afterwards you can walk along the track!

Title: Popular falls
Text: Came across these on the way back to our guest house. They are a very popular spot - you can swim here but you are not allowed to jump off the rocks. There wasnt a huge amount of water coming down but you could see where it flows when there has been rain.

Title: A nice little hideout
Text: a small little waterfall which is actually quite grand with the activities all around it. roadside stalls selling fruits and different foodstuff. Need to thread carefully as traffic is pretty heavy with everyone passing by stopping and trying to get a photo. quite refreshing if you can spend a little time to sit by the rocks to enjoy the surrounding

Title: Rad Ravana falls
Text:
This falls can be viewed for persons wheelchair bound. 
This is suitable for all ages. 
We were super lucky to visit these falls after an evening of rain. This meant the falls were banging.
On this day no swimming was allowed in the falls.

Title: Waterfall
Text: Our Tour coach made a brief stop here in passing by on the main road. Certainly worth a photo opportunity, but not the most spectacular of waterfalls. Nonetheless, very popular with many bathers and tourists. Usual array of nearby shops etc.

Title: Nice falls
Text: On your way from Ella to Yala can you not miss this falls. It is at the side of the mainroad. The falls are not spectacular but nice enough to stop for.

Title: Wow!
Text:
Stunning waterfall at the side of the main road. Need transport to get here. Can be crowded but you can get decent photos. 
Worth a visit.

Title: Crowded but beautiful
Text: This waterfall is nice although a bit crowded. Still worth a stop as you can have a swim and it is quite close to Ella as opposed to other options. Please be careful walking on the stones!

Title: Beautiful BUT ........
Text: Lovely waterfall. Quite impressive to be honest. Get there early otherwise your view will be ruined by lots of tourists swimming and bathing in it. Too busy.

Title: You have to see this amazing fall
Text: It's very nice, near from Ella, right on the street, you can't swim to much here, because it's not deep, so just go inside the water and wait under the water when it fall, get cool and you can continue your trip..

Title: Pleasant pit stop
Text:
On a long drive its nice to get a chance to stretch your legs especially when you can view pretty waterfalls like Ravana.

Its even better when there is a school outing and you organise the kids along with their teachers to have a photo..????

Well worth the effort if you have to go out of your way to come here..

Title: Spectacular cascading waterfall..................FREE
Text:
This is a spectacular waterfall right alongside the main road South out of Ella.
The water tumbles down from a great height under a bridge over the river. A couple of mountain stream pools too if you fancy a dip.
Worth a stop or a small detour for sure.
Usual collection of shops nearby for snacks, drinks etc.

Title: Right on the road
Text: Easy, no walking, no detours. En route, on our way between Ella and Tissa there it was...just needed to cross the street. Some people went a little further than just looking at these falls by bathing at the base of them...would have done so if the time permitted and if I had known it was feasible.

Title: Pretty place
Text: Nice waterfall for photos. The bus down the hill from Ella goes frequently there and back much cheaper than a Tuk tuk

Title: Refreshing stop near Ella
Text:
The waterfall is huge. You can see most of it. There is a viewing point on the road itself. Also there is one slightly off road which is safe and has a good view. Before doing any heroics please check the rock beneath you - few are slippery and few are not very stable.
No entry fee!!

Title: Stop for waterfalls on your way to Ella
Text: On our way to Ella from Mirissa, we stopped to see nice and quite big Ravana waterfalls. You should stop and take some good pictures. Some tourists also swim there even though there is a sign it is not allowed. Just a reminder, be aware of lots of monkeys there and dont provoke them.

Title: Place to stop on your way into Ella
Text: We stopped off on our way into Ella as the waterfall is next to the roadside. Its not in the best location but it is beautiful. There is a waterfall above this one too. Its nice when you see it in the hillside as a view from Ella Rock.

Title: Impressive falls
Text: Worth the visit. Some locals take a cold shower on a side stream, part of the custom. When we went it had been raining a lot the day before and the fall was very cold. Great photos

Title: Disappointed
Text: I was a little disappointed with the location of where the Ravena falls was located in the streets. The location wasnt great and the fall was small- not what I was expected at all. But it was still a beautiful scenery to visit

Title: A nice place to stop
Text: Nice point for stopping on the way to/from main Ella road. Beautiful spot, mango and corn served close by the site by locals. Not a must visit.

Title: Beautiful waterfall
Text:
Absolutely stunning waterfall. There is a viewing platform and you can get a bit closer. Really beautiful place to visit

There is a guy there that sells fresh mango, cuts it into wedges and serves wrapped in a leaf. I really do recommend stopping for a snack from him. It was super tasty and price was good

Title: An easy hike for children
Text: The hike to the top of the falls is certainly achievable with young children. Beautiful vistas the entire way and lots of monkeys too.

Title: Pretty falls
Text: Went to see the falls, was really busy when we went so didnt go into the water. There was a lot of people trying to sell us gems etc, so didnt stay too long. Pretty tho

Title: Great on a hot day - especially with kids
Text:
A great spot and definitely worth the tuk tuk to get there.  Take swimmers and enjoy the cool waters. Realtively shallow and safe for kids....other than the slippery rocks :) 

Something to consider. If you're a foreign female consider what you wear - skimpy bikinis not very suitable for the context. There was some very serious oggling going on.  Perhaps consider swimming with a sarong wrap.

Title: Family time
Text: Great place to Visited amazing there is many nice hotels around and restaurant great food safe place

Title: Over crowded area used for showering and bath
Text:
Over crowded area used for showering and bath.
Maybe went at a bad hour but i didn't enjoy the views either.

Title: Not great..
Text: Give it a look as you're driving by, that's more than enough. Was very crowded and it's nice enough but nothing great.

Title: Famous for being dangerous
Text: During our group tour (on the go) we got to see many interesting sites/sights. A pretty enough cascade down the side of a mountain with an outlook over lush green mountains.  Ravanna is famous for two things: 1) nice waterfall and 2) illiterate people dying.  The theory is they must be illiterate because there is a sign in many languages saying with words to the effect of please dont climb on the rocks, they are slippery and you will die. The total so far (also updated regularly on the sign) is 17 people.  On the day we stopped people were climbing on the rocks.  We thankfully left before any of our tour group could get themselves in trouble.

Title: Must see Waterfalls
Text:
It was so amazing that you really need to stop and go down to see this waterfall it was worth your stay in sri lanka to stop and enjoy the beauty of nature together with fresh water. We go in the middle and dip our feet we cannot really take shower coz its so full. 
It was beside the road and it was so full of tourist and locals so it was very difficult for anyone to get a parking area. But we manage to get. 
Well recommended.

Title: Quick photo stop
Text: The place is packed with people. Its a good quick stop for photo taking and enjoying the view of the waterfall. Grab some corn on the cobs on way back to car for LKR50/- each.

Title: Scenic spot for some good photos and monkeys !
Text:
As other reviewers have said, these falls are quite impressive, and probably busy with tourists most of the time.

The view is nice and you can get some good photos, either from a distance or on the falls themselves.

Definitely need to be a bit careful when climbing over the rocks and pools.

There are some stalls where you can buy fruit and corn on the cob, and plenty of cheeky monkeys who you can feed !

Its a bit chaotic with traffic and tourist buses stopping all over the place, but then so is much of Sri Lanka ... but I mean that in a nice way, it all adds to the unique charm of this amazing, beautiful country.

We spent just over half an hour here, and to be honest that's probably all you would need.

If staying in Ella I would recommend a visit here would be on your itinerary.

Title: Very popular
Text:
Clearly, as with all waterfalls, this would be more impressive after rain.  However even in quite a dry period it is quite a tall fall and worth seeing.  We were warned not to clamber over the rocks (as they are dangerous) but the view from the bridge is fine.

The area is busy and is frequented by various hawkers so remain vigilant

Title: Short stop on the way to south
Text: We stayed 1 night in Ella and hired a car to go to Mirissa/Weligama. It is in a short distance from Ella. We could have swam there but just walked to the bottom of the fall. It was a 15-20 minutes stop

Title: Pretty falls
Text: This is an easy stop along the roadside. The falls are so pretty. You can take a short walk from the road to swim in the falls.

Title: Ravana Falls is an extremely busy sightseeing attraction.
Text: Ravana Falls popularly known as Ravana Ella is part of the Ravana Ella Wildlife Sanctuary, and is located approximately 6 km from the local railway station at Ella. The falls are extremely popular with both the locals and the tourists. The car parking areas are very busy. Our guide was keen to tell us that it is currently one of the widest falls in the country. During the local wet season the waterfall is said to resemble an areca flower with withering petals. There are warning signs about bathing.

Title: Great for a look
Text:
Lovely waterfall
 Lots of people having fun in the bottom pool in the sun.  Great stalls selling chopped up mango for when you come out. Some cheeky monkeys were playing out too

Title: Roadside Falls
Text: If driving by, it's worth it to pull over and take a gander at a nice set of falls.  You can wade into a little pool if you like, midway up.  Some monks were bathing there when we stopped.

Title: Beautiful!
Text: Beautiful spot to visit while your in Ella! It's possible to bathe in it so bring your swimsuits! We climbed up the waterfall to be a bit more private,  great view and beautiful fall!

Title: Nice spot
Text: We wanted to go to diyaluma waterfalls on the way we passed from ravana falls and it was nice spot for a see. But not very special.

Title: Beautiful Waterfalls
Text:
The Ravana waterfalls were close to my hotel and a sight to the eye. With lots tourist and spectators, there were small stalls with fresh fruit and corn around the waterfall.
It was a bit slippery and I would recommend to be careful when climbing up the rocks.

Title: Pretty waterfall
Text: Due to the time of year that we visited, there wasnt a lot of water going over the waterfall, but it was still very pretty, although busy with tourists clambering over the rocks and even bathing in one of the small pools.

Title: Amazing site
Text:
Worth the visit a stunning waterfall 
Can get busy due to its beauty 
A few people trying to sell items but a simple no thank you and they leave you along

Title: Famous fall in this area!!!
Text: From Adam peak i went to visit Ravana fall ,it was great tosee a fall in the hot noon. Lot of tourists were out enjoying in the sun. Even though  the water flow was less as it was not a monsoon time but still worth visiting.

Title: Nice stop for a quick photo
Text: A nice photo stop on the way to Ella. Some people were bathing but we just took some snaps and continued. Our driver recommended the caves.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Really beautiful. Even if not the highest or widest I've seen, it is really worth seeing.  The cool,clear water was refreshing too.

Title: Best place to see  in ella
Text: 20 minutes drive from Ella. Thus is one of a beautiful waterfall in sri lanka. If you talk with locals they will tell you  wonderful local stories which related to king Rawna.

Title: Gorgeous falls
Text: Gorgeous falls just 11km away from Ella. They are just by the road so there's no walking needed. There are lots of shops selling water, fruit, boiled corn (delicious) and food. We were there in the dry season and still there was plenty of water.

Title: Time for A Swim
Text: Ravana Falls is the time to photograph the long falls and scenery. It is suggested that you need a guide to do this but TripAdvisor posts were adamant that you don't, but be aware of dodgy locals trying to send you the wrong way and then charging to guide you when you are lost (sadly. they're everywhere in the country)

Title: Good photo opportunity
Text:
This is easily accessible and clearly visible from the main road, so you don't even need to get your toes wet!

We drove to the falls and were a little disappointed to find a parking attendant there asking for a parking fee on the public road!  It was only 50LKR and I noticed all the locals had been issued with the same ticket, so not much, just frustrating.

The falls are impressive and make for some excellent photos, you can even scramble across a small river just by the road to get some close up shots if you desire.

Having driven past on a few occasions during our time in Ella we noticed it always seems busy, so be prepared to have to wait in turn to get the 'perfect' shot!

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text:
Ravana Ella Falls are right by the roadside - on the road between Ella and Wallawaya so an easy stop on your way through.
There had been a bit of rain around the time we had stayed in Ella so the falls were quite impressive.
There were monkeys around when we visited and they happily posed for photos in front of the waterfalls for us!!

Title: Worth a short stop for a quick photo
Text: Not really impressive, Ravana Ella Falls are located just off the road and may be worth a short stop for a quick photo - nothing more.

Title: Feel refreshed just looking.
Text: A very nice short-stop, remind your driver to get a parking ticket, as one feels refreshed just looking at this delightful waterfall and if you are there when there has been no rain you can indulge with a quick dip in one of the fall pools. Do not swim after heavey rain!

Title: Nice
Text: When we in the Srilanka firstly choose to travel to Ella because my friends recommend this.This was nice place . When we reached this place our minds were floating what a beauty

Title: Nothing to write home about
Text: Sure... An impressively long waterfall, but it's over commericalized, access is on the side of the road and it's not really the type of place for a picnic and swim.

Title: Fabulous waterfalls
Text: We hopped on the bus from Ella which took us 6 kms down to where the viewing is for the waterfalls. Very impressive as these are the first waterfalls we have seen. Bought some reasonably priced souvenirs which are hopefully made in Sri Lanka and are not from China

Title: Its on the way, why not..
Text:
Not much to see here, it does seem for adults and older kids you can jump in but its not too spectacular.  Again, its worth a stop because it takes 30 mins but no need to go too far out of way.

Maybe on a hot day, it would be cool to hang out a little and swim but not the best for that.

Title: Gorgeous
Text:
A short scenic drive to the falls with glimpses of precipitous slopes across a spectayfirested valley. The falls consist of a series of cascading falls culminating in a grand pool fit for swimming. Many wee food stalls and roasted corn sellers for another experience. Caution... dozens of people have attempted to scale the cliffs by the falls and have fallen to their deaths. 
Yukon Bil

Title: Beautiful
Text: Our driver Athula stoped nearest this water fall, On the way from Ella to South Coast. I recommend  you pass the Ravana Falls. Get out and enjoy. There are smaller stalls to eat coconut or a corncob. It's worth it!

Title: Beautiful
Text:
We stopped there just fir half an hour because it turned out that swimming there was forbidden. The waterfall is worth to be seen. It's beautiful as all waterfalls, there is something special in all.
Near the waterfall there are some restaurants and next to them is a family of monkeys. I gave away a bunch of bananas. It was nice watching them eating. I gave one of them also a mandarine. It is interesting to see how they also use legs to hold the fruits to make it easier to open.

Title: Great waterfall
Text: A great waterfall. There are few spots where you can take a bath in it however when we visited it was pretty crowded. Also, be careful at the touts near the bridge who try to sell you rocks. They are quite pushy but if you are strictly saying 'no' , they will leave.

Title: Cool spot to pass by
Text:
The falls are nice to look at for a few minutes when passing thru this road on our way from Ella to Udawalawe. All drivers I feel like ask if we want to stop for a few so you won't miss it. 

Don't think it was anything special to make a separate trip to come see it though. 

There were monkeys nearby as well!

Title: Beautiful waterfall
Text: The lower part of the Ravana falls is nice with a swimming area at the bottom. However, the lower part is quite crowded and surrounded by street side gift shops and tuk tuk stands, which tarnished the natural feel of the water falls. For those seeking some serenity and a more natural feel, perhaps go to the upper ravana falls, although this is harder to get to.

Title: Holiday
Text:
Right next to the road and a very busy spot but so wonderful to sit with your legs in the cool water. Even tho there wasnt supposed to be much water around, it was running fast.

The only spot so far in Sri Lanka where we have been hassled - guys asking for money for their daughters in return for a few semi precious (??) stones and that wasnt too bad.

Title: Dramatic Ella´s falls
Text: If you stay in any of Ella´s guesthouses, you will most probably have view over this waterfall from your window, so I don´t really find it necessary to undertake trip to visit the falls unless you want to stand below it and watch dramatic amounts of water descending down the valley which most likely won´t be possible anyway, cause it is pretty busy touristic location. Beautiful place though.

Title: Excellent access
Text: We visited the falls on our way from Uda Walawe to Ella and they're right next to the road. The antics of the monkeys were enjoyable.

Title: A Majestic Waterfall
Text: A majestic waterfall which flows down a very steep mountain to the river below . The best views can be from the road but one has to be careful with the passing traffic.

Title: Busy, yet enjoyable!
Text: Great place to have a break! Quite busy, but enjoyable experience. Lovely rambutan fruits sold on the road when we were there in January, even in not in its season.

Title: Well worth a visit in the way by to Ella
Text: We were driving past so stopped to admire the view. Its pretty impressive al be it lots of people but a good stop in the way to ella with lots of local food stalls

Title: right on the highway
Text: I walked from Ella to this waterfall, it's easy to get to. You know when you're close, as there are a number of stalls selling souvenirs for the hordes of tourists.

Title: Relaxing and amazing view
Text: Breathtaking view , amazing rooms and the best breakfast ... look no more because this is the place for you !!

Title: Worth stopping on the way to Ella
Text: When we travelled from Yala, we stopped in this waterfall. Its so beautiful to watch from the road side. Great place to take some pictures. Would recommend anyone passing

Title: Beautiful waterfall
Text: Plan to go when you pass by taxi, but just plankning to go here might not be the first choice. We did on our way out from Ella, and it was nice to view.

Title: Road side stop
Text:
Be prepared to jostle for space.

You will arrive from a windy road and it Ill be just off the main road.

Its a beautiful site and you should spend no more than 10 minutes there.

Title: Nice spot to stop
Text: Average waterfall. Nice spot to take photos. Watch out for oncoming traffic when crossing the road. worth spending 10 minutes

Title: A quick stop
Text: A quick stop en route to Yala. An impressive roadside waterfall with a few local food stalls. Nothing more to it than that. Photo stop.

Title: Scenic
Text:
Nice falls on your way out or in to Ella depending on which way you are coming. 
Great picture opportunities.

Title: Very touristy!
Text: The waterfall itself is really nice but so many tourists taking photos it ruins it slightly. Id go out out of season or just not at peak time as you wont get a good view and its just selfies and camera phones

Title: Beautiful, Amazing.
Text:
Ravana Waterfall is a popular sightseeing attraction in Sri Lanka. It is currently ranks as one of the widest falls in the country. The falls have been named after the legendary king Ravana, which is connected to the famous Indian epic, the Ramayana. According to legend, it is said that Ravana, who was the king of Sri Lanka at the time had kidnapped Queen Sita, and had hidden her in the caves behind this waterfall, now simply known as the Ravana Ella Cave.

The Ravana Waterfall can be viewed from the roadside. People try and climb the rocks for a closer view which is not advisable. As told by my Tuk Tuk driver, there were some death cases of tourist who tried to climb up the waterfall. The water is very cooling and you can take a bath if you want, but no place to change clothing. 

Tuk Tuk Driver Name: Jeewantha Madushan
Tuk Tuk Driver Contact: +94711296224

*** He charge at a very reasonable rate which will amaze you, check it out with him if you have some itinerary planned.

Title: nice stop on the road
Text: Good place to pull over, take a couple of snap shots and move on. I am not sure I would make it a destination, but definitely snapshot worthy

Title: Mersmerising experience!
Text: The experience of viewing and listening to the Ravana Ella Falls for me and my friends turned out to be nothing less than a mersmerising.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We visited Ravana Ella Falls on a holiday visit to Sri Lanka. This is one of the good water falls that always have water so you wont be disappointed. But dont expect great amenities at the site. At the moment most visitors see the water fall from the road. That said we saw a viewing platform is being built next to the bridge. The place offers a great opportunity to take some memorable photos.

Title: Great cascades
Text: Close to main road and rocks can be slippy so tale care but the falls are pretty and worth a stopoff on the way to the next venue.

Title: Nice waterfall
Text: The waterfall is only around 6ks from Ella and you can catch a bus there from the main bus stop. I think it is definitely worth a visit it was a very nice waterfall and easy to get too, no hiking nessecary!

Title: Easy to access
Text:
The falls are straight off the road so easy to get to from ella via busses heading to Wellawaya that frequent past. Local tuk tuk drivers tend to offer extortionate rates and the drive there is very bumpy so unless you are in a hurry, taking a bus is the more savy option. 

I wouldnt recommend you swim there. Though some brave people give it a go. There is a sign mentioning swimming not recommend, 36 deaths to date. 

Early morning or late afternoons are better for people who dont want to wait too long for that perfect insta pose location. Otherwise you might be waiting in a long line and share your space with lots of others.

Title: Good if you are passing
Text: If you are driving this road they are well worth stopping by and taking some photo's, not sure I would travel very far to see them though unless I had  alot of time on my hands.

Title: Worth stopping at  as you drive past  or a visit if you have lots of time
Text:
The rocks and shape of the falls are lovely
Enjoyed a quick stop and  you can paddle your feet in a pool
Unfortunately there are sellers that hassle visitors  and ask for foreign  coins  for there children
Which some of the others want to sell back to you
Interesting small scam

Title: Didn't impress me much!!
Text: This place is overrated in my point of view. Didn't impress me at all!! Have been to more interesting waterfalls.

Title: Crazy water fall with nice photogenic location
Text: A lovely waterfall with photogenic landscape for perfect selfi as well groupfie. My guide insist me to climb upwards as he goes little high but I don't try for personal safety. A lot of tourists and local are there. Some picnic and school tour parties also be there enjoying there trips. I loved that place very much. But a lots of monkey also present disturbing time to time ....!!

Title: Lovely swim, until it began to rain!
Text: A lovely waterfall, but the guard would not let us climb up, (for our own safety, I am sure!) and there were not many people here. When the rain began they got us out of the water which began to rise quickly! A short bus ride (two stops) from town, or negotiate with a tuk-tuk.

Title: Cozy but not uniqu
Text: if you have extra time, do pass by. Its a nice scenery, and with a local twist (Locals coming by to do their baths) it has some charm for sure. But rather tough to get to the waterfall if u aint completely mobile

Title: Nice little stop
Text: Nice little stop in our way out of Ella.  The place had a nice viewing platform so you can take pictures.  Unfortunately the water level was low so there wasnt a large water falls as one would have expected to see.  Its quirky and you can walk onto the rocks and if you are lucky the monkeys will escort you.  Definitely worth a stop if you are planning to visit Ella.

Title: Only worth a stop if passing with time
Text: The waterfall was pretty but very crowded with locals swimming and washing, and just off a busy road so there wasnt much chance to relax and admire the view - it was a bit chaotic!

Title: Worth a stop
Text: lovely waterfall although sadly spoilt by the rubbish left by tourists.  I even saw a dirty nappy that some thoughtless parent had left.

Title: Worth a stop when leaving Ella
Text:
We parked up on our way through leaving Ella. Its not worth a day trip there as its literally a waterfall on the side of the road but its pretty and another thing seen at Ella when passing by.
A few kids had a splash but its a quick photo opportunity and off you go.
Note - do not stop on the zebra crossing as the police will fine you as our taxi driver found out!

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text: the waterfall flows from a spring  and people swim in some of the pools. Lots of food vendors with fresh BBQ corn and fruit drinks

Title: Very picturesque
Text: Beautiful waterfall which had a pretty good torrent in late April and is definitely worth a brief visit (we saw it on the way to Udawalawa National Park). A lovely family of friendly monkeys lives nearby!

Title: Not much to see
Text: Unfortunately not much to see here. We drove past it and saw what we needed. Wuite busy with vehicles, Sri Lankans and tourists. No need to stop whilst driving last as what you see from the road appears to be it. Much better to go to Diyaluma and endure the hikexuo to enjoy the views from there.

Title: Worth a look
Text: As a part of a day Tuk TUK trip around about t we came here, wish I had packed the swimmers for the water hole

Title: Beautiful
Text:
The falls is big and beautiful, it was fairly close to our accommodation by car, by walk from there would be probably 40-45min.

When we were there (just a week ago) there was a festival, therefore, was a lot of people. If would have been less people we could have swim as well and if you have the chance you should. The fall itself is beautiful, there are a few stalls selling souvenirs and water. Also, can park by the road.

Title: Worth a stop if you're passing by
Text: This place is certainly worth a stop if you're passing by, but I definitely wouldn't pay a tuk tuk to take me there. Yes it's impressive, yes it's beautiful, but it was packed with people, and there's really no place to just sit and soak in the feel of the place. Five or ten minutes, a few photos, and you're on your way. On the plus side, it's free. Also, I rode there from Ella on a scooter, and the ride itself was beautiful, enjoyable ride even without a waterfall. Beware of the beggers and of the snack sellers. I was charged an absolutely extortionist price on a coconut and some roti. One last note - some people hike in to the top of the falls. Perhaps this would've been a better experience?

Title: Quite nice
Text: We went there as it was in the way to our hostel. It's good to see and it would be even possible to swim in it - even though this is not recommended

Title: Enjoy the mist
Text: Ravana's Waterfall (free) is also place one can spend more than an hour. It's loud waterfall which rocky access where you can get sprayed with fine mist. Don't just take pictures from road, get on rocks, touch the water, get sprayed! Enjoy the corn on cob and fruit platter on road side.

Title: Well worth a stop and see
Text: Easy to find along the main road, it's well worth a short stop to take in this natural wonder of nature. The views across from the falls are worth a stop in itself

Title: Nice falls to take bath in
Text: These falls are just beside the road and you can stop by to just view the falls or have a bath in it. There was enough water to enjoy a bath in the water fall. But do watch out on rainy days, not always advisable to have bath

Title: A simple but beautiful place
Text:
It is situated in Ella, Sri Lanka, which is my home country.
it is a beautiful waterfall though not a very big one.

Title: Brief stop here
Text: If you are lucky enough to pass this on the route into Ella, get your driver to stop. You will only need 5 minutes, so to watch a swath of amusing locals and tourists scream and shout as they shower under the freezing cold water of the famous water fall spout. Unless you really want to p3ss off your driver and your wife, don't join them, as it leads to a clammy and therefore uncomfortable journey to the top of the high street.

Title: It is on private estate
Text: We wanted to go there. But it is on a private estate so we could not go there. It was not very clear that that was the case, and the locals where not that helpful.

Title: Nice 30 min walk along railway tracks
Text: Take a leisurely walk along the railway tracks to the top of the falls. Plenty of photo ops. A train will pass about every hour to 90 mins for extra photo and video moments

Title: Uncrowded
Text: Worth the effort (walk). Almost had the place to ourselves. Pretty.  Once we arrived at the top a local guided us part way down the face and then up the opposite side of the valley to a great  viewing point.

Title: Coll
Text:
Cool but not as cool as I expected.   Was told you could swim here but Im pretty sure its impossible.  
Worth a visit.

Title: Worthwhile stop
Text: We stopped here on our way from Ella to Unawatuna and it was a worthwhile stop. It was very picturesque and we could climb onto some rocks for better views. Pretty waterfall and worth a visit.

Title: Tourist hot spot
Text: Triple overcrowded by food stalls, tourists and cars. Wear adequate footwear otherwise you cant reach the top or simply avoid going there.&

Title: Nice stop
Text: This was a very nice waterfall. Toque Macaques everywhere! Warning signs about dangerous rocks!!!! Great for photo opts. Souvenirs sold along the road.

Title: Serene falls
Text: It is believed that Ravana his Sita from her husband Ram in a cave behind these falls. These falls can be viewed from the roadside.People try and climb the rocks for a closer view which is not advisable as a display board cautions against this and put a the number of people who have died attempting to climb the rocks at 36 as of date.

Title: Nice but theres not much there
Text: Nice waterfall, easily accessed right by the side of the road. But once youve got out of the car and taken a couple of photos, thats really all there is. Worth a visit if youre in the vicinity, but dont go out of your way too far.

Title: Stunning
Text:
Yes of course there are a lot of tourists, it's an incredible piece of nature!!! Go there to see this natural phenomenon and appreciate it for what it is instead of complaining about the tourists. If the tourism is such a huge issue for you then visit in the morning 8am. We arrived before 9 and there was nobody there, other tourists started arriving from 9:30ish. 
This isn't a 'day out' thing, you can't swim in the main part of the waterfall, it's just a passing site which is truly beautiful and well worth a quick detour. Also, the bus from Ella is 25-30 rupee, roughly 20 minutes. (You can get any bus leaving Ella south)

Title: not bad
Text: if you are leaving Ella and have some times it worth to go there, but nothing special. also can buy there some mango and corn. thats all!

Title: Beautiful but only in rain season
Text: Worth to see it, only don't have big expectations when going in dry season as the fall dries out and is not as much spectacular.

Title: Nice falls filthy surrounds
Text: How hard would it be to just pick up the litter and rubbish surrounding a beautiful area in your country?? It's worth a stop but be aware you'll see beauty and rubbish equally.

Title: Touristy
Text: Very scenic falls but very touristy. Touts selling stones of some kind were very persistent. But it's probably the most accessible attraction in the area, an easy bus or tuk tuk ride down the hill from the town.

Title: Beautiful!!
Text: A beautiful waterfall nestled in the mountains!! A lot of tourists around but it is understandable!!

Title: Get there early - its crazy crowded. Avoid the dog poo too
Text: We stopped here on the way from Nuwara Eliya. Like some others say, it is a beautiful place but if you get there at 10am like us, you will have to  fight your way through 500 people to get to it. Dont get me wrong, everyone is super friendly and they help you cross the rocks to the waterfall. The biggest memory I will take away with me though is treading barefoot in a fresh dog poo laid only minutes ago as it was still wet. Nice that a local dog decided of all places to go it picked the narrow path to the falls. I actually commend this dog for its pin-point accuracy. Luckily I wasnt far away from water to rinse my feet before I started wretching and ruining this wonder of nature for everyone. Would I come back yes, with a poop scoop.

Title: Beautiful
Text: I had a chance to visit the famous Ravana Falls in Ella during the month of January. I was visiting Ella with my friends, and when we were leaving from Ella towards the Udawalawe sanctuary, we decided to stop by the falls. The falls are beautiful and especially in January when the waters were more free flowing than during the rest of the year. The falls are of mythological significance for me, so I was truly delighted to have been able to come here. It is believed in Hindu mythology that Ravana had abducted and kept Sita in the cave behind the falls. The falls are crowded so do plan your visit, keeping in mind that there are many locals and tourists here. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: It's a little, crowded waterfall
Text: We visited the waterfall in the afternoon by driving there with a Tuck Tuck. It is a very small one and after a few minutes you have seen everything expect of course if you want to swim in the tidy "pool" under the waterfall. It was also very crowded so that we were not able to take very nice pictures. If you need to fill your day with some activities visit it but you're missing not a lot if you're not going...

Title: Cant climb to the higher pools anymore
Text: We arrived and saw that there was tape around the rocks leading up to the higher pools. Another couple tried to climb over and was chased by a policeman, who brought them back down. Seems too many people have been careless, and theyve got fed up of tourists killing themselves. Shame really, as it looked much more peaceful up there. Go to one of the other falls instead.

Title: Whirlwind stop
Text: Pretty waterfall, again touts trying to sell you stuff and ask for $ or £. On a main road which isnt very pretty but the valley and surroundings are fab.

Title: Nice waterfall.
Text:
We were contemplating walking here from Ella, but figured we can catch a bus instead to save time. Just take 998 service from Ella for 35 LKR per person and you're there in 25mins.

The waterfall itself is really cool and high. Great place to make pictures for your holiday album.

Title: Nice falls, quite far out if town
Text: We visited on the public holiday of Deepawali and it was busy. But not so busy as to be diminished. The falls are certainly impressive, as was the family of monkeys hanging out there waiting to be fed! But I am not convinced the falls are worth the 10 kilometre round trip by foot from Ella along the busy road that is the only access.

Title: Quick visit - but a must-do, don't miss!
Text: This is a *spectacular* waterfall - sure, it's not super famous or going to break records, and there's not a lot to do there beyond take a few photos & have a quick explore (e.g. no trails) - but it's really picturesque and it's so, so easy to do from Ella, being a short tuk tuk ride away. Pop down there for a quick visit, take in the stunning sight - both from the road and then nearer the waterfall - then head back :) A must-see when in Ella!

Title: Quick visit - but a must-do, don't miss!
Text: This is a *spectacular* waterfall - sure, it's not super famous or going to break records, and there's not a lot to do there beyond take a few photos & have a quick explore (e.g. no trails) - but it's really picturesque and it's so, so easy to do from Ella, being a short tuk tuk ride away. Pop down there for a quick visit, take in the stunning sight - both from the road and then nearer the waterfall - then head back :) A must-see when in Ella!

Title: Nothing much
Text: The falls are great but there isnt like a walk around them or anything, its a very quick visit and in a tuk tuk from Ella can cost up to 1500 LKR return which just didnt seem worth it. You can climb a few rocks and get photos of the waterfalls from slightly different angles, but the best photo is just from the road on the bridge, so it would probably be best just stopping on your way to or down from Ella.

Title: Really nice waterfall on the way to Ella
Text:
The waterfall was 2km away from my hostel and on my way to Ella, so I decided to give it a try and visit the Ravana Falls.
It's free and there are a lot of small food and souvenir dealers in front where you can buy fresh fruits, drinks and rocks/souvenirs.
The waterfall itself is impressive and very powerful. Wouldn't take a bad in there.

Title: Awesome... Lill bit crowd
Text: Awesome view and good spot for all photographers. However, it's bit crowded with sellers and dogs. Be careful when u walk around, cause you might step on a dog ????.... !!

Title: Beautiful falls
Text: Had a quick stop to look at the falls on our way out of Ella.  Nice falls easily accessible from the road lots of monkeys and guys trying to sell us rocks, wouldnt leave us alone!  Worth a stop!

Title: The sellers here are over the top intrusive.
Text: Got out of the car and had a seller shoving Crystal's into my pocket as a "free" gift. Yeah right wanted Aussie dollar coins for the free Crystal's. This place is the typical overrun tourist destination. Crowded and full of sellers. What a shame, the falls themselves are very beautiful, it would be nice to view them in peace!

Title: Spectacular Falls.
Text: Easy to find as they are very close to the road south out of Ella and are worth seeing. Water crashes down from quite a height. Parking on the road side is easy.

Title: Nice spot
Text:
While heading to Tissamaharama, we stopped by the road and watch the waterfall.
Be careful not to go down on the slippery road, also be careful from the guys who have a basket of mineral rock and he want to sell, he is very mean. Our driver warm us before we get out of the van, so we didn't had problems with them.

Title: Nice waterfall
Text: This is yet another good waterfall in the hills of Sri Lanka. Visible from the road and well worth a stop if passing.

Title: TOWERING FALLS!
Text: This is definitely a must visit location. We visited this place twice and of course got ourselves wet! To experience the rush and speed of water,is to dip yourself in..Unlike other waterfalls,bathing is possible once you step foot.No 1 in terms of beauty and height

Title: Worth stopping to see this
Text:
We stopped here on our drive from Nuwara Eliya to Galle. The Falls were quite spectacular - as it's the wet season there was plenty of water flowing.
There's a good local restaurant nearby. 
Look out for beggars, there's several all with a unique way of separating you from your money.

Title: Breathtaking views
Text: A beautiful view - picturesque. There is a tea shop across the road which sells a variety of tea to choose from.

Title: Picturesque Location
Text: One can visit this waterfall on the way from Nuwara Eliya to Bentota. A beautiful place for view of waterfalls, tea gardens, mountain railway together. The Viewing spot also offers local pineapple, war mango from local vendors with mouthwatering spices.

Title: Lovely for a quick stop
Text: Easy to take photos of this lovely waterfall from the roadside. The St Clair Falls are on the same road as the Devon Waterfalls - very close together - only short car ride between the two.

Title: Beautiful sight on the main road
Text: During our journey from Nuwara Eliya to Colombo, we did en route visit to St Clair's fall and it was a great and refreshing site.

Title: On the way sight
Text: This is nothing more than a sight that you can see on the way. This is not something you have to take a journey to see. This is quite easily visible from the main road. Its a nice scenic spot for nature lovers and photographers.

Title: Beautiful
Text: This is probably the most scenic and accessible waterfall of the many you will see along the Hatton-Talawakele Hwy.

Title: Picturesque water fall
Text: This picturesque water fall is located on the Hatton- Nuwara Eliya road. There is a good viewing point with parking.

Title: Brilliant scenary
Text: Our driver stopped at St Clair's Falls on our way back to colombo. Wow what a view. The scenary is breathaking. Across the road was a beautiful tea shop which sold some of the tea St Clair's tea factory produces. Proper parking spaces and not just at the side of the road. If you get a chance stop here and soak up the lovely views

Title: Classical waterfall with a high view.
Text: You can treak to the waterfall but wear good shoes. I took a tuk-tuk up to 2/3 height. After that access only by foot. Worth the effort. Don't forget a rain jacket.

Title: Lovely waterfall
Text: We stopped here by chance on our way around Sri Lanka. Beautiful waterfall with fantastic lush, green scenery. Worth a stop to have a look.

Title: Stunning, even from a distance
Text: We made a quick pit stop on our drive from Hatton to the train station in Nuwara Eliya. While we only saw St. Clair's Falls from a distance we could still appreciate the beauty. Great quick and scenic stop!

Title: Beautiful!!
Text: We had a great time looking at the falls and also having a cup of freshly made tea! Great place to stop and have a nice look at the water fall, it is breathtaking!

Title: Very beautiful location way to Nuwaraeliya near by Thalawakele
Text: Obviously very beautiful location way to Nuwaraeliya near by Thakawakele. This is very famous waterfall and travellers are loving St Claire. Rainning season it's become more beauty than others.

Title: viewing waterfalls via traveling to nuwara eliya
Text: we stopped by the roadside to get some quick snaps of this famous waterfall which looked monstrous because of the rain in the hills. this is one of the many waterfalls you get to see when travelling to nuwara eliya.

Title: Nice viwe
Text:
It having a nice view and good landscape appearance of the water falls 
At the time of rain the falls became large 
Just by standing there you will feel relaxed

Title: Potential
Text: Unfortunately I thought because we had heavy rain for an hour in Kandy this would result in increased water flow in the mountains but this was not to be. It is still worth a look to imagine what it would look like with heaps of water coming down.

Title: Wide and picturesque falls visible from the roadside.
Text:
St. Clairs falls is visible from a roadside lookout point on the Hatton-Talawakele road going to Nuwara Eliya. The falls themselves are somewhat diminished to damming upriver but flow should improve with rains.
The lookout point is on a blind curve of the road. Be aware of approaching vehicles from both directions if crossing the road to get to the beautiful St. Clairs tea Center located just across from the lookout point. Climbing to few steps to the Tea Center provides a better vantage point to view the falls and also provides the opportunity to purchase tea grown directly on the adjoining St. Clairs tea estate. Delectable. sit down and have a cup on the porch outside and enjoy the view.

Title: A visual treat and soothing
Text: VEry close to travel point, nothing very great but the vast expanse of greenery makes it a soothing sight

Title: Nice photo stop on way down from nuwara Eliya
Text: We called in at the observastion point for these falls on the way down from Nuwara Eliya. You can park and get out on a viewing platform for a couple of scenic photos. 5-10 mins  max stay

Title: Museum and falls
Text: Right next to Devon falls another beautiful falls. By to roads there is designated view points. You may visit the museum just one stairs below the view point. You dont have to pay to enter the museum. Tea gardens are all around the place.

Title: St. Clair's Fall
Text: One of the many waterfalls you see when you are driving towards Nuwara Eliya; when the weather is good you can stop along the road to make some nice pictures. It is, however, not possible to visit this waterfall.

Title: Beautiful waterfall
Text: One of the most famous falls in SL. Doesn't have the amount of water it had running through it as there is a dam up in the river.

Title: Unexpected Great view
Text: Unexpected Great view , beautifull and all..worth passing by ( anyways since its onee the way down from nuwara ) . Still its not magistic in size...its just picturistic

Title: Great View
Text: Srilanka is a place for many waterfalls. St. Clair's Falls is one of the falls. Falls depend on the season and timing of the Dams. This was created when the Kotmale Hydro Power Plant Dam was built. A lovely view from the view point. The roads that lead to the dams are too good. Beautiful smooth and very winding roads. Lots of places to photograph. The tea gardens surrounding the falls are lovely. There are some lovely cottages/hotels which overlook the falls and they must be getting wonderful views. Though it rained everyday but the water on the falls were not vast. Still it looked beautiful. The view points had several floors and one can easily get down to the tea gardens and other places for taking photographs. During the rainy season, one has to be careful with the leaches in the garden, and in the bush. No entry fee needed.

Title: Beautiful waterfall but carry an insect repellent
Text: This is one of the most scenic waterfalls in Sri Lanka. There will be leeches during the wet season. Please make sure to carry an insect repellent if you walk towards the waterfall. This location can be accessed by public transport. Please be aware of unauthorised travel agent conman. Always organise your trips with the hotel you stay or use public transport. The public transport weren't that great.

Title: WOW
Text: Breathtakingly beautiful, saw one of many similar to this and they were all fantastic... SLR at the ready.

Title: Impressive (at least from afar!)
Text: We saw the falls from quite far off but they looked very impressive. We had lunch at the viewpoint. It was OK, but not much choice. The view was excellent.

Title: Broad and beautiful
Text: Unlike the other falls this is falling in steps and it is quite broad and looks like milk flowing down .. very nice view

Title: St Clair's Falls
Text: We stopped enroute from Nuwara Eliya to view the falls. The water levels were low at the time so the falls were not very spectacular.

Title: I saw it from the tea castle
Text: I had my lunch in tea castle while enjoying the waterfall from a little bit far away. I did not get close to it but it seems nice

Title: Breathtaking
Text: We didn't go close to the falls but stopped at a viewing point. Worth seeing. I'm not sure how close you can get.

Title: Beautiful falls!!!
Text: Very beautiful waterfalls on the Hatton - Nuwara Eliya road, near Talawakele.  Great view point and rest area built a few years ago, also includes a small "museum" that provides information on the Upper Kotmale Hydropower Dam that has been built upstream from the falls.  Also a small restaurant there.  Definitely worth a stop!

Title: This is on the road Hatton - Nuwara Eliya
Text: Very beautiful water fall can be seen on our way to Nuwara Eliya via Hatton.  Beautiful once the water level is high or rainy season.

Title: A spot of tea?
Text: During the rainy season, this area is an emerald gem!  There are a couple of places to stop and have a cup of tea and cake.  The views are spectacular.  I keep finding myself back to this place, still after 14 years of annual visits to the country.

Title: Nice part  of the beautiful countryside in Nuwara Eliya area
Text: We were on a tour bus en route to the Pedro Tea Gardens and stopped to photograph this lovely part of the local scenery. It's not a "knockout" but it is quite beautiful.

Title: dramatic
Text: Some of the best views of any of the multiple waterfalls in the tea trails area.  I wish I had hiked in the area.

Title: Attractive water fall
Text: Our guide explained that the large hydroelectric plant only a mile or so upstream had hugely reduced the water flow. One can understand why Sri Lanka felt the need for such a project but , looking st pre dam photos, the impact is sizeable turning a major attraction into one that is pleasant. Progress?

Title: Waterfall is pretty far
Text: This site is good for taking photographs but the waterfall was not very exciting. It was far and seems not too big. Maybe because the height of this point is more than that of waterfall. As this takes only 10-15 mins, you can take a stop while traveling from Nuwara Eliya to Bentota

Title: Fantastic setting
Text: A lovely view in fantastic countryside. A perfect photo opportunity from a stopping point nearby. I understand it's even better when the water is more prominent

Title: Spectacular
Text: Even though we viewed these falls in a very dry period of weather they still looked spectacular. It is easy to see the falls from the main road so you don't have a long walk to enjoy them.

Title: Impressive.
Text:
We stopped by here after a long drive. It was worth it as it was an amazing view. 

Very good spot for a selfie or a group photo if that is your thing.

Title: nice sight!
Text: Nothing much to write. Its a 5 min stop on your way back from Nuwara Eliya. Looks pretty and makes for a decent picture.

Title: impressive sight
Text:
Perfect stop to stretch the legs and admire the view from the main road opposite the falls with an impressive outlook
Part of the attraction was the energetic boy tempting us to buy delicious mango from a roadside stall which we couldn't refuse. After the mango sale he pulled out a variety of souvenirs to sell. Points for trying.

Title: Spectacular Scenary
Text: You should not miss this spectacular scenery when you travel from Colombo to Nuwaraeliya on Talawakelle Road.

Title: A view from far
Text:
Nice falls but water seemed scarce at the time of my visit. It is close to Nuwara Eliyia and very close to the Devon waterfalls as well. The scenery around the falls and all the tea tress make it a pretty site for some pictures despite the low water volume. There are stairs that seem to take you down closer to the falls, I doubt they would take you all the way there, but I didn't try. 

These falls shouldn't be a destination on their own, but definitely nice to see if you are in the area.

Title: Worth a quick photo stop
Text: En route out of nuweriya eliya we stopped at the viewpoint . Nice pretty waterfall worth a quick stop...

Title: Beautiful small waterfall
Text:
You will see the fall from the street. Although small, it is very beautiful. It is surrounded by grass land. 
There is a small path that supposedly go to the waterfall but the path actually stop somewhere in the middle. The view there is actually less beautiful than the view from the street. So what I am saying is: no point to go down that path.

Title: Nice looking falls
Text: It will be great if one could go closer to it. But from distance it looks beautiful and large. This is one of many water falls in this city.

Title: On the way to Nuwara Eliya
Text: If you take the road via Hatton to Nuwara Eliya this is one of the spectacles you can enjoy. (Not the route via Kandy). One of the widest waterfalls of Sri Lanka, clearly visible from the main road. If you need to go closer you need to trek through the forest.

Title: Not what the pictures show but very nice
Text: We were told that a recent power project have made the water levels of st Claire falls to be less than normal. Most certainly the waterfall isn't what the picture show but it's a wonderful sight nonetheless .

Title: Breathtaking view
Text: St.Clair's falls viewpoint is a stopover on your way down to Colombo from Nuwara Eliya. We stopped by here early morning at 6 and had this wonderful view. The falls though didn't have much water flow at that time. The view of the valley with the waterfall in the centre is breathtaking. The step like falls would look even more beautiful with full waterflow. It's really worth taking a stopover!

Title: Truly beautiful
Text: Surely a place to stop on your way. It's more prettier during the rainy season when the dam gates are opened. You can go down the step near the falls for a better experience

Title: A necessary waterfall stop
Text: One of the very beautiful waterfalls in Sri Lanka. Its a must to stop if your travelling you way to the hill country. Perfect weather and an amazing scenery. Good for photographers, artists etc etc.

Title: St Clair's Falls
Text: Most scenic place for a stopover and clicking some pics. Picturesque scenes like this makes ideal postcards.

Title: Nice viewing point
Text:
The perks about this tea shop is its location. It is situated right opposite Devons Fall so it has its own viewing deck which overlooks the beautiful fall and the valley of Nuwara Eliya.  St Clairs, a brand which is already familiar to me before my visit here, but never knew about its origin. Here we are, at the centre of where it originates from (for its Ceylon Tea). The tea shop has its own charming garden, where you can have a sip of tea overlooking the beautiful Devons Fall.

 

It is here where we bought our most craved crafted tea that I first encountered during my stay in The Westin Palace Madrid. This tea is really special whereby all the tea leaves and some flowers are being crafted by hand, so that you brew it in a hot water, it blossoms into a pretty flowers. In this case, a rose. It is probably the most expensive. Not only the fact that it is artistically handcrafted, but it is also made out of the highest quality tea leaves  which is the silver tip and golden tip tea leaves. We got it here for 1800Lakhs (RM60) for only 6 pieces.

 

This tea centre is more accurately located at Tawakelle. It is the perfect stop over especially if you are on route between Colombo  Nuwara Eliya. It is not as big as Macwood and Bluefield but it sure has its own old planters charm from 100years ago. After a massive tea shopping here (and our last tea shopping for this trip), we continued our journey to Hakgala Botanical Garden.

Title: stair of water
Text: Sri Lanka is a country rich with waterfalls once again on our way from Nuwara eliya we had a halt on the highway facing st.clair's waterfall. It got its name from a tea estate located near it. and all those waterfalls are almost in central province of sri lanka near nuwara eliya which is thousands meters above the sea level and the weather is almost rainy.

Title: gd
Text: another beautiful falls in the midst of green rich hills . its a sight of behold and click goreat pictures with your loved onces .

Title: Waterfall Trek
Text: Steep Hike upto the waterfall. Wish there were better washrooms. Pathway made along most of the way. Good place if you like a small hike and splash of water. But nothing outstanding

Title: Most Beautiful Place in Sri Lanka!!!
Text: It is said to be one of the the most beautiful places in Sri Lanka. We are totally convinced upon visiting the St Clair Tea Plantation Estate with beautiful waterfall where can be watched from multi-tiered viewing platforms. There is a restaurant at the viewing platform too. The landscape in the surroundings and the journey going to this place from Nuwara Eliya are full of beautiful views and greenery. Lovely place and a must visit for nature lovers!!! Hiring driver its necessary to this place with approximately an hour drive as we engaged BLUE HAVEN TOURS with superb driver called Mr Sugath. Two thumbs up to this wonderful place!!!

Title: DAMN THAT DAM
Text: Known as the Little Niagara of Sri Lanka, it is one of the widest waterfalls in the country. It consists of the Greater Fall of 80m or 260 and the Lesser Fall of 50m or 160. The falls are near the Upper Kotmale Dam. The government promised to release a set level of water between sunrise and sunset. The viewing platform is a fair distance away but a zoom lens does the trick.

Title: nice
Text: it's nice to stop when you are on the way.. but no need to make an extra way to see them. It's a Waterfall like many others too but nice for a picture

Title: Waterfall views from the road
Text: Great little scenic stop to get out and stretch your legs whilst taking in the view of the waterfall.

Title: Lovely photo opportunity
Text: These falls tumble over a set of rocks before dropping into a pool which produces another waterfall. Set in a scenic area amongst the tea plantations resulting in a lovely photo opportunity.

Title: Picturesque view
Text: We stopped at this location to enjoy the scenery and the good view with the waterfall in the background. The place was very packed with many young people taking selfies.

Title: Nature's Gift
Text:

Title: The "Little Niagara of Sri Lanka" is now a shadow of its former glory
Text:
This was once a really beautiful waterfall that was known as the "Little Niagara of Sri Lanka" but is now quite small thanks to a hydroelectric project that has curtailed the flow of water.

St Clair's Falls was apparently the widest waterfall in Sri Lanka and has 2 drops, totalling about 74 metres. It is on St Clair tea estate, both of which were named after the wife of the first pioneer tea planter's son, a beautiful lady whose name was Clair.

The waterfall is at an elevation of 1,200 metres and is part of the Kotmale Oya. It can be seen from the Hatton to Talawakelle road.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Zoo at Dehiwala, Colombo: One of the best Zoo in the World
Text:
National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka (also called Colombo Zoo or Dehiwala Zoo) is a zoological garden in Dehiwala, Sri Lanka, founded in 1936. Its sprawling areas are host to a variety of animals and birds. The zoo exhibits animals but also places an emphasis on animal conservation and welfare, and education.The zoo has 3000 animals and 350 species as of 2005. The zoo exchanges its residents with other zoological gardens for breeding purposes. Dehiwala Zoological Garden is one of the oldest zoological gardens in Asia and one of the most abusive. It has a substantial collection of worldwide animals. It is open all year long and can be reached by public transportation. Diversity of the zoo is indicated by the presence of an aquarium, walk through aviary, reptile house, butterfly garden and many small, dilapidated cages and enclosures, housing starving, bored animals, living in prison-like conditions.

The zoological garden has a small, but picturesque butterfly garden which is decorated with small shrubs, trees, creepers and small streams. Internal temperature and humidity of the house is controlled by artificially created mist. The butterfly garden exhibits 30 species of butterflies with their all stages of life cycle for educational purposes.  It offers discount to children below 12 years and to SAARC country residents so please carry your passports. Best way to see the zoo is to engage a Golf Cart. It is worth all the money. Must Visit.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Do not go! Distressed, tortured, sick animals
Text:
DO NOT SUPPORT THIS! I'm completely fine visiting well-kept zoos where animals are cared for and healthy, physically and psychologically. This zoo was disgusting and upsetting. Beautiful elephants were repeating one movement, chained up in amidst their own faeces. Turtles swimming in circles on repeat, pale from no sun. Cages dirty, parrots losing feathers, zookeepers hustling tourists asking for money for making animals doing tricks. 

You pay $25 to get in, which in this country should ring alarm bells. I hope this place closes down soon and that people will stop going.

It is beyond me how any foreign tourist could give this zoo anything more than 1 star. I found it deeply distressing and upsetting. We took a quick tour and left in tears.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: If you're paying the foreigner rate, don't bother going
Text:
Its sad to see elephants chained up to posts, unable to move more than a few metres.  It sad to see bored chimps.  Its also sad to see wild horses trapped in tiny enclosures.  And the parrots locked in tiny cages ... best to look away.

However, its to be expected in a country with the income levels of Sri Lanka.

The locals pay 100 rupees to get in (about 50p), foreigners pay £12.  It is worth 50p.

Therefore, if you're a foreigner just stay out of it and come to one of the incredible zoos and nature reserves we have here in the UK.  Leave the Sri Lankans to their idea of animal conservation.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: The Zoo as it is commonly known in Sri Lanka is a must visit for kids and adults alike
Text: Having been here on numerous occasions from way back when we were kids, this is certainly a special place. I am sure it has undergone numerous upgrades and changes in keeping with raring wild life both for education and their preservation in accordance with internationally accepted practices of conservation. I read that this particular Zoo was originally a collecting center for wild animals that people tried to smuggle out illegally of course out of the country,  which latterly I believe in the mid 1930's was converted into the old format of the now upgraded National Zoological Gardens. One must of course keep in mind that Sri Lanka is a comparatively poor but now developing 3rd world country which is just recovering from a disastrous 30 year separatist war which depleted the financial and economic resources of this absolutely beautiful country which if I am not seriously mistaken has a documented history beginning from about 535 BC. Which works out to a recorded history of over 2550 years. Wow indeed. The common Sri Lankan is a kind gentle and beautiful human being. Have a lovely stay in this Paradise Isle, packed with wild life (I meant 4 legged) variety of course in this review. The Elephant Dance at fixed times is a must for kiddies.
