Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: must visit if you have 3 hours to spare
Text:
1.	Colombo Dehiwala Zoo: Founded in 1936, its over 80 years old and has around 3000 animals and 350 bird species. The zoo has been designed with clear demarcations that you need to follow to ensure you dont miss any beast. It is also in the process of renovation to meet global zoological standards. What we liked best was- the zoo was clean with lots of huge trees around, it had a cafeteria for lunch and other snacks, an enclosure for birds that you could actually walk into where macaws, parakeets and other smaller birds flew around freely. The park also has free WiFi, clean and well-lit toilets, a souvenir shop and a kids play area
-	Open from 8:30am to 6pm on all days
-	Entry fee for SAARC nationality Adult  LKR 700/- Child  LKR 350 (Other nationality, Adult LKR 2500, Child 1250)

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice place to visit in the evening.
Text: Some beautiful places to see.Tigers lions and specially The Elephant dance-In the evening.Must visit. Close to this hotel.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Awful, inhumane and filthy environment for Animals!!!!
Text: Filthy awful zoo, my heart broke for the animals living in those conditions. We where charged $70 AUD for a family (4 times higher than the locals one thing I don't think encourages tourists to visit and let me tell you it was NOT worth it because I don't think much of that money goes to the poor creatures). The facilities where in a disgraceful state of neglect, we saw rotten food in the animal feed trays, rubbish everywhere. The entrance staff where very rude (because being rude to tourists really lures them in...crazy)! The toilet facilities OMG don't even ask about the state of those....disgusting!!!!! We left  feeling angry and really upset about the welfare of the animals! Apparently they get the elephants to perform, but all we saw was them chained up with a chain around each leg. But it was the state in which they where kept  :( It was the lowest point for our trip to Sri Lanka!!! Something needs to be done about that zoo!!!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Wonderful except the elephants
Text: The zoo was a botanical masterpiece, beautifully landscaped and good architecture as well. There were many animals to see and the staff were friendly and helpful. There was a strong emphasis on education which I liked. However the elephants were the one thing that made me sad. They were chained by two legs and could not move except to rock back and forth in distress. I couldn't stay and watch as this is awful treatment. They say they do it on the premise that elephants are dangerous, but if you accept the responsibility of housing a dangerous animal than the proper environment should be established.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: one of the fine zoo i have seen
Text: must visit place for colombo visitors specialy families and kids ticket for foreigners is srilankan rs 2500 but for saarc countries like pakistan has to pay only rs 700 there is sea lion show and elephant show all cages were full neat place rest area and shades at many places

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Amazing time spent
Text: An amazing time spent. Just half an hour drive from Colombo 03, this place is worth visiting. For SAARC adult they charge LKR 700 and LKR 350 for a kid. Total value for money. Our kid enjoyed every minute of 2 ½ hours spent inside. Various species can be seen in birds, reptiles and mammals. Very well maintained and wide open spaces for clear sights. Lots of natural open area inside with seating arrangements in case you want to take a break. Refreshments also available. May be you should check with authorities if any elephant performance or sea lion performance scheduled for a day and plan accordingly, it would be more fun for sure.  Just adding few pics although there is lots to see inside.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Better than thought
Text: Not so bad as i expected. There are special shows (FOC) about snakes, Birds, Tigers, Sea lion and elephants.(Sinhala language only) recommended for kids. food available inside. worth to walk 3-4 hours. better walk with map otherwise you will not gonna see all of it. nice calm place  for those who are love animals and nature in busy Colombo. collection of African Asian and worldwide Animal species.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Amazing Zoo
Text: Perfect day out in Colombo. I would suggest to go early in the morning and try to finish the tour before mid day when it gets really hot. Lots of beautiful animals. Walk in cages for butterflies and exotic birds. Beautiful setup and good nice long walk to complete this tour. I took lots of pictures.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Old big Zoo at Colombo
Text: This is situated very close to Colombo. Very old zoo but now animals getting reduced day by day. Children love this place & very crowded in public holidays. Good elephant shows & must see that.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Average all round
Text:
Absolutely massive zoo with all the animals you would expect... but we didn't get to see the tigers for some reason? 

Most of the animals look unhappy, lonely
And upset as other travellers have mentioned... we thought this was just a joke until we actually saw it to be the case! (Especially the elephants...)

The gift shop was a poor excuse! 

Expect to do LOTS of walking...

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Shame on you Sri Lanka
Text:
We took some school children to the zoo today.  Sri Lanka is a country which is home to some of the world's most beautiful creatures.   This zoo is the most cruel zoo I have experienced though I have not experienced that many. The tragedy of the Brown Bear will haunt me forever as well as 3 hippopotomi in a tiny pond  
We are from the UK and have a charity in Sri Lanka.  We had to pay 100 times more than the Sri Lankans to get in.  Is this to deter us from experiencing the cruelty.  Zebra in a small pen. A tiger pacing in a cage with a small amount of water.  This zoo should be shut down and the animals released.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Oll Zoo, now run down with fewer animals & birds.
Text: It was once a very good Zoological Garden, but it has been run down. The number of animals were down, and the Elephant show, late in the afternoon was short & the items were cut down & the number of Elephants were reduced. The entrance fees were reasonable for the locals, but was overpriced for the foreign nationals.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Emotions and sadness
Text:
I was curious to see how Sri Lanka would treat animals in captivity. I started the visit with a so ridiculously small swimming pool with 2 lonely and bored sea lions who brought me tears. It seems there is a show in the afternoon to entertain people...
A brown bear seems waiting to die balancing its body from left to right, absolutely cruel vision ! Couple of leopards and jungle wild cats which bellies touch the ground because of inactivity. 
Special highlight on a moving male Oran outan is looking you straight in the eyes, what a sad eyes, to make you understand how mad we are to jail such intelligent animals. Will never forget. 
Not enough space and shade for tigers, lions... 
Girafs are living on a dry 'cricket play area' with absolutely nothing on it.
Have you ever swim with a turtle ? In Sri Lanka you can ! And it s free. Can you imagine a 1.5 meter square aquarium for one big turtle... How is it possible to jail a such large distance enduring animal you can see everywhere wild in Sri Lanka ? The same with peacocks, giant squirrel, elephants enchained like in the Buddhist temple, hornbills, spatula, ibis, spoonbill... All these animals can be seen everywhere in Sri Lanka. Why encaged them ? How ridiculous is this !
This is not the worst zoo on this planet, this is just another zoo and it reminds me how the human being is centered on himself and so sure of his superiority on others beings.
We are all animals, this is what i told to the zoo staff, when i gave them my suggestions. One answered me nicely that we need to keep these animals in captivity until they die for scientific studies and maintaining endangered species threatened by Men... 
I hope soon these kind of zoos will disappear :)
It s easy to discover amazing wildlife with FREE animals in National Parks and verywhere in Sri Lanka!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Interesting zoo.
Text: Small zoo but spent an enjoyable morning here. Variety of animals and opportunity to view fairly closely.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Excellent Zoo Experience!
Text: We thoroughly enjoyed visiting this zoo - its extensive and features a large variety of animals in a very beautiful setting.  Animals appear well cared for.   Note that tourists are charged a significantly higher entrance fee compared to locals.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: "Enjoyable, with potential to be a great zoo"
Text: We were a bit skeptical to visit after reading some comments about the zoo earlier in the day. Decided to go see for ourselves and to be frank the zoo is ok, you can see how beautiful it was initially designed to function as but it has been run-down. We had a great day of fun visiting the different enclosures, although not all of them were operational. Overall, the zoo has great potential to become a great attraction for visitors to Colombo!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Tired old zoo
Text: This years marks its 80th year and it sure looks it. Not much of the foreigner entrance fee (Rs. 2,500) finds its way back into development. Like with all zoos, better to arrive morning or afternoon to see the animals do something other than sleeping. You can get around quickly if your only have 1-2 hours, but could spend longer there.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good for kids
Text: Lot of variety of species. Mammals, birds, serpents, reptiles, butterflies.  need at least 4,5 hours to cover all. The restaurant inside was not good.  There was a small area to relax with kids.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Even for a zoo lover this is awful and inhumane.
Text: If you like watching clearly distressed animals kept in cruel and inhumane conditions, then this is the place for you! The chimpanzees, orangutans, elephants are clearly in a bad way, and there are no staff around to stop the visitors constantly feeding all sorts of rubbish to the animals. A horror show.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Inhumane and cruel
Text:
I will just start with a straight "avoid". I was taken here by a Sri Lankan family friend, who told us we were going out for the day in Colombo. I don't mean to be so harsh on somewhere but it's not hard to see when animals are suffering. If you care about the welfare of animals at all, you really shouldn't go, as animals are kept in small cages, look very distressed and unhealthy. Let this be an indicator: they still hold elephant shows, where elephants lift their legs not because they have been 'trained' to do so, but because they have been repeatedly prodded in the leg with a sharp rod and are now avoiding it.
I'm very 'for' the growth of Sri Lanka's economy and tourism industry, but please do not visit this zoo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: OK! Nice walk
Text: Very clean and well maintained gardens and walkways with large trees providing much needed shelter from the sun.  Easy to find your way around with map and sign posts.  Was sad to see the animals, many in poor condition and small enviroment.  Over priced for tourists but many locals and families  enjoying  a day out.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Could not wait to leave
Text: Terrible conditions for the animals, bordering on squalid in some cases.  Could not wait to leave.  In particular, those poor, majestic elephants chained up, moving from foot to foot, was very upsetting to me.  I would never go back there again ... too depressing.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Need much improvement
Text:
Poor facilities.. need work to become better 
It's has really nice natural view but not care for it the price too high for what you will see

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Sad
Text: Zoo has good collection of animals and sea creatures from different parts of the world.  Nice place to spend couple of hours with kids.  Many animals were kept in small cages and chained up, dat was quite sad.   Hygiene level of the place was not upto the international standards.  Good place only if you have kids along

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Dying animals silent administration / Government
Text: This place use to be a good one 10 years ago. The current condition of the animals are really awful. All they need is money!!! When you look at the number of people visiting and the price of the entry ticket I wonder about the maintenance... 10 years ago when i have visited this Zoo it was already needing attention in terms of the health of the animals. Today I can see almost half of the animals are disappeared presumably dead. The other half of the animals are in critical condition. Many of them are sick and not enough food to eat and not good water to drink. Many of them are wounded and the crows are eating their skinny body. I saw the elephants are being feed some handful of vegetables it's not sufficient for their daily needs. The African Elephant has lot of skin problems and wounds all over the body. The lions and Tigers are feed few meats daily and looks so skinny. The place looks nice but not really clean and smelling everywhere. Really sad to see all these poor animals suffering a lot. This please need an immediate government attention. Local medias also must do their part too.... The zoo need to hire some experts working with animals life and health. If not within few years there will be nothing to see.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice visit
Text: It took us three hours to go around the whole zoo. Yes, some of the animals have quite small living spaces - especially some birds. The elephants were tied from their legs so they couldn't move. Other than that all the animals looked fine and well to us. Foreigners have to pay 2500 rupees while locals pay 100 rupees which seems a bit unfair but that's how it is in every place in Sri Lanka. There is quite many clean toilets and small places to buy drinks from around the zoo. We felt happy with the visit in total.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Interesting
Text: Not bad for an asian attraction. Some of the animals needed care, which they weren't getting. Some parts sad. The lions were happy in their big garden.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: I feel for the animals
Text: We visited here and were not impressed with what we saw.  The zoo is in serious need of some good old genuine maintenance and upkeep.  I'm sure the staff love their animals and look after them as best they can on the budget they have, but I don't believe the animals are happy, the elephants in particular.  Same fr the bigger cats - they live in an undersized concrete pound, with very little greenery.  I came away feeling sad.  The cost to get in for "foreigners" was not worth it.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Te best Zoo I have ever seen so far
Text: That was an amazing experience, the zoo have been made in the nature itself, they literally changed the jungle into a zoo, the trees of 500+ years old the tight natural paths between the animals shelters give you the feel of walking through jungles, the area is huge and you need a one full day to see everything. They do have special and different animals than you can see in any other zoo, I was impressed at the bears area where I have seen at least 15 different types of bears that mostly I haven't seen before. The only thing I didn't like is that the Lion wasn't given the space it deserves as the Jungles king, anything else is simple amazing.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good place
Text: Had fun with family. But after when we were done we couldn't find a cab. Also most of areas were under renovation.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Do not visit
Text: As an ex-zoo keeper i can say the animal husbandry standards here are well below standard. Many highly stressed animals (one of the bears and a few of the elephants sway), quite a few solitary species that are naturally social, out dated enclosures and some under-fed animals. There is potential here but seemingly no passion or much understanding. Massive enclosure with a large pond was inhabitated by a few ducks!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Love elephants
Text: If you like elephants this is the place. You can see them going around freely. They are well keeped, you can even feed a baby.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Zoo in Residential Area
Text: The Zoo Located in residential area, its looks very old no renovation since long time. no proper parking available, for long distance peoples, school children's  who are visiting frequently, weekend for them no proper resting area or sufficient bathroom facilities, the management should consider all this.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good collection of animals, birds and reptiles
Text: I had gone there for my 2months little daughter and husband...so many animals...this is my first time visiting to zoo.its amazing

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Disgusting and disgraceful
Text:
Please I encourage people not to go to zoo's.
I went to the one in Sri Lanka yesterday and it was disgusting!!! 
All of the cages were so small, there were 6 elephants change up in an area that wasn't bigger than my back garden! This is obscure they are meant to roam free in the wild! On said it was born in 1949, that's 66 years old and it's whole life it has been cadged up for our own entertainment!! You can see on its face they were all so sad and just  had blank faces, the hippos were in small pools that the water looked and smelt like that water had been there for years and never cleaned/changed. No animal should be locked up and looked at for our entertainment, they are wild animals and that's where they belong in the wild.
How would we like it if we were locked up in a cadge and loads of animals were walking around and staring and poking at us the whole time! It's not right!
It needs to be stopped now!!!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: obese monkeys, beautiful birds
Text: I enjoyed my visit but felt bad for the monkeys who were constantly fed by visitors despite the signs clearly prohibiting it and explaining that it makes them sick. The sadest specimen was utterly obese and picking dried faeces from its rectal area and eating them whilst looking at the guests mournfully....

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Would not recommend
Text: Firstly we were charged ten times what locals are charged, although we didn't mind too much as it was still only 15euro each. However, the conditions were terrible and very upsetting. The elephants were chained in tiny areas and just swaying from side to side. I would not recommend a visit here

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Terrible Zoo
Text: I will never forget or forgive myself for visiting this awful place. The animal are in concrete pits unloved and need to be set free. Don't go please.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Worst zoo ever!
Text: I was absolutely appalled by the inhumanity of this zoo. Animals completely stressed and miserable. I prayed for them to die!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Wide range of animals
Text: This zoo is located in the Colombo city and it was my guide who suggested this place.  I will never regret taking his advice as I got to see so many animals and a few of them I had not even seen on National Geographic.  They have a wide spread of birds, animals and even fishes.  The Sea lions fill your heart with joy.  The number of species of snakes is also quite good.  All in all it is a perfect place if you want to go to a zoo or take your children along for some fun.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Holidays
Text:
Nice place to visit, lots of different species 
But all the renovation works make it dirty and not pleasant, animals are well treated,
And it's a safe place for children 
The prices are completely ridiculous, local people pays 100 rupees and 2500 for foreigners, this gap made want to go back home 
But anyway overall experience was really good

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Visited During Our Trip
Text: The zoo is really huge with a wide variety of animals. It seemed like a popular picnic spot for locals and foreigners alike. Worth a visit to see the stunning array of birds they have.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: One of the best maintained zoos
Text: A wonderful evening spent at the zoological gardens. A good 3 hours can be spent enjoying the organised Zoo and escape the city bustle. A great place for kids with a variety of animals from Asia and a few from Africa. Little expensive for foreigners though.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Expensive not worth visit
Text:
This zoo is very worn down with renovation ongoing but a lot of exhibitis are just closed. 
 Price for local is 700 rb but a hefty 2500 rb for foreningers! 
 Not worth a visit!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Worth a visit
Text: One of Sri Lanka's pare-eminent attractions which is unfortunately missed by many tourists.  I highly recommend a visit.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Traumatised animals!
Text: The condition under which these animals are caged is pathetic - small cement rooms, mal nourished, teased and taunted by visitors. Never again!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice pleasant visit for kids, not too bad for adults too
Text:
The zoo visit definitely makes sense if you have a kid to entertain. It wont disappoint the adults too with nice collection of animals and birds.
All Basic amenities are in place like eateries, toilets, free wifi and the place is clean and well maintained.
Some construction work is going on but it doesnt come in the way of zoo exploration.
Checkout the elephant and money shows to add extra spice to the zoo trip.
Reptiles section was interesting with pythons and cobras.

The tuk-tuks just outside the zoo would try to overcharge. If you can walk a bit farther from the place , you can catch a reasonable bargain with tuk-tuk

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Worth a visit esp. with a kid , has free wifi and basic amenities
Text:
The zoo visit definitely makes sense if you have a kid to entertain. It wont disappoint the adults too with nice collection of animals and birds.
All Basic amenities are in place like eateries, toilets, free wifi and the place is clean and well maintained.
Some construction work is going on but it doesnt come in the way of zoo exploration.
Checkout the elephant and money shows to add extra spice to the zoo trip.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Amazing Animals
Text: It was my first experience to see real animals like tiger, bear, zebra and much more ...the park is so clean and wide and really stunning.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A great place for the kids
Text:
Playful elephants in enclosures; lots of other animals and birds to see; a great day-outing for the children. For an additional fee (tickets to be bought at the entry counter), you get to feed the baby elephants milk through huge feeding bottles ... the kids absolutely LOVE this, plus great photo opportunity for tourists. All in all, we thought it was worth the time and effort.
Only slightly irritating factor was that as usual, non-Sri-Lankans pay a much higher fee than locals (relatively) to get in ... but it's quite affordable if you're a foreigner.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: If you like animals, DON'T go here.
Text: one of the worst zoos I had the displeasure of going to. Animals are kept in horrible conditions like cramped cages with little to no standards of cleanliness. If you truly want to see a bit of Sri Lankan wildlife, please take a safari trip or head to the elephant orphanage at Pinnawala.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: BIG NO
Text:
Had heard a lot about this zoo from my mom , normally the tour operator s surprise at being asked to take us there should have been a warning sign . The zoo itself was badly maintained , the animals looked ill cared for and there was a forlorn feeling to the whole place . 
Huge waste of time .

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Jude was the most fantastic tour guide I've ever had
Text:
What else more can I say. When my boyfriend and I stayed in Beruwala, Jude picked us up from the airport and took us to the hotel. He was fantastic, he taught us lots about Sri Lanka, their culture and history - he was fascinating!
He also took us on a tour to the moon stone mines and the turtle hatcheries. He was lovely and so relaxed which made our stay all the more enjoyable - we are still in contact now.
Definitely would recommend that anyone traveling to Sri Lanka should use him!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Zoo
Text: This zoo is owned by the Government. This is situated just out of the city about half an hour from the city centre. The zoo is good have a variety of animals and birds.If you like zoos O K otherwise you can skip.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good
Text:
This is one of the good zoos in south East Asia.A very well designed zoo.A good selection of wild life . Worth the visit.You can spend a day here enjoying.
.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Very good in parts
Text:
This zoo has some exceptional features that make the 700 SLR [ for SAARC ] entrance worthwhile .
1] The attractions are numbered with arrows pointing to the next stop . Along with the map provided with the ticket this ensures you a trouble free visit without getting lost or making backtracks repeatedly . Using the map , you can skip whatever you don't want to see .
2] Lush green landscaping with giant trees and a waterfall - very pleasant even in July
3] The Reptile house and the Aquarium are really worth seeing
4] Walk in aviary and butterfly park not up to the mark 
5]  Most enclosures are '' new world '' type with all animals in very good health .
This is not the place to debate about the morals and ethics of keeping animals in captivity .  At least an effort is made here to keep everything clean and presentable .

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Life time in prison for a crime which they never committed..
Text:
It is so heartbreaking how these cruel people keep these innocent animals in a prison like Dehiwala Zoo. Most of the cages are just fit the size of the animal and there was peacock who couldn't turn sideways. 

No Matter What Reason. No human being has the right to make an animal suffer.

Never visit this place and do not ever take your children to this place.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Aweful
Text: I gotta say after reading many reviews from expats i thought to myself i don't want to go as it's not worth it. After a while we changed our minds and decided to go and check it out for ourselves. The zoo is disgusting! The animals look sad and the place is left with no maintenance. So you start by paying 2500 instead of 700 because you're a foreigner, then you start the tour and see that it is so bad inside you wanna cry. The water tanks are green, the pool for the seal is all rusty and the water is beyond green. The seal is alone and he looks sad. The elephants are chained by their front and back  legs, the bears, tigers, and many other animals look tired, dehydrated and in a bad shape. Some of the animals are locked in really small cages that are too small for a parrot!  Half of the zoo is under maintenance so they have big tractors working just next to the animals disregarding them. I honestly will never go back to visit as i will not accept to pay to watch animals suffer. And so should everybody!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Only place I liked in Colombo
Text: It is a huge place and the animals dont look sad like some places. There were some animals I had not seen like Double humped bacterian camel, albino cobra and some deers and birds. Get a map of the zoo so you dont miss any enclosures. Considering the temperature, most animals would be dozing off by late morning / early noon types itself. Need to go early or by around 3 or 4 to get a good sighting is what I think.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Avoid this hole of a zoo
Text: Apart from the fact that as a foreigner I had to pay almost 3 times more than locals, avoid this zoo. I must agree with some of the other reviewers, this play is a shambles. It looked like the seal enclosure had been defunct for years and the elephant enclosures were sad, pathetic and heartbreaking. I cannot find anything positive to say. The mere fact that this zoo has been neglected for so long is a disgrace.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: elephant camp
Text:
you can have a good sight on elephants. 
if you are going with kids then its worth, else its not suggest able for bachelors

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Must See attraction if You are in Sri Lanka
Text:
One of the world's largest Zoo.
Pack your lunch and a water bottle in a easily carry back pack.
Make sure you prepare to spend all day as it is massive place to walk around.
Huge collection of animals are on display including rare and native species.
There are food outlets and main central restaurant in the Zoo if you can't be bothered taking lunch or snacks and want to travel light. Good quality food and drinks available including world famous Sri Lankan tea if you are tea lover.
There is Elephant show on few afternoons which attracts large crowed. If traveling with kids they will love it as elephant do few dancing steps to music.
It's good full day trip make sure you start early so you get to finish seeing all the species by the afternoon before it gets dark.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Zoo
Text: There are some very exotic animals but some of the cages are too small not not appropiate, but the Zoo is changing things slowly due to finance.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Depressing
Text:
I really wished I hadn't come.  This place was such a disheartening experience that I can't believe it's still open.  The animals looked neglected, many seemed unhealthy.  The cages were dirty and resembled prison cells.  Many of them were crammed into enclosures far too small.  And a lot of animals just had a distressing look about them that's hard to describe.

There are so many better options, such as the national park, that I can't understand why anyone would knowingly come here.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Not worth the effort..
Text: Went to this zoo for the sake of my three year old son..but it was a disappointing experience.. The enclosures are dingy and not well maintained.. Animals look filthy and unhealthy.. Many exhibits were closed off for renovation..Ultimately it wasn't worth the time and effort..

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: What a sad and depressing experience
Text: I wouldn't encourage anyone who has any sort of compassion for or interest in animals to visit this hell-hole. My one-time-only visit left me heart broken and certainly put a damper on the rest of my trip. Speaking to some Sri Lankan friends it is clear that the zoo is rife with political corruption and the animals are left to suffer the consequences. You only have to see the place to know this is true! The monkey's among other animals were in CONCRETE cages left to wallow in piles of their own feces! Some of the bigger animals seem to have resigned themselves to their fate and pace / rock back and forth or stare vacantly out of their cages. If the purpose of a zoo is to show you a glimpse of animals as they are in the wild, the purpose of this particular zoo is to show you how much depravity an animal can endure before it breaks.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Lovely place to visit.
Text: I love this place and was excited to see the Elephants.  I was impressed by the way all the elephants were treated and enjoyed seeing the baby elephants drink milk.  It was also nice to see them play in the river.  The shops around are good as well.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: One of the Must Sights for a Tourist
Text:
This Zoo does not have the same ambiance or crowds or space or shows or natural enclosures as the other famous zoos of the world,however,it does have more animals than most of the other zoos.At least it beats the Indian Zoos in the variety of exhibits and the shows.
What the authorities should consider is the improvement in the quality of shows,pre publishing correct show information(we visited on 4th of April 2015)and were surprised at the cancellation of Elephant show.The enclosures should be made more natural,and outside  food should be strictly banned in the park.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: So good went twice in three days
Text: beautiful grounds, long walks to the animals, but worth it, they have lions,white tigers, Bengal tigers,leopard, big cats, lots and lots and more lots,the elephant show was the best iv seen, great fun, and if your into birds,find out what time feeding time is! They have wild grey not our usall white ones! I was lucky enough to see a Herron,grey one and a night Herron, all had something very green long and so my crawling out of the water"there verion of the lock ness monster perhaps.? Yor given a map, and if your not sure of the feeding times ask a attendant,why? What makes it so different from anything else. The keepers throw the fish to the birds ok I get that! Normal you think they then open a gate, with. Huge wheele arrow, full of fish, I meen full, and to my suprise and delight, tipped the wheele barrow upside down,,locked the gate,the birds for mikes flew pecking, shaking, ska bling, to fight for the fish! Everyone got one!! Or two if they were lucky, the Herron got lucky, I got lucky as I got wonderful photos and videos, of him guzzling the fat fish, in bliss, it took him a good10 minitues to devour the tasty Morsel! Great entertainment, but not necessarily for all,as the little ones seemed frightened of the noise they were all making, and the claws came out in full force!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: It has to be shifted to a bigger open area...
Text: My wife visited this zoo 20 years ago , then it was one of the best zoo's of Asia, so at the end of our tour of Amazing Lanka this time , my wife wish was to see the zoo again , well to tell you the truth we all were very disappointed to see such a past glorious attraction is crumbling down, the entrance ticket are not cheep, for SARAC Rs 700/ per person, the fish aquariums  I must say is well maintained and attractive display of corals and fish, but the rest of the zoo need lots of attention, its over crowded surrounded with urban population and traffic noises , a new open space in the outskirt of the city will return its glory. I would not recommend this zoo  for foreign  visitor.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Government neglecting their social obligation
Text: The Environmental, Culture, Arts, Social  and the wild exotic Animal Organisations etc. are  is collecting more money for the foreign visitors, the managements and staffs are just feeling the forms and collecting their wages and Government is neglecting their moral ans social obligations. They are giving huge amount of grants to preserve this most valuable natural assets but money goes for wages and not for the welfare of the animals, their health and environments including in the captivity. This is not only happening in one country only but in many other countries, and many TV documentaries, Newspapers & Media are witness. Even there are no separate authority to inspect, regulate,control mismanagement and no complaint system, all goes under the carpet. I personally urged to these Governments in order to SAVE THIS UNIQUE NATURE BECAUSE ONCE IT IS DISAPPEAR - YOU WON'T GET IT BACK.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Disappointing
Text: You can see the animals aren't treated that well. The elephants keep swinging from left to right and are chained up. The toilets are disgusting. The restaurant food isn't that great, it felt like a waste of my money. I was so excited to go to the zoo, but it was just a big let down. They overcharge tourists. I was able to blend in (boyfriend is Sri Lankan) and got the local price.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Seen better days
Text:
One of the oldest in this part of the world has seen better days. 
Recent renovations and downsizing has led to a fair part of the zoo being closed for public. 
However, the elephants and the elephant show still attracts many.

But still a nice place to spend a day with family.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: amazing place to visit
Text: what a nice lovely place to visit, you don't need to travel far but make sure that you are there early in the morning to avoid the heat. the layout is excellent, all you have to do is follow the arrows which they are numbered, the only two things that minorly disappointed me were, even though the sign said that they accept credit cards, they actually don't (maybe the machine was down that day) and the other thing was i didn't get to see any leopards the cage was empty with broken door. apart from that, really a great place to spend the day,

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice place. A worthy zoo thats clean and well kept
Text:
We had a no plan day in Columbo so a TripAdvisor search show us that the zoo was t far from our hotel. A 100 ruble tuk tuk rode later we were there.  

Nice place.  Well kept and well laid out.  Maps are given out at the ticket counter so we had an idea what direction to walk. 

The zoo itself is very clean and the animals are well tended to.  No staving malnourished animals to be seen.  

We enjoyed our visit and walking around. Snacks are available.  Signs saying dont feed the animals are posted so dont waste your resources bringing food for the animals.  We had a green apple and wanted to give it to Prince the horse but I asked the guy first and he said no.  I felt bad for Prince cause I showed it to him already and he looked happy to eat it.  

Admission for tourists is a bit steep. 3000 rubies a person.  Thats about $16.50 a ticket but it is a great way to spend 2-3 hours.  

If you like zoos you should go here.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Great Visit
Text:
After many years with my family we have visited the Dehiwala Zoo (thats the name we call from the childhood). Its far better than before & there are lots of new things & improvements. We love the way of the Macaw parrots were amazing.

We all enjoyed the way of the Tigers its like a glass cage & feels like tiger come near to you. 

We also had lunch in the main Restaurant the food was ok bit over priced however the service was very poor & not enough servers.

Overall good experience there also kids activities which little once can enjoy..
Thank you.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Amazing Zoo with vast variety of animals and kids play area too
Text: Dehiwala Zoo is an amazing place to visit with children. The great variety of animals and the various shows like bird show, sea lion show and elephant dance show are unique and wonderful. There is also a kids play area where the kids can have a gret time while their parents can rest. Overall a very nice place, highly recommended

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Dont go there
Text:
Animals and Enclosures are in bad condition. Entry fee for Overseas is 3.000 Rps (15 Euro), Locals pay just 800 Rps.
Dont buy the cutten fruits from Locals offered in front of the Zoo to feed the animals. Feeding of Animals in the Zoo is strictly forbidden! Only cash accepted.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
User_Location: Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
Title: Good and improved
Text:
The zoo has improved a lot so therefore I scored it as average. My son enjoyed his trip very much. They had a large variety of different animals. One word of advice though, make sure you are well hydrated and carry water, wear loose and comfortable clothing and shoes. because, it is very hot during the day. There is a lot of walking involved too. Although, sometimes the proper signage is not placed properly and we did get lost a few times. There should be a park map available. 
Overall, my son enjoyed it so therefore I'm happy ??. I can't remember the ticket price but for foreigners it's I think around 1000 lkr(adult) and I think for locals it's 100 lkr. The ticketing staff was rude though.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good zoo in Colombo
Text: It is located in the City Colombo. It is a good option for picnic spot for locals. Beautifully landscaped 30 acres in which a rich collection of mammals, birds, reptiles and fishes live in harmony with Nature.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Lovely clean zoo
Text: Lovely day out, all the animals were kept in superb conditions and well fed. Small zoo but doesnt feel small when walking around it. Excellent water park to cool off whilst eating ice cream after a busy day.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Worst experience!!
Text:
I have visited Dehiwala zoo with my daughter and wife, my wife is a foreigner and the reception charge me 2500 Rs (15$) and for me and my daughter charges as locals (100 and 30 Rs)i have explained that she is my wife and we just wanna spent sometime at the Zoo we had some free time, but no one give a damn to understand me.

In my personal opinion this is very inequitable as we were not tourists to visit the zoo, we just wanted to pass our time during our time in my home country and the experience went down to to bottom as i felt it was overcharged for no good reason. I hope the management will think of a fair solution on this rather asking customers to pay just for the sake if earning extra revenue.

We have been to many Zoos where we paid far less than what we paid here and more Animals with great atmosphere.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Very Average and just wrong.
Text:
We decided to go to the Zoo as we hadn't been to a zoo for a while, and had a day free.
In retrospect we picked one of the worst days to go, as it was Saturday and the Zoo was packed.
Upon entry we were greeted with what you'd expect to see in this country at most attractions, and this really has to change if this country's tourism is to move forward.
We were charged $22 Australian dollars to enter, while locals paid $1, this was an insult as one feels that westerners don't have 20+ more sets of eyes than locals, just blatant price gauging, not cool.

Apart from that it's a vast Zoo, but some of the enclosures were not only small, there was little shelter for the animals, and some of the enclosures were quite old, and in urgent need of repair.
Was also sad to see this big elephant pen, but the elephants were on chains, about 10 metres away from water they could have been bathing in to keep cool.

We would never return here, and hope when you visit the place its more updated and the pricing discrepancies and discrimination has been rectified.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Poor animals are suffering and need immediate attention !!!
Text: No proper guidance to visitors especially for tourist who pays 2500 LKR, not even provided with a small map or information leaflet. No proper toilet facilities, No security for animals, locals are feeding animals what ever they wishes. Management need to pay careful attention to this wonderful place.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Worth visiting if you are with kids
Text: I went to the zoo on a Sunday with my 4 year old as I had the day free with nothing to do. We got to see some healthy animals in a nice environment and we both enjoyed it. I don't understand the negative reviews though. We went on a Sunday, yes it was crowded but at no point did we feel overwhelmed. The pricing is different for locals vs non locals but that's understandable. A zoo needs to be affordable for all. In summary I would say that if you set your expectation for a zoo in a developing country you would not be disappointed.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good day out with kids in Colombo
Text: Lots of animals, all looking reasonably healthy, and the zoo follows a decent health and welfare program.  Kids liked the Tigers and zebras best.  Expensive for foreigners (compared to locals).  Didn't try the food outlets as they were way too busy.  Got the train to Dehiwala from Colombo and then a tuktuk from there as most Central tuktuk drivers don't venture that far out.  All in all a good day out if holidaying with kids.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Cool place to go in spare time
Text: Had a day relaxing in Colombo and decided to go to the Zoo. Being a westerner I was immediately ushered to the front of the long queue. I know I paid more than a local, but I was happy to get out of the sun. The zoo itself is cool, been to a few zoos and saw a few different animals in here. Not as crowded as I thought it would be. A little pushing and shoving near the front of the animal pens to get a good view... decent few hours spent in here. Two thumbs up.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Still a great Zoo... Dont be misled by negative publicity
Text: A must stop for our family every time we visit Sri Lanka. This time we were informed by many misinformed that it was not a great place... However, we found it to be still one of the best Zoological Gardens in terms of range of exhibits as well as the quality of care given to the animals. In our view the Zoo is seriously underpriced for locals as it offers fantastic value for money

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Disappointed
Text:
For the price of around £12 each for a foreigner I felt very disappointed as it was not worth it. Most of the animals were kept in too small cages such as the birds and the elephants were all chained up, swaying side to side, probably because they're bored. 
I felt like I was being stared at and pointed at a lot because of my race or the way I dressed. Some kids even asked to take a selfie with us and some tried to take a picture of us. 
Overall I would not recommend visiting the zoo unless you would like to be an exhibit yourself!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Interesting Animals and quite a lot of them
Text: Wonderful to take the kids. You see a lot of wild animals and they all look well looked after.  There is the elephant dance in the evening and if you're lucky you may even see some land monitors walking around freely as they are not captured for the zoo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: The zoo is not maintained And very expensive rate for tourist.
Text: We regret visiting the place. Huge crowd and the animals are in bad condition. The government of Sri Lanka should check the place. The animals look dehydrated. The entrance also for tourist is expensive 2500 rupees. Not worth the visit.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Poorly managed!!!
Text: Animals in cramped areas and elephants tied by legs!! Nothing impressive about this zoo.7500 rupees for tourists to enter and only 100 for locals !!!Huge margin !!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Kids for marvelous place
Text: Dehiwala zoo one of the best attraction for kids,we can see all kind live things here must show kids

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Improvements required !
Text:
Visited with my wife and 2 year old daughter. 
contains a good variety of animals, birds, reptiles etc. however, it was much better few years ago !
facilities for the visitors (human) has improved vastly. but, not much for the "residents" !

new birds' cage is a new addition (for me). nice idea and you are very close to the birds. kids will love it. 

famous elephant show is no more ! number elephants for display are also less. few are kept in the back, where they are going to build a exclusive elephant area. also, many improvements are going in in animal cages which is a good sign.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: So Sad
Text: I was so excited to visit the zoo and see elephants and other animals, but was so sad at the conditions they have the animals in.  lion and leopard in their cages groaning away in pain and had pieces of meat chucked on the floor which the rats were enjoying.  it seemed that nobody care for the welfare of the animals since all cages seemed to have animal faeces which looked like had been there for days.  its ridiculous how they charge so much but cant even look after their animals properly because they are the ones making them so much money.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good Place
Text: Its a big zoo and a good place to visit. They have a big collection of animals not only from Sri Lanka but from all around the world. Its good to watch the seal show, bird show, they also have an elephant show but unfortunately the day we visited they did not have it so we missed that.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: not the best of places
Text: it used to be one of the best zoo's in the world but standards have gone down recently. good place to visit a lot of animals but they should expand the zoo to make the animals more comfortable.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Go there for the Elephant show
Text: There is an elephant show here every evening which is a must watch. Go there early to get the best view seats

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Old Zoo
Text: Dehiwala Zoological Garden is one of the oldest zoological gardens in Asia. It has a substantial collection of animals. Diversity of the zoo is indicated by the presence of an aquarium, aviary, reptile house, butterfly garden and enclosures for animals from various parts of the world. Green anaconda, albino cobra and pygmy hippopotamus are main attraction. There is an elephant show here every evening.We did not find the butterfly garden there.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice place to go with your kids.
Text: Vibrant place near to Dahiwala....If you are on family trip you must take your kids here...seal show and elephant dance are the attractions

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Kids loved this zoo. Pricey for foreigners. 2500R
Text: Annoying that locals are 700 and foreigners are 2500R but the animal mix was great. We got close up to a bunch of animals. Heaps of elephants. Great crocodile exhibit. Worth the admission price.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: I am so angry
Text: Please, please do not visit this zoo. Surly you will realise this is not the place for these wonderful creatures and surely you will realise that it is wrong to make these magnificent animals do these ridiculous tricks. Please, please do not support these treatment of animals. No elephant should be made to stand on it's head it's tragic

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: amazing
Text: there have lot of animals local and forging. the zoo is well maintain and there have elephant show  in the afternoon.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Huge Zoo
Text: Visited the zoo with family , there is a special rate for the fee for Srilankans & SAARC countries, the zoo is huge with loads of animals, & lots of trees. but animals are kept in poor conditions & the map is not very clear. Be warned of the people trying to sell things near the gates of the zoo .. ALSO DON'T HIRE A TUK TUK RIGHT OUTSIDE THE ZOO. they try to cheat on the tourists.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Feel morally incorrect even going
Text:
This was part of a package or I would never have gone.
Very expensive door charge for foreigners, cheap for locals.
Most large animals were kept in appalling conditions 
The lions, tigers, cats were kept in concrete floored cages with absolutely nothing at all. One just walked back and forth this tiny tiny enclosure which stinks . They said they were waiting rehoused but even for one day this is unacceptable! They looked thin to me too. Free them!
The bears looked desperately unhappy also kept like the wild cats one constantly rocking back and forward looking like his brain had already gone! I so badly wanted to let him free.
Elephants standing tightly chained side by side with nothing at all other than ability to shift weight. What a horrendous life for elephants .
The guinea pigs (small animals) were in vast numbers all thin and all with scurvy,guinea pigs can't make vitC so need it included in their diet. All were thin and all clearly lacking vitC I wondered how much longer some will live.
Ponies looked poor and slim just miserable.
Do not go , do not line these owners pockets. This animals should all be renowned somewhere appropriate .Awful and depressing

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: ! Most depressing zoo!
Text: This zoo is the saddest place Ive been to.. you walk in and all the locals seem to enjoy seeing animals but arent even aware of how horrible the zoo conditions are. The Animals look miserable and sick, with no fur or feathers. The penguins has a tiny room, with one pool and a regular office A/C which is broken. I have taken pictures and complained but really urge everyone who feels the same way as me to take a stand for animal rights.. Im not an extremely active animal rights activist but anyone can see how horrible the conditions are. Please speak up, they need to do something about this ?

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Really good zoo
Text: I liked the zoo very much. There are more animals than the zoos in kerala... It was a lot of fun. Just wanted to spend some more time over there

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Sad
Text: Being a Sri lankan it was very sad to see the state of the animals. There were too many staff just sitting and chatting. should reduce the number of staff and feed the animals for god safe.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice Place - had a good time
Text: The best attraction is the Elephant Dance - which is sometime around 4 / 4.30 pm. It is a very good show. I had gone there for my little daughter - 3 years. we all enjoyed a lot - despite the heat.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Like natural
Text: We had not missed the Srilankan Zoo. Like all other tourist spot we have been charged more than the normal entry fee. one good restaurant are here. lots of birds are there. one water falls. Royal Bengal tiger, venomous snake, zebra,. really thrilling and wonderful experience. Very neat and clean and well decorated.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Naren
Text: Very good place to visit for all. Good variety of animals, well maintained and clean premises. Just that for some people, it's not that easy to walk through the whole zoo in April heat ;) ;)

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice visit in the evening.
Text: Very close from the hotel about 20 minutes by a taxi,Nice time is in the evening,to see the elephant show,The place is managed by the government.Nice cool place to have a walk too.Many reptiles birds and many animals reptiles.Worth to visit with kids.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: One of the best zoos in Asia
Text: I visited Srilanka last year and a friend recommended this zoo for a quick peek.I ended up spending more than 5 hours appreciating the beauty of nature. The highlight of this zoo is that almost all the species that you can think of are here.I even saw a meerkat! Refreshment stands/restaurants are placed at vantage points for you to enjoy your exploration without getting tired.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good zoo,but could have been better
Text:
Prices are quite high,considering the conditions in which the animals live here. Birds are more better than animals  and they have a huge collection here. However, most animals looked sick and thirsty. I felt bad for them. Elephants were chained and I have heard they have a few shows(I personally don't prefer using animals to earn money),so I didn't see them. Monkeys seemed cool and the orangutan was eye contacting with me. That was delightful. 
Good place only if u have extra bucks or time to spend. Not a must visit.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good visit-
Text: But animals are in the cages.Very crowded.And we enjoyed the butterfly nest in it.i do not like the animals caged-That is a place for children.Not for adults.Is a big area.Not bad .We witnessed the elephant dances too.Try it.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Unclean and disappointing
Text:
I was waiting something more...
The zoo was so dirty and animals were in very bad situation. The ticket price was too high and the direction signs were not helpful 
Do not waist your time and money

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: wow best Zoo in Sri Lanka
Text: it was the busy day inside the zoo, that many animals to see for one day, the animal all very quiet , we can't take an eye off from them

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Sunday at the Zoo
Text: Animals are pretty same as in every zoo but it has been interesting seeing how locals spend the day at the zoo with the family! Get some street food before stepping-in and sit under the trees to enjoy the local life style!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Revamp required
Text: I have been to this zoo a few times in the last 20 years but my most recent visit was very disappointing. This Zoo used to be one of the best in Asia at some point, but recently has become far less than satisfactory. I blame poor management, maintenance, and lack of funds. During this visit I observed a few areas undergoing renovations but did not look like it was going to tip the scale. Perhaps the worst part was that the animals seemed highly mistreated, locked up in cages not nearly big enough, or tethered to appallingly short chains. Some of the cages did not have sufficient guards and the animals were at a tangible distance.  I am surprised that this zoo has not received any reprimand from local wildlife organizations. The cost was not at all worth it for foreign nationals ($25). The only two exhibits I enjoyed was the white tiger and a talking cockatoo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Forest Feel
Text: Great place for everyone Especially Children's, U can see most of the animals & birds under one roof, pretty well managed, Can be better. One important hint if you don't want to miss any animals or birds follow the numbers bcoz it makes u cover everything............truly we loved it.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: An average National Zoo but the ticket price is quite steep even for a foreigner...
Text:
Ayubowan! 

Visited this place on 21st December 2014 with a local buddy.

The location is easily reached by public buses. Upon reaching the Zoo entrance, I have sensed that something is not quite right as street peddlers, beggars are all over the place and the entrance is quite dirty littered with garbage.

While at the ticket booth, I saw a notice sign telling the entrance fees...Foreigner 2500lkr and Local 100lkr. My friend was surprised with the fees hike since his last visit which was 1500lkr and asked me if I would like to proceed. Since we were already there, why not to go ahead with the plan for the day (we reached about 1.30pm as the weather is drizzling slightly and cool). I really wanted to see and explore a Zoo that is charging high fees as I made Zoo visits a must when visiting foreign countries. 

Well, the first impression at the entrance is already at the point of shocked and disbelieved therefore I do not have high expectation and will now on only highlight the stronger points, enjoy and make the best out of it. First greeting is from the Flamingo on the left and bald bodied Ostrich on the left. Errr...did I mentioned bald bodied ostrich, yup something is wrong. Most of the avian settings are all wet from the weather. The ostriches are losing their feathers and they even have bloodied ends.

Then next salt water aquarium and the fresh water aquarium display. That 'cave tunnel' is very dark with poor or almost no lighting...all you can hear is water dripping in the river setting on the right and the poor tank display on the left...people are pushing their way trough and children are everywhere running...have to be very careful or else you might trip and fall into the 'river'...the 2nd part of the 'cave tunnel' is much better...more lighting and the tank display are more newer and minus the river, more attractive and better maintained. Then at the exit there is a pond with glass viewing panel with hundreds of colorful carps swimming in it. 
In order to cover the compound to the maximum, all you need to do is to follow the cage number direction arrows (1 - 60). The macaw enclosure with yellow dusty soil cover at the bottom are literally infested with rats! They burrowed underneath the ground and feeds on the leftover food from the macaws...then the other cages of the eagle owl and so forth are not spared from litters, dirty water buckets, dried water dish and rusty cage wired mesh walls. What they did was patching up the cage with another layer of mesh. The display cages are basically their permanent home and some has no roosting box eg the african grey parrot. The only lemur collections that can be seen is the lonely ring tailed lemur which loves some head and snout rub...the others maybe inactive. 

Butterfly enclosure is empty too...expected to see all the sri lankan endemic species but...again the enclosure was infested with rats. The waterfall next to the meerkats and ferrets were supposed to house the mute swans but only the domestic goose was seen. We paused the visit at cage no13 because we wanted to see the sealion performance at 4.30pm therefore we adjourn to the sealion arena. It was an open seating place underneath a huge tree but the seating area is soaking wet from the rain and have birds dropping everywhere. The water in the pond where the sealion swims is green and full of leaves litters too. It was a 20 minutes show. 
After the show, we continue from where we stop. 

The open aviary is not really 'open' as peacock, hornbills and white koel are in cages within the aviary. Only ring necks, some fowls and mynah are free flying. Most of the big cats pens are closed for reconstruction, the jungle cats enclosure are dark and smelly...while other bigger animals such as the elephants, tigers, deers, orang utan, rhino and giraffes have fairly bigger enclosure as to compare with the others. Some of the monkeys need medical attention, esp the obese white toque monkey, the formosan monkey that has facial skin problem and they seems lethargy too. Well with the costly entrance fee, the toilets are being charged at 30rs per person. 

As a conclusion, I am 80% happy with this visit as they have quite varied species collected for display. The balance is sad with the avian settings, animal health conditions, the cleanliness and not enough time. Whether if it worth the money paid is up to individuals but indeed this is a pricey one.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A diverse range of animals to see
Text:
Yes, quite a few cages are too small and need renovating, but it is evident to see that slowly the zoo is tackling these issues with a large elephant enclosure renovation going on. I arrived around 10.30am on a Saturday morning nad the keepers had already fed most animals a tasty array of fruits/grass/vege etc and cages were clean or in the process of being cleaned.The animals are not neglected although their housing conditions could be improved. however it was interesting to see such a wide range of animals, and the zoo was quite well laid out. People watching is almost as much fun as the animals, and there are so many cute little Sri Lankan kids around. I didn't try to restuarnats but icecreams and drinks were widely avaialble in the park. Entry a little expensive for foreigners but all information panels have at least one section for english. I went by myself, and as a single lady traveller, was pleased not to be hasseled or nagged by anyone during my visit. Beware of the touts outside peddling fruit and plastic kitsch. Happily I had a driver waiting for me, but unless you are confident with the bus system, I would recommend taking a tuk-tuk or a taxi to the zoo. It would take quite a long time by bus from Colombo.

Your ticket includes the priveledge of the tourist loos (chargeable one) but mae sure to take your own loo paper. A great way to spend a few hours, and probably best to visit in the morning when the zoo first opens to avoid the crowds.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A zoo from the Jurassic Age!
Text: I had been to this zoo when I was a teenager back in the 1970s and had enjoyed the Elephant dances and seeing the white albino monkey that my uncle had donated to the zoo when it became too boisterous to keep at home.  I was back again on holiday to see family and friends and decided it was time to go again.  We went with our wife, teenager daughter, and disabled son in a wheelchair.  We also had our driver and nurse to accompany us.  The first thing to note is entrance fee is 10x the local rate for foreigners.  So or an adult it was Rs 2,400 vs Rs200 for a local.  Still a lot cheaper than London Zoo but then you pay for what you get.  The layout of the Zoo is well organised with numbers for each animal site and well posted signs providing clear directions.  Unfortunately the Elephant dance no longer takes place but a elephants are wonderful to see.  Most of the animals are in small cages and look depressed.  The tiger and bears were just pacing up and down the cage.  The lions sleeping with rotten meat next to them being eaten by crows.  A very sad and pathetic site.  Compared to modern day zoos like San Diego and London this zoo was still from the Jurassic age.  I would not recommend a trip to this zoo until they have provided proper facilities for these animals and habitats more akin to what they are familiar with in the wild.  Also this is not a zoo to take a wheelchair as many of the cages were not accessible due to steps.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice Place To Relax
Text: For some reason, I tend to seek out zoos and botanical gardens in cities that I visit.  Just seems to provide a respite from whatever hectic activities I might be involved in during my stay.  Colombos Zoological Gardens is very well stocked with a wide range of animals from lemurs and wild pheasants to elephants, lions, tigers and giraffes.  The zoo is quite large and if you go, plan on spending 2 to 3 hours if you want to see most of the exhibits.  The cages, tanks and grounds are very clean and well maintained.  In fact while viewing the fish tanks, that were remarkably clean, it reminded me of how many aquarium disasters I suffered as a child.   The park is cool and easy to navigate since all the exhibits are consecutively numbered.  The only down side, is the price of entrance tickets  about $20 for foreigners  but then I found that the cost of living in Sri Lanka is quite high in general and I enjoyed my visit immensely.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Plenty of room for improvement
Text: There are plenty of lovely corners to discover in this - confined urban - zoo. And plenty of other corners you'd rather not see at all. The recently opened bird-sanctuary is beautiful, but why does it host roosters (!) while the leopards - the king of Sri Lankan mammals - are still in a tiny cage that looks (and smells) more like a mid-eval toilet cage. And while some serious renovation is taking place, the elephants new enclosure looks more like the average hotel pool with terrace while it could have looked so much more natural if only they had copied some ideas from other zoo's (even via the Internet). People in wheelchairs and parents with children buggies should be aware that moving about will be a challenge here and there. Apart from this, it is a great location to spot some of the most pretty female Sri Lankan Homo sapiens around as the zoo is a safe haven for young couples that are evading critical eyes of their parents while getting to know each other.Note that foreigners pay 2500 LKR (versus 100 LKR for locals). Diplomates are excluded (!!) but they will have to pay an additional 100 LKR for parking their Mercedes 600 SEL's in front of the zoo. Best time to visit, mornings / beginning of the week. Try to avoid school holidays as it can get super crowded (and there are plenty of them in Sri Lanka). When the street is full of parked buses, go to (nearby) Mount Lavinia beach instead. One star for some of the badly caged animals, three stars for the pleasant atmosphere. Average 2 stars.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: There is a lot to improve
Text: The entrance is very expensive for the tourists (now it's 2500 rs.). The territory is rather large and green, but some amilals are kept in very bad conditions. Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Very expensive for tourists
Text:
The zoo charges 100 rupees for locals but 2000 rupees for tourists!  The zoo is larger than you would anticipate.  There are a few nice exhibits, but most animals are housed in very small concrete and metal cages.  There are a lot of rats, especially in the bird areas.  The elephants are chained, and forced to perform daily.  The big cat enclosures are literally crumbling.  There is little provided in terms of enrichment for the animals.  However, I have seen worse zoos in third world countries before.  At least the zoo workers aren't banging on the cages for money.  And the cages were clean.

There is a variety of animals from all parts of the world.  The highlight for me was the sloth bear.  We did not see one in the wild during safari, so it was good to see what we missed.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka

A nice green place but sad the way they treat the animals.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Dehiwala Zoo in Colombo
Text: Walked at leisure around the zoo, viewing some unique exhibits that i saw for the first time in my life despite visiting  some of the world's best zoo's, including zoo's back home in India.Actually i had not included the "Dehiwala  National zoo" in my tour itinerary as  a review i read about it  was negative , besides, i had visited some of the World's best zoo's.It was the weather and continuous rains that made me visit the Dehiwala National zoo, not intending to waste a precious day sitting in the confines of my lonely  hotel room.In hindsight i thank the rains for leading me to the Dehiwala National zoo in Colombo.Saw the Lemur, Pygmy Hippo, eagle owl, rusty spotted cat and the  Arabian Orynx for the first time in my life.The Arabian Orynx extinct in the wild were  thriving in captivity at the Dehiwala zoo,a large herd being  bred in captivity.The original wild horses called the  Przewalski horse from Hungary was the rarest of rare exhibit at the zoo.Only a few hundred survive in the wild forests of Hungary. Hence i saw two of the World's rarest endangered species at the  Dehiwala zoo in Colombo, the Arabian Orynx and the Przewalski horse.The zoo also had white tigers, tigers, lions, leopards, puma's,giraffes, zebra's,rhino's and  elephants to name a few of the  large herbivores and carnivores that are rare in most zoo's.Wonder which  zoo in the World  was the gentleman comparing "Dehiwala National zoo" during his review, saying it was a bad zoo.The "Dehiwala National zoo" in Colombo was definitely one of the World's better maintained zoo's, although some enclosures were small, a common problem with most zoo's.Remember, read a variety of reviews and blogs on the Internet before taking a decision on a particular subject or on planning a tour.Everyone has an opinion and free to express the same on the Internet, including me.

Title: Zoo
Text: Liked the fauna and the species of the animals kept. The turn off part was the elephant dance display which was so much boosted by the travel agents and the botel people but sadly it was a very substandard display of elephant so called display.

Title: AN ABSOLUTE SHOCKER!!!
Text: i've visited many zoo's before around the world but this one has to top them all of being the WORST zoo i have ever been to in my life! i was sicken and distaught and absolutely disgusted at the way the animals were kept in this place. i've added some pics please check to see how the animals are being kept. The most shocking for me was these fish called arapaima which are very large fish and the tank that they were in was not enough even for them to move around in. I felt sick! the second reason and final which made me just walk out of the place was the elephants and how they were tied up to the chains. i understand to tame and control these elephant a chain is often placed around the neck and around the ankle so they don't start running off but despite that i prefer that were at least the animal can still move around freely but at the zoo they were all 15 of them were tied up with the back leg and the front so much so that they had no movement what so ever to move around. what broke me down and even now as i'm back home is bringing a tear to my eye was seeing one of the elephant looking at me and it raised one of its chained legs. now you don't have to be a zoologist to realise that it was saying to me please release this off my leg. absolute heart breaking!!. These guys that should be looking at the walfare of these animals have absolutely no regard for them what so ever. i don't know. maybe in this part of the world its acceptable to treat animals like this but any person who has a humain side to them would thick once before doing what the zoo keepers are doing in colombo zoo. i would recommend foreigners stay away from this hell hole that charges 2,000 rupees to see what hell animals are living in!!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Poor and bordering on animal cruelty
Text: This was one of my favourite locations when I was a kid as it was the only exposure we really had to exotic creatures like giraffes, zebras, etc but on a recent visit I was appalled. Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Dehivela gardens
Text: This zoo, situated in beautiful gradens, just simply has a lot to catch-up. It needs a competent and a gentle renovation, so the spirit will be saved, while enclosures and living conditions for the animals gets modernized.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: best In South Asia
Text: Its a nice Little Zoo for a small county like Sri Lanka. manage well, I have been couple of times in the paste the Elephant dance is a must See. the Sea Water Aquarium is very nice . its worth visiting

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Animals are in a horrible condition
Text: At least 10 animals at the zoo had died under questionable circumstances in the past three months, but nothing had been done to improve conditions for the animals.Dehiwala zoo has today become a hell hole, not only for its many animals but also for the hundreds of visitors who go there.Many horrible stories are related by visitors with regard to cruelty to animals at the zoo.
