Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Great attraction for kids
Text: Liked the acquarium the best. A little sad to see animals caged. It is a  place to learn about animals and the variety is large. Still enjoy visiting the zoo every year.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Zoo which even adults can enjoy
Text: Knowing the sad condition of the zoo in Mumbai I was apprehensive to visit the zoo in Colombo, but was surprised to see the excellent condition in which the zoo was maintained. The animals are healthy, well looked after, the surroundings are also green and we could see a large variety of animals especially the pygmy hippopotamus, the regal tigers, ancient tortoise etc. The directions given in the zoo for the path to follow to view animals were clear and precise, we never got lost or repeated the animals.A must visit for children and adults !

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: The Colombo Zoo Trip
Text:
Likes - the space, directions are clear & the orangutan enclosure was quite cute
Disliked - Massive crowds, a regular zoo, nothing spectacular & found lot of people teasing animals, lot of rubbish strewn around everywhere, some of the places like aquarium, reptile enclosure,  people are pushing/jostling around - maybe because it was a holiday!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Rip off - 20 times higher entry fee for foreigners.....
Text: The first thing what I noticed was that Sri Lankan nationals have to pay 100 Rp but everyone else 2,000. This is a rip off. The zoo itself has nice gardens but the cages for the animals are old, too small and dirty. You really feel for them in their much too small prison. Can't recommend it at all.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice afternoon at Dehiwala Zoo
Text:
We visited Dehiwala zoo on a holiday day and the queue was very big, but the people were very civilized and the staff was very efficient .
The entry ticket's price was very fair compared to other attractions, and considering the income of the locals it's only fair to have prices to allow their children to enjoy the zoo.
The zoo was very nice on my opinion, many rare animals and birds; beautiful trees, bushes and flowers pleased our eyes.
There was plenty of food for the animals and the elephants were carrying food for the gazelles , delighting  the children.
Everybody enjoyed the afternoon that day at the zoo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Fab day out!
Text:

if you ahve children its a must visit!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A nice day out
Text: The zoo is okay for a day out, it's an escape from the city noise, the birds are awesome, the cafe is not so good best take a picnic, the cost for UK residents is a bit steep, at 2500 rupees per person, locals pay 100,   I don't understand the price difference, in the UK everyone pays the same regardless of nationality,

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: National Zoological Garden of Sri Lanka
Text:
This is popularly known as Dehiwela Zoo in Sri Lanka. This is one of the oldest zoological garden in Asia. There are around 300 varieties of species located in an ideal environment. 
Elephant rides, pony rides, restaurants, boat riding,icecream shop, and a souvenir shop are available facilities for the visitors..

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Lots of Elephants
Text: Sri Lanka is an amazing country for tourism.  Mountains, beaches, history and culture.  One site not to be missed is the National Zoological Gardens.  The primary attraction is their collection of elephants, big one small ones, and babies.  Several times a day the elephants rush to the river to play in the cool waters.  I was more or less trapped between this stampede of elephants and a stone building.  Fortunately the elephants followed a straight line and did not find me worth a detour.  Watching them in the river is a must see for everyone.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A Zoo Which Requires A Lot Of Improvement
Text:
If you are a tourist looking for things to do during your stay in Colombo-avoid the zoo. You d be disappointed at the price you pay to enter, the conditions of facilities, health of animals. 

Dehiwela Zoo used to be much better managed not too long ago. Its spread over a large area with amazing scenery and wide ranging terrain. It also had a large collection of animals. But somethings gone wrong somewhere down the line and the zoo requires serious attention of relevant authority.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: 2-3 hours in Dehiwala zoo for aquarium, birds and animals for 700LKR(SAARC tourist)!
Text:
My husband is animal lover, hence he selected this zoo as our first destination in Sri Lanka. On 6th December, 2015 we both headed to this place around 2.15PM. As it was Sunday, saw local crowd as well as some tourists like us. As I knew there will be language problem to communicate with people if we found lost in this zoo, I asked for map and carried away with that as guide. 

Must see:
Bird show, Elephant show, Aquarium, Snakes, Chimpanzee, Gorilla, Parrots.

Experience:
+ve :-
Time management: Bird and Elephant show punctual.
Proper food allocated to birds and animals.
Trained so well that I saw Indie named elephant rehearsing on his own before show.
Toilets/Washroom are comparatively clean.
No extra charges for Cameras and Toilet/Washroom use.

-ve :-
Language: Both shows(Birds and Elephant) in Sinhala language(local language of Sri Lanka). This is difficult to understand for foreign tourists. So carried away with birds and elephants gestures only.

Maintenance: Found many area under construction, which not allowing some of the cages to view. Some areas stinks badly that have to put cloth/napkin over nose(No idea if it's because of animals or uncleanliness).

Empty cages: There were few cages which were emptied, even white tiger was missing(though there was name plate).
No lion but 2 baby lions.

College couples: Seems this place is more for college going couples who spend quality time here.

Entry tickets: Improper price range for tourists compare to local people.
(2500LKR for Foreign Tourists;
700LKR for SAARC Tourist;
only 100 LKR for Residents)

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Some animals looks really bad, some better
Text:
Zoo was bigger than i expected. It had a lot of animals. 
Some of the animals looks really bad, especially lions and tigers.

We did this on our first day in Sri Lanka, and it was fine. But i would not go again, because some of the animals looked so bad. 

Food and drinks are cheap there, and food was good.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Expensive option

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Really bad
Text: This is a very good example of a very bad zoo.  The animals are housed in small cages and are not in very good condition.  Huge crowds of locals who taunt and tease the animals and none of the officials seems to care.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Appalling
Text: This place is a disgrace.  The animals look in poor condition and are mostly in small cages.  The elephant show is degrading for the animals and the whole place seems mismanaged and without care for animals

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: it's not the worst place in the world, but it's not far off
Text:
they are trying to renovate the place in 2012- and clearly lots of colombo kids love it, as the grounds can get very crowded at weekends and from 4pm onwards

But if you want to kill an hour, with kids under 8, it's OK.  Once.

But I agree with the reviewers who have said the zoo discredits itself with this 'foreigner' policy

I had two staff pointing and shouting "foreigner" at me as we went to pay; like i was a wild tiger escaped from a cage, while the staff then proceeded to insist to my (sri lankan) wife that our two kids looked like foreigners and so should pay the higher rate

The zoo can't make that much extra money from this policy, and probably lose so much good will and potential visitors.

My wife left saying it was embarrassing.  For her.  And for her culture.  It was unpleasant and embarrassing.

We of course will never go back.

And the zoo should change that foreigner' policy.  It's insulting.  I wonder how the average Sri Lankan would react if e.g. they tried to get into a zoo in Europe and faced the same discrimination?  They'd probably be insulted too!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A good place to go with kids.
Text:
Went with my 2 year old daughter in July '2012. 

You indeed need a full day to walk around the zoo. And doing that with my 2 year old kid was a bit difficult. But at the end of day, my kid loved the experience and after the visit she started recognizing lot of animals on TV by name.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Never visit!
Text: Wild animals are meant to be in the wild, this is not a zoological gardens in a European sense, so do not expect it to be.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Needs to improve their representation .
Text: I visited the zoo with my kid July 2012, I did not find it much interesting.Natural environment is not provided for animals, more space surely is needed, although they have got good variety of animals .

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Animals need more care
Text:
Though this zoo has a good line up of animals but it seems that the authorities are just not interested in feeding them. All the animals are very skinny in this zoo which definitely is not a good sight. 
The worst part is that the tigers, lion, leopards are kept in such small cages - they can't even take 2 steps in the same direction ... they just have to keep taking rounds in order to take a walk. Being an animal lover ... i didn't like this. 
I mean that its good to showcase animals to the world but not by hurting them this badly... 
I mean i did get to see a lot of rare animals here but definitely didn't expect to see them in this condition.. especially in a country like Sri Lanka where animals are pampered so well, like in the great Elephant orphanage at the pinnewala.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: A great day out
Text: Wander through the trees and gardens, absorb the scents and listen to the wildlife that lives here. Look out for the fruit bats overhead and visit the orchid greenhouses

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Dehiwela Zoo
Text: I visited this place for the second time after my first visit way back about 15 years,the standard has deteroiated has not made any improvement,not worth the visit

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Very scary.
Text: May be snakes can come out. Not kept the place well & clean. seems like more space needed. good to spend sometimes with nature & animals.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Good compared to other zoos I have visited
Text: I have visited the Zoo in SIngapore, Minnesota, USA and this is better in variety. But might be not good as in presentation and providing the details.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice break from the craziness outside!
Text:
OK, so I'm making it my mission to go to a zoo (or two) in every place I visit.  The guide book said it was 500 rupees (well it was a few years out of date but that must have been for the locals as it was 2,000 rupees for tourists). Some of the enclosures were very small and sparse, BUT they are doing a huge amount of work to improve some of the enclosures. We went early in the morning, arriving at 10am when it was still quite cool, the surrounding gardens provide some nice shad palces. The only down side was we had completed it all in about 3 hrs and all the animal feeding times were in the afternoon.

There is a large selection of animals and birds to see, and worth the 1hr drive from Kalutara (we booked a taxi through our hotel to take us) it made a nice 1/2 day trip.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Very Poorly maintained.
Text: I do not know why our chuffer took us to this place. The Zoo is in horible condition, needs lot's of improvement. I felt the animals are just congested in this place and it's not justified as to why this place kept in such delapidated condition.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Ok
Text: Very well laid out zoo BUT the cages are WAY too small esp. for the lions and tigers, the poor elephants are chained up and are clearly in distress due to lack of food and water and with the heat, you can see signs of neglect where the chains have rubbed the ankles of the elephants  was a really sad sight to see.  Do not visit on the weekend if you dont want to be part of the zoo and to be stared at by the locals.  Locals pay 100 rupees compared to 2000 rupees that foreigners pay!  This place could be great if more space was given to the poor animals, allow the elephants to roam freely, and the monkeys! And to feed them more, we sneaked grass in for the giraffes and other animals!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: If you like animals dont go there!
Text:
I went to the Zoo in Colombo; I made it a habit, going to the Zoo in any country I visit.
Most people go to the Zoo because they like animal, well this Zoo is not for these people.
The animals look like they are suffering.
The cages are small, the elephants are chained in the front leg and in the back leg, they cannot move forward or backwards.
There almost no special animal. The only attraction is the white tiger.
The whole place looks like its in construction.
Very Very poor. 
The admission fees written are 2000 Rope, but I guess that is only for Europeans and Americans, because the guy in front of me told me to give a different country and so I pay only 500 Rope.
I dont mind paying the 2000 but it doesnt look good.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Its an experience
Text:
Very old zoo; if you are animal lover, then it may be distressing.  They do their best, but it really needs some major works done to it to bring it up to world standards for the animals.
The elephant show was the highlight and enjoyed the experience even though there was not many foreigners in the zoo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Sri Lanka Zoo
Text: It is very fantastic...you are able to reach within one hour from Colombo.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Busy zoo with lots of people
Text: There are some rare animals. However, the space for animals seemed inadequate. We went on a holiday and it was full of people.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Nice Zoo
Text:
Big zoo with a lot of animals there. However it seems like they are going through renovation process so seems a bit like a construction site when you are walking there.

Also the recommended path along the zoo seems a bit complicated, but we are a bit topography-challenged.

Otherwise pretty good.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: good one!!
Text: A really nice time was spent here considering i have 2 teenagers....Entrance fee is nominal and a fee for a camera as well ..Video cams not allowed inside. superb variety. Very unique birds and nocturnal animals . A large area to cover..needs about 2hrs. A little crowded though..esp.the beautiful big leopards, panthers and some lions..felt  sad..Dissapointed that there was no elephant show as promised.

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Spices
Text: If you hv botanical interests do land here for say 30 minutes and not more! Guide will do all to goad into buying spices! Advise please do not offer more than 25 per of total value and stick to it!99per u will win!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Expensive & Dirty
Text:
Although the guide books tell you this Zoo is relatively good, we didn't really enjoy our experience.  There is a massive range of animals but they were living in quite cramped and dirty conditions.  It's also quite expensive for non Sri Lankans to get in. 

If you go - take mossie repellant!

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Lovely Zoo
Text: Its a very well maintained zoo. Can find a variety of animals and even some rare species..

Location_Name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka
Title: Small dirty enclosures exorbitant foreigner charges
Text:
The charge for foreigners is 2000rs at the time of our visit. As we had made our way the Colombo from our resort in Bentota we bit the bullet, though I think that 100 times the price for locals is a totally unacceptable (and probably illegal for this type of differentiation in most other countries, but an accepted practice in Sri Lanka). I'm not a big fan of zoos as a matter of principle but thought I couldn't miss the opportunity to see some rare species of tigers and leopards from Asia.
The first thing that hit me was that the enclosures stank of urine and had dried faeces smeared across the walls where the leopards, monkeys and buffalo were. 
The African and Indian elephants had manacles which chained them to the ground and allowed approximately 1m of movement.
The snake tanks were very small for the size of some of the cobras and I imagine lead to potential overheating during the hot season with little or no access to water pools.
I'm by no means an anminal activist or anything but it really upset me the state of the conditions for most of these animals, especially while there are boards proudly displaying that several million rs has been spent on staff accommodation and paving around the zoo.
There are a couple of food stalls selling ice cream and various refreshments.

Title: Ancient and beautiful
Text: The oldest stupa in Sri Lanka, and really beautiful. It's not the biggest, but it is one of the most beautiful we saw. The surrounding pillars once supported a roof, so you get a sense of the size of the building in which it once sat. If touring Anuradhapura this is a site you should not miss.

Title: Water everywhere...
Text: We got pissed of when visiting this stupa, coz they poured water everywhere on the top which made dry flower offerings become disgusting and one should walk around in this mess without shoes?

Title: The First Dagoba
Text:
Thuparamaya is the oldest dagoba of Sri Lanka. It was built over an ancient Hindu temple. The dagoba is surrounded by the ruins of the yore that give a scenic look to the place. The locals in white attire make the place look like a lake full of swans.

One must carry a pair of socks to visit this place as we have to walk barefoot that gives a feel of firewalk.

Title: Srilanka's first Dagoba
Text:
Historical stupa and still magnificent to look at. It supposedly contains the Buddha's collarbone.

It helps to wear socks as walking up to the  site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet.

Title: Oldest dagoba and great moonstone by small temple ruin. Get out of the car!
Text: It's not as big as some other temples but beautiful nonetheless and I believe the oldest in Anuradhapura. The small ruined temple to the right has some lovely carvings at the steps and a beautifully preserved moonstone. Nice to wander around for a few mins

Title: Divine
Text: We visited this place along with Family during Christmas holidays and it is a great place to visit and pay homage

Title: Quick stop along the way
Text: This is one of the smallest dagobas in the area and can be visited along the way from one sacred site to another. If you plan to see all 8 sacred sites, this one can be done en route and you may not even have to get out of the car.

Title: All Dagobas, must visit!
Text: All the Stupas and Dagobas must be visited!! They are sort of similar but different in their own way :) Some are massive while some of smaller in size.

Title: Thuparamaya Stupa at Anuradhapura is worth a visit
Text: This is a compact(small)stupa, said to be containing the collar bone of Buddha,in that respect  it is an important  shrine.A walk around the stupa is recommended.

Title: Disappointed  because it is reconstructed
Text: Small, but sacred to to Buddhists, this stupa claims the title of the "first one built in Sri Lanka." It offers a great Kodak moment, but I was disappointed to learn that the structure is not ancient at all, but rather a reconstruction undertaken in the mid-19th century. Out guide told us that it was not even rebuilt in the correct shape!

Title: Smallest but nicer dagoba
Text: I went to see this beautiful place in the morning which was great because there was almost no people and the stone ground was still cool. This dagoba is much different from the others, first because it isn´t that big and second because of the stone columns surrounding it. This dagoba is very sacred to Buddhists because they believe that there is the collarbone of the Buddha inside. Next to this dagoba ther are the ruins of ancient temple which is worth seeng as well.

Title: Thuparamaya - Oldest Stupa in Sri Lanka
Text: Thuparamaya is the oldest stupa in Sri Lanka and the first to be built in the country after the introduction of Buddhism. It was built in the time of King Devamnampiyatissa (247BC  207BC) enshrining the collarbone relic of Gauthama Buddha which was brought to Sri Lanka by Arahat Mahinda, son of King Ashoka of India.

Title: Oldest Stupa in Anuradhapura
Text:
This is the oldest Stupa in Anuradhapura, probably in Sri Lanka itself.
Smaller in size, but quite attractive. This is a functioning temple and hence dress properly (you will see the local people wearing white dress) and remove Shoes and hat while entering the temple.
The floor gets very hot during the day and hence better to wear the socks.

Title: Different
Text: I have to say that this was my favorite sight in Anuradhapura as it was very different from the other places we looked around.  To see this dagoba was just tantalizing as it has these pillars around it that make you think of Roman or Greek ruins instead of Asian.  The pillars were used to support the roof that once spanned over the dagoba to protect it.  You have to go and see it for yourself to truly understand

Title: Tremendously atmospheric
Text: We really enjoy visiting this place, which has a unique atmosphere. One of the great pleasures of Anuradhapura is the fact that no two constructions are alike and this one is different because of its wonderful columns or pillars which rise some 12 feet into the air in from of it giving the appearance a statement of grandeur. The whole construction is small compared to other buildings in the cultural centre but it is beautifully located in green surroundings and well worth visiting.

Title: Sacred place
Text:
Sri Lanka first - but probably one of the oldest still be seen all over the world - stupa and Theravada Buddhism's most sacred place. No too big, but very charming and the structure of circle sanctuary (vatadage) very interesting. Don't miss it!

Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes.
I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

Title: Stunningly beautiful and photogenic dagoba
Text: Reputedly the oldest dagoba in the world, Thuparama is surrounded by carefully placed pillars which enhance the visual appeal dramatically. They certainly knew how to present a building back then! It is also situated in a lovely green parkland area. If you're lucky, you'll have a brilliant blue sky as contrast for your photographs.

Title: A very old and important dagoba site
Text: This is a much restored but very old and important dagoba site, quite small in comparison to the others in the area but very much venerated.

Title: The best visit in all Anuradhapura
Text:
For us, this was the best visit in all the Unesco site. The columns around the dagoba give it a unique charm and "special" feeling, compared with the similar looking (in style) constructions. It's nice to visit by bike.

When researching for the trip, we decided against Polonnoruwa because Anura would be more atmospheric, mystical and alive. After speaking with other travelers and seeing pictures, I think Polo would have maybe been nicer. 

What I do find abusive is the entrance fee: 25 dollars is way too much, even if you get a DVD in the package. Most other tourists, guides, people from GHs agreed that much harm is done with these exaggerated prices and the cancellation of the combo ticket. A normal day salary in SL is 1200 rupees. One hour in a bus, is less than 100 rupees. A normal rice and curry costs around 300 - 500 rupees. How on earth can you justify 3259 rupees to pay for an entrance ticket??? I understand we pay more than the locals, but this is probably 40 or 50 times more. Probably to pay a Government with approximately 60 ministers, many of them opponents, friends and family to the President..........

Title: A place of Worship
Text:
Considered the oldest Buddhist stupa in Sr Lanka, built in the 1st Century BC. 
Calm and quiet, respectful,place of worship

Title: Another dagoba
Text: Festivities were on and some procession was in progress when we were there. Looked better than other dagobas in Anuradhapura.

Title: Holiest Place in Anuradhapura
Text:
This site does not attract the tourist crowds that the Ruwanwellseya does yet it possesses the holiest relic, namely the collarbone of Buddha. Small and recently restored it is surrounded by columns which once held up a roof. Similar columns abound all over this vast archaeological site. All are remnants of buildings and their role are roof props. 

It retains an odd air of peace and serenity in a site which is mobbed at times of Poya, especially in June

Title: Interesting Dagoba with protruding pillars
Text: The main dagoba does not look very impressive as compared to other Dagoba in Anuradhapura Temple site. But what I find interesting about this temple is it has numerous ancient looking pillars jutting out about 12 ft  high around the main dagoba. Some are vertical and some are tilted. Some are spread over the floor. Not sure the reasons for their existence. Probably to serve as a legacy of the original temple.  As in all temples compound in Sri Lanka, you need to remove your footwear to enter. You need to bear with the afternoon heat and hot floor surface. The crude surface floor is just bearable to walk around.

Title: Most beautiful stupa in Anuradhapura
Text:
Compared to Ruwanwelisaya Pagoda, the Anuradhapura stupa is much smaller. Nevertheless, I personally like this stupa and its stone pillars around. It is considered the first stupa in Sri Lanka. 

Since it is one of the most sacred places in Anuradhapura, there are always a few religious rituals performed here every weekend. We unexpectedly arrived on a saturday and could witness and took part in those rituals. The locals wear all-white clothes to enter the place, bringing lotus and various offerings to the stupa. 

The surrounding is peaceful and calm. Highly recommended to visit. 

Entrance ticket to the entire Anuradhapura site is USD 25 / pax.

Title: Impressive Dagoba (or Stupa).
Text: This is an enormous Stupa of great signifcance.  It is almost too big to photograph so we have more memories than pictures.  Take socks (as this is a 'working' religious site you have to remove your shoes and store them for a few rupees).  We visited near mid day which was too hot, it would have been better earlier or later in the day, but a magnificant sight.

Title: The highlight of our explorations
Text: This was a highlight for me during our explorations of Anuradhapura. The dagoba is beautiful, peaceful and the pillars around it look simply stunning. It makes for an incredible photo, and an even better experience to stand there and see it for yourself.

Title: Wear some thick socks!
Text: I visited the week before a full moon festival so the Dagoba was white washed and looked amazing. As with all Buddhist temples you need to take off your shoes before going in and as my review title says wear socks. Unfortunately I didn't follow my own advise and with my visit being at noon the sand and bricks were so hot I had to run between shade. That aside the Dagoba was impressive and well worth a visit. Also a short walk to see the Sacred Bo tree which is 2000 years old.

Title: A different stupa surrounded by with all the old pillars at odd angles
Text: This stupa features on the cover of one of the editions of Lonely Planet so you can have fun trying to match up the picture. (we succeeded) It is an attractive small stupa but the pillars impart a somewhat surreal atmosphere. One of the problems with many of the stupas here is that you are expected to removed shoes and hats in the blistering heat. OK for locals who are used to it but hard for soft westerners. We pleaded that we had a problem with skin cancer and they let us off except right at the shrines. Entry fee to Anuradhapura was also extortionately high for foreigners.

Title: Ok, small and uninspiring
Text: Unlike most of the Dagobas, it was small with a few pillars with a small shrine. Very much a recommend to those Buddhists. As a simple tourist it wasn't spectacular.

Title: Active religious site
Text: The atmosphere at this stupa site was really good, with pilgrims actively worshipping and living feeling about the place.  The monkeys stealing and eating the lotus flowers within moments of pilgrims placing them at the shrines was initially very funny to watch, but ultimately telling about the pilgrims' acceptance of the greater circle of life and existence as they weren't bothered by the monkeys' behavior as many people would be.  A lesson to be learned.

Title: Definitely Photogenic
Text:
Although a smaller stupa, it is much more photogenic due to the many pillars surrounding it. The temple is still being used and there was a prayer ceremony going on when I visited the place.

Easy to get in. No ticket checks.

Title: Very photogenic
Text: Good place to stop for a photo and short visit! The stupa is a good blend of old and new and the grounds are well kept. We visited in the afternoon and the stones were hot so get ready for some shadow to shadow hopping.

Title: Beautiful and serene
Text: This was featured on the latest cover of the Lonely Planet guide book, to see it in real was breath taking, it's a lovely subject for photography. Do make a point to see it in sun set.

Title: Thuparama
Text:
Thuparama, a brick-built gedige (Sinhala: vaulted shrine) is in a fine state of preservation. Thuparma, the oldest image house at Polonnaruwa goes back the reign of King Vijayabahu the first (1055-1110 A.D.).

A brick base about one meter high with three projections once carried an image of Buddha, which is now simple a pile of bricks. The stone images in the Thuparama date back to Anuradhapura period.

Title: A nice Dagoba from Ancient times
Text: Well kept Dagoba is nice to visit.  However, we found most Dagoba's to be very similar.

Title: Amazing little temple
Text: I like this temple since it shows the old remains and the remoddled stupa in white, so you can see the contrast of old and new. The whole visit takes only 5 minutes.

Title: A truely picturesque stupa surrounded by a vatadage
Text:
The oldest stupa in Sri Lanka, it is said to enshrine the clavicle of Buddha.
The current stupa is a later renovation of the original stupa erected by Devanampiya Tissa in the 3rd century BC. The current bell-shaped stupa is encircled by smaller shrines and stone pillars that 'may' have supported a wooden roof.

Title: Ancient, Beautiful, plus great paintings
Text: The pillars make the temple looks stunning. There are many ancient rocks around the area. The temple itself is pretty.

Title: Another religious and historical place
Text: This would be one of the list of temples in your tour. Must see the moon stone near the entrance. The pillars are very tempting.

Title: lovely
Text: We came to visit at the time of the holiday so there were a lot of Buddhists. They did not mind, as I believe that they are constantly interupted by the tourists.

Title: Small dagoba, but interesting due to the surrounding columns
Text: A smaller dagoba, compared to its larger brothers, but particularly interesting due to the circular columns (actually two circles) that surround the building itself. It is one of the ten-ish places you have to visit in Anuradhapura.

Title: Last stupa of the day and exhausted
Text: Unfortunately this was our last stop in a big day out of sightseeing.The monks were meditating whilst we were there and I didnt want to get in their way.The floor was boiling and I had to move quickly and hop around to stop my feet burning.Not much different to other Dagobas that we visited

Title: Spread out
Text: The stupa and its immediate surrounding buildings and the art work and carvings in the building are remarkable, but the larger area also has many more interesting ruins.

Title: saw from the car
Text: it was so under whelming that we didn't even get out of the car to see it. took photos becausee the guide insisted we do it.

Title: Oldest  Stupa in Sri Lanka
Text:
Thuparamaya  is the oldest  Dagaba in Sri Lanka . It   has a unique architectural feature called "vatadage", 
This  stupa was built by  King Dewanampiyatissa.  
 must visit ...sacred place to visit

Title: The earliest Dagoba to be constructed in the Island
Text:
The Thuparamaya Stupa is the earliest Dagoba to be constructed in the island, dating back to the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (247-207 BC). 

It is just few minutes away from Ruwanweliseya. If you are in Ruwanweliseya and have some minutes to spare should visit this. Since this is a sacred place please don't wear short skirts and exposing blouses. Also if you are visiting on day time it can be very hot, recommend wearing socks.

Title: Its all part of the entrance fee....
Text: Yes another Stupa in another former city. The thing with this is that it has clearly gone under same maintenance that to my mind takes away an element of its history.

Title: Most religious stupa
Text: This seemed to be the most religious stupa in the complex with the amount of the people around when I visited and also the various offerings that were being performed here.

Title: Wear socks
Text: If you're going to do the Sacred city tour - wear socks. We didn't and our feet got so hot - by the time we got to this stupa we couldn't be bothered getting out of the tuk tuk

Title: Smaller, but still impressive
Text: This is one of the smaller stupa's in Anuradhapura, but has more going on at the site than the others and is quite impressive to see. There is more around the area as well, with some ruins from the monastery. As with all temples, you must remove your shoes and dress appropriately. Be aware that the ground can get very hot indeed!

Title: Architectural jewel!!
Text: This is really an architectural jewel of Anuradhapura!! If you visit it in the dry and hot season (for example, in April), bring a pair of socks!!

Title: A small stupa which situated close to ruwanmeliseya stupa
Text:
This is the one of the first stupa that is build in Sri lanka .

Its not much bigger as other stupas that we see here in Anuradhapura but there s a belief that there was a roof around the stupa but now there s no such roof but we can see the stone pillars around the stupa.

Title: A Kind Of Interesting Place
Text:
This is one of the earliest monuments of the country and so from that point of view worth a visit. It was not something that takes a great deal of time in itself but it is another one of these places which is a bit of a trek by car to get to. 

There is not a lot to see as such and I suppose a visit here might be more meaningful or interesting if you are lucky enough to get there when there is any ceremony or something like that going on.

Title: Spiritual highs
Text: Aftrer an afternoon of visiting dagobas and participatiing in some of the ceremonies we climbed to the top of a lookout where I interacted with local people, sharing a laugh and small talk. I saw a sunset from the topmost tower, offered flowers and took in the sights.

Title: One of the great stupas
Text: One of the great massive stupas around Anuradhapura, although with little to see up close. Offers one of the most iconic photos in the area.

Title: Nice Place
Text: We did not go inside this Stupa but we did see when we were on our way to Abhayagiri Dagoba. Its beautifully lit with diyas during evening.

Title: Ruins are Interesting
Text: Enjoyed the grounds more than the Dagoba. It is a very spiritual place but it was just another Dagoba to me. Had hoped for more.

Title: Magnificent Stupa
Text: There were quite a lot of people the time I was here. What a really interesting place to visit. Once again, a sacred place to visit, so be respectful. Nice construction, such a holy place to be.

Title: Reconstruction of the original
Text: Reportedly the first stupa constructed in Sri Lanka, it has clearly been heavily reconstructed and the shrines are very modern even looking a bit dukeboxy. Part of the collarbone of the Buddha is believed to be enshrined here, so it is a place of pilgrimage. However, unlike the Boo tree site the atmosphere here is a bit surreal, with someone announcing on a microphone the names of those who have donated and how much.

Title: The first recorded stupa in Sri Lanka
Text:
The first recorded stupa to be built in Sri Lanka and the legend goes that it enshrines the collarbone of the Buddha . It is a little gem that more than holds its own amongst the larger dagobas in Anuradhapura. For me, it is special given the large number of pilgrims when I visited.

PS wear socks if you are visiting during the day - the stones you walk on get hot!

Title: Really beautiful and serene
Text: As for all the dagobas here, this is really worth seeing and imagining the scale and beauty of the place in its heyday.

Title: The Oldest Dagoba in Anuradhapura
Text:
Thuparamaya Dagobah
Thuparamaya Dagobah is the oldest historical structure and first stupa built in 3rd century after the introduction of Buddhism in Sri Lanka by King Devanampiyatissa on the request of Mahinda, an envoy of Ashoka, the great Emperor of India. The collarbone of Mahatma Buddha was enshrined in this Dagobah
Thuparamaya is derived from the words "stupa" and "aramaya" which means residential complex for bhikshus, hermits and monks. During the course of history, this dagobah was destroyed and rebuilt many times. The present monument was built in 1862 in the shape of a bell with a diameter of 60 feet

Title: The area around Anuradhapura is wonderful
Text: So much to take in and so many Stupas to take in, the twin ponds are also worth visiting and there are some lovely local snacks to be had by the side of the ponds.  The sacred tree is worth visiting and it is interesting to watch the locals wait for a leaf to fall from it, apparently one of the oldest trees in the world the Sri Maha Bodhi has been lovingly tended for 23 centuries.

Title: Archeological site with some ruins...
Text: This is the first Buddhist Temple in Sri Lanka, built since 3rd century, to house the right collar-bone of Buddha. There are nearby ruins site with some interesting stone carvings especially the famous Moondtone carvings which is semicircular usually stood at the foot of first step in Buddhist buildings/ temple. We even explored further to the Elephant Pond as the given name is due to the huge size of the pond. More details to see along the history of Anuradhapura Kingdom in relation to Buddhism culture. It is inclusive in the entrance fee of USD25 or LKR4,550 for the Anuradhapura ancient sites. Hiring a driver is necessary to the scarcity of the site.

Title: Nice Holy Site
Text: The oldest of the sacred sites in this area although heavily restored. Has a nice atmosphere and is worth seeing as part of the sacred city

Title: THE AREA'S FIRST DAGOBA
Text: The first dagoba, or stupa, in the area was built to house the right collar bone relic of the Budddha. It was likely the first dagoba built in the country after the introduction of Buddhism. Its root 'aramaya' is a residential complex for monks. This was a photo only visit without access.

Title: Nice
Text: The structure is inspiring - pious worshippers, statues of Lord Buddha all around, calm ambience - your mind is busy wondering!

Title: Nice Dagoba
Text: Nice dagoba with usually many religious people clad in white attire praying, making for an interesting photo op

Title: Sacred Site
Text:
One of several important Ancient moments at Anuradhapura. Quite striking.

Be sure to dress modestly (no shorts, or bare shoulders for women) to be respectful.

Also required to remove shoes, and be prepared the sand surrounding the dragons can get very hot, and has the occasional sharp stones.

Title: Thuparama Dagoba
Text: Thuparama  Dagoba is one of the smallest dagobas but it is apparently the oldest of the dagobas. It is a fascinating place to visit and is busy with worshippers and full of life as a result.I suggest that you have socks with you as if you are walking around barefoot the floor can get really hot.

Title: Well worth a stop during a tour of Anuradhapura - and no entrance fee
Text: Visited Thuparama during a cycle tour of the various dagobas in Anuradhapure. Thuparama is one of the smaller dagobas in town but it's the most fascinating as it's one of the most popular places of worship in Anuradhapura (unlike many of the others) and is full of life as a result.  It's also said to be the oldest Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. A visit won't take long at all but its well worth it. It easy to find a spot to lock up a bike too.  There's no entrance fee to visit. Just make sure you take socks as if you are walking around barefoot the floor can get really hot.

Title: One of the oldest "Stupa" of Sri Lanka depicting Buddhist culture
Text: Thuparama is a relatively smaller "Stupa" of many in the ancient city of Anuradhapura with a well known history of over 2400 years.  The specialty of this is the stone pillars located around it indicating the existence of a timber structure to act as a roof for this small "Stupa" or the dome shaped brick structure.  This is a good place for those interested in meditating and it is located pretty close to the other main and large "Stupa" called Ruwanweliseya.    The path between these two could be an ideal place for those interested in practicing walking meditation to calm the mind by concentrating on the steps while walking slowly.

Title: A smaller but nonetheless impressive Dagoba
Text: The Dagoba of Thuparama is one of the smaller but still impressive Dagobas in the sacred city. It's one of the few in this area which is still used as a holy place and temple. While you're here for admiring the beauty of this Dagoba, others came for worshipping. Please behave respectfully as well as dress appropriately, cover your shoulders and knees. No shoes allowed.

Title: One of the smaller dagobas
Text: One of the smaller dagobas it is still an active site of worship unlike some of the larger historic dagobas so actually had more people here than at what I would have considered the more impressive sites, but that's because most people here were locals in peaceful contemplation not tourists.

Title: Old columns
Text: The columns standing around the stupa are what remain of the ancient building first built here. I didnt think ahead, and visited in the middle of the day, when the stone is hot hot hot. My feet didnt feel very good when I put my shoes back on.

Title: Perhaps the most interesting stupa of Anuradhapura
Text: The Thuparama is the first stupa built in Sri Lanka after the introduction of Buddhism, and it was built during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (about 300 BC) to enshrine the right collar bone of Buddha. Originally it was in the shape of a heap of paddy but as restorations were done in later years, it took the form as seen today. The story of the stupa, its immaculate white color and the brown, ancient stone pillars surrounding it, give it a strange, special aura and make it, in our opinion, the most interesting stupa in Anuradhapura.

Title: BUDDHIST
Text: This is one of the old Buddhist temple here. The Dagoba is surrounded by old pillars.This is beautiful temple you need about half an hour here.

Title: Nice visit to a different buddhist site.
Text: The one place we visited who really stood out. It is different and scenic. We were about to skip it but decided in the last minute to go and take a look and we are so happy that we did. You'll have to pay another entrance ticket fee but we fount that it was worth it. It is buildt into the rock itself. Overall a nice visit!

Title: Nice Temple site
Text: This was our first stop of the day on our visit to the ancient city. Despite it being early the site was still busy. It is well worth a look at when in the locality. Dont miss the carvings on the rock face above the level of the water tank,

Title: Nice carvings by the tank
Text: An ancient and interesting temple.  Dont miss the carving by the tank and the great carvings in the museum

Title: Nice
Text: You need to buy a separate ticket. The temple is nice - rock-cut structures, a steep climb, pond, mini-stupa etc.

Title: Uninteresting site crowded with people
Text: The view from the top is unimpressive, and the buildings around are being repaired but the work-site seems permanent - only some elephant carved in the rocks are worth a look

Title: Renovation
Text: When I visited the main site was under renovation, what a regret! Otherwise the place is quite fast to tour, there is a 'museum', and there is a place for you to walk up to enjoy some simple view over the flatlands. I think 30 mins suffice and there is an entrance fee.

Title: Nice set of relics and a good temple
Text:
There is not a huge amount to do here, however, I feel it was just enough to give me a taster of what Buddhist life is like here in sri lanka.

There are old relics seen in the museum area and you can walk to the top of the region and see around.  There is luscious green everywhere.  It is a nice place to be on a hot day

Title: Interesting
Text: This temple has an unusual design.  It is small but interesting. Do visit the adjacent Royal Park area. One of the highlights of Anuradhapura.

Title: Different to the other temples
Text:
Isurumuniya is different to the other temples in Anuradhapura and is well worth a visit. The admission fee is much lower too, although the staff were much more strict in enforcing dress codes than the main temples and asked my husband to cover his shorts which were fine elsewhere.

The temple complex is small but really diverse - there's a room with historic artefacts, a cave with a reclining buddha and then a sacred rock you can climb with a stupa a top and a pond at the bottom and even a sacred bhodi tree. It's very tranquil and I came across people relaxing and reading.

While you are here its well worth a walk around the small tanks out front. Its full of herons and other birds including brightly coloured kingfisher!

Well worth a visit!

Title: Anuradhapura has the most well preserved ancient ruins of Sri Lanka ! Isurumuniya is worth a visit !
Text: Isurumuniya is one of the popular places visited by tourists.  The Isurumuniya temple was built by Devanampiyatissa (307 - 267 BC)during his rule of Anuradhapura.  He was son of King Mutasiva who ruled in 367-307BC, who built the Mahamevnawa Park and grandson of King Pandukabhaya founder of Anuradhapura kingdom ! According to historical facts, during Devanampiyatissas reign the Buddhist Monk(Thero) Mahinda(Mahendra) brought Buddhism to Sri Lanka. It stated 500 children of high-caste were ordained into Buddhism, and Isurumuniya was built for them to reside. Mahinda Thero lived here for a while. It also stated Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi Tree Sapling was brought by daughter of Emperor Ashoka, Theri Sangamitta, also sister of  Monk Mahindra(Mahinda).

Title: Very Interesting
Text: My wife and I visited this temple during our recent Birdwatching tour of Sri Lanka. We had previously arranged a guide to show us the temples and stupors. After discarding our shoes at the entrance we commenced our tour, I should say from the outset that this temple is not friendly to persons with mobility issues, lots of steps. We spent about 40 minutes having the history of the the Rock Temple explained to us and visiting the different areas. Of particular interest was the reclining Buddha and the history of his life. As with all the temples and stupors we found them to be extremely challenging in the hot sun, many areas were just too hot to walk on, youve been warned. However, having said that we thoroughly enjoyed our visit and to get the best out of it you should engage a guide. Highly Recommended.

Title: Small but cute rock-based temple
Text: We visited this place at the end of a tour of the ruins of Anuradhapura.  The temple isn't part of the ruins, so you have to pay 200LKR to get in, but I'd say it's worth it.  It's a pretty small site - you can probably see the whole thing in about half an hour, but the architecture is interesting, built into and around a local rock site.  You can ascend to the top and get a decent view over the wider area, which gives a little bit of context to the wider Anuradhapura ruins.

Title: Stunning small place
Text:
We visited this first and were wowed by it. but after the entire Buddhist temples circuit realized this was another cave temple with a good amount of history to it. It takes only 15-20 min for the visit so would still recommended visiting it. 
The paintings and view from top of rick are worth the ticket. Also not much hiking\climbing compared to other places. As with all other places in Anuradhapura, visit before it gets too hot.

Title: Worth it for the Buddha
Text:
Some of his review you will find repeated for other places in Anuradhapura as I could not write a generic one.
Firstly, for sites of relgious signigicance, no footwear, hats or bare legs/shoulders. My tips would be; if in doubt carry a wrap/sarong/shawl and a pair of socks with you as the ground can get uncomfortably hot.
I only wanted to see the reclining Buddha but non of the signage advertised this.
There is a walk up to a view point, there's a museum. Its not a large site so finally I found the entrance to the rock temple. It is stunning....that's all I'm going to say.

Title: Visit only when its daytime (in the morning, before it gets too crowded and hot!)
Text:
PROS:
- its a quaint little place and worth a visit if you have time! there is a cave there (with a swallows nest!) that has the reclining buddha in different poses. i think its only worth a visit if you have a guide with you. Not a "MUST-SEE" but remember if you want to visit, go during the hours where its not so hot! 
-location is accessible by car but also a bit far out from the other big stupas like ruwanwelisaya. but im guessing most people dont really walk here so yeah! :) it was a 5-6min drive from ruwanwelisaya stupa.

CONS:
-there is an entrance fee and honestly its not so much of an architectural marvel worth paying for, but to each his own.
-you must remove your shoes and your feet will probably get wet in this place, so just bear that in mind. better to wear slippers. and in the afternoon the sand around the compound will get crazy hot to step on barefoot so be forewarned!
-the view is only good in the daytime/until sunset. we went at night (mistake! because surrounding it is forest area) so we just saw mostly blackness + occassional lights eg from the surrounding big stupas like Ruwanwelisaya.

Title: A little away from the other stupas
Text: You need to buy additional ticket to this place and not sure why that is. Nothing great for the additional amount that you pay. The small musuem here has the famous carvings pff Lovers and the elephant.

Title: Beautiful ancient temple
Text: Has a beautiful reclining Buddha and a very old Bho tree. Can climb to the top for a beautiful view out over Anuradhapura. Friendly staff, easily accessible.

Title: Beautiful cave temple
Text: We loved this temple alot. After visiting this temple and minthale we decided not to buy the unesco ticket for the other temple sites in anuradhapura, we believed 25 dollars per person is a bit overpriced. So that way we saved some money. I would really recommend to visit this temple, both as an alternative or addition to the other temples.  Tip: rent a bike to explore anuradhapura and the surroundings.

Title: Nice temple
Text: Visited this early before it got too hot. Remember to wear long shorts/trousers. Limited information in English.

Title: Pleasant at sunset...
Text: It's a beautiful place to visit at sunset, when the lights are colorful and the mirador on the top of the small rock hill offer great views of Anuradhapura!!

Title: Important historically
Text: Enjoyed our visit to this rock temple, pity the glass gives so much reflection.  Nice engraved elephants on the rock face but I really liked the reclining buddha in the bigger temple which had some wonderful images painted on the walls and truly excellent paintings on the ceiling.  Nice to have some colour to balance the ruins.

Title: Another one
Text: As SL temples go.  This is a temple in SL.  It has nicer views than many.  And has its win very old history.  But it is no standout.

Title: Important for Buddhist history
Text: First temple on Lanka, I guess. Nice garden and pond. Visited by school children groups, so you get the childhood memory feelings.

Title: Cultural heritage
Text:
A rock temple famous for its sculpture of " Lovers" and others such as the engraved elephants on the rock face. Situated in a serene green area, the climb to the top of a not  so high rock is doable even in scorching sun due to a gentle breeze.  One  must be appropriately dressed and there is a small entrance fee. 
Locals are free.

Title: Ancient and mystical
Text: Beautiful place which has a peaceful ambience. You get a feeling of the past and what it would have been like in ancient times.

Title: Nice
Text: This is a nice temple with many things to see, you can spent there about an hour to see everything. The only problem was that you should get of your shoes everywhere even in the gardens

Title: More than a temple...
Text:
Isurumuniya is famous for the carving of Isurumuniya lovers.. other than that there are two other carvings which attracted tourists namely Elephant pond and the royal family.. this place is a Buddhist temple but the architecture more close to a personal establishment... 

There's a fee for foreign tourists... you can visit Thisa Wewa (tank) which is situated nearby.......You can find tourists every day in the week, but I guess it will be lot easier if you prefer to visit on weekdays.. Please use proper clothing since this is a religious establishment...

Title: Sharp terrain up to the stupa.
Text: We visited in the late afternoon after a long morning of travel.  We encountered very few visitors except for the area where you climb the rock to reach the stupa.  As no footwear is allowed in many of these religious sites, be aware that the terrain is very uneven and the rocks are sharp edged for those with sensitive feet.  The small temple with the small colorful reclining Buddha is nice.  The small archeology museum does not allow photography or video taping.

Title: Extra charge for this temple, only 200rupee
Text: Despite the high entrance cost to Anuradhapura as a whole, there is an extra charge of 200 rupees for this temple. Not a lot, but still, why? It is an attractive collection of buildings, New temple, old temple, constructed around rocks with a pond at the base.

Title: temple
Text: This is one of many places in the city with an entry fee for foreigners, but not for locals. Someone will probably remind you to take your shoes off before you go through the entry gate. There are a few things to see in this temple, so make sure you wander all over.

Title: Sensory overload.  Prayers, Crisp Air, The Smell of Flowers.  Well Worth It!
Text:
Excerpt from my Blog Post:

Though the temple itself is not as grandiose or impressive as its counterparts, there was a quiet tranquillity to it which became apparent as soon as I began to approach the entrance...

As I removed my shoes and payed the toll to enter, I was truly not ready for the sensory overload that lay ahead. Upon my entry I was overcome by the monotone prayers coming from the speakers at the front of the temple, the feel of warm dirt beneath my bare feet, and the smell of flowers which came with every breath of crisp air I took in....

I made my way to the side of the temple and began to climb upward. It was a short climb (as I would appreciate in the coming days), and just a few minutes later, I was looking down from the top of the temple over the pond and out to the lush land that surrounded the are for miles

Though I did not find this to be an overwhelmingly spiritual or religious experience, I drew strength from knowing those on the ground, on the rock, and inside the temple were on a mission of days, months, years, and lifetimes to better understand themselves and their surroundings albeit in a purely spiritual sense.

Title: Buddhist
Text: This is another beautiful Buddhist temple here. A rock to climb.You need more than an hour here. There are stone carvings and a beautiful  Buddha statue here.

Title: Great  visit to the rock temple.
Text: We really enjoyed the lotus pond which was in bloom outside the temple. It is about Rs.50 to store your shoes. Make sure you dont wear shorts or a headscarf. There is a rock temple with a supine statue of lord Buddha. There are fantastic views from the STUPE or DAgoba which require climbing a few sets of easy stairs. We spotted an iguana which was the source of fancy for Several little children. There is also a branch of the oldest bodhi tree that was planted here. Would suggest doing this ancient capital with a guide. We employed the services of Mr. Kithseri who was a passionate Buddhist and conveyed his pride for this place making this an even more memorable experience.

Title: A nice hour spent here
Text: Visited here as part of our tour of Sri Lanka and spent a nice hour here. Not too busy. Various parts to visit - The Old Shrine, The Shrine Room, The Museum and The Stupe.

Title: Small Temple atop a Rock
Text: This is a small temple and whilst perched on top of a rock the climb up the steps is easy with no mountaineering involved. Quieter than the larger temple sites in Anuradhapura. Worth the small detour.

Title: Small temple, great view on top of the hill
Text:
The temple is small. There is a stupa on the small hill, pond, and a bodhi tree. They said that the temple has a very long story which make it becomes a must-go place.

Foreigner fee: 200 rupees

Title: One of the best sites in anuradhapura
Text: This tempel is very interesting. IT is not included in the General ticket, but for only 200 rupees a must! Take your time and see gris beautifull place

Title: Another religious and historical place
Text: If you are making the tour of all the temples, then should be in your list. You need to have a local guide to explain you the story and take you through the right monuments during the trip.

Title: As You Would As A Tourist Visiting Any Other City.  It's A Landmark Thing.
Text:
When you set aside religion and look at these ancient sights as landmarks to this area and to the country.  As a tourist they are worth a visit as much as you would visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris and the Statue of Liberty in New York etc, etc.

There is something to get from visiting them.  Something to feel and understand.  It is the feeling of the heat of the paved slabs or rock steps under your feet and an appreciation and understanding forming of what worship is like for these people here.  It is the physical exertion on your body to reach the highest point.  It is the tranquility of the landscape that these sights are built around.  It is the bewilderment of the age of the relics and the size in which some have been made.  It is the sights of monkeys behaving like this is their home.  It is the noise of traditional music as an organ may be playing if you were to visit a Cathedral.  It is the gentle murmurs of worship coming from peoples prayers.  It is the shade of the tree whether it be regarded as holy or not.  It is the smell of incense and the sight of flowers given as a gift.  It is the welcoming smiles of the Sri Lankan people who are happy to include you here regardless of your religion.

It is something you do and recommend you do when you are visiting another country.

Title: Great little temple visit
Text:
This is a nice little temple with a few things to see:
-lying Buddha and paintings on the wall
-bats in the cave right after it
-a nice Dagoba to see
-and a nice little pond

For the entrance, 200 Rupees per person, it's quite worth a visit.

Title: Lovely
Text:
Isurumuniya Temple was built 250  - 201 BC by King Devanmpiyatissa. It's a lovely place with interesting water feature where on the back wall are gorgeous carved elephants from the 7th century. The temple is good to see and not hard to climb.

 Allow a good half hour here while allowing one full day minimum to see all the sites of Anuradhapura. Wear easy off shoes to enter temples. Out of respect wear light colored clothing (preferably white) with knees and shoulders covered to enter temples.

Title: Breathtaking!
Text: Views are just amazing. I have no words to describe this place to make an honor to it. Lots of steps to walk to, but in the end is the price. Climbing to the highest rock was bit scary but the views! Three tumbs up to this! Entrance fee 500r was reasonable.

Title: Nice place
Text: Its better to wear socks if you are going in the afternoon. Very hot and u cant wear shoes to walk around the temple.

Title: Small temple near Anuradhapura
Text: We went there to visit the temple, and it was a nice visit with beautiful views, but the temple was a little far away and it was small compared with the others from the sacred area

Title: Lovely Lotuses of local tradition
Text: The mix of ancient and modern budhism rest seamlessly side by side the local people obvervant of thousand years old traditions fascinating for foreigners too. Climb up to the stupa and look for Buddhas tooth transported from india to safety in Sri Lanka

Title: Great place to watch sunset over the lake
Text: Interesting temple. Nice elephant relief on side of pool, great views. Well worth a visit. Can be visited without the main site ticket. Just 200 rupees admission.

Title: Isurumuniya temple Anuradhapura
Text: Great sacred place for Buddhist. Nice temple. One of historic places in Sri Lanka. Wearing full clothes is advisable or else carry a shawl or similar robe. Being a temple short clothes are not permissible.

Title: Stirring curiosity
Text: This was my first site in Anuradhapura and I would highly recommend others to start here.  My driver arranged a site guide who was excellent as he not only showed me around here, but other ancient ruins.  The history he told about Buddhism, the meanings behind the Dagoba, image house, the reclining Buddha, the historic Bodhi tree and the moonstones and guardstones brought life to the area and helped in understanding future areas I visited.  The view itself from the top by the Dagoba is worth the visit alone.  As it is a sacred place, advice is to dress respectably i.e. shoulders and knees covered (both genders).  Also you have to take your shoes off and the ground can become hot so it is wise to wear socks.  Take your time, sit in front of the Bodhi tree and chill.  Enjoy

Title: Wanderful isurumuniya
Text:
This place is closest to railway station of Anuradhapura. Have 3 location that you can visit. The rock, Temple and Buddha sleeping

In this area you need to removed your foot wear, they allow us to wear socks

Title: Peaceful and tranquil
Text: A Dagoba with lovely and interesting carvings on the rocks. You can climb up stairs to the top and see a nice view of the surrounding area. The area borders a large tank which can be accessed via a path to the right of the temple complex.

Title: Rock temple with frescoes
Text: Got here late in the day so no crowds. Fantastic art and history. The "Lovers" is a stone carving from 2 AD. Amazing

Title: Gorgeous little temple
Text: This was a delight. very clean and contained space. once again have to take shoes off. Nice museum and good views.

Title: Nice place to start sightseeing
Text:
On tour of historical sites, this was our first stop. Entrance fee was 200 rupees and nominal tip to watch your shoes.

Nice pond and rocks with carvings. Views from top of other stupas was nice. 

Most people seemed to miss the small building on the right as you exit with the Isurumuniya lovers carving.

Title: Not so much to see
Text: It needs entrance fee to enter this temple. But, as a tourists, we did not find much to see, though our driver said this temple was one of the oldest Buddhist temples. I would not recommend this.

Title: Small Temple with history
Text:
We went to this Temple in the weekend. There were many locals which I liked.

The pictures on tripadviser make it seem huge but it actually is (relatively) small.
The museum is tiny and in my opinion not nessecary.

There is a hal with some buddha statues. 
The ceiling of this shrine is beautifull.
On the wall are ancient drawings which depict the creation of this shrine, these alone are worth the trip

There is also a small batcave and the tiny rock gives you a nice view of the surrounding stupas.

At the end of the parking lot are the Royal Pleasure Gardens which we very calm. We saw some monkeys and you can see old ponds that were once connected.

The entrance fee was 200 roepies pp

Title: not so big but ok
Text: go there at early morning, not so big but ok. carving is nice & overall environment is peaceful & beautiful. but a bit difficult when i left at early morning. need to walk outside to the main street for catching tuktuk. maybe later will have more truck coming in. not so crowd but ok to take 30-1hr visit if you have time in anuradhapura.

Title: Must Visit. ..
Text: local and foreign travellers must.visit one ofn important place in anuradhapura. small temple with good stone carving. can visit popular isrumuniya lovers carving.  top of rock amazing view & surrounding area better go early in the morning or evening time.

Title: Nice Place
Text: This is an ancient temple of Buddhist believers. Its a nice place to visit. It also has a small pond in the front.

Title: Our favourite sight in Anuradhapura
Text:
We visited this sight first on our 4.5 hour tuk tuk sightseeing tour of the Ancient sites (we paid Rs 2500 for the tour but appears we paid way more than necessary as we booked this through our guesthouse - other drivers are only charging ~ Rs 1500, however we still felt this was value for money as our driver Fernando was very knowledgeable and a very pleasant). It cost Rs 200 per person to enter, as well as a tip to the man looking after our shoes upon leaving (we gave Rs 50 which he was happy with). We arrived at the site at about 8.30 and it was very peaceful. Our driver described the different aspects of the temple, the components of the moonstone and the balustrades. The views from the top of site are lovely.
As you leave this site walk to the opposite side of the car park where there are new toilet blocks being built. There you will find a sign for the Royal Gardens. If you follow this path you will come to the lovely baths for the female royalty and then the male royalty. Just prior to these baths is a path that leads left up to a rock, at the back of this rock you will find the star gate carved into the rock face, thought to be related to those in Egypt and Peru.

Title: Sri Lanka Adventure
Text: We enjoyed this short stop on our busy day. The artefacts in the small museum date pr? 3rd century BC. And you can get to the top of a small hill to take in the wonderful views

Title: Lovely place
Text: An interesting part of the whole complex. I found lots of interesting features and especially liked the carving of the elephant on a rock just above the tank.

Title: A fantastic temple with a lot of monkeys around
Text: This place is magical. It´s really old and the whole atmosphere was fantastic. The view is great and all the religious Buddha statues are breathtaking.

Title: Great Location
Text: Enjoyed this Temple. The view from the top of the boulders is amazing, even with the air polution. Very serene place. 200 Rupee entry fee for access to the temple. The "foreigner shoerack" is just outside the entry gate.

Title: Another temple, but different view
Text:
It is a small temple, but it is different view and why not take few stairs and see the view.  :)
I also saw bats!

Title: Great Little Temple!
Text: A nice change of pace for those looking to see a smaller but more tranquil stupa. You can climb to the top and get a nice view of the surrounding area. There is a nice pond, well kept grounds, and its much quieter than the bigger places in town. As with all other temples you need to take your shoes off, so be careful if you visit this place in the middle of the day. The hot sand can burn your feet!

Title: A small interesting temple
Text: This is on the outskirts of Anuradhapura. The eatery serves only non-veg food, so not helpful for vegetarians. This place is worth visiting for its calmness.

Title: Small but beautifyul
Text: Compared to the gigantic stupas of Anuradhapura this temple is small yet we recommend visiting it for its tranquillity and interesting interior. It is noted for its wonderful carvings which indeed are worth viewing. Because it is not on the main tourist ticket of the cultural centre, it is quieter than other places and is in a very picturesque location. We are very pleased we visited it.

Title: Sacred place
Text:
One of the very important monument of the Sri Lankan early kingdoms and buddhism history! More than 2200 years history!

Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes.
I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

Title: Not much to see here
Text: There is not much to see here. You can only go for a walk behind the temple where there is a lake. Not a place worth visiting if you are in Anuradhapura just for a day.

Title: A charming temple and view point
Text: This site is not on the main Anuradhapura ticket but is well worth a visit. The small temple is quite beautiful and there are some interesting carvings in the gallery. This site seems to attract less visitors than the other ancient monuments, rendering the visit more tranquil.

Title: Good for a brief visit
Text: Nothing spectacular, but nice little rock temple. Good for a visit of 20 minutes on the way to somewhere else.

Title: A quite fascinating temple, with beautiful carvings - well worth a visit
Text: It's hard to believe that this fascinating place has been around since ~200 BC. The rock carvings are intricate and quite sublime. I liked the elephants by the square pool as much as those carvings which have been moved indoors and displayed more formally in the gallery. This temple is probably my favourite in Anuradhapura. Enjoy it. Don't forget to take a few coins to test your throwing skills at the square pool.

Title: Very photogenic and tranquil spot
Text: This is a very photogenic and tranquil spot and once housed the tooth relic.  There are also some beautiful carvings to see and whilst the site is quite small, it was quiet when we visited and very pleasurable to wander around.

Title: Ancient carvings and stories
Text: The temple was built by King Devanampiyatissa (250 - 210 BC) and this mountainous site of Mihintale was filled with ruins, stupas, temples dedicated to the glory of historic encounter between Tissa and Mahinda.  The temple was located between two boulders with one adjoining a pond.  On top of the rock, you could have nice views on the surrounding.  The reclining buddha was the landmark in the Rock Temple. Worth visiting this spot when in Anuradhapura.

Title: A beautiful quiet place.
Text:
It is here, by the side of the old relic house, that you can see the iconic rock carving of the man and his horse. The place is a quiet haven with a small but well curated museum, a reclining buddha in a cave temple, an old bodhi tree and a sacred rock to climb. In all, it has everything in a small area and  is not much visited so it's quiet. 
The downside is that it's not included in the Sacred City ticket so it will cost another 300 rp (for foreigners) but I think, unlike the Sacred City, it is value for money.

Title: Did not enjoy it much
Text:
While this temple was pretty, I felt it didn't live up to the hype. I would place this temple much below Mihintale, the main dagobas, Bo Tree, twin ponds, moonstone etc.

The temple needs better sign boards / explanatory boards. We did not have a guide, and did not really understand the significance of some of the components.

We later got an excellent guide - Asoka - who showed us the main Anuradhapura ruins. I would recommend him very highly. His number is +94 718907081.

Title: Not to be missed in Anuradhapura
Text: This temple needs to be on your must see list when in Anuradhapura. It can easily be reached through rural roads on a bike

Title: Un believable
Text: steps are very easy to go up, the guide boys are excellent. tfree they explained every this correctly. but monkeys are dangerous. they trying to stealing foods in hands. nice view on the top of the Mihintale.

Title: Loved it!
Text: An interesting complex to wander and climb up to the top, we visited just before closing at 6pm, but they let us wander without pressure to hurry, the museum part was closed by this time however. I think it remains open to pilgrims after this time as a large bus load arrived just as we were leaving, which was also fascinating to see such devotion.

Title: Do not miss this place
Text: This place is just like a set from Indiana Jones. The carvings in the solid rock are incredible and the water garden surround is beautiful. One of my favourite visits during our stay.

Title: Nice place to visit !
Text:
A nice place to visit. The carvings housed separately, are very beautiful, as are the carvings on the rock (outside by the pond).
Separate entrance tickets. Spacious car park.
Almost next to Ran Masu Uyana.

Title: Nicely maintained
Text: Sparse remains of a once grand place of worship.  Neatly kept with no commercialisation nearby.  Steep entrance fee.

Title: Very interesting and varied
Text: Big reclining buddha inside a cave with swifts and bats flying around you; places to climb and view and other rooms to see. Spent a happy hour there with the family

Title: Colorful Buddhas inside!
Text:
While it is unimpressive from the outside, once you enter, there is so much to see. This rock temple has some very fine carvings.

Also in one of the caves is a serious of impressively colorful Buddhas, including a giant reclining Buddha, which was my favorite. It makes a tremendous photo!

Title: A nice walk if not to hot and you have time
Text: An interesting story of forbidden love in a fine natural setting. After seeing many stones and temples the last days this one did not add to much value

Title: Interesting and quiet temple
Text: This is a very quiet temple to visit in Anuradhapura with interesting sculptures. Extra fee is charged to visit it, I think it was worth it. Many locals come to worship here.

Title: Lovely spot
Text: I began my journey around Anuradhapura here. Very pretty rock temple with pond. Close to one of the large tanks built in ancient times by King Devanampiyatissa. Well worth a visit.

Title: Buddhist temple in the picturesque surroundings
Text: If you like to enjoy this beautiful place and not to burn your foot (unless you are used to walking on hot coals), go there early in the morning or late afternoon or take the socks with you. As you know, in Buddhist temple you are not allowed to wear the schoes BUT nobody (so far) cares if you wear socks.

Title: So old!
Text: Even though this seems to be a part of Anuradhapura complex, this place requires separate tickets (Rs 200) and shows the statues. The statues seemed rather unimpressive to me, until I noticed the dates when they were created. They are really old! The piece that is considered to be the most significant item of the collection is The Lovers, but I can't really say it's much better than the other pieces. Consider this place a room of the British Museum or a such.

Title: Different from Other Anuradhapura temples
Text:
Isurumuniya is a little away from the Anuradhapura Stupas and very different too. You can see the Shrine, the Dagoba and the Bodhi tree in the temple. 
Once you climb up to the rock on which the Dagoba is situated, you can have a good view of the surroundings as well. There is a big pond and a museum as well within the temple area.
The Museum has some of the old stone statues and carvings. Of this the statue of Isurumuni lovers is quite famous. This is very similar to the statues seen on most of the old temples in India.
There is an entry fee of LKR 200.

Title: Asian wonder
Text:
I saved $25 admission fee, 100% of airfare and lodging and snacked from my own kitchen... all by using the internet. I think I traveled to Myanmar, Burma that same day. Very cool places to see.
No TSA No Customs No Passport No government hassles. Where do you want to go?

Title: Boiling hot sand and rocks on your feet, otherwise mediocre site
Text:
As with all things holy in Sri Lanka, you remove your feet and walk around barefoot.  The grounds themselves are in decent shape, but I'm sorry to say, and I"m going to come across as an arrogant sounding tourist here, but:  having to skip around from shady spot to shady spot and wincing every time my feet felt jagged stones was not a pleasant experience, and far from a spiritual one.  Be prepared to have your feet burned off.

The temple itself is nothing spectacular.  There is a old bath with some carvings, and stairs to climb up a boulder.  There's another grotto kind of built into a cave with Buddha statues.  Interesting, if you don't mind the hundreds of bats that have made it its home - although you can get some photos there.  Once you see all three things, each worth about 5-10 minutes of your time, you're pretty much done...
