I honestly found the surrounding lily ponds and view of the reservoir more interesting than the temple itself.  Definitely see that.

All in all, a somewhat mediocre site as far as historical/cultural attractions go.  I pegged down because of 1) the shoe policy: temples elsewhere, for example, often hand out clean flip flops to use.  and 2) The site itself was simply not that spectacular.  I mentioned this in another review of Anuradhapura, but skip this town unless you have time.  Sigiriya and Polonaruwa, in the cultural triangle, are both more interesting.

Title: amazing
Text: it just amazing work done by an ancient sri lankan...

Title: Small visit but woth the stop
Text: I was there quite early and there was no entrance fee. You can climb the rocks, visit the temple inside and see some swallows and bats that made the temple their own. The whole visit takes only 15 minutes, you need to take off your shoes.

Title: Footsore
Text: For westerners unused to walking barefoot outside, this is rather hard going but worth it none the less. The little museum has interesting carvings and the view from the top is worth the climb.

Title: Visit if only you have a long stay in Anuradhapura!
Text: The temple is located away from the archaeological center and would take a bus ride to get there. Personally I did not find the temple itself too impressive but if you are in Anuradhapura for over 2 days and are done seeing the historic center then visit the temple for its carvings.

Title: Historical sites at its very best
Text:
I visited Isurumuniya with my family mates, for the "n"th time, and I still can't stop admiring this historical site.

Being a local I must state, that visiting these sort of historical sites require no special local guide, as the directions are given appropriately and besides the local community offers genuine help when you need the most. 

Remember to take off your shoes and hats/ caps while you're visiting the place, obeying the religion and its values. I would also recommend travelers to avoid shorts/ sleeveless materials at the time of visit.

Title: This will help you to understand Sri Lanka.
Text: This was an excellent beginning to my visit to Anuradhapura's many sights. Guides are available and I strongly advise to think  carefully about this. Hiring a guide is helping them to earn a living of course, but at some places it is not really necessary. The choice is yours.

Title: A lovely temple.
Text:
A temple that doesn't experience high volumes of tourists, this site is worth the visit. 

The on-site museum features numerous sculptures that originate from the temple. The most noteworthy are the 'lovers' and the 'kings family'. 
Beside the museum is a rock-cut shrine room featuring an extremely colourful reclining Buddha, a beautifully painted ceiling, and other images of Buddha. 
Adjacent to the pond is another shrine room featuring images of Buddha below a makara torana.
Beside the pond itself and carved into the rockface is a sculpture known as 'the man and his horse', and two sets of carvings of elephants.

Many people will miss this site, but I throughly enjoyed it and would recommend others go.

Title: Waste of time
Text: Not what you would expect. Right now they are "restoring" it but its like a do-it-yourself version and takes away from the fact that this is a world heritage site. It would have been better if they left it as it was.

Title: Compact place - well known statue
Text:
A compact place.  You get to see beautiful sculpture of a sensual couple (you can see it on postcards).  The climb up the dagoba was rewarded with a good view of the surrounding.  A reclining budhha.in one of the rooms.  Good option to spend if you have extra hours in Anuradhapura.

http://clumsycompass.blogspot.sg/2013/03/blog-entries-on-sri-lanka.html

Title: worth visiting
Text: It is little away from main attractions but its the first temple in sri lanka. Museum inside is pathetic...5 rocks with carvings.. cave with bats is nice ans noicy..climb the top  to engoy the view and breez. Entrance is 200 but it seems if to approach construction from left side there is no wall or fence.. funny..

Title: Not too busy and full of interest!
Text: It may not take long to visit, but this is a nice attraction to visit. It has a good sense of intimacy after some of the larger and busier sights.  We took a tuk from town and back which was not far.  One of the nicest spots in Anuradhapura and no selling going on. Great in the late afternoon.

Title: Lovely temple
Text: We almost missed this temple as it is slightly away from the other sites. But we're glad we went. The temple is small but very charismatic. The reclining buddha is beautifully painted as is the room where it is housed. There is also a bat colony, a very busy squiggly bunch but fun to watch.

Title: shouldn't miss!!
Text: It is a beautiful complex and it is one of a few places in Anurathapura, where we can see beautiful stone carving (the lovers and horse man, king and consort) rather than the remaining cement, bricks and gigantic stupa.  Entrance fee is very cheap comparing to the 25 USD price to see the big dagoba where you can see from the road side.

Title: A nice Rock Temple
Text: ... if you hear loud noises, raise your eyes. It could be a huge population of bats living in this temple.

Title: loved the bats!
Text:
nothing special to see, lovers sculpture, dagoba,ponds, but the cabe full of bats did impress me, on my 3rd day sri lanka, not knowing, that bats often hang in trees.
entrance fee 1100 rps

Title: Bats and more
Text: This is a nice location and very well kept, again a hot foot massage. The guide was very limited with his vocabulary of English and we had to fill in the blanks he would create. Being an Indian we were aware of the story of Buddha so it was easier to comprehend what he was trying to say.

Title: Lovely
Text: Also lovely place to visit. In anuradhapura you cant walk in day time as it was very hot.the structure is amazing.

Title: Rock Temple
Text: An example of a small Sri Lankan temple in the rock. Charming place. A lot of bats in the rock uder Dagoba on the top.

Title: Worth the climb
Text: This site reminded me of the world heritage sites in Capadoccia Turkey. Paintings were better preserved here.

Title: Lovers Carvings
Text: Another one of the amazing places in Anuradhapura. The carvings inside the museum are really beautiful. A place where a prince had to hide because of his affair with a low caste lass. Truly worth a visit.

Title: A temple worth a visit
Text: It is a nice temple built as a fusion with a rock, where you can see carved the famous 'horse and man' and the well preserved carved elephants bathing in the small lake. Near to it you can get ot know more about the history of the Isurumunya Lovers.

Title: The site of the beginning
Text: Legends has it that the first relic of the Buddha was put here in the days of the emperor Ashoka, and the atmosphere makes one willing to believe this record from the Chronicles. It was a monastery then, it still is.

Title: Nice, peaceful temple
Text: The temple is located at approx 2.5 km from maha bodhi temple. There is a buddha statue in a cave in nirvana pose & small archeological museum in Temple complex. There is a beautiful lake behind the temple at 100 mtr. You can see it from to of the rock also. Do visit the lake..You will get to see many birds.

Title: Different from the other temples you can visit
Text: Some of the holy sites in Sri Lanka are built around special rock formations and this is a very good example: The temple as well as some platforms are built on, below and partly inside a particular rock. This is not a place to impress you but where you have to pay attention to detail.

Title: A very old rock temple with great views of countryside
Text: This old temple is small with some ancient carvings into the stone.  There is a small museum which is worth a look and a great start to learning about ~Buddhism in Sri Lanka

Title: A less visited but interesting Vihara.
Text: This is a small but very old rock temple that is not as flash as the big stupas but is worth a visit. At the entrance to the temple are interesting rock stone carvings. The ones on the stairs are still really legible . In the pool to the right you can see elephants carved into the rock. Inside the shrine which is lavishly painted with monks and the roof with flowers there is a large reclining buddah. On leaving the shrine you visit the small museum with its stone carvings, then can climb up the steps onto the rock street and get a good view of the lY out of the whole site and the lake.

Title: First temple for our day out in Anuradhapura.Enjoyed The serenity
Text: It was nice to visit this temple when there were few people there.It is a small temple in comparison to others and thats a nice change.Lovely water feature next to the temple and nice views over the man made lake at the back and into town.Its ok as part of the Ancient City tour but is paid for separately at 200rp per person so very cheap.

Title: Pleasure garden
Text: This temple together with all the other ruins of the pleasure garden gives an idea of the life style of the rulers.

Title: Could give it a miss
Text: Religious place, nothing very special in terms of architecture or views but if you are in the area an have time won't be a waste if you visit.

Title: Crowded but nice
Text: Place was very crowded and sun was hot when we went. There is a reclining Buddha here and the cave has bird nests which is fascinating. There are steps to go to top of the rock, but the views from there are nothing great.

Title: Interesting
Text: Some good features and an interesting site, both climbing up on top and the statues and paintings inside.

Title: 4-5 km far from hotel
Text: Adventure proud Sri Lions history tells us this wonderful world is still amazing designs before leaving this wonderful environment full of Sri Lankan heritage bequeathed a proud salute to the past must be given automatically to children respect for our King.

Title: Nice little temple
Text: Nice little temple with a stupa.  Most of the carvings have been removed and transferred to the museum on site

Title: Lovely temple, the famous "lovers", elephant inscriptions
Text: I really liked this temple. You can see "the lovers" (stone carving) in the small museum. There are beautiful elephant carvings on the right side of the stairs, behind the lotus pont, on the left side of the rock.

Title: Nice place and views
Text:
Nice place with great views from the top. Is not as big and crowed as the other places in the zone.

It is a good place to spends 30 to 45 minutes and take rest and have great vies from the top of the temple

Title: Must not miss
Text:
200 Rupee only for this distinct temple.
Amazing big rocks gate to pass under and very big rock to get on top. Easy to discover it was just near to the Anuradhpura heritage site. Lover stone was in small museum there too. Need a hidden cam to take picture. Otherwise ask permission may need some money to pay ?

Title: Worth the visit
Text: This temple is a little out of the way from the main sites and therefore less frequented by locals and tourists. The lack of crowds gives this place a serene feel with it's small temple carved into the rocks and overlooking a pond. Picture perfect.

Title: Buddhist Temple Without Tourists
Text: Anuradhpura seems to be beyond the standard tourist trail so there were really only Buddhist pilgims at this temple when we visited. Large reclining idol of Buddha in cave, great views of Anuradhpura from the top of the rock, and very loud bat colony also in the rock!

Title: Amazing Lord Buddha Sculptures in Cave & Beautiful Scenery from Cliff.
Text:
Review for a solo traveller.

Travel tips to reach Anuradhpura:
Colombo to Anuradhpura: Bus journey more than 200 plus km & 7 plus hours journey. Train option is also there. Train journey is more comfortable than bus.
Kandy to Anuradhpura: Bus journey more than 150 km more than 6 plus hours journey
Dambulla to Anuradhpura: Bus journey more than 70 km & more than 1 & half hour journey
Polonnaruwa to Anuradhpura: Bus journey more than 100 km & more than 1 & half hour journey

On reaching Anuradhpura one has to hire auto at negotiated price for sightseeing. Anything in the range of 1300 to 1800 LKR is the auto hire charges. Auto driver will ask you to pay him little more instead of buying entrance ticket assuring you managing with the ticket check points on the sightseeing route.

Entrance ticket is 1800 of Anuradhapura sightseeing if you produce original passport otherwise more than 2500 LKR. You will be provided with a CD. It will take 4 hours to see complete sightseeing of beautiful ancient ruins in Anuradhapura.

Isurumuniya Vihara will be 1 of the 10 spots of your Anuradhpura sightseeing tour. There is a cave, pond & small stoopa on a cliff. Entrance fee of LKR 200. 

Large idol of Buddha in a sleeping pose is in the cave alongwith other amazing sculptures. You are allowed to take photos of Buddha Idol & other sculptures. You are not allowed to take your own photo inside the cave.  

Sight of Buddha idol & other sculptures inside the cave is excellent. 

From the cliff top, one can see very beautiful scenery all around. 

On the back side of Isurumuniya temple there is a big serene lake at a 5 minutes walk. You have to come out, take left turn reach the corner of temple compound, again take left turn, walk for more than 50 metres, climb up the inclined steps & you are in front of a big lake.

See the attached photos.

Title: Lovely temple and nice view!
Text: A place to visit! Its a beautiful and colorful temple with a wonderful garden and unique stone carvings. If you climb the rock, you have an amazing view of Anuradhapura. I loved being here.

User_Location: Capelle aan den IJssel, The Netherlands
Title: Rock Temple
Text: Do not visit this temple in the weekend, because a lot of locals are going there. The temple is worthwhile to see inside, but you need a good guide who can explain the meaning of the interior of the temple

Title: Romance back when
Text:
This is not the most impressive of sites in the Anuradhapura area but one of the 8 sacred sites. The walk over stone steps and across sand-pebble stone areas is made easier when reading up on the history of the place beforehand. 

If available, bring along coins to dedicate to the deity by throwing it in the pond for good luck.

Title: Limited time? Can skip!
Text: This temple is supposed to be first of them built in the ancient city. It is not covered under the tour package of Anuradhapura (the tickets can be bought from visitor's centre, 50% discount for SAARC countries). One has to pay extra to enter the temple and keep their shoes outside. It was too hot to walk barefoot so carry socks! this site can be skipped if tight on schedule!

Title: Unique carving
Text: A nice to place to visit There are four unique carvings in the rock temple they are the Isurumuniya Lovers, Elephant Pond and the Royal Family. all carving are very unique

Title: Worth a visit
Text: This is quite a large complex, so you have to walk some distance without shoes. So don't go in the heat of the day. However, it is worth the hot feet. There is a lot to see here, and the climb to the top part gives you  a beautiful view.

Title: Not included in the basic admission price
Text: Quite why one is charged $25 for a block admission ticket and we are then charged extra for various sites is not obvious.This site is interesting but nothing special and does not merit yet another fee

Title: Another pretty place
Text: The temple has lots of historical value. Make sure that you visit the park just beside the temple. It has lots of things to see, especially the remains of a palace and other buildings. Once you finish just climb up the bank of the pond. If you go late in the evening you'll be able to experience a great sunset in peace. Very relaxing.

Title: this temple is away from the rest in the city-tourists pay Rs 200 to get in
Text: ancient temple with unusual rock carvings & a small museum includes the famous Isurumuniya lovers carving

Title: " Nice story with Temple "
Text: This is a Buddhist Temple and there is interesting story behind this place. There are four carvings of special interest in this Viharaya. They are the Isurumuniya Lovers, Elephant Pond and the Royal Family. You must come and get experience by .enjoying the visiting this place with its amazing story

Title: Small temple but interesting
Text: Some great statues to be seen here. Rock carvings. As in all temples you need to take your shoes off, be sure to take some socks along. The surroundings can become very hot to walk on. It is not a big climbe to get there, easy acces.

Title: Full of wonderment...
Text: This visit was long planned but due to having so much to see and do around the Polonnaruwa area, we got delayed. It was getting quite dark but we made a conscious effort to squeeze this one in, as our last port of call-of-the-day. And we were not disappointed. The area was quiet but well lit. We left our shoes by the entrance at the  police post. The sandy ground was cool and was less pebbly than in other areas. The climb up the steep stairwell up to the rock summit took some nerve: a small child and his parents had also left it until the last minute and the mum found a less direct route (on the left) to the top, which I recommend to those with no head for steep climbs. The Rock Temple itself, I missed, as I was transfixed by the 'Man and the Horse' carving to the right of the Temple. A man, whom I presumed was a fellow visitor warned us in no uncertain terms that this was 'not the time to be moving around'. It was too dark to see all of the majestic beauty that this temple and the museum had to offer anyway and I took his advice and left. I need to go there again for a proper look.

Title: read the signs
Text: Before you 'take a picture of the famous lovers' sculpture, read the signs prohibiting photography and show a little respect.

Title: Lovers an bats!!
Text:
An interesting site. The rock temple is an easy climb. Underneath there is a cave inhabited by a large number of bats.
The sculpture of "The Lovers" in the museum is worth seeing.

It helps to wear socks as walking up to the  site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet

Title: Tough to Walk Around Without Shoes
Text:
As other reviewers have noted, shoes and hats must be removed before entering this Temple.  The distance from the entrance to the Temple is about 100 yards and the surface is dirt with small stones.  In addition, the climb to the top of the complex without shoes is a challenge.  Wear an extra pair of socks to help cushion the feet.  Picturesque 
view across the pond towards the Temple.  Entrance fee was Rs 200/person on March 1, 2016.

Title: History starts here
Text: In the first capital city it's a modest temple built into the Rock. Said to be the first in Sri Lanka. An insight into Buddhism with the temple, image house, stupa and tree

Title: Perfect for an evening relaxation
Text: Isurumuniya Rock Temple has no special features but it has less crowds compared to other Dagoba's in Anuradhapura. Sitting by the pool side and watching the locals feeding the fish was relaxing especially during the sun set.

Title: Like most other over priced "temples" in Sri Lanka it is also not worth it
Text: This was a cheap option. One can walk from town ( along, sweaty walk) and pay relatively small amount of money to see a substandard temple in the rock. If you are well traveled, don't need to come see this. You leave your shoes outside and pay for it. Then you walk either on your socks or barefoot and keep on jumping from one hot stone to the other. You go up on hot, rocky stairs to see NOTHING. The "museum" is substandard as well. Then you walk out to get your shoes back when you are asked to pay a TIP on top of the money you already paid to keep your shoes. This must be a real practical joke.

Title: A temple carved out of the rock
Text:
It was exiting to visit this little temple, as I had a photo of how it was in 1897 when my grandfather saw it and described it in his journal. There are several exquisite carvings, some carved out of the great Boulder, and others housed in the little museum next to the temple. Some are definately Buddhist, others look almost Hindu.
The main Buddha in the temple is a little hard to see and impossible to photograph, as it is behind glass which reflects the light. As is the case with most of the temples, the steps are very steep. A wonderful view from the top of the temple.

Title: Beautiful Small museum adjacent to the temple.
Text: Small but well worth to look at. The museum has the greatest stone cast Lovers. Also the ancient stone casts. It is really worth to visit this temple, and walk through to the top of the rock.

Title: Small Temple but interesting
Text: My wife and I found this temple interesting. We were fortunate that we received good information whilst we were there from a gentleman who was also visitng with a relative from overseas. Betwen the two they gave us an insight that we may otherwise have missed. One thing though we must have very tender feet from years of wearing shoes and we found the relatively long distances walking without shoes a bit hard. We have walked many temples and this was one of the few places we found the stones hard going. Still glad we did it and would recommend it to others.

Title: Worth watching
Text: It's a wonderful place to watch when you travel around Anuradhapura. If you know the local history it is more interesting.

Title: Historical site
Text: A great way to experience Sri Lankan history from a Buddhist/cultural perspective. The main attraction here is a stone carving dating more than 1,500 years

Title: Nice temple and museum
Text: This is quiet and charming with a nice museum next door. Photography is forbidden inside. Climb the temple, come down and perambulate under the old bodhi tree. Next to the temple pond are rock cutouts of an elephant and naag.

Title: A historical place
Text: I learned that this is one of the oldest temple in Sri Lanka which is now one of the great attraction in Anuradhapura. Nice view around and walking on the top of temples is just great. There is nice museum which clarifies the history behind it. Tourist needs to buy a separate ticket here but if you are foreigner, living on residential visa, do not need to buy any ticket.

Title: Best attraction in Anuradhapura
Text:
Felt this is the best attraction in Anuradhapura. Need to take another set of tickets to see this temple. The tickets purchased for 3250 bucks is not valid here. Paid around 500 bucks per person to visit this temple. Too steep for such a lame attraction!

As usual, it has a Buddha statue. There is a water body next to it along with rocks. There is a formation in the rock where people try to throuw coins. It takes good aim to throw the coin directly into that slot.

There is a cave next to it. It was filled with bats. We didn't go inside as it was dark and would be dangerous. Avoud going in the caves in the evenings. It can get very dangerous.

Title: At the ancient capital of Sri Lanka
Text: There is a small temple within a rock and it is an easy climb up steps to get to the top of the rock and admire the views of the countryside. Judging by the number of Sri Lankans visiting here and the number of cars and buses it is a very important place for them. The area is very well maintained and there are interesting artifacts in the small museum obviously removed from their original locations to preserve them. It is also a pleasant walk to the area wheter there is a large glowing white stupa.

Title: Start anurhapura visit here
Text: Visit the small museum close this monument , before to visit the city of anurhadapura .... and clim to the top of the rock you'll get a wonderful view !

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Isurumuniya though not famous for it's stupa, was a famous temple historically for praying to the rain gods. Minimal effort to climb to the top of the rock. Excellent view of the surrounding area from the top of the rock. Make sure you visit the Museum and take some pictures of the famous lovers, a 6th Century Gupta style rock carving. The figures may represent Dutugemunu's son Saliya and the law caste (Sadol Kula) maiden Asokamala whom he loved. It's known that he gave up the throne for her. the tour can be completed within half an hour.

Title: Peaceful temple with a great view, separate entrance fee
Text:
I like it for the fact that it's breezy on the top though a little (very minimal) climb (stairs) is needed and you will have a great view, overseeing Tissa Wewa. One of my favourite temples in Sri Lanka, and one that leaves a deep impression.  

It is near to the Sri Maha Bodhi temple. Worth a visit if you are nearby. The entrance fee (Rs.200) is not included in the rest of the ancient sites, so do it on a separate day. 

We didnt have guide to tell us stories, nor we are historical buffs who want to write a journal about it, but we enjoyed the view and serenity.

Title: Another masterpiece
Text: Take your socks as this is a hat and shoe free zone.  Socks are acceptable and respectful.   Fascinated watching the local attendees throwing coins into the rock opening, and then the climb to the top of the rock well worth the crowd and wait.

Title: Must visit
Text: It a must see in Anuradhapura. Ancient feeling, nice statues and story. Our guide was very well informed and willing to share what he knows about the temple. Entrance fee is 200LKR.

Title: Beautiful!
Text:
A beautiful temple you should absolutely visit whilst exploring the sites of Anuradhapura.
The site is really beautiful and it's lovely to wander around. The small museum on site is interesting.
It costs 200 rupees to enter.
This is one of the places you should absolutely make time to visit.

Title: A BRANCH FROM THE TREE OF ENLIGHTENMENT
Text: Children of Emperor Asoka of India brought to Sri Lanka a branch of the tree under which Buddha found enlightenment. It is one of the three sites Sri Lankan Buddhists must visit. Now over 2,300 years old, the tree is partly held up by gold works. Devotees attend to provide food for the tree, sometimes in processions.

Title: Nice
Text: Piousness fills the air, with so many saplings, people, images of Lord Buddha around the central temple.

Title: Interesting site but underwhelming if you're not buddhist
Text: Important site of the Buddhist faith in Sri Lanka but the buildings around are quite recent and don't really help as the setting for this millennia old tree

Title: Worth looking
Text:
The history behind this is very fascinating.  Youd expect the story to be about the tree itself, however, upon closer inspection it is clear to see that the branch is the main article here.

You can get close enough for pictures and to view this.

Title: Sacred place
Text:
This is one of the sacred places for all Buddhists. 

You need to wear the dresses which covers your body in full as its a religious place. If you visit ruwanweliseya stupa, its just few minutes away from there.

Title: Sacred Bodhi Tree
Text: Our early morning visit on its opening at 6am was very pleasant and blessed for everyone of us who managed to do our spiritual practices of chanting and meditation on the principles of Lord Buddha.

Title: most ancient trees
Text:
one of the world ,s most ancient trees with a known history 
known to beplanted by a branch of the very bodhi tree which gave shelter to gauthama lord buddha in the hour of enlightenment. it s known to have healing powers and is a blessed place for buddhists who worship with faith

Title: A sacred site
Text: This site has the largest and oldest of th emany bo trees.  It is said that a cutting was brought from India by a princess in the 3rd century BC.

Title: Visiting a Sacred Site
Text: One of the most sacred sites of Buddhists. The Bodi tree was planted in 288 BC and is the oldest living human-planted tree in the world with a known planting date.

Title: Good place
Text: Can be quite busy so choose your timing. This bodi is claimed that it may be the original one brought from India by the buddha

Title: A sacred place in the ancient city of Anuradha pura, Sri Lanka.
Text:
Believed to be a sapling from the sacred bodhi tree under which Lord Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment, this ancient temple is a major pilgrimage centre for Buddhists from all over the world.

It is said that every Buddhist must make a pilgrimage to this sacred place atleast once in his/her life.
The temple premises are clean and quiet.

A sacred place to visit to calm down and meditate.

Title: A smallish but old tree.
Text: Again a hard place to review. It depends on what you like. I knew that the tree wouldn't be big or look particularly special, but if you expect something extraordinary you'll be dissapointed. What is special about the place is that the tree is taken from the original tree where the Buddha is said to have achieved enlightenment. Just that it is a 2000 year old tree is quite amazing, no matter what it looks like. Also to get to observe the reverence the locals pay the tree is fascinating. I suppose it is sometimes loud, confusing and the offerings litter the place. But as long as you know why you go it might be a good experience.

Title: "Serene"
Text:
It is the totally relaxed feeling that one enjoys at this sacred place of worship venerated by the Buddhists from all over the world. Early in the morning surroundings were very tranquil and comfortable, before the area got warmer with the days hot sun and before the premise got filled with larger numbers of devotees.  Environment was very calm and conducive for a moment in silent meditation.  Entire precinct has so many Bodhi trees escorting the sacred Bodhi tree which is at the highest terrace. It is known to be the oldest surviving planted tree in the world with a recorded history.  

The granite balustrades are very attractive with beautiful motifs engraved in to them.

Title: Cultural Visit
Text: the site of the tree and the surrounding are is well worth a visit. Shows you something of the local culture.

Title: Amazing Place...
Text: One of the most magnificent place in Anuradhapura. The spirituality and the presence of Lord Buddha can be felt once someone is near the age old tree. Beneath the tree the magnificent Buddha Temple with all Blue Lily flowers is worth to see.

Title: Magical experience
Text: One of the most sacred places for every Buddhist, it's the oldest tree with recorded history in the world. It's blessed shade provide infinite comfort to everyone as it provided same to Lord Buddha, helping him to attain the enlightenment. Utmost respect in attire and behavior is expected from every visitor here.

Title: Soak It All In
Text: The area around the tree is well built up so you will mostly be seeing the branches of this very old sacred tree. That being said, you will not be alone in this, and the crowds of people paying homage and chanting will make up for what you miss from the tree itself. The entire experience is however long you choose to make it. Give it at least 30 minutes and do your best to soak up all the moments that are happening at this feast of the senses.

Title: Sacred place
Text: This is the branch from the bo tree in india  under which lord buddha attained enlightenment, very sacred and crowded.

Title: Spiritual place, nice experience at night
Text: Go at night time and walk around the tree. Very peaceful experience and a lot to observe and learn. There is a big white stupa nearby.

Title: Most venerated tree in the world
Text: The original tree brought to Sri Lanka by the daughter of Emperor Asoka.  Cutting taken from the original tree at Bodghyia in India very much still a centre for devotion and worship

Title: Yes, Its That Bodhi Tree.
Text: The oldest tree on the planet, this is a cutting from the Bodhi tree where the Lord Buddha obtained enlightenment. You cannot get too close to the tree itself, but the level of devotion from pilgrims makes an impression. Of all the stupas, former monasteries and the like in this ancient region, this is the place that left the strongest mark.

Title: The Most Sacred Tree For Buddhists
Text:
This most sacred tree is worshiped by all Buddhists in Sri Lanka(foreigneres too).
Gauthama Buddha attained enlightenment under the Southern branch of Sri Maha Bodhi at Buddhagaya in India.
Please observe dress code of white (ensure legs & shoulders are covered)as a mark of respect.

Title: A great sense of wellbeing
Text: We arrived to see the Sri Maha Bodhi on the morning of Christmas Day, Following gift-bearsing Buddhist devotees, we gained a wonderful sense of peace and wellbeing. On entering the site, we visited the altar before staring at wonder at this ancient tree, allegedly the oldest human-planted tree on earth. The huge fig is supported, so no branch will ever fall, despite their great length and huge weight. This place is a testament to faith of a gentle people. For me, in the magical country of Sri Lanka, I could not think of a better and more appropriate place to spend Christmas morning.

Title: Religious place to add your journey
Text: Located in heart of Anuradhapura which is 168Km from Bandaranayake international airport. Better to where white or light color dress when you visit this place. Do not where dress like mini skirt, short sleeve blouse or short for men in order to have some respect. You need to buy flowers, Oil and incent sticks if you plan to do observation. Visit to this place on early morning will be great in all the ways. Full crowded on poya days, if you visiting this place on first time ignore poya days. No entry fees. As this is located in religious city you may find some other observation places around this place. Any case if you want to go out after visiting this place, you can try Dhambulla side or Jaffna side or even polonnaruwa side after visiting this place. Around 72Km to Dhambulla, Jaffna 196KM, Polonnaruwa 106KM

Title: Great but could be better
Text:
Some of his review you will find repeated for other places in Anuradhapura as I could not write a generic one.
Firstly, for sites of relgious signigicance, no footwear, hats or bare legs/shoulders. My tips would be; if in doubt carry a wrap/sarong/shawl and a pair of socks with you as the ground can get uncomfortably hot.
A little disappointing as the tree is high up a barriered but of historical interest.

Title: A big complex
Text: The most scared part of the Anuradhapura scared city complex. The tree is very old and believed to be a branch off the Bodhi tree in Bodh gaya where Buddha attained his enlightenment.

Title: Great Religious Place
Text: As a nation we are really prod of this place. This is the branch of the tree that the right-wing branch from the historical Sri Maha Bodhi at Buddha Gaya in India under which Lord Buddha attained Enlightenment. this is the oldest living human-planted tree in the world old over 2500 years.

Title: Sacred place
Text: Well worth a visit once you have the tourist entry ticket to Anuradhapura. Beautiful sacred place. Be sure to dress conservatively or to take a shawl for shoulders and knees.

Title: Nice place
Text: Very nice to visit. Nice grounds with some shady spots. Limited information in English. Cheap entry.

Title: Probably incredible if you are Buddhist
Text: There is an awful lot of religious history tied up in this tree, yet to say how ancient it apparently is, it looks neither that old, nor as big as you would expect. None the less, the significance of it is impressive and it is situated in a pleasant temple area that you can take a short walk around. You can't see the tree all that well as it is protected, but worth a visit.

Title: Peaceful and beautiful
Text: Nice and peaceful place with enough space for all to go around even though we went just few days before vesak day.

Title: One of most Holy place on the earth!
Text: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi is a holy symbol of the Buddhist culture. If someone believe or love to learn about the Buddhism, they better visit this holy place, if someone not interest better avoid because you have to be there with a good understanding, otherwise you might complain as the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi is just a tree & etc. Before enter this holy land you may remove your hats, caps & shoes. If its too hot outside better wear socks because its difficult to be on barefoot during the sunny weather.

Title: Devotion...
Text: It's a great place to feel the devotious and faithful side of Sri Lankan people... It's a magic place to visit after 17h...

Title: Living monument of lord Buddha
Text:
Most ancient tree which has written history.. since King Kithsiri Mewan of Anuradhapura kingdom..

Most worshiped place by Buddhists...

Proper attire required to visit this religious place...

Title: Special experience making an offering and receiving a blessing
Text:
We made a small offering and asked the attendants to pray for a safe trip, it was a very special and powerful experience for us and we felt welcome despite not being Buddhists.

Suitable clothing is required to ankle and covering shoulder with bare feet, bring socks and go outside midday as the ground is hot.

Title: A sincere and moving place
Text: This was unexpected, as our guide brought us here towards the end of a long and tiring day, but it was a highlight! It may not have the grandeur, splendour and decoration of so many major places of worship in all belief systems, but the simplicity of the tree and its surrounds, and the tangible sincerity of the worshippers was a deeply impressing experience.

Title: Holy place
Text: This was the attraction I was most interested in visiting in Anuradhapura as I heard it was the oldest Bodhi Tree in Sri Lanka. It was very crowded when I visited, with the locals all dressed in white, paying their respects to the tree. You can also take a walk to see other Temples surrounding the tree, as well as a huge pagoda around 600m away from the tree.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Good venue, interesting story behind how the cutting of the bodhi tree came to this place.  Nice grounds and obviously a special place of worship

Title: Ancient history alive in the oresent
Text: The Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi is said to be a branch from the bodhi tree at Bodhgaya in India where the Buddha attained enlightenment. This is a significant pilgrimage destination so variations of human devotional expression can be witnessed here. I thought of Anuradhapura as an ancient site but it is actually fully occupied and alive in the present.

Title: A spiritual tree provides insight for Western travellers
Text: This is one of the trees that is said to be an offspring of the one where Buddha was enlightened. Regardless of 'truth', the place offers spirituality and for us held more magic than Western churches, for example. A must-see when you are anywhere close.

Title: Incredible
Text: The history and legend of this site are incredible and it is a must to experience it. The omnipresent budhism is alive here.

Title: The most sacred and revered tree to Bhuddists
Text:
Srilanka abounds great relics of Buddhism. The most scared of them is the Mah Bodhi tree.The sapling of the holy Bo tree in Gaya , India , under which Lord Buddha obtained Gnana, the supreme knowledge. It was sent by Emperor Ashoka through his daughter , Sangamithra , to Srilanka around 250 BC and was planted by the then king . So it is the oldest tree  in the world. Pilgrims all over the world come here and offer their prayers . This tree remains well guarded by the administration. The temple of Buddha around the tree is awe inspiring. 
The divinity here must be experienced by one and all.
A must see in Lankan tour

Title: nothing outstanding
Text:
as an archeological sight its pretty dispapointing. 
Obviously for budhists it's a scared and special place, but for everyone else its pretty meh

Title: One of the most important sites in Sri Lanka - must see
Text: The Sri Maha Bodhi tree is the oldest, recorded tree in the world and said to be a cutting from the bodhi tree under which the Buddha became enlightened. It's a special place to visit for those interested in Buddhism and the atmosphere provided by the pilgrims and devotees is palpable and can easily stir emotions. Loved the place!

Title: Oldest planted tree in the world
Text: Said to be the oldest tree planted by a human - by king Ashoka's daughter. The tree is surrounded by a wall now and can be approached from all four sides by climbing a short flight of steps on to a platform. The complex has many trees where people can be noticed paying respects. The place is quite crowded and  religiously significant. Must visit.

Title: A must for anyone interested in Buddhism or history!
Text: To see the tree grown from a sapling of the original Bodhi tree in Lumpini, Nepal, where the Buddha achieved enlightenment and that was brought here by King Asoka's daughter and planted in 288 BC, is truly overwhelming and yet soothing and totally mesmerizing, indeed. It's the oldest tree of its kind in the world, and it's been attended to by appointed care-givers since that time.

Title: A visit to the oldest tree in the world
Text: The Bodhi Tree in the temple's garden is said to be a branch from the oldest tree in the world. It is the  branch from the tree under which  Buddha found enlightment. As it is sacred and old it is under conservation so you can not get near it. It is visited by many locals as it is a popular site for Buddhists.  We were very impressed by the peaceful atmosphere.

Title: The test of time.
Text:
I found it difficult to understand what the worshipers were getting from their visit to this place. It's not particularly impressive in size for such an old tree but clearly believers felt some sort of energy from being in its presence.
It was a privilege to be allowed to come and see this site for myself and it struck me that millions must have passed the same way over all those years that the tree has been standing.

Title: A very sacred place
Text: It is hard to work out which is the original tree. However, the beauty of this religious site is in seeing the hundreds of devout pilgrims of all ages praying and offering gifts. Never seen anything like it before.

Title: Feel the divine serenity
Text:
It is impossible to cover all the sites in a single day, as there are so many places to see.
The museum is small but has a good collection of artefacts from the ruins of Anuradhapura. There is a gallery showing the original form of various ruins when they were discovered, and their post-restoration form.
There are so many stupas scattered around a vast area. All the stupas are huge that one must be spellbound thinking how they were built so long ago. 
Then there is Samadhi stupa. The highlight of Anuradhapura is the Mahabodhi tree, which is the offspring of the original Mahabodhi tree from Bodhgaya, under which Goutama achieved Moksha!
A visit to Anuradhapura is a must while visiting Srilanka.

Title: Oldest tree in the world
Text: This is the oldest tree in the world and part of the Bodhi Tree were Buddha found enlightenment. There was a really impressive energy around which can be felt. But I expected the tree to be a little more bigger and more impressive, but still it's very much worth visit!

Title: Visiting the oldest (the holiest) tree in the world.
Text: The temple of Bodhi tree is a very nice experience, watching the beklievers who came there to enjoy the presence of spirit of Buddha.

Title: Very important place
Text:
This is a very important place for Buddhist people.  There are so many religious believes and history attached to this.

If you wish to witness the religious offerings then should visit the early morning ritual around 5.00 a.m

In addition to this you still can visit at any time.

Should visit in decent,  long attire.

Title: Greatest place in this earth !
Text:
We have been to Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi whilst exploring Aunradhapura. This one of the amazing place I've been in my life. You can feel that spiritual feeling when you entered. It's so nice to sit in aside and to watch how locals come and worship. 
one of the must places that you need to visit if you go to Anuradhapura.

Title: Wonderful visit to the Maha Bodhi tree
Text:
Felt wonderful to visit the Maha Bodhi tree and meditate there with my wife. Really felt enchanted and blessed. 
Really worth the visit

Title: Inspiring Spiritual Centre.
Text:
I started my exploration of  Anuradhapura with visit to Sri Maha Bodhi, a sacred tree and considered as oldest in the world.There is a common ticket for visiting the ancient historical sites in Anuradhapura and for the passport holders from South Asia there is a concessional rate.It's necessary to hire services of a professional guide and normal rate is 2000 Sri Lankan Rupees or around 20 US$ as the sites are scattered in a vast area that needs timely location and assistance. Thousands of devotees visit this place everyday and there is dress code and shoe and hat not allowed. It's believed that Princess Sangamitra, sister of Mahinda who introduced Buddhism in Sri Lanka brought the cutting of Bodhi tree from India to this place. This place is most important religious centre for people of this country. Since this is a spiritual place one should maintain proper decorum and dignity here
A must visit in this ancient city.

Title: Vy powerful energy
Text: I just love this place. Very powerful temple but the only thing is the tourist got to get their tickets in most of the sri lanka Buddhist temples which doesn't make sense at all. We are coming from far to get buddha's blessing. This is no a theater to sell tickets.

Title: Calming
Text:
We were taken here by our guide as part of a bigger tour.
Very calming and interesting, take some time to relax and think

Title: quiet and spiritual place
Text: It is really nice and spiritual place situated in Sacred city in Anuradhapura. We took a rest there. It is good to go there on Sunday.

Title: Piece of History & Spirituality
Text: Go here to feel the spirituality and the history of the Maha Bodhi. Remember to take some flowers and incense/candles if you like and cover your legs

Title: Really interesting place in terms of history and current practice
Text:
Seeing the bodi tree and temple complex was really interesting. This was the start of our tour of the cultural triangle and it makes a great place to start. 

Our driver suggested a guide which we took for 2000r and it was well worth it to understand the symbolism and rituals s week as the history which you can get from any guidebook. Understanding the moon and guardstones for example set us up for appreciating all the other temples we saw and was a good starting point for our  kids aged 13 and 10.

The site is super busy with tourists but also regular worshippers and that's what made it so interesting compared with other less busy temples.  Stay and watch the processions and you will learn about local/religious customs.

On a practical note as it's so hot and you need to remove your shoes, kids (and sometimes adults) can wear socks so bring a pair with. You need to cover shoulders and below the knee so having a sarong in your bag is very handy if you don't want to wear trousers. You can't wear hats or caps either.

Title: Visit to the oldest tree
Text: Amazing to visit the temple and see such a busy place in action. Small extra charge LKR200 to go into the temple.  We were there when a service was taking place which was extra special and the oldest tree is massive.

Title: Second most sacred place in Sri Lanka
Text: It is a must visit place if you are in Anuradhapura. You can hire a tuktuk in about 1500 Rupees for visiting all Anuradhapura ruins. Very beautiful Frasco paintings are on the wall and add beauty to the place. A lot of native people perform their rituals and offer their prayers.

Title: Most Sacred Tree
Text: This is believed to be the most venerated Fig Tree in the Buddhist world. This place easily can be reached by Train. Just walking distance from Anuradhapura main train station. We saw the ceremony at 6:15pm and it is colourful and and lot of devotees were there.

Title: Best in evening and not on weekend
Text: This is magical . Make sure you are covered shoulders and below knees. You can sit and watch for hours. The main tree is looking very well

Title: Interesting to see the pigrims
Text: The temple itself is not stunning, but  you should pay attention to the pilgrims that have come to the tree from all over Sri Lanka. Very interesting to learn more about local Buddhist practices.

Title: Roots of Paradise
Text:
Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi is the most sacred place in Anuradhapura. It is a raised platform in Mahameghawana Gardens which contains a branch of a fig tree (called Maha Bodhi in Buddhism) under which Mahatma Buddha is stated to have attained enlightenment (nirwan) in Buddha Gaya, India. 
This tree (sapling) was planted here in 249 BC and is known as the oldest surviving tree in the world which has a known date of plantation. It was brought here by Sangamitta, daughter of Emperor Ashoka of India with great pomp and show 2500 years ago. Emperor Ashoka was himself present in the celebrations held at the Indian port of Tamalitta in which this sapling was dispatched to Sri Lanka in a ship. Sri Lankan King Devanam Piyatissa himself received the sapling at the Sri Lankan port with great honor and pageantry. While standing under this tree, I thought that it was like a peepel tree. For about two billion people of the world, it is the most sacred tree and is called Roots of Paradise on Earth by Buddhists.

Title: 2300 Years Old Maha Modhi Tree
Text: In 3rd Centuary BC Princes Sanghamitra planted this tree and now the centre of Buddhist activities in this beutiful Island Country.. A must visit... you will feel calm.. this tree is the branch of original Maha bodhi tree of Bodh Gaya where lord Buddha got enlightenment...

Title: Popular among locals
Text: Take a short visit to see the locals praying and understanding their culture. You require to remove your shoes so avoid going there in noon.

Title: Nice place
Text: I went there when I was in Anuradhapura. Buddhist people should go there also other religions accept but you can't wear less clothes like bikinis.

Title: Buddh'as Relics.
Text:
This Bo tree is the right wing branch from the o tree in India under which Lord Buddha attained enlightenment.
The bars around the tree are made of 24c  gold and a gorgeous sight.

Title: A fabulous journey along the devotional path!
Text:
This shrine is crowded all the time, but worth the long walk to the
main shrine.  You can get a white string around your wrist, receive a blessing and feel at peace with yourself and the world!

Title: A Holy and Spiritual Experience
Text: I felt a sense of awe and humility visiting the Sri Maha Bodhi. Eventhough i have visited the temple a few times over the last few years, the experience you feel, the sirituality you experience and the humility you succumb to is overwhelming. Just to see both the young and old paying reverance and gratitude to the oldest living religious tree in the world is a moving experience.

Title: Talk about a let down
Text: We were actually really excited to see this, shame it's just a pretty uninteresting looking tree surrounded by thousands of people. I'm sure if you're a Buddhist then this is a pretty incredible place, but if you're expecting an amazing ancient tree prepare to be disappointed. Its just a tree with a wall and a gold fence around it. I think we made a mistake going on a weekend which meant thousands of pilgrims everywhere, which definitely detracted from the overall experience. The noise from the loud speakers and the litter being dropped by 'pilgrims' is just horrendous

Title: Enjoyable and serene
Text: I went there as part of my exploration of archaeological sites.  The tree itself I didn't go inside to as they wanted 200 rupees and it was lunch time so it was shut anyway.  I didn't feel the same sacred energy as in bod guya in India plus I have seen and mediated under so many of those trees. I liked it as there was no one there and it was calm but if you should go visit in the evening as the light will be beautiful I am told by the locals. I was going to go back but I never made it. Enjoy:-)

Title: Divine
Text: We visited this place during the Christmas break of Dec 15 and it is very divine place, on our day of visit there were many people paying homage to Bodh Tree

Title: Evening ceremony
Text: Went in the evening for the evening ceremony and stayed for an hour. Bodhi tree looked great in the twilight and there were lots of devotees even at that late hour. A large number of bats flocked to the tree at about 6.30pm. There was a power outage that evening as well

Title: Pay money to see a tree
Text: If you do not believe in this don't go as this is paid separately to the sacred city entrance fee. It is a tree within a house. Many people pray and when you go outside they try to be nice and offer you a candle 'for good sake' bla bla. In the next minute (as almost everywhere in this country) they try to rip you off.

Title: Religious fervour
Text: A must visit for Buddhist devotees, feel the place to understand the sentiments . A tree protected by all here, symbolises the birth of Buddhism in Sri Lanka

Title: A Must Visit
Text: I participated Evening Ceremony  around 6.00pm and it ended around 7:15pm. We can buy all necessary item from the small flower shops at the entrance

Title: Sacred tree for Buddhists
Text:
We visited the sacred bodhi tree late on a Sunday afternoon when many pilgrims were present. Whilst this ancient tree is generally impressive to tourists it is sacred to Buddhists and, therefore, we tried to be discreet when taking photographs - so to be as unabtrusive as possible.

If you are a general tourist and your schedule does not allow time for a visit to this tree then there are many other bodhi trees in the ancient city areas which you will come across on your travels.

Title: Awesome tree but not much more
Text: Perhaps, amongst the oldest trees in the world, growing from a sapling from the original bodhi tree in Gaya, India. It has survived the many ups and downs of the turbulent history of the ancient capital. The tree is phenomenal in every sense but, to be honest, there is not much more to see at that location and it is a long walk to get there unless you have private transportation. Still, worth it.

Title: For devotees only
Text:
It costs 200 LKR for foreigners to enter. It's kind of interesting to see the tree that inspires such devotion among the local. It's still just a tree, even if it's a sapling from the original Bodhi tree. There's not much else to see here except for the attached temple, which is kind of kitsch.

I'd rather go see the original in Bodhgaya. For devotees only.

Title: Beautiful Ancient and historical site
Text:
Such a beautiful site, the Bodhi tree also neighbors other attractions seen in Anuradhapura such as Lovamahapaya ( the stone ruin pillars ) and Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba ( the large white building that normally represents the main attraction in Anuradhapura ) 

Our day was simply amazing due to one key factor, our Tuk Tuk driver "Lalith Priyashantha" This kind man is the only reason I have started my trip adviser account so I could blog about his services to us.

He made us feel safe, welcomed and very comfortable. 

As we only had a short time we needed a place to store our bags so he called his shop owner friends and organized everything for us. 

Here comes the crescendo, he wanted to do it all for only $15 AUD which is 1500 rupees . We could not have asked for a better 6 hours in this beautiful ancient city. 

By the end of it my girlfriend and I were so happy with his service we gave him $30 AUD because how special he made the day, he WOULDN'T EVEN ACCEPT THE MONEY !! He asked us if we were students, we told him we weren't and that we had full time jobs just so he'd take the offer.
