Title: Enlightenment Tree
Text: The oldest historically documented tree on earth were Buddha gained enlightenment. Very sacred and serene place to visit

User_Location: Capelle aan den IJssel, The Netherlands
Title: tempel vist
Text: The bodhi tree is not very interesting only with the story that this tree is very old makes it worthwhile to seen.

Title: The original tree is in India, in Bodhgaya
Text: By all means visit Sri Lanka. It is a special place with all its charm. But none of these World Heritage sites worth visiting. Not a single one of these ancient cities can qualify to be sites worth seeing. Go visit Tikal, Cairo, Varanasi, Chaco, Angkor, and the list goes on. This tree is a hype as well. Pay a lot of money to walk on barefoot to see sapling behind a fence.

Title: Unforgettable experience
Text: Its say that this ancient tree is grown out of a root/branch of the original Bodhi tree in India. The hundreds of pilgrims make this spiritual place very special. It was amazing to see the pilgrims praying, offering gift and worship this place. The tree is surrounded by a fence so you cant see the tree very well. If you want to make an offer to the tree, you need to give your gifts to the guards. They put them under the tree. You experience the Buddism very well.

Title: Bodhi Sacred
Text: Can't avoid feeling the spirit of this (oldest?) tree on earth, grown from a cutting of the Bo tree Siddhartha meditated under when he became Enlightened. Truly amazing.

Title: Interesting to see the worshiping people
Text: If you are not a buddhist the tree does not have any meening to you and from that standpoint isn't overly exciting to see. What's making this whole thing interesting is seeing all the people and what they are doing there. We were there on one of the holy days, so it got pretty crowded. There were lots of offerings and people everywhere. We felt a bit like intruders disturbing the rituals, but our guide told us it would be o.k. to walk around and take pictures there. I hope that was not only him. ;-)

Title: For the devout!
Text: Said to be grown from a sapling brought from the Bodhi tree from Gaya below which Buddha is supposed to have attained entitlement. A bit of a walk from the Ruwanwelisaya stupa.

Title: Last one standing
Text:
The sacred Bo Tree, stemming from the original Bo Tree Buddha found enlightenment under, is an impressive structure surrounded by several small temples and prayer rooms. The site draws pilgrims from all of Sri Lanka to regularly pray and pay tribute. Quite an experience not to be missed when in the area. 

The sand covered grounds are a relief for your bare feet.

Title: Apparently this is where Buddah received his 'enlightment'
Text: Not much really to add to the title really.  Devotees of Buddah would find this of interest as would other tourists.

Title: Very spiritual
Text: It was very busy the day we visited but it was worth the hustle and bustle. We had a priest tie our wrists and say a blessing for us which was very special.

Title: A religious site
Text: If you are religious and into Buddhism then this is a very important site. Its a popular site for Buddhists but if you are tight on schedule and have limited time in Anuradhapura, you can miss it.

Title: Humbling
Text: It is always difficult to be a tourist at someone else's religious site, and this place is a very significant centre for Buddhists. Whilst there were literally hundreds of people sitting around the perimeter, or quietly walking ( always clockwise), around the shrine, and a constant burble of chanting, it was a peaceful and humbling experience, and a privilege to be allowed to be there.

Title: Not quite sure.
Text: We found that there was not a lot of information about the site that was obvious when we visited. Central area was locked off. Nice enough, but without the info, a little mysterious. Yes I know we could have done a bit of research, but some on site information would be good.

Title: A moving site
Text: I'm not a Buddhist, but the site was moving nonetheless. I really enjoyed the serenity of the temple and it was interesting to watch people worship. The Bodhi tree itself was a bit lackluster, but still an interesting piece of history.

Title: Sacred site of Buddhism
Text: Incredibly moving site. The temple has a feeling of peace and serenity. Remember to take socks as the ground is baking hot and as you have to leave your shoes outside you can end up with burnt feet. Also as all sacred sites and temples you have to have your upper legs and shoulders covered.

Title: Excellent place to know Buddhism from close
Text:
Word of Advice: Do not wear any clothing with Lord Buddha on it, it is offensive to locals. Also, your apparel should cover your knees. (shorts etc. may not be advisable)

Anuradhapura is a great place to know about Buddhism from close quarters. Must visit are the stupas near the Bodhi tree. Do spend some time at the Stupa watching people pray. It is a great feeling.

Title: Oldest living tree in the world
Text: Supposedly the longest living tree in the world at over 2500 years of age.  But only a small trunk with a long off-shoot of the original tree survives.  But the ambience is steeped in faith and devotion.

Title: Unforgettable experience
Text: I arrived at 6am to offer flowers to the Bodhi tree. The atmosphere was so good early morning. Flowers are available at the other side of the temple. Do wear decently - long white trouser and skirt. White top covering the shoulders too.

Title: The oldest verifiable tree in the world.
Text: We went to visit the tree but enjoyed being able to take time absorbing the culture and atmosphere of this special place.

Title: A truly magical experience - a special place held in great reverance by so many
Text: So glad we found time to visit - Sri Maya Bodhi is beautiful and the hundreds of people, pilgrims and monks make this a special place, regardless of your faith. Good to visit in the evening when cooler and the light is better

Title: Imagine this trees journey
Text: A most for any one seeking to learn some basics about the spread of Buddism. A magical setting and story. This site is the highlight of the city.

Title: Highly spiritual location
Text: It was very humbling to be in a place which housed a sapling from the Bodhi tree under which Buddha sat and attained enlightenment. To boot, it is located in lovely ancient Anuradhapura grounds.

Title: Historical tree
Text: It is huge tree, but it behind the gates. The guards take gifts from the people and put them under the tree.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Enjoyed a quick visit here on a recent trip to Anuradhapura. 

Skipped paying by coming in the side entrance (good if you didn't buy the $25 pass), no shoes, so be aware of your own needs. Ground gets a little hot and rocky. 

If you are not there for religious reasons, be aware of those that are. Do not walk in front of people praying,  don't take pictures of people without asking (especially monks) and just be quiet as you walk around. 

Definitely a powerful feeling while visiting.

Title: Revered temple
Text: We visited thi temple to see the tree that apparently came from India and was grown from the tree under which Buddha found enlightenment.  It was obviously a very revered temple popular with the locals and it was interesting for a short visit. The surrounding grounds have some ruins from the original city. Good for a short visit.

Title: Sacred tree temple
Text: A sacred Buddhist place, the most ancient tree in the world, from a sapling of the original Buddha's Bodhi Tree. The place has a separate additional fee of 200LKR. Mind that the inner temple closes down daily from 11 to 2, so you cannot get close to the tree during these hours, but you can still wander around the large courtyard (and the ticket fee is waived).

Title: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
Text: This is suppose to be the oldest tree in the world with written records.  A branch from the original Pipal Tree in India where the Buddha attained enlightenment 2600 years ago.  Now this tree is venerated by all Buddhists protected by the governments with security.  beautiful place to visit, giant tree, people gather early morning, around 6am  to pay respects to the Buddha there . Many queue up one could spend some time in meditation and observe and share the food offered free staying outside.  Venerated tree with a meaningful history.  Must visit in Anuradhapura.

Title: A pleasant place to listen to the wind through the leaves and contemplate life
Text: We where here at the end of a warm afternoon in the fading light with all it's atmosphere. Besides the tree there is quite a complex in this grassed parkland. Our small group was honoured with our own prayer service. Spend time to mediate on the Buddha's life.

Title: Very Tranquil Place
Text: A very sacred place for all buddhists with the oldest living known planted tree in the world and one of the sacred relics of buddhists. The tree was in a garden surrounded by a wall and accessed via steps on two sides. Alas a bit disappointed in that when we arrived although we could access the surrounds the gates at the top of thr steps would not be opened until 14.00 and too long to wait for our driver. Nevertheless one could see the tree towering over the site along with others. Tranquil place with many buddhists sitting with offerings waiting in the surrounding area for the gates to open. Check on access times

Title: Sacred and serene, a must see in Anuradhapura
Text:
The great Sri Maha Bodhi is one of the top places a tourist has to visit in the sacred city of Anuradhapura. Mind the dress code please since this is a temple. There is a car park quite close to location and we walked a short distance to a side entrance where two senior ladies operate a shoe-keeping hut. We gave them 50 LRK for two pairs. Then you walk in and absorb the serene surroundings while watching pilgrims pay their respects. There is no fee to get in.

Once we were done, returned to collect our shoes and walked a path towards the other wonderful place, Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba. Do not feed the monkeys or the stray canines for health reasons.

Title: unique
Text:
This place is surprisingly modest. It is very unique. It should be visited with respect. There is a lot of chanting and incense. The tree can't be really see from up close. 
Noone asked us for any entry fee. Bring some flowers instead.

Title: Remember the dress code
Text: We did not know that there is a dress code. No sleeveless shirts for women and no shorts. Also, there is a sign recommending wearing white or light colored clothing. We had to go back and change. We found the place peaceful and was definitely worth the time.

Title: an Interesting temple and the oldest tree in the world
Text: This is an interesting temple to visit with many locals saying prayers. The Bohdi tree is said to be the oldest living tree in the world.

Title: The place to go!!!
Text: Venerated by Buddhists all over Sri Lanka this tree and the temple of he tooth in Kandy are two of the most holy Buddhist sites in Lanka

Title: Very Nice
Text: Not as good as Lumbini, but very nice overall.  Just remember to wear socks if you can't handle the heat of the stones.

Title: One of those place that count for a pelgrim.
Text: The Bo Tree of Lord Buddha, is the oldest registered tree in the world and more than 2000 year's old. Feel the history when you are under it. Be early in the morning so that you can still find a few original leafes from the tree if you want to take a real relic home.

Title: A tree on life support
Text: It was interesting because it is supposed to be a start from the tree where Buddha obtained enlightnent, but total lame as to appearance

Title: Didn't Do Much For Me
Text: This kind of thing is personal to say the least. I liked that they didn't charge the morning we went, and I found the monkeys there more fascinating than the tree. Now, don't get me wrong ... I like really old sacred trees, and have seen a few in my travels, but this Bodhi tree didn't touch me in any special way, and I was left unmoved. But, if you're in town, you might as well swing by and see if it touches you in any way.

Title: most secred tree in the world
Text:
this is supposed to be the oldest surviving tree in the woprld.
the original tree of this was supposed to have given shade to lord buddha when he attained enlightenment.

Title: Majestic Tree
Text: I don't know what I was expecting when I was informed I would get to see a tree grown from the sampling of the tree Buddha gained enlightenment under, but all I can say is that I was surprise.  The tree spans out over the top of this platform and is held up in spots by golden supports.  Worshipers at the temple vie for the caretaker's attention in order to ask for leaves from the tree.  It was quite the sight to see.

Title: One of the world's most famous trees
Text: Anyone interested in Buddhism or the general culture of Sri Lanka must become associated with the Bodhi or Bo tree. This was the tree beneath which it is believed that the Buddha reached Enlightenment. A branch from the tree was brought to Sri Lanka and planted here in the third century BC. The Anuradhapura Bodhi tree is of particular importance for its history and sacred association yet one can find Bo trees in Temple areas throughout the country which are held in the highest reverence and respect.

Title: Sacred tree
Text: We visited it in Anuradhapura. It is the sacred tree of Buddha. The first branch was brought from the tree where Buddha used to rest. There is also a statue of the woman who brought the branch to Sri Lanka.

Title: Sacred place
Text:
Not just one of the very important monument of the Sri Lankan early kingdoms and buddhism history! It's a really living sacred place now.
The world's oldest documented tree, under which Buddha meditated and enlightened. One branch of this tree in 288 BC was brought from India by Sangamitta - the daughter of King Asoka. 

Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes.
I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

Title: one of the greatest places in the world
Text: Different religions and nations find this place good for pray, me too, I was impressed by all this people around me. It was cleaner than in any other place

Title: Must See attraction!
Text: A nice long walk from the Milano guesthoose if you are feeling fit catch a Tuk Tuk back for 200rp, a must go for the age of the tree and an attraction to the Sri Lankan populace. Beautiful flower offerings to buy and don't forget no shots bring a sarong as that will suffice, well worth a visit.

Title: You're there, you have to have a look.
Text:
Great sense of culture, it f"eels" special and significant.
Watch out for the people as you go in trying to give you a flower. If you take one, you'll regret it on the way out!!!!

Title: An interesting religious site
Text: Although this Bodhi tree is very old I think the visit to this site is interesting from a religious or cultural perspective, as opposed to a historical one. The site is actively used by Sri Lankan Buddhists for prayer giving non religios visitors the opportunity to observe Buddhist ritual first hand.

Title: IF YOU ARE A BUDDHIST IT'S WORTH A VISIT. OTHERVISE JUST AN ANCIENT TREE!
Text: In SriLanka, a Buddhist religious country, people worship this tree as a sacred place. This tree is a sapling from the historical Bodhi tree, where Buddha enlightened. It was planted here in 288 BC and is the oldest living human planted tree in the world. (But the oldest living tree is in California USA, is 5064 years old). The tree is surrounded by thick walls, on top of that golden fence also there. Just for anyone it's an ancient tree surrounded by historical statues, walls etc, but for Buddhists this place is a very holy site. My personal opinion if I visit a place for the ancient value, I have to see the place on my own way, not distracted by other people. Already I traveled all over the world, and visited most of the ancient monuments. But here religious value distracted the real ancient value. I am disappointed.

Title: Spirituality Personified
Text: Bodhi Tree - the seat of Vajrashan which provided the shelter to Siddharth Gautam to rise as the Lord Buddha. The most defining tree which historically changed and alter the pace of time and crossed horizons and boundaries of class, caste, creed, culture, race and regions. The tree is magnificent, its persona is symbolic to wisdom-hood. Mere looking at it takes you to millennia at a time when it must only have been a tree, just another tree in the forests of Gaya sheltering thousands of sadhus and monks who were searching of knowledge, enlightenment and peace. With Rahul and Sanghmtra sent by Emperor Ashok himself, who planted the tree at the present site of Anuradhapura is frequently visited place in Sri Lanka. It holds immense importance as it provides the unbroken chain with the original tree of Gaya that was burnt during the 7th century A.D. I have found the site very peaceful and will encourage tourists and pilgrims to visit at the right time and it is one of the most revered and holiest of the sites.

Title: worth a short visit
Text: The symbolism of this place is the attraction, as well as the feeling of peace around it. The story goes that the old tree is a direct descendant of the bodhi tree under which the Buddha found enlightenment. Don't forget to pack a pair of old socks because you have to take off your shoes, and the ground is hot.

Title: Atmospheric
Text: This is a very holy site for Buddhists and most Sri Lankans and the ambience around the tree and the buildings is very peaceful and relaxing.  While you cannot get close to the tree itself you can view the canopy and enjoy the calm.

Title: First stop in Sri Lanka
Text: I rolled in by train to Anuradhapura around 10AM-a little behind schedule-but with plenty of time to see the Bodhi Tree. I was a little disappointed to discover the tree was only viewable from a distance, behind a locked gate.  TIP: No one tells you this, but they open it up after 2pm daily for visitors to get a closer look.  Regardless, while there, I stumbled upon a prayer session and there were these school kids on a field trip there to take part.  It was really lovely to see. I walked around barefoot, took some photos. It really was my first intro to Sri Lanka, so yeah, I guess it was seeing an sacred tree was an alright way to begin.

Title: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi, a sacred place of pilgrimage for Buddhists
Text:
This sacred tree, grown from a sapling of the original Bodhi Tree in Bodhgaya India and brought here by Asoka's daughter Sanghamitta in the 3rd century BC, is of enormous significance to Buddhists from all over the world.  This is a central and very sacred place of pilgrimage and the atmosphere is very special, especially so during daily puja's and poya days.  

Namo Buddhaya, Budu Saranai, Theruwan Saranai.

May all beings be happy and well.

Title: A very special place
Text: As a Buddhist doing a pilgrimage trip this was a very special place to visit, made even better by the fact that it is the only place in Sri Lanka where tourists are not charged anything to get in. A very serene place and a great place to sit and reflect.

Title: You cannot see the tree
Text: The tree is kept elevated and guarded, so all you can see from down below is just a few branches with no indication of how huge it really is. But the temple on the ground is a real Buddhist temple, and you can see people praying, chanting and meditating. Overall, not a bad site, but perhaps not the most exciting one to see.

Title: Stunning history and very holy
Text:
Even though I am not a Buddhist, I could sense the "sacredness" of the place. The original Bo tree is now just a thin remnant (almost like a branch). 

We went on a Sunday, and the temple was quite crowded with pilgrims dressed in white. Perhaps you can avoid Sundays to have a more peaceful visit.

I would also recommend using the guide - Asoka - who gave us an excellent introduction and crash course to Buddhism and the Bo tree (perhaps one of the reasons why we enjoyed visiting this Tree). Asoka can be reached at +94 718907081.

Title: Good
Text: The place was good and neatly maintained. But you need to walk for quite a distance on barefoot with the sun beating down.

Title: An overwhelming ancient city!
Text: To experience the immensity, history and beauty of this complex of temples, palaces and museums, one may want to fortify themselves and plan to tour for a good part of a day.  We visited on a Sunday during which multitudes of pilgrims dressed in white were bringing flowers and offerings to the ancient temple Mahavihara, the site of the Sacred Bo Tree.  Here is a good place to sit or pause to absorb the spiritual meaning of this site for the Sri Lankan people.  After visiting here, my guide led me to the following main sites within this complex:  Ruvansalisaya Dogoba, Jetavana Museum, Jetavana Dagoba, LUNCH (outside of the complex), Lankarama Abhayagir Dogoba and the Twin Ponds (aka Kuttam Pokuna).  To cover this large area you will need a car/tuk tuk or marathon stamina to go on foot.  In the end, this visit was a 5 star experience.

Title: u might achieve enlightement..
Text: spiritual place u dont want to miss when u here in Sri Lanka.. i had an amaizing experience at this place.. my mind was so much at peace as soon as i entered the courtyad of this temple..

Title: Interesting place for worship
Text: The atmosphere and building makes this place more interesting as the tree it self. You have to go barefooted on sand and gravel and after so many temples my feet were becoming painful. There is a place where you can leave your shoes guarded.

Title: Buddhism in a very sacred place
Text:
Fascinating opportunity to observe devout Buddhists - citizens and monks - come together and pray. 

Try to get there in the morning for the monk's procession and breakfast ritual.  Visit The Heaven and ask to hold a pink lotus flower.

Title: Fascinating
Text: Interesting for its history and a privilege to be able to see so many Buddhists visiting this sacred place. The tree itself is not that impressive but the history and atmosphere make this site something special to visit.

Title: Oldest tree of the world (?)
Text:
"A twig coming from the Bodhi tree (ficus religiosa) under which the Buddha found enlightenment was planted over 2000 years ago. And since then this tree was always cherished." - this is the story or legend oft this tree 
It's amazing to see this tree and imagine that it had been standing here for thousands of years.
And it's definitely very interesting to see that nothing has changed, people are coming in masses, all clothed in white (the traditional colour if you go to the temple) with flowers - mostly lotus flowers or water lilies - to bring as offerings. As this tree is important to every Buddhist worldwide I've also seen a large group of Japanese people bringing there offerings. 
Around the tree there are some buildings actually constructed with Japanese money - you can read the memorial plaques.

Title: Historic Religious
Text: King Asokas daughter is reputed to have brought the sapling to Sri Lanka, it is the oldest living tree on the planet. Apart from the tooth relic this is the most revered of all the Buddhist shrines.

Title: What a devotion!
Text: The place(besides the Kandy temple) where we saw that the people from Sri Lanka are very devoted to Buda's teachings. The legend says that this tree (an indian figue) is  an graft from the original one in India where Buda had the illumination.

Title: Bodhi Tree
Text:
The Bodhi tree at Anuradhapura is the oldest documented tree in the world.
After the Muslim invasions in the 11th century, there was devastation of all Buddhist sites in India. On December 8, Bodhi Day is celebrated by Buddhists. Those who follow the Dharma (Buddhism), greet each other by saying, Budu saranai! which translates to the peace of the Buddha be yours.

Title: Blessings
Text: Happy Chinese New Year of Horse *~ <3 ~* Love, Peace, Prosperity and Light to All living things... I love Sri Lanka! The Sacred Tree is amazing!

Title: It's amazing
Text: It's so deserved to visit it, not because there is no entry fee, but the devote of all the Buddhist.

Title: Impressive or not, you NEED to see it!
Text: The bodhi tree itself is not that impressive. It is not particularly good looking or graceful. Its branches are very gnarled, its bark is very rough, and it just shows LOTS of signs of aging. Course, what do you expect for a tree that's hundreds of years old? But the sheer historical significance of it is enough to make any visit to the tree absolutely compulsory for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. It is, after all, more or less the heart and soul of the country. This tree was descended from the very tree that Buddha meditated under and as such is absolutely sacred to Sri Lankans, who, in my honest opinion, seem the most conservative and committed Buddhists I have ever encountered. One cannot truly understand Sri Lankan culture until one is truly aware of how important Buddhism is and how hard Sri Lankans have fought to latch onto it. And it is really hard to get that awareness without beholding this most sacred of Sri Lankan treasures.

Title: wow
Text: Got to see such an important part of buddist culture.  Not to be missed.  This tree is seriously old and sacred

Title: Bodhi tree from India
Text:
Buddha got enlightened in the Bodhi tree in Bodhgaya, Bihar, India. Its sapling is this Bodhi tree in Anuradhapura. It was brought here around 500 years back according to our taxi driver.

You'll see priests chanting Mantras and lot of religious folks here. Overall a nice place to vuvisit when in Anuradhapura.

Title: Memorable visit
Text: Although the tree per se looks rather ordinary, the veneration locals have towards it is something worth experiencing. It is wonderful to see that a tree is still reverenced in some places of this world. The tree is also in the way to the ancient sacred city of Anuradhapura, so I would recommend a first stop here.

Title: Ancient city not worth it
Text: As holy as it may be the maha bodi is just a tree, just like any other tree and you can't even get anywhere close to it. The ancient city of anaradaphura also very disappointing. They wanted us to pay over 3000 to see the sights but the guest book at the ticket office had mostly all bad reviews also. There are some lovely free sights that can be seen in the ancient city however.

Title: Extraordinary
Text: The size, scope and longevity of a living tree is extraordinary ... makes one think differently about nature and living organisms.  Thought provoking.

Title: Ancient City of Anuradhapura
Text: The Historical City of Anuradhapura is the Mother of Culture in Sri Lanka. Buddihism was brought into Sri Lanka through this city. There are numerous Stuphas (Buddist Templates), with each of them in a Unique Fashioned and styled. Some examples are Largest Stupha, Chilli Stupha, Bodhi Tree, Cave Stupha and many more. Relatively Calm and peaceful city, with pronounced Military presence.

Title: Holy atmosphere
Text: We love the holy atmosphere and the temple monkeys there.But feel a bit like invaders,because there were a lot of local people worshipping.We didn`t pay any entrance fee,i think it`s free of entrance fee.At the most places the Sri Lankan departments take pretty high prices from tourists.But there nobody controls tickets.Inside on the yard there was a ticket-counter,but the guy was sleeping with his head on the table.

Title: A tree and a statue
Text: That is exactly what it is. A tree and a statue. Historical, of course. The tree has fallen down due to age. There is nothing else to see apart from the status. May be a 15 min stopover.

Title: From a leaf to many shapes
Text:
Sacred Sri Maha Bodiya, 2,300 year old site - Visited this National Heritage site as part of a 17-day Bunnik tour.
Note: Shoulders & knees covered + Rupees for the person who looks after your shoes + you might like to have an old pair of socks to wear as the ground does get quite hot + 200 Rupee entry charge.
Fold the leaf of the Bodi tree and it represents many shapes = Stupa, Dagaba, Pagoda, etc. 
An interesting site to visit.

Title: Across the Centuries to Buddha
Text:
Having visited Bodh Gaya it was fascinating to see the "son" or "daughter" of the original tree. This is older than the one now in place in Bihar where the Buddha was enlightened. Yet it is also protected behind railings and propped up with gold struts. In addition there is a guardian force comprised of those descendants of locals who protected the tree during various incursions. 

At the time of our visit there was a pilgrimage by the military comprised solely of officers. It did seem slightly incongruous with the juxtaposition of peace/enlightenment with arms.

Title: An amazing experience
Text: This was an amazing experience. We went there in the evening and the place was packed with people. Monks surrounded the Bodhi tree meditating. It was amazing to witness such devotion and serenity all in one place. We had a guide with us, so he explained the history behind the place. I recommend to go there with a guide, otherwise you cannot grasp the history behind this magical place.

Title: Great History
Text: The temple is a wonderful historical site but locals who just drop rubbish anywhere is disappointing. you need old socks for visiting this whole area as shoes off is mandatory in the temples but the ground can be very hot. Females must remember to bring a light shawl to cover shoulders or where a shirt and ensure knees are covered.

Title: A peaceful place for Buddhist worshippers
Text: It is claimed that this ancient bodhi tree,was planted in 246BC and Buddhists believe that it is a sapling of the ancient bo tree in India under which the Buddha achieved enlightenment. As with other such places footware must be removed and other clothing regulations observed. It is a peaceful environs with many worshippers -sitting around.

Title: Wear sunscreen and keep your socks on!
Text: Bit over seeing "bodhi trees" everywhere! However this one has been certified as the genuine thing. There is actually two trees at the site with smaller one being the real tree even though its totally overwhelmed but the larger one. You can't approach the tree but its quite powerful to see how much it means to the numerous Budhists who flock to the place to pray and leave offerings of lotus flowers and jasmine. You have to take off your shoes but you can keep your socks on which helps with the very hot ground. Loved watching the monkey families around the grounds outside.

Title: Living relics
Text: Local people throng hatless and shoeless in the hot sun bearing lotus blooms to perform ancient rituals that seem to have nothing to do with the Buddhism taught to Western consumers. Set among the ruins and other Buddhist sites both ancient and modern, the tree was purported to have been brought over from India as the original the Enllightened One sat under. Worth seeing and free but not so the $25 for a few crumbilng stones and a very ordinary trio of "museums" with artifacts that look more interesting in the gift stalls lining the way to one of the many stupas. Tropical countries and preservation of what looks like sand stone is I would have thought an impossibility. Is there anything to restore - doesn't look like it!!!! The stupas are intact but do not look ancient and no one could tell me what they were for and what was inside. Thank goodness for Google! Tip - get a guide that knows something and watch out - they lay in wait at the station and make promises they don't keep.

Title: Nice to take a tour ...
Text: An highest boudhist site ...lot of people , wonderful flowers offered ...and surprises ..you maight see a beautiful green parrot leaving in the main tree ...

Title: Take your socks.
Text: Arriving on a Poya day, there were a gazillion people there.  Make sure you take a pair of socks, as will all temple and stupa areas it is a hat and shoe free zone.  Wearing socks is acceptable and respectful.  The biggest part of the experience was the immersion in the local culture.

Title: Popular site
Text: Judging by the number of nationals visiting this site you can tell how important it is. The one remaining branch might not overawe as an attraction in itself but its existence and  significance cannot be underplayed. Well worth a visit.

Title: Excellent energies
Text: We had the pleasure to meet a nice guide (he spoke 5 languages - which is very rare here) and he shared tons of information with us. So we visited every single segment of the place and made tons of nice pictures.

Title: Ancient wonders
Text: Most ancient  known tree in the world shows the skills and knowhow of the ancient people in Sri Lanka. When you look at the boundary and surrounding walls made of granite stones with featured round, square and triangular shapes with patterns. Sandakada Pahana (granite entrance step with animal carvings) which only can be found in Sri Lanka is an invaluable asset to a proud history of Sri Lanka.

Title: Highly recommended Unesco World Heritage Site
Text: This was such an ancient tree and so significant in the history of buddhism,  it was hard to take in how long the history is.  We visited just after Poson Poya (June 2013) and the site was very messy after a massive festival picnic had taken place two days before.  Nevertheless it was very interesting and wonderful to see local people as pilgrim visitors which made the site feel very 'real' rather than a spectacle.  Itr was really hot - go early or late in the day.

Title: Rewarding experience
Text: We arrived during a religous festival so it was quite crowded and all the better for it. Unlike many of the temple ruins around this is a living breathing Place of worship. Bear this in mind as you enter.

Title: Peaceful and significant
Text: The walk up to and around the Bodhi tree is lovely, and once in the grounds, it feels so peaceful and serene. People in white pray all around, and the significant bodhi tree stands tall amongst the smaller surrounding trees. Well worth the visit.

Title: To visit at night
Text: Entrance to the Bodhi Tree is free (at least in the evening). I really recommend to visit it in the evening, the atmosphere is really quiet and different.

Title: Beautiful and interesting
Text: I enjoyed our stop at the Bodhi tree along with the other sites in the area.  The ancient tree itself is on a raised platform with other, newer trees around and two small shrines.  Like most of the sites in Anuradhapura, this is a 15 or 20 minute stop, at most, and has to be taken in the context of the whole area.  Together, they make up an interesting day or two.  Like other reviewers, I thought the price was a bit high.

Title: More than just the famous tree
Text:
The area is that much extensive: not to manage without a car. It starts with the Bodhi Tree and all the worshipping people (after having passed a security check!). Then you go out for the ruins an the famous twin pools. Lots of small stores offering (handcrafted) souvenirs, food, drinks...lots of local people, less tourists than in Polonnaruwa. Ruins more destroyed than in Polonnaruwa, and widely spread (under shadowy trees). One needs more imagination to "see" the oldest king's city. There is a small museum: kind of weird - and kind of charming.
The drive from Habarana might take up to 3 hrs (one way). 
You can combine Anurahapura with Mihintale.

Title: cultural wonder
Text: Make sure that you have a good guide to explain what you see and experience. Otherwise it will be a just another Tree.

Title: Only has meaning if your Buddhist
Text: It is best to see all 8 places of veneration at Anuradhapura as we enjoyed some and others not as much. Keep in mind this is a large site and you need to take a car or bike to each of the 8 spots. To walk, it would take you all day. Our guide had a ticket book worth 25$ USD and at each place would detach a little piece and hand it to the soldiers. Something that surprised us was that even though this is a sacred place there is garbage laying around. I can see how the Sacred Bo Tree would have meaning, if one was a Buddhist, otherwise it is a tree, and tree branch, held up by golden pillars.

Title: Incredible living history
Text: This tree came from a graft off of the original Bodhi tree that the Buddha sat under. It is within the complex of Anuradhapura but foreign visitors have to pay a small additional fee. Wear clothing to cover your knees and shoulders as this is a religious site.

Title: Must visit...!!
Text: Had a opportunity to visit one of the great place in the world.. It's with very impressive surrounding.. I went there in a evening.. Temple was busy with many local peoples. Had a great chance to talk with them. Very calm to sit down and meditate for a while..

Title: Always barefoot
Text: Is is really only a tiny part of the tree that is the Bodhi tree....and you have to walk barefoot over sand not really clean, but is a sacred tree so....

Title: See it for the oldest Budhi Tree
Text:
Since you are in Anuradhapura, might as well pay Rs200 and see it.  Only 1 old branch of the Bodhi Tree survives.  Brazen Palace is just next to it (free of charge)

See more entries at
http://clumsycompass.blogspot.sg/2013/03/blog-entries-on-sri-lanka.html

Title: A very spiritual place
Text: A must visit, very spiritual. A highlight in Anuradhapura! Buy yourself some flowers and offer them.

Title: Don't bother buying a ticket
Text: The whole Anuradhapura experience was incredibly frustrating.  Although there are some very interesting sites to see, the ticket price is just extortionate and actually, there were a significant number of people we met who were exploring the area on bikes or in cars who didn't have any tickets.  There were no check points, we didn't have to show our tickets at all, not even at the tree.  Whether this was unusual I'm not sure, but our experience wasn't worth the money.  Maybe it would have been more enjoyable if we hadn't paid $25 each!

Title: nice energy
Text: May be its not the best place as scenary for the picturews but I found it  really spiritual. No harrasment and scam as at some  other temples. People are very helpful and friendly. Definately worth to spend some time incide just to feel harmony and relieve.

Title: An amazing spiritual story
Text: What a spritual place this ancient city is and this tree epitomises the whole place. I am not used to walking barefoot and the heat of the sand and concrete was enough to burn the soles of your feet. But it was  a privilege to join the many  Buddhists who had come to see the sacred Bo tree.

Title: Anaradhaverypoor
Text:
Found the whole ancient city experience very disappointing; Rome or Egypt this definitely aint! You can't get anywhere near the Sacred Bo Tree, and, lets face it, you seen one dagoba you seen 'em all. 

Dambulla and Pollonawura are definitely worth a visit, but if I were planning our trip again, I'd give Anaradhapura a complete miss; think I was fooled by too much guide book flimflam!
But Sri Lanka a great place and the Sri Lankans lovely people.

Title: Sacred Bo tree
Text:
A bo tree that is extreemly important to budhists around the world . 
It'S the sapling of the original  bo tree where Lord budha was meditating  when he attained nibbana/enlightenment .

It's a place of religios importance to Budhists.
A golden fense surrounds this magnificent tree which is more than 2500 years old .

Title: Anuradhapura: great story, less to see
Text: This site has definitely the best history and story to it. However, since it's the oldest capital, there is not much left to really 'see'. It's a whole lot of ruins and some intact statues, tiles and a few stupas. The buddha tree is just ok. We liked Polonnaruwa better (granted, it's a few hundred years newer). The admission price (March 2013) was LKR 3.125 + LKR 200 for the tree (young children are free) - that's 21 Euro or 26 US dollars at the current rate.

Title: Nice - but nothing to die for
Text: Nice to visit if you're in the area - but it's nothing super special, nothing that would justify a trip

Title: Important for buddhists, less for tourists
Text: While the spirituality of place is undeniable, the tree itself is not much to write home about, especially when compared to other wonders of Anuradhapura and Sri Lanka...

Title: One of the oldest and most sacred of trees
Text:
One of the worlds oldest recorded trees and certainly the most revered, visited by buddhists from all around the world.  It is said to have grown from a cutting of the original tree under which the Buddha attained Enlightenment in India. The tree has been tended for 23 centuries and cuttings have been taken and planted in temples throughout the island. 

There is no entrance charge as far as we could tell but security here is tighter than at other attractions in Sri Lanka (a result of the bombings in 1998) and there separate lines for men and women. This is a sacred place so, as for all temples, you must dress respectfully (legs and shoulders covered).  You need to remove hats and shoes. You are allowed to keep socks on and I would recommend this as it is a bit of a walk to get to the tree at the centre of the complex.  

The site was very tranquil and it was interesting to visit for the history.  You need to bear in mind that you will not be able to get a close up view of the tree as it is enclosed by a wall and railings.  Only two branches of the original tree remain, and these are supported by props. This is the main reason we personally didn't feel able to score higher than a '3'.  Devotees on a pilgrimage will obviously feel very differently.

Title: Sacred Tree
Text: Amazing to hear the story behind this tree and then to see it in all its glory. Sri Maha Bodhi as it is known is highly regarded by the local people and rightly so. It is a piece of history that has been treasured and is there to delight all who visit.

Title: Very atmospheric
Text: An active pilgrimage site around the descendant of the original Bodhi tree.  Definitely worth seeing for the atmosphere and religious practices there.

Title: Witness the Buddhist connection
Text: It is amazing to see Buddhist in Sri Lanka still very connected to their religion's root. Atmosphere in the temple surrounding Bo tree was calm and filled with pilgrims. The Bo tree was well kept and maintain, only few people are granted in the inner area near the Bo tree.

Title: Only for the most devoted
Text:
If you're a devoted Buddhist, then this must be a place not to be missed. A small square with a small temple where devotees go in to pray. Others seat on the surrounding sand grounds chanting and singing Buddhist scripts.

The tree is quite large and the windswept grounds is pleasant to walk.

Title: Bo Tree was nothing special
Text: Only part of the tree remains and is supported on a mass of trusses. Interesting due to its age but hardly worth a photo.

Title: A special poya day
Text: The place was crowded with pilgrims from all over Sri Lanka for this special place, on a special day.  The atmosphere was very calm and quiet and we enjoyed talking with people from all over the country.

Title: The famous Bo tree
Text: If you are in Sri Lanka this is a must!!The site is well organised and well kept.Its good to see that it is tout free and people are not hassled as at some sites.

Title: Just OK
Text: Went to visit the temple and tree on Christmas Day. Very spiritual place, whether Christian or not. A bit disappointed, as the tree is encased and hidden behind a wall, then there are ribbons and fabric that surround it, so very hard to get up close.

Title: Buddist shrine in lovely complex of temples
Text: A fascinating shrine which is much venerated. It is surrounded by a whole complex of interesting temples and monuments.

Title: Probably better to come at sunset to experience more atmosphere
Text:
We visited the Sri Maha Bodhi at the end of our day cycling 30km around Anuradhapura. While its undoubtedly a very holy place, when we came it wasn't particularly busy and the atmosphere that guide books and other reviewers write about seemed to be lacking. But it was still good to appreciate the age and significance of the tree and wider site. Perhaps a visit later in the day would have been more atmospheric as guide books suggest.
When we visited the main entrance was closed so we had to walk round to another entrance (not too far). There was no entrance fee and we were able to leave our shoes for free outside.

Title: Good visit
Text: I did all the temples in one day, theyre all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

Title: Oldest Buddhist Tree?
Text: Our guide Sunil from TourMart.lk took us to visit this ancient site. A very peaceful place where you get to experience locals and monks chanting sutras and offering flowers.

Title: Worlds oldest tree?
Text: A religious site & very special for Buddhists, who believe it is derived from the tree where Buddha gained enlightenment some 23 centuries ago. Followers leave donations of flowers, drinks etc. The Priests will chant & bless visitors & tie a thin ribbon on your wrist. Nice experience

Title: The Branch of Buddha
Text: The Sri Maha Bodhi is the oldest historical authentic tree in the world ; a branch of the tree beneath which at Buddha Gaya in north India the Buddha himself found enlightenment. It is supported and preserved. On some auspicious days crowds swell here to pray. Give donations. You need to take shoes off. Enjoy the experience!

Title: Oldest tree in Sri Lanka/world
Text:
Visited this with our guide (Sri Lankan guide, not spiritual guide!!).  He reports that it is one of the most holy places in Sri Lanka.  No bare shoulders, and there is upmost respect for the temple and it's statues.  He reports that people wait all day for one of the leaves, from the tree, to drop.  It's meant to bring very good fortune.  
The tree itself was having some work done on it so couldn't see the trunk.  There were masses of people bringing offerings for the tree and to pray.  Holy man put some twine around our wrists and blessed us.  Not a very religious man but feel that the general acceptance of your fellow man is a great philosophy.  Did not feel like a tourist, more of a guest.

Title: old tree
Text: It was incredible to see the long queues of people ready to pray and recognize the value of a tree. For Buddhists, this tree is incredibly important. It's near the back of the compound, and the queue moves quickly, each person is able to say a few words from their heart.

Title: Curious  Tourists
Text: This is one of the most important place for Buddhist. Botree is  a branch of the actual  botree Buddha sat under for many weeks until he achieved enlightenment.     For tourists I am not sure if it is worth a  visit as there is nothing much as the tree is over the ground level.   I leave it up to the individuals interest.

Title: A special place
Text: no matter your beliefs this is a very special place to Buddhists and to go and walk around this temple with this very special tree is good for the soul.My advice go at dusk. and remember to make a donation to the women who handle all the shoes.

Title: Oldest known tree in world
Text:
This sacred tree is believed to be the oldest planted tree in the world, planted in 249BC from a cutting of the Bodhi tree from India under which Buddha is believed is have gained enlightenment.
This tree has been nurtured for over 2000 years and many Buddhists take a pilgrimage to see this tree and to offer sacrifice and prayer there. 
Wear white and shoulders and legs must be covered.

Title: Old and must visit destination
Text: Beautiful old temple. Very calming. Dont forget to visit the lamp burning area and incent stick burning areas

Title: Holy Tree
Text: The Bo tree here is very old.This tree is venerated by all Buddhist as a holy tree.Lots of local Buddhist pilgrims in white clothes.

Title: Really enjoyed our visit here
Text:
Visited here as part of our Grand Tour of Sri Lanka and throughly enjoyed it. As with all cultural places in Sri Lanka you need to be mindful that there is a lot of walking without shoes, so advise you take an old pair of socks. It is a very large site, spread out and we walked 3.7 miles without shoes and the ground was very hot.
We visited on a Sunday it was fascinating to watch all the locals and soak up their culture and belief.
Definitely recommend a visit and allow 2 to 3 hours.

Title: A very special place!
Text: This is considered to be the oldest living planted tree! Definitely worth a visit. The temple and grounds are beautiful. Visit during the hours the area around the tree is open and you can receive a blessing and white string tied on your wrist. Socks are helpful as the ground can be very hot.

Title: Vibes
Text: I went at dusk, and the atmosphere was wonderfully serene, despite the number of people worshipping, watching and walking around. Even if you're not a believer, this feels like a place of great import. Go and allow yourself to be part of it; you'll feel the good Buddhist vibes.

Title: Nice to see, but...
Text:
When we visited the site it was very crowded by praying people.
Tourist information were very scarce. Nobody asked for the tickets.
There is no place for a good view of the tree.

Title: Great experience.
Text:
This is a place of devotion and prayer. It is like walking into a church in Europe in the middle of a service except that you are most welcome.

Enter with respect for the locals and treat the site as what it is: a place a spiritual significance for locals not a tourist attraction. 

Enjoy the colors, sounds and energy of the place and you should walk away smiling.

Title: Interesting but very crowded
Text: Perhaps it was the day and time we came but it was crazy busy. A lot of people all the time. The tree itself was impressive for its size and age.

Title: Not a Buddhist so it was just a tree...
Text: ... however it was interesting to see how much it mattered to the Buddhists there. We visited here as part of a tour of Anuradhapura given to us by a guide. We visited here last on our tour as it was getting dark. It was actually a nice to see it as dusk gave the whole place a mystical feeling. You'll need to make sure you cover your upper arms and knees to be allowed in. They are very strict on this.

Title: The Ancient historical Bodhi tree at Anuradhapura
Text: The trip to Anuradhapur was just by chance as we had to exchange some money while on our trip to Wilpattu. The sacred city of Anuradhapura is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world and was the ancient capital. The first thing to visit which came on our mind was to visit the Bodhi Tree which was brought from India by the daughter of Ashoka, the great, Sanghamitra, was planted at a very auspicious location in the city. This world heritage and religious site was such awe inspiring to visit though we didnt have much time and daylight it was such a 'yog' to visit the Bodhi tree and be blessed by it - it made our Wilpattu and Srilanka trip such a success !!

Title: The Tree of Enlightenment
Text: I recommend to see this place (including the whole Anuradhapura) when Sri Lankan celebrate their New Year. The feast takes a week and during this time many Sri Lankan families from the whole country go to Bodhi Tree (and other sacred places) to bring sacrifices (flowers, food) and to pray. You hardly see any tourists.

Title: Saturday sunset magic
Text: We biked around Anuradhapura for the afternoon, which was a great way to see the sites, and while there was no sunset that day, we arrived at the Bodhi Tree as musicians lead a crowd carrying a 100m long multi coloured "ribbon" that was delivered to the monks who then wrapped it around the fence of the tree, with increasing chanting by the crowd. This was a moving and beautiful ceremony that really made our day, which had been long and hot and a bit tiring. I'm not sure if this happens every Saturday or if it was a special occasion, but if you're there - check it out!

Title: Just a tree to us
Text: To us this was just a very large old tree supported and surrounded with gold plated posts.  It is hard to believe this tree is over 2000 years old.

Title: Free entry
Text: Please wear white and wear something full length when you go there as a mark of respect. But it is not compulsory. It is quite a nice place and is quite active there. Was good to see people so engrossed in their activities. Also do not forget to visit the Stupa which is near it!

Title: Smaller than expected
Text: We have seen the Bodhi Tree in Bodh Gaya in India which we liked a lot better. This version is very small and as spiritual as we expected it.

Title: One place you must visit if you are Buddhist.. or not
Text:
The Bodhi tree is more than 2600 years old. It was a very special trip for me as I am a Buddhist.  I felt so peaceful and felt like I was giving respect and pray to Buddha, himself. 
If you could, please visit early in the morning and late evening to avoid the heat.

Title: Difficult to See
Text: This tree is reputed to be one of the oldest in Sri-Lanka and important to Buddhists. It is surrounded by fences to protect it (unsderstandably) and difficult to photograph.

Title: Beautiful Ancient Tree
Text: I only wish we could see the whole trunk of the tree! The only part that is visible is the top of the tree as it rises above the temple. The base of it is in the area that is off limits. It doesn't look as old as they say it is, but then again it is very well looked after.

Title: Of enormous significance to all Buddhists
Text:
As others have said, it's just a tree - but it is a hugely important and sacred one if you are a Buddhist. The amount of care and attention that it has received over the centuries has been remarkable, and all carefully recorded too. It's also worth a visit even if you're not a Buddhist.
However, as others have also said, the extra charge for entry is unnecessary. The Sri Lankan National sport of relieving overseas tourists of their money does get extremely wearing after a while. It's like having someone's fingers perpetually in your wallet. Apparently, there used to be a single payment that got you in to all the ancient sites, but that was discontinued and now each site gets to make it's own charges. Hmmmm. Quite a backward step, I think.

Title: A sacred place for worshipers
Text: The branch of bo tree was brought here some 2,300 years ago directly from India by Sanghamitta thero, daughter of Emperor Ashoka.  Although the tree was not very large or bushy in appearance, it has its spiritual value.  As such many worshipers came and made their blessings and offerings and the whole area appeared to be peaceful but lively.  Worshipers could have their lunch in the surrounding area after the pilgrimage visit.

Title: Worth a visit - but why the extra payment??
Text:
The tree itself was a big disappointment; it was neither enormously big, nor specially beautiful. You easily see nicest ones all around the country. I do agree though that the ambience is pretty mystical and the site is "alive". 

By the way don't expect to approach the tree too close: there is a wall around it, apparently to avoid illnesses and make a follow up on its health. 

One thing that I find annoying is that there is a separate, extra payment for the tree: really?! We just paid 25 dollars to the Government (NOT the people or the site, if you listen to the locals)

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Religious site so you have to be aware of your clothing and be prepared to go barefoot. Here it is not good to stress better to adapt the speed of walking to the other visitors. Peaceful atmosphere.

Title: Small but stunning
Text: Despite the 2000 year old tree being a fair bit smaller than we expected, the area is quite magical, it would be a perfect spot for some meditation when it's not too busy,.

Title: Oldest tree in the world
Text: The Sri Lankans claim this buddhist bodhi tree is the oldest tree in the world. It is certainly sacred and the site of religious pilgrimage for Buddhists.  Tourists should go quietly and respectfully.  You will also notice extensive security the result of Tamil attacks in the 90's.

Title: Special place
Text: I'm not religious at all (except for the Flying Spaghetti Monster, look it up trust me) but there is something special about this place. Groups of monks on pilgrimages praying in unison might have something to it but I had goose bumps the whole time I was here.

Title: Really old
Text: This tree is really old. There are much newer and younger trees all around the local area. If you like really old things go to this, but it is seriously old so don't go if you like newer trees.

Title: One of my favourite spots in Anuradhapura
Text: I loved this place so much. We went first thing in the morning right when it opened. Observing the pilgrims making offerings, praying and meditating before those beautiful bodhi trees was a wonderful and awe-inspiring sight. It is a busy spot but so peaceful. Definitely worth the trip!

Title: More than just a tourist site
Text: Visited as part of our day tour of Anuradhapura city. No fee for tourists but 25 rupees for leaving our shoes (a tiny sum of money which I do not resent) and we were too gullible to avoid buying flowers to offer to the Buddha but this is clearly a holy site for practising Buddhists and we were happy to leave flowers. We were reminded by our guide to avoid being photographed with our backsides to Buddha as this is considered  to be offensive but Buddhist worshippers were happy to photograph us with a side on view. Difficult to see much of  the Bodhi tree but glad we visited.

Title: Ancient city of Anuradhapura by bicycle.
Text:
Ancient city is amazing,  $25 entry. Can get a tuc tuc anywhere in the new town and do the ancient city in a couple of hours or much cheaper way is to rent a bicycle for the day. It took me almost a whole day to see all the sites in old the city by bicycle ask your hotel for a map. I stayed in Melbourne Hotel, cheap, nice, they have bicycles, see review on Melbourne Hotel. List and brief review of the sights I went to in The Ancient city:
    
Bodhi Tree Temple (The Sri Maha Bodhiya), this was the main thing I wanted to see, bit dissapointing, you can not get close to the tree, big wall around it. it is not possible to drive up to the temple, and one must go through a metal detector before entering the complex. Shoes can be left near the entrance. It is polite to leave a tip.
Ruwanwelisaya: the oldest and most largest stupa at Anuradhapura, has , been fully restored, painted white, and is currently a centre of worship. 
The Archaeolgy Museum, interesting, ask at the entrance for a museum guide, it is free. Showcases many of the artifacts found at the site
The Folk Museum: Showcases the archaeology of Anuradhapura from a more folk perspective.
Jetavana: Large stupa 
The Citadel: This was the secular centre of the city. 
The Moonstone. This moonstone is of particular note, for its size and impressive decoration.

Title: Great place to observe religious villagers.
Text: It was very impressive to see the way Singhalese express their regards to the Lord Buddha with their praying, wearing white dress and walking on bare feet.  People just do not bother where  they sit as long as they are praying.

Title: My sight of the oldest living tree in the world, The Bodhi Tree of Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka.
Text:
I made an 8-day-trip to Sri Lanka from 8/11/12 to 15/11/12.  On my seventh day in Sri Lanka,  I arrived at the Anuradhapura Railway station at 4.30am.  Earlier, on my sixth day in Sri Lanka,i.e. 13/11/2012, I had boarded a 4.30pm-train from Hatton railway station to Colombo Fort Raiway station.  

Upon reaching Colombo at 10pm, I hopped into the 10.30pm train to the north of Colombo and reached Anuradhapura, one of the ancient capitals of Sri Lanka which is famous for its well-preserved ruins of ancient Sri Lankan civilization, at 4.30am, i.e. after a 12-hours-train-journey from Hatton. Anuradhapura is one of the ancient capitals of Sri Lanka, world famous for its well preserved ruins of the Great Sri Lankan Civilization. The Civilization which was built upon this city was one of the greatest civilizations of Asia and in the world. The city is now a UNESCO heritage site.  Today this ancient city of Sri Lanka, which is sacred to the Buddhist world, and which its surrounding monasteries covers an area of over sixteen square miles ( 40 km²) and is one of the world's major archaeological sites.

After a morning quick tour of the Ancient Ruins & Holy City of Anuradhapura, including Thuparamaya where the collarbone of Buddha is enshrined, Isurumuniya(a picturesque rock temple) and The Sacred Jaya Siri Maha Bodhi at Mahaviharaya/ Mahameghavana Park which is recorded as the oldest surviving historical tree in the world, I took a bus back to Colombo from Anuradhapura New Town at 1pm. 

The oldest surviving tree in the world, The Sacred Jaya Siri Maha Bodhi at Mahaviharaya/ Mahameghavana Park, Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka, is believed to have been propagated from the original Bodhi tree.  This original Bodhi Tree, also known as Bo (from the Sinhalese Bo), was a large and very old Sacred Fig tree (Ficus religiosa) located in Bodh Gaya (about 100 km (62 mi) from Patna in the Indian state of Bihar), under which Siddhartha Gautama, the spiritual teacher later known as Gautama Buddha, is said to have achieved enlightenment, or Bodhi.  According to Buddhist texts the Buddha, after his Enlightenment, spent a whole week in front of the tree, standing with unblinking eyes, gazing at it with gratitude.  The term "Bodhi Tree" is also widely applied to currently existing trees, including the Bodhi tree in Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka, which has a great significance in the history of Buddhism.  

This Bodhi tree in Anuradhapura is widely mentioned in Mahavamsa.  While not considered a canonical religious text, the Mahavamsa is an important text in Theravada Buddhism. It covers the early history of religion in Sri Lanka, beginning with the time of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism.  According to the Mahavamsa, the Sri Maha Bodhi in Sri Lanka was planted in 288 BC, making it the oldest verified specimen of any angiosperm. In this year (the twelfth year of King Asoka's reign) the right branch of the Bodhi tree was brought by Sanghamitt? to Anur?dhapura and placed by Dev?n?mpiyatissa his left foot in the Mah?meghavana. The Buddha, on his death bed, had resolved five things, one being that the branch which should be taken to Ceylon should detach itself. From Gay?, the branch was taken to P?taliputta, thence to T?malitt?, where it was placed in a ship and taken to Jambukola, across the sea; finally it arrived at Anuradhapura, staying on the way at Tivakka. Those who assisted the king at the ceremony of the planting of the Tree were the nobles of K?jarag?ma and of Candanag?ma and of Tivakka.  According to the Mahavamsa, branches from the Bodhi trees of all the Buddhas born during this kalpa were planted in Ceylon (Sri Lanka) on the spot where the sacred Bodhi tree stands today in Anur?dhapura.

Later, after completing my visit to the other attractions of the Ancient Ruins & Holy City of Anuradhapura I took a bus back to Colombo from Anuradhapura New Town at 1pm and reached the Pettah bus station in Colombo at 8pm to put-up a night at a nearby low cost lodge, i.e. Classic Inn in Panchikawatte Road before leaving for the Bandaranaike Airport at 6am of 15/11 to catch the 12.55pm flight back to Malaysia.

Title: Sacred place
Text: This is the most scared place and it is maintained like that as well. Need to improve on sign boards and guide facilities to under stand the place importance.

Title: Worth a look
Text:
The surrounding grounds and trees make this an interesting cultural place to visit .. You really need to understand the meaning of religion to Buddhists to appreciate the peace that comes to the followers .. The tree as described is the oldest anywhere, but worth taking a look it ..
The temple itself probably looked much grander in its earlier days but historically has meaning .. Statues around the area are visible for all to see .. I didnt have a guide to pass me any information but still enjoyed wandering around ..
As everywhere else around Sri Lanka monkeys run freely, and might try to grab your bags .. Dont carry any food or they will chase you, otherwise will just leave you alone ..
Its also pretty hot and you will have to walk around barefoot so wear socks to keep your feet protected from the ground ..

Title: A sacred tree supported in golden poles
Text: From the LP guidebook description I was not expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised by the way this tree has been preserved, and protected.  It stands on a tiered platform, which has been built up over the centuries to support the branches as the tree has developed.  Only two branches of the original tree remain: one old original, supported on magnificent golden poles, and one relatively new shoot.  It is also surrounded by 'daughter' trees.

Title: The oldest tree in the world
Text: The original Bodh tree looks a little sick, but its offspring that is surrounding him looks much better. Definetely a very holy place and a must-do when you are interested in the culture of Sri Lanka

Title: Important Buddhist relic
Text: I am a Buddhist myself, I found this visit to the original Bo tree was out of this world, really glad I made it to see this.

Title: Sacred Bo tree. (Sri Maha Bodhi)
Text: Please visit to  see the sacred Bo tree. (Asathu tree). It was a gift of friendship from the indian king Asoka.

Title: The hot foot massage
Text: Feet were on fire....by the time we walked half the distance, the foot wear stand can be near the place and we dont have to burn our feet. The place is beautifully preserved and rebuilt.

Title: Sri Maha Bodhi
Text: Probably the oldest documented tree in the world. It's interesting to visit this place in the evening, when people are praying.

Title: a sacrat tree ever seen
Text: the guide who was provided by Merveille Holidays explained us this tree is one of the oldest trees in the world. going to this place was a blessing for all our family. As it was said by the guide Vipula, most people had seen and believed lots of deities had been visiting this place at night.

Title: special place to visit
Text: It's not super impressive, but you should visit when you are in the neighbourhood ... The devotees make the ambiance of the place quite special and it's nice to go with that flow

Title: Cost Extra
Text: I was disappointed that it cost extra just to see the tree even though you paid to visit the sight. Watch what time you visit or take a pair of socks as the ground is hot.

Title: Important place for buddhism...
Text: This place is in the sacred city of Anarudhapura, and has an ancient Bohdi tree that was grown from a branch of the same tree under which the Buddha was enlightened. It is a nice place and very important for Sri Lanka and buddhism, but as a tourist may not be the most remarkable place. Anyway, is really near to Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba, that is definitely worth a visit.

Title: Sri maha Bhodiya
Text: A branch of Bo tree in india where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment. One of the great buddhist pilgrimage site.  Damage by LTTE attack 15 years back.

Title: Sacred tree. Important, historic, beautiful - but still a tree.
Text: Every stupa or dagoba has an accompanying sacred tree. You can find more about the reasons for this at this lovely place. The tree is ancient and supported by gold pillars (Sherwood Forest please take note for the Major Oak!). It is a sacred site and has an intense history. However, it is 'just' a tree, so don't go expecting sideshows and playparks.

Title: " Very old sacred tree "
Text: This is a one of main sacred place among Buddhist peoples but there are many visitors in every religion. You must see this place and when you entering to this place your mind getting peaceful in naturally. Many ruins around this  place to visit and there is historical value in each places. This Bodhi Tree one of branch of the Bo Tree which was in India and that tree famous among Buddhist peoples because Buddha got the enlightenment under this tree that's why this is very important for Buddhist peoples. Most of peoples believe that  the tree can bless to our life. According to the records this tree has planted in 3rd century B.C.

Title: A tree with history
Text: The branch that is held up by the gold pillars is believed to be a branch of the exact tree that Buddha himself got enlightened under. The original tree is destroyed and this is the only thing that is left. There are a number of people worshiping and you can feel that this is a place very sacred to the Buddhist. A place to visit if you are in the area.

Title: Enjoyed the visit
Text:
This is a shrine built around a sacred Bo tree.
We really enjoyed listening to the prayers being recited by the worshippers in the temple surrounding the tree.

It helps to wear socks as walking up to the  site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet

Title: Be Prepared to Walk on Hot and Rough Surfaces
Text: As with other Temples, shoes and hats must be removed before entering the Temple area.  I was there around noon and the hot sun and hot surface with no shoes and hat were an issue for me.  The Temple was closed at noon, but the Bodhiya Tree, reported to be the oldest tree in the world, alone was worth the visit.  Rs 200/person on March 1, 2016.

Title: Good
Text: It was a nice place.people sold flowers in front of it.it was the first time that I saw a temple and it was so intresting for me

Title: More than 'Just a Tree'
Text: I have to disagree with my compatriot below. The most important thing about visiting here is the wonderful spiritual atmosphere. This tree is of enormous significance to the people of this beautiful island and both times I have visited I have felt privileged to see this place and understand and feel what it means to them. Visiting today on a public holiday the place was teaming with Sri Lankan people dressed in white and it was a marvellous place to be. Go and make your own mind up though and hopefully you will agree

Title: impressive
Text: and linked to the Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba by a very long and exposed walkway. No hats and shoes allowed, the guard at the entrance seemed to want a little extra $ for keeping our shoes extra safe.

Title: Must see
Text:
This tree is very old and looks like it is tired.
Well protected by a fence and security.
Many Buddhist people visit this place.
Nice to see how devoted the people are.

Title: oldest tree in the world, really!
Text: The fact that you cannot get close to the tree shows that it must be at least very old and under conservation. However, i have seen trees which are thicker and higher and that's why I doubt that this tree is the oldest in the world. Hiowever, it's interesting to hear the stories and see the people practicing their religion.

Title: Bodhi Tree in Anuradhapura
Text:
We visited this place in the evening. It has been said that this tree is the part of the main tree under which Sree Buddha attained enlightenment in India; and this was brought into  Sri Lanka by Sanghamitra, the daughter of King Ashoka more than 2000 years back.
The main tree is not accessible by the public for security reasons, and a temple is also made surrounding the tree where Buddhists visits with offerings like flower and food. Looking at the tree and considering its historic values the mind gets blown away with thrill. A must visit in Anuradhapura.

Title: Significant Temple
Text: One of the most important temples and worth a visit. Fascinating that the tree is reported to be 2,500 years old and so important that it's propped up like an old human. Go early to miss the heat.

Title: Not possible to get close to the tree
Text: If in Sri Lanka, make sure to visit a Buddhist temple.  This is a nice one,  giving you a good impression.  However,  the tree can only be seen from below and you cannot get real close.

Title: Hot and busy
Text: This was the second last stop in our visit of the ancient city, we had started at 8.00am which was great before the crowds and the heat of the day. By the time we arrived here it was the middle of the day, incredibly hot and extremely busy as it was Saturday, a holiday for the locals. An okay visit, would leave it out if you were stretched for time, would be a totally different experience on a quieter, cooler day.

Title: Just a Tree
Text: I realise it's a place of special significance, but they have gone to great lengths to support this tree.

Title: visit to bodhi tree
Text: Very pleasant and satisfying experience. Makes you  feel at peace. It has a very tranquil and peaceful atmosphere.

Title: Tree just like any other tree
Text: But overall experience of all the devout worshippers, the flowers, the colours was fabulous. Warmly recommended.

Title: A special and holy place
Text: In Sri Lanka's oldest capital all attention is focused on an ancient tree, documented as a sapling of the tree under which the Buddha has sat, now over 2,500 years back. It is a popular spot. Local people pay homage, foreigners are curious, there are touts, as there are on most important religious centres. Perhaps not everything is as perfect as Westerns would like to see - but if you just sit down, disregard touts and monkeys as well as your own prejudices, then this is a very special place. Try to go early in the morning or late in the evening.

Title: Really Worthwhile
Text: This is an extremely picturesque area.  The Bo Tree is only one small part of the area. The tree is extremely sacred and this site is very different to most buddhist temples in Sri Lanka, as it is very strict on clothes and shoes.

Title: Touts ruin what should be a solemn and peaceful site
Text:
Let me create a laundry list of pros and cons explaining my poor rating:

Pros:
+ The surrounding park area is nice and relatively peaceful, filled with monkeys and chirping birds.

Cons:
- Touts, touts, touts.  As is endemic throughout Sri Lanka, you find yourself having to stave off wannabe tour guides, and overly aggressive "park attendants".  There was a place left to deposit shoes before entering the holy site, with no sign mentioning a fee.  Within seconds of leaving, I was aggressively hounded for a full 5 minutes by a tout demanding a ridiculous "donation" or "fee" for leaving my shoes outside.  When I politely declined, he left for a moment, then returned to demand a 100 rupee note.  I politely explained that I had paid thousands of rupees to enter the park and grounds (itself an exorbitant 3125 rupees) and that I wasn't in the mood to deposit 100 rupee notes in each and every site I visited, or to every tout who crossed my path - I would have easily been short another 2000 rupees for that day alone.  I ended up, perhaps immaturely, offering a small handful of 2 rupee coins.  He eventually backed off.  This collection of experiences ruined what should have otherwise been a peaceful visit.

Title: SriMaha Bodi...
Text: Its very Peaceful place in the morning by 10.30am it gets really croweded.you may lose were you are even.but it was nice expence all in all

Title: The Real Bo tree?
Text:
The problem is that saplings from the Bodhi tree have been planted across the world. So ever Buddhist shrine has a Bodhi tree. What you need to ask for is the Maha Bodhi tree, the big one, the original one.

You can't really see the tree as it is enclosed by barriers and structures. I went on a Monday about 4 days before the Buddhist new year for Sinhalese and there was a huge crowd there. But, given my experience of crowds in Indian temples, this was a very peaceful and well mannered crowd.

Title: good cultural visit
Text: Take an umbrella to sheld your head from the blazing sun

Title: great

Title: A holy site
Text: this is very special site for Sri Lankan Buddhist.  However, it will look like another ordinary temple for rest of the tourist.

Text: After a 5 minute walk you can see the branch of the Bo Tree that was brought here to Sri Lanka by Indian Merchants and it is supposed to be the tree where the lord Buddha meditated under some 2500 years ago. Together with the temple of the tooth in Kandy these are the two most sacred places on the island.

Title: Nice monument
Text: Very interesting shrine, well worth a visit if you are in the area

Title: Remarkable
Text: A real hive of activity. Unlike many temple areas which are often deserted, this was full of people, both devotees and tourists. We went in the evening but it may be just as busy all day.

Title: busy bo
Text:
The temple was busy with pilgrims so you needn't take your round ticket to this place.

Quite interesting to watch devotees chanting and walking around, making offerings of fruits, etc but the Sacred Bo tree was barely visible so just be aware of that. A couple of scammers tried to get us to pay Rs200 for a piece of cotton which was wrapped around my partner's wrist without asking first.  then someone else tried to sell me some rare coins or something. Text: i liked the old architecture and ruins. well kept.

Title: Interesting place, but we had no time to enjoy it.
Text: We left our shoes far before the temple. Unfortunately we were in the Temple with Bo tree 5 minutes before the doors were closed for preach.. We had time only for a glimpe of the tree and it was difficult to go out of the temple. The area was crowded. Nevertheless we had to pay the entrance fee of more than 10 US dollars. There were too many people coming there for a celebration of the temple. They brought flowers. The place were full with monkeys. Interesting place but we had no time to enjoy the place

Title: A magical experience!!!
Text: I visited the Bo Tree in the evening during the puja time and was amazed with the energy around. It was a humbling experience. The place has many Buddha statues in different positions scatter all around the holy Bo. There are prayer flags all around and can see people add more to the collection. The evening I had been here there was a special prayer service for all the families who had lost their loved ones in war. The atmosphere was emotionally charged. I was just glad to have been able to be a part of it. Definitely an experience I will remember!

Text: It was amazing to stand in front of this Stupa. So big, so white. I walked around it as you should do when you come from afar. But better bring some socks as you have to remove your shoes and the stones on a sunny day can be very very hot!
