Text: Its a historical temple visited by both local and foreign tourist. Amazing sculptures and architectures

Title: Not worth the time and money
Text: Governments main job is to rip the tourist off and even the officials behave this way, arrogant and not customer oriented at all. It is all about money here. The price for tourist RP 3500 compared to almost nothing paid by locals. You have to pay that to be able to access the entire area. Not worth the money. "My generous donation will help you preserve the heritage" (as stated on the ticket) however should the locals be also interested to take a part? After you pay the entrance fee almost nothing is in English. You have to open google to get at least some information. Also you would expect at least basic English knowledge of the staff if you charge this entrance fee. We had a disagreement with the staff I took as 15 mins to find someone who can speak basic English. Or at least clean up at the historical sites from all the garbage. I can't really see here that the money is actually going in the heritage. Didn't buy it. Also to be honest there is not that much you can see for the money here unless you are really a big history fan or Buddhist.

Title: Nice monument
Text: This was our first temple in the Anuradhapura tour and it was particularly nice especially for the bright color of the Buddha.

Title: Stunning

Limited what you can write about a stupa, but they are an absolute must-do in Sri Lanka. As with all temples, you must remove your shoes and dress appropriately. But despite this fact it is worth the visit and especially inside with the temple and the recognition of the king of the time to commissioned its' build. Title: 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction.
Text: The Jetavanaramaya is a stupa located in the ruins of Jetavana in the sacred world heritage city of Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka. Mahasena of Anuradhapura (273301) initiated the construction of the stupa following the destruction of the mahavihara. His son Maghavanna I completed the construction of the stupa. it is also significant in recorded history as one of the tallest structures in the ancient world and the second tallest non-pyramidal buildings after Pharos (lighthouse) of Alexandria; the height of the stupa is 400 feet, making it the tallest stupa in the ancient world. The structure is no longer the tallest, but it is still the largest, with a base-area of 2,508,000 sq ft. Approximately 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction. Its not very popular as some other stupas in the area still very impressive and a must see sight if you are at that area. It is a religious sight and you have to walk bear foot.

Title: Mind-boggling architecture of ancient world !
Text:
The Jetavanaramaya is a stupa located in the ruins of Jetavana in the sacred world heritage city of ANURADHAPURA,, which was also the ancient capital,  Sri Lanka. It was completed at the beginning of 4th Century AD.  A part of a sash or belt tied by the Buddha is believed to be the relic that is enshrined here.

It is also significant in recorded history as one of the tallest structures in the ancient world;  the height of the stupa is 400 feet (122 m),making it the tallest stupa in the ancient world.  Approximately 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction. Conservation work has been funded by the income from ticket sales, mainly to foreign tourists . The entry fee for Foreign tourists is quite high at Rs.3750 per person. As you are required to remove your shoes ; on a hot day you may not be able to walk around the stupa.

Title: The first
Text: This was the first statue of the resting Buddha we saw. Another guide told us it was the dying Buddha? Who knows?

Title: wonderfully colourful
Text: amazing to think this statue once stood  upright. spectacular ceiling and wall decorations. not to be missed

Title: An extraordinary building
Text: Just imagine that this Stupa - in its orignal height - was probably the third largest building in the world (after the pyramids) when it was built in the 3rd century (higher than it is today). Millions of bricks form a magic shape that seem to have been covered previously.

Title: Huge brick Stupa
Text: Once one of the tallest buildings in the world, this is still an impressive sight. I think the guide said it was and still maybe the largest brick building ever made. Certainly should be on your list if visiting Anuradhapura.

Title: One Big Stupa!
Text: They say at the site that, at the time of its building, it was the third largest structure in the world, after the two biggest pyramids of Giza.  I doubt this, as there are other pyramids in Egypt that are bigger, but none the less, this is one big stupa!  It's quite dramatic to walk around it and get a sense of its size.  They say there are 90 million bricks in the stupa.  Now THAT'S easy to believe!

Title: Amazing
Text:
This is a must see in Anuradhapura, as part of a larger World Heritage Site.
It is a huge Buddha in the nirvana  position. The colours of the Buddha and the murals are fantastic , despite its age. 
It is very spiritual.

Title: Anuradhapura never stops to amaze
Text: This Stupa (treasure chamber) with its Budha statue in a dead position (according to the position of the feet) is another example of a magnificent building in Anuradhapura

Title: Impressive Structure
Text: When this stupa was built in the late third century CE, it was the largest brick structure in the world and the third largest structure of any type, exceeded only by a few pyramids in Egypt.  Consisting of over 90 million bricks, it has come down in stature from 120 to 73 meters due to the loss of its spire.

Title: Huge
Text: THis is not only the worlds biggest Stupa, but probably the worlds largest brick structure. Stop off whilst visiting the World Heritage site of Anuradhapura, which is a huge complex and you probably need a few days to see it properly. Has an interesting small temple attached. You don't need long here, but a must visit.

Title: AMAZING. Largest stuppa in the world
Text: This stuppa dates back to the 1st century and is comprised of 93 million bricks.  Wow !  The sheer size and the whole area around left me awe-inspired .

Title: Amazing
Text: Visited here ina recent tour, just before we saw the adjacent Ruwanweli Says Stupa. I have to say I enjoyed this one more - the crowds were far smaller and you actually felt like you could sepnt some time alone with such an incredibly ancient monument. A wonder of ancient engineering and a great place to consider your place in this world!

Title: Very Large Reclining Buddha

Title: Amazing
Text: Jethawanaramaya Stupa is one of highest and biggest Stupa in Sri Lankan. Its an unbelievable creation. Jethawanaramaya is one of must visit place in the Anuradhapura tour.

Title: One of the tallest structures in the ancient world
Text:
King Mahasena initiated the construction of the stupa following the destruction of the mahavihara. His son Maghavanna I completed the construction of the stupa. It is significant in recorded history as one of the tallest structures in the ancient world and the second tallest non-pyramidal buildings after Pharos (lighthouse) of Alexandria; the height of the stupa is 400 feet (122 m),making it the tallest stupa in the ancient world.

Text: This stupa was not as popular as Ruwanwelisaya however it was interesting to see how stupas are built as this one is exposed brick not covered in white like the rest of the big stupas in this town.

Title: One of the great stupas
Text: One of the great massive stupas around Anuradhapura, although with little to see up close. It also has a small museum nearby.

Title: An Expensive Visit
Text:
To enter the complex which includes 4 religious sites and the small museum was USD20 per person and an additional USD20 for a guide. The first site is this Stupa that dates from 300BC or thereabouts. But actually it is almost 100% reconstructed. Yes it is big and made of fired bricks but it is not very exciting. As expected it was shoes off at the steps and a quick look at the statues inside.

Then it was time to visit the second Stup complex and the oldest tree in the world.

Title: Awe inspiring
Text: This dagoba was the first stop on our 4 hour tuk tuk tour of the sites and very impressive. The sheer scale is breathtaking.

Title: Last stupa I saw and wouldn't recommend paying 3750 rupees ($25)
Text:
I was taken on a great tour of all the free sites and the Isuruminiya (200 rupees)  before visiting three main stupas for which you had to pay 3750 rupees ($25). By the time I had finished the free sites, it was approaching noon, and I don't think it was worth paying $25 to see the last three, the moon stone , and tank. But that's only my opinion.

Jetvana was empty at 1pm. It was very impressive in its size and I liked the exposed bricks as opposed to the white stucco surfaces on most of the stupas I visited.

Definitely wear socks as the pavement and sand is very hot.

Title: Large Brick Stupa
Text: Very impressive stupa rising above the flat plain. Just viewed from a outside to photograph  since having to be respectful and remove shoes the surrounds looked far too gravelly. One of many stupas to visit in the huge Anuradhapura area.

Title: Under Reconstruction
Text:
This stupa isn't white, we see only pricks, because when it wast discovered in the old town of Anarudhapura had been hidden in the jungle and fully grown over with bushes. Now they are refurbishing it - maybe work takes another five to ten years.
For us, when visiting it was very impressive, because we could see how stupas were built and of which material they really are made thousand of years ago...

Title: Nice Place
Text: Again it has to be among the biggest Stupas in the Anuradhapura area. Looks very old and is a nice place to sit around.

Title: Part of Anuradhapura ancient city
Text: This is a must see amongst all the attractions inside the ancient city. Admire the building work and the longevity of the stupa. Many people come here to pay their respects so be sure to dress appropriately. If you are lucky you will see groups of people walking around with yellow clothes they donated to the temple and supplies to the monks.

Title: took a drive around
Text:
our tour guide said, there was no need to go around the place, so instead he just drove us closest possible to the area
since we had seen quite a bit of stupa, they all looked the same

Title: Big site
Text: This is a big site containing big stupas with a big entrance fee of £25, I also was expected to 'tip' the official guide another £5, thus I think a total entrance fee of £30 is extortionate. The guide walked me to the first building complex, then drove to the next, where we wandered through the trees viewing the ruins as he explained their significance. We then drove to visit a few of the large Stupas situated around the site. As it was a Buddhist holiday, here were large crowds thus only took photos from the outside of the buildings. I spent about 2 hours here and sure you could spent much longer but it was too hot and humid for me to stay any longer. Worth visitinf despite the entrance fee.

Title: very old stupa

Title: calm and peaceful

calm and peaceful ancient complex.
try going on a evening, when the sun is almost down. you will love the calm and peaceful surrounding. very relaxing.

Title: Beautiful complex

Title: Good watch

Text: It was just Ok. Walked around the stupa. Nice wall to sit on surrounding the grounds. Did not really enjoy this stop.

Title: Huge pile of bricks.
Text:
This is clearly one of the great brick built structures of the world and the effort that went into moulding, baking and laying the countless millions boggles the mind.
Restoration has not achieved the perfect curves that once must have impressed all who saw it but this is still an amazing sight.

Title: Sacred and Amazing
Text: When you visit this place, it requires pure respect. The place is visited by the locals and I can see how much they take care of this place. For foreigners like me, it is an amazing place to see. Not to miss.

Title: If you took all the bricks from here you could build a 6ft high wall from London to Scotland
Text:
From my Blog:

In no time, we were approaching the Jethawanaramaya Stupa, an impressive structure in its own right. Though the lack of fresh clean white paint made the structure less impressive from a distance, as I began to walk around it, and fully take in its enormity I was finding it hard to believe that this was man made. Ive seen the pyrimids in Giza, and the temples in Cambodia, and though both are jaw dropping in their own ways, this structure held its own with the aforementioned best of them.

Apparently if you took all the bricks that made up Jethawanaramaya and stacked them 6 feet high, you could build a wall from London to Scotland (or so my driver had led me to believe). With that being said my driver said the same thing at Abhayagiri Dagoba,

Title: Historic and Sacred
Text: Before you get too "stupa'd out" be sure to visit this historic stupa. It's remarkably preserved with beautiful statues and monuments inside.  You are certain to encounter a number of Buddhists praying and meditating in the area, and if lucky you'll be there when local music is playing.

Title: Buddhist
Text: This is a old Buddhist temple here to visit.The temple is big . The Buddha statue is beautiful. You need about an hour here.

Title: Important history
Text: A guide is a must. No shoes or hats. Cover knees and shoulders. Go in the morning to avoid the extreme heat. Plenty of facts and information at such a small site.

Title: Well worth a visit!
Text: If you visit, youll see a spectacular Stupa. We were lucky to visit at a time around one of the largest Buddhist festivals (Perahera) so the place was teaming with Buddhists dressed in white, chanting, praying and carrying an array of beautiful flowers (as offerings to Buddha). It was a very peaceful and calming experience.

Title: Great view at night, Peaceful & refreshing atmosphere
Text: The stupa is well-decorated. It is a large, stunning, sacred place. You simply can't miss it. One of the best places in Anuradhapura sites.

Title: Don't miss the Bouddha and the evening view
Text:
Jethawana Stupa is the largest stupa in the Sri Lanka. Built around yr 300 was originally 400 feet (122 meters) in height and was the third tallest building in the world at that time. Of course it suffered during wars and invasions but was rebuilt. We were said that today as a brick monument, Jethawanaramaya still remains the tallest of its kind in the world.

What is worth is visiting the room with coulourful Bouddha sculpture. The building itself impressive but it looks very nice in the evening when lights make it look like a fire amongst trees.

Title: Magnificent
Text:
Unbelievable place and for me the absolute highlight of wonderful Anuradhapura.
This wonderful stupa dates from the 3rd century and what's most striking is that it is totally unplastered and is made up of 90 million red bricks! You can see the massive domed structure towering above you as you approach through the leafy grounds. 
It stands 70m high but was once 50m higher than that making it the third largest building in the world, behind only two of the Giza Pyramids in Egypt.
You'll have to take off your shoes and have knees and shoulders covered but socks are okay and necessary as the paving slabs can be red hot.
There is a nice temple at one end with ornate paintwork and a reclining Buddha statue.
An absolute must see.

Title: We loved this place
Text: We did this at the end of our tour and loved it . Very serene and bright image of the sleeping Buddha

Title: Historic preservation.
Text:
This stupa is spectacular in size and construction. It is amazing to think about first making all those bricks and then building this structure. Walking around this stupa I felt connected to the past. 
Dont forget to bring socks as the brick underfoot can get very warm. 
As you make your way through the Anuradhapura dont miss this stop.

Title: Tour
Text: Went here during our tour and was impressed by the structure and likeness to others I have visited but no where near as large as the ones in Rangoon or Kathmandu.

Title: Huge Stupa and Archaeological site
Text:
It's so impressive to see such a huge Stupa at this site.
The Archaeological site excavations are quite extensive and well maintained.
The museum hare has extensive collection from the earliest times.

Title: Very impressive
Text: A very impressive feat of building work, not in the artificially pristine state of repair of some of the similar monuments.

Title: Heritage monument well maintained
Text: Worth visiting the place.There are no entry charges.The structure is  very well maintained.A historical monument.

Title: Even greater !
Text: I found this stupa even more attractive than Ruwanweliseya, with its "primal" look and dimensions, knowing that only pyramides can match with her.

Title: Calm place at sunset

Title: Huge dagoba - energy for focus
Text: The place is not fully renovated yet.  This is the largest stupa in Sri Lanka.  The place is not attracting pilgrims like Ruvanweli Stupa.  Therefore, a quieter place.  It has an ambience that allows you to attain mental focus quickly.  (this could depend on the individual).  Sit without any pre-conceived notion and start meditating there (if you're a person doing meditation). Experience it for yourself.

Title: Wow!
Text:
You can't put this place in to words...
Spiritual and enchanting. This had our hearts!
Very hot though. No shoes or hats and must cover up...

Title: Sri Lanka take 3

Title: Massive Dome.
Text: When I visited this place there were no crowds at all and looks abandoned in it's past glory.It was built in 3rd century by Mahasena, the Dagoba was considered as third tallest monument in the world( first two are Pyramids from Egypt). Beware of monkeys that were waiting to snatch any bags of eatables from careless visitors. Behind the Dagoba there are ruins of Monastery that once housed thousands of Buddhist Monks.

Title: Impressive
Text: This is one of the core sites across a collection of ancient Buddhist sites in Anuradhapura. We visited during school holidays and near a full moon so it was especially busy, which made the experience that much more interesting. Not many foreigners, but people were very friendly. The entire complex is worth a visit and unlike anywhere else I've been. Exploring the whole area on rented bicycles is a good way of getting around, but it would be easy to explore by foot and tuktuk too.

Jethawanaramaya is one of the other biggeststupa in anuradhapura. There are more as this stupa. But actually every of them is interesting and when you went there you hardly leave from there. It feels strange and spirutual. You can visit evey month of the year. We have visited on august because of Pera- Hera festival.

Title: Quite impressive
Text: The stupa is very tall.  When it was created, it was the tallest structure after the great pyramids of Giza.  While you're not able to enter the stupa, you can walk around it.   Worth visiting to experience its size.

Title: Awe inspiring
Text: Go with a guide to get the full history if this ancient place, once the third highest building  in the world ( after the Pyramids).

Title: A must see
Text: Anuradhapura has some amazing stupas and this is one of the best. Huge and lovely as it has not been replatered. Very peaceful with monkeys running up and down the sidws

Title: The big one
Text:
It is the big pagoda in Anuradhapura 
They conserve this pagoda without painted as the pagoda is normally painted and gold-plated.

Title: Impressive
Text:
Huge Dagoba (or stupa) which is free in the middle of an archeological site. 
We arrived with bycicles and wandered a bit in the "garden".
I do recommend to start with this one, we did it in the end and were a bit tired to appreciate it fully.

Title: Just incredible and awe inspiring
Text: This was my favourite of all the dagoba's we visited in Anuradhapura, just huge, incredible and awe inspiring and still one of the largest/tallest brick built structures from the ancient world.

Title: How did they do it?
Text: This is the most incredible structure. One can only gaze in awe and wonder how on earth did they manage to construct it. Also a peaceful place (I guess we were there in the off season) to wander around without getting hassled by anyone.

Title: Monkeys climbing of the Stupa
Text: Traveling in Sri Lanka you can get a bit "Stupa'd out". What added to the magic was the black faced monkeys (so much friendlier and cuter then the white faced ones), climbing and running around the Stupa. It is dry season so was very hot. Take a lot of water with you.

Title: amazing ancient site
Text:
This was the first site in Anuradhapura that we were taken to by our driver/guide and we were very impressed. To think that this 'building' pre-dates Christianity puts it, to my mind, alongside the pyramids in Egypt. OK there is not a great deal to do here except wander round but it is truly amazing. Additionally we were treated to the company of several coachloads of Sri Lankan children visiting at the same time as us. They were delightful and seemed to be fascinated by our fair skins and hair ( our driver suspected that they had come from remote village schools and not familiar with Westerners) and wanted to be photographed with us. This was a worthwhile visit for us.
I would also like to put an alternative viewpoint to those posters who complain about the cost of entry to Anuradapura. The cost at around 3500 rupees is under UK£20, less than you would pay for a decent evening meal and this is for the whole city site which I doubt could be visited in full in one whole day. It is an historic site of world importance which housed an amazingly sophisticated civilisation pre-dating the birth of Christ. That it is not better known is surprising. As for the fact that locals pay a lesser entry fee (and this applies to sites throughout Sri Lanka and in some shops and restaurants too), I grant that this is an unusual arrangement but I personally do not begrudge them. We Westerners have probably spent more on our trip than the average Sri Lankan earns in a year. Third World country residents need all the help they can in improving their lot

Title: Impressive!
Text: A not so well known fact is that Jethawanaramaya was the 3rd tallest structure in the world (after the great pyramids of Giza) up until 800 or so years ago, and while not the tallest stupa in the world anymore it still is the largest in volume, and supposedly 90 million baked bricks went into making it. And when you're there, it shows; the base of the stupa is VAST, and even without two thirds of the top of the structure it still casts and imposing figure. It truly is a marvelous feat of human engineering!

Title: Nice and huge old stupa
Text: All old Anuradhapura are in ruins. If you are Budhist, go and see them, if you are an archeologist, go and see them, if you are a simple turist, go to Polonnaruwa or better to Sigiriya or Dambulla. Too much ruins, but the old main stupa is beautifull, maybe not for 25 dollars. The new stupa is olso nice. Finally 2 stupas against lot of ruins - average.

Title: Stunning and Overwhelming
Text:
This is the most impressive place in Anuradhapura - I would place it on top with Mihintale in "places to see in Anuradhapura".
The stupa is the largest in the world, and overwhelms you with its size and symmetry. If you want to walk around the stupa, please choose early morning, or wear socks. The stone floor gets quite hot for bare feet.

Title: Largest Stupa
Text: so far this is the largest Stupa I have seen..its visible from quiet a distance from Anurathapura.. the Stupa shows how big the capital must have been and how rich was the state during Jethawanaramaya's time.. we loved it also because it was the first Stupa so large we saw for the first time and from where we started our tour to this rich old city of Anuradhapura which is also famous for their Moon Stone and Guard Stone..

Title: historic/religious
Text: This Stupa in Anuradhapura area is huge. You need to remove shoes to enter the temple, but the artwork inside is fantastic.  Fees were paid at the museum by our travel guide. You need your pass to travel around Anuradhapura. Be warned it is a vast area and the museum is the only place where you get the pass, so visit museum first.

Title: Another awesome stupa
Text: This is also a great stupa with ancient carvings scattered around the premises. Keep in mind you need to remove shoes so the best times to visit are early morning or late evening.

Title: Not worth the entrance money
Text: Since we were staying three days near Dambulla we decided to visit Anuradhapura since it was a World Heritage Site. Frankly, compared to Polonowarra, there is not that much interesting to see here to justify such high entrance price. The large stuba and renovated baths are interesting but after that you have to travel large distances to see things that in my ignorance were not that interesting. On the other hand you do not need to pay the entrance fee if you just want to visit the lovely Buddist temple and the tree of knowledge

Title: Visit it since you are already in Anuradhapura
Text: 3250 bucks for visiting places in Anuradhapura. 1625 for Asians. Too pricey for the so called attractions. This is just a place of working for Sri Lankans. There are so many Dagobas and Stupas in Sri Lanka that this doesn't feel special in any way. Just a place to visit since you're already here and paid for your hotel.

Title: Pricey dagoba
Text:
Most of the Sri Lankan sites that we've visited are expensive.  The locals get a much lower rate and foreigners pay whatever they can get away with.  This dagoba is no different...

I liked this dagoba more than the others because not a lot of people are here to worship.  I feel like intruding on others pilgrimage when when they are all around you, praying. At JS, I was able to linger, take pictures, and look at the site instead of people.  

If this site wasn't so expensive, I'd rate it excellent.

Title: Miss
Text:
The area is nice, no doubt about it. But entrance fee is insane. 3250 rupees each, and after seeing three sights they started to feel the same. That price does not include a map or any information about the area so we had no idea what we were looking at until we went home and googled it. Hired a tuk tuk driver to take us around, he was friendly and helpful but it added another 1500 rupees to our bill by the end of the day.

Also, my wife was hassled at the entrance of two stupas because the back of her neck was showing in her modest dress, this infuriated her because local women were obviously showing far more skin and left alone. We are seasoned travelers that understand the dress code in religious places, but being blonde seemed to be innapropriate here. My wife was almost reduced to tears.

Overall, this expensive and uncomfortable day was not enjoyable for us. Maybe history buffs would get more out of it then we did.

Title: Not much to see.
Text:
We were there and had visited the sacred city with Jethawanaramaya Stupa and the museum and the Abhayagiri Stupa with museum.The museums were not really impressing,
because there is not much explained on the antiques and they were really small museums.But i can recommend the `gold fish park`where you can have a really nice walk and it`s free of any entrance fee.Next to the park is the big reservoir called `Tissa Wewa`.

Title: Ancient Dagoba
Text: An amazing level of architectural brilliance. 120 metres high made from bricks and hundreds of years old. In the process of being restored. Important Buddhist monument.

Title: World's largest brick structure - Jetavanarama Dagoba
Text:
This Dagoba was built in 3rd century by king Mahasena, It was the third largest structure in the world that time (first and second being Egyptian pyramids). In addition that was the first ever largest brick structure built by man. It has been estimated over 90 million bricks were used for the project; enough bricks to build 3m high wall from London to Edinburgh. The original height estimated at 120 present day it is only 70m tall.
You will not wast your time visiting this place as this is only a single place in an ancient city.

Title: Majestic
Text: Awesome and worth the trek!  But be-warned, wear simple footwear as you will need to remove both shoes and hats when going near the stupas or any sacred sites, of which there are many.

Title: A DIFFERENT BRICK STUPA (DAGOBA)
Text:
The stupa is located in the Southern part of the Anuradhapura site.
It is original because it is not a traditional white stupa, it is a brick one. When it was built (3rd century) it was the third tallest structure in the world after the pyramids in Egypt!

Title: Largest Stupa in Anuradhapura
Text:
Jethawanaramaya is the largest stupa in the area and probably the largest in Sri Lanka itself. Our guide mentioned that this is the largest brick structure in the world. 
Irrespective of the superlatives, this is a magnificent structure. The size does impress you. 
There is a very long history around this Stupa. The Stupa was built by King Mahasena ( 3rd Century AD) and was renovated and developed by successive kings. At the time of King Parakaramabahu the Great ( 10th Century) the Stupa was around 120mtrs high.Currently the Stupa stands at 73 mtrs till the broken Spire.

We visited in the morning time and there were hardly any one at the stupa. There wasn't any one to check the tickets too.

Title: Huge and Impressive
Text: I preferred this to the Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba as it is far less crowded and appears a little forgotten compared to its rival, but the greater proximity to the trees and the additional troops of monkeys drives a feeling of awe and exoticism to the stupa.   This is amplified further by the sheer size and worn exterior, and with there being fewer visitors to distract you its somewhere you can take it all in and enjoy in your own time.

Title: Huge and testimony to building skills
Text:
This stupa is more than 120 metres high and quite incredible to look at even from a distance given that it contains so many bricks.

It shows a level of technological sophistication existed hundreds of years ago.  

I observed many monkeys in and around this stupa.

Title: Interesting Historic Site
Text: Very Good.  The Stupa is one of the oldest in Sri-lanka and a place of importance to Buddhists. The building is old and very tall for the date it was built.

Title: Enjoyable, but same for me as most of the Sub-Continent
Text: I do not suggest a driver.  I prefer solo.  Try not to engage the locals  The tuk-tuk driver tried to get me to pay 2000 rupees for the day.  I enjoyed the pictures and the hike and the history.  As I learned in Nepal and Kenya, always barter and start REAL small.

Title: One of the ancient monuments you should not missed with Buddha's relic consecrated
Text: The ancient wisdom of building dome shape from the unknown bare hands method always a big wow to witness! One of largest stupa with widest base structures, believed to host as large as 10,000 monks during that time.

Title: One of the tallest structures of the ancient world
Text:
Definitely worth to be seen. Stupas are where the ashes of Buddhist monks are kept. You can walk around it but barefoot only. Many monkeys can be seen on the stupa as well. 

The stupa is 122m. high so it's quite impressive.

Title: Great experience
Text: Again whole Anuradhapura Sri Lanka trip gave us very pleasant feeling , nice place to explore and also to spend days in a great historical site.

Title: Unique
Text: All I know is that I keep wondering what happened to the top of the stupa itself as out of the three giant stupas in Anuradhapura it is the only one missing a chunk.  Also out of the three stupas this one seemed to be the most tranquil and the least visited (very few people there when I visited).  I say go and take a walk around.  There were also a lot of monkeys at this compound and they made for great entertainment.

Title: Unique and inspiring
Text: This is one of the greatest attractions of the ancient sacred city of Anuradhapura and is a 'must' to see. One of the many wonderful things about the Anuradhapura experience is the immense variety of structures to be seen and this huge building of Jethawanaramaya is very different from others because of its construction from brick. It is quite amazing how the brickwork was done. If one purchases a ticket for the main attractions of Anuradhapura, this stupa is included in the price. As with all of the sacred places, shoes must be removed before entering and appropriate clothing worn.

Title: The third highest building in the ancient world, after pyramids in Giza.
Text:
One of the very important monument of the Sri Lankan early kingdoms and buddhism history! Don't miss it!
Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes.
I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

Title: An integral part of the Anuradhapura experience
Text: A wonderful structure which must be visited whilst in Anuradhapura. It is quite different to the other stupas in the area and the brickwork is impressive. It is included in the main ticket.

Title: Vast and awe-inspiring
Text: Amazing that this massive, apparently younger structure is so old - and the brickwork is really impressive.

Title: Too high entrance fee
Text: This is just like any other buddhist stupa only probably huger than the rest. The entrance fee is too high LKR 3250 per person. SAARC nations get it at half that price, but it is still expensive. When you buy the ticket, you get entrace to about 7-8 religious places, but all are alike. There are either brick stupas or white ones. The same kind of ponds with garbage strewn in the sides. The guardian stone and the moonstone also aren't anything great. You need to remove your footwear to visit these temples. I don't have a problem with that. It is religious. The only problem was the stone heats up too quickly and it was like walking on burning coal. Something needs to be done for this. By the end of the tour, we were less interested in seeing the monuments and more interested in finding shade for our feet. The museum has random pieces of pottery, jewellery and statues. Some are from India and other countries. All in all, I did not find it worth the price of the entrance ticket. And if you are from India, it is not too different from the local ruins we find in Hampi, Halebeedu etc.

Title: Don't Forget the Museum
Text: Another impressive dagaba, this time with the bricks exposed. It is located away from the main pilgrim site. Even so it attracts the masses at religious festivals. The small museum displays the finds made from around this structure

Title: A wonderful Dagoba
Text: A perfect dagoba , build long time ago ...perfect design and esthetic result is top ....move around don't forget to go according a clockwise way .

Title: Huuuuuge
Text: They say that you can build a three metres high wall from London to Edinburgh with the bricks that were used to build this Dagoba. Pretty impressive. And could you please use some of the massive entree fees(US$ 25)  to Anuradhapura historical site to clean up all the litter. Would show as much respect for these holu sites as taking of your shoes.

Title: Really Impressive!
Text: A really impressive piece of historic architecture. Absolutely put this on your list of places to visit whilst exploring the ruins and historic sites of Anuradhapura.

Title: Good
Text: Like most of the Dagobas it is large with a small shrine. Very much a recommend to those Buddhists. As a simple tourist I enjoyed it but wasn't spectacular.

Title: After visiting Myanmar this is really poor
Text: This Stupa might be nice in case you haven't visited Myanmar - but after visiting Myanmar with all the great Stupas - this one is below average.

Title: Towering and impressive dagoba (ancient domed temple)
Text:
Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura is a long distance to travel from the main coastal resorts and so you should probably only consider if you are touring the island.  It was about a two hour drive from Sigiriya.  The area is too big to cover on foot in a single day and, whilst bicycles and TukTuks are easy and cheap to hire, I would recommend a driver/guide who can direct you to and provide commentary on the most significant sites.  

The four main stupas (Jethawanaramaya/Jethavanarama, Rutwanwelisaya, Thuparama and Abhayaagiri) are all different.  You wont need more than 10-15 minutes at each unless you want to stay to worship, We dont think there is any entrance charge  we werent asked for any money and there were no ticket checks. As for all temples, you must dress respectfully (legs and shoulders covered). You need to remove hats and shoes but you can wear socks which I would recommend as the stones underfoot can be hot and sharp.  

Of the four main stupas, we liked Jethawanaramaya/Jethavanarama the best.  At 400ft high with a 370ft diameter base on a 670ft square rock base, this is the largest stupa in Anuradpura  and one of the tallest brick structures in the world.  It was built in the 3rd century. The dome is unpainted. It was very quiet and tranquil. Once part of a huge monastery and you can see the ruins all around.  It is worth visiting the museum where you can see a good collection of guardstones and ancient jewellery.  There is a clean toilet here too.  

Rutwanwelisaya has a massive white painted dome. It is 180ft (used to be twice that).  It is surrounded by wall with over 300 elephant sculptures but almost all these are restored or replacements.  It can get busy with devotees coming to pray.  

Thuparama is the smallest and oldest of the main stupas in Anuradhapura (what you see is mainly reconstructed).  Its significance is that it is said to enshrine the collarbone of the Buddha and as such there are lots of pilgrims actively worshipping. A white dome surrounded by stone pillars which used to support a wooden cover.  

See separate review of Abhayaagiri.

Title: Impressive opener
Text:
First we would like to say what we think the Anuradhapura Sacred precinct is and what it isn't. It is not Angkor Wat. We met lots of people that were slightly disappointed because they were expecting Angkor Wat scaled temples.
It is however very impressive in its own way, especially if you use your imagination to envision what was once there and that thousands of monks once roamed around here. 
Apart from the Stupa, only the foundations of the monasteries are left because the buildings were wooden structures and rotted away centuries ago. But the sheer size of the this complex and the other complexes makes it worth coming here. Details such as beautifully carved gnome like creatures, animals and Cobra Kings provide delicate finishing touches of the monuments.

Title: Our favourite on our "ruined" day
Text: This was our first and best of the day. It is massive structure which dwarfs you the closer you get. The kids enjoyed walking around

Title: Become a dwarf in the shadow of this Stupa
Text:
Jethawana Stupa is huge. Its huge from along way away and its even bigger as you get closer. You can see it from Minihtale and everywhere in Anuradhapura! Its 80 m high and 220 m wide. You cant miss it and you will be drawn to it. Its so impressive, its a statement about the power of the religion which built it. 
I prefer to view it in the morning.

Title: Arrive late afternoon
Text: We arrived at late afternoon, a timing when it was uncrowded and definitely cooler. Dusk spectacular.

Title: An amazing brick structure
Text: As one of the tallest brick structures in the world this stupa is truly awe inspiring. We went here in the evening and it was far less busy than the other main temples in the city. Well worth a visit for all those who like history and to admire the marvels of the past.

Title: This entire area is worth the visit
Text: All of the ancient ruins in this area are very interesting. The museum that starts the touring area is very informative. Lots of barefoot walking involved and much on hot ground.

Title: Another marvellous example of human endeavour
Text: Whilst some seem to be unimpressed it is amazing to think of the effort that went into constructing this building which is large but nevertheless very beautiful. I agree that sensible folk might enjoy their tour of the Sacred City more in the early part of the day to avoid the heat and crowds. Allows time just to enjoy being there without hiding from the sun or having the ales of your feet burnt. This is one stop that all who visit Anuradhapura will want to make

Title: same as Jethawanaramaya Stupa
Text:
This is the same thing, yeah? twice in TripAdvisor  = once as stupa and once as dagoba. 
Oh well. It was cool to see it, very large, impressive and fascinating ruins around it.

Title: Largest?
Text: There seems to be some confusion about whether this is indeed the largest, it was impressive nevertheless and wandering about the ruins (including a nice large image house) was fun.

Title: Simple Beautiful, need to be taken care of.
Text: When we get there you feel big, and proud about what the Sri Lankan kings did for Buddhism. This place need government attention, and need to be looked after well.

Title: Amazing structure
Text: For me I find it hard to comprehend the age of the stupa, quite amazing. Best seen early in the morning no heat, no people, just a few monkeys and a lot of bird life. I think it would be difficult to walk around the stupa in the middle of the day, as you have to remove your shoes and it would be hot on your feet.

Title: Largest Stupa
Text: OK so it's the largest Stupak, with many millions of bricks, but apart from walking around the outside, that's it.

Title: Good Stupa
Text: This building is very good and deserves its status. However my lasting memory of the Sacred city will be the filth and rubbish, not to mention the scabby starving dogs. If the city is so sacred why do the locals treat it so badly?

Title: Absolutely astounding
Text: The whole Anuradhapura area is a sight. We got bikes and went around to look at everything, all the Stupas and it was gorgeous. We did't even get that 25 USD ticket, you can get so close to the Stupas and even walk through the ruins, it was enough for us. It feels a little like tomb raiding, a mystical place with lots of monkeys running around. We even got to see a varan near the Jethawana Stupa.

Title: Nice deserted stupa
Text: Other stupas were filled with people but this stupa was a bit off the beaten track and not as well restored so had only a few people but with wildlife just roaming around. Monkeys climbing over the stupa and the rich red brick of the stupa made for some nice shots.

Title: Well preserved site
Text: It was a nice visit to see the old Stupa with devotees around it. Peaceful place to go around. Close to a small informative museum

Title: Impressive
Text:
The ruins are very impressive and compare favorably with other Southeast Asia destinations.
 A day well spent

Title: Large and important to Buddhists
Text: Having said that its not that impressive if youve seen this kind of thing in Myanmar and Thailand. If you havent its worth a look.

Title: An Atamasthana Attraction.One of the Eight sacred locations in Anuradhapura.
Text:
Also known as Uththararamaya it is the 4th largest manmade
structure and the 2nd largest Dhagoba in the world.

Title: The tallest of the Buddhist stupa
Text: Apart of being a sacred edifice, Jethawanaramaya by far is the giant of all the stupas. Of the man-made structures in the world it has been recorded that this edifice was only the third to pyramids and the tallest of all the stupas in the world rising to almost over 120 meters. With the gradual weathering over the years and collapse, apparently the height has reduced and what remains today is the outcome of the last restoration by another great Sri lankan king - Parakramabahu in 12th century. The Stupa is conserved beautifully and reflects the engineering skills of the ancient Sri lankan people.

Title: Not so popular but interesting
Text: This stupa is close to the archeological museum which in closed for reconstruction. Therefore there was nobody there when we visited the stupa. Really an experience, especially with a big her of monkeys climbing the stupa

Title: 3rd biggest stupa in the world
Text: You feel very humble when you standing close it , glad to see it getting well maintained and the playful monkeys around it

Title: Largest Stupa in the World
Text: This was our first stop visiting the Anuradhapura ancient site which is the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Entrance fee for the entire site is LKR4,550 or USD25 per person per entry. It is the significant structure as biggest and tallest building in the ancient world of Anuradhapura Kingdom in 3rd-4th century. Best way to visit the site is by hiring a driver since the site is huge and scattered and not within walking distance. We engaged our driver service with BLUE HAVEN TOURS with fantastic and dedicated driver. Dress appropriately with cover shoulder and pants/ dress below knee. If possible, wear socks as walking on the sandstone under the daylight can be burning for the feet. Drinking water is essential too. Nice start to explore the Anuradhapura Ancient site. Unfortunately, the museum was closed for renovations during our visit, otherwise it would be informative prior to visiting to the sites.

Title: Review of the entire Anuradhapura experience-self guided
Text: We are traveling by rented tuktuk and had read that we could drive ourselves to the different sites after purchasing our ticket. We did not hire a guide, as we had read extensively and had a map. However, the map provided by the ticket counter wasnt entirely accurate and so it was a little tricky to figure out where exactly things were, as they are quite spread out. Allow yourself a full day, perhaps find a good guide, dress appropriately for temple visits (we did not know that white dress is recommended for viewing the ancient Bodhisattva Tree, but luckily covered my black shirt with a sarong Id brought), and bring water! There are some good food stalls next to the Moonstone site that sell cold coconuts for water, and make excellent veggie and coconut roti-highly recommend this too. An excellent day spent.

Title: This place was amazing!
Text: The sheer scale of it cannot be captured in a photo. If you are travelling here, I highly recommend hiring a guide to explain the significance of it, as the information they provide gives the experience a new level of depth allowing you to appreciate the site even more.

Title: Magnificent Stupa
Text: Very fine stupa.  Nice ambiance around it.  Visited late afternoon which was a good time for the light for photos

Title: Rustic Stupa with Strong Spiritual Vibe
Text: This stupa left the strongest impression. Hidden by forest overgrowth and abandoned for centuries, the plants enveloping it have been cut away and what you see is what was left. Rustic in appearance and only slightly restored, this stupa also has a small shrine to the Buddha, with a large reclining Buddha statue with offerings laid before it. It has a curious authenticity, and you can best view what these stupas are made of: Millions of handmade bricks. This was once the largest brick structure in the world.

Title: MONUMENTAL SCALE
Text: At 122m, this is the tallest stupa ever built. Some 93 million baked bricks were used in the construction. Its foundation is 8.5m deep, sitting on bedrock. Like many sites here, it was rebuilt. It was built as an act of attrition.

Title: Superb
Text: The stupas at Anuradhapura are mind-blowing! Jethawanaramaya Stupa is massive, and you keep wondering how they built these huge structures during those times!

Title: Incredible stupa.
Text: We visited this area and saw this magnificent stupa when touring Sri Lanka. It was a recommended visit by our guide who took us to some amazing areas. We took some great photos as the area wasnt too busy as it was the low season. I imagine it could get very busy and hot during the peak season. There were some people selling items but they were not a nuisance.

Title: Another great Buddhist pilgrimage site
Text: This stupa is believed to contain a sacred bowl which lord Buddha is believed to have ate from. The bowl is believed to be buried almost 200 feet deep.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
This is worth seeing on your trip around the sacred lands.  This is enormous.

I was told that there are an estimated 93 million bricks used for this relic, as it is solid inside.  The shear quantity is impossible to fathom and still makes me think now.

The grounds themselves are very large and every angle keeps showing you the scale of this.

Title: First of our visits in Anuradhapura
Text: This is the tallest and largest of the stupas in Anuradhapura. Originally it was 400fy high. It is a world heritage monument. It has a long history with the first Sinhala Buddhist king who built the stupa. He dedicated to a monk named Tissa who lived in a local temple. Jetavana is the stupa of this monastery. It will s huge to walk around and admire the architecture and engineering even if one is not a Buddhist. Enshrined in the stupa are relics that some believe belong to lord Buddha himself.

Title: How did they build this?
Text: Largest stupa in the world. Lost of monkeys running on top of stupa, an amazing sight. Incredible feat of engineering for it to be built during it time with no heavy machinery or technology.

Title: Fascinating visit.
Text: This is very different from other stupas as it is made of brick and a visit is worth it and the nearby museum as many wonderful artefacts including jewellery and carvings.

Title: Different Than The Rest
Text: This was build almost 2,000 years ago and was one of the tallest buildings in the world at that time.  Most of the stupas in the area are white, so this one stands out.  Nice place to take a photo, but don't fly a drone here.  They are very strict about this and could even arrest you.

Title: Great temple and plenty of birdlife
Text:
This was our first stop using our Anuradhapura cultural ticket and we really enjoyed exploring Jetavanaramaya Dagoba. Walking through the grounds before we reached the dagoba we came across a number of different birds including egrets, grey hornbills, flycatchers and bee-eaters, which was lovely.

The dagoba itself is huge - it's lost some height so must have been really impressive back in its day. Walking around the base is a must but be minded to wear socks - the floor is hot and a bit gritty and my husband even managed to stand on broken glass, so barefoot is not ideal. There's a brightly painted reclining buddha here too.

Take time to explore the grounds as they are a pleasant place to get lost. We didn't spend long at all in the museum - just walked around the 3 different rooms rather quickly.

Lots of decent bike parking if you are cycling the temples.

Title: Interesting
Text: Interesting place in good condition, beautiful paintings showing the story of Buddha and the kingdoms

Title: An attraction for devote Buddhists
Text: It has almost the same Buddhist statues you find in most Buddhist places. Interesting only if your a devoted Buddhist, if not I would recommend you skip this place.

Title: Disappointing after Dambulla
Text: Having been to Dambulla caves this stupa just seemed too bright and over renovated.  Admittedly we didn't have a guide but generally the temple site is pretty and worth a visit as part of the Anuradhapura experience.

Title: One more ancient stupa
Text: Good to visit if you are devout Buddhist. Not being a Buddhist nor of religious bent of mind and the stupa not being of particular architectural interest, I could easily have given it a miss.

Title: Vacation
Text: A Reclining Buddha inside part of the Stupa's structures. Brighty painted and walls also. People come inside to prey. Dress accordingly.

Title: Big stupa with large reclining buddha
Text:
Along with the Abhayagiri Dagaba  this is one of the main attractions of the Anuradhapura heritage site and, to be fair its an impressive structure - a huge domed structure built from over 90 million bricks. There is also a chamber housing a large reclining buddha.
Other than the scale of the structure thetes Not a lot to it and I have to say we found th3 whole archaeological site to be somewhat disappointing - over rated and hugely overpriced.

Title: The reclining Buddha photo Tripadvisor headlines isn't here, its at Isurumuniya
Text: This is an ancient temple, the one that is reputed to be the largest brick built structure in the world using over 90 million individual bricks. Very impressive, they compare this to the pyramids of Giza as an ancient structure, and having been there a few times I can understand why considering the work that would have taken place is comparable to Egypt. In fact If all the stupas in Anuradhapura were together on an open plain like those in Giza these might be as famous, but dotted around the old city with lots of the famous green vegitation and trees of Sri Lanka it renders the comparison impossible. As with most of Anuradhapura signage was practically non existent with very little in the way of historical description at each monument.

Title: Nice reclining Buddha
Text: Located at the stuppa this is a nice reclining Buddha. The whole entrance is surrounded by Hindu scenes from the Ramayana which of course ties it to Sri Lanka.

Title: Tallest stupa in Sri Lanka
Text: There are several very famous stupas, and this is the tallest. It is visited by families, children and visitors offering flowers and lighting incense. A very popular place and a recommended visit.

Title: BIG STUPA
Text: Its HUGE. As far as I could tell, it is the main sight of this section of ancient ruins in Anuradhapura. As always, there is an area where everyone leaves their shoes.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: A calm and peaceful place, well worth the visit. As always it's barefoot so avoid the midday sun. Early in the day would be best.

Title: Very Impressive
Text:
Incredible piece of engineering and a very impressive sight. Well worth a look at this Stupa as well as the other ones dotted around Anuradhapura.

We were driven around by Ranil from artlankatours.com  Ranil gave us a whistle-stop tour of the main attractions in the city and was very knowledgeable about all of them, highly recommend him.

Title: Another Dagoba  / Stupa
Text: This was our third dagoba / stupa of the day and if we are honest, they were beginning to get repetitive. However, having paid an eye watering 3,500 Sri Lankan rupees each, we were determined to see as much as possible in the day. Underwhelmed by the whole experience.

Title: Huge Dagoba
Text:
This was our third dagoba of the day and whilst the temple and the reclining Buddha  were impressive, our poor bare feet could not cope with another circuit of another dagoba. 

The tourist board should reconsider its policy of forcing people to cram so many sites into one day (as there is no way we'd pay an additional 3,500 Sri Lankan rupees as a European visitor for the pleasure of having a more leisurely visit over two days).

Title: Impressive feat of engineering
Text: This is the biggest stupa in the world in terms of area and an impressive feat of engineering. The stupa has an attached museum, which is above average and gives a lot of context about the visit to the stupa. The area around the stupa has lots of archaeology, so interesting also for the history buffs.

Title: Small bricks amazing size Stupa
Text: This Stupa is believed to be the biggest brick built structure in the world and when you visit it you will be amazed at the size (small) of the bricks used in its construction, it is an amazing sight.

Title: Fantastic
Text: This site is listed twice here and may support the must see importance of it amidst the sacred sites in Anuradhapura. Please see rating for first listing of Jetavanarama Dagoba.

Title: Most impressive stupa ever
Text: Somewhat ignored by most pilgrims, yet this is the most impressive of the stupas in the historic city (and one of the 8 sacred sites). Without much ado, the focus here is clearly on the stupa (highest brick stupa ever built), the Bo Tree and the Buddha image. A tour towards the end of the day will give you fantastic light for your walk around. Makes for superb photo shots! The remains of the adjacent monastery are impressive both in size as well as functionality. Do not miss this stupa on your tour!

Title: Jetavanarama Dagoba
Text: Can't enter this temple but can walk right around the perimeter. Very large, so remember to wear a sun hat or carry an umbrella as there is no shelter from sun.

Title: One amongst many Dagobas!
Text: There are many Dagobas and Stupas in Anuradhapura but each one must be visited to experience the scale again and again. Walk around it and grasp its vastness. Be sure to carry socks as in summers the floor get too hot to walk on and one cant wear footwear here!

Title: Amazing Scale!
Text: The scale of this Stupa does it. It is amazing to just walk all around it and experience its vastness. Must visit and must walk around. Be careful of summers! It gets very hot and the stone floor burns the feet as you cant wear footwear. Carry socks!!

Title: Superb site
Text:
The massive stupa remains in front of your eye for hours after the visit. 

The broken top of the stupa has its own interesting story and the circumferential pradikshina (roundabout) is best attempted in the mornings or evenings when the sun is a good deal lower.

The weather can be intensely hot at times - hence dress accordingly. However do note that caps and hats are not allowed - also women are expected to cover their shoulders and cover themselves below their knees. 

Together with its sister stupa, this one offers some of the best preserved potions of the Anuradhapura archaeological complex!

Title: Incredible!
Text: This towering structure is the largest stupa in Anuradhapura and demands a stop. Unfortunately my spouse and I experienced a heavy rain during our tour and we were unable to get good photos. As such, we did not get to see all that wished.

Title: See both Stupas and enjoy the jungle
Text: A major step back in time to see this brick tower rising from the jungle. Stepping of tonthe renovated stuba you then have a picture of a lost world and one refurbished and continuing as a place of worship.

Title: Biggest brick stupa!
Text:
Stopped here on a quick visit to Anuradhapura.  No ticket needed, just drove up, took shoes off and visited.

Be careful,  the cement gets very hot! 

Not much info in English, so read about it before visiting. 

Enjoy!

Title: The scale of these stupa is unbelievable
Text: Really interesting part of the anuradhapura complex. The sheer scale is amazing and as it's not rendered you can see how they were built. It gives you a feel for how magnificent the site was in its heyday

Title: Massive and Vast ancient kingdom!
Text: The scale of ancient settlement Anurahpura is one of the most impressive archeological sights the technology and the cultural enlightment of these ancient forbears of the modern day Ceylonese is amazing. This city is vast and takes a full days expoloration. Be aware take plenty of water and sunscreen.

Title: Amazing temple
Text:
We arrived at about 4 pm and we witnessed a prayer ceremonie with traditional trumpet play. Amazing impressive site. Apparantly, according to our driver, the ceremonie was rare and symbolised prayer to people. 
To see the temples, you need to pay a pass worth 3500 roepies a person. Only tourists pay this.

Title: Unique and inspiring
Text:
I have travelled all over Asia but the stupas and temples here in Sri Lanka are unique. The size and mass and scale of Jethawanaramaya is truly awe inspiring. Why this sight is not up there with the likes of the Pyramids or Angkor Wat I don't know. The size of the surrounding plaza makes it easy to step aside and be Alone for a moment. Take time to sit away in a corner to soak this place up. Watch the locals worship. Just be... Try to hook in to a moment of spirituality. 
Surrounded by ancient ruins this site is easily accessible by car and should be incorporated into any tour but it's beauty is its simplicity so I am not sure a guide is necessary. 
Don't think about it.... Go there!

Title: A vision of local history
Text: There's ruins seem to share a theme with others in other parts do the world ie Canbodia where Indian themes are present.

Title: Amazing piece of history
Text: This stupa has been restored but without rendering the outside walls as was the norm in this period,because of that you can see more of how it was built and all the brickwork

Title: Jethawanaramaya Stupa
Text: Incredibly, we were the only ones there when we visited.  Something Like 93 Million bricks were used in its construction Very impressive and a must see if in the area.

Title: Once the Tallest Structure in the World after Pyramids
Text:
JETAVANA DAGOBA
The Jetavana Dagoba (Stupa), a UNESCO world heritage site, is the highest brick-built Dagobah in the world, founded by King Mahasena (276-303 AC) upon Mahayana Buddhism, on the ruins of an old monatery. When built with over 93 million bricks in 27 years, it was the third tallest structure in the world after two pyramids of Khufu & Khafra in Giza, Cairo (Egypt). Originally its height was 397 feet and it was erected on land measuring 8 acres. Its diameter was more than 330 feet. Today it is 230 feet high and restoration work is in progress. Before wearing down of its pinnacle, erosion of ground and burial of the base, its height was 400 feet. The Jetavana monastery in its hey days housed bout 3000 monks. It is one of the sixteen most sacred cultural destinations in Anuradhapura.

Title: One of the most calming places in evening
Text: We visited Jethawanaramaya Stupa in the evening. The lighting was really great and the calmness is at its best. Its not very popular as some other stupas in the area. On that day we were the only people there. And the brick work is quite beautiful with the lights.

Title: Oldest Vihara of Sri Lanka
Text: Great Place to see.. Oldest Vihara .. of 1st century...Worth visiting ... structure is entact... and appealing...

Title: Another beautiful stupa - but take socks
Text: This stupa was recovered from the jungle not very long ago, there are boards showing it as it was with trees growing out of the brickwork and vegetation swamping the base. As with all the religious sites in SL take your thick socks so you can walk around easily.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Take socks to protect your feet when it's hot as you're not allowed to wear shoes. Wear full length trousers or skirts.

Title: Huuuuge stupa!
Text: Its really big, which makes it impressive, but lets say it, its just a stupa. There are couple stands on the right which sell refreshing coconuts!

Title: Nice stupa but you can only walk around
Text:
Nice Stupa.
The only thing you can do during a visit of a stupa is walking around it

Anuradhapura it self is nice, but all the sights are so scattered that you never have the idea that you are visiting an ancient city. The local people are also living in between the ancient stupas and other sights. You can't blame them but it is a pity of the total experience. We liked other big sights as Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa more mainly because of this.

Title: Impressive in scale
Text:
Large red brick stupa. It is really impressive in its scale.

It helps to wear socks as walking up to the  site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet.

Title: Impressive
Text:
The scale and the size of this stupa is really impressive. It is wonderful to look at and admire

It helps to wear socks as walking up to the  site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet

Title: Beautiful site
Text:
This place has been associated with the earliest introduction to Buddhism in Sri Lanka. There is a small ceremony at 18:00 every evening. A few monks walk from the monastery up to the white stupa carrying offerings and drumming. Its best to already be at the top of the stupa before it starts. 

If you go here with a driver, ask them to stop at Mihidu Aranya. Its close to the Mihintale site. Its the one of most impressive trees you will ever see. Monks use it for prayer.

Title: One of the nicest sites to visit in Sri Lanka
Text: A must do if you are in the area, quite the climb but should pose no issue if you are willing to make an effort. Would recommend this site to all people who are even remotely interested in culture and/or nature. The view is absolutely stunning!

Title: Feel the vibes
Text:
Beautiful historical site, where Buddhism was first introduced to Sri Lanka. 
The site is very popular with the locals, which really makes you appreciate the importance of the place. Don't miss it.

Title: Well worth the climb
Text: We visited Mihintale late in the afternoon on a Saturday. Wasnt overly crowded but plenty of locals making pilgrimage up the hill. 1,840+ steps to the top, mostly shaded by huge trees. But you can also cheat if you have a driver they can drive you halfway. There are 3 peaks to ascend - a giant Buddha, a stupa and a lookout rock. Very windy up top. No shoes allowed. Well worth the views.

Title: Beautiful sunset
Text: I had heard of this place but hadnt really looked into it. So we hadnt really planned on going here. It was only because our tuk-tuk driver, who had taken us to the old town in Anuradhapur, had suggested us to go here that we went in the evening. In the end, we were very glad that we went there. The sunset was beautiful and we liked it even more than the old town. Before the sunset, we also took a guide on the spot. His English was very good and he explained a lot but didnt overdo it.

Title: A beautiful visit at sunset
Text: We visited this area at 4:30 pm and found lots of posted information, describing what we were looking at.  There were also 3 big climbs - up to the Buddha, up the rock and up to the Stupa.  The views were spectacular.  We did the Stupa last and sat and watched the sunset.

Title: Spectacular mihintale
Text: Head up in the afternoon to skip the heat but allow time to climb each of the three sites and end on one ready to watch a spectacular sunset.  Climbing looks. Much harder than it is. Give it a go!!

Title: Excellent views and really interesting area.
Text: Our visit here was worth it as from the car park we came across the ruins of a hospital and on entering there was a stone with the interior carved in a human form. Nearby is a museum with archaeological finds.

Title: Fabulous views
Text: This temple is quite small with elements rather spread out.  It is located on a hill, so expect to climb lots of steps.  The views are excellent.  The topmost sections are sacred, so you need to climb barefoot

Title: A must see
Text: Loved it. It is a climb but should not be missed. Very good views. Be careful to go at the top of the rock as you bear foot.

Title: Mihintale Temple
Text: We were there two days ago. Not very crowded (not sure is it because of the recent bombing incidents). Entrance fee 500 rupees each and we spend about 2 hours here. Nice temple with great surroundings

Title: Stunning views, absorbing site
Text:
We visited Mihintale for a couple of hours while travelling between Anuradhapura and Sigiriya and it was well worth the stop.

We picked up a guide at the entrance which made the whole experience all the better as he described the history and relevance of the site and showed us some spots we may otherwise have missed. 

Shoes have to be left before enterning the main site so take socks to avoid the grit and the heat. There are four main components to the complex at Mihintale and three require climbing up steps/rocks so it's not a good option for anyone with impaired mobility.  The centrepiece in Mihintale is the Ambasthale Dagoba which is where a former King is said to have converted to buddhism. Up some steps to  one side of the main Dagoba is a relatively new white statue of buddha which looks great against the blue sky. On another side is the large Mahaseya Dagoba which offers good views across the area. We visited when it was offering time so were treated to a bit of ceremony. Then there is a tricky rock to climb (especially if you are wearing socks as it can be a bit slippy so think about taking them off briefly) which gives wonderful 360 views of the site and surrounding area, all the way back to Anuradhapura, where you can see varous dagobas in the skyline. On the way back down we stopped at Sinha Pokuna to see the lion carving.

Its a wonderful and fascinating site and would be a great place to be for sunrise or sunset

Title: Great Views
Text: This smaller site is cheaper and better maintained than the whole of Anuradhapura.  Nice views, but since you have to remove your shoes, some of the steps can be slippery in socks.  Watch out for aggressive monkeys too!

Title: Very interesting site!!!
Text:
I enjoyed my visit to Mihintale and it is a great half-day trip while in Anuradhapura.  It is very interesting, and everything can be visited in about 2-3 hours.  Note that as all sacred placed in Sri Lanka, you will need to walk around without shoes, so try to take a pair of thick socks to make your visit more comfortable.  Also, try to avoid going in the middle of the day as it gets extremely hot.  Even the rails to go up/down the rock can get very hot at times, so a pair of gloves would not be a bad idea.

The views from the rock are great!!!

Title: Amazing sunset
Text: Came here for sunset, climbed the steps to the temple and the rock to watch the sunset. Such a beautiful view. There are a lot of monkeys!! One followed me for a while as he saw I had peanuts and he stole them from my bag haha! Enjoy, being modest clothing as its a temple.

Title: Good for the physically fit
Text: The stair case to the top of the rock is steep and cut into the rock. I recommend this place for the younger crowd and those who are fit. The view from the top is awesome. Mostly visited by local buddhists and foreign vistors.

Title: Birth Place of Buddhism in Sri Lanka
Text: Travelled by lots of Sri Lankans and Foreigners!. We are grateful to our guide Sunil at TourMart.lk for introducing this place while visiting Anuradhapura. He gave us a very good explanation about the history of Mihintale.

Title: Impressive- great experience
Text: Group visit. Steep climb to Invitation Rock for the panoramic views. All the more awkward with no footwear or headgear allowed in the very hot sun. Then climb again to the Stupa. A fascinating site, but difficult for those not very able.

Title: Awesome sunrise
Text:
Use a Tuk Tuk to get half way up so its less painful to climb and arrive by 06.00 to be sure of the sunrise.
Absolutely do it for sunrise! Cool  temperatures and few tourists.

Title: Well worth it
Text: We left our hotel in Anuradhapura at 3.30 pm for the trip to Mihintale to get there for 4 ish to make sure we got to summit for sunset. Lots of steps but our tuk tuk driver took us to the car park entrance half way up to save our legs. Great views although clouded over a little at sunset. Beware the monkeys as they steal from any bags left open

Title: A great alternative to the larger site at Anuradhapura
Text: After a hot and discouraging day at Anuradhapura, with no maps available, very few helpful signs, and staff that couldn't direct us anywhere, we were glad to take a tuk-tuk to Minintale the following day. Much of the walkways are shaded, and the lushness of the setting is more welcoming.  We picked up a stronger sense of the past, of the island's Buddhist heritage as we explored without a guide. Take the time to wander off on side paths, away from the throngs along the 1,800 steps.  There's refrigerated bottled water available for sale at the top.

Title: Better than the Anuradhapura site
Text: This is a much better place to visit than the Anuradhapura Archaeological Park and for a fraction of the entry fee - 500 rupees!! Mihintale is easily reached by bus from Anuradhapura new town bus station, it takes about half an hour and costs 40 rupees. From the bus stop its a walk of about 400 metres to the museum which makes for an interesting stop before entering the park itself. Just past the museum you climb a long stone staircase to a landing area where the ticket office is. From this area further sets of stairs lead to the various sites (it has to be said there are lots  of stairs to climb to cover this site properly but if you take it easy it shouldnt cause a problem). The main route takes you up to the core area of the site where you find the Ambasthale Dagoba, a large seated buddha statue and a rocky viewpoint. The area is peaceful and scenic and the views from the upper levels are stunning. A less travelled set of stairs from the area around the ticket office takes you to the ruined stupa of Et Vihara. If you head this way chances are youll be the only one up there and the stairs and path are semi-overgrown. It feels like a bit of an adventure getting up there and the views are stunning yet again.

Title: A definite must!
Text: We went later in the day and it was perfect timing.  Got to see a spectacular sunset and the views were spectacular as well.  Didn't find it to touristy.

Title: We climbed it, so can you!!
Text:
When you look at this site, you think that it looks impressive down here.  It is worth climbing up and seeing for yourself.  The views are stunning.  I dont like heights but i was determined to do it.  The fact that you cannot wear shoes here actually makes climbing easier, but the rocks do get a bit hot!!
You just have to wonder, how they managed to built such impressive temples.

Title: Marvelous and impressive
Text: Quite a marvelous historic spot. The lore says Buddhism was created in Sri Lanka here. The place is historic and impressive. Terrific views. The climbs can be quite tough, especially if you're not so well on foot. You can choose to skip the steep climbs though. Look out for the monkeys! They'll rob you once they can get the chance.

Title: You can do this and Anuradhapura on the same day
Text: Visited here and Anuradhapura on the same day and really enjoyed both places. You have quite a few steps to climb coming from the car park and then when you get there it is shoes off, so it is worth wearing some thick socks as the ground can get quite hot and it can be rough in some places. The temple is quite large, but not as big as the one in Anuradhapura and there is a stunning buddha. It is worth climbing the rock there as you get a different perspective of the setting. Entrance was $5.

Title: Quick visit from Anuradhapura away from Masses
Text: We opted to this off the beaten path visit to Mihintale which turned out to be a great experience. It is smaller and less crowded by tourists as opposed to the main sights in Anuradhapura. We were lucky enough to find a wonderful local guide to take us around - very knowledgeable and great spirited. His name is Athula Wansa and he can be reached by phone at +94-76-693-8585

Title: Interesting climbing experience, nice views from the top
Text: Mihintale is a huge, smooth bolder, about 1,000 ft. in height and associated with the introduction of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Although there's a metal cable you can hold on while climbing to the top, the climb is made a bit difficult by the fact that you need to take off your shoes beforehand and socks on smooth stone make for quite a slippery an experience. Once on top, you're treated to a nice view all around, including a large, white stupa and statue of a sitting Buddha. An experience worth trying ...

Title: Inspiring
Text: Here is the origin of Buddhism in Sri Lanka and what an inspiring place it is. Be ready to make a difficult climb up rough stone steps. Be ready for a sense of peace and serenity. Be ready for stunning vistas and Anuradhapura in the distance.

Title: A tough climb but worth it for the views
Text: This is a very interesting site.  As with all temples you need to remove your shoes and cover shoulders and knees.  The climb to the top of the rock is difficult as poeple are travelling in both directions but totally worth it for the awesome views.

Title: Buddhist
Text: This is a famous and popular Buddhist temple here. You have to climb the rock.The view from the top is beautiful.

Title: Good evening  Experience
Text: We visited at 6 PM around sunset. Parked our car the second level which means about 300 easy stairs to the top. It is Well illuminated at night and the statue floor Buddha was fantastic. It was more about the journey to make it to the top. It was also less crowded at that hour. Can accomplish this trip in less than an hour.

Title: A lovely Afternoon visit
Text:
Visited here as part of our tour of Sri Lanka and loved it. Just be aware that there is a lot of climbing and most of it has to be done without shoes. (Take an old pair of socks as the ground is rough and uneven - keep these handy for all the religious sites you visit in Sri Lanka)
The views at the top are amazing and worth making he effort. 
I was gutted that my camera battery died as we got to the top. 
Also be aware of the monkeys - dont put your bag down it might quickly disappear

Title: Great and easy climb, full of temples, fantastic views from the top
Text:
Much better than the nearby Anuradhapura. A large amount of temples of different ages concentrated in a relatively small mountain. Most of the climbing is relatively well preserved stairs (my kid counted 430), only the very top is challenging, but it's not a must.

The views of the surrounding area are awesome.

Beware of the monkies! They steal. Everything.

Return tuktuk from Anuradhapura should be no more than 1500.

Title: Recommended with a guide!
Text:
Mihintale was one of our favourite places in Sri Lanka. It was the only place we had a guide, Athula, explaining the historical and religious background of the place, which really added a lot to the limited information we had in our tourist booklet. We first agreed on 1000rps, but we added a little tip because of the excellent explanation and kindness. We promised to put his name and telephone number in a TripAdvisor review. His name is Athula, he is an official guide in the Anuradapura district. He does not have e-mail or WhatsApp, but you can 
reach him with this telephone number: 0766938585.

Title: Great place with views
Text: Come early,  you have a lot of stairs to climb.  And a rock with feeble stairs after that.  But you will enjoy the wind,  the view and the feeling of serenity here.  Don't forget to go of the beaten path and 'hike' a little way to the naga pond or some other way round.

Title: Avoid the Crowds
Text: We visited in mid-afternoon and there was only one other visitor. We were told sunset is when the crowds appear!  The walk up to the top was not easy as the 'steps' are very worn and the stones and metal handrail super-heated by the sun.
