But turn around and another set of unworn steps can be seen leading up to a stupa on an adjacent hill giving a perfect view of Mihintale and the surrounding countryside.

Title: Nice sunset
Text: The mountain is really nice to visit during sunset. There is a ceremony and you can climb to a high point and see very far.

Title: Fascinating place
Text: This ancient site is fascinating, but you do need a guide to get the most from it.  Fabulous views. The monastery site is huge.

Title: Wonderful excursion from Anuradhapura
Text: Mihintale is a favourite place in the whole of the island.  The modest effort required to climb to the dagoba is amply rewarded with marvellously extensive views all around, of wewas and jungle.  This is a historic place and has a spiritual feel about that one finds rarely, even in Sri Lanka.  There are several monuments on the way and the hike can be extended in two directions, given that you have suitable footwear, not deposited as required on the way.

Title: Epic at Sunset
Text: Chose to have a guide which was worthwhile, he gave insight into the site and Buddhism in Sri Lanka.  Nice combination of manmade features and rock formations.  Nice view.

Title: A really excellent place to visit
Text:
Mihintale is a really interesting site and despite being listed under Anuradhaura on TA it is in fact 12 km away in the village of Mihintale.  Contrary to some advice tickets were not at the museum, which is small and not too interesting and you can miss, they were at the upper level car park. This is back to the road and then second left after the museum and gets you three quarters of the way up.
The stupa was impressive on top of one hill, a reconstruction not original, a Buddha statue on another hill, the pilgrimage hill a third point all off a central area with another stupa in the centre. With many local people there worshipping and visiting it made for a colourful interesting visit and the Buddha and stupa hills were quite quiet to walk up whereas there was a queue and more difficult walking up the hill crowded with genuine pilgrimage locals so perhaps its a better idea to leave this to genuine worshippers than sightseers.

Title: Sri Lankan landmark
Text: Wonderful views from the top and, if you are not a climber, a driver can go up a good part of the way. You have to climb without a hat or shoes the last bit as it is a holy site, but there are railings.

Title: stairs
Text:
I didn't put five stars because it poured while I was visiting, so my visibility was greatly reduced; I didn't get to see some of the views over the area. 
You get to climb a lot of stairs to see this sight. It's pretty impressive, knowing that devotees climb all the stairs regularly.

Title: Worth the trip
Text: Cycled from Anuradhapura (12km) to visit this temple that sits ontop of more steps. There is a climb up to a prayer rock with the most stunning views however its not for the faint hearted...the steps are in fact grooves into rocks. My advice is to take off your socks for extra grip!!

Title: Pretty views, hectic climb
Text:
We drove to the parking halfway up, then there are a few stairs until you are in the main complex. The stupa is easily accessible and very impressive, the rock with the viewpoint was a challenge- the stones were extremely hot, but sometimes there were no proper stairs so wearing socks made it too slippery, also the railing was scorching. But if you're up for the adventure the views are 100% worth it!
Also keep your eyes open for monkeys, within a second they had jumped in our car and stolen the apples!

Title: Beautiful and Meditative
Text: A few miles from Anuradaphura lies this amazing viewpoint atop a small mountain.  You can take a vehicle most of the way up to a parking area and explore from there--a rock viewpoint, stupa, and Buddha statue..... or just find some shade and enjoy some quiet time.

Title: One of our favourite cultural sites in Sri Lanka - a surprise!
Text: We stopped in unplanned while on a cycle tour and really enjoyed this site at dusk / sunset. A very significant and unique combination of archeological site and a site of active Buddhist worship. Includes an optional climb to the top of an oddly shaped rock (a very short ascent in bare feet; decent fitness and mobiity needed). We were treated to incredible views as the sun set and the eerie sound of drummers at the nearby stupa. A long flight of stairs leads to the upper level sights and these are what really makes the visit special.

Title: Fantastic views
Text: Mihintale is a wonderful place, you can really understand why someone would go up there to meditate and to pray. Its a very relaxed place and it has some fantastic views over the gorgeous valleys around.

Title: Climb up Mihintale
Text:
It cost 500 rupees each to get in. Wear white and shoulders and legs must be covered.
Barefoot its a fair climb up to the Buddha and to the temple and to the lookout.
There are spectacular views from all 3 climbs, so go on a clear day and maybe near sunset?
Steps cut into the rocks make it a little rough on your bare feet but barefoot is mandatory.

Title: Ready for climb
Text: Very very sacred place Buddhists. Nice place in the old place [Now ruins] but the one big Buddha statue, one big Stupa and one small hill are main attractions there. You are to climb little height in all the three attractions. But after reaching there, the sight was very nice. Entry ticket of Rs 500 LKR for foreigners.You are go on bare foot after a certain distance.Approximately 1.5 hr time will be required for this place.

Title: Apparently the birthplace of Buddhism in Sri Lanka
Text: Good views from the top looking over Anuradhapura after walking up some uneven steps, with handrails.

Title: A must do!
Text:
This site lies 12 km east of Anuradhapura and was where buddahism was first introduced into Sri Lanka. There are a total of 1850 steps so I am told, but if you drive up to the car park you miss out the first 200. The first thing you see is the ruins of alms house with its large troughs for rice and curry! Next comes a long flight of steps up to the upper terrace where you can visit the image house which contains some relics found in the area, jewellery, ivory beads etc. Across from the image house you reach the Ambasthala Dagoba which is the site where buddahism started in Sri Lanka. It is surrounded by a metal post fence.  Ext is the steps leadin to Aradhana Gala- it is the where the minks meditated and it is a steep scramble up there. The steps aaa are irregular or missing sand you really need to use the handrail for help. The view from the top is excellent. Coming down is also difficult. To be honest this climb is not for the faint hearted - especially when there are lots of people doing the climb!!!
There is also a large modern white stone Buddha and the large white Mahasseya Dagoba to visit. Theres are lots of other smaller things to see but after all the steps and the rock  climb, I was pooped!

Title: One of Sri Lanka's highlights.
Text: Very interesting place, even if it's overshadowed by more wellknown and visited Anuradhapura, Pollonaruwa and Sighiriya. The ascent is vey rewarding, panorama from the rock is very nice. Pay attention to the monkeys, they are agressive and potentially dangerous. Hide food and drinks as they will try to stole it.

Title: Mihintale by Public transport
Text:
We visited this place yesterday. Regular buses goes to Mihintale from Anuradhapura new town bus stand. Ticket 30LKR per person. We started at 4pm by bus and reached Mihintale at 4.30. we walked around 500 mtr till the starting point of steps to the temple. Withing 10 mins we reached at the parking area. It took us more 5 mins to reach the temple. I loved the place..Very peaceful with good positive vibes!
View from top of the rock is amazing. Steps to the top are uneven but one can easily climb it...It's not that difficult. 
We started walking back at around 6.15 and within 10 mins we walked down all steps. The last bus from mihintale to Anuradhapura is at 7pm. If you miss it you can hop into any bus coming from Kandy, Colombo. But not sure abt the timings of such buses so better to leave early and catch the last bus. We got the last bus and reached Anuradhapura at 7.40

Title: Go at dawn
Text: This is a magical place to watch sunrise. Dont worry about all the steps, they are shallow and easy, but the climb to the top of the rocks is a bit more challenging

Title: Favorite Place in Anuradhapura
Text: Located about 13 kilometers from Anuradhapura, this is a great, fairly small temple complex.  You have to climb a bit from the parking lot to see the major sites, such as the wonderful dagoba and the big rock, but it's worth it.  Views are lovely and some of the ancient structures are quite beautiful  We met an 80 year old lady who climbed to the top of the big rock, so I think most people can do it.

Title: First foot step of Lanka Buddhism
Text:
Situated near to ancient city Anuradhapura, Mihintale believed to be the place where Arhat Mihindu Thero meets King DevanampiyaThissa ruler of the country at that time. 

Mihintale becomes a Buddhist monastery and still we can find ancient evidence to prove it.

Foreigners who are visiting Anuradhapura never miss to visit this place due to its close proximity. 
You need to wear proper attire since this is a religious site. You have to climb hundreds of foot steps to reach this place, so better to prepare.. however theres Road which will reduce the half of the burden but Im not aware locals can use it.

Title: Interesting place with history
Text: I didn't the rockclimbing but the walk uphill to the temple is nice with the Buddha and the panoramaview. The steps are irregular, can be slippy and there is no rail

Title: Great Views
Text:
This is well worth the climb up the steps. Not too bad by reference to some other atractions in Sri Lanka. 

I only went to the Temple, from where you have a great view of the Buddha and the rock/stupa. 

Frankly, the views from the temple are probably the bets and easiest (as less crowded). 

Very peaceful, and well worth a view at sunset.

Title: Lots of steps
Text: You climb a long way to this temple but the steps are gentle although not uniform. As our first Temple we were unprepared for how much walking we had to do barefoot. There late so saw sunset over misty valley. Definitely worth a visit but go prepared!

Title: Great place!
Text: Mihintale is the cradle of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. On the hill there is a rock with a view of two hills - on one we can see a statue of a Buddha, and on the other a giant stupa. There is a lot of monkeys out there!

Title: Great
Text: Great historical place where the buddhusm came from india to sri lanka. Top of the view also amaizing

Title: More and more
Text: When in Anuradhapura one is confronted with so many historic structures and legends and history in one area. Amazing

Title: Good view from the top
Text: Three hills to climb. One with Buddha statue, one with stupa, a peak from which you can enjoy the sight of both. Good for sunset time. Pay attention climbing to the peak.

Title: Amazing view
Text: The way up and down is easy, loved it! The view is amazing once arrived at the top. Dont forget to take off your shoes.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text:
We did this after doing the various sites in Anuradhapura and it was well worth the extra day to visit it.
Try to make the time to see it all - even the rather scary climb up the rock to the side of the Buddha and Stupa climbs.

Title: Incredible views
Text:
Extremely interesting sacred site. Strenuous climb 1800steps to top area. Many additional steps to climb up to two points, one a dagoba and the other high rock. Amazing views of the area. Interesting Buddhas there.
Highly recommend it when visiting Sri Lanka

Title: Minhintale MUST!!!!
Text:
Feeling exhausted from a day spent exploring the Ancient city of Anuradhapura my girlfriend and I rather reluctantly forced ourselves to minhitale ruins for sunset and thank god we did. 

Minhintale is a beautiful mountain monastery with jaw dropping views of the surrounding landscape and appeared a lot less touristy than than the sites of Anuradhapura's ancient city. 

We had a wonderful personal experience with one of the ' authentic' guides who gave us both an entertaining history lesson and took us to some great vantage points for photographs and to view the incredible sunset which we would have missed completely had it not been for our guide.

Just watch out for the cheeky temple monkeys, one of which swiped my hand towel and was up a tree before I even noticed

( I'm usually weary of guides but on this occasion I highly recommend one. They Rely on donations based on how you rated the experience, we never felt forced into giving him a certain amount)

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Stairs to steep for this 71yr old to climb but grand daughter was fine. Very interesting and historic ,worth the effort

Title: Great views from the top, plan to avoid the heat
Text:
Unless you want to prove something to yourself, there is no need to climb all 1800+ steps. Ask your driver to take you up Old Road, which gets you almost halfway up. That leaves only a few hundred steps to climb. Bring water.

The ruins at the level of the ticket booth (at the end of Old Road, halfway up the hill) are good for a 15-minute walk-around. The stone canoe at the alms house is quite impressive. Apparently, lay people would fill this with rice as donation to the monks who lived here.

Dont miss the lion carved into the side of Lion Rock.

Up the hill, there are three peaks forming a triangle around a basin. The basin is not large -- little bigger than a football field. The lowest peak has an imposing modern statue of the Buddha  very easy climb, but not much by way of views from there. The second peak has a huge white stupa; good views from there, especially of the other peaks. The tallest is a steep climb up bare rock (steps cut into the rock with handrails). Great views, but dangerously slippery if wet.

Because its a sacred place, you have to take off your shoes as you approach the three peaks and basin. Wear old socks if youre not accustomed to walking on paving stones or sand that is frying-pan hot from the tropical sun. Even if not hot, the sharp grit underfoot makes it painful. 

Th historical significance of this place has to do with being where a king first accepted Buddhism.

Entry was 500 rupees. The site does not seem to have any cafe, toilet or shop selling water -- but then again, I didn't look that carefully.

Covering the upper steps and peaks leisurely takes only about 90 minutes. To escape the worst of midday sun, you can start the climb at 4pm and still have plenty of light when you reach the top. But there are plenty of shrine-caves and ruins in the area. If you are intent on visiting them, I think you will need an hour or two more, which means starting much earlier than 4pm. I didnt bother, as by this point in my visit to the country, Ive had my fill of Buddhist places. 

My hotel arranged a tuktuk from Anuradhapura for 4 hours at a cost of 2,000 rupees (leaving little time for shrine-caves). Its only 13km or 30 minutes journey time. The driver took me to a few other places before reaching the Mihintale peaks. One was a big tree monastery (nothing much to see except a big tree and a human skeleton); another was the site of a hospital dated to about 800 CE (OK for a 10-minute walk-around); and the third was Black Water Pool (more ruins, so-so views).

If your hotel does not offer such a service, its still very easy to hire a tutktuk from anywhere in Anuradhapura for 3 to 4 hours for a similar price.

Title: A Fabulous Way To Start Off Seeing Ancient Sights and Temples in Sri Lanka
Text: There is a lovely amount of variation here.  It's the monkeys, the giant squirrel.  It's the steps, then a flat then more steps then flat then steps carved into rock then 360 views from the highest point.  It's the learning when and where is holy ground with shoes on or off.   It's the ledge with superb views (no need to sit on the edge my 14 year old son - no seriously!!)  It's learning that Stupas are so large that you can easily lose sight of those you are with and go round in circles for a little longer than necessary.  And then there is a word that escapes me to describe the whitest of white for that magnificent Buddha and Stupa here.

Title: Beautiful site
Text: A really lovely place to visit. Dont be put off by the number of steps, you go up and down so you have respite in between the climbs! I was wondering why it is not more popular ... I spent a peaceful couple of hours exploring here. Well worth it. The entry fee is only 500rupees and so you can afford a guide for a quality experience :)

Title: Tour visit.
Text: Went here during a local Bank Holiday so there were lots of people paying homage. Not sure that traditional custom of removing foot wear before entering site is appropriate nowadays.

Title: Interesting site , but may not be worth the time
Text:
This is a temple near the Anaradhapura complex.  But there is no temple to speak but an open holy site for praying. With a Bodi tree on its grounds. 

There is a large Stupa,ruins of a refectory , and a large Bodi tree. Really not much to see once you get up there.   The climb up is quite a bit. About 1800 steps but on a gentle gradient. But still a climb nonetheless.  
The steps up to the temple are like a broadwalk which is quite impressive and the views are also quite good .  Shoes will need to be taken off before entering the temple grounds. ( for your info, the donations to the shoe keeper is used to fund the running and maintenance of the site).
unless you  have  lots of time , its a place which could be missed out.

Title: Beautiful place to visit
Text:
We visited here as a trip for a few hours from Anuradhapura to see the sunset. 

We stopped at the ruins of the hospital, the black lake and went up to the stupor and Buddha at the top of the hill. Everything was very beautiful, including the view from the stupor. 

There was an entrance fee of 500 rupees for the top sector (the stupor etc) and in this area you can't wear shoes.

Unfortunately a thunder storm started as soon as we reached the top....but goof fun running down in the warm rain.

Title: Beautiful place to visit late in the afternoon, when the sun starts to set.
Text:
It's a buddhist holy place, which you have to visit bare foot.  But the impression is special.  Starting down the hill and climbing the stairs to the upper dagoba brings you in a serene atmosphere.
Climbing the rock nearby gives you a beautiful view on the surrounding landscape.

Title: Perfect place to watch the sunset
Text: Don't be put off by reports on the number of steps or how far you have to walk without shoes as it's only the last part where you need to remove your shoes.  I recommend timing your visit to coincide with the sunset as the view from the top is speculate and if you are lucky you will have monks and monkeys silhouetted against a stunning sunset.  There is lots to do at the top - stupa, Buddha statue and a lookout rock - and lots of ruins along the way to get to the top so I really didn't notice the number of stairs.  That said, admittedly we did only walk from the upper car park.  If you time your visit for sunset, the heat has largely gone out of the rocks but it's a good idea to wear socks anyway.

Title: Superb!!!
Text:
One of my favourite site in Sri Lanka so far. The scenery is simply stunning! 
Carefull this is not for the faint of heart, there are more than 1700 steps before you get to see what you have camed for, so you must be in a good phisical shape.
Bring some ankle socks with you, it is almost impossible to walk bare footed on a sunny day.

Title: Slipper Socks needed
Text: You will be climbing up the rock in high temperatures without footwear (1840 'steps'). Take some slipper socks so you have some grip!

Title: Cradle Of Buddhism
Text:
Mihintale is 12km east of Anuradhapura.It is mountain area where Mahinda met king Devanampiyatissa. Birth place of Buddhism dated back to 247BC.
Every year in month of Poson (June) Buddhists visit this area. King constructed many Viharas & caves for monks.
Car parking is at lower level but bigger buses go to next level where ticket window is located. There are 1840 granite steps to view it completely. 
At lower level you find a place called Refractory probably a place to store cooked food, two stone troughs ,large one for rice & smaller for curry. There are many spots for grinding spices. 
Above it a place having two granite inscriptions telling us records of payments to service staff.
After further climbing you come to a plain platform area where you have to remove your shoes for further visit.
There is a temple in center of this area. Now 3 peaks to climb
One is having a Maha Stupa, no clear steps,climb with help of railing, 7-19 AD
Another peak called Aradhana Gala) where Mahinda landed. Difficult for senior citizens to climb.
Third peak has a Buddha statue.
Stunning views from all peaks.
Entry ticket- LKR 500/per person. No concession for SAARC nationals
You find here Giant Squirrel ,national animal of Sri Lanka. Lot of monkeys also
Suggestion- You must hire a qualified guide for all places in cultural triangle.
Normal charges for guide LKR 1000, we hired in LKR 800 but came to know that guide is included in our package. 
Must visit place

Title: TO GET A NICE IMPRESION ABOUT THE BUDDHISM IN SRI LANKA
Text:
Mihintale, in about 20 minutes drive from Anuradhapura is an ancient Buddhist pilgrimage  where according to the sayings the Buddhism has been inaugurated in Sri Lanka 250 BC..
It is a complex of several religious monuments  and preserved ruins, including stupa and dagoba(s)  most of them restored with the ages.
It is topped by a rock, and all together1.800 steps leads you there.
(Did not check it looked to be 3.000...).
The final stage (to climbe the rock) is quite a challenge you have to find the place, what one may call stairs..   But obviously there is a nice view from the windy plateau.
An existing monastery keeps the place alive, and the sunset is also a long lasting remembrance

Title: Amazing off the tracks temple
Text: Although you really have to be careful for naughty monkeys this place is definitely worth the visit. After a small stairs climb you will benefit from an amazing view and a beautiful Buddha and temple. Not many tourists at this hidden gem !

Title: Lots of climbing and exploring, to keep all ages busy
Text: We chose Mihintale as it looked more manageable that the much bigger Anuradhapura complex.  Worth taking a guide, who may charge you a bit more than the guide books suggest, but still worth it we found, plus you will see the whole place, not just the obvious bits, and understand it more fully.  There is plenty to see, not just the often pictured talk at the top on the exposed rock, which only has one way up and down, so becomes a bit of a jam when moderately busy.

Title: Very nice place
Text:
It is a must see
When you reach go right opposite the ticket counter
You will climb to the the highest point overlooking the stupa which is much better that climbing the rock 
You will have a 360 view and the climbing is very scenic

Title: Windy at the top
Text: Everyone is going for sunset.  So, if you like the crowd it is the best time to go.  If you go a little earlier, you won't have the crowd, it won't be so hot like mid day and still you'll have beautiful pictures and views.  The walk up the rock is not that easy.  A little slippery (way down worse) and no hight fear allowed...

Title: Challenging climb but Great view
Text: It was a challenging to get up and down from this mountain but definitely worth it. Best way to climb is with barefoot. Must safer then footwear unless you  have sweaty feet ??

Title: Stiff climb
Text: In the heat it is a climb to make it to the top of the mountain, but what you will see is totally worth it.

Title: Beautiful Little Place
Text: Spent a lovely couple of hours here. Go at sunrise or sunset. Great views from the large stupor and Buddha. We didnt as were both not great with heights but if you are, climb the main rock for spectacular views (weve seen photos). A surprisingly picturesque little spot. Well worth an early morning or evening visit. Google for photos, mine are on my main camera.

Title: Birth place of Buddhism on the island
Text: This is a sacred site so you have to remove your shoes before entering. There are a lot of steps and a steep narrow pathway with a handrail to climb the rock--with bare feet! Very hot and windy up there but a super view of the whole site.

Title: Great walk!
Text: This was the pick around this area. Burned off some calories after too many curries! Lol! A nice walk up steps and a cool walk up the rock which my 11 year old enjoyed and did not fret too much about. If you are stupored out come for a look here!

Title: Great
Text: A beautiful place with a lot of history. I would recommend to all people to take a guide who will tell you all about the history and the Buddhist religion. Super interesting and really ads up to your visit here. If you come across Nananda go with him, he is super kind and will give you amazing background stories.

Title: legendary place
Text: Mihintale is the place where it all started for srilanka , legend has it that at this very spot Mahinda , son of emperor ashoka preached to the king about buddhism , the place itself is serene and calm , very well maintained , from the car park its about 500 mts walk to the bottom of the great stairs , the stair case is wide and dotted with trees , very charming climb if there is one , be sure to wear comfortable walking shoes and light cotton clothes , the entry ticket for non sri lankans is about 1000 LKR , once at the top there are different stupas and a giant buddha statue , and a observation point , the main stupa requires further climb which is bit tricky , a guide is advisable and is available near ticket counter , also there is a museum and relic temple , the entire visit may last upto 3/4 hours

Title: The foundation place of Buddhism in Sri Lanka
Text: Must visit place, you need not be a religious or history lover, if you like nature and culture then you would enjoy this place. Try to take a guide with you to tell you he story. Better visit it in late afternoon, so that you can watch the sunset from he mountain top. You must climb all the tops, its worth the climb. The view is magnificent from the top.

Title: Peaceful
Text: We hired a tuk-tuk in Anuradhapura to take us to Mihinthale one morning.  There was a ceremony taking place when we arrived and it was really lovely to watch.  Such a peaceful place.  Fewer tourists than at Anuradhapura sites.

Title: Sri Lanka in the rocky hills
Text: Just 13km east of Anuradhapura is Mihintale, the place where Buddhism was introduced to Sri Lanka . The story goes that Mahinda, a Buddhist missionary from India (and the son of the great Buddhist Emperor, Ahsoka), had a chance meeting with the Sinhalese King, Devanampiya Tissa, who was out hunting in the hills and promptly converted the king and all of his entourage.

Title: Worth a walk up the hill to see the sunset
Text: It can get very crowded so you might not be able to stand on the small summit. Still, there are other places to go for a view. If you want to see the Buddha in sunlight go at sunset. For the stupa visit at sunrise. Tip - take a pair of socks since its no shoes for the upper part of the climb.

Title: Lovely view. If you have time it is worth a visit, but not a must.
Text: Beautiful place, located on a little hill. For sunset you'll have a stunning view and a nice calm atmosphere. It is a bit pricey to go inside is you are a tourist. The stupa and Buddha Statue looks nice in the evening light. I really enjoyed our visit. It was quite empty except for a few monks, local devotees and some few tourist so maybe that added to the good experience.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Important religious site in Sri Lanka. However, even if you are not religious well worth a visit to take in the spectacular views back to the ancient city of Anuradhapura and also to Ritigala. In fact you have 360 degree views from the Stupa and even better from the top of the rock. The latter is quiet tricky to climb even when there are no people around, but yourselves. Entrance fee LKR1000. Approximately 30-45 minute drive from Anuradhapura, but well worth it.

Title: Arahat Mihindu(Mahinda) had an audience with the then King Devanampiyatissa in this location.
Text:
Plan your visit early hours in the morning or late afternoon.
Be prepared to navigate 400 to 700 plus stone steps.

Title: Buddhist Temple
Text: Very beautiful Budhist Temple. This is the place where Mihidu Himi met Sinhala king Thissa. One of significant place of Buddhism history

Title: Wonderful atmosphere
Text: A wonderful site, but be prepared for walking over a huge area without shoes and some areas are rough underfoot.  Stones very hot to walk on, so take some old socks to wear.

Title: Great sites
Text: This site is well worth the walk up. There is a "hard" climb to the top of the rock but worth it. All the other places of interest at the site are easier. Well worth a visit.

Title: Unexpected and beautiful.
Text: We slept in Mihintale and found out there is a place worth to visit. It was a good shot. Our driver took us there and organised a guide with umbrella (very useful because of the summer rain that caught us). Interesting monuments, Temple and Budda statue and the rock which You can hike and See a beautiful view from the top. If You have time don't miss it.

Title: Interesting
Text: This was very interesting and historical. Had to take our shoes of and our tourist feet baked on the rocks. Busy place. Grab a guide for a more detailed lesson on the area.

Title: Nice place
Text: This was a very nice place to visit. It was far cheaper than Anuradhapura. During out visit there were many locals

Title: Don't skip this
Text: It's a nice temple complex, offering nice views if you're willing to climb couple of steps and wait for others to pass :)

Title: Be careful if it's raining!
Text: We went up and having seen the limited steps up to the view on the rock I sat it out and my husband went up. The steps are worn and although there is a handrail there is only one for people going both up and down! As it was the heavens opened and we all got soaked and there was water pouring off the rock making the descent fairly treacherous. Our driver took us half way up so that we did not have to negotiate too many steps - this was a wise decision.

Title: Climb worth a view
Text: 1840 steps to a breathtaking view. Langurs and birds are a great watch. Nature trail is lovely. A must do if you have energy and knees are in good shape. The available material on history of the place is limited which is disappointing.

Title: Worth the climb
Text:
Another holy site where hats and shoes need to be removed. We visited at the hottest part of the day, climbing the rock was OK but my feet were burning on the way up to the Buddha. The "steps" to the top of the rock are really just grooves but there is a handrail to help hoist yourself up. Certainly not for anyone with mobility difficulties. 
An amazing view from the top. 
One or two of the places we saw on our tour I could have missed and not been too bothered ( with hindsight) but this was an important site and I'm pleased we did it.

Small shop selling drinks on the way up.
This was the place where we saw a land monitor ( large lizard) attacking something, we asked our driver what it was and he said "its just a scorpion"

Title: Climb the many stairs to enjoy this temple site
Text: It's worth to climb the many stairs to visit this temple site. The view on top is very nice. Wear proper clothes.

Title: Stunning view
Text: Nice place with a massive Buddha statue, a stupa and a rock to climb to enjoy the view from the top. It's the place where seems the buddism came to the island so it's quite interesting.

Title: Beautifull complex
Text:
It is not so big but it is beautifull to visist.
When you go upstairs you van visit the stupa.
You can also climb the rock and rhen you have a amazing view over the country.

Title: Good place to visit
Text:
Being birth place of Buddhism in Sri Lanka with a enchanting historical event occurred there, the place has plenty of history and very ancient ruins. It was worth the visit though no one checked our tickets and we had proactively gone and purchased them from a small booth in a corner. 
We get a feel of Buddhist monks daily lives 2000 years ago. Try hiking off trail steps in the site, it leads to more interesting ruins. Recommend visiting in evening when it gets cooler. Carry your own water + food as the place does not have any facilities including toilets.

Title: Relaxing visit
Text: I like Mihintale, it is very nice place, calm and lot of to see there. Also a nice view of landscape, It is worth to visit. Do not miss lion fountain opposite to parking. :)

Title: 500 rupees PP to kill yourself up so many steps and the rock, good socks a must
Text: The birthplace of buddhism in Sri Lanka. Very holy site, so make sure you have good socks or very strong feet. My wife suffered a little as it was hot walking barefooted on the rock. Some of the steps up to the top of the rock are a little slippy and it is not an easy descent, although you can grasp the had rail. The Buddha is also worth a visit, although it was far too hot for us to do the stupa's. Take a lot of water, although there is a shop to buy drinks. You have to visit and make it to the top of the rock - its an achievement and provides some lovely views. We were not bothered by the "Helpers", but we did have our driver with us.

Title: So much hidden treasures!
Text:
Though the huge number of nice steps and the rock climbing seems to be the main part of Mihinthale journey; there are plenty of important things to see around there. One is the relics of the ancient hospital situated in the "??? ????". 
"Kaludiya Pokuna" is another interesting place that you should visit that is only 500m away from Mihinthale.

Title: Beware the wayside 'Helpers'.
Text:
This is the birthplace of Buddhism on the island and we were looking forward to making the arduous climb to the rock pinnacle, however, the entire experience was marred by the so called 'Helpers' who lie in wait for tourists and engage in conversation with them, bringing out family photos etc to garner trust/sympathy. Once you have responded to conversation they have become your unwanted helpers at an undisclosed fee.
As stated earlier, the climb to the pinnacle is quite arduous as one has to climb using small steps carved into the rock (there is a handrail to the top). If you are using the helpers, do yourselves a favour and negotiate a price prior to accepting their help.
If you are considering the climb, do so in the early hours of the morning before the rock heats up. We had blistered feet from the experience as it is a temple and footwear is not allowed.
Personally I will not take another group of mine there until the situation with the helpers is resolved as members of my group felt very uncomfortable with all the arm grabbing.

Title: Beautiful historic site with good views
Text: This is a lovely historic place, plenty of steps to climb and most of it is barefoot. As it is of religious significance, shoulders and legs should be covered and no hats. My tip would be, if in doubt carry a wrap/sarong/shawl. My other tip would be to carry a pair of socks with you as the ground can get hot. The climb is manageable at a steady pace. However,  the very last bit for the views, is one way traffic only. This is where you meet 2 types of people; the impatient who barge by and the helpful who offer their hand as support, or who lift a child or make way for the old. It was uplifting to see that language was not a barrier.  We noticed the locals taking bags of stuff up with them and assumed it to do with 'pooja' but only at the top did we see that it was sand.  On descending we asked about it. ... the sand is being used to replace the foundation of the stones. We strongly suggested signs should be put up in various languages as had we known we would have carried a few bags up.

Title: Loved this place
Text: We left early from Anuradhapura on our way to Sirigya with our driver and had this place largely to ourselves, and, though the top of the hill was covered in mist at first,  this added to the atmosphere.  We hired a guide at the start of the climb  a must do  and we really enjoyed our visit to this site.    For us, it was the best single place to visit in the Anuradhapura area.

Title: Nice and beautiful place
Text: We didn't climb from the lowest level but mid-level. The climb was very nice and easy. The view from the rock of the Dagoba was super.

Title: Stunning place
Text: This site has 3 main areas, all at the top of hills, all of which you go up bare foot. The rock was definitely worth the climb, as the view was spectacular. We went around the stupa (white hemisphere) and finally went up to the big Buddha statue for sunset. The views are amazing, the site is stunning and it was definitely worth going to see

Title: Worth the Climb
Text: This is well worth the climb. The ruins were really interesting and the views at the top were speculative. Try not to go in the middle of the day like us as it's very hot. Also you cannot wear shoes on the walk and the stone steps get extremely hot!

Title: Great Views
Text: A bit of a climb, something I let my husband do while I sat this one out, being a bit dubious when sharing a set of steep, narrow stone cut stairs and one handrail with people moving in the opposite direction.  My husband tells me the views from the top were great, but I enjoyed the views from lower down as well.  Like a lot of religious sites it is shoes off for quite a bit of the time you are in the general area - so take a pair of socks as the ground can get very hot.  Much more to see than just climbing the rock, US$10 so one of the cheaper sites in Sri Lanka.  A lot of pilgrims when we went, which made it very special.

Title: Nice to do the stair climbing
Text: Nice location to see some heritage from this area over the nudism and have a nice walk over the stairs and area

Title: Interesting temple
Text: Worth a visit, especially to get you into training for the later climbs (Sigiriya, Adm's Peak)! Various things to see once you reach the top, and also good views.

Title: A special experience an amazing view
Text:
Amazing view from the rock after a scramble up. Also a beautiful and well maintained Buddha statue and Dagoba.

City guides offer service, but we enjoyed exploring by ourselves.

Choose a cooler time to climb as bare feet or socks are required and the rocks get quite hot.

Title: Beautiful but inconvenient...
Text: Mihintale is a must in this area of Sri Lanka.  The temples, caves and water tanks are all fascinating and the views incredible.  There are areas adjacent to the main temple which are often missed and deserve exploring.  Luckily we visited as soon as it opened in the morning since it was a significant climb on variable surfaces and steps and it gets hot quickly.  For me (not too much hair...) having to remove my hat, protecting my fair skin from the sun, was not convenient, nor was having to remove footwear for the last part of the climb on uneven rock and gravel surfaces.  These measure were necessary because of the religious nature of the site and I had no option but to respect this.  But visitors ought to be aware.  Perhaps sun cream on the head and thick socks?

Title: Where Buddhism started in Sri Lanka
Text: A beautiful and serene place where Mahinda, son of the Indian King Asoka, converted King Devanampiya Tissa to Buddhism in 3rd century BC. This "sacred Hill of Mihintale" is less visited than the sites of Polonnaruwa and Anuradhapura, but should be a must see because of its history, scenery and serenity. Visit in the morning preferably as it gets very hot. No shoes allowed. The visit should take a couple of hours with a good guide. For the more daring, a climb to Aradhana Gala (Meditation Rock) is worth the effort (it is very steep on narrow steps - remove your socks if you kept them as the steps carved out of the rock can be slippery). From the top, the view over the plain, the Dagoba and the Buddha statue is breathtaking.

Title: Hidden treasure
Text: There is not much to see in a tourist way but this place can bring peace to your mind. The guide took us to a small hermitage. Monks are still living here.

Title: a must see on your trip!
Text:
we have been there in the late afternoon, when it was not that crowded. from the parking lot, it takes you a five minutes walk over some steps to reach the top of the place. there you will see a beautiful buddha statue, a stupa and a sacred hilltop, where you can climb up.
from the top you have a wide and beautiful view over the countryside and you can also see the stupas from anuradhapura.
 
it takes about two hours to explore the whole place, and it is really worth it. not that crowded and very beautiful!

Title: Calming and peaceful place
Text: Nice nature around, best view to area, spoilt monkies, kind monks, calming music, fresh water, lot od stairs

Title: Adventure meets Culture
Text: Climbing to the top of the rock is an adventure rewarded by wonderful views. Walking and climbing barefoot is not for a tenderfoot. This is one of the original sites of Buddhism in Sri Lanka and even the ruins recall an impressive history.

Title: Lovely views from the top
Text: It is a decent walk, you need to be on steady feet as it can be quite slippery however, the view is worth the trek up to the top

Title: Lovely at sunset
Text: Rather a last minute decision to visit and only arrived by tuk tuk at 4.30 but place not heaving though one large school party there. The temple complex is beautiful and the views stunning especially with thunderstorm in the distance. I would recommend wearing socks but the walk up the steps is far easier than expected though would not recommend at the heat of the day and good value at 500 rupees

Title: Stunning! Definitely worth the visit!
Text: This is such a beautiful attraction and is a must see - the view is amazing! Just be warned that you have to take your shoes off & climbing up the rock in midday heat barefooted (like we did!) is unbearable - take socks! Also make sure your shoulders and knees are covered otherwise they will not let you in.

Title: A must see site
Text: Well worth the drive out to Mihintale, one of the best sites in the Anuradhapura area and at a fraction of the cost.  Amazing views and we had a superb guide, have posted a pic of him (can't remember his name!)

Title: Better than Anuradhapura
Text: Mihintale is not far from Anuradhapura, accessible through bus or tuktuk, about 10km I think. The entrance fee is ok and it's worth to take a guide who shows you the area. Take about 1.5h time and take a nice picture just below the summit in a narrow niche between the rocks, you can lay down on a stone and take a nice picture! Guide was 1000. we negotiated him down to 500 but were so happy to give him the full amount (which made him happy as well:-))

Title: Beautiful sunset
Text:
This tour is best in the afternoon to see the sunset. 
A good idea to take a guide which will approach you in the car park.

Title: Excellent
Text: A must see place!  Breathtakingly beautiful. Lots of steps, however so worth it! A piece of tranquility and beauty.

Title: Interesting spiritual site
Text:
This was first visit on our Sri Lankan holiday and an introduction to the necessity of removing one`s shoes when visiting these holy sites. As some reconstruction was underway, and builders grit had been left around it was quite painful for my pathetic western feet!
Worth and visit and great views.

Title: Not just another Buddha, Dagoba n Rock!
Text:
This is special as it's the where Buddhism started in Sri Lanka!
Frankly, the place is bigger than I expected.  It was a blessing in disguise when I arrived at 2pm, way earlier than planned. The sun was blazing but I decided to go ahead!  I was able to enjoy the sights due to the lesser crowd and the time to spare, helped by the occasional passing clouds and nice breeze.  At one point, I was the only one on top of the meditation rock - Aradhana Gala.  The climb can be taxing and risky; so take your time and watch your steps!  The socks helped but the grip can be compromised too.  
Overall, I enjoyed the sights and experience - it's a place not to be missed!

Title: Unforgettable
Text: We will never forget this experience. The climb is very difficult and potentially dangerous. The view from the top is outstanding. The whole climb has to be made shoeless and hatless

Title: Excellent and spiritual place
Text: Mihintale hilltop is a very spiritual place, with several sights, also offering great sunset views. The 1800 steps are far less strenuous than they sound, it takes about 20' to the top. Mind that it can be crowded.

Title: Get a guide Rangana 0713171919
Text:
On arrival we met a guide who offered to show us around. We were glad he did.

From what we planned to be a 30 min visit we spent 90min learning whilst taking some great pictures. 

I would highly recommend that you too seek him out.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: It's a one hour ride by bike from Anuradhapura and an approx. 20 minutes walk up. Entrance fee is Rs. 500 and on the top you'll habe the chance to go up to three different peaks. We enjoyed the one with the dagoba most. Btw: There's some maintenance work going on at the moment, bit still wort a visit.

Title: Interesting place to visit
Text:
Worth seeing for the black pond which is very tranquil, and climbing the "rock". 
We went on a weekend which was busy but a real experience seeing and meeting Sri Lankan people on a day out.

Title: 1600 Years Of Rich History
Text:
A visit is best with a local guide whom will provide the background story which will make the Visit much more interesting.
With do many choice to chose from in  Anuradhapura this is highly recommended and cost only 500Rb .

Title: Puts Buddhist History in Perspective in Sri lanka
Text: It's always interesting to find out more about the roots of a culture by learning about its early history and this is a great site to begin your exploration of the surrounding sites.

Title: A small archeologic site with a lot of magic
Text: A very nice place to visit in around 1 to 2 hours. Amazing to see at sunset. Peaceful and quiet, with a great view on the region from the top of the big rock !

Title: Mihintale is a renowned and very important historical place for Sri Lankans
Text: This is the mountain where Buddhism was introduced to sri Lanka by Ven Arahat Mahinda and Inian saint to the King Devanam Piyatissa 2500 years ago and is an important place to visit.  It could be crowded during Full Moon days, the mountain top can be climbed all protections are available. very peaceful place and important for any Buddhist specially.

Title: Great to visit in afternoon
Text: We visited in afternoon as too hot during the day. have to take shoes and hats off so bit hard on feet. but worth a visit.

Title: Loved it!!!
Text:
We came along and went up here spent about 2 hours and LOVED it. 

There are three things, the stupa, the Buddha and the rock, it's worth climbing up to all. The views are amazing. 

It's just 500 a person entrance and absolutly beautiful!!!

Title: Lots to see up the 1840 steps
Text:
You can climb from the main car park at the bottom right up to the Mahaseya Dagoba at the summit but simpler to take your transport three quarters of the way up to the higher entrance. You can be helped by the rock boys for a few rupees the rest of the way from there. The reference to 1840 steps must include the whole of the complex and not the direct route up, which many of our 60+ age group did!
For those who want a thrill try barefoot up Aradhana Gala (meditation hill) - with help!

Title: Interesting
Text: Great place to go and learn about the philosophy of Buddhism. The temples are incredible, you will also see the so called oldest tree in the world where locals visit and present their offerings. You can also be blessed here if you wish, lovely place.

Title: Historical/temple site with accessible ancient ruins
Text: Many steps but there is a road that will bring you 1/2 way up, we were there in Independence Day for Sri Lanka so many wonderful Sri Lankan folks visiting, the place where the monks ate is not to be missed with a big trough where the rice was put and a smaller one for the veggies

Title: beautifull halfday tour from Anuradhapura
Text: It is definetly worthwhile to visit Mihintale for a half a day from Anuradhapura. It is easy to get here by public transport. The temple and the view from on top of the hill are beautifull and the hike uphill isn't too tough. Especially nice is that there are not so many tourists here, which gives it a more authentic feeling. Take socks with you, because on the top the sand and stones can be pretty hot on the feet, as shoes are not allowed.

Title: Easy to under estimate the power of an amazing view after a long flight.
Text: Walking here was hot and tiring, which works well with trying to get into a time zone and sleeping later. Distance is not far but its difficult as the final bit is up 'steps' (basic ledges) cut in the rock with a wobbly handrail and people (friendly sri lankans) going up and down at the same time. Be brave and careful, its slippery - the views at the end of it are wonderful, with the white buddha on a nearby rocky hilltop and a green panorama as far as the eye can see. Unforgetable.

Title: Well worth a visit but needs good weather
Text: Unfortunately we visited in heavy rain and we're unable to full appreciate the site. There are many steps up to the top but there is also an upper car park which does reduce the number you have to climb. You need to take your shoes off quite early and there is a lot of walking in bare feet. Despite the weather we were able to climb up to the viewing point, this is a difficult climb and also up to the stupa, this climb is much easier.

Title: Nice place
Text: Nice place to see if in the area. We were unlucky enough to get caught in a heavy rain shower at the top. Very dangerous as you are barefoot. Shoes must be given in before entry (after all of the steps of course!). Appropriate clothing also required. 500lrk p/p entry. A lot of steps but won't take too long. Plenty of tour guides there if you want one!

Title: Amazing at sunset
Text: My favourite place , so much to discover and the views are amazing. We had a guide who explained all so well, loved the story of how Buddhism started there under the Mango tree. Unfortunately we only did the top bit and missed the first level, caves etc. As it was late to do it all.

Title: Nice place, but go early!
Text:
Nice place, where Mahinda introduced Buddhism to the king of Sri Lanka. 

You have to climb some steps and most of it without your shoes, so it's wise to go early. This way you avoid the heat and don't burn your feet on all the hot stone surfaces everywhere. Or: wear small socks.

Stupa's, rockviewpoint & big buddha statue nice.

Title: It's a long way to the top
Text:
Mihintale
This is the birthplace of Buddhism in Sri Lanka and as such is a highly religious place for the faithful. It is not an easy place to get to as there are some two hundred steps, some fairly new, some at the top are extremely worn and slippery. Once at the top you will see a large Buddha to the left on the top of another hill, so more steps. In front there is a small coloured Stupa. On the right is a large Stupa on top of another hill, so more steps. Finally up more stairs is a rock outlook point with fantastic views. Unfortunately it was quite misty on the day of our visit. Beware the unofficial guides who are simply there for your money, although they can be a source of good information for a price. Make sure to take water.
At the bottom, the younger males were being asked to carry bags of rubble to the top not just to impress there girlfriends but to earn life points. We even saw a group of four lads carrying large granite slabs on poles, presumably to repair the stairs.

Title: Beautiful
Text:
We walked up during a cerimony of the full moon.
It has been very nice, spiritual and of course amazing view!

Title: Stairs
Text: We visited in the evening when most of the other travelers were leaving.  Encountered a large troup of monkeys on the first set of steps (there are many).  Some good views from the top, but not a good choice for a hot day.  1000 rupee admission fee is excessive.

Title: Tough climb in the heat
Text:
The drive up to the halfway point at Mihintale was lovely as it is shaded by mature trees that are home to many Monkeys. The mango trees were all either flowering or in fruit and we were able to see many of the monkeys impatiently harvesting unripened mangos for their troops.

The entrance fee to Mihintale was approximately 1,000.00 Rupees for two. There is parking at the halfway point entrance. There are some stalls selling drinks at the car park and also at the halfway point when climbing. Just beyond the entrance, there are several ruins to view and then to climbing the steps towards the summit.Unfortunately we attempted the climb at almost midday and the heat was rather oppressive. As a result, we decided against the full climb to the top. There is a halfway point in the climb where one can rest at a small stall selling cold drinks. At this point, you can get a glimpse of the main stupa at the top.

Title: Lack of signs made it frustrating
Text: We couldn't find some of the places because there weren't any signs in English - this would be ok if we hadn't paid more than locals to enter.

Title: Worthwhile
Text: I had been a little put off the climb of over 1800 steps suggested in our guide book. However, as our driver drove partway the ascent was much more manageable. I felt it to be a wonderful peaceful location with lots of pilgrims dressed in white ascending and descending the steps with flowers. The climb to the highest platform was beyond me as the steps looked slippery but my husband (aged65) managed it easily as did many others. The hospital at the base was most interesting.

Title: Sri Lanka Adventure
Text: Visited here as part of a day tour of the cultural triangle. Yet another peaceful place in this amazing Country

Title: worth every step...
Text: A must visit place when you touring Anuradhapura, this is the place where Buddhism first came to Sri Lanka. A very beautiful and scenic place and worth every steep step you climb to see the temple. Highly recommended...

Title: Must visit when in Anuradhapura
Text:
Many people visiting Anuradhapura might get tired after visiting many of the points in teh town and miss this
in addition to being the spot where Buddhism was supposed to have originated in Sri Lanka, there are a couple of small climb / hike options that make the location very interesting

Title: Definitely worth the trip!
Text:
We ve been there at Sunset and the colors were beautiful.
This site gather wonderful Dagobas, Bodhi Tree, Buddha and many other interesting curiosities.
The final  rock climb can be a bit tricky if you re not fit but we had a 4 years old with us and she made it easily!

Title: Interesting site
Text:
Nice site to visit. Note that the climbing is not too difficult. The different point of views are really great from there. You have a dagoba, a buddah statue and rock to climb, an ancient water pool, etc... so different things to see.
Just be aware of the monkeys which can be a bit aggressive if you get to close to them.

Title: Beautiful views and nice relaxed atmosphere
Text:
Don't let the 1850 steps out you off! If you can get a tuktuk or driver to take you to the upper car park you're half way there! 

After your first climb, you've a few more but it's worth it for Lovely views from stupa, cave and nice breeze to refresh. Less touristic, so Had a really nice vibe to it. Lot of walking on hot stone or sand without shoes so bring socks if you wear flipflops!!

Title: Amazing view
Text: A must see, because you can see a very nice sunset! You will see a lot of monkey's and you see a big Buddha andere mihintale temple! Don't skip this, it's really worth it!

Title: Overpriced sunset and view
Text: As most attractions in Sri Lanka Mihintale is overpriced. Then, when you arrive at the Budha statue one thing is clear; they don't use the entrance fee for cleaning up the place. You can take a tuktuk but a cheaper option is the bus. Sunset from the dagoda is nice as is the view but I would't spend so much money again.

Title: Surprisingly better than expected.
Text: That was our fourth day of visiting ruins or temples, so weren't too sure. But the views are well worth it!!

Title: Astonishing place!
Text:
I went to Mihintale when I was on vacation with my parents. The place really is amazing. The climb to the mountaintop was somewhat hard on socks, but well worth it! 

I especially thought the huge white buddha statue was amazing! 

There were also a lot of moneys, which was fun :). 

Would highly recommend checking this place out!! However, if you have problems walking or walking stars, this might be to challenging for you.

Title: Place where Sri Lankan's got Buddhism
Text: Eight miles east of Anuradhapura, close to the Anuradhapura - Trincomalee Road is situated the Mihintale.Thera Mahinda came to Sri Lanka from India and met King Devanampiyatissa and the people, and preached the doctrine. This is

Title: A must do when at Anuradhapura
Text: This hillock is around 20 kms from Anuradhapura having a big stupa and buddha temple and surrounding ruins. This is believed to be the cradle of Buddhhisim in Sri Lanka where Mahinda son o Buddha is suppose to have given is first sermon. About half day worth visit.

Title: Beautiful, quick climv
Text: Climb for only 12 minutes and you'll reach the main area. Then reach the rock, Buddha or temple in only another 5mins for each place. We spent a total of one hour and saw all three. It is only 10-15min drive/tuk tuk from the ancient city. Beautiful views from the rock and the buddha. We enjoyed this more than the ancient city. Highly recommend on a trip to this region.

Title: A great place to visit
Text: You can climb up the main rock as well. The best time to visit during the sunset. It can be windy. The view from the top is spectacular!

Title: Incredibly moving, peaceful and interesting place to visit
Text: An ancient place and historically important place for Sri Lankans as well as for Buddhism followers around the world. It is believed this is the place where  Lord Buddha's teachings arrived in SL. The then King who ruled the country started following Lord Buddha's teachings. Incredibly moving, peaceful and interesting place to visit. Be aware of the monkeys, they will grab anything from your hands, ice cream, flowers, phones!

Title: Beautiful and peaceful
Text: Minhintale was one of my most favourites places in Sri Lanka. beautiful, peaceful, scenic, not so crowded with tourists, definitely worth to visit

Title: Sacred and religious sight....
Text:
This is Sri Lanka's one of leading sacred places .... 
if you are willing to visit the sight recommend to visit in early morning or morning hours or else in bit late evening as the rock is not covered by any single tree it will literally burn you out... 
please wear nice n neatly as it's a religious place

Title: The peace
Text: This mountain peak is located about 13KM from Anuradapura. About 1800 steps to climb, seems a lot of psychical activities but in my experience a good half an hour would be enough to reach the top. You can enjoy the fresh wind, calm and peaceful environment on the top. This sacred mountain is so special among the Buddhist because they believe lord Buddha had visited this place. Good time to climb around 3PM so you can enjoy the sunset and the view.

Title: What a view!
Text:
We've done Adams Peak and Sigiriya but this was a wonderful way to finish or trip.

We did sunrise and only ones there. Sat and watched for an hour. Best thing to do!

Title: Wonderful early morning visit
Text: Having visited Anuradhapura in the past it was lovely to find quiet and beautiful Mihintale and to climb up the many steps exploring the ruins set among frangipani trees early in the morning before many pilgrims arrived. A most interesting and sacred Buddhist site with superb views from the dagoba  set on top of the hill.

Title: At least it did not cost a fortune.
Text:
After traveling to Sri Lanka to see the historical treasures, we were put off by 2 things. the high cost of entrance fees (85% higher than locals) and the underwhelmed reviews of fellow traveler. We poured over the photos of "free" areas vs "Expense Entry Fee" areas and frankly we could not see any difference. Therefore, we toured with the intent to NOT pay any of the "Expensive Entry Fees". The thing about the ruins in Sri Lanka is that only the foundations are left and they are not well kept. The dagobas that have been maintained look brand new.
We were advised to take a lunch, which sounded like a great idea, but as soon as we sat down about 20 aggressive moneys appeared, growling and grabbing.  We quickly left, climbed 500 steps and found a security guard sitting in a big cage behind the ticket office. He kindly allowed us to eat our lunch inside the cage while money's drooled outside. 
We appreciated visiting Minhintale for very little money, but, removing ones shoes and hats ( out of respect for the Buddha), then walking over scorched hot sand and rock, seemed pointless while stepping over plastic bags and litter.
After spending 3 hot dry days in Anuradhapura, we jumped off the Cultural Triangle Trail and are spending the rest of our days at the Beach.  
While Sri Lanka is a lovely country with lovely people, if you want to see ruins, go to Angkor Wat or Myanmar.

Title: Watch the sunset here!
Text:
I've been brought to this place by the hotel owner. He told me not to miss this and he was right. On top of the mountain, climb the stairs to the Stupa (on your right) and watch the sunset from the deck: BREATHTAKING! 
I recommend you take a look at the other sights befor it gets dark. It's quite a climb with 1840 stairs and if you're in no good condition, you can drive halfway and start there ;-)
Remind yourself to cover your shoulders and knees. If you don't have it, you can borrow sarongs there for free (where you leave your shoes/flip flops)

Title: Breathtaking!
Text: Awesome views! I can say that I have never seen this beautiful scenery. You have to climb a few steps so take some snack and water bottle with you if you feel that you might need it. Entrance fee was 500rs and that was totally worth it! Don't miss this! Highest rock was bit hard to climb was all the other places you can reach easily!

Title: Worth the visit
Text:
Only 13km east of Anuradhapura, Minhintale is well worth a visit in the early morning or late afternoon when the sun is not so hot. You have it all here; plenty of holy-place steps to tone those calves, ancient history and ruins, a living holy site with dagobas and bodhi tree, a rock summit with magnificent views of the surrounding countryside and naughty Macaque monkeys. 
Mihintale has been associated with the earliest introduction of Buddhism to Sri Lanka. It is a place where you might benefit from the services of a guide. It really is a lot of fun struggling up the final stone steps to the summit with all the locals. There is a rail so hold on tight.

Title: So beautiful...
Text: We went there from Anuradhapura to see the sunset, and it was really beautiful, I would really recommend to go because it's not very far away from Anuradhapura and you can get there by bus

Title: Must go for the sunset!
Text: Nice walk up to the temple area. There's a ceremony for the sunset on top of one of the rock, but we climbed up to the other rock. It was pretty windy up there but view was breathtaking!

Title: Nice temple complex, great views!
Text: Great views when you walk up to the big stupa or the other viewpoint. Entrance for foreigners Rs500. We got a tuktuk from Anuradhapura for Rs1500, waited 2hours for us and then drove back. You walk a lot on the site on bare foot which is pretty hot at times (saw lot of people with socks on, probably a smart idea). We didn't stay until sundown but I guess that will be a very nice view. Lots of (cheeky) monkeys for nice photographs but look out they don't take your belongings..!

Title: Great views
Text: Excellent site for views of the anuradhapura region with a beautiful giant sitting buddha. Modest entrance price of 500 well worth it.

Title: We came in the late afternoon, well worth seeing
Text: It is good to see another aspect of this area that has so many interesting and mysterious places, climbing to the top of the rock gives you a good perspective and is well worth it. Not sure how slippery it gets in the rain or how crowded, both would make the experience less enjoyable.

Title: Amazing
Text: Loved climbing this. The main climb takes about 25 minutes and isn't too bad. You have to take your shoes off half way up which makes climbing the rock a little trickier. Climbing the main rock is a mixture of steps and actually climbing but the view is breathtaking.

Title: try to visit with a local guide, it would be worth every penny
Text: we have been lucky we had a great local guide (who we ended up paying twice the amount we agreed upon out of our own initiative) we therefore received a great explanation and background about the history of this place (and the area), he even turned out to be a good photographer. The entry fee (as of summer 2016) is 500 RS per person for foreigners

Title: Enjoyed the climb and significant place for Buddhists
Text: The climb can be done in 2 ways. There is an easy way from the park and another hard way. I took the hard way but its not that bad and enjoyed and glad that i made it to the top. There are about 2000 stairs and the top is the Mihindu gala where the Mihindu thero appeared to king Dewanam piyathissa during Anuradapura monarch. There is a huge buddha statue and a stupa and the view is significant.

Title: Beautiful views of the area
Text: Our favorite site at the area of Anuradhapura. Climbing the stairs is not hard (not from the car parking anyway), the ancient part near the parking help to understand how the monks lived those days. But it is it is the top of the hill-top that makes everything grand. The views to the site itself and all the area is wonderful.

Title: superb views and ancient site
Text: A small uphill hike leads to a  wonderful site and views. The statutes are well maintained and yet the steps to them are carved into the rock

Title: Fascinating and beautiful place
Text:
We visited as a group and had our holiday guide show us around. This is a beautiful, peaceful complex with stunning views of the surrounding countryside and of the statues and buildings here. 
Top tip: Bring socks in warm weather to put on to walk on the sand / steps as it gets incredibly hot. 
Don't miss this wonderful place if you're in the area.

Title: Lovely place
Text: Well worth the visit. Be prepared for some 1840 steps plus some walking. Better to visit sometime in the evening as it will be slightly cooler. August is extremely hot here.

Title: Nice but not worth the trip
Text: We went to Mihintale simply to see the sight and climb the 1840 steps. It's a very good site if you are around (possibly in Anuradhapura) but I wouldn't recommend traveling a long distance just to see Mihintale. It's very crowded and noisy so the basic idea of "meditating while climbing" looks to be more of a myth. You cannot go inside the temple and like most holy sites it's required that you take off your shoes, which is a little tough with the stone burning up.

Title: Fantastic
Text:
We went there as a surprise as we did want to travel from Anuradhapura to Trincomalee...luckily we looked at the map and decided to make a stop here. 
What an incredible place to visit..beware of all the stairs!! We where spotted by a guide and.....fair is fair...he gave us a fantastic tour....
Be aware at the area were you need to leave your shoes that you have some socks to protect your feet from the heat of the stones!??....
It is worthwhile to put this on your travel list.

Title: Nice views
Text:
Make sure you wear something that covers your knees. They will offer you cloth to wrap around for a small fee if you do not have appropriate clothing. 

Stairs up but not to strenuous, you can stop on your way up.

Very peaceful with great views.

Title: Don't miss this
Text: This place is special. Don't miss it!  Much preferred it to the main sites in Anaradapura and the kids liked it too. The climb to the top of the 'rock' is a little tricky and gets a little crowded so patience is required.

Title: Awesome view from the top and amazing sunset
Text: This is my most favourite place among all visited place in Sri Lanka. You have to climb a lot of steps, be prepared. Take a guide, it is worth than roaming alone. My guide agreed for 200 Srilankan Rupees. Watching sunset is a surreal experience, so please go in the afternoon. You will surely love the place, greenery and water bodies in the surrounding area.

Title: Pilgrimage Site
Text: This cultural site holds significant Buddhism history in Sri Lanka. It is a Buddhism Pilgrimage site where is believed that Buddhist monks met up with the King as far back as 300BC and the Buddhism was inaugurated in Sri Lanka. Foreigners fee of LKR1,000 per person per entry. It took us about 30 mins to walk up the staircase to the site with some notable ruins. There are 3 other sites which include the access to the massive white stupa, a massive Buddha statue and clim-up to the top of the rock which provides stunning panoramic views. The climb up to the rock is not so straight forward for people afraid of height since it is not easy to climb up bare footed even most of the path is built with railing as some part are quite steep and much precaution is required. Proper dressing is necessary to cover shoulder and pants/ dress below knee with no shoes allowed at the site. It is easier to visit during morning or late afternoon when the ground is not too hot for the bare foot walking. Recommended for anyone into cultural/ historical sites in Anuradhapura.

Title: Nice views
Text: Good spot to visit at sunset. The view from the stupa is lovely. There is also a second lookout and a giant Buddha to see.

Title: Interesting site-- ancient hospital and more
Text: there is an ancient hospital here, a small museum, and a few monastery compounds (if I remember correctly), and then there is Kaludiya pond which is a beautiful place to relax and enjoy nature (there are also ancient structures here too).

Title: Great trip out from Anuradhapura
Text:
Great experience. Lots of history to explore as well as climbing up to the temple area which is still a holy site for Buddhists today.  Nice to see active pilgrims still enjoying this famous and historical site for family devotions and enjoyable days out

Make sure you explore the whole site and dont just visit the top temple part

The ancient hospital is fascinating. Dont miss the medication bath by the entrance

Title: GREAT LORE AND GREAT VIEWS
Text: East of Anuradhapura, this fabled site was where Mahinda, a relative of Ashoka, the Buddhist ruler of India, met the local king Devanampiya Tissa in 247 BC. After the latter successfully answered the riddle of the mangoes, Mahinda provided teachings of the Buddha. The setting is rugged, quite apart from the 1,850 possible steps to be climbed to see everything. The upper terrace has the most important areas associated with the site, a small dagoba or stupa marking the spot of the meeting. The higher up Mahaseya Dagoba reputedly holds a single hair of the Buddha. There are great views from this level and also the Aradhana Gala, a rock face with iron railings, the location of Mahindas first sermon. The upper terrace needs to be done barefoot and without a hat. It will be worth your while.

Title: Historic, But Not Much Else. Great Views.
Text: Yes, historic (where Buddhism has first established in Sri Lanka) but there is not much to see. Nice views from the modern Buddha statue, from the main stupa, and from The Rock, but be prepared for much uneven climbing (especially to The Rock) in bare feet. Now, The Rock is where a monk first called upon the deity when Buddhism became established in the country, but its just a big rock on an uneven, steep rock outcrop. If that excites you, great. Really a bit underwhelming, though the historical importance cannot be denied. No fun in bad weather.

Title: I wish I had the opportunity to visit
Text: After a wonderful experience at Sri Maha Bodhi, we arrived in Mihintale to walk around the stupa. We walked up to the second landing, where we were accosted by the rudest people we have ever come across. After accusing us of not paying the entrance fee, we walked over to a hidden demountable ticket office to pay the fee. However, when we were vilified for being white, we decided not to stay. There is no fee for non-white people at this place and the touts are extraordinarily rude. However, if our driver had warned us about the wannabe guides, we may not have had these problems.

Title: Worth a visit to Mihintale
Text:
We have been to Mihintale in a evening around 4 pm, we believe it is the great time to climb the rock, not too hot and nice wind blowing through you. Absolutely amazing view from the top. Also the feeling you get around is so spiritual. 
Mihintale is about 13Km far from the city. But do not miss this place if you are panning your trip to Anuradhapura.

Title: Ancient city of Mihinthale
Text: Lovely look around the old city easy to drive around. Great ruins and amazing rock to climb up very steep.

Title: Feel the spirit
Text: What a beatiful temple after a bit of climbing. I feel all of the spirit in my brain and heart. Greeneries,views was awesome , ?t worths to climb without shoes

Title: Views are amazing!
Text: Easy to navigate. We went here very early in the morning from Colombo. We arrived at 3am and were not allowed yet to go up so we went back at 5am. Sunrise view is amazing. We spent more than an hour just appreciating the views.

Title: Excellent
Text: Superb ambience all around, with Lord Buddha gracing the place with his presence everywhere. Serene, beautiful.

Title: Stunning vistas and fun climb on crowded rock
Text: Easy to navigate the vast site, the temples themselves are not that impressive the panorama is - the rock is fun although tedious to climb, the best being the remote summit

Title: Please help me thank again the men at the shoe rack area!
Text:
Two uncles at the shoe-keeping area had noticed that my sandals were spoilt though I merely left them at the shoe rack, and when I headed down, I saw they were trying their best to fix it (it is hard, as I'd tried for myself..) . SUPER THANKFUL FOR THE LOVELY TOUCH and this was the most heartening part of my whole trip. :)))) Bless and lots of gratitude for you guys!

Location: Superb view at the highest point, do climb up the place where there hoardings for you to hold, it is very worth it. Beware of monkeys ;)

Title: With Sweet Home Special Tour
Text: We did this with Sweet Home Special Tour. It was amazing. And we were able to visit some hidden places there.

Title: Nice site close to Anuradhapura
Text: Nice to visit because close to Anuradhapura but I would not go out of my way to visit here. Nice view from the top though

Title: nothing special
Text: don't waste your time. archeologically its nothing special. so rather spend your time in Kandy nuwera eliya or other nicer places

Title: Worth a visit
Text: It is a Buddhist temple located at an elevated area with a lot of fauna and flora around. The place is quite and less crowded than sigiriya rock. To reach the temple you need to climb a decent amount of steps. Prior entering the temple compound one is required to remove shoes.  With in the temple compound there is a small climb to reach the top of the rock, you get a good view of the surroundings from this point. a pair of socks is advisable with in the temple Complex as the area is covered with sand and gravel. Visit this temple either early morning or in the evening as it becomes hot during the day. Temple has a entry fee of 500 LKR. If you are visiting Anuradhapura, then this should be visited.

Title: Better than Anuradhapura!
Text: Easy to access by local bus. 500 entrance  rupees fee for adults. Compact site. Loads of monkeys. Lots of stairs.

Title: AWESOME!!!
Text: We planned to stop at Mihintale on the way back from Anuradhapura to Sigiriya. An absolutely amazing place. Three separate climbs with amazing views. Worth making the trip

Title: A Rock with a View
Text:
Our guesthouse Amsterdam Tourist Rest arranged our visit to Mihintale. It cost LKR 2500 for the tuk tuk and an entrance of LKR 1000 for the two of us. 
I believe there are 1800 steps from the bottom (you have to take your shoes off at the final ascent - worth having a pair of socks as some of the area is rough gravel) but there is a car park at a higher level which reduces your climb. We started at the bottom and made the climb it takes you to a wonderful 360°view point at the top. The best time to go is late afternoon when you can watch the sunset.

Title: Fabulous, historic site
Text:
If you're interested in Buddhism and/or the history of Sri Lanka, this is a must visit. This is the place where Buddhism is said to have arrived on the island. There's a steep climb, much of which without proper steps to the top of the rock. it's not too difficult a climb but you have to be in reasonable shape to attempt it. The views from the top of the surrounding area are spectacular and well worth the climb. I recommend wearing socks for this site - I don't usually and wish I had!

Mihintale often isn't offered on tours as it's away from the main Anuradhapura site. Keep this in mind when on tours and ask to visit if you want to include a visit to the site.

Title: Incredible views
Text: Worth the walk up! Beautiful temple and Buddha statue at the top. A bit scary with the unstable walking and bridges but incredible sunset!

Title: Stunning place to visit
Text:
There are three distinct places to visit all from a central area. The assembly hall and the Giant Buddha statue are the best but the climb to the other, a large rock outcrop provides great views.
There are hundreds of steps to each and it is up and back down before going up again!

Title: Don't miss the Black Lake!
Text: There are a lot of temples to see in and around Anuradhapura, but this one is not to be missed. This had some of the most interesting historical structures for me, and the Black Lake and the monastery ruins there...what a special place. It's not crawling with tourists either, in the way that Sigiriya (also 100% un-skip-able) is.

Title: Must do
Text: I would suggest strongly doing this - catch the bus and walk up to the temples. Don't forget the Black Lake after!! Also use a guide for doing this otherwise it is useless

Title: Amazing views
