Text: The view from the top of this place is amazing. Our driver took us half the way and there was a small climb with stairs to the plateau. Climbing up the rock was quit difficult and slippery but a must if you have the fitness. The view from the top is very nice.

Title: Definitely worth a trip
Text: Take the option of getting a taxi to the half way point. The remaining steps to the top are tough enough. The sites at the height of the complex are good in a simplistic way and worth the effort of getting there

Title: Wonderful ruins
Text: Enjoyed our trip this morning. A relatively challenging climb to the main area. One of our kids has a knee problem at the moment  but she managed to get to the top albeit more slowly than usual. We took a tuktuk from our hotel with a guide. I recommend going early before it gets too hot - we were there by 9.

Title: A must visit place
Text: This is the place where Sinhalese people believe that the King Tissa was met by the enlightened priest Mihindu and convert him to Buddhism and the spreading of the religion started from here. So they consider this place as the birth place of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Please remember to wear decent clothing when you visit this place otherwise you wont be allowed to enter by the huge number of security personal stationed at the premises.

Title: Better and cheaper than Anuradhapura
Text:
We went there and back by tuktuk from our guest house in Anuradhapura for LKR 2,000. We visited the dark pool area first then onto Mihintale where we were pestered by guides but pleased we decided not to use one entrance fee at LKR 500 was very reasonable compared to Anuradhapura.
The site is a lot more compact than Anuradhapura (which we were disappointed with and felt not worth the entrance fee). We thoroughly enjoyed this area and with the benefit of hindsight would have just visited this site

Title: Rich history and beautiful view
Text:
After our driver/guide dropped us here, he handed us to an other tour guide, Mr O.V. Athula Wansa. Mr Wansa was one of the best tour guides we met in Sri Lanka. He gave detailed information and historical backgrounds about the remains, the Buddhism, and even the plants. We had a pleasant little walk up to the hill and enjoyed the amazing view. 

Mr Wansa does not have an E-mail, but you can reach him by phone: +94(0)766938585. He is a certified tour guide and is passionate to his job.

We were quite surprised to found out that the fee to these on-site tour guides was NOT included in our payment to the driver/guide. We almost left Mintale without tipping Mr Wansa. I would be happy if our driver informed us about the payment first. Other than that, this tour was awesome and we learned a lot too.

Title: Nice place
Text: The main advantage of Mihintale is that the place is compact, so the visit is easy to do (even when it is really hot). The entry fee is cheap, but the guides aren't. All the upper part (the biggest part) has to be done bare feet and without a hat, so it is a good activity to do on a cloudy day.

Title: Well worth the climb, not too taxing
Text: We stopped off on the way through and are pleased that we did. Check the weather forecast, especially in the shoulder season - definitely carry a small umbrella or some waterproofs. If youre feeling energetic, and the other hills havent take it out of  can climb both stupa and rock, to get photos OF both, FROM both.

Title: Poson mihinthale
Text: I visit every year in poson season with my family.very beautiful and nice place.mihindu thero came to this place and he met dewanampiyathissa king in this place. Mihinthale rock is very nice.you can see everywhere in the city when you climb the rock.very good place for everyone.tourists people are mostly like to climb this place .we also like.we are celebrate the poson festival in mihinthale

Title: Temple visit
Text: When you like ancient citys its great . Its hot so take socks for your feet. And take care of the monkeys they love the flowers people are carrying with them.

Title: No miss
Text: If you are in Anuradhapura please as maxium time better spending your time seeing all archeological sites.

Title: Great half day trip
Text: We rented a tuktuk for 2000 rupees from our guesthouse the day we arrived. The driver was also an excellent guide who explained the different ruines. In Mihintale you can walk up the 1800 stairs to the temple but we chose not to do this because it was too hot. Instead the driver drove us to the different sites. Entrance fee is 500 rupees to visit the temples and was worth the money not like the entrance fee of anuradhapura (3750 rupees). The view on top of the big rock was just exceptional.

Title: A must
Text: Very interssting, nice view from the top. Don't miss walking all up the staircase from the very beginning. I guess: avoid the crowded festival in June. As we walked the staircase an early morning in October we were totally alone.

Title: Nice sunset!
Text: Drove from Anarhadapura to the mihintale with a tuk tuk for 1500 rupees. Had a lot of time to see the Buddha Statue, climb a viewing point (both people (of which many locals) climbing the mountain need to share the small "natural stairs" with those on their at back, but it all happens very peaceful and respectful, great experience!) and sat down at the stupa to see the sunset.

Title: Wonderful!
Text: This was a wonderful place to visit. Steeped in history, religion and surrounded by stunning scenery. We very much enjoyed this visit and would definitely visit again if we return to Sri Lanka.

Title: Absolute must see
Text: Beautiful scenery! Not many tourists so really peaceful. Very special experience indeed. We met a buddha monk who let us see where he lived and meditated which made the experience really unforgetable.

Title: Don't skip this experience
Text: This  mountain peak is a pilgrimage iste near Anuradhapura. There are not much tourists but you see many locals.You nead to climb a lot of steps to get near the area of the rock. At a certain point you have to take off your shoes as this is a holy area.So it is wise to have extra pair of socks with you. I can say from our experince that the best visiting time is late afternoon towards sunset because there is a magnificent sunset. We didnt climb the rock itself  because we didn't feel safe with socks, but the locals were climbing with barefeet even with newborn babies on their laps.However we climed the stairs to the Stupa on the opposite side of the rock.

Title: Worth the 1800+ steps to get to the top
Text:
A tranquil and beautiful place with 360 views of the countryside at the top. 
500 rupee entry fee.
From Anuradhapura it will cost you about 1500 rupee return by tuk tuk including driver waiting for you for the sunset in the late afternoon.
The hardest part of the walk is the small pebbles on the way for people with soft feet.
Keep going it's worth it.

Title: Must go
Text: This is the place where Buddhism first arrived in Sri Lanka. Worth climbing up to see the stupa and the Buddha statue. The rock however gets really busy with the queue especially during school holidays. A small entrance fee but get ready to walk a fair way without your shoes. Enjoy the view at the top.

Title: Unique experience
Text: We were lucky to be here during the long xmass weekend and experience first hand  the pilgrimage of Sri lankans at this special and peaceful place.

Title: spiritual place besides the main tourist route
Text: Mihintale is definately a spot to be visited once you are in Sri Lanka. It is by far not so crowded as Anuradhapura or Pollunaruwa. walk up and enjoy the peace.

Title: Worth a visit if in Anuradhapura
Text: This is a sacred place for people who follow Buddhism. It's considered that King Ashok's son and daughter came here and preached Buddhism . There are ruins which date back a couple of thousand years back. The view from top is quite nice. Found a couple of old ladies going all the way up to the hill top. The climb to the top isn't an easy one. And risky if it rains. Overall nice experience. We took a guide too who narrates us stories.

Title: Sacred City
Text: Take a tuk tuk around. This gives you great access with plenty to see. You need at least a full day.

Title: Beauty spot and spiritual sight
Text: Mihintale is a spiritual place of deep significance to Buddhists and Sri Lankans. As well as a large stupa, there is a smaller, more decorated one around which ceremonies are performed, and a monumental Buddha statue. I would recommend travelling here late in the afternoon once the heat of midday has reduced, as there's quite a long ascent to the top of the hill (and you don't want scorched feet at the top!); plus there seems to be more activity and ceremony in the early evening so it's a nice place to chill out and soak in the atmosphere.

Title: A mad climb.
Text:
The object of the exercise is to climb to the top of this bare rock to admire the view. Footholds are non-existent for large parts of the climb and handholds shakey at best. All this in bare feet and under a baking sun - I'm still not sure why we did it.
The view from the top is great though and there is a certain camaraderie that builds up with your fellow climbers even when there is no common language.

Title: Breathtaking view
Text: This Buddhist religious place should be on everyone itinerary to North Central Sri Lanka. It is the location of introduction of Buddhism to the island nation over two thousand years ago.

Title: Nice visit, beautiful view
Text: From Anuradhapura, we went by bus to Mihinthale. It was recommended by our hotelowner and it did not disappoint. We did not take the steps right away, but went right and then left on the main road. After 150m we went left again to get to the stairs that lead to the temple. (We should have continued another 250m on the main road to visit the black water pond). Before you get to the temple there are some ruins that are interesting. On top you can see the budda, the temple and a nice view from the rock. It recommended that you take some socks with you because the rock can be very hot and you will have to walk without shoes or slippers.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: We went there in November 2016 enjoyed every minute there. There is quite a lot of climbing but then you get rewarded with an amazing view over Anuradhapura and a huge Buddha statue. On our visit there was not so much to see because of the fog but I believe when it's really clearly that the view must be even more amazing!

Title: good view after climbing
Text: Nothing spectacular, but the way to the place with massive stair cases and monkeys around are spectacular. Also, once climbed you can see spectacular surrounding with lush gardens, lakes and sthupas around.

Title: wear socks!
Text: this is a bustling but at times very tranquil and peaceful place.  the light can be amazing and the large viewing rock isn't great if you don't like heights are a stickler for health and safety and don't like crowds.  even if you are a stickler for health and safety just avoid the big rock and enjoy the rest of the site - ooh and the socks is for the gravel and the, at times, heat underfoot as no shoes can be worn.  we took socks with us after out first temple visit and they really do make everything more pleasant without shoes and it is perfectly acceptable.

Title: Great temple and view with a bit of wildlife
Text: my driver recommended me to visit it at this time of the afternoon to avoid the midday heat. The Stairway is a series of flights, 1843 ancient granite slab steps lead majestically up the hillside. On the second landing I took on the services of a guide (Rs 1000), it is also where the monks refectory is located with huge stone troughs that the lay followers kept filled with rice for the monks. Nearby, at a place identified as the mon¬asterys relic house, are two inscribed stone slabs erected during the reign of King Ma¬hinda IV. The final steep stairway, lined with frangipani trees, leads to the place where Mahinda and the king met. The Am¬basthale Dagoba is built over the spot where Mahinda stood. The bodhi tree to the left of the base of the steps is said to be one of the oldest surviving ones. From here there is a fantastic view over the lakes and trees to Anuradhapu¬ra, a horizon studded with the domes and spikes of all the massive dagobas. The guide did prove valuable as he had to race back up the steps to retrieve my camera that I had left on a bench whilst putting my sandals back on. There were also plenty of resident Macquae Monkeys, Langur Monkeys and a lone giant squirrel.

Title: Amazing. Loved it
Text: Not really a lot I can add other than worth taking a guide, lots of history you won't get otherwise. Very quiet for tourists and lots and lots of locals. We became a bit of an attraction with local kids with them photo bombing us. They were so friendly. Summed up Sri Lanka for us. The views are just amazing, have I said amazing enough. 500 steps up, be warned but old locals doing do no excuses.

Title: Very beautiful
Text:
We visited this place in the afternoon. Around 4 pm is the recommended time because of the heat. You have to walk on your socks or bare feet and the stones and sand can be very hot. 
We had a guide and he explained everything very well. We also visited some secret hidden spots. The sunset is also very nice to. Overall a beautiful attraction!

Title: 1,600+ steps
Text: Good temples some interesting sites the old hospital is thought provoking a lot of steps to some amazing views back to Anuradhapura and other directions

Title: Nice Sunset
Text: This is only place where you can see clear sunset in Anuradhapura. But it is 18Km away from Milano Hotel.

Title: A sunset to remember
Text: Went here to admire the three temples & sunset. It was a good workout but worth it. We went by tuk tuk.

Title: Beautiful Buddhism
Text: Have been here before and had to see it again. An amazing place. Amazing views, Buddha and large Dagoba. The large stairway leading up to the site is magnificent. A must see.

Title: Dam hot
Text: We should have thought more but schedule was tight so out in the midday sun! It's hot. Get a guide and hear about monks life's and the beginning of Buddhism. Truly beautiful spot . A couple of hours here to ponder and climb stairs

Title: Must see!
Text: I think it was best place in Anuradhapura actually. It was a little bit tiring to reach the peak as there are many stairs (and we did it around 1pm when temperature was extremely hot) but it was worth it as the views are stunning and we learnt a lot about Buddhism. We went with local guide which was talking really interestingly and showing us little things that possibly would be missed but at the end he wasn't very happy about tip we gave him and was trying to make us feel guilty about it what kinda ruined my first feelings about the trip.

Title: Amazing place
Text:
We are fascinated by the history/legend of this place. It is a significant place for Sri Lanka Buddhism. The stairs were easy as they were not high or large. 

When nearer the landing (Ambasthala Dagaba) - that leads to Stupa, Buddha and Aradhana Gala), you have to deposit your shoes (tip them Rs25 after you collect your shoes when you completed your visit)

From landing onward, no shoes and attire must cover below knee.

There were some steps toward Maha Stupa. The view from the Maha Stupa is beautiful. 

The steps up the Aradhana Gala is alittle more challenging as they aren't well formed steps. Some steps were created out of carves into the boulder. However it isn't a long way up. I didn't manage to take photos as i had to keep my hands on railing as it was so windy.

Overall it is a well worth visit, especially if you read about the story behind it.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Definitely worth a stop, the rock was a little treacherous to climb as it is was quite busy but added to the fun of it and the view from the top was certainly worth it

Title: Historical site with great view
Text: This site can be visited after / together Anaradhapura site . It is a very historical site as it is where Buddhism began in Sri Lanka . Get a guide to explain you all the history and details about how the monks lived up there . Do not miss to climb up to the rock where the view is amazing !

Title: Interesting
Text: Plenty of history , ruins and steps. Please take out the modern street lighting - it completely spoils the feeling of this ancient city

Title: Beware guides
Text:
Interesting enough but it seems to be a magnet for guides who won't take "no" for an answer.When you arrive,they appear by the car and ,even if told that they are neither wanted follow you around the site,supply the odd snippet of information and then look doleful and offended if not paid once back at the car,regardless of the fact that they were told they were not needed,earlier .This appears to be their MO
In other respects,the site has a high admission fee and,whilst interesting,appears over stated.

Title: A Must Visit Temple...
Text: A Must Visit Ancient Buddhist Stupa. The Ruwanwelisaya is a stupa and a hemispherical structure containing relics, in Sri Lanka, considered sacred to many Buddhists all over the world.

Title: You have to, but don't expect too much
Text: You cannot visit Anuradapura without going to this Dagoba, but expect a lot of people and an all renewed religious monument. Gives a good vibe of the Buddhist religious life but it was not on the top 10 of our places to visit.

Title: Numinous!!
Text:
If you visit this beautiful stupa please do in the morning or the evening time. 
It is really peaceful and pretty! You will need to dress and behave respectful. Pictures are allowed.

Title: Second stupa in our tour
Text:
This is the most sacred of stupa in Anuradhapura. The stupa was built to honour the goddess. To build the stupa her house was cleared. 
A stupa is an architectural monument that does a part of the monastery. It is a memorial for the dead. The dead were great beings like the Buddha or sages who had gained nirvana. This stupa is from the great monastery. The maha vihara monastery is the first in Sri Lanka and the largest with about 3000 monks in 5 th century CE.
It is amazing piece of architecture and its brilliance is still obvious when visiting. One must wear white as a sign of respect and long dresses and no shoulders are considered respectful.

Title: Spiritual well-being
Text: Ruwanmeliseya is a pinnacle of Buddhist places of worship. The reason we visited Anuradhapura was to visit these places of worship including Sri Maha Bodhi. Anuradhapura was the fist capital of Sri Lanka. These religious monuments speak to the spiritual well being of ancient Sinhalese people. Ruwanmeliseya has a very close affinity to Lord Buddha. We spent time meditating in the late afternoon it was so peaceful and relaxing with spiritual nourishment.

Title: Bright White
Text: Big and shiny. Super white stupa. Apparently the stupas get painted yearly! Free entry. Well worth a visit. Shoulders and knees need to be covered, no shoes.

Title: A sacred site and worth a visit.
Text: This is a must see as it has one of the most sacred places to visit in the country.   Although it was busy when we visited the visit  was worth it.The Ruwanwelisaya stupa apparently contains a handful of Buddhas relics.

Title: Visit Sacred Site
Text:
One of the most ancient sacred places to visit!
No matter what religion you are one must visit Ruwanwelisaya stupa which holds handful of Buddhas relics.

Title: Most serene place on earth
Text: We did puja its best puja we have done it was amazing place must visit if you travel to srilanka it takes 3/4 hrs from Colombo if possible visit during eve after sunset

Title: A great sense of Peace
Text:
If you are a history buff a Buddhist or just like the unusual this is a must. A wonder of the world it should be, this Stupe looks like its always been there the King that built this did himself proud, Also there is a sacred Bodi tree there which you must walk around 3 times they took a branch from the original Bodi tree(in India) of the first Buddha and grew this here, I myself had an unusual feeling of being in the presence of this blessed  tree and an overwhelming feeling of peace happiness and joy came over me.
Depending if your left or right handed is the way you should do your 3 laps of walking around this great spirited tree after each lap stand in front of the tree and make a prayer of your choice.

Title: Amazing place!
Text: Loved the historic tour we took, well informed guide and awesome size! Well worth a visit. Make sure you walk around at least one stupa with no socks on...

Title: One of the must sees in Anuradhapura
Text: Ruwanwelisaya is one of the major sites in Anuradhapura and doesn't charge admission unlike other Dagobas. While mostly reconstructed it is still a beautiful site, with its brilliant white dagoba at the centre making for a serene visit. There are walls decorated with elephants to admire before you reach the dagoba itself. As is the case for all other temples in Anuradhapura (and Sri Lanka) its worth taking socks so you aren't walking around completely bare foot. I was really hot underfoot in the afternoon sun even with socks on!

Title: Sacred stupa
Text:
The Ruwanwelisaya is a stupa, considered sacred to many Buddhists all over the world. The stupa was a ruin in the 19th century and, after a fundraising campaign, was renovated in the early 20th century.

Anuradhapura was the first historical capital of Sri Lanka and today is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the Cultural Triangle), often on the touristic routes. 

Dating back to 380AD, the site contains ancient ruins, dagobas and temples, all "contained" in an archaeological park.
You will need to organise transport to explore them as I think there is simply too much distance to cover by foot. 
The most common options are either by tuk tuk or by bicycle.

In my opinion, in general, the whole site is pretty disappointing. 
As the country has better attractions (i.e.Polonnaruwa), I would visit Anuradhapura only in case you have some spare time (and an extra budget).
Unfortunately, not worth it from my point of view

USEFUL INFO
Entry ticket to the site: 25,00 USD per person (only cash)
Journey time from Sigiriya by tuk tuk: around 1h30mins

PRO TIP
Since it is a religious site still in use today, please bear in mind that everybody is asked to dress properly (shoulders and knees must be covered, and shoes and hats must be removed).
Because of the latter, I highly suggest to carry also a pair of socks into your bag as sometimes the ground can be very warm/hot.

Title: Beautiful
Text: I did all the temples in one day, theyre all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

Title: Largest Dagabo in Sri Lanka

Title: Significant Buddha temple
Text: Sited at the historical centre of the Ancient City, part of the Mahavihara Monastery site, this enormous dagoba/sthupa is one of the Buddhists most spiritual Temples. There were thousands of Monks here in its day.

Title: The main Stupa of the ancient city of Anuradhapura
Text: This is a very tall and large brick structure built about 2300 years ago and it has been restored during the 20th century since it is considered as one of the most sacred places visited by the Buddhists of Sri Lanka.  When lit in the night, it is a wonderful scenery and many feel like spending one to two hours    just relaxing at this very nicely kept place completed with large granite blocks.  It is a location that shall not be missed by any visitor to see the historical monuments of the ancient city of Sri Lanka that remained as the Capital City of Sri Lanka for nearly 1500 years.

Text:
We went here a friday of the full moon, we didn't know that it was a public holiday, and it was crowded! Crazy amount of local devotees who prayed and left offerings. Title: The Big Pagoda
Text: There are so many Pagoda in my country Thailand, but this pagoda is bigger than all of that. As being a Buddhist, I am very sensational to be here.

Title: A Sacred Marvel
Text: It is a magnormous edifice which no one can escape from seeing if one is in the sacred area of Anuradhapura. Built 140 years B.C the stupa is enshrined with sacred relics of Lord Buddha. The stupa is in a tranquil environment. The perimeter wall of the stone paved upper terrace (salapathala Maluwa) is decorated with forepart of Elephants making it a very attractive feature. Cylindrical neck "Devatha kotuwa" just above the tee cube "Hatharas kotuwa" has beautiful sculptures. The design, decorations and the structure are fascinating.

Title: Originally, two millennia old, but looks  to be regularly maintained and recently embellished
Text:
This huge white stupa is another place of active Buddhist worship, though less busy than Sri Maha Bodhi. Its construction is said to have begun over 2,000 years ago, but from its well-maintained look, much of it may be of more recent origin. It is characterised by a parade of elephants carved in relief all around the base of the stupa. As a place of worship, shoes have to be removed to enter the area.

Ruwanwelisaya is usually listed as among the sights of Sacred City/Ancient Ruins park, but it lies outside the paid area, in other words, entry is free. From here it is a short walk southwards to the ruins of Lovamahapaya Brazen Palace (nothing much to see, free) and further south, to Sri Maha Bodhi, the chief Buddhist site in the area (also free).

General info about places in the Sacred City/Ancient Ruins park: The sights are quite spread out such that while walking from one sight to the second may be possible, covering many more on foot is impractical. Youll need a map and a bicycle or a tuktuk hired for the day. Also, there few toilets, and few places to buy drinking water. Be prepared.

Title: It's A Landmark Thing
Text:
When you set aside religion and look at these ancient sights as landmarks to this area and to the country.  As a tourist they are worth a visit as much as you would visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris and the Statue of Liberty in New York etc, etc.

There is something to get from visiting them.  Something to feel and understand.  It is the feeling of the heat of the paved slabs or rock steps under your feet and an appreciation and understanding forming of what worship is like for these people here.  It is the physical exertion on your body to reach the highest point.  It is the tranquility of the landscape that these sights are built around.  It is the bewilderment of the age of the relics and the size in which some have been made.  It is the sights of monkeys behaving like this is their home.  It is the noise of traditional music as an organ may be playing if you were to visit a Cathedral.  It is the gentle murmurs of worship coming from peoples prayers.  It is the shade of the tree whether it be regarded as holy or not.  It is the smell of incense and the sight of flowers given as a gift.  It is the welcoming smiles of the Sri Lankan people who are happy to include you here regardless of your religion.

It is something you do and recommend you do when you are visiting another country.

Text:
As many attractions in Anuradhapura, this would be of great interest to anyone who likes his/her history, archaeology and folklore.

Title: The Magnificent Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba
Text:
A monument worth seeing. An important pilgrim place for Buddhists. Said to have been built in 140 BC by the king   Dutugemunu  whose statue can be seen the complex. Also we can see the statue of Sangamithra, daughter of King Asoka. It was she who brought Buddhism to Srilanka.. A huge dome is awesome. Surrounding the dome there are many Buddha  shrines. 
There is a big parking space and many shops selling flowers to offer .

Title: Best time is going early evening...
Text: Very quiet and calm time is late afternoon. Did not like high price for tourist .  Three type of ticket is make you uncomfortable.

Title: Hard to justify 25USD entrance fee
Text:
To visit the ancient Anuradhapura city it will cost you 25USD (for Sri Maha Bodhi Temple there are additional 200LRK + "donation" for the place where they store shoes that you have to take off before entering the dagoba). I find the entrance fee heavily  overprices for what it is. The Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba is just one of many historical sites scattered across many km2. When buying the ticket (which is at quite some random place) you get basically nothing. No map/no brochure nothing. So unless you do home work on how to visit the place/what to see you will have to hire a guide (so additional cost). If you do not have a driver there will be also an additional cost to hire a transportation as well as the area can not be seen on foot.
The Anuradhapura has few pagodas (dagobas) which are in general well preserved (looking very similar) and then tons on badly preserved buildings (only things what is left over are some brinks showing the outline of the buildings) and this is basically it. Few sites will have some basic information about the site. There is also an museum which is like 2 or 3 rooms with few artifacts that one can see in like 10min. If you are on the budget/time constrains I would skip this place all together and just visit Polonnaruwa as I think it is more to see/better preserved sites and just a better value for the 25USD that you will pay for Polonnaruwa as well.

Title: Monkeys as well

Title: Beautiful at Sunset
Text:
This was really amazing to see in the late evening until the sun went down. There is a temple not far from this area which is connected with a walking area.

The temple was beautiful. I really felt apart of the local people when I visited. The scent of the oils as well as the various incense they burn is truly amazing.

The smells constantly change and as you walk around every smell is unique and special.

The locals were very pleasant. They shared their flowers with me and showed me how to pray.

Prayer here happens everyday, three times a day (3am/ 12pm - noon/ 6pm). These times could vary so asking the locals is best.

Side note. Given this is a religious area I did not feel comfortable taking many pictures. 

Also, there are a lot of fruit bats when the sun starts to set so you will hear them, see them and will find pits falling from the sky as you walk around.

Title: One of the most sacred places in Sri Lanka
Text:
I visit here normally 4-6 time an year. It was built by King Dutugemunu c. 140 B.C., who became lord of all Sri Lanka after a war in which the Chola King Elara, was defeated. It is also known as Mahathupa, Swarnamali Chaitya, Suvarnamali Mahaceti (in Pali) and Rathnamali Dagaba. The stupa is one of the worlds tallest monuments, standing at 103 m (338 ft) and with a circumference of 290 m (951 ft).

If you get down from Anuradhapura Railway station you have can have a 20 mins walk and arrive here. But also you can get a tuk tuk also. It can be expensive for foreigners, make sure you negotiate the price before starting the journey since the rate in tuk tuks aren't fixed in Sri Lanka.

Make sure you are not wearing short skirts, short trousers, tight trousers, sleeveless tops, tank tops etc. Also don't wear hats, caps or any kind of slippers since this is a very sacred  place for Buddhists. It can be hot in day time. Make sure you are wearing socks or else it will be really hard walk. Don't turn your back to stupa when taking pics. 

It will be really beautiful at night with the lights on as you can see in the pictures. in Poya days it can be crowded.

Title: Amazing dagoba in use!
Text: This place is magical, you can sense the power of spirituality as you walk counterclockwise(!) around this massive dome. There are many locals around all dressed in white. If you can it's best to also wear white as a sign of respect. Go here early in the morning. Around 7:30 you will have the best experience. Take a moment to sit in the shade cast by this ancient monument and let your thoughts pass by. It isn't the same as Bagan or Angkor Wat, but it gets pretty close!

Text:

Title: A memorable visit.
Text:
We visited this historic stupa as part of our tour of Sri Lanka,and yes, it is a very sacred place for Buddhists and well worth a visit. We were there on the day the Bodhi tree - a very ancient tree -  was celebrating an anniversary and there were hundreds of pilgrims dressed in white and bringing gifts of flowers. A very memorable visit.
Appropriate dress for all Buddhist temples includes no hats or shoes.We were asked to wear long trousers, but as it's very hot and you're often travelling elsewhere, I would say that zip off trousers for men are really useful. Ladies - knees must be covered , crops were fine and some other tourists wore a sarong to cover their shorts whilst visiting. Another reviewer has mentioned the heat of the paving you have to walk on with bare feet.We were there late morning and the paving  ( and there's a lot of it!) was red hot - so hot that we were hopping from one foot to another trying to avoid burning our feet. Little trainer socks are invaluable!! It's quite acceptable to wear them and your feet don't burn. All stupas / temples require shoes to be removed (there's always someone to look after them for you for a very small sum) but some are surrounded by large gritty areas and those little socks are great!
It's a wonderful country - so many great sights and lovely people!

Text:
If you're a Buddhist this is a must see place in Sri Lanka.  Sometimes it becomes crowded.  If you are looking for quietness during the visit better to go early morning.  That will allow you to meditate without disturbances.  
Amazing and huge stupa in a place with very good 'vibrations' (or quieted vibrations)

Text: Beautiful place, you should definitely visit if you are in SL. Because everything is located so far from each other, we used a tuktuk.

Text: very interesting place , nice helpful people , so many tourists were visiting the place but we didnt feel it is crowded

Title: Beautiful stupa

Title: Super Stupas
Text:
This is a general review of the whole of Anuradhapura.  If you are going to Anuradhapura it is highly unlikely that you will just go to see just one of the many attractions there.
This is an interesting place to visit for those interested in history and culture.  It covers the ruins of a vast Buddhist monastic city.
There are gigantic stupas the size of Egyptian pyramids, which contain holy Buddhist relics and an incredible irrigation system that are both nearly 2000 years old.
Also to be visited on the site is the Sri Maha Bohdi  apparently one of the worlds oldest and most revered trees.
It is probably worth retaining the services of an official guide, such is the complexity of the history and scale of the site.  We attended on a Sunday which due to the sites highly religious importance meant it was very crowded with pilgrims.  From a cultural point of view this was fascinating, but those interested in the history of the place might find a less busy, mid-week visit, more rewarding.  Whenever you choose, Anuradhapura is certainly worth seeing.

Title: The place to be after sunset
Text: First of all: It's free because outside the temple complex. Second: It's the best stupa and third: after sunset it's full of locals praying, lighting candles, etc. go gor it and the bodhi tree next to it as well. Don't leave Anuradhapura without the evening experience!

Title: A living Buddhist experience
Text:
This is just one Dagoba in the Anuradhapura historical site, but it is the one used by pilgrims and worshippers today.
Well worth and visit, even if not Buddhist. Beware the hot stones as you  can`t wear shoes.
We had a great guide, who was a student of Buddhism and spoke excellent English, who took us round the whole site of the ancient capital and explained it really well. Without his help the large site would have been difficult to understand.

Title: Nice stupa
Text: We visited this nice big stupa on a Sunday morning it there was a lot of people there praying and offering different things. We should take of our shoes to get inside the stupa area and the stone floor was hot because of the strong sun, it may be better if we visited earlier in the morning. Outside there were many monkeys, it was really nice to see them with there babies.

Title: Unmatchable...
Text:
Great Stupa ever of the Sinhala Buddhist history... built by great king Dutugemunu ( Dutta Gamani Abhaya).. due to it's high position also known as Maha Stupa....

A must see location of Anuradhapura sacred city...

Always crowded with Buddhist pilgrims as well as tourists ( both local and foreign)...

Better to avoid in poya days ( specially in Wesak & poson poyadays) ...

Appropriate clothes should wear to visit this sacred place...

Title: Heaven on earth
Text: We saw this temple at the height of February's Full Moon festival. The vibrations of this place were so peaceful and the devotees were so warm. everyone in our party felt the love and happiness that pervaded the atmosphere.

Title: Great stupa
Text: One of the great massive stupas around Anuradhapura, restored and still used today as a religious site.

Title: Impressive structure
Text:
We visited the Dagoba in the afternoon, since we had to catch an early train the next day. It is a very impressive structure to look at, but as many have commented, it does not looks its age, due to the regular whitewashing. 

Needless to say, it was very hot, and there's not much in the way of shade at the site, so if you can visit early or late in the day it would be a much more pleasant experience.

Bring an old pair of socks with you so your feet don't get scorched on the hot stones!

Title: A Famous Stupa Shrine
Text:
We visited Anuradhapura complex and this was the second stop on the tour. To me it was a nicer stupa although not as large nor old as the first one. The main problem is that for me, a stupa is just a stupa.

Of course it is off shoes in the grounds and it had been raining which made the ground very wet and sandy. Consequently on collecting your shoes from the attendant at 50 Rupees each it was not too pleasant putting them back on. On a hot day I fear the flagstones would be too hot to walk on with any comfort.

To conclude, I admire the way they look after their religious buildings but the high entrance fees are moy mayched by the tour which is not well presemted.

Title: Very impressive Stupa
Text: We arrived in the late afternoon to witness a buddhist procession walking around this very large stupa.

Title: Bearutiful Stupa
Text: Was amazed by the history of this place. We wandered around the base of the Stupa and saw a ceremony taking place with many pilgrims.

Title: Best stupa in Anuradhapura
Text:
I really enjoyed this stupa the best of all the stupas I visited in Anuradhapura.

I especially liked the explanation to the left before the steps. The explanation in English was on the backside of the explanation in Singhalese.

After I visited this stupa for free, I was disappointed with the ones you had to pay 3750 rupees ($25) to see.

If you need a tuk tuk driver, Prasad is excellent. For 1500 rupees, he took me to all the free sites (seven) first, then gave me the choice to pay the 3750 rupees for the entrance to the main three. I would recommend him as his English was very good and he took me to a very nice place for lunch near Jetvana which had excellent food for a reasonable price (180 rupees).

Prasad 0777648005

Text: This is one of the greatest historical Buddhist pagodas in the world if one wishes to visit and see.  The level of serenity and atmosphere is overwhelming.

Almost burnt soles of the feet and have to move around the stupa dashing into any shadows to cool off. A rectangular outside wall surrounds the Ruwanwelisaya Stupa embossed in elephants. Title: Very impressive Dagoba!

Title: Amazing
Text: See my other review about Jaya Sri Maha Bodhiya. Which is nearby. These two can be easily combined by walking.

Title: Impressive
Text: One of the big Dagobas or Stupas it is really worth to have a look  on such a high building. respect the Buddhists in surrounding it clockwise...

Title: A beautifully maintained stupa
Text: We visited this stupa on the day before Poya Day and the devotees were preparing the stupa for poya day with dressing it up with flags and cloth. This stupa we were informed is usually whitewashed every year to maintain it in its bright white state. It is definitely worth a walk around even in the heat of the day just to get a feel for how large a stupa it is. There are also many monkeys living around the stupa. The floors are clean and even for the walk around the stupa, which you must do with your shoes off and no hats or umbrellas allowed.

Title: Amazing Stupa, another must see
Text: A short walk from the sacred Sri Maha Bodhi gets you to one of the most amazing structures in the Buddhists world, built around 140 B.C. The square location sits on raised platform that is lined head-to-head of elephant heads on the outside. This is quite rare in the ancient world. The base of the stupa is wound around by cloth that seems to a recent event. While we were there, a group of pilgrims carried an endlessly long new orange cloth to be offered. This is something we have never seen before. The Temple structure with the Buddha lying down is really beautiful. Do stop by and spend time looking at a recreation of an ancient battle between the great king Dutugemunu and he Chola King Elara.

Title: Nice place to visit
Text: Visit if your a bit devotional and want to visit religious places else u may get bored as there are lots of such stupas in Anuradhapura

Title: Nice Place
Text: Visited this grand Stupa this December 2016. We actually walked from the Mahabodhi Tree place to this Stupa. The Sleeping Buddha statue outside the Stupa premises is very beautiful.

Title: Beautful Structure
Text: As expected, the this dagoba was a highlight of our time spent exploring the Anuradhapura heritage sites. It blend of historic and current Buddhist significance makes it a very special place indeed.

Title: Impressive
Text: The shear size of this stupa is impressive and worth visiting. When I visited there were many pilgrims and the women were all dressed in white. It is certainly a very active religious place but because of the renovations does not look ancient.

Title: Amazing Stupa. Beware of scams
Text:
Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba, as many others in the area is really beautiful and the fact that so many locals visit it for their prayers makes it even more interesting.

But beware of scams in the area. For Anuradhapura you need to buy a USD 25 ticket but only in few temples and museums they really check it. In the hotel I stayed in, City Centre Lodge, they offered me a tuktuk tour (they insisted it was impossible by bike). The driver took us only to the places where they never check the tickets and lied to us about the other places, saying those could only be visited from outside. I was following the map and we missed the most important ones and, as we finished by 1pm we finally had to stay one extra day (of course in a different hotel) in order to visit the main places.

When we went back to the hotel and complained about the places we hadn't visited the owner started to follow us on his car shouting and threatening.

We had a horrible experience as we felt scammed and threatened. It's a pitty this bad experience stained such a nice experience.

Title: Amazing to see
Text: The scale and size especially as it's painted white is quite something to see.  A feat of engineering especially given when these were built

Title: Very impressive site

Title: ""Late afternoon best time to go"
Text: This was a beautiful experience watching people arrive in white with their offerings, we felt very humbled to be part of the evening

Title: Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba
Text: Peaceful, beautiful, serene; enchanting when lit at dusk. The surroundings makes you feel calm and reflect on life. Time stands still and you are aware of the moment. One realises that the words of the Buddha, said more than 2500 years ago are more true today, than ever before.

Text:

It is great to visit a sight still used for its original function as a working Buddhist place if worship. But it is the sheer size and blinding white colour that takes your breath away. Go on a Sunday morning and you will see the locals carrying out their rituals such as dressing the stupa in an orange sash hundreds of metres long.
There is a real energy here that is different from the other equally beautiful sights in the ancient city.
You will have to leave your shoes at the gate for a nominal fee.

Title: Magnificent Buddha Vihara
Text:
RUWANWELISAYA DAGOBAH
Ruwanwelisaya is an awe inspiring Dagobah of magnificent architectural style, built during the reign of King Dutugemunu (140 BC). The Dagobah has circumference of 950 feet and height of 338 feet. In 19th century AD, this Dagobah was nothing more than ruins of a magnificent structure. In 20th century, it was renovated and restored with local donations and assistance from UNESCO. It is now a World Heritage Site.
A Dagobah is a sacred place of veneration. Generally it is a shrine like domed structure in which are placed relics related to Buddha, Buddhism or remains of Buddhist monks and nuns. The place is also used for meditation and worship. It is also called Stupa, Pagoda or Chedi.

Text: We saw a video in a Washington D.C. museum depicting worshipers at this stupa. It immediately went onto the bucket-list. A few months later and there we were. The experience is really one of the more unforgettable of our travels. We went on Christmas and it was full of people. There was a huge procession for a cloth long enough to wrap around the entire stupa, and scores of people chanting. Anuradhapura is not a close destination to many of the major sites, but it was well worth the 7 hours it took to get here.

Text:

You can spent a longer duration of time with your prayers and meditation.
Bear in mind when the sun has risen one might feel the heat from above & the cobbled surface.

Title: A WALK AROUND THE STUPA
Text: This bleached white structure contains relics considered sacred to Buddhists. It is one of eight places in Anuradhapura of veneration. At 103m, it is one of the tallest stupas with a circumference of 290m. You have to removed your shoes and not wear a hat when it the immediate vicinity. It is surrounded by the colourful Buddhist flag, the colours themselves acting like giant ribbons around the stupa. It is certainly worth a visit but the exterior emphasis--no relics to be seen--limited its touristic appeal. Most devotees--and frankly most tourists--were dressed in white shirts.

Title: Another stupa in a large property
Text:
We visited Ruwanwelisaya and hired a local guide (for US$20) since we wanted to get some history out of the site.  

We walked through a garden and come to the area that we had to remove our footwear and stored them with a pay.  That is part of the reason that I dislike this visit.  You have to walk with a lot of people on cobble stone paths, sand ground, marble floor and fake grass mats, along with rock chips, water and debris.  That hurt my feet and it is totally unhygienic.

In the main area, there are a few shrines with statues here and there.  The local guide took us to another stupa within the same propery. The guide took us to 2 pools and gave a brief description of the structures.  Overall he did a good job.

Text:

Title: The second most sacred place in Sri Lanka
Text:
This huge white stupa built around 150 BC is the second most sacred Buddhist centre in Sri Lanka after the Tooth Relic Temple in Kandy. What impressed an uninitiated me most, in addition to its antiquity, is the aastha (great belief and devotion is the closest I can some to in English) Sri Lankan Buddhists still have. I saw groups of devotees chanting and a couple lying prostrate and praying. 
Great place to visit, if you are a devout Buddhist. Be sure legs and arms are covered or you will not be allowed to enter.

Title: Vacation
Text: The only white plaster Stupa of the three. I believe its the tallest of the three and a very active Temple. Long pants and sleeved shirts are required and no shoes so wear socks, The ground is very hot. Oldest kingdom in Sri Lanka and worth the visit. Plan on 3/4 of a day to see all thier is to see here.

Title: Beware of tuk tuk drivers!
Text:
Mine is intended to be a general review about my trip to Anuradhapura. The archeological area to visit is really huge. You can see many beautiful stupas like Ruwanwelisaya and many other things. If you want to visit the area in the matter my suggestion is to rent a bike. If you think of walking only you are going to miss many things also because you cannot find many signs. Another way to move around is by tuk tuk. You can bargain the price and get a full service at a reasonable price. 1500 rupees is a good deal. However you need to be aware of tuk tuk drivers. I would say that 99% of tuk tuk drivers are really nice but black sheep are behind the corner. The price of the ticket to enter Anuradhapura archeological area is pretty expensive. More precisely it costs 4600 rupees. A ticket is made of three stubs that need to be torn off every time you enter one of the three areas. There are some tuk tuk drivers who might ask you to give them your ticket so that they can show it to the surveillance staff in order to enter the area. If they ask for your ticket, DO NOT give it to them. The ticket belongs to you. It doesn't belong to the tuk tuk drivers. The point is that there are some tuk tuk drivers who take their customers tickets just to show them what they want to show. They aim at ending their trip with the customers asap so that they can start a new trip with other tourists who will be sold the same tickets partly used by the previous tourists.To cut it short tuk tuk drivers resell those tickets to other tourists at a reduced price and take the money deriving from the sell. 
So be careful. I also want to give some quick information on how to arrive in Anuradhapura if you come from Dambulla.
Dambulla is a small city. There is not bus station but of course there are bus stops. The one where you can catch the bus to Anuradhapura is on Kandy road (the main road) 200 meters after the clock tower on your left next to Bata shoe shop. The bus numbers to consider are 15 and 43.
If you wanna go to Polonnaruwa from Dambulla the bus stop is the same. The bus number is either 41 or 48. 
Hope these suggestions are of help.

Title: Bustling temple
Text: This was the first dagoba we visited during our tour of the archaeological park so it caught us when we were still enthusiastic. Its a huge white plastered stupa set within a courtyard behind a perimeter wall that includes an impressive frieze of elephants. Its also clearly very much a working temple and during our visit we witnessed 4 different processions of pilgrims bringing their offerings - all very colourful and atmospheric.

Title: interesting
Text: all the sites are  very interesting. But they are widespread so it is good to have a tuk tuk or bicycle to go round

Title: Captivating
Text: We went in the evening, and it was one of the most interesting sights on our trip. So many worshipers gathered around, wrapping the stupa in prayer flags, and clouds of incense all around. 100% do an evening visit around sunset and just after.

Title: What a day to visit
Text:
Having been to Mihintale in the morning, the best was left to the afternoon. Shoes off again and we walked a long way without them, so wear thick socks as the ground is hot, although there are areas where they have laid astro which is easy to walk on. Entry was 9500 rupees which covered the different sites in Anuradhapura.

We came on a national holiday, Makarsankranti/Pongal, and thousands of buddhists from as far away as Colombo will come for the day as this is the most significant temple in Sri Lanka. It is reputedly built with 100 million bricks and the original temple was built in 140BC. Over time it has had to be rebuilt as at one time it was a ruin in the 19th century and it was rebuilt to twice the original size and completed in 1940. It is 103 metres high and 290 metres in circumference. Stupas were built to enshrine relics of Buddha

Most people were dresses in white and families were there as well. There was incense pervading the atmosphere and people were buying flowers and gifts to be left by the temple. People were praying near the temple and it was so peaceful even with so many people (not many Europeans visit here and they are really missing out).  There was a procession of people making their way to the temple and a bolt of cloth in bright red was gradually unwound as people took hold of the cloth so the cloth procession just got longer and longer as more people joined it. Just an amazing place to visit and a wonderful day.

Title: Definitely worth seeing
Text:
A fantastic site in a beautiful location.  The monument is truly monumental and it is interesting to observe the significance that this site has for sri lankan, who make pilgrimmages to it from all across the  country. 

I cannot recommend enough the guide that took us that day.  He had the best english out of all the guides we met and was extremely knowledgeable about the history of the ruins and buddhist philosophy.  I also liked that he took the time to share his knowledge without trying to rush you through the tour.  He took us on 3 1/2 hour tour through all the highlights of the ancient city at a very reasonable price of 3500 rupees. You can contact him on wasanthamapa1968@gmail.com. Name: Wasantha.

Title: Impressive
Text: A large white structure still in use as a place of worship so very colourful with lots of locals on the day we visited. A very impressive site.  As with most of Anuradhapura, signage was practically non existent with very little in the way of historical description at each monument.

Title: old stupa
Text: One of many ancient sights to see in Anuradhapura. Follow the crowds to circle the stupa. There are smaller stupas in each corner.

Title: Wonderful to see
Text: Nice to see a amazing site like this, far from the madding crowds. Try to avoid the midday sun. Barefoot visit so can be harsh on soft western feet !

Title: Massive Stupa full of vibrance and spirituality
Text:
Review from my Blog

As soon as we arrived at Ruwanweliseya, the first thing I noticed was the long line of people assisting with the wrapping of the base of the stupa once in a bright orange cloth. The next thing I notices, was the group of people working feverishly infront of the dagoba, braiding tree branches together to provide roofing for the hastily built market that lay in the parking lot at the foot of the structure...

As I got closer, I began to truly understand the length of the cloth being wrapped around the structure. Not only did this put its size in perspective, but seeing the size of the workers in comparison to this massave structure was truly awesome.

I shed my sandals and began to walk around the stupa. The ground was hot, and the rocks on the side facing the sun were like hotplates as you walked.,,

Every so often as you walked around the structure you would see small structures showcasing Buddhas. At many of these youd see entire families with cloths laid out, sitting for presumably hours and meditating en mass

When I finally finished circling I headed to the small shanty market set up infront of the temple and picked up some water.

Title: Impressive and Peaceful
Text: A massive stupa (largest in the world), it is well worth visiting when you're in Anuradhapura.  You can get impressive views from afar with as many photo ops as you want, but to truly experience this stupa you need to take off your shoes and walk around (clockwise) to get a sense of its sacred nature. You'll see a number of Buddhists praying to help you get into the proper spirit and may be fortunate enough to hear local drumming, music, chanting, etc.

Title: These ruins world class engineering marvels. Very inspiring and emanates the peace of the Buddha
Text:
Great place to visit.

However make sure you start out the visits EARLY at least by 6 AM ( before the sun gets very hot and dry ) 
Per tradition you have to leave your footwear at the entrance. By midday when the sun gets hot, so does the ground of the temple, making it extremely uncomfortably hot and blistering on bare feet despite the socks.
Take a spare pair of socks. Deck in cotton or loose comfortable clothing. The temple grounds will not allow any revealing clothing, tank tops or shorts.
 Temperatures by mid day sun reach 85- 95 Fahrenheit.

Title: A sacred temple. Dress appropriately
Text: We visited the place at around 7 pm and found the place a bit busy but extremely calming and peaceful.  Would have loved to site there for more time and absorb the atmosphere.  A great place to visit and reflect.

Title: quaint and beautiful
Text:
we were very lucky as the day in which we went to visit, there was a festive celebration and there was a lot going on, culturally.
overall the place was beautiful and majestic
quaint

Title: Awesome stupa
Text: It's white, large and magnificent.  We went on a weekend where we saw a continuous stream of people bring yarns and yarns of coloured cloth to tie around the Stupa besides lotus flowers and other offerings. There were monks all around to help.  It was quite a sight.

Title: So Big and Impressive
Text: This is a really nice place to visit. Of course, you have to take off your shoes or sandals for respect. Nice place to walk around observe everyone worshipping.

Title: A huge structure.
Text:
Firstly, if you're not used to going barefoot then avoid the middle of the day as the stones can get very hot. That said a walk around this massive structure will give an insight into what it must have taken to build this thing.
Also it's well worth a visit after dark as the illuminations are very good.

Title: Very impressive dagobah
Text: Approximately 107 meters high, shining white and very impressive stupa / Dagobah is located in Anuradhapura in the sacred city. When you enter the area, you need to take off your shoes. The wall around the Dagobah is decorated with 344 elephants reliefs.  Walk around the impressive building.

Title: Another White Dagoba
Text: This was the last place we visited on our tuk tuk tour and based on reviews we had very high expectations. There were a lot of worshipers at the site and the "foreigner shoerack" was a bit of a hassle. It is a very spiritual place. Had hoped for more.

Title: Interesting place
Text: Top of the list of attractions in the area and quite busy in the mornings. Go early because there is a lot of walking and quite a bit has to be barefoot (as it is within the Buddhist shrine). The stones get quite hot! Wear socks.

Title: Not as good as Polonnaruwa
Text:
We visited various sites in Anuradhapura during our time in Sri Lanka but it was a bit underwhelming.

It's an older site than Polonnaruwa and therefore less preserved. There is less to see and it is harder to understand it's historical significance.

My advice would be to cover legs and shoulders, to carry a handbook and to make use of a licensed guide, in order to get even a little bit out of the visit. Guides don't cost anything but a minimum tip of Rs. 500-1000 would be recommended as they're extremely knowledgable.

Title: Living religious site
Text: Nice break from other attractions were you only see ruins and rubble. This place has intensely alive with many Sri Lankan's worshipping and praying. Good place to feel everyday Buddhism among locals.

Title: Lovely place - could be better
Text:
Some of his review you will find repeated for other places in Anuradhapura as I could not write a generic one.
Firstly, for sites of relgious signigicance, no footwear, hats or bare legs/shoulders. My tips would be; if in doubt carry a wrap/sarong/shawl and a pair of socks with you as the ground can get uncomfortably hot. Beautiful glaring white building of historical significance. Read up about it before visiting as very little information is written in non Tamil or Singalese.

Title: Probably one of the biggest dagaoba
Text:
Probably one of the biggest Dagoba in Sri Lanka. Note that the floor can get very hot during the day and maybe you should consider keeping your socks while visiting.
It is really a pilgrimage place and very interesting to visit. There are also many monkeys in the park around the Dagoba.

Title: Impressive
Text: What an impressive visit we had here; if you are in Anuradaphura this is an absolute not-to-miss. Be aware that shoes are not allowed and your knees need to be covered

Title: Beautiful! Visit at sunset to get both daytime and nighttime photos! Go with a guide if possible
Text:
TIP: leave your shoes on the bus/your car so you dont need to pay for them to tend to your shoes.

- would recommend visiting this place at sunset so you can get nice daytime as well as nighttime photos. it looks impressive any hour of the day
- we didnt have a guide so were quite clueless as to the significance of the temple so try to go with one!
-an impressive, magnificent sight to behold, could be considered a wonder of the world in my books! 
- the grounds are EXPANSIVE so dont worry about it being crowded unless it is a festival day in sri lanka, do double check before you go.
- the grounds will probably be really hot in the afternoon so just bear in mind you have to walk barefoot and as i said try to visit in the late afternoon during sunset.

Title: Marvellous Stupa
Text:
Its a pilgrim site for Buddhist, i like this stupa very much. Its so majestic and serene. I went to this stupa twice already. In Srilanka its a custom to take off sandals or shoes to enter the temple area or dagoba area. Socks are allowed. resisting and be patience to the hot floor will also be part of heart training.

Must go. Do pradaksina ( walk around the dagoda 3 times).

Title: Ancient Stupa at Ancient City
Text:
A very ancient stupa and there were so many people coming to pray. You have to take off your footwears but socks are still allowed. You have to keep them at the counter and pay small donation to the keepers (maybe about LKR50 but it's up to you)
It will be extremely hot when you visit in the afternoon, it was suggested to visit in the evening because the lightings would be great.
And also there are a lot of wild/un-owned dogs around but they don't bite.

Title: The tallest stupa of the ancient city
Text: This stupa is one of the tallest monuments in the world. The outside wall is decorated with black elephants throughout the circumference of outer wall. The stupa is considered to be very scared and hence usually this place is crowded.

Title: A Magnificent Stupa in Anuradhapura Sri Lanka
Text: Built by King Dutugamunu around 200 BC. Another must visit site for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. Buddha's relics are kept here. One of the biggest Buddhist stupa's in the world.

Title: The Pagoda of King Dutu Gamunu
Text: Tallest pagoda in Sri Lanka and this was made by the Great ruler King Dutugamunu. People in Sri Lanka believe that There is Lord Buddha's relics inside this pagoda. This away from the Colombo area and it's 4-5 hours journey from the Colombo. This is very religious place in Sri Lanka. You should be here when you will be in Sri Lanka

Title: Majestic Dagoba (stupa) started in 2nd century BC
Text: Enclosed by a wall with a frieze of elephants, this enormous restored Dagoba, 180ft high, testifies to the splendour of Anuradhapura at its peak in the 9th century. It is so big that it is difficult to take a full picture once inside the surrounding walls. We were amazed to see how 7 workers on a very tall bamboo ladder clean and maintain the stupa. It can get very hot in the afternoon as there is absolutely no shade.

Title: Impressive Dagoba
Text:
Completely restored with white painted plaster, this is a memorable sight. Even more impressive are the bamboo ladders that climb to the top that the painters need to climb to work - scary.

This is probably the most important and impressive dagoba at this site and should not be missed.

Title: Very impressive, but take care when hot
Text:
This is a very impressive artefact, steeped in religious history, with a real feeling that the locals who throng to this pace really do care. It is quite a feat of engineering and manpower. 
Apparently, the manpower was essentially voluntary, with the people really involved and cared for - cf the building of the pyramids. 

A word of warning, the footpath to the main area, from where you have to go shoeless, can get hot for the pale skinned visitors. After noon, it can be VERY hot as the local administration, in its wisdom decided to convert to tiles from sand. Bad move!

Well worth a visit.

Title: Part of the Ancient City and important pilgrimage temple
Text: This stupa is huge.At the time we were there they had the men scrubbing the outside and painting.Not a job I would want.Be prepared to be amongst the throngs of the faithful which is nice.Very hot on your bare feet so maybe bring socks as we were recommended to do but didnt.Lots to see.

Title: Amazing sight
Text: A must see, impressive structure and a beautiful view! Unfortunately also a lot of tourists at this place but thats unevitable these years..

Title: Amazing
Text: The size of this structure to house a treasure is amazing, and it doesn't even have an entry that one can view the treasure. Absolutely amazing.

Title: Nothing special
Text: We came here and it was just another stupa! Nothing special to make your way here if you dont have time you can Skip it

Title: Place of Pilgrimage
Text: Our driver claimed this is the largest stupa in Asia.  I'll reserve judgement on that. But it is a place where Buddhist faithful congregate in great numbers.  You get a good sense of Sri Lankan Buddhist piety here.

Title: Awesome structure
Text: Another beautiful Dagoba on this amazing site. Walking distance from the Sri Maha Bodhi Temple.  Pictures don't do it justice. Beautiful elephant frieze round the wall base

Title: Must go place if you are a Buddhist
Text:
We go every time when we visit Sri Lanka. Place can get very busy, especially full moon days. 
A lot of worshipers come here. Get the timing correct. floor is made by granite so it gets very hot during midday.
It will take 20-30 minutes to walk around it.
Buddha's relics are kept here, Hence this is must go place for Buddhists.
Also walking distance to Sri Maha Boodhi, Bo tree.

Title: not to skip this good to visit
Text: this is largest sthupa in Anuradhapura. built by king of Buddhist time and fond it as sacred place must see Lord buddha engrave

Title: NIce
Text:
There is nothing outstanding..
Just one more stupa, except this one was white so I guess makes for a nice background in a photo

Title: Massive stupa
Text: Lovely place which gives a sense of what humans can achieve. Massive stupa. Not as crowded as some other places. Enjoyed our time there

Title: Amazing and awe inspiring
Text: There is really no way to capture the scale and the sense of awe that this Stuppa makes one feel when you are there.   There are counters to hold your shoes and its great to be able to circumambulate and earn merit.

Title: Awe inspiring
Text: Visited here in a recent tour with my wife. It was a beautiful sight - the stupa is absolutely huge and with a lot of people visiting on the day, it was incredidbly atmospheric too. Quite unlike anything I have seen before - a must-see if you are visiting the country.

Title: Large stupa
Text: This is a very large & decorated stupa in Anuradhapura. The outside of the temple is decorated with large elephants. It is still used & busy on a daily basis.

Title: 7 day Srilankan trip
Text:
was a good experience to see these types for the first time.
I think its the biggest or the second biggest of Dagoba

Title: Neat place to learn about buddhism
Text:
This was one of my first stops in Sri Lanka. 
It was neat to see so many people praying and making offerings to Buddha. It really gave me insight into Buddhism. Bring a few rupees to check your shoes if I recall correctly.

Title: Massive and Beautiful
Text:
Absolutely massive white domed stupa, perhaps one of the most impressive structures in Anaradhapura. 
You can walk around the paved circumference and admire the ornate carvings at the base, the elephant carvings in particular.
You have to take off your shoes of course but be sure to keep your socks on as the stones can be burning hot as it is totally exposed to the sun. Shorts need to be below the knees and shoulders need to be covered.
Just over 50m high, the original structure was much higher, the highest stupa in the world when first consecrated. Very, very impressive.
Go early as it is one of the most crowded sites in Anuradhapura Nd as I mentioned the heat is a factor.

Title: Strikingly peaceful
Text:
On a hot day, with burning hot pavers suggest wearing socks or keep to the white quartz stone where you can find them. You can walk at good pace though. We visited midday, so hot but not many other people around. Very peaceful and calm (if you can stand in one place for more than 30 secs. The Dagoba is beautiful and very sacred. 
Standing at the side and looking up to the clouds was fun, and made the earth sway.

Title: the buddhist destination in sri lanka
Text: and seeing all the students enjoy it added t the experience.  It can get quite warm and note that shoes and hats are not allowed in the temple vicinity.

Title: Move on!
Text: The stupas around here are big but lack any sort of atmosphere. There needs to be a lot more work to get these places into something that is interesting. Im sure it will happen over the next few years. It has lots of potential.

Title: Like any other historical place
Text: You need to have a local guide to explain you the story and take you through the right monuments during the trip.

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Loved this temple, very beautifully kept with current work happening to maintain. Very spiritual  place with many locals praying and chanting.  Very enjoyable

Title: Amazing Stupa
Text:
Totally breathtaking. This huge stupa is an incredible testimony to ancient architecture and devotion 

For me the best thing in the sacred city of Anuradhapura

Title: Nice
Text: As the stupas at Anuradhapura are all impressive, Abhayagiri Dagaba is no different! Wonderful, a real sight for the eye.

Title: Great Stupa
Text: This stupa has built by King Walagamba, in order to pay his gratitude towards the Buddhist monks. This area is considered to be carrying the secrets of Theravada Buddhism. This stupa has met-up with several disastrous situations in the past, but with the help of government and the fellow Sri Lankans, the stupa rebuilt in several years back. This Vihara area contains with a museum as well, which hinders the history of Abayagiri Stupa.

Title: Best site at Anaradhapura
Text:
Theres some scaffolding on parts of this dagoba at the moment, so youll need to find the best vantage point from which to photograph it. 
The park as a whole is a sprawling complex with ticket checkpoints all over the place. By far the best way to see it all is on a bicycle. We spent an awesome day riding through some beautiful scenery, with monuments peeking through the foliage. 
Having done Polunnaruwa earlier in our trip, we found Anaradhapura a little disappointing. If youre planning your itinerary and are unsure if you need a night or two here, I dont think you do if youre taking in the far superior park at Polunnaruwa. Its all a bit same-same here. The two big dagobas are certainly impressive but the rest of the sites arent much to write home about. The sacred bodhi tree was a let down. Really just a temple for locals. You see very little of the tree itself. 
All in all, a lovely day out cycling through rural Sri Lanka, but the day will not be remembered for the monuments.

Title: A large stupa
Text: This stupa is unusual in not having a white covering. Otherwise its layout and features are much like other stupas.  It is very large though

Title: Imposing dagoba
Text: You can't help be wowed by Abhayagiri dagoba, with its tranquil woodland setting, its history and the huge stupa. But there's more to Abhayagiri Dagoba than its sheer size - there are a few carvings, and moonstones and a few other relics around. A walk around the base of the dagoba is a must to really appreciate its size (wearing socks as the ground is so hot). A must see in Anuradhapure and included in the cultural ticket. A visit by bike is highly recommended.

Title: The site I liked the most in Anuradhapura
Text:
Focal points of the Abhayagiry complex is an ancient stupa, the Abhayagiri Dagaba, which was the original custodian of the Tooth relic in the country (today in Kandy).

Also because of its beautiful interiors, this site has been the one I liked the most in Anuradhapura.

As many knows, Anuradhapura was the first historical capital of Sri Lanka and today is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the Cultural Triangle), often on the touristic routes. 

Dating back to 380AD, the archaeological park contains ancient ruins, dagobas and temples, and a museum.
You will need to organise transport to explore it as I think there is simply too much distance to cover by foot. 
We opt for a tuk tuk. Others for a bicycle, that doesn't seem a bad alternative.

In my opinion, in general, the whole site is pretty disappointing. 
As the country has better attractions (i.e.Polonnaruwa), I would visit Anuradhapura only in case you have some spare time (and an extra budget).
Unfortunately, not worth it from my point of view. 

USEFUL INFO
Entry ticket to the site: 25,00 USD per person (only cash)
Journey time from Sigiriya by tuk tuk: around 1h30mins
PRO TIP
Since it is a religious site still in use today, please bear in mind that everybody is asked to dress properly (shoulders and knees must be covered, and shoes and hats must be removed).
Because of the latter, I highly suggest to carry also a pair of socks into your bag as sometimes the ground can be very warm/hot.

Title: Good visit
Text: I did all the temples in one day, theyre all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

An absolute must see if in this area. The surrounding elephant head carvings are impressive on their own. We didnt go inside though

Title: Very Impressive
Text: My wife and I visited this ancient Stupa during our recent birdwatching tour of Sri Lanka, we had pre booked a guide to show us the Anuradhapura Temples and Stupas, as without one we wouldnt have gained such an insight in Buddha and his teachings. This Stupa is over 2000 years old and we found it to be by far the most impressive. Unlike many others this is in its original brick form. It was originally covered in white painted plaster but over the years this has been allowed to fall away, there is still a small area with remnants of the original plaster. It was far to hot for us the enter the curtilage of the Stupa so we just enjoyed it from the the shade of some nearby trees. This was a really impressive building which wed have liked to have viewed close up, maybe next time. Highly Recommended

Title: One of the tallest brick structures of the world
Text: Abhayagiri Dagaba has been built well over 2000 years ago by a king who is known for restoring the "Therawada Buddhism" which is considered as the more conservative type of Buddhism that follows the original teachings of the "Lord Buddha".  This is a very large compound and this tall "Stupa" has been restored while retaining its remained shape and hence does not look like a perfect dome.   This allows the visitor to see some of the ancient special lime based plasters used to give a pleasing finish covering the brickwork.  The present appearance is purely based on bricks since no attempt has been made to restore it to the original shape in order to allow the visitors to see what was there before the restoration began about 15 years ago.

When you're walking on the equivalent of hot coles you tend to miss out on the experience... perhaps wear trainer socks and then you can enjoy it more!

Text:
This is one of the main attractions of the Anuradhapura heritage site, the other being the Jetawana Dagaba, and , to be fair, its a fairly dramatic piece of construction and, in its day, was apparently the next biggest building on the world after the pyramids of Giza.
Other than the scale of the structure theres not a lot to it and, to be honest, we found the whole of the archaeological site to be something of a disappointment. It certainly doesnt rank alongside the likes of Sukhothai or Ayutthaya in Thailand yet at $25 entry fee the price is well above these locations. The park is basically a collection of stupas supplemented by ruins of other buildings that are little more than stone outlines on the ground.
