Title: Don't just visit the stupa, wander about the nearby ruins too
Text:
The Abhayagiri Dagoba is a huge brick stupa built slightly over 2,000 years ago, and for centuries after that, served as the focal point of an expansive monastery complex, stretching for hectares around.  Other than sheer size, the stupa itself isnt much to see -- though you should spend some time contemplating its age and the feat of construction it represented for its time -- but the parkland around is chockful of ruined foundations of all sorts of buildings.

The stupa/dagoba  was the focal centre of a major monastic complex, said to once have housed and served 5,000 monks. Today, its a shady area with mature trees, with hardly anyone else around, so its a pleasant stroll wandering around the ruins. As bonus, I saw three wild peacocks strutting around the site too.

Not so pleasant were inquisitive monkeys and wild dogs.

Also, sun block cream and insect repellent would be handy.

Among the ruins to the east, a short walk away leads you to a lovely piece of sculpture called the Samadhi Buddha. More ruins can be found to the west of the stupa; these ruins (Ratnaprasada) once housed the more ascetic monks. To the northwest of the stupa is the most elaborately-carved moonstone in Anuradhapura -- a moonstone is a stone slab placed before a set of steps.

Its interesting to try to imagine the hustle and bustle that once characterised this site, with monks chanting prayers, debating sacred texts, and lay people presenting donations. No doubt it was also a location for political intrigue since organised religion was closely intertwined with government in those times. I also wondered what sort of economy could support such a large number of monks.

But today, its a tranquil, relaxing parkland.

About 300  400m south of Abhayagiri Dagoba is the Abhayagiri Museum. See my review of it under that name.

The stupa, museum and ruins around are all within the paid area of Anuradhapura's Sacred City/Ancient Ruins archaeological park. However, tickets to the Archaeological park can only be purchased from the Archaeological Museum (not to be confused with the Abhayagiri Museum) located about 2 km south (ridiculous!) of the Abhayagiri Dagoba. Cost = US$25, or 3,780 Sri Lankan rupees and valid only for the same day.

General info about places in the Sacred City/Ancient Ruins park: The sights are quite spread out such that while walking from one sight to the second may be possible, covering many more on foot is impractical. Youll need a map and a bicycle or tuktuk hired for the day. Also, there few toilets, and few places to buy water, though there is at least one rustic shop near the Abhayagiri Dagoba that has cold drinking water for sale.

Title: It's A Landmark Thing And As A Tourist ...
Text:
When you set aside religion and look at these ancient sights as landmarks to this area and to the country.  As a tourist they are worth a visit as much as you would visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris and the Statue of Liberty in New York etc, etc.

There is something to get from visiting them.  Something to feel and understand.  It is the feeling of the heat of the paved slabs or rock steps under your feet and an appreciation and understanding forming of what worship is like for these people here.  It is the physical exertion on your body to reach the highest point.  It is the tranquility of the landscape that these sights are built around.  It is the bewilderment of the age of the relics and the size in which some have been made.  It is the sights of monkeys behaving like this is their home.  It is the noise of traditional music as an organ may be playing if you were to visit a Cathedral.  It is the gentle murmurs of worship coming from peoples prayers.  It is the shade of the tree whether it be regarded as holy or not.  It is the smell of incense and the sight of flowers given as a gift.  It is the welcoming smiles of the Sri Lankan people who are happy to include you here regardless of your religion.

It is something you do and recommend you do when you are visiting another country.

Title: Largest Vihara
Text:
It is one of most important & largest vihara in Anuradhapura. Built by King Walagamba in 89-77 BC. It was a massive ruin when discovered. Central Cultural Fund started its renovation in 1997. Roughly 2.8 million bricks were used. It was original custodian of Tooth Relic. It is most sacred monastery for monks.  Two slabs erected on either side of steps of flights are guard stone.
Impressive image house having reclining Buddha. Walls have beautiful paintings.

Title: Massive brick built stupa in the North of Anuradhapura
Text:
This is a large brick dagoba - it was built in the 1st century and has been restored in the 12th century and of course more recently where it was re-furbed into what we see now (this re-furb used 2.8 million bricks!!). It once stood an imposing 115 meters tall but part of the pinnaccle fell off and it is some 30 m lower. The pinnacle can be seen behind the dogoba, lying on the ground.
You enter thru 2 large white stupas affairs then in front of the dagoba is an image house with a large highly painted reclining buddha in it.  The walls of the image house are highly decorated too. As you walk around the Dagoba -there are a number of statues and on the cardinal points there are highly carved stone structures.

Title: Expectations
Text:
Whether the LKR3.5K/foreigner fee (half price for under-13s) for access to Anuradhapuras ruins is worth it depends on your expectations. Angkor Wat its not; but its cool. If you want to see it, pay it (and if you dont, dont). (Sure, you can sneak around and see most stuff without having paid. But do you think of yourself as a cheater? If not, why cheat?)
	NB at least as of the date of this review, the Archeology Museum is closed for renovations. That sucks. But, expectations.
	The guards didnt seem to like us climbing up the base rings of the Abhayagiri Dagoba (stupa). That sucks. But, expectations.
	The Sanctuary at Tissawewa, which wed pegged to be high-class, was a disappointment. No ice! No Diet Coke! No, we dont have that dish, or that one either. The New Zealand beef in the salad was practically inedible. Expectations.
	The contemporary-Buddhism-related sites (temples, the tree) require legs be covered down to below the knee. Dress  appropriately, or buy and carry a sarong to put over your shorts (or borrow one from your guesthouse host). Par contre, the wear white signs didnt seem enforced at all.
	The tree, although it certainly didnt look 2,300 years old (and probably is a descendant of the original tree, not actually it), felt like the most genuine piece of Anuradhapura.
	The bikes our guesthouse gave us, like all the other bikes we saw tourists on, were complete crap, which measurably decreased the pleasure of cycling around. On our way out of town we noticed a sign for Indika Bikes, at the Tourist Information Center Restaurant between the Dutugemunu Roundabout and The Lakeside at Nuwarawewa (across from the tyre place) looked like it was offering nicer bikes.

Title: Magnificent Ancient Vihara
Text:
ABHAYAGIRI TEMPLE
Abhayagiri Vihara (temple) in Anuradhapura is one of the most sacred places and oldest temples of Theravada Buddhism. It is one of eight most venerated places (Atamasthana) and one of the five highest/tallest Viharas in Anuradhapura. Abhayagiri monastery was founded by King Vatttagamani Abhaya (also called Valagambahu) (89-77 BC) in 88 BC.as a religious school. Originally its height was more than 330 feet and it was built on the ruins of a Jain hermitage, destroyed by Abhaya. Within next 200 years it became a great international institution for Buddhist learning alongwith its rival orthodox monasteries of Mahavihara and Jetavana which professed Mahayana Buddhism. 
Abhayagiri means Hill of Protection or Fearless Hill. Reportedly a statue of a bull made of pure gold, containing relics of the Buddha was buried in the core of the stupa. Reportedly the dagoba was built over a footprint of the Buddha with a circumference of 1300 feet (400 meters).

Title: Exquiste moonstone and guardstone - best in the area
Text:
Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura is a long distance to travel from the main coastal resorts and so you should probably only consider if you are touring the island.  It was about a two hour drive from Sigiriya.  The area is too big to cover on foot in a single day and, whilst bicycles and TukTuks are easy and cheap to hire, I would recommend a driver/guide who can direct you to and provide commentary on the most significant sites.  

Abhayaagiri was a complex of monastic buildings founded in the first or second century BC. It is still being uncovered and restored.  The stupa is huge (230fit high and very similar to Jethavanarama) but as it still under renovation there is lots of scaffolding.   The grounds are the main attraction. The Twin Bathing Pools (Kottum Putan) are very tranquil and worth a 5-10 minute stop as its a great example of the amazing engineering and water management that was typical across ancient Sri Lanka.  Here solid stone was carved out to create two large pools used by thousands of monks for bathing. Elsewhere across the island earth was excavated on an even larger scale to create huge water tanks which were used for feeding crops as well as bathing. 

If you are in the area I would recommend that you also visit the ruins of King Mahasens Palace to see an exquisite example of a moonstone doorstep with finely detailed symbolic carvings; the Ratnaprasada (Gem Place) for the guardstone; and the Mahapali Refectory with its huge rice trough and bathing pools.

Title: Moonstones and extensive monastery ruins are the best
Text: While the stupa is monumental, one of the best parts of Anuradapura was wandering in the very extensive area covered by these ancient monastery ruins, still not widely recovered and restored from the overgrowth.  It's got a great atmosphere for those who like to explore and imagine they are one of the first to discover this site.  The moonstones are beautiful and not hard to find.  Check out the big pools as well and have a good wander around the fallen down monastery residences that stretch out through the woods.

Stock up on food and drink from the stalls nearby and also go to the museum at the entrance to the precinct.

This is one of the most impressive ones and there is a museum as well that tells you more about the place.

Title: The Classical awesome  Abhayagiri Stupa
Text:
A great monastery among the three found in  Anuradhapura.was founded by the King Abhaya in the first century BC !/ We are wonder-struck by sheer size if the same.It is said to be a sacred place for the  Mahayana, Theravada and Vajrayana Buddhism.This ancient monument was renovated by the Sri Lankan Central Cultural Fund as a UNESCO project.Today, the main attraction of this  complex  is the massive stupa  which stands at 74.98 meters to the tip of the damaged spire. It is the second largest stupa in the island today.It is said that this stupa has been 400 feet (122 meters) in height and has been decorated with gold and silver and studded with all kinds of jewels. There also has been a 20 foot (6.1 meters) high Buddha statue made out of green jade..
It is also a must-see place in Srilanka/

Text: Visually stunning, this colossal stupa soars above the forest floor. Constructed of bricks, its scale is matched only by the Giza pyramids. According to our guide, the dagoba was the centerpiece of monastery of 5000 monks. It is the third of Anuradhapura's great stupas.

Title: Amazing
Text: The dagoba itself is interesting, but the area around it is well worth exploring. There are so many ruins that were fun to walk around to find special elements that made some of them unique. Riding a bicycle is the perfect way to be able to explore this area. Remember to stop and walk around for a close up experience.

Title: scaffolding now gone and fully restored
Text: Not the biggest of the three on the site but the pictures of before and after show how much work went into refurbishing this monument. There is a nice guidebook for sale in the museum attached to the Isurumuni Vihara monument for R250 22pages of A4 colour pics and detailed accounts of the main sites that shows how overgrown this was before it was restored.

Title: Evidence of rich history and tradition of Srilanka
Text: The entire cultural complex of Anuradhapura (The ancient capital of Sri Lanka) is worth visiting. The systematic way of life planned by the people then is evident through the ruins. I had hired a bicycle from the hotel at 600 LKR per day. The entry ticket to all the holy city complex is available at Abhayagiri Museum. The tickets are available at concessional rate for tourists from SAARC nations. I will recommend the tourists to spend one entire day in the ancient city on bicycle to understand the culture of Srilanka. Cheap banana roti, veg roti are available for lunch along roadside restaurants.

Title: Good but Touristy

Title: Part of the Second Monastic Complex
Text: This stupa is the center piece of the second monastic complex and is very much like isn't white cousin at the first complex.  As I was more excited to see the stupas at the first and third (one with the broken top), I opted to just view this one and not walk around it.  It is well maintained and is nicely places near trees and shade, but I wanted to optimize my time....

Title: Buddhist Beauty and Solemnity
Text: When visiting this site during the hot season perhaps try going earlier in your tour or later in the afternoon and go by tuk-tuk as the area is far too large to do on foot and the $25USD pass is for 1 day only of the Ancient City. As the sun and reflective heat is powerful apply plenty of sunscreen, remove hats and shoes at each temple site though you are allowed to wear your socks so a thicker cotton pair is advisable if you wear shorts carry a sarong to wrap around your lower half to abide by Buddhist custom when entering temple areas. At the Dagoba a big Buddha footprint is on the north side, this site has a feeling of strength and bas reliefs and inside the inside section many beautiful Buddhas to look at we always have  small compass attached to our day pack and you find this a handy item when touring all historical sites.

Title: Worth visiting for understanding of history
Text: This Dagoba is actually a complex of monastic buildings and is thus different from many of the other constructions on the Anuradhapura tour. It holds an important and fascinating place in the history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka and our advice is to do 'homework' and familiarise oneself with something of the history of the place before going as the visit will be then so much more worthwhile. Like all of the local sites it gets very busy and indeed hot in the middle of the day, so we advise going as early as possible in the morning.

Title: Went early to avoid the crowds ...
Text: By chance, I went to the Abhayagiri Dagoba early before the ticket booths opened at 8:00 a.m. I found it mysteriously powerful. During the rest of the day, the other dagobas I saw from the road, which was enough for me. When approached by a man who said he worked for the sites, insisting that we pay for walking along the street, I contacted the tourist police, who said we were well within our rights to walk along without a ticket. There's talk that the new government will offer an island-wide pass for all the sights which would be an improvement in our eyes, since rushing around in one day in a frantic attempt to see the Anuradhapura sacred sites is not our idea of a good time.

Title: The Samadhi Statue worth a visit
Text: Like most of the sites, the statue is located in an enormous area full of smaller and bigger sites, all of which has it´s own history. The Samadhi statue is thought to be constructed in the 3rd or 4th century. Found on (in?) the ground in the late 1800s, it is a well preserved statue in marble with a broken nose. The statue itself is surrounded by several old ruins, many of which still remains to be uncovered

Title: You need to find the secret of this statue in order to appreciate it
Text: Maybe you think this is just one more Buddha statue. Our driver told us to take two pictures from either side and compare. If you do this you will find out about one of the specifics of this statue - apart from the fact that it belonged to one of the largest complexes in Anuradhapura.

Title: A must visit.
Text: This buddah is an early example of Sinhalese carving and is very famous amongst the local people. Here is buddah is sitting in a meditation position- a classic pose. The buddah is in good condition despite being carved out of limestone, and now is sitting under a concrete roof. It was thought to be one of four statues but all that remains of the are a set of legs!

Title: Lovely Buddha Statue
Text: It is said in many guidebooks that this is the most sublime statue of Buddha in Sri Lanka.  Well, I wouldn't go that far, but it is a lovely statue nonetheless.  Worth a stop, especially if you enjoy ancient Buddhist art.

Title: Impressive sculture
Text: This is an impressive and well done sculpture of budha in his lotus position. Well worth a visit together with the other items in its vicinity

Title: Inspiring Expression of Meditation
Text: This is one of the best-loved expressions of the Buddha meditating in Sri Lanka.  Dating from the 4th century CE, it is a timeless evocation of world transcendence.

Title: A Grand exquisite Buddha Statue
Text:
The Samadhi posture statue of Buddha is considered to be the  finest one in Srilanka. It is of 3rd/4th century period. The 7 feet statue has stood the test of time and is a holy place. The statue presents three different views when seen through over three directions.
It is situated in the middle of Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura,This meditate pose of Lord Buddha is called Dhyana Mudra, sitting cross legged and upturned palms placed one over the other on the lap. It is said that the eyes of Buddha are unique in that no where in the world such an arrangements could be seen.
A  relatively calm atmosphere when I visited this place on 27.9/2017 in the evening.A serene experience indeed.

Title: Average
Text: As part of the entrance fee , I hoped for more than an average Buddhist statue . It may well look happy and sad from different angles but it appeared just another Buddhist statue to me and I wondered what all the hype is about .

Title: Amazing
Text: Samadhi Buddha statue is another amazing creation of the ancient Sri Lankan artists. Samadhi Statue is a must see place in the Anuradhapura trip

Title: Not worth the money
Text: Governments main job is to rip the tourist off and even the officials behave this way, arrogant and not customer oriented at all. It is all about money here. The price for tourist RP 3500 compared to almost nothing paid by locals. You have to pay that to be able to access the entire area. Not worth the money. "My generous donation will help you preserve the heritage" (as stated on the ticket) however should the locals be also interested to take a part? After you pay the entrance fee almost nothing is in English. You have to open google to get at least some information. Also you would expect at least basic English knowledge of the staff if you charge this entrance fee. We had a disagreement with the staff I took as 15 mins to find someone who can speak basic English. Or at least clean up at the historical sites from all the garbage. I can't really see here that the money is actually going in the heritage. Didn't buy it. Also to be honest there is not that much you can see for the money here unless you are really a big history fan or Buddhist.

Text: This is a religious place, so shoes off, legs and shoulders covered. Locals make offerings here, so it is a place to respect. The statue is interesting as is the thought there used to be four of them, the second is only partially there. Worth a visit as part of the Anuradhapura visit.

Title: A serene statue of Buddha
Text: Buddha in Sri Lanka more or less you always see in the reclining position while this statue is the sitting position in dhayana mudra. A very beautiful statue.

Title: Famous Buddha Statue...Don't miss it!
Text:
It is made out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches (2.21 meters) in height and it is considered one of the best sculptures in the Anuradhapura era.If you are going to Anuradhapura don't miss this.Also go there when it is morning or evening.Coz you can sit there for a while meditating.The experience is tremendous.
It is thought to be done during the 3rd or the 4th century and it was found in the present location in 1886 fallen to the ground with damages to the nose.

Title: Very nice statue
Text: Nice statue in a tranquil spot - under some trees. You have to walk through the souvenir  market to get to it

Title: Yes.  It's nice
Text: In SL you can think.  Another Buddha statue.  Another temple.  Does this one stand out.  No.  Was it worth seeing.  I guess.

Title: So serene
Text: Beautiful statue - so serene and what a marvellous unspoilt setting - not many tourist around so peaceful and quiet

Title: Nothing extraordinary
Text: You can visit their for some photos but remember not to turn your back towards the statue. One of the many buddha statue  you will see in sri lanka.

Title: Impressive!
Text:
Shoes and hats off!  Don't turn your back on the Buddha!  The crowds, their
devotion and dedication and offerings make this a worthwhile place to visit!

Title: Just another buddha
Text: Just another buddha ... Its nothing soooo special, made by stone. The locals love this place, so it gets crowdy compared to other places

Title: A old statue with a history
Text: This statue is not very incredible in itself, but it has a history which is worth noting. An English general would one day during the occupation start shooting at the statue, you can see three patches on the statue where he hit. When the general was shooting suddenly a Tusker (Elephant with tusks) came out of the forest and killed him on the spot. For the Buddhist this shows that the place is utterly sacred.

Title: Nice statue but nothing compared to others in Sri Lanka
Text:
Nice statue, but you will see much more beautiful statues around sri Lanka.

Anuradhapura it self is nice, but all the sights are so scattered that you never have the idea that you are visiting an ancient city. The local people are also living in between the ancient stupas and other sights. You can't blame them but it is a pity of the total experience. We liked other big sights as Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa more mainly because of this.

Title: Popular with local pilgrims
Text: A holy place in the area of Abhayagiri Dagoba, very popular with local pilgrims. A marble statue of a seated Buddha with a particular thing: if you look at it from three sides (in front, from right and from left) you will notice three different expressions of the face! Remove your shoes before approaching the statue.

Title: no hats/shoes
Text:
and no pictures with your back to the statue! 
Fun snacks and lemonade in the walkway outside leading to the carpark.

Title: Remember to look at the statue in Three directions
Text: This statue tells us the story of meditation. When you look at the face of this statue from the left side you will see a sad face, and straight look will show you meditation pause, and then the right view will have smile on the face, therefore Remember to look at the statue in Three directions. This is one of the greatest creations of Sri Lankan history.

Title: Go on a Friday to experience meditation in the park
Text: Beautiful Buddha statue in a lovely park. Best advice: wear inexpensive flip flops that you can take off easily because you must walk barefoot at these holy places. Don't wear sneakers because 1)they are difficult to take off easily and 2)when it rains, they will be soaked and uncomfortable. Also, don't wear expensive sandals because of the rain/mud. The locals just wear inexpensive sandals and flip flops.

Title: Peaceful, spiritual area
Text: Enjoyed walking to the statue, lots of lovely trees and bird life. Lots of locals meeting and sitting in groups learning how to meditate from the monks. A beautiful scene visually, the white dress of the devotees and the orange robes of the monks seated amongst the trees. Very peaceful setting.

Title: Really nice place
Text: Really enjoyed spending time in Anuradhapura. Samadhie Statue is a must see. Really peaceful place where the locals come.

Title: Wonderful Unesco world herritage park
Text: The old city is a must to visit when you are in Sri Lanka! 7 stupa's and a convent ruin where 3500 monks lived is incredible to imagine!

Title: Majestic
Text: Lord Buddha with historical background is clearly depicted at this place and is quite relaxing and divine location

Title: Oldest Buddha statue of Sri Lanka
Text:
This is the first one of the places you should visit in Anuradhapura. If you are a non Buddhist but love to explore archeological sites this would be another land mark for you. This is a Buddha statue located in the Abhayagiri Stupa complex.  This is a statue of Gautama Buddha in meditation posture or Dhyana Mudra made out of out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches (2.21 metres) in height and width. This belongs to the old Abhayagiri chapter teaching monastery which was built in the 89-77 BC. Old records of Faxian Buddhist monk from china mentioned that this Agayagiri monastary was a huge university at that age with four faculties. This is belongs to one of those faculty. Some of the historical archives give evidence that the king bought a Buddha statue from Maha Vihara  great monastery located around the Sri maha Bodhi temple. So some archeologists clams that this is that statue. 
The first prime minister of India Javahallal Neru once visited this Buddha statue and said this place gives him inner peace. And he kept a photo graph of this statue also in his residence.

Title: Tranquility unsurpassed in a statue. A must for Anuradhapura visit
Text: This Buddha statue said to be made of stone is just over 7 feet tall and sits on a square base.. The Buddha is said to be depicted in a state of "Samadhi" which is difficult to translate directly -as a state of intense concentration and deep awareness is fitting. It dates to 2 or 3 AD. When you gaze at the statue, a feeling of calmness and peace overcomes you. The expression on his  face is overpowering. The statue is now protected by a concrete hood which does take away some of the attraction of this most famous meditation statue of the World. The expression as seen by the observer is said to change depending on the angle from it is viewed. It is situated in a beautiful park and the whole atmosphere is one of serenity. It is not too far from the main Dagobas and is well worth a visit. If you go all the way to Anuradhapura to witness the ruins of an ancient and advanced civilisation, you will feel very bad if you miss this amazing statue.

Title: For the religious only
Text: This statue is for the religious only who believe in it's significance. For everyone else it's just a fairly worn statue. It's kind of out of the way and I came along because I was seeing Abhayagiri Dagoba anyway. Otherwise, give it a miss.

Title: two Buddha statues in the Dhyana Mudra
Text: Mahamevn?wa Park (in the Northern part): you walk by the park and you feel peace and dignity of the place, then you conturn the both granite statues, on the left - a tree with big fruit like a cannonball tree - Couroupita guianensis. Buddhist scriptures tell  the Maya Devi have given birth to Buddha under the shade of a Sala Tree and passed away between two of these trees. Buddha is shown with scented flower petals on his deathbed.

Title: An attractive and important statue
Text: This is an attractive and important statue, especially for the Sinhalese who praise it highly.  The statue is partly restored (the nose) and personally I preferred the samadhi sculpture (and the other statues) at Gal Vihara.

Title: Ok it is old, but seriously!
Text: Yeah it is an old Buddha, but it is very small and had us wondering if we were in the right place. As it is near some other sights you might as well take a look but not worth the journey to see it alone.

Title: If touring Anuradpura then a must
Text: To some another Buddha, to us it was one of the first Buddhas we saw in Anuradapura and it was where our guide began to explain to us the various poses of the Buddha. It does feel spiritual at this site and I am glad we visited it. It was where we learnt not to have our backsides to Buddha when being photographed (as our guide eloquently put it)

Title: Another stature.
Text: As a non Buddhist, I didn't find this sandstone statue exceptional. Maybe it's a case of too much within the site. If you are passing through, it's worth a look but not a special effort.

Title: Impressive
Text: This huge Buddha is a very impressive statue, what a beautiful work. Maybe it's good to see this one before visiting the huge granite statues in Polonnaruwu (Gal Vihara) which are more impressive. But the setting here is beautiful, I visited in the evening, there were no other tourists around, all very peaceful.

Title: The most beautiful Buddha stature I have seen
Text: Located in Mahamewna park, a very pleasing park with lots of tall trees and comforting breeze from nearby tanks, Samadhi Pratima (meaning statue in English) speaks of ancient aesthetic and architectural skills of Sinhalese people of 3rd BC. From left it gives a feeling of slight sympathy and from right a feeling of happiness. This is a must see site if you love art.

Title: Just an average statue
Text:
This is just the statue of Buddha in the so called 'Samadhi' position. There are lot of such Samadhi statues in Sri Lanka. Really makes me think how this is different in an way.

You'll have to leave your slippers outside and walk on the pathway for quite some distance. The pathway is not that well maintained and can hurt your leg.

Title: Take the time to have a look at this one
Text: The slightly different expressions when looking from one side or the other of the face are intriguing. I didn't pay to much attention to it when I was there, but, as the other reviews say, this is indeed one of the most peaceful buddha statues we have seen in Sri Lanka.

Title: Historical value larger than artistic
Text: One should not judge holy statues by their artistics value. In this case these ar not totally on par. And it would be much better  and more peacefull not to have to run the gauntlet of shops that reach up to 20 meters from the statue.

Title: One of many memorable statues of the Buddha
Text:
This is a must see  A beautiful rendition of the Buddha in Samadhi. As a tourist and not a Buddhist it was still a powerful experience to just stand and contemplate the Buddhas life and the life of his devotees who carved this so many centuries ago for us still to be enjoying. The full Moon festival of Poya meant that there was many Devotees of today visiting this Holy Statue and it was a delight for us to see even small children bringing their offerings.
A must see

Title: I can still see the face
Text: I can still see the face on this remarkable representation of the Buddha. He is obviously in deep meditation. If you look from one side he appears to be happy and from the other, he appears to be sad. From the front, he appears to be deeply at peace. A memory to savour.

Title: Serene Buddha
Text: This large Buddha is carved from limestone and dates from the 4th century AD. Unfortunately the artistry of the figure is compromised by a rather ugly concrete shelter under which it sits.

Title: Nice, but nothing special
Text: We visited this place while roaming around the stupas of Anuradhapura. It is a nice statue, but is also something you can give a miss if you are short on time.

Title: Just a Buddha Statue
Text: A significant Buddha statue, highly praised by the locals, although with little interest to the non-religious traveller.

Title: Protected Buddha
Text: Stopped at the edge of a small village and had to walk past a myriad of shops, many tourist until at the far end an isolated statue of a Buddha, covered with 4 posts holding up roof and protecting the Buddha from the elements. Man asking us to remove shoes as we approached. However ground very mucky and rough even for socks and we observed quite clearly some 30 metres away.

Title: One of the best sculptures in the world
Text: Must visit place in Sri Lanka. One of the amazing sculptures in the world. Situated in Ancient city of Anuradhapura.

Title: beautiful Buddha statue
Text: The Buddha statue has a nice stone canopy over it ,is surrounded by lovely trees and part of the Anuradhapura old capital

Title: Decent
Text:
A decent place to go.  Nothing really great.  Can skip this place if there is scarcity of time.  
We stopped by for some pics.

Title: Just Can't Help to Have Peace when You See this Buddha
Text: Located in a nice park, this Buddha is beautiful. There are plants and trees around which adds to the tranquility one might feel when visiting this place. My tour guide told me to take off my shoes as we approach the Buddha.

Title: Located in a Quiet Park
Text: Nice gardens and inside a perimeter wall. The statue itself is beautiful but for me it was just another buddha statue.

Title: Seated Buddha statue
Text: This seated Buddha statue is reportedly one of the best sculptures of the Anuradhapura era,  and as one of the sacred places at Anuradhapura is a place of devotion. However for non buddhists there is not too much to appreciate.

Title: Must visit
Text:
A very nice construction.  And lovely environment surrounded by many ancient ruins.

This and Abayagiriya stupa both can be visited together.

Very sheltered place with many trees. 

A bycicle ride will be ideal. There is parking for larger vehicles. 

Not very suitable to go after 5.00 p.m

Title: Spiritually elevating.
Text: This is the finest and spiritually elevating image of Buddha in entire Sri Lanka. From 4th Century AD, the beautiful posture reflect compassion and benign Grace of Buddha in perfection.A must place to visit in Anuradhapura.

Title: Beautiful serene statue
Text: Well worth a visit while you are in anuradhapura. Remember you can take photos but not with your back facing the statue

Title: Marvelous Buddha Statue
Text:
SAMADHI BUDDHA
Samadhi Buddha is a statue of Mahatma Buddha in Mahameghawana (also called Mahamevnawa) Park in the midst of ancient city of Anuradhapura, near Abhayagiri Monastery. This statue shows Buddha in the posture of Dhiyan Mudra. This 7 feet high statue with Buddha face showing three different moods (plain, sad, smiling) from 3 different sides, is considered one of the best sculpture in ancient history of Sri Lanka, supposed to be carved from dolomite marble in 4th to 6th century AD. 
It was found at the present place in 1886, fallen on the ground with damaged nose. It was then repaired and erected.

Title: Statue of Lord Buddha
Text: Its near by the twin baths only and a statue of Lord Buddha in Samadhi.. No Photograpghy allowed... You can just see

Title: Buddhas Enlightenment
Text: Samadhi refers to Buddhas enlightenment which is depicted by the statue with the sitting position of meditation. The statue is located in the Mahamevnawa Park in between the Twin Ponds and Thuparamaya Temple. It is inclusive in the entrance fee for Anuradhapura Ancient Site at USD25 or LKR4,550. Hiring a driver is necessary since various sites are far from each other. Appropriate dressing required and no shoes are allowed. There are locals here for the worshiping. Good representation of the heritage of Buddhism culture since Anuradhapura Kingdom in 3rd century.

Title: ONE OF THE MORE STRIKING REPRESENTATIONS OF THE BUDDHA
Text: At any Buddhist site you are going to see many depictions of the Buddha. Perhaps it was the colour [ivory with hints of greenish yellow] that caught my eye. It is the meditation pose. It is just eight feet tall. It dates from around the 4th c A.D. It is made out of dolomite marble. Its setting with trees behind it adds to its grandeur.

Title: Nice
Text: Rich in history, the reading at the site helps your mind invoke images of the past....lots of worshippers around as well..

Title: Unimpressive Statue
Text: You can go there while touring Anuradhapura, but that diminutive statue has strictly nothing to rave about

Title: A nice buddha
Text:
This is a very well preserved buddha statue.  You can clearly see all the details still, even so far as a strap line on the shoulder. 

It was in the middle of the woods which made the whole setting even better for me personally.

It is worth having a look at.

Title: Very busy
Text: This buddha statue is large.  It is thought to date from 4th century AD.  However old it is, it is an impressive piece of stonework.  Very busy so choose the time of your visit

Title: Worth a visit if around Abhayagiri Dagoba but doesn't necessarily warrant a dedicated trip
Text:
This statue of seated Buddha is within the Abhayagiri Dagoba complex and is included within the $30 Anuradhapura cultural ticket and you get your token for the statue ripped off when you enter the complex. Its a short and easy cycle ride from the main pagaoda and you can park your bike up at the main car park, from where you walk by a large number of market stalls before reaching the statue.

The statue itself is relatively small and there is a rope on the floor where your ticket is inspected again and you may enter (without shoes) for a closer look. You can also see quite well from outside the area too. The statue attracts tourists and worshipers alike which is good to see.  A visit doesn't take long and I'm glad we didn't make a specific trip as it doesn't quite warrant one if you are short of time in Anuradhapura.

Title: Beautiful statue of Bodhisattva or Buddha sitting in Siddhasana near Abhayagiri Stupa !
Text: The statue resembles the meditating Buddha sitting in Siddhasana and palms turned up, right palm almost on top of left palm!. Samadhi statue which is 8 feet tall is made of granite entirely and is a wonder to followers and worshipers. The statue also symbolizes Dhayana Mudra. The posture of meditation of this Statue is a popular for learning of meditation. It was done during the 3rd or the 4th century. It is made out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches in height ! There is another statue similar close by but it's right arm is broken !

Title: Vacation
Text: Very nice statue of Buddha in a sitting position. Holy place so no shoes. Set inside a huge complex that dates back over two thousand years.

Title: Routine artefact
Text: Well, its a certainly a statue of buddha and hes certainly sitting down so I guess it does what it says on the tin.

Title: Buddha statue
Text: This is another Buddha statue. Take off your shoes before you get close. I was expecting something more spectacular but it was not coloured, or as big as I expected.

Title: The statue may not be impressive, but the surroundings make a visit worth it
Text:
From my Blog:

I approached the statue, and to be honest was not as impressed as I thought Id be. The realist in me saw it as a basic statue, while the traveller in me scolded myself for judging this as merely a place to visit while dismissing the spiritual power this site holds for so many.

As I walked off, in the corner of my eye I saw two boys who could not be more than 9 years old playing cricket between two small temple ruins. I took a moment to let where I was hit me. How many times in your life do you have the privilege of being allowed into another religions sacred grounds? How often in your life do you see children playing amongst ruins built thousands of years ago?

Title: Samadhi Status ( samadi budu pilimaya) - anuradhapura Sri Lanka.
Text: The Samadhi ( means in deep meditation) Status which belongs to the 4th - 3rd century BC is the work of an anonymous master - sculptor of the Anuradhapura period who has breathed life into a solid rock. Here, the Buddha is depicted in the Dhyana Mudra, The posture of meditation. This unique piecs of sculpture, was fallen to the ground when re-discovered in 1886. It is 7 feet 3 inches in height and is a depiction of the spiritual purity and serenity of Load Buddha.

Title: Considered a masterpiece of sculpture
Text: This Buddha statue is considered a masterpiece of sculpture. Don't miss going to the nearby sacred Sri Maha Bodhi tree as well.

Title: Along Pilgrimage Route
Text: Although tourists may not be especially impressed with yet another Lord Buddha statue, this site is important for locals and worth visiting as you explore various pilgrimage spots in Sri Lanka.  So it's not to be overlooked. You can research later to discover additional layers of meaning for this site.

Title: Not impressed
Text: It is a Buddha.  It isnt the biggest, thought it is supposed to be the most exquisite in Sri Lanka.  I didnt think so, but its worth a visit if you are in the neighbourhood

Title: BUDDHIST
Text: This is another beautiful temple area to visit.The Buddha statue in the middle. The surrounding area has shady trees .

Title: Serene Samadhi statue
Text: Walked through the market stalls (selling mostly tat) to get to this attraction, what a shame. The statue site is well kept and there is a peaceful serene feeling when you are there.

Title: Peaceful
Text: After visiting the buzzing sites of the big dagobas and stupas all day, you may appreciate the peaceful setting of this sacred site. Embedded in a beautiful park, this site invites you to take a breath and mediate while enjoying its beauty. A very good place for a short break in your pilgrim day.

Title: Serene!
Text: It was beautiful to visit this site. I reached there and saw a man raking the lotus flowers kept as offerings on the table in front. It was lovely to experience the space as such and walk around it. The statue is beautiful!!

Title: Peace after monsoon rain
Text: I visited here late afternoon after a monsoon downpour . Quiet and utterly peaceful. Take a while and be in the moment with this elegant understated ancient representation of the Buddha.

Title: Historical Statue
Text: Like everything in this historical area of Sri Lanka this statue is well worth a visit. The culture in this area does not dissapoint

Title: It's a statue
Text: It's a Buddha statue like many others, but it's old. Since it's near Abhayagiri, you might as well stop to see it on the way. But it's not worth going out of the way to see. A plus is that there are food and drink stalls nearby.

Title: A serene and beautiful Buddha
Text: This Buddha is beautiful - not as large as the Gal Vihara Buddhas at Polonnaruwa, but perfect and peaceful.  You can buy flowers on the way to leave as an offering.  This is an active place of worship with many more Sri Lankans than tourists - take shoes and hat off The atmosphere is tranquil and spiritual.

Title: Tranquility
Text: Samadhi Statue is a must stop for all visitors to Anuradhapura. The tranquility in the surroundings is miraculous!

Title: Budha Statue
Text:
As such this may seem like another Budha Statue in Samadhi state. Probably the Statue at Gal Vihara in Polonnaruwa is more impressive.
This place originally had 4 Budha statues facing each direction, with a tree in the middle. Right now only one statue is left out. Though our guide mentioned that Budha looks sad when seen from one side and happy when seen from the other, I was not able to really identify that.
Place is considered sacred and hence you need to remove the footwear. Since there are a lot of trees, no need to worry about the hot floor. No Separate tickets.

Title: More than meets the eye
Text: This is a stunning statue to see up close. As you walk around it, you can see that the expression on Lord Buddha's face changes. Its fascinating and speaks to the great craftsmanship that went into building this statue. Folks come and set flowers before the statue, so its a calm and serene place. Definitely recommend stopping by if you are in the area.

Title: Utterly stunning craftsmanship
Text:
This statue of Lord Buddha is made in a way that it depicts different   emotions of life, when looked from different angles.
Just looking at the statue brings in calmness and serenity into your soul.
It also is situated in a very calm surrounding.

Title: One of Four
Text: This statue was original one of four that faced in each direction.  Though this one and the base of the one opposite it are all that remains.  It is in a very serene setting and made me feel very humble.  You do have to remove your shoes to walk up the dirt path to it and to walk around the general area.  The neatest thing is that from one side it is frowning and from the other smiling.  Please be respectful when you visit.

Title: Buddha in characteristic posture
Text: This statue is of the Buddha depicted in the position of Dhyana Mudra, the posture of meditation associated with Nirvana. It is a very attractive and culturally important statue carved from granite. Standing around 8 feet in height it is nowhere near as vast as many other similar statues found in the cultural triangle of Sri Lanka but has an elegance and charm that is worthy of a visit. It is located in Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura which in itself is a place of peace and tranquillity.

Title: A lot to see
Text: There is so much to see in this area. Be prepared to spend at least 2 hours here. It is nice, but there are other places in Colombo I liked so much better (Seema Malaka and Gangaramaya Temple).

Title: Amazing
Text:
What a wonderful spiritual experience.As soon as we entered the place we could feel the difference.People were looking at us and smiling.It was so welcoming.Even though we were not able to communicate verbally we felt so uplifted.We were invited to take part in their ceremonies and were shown every kindness.
For me this was the highlight of our 3 week visit.

Title: One of the places visited by Lord Buddha
Text:
This is one of the most popular Buddhist temples in Colombo.
It is also preferable to try and visit during the day and to avoid the rush during the monthly powa celebrations

Title: Great View
Text: Kelaniya Raja Maha Viharaya is a popular temples in Sri Lanka, and best place to understand the cultural & history of the Sri Lanka.

Title: Kelaniya Temple Buddhist Temple
Text: The Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara or Kelaniya Temple is a Buddhist temple . We visited on a Full Moon Day, which is primarily a buddhist  mass prayer day and a national holiday in Srilanka. Hence, had lot of devotees in the temple. A nice place to understand the cultural of the country

Title: Make the effort
Text: A little out of Colombo, but definitely worth the trip. You will require at least an hour to appreciate this place.

Title: Visit only if you happen to be in Colombo
Text:
It's a good place.

Visited it in November on a weekday, hence could see the idols without much rush.

The location takes around 40 minutes from Colombo (Galle Face).

One can book tuk-tuk on Uber.

Wouldn't recommend a Colombo tour just to visit this temple, rather visit it when you happen to be in Colombo.

The descriptions are written in vernacular language. 

1 hour is a good time to spend here.

Title: Beautiful temple outside Colombo!!!
Text: A Buddhist temple outside Colombo city. It is a beautiful place with religious and quite atmosphere. Also the temple is very old and go back to the Buddha era. It also has some Hindu gods impressions. The craft and sculptures are a thing to visit. The temple displays journey of Buddha in Sri lanka through wall painting. A must visit place for Colombo trip.

Title: Important Temple
Text: This is probably the most important Buddhist Temple in Colombo. It's actually on the outskirts of Colombo on the road to the airport. Best visited early morning or at sunset.

Title: Asian Religious Culture
Text: I had a chance to have a Kalaniya Temple Visit during my Sri Lankan tour and this was an amazing experience in terms of understanding variety of religious cultural ceremonies and events.

Title: Beliefs galore
Text: This is a place believed to be personally visited by Lord Buddha. It is an exceptionally well maintained place of worship which offers a peaceful ambiance.

Title: Sacred place of worship as lord Buddha visited by him self.
Text: Legend says Lord Buddha him self with 500 Arahath monks visited this place. Crowded always and even non Buddhists visiting this place as this an ancient temple. Plenty of transport options available. Completed with Maha Bodhi Tree, Stupa and a Buddha House surrounded by golden sand and with a quiet atmosphere make it a really calming place to spend some time regardless of your faith.

Title: Beautiful peaceful temple
Text: Such a peaceful place, it is beautifully preserved with beautiful paintings inside the main temple telling the storey of Buddha and the magnificent tree in the centre which is approximately 2500 years old

Title: Sacred and Cultural Sites
Text: This place is located at a suburb of Kelaniya, where is 11km away from Colombo. We used UBER-Tuk to come here from Jami UI Alfar Mosque which saved the trouble of haggling and cost us LKR350. No entrance fee for foreigners, but we saw many local devotees here for worship and meditation. We also happened to see a blessing ceremony to a toddler done by a monk with the parents. The temple is regarded as sacred place by the locals who believed that the Lord of Buddha had visited this place. The architecture of the temple is intriguing with sculptural images. There is graffiti inside the temple that narrates the life of Buddha with famous Reclining Buddha statue inside the temple. Very interesting cultural site with intriguing architecture and history.

Title: Fascinating but if its so holy why is it so FILTHY.
Text: We were taken to this temple by an over enthusiastic tuck tuck driver (never, ever, trust a tuck tuck driver) and yes, it was quite interesting but fir a place with such history and such important wall art the thing that came across was that it was totally uncared for and filthy.  If the religion has all the devout followers it seems to why arent some of them cleaning their religious, holy places?

Title: Stunning Temple
Text:
This is a very beautiful temple to worship the Lord Buddha. A very sacred area and  shoes must be removed of course,  however they are removed before you enter the grounds which are quite extensive so do remember to wear socks as the sand and  paving stones can be very very hot!
There are places around where worshippers leave flowers and gifts for the Buddha and pray. Inside the temple there is a marvellous gold sleeping Buddha covered with the finest muslin or silk. The frescos are very old and tell the story of the temple.  
A very beautiful sacred place.

Title: Beautiful Temple
Text: We visited this temple on a Sunday and everyone was wearing white. The place is so nice and picturesque. The attention to detail on the temple is magnificent, every elephant, baby and flamingo carving is unique. Must-visit!

Title: Most beautiful and serene temple
Text:
On our way back to Colombo, we swung by this temple. 

It isnt really a main tourist site but non worshippers can come to take a look. 

It is said that Buddha came here in his 3rd and final visit to Sri Lanka. 

The interior of the temple is simple magnificent. The paintings and the art depicted the different stories in Buddhas life. It is the most beautiful temple Ive ever seen. 

According to our guide, the locals come here to pray and worship especially under the Bodhi Tree to ask for blessings or wishes. They will walk around the tree 7 times carrying a bucket of water. After that they will pour the water to the tree.

Title: Gorgeous paintings and impressive structures
Text: The experience at Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara was very satisfying. Brilliant sculptures and lovely wall paintings took the breath away !

Title: Nice Buddhist Temple
Text:
nice to visit and Historical temple in Sri Lanka, 
you can see the arts in this temple, if you came to Sri Lanka please don't forget

Title: Buddhist sanctuary
Text: This temple is located outside the city of Colombo. It is not a must visit temple if you are  touring the island and seeing other Buddhist temples. Well worth a visit if you are passing by and have time to spare.

Title: Budha .

Title: Historic Buddhist Temple
Text:
Also known as Kelaniya Temple is a Buddhist temple, with a history believed to be dated back to before 500 BC, located in Kelaniya, Sri Lanka, a few miles from Colombo. It is believed by the devotees that the temple was constructed during the third and final visit of the Lord Buddha to Sri Lanka which occurred eight years after Lord Budda was said to have gained enlightenment. 

Mahawansa records specify that the original Stupa, situated beside the main temple,  enshrined a gem-studded throne on which the Buddha sat and preached.  The temple is well-known for its reclining Buddha and the paintings, very detailed in brilliant colors, which adore the interior walls of the temple which depict events in the life of the Buddha in Sri Lanka and events that took place in the Jataka tales.  Although it can be crowded mid-day you gain more knowledge of the temple grounds because of all of the activities that take place during the day.  There are a group of monks that live on the temple grounds who will be observed monitoring the activities and offering blessings to the devotees that are on the ground to pray and pay respects.  Plan on spending about one hour on the grounds in order to view all of the important activities and structures.  You will be required to remove your shoes to walk around the grounds.  If your feet are tender at least wear socks for your walk around the stone or sand filled payment.  Stairs are minimal.

This ancient place of worship denotes one of the three places visited by Lord Buddha for the last time (3rd visit to Sri Lanka) on his 9th year after attainment. Title: Serenity and tranquillity...
Text:
Kelani Rajamaha Viharaya, is one of the most revered historic Buddhist temples in the world I believe.

Among the many Buddhist temples of Sri Lanka, the Kelani Viharaya stands out as one of the most exquisite examples of the sculptors art. Its history runs back to more than 2500 years. From the early days to date, it always received full royal patronage,  its has been highly venerated by the people of the island.

Title: A must visit holy site in Colombo
Text:
This is a temple once visited by Buddha himself and so of very high value to Sri Lankans. Located about 9 Kas from central Colombo, I ended up going there taking Uber for about 750 ruppi, not a bad price. 

It was first day of the year and so temple was full of prayers who usually frequent religious places on this special day. It covers a big land space with many building, the most prominent of which is a temple with beautiful wall paintings and a reclining Buddha, a smaller version from the one in Bangkok. 

Other buildings include some featuring relics such as Buddha hair preserved in a golden jar behind glass, and lots of meditation spots. They even had a building where kids were performing dances etc. place was very crowded because it was first day of year but I can imagine how it can be peaceful on other days.

Other main features was a huge tree which worshippers were queueing around to water. Meant to originate from a branch of a tree that Buddha grew in India, and also a big white dome with many Buddha statues around.

Like all Buddhist temples shoes have to be taken off on site; however sand was quite rough and so were the rocks and so my advice is sacrifice an old pair of socks and put them on to walk around with.

People are very friendly inside and will not treat you with coldness or aggression because you are a foreigner.

I could fee a general ambiance of safety there, and didn't feel there were people attempting to pick pocket or invoke trouble despite the big numbers around.

One restaurant about 2 kms away from temple called Seth, is run by a family and supposed to serve delicious local food. Sadly it closes at 3 pm and was closed by the time I got there. Check its details on trip advisor.

This temple is a must if you are in Colombo and like to explore Buddhist. Culture in Sri Lanka, enjoy!

There is an attached museum but all the artefacts are sort of in storage / waiting to be stacked/arranged. Everything is just lying around, barely any information either.

Title: Bhuddam Saranam Gacchami
Text: Bhuddam Saranam Gacchami..??.. Very pleasant bhuddist temple in Colombo.. Visited this temple in the transist time at Colombo Airport..

Title: Highly recommend you visiting this temple
Text: I have always been very interested in learning more about South Asian cultures and religions, so we visited multiple temples in Sri Lanka and India in one trip. But trust me, this temple was beyond beautiful. Its a big temple with a lot of statues, and antique decorations. It took us about an hour to walk around and see everything.

Title: Very unusal temple with many ancient artefacts and statues
Text:
A combination of a Buddhist temple and a museum. it contained many items of religious relevance, including gold, stones, elephant ivory, porcelain, Chinese statues, stamps, watches, cameras, photographs, coins, one taxidermied elephant, stereos, shells, swords, and some other very weird items.  

I believe many of these items were donations made to the museum. The centre of the temple was its main prayer area. The whole vibe was quite peaceful but also a little eerie. 

To get a good feel of the place, I'd recommend going at night or in the evening. 

Location - Sri Jinarathana Rd
Entry fee - LKR 400 per person

Title: Gorgeous Buddhas
Text: I was in a tour group viewing this temple.  The gold is almost overwhelming.   Don't leave Colombo without visiting.

Title: Well, it was nice
Text: Unfortunately, a lot of tourists are driven here. For us it was just a temple like many others. It was okay if you have nothing better to do.

Title: Very nice Temple
Text: Very nice temple. I alwys enjoy going there. Always a Hightlight to go there and enjoy this beautiful place.

Title: Love
Text: Gangaramay is buddhist temple in colombo .such a huge and beautiful temple it was .i love the surrounding area also .grest spiritual feeling out there must visit

Title: Ok
Text:
We went here as a tourist,so they ask us to pay 400 rs. as charges for entrance as we are foreigner.
They exempt our son,14 years old to pay.
In front of temple old time machines are good to see.

Title: A Colombo MUST VISIT!
Text:
Amazing place. Gigantic statues with exquisite detailing and accompanying statues.  An eye opener on how unique Sri Lankan culture really is.

There is a Buddha relic here.

Lots of material artefacts such as jewellery and objet d'art.  Plenty of vintage cars including a Rolls Royce.  Probably a vintage Bugatti.  One top end Mercedes Benz near the main entrance.  Somehow left me perplexed as in my view monks are supposed to lead austere lives and not be obsessed with the dazzle of extreme riches.

The arrangement of stuff seemed a bit haphazard and most likely grew organically.  A physical rearrangement of the place a crying need.

Title: Unique and Peaceful
Text: Lot of buddhist artefacts are kept. Very interesting. Huge statues of the great Buddha along with wall paintings of related stories is the highlight. Very calm and peaceful. Unique and awesome. I had never seen a Buddhist temple like this. Must visit.

Title: Amazing must visit
Text:
Do go if you are in Colombo.
This is worth experiencing.
Though the tickets were high priced.

See both temples.

Title: How can a temple be left so unclean, just plain dirty?
Text:
We visited this temple at the time that the Coronavirus was beginning to spread and we were shocked at how dirty the place is.  Nothing is cleaned on a regular basis, quite clearly.  Maybe we had a heightened consciousness around surfaces because of the virus risk but the filth in this temple was more obvious than the millions of dollars worth of jewels, cars and artefacts, and yes, I mean $Ms.  There are cars there worth more than $1M each.  All thickly covered covered in dust and dirt.  Its criminal.  
Anywhere else in the world at temples, churches, mosques, synagogues and other places of worship are kept clean by worshippers, people who take pride in their place of worship.  Not in Sri Lanka!  We came away wanting a shower.

Title: Amazing experience
Text:
This is a must. And make sure you allow yourself plenty of time. 

Lots of history here and just amazing items on display. 

Ancient coins, lamps, compasses going back centuries. And then the statues and jewellery. 

Plus for some reason some old cars.

Title: A fine example of preserving Buddhism in Sri Lanka!
Text: More than 2,250 years after Indian Emperor Ashoka sent his son Mahindra and daughter Sanghamitra with saplings from the Bodhi Tree in BodhGaya (in India's Bihar state) under which the Buddha had attained enlightenment, it is wonderful to see that Buddhism thrives in Sri Lanka. What a pleasure it is to visit Colombo's famous Gangaramaya Buddhist Temple for someone like me! I have visited Lumbini, Kapilavastu (Nepal), Kandy, Anuradhapura (Sri Lanka), Sarnath and BodhGaya (where I sat under the Bodhi Tree!) in India. A magnificent effort is being made to preserve and spread the Buddha's teachings by this Temple's management! A trip to beautiful Sri Lanka is incomplete without a visit to this temple!

Title: A complex of temples and little museums worth a visit in Colombo
Text: Gangaramaya temple is surprising, to say the least. To start with the fact that it is a complex of temples, museums and open areas for praying, not just a single temple. Some of them are, for a non-Buddhist like me, more like Hinduist, with images of Vishnu, Ganesh and other Hindu deities abundant in some of the temples. There are many Buddha statues in all sorts of sizes, materiais and forms. The jade Buddha is beautiful. There is also a relic - a hair from Buddha - that was given to the temple by Bangladeshs government. There is a sacred tree inside the complex, a huge Fig Tree, and that area, with many people praying, is very peaceful. There is also a replica of Borobudur, the huge Buddhist complex from Java, very interesting. It is definitely worth a visit if you are in Colombo.

Title: One of the Best places to visit in Colombo
Text: Located on the Beira Lake, Gangaramaya temple is built in an unusual mix of Indian, Thai, Chinese and Sri Lankan architectural styles. The temple complex comprises a cluster of shrines that surround a peaceful courtyard, with a dagoba at the centre. The museum just off the courtyard displays various gifts donated to the temple over the years, ranging from Buddhist statues to vintage cars. As with any Buddhist temple, visitors must first take off their shoes before entering; however, the floor tends to get heated very quickly, so it is wise to take a pair of socks with you.

Title: Stunning Buddhist Temple
Text: This temple is well worth a visit. Every room you walk in is a new visual adventure. Much of what is in the museum is gifts given to Buddha from devoted followers and it was so interesting to see their offerings. There are many rooms so make sure you dont miss any of them. If you visit Colombo, in my opinion this is a must see.

Title: Budist experience
Text: Is one of the important visit if you go to Colombo. Is a must! If you are a woman don't go with shorts. You will feel comfortable wearing your own long jeans than the piece of fabric that they give you.

Title: Nice temple but strange museum
Text: We went there on our last day in Sri Lanka and it was interesting to see this temple which was recommended by our hotel. The temple itself is interesting and you can spend a couple of hours there wondering around. They display the hair of Buddha in one area of the temple. There were many worshippers in that morning so I felt a bit uncomfortable taking pictures but it was nice to be part of the ceremony. What I found strange is the museum which had many non related pieces exhibited like old cameras, reading glasses and watches,.... these items were gifted to the temple. Anyway it was a nice place to see.

Title: Amazing Temple
Text:
I never saw such a beautiful temple, really amazing. 
This is the best Buddhist temple I ever visit. 
Amazing

Title: Serenity Amidst the Chaotic!
Text:
Super peaceful locale. Wish additional info were provided on the plaques. Victoria Garden nearby is another lovely public garden. Adorned respectfully by the bearers. 

Send papers we'll resolve them!

Title: Mr Abu
Text: Very beautiful and respectful place. Always crowded. Historical and religious monument. Retract Sri Lanka history. Old vehicles, coins, gold and stone statues ...

Title: Good visit
Text: Great temple (you really only need to see one on each visit) 300 rupees each, our 9yr old went free and they offer you cloaks to cover bare shoulders and another if you have legs exposed over the knees

Title: Beautiful and peaceful
Text: Full of charm, the gangaramaya temple is a quiet and beautiful place. Make sure you don't turn your back to the Buddha when taking selfies. It has tight security after the terrorist attack previously. This place is a beautiful and quiet place

Title: Family Visit
Text:
We were really amaze at the Buddhist Temple.
The experience was just great. Parking was a bit uncomfortable on this narrow road, but once inside, the experience perspective completely changes.
Loved the statues and the cleanliness. well preserved temple.

Title: Nice temple
Text: Nice temple with lots of lord buddha statues and a museum with lots of artefacts. They also have smallest buddha carvings. Foreign tourists are expected to pay srl300 per person.

Title: Beautiful settin
Text: Definitely worth a visit even if you are not a Buddhist. We visited on a Sunday and the sky was overcast making the outdoor setting a pleasure to visit. No shoes allowed inside the temple and cover your knees.

Title: Good attraction in Colombo
Text:
Gangaramaya Temple is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Colombo. It features several chambers, statues, a vihara temple, Bodhi tree and assembly hall for monks. As you wander through the Gangaramaya youll see massive collections of Buddha statues and gold vintage stuff, furniture etc so marvel at the craftmanship
You need to leave shoes,hats in the free counter before entry.
Avoid sleevless and knees need to be covered
Avoid showing Back to Buddha as it is not liked by priests.
Timings: 05:30 AM to 10:00 PM, Price: LKR 300 per person
This ticket also allows entry to Seema Melaka temple in Beria Lakw

Title: Beautiful temple (museum?)
Text: All things Buddha (and some non-Buddhist things) are on display here. Some of the Buddhas are gorgeous works of art. Read up on the history of the place and the monk with the machines who taught kids how to work.

Title: An excellent old Buddhist Temple which must be seen by any traveller in Colombo
Text: We ,with our friends ,have recently visited this excellent old temple and museum .This is really a place where beautiful ancient collections of statues of Lord Buddha and different materials of elephant tusks will please your mind and soul.

Title: Hidden gem
Text:
I visited this small Buddhist house with a local. A very special place with a resident monk who is 104 years old. 
The museum has lots of pieces which have been returned to Sri Lanka following different conflicts. Well worth a visit.

Title: Religiously serene...
Text: Wonderful calm temple in the city of Colombo. We were taken to the buddhist monk and we got blessings also. If you're in Colombo, this is a must see place.

Title: Temple
Text:
Close to Galle face Hotel.
Small temple
Kind people

Title: Endless treasure here...
Text: An absolutely wonderful temple. Varied and interesting and very sacred. Not to be missed. A lock of Buddha's hair was on display when we went which is quite special as is the Bodhi Tree and the museum is an amazing treat!

Title: Buddhist temple
Text: Nice place to visit. Tourist fee Rs300 for visit to this temple n temple by Beira lake. Walking distance between these 2 temple 4mins. U may visit Colombo city centre after that to escape the heat ??

This temple is one of the oldest temples in Colombo and is also a tourist attraction point. The temple is situated in a very calm and peaceful environment and it's freely accessible to anyone (for tourists I think they may have to pay some entry fee) . It's very much suitable for meditation and as well as other religious activities.
It's suggested to visit the temple wearing appropriate apparel.

Title: Fascinating
Text:

There are many devotees visiting and there are a lot of artifacts to be viewed

The 3 star is for the statues because all the rest is very confusing and strange. 
At the same time you find a religious and peaceful place you also find weapons such as swords and pistols and old nice cars such Jaguars and BMWs.
You have nice and peaceful poster talking about loving and not hurting no one and have a dog in one meter chain.

Title: Amazing temple in the heart of Colombo
Text: Absaloutly beautiful temple in the heart of  Colombo! Do yourself a favor and spend some time taking it all in and wandering around the grounds. The monks also collect slot of random stuff not sure why but some of it was super random.

Title: Buddhist temple Near a Lake

Title: well worth visiting

Title: Calm place to be
Text: Been to Gangaramaya temple. It is a buddhist temple which make you feel calm and composed. You can go there at any time during the day and visit. You will find serenity, calmness and peace in the surroundings.

Title: OUTSTANDING AND UNUSUAL
Text: This Buddhist temple offers (beside Buddha statue) a large variety of statues with bright colors and sceneries going from ground to ceiling. The Buddha statue is reclined and quite big. There was not many tourist the day we visited and it offered us the oportunity to go around to see all the antiques as well as the old cars. We loved this unusual place and advise you to go to visit.

Title: Pleasure
Text:
Excellent location with historical feel...

Very picturistic and extremely detailed with information 

Located at a central location near a mall it was easy to grab a bite post the sight seeing

Text:
I felt like I was at an antique show. This temple was so cluttered with old relics such as watches, glasses, dishware and even weapons such as rifles. There was even a cross bow. 

The initial entrance is majestic, but then when you continue, there is just so much junk here. Lots of Ivory tusks...hope they get from dead elephants. Very disappointed in this place.

Title: GangaRamaya Temple Visit by Dr.Saleh Bakar
Text: The best for Art Lover, you ll find many many old sculptures which are spiritual as well for budhist people, Easy to go their by Tuktuk or public Bus.

Title: Amazing temple
Text: The temples themselves have sitting, standing, reclining buddhas, colorful, gold, bronze, stone, wood, white buddhas, small and large buddhas. A place that you never forget in your life when you visit here with some hope or some message a place that makes you more relaxed

Text: Gangaramaya Buddhist temple is one of the famous attraction in Colombo city. Temple is mixture of cultural essence and modern architecture. Templex complex is having museum, library, tree etc. small Buddha idol is kept in small box.Entrance fee is there for visiting this temple.

Title: A visit to the Buddhist temple
Text: Gangaramaya temple had lots of Buddhas including the jade buddha. It is an interesting temple with different areas to walk around. Highly recommended

Title: As temples go this is not one of my favourites.  Relatively new temple that achieved its prominence due to politics.
Text: All the usual things and an island in the lake nothing to write home about.  Not a historic site, relatively new dating back to Premadasa era.

Title: A happy accident
Text: We were only in Colombo briefly and accidentally ended up visiting this unusual and quirky temple.  It is a strange mix of the utterly beautiful and serene, slightly garish and oddly bizarre, We loved looking at all the offerings left over many years including some vintage English cars.  At times it felt as though you were walking through some surreal bric a brac market with the cases full of old glasses and jewellery. My favourite of all was the Tiny Buddha encased by a miniature glass dome whose face can be seen very clearly through the magnifying disc.

Title: Healing experience
Text:
What a truly joyful, peaceful place to visit this is! 
Dress appropriate and be respectful as this is a place of prayers and not only a museum and artifacts. 
Will return for sure!

Title: Gangaramaya Temple Colombo
Text: Very famous buddhist temple with big museum. Museum is full of buddhas from different part of the world. The temple has got buddhas original hair for display. Must visit place in colombo.

Title: A important buddhist temple in Colombo
Text:
Gangaramaya Temple is one of the important buddist temples in Colombo.We had to remove our shoes/slippers to enter the temple.The best part of this temple was the number of Buddha statues in this place.
The thing that impressed me was the Bodi tree which was inside the temple and was very well maintained, a lot of conservation is done towards this tree,that wherever its branches grew it was allowed to grow freely,in fact they altered the building to suite the growing  tree.
They can maintain it a bit more well.They have an excellent collection of artwork and artifacts but it was not organised well.

Title: Peaceful abode of Lord Buddha
Text:
You are charged when you enter. You will be taken to a transcendental mood unknowingly. Jade Buddha is very serene and luminous. You can see and touch a huge Bodh tree inside. Meditation can be done as there is eerie silence inside the mandir. 
A must visit for all tourists to Colombo.

Title: Eclectic mix
Text:
Parts of this temple are very striking, the carved wooden wall at the entrance and the jade Buddha. There is a massive odd collection- made by a former monk from what I could gather- which looks like several house clearances have been dumped together. Literally a pile of rifles next to Buddha statues, my daughters spotted old plastic MacDonalds Happy meal toys! Didnt quite know what to make of that. 
The other small part of the temple is separate and extends out into the lake.

Title: Biggest Buddhist Temple of Colombo
Text: Vihara is not only the biggest, but also very important Buddhist Temple in Colombo. During the 2019 Poson Festival, the Temple was crowded with a lot of Colombo people, from local Buddhist Community. The entry ticket bought here, is also valid in another nearby Buddhist Temple.

Title: Nice but a bit messy
Text: The temple was nice but nothing out of the ordinary. If youre a tourist and not Buddhist then maybe you could skip it, it was very messy and was not extraordinary

Title: Amazing temple
Text: You have to visit this temple, its the best temple experience we had in Sri Lanka. Quite, peaceful place in the midst of a busy bustling city. I'm not religious, but wanted to experience the temple and found it to be a wonderful place to visit. There is so much to see, and its well signposted with lots of information available.

Title: Nice quiet surroundings..
Text: There is an entrance fee over here..it's a nice quite place with lots of Buddha's..you can sit and meditate or just have a walk around..

Just overwhelming to walk thru.

Title: Amazing

Please visit - well worth it. We were fortunate to visit during Poya and enjoyed a great experience 
People are beautiful. Come an visit Sri Lanka

Title: Nice Place!!
Text: The place is nice. Not that big. View over the lake was good!! Good to take some nice pictures. A must-see place in Colombo!!

Title: The Heart of Colombo
Text: in many ways, this is the heart of Colombo, representing the heart of the culture and as such the heart of the city; as a temple it comes with an unusual exhibition and library of photographs, collectables, and paintings donated over the past couple of centuries that provide a glimpse of life in Colombo in days past.

Title: Buddhist Temple
Text:
lots of statues of buddhas in all sizes and colours.
very informative place for buddism,one at srilanka must definately visit this temple.do not forget to worship the world's smallest buddha statue which is being kept in a cupboard.

Title: It is an unusual temple
Text: The temple has a large collection of items which have been gifted to them by devotees. They are on display and make an interesting tour. The main Buddha statue is lovely and serene.

Title: A Small, yet Peaceful and Important Monastery.
Text:
Ganga = River; Rama = Temple.

Gangarama used to locate in the middle of a lake, and people had to get to the temple in boats.  The lake had long been reclaimed and now visitors could reach the temple by foot.

Gangarama is a sanctuary for those who seek peace in the buzzing Colombo city.  It has a museum that holds items that are worth viewing.  They also used to have an elephant residing in the temple, and this elephant participates in the yearly parade held in Kandy City and he is the elephant to carries the sacred tooth relics of the Buddha during the possession.  I visited Gangarama probably around ten years ago, and I really wish I could return for a visit.

Title: The many faces of Buddha
Text: A definite must see and visit on any visit to Colombo. A temple and museum all in one featuring Buddha from all over South East Asian. History and artefacts  in the one location. Tip- allow yourself plenty of time to not only explore but also sit quietly in this peaceful sanctuary.

Title: Temple and Museum
Text: Fascinating Temple complex comprising the temple of worship, Relic Chamber, Seema Malaka,  museum,  library,  residential hall,  a three storey Pirivena, educational halls and an alms hall. it is a Centre of worship and learning, and involved in welfare work including aged persons' homes, a vocational school and  orphanage. There is a feeling of calmness here and then you reach the 'museum' area with its vast accumulation of treasures and trinkets including numerous Buddha statues, gold items, precious gems, carved ivory and large tusks, porcelain and a couple of elephants looking lifelike thanks to the skill of the taxidermist. I wondered why there are displays of watches, coins, stamps, weapons, etc. and was told that they are bequests from the faithful. Mustn't forget the cars, vintage types including a Rolls Royce. There is a minute carved statue of Lord Buddha also on display, so minute that it's hardly visible. Such craftmanship and dedication. Doesn't matter if you  are a believer or just inquisitive, this Temple complex is definitely worth visiting.

Title: Buddhist temple with Hindu architecture.
Text: Buddhist temple with Hindu architecture. i think one of most important thing you should know about the temples is that your arms and legs need to be covered and you are not allowed to enter with hat  and shoes.

Title: Huge temple complex
