Text: Huge temple complex situated in the heart of colombo. Entry fee was 300LKR. Would suggest to dress modestly when u visit. Spend a good 45 mins here to explore the whole temple. It has a lot on display. Beautiful Buddha statues in every corner. Such peaceful vibes all through the temple. U cant stop urself from clicking pics here. Every corner demands a picture. Its quite popular with tourists so gets crowded all day. The same 300 LKR ticket lets u visit the temple right opposite on the lake called Seema Marakaya. Must Visit.

Title: Sinhala wedding in a bargain house of curiosities
Text: I had my wedding blessing here in Kandyan outfit so didn't get the chance to see all of it but will go back next time. You are paying £1.50 to see an antique museum and tourist temple but a large interesting one with gold and jade buddhas, hair relic and bodhi tree, and it includes the annex at Seema Malaka on the lake down the road. At that price and given locals spending power it is churlish to moan that it is a tourist tax. It remains the case that gem touts will take an unhealthy interest in you - one remembered us the next day from the ceremony when he must have been looking for punters and caught up with us in Fort where he pretended to befriend us as he happened alongside us but when we said we don't want half price gems he suddenly jumped in a tuk tuk and went back where he came from. We were given a blessing in the hair relic chamber and became a minor tourist attraction ourselves. You can get great photos. If you are in Sri Lanka presumably you accept the pros and cons of their animal rights, they have tusks on display although I gather the chained elephant predictably died.

Title: Serene Temple with Buddha idols
Text: We spent more than one hour seeing several statues of Lord Buddha including those built in marble and jade. There is an entry fee of SL RUPEES 300. Photography is allowed. It is a must visit place for those who are looking for peace of mind.

Title: Awesome
Text: A beautiful Buddhist temple right in the centre of the city.  A place of peace and calm.  Floor to ceiling sized statues dominate the main entrance.  The Bodhi  tree inside is protected with fencing.  Prayers are offered here and tumblers of water to sprinkle on the roots.  The other chambers house statues of Jade, ivory, studded with precious stones.  A must visit when in Colimbo.

Title: Very nice place
Text:
We went to this place in the morning, beautiful temple with ancient things and statues displayed. Entry fee is LKR 300 per person kids are free. 

If you are in Colombo you should definitely visit this temple.

Title: Amazing!
Text: Very beautiful Buddhist temple in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The head of the monks here is so kind and friendly. So much in love with the colourful decoration and art in the Vihara. The way they ask for taking off shoes before entering made me feel more peaceful within my mind of living. Glad that I have given red holy thread by the head of the monks. The museum is great to explore and old printing machines on the other side of the road are so remarkable. Worth a visit indeed.

Title: Absolutely breath taking
Text: A beautiful temple, decorated in vivid colours. Quite awe inspiring. The attached museum displays so many varied treasures - a "must-see" when in Colombo.

Title: A good walk through.
Text: The temple has some remarkable pieces of antiques in the museum and porvides a glimpse of Buddhist history. Good to spend an hour or so... Not beyond that.

Title: Temple museum
Text:
Its nice temple in the miss of the city. Its more like museum old stuff there. 300lkr for price of ticket.
Nice to visit.

Title: Vacation in Colonbo
Text: The temple has great treasure of ancient art pieces that were used by Buddhists. Gangaramaya has built this temple. Great statues of Buddha painted in gold and some statues are of jade some are marble. There are so many items , but no space to properly dispaly. It may be good idea to shift some of them to a good museum. Or create space inside to preserve and display well.

Title: One of the most respected temple of Srilanka
Text: We visit this temple several times almost every year but never reviewed the peaceful and beautiful atmosphere of this holy temple which comprised of Srilankans styles premises,pagoda,Buddhas statues,and Maha Bodhi tree especially we are very glad to be able to make the most respect to the Buddhas Relics that contained in the small pagoda on the golden tray which donated by Thai devotees.

Title: Must see in Colombo !
Text:
A unique jewel in the middle of Colombo.
Take your time to share with the 
Monks !
It is a real treasure physically and spiritually.

Title: A novel experience
Text: This was our first visit to a Buddhist temple and it was an unusual experience. There was much to see in terms of Buddhist culture with highly colourful statues and there were quite a few devotees. It was the oddities I hadn't expected, like the collection of vintage cars and used spectacles on display, not sure if they had spiritual significance or were simply a device to attract tourists. Highly recommended nonetheless.

Title: Wonderful temple
Text: We loved this temple, very interesting and peaceful place. So relaxing to just walk around and look at all fantastic statues and holy relics, and it´s a lot to see. It´s always special to visit a Buddhist temple and we love it. This is a temple we highly recommend.

Title: Very Different place
Text: It's nice to visit this place, as there is not to much place to visit in Colombo, surely this one will be one of the destination to visit..

Title: Nice sculptures and big Buddha
Text: This place is a nice temple and place to see Big buddha and some paintings and other things related to Buddhism.

Title: Good place of worship
Text: Such a good place of worship. Very cleanly maintained . Guide explained us about all the places situated in temple.

Title: Our visit to Gangaramay Buddhist Temple
Text: Gangaramaya temple has a history of over 200 years and can be considered as a one stop place for any visitor to Sri Lanka to get a feeling for the Buddhism, the main religion of majority of Sri Lankans (nearly 70%).  It is a good place to learn about the history of Buddhism for a visitor to Colombo.  The temple is so nicely built and it also have a peagent organized every year with so many elephants and traditional Sri Lankan dancers participating along with so many drummers.  The visit to this temple is like visiting a museum.

Title: Second visit, still nice
Text: This visit was my second here and still nice and maybe nothing change. Love the Buddha's, the main building with statues and paintings. My son loves the cars. A good choice to see a temple in Colombo. The entrance is for tourists 300 lkr od 2usd, it is good to reserve at least 30 mins to see it and wander between the buildings. If you love make pictures, reserve for a visit an hour.

Title: Tourist Vis to Temple
Text: What an exquisite collection of Artefacts and artistic items. wonderful collection        of beautiful sculptures.

Title: Something not quite right
Text:
This temple doesnt feel right from the moment you enter the gates. It appears to be a collection of statues for the sole purpose of a tourist experience.

I am sure there was a point in time when it was a unique sanctuary for prayers but this time as long past.

I recommend visiting Kelaniya Raja Maha Viharaya instead.

Title: A Must Visit
Text: This temple is a must visit if you are in Colombo. It is beautiful and has many artifacts related to Sri-Lanka and the Buddhist culture. In addition to that, the place is also quite peaceful and relaxing to spend some time at.

Title: A bit different then your typical Buddhist Temple
Text: Worth a visit as it's more of a collection of Buddhist paraphernalia, a museum of sorts and a temple.

Title: Nice place to rest
Text: Even if it is clear that this temple is not very ancient, the mixture of skyscrapers on the sky, the presence of water and the serenity of believers who come here to pray makes it a truly evocative place, especially at sunset

Title: Vibrant and Colourful
Text:
The colours were so vibrant it was hard to believe that you were in a place of worship. There was so much to see and the collection was very eclectic from conquistador to stuffed elephant, from Jade Buddah to angry statues and a naked mermaid.
Keep your ticket for the other sites and remember it is not a museum but a temple.

Title: A complete Buddhist place
Text:
Very calm, peaceful and a best pilgrim for Buddhist and also non Buddhist. Holds a great collection and idols of lord Buddha and other disciples and also has a meagre collection of cars, coins etc. 
There s a Bodhi tree, which is atleast a 1000 Years old. And u can find more than 1000 idols in it. 
A must visit in Colombo, SL. If u are detailing each and every idols and sculptures, it will take atleast half a day for one to complete it. Or else an sparing an hour will be worth.
Though there are large number of idols throughout, but needs clear maintainence. Since it's a large area it is definitely impossible to maintain with few staffs and volunteers.

Title: Rome around
Text: Don't wanna any Assistance to go there just walk through only USD2 FOR ENTER very nice place to see the differenciate of Buddha

Title: Historical
Text: A temple that you absolutely must visit if you are in Colombo. Do take sometime for this place as it has a lot of Artifacts that have been donated over time. Theres a beautiful marble Buddha and many others around.

Title: Religious
Text:
Wishes come true !

Statue of Buddha was so lifelike !

Beautiful & Peaceful!

Wish to go back there again

Title: Worth spending some time!
Text: This beautiful Buddhist temple is a wonderful example with plenty of rooms and areas to visit. Try and get there in the morning to give yourself enjoy time not to be rushed

Title: Beautiful serene Buddhist temple with museum in the premises !
Text: This place needs tickets ! Beautiful temple with hundreds of Buddha statues of many colors and sizes ! Many Buddha statues are sitting, standing, sleeping, reclining !  The architecture is mix of Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian, and Chinese ! Very serene place ! Lot of Sri Lankan people come there to pray ! The place has temple, Pagoda, the Bodhi Tree, the Relic Chamber, a Library and a museum which has lot of antique furniture, old cars, old utensils, Wrist watches, statues, photographs, and many more things.

Title: Temple visit
Text:
An interesting introduction to the Buddhist temples, but like so much we found in Sri Lanka, the exhibits ( offerings) were not well laid out for tourist viewing, and in need of a good clean! However, it is important to remember that this is a working temple, not a tourist museum.
The Bodhi tree is an important feature and we were able to watch the ceremonies of devotees .
Well worth a visit whilst in Colombo

Title: Beautiful Temple!
Text: A beautiful temple in its entirety! Inside and out, both the interior and exterior are very scenic and awe-inspiring! Very colorful and bright. Located around many trees and shaded areas, the colors help illuminate the site. I took the opportunity to pray and take many photos while on location. I had an awesome local tour guide that informed me on the background behind this temple and its significance. I enjoyed my time here and had a mini photoshoot on its grounds. Highly recommend everyone stop by and visit if youre in the area!

Title: So many Buddhas
Text: I have never seen so many Buddhas. They are everywhere. The temple is filled with furniture, jewellery, even cars that have been donated. The temple contains the world's smallest Buddha. You have to remove your shoes before entering the temple. An interesting place to visit.

Title: Busy working temple with a lot to see
Text: It's quite a walk around this busy temple, up and down a lot of stairs, but well worth it, a lot to see & very close to Seema malakaya.

Title: Gangaramaya Temple & Museum - Visit
Text:
Beautiful Temple & Museum needs tickect to go & see inside. It's worth for visit for history & archaeology lover's.  There is a Emerald Buddha statue, Ruby Buddha statues along with Buddha Hair & tooth relics. 

Down of this temple has Car Museum with Antiques.   Good place for photography as well as there is a huge tree inside where we can pray.

Title: Two temples instead of one.
Text: The reason why I decided to visit Gangaramaya temple is because I am very interested in Buddhism. Aside from that this temple is regarded as the most important in town. However to my surprise I have realized there are two Gangaramaya temples...let's say the old one and the new one. They are very close to each other but the latter has been built on a city lake. It is almost done but there are still works in progress. The entrance ticket costs 300 rupees. Once I arrived there by chance I asked at the entrance if that was Gangaramaya temple and I was told yes. After my visit I was kinda confused as what I saw didn't match the pictures I saw on the Internet. This is why I asked a passerby where Gangaramaya temple was. He told me the real temple is not the one on the lake but 200 or 300 meters from the new one. The entrance fee for the real Gangaramaya temple is still 300 hundred rupees. With a total of 600 rupees you can visit the both of them. Also in the old temple there are works in progress at the time of my writing. However you can pleasantly enjoy both the new and the old temple.

Title: A truly jaw dropping temple of gigantic proportions
Text: One of the world's largest operational temples of lord Buddha.  A huge complex of multiple shrines of Buddha.  Visit it at night.  Looks awesome in lighting. A white jade monolithic statue of Buddha is a masterpiece. There is an entrance ticket which is also valid for Seema Malaka temple nearby.

Title: If youll go just for one temple- this is the one!
Text:
Not touristic,  with many Buddhas from around the world. A guide  is needed because of the unlimited pieces. 
Amazing!

Title: Spirituality and The Supreme
Text:
They say, "Prayers go up and Blessings come down".

Visit this great place of the Lord for living this experience.

Title: Worth a visit.
Text: Its ever flowing with artefacts all over the place. Statues big a small of Lord Buddha adorn all over the area. As a mark of respect shoes are not to be worn inside the Temple area. The Museum which houses so many ancient arts from all over the world kept in showcases. Sad part it tht they are very dirty to look at. No one has I guess over the years cleaned any of these ancient artefacts... The special showcases holding real Gold statues of Lord Buddha, the Hair Fossil, one of the smallest Buddha statue in Gold & Lord Buddha statue made out of Jade are some of the treasures to be seen, besides some very antique cars placed in the rear of the Temple...  its again sad that none of them have been kept well or in running condition... lots of showcases full of old eyewear & watches donated by people over the years, also in dirty condition... Sad tht such a lovely Temple is not kept up to cleanliness of the huge amount of artefacts that are seen by thousands of tourist everyday. Ticket price of LKR300/- p/person is charged as entry fee.

Title: More like an eclectic museum with attached temple.
Text: More like an eclectic museum with attached temple. Fascinating place, worth the 300rupee foreigners entrance fee see the eclectic collections of things donated to the temple including vintage cars .

Title: A museum Temple
Text: A very lovely serene place to visit.. u can spend time meditating.. the museum is even nice... there are lots of antiques and collection of gifts from all around the world..

Title: Fascinating temple
Text: The temple is fascinating in many ways as part of it is so peaceful and creates such a lovely atmosphere.   However, there is also an amazing amount of artefacts of all sorts which apparently increases every year.

Title: Hodgepodge of practically everything
Text: I've been to many Buddhist temples during my travels.  This one seemed a bit overcrowded with stuff.  It's like it had everything but the kitchen sink.  There are many things to see as one meanders through the different rooms and outside areas, but for me, I found it a bit too much.  Sort of information overload.  I would have preferred a cleaner and less cluttered atmosphere.

Title: Have never seen anything like this and was very interesting
Text: An amalgamation of Hindu and Buddhist artifacts and an astounding collection of objects of interest of every kind given by pilgrims.   A definite must to see.

Title: Amazing Temple with lots of history
Text: Our day guide brought us here & led us around.  Huge area & the museum is amazing.  Couldn't get over all the items (a Rolls Royce!!!) that were donated to the temple.

Title: Most important temple in Colombo
Text:
My favourite attraction and, at the same time, one of the most important temples in Colombo. 

Gangaramaya is a sacred site of great significance to locals and travelers alike, and an example of architectural brilliance.
It features Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian and Chinese elements and the result is a mix of modern architecture and cultural essence.

Today the temple serves not only as a place of Buddhist worship but also as a centre of learning and welfare.

Title: Buddha
Text: Most famous temple in Colombo and also know as temple of hairs. This temple have few hairs of Lord Buddha

Title: Buddha's attic
Text: Recommend this even if you have no particular interest in the religion - for hundreds of years, the faithful have been donating "stuff" to this temple, which it can't sell, so now they have a whole floor that looks like a crazy antique shop.  Even cars! fun to see

Title: DO NOT VISIT THIS PLACE
Text: We admired this temple and then we were taken round the back to see this poor adult elephant in chains lying in a filthy pit for a bath. DISGUSTING and so UPSETTING. Ive sent a photo to PETA animal welfare group. Please do the same.

Title: This place will blow you away
Text:
we visited here as part of a tour group, at this point we were of the view seen one temple seem them all, how wrong were we this place is amazing.

smallest buddha in the world
A piece (relic)of buddhas hair
The temple literally thousands of buddhas, in stone, plastic, gold, you name it. 
The museum, houses a huge collection of Buddhist relics from around the world.
All the gifts from devotees are on display all around the temple, and it is a huge, you name it, its been given ie, watches, stereos, 

We spent almost 2 hours in the complex just looking at stuff and here amazing stories, from our awesome guide.

Title: Worth a visit, if only for the antiques.
Text: This popular, famous Buddhist temple is pretty fascinating. There's a ton of stuff to look at, in the rabbits warren of rooms. Not only is this a functioning temple, it's also something of a museum. There are several old cars (Rolls Royce, Mercedes, etc), plus thousands of historical artefacts stuffed on shelves in one room after another. As we walked through the temple, we wondered if it ever ended, because it seemed to go on forever. So much stuff! You'll need a good hour to wander through it, if you are at all curious.

Title: Disappointing.
Text: Not much of a place to visit. Hoards of tourists being herded through what looks like an antiques market. It is a place of worship and is interesting in its own way. Call in, if passing.

Title: CHAINED UP ELEPHANT - DO NOT VISIT
Text: Chained up baby elephant at back of temple. Also at least 10 sets of tusks within the temple itself.

Title: interesting
Text:
It's a beautiful and historic Buddhist temple located in the heart of Colombo.
The part of the temple that resides on the Beira lake is the most beautiful part of this temple.
People sometimes come here to have wedding photo shoots due to how beautiful it looks with the surroundings.
It's a very relaxing place to worship specially during late evening  times when there's very little crowds.

Title: Go if you have time
Text: The temple has many things to display but it is now well coordinated . So its kind of confusing with temple stuff and donations received from other country. The buddha altar is great otherwise.

Title: Nice Temple of Lord Buddha
Text: A serene and calm place in the heart of the city. This place has it's own beauty especially at night. Must go when in colombo

Title: did I miss something?
Text: The man taking money for foreigner tickets was quite rude, and initially denied that the ticket I had for another nearby temple was also valid for this temple even though it was clearly stated on the ticket. As far as I could tell, this was just a huge collection of Buddhas. I didnt see anyone praying, but maybe it was the wrong time.

Title: Disgusting treatment of young elephant held in chains
Text:
I was so sorry I visited here. The temple is known for holding a young elephant, Ganga, captive. As I was leaving the temple, I saw Ganga being taken out a building across the road with chains all around her. I was so upset seeing this beautiful creature in chains and in a busy city so I looked into further....She is whipped, poorly fed and sleeps in her own waste. A quick online search will bring you to the wiki page. 
Please avoid this temple. If anyone knows a local charity or government department that I can write to, please message me directly. Thanks.

Title: A short visit but well worth it
Text:
The temple is spectacular loaded with gifts and offerings from all over the world . The Buddha statues inside are well worth a visit so also the lake in the opposite side of the road. The ticket to the temple entitles you entrance to the lake temple too ad ensure you have the ticket handy 

Its a photographers haven and tread quietly to maintain the sanctity and peace in this beautiful temple 

Do not give a detailed look at old safes a train engine etc opposite the temple as also an antique bus worth a thousand photographs

Title: Wow!
Text: Our first temple of our stay. 300 sru per person. Almost too much to see and take in, especially if you have not done much research on Buddhism. Worth taking time to look around, and also head toward the lake to see the floating part of the temple. The entry price covers both parts of the temple. Tourist toilet facilities available at main temple.

Title: Temple with Treasure
Text:
A must see attraction in Colombo. A mix of modern architecture and cultural essence.
it is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Colombo,

Title: Weird but great
Text: Lovely Buddhist temple near the Galle Face... interesting and friendly... has an odd Collection of vintage cars at the back... very enjoyable..

Title: Short temple visit during our three days stay in Colombo
Text: Totally recommended. This temple is about 5 min tuk tuk ride from the Hilton where we were staying. The tuk tuk driver was very nice gent, speak fluent English, and recommended this temple visit which was not disappointed at all. Lots of history, very impressed and well respected Buddha statue in various size and the main one is quite big. Lots of artifact, history record, and photos. If we go to Colombo again, we will visit again.

Title: Unexpected visit to the temple
Text: We ended up here because we got scammed! The temple is probably not the best example in Sri Lanka.  We went to Dambulla and it was way better.

Title: A collection of Museums
Text:
We were directed to the "Foreigners" section on the right as we entered the main gate where we paid our fee and deposited our shoes into small laundry-like plastic baskets.

We walked through every structure, temple and building on the property.  A few men offered their "tour guide" services but we declined.  There is a taxidermy "elephant head" in one area, and a full elephant near the Ruby Budhhas.  You definitely do not see this in every temple.

The main Prayer Hall contains large colorful sculptures of Lord Buddha.  Thousands of Lord Buddha statues crafted in many styles from many countries are situated throughout the complex.  A Bodhi tree was being sprinkled by water from people offering their prayers.  

Make sure to see the 3 red Ruby Buddhas, the Jade Buddha and Sri Lanka's smallest Buddha.

Title: DON"T MISS THIS! FABULOUS!!!
Text: One of the best temples we have seen in Asia. Schedule plenty of time to spend here. The atmosphere was amazing with so many beautiful things to see. We have never seen so many Buddhas in one place plus a taxidermied elephant! Definitely don't miss this temple.

Title: Really nice at evening time
Text: By accident we discovered this place one evening, when buddists were celebrating some big event (full moon, on this day you can not buy alcohol). And at evening time it was soooo nice! Just it was very crowdy, so we were not entered inside.

Title: A Colombo Must See
Text: Never expected to see so much inside a Buddhist temple. It houses religious artifacts and antiques including vintage Mercedes and Rolls.

Title: Random but interesting
Text: A great example of a Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. The place is much bigger than it looks from the outside and as well as the standard Buddha statues, it also houses items which assume were gifts to the temple such as a full size stuffed elephant and a collection of classic cars and everything in between. It was 600 LKR for entry but this also includes entry to another temple round the corner built out into Biera Lake which is worth seeing too. Shoes have to be removed and there are dogs roaming around so watch your step, you might feel more comfortable wearing socks as floors are hard and they can be thrown in the wash straight away when you get back to your hotel.

Title: So many artifacts
Text: From the outside it doesnt look like it could house as many of the artifacts it has. 300 LKR to enter, cash only. Must take your shoes off and women/men are given a skirt if you have bare legs showing. Everything displayed is a donation, from cars to the smallest golden Buddha statute in the world. You can take pictures of everything. Very impressive temple. Many people there worshipping as you walk around. Lots of buildings attached and steps up and down. A bit warm with no AC anywhere. Would recommend you bring water. Also, a second temple across the road near the river. You can enter the other temple (Seema )on the same ticket. Well worth the visit and would recommend.

Title: Highlight for Colombo
Text: At the entrance we were asked to pay 600 LKR for foreigners. At first thought it was disappointing, but later the person gave a receipt and drop the money into the donation box for good cause. In many asian countries they started taking special fee for foreign tourists. Rest were good experience. The Buddha, Bodhi tree, felt something good. I would say this Temple is main part if we go for Colombo city tour. There is no restrictions to take pictures inside temple, but need to follow some customs. Dont show your back to any Buddha statues. The city centre mall was walkable from here.

Title: Must visit place in Colombo
Text: One of the oldest and very peaceful temple. Must visit if you also you have a  hour or two in hand while you are around in Colombo. One can spend anywhere between 45 minutes to hours in this temple. Will definitely come back again. So much to know and explore about history there.

Title: Speechless
Text:
Such a great experience!!
I can't state something in particular that I liked more. I LOVED IT ALL!
So much to see...So much to admire... Even watching the locals praying it was an experience. We had our tuk yuk driver explaining to us, I think it'd be best to have a guide.It makes a huge difference. 
If you want to visit one temple in Colombo, this should be your #1 by far!!

Title: Lovely Temple and artifacts
Text: Small but very full of artifacts and gifts that have been given. Large tree for prayers that is worth viewing. Very well maintained. Peaceful. We enjoyed our visit and tour guides knowledge of the various artifacts and rooms.

Title: A maze of things to see
Text: A really nice temple but also quite an eclectic one . cabinets of old cameras, lighters, and other bric-a-brac.. Worlds smallest Budda. A piece of Buddas hair. Lots to see.

Title: More museum than temple
Text:
This is quite a unique place of worship. Along with the temple area, there is an amazing collection of artefacts, not necessarily to do with religion. Watches, cars, statues, etc all jostle for space in this large space. These artefacts are not displayed or labeled in any logical manner. 

An interesting place to visit

Title: Good temple but why entry ticket?
Text: Gangaramaya temple in Colombo is a very peaceful and calm place to visit. The temple has some amazing sculptures and design patterns. However I don't understand why they charge you LKR 300 to enter the temple?

Title: the most strange temple i've ever been.not really worth visiting
Text:
as a (kind of) buddist, i felt it was disgusting..
i think it's not worth visiting.
only for people who want to see strange things by their curiosity.
literally every kind of religious statues all together.
it was like somebody who don't know about those religions collected  from all over the world, then put it randomly(in bad way).
but i also saw many locals come here to pray seriously, even elderlies.
I want to respect their prayers, but I felt it was chaotic.
Some of them even looked like somebody cut it out from heritages...
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????(????)????????????(??????????????????)???????????????????????????????????

Title: Nice
Text: Had a nice visit. Be sure to bring local currency to visit. It's not expensive, and definitely looks different from other Buddhist temples we visited while in Asia.

Title: More museum like not a temple
Text: The whole complex seems to be more like a museum of religion that a real temple, as you can see everything from the Buddha statue up to a British buss there. So if you treat it as museum - it's OK, as a temple - not looked after.

Title: Very beautiful, calm, must visit
Text:
Gangaramaya Temple (5:30 am - 10 pm, Rs. 300 entry ticket) is must see place. There are two separate temples accessible with same ticket so keep hold of ticket till you visit both. One on the Beira Lake is small and other one is huge with many smaller temples, exhibits, museums, and sitting areas. Main temple was stunning in beauty and had very peaceful ambiance. You can also do boating on Beira Lake (Rs. 130 for 30 min) and there is small island to walk around near smaller temple.

I will go as far as to say that you skip famous Temple of Sacred Tooth Relic (fee Rs. 1000) and visit this. You can spend 1-3 hours here easily.

Title: Nice visit
Text:
Good place to visit and discover the Buddhist culture. Calm and clean and orderly 
Has good Buddha statues and artifacts.

Title: V interesting and beautiful
Text: Lots of interesting things to see and many photographic opportunities. A working temple with a 200 years old tree which stretches around a central yard - really impressive. Well worth doing.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: It's a beautiful Buddhist temple with different forms of the Buddha. The paintibgs and the beautiful statues make it a worthy visit

Title: Impressive
Text: We have seen maybe one to many temples but this is one worth seeing without a doubt, despite needing to pay an entrance charge. The colourful decoration around the Buddha is spectacular and not to be missed.

Title: An imposing temple of great importance
Text: The Gangaramaya Temple at Colombo not only houses the hair relic of Buddha but has a huge collection of artefacts presented by persons entities and even countries to the Temple. There is the smallest statue of Buddha which is encased in class and viewed through an embedded magnifying glass, revealing a serene golden face of Buddha. There is a beautiful Jade Buddha a replica of the Emerald Buddha which is with the Royals sculpted by a sculptor from Thailand. The gifts to the Temple include gemstones jewellery and even motor cars ranging from ancient Rolls to a modern Jaguar donated even before obtaining a permanent registration number! Entry tickets are LKR 300 per head.

Title: Perfect getaway from city
Text: Gangaramaya temple is a perfect getaway from the busy and fast life in colombo city.The temple have lot of antiques and artificacts as well.Entrance to this temple is free.This place is much visited by the local people to offer their prayers ,so sometimes it can get busy.there is also a museum inside the temple.You can only enter this temple barefoot ,so you have to pay 50 bucks  to people who will keep it safe.The Gangaramaya park is also nearby

Title: Fascinating Collection!
Text: Its a fascinating collection of all kinds of collectables. Truly a collectors delight in a serene setting. Maintenance and upkeep of artifacts needs to be a tad better!

Title: Very nice experience
Text:
We spent a few hours in the temple the day of the full moon festival which was very interesting.
Nice experience and people where friendly 
Paid 600 for 2 of us to enter and very interesting museum on there

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: It is a must visit in Colombo! Mixture of different architecture influenced by Sri Lanka India China and also a western architect ! The museum is a wonderful collection of various items .

Title: Should Visit but buy entrance ticket
Text: This place is undoubtedly should be visited among not to many sightseeings in Colombo, it is really spectacular. 2 parts of temple are beautiful, you really will have a lot to see. But why you have to pay the entrance ticket to the temple is still question to me, it ruins the atmosphere in first three seconds you step inside! Thought to get more mentally from this place, instead get really a lot of photos!

Title: Very cool place to go
Text: This was very neat. It costs 300 per person and the ticket is also good for the other temple about 5 minutes away walking. Big complex with neat things to see. The world's smallest Buddha statue is here.

Title: Nice Buddha temple
Text: Nice divine place to roam around. Lots of Buddha statues. Lots of historical stories to learn. Every statue is mind-blowing not only for its sculpture, also for its behind screen history. You can also see different Buddha statues made with different stones which is just amazing.Every traveler must visit this location.

Title: Interesting with few people
Text:
Nice place, good to go with a guide. Lots of interesting things to look at.
Photos allowed. Covered up clothing can be borrowed at the place.

Title: Review by Indian
Text: Worth of visiting the place. Tell lots about Buddha history. We get to see Buddha statue made with different stones which is just amazing. Do visit the place.

Title: Beautiful, but not much to see
Text: This beautiful temple is right in the heart of the city of Colombo, and is ironically, opposite the newly opened high end shopping maul called Colombo City Center. So it's a real mixture of tradition and modernity. The temple is set on a beautiful lake and features various Buddhist/ Hindu statues, information about gifts donated to the temple from across the world. However, other than that, there is little more to it than a religious shrine/ temple, which in its simplicity is truly beautiful. Entrance for locals is free and 300 rupees for tourists or £1.30 in sterling. Maybe everyone should pay, or everyone should be permitted to enter for free, as we are all equal wherever you are from. However, definitely worth a visit, in conjunction with other Colombo sites.

Title: Excellent, well worth visiting
Text: Got here by tuc tuc and then my tuc tuc driver showed me around the temple. Was great to have someone who knew where they were going. So many different aspects to the temple to see and am amazing array of artifacts. And make sure you go over the road and visit the elephant too!

Title: Temple visit-gangaramaiah
Text: A must visit temple. It was a wonderful.learning experience for me to understand the society and the culture.

Title: Lots of things to See
Text:
We walked to most of the sightseeing locations, and i would say 3/4 of the time someone would approach us and talk to us. We thought wow the people here are friendly here but in actual most of them are trying to sell you their service. 
We were walking and exploring the streets then someone came up to us and started talking asking where we are from, where we heading to and suddenly started called to the tuk tuk to bring us to the temples. Even though we didn't agree to anything. 

We walked off and he kept calling to us changing the price lower =.= (local price, good price, YEAH RIGHT!)
Anyone that approach you, you can be friendly but be wary at the same time because chances are most of them are not really interested in where you came from or how you are doing. 

Entrance fee is LKR300/person. You don't have to worry about wearing long pants, I wore shorts (not to mean any disrepect but it's hot), the guy at the counter will give you a huge cloth to wear like a sarung with no additional fee.

Once inside you are free to explore, there's loads of statues/artifacts. Not much on wording/description unless you want to take a guided tour. Not sure about the tour but I have seen a local bringing a couple around explaining.

I think LKR300 is very reasonable to see so much, do it if you are nearby.

Title: have seen nicer
Text:
This temple is an excellent means of capturing tourist dollars - LKR 400 entry fee for foreigners

The main temple with the large budha was nice enough but the rest seemed very junky. People seem to donate everything. There were three nice old cars but then a room with a wide range of old radios and another of old clocks.

The highlight of the visit was the feeding of the resident elephant who made a short work of a pile of bananas

Perhaps temple visits in Malaysia and China have spoiled me but I would not recommend going.

Title: very peaceful and serene temple
Text:
this is a fabulous temple. being in the city,it is so tranquil and serene.
we can see various statues of lord buddha,including the world's smallest statue measuring 7mm.
also there are vintage cars collection inside the temple.
beautiful feeling once you visit.
please ensure that you are dressing appropriately in accordance to the local laws.
you have to be fully clothed.

Title: Nice and peaceful place
Text: We have gone here in the morning not much of people and very nice and peaceful place with lot of antiques on display.

Title: Very calm and relax place
Text:
A must visit in Colombo!!!
The temple was super nice and quiet. There are lots of local coming here to prey and to meditate. Also there lots of Buddha Statues and images from all over the world. Very nice and sacred place that you need to visit once you are in Colombo.

Title: Beautiful Buddhist Temple
Text:
This was one of the nicest Buddhists temples that I have seen.  We needed to take our shoes off and leave them in the entrance. Our guide did an excellent job of explaining the various areas of the temple.

 The temple has a lovely Bodhi tree that is descended from the tree under which Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment.  It also has a museum containing a lot of memorabilia that people have donated.  There are also lots of buddha statues as well. If you waited in line you could also get a blessing from one of the monks.

Title: Amaizing Temple
Text: One of the best temple during the tour. The elephant was well discipline. Heard that it was used for the scared pageant.

Title: Full of junk stuff
Text:
It was supposed to be the best temple in Colombo. To me it was left behind. Toys, wristwatches ... has nothing to do with a temple!
Not well organized at all. Leaving your shoes in a basket, not a box, no receipt.

Title: Super weird temple
Text:
Super weird. They have a museum, which basically contains a random selection of cr*p, including guns, old watches, plastic Buddha replicas.....
The temple itself is pretty, but they also have a live elephant, which Im not sure is kept in great conditions.
Worth the visit, but just because of the weirdness of it all

Title: Must Visit in Colombo
Text:
Wonderful and beautiful temple. You can see lots of donated stuff from people in this temple. Lovely temple with a large collection of various Buddha statues, relics, artifacts and all things related to Buddhism. it would be great to take photographs without disturbing the devotees. Buddhas hair and the worlds smallest Buddha statue are added attractions. You can easily spend 2-3 hours here if you are seeking full details of the artifacts. The shrine is a small part of this complex and worth a visit.

Entry fee for foreign tourist is $2 or LKR 500 per person this includes Seema Malakaya also.

Title: This Buddhist temple is a must see in Colombo
Text: We were encouraged to visit this temple by someone we met on the street in Colombo. We were not disappointed as this is,one of the most most amazing Buddhist empowered we have ever seen. So many rooms with so many relics. Prepare to see vintage cars, display cases of watches, jewelry and even cameras that people have donated. It is practically a museum or antique store (but cant buy anything). Fascinating really. This is a must see in Colombo and you will need at least a couple of hours to visit it well.

Title: Must Visit in Colombo
Text:
One can't miss this amazing Buddhist Temple while in Colombo. Rich in cultural heritage and history, this beautiful temple also houses a museum which has the smallest Buddha statue in the world in an enclosure. Various Buddha statues adorn the temple, one of the most notable one would be the Jade Buddha. The temple would take a couple of hours to look around and is worth the time spent. 
The Beira Lake situated close by to the temple is a couple of minutes walk away  and a good idea to visit during sunset.

Title: Bizarre Temple Of Wonder
Text: This is not your average temple.  Filled with old cars, thousands of wat hes, ceramics and old items that should be on a junk yard, yet pure of Great Buddhist culture, chanting and wisdom, this is perhaps the most bizarre place I have visited.

Title: Amazing temple in the middle of Colombo
Text: We loved our visit to Gangaramaya Temple. The temple was an interesting view of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, and we were able to watch as devotees prayed in this sacred place

Title: Temple visit as part of tuk tuk tour
Text: Beautiful temple in a beautiful location. It is interesting to have a guide if you are unfamiliar with the religions.

Title: A must see
Text:
On arrival we had to pay a small entrance fee to enter this beautiful temple. We had to remove our shoes and all the ladies had to cover their legs and shoulders with coverings provided.

It was very interesting to see the different Buddhas and worship places, lots of colour and detail.

Definitely a must see when in Colombo

Title: Famous and Popolour temple among locals
Text: Entry fee is free.  Taking photo with some restriction   Hindu God also available in the temple Worth to visit

Title: Impressed so much
Text: Every point of this temple impressed me so much. The buddhism theme and art was very powerful on ?ts every corner. Museum area was very beatiful, and all of the building are worth to visit place.

Title: Pleasant Temple with much to see.
Text:
A must see temple in Colombo and in Sri Lanka, in general. Aside from the entrance fee for foreigners, the temple offers such a peaceful atmosphere and energy. 

The temple and surrounding areas are occupied by multiple smaller and larger spaces to view carvings, ancient pieces and script that relate to Buddhism, outdoor places of worship including a large Bo tree as well as a small glass box which houses a claimed hair relic of Buddha. 

A lovely experience where you can spend 10-15 minutes walking through and glancing briefly or close to 1 or 2 hours, taking your time to go through all the pieces, ancient scrips and items.

Title: Puzzling experience
Text:
Firstly, we were surprised to be charged entry. It's not expensive but, when we got home, we read on the ticket that the cost was for visiting the other temple, Seemamalakaya on the other side of the road, as well but when we went there they charged us again, even though we told them we had just come from Gangaremaya. 
Secondly, the whole place felt more like a bric-a-brac shop than a temple. The displays of gifts to the temple was higgledy-piggledy and there were no signs or explanations  as to where anything had come from. And such an extraordinary array of "stuff" from vintage cars to plastic toy dinosaurs, from safes to weighing scales; watches, jewellery, pianos and even rifles. It did not feel very sacred. It seemed to be more about materialism. I have been to many temples, much less important, and with far less objects but with way more feeling of Buddhism. 
Sorry, but quite disappointing.

Title: Tranquil Temple
Text: Like Indiana Jones with jet flag we decided to explore this temple at 6am after landing at 1am. At that time it was peaceful and serene with locals praying under the Bohdi try and us strolling somewhat aimlessly. Given there were no tourists we didnt/couldnt pay for entry and were left to our own devices. The temple has lots of nooks and crannies and so many strange items that he been donated. Whilst most of these items are far from treasures it was nice to slowly take stroll around and immersive time capsule.

Title: Definitely visit this temple.
Text:
Its a nice temple and worth a visit.  We hired a tuk tuk to take us around and it was his first stop.  A worthy temple with more than just the normal bunch of Buddha statues.  One of the exhibits has a piece of Buddhas hair. Theres also a vast collection antiques and even old cars and some guns and jewelry.  

The cost of admission $2 or 300 rubles is low and its worth 1/2 hour to tour it.  Reminder to dress appropriately

Title: Interesting place to visit
Text:
Short visit to the temple with our Tuk Tuk guide. A wander through to many donated items.
Worth a visit

Title: My Tour of Srilanka (Dec 2019)
Text: I Visited Srilinka with my family and friends.  This place is peaceful and clam.  This is an important attraction in Colombo.

Title: Very accessible
Text: Because Buddhism is the national religion, Buddhist temples are "everywhere". The Gangaramaya Temple in Colombo is one of the city's most prominent, important, and well-known temples. Situated near Beira Lake, it is readily accessible by road, including being on many bus routes. A quiet oasis from the hustle and bustle which is Colombo.

Title: It's just OK
Text: Its surely a good place to visit but you will not miss something great if you miss it. Places in Dambulla are much better , however those with core religious mindset should go.

Title: Nice Tempel with hidden elephant on chains
Text:
I did not like the place. Our driver showed us sadly the hidden temple elephant. The elephant is on the other side of the street (in a backyard) and bound to chains for the whole day: One on the front leg and one on the back leg. 
He can not move for one step for the whole day. He looked very sad and tried the whole time to move.
The driver told us, that he hast to be like that 24/7 except the temple need the elephant for a ceremony.
We were really wondering how the monks could treat an animal without any respect.
My kids were so sad, that the refused to enter the temple.
I tried to ask the monk about the elephant. He just get angry and shouted to me.
Therefore, I do not recommend to visit this place.

Title: December 31 st
Text: We visited on December 31st night at 23:00 and it was worth visiting I must say. The aura, atmosphere, chantings were a blessing.

Title: Must visit place.
Text: Amidst the bustle of Colombo the white jade Samadhi Budha sits peacefully at the Gangaramaya Temple inviting the faithful for a time of worship. The statue that weighs 8 Tons inspires reverence. The statues of the Vitaraka Buddha and the Laughing Buddha carved out of natural ruby are rare sights in Sri Lanka. The statues that are placed at the Temple are a treasured or devotees and explorers. There is a entry fee for non Sri Lankans.

Title: Beautiful temple in a serene surrounding
Text:
Loved this Buddhist Temple and its grounds. The entrance fee was 300 Sri Lankan Rupees and there is a place to keep your footwear. Free sarong to cover up for women wearing shorts.

It was interesting to see an idol of the Hindu god, Ganesh at the entrance. The place is loaded with gifts from devotees. We saw a wedding in progress.

Title: Not maintained
Text:
It doesn't feel like a temple at all. There are many deities of Hindus and numerous Budhha statues. It's a museum of antiques. They charge foreigners and you can negotiate the cost!
The lake temple is in worse state. Overall wasn't a pleasant experience

Title: Buddha temple
Text:
This a very big sacred buddhist temple in Colombo.
There is a hair of Lord Buddha,and a big muslim..
Foreign visitors have to pay entry ticket.Shoes are not allowed.

Title: A Historical Heritage cum Temple site
Text:
This Temple is more of a museum besides being a sacred site. It houses several arte facts, antiques such as kettles, wrist watches, pieces of furniture, jewelry alongside uncountable various sized statues of Buddha including some made of pure gold and some replicas of originals of those in other parts of the world. 

It would be a delight for a History lover to do research at this temple. The outer walls too are depictions of various life scenes from Gautum Buddha's life. We witnessed people praying there and making offerings at the Bodhi Tree and were also shown a hair relic of the Buddha.

Title: Go in the evening
Text: We went in the evening as we had a ticket from a different temple which allowed entry into both.  It was wonderful. Quiet, and more impressive because of the lights inside. We also went during the day as part of a tour we had signed up for and it was less impressive and very crowded.

Title: Oldest Temple in Colombo
Text:
As a Japanese traveler i love to  visit temples and srilankan temples are one of my most favorites. i went to here as i told my tour company (srilanka travellers) to make some temple visit in the itinerary after visiting temples out from colombo at last i came to this beautiful temple most of the things inside are verh antique and very beautiful. even if it's in the capital of colombo when u went inside u wont feel any disturbance as ur mind will get peacefull in here
recommend to people who  love to visit temples.
ARIGATO

Title: Tranquility at its best
Text:
The place is so so clean despite the incredible footfall from various travel agent tours ...
It was really nice to see the traditions being maintained... amidst the tourist footfall. 
I somehow get that they could introduce audio guides to assist with the history of the place in the near Future:)

Title: Interesting
Text: We visited within the city tour, it is a nice place, lots of history and things to see, so many Buddhas as expected and very ancient items. To go inside you need to remove your shoes, so if you are not up to it, I recommend to wear socks that you can use to visit these places, they allow it. You can take pictures of everything but never selfies or any other pictures giving the back to the Buddhas, so be careful. They have the smallest Buddha statue and a piece of hair, difficult to see due to the lack of cleanliness of the glass, but interesting anyway. A must to visit in Colombo

Title: Very interesting collection
Text:
A good temple in the city, some of the collection is amazing and very well kept. 
Cheap entry fee too. Lots of people have donated their belongings

Title: Gangaramaya Temple Visi
Text: Chamring temple in the midst of busy Colombo. There are lots and lots and lots of collections, trinkets and countless statues of Buddha, big and small. Interesting to see how many devoted pilgrims just praying, touching and providing offerings. Highlight for me was the huge sculpture of Nawan Raja the elephant that had served at the temple for 25 years, albeit according to some a form of animal cruelty.

Title: Impressive temple with unique touches (Rolls Royce, anyone?)
Text: Gangaramaya Temple is Sri Lanka's most important Buddhist site. It is centered around a tree that is said to have grown from a cutting of the Bodhi Tree in India, under which Siddhartha Gotama (the Buddha) is said to have meditated for 49 days before receiving enlightenment. The temple features a large Buddha statue flanked by smaller statues of followers, a variation we have not seen before; it strikes us as a nod to the Hindu temples with their many colorful figures. The temple complex is also a museum, with its attractions designed to draw in visitors who will make donations. There is a seated figure carved from ruby. Copper wall panels depicting Buddhist themes are a feature we've seen nowhere else. There are even worldly goods like vintage Rolls-Royces, donated to the temple by believers.

Title: Gangaramaya Temple Visit
Text: This one of the very informative temple some one can learn Buddhist Religion within very short time. We took our daughter's boy friend this time and he was very pleased to learn about the religion. Maha Nayake Thero was very calm and was able to explain all the foundation on the religion.

Title: Beautiful, Interesting and rich experience
Text:
This place is beautiful, charming and has a lot to see. 

There is charm in its chaotic arrangement and structure but Unfortunately there is not much public information available in English in signs, explanatory planks or posters, which is a pity because there is so much to see. 

Furthermore in hot days the place is a liberal sauna, which could seriously benefit from some climate control if not for the visitors than for the sake of relics and treasures the place houses.

Title: Its most popular in Colombo
Text:
Its day 12 here in Sri Lanka 

I visited 4 cities but didnt go to any temple 
I met local Frind in lobby of hotel in Colombo we was talk about religions than I ask him to take to most famous temple in town 

I like the Place lot of stuff to see

Title: Didnt meant to visit but I was there
Text:
I was walking around the neighbourhood and found this Gangaramaya Temple.

I was fascinated by its look from outside and decided to join.

As anywhere else, there is a special entrance price for foreigners but its worth while observing inside.

I was most impressed by the bao tree inside the temple. Displays are mishmash but very interesting.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text: The Temple is easily visited.  There are many rooms and it appears more like a museum at times. At night there was a musical performance.

Title: Treasure trove for history buffs and relic hunters
Text:
While this is called a buddhist temple, it is more a collection of all sorts of relics and antiquities. It ranges from statues to stuffed elephants, watches, cars, ivory and even has Lord Buddha's original hair!!

If you are into that sort of stuff, you will spend a long time here as there is just too much to see and it is just lying around. They have not organised it very well and you will need to take your time to find what you are looking for.

Must not miss - Lord Buddha's hair, world's smallest Buddha statue, huge ivory tusks (hard to miss), 14kg solid ruby Buddha statue, Rolls Royce cars, ancient manuscripts.

Be warned that men and women alike need to cover their shoulders and wear trousers covering their knees. If you are not dressed appropriately then the temple will offer you shawls that you can use to wrap around yourself once you pay the entrance fee.

Also, while photos are allowed, it is considered rude to take selfies as your back will be towards Buddha.

Title: Budist temple
Text: Very nice , large number of Budha statues are there, they are asking donation for entry ,and for keeping chappals.

Title: Holiday
Text: Temple is absolutely amazing. Beautifully kept and very clean. A must visit when in Sri Lanka. Well done.

Title: Different temple
Text: Very interesting place with numerous gifts and offerings that were also interesting. Worth visiting. Various different Buddhas to be seen. Nice atmosphere

Title: An over-the-top Buddhist temple with an interesting collection
Text: So glad we visited this temple. The first temple was amazing, I've never seen anything quite that colourful, almost over-the-top. Interesting collection of painting, statues and memorabilia (Rolls Royces,  Rolexes and antiques). There is a Bodhi tree (a fig tree), as well as a majestic stupa (sealed dome-shaped structure that contains symbolic relics and the ashes of Buddhist monks). I would be remiss if I didn't mention the temple elephant chained behind the building; what a shame that this tradition continues in this day and age.

Title: Peaceful
Text: Amazing feeling so much to see and learn.. feels like time stop in the temple ..donations really appreciated over there to help other small temple so we told but worth to visit if u in colombo

Title: Chained elephant at the back of the temple!!!!
Text:
I am a tourist currently staying in Sri Lanka, Colombo. Yesterday, I visited Gangaramaya buddhist temple. It is indeed a beautiful place with an amazing history behind it. Nonetheless its glory is greatly undermined as in the parking just opposite the temple, on a small patch of land, people keep an elephant that is chained. I can't understand what could possibly be the reason of keeping such a great wild animal in the middle of Colombo, chained and without space to move, and as much as I respect the buddhist culture and its traditions, I really feel the call to do something about this. Apparently the elephant has been chained there for 20 years! I can't even imagine this in the 21st century when we know how precious are these animals, and Sri Lanka has so many elephant orphanages. Apparently again, as people at the temple did not want to talk to me about the elephant as if it was some kind of a secret, they use the elephant for sacred services at the temple. The temple itself is full of animal relics, such as tusks, ivory statues, elephant legs, head and even a tail. There is also a huge stuffed elephant called Raja, which had its tusks growing in a peculiar way and was considered sacred. 
Is this the way to protect these majestic animals of Sri Lanka? Surely not. Please help me take actions and change its life.

Title: Tour the Temples
Text: We did this temple with a tour guide on a Tuk Tuk and he was incredibly knowledgeable. The artifacts and idols were incredible to see the smallest Buddha in the world was on display which was so detailed. It was great to get involved whilst inside. Worth doing.

Title: Good tourisp spot
Text: One of the places to visit in Colombo. Has good collection of antique items in their museum. There is a collection of old watches, old war memorials and other artifacts

Title: So much to see
Text: I was impressed by this temple and the collection that is presented here. It's great value for money and a great way to lose a few hours. The only thing that would improve it would be notices to give information about some of the artifacts.

Title: Divine
Text: Beautiful Buddha Temple. Must visit. its a divine and serine experience. Huge Buddha statues made in Jade and mural paintings. Divine chantings were so soothing to hear.

Title: Stunning
Text:
A lovely spiritual visit .
Though busy - you will never feel that it is busy - all is calm and tranquil. each person is allowed to be there in their  own personal moment .
Lots to see and appreciate and experience .
So grateful for the blessed opportunity.

Title: Awful place, avoid like the plague. Elephant kept chained
Text: Having visited many temple all over Asia this place is just a tourist trap. Nothing impressive to see. 300 rupees even though the hotel and guidebook told us its 100 at the door. Building work taking place, no way is this a place for meditation. The saddest thing was when the monks brought out a chained elephant who clearly looked distressed - no place for a wild animal. Upsetting, where is there compassion

Title: Must be in your visit list for Colombo trip
Text: Its Buddhist Temple and museum. Center corridor has lord Buddha statue and around other corridor is for museum. Place is calm and has both opportunity religiousness and photography.

Title: This temple is like visiting a museum.
Text: This temple is a must visit if you are in Colombo. It is beautiful. We liked it. It not really old, but had some quiet and peaceful atmosphere, it is really relaxing. You can spend some time in here. And there was many artefacts related to Sri-Lanka and the Buddhist culture.

Title: More of a museum...
Text:
The bodhi tree area is quite spiritual. Rest of the area is more like a museum with mostly photography opportunities. 
Worth visit once.

Title: Very beautiful temple
Text: I visited this temple in April 2019. Temple is well located in city. It has big statue of Lord Buddha. It has so many antic pieces of many different items (like camera, knives, coins etc). Entey fee is 1000 LKR per person for foreign visitors. You can also use same ticket for another Buddha temple located near by in lake. It's just 500 meters from this temple.

Title: Wonderful working temple and museum
Text:
There is a lot to see and absorb in this wonderful working temple.
Situated in  the heart of Colombo, this large Buddhist Temple contains many beautiful Buddhas, many of which have been donated. One of the most visited is a 228cm gold leaf plated Buddha made from jade stone. Many other Buddhas and statues are displayed including a large elephant. At he back of the temple is a museum quality eclectic collection of artifacts providing reminders of this countries past that extends from old cars to watches. 

Our guide reminded us that we were told not to take any photos with a person by the Buddha. We obliged but many disrespectful people still pose or take selfies at Buddhas.

Title: Temple  in a museum
Text: Good collect of Articraft and Buddha...the entry fee  for temple is not fair and acceptable.....This temple has hindu sacred tree at the centre of the temple and it has got  collection of of vintage cars

Title: Must see this
Text: This temple is the most interesting temple and to spend hours and hours looking at all the little trinkets and relicts. A museum of the ages. Go find ya he one donation box that sings a song for your generosity....

Title: Gangaramaya Buddhist Temple
Text: A Buddhist temple which was imposing and unique. Vast number of various offerings ranging from wrist watches to cars were on display. An important destination in Colombo to be covered by any visitor.

Title: So many Buddhas
Text:
This temple has so many Buddhas. The main parts of the temple are ornate and colourful. 
The rest of the temple is more of an antique collection, but does have some interesting artefacts. 
Strangely, mainly because I do not know why, they have a stuffed elephant here. It is clear this elephant had some significance, but I never found out what it was. 
The island lake temple has some good photo opportunities.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Please stop for a visit. Beautiful temple. Lots to see. Ancient tree in the middle. Ladies will be asked to cover arms and all shoes are too be removed before entering. Small fee for vistors to enter. Lots of photo opportunities.

Title: Good learning experience
Text: If you are interested to know some history around Buddhism in Sri Lanka , view antiques and historic collections relating to Buddhism,  this is the place to go. They have a museum which showcases the footprint of buddha in colombo , some amazing statues and antiques, and also a huge auspicious Bodhi tree. Worth a visit if you are in colombo!

Title: A must watch
Text:
I loved the ambience and the impeccable way that its maintained. 
High point - was the Budhdha relic
The idols of ruby and jade are a treat for the eyes.
The jade Budhdha is amazing too.
The  statue of Budhdha and the decor around should not be missed

Title: Very nice. Worth a visit
Text: The temple has a number of relics which are very nice. The temple also has a number of jade and ruby Buddha statues which is very nice. Its well maintained and certainly worth a visit.

Title: Quirky temple
Text: This temple has an interesting collection of local as well as Chinese artifacts, as well as old cars, and it's great place to meditate, and walk around its interesting grounds. Also it looks lovely at night with all the lights but it's closed for visitors at night time.

Title: Place for Peace of Mind
Text: I visited this Temple with Er chander Sain of Delhi- This is mixed temple of Hindu and Buddhist Culture. We get picked up outside our Cinnamon red hotel by Tuk tuk to go to the largest temple in Colombo from Galdari Hotel. Whatever you do negotiate the price FIRST BEFORE GETTING IN. Our driver parked and walked with us giving us a guided tour of the whole temple. Its quite old with a lot of gold and a lot of history. This is the strangest place - a very grand temple, which is used by locals for worship, and well worth a visit on its own. Then there is the most crazy collection of things, just piled into cabinets or display cases with little or no explanation - reading glasses, watches, cameras, Encyclopedia Britannica. Also I counter Regretfully, to me it looked more like a warehouse of unrelated things than a place for awe, for meditation and for prayer - just an eclectic accumulation of items, many of which had little to do with Buddhism.Also return by Tuk Tuk to Galdari Hotel.

Title: Gangaramaya tour
Text:
We get picked up outside our Cinnamon red hotel by Tuk tuk to go to the largest temple in Colombo. Whatever you do negotiate the price FIRST BEFORE GETTING IN. Our driver parked and walked with us giving us a guided tour of the whole temple. Its quite old with a lot of gold and a lot of history.
Our driver then took us to a couple more places (Independence Hall) and a jewelry store before talking us back to the hotel.

Title: Lovely temple, and bizarre collection of things
Text:
This is the strangest place - a very grand temple, which is used by locals for worship, and well worth a visit on its own.
Then there is the most crazy collection of things, just piled into cabinets or display cases with little or no explanation - reading glasses, watches, cameras, Encyclopedia Britannica. Then onto some vintage cars including a Rolls Royce, and outside along the footpath, a big collection of old machinery such as printing presses!
Certainly unlike any other temple I've visited.
They're happy for you to take photos, and there's also a toilet (but only for tourists.....)

Title: Not worth your time ...
Text: Regretfully, to me it looked more like a warehouse of unrelated things than a place for awe, for meditation and for prayer - just an eclectic accumulation of items, many of which had little to do with Buddhism.. The Dmbulla Cave Temples and the Alu Viharaya Temple in Matale would give you a much better feeling about Buddhism in Sri Lanka...

Title: Temple cum Museum
Text:
As the name suggest it is primarily a Buddhist Temple, but there are also some Hindu deities worshiped in the temple. The temple also has different sections where various types of items have have been displayed. The items range not only from religious items, relics to idols of deities, but also Automobiles, old discarded consumer items, antiques and many other things. Some items on display are quiet interesting.
Overall, the temple appears more like a Museum. There is a nominal fee charged for entering the temple. All the sections are clearly numbered and marked.
The stroll through the displays overwhelms the senses as there is so much on display. All the items are not very systematically displayed and there is a lot of clutter.
This is, though, a place worth visiting.

Title: Bhuddist temple?
Text:
Wasnt sure if I was at a Bhuddist Temple or an audition for the BBCs antiques roadshow.
The place is full of antiques. Jewellery, traction engines, printing presses, you name it, it was there.
There was an interesting tree inside but as for the rest! Surfice to say I wont be rushing back.

Title: Worth a visit, certainly some interesting artifacts around the temple and museum area
Text: Worth a visit, certainly some interesting artifacts around the temple and museum area.  You can easily spend 1-2 hours.  Watch for the elephant! How it fits around the museum display cases without knocking things over is beyond me.

Title: Very nice working temple
Text: Bit of a different temple. Large typical Buddhist temple but with a museum feel. It's loaded with "offerings" from devotees on display, all manner of things,classic cars, jewellery, watches, gemstones, all manner of ivory artefacts and so much more. If you like perusing you will like this. I did as we're a bit templed out. We got in for free after visiting the nearby lake temple using the same ticket on the same day. We went late evening and not many people, just worshipers, incence and chanting. The much spoken about elephant was apparently in a nearby park. Bit quirky worth a visit. Don't know about elephant but other negative reviews a bit unfair I think.

Title: charming temple surrounded by water
Text: When my guide first took me there I couldn't believe this. This much charming peaceful temple in the middle of a rushed city. It was a old temple with a quite a history. also it has a museum. I saw some of very old printing machines in the museum which was quite interesting. you need to buy a ticket to enter the place. there were young local couple who came to worship. They were kind enough to share flowers with me and taught me how to do the rituals for Lord Buddha. had a nice evening thanks to my guide - Roshan.

Title: the closest temple in the city of Colombo
Text: This temple is very attracting. You can see directly the activities for the pilgrims and the visitors together. Many antiques things can be found in the areas. very interesting temple.

Title: Lovely Temple but why is the Elephant chained up!!!!!
Text:
We found it quite distressing to see this elephant chained up, it took away the enjoyment of what is a lovely temple.
We werent the only tourists who found it difficult especially as they would like donations and I got the impression that they thought the elephant would help.

It is a very nice temple with lots to look at but as you can tell we hated this exploitation.

Title: Great temple and museum
Text:
Be sure and take an english speaking guide.  That said we had a great tour by our tuk tuk driver and also met a very personable monk that spoke some english and we enjoyed meeting him and hearing about his life.
Don't miss the automobiles that have been donated to the temple on the lower lever including 2 Rolls Royce and a bullet proof Jaguar from the first president of Sri Lanka.  Must be the world's record for statues of Buddha.
Allow at least 2 hours.

Title: Relaxing
Text: A thought provoking place to visit. However the chained elephant on the site is not something to relish. It was depressed and clearly suffering. An interesting Buddhist dilemma.

Title: Genuine cultural immersion.
Text: Go at night for an eternal experience! Lots to observe. Lots to look at. Some special stuff and real treasures as well as some surprises like the museum load of benefactor bequests including furniture and old cars!

Title: Pretty amazing temple and showcase
Text: Our guide took us to this temple, and it was one of the most impressive of our Asian tour.  You will need to take off your shoes, and for a small price they will be put in a special area, although it didn't look much more protected than the sidewalk.  The main temple and the one closest to the street is gorgeous.  The exterior of the building is highly decorated, and the interior is stunning.  There is not a lot of room inside for all of the statues, pillars, etc. but it is definitely worth a lingering look.  Once you leave this building, things get very interesting.  There is a centuries old sacred tree, but the most surprising thing about this temple was all of the "stuff," and I do mean stuff.  The faithful leave gifts and these gifts include beautiful religious objects, but also dining room sets, money clips, even artillery shells.  These objects are housed in several buildings, and if you have a very diligent guide he will want you to see everything.  By the time you arrive to the building with the machine gun behind a glass case, you will be exhausted.  You might discuss with your guide that you are interested in the main features of the temple complex so that you won't end up spending more time than you wish.  That said, it is very beautiful and worth the stop.

Title: A serene temple in the middle of the bustling city .. (w/ a pricey entrance fee)
Text:
- a refreshing visit from the rest of the bustling city
- expensive entrance fee for local standard
-

Title: A well maintained Buddhist temple
Text: This is a well maintained Buddhist temple in the heart of Colombo City with roadside parking. Apart from the usual prayer room, they hold a huge collection of items of Buddhist era and a good museum. The foreign visitors have to pay an entrance fee of SLR 300. One may need a little over an hour to cover this temple in full.

Title: Huge Buddhist temple
Text:
This is one of the most important temples in Sri Lanka. It is said that the tree they worship here is grown out of a branch of the tree where Buddha has been meditating. The temple itself looks like a huge museum. Lot of pieces collected over the years.
Entrance fee is rs300

Title: Nice temple
Text: Nice temple, personally I think in need of a little maintenance and education sources for tourists visiting as its always nice to have a little more knowledge available

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Great temple just don't bother going for the evening service
Text:
Our guide took us in the evening to see the great buddha tooth - we queued for over 30mins in the heat (no AC inside and lots of people) with people trying to push infront of us! When finally the awful loud procession music stopped, the queue moved forward to see the tooth - except is behind about 2 distance walls of glass and you're not allowed to stop so I had no idea what i was looking at, honestly comical. And locals leave offering to the 'buddha tooth' that the monks love im sure. 
The temple itself is lovely, lots of detail, nice paintings but don't go with the crowds in the evening its not worth it. Enjoy it at a quieter time to take it all in. 
(Note - there is a place to store shoes outside as you have to take them off so pack socks as the floor is dirty) 
Theres also a weird room with a huge stuffed elephant that the president or someone loved. After going to the elephant freedom project sanctuary earlier in the week (highly recommend) it felt cruel he had this as a pet in his garden.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Visit hampered by rains
Text: Visited in the evening with some ongoing rain. You don't get to see the tooth even from a distance and there is an entry ticket of 1500 SLR for foreigners. Can avoid if you are not a pilgrim.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Without any information got in advance, you won't understand what's happening and why
Text:
If you are not a religious person that understands where to go, when and what's happening there at that moment, you won't enjoy the place much, neither the ceremony that happens at the place when it's open to the public. Not to mention that the place is a maze and it took me and my boyfriend some time to get to the entrance that we needed. Different prices for locals and for tourists are present also here, as everywhere else at Sri Lanka. 
The ceremony is a mass activity where a lot of people pushes themselves to a certain place at the temple, and you push yourself to get there also, since you don't know why are others pushing themselves so much. The fact it, the religious people want to give their offerings to the temple and to Buddha. You will end up in a room where everyone is packed, waiting to get to the room for offerings, where you won't get. So since you know about this now, you don't need to push yourself together with them and I have just saved you some time and nerves. 
Instead of pushing yourself with the mass, I recommend you to walk around the temple and the parts that are accessible for the visitors, and e.g. burn some candles as your offering outside. The place looks magical, especially in the evening when it's already dark outside. To burn something, you need to buy a special oil for that. I didn't figure out where to do that, unfortunately. 
What got me was a payment payment machine looking as an ATM that could be used for donations for the temple. Like wow. A way to go, The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic! This is what I call progress.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting and lovely views
Text:
Our driver took us here and it was helpful having him to explain everything. Lots to look at, was a nice experience. 

There's a small entrance fee. Shoulders and knees must be covered.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Such a Sacred and Beautiful place
Text: This place is well maintained and well organized. As a tourist you are sent different ways to enter the temple.  You can always take some amazing lotus flowers to honor the place.  One of its kind in the world and well worth a visit.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Definitely visit
Text:
Was a nice holy place to visit I believe in July or august each year there is quite a bit of fanfare around this article 
We understand not many have actually seen the tooth relic

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Amazing location
Text: amazing place to visit kandy. Beautiful painting. Its super also beautiful culture dance dont miss it

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Worth the visit.
Text:
We visited in the evening, when the pooja (drum ceremony) was on. Our guide had a lot of information for us as well, so I'd recommend having one to know what's going on, but even without, the visit is interesting.
The weather was beautiful, so it made it even nicer to be out and with the locals.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Animal abuse at religious institutikn
Text:
Made the mistake of visiting the temple on a Saturday. The crowd was extensive and we had to literally juggle ourselves through. Therefore could not really enjoy the experience as we were pushed aroubd a lot
Also feel it so unfair that Foreigners get charged so much more for visiting the facility.
What upset me mist was the mistreatment of the elephant that was on display. Not only was it in chains but clearky visible wounds were present where the chains were tied. Where are the animal rights activists?

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Best to see kandy
Text: Nice temple. 2500 years old buddha tooth it is amazing. Lot local people but real place to see in kandy.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A favourite place, calm and beautiful.
