Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: The temple is already sacred and being in Kandy makes it divine
Text: Kandy was not in my list and not even the temple unless someone suggested me and so made time to visit this place in my tour to Srilanka and after reaching Kandy you find the place is not any typical of hill stations its do surround by lush green huge hills with lake and the temple. the temple itself is quite important for Buddhist and it being in beautiful place like kandy makes its divine.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Beautiful temple in the heart of Kandy
Text: We spent about 3 hours visiting this beautiful temple close by the lake.  A very special place for Buddhists and the queues waiting to visit the room where the relic is stored was very long. Incredible building and grounds. Well worth a visit

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Nice place
Text: Overall the temple is worth the visit. However, if you are a foreign visitor they charge you 1500 Rs... and remember to wear long pants, otherwise they wont let you in.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

You dont queue, you just push your way and get your elbows out, as the Sri Lankans dont queue!  All a bit crazy, totally wasteful with all the flowers given, and then thrown away every day. Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Text:

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Text:
What is the sense in charging anyone to enter a site that is designated as a place of worship?  Another place where Sri Lankans grab money from foreigners.  

They should stop using animals for their parades held in August.  The elephants are chained and harassed by the mahouts.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Clean. Well maintained. Not pricey. Historical importance.
Text:
This is the place where they house the tooth of the the great Gautam Buddha. 

Points to note:
1. Pl wear at least knee length clothes to respect the area and the concept. 
2. Avoid visiting during peak noon hours as the distance between the shoe stand and the covered temple premise is a long one and you may get discomfort due to the heated stoned pathway.
3. Take a guide and as k him not to hurry.
4. Do not take snaps with the idols in the background. It is considered as a mark of disrespect.

My experience for a guide was not very great. So, will not dwell in this issue much. The entry fees is less for SAARC country members, so pl use the correct machine. The machine is automated well enough to provide you with the tickets. 

The casket - made of gold and the tooth is protects is not open throughout the year. So, check your visit date and EXPECT accordingly. 

There is a museum within this premises and it is heart touching enough to see how well they have created the various blocks of all countries where Buddhism is or was prevalent.

Date of Experience : March 2019.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Nice!
Text: It's a nice Buddhist temple. We were clueless and confused without a guide. It would help if you could hire a guide or someone who could explain and tell the history.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Serene
Text:
Lovely Temple. Beautiful and serene. Good walk around about an hour. Shoes off.
Buddhist Temple in the Royal Palace Complex.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Guides are 1000-1500 rs

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of Lord Buddha 's sacred tooth relic at Kandy, Sri Lanka
Text:
Considered as a sacred temple complex containing the sacred tooth relic of Lord Buddha, Shri Dalada Maligawa also known as Palace of sacred tooth.

This temple is a must visit for every Buddhist.

The tooth relic was originally housed in a rock carved temple in Anuradha pura before it was moved to the present palace / temple at Kandy about five hundred years ago.

This centuries old temple is serene and the worshippers pray in silence.

The temple was originally built as a royal residential palace by the royal family of Sri Lanka long time ago.

The remarkable features of this temple is the renowned recital of Kandy drums is a joy to hear.

The musical performance is unique for Sri Lanka.The musical instruments are two drums and a pipe instrument. The performance lasting about half an hour is precisely choreographed.

The puja timings are fixed  lasting about half an hour three times in a day - morning, noon and evening.

The temple premises are very well secured and spotless maintenance is visible everywhere.

You need to be properly dressed to enter the temple. Ensure that your shoulder and knees are covered.

The temple management treats every body equal. No preference seems to be given for any one. There is no shouting at or pushing of the pilgrims in the sanctum sanctorium. Everything is done in dignified silence.

The temple is a must visit while you are in Kandy, Sri Lanka.

Highly recommended.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Awesome Experience
Text: In my opinion its best to go to the temple in the evening around 6:30pm at dusk. The temples lights up and you get to witness the ceremonies in the temple. It was a great experience and culturally enriching.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Text: Normally crowded place with all people wearing white clothes. very peaceful place. many flowers, candles, incense sticks.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting Buddhist history
Text: Large Buddhist temple and surrounding buildings and grounds. Lord Buddhas tooth relic is here and can be seen on special occasions. The most spiritual place for Buddhists in Sri Lanka. Make sure your shoulders and knees are covered, both men and women.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting temple
Text:
This is a significant temple for Buddhists and was interesting for a short visit. The Buddhas tooth is housed in a special richly decorated building and not visible to the visitor.

Worth a short visit.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: interesting
Text: I guess when in Kandy it's a worthwhile visit, just be careful and don't get conned into taking a tour guide...certainly useful but there are some uninformed self appointed guides at the gates with a recitation in head and you dare not interrupt them whilst on tour. We stupidly got someone to "guide" us and each time we had a question he got more and more annoyed with us. Eventually he stormed off and we were told to ask our "English masters"...funny thing neither my husband nor I are Brits!! The temple itself is lovely and its certainly best to go as early as possible.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Calm and quite place
Text:
One of the best places I have visited during last year and it was so calm and quite place to stay for 2 3 hours. During evening time there are lots of tourists are there and locals too. 
You have to dress in white and cover all over your body because of sacred thing of the place.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of Calmfulness
Text:
We had this amazing temple tour which we loved the most. Before you enter you have to cover your whole body and it would be better if you use white cloths. 
Inside you will find spiritual calmfulness. 
They will charge around less than $10 to enter the temple but its really worth the money you spend. 
You can find a guide who will teach you history of the temple.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A real privilege to witness this ceremony
Text: We attended the 5:30am (and least crowded) ceremony at the Temple of the Tooth.  The impressive temple complex houses the single most important relic in the Buddhist faith, the tooth of the Buddha, and devotees turn up in great numbers with offerings and prayers as the casket containing the tooth is briefly displayed.  It was a real privilege to witness this special moment (although you dont actually get to see the tooth) and later explore the riches the temple complex has to offer.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Have to do it, UNESCO site
Text: One needs to go here early since many people queuing to give offerings to Buddha. There were very few tourists, but then, the country does not have that many tourists. Entrance includes some other museums, including the World Museum of Buddhism. Even if you are not religious, this is very informative. Highly recommend it.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Beautiful
Text:
We visited the temple as part of our tour of Sri Lanka and it is certainly not to be missed! Our driver took us around and it was great to have a guide with us to tell us about the history.

It was very busy around midday (and very hot!) but absolutely worth the visit. It's a much larger area than we first thought so take the time to look around and visit the museum there too. 

Shoulders and knees must be covered, photos allowed in most areas (but don't turn your back for a selfie!).

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Evening Ceremony
Text: We visited Temple of the Tooth in the evening and watched the Puja Ceremony. There are 3 ceremonies every day 6am, 10am and 6pm. Both men and women must have their shoulders and knees covered. During the ceremony drummers fill the air with rhythmic beats and  prayers.  People line up for the chance to catch a glimpse of the golden case with the tooth inside and offerings of flowers are laid before the sacred tooths chamber. It was very interesting to go at this time of the day and it had a real ambiance about it

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Best place to visit in kandy
Text: Visiting Kandy is incomplete without visiting temple of Sacred Tooth Relic. The place is heaven for those who have interest in History.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Pleasant and peaceful place
Text:
Ancient temple that houses the Tooth relic of Lord Buddha. Very pleasant surroundings and beautiful atmosphere. Must visit for peace lovers. There's a lake nearby with splendid trees and serene location. Traditional drum music played inside the temple premises is very enchanting. It also houses elephants. There's a souvenir shop next to the temple where one can buy handicrafts and other memorabilia. 

Though quite far from Colombo airport, it is worth a visit!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Sacred and unique place !
Text:

Expect lots of walking though

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Not Buddhist
Text:
I'm not a Buddhist so I'm reviewing the place and there it excels as it is designed to wow the visitor. I would recommend going early as the place quickly fills with visitors and the faithful. In the viewing gallery there is a dedicated section for the faithful to sit and a walking route to see the Mounting Point for the tooth.
When visiting please be careful to follow the viewing route as some guides send you through the faithful.
Not really a highlight for me on this trip

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: You must see!
Text: We were on a tour so were taken to this Temple. There is a lot of security there due to a bombing 24 years ago which killed a lot of monks, there are photographs of the damage that was caused. After dropping our shoes we walked through a big hallway where there were a lot of people praying and giving flower offerings. It was very interesting and well worth a visit but once seen I wouldnt go again.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Overhyped and overpriced
Text:
Overhyped and overpriced tourist attraction/temple that doesnt seem to have much of an atmosphere or pays respect to a religion.

Its starts with paying the entrance fee, which basically feels like sponsoring the government. After dropping your shoes you enter the temple and dont really know what a logical way is to start, especially since its super crowded.

We went for the ceremony but all it really was, was some guys banging a drum really loud for more then an hour. While that happend on the first floor on the second floor a queue of people pushing each other around formed to look in to a window (for not even a second) which apparently showed something important. Im still not sure what it was.

The temple has some pretty aspects but they mainly show in the hallways in the form of patterns and wallpaintings.

After your whole experience youll go and pick up your shoes and get to deal with the guys behind the desk forcing you to put money in a donation box while clinching on to your shoes. Kind of defeats the purpose of a donation doesnt it?

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Long queue
Text: A bit of a hike from the nearest parking on a hot day. Shoes have to be left at a kiosk outside the temple and there is a dress code. No shoulders or knees allowed to be on show. There is a queue to see the tooth relic and you are not allowed time to admire it but ushered past quickly by security. We had a good guide otherwise wouldnt have a clue what it was all about.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A beautiful cultural insight
Text: We visited the Temple with our guide - the best way to have the inside knowledge. We went to see the offerings at 9.30am, at this time some separate rooms are opened which arent usually open during other hours. FYI you cant actually see the tooth; it is well protected in a stupa which is behind a closed door but open during the offering time. It was quite busy but use your manners and getting around is fine. As it is a sacred place, clothing is more strict. Leggings for women need to be covered appropriately and men preferably trousers however my husband just wore a sarong over shorts. Shoulders are also covered accordingly. Make sure you take time to see the ancient paintings portraying the story of the relic and see the taxidermy elephant!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Atmospheric working temple
Text: Spectacular temple with locals using it actively for worship. So much to see and what there is is beautiful. A must visit while in Kandy

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Timing is Everything!
Text: We were staying close to Kandy and knew that this was one of the biggest attractions in the area and our only available day to go was on a Saturday. We left early and got to the temple area around 9:30am. You must leave your shoes with a shoe keeper and buy your ticket in the same area. Make sure you are properly dressed as they will not let you in with any knee or shoulder showing (although you can buy a sarong right there if necessary). Women and men go through separate security lines and for us, the lines were extremely long and quite slow-I believe this was because of our timing. From there, you can make your way into the main temple and line up in a hectic, crowded, and sweaty manner for a VERY quick look at the golden casket which holds the sacred tooth of Buddha. From there, you are free to wander the grounds and look into the different buildings, including a museum with artifacts under glass, a room devoted to the famous temple elephant Raja the Tusker, and also some archeological artifacts. Altogether a very fascinating look into the passionate devotion to Buddha in Sri Lanka.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: profoundly moving experience
Text:
We visited this temple as part of an organised tour with Walkers tours and definitely benefited from having our guide, Sumith, giving his insight and sharing his expertise whilst we were there.  I don't think the experience would have been the same without this personal insight and informed commentary.

Firstly, to be clear you do not see the sacred tooth! If you are lucky you may get a quick peek at the casket (with its separate 5 locks) where it is housed.  If you are a tourist you can reach this by one very quick queue where Buddhists who wish to leave an offering may queue for 3 hours to reach the relic.  The feeling of reference and respect is overwhelming and moving, just close your eyes for a moment and take in the sounds of chanting and drumming, the smells of essence and offerings, the emotions shown by people of faith.  I can honestly say I felt completely overcome and still shiver at the memory.

On leaving this area there is plenty more to see which are less crowded and easier to view.  We particularly enjoyed the room with the pictures outlining the history of the sacred tooth around a statue of Buddha with another place for offerings

a must do place in Kandy, particularly if you can have an insight as to why it is so important to the people of Sri Lanka

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Good trip but a little overpriced.
Text: The temple of the tooth is a large temple which was impressive but nothing hugely original as you can't see the famous tooth. The architecture is stunning and I enjoyed our trip. The guide on the lockers where we left our shoes demanded a 100 rupee "donation" to charity, once we put the money in the box, he removed it when he thought we weren't looking and put it in his pocket. Don't fall for this if he tries to do the same to you!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Lovely temple
Text: Visited in the morning with our guide and have to say the temple is beautiful, lots of locals bringing offerings to the temple in the form of lotus flowers which were lovely. Would highly recommend a trip if in kandy

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Serene experien
Text: This visit will have a bit of a walk and climb to do. I do not recollect wheelchair access being available. The sacred tooth is placed inside a casket. Photography is permitted only of the casket, and no individuals are allowed to be photographed. Overall experience was excellent. This is a must do in Kandy.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Just okay
Text: Kind of overpriced for what it is. Nothing is especially interesting here of all the sites weve seen. The Buddhism museum is interesting and informative. Also note that while it does not say so anywhere, the dress code includes no fitted pants like yoga type pants. Apparently tight jeans and t-shirts are fine as the girl in front of me was let in no problem. Yoga pants and a long loose shirt are inappropriate? Just a heads up.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Disappointed
Text: Having visited Buddhist temples in other countries, this one was a disappointment. It was very busy, parking was a nightmare. We bought flowers and they were wiped away into the rubbish before we even left the room! Not much to see, only on special days can you see more. The cultural show afterwards was worth seeing, but beware, as groups reserve the best seats so get. There early - upstairs is good.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Beautiful but very busy
Text:
Entry fee is 1500 Slr ££6.50 per person, a guide will take you round without telling you there a fee for his service, then he expects 2000Slr (£9) tip, we gave him 1000Slr, i'll let you decide upon your own tip,
  Women & men must have shoulders & legs covered.
TIP do not turn your back to the Budha as this is a mark of DISrespect and you will be told off !

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Far too busy
Text:
Although the temple and surrounding buildings are very pretty, there really is not a lot you will see unless its a special occasion.
We queued for around 1hr, to then be ushered past a small opening with the tooth apparently is. Far too many people for it to be comfortable.
The adjourning Buddha museum was fun, but you have to really enjoy the history and geography of the religion to fully appreciate it.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Must visit place
Text:
I am not religious. We are here for however long whatever you believe in wants you to be and then that's it. Religion has been the cause for more trouble than almost anything. However going to see sights like this and respect another culture is surely a good way of learning. I might not understand people giving offerings but the passion and belief they have is hard to ignore. Yes its busy, yes we were pushed and shoved as people tried to get to give their offerings and yes you need to cover up. But respecting another way of life is surely what we all need to strive to do. It hasn't changed my mind, I'm not a believer but seeing people that are makes me rather humble.
Go and visit.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Need to buy ticket for temple
Text:
They are charging to go in the temple. 1000 LKR per person.
I have paid first time in my entire life to visit a temple.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Culturally important
Text: Another example of free entry for locals and huge prices for tourists. Fascinating to see the entire ceremony but there were so many people that there was a lot of pushing and shoving which detracted from the holiness and respect for the temple.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Great cultural building
Text: Very interesting temple with many local people paying respect in this historic place of worship. Beautiful flowers everywhere to give thanks to Buddha and some beautiful Buddha statues.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Must see in Kandy
Text: The most important point in Sri lanka amd Kandy city also. Its not a big place you can visit for a 1 hour and you can share your flowers.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Religeous temple
Text: We went to the temple as it was the top thing to do in Kandy. We went early and as my friend and i are nlt religeous we felt we a bit out of place walking around. If you are religious i understand the need to go here but otherwise it felt like just another temple for us. 1500 entry per person and there are signs everywhere saying not to take photos.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A must visit place
Text: Sri Dalada Maligawa, AKA Temple Tooth of Relic is a religiously important place for Buddhists. Yet worth to visit for everyone to experience the serenity and tranquility of the place,while witnessing the ancient historical context of Sri Lankan culture and Buddhism

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Very interesting and a must see in Kandy
Text: This temple is a wonderful place to experience and view the religious life of Buddhists from around the world who come to worship there. Not to be missed. There is so much going on in the large buildings and surrounding out buildings. A positive experience for my wife and me.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Great Experience
Text: It was very busy here on the day we went and it overflowing with people offering gifts and coming to worship. It was a great experience to get a feel for a different culture and religion and would highly recommend coming here. My wife had to get pins to close up the slit in her long skirt so be aware that there is a strict policy on covering up.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting Temple
Text: Worth a visit, busy with lots of people coming to worship and visit the site. Tight security to get in.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Blessed place
Text: You will definetly feel the amzing calmness wen you vist One of the blessed places in the world.a must vist place in kandy.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Kandy
Text: Excellent trip with family , awesome experience at night with the cultural show . Never miss ! Must do in Kandy in the evening .

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Visited in the morning
Text: We went in the morning and it did not seem too busy. There is an area to hand in your shoes which cost us 100 Sri Lankan Rupees.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: It wasnt anything special.  Not a must do
Text: We went there today and while it is overall a nice temple it was very mundane as far as the tooth relic is concerned.  Wheres the beef? Wheres the tooth?  Didnt see it.  Just an alter to it.  We walked around a bit and sat in the shade.  While the museum was ok I didnt see much special about this place.  And the price to Foreigners is high.  Not worth the value.  For all I know that alter has the Covenant Of The Ark behind it.  Not that seeing one of Buddhas teeth really excites me but if you are going to advertise it then show us.  If you give it a miss youre life will still be complete.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting and beautiful
Text:
We visited the tooth relic on two occasions, once in poya day and loved bern in the middle of the ceremony and we also re visited on a normal quiet day so we could soak up the atmosphere and see the beautiful buildings. 
Loved it

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Over priced for what it is
Text: I went a couple of days ago and was very disappointed- it was 1500 to get in and there was not much to see at all. Would not recommend it. I have been in many better temples elsewhere for no / minimal cost and they have been much more interesting

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Pooja
Text: The pooja was something else. The history behind the tooth was nice to learn about. A calming place of worship

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Visit to the temple on a Saturday
Text:
We came to visit on a Saturday at around 7:00am. There were already lots of devotees coming in since it was a day of worship and offering for most of the locals. 

Upon entering the temple grounds, we went to buy our tickets and leave our shoes at the designated counter.

Although I am not a Buddhist, it was still a very special spiritual feeling coming inside. Devotees mostly in white were already lined up to go to the top to give their offerings. While the relic room was not yet open, we went inside the other small rooms. One room housed many books written by Buddha himself.

Wearing modest clothes is a must. Please also be mindful and respectful of the rules. This is their sacred place of worship and we are very lucky to be granted access inside. Read the signs around and be sure to follow them.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Average temple
Text: I do understand that this temple means a lot to budists, however, tje temple didn't impress me. We came in the afternoon. First, there is check point. You shouldn't have cigarettes, lighters nor alcohol. Also, dress restrictions. Overcrowded. People standing in line to see the tooth. But you see no tooth. Just the boxes. That lasts 5min. And tourist go mad about it. Not very pleasant for worshipers.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: No clarity
Text: We visited the temple, but couldn't see the tooth as doors open at particular time. That evening, the designs time was 1830 hrs. While buying the tickets, the authority should inform about the timings. Otherwise it's a beautiful place but needs more information for the tourist. Further, there is dress restrictions, which u come to know when u reach the location. Quite unhappy with my experience.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Dont miss this
Text: This is a stunning temple and visiting it was highly informative. We had a guide who approached us and we learnt a lot as well as what to see at what time. The drummers perform in the late afternoon and it is an amazing spectacle. Highly recommended.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Yet another temple to see.
Text: Unfortunately our tour of the temple was stuffed up by our tour guide spending way too long talking about stuff. So long in fact that we missed the start of the cultural dance show. No shoes allowed.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: evening visit in heavy rain
Text: our guide rushed us here and bare footed we walked in the dark and rain to get to the Temple - well worth it we saw the evening service and whole experience was fantastic

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting Temple to visit
Text: It is definately worth taking a guide to explain some of the religious and historic importantant of the different rooms and buildings in the temple complex

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Sacred Place in Sri Lanka
Text:
This is a must visit place in Sri Lanka for every traveller, so peaceful and calm place

They charge $ 10 per adult, but really worth it

Make sureto buy some red color nice lotus to offer Lord Buddah ( Thats the way you should worship Lord Buddah )

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Highlights of Sri Lanka
Text:
First day in Sri Lanka and a nice start learning a bit about local culture and this amazing place.
We are. Not so addicted to temple or museums but this was a nice spot and a must see for Sri Lanka.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of the Tooth
Text: Everyone must visit the Temple, go in the evening to the drumming, its wonderful and we had a very nice helpful guide who told us everything we needed to know. He helped me as I have a bad leg and showed me the lift which was very helpful. Wear pants and cover your shoulders.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Not much to see.
Text: Too much touristic place. Fees everywhere. And the temple isn't that big or interesting. The ceremony that happens 3 times a day is nice to see but there is too much of a big hype around it.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Huge temples complex
Text: Amidst of Kandy is this sacred temple where it is believed that tooth of Buddha is placed. There is a big hall depicting the story behind how this tooth was brought and worshipped. Saw lot of locals bringing small babies (<6 months) to the temple(maybe some belief on longevity ?). There is an entrance fee for foreign visitors (not sure as it was arranged tour).

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Insightful Experience
Text: Well worth a visit. We walked into the temple and were shown around by a guide for a small fee (recommended as you then understand all the different items and rooms and their context) and it was a hugely informative and insightful experience. There is a small fee to get in for foreigners (1500rupee) but well worth the experience to understand the hugely dominant religion in Sri Lanka

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of the Sacred Tooth in Kandy
Text:
A delightful early morning visit here. It wasnt too busy at 8am!
There is plenty to see, as well as the building housing the relic (which you cant see), there is a museum, an interesting preserved elephant, gardens and many other buildings. You have to leave your shoes outside. Highly recommend spending at least an hour here.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Traditional veneration ceremony
Text: Visited the Temple of Sacred Tooth Relic on an evening. Tourists entrance fee is 1500 LKR. I recommend getting there for 5:30pm and start with the museum situated on top floors showing artefacts and historical information, paintings and jewellery given to the temple over the past few hundred years and dignitaries and devotees. Its quite impressive. Then come back down for 6:30pm when the veneration ceremony takes place. Tourists are allowed to watch and film. Then queue up to go to first floor to have a look at the relic. I wont spoil the surprise, and it cant be photographed anyway. By the way there is a replica in the museum upstairs ;-) ask one of the guards of the museum...

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A must do in Kandy
Text:
I spent half the day at this by far the most relevant sightseeing spot at Kelly. I recommend to visit late in the afternoon if you get the chance to see the ceremony at 18:30. Be aware of that you cannot enter in shorts for men. I managed with a beach towel which made some locals laugh but it did its job ??.

The interior is awesome but I would also advice to reserve some time to wander around the surrounds. Around 4-5pm it tends to rain like the end of the world quite often.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Serene & Sacred
Text: A must visit place to understand the Buddhist inroads into Sri Lanka from India...A serene place with beautiful surrounding ambiance. Actually a royal palace converted to Temple to house the Tooth Relic....The 2 floor museum is also interesting.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Great place to visit
Text:
Surrounded in lovely grounds the Temple of the Sacred tooth is a great place to visit. Dress respectfully as shorts even for men are not allowed, also uncovered shoulders. At this temple I felt they were the most strict than any other temple visits. Bags are also scanned as you go in.  Inside is very grand and you are allowed to take photos.  There is a lot to see with 2 museums
Inside. Well worth a visit!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Take a tour guide
Text:
Tour guide is cheap 1000 LKR. Absolutely worth taking them to understand the history.
The temple is quite large and lots of places to visit 
Minimum 1 hr to 2hr time allocation

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: See the importance of this temple to Buddhists
Text: We went for the 6:30 showing of the tooth chamber and even though there were many people there (both tourists and those wanting to make any offering) we observed how important this temple is to Buddhists.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Very historic place
Text: This place was handed over to the local.Manning and Sir John Doyle after the 1815 convention. Now it is a holy site and a visit to this place is a must. Don't forget to visit the British Garrison cemetery nearby.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Fantastic atmosphere
Text: A piece of art with great history. The museum pieces and artwork tell a great story. Whilst the processions are on there is a great atmosphere!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting experience
Text: This is a very beautiful temple, it is believed to hold a tooth from Buddha inside a shrine. There is a ceremony three times a day where they open the doors to the shrine and you can see it-- cannot see tooth itself. During this time, it gets really crowded, but if you want to see the shrine up close, you will have to stand in the line. Even though it might be really long, it moves quickly. I think it is best to visit the temple during the ceremonial times at is make the experience unique. Otherwise, it is just entering another temple and looking around. Costs 1,500 rupee. You cannot bring in drinks, cigarettes or lighters.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Over crowded
Text: I felt sad for the many people on true religious pilgrimage as it was like a scrum of iPhones in there. As its the top attraction in Kandy, if I did our trip again I would miss Kandy off entirely.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting
Text:
This is Sri Lanka Buddhism's most sacred shrine which is said to hold Buddha's tooth.
On our visit it was extremely busy with locals and tourists, would recommend that you visit early to miss the crowds and by doing so feel the peaceful atmosphere of the temple

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Please ask the guides to not pester visitors once gotten a rejection
Text:
The touts at the ticket booth are slightly pretentious and fakes.

The silver lining was meeting a local family who brought me up and taught me how to present my prayers, really nice of the lady and the family ;))

Tip: Go at certain timings where the prayer sessions are on.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Nice experience
Text: Not much more to expect from a temple. Let yourself pick up by a guide to get some extra  information.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Stunning temple with significant religious meaning
Text:
A very special place for Buddhists
The architecture and relics are amazing
One of the best parts, as a westerner, were the paintings and descriptions below each explaining the story of the Sacred Tooth. A very interesting visit

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Mesmerizing
Text: One of the best temples i have seen in Sri Lanka . Thought little expensive but worth. If you want you can as well take a guide which will be further expensive. There are three museum and one temple in one ticket. lot of stories on the importance of tooth. The museum on presence of Buddhism across world was simply enchanting. It has small  government souvnnier shop. Not a lot of variety but still less costly than most of the shops. You need minimum  3-4 hrs if you really like history.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: You Have To Visit
Text: What an amazing and calm place. From a spiritual point of view just stunning and calmness seems to come over such a busy and sacred place even with all the tourists and local worshippers. Security is tight but not in your face and you have to witness the energy of the place. YOu have to go and see it for yourself and experience.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Nice history and spiritual place
Text:
From a religious spiritual perspective place is great.

From a tourist perspective its something else. Very interesting story about the tooth, big place and easy to walk around since roads are closed for cars.

A bit hard to find parking but easy to buy flowers and such to bring into the temple and sacred city.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Far too busy
Text: Bit disappointed with this temple, purely as it was so busy! Its a beautiful place to visit but i would avoid going at 6pm!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: valuable location
Text:
people working inside so friendly.
oil lamp during night is so attractive and the  important one is below the peepal tree .

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Well worth the visit
Text: It was quite amazing to witness the daily service where one can glimpse for a moment the Sacred Tooth Relic housed in it's golden urn.  Remember to cover shoulders and knees though.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Heart of kandy, Sri Lanka
Text: Most respected Buddist temple in Sri Lanka. Local people are very lovely around. Must visit with white dress. Nice lake and atmosphere.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Absolutely worth seeing
Text:
Buddha tooth relic temple ensures you direct meeting of another culture and worship. When a good guide explains you a history and the rules of buddhism you can sometimes bethink if Buddha wasn't right... 
Worth seeing, one of must see in Sri Lanka.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Temple of the Root Canal
Text:
Very little of any depth or breadth to see or experience, with or without a tour tout.
I came. 
I saw. 
I left.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: INTERESTING
Text: Visited the temple as part of a cultural tour. Lovely building, busy with many visitors paying homage to Buddha. A tooth from Buddha is said to be kept here but it was more or less impossible to see it! Very special place for Buddhists and definitely worth a visit

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Serene, quiet
Text: Well maintain. Buddhist temple with a story attached to it. But from a visitors point of view, well maintained, very quiet and serene. Sprawling land, and area.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Worth it!
Text: Ill admit its hard to catch a glimpse of the tooth, but its worth the visit simply to see the temples and artifacts! As well as the sacred chest the tooth is in. My recommendation is to contact Sanjaya Tours Kandy.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: A Surprising Highlight
Text: We were surprised how much we enjoyed this temple. We originally planned to go because what else were we going to do in Kandy, and ended up spending far longer here than anticipated. It felt like there was something beautiful to stop and notice every time we paused during our time in the temple, and we were happy to wander around taking in each and every piece. We recommend circling the interior temple twice just to get a view of each of the different elements. The grounds are also lovely, and you could easily spend long moments quietly watching the people stream through. Our advice: Go in the morning! We practically had the place to ourselves...when we left a few hours later, the place was really filling up!

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Crowded and rushed though the viewing rudely.
Text: So you only get a 1 or 2 second glimpse of the casket or urn of the Tooth Relic. The man rudely ushers you passed the small door so fast that you can't see much and left feeling disappointed especially because this comes after waiting in conjested hot and humid line up of people for 45 mins pmus. Not really my thing. I wouldn't recommend doing this but certain aspects of the building are nice, like the flower offerings and the galleries, as well as the  outside of the building and grounds. It's the viewing of the Relic that was not worth it.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Packed during viewing time
Text: This UNESCO, historic temple houses the famous tooth relic of Buddha.  Believers pack the temple at viewing times to receive blessings and be spiritually moved.  There's a separate line going up the stairs for viewing with a parallel line for those just passing by.  Be prepared to wait in line.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: worth the visit
Text:
We were amazed at the crowd ,but the entire activity was well coordinated and we had a good view of the stupa in which Lord Buddha's teeth is kept. 

Very nice positive feeling after the visit.

the temple is very well maintained and staff is very polite and directs you properly,in case you ask questions 

there are timings when the  rituals are performed.like we waited to see the 6.30pm rituals.

please ensure you are wearing proper clothing before entering the temple.the attire should be as per the customs.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Very impressive
Text: Very impressive but situated 1.5km from nearest parking so if you cannot walk this distance there is a problem. Also be aware that shoe removal necessary inside out of respect

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Interesting Temple
Text:
A cool temple that's worth a visit, although you'll probably be done in a couple of hours unless you really love temples! 
As you go in, your bag will be checked and you'll be patted down. Make sure you buy tickets from the foreigner's desk (1500 rupees) - you leave your shoes there as well. We went during a Buddhist holiday, so it was pretty packed and we ended up being swept along, but it was very atmospheric. Try to catch the daily ceremony if you can - there's drumming and people giving offerings.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Wear socks or your feet get dirty and too Hot but amazing and wonderful place
Text: We had a wonderful guide his name was Fernando he spoke English German and his knowledge was incredible he made our visit so special and the Buddhist way of life is magical and wonderful. The only thing they believe is life of all living creatures is sacred and has value. Everything was explained and we had a blessing I felt honoured to be welcomed and treated so well buy all the Sri Lanka people. One of my highlights of our 20 day tour.

Location_Name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
Title: Important Sri Lankan Temple
Text:
Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is a Buddhist temple in the city of Kandy, Sri Lanka. It is located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy.  It is a very important Sri Lankan temple as it houses the relic of the tooth of the Buddha. 

We visited this temple as part of a G Adventures tour in the evening when the doors of the area where the casket that houses the tooth relic is open,  This allows the locals as well as the tourists to see this casket.  

Due to problems with possible terrorists, there are high security measures taken before you can enter the temple.  You must also be appropriately dressed with women wearing clothes that cover their shoulders and knees and men should wear full length pants.  Most of the locals wear complete white outfits to show their respect when visiting the temple.

It is a very busy in this temple and you cannot wear your shoes in it.  I had a guide help me through the temple, which I would not have been able to do if he had not helped me up and down the numerous stairs you need to use to see the entire temple.  

The museum that is attached to the temple was also interesting to see as it held many sacred texts about Buddha's life.

Title: Unique temple
Text:
Lovely set of small temples on top of a hill. The abundance of statues and wall paintings is truly unique and worth a visit. It costs 2000 LKR per ticket (around $10 atm) but its definitely worth it! 
Tickets can be purchased both at the bottom by the golden temple and at the top. 
Make sure you bring socks since you have to take off your shoes to walk around the temple grounds and the ground is scorching hot in the sun!

Title: Need a guide.
Text: A knowledgeable guide needed to get the most from this visit. Blessings available as you enter various caves although the latter ones are somewhat underwhelming. Worth a visit though.

Title: Buddhas and Stairs
Text:
There is about 700 stairs till you reach the temple. ( a nice FYI)

The temple is very interesting and build inside the caves. 

It has plenty of history which you will need a guide or potentially do a bit of reading beforehand.

Title: Not for us
Text:
We found the cave temples quite underwhelming, despite their history. Were not Buddhists, and have seen quite a lot of temples travelling across Asia  our experience here didnt feel hugely special. If youre at Sigiriya for the day, wed recommend spending more time there and giving these a skip.

Youll need to cover your knees, but can hire a lungi for 100 rupees. As others have said, the climb up is pretty steep, especially if youve already done a lot of walking at Sigiriya that day.

Title: Hundreds of uneven steep steps before you reach this beautiful place
Text: Worth a visit, leave a couple of hours in your schedule for this! Its not suitable if youre not fit enough for the stairs that lead you up as there are no alternatives.

Title: Great sight and great views
Text:
Definitely worth a visit for the Cave Temples, fascinating sights and history behind it. 
What surprised and delighted me was the view from the caves over the surrounding area, absolutely stunning. 
There are guides offering their services to explain the whole thing, they do it for tips. 
Be aware that it is quite a tough climb up steep steps to get to the caves (about 300 to 400) and you will come close to monkeys, but they didn't try to  approach us.

Title: Ancient place
Text: Very ancient place in Sri Lanka to must see in your visit. This place have very beautiful and ancient paintings of the walls. This have mainly 5 caves. You have to to do a little hike to go there. But don't miss this place in your Sri Lankan journey

Title: Phenomenal Cave Temples
Text: This was an amazing site not to be missed. Ots about a 20 minute wall up to the caves if you wall slowly in the heat. Once three of the Temple rooms were opened for viewing or praying. My favorite was the third Temple. The ceilings, walls and the Buddha's were spectacular. The first Temple had a Specular Buddah statue. Bring water because it is very hot up there especially in the caves.

Title: Not to be missed! So beautiful.
Text:
Foreigners! There is a parking lot halfway up the mountain, you dont need to park at the bottom. We were driving ourselves and didnt realize this. We of course got the full experience walking up from the bottom, but in bare feet and that heat, we probably would have gone the easier route :)
Absolutely worth it though, weve never seen anything like it.
Make sure you bring a cover up if your knees are exposed, this includes guys who arent wearing longer shorts (my husband was wearing pretty short shorts and he had to buy a coverup for $9 well never use again).
The temples are closed for prayer at a certain time everyday so we had to wait, so check before you go when those times are. 
Absolutely beautiful though!!!

Title: Breathtaking as how beautiful it is and it was built / painted 1000+ years ago. MUST SEE
Text:
It was very stubbing to see how the status were perfectly craved and the painted work throughout the caves. Given there is limited to no sun exposure, the paint work has been preserved.

Note: I am writing this review is after completing 15 days holiday in Sri Lanka; therefore, I have considered all pro and cons.

Title: nice walk to see some ancient history
Text: not as high as sigriya but a nice spot to see some ancient history. the walk isn't as bad as it seems but I feel coming around 4 pm might be less hotter than going at 10 am.

Title: Extraordinary caves
Text: After a short climb, getting to the entrance to the caves is easy.  The five caves have fascinating and beautifully painted buddhas.  The figures have been really well kept and in some cases restored.   The bare rock is painted so that the ceilings look as if they have been covered in material.

Title: Reasonably good caves, up some steps and around 1500 per person
Text: Caves are fine, well lit and not much in the way of text to read so google it or bring a guide book. The caves are closed 10:30-10:45 but when open are pretty good. Not exactly world beating stuff but still worth a visit if you have time. Must take off shoes, though they want you to pay to have them. Remember to cover shoulders and legs, bring a covering.

Title: Ancient Caves with a lot of historical significance
Text:
This Cave Temple is one of the best preserved rock edifices and the caves have numerous statues and paintings, on the walls and roofs. 

There is a lot of history attached to this place.

There are about 400 steps to climb up to the temple and can be reasonably managed by most age groups. You can either come down the same way or on the opposite side, that comes out at the Golden Temple.

Title: Beautiful decorations, worth seeing
Text:
From the car park, there is a 10-minute walk upstairs, it is steep but mostly in the shade. The caves are next to each other and the total time you need for this place is about 1 hour.

The cave temples are well preserved and very richly decorated -statues, wall and ceiling paintings with vivid colours and nice details. Absolutely worth visiting. After looking at other drip-ledge caves this brings the whole idea to a new level.

Some caves are lit up by nice yellow lights, which are properly positioned and I assume to give some resemblance to the candles once used in those temples. Others, unfortunately, are blasted in all directions by bright white hospital-like lights.

On our way out we decided to revisit some caves, but the power was down, so if you are unlucky to visit during a power outage you won't be able to fully enjoy this site.

Entrance fee: 1500 LKR
Guide: sign says 750, the one who tried to trick us into guiding us offered his services at 500 before us declining his offers, unfortunately, I couldn't understand him well. 

Some unpleasant things:
- We encountered a very rude staff member at the entrance.
- Scaffolding has been left inside some of the caves, despite no signs of any work going on. Ruins the atmosphere and some photos.
- No information at the site at all, hire a guide or read online.

Title: Amazing EXPERIENCE
Text: Most Peace full Visit to the temple , My visit to the temple after more than 20 years and this time with wife and 2 kids.This was the first time to clime the steps all along.. we were accompanied by the monkeys and the Guide explain all the 4 caves for 750 Rs  in English. What an amazing experience!!

Title: Cave Temple
Text:
Dambulla Cave Temple is made up of 5 smaller caves with different statues in each of them. 
The ticket office is no longer at the Golden Buddha but at the beginning of the steps around the back. You are best to get your ticket then walk up the back steps, then when you are finished walk down to the Golden Buddha.
You must have your shoulders and knees covered and take your shoes off. They have  shoe minding for a fee.

Title: Interesting Caves
Text: We enjoyed the 5 little cave temples at this site but cranky our guide didn't take us to the golden Buddha for whatever reason ? He actually proved to be a crap guide ! The Cave Temples are very different with a multitude of statues & Buddhas in different poses and sizes. The painting of walls & ceilings is well done & colourful. The walk up is fairly steep but we came in the shorter back gate. They sting you for the shoe minding service and the touts on our visit were very annoying, no thank you politely repeatedly ended up being F.... Off Idiot ! I suggest the authorities do something about their touts as they are detracting from the natural enjoyment of their sites !!

Title: Buddha statues in caves
Text: This is a really interesting place. It's a small temple complex at the top of a hill off of the main road through Dambulla town. It is quite a long, steep climb from the Golden Buddha statue up the steps to the caves so take your time. No shoes allowed in the temple area (there's a place to store them outside the entrance) so have some socks with you as it is very hot underfoot. Once you're in, there are five main caves accessed by a small temple facade built into the rock face. In each of the caves there are lots of Buddha statues of various sizes ranging from human sized up to massive lying down Buddhas about 15 metres long. Take a note of the ornately painted cave ceilings too. Depending on when you visit, the monks do occasionally shut the caves for prayer, but no problem it's only for about 15 minutes. Tip - if you're driving or being driven, enter by the rear steps on the access road a little further into town, as this way you pass the ticket office. Otherwise you'll climb all the way up to the entrance and then have to descend by about 100 steps down to buy your ticket, then climb back up again to get in.

Title: Steep climb up those steps
Text: It was quite  a steep climb up those steps to the temple. Just a word of caution, do not visit these caves in the midday sun, which we did, rather go in the morning. The caves are pretty spectacular, but it was a bit crowded when we were there.

Title: Dambulla cave temple
Text: This is one of the most special places we visited. The temple is unique and the Bhudda statues quite amazing

Title: Stunning
Text: I loved the caves. So many beautiful Buddhas.  I think I had Buddha overload afterward. The architecture was fascinating. You need to remove shoes, so remember to take socks as the concrete is very hot.

Title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
Text: More steps to the caves 395 to be precise. But not too bad a climb. The 5 caves are well looked after and worth seeing, The surrounding views were beautiful.

Title: Good visit
Text:
At the outset - understand that this is a monument on a hill. So it involves climbing around 300 steps and the climb is not easy.
Another thing - there is an entry ticket which can be bought at the start of the steps.
The Temple by itself is magnificent - but its important to have the knowledge of the temple beforehand or at hand - since there are no explanatory boards anywhere.
All in all a good experience

Title: A must visit
Text: Wow, what a place to visit.  You must have shoulders and knees covered but you can hire a wrap at £1. Its hot and many steps to climb so take water with you.  I was amazed at this place.

Title: Poorly organised and disappointing
Text:
We stopped off here on our way to sigiriya and honestly wished we didn't bother. You have to walk all the way up to the entrance to the temples and walk back down the other side to get a ticket. In the sweltering heat this is not ideal as it's a lot of steps (and we're pretty fit!). There were a lot of older people who made it all the way to the top but then had to give up because the paving is so uneven and there are no hand rails, we felt really bad for them!!
Once your shoes are off you have to walk on boiling hot stones, so I would recommend you bring some socks to prevent blisters/burns. 
Once we were up there the temples were ok but not great... Maybe we're just not that cultured?! 
You get constantly harassed by people asking if you want a guide/ buy a 'magic box'or very sadly if you want to watch a poor snake which has been 'charmed' and shoved in a basket. 
The monkeys on the way up are cute though!

Title: AWESOME
Text: I totally recommend a trip or a short visit to this awesome ancient Buddhist cave and the site that the faithful Buddhists keep and maintain in an incredible way and, therefore, gives us (to visitors) such a lovely, enchanting and unforgettable experience within the monumental site.....

Title: Worthwhile a visit
Text: Interesting both cultural and religious points of view. Quite crowded. Our guide at the caves was poor, otherwise I would have given full marks.

Title: Amazing!
Text: A hard climb to the top from the golden Buddha but well worth it for the amazing wall paintings and statues. A must visit location!

Title: Better visit in a cloudy day
Text:
We visited this world heritage monument on a combine tour to Sigiriya rock fortress from Hikkaduwa. After visiting Sigiriya, Dambula cave temple looked easier but still one so important monument without any signs or information. Just grabing the money which might look like less than Sigiriya but still is a generous amount.
The monument itself is amazing and unique, a temple full of any kind of buddha statue but unfortunately left at is fate without any signs anywhere.
Since you need to put off the shoes when you enter is much better to visit the site a day that is cloudy and more breeze as walking barefoot on hot stones is not so recommended.

Title: Amazing temple.
Text: Have to climb up 500 steps to reach the top. Lots of monkeys around so be careful not to expose your food. Total of 5 caves, each cave have lots of Buddha statue created by past kings. Beautiful wall painting inside the cave. This place does has it's history.

Title: Dambulla Cave Temple
Text: Fascinating place to visit, spread over 5 caves. Lovely ceiling paintings and many statues of Buddha. In a great setting with nice views. Lots of monkeys around. Shoes are not allowed and have to be left with the shoe man before entering the caves.  On the way out small fee of 25 rupees each has to be paid to get your shoes back.

Title: Dambulla in the monsoon !
Text: Very impressive site especially when dodging monsoonal downpours.  Women must not wear shorts or at least must have a sarong or wrap to enter the caves.

Title: Worth the walk up the steps !
Text:
Despite the many steps, once you get there the caves are fascinating and beautiful 

The sculptures are amazing

Worth seeing for sure

Title: Interesting place
Text: Hindu and Buddhist temple side by side . Like the fact the site is dug out from a rock . Moneys are found everywhere but they are harmless. The place should have more light to read the information .

Title: Excellent visit.
Text: My partner and I visited the cave temple while staying at Habarana. Its a climb to the top and its advisable to carry some water. Get a cool drink afterwards at a stall at the car park. There are some great photos to be taken when you have your breath back after the climb. Its well worth visiting, the views are good.

Title: Amazing Place
Text: A visit to this impressive cave temple is a must.  The work that went into creating these impressive caves and statues, and is now going on the preserve them, is incredible.

Title: The Wonders that Exist in our World
Text: This site is also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, a UNESCO site, and the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The climb to the caves can be fairly taxing depending on age and fitness levels, but worth the effort to view this great complex. There are five caves containing in excess of 150 statues,  and extensive murals relating to the Gautama Buddha and his life. The caves are formed by a very large overhang in the face of the rock that has been partitioned and now sits behind a structure of white painted arched colonnades and gabled entrances. It is a mystical site. Enjoy wonderful panoramic views outside, the sun shone and the Rock of Sigiriya was visible in the distance. The visit was made more relevant and informative by our excellent tour guide.

Title: Nice to see but lack of guides
Text: It would be nice if they had guides that leed you through caves and explain everything. For us, not beeing buddist,everything looks the same. Would be nice to learn something about the place.

Title: Beautiful cave temple
Text:
There is a flight of stairs before reaching the temple. The route has shade. There are many monkeys so make sure not to feed them and keep your bags closed and belongings in check so the monkeys will cannot snatch them. 

We entered the temple complex on foot. When visiting any of the temples in Sri Lanka, it is a must that the knees and shoulders are always covered. Wear modest clothes during your trip. Bring along a skirt and a shawl inside your bag. It really comes in handy.

As I entered each of the five chambers of the Golden Temple, I felt a sense of serenity that's almost overwhelming. 

When planning your trip to Sri Lanka, don't miss this temple. It is amazing, I guarantee. Take some time to close your eyes and meditate for a few minutes.

Dambulla Royal Cave Temple or the Golden Cave Temple of Dambulla is the most well preserved cave temple in Sri Lanka. The paintings and statues depict the life of Gautama Buddha. The paintings on the walls and the ceilings tell many stories. These paintings are all made from natural dyes mainly from saps of plants.

Title: Cultural tour
Text: If you are on your way to Signorina from Colombo, this is a good  stop to get a sense of the local area. A nice temple with friendly Sri Lankans and pleasant hike to the top with views of surroundings at specific points. Easy to dismiss as just another Temple, however consider the setting and the people and it's a good place to spend some time to reflect on your own inner peace. Even for a few minutes. :)

Title: beautifully carved & painted caves
Text:
Dambulla cave temple is close to Sigiriya on the way to Kandy. Climb from the ticket window side else you will have to climb down to buy a ticket, also there are less number of steps ~300. The ticket is LKR1500 per person. The steps are easily walkable and the entire route is covered with trees. 
The caves have many Buddha statues. The wall paintings are very old and are beautifully done. 
Dress modestly, cover shoulders and knees before visiting the temple. Caps and footwear not allowed inside the temple. 
Do visit Dambulla Cave temple and the Golden Buddha, it is a UNESCO World Heritage site and an important part of Sri Lanka's cultural triangle

Title: Loved it
Text:
As a Buddhist I simply loved this cave temple! It is so well preserved, especially the wall n ceiling paintings! So very colorful not much fading away! It is also enlisted in UNESCO! 
It also very picture perfect! 
You do have to remove your shows, socks, go in barefoot! Which under light rain was quite okay! 
I believed we are blessed!

Title: Awesome - do not hesitate visiting this Temple
Text:
An incredible beautiful temple, it was busy and they were renovating parts but it was truly awesome.
We actually had a priest bless for us a rope bracelet  (which i didnt take off until i got back home) kept us safe and brought us good luck-the ceremony was fantastic to watch.. once our tour guide spoke with the priest he couldn't stop smiling for the whole day - it did give you a sense of accomplishment once you left there plus the very steep climb but well worth it -you wont be disappointed

Title: Visit it now when you still have the chance!
Text: Very nice religious site, a definit must see! The price was also very cheap thanks to religious management (opposed to other sites that are managed by the government), but this is also the reason it will be gone soon. You where able to walk up to the wall paintings and actually touch them. Which we did not, but a lot of less cultured tourists did... If they don't close it down and replace it by a fake copy or cut access to touvhing of the paintings, this site will diminish in beauty very soon.

Title: Great culture place
Text: Enjoyed my visit not for people who dont like steps as there are many but a amazing place and some cultural things to see

Title: Good for a short stop.
Text:
Some nice artwork and statues, the largest chamber is very good, a lot of detail in the ceiling art.
Only need less than an hour to visit, often there is a snake charmer on the pathway outside which is fun to see.

Title: Beautiful and peaceful
Text: The calm and beauty of this working temple makes the climb worth while.  The stayed are numerous, beautiful and very old. Its with reading up on history if youre not visiting with a guide.

Title: Extraordinary cave temples
Text:
A series of Buddhist temples carved out of the rock in caves. Many buddhas and buddhist scenes shown.
As usual shoes have to be removed before entering.Be warned - leave your socks on, the stone floor on the way in can get very hot. My feet almost burned.

Title: Well kept temples
Text: We accessed this by the stairs, there were a lot of stairs so not ideal for those with poor mobility but I have read you can access part of it by road. The temples themselves are very well kept, the area is clean. There is a place to store your shoes for a small fee as you cannot take them in. Be sure to wear trousers and cover your shoulders. Inside the caves are beautiful paintings and buddhas which are worth going to see. One of the nicer temples we visited.

Title: Well looked after temple
Text:
Very attractive temple and being looked after, area is clean too. 
Great views of the surrounding greenery 
Please remember to wear clothing that covers legs and shoulders

Title: The mighty Cave Temple of Buddha
Text: The place was easily accessible on the way back from Sigiriya with a lot of open parking space. The temple is newly built that is on the road side and to the back of  it is the actual old Dambulla Cave temple.

Title: Remarkable site
Text:
Pretty mind blowing to realise this site has been an active Buddhist monastery since 2-3rd century bc.

The Buddha statues across each of the caves, along with the beautiful fresco and other ornamental work are stunning. 

One of my favourite sites visited in Sri Lanka.

Title: Very interesting history
Text:
We stopped here by suggestion of our guide who came up with us to explain some of the history, The architecture given its age is impressive and well worth a visit. At 1500 LKR well worth the money. 

Tips for travellers - make sure shoulders and knees are covered and have 50 LKR change for shoe storage as you will need to leave shoes

Title: Well preserved temple
Text: Very well preserved temple in the rock. You need to wear long trousers and shirt or rent a sari at the entrance.

Title: Beautiful Buddha temples
Text: Must watch for travellers within the region. The caves fall on the way to/from Colombo and are very convenient to reach.

Title: Good to see
Text: Very cool and great to see people working on preserving the statues too. Loved the cave art and the staircase up to the temple itself. Must see if you're in the area

Title: Nice experience to explore
Text:
The cave located in top of mountain,  240 steps you need to claim.  You will enjoy different designs of buddha statue in different locations, in your way dow  , enjoy the views from top .
Make sure don't even come closer to the sales people around th4 temple,  the time you touch any item they consider it yours , so stay Way from them .

Title: worth to visit
Text: It was nearly 1km of hiking to the caves from the car park. First we visited the temple museum, but there wasn't anything in it to see, total waste of time. Then we climb up the rock and reached to the caves, which was stunning. It was a quite a piece of work and survived for many hundred years. There were 5 caves full of Budha statues. When you are top of the rock you can have a stunning view, including Lion's rock. The sad thing is I didn't see any preserving measures take place around the caves.

Title: Serene
Text: A highly recommended visit . A nice walk up several hundred steps ( with beautiful views along the way ) is rewarded by a fantastic cave temple . A special place

Title: Awesome
Text:
This is a complex of caves/ temples, accessible after a fairly steep climb. The climb might be difficult, especially once the sun is up but this attraction is worth all the effort and trouble. The statues, carvings and paintings on the walls and ceilings are all awe-inspiring, making you wonder how this must have been built centuries back. The people are very friendly and the place spic and span. 
I would suggest wearing loose and comfortable clothes which cover your body (at least the knees), to counter the heat and the climb, as well as to avoid hurting religious and cultural sentiments.

Title: Divine srenity
Text: An absolute highlight of our cultural trip; the cave interiors are simply stunning & awe inspiring. Just wonderful

Title: Very Interesting
Text: Little bit of a trek up to the temple but it is a very interesting place to witness. Make sure to have your shoulders covered and pants on past your knees. Also, they make you pay to have your shoes checked in. You cannot put them in your backpack so make sure to bring cash. I think its only 20 rupees though.

Title: Beutiful
Text:
Both the caves and the view from the rock worth the (not very hard) climb..
Do not hesitate and pay a visit if you are in the area.

Title: Dambulla cave temples
Text:
Very interesting place and one where you can take photos inside (which is a bonus).
The floor is very hot though so you may want to take socks. You have to pay 25 rupees for your shoes to be looked after.  A few hawkers about - but its not too bad!

Title: Stunning UNESCO Religious Centre
Text:
It was early evening when we arrived at the temple of five caves of varying size and interior dated 1st BC.

There are more than 80 caves in the area with the 5 caves most worth viewing. The first king turned the caves into a temple complex and many kings added to it later until the 11th century. It is still a functioning temple complex till this day.

The spectacular murals on the ceilings were of sheer magnificence. They depicted Buddhas life and sermons. 

The guide pointed out the large statue of the reclining Buddha on his deathbed judging by the way the feet was displayed. Stupas, a hundred small Buddha statues, some gods and goddesses and kings statues were on display. 

One of the five caves was under repair, and we managed to take a quick look of it. The second cave was the largest and most impressive.

They say you must never turn your back to the Buddha when taking a photo. I felt intense spiritual power in these ancient caves and decided against taking any pictures out of respect.

There was a small basin with water dripping down from the ceiling that the guide said would never dry up and have healing powers.

Once out of the temple caves we realised how the temple was cut out of a massive overhanging rock. We went under a huge Bodhi tree and made a wish. It was just too bad we could not find time to see the ancient Bodhi tree at Anuradhapura. 

A very moving spiritual experience indeed.

Title: Interesting
Text: We visited here as part of a tour in Sri Lanka, a very interesting place, easy walk to access it. Just be careful of the monkeys if you take a flower with you - they may try to take it from you! There are 5 cave temples, all varying in size. The statues are fascination and the painted frescos on the walls and ceiling are incredibly detailed. Quite different to other temples we visited. There is quite a strict dress code, you need to ensure your shoulders and knees are covered. As with all the temples you remove your shoes, the ground gets very warm. Highly recommend a visit here

Title: Different types of Buddha in the cave
Text: It is up at the hilltop with varieties of Buddha statues. Take short climbing up on the stairs then you will reached the top. There is a shelf for shoe, gotta pay for it. It seems nothing much outside those temples but inside are would be a wow setting. The lights are quite dim but still can see the features of the Buddhas. The painting are quite worn out, not much restoration has been done, I think. They are some guides that would like to show you around and explain all the stories to the tourists (of course they will charge a sum) but I didnt engage any. 1.5hrs would be good enough to explore the entire place.

Title: Remarkable painting
Text: There are 5 sites at the temple.  You need to leave your shoes at the entrance and walk bare foot.  You also need to cover your shoulders and knees.  Not to worry if you are not dressed appropriately as there are sarong for rent.  There are loads of monkeys around the area.  The cave paintings that used herbal paint stood the test of time.  This is well worth a visit.

Title: Quaint temple
Text: 500 steps to the top but the caves featured lovely frescoes. Ladies need to dress modestly. You can walk down to the Buddhist museum also.

Title: Beautiful Dambulla
Text: Another temple, but with 200 Buddhas.  Thanks to our guide for explaining the differences etc.  Such an amazing place in the caves.

Title: Great temple great art
Text:
Walked up to the caves in the morning the walk up the mountain is very beautiful 
And the caves them selfs are spectacular 
Don't miss

Title: Spectacular
Text:
About 400 steps. Not too difficult for a couple of 60 yr olds. It was a very hot day when we went. No shoes when entering.
Beautiful arts and statues. Peaceful. Well worth the climb to the top. Also had a flat path to the top, end section a little steep.

Title: Well worth the climb; a must-do visit
Text:
The climb up the steps to the temple offers some wonderful views including a panorama of Lion Rock and Pidurangala Rock.  It is steep in places, so take some water with you; there's nowhere to buy any at the top!

You need to leave your shoes (100 Rps per person) and entry to the temple complex is 1500 Rps each. Remember to dress appropriately for visiting a temple.

There are 5 caves; the newest being the furthest away.  Perhaps worth starting here and working back as the older caves have the better workmanship.  The statues and wall paintings are very impressive. You can get up close; which is maybe not such a good thing given the age of some of the caves.

There is little (or no) information whilst walking around.  If you are touring Sri Lanka with a guide, then not a problem as the guide will relay the important information.  Otherwise read up beforehand as part of what makes it really impressive is the knowledge that some parts are over 2000 years old!

The whole visit only takes an hour or so.  For us it was a really convenient stopping off point on the drive between Kandy and Habarana (where we based ourselves to see Lion Rock, Minneriya and Polonnaruwa)

Title: Morning tour
Text: Quite a climb to the top but have to say it is well worth it. Temple is amazingly maintained. The views from the top are breathtaking.

Title: Nice, but the money grabbing attitude is arguably enough to boycott it
Text:
For our final stop in Sri Lanka we came here in the late afternoon on the way from our hotel in the Sigiriya area to the airport in Negombo. 

It was very hot and impossible to avoid dripping in sweat by the time you get to the top (not ideal when heading to the airport). Once at the top, the cave temples are fascinating, though relatively compact. As ever there is the annoyance of having to take your shoes off and navigate the burning hot stone.

Major disappointment though was the absolutely outrageous charge for the toilets once we got to the bottom. R100 is 5-10x the going rate in Sri Lanka. Money grabbing attitude that is going to get a bad review from me every time

Title: Stunning temple experience. A real must see!
Text:
Awesome place! So beautiful and interesting. Yes it was a climb, but it was so worth it!
There were some local guides. We decided to pay one which turned out as a good idea. He explained very well and made the experience even better. 
Make sure to wear clothing the cover your shoulders en knees.

Title: relaxing spot
Text:
my husband and I climbed up to this cave temple, the views from the top were amazing. it is truely a very calm relaxing place. 
but you have to be aware that there are a lot of monkeys, they won't attack you, just leave it alone.

Title: It was average
Text: Overcostly. Milking in on relegious belief of people to extort cash. Other wise a very nice and peaceful place to visit.

Title: Interesting temple cave experience
Text:
The Dambulla Cave Temple is reached by climbing a lot of steps. The trick is to make sure you buy your ticket to enter the caves at the bottom of the steps, as it is not obvious this is the process. To enter most Buddhist Temples you need to dress modestly, no exposed shoulders and knees covered - they do rent items to cover you at the temple entrance. You also need to pay to have your shoes minded whilst you are in the temple and the person you pay is very reluctant to give change so make sure you have the exact amount of 25 rupees. The cost to enter the cave is 1500 rupees. 
There are five caves and they are stocked with many Buddhas in all manner of positions - if you are yet to visit Myanmar, Thailand, or other such Buddhist countries you will be amazed, but to be honest the South East Asian countries have many of these caves and do it all a lot better. 
It is though an interesting experience to visit this cave temple.

Title: Beautiful 5 cave temples.....
Text:
The cave temple complex is around 300 steps from the plains. The ticket price is 1500 Srilankan rupees. Please make sure to cover your legs and shoulders. Incase if you dont cover, they provide some clothes to cover and charge 100 Rs. You have to remove shoes before you enter the temple. There is a shoe stall, you can leave your shoes there, they charge 25 Rs.
