As soon as you enter, there are tour guides, who will approach you to take the tour with them, they will try to insist on it but decline them politely. Incase if you want to take, fix the price first.
There are no written stories about the 5 cave temples, so i guess the tour guides can be helpful, if you really want to know the stories. Orelse you can google about it and find it on wikipedia Dambulla cave temple 
There are around 150 Buddha statues with lot of fresh flowers, some Srilankan Kings and Hindu gods. The paintings on the ceilings, walls are amazing.
After you leave the temple, you can take another exit and head down to the Golden Buddha temple where the huge statue of Buddha facing the mountains is astonishing.

Title: Great place but not for people with walking issues
Text: The best time to visit the cave is in the morning hours, early you leave better will be the hike up to the cave. Yes, around 600 meters of a hike from the ticket counter will lead you towards the cave. I will not suggest this to people with issues while walking, but for others, you should visit this place. Word of Caution: Stay away from monkeys, they snatch things from tourists. For photographers: do carry a small mini tripod which can be used inside the cave for good pictures as the light inside is really low and the authorities won't allow you to carry a bigger tripods

Title: Interesting cave temple
Text: Quite a decent climb to reach the cave temples, a series of temples with carvings and wall paintings built into the rockface.

Title: Unique cave
Text: The walkway of the steps aren't event and difficult for older person. Need to hold my aunt hand to go up and down. Please remember to wear socks as it'll be hot as need to walk on bare foot.

Title: Breathtaking
Text:
Fabulous Buddhist temple carved into rock caves, filled with wall paintings and statues.  You remove your shoes on the approach - beware, the path is very hot!
Very impressive and well worth the visit. You are allowed to take photos inside. Sad to see some tourists ignoring the request not to take photos with your back to Buddha - this is offensive. As with removing your shoes, these things should be observed as a courtesy to your hosts.

Title: Must see but BEWARE of temple guide!!!!
Text: You have to walk up a bit but its totally worth it! The temple is a must see! As soon as you walk in the temple guide(men in white) will appear. They greet you and start showing you around. STAY AWAY  from them they will want money from you! They lead you to believe its free and part of temple service but they are crooks working at the temple grounds!

Title: A Buddhist temple with magnificent devotional cave frescoes
Text: This temple gives a wonderful insight into Buddhism.  There is a fine reclining Buddha and an uncountable number of images of the Lord Buddha in meditation having attained enlightenment.

Title: So many Buddhas
Text: Dambulla Cave Temples houses an impressive collection of Buddhas. There is a hike up a number of stairs to reach the entrance. As it is a temple, you will be required to be dressed appropriately with shoulders and knees covered. There are a series of caves which house the Buddhas. Each one is similar. There are guides who are available for a fee to guide you through but this is not necessary. As we visited just after the terrorism incident in SL, the place had very few people visiting so we could take our time in each cave, Recommended.

Title: Very nice
Text:
The place was wonderful. 
Although caves look more or less the same, we really enjoy the place. 
On the way you see monkeys and the landscape is breathtaking.

Title: Nice hike to amazing Dambulla cave temple.
Text: The Dambulla cave temple was about 10 min ride away in Tuk Tuk from main Dambulla town. The Tuk tuk driver charged me Rs. 300/-  for one side. The entrance fee was Rs. 500/- for foreigners. And the dress code was full selves and bottom must be below the knee level. At the temple entrance clothes are available to cover up which cost Rs. 50/- per piece in case you forgot to bring something along. Paid guides are also available inside the temple but its a small place so you won't need one. Always remember that turning your back towards Buddha is said to be very disrespectful. There are many caves with Buddha idols and painting in the temple. Outside the temple you will find many locals selling things, but do bargain if you want to purchase something. After visiting the temple you can head over to the Golden Buddha temple which is on the way down from other side, so take the other way down and its the entrance is free of cost there.

Title: A very nice place and a big temple
Text: A very nice place and a big temple. To arrive to the cave you have to clipm some big steps and pay a fee at the entrance. Do not forget that you have to leave the shoes at the entrance.

Title: Stunning frescos and carvings, peaceful, spiritual place.
Text:
You don't need a guide, just a guide book to appreciate the history and beauty of the cave temples.  
You will need to wear clothes that cover your knees and your shoulders.  Don't be one of those disrespectful tourists that hasn't bothered and has to borrow a sarong.  Also, it's worth wearing socks - you are asked to take your shoes off but the rock paving is very hot by the afternoon and hard to walk on in bare feet - socks help!
The temples date back to the 1st century BC and there is evidence of settlement here before that.  The main attractions are 5 caves full of ancient Buddhist frescos and Buddha statues.  Because they have been protected from sunlight the colours are vivid and beautiful.  The whole place is very peaceful and relaxing - enjoy.  Also, there are lots of monkeys outside who provide great entertainment!

Title: Worth the climb take a deep breath
Text: A long set of steps up to the top but worth it, take your time. Amazing place goes back to 1st century  BC, lots of temples  built into the granite rock, some now under restoration but still accessible.  Incredible ceiling paintings all telling stories, Stunning views of the countryside included. Definitely a high light of Sri Lanka

Title: This is why you visit Dambulla
Text: We went to see cave temple which is fascinating, even more if you learned about the history of the place. Definitely worth a visit. However choose time of the visit carefully as you will walk around barefoot. You should go early in the morning when its not that hot. The entrance fee is 3000 rupees for 2 adults and 2 children and extra 25 rupees per pair of shoes which you need to leave outside. When you are finished proceed to Golden temple.

Title: Lifetime experience
Text: Climb 221 steps and take in the grandeur of Buddha carvings and paintings from a forevone era. Marvel at the golden Buddha. Be quiet and respect meditating monks. Its another world like movies about ancient past and you are sure to be transported to times and eras now lost in history and fiction. Keep three hours at least if not more. Climb slowly resting all the while. Then take in Buddha in his glorified carvings on the walls. Out of this world experience.

Title: Amazing UNESCO site
Text: It's almost incomprehensible to think about the massive and creative work that was involved in building this extraordinary rock sanctuary.  I'm not a Buddhist,  but I very much appreciated seeing the golden temples, statues,  grottoes and wall paintings.  This was one of the stops on the Gate1 tour that I was on, and I'm pleased that this UNESCO World Heritage site was included on the tour.

Title: Climbing at 72
Text: A very clean and neat Cave Temple in Dambulla but a word of warning to the elderly and any one with cardiac or breathing problems. The steps are over 200, uneven on a stony surface. there are stretches with no hand rails and the descent is equally telling on the knees. However the climb is finally worthwhile. Statues of Buddha bring serenity all around. Washrooms charge a lot available on descending. Must have is coconut water available all over the country. About SL Rupee 80/- for tourists. Choose the orange variety.

Title: AWESOME PLACE
Text:
The only thing I can say on this place is AWESOME.
You can't go in Sri Lanka and don't visit Dambulla Caves

Title: Fascinating place
Text: A complex of five Buddhist temples carved into the rocks. All are fascinating. The first has a huge reclining Buddha statue and the next two each have 50 or more different statues. Make sure you leave your shoes at the entrance (25 rupees a pair).

Title: Cave paintings
Text: Cave paintings dating from 1st century and onwards, together with hundreds of Buddha statues make this an impressive and interesting place to visit. There are, however, many steps to climb before you reach them, giving magnificent views over the surrounding countryside.

Title: This is in Dambulla not in Habarana and is different from the Golden Temple, Dambulla.
Text:
There are a lot of reviews in the wrong place here and Trip Advisor should sort them out.
The Dambulla Cave Temple is a must-see and probably the best sight in Sri Lanka. Despite the steep climb, though you will be accompanied by well-mannered monkeys, it is worth the effort and really spectacular. There are six caves but each is separate and not very deep so you can come out to cool off it is gets too hot. The usual shoes off, though the floors are fairly clean, and cover shoulders and knees. Trips usually start at the ticket office and return the other way past the Golden Temple.

Title: Visit during morning hours
Text:
Entry Fees: LKR 1500 per person for foreign nationals

There are 3 different entry points. But there is only one ticket booking office. The entry point from the Golden Temple is most painful if you dont have the tickets. From here you will have to first climb a bit, then get down, take the tickets and climb back again.
Easiest option is go from the back side, pick the tickets from the booking office and get down at the next gate. From there the climb is lesser. Also there arent steps to climb from here. So slightly easier. 

You may be able to spot "Giant squirrel" if you are lucky. There are loads of monkeys near the cave and they snatch food. So be careful.

The caves are good and maintained well. I met lot of crowd there.It can be done if you have time. But would recommend to visit in the morning hours.

Title: amazing sights
Text: well worth a trip to see the various caves and statue but if you can get a guide as the rooms can be quite complicated to understand, go early to avoid crowds or you may struggle to get in some rooms which are quiet small. Very decorative and very interesting. You can get access from the car park half way up if going by coach to avoid most of the steps from the entrance

Title: Stunning
Text: Dambulla cave temple is an excellent way to while a way an hour or two? There are lots of steps to get to the entrance so I would suggest you should be reasonably fit and healthy to enter but once in the temple areas, Buddhas and fresco pairings are marvellous. Our guide explained many things to us whilst there which helped us understand the importance of particular things, but with or without a guide its a must see. Its amazing these beautiful things were created so long ago and still exist today. Definitely worth a visit but things to beat in mind are that can be very hot in the caves, and always leave you shoes with the shoe guy. It only cost 20r to ensure they are there when you get out?

Title: Very interesting
Text: An important religious and cultural site. The climb is nothing compared with Lions Rock. The caves are all highly decorated and very interesting. One was being restored but you could still go in and it was interesting to see the team of conservators at work.

Title: Nice place
Text: We went early so was not crowded when we went up. They have a room where you can keep the luggage and when you arrive to the top they have a clock room for shoes in exchange for a fee. The temple is nice and the handwork impressive. We had the opportunity of seeing the paintings of a room being restaured and then you realised how hard work is everywhere. Nice view also from the top

Title: Worth the trek
Text: Worth the trek up the steps. Stunning views along the way with plenty of places to stop and enjoy the vistas. Amazing statutes, intricate design and colours. Remember to wear your socks as the ground gets hot!

Title: better than Kandy
Text: We liked this place more than Kandy (if I may compare apples and oranges).  We did as the Rough Guide recommended, i.e., started visiting the caves from the one furthest from the entrance (cave 5, the smallest one), building the momentum up to cave 2 (the greatest) and cave 1 for the dessert.  I use the scare quotes around caves, as they are not real caves, but a space under a hanging rock partitioned into five areas.  Very atmospheric place.  The entrance (for foreigners) is 1500 LKR, with additional 25 LKR for each pair of shoes you leave in a safety shack just before entering the caves.  Worth the climb.

Title: Definitely worth the trek
Text:
There are two paths up to the caves. One has steps the other a steep slope. We didnt fancy the steps so went the other way, which I believe takes a bit longer. It was a bit of a trek, but fine, definitely worth it to see the cave temple. Its amazing how tranquil they are considering the crowds. There are 5 caves in all. The first one is tiny so some patience (and queuing) is needed. The second one is huge and the third is pretty big too. When youve seen those three youve seen the best of it and the other caves are just more of the same. 

Remember to cover your shoulders and knees. Take a pair of socks because you cant wear shoes inside. They will look after your shoes outside the entrance for 50Sr a pair. Otherwise take a bag and carry them around. Also, most importantly dont pose for pictures with your back to Budda, its a big no no. The path to the left on the way down leads you to the Golden Temple Of Dambulla, with its giant Budda, which is worth seeing just by itself. Overall this was definitely worth the trek and were happy we saw this impressive cave temple. 

Iain, London

Title: family visit
Text: Not so great, USD 7 entry ticket, too much crowd,It is having many top ceiling drawings, other than, no much special attraction

Title: Fantastic caves of Dambulla
Text:
This was a visit whilst on a tour of Sri Lanka. I was looking forward to this.  There is a small climb to the top which is not too strenuous for most.  The caves are fantastic and hard to believe they are man made.  The history is incredible and all the caves are worthy of a visit. Hard to believe the paintings and Buddhas in the caves.

The views are also good from the top.  You can also have a blessing whilst there.

It is worth rembering that shoulders and knees must be covered and no shoes allowed when you go through the entrance.

Title: Is this place real??? (the answer is yes)
Text: This place is unbelievable.  The paintings are brights despite being centuries old...they look like fabric hanging from a ceiling.  The carvings are beautiful.  There's definitely a sense of of peace in the temple and on the rock outside.  Worth the climb!

Title: The cave is on top of the hill
Text:
We thought that the cave is at ground level but it is wrong. You have to walk up around 10-15 minutes. You cannot enter if you wear shorts. The floor is super hot at day time so socks are good options.

The cave is not big but very beautiful.

Title: Impressive
Text:
Impressive temples. Worth a visit and.... the climb. In the last one, there was an agressive high pith tone. It hurted my ears, while the others did not hear anything
 Strange.

Title: Great cave temple complex
Text:
If you climbed the 1200 steps of Sigiriya, than these 450 steps are easy for you to reach the top. Like all temples, there is a dress code. Inside this cave temple you find great sculptures. Pay also attention to the ceilings. They are very nice decorated.
On your way down to the street you see a huge golden buddha. Entrance fee is Rs1500 for foreigners. This is a very interesting site.

Title: Fascinating Three Caves.
Text:
Made a special trip here based on TA reviews and very glad we made the effort. 

Three very different caves the last one of which used to be a store room before being converted. The reclining Buddha which had been carved out of the granite is truly wonderful. The effort required to carve the granite with what we a know as very primitive tools must have been immense. 

Our guide talked us through each cave and the history surrounding it.

One piece of advice, we ate in the cafe by The Foreigners car park, the food was amazing. Two Rotis and a bottle of water 150 rupees, its government funded which is why its so cheap.

Title: Steep climb but worth it
Text:
We arrived at the site about 2.0clock , steep climb up about 500 steps to the caves.  At the top you need to take off your shoes. But the tiles outside are incredibly hot. Tip is to take socks with you to put on when you take your shoes off.

It is worth the visit especially with a guide

Title: Interesting Religious History
Text: All you need is approx. 2 hours and a long flight of steps with an awesome view to explore these interesting caves of religious history. I was more fascinated on how these statues were placed in these caves. Note that you need to be covered from your shoulders to your ankles as a respect. Just a pareo or a sarong should suffice. Ladies no baring of shoulders please. You must leave your foot wear outside the temples. There is a fee for keeping your sandals safe. Less than USD$1. Don't leave your sandals unattended cos the monkeys will take it.

Title: Amazing
Text:
Lots of steps but worth the effort. As per the other reviewers, try to go early as the sun heats up the rocks you need to walk on. You have to pay to store your shoes to just before you go into the temples so allow 50 rupees for each set of shoes.
Caves are amazing!

Title: A Historical Place
Text: Worth visiting if you are passing by the temple as you can gain some knowledge about history and specially enjoy the ancient paintings. Make sure to go in the early morning or in an evening as the scorching sun can burn you during the walk to the cave temple from the vehicle. However,  it is not worthy to make your plans purposely to visit this temple itself. Just take a visit if you are passing by.

Title: Lots of steps but worth it.
Text:
This is a very interesting temple with an amazing history. Get a guide.
There are a number of steps up from the car park but they are level and easy walking. There are five temples to see each with different statues, rock carvings and wall paintings.
The views are stunning, the temple flowers beautiful and the monkeys delightful.
In the car park is a cafe (of sorts) and toilets. Look out for the "Jack fruit" tree with the amazing and very large Jack fruits. Tasty too.

Title: A hard climb but worth it
Text: There are a number of cave temples, most of the Bhuddist but one is Hindu. We had a monk show us around well worth the small charge. In spite of the large numbers of people the site remains tranquil. Watch out for the monkeys

Title: Excellent
Text: World Heritage Site, beautiful and very interesting temples, bit of a walk up but worth it when you get to the top.You have to take your shoes off so socks are useful !

Title: Very steep climb -  for temple enthusiasts!
Text: Steps rise steeply from the car park for approx 100m. Sari hire (for those who need to cover knees approx 100SLK). Three main caves to explore. Return to car park avoiding steep steps possible half way down far side (right at shop). Golden temple easier to reach by road rather than walking.

Title: Well worth it
Text: Wear good walking shoes to climb the rocky stairs and socks to manage the hot stones after you leave your shoes at the entrance- take your time to look at the ceilings and the statues- very rich!

Title: Worth the climb
Text: The hike up to the caves is by a longish flight of steps and takes about 20 minutes. There is an extensive array of Buddha statues and painted images (>150) many of which are interesting. We were unfortunate to arrive at a time when the caves were closed for prayers and so a large number of visitors accumulated outside the caves waiting to be admitted, which meant the caves became extremely crowded and difficult to move around once they reopened - I imagine it would be much less of a problem if you are able to arrive some time after the caves have been reopened (unfortunately I do not know when the prayer times are).

Title: Nice caves, shame they are not maintained
Text: For almost $8 a visit and with so many visitors, youd think these caves could be properly maintained. They arent properly lit, the outsides are crumbling and wooden tables keep the visitors back. Touts bother you a lot. There is zero information on the caves around the site. No signs to the golden temple (which we almost missed). Disappointing.

Title: Wonderful experience
Text: A climb almost couple of kilometers up on the rock you will reach an amazing site of golden temple under the cave. It constitute 5 temples with numerous Buddha statute and the statue of Bodhisattva. Just an amazing site and worth every second and seven step. From up you will see a well preserved forest and small villages interlocked with nature. Amazing. Please visit.

Title: Worth the stairs
Text: We really enjoyed this, but I would recommend using a guide. Very well preserved/updated attraction with a very interesting history.

Title: A perfect historical experience
Text: This is one of the best places we visited when we were in Dambulla and it is a beautiful place. You get nice and calming experience when you are there. Lots of information about the history, beautiful paintings and sculptures done thousands of years ago. Started with the cave and visited backwards which is the recommended way. Visit in early morning or in the evening to avoid scorching sun.

Title: This is a must see sight!
Text: I have to say that the Sri Lanka Government takes advantage of it's tourists and charges a small fortune for visiting each site!! Saying that, I would not pass on this site. You have about 5 caves that have Buddhas of different shapes and sizes inside them. You also have a beautiful view of the area.

Title: Interesting visit
Text:
Stopped here on our tour of Sri Lankas cultural triangle. 

Very interesting place and worth a visit (and worth climbing all the steps). 

A few pointers:

Its worth having a guide with you. We were on a private tour of the country with a driver/guide and he was able to explain the history of the caves and the significance of the paintings in each one. It would have been quite difficult to have the same appreciation if you just went up and looked around by yourself.  

Its a fully functioning religious site, of huge significance to the Sri Lankan people. There are periods of worship throughout the day when visitors need to wait outside. Both ladies and gentlemen need to wear clothes which cover the elbows and their knees. Transgressors were turned away without exception (and left at the mercy of the very enterprising sarong salesman on the steps outside!)

Our guide intervened when a Japanese tourist was about to commit the massively disrespectful offence of photographing his companion with her back to an image of Buddha. There are warnings about this everywhere and in every guide book, so there is really no excuse.

Title: Must visit
Text: Up the steps, monkeys, great view and amazing visit. Even the kids loved the visit. Ladies remember you need to cover up shoulders and legs.

Title: Interesting Heritage Site
Text: The Dumbulla Rock Temple is an impressive and interesting place to visit. However, be warned that there are approximately 350+ steps to navigate before you reach the actual caves! I would definitely recommend going during the early part of the morning, before the heat starts to rise. As you enter the complex, you are greeted by a magnificent Buddha statue, and a general information center. Then the ascent begins. I am fairly fit, and it took me and our group about 40 minutes to get to the caves, with a few rest bite stops. Please remember to wear clothes which are longer than knee length as you will not be able to enter. They only seem to charge foreigners (approximately £7), to enter the main cave complex, which I don't think is fair,  as either everyone should pay something, or it should be free for all. Either way, the caves are impressive, with several ancient paintings and statues, created over several centuries by devotees to Lord Buddha. As we all religious sites, it is always an interesting visit, and the history of the caves are impressive. As an added bonus, the views from the top are breathtaking and shows the real beauty of Sri Lanka. Definitely worth a visit, but go early to avoid the crowds and the heat.

Title: Worth visiting but beware of dressing code
Text:
The most impressive thing is being there and try to imagine how it was built. Out of the 5 caves I found 1 very beautiful. 

I think staff at the entrance is very picky about clothes so you have to borrow a scarf from next door (100 rupees). I was wearing long trousers and very short sleeves t-shirt and they made me go for a scarf. I think it was adequate dressing code but anyway...it seemed to me they have a good business up there because once you are there, it is very unlikely to go down just to bring something to cover your arms. Also, there is a paid place to leave shoes whereas in other temples you could just leave them outside

Title: Stunning hill top views
Text: Great views of the town around the hill top cave temple. Very well kept cave temple. Strong history. Amazing sculptures and ceiling paintings.

Title: Very impressive and worth the trip
Text: These caves are very impressive, start at the last cave and work your way back - each cave becomes more and more spectacular.  Just stunning and be sure to cover up.

Title: A must see
Text: There are two access routes, slopes or steps.  We took the slopes option but the last slope was very steep as such we used the stairs for a short distance coming down and then reverted to the slopes.  It was worth the trek.  The caves, statues, walls and ceiling paintings are amazing.

Title: Amazing pieces
Text:
What Ab amazing set of caves with some of the best preserved works ... like most attractions the foreigner counter can be hard to find and is actually down a steep set of stairs that you need to re climb to get to the entrance - shoe storage charges, gauging guides and also compulsory sarong hiring abound - which detract from the natural beauty. 

For any foreigners ensure you driver goes
Around the back to find the ticket office first and when you get to the entrance just say no to the guides and other items.

Title: Well maintained cave temple
Text: Though the steps are not fully safe, the temple is well maintained and inside the caves there are no birds/bats as seen in other cave temples. Must visit if you are in Dambulla.

Title: Amazing ancient preserved artwork
Text: We've seen a LOT of temples here in Sri Lanka, but these blew me away. The natural eneven stone ceilings on these caves are fully painted, and maybe because they're in caves they're amazingly preserved. They make Michaelanglo's Cystine chapel ceiling work look modern! It's worth the walk up to see these, not to mention the many Buddhas inside each one.

Title: Wonderful
Text:
This really is wonderful. 

Even though its 400 steps up, taken steadily it wasnt too difficult. My mum who is 79 (sorry mum) and has had a hip replacement took it slowly and managed the climb. 

The views on the way up are lush and beautiful. And even better from the top. Its a temple so shoulders and knees covered (please)

The cave temples are full of different Buddha (not sure what the pleural is) and unlit. 

The place is fascinating - from the undercut rock (so the rain doesnt damage living space) to the net hammock catching tree blossom (it cant be used as an offering if taken from the ground) 

Loved it here.

Title: Worth the climb of stairs!
Text:
Dambulla cave temple is stunning. I have been to Ellora and Ajanta caves in India and I found these to be just as beautiful. It is worth the visit. This kind of work, done more than 2100 years ago is impressive on every level. The g
conservation of the paintings is wonderful. Lighting could be a bit better. Some parts are rather dark. 
You must walk up a lot of stairs that are uneven in size to access the cave. We went at noon and it was quite hot. Women must cover their shoulders and knees. Men as well. We hired a guide at the top and charged 1500 rupees for a 40 min tour.

Title: Cool
Text: Temples are all nice, this one is also great, nice view and nice feeling with the presence of spirituality around

Title: Part of Sri Lanka's rich history
Text: Another of the must places to visit and yes more steep steps to climb as they always seem to be at the top of a hill. There are 5 caves to visit of different size, and it is suggested that you go in reverse order, 5 to 1. The ceiling painting is fantastic and there are lots of buddhas of varying size. We went at 0900 on leaving Kandy and the visit lasted 2 hours.

Title: Dambulla tuk-tuk
Text:
We were in dambulla for 2 complete days even if you can do it on a 1day rush trip.
We managed to hire a great tuk-tuk driver o took us to everywhere nearby the city and more... Through rural areas and off the beaten track areas.

Dambulla caves were the first Stop on the Sunset of our first day. Amazing time to visit this really charming place.
They have 5 different small temples wich are full of statues and a Nice surrounding área.

If you need a good tuk-tuk driver for hoje Stay in Dambulla here is our driver phone Number: 
Sunil 0776178324

Title: A long climb, but worth it.
Text: A mesmerising experience. Each cave has its own character, containing beautifully carved and painted statues. The atmosphere inside is like that of an Indiana Jones movie. Also good to see the worshippers bringing their offerings.

Title: Fascinating
Text: Another must-see attraction in the Dambulla area.  And another steep climb - about 300 steps.  The five cave temples are from different time periods and varying styles.  All very interesting.  Large areas roped off to avoid destruction.  Crowds can make the smaller caves claustrophobic.  Go as early as possible.  We saw this the same day as Sigiriya.  If possible do on two separate days - quite exhausting to do both!

Title: An Interesting Visit
Text: This complex is well worth seeing even though there are quite a few steps to climb to reach it not all of which are even. There are several caves with many figures within them and the lighting makes it very atmospheric.

Title: Place you should not miss
Text: Fascinating rock temple with origin in 1st c. BC is definitely place worth the visit. After taking lots of stairs up the rock, well-deserved view over jungle and distant hills presents itself. Temple that is inbuilt into rock masif is part of world heritage and despite it´s honourable age, statues and cave paintings are well preserved. We arrived late afternoon and we stayed to watch sunset from the top which was wonderful. I really recommend to not skip this place if you visit Sri Lanka. Be prepared for a climb, carying some water with you, covering yourself while entering the temple and also for lots of locals trying to sell you souvenirs. Exiting area is by descending down to Golden Temple which is nice too, pretty new place but what were we more excited about was small stall with delicious local snacks next to it :)

Title: Amazing statues in a series of temples
Text: There is a series of caves from different centuries filled with statues and carvings and rich colours. Well worth a visit and a pleasant 15 minute stroll up to the top,making friends with the monkeys along the way.

Title: Dambulla Cave Temple
Text: A World Heritage Site in Sri Lanka. The rock towers 160 m over the surrounding plains. It has  five caves, which contain statues and paintings. Around 400 steps to climb. Entry fees 1500 slr.

Title: Amazing historical site
Text: This temple has many chambers or rooms, many Buddha statues and some fantastic painted ceilings.  You need a guide to tell you about what you can see as there are not many information panels. Well worth taking time to look at all areas.

Title: Budha statues and temple not made in china style ;-)
Text: A very nice temple with passion made in the past and without made in china plastic tingelings all over. Only minor is that foreigners have to take a totaly different entrance (walk around the whole complex) and like all over sri lanka have to pay 10-100 times more.

Title: Spirit of place
Text:
The walk up is scenic and the steps manageable as you can admire the view and take photos if you need a breather.

Go early because its cooler and especially at the weekend when the locals will visit to pray.

Its the largest conserved cave temple in Sri Lanka. There are four caves containing statues and painted images of budda. The paintings cover the walls and ceilings and you need to allow your eyes to acclimatise to the dim lighting and then take in the detail. It was pretty busy on the Sunday morning that we visited and the caves were humid and full of visitors trying to get the perfect shot which created some bottle necks. Then, in the midst of all the tourist footfall,  there were the local worshippers making their offerings which helped to remind you what this place is really all about. Its worth taking some quiet time to soak up the atmosphere and to enjoy the place before heading back down.

Dress modestly, remove your shoes and turn off the flash.

Title: Good walk, unusual temple.
Text: The Dambulla Cave Temple is located on top of a mountain and to get to it you need to climb hundreds of steps, so wear appropriate shoes, and also it is a requirement that you wear clothes that cover your knees. The view from the top of the mountain is spectacular. The temples are well worth seeing, set into caves and with an interesting history.

Title: Great to learn something about Sri Lanka's history
Text:
This is an ancient Cave temple that dates back to the 1st century. There are five chambers with murals painted all over the walls and Buddha's carved out of stone. 

The golden temple is also part of the UNESCO site.

Physical challenge: we came up from the cave carpark and there are a lot of steps that are uneven, we saw a lot of older people stopping to take rest along the way. There is some cover, but on a sunny day it was quite intense. The view going up is amazing.

Costs: it cost 1500 rupee for the entry ticket. At the temple you must remove your shoes. There is a shoe cloak bay where people look after your shoes for about 50 rupee. I was told shoulders and knees.must be covered. I had shorts to my knees but was still required to hire a wrap to cover the lower part of my legs. Wraps cost 100 rupee to hire

Title: A small but unique cave temple complex
Text:
Having been to a large number of buddist temple sites in SE Asia - including other cave temples - I found Dambulla interesting and beautiful but not entirely unique. If you have not been to many other places that are similar it is definitely a must visit. Otherwise, I'd recommend it if you have time and interest in this type of attraction but I would not rearrange my schedule to fit it in.

The caves themselves are not very large and are quite warm inside. The walls and ceilings are painted and beautiful to look at - more so then the Buddhas in my opinion. The lighting is ROUGH for photography unless you have specialized equipment. The caves are dark with spotlights in various areas. This makes the location less of an Instagram-worthy location if that's your thing but most people should enjoy the sights just fine. 

I'd recommend going first thing in the morning to avoid crowds and to avoid the heat. The caves were already hot at 8 am so I can't imagine what it gets like later in the day. Also be prepared to climb stairs to get there. About 365 of them. Its steep and while I thought it was worth the cardio workout - someone who is out of shape or who has impaired mobility may not be able to make it.

Tips:

- don't forget to wear long pants and tops with shoulders covered. Men included. or bring a sarong to wrap around if you have shorts on. 

- This is a Buddhist temple so you need to leave your shoes near the entrance (there is a safe location to do so) and walk around barefoot. You will be walking on stone/concrete. 

- With the climb up and plenty of time spent in each cave we did the whole thing in 1.5 hours. 

- There is plenty of parking and clean bathrooms at the bottom of the stairs for public use.

Title: Must See
Text:
Like most iconic sights there is a foreigners rate for entry. This is still a reasonably priced attraction though. I would say if youre only going to do a few Buddhist temples then this is one to do. There are quite a few large steps up from the car park but worth the effort. Take a bag for your shoes as you have to take them off and not have them on show. Also youre required to cover your shoulders and knees. 
Depending how interested you are the Buddhist faith will depend on how long
you wish to spend here. We did the whole thing with lots of photos in an hour.

Title: Confusing grounds
Text: Our taxi driver dropped us off at the Buddha statue which is very far from the ticket office for the cave temple. It is not very well marked, so as long as you know where you're going, it is well worth the many stairs and higher entrance cost!

Title: Amazing Buddhist Temple
Text: Temple with various statues of Buddha located in caves, beautifully painted. One has to climb a number of steep steps to get there but well worth it. Entry fee is 500 Sri Lankan rupees for adults.

Title: Totally amazing but beware the stairs
Text:
Visited Dambulla Caves and potentially foolishly, assumed caves would be fairly close to ground level. They aren't, they are near the top of a mountain, at the top of a lot of stairs.

Seeing the caves really was worth it but i have some mobility problems, so the trip up and then back down, was very hard.

Not saying don't go - but do your research if you have trouble walking or climbing stairs for any distance.

Title: Amazing place
Text: A must to see when you visit Sri Lanka.Very old,culturally interesting place.You should definitely not miss it!

Title: Ancient cave temple - not like anything you have seen before
Text: There is a modest uphill walk to get to the cave temple. As with all Buddhist temples, you have to check your shoes and take off your hat. The interior of the caves are filled with many different version of Buddha statues. The walls have ancient paintings. One of my favorite Buddha statues was in the first cave that you reach. Behind it, peaking out to greet you was a smaller statue of the last king of the second kingdom. He seems to have been a bit of a narcissist and was known as the Inscripton King for leaving carved inscriptions of all the great things he had done.

Title: Great caves!!!
Text:
Get your tickets before you go upstairs!!!!
After you get to the top you leave your shoes in the rack and then you are allowed to see the caves. 
There are 5 caves all in all. The first 3 are the most impressive ones. The paintings in the ceilings are truly impressive.

Title: Another interesting Buddhist temple
Text:
The climb, although not that long, could be considered by some to be pretty steep. The temple itself is interesting, especially considering how the caves have been dug into the rock. 
There are quite a few tourists, which can be expected but detracts from the overall experience.

Title: Very beautiful and definitely worth a visit!
Text:
We visited the Dambulla caves on the 18th of December 2018. The caves are at a slight altitude so I would recommend wearing something comfortable for a 20-30 minute hike up some steep steps. Also there were many monkeys near the steps so I would recommend not taking anything edible like fruits etc openly since it could attract the monkeys. Also remember that there is an entrance fee of ~1500 LKR so don't forget to buy these tickets before climbing the steps

Once you climb the steps and reach the top, the view is absolutely beautiful! There is a place to store your footwear near the cave complex just besides the entrance.

The caves themselves are very beautiful and I would recommend that you take your best night/low light photography equipment you have. The paintings on the top of the caves are very colorful and detailed and you would definitely want to take a few shots of these pictures. The statues of the Buddha's in various poses are a real sight to see. The cave complex itself is very well maintained and shouldn't take you more than 50-60 minutes to complete.

TIP: if you plan to visit the Temple complex during the evening I would highly recommend a torch light and some mosquito repellent. It can get very dark once the sun sets and there were many mosquitos on the way down mainly because of the surrounding forests.

This place is definitely worth a visit with family and friends.

Title: Rather unusual, but perhaps too many Buddhas
Text: Its a long climb up the 2-300 steps on a hot and humid day, but worth it for the views. There are many monkey's, even a couple of Temple cats and you can see Sigiriya in the distance. To be honest when you have visited one cave you have probably seen all that is necessary.

Title: Unique
Text:
Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.
Took around an hour to climb up and walk around.
A very unique temple with some lovely cave paintings and statues

Title: Dambulla Cave Temple
Text: The temple is built into the rock. It is a world heritage site and really worth a visit. Very impressive

Title: Superb Heritage
Text: This beautiful cave temple is placed at a considerable height but the stairs are OK and after reaching there you will fill happy. Entry fee for foreigners is excessive high in comparison to locals, it is 1500 LKR. There are total 05 caves in same complex one by one where so many Buddha statues of different sizes can be seen. Some are standing, some sitting and laying but all are nice. In Dambulla, it is must visit site.

Title: Serene
Text: Well maintained caves laden with Buddhist history.Wall n roofs of the caves painted and preserved belonging to different centuries.Very cool and peaceful place with Buddha statues all over the caves.Serene.Just remember to visit in proper attire.Shorts and short skirts not allowed.

Title: Ancient temple with a lot of history
Text:
A visit to SriLanka is incomplete without visiting these Ancient caves with natural painting. I would recommend you to wear socks to avoid heat.
Hire a guide to get a good knowledge about the history of the temple.

Title: My favorite of our trip!
Text: Dambulla Rock Cave Temple with its 100s of Buddhist statues and ancient Buddhist cave paintings does not disappoint. I absolutely loved it here and was impressed by how well things held up to time. Spent a long time here in this lovely spiritual place.

Title: Really interesting and worth a visit
Text:
Called here in November. I think the guide said there were 450 steps but not arduous, although the steps have been worn in place. Taken carefully well worth the effort. Once at the top you will need to remove you shoes, and there's an area that will cost charge you 25 rupees to look after. You can put socks on and some may need it when really hot as the stone does hold the heat. 
Multiple caves with a huge amount of Buddhas and statues.
Worth having a guide or reading the story beforehand as this helps understanding what each area represents. 
Please bear in mind when what their culture finds rude and offensive especially taking photos (turning your back in the Buddha I've selfies is offensive and unacceptable as well as posing with the Buddhas)

The toilets and facilities at the bottom of the steps is basic.

But would recommend this area.

Title: Very interesting
Text:
Ancient caves turned into temples. Very unique and interesting!
Quite a lot of stairs to get to the caves, but not bad unless you have health issues.

Title: Excellent place to see
Text: Nice place to see. Inside they do not allow selfie...so be careful. It is a cave temple and you need to mind your head in certain places. Buddha in reclining posture is good. Can see once

Title: Totally humbled by the intensity of this experience.
Text: You have a lot of steep steps to climb to Nirvana, and you will be beset upon by hawkers en route, but on arriving at the Temple you will be astonished. Five caves are open for viewing and the carvings and paintings are extraordinary. You will need to be comfortable with walking for a few hundred metres barefoot, as your shoes must be surrendered on entry to the temple. Do not miss this, not only is it a spiritual experience, but it is pretty much smack bang in the geographical centre of Sri Lanka.

Title: a lot of buddhas
Text:
hot, humid and touristy. Interesting paintings and use of the rock to make the temples
I would give it a miss in retrospect unless you are a Buddhist or and archeologist

Title: impressive temple
Text: it's a place to visit ... easy to get up to ... and very impressive. the temple is in the caves and is full of statues

Title: Very impressive!
Text: The caves with hundreds of Buddah statues are really impressive, and if you are in the area, are a place you should not miss out

Title: Great views
Text: We visited the cave temples as part of our tour of Sri Lanka it was really interesting but not for the feint hearted as it is quite a climb up some very steep stairs but was well worth it when we got there eventually! The views were spectacular!

Title: Climb
Text: This is a beautiful old Buddhist temple here. The Buddha statues are beautiful. The time you need here depends  on your ability to climb.

Title: Nice to see if in area
Text: Much history for this site, which is a climb and good to see if any the area, though i have seen better Budhist temples

Title: Nice place
Text: Its a great place to visit and learn the ancient history and Buddhas life. It is not allowed to be head covered and they will ask you to remove your scarf and for the men shorts arent allowed so make sure u take a scarf with you before going.

Title: Tradition and art
Text:
We stopped by these amazing caves dug into a huge rock at the top of the mountain. You will need to climb the steps to reach this point in which you will surely enjoy an incredible overview.

You will have to pay between 200 and 400 rupees. When you complete the visit, the monkeys will be waiting for you outside and will easily entertain you.

Title: 5 cave temples and about 200 steps up
Text: There is a parking spot right at the bottom and there is a 200 odd step to climb to the entrance of the caves. There are 5 caves in total, dress code is shoulders covered and shoes off. Quite an amazing site with some do the caves very small and crowded. We spent an hour an half here and the kids enjoyed the climb!

Title: A Mystical Cave Worth Visiting
Text:
I had the opportunity to visit the cave two weeks ago.  It is an inspiring experience where you feel that you have gone back in time.  The caves are full of incredible carvings of the "Lord Buddha."  The expertise of the artists who created this incredible religious sanctuary is up there with the tomb painters of Egypt.

The view from the temple complex is beautiful and looks over a lush and verdant valley. Look out for the monkeys - they might grab food out of your hands.  The climb is not to bad - nothing like Sigiriya and is a experience that children of all ages will enjoy.  Bring drinking water with and do the climb early or late to avoid the midday heat.

Title: Beautiful caves and worth the climb
Text: After a big climb which I found not that easy however that could be that I am not as fit as some the Dambulla-Habarana caves were worth the climb. Magnificent paintings and massive Buddhas which our guide explained everything about. Make sure you have covered knees and shoulders and you will have to take your shoes off. We were allowed to keep our socks on. You can either leave them and pay or put them in your bag. Make sure you have small denomination money as they dont have change. Fabulous views from the top.

Title: Beautiful series of caves
Text:
There are 5 caves here reached by a staircase which is a little climb. These are temples and you need to remove your shoes and be appropriately dressed before entering the complex. There is a shoe place just by the entrance where you can pay to leave your shoes. 

The caves are of varying ages and interest. There is still a lot of restoration work taking place on the walls and ceilings but the main caves are quite beautiful and glisten with the colours of the various Buddhas; there are over 150 of them. It is the best preserved cave complex in Sri Lanka.

Its also quite dark in the caves so you need to push the camera settings if not using flash.

Its well worth the visit which we did enroute to Kandy from Sigiriya.

Title: Worth visiting
Text: Beautiful done with many nice details. many stairs to climb but it is really worth. you may spend there an hour or a bit more.

Title: Worth the climb
Text: Ditto to most of the previous reviews. Take your time climbing the stairs, as did I. If you like temples with a difference,  you'll love these.

Title: Wonderful
Text:
The Cave Temple are amazing, the paintings, the sculptures and the view from the top.
Notice: you have to cover the knee and the shoulders (man and women)

Title: Incredible and humid
Text: First of all, it is not an easy climb to reach the caves. If the air is also humid, it will be challenging. But it is so much worth it! Be careful, you have to go barefoot and if it rains, you must have some tissues to clean yourself.

Title: Incredible
Text:
Tucked away in five caves you'll find an incredible sight of around 150 perfectly preserved statues of Buddha. There is a definite serenity about the place that makes the slog up a couple of hundred steps worthwhile. 

One of the highlights of our trip to this wonderful country.

Title: Do it!
Text: Dambulla Cave Temple was one of our first sights to see and it didnt disappoint. Its a good walk uphill (stairs) especially in the heat but the views and Temple are so worth it! We were recommended to bring a pair of socks as shoes are not permitted and the ground is very hot. Also note, men and women need to be covered over shoulder and below the knee - take a sarong/scarf. The caves are amazing inside, we were wowed by the intricate details and beautiful paintings. Worth the trip!

Title: visit enhanced by being being with a knowledgable guide
Text:
We visited this temple as part of a guided tour of parts of Sri Lanka.  I definitely consider our experience was so enhanced by having our tour guide, Sumith, take time to point out to us the history of the 5 caves, the meaning and differences of the various statues and cultural aspects - so much more interesting and of value than "just" walking around. 

If you are not within a guided tour then would highly recommend finding detailed information about this site before you go.

at the time of our visit the only option was to reach the temple caves via about 400 steps, some very steep but there was help at hand along the way, places to stop and good handrails, so dont be put of - well worth the climb

this is a religious site, so light coloured clothing covering legs and arms is required - this was not clear from info provided by tour operators

a stunning temple to visit

Title: Quick tour
Text: Fantastic glimpse into the rich cultural and religious heritage of Sri Lanka.  After a long climb up the hill you are rewarded with 5 caves full of intricate paintings and statues.

Title: U would want to go
Text: Dambulla caves are natural but the temples built in it are man made cave temples about 30yrs old. Here u'll find sitting Bhudha, sleeping bhudha and many more statues of Bhudha along with the gigantic look alike helmet of the king preserved. But b4 u reach the temple there are about 300 - 500 stairs one way u need to climb to reach this temple. Its open all but there is 1 rule u cant break may it b men or women, that the body should be completely covered.

Title: Incredible experience. Definitely worth the climb.
Text: Whilst there are many steps to climb, it is definitely worth it to experience the amazing views and cave temples, created over 2,000 years ago. The paintings and sculptures are incredible and provide a real insight into the history of Sri Lankan culture and relligious history.

Title: Overwhelmingly beautiful and serene
Text:
It's a steep climb up well made steps to reach the caves which are actually rock overhangs which have walls to protect them from the elements. This is is also the site of a monastery and at times of worship ( preceded  by drumming) the caves are closed to the public for a short time.
It's a temple and ladies must have legs and shoulders covered, no shorts or vest tops for men. Shoes are left at the top of the steps ( take socks in hot weather so you don't burn your feet in the courtyard).
The art on the walls and ceilings is magnificent at times looking like beautiful embroidery. The lighting makes the caves very atmospheric with the numerous Buddha statues illuminated.
It's well worth reading up on the caves before you visit as they all date from different periods. The far left cave has had some poor restoration ... it would have been better to leave it as it was. 
You can buy lotus flowers by the main road to leave as offerings.
It is a wonderful place of great beauty.

Title: Unique
Text: It's quite a climb, lots of steps. The caves at the top are worth it as it's one of the more unique Buddhist sights on the island.

Title: Great views, caves
Text: Great views of the surrounding area, a few steps up to the top. Prices were 1500 rupees each to enter. 25 rupees each to leave shoes outside the temple. 100 rupees to hire a sarong to cover knees. We also paid 1000 rupees for a tour guide - be careful as they show you the first temple and explain what is in there, then continue on for the next 4 temples and will charge you. So if you dont want to pay then say no to the tour guide. Very informative though and lots of information given. Worth a visit if you are going past!

Title: Must see
Text: Do not miss this temple if you are in the area, it is in a fantastic scenery! The place itself was built inside a rock cavity. Make sure you have a good guide to get the historical details.

Title: Worth the Climb !
Text: After climbing up over 300 steps (some of them had quite the height / rise) and by many monkeys, we arrived at these beautiful caves and all of us felt the climb was certainly worth the work of the steps.  There is an alternate way up and down and we chose this route for the descent... but it is too long and steady up for the 'going'.  Would recommend the steps up and switchback going down.  Also recommend taking a pair of old socks to wear in temples.  The ground can be either too hot or a bit rough on the feet.

Title: Beautiful, peaceful, historic place.
Text: BUY YOUR TICKET AT THE BOTTOM! You cannot buy your ticket at the top/entrance to the caves. Even if 3 official-looking people assure you otherwise.

Title: Hot, Nice Views
Text:
From the base, we climbed the steep stairs to the Cave Temple. Being Unesco recognised, must visit.
The entrance fee is LKR1500 + shoes deposit LKR25 per pair compulsory, cannot keep in your bag.
After deposit our shoes, start from the last Cave to the first. All the 5 caves are almost similar at least to me. A sleeping statue and some standing. The walls and ceilings are all with mural paintings using natural plaster and dyes at its original state.
The 2nd temple is the largest of all 5.
Taje a look at the view outside the temple - mountains and valleys. And many hosts welcome us on the way up and down - monkeys.

Title: Well worth the climb
Text: It was amazing, well worth the climb. Incredible how they managed to get all those Buddhas up there. The cave paintings were fabulous, a must see.

Title: very nice place
Text: the caves are very old. In each cave there are nice carved Buddhas and nice old fresco's. From there you can easily walk to the golden temple.

Title: For temple lovers
Text: Great if you like temples but you have to take your shoes off so be carefull of the very hot floor outside.

Title: Amazing
Text: Well worth a visit, the carvings and work are amazing but it is a religious site so appropriate dress has to be worn- it is interesting to note some tourists take no notice of this.

Title: worth to go
Text: worth to go this place and it is better if you have a tourguide. our guide is a knowledgeable! and of course you can see a lot of monkeys as well ????

Title: Lovely visit
Text:
Visited here as part of our tour of Sri Lanka and thought it was very impressive. The climb took me by surprise and after a busy day doing lots of climbing struggled abit but just take it steady.
As with all temples remember to take a pair of old socks to wear as you need to remove your shoes and the ground is uneven and rough under foot.
The caves were amazing and so much better than I expected that this place is definitely worth a visit. 
I read afterwards that you should start with the cave further away and work backwards, we did not do this but would recommend you do.
Outside lots of locals trying to sell you their goods -make sure you barter.

Title: Stunning temple!
Text:
Great temple any many statues of budda.

Make sure you buy your ticket at the entrance which is BEFORE the large climb. The ticket booth is a tiny grilled window which is very easy to miss.

The temple is amazing inside considering how much rock there was to carve out.

Make sure you cover shoulders and legs.

Avoid the hustlers at the top by not hanging around. The shoe guardians are also hustlers themselves which is very surpirsing but just roll with it.

The climb is ok but the stairs wear to a slope at one point.

Title: Enjoyed the climbing path than the cave itself
Text: I enjoyed the climbing path than the cave itself, it was fun with kids.  As the cave is very ancient, it will be more interested if you are a retrophiliac.  Keep enough water and snacks if you have enough time to spend on the top. You can skip if your schedule is tight.

Title: A unique place
Text:
A very unique place. We went there on February and it was rather could on the mountain top but in the cave it was warm and humid. Bring something to drink if you are having circulation problems!
Also you have to take off your shoes (as in other temples as well). Pay an inheritant to look after your shoes or the monkeys will take them!

Title: A must!
Text:
Be prepared for a long, steep climb following the Kings Way! But worth it and the inevitable stops allow the admire the stunning views over the country side. As in some other places of worship, shoes have to be taken off. May be wearing socks is a good idea. Engaging a guide is highly recommended. Ours was really very good and gave us information broader than only concerning the Temple.
The Temple in the five caves starts from 100 BC - caves 1,2 and 4. The fifth cave is from the beginning of XX century. There are impressive statures of The Buddha as well as other statues all from different materials. The wall frescoes are from later times or have been repainted later. Really interesting and impressive. There is a Stupa which appears broken and repaired. And indeed it had been broken in 1936 and all the treasures, jewellery donated by kings and queens through time, have been stolen. Regrettably, never found and recovered.
Highly recommended and it is a must as it sheds light on Sri Lankan history and relation to Buddhism, stimulating further learning about this nation.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Loved visiting this place and enjoying the amazing caves with their Buddha images. There were paintings on the walls and ceilings as well. A must when you are travelling to Kandy. Good views from the terrace as well.

Title: Stunning
Text: Beautiful art works in a timeless setting. The cave paintings and statues blend down the centuries to create a unique and lovely experience.

Title: worth visiting
Text: Super place to visit - well worth it. Bring socks to wear as the ground gets very hot. Have a good guide to give you all the information

Title: Very impressive and atmospheric
Text: The cave temples are remarkable. They have been in existence for over 2000 years. Each cave was something different. We were fortunate to have our driver guide who was able to tell us about Buddha and the history of the caves. Be prepared for a steep walk. A few stray dogs and monkeys along the way but was safe enough.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: Get here early to avoid the heat. The caves are beautiful. There are 5 of them, the second and third I think are the most impressive. Make sure you bring something to cover your shoulders and knees as its a religious place. If youre lucky youll see loads of monkeys on the rocks at the star of the steps you have to climb.

Title: Not to be missed!
Text:
There is a steep 10 minute climb up to the rock cave temple from the parking area. Shoes need to be removed and shoulders and knees covered before entering. Socks are a really good idea to take along.

Spectacular Buddha statues and artwork fill the caves. An amazing experience.

Title: Nice spot
Text: Nice spot to visit - less than 30 minutes away from Sigiriya's center. You take stairs up to the temple where you deposit your shoes and can walk barefoot into the temple. It is a cluster of temples and you can walk from one to the other. Have something on you to cover your knees (males and females) and shoulders and socks because the floor is hot. There's an entry ticket and a fee to deposit your shoes. More reviews @myra.recommends

Title: Local Buddhism and History
Text: Beautiful place, well maintained. Would definitely wow those who love history and buddhism. Worth a visit just to understand local culture.

Title: Dambulla Cave Temple: Ancient Art and Stunning Views
Text:
The Dambulla Cave Temple, also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, is a must-visit attraction when traveling to Sri Lanka. Located just 10 minutes away from Dambulla village, the temple can be easily reached by bus or tuk-tuk. The entrance fee is 2000 LKR (around 5 Euros), which is well worth the cost to experience this unique and sacred place.

Upon arrival, visitors must remove their shoes and dress appropriately out of respect for the temple. The climb to reach the temple takes around 20 minutes, but the views of the surrounding mountains along the way are breathtaking and make the journey even more worthwhile.

The Dambulla Temple is divided into two parts: the temple cave and the golden Buddha. It's important to note that if you want to see the golden Buddha, you should not go back to the main entrance. Instead, continue on to the lower level of the temple, where the golden Buddha is located.

Inside the temple cave, visitors will be amazed by the intricate and well-preserved ancient cave paintings and statues of the Buddha. The peaceful atmosphere of the temple is truly awe-inspiring, and visitors can take their time to explore the cave and take in the stunning surroundings.

Overall, the Dambulla Cave Temple is an unforgettable experience that shouldn't be missed when visiting Sri Lanka. The climb to the temple may be a bit challenging, but the reward of exploring this sacred and historical site, along with the breathtaking views of the mountains, is worth the effort.

Title: Amazing place to see it
Text: amazing place. Five caves it is a beautiful . Amazing wall paint. Dont mis it your tours in srilanka

Title: Amazing
Text: Must to see amazing temple , so kind person and highly recomended place to see , kids are visiting and learning also taining in temple

Title: Amazing rock temples
Text: Quite a few steps to climb but worth it. The statues and paintings in the rock temples are amazing. The temples are actually set in natural rock caves with walls built in front to seal off the temple. Suggest good footwear.

Title: A grateful king's tribute to his saviours a thousand year ago.
Text:
This almost thousand year old temple was built by a grateful king who was given shelter by Buddhist monks when he was on the run from enemy armies.

The paintings look like they were painted only yesterday but in reality they are many centuries old.

The temple is very well maintained and is a sacred place for Buddhists.

The staff are polite and friendly. They waited patiently for us to see all the caves before closing the temple complex for the day.

The approach to the temple has been very well maintained with chiseled steps, handrails, lights and resting places.

It is suggested that a cable car system could be installed for the pilgrims who are unable to climb all those steps.

The temple is in excellent condition and the rock temple is a beautiful place to visit and meditate.

A must visit while you are in Dambulla, Sri Lanka.

Highly recommended.

Title: Worth a short visit
Text: A little bit of a climb up the road and a visit to five ancient caves was worthwhile. It was our first temple visit so interesting enough with many ancient Buddha statues. A bit different being constructed within the natural caves.

Title: Great way to spend a few hours
Text:
Visited the cave complex from Habarana for a few hours after a day by the pool. 

Easy to get to by bus (45/48 from Habarana junction in direction of Kandy) but make sure they let you off by the front of the golden Buddha rather than in town (my conductor refused for some reason which meant a bit of a long walk). 

As others have said I can highly recommend getting a tuk tuk round to the ticket office then its only a short climb up to the top (15 mins). 

Once you are up there the views are epic, if you go late afternoon (around 4.30pm for me) there are not too many people around so easier to see the caves properly. Suggesting starting from the furthest cave and working your way back towards the entrance as this gives you more of a build up. 

Caves were impressive and had a really peaceful atmosphere, highly recommended. Afterwards just head down main staircase and flag down a bus going back your direction from the road.

Title: Must see
Text: Beautifull caves, a guide is needed for full value due to the complex history. Few visitors due to the current situation.

Title: Terrific Temple.
Text: As this is a temple be prepared to dress appropriately, knees and shoulders covered for both men and women.  Note that unlike some temples around the world there is no option outside the temple to hire a sarong type thing to cover up with.  Plan your day accordingly and do what we did, which was to do a quick change in to long pants inside our van prior to heading to the temple, our last activity for the day.  We had a guide which was organised by our driver, he was very good sharing extensive knowledge throughout the various caves.  Be mindful when taking photos as it is disrespectful to face your back to Buddha, so dont try and take selfies with Buddha in the background.  You need to leave your shoes outside with attendants who charge you a small donation fee, you pay the fee on retrieval of your shoes so have some small change on you.  The caves are amazing and will take approx an hour at the most depending on how much your guide likes to talk to complete the caves.  Another must see while in Sri Lanka.

Title: A nice visit If passing
Text:
Entry was 2000lkr per person which seems slightly on the expensive side. The cave temples were nice and well maintained however there was little to read in English so without a guide its hard to understand what youre looking at I.e the history behind it. 

Worth a visit if nearby and have time.

Title: Just stunning - a must go to place!
Text: We didn't know what to expect and certainly didn't expect the amount of stone steps we had to climb, but it was so worth it when we got to the top.  There are a series of 5 Buddhist temples in the hillside caves.  Start with the oldest, several hundred years old up to the last one which was created in the 1950's.  It's interesting to see what changes and what stays the same.  The amount of statues is amazing.  Our guide told us about the contents and wall paintings of the various caves and this made it more interesting, as there are very few captions.  Well worth a visit if you are visiting the area.

Title: Beautiful Buddhist Temple
Text: Lots of steps to visit the temple, but well worth the effort, beautiful temple with lots to see, would highly recommend

Title: Worth a Visit
Text: The caves are an interesting stop, however very busy and a steep climb. It is also quite expensive. There are other temples in the area that are less touristy.

Title: Inspiration
Text: One of my favourite temples. A long climb up the stairs in extreme heat but worth every minute. Take a tour with an expert if you can to get an explanation of the Buddhas as well as the designs of the temples

Title: Stunning
Text: Well worth a visit, stunning. Not that many steps and quite easy. Temples are full of amazing statutes some carved out of the rock.

Title: 2000 years old amazing condition
Text: It is quite a hike up to the caves but worth it for the views and then the caves themselves. A guide will take you around for a few $'s and its worth it to hear and see the history. You will need to be covered so no shorts but they will lend you a sarong. Incredibly amazing condition for how old they are.

Title: Not caves. Average at best
Text: These are overpriced $35 a person five buildings built under an overhang falsely called a cave.  Absolutely buy your ticket at the bottom of the hill as they are not sold on top.   These are old. Much better caves in India and other places in Asia.  Good for an hour and go enjoy rather than watch TV

Title: Interesting temple cave
Text:
Steep walk up to caves. Be aware that the place to purchase tickets is not at the entrance to the caves. Make sure you know where the ticket sales are. On the day we were there an older couple who had struggled to walk up the hill were turned away because they had anticipated that the logical place to buy the ticket was at the entrance.
The caves themselves are very beautiful and well cared for. Make sure you go into every cave.
You will also need to make sure that you are dressed appropriately.

Title: Whatever you do in SriLanka dont miss this!
Text:
The caves at Dambulla blew us away!
We very nearly missed them as we didnt wish to stay in Dambulla. However we figured we would give it a try and see what might happen. Well it seems like we arent the only back packers not wishing to spend a night there and a couple of guys have caught on to the trend and have made themselves a great little business. 
It goes like this:
You get off the bus in Dambulla, catch a tuk tuk to the  caves where you find a really nice helpful guy willing to look after your back pack in his shed for free!
Well we believed him as did a number of others
Off we went up the stairs without the additional weight of our back packs, all 320...
It was truly one of the best sights in SriLanka!
On our return we picked up our bags, a donation was suggested, some paid some didnt.
However these guys knew we didnt plan to stay so this is when the real business kicked in, bartering a price for a tuk tuk to our next destination.
We went onwards to Sigiriya others to Kandy 
The price agreed in was fair and all in all it worked out perfectly 
So pleased we made the effort and tried our luck

Title: Beautiful
Text: The walk to the cave temple is steep. Once you reach the temple, the views are gorgeous. A superb combo of human skill and natural (stone) beauty, the cave temples with the paintings and many statues of Lord Buddha, leave you spellbound.

Title: Sacred temple
Text: Very well kept temple and just cost us 8 USD per person, you have to be dressed well before you enter the temple and remove the shoes, people who dont like to walk on bare foot, sock are allowed. Its worth to visit ??

Title: Best temple on Sri Lanka
Text: This was the best temple on our 21day Sri Lanka roundtrip. Very historical and beautiful statues and paintings on the wall. Must do!

Title: Excellent
Text: Really enjoyed it here. The carvings are beautiful and so intricate. You must have your legs and shoulders covered here and take your shoes off. It is 25 rupees per pair. Lots of monkeys roaming free and lots of steps up to the caves. You are able to take photos if you wish. Very nice views and each cave offers something a little different. Would recommend.

Title: Amazing cave temple
Text: Quite a climb of many steps for me but it is an amazing example of religious devotion. The cave paintings are so intricate and beautiful. We were there late morning so it was difficult to walk on the hot stones. But the cave temple and the views were worth the difficulty. It is a place of contemplation. Photos are allowed but one has to follow the instructions.

Title: Interesting Temple
Text:
ThTemple is located in Dambula. Entrance fee is LKR1500. 
You have to climb around 300 steps to get to the temple. This consists of several caves with statues of Buddha and some wall paintings.
Quite an interesting visit.

Title: Historic Cave Temple !!
Text:
Entry fee is 1500 LKR per person. You have to walk uphill for about 10-15 minutes before you reach the temple entrance. 

The views are good from the top. Cloudy weather made our climb easier else, you would have to wear socks inside the temple as the floor can get hot. 

Make sure that clothing is suitable since it is a religious place and has a dress code. Ankle and shoulders must be covered.

The temple is nice with close to 150 statues of Buddha in different rooms. The place is clean and tidy.

One can spend close to 30-45 minutes at this place and have a peaceful time.

Title: Ancient cave temple so calm, serene and beautiful
Text:
Dambulla cave temple Alsop known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site (1991) in Sri Lanka, situated in the central part of the country. 

Dambulla is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The rock towers 160 m over the surrounding plains. There are more than 80 documented caves in the surrounding area. Major attractions are spread over five caves, which contain statues and paintings. These paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses. The latter include Vishnu and the Ganesha. The murals cover an area of 2,100 square metres (23,000 sq ft). Depictions on the walls of the caves include the temptation by the demon Mara, and Buddha's first sermon.

The Dambulla cave monastery is still functional and remains the best-preserved ancient edifice in Sri Lanka.

Source #Wikipedia

It is a must visit as the statues and paintings are such a delight to the eye.  The serenity of the place is something not to be missed. It's not a tough climb and can be completed in about 15 mins up and down. We were blessed with light showers which made the climb bit risky, it was indeed worth the effort.

Title: The best cave trample on earth with misty
Text:
Over 2000 years history
Many beautiful frescoes and status 
The mysterious large pot to collect water dripping from the top 365 days but never overflows or get dry

Title: Decent visit
Text: We walked up from the ticket office at the back which is a relatively steep 300 step climb. The caves them selves where really good to look at and bear about, however wear socks as you must remove your shoes and ensure your knees are covered to enter. Without socks the hot floor can be a real pain. Finally take a little cash, 25 rupees for safe keeping of your shoes. (About 12p). Overall an interesting hour, however not spectacular

Title: IMPRESSIVE CAVES
Text:
After seeing so many Buddhas, our interest was slightly on the wane.  The caves are not particularly deep - I was really expecting some kind of grotto.  There were various Buddhas of all shapes and sizes around the room and a patterned ceiling, a bit dark for real appreciation.  The visit concluded with a giant golden Buddha, must have been 50 feet tall - rather bling.
PLEASE NOTE YOU MUST WEAR TROUSERS, OTHERWISE YOU'LL GET DRAWN INTO ANOTHER CON - YOU WILL HAVE TO PAY FOR YOUR SHOES TO BE LOOKED AFTER!

Title: Interesting- but not a must see
Text: To infer the temple foreigners must pay 1500 LKR per person. The ticket office is a bit hard to find if you start your visit from the main entrance. Inside the caves there are plenty of statues and paintings which are very nice. But at least for us it was not so impressive as we have hoped for

Title: Impressive
Text: It is a great opportunity to learn about some of the culture of Sri Lanka and to see the many Buddhas that are hundreds of years old. It is a fairly challenging climb up steps to reach the cave, but its worth it. You have to take off your shoes when you get to the top as well as be wearing something past your knees, so maybe take a pair of socks to protect your feet from the scorching hot floor and a sarong to wrap around your waste to cover up. Definitely worth a visit.

Title: Worth visiting Dambulla Cave Temple
Text: Dambulla Cave Temple is worth visiting place. Its a world heritage site. You get to see paintings related to Gautam Buddha & his life on the ceiling of caves.  From top, you also get a superb view of Dambulla Town.

Title: Just amazing!
Text: Go here early to avoid the crowds and the heat. It's a bit of a climb to the Temple but it is worth it for the amazing paintings.

Title: A fascinating temple complex to visit
Text: Like all sites in Sri Lanka, it's either going to be hot or very hot so just be prepared.  The complex is up some stairs but our guide took us to an entry that did not appear to be too strenuous a climb to the caves itself.  Having a guide makes all the difference to help through interpretation, tipping re footwear, just general things.  The temples are obvioulsy very popular with tourists so be prepared for the heat and crowds.  Don't feed the monkeys no matter if there are people selling food for them.

Title: Fascinating and oh, so beautiful!
Text: A must see.  A fairly good hike up stairs to the caves in the mountain top.  The temples are just breathtaking.  Start with the Temple at the far end, and work back, saving the best for last.  We visited on a VERY hot day and the stone plaza and walk ways were burning hot.  Have socks available to wear and save damage to your feet.  Temple guides are available for a fee, if desired, but will take "no" for an answer if you don't need the help.  Very happy we saw this while in Sri Lanka.

Title: Interesting visit
Text: We made a short visit to this cave temple on way to Sigiriya. It was historic and magnificent and is still used as place of worship. Entrance fee for adult is LKR1,500/- each.
