As it was a religious public holiday, we saw many worshippers too and walked up to the temple with one family who showed us the way. I tried to walk barefoot with them but was too much for me. They told me it was okay to wear my shoes up and took it off before entering the temple. We left our shoes at the shoes counter for LKR25/- a pair, no tickets are issued for this but the man with fuzzy hair assured us not to worry as he would remember whose shoes they belong to.  Alternatively, you can leave your shoes in the open at your own risk.  There are many Buddha statues in the various caves, a bit dark inside the caves but interesting sights to see how this worship place for many centuries are within the caves.

Title: Interesting temples, beautiful and peaceful
Text:
A short hike up the hill, the Dambulla cave temples are a really great place to be. As it is a working temple, you need to be covered shoulders and below the knees, and take off your shoes when you get there, but this is normal practice around Sri Lanka. 

The 5 temples are cut into the side of the rock - put there by different kings across time, to show their devotion to Buddhism. Do beware of the "guides" that will talk you through the first cave and then offer to take you around the others in return for payment - you can just say no and they will leave you alone.

They are beautiful, the detail and differences between them is amazing. There is also a bag drop in the Buddhist book centre at the bottom of the hill so if you come with travelling backpacks you can leave them there!

Title: Interesting rock temple
Text: An impressive Buddhist temple in caves on top of a high hill, accessible by a long steep staircase. Worth a visit.

Title: Amazing experience
Text: It is a 30 minute climb from parking lot. It is recommended to do it when it is not too hot. Also visitors are required to cover knees and sleeveless tops are not allowed. It is ok to put a temporary cloth to cover up to get inside and it can be rented from the ticket counter person at the top of the hill for a small fee. It is very peaceful and nice experience to see so many statues inside the caves.

Title: Below expectations
Text: Pictures are no longer a trusted source. This temple was not as beautiful as expected. There's a long and steep walk, hence it's quite important to wear the right shoes. Women must cover their legs and arms. A simple wrap around will do the work. There are 5 temples once you're on top. The pond with lotus growing in them is quite pretty. But it's a very average place.

Title: Worth the climb
Text: Very interesting site. As a temple dress restrictions apply No shoes but socks are worthwhile. Our guide gave us a detailed explanation which certainly helped with an understanding of this very old site

Title: We passed by en route to Kandy but would return
Text: Sadly didnt have enough time to spend at this destination. But would gladly put it on the list for our next visit to Sri Lanka.

Title: Go first thing in the morning.
Text:
To get to the temple you have to take a tuk tuk from Dambulla, expect to pay around 250-300 LKR. Bargain if they ask for more. 
Get your tickets at the office before you start climbing up stairs or you'll have to go back down and you really don't want that. 
The stairs are not too steep but it's being the hottest April in Sri Lanka in 140 years... So if you're planning on going April-May 2019 make sure you take enough water. There's a juice bar near the entrance and after that NOTHING, so again, bring plenty of water and a hat. Socks are recommended cause the floor gets very hot and you have to lose your shoes. 
The caves are nice, totally worth going, specially if you come from another culture where you never get to see budist temples. If you want to see the Buddha of the Golden Temple, go down the stairs right next to the shoe keeper.

Title: Incredible place.
Text: Absolutely stunning visit. Our driver/guide talked us through the story of the temple, explained the paintings and ceremonies. A place not to miss.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Certainly worth a visit when visiting the region and can be easily included as part of a visit to Sigiriya etc. The frescos and Buddha shrines are located in the series of caves and are can be seen quite well from the lighting supplied. Flash photography is not condoned so taking pictures can be a challenge. You will have to remove your shoes and have clothes that cover your legs and shoulders.

Title: Pretty Amazing
Text: The cave temple was an amazing stop on our trip. The temples are impressive and fascinating. I would recommend wearing socks because you need to remove your shoes. It just makes walking over the hot stones more comfortable.

Title: Ok,not that impressed
Text: For a start this is a rock ledge ,not a cave.It is a long walk up and as it was lunchtime it was really hot and you must have armpits and knees covered.Maybe I've seen better buddhist sites in thailand and nepal but I was not that amazed.

Title: Suitable for the fit
Text: A path upwards of some 250 steps is the way to this site. Hot walk! Site is crowded and interesting once there.

Title: Very interesting, important site
Text: This site contains over 100 buddha statues located in a series of shallow caves.  Access is via a flight of over 100 steps (or the adjacent service road).  They are stunning and magnificent.  Mind, we did witness how this has been achieved - they are repainted.  If you are able, a must see site.  But do try to visit when it is cooler and quieter

Title: Another really important historic site
Text: I got a guide who explained each of the caves and as i had visited some other sites the history had made sense. You see the progression in the artwork of the statues of the Buddha.

Title: Unique tribute to Buddha.
Text: The climb up could be a challenge for some - My count was 393 uneven stone steps up. Aim for the cooler part of the day and take water. A couple of t shirt sellers along the way, but no hard sell. The view is lovely. As per usual no shoes inside. Just leave outside or pay a small amount to store them. Inside you'll see dozens of ancient Buddha statues(up to 45') and  ancient murals. Quite impressive.

Title: Stunning and Ramshackle
Text: At times, especially on the climb to the top, this site is ramshackle and dilapidated.  Cons and grifters line the route.  Need a ticket?  Go back down to the gate, avoid the snake-charmer, pay to ride a tuk tuk to the ticket office, then ride back.  At the top, every stop "holy men" panhandle for "donations".  That being said, once inside the actual caves, they are absolutely amazing.  The plaster painted walls look like draped tapestries wrapped over the rocks.  Beautiful attention to detail hides among the penny-pinching hustling.

Title: Hot, hot, hot!
Text:
A hand held fan salesman would make a fortune here. 

To reach the temple, you must climb many steps and if you came at midday I imagine this would be very difficult! 

That said, the Cave Temples were fascinating and worth the walk. There are 5 caves to visit, however restoration work was being carried out on one during our visit so we couldn't see it.

Title: Wear comfy Trainers
Text: You have to climb many steps and steep inclines to reach the temples but they are well worth it. To see the numerous Buddhas, so different and so colourful is breathtaking and to see how they have cut into the rocks to form the temples is truly mind blowing. Deffo worth a day out.

Title: Bring socks!
Text:
It's a bit of a hike - about 200 steps - to get to the top, but it's worth it. The statues are incredibly colorful and well-preserved. The five caves differ in size and in the number of Buddhas, but they all have something special to offer.

Don't miss the Dambulla Cave Temple!

One bit of advice - take an extra pair of socks. As with any temple, you'll have to take your shoes off before entering, but the ground and the walkways between the caves can get VERY HOT, so bring a pair of socks to slip on. Also, go early in the day to avoid the crowds and the heat.

Title: Dont miss it
Text:
Small but filled with spirituality. Incredibly well preserved statues and incredible different techniques. Some of the statues are made from a single rock, some assembled right inside, some of wood hundreds and thousands of years ago. Very important to have a guide, its not worth it without one. You will not understand anything. Every posture of Buda means something else and you need someone to tell you about this. 
Its cheap, quiet and chill.

Title: climbing high
Text: you have to climb many steps to reach the temple to see the many faces of the Buddha, but it is worth it, remember to buy your tickets downstairs, as they do not sell tickets at the entrance

Title: Worth the 200 steps to get there
Text: There are 5 caves, each with paintings and statues of the Buddha, but to get there you have to climb a lot of uneven steps. They are worth the trek but as with all the tourist sites we have visited so far, they are heaving with tourists.

Title: Crazy busy
Text: As with all the temples in Sri Lanka they are beautiful and the history is breathtaking - go early as if you leave it too late you are with the hordes of tourists buses!  Also wear trainer socks as you have to leave your shoes outside and the ground gets really hot!

Title: Stunning group of temples
Text: This was one of the best things in Sri Lanka. On top of a hill (a bit of a climb), there are five temples within caves, some dating back over a thousand years. There are many elaborate statues of the Buddha and artefacts alongside. A really beautiful sight with gardens alongside and a lovely walk down to the new temple

Title: How many Buddhas can one cave hold?!!
Text: The answer is a lot. Kids liked it and so did we. Just remember to dress appropriately (cover shoulders, long pants). And no, we dont feel a guide was necessary for this place.

Title: Beautiful Buddhas
Text: It's a relatively short hike up to the cave temple but it was very hot when we visited at midday but there is some shade with trees overhanging the path and lots of monkeys. At the top, the ground is very hot when you take off your shoes. But the caves are relatively cool and the Buddha statues are glorious.

Title: Lovely temple cave complex
Text:
Despite a bit of a walk up steps (about 500 - so nothing on the rock!) the ascent wasnt that arduous! 

You had to take your shoes off to go into the temple complex but they could be stored for a few rupees outside.

The complex was very interesting and the carvings and paintings were very spectacular and amazingly beautiful especially as they were sold old. We enjoyed seeing them all and also the lovely views out of the temples.

We spent about 1 and 1/2 hours there and definitely recommend as I have not really seen anything like it.

User_Location: San Rafael de Escazu, Costa Rica
Title: Interesting
Text:
Though climb
Not cheap
Special temple curved in the mountain caves .
 Need  to cover  the ladies for it is a holy place
Take cold water with you
Beautiful view from the top. 
If you want to hear legends about the place
There are tour guides at the ticket office

Title: A must-see in Sri Lanka
Text: We went to see the cave temple with a Buddhist guide from Sri Holidays, which we highly recommend doing (if you can, ask for Indika). We learned a lot about the religion and enjoyed the beautiful statues, traditional offers and paintings for Buddha. It was a very humbling experience.

Title: Very pretty but not much to do other than view the buddhas
Text:
Very beautiful and interesting place. Bit of a hike to get to (especially after climbing Sigiriya earlier the same day!), and slightly annoying that they make you remove your shoes then charge you to look after them...
However well worth a visit. Remember to cover legs and shoulders (that includes the men). 
Try to stand up to the monkeys- I got mugged for my mango but apparently if you just shout at them they leave you alone!

Title: Must visit
Text: Make sure you have a guide with you before you go in. The place is well worth a visit, very interesting to learn about the history of the temple and see all the Buddha statues.

Title: Very interesting tour
Text: Well worth a visit; make sure you employ one of the guides hanging round the temple as youll get far more out of it if you do. We only paid our guide around LKR 700 and it was worth it. The history was very interesting; we enjoyed it, tho our 13 year old got a bit bored. There are lots of monkeys around, be careful of your things as they will come and grab stuff!

Title: Different to the usual temples
Text:
Having visited many Asian countries, we thought we were "Templed Out".  However, these are just a little different, being literally in caves. Lots of paintings, statues etc.

Worth the climb to see something just a little different to the normal temples.

probably not worth going miles out of your way to see, but if you are travelling to Kany from Dambulla or vice versa, definitely worth the effort.

Check out the dress requirements - knees and arms to be covered.

Title: Amazing caves!!
Text: Very impressive caves with some amazing and very ancient buddha statues. Totally worth the small climb up the hill.

Title: Méh
Text: It is fairly expensive and honestly not all that impressive. It's probably pretty good if you haven't seen any other temples. But to us it was just ok.

Title: Very interesting
Text: Enjoyed our visit which was both enlightening and interesting. Did not encounter large crowds which was pleasant change from other temple visits in Sri Lanka. Access was easy and our outing was worthwhile.

Title: Fascinating frescos
Text:
A Buddhist temple built into the rock in which there are 160 statues of Buddha and some extraordinary frescos on the walls and ceilings.  
Cautions - access by stairs and dress appropriately.

Title: Mystical
Text:
The Dambulla Cave Temple, famous for its ancient mural paintings depicting the life and work of Buddha, is a significant site for cultural and history of Sri Lanka.

There are five caves housing statuses of Buddha from different time ranging from 1 century BC to some 200 years ago. It's advisable to get some background of it or hire a guide (in white clothes) from the temple to walk you through. There are so much subtleties on display - for examples, the different postures of Buddha, the material used at different era and the reasons.

There are 2 ways of reaching the temple - one from the Golden Temple from town, and the other one from an open car park. The latter one is shorter but the view is breath taking.

Title: A Steep Climb That's Worth It!
Text: We did Sigaria in the morning and followed that up with Dambulla in the afternoon - about 15,000 steps! Well worth it. Visit this temple if you are interested in Sri Lankan history, religious history, art, or just want to see something you'd never see anywhere else! These caves are amazing and you will be taken by the beautiful painted colours used in the caves. After a steep climb up (which is all you will be focused on while climbing!) you will be rewarded with the most amazing visual experience. You will make the most of your time if you hire a guide (incredibly cheap - tip well!) and have the history explained to you. Ensure you dress appropriately for a temple visit. It's worth buying a pair of 'elephant pants' to cover up those legs if necessary!!

Title: Beautiful
Text: Our hotel hired a local guide who turned out to be the curator.  He made the trip worthwhile because he gave us so much info.  If you don't hire a guide you won't know what you're looking at so I would suggest it.  Men and women must cover shoulders and knees, so bring pants or shawls.  This is enforced.  You also take your shoes off.  Also do not take a photo with your back to Buddha.  You will be yelled at if you do, and no one wants that embarassment or to disrespect.

Title: Don't miss it !!
Text: It's a must when travelling from Habarana to Kandy or the opposite ...The scenery around the Temple is attractive.... The frescoes and the sculptures are brilliant,... Still  t's no art but profund devotion ! We enjoyed there a great moment of spirituality.

Title: Amazing
Text: If you are OK with the high number of steps, and warm, inside you are for a treat. This collection of 5 caves with their internal paintings has been carved in the rock. It is very busy and photography is not easy. But it is definately worth visiting

Title: Vacation
Text: What a great treat this was. About three hundred steps you reach this amazing five cave Temple complex. The statues and ceiling art are beautiful. A very much must see. Its very hot so bring plenty of water and an extra pair of socks for walking the grounds. Long pants and sleeved shirts are required. Absolutely stunning.

Title: Fascinating
Text: An impressive collection of statues. We really enjoyed this visit. Very atmospheric rooms carved into the side of the mountain full of beautiful buddhas.

Title: A MUST TO VISIT IF YOU IN DAMBULLA
Text:
Dambulla cave temple also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site in Sri Lanka. The largest and best-preserved cave temple complex major attractions are spread over five caves, which contain statues and paintings. These paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses. The latter include Vishnu and the Ganesha. The murals cover an area of 2,100 square metres. Depictions on the walls of the caves include the temptation by the demon Mara, and Buddha's first sermon.

Entrance Cost: 1500Rs
Shoes Deposit: 25Rs

Title: Awe inspiring but strenuous!
Text: but be warned -360 stairs to reach the caves - but totally worth it and there are losts of resting places

Title: Beautiful place!
Text: We visited here mid morning when the temperature was a little cooler. A 300+ step climb to the top but well worth it, we felt. The caves are impressive, as are the carvings, and the atmosphere is very tranquil despite the number of visitors. Some great views from the top too!

Title: Amazing!
Text: Definitely a must to see.  Nice to be out of the heat and in the caves, but still it is very humid.  You need to be respectful and hat and shoes are taken off.  Make sure and check out the ceilings as well.

Title: Very expensive...
Text:
We visited the temple because our private driver recommended it to us. You have to buy the ticket for 1500 rupees and walk up the stairs. On top there is someone you have to pay to watch your shoes and if you dont wear long pants or a long skirt they won't let you in. There is someone waiting for those people to borrow a sheet to cover your knees, but afterwards he wants 100 rupees...
The temple is not that spectacular...

Title: A bit of a hidden gem
Text: We visited these temples in the afternoon and started the 300 or so step climb up the King's way about 4:30pm. It was a bit of an effort because of the heat and the unevenness of the steps. A couple of stops on the way up to observe the monkeys and take in the views helped. The whole area around the temples was intriguing and scenic - after all its not every day you see such intricate paintings  set in such an environment. You can take photos but not with flash so phone cameras do quite well here. We decended on the opposite side of the rock which takes you into the Golden Temple that houses the giant budda. We were also able to view Lion rock in the distance and teh nable to do this in reverse the following day at Sirigiya. Worth a short visit as it is unusual.

Title: Stunning
Text: Wow !! This is an breathtaking site. We truly were awed by what we. Its easy to spend a lot if time here. Bring a flashlight as it will help you see in some of the darker portions. Dont miss it !

Title: Overrated for the climb
Text: I climbed up the 364 steps and found that there is actually another way up slope without having to climb so many steps. When I reached the top, it was drizzling and the guard was very kind to allow me to sit down to rest in one of their chairs and even offered me some water as I am totally exhausted and feeling giddy/ after the climb. Remember to bring a bag to keep your shoes inside your bag or carry it around without having to store with others' shoes.  Many tourists had to use the scarf provided as the guards are pretty strict about covered sholder and over-knee attire. Honestly speaking I find that this place is over-rated after the diffiicult climb.  Been a South-East Asian, I have seen all kinds of temples so there is nothing special for me here except the structure of the building under the rock. Maybe unless one is Buddhist then it may be a must to see Otherwise, I will gladly give it a miss.

Title: Worth the effort
Text:
The steps up to the cave are steep but the distance is short and it's well worth the effort when you get to the top.

I'm not keen on walking bare foot )stubbed my toe) but you have to observe local customs. 

There are over 150 images of the Buddha painted on the walls of the five caves - impressive.

Title: Outstanding
Text: The climb is worthwhile and the 5 caves holing the Buddhas are different but all good in their own way.

Title: Worth a visit
Text: It is just another place of statues and paintings of 1st century BC. However, the paintings and statues were repaired and repainted in 11th, 12th, and 18th century AD. These caves were the place where Buddhist monks were meditating. This rock temple built by King Valagamba in the 1st century BC. Very disappointing to see that there is no proper lighting, cleanliness and guide service at the caves. In spite of collecting entry fees no enough attention is given to the visitors. Serious efforts are required to bring back the glorious past to the caves, statues and the surroundings.

Title: Very interesting, worth the climb!
Text: The temple is situated at the top of a steep hill and several older/less fit struggled to climb it comfortably in the oppressive heat, but once there the paintings/statuary are quite stunning.

Title: Disappointing
Text:
If you have travelled much around South-east Asia you will have seen all of this before, often better and probably for free. Sure, the setting is a novelty with the temples set inside five decorated caves and there are an incredible number of Buddha statues but, fundamentally, there is little to set the place apart. We had anticipated a series of caverns but the caves are actually 5 individual units. Inside each the lighting is subdued and, as a result, the whole atmosphere is gloomy and uninspiring. We have visited many, many temples in the likes of Thailand, Myanmar and Cambodia, generally without charge, and seen some stunning interiors. Sadly this place didnt live up to those standards.
On a practical level, the ticket office is located a considerable distance from the road which makes for a significant walk (for those arriving independently) before you even begin the climb up the hill. Enter at the Golden Temple, follow the sign for the Cave Temple and just keep going until, eventually, you get to the ticket office. At 1500 rupees we felt the entry charge was way too much for what is on offer. Also, remember to take a sarong or else you will have to hire one there at additional charge (including men if youre wearing shorts).

Title: Overrated
Text: Interesting Temple. It is quite different from the other that we have seen but to be honest the ticket price for foreigners is too expensive for a 20 minutes attraction. However, it remained as a good memory in our minds. They should do something with the touts inside who are pushy and try to give you different explanations in exchange of some money.

Title: Very interesting visit...
Text: You will need to take a bottle of water with you and it's a 700 step climb to the top, which in humidity of 80% is a bit tiring.  We enjoyed the visit and a guide showed us around.  The colours of the paintings are incredible - they look like they were done yesterday and are 1300 years or more old..  a must visit .

Title: Incredible place
Text: Went as a group of friends. A long walk from where we got dropped off as our bus was too big. Uphill walk and some of us struggled a bit but we eventually reached the top. Amazing architectural structure: beautiful views from the top. The Raavanan Vettu was worth a look too. Enjoyed the visit very much - even those belonging to other faiths.

Title: The Romance of Ravanna
Text: A beautiful Kovil with deer and peacocks in the grounds. Beautiful shrines and a lot of history.  Our 6 year old kids loved it !

Title: Trincomalee Land Mark
Text: The Koneswaram temple is one of the main highlights of the east coast of Sri Lanka in Trincomalee. The temple is located high above the bay, and you can view the breathtaking and awe-inspiring scenery on all sides. The site is a religious pilgrimage for the Hindus and is also known as the Kailasa of the South. The Koneswaram temple is one of the five Pancha Ishwarams (abodes of Shiva) which has been built to worship Lord Shiva- the supreme God of Hinduism.

Title: Beautiful temple with a great view.
Text: Located in one of the most beautiful locations in Sri Lanka, it is a must visit for the travelers. A religiously important place as well

Title: A must visit temple, unique
Text: A temple that must be visited. Stunning view of the Indian Ocean from the temple hill rock. A unique view and location, which no temple even in India offers

Title: Always a must visit when I go Trinco
Text: A must thing to in Trinco & amazing view always make me visit. The whole area surrounded by water & green, the temple history portrait nicely on the walls. Highly recommend for nature lover & first time visitors.

Title: Temple with a View
Text:
Unfortunately, due to COVID, the Fort overall was very empty and most of the temple was closed to us. 
Otherwise, this was a very lovely temple to visit. The statues were amazing to look at as well as the architecture of the temple itself.

Title: Colourful place
Text: Very colourful place high on a cliff top. You have to leave your shoes at a booth before you can proceed to the temple. Knees to be covered sarongs available at the door if required. Should have worn socks as the ground was so hot a bit uncomfortable to say the least. Plenty of stalls along the way.

Title: Thirukkoneswaram Kovil
Text: An ancient temple to the Hindu god Shiva surrounded by jaw-dropping scenery.  Golden statue of Shiva in front of partially restored Koneswaram temple with colourful design, shoes not allowed..

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: A must see temple in Trincomalee with such a beautiful view. This temple holds a lot of history and is situated right by the water and looks out to the mountain. There are many street vendors and a cafe along the way if you want to grab a quick bite and buy souvenirs.

Title: Very colourful also very busy
Text: It was the weekend when I visited and also a festival, people friendly. I was the only westerner on this occasion. I think more tourists visit at other times

Title: Lovely Temple
Text:
The Temple is situated on top of a hill, not far from the entrance to Trincomalee Harbour. The statue is spectacular and the interior of the Temple looks interesting.
There are shops at the entrance to the Temple.

Title: prachige tempel op top locatie
Text: temple in Fort Frederic. Fischerboats first pass the temple in the sea below before going on long fishing trips.

Title: A sacred temple with a view
Text: There is something exhilarating about standing on the top of a rock and taking in a magnificent view. From this temple, which is as close to God as anyone can get here in Trincomalee, the views over the Indian Ocean are sublime. There are small shrines built into the cliff and it is lovely to stand with Hindu devotees as they perform their rituals. The temple, the people, and the wonderful view make this place a worthy place to visit. On our way down the hill, after collecting our shoes, we sat in a coconut cafe, high above the cliff, sipping coconut water whilst immersing ourselves with this unforgettable cultural experience.

Title: Cultural Experience
Text: I loved going to the temples because it helped broaden my perspective on different cultures and religions as well as my own. You have to go barefoot for a large portion of this temple which was fine for me and my wife but not everyone will be comfortable with it.

Title: ravana's folly
Text:
Ravan wanted to cut off the temple from the mountain it was on to let his mother, who was ill, have darshan. As he was cutting it away he got news of her demise.and rushed back.there is a huge cleft between the rocks which is called Ravana's cut,
There is a lovely viewing gallery for looking out at the sea.
the temple itself is relatively new as it had been destroyed by the Dutch in 1614 and was later reconstructed but a real worth it visit.

Title: The sea view is amazing
Text:
The temple is built on a cliff.  At the parking lot, we saw a couple of deer.  Then we walked through a small market place and come to the area where you have to take of the footwear and pay a fee to store them.  We walked on the concrete path which was very hot in that weather.  That hurt my feet and it is the part I dislike about the visit.

The building and the statues are well maintained.  The ground inside and outside the temple is quite clean.  We also witnessed coconut sacrifice outside the temple.  There is a small path you can walk down the cliff and see the amazing view of the ocean.  There are also a few wildlife peacocks on the cliff.

On the way back to the parking lot, we walked through the little market again,  We bought some Sri Lankan snacks and nic nac.

You have to wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees.

Title: Hindu temple
Text:
Only acces with long trouses or rent skirt. No shoes allowed.
Lots of shops before entering.
You may see dear, monkeys on the way.

Title: Worth a visit
Text:
Very beautiful maintained tempel that's definatly worth a visit when you're in trincomalee.

Keep in mind you need to cover your knees and shoulders

Title: Great location
Text: We had visited great place located in trincomalee. At the time little bit rain we are enjoyed and really happy my kids for great place.

Title: Hindu
Text: This is an old Hindu temple here. The view from here is amazing. This is in the Fort Frederick army  camp.

Title: Divine Experience with Serene Nature
Text: One of the oldest temple dates back to BC 200 approximately. Kondeswaran temple is dedicated to Hindu god Shiva. The temple is located on Hill top in thirukonamalai ( Trincomalee). The temple is accessible by vehicle upto the top. The scene atop of the hill is breath taking.

Title: Important Hindu temple
Text: One of the most important Hindu temples on the East Coast of Sri Lanka; it's usually very busy and so it's worth observing the religious practice of the visitors. Taking photos inside is forbidden, except if you are so lucky as to witness a Hindu wedding there (as we were :) )

Title: Must see place
Text:
This is another must see place with religious and historic value. It also has a great surrounding of the gorgeous sea.

People be dressed modestly . Must wear cloth below the knee.

Avoid visiting during the afternoon because has direct sun light .suitable for morning or evening

Title: Iconic Eezham Temple
Text: This temple is one of the two Shiva temple in the Island which got revered by Devaram poets from Tamil Nadu. Other temple is Ketheeswaram temple.

Title: Old hindu temple
Text: Very old and holy temple. Don't try to take photos inside temple. Somebody tried to do it and officials were very angry. Outside temple its ok to take photos!!

Title: Spectaular Location
Text:
Another  very colourful temple, but in a spectacular location, and so colourful and bright.  Worth the visit for the views and lovers leap.

Few stalls on the way up that have some interesting local food.

Title: Nothing so special!
Text: It is a Hindu temple but a small one . Found probably manny years ago and seems to be a temple for blessing to have more children. A seaside view from the temple that is on the cliff do have a great look of the Indian Ocean ! You prepare to pay and remove your shoes to walk there! Do prepare to wear a modest dress when visiting .

Title: Sri lanka hols
Text: Loved this Hindu temple, so bright with its beautiful paintings and statues. Very movi g and spiritual place with an i teresti g yet sad story of the girl who lost her lover and jumped into the ocean.  Beautiful setting over looking the sea. A must visit

Title: Fantastic location by the sea
Text: It was a nice experience ..... remember to bring socks to wear as the ground can be very hot on barefoot

Title: Koneswaram Kovil
Text: One of the pilgrimage places situated in Trincomalee and having some sort of unique attraction. Unfortunately, we couldn't make the poojawa time but worth to visit other times as well.

Title: Market Entrance with Interesting and Large Temple
Text:
On the walk up to the temple there are a number of wild deer running around. Around the entrance are a number of market stalls selling food, drink and souvenirs. King coconut drinks are cheap if you haggle.

The temple is very vibrant and colourful, and also busy. Women are given extra robes to cover of up if required. Shoes are looked after for 20 rupee.

Temple has great views of the main bay. Would recommend the walk up there.

Title: Welcoming hilltop temple
Text: Our tuktuk driver wanted to show us this place, because he wanted to visit the temple himself. It was really interesting to go with someone who was familiar with and reverent to each part of the temple and surrounds. There is a not to be missed main worship hall that has a awesome ceiling, full of figures, and don't miss the view from the front of rock, with the shines in the rock wall nooks. Everyone was was very happy and friendly. The fact that Buddhist monks were among the mix of demographics visiting a Hindu temple made our visit more rich and interesting. The deer were a bonus.

Title: Very colourful and interesting ..
Text:
A great Hindu temple on the cliffs.

Very colourful and interesting to visit, seeing the locals coming to worship and making oferrings

Title: Temple on the water
Text:
The views of the ocean are beautiful from this temple. 
generally very interesting.  Take the time to read some of the explanations on the walls.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Gorgeous colourful temple situation on a cliff overlooking the ocean, very interesting place to see!

Title: Old Shiva temple . worth a visit
Text:
About 15min drive from Trinco Blu, this is on Fort Fredrick. An old temple , it is worth a visit. Super hot by the day, it is hard to walk barefoot. Main diety is Shiva.

Didn't witness any special puja when we were there. Lovely ocean views from the top. Lot of over priced shops on the way to the temple.

Title: Bit hectic, but overall nice
Text:
If you wanna experience a hindu style of temples and atmosphere there, go ahead, but we came from India, and places like that, are many. Nothing much to see there, i admired the views on the whole coast, enjoyed a cool fresh juice and spotted some deers.
You can find More spiritual place in Kali kovil, centre of Trinco

Title: Beautiful!
Text: We walked up to Koneswaram Temple from Trinco town. The walk was about 2 km through the fort, and is a beautiful walk. The temple itself is gorgeous, parts are under construction but the parts that are open are so worth it! There is also an amazing view from the top that is unbeatable. Highly recommended!

Title: Beautiful views, under renovation at the moment
Text: We walked up from Trinco and enjoyed walking through the army base and seeing all the deer. Small entry fee and remember to cover up. Temple was very colourful with lots of ancient relics. Is currently under construction so some bits were covered up. View of the sea is amazing - whilst there we saw loads of huge jellyfish in the sea! Worth a visit if you want some time away from the beach!

Title: Temple with the great view.
Text: The view around the temple is magnificent. Devotees flock to the temple and performing religious service to the tradition while exploring the legendary story behind the temple. Sacred and calmness shown around the temple by leisurely roaming Spotted Deers. All the ingredients are there for a must visit place in Trincomalee.

Title: Very colorful
Text:
This location is accessed through the fort. You walk for about 1km from the car park to the temple gate. Along the way you see some interesting sites, there are plenty of vendors selling goods, but our highlight was stopping and enjoying freshly squeezed passionfruit juice while overlooking the sea below. 250lkr for a good size glass.
Remove your shoes and cover up, then be prepared for a very colorful exhibit both outside and in.

Title: Peaceful & Spiritual atmosphere!!!!
Text: It was my first visit to koneswaram Temple (Kovil), Peaceful & Spiritual atmosphere!!!! It's one of great heritage & belief full places to visit in Sri Lanka.

Title: Not much to it
Text: We visited the temple after a dolphin watching boat trip (highly recommended) - and although the temple is of historic significance in the local area, there isn't alot to it. We only really spent 20 minutes here - just to put it into perspective?

Title: A special place.
Text:
This is one of my favourite temples Im not Hindu but I alway feel drawn to this place. Ive been 3 times now each time we visit Trincomalee. 
Its beautiful, peaceful and full of history. I always wonder and marvel at how much energy, love, patience and hard work  goes into building these Hindu temples in Sri Lanka. Especially the hand painted shrines that surround the god statues. 

This Temple is built up high on the cliffs and we were told that young lovers that werent allowed to marry would come here and jump off the cliffs so they would be together forever. Its know as Lovers Leap. 

The local people are also very friendly and welcoming but just be warned about the few people mainly ladies that will try and con you outside the temple at the end of the road. They insist on reading your palm for a price then tell you that youre are cursed or put a curse on you and tell you it wil cost you more (a lot more) to remove it! Just downright cheeky!

If you are visiting Tricomalee then this temple is a must.

Title: Temple with Best View
Text: barefoot and silent are required. there is special place at the entrance where you can keep your sandals or shoes with guard. the temple is classical-medieval Hindu dedicated to Lord Shiva, located atop Konesar Malai with wonderful view to the indian ocean, around 2km from town central bus station. many visitors I observed coming here by hiring tuk-tuk. there isnt much information on the spot, so you might need to read written information from other source to know more about this temple. you can combined visiting this temple with Fort Fredrick. the parking area is ontop the old bunker. it is really worth of visit.

Title: Amazing location for this lovely temple
Text:
This place is more than a temple. Build on the kliff it offers several amazing views and hidden spots along the steps curling down the hill.
The Kovil itself is really worth seeing - in mornings around 7-8 am there is a service where you can participate and see prayers. Not many tourists luckily but local people are very inclusive and welcoming...
No photos alowed inside - what a pitty as there are some lovely coulourful 3D fresques. Definitedly worth a visit.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text: Large hindu temple next to Swami Rock with an amazing with of the sea and bay towards Trinco. Interesting place to visit, wild dear are seen many places in the area.

Title: Nice for an afternoon visit
Text: Before you get to the temple you are asked to take off your shoes. It is nice to walk through the temple grounds and take a few photos. Inside the temple, however, you are not allowed to take photos. If you have a few minutes to spare, stop by one of the cafes on the side on the road and enjoy a cold drink and a panoramic view of Trinco. Also, be aware that taxis and tuk-tuks are not allowed too close so you will have to walk a few minutes before getting there.

Title: Shiva Idol Consecrated by Rama
Text:
A must see place. For historic and religious reason. Temple is located atop a hill overlooking the sea. History of over 7000 years behind it.
Downsides are - the temple staff are very rude. Closed the temple 20 minutes early the previous day and we had to revisit next day. No English signs and we could not understand the story behind the statues and idols inside the temple.

Title: Beautiful temple overlooking the ocean.
Text: This is probably the most famous temple on this part of the Island, in Trinco. It has a very nice exterior and is very colourful. It boasts some great views over the ocean, where you can supposedly spot whales from here. Nice place.

Title: Temple with a view
Text: Took a tuk-tuk to this temple, well worth a visit. There are market stalls trying to sell you stuff as you walk up to the temple.  The temple is is good condition and is set on a cliff with lovely views of the sea. We accidentally forgot our longer clothes and thankfully there was some we could borrow (20rupees) to use. The shoe man who minds your shoes cost 20rupees also-just to be aware. But it was lovely and afterwards we stopped at the first stall on the right as youre going back down and got a lovely king coconut and pineapple juice (best Ive had on the trip!) drank them overlooking the ocean and the town of Trincomalee as the sun was starting to set-heaven!

Title: Must see in Trincomalee
Text: Colours and odeurs are amazing. Often an active hindu service is going on. When visiting with young children try to get a ride till the parking at the last walk up to the temple. It is a 10min walk up to the temple and there you can enjoy great cliff sea views.

Title: Koneswaram Temple, Trincomalee, Sri Lanka
Text: This was the temple that caught my eye and I wanted to go to Sri Lanka, Which I did in December 2018. Most amazing experience, beautiful temple and views of the sea was breath-taking

Title: Temple with great view over the Indian Ocean
Text: Located on the top of a rockhill, this temple is worth to visit also for the great view over the Indian Ocean. Unfortunately the Koneswaran statue is still under renovation. One hour visit is enough since the whole area is not very large.

Title: Mythological importance
Text: The sacred temple is abode of Lord Shiva & is also a Shaktipeeth. There is also belief that Ravana mediatated & worshipped Lord Shiva at this place. There is also a Ravana cut rock. Truly amazing place to visit.

Title: A must
Text: As one of the 5 Siva temples in Sri Lanka this is a must to see and experience. Great views out to sea from here as well.

Title: Ramayana places tour
Text: Koneswaram Temple is one must see. It is presumably one of the 5 Shiva lingams  installed by Rama to overcome brahma hatya dosham. It is on the sea shore. SHANKARI Shakti Peeth is in the same temple.

Title: A nice peaceful temple
Text:
A nice clean and peaceful temple surrounded by indian ocean.

Prayers start at 6.30 am and then from 8.30am till 11.30am.

Need to park a distance away and walk up the temple.

There are shops along the way to buy the neccessary prayer items.

You may see deers on the way up to the temple.

Title: Beautiful Temple
Text: This place is definitely worth visiting. There are many beautiful temples. Very colorful and historical. I highly recommend.

Title: WHAT A LOCATION?!
Text: In terms of location,this temple is no1. Located at the top of a rockhill overlooking the Indian Ocean,i think no other temple can match its beauty. Its a very colourful temple with so much history and a lot of detailing. My only regret is was unable to see the giant koneswaram statue as it was under construction. Lots of deers and peacocks enroute the temple. The entrance is via the Fort Frederick...you feel like going back in time. I spent about 2 hours here.

Title: Historically famous location
Text: Great views from the top and a bunch of deer and peacocks were roaming about freely.  It's of great religious importance to Hindu folk as well. Located within an army camp and a lot of history to be discovered here.

Title: Impressive Temple with Pretty Views
Text: This is an impressive temple worth visiting. The inside was beautiful and there were several areas around it to explore as well. Stunning views of the ocean from the path around the rocks. There are many people selling shells, children's plastic toys and sweets along the walk to the temple. You will have to leave your shoes and walk barefoot for a bit. Consider wearing socks if the sun has been heating up the ground.

Title: Wonderful small temple
Text: Very low key Hindu temple. The paintings are excellent and tell the story really well. Very life like. One of the few places you see Ravana and the entire Shiva family together. The priests leave you alone and have no expectation of any money.

Title: Wonderful Temple
Text:
This is such a wonderful temple. We went there during the pooja time and it was extremely good. Ravana's sward cut is a must see, it cannot be described. 
On the way to the temple you will find many deer.

Title: A Dravidian gem.
Text:
The temple is small but colourful to madness and there are representations of unusual deities. 
It's atmosphere is relaxed. There is a service at 11 am.
Also visit the little cave facing the sea. Great picture spot. 
The merchants on the way sell excellent honey based candy by the weight. Take your pick.

Title: Historic place and should visit
Text: It is on the top hill surrendered by ocean. Beautiful location. It is a historic place. Priest did a quick pooja not with a full heart.

Title: Situated in a great location
Text:
The Hindu temple was quite interesting and its location on a rocky cliff above the beautiful blue ocean was truly beautiful.

Our guide explained the temple's connection to the ancient king Ravana and also many of its statues.

Although there was a bit of climbing, it was not difficult to get there.

Glad we visited the place.

Title: Breathtaking
Text: This temple is amazing - the location on the cliffs with a beautiful ocean view; the vibrant colours and the calm, special feel about it. Im not Hindu but I could sense why this place is sacred. No entry fee made a nice change. Really enjoyed spending some time there.

Title: Amazing and Inspiring
Text: The temple was beautiful. Situated in the east of Sri lanka trincomalee and overlooking the Indian Ocean. The temple is filled with cultural significance. It is said that ravana used to pray here to shiva along with his mother and is also said to have brought the lingam from kailash. It has been destroyed once by tsunami, once by the tsunami and is the third construction standing now.

Title: On the hill above Fort Frederick
Text:
Climb the Fort Frederick hill and the temple is at the top.One of the more interesting of the dozens of Hindu Temples that you will visit. It is one of the three principal places of worship dedicated to Shiva.
There are no photos inside but great water views outside.
In the afternoon they have a special ceromony with lots of drums and music.

Title: Interesting temple
Text: Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area. Large statue of Shiva is impressive. Setting is quite extraordinary, perched on a promontory above the sea.

Title: A majestic Temple on a Hill
Text: A majestic Temple on a cliff with breathtaking views of the Indian Ocean. The temple has a significant history where the idol was found buried in the ground and was resurrected to establish the temple. The temple is surrounded by forest and a large population of deer and monkey. A picturesque place to visit.

Title: Holiday
Text:
No regret as all friends told to visit. 
Was there at 4pm and lucky as evening prayers started. Managed to join and have 
good view and blessing.
Top view was good especially the ocean and the rocks.
Picture scenic view from Top and deers freely every where.

Title: Hindu Temple on top of a massive rock.
Text: I've already reviewed this temple as part of my review of Fort Frederick, which you have to pass through to reach the temple.  It's very colourful with lovely paintings and statues showing the destruction by the Portuguese of the original temple built on this site.  There is an enormous Hindu god statue next to the temple, and several small shrines among the rocks nearby.  Anyone is allowed to enter the temple as long as they remove shoes and headgear.  It is one of the most important temples in Sri Lanka, and receives a lot of visitors.

Title: The Magnificent  Temple with a long story - from mythological period to the present
Text:
One of the most ancient temples of South Asia ,dedicated to Lord Shiva, dates back to the period of Rama mythologically,  and to the 6th Century B by historians. Said to have been worshiped by Ravana , ithe temple had one of the Suyambu Lingams as the main deity. During the 17th Century AD ( around 1630 s) the temple was supposed to have been razed to the ground by foreign invaders to build a harbour. The local priests hurriedly burred the important idols of the Gods before leaving the temple , fearing vandalism. And in 1956, in an underwater exploration , the old temple ruins were found, Besides a lot of inscriptions about the temple etc were also discovered . All the bits and pieces dicovered were put together and now a grand temple is there once again for us to worship.
A great work of reconstruction of the temple as well as the history.
The temple is sung about gloriously by the great poet saints. Sambandhar and Arunagirinathar. 
the Pandya Chola and Chera kings of south India  were said to have patronized and visited the temple.The Vilva tree is the Sacred tree of this temple.
In 2013, when the civil works were undertaken for the temple, a beautiful Nandhi idol was discovered and it was found to belong to 11th Centurt AD.
People believe that there many be many more to be excavated.
The temple is also a seat of Sakthi Peetam, where the feet of the Amman were supposed to have been assocoated.

Title: THIRU KONÉ?WARAN KOIL, Trincomalee, Sri Lanka
Text:
The Most Sacred ?r? ??nkar? Dévi Temple (Thiru Koné?waran Koil) complex is located within the sprawling old Portuguese Fort. From the parking lot there is a 10-minutewalk up to the Temple. Among the several foreign visitors we met German, Spanish, Italian, Scottish and Chinese tourists. That shows the popularity of this place. 
Laxmis long-term wish got fulfilled this evening after we were blessed with a very happy and blissful Divine Sight of ?r? ??nkar? Dévi and Her Lord ?r? ?iva in this only ?akti Pee?ha? in Sri Lanka  known locally as Koné?wara ?laya?  ?r? Mah? ?akti Pee?ha? Temple - of the eighteen (the remaining seventeen being located in India) at this MOST SACRED PLACE in Trincomalee. The surrounding views are full of greenery and so beautiful. The blue Indian Ocean appearing on both sides of the Temple Complex presented a lovely spectacle! The Scottish couple took me to be a Guide and said they were not going to pay me anything when I volunteered to explain the story of ?r? M?rka??éya in the complex. However, they were very happy to listen to the Pur??ic legend narrated by me - about Sage M?rka??éya as even the God of Death Yama had to take off his crown and mace and surrender totally before Lord Siva when commanded by Siva to spare the life of His devotee M?rka??éya!  They profusely thanked me after hearing my narration and felt so happy knowing that I was a student at the Imperial College, London, long time ago but  that I was not a Guide! The Scotsman respectfully took off his hat and bowed before Lord ?iva in reverence.    
It was learnt that the Portuguese who were in occupation of Sri Lanka in the 16 Century AD destroyed the original Temple and threw all the magnificent sculptured stone columns down into the sea below. Three bronze statues were lately brought up by divers, found among the columns buried in the sea, one of which has been mounted atop the hill facing the entrance to the renovated Temple.
The Temple opened at 5 OClock in the evening. The Tamil priests first performed the prescribed customary rituals to the Lord. We have then made our own humble offerings to the Presiding Deity ?r? ??nkar? Dévi. We had the Most Divine Sight and blessings of the Holy Lord and His Divine Consort while witnessing in awe all the P?ja Worships done by the Tamil priests in the huge, peaceful and Serene complex.

Title: Strategically Located and Well Maintained Temple!
Text: We visited this famous temple and were impressed with all aspects. The location of the temple on a hill overlooking the sea made for great setting. The priest's prayers were soothing to listen to and we felt the presence of God. The link with Ravana and Ramayan showed the closeness of Sri Lankan culture to Indian culture. All in all, a visit to remember!

Title: A beautul temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Text: We went up to the temple but was not permitted to drive up all the way up the hill to the temple as there was a problem with the historic arch leading up to the temple. There was water leaking from beneath the arch and the authorities were worried that it might collapse. so we walked up the rest of the way which was a few hundred from where we had parked our coach. The temple and it architecture was beautiful and it s location on the hilltop overlooking the bay was beyond description.The view from the temple across the bay was fantastic. We even sighted a peacock in the vicinity of the temple in the bushes surrounding the temple hill side.We spent about twenty minutes in the temple and having prayed left and walked back. As you cant wear your shoes into the temple, there is a small stall on the left hand side as you near the temple where you can leave your shoes for a small token sum. All of you in the group can put your shoes/ sandals or slippers in one compartment. A number of the closet holding your shoes will be given to you to collect them on your return. the temple is worth a visit as it is of historical interest.

Title: Great temple at an excellent location
Text:
This location is at the tip of the land at a high point and as such offers great views.

It has a rich Hindu legend and so my parents were keen to visit it. You need to reach the naval base and from there, the only way up is a tuk-tuk (auto-rickshaw in Indian). Very elaborate art on the walls depicting a lot of history. 

We also bought some local sweet-meats on our way back and they were delicious!

Title: Ancient Shiva temple in Trincomalee
Text:
We reached the temple in the morning and had a good darshan. This temple is close to the shore. You will be able to see the sea from the top of the temple. 
The temple follows rituals as in Tamil Nadu. Once you enter the temple, you have the presiding deity of  lord shiva. 
You can easily spend 30 to 45 minutes in this temple. This is MUST visit temple in Sri Lanka.

Title: Breathtaking !
Text:
This is a beautiful temple , breathtaking and enormous.  
We had a lovely trip from Uppuvelie in a three wheeler.  On the way we stoped to see

Title: Beautiful Temple
Text: It was a beautiful temple located on top on the hill overlooking the indian ocean. We bought pooja tray from one of the stalls for reasonable price to experience the rituals and must say it was simple and tourist friendly. The priest was helpful and friendly, The pooja started on time and it was simple and short pooja. Thank you temple management for giving us this beautiful experience.

Title: Cultural requirement
Text: If you are into temples then worth a look because its built on the hill and the scenery is worth the trip ,you will have to go through the local market place to get their, as usual the markets are full of local produce all very snuggery so be aware you diabetics , and pick the stall that has a cover over the food because the place can be full of flies , do keep your hand bags secured or the monkeys will have a field day pulling things out that you do not want anyone to see. I am not into pagan worship mind you we do have a lot of pagans ruling our world at present.

Title: A nice Hindu temple
Text: This would be one o the things to do ar Trincomale apart from enjoying the beach. The temple is up a hill and quite a walk from the bus station so preferably take a tuk-tuk uphill. The temple is nothing great but does give you great views of Trinco. There are any small shops lining the temple. On your way back walk downhill which is pretty pleasant and worth the effort.

Title: Visit if your are in Trincomalee
Text:
I went there with lot of expectations after reading the reviews, especially of the views from the top, since this temple is located up a small hill. Tuk Tuk will charge your 150 LKR from the bus stand. Fredrick. I reached there only by 6 p.m. Hence did not look at the fort and went up the hill to the temple. You will have to walk the last 50 yards to the temple. There is a place where you can leave your footwear. The views of the sea and other places is good but you do not get a direct unhindered view. There is no view point as such. You will have to see through fences or over the walls or through the trees. Neither do you have a place to sit  so that you can sit and enjoy the views. 
The temple is one of the five ishwaram temple in Sri Lanka for Lord Shiva. The temple complex is small. You can spend maximum 30 minutes here.

Title: Stunning
Text: Wonderfully peaceful and beautiful retreat with a most imposing image of Khali as you arrive.  Take some smaller notes for buying offerings (as stallholders will tell you that they cant change larger notes  this happens a lot in Sri Lanka, be prepared).  Women will need to take something to cover legs and shoulders and shoes/sandals left at the approach. Make sure that you see the deer too, there are a lot of them!

Title: Simply amazing temple on a sea cliff
Text: This Indu temple is simply amazing with a wonderful view on the sea! Absolutely worth going! Dont miss it!

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: The level of details in this Hindu temple was impressive. We unfortunately missed the pooja (prayer). You should plan to be there at the right time, so you get the full experience. 30-45 min drive from Trinco city.

Title: Another wonderful example of a Hindu temple
Text: If in the area, you must come and see this holy temple. it is ornate and pretty. It does get hot, and although there is some carpeting your feet will still get hot. There are plenty of stalls on the walk up, and you are also passing through the old portuguese fort, now home to the SL army. Odd to think that only 9 years ago this area was part of the civil war, but now so peaceful.

Title: Interesting insights into Hindu culture
Text: Having dived below the temple, it was interesting to visit and see the various icons inside the temple. Well worth a visit.

Title: Siva temple in Trincomalee
Text: Avoid going between 1 & 4 when there is no darshan. The view of the ocean is amazing from the staircase that goes down right across the main door of the temple. Best view of the ocean I have had in a decade.

Title: Beautiful location
Text:
Nice setting on a cliff  high above the sea.

Mainly frequented by local Hindus who can purchase in one of the stalls along the road leading up to the temple. Some tourists also stop here on their way to a beach resort. 

On hot days the ground can burn your feet outside the temple so you might want bring socks...

Title: Hot place to visit only worth it for the passage through the fort.
Text: Go for the views and look at the colonial buildings and grounds of the fort. Don't forget to have shoulders and knees covered. The ground from where you leave your shoes to the temple was scalding.

Title: Go at service time
Text:
Unseasonal rains started up just as we arrived which added to the atmosphere. The open design meant that everyone was confined to one side of the temple to shelter from the rain. After a few minutes the bell rang and a service started. This was a very nice experience to observe people without feeling like we were intruding.
So I'd try time a visit for just before a service, we were there at 4pm, there is maybe 3 in the morning and 3 in the evening. Temple could close in the afternoon I'm not sure.
The original temple was destroyed many years ago.

Buy some sweets from the stalls lining the path up to the temple. I'd recommend thali

Title: Beautiful
Text: I had seen a lot of Buddha buildings, so this was the first time I saw something of the Hindu religion! Very nice and beautiful, if you are in Trincomolee, please visit this place!

Title: Impressive
Text:
Best view of Trincomalee and the Temple is very impressive

Colorfull with a lots of paintings, statues and sculptures: we loved this place!

Title: Wonderful Shiva statue
Text:
What a colourful and nice temple this is in Trincomalee. After you entered Ford Frederick you have to walk a bit towards the temple; we did this late afternoon which was great with regard to the heat. 
Outside there is a large statue of the Godess Shiva which is impressive. Inside there are lots of colourful statues to see; we were lucky as a ceremony just started when we arrived. 
Be aware, at an Hindu temple women need to wear a sarong and you have to enter without shoes.

Title: Wonderful colourful Hindu temple
Text:
Full of locals, with the real atmosphere of a saint place. There are great views from above all the city and harbour. We took the tuk-tuk up the hill (it's quite fat from the city center) and made a deal with a driver to wait for us. It took about half an hour to see all the place. 
Take socks with you! The path is really hot  and you are obliged to leave the shoes at the entrance (for free, but we packed ours to the bag and took with us).

Title: Must visit
Text: Ancient Shiva Temple on the cliff. Closely attached to King Ravana. The story of the temple was superb. The view on all the sides were breath taking. Well maintained temple. Family can spend sometime on the top enjoying the views.

Title: Good excursion
Text: This is a good trip to provide some variety from lying on the beach. There are great views from the bay from the top. I would recommend getting a tuk tuk up and walking back down.

Title: Great to visit
Text: Got a tuk tuk to the temple which is at the top of the hill. The temple itself is very beautiful. There was a ceremony going in when we visited but we were still welcome to enter- just couldn't take photos inside the actual temple - only outside. The view of the ocean, beaches and town is amazing. We then walked back down the hill - through the market along the road - and down through the Fort to the fort entrance. At the entrance to the temple you leave your footwear in a basket, you get given a ticket, and on return you collect your footwear and pay a 10 rupee fee. This temple is a must visit.

Title: an old Hindu temple
Text: historic temple, but avoid going midday as one has to remove footwear & the road/ground gets far too hot -likely to end up with blisters

Title: Very lovely peaceful temple in exotic location
Text: This temple is exactly on the land tip with sea on almost three sides. we felt very peaceful in this location and the place where Ravana statue stands the steps leading you downhill is really beyond words. One has to experience the sea breeze. The evening pooja at the temple is so ceremonial and keeps you absorbed and i just got so involved and never realised it was almost a 45minutes pooja. The sea lashing inbetween two mighty rocks is a sight to see. The best temple I have come across in Sri Lanka. Would love to visit again.

Title: hmm... maybe I didn't get it...
Text:
I've seen a few temples and sacred places, but I did not like this one at all. I don't understand all the positive reviews... 
Ok, the spot above the ocean is nice and the path to the temple is also very peaceful with those chunky trees and the deer around...
But the temple itself was very dirty and not really nice. No interesting paintings or other things, very impersonal... Oh there were some monkeys... but that's it ;)

Title: A Hindu Masterpiece
Text: This is an amazing Temple with many legendary stories about its history and rituals carried out by its religious pilgrims who visit. It is recommended that you have a tour guide who is of the same faith or well versed in its history.

Title: Spiritual Expierience!
Text: Visit this temple when a mass is going on! It´s an expierience you will not forget! Really a Must-See in Sri Lanka!

Title: Koneswaram Temple a must visit
Text:
Located inside the old fort and restoration is amazing. 

Try go when they are doing the 'Pooja' it is a soul touching experience.

Recommended to walk from fort door as the walk is quite nice ( if you like walking ).
 
View from the Kovil is breathtaking. Words cant say how beautiful it is.

Title: Beautiful view
Text: This is one of the beautiful place I have been.... The view was awesome and the total environment was so good with lots of deers.... Pleasant place for devotees.... Huge Shiva statue makes us wow......

Title: Historical place with breathtaking views
Text: Very popular place with both Hindu and Buddhist locals. Historical place with beautiful sea views of Indian Ocean. Very colourful place. One of the must visit place in trincomalee.

Title: Fascinating temple and location (sea views)
Text: I like temples so this was high on my list.  It sits on the hill at the top of the cliffs at the end of the peninsula with great views.  The temple itself is impressive with fascinating pictures and artefacts.  If you like temples, this is a great visit.

Title: Attention Getting
Text: The colors and decoration of this Hindu Temple certainly catch the eye. I would recommend visiting during a service in order to obtain an idea of the ritual and solemnity of the place.

Title: Interesting and lovely
Text: This is a really lovely Hindu Temple in a great setting, up on a hill, right by the ocean.  There are various caves and niches in the rocks that have been used to house some of the Hindu idols / artifacts.

Title: A nice kovil to visit during afternoon puja.
Text: A nice place to visit especially during the afternoon puja. The temple complex has some interesting sights apart from the main temple. The locals are very friendly and welcoming and they might even invite you to join them in a simple meal after the puja. As with almost all kovils in Sri Lanka, pictures are not allowed inside the main temple but men do not have to take their shirts off. The puja itself is more subdued compared to the ones we have observed in other parts of Sri Lanka.

Title: Wonderful temple is superb location
Text: The Koneswaram Hindu Temple is definitely a 'must see' when in Trincomalee. One has to walk for a few minutes along the road leading to it (with no shoes), then a short climb up into the Temple itself. You pass numerous street vendors selling sweet foods, hats and souvenirs. The Temple itself is a masterpiece of architecture and Hindu decorations and art work. Apart from the glory of the Temple one can enjoy superb panoramic views from the grounds, overlooking the town and distant beaches.

Title: Religiously breathtaking!
Text: A great place for theologians and others seeking insights on the Ramayana! The place is situated with a great panoramic view of the city and sea! A must for visitors to this city! Dressing must be decent in view of religious sentiments and taboo. The pictures and paintings inside which includes archeological findings really heartwarming and breathtaking! The stalls leading to the temple a great place for souvenirs and fair priced! But please do bargain for a great deal! Do not miss catching a glimpse of the deers!

Title: Fun walking tour
Text: Walk around a Hindu temple barefoot. Look at the ocean and get a taste of Tamil culture. Just a short walk from the bus station. Not to mention the very tame deer.

Title: A Place of Worship
Text: This ancient Kovil has a history of being a magnet for childless women. You will see toy cradles hung on a tress by women praying for a child.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
There is parking available at this temple free of charge. The walk to the temple is quite short but a little on the hilly side. There are stalls selling offerings to take with you to the temple and also stalls selling drinks and ice-creams. Once you get closer to the temple you have to remove your shoes as usual and pay Rupees 20.00 to reclaim them again.

The ground in the afternoon to the temple once you remove your shoes can be rather challenging as it becomes very hot. The temple itself is well worth a visit and the views from the top are truly magnificent. 

Sadly there are many spotted deer that have taken residency next to the temple, and have begun to beg for food from the devotees. Many people, including ourselves, stop to take photographs of the resident spotted deer. I only hope that people do not get them too familiar with begging for food due to feeding, that they completely forget how to forage for themselves.

Title: shakti peetham
Text: Koneswaram temple is a hindu temple an dknown as teh first among the shakti peetams .. very very nice .. well maintained ,clean and perfect place to worship... as the place is visited by many Indians  .. they are accepting Indian currency also....

Title: worth a look
Text: went and had a look, wasn't planning on it, but we went; had to remove shoes, put on sarong, but no worries. be respectful of people worshiping, and taking photos without asking.

Title: Peaceful place with rich history
Text: Visited on an early morning excursion with the family. Love the rich colours of this temple and with few people around you got a definite sense of peace and calm which was appreciated. Lots of little nooks and crannies with different deities and enjoyed the views of the Indian Ocean as well. Would definitely recommend any travellers to Trinco to tick this exquisite temple off the list.

Title: Amazing location
Text: A picturesque stroll from the fort that borders the temple allows amazing views back over Dutch bay and Trinco town. There is a number of vendors just before the entrance, selling an array of gifts for the locals. Do yourself a favour and sample some of the sweets, they are delightful. The temple itself is visited by large numbers of locals, making the short walk.

Title: Clifftop temple with an interesting history
Text: This is a beautiful temple with a lot of old artifacts and history dating back to the time of King Ravana. The location is fabulous, with views of the Trincomalee town and the beaches from the temple.

Title: Best place in trinkomale
Text: Mostly Hindu devotees visited to this place for engage with their religious works .Beyond that it is wonderful creature of nature. Every one should visit this place.

Title: Nice place to visit
Text: Very crowded, interesting place. You dont see many tourists there. On the way to the temple you can buy tacky, chinese stuff and snacks. The temple is worth to see. Very colorful and the way through the Fort is nice

Title: Nice temple with great views.
Text:
While I stood through the morning service I can't pretend to really understand what was going on but the Faithful were clearly enraptured by the spectacle.
Later we went along the cliff-edge path with great views of the ocean.
Those unused to walking barefooted should be aware that you have to leave your shoes a fair distance from the temple so socks may be a good idea in the heat of the day.

Title: A Must See Attraction
Text: No visit to Trincomalee would be complete without visiting Koneswaram Temple. We were in a self drive car so were only required to walk the 500 or so metres from the car park, but from Trincomalee town it is a bit of an uphill trek particularly in the very hot conditions. As with all Hindu temples shoes are not allowed within the temple or the immediate surrounding area, so a pair of socks is a good idea to protect against the hot sand and gritty ground. Entry is free but shoes must be deposited at a kiosk for which a small fee of 20 rupees is charged.  The views from the temple are stunning particularly over 'lovers leap'.

Title: Temple
Text:
I had a tuk tuk take me it's lovley entrance old fort. But army still there  staying and looking after it  big grounds lots of deer my driver took food and they came right up  eat out our hands. 
No shoes at temple  my driver was explaining things which made it far more interesting there was a bit that was locked  this is for people's safety there's been a lot of people taken ther life's there 
The views are amazing

Title: Colourful
Text:
A very colourful Hindu temple set high on the cliff above the sea. Very important Temple for Hindus.
Am not a massive fan of temple visits. This ticked a box and would probably tick many for temple aficionados.

Title: Great view from top
Text:
The temple is located on the top of the hill. This is a temple of lord Siva with big statues outside. The parking is approx 300 meters from the temple and then you need to walk. Before entering you need to take off your shoes and keep in the racks available there.
Since the hill is on the edge of the sea, the view of sea from the top is real breath taking. A must see place while you are at Trincomalee.

Title: I had the intention of visiting the temple. I did not. See the picture
Text: I´ve visited many temples of a wide variety of religions in many countries. I never saw an advertisment like the one they have in the entrance. It seems they are quite rigid!!

Title: Shiva ..
Text: A pretty little temple with outstanding views over the bay , stalls are lining the road up to it with the usual temple tat . Very pleasant .

Title: Very beautiful temple in the mountains
Text: This is a very famous place among all religion. They have magnificent statues. Can see the whole trinco city when you reach there.

Title: Significant Hindu temple
Text: One of the most important and holy Hindu temples in Sri Lanka, open all hours, gives you a good feel of the local Tamil culture.

Title: Historical
Text: It was a rainy day hence the temple was almost empty.  Neat and clean environment! Not dress code restrictions!  Loved this place.

Title: Historic Hindu Temple
Text: This is a very historic temple in Trinco and definitely worth a visit. Its on top of a hill next to the ocean. Its a very touristy place with full of tourists. You need to park the vehicle quite far away and walk up to the temple

Title: RAVANA CUT
Text: It is very nice &beautiful place in sri lanka...visited the temple in evening ,the temple is located at the edge of the  hill which is facing the sea.It is pleasent atmosphere.

Title: Star attraction in Trincomalee
Text: This is a place never to be missed any one visiting Trincomalee. Threre are so many stories of this place in the past which cannot be written one by one. I had the opportunity to visit this ancient site after about 35 years and there are lots of changes. In my last visit on 1980's there were no temperary souvenier stalls and the kovil was not this large like now. What I saw was one of the most beautiful places over looking the entrance to the port from the ocean, the natural harbour and the fishing harbour. All could be sighted so well and it was one of the most spectacular senaries. But now there are so many temperary shops as well as the kovil has extended all sorts of buildings at the edge of the rock the spectacular scenary has vanished. Thre are only few accesses to the scenary it is so dissapointing. The authorities have authorised build all the scenery covering buildings it is really really dissapointing. I reckon still its a very good and beutiful place to viisit. One advise read about the history of this place before you visit!

Title: Koneswaram Temple, Trincomalee:well worth a visit
Text:
The Koneswaram temple is one of most holy Hindu shrines to the god Shiva in Sri Lanka and is well worth a visit. It is easily approached by car or the ubiquitous tuk tuk readily hired close to most local tourist hotels around Trincomalee town. The high rock on which the temple stands gives great views out to sea and coast.

Be aware that the dropping off point is a hundred yards or so from the temple near a range of souvenir stalls. The last part of the approach requires bare feet (this can be a bit hard on the feet) as is usual when visiting shrines and shoes can be deposited in a rack for this purpose. 

The temple and surrounds are lavishly decorated with colourful statutes and a number of dioramas illustrating stories from the lives of the gods.

Title: Visit to Hindu temple
Text:
Following a gentle walk up to the temple passed a few stalls selling hats and souvenirs we saw the colourful statue with the temple behind. We were privilaged to be allowed to join a ceremony  and (we are female) local females showed us what to do. We bought a ticket at a kiosk to give to the priests to bless us. The temple is beautiful inside but no pictures allowed. Behind the temple were lots of little cradles hung on trees for fretility wishes.
Beautiful views out to sea and across the bay.
We ended with a cool orange juce in the cafe on the hill where we watched the sun set.

Title: Majestic temple!!
Text: Visited this place on a rainy day. The temple is located right on the edge of a hill facing the Blue Ocean. You get pleasant sightings of deer as well.

Title: A Must See in Trincomalee
Text: We went there during late January and unfortunately it turned out to be a very hot day. You have to leave your transport a fair way from the temple and walk the rest of the distance bare foot. We found it very uncomfortable to walk on the tarmac which was  extremely hot for us. Managed to get as close as you can to get a good view of the temple  but could not venture in.

Title: Very busy temple
Text: Went to the temple towards the evening on a special feast day so it was quite busy. Dropped off well before temple since unable to get closer and walked down road through many shops selling everything either side. Ahead was the temple, splendid location on a promontory the cliff edge. Down the side of the cliffs were various statues and places for prayer. Outside the temple we were met by a huge statue and inside was extremely colourful and beautiful and well worth seeing. The only downside was the temple guardian. Some musllim ladies walked in, heads covered. [not allowed] A few words were passed and as they removed their head wear as a mark of respect more words were passed and they were ordered out. Surely in a religious setting  tolerance and empathy would not be amiss. Despite this episode some interesting customs outside, smashing coconuts for fertility..  Back up the road to the shops and to collect ones shoes.

Title: Ancient Hindu temple
Text: Right on the Indian Ocean, this temple is a relatively new version of an ancient temple that Portuguese invaders destroyed several centuries ago. But Hindu Tamil priests keep the services going, several times a day. This temple was out of bounds for several years during the civil war and is now opening up again as peace returns to Sri Lanka

Title: A long climb in bare feet!
