Text: We are told there are over 1800 steps but they are shallow and should not prove a problem for anyone of average fitness.  More of a challenge is getting to the final high spot over steep, smooth rock with a few footholds, there is a hand rail but you may have to let go to let people down!  You will need a head for heights at the top the barriers are low but the view is stupendous.  There are several other shrines on the way up with their own story and well worth the visit.  For more information visit the web page for the temple.

Title: worth a visit!
Text: what a celebration of colors, smells, sounds and more....located on a very nice spot, overlooking the trincomalee bay and has a vey nice market. Recommended

Title: Get away and see some culture
Text:
A nice trip out, what a setting..set in a military fort you get to see a different side.  The temple is amazing, bare in mind the temperature of the floor as you do have to remove your shoes....

But lovely.

Title: Beautiful Hindu temple
Text: Visiting this beautiful temple late in the afternoon, we found ourselves almost intruding on everyday Hindu live. But we met only smiles from the people :) Impressive and worth a visite!

Title: Visited this temple after 25yrs. no word to describe the spiritual place.
Text: Travelled to this place on a three wheeler from JKAB Hotel. Enjoyed the beach and scenic view from the temple.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text:
This temple to the Hindu god Shiva is very colourful and there are a lot of historical pieces to see. Some of the details/history of the temple are in English but not all. It might be best to read a description of the temple online prior to entering. 

Cameras are not allowed inside the main part of the temple. Shoes are not allowed in any part of the temple grounds. Note the pavement will be extremely hot and difficult to walk on if you come during the day time - look for shady areas to walk on. Women must have the legs and shoulders covered before entering.

Title: Lively place
Text: As you enter this place you can see loud music which can be for some people disturbing, but for me it was quite a fun. The place is very nice and offers a stunning ocean view.

Title: Nice and interesting
Text: Come in the evening around 6 or 7 PM to see the amazing sunset from the top of the hill and the ceremony in the temple. One of the most beautiful temples we visited in Sri Lanka.

Title: Hindu Images galore
Text: If Hindu temples are your thing this is the Grand Daddy of them all. Worth a visit. Just remember that with all religious sites no footwear can be worn and if it is hot you may need a good pair of thick socks.

Title: Impressive
Text: Impressive to see. Remember to put on long trousers or a long dress (and no bare shoulders) should you want to enter the temple. Shoes can be stored for 20 Roepies a pair close to the entrance of the premisses.

Title: Nice temple, Great view
Text: It's a great temple with lots of action going on. Drums and trumpets playing in a very nice and colorful temple. Lots to see for people who are new to Hinduism. The view from Swami Rock is great aswell, especially during sunset. Would advise to go one way at least by Tuk Tuk if you stay in Trincomalee.

Title: Elegant building worthy of a look around
Text:
Situated at the top of the hill within the fort, the building is very attractive and elegant with numerous figures upon parts of the roof and a very large statue of Shiva at the entrance.

Quirky little place really and worth popping into if you're in the area.

Title: Nice view, fairytale Like temple
Text: Nice trip in 'trinc', views are superb, temple is beautiful Hindu piece of work, certainly worth the detour (entrance is free)

Title: Interesting temple
Text:
Not the best temple we have seen in Sri Lanka - this temple is a Hindi temple rather than Buddhist hence looks significantly different! Colourful but lacks of English texts for us to understand the religious importance here. Also it is relatively small! 

Go and have a look! May not be everyone's cuppa!

Title: Intricate Colorful Temples!
Text: The temple is right on a cliff that overlooks the ocean, beautiful sight! The temple itself is SO colorful and full of life. It is a real operational temple where people come to worship. The trees were bent over with the intense weight of the offerings. It was a super gorgeous temple, but not a whole lot to do besides admire the temple.

Title: Great view of the coast, colourful Hindu temple
Text:
Inside the Old Dutch Fort (still functioning today as a military base), atop the promontory overlooking Trincomalee, Back Bay and the Indian Ocean - the Temples' position provides a wonderful view.

The Hindu Koneswaram Temple itself is small yet colourful. Its foundation is also very old and its history long.

Make sure you venture around the outside of the Temple, particularly towards the cliff face. Don't forget to look down - the water is crystal clear.

Remember, cover your knees (shoulders for females too). Its hot ! And, it's shoes off..... Be prepared to have your feet heat up real quick or run fast.  You'll need some small change for the 'shoe guy' too.

Worth a visit if you are in or near Trincomalee.

Title: Lovely temple with sea view
Text:
Definitely a must see in trincomalee. Situated in fort Frederick, this temple overlooks the sea. It has a beautiful large statue at the front with many other statues around and inside. Go there early if you want to avoid burning your feet on the way up (you need to remove your shoes and walk a small distance to the temple)

We were lucky to witness the pooja or prayers and blessing. There are lovely views of the Indian Ocean. Entry is free to the temple although donations are welcome and there is a small fee for keeping the shoes.

Title: Scenic temple
Text: The temple is situated on top of the cliffs in the fort. We took a tuk-tuk to the top and walked down, which was interesting. No charge to enter, just a small fee to store your shoes as you can't wear shoes in the temple itself. We were there during a ceremony, which was very interesting to see. The temple is very colourful and has modern statues and paintings alongside older statues that were excavated from the original temple. Lovely views from the cliffs. It was a little difficult to understand the significance of all of the figures as most of the signage is not in English. Worth a visit.

Title: nice temple on the top of the fort
Text: it is must see place, hindu Koneswaram Temple is on the top of the Fort with long history.You can see colonial buildings and old trees.

Title: Nice example of a Hindu historical site
Text: Situated atop the promontory inside the old Dutch fort of the city, this large Hindu temple is a good example of the artistic talents of the followers of this religion.  After a short walk past the hawkers selling religious and other trinkets you remove your footwear before seeing the large, blue statue of Shiva sitting at the forefront of the temple.  The walls of the temple are adorned with painted representations of Shiva and other Hindu deities, and the rooftop and cornices are covered with statues of the same.  There is a short walk around the cliff top overlooking the ocean with other, small shrines to Shiva and other deities for those who are interested.  Views of the ocean from this walk are amazing.  Photos of the external areas of the temple are allowed while none are allowed inside.  No cost.  Highly Recommended.

Title: Ancient Siva Temple, a must visit while in Sri Lanka
Text: This majestic temple build on the sea shore is an example of great architecture. The serene and peaceful atmosphere is very calming. The view of the temple from the sea is also great.

Title: Beautiful temple!
Text: I would recommend to go to the temple either early in the morning or late afternoon. It is not allowed to have shoes on, so it can get quite hot walking around barefoot in the middle of the day. It is a beautiful temple and absolutely worth the trip.

Title: Approximately 6th Century BCE
Text:
The building is beautifully re-constructed and multi-colour carved statues like most Hindu Temple. 

The statues inside were the original ones excavated/found under the sea.

Please remember to wear attire longer below knees & shoulders covered as a form of respect.

We coincided our visit with the  Puja ceremony which is at 1130am. Locals will bring their offerings. 
After the priest prays, he brings a flame around. You put your hands beside the flame/touch the container briefly to receive the light.

And he brings around the white powder where you dab on the forehead between the eyes. The white liquid (sweeten coconut milk) to be receive on your palm and you sip it. And the orange/red powder is also meant to dab on the forehead.

We receive blessings. :)

(No photos allowed inside)

Title: Most Tranquil Poetic Place
Text:
I spent a few hours up at Koneswaram Temple which is only a five minute bicycle ride from me. It stood here since 400 BC, one of the sacred sites for Hindus, and is mentioned in Mahabharata. I wasnt looking for the temple, just felt like climbing up above the ocean, but there it was.

You will be given a piece of fabric to wrap around your deliciously brown knees if you happen to wear shorts. It is free, give it back on return. You will need to take off your shoes and leave them in the box rack. Walk barefoot on the baking hot slab stones and sand of the main approach. It will make you hop and run into the shade of temple real fast.

I loved being up there. It sits atop the Swami rock over the Ocean into the vertigenous cliffs, the crows fly between the columns, there is an air of gentle decay, abandonment and a spirit of generations who lived, believed, perished; nothing, but a fairytale left. The breeze from the ocean sings in the ears, and a giant statue of Golden Shiva gazes past you into the distance of the harbour. So peaceful, no crowds, no tourists. I shudder to think about this becoming like the Pyramids. When I saw those at 25, I wanted to cry.. from a shrill sense of impossibility to be one to one with eternity bloody crowds, and sure I was one of them too.

A Temple worker perceptively told me You love it here, dont you.. come any time. The devastating beauty of the location and a strange air of dignity that the human touch afforded it.. when you see both the military ship patrolling the harbour AND a giant turtoise splashing at the surface.. just fills one with gratitude for being part of it all in this needle of space and time. I could die there tomorrow, and that would be OK.

Title: Serene
Text: Very well maintained amidst serene surroundings. Very clean and calm atmosphere. The temple management seems to be very capable

Title: Temple
Text: You'll have to remove your shoes and cover your shoulders; there is an air of peace and respect you'll want to abide by. Beautiful temple overlooking the sea

Title: Worth a visit at sunset.
Text:
I've seen Hindu temples before but not set in such an amazing scene. The temple sits on a bluff with more 270 degrees surrounded by water. Not much to but walk around to see some of the statues and look inside the temple (no photos allowed inside) but worth an hour.

Best time to go is late afternoon. Beautiful lighting and the ground isn't so not (you must take your shoes off 50m front the temple).

Title: Perfect spot for a birds eye-view of Trincomalee
Text: A temple perched up on a high vantage point in Fort Fedric. Wonderful views while visiting a Hindu temple.

Title: Sri Lanka take 3
Text: Second visit to this temple. Definitely worth checking out. The view from the temple is amazing, but try and visit late in the day, ground is very hot during the middle of the day

Title: Heritage temple within a fort, right on the cliff
Text: Don't ever miss this amazing temple. If you need a closer darshan inside the temple, you need to wear dhoti or saree. Else you can see from outer Praharam. Dont miss the beautiful sunset..

Title: Interesting Hindu Temple Worth to Visit if You Stay for some Days in Trinco

Title: Well worth the visit
Text: Colourful and very inviting temple.  Great place to see a sunset as well if you go in the cool if the early evening.

Text:
It is very much worth a visit as a break from the beach. It's at the top of a hill inside the Fort.  A car can take you most of the way up but you'll have to walk the last couple of hundred meters. You'll run a gauntlet of vendors. They are actually half the fun.

You'll have to take your shoes off, and pay for the privilege, for about the last 100 meters. The pavement can be hot, very HOT. Even the locals were screaming and running for spots the sun wasn't hitting. Visiting early in the morning would probably solve that.

Title: Beautiful Temple.
Text: This is really worth a visit if you are staying around Trinco. It's location on a clifftop really adds to the atmosphere. Koneswaram temple is one of the few Hindu temples I have visited but definitely the most impressive with a huge statue of Lord Vishnu towering above the entrance and numerous, colourful examples of Hindu art both inside and out.

Title: it was beautiful!!!
Text: i love every inch of this place... the view was just breath taking, and the temple architecture was absolutely gorgeous

Title: Beautiful View Beautiful Energy
Text: This temple is profound. One must experience it. Make sure to wear traditional dress if you want to do pooja offering.

Title: Beautiful and intricate temple!

Title: Impressive site

Title: Clifftop temple with lively vensor scene on the grounds
Text: The biggest tourist attraction is Koneswaram Temple, on a high clifftop overlooking the ocean. A temple was first established here around 500 BC, but when the Portugese took over around 1620, they demolished the temple and used stones from the rubble to build a fort at the base of the cliff. The fort remains and is now a military base, but the temple has been rebuilt and the site's antiquity attracts many pilgrims.

Text:
I visited this Temple two weeks ago and spent a fairly short, but interesting time there. The surroundings are vibrant with colorfully-clothed worshipers (there was some sort of festival on) and the temple itself is a riot of color and design.  Entrance was free (though they like a very tiny donation for minding your shoes) and we were not under any pressure at any time.  Previous advice about wearing socks is excellent as the tarmac forecourt of the temple etc can be burning hot.  Luckily my driver/guide had warned me in advance. 
I know nothing about Hindu gods but I did notice in some Guide Books that the huge statue at the front of the temple used to be a gold-colored figure, then a blue-skinned one - the current entity holds a different pose and is orange-skinned. My guide/driver told me that it was covered in scaffolding until very recently, so I was lucky that this had been removed.
There are deer, many vendors (who do not annoy) and some lovely views around the temple so I am sure the majority of visitors would find this a worthwhile trip.

You have take your shoes off and walk uphill on tarmac for 100m. As the weather is so hot, the tarmac is burning hot!! There is an ice cream van, toilets (take your own paper and hand gel), lots of souvenir stalls and stalls selling drinks and fresh fruit and coconuts. The souvenirs are all the same, mainly keyrings and plastic toys!
The temple is accessible to all, free entry - 'do not pay anyone anything' was the advice we were given, yet no one tried to ask us for money. You could spend 20 mins looking round but not too much more than that. The outside of the temple is interesting, as there are many open wooden crates tied to trees - apparently they are pregnancy wishes. There is a stunning view of the sea if you follow the path to the top and to the right of the temple entrance. 
A very worthwhile experience.

Title: Beautiful location

Title: Visiting the Siva Ishwarams (Pancha Ishwarams) in Sri Lanka.
Text:
Visiting the Siva Ishwarams (Pancha Ishwarams) in Sri Lanka.

The reunion with relatives in Jaffna took us to four of the Siva Temples in Sri Lanka during the first seven days of our Sri Lanka Odyssey.

Our first stop, on March 3rd, was at the Munneswaram temple situated in a village in the Puttalam District. Hindus believe that it is one of the the five temples they need to visit in their life time. The others being Naguleswaram temple which we visited in Keerimalai in the Kankesanthurai district on March 4th and Thiruketheeshwaram in Mannar District and the Koneswaram temple in Trincomalee (Thirukonamalai) -- both the next day.

All these, including Rameswaram in India form the five ancient temples (Ishwarams) dedicated to Shiva.

According to Hindus, the Munneswaram temple near Puttalam is the temple where King Rama prayed to Shiva after killing Ravana to seek forgiveness over the death of many in the war.

Hindus believe that the Naguleswaram temple's adjacent water tank, the Keerimalai Springs, has curative properties. The temple was largely destroyed by Jesuit missionaries following the Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna kingdom, restored by Arumuga Navallar in 1894.

The Thiruketheeshwaram temple had existed for more than 2,400 years. During our visit to this temple, we witnessed a temple devotee from Vavunia singing Thevarams. His aim was to complete the 800 thurmurai thevarams in one month.

The Trincomelee Koneswaram temple was built by the Cholas/Pandian kings. The temple is situated atop Konesar Malai, at a commanding position overlooking the Indian Ocean. It is also known as the "Mount Kailash of the South".

The temple, mentioned in Mahabaratha and Ramayana, was visited by Arunagirinathar and is the easternmost shrine of the five ancient Ishwarams of Shiva on the island.

Title: Koneswaram  Temple
Text: Koneswaram Temple is one of the Oldest tourism and devotional place in Srilanka. Pleseant for all Peoples. Visit Srilanka

Title: A great clifftop temple
Text: After a stroll up through many stalls selling drinks and offerings for the temples, you leave your shoes at the minder and wander up to the top of the hill.  It is a lovely temple with great paintings and an interesting collection of "cots" hanging in the trees -offerings from those hoping to have children. Many boats come here so the fishermen can come and pray before going out to sea. The temple has laid in ruins, been restored and enlarged over the years, and it became one of if not the most important surviving classical Dravidian structures by the 17th C.

Title: Best temple in Srilanka
Text:
Weve visited a TON of temple in our months travelling India and Srilanka and I have to say this is one of the most beautiful!

Its perched on the edge of a cliff (lovers leap) and the paint work inside and outside is second to none.

Leading up the the temple there are lots of stalls selling bits and bobs (the sweet stalls are great).

If youre thinking Ive seen enough, make this your last you wont regret it

Title: Worth a short visit
Text: Hindu temple inside old fortress. Interesting to walk around but an uphill climb from the Fish Market area so maybe best to take a tuc tuc there and back.

Title: A much visit
Text: This is a beautiful, spiritual Hindu temple located on top of a large hill/ mountain in Trincomalee, fully accessible by road and by foot. The carvings, paintings and religious artefacts are amazing and very interesting, with English texts providing guidance as to meanings etc. The views are also stunning, with views over the bay. Definitely worth a visit if in Trincomalee.

Title: Beautiful View
Text: This hindu temple located on a mountain near the sea. It has a wonderful view around the kovil. You can see the indian ocean and trincomalee city and harbour too. And it has a historical background with King Ravana.

Title: Wonderful
Text: A gorgeous and beautifully located temple full of friendly worshippers. Colourful and glorious. An easy walk. The sweet looking cow outside the temple is actually an attack cow... beware!

Title: Worth the visit!
Text: This temple is beautiful and it's free. You can see the locals pray and catch a great view of Trinco. Women should cover shoulders and legs. They do have covers available at the entry. We were pleasantly surprised by how much we enjoyed this.

Title: Good view of harbour
Text: Nothing else remarkable to say about this site. Lots of deer were seen. Lots of local sweet delicacies to buy. Have to take of shoes to store at LKR20 per cubby hole. Very hot day so could not stay long.

Title: Must visit if you are in Trincomalee
Text:
Grate Hindu Temple. Best time to visit early in the morning.
Lot of visitors from all over the world visit this temple.

Title: Interesting
Text: Seeing the temple was an interesting experience. Please remember that if there are people who are not able to walk a long distance, they can go in a vehicle all the way up to the temple. There is a sign that says no vehicles are allowed but there are exceptions.

Title: Fascinating temple on a superb site
Text:
This is an important Hindu temple and primarily a religious place. The sea views around the temple are stunning and lovers leap is beautiful although the sight has many sad endings!! 

The spotted deer that roam around are also worth a look.

We enjoyed spending about 45-60 mins here but you could spend a lot longer. Well worth a visit if you are in the area.

Title: Very nice temple with good views
Text: I recently visited the Koneswaram Temple.  It is a small temple, and nice for a quick visit. You have to take your shoes off a way before the temple and it is very uncomfortable walking on the gravel up to the temple. No idea why they don't put something down over the gravel. Hard for tourists to walk on this and also the ground gets very hot.

Title: Historical Place you must see
Text:
This was the second time i visited the temple. You have to park it and climb a small mountain to go to the temple. its inside the fort. along the way there are many shops to buy local sweets, arts and crafts. 
please wear clothes that do not reveal bare arms and thighs if not you have to cover.

Title: Colourful and wonderous.
Text: An amazingly detailed and painted temple. The figures of Hindu mythology are a treat to see. A functional and busy temple that's definitely worth a look.

Title: Excellent view
Text: Beautiful temple, but the best thing is the city and sea view. Fantastic view of the city of Trincomalee and the Indian Ocean.

Title: Religious / Cultural / Strategic
Text: One of the must see if you are travelling on the eastern coast.  This is indeed a strategic place where you can have control over eastern part of Indian Ocean as nothing in between till Andaman Sea. The view of Lovers' Leap or Ravana's Cleft is beautiful. Also walking all over naked feet is another experience. Listening the Temple Bell at the time of sunset along with traditional music coming from inside was unique.

Title: Beautiful temple on the Indian Ocean
Text: This ancient Hindu Temple dedicated to Shiva has indie interesting murals of Ravana, the Shiva devotee. We were present for the evening Aarti and it was very nice to see the devotion and faith of the people. Ravana's cut - in the rocks outside the temple has an interesting story

Title: A beautiful Hindu Temple high on a hill with great views.
Text: We walked here from Trinco center. It was about a 3km walk and took about 45 minutes one way. This temple sit at the top of Swami rock. Along the way, near the top there are restaurants and many souvenir shops. At the top sits a giant blue Shiva as well as a beautiful Temple with many beautiful murals. There is no fee. There is a scenic walk along the cliff decorated with 3D Hindu stories. Take socks to protect your feet from the hot sand. You must take off your shoes....there is a shoe fee. The walk takes you thru Fort Fredrick, and past a path leading to a Buddhist Stupa.

Title: Shiva sits in a great view!
Text:
This Hindu temple is located like many places in a beautiful spot, but this one has a great view over the Indian ocean and the Dutch harbour.
We where informed that it is the 5th biggest natural harbour in the world!
Fort Frederick is a delightful park and contains both colonial buildings and are still used today by the Sri Lankan army.

Temple lover or not, it´s worth the visit while in Trincolombee!

Title: Must visit at Trincomalee
Text: Good temple. Learned new stories about Ravana. The temple is very neat and clean and offers excellent views of Indian Ocean.

Title: Exquisite sea view from temple
Text:
This is the best place in trincomalee to spend your evening. This place is inside the fort. If you are walking towards the temple, there is a high probability that you will see plenty of deers who actually do not care who is around. They are quite used to people around and will not run away, so plenty of time to click a pic!

As the temple is on a cliff, you get a wide view of the oceans and speed boats. There is also a lover 's leap here..which is a scary drop from the cliff. The temple premises has several gods and goddesses statues and pictures on the wall. There is a huge Shiva statute just outside the premises and visible from quite a distance. 

Tip: Do not forget to shop for local items just outside the temple complex. You can busy certain packed items to eat which are local delicacies, jewelry and craft work at a very reasonable price. Still, you can bargain to get a better price. Irrespective of that the prices are very reasonable and a good point to shop for souvenirs.

Title: Amazing view and bit of history
Text: The view is breath taking from the top of the cliff. If you go in the early morning you can enjoy the sun rise from here. As well participate for a traditional Hindu prayer and learn a little bit of the Hindu culture and history.

Title: Beautiful and Peaceful
Text: It is a very bug temple and is also very peaceful. It has many god in there. The architecture is nicely done.

Title: good view of Trinco harbour
Text: The best part of this location is you can get a breathtaking view of Trinco harbour. Apart from it, it's typical Hindu temple with lot of statues. You feel relaxed when going inside the temple.

Title: Must visit temple while in trincomolee
Text: The location of this temple complex is amazing. Right next to the ocean, Since it is on top of an hill, the views from the complex are breath taking. The temple is very religious and is in indian style.

Title: Very sacred
Text: The temple on the shore next above the sea level and one of the most prominent places in Srilanka.It is well maintained and very clean.The view from the temple also isvery good.

Title: Great Temple Great Views
Text: Had no idea what to expect but was surprised ,very interesting Hindu temple. Leave your shoes with the shoe man for 20rp wash your feet with the plastic cup and walk up the hot stairs to the entrance. Perched on a clifftop with great views out over the ocean. Apparently it's a green zone no plastic or rubbish allowed in but look over the fence and there it all is !! Why throw it over the fence at a sacred places I don't understand It's a beautiful place and it's treated like a tip. The temple itself is outstanding ,the artwork over the top and incredibly colorful. Definitely worth a visit

Title: Amazing View!
Text: A beautiful temple located on the cliff with a amazing view of the ocean. The history of the temple either written in sinhala or tamil language. If someone could explain about the stories the visit would be more interesting.

Title: Worth the effort
Text: A real must see when in trinco. The views from the temple are fantastic and well worth the effort. The temple is in an army fort so would recommend a tuk tuk or van to take you in.

Title: All the colours!
Text:
Pretty awesome temple. Nothing is in English though...
No shoes and must cover up!
Although there isn't anything to read, it's still a wicked temple and calms you when you enter.

Title: very comfortable visit
Text: if your visit tricomali, this certainly is a comfortable place which is inevitable. you can feel clearly of the local flavor, but buy something local with local price too

Title: The Hindu temple in Trincomalee
Text: Best to be there for the 6:30am Pooja - best time, great light and few people especially on weekdays

Title: Food was OK
Text: Was lovely and cool inside this air conditioned restaurant which was a bonus. Kids had pizzas which were fine but sadly my nasi gorang was burnt and every mouthful tasted of burnt rice which was very disappointing. I'm not one to complain but I won't be going back. Also were bothered by flies so waiter positioned a fan next to the table to try and blow them away from our food!

Title: Beautiful Temple
Text:
This temple is located inside of Fort Frederick in Trinco. It's an uphill path so a tuk tuk might help those with mobility issues, but it's not that hard to get to. 

You leave your shoes at the entrance and pay 20 rupees to get them back when you leave. I didn't heed the previous reviews and went barefooted and it is really hot on the soles of your feet, so be warned!

The temple itself is beautiful - lots of colourful deities and carvings - when we got there, offerings were starting and so a lot of things were being covered up. this didn't detract from the experience overall, but just know that this sometimes happens. 

There's also an outdoor bit around the edge of the cliff - you can look out over the Bay of Bengal and hope to spot a whale. 

All in all, a lovely temple to visit - there's not much to do in Trinco, so definitely give this a shot!

Title: Historic Temple with a stunning view of the Bay
Text:
You enter the temple after a nice walk down a winding road.

As you turn into temple you see a HUGE statue of Lord Shiva - in bright blue !

The temple is not very big (unlike its counterparts in India), but airy and roomy.
And  not very crowded like most temples in Sri Lanka...

As you walk around the temple, its 2000+ year history begins to get into you !

The Bay looking stunning on the eastern periphery of the temple. 

Caution - the walk from the place you remove the footwear to the covered portion of the temple can be cruel on sensitive feet ! We reached at noon - and we really felt the heat. So plan your visit before 10 am or after 4 pm, if possible.

Title: one of the holiest temples in Srilanka
Text: Worshipped and sung by noted scholars and spiritual gurus, this most sacred temple is where King Ravan was supposed to have prayed Lord Shiva.

Title: Amazing and insightful
Text: For me a person who has never bee to India, seeing hinduism practiced in front of me was an eye opening experience. The temple's architecture is fascinating!

Title: Great scenic spot for a temple
Text: A high point projecting out into an endless sea with a backdrop of the entire town. This is a great location to meditate and look over the town, chosen by the guardian of the town - Thiru Koneshwaran after whom the local Tamil name of the town is derived - Thiru Kone Mallai later Anglicised to Trincomalee

Title: Great experience to learn more about religion
Text: Beautiful temple with amazing location right on the cliff top overlooking the ocean. Such beautiful details and worth a visit.

Title: Iconic temple in Trincomalee
Text: Hindu Temple on a mountain. You can get a great view from the Temple out to the ocean. Avoid to visit this Temple on mid-day as it will be too hot to walk around.

Title: Might be the only think worth visiting in Trinco
Text: If you are in the area it's worth a look.  The view from the temple grounds back to Trinco and the temple itself is worth a photo or two.  Nice place to pray if you are Hindu.  I did not like that the souvenir stands and shops along the road leading up to the temple are mostly Sinhalese/Buddhist operated.  Would have liked to have seen more Tamil/Hindu's to whom the temple has more meaning that just another tourist cash cow.

Title: Very picturesque temple and cliff-side views
Text: Probably one of the few interesting cultural sites, along with the fort that you traverse to get here.   If this is your faith, probably a much more meaningful.  If not, it's worth a 30-40 minute visit for picture-taking and brief cultural interlude.

Title: A chip from Tamil Nadu
Text:
I went to this temple complex out of curiosity to see  how different it was form the temples in Tamil Nadu where I was born. There is nothing Sinhalese about this temple it is out and out a chip  splintered from the temple culture of Tamil Nadu. If there are differences I cannot spot them for I am no temple expert. 

I did not enter the temple because it was necessary to remove one's shoes and I was in no mood to walk barefoot on a hot day on a  dirty pathway. 

The temple was located high on a mountain peak and the view of the sea was panoramic and brought in a mood of peace and well being all around. 

The shops on the path leading to the temple sell all kinds of items used in Hindu religious rituals. This may be one of the best places to buy souvenir for yourselves and gifts for your Hindu friends.

Title: A visit to the Hindu Temple Koneswaram
Text: A beautiful temple that is situated on the hill. We chose to visit independently although you can hire a guide.

Title: Huge and magnificent
Text: This temple is magnificent, dramatic and huge.  It is much bigger than any other temple that we saw on Sri Lanka.  Well worth a visit for the pure drama.

Title: Serene
Text: We visited this sacred hindu temple in March 2019. It's a beautiful temple with a calm atmosphere.If you visit north of Sri Lanka, you must visit this temple.

Title: A most holy and beautiful temple
Text: A very beautifully decorated Temple, and a most holy Hindu one in Sri Lanka. Men must take of Shirts. A must see while your in Jaffna

Title: Wonderful temple which is open to visitors
Text: Jaffna Nallur Kovil - a sacred Hindu temple - has beautiful, bright paintings and statues. While we were there a ceremony/service took place accompanied by drumming, a shehnai (wind instrument) and lit oil lamps. It was a special experience.

Title: Very Moving experience
Text:
We visited this temple on our one day in Jaffna and would definitely recommend it as a must do for anyone visiting the north of SriLanka. We arrived as a Puja was about to commence and were lucky to take part in the ceremony. The devotion of the people attending was remarkable.

A very hot day so a visit to the fresh juice shop opposite the temple entrance was most welcome afterwards. Definitely worth a visit also. Delicious banana lassi

Title: Magnificent
Text:
Really nice experience. Beatifull building. Experiencing a puja is also wonderful.
No photography inside allowed and man should be shirtless

Title: Amazing
Text: A beautiful building - no photos allowed inside.  As there was a ceremony underway, all men had to remove their shirts.

Title: Interesting stop on walking tour of city
Text: We walked to fort and later in day along to nallur kovil which was stunning to view and well worth seeing

Title: Iconic temple
Text: An hindu temple, which is one of the largest I have visited. Apart from the size there is nothing much to see inside.

Title: Ornate temple
Text: Large temple with a number of ornate gopuram gatehouse towers. Located a little way out of the centre so a tuk-tuk is needed if youre not staying locally.

Title: One of the most impressive hindu temples in Sri Lanka
Text:
The Nallur Kovli is the most impressive building in Jaffna. Decorated with little statues, this breathtaking gold-ish temples rises high into the sky. The temple area is huge, cows are roaming the area while people a re sitting in the shade of the trees. The inside is even more breathtaking, the walls are covered with huge, colorful paintings depicting holy scenes and the whole place exhales a spiritual calmness like no other temple in Jaffna. The most impressing ritual is performed in the afternoon when the idol rides on a chariot to it's "resting chamber".
The Nallur Kovil is accessible for everyone as long as they follow the "dresscode": no shoes as usual.  Covered knees and shoulders for women, no shirts for men. You're not allowed to take pictures inside the building.

Title: 6pm puja at Nallur temple
Text: Lovely temple and grounds with a puja we attended. Makes need to take their tops off as it is their custom.

Title: Identity of Jaffna
Text: This temple is very historical and identity for Jaffna, a must visit place whenever you visiting Jaffna. Temple and its surroundings are huge.

Title: Gorgeous temple with beautiful murals
Text:
Can�t take photos inside, so wasn�t able to capture the murals. Was beautiful. Felt at peace and calm inside- even though we visited on a Friday- the temple is big enough to accommodate many comfortably.

Strongly recommend paying this temple a visit.

Title: Fascinating insight into the Hindu religion
Text:
This temple is most revered in Kaffna where the majority of the population are Hindu. We arrived for the morning 'puja' or service which is conducted at 10 every morning and it was very busy when we got there. There is a dress code, and for men this means both shoes off and bare chested, for women shoulders and legs covered.
It was extremely busy the day we visited and the roads had been closed round the temple for the crowds. The evening puja, around about 5 is even more busy. As we went round, the ceremonies started and although there were very few none Hindus there, no one seemed to mind us observing the proceedings, which were extremely colourful, noisy and seemed at times to unfamiliar eyes, to be a little bit chaotic.
Masses of incense, cleansing of the gods and a number of the congregation prostrating themselves on the floor, plus the elderly man we saw rolling on the ground all the way round the temple.
It was a really interesting and informative visit to a significant religious sight.

Title: A unique experience
Text: If you are a man,  be forewarned, you will be asked to remove your shirt as you enter this temple. It is an important temple, and very well kept up. The towers are beautiful. For me, the musicians at the front porch were the highlight. Grab a seat, join the audience, and discover a new world.

Title: must visit temple . popular place
Text: one of the popular in Asia. many tourist love to visit. The temple is clean and nice. One of the best place to visit.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: It is worth a tour: one of the biggest Hindu temples in Jaffna. Shoes have to stay outside and men have to put off their shirts. Wide area with several sections. You can see locals praying. People from the temple can answer our questions. Seems to be very important for the Hindu local population.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Beautiful Hindu temple, the largest in Jaffna. To go in you must wear conservative clothing, shoulders and legs covered. Very intricate decoration inside. A must visit if you are n Jaffna.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Beautiful, huge temple. At first we couldn't find the entrance, but we're happy we found it. They were performing a morning ritual when we visited which was very nice to see.

Title: Nallur temple
Text: The presiding deity is Lord Murugan. The temple is in Jaffna town only a few kilometers from the railway station or bus stand. By tuk tuk you pay 200 LKR one way. It is a big temple. The Gopuram or the towers at the entrance is impressive and is in golden colour. I was informed that the temple will close by 6 .p.m so went there at 3.30 and had to wait till 4 p.m. for the sanctum sanctorum to be opened. Males have to be bare bodied from waist upwards when you enter the temple.

Title: Amazing Hindu Temple
Text: Go during a daily ceremony. Men: Prepare to remove your shirt per requirements of facility. Amazing smells, beautiful temple, interesting sights. Worth a visit. Worth a tuk tuk ride there.

Title: Jaffna Nallur Kovil
Text: Iconic landmark in Jaffna....One of biggest hindu temple. you can always see huge crowd in Nallurkovil regardless of any seasons.

Title: Large temple, interesting for a few minutes
Text: There are dozens of temples scattered throughout Jaffna. This one is the biggest and while its interesting to look at, it isnt of the same calibre as those found in other parts of Asia. It felt disrespectful to hang around when people gathered for prayer, which the guidebooks suggest you do...

Title: What a beautiful temple - brilliant architecture
Text: It is quite a large complex and extremely well maintained. If visiting in the afternoon be sure to reach in time for the 4pm prayers and temple opening. The architecture is stunning inside and outside. Lovely interplay of light on the golden colours

Title: A nice temple
Text: I could not go inside as one has to remove his shirt while entering any temple in this part, somehow i was little uncomfortable, though it was a solo trip.

Title: Beautiful holy temple
Text: Took my mum back for the first time in 25 years. My first time visiting and I found it to be peaceful, clean and spiritual.

Title: Interior is awesome
Text: The most beautiful Hindu temple in Sri Lanka.Interior is awesome. The temple is so clean and peaceful. crowd people there during the festival.. it was big ceremony. hanging man is highlighted in this event.

Title: Must-Visit
Text: Nallur Kovil is the largest Hindu temple, in terms of area covered, in the whole of Sri Lanka, and is clearly an important place of worship to Jaffna Hindus. It is located a couple of km outside Jaffna centre, an easy bike ride along Temple Road (not sure where the name came from ??), in the sub-centre of Nallur, which served as the capital of the Jaffna kings from the 10th Century until the arrival of the Portuguese here in the late 16th century. The main temple building is massive, although quite dark and dingy in places. No photography is allowed inside, which is understandable but slightly regrettable in that there are some wonderful painted murals that I would have liked to share with others. Worshippers make a contribution of precisely 1 Rp (for which you even get a receipt!), which I think is a beautiful concept - it is the same for everyone, from pauper to president ?? Men must remove their shirts when entering this, or indeed any, Hindu temple. Well worth a visit for a moments quiet reflection amid the laid-back hustle and bustle of Jaffna city.

Title: Famous temple must visit!
Text: Very famous temple check opening times before visiting!  I think its between 9-11am and then later in the afternoon around 4-5ishpm.  Its beautiful inside and out, no shoes aloud, girls cover legs and arms and men have to go shirtless.

Title: An amazing insight into Hindu worship
Text:
We visited this place as part of a guided bicycle-tour of the city.
Our guide was Hindu and he invited me to go inside the temple. In order to this i was required not only to remove my foot-ware, but also to be naked above the belt.
It was visually spectacular, and most enlightening, for I had never before entered such a place.

Title: A must to visit
Text: This vast gold encrusted Hindu temple is centrally located and is enormous with lots to see. Shoes and shirts have to be removed

Title: Peaceful hindu temple, worth a visit
Text:
We arrived at about 2pm and were told the temple didn't open until 3pm, so if you want to see inside make sure you go later in the afternoon. We went for an ice cream and came back at 4 and the temple was open. It's definitely worth going during prayer time (4 to 5pm seems good). 

As mentioned by many, you need to take off your shoes and men need to remove their shirts. It was interesting to wander round and have a look inside. We asked but couldn't find any English speaking guides when we were there - I think that would really help you understand the rituals and areas of the temple.

Title: My Most Favourite Devotional Place in Jaffna
Text: One of Favourite, Devotional, Spiritual place in Jaffna, Peaceful Place in Srilanka, Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is one of the most significant Hindu temples in the Jaffna District of Northern Province, Sri Lanka, , Kindly visit Srilanka and Visit Jaffna,

Title: Centre of faith
Text: A beautiful temple wth Dravidian  architecture The temple Is a bit different from that in India .There is peace within

Title: A Famous ancient Hindu Temple in Jaffna Northern Sri Lanka.
Text:
I believe this temple steeped in history and venerated by almost all Hindus in Sri Lanka and probably known world wide was founded in 948AD, that is 1070 odd years ago. 
The grounds even after 30 plus years of an absolutely destructive civil war that engulfed this lovely peaceful Island Paradise of Sri Lanka (earlier known as Tabrobane and Ceylon) , well known as the Pearl of the Indian Ocean. Is quiet, peaceful and reflects the ancient origins of this must visit venue.

Title: Good to see
Text: Was closed so more of an opportunity to take photos. Quite amazing. Rent a bike and go if you're not scared of traffic, adds to the charm.

Title: Most sacred place
Text: This kovil is devoted to Hindu god Lord Murugan.  One of the most sacred places of worship for the Hindu people. Every year thousands of people and devotees are visiting the kovil. There are full of artwork and statues in the kovil. One of the most significant Hindu temple in Sri Lanka.

Title: Really beautiful Kovil and worth the visit
Text: We had been to a lot of Kovils in our Sri Lanka stay but I must admit this one was particularly beautiful.The inside is opulent in reds and golds with vaulted arch ceilings.Stunning.Free entry and worth the visit in Jaffna

Title: Awesome looking temple
Text: Unfortunately the interior of the temple was closed when i visited, but i was able to walk the grounds for some great views of the exterior buildings.  The art is amazing.  Be forewarned, you must remove shoes before entering the grounds, and the sand is quite hot in the sun.

Title: Temple
Text: Had a good view in the evening. It is an ancient temple and quite nicely done up. Not very strict dress regulations except that men need to take off their shirts.

Title: Heart of the Jaffna
Text: Located in jaffna town and its like the heart of jaffna. Many Hindus come for this place every day. You have to wear a proper dress and males have to unress the top

Title: Secret place for Hindu... need to remove your shirt to enter
Text:
Its a religious place nice and well maintained. If you are visiting Jaffna go there make a wish n go... 
no cameras allowed inside temple/kovil

Title: Amazing temple
Text: This temple is dedicated to Kandaswamy or Murugan, the 2nd son of Shiva. Not only is it a beautiful temple, the rituals are done in the most amazing manner. Try to be there by 5.30 pm to witness the idol being brought in a chariot and taken to the "palliyarai" or resting chamber.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text:
Came here with the family. Just to say you have to take your shirt off to go inside.
There are really good sculptures all around.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: The Nallur Kovil is a very big temple but you can only visit a small portion of it and pictures are forbidden inside. Its a beautiful building and best in the afternoon so after your visit you can enjoy a good ice cream nearby.

Title: Visit to Nallur temple
Text:
If was amazing if you visit Jaffna in Srilanka you should visit this amazing place 
Devotees waiting for Poona performance and men half bare bodied waking around with silence is quite breathtaking

Title: MUST SEE TEMPLE
Text: Our first visit the day after we arrived in Jaffna. Beautiful temple. calm and serene. surely a must visit.

Title: Really impressive Hindu temple
Text: First time tried to get in it was closed. We returned at 3.30pm and it was open. People were coming in, music being played; the atmosphere was good. Men have have to take their shirts off as well as hats etc. We had a good look round and I rate it one of the best temples I have visited.

Title: Hindu
Text: This is the main and popular  Hindu temple here. A beautiful architectural temple. The annual festival attracts lots of Hindus from all over.

Title: A beautiful temple
Text: You must visit this temple when you come to Jaffna. A very historically significant temple in Sri Lankan history. We arrived in time for the puja which was very moving to watch.

Title: Rich history and quite popular
Text: This is a very old temple which has references in texts like Mahavamsa and Yalpana Vaibhava Malai. The idol is supposed to be fabricated in India and shipped to Gangesanthurai by a Pandya king. It is quite ornate and exceptionally calm. The quality of the structure has not been affected by decades of unrest in this area which itself is a minor miracle. A must visit if you are in Jaffna

Title: Beautiful and interesting Tamil Hindu temple
Text: It's interesting to stay inside for a while and watch a few different ceremonies. Men should take off theirs shirts in entering.

Title: Famous Hindu Kovil in Jaffna
Text: This is a very famous kovil in Jaffna city. Not far away from the railway station. This is a massive Kovil. Very colorful & attractive kovil.

Title: Mesmerizing
Text: The kovil is impressive and is a landmark of Jaffna. Hindu devotees worship the place and is a busy place.

Title: Sacred Hindu temple in Jaffna.
Text: As the festival is on to celebrate and observe the powers of Lord Murugan, there was a large gathering of devotees. Must enter with bare feet and males must go in to the temple without any clothing to the upper body- bare chest. mirror pieces enclosed golden colour decorated walls give an extra majestic appearance due to the height of levels. Music and sermons continuing with beautifully decorated statues and flags. Huge complex guarded by Police and devotees them selves it is open to anyone who wants to visit.

Title: Nallur Festival.
Text: We visited the temple during the annual festival. It was an experience we'll never forget. A once in a lifetime experience.

Title: Amazing Structure
Text:
Nallur Kovi is an amazing. Colourful with lots of gold details.
Don't go when its hot as there is a long barefoot walk to the kovi. The feet got really burnt.
Remember to wear appropriate clothing which is legs and shoulders covered.

Title: Surreal
Text: Beautiful Temple. Absolutely calm and what a surreal experience. Must visit when in Jaffna, one of the most popular temples in the country.

Title: Hindu Temple
Text: A beautiful temple in the centre of Jaffna. It was in fact one of the biggest temples I have seen in Sri Lanka. A very calm and peaceful environment

Title: Auspicious and stunning!
Text: Amazing architecture and a very beautiful temple to visit. Definitely recommend people to visit at least once in a their life times.

Title: Good vibes
Text:
We walked in at the evening pooja time @ 5pm and it was simply amazing....somewhat of a modern-ish building there are numerous shrines located throughout the temple althogh the main temple is dedicated to Lord Murugan 
Photographs are not allowed inside and they may even put your camera in a cloth bag & tie up if they feel pictures will be taken
Traditional attire or covered shirts & long skirts / pants are recommended

Title: Hindu temple
Text: An amazing temple painted in gold .. dedicated to many gods, deities? You walked barefoot in the sand and round the temple . Lovely chanting going on... magical. Lots of old men in dhotis lying around chatting. A peaceful place.

Title: Fantastic temple
Text: An amazing temple. Probably the finest southern Indian style temple in Sri Lanka.  Men must take their shirts off to visit

Title: "???????" Nallur Temple
Text: Nallur hindu temple is a socially important institution for the jaffna Tamils. Beautiful  temple architectur. The poja was conducted with strict discipiline of timing . Nallur is one of the Sympolic Hindu building of Ceylon-tamils who are scattered and dispersed around the globe.

Title: Definitely worth seeing
Text: I havent been to India, so for those who have maybe this wont seem as grand. I was there and able to see the poojahs, stand there with my belly out and try not to be too embarrassed because all the old dudes like me did the same. Anyway, quite a scene.  No photography.

Title: Exquisite
Text: Truly an amazing temple, we admired its architectural beauty & pious ambience. Impresses you even as you catch a glimpse from afar.

Title: Immersive and fascinating temple
Text:
Nallur is a fascinating example of Hindu temple in Sri Lanka. We visited during afternoon puja (around 4pm) and felt very welcomed in by locals partaking in devotion. 

An incredible opportunity to see the fascinating rituals performed at the temple. Was really mind blowing!

Men need to remove their shirts upon entry and as usual modest clothing should be worn (trousers/long shorts and sleeved tops for women).

Title: building, the work on the building,  the way they built
Text: This is one of the MUST see temple to see.  You Must gi inside to view the work has been done many many years back

Title: A great religious place
Text: The Architecture, carvings etc are amazing and beautiful. It is quite a busy place with many coming to worship and for religious vows. But once you enter it is very serene and clearly is holy place. Even if you are not a Hindu please try and visit to see the beauty and serenity.

Title: Beautiful Temple
Text: Must visit place to visit in Jaffna. The payment for pooja was only rs1 and the temple is  tourist friendly-helpful with information and guidance.

Title: Festival Time
Text:
We experienced this vast Temple in the evening of an annual Hindu Festival. For men and boys this meant, long white sarong and bare torso and feet. The sand and floors clean and cool to walk on in the approach to the various alters and beautifully forged and carved gods. A spiritually charged and powerful encounter. Although there were thousands of devotees there, I never felt huddled or overwhelmed in the vast openness of the temple interiors. 
Outside the streets were thronged with people gently carousing and celebrating in the brightly lit and decorated street stalls set up for the occasion and selling everything from peanuts to saris. Even on a quiet day I imagine this temple a wonder that is well worth the visit.

Title: Interesting Hindu temple
Text: As always, there's so much to see in a Hindu temple and this one's no exception. Men need to take of their shirts before entering. No pictures allowed.

Title: My favourite temple in Sri Lanka
Text: This temple is amazing. If you are in Jaffna you should visit this temple. It was a very interesting, clean, big and beautifu temple. It was also the first Hindu temple I've seen so quite an experience.

Title: Very nice Hindu temple.
Text:
Must visit this place. specially in august festival time. whole area is full of ppls and shops.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION: The Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is one of Jaffnas most significant Hindu temples and is the fourth re-built structure, since the original temple was built in 948. The temple is a socially important institution for the Sri Lankan Tamils Hindu identity of north Sri Lanka and for the Sri Lankan Tamil diaspora. Located in the ancient capital town of Nallur in Jaffna, it is recorded that the center of the city was once a bustling market place, surrounded by a square fortification that sheltered courtly buildings for kings, Brahmin priests and soldiers. The old Nallur Kandaswamy temple functioned within this ancient defensive fort, among a city that was laid out like the traditional temple town according to Hindu traditions.

Title: Worship Temple
Text: We went there about 2 weeks ago. The temple is very big and beautiful. It's a very famous temple in Jaffna. We went during the festival, so it was crowded. We went inside and saw that it is very clean. Because of the festival, there were many small shops.

Title: Amazing expericence
Text: This temple was different experience, but worth of visiting. Getting knowledge about other religion makes people more open minded, make sure to visit this temple when you are in Jaffna!

Title: Beautiful Temple - Make sure to come here during the festival period in August
Text:
A beautiful temple with gold gilded interior. 

Warning: Men must remove shirt to enter the temple.

We were here for the festival. The nightly festival starts at 16:15 and ends around 19:00 and that is when the temple closes. It is a not-to-miss event in Jaffna. In fact, we came to Jaffna specifically to check out this event and it was worth trip. Highly recommend it. I suggest to check it out before the secret gets out and turn Jaffna into another tourism madhouse.

Title: A must
Text: Busy, interesting and easily reached. Buy some incense sticks to burn from outside to enhance your experience.

Title: Huge Hindu Temple
Text:
The Namur Kovil has to be one of the must see places in Jaffna.   Huge and fascinating!   Beautifully painted frescoes.  It is under some renovation and so perhaps a tad dustier and noisy than usual.  Men must remove their shirts and everyone as is usual, must remove foot ware.
Some gentlemen were seated and meditating and others offered smiles.  It felt welcoming to strangers, believers and those who didn't believe.
I realised how little I understood about Hindu deities!

Title: A Huge and Beautiful Lord Murugan Temple
Text: It's a beautiful Lord Murugan temple, located on very large grounds. The temple gives you a special feeling that you will instantly feel. We were there for the morning prayers which was about 10.30 am. Men have to remove their shirts wen they enter this temple. After the pooja, it makes you fulfilled with Lord Muruga's blessings

Title: Famous and important shrine
Text: One of the most famous and important Hindu shrines in Sri Lanka. It's open (and most rewarding) during puja, around 17.00 in the afternoon. There are ice cream parlours on the main street nearby.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: The temple is huge. We could experience poya at 5pm, try to be there at that time so you can enjoy the traditional show. I liked the decorations as well.

Title: Very beautiful recent temple
Text: This temple is really huge and very beautiful. We really felt welcomed there and attended to a special celebration. Good vibes !

Title: Try to be there at 5pm
Text:
On arrival at 4.45pm, we were told that males could not enter the temple wearing shirts, so we women covered our legs and the men all went in bare-chested. At 5pm the most spectacular ceremony began, with everyone following a procession of musicians and flame carriers all round the temple. Lasting about half an hour, it was loud, lively and exciting. 

The temple itself is very ornate and well worth a visit, but it would be a shame to mis the daily ceremony.

Title: Historical temple with a famous festival for Lord Skanda.
Text: The temple is well maintained.  But is not open at all times.  It is good to attend the festival to learn more about Jaffna Tamil Hindu culture.  Many small shops within walking distance.

Title: A must visit Kovil in Jaffna
Text: One of the biggest or the biggest kovil in Sri Lanka. P.S ; Men have to remove their shirts/t shirts when entering the kovil.

Title: An imposing building.
Text: This is a beautiful temple and the largest I visited in Sri Lanka.  Considering the troubles during the war it is in beautiful condition.  The murals on the wall are bright and descriptive and the temple is a haven of peace after the streets outside.

Title: An interesting temple to visit especially during puja
Text:
A big Hindu temple with a very well-attended puja in the late afternoon which I think is the best time to visit.

The local devotees are friendly and after puja some are willing to spend time explaining the ceremony.

It's a big temple with lots of different shrines inside. Definitely an interesting place to visit.

Title: Simply beautiful
Text:
A major temple in Jaffna with impressive architecture, interesting history and significant following.

We visited the premises during poya and, being quite ignorant of hinduism altogether, we were quite transfixed with the mystical worship, mixing chanting, hidden and exposed lights, gongs, colours, smells ...

Photography is forbidden inside, so the beautiful frescoes that line all around  the temples yards are for the eyes only.
But photographers (and all) can marvel at the temple in the stunning descending light, basking the sculpted kovil in warmth and golden magic.

Men are expected to be bare-chested to visit the temple.

Title: Pretty impressive
Text: Went here as part of our list of places to visit via tuk tuk. Pretty impressive. No guide or anything in English to explain it

Title: A lot of history in Nallur Temple
Text: Beautiful paintings which tell the stories of hindu Gods;  The walk around the inner courtyard of the temple is pleasant and breezy. The architecture is amazing.

Title: Fantastic!
Text: This ancient temple has an atmosphere of deep serenity and restfulness. The architecture is interesting and heavily detailed. We attended the evening puja, following the priests from sanctum to sanctum. It was a lovely experience spiritual experience. Highly recommended.

Title: Great experience!!
Text: Go to this beautiful, colorful and well-smelling temple during the many rituals daily!! I went there between 16h and 17h, as indicated in Rough Guide, and it was really a great experience for all my senses!! Men have to take off their t-shirts and everyone have to enter without shoes (if you don't like to be without shoes, bring a pair of socks).

Title: Interesting
Text:
This is one of the most sacred Hindu temples in Jaffna. It is huge and well maintained. You will see a number of devotees in the premises at any given time. The inside features many statues of Hindu deities.
But the highlight for me was the music. There was a group of devotees who were singing and playing traditional Tamil musical instruments at the entrance of this Kovil. The music was simply magical.

Title: Biggest temple I've been to
Text: The work that was put into creating this temple is astonishing. Anyone in the area shouldn't miss out. The only thing to keep in mind is that men are requested to remove their shirt

Title: Beautiful Murgan Temple
Text: Not far from the city center.  Beautiful architecture. This temple is part of the Tamil culture.  Visitors must follow the dress codes.

Title: Holiday sightseeing
Text: Got chased out of temple by a rude priest.shouting at tourist who tried to see the temple.not much to see here.walking on hot sand  was so uncomfortable.

Title: Splendour of Nallur
Text: Visiting the Nallur temple on the morning of thai pongal day was very fulfilling. We witnessed the special poosai (offering) and the "swamy oorvalam" (procession). The majesty and the beauty of temple is simply breathtaking.

Title: Historic Temple
Text: Having withstood the perils of war, this beautiful temple is a must visit , if you ever find yourself in the city of Jaffna.

Title: Nallur Kovil, Jaffna
Text: Nice temple spread across a vast piece of land in the middle of the city. Very neat and clean. Men have to remove their shirts to go in.

Title: Nallur Kovil
Text: Best place in Jaffna for Hindus and the like to go to pray, very clean and everything happens to accurate timings. Good décor and good surroundings giving excellent  conditions for meditations and prayers.

Title: Great mid morning visit
Text: Nallur Kovil temple is a lovely complex to visit with Gopuram that unique compared to the very colourful ones that I have visited previously in the region. Inside is peaceful and a great place to wonder about lost in your thoughts.

Title: A special temple worth visiting
Text:
A enormous Hindu temple just north of the Jaffna City centre.
It's a wonderful experience to visit during the offering ceremonies held at different times during the day.
Temple is closed outside of these
Should cost around 150 in a tuk tuk one way from the city centre.

Title: Well worth a visit
Text:
If you are in Jaffna I think this is a must.
It is a well-known and renowned place of Hindu worship. It is situated in the heart of Jaffna, and what is extraordinary about it's décor architecture and fittings is the overlay of gold over everything there. The walls, ceiling , pillars, statures and painting are all covered in gold, but they do not look garish or gaudy, convey a special aurora that does not take away it's ambience as a place of worship. You are allowed to walk around at will, with bare feet and males need to shirts and any upper clothing.
Visitors need to be quiet and respectful, remembering that this a special place of worship.
If you can take someone who can tell you the tales and meanings of the pictures and etchings and statutes , then you will make your visit more meaningful'

Title: Worth seeing
Text: We arrived just before 4pm so we got in on time for the ceremony. It is a beautiful temple and much bigger than I expected. The paintings at the walls were really interesting and you can also see some peacocks on the side of the temple if you are lucky.

Title: Nice but nothing special
Text: The temple appears to be a bit neglected but still we did not see much of an architectural feat or other significance. Its a place to visit if you have time on your schedule but there are many other places which are worth visiting.

Title: Historical sacred Hindu temple
Text: Very serene. All males are required to enter the temple without any upper garment. And no photos inside

Title: Pleasant

Text:
This Kovil is a beautiful place, obviously sacred to Hindu worshippers. 

A kind man (priest?) took the time to put ash and a dot on our foreheads.

Title: Nallur Kovil
Text: It is a huge temple and beautifull atmosphere. The inside of the temple is clean and peaceful. Was very impressed.

Title: Hindoe tempel nr 1
Text: Looks great and has a majestic sense to it. You need to leave your shoes behind. And if a man wants to enter the tempel take off your t shirt. Beautiful paintings on the wall. They are renovating this place. We walked and we did not have to pay entrance fee or a donation. Recommended to see this place, 1 hour max.

Title: Holy of holys.
Text:
This is a very important site for Hindus and all males have to strip to the waist. As non-Hindus we were tolerated but more or less ignored by the throngs of worshipers. Inside to place is huge with a central bathing pool.
Worship at 5 PM was accompanied by much clanging of bells.

Title: Lovely temple
Text: One of the most beautiful temple I have seen outside India. The architecture is lovely. You will need to go to the temple before the sun sets as the temple is very dimly lit.

Title: Fantastic! So worth a trip!
Text: We loved the Nallur Temple! For anyone visiting Jaffna this is a must see! It's beautiful to look at both inside and out, lovely and peaceful to wander around.

Title: Amazing!
Text: Went during the time of Aarti. Beautiful temple brimming with devotees. Oil lamps. Drums and the traditional music made this an wonderful visit. Must see!

Title: Nallur Kovil: An architectural piece of Jaffna Kingdom.
Text:
One of the beautiful experiences I had in Jaffna.
The aesthetic views, the exquisite craftsmanship, the  towering gopuras, the ambience - everything is so perfect.
 The temple is dedicated to Kandaswamy (murugan) and once you move through the circum ambulatory space you can see the sub shrines aligned along your pathway. There is a central courtyard in the temple complex along  with a temple tank.

You can take a point pedro bus from the jaffna main bus stand and get down in front of the temple.
I went around 5.00pm in the evening  and the temple against the setting sun was a entrancing site. If possible i would suggest you to visit around this time.

PS: males have to remove their shirts before entering into the temple and they don't let you in short skirts or shorts.

Title: Nice temple but parts under construction
Text:
It's a colourfull, big and very nice temple. There are not that many tourists because most of them dont visit the north! There are only a lot of Sri Lankan people! 
When you enter the temple men should take of their shirt and woman should cover shoulders and ofcourse you should take your shoes off.
We think it's worth the visit.

Title: Beautiful Experience
Text:
We visited here during the festival in August. 

It is such a beautiful temple. Neither me or any of my party practice Hindu, none the less, the experience was amazing. We arrived at 11am and stayed about an hour, taking in everything and observing the dedication of everybody that was attending.

Seeing it again in the night time was such an experience. Seeing it all lit up with all the worshippers. Again, it was just an amazing experience.

As with all temples, you must remove your shoes before entering. Men must remove their shirts and women must wear modest clothing.

Title: Hindu temple with 25 days of festivities
Text:
The Nallur Kovil is one of the most significant Hindu temples in the Jaffna peninsula. We went to one of the festivities in August - part of a 25-day series. It was interesting to see the procession with lots of music, and subsequently in the evening when the temple was already closed the celebrations continued (but not for very long). Note that all visitors are expected to take off their shoes and men also their shirts when they enter the temple. 
Also no pictures inside the temple.

Title: Truly intriguing ceremony, must see in Jaffna
Text: I am not surprised this attraction is number one on TripAdvisor for Jaffna. I have never been to India and the only other Hindu temples I visited were in Jaffna. And this one was by far the most beautiful. Go there at the right time for the procession which occurs several times daily (ours was at 5pm). You will have of course to take off your shoes and cover yourself if you are a woman or take off your shirt if you are man. It's amazing how so many devotee are coming to this place everyday. It's not just a museum, it's a real life place.

Title: Beautiful magnificent temple
Text: Well maintained temple in Jaffna. Dedicated to Allangkara Kanthan. Orderly place of worship. You're not allowed to photograph or take video inside the temple. Men have to remove shirt before entering the temple.

Title: Beautiful Hindu Kovil
Text: A very beautiful Hindu temple to visit while in Jaffna. For someone in the US, this was a very informative visit to see the inside of a Hindu temple.

Title: Gold
Text: Makes a change to see a temple gold & not brightly coloured,try to put your shoes in a bag hidden as they ask you to leave them quite away from entrance also no photos allowed

Title: Place of worship
Text: Popular Murugan temple to visit. We went for the 10am pooja time and it is great to see the time management of the pooja.

Title: Lovely temple
Text: This was our first visit to a temple in Sri Lanka and we were not disappointed, this one set us up for our visit to the Nagadeepa temple on the peninsula

Title: Fantastic visit to our first Hindu Temple. Nallur Kandaswamy temple
Text:
We were not sure of procedure or how to approach our visit to this temple.  However, we did our research and donned a sarong to cover our lower half.  The Hindu Temple Nallur Kandaswamy temple is situated in the not so tourist area of Jaffna. Visitors before entering the Temple complex must remove their shoes; men need to remove their shirts as well.  

The Temple is about 1.5km northeast of the centre. It is exceptionally beautifully colourful, as one would expect from a Hindu Temple dedicated to sacred deity is Lord Murugan (or Skanda).  

One thing that struck me was the friendliness of the devotees and visitors entering the Temple complex.  Even though we could not speak Tamil or Sinhalese the people actually pushed us into places where we could view the ceremony of the "Puja" and then took us by hand to the following 3 or 4 places so as we could be and feel integrated into the ceremonial process. 

In western religions it's normally first come first served and you're pushed out of the way by the surge of petitions and penitents trying to gain a favour or miracle from the devotion.  But here the people were so keen for us to see the adoration of their gods and the ceremony unfold that we were at times led by the hand to "the next installment" - for want of a better phrase.  

Then once the ceremony had finished we wandered around the Temple complex and some visitors - from the southern part of India,  took us to one side and helped us understand what we had just witnessed  

Several friendly priests, some of whom speak English, can answer questions about the temple and its traditions. Do go to this and any Temple that you find near you on your visits and be inspired and blessed as we were that day at The Nallur Kandaswamy Temple.

Title: Most Popular Temple in Jaffna
Text: The temple is spacious and the inner architecture is excellent. The surroundings are calm, quiet making you feel the peacefulness of mind and body. It is to be visited before 1730 hours after which it is closed.

Title: Hindu Temple
Text:
Very famous in North part of Sri Lanka. Must see place for believers and none believers. 
Have accommodation and vegetarian food outlet available nearby. Best to avoid busy period in the evening due to amount of people visit the place at one time. Very good experience. Must follow rules regards to outfit you wear.

Title: A holy place
Text: High religious significance. But there is not much else from a non-religious point of view. Not a touristy place.

Title: Dont elave Jaffna without visiting
Text: A huge temple in Jaffna. Amazing intricate designs inside. Men have to remove their shirts befoer they are allowed to enter.

Title: A must visit while in Jaffna town
Text:
We spent two days in around  Jaffna town. The Nallur Kovil ( Hindu temple) is in the center of town and easily the main attraction.  Recently restored and  repainted with a magnificent central shrine and several smaller shrines in the perimeter of the main shrine. try to coordinate visit with a time of "pooja" ceremony ( several times per day morning and evenings) when the priests offer prayers and offerings on behalf of the devotees gathered. This is done to the accompaniment of traditional music ( drums and long flute ) providing atmosphere and charm. After the pooja ceremony take time to walk around the inner perimeter of the main temple, with long corridors in classical style to take in the several large murals and carved stone statues depicting other gods and goddesses exquisitely done in gold and vivid colors.  Also take note of the 20 foot carved wooden doors at each of the entrances and the "gopurams" towers that painted in gold.  Striking are the two newer gopurams on the north and south completed recently.  to enter the temple you must go barefooted and males must be bare waist up. No photography.
 Outside and in the surrounding streets outside this temple are several smaller "kovils"  that also prvide interesting viewing and early morning "poojas".  Well worth a visit to this vicinity...  devote about 1-2 hours

Title: Beautiful , well kept temple
Text: Sprawling temple complex.  Well coordinated crowd management . Beautiful architecture . Devotional and visual treat.

Title: Top thing in Jaffna
Text: There's a dearth of interesting things to do and see in Jaffna, but this is definitely the top thing. The temple is an interesting shade of beige that blends in well with the surrounding. This is also one of the few Hindu temples where non-Hindus can enter the inner sanctum. Men do have to take their top off though and I didn't need a 2nd excuse.

Title: Pretty amazing....
Text: You need to check when it is open - we turned up at 14:00 and were told to come back at 15:00 when the gates were still locked  but we slipped through a hole in the fence and off we went.    No problem at all - they had just forgotten to unlock the gates.    Men have to remove their shirts to go in - much more relaxed for women - and it is a working, functioning temple.     I would suggest you aim for arriving at about 15:50 and stay until about 16:40 when the band strikes up and the bells are rung.   The place comes to life (sort of) between these times.    Otherwise you will just wander around and look at the (very impressive insides.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text:
Enormous and stunning temple. However, it is only open at time of worship so be sure to double check when it will be open if you want to go inside. It is definitely open at 4pm.
There are a number of restaurants close by and a few ice cream parlours.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Was the first Hindu temple I went to, and wow oh wow. It was huge, and we went around half 5, and there was a ceremony going on for one of the gods and was amazing to watch. It's beautiful on the inside, and very different from the Buddhist temple I had been used to seeing. Well worth the visit!

Title: Imposing, colorful structure
Text: Big, South Indian temple with a colorful, imposing Gopuram (gate). One can take a bus from downtown Jaffna (the same bus thatgoes to Point Pedro) and get off in front of the temple.

Title: another temple
Text: I admit up front that I'm not into Hindu temples. This was an obligatory stop for seeing the main things in Jaffna.

Text: According to the tour guide, this Kovil was founded in 950 AD with the current structure being developed in the 1700s. It can get loud and bustling during the prayer times but besides that it can be incredibly peaceful to walk in and around the place. Keep in mind that it is a holy shrine so be respectful of your surroundings, particularly when it comes to taking photographs and videos and also dress requirements, (covered legs and cleavage for women, nothing covering the top for men and bare feet).

Text: Was a special place and enjoyed the visit to this majestic temple. It it full of vibrant colors and a very spiritual place for Hindu devotees

Text: Very clear secluded sacred area - well maintained. Very Punctual Prayer functions - quite likable. Festive seasons are a real Gift to watch and enjoy and get spiritual enlightenment

Text: The temple is Ok, but nothing if you compare with tamil temples in Tamil Nadu, since this Nallur is quiet modern as a building. But it is the main attraction in Jaffna and pujas are performed often in the evening. Priests are friendly and helpful with the tourists

Title: Jaffna icon
Text:
A temple with a lot of history and great structure of gods and goddesses.
Going during the prayer times would be interesting with crowds walking from one god to another with priests chanting and performing different rituals.

Title: Nallur Hindu Temple evening puja
Text: Yes indeed, this is for connoisseurs....to see the God of Kataragama, (Murugan)  lifted from his place in the main concourse and placed gently on a little cart which is pulled  by two men stripped to the waist round the temple while a brahmin priest wafts a whisk to keep the flies and other desecrations off the God and then He is placed reverently between his two Wives in a side chapel so He can spend the night with Them...and the gold of the gopuram in the early morning or early evening light of a low lying sun!!

Title: Magnificent temple not to be missed
Text: Temple is still being renovated but you can  still marvel at its architectural beauty & lovely murals.  You may be lucky to see one of the several puja ceremonies.  Unfortunately, no picture-taking inside.

Title: It's not wat you expect
Text:
