Outside the temple, the nice sculptures the Hindu temples are so famous for, are painted in one colour.

Text:
This temple is open early 4:30 AM and closes 5:45 PM.  plan accordingly. Easily accessible, and a must see in Jaffna.

The temple has a huge building.

Text: If you visited Hindu temples in South India like Madurai Meenatchi Amman, Srirangam, Thanjavur Kovil, this temple not impressive. Title: Spectacular building, incredible energy
Text:
Be sure to visit while a puja is happening (5am, 10am, noon, 415pm, 430pm, 5pm and 645pm).  This is a spectacular building, both from the outside and the inside.  You'll need to remove your shoes to enter.  (take them with you or leave them at the gate).  Men need to remove their shirts to enter the temple (tuck it in your waistband at the front of your trousers).  Women need either a skirt or long trousers and long sleeves.

Don't be afraid to join in, the locals will put you right straight away if you do something wrong or watch them first.   We entered and immediately were pushed along with the crowd - where women and men were separated and walking bakcwards, we walked in front of the deity as it was borne around the inside of the temple.   The deity is lit up (electric lights, as there's a small generator following it round), and there are frequent stops and offerings.   It's a magnificent spectacle - no one looks bored and everyone is engaged.

The ceremony is noisy, - with drums, with wind instruments and with worshippers getting involved.  Let the noise and the experience wash over you - its like a healing ceremony, as it was explained to us.  Believers come as often as they need, to soak in the atmosphere of the ceremony and if you do come along during the ceremony you'll feel it all resonate through you.

There are no photos allowed inside the temple and there were no social conversations, this was about the ceremony.

Text: Superb with the front view and interior also massive and it has marvelous paintings on wall.it is great cultural value for jaffna

Text:

It is known to be quite accurate on timing, so make sure to come on time for the puja (around 5:00-6:00pm evening puja).

Title: Fantastic temple in good location
Text: Jaffna doesn't offer a lot of sights for tourists to see and for me this is its only real attraction. A great Hindu Temple with market streets leading to it. The Police are friendly and eager to know where you are from and are proud of there temple. Inside looks even better then the outside, but you cannot take photo's inside the temple. The locals go about praying, All men have to be shirtless, including any Police inside. The best place to visit in Jaffna

Text: The interior of the Kovil was very grand and majestic. The gopurams (at the entrance) were quite elaborate and high. They were like masterpieces. The pooja happens only during a few times of the day so inquire about the times if you wish to be there to witness a pooja. We went on a Saturday for an evening pooja at 5pm.

Title: Stunning, Unique
Text: Possibly the most beautiful gopuram I've ever seen and the temple is fascinating. This one is far better ( and cleaner) than the big one to the north ( reached by bus an ferry) Gents must remove shirts,

Title: Impressing!
Text: This Hindu temple is right on par with all the great Buddism temples on the island. It gives an intriguing view on the daily Hindu rituals and shows off a beautiful layout and a collection of impressive shrines. Do make sure to visit between 4pm and 5pm to experience the most impressive rituals that take place daily. Too bad you aren't allowed to take pictures insides because this is a true photogenic place! And men: you have to take off not just your shoes but also shirt, so be prepared ;)

Title: Majestic grandeur
Text: Impressive temple. Definetely a must see if you're in Jaffna. No footwear allowed inside. Unfortunate that no photos are allowed to be taken as I would have loved to capture the splendour of the interior.

Title: Best Hindu temple
Text: We have traveled extensively around southern India and this temple is as good if not better. A must do when in Jaffna. We took a Tuk tuk on the way to our guest house. Only 3km from city centre. Don't forget to take off your shirt gents.

Title: Peaceful
Text: Check on time of being open. Closed between 12.00 and 15.00. Have lunch first at Mango Restaurant near by. Remember that all shoes removed and males remove shirt. Highly decorated Hindu temple and large. Very peaceful surroundings and ideal for meditation.

Title: Impressive temple
Text: The temple is large with impresive gopuram. Visit is topless for men and unfortunately no pictures allowed inside

Title: Slightly tourist targeting temple
Text: As a Hindu I found this temple a little more tourist attraction than spiritual sanctuary. It is worth a visit as it's quite a large temple but for divine inspiration I preferred the the Veera Amman temple down the road.

Title: The most beautiful Hindu Temple in Jaffna
Text: This is the most beautiful Hindu Temple in Jaffna.Not allowed to take photographs. Men are required to take off their shirts before entering the temple.

Title: Nice evening at Temple.
Text: After rent a bicycle from travel desk jaffna, (you can also hire motobike there) me and my friend went to fort, jaffna market , Buddhist temple finally arrived to Nallur in the evening. The travel guide was friendly and helpful. There are very interesting art on the wall inside of the temple. Unfortunately photography is not allowed inside the temple. We have enjoyed Rio Ice cream behind the temple. It was delicious.

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: A big temple built many years ago. Dedicated to Lord Murugan, the architecture deserves recognition. Be cautious about the temple visiting times though.

Title: beautiful kovil
Text: surprisingly beautiful piece of art in this northern part of Sri Lanka. The innerside is fantastic but often closed for visitors. When we came, with quite a group, they closed it just in front of us and only opened 2 hours later.

Title: A must see in Jaffna
Text:
Fascinating and atmospheric place of worship ... Astonished at the size and elaborate interior of the temple . 
Buy a coconut to crack on the wood before entering .. Walk round with your right side to the main interior  temple area
Purchase a 1 rupee ticket to give to the swami who will offer a prayer chant for a family or person .. Tell him their name..

Title: Got to visit to see and get the real feel
Text:
This Murugan Kovil is peas and calm. This is one of the biggest temple in Jaffna with a massive festival which lasts for nearly 27 days (I am not exact with this number but close) Festival time can be very crowded but worth a visit with family.

I have been visiting this temple since 70's and the temple has not changed much, the ticket for pooja is still Rs1 but the festival stalls has changed a lot to keep up with the need. On my last visit I was able to see remote controlled cars, Pizza and donut stalls.

If you ever go to Jaffna do visit this temple. Please obey the local rules in going into the temple.

Title: Moving place
Text: Very attractive and impressive religious place with access to all. Need a bit of parking space on a crowded day I believe. We went early around 3.30 PM before the pooja starts, hence it was  quiet. Must visit attraction in Jaffna.

Title: Famous
Text: This is a famous big beautiful kovil. The annual ther festival is very popular with Hindus in the north of Srilanka.

Title: Sacred place
Text:
An important Hindu temple in Jaffna, that if quite impressive and transporting.

Beautiful carvings and art work throughout the large site.

Respectful visitors should remember to dress appropriately (modest attire, long pants, covered shoulders for ladies, men must remove their shirts, and not footwear, no hats).

Also keep in mind it closes from noon to 3 pm. We did not realize this and had to cut our visit short.

Title: Great to see after 50 yrs
Text:
Would be good to have info and guide for non culturally attuned visitors. 
From memory some of the shops around seem to have proliferated in recent times and detract from the holiness of the place

Title: Great historic temple
Text: This temple is the number 1 tourist spot in jaffna.  Locals and tourists visit this famous murugan temple when they go to jaffna.  All are welcome and the temple is open from 6am to 6pm everyday.  Males need to remove their shirt before entering the temple.  The most interesting routine everyday is the taking of the statue of murugan to sleep at the back room. This is performed at 6pm everyday and it's quite interesting to watch the ceremony.  It's free entry to the temple and its a very clean and well maintained temple.

Title: What a shame
Text: This is a beautiful temple and we have visited many times . Never have I been treated so rudely as I was on our last visit anywhere before. . I was pounced on as soon as I set foot on the threshold (I had just put my phone and camera in the bag before entering - well aware of the no photo rule) The priest demanded I removed my phone and camera, took them off me and looked through. No photos - no apology and to make matters worse followed me around the temple. How sad I could not enjoy my visit

Title: A very strange experience
Text:
We visited during the festival in August 2019.  The roads around the temple were blocked to traffic and we were not allowed past these blockades wearing hats or shoes.  Oddly, once the festival is over there is no problem in wearing hats and shoes on these roads. Seems that these roads are only scared during the festival!!

Males have to remove shirts to enter the temple and photos inside the temple are not permitted.  People outside the temple were smashing coconuts on a rock, and some devotees were rolling around the temple site chanting.

Overall, a very strange experience.

Title: Stunning temple....
Text: We arrived just after the Nallur festival and the temple was open to everyone. Men were asked to remove their shirts but other than that all that was required was quiet respect. the temple is large and ornate and coversquite a big area. The two tall structures either side of the kovil are very intricate and ornate. This temple is well worth the trip to Jaffna

Title: Beautiful Hindu temple
Text:
This is one of the more impressive Hindu temples I visited in Sri Lanka in terms of size and presentation. It stands out for me for the reliance on gold and more subdued colours externally than others Ive visited.  Inside was less subdued and had the burst of colour and polished metals that is seen in other temples visited. 

A must do in Jaffna

Title: Beautiful temple
Text: Nallur Kandaswamy Temple is an old beautiful temple in Jaffna. photography is strictly prohibited inside. It has a wonderful archy interior with paintings on the walls depicting stories from Hindu mythology. They follow strict temple timings for pooja. There is a silver and gold chariot which is taken out on special festival days. Tamils and Sinhalese both come in large numbers. Must visit.

Title: A fascinating experience
Text: For anyone with an interest in culture, architecture or religious shrines this is a must visit.  It is worth going with a guide who can explain the Hindu rites that are taking place.

Title: Nothing special
Text: The building looks interesting. Worth a visit only if you happen to be in the area. Not really worth a detour.

Title: Interesting temple.
Text: This temple in the heart of Jaffna is in dravidian style. I very much enjoyed my visit and I was able to observe offering ceremonies. There is a fabulous processional carriage tucked away in a corner, when there are no functions. Don't miss it.

Title: Beautiful
Text: Very beautiful temple! Be warned, if you are a male, you need to remove your shirt. I wish there was a visitor's centre outside the temple to cater to tourists. However, I was guided by a tour guide who was able to give me the insights of the Temple.

Title: Amazing
Text: The temple was wonderful and is dedicated to murugan. To the left it has a shivan koil which also is to be visited.

Title: WAW as always
Text: This is one of the must visit temples in Jaffna. As most of the temples they have changed the granite rock to gold look which for me has lost a bit of character. Apart from that it is the same temple which I know from my child hood. Brilliant temple to pray.

Title: Impressive!
Text: I visited Nallur Kovil in the evening, at around 5:30pm. A certain ceremony took place in front of it on the street. Later I walked around to find an open entrance ( it is open only on one side ). It felt very spiritual and holy inside. An evening ceremony followed also inside.

Title: Majestic Kovil
Text: this is a very majestic kovil and a must visit in jaffna. Not that much of parking around, but if you hang around for a while you would get a space. No pictures allowed inside.

Title: Prayers
Text:
We were told to go here numerous time and main reason to Jaffna was for this.
Its a great visit and was need to remove my shirt .need to be here to experience it. Managed to attend their Pooja and was mesmerized with it.

Title: A must-see
Text: Especially during celebrations you should visit this main temple in Jaffna city. You can walk around the courtyard

Title: Mesmerizing Hindu Temple
Text: Lovely and inviting feeling. There is arichanai where gods are opened and worshiped every hour. We observed that the native people near the temple nor the Ayer at the entrance of the temple didnt start speaking with us in the  native language Tamil nor English but Sinhalese, which surprised us. After they new that we were originally from Jaffna they were comfortable talking to us in Tamil.

Title: During the Aadi festival
Text: The temple was splendid with its extravagant structure and opulence. People from all over the world were there to witness and be part of the festival. Men had to take off their shirts, which is a part of the culture and reverence to the deity. Inspite of the massive crowd, (even foreigners are allowed inside the temple) there was peace and quiet, and abundance of fulfilment from a devotee perspective. I happened to visit this temple by chance during the festival and I consider it a blessing.

Title: High spirited vibes..
Text: A beautiful place to visit, relax, calm down and recharge..very serene and loving atmosphere..helpful priests and uplifting pujas..a must visit, if you are on a spiritual quest..

Title: A must visit in Jaffna
Text: While dreaming to visit Jaffna this is the main attraction for any tourist who have faith and belief in religion.

Title: Wonderful Hindu Kovil...A Cultural Experience!
Text: The Nallur Kovil is definitely worth the visit as it is a major Hindu shrine in northern Sri Lanka.  Men are required to remove their shirts upon entering the Kovil.  There are not many foreign visitors with most of the people being local.  It is best to visit during the morning as it is often closed in the afternoon.  Definitely a cultural experience.

Title: Well worth the visit
Text:
We were fascinated by the place and it's a must view temple with very view foreigners venturing there.
Makes must be bare chested.
Go take a look and staff are very accomodating.

Title: Spectacular temple
Text: It's a spectacular temple. Enjoyed the puja. Remember that only gents should remove there shirt or t shirt when entering the temple. Foreigners are allow to go in.

Title: Beautiful
Text: This temple is very well known in Jaffna. They manage to maintain and improve the interior of the temple each year. It looks much better compared to the last time I visited this temple 4 years ago.

Title: Fantastic temple
Text: Beautiful temple. The outside is amazing and also very similar inside. There were some construction work going on inside which kind of ruined the experience a bit. People have to respect the people and follow the clothingrules and the native people will greet you when you enter.

Title: Amazing temples
Text: I spent the day cycling around Jaffna while I was there and this was my favourite of all the temples and holy sights that I came across. Go in the evening from about 4pm when the light is at its best

Title: Must Visit Place in Jaffnna
Text: Very beautiful temple in Jaffna very close to the city and must visit place for travellers who visit Jaffna

Title: rich murugan temple
Text:
one of must visit temple in Jaffna! must visit during their festival in August.

Title: Famous temple
Text: The Nallur temple is a famous attraction to Jaffna.I visited the temple on a Friday and the temple is little crowded.The temple is in the heart of Jaffna.While entering inside the temple,gents must remove the shirts as per the temple rules.The premises are well maintained and a must place to visit.

Title: Typical Jaffna Temple
Text: Beautiful interior and lovely to walk around.  No photography allowed inside.  Shoes to be left at the entrance.  Men - no shirts.

Title: Exquisite temple
Text: one could spend hours inside this elaborate and ornate  temple. though the temple tank is currently being renovated, the rest of the temple is fabulous. Go at one of the "pooja" times and you will experience something exquisite.

Title: Definitely worth visiting in Jaffna
Text: Under restoration at the moment but beautiful Hindu temple. We visited for the brief midday puja which was worthwhile. Certainly a good insight into a culture that is different from that which dominates most of Sri Lanka.

Title: Famous Temple in Jaffna
Text: A must visit to all visitors to Jaffna, you need to be on time to see the service. A very memorable visit to Nallur Kovil. very limited time inside the temple you need to keep up with the service and you need to leave as they close the temple soon after service. Men's are required to take off their shirt before entering the temple.

Title: Famous Lord Murugan Temple in Jaffna
Text: This is one of the huge temple in Jaffna .The festivals begins on ist August and goes for nearly 3 weeks.Devotees come from different parts of SriLanka and worship the lord Murugan. At Night  you can  see colorful beautiful lights. This is situated  on the way To Point Pedro Road.People take buses from Jaffna Bus stand and who are residing  walk to the temple.During the festival time it is packed with crowds and mini shops,Ice Cream,rubber product,Bangles vendors..It will be an exciting evening.

Title: Religious place - great history
Text: We wanted to visit the temple during a pooja but we coudn't do it. If you are planning to visit the temple make sure that men has to take of their shirts before going to the temple. It is a place you must see.

Title: Evening Visit
Text: we visit at evening time. it was quite place. we couldn't enter inside of the temple, because the entrance door was shut. i didn't event get the pooja times. But we spent lots of time on the temple surrounding. Rio Ice cream is on the surrounding. It is really nice

Title: Great historical landmark!
Text: Well kept and definitely a place to visit if in Jaffna. Parking is done right out side the Kovil, so has easy access. Must Visit!

Title: Religious
Text: Well known and must visited place in Jaffna - local people visits regularly for pryers and now another good attraction for tourist. The temple is constructed artistically. Must visit

Title: Beautiful Hindu Tempel and great Architecture
Text: Beautiful Hindu Tempel and great Architecture. If you're in Jaffna, a must see Tempel. Unfortunately no photos are allowed inside the tempel. But it was one of the coolest tempel in whole Sri Lanka, therefore no regrets.

Title: Beautiful temple, but why build more towers?
Text: A large beautiful temple with monumental brightly-painted ornate towers. But I am not sure why they are building another tower. The money could be spent on other charitable social programmes.

Title: A bit boring
Text: One of the major sights in Jaffna, so probably worth seeing. Just dont plan to spend too much time on it - after all, it is quite boring.

Title: temple
Text: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil or Nallur Murugan Kovil (Tamil: ??????? ?????????? ??????) is one of the most significant Hindu temples in the Jaffna District of Northern Province, Sri Lanka. It stands in the town of Nallur. The presiding deity is Lord Murugan in the form of the holy Vel. The idol of the Nallur Devi or goddess was given to the temple in the 10th century CE by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, in the style of Sembian bronzes.
